name: Superliminal
detailed_description: Superliminal is a first-person puzzle game based on forced perspective and optical illusions. Puzzles in this game give you a sense of the unexpected. Players need to change their perspective and think outside the box to wake up from the dream. WAKE UP As you fall asleep with the TV on at 3AM, you remember catching a glimpse of the commercial for Dr. Pierce’s Somnasculpt dream therapy program. By the time you open your eyes, you’re already dreaming - beginning the first stages of this experimental program. PERCEPTION IS REALITY Explore a dream world where everything is exactly as it seems. Tread carefully as the world slowly unravels around you and subverts your expectations. What you see isn’t always precisely what you get. MAN VS MACHINE In this fully-voiced adventure, Dr Glenn Pierce is doing his questionable best to guide you home and out of the dreamscape. His artificial intelligence assistant, however, is having trouble understanding exactly how you’re here at all, and has other plans for you. DEVELOPER COMMENTARY We’ve added an extensive developer commentary throughout the game, so you can learn the secrets and history behind the game’s development. CHALLENGE MODE The overwhelming response from the speedrunning community to Superliminal inspired us to add a new Challenge Mode, which will score you per-level on metrics such as time to finish, grabs, and jumps. EXPERIMENTAL WORKSHOP SUPPORT Superliminal features Steam Workshop integration. Bring any 3D object into the game and play around with mind-bending perspective tricks.

short_description: Perception is reality. In this mind-bending first-person puzzler, you escape a surreal dream world through solving impossible puzzles using the ambiguity of depth and perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I would only recommend this game to those who aren't completionists, and overall would not recommend picking this game up if you are a completionist because there is a number of achievements that are just terrible. I felt forced to upload things on the workshop, even though I didn't want to, and needed to figure out how to upload a 3D image. Not to mention that any game with a speedrun achievement of under 30 minutes is just awful. If its on sale, and you do not care about achievements, pick it up, but if you care just save yourself the headache.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very good art, peaceful pace and chilling atmosphere. Speaking of which, sadly, the  feeling has not been accomplished, at least for me.Puzzles are easy and do not crack a brain. I feel, that a more challenge would be good.There were levels, that lacked logic and consistency (maybe it was intentional, having the conclusion from the ending in mind), where I had to run in a random directions.Generally, it is a decent product, but feels the lack of inspiration. .
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I could make a case for both recommend or not recommend this game, but given how I ended up feeling about it, I guess it's more a not recommend after all.The game starts ok, the mechanics are really cool the first time you use them, the puzzles go along with a nice curve of difficulty, and the setting of the game (hardly can I call it "story") is ok at best, and that's the first let down for me: it tries so obviously to be Portal that it hurts, it's not a direct copy, but in the end, it's a carbon copy of the structure of Portal, but poorly done.First part it's fine, puzzles are fine and it keeps you intrigued on what's going to happened, but then in the second half when  the game goes to hell, puzzles suddenly become more and more scarce, to the point where near the end the last hour of so it almost become a walking simulator, also no new mechanics are introduced, it felt really rushed, also the ending is awful boring and uninteresting.There are secrets, collectibles and I got a secret ending which made me chuckle a little, but I feel zero motivation to try to get all the secrets and achievements, also it's VERY short, I beat it in under 4 hours, probably under 3 hours because I left it open for a while one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a very inventive puzzle game, which I quite enjoyed playing through for a couple of hours. This game reminds me a lot of the Stanley Parable with the funny narration and surreal "office" setting, but with some fun new mechanics that really keep it engaging. Using the perspective trick is taught smoothly, and I blew through most of the early puzzles, but later on you do have to think outside the box a bit. Puzzle game fans should definitely check this out!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfect. You can tell the devs really enjoyed making this game and put effort into it. The soundtrack is beautiful, the voice acting is amazing, the level design is intricate and detailed, everything about this screams great game. I've played through the main story about nine times now and I could do it nine times more.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Generally amazing and mechanically impressive game, the object scaling through perspective mechanic specifically never fails to impress. The puzzles weren't so easy they were boring or too frustratingly hard, they hit that spot where solving each one feels like a victory in of itself. It takes the tired "the entire video game was a dream" trope and flips it on its head in a new and exciting way. The soundtrack is one of a kind and I find myself listening to it outside of the game all the time. In my opinion the main game ends too soon, but then again this caliber of game requires a monumental amount of creative effort. Would immediately buy a DLC with more official levels if one ever drops. Workshop content and Multiplayer keeps me coming back for more. Lastly, I find myself applying the theme of the story to real life all the time, after all, some problems just require a change in perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazingly creative puzzle game.The game is beautiful in a minimalistic way, some puzzles make you exclaim out loud because of how creative they are. I can also praise the fact that 3D models are very high definition even when made very large, scaling objects up is very seamless.There was only one part of the game which I deemed unfair and for which I think the vast majority of players will need a tutorial as I did (perception is not reality), and shadows were pixelated even at highest settings.The game is also somewhat short, so players trying to specifically get their money's worth might be left slightly unsatisfied if they buy it at full price. 9.5/10 definitely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It's a perfectly functional game with a fun mechanic that it seems the developers seem to have run out of ideas to use. The apparent size = real size trick just doesn't have enough uses to make complex puzzles, meaning the developers (cleverly in my opinion) have each section of the game based around a secondary mechanic -- often based around a type of optical illusions. Unfortunately, these illusions are not implemented particularly well, and after playing View Finder (another puzzle game with a more versatile but similar core mechanic) were a bit of a let-down.To somewhat pad the game, there are 4 different types of collectibles to hunt for. Unfortunately, rather than being an award for clever thinking or mastery of the game mechanics, they instead can only be found by going over every part of the level with a fine-tooth comb -- an experience akin to sifting through sand.Without going into it, the story is also nothing to write home about. It's a one-trick pony whose one trick you can tell is coming from about a 1/5th into the game. Its message lukewarm, prepackaged self-help advice. I will say, however, there is one sequence that uses the established mechanics in a totally new way -- in a sense subverting them -- that did get my blood moving. Unfortunately this was one glimmering moment surrounded by tedium. This is a ridiculously easy puzzle game with such a brittle core-mechanic that even the challenge mode offers no real challenge, as all it does is have you replay the same puzzles, no alterations, just using the fewest moves. If you've already beaten the puzzles normally, you know what moves you already need to make and so the real challenge is staying awake through puzzles you've already solved.Just play the free demo and move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like migraines? Do you like sitting at the computer and just asking yourself what in the absolute f you just witnessed? This is the game for you! It's a puzzle game with a beyond unique mechanic that makes every level astonishing with near-endless replay value in spite of the fact its a puzzle game.Good stuff, my brain hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: A colourful first person puzzle game that seems desperate to copy Portal, but lacks both the versatility of mechanics and quality of writing.While the perspective-based puzzles seem clever and interesting at first, it quickly becomes clear that there are really only a handful of challenges that they can solve - typically a button that's difficult to press or a ledge that's too high to climb - and the solutions are similarly limited. As an attempt to address this, the core mechanic behaves differently in certain levels (e.g. at one point rather than picking up objects, it clones them) but you have no control over these temporary changes and there is almost no effort put into explaining them so ultimately it undermines the internal logic and feels out of place.There are some clever perspective tricks here and there which often made me chuckle in surprise, but very few of these are interactive: a corridor will turn out to just be painted on the wall, or what looks like a shadow will actually be a doorway. One redeeming aspect of the puzzling is that the bonus collectables in each level require a bit more creative thinking, but I often found myself frustrated trying to reach them because positioning objects is fiddly and the physics sometimes freak out when stacking things.Despite my complaints, the puzzles are probably the best part of the game because the writing certainly isn't. As previously mentioned, the game really wants to be Portal but takes this much too far: You play as a subject going through various tests while being overseen by an AI that speaks with a woman's voice and makes vaguely sarcastic and/or sinister comments; eventually you get 'out of bounds' which causes the digital personality to become increasingly hostile; and then you work your way through various different areas with the final goal of escaping the tests. This alone would have been enough to have me rolling my eyes, but it's also delivered with uninspiring dialogue and terrible pacing.After a fairly strong introduction the mid portion has very little plot advancement and is essentially just a series of unrelated levels, including one long section with no puzzles that tries to evoke a horror atmosphere but only succeeded in boring me because there was no sense of threat. Even as the story nears its end a lot of the dialogue seems irrelevant or repetitive, and the ending itself is offensively smug and saccharine  as if the developers believe the experience to be somehow profound or educational.Normally I'm not one to criticise a game's length, but somehow this game felt both too long and too short. The poor pacing left me wishing the game finished sooner, but upon quitting I was shocked to see it had only been 4 hours and I'm unlikely to go back anytime soon.All in all, I had hoped for a lot from this game but was ultimately disappointed. It might be worth a go on sale just to see the various perspective tricks, optical illusions, etc. that are genuinely smart and surprising, but maybe just watch a playthrough instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: In the end I was disappointed by the game. It's not a terrible game and can be a bit fun, but in the end I can't recommend it.Having seen the tech demo and the screenshots, I feel there was nothing new or challenging in the game. I kept waiting for some actual puzzles, but the game just became more random.One could make the argument, that the game is less meant as a puzzler and more as an interactive experience, but for that the story felt too unoriginal and the graphics very bland.The game reminded me of "Antichamber" which I feel has done the "Perception is the game" a lot better.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Another game strongly influenced by Portal. It has a DAMNED good 'gimmick', shifting perspectives and all that. A lack of a hook like this is what's supposedly keeping "3" (both Portal and Half-Life) from happening.Indeed, it's a real shame Valve couldn't have scooped it up early and groomed it into a legitimate Portal sequel (a la Narbacular Drop).I say that because, while the puzzles were interesting and there's a lovely otherworldly quality to it all, there isn't really enough gas in the tank, narratively speaking, to push it over the finish line into greatness.What would The Stanley Parable or Portal be if you removed all the narration, world building, humor, and overall personality?Something close to Superliminal, I'd wager. Oh, it tries here and there, but it feels halfhearted. Sometimes it's a voice on the radio. Sometimes it's a GLaDOS-like PA announcement. Sure, it's a treat to wander around and experience the puzzles, but there's absolutely nothing making me clamor for more. And it doesn't go far enough to compete with the complete mind-♥♥♥♥ heights of, say, Antichamber.I can say this with no hesitation, however: the lighting in this game is absolutely gorgeous. And for such a terrific gimmick, it was weird how it all just worked with very little in the way of a tutorial. That's amazing.It's also worth noting that this is a very short game. Roughly 3 hours for me, but I was really digging around for secrets. Considering the narrative issues discussed above, this is probably a good thing. Do the trick. Then get out.Superliminal will sit next to Stanley Parable and Antichamber as some of my favorite alt-thinking FPS puzzlers, but at a distant third.The frustration of how great this could have been will haunt me until at least later this evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: There were neat aspects in this game. The mechanics unique and fun to mess around with. But the performance is not great considering that it's not the most graphically complex game out there. The play time is also pretty short. I feel like I got stuck a lot and I still finished pretty quickly. I'm not opposed to short games, but I'd wait for a sale.On a more personal note, I feel like the story was disappointing. I really liked where it was going for most of the game. It got a surprising amount of emotional reactions from me. But the end not only felt kinda phoned in, but it also trampled over all of the parts that I liked about the story up until that point.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a wonderful, thoughtful first-person puzzler with an emphasis on perspective mechanics.The story is surprisingly heartwarming and the gameplay takes a few good twists and turns.I highly recommend this game, but beware people who get motion sickness, this game will trigger it after about 30min of playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from being a great gameplay experience, this game teaches an important lesson about solving ones problems in life. Doing so through the metaphor of thinking in a different perspective to solve puzzles within the dreams. This game is the definition a of shot but sweet game.I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic and well executed concept.The simple presentation and story helps well in putting the puzzles in the focus, with calm music keeping you relaxed while you try to wrap your brain around the unusual problems.Trying to find out what twist the game put on your perspective next makes you want to keep going, and the witty story bits in between puzzles keep you entertained.I also found it entertaining to search for all secrets, though it can be grueling to have gone through a level multiple times over and over again and still missing that one fire alarm or chess piece.... Still, with some neat little easter eggs, bananas and hidden drawings to be found, it felt rewarding to look at every corner of the game, and trying to exploit the mechanics to the fullest.All in all, a very entertaining and well made puzzle game with a very unique mechanic that I had not yet seen before.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Can we break free from the constraints of one's mind?To shift one's perspective is to challenge one's mind. Our mind can anchor our thoughts, trapping us into thinking linearly, and when we do, we flatten our mind and vision. However, if we successfully shift our perspective, we can shatter the constraints of one's mind, which then ultimately sets us free.Superliminal is all about perception and perspective. The narrative and gameplay harmonize, making Superliminal stand out more than most games. The gameplay is creative in an abstract way. To solve puzzles, you have to think outside the box. Though the puzzles are not too challenging, they serve as narrative stepping blocks.Superliminals narrative is more than just an entertaining story. It truly feels like the story is trying to convey a meaningful message. The voice actor of Dr. Glenn Pierce delivers voice lines in such a clear and vibrant way, enhancing the narrative and making the story come to life.The music is nothing short of brilliant. Smooth classical jazz makes the setting come alive. The music evolves, making the chapters memorable to such a degree that I can remember which chapter they belong to.I'm not here to tell you that Superliminal is going to change your life, but perhaps it will give you a different perspective. And sometimes, a different perspective is all you need.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: By far one of the best games I've ever played. The challenging puzzles mixed with the amazing story/narrative is one of a kind, and i would definitely recommend this to anyone who is looking for a game to sink a good amount of time and thought into.(p.s the graphics are amazing and the game runs amazing)
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this to anyone looking to play a relaxing (if, at times, unsettling) puzzle game.It encourages you to explore off the beaten path, and finding the collectibles is ever-so rewarding (especially as they tend to be hidden behind their own obstacles).I found the story to be quite sweet and fairly well-executed. The majority of the puzzles weren't too difficult, and there was only one in which I feel I didn't solve it the intended way, as my method was slightly tedious and relied on excessive cloning. At very few points did I feel stumped or that I was out of things to try.As a player who tends to try and push games to their limits, I love that Superliminal rewards you for doing so, and I can say that I only had to reset to checkpoints twice (the first time getting caught in the ceiling whilst trying to get over a wall that I wasn't meant to; the second by some problem with loading the next section).The only complaint I truly have is that some of the movement and visuals made me slightly nauseous, but that may just be some of the disorientation that comes with the mechanics of the game.I plan on replaying this to get the remaining collectibles, and to try out the extra modes unlocked by completing the game, so while the main game is rather short (it took me 5-6 hours with slightly excessive searching), there is still more to do!I hope this was helpful :)
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Super liminal has an amazing in depth story,from the first part of it everything seems goofy and simple, but the story takes the simple and makes in hard, they take that goofy part and make it twisted. the way the rooms were designed it feels like a safe dream, a safe place. but the game shatters the reality of the safe place and flips everything around, what it seems is not what it is. the creepy parts are broken with a sense of hope and then the safe place that is twisted again in a different way everytime. and at the end it feels like you just went through a long dream, but it wasn't. the alarm clocks give everything a stranger darker vibe.10/10 AMAZING!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's portal 1, but instead of the game's gimmick being a portal gun to move around a level to get to the exit while a computer makes snarky comments over a speaker system, this game's gimmick is that you can resize objects to move around a level to get to the exit while a computer makes snarky comments over a speaker system. It's kind of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't think this is a bad game, don't get me wrong. The aesthetics is nice and the atmosphere good. And the game has an interesting concept. But after finishing it I feel kind of disappointed. Most of the puzzles are kind of easy and the difficulty doesn't increase as you progress through the game. _childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun little game, definitely worth a play.Came in around 3-4 hours, with the odd interruption.I was after something kinda chill, calm, not too taxing, and this fit perfectly - passed some time while I had a fever.(Looks like there's tons more completionist content though).There's a really neat variety of mechanics, which can broadly be summarised as:- the scale thing- the duplication thing- portals with scaling- walls that look solid but aren't.- painted stuff becomes 3D stuffThere are some excellent puzzles amongst them, and nothing's over the top hard.It never really felt unfair.(except the apple thing with the fan - you'll see)Graphically, yeah I was quite impressed.I guess it's like the Stanley Parable with a fresh lick of paint, slightly higher res models, slightly newer shaders.Some scenes are genuinely beautiful, but that's not the main focus, and I think it strikes a nice balance.Audio-wise, again, very simplistic, reminiscent of Portal or The Stanley Parable, but without being too derivative.It definitely does its own thing within a familliar framework.The only issue I really faced is that it suffers so badly from pacing issues.Mainly:A: some of the game feels like filler they threw in at the last minute to stretch out a few encounters. There's not a ton of cohesion, which could be expected from the subject matter, but some mechanics are a bit underused, and some a bit overused. Often a hallway can feel like a tech demo that was left in because the author liked it (like Fugue in Void), but it's not obnoxious.B: Towards the end I was willing it to finish, as it tries to be a little more profound than it pulls off, but overall, it's a positive message, and they tie it up nicely.Seems pretty minor though?Give it a shot.p.s. 10/10 for the loading bars
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It starts as a quirky puzzle game, with an interesting set of game mechanics, but soon devolves into a bad joke. It tries to be copy a bit of what The Stanley Parable did, but without the smartness and humor. The puzzles could be so much better with these game mechanics. But it's wasted on a handful of simple puzzles.After a while it becomes really annoying. And I just gave up on this thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Portal but with the surrealist humor of the Stanley Parable with a touch of derealization puzzle elements as the cherry on the top. It is fantastically and brilliantly original in its puzzles, but unfortunately, due to its short playtime of just a couple of hours, it feels like it just barely scratched the surface of what is possible with its mechanics. I still highly recommend it, but I don't believe it warrants the full $20 pricetag. Buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It's always nice to think outside the box, and Superliminal forces you to do so each and every step of the way.While not excruciatingly difficult, the game does pose some challenges via the use of forced perspective, which the whole plot is centered around. In fact, I would say it's more of a nice, fun and easy way of forcing the player to think about what they are doing if they want to proceed to the next section.The narrative, while eerily similar to The Stanley Parable, does manage to differentiate itself, though at times I felt it was headed in the exact same direction (despite the game being very lineal in nature). By the end it draws parallelisms to the feeling of being stuck in a problem and how to overcome those challenges, and I thought that was rather cool (I was expecting a 4th wall break much like TSP).I am more than certain that, technically speaking, Superliminal is an amazing achievement in how forced perspective is achieved without breaking, but I am also certain that there is a documentary about it, and if not, it should be as I would binge watch it in an instant.Overall, I'd say give this one a go if you are tired of the straight forward games and looking for a nice, short puzzle game that sends a nice message.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning slight spoilersSuperliminal is a optical illusion perspective puzzle game about the theme of perspective. You can tell the game is taking a lot of influence from Portal and The Stanley Parable from it's presentation. This works in most of the puzzle aspects. The puzzles are fun, with a few duds in the mix, and a lot of them end up being funny. It felt like the game was just messing with you, which is where I found much of the humor. The last chapter felt a lot more like a walking simulator than the rest of the game. Which is where I felt the game was the weakest.  The end feels like its hammering down the theme of perspective way too hard; which, for me personally, wasn't exploring the theme more than the surface level ideas on perspective. not that I disagree with the game was trying to say. Wrong I think was that our dreams can distort or perspective in such a way that's hard to change that perspective, or at least that feels like the game is close on touching on. Part of that problem might be the dialogue in the game. It wasn't all that interesting, or funny, so it didn't hit in the way I felt it should.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Often when we wake up after a dream it evokes a strange emotion. Usually dreams are difficult to recall and their details slip between our fingers before we can place them. If you have ever wished to enter that in between state of sleeping and awakeness, a lucidity where dreams can be experienced in the most vivid of detail, Superliminal is this in a perfect package.I am writing this review right after I have finished my first ever playthrough, so admittedly I don’t have all the detail on the extra content, but regardless of anything else it provides I think this game even in its most barebones is worth the money.The game play is similar to that of games like “Portal” or “The Witness” and also is reminiscent of “The Stanley Parable” though it is more linear and only with a total play time of under three hours. Unlike “The Witness” though, I think the puzzles in the game are considerably easier and less obtuse, so more than likely you won’t be spending any longer than twenty minutes on any one which I see as a massive plus side. The puzzles may not take very long, but I wouldn’t call them “simple”. They are more elegant in nature and often if you are doing something that requires a lot of keyboard maneuvering or multivariable calculus to figure out, you are overthinking it.Usually after I finish a game I am happy and excited of course, but it more comes from some kind of relief. Superliminal differs in this aspect. Finishing Superliminal feels like finishing a book. After its completion, it gives you something to think about.	If you have made it this far in the review and still are on the fence I only have one closing remark: There are other games with puzzles, with interesting atmospheres, and with good messages or stories, but I would put any one of them against Superliminals pure originality on all three fronts. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: for more reviews like this.Superliminal is not the masterpiece that many claim it is. I'm not saying this because I didn't enjoy the game, I actually quite enjoyed my playthrough of it, but I'm saying this because it does have a couple problems with it. The most important part of a puzzle game in my opinion is the rules that exist within said game. Rules are crucial in a puzzle game because they define what you can and can't do in the game. Building puzzles around these rules are what every great puzzle game does. Superliminal is a game about perspective. The puzzles you solve all focus around perspective and how you view the world around you and how you interact with the world to solve the puzzles. Unfortunately in Superliminal, the game is constantly changing its rules with what you can do and what you can't do. The first 30 minutes of the game actually did this brilliantly and was when I was having the most fun with the game. The puzzles built off of each other and we're very enjoyable to solve. Unfortunately soon after, the game decided to do a 180 and every room has its own set of rules with what you can and can't do and it introduces new ideas without giving you the necessary knowledge of said idea to solve the puzzles. Multiple puzzles in this game are so frustrating and needlessly difficult because the game doesn't properly introduce and teach you the new rules and ideas it keeps throwing at you. You will most likely need a guide at some parts of the game which is unfortunate because the game could've just added in more puzzles that gradually introduce the new ideas this game has into the game instead not only increasing the play time of the game but also making the overall experience better. The game has some genuine moments of beauty and genius that I think are worth playing the game to see. The "story" of the game is incredibly meh and extremely predictable but it doesn't get in the way and gives you a reason to keep moving forward. Overall, Superliminal is a game with moments of genius that genuinely could have been a masterclass in the puzzle genre but ultimately falls just short. The game isn't worth $20 but if you can get it for around $10 and are a fan of the genre I think you'll enjoy your time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember picking up Superliminal because lots of youtubers were playing it, and many people thought that it shared a lot of similarities with portal and the Stanley parable. Which are two games that I remember fondly.When I picked up and finished the game however, I found myself being incredibly disappointed. I expected to play a game that had clever writing, an engaging story and/or enjoyable puzzles.Unfortunately the only game I received was one that had a few novel ideas for game mechanics, but were so half-baked it was like eating a sandwich with nothing in it. The premise and plot of the game is setup at the beginning but also goes completely nowhere; which is odd, because they do spend a fair amount of time setting up a possible conflict, but never really followed through with it.The game suffers from a lot of the same problems that other puzzles games like 'the room' do. You're spending your time trying to figure out what the puzzle is, rather than solving it. And once you do figure out what you're supposed to be doing, it's disappointingly easy.The events in the gameplay don't seem to build towards anything interesting. Things just happen and keep going before they stop abruptly and try to do something radically different or unexpected. In other words, it tries too hard to subvert your expectations, before their even set up in the first place. There's no 'game' here. It's mostly just going from one room to the next, waiting for the next subversion that just falls flat.The ending doesn't feels earned. It basically amounts to a character explaining what the  meaning of the game is supposed to be, leaving no room for personal interpretation of what you've just played. And the interpretation they give, feels shallow at best and insulting at worst. If you're looking at this game and expecting a fun puzzle game, you might be wowed by the introduction of the mechanics, but that's all there is to it; it's never properly built upon. If you ask me, it feels more like playing the alpha demo of a proof of concept that was taken as a finished product and polished up to the state that it's in now. Which is basically what the precursor to this game: 'The museum of simulation technology' was.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly inspiring game that forces you to take a look at the problems that face you from a new angle, and in doing so, makes you learn a new thing about the way you think. It teaches us that the problems that we face in our day-to-day lives may only be problems because of their presence in our day-to-day nature of living. When we take a deep breath, a step back and a long hard look and a think, our problems seem to disintegrate because the context that deems them "problems" is not there. This game shows the importance of looking at things from another angle, and realising that dead ends are only subjective to the person experiencing them; and that when that person decides to change their viewpoint, they become unstuck. A sobering and inspiring message for those that feel like they are at the tail end of circumstance, and a brilliant way of highlighting the importance of change. Change helps us grow, and playing this game helped me realise that we do not solve our problems simply by "getting stronger" or "smarter", but by growing and allowing the way we perceive things to change, and thus changing the environment around us and the old problems it presented to us; this means that change is the only true constant, and if your problems are constant, then they are not truly unsolvable, and that you are never truly stuck. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: What is up is now down. What is left is now right. What is hot is now cold. What is day is now night.What is not real is now real.In Superliminal, you'll be waking up in a perpetual loop of you moving around a science facility, where you'll encounter dozens of puzzle rooms very akin to the Portal games. But while in the Portal games you moved yourself around the environment via two-way portals, in Superliminal you'll be transforming the environment simply by looking at it a new direction. That normal-sized chess piece in your hand? Back up a little bit and now it's actually four feet tall. That model house in a kid's room? Pick it up and look from a different angle to see it as large as a full-size house which you can now walk inside of. Everything in Superliminal requires you to simply adopt a new perspective, and uncover new secrets by looking at things in ways that may not seem obvious. Superliminal was a fantastic experience, and though it was a little short, it will give any puzzle enthusiast a challenge and a delightful time. A must-buy for Portal enjoyers and puzzle fans.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Not at all what I expected. Bait-and-switch that suddenly abandons puzzles for a pretentious walking simulator.A few hours into the game, where MOST puzzle games would begin to weave together multiple mechanics that have been introduced in the previous challenges, Superliminal instead abruptly transforms into a pretentious walking simulator with almost no more "gameplay" to speak of.All the rules you thought you learned immediately go out the window, and instead the game becomes a series of brightly-lit hallways where you are expected to trial-and-error click on random objects or mash your face against walls to progress. When the rules change in every single room, they're not puzzles anymore - they're just blind guesses. To keep you company, a series of voice-over lines wax poetic about the power of perspective and how this experience is so transformative and profound.The last 30 minutes of the game were incredibly tiresome for me, as the designers clearly ran out of clever PUZZLE ideas and instead just decided to beat me over the head with a laborious metaphor. The final room in the game that could I would say counts as a "puzzle" even has a voiceover that plays after a few minutes, telling you what to do to progress, as though the developers were aghast that you might be accidentally spending too much time  in their incredibly deep and meaningful narrative masterpiece.On the plus side, the first hour-and-change was great, and the game has a very lovely soundtrack and some great visuals. But I can't give this a thumbs up when it pulls such a blatant bait-and-switch RIGHT when it's getting good.Don't pay more than $5 for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked either of the Portal games, that alone is a HUGE reason to get this game. Superliminal is one of the only games I've seen that manages to capture a similar atmosphere to Portal while still staying its own thing. The mechanics of this game's puzzles are simple to learn, but the game manages to put a LOT of mileage into them. These mechanics are fun and enjoyable to mess around with, and the game rewards you for thinking outside the box. The puzzles are challenging, but rewarding. No solution to the game's story mode ever felt cheap or unfair. Not only that, but the music is amazing, and Superliminal handles its own atmosphere perfectly.If you liked GLaDOS and her sense of humor, you'll definitely like the humor this game has in it. While the robotic voice in the halls isn't nearly as evil, it perfectly illustrate's Superliminal's ability to appeal to Portal fans without being a Portal clone. If you like puzzle games and you like humor, I'd seriously recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.. just wowLet me go into detail of why this is one of the best games I've ever played.First of all I would like to mention that I'm an actual sucker for story platformer puzzle games like this.Superliminal is similar to games like the Stanley parable and aparture desk job. It does so many things well that Stanley parable has done well too however it is still a very unique experience.And by experience I mean EXPERIENCE, for this type of game will fascinate you in a way an art gallery or an escape room would. What stands out most to me is the incredible LEVEL DESIGN:* the game guides you through levels seamlessly and without annoying unsolvable segments while still surprising you*It makes amazing use of sounds and light as guidance for the player*the pace of the game is incredibly well made, audio segments are pretty much never cut off too early*every segment seems to be unique and not too long so it doesn't get boring*the way some levels are made is so incredibly creative (and honestly probably so complex to make wtf) that it made me chuckle*the players view is seamlessly directed to the next obstacle or pathSTORY:*slow but steady building story/ you might not immidiately understand wtf is going on (personally I love that)*nice narration of 2 different voices, they kinda feel like buddies by now (sometimes the narration was cut off or audio was too fast for the text, needs fixing)*atmosphere changes throughout the game, chaos ensues*you might end up finding a new spiritual view to life... or just feeling dizzy idkwithout spoilers.... this could actually be seen as a little bit of therapy heheVISUALS:*rather simple style, not a lot of detail but why would this game need it?*some scenes have pretty scenery or an atmospheric feel*I would have loved a few more eastereggs but maybe I just missed them (dunno why I put this in visuals)UPDATE: after completing all the achievements, I've obviously changed my mind and realized that I was indeed too dumb to find them*many different kinds of environments  *funnily reused props*obviously the scaling aspect is so funAll in all in terms of level design this game is an absolute ace, it should be shown to anyone who wants to learn level design.PRICE vs WHAT WE GET:I received this game on sale, it was like 9 euros or some. For what it cost it's almost way too good, ngl.It's got a solif length of around 2-3 hours firt playtime however you can also play it with your friends on multiplayer and there is some more modes I havent tried yet. Would definitely buy this game for 20 euros, no question.All in all I never expected such a great experience and recommend this a lot.Thanks to the devs for a great game :)

_childDocuments_.review: My love for perspective gameplay is well documented at this point in other reviews, so I was really happy to finally play Superliminal. The game is about picking up objects and changing their size depending on how they’re framed against everything else in the scene from your own point of view. I mostly enjoyed my time with Superliminal a lot. It manages to employ its central mechanic creatively and in varied ways. It absolutely nails puzzle design 101 whenever it presents you with a challenge that resembles the one you’ve just completed but forces you to solve it a different way and makes solving it with the previous solution impossible, thus forcing you to really pay attention and learn how the mechanic works.Unfortunately, outside of the main mechanic, there isn’t all that much to the game. Sure, there are a bunch of easter eggs and other hidden stuff, but narratively speaking, it has the bare minimum of what you’d expect and nothing more. The writing tries to have a comedic tone about it similar to games like Portal or Quantum Conundrum, but it mostly just falls flat. Oh, and it really likes to employ that trick where you walk along a hallway or something with some kind of eye-catching object in front of you that you intend to reach. Only there’s a hole in the floor that you can’t see because the walls of the hole are shaded exactly the same as the rest of the floor and you fall down somewhere completely different. This happened a few too many times so that I was even able to anticipate these instances whenever I was walking along a lengthy hallway with not much to interact with.But other than that, it’s a pretty good game. I’d say it’s a bit expensive for the 2.5 hours of time it takes to get through, but price and game length are always a contentious point where everybody has to make up their own minds for how much game is worth how much money. Regardless, I’d say it’s definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, just take a tab of acid instead. You'll have a better time, it'll last at least six times longer, it's safer, more upbeat, half the price, and you will have much greater introspective than the message this game attempts to force.Superliminal isn't a bad game, it's just really mediocre. The only thing the game offers as a positive is the perspective play and the potential of Steam Workshop, but the negatives severely outweigh any positives. The main game can be beaten in about an hour by anyone competent, but don't worry, unless you already know how to beat the game you'll be stuck clicking and walking into everything trying to get passed the level because the game does not have any definitive rules.While you might say that this is quite obvious, let me explain from a developer's point of view. You want to introduce sets of rules throughout your game as to let players know what they can or cannot do, by breaking these rules the player can become confused, infuriated, or outright quit the game because it feels like more of a chore than an experience anymore.  Superliminal defines specific rules and then breaks them only minutes later, leaving the player confused on why things only work sometimes and then hugging walls and clicking everything only to look up the solution to what should have been an extremely easy problem to solve, yet took extremely long because the player never knows what does or does not work.The gameplay is the only reason you'll buy this for obvious reasons. The story is silly and acts as if it gives the player some sort of unknown knowledge of, you guessed it, viewing things from a different perspective to solve problems! The story content and message are so heavily fisted to the player that it's somewhat laughable and can be seen from miles away. It is somewhat condescending and is only a device to lengthen the game via turning certain portions into a walking simulator as to extend the game as much as possible.Overall, I can't recommend Superliminal for more than $10. I got it in a Humble Bundle with some other games, so I don't really feel burnt on this one, but can absolutely see why others do. The game is short, overrated, and relies on gimmicks which don't always work and turn the game into a Stanley Parable themed walking simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was, considering its observed reliance on gimmicks, a pleasant surprise of a game. anyone with a good appreciation for a well designed game will love this. The Controls are smooth and easy to understand, without being too complicated. The game is short and condensed, utilizing these shockingly clever gimmicks to catch you off guard. The whole game constantly throws new ideas at you, none of them ever overstaying their welcome, but not just dissappearing after their respective sections either. Every single room has so much deliberation and thought put in, and the rewards for exploring are plentiful. The soundtrack is beautiful, every theme fits its section and really sets the tone. The ending of the game is spectacular, I don't want to say too much about it for fear of spoilers, but it really feels like its throwing everything it has at you for this really intense mind bending peak, leading into a very fitting and calm ending segment. The message of the game is also oddly touching. The game as a whole is about perspective. This idea is implemented to deliver a very simple message that really struck me more than I would have anticipated. Their message of choice was that if everything you just overcame could be conquered by looking at it from (literally) a different angle, then maybe the key to overcoming the obstacles in your life is to do the same. The idea really doesn't come through well in text, but after playing through this game it will all make sense. Though there are plenty of cool secrets to go and find, this is really a one and done experience. The game is meant to blow you away, but only on the first playthrough. despite this, its one of the best games I've ever played, and though its maybe not THE best, I don't think it has any flaws.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is a gem. A puzzle game in the post-Portal style of "walk around in first-person 3D, solve puzzles that rely as much on you being clever as mechanical solutions". I got through it reasonably quickly (not enough so to trigger any speedrun achievements, mind) and enjoyed every moment. The premise is that you're having some dream therapy and they would rather like you to wake up, but you have all these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puzzles to solve and so you don't. You repeatedly don't wake up, so you can solve puzzles relating to perspective, forced-perspective, orientation, exploration, [redacted] and [super redacted]. You just really love puzzles okay.Well that's why I was doing it, you may vary.Absolutely time well-spent and I plan to go back and play again to listen to the developer commentary and whatnot. Strongly recommended if you enjoy dream logic, Portal-style puzzles and questioning what reality even is anymore, man.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the greatest puzzle games I've ever played. I've enjoyed games like Portal, The Witness, Antichamber, The Talos Principal, and others in a similar "break your brain" and "you're going to feel like a genius when you solve this" style, and Superliminal is for sure up there with those. The music is nice and the visuals are pleasant, but that's not why you're really here. The draw is how this game uses perspective to distort your reality and how you can use it to change objects around you. I'm sure I missed a lot of content as there's lots of hidden goodies in each level. Only negative I can say for the game is that it's over so quick. I finished it in a few hours and then it created a void in my life that needs another crazy cool puzzle game to help fill.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I usually never comment on these kind of things but this one was really good and I enjoyed every bit of it.It doesn't require specific movement skills but only thinking outside the box, if u overthink it u already lostIf you enjoyed Portal, you will definitely enjoy this one too!Hopefully it will have a second part too, might have seemed a little too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: this was such a fun experience, i love the art and the gameplay. it's truly just a really out of the box idea and it was great figuring out how to progress. also i love how the game sometimes took you for a fool in a very charming way. (that said the ending is a little whack ngl. but i didn't play this one for the story anyway-)
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of all time. It's only 3-4 hours long, but it's all it needs to tell this story. Perfect surrealist environments paired with great piano work done by John Reeves to create an otherworldly, but calming(?) atmosphere. It's a liminal environments game that doesn't try to be scary or creepy and it makes it different and great. Great sense of humor and the gameplay is purposeful to the story and makes it unique to this medium of storytelling. Incredible video game that I will recommend to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10, would recommend. Don't spoil it for yourself. I'll say it's a very good game, the only complaint I have is that sometimes there are graphical glitches, like the screen briefly going black, that break immersion. People say the story mode has about 7 or 8 hours of content, but in my experience it's more like 2 or 3, which makes the price a little bit not great.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Really cool use of perspective and color. I enjoyed all the levels except for one, which required a bit of moon logic to progress. Other than that, it was fun! Since it is so short, I would only recommend it on sale.The music is really calm and enjoyable. You learn about the story from the narrator and try to progress from level to level. The controls and mechanics are very simple, but not everything is what it seems. I wouldn't call it profound, but I do think there are some thought provoking elements that some people would really enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece in which it has perfected it's craft. This game is a environmental puzzle game where perception is the main game mechanic. It will trick you and it is a very fun playthough. This game has to be in my top 5 favorite games that I've ever played. I would highly recommend you try it.*Besides the story mode there is a multiplayer race mode where you compete to the finish line and you can directly mess with opponents. It's really fun. If you see me in there, raise me to the lobby ceiling please, thanks.*
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a one trick pony. I admire the developers, any developers who can make a half decent coherent game, like this one. But 3 hours total?? So not worth it for the price. And Superliminal soooo wishes it was the love child of Portal and The Stanley Parable, but it is no where near as clever as either. Sure pick it up a £5 or less, you can expect one or two mildly funny moments, and a couple of interesting puzzles. But nothing that makes you FEEL smart for having solved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience that I will definitely love to replay soon! The creators managed to find just the right way to tell this particular message through the game mechanics  - if you really let the game suck you in without rushing through, the timing of your awakening to what this game is actually trying to teach you will be absolutely perfect! - in my case, it led me to the secret ending before I could finish the game as well : ) I went in without having anything much spoiled and I am glad I did - whoever plans to play this, DO NOT SPOIL IT BY WATCHING WALKTHROUGHS, EXPERIENCE THE GAME YOUR SELF , FIRST!!  And truly - indulge into the game and you will be rewarded much much more than flying through it. Loved the music as well, overall a really great experience worth your time and the buy (even at full price)! Definitely one of the most unique games currently out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and trippy, I enjoyed the whole thing, though it got me addicted to soda again. I got stuck on one level for like 30 minutes because I looked at something once from the wrong angle then never looked again, and had to look up how to beat that level, but other than that the game was very straightforward and relatively simple. The multiplayer is fun to mess around in but the announcer is annoying since he calls you cheats the whole time, even though we were in a private lobby. When we played public lobby we just got a cheater who insta finished each level so don't expect there to be people to play against unless you brought a friend. Game was fun when I played through the story solo and then again with my friend. I just wish the game was longer.solo 9/10with friends 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it when it was on sale for $12. I definitely think it's worth it. I've taken a bit of computer science and I was blown away with this game. Didn't think some of the stuff they did was even possible to code. This game really bends your mind. I looked at some of the negative reviews and it's just people who egos are to big for their heads or those who think $20 for a 2 hour experience isn't worth it. I also played it over a span of a week so maybe that's why I didn't get "bored". Also my goal wasn't to finish it. I took my time pulling every fire alarm and spamming every button on the vending machines. However I believe $20 is definitely worth it with the amount of coding and testing I know they had to put into it. I don't know of any other game like this. If you like portal I think you will like this. Also if you're open minded and love questioning reality you'll enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Very short but fun and artsy experience. I think the devs could have done a bit more with the mechanics, but I felt it was worth the 8$ on sale.The Battle Royale mode would be a fun trippy version of fall guys, but unfortunetly there are not enough active players.Can recommend on sale, if you like games like The Stanley Parable or Beginners Guide. But the puzzles are not sophisticated enough to be compared to Antichamber or Portal.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: it's a great game it took me a while a few extra tries where i wouldn't be proud of admitting, overall a great, slightly stressful, perspective changing experience that allows you to (take a second walk back and change your perspective) ending did make me cry tho, i wasn't ready for that one but if you finish the game you get a very nice, message that more people should hear.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun. It's a game filled with cool puzzles that make you think outside the box. You're made to view the puzzles from a different perspective, which is also something the game is trying to teach you about. With a mix of fun gimmicks, brain grinding puzzles, a bit of spoopyness and a really nice message at the end, you have yourself a game that is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little puzzle game. Cool idea to use perspective and out of the box thinking rather than multi variable trail and error puzzles. There are a few parts that it forces extra constraints on you that don't allow you to use the same principles you've learned which cheapens the experience, and there was one part when i got glitched/bugged out of a puzzle and had to check a walkthrough to see if i was doing the right thing. Story sucks too btw. But overall its fun and inventive. It is short but its still a good time. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting puzzle game, some of the levels were pretty challenging and the length of it felt pretty good too, it would have been a little teddious if the game was longer. There are a couple of side content you can do but it requires to replay the entire game again and it can be a little tiring if you wanna 100% the game. I haven't tried it yet but the workshop stuff looks pretty cool and the multiplayer could be fun to play with friends!Overall really nice game!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is  The mechanics are novel if a little under-explored, the writing got me to smirk despite mostly falling flat, and the audio-visual artistry is pleasant if unmemorable. The narrative does reveal itself to be a little conceited, but it only shows up right at the end and isn't apparent upon replaying specific sections. There's a part of me that wishes Superliminal was stronger in any one of its foundations, if only to make the short playtime a little more impactful. That said, the game ends when it runs out of ideas. That's a rare treat, and it highlights a level of restraint that most development teams don't have.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: After my first playthrough, I think this game is more similar to "The Stanley Parable" or "The Beginner's Guide" than "Portal", at least in its narrative structure. I was also reminded of the end of "Life is Strange" in some parts. The gameplay itself mostly consists of puzzles and exploration.The puzzles mainly use scale and perspective which works surprisingly well. An issue with those however are two or three puzzles being kind of cheap or too think-out-of-the-box-y. I believe these issues are caused by the player not being taught some mechanics needed here directly, e.g. . In total, the gameplay works very well though.Together with the gameplay, your surroundings tie in with the more "philosophical" aspects the narrator is talking about. Those however make more sense while playing, so they don't need spoiling.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The game was really fun and I loved how nothing quite made sense, but certain things were consistent just like dreams. The core mechanics were mind bending to use and I never did quite get used to them even after I "understood" how they worked. The music was perfect for the game and the visuals were well balanced.The mechanics are very well made and finely tuned, but I did notice issues that just kind of felt clunky if you were doing things on the move or trying to interact with things that were right next to your face. I really wish the rotate mechanic would allow for more than just rotation around the up/down axis.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This review is based solely on the main campaign (no challenge, multiplayer or workshop levels).I would give a "Mixed" review if I could. The core mechanic - perspective puzzles - is ingenious in theory, but in practice, the game fails ... well, at being a game. The puzzles are very shallow and straightforward, the hardest part being the search for the interactible object or finding out what you are even supposed to do. One may now argue that this "thinking outside the box" is exactly what the game is about, but that wouldn't make this aspect any more fun (at least for me). The core mechanic offers so much potential, but the game rarely taps into that. For perspective (haha), look at games like The Witness, Portal (1,2, even some mods) and The Talos Principle to see what one can with a small set of mechanics.Oh, and that for almost 1/3 of the playtime, the game turns into a pseudo-intellectual walking simulator, doesn't help it either.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this game is a cross between The Stanley Parable™ and a light version of LSD: Dream Emulator - and as you can probably expect, it’s . First though,  that you go into this game as blind as you can, with even the trailer spoiling quite a bit of the game, and is why this review will be short and to the point. I went into this game thinking that it was going to be an ordinary puzzle game with the quirk-of-the-year added for some flavour, but after just a short time playing I can safely say that it will start playing with your mind. The mechanics of this game are the most unique and innovative I’ve seen in a game in quite a long time, and while the story might not be on the same level as others such as Portal, it’s still pretty good. The only huge negative I would say is that it’s sadly rather short, coming in at around 2.5 hours for a blind first completion, although there are extra modes, lots of little secrets and achievements, as well as a workshop - all of which I really didn’t expect at all. I honestly wish more games had those things, as they’re becoming rarer and rarer these days. Overall, I would highly recommend the game, but not at the retail price of $22 CAD. There’s just too little game content to justify that. However the on sale price of $13 isn’t completely terrible. Dream well friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start off by saying that SUPERLIMINAL defied my expectations. I went in expecting something completely different. "Maybe it'll be like Stanley Parable", I thought. "Or maybe, it'll be a bit more like Portal, with these vibes."The game I experienced was unlike any game I've played before. Sure, it had puzzle elements of a game, like Portal; and sure, the initial narrative bits gave vibes not unlike Stanley Parable. But it would be  to compare the game to either, as it ultimately provided a unique, refreshing experience.I played this game, on stream, barely knowing what to expect, and came out the other side... feeling refreshed. At every corner, every puzzle, I found myself... . I found myself , yet my . I found myself giddy at almost every moment of the game.I also pulled almost every fire alarm.In all, my only regret coming out of this game is that... it ended.Thank you for the experience. Hopefully, we can dream together again soon.- Misu

_childDocuments_.review: I have always had a deep love for puzzle games, and came into this game with no expectations or understanding of game mechanics.  This game featured an absurdly calming/engaging soundtrack.  Each bit of the game felt expertly directed, and the vision of the creators is pretty stunning.  There is humorous narration and monologues throughout the game, and I felt this wasn't just a video game they created.  This was a work of genuine love and ingenuity.  My only complaint is that after beating this game I am left in a sense of sadness.  This game is one-of-a-kind and relatively short, so it pains me in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly a subversion of expectations, in a great way. It plays along the lines of Stanley's Parable and the Portal series. Using liminal spaces, ambience to set the mood to a great extent, and tricky puzzles; you get a heck of a concept.However, while this game does focus on liminal spaces being a foundation of the tech that is used on the PC, it kind of limits the capabilities of what you could put into the game. I felt like there were a lot of options to add more abstract dream set pieces than there actually was in the game. The mechanics are sound, if not a bit janky at times, but I've thoroughly enjoyed this title. I hope to see more from the devs behind this ambitious concept. Maybe a sequel? Who knows. Though for the play time, twenty dollars seems like a lot, but you get a decent quality game with interesting mechanics, a decent enough story to hold it together, and a solid message. (Despite how tropey it is)
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal feels very Portal-esque, and that's a good thing! It has the same kind of subtle humor and fun level design that really takes off once you get to the "behind the scenes" levels. Superliminal encourages outside-the-box thinking, and once you realize what some of the hidden items look like, you'll want to replay it to find them all.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This game blends together elements of puzzle solving and walking simulation. There is a clear influence from, besides the WS genre in general, particularly from  Parable, two particular important puzzle games, which are  and  . Specifically, the organicity and fluidity of puzzle solving from the first and the awareness of the relevance of level design from the second. Unfortunately, all this lead to an underwhelming ending, which I will comment upon later. That all said (which, by the way, are compliments), we can go on to the venomous part.The apple-fan puzzle was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. There is even a “secret” room in which there is even a commentary about the expectations of players regarding secret rooms no being fulfilled, so they are pretty much aware of what they are doing for most of the time. There is no excuse, however, for that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ apple-fan puzzle. The fan is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ red-herring. Actually, you could call it a prop since it is . Unless the intention is to deliberately mock players and make them waste their time (which is something minor creators aim to do), I don’t see the point of putting the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fan there. So, if the developers ever read this: go ♥♥♥♥ yourselves for that one. I had to look up the solution for this one.The other thing is the ending, which was disappointing for me but not as near as enraging as the previously mentioned puzzle. I went through the commentary that explains why they chose to go with an ending like that and I understand what they were aiming for. Nonetheless, it felt underwhelming because I felt I was watching a Disney movie or a bank commercial. You can convey a meaning that , but you don’t need to do that in a Disney-ish or marketing-ish way. But just so you don’t say that I only cursed: the ending fits perfectly the breaking of expectation that was created from the beginning and was kept on throughout. I mentioned The Stanley Parable because I felt the game was being led by a satirical tone. But our expectations are broken since there is a movement from the satirical comic into the more purely comical – comical here in the sense of salvation. And that is something that is neither easy nor currently fashionable, so they deserve some credit for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. Cheaper than therapy and probably more helpful. If you thought Antechamber was too hard but loved the style, this is mind bending enough to scratch the itch while delivering a "Stanley Parable" like experience.I found a few ways to break the game, notably not the way the game *wanted* me to break it, whoops but over all a wonderful few hours of play.If you're a puzzle fan, get it.

_childDocuments_.review: - DIFFICULTY -🔲 Not difficulty based🔲 Easy☑️ Normal🔲 Hard🔲 Insanity- GRAPHICS -🔲 Pixels🔲 Bad🔲 Graphics don't matter in this game☑️ Good🔲 Beautiful🔲 Masterpiece- MUSIC -🔲 Bad☑️ Music🔲 Good🔲 Beautiful- STORY -🔲 This game has no story☑️ Very mind numbing🔲 Available if people want it🔲 Well written🔲 Epic story- PRICE -🔲 N/A🔲 Underpriced🔲 Perfect price☑️ Could be cheaper🔲 Overpriced🔲 Stupidly priced- REQUIREMENTS -🔲 You can run it on a calculator☑️ Mid Spec🔲 High end🔲 Top of the Range- LENGTH -🔲 Very short (0 - 3 hours)☑️ Short (3 - 15 hours)🔲 Average (15 - 50 hours)🔲 Long (50 - 90 hours)🔲 Extremely long (90 - 110 hours)🔲 Continuous- FUN -🔲 Dead🔲 Hard to enjoy🔲 Repetitive☑️ Actually pretty amusing🔲 Ride of your life- REPLAYABILITY -🔲 None☑️ Only for achievements🔲 If you wait a few months🔲 Definitely🔲 Infinitely replayable- WORTH BUYING -🔲 No☑️ Wait for sale🔲 Yes🔲 Free⏰ How long to beat Superliminal:- Main Story - 2½ Hours- Main + Extras - 3½ Hours- Completionist - 9½ Hours⭕ - Conclusion -:Superliminal is an awesome perspective based game which requires you to think outside the box to complete the different challenges and rooms it presents to you. The game is weird and wacky and an awesome first playthrough however it lacks replayability due to the nature of the game. The achievements were fun but some were extremely long and pointless which was a shame. The challenge mode for this game was a great addition giving people an extra bit of fun to conclude the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, great game.I highly appreciate and respect small studios that create amazing games with a smaller crews.I believe 10 people in total that had a main part in making this game work.Negative reviews come in saying its short and that they do not create the hardest puzzles and mix all of the mechanics, but is that not the point of this game??? It has a narrative that would be completely drowned out if that's what they did. I'm glad it's short and does not create near impossible puzzles, all they want you to do is to think outside the box... that's it.Do Challenge mode (same thing but limited grabs and jumps), play with the developer commentary, speed run it (developers encourage it), WORKSHOP maps are coming out soon to help appease the people that want only the mechanic (Which people happily praise when they wrongly write a negative review because people thought that's the game's only purpose.)I think what they did with the game is perfect and well worth playing and supporting teams like this.The only thing i can complain about, is that the music can stand out when finding the hidden collectibles/finding bugs in a certain area for a while. There are a quite a bit of bugs/glitches if you mess around too much, but i believe I only fell through the map once on my first play through it was more funny than annoying as checkpoints are everywhere. (I spent about an hour looking for glitches, it was quite enjoyable getting launched through a barrier and landing where your not supposed to be.)I'm a little disappointed with how many negative reviews there are. I believe the developers have done as much as they can do with this steam release, especially with the workshop maps, I cant wait to see the creative mixing of mechanics and tough puzzles being made in the future.This is definitely and always will be a positive review from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: (Edited as I paid closer to 30 dollars CAD for this, not 20 as stated before)This game was okay. Long review ahead. There are definitely some cool innovative mechanics, which at first I enjoyed immensely, but after being reused over and over, I don't know. I just expected there to be more, I guess? We get to change perspectives, we get to duplicate things. That's uh.. about it. Not a very long list of "innovation".  The puzzles were just okay. A bit bland and repetitive, and towards the mid-game point, the game just stops showing you how to solve any of the puzzles. Not a hint, not a "hey I just used X skill, l can try it on Y puzzle now" thought to be heard. I got stuck dozens of times only for the solution to be to drag the one thing I didn't try to already, or to place something just a hair to the right or left for it to register. Other than the puzzles, this is just a walking simulator. You can't even sprint! Or crouch.I don't understand why people are saying it's got such a deep message or meaning, when it's your run-of-the-mill "You Are Not Defined By Your Thoughts And Therefore You Are Free Of Limits". There was no story. Nothing to the protag, no explanation as to why you even want to be there, how the facility works, etc etc. I wanted /lore/. I wanted a /story/. That's what I paid 30 bucks for, and I got Portal but with only 7 or 8 levels and sparse voice acting acting as the "story".I know it's an indie game, and I will cut it a little slack for that. The soundtrack was quite nice. TLDR: it isn't bad, but it's not great. Ok if you just want a couple neat puzzles. Total disappointment if you're looking for a story rich indie game. I'd have paid 9 or 10 dollars for that, maybe. I feel ripped off based off the trailer.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool puzzle game akin to Portal and similar, but instead of regular puzzles you play with perspective and how it affects the objects around you. It's very clever and original, fun to play, later levels can get a bit challenging but it's never annoying or hard, just needs a new perspective hehe. You also get the narrative in the form of radios you find along the way. Overall a must for people who like these kind of games or who like to try out something new
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is boring, the game is too long, I did not understand the story.If we compare it with another game in the puzzle genre - The Witness, then the second one is many times better in all aspects.Superliminal comes out as a good tech-demo of the possibilities of the game with perspective and non-Euclidean geometry. _childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "meh" option - this game certainly isn't bad per-say, but the trailers made it a lot more exciting than it actually is. I love puzzle games like these, but I found Superliminal suffers from one "beating a dead horse" mechanic - pick up an object and based on where you release it the object becomes smaller or larger. Rinse and repeat and mix in some very mild, uninteresting platforming to solve every single puzzle in the game. If there were more varied and interesting mechanics to explore other than increasing and decreasing object size, and if there was added complexity as you progress throughout the game, this would be a very solid addition to the genre, but as is I felt underwhelmed by the experience. I took my time with the game and even then it barely lasted me 1.5 hours, and the story was pretty much non-existent. Some of the story feels a bit derivative of Portal, with a snarky robotic voice chiming in with mildly humorous commentary from time to time, but it pales in comparison to the clever writing and engaging plot of Portal. All in all, if you're an absolute hardcore fan of first-person puzzle games, this is worth a try, otherwise I'd recommend skipping this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: i cant tell you how much i loved this game. there isn't a word in the english dictionary to express how great this game was. thank you. the ending was tear jerking. one little feed back though please add a level selection menu so i can try specific levels without having to run the whole game after i beat it once

_childDocuments_.review: I love the way Superliminal just casual messes with your head the entire time. It constantly is making you discover a new way of looking at things. My one complaint is that its short. I beat the main story in 1 hr and 30 min. In that time though it does not disappoint. The mechanic, puzzles, and level design are really what make this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a 3D puzzler, clearly inspired by The Stanley Parable, Portal, and a bit of Antichamber, but with its own unique mechanic: changing the physical size of objects to match their apparent size in your field of vision. Despite this, the game falls a bit short in my opinion, lasting only a couple hours and not providing much beyond what you might expect from the very beginning. You are immediately introduced to the core mechanic, but that's about it as the game struggles to find much of anything interesting to do with it, aside from a few briefly interesting things here and there related to spacial geometry. The resulting puzzles were mildly interesting and quite easy. The ending Overall, the game tried too hard to fill the shoes of the classics in the genre, never digging deep enough into any of its mechanics to really get anywhere with them. Worth a shot on sale, but barely worth the price for what you get.
