_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun, short but sweet puzzle game whose gimmik is being screwy with the reality of the dream environments you're in. Superliminal's main story is structured like Portal, whereby you progress through puzzle chambers while receiving exposition from wacky characters and your situation becomes increasingly dire.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game from start to end. I especially loved how the visuals and illusions change as you progress through the game.. and the ending was well worth it :) I feel like Subliminal took inspiration from Portal, the stanley parable, Truman show, and some Alice in Wonderland. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game changed me as a person, just a tiny bit.  It starts out with a Portal like level of mechanical innovation, mixed with Stanley Parable backrooms exploration, but it finds it's own distinctive voice.  As a person who does have lucid dreams, and does sometimes get stuck in them, this game was able to evoke a very specific niche of discomfort that no other game has. It starts out with simple object perspective tricks and escalates the concept until perspective is the only thing that exists.   The puzzle and atmosphere design is very tight and high quality, but in terms of £ per hour this is one you want to buy on sale. I got badly stuck a couple of times and woke up in just under four hours.  I'm sure I'll play through again with commentary, and try the challenges and workshops, but there's otherwise no reason to replay the main story except achievement hunting - the puzzles are so memorable you won't ever forget how to solve them.No matter how stuck you get, don't look it up, keep trying to find the perspective you are missing.  It feels extremely fair and rewarding when you do.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The central mechanic of perception being reality is interesting, and it's novel and fun to play around with for like 30 minutes but for me it got old pretty fast, and the game doesn't seem to do much with it. The puzzles never evolve beyond the first few puzzles, and they are not challenging because the solution becomes obvious once you can see all the pieces and you know where the next door you need to go through is. A lot of the time it felt a lot more like a walking simulator than an actual game.Environments look nice if a bit plain, music is alright, general atmosphere is solid.I'm not sure what the story was trying to do but it didn't really click for me, and whatever deep and philosophical point it was making was either not actually that deep or philosophical, or was so deep and philosophical that it went straight over my head.Overall, I think Superliminal is not as clever as it seems to think it is, and for me it was boring and underwhelming, and spent a little to much time talking without really saying anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: What an one of a kind experience. Games like these remind me why video-games are such an important art form. The puzzles aren't exactly brain busting, (a few can be) but they encourage outside of the box thinking in wacky fun ways that feel great throughout the game. Even if you're not a fan of puzzle games, "Superliminal" manages to deliver through with it's intuitive mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly really mixed on this game. The puzzles are fun, but those puzzles and the atmosphere the game builds during the first hour quickly goes out the door halfway through, essentially becoming a walking sim with no semblance of the game you were just playing. Did the level designers get lazy, become unimaginative, or give up? It honestly feels that way, and that sucks given the fun concept of the game. Problem is. all the puzzle-solving techniques you start to pick up early on just... disappear? The game is described as "using the ambiguity of depth and perspective", and that quickly stops being the case and more of a fun trinket when the game starts bashing you again and again with metaphors and more time spent walking than doing anything else.At a base price of $20 (for 3 hours of gameplay), it's hard to justify recommending given the actual fun puzzle solving stops barely an hour and a half in. There are other modes, but the overall replayability still feels scarce - once you know how to solve the puzzles, the only thing left to do is speedrun (and the game even acknowledges this with achievements) because there are no alternate methods allowed to solve the puzzles. If this is on sale for 50% off or more, sure, it could be worth the buy, but otherwise I feel like I'm wasting my money.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that could change your perspective on life. Finished this game twice - once with dev commentary turned on, just to find out how they could even come up with this.Kinda short but well worth the runtime. Excellent use of props, lighting, environment storytelling.If you love portal, this masterpiece could be something right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a game to make you question everything. It's like some people when they see The Truman Show or The Phantom of the Open or Inception, or something like that. It makes you question why you do what you do. Where you could've gone. Where you should've gone. What have you missed? Where did you find something you shouldn't have? How can I change to be more efficient? Am I at my peak? It makes you question everything. While the multiplayer is dead, and the Workshop is slowly dying, you can't help but love the story it tells. Remember.Wake.Up.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool puzzle game that will mess with your head but in a fun way. It all revolves around perception, and challenges you to think outside the box in a way that no other puzzle game I've played has managed to do. The puzzles aren't particularly hard but they do feel clever. What it does well is that it never really manages to be frustrating. Well there was one part I found frustrating but compared to other puzzles games I've played before thats still quite good. As a result is has quite a chilled out laid back feel, especially with the nice relaxing piano music in the background.It also has a sense of humour that reminded me a lot of the Stanley Parable, where it's quite quirky but fun. It's not a very long game but it does offer a challenge mode if you fancy trying to solve the puzzles with limits set in. I would recommend it especially as it's a puzzle game that offers something a bit unique compared to other puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally finished the game after falling asleep many times. I got to the part where they put an alarm clock puzzle that keeps playing the alarm clock (hence how I was finally able to finish the game).Subjecting a player to a beeping alarm clock dozens of times was really bad game design, and the designers should feel bad. (it's a requirement of the game's level progression, to hear the alarm over and over).Another example... why does this game have a big ugly white crosshair that you can't turn off?! Why? And overall, the gameplay was too limiting. The maps are aesthetically too crowded (with bland objects) to keep track of what the game wants you to do, and I found it too tedious always having to play the game its way, barring you off from things that most games would let you explore. It ignores or disallows many more interesting things it could have done.A lot of missed opportunities. It wants to be Portal and/or The Stanley Parable so bad, it couldn't decide what voiceover to use, but there is zero writing quality in this game.I was going to change this review to positive on one part (where every time you click on the door it spawns a clone) but even that stopped once I got an achievement. Lame. It just takes a fun gimmick-like mechanic and beats it to death or stifles it or marinates it with generic unity assets, or fails to overcome the bugs of its implementation.There are some cool parts to this game, but it's not worth the price. If the price was less, and it didn't have all the stupid repeats of the same idea (with various bugs), I would be more interested in sharing its praise.More like Super Lame In All. This thing makes me cringe long after finishing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fascinating and innovative puzzle game that uses optical illusions and different perspectives to confuse and challenge players. It requires creativity and a good spatial sense to avoid getting stuck. The controls are kept emphatically simple, which is exactly how it should be with a game like this, the graphics and soundtrack have also been done very well here.Just let friends who are visiting play this game, I can tell you, it's almost as much fun! I had 2 musicians in the studio for a recording session, after the session we had some drinks and pizza and I let one of the guitarists play Superliminal because I told them about the game Pools beforehand. We had an unforgettable evening and laughed a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a game about mind bending puzzles, some perspective shenanigans, and a touch of narrative. Now this is probably going to be a hot take and a half, but I think superliminal makes a better lets play than a game. Shameless full breakdown here -> The game is beautiful, wonderfully polished, trippy, and very very unique. But for a puzzle game to be truly amazing in my eyes, it needs to make puzzles. Puzzles that build upon their existing mechanics and layer upon them to create amalgamations that the player never considered possible. We didn't quite get there. But, everything else we got was beautifully done and it looked beautiful.Some will complain that the game is short, but I would certainly prefer a perfect hour over one hour of content dragged across two. I think the game could use a few more hard cuts, but overall I think they made the right choice with how short it was.For gamers who are newer to indie games and experimental games this is almost certainly going to be a perfect 10 that sticks with them forever; but for older gamers who have experienced the past greats it will likely be good at best. I wish I could give neutral on this one. I think it's worth a play, so a positive review it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+Cool and calming soundrack+Fairly optimized+Inspiring story messageCons:-Gameplay mechanics are extremely simple-Frustrating gameplay loop-Much more of a walking sim than puzzlerThis was a weird one.  Shortly into the game I got very annoyed by the stereotypical indie motif of randomness where nothing makes sense.  Though it does fit the overall narrative of the player being in a dream.  To be honest, this one fell pretty flat for me.  Superliminal had my eye since it was announced and it looked very promising.  However the gameplay mechanics - while unique - just got pretty boring after a while.  The game has quite aggressive "what the hell is going on?" pacing and I found myself just wanting it to be over.  Lucky for me - it's an incredibly short game so the end was not far off.  On a positive note, the music is pretty relaxing and the overall messaging of the game's story is solid.  The explicit narration has a clear point that it wants to make and it delivers on that point.Overall, this felt more like a walking sim with minor puzzle mechanics than a puzzle game. Regardless of my opinion, $20 for 2.5 hours of gameplay is pretty far from justified unless one is feeling charitable towards smaller dev studios - which I respect.  This is a cool game for a certain audience.  Not worth $20 though.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty mesmerizing, but not really a puzzle game.I will preface this that I bought the game after seeing promotional demo clips years ago. The one of the objects changing in size and the objects that are painted on the wall that materialize if you stand in the right spot, what exciting concepts! I wondered what else they’d develop to enhance the dream like experience? The answer is: nothing. Not really.You’re almost immediately presented with these concepts, which you use to solve simple puzzle games, usually enlarging an object to reach a door that’s higher up. Which is… fine.After the initial stint of “training” in a “dream environment” things go awry and the game tries to give off eerie horror vibes. The story is that something has gone wrong in the dream facility and now the dreams are out of control. The game at this point is not really about puzzles anymore, but about navigating thru the room, finding your way in the dark.Later on puzzle elements are reintroduced, and occasionally pretty original (I especially liked the warp doors that make you grow or shrink, which you use to escape a small box), but ultimately the puzzles are nothing more than speed bumps to navigate the WACKY DREAM world. Oh no! I fell! Oh no! I’m now walking on walls. That doesn’t happen normally!I feel as if this game tries to be Portal a little bit , maybe combined with some Antichamber and a little bit of Stanley’s Parable sprinkled on top. I feel storywise the buildup isn’t as good as in Portal. In this game things pretty much immediately go wrong, and you don’t feel any sort of despair or worry. It is what it is. This due to lack of buildup. Antichamber is an amazing puzzle game, hard to navigate, following its own rules. Thing is, once you know the rules, you can navigate Antichamber fine. Superliminal has very limited interaction with objects (understandable, as they could be puzzle breaking), but sometimes you are reintroduced to interactable objects, and you can’t grab them anymore. They serve a decorative purpose. It’s pretty jarring. Also the fact that you can’t walk or grab thru open spaces  in enlargable objects is kind of jarring. I guess it has to do with how the models are made.Generally, puzzle games, even abstract ones, give you a premise and rules on how to do problem solving. Oftentimes however, especially towards the end of the game, I found myself in a room with a bunch of stuff I couldn’t interact with, clicking around looking for the one interactable object or the wall that turns out to be fake. On occasion the sudden shift in scenery would be pretty impressive, and there were some original objects to be found. But it gets a little bit old rather quickly, especially when there’s no real puzzle left, just weird scenes.Another thing that was a slight disappointment: the game doesn’t really reward you for exploring. In the beginning of the game I figured out I could climb up on a structure in stead of just going thru the door and found a (secret?) blue pawn, which disappeared. Satisfied, I assumed these would be scattered in the game, like secret objectives. However, later on, I tried to scale a wall using a giant chess piece, and as I finally managed to climb it a bit a grid appeared above my head. This is the developer saying “nope”. Again, this is fine, but it’s just one example of how I felt it a bit railroady and without much buildup. Sometimes there are very big spaces to explore, and if you manage to go “off grid” it’s more of a punishment than a reward because of the big empty space. The game seems to expect you to go from door to door at some point. Which is a bit in contrast from thinking outside the box. Also, it should be noted that it is quite a short game. I finished it in under five hours.Superliminal reminded me a little bit of a game called The Beginner’s Guide. Which is just weird environment after weird environment, with more variation in scenery but less interaction than in this game. Unlike that game however, I did feel content about this game when it wrapped up.Regardless of my critiques, I would still recommend this game if you mostly want a mesmerizing experience. I myself do like experiencing Kafkaesque vibes, this game is fun to submerge yourself in. Just don’t expect to do too much rational thinking. I do not regret my buy, especially given the launch price. Thanks devs!update: I decided to change to "not recommended", because I think people will generally be disappointed if they expect a puzzler.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend once had a dream that he picked up distant cars between his fingers, put them in a sandwich, and ate them. OK, he didn't actually dream that - he hallucinated it while tripping balls, but shh. I bring that up because that (the picking up cars and eating them, not the tripping balls part) is the main mechanic in Superliminal, a dream-logic first person puzzler that takes place in the wholly mundane corners of dreamland. You pick up things and through tricks of perspective you reduce their size or embiggen* them, usually to build stepping stones to get somewhere else. It's a satisfying (if somewhat fiddly) trick, and technically impressive. Unfortunately, there's not a whole lot else going on for way too long, and the game suffers for it; about three fourths of the game feel like a chore. The levels compensate for it by throwing some extra mechanics like cloning objects or lining up visual elements, adding some humour, and by setting up clever visual illusions, but after a while repetition sets in again and things start feeling like a trudge again. The plot fails to provide a hook to pull the player in: You're in some sort of dream clinic, things have gone pear-shaped, and you're lost in a bunch of really unimaginative dream worlds. There's also a passive-agressive, contrarian, monotone-female-voiced AI talking constantly down at you because well, I guess this is a first person puzzle game and that comes with the territory. The ending is cute but honestly, it's kind of undermined by everything that went on before; It works as long as you don't think too hard about it, I guess. Like the great Japanese movie Afterlife, where the... uh, afterlife is managed by exhausted menial workers in what looks like some sort of  public institution building, or Inception, where dreams include such exotic and imaginative settings as a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Bond ripoff scene, Superliminal takes its fantastic premise and makes it look utterly mundane. There are so many vaguely institutional corridors; You get a few nicer hallways and rooms, but everything remains resolutely banal for, again, way too long. I'm sure it kept costs down in a small indie game, and it is kinda justified by the script, but it really doesn't help maintain interest when so many of the other elements fail to do the same. Luckily, things perk up noticeably towards the end. In the last couple of levels, the music and the pace picks up and -finally- the game starts actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with your expectations. It sets traps, does all sorts of fun, unexpected things, and really delivers (conceptually, if not visually) on the game's promise. That, combined with the fact that it isn't a long game, make this a fairly firm recommendation as long as you're willing to muddle through some of the less than stellar bits. My enjoyment of the game also immediately went up when I stopped looking for collectibles, so if things start going slow for you that may help as well - just play to finish, and if you like it enough you can always go through the levels again with a fine-toothed comb.*: Eh, it's a perfectly cromulent word.

_childDocuments_.review: Labelling Superliminal in a few words is a challenge because it’s not entirely a puzzle game and not wholly a guided exploration game. Both elements flow between one another without much fanfare or notification, the only signifier being a loading screen when transitioning from one chapter to the next. Despite how organic the games’ progression is, its own story partially betrays the gameplay resolved only by its ending.Don’t let the concept of dreamscape puzzle-solving intimidate you as the marketing implies, as the overall gimmick here is playing with perspectives and cheating the rules of (meta/physical) space. How you interact/look at objects, including their distance or proximity, are your bread and butter here*. The puzzles are relatively easy enough to figure out with enough experimentation, as there’s nothing dextrously complicated like particular timing or setting off multiple flags/triggers in a row. Superliminal doesn’t stay on one mechanic for long, as it’ll introduce a new puzzle type for a few rooms then move onto the next. Encountering new things happens at a steady rate which is impressive for a game that takes around two hours or so to complete, leaving no time for needless fluff or filler.The story is ultimately moot as your role is that of a faceless, voiceless player character visiting the Pierce Institute to participate in patent-pending dream therapy. This premise is fine, but Superliminal’s campaign does little to expand on this and disconnects the gameplay. From voice-overs advising that you’re off the intended path or not following the treatment course correctly, for what’s primarily a linear experience, the tone feels needlessly snarky for what ultimately isn’t your fault. So infrequently is there anything resembling a therapeutic experience, and it ends up feeling like you’re a test subject instead of a patient. There are multiple instances of being faked out that you’ll wake up so that things reset or get back on track, but just as quickly do things continue to go off the rails for the sake of new puzzles.They’re effective fakeouts by way of sudden cuts or misdirection; I’ll give Superliminal credit for that. It’s also quite funny when perhaps not intended: Placing a tangible object down only to find it’s become intangible and smeared onto the wall and floor, using a bouncy castle to change your size or even causing a catastrophic paradox by accident. The puzzles frequently made me have strong reactions through surprise or laughter upon realizing the concept or solving them, even if they’re ones I got stumped by. The direction and programming of Superliminal are fantastic that way, and even if these ‘dreams’ feel imposed and transposed, I was eager to chug along to the next puzzle or downright cinematic setpiece.… That is until chapter four, Blackout. For those with nyctophobia like myself, this chapter is less a test of puzzle-solving skills but keeping one’s nerves intact while traversing mainly in the dark. It’s also the weakest stretch of puzzles by far, relying on using little light and purposely surrounding yourself with darkness to proceed. It’s a profoundly unpleasant part of the game that, to its credit, has no instances of inappropriate jumpscares and even uses perspective for a couple of gags. That’s the only real blemish on the campaign, as the chapters preceding and following Blackout are far more enjoyable and make better use of the games’ warm lighting and soft colour palettes.Most of my criticisms about the story get wrapped by a nice little bow upon reaching the incredibly touching (and I’ll dare say emotional) final chapter and ending. Still, I just wish these dreams were more… Dreamy. There’s no getting around that the puzzles, rooms and so on are imposed by the Pierce Institute’s therapy, but it always ended up feeling like the treatment itself was breaking at the seams and not the dreams themselves. The ending implies this was intended, though that comes across as a cop-out.I can think of many games that better provide a puzzle experience or a guided exploration experience. However, I can’t think of many that come close to riding that middle ground as nicely as Superliminal does. Up until its finale does the story disconnect me from the gameplay, but that’s ultimately my biggest gripe outside of the fourth chapter being beans. Nevertheless, strong puzzles surrounded by well-realized and well-executed premises and programming make Superliminal an easy recommendation.*Discussing the puzzles in great detail would be spoilers, of course, and I do think they’re worth experiencing with little to no context going in.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Would limbo again!In all seriousness, this game is a masterpiece of innovative first person puzzling. The pacing is excellent. The challenges are just the right balance of difficult and intuitive, once you fully grasp what the game mechanics are. Speed running it after a couple play-throughs is also a challenge in and of itself.The level design progresses from familiar spaces, akin to Portal test rooms, into back maintenance passages, all the way to the surreal and otherworldly. The movement mechanic could be a little smoother, but this is not a con as it is pretty damn good.If I were to give this game any negative mark, it would be one of personal greed in that the main content is too short. I was able to finish the story in around 2 hours (your mileage may vary), but I immediately jumped back in to start exploring all the things I missed. The achievements in this game offer a great incentive to jump back in and really start studying all the walls of each level and look for hidden passageways in the darkness.All in all, if you are into games like Portal or The Room, add this to your collection!

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is an incredibly well made puzzle game a la Portal and The Stanley Parable. It has great design, pacing, graphics, and is more clever than you expect. _childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing experience. I genuinely have to wonder how you can craft something like this.For those wondering, the premise of the game is that you are . It feels very similar to the Stanley Parable in particular, but not at all the same. The perspective tricks are only the start of it- very nearly every weird dream thing you can think of comes up at least once, often more.With a little help I was able to finish the game in three hours, but I didn't grab most of the secrets (and I'm okay with that for the moment).The writing, storytelling, environments, puzzles, audio... this game is really a masterpiece.Fair warning - while there is a (slightly too fast) warning at the start, this game has flashing lights and repeating patterns (particularly near the end) and a huge dose of unreality. While not a horror game, there are a few legitimately worrying moments, and I think it's worth mentioning that a lot of what the game does is designed to cause unease, at least in me. Also, there's a lot of sudden shifts and lots of unexpected falling, particularly the farther you get along. There's also (mild spoiler but important) a repeated failure to wake up that might be very unsettling to people.That said, it's a great game and truly worth trying out.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: [SPOILERS AHEAD]The gameplay was super fun: much like Portal, the entire game just explores one mechanic, but it's a very unique mechanic and was well-executed overall.But compared to Portal, this game felt too short, and the ending wasn't as great (I'm oversimplifying a little, but the message at the end was basically just "you can solve all your problems by finding a new perspective", which is a nice thought but also feels both patronizing and overly simplistic).But overall I'm glad to have had this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Went into it expecting a perspective based puzzle game, with very little other expectations other than solid reviews, and I was pleasantly surprised. Started out feeling like a portal game. Then I got going, and was like "woah, this is non-euclidean AF..." which made it feel more and more like Stanley Parable. Game starts to get a bit trippy at times. VERY mind-bendy. One section was actually really spooky, so might not be the best one before bed, especially if you have bad dreams (the game is literally based on dreams within a dream with altered perspectives). Was pretty short, and I'm sure there are some easter eggs and other stuff to check out, but it was still a great experience for what was there. Beat the game in less than 3 hours (although I tend to blow through most puzzle games). Even had a really positive message at the end which was great. Even though this was a solid experience, still probably wanna wait for a sale for this one. Neat game!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes all you need is a change in perspective.The entire game can be summed up in the line above. Superliminal is a fairly unique puzzle/narrative game which feels like a love child between Portal and the Stanley Parable. A wonderful bite sized game that is a treat for the brain. Perhaps the narrative is not the most engaging but the ways in which this game plays with space, optical illusions and how we perceive them are quite unique. It's worth playing just to see what the game does in order to visually confuse and trick the player.A fun brain teaser that's not too hard and makes me happy about the concepts that can be explored in the medium of video games. A good time all around.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 You did pretty good son!I wont really touch on what made this a good game, because it literally is all in the trailers and screenshots. And while I wont spoil anything for you, it becomes a bit of a generic motivational speech with a major lack of puzzles; in contrast with the rest of the game which was puzzle-heavy and was much more comedic/lighthearted.I personally wish I had bought this while it was on sale, because even $20 is a bit much for the amount of content, in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: Portal meet antichamber meets the stanley parable.It starts extremely strong, has a much longer than expected middle part, and a fantastic ending.Add to this top notch soundtrack and voice acting, a level editor (!) , several speedrun modes, and a full on developer commentary, this is one not to miss.I'm personally a huge walking simulator fan and I was a bit disappointed than only the last quarter of the game contains exposition. I would have preferred a more story-heavy beginning, but the game does such a good job at throwing optical illusion after optical illusion at you, it's forgivable.Which reminds me - the game is much longer than expected - in 8 hours I didn't see everything and I have yet to try the various unlocked mode. I recommend playing it it short burst, otherwise you might rush it and miss out on some of the fantastic details the devs left in there.Considering it's their first release, it's quite incredible to see they optimized such a visually complex game to run at 170 fps on an RTX 2080 on ultra at 5x x 1440. Kudos for the extra effort that went into the optimization here.A definite 'buy' for anyone who liked 'Portal', 'antichamber' or 'the stanley parable'.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is an experience/puzzle game a bit like the stanley parable.This is one of those games you probably best go in blind with as few expectations as possible. While the puzzle gimmick prominently displayed in the trailers is a large part of the game, I would actually say it isn't the biggest focus. The game prides itself on surprising and subverting your expectations, and it does this pretty well. Your eyes will play tricks on you.One criticism I do have though, is that there are not quite enough puzzles in a playthrough. It took me about 3 hours to beat the game once (I then beat it again under an hour to listen to the developer commentary). And in those 3 hours I spent maybe half solving puzzles, and the other half experience the sights and tricks of the game. Most of the puzzles I did not find that challenging, and while many are very clever, it does feel light for a puzzle game. Portal to me is an excellent example of a puzzle game of introducing a mechanic and then slowly escalating the applications of it. Here, it feels like they introduce a mechanic or gimmick and then are kind of done with it after a puzzle or two, instead of really delving into it.So as a pure puzzle game it is ok, but that is where all the surrounding stuff comes in to make it well worthwhile. Again, experience it yourself, but if you must have more of a hint Bottomline is that the game is a trip to experience, and while it isn't the most challenging puzzle game, there is enough other stuff to make it worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Would you like to spend a couple hours in a haunted IKEA while on acid?  Hey, who wouldn't!Superliminal is a little over three hours of mind-bending puzzles, somewhat akin to what you might get if you mixed The Stanley Parable together with Portal and salted it liberally with AntiChamber.  It's totally chill, often funny, are very rarely terribly frustrating.  I'll admit to having to cheat twice:  one I feel totally justified in, and another made me feel pretty silly when I discovered what the solution was.  There's one more puzzle that I somehow brute-forced through that I *still* don't understand.  It turns out, some of the puzzles have solutions that just amount to brute-forcing, though.  There are times when, after you've walked far enough and given up, you will find that the world has been swapped out behind you. Don't forget to look up, down, and backwards!The graphics are super-tidy and have that too-clean aesthetic that skates on the edge of the uncanny valley.  It looks good, but nothing looks real.  The simple aesthetic seems to result in good performance.  Controls are simple walking-simulator style and work well when they're supposed to.  The physics engine is set suuuper sloppy, which is good; it makes a number of puzzles forgiving when a more strict engine would cause unending frustration. There's a bouncy castle in the game, and I'm deeply disappointed that I couldn't jump on it. If these were star-ratings, I'd knock off a half-a-star just for that unforgivable crime. The music, is excellent. Sure, it's inoffensive hotel lobby muzak for the most part, but it is well produced and is well fitted to the game, especially in the later sections.There's little voice work -- mostly provided by computer text-to-speech -- and no characters, so there's nothing to be said about that.  The story is fun: you're basically stuck in a dream and you're trying to break out. There's a kindly doctor -- the only real voice -- who is trying to help you through a selection of dreams, including one that gets a little nightmarish.I recommend picking this up. It is probably fully worth its $20 asking price, but I picked it up for $13 during a sale.  I'll probably be picking up the soundtrack, though... Anyway, having just finished the game, there's still some work to be done! I'm looking forward to a second playthrough with the developer commentary, and attempting to find more of the many easter eggs hidden around the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a game I want to recommend but really can't in good conscience. It's got some decent humor, a quite interesting mechanical premise (picked up objects that remain the same apparent size when picked up but grow or shrink to match the size at the furthest possible position they could be in), and a couple of decent puzzles. Unfortunately, there just aren't enough good puzzles that really explore the mechanics the way a game like Baba is You or Recursed does, nor does it really do anything with the philosophical themes it vaguely gestures towards. It's too short (clocking in around 4 hours for me, half of which was spent poking around at the edges of the maps to see if there would be any interesting easter eggs off the obvious path, which there weren't), and compensates for the lack of many substantial puzzles with uncommunicativeness in a few places, and clever but basically non-interactive perceptual tricks that feel like they're more chances for the devs to try and impress you with how clever they are than give you the chance to actually be clever yourself. It's also got a fair amount programming jankiness, only some of which is forgivable by the bizarre things they were making the physics engine do. On several occasions I ended up falling through the level or rendering it unsolvable, and when I used to "reset from checkpoint" feature, it had 50/50 odds of borking the graphics and leaving bits of the screen from before the reset overlaid so I can't see anything. Overall, it feels like a somewhat overproduced demo for a bigger game that actually develops on its ideas. As an interesting thing for students of game design, it might be worth getting at a discount, but as a functional game to play, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would prefer to give this one a sideways thumb, because it's not exactly bad, but really 'meh'. The basic mechanic the entire game revolves around is novel and fairly fun, but it's not enough to carry the entire game, especially since there are rather few actual puzzle moments. Later in the game most time is spent on running through corridors and/or trying to figure out where to go, which in some cases also felt quite cheap to me. Also, beside the resizing mechanic, everything else is not just reminiscent of many (much better) games like Portal (of course), the Stanley Parable and NaissancE, but feels extremely derivative. Especially the narrators (the compulsory AI commenting on your performance and a doctor spouting pseudo-psychoanalytic drivel) are really stale and uninspired at this point. And finally, the game is way too short to justify the full price at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I played it.  I finished it.  2 hours.Loved it.  Some of the puzzles are just stackabox type puzzles, but after a few to teach you how to manipulate objects with perspective, they get... weird.About 75% of the way through the game, I got moderately stuck on a puzzle.  Ran around in circles, looked around trying to figure out what I could interact with, then just stopped.  I thought to myself "okay, what here isn't what it seems to be?" and that was the answer.  That's the answer a lot of the time.  You saw something, made an assumption, turns out what you saw was not what you thought you saw.  It's unique.  It doesn't stick with a single mechanic - it jumps all over the place, and constantly tries to trick you.  I absolutely enjoyed it.Also feels like they rummaged in the stanley parable's garage sale for props in a lot of places

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned: this is not a puzzle game. It starts out as one, albeit with middling difficulty, but by the second half it drops the pretense and reveals itself as: a walking simulator, closer to The Stanley Parable or The Beginner's Guide than anything else. For the second half of the game you are just walking through rooms that arbitrarily change themselves and sometimes click on something to move it out of the way while some pretentious music and voiceover drones in your ear about how amazing you are for having made it through the experience.If you want mind-bending mechanics that actually manifest as puzzles I recommend Portal, Braid, Baba Is You, or Recursed.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, it's not bad.Pretty short game, and you can definitely tell it was inspired by Portal a little bit, but I was pleased to see that it didn't end up being a complete copy. It took me a little over 2 hours to finish, and I was going average pace, so I'd say the game is about movie-length. It's nice entertainment for the evening. _childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is an incredibly innovative and captivating puzzle game that is sure to leave players in awe of its unique gameplay mechanics and stunning visual design. Developed by Pillow Castle, Superliminal challenges players to navigate a series of mind-bending puzzles that require players to think outside the box and utilize perspective in creative and unexpected ways.One of the most impressive aspects of Superliminal is its visual design. The game's use of forced perspective and optical illusions creates a surreal and dreamlike environment that is both captivating and disorienting. From the perspective-bending rooms to the seemingly endless landscapes, every aspect of the game's world is crafted with incredible attention to detail and a sense of wonder.But it's not just the visual design that makes Superliminal so remarkable. The game's puzzle mechanics are equally impressive, requiring players to think creatively and utilize their surroundings in unexpected ways. The game's puzzles are challenging yet rewarding, providing players with a true sense of accomplishment as they progress through the game's various stages.Perhaps most importantly, Superliminal is an incredibly immersive experience that draws players into its world and keeps them engaged from start to finish. The game's unique mechanics and stunning visuals combine to create an experience that is truly one-of-a-kind, leaving players with a sense of awe and wonder that is all too rare in modern gaming.Overall, Superliminal is an outstanding game that is sure to captivate and delight players of all ages. With its stunning visual design, innovative puzzle mechanics, and immersive gameplay, Superliminal is a must-play title for anyone looking for a truly unique gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam would give me the option to leave a neutral review, this would be one. I'm neither blown away nor totally disappointed by this. It's just enough fun that I don't consider a getting a refund but bland enough that I feel slight buyers remorse. I'd say wait for a discount that is closer to 50% than the 20% on offer right now, for around €10 this would have been a recommendation even with all its faults.The puzzles, if you want to call them that, are based on perspective or the lack thereof. They are grouped into distinct sets of levels and rarely, if ever, combined to make them even somewhat challenging. Most the time you get "stuck" for a few seconds it's either because you need to hunt around for the object that can be manipulated or walk along the walls to find a more or less clever hidden doorway. To make it worse, the puzzles all but disappear towards the end and the game devolves into a walking simulator with more or less pretentious narrative.The humor is hit and miss, and in most cases it really feels like they're trying too hard. Budget GLaDOS doesn't do it for me at all, the "funny" loading bars got old fast. My guess would be that the devs were heavily inspired by Stanley's Parable and Portal but just didn't get there.Visually the game is quite nice, it ran smoothly on my system (5700x, 1070TI, 32GB RAM) at 1440p with max settings. There were some visual glitches here and there but nothing too distracting or game breaking. The music was never repetitive enough to go on my nerves and the sound design is actually really nice.It took me around 1½ hours to finish the game on my first run, there's the possibility to play it again in a challenge mode with limited movements / jump targets per segment, dev commentary or just speed run or hunt down the fire alarms / extinguishers and secrets for the achievements. If this floats your boat you might get some replayability out of this. I personally don't see much sense in the workshop integration but that might be me.

_childDocuments_.review: Good first-person puzzle game. It reminds me of portal, though Superliminal is a lot more serious and takes place in a dream world. It's very short. I spent 5 hours on my first play through and I was very meticulous in exploring every nook and cranny of each room. I expect most people could finish this much more quickly if they just focus on solving the puzzles. I purchased the game at 40% off and did not feel cheated despite the short play time.Completed the game but I expect I missed a lot as I only have 40% of the achievements. This is a puzzle game, so now that I've solved all of the puzzles, I find it unlikely that I'd enjoy playing through it a second time. I may revisit some of the puzzles to visit areas I overlooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a game that challenges players to manipulate perspectives to solve intricate puzzles. Players navigate dream-like environments, resizing and reshaping objects based on their perspective. Most puzzles in Superliminal are well-designed, requiring players to think creatively and logically. Each of them offers a satisfying challenge, encouraging players to constantly reevaluate their surroundings and search for hidden clues. Unfortunately some of them require blind pixel hunting instead, which annoyed and frustrated me to no end. Visually, Superliminal impresses with its minimalistic and stylish aesthetic. The clean, white environments create a visually appealing contrast with the interactable objects. Though in the latter half of the game I would prefer more diversity in environments. Audio design, including the soothing soundtrack and ambient sounds, adds to the immersive experience. Despite its shorter length, Superliminal delivers a fresh and engaging gameplay experience. It's a must-try for puzzle game enthusiasts and anyone interested in toying with perspective =).
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best puzzle game I played recently.The mechanics are fresh and fun, and the story is blended well with the game.I enjoy exploring outside the "main path" in games, and in this game you are rewarded for that.Integration with steam's workshop adds a lot of replayability. But sadly it is full of things people did just to get the achievements (you can still find some gems there).
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique concept with pretty decent execution. Most puzzles were well made while still being pretty easy. The overall ambiance and humor was on pointI'm glad the game was on the shorter side because it didnt really iterate or add new concept so it was getting a big repetitive at the end. However, the price is a bit high for game that took me around 2 hours. It's a good deal if you get it on sale however.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is a blast! The main story keeps throwing curveballs that I can't get enough of, and it's like they cranked up the challenge dial with every level – it's like a rollercoaster of fun and frustration.And don't even get me started on the extra stuff – it's like they sprinkled a bit of crazy on top. The challenge mode? Hoo boy, it's like trying to juggle cats. Challenging, somewhat frustrating, but you can't help but laugh.All in all, this game is top-notch, like they crafted it with a mix of genius and mischief. Good times, my friend, good times.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The base game is quite short and not that difficult. I got stuck a few times looking for an object to interact with - this was more tedious than engaging to me personally. The challenge levels are harder, but it often comes down to finicky object placement and one silly mistake will force you to repeat the level from scratch. The levels themselves are just a repeat of the normal mode so many of the usual secrets are already spoiled after the 1st playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: While nothing will ever live up to the unique synthesis of videogame mechanics as a showcase of story and artistic intent as Beginner's Guide, Superliminal sure comes close. There's much more of a focus on the gameplay aspects within Superliminal than Beginner's Guide, in case that's an interest for anyone, but its story does not hit as hard or have as much to say as Beginner's Guide. Not to say that this isn't a great game: it is, but it's much more of a showcase of mechanics instead of meaning, per se.Also, I'm a sucker for The Stanley Parable style near-minimalism rooms that games like Superliminal offer. That polished, office space/back rooms, look of these types of games has a beauty and style that not a lot of games pull off the potential beauty of well. Superliminal does this style justice, and there are some genuinely beautiful sights in this game; or, at the very least, it's a unique aesthetic that isn't done often. With the deftness employed, that alone is a reason to give the game a play.In general, it's a fun, beautiful, short (in a positive way), experience that should be played to see the incredible avenues that games can go through. No other medium offers experiences akin to what you'll find in Superliminal.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoy this game. Really makes you think in ways other games don't. Best advice if ever stuck is go around and question whether a wall is there or not. Or if a picture on a wall is really a picture. Warning you may become dizzy when playing. Some people are fine, others may become nauseous after a while. I am unfortunately unable to more than 30 minutes without feeling sick. Again really neat puzzle game, just limit play time to make usre you do not become dizzy
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little experience, going through some genuinely fun puzzles. I only had to look up a walkthrough for one part, and that's because I hadn't explored well enough. You're likely to find something to be surprised by at every turn.However...this does not feel like it was worth $20. You're able to get through the entirety of the game in less than 2 hours without much trouble. And I was messing around, too. There's achievements for 1 hour speedruns, and 30 minute speedruns.And therein lies the problem. It's an experience with little replayability. Sure, there's workshop support, but...is it really all that good to rely on fans to build more of the game to make it worth the money?I got this on sale, and I'm glad I did. But for a puzzle adventure game, there's not much of an adventure to be had. I'm glad it exists, but there's not enough meat. I don't know how you'd lengthen this game, but I feel like you'd need at least double the playtime to really justify it. Perhaps some more complex puzzles, or combining mechanics. After all, games like Portal are able to make single puzzles worth chewing through for good amounts of time. Puzzles in this would get wildly frustrating if you're stuck for too long, given it goes for a simpler approach most of the time.If you can get this game for $10, or maybe even less, I'd say it's worth the price. But expect the ability to complete this in a single sitting, about the time you'd spend watching a movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but not bad.Inevitably it's going to be compared to Portal, and at the start of the game it looked like it was going to go that way, but I was surprised that it changed directions pretty quick.Some of the puzzles slowed me down a bit, like the one late game with the looping t-bend corridor, but weren't impossible. I do wonder if I was exploiting past some parts, but the game DID tell me to think outside the box... so I'm not sure if I cheated.It had a bit of philosophy in there. Nothing profound though for anyone that already thinks.Worth no more than $20AU in my opinion.If you see it cheaper and liked portal, it might be worth getting this.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Normally I don't put an actual review and just give it a score, but I have to sing this game it's deserved praises. I haven't had this much fun playing a video game in a long time. It was confusing, mesmerizing, funny, and trippy all at the same time. I was sad at the end since it was so short, but I had a massive smile due to how the game ends. This game is a MASTAPIECE
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: A mind-bending puzzle game with a perfect soundtrack.  The puzzles are no cake walk, and require out of the box thinking.  The game has more interactions than you think, and you have to change your perspective quite heavily.  Great game to get your brain going.On top of the great gameplay and puzzle elements, the underlying story is deep yet meaningful.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The most original concept for any game I've played since Portal. Puzzles are my jam, puzzle games make up the majority of games I play, and this one is truly not to be missed. It's reasonably short (can be completed in 3-4 hours), but it consistently puts new spins on the premise throughout, which makes it consistently challenging and interesting for the whole of the play time. Highly recommended for everyone who enjoys a good puzzle in a weird immersive game world.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND I played this game while I was on A. C.1 D, it was really an experience, it distorted my perception IRL, however I had a lot of fun playing it, is really satisfying solving the puzzle, although I think they won’t be difficult if you are sober, otherwise it really makes you think in clever solutions, a must buy
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. You see the trailer and think "oh, that looks pretty cool, I wonder if it gets old though?", but no it does not. Every room and corner hides a new puzzle, but they are designed in such a way that you intuitively figure them out pretty fast, but still have a sense of awe and wonder at how the game works. Astounding, and right up there with the best of them. Good job developers \(  0o0)/
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is a genius game, It felt like a spiritual successor to The Stanley Parable, another great game I recomend.Main Story: 8/10, Although it is pretty simple, It felt like a journey I would have and many others would have inside their psyche.Gameplay: 10/10, Feels really fun to control and I really love the mechanic of resizing things using your perspective, When i first heard about this game back in 2014 when it was a prototype, I thought it would be amazing for a full game, and now here we are.Music: 11/10 It's calm and feels very relaxed, Something i'm looking for in games and I applaud whoever made the Soundtrack of this game.(LIMITED TIME) Multiplayer: 12/10 How can i start? It's that fun to play with other chess folk dressed snazzy with!Real shame it doesn't have Voice Chat, even though you can use Discord.Otherwise, this game is a big 14/10 for me, I recommend this game with all my heart (and mind) and bring your friends along for the ride that is Superliminal! It's that good and definitely one of the very vast amount of gems for a game that released in 2019.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every Minute of this Game!Once again Indie Developers blew my Mind with such great Innovations.This is by far the most mindf*cked Game i played since Portal 2...maybe even more! :OThe whole Time i was thinkin' how they programmed such Puzzles and Mechanics - It's like MAGIC!Buy it if you like Puzzle Games like Portal or Quantum Conondrum. Or even if you want something more Relaxing. And also, if you want to be in constant "Whoa" ;)But don't buy this Game, if you want senseless Action.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun to play. Some of the puzzles really tripped me up. Its visually impressive, mechanically impressive, and overall just a good solid game. The story is compelling, the level design is on point. The achievements are difficult but not too difficult, I very much enjoyed playing through this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal has an amazing story mode that is not very long but very fun and creative, This games online challenge mode is so fun and playing it with other's is such a blast. I hope this game can also come out with other game mode's. Personally hide and seek would be a great multiplayer experience by Turning into object. overall this game is something else and I love the way they have work with the mechanics by going to a specific angle to grab a check piece or a box i get to a higher place.this games is amazing and so entertaining turning
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a complete mind♥♥♥♥ paired with philosophic thoughts about lifeit catches you offguard again and again and again while managing to look absolutely beautiful at the same timeyou can immediately see the devs put alot of thought into this gamereminds me alot of antichamber but this game is way further evolved and features a storyline with it
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept but not worth the $20 price tag. The game is a little underdeveloped and seems to have been made as an afterthought, like they made a tech demo and then floundered trying to come up with uses for it until they struck on this.On another note I have the distinct feeling that they purposely made the main game just long enough for new players to take more than 2 hours on just so they'd have a more difficult time trying to refund it. I'm not refunding this because while I didn't get $20 worth of product, I did enjoy what there was.Pick this up when it goes on sale for $5 or so
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for new/refreshing gameplay, especially if you like (physics-ish) puzzle games, definitely pick this up. It's relatively short, probably 2-6 hours, but still well worth it. Loved the game, really groundbreaking idea IMO. I would easily replay it with the unlocked dev commentary mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It's a perfectly fine puzzle game, although I don't like the mechanics introduced halfway through. Be aware that the game feels quite suspenseful due to the liminal spaces and one stage takes this further with light horror elements.What I take issue with, and why I don't recommended it, is: the core message ("just look at things from a different perspective") is so common that it lacks meaning; and the levels are designed in a way that they look nice when you go through "as intended" but get more and more awkward if you look for secrets, of which there are many.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Would recommend to any puzzle fan. The game looks good and has great music. It has a unique concept and the puzzles are executed well around it. Any negatives feels like complaining. Like I guess there are a handful of puzzles that can summed up with: make thing bigger or smaller. But the number of cool puzzles that make you think out of the box or do something cool visually is a lot higher. It is hard not to draw comparisons to Portal there are a few similarities. Though you could probably say that about most 3D puzzle games. And Portal is a great game so *shrug*. This game took me 3hrs or so to beat. So it is on the shorter side. But I have to say the bottom line is: If you like puzzles, play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Although the story was short, it was meaningful and very perplexing. Yes, I'm using my big boy words for this review. It's hard to fathom the coding that went into this. I felt like I was on acid about 90% of the time and the other 10% felt like I was dreaming. Somehow the nightmare section actually made me scared and kept me vigilant for the rest of the game. It had great puzzles that I would have never thought to add if I attempted to make a puzzle game. If you want something to test your brain on "perspective" then I would highly recommend giving this game a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game. Even though it is surprisingly short, the journey it takes you on is unlike anything else I've played. My only major complaint it it seems strangely unoptimised in some areas - while I would usually get ~45 and up FPS, in some areas (mostly around the finale) it would dip to ~15 to 20 FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: wow. i initially thought that this was only a neat and innovative mechanic + some cool maps to mess with, but the narration was absolutely beautiful. the way the game really drills in the sense of scale is incredible. i love how the studio made the game's gimmick into an impactful and poetic way to view emotions. the map designs were really fascinating as well. plus the end is probably one of my favourite endings of a single player game of this type. a must play if you're either sick of multiplayers, or brand new to games. very innovative!
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: A really, really good puzzler, albeit a mediocre narrative game.The puzzle elements in Superliminal are really well executed and they really tend to ♥♥♥♥ with your mind at times.The narrative starts out okay, but ends up being really, really pretentious by the end of the game. Don't expect Stanley Parable or Portal levels of writing.Sadly, it's also incredibly short. My playthrough clocked in at around 2.5hr of gameplay. I expected the game to be a bit longer, judging by the hefty price-tag.Still, if you're in it for the puzzle elements, and considering that they're already working on a custom level editor, I'd recommend buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommend, I loved it! This is a puzzle game that forces you to look at things from a different perspective, quite literally!The messages the game delivers are very positive, loved it. Developer commentary was quite entertaining and enlightening, challenge mode was less challenging than expected, but made me realize there are easier solutions to some puzzles than I originally thought. There's also a workshop where you can create your own levels or play someone else's levels. And there's speedrun mode that had me sweat for a bit to fit into 30 minutes, but it's quite doable.Overall: an easy recommendation if you love puzzle games and are okay with mind-bending techniques this game provides. May not be for everyone, though, some people dislike their mind being pretzeled :DI didn't have significant technical issues, but had to drop to 60 fps for the speedrun. Had no issues at 144fps during normal playthrough. Puzzle difficulty isn't huge either, I only had trouble with a single puzzle at the very end (a box in a white room). But I won't spoil it for you.The only sad thing is that the game is rather short, but I loved it very much. If anything, I'd make speedrun time limit a bit longer, but I managed to squeeze in 30 minutes after a few tries.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for three hours, and have completed the game, so clearly it's on the shorter side. However, the puzzles are certainly something completely different than I've seen elsewhere, and there were only two puzzles that stand out to me as being needlessly obtuse to complete, One of them I think I brute-forced and which  have been the correct answer, though I can't say for sure, and the other which is absolutely pointlessly upsetting. I will say it relies on a mechanic which is not used before or after. Several times I knew what I needed to do, but simply could not pull off without repeated trial and error.Aside from the puzzling, the theme starts out feeling like a flat Portal homage (female computer voice hints at psychopathic scientists), and during the last ten minutes or so it begins getting overbearing with  I should mention that this is optional, but any first-time player is going to activate the audio recordings and they aren't exactly hidden.TL;DR: Would I recommend you play this? Sure.Would I play it again? No.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Many great ideas that require you to think outside the box. It worked in most of them but I remember two of them (apple and hallways) where I wouldn‘t have guessed the correct answer in a million years. That was maybe a little too far outside the box, but maybe it‘s also just me.Overall a great little experience that I definitely recommend in a sale. If you liked this game definitely also play Viewfinder.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Just. Wow.This game is really something. Sense of lost, puzzling, creeps, wonder and so many other emotions I felt playing this game in which I really felt lost in a “inception” dream that was happening in a Overlook Hotel.Amazing, it may have had some flaws, but I was really caught. I did nothing but playing and going forward. To discover what was next. Suggested? No, almost a must play if you ask me
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: THE BEST 3 HRS.this is the shortest game i have ever played yet the most mind-blowing one. Never expected a 2-3hrs indie game would be this good, such an under-rated masterpiece, the devs deserve all the praise and love for this gem. Been years since i last experienced anything like this. _childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I've been struggling to get into games lately, but this game was so fun for me and really helped me get out of my head. Initially, I felt a bit sick while playing, but the puzzles weren't too complex, and I found the mechanics behind them incredibly interesting and enjoyable. I don't normally have the energy to try to 100% a game, but finding the secrets in this game felt incredibly rewarding. I adored the soundtrack; it was just as charming as the dialogue and the developer's commentary. Overall, I found the whole game to be a lovely experience, and the ending made it even more worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Whoa this game is trippy! I could only play a little at a time or I'd feel sort of sick. Saying that, I loved trying to solve the puzzles throughout the game. Some levels really had me scratching my head. It's relatively short, and saves after each part of the puzzle you do and makes a check point. Which is great because you don't need to start at the beginning of the level if you want to stop. I did a lot of starting and stopping! Great for people who love puzzles or want to watch their friends mind melt and spiral into a mess.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: genuinely an amazing game. the secrets and hidden detail are AMAZINg. i seriously recommend this game. the ending of the story is so beautiful. buy this, its worth it. ive never written a review before but this game solely deserves it. i seldom play games that captivate me and usually delete games or lose interest in them super fast. but the depth of this game is something i rarely see in any other game. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Super trippy and fun game. Bought this on an impulse and absolutely don't regret it. Some of the secrets are easier to find, and others I don't think I would've ever found without a guide. I wish there was a bit more comedy in the writing, and I wish the story was just a tad longer. I did somehow get out of bounds exactly one time, and I was REALLY messing around. I would definitely recommend this game, worth the price for sure. Would love to play a sequel some day

_childDocuments_.review: There is about 20 minutes of game in this, the rest is a literal walking simulatior. The voiceover is neither funny nor insightful and doesnt add much to it. The few puzzles the game has are sometimes finicky due to the fact that you cant move object freely in space, so getting them to exactly where you want them is hard, for example putting a box ontop of another taller box is basically impossible because you cant place things behind other things.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as much a game per se as an interactive Art piece with puzzles. The puzzles are good and keep you moving forward, but the really important aspect of this is the experience. 110% worth every penny if you go into it looking for that. Don't try and blitz through it just looking for the next puzzle to solve. Take it in for a moment. Look around at the environments, immerse yourself and this experience can be profound.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but it gives me motion sickness, dang, I'm in so much pain right now for just 0.7 h of play. I think I'm gonna puke, I'm also dizzy. I'm not feeling good right now and I can 100% associate it with the game. This is not a joke, I'm so sick right now, I'm gonna lay in bed and cry. Why did u make me this way, God?
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It started out as really interesting and had a lot of mindblowing experiences and thus far I liked it. But later on in the game I was getting frustrated with the puzzels and slow repetetive walking. Walking really slowly in bright white rooms without visible edges was really boring and it got both frustrating and repetetive. It started off strong but it didn't keep it up. I see over 90% recommendation so I guess I'm in the minority here, but that's my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun and charming enough for the first little while, despite the GarageBand-tier musical instrument sounds used at times. I even have an innate bias in favor of any game that's physics and puzzle -driven, and/or meant to be a meditation on the concept of perspective. Still...The thing that convinced me to quit and refund the game was the sudden drastic tone shift of the Blackout/Horror section AND a not immediately clear 'puzzle' in that area, somewhat similar to the now-infamous East-West Exit Sign puzzle from later in the game--. How was I s'posed to know that was there? How was I supposed to know what to be looking for? Another mechanic tossed in and tossed out willy nilly? Hmph.Anyway, the game lacks focus and wastes most of its potential. More objects in the world should be scale-able--too often it becomes a 'hidden object hunt' for the scale-able item, not much of a puzzle. There should be more actual puzzles, with more varied solutions. I do appreciate the nods/homage/pastiche of Eternal Sunshine and whatnot, but ultimately sticking so closely to the aesthetic, tone, and typeface of The Stanley Parable almost seems like a marketing gimmick designed to trick people into thinking it's from the same creators.... Go play that game instead, first, honestly. Then Portal 1 and 2, then The Witness.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much, the very concept of it is very creative. The atmosphere and setting just feels right and calming, the music aids the calming part very well. Superliminal is a puzzle game with its own secrets to be found. The story is very simple and not to in depth, and that's ok, it meshes very well with the game play. Definitely one of my top 10 games. Absolutely get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: It was over a year ago when the demo dropped for this game. I was hooked within 5 minutes and I did not hesitate to buy it when the full version came out (and I had money). I don't regret that decision one bit. Superliminal is a mind-bending game in the vein of Portal and the Stanley Parable with an overarching narrative that is just fantastic. The voiceover work is very well-done and the puzzles get stupid hard later on. For ten bucks, it's absolutely worth grabbing for quite a few hours of fun. Now that there's multiplayer, that's going to bring the replay value up even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the Idea of making a game about scaling items by moving them around, playing with the relativity of size - that could have been really great.But the implementation is weak. The game itself is slow, rather a walking simulator than an interactive game. Then there are not many items to interact with at all, only the ones you need to get to the next room.But still, it had some appeal, it got me interested, in a relaxing way, and the gameplay reminds of the Stanley Parable. Until I reached the level where you start with the little cardboard house. As you advance throughout the stage, everything around you becomes bigger and bigger, what gives you a mouse-like experience.But at the same time, your movement gets slowed down with every room. So slow, that it becomes a real drag getting across the room. So slow that I eventually got ultimately bored and had to quit the game.You think it is funny to annoy your players? Well, mission accomplished. I'm out.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Why is this the first game to make me cry?I've played a lot of good games that have hit me solidly in the feels. But few games have kept me staring through all of the credits, no less with actual tears in my eyes. I'm bamboozled, shocked, and most importantly delighted at how this game made me feel. Well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: This game hit me incredibly hard and really surprised me with its deep and spiritual ending, its something I go back to watch time and again whenever I feel sad or frustrated. This game is absolutely a hidden gem and needs to known by more people. This game proves that games are not only Art but also Transcendental. Keep up the great work and look forward to your future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: There is no way to describe just how wonderful this game is. It's all about perspective, about how we perceive the world and how we must constantly shift our view in order to progress. There is no "wrong" answer in the game, there is no win or lose. There is only learn, there is only trial and more trial. It's a game I hold very near and dear to my heart. 11/10 will be replaying.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: The best lines of my life ever heard in a video game... So motivational!'The problem is that we become so afraid of failure that we refuse to see our problems from a new perspective and so we do the same things again and again and again. And therein of course, we find exactly the failure we were looking for.Your life will always be a struggle and you will always have problems. But today, you had the chance to see things differently. Even though it meant facing obstacles that seemed impossible at first, you thought outside the box - and you overcame them. Because you saw things from every angle, you understood them for what they really were. Because you kept moving forward, no matter how far off the path you were told you were headed, or how unexpected it became...you found your way.In a few minutes, you'll be back in the real world, and some part of you will say that none of this was real: So how could it have meant anything? But - just like the power of perspective itself - it will have been as real as you believed it to be. All you've got to do is...wake...up.'
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: What a refreshing, original experience!  I have to say I thoroughly enjoyed playing this one.  I found the expert blend of soundscape, level design and artistic presentation to solidly underscore and bring service to the unique game play present in Superliminal.  Overall, I found it to be a relaxed, thought-provoking, fun and well paced experience.Would definitely recommend if you are looking for something to engage and distract your mind away from all the current stresses reality brings these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Superliminal

_childDocuments_.review: Superliminal is an incredibly creative and engaging puzzle game that will leave you both entertained and mind-boggled. The game's unique mechanic of using perspective and perception to solve puzzles is both innovative and challenging, keeping players on their toes and making every level feel fresh and exciting. The visuals are stunning, with the game's dreamlike environments and surreal objects making for a truly immersive experience. What I appreciate most about Superliminal is its ability to make players think outside the box, and the satisfaction that comes with finally solving a particularly tricky puzzle is unparalleled. The game's narrative is also intriguing, providing an extra layer of depth to the already rich gameplay. Overall, Superliminal is a must-play for puzzle game fans, and its clever use of perspective and perception make it stand out as a truly unique gaming experience.

name: Minute of Islands
detailed_description: You are Mo, a skilled tinkerer, living with her family on a pastoral archipelago, once inhabited by an ancient race of inscrutable giants. Their otherworldly but vital machines, festering in the underbellies of the islands themselves, must be kept going or an almost forgotten threat will swallow all. Mo vows to restore the hidden engines in time, but is this truly what she needs? Features Wield the powerful Omni Switch throughout story-based environmental puzzles and platform gameplay to regain control over the giants’ machines. Face the dark truth beneath the islands’ surfaces and unravel an emotional poetic story, narrated by actress Megan Gay. Explore a fantastic handcrafted world across multiple unique islands, meet curious characters and creatures, and uncover the archipelago’s secrets.
about_the_game: You are Mo, a skilled tinkerer, living with her family on a pastoral archipelago, once inhabited by an ancient race of inscrutable giants. Their otherworldly but vital machines, festering in the underbellies of the islands themselves, must be kept going or an almost forgotten threat will swallow all. Mo vows to restore the hidden engines in time, but is this truly what she needs? Features Wield the powerful Omni Switch throughout story-based environmental puzzles and platform gameplay to regain control over the giants’ machines.
