_childDocuments_.review: Visually, the game is beautiful. The levels themselves are quite thoughtful, with excellent colors and stylistics. Locations in general are interesting to explore because they are visually different. It is unclear why there are levels with music boxes at all. It does not affect anything, and are designed as if to "stretch" the gameplay. Of course, you can consider them as drug-trip due to spores, but still it does not affect anything. A great ending, symbolizing the acceptance of reality. Overall, the game is interesting and worth spending time on, but I won't say that I'll ever run it a second time.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Brings me back to the memories of The Heart of Darkess. a classic game back in the day that does the whole journey through a land like this.  but not so much...  Idk. I think of it when I see games like it. and also enjoy games like it. I recommend. this pretty chill experience of a gameplay style you don't see as much anymore.The Backgrounds are great and interact-able  just like Heart of Darkness, you play as a (kid?) mc who uses the background puzzles to proceed though the levels. I enjoy this when its done right..  and this game does it right. A perfect journey though a strange unique setting.(For those who are too young to experience it.  here is a heart of darkness video. I recommend it to others who enjoyed this game.) I recommend it on the artstyle and creative decisions.  I wish I could see more games like this. but its a dying genre or more or less a overlooked one.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: The story itself is very fulfilling. The design is very rich that i got mesmerized when i saw the game for the first time. Sadly as everyone else says here the game is rather slow with a lot of confusing locations and stages with improper guide for the player.Yes we do have the omni but it just point where you need to be not where to navigate your way too it. I loved the game i really do but it could have been better with the platforming and navigation. For the last problem is very long loading sequences. I played Far: Lone Sails before this but this one surely lacking a certain aspect i wanted from an indie game.Other than that i highly recommend this game for achievement hunters and peoples who wanted to... sigh.. Play an hand painted story book with sluggish phasing. Story 9/10Art    10/10Controls   8/10Overall  7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands is a different take on post-apocalyptic games. Instead of presenting way to survive or change the world around us Minute of Islands tries to focus on how we can move forward and live within a dying world. While I think there were tedious sections of the game, the slower pace and somber atmosphere gave way to a beautiful experience. The story and themes may not be the clearest but I think if you stop and give this game a chance you will see something beautiful, if only for a minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, well written game. It's not a challenging game, but one more focused on story and atmosphere. However, if you currently can't be patient I would have to tell you to wait to play this game. The movement is not very fast, and sometimes you have to back a fair amount through places you've already explored, so I got very frustrated and impatient during these sections, even though the world I traveled across was beautiful and interesting. I felt like the designers were truly making me resonate with the feelings of Mo. It was so annoying. Also if you are in it for the axolotl-otter I'm gonna warn you and say it's presence in this game just barely makes mascot character level
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: pretty cool little game :) very pretty and at times heavy on graphics resources, but cool! quite slow paced and very easy difficulty once you get used to the mechanics (which is quite quick), so if thats not your jam, i wouldnt recommend iti like the story tho! not sure if i like the ending (just felt a little rushed), but overall quite fun :) quite short so idk if its worth the money, but its more of an art piece than a game
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing artwork, amazing soundtrack, amazing world and worldbuilding. Some good puzzles but a bit easy, and i find the sporeclouds/visions a bit boring.Length is perfect, and pacing is good (might be a bit slow for some).Reminds me of a mixture of Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind, Hyper Light Drifter, Adventure Time and with a touch of Akira for good messure. Would love a bit more backstory/lore and maybe a ruined city of some-sort somewhere but that's me.90/100 in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one wonderful and complex emotional journey. Masterfully written and beautifully illustrated, you can feel the whole experience has been crafted with care. It is slow, linear and narrative-driven. The gameplay is very simple and the overall flow is not going to be up to everyone’s taste - it’s not an energetic-fun kind of game, but a relaxing and reflective experience.I did encounter one almost-unforgivable flaw which would have prompted me to quit and leave a bad review, had I not found the solution very quickly in the discussions section here: a bug where an uplifting music theme keeps playing on loop and over other music and sounds, creating a cacophony and totally breaking immersion. This would keep happening even after restarting the game and the only solution was to delete a line of code from the save file located in a hidden folder - what a mess!So yeah, if you encounter the same bug, just look for a thread here named "music mixing" and you'll find the solution.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful story with few platformer and puzzle elements. Don't expect a fast, snappy gameplay experience. Do expect however an emotional journey and view into what could possibly go on inside a person that is carrying the weight of the world. And what a world it is. Incredibly imaginative visuals, beautiful handdrawn landscapes and an intriguing setting full of mystique and fantasy. This game doesn't give you all the answers. But neither does life. You have to make up your own explanations. Introspective, heart-wrenching and stunningly beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly some things the main character Mo has done made me reconsider whether i liked her character or not. She was too harsh and uncaring about her sister, she also hit her rival that made so much more sense than her. But i guess that can all be explained by her being even more isolated than everyone and being the only one to be chosen as an apprentice by the giants. Her mind in general seemed clouded and focused on only doing her "task". Although the end did make it better, as she finally learns to let go and not shoulder it all alone.I felt really sorry for the Giants :c I was curious to know their story more in depth. The art was beautiful if albeit somewhat grotesque but still unique and even cute in some places.The Negatives:- Puzzles triggering scenes every time. Specifically the moving eyes puzzle, when failing and triggering the mechanism again to try once more, it also triggers a scene, every time. it can be too much.- The Controls/Buttons can be jarring, especially the Jump+down/up button, which sometimes don't do as supposed. like going down, doesn't go down despite pressing the buttons. It could've been made better i think? or even an option in settings to rearrange the controls would be good
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the atmosphere, world-building and visual style, really great game in that regards! Also enjoyed how purposefully slow the game is, really forces you to sit back and take in everything that is happening. The narration is great, and the story is somehow simple & intricate at the same time, all while being very sentimental. Overall a great & unique story-driven game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really beautiful game with a touching story. Be warned though... there is A LOT of graphic animal death content. Visually, it's beautiful, the sound design is great, the narrator is perfect, and the animations are simple yet add so much to the story. It would honestly make a great book too. It is a short game which is nice because sometimes the pacing in some of the scenes feels slow. The puzzles are fun and fairly straightforward. Overall a fun and heart warming, and at times heart wrenching, game!Hug your loved ones all!8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Island is an interactive tale.If you are looking for a puzzle platformer, you'll probably be disappointed.That said, the ambience is quite well polished with very original artworks, music & sound design, a vivid story.What's first missing in my opinion is an age rating. Minute of Islands is talking to young teens about hard struggles they may go through. As an adult I find the whole thing over-simplistic, but I'm clearly not the target even if it hasn't been advertised. Other reviews mentioned instabilities, I didn't suffer any and I played on both W10 and linux/proton. But I found it's a shame that the hardware requirements are so high for a 2d game, there was stutters and lags that ruined some moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most gorgeous looking game I think I have ever played. The narrator is also top notch. Despite my first impression this game is for adults, unfortunately my first impression kept me away from this, it looked so "cute" in the bed sense. And the trailer is partly to blame.The underground puzzles are really a dredge and boring, so if there was a button to skip those. That would be a plus, but I guess you can always look up the cut scenes on youtube.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: - Story-driven "sidescroller" with some platforming and puzzle elements sprinkled on top.- The key components are spot on: splendid sountrack, great artwork and a soothing voice acting. Controls and animations are fluid as well, the former being specially welcome taking into account this is a slower pace-type game.· All of this combined helps inmersion tremendously, and inmediately gave me an "Adventure Time-like vibe that I enjoyed a lot.- Platforming may fight the player sometimes, requiring calmness if so.· Since the game incites a slow pace that wasn't a problem, only when trying to speed through a section.- Didn't find anything worth appearing in this section.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This game's art and story are genuinely gorgeous and compelling, and I'm certainly glad I "played" it.In order to understand whether you might enjoy it as well, ask yourself this question: Can you imagine saying whole-heartedly "that game was so gorgeous and compelling, It was absolutely worth sitting through some of the most ass-draggingly bad excuses for platforming and/or puzzling I have ever seen".If not, sorry but this game's not for you. watch a play-through. If you're a decadent libertine who can appreciate that having to hold a button turns a movie into an interactive experience: you're in luck, this movie is (technically speaking) very much interactive. Not that it really needed to be, honestly. I really think it would have been better for some of the "levels" if you just had to hold right.That said, I'm not being snarky when I say that this is one of the most attractive art experiences I've accessed through steam, and I say it's well worth encouraging the industry to explore and develop the medium further. Maybe they'll put some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puzzles in the next one
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I am giving this game a positive review, but my feelings are mixed. The game has beautiful art and an enjoyable story. But the game play aspects are a little dull, and very repetitive. This game would also be better with a chapter select option once you have completed the game. Replaying through long portions of the game to get to the point where you can get the achievements you missed is frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Very emotional story told with beautiful art and soundtrack, all the feelings will hit your sensation through your eyes and ears, it's a lot. Negative feelings when exceeding limit they're really hard to constrain, Mo is very brave and tough, her family tried very hard too.My only complain is that all the movement, climbing, going up and down are very tedious, it makes me give up on achieving perfect game, I don't think I can play it all over again, at least not now. :') I guess that's how most of the puzzle games work.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the art, the cartoonish hand drawn style looks very nice and compliments the themes of the game.In terms of gameplay, it's a pretty standard walk and interact narrative adventure, which i think is the best gameplay that would fit, too much going on would take attention away from the narrative, which is the central point of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: After I played through it:- The art style in the whole game is just great!- The music is also very beautiful- The story is a bit depressing, you have to like that or be able to cope with it. But for me personally it was perfectly ok.- The puzzles by the giants could have been a bit harder. I found it a bit too easy for me sometimes.- Sometimes I found it difficult to recognize at which places I could climb up or down with Mo. Discovering the way is certainly part of the game and is also fun. Only at some places I really had to search for 5 minutes or so until I finally knew at which rock etc. I had to continue climbing. That was a bit frustrating.- Sometimes I couldn't understand Mo's decisions or would have liked to have the chance to decide for her myself.But all in all I really liked the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Ok... The game is weird and slow. The sceneries are exquisitely horrid and the puzzles only require patience to be solved. You have to walk a lot and when you think you have found a shortcut, you need to walk double.But the game is just stunning. The story (or the absence of story) is just touching.And you can feel at every sprite or piece animation how much time, effort and heart is put here.I can't help recommending it, to be played till the end.I'm really thankful.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super beautiful game! Although there are definitely many pros and cons.Overall this game is mostly enjoyable for the aesthetic, art style and scenery, other than that there's not a lot of action or really mind boggling puzzles. The story is bittersweet, I think the idea and world design was great and does shine through a little as you progress through the game and learn more about different characters and their relations to the bigger picture, although the ending left me with a lot of questions and kind of feeling disappointed. It felt kind of rushed and everything changed so fast I was completely taken aback. Although the final verdict is fine and an interesting contrast to most games, I feel like I wasn't really sure of next steps for the character and the world and didn't feel any sense of closure.ADDED NOTES:-if you're someone who enjoys challenging puzzles this is NOT the game for you. All the puzzles are very easy to complete and beginner friendly.-The game is pretty easy to 100% I was able to do it first try. PROS: -SUPER beautiful art style and very beautiful aesthetic. Very good character design and just overall pleasing to look at.-The music isn't absolutely AMAZING, though it does always fit the vibe of the scene and evokes emotion in my experience.CONS:-felt like there wasn't much resolution to the story, left me confused and wanting to know more.-to be super nit-picky some of the animations did go on for a while for ex. crawling through holes and what not, consisted of a lot of cut scene time that isn't always necessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: the art direction is phenomenal, really to my likinghighly reminiscent of Adventure Time's drawing style for me, especially some backgrounds (bones and remains everywhere, everything is abandoned, worn down and ragged equipment)character design is cute for Mo and Mirimusic is mysterious, gives a feeling of adventure, very atmosphericthe game is mostly narrated but it isn't overdone
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful experience with a bittersweet story, and a nice message. I was expecting something along the lines of those platforms where you don't understand what it's happening all of the time, and in the end you feel like you've been mocked. This is NOT the case. The game just wants to tell you a good, old, story, and it does so in a honest way.The gameplay is ok, it's an exploration game with some puzzles (usually simple), but what makes it great is the very distintive art-style. Every island is FULL of details, with the bravest colour combinations I've ever seen in a videogame. This is a game where you will love every minute you'll spend on those tiny, beautiful (and often groteque) islands.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So, what to say about this game? Well, let's start with what's good and/or ok about itGraphics are awesome. Really they're beautiful. That's the strongest point of the game. Most likely, that's what attracted you to actually want to buy this game in the first place.Sounds effects are ok and well implemented. But you know, nothing Earth shatteringNow for the badMusic is bad. I hated it. Was more like a couple of annoying sounds put together then called music IMO.Controls are so-so. I would say they're not always properly responsive, which can lead to some problems in timing things right.While all the puzzles are easy to figure out, some of them are "interactive" after you find their solutions, and moving around the screen and hitting "moving" parts of them will have you to start back from zero. And with the so-so controls, you might have to re-start them 1, 2, 5, 8, 12 times before being able to be able to continue!Cut-scenes take REALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLY long to actually show what they want to show and AREN'T skippable, even after beating the game once.Another of my gripe with this game, is that you CAN'T choose the actions or dialogue you'd want Mo to do/say.Now for the story. Well, it's a story that would mirror someone's getting an important job, and said job end up putting pressure on them AND the relationships they have with family and friends. Thing is, the main character is a jerk. And you CAN'T choose actions or dialogues that could help her being less of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ person, while still taking her job seriously. In fact, it's surprising that her family stuck up with her 'till she break apart and finally understand she was wrong! The blue doggo thing in the picture don't do much. In fact, it's not really clear if it's a real doggo or somehow an hallucination that represent that Mo actually knows that the way she treat her family and friends is wrong. Tho, I'm fine with that part.The game is pretty short too. And in the end, I can't really recommand it. It is an artistic game, aka, a game that try to be art. Now, it's not a bad thing in itself, but Minute of Islands couldn't pull it as good as Far: Lone Sail did.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting the feels that hit me while playing this game.  The storytelling was really good and I was fully captured by the game. The platforming isn't super difficult, but sometimes what you can and cant climb on is difficult to differentiate. The ending was a kind of abrupt, I assumed it would be a bit longer going back through everything but it was still poignant.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I got very drawn in by the story and artwork. The artwork is so detailed I would spend minutes just scanning over new screens. When you go into living spaces, in particular, there are so many revealing details about the characters. The characters say and do little, yet have so much personality and history to them. I really wanted to see what would happen. The overall plot is very clear, but you are left to connect a lot of dots on the details, which got me wrapped up in the story more.That being said, those who label this a walking simulator are correct. There are no real puzzles, just things to find/collect and some basic, short sequences to follow. There are times the game feels agonizingly slow, such as any time you crawl through a tunnel. But most of the time the leisurely pace felt entirely appropriate since there was so much to take in. If you find the idea of a walking simulator objectionable, you probably won't like this game.But it is a damn fine walking simulator. One of the best I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands tells a fable full of allegory and existential dread (the nods to climate change and the impending doom of humanity are unmistakable) that is communicated through expert storytelling, extremely professional voice over (seriously they couldn't have chosen a better narrator), lovely but also wrenching music, and some ridiculously RIDICULOUSLY gorgeous art. The art above everything simply blew my mind, the level of detail is painstaking and really brings you into this tortured, post-apocalyptic world that despite all the dread and gloom, has moments just bursting with exuberant color. The game is a bit too slow-paced at times and the platforming segments become more of a chore after awhile as opposed to an essential gameplay mechanic. But despite these minor gripes, this short tale of 6 or so hours really draws you in and all of the elements come together in a magical way, building a world that is at once fascinating as it is terrifying.Word of warning, if you have any issue with seeing dismembered and disemboweled aquatic creatures, then you may want to consider steering clear. Some of the art can be quite graphic (though not at all violent).
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: If you want beautiful art and an emotional story, this is the game for you. Follow Mo as she tries desperately to save the archipelago she calls home. The narrator being both a medium for her thoughts and a guide for the player. The game is very slow paced and has no challenge to it, which some people may not like, but I personally have no problem with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral/Mixed rating but marking it as PositiveI did like the game, story, visuals, music all goodBut as mentioned by many other reviewers, the game mechanics are horrible. Extremely slow cut scenes, you can not even move during them or skip them. And there are lot of them. So you are just staring at the screen and waiting. Very painful experience. Other than that, sometimes not clear way forward but that just minor detailToo bad, if this was fixed it could have been really good game. Right now, play only if you have lot of patience or keep you phone next to you so you can do something else during cut scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I like story driven games and a good story game feels like you have taken part in that story. This game didn’t done that for me. It felt more like… interactive comic book.It is quite shorty, it takes only around 4 hours to finish the story. There was not that much of a gameplay, what you mainly do is explore to gather lore, extra bits of story and take in the fabulous artwork and music. Other than that you have a tiny tiny bit of platforming and puzzles and they are not great. Yeah, it is barely a game. I don’t think it is worth £20, I would probably be disappointed with it if I paid full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for the amazing art style and story. Mo is the protector of giants that are tasked with running machines that purify the air from a deadly fungus. She travels around to different islands to save each giant from suffocating, and encounters members of her family along the way with whom shes lost touch with due to her own battle with mental health.I loved the story, and how Mo grows as a character. The only thing I didn't like was how slow it was. The are scenes where Mo is on her boat traveling to new islands and it takes forever to arrive and for gameplay to resume again. Crawling through tunnels also take foreverrrr. It sucks because the story creates a good sense of urgency to help the giants, but you cant do that when you're waiting for character animations to finish.If you can look past the slow pace, you'll love Minute of Islands
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful, fantastic, weird, strange, unnerving, horrifying, mesmerizing game. I went into this blind and ... wow, what a mind trip. This game is all about the artwork and story, and wow does it deliver. I recommend this for all. Maybe not children, unless the child in question is Wednesday Addams. But everyone else, especially if you've got a flair for the macabre, get into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is another great puzzle platformer with a unique artstyle, enjoyable soundtrack and simple but enjoyable puzzles. The characters are interesting, albeit a bit boring at times and the story is heartwarming that captures the feeling of loss, helplessness and coming to terms with change. Although this game is enjoyable, it does have a few faults. The movement in the game can feel a bit slow at times and I found myself trying to mash through game actions that took just that bit too long. some of the platforming can feel a bit repetitive and this game might feel a bit too slow for some, but if you can make it past that, its worth it for the endearing story which you can also get extra context for through exploring the islands for collectables. The game takes around 5-6 hours to complete if you want to go and look around and collect every item and spend time listening to all the dialogue and looking around the islands. I would say for $28.95 AUD it's not priced too bad, but I think you'd get your money's worth if you were able to snag this game for $15 and under.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a work of art. You can call it a masterpiece. It easy in some bits other bits its a little difficult handling the controls of the game and had a little struggle moving around the environment sometimes but the game isn't really about that its more about the story of the game and let me just say it hits hard. The art and the music just makes the story more moving and move me. Not going to lie but I feel like this game is under rated in comparison to other games. People need to show this game more love!Id highly recommend for you to buy this game if you like story rich games, even though it maybe a bit short in comparison to like Iconoclasts or half-life 2, but its well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gem, a true piece of art made game. I waited long enough to write a review of this platformer as it stole my heart since the very beginning. Minute of Islands is a must if you love a story rich game.Must to say, puzzles could have been way more elaborated as they are not challenging at all. Everything is at hand. So, if you are looking for actual puzzles please consider that in this game they are subtle. However, one does not mind as the music, the story line, sound effects, graphs, environment and design merge beautifully that you don't actually care of them.I cried, yes. I even went back after the ending just to see if I could find things different. This is a 9/10 game. Why not 10/10 despite my obvious love for this game? Well, keep reading.In several occasions the layouts are not loading properly meaning that you can see the protagonist walking on a pink or white layer and they then quickly load one by one to get the full picture. Sometimes as well you can see the prota walking straight but the layers are overlapped, which gets fixed as well immediately as you keep walking. Minor details, though.So, congratulations to the team behind Minute of Islands. Can wait to hear from your studio again.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty mixed feelings about this: the story is interesting, and the artwork is absolutely stunning! The themes are dark and the fact that the main character makes very frustrating choices that you can't do anything about actually feel fitting with the self-destructiveness that trauma/poor mental health can lead to. The ending feels a tad rushed, but overall I love the narrative and visual aspects.The gameplay on the other hand feels quite clunky and slow. Playing on a pc isn't great, since the keybinds are awkward and you can't change them. The mechanics are very repetitive, and so are several of the puzzles. I'd still recommend playing through the game for it's beauty, but bring a lot of patience and know that it isn't really a puzzle platformer, more of a walking sim with some puzzle aspects.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of islands is a beautiful game about struggle of letting go. Themes of sci-fi-like machinery, saving lives of characters, and ever evolving fungus, devouring everything that it comes across, make for an unforgettable landscape that we get to explore. The story of Mo and her family made me cry multiple times.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork is great. It was like playing a comic book similar to Adventure Time.  The game play is pretty straight forward, nothing to difficult or challenging.  The main standout in this game is the hand drawn graphics, the story, and the narration within.  This is not a long game, but the story carries it to the end.  Not your typical happy go lucky platform game that's for sure, but this deals with loss and some real life issues that some people might be going through or has gone through.  So the subject matter is more adult, dealing with emotions and dealing with a fractured family life.  This game was still a pleasure to play just because of the subject matter and the scenery.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with an amazing story that kept me immersed within the world!The art style is so lovely, and it goes well with the music too! The puzzles and worlds were fun to explore, and I loved gathering all the memories! The ending was beautiful and made me cry, but I adored it so much! If you're looking for a beautiful, emotional game then this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A little tedious. Every time they froze my character to show the area I had just entered instead of letting me explore, I died a little inside. But if you enjoy the art and lovingly designed soundscape, it is an enjoyable little game. A very unusual setting and a very unusual plot make this one-of-a-kind. I adore it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Everything from the mesmerizing voice acting, to the thorough and detailed illustrations, Minute of Islands stole my heart and I just wish there could be more. It successfully immerses the player into the world Mo lives in, and you can’t help but keep playing and finding out about the story behind everything that encompases the islands and the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A short, very light puzzle game. The visuals are interesting, the music is great, and the story pretty interesting. The only few problems I had with it is that cut scenes and actions usually take waaaaaay too long (the crawling through tunnels action being the worst offender, in my opinion) and a lot of the mysteries of the world don't really get answered. Overall, it's still a pretty interesting game. Maybe check it out on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Cool visuals and narrative elements but the slow movement, animation interruptions and movement bugs took the toll on me.Slow pacing adds value to the story and help understand Mo and the severity of her task better but after waiting for the boats boarding ramp(the tentacle) animation for the nth time you question that thought. Once a cool thing became torture real ~quick.I won't endure this myself anymore and watch the rest of the "game" from YouTube.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands is set in a strange mysterious world that the player gets to explore. Its art style, detailled background and a great soundtrack combined offer an interesting atmosphere for the main character on their journey through the world and that's why I recommend this game, and only because of that.If atmosphere and art are what you are looking for, Minute of Islands delivers, however, the gameplay in this game, be it "puzzles" which are usually as straightforward as "do thing and then other thing happens" or the platforming, I was deeply disappointed of them. The character moves slowly, it feels like wading through water even if you sprint and everything, be it using a lever, riding an elevator or just the camera showing you what solving a puzzle did, everything is agonizingly slow. Some of the input (sequences) are also unnecessarily complicated, requiring you to press a variety of buttons in different ways to achieve a single action, which feels tedious.On top of that, it feels like the developers realized after creating the first chapter that they have to design more content than just that and ended up more or less copypasting a lot of things. After you play this game for around one to one and a half hours, you have basically seen everything that this game offers, gameplay-wise, and then it is just "on repeat" for the rest of the game, with the same (puzzle) sequences coming back in a different color and environment. There is simply not enough variety to keep you interested in the game gameplay-wise and only the detailled art, the beautiful soundtrack as well as the overall atmosphere keep you going, definitely not the puzzles or platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful picturebook, but not -really- a game. I say this because you don't get to choose what the character, Mo, does or says. In fact, she's pretty dang unlikeable. Mo has a messiah and superiority complex that ruins her relationships with pretty much everyone. There's a real struggle between saving the world, and determining what's even worth saving anymore. This is ironic because the world itself is so beautiful as it succumbs to the blight. The gameplay is flat out boring. Do not play for the gameplay. But for me, the visuals, world-building, and atmospheric music were enough to tip the scales. The storyline is also surprisingly somber - a narrator shares Mo's internal monologue, which grows increasingly spiteful as the story progresses. This is not a cheerful game. But there are set piece moments, incredible art, and I have 500+ screenshots because it looked so damn good and I do not want to replay it. Worth getting on a sale in my opinion. If you want to 100% steam achievement it, just be careful before leaving islands because you cannot return to them, and only play if you don't mind some post-apocalyptic bleakness mixed in with nostalgic remembrance.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This title should be called Adventure Time: Journey of the lost Islands starting with Mo on the other side in the land of Ooo where humans are the last of their kind ever since the great mushroom war ( I mean WW3 or Nuclear War) ravage the seas and Islands, lore asides though the art and animation are kinda bit of adventure time and similarly but the characters and art style are different and the story depicts Mo on her struggle to maintain the Island from ever coming of the unknown carbon spores and fog that threatens the livelihood of all the islanders but Mo has her own terms between the family and her giants comes to an good answer and the ending gives a meaning of let go things around and by the way the Narrator of the story was kinda of a douche really LETS REPLACE THE NARRATOR WITH A DEADPOOL hehehe jokes aside though you guys did a very good job in this game and its story, it feels refreshing to play on this game again and thanks for having me to play this game in a enjoyable and unique art style that is for everyone to enjoy for make another sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: The yellow specks indicate a hint and a stink, and it's so clear when we play that we can almost feel the character's anguish. The scenario is made up of two elements. It suggests solid pollution and useless things that we have on a daily basis, organic elements that have a certain sexual connotation. The combination of all this with beautiful and simple graphics like this requires an advanced sensory skill to understand what the artist went through in the scene. For me it's the best game I've ever seen in 2D style. It is a slap in the face of machismo, prejudice, women's sulbjudgment of the destruction of the environment, and a world after the greenhouse effect after the flood of cities.I could say more here, but I'll leave it to you to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands is a platformer/puzzle story focused game. This a short but emotional game that transposes you into a unique and bizarre world, a set of strangely beautiful islands. You play the character of Mo, a young lady on which falls the hard task of saving the world and its inhabitants. The game strength comes from its narration, art and sound design, which are really stunning.But beware, as the gameplay is truly lacking. I would describe the game more as a walking simulator with narrative elements. Experience it for the story and art rather than the thrill of solving puzzles. But If you are not afraid of a slow paced game, then you will surely enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This game already caught my attention when I saw the first images and trailer. What I can say is that I wasn't disappointed. I really love the art style and the level of details is great. They did also a great job with the narrative voice and the music. It all fits very well all together. The story is also nice and it's a pleasure to explore the envirorment and listen to the memories. I always wanted to see how the next island was going to be.I wish the game would be a little longer and more interaction with some of the other characters. Don't miss this great gameI really hope there's going to be a sequel
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: The art is gorgeous, the story is linear and not terribly complicated, but it's a gritty and bittersweet narrative containing characters with complicated emotions and relationships. Did I mention that the art is gorgeous? Play this game to relax, explore its little tragic world. Each chapter takes about an hour and a half.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: If you are in the mood for beautiful graphics and a short story this is the game for you. Will leave you with more questions than answers and sometimes that's a good thing. Game play is a little basic and controls a little funky but not game breaking. If you need a chill game that you can delve into for a afternoon I would recommend Minute of Islands.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful well-made game about relationships and isolation (among other things). I picked this up pretty much as soon as it released and played through in 2 sittings. It was engaging, emotional, and had just enough challenge (although I did have to look up a solution to one of the problems after spending waaaaaay too long going in circles). It's not a stressful game - gave me GRIS vibes even though everything is completely different. 10/10, will definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: hosts a truly unique world filled with bioelectric technology and fantastical giants, mixed with a seafarer/fisherman aesthetic. The hand-drawn art and animation are phenomenal, with a style that reminds me of  and . The story is delightfully bittersweet, and follows Mo as she tries to save her world all on her own. Definitely recommend, especially if you enjoy story-driven indie games with unique art direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing Minute of Islands. The art style is outstanding and every image is well composed and brimming with details. Through art work, sound design and its slow pace the game creates a very unique atmosphere. For the most part it's more an experience than a game, which also shows in the gameplay. The puzzles are not difficult at all and sometimes a bit too repetitive. Thus, for me personally the game was not challenging but after finishing it, one has to realize that Minute of Islands is less about puzzles but more about exploring a dense world and experiencing a engaging story.Unfortunately, the game creators use frequent back tracking to stretch the game. Considering that it still takes you only around 5 to 6 hours to finish it (including almost all achievements) the trip to the islands felt a bit short. However, the art work itself is totally worth playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the games I've bought during the Steam Sales, this was probably my top favorite. I know for some at first glance, paying 20 dollars for a hand-drawn game may seem a bit much. However, after playing through the whole entire story, I guarantee that this game is absolutely worth the price. If you are looking for a game that has an epic story line, wonderful sound design, and a meaningful core message, then this is definitely the game for you. Happy sailing :)PS: If you do plan on buying this game I highly suggest you play it blind. It will absolutely be worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings about this one.The good parts:- The art style and sound design are great. Would love a bit more visual ques on the platforms. Sometimes it was hard to see where I can and cannot go.- The story and setting were nice.- The narration is really nice. It added to the experience.The meh / bad:- Level design. The level traversal seemed tedious and mostly used to slow the player down. Using level design to pad out the game is just meh.- Puzzles. Interesting in the first hour. Becomes old really fast.- Character interactions were bare bones. It made the characters seemed one dimensional. A missed opportunity for more story telling. Example: Granny could talk more about the big exodus. Sister could talk more about their parents. Uncle could tell you more about the outside world.- Length of the game is 5 hours. Mostly meh. End quite faster than i expected.The things that made me angry: -The Omni switch. Okay, real talk. So, you can make this magical item do anything. So, you make it be a glorified light bulb + crank.  What a let down. I was expecting the puzzles to get a bit crazy. Maybe make the omni switch like a miniature spore repellent and have the character navigate a level full of spores ?Or maybe make a way to hunt secrets? It could light up circuitry behind spore covered walls and you can collect more memories. Maybe expand the energy manipulation (The thing that you need to connect to pink spots to power machines). Make it challenging to power these machines. Prove to me that Mo is not just a girl with a glorified light bulb, but it takes skill and dedication to use this item. If the item a hero uses is not powerful or impressive - then the hero looks weak and insignificant.- The dream sequences. I get the 'Night in the woods' dream sequences you were going for. However, half of them felt unnecessary and out of place. No world building was done in them. It did not reflect the characters mood. If you take them out - nothing is lost.Only good ones were the first dream sequence and last one.Bugs: - I have encountered numerous visual glitches throughout the game. Its nothing game breaking but did take me out the experience.- The player character interactions with objects (such as the eye tubes you need to move) are really rough. Often it feels that i am playing GMOD and trying to put two walls together. Sometimes it works, sometimes I need to move around awkwardly until it clicks.Overall: I dont regret playing this game. Its fairly short and focuses heavily on the aesthetics. It feels like some sort of parody of adventure time and I really love it. But its not a good 'game'. The game part of this game is packed with tedious game design which often is more frustrating than enhancing. Overall, i would compare it to 'Night in the woods'. Its a good game which focused heavily on aesthetics, music, story and sound design. However, it also has the same problems as Night in the woods. There is not enough game in your video game. Combined this with just a good story, minimal character interactions and short length and I can only give this game a 6/10. Its an above average game, but has potential to be something great.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Stellar game, notwithstanding a few minor flaws (most of which the devs are working on fixing). This game exhibits beauty, not only with its artstyle, but also its soundtrack, its narration, its dialogue, its story, its characters, its ideas. It's a haunting game of allegory, and I hope that it finds its way into the annals of narrative Video Game history, together with the likes of What Remains of Edith Finch, Firewatch, and a few others. For my criticisms of the game, I've compiled a short pros and cons list, for brevity's sake.Please keep in mind that most of this is not objective:Pros:- Beautiful, Heartfelt Story- Great Characters- Awesome Narration- Fantastic Dialogue/Writing- Incredible Artstyle and Animation- Fabulous, Mysterious World- Some nice Puzzles here and there (but do treat this game more like a Walking Sim, the puzzles are fairly few and somewhat rudimentary at times)- Solid ControlsCons:- Most Puzzles are fairly basic, even rudimentary (Great for casual players, like myself, though)- Some Animations outstay their welcome (Note: I personally don't mind since I think it tends to, more often than not, add a lot of much needed athmosphere into many of the games moments)- More could have been done with the dream-esque sequences- A menu for replaying individual chapters, and re-listening to some of the "memories" you collect throughout the game, would have been great.BUGS (Devs are working hard on fixing them, so they might already be dealt with once you read this review):- One Softlock at the very beginning of the game (fixed with a quick reload without further issue)- Another Softlock about 3/4 of the way through the game (likewise fixed with the quick "reload" option provided in the games menu)- Music overlapping/One piece of the OST playing over another (I've received personal confirmation from the devs that this isssue is being worked on): This is hands down my biggest pet peeve, since it ruined some of the grander moments for me. My suggestion for anyone struggling with this: Turn off the music completely in the game's options. The game's ambience carries it well enough. Alternatively: Wait until patched.In summary, fantastic game, congratulations and giant thanks to Studio Fizbin for enriching my life with this game's story, world and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: First time I stumbled across this game was back in 2019, on a book fair of all places. They had the demo available so I started in the middle of a level where someone else left off. The artwork and music instantly cought my attention and I played through the demo after I got home.Now that it's finally here I played through the game in one sitting and took my time to take in the atmosphere and just let it all sink in.The main point of this game is the plot and the way the atmosphere as a whole makes you feel. The emotional weight of the story takes precedence over action-packed gameplay. If you are aiming for challenging gameplay instead of a "story based walking simulator", then I suggest to look somewhere else, since you probably won't like this game too much. However, I thouroughly recommend this game to anyone who ever felt like no matter what they did, it was not enough. This game lives off its emotional core and is best engaged with as a story to live, not necessarily a game to beat.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game feels like playing a really quality cartoon, one of those miniseries that leaves something with you when you finish. The puzzles and platforming elements are easy, and are mostly there to give you time to meditate on the rich and detailed environments you're moving through. The story of the game is told mostly in brief snippets of memory, by the voiced narrator, and never perhaps as explicitly as your curious mind might want. But it's enough to get the emotional point across.I cried a bit, in the end. I don't think most people could relate to being a "chosen one," like Mo. But hanging your entire self-worth on a single goal, self-sabotaging your life because no one can hurt you if you hurt them first, hiding yourself away from reality so you don't have to accept it... I think if you don't see the protagonists struggles in yourself, you probably do in someone close to you. Ultimately, it's a beautiful and hopeful story.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I've been staring at this title on steam awaiting its release and now that it's here I couldn't be more happy with my decision. This game is a treat for the ears and the eyes. The player is encouraged to explore extra tunnels of the game to find out more about the world and the characters. The narrators voice is intoxicating. Really well written interactive novel. Sometimes mechanics feel a bit clunky but for the most part the game flows so well. Can't wait to finish this compelling story.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but this game REALLY deserves it. It's beautiful. A bit like Adventure Time mixed with Lovecraft, but it offers even more than a bizarre crossover. A story that's a bit sad, and while devs say this story is Mo's alone and wasn't created to depict specific phenomena or people, I think it still makes you ask yourself important questions. So yes - it does make you think and feel and that's a great thing. It can touch some strings you never thought you have. Dear devs - thank you for that wonderful game! I still think the story isn't only about Mo, but about other things to. Really - be proud of what you created!EDIT AFTER FINISHING THE GAME:The game is even better than I thought. And the story is touching. And it's so many things at once. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game on stream and we all loved it! It is such a underrated piece of art and I can recommend it everyone who loves games like GRIS. The story is really heart warming and the graphic style is unique. Also the music hits different and creates a fantastic atmosphere.Minute of Islands don't want to be fast everything is a little bit decelerate but I thing that is a part of the whole relaxing concept. But don't underrestimate the Trigger warning there are indeed some really triggering scenes and if you having problems with mental health then think twice of playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: wonderful story overall my only complaint was the plot holes and unexplained parts of the story that i noticed i see this as more of a story game than a puzzle one and the game could of been more compressed into maybe couple of hours for more of a cinematic experience but overall good game my main con for this was the random crashes but that may of been on my end
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a visual- and audio-wise beautiful game. The gameplay is minimal and is almost the most basic variation of a walking simulator. However the story is told both graphically and vocally in a very compelling way. I'm not normally a person that just stops to enjoy the surroundings in the game but the environments are so interesting so in this game I did.The downside is perhaps that it is sometimes a bit hard to navigate yourself as the graphics are so intensive. There is basically no game play. Despite that I would recommend this for anyone who like compelling stories and just want to follow it for a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic art and sound design. The story was the intensity level I was looking for. Gave me the feels throughout most of it. The puzzles and platforming was quite casual. For me the causal play level provided engagement without threatening frustration. Personally I enjoyed the relaxed pace of the game. Will definitely be playing again for the story and completion. Curious if a few key choices are baked into the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Great story with impressive and immersive visuals. However it's certainly not for everyone. The game play is very slow, it's more like and interactive story than a game and the puzzles get repetitive at the end. But if your looking for an engaging story and interesting world to get lost in for 4 to 5 hours it's a great buy. If your on the fence, probably wait till it's on sale. It will at least offer an interesting experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands is a beautifully done, linear adventure that delves into topics like trauma and self isolation. It's well written, told from the perspective of Mo, our player character, as she goes around to a variety of islands in an attempt to get the air purifiers up and running again so her family doesn't succumb to the fungus spores that have chased off and killed all of the other island's inhabitants.Highly recommend, though be ready for some drawn out sections that get a little boring. This game is far from action packed and is more of a walking sim with platforming elements. The puzzles are decent as well, and increase is difficulty as the campaign progresses.Playing again to get the rest of Mo's memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: A Beautiful puzzle adventure game with a deep story that tackles powerful and grim subjects.The game is rather slow-paced but that gives you time to enjoy the world at your own pace and take everything in. I was super interested and invested in the world and the characters you come across. The main character goes trough some very heavy stuff during the game and the things she does made me as a player conflicted about her at times and at other times I was rooting for her or even felt sorry for her. The game also has a good narration. Few puzzles felt like filler and they appeared at times when I was most eager to find out what happens next. (They felt like interlude puzzles and I believe that's what they were going for) These puzzles do have a good story reasoning however so I can't be too mad about them. And like previously stated the game is slow, more like a great story rather than an active gameplay experience with deep mechanics.Overall I really enjoyed the game, the world and the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: The game has beautiful art, and a soundtrack that contributes to the emotional overtone of the story. Both the snippets of info you find by examining the environement and the narrator are on point, and further immerse you in this decaying world.In terms of game mechanics, there is not much variety on what you can do, but I'd say the game doesn't last enough to make it feel repetitive. In that sense, the pacing goes along well with the context in which the character exists, that is, this small archipielago filled with memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have the most beatiful art and sounddesign I ever experienced in a game. The artwork is so endearing and unique, and it carries the emotional journey so well along with the music. Seriously, you won't have seen anything like it! The worldbuilding also stands out and really makes you wish this game would be something bigger (I would easily spend 100 hours in this world if it was a RPG). But the premise is much smaller and much more personal. You might criticize the short playtime (5 - 6 hours) the lack of challenge, the super slow pace and backtracking (even though I think its intended and fits the narrative, sometimes it is just too much). I liked some of the puzzles and I would have loved to see some more of them instead of walking a lot. Nevertheless these flaws are overshadowed by an amazingly thought through journey whose key moments are delivered masterfully. I couldn't resist to cry in the end. The ending is just too beautiful! My soul thanks you very much for creating this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Minute of Islands is a game about trauma, self-hatred, and isolation. It is also has people having to stay inside and wear masks so they don't die to a horrible disease.Fitting.This is a very solid indie game with absolutely gorgeous art that especially picks up during the latter half.The only gripe I can come up with is how some of the animations are slow and can get a bit tedious when platforming.I definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

_childDocuments_.review: Explore strange and wonderful islands and dark labyrinths below in this narrative puzzle platformer. Guide young mechanic Mo on her quest to repair a world on the brink of collapse. The powerful Omni Switch at your disposal may not be enough to fix the damage that hides beneath the surface..
_childDocuments_.name: Minute of Islands

name: Little Witch Nobeta
detailed_description: The Little Witch Nobeta is a 3D action shooting game. Players will explore ancient, unknown castles and use different magic elements to fight against the soul! The game uses a comfortable Japanese art style, but the battles are quite challenging despite its cute looks. Underestimating your foes will lead to troublesome encounters. You must discover enemies' weaknesses and learn the precise time to dodge attacks in order to gain the advantage in combat. Game feature: Complete plot cutscenes. Moderate puzzle-solving elements. Various combat styles including physical melee attacks and four types of magic: Arcane, Ice, Fire, and Thunder. Each magic spell can either be shot normally, or charged up to unleash a devastating magic trick! Each element has a unique design, allowing players to find one that suits them. Although charging magic spells takes some time, successfully attacking enemies will charge the gauge automatically. Go on the offensive to use powerful magic more often! Story: Nobeta, the little wonder, came to the castle alone to solve the mystery of her own life. Constantly challenging powerful crafted souls, she learned all kinds of magical abilities and befriended a mysterious little black cat. What secrets hide in the depths of the castle?

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is hard!It tricks you with the extremely adorable main character, but its actually quite a dark tale and brutal difficulty. I'm playing on what the game has markes as "the intended difficulty" and except for the first one the bosses have been difficult as balls. I really apreciate that, games nowadays are too afraid to challenge the players and its good to play one that doesn't treat me like an idiotThe levels are huge with fun plataforming and lots of exploring to do. Fighting with magic, finding is really fun, makes me think "what if souls game was actually balanced around the player shooting lots of magic" but more mobile and not reliant on a stamina bar. The default camera was awful for me, but luckily the game has tons of options to customize the camera to whatever each player may find better. As a final note I'm so happy that it has great music for each level, specially the lava one

_childDocuments_.review: It is a cool game that could be much better if not for some negative points that hold it back. It is a "ranged dark-souls" where the focus is mostly on shooting spells (although there is a melee attack, it is not the main form of attack). Obviously this indie game can't seriously reach the same standards of dark souls (not even close), but it is a respectable "lite" version nonetheless.GOOD:+ Decent visuals; cute characters; costume options; decent voice acting (japanese); good movement and controls; decent combat; rewarding souls progression.BAD:- Repetitive enviroments and boring level design (dark, stone brick corridors and walls); weak story and world-building; disapointing enemy variety; a few unbalanced and unfair bosses; limited playstyle options; bad and repetitive music.So if steam had a neutral option for reviews I would probably pick that, but on second thought I did enjoy the combat and characters so a positive rating is fair. Just be warned and tame your expectations going into the game, and get it only on a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this game for what it is, which includes a cute anime girl, decent gameplay mechanics, and interesting story. _childDocuments_.review: As a favour to someone, I'm reviewing this game, now that's out of the way.I genuinely think the game is fun, it has few dark souls elements such as dodging, a parry system linked to your attack button, stamina, and arguably the difficulty of a souls game, but it has it's own elements, which separates it from most souls-like games.Your main form of attack is magic, in a third person perspective you can hip fire your magic, or aim down for more accuracy and you can charge it up for a more powerful attack, then there's the second form of attack, a melee strike, which is maybe just as important to you as your magic, melee allows the use of a counter, though tight, with just the right timing you void damage and even regenerate HP and MP all the while dealing a fair bit of damage to the countered, another use is for charging, melee attacks also regenerates a portion of MP this is useful for two reasons (I'm aware of) 1) MP of course runs out, leaving you without your strongest attack, magic, and 2) Your charge attack isn't a hold down the magic attack button, it's keybinded and takes a hot second to charge, whilst charging Nobeta is slowed down to a walking pace, but dodging can still be preformed, however doing so stops the charge until the charge animation begins again, striking an enemy whilst charging speeds up the charge time by portions.they're other mechanics the game will tell at the beginning, so I won't go into anymore detail.as of this review the game is still in early access, meaning bugs are still apparent, but nothing game breaking in my play time

_childDocuments_.review: To get the elephant in the room taken care of firstCalling this game Loli Souls? Not wrongThe developer’s discord server for this game being shut down due to CP?And 18+ content period was banned on that server, anybody who went there knew it wasn’t okay, it was definitely posted by someone trying to get it shut down, this game’s community means nobody any harm and should be treated as such.Now for the actual review.I came into the game expecting a janky indie soulslike, which to a point is what I got. The plusses first, the writing and story is nice, if a bit barebones, the combat is excellent and finely tuned, long as you keep up with your upgrades, I didn’t have to grind any to keep myself feeling up to snuff. The character models are where most of the effort went in the art and it shows, the normal castle environments look as generic as it gets, later ones are better, with the final area being fun but still nothing to write home about. The music is great and atmospheric, it’s a crime that the ED/credits song isn’t in the OST though, just the songs from the rest of the gameplay, which ARE good if you like orchestral bgm type stuff.The gameplay is relatively unique to most soulslikes, melee isn’t your main damage dealer, instead your damage comes from four elemental magic attacks, each of which can be charged for a unique attack at the cost of more mana, which is regenerated in several ways; slowly passively, when you do a perfect dodge, when you melee an enemy, and when you do a counter (melee when an attack is going to hit you) all of this comes together to make the combat loop incredibly fun and engaging especially when combined with the soulslike stamina mechanic, instead of just being unable to move when stamina drains, your character trips and is immobile for a few seconds. The game IS relatively short, though they clearly encourage two playthroughs (normal and NG+) and some time after launch the trial tower was added, a boss rush mode which felt much harder than the main game, it contains more lore tidbits and takes place after the main game, but far as gameplay is just all of the main game bosses again.The story stars the titular witch Nobeta, she has few memories, but hears a voice urging her to find the Throne, the ultimate end goal of the game. More happens, but that’s the setup, and all I feel comfortable mentioning here. If you want more story than is inside the gameplay, there is the supplemental manga, five of them, available online. However, of the five, two of them are 100% intended to be read after finishing the main game, the ones called Wanderer in the Dream and Little Black Cat.This leads into my main complaint, the VAST majority of the context of the story is contained in these manga and it’s a real shame cuz it’s all great stuff I would have liked the game to give me as I was experiencing it, maybe the devs weren’t confident they could portray these events well in engine and opted for that method? I don’t know. The other main complaint I have is the progression system. All through the game there are 45 treasure chests, nearly all of them hidden, some hold generic healing/buffing items, others contain upgrades to your moveset in the form of grimoires for your spells, which raise their level up to 5. Aside from one exception, this is the ONLY way you get these, though you WILL get every element, some, like wind, really need to be upgraded as they gain super important extra abilities at higher levels.These two are my only major complaints, I’d give the game an overall 8/10, I enjoyed every moment of the game and really hope the developers continue to expand on this world as they seem to want to.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a hefty discussion page about my feedback. I think it's quite good where it is, I think a lot more could be improved on. I think both design and pattern design is quite good, I think balance between spell elements and gameplay styles are not quite there (certain tactics work way better than others through the whole game, rather than vs specific bosses).The most enjoyable parts were: the spells feel rewarding to use, stuff like stamina and health often feel restrictive enough to have to play around them, but not so restrictive they feel frustrating, the exploration is done well, the puzzles integrate spells kinda well, and there's quite a good balance between ranged spellslinging + melee combat + looking for opportunities to charge spells and fire them. I think the most disappointing parts are: leveling up magic involves picking them up out of chests rather than actively getting currency or xp to level them up (some of which make fighting bosses massively easier), the melee is slow and there's no stat to help speed it up, certain elements objectively negate entire boss mechanics (ice vs boss 3), there's a lot of clarity issues (ice charged to beat 3 fire rocks for example), and some visuals (needs more fire monsters for fire levels, not just more maids, blobs, and dolls).For temporary newgame+ content: I hated newgame+ not having a boss rush, I thought newgame+ had too big of a hp pool increase the first time over, they could have had it at 75% of what it is now and it would be better. I hated having to kill mobs to buy potions to retry bosses. Boss 4 was quite fun overall; I wish newgame+ had that boss replace the actual boss 1 when the game is finished, and other bosses also get a new mechanic or two instead of just +hp and +damage.See:  for more details.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun overall. After 38-ish hours of messing about in Little Witch Nobeta, i can safely say this has a ton of promise. The whole idea of this game is interesting and fun. I have only a few gripes with this game, and to shorten the wall of text that'll half be about one boss, here's a Pros/Subjective/Cons points.I'll try to keep this as spoiler free as possible, but i will spoil half of the third boss.Pros -Quite polished.Looks great.Cute.SFX is quite good.Combat is fluid. The ranged combat is done quite well.The boss fights are fun and challenging.Subjective -Souls-like, so difficulty may be an issue. There are 2 difficulty modes though.Infinitely more of a tutorial than other souls-likes. Being given directions on how to use elements and what they do.The more cute style may turn some off if they're fans of a more dark theme.Ranged focused combat. May not appeal to some, or just feel off for them.Movement is surprisingly fluid. Not as clunky as Dark Souls or other souls-likes.Cons -Monica, the third boss. I have issues with this fight that ill get into after the cons.Most non-boss enemies are lackluster and sparse.A massive issue that me and many others have with how little the update have been, and how we have been told nothing as to why we've gotten none for 184 days-The one big issue i have with the game is Monica, (spoilers for the fight incoming!) The entire second half of Monica's fight is a bit of a mess. Monica has a titanic health pool and will catch the player off guard and check them right into the grave. The first attack is pretty counterintuitive, Monica preforms a telegraphed to hell and back slam. Doesn't sound bad right? Well it wouldn't be, but even if the player dodged it, they would get tripped by the force of the slam, exhausting all of their stamina and giving Monica enough of a window to slap the player halfway across the arena. While a bit against ones intuition of what would probably happen, one somewhat poor attack wouldn't make the fight a much of a mess that i say right? Besides you can just parry it, or if you got 2 wind tomes to get the air dodge, you can jump before the slam lands and dodge midair, completely avoiding damage. While yes you can do that, the doesn't make the attack any less poor than it is. But this isn't the only poor attack in Monica's kit, no no no my friend, there is one more, and this attack will either make this fight into a borderline display fight, or just pure suffering, depending purely on if the player knows how to counter it.So the third attack Monica uses has her conjuring a ball of fire for 3-4 seconds, after those 3-4 seconds, she clasps the fire ball with her big mitten things, empowering her, she winds another very telegraphed slam, and breaks a portion of the arena, making it more cramped.Alright, that doesn't sound all that bad, just defeat her before she destroys too much of the arena. If you thought this, good luck in that endeavour. Remember that health pool i talked about? When i say it's titanic, i mean it, she has just around 18,000 hp, compared to Specter Knight, which has just about 1,700 hp, and Tania which has about 2,200 hp. This might raise the question, how are you supposed to deal with that amount of hp with just your puny little spells that will barely scrape her?Well! You have to do something that very much goes against any intuition the player might get, you know the fireball i talked about? Well that's the secret to winning, while shes charging the fireball up, shoot the fireball. If you preform this correctly, congrats! You just dealt like 1,700 damage, or 3,600 damage if you wait for it to fully charge. Now all you have to do is repeat this until shes done.I'd wager that 99% of people who know this, found this out on accident, maybe you threw out a channeled arcane shot and it ever so slightly slapped the fireball, or you just were aiming center mass. I feel like the game should've shown you something similar in the lava ruins, maybe through some puzzle involving fireballs that you have to shoot in order to complete it. Just something before Monica to show the player that the mechanic exists, so they feel some accomplishment in remembering what they were shown, and applying it. I don't know, this attack just got me, uh,   -Ok ok ok, you might be wondering, why is this review negative? Are you really not recommending this game just because of 1 boss?No. I would still recommend this game in spite of that, but i don't recommend it because... That's why i'm not recommending this, because i don't want you to waste money on something that may never get finished. Every announcement they've made since July 10, of 2020,  has been about non content related things. Let me tell you about every announcement from July 10, 2020, the time of the last content update, to January 11, 2021, the time of me writing this review. So first up, on July 11, 2020, they announced a discord server, not much that's wrong there right? Second up, on July 20, 2020, umm-uhhhh? Something about Monica's panties... I-i don't know why but, uh.Third up on the block, on July 31, 2020, they announced an exhibition for Little Witch Nobeta in Taipei, where you could buy Little Witch Nobeta related merch.Forth up, on August 17, 2020, they showed a thing on alternative colors for Tania, and they wanted to know which one we liked the most. Fifth up, on August 19, 2020, they announced the fact that they sold 150,000 copies of Little Witch Nobeta within 50 of release. Impressive numbers all things considered.Sixth up, on October 26, 2020, they announced a Patreon page.Seventh up, On October 28, 2020, they announced a Q&A sort of thing, they just answered three questions that were commonly asked, with one of the questions being when do they plan on finishing the game, they said by the second half of 2021, or 2022 if they decided to push the game onto multiple platforms. I doubt that.Eighth up, on November 17, 2020, they announced something about a Patreon milestone reward? Eh it's unimportant.Ninth up, on December 22, 2020, they announced some stickers you can buy.Tenth up, on December 25, 2020, they announced some merchandising in Japan or something?Eleventh up last, on December 31, 2020, they wish everyone a happy new year, and pushed their Patreon.So that's eleven bloody announcements, and none of them were things related to new content in game, not even a single bug fix.And with all that, we still have no reason why we've been so in the dark about why there has been no updates for so long. At least let us know that things are still in development, so we have some peace of mind.I'm just worried that this wonderfully good idea for a game will go to waste, this has such vast potential to be an amazing game, but it seems that nothing is getting done. I have no definite reason as to why nothing has gotten done, i don't if it's something up with Pupuya, or SimonCreative getting in the way of the development, like publishers tend to do. Who's knows? It could be both!But i only fear the worst.
