_childDocuments_.review: This game is about 8 or 9 hours long if you're taking your time! It's mildly replayable, but it's mainly just a one-and-done experience. If you're looking for a triple-a level of polish and length, you might want to try something like Code Vein instead (but if you're looking at this game because you're a lolicon, there isn't much else out there for you).This game feels like Dark Souls except if magic casting felt good and was more integral to the game. The game is fairly polished, with some bugs that I was fortunate enough to not encounter. The combat is really fun, especially once you get all of your magic abilities and can destroy basically anything from any range. The game is pretty easy up until the last quarter of the game, during which the difficulty ramps up to being  (in the normal mode, I can't speak on the hard mode.) The story is alright. You probably won't feel any emotion at any of the plot unless you're a huge crybaby. Like Dark Souls, a large chunk of the story is told through item descriptions. The difference between Dark Souls and this game, however, is that those items have  other than exposition about stuff that usually doesn't even matter to the plot of the game. They're mainly just there for world-building. Don't get me wrong, it's cool that they thought of a whole world and lore around the events of the game. It's just, the fact that they wrote all of that stuff for it to not even matter to the game boggles the mind. It almost makes you wonder if there's supposed to be a sequel or DLC or something.The visuals are pretty good when it comes to character models. It's nothing crazy, but the humanoid characters have visually appealing designs. The environment, on the other hand, could be better. None of the areas are particularly good looking, nor are they unique. The most stand-out area is the lava area, if only because it has an area-spanning obstacle unlike the rest of the areas. Most areas in the game look like some low-quality architecture you would see in the distance in any other game, especially in the outside areas. They don't look , but they're certainly not pretty.For me, the gameplay is definitely the highlight of this game. It's definitely not Horizon: Forbidden West or some other visual equivalent, but the gameplay makes up for it. I just wish it was longer. I wouldn't hate it if the devs opened up the workshop for custom levels or something like that. I would absolutely buy a sequel if it had more in-depth systems, but this game is good as-is even if no sequel is to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta is a Souls-like created by Simon Creative and Pupuya Games where we control the titular Nobeta who doesn't remember who she is, with her sole mission to reach the throne. What secrets does the Castle hold? Will she discover the truth? Find out by playing yourself!Now I don't want to spoiler anything but let me just say that I was pleasantly surpried with how good it was. The game might look cute on the outside but the World inside of Nobeta isn't. Whilst simple yes, I really enjoyed it! If by any chance you are intrigued by the world and characters you can read all item descripions which give quite a bit of insight. There is also spinoff manga about all Major characters that focus on their backstories (these are amazing btw).Visually Little Witch Nobeta looks great, every character looks cute while the environment emanate this griddy, dark and mysterious atmosphere. Some textures do look a bit dated and blurry but it doesn't take away from the experience whatsoever. There a loads of outfits to choose from for Nobeta some bought as DLC and other by completing in game challenges. I really love the boss designs in this game since they are really cute of course.Now I decided to dedicate and entire paragraph for this for a simple reason. Sounds in this game are absolutely 10/10 for me, from the music to blasting spells. Good audio is key to all games in order to have a great feedback when attacking, getting hit or doing anything at all. Blasting spells is sooo satysfying charged fire spell sounds like a true EXPLOOOOSION, arcane like a canon and lighting (duh) is just insane. Now soundtrack... MY GOD It's amazing, It was THE reason I bought the complete edition, every single OST was a banger from the start to the end.Let's talk gameplay. I wouldn't be so passionate with this game If the gameplay wasn't good. I'll be brutally honest. Little Witch Nobeta features . So here is how the combat works. You can dodge with SPACE and melee attack with your staff by pressing , these actions (and sprint) cost stamina. You have to be careful with stamina however, as depleting it all with cause you to trip and that can kill you when in combat! Magic can be cast by pressing M1 or charged with , these actions cost Mana, you can also use  to aim your magic. Whilst charged you can either keep the spell (this grants different effects for example while holding fire spell your staff attacks deal bonus damage) or you can unleash your charge with . If you run out of mana you can't charge or cast any spells so what do I do then, you might be asking yourself. Hitting an enemy or doding an attack will generate mana, If your mana is at max it will instead overflow into air and will come back to you in a couple seconds. You can start charging the attack and whilst thats happening you can combo it with said overflowing mana to instantly charge your spell or you can use your staff to charge a spell quicker. There is also a Parry mechanic that functions simillary to other souls games but unlike those or souls-like games is extremely useful since it completely blocks any incoming damage and also generates a LOT of mana. Now why did I bother explaining everything? It's quite simple really. This whole system means that Agression is  rewarded.  Which might be reminiscent of Bloodborne in that regard. This also makes it so when you master the combat you feel like a GOD. Now there are of course even more mechanics to go even more in depth but I think you get the gist of it. It's fun, satisfying and it feels just right! Your abilites will be tested once you complete the game as that's when you will unlock THE TRIAL TOWER. Best of luck to you If you wish to challenge it!By the time I managed to 100% complete this game I had 45 hours and I think there will be a lot more where that come from! This game just absolutely slaps in all aspects! It's cute, funny but also grim and dark. If you are looking for a great souls-like then look no further! Long live the cunny... TOT TOT

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta is a light but worthy twist on the Souls formula for the weebishly inclined.The biggest twist in question is that Nobeta is a witch, not a melee fighter. She out-ranges most of the enemies she fights and is considerably powerful at that range, but her mana is limited and recovers very slowly on its own. She must chant to access her more powerful attacks, slowing her movement to a walk. Mana is recovered during battle by dodging accurately or physically striking the enemy with the wand. It's a simple, elegant system that encourages you to work on your timing and take risks to fight effectively. I really like how this game focuses on making the solo mage work and keeps it feeling powerful, instead of compromising by introducing too many melee options.The magic itself feels great to use. Sure, it comes in four generic flavours, but the visual and audio effects really pop and fizz. The elements each have distinct uses, both when it comes to solving puzzles and dealing with enemies at differing distances. Pulling off a perfect dodge and following up with a huge strike really does feel great. In general, the visuals are clean and polished, even if much of the design is generic high fantasy JRPG fodder.I think it's fair to say that a lot of the success of Little Witch Nobeta comes down to Nobeta herself. It's clear from her animations that a lot of work has went into making her the most adorable moe protagonist possible.  She has so many little flourishes, from the way she falls over when out of stamina to how she clasps her little hands together to pray. Once a certain objective is met, Nobeta's character is considerably fleshed out, and it was great to discover that her animations also change to reflect this. It is worth noting that some of the fanservice options - such as the alternate costumes - might be objectionable to some, especially considering the protagonist's apparent youth. It should be nothing unmanageable to an anime veteran though.While Nobeta sticks out as particularly charming, the narrative is not very impressive. I can praise the decision to keep things abstract, but there's very little substance to reward the sense of mystery. There's at least no annoying JRPG exposition here, and thank goodness - the dialog between the characters plods along at a snail's pace, and the voice acting while clear isn't exactly motivated. The numerous items you can pick up contain lore, but the contents are so basic and vague that you've probably played more unique beginner D&D games. Still, there's something to be said for the game's dreamlike, simplistic tone.This is an indie release by a small team and it very much shows in its presentation and how much the assets are reused. Similar concepts, map layouts and enemy types are retread so often that the core game starts to feel like merely hallways between bosses. The bosses are good, but their difficulty is uneven - I had far more trouble with the second boss than any of the subsequent bosses. Not that any of this game is that difficult - it's harder than its cute looks might make it appear and it takes some getting used to, but while it's clearly Souls inspired, it's in no way Souls-hard.Nor does it need to be - Nobeta is a success on its own terms, but you need to weigh your expectations. I'd really like to see this team or another take this Souls-Mage concept and flesh it out, because the truth is that if you weren't taken in by the adorable protagonist and core combat like I was, then you'll probably find very little beyond them to keep you entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta isn't quite a soulslike game, but it does share some similarities with the stamina based dodges, parries, and generally high difficulty. Despite being an indie, it has unbelievable amount of polish in the general game feel. Although there is an easy mode, it's not that much easier than normal mode so you'll still need some skill to beat it.For the current price, I'd say this is a worthwhile game to get if you don't mind a difficult game you'll have to retry a ton to master. The game has a wonderful style and interesting gameplay when it's not destroying you.Also the Blue ribbon girl is super cute!Edit: I'm nominating this for GOTY, it's not a full game, but it has more heart and soul than a ton of others even at this early stage.Edit 2: After completing the game fully I can still say that it is a great fun game with a decent amount of challenge, however I feel that the difficulty was made slightly easier than in the original early access build, even when playing on advance. The parrying and movement are still satisfying and consistent, allowing for players to get better as they get used to the controls, which themselves are quite fluid. One criticism I have for the controller gameplay is that aiming is not perfect with difficulty combating late game ranged enemies, but this is something players can still work around.The full game adds a few extra areas which are about the same quality as the initial levels available in the early access, although there is some asset reuse later in the game. The difficulty for each of the new areas is on par with the earlier levels, never taking things too far in an unfair direction. I do feel that the final boss even on advance difficulty is a bit too easy compared to earlier fights, Monica and Tania being the highlights of the game still.For the price, the game is a good fun time, I hope we see a sequel soon which could possibly expand the souls like exploration to an interconnected open world.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is still in early access at the time I am making this review.  A lot may change between now and the point when it's a finished product.Little Witch Nobeta is a deceptively challenging game in a similar style to Dark Souls.  The combat is heavily focused on range and rewards well-timed parries and dodges.  There are a few breakable walls, simple puzzles, and platforming sections, most of which for optional loot.  The platforming is generally easy, yet satisfying but isn't a major factor in the game.  Memorizing boss telegraphs and attack patterns is important to succeeding, and each boss gains new patterns at low health.  Making a wrong move in a boss fight can often lead to you being stunlocked or knocked into lava for an instant death, but every attack is possible to dodge, parry, or simply move out of the way of if you watch the boss to learn how they let you know exactly when they will attack.  You start with a basic magical element and gain up to 3 more through playing the game, each of which combining its own unique magical gun-like attack, a spell with unique properties, and a unique buff gained while you have full charge to use a spell.  As for the story, it seems like it may be interesting when there is more story to experience.  As of now, there are just a couple revelations and cute moments after boss fights.  If you like magic, cute girls, ruthless bosses, exploring to find loot and your destination, and Dark Souls mechanics, this game shows signs of being pretty solid.EDIT:The game has been fully released, and I experienced the entire campaign.  First thing to mention, the devs deserve a lot of credit for allowing an old save from 2 hours ago to be loaded for me to experience all the new content without losing any of my element and skill upgrades.  The game is also longer than I had expected, giving it a decent amount of play time and proper buildup for certain parts of the story.  There are over 100 items which don't have any impact on gameplay but reveal a bit of lore to help give more context to the story.  The outfits in the base game are all cute, and I plan to get the DLC so I can unlock two more for future playthroughs.  The voice acting from Hololive members did a lot to bring some bosses to life and was clearly properly cast.  I also really loved how the game ends, although I won't go into detail on that since I don't want to spoil it for anybody reading this before playing.  I saw a lot of potential in this game way back when I played it in early access, and it far exceeded all expectations.  I have nothing but respect for the developers who dreamed up this project and put their hearts into making it a reality.

Now, the downgrades which could be polished in the future: when you interact with a lever there's a split second of Nobeta walking in place; sometimes when you jump near coffers you remain stuck and only a jump can free you;  when you die with curse, you lose a VERY little amount of souls; the first two bossrooms (plus the secret one) are lacking a pinch of inventiveness; Arcane magic should be integrated better in the future (I barely used it after acquiring Fire; *SPOILER AHEAD* Monica's second phase can be very easy if you stand on one of the pillars. *END SPOILER*Code Vein showed us how good can be the synergy between souls mechanics and anime scenery, this is just a cuter way of doing it. _childDocuments_.review: I played the demo of this game and found myself pretty enthralled by the premise. Given everything I've seen of the dev's work I'm incredibly excited to see how Little Witch Nobeta ends up. I'll be updating this review once I fully sink my teeth into the content offered in the current early access version of the game, but at its price point even just what was offered in the demo would be well worth the purchase. With the current build you're given three bosses to fight against which will take you likely 3-5 hours total to complete. There's more to come, of course, and the foundation set here is phenomenal.In short it's Dark Souls but in order to attack you need mana which can pretty much only be recovered with tight dodging or hitting enemies with a weak melee attack. It leads to a pretty great ebb and flow in combat and provides a great sense of risk vs. reward. There's more techniques you obtain along the way (which weren't in the demo) that give you further options. The most notable of which that I've found thus far is an option you have to counter enemy attacks by timing one of your normally weak melee attacks right as their attack lands to parry it. As your mobility increases the bosses are given mechanics which make use of them to an extent, and various little puzzles/hidden areas require mastery of the game's movement techniques.All-in-all there's a bright future ahead of this game, and even in its current state it's certainly worth a purchase and, without a doubt, is among one of my favorite experiences on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: What a journey! I had bought the game way before the official release of the full game, but didn't finish the game only until now. Being the first soul-like game I have ever played, Little Witch Nobeta gave me an undisputedly enjoyable experience, both gameplay-wise and story-wise. It is definitely worth the ~250 NT I payed at the time, but I doubt the 1190 price tag is commensurate with the content I have played until now. I would suggest wait for a discount if you haven't bought this game, and get the costume DLC with the main game.I have finished the main story of Nobeta with easy mode, no extra farming, no items used, and no guides at all. I also play the game using a controller. I have not collected all collectibles nor beat the secret boss, so I haven't 100% completed the game. Yet.As I said before, I had no experience playing a soul-like game. In my knowledge, this genre focuses heavily on combat, especially actions like dodging and counter attacks that rely on reflexes. At first, I feared my clumsiness would give me a hard time, but it turned out to be much more comfortable then I expected. First of all, successful dodges and counters are very rewarding, which encouraged me to practice these techniques. For example, I would try countering attacks at a pinch, because successful attempts heal me. In addition, enemies are extremely forgiving. Almost every attack is hinted by long animations and loud sounds, creating sufficient time to prepare for them. To sum up, this game is very friendly combat-wise, and I believe most casual players would have a great time getting along with the system.Jokes aside, exploring the map in Nobeta gave me a variety of experiences. At first, when I was weak, dumb and awkward, every step required great courage. Every corner could be hiding a whole army of souls, ready to smash energy balls at my face. All of this horror game experience abated after picking up some spells and leveling up my stats. Regardless of fierce battles, the dungeon puzzles every now and then let me stop for a while and appreciate their dungeon design. In addition, some locations have beautiful scenery. I was grateful I can immerse myself in such scenery after a volley of fire blasts.These aspects may include spoilers, so I chose not to elaborate too much. To begin with, boss fights are what I loved the most about this game. The bosses have amazing movesets, both visually and mechanic-wise. I wish there was a challenge mode with only bosses so I can enjoy them without being bombarded with a rain of Pikachus. Equally enjoyable, the story fits well with the gameplay. I won't be going through all the shenanigans about inconsistencies or loopholes, I would just say that the story makes sense casually, and I'm looking forward to read the back stories written on the collecitbles.Buy it, because why not. At least you can spend a little time recovering with your loli after being demolished by other lolis.Ignoring the Hololive cast is advised while estimating the value of this game. It's not worth it supporting the VTubers buying this game, you should toss superchats instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The developer paywalls development information behind Patreon, and strawmans the community as 'impatient' for simply desiring what is standard practice for indie games. He also appears adamant in not releasing segmented content, which would ultimately be beneficial for both marketing and game quality by retaining hype and minimizing the post-release flow of bug/balance patches. This is not an attack upon the developer (at the very least, they appear to be constructing the game, according to a hidden community log/timeline), but their practices in game development and community management.From a discussion post on the announcement '20210127' (a relevant source of this review's information, along with their Twitter): 'Update information information is a traditional right for those who afforded the game; releasing it free is standard practice for... every community-connected developer I know. It induces a positive reaction (or hype) for the playerbase, and thus prevents everyone from forgetting the game exists in their library. As well, it is beneficial for advertising, as inactive communities are... inactive, and don't speak of the game. The same principle applies to segmented updates rather than simultaneous releases. I don't know any reason why one would implement this practice - it's detrimental for marketing and the community... the standard of segmented updates also ultimately results in a higher-quality game as feedback is more efficiently received, and less post-release bug/balance patches will occur. One cannot counterclaim that 'rushing the game' will be detrimental while ignoring, no, outright objecting to this fundamental of game quality.'As for the game itself, it's playable at the time of this review, though I wouldn't gamble upon consistent quality, and would expect a swarm of bugs post-release.Update: There was no news update in April as the developer promised. Likely, they lied to revert more reviews to positive.~ owner of the now-obsolete English Discord server

_childDocuments_.review: Game has good controls, pretty responsive overall, traversing and platforming feels pretty good. The  mechanics have good synergy with each other. It feels like the game gives you freedom to use the tools however you want, rather than requiring you to use fixed strategies to overcome conflicts.Gameplay is basically exploration with enemies throughout the stage, which you are free to explore at will, sometimes finding combat rooms with crystals you have to destroy in order to proceed. Exploration rewards you with items and upgrade to your spells. Defeated enemies will only return upon praying in one of the statues(similar to bonfires in Dark Souls) or entering a new section of the map via load screen. Enemies give you currency used to upgrade your character or buy support items in the statues. The maps have enough space and your character is fast enough to run past enemies if you wish to go straight to the bosses.In combat, your main form of attack is by shooting spells, where you can either lock on and shoot at an enemy or manually aim. Spells cost mana, which regenerate pretty slowly on its own, but you can regain it faster by hitting enemies with your staff, dodging as they're about to hit you, or by parrying. At cost of mana you can also charge your spells for more devastating attacks or temporary passive bonuses depending on the element, while charging you can still melee, dodge and parry, those will make you charge faster, the drawback is that your character will move slowly until you either finish charging or cancel the concentration. There's also a stamina bar which will be used by running, dodging, or jumping, if your stamina depletes entirely, performing any of those actions will make your character stumble and fall to the ground taking time for her to get up, in that time you're completely vunerable to attacks. Melee doesn't use stamina, but it will preventing the bar from regenerating.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good. I am not that far into the game and I kinda hit a wall of difficulty and kinda take a break from it to cool off. Even with that said, I still can appreciate the game overall though. First off all, about difficulty that many people might concern, There are 2 difficulties in this game as of this review. "Standard" and "Advance" (Used to be called "Easy" and "Normal" which, tbh, I think it seems more fitting) I am playing on "advance" or the used to be "normal" difficulty. the other one is too easy can you can just walk and tank damage almost the whole game. But this one really requires you to actually pay attention to everything you do. You can't really just YOLO and hope to win like Easy mode. TBH, the difficulty are too different from each other and I wish there is something in the middle. One is being way too easy, and the other seems kinda hardcore for a casual player like myself (yes, the easier difficulty is still TOO easy for casual like me). With all that being said, I still enjoy it as it is.The control is super on point. I am playing using Mouse and Keyboard, and it is perfect. Not once I think I have issue playing and wish control is better. Every death I had were all my own fault for not being good and not because of the control issue or the game being unfair. The skill set the change the menu are all in well thought out place and easy to get used to. So, as for game control goes, this game has it simple, but charming and smart. Let's talk about Game environment. Although I am only at 4 hours mark as of this review, I have seen 3 areas so far, and this game has those area done right. The mood and tone and the enemies looks just right and while sometimes it seems too dark in some area, but that might be what they intended seeing I was at a place that is supposed to be dark (?) But yea, For a game of this scale, it's done really well.Music is easy to review, really good. Sound effect, kinda meh. Esp the cat. It sounds so unnatural. But that's just minor detail.Overall, I think it is worth it even at full price even though it is still early access game. I still have some left to go for this game. But so far, I am loving it. And even though later area I haven't seen might be too hard like other people said, I still think most of my point should still be valid. Note: I am not "souls" fan and I am more on the casual side of player. So I tend to not be able to get past harder part of "soul like" games. So, this review should be more relatable for people who isn't DarkSoul or the likes fans or people who are casual gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like my reviews? Take a look at my Curator Page and drop me a follow! Little Witch Nobeta is a cute little game and very lightweight on your computer.It combines evasive and tactical combat with a cute little Loli with Overknees. Just that already is worth a buy for just 8€While our little Loli is cute, sadly all textures ingame are very low, even on maximum settings and feel like it was a PS2 game. But since this game is still in early access I really hope that textures will be reworked and rooms be filled with more details and life.The controls are okayish but sometimes you don't quite understand why something hits you eventhough you evaded and sometimes you evade very badly and it still counts.Animations are also something that needs a rework, just looking at you little feline friend makes you feel weird, as the cat only floats around with animations that nowhere fit how it moves.When it comes to enemies the game ist really nice, your first enemies are tentacles with eyes! Over time you will get to master 3 different elements that not only give you different attacks but also give you boni like a fireshield making you immune to fire and you will have to use those skills for little puzzles that want you to utilize and understand how spells can be used to your advantage.All in all the game has big potential and I really hope the devs will listen to the community and keep on adding stuff to this cute game.And where Deadpool wanted to have a super hero landing, we have a super cute loli stumble landing!And remember: Lolis are for huggu, not for fuggu!

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the demo for this game a few years ago, and I remember being super antsy and excited and like desperate for the full game to come out. But after a few months, I had a bunch of things come up with school and essentially forgot about this game until a few months ago. It's a super intricate and cunnypilled game. I love it so much, and I'm still working on getting 100% on it. It's a fun game reminiscent of Dark Souls with its bosses, puzzles, and roaming. I'd highly suggest it to anyone who likes magic based combat games or games where you can just roam around the pretty levels. If you have this game on your wishlist or something then I'd definitely say you should get it and atleast try it. The game itself is pretty short, it only takes around 7 or so hours to complete the story. Despite this it has really good replayability especially because 7 hours isn't enough to 100% the game and collect every item. There are also bosses and things you can only really do upon replaying. It has a good leveling system, cute costumes, an interesting and vague storyline that's fun to put together, and is overall just really cool. Moving on, this game runs really smoothly and my laptop handles it pretty well. Do keep in mind that I have a convertible HP laptop which isn't built to run games and struggles to run most other games, but despite the attention to detail with the visuals and the 3D graphics, my laptop handles it really well. It really only lags during certain combat situations, but outside of that and some visual chugging it runs really smooth and pretty fast, so I imagine that most people can run this game regardless of their setup. So, yeah, this is a great game, super fun and super cute. Definitely worth it, I highly recommend trying it out at the very least. The team clearly put a lot of effort into it and they deserve the support.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have yet to put in much time with this game but I've been very impressed by what I've seen so far. Mostly. This game does seem rather early and lacks polish in terms of optimization, but the gameplay is incredibly promising already and the art style is quite pleasant as well. It's anime but not too obnoxiously so. I'm excited to spend more time with it and see how it evolves. And for $10 WITH a demo? If anything about this game seems interesting to you I'd say you owe it to yourself to try it out.Update: I've put more time into it and it continues to get impress! Initially the boss battles can feel a little difficult and I do think there's some balancing to be done with dodging as some attacks are quite simple to avoid while other require a very fine precision even in the very first boss encounter. But with all the tools available to the player no boss is insurmountable and can be tackled in a variety of ways. My only major complaint is one that I see other reviewers have made note of, the lengthy animation you have to wait through after dying. It's a cute animation, clearly the developers want to show off the work they put into it, but it gets annoying fast when you have to wait for it to finish before you can run back to a boss. But I feel like this is a pretty minor issue and one that could be addressed fairly easily, hopefully someday it will be.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and funny? I don't get it...A third person shooter souls-like where you play as a loli with a magical staff that is actually a gun. The game is hard but not frustratingly difficult.You start off with 1 spell and can unlock addition spells to aid you throughout this tower. Each offensive spell has a basic shot and a charge shot. Each spell also can be viewed as a different gun type: Arcane = rifle, Ice = machine gun, Fire = shotgun, Lighting = sniper. Their charge shots have different functions and properties, such as charged ice gives you armor, charged fire enhances your melee attacks, and charge lighting slows down time. All the spells shares the same mana bar. Your mana regenerates fairly slowly but there are other ways to refill it: hitting enemies with melee, breaking pots/etc, using items, and parrying.You can dodge roll, which has invincible frames. Later you can unlock the ability to double jump, dodge in mid-air and the ability to do wake-up roll on the ground or air recovery.There is a casting time for charging your spells which slows down your movement but you aren't necessarily a sitting duck. You can perform all your actions while charge except shoot which will cancel your charge.This game has a parry mechanic and it feels really satisfying to do because of the animation and sound from parrying. Outside of being invincible for a few seconds, parrying also refills your mana and health. But most importantly it speeds up charging time, strangely making it one of your strongest offensive tools as a defensive mechanic.Souls are used to level up your stats and buy items.The tower for the most part is linear save for a few detours but not necessarily a bad thing. There is a point of no return at the 70%ish mark for exploration. Death's aren't too punishing, you are placed back at the last checkpoint the only thing you lose is whatever items you consumed. You only lose souls if you have curse stacks which you only get if you use certain items, but you can remove curse at the checkpoints.The boss fights is probably the best part of this game. A lot of pattern learning and attack recognition. Outside of maybe 1 or 2 bosses, the bosses don't have any particular patterns to them, they can and will spam a certain move on you if they want to.There are a lot of outfits you can dress Nobeta in and they're all cute and based. Some are a little unhinged.They recently added a boss rush mode in the game and I think it's fine. You unlock it after beating the game. You basically challenge each boss one at a time in order until you beat them but you can only level up your spells, not your stats. After you beat them all, you unlock practice mode where you can fight any boss at any time. Strangely enough they excluded a variation of the first boss from this.This game has some deep lore but unfortunately most of it aren't found in the main game mode itself. Beating the game unlocks some manga chapters to learn some of the character's past, in video format which is really cool. The boss rush also contains some details about the characters. They're also still making manga chapters that aren't found in game, like through twitter or discord (both are very special places just as a warning). I dislike the fact that you have to go out of your way to learn more about the story.Overall I enjoy this game. If they ever make a sequel I would play it. I'm just waiting to see if they make wall scrolls based off of certain artworks...

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with everyone else that Little Witch Nobeta is the Loli of Dark Souls. Between the gameplay and the creepy castle environment, you can tell right away that the dark souls franchise is what inspired this game. Literally anime modded dark souls. Now right off the bat, the story makes it seems like the game is following after the events of learning this magic. False. The game centers around Nobeta learning these magical abilities. There is no tutorial for this game. No little beginning where you learn all your base moves or what to do during certain events. However, there are glowing spots in the ground that give you hints. These hints consist of “use this button to jump”, “Press this to dodge”.Visually this game is alright. There are two different art styles in the game that don’t mix very well. Nobeta is beautifully drawn, as well as the scenery. While the two art styles are nice on their own, they do sit right together. While I have to acknowledge that the game is still in early access, the game doesn’t run as smoothly as I want it to. Nobeta’s hair is very stiff and clips through things at times. Hopefully little things like this will be fixed?

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game! This is easily my game of the year. (It probably would have been Elden Ring but I have no way to play it.) I like the character designs. The bosses are the best looking parts of the game. Unfortunately the rest of the game is a bit bland. The controls feel great. I heard the game was really short. I was hoping for 15 hours. I was worried it would only be 10 hours but it was a lot longer than I thought it would be. I like to take my time playing games like this and it took me around 20 hours to beat and another 8ish hours for New Game+.What surprised me the most is the story. Normally especially for games like this I don’t care at all I usually just go whatever but I was actually a little interested in it. I read all the lore items I picked up. I wanted to know more about the world. It’s a very simple story. Girl goes to the castle to find the throne that has the answers of who she is. We kinda don’t actually find out well we kinda do and not at the same time. I won’t spoil the ending. There was some really sad moments. I like the magic system. It’s simple and easy to understand. The more you upgrade the more abilities you will have. Like if you get level 2 or 3 of fire the explosion will get bigger. There are four elements that are for attacking and two more for support. One of the Wind levels makes your dodge better. The Arcane magic you start with is a good starting magic but once I got another magic I never used it again. Even upgraded it doesn’t do as much damage as the other three elements. Leveling Arcane doesn’t do much. The other elements have very useful levels. The only thing that Arcane has is that it charges pretty fast but uncharged lightning still does more damage. This feels like an indie game. There aren’t very many enemies. Most are just recolored to be stronger. Black->red->blue->shadow black. The environments are a little bland but at least each area looks different. I would like to see what this could look like with a big budget and team. The foundation is great.The voice acting is great. At least what little there is in the game. All the character’s lines are fully voiced but there’s not a whole lot outside of bosses. Nobeta’s VA is Chika from Kaguya-sama: Love is War. The bosses are Vtubers that I don’t know but they did a great job.New Game+ was really fun. You keep all your levels and the enemies get harder. You can New Game+2 but I heard nothing changes and the enemies don’t get any harder. I really like the videos you unlock after beating the game. If you can unlock all of them it shows a lot more lore.This game needs more love. I want a lot more people to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta. This is an anime action game developed by Pupuya Games and co-published by Simon Creative. The Steam page for this game was opened in March 2019, and since then it has caught the attention of many anime game fans. At last, the game began early access in June 2020. There are some rough sides, but this game is pretty exciting!Little Witch Nobeta combined a cute anime girl with a soul-like genre. The player becomes the cute witch Nobeta and starts the game. She enters a dungeon-like castle to challenge the throne. She can collect souls by defeating monsters. You can use them to enhance her abilities. Her stats include health, mana, stamina, attack power, agility, and so on. Basically, she can perform ranged magic attacks, wand melee attacks, and powerful charging attacks. As she gradually explores the dungeon, she learns additional magic, solves some puzzles, and battles with the stage boss. According to the game development roadmap, a total of six dungeon stages are planned, and the first build of Early Access includes three stages. There is quite a bit to be polished, but the game has good potential overall.Little Witch Nobeta. It's an anime character game with good potential. Gameplay focuses on dungeon exploration and boss battles based on third person action. Honestly, the game experience in the current build is rough overall, but nevertheless this is interesting enough. Best of all, taking a challenging adventure with a cute anime girl excites us. As you can see from the developer roadmap, he/she aims to make his/her game a long-term project with great content. This early access game has shown good possibilities. If you want to support this nice anime game, don't hesitate to try it! Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta is action adventure game developed by Pupuya Games. A Small team originally comes from Taiwan but the developers make sure the game support at least a basic language such as English when a game comes out, so it can reach out to a bigger audience. The game was put on steam on 2019 with one demo for players to give to give it a try, since then it had been on radar for awhile as people thought it might become one of the great game in the future. Now a game is currently in early access, but from the look of it this game has already surpassed people's expectation. Not only it's fun, it's well crafted with care and it's full of potential. Early Access has at least 6-10 hours of contents depending on how much you're familiar with the game of this genre, it's short but with the current price, it's very well justified.An extremely fun action adventure game and challenge. The gameplay was crafted and balanced around ranged attack or magic, which character the little witch Nobeta can use them to defeat enemy on various situation or battle. In additional to "Stamina" bar which consumed each time you dodge or run (and will trip while making cute sound of ow when she tires out), the character will have "Mana" and it will be consumed each time you use magic. Mana generally recover over time but in much slower rate compare to usual Stamina, in order to regain Mana quickly and more effective, Nobeta must close in and melee attack an enemy with her staff, she can also regain mana through precious dodge and counter enemy attack. These flows of combat are common throughout the game and in order to fair against it, one must understand how this mechanic works and master them. By taking advantage of everything Nobeta has up on her sleeve only then player will be rewarded with such a smooth flow of battle and experience the most out of it.When Nobeta successfully defeat an enemy, she will gain "soul essence" which acts as a currency and can be used to upgrade her stats like more HP, more Mana, more Stamina etc, or buy an item at the save point. Dungeons are designed to have some of the platforming which require performing a right moment of jump and mid air attack trick, medium puzzle, and hidden entrance. Which mean the dungeon isn't completely linear, there're path to explore and the reward of exploring them thoroughly is a nice item or a permanent upgrade to make your character more versatile such as expand item slot or stronger magic. Some path can unlock a shortcut which establish a safer route for character to traverse or backtrack the dungeon.  The most important feature of this genre is boss fight. Most games of this genre have cool or nice concept and executed very well in foundation when in comes to combat system as a whole but usually fail flat on boss design and comes out messy or imbalance. That happen because everyone want to make their game of this familar genre "hard" without understanding how to actually make it good and fun. Little Witch Nobeta surprisingly does it right compare to other similar game. All available bosses have good telegraphing attack and noticeable different in variety of move. Not to be confused with a predetermined attack or "pattern", the telegraphing attack means enemy has shown some sight where player can immediate guess what they're going to do and thus can react just in time to keep up with battle flow. A "pattern" means enemy will perform several moves in fixed order which most don't actually require player to read their move thoroughly. Little Nobeta has nailed both telegraphing and pattern right as they're not just doing some giveaway "flashing" light before an initial attack, some bosses also show to have their "expression" changed or limb tweak or sound effect of object moving when they move or attack which show how much they care when they design a boss, and put in so many little details that would not only define game mechanic but the personality of the bosses as well.The game comes out as cute anime girl in first impression, and it's exactly a cute anime girl but also destroying stuff while look cute doing it. However the game sets in the Medieval Era as it has structured middle era castle like, trace of alchemy usage and worshipping goddess status. It seems to never meant to be realistic compare to other game of the same genre but it does have some hidden dark history going on judging from enemy design and some scenery found on each corner of dungeon, but I can't really comment of that yet because the game is in Early Access and story hasn't gone very far depth in current build.Music is right on track, each boss has it own version of music which surprisingly rhythm to the ear, it's not metal rock nor any loudy voice soundtrack, it's composed to fit the theme of classic JRPG mean there's an "opening", the "tense" and then "cilmax", it was designed so it stuck on people's head for awhile just like how JRPG done their music sheet. I would recommend people to give it a chance anyday. Its gameplay is very much justified and definitely belong in this genre. It honors a genre in a very respectful way.

_childDocuments_.review: While there are a few things that could certainly have been done better, I believe the game does much more right than it does wrong. I'd be happy to recommend it to just about any action game fan or fellow degenerate. Thoroughly exploring the game on advanced, I think a first playthrough ran me about 16-17 hours while a NG+ run to finish out the achievements only added another 2 hours or so to my play time. I would have been perfectly content to have paid full price, but it's possible some people disinterested in exploration and item collection or some more skilled players might not be fully satisfied with the price to time ratio they might get. Combat is quite good, pretty well thought out. The mesh of ranged and close combat works well. You've got four base types of magic; your ranged attacks, all of which are very usable throughout the game for different ranges/purposes. For each type of magic you also have a chant/charge attack which takes some time and mana to ready. In addition to the charge attack itself there are some different effects you can gain just by holding that charge before using the attack or letting the meter run out, such as strengthening your melee attack, for example. What really elevates the combat is that you can fill your mana or otherwise that chant meter by either closely dodging enemy attacks, parrying enemy attacks, or through physically attacking an enemy with your staff. This creates some really satisfying combat cycles of chanting then dodging, parrying, and/or melee attacking to build charge while taking pot-shots with magic in-between charge shots. If you get good you can speedily max your charge repeatedly and totally ruin enemies which is just really quite fun. The primary downside to the game has probably got to be the somewhat lacking common enemy variety and boring designs. The majority of the enemies more or less just look like some shadowy figures. There's four different varieties of these basic enemies, each of which has a couple palette-swapped versions. These alternative versions usually are different enough attack-wise I guess but nevertheless it is kind of lame they couldn't get a few more unique enemy designs instead, especially given just how basic they are. There is another I believe 7 basic enemy types which have better designs, 2 of which also get a palette swap.I found the story enjoyable, although I'm not really a fan of the method by which much of it is told. Although the basic story of Nobeta is told normally via events throughout the game there's much more to be found surrounding her story as well as the world, and the boss character's stories both through items found in game whose only purpose is to provide lore, and through some extra manga which can be unlocked. Although the manga is unquestionably well made, experiencing the full story through the game itself would obviously have been much more preferable. But then there's the issue that this manga is also heavily censored in the game (there are official uncensored versions uploaded) for whatever reason, which leaves me a somewhat conflicted since although it's not ideal, I'm still glad they were able to provide a full version of the story one way or another.

_childDocuments_.review: May 2021 Review:Stuck in Early Access purgatory now. Devs are pushing for Patreon subscribers, doing side projects, looking to create an anime, etc.I have nothing against side projects, but I get the feeling that this is either never going to be finished or is going to be finished in an underwhelming matter a long time after EA opened. I'd recommend not buying until after it's officially released.That said, I still wish the devs the best of luck. I don't think the lack of focus is a sign of ill intent on their part. I think any issues are likely because the level of success Little Witch Nobeta had was unexpected and it led to content creep and forgetting to finish the actual game prior to branching out into a dozen other related projects.Original Review below: Extremely fun game. The term is a bit overused but this does absolutely follow the base Souls-like flow of action RPG gameplay. Explore, kill enemies, look for checkpoints, heal and level up, and repeat. The exploration part is actually much more forgiving than a typical Souls game though, as under most circumstances you won't lose any exp/currency for dying.The combat, on the other hand, is unforgiving (at least at Advanced, haven't tried Standard) and takes a notable mechanical departure from its obvious inspirations. Dodges on their own aren't as strong as they are usually are in these titles, mostly because of the rapid nature of enemy attacks and the boss design. You'll have to make good use of running, jumping, and counter magic in addition to dodging if you want to avoid a trip back to the last checkpoint. Likewise, when it comes time to go on the offensive the combat pacing is designed around building up enough mana by meleeing, dodging, and natural regen to take down your enemies with spells. If you take the time to understand the game's mechanics, understand what the spells do, and practice using everything you're given, you'll be rewarded with challenging but fun, satisfying fights. If you try to play this with the mindset of last second dodging and chipping away with a few hits at a time, you'll be rewarded by seeing the boss's intro cinematic again in short order.Which brings me to my only major criticism of the game: it needs some quality of life touches. A faster trip back to the last checkpoint on death and the ability to automatically skip boss intro cutscenes after seeing them the first time would be much appreciated.All that said, if you're a fan of Souls-like games, cute anime girls, and/or gameplay that rewards practice and skill, this is a fantastic choice and I would highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that I fall in love with a game. People have kinda dubbed it as "loli dark souls", while it's definitely inspired by Dark Souls, it does have its own unique identity. At this time, It's early access and not finished yet, but it's incredibly promising and has great potential. I've already played through the whole game over 5 times and 100%'d the achievements. New Game+ also adds more replayability (but make sure you do the bonus area before starting NG+!)The game is cute and difficult. Level and character design is absolutely gorgeous, I found myself stopping to appreciate the view alot while exploring. The soundtrack is also quite nice, I was a fan of the second stage music in particular as well as the first boss music. I must also say that the UI and HUD design is fantastic, I've never had less trouble understanding a game before.Nobeta can get a total of 4 main attack spells, all of them are unique and have their own use depending on the situation (be it combat or a puzzle), but I often find Arcane and Ice to be the best overall (atleast at this point in early access). Chances are you won't end up using melee on your first playthrough very much, it can be intimidating to get close to bosses and enemies when you're new, but it's a good way to get mana when you run out. You can melee enemies in their dying animation for free mana as well. There's also an upgrade system, I found Intelligence, Mana, Health and Stamina to be the most valuable upgrades personally.There is currently 3 boss battles and a 4th bonus one. All of them were very satisfying to fight and overall didn't feel too unfair with the exception of the third one until you learn some tricks. The Counter system in this game (equivalent to parrying in Dark Souls I guess) is very addicting to pull off due to it requiring very tight timing, only thing is that it is slightly op since it provides temporarily invincibility, mana regen/faster spell charge and also health regen if you receive hits during the invincibility. If you master the counter spell, it does mitigate alot of the game's difficulty, so I kind of hope to see it nerfed in some way in the future.Something worth noting is that the English translation is a bit poor at some bits, but usually enough to get the general idea. Something that may have gotten lost in translation however is the fact that the ice spell while charged can lock onto multiple targets then released. Without this info, many people get stuck on the puzzle immediately afterwards.Oh and the difficulty options used to be named Easy and Normal but now they're called Standard and Advanced which implies that Standard (Easy) is the recommended difficulty which it definitely should not be. It makes Nobeta a HUGE sponge and your mana will not run out as easy and this removes basically ANY challenge from the game. Don't really have anything else to say. Fantastic little game, I can't wait for the full version. Support the developer. Happy loli witching.P.S. I've only played the first Dark Souls game and it never really appealed to me, but I was able to greatly enjoy this game regardless, so hopefully the comparison doesn't put you off. I don't think it's even nearly as difficult as Dark Souls.P.P.S. Ignore the bad reviews or people claiming it's an abandonware scam. The game appeared on Steam unfinished as Early Access at first with plans for the game to get updated with the full rest of the game when it is finished. For some reason people live under rocks and don't follow news or they expect Early Access means regular content updates for some reason when in reality it just means an unfinished game that is still in development.After beating the full game most of my points stand however they did a price increase and I do think the game is a tad pricey for how short it is, so do keep that in mind. Early Access was a more realistic price. Most of the game from EA seems untouched progression-wise.I'll start off singing some praises. New levels were quite gorgeous especially the later ones. New music was nice and the music layers in certain levels (where it adds in part of the music when you enter a large main area) were a nice touch. Sad that the some of the OG music is gone though (rip old cave music).Collectables also a nice touch. Gives you an excuse to break every barrel and pot and they have some background lore if that's your thing. Achievements too. Speaking of, some achievements will give you costumes which are a lovely addition! I recommend the Sailor outfit for obvious reasons (If you know, you know).Story was a bit predictable and kinda cliche, but it's ok for what it is. Nothing ground breaking or anything, but it's enough to keep your attention. A few twists here and there. Voice acting was an excellent addition. Hololive VA's did fine as far as I could tell and Nobeta is absolutely adorable (and cute and funny etc.)Unfortunately one of my fears came true where most of the mid to end game becomes thunder magic spam. That magic is truly too overpowered and it doesn't help that they add alot of long range enemies to encourage just sniping everything before even getting close. It also lets you cheese bosses with the slow-mo followed by the huge AOE blast. Last boss was especially anti-climactic while slowed by charged thunder constantly lol. Ice magic + parrying also still dominates the early game bosses (especially Monica) as usual. I guess the ability to cheese things just naturally comes with featuring ranged shooty combat and is unavoidable.All-in-all it's enjoyable for what it is. Just don't compare it to Dark Souls, it's very different (and far easier!) and you'll just be disappointed. Giving it a bad review for not being like Dark Souls is unfair. I just REALLY wish the game was longer. Most of the love went into the late game, so the beginning feels very short and rushed by comparison and it feels weird. I feel like the game had alot of potential, but it didn't quite realize all of it in my opinion. Game is still great fun regardless though.P.S. Screw the maid enemy that gives enemies shield buffs.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game?Yes*It's a Yes, but with a few conditions*.First, the game's Early Access is that of a Beta (on July 22th 2020). _childDocuments_.review: This game's biggest strength is how smooth the gameplay feels, especially for something with many souls elements. People loved Bloodborne for how the rally mechanic encouraged aggression, and Sekiro for the mobility and intricate combat. This game has a little bit of both of those elements in some form. Once you learn how landing melee hits regenerates mana AND speeds up your channels, as well as the ability to dodge/attack/jump/run/parry while channeling, it becomes a very satisfying experience. It isn't perfect, there is a fair bit of jank as expected of a game without a AAA budget, but I would say it's very much worth the price for the experience, in my opinion.The story is nice, you can collect over a hundred lore items that just exist to offer a bit of backstory about the world and how everything ended up the way it is, but the main story won't require you to read any of them to know what's going on. The items don't mention the characters or current events, just the world and various factions of the past. I think that's a really good touch, since dark souls in particular really required you to research and read to know who anyone was or what was really happening. It still offers that rich lore backstory while having a self-contained and satisfying story on the surface.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, well, pretty damn good.First of all, the game looks nice. The art style is sweet, and is guided by a wise art direction. Overall, the game is quite effective at communicating visually and with a stylish way.Unlike the visual department, the sound department is, in one word, lacking. Hearing one backround music only for each stage, regardless if you're just exploring, in the middle of combat, or almost getting killed, gets old very fast, considering you're supposed to spend hours on a single level. The developers are really doing the bare minimum.The gameplay is where this game truly shines. This game is very good at teaching you without too much text (and you're not forced to even open it), it's challenging, but not unreasonably punishing. The platforming segments are no Super Mario Odissey, but are quite clever.Combat is tuned very well, from the individual perks of the spells to the enemy placement (and their variety), everything is set so that you'll actually use all your options in combat, from sniping the enemies to ramming into them and beating them down with the staff. All is tied together by very thight and controls, with very little perks, like the staff attack greatly recharging the mana, or being able to cancel the obnoxiously long end lag of the last staff attack with a dodge or a spell, that really makes it flow seamlessly.Also, play in Advanced difficulty: Standard makes you a tank with passive health regenaration, with lower mana cost, and more mana regenration, while the enemies are much less resilient, it really has no difficulty to it, and this isn't the sort of game you would play for the story. I've changed my save file to Standard to get the last achievement, and I regret it, because I can't get it back to Advanced.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, you would normally look at a title like this and go "Hm, this looks like a crappy indie game purely for cash grabs." Wrong, this game is one of the most fun souls-like games I ever played. This game has a great level of polish for a project by a small dev team. So how does this game differ from all the souls-like games? Well, for starters, there are no weapons you can pick up or craft, you have one weapon. And that is your magical staff, however, you can cast magic. You can either: -Buff your melee attacks by charging up your magic-Charge up your magic to do a unique spell-Rapid fireNow your attacks don't cost stamina, but this is fine, it does not take away from the difficulty at all because you will have to focus on managing something else, and that is your mana. Your mana depletes pretty quickly depending on what type of magic you use.How do you gain back mana? Simple, you either:-Consume a mana crystal-Melee enemies-Dodge enemy attacksThe game is VERY generous with how much mana it gives you. Overall, the game is worth checking out, for 10 dollars you will get hours of fun, the enemies are challenging, the bosses are unique and you need to stategize on what type of magic you should use against them. The bosses are all easy to memorize, but hard to beat. I recommend this game to people who are new to the genre, and ESPECIALLY souls veterans. This game will test your timing windows and skills. As a souls veteran myself, I considered this game challenging. Give it a try!I really can't think of any con besides the fact that when you die, sometimes the game takes a few seconds for the respawn button to pop up. The dialogues is very roughly translated but that's pretty much it.I would give it a 9/10 . Solid indie souls-like game

_childDocuments_.review: A little on the short side at the moment, but it's quite a fun game. Running, jumping, and dodging will all burn your stamina pretty quickly, and while it recovers almost as fast, there is a penalty for attempting to run or dodge without having enough stamina to spend—the player character trips and falls flat on their face.I did not know how much I needed that as a mechanic until I witnessed it happen in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly exceeded my expectations and they were already pretty high to begin with. This game has a pretty impressive aesthetic and visual design to it, but what truly pulls you in is just how good the fighting is. The game is magic based, so most of the time you will be going around using ranged attacks, but you can opt in for pure melee if you want as you can imbue your staff with your current spell and it does more damage depending on what spell you use. You can get 4 spells throughout the game: Arcane, Ice, Fire, and Lightning. Of those 4 spells, you will also quickly learn that Arcane is absolutely useless. By the time you gain your first spell that, the game immediately shows you that arcane is outclassed. There's only one thing that Arcane is used for and that's involving barriers and you're only forced to use it 3 times throughout the entire game. Ice does more damage with less mana usage per shot, fire is a shotgun, and lightning fills the same role as arcane but better as it one-shots most enemies in the game if you get a headshot.The bosses of the game are all really fun, even the most basic one that is the tutorial boss. You may fight bosses that are similar, but no two bosses are fought the same way, so it manages to keep everything fresh. Even the worst boss in the game is really fun to fight. The only problem I have with the game is pertaining to that specific boss: Monica. She's a boss that really shouldn't be early in the game as she is considering how powerful of a boss she is. To give a good idea on how powerful she is even when taking using her gimmick to defeat her, she's harder than the final boss. With better stat balancing, she would be fine with where she is but that entire first phase of her is just not fun to fight against because she's just a health sponge.The level design in the game is probably my favorite part of the game as the levels are all really cool, especially when you're trying to 100% the game.Nobeta isn't a perfect game, but it's really good for what it is and it is a very enjoyable experience. It's not ultra long, but it has a good amount of replayability because of that fact and you could probably even do a couple of challenge runs out of this before you stop playing for the last time.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Witch Nobeta

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who rarely plays soul-like games it was quite difficult at first.Getting to know the mechanics: how to parry, dodging and attacking with melee so you can regain mana in order to keep using magic, learning bosses patterns and moves and so on. At first the map seems to be very lineal, but as you progress you will find them a bit larger and this makes for finding items and chests a bit more difficult when you backtrack to collect them. But it shouldn't be an issue given you cleared the area from enemies so it's just going back for stuff that you might have missed.Though there isn't some ideal level to beat a boss, if you die (which happened to me a lot in the first half) you can level up your stats and slightly make the fight easier. Of course, you should play in advanced mode by default, I think it's the ideal difficulty for the game to feel fair and balanced. At some point you unlock thunder magic which almost trivializes the rest of the game IMO, although you'll probably switch from magic type in certain parts due to how some enemies behave.Now, after beating game once (haven't started NG+ tho), I must say it was for what it offered a decent experience. Just wish there was more attention to props, assets and backgrounds. Nobeta and the bosses you fight had really good detail which makes the map look not as great in comparison. Nonetheless, animations, music and story were a good highlight.Here's to see what Pupuya Games will offer next.Edit: After seeing the lore videos (which I forgot to watch before this review lol), there is a HUGE story behind the throne you are looking for since the start of the game. The items you find on the way to the throne give you some hints of the story behind everything, from years before the time where the game takes place. And these videos you unlock after beating the game, revel an important backstory which that has a more mature tone of the aesthetic you see in-game.If they decide to make a sequel, I wish for the game to have the same tone as seen in the manga with that same level of "edgy" which made hooked with the story.

_childDocuments_.review: The following review has been written without having finished the game. I've been some hours into this Little Witch Nobuta and, although i havent explored so much, there are a few things that I would like to point out. First at all the game despite being an early access (as of writing this review) it's really well done. The map designs, the enemies and even Nobeta herself are all charming and beautiful. Enemy AI is pretty basic even on normal difficulty so experienced players in these sort of games can find it a bit unchallenging, though the real problem comes with dealing with a mass crowd of enemies but is still manageable.On the other hand, one of the major cons i've experienced is being unable to quickly get up back on my feet after being knocked down by an enemy, this makes impossible to escape a combo once it lands and you fall down and eat damage for free. Some skills (like magic counter) seems to be broken or not working properly or the requirements to perform it isnt quite well explained.I'll keep playing it and continue this review once i have more experience and go deeper into the game. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the demo of the game but after playing it for a bit longer and getting to the third area some issues became extremely obvious. The levelling is extremely tedious and grindy which makes the gameplay less enjoyable and the boss of the third area is extremely annoying. It starts off as a fight against a giant possessed teddy bear which has a weak spot on its chest, but if you hit it anywhere else the damage you do is negligible and when you get it down to half health its attacks leave a lingering fire effect which is most likely to do damage to you even if you dodge at the perfect time. And then after you beat that, theres a second boss fight (With no health recovery in between) against a giant doll with badly telegraphed attacks for how strong they are. For example they have an attack where they slam their hand down where you are and then sweep it across the platform to the side you dodged, however there is no cue as to when the attack is incoming so it feels really bad since you're basically being punished for not being able to predict when they attack, and just to add insult to injury, the amount of damage they do is really high and since you'll most likely be damages when going into this fight, you will die after the first or second attack. And the cherry on top of all of this is you have to fight the bear again before you even get to attempt the second fight again so you better hope you can afford more healing gems after using them all in a desperate attempt to not die.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this wishlisted from a while back and someone mentioned to me in chat today that it was out, so I figured I'd give it a try since I like witches and I'm generally a casual fan of Hololive and a few of them did VO for some of the bosses. I beat the first boss after about half an hour but the gameplay didn't really feel very satisfying to me.The gamepad controls feel a bit wooden, it seems way too easy to get locked into melee combos, and the ranged combat isn't very accurate. My assumption would be that magic attacks would aim at whatever you're locked onto but that isn't the case, spells initially always target the center of the screen, and when locked on the right stick moves the camera instead of retargetting different enemies (as is the case in Dark Souls, which I see people are making comparisons to) so it's really easy to whiff magic attacks if you don't stop and target manually before attacking, which, at least for me, breaks the flow of combat and makes it easy to stumble into an enemy and get stunlocked.I would also say the level design and music is somewhat lackluster, nothing about the first area really caught me, as a player. Maybe it gets stronger deeper into the game but for a first impression I wasn't really vibing with the game and you gotta lead with some strong content.Additionally, there's settings for this in the game but the camera distance from the player really should have defaulted to like 3 or 4 and the camera speed should also have been knocked down a couple notches. I recommend going in and changing those immediately if you are picking up the game.I ended up getting a refund since the gameplay didn't really feel all that great, I don't know if its a polish thing or what but I didn't see myself finishing it.That's about it. Like I said it didn't vibe with me but ymmv.

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't recognise my DS4 inputs properly despite saying it supports it though, furthermore after trying several different ways to start the game and use my controller either it spammed Left/Right inputs and made it impossible to set anything in the options menu, or my cursor got stuck going up forever. Trying to set controls up at all also got my inputs swapped, I.E. X was Square, O was X, etc. How the ♥♥♥♥ does that happen? I hope that gets fixed, it's really annoying. I did get to play it anyway though, with mouse and keyboard which is better for it anyway since it's essentially a third person shooter, and what I have played of it so far is really good. There's some jank here and there, you can get stunlocked easily but it's easy enough to get out of that and fight back. You also have a lot of health to work with and lots of ways to regain it, like the magic parry you get after a bit, so it kinda balances itself out but ideally that would just not be a problem in the future.What IS a problem though is the explosions in the lava area. The death cutscene takes at least 10 seconds to happen and with the janky eruption hitboxes it's really easy to die and have to walk back all the way. That's not good, it's very frustrating. I would personally have liked it if you didn't just die instantly but were teleported back to the nearest "safe" platform with some health reductions ala Sekiro, and only die if the % of health that would be taken off were in the kill zone. Otherwise good game so far, but it needs some work.Edit: Well, I got to the lava boss. ♥♥♥♥ this game actually. It's basically the Iron King but it's a giant loli and somehow far worse. I'm taking away my recommendation because this thing has a ton of health, has an arena that crumbles away when she hits it, and throws you into lava to instantly die. Her hitboxes are massive, and they're janky as all ♥♥♥♥, lingering extremely long after she seems to have stopped moving, and hell all of them seem to be specifically designed to cause a 1shot. Since the hitboxes and timings in this game are so off dodging them properly is nearly impossible, inevitably landing you in the lava and then causing a 10 second death scene, a walk back to the fight, and a repeat. I was worried this game would flip and turn into Dark Souls 2 sooner or later given how heals work, and there it is. It's such fundamentally flawed and bad design I can't even excuse it because it's Early Access because it informs the mentality of the developers, this is their idea of difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: I feel like a serious review of a game with this theme is extremely difficult, mentally, but I want the developers to know this is actually good and not just a lolicon draw. A comparison of this game to the souls series is almost laughable, and not in a negative sense. The game is 'souls-like,' employing many mechanics directly from dark souls, but it plays almost nothing like it. A single enemy, and not even a boss enemy, can give you a sense of dread in souls games. Little Witch Nobeta has you dreading the situation, not the enemies; it is also much more technically demanding, and plays at speeds closer to traditional action games than souls games later down the road. The game beautifully melds its core fighting mechanics in ways that forces you to use each in tandem to grow in skill; however, each core fighting mechanic could be considered entirely different gameplay styles as well. The game is best played while constantly switching between styles of play, as well as tactics benefiting each style of play depending on each situation, which is why you dread the situations. All valid tactics are preemptive, and situations can completely counter some devised tactics.I recommend this game because, when you're good at games, the vast variety of playstyles available to you allows you to play with overwhelming tactics and skill.
