_childDocuments_.review: September 07, 2023:As of this new boss rush update, I can no longer enjoy this game at all. My old review for the early access is down at the bottom, but clearly the developers are incredibly lazy and love to hate their long-time players.I already had issues with how the later parts of the game felt rehashed and reused from what was already available in early access, but this update takes the cake both in that regard and being horrible. The boss rush mode is 100% reused content. They reused the arenas in entirety, not even properly blocking them off since there's no form of progression, and the ones they did block off have bugs where you can get caught in walls.All of the bosses in the mode have new mechanics. They are not good mechanics. The first boss is mostly the same, but has more HP, more damage, and when you get it below 50% HP it's an MMO-style enrage where he spams the same attacks over and over to kill you. The second boss punishes dodging even more than before with one of her follow up attacks. The third boss has gone from a skill check to an RNG check because if you're unlucky you can get the same half-map attack back-to-back leading to an unavoidable death from nowhere to stand and you can't stay airborne that long. The fourth boss had his absorb timings changed and made it to where you can only start absorb with the first hit of each attack while the second hits go through walls, he's faster and he has hard coded combos that keep going even if you die. The fifth boss has completely and totally reused animations and tells for her new attacks making avoiding her a guess in the dark.This is the definition of a bad update. Crapping on your older players with reused content, changed timings despite same animations, and new attacks using the same animations leaving you guessing. To further lock things behind a perfect run of this mode despite the clear RNG element is cruel. I was already unexcited for this update because getting 100% was tedious as it was, they added the achievement removing that 100% months before making the content available, and it's *bad* content.Old:As someone who is unable to enjoy Souls or Souls-like games in general, I took a shot at this game due to having a general interest in "Anime Souls" games, and this being "Loli Souls" with a focus on magic helped drag me to it. The game, at the current time, is pretty short. At about US$10 during Early Access, I definitely feel like there's plenty of content for the price when compared to many other games that are available today. There's roughly 3 bosses and one bonus boss. I would say that, for something revered as a Souls-like, it's not necessarily that difficult. The largest issue would be the balance itself. If you're playing on Standard, and you don't have a lot of experience with action type games, you may have some slight difficulty, but by the time you've cleared what's currently available you'll likely be left feeling a little unfulfilled.On Advanced, however, the balance is a little bit off I feel. There's not a huge variety of enemies yet, and because of this once you learn their attack patterns, they become pretty simple to defeat. Your primary way of fighting is with spells, with melee being supplemental by regening mana and charging your spells more quickly. Dodging an enemy attack is more forgiving than countering them in that if you miss the exact timing, it's still possible to avoid damage, but simply get no restore. Meanwhile if you miss a counter, there's a very good chance you'll be stunned and pummeled. Currently in Early Access I've only really seen 2 enemies that you basically have to know they're there to survive them, or otherwise be prepared for them. Both of these enemies are placed prior to the second boss. They're not necessarily difficult enemies, just with other things going on at the time if you're not aware of their presence, you're likely to die, meanwhile knowing they're there you're likely to kill them before they even know you're there. For the spells, there's only 4 elements currently available, but the variety still feels pretty solid. Each spell has 3 types of effects: Uncharged, Charged and Aura. Uncharged is exactly as it says on the tin - It's an instantly launched attack that generally does lesser damage. Charged is, also, as it says on the tin - an attack that has to be charged up and during the charge time you can't cast any other spells, and slows you down for its duration. Aura, however, is different. Once you've fully charged a spell, you gain effects until you either choose to shoot it, or until its Aura dissipates.As things stand, it seems that Arcane is the weakest of the bunch. It has similar charge times and cost to the others, but does a lot less damage and has lesser range. I was also unsure as to what precisely its Aura did. Ice is definitely among one of my favorites. Ice uncharged attack is very fast, although low damage, and is great for taking out weaker enemies. Its Aura causes a type of "super armor" that will reduce your damage taken and reduce your chance of being stunned. While charged, and you must learn this to progress at one point, you can "target" various enemies and objects that it will hit when you finally decide to shoot it. Fire, however, is where things get interesting. Fire's uncharged shoots out 3 projectiles that can hit fairly randomly if you're not both locked on and aiming, that does about equivalent damage to each projectile from Ice for a similar cost. When fully charged its shoot becomes a single, large projectile that explodes on contact, damaging nearby targets. The interesting part of Fire is its Aura. While its Aura is active your melee attack becomes faster and surrounded in Fire, causing it to do more damage.Lightning I didn't play with a whole lot. I had only gotten it on Standard and had felt the difficulty for Standard was too low, but then never made it that far on Advanced, but it looks like a pretty neat targeted Area of Effect (AoE) spell in a way that the others are all lacking.Graphically speaking, the game is beautiful, like many others made with Unity. However turning the resolution down from native will cause a lot of aliasing, and furthermore the only "Fullscreen" option appears to be "Borderless", which may make it harder for some that can't obtain full framerate at their native resolution due to the nature of dodging and countering. My only true graphical gripe would be that, and this is still Early Access, many areas don't seem to match aesthetically, but being an anime game this is pretty normal anyways.The music thus far has been pretty solid. It has felt mostly fitting, and even changes some if you're fighting. I noticed the settings menu contained a "Voices" volume, but I never noticed any voice acting, so I assume this may be planned for the future.In the grand scheme of things, I would suggest this game both for people who do and don't enjoy Souls-like games. If you're not used to action games, if you go on Standard and grind enemies a bit you can pretty much clear everything fairly easily. If you are used to action games, I would highly suggest Advanced due to the higher difficulty. There's plenty of content right now, more than most games would offer at this price nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this with just over two hours of playtime and after having cleared the first major area, defeating two bosses in the progress. Consider these my first impressions rather than a full review.So far, I am very impressed with the effort put into the game. While it is clearly a budget game, as made clear by the cutscenes lacking voice acting and the copy-pasted environments, the visuals are still servicable, as is the audio.Where the game truly shines is in the gameplay, which feels responsive and impactful, and is very unique in how it handles combat.A lot of people have compared it to Dark Souls, and not without reason, though as others have pointed out, it more closely resembles Bloodborne. Just like in the Soulsborne series, you gain experience by defeating enemies that can then be spent at a rest point to increase your various attributes. Likewise, enemies hit hard, and you have a stamina system that depletes when you dodge attacks or perform certain other actions. Dying sends you back to the last rest point you used.Where this game stands out, however, is with its magic system. Rather than Mana being a finite resource like in some Soulsborne games, you have an infinite supply here, though you have to actively work to regain it after spending it. Hitting an enemy with a melee attack will deal absolutely pitiful damage, comparable to striking while unarmed in Soulsborne games, but it will refill your Mana gauge, which lets you use your much more powerful ranged attacks. While I find this idea very neat, it is somewhat impractical in its execution, I find. To put this into perspective, imagine if in Bloodborne, every time you attacked with your weapon, you would deplete a bar specific to weapon attacks, and the fastest way to recover that bar would be to hit the enemy with unarmed attacks. It is possible this issue will be mitigated later in the game, but for now, melee attacks primary feel like a really slow, risky reload to my primary method of attacking.That's not to say the combat is bad, however. Far from it. A feature that I am absolutely in love with is the dodge cancelling. Almost any animation in the game can be cancelled into a dodge at any point, except for another dodge. This means that you will never feel like you're trapped in the recovery of a move, since you can simply dodge out of it. This even extends to completely silly things, such as the animation where Nobeta stands up after restarting from a checkpoint being dodge-cancellable, or the animation of her stumbling after jumping from too great a height.If you're interested, I'd highly recommend giving it a try. The difficulty can be off-putting if you're not used to games that will unapologetically wipe the floor with you at times - I spent a good ten or so attempts at just the second boss - but it can be incredibly rewarding to overcome such hurdles and triumph at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta, is a game with No Beta. As opposed to its older brother, Big Sorcerer YesAlpha which is a very early access alpha prototype that never actually got out of it's alpha stage. If you thought that joke was stupid, at least I'm not calling it LoliSouls. In fact, here's 15 other names that could replace LoliSouls; Witchsouls, Witchborne, ERatedDarksouls, BrightSouls, FBITrapSouls, ThisDevUsedToMakeHGameSouls, EarlyAccessSouls, BrightGreySouls, CastleSouls!, She's12BTWSouls, Dark(Magic Build only)Souls, LittleWitchAcademia:TheGameSouls, BokunoLittleWitchAcademiaSouls, I'mRunningOutOfIdeasSouls, OhGodwhyDidIPromise15OfTheseSouls, and HowManyDidIPromiseAgain?Souls. I have no idea why I wrote all of that, but there you go. Now stop calling it LoliSouls.That being said, contrary to the name, Little Witch Nobeta is still in beta. 3/6 out of all the planned stages are completed, there are 3+1 boss available currently (more to come), and some bugs here and there. Now, I won't be fully reviewing this game, at least not yet. I don't eat cookies while it's still a dough and I much rather wait for it to be baked even if it's gonna take a whole year (or two) to do so. If you're pondering whether or not to buy the game, just play the demo and see whether or not you like it. It's very much a souls-like, although with a lot more Jrpg element to it (more character driven, no character customization, and non realist artsyle) and you're stuck playing mage. There will come a time when we stop comparing everysingle thirdperson RPG/JRPG that has a windup animation to darksouls. Remember, we used to call everysingle FPS game a Doom-clone, but the change to calling it an FPS took a decade. Anyway, that's as much I'm willing to talk about this game. Again, Not super into the idea of playing a story driven game when you know it's not finsihed, play the demo to see whether or not you like it. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: During the game's Early Access period, I decided to recommend the game based on the state, content, and price of the product at that time. Having finally gotten around to playing the full release, some 2+ years later, I feel the need to make it clear that I don't recommend it now.To begin with, the content that was in the EA version is pretty much completely unchanged from what was available years ago, with two exceptions:- Voice acting- An overabundance of collectibles scattered throughout the entire gameAside from that, technical problems and all, it remains the same.Moving on, let's talk about the content that was added. I'd say roughly 60% more game was added for the full release, but this 60% is at best equal to and in many cases worse in quality than what was already there. The levels, design-wise and visually, don't make any real leaps, but towards the end of the game it outright repeats some early game areas.Enemy variety is absent from the expanded content. I can think of one distinctly new enemy, who appears in one particular level (where there are quite a few of them, I like them, but it got annoying having 1-3 around every corner real fast), while the rest are just recolors. The colors typically denote the element they use, but not really, since the thunder enemies are blue when blue is used for ice magic, and yellow for thunder.Apart from that, we have bosses and minibosses. Starting with the minibosses, they're just bosses in every aspect except having a health bar plastered on screen. They have full arenas, they're unique to other enemies in the game, they have roughly equivalent levels of health to a boss, I think it's entirely possible they just forgot to add the health bar. The bosses that are distinctly bosses...well, they've gotten rather dull from the uniquely-presented ones in the EA version. The game's final boss even . I would also like to say that some of the boss fights drag on, are poorly placed, and have excessive but unchallenging movesets.Lastly, the game offers a NG+ mode. The scaling on NG+ enemies seems pretty excessive, however, as those who would go down in 2 shots in NG take 4-5 in NG+, regardless of my pumping everything into damage throughout NG. It makes NG+ a bore, above everything.Overall, the quality of EA vs post-EA content is pretty clear, with the EA content being generally better. Considering the price hike, as well as the dubious practices of the development studio in spending a not-insubstantial amount on manga adaptations, merchandise, and publicity, when the game clearly would have benefited from an increased budget, makes me lean towards putting a nail in Nobeta's coffin, despite having high hopes for the game.Early Access Review:

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. The focus on ranged combat is fun and it requires a good amount of positioning and knowledge of your enviroment to be effective at it. If I had a few criticisms it would be the patterns the boss's attacks, particularly phase 1 Monica who can sometimes ground slam 4 times in a row. I also feel like arcane is completely outclassed by the other spells and needs some buffs or a bit of a rework so that it has its own niche. Ice on the other hand feels a bit too impactful in terms of damage and crowd control, while also being the best element to use on the majority of bosses. I would suggest focusing on ice's niche as a crowd control tool rather than have it do so much damage.Overall, despite these criticisms, I had a lot of fun with this game and I definitely felt rewarded for getting good at it. I look forward to further updates and a completed release.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was fun enough, the way most of the magic types function are all different enough to have different uses though some of them reach a point during the game where there's little reason to use the others.  The leveling doesn't really feel important, you can't really go for different builds, but it's there.  Most of the enemies are rather forgettable but the bosses standout and some of them were genuinely fun while some were misses.  It'd be fun to be able to just fight the bosses, but the Boss Rush mode is somehow not what you'd want if that's what you're looking for.Advanced Mode and Boss Rush aren't even REMOTELY similar in terms of difficulty.  Boss feels more like It's 2 difficulty levels higher than Advanced, which is the only difficulty other than Easy.Your level is fixed so you can't gain any stats, you have to buy all your magic upgrades, which are kind of expensive, and the only way to get currency other than killing a boss (which you can only do once because you can't rechallenge ones you beat) is performing parries, casts in under 1 second, and casting in melee range, and those only give like, 3 souls per, when the first tier of certain spells have costs in the 90's.  The bosses have WAY more health, are faster, hit harder, have changes to their timing, and have new moves.  Some bosses are vastly harder than others, and it's not a steady increase in difficulty. It honestly feels like it was made by an entirely different group of people with wildly different design philosophies.Overall though I would recommend the game as something to binge through, a playthrough I'd say should be roughly between 8-11 hours in total depending on if you get stuck on a boss or not, the game (aside from boss rush) is pretty fair in its difficulty, and playing around with the different types of magic was fun.  Also the bear kigurumi is the best outfit other than the default, fight me.

_childDocuments_.review: *Review edited*NOT RECOMMEND FOR NOW.The dev seems to care more about the hentais of the characters than actual updates of the game. Check their official twitter, there are barely any updates about gameplay.---------------------This game is a good example of an amazing RPG. For a game this size, its combat system is really well fleshed out. At the time of writing this review I have unlocked all achievements except one that requires NG+3, won't be long till I finish it. Note that I played the game in Chinese so there might be some difference in vocabulary.First, the stages and puzzles are decently designed and I especially like the  a lot. I won't say much about the lack of mob variety for now since it's still in early access. The really memorable parts are Tania's boss room, which the dolls in the background really fits her atmosphere and theme; and the moving platform area, which felt like a Rambo one man army scene with bullets flying from all directions.Second, the bosses are easily the best part of the game. I don't have much complaints about them, pretty much all their attacks are well choreographed and balanced... except for Monika's Phase 1 mini fireball pokes. These lingering ranged attacks create a situation where if you had to dodge them, you might get roll-caught by the boss. It's really frustrating when that happens. I have one more problem with the bosses which I'll get into in the combat part.Third, the combat. The four elements that you can obtain in the playthrough are simple yet distinct enough to make you think twice before choosing which to use. The spells can be leveled up by looting their copies in treasure chests, though I find the power scaling of the spells to be really poor, but there isn't enough content in one NG run currently to make this feel really obvious, I only felt this way because I went to NG++. I've noticed some problems with three of the spells in the game.Arcane, the spell you start with. It introduces itself as a mid-long range artillery shot, and the charged attack can be used twice starting from Level 2. It's damage falls off heavily in the end game. Two shots of Arcane charged attack has less damage than a Lighting basic attack. It's pretty disappointing considering that the two copies to max level Arcane are hidden behind puzzles that reward more observant players. Fire, the third spell you obtain at the third stage of the game. You won't encounter any issues with this spell in a single run because you can only raise it up to level 2 in a single playthrough, you need NG+ to max it at level 3. The level 3 of Fire is pretty much a downgrade. Before level 3, the charged attack is a useful explosion that staggers enemies, but at level 3, the charged attack does a lingering combustion before exploding, which means it doesn't stagger enemies on hit anymore, making the spell totally useless because enemies can just run out of the explosion radius.Lighting is a secret spell that you can obtain after you beat the extra stage boss. The charged attack is a lightning strike which you can aim with a circle on the floor. With the camera angle, aiming this feels quite clunky but it still gets the job done. Here's the real problem with the lightning spell, There's a specific interaction with the extra boss' dash double spin slash attack with the lightning spell. At normal speed, that attack can be dodged with a single roll. Having full charge lightning slows everything else, which doubles the time of that attack, and 2 rolls are needed to dodge it, but that's not the problem. When you roll dodge attacks, the game gives you mana and enter a slight slowmode, right? If your spell full charges from dodging the first attack, you'll still have to roll for a second time to dodge the second since you've entered full charge mode. Because the mana required to enter full charge won't be the same everytime, timing the second dodge is unnecessarily difficult, in addition to that the initial dodge will also slow your character. Well, counter magic is an option, but it shouldn't be the only option. And also you'll have to relearn the timing for counter magic in slowmode since only the boss is slowed yet your attack frame time still remains the same...Counter magic is easily one of the most fun mechanics in this game, but the explanation of this mechanic in the game is quite vague and honestly a little inaccurate. It actually only activates when you're in your attack frame while the target's hitbox collides with yours. Also the interaction with full charge lightning's slowmode...Other than the problems listed, it's a really neat indie game that I had a ton of fun playing. I'd recommend this to anyone who loves games with a difficult learning curve. The game being really cheap is also a big plus, grab this and try it out if you haven't! That concludes my review, thanks for reading.Huh? What do you mean I haven't talked about the character designs? They're really cute, yeah... (god lolis are amazing)Wait I hear someone knocking on my doEdit: As of right now (19.5hrs played) I've gotten all of the current achievements! I've complained about the lightning slowmode problem but I "got gud" and my workaround was to not charge the lightning until after I dodge the attack and charge it with the airborne mana blobs. I'm not gonna say that the slowmode problem is a bug, for now I'll just assume it being a realism "your tools don't always work in your favor" thing or just an in development spell.

_childDocuments_.review: Screw the angry wumao review-bombing this because of the legal notice containing "Taiwan is a Country", and because some Hololive VTubers are doing VA.This game is cute and fun, and no australian nanny state shill full of 50 year old catladies upset over being lards or CCP genocide denying bootlicker is going to get in the way of gaming becoming great again.EDIT: Now that I finished the game, I have quite a few thoughts on it.It's a pretty fun game with some Dark Souls adjacent gameplay mechanics and level design structure. The game doesn't really open up until you get the lightning ability, but the movement mechanics are pretty fun to play around with when you do.It's a bit on the short side, but 12 hours or so for something that still feels rather focused without much bloat is still pretty good considering the budget (or lack thereof) for this game.The only gameplay related things that bothered me was how cheap the AI behaved, and the over the shoulder camera, which frankly is a trend that needs to die in third-person games already outside of a few scenarios where it actually feels appropriate (like a horror game).There is indeed plenty of cute characters in this game. I personally think Monika is adorable.Some of the videos that are unlocked after you finish the game were reportedly censored, but the developers at least put up the uncensored versions somewhere, which shouldn't be that hard to find.As for technical and PC version related issues, the most that I can really say:* The game has hardcoded resolution options. From my time investigating this game with external modding tools, it would be very easy for them to get that working with some small UI related tweaks, and even have support for ultrawide displays and even resolutions narrower than 16:9.* A lack of some scalability/quality settings and forced MSAA out of the box (this can at least be worked around easily with mods).  * The game doesn't really give you the option of PlayStation button prompts.* Hair physics can be a bit juddery above 50FPS (due to physics updates being done with FixedUpdate without transform interpolation), but you can also easily work around this with external modding tools pretty easily without anything noticeable being affected. That part isn't a huge issue, but I figured I'd note it here, as plenty of Unity games have more egregious problems with using FixedUpdate incorrectly.* The strange default keybindings, but you can at least rebind those. The game feels really good to play on Keyboard and Mouse afterwards.Outside of those few things, I can say that it's serviceable. It works on the Steam Deck with very minimal slowdown issues, pretty close to a locked 60FPS. As for my main rig, I'm easily getting over 240FPS at 3440x1440 with high settings on a RX 6900XT and i5-13600K, which is plenty for a game like this. I need to do some testing on my gaming laptop with a 360Hz display to see how that fares.Anyways, in terms of most of those technical issues, and the game's camera, I've managed to make a patch (using BepInEx) to patch those few things, which I'll have available (alongside source code) pretty soon.I'd recommend the game, it's an easy 8/10 for me. _childDocuments_.review: My playtime is not accurate because reasons. For $9 and what I presume is a solo dev (or at least a very small team from Taiwan), this is a pretty solid base for a cute action witch simulator so far. The combat takes some getting used to, but once you do it becomes fun and fluid. The magic feels nice and meaty, Megumin would probably be satisfied. The game avoids the trap of just spamming magic missile everywhere by letting you recharge mana via liberal application of your staff onto the skulls of enemies, and dodging. There's also a parry function which has a small window, but is very rewarding (think Royal Guard from DMC). However, the counter is also a bit game-breaking, as once you get the timing down you're pretty much invincible since it also recharges your health and mana. So that will need tweaking. I also recommend rebinding the keyboard controls, and playing with MB+M instead of a controller.The environments and enemies aren't too interesting at the moment. Enemies are just black shadow blobs who almost seem like filler enemies, since the bosses have way more design and effort put into them. The environment so far is a castle with a few other areas that have lava, glowing mushrooms, etc. to spice things up. The bosses are hard, but I don't want the dev to make them easier -- just git gud. There are also a lot of small details put into the game, such as idle animations, falling flat on your face when you try running or dodging with no stamina left, hidden shortcuts that give you magic upgrades, etc. The English translations is iffy in some parts as well, but not enough to bother me while playing. I'd also like more staff varieties, magic, some more outfits to wear (it seems the dev intends on implementing this), and just small quality of life improvements that have probably already been mentioned elsewhere.Overall there's a base for a decent, even good, game to come out of this. One of the better demos I played during the Steam Demo Festival. However, since it's very much early access (roadmap says it'll probably be 1-2 years), there's no harm in waiting if you have a backlog (aside from the dev needing money I suppose). It has some bugs that need to be ironed out (such as being able to fly across the entire map if you swing your staff mid-air, and being able to bypass invisible walls by exploiting the super armor that the Ice ability gives you -- I can see a speedrunning community quickly forming around this game). For $9, I definitely got my money's worth. I'm looking forward to this game's development.Also Tania is the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly smooth combat. Great dodging, very well telegraphed attacks, and a mana/spell charging system combined with a health-restoring counter-attack make it so that you can always stay in a fight as long as you stay alert. If that sounds too easy, don't worry. The game is actually reasonably difficult on Normal mode, with the third boss in particular being quite brutal.Exploration is rewarded with upgraded spells that add new unique effects. Nobeta is able to sprint, double-jump, and hover in the air while attacking. It's a little Souls, but also a little Devil May Cry, a little Vanquish, and a little Hat in Time. The controls for every aspect of the game: the dodge/stab melee combat, the third person shooter magical combat, and the mobility options, all feel like they were polished to the point where I would play a shooter or a platformer as Nobeta without hesitation.At the time of this review the game takes about 6 hours to complete, and around 10-12 hours to get all of the achievements. Rather than having a lot of unfinished content like many Early Access games, Little Witch Nobeta has a moderate amount of very well-made content. It's not perfect...  But there is an extremely solid foundation here, and if the rest of the game follows the standard of this Early Access release, this game honestly deserves to be among the top action games ever made. It holds up very well compared to some of the most popular games in the genre, and even though I said it was short, it is actually about as long as some fully-released action games of the past. Most of them take around 10 hours or less to complete, and Nobeta is around that time frame already with only 3 of the planned 6 levels currently released. I would absolutely recommend this game whole-heartedly. It is a hidden gem that I hope doesn't stay hidden for very long.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta surprised me outta the blue by just being a pretty fun spell slinging 'souls-like' (for lack of a better term) with a decent amount of bite behind it. My first run not including demo time took around 7-8 hours to beat, with an additional 5 hours to 100% what is currently available in the Early Access period. Which for £7.19 or so I really don't think is too shabby at all.Game looks nice, runs buttery smooth and has decent mouse and keyboard customisation options and generally just performs really nicely.The game it's self has a rather cute little charm to it coming from the character designs and soundtrack, while the dialogue it's self sounds a bit more stilted it still conveys well enough but could do with some more polish and personality to more of the characters. Although given the size of the project as well as the budget they had before release ya can't really fault them for it.Gameplay it's self as well is quite nice and well rounded, spells feel nice to use and cast with their powered versions feel varied in use as well as appropriately powerful, with staff attacks regenerating mana it makes for quite a nice flow in combat with mobs and bosses alike. Exploration is rewarded by chests that give consumable items as well as grimoires to unlock/ level up your existing abilities. Once you start getting more grimoires to unlock new abilities such as double jumps, counter attacks as well as new castable spells it really starts to pick up steam and I really hope they look at adding additional spells down the line as they are by far the funnest things you can unlock.The game's not without some gripes though, enemy variety is a little low right now, there's a good amount of them but just a couple more types would do wonders for encounters. That and the level's are a little bit bland in terms of hazards and such, while I never found myself getting lost due to recognisable landmarks and rooms I did find running through the empty hallways wasted more time than it should've during my second and third runs. While the game does seem to have the early half at most of the game so it's understandable balance wise, future levels could do with some more traps or general hazards that'd keep you on your toes. (The fire Temple's fire geysers is about the closest the game gets right now)Overall It's honestly just a really solid little indie game and I can only hope the future for it is bright, really looking forward to what the game will be like coming out the other side of Early Access. Definitely can Recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't trust early access games, but for ten dollars this game delivers a fun, challenging, sometimes frustrating, but completely rewarding experience. It's been called the "Dark Souls of loli witch games", and while I've never played a Dark Souls game before, I'd be inclined to agree. The enemies are unforgiving (no invincibility frames when you get hit), the timing for dodging and parrying is tight, and you can easily go from full health to dead in three seconds if you're caught in a bad place.Now, that may not sound like a positive point, but death isn't too much of an inconvenience. Current levels aren't too large or complicated, so you can easily get from the last check point to where you died in under a minute if you remember the way and rush past or know how to defeat the respawned enemies. You keep your items, learned spells too, and your experience points aren't affected unless you used a cursed item; even if you did, the penalty isn't too bad unless you used a lot of them (curses stack).You don't have to die though. All enemies have attack patterns and telegraphs, some visual and some audio, and exploiting these with skilled play means you can take them out even faster than they can you. For instance, a charged spell will grant you a beneficial aura and can be fired for tremendous damage, but your move speed is at least halved while you're charging. You can charge them before entering combat, but you can also quicken the charge by absorbing mana drops, hitting with melee attacks, precisely dodging enemy attacks, or by parrying. Parrying will instantly charge the spell, usually knocks the enemy back, and gives you a second of invincibility while you're doing the parry animation. With good reaction speed, the right knowledge of enemy attack telegraphs and some forethought, you can chain parries and charge spells until your enemies are reduced to dust.You can do other things too: snipe them from across the room, knock them off ledges or into lava pits, bash their brains in with your staff, blast them with close range standard spells, etc. The game gives you different tools for dealing with the same encounter, and tries to throw curve balls every now and then to keep you on your toes.Replayability is pretty good for an early access game: finishing the current levels allows you to play a NG+ with enemies that hit harder and have more health while retaining Nobeta's stats and magic levels. Books that granted you access to new magic can be recollected to level that magic up, although some of the magic can be maxed out (at lvl. 3) in your first playthough if you find the chests where copies are kept. Beating the extra dungeon at the end will grant lightning magic; I don't want to spoil what that does, but it is 100% worth, especially if you want to run through the game multiple times. It also only spawns once per playthough, so you'll need to do two NG+ games to max it out.There's more that can be said, but I think the gameplay is strong enough to carry any flaws the game might have at this stage. Definitely worth more than $10; I'm happy about this purchase even if the devs are unable to deliver on the promise they show here because the game is fun right now.Also, Nobeta, Tania, and Monica are adorable. And after facing Scissor Doll LITERALLY DOZENS of times on my way from the statue to rematch the last boss on my first playthrough, I feel a connection with her, like she's more of an elder sister than an enemy. I can't hate her, even when she murders me after I mess up my parries.I'm going to run through the game one more time before putting it down and patiently waiting for the next installment. Good work so far, Pupuya Games!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Solid souls-like game on the forgiving side, one of the spells feels designed for game journalists, simple graphics with cute animations, good art direction, good voice acting and the overall OST is very good with two or three gems in particular. Absolutely recommended.I would recommend playing on "Advanced" difficulty rather than "Standard". Despite the misleading names, "Standard" is what you would call Easy mode, and you really don't wanna play that. I'm saying this as someone who absolutely sucks at the genre.On the gameplay side, it presents itself as a regular souls-like game. You dodge, you whack, you parry. The spell chanting gimmick is fun and gives the gameplay loop a good feel, rewarding people for going out of their way to play stylishly.The various spells are fun to use and all have their job and fun factor. I love the lock on on Ice, and Fire and Thunder hurting yourself if you're too close is a nice and funny touch and adds a strategic element to these otherwise overpowered spells.Thunder is honestly a spell that shouldn't exist and completely invalidates all enemies and bosses the moment you get it. I feel like instead of slowing down time they could've just given a movement speed buff and maybe lower stamina usage in order to keep the "Im fast as ♥♥♥♥ boiii" element of the spell and it would've been just fine.The graphics are simple, but that's a not a bad thing. What really matters is the art direction, and the game is excellent on that front. The animations are adorable to the point of running out of stamina on purpose.The voice acting is good. Even as a vtuber fan I initially saw casting vtubers for some of the roles as purely a marketing move, but I have to say Fubuki and Polka REALLY nailed their roles. It goes without saying that Konomi Kohara (Roxy Migurdia, Chika Fujiwara) is the best voice actor they could have picked for Nobeta.The story is largely predictable since the hints they drop are far too big to qualify as mere hints, but it didn't detract from the enjoyment as I liked the execution. In souls-like fashion the world has a lot of hidden and interesting lore, and several pieces of content outside the game to expand on it.The game has a lot of good ambient music, and a couple excellent boss tracks. I'm probably gonna keep listening to the credits song until I hate it.I'm really hoping we'll see a sequel as there is so much that can be done with the world it set up.

There was a Day 1 error within an hour of drop, and they posted everywhere letting everyone know there was a known issue they were working on. Minimal and not game breaking. The progress of the game now?When I found this game, Monica was the final fight available. Now that we have the full story, the scope is exciting and thrilling to see. The game has a fun, dynamic engine to play around with in the magic system, and it feels extremely satisfying to play around with Nobeta in the world.You're rewarded for adventuring around and looking about to see what the world has to offer you, and the game is not afraid to punch you down for messing up. At the easier difficulties its not bad, mainly just learning the mechanics. But if you go for the more intense difficulties, the game has no problem punishing the Crap out of you for messing up and that's greatly appreciated in a world where this is either frowned upon, or taken to the other extreme like in the form of Dark Souls. It feels like a healthy balance. Deaths don't feel cheap or cheated, just that your moves are polished enough.Each magic has good uses and never falls off of usefulness throughout gameplay (though you can easily take a preference of specific magic and then take that one to town). My personal preference is to using a mix of Lightning and Fire.Final Remark: The game is not perfect, but for what it's brought to the table and the team providing us with updates the way they have, the game is pretty dang close. I would recommend this to any fan of Dungeon Crawling, Magical systems, Adventure or Action, and RPGs. It is an amazing game, and I can't wait to see what more may be in store for the future.

_childDocuments_.review: First, for ten dollars I'd definitely recommend it. It's nice and enjoyable for the most part, the bosses can be interesting, the story does make you a bit curious, the style of gameplay is unique enough to feel interesting but close enough to others that you can still jump into it and enjoy it without too much time.The core movement still feels a little slow, lacking recover and smooth blending between some actions, so it does feel like there's room for improvement, but it is overall pretty good and once you get the counter spell and double jump and raise your stamina enough to not trip over your own feet every couple seconds, turns into a solid game that you can work with and you stop feeling like your character is getting in the way, though coming from souls or other games she will feel really slow and bad at first (hey, she's a little kid, it's not like it doesn't make sense and it does still work so once used to it it'll feel good and fully usable with the enemies).My biggest issue here is probably the camera. Some nice options for it, but what I'd want is the height above the character.  Far too often it hangs down low, and so you can't see past your character well, or even if you can, the cameras just too close to the ground so it's hard to determine distances sometimes. I spend so much time constantly angling the camera down so I'm looking from above in fights, espeically boss fights, but it just keeps slowly aiming straight back towards the enemy you locked onto making it really hard to tell distances well, and up close you can't see movements of some enemies that are small enough to hide behind you. So thee is room for improvement on the game itself here.The biggest problem is probably the enemies, they are... probably a bit lacking in the clarity of their moves and movement. So for some of them, timing a counter spell (parry) can be frankly really hard with some of their attacks. Collisions aren't always perfectly matching the models, or visuals of some effects so you also can spend some time learning just when/how you'll be hit, but after a few hours I still have issues just fighting some basic enemies up front purely with melee and dodging/counter spell, and honestly that's an issue. Now with magic you can still deal with them well enough, but it is a problem that they might want to look into. Also at this earlier stage enemy variety is not as big as it could be, though the ones they do have at least feel decently different and require different play to counter for the most part.The bosses, currently 3 of them in alpha, are overall good. The first boss I'm not a fan of though. Shame since it's the demo boss, I feel people playing the demo would be put off as the game really starts getting good just AFTER that first boss and tutorial areas, in other words right after the demo ends. Well, first boss lacks some move clarity when up close recovering your mana by hitting him, making it hard to reliably dodge with your camera in his ass. And you have to do that to get mana then to deal ranged attacks without lots of waiting. No counter spell means you can't recover mana through that means yet sadly. So melee is super important in this fight, yet you probably still are in that low stamina stage where you trip over your own feet half the time.Later bosses though, generally good reads, really nicely done designs and telegraphs for the most part. Overall good fun to fight. The third boss though does have a bit of a multi phase issue. You fight through the first phase, this takes some time even if you're good and learned it all well. But then in the final phase... there are MULTIPLE attacks than can basicly one shot you and these are mostly unique, no easy intuition on what to do from previous moves or enemies you've faced. One attack in particular just... it really looks like jumping is the answer, yet jumping wont save you, you need to roll, despite that really not looking like it should work given the nature of the attack. So I did spend probably half my play time just learning to fight her second phase. Play through the first, get to the second phase, die. Play through the whole first again, second phase finally, die... repeat until I figured out the answers to it, but mechanicly they might want to rework that. Now, that type of challenge is ok for a final boss or major enemy like that, but the second proper boss/third boss after the tutorial ish one feels a bit early to require that type of grind, or ability look up online. So I do hope they either tweak that fight a bit so you don't as often instantly die from one wrong move in that second phase, or at least pull back a bit on future bosses so they don't have that same almost time wasting feeling as you work through an early phase to get to the next ones. Honestly though a really fun boss, I mean I did keep fighting her all that time and did keep enjoying it for the most part, even as it got a bit repetitive.So overall, a game with excelent potential that I am really looking forward to playing once it's finished, and possibly the future games of this IP afterwards. Overall lots of fun, though the start is a bit slow to work through. Easily worth the ten dollars, even as it was now I'd say it's almost worth that ten dollars, let alone once done and with more content and polished up.

_childDocuments_.review: A peculiar game, and a little difficult to sum up. The weapons are magical elements fired from your staff, and the awesome collection includes Fire Shotgun/Rocket Launcher, Ice Machinegun/Bullet Rain, Lightning Sniper Shot/Area Blast and Arcane Rifle/Fricking Howitzer. You access the more powerful attacks by chanting a spell, while the basic attacks can be used instantly. Melee attacks can accelerate chanting, as can well-timed dodges, while poorly timed dodges can get you hit, potentially losing the chant and the mana you spend on it.Mana, yes. Ammunition, regenerates, there are stats you can improve to increase your reserve, or make it recharge faster (with a little melee damage boost as a bonus). Melee attacks are weak, but recover a bit of mana with each hit. "Absorb" Counters (hard to time) recover a lot more. Other stats you can improve: Health, magic attack damage, stamina reserve (for dashing and dodging). You gain soul essence much like in a Soulslike game, but I'm reluctant to call Nobeta a true Soulslike for a number of reasons...First off, the locations. Dark Souls and its true genre kin, feature large, detailed worlds made up of interconnected locations. Stand atop a great bridge, see a great swamp below, a forest ahead, all places you will visit, sometimes hours later after many other adventures. That is part of the charm. Nobeta, unfortunately, lacks this pretty much completely. Instead you get a castle, a short cavern section, another part of the castle, more of the same castle, still more castle, and finally a bunch of floating islands with pieces of castle strewn about them. If you like spending the whole game mostly in the same, largely same-looking castle, this game's got you covered! If not... errr. Yeah.Next, enemy variety! Your true soulslike has about a hundred different enemies, from the lowliest zombie-like husks of civilians and soldiers, to ferocious beasts, to large monsters with unusual bodies and attack patterns, and of course a variety of imaginative boss enemies with chonky health bars and anywhere between half a dozen and over a dozen different attacks and maneuvers at their disposal.Nobeta... does not.Instead we have the formless blob monster, stretched upward a bit but still highly boring. This comes in multiple palette variations with different strengths and stats.  Yes, we're on this song and dance; just off the top of my head, the enemies I can recall are Blob Monster, Floating Sphere-Blob Monster, Headless Puppet, Legless Puppet, Blob-Like Cloaked Shade, Large Puppet With Shield, Large Puppet Mage, Unusually Detailed Maid Puppet With BS Invincibility Power (arcane howitzer seems to break that, luckily), Unusually Detailed Female Knight Wraith (sword, bow and possibly spear variants), and the bosses.That's not a sampling; that's  All of the game's enemies, unless I missed one or two. Yes, there are palette swaps of the blobs and cloak blobs. This does not an interesting new enemy make, though it does offer some much-needed life support to the strugglingly monotonous gameplay. Samey castle areas with confusing layouts to make them last longer as you wander around trying to get your bearings time and again. Samey enemies. A lack of challenging multi-enemy encounters, especially until quite late in the game. Little need or use for the cooler attacks (and they ARE cool, that's what kept me playing through to the end).The story is passable. A lot more grimdark than it needed to be, which undermines the cute wholesome vibe of the protagonist (if you don't see some tragic plot twists coming after reading even a few non-usable "item" pickups' lore, I'd be very surprised). The ending was pretty good, but without the enjoyable magic design I might have quit before seeing it. Seems a lot of people did, and I can't say I blame them. So much more fun could have been had with more enemies to blast to smithereens, harvest for essence and get through the game with less running of lap after lap around already-cleared areas just to farm more soul essence so you can handle the next boss. I played on Advanced difficulty as I'm familiar with Souls games and enjoy their level of challenge, but anyone else should probably stick with Standard so the farming becomes less necessary.On another positive note, you don't lose soul essence on death, at all - normally, anyway. If you use the freely provided crappy healing items, you lose more and more of your held, unused essence the more you items you use - but this only applies to your next death, and the penalty vanishes if you rest at a goddess statue (respawn point). But if you die without using crappy restoratives, you keep it all and can pump it straight into upgrades as soon as you revive at the statue. Which is nice, as it helps reduce grind. But there's still some grinding, and as mentioned, too few enemies to make it feel like an action-filled romp so much as a slogging hunt for scraps of power.Oh, and the "sexual content" tag is misleading. A few provocative outfits on female boss characters which are seen briefly in a cut-scene... some questionable noises in the voice acting when Nobeta gets hit, dodges, etc. But nothing that will satisfy someone actually looking for a lewd game. Mildly ecchi, at most.In the end, I will give the game a very weak recommendation. It is fun some of the time, repetitive and dull some of the time; the weapon design is awesome but the enemy design is not, nor is the world design. I recommend waiting for a sale, or giving it a miss in favor of the many more enjoyable souls-likes out there.

_childDocuments_.review: 😭😭😭I bought this game with low expectations. I did not expect much more than a Unity asset flip that happened to be cute and funny. That is not what this game is.Little Witch Nobeta is a third-person action game that is closer to a souls-like than the vast majority of games that claim to be souls-like. You play as Nobeta on her mission to reach the throne room of the castle. She is guided by a black cat along the way.The style of the game is very cute. Nobeta’s actions and mannerisms are funny. But don’t let that deceive you. The mechanics of this game are comparable to Bloodborne, and the world that Nobeta inhabits is darker than Demon’s Souls. Nobeta is a witch. Appropriately, her attacks are all centered around spells. You start off with one element of magic and throughout the game you can find three additional ones. Everything is projectile based and each element has a different style of shot. One is like a shotgun. Another is a machine gun, and so on. Little Witch Nobeta is secretly a third-person shooter. The amount of spells you can cast at once is limited by your mana bar, with goes down with each cast but refills over time. Mana is also gained restored with each kill, or with Nobeta’s limited melee attack. You can also charge the spells, which grants additional abilities. After the first boss you gain the ability to parry, which also restores mana and does damage. The window is very tight however.The game is not that hard. It is not easy, but it is doable on the standard difficulty setting. The advanced difficulty setting does nothing but make the enemies damage sponges, hit harder, and hamper Nobeta’s abilities. Just play on standard difficulty.The varieties of enemies have slight weaknesses to different elements. But more so to different styles of attack, so you have to get creative. The enemy variations seem dull at first, but there are some twists that keep it interesting. The difficulty spikes as the game progresses, but it never gets too crazy.In true souls-like fashion, the areas are interconnected by multiple routes. There are hidden walls in this game, hidden treasures, hidden movement mechanics, even hidden bosses. Exploration is immensely rewarding. Some areas seem like flattering fan versions of Demon’s Souls levels.Saint statues are equivalent to bonfires. It is your respawn point, your level-up point, and your shop. You level up just like souls games, putting points into the stat or stats of your choosing. You can make Nobeta a glass cannon, or a tank, or a melee pure, or a balanced witch. There’s plenty to play around with here. Respawns are on a checkpoint system like all souls games, but there is little penalty for death. A feature that Little Witch Nobeta shares with the metroidvania Ender Lilies is that you can return to the last visited shrine at any time from the pause menu.I think the story is what separates Little Witch Nobeta from the run-of-the-mill indie souls-like. The enemies and item descriptions in this game tell a story. The cut-scenes mostly do not, until the very end. The world of Little Witch Nobeta is extremely dismal. It is a world of intense racism, genocide, civil wars, caste systems, backstabbing, organ trafficking, grave robbing, torture, and slavery. I will leave the details for you to discover for yourself in the game. Like in the Souls games, the player character, Nobeta, is aware of these things but never voices her own opinions on them. She is very much involved, but in what way is left vague until the very end of the game.There aren’t even a ton of glitches in this game. It’s hard to clip out of bounds or exploit the animations. It seems like the developer thought of everything. I tried to sequence break in a few places and there was an invisible wall. But not just any invisible wall. It was a magical barrier that had its own animations and Nobeta recoiled off of it quite cutely. There was a lot of detail and polish put into this game. It does not drag on too long when it runs out of tricks, although the very very last area fells a tad bit thrown together from watered-down ideas. But there is a new game+ and any costumes you unlock on one save file carry over to other save files. Little Witch Nobeta is legitimately a good game!😭😭😭

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up, I really enjoyed the game. It combines concentrated cuteness with what I guess you could call Souls-like gameplay. I ended up enjoying the combat much more than I thought I would. The actual combat feels like a third person shooter. You mainly fight with magic, of which there are 4 main types of magic, each possessing a basic projectile attack, a charged up state, and a powerful spell. As an example, the fire magic basic attack is basically like a shotgun; short range, multiple projectiles with a relatively large spread, and  hits very hard close up. When fire magic is charged, it enchants your staff with fire, giving it a massive boost in melee damage. And once charged your magic attack becomes a fireball that causes a massive explosion. However magic attacks also use up your magical energy, which regenerates over time, but quite slowly particularly in combat. This is were melee comes in.In addition to the magic attacks you can use your staff with melee attacks. These are not particularly powerful unless your staff is infused with magic, however when you hit enemies with your staff it very rapidly recharges your magic. Thus while you can sit back and passively wait for your magic to recharge, you also can rush in and attack with your staff, which charges it significantly faster. In addition, well timed dodges also charge your magic up, meaning that if you really want to have a high and constant damage output, you want to play very aggressively. Lastly there is a sort of magic counter. If you do a melee attack right as you are hit, you take no damage and get a ton of magic back in addition to knocking away enemies. Not much in terms of story right now, but so far the premise is you have to find the throne. I am assuming the kind royalty would sit on and not a toilet, but that would be an amazing plot twist. Also you have a cat that is a jerk, which is realistic so that's neat.And lastly, yeah it's super cute. I have played a lot of Souls-likes, but not one that just was filled with wholesome cuteness. If that is what primarily drew you to it though, do keep in mind the actual combat may be difficult for you if you haven't touched a Soulsborne game. If you have, then you will probably find it ranging from very slightly to fairly challenging on the hard difficulty.If you haven't played and enjoyed a Soulsborne before, I highly recommend playing the demo. It features the first area and its boss. If you find it overwhelming, then understand that is absolutely nothing compared to the next areas. The first boss seriously is a complete joke compared to the others. Oh and lastly, this game will have Hololive vtubers in it. This has catastrophically triggered certain people, who then decided it was a reasonable response to review bomb the game. The game formerly had overwhelmingly positive reviews both for the recent reviews and overall. There is plenty of valid criticism out there for it which you should look into, but do keep in mind a lot of the negative reviews are just people salty over things like a vtuber showing statistics which listed Taiwan as a country.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 2024:After finally completing the full game story from beginning, it is still a good game, the level design is better in the second half of the game, though there were some annoying sections. Enemy variety is still an issue, as there are still like 10 unique enemies overall plus some elemental variants. Voice acting was a good addition! So for the most part the original review stands.------------------------------------------Original review 2020:For a Souls-like game this felt very relaxing to play, partially helped by the cute artstyle and sounds. It's definitely not that hard but very charming. In its current state the game is very short (3-6h), and only contains three areas and bosses. But all of these are very memorable and fun. The mana system is very creative, as it depletes fast and you get it back mostly by dodging and using melee, which prevents just running away and shooting. The different magic types are all distinct and have their uses, but as you only get some of them at late game, going to NG+ might be best to test these out.Some things the game should really improve going forward are:1. Level Design: The 3 levels themselves are rather bland looking, mostly consisting of same looking one way corridors, and only feature few shortcuts before bosses. The last level was the best, but the first level really needs some polish.2. Enemy variety: The game has maybe 8 different enemies, and maybe 3 of these were fun to fight3. Music & Voice acting: Aside from boss fights, the game has maybe 2 songs that play during the levels, which got repetitive, so maybe add more variety or add more sound effects or quiet sections. The game currently doesn't have voice acting aside from Nobeta's miscellaneous sounds. So adding voices or any sounds to other characters or perhaps more dynamic cutscenes should be a priority.But aside from these I hope the development continues! Also props for providing a demo in times where they are exceedingly rare.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing this game. I bought it when it first released in early access like two years ago. Then it was only three bosses available, ending with Monica. Now when they released the real game I tried it again, starting from my old save where I beat the game. So my experience playing this was NG+ Advanced mode.Enemies feel a bit repetitive. You have the shades, the dolls, and later some tanky demon girls? The larger more interesting enemies only appear a few times. Would have liked to see them more. The stone dolls where also a good mix-up.The bosses where fun and have variation, but when you learn to use the parry they become way too easy I think. But overall good. One issue with the bosses is that I feel they are supposed to have a place in the story, but most of the time they just appear once, have small dialogue, you beat them and they are forgotten. I think it is lost potential for interesting characters. Bosses are also voiced by Hololive members which is cool, but there is not a lot of dialogue so again lost potential.When it comes to the story it feels very messy. Not sure if you are supposed to like the cat or sympathize with it but I hate the cat. The cat has a few cool abilities but again it is not used or developed in the story so lost potential. I want to believe the final area is supposed to tell some more story or background why things are as they are but it is not explained. Maybe if I read all the item lore I will learn it but I did not bother.As a game where you use magic to attack and roll to avoid enemies it is good. If you like "soulslike" games (hate this term) this is fun, but don't expect the story to be too interesting. I also don't see how it took this long for the developers to complete the game when they had time to make merch and other stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple, straightforward, and is a pleasure to play. The characters are cute, and the enemies even cuter, but all entrapped within an extremely bleak world. _childDocuments_.review: Despite being a $10 indie game, LWN is surprisingly good in a lot of areas. While the number of enemies is pretty low, and mostly black blobs, nobeta herself and the bosses all look great. The music is solid and the effects give the game plenty of happy explosions. Combat is tight, though very gentle compared to other souls-likes, and has a reasonable variety of ways to approach the boss.The ranged dark souls thing is also pretty fun, through the controls can take a bit of time to get used to. The only major complaint I have is level design. There are a lot of same looking corridors, especially in the castle, which can easily get you lost, due to a lot of connected areas and backtracking. The game also has trouble pointing you in the right direction to proceed, aside from when the (decidedly unfriendly) cat is there to give orders.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me just say I am very impressed with how serious the devs take this mediocre game.There is a short anime teaser on youtube. Additionally, there is an interview with the Nobeta's voice actress and a recording of the orchestra recording theme songs.There is $35 worth of DLC and the base game is $25. The most complete version possible requires $60 standard price (bought individually).After all that hype and meaty asking price, you get is a 5hr. long Souls-like with a handful of areas and enemies and a thin plot.Now why the ♥♥♥♥ would I recommend this game still?I paid $9 for it years ago in early access with the promise they'd eventually finish it. They actually did. They even made the 5hr. run time enjoyable with cute little animations and combat that isn't tedious due to regening HP/MP. No the story isn't special and characters barely get any screen time (even the protag really, given how sparse her dialog is).However, based on $9 and a promise kept, I can recommend the game to those with moderate expectations. _childDocuments_.review: Very good aesthetic. Nice and simple premise. But I feel like I'm fighting the controls. I get that this is a ranged FPS, but it ends up feeling like the opposite issue with Souls games: melee focus with limited ranged capabilities. Here, it's ranged focused with limited melee capabilities. However, unlike ranged in Souls be completely optional, melee is necessary even in its limited scope.The control scheme is schizophrenic as well. I feel gimped trying to do a FPS with my controller when I have a mouse and keyboard RIGHT THERE. But then if I got mouse and keyboard, there's too many other things that feel unnatural for keyboard and mouse. For example: jump, dodge, and sprint. I usually bind them to a my space because you usually only have one or maybe two you use often. In TF2, space is jump. In ME, space is sprint. In Amalur, space is dodge. But all three? It just feels awkward for me. Maybe I could go with C for sprint, but then jump and dodge? And then I have aim, shoot, and attack. Aim kind of feels superfluous, but it's nice in some place. All of these actions are in natural places on a controller.Just from my intro experience, it just feels like lock on should just give magic a large amount of tracking unless the target dodges or something. The first boss's shield basically stops front attacks unless you manually aim at his arms anyway or just charge up the spell. Getting recoil on the attack is actually kind of cool and interesting, especially since that would naturally fall under the strength stat, but I don't believe it adds much to the mechanics of the game. Aim assist doesn't feel like it's doing anything.I also don't like the parry system either. There's not clear feedback for if you timed it too late or too early. A shot in bloodborne will briefly light stagger someone. If it makes their attack hesitate, it's too soon. If it keeps going or hits you, then it's too late.The game has a very good aesthetic with nothing over the top as a premise. It just needs polish for its controls

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game after I saw it had an overwhelmingly positive rating and that it had the tag "Souls-like", so here are some pros and cons.Pros:-Runs great at 1440p and 144 fps (tested with i7-8700K / RTX 2080).-Combat mechanics. As other souls games, it includes parrying, dodging, melee combat (although not very effective) and ranged combat, which is the core of the game.-Boss design. Not too easy nor too difficult, and I think these are the best part of the game.-Character design.Cons:-Spell damage and utility need some balance (non-charged ice spells feel a little overpowered compared to other spells).-Lack of variety of enemies.-Some levels are very easy to clean up from a safe distance, maybe a maximum range for spells should be considered.-Basically the game has no story, you just have to go to certain place, which you can't reach yet.-Counter. _childDocuments_.review: If you like anime aesthetics, cute little witches, and Dark Souls, then this game is definitely for you. Main character Nobeta is very cute, and she has a variety of animations that make her even cuter. If you pick up an item, Nobeta will physically grab it and place it inside her bag. If  you run out of stamina while moving, Nobeta will trip. If you want to pull a level, Nobeta will jump to grab it and effortfully pull it down. All these animations make Nobeta come across as someone who is trying her best, and makes you, the player, want to root for her. In terms of gameplay, the game is a third person shooter in which you shoot (cast) spells. There is melee too but it has more of a support role (melee hits refill Nobeta's mana, and allow her to charge up spells faster). As the game progresses, Nobeta will unlock different spells. Ice magic for example feels like a machine gun and, when charged up, you can mark enemies from behind cover and watch as icicles rain upon them. Fire magic to give another exemple feels like a shotgun and, when charged up, it enhances your melee attacks giving them much greater range and power. So different spells actually feel different and do open up new gameplay possibilities. It's not just numbers.  The most memorable thing about the game are the bosses. Boss fights are difficult but fair. You will most likely die a lot as you learn the bossess' attack patterns and how to respond to them. In my opinion, that's part of the fun; being utterly defeated at first, then learning how the boss works and finally using that knowledge to defeat it feels very satisfying. If you played Dark Souls, you will know what I mean. The bosses are also memorable because 1) pretty much like Nobeta they are super cute and, 2) because dialogue happens before and after fighting them. That dialogue gives you insights on the bosses' personalities and also serves as character development for Nobeta. Besides combat, the game also features exploration and some minor platforming. Carefully exploring the levels will allow you to open shortcuts and find hidden rooms and treasure chests. Keep in mind that there is no map or marker of any kind, so you will have to pay attention or you will get lost. Since the game is early access, you may wonder if the game is too buggy or too short. In my experience, the game is extremely polished. It's early access because it's missing some levels and Nobeta's story isn't over yet (the current game features three levels + a secret one, and at least three more are planned). In terms of length, the game can easily take you 10-12 hours in a first playthrough (there is NG+ too). A good chunk of that time will be spent dying to the bosses and challenging them again though. If you are very good at souls-like games, you may be able to finish the game much faster.

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays along the lines of the Dark souls games in terms of combat: Dodging in-between attacks and parrying is the bread and butter of fights and dodging at the wrong time can get you stun locked by even the most basic of enemies and lose about half your health, if not killing you. The game more heavily relies on ranged attacks though, being a protagonist of magical power.The melee attack would be used to parry incoming attacks and also to regenerate mana, your ammunition, by just simply hitting enemies. There are a few "styles" of magic that the game gives to you, four in the current state of the game, which can allow for a dynamic movesets on the part of the player so that they can play around and find their own style in combat.This game uses Japanese Anime art style, which means it leans heavily on being cute, but the anime feel stops pretty much there. The textures and graphics look like something that came from the PS2 era but it works well and achieves what it needs to do in terms of making the world. The animations work well and are very expressive, very good when it comes the faces of the characters and to see when an enemy is about to attack, but it's choppy and weird in some places, however I've only seen that happen in cutscenes so it doesn't affect combat in anyway I can see.The BGM of the game is achieves what it needs to, either by creating an atmosphere and hyping you up in a boss fight. It is nothing innovative and it doesn't need to be. The sounds from the enemies work great and will effectively signal you when an attack is incoming. There is no voice acting in the game, save from the grunts and cries of pain by the main character.The game play is very much like Dark souls and is very rewarding when mastered. It is not the easiest of games and can provide a challenge. The graphics and sounds aren't anything to write home about, but they work well enough that gameplay isn't affected and enough that they still add to the experience. I am having a lot of fun with the game, and Nobeta is really cute! I hope we can have voice acting in the future so that we can connect with the characters a lot more. For me, it's a good balance of fun and challenge and the quality of the game given the price is amazing!I  if you like challenging Dark souls type combat and anime! I am very excited for what becomes of the game in the future!Edit: I've finished the game and already playing the New game+, I'm loving the game! I don't know if it's an oversight, but picking up the inventory slot expansion at the start of the game gave me an additional slot so that THEORETICALLY, you could probably get infinite slots if you kept playing the New game+. I don't know though, I'm still playing through it again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has insane gameplay quality for an 8eurobucks title.People might have a point that this game will be in development for a long time, but to be fair, the early access is 2-5 hours depending on how much you want to explore and parkour around the areas and how well you do against the bosses and that is already worth the little price they ask, in my opinion.This game offers a lot of different playstyles, you can go crazy with dodges and countermagic to replenish your mana and charge up your big spells really fast to destroy your enemies or you can take it slow, snipe enemies with arcane or charge your spells in a safe spot to rain down the pain from afar or find some playstyle between.No magic feels underpowered, I played a gigaton of dark souls and one gripe I have with that game, which is not present in Nobeta, is that it has so many useless/weak weapons and playstyles and later weapon arts that have absolutely no use in PvE.I am probably going to finish up the achievements, pick up the game one more time when it has a nother 1-2 bosses or areas and I am gonna play the crap out of the game once more when it releases.The bosses without spoiling too much:The first boss is uninspired, the second boss is good and the third boss is great. _childDocuments_.review: pleasantly surprised this is unironically a good game. very, very polished gameplay. love the balancing act between melee and magic. love that every spell is basically a gun. nobeta's magic is gun. love being able to blow out my enemies' brains from across the game world with what is for all intents and purposes a sniper rifle. love the charged spells and the buffs they grant. love the parry. love being able to go ham with buffed melee with charged fire, or switch to charged ice armor when focusing on playing defense to parry myself back to fuil health.enemy placement can be a bit of a gotcha at times but that's par for the course.bosses are all amazing and do a great job at teaching you various mechanics, though they can really push your ♥♥♥♥ in if it's not clicking for you. special shoutout to tania teaching parrying so well. i did stonewall on monica for a dozen or so attempts before i realized you're meant to spam base ice at her charged attack, but aside from that everything was a blast.cute characters, but very meh graphics when it comes to environments. stage music is okay, but one stage conspicuously has no music and the entire last section of the game reuses one track for all areas. boss music is straight bangers front to back, though.story is a little scuffed but bear with it and it works a lot better once you can see all the pieces. items also help a lot for worldbuilding. after beating the game and collecting enough items, extra videos unlock that add a lot more depth to the story (though all the censors are a little annoying). i do wish more of wanderer in the dream's interpretation of the plot and overall composition and mood were in the game itself.hololive VAs are cool but there's a very conspicuous gap in performance between nobeta and tania's voices vs vanessa and monica. still cool to see them though.roughest parts of my experience were A. game freezes at random intervals anywhere from once every other day to 3 times in one session of a few hours, and B. trying to get the achievement for opening all treasure chests in one run. ended up resorting to a guide because i was tired of scouring 99.9% the entire game world per run, overall covering 100% of the game world but losing track of the chests and never quite getting all of them in the same run. btw tip for readers so you dont suffer like i did: your gameplay history counts how many chests you've opened in the current run!!!! though, you'll still need to check a guide to know how many chests you should have at the point of no return and before ending the game...i really can't overstate how well the game plays and handles. you could binge the game in a day or two, and complete everything in a week or two more, but what i got out of the game was definitely worth my money. overall 8.5/10, only really losing out on the weird crashes, length, and a bit of graphics. 9 if we ignore the length. really interested in some proper content DLC, or better yet a sequel. would definitely recommend the game and at least check out its supplementary materials like the animated manga (free to watch!)
