_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for a decent amount of time. Since the early access, I've been waiting for the completed version and now, it's here.I've anticipated a good amount of souls-like feel of it, and they did manage to deliver with flying colors.I've read other comments saying "a huge spike in difficulty", but in all honesty, they were actually generous to even have "tutorial" like area. They never gave a "go figure it out" vibe, which most authentic souls game will beat the crap out of you.Controls wise is decent enough, responsive enough and no unreasonable hit box be it your character or the enemy.Environment and the atmosphere is too light at some regard except for that stage where it gave me anxiety on "figuring what to see". That was an awesome experience. It would have been really thrilling to have the entire game like that. shhhhiiiiiii~ it was a GOAT! anyway.The design is cute... almost too cute for this kind of... feel. It felt some how of a Kiddie souls game. Dont get me wrong, it's actually pretty good to have such feel on it.Story wise, it's... not as profound. On the contrary, it quite simple and straight forward. You will just wonder "why" a lot with several tropes that will make you cringe at some degree. However, the lore of the game is pretty damn dark! take some time to read the items and man, it can trigger you why to hate humanity. Take some time finding items, it makes the exp of the game much more immersive.Although, the end of the story was........ I suppose "unexpected" would be the word.One of the things that did pretty get old is "not so much variations" of enemy. They are annoyingly challenging at times tho, especially in mobs.   It's a pretty decent game considering they are an indie company. I dunno what other games they made, but this is pretty decent enough for a souls like game.It's a 4/5 overall. People should try it and actually finish the game, it's worth the time.For the publisher, developer, or whom ever.I wish to request if you can add a higher difficulty level than the "how it should be played" difficulty. I will really appreciate it. No, I am not talking about New game plus. Like from the start. lvl 1 and absolutely Very Hard... Hardcore kind of hard core kind.

_childDocuments_.review: So when I first played Little Witch Nobeta in early access, I was immediately hooked. It struck every chord for me. Cute characters, anime loli girls that murder you, goofy enemies, big boss fights and a sad story? Hell yes, sign me up immediately. I waited a very long time for the full version to drop, and I was not disappointed in the slightest. The magic was fun, the bosses were funner, and I couldn't have been more hyped for what was in retrospect a fairly small game. I cleared the entire game in Advanced after roughly 20 hours time (mainly offline which is why Steam only shows 6 hours) then replayed in Standard mode. Standard only took 1 hour and 30 minutes total to beat (literally, it was exactly 1:30:08) a stark contrast from Advanced mode. Every boss was genuinely fun and I have almost no notable complaints about them. I must say I was sad that NG+ did not change anything other than the difficulty. I think it would have been very fun to play through again as the true Nobeta with the black cat as a companion, or at least have some more changes and easter eggs to be found. I do have three gripes about the game which I really wanted to address here.I had initially began Little Witch Nobeta in Standard mode, but I quickly realized enemies would not pose even a slight threat; therefore, I restarted the game in Advanced mode shortly after defeating the Unknown Specter Armor in just 30 seconds. Standard enemies are so weak, you can clear the entire game by levelling only Intelligence to one-shot most of them. In Advanced Mode, this game's difficulty escalates from that of an Animal Crossing game to almost Dark Souls level challenges. Those basic enemies go from dealing mere chip damage to being capable of one-shotting you at max HP. The difficulties of Standard and Advanced mode are so far apart, it could easily catch even players who have finished this entire game off guard. Difficulty aside, the environments of some areas feel quite bland overall. Common enemies encountered also consist of very simple monsters and a handful of mini-bosses (most of which will show up repeatedly or with reskins.) There are a small number of truly unique enemies in the game barring reskins; hence, certain locations can feel very lifeless. This issue is most prevalent at the beginning, where Okun Shrine presents only one unique enemy: the area boss, Unknown Specter Armor. That being said, boss designs in Little Witch Nobeta are very good; besides, the normal enemies are often very dumb and goofy looking despite their blandness, which I enjoyed. I was also slightly disappointed after learning of there only being 4 obtainable Elemental Magics, each of which only has two different attacks (uncharged and charged shots.) These spells were fun, required careful thought and skill to use, evaporated hordes of enemies, and could be mixed up to overwhelm and punish bosses with devastating effect; however, the developers really could have done a lot more with them. Vanessa's magic and attacks are some of the most visually appealing in the game, but we never get the opportunity to use those ourselves. The same goes for Monica and Tania's abilities. Even though we play as Nonota and presumably have the souls of eveyone we defeated up until reaching the throne, we are never able to utilize their abilities (even though Nonota as a boss fight is able to.) Overall, Little Witch Nobeta is an 8.5 / 10 game in my opinion. Reviews for the game seem overwhelmingly positive; thus, I anticipate the possibility of future DLC, or hopefully a potential sequel if the game does well overtime. It is of note that Chinese "antis" review-bombed this game, and still continue to do so (albeit in far smaller numbers.) This is fueled by their childish hatred of hololive, whose members voiced the main bosses. If you see random and nonsensical negative reviews, this is likely why. I hope that developers take this into consideration when surveying Little Witch Nobeta's reception and planning for future content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game that should last you about 10-ish hours.The good parts.+ There are 4 spells and they all are fun to use especially if you upgrade it. Sprinting around, dodging and parrying while pew pew the spell down range has never been more fun.+ The combats are enjoyable, however parry is rather hard and require a precise timing which can be difficult when dealing with melee attack from enemies as they have an awkward timing (slow wind up then almost instantly hit you) or maybe i'm just suck idk.+ I use keyboard and mouse and the controls are decent. Nothing to complain about ,really.+ Pretty good performance.The not so good parts (Mostly just the aesthetic of the game and QoL.)- All of the maps are really bland as the assets keeps getting reuse over and over, you'll see the same wall, the same pillar, the same arch over and over again which make everything looks just the same and confusing to navigate. (Sure the theme do change but they are still pretty forgettable). You'll definitely find yourself confused and lost a lot if you decided to backtrack the map for the chests and items which leads to the next downside.- There is no map to look where you are (I'm not asking for a minimap but that'd be nice if you can chose to have or not). Like I said earlier, you'll find yourself lost a lot in the game as there is no map or point of interest to refer to. I sincerely wish the devs would spend more time adding a bit more props to the map like armor stand, wall decoration or banners so that it can serve as a point of interest to refer to when you are navigating though the map.- Confusing translation. There are quite a number of translations which could be word more clearly.- Aesthetically speaking, there aren't many variation of enemy. You'll see a lot of re-skin or should I say recolor model of enemies with slights difference of attack type for each color. It'd be nice if they made different model for the dark/red/blue type enemy.(-/?) Story is meh but I guess that's not the point of this game as there are manga for it.But hey, the pew pew and whacking enemies with a spell infused broom is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit like dark souls in that it is hard, you get world building through items and that it is dark. The characters are cute and the voice acting is mostly pretty good. I didn't even notice that the bosses was voiced by Hololive talents until i looked at the credits lol. As a loli connoisseur I approve of this art.The combat is a little bit like dark souls in that timing and spacing is important and that both you and the enemies dies relatively fast. You can use different spells that you can just shoot or charge it for a different effect. What they have done with charging is pretty interesting, as in you can speed up the charge by dodging attack, parrying and hitting the enemy with melee attacks. Some charged spells also enhances your melee attack once it has finished charging, so you could play around melee too instead of just using spells. I think the combat is satifying.The world-building is built through the items and every item is voice acted (in jp) which I appreciate a lot (since I like jp voice acting) and the descriptions add context to the world and bosses. Despite the cute characters the world is quite dark. I wish for a some kind of sequel continuing in this world since it hasn't been explored much and it is quite interesting imo.Basically this game is cute, interesting and challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for 9 hours so far, and I gotta say.. I'm really happy with what I bought on a whim. At first I didn't know what I was getting into. The anime-style look and its aesthetics made me thing it was going to be something super short.Man. Was I wrong. Hella wrong.The way the game showed me its mechanics and how everything flowed together gave me a comforting feeling. I liked how they included this one tutorial to show that the main character can 'Levitate when using the Melee Attack for a brief moment'. That advice alone helped me get through some platforming, and even helped me get creative with how to get around! I love the style it has. The way the models and textures really sell the animated look! The levels are all interesting in their own way, each having a ton to explore! Difficulty is just right, what with it being a Dark Souls game and all. The boss fights were all interesting in their own way, each having their own unique patterns and different ways on how to beat them! The Magic System works very well and is very fun to use, what with being able to charge your magic and enhance your abilities while charged up. It's all good! Of course, there are some things i have a slight gripe with. Just slight though: 1. Controls for Controllers are kind of broken. Anytime I hooked up my controller to my computer and got it set up the game would make Nobeta rotate either right or left constantly, as well as several buttons being the same button, or the button layout in-game is wonky. I.E. Square on my PS4 Controller was X while X was O, etc. 2. Inventory. I have no gripe with how it is managed! I love it actually! Makes you have to make decisions on what to actually bring with you and not just stuff in your bag! My only gripe is the Healing items mainly. Give the player something similar to the Estus Flask with maybe one or two charges, and make it to where the only way to get more charges is to pray at Goddess Statues. Think of it as a *Oh Crap!* sort of thing! Keep the healing items as well! That way if some players feel they will need it, they will have more incentive to use them! Other than that, everything else is good! Those are my only main complaints right now honestly. Everything else was super minor: 1. Map/Minimap to show me where I am. 2. Maybe more costumes for future use. 3. More wand and accessories. 4. More jumping puzzles! I love the fact they give us a tutorial over the whole 'float when swinging wand' mechanic! I plan on coming back to add more as the game continues to develop. 10/10 recommend to anyone wanting to commit murder death kill as a little witch.~

_childDocuments_.review: Fun 'hard' game. Worth the price for what's currently here but I look forward to future updates. ^ - that was before 1.0 Okay, finally finished it. And I mean everything, including watching the (official) lore videos. 10/10 would recommend to weebs. 8/10 for people who like souls like games. All the bosses were fun to fight. There is a 'boss rush' mode where you fight one boss to the next (timed but not limited) which is a really nice addition the Devs added several months after release. There are lore bits to find throughout the game (items). The game unlocks a new main menu 'videos' selection after you beat the game. (At least I'm pretty sure it wasn't there until I beat the game.) Those videos give you lore (and a lot of it). It's really nice to see the Devs add those to the game. (voice acted with English subs). The lore videos really did make me fall in love with Little Witch Nobeta's world more. The only downside was that the videos were censored... I later learned you can watch the uncensored versions by entering a password somewhere in the files... (You got a password at the end of every? video) Mind you the censoring is just gore stuff. Age ratings and all that. You get a few different spells going through the game. You'll mostly be using one or two different spells most of the time (like the first spell since when it's charged it can stun enemies) But that doesn't mean you won't be using ALL the spells at all. Because you will be using them all. (even more so if you're planning on 100% the game lol) There are some grindy achievements but nothing too long to grind for. (I'm looking at you Aliens: Fireteam Elite). There is a few different ways to grind for those achievements. One of the easiest spots to grind, all you have to do is rest repeatedly at a statue. And I'm not going to go into spoilers. :P Almost forgot to say you can unlock skins in the game for free! TDLR: Great souls like game with lore. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is pretty fun and enjoyable but dodging's invincibility frames are too generous and the parry window is a bit too large. Running out of stamina is almost never punished since the time between boss attacks is long enough that you can dodge or get up before the next attack. Despite playing as a mage spacing isn't very important and positioning is mostly reserved for fighting multiple enemies.Currently the story is the part that is on the store page with one or two items of information minus the secrets.There are a few inexplicable wind noises throughout the levels (Tied to game sound and not music).The puzzle elements are easy platforming and which attack interrupts the boss' attack vs which one does the most damage.The boss fights and the bonus level are the most fun parts of the game. From what I heard the normal mode of the game was originally the easy mode so don't make the mistake of playing easy mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to leave a positive review as my experience with about 90% of this game was extremely positive.I really enjoyed this game and worked my way happily to the last boss on Advanced mode.The gameplay mechanics are unique, and interlock with each other in a very clever way. Ranged (your most damaging) attacks cost mana, mana is regenerated by using melee and evading enemy attacks at the last second.The bosses are challenging and have impressive move sets, that test your reactions and upon subsequent tries will have you adjusting your strategy.Enemy variety is sufficient. 2 enemies are added to the fray each area, and compliment each other in fantastic ways. Seriously, the enemies are thematically sort of "meh", but their function as a hostile unit reminds me of Doom 2-- where every enemy has a specific purpose, and their placement on the map is deliberate and increases the challenge.The last boss made me alt f4 and close the game and write this review lol. I'm a soulsbourne fan, I love the challenge of these games. And Nobeta's boss fights were all challenging but fair except for the last.I pulled up videos on youtube on how to kill her, and the player im watching is doing ♥♥♥♥ im assuming is an exploit (dodge rolling in mid air?)Without this, the last boss seems to have an attack that is unavoidable. You dodge roll the overhead slam, but the shockwave will knock you down, and then she'll swipe the floor and often just toss you off the boss arena to instant death.Extremely frustrating to say the least.An excellent game for 10 dollars, and in Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Be advised:  This game's Early Access is not like other games'. This is more of a paid demo than an early access title. Why do I say this? The developers have no intention of incrementing out content. Instead, they would rather drop the full game late 2021 or early 2022.Play the demo before you decide whether or not you want to buy the game. It includes the first level of the Early Access content. One spell, limited evasive maneuvers (no air dodge or double jump or Counter Magic), and generic enemies.After getting a platinum in this game after 14 hours, I can definitely recommend the game. Controls are very tight with a gamepad, and the magic feels fluid. Soundtrack and environment are kind of generic, but the cute anime feel definitely overcomes that hurdle for me, personally.What really stands out about LWN to me is the boss designs. Even something as common as living armor feels great to fight, not to mention Tania and Monica.Spells are fairly well-balanced, in my opinion, though Ice is definitely the favored "general use" spell. I know a number of people complain about Arcane's limited use after the first stage, but honestly, I think Arcane Cannon is great for the mana cost.--- BOSS SPOILERS AFTER THIS POINT ---Tania and Monica have a couple of telegraphs that aren't super intuitive. It took me a few tries to figure out that I can, indeed, shoot Tania's blue projectiles and Monica's stage-destroying super move in order to interrupt them. And honestly, I found out by accident.--- SPOILERS END ---***Not changing my rating (because I still do recommend the game), but I'm rather annoyed that they chose Hololive girls to voice act the characters. _childDocuments_.review: A genuinely good souls-like, game-play wise. It both does the good parts of souls mechanics well, and adds its own spin on things.Somewhat shorter - 6 main story bosses and 1 optional boss.The main concern is the character design. While it is no crime to have kids as characters, when 5 out of 6 of the characters with dialogue are prepubescent girls, it is pretty clear where the developers were coming from.Deeper dive into mechanics for anyone interested: As the title suggests, the main source of damage is spells. Those spells have a single-shot version, where you just transform a bit of mana into a shot, and a charged version, where you walk around charging the spell and then fire off a modified shot with various effects that depend on the selected element. What makes the system much more interesting is the way one gathers mana. The most effective ways to do so are dodging and . When you roll trough an attack - one that connects with your model during its i-frames - balls of mana float in the air for a second, and then towards you, and upon reaching you enter your mana pool. However, that interaction is altered by charging. If you are charging a spell when the mana reaches you, it gets added to the charge directly instead of to your mana pool. More importantly, if you are charging a spell while dodging, instead of floating in the air, the mana once again gets added directly to your mana pool. That means that you can start a charge, dodge, and then cancel the charge, and you receive the mana immediately instead of having to wait a few seconds to get it - something that can matter in speedrunning (to be fair it is rare to have it actually be useful - it's just a showcase of what kind of versatility the mechanics allow for). More commonly. I also think that  is done well.

_childDocuments_.review: Loli Dark Souls is amazing. The quality is really outstanding. So far the game gets everything right. The art, the controls, the performance, and the game balance. As of this review, I've finished the second dungeon.  I breezed through the first one because I played the demo, and familiarized myself with the game mechanics before buying this version,.The graphics and the lighting or fantastic. The only spot I noticed that needs more work is in the caves where some of the textures weren't loading. The level design is pretty souls-like in that it is linear, but does have some diverging paths and unlockable shortcuts.The gameplay is fantastic. It's a souls-like for sure, but what makes it different is your main weapon, the staff. It fires spells like a gun. it uses mana that you recover through dodging, melee attacks, defeating enemies and using items. The platforming in this game is so good. the movements are so fluid, and the jumping mechanic is nice. The physics for the movements and objects are also really well done. The Game balance is just right. It's not stupid hard, but it's not really forgiving either. Instead of estus flasks, you heal through breaking objects like boxes and pottery, and using items, and of course through statues that function like bonfires. Healing items are found around the statues and right a boss fight so you'll always have some to get through the level and the boss fights. This game is really special, and I recommend it to those looking for a cute and high quality souls-like experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the Souls-like tag and description scare you, there are two modes.  Advance is a typical "Souls" experience, with high damage, tight timing windows, and a lot of practice and deaths to get used to the fights.  Normal is a far easier mode for those who are not comfortable or familiar with Souls style gameplay.  Normal can be treated as a standard action/exploration game instead.  Bosses can be tough, but most players will be able to beat them in a few tries.  For the real experts, a boss rush mode that uses full Advanced stat/moveset bosses and does not allow you to level up is unlocked.In Normal mode, your leveling currency is only lost on death if you use items that grant a curse.  Otherwise, it's kept on death.  This is very useful in areas where you can be knocked off the terrain.  Levelups are pretty minor boosts individually, but it adds up to be a pretty significant boost toward the end of the game.  You can tell just how powerful you can get when you compare an end-game save against a tower boss rush save that doesn't allow leveling up.Overall, combat is pretty good, you have a selection of spells, that operate a lot like a third person shooter's weapon choices.  Arcane is like a pistol, Ice like an SMG, Fire like a shotgun, and Lightning like a sniper rifle.  You also have a melee, a charge up for your spells that changes the behavior of your melee attack and gives you a powerful spell to release (a series of homing ice balls, a powerful arcane shot, an explosive fire orb (like a grenade), or placing a circle where lightning will strike.  These charges are going to be one of your main forms of attacks and puzzle solving, charges take time and slow your movement (but dodging works and helps speed it up).  You can also parry some enemy attacks, by perfectly timing a melee hit.  The parry is essential in the boss rush mode.  Melee'ing and dodging attacks will help restore your MP for casting spells.Storytelling is mostly in a Souls style, with most of the background, worldbuilding, and lore locked behind item descriptions for collectibles you find.  There are some cutscenes that can be skipped on NG+ modes.  It works, but it's mostly a plot to keep you moving along to the interesting boss fights.Graphics wise I feel like it's a PS3/XBox360/Vita style, it's fairly simple and non-obtrusive and doesn't interfere with the very cartoonish style for the main character Nobeta .  Almost all your bosses are dolls, and each one is fairly unique in design.  The low detail probably runs pretty well on lower end hardware.  Nobeta is completely adorable, and you can unlock a few additional outfits for her during play.  Four additional outfits are locked behind the bonus boss rush mode.  Each one is unique, but I tended to stick with the default outfit.Overall, on normal mode the challenge is not extreme, it requires some care and attention, but it's something that should be playable by almost anyone.  Advanced does get rough, you have to fully involve yourself in the game's mechanics and there is not much leeway for victory.  There is no reusable healing item, each item is a one time use gem that you'll drop if you get hit during its use.  This means very careful timing is needed on the higher difficulty!  A few puzzles are a bit obscure, the lightning puzzle in particular was tough to figure out Overall, solid title that provides both a tough combat experience for Souls lovers and a cute action game for those who prefer less punishing fare.  It's adorable, inexpensive on sale, and a fairly solid exploration title that has fairly low system requirements for what you get.

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable game, but it's so much more than that. This is an inventive blend of soulslike and tactical third person shooter with a stripped-down yet very fun magic system and fast, brutal combat. Think Dark Souls meets Doom meets Genshin Impact, but much more accessible than any of those. Zipping around and blasting enemies as you clear through levels is incredibly satisfying; your progress will be impeded only by puzzles that are just challenging enough to be interesting and surprisingly tough boss fights.The story is somewhat generic dark fantasy, but serviceable -- it starts off as a Dark Souls ripoff and then develops. You unlock cute costumes as you progress and you can get more by buying DLC. Good soundtrack. Would highly recommend, especially on sale. I'm middling at soulslikes and got about 20 hours out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: [Cute] [funny] [souls-like]Yes, it is those things. It's more than the sum of those things, however. Casting as the central combat feature invokes "shooter" without over-emphasis. Dodge, parry, and timing in melee combat are still very important. You are expected to be a well-rounded fighter, rather than heavily focusing on one play style.Platforming is definitely a thing, and a complex thing with subtle but important variations. In some ways it is arguably more of a metroidvania than a souls-like (though, one could argue Dark Souls is a metroidvania with RPG elements).Like a good metroidvania or souls-like, it has clever map design and the combat is challenging, yet rewarding. It knows what it is, and it knows what it's borrowing from. But it's still kinda its own thing. Not just because of the cutesy visuals, and the magic focus, but because it's not pretending it invented anything. While it's certainly clever, and somewhat unique, it's not reinventing the wheel and it shouldn't have to in order to stand apart from its predecessors. A lesson other games could learn.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun time for anybody that likes fighting hard bosses with unique combat mechanics. You will probably die a lot but you'll learn to love each boss as you figure them out. The rolling and parrying feel comparable to Bloodborne, but the third person shooter elements make this game feel unique. The combat is altogether very thoughtful and fun.Cons:The stages and art design (outside of the MC and boss characters) are serviceable but bland. Platforming has some jank to it, but it doesn't come up much. The difficulty (I played "advanced" mode, formally "normal") presents stages that are a cakewalk compared to bosses. Bosses also have the potential to heavily stunlock/combo you, meaning that getting hit might be a slap on the wrist or an overly quick death depending on boss RNG. The result is that the proportion of boss attack avoidability vs. damage done feels unbalanced if a quick hit happens to result in a combo.For 10 bucks though this game is recommendable for people who like bashing their head against cool bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: Loli Witch Nobeta claims to be a 3D action shooting game with comfortable Japanese art style and “quite challenging“ battles despite its cute looks.It’s not. Don’t let the pretty pictures fool you. Avert your eyes from the loli witch if you must. Don’t let the popular user-defined tags tempt you into thinking you’re in for a “cute and funny“ product. The only tag that truly matters is “Souls-like“. As someone who sucks at the Souls series, but completed it, let me tell you: don’t judge a book by its (adorable) cover.In short, Loli Witch Nobeta is a game about a young magical girl / witch. You venture into a castle overflowing with all kinds of enemies your magic should, in theory, tear to shreds. You have to find a cat, which will help you find the throne. Okay, good. That’s as far as the game goes in terms of story (at the beginning at least).This is the part where the game’s description lies to you. First, our witch doesn’t befriend a mysterious black little cat. In fact, it’s probably more powerful than you, and quite a rude cat at that. Second, you don’t need to underestimate your foes. They don’t care about you. They’ll tear you a new one for free. You’re dirt beneath their boot heels. They grow in number and variety the further you go, because it’s their town and your not-even-close-to-ten-years-old face shows up in the hood past midnight. Their deaths are never in vain. As they die, they chip away at your sanity (and your health bar), showing you that little girls really aren’t as durable as certain “sacred scriptures you may find online“ make them out to be. The game despises every hitpoint you have, and it wants you to know that at every turn.In all honesty, I do enjoy the game. It’s a challenging and aesthetically pleasing (+ made in Unity) game at that. So, I’ll try to mention its strong and weak points from my filthy casual perspective without spoiling the game’s story too much. Writing this, I got bored about halfway through, so this is all I could be bothered to write.There are two difficulty settings when you begin: what I suppose is “normal“ and the more challenging “advanced“. On Advanced, you get fewer “souls“ and take more damage. I’ve been playing on the „Advanced“ difficulty.Aesthetics. The game’s definitely good looking, charming even. The characters and environments are stylized well, without elements feeling out of place or highlighted poorly in the grand scheme of things (although I do recall seeing some strangely shaded patches in one place or another). On top of that, the game runs very well (unlike a lot of ‘unpolished‘ Unity titles). There’s never been a moment I recall my game freezing up or slowing down to a noticeable degree. I can’t speak for those with 60+ Hertz displays.Gameplay. It’s simple. Character attributes go up to level 30. You cast spells, dodge enemy attacks or go into melee. You charge up spells to deliver more powerful variants of the same element. There’s a sufficient amount of variety here, since the magic is split up into four elements: arcana, ice, fire and lightning, each with different regular and powered up moves. My only criticism here would be that ice is a bit too versatile. While other elements reduce power usage, increase movement speed, and the like, ice actually deals more damage (due to greater number of projectiles) as you level it up. It’s also a lock-on ability, meaning you don’t even have to have line-of-sight to crush your foes (once you’ve locked on). At least it feels like the path of least resistance.Story. It certainly has some strong moments, in my humble opinion, but in that regard leaves a bit to be desired. There’s simply too many unknowns, probably on purpose until the game’s completed and the story reaches its conclusion. I’m not quite sure what the end result will be, as there’s only a few bits of dialogue allowing the player to make a somewhat educated guess. Sadly, it is also quite a linear game.A Linear Title. You can’t bypass encounters or ignore them altogether as you might in Dark Souls, which is a bit of a shame as it leaves little variety in the way you tackle your inevitable opponents. The world’s parts are interconnected (shortcuts to one bonfire-equivalent or another), but that about sums it up until you finish the current story (which opens up paths to just about everywhere). Sometimes you wind up going through whole areas and a boss fight just to get from one floor to the one above you, which is still quite amusing.A Lack of Voices. Despite the protagonist having voice lines for casting, falling, receiving damage and staff attacks, neither Nobeta nor other characters are actually voiced during cutscenes / dialogue which detracts from an otherwise pleasantly cutesy (some might say sickeningly cute) experience. Unfortunately, the game is not yet complete. Of course, it’s an early access title. Still, you can enter NG+ once you’ve finished the story, and do it all over again (if you’re not just a masochist, but something far more degenerate than that). Replaying the game allows the player to collect more grimoires, which in turn grants higher level magic (up to a maximum of lvl 3) should you have missed any particular grimoires on the first playthrough or just cannot find them. Beating the game a 3rd time is pretty much required to get max lvl lightning magic at the moment.I‘ve got a good 8 hours out of the game on my first run (due to exploring almost everything, looking for hidden passages and the like), and doing the secret stage at the end of what’s currently available. For a little more than 8€ over here, I cannot recommend it enough, and look forward to whatever updates may become available in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Advanced mode does not feel like it was the difficulty that was tested. One of the key things about good souls like games (an any games) is that enemies cannot surprise you with no reaction time. Its what makes things like Halo 2's legendary difficulty so infamous. Its (part) of what made DS2 so infamous. If I walk past an enemy, and it doesn't communicate it is going to get up immediately, then I don't know to retreat to get out of danger. There's a reason ambushes work so well IRL. Overall just needs better enemy placement and telegraphing. Its a game, you're not actually trying to kill me.Everything else so far is standard in terms of gameplay. Feels like the anime girl was the main attraction here, with no real innovation for gameplay being the main attraction. That's all anime games though.I'd give it a maybe, but SoulsBourne is not good series to set the bar for "Will I like this game".

_childDocuments_.review: You are Nobeta, a witch with the goal of entering a random castle in search of answers about yourself and a place called the Throne. Whatever that is. Oh you also brought a cat with you but seems to have run off. Time to go searching.The Little Witch Nobeta is kind of mix of both Remnant From The Ashes gun combat with The Legend Of Zelda exploration. Weird i know. But don't be fooled by this game's cute anime art style. This is a souls-like game in nature and models itself like Dark Soul. Its difficulty as a soul-like game is chill and doesn't demand so much out of you. It's forgiving i would say. Written dialogue are great and some i really liked. They were good and well written. But that could just be me tbh. The art style for this game is pretty good. Specifically on the characters and bosses in this game are very well done and i even liked some of the character design. The levels themselves aren't anything special but it gets the job done.They are good. That's all you get for now. >>UNDER CONSTRUCTION<< For 1080p it's ok. Maybe if the devs want to add more graphics options that would be cool but i would not expect one. I played this game in 1440p and it looks great. At max settings it ran fine on my Rtx 2070 Super. Well over 200 frames. No crashes so far however sometimes while running in some locations i experienced some small stutter/lag and i don't know if it's the game still loading the next scene. It last for like a second or two while running around corners. Overall it ran fine. I usually like to make it its own section if there's stuff i want to talk about but for engine it's running on the Unity engine. Nice. This review is obviously not complete as i want to wait for the full thing to review it more in depth or at the very least add more to what i already have listed. I got this game during the holiday sales of 2021 for 10 buck on sale. I was browsing for something and i spotted this game. It was a souls-like game with a coat of anime cuteness layered on top which i found funny and interesting because you play as a little girl dressed as a witch entering a castle not knowing anything about it. I wasn't expecting much from it but the more i played the more i started to like it. Anyways i left a lot out but that's ok. For the price for what i played i think it's fair. There's definitely a solid game here. You can get about 4-5 hours out of it. _childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about it, just buy it. You will not regret it. Veterans of soulslikes will enjoy familiar mechanics combined with run'n'gun gameplay; fans of action games will get swept up in the variety of spells and unlockable powers, and have ample enemy types to test their playstyles on; and people who aren't necessarily elite gamers will find a game that can be as easy or as difficult as they want it to be. Putting aside its interesting story, fascinating lore, and great soundtrack, it's a fun game to play and will appeal to a wide range of people.===I first played this game when it was an itch.io demo, and shortly after the Early Access version released and I jumped onto it. It's been a long wait for me, but I can say the full release has been worth it. The new levels bring in new mechanics, enemies, puzzles, and secrets, and continue the story that had been left unresolved since the EA release in mid 2020.Other additions in that time has been a re-recording and refresh of the soundtrack, as it seems every track is now a live recording of an orchestral arrangement, and the addition of Japanese voiceacting. These additions were not originally planned for the full release, so the fact they're there and the rest of the game hasn't endured sacrifices to accommodate them in the development cycle is impressive, at least to me.The runtime promised in the Early Access version was met in the full release, featuring six major, mandatory boss fights you must face over the course of the story. While some people may criticize the game for having a low number of bosses compared to traditional soulslikes, in reality there is a large number of mandatory and hidden minibosses spread throughout the game that more than double the number of difficult encounters, and require different approaches to beat. These include an optional rematch with a powered up version of the 1st boss; a completely hidden, unique miniboss that dominates their arena; and a 2-part set piece against a relentless, monstrous entity, These minibosses break up stretches of exploration with difficult encounters, without encroaching on the main boss fights and their position as the climactic battle at the end of a level, and the fight that ultimately drives the plot forwards.On the topic of plot, the story cleverly avoids showing its hand too early. Instead it deliberately sets up an air of mystery and uncertainty, keeping things secret and leaving only clues and hints as to what is really going on. This allows the plot to pull off some really interesting twists, and gives it the space to build up the stakes and set the tone for the final boss. Paired with the lore one can learn from collectible items, and the final boss can be one where you actually dread the outcome and consequence of actually winning.The gameplay is more closely that of a run'n'gun action game. Sure, you have your dodge rolls, i-frames, and parries (unlockable spell type available after the 1st boss, carries over in NG+), but the central loop of the action is centered around movement and good use of your available skills. You can play very safely for the most part, and while you'll be able to survive taking your enemies on at a distance and avoiding risk, the gameplay really shines when you become more confident with the mechanics and the enemies you fight. The different attack spells fulfill different roles and niches, and a charged up spell grants passive bonuses and a special all-out version of the regular attack spell. Collecting spell tomes improves existing spells and unlocks additional features, allowing the player to become absurdly powerful, yet still quite fragile.There's a lot of fine details I could talk about, but they're beyond the scope of a steam review. So if you want my final thoughts, I put them right at the top.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, underrated gem for sure.Fun and unique, especially the magic.You can really tell that care and passion were put into it.Devs, please make a sequel.More review:I found myself having fun and even smiling before even fighting any enemies. If you run out of stamina Nobeta falls on her face and makes a cute sound. If this were a feature in any other game I would hate it but it just works here and I wouldn’t have it any other way.Lots of souls-likes struggle to have identity but this game has it in spades. The combat and magic feel fresh and creative, not like something you would find in other games like it.The style is super cute and charming, but also pretty dark especially if you read the item descriptions. I found them quite interesting but it has little bearing on the world you are interacting with, so it’s completely optional to read them. They have nice art though, so worth looking at.There is a story with cutscenes and dialogue as-well. It is pretty good, nothing revolutionary but it had some cool moments. The story serviced the gameplay and tone well, it’s not much more than it needs to be. I certainly prefer this sort of unobtrusive story telling style, and you can always skip the cutscenes if you are a pleb like that.The difficulty is well tuned, some bosses might have a bit more health than necessary but it doesn’t really make them any less good. Speaking of boss fights, they just get better and better as the game goes on.I like how there is a give and take with the magic, you can shoot it normally or charge it up and fire a big, basically different, spell. While charged up, instead of firing it, you can hold onto it for a bit and gain a unique buff, but you lose the buff if you fire the charged spell. It all works together and each magic element has its own unique identity. Just really good stuff.Banger game all the way through.Nobeta falling on her face is still cute and funny even after beating the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A short and fun little soulslike that I can easily recommend if you're a beginner or just looking for something on the more accessible side of the genre. Gameplay still punishes mistakes as much as you would expect from a game like this, but losing souls upon death (a big hang-up for me back in the day when I was trying to get into Darks Souls and the like) is optional, depending on whether you resort to the cursed healing items, which are free, plentiful and effective but apply a soul loss penalty (a percentage loss of souls on death that increases the more you use them between bonfire visits). It actually strikes me as a bit of clever design, as either you accept the risk of losing progress to your next level and learn to use heals more carefully, or if you're a greedy motherhubbard and forego them you learn that much faster to tread carefully through levels, as well as how to handle fights safely (after all, death still means loss of progress to the next bonfire, as well as whatever souls you have to spend to buy more non-cursed restoration items you might have used). Either way you're building skills that will benefit you in other games like this.Combat design is another part I think was done particularly well. As a point of comparison, when playing a mage in Elden Ring (no judgments here, I am a fellow magic-using weenie) the winning strat is generally to keep your distance and shoot down foes before they get into attacking range. It's effective, but also means you don't engage in a good chunk of what makes a souslike's gameplay what it is. Little Witch Nobeta addresses keep-away game this in two ways. One, the only thing shorter than Nobeta's height is her MP bar, and it doesn't take long at all to run out if you're unloading on a boss from a distance. Two, every time you land a melee hit, dodge through an attack or successfully parry one, you regenerate a bit of MP. And with that, you now have a mage who can eventually nuke everything from orbit, but still wants to get up close and personal with targets all the time. Time to learn how to watch for dodge and parry windows, as well as when it's safe to sneak in a few whacks with your staff. And I won't lie, seeing those blue wisps when an enemy attack is properly dodged makes for a nice little dopamine shot to the brain that Fromsoft's dodge rolls can't match.Sekiro taught me this genre can be fun even if I'm terrible at it, Elden Ring taught me I can actually win with enough patience and planning. Little Witch Nobeta is one that, if I had the opportunity to go back in time a few years and tell my past self to not sleep on the version I was gifted back then, I would probably take it. Perhaps if that happened, the core skills I would have built could have made my later quests to rescue a dragon boy and become Elden Lord go much more smoothly the first time around.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers for areas in this reviewHaving just beaten ng+ deranged armor and cleared the entire underground area, I will say that the first time through seems like a tutorial for the complete form of combat. The game is like the fast paced respawn of super meat boy meets dark souls, where unless you use the lowest grade of healing you never lose any souls. the combat is really smooth with all actions being cancellable with the roll that also regenerates mana. But the unique thing that makes this game stand out to me is both the charging mechanism that provides both a powerful spell and passive ability and the ability to parry projectiles and melee, but instead of getting a riposte you get mana and health back, which kinda reminds me of doom's glory kill. Combine this with no estus-like rechargeable healing and the passive effect of the fire elemental and the insane dmg of lightning, and the ultra buffed enemies in NG+, and you are in a situation where you are given multiple powerful tools and to make it through you have to use them all. PS: for the bossfights, one parry can heal you from 30% to 70% of your health, skip the charging time, and once upgraded force a stagger on the boss so I would really advise getting good at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to the store being swamped with terribly cobbled together games made with kawaii aesthetics to make a quick buck, this game could easily be mistakenly overlooked.In truth, this game is extremely charming with quite beautifully done art assets for the HUD, and each of the crosshairs for each magical element. I also am impressed by the sound design which adds an incredible amount of weight to your attacks and the game itself. The magic could very easily come off as boring or bland, but the sound design makes each ability feel powerful! The mechanics are tight, and while combat can be surprisingly difficult, I never once found myself blaming the game for my failure. After you die a couple times and learn how each enemy behaves, you should be able to push through with much less trouble each time.The game itself is a kinda bland dungeon crawl with interesting but few enemy types placed around, until you reach the boss of the stage, which is where the game truly shines. Each boss looks fantastic and has a unique and interesting set of attacks and phases that will have you learning the best approach while dying over and over again, lol.While writing this review I am stuck at the 3rd (Lava world boss), and while being able to defeat the first phase easily, I'm stuck at the second phase! My only criticism is that with some boss battles, the attacks have no sound cues or have no telegraphed movement, which means it's literally impossible to beat some bosses the 1st time around with sheer skill, and the game is forcing you to die over and over and learn the boss battle patterns like a dance until you get it right.However, please buy this game, as I hope to see it succeed and grow into something more. It's definitely worth the money and is incredibly charming. Protect Nobeta!!!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the only non Fromsoft souls-like that I liked. The spells and how they can be used to solve some environmental puzzles are well made. _childDocuments_.review: To put it simply: Little Witch Nobeta is an action/adventure game where you use magic spells to destroy enemies in an old castle on your quest to reach the throne.The combat has a fun loop of charging spells to destroy enemies and using your staff melee attacks/dodges/parries to refill your MP. There are a total of 4 elements you will obtain during the game, and they're all fun to use and useful in different situations. There are secret areas and bosses scattered around which makes exploring fun. The lack of a map might confuse or irritate some.The game has a New Game+ mode after you finish it, allowing you to start over with your current status. Enemies are beefed up so it won't be entirely one sided.I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and plan to play it more just to keep experiencing it. I sincerely hope we get some DLC and see more from this franchise. A prequel would be great, as the in-game lore items paint the picture of a truly terrifying world outside of the castle.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta (LWN) is an indie project I’ve been following since 2020 demo because of the gameplay mechanics and of course, cute anime girl!, developed by Taiwanese team named Pupuya Games. Please keep it mind this is subjective opinion based on my experience (19 hrs. - early access / 7 hrs. – full release). You may disagree and enjoy the game without nitpicking which is totally fine.The game tells the story in the perspective of Nobeta, a skillful witch who is seeking the truth of her past by descending into the depths of mysterious castle. It’s a simple plot and yet somehow intriguing because of cryptic dialogues and mystery. I enjoy learning a bit of character background and tragic story related to crafted soul. The sympathy toward non-living matter is one thing I learn from the story which can be complicated feelings, but still carry sense of comfort and connectedness between characters. I wish the game has more screenplays for each character to build up and fully develop.The dark gloomy world and cute character design in anime aesthetic is such a nice contrast and sweet spot for people who prefer light-hearted story and less graphic. In-game animation work and combat feedback are very well done even it sometimes looks bit stiff in cutscene and awkward camera angle. I also appreciate minor changes in animation and voice tone which tie to a certain part of the story.LWN plays like third-person shooter with some soul-like elements. Player progresses and fights through each area interconnected by small hubs and gate. Defeat enemy to earn soul as upgrade currency and lose some if you die. Exploration rewards shortcut, useful consumable, spell tomes (only way to upgrade elemental spells), and collectable which reveal a piece of backstory of game world. Goddess statue serves as checkpoint, allows player to upgrade stats (pretty straightforward and self-explained), buy items, fast travel, and change Nobeta costume. The world resets and common enemies respawn every time player revisits the statue. This is pretty much soul-like formula if you’re not familiar with this genre.LWN emphasizes on positioning ranged combat with melee backup. You start with arcane spell and learn more spells as you progress. I like how each spell represents and function similar to IRL firearms (ice – machine gun, fire – shotgun, thunder - sniper). Each spells also can be fully charged to alter additional effects or perform powerful charged shot.Your movement and evasion are tied to stamina bar while casting spell is limited to mana gauge in order to prevent player from spamming. You can gain mana back by direct-hit melee, dodging attack, or counter magic (melee attack right before the enemy hits player). It may requires timing and practice for different enemy/boss but the payoff is worth and satisfying. Dodge or melee during casting spell also greatly boosts charge speed which comes in handy when your ability is not fully optimized and timing is crucial.There are also minor features like headshot damage, body part damage (some bosses), enemy does friendly fire, and movement tricks allow player to bypass or reach some hidden area. Probably not by intended design, but it’s fun to mess aroundThe combat in general is probably the strongest point of the game which keeps me replaying from time to time including aggressive and tricky boss fight. Death penalty might be more generous compared to other soul-like games, but the full release still deliver skill-based and high-risk high-reward combat mechanics. Simple yet engagingHowever, there are some aspects of both level and gameplay design that could have done better. The environment has no improvement from early access; they consist of bland and generic looking hall and long corridor, full of empty space. The later stages might have different tone, but you still notice tons of reused assets and same looking environment/structure throughout the campaign. I think adding detail and interaction could benefit the environmental storytelling and relationship between characters (especially Nobeta and Black Cat, both need more screenplay to develop).The game also suffers from lack of interesting enemy design and variation especially non-boss types. You’ll mostly encounter same dark spirit and dolls with slight change of skin and attack pattern. There are few encounters that encourage player to utilize special ability of full charged spell like breaking shield or interrupt deadly move, but that’s about it. Once I got Lv.3-4 fire and lightning spell and abuse dodge/absorption ability. Things become unbalanced as they can trivialize and breeze through most fights (Arcane full charge is also great for knocking boss from distance). You don’t expect depths of elemental-based combat here but treat it like typical third-person shooter. Similar to puzzles which only involve specific spells and timing for couple times. I just personally wish the elemental spells play much more important role and expand its creativity.My expectation is probably bit high from this indie title. Considering that the amount of budget could went into mentioned aspect instead of focusing on marketing and promotion.There is technical report by players, but I had no major issue or game-breaking bug during 26 hrs. of total playtime. Most common problems I found are enemy stuck in some level geometry (mostly pile of rock or between pillars) and visual glitch on grass sprite. Performance is solid for Unity game with stable 60 FPS (Win7, GTX1050ti, 8 GB RAM, 1080p on max settings) and responsive keyboard control.The game offers two based difficulties and new game plus which carry all player progression. NG+ is required if you aim to max out stats and duplicate tome to fully upgrade spells. Optional costume can be obtained by specific condition and animated comic which include jokes and backstory of each doll (and they take space more than an actual game).LWN has decent amount of soundtrack from boss battle theme to sad and depressing main theme. They are good along with ambient soundtrack. My only gripe is few sections have no background music at all. For sound effects, most are strong and punchy which help to enhance combat feedback. Plus, ambulance siren on critical health is so goofy and I love it.The game features fully Japanese voice over dialogue and collectable lore. Boss characters are voiced by Hololive members (Popular JP VTubers). Either you are VTuber / VA fan or not, I personally enjoy their work and respect voice talents that put their effort and personality into each character despite amount of their short screenplay (ignore those negative review bomb that have nothing to do with game but just pure anti). Voice-over index of each collectable is surprising even I found it’s unnecessary and could be improved better in-game story/dialogue.Overall, I do enjoy what the game has offered. Maxed out everything and complete multiple playthroughs. It has many interesting ideas and utilities of each spells even the some aspects feel underdeveloped and hold its full potential. It’s worth full price if you’re looking for anime action game with decent challenge or being completionist like me. I hope the developers expand their in-game creativity and improve wherever their next project would be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. It has great mechanics and plenty of content for a $8 to $9 game. There are even some simple puzzles here and there that tie in with the magic mechanics.If I had to say anything negative about the game, it would be that some boss attack hit boxes are bigger than expected and the counter magic system is tricky to nail down. You can get combo'd easily if you miss the timing to dodge or you don't watch your stamina which causes you to trip when you run out. Also you run out of mana extremely quickly which makes kiting more difficulty as in order to gain more mana, you either have to wait and bide your time during a boss fight while dodging their attacks or go in to melee them to regain mana. If you mess up then you can lose half your health very quickly. The game doesn't have much of a story or lore either like Dark Souls but that's completely fine.I'm glad I found this game. It's still in early access and if it isn't finished yet, then I really can't wait to see what other content it will get. If you enjoy souls-like games and want to play as a cute loli wizard, then Loli Souls is right up your alley. 10/10 would run out of stamina and faceplant the ground again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful, which is rare for either early access games or souls clones, let alone a game that's both. This one pulls it off beautifully. Level design is fairly good, very nonlinear and lots of hidden goodies. Hell, I never even found the upgrades to Arcane. I fought all the bosses except the secret boss with all level 1 spells just because I wasn't expecting the level design to be so deep, and just wasn't expecting there to be that many upgrades in an early access game.Speaking of bosses, I encountered a sharp difficulty spike on the Monica fight. Since I hadn't really been grinding and didn't find the spell upgrades, I had a very rough time with her compared to steamrolling Tania and the Specter Armor. My only complaint about Tania is her lightning ball hurricane stunlocking you; if one part of the attack hits you, everything after it hits you. It's not unfair though, since it can be countered / dodged with good timing. Monica, however, just seemed to have too much health. I'm not sure if they're planning on putting another boss between the two, or normalizing the difficulty curve somehow else, but Monica kicked my ass for about an hour. And then I found out that there's a 2nd phase with even harder hitting attacks. Let's just say that of my 8 hours of playtime, 4.5 hours is just Monica.The visuals are great! I'm someone who loves Gothic settings, Victorian era apparel, and cute things in general. I just find this game so damn cute that it's sometimes hard to remember that I'm playing a souls clone, and that the beautiful dolls are actually trying to murder the precious little witch (there actually were several moments where I died due to being distracted by thinking "oh wow, she's so pretty!" for some enemies). My only complaint here is the enemies that just look like ghosts are everywhere, and they just seem too generic. They might just be placeholders or something tho, so idk.The game's real weak point is the tutorials. The big one being the charged ice spell and the three fire obelisks: it tells you to lock on to them (click the right stick), but means to target all three (left trigger and point at them) and then fire the spell. I'm sure they'll be fixed eventually.Anyway, I give this game a solid 9/10, and I can't wait for the full version.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta allows the player to live out their fantasy of being a loli witch in an anime. Wait, what? You’re saying you never had that fantasy and that I’m weird for even mentioning something like that? Well, first off, my feelings are hurt. Second, fine, you might not have that fantasy, but there’s a lot more to the game than just this.	And if you’re worried about spoilers, rejoice: this review is spoiler-free!—----------- And truth be told, a lot of the actual gameplay elements you often see in games of the genre are here. You get your dodge-roll, your heavy hitting enemies with plenty of opportunities to die, your interconnected map with some shortcuts here and there…  Allow me to explain.You play as a witch, the titular Nobeta, throughout the game. When you think of a witch, what exactly do you envision? Pointy hats, flying brooms, staffs and spells? Well, I’m pleased to say most of those are in - sorry, brooms, you didn’t make the cut this time, try again next game. Nobeta’s iconic outfit has a pointy hat, but most relevant to us at the moment are the other two elements.  There are 4 elements of attack spells in the game, all of which are unlocked as you play, plus two other support elements that add passive abilities: one that increases your air game, with abilities like double jump, and one that gives and improves parry. Casting spells, for example, uses up MP, and one of the main ways to get MP back is by hitting your enemy with melee moves. At the same time, spells can be chanted to give them special effects. Gameplay-wise, this means pressing a button and waiting for a bar to slowly charge. Your character is also slowed while this happens and becomes more vulnerable to attacks. You can, however, still dodge, and in fact, dodging attacks at the right moment makes the chant charge up faster. One of the elements’ chant power is actually to massively enhance your melee attacks. Both sides of the combat end up complementing each other, even though magic ended up doing most of the damage in my playthrough. In fact, late game upgrades end up more or less being vastly overpowered, even on the highest of the two difficulty settings.While this system is nice and works well, it’s also very… simple, and not necessarily in a good way. There is no way to defend, for example, which means the parry involves just attacking at the last possible moment that you’re about to take damage. It’s a risky move, and the parry window for the un-upgraded version of the parry is not good.  You start with 4 slots, and can find bag expansions hidden around the world to increase that number. What you then choose to hold is up to you, but there are 6 types of items. You can both buy these items and collect them from the environment, but if you have no money and you’re stuck at a boss fight, you might find yourself letting the boss kill you just to get the health drops to respawn and fill up your item bar with healing before attempting for good again. Sure, you can level different stats, but your moveset and your equipments will remain the same throughout the game. Well, kinda. As you play, you can find items that are very well hidden that upgrade your magic spells. That’s the only way you can enhance them, and it isn’t something that’s playthrough dependent. The chests will be there for all players, and all spells will always be usable by everyone that finds them. So basically, the only variation possible between playthroughs is what stats you level up. If you want a different build aside from that, you’ll have to force yourself to not use some of your spells. You can’t even change your weapon - your original staff is all you get. But what exactly can you expect to fight with this combat? Well, turns out, quite a few things!  There are also lots of reskins, but those change their attack pattern quite drastically. Quite often, from any given zone, I can see and snipe enemies that are ahead in the zone if I pay attention to my surroundings and notice these opportunities, which is something I really appreciate in a game like this. No joke, a lot of my zones were at least partially cleared before I started traversing them. And speaking of enemy variety,  Monica was my favorite. It employs the one tactic that always gets me: mystery. From the beginning, you’re Nobeta, and all you know is that you’re looking for the throne room of a specific castle. You begin the game entering said castle, and soon find yourself a guide: a black talking cat. Even if the story isn’t anything extremely memorable, the way it’s slowly revealed is done really well, which I always appreciate. Personally, I’m a massive fan, even though I don’t actually watch anime. Weird, huh? The level design is… not the best. There’s not much variation in the actual environments for a lot of the game. But again, it ended up being something I could overlook.  You even get a voiceover option for them. Some of the tracks that were there, especially the main menu and the credits tracks, were good, but there were plenty of moments that lacked background music, relying instead just on ambient noise and the player’s sound effects. Some others had background music that fit the ambience, but wasn’t really noticeable.  This does mean that the game’s only language for voices is japanese.  And if you want more of this world, rejoice: there are animated comics unlockable with the collectibles you get, and they’re pretty nice! If you do pick up the game, I hope you enjoy it - and feel free to hit me up so we can chat about it. I’m always down for meeting new people, especially those who share my gaming passion.

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, I found myself thoroughly immersed in the magical world of Little Witch Nobeta. As a fan of Souls-like games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring, I relished the challenge this game offers, especially on the highest difficulty. But this game isn't merely a rehash of the challenging elements that are synonymous with the Souls genre. No, Little Witch Nobeta stands out in its own right as a unique and compelling adventure.If you're someone who appreciates the progression, strength-building, and magic that define Souls games, then I wholeheartedly recommend this. Little Witch Nobeta shines in these aspects, offering a deeply engaging experience for those willing to sink their teeth into it.The visual style is anime-inspired, which I absolutely adore. This isn't just a stylistic choice; it intertwines with the game's narrative to give life to a beautiful story. The commitment and passion that the developers poured into this game is palpable. This extends to everyone involved in the project, from the voice actors to the animators, the set designers, the translators, and perhaps others I'm overlooking.Little Witch Nobeta does incorporate some puzzles, which provide a nice variation to the gameplay. They might seem a bit tricky initially, but once you get the hang of them, they're not overly complicated. However, the heart of the game lies in following the story while simultaneously leveling up and getting stronger. You can grind to your heart's content, making your character as powerful as you'd like, which I found to be a satisfying aspect of the game.In short, I loved Little Witch Nobeta. It's a testament to the beauty that can be achieved when developers infuse their projects with love and dedication. Thank you to everyone involved for creating such a memorable gaming experience. If you haven't played it yet, do yourself a favor and dive into this enchanting world. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think it's worth the asking price, even if Nobeta is very cute. Buy it on sale if you can.--- and only starts to come together if you read through the dialogue after beating bosses in the Trial Tower and also read all of the item descriptions, that is, if you bother to find them all. The world building through all of this could have been done better. To me, it's very much "anime", but I don't think that it needs to also be generic on top of all of that. The Trial Tower lore information is nice, and shows promise in improving this area of the game.--- There isn't much enemy variety, and a lot of them are quite lame. Broken doll, broken doll 2, broken doll 3. Ghost. Ghost with hands. Ghost with mouth... And some are even red! Amazing, lol. --- It has an anime style to it, but it's nothing special. Dungeon walls, cave walls, dungeon walls with lava lighting, dark dungeon walls, dungeon walls with some grass... Areas will start to feel very samey, and even more so when you go through them again at the end of the game to close out the story.--- You will soon learn why this is annoying if you don't already. You have to confirm you're skipping and then once the screen gets back to you, the boss is already beaming you in the face with an attack sometimes. (Matters less if you're a gaming god.)--- You can cheese through the areas that are supposed to stop you until you use the mechanic correctly, so you'll never actually understand what you were supposed to learn. I personally got past one such roadblock without using the intended mechanic to pass through, so I had no idea about it until much later.--- For the current asking price of $24.99, there are better games to buy.--- You get to snipe fools with magic and beat them up with melee attacks to fill your mana bar. You can "absorb" attacks to basically parry it and get more mana without taking damage. It's fun to try and land these. Makes me wish there were more enemies to fight!!--- I think thunder is the best, but they're all pretty cool. The charged modes actually doing something other than "bigger damage" is very nice. I think this could be improved and fleshed out more, but I appreciate what's there.--- Cute outfits. This will heal your heart as you get beaten down by the bosses.--- Without these, this game would be a joke, even on Advanced Mode. These guys don't show you any mercy, and will force many gamers to grind for more levels to stand a chance against them. Honestly, these things kicked my face in. I had to grind levels like I isekai'd as the "hero" with some OP skills. And even then, I tasted defeat more than I'd like to admit. (I only played on Advanced Mode, so I don't know how less of a threat they are on the lower difficulty.)--- Looping shortcuts, a few ambushes, and hidden treasures will be a constant. Basically, what you'd expect from a souls-like.--- Introduces a new twist on the old bosses, and adds more lore. I'm glad to see this included.All in all, I hope to see a sequel to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Witch Nobeta is a 3D Action Platforming Game where you play as a Braindead Duck with a Shotgun. This is more fun than it sounds.You can say its souls like, but aside from having a dodge roll and being difficult, it's REALLY not? There's no leaving souls behind when you die, the camera and movement feels much different, and again its partially a platformer. It has a very in-depth world which you can glean through a variety of collectable lore objects, however aside from being lore objects, they do nothing for you. If you're not interested in the world, which you don't really need to be to enjoy the story, then you don't have to bother with them. That's fine, though a missed opportunity. The story itself is tepid but serviceable, nothing you'll want to sing to high heavens, but it does its job for the 8-10 hour campaign (probably a lot shorter if you're really good, or a bit longer if you really want to try to explore every nook and cranny to find upgrades and items). Nobeta herself is cute but bland, and her cat is just a raving ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who I don't like. Still, the gameplay is really the focus. The gunplay is fantastic, you have a staff with a few modes. Arcane, Fire, Lightning, Ice, which correlate to Rifle, Shotgun, Sniper, and Machine Gun. Each of these modes also has an ultimate, which you charge up and unleash to deal devastating damage. The bosses are BUILT around this mechanic, you're intended to charge and get free magic off of mana you get from dodging and attacking, speeding up the charge and allowing you to knock huge chunks off of health. Some of the bosses were a bit brutal, but if you can manage your dodges and figure out good strategies, you'll be fine. The walk backs are often not too bad either.It's a fun game! I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is shockingly a better title holder of "anime souls" than Code Vein. The combat and bossfights, as well as some mobs, are designed and programmed so much tighter than the latter that it's surprising that this was all made by one person. Serious props to the Monica bossfight, especially her second phase, which is frankly Bed of Chaos from Dark Souls 1 done right. At first she comes off as a the same kind of annoying puzzle boss, until you realize that there are tricks to counter every part of her attack; even the move where she destroys parts of the arena. Code Vein doesn't have any of this.I'm really looking forward to the finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, Definitely would be a must play when Fully ReleasedPlease take this review with a grain of salt esp the Cons, as it is an early access titlePROS:-Super polished and engaging combat system with a working dodge/ parry system -Amazing Bosses and boss mechanics, super fun -Well paced combat-explore-puzzle ratio altho at times the puzzles can be too child friendly following games like zelda etc where it takes no brain power to figure out what you have to do-Anime meets Souls, The environment, design, storytelling are all great -Super lovable characters and memorable designs -Good replay value even in EA with New Game Plus as well as different difficulties-Devs have a clear road map and always follow up and inform the community of how development is goingCONS:-Lack of enemy variety, can get very repetitive -The are designs while very nice to look at, gets old quickly, not alot of area variety it feels like, castle-castle with fungus-castle on fire- castle ruined-If you're only interested in 1 play-through and done, there are 4 levels that you can knock out in a 3 hour sitting -No voice acting (YET) except for the cat, which honestly should have been left out, the cats meows are ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE Personal Opinion: *MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS*I would like to see more mature enemy variety, The bosses and characters that exist right now are super lovable and amazing plays on childhood feelings and emotions but maybe there should be a darker character, not one whose intentions are warped child like emotions, but rather a more serious actual malicious character that might serve as character development for Nobeta, as adorable and lovable as she is, she's ABSOLUTELY naive and sometimes borderline dumb
