_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;Putting uwooh and cnuy aside, game has good substance and solid mechanics that makes it not only fun to play multiple playthroughs with, but also accounts for variable playstyle so you could experiment and have fun. Pick it up if you like soulsborne, unique and fun action magic combat, or you just simply like the cute and funny. Hot take: Better magic combat mechanics than the entire Souls series and Elden Ring.Most of the negative reviews are from TW bros that couldn't cope with Hololive being included in the game, or the controversy with Simon Creative. While I personally do not like Hololive and the simps, I do not care much if it is in the game or used to promote the game. Even though I personally prefer professional voice actors (Konomi Kohara did a fantastic job as the main characters), as long as the talents deliver their job fairly well (which they did except Vanessa's VA), I support it. What I do not support is review bombing a game just because you do not like a minority of the people working in the game, invalidating the efforts of vast majority of other developers's involvement in the game.About the publisher Simon Creative's controversy, I am not from TW but I did some research about it. In short, Simon Creative seized copyright of some works and is strict towards doujin culture creating doujinshi of works with their copyright. Therefore, TW bros are boycotting Simon Creative, and part of it is by review bombing this game. While I support doujin culture and boycotting of trash companies, please do not invalidate the game developer's (Pupuya Games) work in creating this game. I understand that because of Simon Creative's involvement in this game, a lot of the game's potential is wasted because of budget wasted in Hololive marketing, manga spin-offs and such trash before the game's foundation is even built. But the game itself is not a bad game still, and it is worth the price. Please do not bark up the wrong tree and destroy everything Pupuya Games tried to build.Though it is only from what I gathered based on observation. If there is anything wrong about Simon Creative, TW bros feel free to correct or add anything in the comments.Precedence:I played on advanced difficulty and I am a soulsborne vet. I play this game like sekiro, often trying to parry and absorb so that I could have a high octance magic battle. It is relatively easy to go through the game if you were to play cautiously. I also played and liked it a lot back in early access.Pros:-Variable play-style. You can be a p**sy and stay far away to shoot and only melee to get back some mana, or you can go full action and use counter-magic to constantly charge up your spells under a few seconds and annihilate the enemies like a chad.-Great character designs.-The main 3 spells are varied and each serve their purpose. There are no useless spells. However I'd say the 4th spell, the lightning spell is a bit too overpowered. Once you have lighting spell you basically do not have to use other spells.  .-Complex magic mechanics. Although you can't mix magic, you can switch magic on the fly and truly dish out successive casting. Spells have 3 main kinds of usage: shoot, channeled state, and channeled shoot. Every spell plays out differently and it is very fun to explore.-Great boss design and fights. Tania, Monica, Vanessa and . It truly brings out their unique souls-like magic combat style. -Fluid magic combat. Melee is purposely designed to be a bit slow and clunky so that your focus is using magic. My personal favorite however is using the empowered melee fire aura for both bosses and mobs.-NG+ enemies scales up, so it cant be said to be easier than before. (Unless you spam lightning lmao)-Great voice acting. Konomi Kohara carried this game so damn hard by voicing 3 main characters. While I won't reach and say that she has a great voice range, but the tone for each character is diverse, well done and true to the character. I do not care much about Hololive, but they did a relatively good job on Tania and Monica. However, Vanessa in my opinion is voiced subpar and monotoned.-Great rewards for exploration. -Great atmospheric music that suits the environment.-Main character development, . Nobeta is relatively well written in the story, as well as the black cat.Cons (and feedbacks): -Most of the voice acting is in the item description. While I appreciate lore narration, this budget could be utilized far better in the game experience itself.-Stamina bar too far from the center. It's hard to keep track of your stamina when you're in action. I suggest the 3 bars (Stamina, Hp, and Mana) switch places with item bar and keep stamina bar on top of the 2 other bars. Other than that, UI design is great and easy to understand.-Bland level design. The mechanisms and platforming is well designed, however the colour scheme and texture of the walls and environment stays around the same. It makes it harder to remember if I have walked through a part of the hallway, when all the hallways look about the same. Especially so for this kind of game where you have to know the map layout by heart.-Sub-par Chinese to English translation. I understand both Chinese and English, so I can tell where it's coming from. But it still needs to be improved.- .-Questionable marketing of the game. Just do not interact with the official social media pages unless you're a degenerate. I would have preferred it if they just keep it cute and wholesome without the lewd. Thankfully the game itself is not largely affected by the degenerate marketing except one skin. They were only sucking money from the degenerates to fund their game. -Needs quality of life changes, such as :1) being able to access the statue without praying to it first. (adding "pray" option to the menu after interacting with statue)2) auto-skip boss cut-scenes after the first time.3) Improve lava death animation.4) Stamina should not be decreased when running out of combatAbsorption gives a bit too much benefit. I understand it is difficult to time and as much as I love it, it is pretty overpowered. However, it does make the game more fun, being able to instantly charge mana, spell, heal and knockback stagger bosses all in the same time, so I am not sure how to handle it. I really love it tho.Expectations not fulfilled in full game from the early access:- English translation is still pretty ass.- Expected more type of magic, but only levels are added to each magic.- Not as long as I hoped it would be, but I suppose it is long enough for an indie game of this caliber.- Nothing changed at all for the early levels that was part of early access (except item collection).Overall, I give 9/10. Might be a bit biased despite the flaws I've mentioned, but the souls-like combat is my thing, cute things is my thing, difficult video game is my thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple game, but the levels are nice, the graphics is cute the game is dubbed... surprisingly (but a welcome surprise), the collectibles lore is interesting (especially considering how they integrate with the manga that a user has translated, thanks btw!).The story, for what I've played so far at least, is pretty simplistic (not talking about the lore of the game and it's world, just the main character story, the first 5 hours of it), but the interactions between the characters that I've seen so far are nice. I suspect that there will be more to be added to the story as I progress, but I have no idea how far in the game I am honestly.The gameplay is nice, surprisingly there is input buffer, the lock on is decent and even the shooting works great, even on a controller. The different type of magic are all pretty cool (though, I guess you don't really use the first type after you unlock any of the others), some times the hitboxes are not great, but for the most part it plays like a well made simplified souls like.There isn't a huge variety of enemies (again, in the first 5 hours at least), they the ones that are there are alright.The game is much harder than the demo (the free demo on Itch), which I enjoy, it would have been too easy if it was left like it was in the demo, playing on "advanced" which is the equivalent of the demo "normal" difficulty and the bump in how hard the game is is definitely there, but the game is not unfair, except for one boss so far that had me farming for a bit.The level up system is easy but nice, the descriptions are clear about what you are upgrading and what effects you can expect, though, they don't really show how much of an improvement there is from one level to another.I'd suggest reading the manga chapter related to the bosses after finishing the game or after beating the boss, in theory all the chapters are a prequel to the game, but just to be safe. Gives a lot of background story and makes you empathize with them more (at least, for the one I've read so far).I would say get the game demo on Itch io and if you like it go for it, the demo is much easier and it doesn't have dubbing and some of the sounds, but it's nice regardless.Update:Actually nevermind, the level design is pretty cool and stuff is interconnected, there some cool side areas which are completely optional, fairly large, and offer a ton of rewards and lore filled items.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very well made experience, beautiful graphics, with simple but compelling game play which can be very easy to rage inducing depending on the difficulty you select.normal will require a considerable amount of grinding. since you won't get anywhere near enough otherwise.easy is easy with little to no grinding expected.the challenge of this experience comes from the bosses and to a lesser degree fodder found later in the game.of the 3 bosses in the current version. i only felt the 3rd was unfair do to it being 2 battles in a row with no checkpoint and...both bosses are capable of killing you instantly by knocking you into lava.making health upgrades for that boss less useful.the magic you obtain looks great and is fun to play with! adding simple yet entertaining strategy.the story almost feels like it was given away already. but i'm interested to see where the rest of it goes.there were some grammar errors found in the game. some examples arelevel 2 wind - "dodge" is spelled wrong"lightning" (from box in challenge area) is spelled wrongOVERALLthis is a fantastic game, i highly recommend this!

_childDocuments_.review: Done all achievements and can finally review this game!Story is nice, and the battle is manageable enough now after putting the game away for one year and also after finishing Sekiro first.Play as a witch, so the battle mostly done with magic and you have to manage the mana.And not long in the story, you can parry, yes PARRY (aka absorption magic) where you have to melee with your staff right before an attack connect, and yes you can melee bonk with the staff if you want, but that's mostly to regain mana and to finish charge enchant faster. And also yes, there's a click shooting, and there's also a charged mode which of course consume more mana and take time to charge (aka enchant).The chests hunting here are not that many and it's actually important to do for new spells or upgrading already gained ones, so you can just use guide if needed, no need to feel ashamed 'cause there's achievement tied to it regarding getting all chests in one run.The boss fights, they can range from fun enough despite getting folded around, to almost annoying when you made a mistake in the last bit of boss health and died miserably. But all in all, it's a very rewarding experiences. And from my experiences, I almost thought that each bosses has one of the four elements as weakness, but I think it isn't, so you can just blast them all away with any spells you want (this is if you decided to go NG+, since not all elements are open right away, because the chests that have the books are apparently almost tied to the each of the map).The trial tower, or if you play Sekiro, is like the gauntlet of strength, but worry not if you died, you don't have to restart from the very first boss, but just fight the boss u lost to, your stats are stuck at default, with the only thing you can purchase are the skill books and healing items in the other goddess statue. And for more pressure either to motivate you or to mock you, there's the "how long you fought this boss" and "how many times you get folded by this boss" counter alongside it, which will sum up all after you done all 8 bosses, so good luck there, champ. And oh yea, the trial tower is after you beat base game once, so feel the bosses from base game first then get wrecked all over again.OVERWHELMINGLY RECOMMENDED for souls-like enjoyers and if you like cute anime girl to blast enemies with magic spells! xD

_childDocuments_.review: [Review written 03/30/2021 during Early Access, update to come upon official release]This game has a lot of charm, smooth controls, fun combat and an amazing potential upon release. If you want a quick recommendation, I highly suggest buying it.Playing as a young (smol) witch who can dodge, double jump and utilize four different elements to kill enemies, your goal is to make your way through different stages in pursuit of reaching 'The Throne'.This game has been labelled somewhat of a Souls-Like, whether ironically or in full seriousness. While your attacks mainly consist of range-based magic, Souls-Like is a good representation of combat and progression in a general sense. LWN does not have the same depth of a Souls game in terms of customizability, world building and combat. But the strength of this game lies in the fact that it handles combat and atmosphere with simplicity and polish. Controls are responsive, magic is fun to use, and each stage is small but unique.The cast of enemies is small, but each has enough character to feel genuine and take advantage of combat and art style. Bosses all feel like worthwhile and memorable encounters without overstaying their welcome.Tania is best girl.If you want something a little more chill with a charming main character, style and tight controls, I recommend picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best indie Souls-like out there. Since the first beta, plenty of new amazing games in the genre released, but I think Nobeta still manages to hold its ground by giving the formula a new twist (aka a shooter-like magic system). The combat is well polished, the level design very well made (despite looking kinda bland most of the time, which made me get lost more often than I'd like to admit) and the characters look amazing. If you like Dark Souls and cute anime girls, you won't be disappointed.The game was surprisingly short though (took me 6-7 hours to beat), only being about twice as long as the previous early access version. It also felt a bit too easy, as the only boss I didn't beat first try was the last one, which only took like 3 attempts. Looking forward to trying the hard difficulty once the developers fix the bug.It took them a while, but the developers truly made an amazing game, and I look forward to seeing what other games they can make in the future, hopefully with a larger team as well. I hope Pupuya recovers quick and gives us more cute and funny games!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice cute game so far, for being just out of demo. It has 2 difficulty modes, with the easier one allowing for less frustration, but also allowing you to play with a wide range of strategies. Many difficulties can be made somewhat easier through some minimal grinding as well which may help out players who need an edge. What it lacks in polish and detail it makes up for in good design, though only time will tell if the story can keep up with the gameplay.Pros:-Cute and funny protagonist -Cute animations -most model designs are good-fairly cool magic so far-reasonably interesting story though we will see if it can become anything exceptional later-memorable enemy designs (though some get recycled, and their aren't that many types) if they can keep changing it up after each boss it would be great.-unique boss fights (though the second one fell a bit short for me)-a couple nice little secret's here and there, would love to see more side paths and rooms!-A solid foundation for a great environment.Cons:-Movement feels just a little clunky to me (may be intentional)-My area this game would MOST benefit from is more attention to detail in the levels, some parts look nice but ultimately it felt a little sterile and empty.-in the same vein, i think slight changes to lighting could go a long way to making the castle look more beautiful.-i felt one of the puzzles where annoying due to poor (maybe lost in translation) tutorials. The targeting for the ice spell is NOT the same as the target lock mechanic, and this took me an embarrassing amount of time to find out on my own.I feel like this is a very nice game for the price, especially if they add a reasonable bit more content. It is of course early access and indie so I can't expect the world, but they have made something with allot of personalty to it, that has solid gameplay and is nice to look at. I highly recommend to anyone who likes the style and wants a little challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Summary: Wait until full release and/or possibly a sale. Currently too short, 2~3 hour experience.If it looks fun to you, it probably will be. It was for me, too. I struggle to recommend it purely because of it's duration... But I know I likely won't remember to update it when the last 3 zones are added.Combat: Souls-like elements in regards to leveling up and needing to dodge in boss encounters - but different enough that it feels more like it's own thing. The 4 elements for your magic are mostly diverse with room to expand to more if the Dev Team wants to. Spell-casting takes a long time so being good at dodging is critical. I would like to see a moderate boost in melee power as it really is a 'last resort' in terms of damage output. Normal mobs are generally underwhelming and not much of a threat where-as the bosses vary in their difficulty.Story: Almost non-existent. I hope the devs put more focus in the full release on the lore of Created Souls and dolls from the start instead of having to stumble upon it. As of currently, you aren't clued in at all until your character mentions them and the main plot-line is "Go to the throne for [unexplained reason]." All that said, The combat/magic is the primary draw of this game.Other notes: Some areas are a little samey when traversing them making it easy to get turned-around or lost. Standard non-dashing movement speed is a bit too slow and could stand being increased by ~15%. Animation is surprisingly well done namely for the main character. I have noticed that some gates you open will close again if you do not pray at a statue before dying. Not the end of the world, but can be annoying if you're not aware of that. 10/10 cute magical girl. Maybe add a couple unlockable outfits?Final note: I don't know if the devs should increase the game's price too much once it's released (Depends on how much content they add) but judging from how much is here and yet to go... I would assume the total length of the game would double to around 6 hours with little replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool game, definitely a souls-like. What i like about this game is that the game feels inspired by dark souls and not based off of dark souls. Combat is fun and different, with using magic and having to manage a health, mana, and stamina bar rather than just two. running out of stamina has dire consequences. Bosses are fun and unique for the game. the characters are fun and interesting. i have not finished the game but its really fun and a blast. I read comments saying it short and if it is true i will definitely be sad and disappointed. Good game i hope they expand on it more and release more content for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Witch Nobeta

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, Little Witch Nobeta is a game with an incredible amount of potential, all memes aside. The gameplay is some of the smoothest and most rewarding I've ever had the pleasure of being in possession of, and as someone who has played every Souls game, this is sometimes even better than what it's inspired by if you love timing everything down to the exact frame (I'm a counter magic freak) and learning how to fight each boss is one of the most fun and difficult processes I've went through. I don't know how standard mode looks like so I may have chosen the harder route but being able to beat Monica was super satisfying after a lot of tribulation.As far as story goes, it's simple, but it relegates a lot of it's storytelling to mystery and we don't know much about the crafted souls, our main enemies thus far, at the moment. I imagine as the story progresses we get to know much more and I really want to know who Nobeta's cat is as well. The character design ranges from simple to complex, but they all seem to mix together really well and they're quite creative. Nobeta's and Monica's designs are fantastic for entirely different reasons; Nobeta's is traditional and does a good job at expressing the classic fantasy protagonist and Monica's is very futurist while remaining in the realm of old-era fantasy, just more complex and more expressive of her manic personality. There isn't too much I have to say that's bad about this game at all, most are minor nitpicks that will eventually be fixed in due time, like some minor glitches with walls and being able to pass through invisible barriers sometimes to get in to usually inaccessible areas. Regardless of whatever your views are, and yes, I'm looking at a few certain people, you can't say this isn't a possible classic in the works. This game will be more important than ever in a few years and is an exemplary statement from indie developers who are able to make amazing homages to games and communities they love.Now excuse me, I'm going to keep trying and failing a speedrun of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Witch Nobeta

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a strong recommendation, but I enjoyed the game enough to beat it. The combat is fairly simplistic and the level design can be rather archaic and confusing at times, however it's still a fun and cute little game.  My biggest problem with it is a lot of the deaths you are likely to have are fairly cheap, in the form of being knocked off a platform. Recovery times after taking damage is fairly slow as well, so if you are up against multiple enemies, prepare to be stun locked for awhile after taking a hit.  Despite all that, it's still a fun little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Witch Nobeta

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:A cute Souls-like that's still quite rough around the edges, but the gameplay and bosses are pretty great.Longer version:It's a Souls-like with a cute loli witch protagonist trying to, for whatever reason, get to the throne of the castle.You go through somewhat maze-like levels fighting various enemies with different abilities, including a handful of pretty well-designed bossfights.You can sorta parry (haven't quite figured out how to do that deliberately yet) and use up to four different types of attack magic with a regular and a charged mode each.Due to the fact that it's not melee-focused and the way the bosses are designed, they feel a lot more dynamic than in, say, Elden Ring, where it's basically "dodge the combo, do two attacks OR heal" without much flexibility. In LWN you have a much more varied approach and more windows of opportunity to do certain actions and counter certain moves (e.g. leaving your frost magic charged nullifies fire-based damage while you either regenerate mana and deal some extra frost damage with your staff). Since charged spells are generally the way to go against bosses and spells charge by absorbing floating mana orbs, dodging correctly, countering enemy melee attacks and melee attacking yourself, it does feel quite nice and quick. My only hangup really was one boss where I failed to see a moderately obvious counter to a devastating attack, which was kinda my fault.You will also be punished if you're careless and underestimate enemies. Getting surrounded unprepared can be very bad news, as it should.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Witch Nobeta

_childDocuments_.review: My oh my, what a surprise. I haven't fell in love with a game since Dark Souls 3,  this alone speaks volume about how fun this actually is. With that being said, do not expect this game to be a literal "souls-like" : it definitely has its own identity.I'll start with what I enjoyed the most : the Gameplay. It's just so smooth, you sprint around while shooting at enemies, all of your four magic spells have their uses so you should really think twice about which spell you want to use for which situation, the "magic counter" system feels so satisfying to pull off, it's just plain addictive.This game is straight up challenging and it will take you a couple hours to get used to all of the gameplay mechanics it has to offer. Once mastered, the fiercest players might want to try to speedrun, no-hit run, melee run, lv1 run this game, it really seems to be a fun game to run that's for sure.The Graphics are pretty basic, not ugly, but not transcending either, it's just a cute anime-style game, nothing much to say  here, they get the job done.Finally my only really complaint so far would be the plot : it feels really, reaaaally lacking and the character development is nearly nonexistent. With that being said, this isn't the full game yet, so there might be hope for the following content, but it didn't  look too bright so far.Long story short : Challenging & Rewarding gameplay, smooth controls, the game itself comes cheap. Just don't expect insane plot twists, other than that it's absolutely great.

_childDocuments_.review:
Nobeta, the little wonder, came to the castle alone to solve the mystery of her own life. Constantly challenging powerful crafted souls, she learned all kinds of magical abilities and befriended a mysterious little black cat.

What secrets hide in the depths of the castle? 

The Little Witch Nobeta is a 3D action shooting game. Players will explore ancient, unknown castles and use different magic elements to fight against the soul!

The game uses a comfortable Japanese art style, but the battles are quite challenging despite its cute looks.

Underestimating your foes will lead to troublesome encounters. You must discover enemies' weaknesses and learn the precise time to dodge attacks in order to gain the advantage in combat.

name: LUNARK
detailed_description: Join the revolution in this cinematic sci-fi platformer Set on a distant planet ruled by a totalitarian regime, LUNARK is a modern take on the 2D cinematic platformer genre of the '90s. As Leo, a courier with unique abilities and a mysterious past, you'll run, jump, hang, climb, roll, and shoot through gorgeously animated pixel-art environments ranging from a dystopian megalopolis to eerie caves to an alien forest. You must overcome traps, solve puzzles, earn upgrades, and battle enemy droids, and when you're not fighting for survival, you'll meet a cast of colorful characters who will put Leo's allegiances to the test. Uncover the dark origin of humanity's new home and the truth about yourself in this epic sci-fi adventure! Key Features: • Experience a modern 2D cinematic platformer with precision gameplay, stunning animation, and rotoscoped cutscenes! • Immerse yourself in a compelling sci-fi story of survival, revolution, and mystery • Intuitive but versatile controls: Run, jump, hang, climb, roll, and shoot your way to freedom! • Explore glorious pixel-art environments, including mysterious alien ruins, a flying penitentiary, a high-tech megalopolis, and an alien forest • Solve puzzles, overcome traps, and interact with a variety of characters • Discover hidden upgrades to expand your health and weapon capabilities • Yes, you can pet the dog (and cat)!

_childDocuments_.review: I have some very subjective criticism for this game, but as a big fan of the genre, I can't ignore it...  I always thought games like Flashback and Another World were extremely immersive experiences, sure we remember them for their platforming momentum, but when they came out they were very unique among other games, playing them was like learning to swim by getting tossed into the ocean and figuring out everything as you go, I never had a feeling of the game watching over me, and I felt like LUNARK was holding my hand the entire time, not just from the gameplay perspective, but the narrative as well, a lot of the characters were there to provide more hints or point me to the next location, the world-building being mostly goofy, and it does not help that final boss was a forgettable character.The gameplay is pretty much perfect as far as the 'cinematic platformers’ go, it's a bit optimized so it's not as hard as some of the classics, I would say the difficulty is mostly fair - if you have prior experience with the genre. The checkpoints are usually only 30 to 50 seconds apart so even if you die, it's not hard to backtrack, maybe with the exception of the last 2 stages where it got a bit more annoying. You also have a hitpoint system that can be upgraded with collectibles, overall it's just much easier than anything from the past. I did run into some technical issues toward the end of the game, but for the most part, the game felt relatively polished. The playthrough is about 5 hours, depends on your experience I guess For me, the mood of the game was all over the place, and that is my main problem, sometimes it seems like the game wants me to be immersed and pay attention to the world, but then it just kinda drops it at random. Now there were parts of the game where the soundtrack reminded me of Flashback and had those upbeat industrial vibes like in the original theme, but then I am fighting a boss in this game, and it has like JRPG music, it feels so odd. Actually, everything between the "explosion and the city exploration" felt good, that was my favorite chunk of the game, everything after that did not feel on brand for the world-building, feels too much like playing a game, not exploring a world that I am interested in.Don't get me wrong, the cutscenes were still great, it's more or less Flashback in terms of formatting and presentation, although having such small sprites does not feel right for the genre, in my opinion anyway. I did feel like the level design varied a lot, sometimes for better, and sometimes for worse. Some parts of the game did not seem designed that well, like it has boss fights but they are very dull. I got a few laughs here and there, but the game traded the world-building for it, I just could not take it seriously anymore.(+) The gameplay was perfectly fine and faithfully implemented, it's pretty much a modern take on it, if it's still hard for you, well it's not gonna get much easier now without changing what it is. (+) For better or worse, the game is relatively forgiving for the genre. Lots of checkpoints, constant heals, and maximum HP upgrades. Is it fair difficulty, kind of, depending on the level.(+) The cutscenes were great, as expected. I liked the level design here and there, but some of the stages were a bit dull. I thought the open areas looked nice with all of the random characters.(+) Has some optional exploration, not too deep though. Find some shards, upgrade your health, and pet the dog. - you kept using so many characters just as a hint dispenser, it just feels like the entire world exists for the player but I am not inside this world, it's not a great way to build your story. For me, you were changing the mood of the game too much, sometimes it felt more serious, and sometimes you completely dropped the entire thing, I just did not have the immersion that I felt playing Flashback, I can't take this game or its characters seriously, it holds your hand almost the entire time, and feels too much like I am in the game, not inside an interesting world. I thought the villain was awful too.Some of the music tracks really felt out of place. Now some of them were great, like the song during first explosion, that was very on-brand, but I don't know, there is a lot of strange music in the game that makes no sense, sometimes the game sounds like JRPG, like what is going on. I had a very hard time doing the standing 45 jump, maybe I just missed the controls, perhaps you should save the tooltip somewhere. Last 2 stages did not have very friendly checkpoints, doing easy things you already did for every mistake. Boss fights were kind of awful, easy, and dull. Initially, I thought the game was kinda average, then it got much better, and then it got worse again.  I paid $18 for it, and I just did not get that immersive experience I was hoping for. It's a decent tribute, it has some okay moments, but honestly, the magic was not there for me, everyone is saying look it's like Flashback, no that game was immersive as hell, and it's not nostalgia for me, it's the music and narrative choices they made, this game exists for the player, not for interesting world-building. Sorry if I sound negative, I was expecting something else, something with a more refined atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Hm, this is a love letter (especially) to Flashback, a famous game from the early nineties. If you enjoyed Flashback from Paul Cuisset (Delphine, 1992), than this game is like a balm massage for your soul. If you are one of the five people on earth who didn't enjoy Flashback that much (or if you are too young to have played in the 90s), but actually liked the reimagination from Ubisoft (like I did), you might get the same feeling. The core gameplay elements are very similar.First you have to get used to the controls. They work rather good, once you understand the basics. Just move your joystick up to jump upwards. For jumping in your walking direction, you need to press a button. Roll, shoot, thats more or less it. When you run, you can jump a bit farther, and there is a special way to reach platforms above by jumping up diagonally. You have to navigate over platforms, avoiding hazards and sometimes shooting a few enemies, from spiders, birds to robots or droids. You will spend your time opening doors, activating moving platforms, not getting lost, using items at the right spot, using shield cells... but there are also hidden objects (collect three for a bonus) or gun upgrades and there is a story to uncover about the post-apocalyptic world and about your character, Leo (not Conrad). The game is a bit more playable (=easier) than the original Flashback was. When you die you just restart at the last save point, often in the same room, but never very far back. When you quit the game, it only saves at the level start, though, this is a bit hardcore (or like in the good old days). Also the game never tells you if you reach a new level, so you only know where it has saved when you start it the next time. Your ammo is unlimited, but your gun soon overheats, so you should make your shots count. Healing plants regrow, killed enemies stay dead. The game has a few quirks, though. You still get attacked while you read messages or watch cutscenes... come on! Sometimes your character just doesnt't jump and falls to his death. You cannot look down when you stand at an edge and will more often die from fall damage than from enemies, mines, security lasers or other man-made hazards. The game is very low res, sometimes it is difficult to recognize items or even characters.Pixel art sci-fi platformer. Run, jump and use your gun. Solve simple puzzles, fight enemies. Quite fun, actually.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some excellent components here, but it fails to live up to it's inspiration.Enemy attacks that can't be avoided and unreliable controls are an issue. The biggest problem is the checkpointing. There's a reason we left harsh checkpointing in the past. Failing a jump and having to redo five screens of platforming challenges gets old very fast.Some better checkpointing options and the other issues become less frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave a negative review, but sadly no other option here.This game has a great potential, it's clear love letter to Flashback (and Another World, etc) and mostly delivers similar experience, but there is something missing to make it great.That alone wouldn't make it negative, but the save system is just plain silly (for this day and age). If you are not able to finish a level for whatever reason in one go, you start from the start instead of from last checkpoint. For some levels it's fine as they are just few minutes, but for other that are pretty long it's pretty annoying. What infuriated me is that I died on the last boss, and then the game crashed after checkpoint, and that would put be me back trying to finish last level from the very start... no thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME IF YOU PLAN TO PLAY IN SESSIONSThe checkpoint system forces you to play ENTIRE CHAPTERS at a time. Some of the chapters get pretty long. You'll be playing for an hour and think you've made some progress and and your play session with a lot of progress made. But then when you come back and continue the game starts you back at the BEGINNING of the chapter! Ridiculous! There's no reason for any game to do this. It's an unnecessary forced difficulty. The game should save your re spawn points or something.Finding out the game lost my progress took all the joy of playing this. I deleted the game. Unless they patch in a better save system this game will remained uninstalled. I'm so annoyed right now. What a shame.The game isn't crazy difficult or anything. But if you're gonna make the player solve dozens of platform puzzles maybe throw in some checkpoints or a save system. Imagine any other puzzle game doing this? THEY DON'T! What a waste of my time. Can't believe I kickstarted this, I'm so annoyed right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I am old but lucky enough to remember fondly the titles that LUNARK pays homage to. I was a perfect candidate to back the project on Kickstarter. Usually I back things and then forget about them, but this is a rare example of a game I was actively following and interested in. I played and enjoyed the demo, and have enjoyed watching some of the behind the scenes coverage over social media.I can happily say after completing the game, I am not disappointed.Visuals are bright and colourful with cut scenes given a wonderful rotoscoped art style that evokes a very nineties feel. The environments are varied and have lots of nice touches which give the world character and a lived in feel.The controls are tight and fluid which is the crux for enjoying a cinematic platformer. The main character Leo moves very similarly to the heroes of classics in the genre. Another World and Flashback are major references throughout but really only for those who know what they are looking out for.Animations are silky smooth and the pixel art is just lovely; detailed and expressive. When you perform a flawless jump followed by a combat roll then catch a ledge, drop down and knock out a guard, it really feels like an action movie and that's really what a cinematic platformer is aiming for.Sound design is appropriately spacey and futuristic, with all the whooshes, zaps and kapows you could hope for. It's a very classic sci-fi world and the soundscape is crucial for building the atmosphere.Music is excellent. There are plenty of atmospheric tunes which fit in very nicely with both action set pieces and narrative beats. The final couple of levels have particularly strong themes and interesting compositions. There are definite nods to classic action movie scores throughout and some will bring a knowing smile to a specific type of gamer (i.e. an old one).Beginning to end, the game won't take much more than a few hours and you could probably finish it in one sitting. If you engage with all the NPCs and take the time to investigate the world and search out all the secrets, you can bump that up into double digits.The presentation and feel are cohesive, and makes for a nice five to ten hour ripping sci-fi yarn. There is just enough challenge to keep players engaged without punishing newcomers to the genre. Your mileage may vary, but I had a great time and look forward to seeing what comes next from the studio.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original Prince of Persia dilogy after LUNARK, and couldn't believe it didn't have the diagonal ledge grab, as it felt so natural to use it, as well as a pull-up direction reverse.This game was entirely made by one author in 6 years, so it belongs to the same league as Cave Story and Axiom Verge - what I call the Gesamtkunstwerk of videogames. Story, gameplay, graphics AND music by one author, no exceptions. That's the way the most truest of true indie games are made. Why don't we have a separate word for that yet?

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I am blown away by Lunark.  I'm of a particular age (clue: I was 15 when Delphine released Flashback).For those of you who suck at maths, Delphine released Flashback in 1992.I haven't enjoyed playing a platformer as much as back then SINCE back then.  However, Lunark has perfectly slipped in there as my second favourite platformer of all time.  It's a beautiful game - so perfectly put together. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Lunark with its futuristic themed music, graphics, and story. It felt very immersive for a platform game, with lots of unusual locales and interesting characters to meet, and although they didn’t have a great deal to say, they managed to spin a web of intrigue that I felt invested in.You are Leo, a humble courier just delivering parcels around Lunark, when one day you become embroiled in a terrorist plot that makes you a wanted man, and leaves you running for your life.Navigate the twelve extensive levels in search of answers to why you feel different and who has set you up.You are now on the most wanted list and must move stealthily past guards then knock them out, avoid triggering alarms which alert enemy droids, and work your way through the city to escape. Your journey takes you through many different futuristic landscapes all with their own set of problems. There is quite a lot of stealth involved in gameplay, although you can go gung-ho, it just means you will need to deal with the enemy droids that emerge due to your clumsiness. You have a gun, but it only shoots a few blasts before overheating, and there is quite a long cooling down period before you are able to shoot again. Throughout the adventure you can stumble upon upgrade desks that give your gun longer periods of fire, and these really help. When your blaster lets you down, and you have droids hot on your heels, you can roll away from danger which is quite effective, but be careful as environments are usually very cramped and it can be easy to roll off a ledge to your death.There is also a shield which you can activate to stop bullets and missiles, but these are limited and need to be replenished by shooting crates and picking shield items up. You have three lives initially, but there is scope to add more if you complete special quests, and there are also plants which can replenish your health along the way.The action is quite frantic, and there will be many deaths in this game, and where you respawn can be a source of frustration. I had to repeat a lot of game play because I respawned in a place way back from where I died. During a session it isn’t so bad. It may mean you have to repeat difficult sections, which is annoying, but they are manageable. Levels are easily an hour in length so you can see how frustrating that is, and it meant I had to plan my game sessions when I knew I had time. Controls are quite laggy which can also add to the anger levels. I understand that the developer was trying to get a balance between retro and modern controls but sometimes when you’re in a tight spot and you need to duck a bullet, but his reactions aren’t quick enough, it does mean you might be swearing at your monitor. It’s all forgivable stuff though. Some of the stages required puzzle solving, and I did get stuck a couple of times, but mostly things are quite straightforward. There is a bit of precision platforming involved and I did get confused quite a lot with the controls for long jumps, and medium jumps, and there is a whole thread on this, which is being addressed. There is a small tutorial at the beginning but because of the save issue I found myself only playing when I had time and I sometimes forgot the controls, like hanging from a ledge, and there are no reminders of this anywhere. After the game ends, there is no chapter select, so this means achievement hunters will need to play through the game again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an og backer and I knew what I was signing for when I supported this game but sadly I had to stop playing this game when the big spider is chasing you. Very frustaring moment!I don't mind clunky controls, it's a nice comeback from the old games, as long as the game has a slow pace and it doesn't force me to be precise but when I have to time everything perfectly for that chase moment I felt I was playing with a hand tied to my back. It's sad to me to say this but the animations on this game look incredibly smooth and is a pitty the controls are not more dynamic/responsive.Maybe I would continue playing if the story had me hoooked, but I felt the story didn't have any depth or interesting development other thant action because there is a conflict which you don't much understand.
