_childDocuments_.review: You have to know what you're getting into with this game, and reading the Steam page and looking at screenshots should tell you, but just to reiterate/re-emphasize: This is *not* a typical platformer. It is one of those slower-paced, rotoscoped, parkour platform games. You can't play it like Mario, you have to play it like (old-school) Prince of Persia, Flashback, Another World/Out of This World, Blackthorne, etc. Much more methodical and animation-based gameplay. I'm a big fan of those games, and that was why I wishlisted and bought this one, but if you're not, you might want to pass.Mostly the game presented a pretty steady increase in challenge. There were one or two frustrating sections, one of which got patched to be less frustrating (looking at you, spider chase). I liked the story, which had quite a few twists and turns, at least one of which I didn't guess beforehand. The color palettes are gorgeous and I like the cutscene animations. The general platforming animations are a little less "rotoscopey" than I wanted, but I'm one of those weird people who kind of likes how rotoscoping (and/or heavily-referenced animation) looks, and nothing in the game looks bad by any means so this probably won't be an issue for most players. I also felt like, while I would have enjoyed playing maybe one more level, the game overall didn't overstay its welcome or end too quickly--it's a total package. It's not too much of a hassle to get full completion, either. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who likes Flashback or any of those other methodical platformers. A solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: There are several games from the '90s that have marked history, that have remained in the hearts of many gamers either for nostalgia, their charismatic retro graphics, or for memories of frustration, because of the difficulty that some of these iconic titles handled. In my case, I remember very well Prince of Persia on the SNES, a game that devoured hours and hours of my childhood, and that undoubtedly left me quite frustrated; after all, I could never finish it, and what's more, I would dare to say that I never even came close to doing it. This is one of the reasons why Lunark caught my attention, with that very similar, but updated style, that made me want to give it a chance; initially for my own personal vendetta against the old SNES title, but also because it looked quite flashy and charming.Lunark is a platforming game with some emphasis on cinematics and action. It's what one might call a modernized retro, taking inspiration from titles like the aforementioned Prince of Persia, and also Flashback, another renowned title in the same style. Wrapped in a futuristic setting, classic sci-fi, we will have to make use of our athletic skills as we go through the various biomes of the planet Albaryne, unraveling a mysterious plot of which our protagonist is the center.The story follows the adventure of our hero: Leo, a skilled courier afflicted by a rare disease that accelerates his aging, but that also seems to give him incredible athletic abilities. At the start, we will have to meet his benefactor, who resides in a scientific facility and where we will find our first tutorial; and I must admit that I found it quite creative, since it makes us take control of an android to learn the movements, instead of making our protagonist suffer trial and error, a detail that pleased me.After meeting the subject in question, Gideon, we will be entrusted with a mission: to find an ancient artifact hidden in some old ruins. Without further ado, Leo will get into action, and will get on his ship to set course to the objective. Between platforms, enemies and some puzzles, we will encounter an enigmatic resident in these ruins, who will present himself to us as a member of those who call themselves "The Immortals". This individual will sow some uncertainty in our protagonist with cryptic comments, before sending us back on our search, and if anything will be clear, it is that we will cross paths again.The plot will progress as we complete screens and face the adversities of the ruins, and eventually we’ll encounter the "boss" of the dungeon: a huge spider that will challenge our physical skills, as well as our gun handling. At the end of these trials, we will return with the artifact for Gideon, but some events will develop that will hinder our mission. From here on, the story will unfold little by little, revealing mysteries and deceptions, with some twists that will question Leo's loyalty and everything he believed in. It's an entertaining tale, told in small bits and pieces between platforming moments, and I quite enjoyed it.The gameplay focuses mostly on platforming, clearly, and we'll be able to make use of Leo's athletic prowess to run, jump, climb and shoot our way through the game's various maps. As for combat, we will have a firearm that we can use to shoot down enemies, but we must be careful with our rate of fire, because the faster we shoot, the more we have to wait for recharging; however, as we progress and find upgrade stations, we can improve its effectiveness. We will also have single-use shield capsules, which can defend us from an attack, as long as we remain still, and healing plants to recover our health at specific points. We can also improve our hearts, which represent how many times we can take damage, by collecting three collectibles that are usually hidden in "secret" places, and of which there are quite a few of. This, along with various puzzles and enemies, make the gameplay entertaining between stretches of chatting with NPCs and the story. While I'm pretty bad at this specific kind of gameplay, I really enjoyed the experience I had with this particular title, and I can say that I finished it with good feelings, which I can't say for Prince of Persia.The artwork is very colorful and vibrant, making use of a pixel style for the sprites and environments, as well as for the menus and cinematics. Touching on the subject of the cinematics, the most curious thing about them is that they were made with "rotoscoped" scenes, and using this traditional animation technique they created very cool and detailed moments. However, I must admit that some of the cinematics in question are quite repetitive, such as those of picking up objects, and became somewhat monotonous for me; luckily, they can be skipped, and although I appreciate the work and effort put in them, I could not avoid skipping some that I had already seen.The environment and characters blend a bit at times, but not enough to be that noticeable, and I quite liked the color palette chosen for the different areas. A section that, all in all, is very nice and well cared for. The soundtrack is quite varied, from slow piano melodies to more moving and electronic, but in general maintains a "synthwave" or "retrowave" vibe throughout the adventure. I found the quality of the tunes to be excellent, a perfect accompaniment for the different sections of the game, and it made me experience a certain nostalgia for the electro music of the nineties.In conclusion, Lunark is a charismatic proposal in a beloved genre, aiming for a captivating cinematic retro experience. Counting with a creative story and an audiovisual section that blends very well, it is a game that I liked a lot, but I must say that its duration left me somewhat unsatisfied; not because it is bad, quite the opposite, because it left me wanting a little more of this universe and its inhabitants. All in all, it was a pleasant experience, and I recommend it to those looking for a retro platform video game, with difficulty of the ol’ times and a lot of particularity.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Went into Lunark thinking it was a shorter game and was surprised by the several different levels and designs.The levels aren't too extensive but they are still quite satisfying and creative.Inspired by several past games and movies, it does a great job of capturing a lot of those good things, and mixing them with new stuff into a new identity.Animations are gorgeous, and impressively well done with a "minimum" amount of pixels per sprite - there's mastery in this.Some mechanics may take some getting used to, as the animations prevent the responsiveness of actions, but that's part of the game's DNA and forces the player to a certain pacing. It requires the players to observe, analyze patterns, wait and move at the right time.One thing I wished was different in this game, is the checkpoints / auto-save system:The game has 12 levels, and the auto-save works only at the start of those - this isn't made clear for the players.There are some checkpoints during gameplay (also not clear when/where), that allow the player to resume in the level (if they die), but if they quit and resume later, the game places them back at the level's start point.I chatted with the developer and this is already being addressed.Conclusion: felt like a very balanced title - totally worth it for fans of platforming games (may they have played the games that inspired Lunark or not), and a masterpiece of pixelart and animation.Will remember Canari Games and be waiting for their next creation.If it's as good as this, it's already a winner, but from the care and attention to detail in Lunark, I believe it will only get better.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Like many of the other reviewers here, I was an 'Amiga' kid of the 90's. Lunark's mechanics are very similar to the classic Amiga game Flashback from that era - which isn't a bad thing as that game was a certified classic.So the game is essentially a grid based platformer with some gun based combat and minor puzzles to solve. Nothing groundbreaking and doesn't take the genre any further that Flashback did all those years ago.However, it has a solid storyline, chunky stylised pixel art (both in game and during the brief cutscenes) with great animation and an inspired atmospheric soundtrack. It all adds up to a game full of wonderful charm which is all the more amazing when considering it was developed mostly by one man.From start to finish took around 7 hours (it could probably be done quicker) and was great on Steam Deck apart from the fact the audio could get a little messed up when resuming from standby.I really hope it's a success as I would love to see a sequel. Things I'd like to see in the sequel:-- a slightly higher resolution of pixel art - maybe something akin to Huntdown- more boss fights / climatic moments- more variation in the puzzlesOverall, a charming little game that's more of the sum of its parts.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark is a truly amazing experience.It will surely bring back memories from games like Flashback, Prince of Persia or Another World, but in a very good way. The gameplay was properly updated to modern standards, while staying true to the originals. Jumps are easy to perform, with a special mention for the vertical one (to climb to upper floor) which can now be done in the middle of a run.Some may find the movements a bit rigid, if compared to "smoother" platformers like Ori. But in the case of Lunark, this produces very cinematic moments which I definitely enjoyed a LOT.Another good point is the level design: very solid with a good balance between wandering phases and "figuring it out" moments.My only current issue is with the Dodge movement which is sometimes hard to pull out, because it can't interrupt your current player animation. This is a bit old-school, but definitely not a deal breaker: it simply forces you to anticipate enemy movements properly, which is, in itself, a fresh experience.Would buy it again.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a Flashback clone, except inferior to the original in every way possible. Level design is particularly bad, with out of place backtracking, many uninteresting rooms which will repeat the same situations and platforming over and over, and poorly placed checkpoints. Controls follow the grid/animation-based platformer formula, but they feel unpolished, especially in combat. Perhaps the saving grace could be graphics, which are pretty good except for the fact that resolution is way, way too low (even lower than the VGA roots of this kind of game), to the point where it hurts gameplay: many backgrounds, characters and traps are hard to see simply because they could be made of one or two pixels.Another sore point is the story. Flashback had a surprisingly good narrative, told in a few excellent cutscenes but also mostly by level design. In this one, the story is told through extremely poor, cringe-worthy dialogue. The game tries to mimic the vector animations of Flashback and, again, fails spectacularly, with most custscenes being relegated to mundane actions such as grabbing an object, which need no cutscene.This was a good idea but, unfortunately, those are some big shoes to fill and the game is simply not good enough.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: A short but find puzzle platformer. Clearly inspired by Flashback, this is a must-play if you enjoyed that classic game. Beautiful pixel art, wonderful animation, great gameplay and top music. My only complaint is that the in-level graphics were a little *too* pixelated. Still, I wish there were more games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: if you like good indie games = you'll like this gameif you like action platformers = you'll like this gameif you love old school flashback, prins of persia and another world = you'll love this gameRate it 7 out of 10,  would be a 8,5 out of 10 if:- control(s) would be updated to 2023, instead of 1 on 1 copy from oldschool 90s choppy flashback controls- the graphics where sharper and a little more detailed (a little higher resolution sprites)Flashback from 1992 looks shaper in pixel count then lunark when it comes to ingame gameplay sprites. - the music was a little better! - more content like (local or online) coop, map editor, instead of only singleplayerbut dont get me wrong, this game is definatly worth the 18 bucks_______________________________________Very positive is definatly the correct statement for this game....
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Neat graphics, sluggish gameplay.While the animations look smooth, they also take their sweet time. The player character isn't terribly reactive or fast - so even running away from robots doesn't make you gain ground on them. Enemies move on screens you can't see. At least they only fire on you when you are on the same screen - but the projectiles will hit you on the next screen! This game is not made for quick reactions, yet the levels are designed for them. Quick changes from running to ducking to firing do not work well.The story isn't particularly novel, and the world building doesn't paint a comprehensive picture. Lots of questions you could have aren't entertained at all.Finding "secret" places at least gives you some reason to look around - the extra health or weapon upgrades are useful to have, even when there are unlimited lives.Why somebody decided that levels need to be played in one sitting without saving when there are respawns in the level, I'll never understand. Annoyed by the Boss? Well, if you don't like it and need a break, you can play the entire level again.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time with LUNARK. If you come to this from the nostalgia angle and have been longing for a 2D platformer with slow and methodical buffered inputs like in the old days, then you will enjoy it. Even more if you have a particular fondness for Flashback, since the game is practically a love letter to it -- not just through the gameplay but all over the place, from the lightness in narration and worldbuilding, the consistent sound and visual design to the rotoscoped cutscenes. As far as I'm concerned, what I saw in the trailer was what I got. And about that, I want to give a nod to the developer. This was a perfect scope for a solo dev, doing exactly what they set out to do without overcommitting. A pleasure to experience.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: a great homage to Flashback and Another World, Lunark is a fantastic cinematic platformer with some lovely, chunky, pixel art, great music and good pacing. You may need some getting used to the movement system if you're not used to those aforementioned games from the 90s. Compared to Flashback, Lunark adds a handy auto ledge grab move (read the tutorial inscriptions), I wish I could perform the roll just by crouching and pressing left/right through instead of having a separate button
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Big hopes for this game, being in my Wishlist for a long time and a big fan of the cinematic platformers.After reaching the end, and quite some secrets, all I can say is that Lunark is mediocre at best, and absolutely annoying at worst.First off the graphics are so low-fi that from the get go you don't really understand what's what. I'm a big fan of pixel art but this is just over simplifying too much. One of the best point of pixel art is that you can fill the void with your imagination: now this feels more like a throwback to Atari 2600 than VGA games of the nineties.Second the controls are just a pain in the ass. Literally. You can solve the problem using a controller, but that keyboard layout is so damn complicated: especially the mechanic of jump & grab and running jumps is plainly ridiculous. Also you have totally zero feeling of control over your avatar: it all feels so weightless.Third the story: so underdeveloped, you don't really get a sense of the world, of what's happening, the true motives behind the actions of the people presented, so you're not really connected to anyone really. You just talk with a bunch of no-ones, not really giving a damn about them.Should we talk about the ending-which-is-not-the-end?Oh on the positive side there are cats. And dogs. Lots of.And you can pet them all.Not exactly what I hoped for it to be. Certainly not worth about 20 €.If anything, stick to the game "THE WAY", because that's how modern cinematic platformers should be made.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I love Flashback, it was one of my favorite games of all time. This is very much a spiritual successor and to my knowledge the only true "cinematic platformer" game released since Blackthorne, back in the mid 90s. For that reason alone this game is worthy of a recommendation. Thankfully Lunark is also fun and challenging and is perfect for the Steam Deck. If you liked Prince of Persia, Another World, Heart of the Alien, Flashback and Blackthorne, you need to play this game.If I was going to offer some criticism, it would be that some of the puzzle mechanics could have been explored a little more deeply. The last couple of levels feel rushed as well, leaving you wanting more than the roughly 4 hours of content on offer here. But if a game leaves you wanting more, that's kind of a good thing. I'd love to see a sequel, or another game in this genre from the same developers.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game a solid chance and spent a couple hours with it, but it really isn't for me. I like RPG platformers in general, but there's one main issue with this game for me. Maybe it is just a trope with the genre, though, so take this with a grain of salt. This game's controls are too funky to justify the fast pace of this game. Not rarely does the game feature tight jumps right after another or enemies that cannot be dealt with all at once. The solution? Waiting; or slowing down to take the jumps one at a time, rather than carrying the momentum through. Similarly, the weapon firing is incredibly inconsistent, sometimes firing incredibly rapidly and other times not allowing a second bullet to fire after the first. The main issue, is that input buffering isn't reliable, and animations are often times too long and not able to be interrupted. For example, turning around can render you dead. Maybe this kind of punishing control scheme is for you, but it really isn't for me.If this is what you're looking for, go ahead, but it is not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it. It has its flaws in level design, there are moments that add unnesesary friction, but it's not that big of a problem overall. Also has some obtuse moments, where you dont now how to deal with specific threats, but nothing that bolcked me for more than a few minutes.On the other side, it nails: the aestetic, the sci-fi setting, the story, the exploration, the slow-deliberate movment controls, and it also has a few innovative combat mechanincs. All that should be more than enough for anyone looking for a decent 2d plataformer. It's a game that clearly takes a lot from another era, and that can be anoying to some. In other words, you'll enjoy it more if you are above 35 y/o ;)
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark has a nice Retro feeling about it but sadly that charms fades soon enough. The clumsy controls and the very unfair save point system makes it incledibly hard to play...at least on the pc. I gave up on the train, with the fast enemies and the slow hero some sections are unplayable and no fun at all. And since there is no easy mode or at least saving in every room (as it is common in the 21th century jump'n run gaming)  that's it for me. There are many Indie-Platformers on steam who do a much better job on the gameplay. Even the old FLASHBACK had a better gameplay.  Sadly. I really liked it at the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. You go on quite a nice adventure. Difficulty is just right to make it challenging but not frustrating. You could consider it short, 5-6 hours, but I think this is a proper length. You could play through the whole game in a single day and have a great time.My only negative points would be that it is quite easy to miss jump and fall to your death. It has plenty of checkpoints, but those are sometimes far apart. However, you won't lose key progress when you die. Save points are far apart though, you cannot really quit in the middle of a level.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: LUNARK is a decent little cinematic platformer obviously inspired by classics like Another World and Flashback. It doesn't quite stand toe to toe with those celebrated titles, but it's solid enough for a playthrough. The pixel art graphics are colorful and smoothly animated. The rotoscoped cutscenes look right out of Another World. The soundtrack is incredible and one of the best of the year. I wish I could've been able to turn down the sound effects volume to hear it better. The level design deserves some praise as well for being expansive, varied, and challenging. However, the levels lack any sense of believability which is a hallmark of this niche subgenre. I found it bizarre that the final level had the antagonist's diary entries just scattered around randomly on terminals. The writing and storytelling in general are really amateurish which play into the levels feeling less like places and more like traditional platforming levels with sluggish controls. The story's pacing is rapid. Characters get introduced then disappear for most of the game in the same scene. The plot device of the character's condition is resolved so suddenly with little to no explanation that it makes me wonder what the point of it was in the first place. The controls are sluggish even for a cinematic platformer. There's a clear delay between button press and character action making certain combat sections and chase sequences very frustrating. On top of that, the checkpoint system is terrible. The game was literally placing checkpoints under environmental hazards that would inflict damage on me upon spawning in. What makes it even more of a nuisance is the fact that if you quit the game before finishing the level, you have to start it over completely. My power went out once mid-level on the final stage and I had to start over completely. Combat suffers the most because of the unresponsive controls since certain enemies move very quickly and require quick reaction times that feel out of place in a game with such deliberate movement. It's a fairly short game as well (4-5 hours), but damn if it doesn't still feel padded out. There was no reason to have you do so many pointless fetch quests with tedious backtracking. It adds nothing to the game. Bosses are a bit of a joke as well. There are really only two and they're easy and basically the same. I wish there was more careful consideration put into the narrative and pacing here, but for what it is, I did enjoy it. I definitely think Full Void is the better cinematic platformer to come out this year, but if you're craving something that's nostalgic, this should scratch that itch. (6/10)
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I supported this game via Kickstarter and boy do I not regret this. I planed only to play it for a bit during the weekend and suddenly it was 3 hours later and I completely forgot the time.This game is an amazing tribute to the classic cinematic platformers and you can feel the love and attention of detail that was put into this game!Note: Controls need a bit to get used too as this kind of cinematic platformer have quite a complex control scheme but Lunark solves this great and gives you enough time to learn the details.Also recommend to play it with a controller, or on Steam Deck where it runs perfectly btw.Can't wait to see Canari Games does next.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Flashback, Another World/Out of this World, Blackthorne or other games of this genre then you pretty much know what you're getting into. Everything feels just as it should. The world and animation is gorgeous. My only gripes with the game are the story and length. The plot is pretty predictable and for the amount of characters going on it's too short to feel any real investment in any of them. By the end you meet a good number of characters and all this bonding is kind of implied even though you've spent literally 10 mins with them. So basically I just wanted more. It's a great game and for the price I think it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe this review isn't going to be totally fair.  See, Lunark is a member of a rare genre, the "cinematic platformer" or the "gridded, deliberate movement platformer", that I happen to massive fan of, going back to the first time I loaded Prince of Persia up on a... (commodore?  apple2c?  I don't even remember) at summer camp.  Lunark is not trying to move the genre forward, it is one hundred percent a love letter to the cinematic platformers that came before, most specifically, Prince of Persia, Out of the World/Another World, and Flashback.  Its chunky pixels, rotoscoped animations, mini cutscenes, and chiptunes are all an absolute delight.  The screen is completely gridded out, and the movement options are very similar to those old games.Lunark has a simplicity to it.  The levels are short and sweet, once you have proven you can figure something out, unlike most games, they don't pad the game by hitting you with room after room with slight variations on the theme, which I appreciate.  You only meet a handful of characters, and dialog sections are brief.  Despite this, there is an attempt to make the plot pretty epic, and it mostly works.  Lunark has some clever secrets scattered about, I got more than half of them I think, but did not obsess over finding everything.  I finished the game in a breezy five hours, it certainly does not overstay its welcome.  As a fan of the genre, I really enjoyed Lunark, it is not groudbreaking in any way, nor does it really push the genre forward or anything, it was just an enjoyable little romp.8/10 (point added due to my deep love of the genre)NOTES - Steam Deck - Game runs great on deck, I played a bunch of it on my commute.  You could argue the chunky pixels look better on the small screen than a big one even.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of classic platformer games, then this game is definitely worth checking out. The gameplay is smooth and polished, with a great mix of challenging obstacles and satisfying combat mechanics. The controls are responsive and intuitive, making it easy to get into the flow of the game.The game has a distinctive style that will appeal to fans of Flashback and Another World. The graphics are crisp and detailed, with a great attention to detail in the environments and character animations. The sound design is also top-notch, with a great soundtrack that perfectly complements the action.That said, the game does have a few minor issues. Diagonal jumping can be a bit finicky at times, which can be frustrating in some of the more challenging levels. Additionally, the game is relatively short, which may disappoint some players who are looking for a longer experience.Overall, however, this game is a solid addition to the platformer genre, and well worth checking out for anyone who loves classic games like Flashback and Another World. If you're looking for a fun and challenging platformer with great gameplay and style, this is definitely one to consider.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true homage to the 90s cinematic platfomers except, that it is so much better in every aspect. The art and animation sequences are amazing!! Controls and movement resembles those from the 90s but it feels so smooth and responsive and they work well with other gameplay elements. Story, exploration, action and puzzles are given to you in small doses so it never gets boring. This is a true piece of art and you can feel the love and passion that went into the project with every step you make. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: A great sci-fi side scroller that gives me the 90's feelings I had a as a kid growing up on games like Flashback and Prince of Persia, the art style is the same and I was very happy to be a backer on Kickstarter years ago when this kicked off.Very happy to finish the game, I really enjoyed it, my only gripe would be it was too short!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game hoping for a fix from the hole left by the Flashback Remake (eww). This game has heart and someone involved that clearly loved the same games I did growing up, was able to add their own flare and story and made something almost perfect. I say almost as I have one or two gripes with it.Main thing is though I very much recommend this game if your childhood was Another World/Flashback/Prince of Persia/Heart of Darkness etc.. because it will scratch that very specific itch and will do so well, well enough I hope to produce a sequel. Inasmuch as I hope this has made the dev a bucket load of money and spur on a sequel/prequel. One gripe I have with it are the godawful boss battles, designed to slow you down and make the game last longer and give a degree of difficulty so it's not too easy. Bosses are supposed to be hard but the only thing I felt after defeating the boss is relief I wouldn't have to go through the sequences again or get to the second stage of a boss, die, and have to restart from the initial stage. I know the classics had frustrating sections but there are some things better left in the past. Which brings me to a second gripe, there is no save system in the game. It starts you from the beginning of the section you're in so if you have to stop playing suddenly and come back you lose any progress you have made. Understandable to a degree as making a save system can be hard in some games but it would have been nice to not have to repeat everything on my return to the game. However this gripe aside I would immediately pick up any other game that brought me back to this style again. I have to add, the music is awesome and I wish I had bought the bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a review is not fair, as I was watching the game from the very beginning and I have watched Johans art for quite some time. For some this might be bit much retro, but for me this is exactly what I wanted. I loved to discover every little piece of the game and observe all the little details that are included. Amazing piece and I just hope this is not the last game from Johan.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: A great tribute to Flashback, Prince of Persia and possibly Another World. The minimalistic pixel-art is very stylish and gives the game its own face. Especially the hero and his movement looks amazing. Also, I really enjoyed the controls. It takes a while to get it under your skin, but then it's a joy to run, jump and shoot.Gameplay-wise, Lunark surprised me mainly because it is not just a small game where you jump and shoot. I was really expecting a simpler Flashback clone and that's exactly what I was looking forward to, but I got so much more! The game gradually introduces a different gameplay mechanic in each level and spices up the game slightly. You search for keys, avoid lasers, destroy enemies, activate elevators, and occasionally solve a lighter puzzle. I don't want to give anything away, but the game can surprise. Level design is well done and smart.The story grabbed me too, usually I tend to skip the dialogue in games like this, but I enjoyed it here. I's nothing groundbreaking but there's just enough of it, and the short cut-scenes, created just like in Prince of Persia all those years ago, are magnificent to watch. I could criticise the game in some small ways. For example, I would have liked to know in advance the checkpoints where the game saves. But these are small things that didn't affect my experience. The long wait was worth it, Lunark is great. I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I bought my first PC in 1993 just to be able to play Flashback, and Lunark is the perfect homage to the genre. It's visually stunning, and the gameplay is excellent. While it's not a difficult game and the story is very light, I still love every moment of it. Great job to the team behind this game! So glad to have back this project on Kickstarter!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little adventure/platformer in the vein of the original Prince of Persia, Out of this World/Another World, and Flashback. The graphics took some getting used to, they are far more pixellated than any of the games mentioned above but it doesn't ruin the gameplay once you get into the swing of things. The music is excellent and contributes well to the overall experience. Recommended for anyone craving that style of adventure/platformer, though you may prefer to wait for a sale if you are concerned about overall length.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I was a backer on Kickstarter and having now played for an hour, I can say this game is awesome!If your old enough to remember Flashback (sequel to Another World) then you will get throwback vibes in abundance!The graphics are cool, but most importantly the controls work perfectly. You always feel in control and with practice you will be running and traversing platforms in no time.Lots of fun to play, has bosses and a nice set of achievements as well to polish it off. Really fun game and highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you make a retro inspired game! Art and gameplay with obvious and beautifully made callbacks to it's inspirations. But modernized enough so there's no trouble with lagging controls or issues with visibility or to know what to do or where  to go next. And the games lenght was perfect in my opinion! Long enough to not feel undercooked and short enough to not overstay it's welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark is an excellent tribute to Flashback and shares most of its DNA with it (disclaimer: I've never completed Flashback, just dabbled a bit and viewed longplays). If you're looking for an emphasis on 'run-and-gun' gameplay and an abundance of evil droid enemies in space stations/the wilderness, you'll find that here. The influences from Another World (some cutscenes) and Prince of Persia (rotoscoped animations, swinging jumps) are definitely present, but in much weaker quantities-if you're looking for a game that does prioritise those things, as well as a more minimalist interface (no text, just visual cues) go play Full Void instead. Lunark's controls are really good for the most part. Unlike Prince of Persia, the default movement is a slow-walk and you need to press SHIFT to run, which I would have preferred reversed, but Canari Games does improve upon a few things. Ledge-climbing is much smoother because you can jump up and grab a platform while underneath it no matter which direction you're facing and that's an extremely satisfying innovation. There's also a really cool running jump that lets you reach higher ledges on the opposite side, as well as a move which lets you hang on the edge of a platform, and fall safely onto a lower level on the opposite side. These are both animated very well and will make you whisper "sexy pixel art" at your monitor.While controls are indeed solid and intuitive, they do fall apart in some sections. For example, the beginning of level 12 has a part that involves a big climb to the top with large gaps-I had to be facing left, then press SHIFT to run, then immediately press D to move right, then jump with I, then press W to latch onto the ledge on the opposite side. None of the other jumps in the game involved this much maddening guesswork. Another level which caused my enjoyment levels to seriously dwindle was level 10. It's basically a stealth mission but if you get spotted by any guard NPCs, you have to begin the entire thing from scratch which is excruciating if you've failed a few times already. I never found Lunark's checkpoints too sparse until then, and the final boss battle could have used a midway checkpoint as well; the difficulty was fine, but repeating the initial phase and needing to skip through dialogue each time was a little annoying. Level select will unlock once you complete the game (I do think this should become available immediately after completing a level) which is great if you want to clean up achievements.   Huge thanks to one of my Steam friends for reminding me about this game-would not have played it without them.

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark is a revival of the Cinematic Platformer genre that includes classic games like Another World, Flashback, and Heart of Darkness. This genre is known for its highly stylized 'rotoscoped' graphics, complex puzzles, and strong emphasis on slow, methodical platforming and action. Lunark builds upon the foundations of these classic games and adds its own unique spin on the genre.The game features heavy and deliberate controls that may seem clunky at first but become satisfying once mastered. The snappy combat sections acts as mini puzzles that will test the player's timing, pattern recognition, and spatial awareness. The game's puzzles and combat mechanics are well-designed and provide a great challenge for players who are patient enough to work through them.However, in the Cinematic Platformers of the past, it was all about "show don't tell". Lunark, unfortunately, spoils the quiet atmosphere of the genre with filler chatty characters that all sound the same, and attempts at humor that fall flat. This detracts from the overall immersion in the game's world and narrative.The demo offered a promising adventure of exploring mysterious biomes and tombs, but the final game ends up consisting mostly of Cyberpunk-Lite urban environments filled with too many NPCs. This can make the game feel crowded and less immersive than the demo promised.Despite its shortcomings, Lunark is still a thrilling adventure for fans of the Cinematic Platformer genre, offering a unique take on the genre with its own distinct style. If you are willing to work through the game's challenges and overlook some of its narrative flaws, Lunark is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: YOU CAN PET THE DOG / CAT!Had a fun time experiencing LUNARK! A great 2D cinematic platformer. Most similar to the game "Flashback" with a sci-fi setting and general gameplay, but the tone, music, and colors give it a strong identity! I typically only dabble in games of this style since they can be difficult, but I have a ton of respect for them. AND LUNARK is the first game in this genre that I sat down and completed from beginning to end. I really liked it!Leo, the main character, feels tanky to control. HOWEVER, this is by design, and as much as I enjoy reactive games, I don't consider rigidity to be a negative! It adds a bit of tension to gun-play, forcing you to handle situations with a little more thought and strategy... or excessive rolling! Speaking of, with options like dedicated jumping and rolling buttons, it makes a rigid genre feel a bit more modern and easier to control. I did die A LOT toward the end of the game, but this is due to my own impatience in trying to react too quickly to things, or trying to cheese jumping puzzles like a dingus. It's often best to take it slow, and plan your next move rather than jump into danger! Of course now that I've beaten the game, I know how to handle these situations better!While the adventure feels linear, I feel like there is a decent amount of replay value here. Although there are no unlockables, the cutscenes and dialogue are skippable, and many NPCs aren't necessary to talk. SO improving my gameplay to perfection on a 2nd playthrough still felt super satisfying, but I know not everyone is like me in this way! It also clocks in at about 4-6 hours on a casual playthrough, which again I do not consider a negative! My mindset has always been that game length does not matter as long as I'm having fun and improving!As far as visuals, the colors are fittingly otherworldly! Everything pops, nothing looks drab, and animations are expressive! That also goes for the beautiful rotoscope cinematic cutscenes, which are SUPER WELCOME! I want to see more! (maybe a sequel?)The OST has appropriate sci-fi themes, and I was truly vibing for most of the game (with exception for 1 stage perhaps). It's a very different approach from "Flashback", since that game opted for atmospheric SFX over music in many areas. I think both methods work, and contribute to wildly different overarching tones.If I had any criticism, I'd say to make the NPCs a little less heavy handed with hints and tutorials. I get that this genre has some instances of cryptic progression, but this game does a pretty good job of leading you through the game at an understandable pace!I'D SAY GIVE THIS GAME A GO!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a big fan of the game Flashback:The Quest For Identity since I was a kid and there wasn't any other game really like it (I know there's Another World/Blackthorne).So when I saw this game on Kickstarter I was like- wait what? YES. I kept away from any other trailers so I could go in blind and I can say I've been enjoying the heck out of it. It's not leaning on Flashback for it's identity, it's it's own thing and has it's own unique platforming puzzles and ideas. The game is a a lot of fun so far with great art design and music. The only cons I can levy against it so far are: The game has a serious story but there's a lot of humor that feels a bit disjointed from the game's tone. Is that a bad thing? I think that's subjective, while I don't hate it I wish it took the dialog a bit more seriously but in all honesty it's fine. The animation is really well done, rotoscoped and really shows the creator had a lot of passion when making this game. I really recommend this game as we don't have many step-platformers like this and I think for the time I've put in so far I'm very happy to have backed this game.Edit got further in the game and encountered different robots, here's another con I wish the creator did: There's robots later that take a lot of damage, I wish they instead of made them so tanky, the creator instead took a note from Flashback and had these enemies perhaps recoil and fall over to show they were taking damage. The only hint is after they fall over 3 times they start smoking, which is after 7+ shots. This is noteable because earlier you run into invincible rocket turrets- which were fine because you;'re warned of that- with these bots I was left wondering. This isn't a huge negative but took me off guard the first time & just wish there was a bit more of a reaction from these enemies

_childDocuments_.review: I will admit it. I'm a bit jealous of the developer! You see, a while ago I tried making a cinematic platformer. I made all these cool animated sprites and story, but the gameplay was boring. I could not make the prototype fun. Then I went back to the original cinematic platformers to see where I went wrong and, honestly, these games are all kind of... not very good? I mean, the controls can't be the focal point. They were good because they had amazing atmosphere, environments, and riveting plots. They are like point and click adventures with slightly more gameplay. That's how you make them work. And that's what Lunark did. Lunark hit all the right spots. It's an enthralling story filled with interesting characters and no repetitive tasks. And it even improved on the gameplay aspect of its predecessors, reducing the sluggishness. The movements, while still retaining the defining characteristics, are much faster and more fluid. The main criticism I have concerns autosave points and checkpoints. A lot of people experienced the nightmare of closing the game and opening again, only to be met very far away from the last checkpoint. That's because the autosave is not well communicated. But this has already been acknowledge by the dev, who is working on it. I played the game at the day of launch! for this to be the only issue is nothing short of impressive. So yes, I highly recommend playing the game! However, if you are not familiar with grid platformers (or "cinematic platformers"), the controls will seem quite strange, and maybe even off putting. So maybe check those games first, or play Lunark's demo (I think there's a demo).

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Gorgeous game that plays a bit clunky and doesn't seem to have nailed down the tone it is going for.I first learned of LUNARK through seeing its art posted online, and picked it up primarily on its visual merit. I had heard of and seen the games it is inspired by (Prince of Persia for DOS, Another World, etc.) but never played them before, and so I approached this game without any deep-seated fondness for or intimate understanding of the genre. I can say that the final game is indeed gorgeous to look at, with stylized and fluidly animated environments and characters. However, as the allure of the visuals wore off I found the game beneath to not be that fun. To be clear, I did not finish the game in its entirety. Having made it to a subway segment, I decided I'd had enough and stopped. My reasons for moving on are primarily the controls and what I saw of the story:Controls:These frequent stop, tank-like controls may be an artifact from the "2D cinematic platformer genre of the 90's", but they are one I feel is worth revising.Story:From what I saw, the story didn't do a great job of conveying its tone or messages clearly. The store page states that the game is set "in the midst of a rebellion against a totalitarian regime", though in my playtime I saw a single act of oppression by a robot and no rebellion, not counting the destruction my character was causing as they made their way through the city. The player character is apparently some kind of human-adjacent or humanoid species who was repeatedly asked by NPCs if they suffer from "accelerated aging", which seemed to make the player character uncomfortable. The player character was also told by paternal figure Gideon that taking care of one of their kind had been an act of kindness they "collect" on by sending the player to explore the first cave. Yet the player character by most accounts looks and acts identical to everyone else, and any particular motivations, abilities, or stigmas they had weren't explored much in my playtime. If the game wanted to make me take its "rebellion against a totalitarian regime premise" seriously, it may have been advisable to find a better way to explain the function of missile turrets than a conversation with a "Weaponologist" named "Weapon". Maybe have a brief snippet of an actual resistance fighter or fighters getting defeated by a turret, showing the regime's willing use of violence to quell unrest, which could serve to build the world and teach gameplay lessons at the same time. Related to that, most of the subway passengers seemed completely uninterested in the fact that explosions and gunshots were ringing out directly next to them, content to just continue staring at their devices. The fact that the passengers generally didn't care about the conflict happening right in front of them either meant conflicts happened so often that it was not notable (in which case some kind of uninterested but visible response would be more appropriate than no response at all) or that it was overlooked as a way to add to the intensity of combat in public spaces. If passengers are supposed to be scared, have them hastily stumble to a safe area or something similar.  The music I heard was rather bare and not assertive, didn't seem to be trying to evoke any emotional response from the player. Serviceable, but nothing memorable or standout.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video Review: The Cosmos imaginary has always been present in the most diverse areas of entertainment. Since movies, books and video games the premises behind a Sci-fi story have never had an end in sight. Lunark is a love letter to a genre that has remained active since the early days of video games, the cinematic platformer genre. Who doesn't remember spending a good few hours jumping from platform to platform in Prince of Persia, the title released in 1989? Or the cutscene super ahead of time from Flashback? Lunark is inspired by the super methodical jumps of those same titles, but it prints its own identity, although it does not revolutionize the sci-fi genre, it is an adventure that keeps the player attentive to what is happening on the screen.This adventure is set in the world of Albaryne, where the player will play the role of Leo, a boy with very different physical characteristics and who has a rare condition that causes him to age prematurely. Centuries ago the Moon was transformed into a gigantic spaceship by an Artificial Intelligence called Noah, with the intention of saving the human race from its extinction, since the Earth was going through very complicated periods. The idea was to transport millions of human embryos to the nearest habitable planet, in an initiative called Lunark.The player will begin their time in this title in a moment where Leo is caught by surprise in the midst of a rebellion against the Lunark regime. Leo is seen as a rebel after an event that led to the explosion of his ship near Gedeon's Headquarters. With no other alternative, he starts his escape after being tasked by Gedeon to look for an artifact with very special characteristics. Throughout the adventure and in the midst of jumping, puzzles and shooting against an army of droids, the mystery of its origin will gradually be unraveled.There is a specific feel in controlling the character that is undoubtedly one of the most striking parts of this title that, for those who are not used to it, can print equal amounts of charm and frustration. Movement and all the actions that Leo can perform, like firing his weapon, using his protective shield, or jumping while running, have to be measured and calculated perfectly. It's a system that at first glance can convey a feeling of unresponsiveness, but once you get used to it, you can enjoy every little moment. In fact, I didn't find any bug or problem related to the game mechanics, just my lack of skill when jumping in motion.To cross a room full of guards it is possible to have one of two approaches, stealth or combat. Leo is equipped with the roll ability that not only allows him to pass through tight areas but also allows him to dodge attacks from guards or position himself more favorably. Each enemy type needs to take a different number of shots to go down and has a different attack pattern. The important aspect in this sense is to really learn their attack pattern so that it is possible to calculate the next move.Checkpoints can sometimes be quite far apart, and a misjudged jump, traps, or enemy encounters can easily reduce Leo's health hearts to zero. However, the objects collected so far will be stored in the inventory, thus allowing the player to continue the action without the need to repeat his task again. As I mentioned, in this title habituation and patience are a virtue.Lunark is undoubtedly a milestone in cinematic platformers. The brilliant animation translated into low-resolution pixels adds a very demarcated detail of charm. The affection imprinted in this game is also visible in the fantastic cutscenes scattered throughout this title. While it's possible to finish your story in about 6 hours, it's a pretty juicy 6 hours. Albaryne's history is a lot more complicated than it appears, and Leo's journey to Lunark won't leave the planet and the player the same as when they began.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's a good retro platformer with some serious technical problems.Yes, it's Flashback. Feels like Flashback, plays like Flashback, looks like Flashback, except it's even more low-res than the 30-year-old original. The controls feel a little stiff now, but once you get used to it, it plays very well. The game itself is very pleasant.Except for one thing. There's no save on exit. You save at the beginning of each level and that's it. In a game where you can easily spend 30-60 minutes in a level. I mean, there are a lot of checkpoints, but you don't keep them when you leave the game. Really? Do the developers know that people have real lives? That people often have to leave the game and don't want to replay the whole level? My playthrough would be about 1.5 hours shorter if there was an exit save, and that's only because I managed to have an exceptionally long session.This is made worse by technical problems. Setting the game to full screen doesn't work half the time, and when it does, it actually prevents you from alt-tabbing to another application. If you try, the game immediately takes the focus back. So you can't quit or switch to another application. I felt like I was back on 8-bit. Once the game lost the sound and once the game stopped accepting any input - in both cases forcing me to restart and lose all the progress I had made in a level.So, as I said, the game is fine, but all of these problems take away from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game surpasses its inspirational predecessor, Amiga's Flashback, in both gameplay and narrative depth that elevates that classic experience to new heights.  The developers have meticulously crafted the control mechanics, ensuring they are not only free from the frustration often associated with Flashback's controls but are genuinely enjoyable and intuitive. The storyline unfolds in a manner that keeps you engaged, with well-paced plot developments and a rich, captivating world that draws you in deeper with each level. The retro graphics and sound design complement the gameplay beautifully, creating an atmosphere that is both nostalgic for fans of the genre and inviting for newcomers.Additionally, it runs flawlessly under Linux (Ubuntu 22.04, Kernel 6.2)Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Very reminiscent of the 1992 Action/Adventure sidescroller "Flashback" by Delphine Software. But, it's almost unforgivably short. As in, I bought the game on Black Friday and conpleted it before Cyber Monday......and that's even with the game forcing me to do the whole final stage over just because I had to quit when I was near the end.The writing and characterizations were also a bit dry and "kooky" at times. And there were far too many instances where the game would outright ignore inputs and button presses at crucial times in a deliberate and clunky attempt to recreate/mimic the stiff feel of its most obvious inspirations from the 90's like Flashback and Prince of Persia.Still, as a first game from the indie outfit Canari, competently published by Wayforward, Lunark is still an enjoyable enough game that's worth spending the short time with. Although, I would appreciated it more if, given the length, they had at least given it a proper ending rather than sequel-baiting.

_childDocuments_.review: It brought me back to flashback from days gone by. A bit short though. There's a few frustrating platforming sections but nothing that can't be handled after a few tries. I do like how they attempted to incorporate boss fights that didn't rely on stuff that would be hard to dodge with the control scheme.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Having backed the game when it was launched on kickstarter due to the aesthetic being very reminiscent of flashback and another world, I had been waiting for the final release of this.Lunark has been made in very much the same style as the aforementioned games ; Another World and Flashback.   It adopts a very pixellated approach that may look chunky when viewed in a fullscreen mode on a high resolution display.   This may put off some people, but the fluidity of the animation is fantastic (especially on the main character) and absolutely captures the feel of the classic delphine games.Lunark has an interesting story, which is told in the classic style of text on screen (no in game speech).  Again this may not appeal to some. The controls have been tweaked since launch, and have improved some of the rigid behaviours found in flashback.  This said, I did still have occasions where I died whilst trying to chain jumps together (this is something that mostly affects chaining long jumps).The game length is around 5  hours (it can be done in 4 if you know what you are doing, and aren't trying to get all of the achievements).   Generally the difficulty is not too bad, but some exploration is needed if you are aiming for 100% completion.The music is well done, with many small but memorable tracks that are do fit in well with the game.Overall Lunark is a fun title and worth a purchase if you enjoyed Delphine's classic platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I followed the development of this game since it was just a couple of gifs on twitter by the developer and backed it on Kickstarter as soon as it launched. It totally paid off! the animation is superb, the gameplay is pretty polished but can be a little weird if you're not used to cinematic platformers. Some checkpoints are kinda rough but usually I took it as an incentive to challenge myself to do better, except maybe the last part, that was a bit too rough for my liking, but I got through after some extra attempts.Loved it, recommend it, it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark is something really special, growing up i always found the super nintendo games, Flashback, Another World and Blackthorne to be something REALLY special, most of my friends just wanted to play the regular games in my collection, the Mario, Mega Man, Super Metroid, Chrono Trigger and such, they showed little interest in the cinematic platform action-adventurer titles i had to offer :+)WELL!Lunark is for SURE an inspiration to those unique games i found my self playing alone .... by my self .... in the dark .... AND THAT WAS FINE! because the platforming i did, were adventurous!Lunark offers gorgeous pixel art! not only that! it is full of the good old Sierra FEEL to it somehow!ALSO the cut scenes are .... Ninja Gaiden NES level of epicness!looking forward to sit down and beat this game ... alone .... by my self ... in the dark!!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect tribute to old-school platformers. The game is made with so much love for Flashback and Prince of Persia. You can feel it in every pixel. Great variety of locations, atmospheric music, gorgeous cinematographic cut scenes in the best traditions of FB, and just the right gameplay old-school and up-to-date at the same time. Thanks for the strongest shot of nostalgia for years!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you are a fan of games likes Another World. It took me about 6 hours to beat it. The game is made up of different areas that you will travel to throughout the game. Each area requires a mix of puzzle solving and action. The action involves shooting robots and other characters. You can shoot high or low. You also have a shield that you can use if you are standing still. Each area has a unique feel and changes up the gameplay in minor ways. This game has a lot of dialogue, so in that way it is much different than Another World, where the story was mostly told through the gameplay. The story in this game is more direct.I enjoyed the music and the art style. The game looked a little too pixelated when I started, but I soon got used to it and eventually came to enjoy it. Speaking of the art, there are sections of the game where you see full screen rotoscoped style animation and it looks incredible. These scenes usually pop up when you interact with an object. I wish there were more parts of the game that had these animations. There were a few frustrating sections, but after you understand what you need to do, it's really not that bad. The checkpoints are generally good, but there are some that start you at the very beginning of a long puzzle if you die and that was definitely a little frustrating. Though if you interact with certain things, they will still keep that new state, even if you die, which definitely helps lessen the problem of having to replay a section over and over again. Overall, I enjoyed my time with Lunark.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I backed the kickstarter for this game.Just completed the game. It's a super tight, very nicely realized makeover of Flashback that lasts long enough to scratch the nostalgia itch without repeating itself or its predecessors. I'd highly recommend it for anyone with such an itch!Nothing groundbreaking (apart from, ironically enough, the super low resolution which works surprisingly well), a bit too easy, but the ride was very enjoyable nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I helped kickstart this game.Having just finished it, I can say I greatly enjoyed it. It takes inspiration from other cinematic platformers like Flashback and to great effect. I backed it on the strength its early screenshots and the idea of another cinematic platformer, and it delivered on that promise. It has beautiful pixel art, excellent platforming, and rotoscoped cutscenes. What more could you want!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and OMG after playing the demo I was waiting patiently for this game to come out fully. I'm glad that I waited.This game is AMAZING as it has the feel of playing the SNES/Genesis version of Flashback. The controls are extremely responsive and the story line is extremely good. I did die a few times trying to figure out some of the platform puzzles at the end of the darkness areas but all I could do is just say "ah" or "crap" and keep going at it. I hope that the creators make a follow up game sometime in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Flashback you will like this game.  There's lots of cinematic eye candy as well, and a lot of the areas are beautiful (unless you hate low res pixel art, then you won't like this game).The major con is sometimes the story can feel a bit forced (Flashback had sort of that problem too) but with the short playtime/game format theres not much to get around that. Also for those that didn't play Flashback: the controls will take some getting used to.Game length is something like 3 to 4 hours, with a few secrets to find. Replayability is for finding secrets you missed or doing speedruns.Overall a good experience.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played enough to respond to some of the reviews just yet, but I love the Flashback nostalgia of this game.  I love the cut scenes especially.  Someone mentioned the controls being horrible, well I'm going to tell you right now, this game is meant to be played with a CONTROLLER.  Trust me, I'm all about keyboard/mouse for gaming, but just like Flashback... use a controller.I'll update my review as I play more, but I like what I see so far.  I do wish that the graphics outside of cut scenes wasn't so bland, I understand it's a pixel-style game, but they could definitely be better and more detailed.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the games that influenced this one growing up, but following the development process from early concept tests on twitter years ago immediately got me really excited for it. I backed the game as soon as I could when the kickstarter went live and I do not regret it one bit. This game has gorgeous pixel art, wonderful rotoscoped animations and genuinely fun (and at times difficult!) gameplay. Every level was an enjoyable puzzle to solve and I can't wait to go back in and find all the remaining secrets! Excited for what Canari Games cooks up next.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: Lunark is something special.Never played the games Lunark was inspired by, yet I found the controls to be pretty good. At first I was a little turned off, but unconventional controls like this, when intentional, are very easy to get accustomed to. None of my input so far have felt inconsistent, which was great to discover.There's a great charm to the game, to the music and visuals -- loud, bright, and demanding.It's easy to get consumed in focus while playing Lunark as it just has this kind of pull. Milestones are very well paced.If you were always interested in those old games like Out of This World, but only really watched gameplay and never played them, you might enjoy playing Lunark, as I am so far. It's very modern in design and respects your time.This game is an experience worth having. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: This game wants to be Flashback and it succeeds!  I recommend this with one caveat.First the good stuff, it's literally Flashback.  Exact same gameplay, movement etc.  The graphics are awesome, sound, and presentation are on point.  It's an incredible feat to be made by mainly one person.  The gameplay is literally the same as Flashback, and that means that the same grid-based platforming controls are there and they can be awkward and brutal sometimes.  It's not a twitchy platformer.  If you're good with all that you'll have a blast.  The caveat: the dialogue and story feels a bit flat.  Again, it's a great homage to Flashback, Another World, and Prince of Persia.  If you're into that stuff, then I recommend checking this out!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review: An instant classic for cinematic platformer lovers. Hope that Jordan Mechner hires Vinet for Prince of persia 3 < 3Everything works but i find some issues with "high jump", becouse PS4 pad make the player jump again after you climb (i dead like 20 times in the last stage until i decide to use the keyboard). I've got some issues with the long jump too during the chase in lava stage but maybe is another pad issue!Anyway i will replay cos it was a great adventure (i loved the back to the future "mistery sound")!
_childDocuments_.name: LUNARK

_childDocuments_.review:
A pulp adventure set in the midst of a rebellion against a totalitarian regime.

You play as Leo, a lonely young orphan with unique physical and physiological characteristics that arouse the curiosity - if not the hatred - of its fellow citizens. You'll help him fulfill his destiny in the midst of a rebellion against LUNARK, and meet a wide cast of colorful characters, stuck on either side of the escalating conflict.

LUNARK is a 2D cinematic platformer in the vein of the '90s classics. Run, jump, and shoot your way through gorgeous and mysterious locations!

name: Wavey The Rocket
detailed_description: Control the wave and save the Cosmos in Wavey The Rocket, a unique and addictive precision side scroller featuring lucid levels, memorable characters and slapping bass lines. Drawing inspiration from modern platformers with tight controls, fast respawns and tantalizing collectables. Wavey The Rocket provides a fresh new challenge for both newcomer and veteran gamers alike! Have you got what it takes to be The Grandmaster? Complete 80+ levels across 10 themes in the main story and take on challenging Grandmaster levels or beat the buzzer in tricky minigames. Cartoon-inspired heroes and villians! Explore the rad hub world and follow Wavey’s story in his cosmic adventure against The Evil² and their nefarious schemes. Learn to master the wave! Adjust your wave along two axis, and use Dash to quickly reposition yourself to avoid obstacles. Controls are easy to understand, but will take wit to master. Challenge yourself and compete with the best! A bespoke scoring system and speedrun conscious design provide options for high skill gameplay from the first level. Out of this world music! Radical riffs and bombastic bass lines to keep you movin’ in an original hip-hop inspired soundtrack.
