short_description: 🚀 Play as Wavey the Rocket as he tries to stop the moon from being destroyed by an evil corporation that removes fizz from soda! A precision side scroller like no other, it's hand-crafted and set to some seriously funky hip hop.

_childDocuments_.review: The control scheme is exactly as wacky as it looks and I love it.  At the beginning it's funny to figure out how to even to begin to control Wavey, and then when it starts to click the maneuvers start to get really satisfying.Also, I was surprised to see this game isn't just a one-note control gimmick but has carefully designed stages with perfect pacing to teach beginners the ropes, and at the same time clearly intended for expert players to return to for score attacks.  And it has chill 90s beats that give it a calming quality despite how difficult it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game mechanic with very tight controls. Great art and music too.EDIT: OK THIS GAME IS COOL. Currently halfway though the game and the levels keep getting  crazy creative. At first one would think "Sure its a cool gimmick, but I'm sure you can only push this game mechanic so far" but that is NOT the case. Its a trip for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Crazy game control method but worth persevering at to learn. Difficult at times but not frustratingly so once you get the hang of the frankly madwhack mechanics. Lots of difficult to master techniques and super hard endgame style challenges for those who like that kind of thing. Runs well with no bugs that I'm aware of and sports a massive 80 levels to complete.Its got that kind of playstyle where you run on autopilot but simultaneously have to focus intensely. An underrated gem in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Game bought during the Wavey Dash promotion with European Speedrunner Assembly.The screenshots and videos on steam page are a very good representation of what you get: unique sine wave controls, with the player character following the sine wave and not being able to stop. It's exactly what it looks like and I'd compare it to weird games centered around an uncontrollable player movement cycle, like the spinning stick game Kuru Kuru Kururin (GBA) or star riding in Gimmick (NES). There's nothing quite like it, which can be fun, but not recommendable if you're not down for learning highly specialized controls & mechanics totally different from most other videogames.There are a lot of levels, and some interesting variety in them, though the difficulty curve is wavey and the latter half of the game spikes way up. Most likely you'll give up before unlocking, let alone beating all of them - I made it to around level 50 out of 81 so far.I've been told the difficulty is being tweaked in an upcoming patch, but even without it I would recommend the game if the sine wave premise sounds like your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: The control scheme is easy to use, but difficult to master. I am a very casual gamer and I had no problems with the controls (unless I was panicking). Even though I had the graphic settings turned down it still looked beautiful.The music is fantastic and I can't wait for the soundtrack to be released! It has leaderboards for time/score and has extra levels to unlock for getting 100% in each level (which I will be going back to previous levels and  to complete).There are multiple routes in most levels that look like they are designed for speedrunners. Speedrunning isn't for me, but I would very much enjoy watching people speedrun Wavey The Rocket!:
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Was excited to try this out when I first encountered it. Moving along a sine wave was a really fascinating concept to me for a sidescroller. It works well, it takes getting used to and is rather difficult but it's balanced well in that you don't have to get all the collectables in a level to progress in the game. So there's a nice adjustment in each level to account for different levels of players. What was interesting to me was how the sine wave acts as a visual for the player's future actions. It's interesting to me because I was looking more at the wave than the actual character so it asks interesting questions about who we are in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: A really addictive, compelling game with a satisfying gameplay loop.It reminds me of some of my favourite platformers I played back in the 90s in terms of aesthetic, but the control scheme is something new I'd never come across before.Initially, it's like trying to fly a plane with your feet, but once you get the hang of it it's a really enjoyable experience. At its best it reminds me of Sonic the hedgehog, with the player zooming through the levels at a fast pace, in a flow state. The amount of content in the game is also really impressive. After 4 hours I'm only 1/4 the way through completing the levels and haven't touched any minigames or similar.If you're a fan of "just one more try" games of skill and reflexes like Celeste or Hyper Light Drifter you'll get into the zone with this one too. Definitely give it a go!Also the music is great. Props to the music guy, whoever you are.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: I was legitimately frustrated & down on myself in the first hour of playing this game because I was SO BAD. This game is unlike anything that I've ever played, so there is a definite learning curve.BUT THEN, things started to click. This game is very challenging, but extremely rewarding when you finally get through a level that's been kicking your ass for the last 10 minutes. SUPPORT THESE DEVS. They have clearly made a gem & have put a lot of effort into making this game great. Don't even get me started on the music! It's fantastic! Definitely 90s vibes all around and you love to see it.Only 13 levels in (out of 80+) and ALREADY hoping for more DLC levels! Hope this helps :)Note: The devs reached out to me about playing & I figured "why not?" I wasn't paid a penny & mostly wanted to check it out because of the music/visuals. But, it's fantastic. I would easily pay $30-35 for this game. If you like a challenge, this is definitely for you <3
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: I sat here for an hour-and-a-half straight, holding back a  huge crap, hoping that I would get the 'knack' for this game while watching Wavey crash stupidly over and over.Four directions and a Dash button are all that's required  but Wavey travels much too fast down his wave.There needs to be a 'Slow' button. Slowing down requires using the four directions to properly and VERY accurately adjust your path but the game moves far to quick to accommodate that much fiddling.Only thing I could really compare Wavey's game play to would be R-Type at 4x's speed while holding your game pad upside down and rapidly spinning in a swivel chair.You can't blame someone for trying something new but if that something new is a sloppy mess it shouldn't be celebrated with a twenty dollar price tag.BTW - get ready for the 'Carousel' optical illusion when you exit the game; don't stand up too quick. Like what happens when some people bite into a York Peppermint Patty I wound up face flat on the floor with a turd sticking out of my ass.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure what's wrong, but when I try to enter the first level, it doesn't move at all.I mean, the stage does not begin from the first place... Only I can see is protagonist watching the screen of selecting the stage.So I tried to go other stage, but I couldn't cause I could not finish(even begin) the first stage at all.plz fix the problem, I was really looking forward to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: What a unique game! Quite difficult! Awesome music! The controls are so wacky and so unlike anything I've ever played before, but game is paced pretty well to ease you in. It'll be a little bit of a struggle at first but then it becomes really satisfying navigating through the levels!The first section in Level 59 though  -_-If you want a challenge, you'll definitely get one with this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, super unique and fun. Is it frustrating? Heck yes. Is it rewarding when you finally beat a level after 15 minutes of restarting? Heck yes. I tried it both with controller and with mouse +kb and found mouse and keyboard a little smoother and more intuitive for me. My movements were a little more precise overall, but that may be because I play almost exclusively games with KBM. Looking forward to many more hours of runs, hoping to be able to get sub 60 in the time allotted to earn a donation for ESA.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: If you like unique games and/ or platformers, then there is definitely something here for you. This is a unique take on the platforming genre that will appeal to those seeking a challenge, but also a breath of fresh air.You navigate through obstacles via a wavelength scheme. You can choose how fast and how high you bounce. It has a massive learning curve. The fun audio design and funky graphics make it worth it(Received license from GMG. My opinion is my own and not biased in any way shape or form due to the free provision of the license.)
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played much Tetris. There is a point where your skill level and muscle memory put you 'in the zone' and the fast pace makes for some exciting wins.This game has a great likeness to what I describe above. Once you get the controls down this game is a blast. Also I really like the music so far.Definately a great party game, levels are short and challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent indie sidescroller with a unique and interesting way to control the character, which you do indirectly by manipulating the size and frequency of the wave it moves along. Watch out though, the videos make it look much easier than it is! Quite a steep learning curve but it's oh so satisfying once you start getting the hang of it.Definitely one of those games where you can get addicted to trying to beat peoples' scores on the leaderboard! Reminds me of the frustration/satisfaction I get from trying to move up in rank with games like N++ and Crimsonland.The visuals and music are very retro and funkadelic while obviously looking and sounding a lot better than any game people could've made back then. Pretty decent price for what it is and at the time of writing they've further discounted the game to celebrate its release. Definitely worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game. The concept is original and quite fun but also very challenging. A bit like Super Meat Boy, you'll really need to die and retry until you konw a level inside out, at least if you wish to collect everything. As you progress, levels will become more complexe with narrow passages and moving obstacles, requiring a true mastery of the precise control. While the visual design is a bit too flashy to my taste, the groovy soundtrack perfectly matchs the flow of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: Wavey the Rocket is giving me serious flashbacks to Trials & Super Meat Boy... There's nothing like crashing into the same wall 50 times in a row to give you a real sense of achievement when you finally get past it and crash into the next one.If you like the fast reloading, side scrolling platformer then this will be right up your alley. You control Wavey on his treacherous quest to get some soda, a task many of us can relate too. Controlling the speed and pitch of the wave, you would think seeing where you are going would make the game easy but it really doesn't. It does however make it easy to get a hang of but extremely difficult to master as you try to avoid walls, floors, arms, mines and whatever else they can throw at you.In all seriousness though, this is a good fun game from an indie team that you can sink some real hours into... and considering were all stuck in our houses right now, it couldn't have come at a better time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wavey The Rocket

_childDocuments_.review: If you love addictive arcade side-scrollers and can overcome the steep learning curve figuring out the wacky controls then Wavey The Rocket might be the game of your dreams…or nightmares in my case.   I would never penalize or criticize a game simply because I suck at it. There is no doubt Wavey is an incredible game, both in design and presentation, and it’s addictive gameplay helps fuel my “one more try” perseverance. I will conquer this game if it kills me, and you can put that on my tombstone.Full review at

name: Nightmare Reaper
detailed_description: A dark and violent meld of retro and modern action games, inspired by the classic 2.5D first person shooters of the 90s, with elements of modern looter shooters and rogue-lites. Intense and addictive gameplay Tons of enemies are crammed in open-ended levels full of surprises and geysers of blood and treasure. Character progression Use the gold you find to purchase tons of character upgrades and new abilities via minigames. Ludicrous weapon variety 80 unique weapons that can drop as loot and can contain a funky mix of over 30 enchantment types. SO much more Music and audio by the great Andrew Hulshult . Non-intrusive but mysterious story. Many game modes. A mix of manual and random level generation. Tons of random events and secrets. You rise to prevent her doom and duke it out with nightmares to reap salvation in blood.

short_description: Progress through the cursed depths of a nightmare while finding an arsenal of powerful weapons and improving your abilities along the way. This retro-inspired FPS with looter shooter and rogue-lite elements breaches the wall between classic and modern gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe a quarter of the way through NG+. Easily, and I mean easily, one of if not THE BEST retro-fps/boomshoots out right now. Dozens of weapons, randomized stats and perks on them, alt-fires, randomized level layouts, hundreds of unlockable skill upgrades and abilities(unlocked through their own minigames). So much content. The only negative is once, ONCE, was the level layout a little confusing and I got lost for a bit. That was one level in my first 25-ish hours of gameplay. Do not skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 1 word: . Unfocused in so many of its systems that compounds on top of each other creating a very, at best, mild and , at worst, frustrating experience of a old school shooterWay too much visual clutter, superficial weapons, and horrendous maps. Feels like the original spec of the game is a old school / retro / Arena shooter roguelite but changed mid way while not updating previous systems.Mild highlights of the game is not worth the large flaws- 4 or 5 out of 10.As of writing, I put in around 7 hours, however its genuinely difficult to get through, not due to difficulty but due to unfocused and flawed design. Probably went through around 40 auto-generated levels.-----The good / bad. Mix of core elements and specific things+  NR is going for a retro game. Keeps with a retro aesthetic+  A lot of the staple weapons feel dope. Shotgun/Double Barrel/Nade Launcher/Railgun/etc. Some unique weapons like blackhole/Skull thing/etc+  Other than (almost) hitscan enemies and meat sponges, enemies wont make you bored. AI is kinda simple.+  Mid-game tool. Adds A LOT of movement and verticality that this game lacks.+  Maps are more thought out therefore better than campaign.|  TBH pretty bad but you don't play boomer shooters for story. All tell no show.|  Useful movement options are upgrade-locked such as double jump and dash. Overall feels alright.|  Workable but the music lacks the kick like Ultrakill or the memorability like Modern Doom.|  More thought put into it compared to early. Maps more open and arenas a bit bigger.|  Can be interesting. Still a meat sponge but they tend to be unique moveset.- . Shooting and stuff is alright but everything else makes this game uninteresting and superficial. Combat lack any depth due to weapons. Movement feels bad due to maps. Major issues mentioned compounds on each other, making the overall experience poor. -  Bunch of enemies, particle effects, and sprites in your face makes it difficult to play this game.-  Just not good. "Entrance based combat" in early acts. Very little verticality. Everything is squares / lack of smoothing requires jumps for nearly everything. -  Bad map design. Corridor shooter. Just not good. Arenas are TINY.-  Way too bloated. Why have an AK, M16, rapid fire weapons. Too many copies. Many fall under "I need a weapon, this will kinda suffice"- . Anything Auto-generated, 1 weapon carry over, etc should not be in this game. Roguelite works b/c all the game mechanics work in tangent but NR is not a roguelite.-  Boring and pointless. Upgrades are locked behind something boring and pointless.- . So many same-y levels. So many same-y weapons. Secret systems feel like its added for the sake of secrets but then add 4 of the same exact thing.- . "Color key -> Lock door" game mechanic generally alright but does work well with current map design. Also back trekking happens OFTEN. Also not a bad thing BUT NR doesn't add stuff to do during back trekking. : Rapid firing persistent issues. Going deeper in issues i mention above.- Due to the cluster♥♥♥♥ of stuff thrown at you, don't be surprised if you are stuck at the entrance. The early acts I spent way too much time shooting enemies through the entrance b/c the map and amount of enemies don't allow you to go through. Either play defensively or play head first and lose 70% of health. - I like the shotgun but based on my experience, you always want an AOE heavy weapon. A double barrel shotgun will keep you in a fight WAY longer than it should. Engagements that should be 2 mins become 5 because you lack AOE. I remember feeling this issue HEAVILY during the levels in the city. If you make the dire mistake of taking your favorite weapon, don't be surprised you will be killing a lot of your time. Feels like a possible roguelike feature that was leftover. I understand the idea to force you to play with other weapons but playing with weapons that don’t fit the situation isn’t the best idea.- All the money spent on working on the code should have went to better maps. Please Please Please make actual arenas. Legit feels like i’m playing COD due to the amount of corridor shooting I'm doing. Your character lacks good movement options (until grapple), so the more aggressive / fun option tend to be the dumbest.- The acts before the city act is very bad. Pretty the accumulation of the major issues I presented so far. - A lot of boomer shooter mechanics tend to show their age. They tend to be fine due to the thought put into it. Hell Doom2016 uses key cards but the placement, action to get to it, and actions coming back are thought out. NR lacks this so the "color key to locked color door" shows its age HARD. Plus lack of stuff to do while back trekking makes it the game boring. The secrets don't feel like they carry weight. Secrets in other games can be Easter eggs to getting the next tier weapons. All you get is gold for small iterative upgrades.- Not 100% what causes this. Maybe recoil or getting hit by an explosion. Just does not feel good from a player perspective- The power ups are cool. I would love to use them in fights but the algorithm that decides maps decide to put these upgrades in the most random, useless spots. 90% of the time i find a power up is AFTER a fight.  I'm going to assume this is a result from auto-generating maps.- Yes i know i can disable mini games but think about it. The fact there is an option to disable them probably means they are flawed in the first place. Also if you disable mini games, there should be new menus for upgrades.- Should have more ideas to SHOW the story. The report idea is a quickest way to not care about the story.- Roguelite elements work well because all the game mechanics are working with each other. NR is not a roguelite but a singleplayer game with roguelike elements that don't work with a campaign based single player game.- Bloated in so many aspects. I can't tell you specific things in each act other than the general idea. There was the underground act, underground mine act, etc but there are literally no highlights in between b/c each map is auto-generated. All the same. This could be fine if the core game play loop carries it but it doesn't. Also so many weapons that do the same thing. Usually for boomer shooters the weapon loop is weapons have a purpose and identity. But in NR, you have a weapon go shoot it. IMO this isn't fun.Ever since the resurgence of boomer shooter type games thanks to Doom 2016, we are getting a bunch of great games that modernize the equation. I understand the desire and desperation of these types of games, especially after a era of tactical shooters. Games like Ultrakill, Doom Eternal, Prodeus all revolutionize the genre but it doesn't mean every boomer shooter to come out post 2016 does the same thing and should be given a pass.There is a large demand for games like these but that doesn't mean any boomer shooter to come out should get an auto positive response. This game has major flaws and we should hold these shooters to a higher standard.edit:typos

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is a boomer shooter with rogue-like elements. The premise of the game is you wake up in a locked room in a mental asylum with no recollection. You sleep in the your bed to enter the levels. The levels are randomly generated but have a consistent theme like Gungeon or Isaac. As you progress through more levels, the asylum opens up more and the story/power-ups/skill-trees become available. Overall, I'm addicted. The weapons are fun, and some of the enchantments are broken. For example, I have a double barrel shotgun that leeches health and has explosive ammo, so basically I never die. I do have some complaints. The power-ups in the levels are often placed at the end of the arena so they often go to waste. I have a feeling this is a bug with the level generation. Another thing is the levels often spawn hallways that go to nowhere. Sometimes, the secrets spawn right next to the exit.

_childDocuments_.review: Linear boomer shooter like Doom but with rouge-like elements, a lot of randomly generated levels and weapons and good replayability.Nice concept, good execution.The game could use some more weapons but the selection is already not bad.One bad thing I found that really annoyed me is the restrictive nature of more open levels - invisible walls above rooms and that rooms in these open maps have glitchy textures above and below them which generally feels unfinished. I would really like that to be fixed so it doesn't feel and look as bad.But overall a good game.In my original grading algorithm this game got 9,00 / 10,00.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper could have used more pixels in its pixel art, Andrew Hulshult's soundtrack is the standard retro shooter metal jams, and there's some rough edges regarding the frame rate and the pseudo-procedural levels. None of that matters in the face of gameplay this good. Nightmare Reaper avoids many of the pitfalls that plague the roguelite and looter-shooter genres, while mixing them with deeply satisfying first-person shooting to create a downright addictive experience. A surprisingly long campaign, survival maps and new game plus also give it plenty of replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a mish mash of ideas and not one of them is executed well. The boomer shooter elements feel totally lacking. The things that make boomer shooters fun are the level design, the weapons and the gunplay. Nightmare reaper fails on all of those aspects. Then it sprinkles in roguelite elements that add nothing but annoyance. Top it all off with boring mini games that are watered down copies of old nintendo games.The game is ugly as hell and an absolute mess at times with no visual clarity. The environments all blend together and look very samey. I could probably go on if I played more but I don't feel like continuing.  Overall it was one big disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper takes you to a special place. Not only if you're a fan of First Person Shooters but also a fan of climbing up the wall and and hanging in the corner like some Gibbon or Common House Spider.Let me explain.The movement of this game is absolutely incredible. Some of the best i've ever seen. You have full control over your character and thus the environment at all times but that's not to say that death is ultimately your fault. There are some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments in this game, mostly involving opening a door to a literal firing squad but such is the nature of randomly generated levels.I don't want to get too technical, I just want to talk about the FEELING.You know that bit in Commando where Arnold MELTS an entire base full of goons with an M60? You can have that feeling. You can know what it is to be a death god that no matter how many times they are 'killed', they always COME BACK.In summation this is a great fps game with fantastic movement, music and weapons. I'd recommend it to anyone. I think even the Amish would like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Likely one of the finest games I have ever played in my life.The combat is intense, fluid, and evolving as you go.  The action never disappoints, and you develop a fluidity of movement that gamers of all skill levels can adapt to and exploit.  And speaking of exploits, this game does not shy away from randomized weapons that are completely unfair--I had a missile launcher that fired over a dozen incendiary bombs at once and had kickback that could send you into the stratosphere.You want arena combat?  Great, go have fun.  You want upgrades?  Have THREE different skill trees.  You want satisfying headshots?  They NEVER disappoint.  It's got enough story to keep you intrigued, and a variety of environments that is wild, engaging, and fun as hell to play in. This game straddles the knife edge between perfection and simple legendary greatness.  It needs to be at the top of almost everyone's list.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game despite not liking A LOT about it, which I elaborate upon in the review. The recommended verdict is solely due to the shooting itself being fun - which is the most important thing in a shooter. I could recommend Project Warlock or Ion Maiden safely, but this...More about cons below (skipping pros cuz dumb character limit).Most skills are just as boring as the weapon attributes. The "skill tree" so prevalent in games nowadays is at it's worst here. The upgrades are not fun to engage with and there are few meaningful ones with most of them being just a means to an end of power creep.The way you unlock these skills is also not good. The idea is solid - your character unlocks skills through a minigame which has ties to the backstory. The minigame in question, however, is one of the worst 2D platformers I've ever played. It's slow, unresponsive, clunky and most of all - a lot of levels are designed to infuriate you with one-way paths that you have to blindly take to reveal if you've taken the right way with lots of rewards or a wrong way with nothing. There are also segments that require pixel-perfect jumps.You can remove the minigame and just buy skills without playing it, but then you don't get any gold rewards from playing the minigame, and gold is needed to buy skills. It doesn't punish you too much if you opt out, but the feeling of being punished for not engaging with this mechanic is enough to leave a bad taste in your mouth.I prefer games that give skill points for completing levels and killing bosses with less, but more meaningful skills.Nothing can replace hand-made levels with good variety. Then again - creating good levels takes time and skill, so randomly generated levels can sometimes be a good move. Here the levels are constructed from a pre-made chunks (or so I believe considering their design and repeating room layouts). It's not enough to destroy the fun you can have from shooting, but still...After every stage you can only keep 1 weapon of specific level (there are 3 levels with increasingly better weapons). The level of the weapon you can keep is determined by a specific skill in the skill tree and it only lets you keep up to a level 2 weapon. This means that once you find a legendary level 2 weapon you will probably keep it for majority of the playthrough since it's going to be the best weapon you can have. The rate at which you get strong weapons is very low. I got a level 2 self-guided rocket launcher in chapter 1 and then I just kept finding legendary flails and swords and relatively weak level 1 weapons like the revolver or a double-barrel until the end of the game. This means there was little reason for me to ever switch out my rocket launcher for anything else, save for experimenting.I have no idea how would one fix this issue. I get what's the goal behind this - random loot is fun. But when the game encourages you to use a single gun when there is so much variety - that's a problem. This ain't Borderlands where the game lasts for many, many hours and grabbing loot is the very point of the game.Some level 3 guns are really cool, but you may only use them in a level you found them in and levels are very short. I have a feeling this was just a bad design decision that can't be fixed save for remaking the entire guns, skills and drops system from ground up, so chances for that are next to 0.This is mainly a problem for chapter 2. This chapter introduces sewers and grappling hook. Some sewer grates are highlighted to let you know you can enter, but some of them aren't and you can still enter. And some of them you just can't enter. What gives? In the docks area there are open levels where you would be able to easily get around using grappling hook, but the game doesn't let you use it there. Or it does let you use it, but it immediately retracts back giving you no chance to use it to move around the map. This artificial restriction wouldn't have been a problem if you didn't introduce the damn grappling hook in that chapter in the first place!The graphics are bad. It's not a question of style - games like Project Warlock (which also was made by a single guy) look great. Clean, crisp, nicely animated. Here everything is a cardboard cutout with no detail and weak style and the latest sprite updates, while improving the detail for the enemies, didn't change much for the entire presentation of the game. When you kill an enemy, it falls down like an already mentioned cardboard cutout instead of crumbling into a corpse-sprite like you'd see in Doom or, indeed, Project Warlock. The levels are squares in a hight-map, making them look like minecraft maps.At this point the graphics are pretty much unrecoverable. What you see is what you get and what I got I didn't like. Good thing that shooting is so much fun it saves this game.Each level has 1 puzzle-platform segment with a weapon chest at the end. Some of them are straightforward - platforms with timed spikes, jump over, got it. But some are ridiculous. In chapter 2 (yes, btching about ch2 again, not my fault it got so many things wrong...) there are some timed water or door puzzles, which are unnecessarily complicated and obtuse and, often times, strictly timed with a short limit leaving no room for error. That with very slippery jumping controls that simply don't feel good makes these segments obnoxious.I still don't know how I were supposed to do one of those skyscraper-climbing puzzles with electro-blobs on the sides which make gapple hook detach. At first I thought I had to find my way up by looking for gaps in the electric thingies, but no - there are too close together to squeeze between them and if you try to move horizontally using the grapple hook you will trigger one above or below you. Instead I somehow just glitch-launched myself upwards high enough to get to the top.Bad, bad, bad platforming. Moving on.This thing is pointless outside the few jumping puzzles mentioned above. Your double jump can get you anywhere anyway and in the few areas where the hook would be usefull, like the docks - it's artificially gimped so that you can't use it. Granted - there are some spots where you have to use the hook to progress, but it's use is very limited.Melee weapons are the exact opposite of the ranged ones. Floaty combat, no real sense of your attacks connecting with an enemy, questionable usefulness thanks to how most enemies are dangerous in melee or explode on death...Stick to ranged. Melee feels weak in comparison to shooting guns, rocket launchers and black hole generators at monsters.Story is barebones and very edgy, going into predictable directions to show how dark and gritty the character's backstory is. Needs better pacing and some proper reveals, because for now we know far too little at the end of chapter 2.Then again, I play this game for the guns, not the story, so it's not like I care much either way.At this point I'd give Nightmare Reaper a 9/10 for guns and shooting, 3/10 for everything else, so aboutI recommend it, but only a little.

_childDocuments_.review: Being hardlocked from the game was fixed quite fast. _childDocuments_.review: Nightmare reaper excels with itself because nothing is like it but it becomes a victim of its own isolation .My main dislike of Nightmare reaper is formatted into many things. I understand the story  is about someone in a mental facility who is going to escape because all is not what it seems. But the story is pacing of the game are horrifically slow and boring. It is a grind where your only focus is not sadly killing enemies but collecting loot, treasures and selling all but one level 1 weapon for money to buy skills in a horrible mini game.A lot of powers and abilities or gear become optional to use and the maps are a gross collection of interesting places I wish where more expanded and had better gun play. But dont get me wrong the gun play is solid and the secondary functions of weapons are very wonderful.  The game is sadly bottlenecked and gridlocked by upgrades, skills, and randomized weapons that really dont always help you. _childDocuments_.review: I intend to keep playing and might change my mind but so far my experience has been pretty mixed. As far as DOOM elements go, the textures are pretty good, the soundtrack can be pretty bangin' and the gunplay itself is great. There's a fantastic variety of weapons and a decent variety in enemies as well. If the game was just that, I'd be all about it but unfortunately everything else kind of gets in the way.First and foremost, the mini-games. Playing the main game earns you currency which can be used to play minigames which in turn upgrade your character for the main game. The first minigame is a simple sidescrolling platformer. It's a little floaty, a little ugly, and a little repetitive but it's serviceable and it doesn't make you feel like someone is just trying to waste your time. Which unfortunately brings us to the other two minigames. The second is an incredibly shallow Pokemon clone. I'd spend a bit of time complaining about it but it honestly feels like the game is a joke and you actually spending time playing it is the punchline and at least in that regard it succeeds. The third and final is a simple sidescrolling shmup. The levels are very slow, very easy, and incredibly repetitive. Maybe they ramp up later, I don't know. I did a dozen identical levels, reached a second mission and decided I didn't want to do that one another dozen. No More Heroes 2 these retro minigames are not.Secondly, the story. I'm pretty interested in it so far and I really like the hub area conceptually. Unfortunately the story is told in the format of single sentences read by a Neil Breen sound-alike between missions which ends up feeling as frustrating as it is rewarding. I think it would flow better if it was more concentrated and given after every third mission or something like that. Maybe I should just start holding myself to that.Lastly, the rogue-lite elements. For me, they really just don't work. For me, rogue-likes are all about how they force the player to adapt to something new and unique and there's so many elements in service of that. Without the tension of restarting a run, the uniquity of a build or the stress of any real item management, the game doesn't really succeed as a roguelike for me. Which is fine, it just feels like a waste to have randomly generated levels instead of designed ones when it's not really in service of anything other than randomized weapons.I'd like to reiterate that at it's core, this is a great shooter, and if you're more willing or more prepared to look past the awkward elements, you'll probably have a great time.edit: I forgot to mention this game is pretty surprisingly poorly optimized. My computer was generating more heat running this at 120 than Elden Ring at 60. Could be a specific issue on my end or something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an early 90's kids dream game. It has elements of Rogue Lite games, FPS's, and a bit of Side scrolling bonus games to get upgrades I take a small chunk of my days to pick this game up and play it and I have not found any flaws in its very enjoyable and creative gameplay mechanics and brutal Combat; it is the perfect blend of New and old gameplay. Shout Out to Civvie 11 for Supporting this game and convincing me to buy it through multiple videos on this game. People should buy this game as it is worth every penny. I Even recommend getting it for a gift to a friend who has had their eye on it and loves classics like Doom and Blood.

_childDocuments_.review: The first episode feels balanced right, enemies are unique and when working together really makes it a challenge. Nothing about the current build is bad, but it does begin to feel stale if you hard charge your way through the game. * The music is also nothing to ignore, it makes you feel like you're there to rip and tear your foes apart like the Dream God you are.With a lack of difficulty settings, modifiers, or level selects you'll likely have a hard time motivating yourself to run through the game a second time. The only real variables being procedural levels and guns, but after you get in the groove and master what the AI can throw at you it really becomes a breeze. I never really felt all that challenged once I got a Claymore with a vampire effect healing me 1/3 of every swing. I hope to see the option for a harder difficulty, and future mobs with the next episodes to fill out the roster of enemies.What I'd like to see on the side is-Gameplay modifiers, there are tiny things in some levels that will act like a modifier, i.e. reversed gravity. But these are fairly unobtrusive to the regular fight as they come at the end of one. -More Weapons-Legendary Mobs or mini-bosses sprinkled into levels.-New Game+I would definitely recommend this, I believe it has great potential to be a big shot classic up there with the rest. Especially if they manage to build upon the story and keep trickling in our player characters mental state into her levels.

_childDocuments_.review: A promising and fun game at first. I bought it after seeing some gameplay of it posted by a popular boomer shooter reviewer. It catches you with it simple and fun gameplay loop, and it's interesting weapons.Unfortunately this honeymoon phase goes out fast, as you start progressing through the levels, it starts ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with you more and more and more. It just stops being fun.Pros:+ Simple, fast, gameplay loop.+ Interesting, fun weapons.+ Andrew Hulshult soundtrack.Cons:- Very annoying platforming puzzles when movement controls are very floaty- RNG makes it or breaks it- The fact that you can only keep 1 level 1 weapon between each run means eventualy as you progress you will start running into fights you are not equipped to handle- Even with skills ,ammo starts feeling scarce as the game progresses- Many environment hazards are added as the game progresses, by the "Descent" chapter it was getting very annoying to fall into lava while kiting enemies- If you don't have a chainsaw by that point , you're SOL, basically having RNG grant you a chainsaw makes or breaks the fun you can have in the game- RNG can kill you just as easy. Sometimes after clearing a room, a random encounter is generated in that room. Some neutral, some beneficial, and some outright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. I had the misfortune to generate an encounter that generates a haunting ghost (similar to the reaper in Blood,)that damages you,  that you can't avoid without killing the source,  just after surviving a fight by the skin of my teeth with 10 HP. That really was not a pleasant experience.- setpieces start getting repetitive after a while, you start recognizing the patters in which the rooms are generated in- annoying as hell enemies as game progresses:* mobs that bleed acid when killed* mobs that spawn mobs that bleed acid when killed* mobs that spawn exploding mobs before and after being killed* exploding mobs can platform and kill you while you're trying to solve an annoying platforming sequence* mobs that teleports behind you kid, nothing personnel* annoying damagesponge mob that kills your mobility, which is the most important aspect in a game like this- sountrack does get a bit repetitive, as it's one single track per 3 levels, and if you keep dying...- story seems realy realy cliche- powerups that make or break a run are usualy placed in such a way that you only acquire them after clearing the room, making them uselessI honestly think this game would have been a lot better with handcrafted and balanced encounters, and with a little less anoying hazards and mobs as part of the design. It's not hard, it's not a factor of skill, or gitting gud, it's just annoying RNG based artificial difficuly.EDIT: I wish I could give the game a meh rating. It does get better after passing descent. The city gets quite interesting with more gameplay features and more diverse set pieces. However, now that it's less annoying, I have come upon another issue: The performance drops horribly once you reach the city. I start getting stuttering during the levels and after them, while in the hospital.I don't know what could be hogging so many resources as I'm playing it on a pretty decked out PC...
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, now that i figured out how to move the window from my second monitor to my first, i can play so that's fun.The game itself still has it's quirks, bugs and performance issues but it's still fun and has alot of room for improvements.I was sceptical about buying it for the fact that it was early access, since i have never bought an Early Access game but when i bought it and got it running, i was happy to see it wasn't too bad.I'd say it's good. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like every detail was thought out and masterfully executes on all of it's ideas. The loop is super fun, the soundtrack is an absolute BANGER, and even while the minigames are a shift in tone, it doesn't feel out of place and is a nice distraction in between levels as a palate cleanser. If you even remotely enjoy games of this genre, or never have tried any but are pondering on whether or not to give it a try; do yourself a favor and just try it already.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly the first rogue-lite that has really grabbed me and pulled me right in, even with games like Binding of Isaac available, which many consider to be what really molded the genre into what it is today. I've sat for 9 and a half hours over the past 2 days playing this, and the gameplay just kept evolving; new enemies being introduced, new weapons constantly being tossed my way, and little tiny bits of story trickling down every so often, making me yearn to learn more.And then I reached the end of episode 1. After 9 and a half hours, I've gotten through 1/3 of the planned length of the game, and I haven't felt bored yet. I can't wait to see what's in store for us in the other two episodes. Highly, HIGHLY recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: There are a ton of weapons which are fun to play with, but the levels themselves leave a bit to be desired.  Given the nature of this being a roguelike game - RNG has to be something you're willing to deal with.  Levels are typically pretty short and you have a map to help you get around to where you need to be.  But occasionally you get a run where your chosen carryover weapon is ill suited for the enemies the level throws at you.After 2 hours I feel like I've barely scratched the surface, but there isn't enough enticing gameplay here to keep me playing versus most anything else in my library.  Still, I had plenty of fun with this and find it a good mix between old school FPS games and roguelike elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: duke nukem meets borderlands meets diablo. the perfect combination of old school shooting and roguelike.there are so many interesting guns. tons of environments and variety of random events that can happen to you always keeps things going. I will be playing this for so long.one complaint is the key hunting can grind things to a halt a bit but that's only happened to me once or twice. oh and bodies and some things disappear which really doesn't need to happen with these graphics.highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect FPS, top of my list in its genre.Huge variety of weapons, power ups offer a huge boost while still forcing you to examine your surroundings (remember; that sriracha is badass but it doesn't make you invincible,) enemies have a good variety in appearances and abilities. The story definitely feels tacked on, but its still engaging - especially when put in context of the slowly-changing hub.This game gracefully touched alot of nostalgic soft spots on me and made me giggle like a tickle-me-Elmo. If this thing had been around when I was a teenager it would have been life changing.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: It booms.It shoots.Difficulty scales nicely. You only start feeling overwhelmed when you deserve it. Map types don't get recycled often enough to become repetitive- even when you recognize corridor configurations.Physics puzzles and environmental changes to the physics via enemies and power-ups and weapons is good fun. Hook-shotting around the map with the chainsaw feels SO satisfying. Movement is neat and tidy, tight as the weapon choice, variety, and utility. Weapons I would never find myself using in other games swiftly prove their utility and lethality without hype or introduction.Platforming can be challenging but fair and is trivialized whenever you have the chainsaw at your disposal- a neat inclusion that has been an asset the entire time.Atmospheric storytelling is as non-intrusive as advertised, but also provides just enough subtext to make the aforementioned booms and shooting even more compelling. That said, sparse enemy typing is glaringly apparent. Boss looked like a recycled enemy from in-game with a health bar. I also love that I'm playing an adorably deranged female main character- the variety from the norm is refreshing when considering the gameplay from the perspective of the main character- but even if I was completely faceless this game would sell on it's gameplay and visual elements.EDIT:F**K the bomb trap events. No, seriously, they are a huge middle-finger when you're on a good run. Especially when they trigger when you've already cleared the last enemy and you're on low health. Not fun.Just no.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Look i could give you a new run down of this game.However its better to just say.i love loot, i love random stats, i love random effects infused with random proiectiles.This game can give you hours on hours of fun.Sometimes you find a god gun that just evaporates everthing and you just glee like some kind of drugged up patient as lights, blood and guts rain.This game is absurd, the maps are insane as as the enemies and that is why you need to find a broken gun and show them all how how insane you are.GET THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good super modded and modern Doom / Wolfenstein / Duke Nukem FPS with rougelike elements that work pretty well.You have merchants, random events, bunch of weapons and fun stats attached to them, pets big variation of enemies, loot that drops when you break stuff like creates and barrels, and they have NEW GAME +.You can also unlock stats (Inside a gameboy), and a bunch of more stuff.And the best thing of all, a really cool main character with some of the best female voice acting I think i've heard before, and best thing of all is that she comes with a interesting story.--------------------SCORE: 8,5/10--------------------+++++I would give it 10 if they added multiplayer CO-OP / PVP ARENA+++++
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, addictive, decent replayability, great gunplay, surprising amount of fun weapons with various fresh ideas and plethora of ascendingly complex and dificult enemies...Demon slaughter sprinkled with some optional old time platforming for upgrades, and with tiny bit of exceptionally creepy exploration horror between missions with tiny bit of psychological horror laid out in psychiatrist messages left for you to explore. There really is not much negative to point out.But there is some. Since you no longer retain money after failed run, since the beggining you are on timer for gold for your upgrades against number of available missions. Weapons can be changed only in random events which can, or cannot come at all. Even with sound and visual cues, the hunt for secret rooms after level has been cleared can be infuriating (maybe some upgrade in the future will help?). Achievements for buying all upgrades from tier seems to be bugged. All minor nitpicks, but they are there.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:+ Insane array of weapons, practically limitless upgrades and buffs+ Killer music, kicks in just in time for every combat encounter+ Fantastic gunplay, all the guns felt great to use + Slick movement, the grappling hook takes it to the next level+ Levels are short and sweet+ The randomised level layouts keep things fresh and interesting+ Truly immense skill tree masquerading as a series of cute retro minigamesTHE MIXED: / The skill tree buffs and getting good RNG on weapons can make you feel super strong but can also trivialise some boss fights / Combat encounters can be amazing; the glorious explosion of blood and gore and giblets is incredibly satisfying, BUT it can be difficult to read at times, with lots of sh*t happening on screen and a million particle effectsTHE BAD:- Every little thing damages you (an enemy's acid blood, random fire spurting out of the ground, exploding enemies, etc); this was annoying at first but less relevant as your character gets stronger- Although levels are short, there are A LOT of them, probably way more than is necessary and just adds extra hours to the endgame- Key hunting has extra hoops (feed the barnacle, get the battery, heat up the rune stone, etc) that are unnecessary- Random negative events are irritating, most of the positive events seem pointlessNightmare Reaper has more of a Serious Sam-esque arena shooter mayhem vibe than the feeling of the classic boomer shooters with their health/ammo tension, especially once you've upgraded your character's health and damage resistance to astronomical levels. All in all, I had a lot of fun with this one. A retro-style FPS with a modern roguelite/looter-shooter twist. Worth a buy if for nothing else than to see the amusing and absurd selection of weapon combinations that the game's enemies can drop for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: in this world, not everything we love unequivocally is held in the same esteem by our peers. and it is always important to be mindful of how the perceptions and experiences of others can lead them to finding no merit to something you find overflowing with it. this does not make either of you wrong. the fact that you can feel such overwhelming adoration for a work is validation enough.all that fluff to say this game might not be for everyone but it slaps my ♥♥♥♥ diamond, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. every box i have is checked with such visceral precision. the combat feels so smooth and accessible; it makes me feel like a better player than i am without patronizing me, always ready to knock me down a few pegs when i get complacent. the music is Hulshult wizardry and fits the frantic combat moments so well.  for me, what works the best is the variety and the way in which the game keeps things mixed. the platforming, especially in the challenge rooms but throughout each level, the combat (oooooh the combat. so meaty, so punchy, so precise, it feels so good), the secret/treasure hunting, the collecting and the heartbreaking decision of which one weapon to keep at the end of each level, the mario 3 style minigames to upgrade your character, and even the plot playing out around you between levels. it all feels so good to me, so satisfying. the lack of comfort my chair provides is the main reason i don't log longer sessions and more hours in game. i love this game, without question. yes, it has ♥♥♥♥♥♥ me over a handful of times, but i am more responsible for those than the game.as of this writing, the game is early access, and the second episode released very recently. the second ep has added so much to the game, from a dedicated grapple hook to a hub world for each individual area, and a slew of new weapons, including dual p90's, a plasma sword, a junk launcher, a nail gun, and a nuke.this game might not be for everyone, but by ♥♥♥♥ it's for me and i can't thank blazing bit enough for blessing us with this.  10/10,
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: I like to start off reviews with the key details and then add color.Why not to buy the game:- 2. Yes TWO, 2, pain elemental type enemies. These are standard enemies- An enemy that can chain pull you through obstacles into lava. Another teleport-behind-you type. Key thing here is these are anti-mobility enemies and make you stop playing the game to deal with them.- one of these pain elementals have acid blood and spit and create acid floors (this forces you to stop and wait or take forced damage. No way to negate like using gib blood to erase acid on floors like in STRAFE )- Awful jumping puzzles- soft-locks galore (see above)- lets the beast forced damaged into your household until you quit the game- The worst skill tree ever. You have to play an awful mario game to level up. ---Important to note my experience is from never using the f*** awful leveling system in my play through- SKELETON COWBOYS DON"T HAVE HATS. IMAGINE THE INCREASED QUALITY IF THEY FLEW OFF WHEN THEY EXPLODED- suicide is the answer (THIS IS LITERAL AND NOT HYPERBOLE. Procgen can be real bad sometimes and just killing yourself is the best option instead of wasting your time on a level filled with pain elementals)- lack of midmission saving + boss fights + random drops is really really bad- FALL DAMAGE (with jump boost tiles no less) (but synergizes with withe suicide is the answer)- Gameplay changes significantly after the 2 or 4 hour gameplay mark. This means when you realize the crap you've gotten into you can't refund the gameNightmare reaper is about a struggling female video game developer that was making a doom'n'duke style procgen rogue-ish fps game. She went insane and added 2 pain elemental style enemies to her game. When her friends and family played the alpha of it they could clearly tell she was mentally unwell and had her committed for her own protection. The meat of the game is playing through the repetitive BS, pain-elemental stained hell of her own creation. Only until defeating the game can she realize how awful her design decisions were and set herself free from development hell and move on with her life.Guns:So guns here are randomly generated. There are basic types and they can get modifiers. The important onesshottys: Boom boomrevolvers and deagles: blam blamchainsaws: One of the most important weapons as it's alt fire is a chain pull/ grappling hook. Having one of these allows you to escape or lessen the pain and misery of jumping puzzles. STUN LOCKS ENEMY.sticky bombs: allows you to set up traps to kill yourself if damage floors aren't available to reset the level in case of soft-locksheavy guns: oddly more ammo available for. magic stuff: mostly bad with good utility (usually in the alt fire)Ammo:Bullets, BIG Bullets, Magic gloop: Since the game is procgen fixed ammo drops wouldn't really work. So they use the guns use the same ammo mechanics to make things easier BUT...Ammo Usage:Not all guns use 1 bullet to fire. The revolver for instance uses 3. Most heavies use 1 BIG bullet. This creates the odd heavy ammo is more plentiful thingWeapon Mods:Guns will sometimes spawn with modifiers. The important ones:- recoil reduction- pierce= elemental damage - fire sets the enemy on fire (also you if you are close enough (THIS IS SUPER BAD ON MELEE WEAPONS)) - ice freezes them and makes them slow - shock tazes them (maybe does more damage) and does shock effect to everyone standing in water if shock effect hits  water or an enemy standing in it. This is not as cool or effective as its sounds- Ammo consumption reduction or BLOOD AMMO (you shoot your blood at people. super cool and good)- area of effect increase- Rate of Fire- leech (I never noticed it work)Gun Limitations:You can only take one gun of level 1 variety through the level. You'll usually get a legendary one so it isn't a problem. I stuck with a revolver with pierce chance, low recoil, and shock effect. I upgraded to another legendary with less mods but less ammo consumption. It might work less well as the shock effect may have added damage but i couldn't tell.Either get a gun or a chainsaw. The chainsaw alt fire adds SOOO much mobility and allows you to escape crappy procgen jumping puzzle hell.Enemy Drops:Bullets, Big Bullets, magic goop, and Health ORBS. Health orbs do not respond to gravity normally and killing enemies in mid air can make health inaccessible. Some anti-randomness seems to be applied so the player isn't royally screwed.Enemies:I'm first going to note they don't make much sound at all. Really annoying that the sound of people running at you is quiet but your foot steps are not.Skel girls: Claw you. Jumps and dodges bullets. MELEE ENEMIES JUMP AND WILL TRACK YOU DOWN. I was surprised they had this. It is good. Skel Vietnam Vets: Skels with shottys. Slow. Sometimes BS procgen will result in a swarm of these placed somewhere you can't see and result in a bunch of pellets in your flesh. Mildly annoying.Skel Cowboys: Skels that have revolvers. NO COWBOY HATS. ---None of the skels are dangerous. They become dangerous when face with other enemies that force you to deal with them first♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Gargoyles that look like those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from Hexen or Heretic (pain elemental 1):5 sizes- tiny, acid blood on death- smol, minor acid spit and acid blood on death- normal, acid spit and acid blood on death- large, same as above but a bullet sponge and much larger acid spit- BIG MOMMY TYPE: spawns eggs that become tiny ones that can grow over time into normal size (maybe even large). Still have acid spit and blood. Massive annoyance and unfun. Commit suicide until the game stops overspawning them.Infested fat people (pain elemental 2): Explode on death and throw suicide gloops at you. They spawn 1-2 suicide gloops on death. The gloops can jump and chase you. Suicide gloops will sometimes spawn normally in levels. Ground clutter and gibs will obscure them. Seem to choose paths that keep them out of LoS.Wiz Robe: Teleports behind you on spotting you. Annoying and feels lame. Fire attack obscures vision and is annoying.Big Chain Boys: Grappling hook pull that doesn't care about feelings and pulls you into lava. Would be fine if they were such damage sponges. As such just feel lame.Boss 1: For the life of me I can't remember what it wasBoss 2: Big Wiz. Annoying with attacks you practically can't dodge without solid coverBoss 3: REALLY BIG Chain Boy.Maybe more, but I'm giving up and playing openXcom so i can be splatted by cultists with nuclear missile launchers as that is less BS and more fun than this game.Levels:There are 3 level design templates: Caves, Forests, and Town. Everything else is derivative of these concepts. Jumping puzzles and progression get worse as the game goes on.Final area has some of the worst parts with weird jumping physics resulting in you going splat repeatedly from jump boost platforms. Bad jump controls are bad. BUT WHAT IF YOU ADD INESCAPABLE LAVA PITS???? None of the jumping crap would matter in a game with mid-mission saves. In Duke Nukem, Doom, Quake, etc you could quicksave and reload until you learned each game's respective jump BS. This game does not have that and the jumping puzzles become awfulGraphics:its goodSound:Lacking enemy sounds. Music is a joke when you are listening to rad guitar metal and peeking around corners to see if any BS pain elementals are lurking nearby or suicide gloops are waiting for you. Gets repetitive after a while.Overall there are positives to this game but the negatives are so prevalent, inescapable, and just keep poking you in the eye it is just awful. I wish i could have gotten a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a constant source of entertainment and frustration. Its fluid movement, shoot loot,  rpg skill trees, and many reference/Easter egg all make for a constant happy chemical rush. The frustration comes when the grind for currency to skills/ bonuses (thankfully you can turn off the mini-games if you don't want to play them and grind) and level repetitiveness (happens when you die lots and the levels are set pieces that get stitched together at random). Started playing when chapter two was added and loved the way game scratched every itch I had from Borderlands, Enter the Gungeon, Dusk, and Slay the Spire. If you give it the time, just click the buttons to make the myriad of enemies explode into loot and find that next stupid weapon to keep going. It will be well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: An unholy marriage of old-school aesthetics with modern looter shooter mechanics has created a fun and addictive game. There are tons and tons of weapons with endless variations of traits, plus three huge skill trees to gain power and plow through dozens of levels. Now, "plow" is the key word here: the game is never very challenging, and doesn't require much skill: if a level feels too difficult, it doesn't mean you need to git gud, just grind for some upgrades and better weapons unless you become a walking meatgrinder. This makes the gameplay a bit bland, but the simplicity of the gunplay is compensated by the sheer amount of toys to play with and the aesthetic pleasure of gibbing hordes of pixelated monsters.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very very good! I really liked Act 1. Act 2 was a little boring. Act 3 felt a little one-note on the "void levels". Brimstone was frustrating as hell. Flesh pits were a nice throwback to Blood! I think my only complaint with the game is a lack of map markers for key items (gold statue, egg, rune) and their respective "slot". At least allow me to mark them on the map myself. It would save me the arduous task of running around the same level 5 times because I wasn't paying attention when I initially saw it. Aside from that though, the music in this game was kick-ass! It was always getting the ol' heart pumpin while mowing down hundreds of enemies. The controls felt great, and there were a few movement upgrades available to help you with traversal. Speaking of upgrades, I really liked the pace at which they gave you major upgrades in all of the different cartridges. Personal Rating: 9/10Difficulty: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: 25 June 2024: I will be keeping my negative score because of 2 reasons, bullet sponges and those crystals that keep spawning enemies. They are not fun and I'm still wondering why they're in the game. Either remove them or lower their health significantly or idk, limit the enemy spawns, IT IS NOT FUN TO SHOOT FOR 2 HOURS AT A CRYSTAL WHEN THERE's 16 OR MORE THAT CONSTANTLY SPAWN ENEMIES.If that gets fixed, I will be turning this review into a positive one cause other than that the game is pretty fun.Edit: I have gone overboard on blasting the game as I obviously was mad at it at the time so the review could've been way more carefully crafted, so for that I'd like to apologize. I would still say the complaints remain valid for the version of the game from April 2022, with the exception of the dash as it can be modified, but I'll give it another shot to see if anything has improved over time, For now this review remains till I get to play it within the coming weeks or so. THIS REVIEW IS FOR THE APRIL 2022 VERSION OF THE GAME AND MIGHT NOT BE ACCURATE TODAY: Nightmare Reaper used to be pretty fun back when Civvie reviewed it and I bought it, man has it fallen off into yet another far too difficult indie game that doesn't allow you to breathe before killing you instantly from essentially nowhere. Legendary weapons feel like peashooters when shooting the most basic of enemies while enemies deal so much untelegraphed damage from literally nowhere that not even a 1 ms reaction can avoid it. Sadly I am blocked from progressing as the level I need to finish is impossible to complete, even with 5 worlds worth of upgrades. Also, could you make the dash slower and more controlled so I don't yeet myself from Europe to Antarctica back to Europe in like half a second?

The random weapons, weapon features and environments really keep the gameplay loop fresh, but the game never strays from being a love letter to classic shooters that came before.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda wish there was a "Meh" option.The game is not bad. But it is repetitive, and not in the best of ways.The first few levels you feel are okay because, soon, you realize that there is only a single track of combat music. (Or they are so similar that I couldn't notice)So I ended up turning off the music, so I could play "Doom-like" playlists in the background to compensate.The gun part is okay.
