_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare reaper is a lot of fun to play, mashing the best elements from more classic titles and roguelite into one package. The real standout is the great flow of the combat combined with tightly crafted enemies and a fair variety of weapons to choose from that people well versed in retro FPS games will feel right at home with with the exception of a few neat twists thrown in. The enemies start out simple enough, a quick but fragile melee attacker, light ranged guy, heavier ranged guy, but eventually more complex enemies get thrown in that spawn enemies themselves, enemies that jump and rush, teleporting mages, and tanky melee enemies that pull the player in. To wreck the growing roster of enemies you pick up and use a wide variety of weapons throughout your play time. These range from simple melee weapons, rifles, or shotguns to a huge range of explosives and magic weapons with their own little quirks and advantages. Some of my personal favourites from the list include the chainsaw with a grappeling hook, a throwable spiked manually detonated grenade, a spell book that shoots bolts of lightning and spawns balls of lighting that shock everything around them as well as an explosive harpoon launcher. To keep things from getting too complicated you only have 3 ammo pools, light, heavy, and magic. Each weapon depending on the type eats more or less ammo from these pools per shot. A weapon can also have different rarities which can give simple buffs like more fire rate and crit chance or do exciting things like do elemental damage, pierce or leech life. The catch is that you can only actively use 2 weapons at a time starting out (you can upgrade this later though a skill tree) and at the end of a level you can only hold onto 1 weapon. The level design is great despite using a random selection of pre made tiles. You'll see some reused rooms but they are well designed enough and have enough variety that you don't really notice with how the combat flows. Levels also have random events and powerups. Some can help you such as golden birds the give treasure when shot, a dog that gives you gold in exchange for bones, neutral events like a slot machine showing up or events to hinder you like magic orbs that spawn elemental damage or a scary floating head. This makes a lot of encounters interesting and are a fun bit of spice to run into during a game. This is an early access title so it's not without it's bugs but they were mostly minor and didn't cause me to lose a whole lot of progress. There were a few crashes mainly when picking items up but i think it only happened like 3 or 4 times in the 10 hours i played and after the patch i haven't had a crash. Despite being early access it still has a fair amount of content (took about 10 hours to complete my first playthrough) and the devs are taking advice as well as interacting with the community. New game+ is already being planned which is good. The only real gripe i would have is that the skill tree has a platforming mini-game attached to each skill that is kinda janky at the moment. The big problem is that the character hitbox and enemy hitbox is a square so you need to be careful jumping over things or trying to jump up through small holes. They aren't too hard and if you don't complete the minigame it doesn't take your money so you can try it as many times as you feel like but they do kinda get annoying. One suggestion i would make is add an option to skip for more money or have it cut the cost in half if you actually play the level. Again, devs are taking advice so im confident that it will be addressed. If you enjoy classic FPSs and Rogue Lites then i would 100% recommend this game. It's easily worth 20 bucks just for the content currently in the game. Nightmare Reaper is a very tightly put togeather game and a real joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Currently playing three other games within my game to make sure i'm upgraded. Now if only we could go DEEPER and find a game within a game within a game. Oh, it's also an AMAZING DOOM-like shooter, but that's not important because i'm looking for more game cartridges, have you seen them?Real-talk, it's a unique Doom-like FPS with a good retro feel, whilst still maintaining a fresh twist of content, weapons, levels, upgrades, and mechanics all in one. There's no 2 hour tutorial so I recommend giving the game a shot, I don't think anyone'll be disappointed by it and I feel like most people could pick it up with ease whilst the game still manages to maintain some solid thrashing even with good skill and b-hopping.Only real gripe i've had with the game, is that i've had 2 instances of getting instantly 1-shot despite having 140+ health and i'm just willing to chock it up to bad circumstance or placement on my part, as it seldom happens and you almost always feel like you're in solid control of yourself. It even opens up and allows you to get upgrades to make mobility, parkour, and even combat much more free-flowing or even combo-able as the game goes on.

_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible throwback to 90's FPS games: great shooting mechanics, diverse and numerous enemies, straightforward levels with lots of (optional) exploration throughout with minimal wasted time with useless mechanics found in most modern games (crafting, weapon upgrades or bullet-sponge enemies).Most impressive is how it manages to stick to the tenets of classic FPS while adding features and small details that aren't present even in modern games. The way secret rooms work, having a visual and audio cue, makes exploration interesting and not a random affair of mindlessly clicking every wall you see.Very creative with its skill upgrade system, adding some classic mini-games for skill progression: platforming, shoot-em-up and survival-like arenas.Just a blast to play through. Can't wait to see what the developers will bring up next.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game that you can sink hours into. The gameplay has a fun throwback to shooters of a by gone era, yet the light RPG mechanics make the game worthwhile. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not a real fan of the rouge-like or rouge-lite concept, so maybe this thumbs-down is one of the infamous "it's not you, it's me" things, but anyways: Although I really like retro-shooters, this game is riding the retro-thingy a little bit too hard in pretty much every aspect in my opinion.First of all, the sprite resolution is so low that I don't even know what I'm fighting here: Demons? Zombies? Girl scouts? I have no idea! What's that on the floor? Gold bar? Ammo box? Butter? Seriously, I think this game has gone below the limit of what could be considered a healthy minimal sprite resolution. This gets even worse when you're mowing through a pack of enemies and guts, drops and debris starts flying around and then the battlefield is drowning in a sea of sprites uniting in a giant mess of pixels so that you have no idea what you're looking or shooting at.Next is the selection of weapons: You're only allowed to keep one level 1 weapon when transitioning from one level to the next level. As the levels and weapons are randomized, it's pretty much just a matter of luck whether the game spawns some useful weapon for you or whether you'll be shooting with a bunch of junk for dozens of levels. This can be especially frustration when the game decides to throw you into a closed-room fight with a horde of dozens of enemies, preferably at the beginning of the level when all the weapons that are at your disposal is a level 1 pistol. Oh, the game also has occasional powerups similar to those from Doom, but in my case in 9 out of 10 cases the powerups spawned in a place where no enemies where close, so the powerups were completely useless...Then there's the skill system, where you have to play a Mario-like minigame to unlock upgrades. That's somewhat fun for the first three to ten times, but it gets pretty much annoying after that. There's also some other minigame involving some JPRG style stuff, but I haven't really tried that so I cannot even tell you what it does.I really like heavy metal (the music, not the chemical elements), but being forced to listen to the same heavy riffs for several hours like in this game gives me headaches -- a little bit of variety would have been nice here.Finally, there's the length of the game: this game is way too long. The game is stretching its playtime by making you play each (randomized) level type three times. I have stopped playing this game after the 40th level, because it simply got too boring.-- Edit --Okay, I've pulled myself together and continued playing a few more hours in the hope of completing this game and let me tell you: it only gets worse after level 40... I'm now stuck at level 48, which I have tried to beat about 25 times now: The game has decided that the first room in that level should be a room with red spawning crystals that continously spawn badass enemies until they're destroyed. Now all I have at this point is my legendary (yet crappy) Level 1 Nailgun from the previous level, because the game only spawned crap weapons in that level, and the enemies now drop barely any health drops at this point. I managed to beat that crystal room one or two times just be butchered in a another spawning crystal room behind the first one, before even being given the chance to pick up another weapon or regenerate health in any way...The game has now become pretty much officially unbeatable for me, because I have no chance to get any other weapon before that crystal room and I'm not getting anywhere with my nailgun here -- which is just a perfect proof of how screwed up the basic concept of this game is -- it is pretty much up to the mood of the RNG whether you are allowed to beat this game or not...
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun and addictive retro-styled FPS. Some consider it a roguelite but there aren't "runs" nor permadeath. The only thing lost if you die is progress on that level specifically. The random level generation doesn't create those feelings of monotony that I think a lot of other recent indie FPSes with randomization suffer from. Weapons are plentiful, feel fantastic, come with altfires, and can be spawned with some very fun random perks attached. If I was forced to compare the combat feel to something, it would be Blood. The juking of enemy attacks and constant exploding scenery just give me huge Blood vibes, but with added showers of gold coins from every kill. There's a huge amount of content here if that's a concern. You've got three episodes to beat, multiple new game plus runs, a wave survival mode, and a smattering of minigames that you need to dip into occasionally. And all of this ties into your progression in satisfying ways, making you stronger and stronger.  I really can't say much more other than if you like FPS games Nightmare Reaper is absolutely worth purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, old-school shooter feel that uses RNG well enough to add consistent variety. There's a little mini game you play to unlock new skills, increase damage/resistance, etc... that can get a little sloppy but the idea is good; it adds a little break between missions. My favorite two things are that it throws you right into the game without even a menu and that you get points for destroying objects. A must play if you enjoy fast-paced 2.5-D shooters.Edit: Please allow the player to disable dash.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure where this came from but it's like someone got really high and said "wouldnt doom be a cool lootershooter but instead of fighting demons from hell you're fighting your own neurotic disorder?" and just sat down and put real work into it, I'm honestly impressed. Good ♥♥♥♥ my guys, and Rock and Stone forever :)
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well made. Violent, gibbing, and much more.There is a minimap which will help you if you get lost, but the level design is very good. There are noticeable landmarks and the levels are very recognizable.The difficulty feels very balanced. There is hit scanners, but they have animations to show they are attacking. In no time at all you'll master different types of weapons and use what's best for every situation you find yourself in. If you need more convincing to play this game, watch Civvie's video about it. The feedback is extremely satisfying and before you know it you'll be hooked. There is much more to talk about but you honestly should just play it yourself and find out ;).Without a doubt this has been one of the most thrilling games I've played in a long time. I would recommend it to people who aren't a fan of doom-likes even. The dev is also very responsive to feedback. I'm sure this will be one of the greatest games this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: this is a tough "No" but only as a total review i like 75% of what the game is going for but the 25% i dislike is impossible to ignore. the game has a wealth of options and weapons that randomly drop but the weapon balance is terrible. out of dozens of options only 3 or 4 or viable as enemies gain more HP and you're faced with hordes. level structure is iffy when the RNG sets up an unfun random encounter but for the most part the random level design worked well...until the last leg of the game. once you're expected to bungie jump from tiny island to tiny island while in a oxygen vacuum i finally checked out. its not fun and never will be for me. if you want looter shooter wrapped in a retro shooter candy shell you will get lots of fun and very worth the price if grabbed on sale.  this is very much a case where a "Neutral" review might be more accurate.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: A great rogue-lite classic themed fps game, every weapon seems viable, yet gives you incentives to find better. the enemy's are varied and keep the game-play fresh, the weapons have what can only be described as "good gun feel" and are varied from projectile based, hit-scan and explosive. The secret rooms are hidden but not impossible to find and are always worth it due to the currency system that lets you purchase perks. you will see a couple rooms more than once but the theme of the level changes episode every 3 levels so it always seems fresh. The only problems I have with this game are small in the comparison to the upsides, for example the optimization is a little spotty, I play the game at 1440p with an I7 8700k and gtx 1070ti, which you would assume with the chunky pixel graphics would have no problem but I see dips in frame rates down to 30fps on occasion (I should add that the game is completely playable expect for some lag) and the first couple episodes can seem a little slow because you don't have any perks. These problems can be forgiven and definitely are not a deal breaker. overall and this game greatly exceeded my expectations. Cant wait for it to come out of early access and am very excited for the future of this game and the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Moments of quiet dread and maniacal bloodbaths filled with bullet hell mayhem are interspersed with flashes of anesthetic nostalgia. _childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.Really addictive and fun : the weapons (with random stats and qualities) are great, the music is killer (good ol' Andrew Hulshult), you get randomized level layouts for extra replayability and ALL the secrets and easter eggs. Also a skill and level up system with minigames (you can deactivate if you can't be bothered with it but I liked them) with all the good stuff : more health, more mana, more money, more elemental effects... _childDocuments_.review: Intense Retro Shooter with a Fiery SpiritRating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐Nightmare Reaper is a love letter to the classic retro shooters of the past, delivering a fast-paced and adrenaline-fueled experience that will satisfy fans of the genre. Created by Blazing Bit Games, this game embraces its old-school roots while injecting its own unique style and modern twists, resulting in a thrilling and challenging adventure through the realms of nightmares.From the moment you step into the shoes of the Reaper, the game immerses you in its dark and atmospheric world. The pixel art visuals are beautifully crafted, capturing the essence of classic shooters while adding a touch of modern flair. The variety of enemy designs, levels, and weapons keeps the gameplay fresh and engaging, as you mow down hordes of monsters and face off against menacing bosses.The gameplay in Nightmare Reaper is intense and action-packed. The combat mechanics are responsive and satisfying, allowing for precise shooting, fast movement, and skillful dodging. The wide range of weapons and power-ups provides ample opportunities for strategic decision-making, catering to different playstyles. The game also introduces a unique combo system, rewarding players for chaining together kills with stylish flair.One of the highlights of Nightmare Reaper is its level design. Each level is meticulously crafted, featuring intricate layouts, hidden secrets, and intense encounters. Exploring the interconnected corridors and rooms keeps you on your toes, never knowing what dangers or treasures lie around the next corner. The non-linear structure encourages exploration and rewards thoroughness, adding replayability to the game.The soundtrack of Nightmare Reaper deserves special mention. Composed by Andrew Hulshult, known for his work on iconic shooters like Dusk and Amid Evil, the music perfectly complements the fast-paced action and eerie atmosphere. The heavy metal and synthwave tracks enhance the adrenaline rush and immerse you further into the nightmarish world.While Nightmare Reaper excels in many areas, there are a few areas where it falls slightly short. The difficulty curve can be steep, posing a challenge that may discourage more casual players. The lack of a compelling narrative or deeper story may also leave some players craving more context or motivation for their actions. Additionally, the game's retro-inspired graphics, while charming, may not appeal to those seeking a more visually polished experience.In conclusion, Nightmare Reaper is a thrilling and nostalgia-inducing journey that captures the spirit of classic shooters. Its intense combat, atmospheric levels, and captivating soundtrack create an engaging experience for fans of the genre. While it may not be the most accessible or narrative-driven game, its unapologetic old-school approach and stylish gameplay make it a must-play for anyone craving a challenging and action-packed adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent blend of retro and modern mechanics, Nightmare Reaper has the charm of HD-2D graphics combined with an addictive gameplay loop of looting, upgrading and playing three different minigames to continue buffing your character for dozens of hours. I only finished the main game at over 30 hours' playtime and have nowhere near completed all the minigames or the horde mode Arena missions. The amount of content you get in this game is astounding - it's like buying a base game that has about 3 paid DLC bundled in. I'm going to take a break from it as I've reached a point of fatigue playing this much of one game, but I may well come back to it later to see if I can complete some of the minigames and skill trees. It continues to be fun dozens of hours in - so the pacing has clearly been well considered. If you like FPS games, roguelites, or boomer shooters, this game is for you. 9/10 (I think this could easily be a 10 for some people, but personally I have a preference for slightly shorter games; also the theme of the game, while well executed overall, doesn't feel particularly cohesive or aesthetically inspiring - this is usually the case when a game has tons of content and a focus on mechanics - the nature of roguelites and looter-shooters usually tends toward a "maximal" approach, but it's not a design style I find satisfying. Seeing as these gripes are very much about personal taste, I've still given NR a high score as it is very good at what it does!)

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. Screenshots and videos don't do this game justice. It *starts off fun* and *keeps getting funner*. Play a level->return to hub. Hub gradually opens up, and you gradually get little bits of small boosts (more hp, ammo, etc.)... but instead of a skill tree, it's through a Mario-3 style minigame. Gradually get more stuff to explore in the hub as the campaign goes on, more coins to unlock stuff, a couple more ways to unlock *more* stuff, an arena-mode accessible from the Hub that keeps going...So many small little "random event" minigames that range from a DDR-like to Viscera Cleanup Detail to a Doom reference to stuff I probably didn't even understand.Weapons drop in each level, but you only keep 1 at the end of the level... however... that means each level/arena starts off with that gun and then you get a ton of drops during which you can either pick a new favorite or just try out a ton of semi-random stuff. My favorites so far have been shotguns with "Random Projectile" that have included Rubber Chickens, Toilet Paper, and actual projectiles from other weapons.Just... so much to love, so many weapons to try out and have ridiculous amounts of fun with...This is definitely one of the best FPS games of all time.Highly recommend even at full price for anyone that wants a fun, sometimes hectic, but with some nice downtime to explore the levels once you've cleared them, FPS.Also, the arena mode you unlock early on is stupidly good too. I probably stopped playing the main game for a few hours just having fun in that.The game starts off fun, and keeps that up for however long my playtime currently is.Update: The weapon variety and stuff in this is still better than sex. 11/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Trying to find the right words to describe Nightmare Reaper is a bit tough for me. On the one hand, its a tribute to classic 90s shooters, and on the other, It has a bunch of roguelite personality.I found out about it through Civvie-11's youtube channel and have been watching its development for a little while and decided to take the dive, in spite of having pretty bad reflexes. I like that the maps are procedurally generated. No two maps will be quite the same. You might see similar elements between two maps, but they're never identical. I also appreciate that If you die on a level (and you will. A lot.), that you keep the loot and money you've made. The game wants you to push forward, and if the way forward is picking up perks and bonuses from the mini-games, then the devs just want you to have fun.I had a couple of hard maps early on in Chapter 1, but then I got a hive-hand like weapon that lets you shoot homing bees, or just shoot out an entire nest of bees. That brings me to the weapons. Oh god, the weapons. AK47 with explosive rounds, an assault rifle with underbarrel grenade launcher alt fire, Harpoon grenade launcher (as in, shoot something, pin it to the wall, grenade blows up). and so much more. My other favorite weapon aside from the hive hand for shooting around corners in the first few chapters are the sticky bombs. Name says it all. Makes it easy to create choke points, and take out multiple enemies at once.If there's any advice I can offer is that I have a REALLY sensitive mouse, and it lead to me swinging too wide while aiming towards enemies. Turn your mouse sensitivity down. It'll help out a lot. Also, every map seems to have a section dedicated towards running a gauntlet - spike pits, flames, precise jumps, etc. If you want to trivialize these challenges, get a chainsaw, and use the hook alt fire to pull yourself up to the end of the gauntlet, and deactivate the traps.Gameplay: The game complements many different playstyles. Due to poor reflexes, I have a tendency to bait my enemies to a choke point, and let the explosives take over. But if you're a guns blazing kinda lad, good luck. Controls: The FPS controls are pretty intuitive for anyone with any sort of experience with a first person shooter. You'll pick things up in no time.Music/Sound: The heavy metal soundtrack that belts out during combat is just chef kiss, and goes so well with this game. The sound design is also very thoughtful. The wind howling sound is a nice audio cue that there are secrets nearby. Enemies grunt and growl and squeal as you approach, audio cues giving you clues as to what actions they intend to take. I'll note that the skeleton soldiers with pistols, and shotgunners however are DEAD SILENT. If you're not keeping aware, you won't know a shotgunner is there until they point blank you with a shotgun. Sound feedback from the weapons is rather nice as well.My Verdict: Its fun, its relatively cheap and it has a little something for everyone. If you like 90s FPS, grab a copy. If you're not sure, go grab the demo, see if its something you might like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has taken far more of my time than I have anticipated.Nightmare Reaper is a lot of fun to play.  Not something one needs to spend a ton of time into learning, but does have a surprising amount of depth to it.  Each level is randomly generated and keeps things fresh.  If you don't make it through on one run, just try again.  You collect money and weapons on each play through.  If you die, you lose the weapons you have gathered, but keep the money which is used to spend on increasing your skills and abilities and making you more powerful.  There are a variety of weapons in the game that also increase with power as the game progresses.  I have seen chainsaws, swords, shotguns, ARs, magical books, nukes, etc.  There are so many to chose from and they also have different levels and rarities to them as well.  If you finish a level, you get to keep one of the weapons and sell the rest which also helps increase the amount of currency you have to spend on new perks and abilities.  Sometimes it is a difficult choice which to keep, so make sure you pick the right one to keep or things might get more difficult.  Gaining abilities is really unique and fun.  Your menu is something with the likeness of having a GameBoy Advance with one "game cartridge."  The first one you get gives you mini games to play that play like Mario Brothers, which upon completing a level, you unlock upgrades for your character.  As you play further, two more become unlocked with vastly different styles to play, modeled after two other popular styles of games.  And wow, I have played this a lot and feel I still have a lot left of the game to go.  So much to do.  Levels are quick and short, but there are a ton of them with plenty of variety and ways to accomplish each.  On top of that, you can unlock a sort of horde mode to play which gets another style of currency for other unlockable perks and abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.... this game.... simply fantasticIt takes you back to retro styled version with remembrance of Wolfenstein / original DoomIt's really well made, combat system, the sheer variation of weapons to make the constant looting and changing match the pace of the game.It's fast, it's brutal and it's on the wayYou have a passive upgrade system as well, nicely embedded with sorta minigames (which i found pretty fun to match the retro style environment)There's really not much of a story, but it's still a nice touch that pseudo horror feeling that you get while "awake"I'm already knee deep into the game and can't keep away from it, having a blast. Thanks for indie developers that can bring us this hidden gems while triple AAA just vomits the same crap over and over to mindless average.If i would like anything to improve, it's the optimization.... I don't think i should see fps drops on a high end rig, nothing major nor too bad, still...While the game might not be everyone's cup of tea, i strongly suggest to give it a go.... even more so if you enjoyed  retro style games like the ones mentioned.The dev made something amazing here, and the level of detail shows how much effort was put in this, i can only imagine how much iteration everything took to get up to this point. It's massively appreciated! Kudos for the masterpiece!And also....PetDatDog!Rock and Stone Brothers!

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is a retro first-person shooter that pays tribute to old-school FPS games such as Doom, Blood, Duke Nukem, Half-Life and Quake but with modern mechanics.The game has a decent default difficulty and I died more than once during my playthrough, You have to finish level on one run, no quickloads and quicksaves, you either get it done or get kicked back to the beginning. The map is always randomized so If you die and jump back again to retry,  you won't be able to complete it more easily by remembering previous encounters and locations.Game also allows you to carry tons of weapons with you and use them at the current level as you please but at the end, you have to give them up and can keep only one of them for next level.Gunplay has a kick, recoil and the audio response of superb level, It just feels so freaking good to blast that quad barrel shotgun right into someone's face with satisfying clicking of slugs dropping on the floor.Nightmare Reaper currently offers around 50 weapons to choose from, knives, swords, revolvers, sub-machine guns, assault rifles, classic broomsticks and weapons of mass destruction such as Mini-Nuke launcher, Black Hole gun, Laser gun or Railgun and many more.Each weapon has a primary fire on LMB and alternative fire on RMB, it can be your good old aim down sights, trigger button for your bomb to explode before impact, charge attack or toggle of alt. fire.Weapons have Levels 1-3 and rarity - Common, Uncommon, Rare, Legendary - rarer it gets, more perks it has but perks this game offer for your weapons are not always on your side. There are perks as pierce chance, leech, freeze dmg, magazine size, fire rate but also rather negative ones such as screen shake, ammo consumption, blood ammo, charge time and knockback that can go either in +/-I once found a legendary semi-auto shotgun that had leech, + 30% magazine size but with LVL 5 Kickback so every time I shot I went flying backwards but It keeps things fresh and it makes you think more how you use your weapon before you get in combat.Movement is fast and tight and as you progress you will get dash, double jump and a grappling hook that helps you to move around the battlefield.  There are even  some puzzle/jumping sections that put your movement in the test but they are optional.What about the soundtrack?To simply put itThere wasn't a single moment where I wouldn't be Pepejaming while playing.This game was surprisingly a lot of fun and a great game where you can just put off some steam after a long day and its one of those "just one more level" type of games. I'm looking forward to upcoming updates and chapter 3
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what I expected, but not this. It's a bit of an everything-and-the-kitchen-sink affair, with tons of content not all of which is relevant, balanced or enjoyable, but most of it is and some of what isn't can be skipped and it works out very well. The game might feel very grindy at times with its steep price tags for climbing the skill trees and the glacial drip-feed of what little plot there is, but the actual shooting gameplay is proper fun so you can actually play another level just for its own sake instead of merely to forge on through the progression. Oh, and the game mostly refuses to explain itself; be prepared to look things up on the internet.Even secrets hidden in the levels, normally a feature that requires you to smear your face across the entire level geometry while trying to interact with every individual pixel, are tolerable to fun here. There are visual and audio cues and later on in the game you can even buy a pet that notifies you when there's something to be looked for. And even if you can't be bothered to backtrack to fit that last key into that last lock so as to get that last bit of treasure out of a level, it's not a problem, because there is nothing missable- everything you can do in a level translates into a single currency in the end, so playing two levels quickly can be just as profitable as playing one level thoroughly.Overall perfectly solid. Doesn't take itself too seriously, but also doesn't jump the shark. Nice balance of traits there.

_childDocuments_.review: The gun gameplay is well executed and the movement is responsive. I like the random weapon system which makes the endless killing endurable. Thats all good I can say.While the FPS part is fun, I have to say that this game suffers from bad core gameplay progression. You get character/weapon upgrades by playing minigames that are like standalone games next to the "main" game so you play 2D versions of a spaceshooter, pokemon and platformer to earn increased HP, ammo etc. for when you return to the FPS levels. While moving and shooting is fun, the levels themselves are not. Every time you start a level it gets procedurally generated so if you die and start the level you get a different seed. Sadly this is another case where procedural level generation is complete garbage. Every level has the same building blocks with different textures, everything is very crammed and bad to navigate. It doesnt look good and it plays worse. Enemy mobs have arbitrary density and spawn points, additionally there aren't that many and they are pretty much all the same between level sections (same enemies in caves, woods, towns). While the main goal is just to get to the end of the level, there are "secret areas" where you earn currency to spend on your minigames. Because its procedurally generated these areas are not cleverly hidden but you have to find random walls with cracks in it so have to run around and look everywhere (they at least make a sound if you are close). Often all three secrets per level are clustered together in one spot.Going from level to level is just no sense of progression in this game. Level 1-30 that I played are all completely the same gameplaywise, you cant keep weapons between levels and most of the time the character upgrades are pointless. After every level you land in the asylum hub to read another 3 sentences of stretched out lore. The minigames feel like a chore very fast but the game keeps giving you new minigames where almost all of the upgrades are pointless because they give something like +1 HP or 1% weapon quality. Every meaningful upgrade is gated behind 20 filler upgrades. The same goes for guns, why even have 5 weapon slots if you end up using the one good gun you find for the rest of the level anyway? Its just stretching game time. After the 8 hours I played I felt like there is just nothing interesting coming, if you played one level you played them all. There once was a boss that I killed in literally 3 seconds and I havent seen another one since. This game for me is another case of failed procedural level/gameplay generation to create dozens of hours of dull and soulless content when you could have just manually created 5 good maps for 10h of great gameplay instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I find it very strange that I ended up typing out a negative review for this game, because I absolutely loved the first ~8-or-so hours of it. It started out really strong and fresh, a simple throwback action FPS-game with charming graphics, an interesting premise, a fun weapon collection system and a bunch of quirks to keep you interested along the way. But I'm 20 hours in now and the game has overstayed its welcome by a large margin, at the moment I'm just suffering through it just to complete it so I can feel finished with it. I'll make a comparison regarding what the gameplay-loop of the game initially was and compare it to what it has devolved into for the last half-or-so of the game: Initial (good) gameplay loop: Enter new and interesting area. Explore rooms, encounter new and varied enemies, find new and interesting weapons to try out and use, collect money to use in a small and simple minigame that serves as a cute little upgrade screen. Current (bad) gameplay loop: Enter new area that isn't that much different than the previous dozens of areas that you have already been through, after w hich a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of enemies will spawn in, most of whom will have fast moving or homing projectiles so you'll be absolutely barraged by a storm of all different kinds of bullets/rockets/fireballs unless you bounce around like a spastic bunny and have extreme AOE-weapons that will render the screen a shaking light-glared mess for 90% of the fight (often times I don't even know what I'm shooting at, the screen is just a mess of colours and lights). Collect one of the 5+ amounts of coins/orbs/whatever to use in the ?-amount of minigames (I honestly lost the will to count of explore new ones after the third or fourth) which will vary in quality from passable (the pokemon parody) to so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring that they are a pain to play (the space shooter game). The general quality and balance of the game seemed to take a steep dive right after the point where you receive the (in my eyes) pointless grappling hook. What happened here? I wish the game has ended at around the ~10 hour mark, at that point it had delivered the short and sweet retro-FPS action experience that I think the game would be much better suited as. The game does not have the quality needed in level-design and balance to hold up for the very long gameplay that it has. It just starts to feel like a randomly generated slog.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's good, quite good and even more so impressively since it has one dev behind it. HOWEVER it is still rough around the edges. Fun? Well, it certainly is if you like old school FPS games, but as of the moment you should approach it with a bit of caution; it is a somewhat unstable game and needs optimization (Amid evil and Dusk run flawlessly even in their most chaotic moments so a "mostly" sprite-based game shouldn't have issues but it sadly has some). Music can be a bit off given that it pops in when in combat and disappears just after you're done: it's not an issue, per se, but it can be a bit jarring how you go from 0 to 100 and then right back at 100 in seconds, just with silence around. In a game like Dusk it works because the mood and level design goes hand-in-hand, here it kinda doesn't, like that one girl in primary school who you had to hold hands with but you could visibly see her not wanting to.Gunplay feels a bit stiff, but you get the hang of it sooner rather than later, though it certainly still feels a bit off given that you get a big loud sound but the weapons remain mostly still. Even so, it is not bad by any means, might just be me being picky.It is defiently a game to keep an eye on, but I'd advise those who are a bit iffy about it to wait some months until optimization and other improvements come around, but I canno't bring myself to recommend it 100%. Worth checking out, but with caution as of the moment of writing this.

_childDocuments_.review: Time to update this review since I've now pumped a hundred hours into it.My original review when only chapter one was out was : low resolution gory graphics, extremely satisfying gunplay and powerups, smooth controls, random level generation. Pretty much the ideal classic FPS experience, if only it had coop play possibilities.And that is still true, but now the game is also huge and has varied level generation in each of its three chapters. On top of that it has arenas and new game+ modes to make the game harder. If you want to judge this game, I wouldn't do it until you've actually played at least through it once and then you go through new game+. At that point the game is no longer slowly opening up abilities to you, you are already a jacked monster and you can literally fly through levels and cut your way through armies of enemies. That is when the game shines, when you fly through the air like an eagle using your grappling hook, triple jump and air dash abilities and drop mini nukes on hordes of enemies, or shoot them with a 4x times damage machine gun with exploding bullets.Sometimes you'll meet a doctor who can change a specific weapon stat to a random different one, or create a new rare weapon based on a weapon you already have. Those are the moments where you can create insane weapons, always be on the lookout for that dude. Just keep in mind that a negative stat (say: recoil or increase ammo usage) will generally stay a negative stat, so if a stat is not THAT negative... maybe just keep it.You have three upgrade paths in the full version. Skills, the jade tree and the topaz tree, each governed by a different type of mini game. I'll have to be honest, I'm not a fan of the mini games (but you can turn them off!). So far I've pretty much ignored the topaz tree with a pokemon-esque mini game, it is such a slog for me. I'll give it a looksie when I get to new game+ round 2 when I'll probably start to need the upgrades. To make your life easier, I would not ignore the jade tree though (with a pretty naff horizontal shoot em up mini game), which means you'll have to do arena battles to get the currency for it. The upgrades you can get there, especially pets, are well worth it to take some of the grind out of the game. Some extra skills I experience as a hindrance though so maybe see on Youtube what they do first before you get them.Arenas are pretty fun, pitting you against increasingly bigger waves of enemies. My favorite is to do the cemetery with a mini nuke as one of your two carried over weapons. So much carnage.A few gripes I have, besides the repetitive upgrade mini games.1. Turn off automatic weapon switching. I don't know how many times I've been killed because I pickup a weak weapon and automatically switch to it. This should be off by default to be honest.2. Some enemies have attacks so strong they don't knock you back... they knock you around. All of a sudden you'll be facing behind you, or looking all the way up or down. It's quite jarring.3. A few weapon types are pretty pointless. Is there anyone that knows how to use the gravity gun?That's it really. This game is a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: It's been a long time since I wrote this, pretty sure it turns out I was wrong and a lot of what I complained about in this review changed significantly and the developer has/had no intention of abandoning it and probably hasn't stopped looking into ways to make the game more in line with his vision for it. I already acknowledged it would be a pain in the ass to optimize, so props to him for keeping at it. I'll pick it up again some day in all likelihood, but you guys can keep giving me free steam points. I like clowns.I've been looking for as many good and challenging Rogue-lites as I can, and have been loosely following the development of this title for some time now. Conceptually, everything about this game is right up my alley, and I feel that it's definitely a very solidly built game on that level. However, as many are continuing to point out, this game has a significant chance to have impossible to ignore performance issues that render the game at certain points unplayable, even on higher end PCs. This has a serious optimization problem. Still, with how this game is built and processes its math, it might be too late at this point to really go back and patch everything up nice and perfect. Given the timeline of development, I'm inclined to suggest they likely felt this was simply good enough relative to how long it took to put together. If that's really the case, I'd be hard pressed to disagree. Some things really stick out as generally too busted to fully enjoy, like the Arena unlocked after Jade Tree. I actually kinda liked the Gradius minigame beyond the disjointed and time wasting wormhole system, but it should have been reworked or possibly even scrapped because of how it's functionally capped by crashing when the waves inevitably spawn too many enemies that are doing too many things at once. I really wanted to keep going and completely make the arenas my ♥♥♥♥♥, but the game just couldn't handle how hard I was rolling after getting a bee shooter with 72% leech and 75% increased missile size.In terms of its execution, the game really needs more of quite a few things, especially since certain elements like Topaz Tree are an absolute chore that I doubt many people will ever like  pausing their high-speed boomer shooter to play a minimalist Pokemon homage. It's just not fun, and keeping track of which NPCs are where is another total waste of time. The interface itself isn't really that great either, and I set myself back by accidentally releasing the pet I spent 2k topaz on. My mistake, but the fact that you can execute actions with keybinds and mouse controls in all three minigames means those mistakes are probably gonna happen for more people than just myself.Overall, this game shows the developer is full of really cool ideas that are sometimes harder to implement than they might have appeared during the earlier development stages. While the minigames felt clunky, they added tremendously to the overall atmosphere and helped drive home the kind of sincerely broken set of lenses the protagonist has to view and interact with the world. One of my favorite parts of this game was the hospital, and I hope that if something like this is attempted again, that significantly more detail be added to the subtle changes and quirks of the hub world because there was such a particular feeling to seeing the developments and getting access to other places.Ultimately, I think this is a solid 7.5/10 and would be much higher if the endgame wasn't throttled by performance issues and full on crashes, meaning I'll have to call it early on in New Game +. I really can't complain since I received this as a gift and it was half off, but I don't recommend it at its standard price point. While my playtime is 58.3 hours, I probably spent less than half that actually playing the game (bad habit of leaving games running and doing other stuff). The last few hours were repeating the same levels that kept crashing until I gave up.In a nutshell, the game is great in concept and aesthetic execution, but performance issues mean it's not nearly what it could've been and if you haven't bought it already then either buy it on sale or hold out hope for a patch or expansion pack; I'd even be happy with a full sequel if it would just touch up and refine everything offered here. tl;dr: If it's on sale and you're still curious or if you just really like boomer shooters and might be running out of options, I would say yes. Otherwise, no.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper represents a first-person shooter (FPS) game, developed and published by the company Blazing Bit Games.++ It begins with an uncommon claymore, continues with a rare howitzer, and escalates further where wielding a legendary grimoire of infernal origin is no longer a curiosity, but part of a never ending array of randomly generated items with various statistics. An addictive loop and main motivation to keep moving forward.+ A smart upgrade system, hidden behind in-game platformers, allows for sufficient number tweaking to your advantage, including abilities and features from more than 20 years of FPS gaming.+ Andrew Hulshult strikes again! His soundtrack contributes to the fast-paced freak show like a proper adrenaline rush.-  Do yourself a favour and ignore the plot; there is little content anyway. Just make sure to check out the hospital once you kill a boss, in order to unlock the arenas [credit to WorldWarWiesel for pointing it out].Being an insane patient in a mental hospital, while fighting for survival in nightmarish episodes, has never been so entertaining. Experimenting with the sheer endless variety of weapons and their ever-changing modifiers is the main attraction of the game. And to my utmost satisfaction it keeps me royally entertained.Recommended for fetishists of crimson pixels.Estimated time for 100% completion: +100 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 149Multiplayer achievements: none

_childDocuments_.review: Let me say this first because it is really gonna sound like I'm an ungrateful ass who doesn't enjoy whatever I'm given, but I love, LOVE this game! Its an easy 11/10 for me, and  by far one of the most unique and fast paced retro FPS games I've played in a while! The music is awesome! The combat is fun! The weapons are varied and unique, and the enemies are a blast to fight!With that said, this is an Early Access game which means... there are a few little kinks that need to be ironed out before you can call it an "official" release. So, here are a few little things I noticed that kinda bug me about this game:1. Sometimes in the 2D side scroller portions my character doesn't like to listen to inputs. I play mouse and keyboard because that's how an FPS should be played, so I think that the side scrolling controls for K&M controls could use some tweaking.2. Random encounter orbs are a lot of fun when they don't spawn half way across the map locked behind a door that you need to do some complex puzzle to get to! I've died several times because the random encounter orb I needed to break was nowhere to be found, and it honestly felt like the game was saying "that's enough fun. We want you to die because we felt like it." It would be a much less painful experience if these orbs only spawned in areas you have explored (eg, wherever you've opened a door), that way you can enjoy the game and not get screwed over by the RNG machine.3. I honestly feel like I run out of ammo way too much in this game. And this isn't a Doom Eternal situation either because in that game you had a means to get ammo back quickly, but in this game it is really easy to run out of ammo when your knee deep in combat with 50+ enemies, which means you've gotta run around like Benny Hill and find some more before you die and have to start all over again. 4. The ice runners from Chapter 2, dear Lord those things are way too fast! Like, we're talking absurdly fast! And by absurdly fast I mean moving out of the range of your crosshairs at the speed of plaid fast! Tone the speed down just a tad on them and you'll be golden, because the concept of an enemy that can freeze you in place is mwah! Genius!5. This might just be a hardware problem on my end, but sometimes my mouse inputs for firing don't register. Granted I'm using a very cheap, very old wired mouse for this game so I might just need a replacement, but I figured I'd just bring that up just in case it is a problem with the game.Again, I want to stress that I do enjoy this game, and it is definitely worth the $18 price tag. You will not go wrong playing this game that much I can say! If you like rougelikes, if you like retro FPS games, if you like Borderlands, and if you hate Randy Pitchford and wanna jam a Super Shotgun up his rear end, this is the game for you! Its still bumpy, but not enough to ruin the experience.UPDATE: Been playing it some more and after encountering the ice rain random event again and not being able to find the event orb again and dying because of it AGAIN, I have come to the conclusion that this specific random event is broken and/or haunted and either needs to be removed entirely, or be exorcised from this plain of existence.

_childDocuments_.review: A game mostly about excess, where you’re constantly showered with powers, weapons, and bad guys. Problem is, inflation sets in really fast. Points and rewards start to feel meaningless, and after a while you’re just going through the motions -- blasting monsters to find the nearest exit. No stakes. No impactful decisions. No feeling of progression. Randomness is great at creating a sense of variation and facilitating replayability. But too much of it, paradoxically, creates obvious patterns. Nightmare Reaper ends up as a very monotone game that loses a lot of stock fast, that frantically throws confetti and achievements at you in hopes that you’ll stick around.To me, Nightmare Reaper works up to a certain point. The moment-to-moment gameplay is mostly excellent, if you manage to parse what’s going on on-screen among the insane amounts of bits and pieces flying around. But once that novelty wears off though -- and it will, hitting you like a brick wall -- you’re left with something that sacrifices a lot in the name of just gunplay and shiny, meaningless loot.Carefully recommended if you enjoy arcadey shooters and shiny things.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this off Civvie's reccomendation. Really enjoying it so far, the difficulty curve feels a bit scattershot, but I'm sure as I upgrade more it'll even out a bit. Otherwise only 4 hours in and I've noticed solid gunplay, kickin music, awkward platforming and some really nice atmosphere out of something that looks like it could've been rendered on an SNES. Looking forward to the rest of the game!Update:10 hours in- The platforming is awkward and the grapple is awful, no other way to say it. Ultrakill's absolutely destroys it in terms of responsiveness and overall use. Clipping through textures  and inconsistent slingshot physics make it a chore to use at best. The gunplay remains solid, but relies on finding at least 1 weapon that really hooks you to keep using. Melee is laughably balanced in terms of reward/risk ratio and certain arenas are basically death sentences if you hit them as your first stop. I'm still keeping the positive rec because the gameplay loop is still enthralling me, but the platforming and arena RNG are really bringing down the overall experience. I'm a big fan of movement shooters and the movement mechanics here just aren't refined enough compared to Doom: Eternal or Ultrakill to scratch that same itch.Final Update:Beat the game. Final opinion- A flawed engaging boomer shooterGreat-Very engaging core combat loopWeapons have kick and a ton of varietyMost levels are Doom-esque and don't overstay with a few major exceptionsThe handcrafted levels are almost all excellent with the exception being The EmptyGood musicBleh-UI is unintuitive, which is something I shouldn't have to say about a shooter. Upgrades are hidden, missable and generally just not explained in any useful or rational way. Oh you can have a pet sidekick? Glad I figured that one out on map 73/82. Oh and that one time I accidentally sold my weapon, died and had to start the level with 0 weapons. Yeah, that was not a lot of fun.It's easy on certain levels to get lost, even with the map, due to the poor signposting, copy-pasted corridors/rooms and RNG nature of the map creations. It is INCREDIBLY easy to spend 10-20min hunting down a switch you just found a key for in a huge map with nothing to do and lots of backtracking because you can't remember if one dull gray/tan muted room is the same as anotherThe movement isn't as responsive or satisfying as the best movement shooters (Doom Eternal, Ultrakill, Ghostrunner, TF2, etc.)Enemies are stupid as hell and can be cheesed as necessary, which some may not see as a bad thing considering how brutally unfair some of the arenas can spawn in the later game The RNG level creation is a mixed bag, as most procedural generated maps areLow draw distance and random walls to try and stop sequence breaking (which doesn't always work BTW) are very annoying later in the gameHate-Late game arenas enemy spawns can be so bad that they basically act as insta-restartsThe level of late-game flinch is OUT OF CONTROL, it's idiotic that you literally cannot control your character if you ever get stuck on an enemy, corner, etc. and happen to eat certain types of attacks. The red haze also stays way too long.The sheer number of particle effects on screen will blind you and acts as a similar deterrent to living as the aforementioned flinch. This is one of those times where less is more.Unclear visual feedback about where the hurt is coming fromAbsolutely bottom tier hate the player level design by not including any indication of where the last enemy(ies) are on arena maps when they get stuck somewhere or you need to find them for a door to unlock in story mode. Nothing on screen, nothing on the map, just GL HF complete pace killing snorefest the same as the keys, but more annoying because you feel helpless.It's a solid game with a great core wrapped up in some major balance flaws and baffling UI decisions. If any of this sounds like a dealbreaker, watch a vid or two or later stages (recommend the city or boat) and it'll probably give you an idea of if you can live with it. Not quite Dusk Tier, but I enjoyed it enough to beat it and put in 20+ hours. Will I go back for New Game +? Maybe in the future, but not for a good long while.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that version 1.0 has arrived, it's time for a review!Nightmare Reaper is a fast paced, random-generated (!) shooter that feels like a mix of Quake, Painkiller, and whichever games give you random generated weapons. Combat is incredibly fun, there is a gigantic variety of weapons to discover with the possibility for really crazy effect combinations, as well as a lot of different enemy types to defeat.For each save slot, you also have a skill tree where you can buy upgrades with the gold you farm in the levels, which is packed into a nice mario-style platformer (this can be deactivated in the options menu however). There are two more skill tree systems as well - both resembling other classic 90s games - which carry over to all other savegames as well, but I'll leave it to you to discover them.There is now also an arena mode, which is exactly that: You are thrown into an arena and fight off wave after wave of enemies.The game difficulty is extremely variable and depends on three different factors:- How the level is generated- What kind of weapon you find- What sort of enemies are spawnedShould a level prove to be too difficult, you can keep trying until you finally find "that" weapon or the random generation is less demanding.The graphics style of the game is a mix of 90s style pixellated textures and 2D enemies (similar to the Build-Engine used by Blood or Duke Nukem 3D ) as well as modern, extremely demanding graphics effects such as very detailed shadows and lighting. Depending on the graphics settings you choose, you will either need a potato or a nuclear power plant to run this game smoothly.Soundtrack is mostly classic shooter-style heavy metal. Thank you Andrew!If you like oldschool style shooters and are looking for a game with a high replayability factor (no level will ever be exactly the same) then this one is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic boomer shooter / shower-me-in-gobs-of-loot-crazy-asylum-lady-daddy... with one incredibly obnoxious bug.This bug won't become apparent until the late game. I ran into it sporadically in the main campaign but it became OPPRESSIVE at Carnage Way 2 in New Game+.When the screen gets really busy (like say, a city block of crystals that spawn enemies that sometimes also spawn enemies) the engine will DEVOUR your inputs. As in, hitting left click 4 to 5 times to fire once and good luck grappling anywhere because it just won't fire. Movement itself is fine, it's actions like firing or grappling that just seem to disappear into the void. This might be something that's showing up significantly more because I'm using the Black Hole Launcher (because that's a thing) but it showed up enough in the late game of my first run that I don't think it's just that.That's it. Otherwise game is fantastic. I didn't know that I needed a rocket launcher that fired beehives in my life, but now that I have it I don't think I can give it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but very inconsistent experience. Due to random nature of drops, you'll find yourself struggling to do anything in one part of the game, and then you'll spend the rest of it almost effortlessly clearing levels with the same gun until pretty much the end.This game feels like a sandbox. Like a Half-Life 2 mod with a ton of options to chose from, but since none of them are properly explained to you, you'll end up doing whatever sticks with you, which will probably result in a very easy and repetitive gameplay loop. The game is a mess. Fun, enjoyable, but a mess.Come on, in 2020s we can do better than needing a text guide to explain 500 different mechanics in your game. If I were to choose, I would sacrifice 80% of this game's 'features' for some direction. And throw away some randomness, as it has barely contributed anything to my personal experience except for getting me an OP level 2 weapon 2/3 through the game. There's just too much stuff for such simple gameplay loop.As it is now, the game is a sandbox that pretty much relies on you making your own game in your head, and applying restrictions on weapons and perks. Because if you don't do it, you can easily complete it without any of the amazing stuff the dev have put in and not even notice it. You'll just end up doing the same thing for several hours, which is fun if you like it, but could be tedious if you happen to not be such a big fan of the genre.Some environments look spectacular considering the artstyle.If you're reading this comment and thinking about playing the game: you should. You wouldn't be reading this if you were not the kind of person who would enjoy it. I certainly did. Wouldn't replay it though probably.

_childDocuments_.review: The main conflict of this game in the later phases is dropping one of your two absurd weapons to pick up an equally absurd weapon.I have a (admittedly vanilla) launcher that shoots huge metal rails that explode both when they impact something, and after a little while that has a 93% chance to heal me when I shoot it.I have a minigun that stuns enemies 100% of the time with electricity... and it fires bowling balls that still hurt enemies if it the projectile bounces off a wall.I just found a shotgun that uses my blood for ammo, pulls enemies that survive the double-barrel shot closer to me for a follow up shot, has a 32% chance to heal me, and fires pizzas instead of bullets.Nightmare Reaper has the audacity to only let you keep at first one, but now two weapons, forcing me to full-stop and consider the ramifications of swapping one of the first two weapons I described with the third. I am currently processing the benefits of electric bowling balls vs the endorphin release of watching walls repeatedly get splattered with guts and pizzas.If that sounds fun to you - do yourself a favor - get Nightmare Reaper. If the skill progression system gives you a headache, just look at a guide and let RNGesus take the wheel.Blood is fuel,Head is full of nightmares,Double-barrel pizza time!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting twist of an FPS. I was expecting a typical horror boomer shooter, but instead, it became a clinical delve into psychopathy. A slow journey into the mouth of madness, if you will. I didn't know pixels could bring a sense of creeping horror. You start in the psychiatric ward of a hospital, initially confined to your cell. As you sleep & dream, more parts of the hospital are unlocked. Every time you complete a map, a psychiatrist's report unlocks itself. I note with amusement that the narrator sounds like Frank Herbert.The gameplay itself is satisfying, as is the variety of weapons one can wield. Given the nature of NR, you can only carry one weapon forward into the next map. A shame, since it would have been nice to go all crazy on the mobs.NR has its moments, like the minigames in the skill tree & elsewhere which are oddly endearing & adorable. Even a Pokemon-esque minigame to boot. Likewise when you play on the main maps, you'll come across a little dog whom you can feed treats for rewards & which you can pet. A little bundle of pixelated cuteness if there ever was one.The music's alright, but became somewhat repetitive over time. However, as much as I enjoyed NR, I eventually gave up after 35 maps or so since it became somewhat puzzle-like, which I didn't relish. Nonetheless, it's a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, since it has everything I could like. It's an FPS with a retro look, and the weapons have modifiers that can be rolled randomly, leading to interesting combinations. But there are some things that keep me from enjoying the game.One thing that gets brought up often is that you can only bring along one weapon, and specifically only a level 1 weapon. This is enough to limit weapon variety, as you'll probably bring your strongest weapon that'll outshine any random weapon you pick up. The RNG stats can also screw you over if you don't roll a strong weapon that you can bring along with you. You can bring higher-level weapons, but that doesn't happen until much later and when you have enough money.The cartridge minigames are also a common pain point, but thankfully there's an option to disable them. The first cartridge was fun since I personally enjoy platformers, but the Pokemon cartridge is possibly the worst grind I've seen. The topaz rate per battle is atrocious, and the battles lack the substance that the platformer's levels had.Another issue is that I started getting headaches and nausea from playing this game specifically. There's a lot going on to the point where it hurts to look at. The textures are sharp and contrast a lot, which is made worse by the next point.My biggest issue is that trying to 100% a level is absolutely awful. More than half my time was spent looking for one piece of loot, or one enemy, backtracking through levels several times just to find the loot under water, or hiding under decorations. I had a situation where treasure was on a platform that was too high to jump to, but also couldn't be reached from other platforms as the ceiling was too low. I cheated by jumping off a barrel, which is unintentional since you slide off when you're on a barrel. You can often use the treasure counter to infer whether a secret room exists, but it gets repetitive looking for the same telltale crack in a wall. The forest levels are also dreadful when looking for secrets, as the tree wall texture is mainly the same color as the crack, which didn't help my headaches.I think this game would have been better without the treasures, secrets, and minigames. The game is definitely enjoyable if you speed through the level and kill enemies, but having to pick up all of the loot and check each individual wall for secrets slows the gameplay down from what it wants to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the full release is nearing, I'm going to give my Early Access review and then update it in post (05.03.2022)EARLY ACESS REVIEWGAMEPLAYNR is played in two different parts. First is the main part, which are the Nightmares. - It is first-person-shooter action in its finest. Hip-fire, aiming down sights, full 360 degree viewing and plenty of verticality instead of flat ground- Each level is randomly generated, using pre-set rooms to construct the map- Monsters and Loot are strewn about, hidden in chests, destructible and secret walls- The game has a healthy amount of weapons to choose from: Pistols, Assault Rifles, Shotguns, Rocket Launchers, Axes, Swords, Sniper Rifles, Revolvers, Magic Books that cast spells and Staffs of various elements. Each weapon itself has also different stats that makes them better than the previous one, allowing you to pick up more and more powerful weapons as you advance through the levels- The game does have a Perk System which can be used to improve your character. The majority are stat increases (More Health, Hold more Ammo, etc) but there are some that grant new abilities to navigate the levels with, especially during the later sections as the maps get bigger and biggerThe second is the Asylum part.- In between Nightmares, you can explore the Asylum which acts as a sort of break area, where you can discover more lore about the Patient and the asylum- After Episode 1, Map exploration turns into a mini hub that allows you to choose which level you want to visit next. Each area has its own theme with different enemies and bossesSTORYYou control the Patient, a young woman that has been sent to an asylum due to their aggression and violent tendencies. As you progress the story, you'll learn more about the Patient through notes left by an unidentified doctor who is monitoring her, as well as discover the secrets that lurk in the asylum.ARTIt's high res pixel art in all its glory. The world and character are well detailed, the lighting effects element affects help it pop and the blood splatter and destructible just amplify the feeling of carnage. The music is, of course amazing and the sound design for the weapons are grand.FINAL NOTESIf you enjoy FPS with an element of randomly generated goodness, then this is the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I came back here and looked at this game again, just cause something was nagging at me after I went through it twice, and did several things multiple times, and even eventually almost got to NG+2.The main reason to come here would be for the sheer slaughter and fun of some of the weapon craziness that can arise from the affixes on rare+es- that's why Jade Tree and Arena are really fun to do, btw.The main hanging point here, though, is that the roguelike aspect isn't really there aside from buying meta-progression and retrying levels, which does actually fit the lore. If anything, this game is what would happen if you made Borderlands have a set amount of droppable weapons/types, gave them a limited 4 rarities, and a cupfull of possible affixes, then made it a Doom-like linear shooter with randomized tiles and randomized enemy/secret spawns, then added annoying, extended switch hunts in the entire last third of the game (the second third has the normal 1 or 2 switch hunts, but later levels have you getting every key, doing every power-socket after you feed the barnacle a crystal, with all those being randomly placed in the levels...), topping it off with (spoiler, skip to next paragraph if you want to avoid it) a mental-world reveal that, admittedly does actually make the title of the game relevant and isn't a stretch- you are literally playing the Reaper of the Nightmares of the character in the story, which, is good.There are two endings, but, they don't currently matter, and going past that point is literally just looping through the campaign over and over again for fun or for achivements, becuase you need to get to NG+3 if you want to 100% the achievements.A future update will have modding, that is confirmed to happen, and when it does, I'm sure some great mods are gonna come in and shake things up, but until then...

_childDocuments_.review: It has a lot of good ideas but it's not done well enough. It's an FPS like DOOM at it's core. You get RNG weapons and earn different currencies to upgrade various things like hold more weapons, pick up more ammo, etc. The problem is the 'escalation. Levels come in 'chapters', the "creepy village" or the "dark forest", right now I'm in the 'Sulfuric Mines". Each chapter escalates the challenge, harder secrets, more power enemies, etc. HOWEVER, what doesn't escalate? You're weapons. For all the 'RNG' goodness the game touts, I found a weapon very early on and have held onto it since then, because it was randomly awesome, at the TIME. Now in the sulfuric mines, I'm completely out gunned. I'm fighting hordes of enemies that just won't die. The items they drop are still worse than what I've got though. It's insanely frustrating. For all the praise this is getting in reviews, I guess my computer is incorrectly running the weapon generator or something, because the weapons mostly suck, you are always out gunned and levels require multiple playthroughs to grind through. At one point, I realized I wasn't playing this game, I was working. I was working my way through level after level in some weird sense of 'needing' to progress. Why? I wasn't having fun anymore, the 'new' items sucked, every set of levels looks the same, the game has about 30 textures from what I can tell. It just became a painful slog of 'completionism'. So, I say goodbye. I'm uninstalling this and likely won't ever reinstall, there are too many good shooters to force myself to complete this one. I'm sure plenty of people like this, and for the first few hours I loved it. But as I got deeper into the levels I realized the gameworld was escalating and leaving me behind, that's just not fun for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is already a great shooter with some old school influences and well worth the price in early access. The core combat is very good, and each procedurally generated level is a nice length making it easy to jump in and out without having to commit hours of your time. Compared to modern titles which you are forced to wade through pages of menus, scripted sequences and cutscenes its a breath of fresh air.GOOD - Weapons, Combat and ThemeEvery weapon I used in this game feels fantastic. The particle effects and feedback are great and you can tell alot of effort has gone into this aspect.There is also a nice range of weapon types to vary up the play style as you progress through the levels. The game also doesn't waste your time with forced exposition, but manages to have a strong theme and meta narrative by tying these directly into its gameplay and features for which it should be commended.BAD - Chapter 1 PlatformingChapter 1 has some honestly awful platforming with insanely narrow floating platforms.A large amount of it is optional, but it is simply so annoying and poor compared to the combat it detracts from the whole experience.Nitpicks - Movement ability order/restrictionsHaving the additional movement abilities simply makes the game more fun to play and I wish they could be unlocked faster.I felt the double jump should atleast be unlocked before the dash move.Most the levels in Chapter 1 are small and confined areas where a double jump/ledge grab is useful but a dash feels rather out of place as there is little room to maneuver horizontally.

_childDocuments_.review: Best boomer shooter I've ever played. Probably the most hours you can get out a single boomer shooter as well.Only major issues I have with it is performance is much worse than I feel it should be considering the map size and graphical fidelity and enemies that knock your crosshair around when they hit you is extremely annoying. Level design ends up suffering throughout the game despite the variety so the first chapter is a lot stronger than the second and third.My suggestion of improvements outside of that is to make the map show where the items you have to carry to points on the map (like the fuse etc).

_childDocuments_.review: Some people might write this off as Yet Another Early Access Boomer Shooter but it's actually a very well made looter shooter. Nightmare Reaper is really close to a pixel art Borderlands inside bite-sized dungeons, if that makes any sense. I was initially turned off by the pixel art but overall its well done; most modern pixel art games are poor quality art or too chunky but this works because everything is made with pixels, including explosions and environmental effects. The weapons scale really nicely, slowly ramping up from simple pistols and pump shotguns to room-clearing full auto explosive ammo life stealing miniguns. With over 80 weapon types, 80+ levels, an endless arena, and NG+, there's an insane about of variety of toys to play with. There's also over a dozen tilesets ranging from caverns, to cities, to outer space and other surreal landscapes so even though its a bit claustrophobic at the beginning, it really opens up after a few zones.An astounding amount of work went into this and it really shows. I was really impressed with the Early Access previews and it only has gotten better since release. Its honestly hard to find anything bad to say about NR; there were some balancing issues and performance bugs at 1.0 launch but the devs have been hard at work with post-launch patches. Nightmare Reaper is my favorite game this year so far and will probably end up being my GOTY for 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper makes up for its ho-hum busy graphics and simplistic map design with the rule of cool. A looter shooter with a truly extensive roulette of crazy weapons, Nightmare Reaper is the kind of game that immediately appeals to the power leveling just-one-more-run center of the brain. The weapons list is as extensive as the skill tree in three different currencies with the usual assortment of assault rifles to orbital cannons modified by an awesome and often humorous allotment of modifiers. Don't turn your nose up to a minigun that fires toilet paper rounds as it's just as interesting as a damned book that fires enemy seeking soul-skulls.Reaper's kitchen sink approach to game design is messy and muddy with some levels stitched together in frustrating ways that results in doors being blocked by environmental hazards that hand crafted testing could've accounted for but what it does it does exceptionally well. At 20+ hours for just a single run, not counting new game+ that has a lot left unlocked in the first run, this is a game that respects your time whether you want to dive deep or just play a level every once in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat my first playthrough of this game and I gotta say this is up there for me. I love boomer shooters and always have, starting with Shadow Warrior on my old laptop.
