_childDocuments_.review: If you want the short version, read the bottom, concluding paragraph. I recommend you read the full review for the full detail. This game has a lot going for it!-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I've waited until the game's full release to write this. As of today I have 179 hours in this, and I've beaten the game 4 times. I think I can write this review pretty confidently lol.I bought this game after seeing Civvie's 2 videos on it. It looked like so much fun I had to try it...before I knew it, it was 2am and I had no intention of stopping. Even now, it remains just as enjoyably addictive. This is just as well, because the game goes on forever. Literally, forever. With the Chapter 3 update, New Game + was implemented, and you can play this game with progressively stronger weapons and enemies for as long as you want. Even if you don't decide to play NG+, you've still got at least 50 hours of levels and bossfights- that's about how long it took me to finish the game for the first time.But what about the details, Mantha, the DETAILS?! Very well: 3 game-modes, 3 minigames, 3 chapters, featuring 80+ levels, with 80+ weapons, and 50 enemies, officially-speaking. Technically, there are 25x as many levels, if you count all their variations (each level has a set of variations you can encounter. If you die and retry a level, the layout will be different), and for the weapons, there's...technically, there's like 1000+. All the different combinations of modifiers (including my favorite, "Random projectile") make for very, VERY different weapons. For instance, on one of my saves, I have a shotgun that shoots explosive fireballs. Another shotgun I have uses explosive pellets that deal shock damage. Yet another shotgun I had is able to shoot on automatic, has 3 extra shells, and does ice damage, which can freeze enemies solid. So in reality, the amount of different weapons in Nightmare Reaper is innumerable. As you can probably tell, this aspect of the game is my favorite. I I love collecting new, wild, powerful weapons in games, especially when each one feels and sounds satisfying, as they do in Nightmare Reaper.Speaking of sounds, have you *heard* the soundtrack for this game? Listen to the trailers, watch someone stream the game. The music is fantastic and matches the mood of the dream-based slaughterfest...oh would you look at that, it's by Andrew Hulshult. That explains it. As for other, non-musical sounds, the weapons all sound gorgeous (the sawed-off's alt-fire is how every shotgun should sound), to the point that sometimes I start using a weapon not because it has particularly strong modifiers, but because dammit, I really love the way it sounds. You will also enjoy the sounds of the enemies, who each have various idle sounds, alert sounds, pain sounds, and death sounds, all of which make the killing even more satisfying.How about the graphics? Every game's gotta have shmexy graffix, right? Nightmare Reaper does not disappoint. Its pixel-heavy retro style may put off the zoomers who have no appreciation for art, but for those who understand the uniqueness of old-school sprites and textures, this game delivers. Modern lighting and shading techniques coupled with lovingly-made textures give each level its own particular atmosphere that you simply have to play to fully feel. ...Okay, this section of the review sounds like a snobby game journalist wrote it, but I stand by my words! It looks great. One of my favorite things to do is to sneak up on enemies and just study the way they look. Gaunt, the man responsible for the enemy designs, made some eerily, disgustingly-beautiful creatures.What about the story? What is all this dream stuff about? Why are you in a mental asylum? Who are you? Da ♥♥♥ is going on? If you've read my reviews before you know I abhor spoiling a story, so don't expect any. You play as an unnamed young woman who has lived a...rough life...and has developed some serious mental scarring that's left her with a struggling grip on reality. She experiences vivid nightmares, in which the player can find small clues and hints as to her past, and how she got to this place in her life. During her waking hours, she is left notes by her doctor, which serve to explain the story in more concrete terms. Ultimately, the battle for sanity is fought in her dreams.Lastly, I want to talk about the smaller, less fundamental things. The game has lots of settings, so you can customize graphics, UI, controls, and even gameplay to a fair extent. The minigames act like skill trees, helping you become more powerful and gain new abilities, so they aren't just bland bonus features. There is also an arena mode, where you can take the outrageous weapons you find in the proper levels and test your might against endless waves, while also earning currency to spend in one of the minigame skill trees. There are also secrets to find in the nightmare levels, most containing various references, and upon clearing out a large room of enemies, special "events" can occur...some good, some not so good. The game keeps you on your toes! And finally, perhaps the best aspect of this game, its community. The Nightmare Reaper community, specifically the Discord server, is a joy to hang out in and be a part of. It's especially fun talking to the developers...even if the lead dev has some questionable hot takes on movies here and there...and seeing people post clips and images from their experiences in the game. To conclude this lengthy lad of a review...Nightmare Reaper is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome and anyone who enjoys the FPS genre should try it. Seriously, it's that much fun that I can confidently give a broad and sweeping recommendation like that. If you enjoy running around, playing with fun weapons, jumping, shooting, and fighting monsters, you will very likely enjoy this game, especially as the levels grow larger and more complex. It's fun to play, it's full of good music and satisfying sounds, it's got lots of those "little touches" that make it all the more enjoyable, and the community surrounding the game is a big ol' family of videogame nerds. What's not to like? :DTo ItBurn: Congrats on finally finishing your passion project. I hope you take a well-earned rest after this. I wish you the best of luck in future endeavors, and if you ever need a beta tester for them, I'd sign up again in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks ugly, but I honestly think this is the best action rogue-lite yet. The main factor, beyond the moment-to-moment gameplay (which is great), is that the developer had a really good grasp on when, and when not, to incorporate randomness and RPG mechanics. There are no random upgrades and the guns you use aren't randomly generated either. Unlike other games, say borderlands, this game has a massive arsenal of handcrafted, specifically-designed weapons that can roll with positive and negative affixes. This means that you'll never be completely stuck with busted, unsatisfying guns due to RNG.Likewise, you deterministically grow your character via skill trees contained in 3 completely unique minigames that you can play anywhere at anytime (a Mario-style platformer, a pokemon-style RPG, and a Gradius-style shooter.)

_childDocuments_.review: Great value for money. I was not expecting to get 36 hours of gameplay on my first run.Pros: - An amazing labour of love with an incredible amount of detail in the environments, enemies, weapons and skill trees.-Fun and responsive weapons to fit any way you want to fight your way through hoards of enemies- Very effective mechanic of having to pick only 1 weapon to carry over per round. Creates a good sense of familiarity while offering you almost always something new with a flurry of weapons each round with a ton of different modifiers- The game is challenging but never too much to handle. -  An amazing modernisation of the classic 2.5D arcade shooter- Quick to jump in and out of a game after a hard day's work Mehs:- The story is not that compelling but clearly designed to be as unobtrusive as possible, and informs the level design and enemies enough to keep things fresh- Music is great, but does get a little repetitive after a while until you reach a new area. - The procedural level design does a good job of making things different enough every time, but does sometimes feel like it lacks variety in how you can traverse it, and does make some fight very awkwardCons: - Finding treasures and secrets can sometimes have you running round empty levels for quite a while and does deflate the pacing of the game overall. Finding them all is obviously only a bonus, but unlocking skills  in the skill tree is very useful in keeping your strength balanced enough as you progress through the game, and they quickly get expensive.- The mini games in the skill trees are a fun nod to retro games, but get stale and time consuming quickly. Thankfully these can be deactivated in the settings- Accessing New Game + once you have beaten the final boss is a little complicated and I had to look up a guide on how to do this.  Overall highly recommend this game if like me you are enjoying the flurry of retro looter shooters we are going through these past couple of years

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper.. oh boy is this game a joyride. This experience is a 1968 Camaro SS suped up with modern engineering. This game gives me hope that the FPS genre, and especially the looter shooter subgenre are not going stale. I have put so many hours into this game already its unbelievable. It does almost everything right, there are a few problem areas that need addressing imo, but these aspects that aren't so enjoyable are not part of the CORE gameplay loop and thus, are minor issues and nitpicks or really just elements that just don't appeal to me. I will break down this game into bits and discuss my opinion and any criticism I have.Gameplay: The single most key aspect of an FPS is the shooting and the feedback the player receives. This element alone is masterclass in Nightmare Reaper because of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun it is to kill these demons. This game achieves something most high budget FPS studios dream of doing. Turning a simple concept such as shooting an enemy and building upon that foundation. Nightmare Reaper does everything in its power to encourage you to play aggressive(or defensive if that is your playstyle), play fast, and shoot straight. But how is this any different from COD, Apex Legends, or Halo? The key is the vast array of enemy types, different platforming elements(floor is lava in some cases), different weapons, power-ups, rarities of weapons that WILL change your playstyle, character mobility(more on that later), environmental dangers such as explosive barrels(which will kill you a lot). Each time you sleep your game world will change, not completely mind you, but enough variations to the handmade levels to where it will always keep things interesting no matter the hours logged. Trust me on that. It even features "mini games" that hearken back to the all time greats such as Mario and Zelda. You play these games to unlock more treasure value, get bigger ammo pickups, more max health, or +1 dash, etc.So rarely have I seen all the above come together so well, AND with such archaic graphical design, simple controls, and yet quite unconventional premise for this genre. It really stands out from the rest.Story: Without spoilers I will tell you this game explores psychiatric health in a very unconventional way. It seems purposefully disconnected and ambiguous because psychos, schizophrenics, sociopaths all are disconnected and all are very difficult to understand. I have not finished this game so my final verdict on this subject is inconclusive. But the story does seem very cliche at times and very low budget, but is serviceable in that it progresses the game in a non-combative sense. It serves it's purpose to progress the game and love it or hate it it will not disturb your time within Nightmare Reaper. This game was never made with the intention of the story taking center stage and it shows. Graphics: This is where my modern engineering in a '68 Camaro comes in. This game is callback to the 90's classics that still to this day define gaming and gamer culture. Dynamics Shadows, Resolution Scale, View Distance.. The adored pixelated graphics of yesteryear get a major facelift with higher resolutions and the water, lava, acid textures look incredible. Best way I can describe it? Imagine running those crazy demanding texture packs for minecraft for lolz right? Here you can without a NASA computer and you can change color filters to have some added effect and flavor to your game. Try Clown Vomit in Sewers.. thank me later!Audio: Have you *HEARD* this game's soundtrack? It's free on youtube so give it a listen. In my opinion this goes much much harder than the DOOM ost could ever hope because its cohesive, it flows, it doesn't just give you tinnitus because muh gore. Andrew Hulshult is a highly respected artist. Mick Gordon did good. But Hulshult is my choice. This is songwriting, this is metal. The Shadow only mocks it cannot make. Enemies sound like demons of course but with that nice added touch of it being DOOM-esque. Everything is not blended together so you can make out your double barrel getting ripped in the face of those summoned skelly boys. It all comes crashing down when you clear the arena and that soft, longing drone ambience takes hold as you loot and collect all your precious coinsConclusion: This game is completely worth the price. you will get your 1 hour for $1(my philosophy when buying games) and many more. As I understand it Nightmare Reaper is still having content added in the future even when it just left Early Access. Do yourself a favor, skip having a night out with your old lady and buy this game, get yourself a beer or 5 from the fridge and have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast because this game is one of a kind and one HELL of a ride!!

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off strong, but quickly degrades into a mindless grind. You might have seen the screenshots and thought them very pretty, but all that fancy lighting and all those effects don't make for good gameplay -- the explosions and debris and piles of coins flying out of enemies become one huge indistinguishable mess. At that point, you can't see the enemy projectiles -- nor are you expected to. Once you get enough upgrades and a health-leech weapon with a high enough firing rate, the gameplay becomes «point at the huge mess of pixels, hold left mouse button and wait for the hit indicator to stop appearing». Even when you can dodge a projectile, you have no reason to bother to, since health is so plentiful. Yet another example of meta-progression making for horrible difficulty balance.This game could have been a nicer -- and cheaper -- timewaster, but it has so many unnecessary elements that don't add anything at all to the experience. There are boring minigames that even the game itself half-admits shouldn't be there, since there is an option to disable them entirely; there is some excuse of a story, delivered through one line at a time every time you beat a level, which never leads to anything interesting or consequential. And half the time, instead of shooting at enemies, you'll be wandering around the map trying to find the one small key item you need to unlock a door to progress, completely killing the flow of the game. It had potential, but tried too hard and became a pile of tedium. What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game that quickly devolves into repetitiveness and boredom. It looks like the game was artificially extended out to meet a playtime target.- The level design gets very repetitive very quickly; for example I've opened a level only to start out in the exact same dock area with a ship in or a city block with a skyscraper in the middle and a bus stop on top of some stairs like 20+ times, and I've noticed very similar map layouts in several levels I've played through. The scenery would be different, but the physical layout would be pretty much the same. It seems like the "pool" that levels draw from to generate is very small. That should either be expanded for more unique levels or the amount of levels you play through should be cut down by 2/3.- The skill trees are fun, I really do love the concept that each skill tree is a little mini game that you play through. The first one is a Super Mario Bros 3 spoof, the second one is a Pokemon spoof, and I am not familiar with the 3rd one. It seems kinda like a Star Fox spoof. Other than the Super Mario spoof tree, the skill trees get very grindy very quickly with the 3rd skill tree (The jade tree) being the worst. You unlock it when you unlock an arena battle system and playing through the arenas at first it seems like you can get through it pretty normally, but when you replay any arena the coins you get after each round drop from roughly 10,000 to 3000, and very quickly in the jade tree you start seeing upgrades to progress through the tree priced at 45,000 coins. Again it really seems like this was made to artificially extend playtime.- The keep system. This is a roguelike, so as per usual you start over after every run whether you beat the level or you die. The thing is most roguelikes have a "keep" system where you can hold over some things from previous runs, and this game's system is harsh. You basically only get to keep one weapon, period, that's it!- The weapons get repetitive very quickly. It seems like there's not actually that many stats that can be rolled when a weapon drops. It's just faster reloads, bigger missiles, splash damage, etc. There is not much variety in weapons themselves either, but there is at the same time. Here's how it goes, most of the time you're only going to get a shotgun, a rocket launcher, a chainsaw, sometimes a railgun, and very rarely anything else. The thing is, that "anything else" has some very cool weapons! There's a freaking black hole launcher! There's also a plasma sword that's basically just an automatic sword that deals massive damage to enemies. There's a whole ass side of a ship that you fire 3 cannons out of! There's even an orbital laser cannon@ The problem? I've only seen these weapons once! It seems the drop rates of these weapons are so low (even when the rarity of the weapon itself is common) that you will almost never see them. As mentioned before you only ever really see your basic shotguns, machine guns, rifles, etc etc. That M1 Garand ping you get on the "semi-automatic rifle" is ever so satisfying though, plus you can melee with that rifle. - The bosses. You seem to have a random chance of "Ok so this next level is going to have a boss until you beat it" and honestly the bosses are kinda boring. It's usually just a beefed up enemy you see on the normal level. Sure it's fun and provides extra challenge, but I'd like to see unique bosses that you will have to die to at least once to develop a strat to beat them; instead of "Oh I've seen this enemy before." I feel like this could add playtime to the game without it being repetitive. - The story is interesting and is primarily what compelled me to keep playing the game. I think it's neat how things change up in the real world as you play through the nightmare levels, but again things happen so slowly it feels like this was yet again another way to artificially extend playtime. You only get a 1 new page in the doctor's notes per level beaten, and events in the real world happen maybe once every 10-15 levels.Overall, I think this game is borderline. It has so much potential and again it is fun as hell to play, but it seems like the devs wanted to artificially extend playtime in the most annoying way possible. Right now it is just over the threshold where I don't recommend it, but if these issues can get resolved and refined I will happily change up my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice FPS that many "reviewers" mistakenly label as "roguelike", when it's as much of a roguelike as Shadow Warrior 2. And I never heard about people calling SW2 that.If you want quick comparison, it's Shadow Warrior 2 minus Borderlands feel, blended with almost everything that is great about classic FPS games. Level are mostly based around arenas, to pepper things up there are skills you unlock with currency for each tree.Game pacing, though, is far from modern shooters like SW2 and it's more on par with Doom Eternal or any other build engine game. It's solid in terms of main gameplay, but where it somewhat lacks is level design. While Episodes 1 and 2 are for the most part fun, half of episode 3 is recycled garbage with floating islands - those suck hard. They are really disappointing in comparison to other levels, especially with its recycling, but also simply boring design, making me want to shut the game off and slap negative review. It's that boring and bad in those parts, because searching for secrets is beyond annoying and everything feels random, like 90s shooter garbage floating in space.The Good:- great gameplay that nails everything that makes FPS great (for the most part)- awesome weapons, some being recycled and not that interesting to use, but with their own personality- crazy combinations of weapon stat that ARE meaningful (unlike in SW2)- for the most part, guns sound excellent- best Andrew Hulshult work to date! OST is simply excellent- skill tree is basic, but ok 2D platformer for the most part, with some frustrations taking you back to TMNT sewer level jumps- most of the levels are fun, even if basic in design- packed with content - you're looking at at least 25h of gameplay for your first playthrough, more if you want to unlock everything (and there is NG+ and more)- well balanced with reasonable difficulty curve (with some small and cheap spikes)- graphics, while simple, they get the job done and it will grow on you, even if sometimes it can get messy and you won't know what you're looking atThe Meh:- topaz is RNG mediocrity that removes every shred of strategy Pokemon had- jade is incredibly basic space shooter, more on the level of StarCraft 2 mini-game, but a lot less than Gradius, R-Type or Gun Nac. It's getting repetitive pretty quickly, even with stages being, thankfully, rather short- changing stats on the gun is rather pointless, you're better off searching for other gun with stats you wantThe Bad:- garbage chapters that feel like they are half of the episode (Crushing depths, Sorcerer's Mantion, The Empty) with heavy recycling between those levels, making them look the same- guns from reflection power up sound terrible, way too loud, to the point it causes distortion- even though game graphically looks passable and game doesn't do anything impressive, performance in some instances can be terrible and even on minimal settings, it can tank framerate hard like it's doing real time ray tracing (rarely, sometimes it requires specific weapon to do that)Overall, great and fun game if you're into old school FPS games. Little unpolished, at final act can bore you out of your mind, but it makes come back for 2-3 final chapters and game itself makes you come back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing it for 5.6 hours, I think I can pretty confidently give my opinion since this game is really repetitive and I don't think that it will change much in the remaining time.Nightmare reaper is an alright game. It is fun. Not excessively so, but it is quite decent at that.I think the biggest problem with this game is its focus on quantity instead of quality; It has a lot of weapons, but most of which feel pretty meh to use, with them also having a big range of random modifiers based on the weapon's "quality", and the levels are procedurally generated, which I think is the worse of these aspects, since despite being each time something different, they feel like each time the same. This description may lead some to believe this is a rouge-like, and that is not really the case. The game do is divided by levels (or at least I think so, since it is very hard to distinguish each level), with each one being harder than the previous one, but always randomly generated. You need to complete each level without dying, and you can only keep one weapon at the end of each level, meaning you will have to loot in each level. There do is a permanent upgrading system though, which also features platforming mini-games which feel really awful to play. And that's all the game (I think, since I didn't beat it). Going trough unmemorable and random levels, killing stuff and looting weapons. I wanted to at least finish the game, but aparently it is about 20 hours and I have already passed more than 5 doing the same thing over and over again. So no thanks. Really a shame because I think that the concept of the nightmares and stuff could be great to ambient a game and if this had a more lineal and quality before quantity approach I think it could have been a really cool game.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper has fallen down the pit of "Boomer Shooter" comparisons and I personally don't think that's very fair. Visually the game reeks of classic pre-quake shooters from the Build Engine era; however, the gameplay is a little bit closer to what you might find if you were to slap a level by level roguelike directly in the middle of a fusion of Half Life with the weapon sandbox of Borderlands. The game is fantastic. It is bleedingly, ridiculously difficult and the moment to moment to moment decisions are not the only ones that can impact your playthrough. Choosing to hold on to certain weapons for a long time vs using the newer shinier one you just found. Getting wacky zany equipment such a knife that lets you fly, or a sticky grenade that deals incendiary damage but also allows you rocket jump. Homing Missiles, Trip Mines, Katana, Rifles, Pistols, A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 50 BMG. It is endless and the effects are nearly endless. The problem of course comes that rolls on guns can be uniquely terrible, more than any other game I have played. I once got a gun that dealt negative damage and I'm still not sure if that was glitch! Overall great game though wait for a sale because it is certainly not the kind of game that you can just apply forehead to enemy for 8 hours or more in a single sitting and some people probably will buy it and just forget its there after awhile because of how frustrating it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is basically the official-unofficial blueprint for the new POSTAL boomer shooter sequel, Brain Damaged. I was hooked on Nightmare Reaper during its Early Access launch and couldn't put it down, so much so that when I suffered a loss of FiOS service for three months, Reaper was pretty much the only thing I played in offline mode whenever I had an itch to scratch. The combat is mellifluous and impactful(weapons and spells have 'weight'/'feel') , the aesthetic is inspired and will deeply satisfy any 80s/90s baby's gamer nostalgia withdrawals(especially if you were there for the transition from 5" floppy disk games to floppy\cdrom gaming on your Windows\pentium 133 rig), and the loop is surprisingly varied and vast in length and biomes traversed. There's a lot of meat on these bones for the price, and as far as boomers go its definitely one of the best offerings for the genre on steam store. If you're looking for an.immersive short, nightmare reaper most likely isn't the narrative driven experience you're looking for. It has a story with plenty of lore, but there's very little-to-no hand-holding or direction in regards to traversing the plotline. Unfolding the story is.almost entirely dependent upon you exploring and choosing to interact with various in game objs. You're not required to flesh the story out by any means, so if you're just looking for that frenetic boomer plat former shooter roguelite kind of experience then you will find everything you're looking for and then some--the story is something like a well thought out garnish that dresses a bountiful entree of blood bullets and gibbing bodies. 10/10 A+

_childDocuments_.review: This game's REALLY fun for the first couple of hours then it falls off hard. Not worth $25, the only reason I have 34 hours played is because of achievement hunting and the hope that the game would eventually get better. Lots of complaints ahead, so here are the bullet points:-The rogue-like aspects are cool but not implemented well enough to really shine through. -The levels are incredibly repetitive, you essentially need to go through each map 3 times to progress to the next one. Has lots of fluff to make the game WAY longer than it should be, I got bored before I finished my first playthrough.-Game turns into a scavenger hunt the further into it you go, eventually you spend more time fetching and delivering items to progress than you do shooting.-Monster variety is lacking compared to the number of stages in the game, elite and boss monsters are just regular monsters with more hp and an extra ability. Only one unique boss in the entire game.-Barely qualifies as a looter, all you can pick up and keep are guns and the mod pool is pretty limited. Can't reliably modify your guns to your liking, some of the guns are cool though.-Arena/survival mode almost saves the game but some stages feel clunky due to how certain monsters are spawned.I had a lot of fun with this game for the first couple of hours but there's just no longevity/replayability to it. Each area has 3 parts, which most of the time means you're just playing the same level with the same basic layout/appearance 3 times in a row with slight changes. It feels like the developer probably originally did this to stretch out content during early access before the entire campaign was finished then forgot to remove the fluff. This leads to the campaign feeling incredibly repetitive, by the time I had made it to the last act of the game I was just rushing to the exit every level without trying to find secrets or get completion bonuses because I was bored out of my mind. To make things worse enemy variety is really slim, throughout the entire game there are MAYBE 20 different types of monsters to fight. Sometimes elite monsters will spawn that are just the same as regular monsters but with 10x or so their normal HP and one additional effect (frost/shock/burn/exploding/armored.) Armored elite mobs will make you pull your hair out because they're just gigantic bullet sponges, unlike in most games there doesn't really seem to be a trick to dealing with armored elites they just take a really really really long time to kill, even when using elemental weapons. Bosses are uninspired because they're literally just regular mobs with a boss's HP bar that summons adds. The way the skill tree(s) are implemented is interesting, there are 3 different skill trees with different classic video game inspired mini-games to go along with them. Unfortunately these mini-games are all very basic and don't evolve or get more interesting as you progress. The mini-game you were doing on stage 3 is exactly as in-depth/difficult as it is on stage 40. Luckily the developer added the ability to disable the mini-games completely so the skill trees just function as regular skill trees without wasting time. You don't really miss out on anything by doing this except for a tiny bit of extra currency that you would've gotten by doing the mini-games. Some of the unlockables from the skill trees are fun, they range from new skills and stat increases to having a pet helper that helps you during levels.The looter aspect of the game is limited just to picking up weapons with varying stats and rarities, this is fun at first but due to the limited amount of available stats to roll it gets boring pretty quick. Some of the weapons are really fun to use and visually interesting, but unless you get lucky on dropping a high level weapon that's also a high rarity AND has good stats, you're probably not going to use them very long. There isn't a reliable way to craft a gun exactly the way you want it, so it never feels like there's real weapon progression, you're just dropping your old gun for a new one that has a slightly better combination of mods. There's an NPC that has a chance of spawning during levels from random events that can offer you the option to reroll a mod on your gun or make a higher rarity copy of a gun you own. The downside is he can do a few different things, so you're not guaranteed a chance at the upgrade option if you do see him and it's fairly rare that he spawns in the first place even if you use every unlockable option to upgrade your chances of finding him. The story is about as uninspired as the rest of the game and is told through pages you find in your room when you wake up after completing a level. Considering the genre I wouldn't usually bother mentioning the story since that's one of the last things I personally look for in a shooter, but it's so par for the course on being bland and boring I wanted to bring it up.The ONE thing I really enjoyed about this game is the arena/survival mode that you unlock a little bit into the campaign. It feels pretty well done and doesn't have many pauses or distractions, so it's the one time during the entire game you feel like you're actually playing an action shooter. Sometimes enemy AI makes certain arena stages more annoying than others as certain creature types start burrowed and will only pop out if you get close to them, meaning you can be stuck on 1 monster remaining for the wave and you'll have to make a lap of the entire stage to flush it out. Luckily those enemies don't spawn on every arena stage so you can just avoid the ones that have them if you get annoyed by doing scavenger hunts.Speaking of, this game really goes out of it's way to turn your shooter experience into a scavenger hunt and it does it often. The further you get through the game, more things get added that you're required to find and put together to progress. Having to put a battery into a switch to power and open a door isn't that bad on its own, but more often than not the door and battery are on complete opposite ends of the map which has you backtracking through a mostly empty map searching for the battery, the lever to put it in, and then the door it opened which somehow can also be nowhere near the lever that activates it. Once you get to act 3 this happens once nearly every stage and sometimes you have to hunt for two items/receptacles to get to the end of the level. The whole process feels like a slog and turns an otherwise fun shooter experience into an easter egg hunt.All in all this isn't a $25 game and it certainly isn't a finished game. This plays like a doom mod that someone got bored with halfway through making and rushed to finish for the sake of being done with it. This game had lots of potential, but now that it's out of early access it's unlikely that potential will ever see the light of day.

_childDocuments_.review: May 2nd 2022 edit: review updated to match the full release of the game.9/10A fantastic oldschool shooter with lots of character progression.Nightmare Reaper is a game with a simple premise: kill enemies on your way and reach the end of the level, while collecting money and weapons on the way, with extra rewards based on how much of the level was completed (all enemies killed, all secrets found, etc). After the end of each level, the character then wakes up in a psychiatric ward, where they can explore some of it and read notes about the character's story, with a new note unlocked after each level and more sections from the ward unlocked as the game progresses, and each level starts when the character goes to bed.Weapons are split between 4 types - light, heavy, magic and melee, and there is a LOT of variety between guns. Just on heavy weapons alone there are molotovs, sticky bombs, bazookas, railguns, laser cannons, mini nukes and these are only some examples, plus this is also based only on the content currently available for the game. Weapons also have different levels and rarity levels, with some randomly generated stats for uncommon, rare or legendary weapons. Power-ups can also be acquired to use two weapons at the same time, activate slow motion or increase the character's speed. There is also a decent amount of enemy variety and locations throughout the game. Secrets can be found to acquire extra treasures and also to find some cool easter eggs. There are also some random events that happen when entering a room or when killing all enemies inside, which vary between traps or extra rewards. At the end of specific levels, there are also some boss fights, which are not overly hard but can still be pretty challenging. The game itself has a nice balance in difficulty, ammo and health pickups are plentiful enough and the game gives you enough resources between weapons and skills to fight off enemies, but at the same time enemies can also deal a lot of damage, so being caught offguard can cause an unexpected death. Dying itself is not too bad, however, as the only downside is having to replay that level. Finishing the game also unlocks a New Game+ mode, with harder monsters and better weapons.Character progression is done via three minigames - a platformer, a shoot'em'up and a minigame similar to Pokémon and they're all very extensive, with hundreds (I didn't count, but I'll risk saying over 300 total) of upgrades to acquire that range from more HP and ammo to new abilities or improving those abilities and it all really makes a lot of difference between how you start the game and how you play when you have all upgrades. One of the skill trees offers very small upgrades, but they carry over to other saves, so it's possible to start a brand new game already having some upgrades, specially to how much money is earned during the game which will also allow many upgrades from the "main" skill tree to be purchased quite early into the game. The minigames can also be turned off - this makes it so skills are just purchased directly without having to play the minigame, only with the downside of not obtaining some extra currency from beating these levels. There is also one skill tree that unlocks arenas as well, where beating each round of an arena earns currency for that skill tree.While the game isn't too focused on story development, the game still has an interesting story nonetheless which develops after each level is beaten and you find out more about why the character is in a mental hospital, what happened in her past and why she's fighting through levels when she sleeps. The narration for each page of her story is also very well done.In terms of graphics and sound, the game has a nice pixelated style and there is a LOT of gore involved when killing enemies. The soundtrack is fantastic, made by none other than Andrew Hulshult, and it certainly helps keep the player pumped up while fighting enemies as the music picks up when combat is happening.In terms of performance issues, there weren't many, but I did have some issues with framerate drops and the game occasionally freezing for a second, sometimes more. It's not an issue for the most part but it can be annoying and the framerate drops are specially bad during later arena rounds - it seems like the more the arena progresses, the more the framerate drops, and at some point it starts to affect how the character is being controlled as you try to navigate through the hordes of enemies.Outside of performance issues, the two sections of the game that I think could be improved on are difficulty balancing and the mechanics involving Pills and Toxicity.The game becomes harder the more the player progresses through each New Game+ as enemies deal more damage. The problem with this is that the game is very focused on offense and very little on defense - there are some defensive skills and abilities, but most of the game's upgrades are focused on making the character better at defeating enemies, which then turns both the character and the enemies into glass cannons. With the right weapons, you can absolutely mow through enemies, specially if you manage to get lucky and get some absolutely OP weapons, but at the same time it's also possible for enemies to burst you down from full HP to zero in less than a second or sometimes just one-shot you entirely in the case of some elite enemies. It'd be good to have some ways of preventing this from happening like the inclusion of health gating or a max threshold of how much damage the character can take within a second. However, as the game isn't too punishing with death, this isn't a major issue for the most part, mostly an annoyance, but it can be a problem in some harder levels and specially some boss fights.Using Pills grants some bonuses like damage reduction, more Gold or reduced enemy senses while at the same time generating Toxicity, which then generates random penalties during each level. The higher the Toxicity, the higher the penalty. The problem with this mechanic is that some of penalties you can get from Toxicity will just downright negate the bonuses you got from the Pills you equipped (example: equipping Pills that grant damage reduction, then getting a penalty that gives you +100% damage taken), which then turns it into a sort of catch-22 situation, where not equipping these Pills might just not give you these penalties or make them come up less often. The dev has mentioned that this is supposed to make the game harder, which is understandable, but it still feels like the execution could have been better. First because the only actual rewards you can get from Pills are more Gold and, indirectly, more weapon drops (as there are pills to increase number of enemies and chance of elite enemies, which then makes it so you get weapon drops more often), the other Pills offer stat bonuses instead, and second because of the forementioned reason of Pills bonuses being often negated. It would have been much more interesting if Toxicity generated unique effects as penalties like limiting the character's FOV, making it so all enemies can fly, the character has a small but permanent DOT effect that lasts through the entire level, enemies can cause random status effects, etc, rather than just providing penalties that often negate the Pills bonuses that were meant to be granted.Despite these two issues, however, neither of them are significant enough to hinder how fun the game is, it's still a very fun game with only the occasional minor frustration involved.Easily recommended, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. If you grew up playing the original Wolfenstein, Doom, Rise of the Triad, Blake Stone, or Heretic/Hexen, do yourself a favor and pick up this gem of a game. I wasn't sure what to expect at first but I couldn't believe how much fun this game is. The levels are procedurally generated, which makes for excellent replayability. then you have the WEAPONS, and OMG THEY ARE SO MUCH FREAKING FUN! And highly varied, so you can get a good breadth on weapon types which are a blast. My favorite are the trap cubes, which you use to capture enemies and then turn them to your side Pokemon style hahaha. The difficulty scales as you keep playing, and the levels have secrets and all kinds of fun traps, barrels, branches, pits, etc. So yes, please do yourself the favor of playing this game if you like old school shooters. I'd be very surprised if you were disappointed.

There's, at least from the vantage point that I can observe from in my current progress of the game, a few hundred skill tree upgrades.There's an overworld in an asylum where you jump into wards 'ala Mario 64 paintings.In the actual missions there's a ton of random event modifiers and powerups to mod the flow, not even counting the randomized weapons/levels. This is all just so crazy.This probably took the developer ages to make, because everything they imagined, they probably added to the workflow without compromise. My condolences to their mental health as an indie dev. I'll be following this guy's future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game? Yes. Do I think It can be improved vastly? Also yes.When Nightmare Reaper feels good, it feels great. And I mean GREAT. The randomized guns are a blast, the action is visceral and satisfying, the gameplay loop of shoot/dodge/strafe feels tight, there's a good learning curve that provides a healthy challenge, and the individual levels have a great deal of diversity and detail. If the game was just about these core mechanics, it would be a blast through and through. The problem though, is that you only get to spend maybe half your time doing what makes this game so awesome. My main issue is with the key items and doors. I often find myself circling a level over and over again, trying to find a key, or a battery, or whatever I need to progress. More than once I've simply reset the game, because I know just beating a different configuration of the same procedurally generated level instead will not only be more fun, but probably take less time. This feels like something many game developers have been struggling with since forever. Wandering around aimlessly while looking for the next thing to do isn't fun, nor is it a "puzzle." It's just tedious. This issue could easily be fixed by marking important stuff on the mini map, the same way doors and purple pentagrams are marked. As for the actual puzzles, they tend to have the same feeling of tedium. The controls feel great for running and gunning, not for platforming. There's never a feeling of satisfaction, or an "Aha! I've solved it!" moment when a puzzle room is completed, just "Thank god that's over and I still have some health left. Anyways..."I think its also worth noting that the mini game upgrade system is very cute and a lot of fun, and it's cool that you can turn them off if you feel like simply buying the upgrades. They seem to give a lot of customization in that regard for both preference and accessibility purposes, something a lot of games simply don't bother with, and I think that's great. I also really love the arena, which lets me do exactly what I want to be doing in this game- running and shooting stuff. My final score? 7/10. Would probably be closer to 9/10 if it wasn't for the "puzzles." It really is a wonderful game during its best moments, but if you can't see yourself handling 15 minutes of slog for every 15 minutes of blowing stuff up, I would pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is an impressively well made, fast and fun shooter. If you're into Doom, Quake, etc. you'll probably love it. You can really see how much work the developer put in to this game, a lot of love and passion for the genre. The weapons range from normal firearms to ridiculous spell books and exotic weapons pouring out death and fire to melt your enemies. It also has one of the best sound tracks of any game I've played, crunchy hard riffs and pounding bass lines. Andrew Hulshult is amazing and his music is a perfect fit for this game. He also wrote the sound track for DUSK, if you like Mick Gordon you should check out Hulshult's other work.

The guns are cool and varied, there's so many possibilities now it's insane.I found a chain gun that shoots napalm.I found a deagle that shoots 3 bullets per click.I found a single shot railroad spike launcher that burst fires instead of being single action.I found dual p90s with 95% life drain and 20% crit chance.I found a "judge" that had 100% pierce chance and homing shots, so the armor piercing rounds would infinitely pierce whoever it hit and hit them multiple times until they died. _childDocuments_.review: 11/10Many times in the past games have gone into early access on Steam, stayed there for years, then come out of the oven undercooked and underwhelming. This game, to put it lightly, has not. Not in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slightest. This game has so much ♥♥♥♥ to do that I'm not sure 100 hours would be enough to cover everything it offers. Let me give you an example of how this game is a rabbithole of features.At the beginning of the game you gain access to the skill tree. This allows you to spend gold to get buffs and skills. Later on you get access to another skill tree, the topaz tree, which requires topaz to purchase skills. The way you get this currency is by playing the game within the game, which is a pokemon clone where you capture creatures and level them up and fight people to get buffs and skills. Did I mention that in the first skill tree you have to play a platforming game to get the upgrades?And even later on you get access to the Jade Tree which requires Jade, which you can only get from playing the minigame more, which is an arcade space shooter, or playing The Arena, which is an alternative to playing levels where you fight hordes of monsters in waves. You can also get access to different flavored arenas as you beat levels in the main game. And what was the point of that last section you ask? To illustrate the point that despite the wall of text it took me to explain the features, at no point did these features become overwhelming or convoluted. And if you don't like doing the minigames you can just turn them off.At it's core this game is an extremely intricate and well designed roguelike looter shooter with touches of RPG and arcade games all wrapped in a beautiful looking retro style.This game is amazing and well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: The zenith of Boomer Shooters, it's going to be hard for anyone to top this. I play a lot of shooters. Always have, always will. But Nightmare Reaper is simply one of the best out there, and I cannot recommend it enough. It's so thoroughly fine-tuned, and it feels like its years of early access truly helped it to solidify itself as the game it is today. It's got enough content to fuel well over 100 hours, and truly could be infinite in some regards. The story feels very optional, never a requirement, but there if you want it. If you like shooters, you simply must give Nightmare Reaper a go. You will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun retro-style shooter with rogue-lite elements. The shooting is impactful and satisfying. Weapon variety is substantial and will only get better. Enemy variety is pretty good and will likely improve as well. Game is still unfinished and in early access with the developer actively releasing patches and updates. Most importantly the game is fun and engaging even in it's young state. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy f*ck this game has a lot of achievements and it drives the completionist within me up the wall.But damn I love it.Fantastic retro shooter, tons of randomized stat guns from things as simple as pistols and knives to things as wacky as black hole guns and mini nuke launchers. Impacts are punchy, satisfying and look amazing for the pixelation within the game. Loads of enemies, mostly just more difficult re-skins of previous iterations but they still remain interesting. Level design is nothing that interesting for the most part; lots of corridors and doors and more corridors and more doors. What makes this game so interesting is the fact that you're kind of playing 6 games at once. 1: the fps shooter, main meat and potatoes of the game2: between fps levels you wake up in your room in an insane asylum, this is where the lore and slow exploration of the building come in. 3: arena fps mode, unlocked gradually and gives currency for game 64: mario like minigame/skill tree which you unlock by earning currency in game 15: pokemon like minigame/upgrade list that you play by completing levels in game 16: galaga like minigame/attribute + ability upgrade list This system keeps the seemingly repetitive gameplay fresh, and allows for breaks from one another while continuously upgrading yourself. Loved this game, will 100% eventually but I gotta stop for now cause it's TOO MUCH
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes, with its restraints, it is a jack of all trades but a master of none. I enjoyed the classic fast-paced shooter nature with all of its mini games. To the point where skill tree encapsulates a game-in-a-game, where the other two games feel VOID of any real game time worth giving (stats & content). The main game has the hospital and the adventure mode which are well worth my time exploring their eerie nature. Combat evolves well with scaling through the game. Difficulty maxed midway and feels nice, getting more complex with the levels later game. My biggest drawback, random generation, which makes some of the puzzles & levels a bit soft-locking at points (main beef was teleporter monoliths blocking single lane traffic). Vast maps with a map that doesn't improve late game with very complex levels. Restarting a fun level is never a good time, but if you can look past this, I had a very enjoyable time with this game. I may pick this game back up, but I think its in for a deep, deep sleep.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is just fantastic. first off you have some fast paced combat with plenty of gore and tons of weapons and variants.then theres the real meat of the actual story.  you're in a mental hospital, when you interact with your bed to sleep you go to your next level. as you progress through the game and return to your room after dreams you'll notice things changing. you get a new page of voice acted backstory by a doctor who seems to have taken you on as a patient. theres also a psychological horror element. lets just say you have visions in levels and when you wake up you can leave your room after a certain amount of levels. the creativity keeps amping up as well. you have a GBA type device for your pause menu and it has different cartridges (3 mini games in total) once you have enough in game coins you can start a mario style mini game with a over world, where each level gives you new perks. theres also a Pokemon mini game that's somewhat fleshed out that also gets you more perks. i think this might be the best old school style shooter, ive been going through alot of them and this constantly sticks out. awesome graphics as well

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is a really cool looter shooter FPS game with awesome old school style and pixel art. You're some lady who went insane and is in a mental hospital and every time you go to sleep in your bed you go into her nightmares and kick some ass.There is so much content in this game that it actually seems excessive at times. I think there was 84 or so levels that I completed and it took me 26 or so hours to get through the game, but there is also a new game plus and if you beat the game again, there are 2 more new game pluses for even more playthroughs.There are so many incredible guns in this game. Normally an FPS game will have 6 to 9 guns and occasionaly there may be a secondary fire. In this game there are so many weapons I can't even think of them all. I am going to guess at least 50 weapons, and every weapon has a least one secondary fire, some have multiple other firing modes. On top of that, each weapon will have different rarity grades and based on that, different effects of buffs. At the end of every level you get to keep 1 weapon and the rest are sold for coins which you can use in the mini-games to permanently upgrade your character.You also later unlock a dash ability which is extremely handy and the coolest thing ever, a grappling hook. OMG this grappling hook is fun to play with and swing around on.Each world has 3 levels, and every world brings with it new textures and at least 1 new enemy type which you may then see in other levels as you proceed further along the game. The pixel art is amazing for everything, especially the enemy characters. They all look so good and only a few are reskins while everything else is unique. There are so many enemies in this game, just like with the guns. You will always have something new to see throughout the entire game from start to finish.The music is great, real nice metal sound with guitar and drums and the music kicks in once the action gets going otherwise it's just nice background ambiance and sounds as you explore.There aren't many things that take away from the awesome game experience but one would be the length of the game. It's weird to say this but it almost feels like there is too much content at times. For example, to increase your characters abilities you play some different mini-games, but these mini-games are huge. One is a Super Mario Bros 3 type world map with individual levels all throughout and leading to the castle boss at the end, and they have ALL the world maps. It's not just one, it's all of them, and as many levels too. There is a Pokemon type of game, again, massive, just to power up your character. Another is a shmup that is once again huge and seems endless.Another thing that is a bit annoying is during the first 1/4 of the game all the levels / worlds are too similar. The maps are procedurally generated and the way they are done in the first part of the game will have you running through the exact same rooms in different levels, just connected differently. Now this is only a problem during the 1st 1/4 of the game, but it made me less interested in playing. I powered through it though and am happy I did, the levels got way better after that.There is a really cool Arena in this game where you have 4 different arenas and fight waves of guys and get paid in jade coins which you can then use in the shmup to buy more upgrades and unlock more shmup levels.Nightmare Reaper is another top tier retro style FPS game and if you like these games you absolutely should play this, it's incredible.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that got me to respect retro-shooters, again.  Nightmare reaper is a joy to play.  The game feels like all the good parts of Blood, Doom and Hexen.  The game starts out by placing you in a mental asylum as a patient.  Every time you go to sleep, the game throws you into a randomly generated level, with a chance to loot randomly generated loot and weapons. In addition, there are themes to each set of levels, so you don't get too tired of the background and level design you see, as it keeps changing up.  All of this works very well, and there are high levels of blood and gore to fill the environments with.  The only complaint I really have with the game is optimization.  Frames can dip a lot while playing on higher resolutions, and this is coming from someone playing on a fairly high end system (see profile for specs).  Hopefully in the future outside early access, this is addressed, as it’s the only issue I have with the game.  Nightmare Reaper is amazing to play, and you will have a different experience every time with the random weapon and level generation.  If you love retro shooters, do yourself a favor and play this game!  Although it is early access, it shows extreme promise as a full title.

_childDocuments_.review: I started out really enjoying this game, but by the end I was too exhausted and worn down to finish it.The best way to describe this game, albeit in the nerdiest niche way, is "pistol start oblige megawad". Every level you start over with a basic weapon you carried over from the previous level. You gain more weapons - as well as upgrade currency and power-ups - traversing through procedurally-arranged level chunks and killing everything in sight. As you progress, you can choose to keep more powerful weapons, gain dashes, and become very powerful. There's an enormous amount of gore and violence, the most insufferable writing ever, and some nice chunky pixels. But I didn't like it for a bunch of specific reasons.First, there's so much AoE flung your way. A common enemy has acid for blood, and brushing into fire and damaging yourself is super common. While this isn't really a difficulty increases, since you gain health killing enemies, it limits the sort of tactical, health/ammo tension I look for in retro shooters. This feels like it impacts the level design as well; since there's so many AoEs, the levels are all big enough to let you dodge them, which makes the maps feel too similar.Enemy variety is pretty bad too. Enemies just charge straight at you or shoot you, which is normal, but you are so powerful that none of them are threatening. After ten levels the combat felt rote and at that point I was just playing for the puzzles. After 30-plus I was too exhausted to continue. The only time you are likely to die is at the very beginning, or maybe further along in the game than I got. I'm not looking for perfection here, just something more interesting than backpedaling and emptying my mag. I cannot overstate just how boring I found the combat by the time I stopped playing.Leveling up is whatever, I think I would've much preferred a static difficulty curve of upgrades or none at all, but in the end it's fine. What I hated about it was the platformer. Feels like trash, completely pointless to do anything but beeline to the end. And EVERY UPGRADE is a different level. You can turn it off, which I did, but what should be a reprieve from the boring shooting is instead a boring platformer. Missed opportunity for a nice change of pace. Plus making every upgrade a new level robbed it of magic. If the levels were twice as long, only on major upgrades, and had better character physics, I'd be in love.I wish I could recommend this. I really wanted to like Nightmare Reaper, and did, for a time. But after I cleared about a megawad's worth of levels, and saw how much more I had to play to finish, all with this tedious combat that felt hollow and boring, I gave it up. If you're looking for something that's basically mindless murder with some funny weapons and itemization, this game will make you happy. But I want more from an FPS, and this didn't deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't say I recommend this game. After 3 failed attempts to finishing the main story, I can safely say that this is simply not worth the time it takes to beat.This game is an endurance-run incarnate. It goes on for way too long, and the only trick the game has up it's sleeve to mitigate that issue, is to make the levels longer and adding backtracking mechanics to make it even longer. The map doesn't help in that regard, since important items, weapons, treasures or anything of significance aren't highlighted or shown on the map, meaning you can spend a while combing the level for the thing you need to progress, while still missing it because the pixel assets bleed into each other in a way that makes certain things almost impossible to spot at a glance.The combat feels very fast and fun at first, but the longer you play, the more reliant on corner-peaking and slow paced engagement you become. The enemies start hitting so hard you'll die in only a few shots, and with some of them having elemental attacks that slow you, disable your weapons, or simply blind you with the amount of particle effects on screen, the game becomes a cover shooter in a sense where it's just a lot safer and better to engage the enemies from afar. And with how unbalanced some of the weapons are, and how some of them are actually just a straight up downgrade from the standard kick attack, it's hard to engage a fight with any sort of consistency or plan other than to just shoot at them from far away and hope they don't make it to you in time to drain your health bar.The enemy variety is fun, but the game is quick to add hit-scan enemies and summoners, which quickly flood the room with enemies if they aren't taken care of. I've also encountered an event countless times, where the game spawns a dozen or so summoning gems into a room, with far too much health. Which means by the end of it, I have 5 stunners, 10 hitscanners, and countless other chargers and shockers all swarming towards me.The level up system is a neat idea at first, with you unlocking traits, buffs and bonuses for yourself by playing a brief yet repetitive sidescroller. The levels all feel similar enough to quickly become bored of them, and with infinite lives and respawns being on every screen, you can't really skip them as they are an essential part of progressing the game. Each one costing around a few thousand coins at the start, but by the end, you're pouring millions of coins and treasures into the smallest, insignificant power-up.The weapons start out simple enough. Pistols, shotguns, rifles and laser guns being a pretty good standard, but by the end, you're getting bootleg pirate cannon rigs, Bolters from 40k, tesla coil-guns, auto-aim pistols, and the game just starts feeling silly at that point since it keeps giving you the basic weapons from the start of the game. The weapon stats aren't any better either, since some are far better than others, and honestly just add another gimmick to a weapon that is already bordering on being silly. Which usually means there isn't much reason for me to not pick the same weapons over and over again to keep between stages.The bosses aren't anything to really talk about, since most of them only have around 2-3 attacks, and their difficulty mostly comes from how small their arenas usually are, and what weapons you just happened to get in the level leading up to them.The levels start out promising with good themes and lovely atmosphere, but as it goes on, you can feel the levels really starting to overuse the same texture. The tilesets for the later levels are mostly comprised of claustrophobic hallways that use the same textures, and caves that have copy/pasted sprites and aesthetics.I know I have a 100+ hours in this game, but most of those were spent during the early days of the game before the 1.0 release. I spent hours making up new challenge runs for myself,hunting for achievements, and noting down bugs to report, but now that the game is out, I can't even bring myself to finishing it. It goes on for way too long, pads itself out with mindless key hunting and backtracking, and starts feeling repetitive at around the half way mark. You can tell where the new chapters were added in the development phase, as you feel an abrupt flood of new mechanics and level design being dumped on you out of nowhere. I often feel myself not playing this game for months, before seeing it in my library and remembering how fun the first few levels are. And then after a few hours of playing, I remember why I stopped in the first place and the cycle begins anew. I honestly can't recommend this game on the grounds that it is such a slow and boring grind towards a story the game doesn't seem very interested in telling you, seeing how it's all told through a series of notes after each level, which you could honestly completely miss if you weren't actively looking for it. I know this game has a mode which shortens the game significantly, but that just begs the question why the game doesn't have that be the default experience, while keeping the longer version as an "extended cut" for the players who want more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so spectacular partly because it has such an immensity of straight content, all of which contributes to each other. There are multiple "skill" trees, all of which might be considered content islands, but all of which go towards the main progression of the game.This game is so spectacular in another part due to how simple yet satisfying the core game loop is. The gore is satisfying, the weapons are weighty to handle, et cetera. Yet another reason this game is so great is because the devs clearly made conscious, clear attempts to understand what works and what doesn't in games in this genre. When the violence gets incredibly hectic and impossible to follow, the game enters bullet time. There's no superfluous cosmetic reload animations that beckon animation cancelling. The movement is very quick to encourage quick map traversal and reduce downtime. The reward structure rewards players that meticulously comb each stage, but does not punish those that don't; you still get a bonus for only getting part of the treasure. Unlocks in later parts of the game are meaningful, such as eventually being able to unlock a ledge grab, et cetera. There's a lot to like in this game in the basic gameplay loop, but that is genuinely the tip of the iceberg. The only downside I'd list about this game is that the optimization is poor. Other than that, though, it's an absolute blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, this game comes so close. It scrapes the greatness trophy before falling back down to niche but pretty good territory. I initially played the demo and loved it so much that I purchased the game without waiting for a big discount (which, if you know me, almost never happens).Nightmare Reaper is the second roguelite FPS I have played this year, the first being the much earlier, simpler, but more polished Immortal Redneck. NR is in every aspect a far more complex game than IR, and it is both better and worse for that complexity.Briefly:The core gameplay takes place inside the dreams of a woman locked up alone in a haunted, derelict psychiatric hospital. The game has three episodes, each split into several chapters. Each chapter consists of three levels which take place in the same setting (forest, the moon, hell, etc). Each episode introduces a new skill tree, new mechanics, new enemies, weapons, and environmental puzzles. There is a basic story, told entirely through very short journal entries which unlock upon completion of each level.The roguelike elements:randomly arranged levels consisting of several pre-designed rooms which are arranged randomly. The same idea as Immortal Redneck, but with a lot more room possibilities.weapon stats (from base through to four slots for random positive and negative perks, plus a damage multiplier for NG+)enemy placement, modifiers, and varietysecret and puzzle placement (with a staggering number of easter eggs)random events (positive or negative; like weapon rerolls, barrel or icicle rain, doppelgänger attack)randomly placed powerupsLoved:Variety. The weapons, enemies, level designs, artwork, secrets, powerups, perks, etc are hugely varied. It is hard to get sick of anything for more than a few minutes before you get something entirely different.The "real world" of the hospital, which is revealed slowly and over time through progression, exploration, and experimentation.The amount of replayability, as with most roguelites, is wonderful.The sound design. Screaming in the hospital, whistling cowboys, the wind blowing through a cracked wall. Good stuff.The slow burn nature of the skill trees, designed to be unlocked over several playthroughs.Mixed feelings:All the things which come with RNG: having to stick with the same weapon forever because everything which drops is garbage, soft-locks caused by random placement of objects and tools, levels which are far too simple or far too complex.The game explains almost nothing. I appreciate this in a game like Spelunky because the game teaches the player organically. Here there is so much complexity built in, but it is not always easy to see or understand how a system works -- especially the skill trees and weapon modifier -- without referring to a guide or the forums. There were several entire features that I only discovered because I looked at a guide.DPS. It is impossible to reliably determine a weapon's DPS, and due to the nature of the game, I often come upon a weapon after I've killed everything in a level and simply don't know if I should keep it or not.Secret hunting. Oh man, I like secret hunting, but too much backtracking and tool hunting takes away from the pace of the game.The difficulty ramping after several playthoughs is not well balanced. Some enemies can kill with one or two hits and a few cannot be dodged reliably. This is fine sometimes, but the more I progress, the more I die to BS.Hated:The skill tree mini games, which can be "disabled," are unnecessarily complicated and, especially into NG+, tedious. Disabling the mini game part is great, but why are the maze-like worlds not disabled as well? The topaz tree (which can easily last into NG+5 and beyond) is the worst, as one has to constantly navigate back and forth in order to process gold or jade into topaz, then find the upgrades to unlock. Way too much clicking.Screen readability is a problem. The pets float at head level and will often momentarily obscure large parts of the screen. Enemies often die but remain frozen in the same position for a few seconds. The same can happen with certain projectiles. When things get chaotic, it can be very hard to do much about it.The unlockable arenas are fun, however due to some enemy pathfinding and awareness issues, they bog down at the end of rounds when there is one last enemy stuck somewhere.The melee weapons feel almost entirely useless. This could be me, but I never found a melee weapon which felt workable against tough enemies, no matter the stats or multiplier. The same goes for stuff like the sniper rifle and molotov.Sprite-based enemies. Specifically when they are close up or in levels with a lot of verticality. It is pretty hard to hit two dimensional enemies when looking down at them from ten meters above. But they sure don't struggle with their aim at all. Not a problem unique to this game, but annoying nonetheless.Powerup hit boxes. When I'm fighting 50 enemies at once in an arena, it is often near impossible to jump precisely to a powerup which has spawned in the air.Performance and crashes:For the most part, the game played reliably and smoothly on my aging system (I5-8500/GTX 1070). I experienced three crashes during the main campaign, but lost no progress. The arenas are a different story. On high levels I experienced frequent instances of single digit framerates and numerous crashes. The dev currently suggests quitting and restarting at ten round intervals (which is when arena progress is saved), but that isn't an acceptable solution long term.Suggestions for the future:I think the game needs UI tweaking to expose the underlying systems. Specifically the menus for pills and pet/jade loadout should be selectable within the mini game without the need for a shortcut key. Weapon DPS (or at least viability) needs to be discoverable without an enemy being present. Weapon stats and possible reroll outcomes should be defined and the specific "random projectile" should be named because it isn't random once it has been rolled into the gun. The mini games should have the option to disable them clearly visible, not hidden in settings. Furthermore, when disabled they should be pared down to a simple menu or tree. Other stuff like poor arena performance, rebalancing NG+ ramping, and adjusting the speed at which jade drops is mentioned above, but these are the core issues I have.As far as additions, I would really appreciate a test room where I can build a weapon and experiment with the stats as I see fit, then choose enemies to attack with it. A freemode, so to speak.Conclusion:For the most part I have a lot of fun playing Nightmare Reaper. With a little tweaking, it can be something truly great. I do think that my interest waned significantly once I had completed it once, and I do wish there were more possibilities to unlock in NG+. Play the demo, you'll know if it is for you within a level or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Never in my life have I been THIS impressed with an indie game. This game is simply astounding. There's so much to praise about this game, but I don't want to spoil the surprises, so I'l just go over the basics. Gameplay is amazing. 10/10. Everything feels meaty and impactful, and I can assure you that the gibs do not disappoint. The game looks fantastic, with styled pixel art that doesn't fall into the trap of being hard to look at or obscuring the gameplay in any way. The movement is stellar, fast paced and precise but not too technically demanding of you to be unfun. The roguelike elements work fantastically, and seamlessly blend level-based arena shooter and randomly-generated roguelike.Yet what impresses me most out of everything is the weapons. There are dozens upon dozens of unique, fun, and useful weapons. I cannot stress enough how impressive this is. The game manages to make a huge arsenal of weapons  all viable in their own way while making each one feel like a joy to use. (I cannot emphasize enough how great everything feels btw. I audibly said "That's so effing cool" when I saw the special attack of a certain weapon)I'm not typically one for hyperbole, and tend towards the critical side when discussing games, but Nightmare Reaper blows me away in the same vein as Hollow Knight. I've only played for 2 hours so far, but God do I want to play more. This game possesses a level of polish worthy of AAA games (Minus the soul-sucking greed) for half the price. Instant must-buy.
