_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is a horror-themed first person looter shooter, with slight RPG elements and slight roguelite elements, a blend of genres and mechanics that not always works well, but executed almost perfectly here. The story is barely existent, and I think some will appreciate the fact that you can skip most of the backstory given to the player. The main character is a nameless mental patient stuck in her hospital room (which functions as the game’s hub) where she can find notes written by her doctor providing context as to why the main character is locked in there, what the treatment they are giving her is, and why the gameplay loop is exactly the way it is; with a new note appearing after every single mission is cleared. The patient (or “Pat”, for short) has horrible nightmares where she faces hordes of demons and other kinds of monsters every time she goes to sleep. I will not go further into why this is the case, since I do not want to spoil the doctor’s notes.Gameplay, as is usual in the genre, is where “Nightmare Reaper” shines. Not only is the gameplay loop of going to bed, killing a bunch of demons, exploring your nightmares, exploring the hospital then repeating highly addictive; it also features some of the best gunplay in a modern shooter. It’s frantic, it’s gory, it features a fantastic soundtrack by Andrew Hulshult.Nightmare Reaper’s gameplay is divided into three kinds of segments: The nightmares, where you kill demons, find new weapons and put them to use, and progress through the story. The hospital, which serves as a hub of sorts, and you can explore as it opens up more and more as you progress through the story. And lastly, the minigames and skill trees, of which there are three, and they all use different currencies to unlock new abilities and power up the patient.The nightmares are the main draw of the game, and for good reason. As I mentioned before, the gunplay is frantic and requires your full attention to dispatch most enemies, especially when you’re starting out and you’re relatively weak, with no strong weapons to carry you through the first portion of the game, but also as stronger enemies start to join the roster and you have more movement-related tools at your disposal. There are different weapon types, each requiring a different kind of ammunition, of which there are three types (Bullets, explosives and magic); as well as four different grades of rarity, rarity giving your weapons different attributes, both positive and negative, that range from the practical but boring reduction in ammo consumption, to the absolutely ludicrous such as adding more projectiles to your attack.Every time you finish a level, the game lets you keep one weapon you’ve acquired through the run for the next one, then sells off every other one you have acquired. Killing every single enemy in a nightmare, obtaining all the loot and finding all secrets also gives you large gold bonuses, so trying to get 100% completion on every run is optimal.Speaking of weapons, they also range from the mundane to absolutely insane. You could wield a shotgun, a whip, a katana, molotov cocktails, a quad-barreled shotgun, a black hole launcher, a mini nuke launcher; all of which are useful in their own right. To give an example of how zany weapons can get with the right modifiers, a mini nuke launcher with the modifiers “+2 attacks” and “Burst fire” would fire three barrages of three mini nukes each in quick succession. Playing around with different builds, weapon types, and modifiers is encouraged. As a result of the aforementioned mechanics, combat is very satisfying when you massacre an entire horde of enemies, and very rarely frustrating when you die.Exploration is key to finding better loot, as well as acquiring more money that you will need to upgrade  the patient’s stats. Not every single room in a nightmare is combat focused, some of them are what I like to call “challenge rooms”, where you have to solve puzzles or platform around small platforms in order to get a reward at the end. Said rewards aren’t always worth it, but it’s good to go through them at least to sell the weapon you get at the end for more gold.The hospital segment is limited, but wonderfully crafted. You can explore a relatively small portion of the facilities. However, it is one of the most frightening experiences the game has to offer. As more areas open up to players, things are left behind for them to access those areas by themselves later on.  As they explore, they will hear loud thuds, screams, sobbing, manic cackling; light bulbs will flicker, suddenly explode, or simply stay on as the patient passes by. As mentioned before, it’s also the place where you can read more on the backstory.As for the minigames, it’s the main form of character progression aside from acquiring more powerful weapons on the main gameplay loop. The three skill trees, namely: Skill/Gold Tree, Topaz Tree and Jade Tree, all feature different maps and minigames for you to play as you acquire the respective currencies. The skills are most passive, and you can turn the minigames off if you get bored of them or just don't like them.In terms of presentation, the art style is great for what it’s trying to convey. Don’t let the voxel graphics turn you away, the developers created some of the most interesting scenarios and terrifying creatures I’ve seen in a “boomer shooter” in a while. The use of lighting and shadows is outstanding, especially with dynamic shadows on (which may sadly cause your game to lag), which is more noticeable when you’re exploring the hospital.The settings are fantastic as well, going from caves and small villages in chapter 1, to urban set pieces in chapter 2, to the most eldritch of dreamscapes in chapter 3.Sound design is spot on as well and integrates greatly into the gameplay. The player will hear the wind blowing when they’re near a secret, hear the sounds certain enemies make as they get closer to them, or get guided to the source of random events. As mentioned before, they also help set the atmosphere perfectly, especially during the hospital segments.Nightmare Reaper’s biggest issue is how much the performance can dip at times. That said, I could run the game at 60 fps consistently with everything but dynamic shadows on the highest settings, with very few dips in the 20 hours it took me to beat the game on my second savefile.Another issue the game has, and your mileage may vary, is how obtaining all treasures during most chapter 3 levels might feel like busywork due to the way some levels are structured. That said, there’s a pet that makes this a lot easier.Another con the game might have depending on how skillful you are, is how overpowered guns can trivialize most enemies. However, less skilled players will still find the game challenging, especially if they haven’t mastered the game’s movement. Would I recommend Nightmare Reaper? Yes. It’s probably one of the best roguelites made in the last few years: The combat is fluid and fast paced, the music is phenomenal, the atmosphere really adds to the game and does a great job at keeping the player hooked. Tutorials are clear and make the experience very accesible. The 25 USD price tag might be a bit too much for some, but considering the game features two different endings, a new game + mode and such great gameplay, as well as 82 levels, it might be worth getting at full price. If you’re not entirely sure, there's a demo available.

_childDocuments_.review: For me the game is fun in short sessions, but gets repetitive very quickly.During a session I usually play a couple of levels (one level is three parts and sometimes a boss fight) and that's enough for me. Procedurally generated levels help a little, but it's still strange that you often play EXACTLY the same level twice in a row.Movement feels good, but can feel a bit slippery after dashing or using the grappling hook.All the bunny hopping and rocket jumping makes combat enjoyable, but still sometimes it feels like you can't get away from enemies or their projectiles. Also sometimes it can be hard to tell if you're picking up ammo/health or are you getting hit since the screen just keeps flashing. Enemy attacks (especially melee) don't make a lot of sound.Game has many weapons, but you'll probably stick to a single weapon you can keep after finishing a level and that has the best stats. Enemy variety is also a big plus. Boss fights are usually pretty easy, but still some bosses might just immediately kill you in one hit even when you're full HP - especially the bosses with rocket launchers. Especially in later levels the boss fights can get cheap AF and almost impossible. When you'll encounter a boss with black hole launcher you can just quit the game.Game has a great soundtrack. Although it's the kinda typical metal soundtrack that every Doom clone/retro FPS these days seem to have, it's very well done. And this time the metal soundtrack fits the gameplay and setting.Apparently game has about 90 levels and I'm about half way thru the game.Story and the setting make me want to continue playing, but in short session as said earlier.I like that game just puts you straight back to the main hub without having to go thru menus after you start the game.EDIT: Gotta say the more I play the levels designs become A LOT worse. Just arena levels one after another with insane amounts of enemies. If you start with a bad weapon, you just have to play the level over and over again so long that you get a feasible generated level and you are able to get a proper weapon to fight the enemy mob spawns.So I liked the game about until level 60, but after that... thumbs down.

Somehow they decided what they think makes this game fun is bullet sponges and enemy spawners.I have zero interest in continuing this game now, because I know it's just going to be extremely unfun the next time I come across a developer pre-made level.TL;DR- Beginning 50'ish levels are A TON OF FUN.- Premade dev levels are absolute garbage and, in fact, are the anti-fun.Much like Game of Thrones, I can't recommend this game to anyone anymore based on the fact that it will become so incredibly frustrating, un-fun, and does a complete 180 on what this game originally gives us and fails to stick any landing.Sup devs? t(**t)

_childDocuments_.review: I truly wish there were a middling option for reviewing, but since there isn't, I'm more inclined to not recommending this. Simply put, it's just uninspired. The game is clearly a labor of love, but holds very little to set it apart from anything else, let alone the other options out there in the ever expanding world of the doom clone/boomer shooter genre. The "rogue lite" elements are that you can buy permanent upgrades for yourself, and each "run" yields different weapons. The upgrades are great, and the developers put a cute spin in the form of optional minigames in the style of old Gameboy games to gain your upgrades. You still have to pay though, but you can gain some extra coin if you do them...even if it is a laughable amount. The issue with this is that most of the weapons absolutely blow chunks. They range from useless to god tier, but 90% of what you get is useless since it takes 4 to 5 hours before you can get the ability that keeps you from exploding. The strongest weapons have AOE effects that also kill you faster than normal enemies, and a few hours in, enemies also start exploding. If you have any weapon with AOE, you just kill yourself. If you get any of the melee only weapons, you kill yourself on the enemies that explode into several other exploding enemies. The weapons are not only mostly just not viable, but most are also boring. I didn't get a single automatic weapon until 3 hours worth of playing either, and I've only gotten a total of 4 after 5 hours of playtime. Even if the weapons were bad but enjoyable, it would be one thing, but they just aren't. I enjoyed the melee weapons right up until the majority of enemies in my levels were exploding blobs that dropped more exploding blobs, making them utterly useless. As for the procedural bit, the part that interested me the most so that I could at least look forward to replaying the game...there's nothing. The "procedural" portion of the game is just the same map with different doors opening, meaning you can have almost the exact same run back to back. I had that, and it was a huge disappointment. To top things all off, the gameplay is s l o w. The trailers make this out to be something fast and heavy, but it's just not. Combat encounters are sloppy and uncoordinated, the difficulty purely being from spamming enemies that explode. You fight for maybe a minute or two, then have to run around finding every door (and secret, if you're one of those people. I am, and it adds a lot of time.) until you clear an area completely. The combat is not nearly fun enough to balance out the fact that you spend more time exploring than you do fighting, which is a horrible "balance" for a game sold as being so fast paced. Lastly, the game looks fine for what it is, but it very clearly doesn't look great. Despite this, it runs worse than Doom (2016), a graphically impressive game that even had Denuvo for a time. A game operating on sprites running worse than that is just...sad. I don't feel that I should be dropping frames in a game comprised of sprites and small maps (that you can also see through, almost like noclipping through Gmod, but by simply jumping instead) with an i9 and an RTX 2080. The performance is just dreadful.Boring gunplay, laughable procedural elements, inexcusable optimization, and a horrible selection of "shootable loot" makes for an experience that just isn't worth it. The only thing that left me middling was that it clearly isn't a cashgrab. The developers put obvious care into the game, but lacked anything that made the gameplay fun or unique. The gimmicks within the game hold the most life within, but everything else falls to the wayside. The "plot" is oddly captivating, but only because it's drip fed to you with 1 to 3 sentences of "plot" every time you complete a stage. I want to know where it's going, but I also only care because I'm already playing it. This game is just something to do, and I wish it were more than that, but it's just not.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access Review:Really good retro FPS mixed with looter shooter mechanics and a skill tree that plays like old 2D platformer games ( It can be turned off and you just buy the upgrades and skip the jumping minigame if you dont feel like doing it). And the pause menu is a GBA which is amazing.Early access content is only 2 chapters, second one is longer than the first by a big margin, and the stages have more verticality to them, the game gives you a grappling hook at the start of the second chapter so you dont rely on the chainsaw and the rng to find one(Grappling hook doesn't work over water unlike the chainsaw hook, but it has more range), there is some story which i won't spoil but you can see it on the notes that are left behind once you finish a stage on your desk.Gunplay is really good, gun sounds and overall audio is amazing, must have one of the best gun sounds i have seen for an indie retro fps.Performance is good enough for an early access, there are some cases where you can get some fps drops, mostly when there are tons of enemies that are doing AoE attacks, and lots of props breaking at the same time, happens mostly in second chapter when things can get way more chaotic, but overall its good.Totally worth picking up if you want to scratch that retro fps itch and you also like looter shoters.Will update the review when Chapter 3 comes out and i finish the whole game.Full Release Review:Most of the points of the early access remain, but the third act is way longer than the second one, a whole run starting a new save slot took me around 36h~, though the game is meant to be played on new game + and a few more times to unlock all the skills, later skill trees get grindy, either because high price on skill bought with coins, jade points or amber ( 2 new currencies tied to minigames/skill trees).The full release also includes 2 more skill trees tied to 2 new minigames, you'll need some of the upgrades to make your life easier in act 2-3, like reduced damage from elements, more health,  lava inmunity, etc. You are not supposed to be able to get everything in just 1 run so bear that in mind.Amber is earned really slow playing the minigame, or earning 100 or so each time you beat a level of the main game.Jade is earned for playing the arenas, it's easy to get lots of upgrades if you have already unlocked a few arenas, right now higher waves like +30 can be a pain in the ass, FPS tank because of explosions and other effects with almost 100 enemies if there are summoners.There are 2 endings to the story, won't spoil but you might be able to see both if you play new game + :DOverall the game is fantastic and totally worth checking out even at retail price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me by surprise.  Kinda just stumbled on it, checked out a few gameplay videos and picked it up on a whim.  Haven't been able to put it down.  It's got a really interesting way of telling its story but gameplay is king here for me.  Very doom-like but I actually like this game far more than doom (2016) because of its randomly generated levels, weapon variety and progression systems.I also like that if you die (and you will die a lot) you just restart that level.  You can also always keep one weapon of the multitudes that you will find.  There are so many crazy weapon types, and they can all roll in different rarities and have various stats.  The hunt for that perfect weapon you decide to keep is crazy addicting, as is unlocking the progression nodes in the various mini-games.  Very few games keep me this engaged for this long as of late, but this game's design is just so tight and satisfying.  I will say however that I'm not really fond of the mini-games, thankfully you can turn 2 out of the 3 off.  The other one, you will need to play a bit in order to unlock some really cool passives, skills and pets but it's not too bad.  I get what the dev was after here, but for me personally I'd just rather be playing the main game because it's so good.Arena mode is really fun too and the rewards tie directly into the aforementioned progression and it's a nice break from the main story mode.In conclusion, this game is brilliant, fast-paced crazy and amazingly designed.  There's always something to upgrade, or another weapon to craft (by using the doctor to weak stats, etc.).  Has that addictive flair.  Performs well now since last playing it a while back on both PC and SX.  Rarely do I encounter any hiccups.  Lots of nice tweaks as well like reduced explosion shake, etc.  Thanks dev, we appreciate it lol.EDIT:  I just dumped over another 100 hours in the xbox version.  So yes, I double-dipped this game which I rarely ever do.  I do believe I have a love affair with this game and I keep trying other indie boomer shooters to fill the gap, but nothing ever does it.  Just more of this game lol.

_childDocuments_.review: RECOMMEND ON SALE.ULTIMATELY TL;DR:If you're a fan of the retro FPS games, Nightmare Reaper captures the essence incredibly well. Action keeps you moving, and keeps you gunning. After a certain point, you really get tired, and a lot of the negatives start to aggravate you more.I think I would be cautious to recommend this game wholly without letting you know the faults that might turn you off toward purchasing this game.Nightmare Reaper lacks severely in a couple of areas - Mainly...a STORY LINE - it is very weak and straight forwardNO CINEMATICS - The cool animation for the trailer is legitimately the only animation outside of the retro game play throughout the entire game. I believed there would have been some kind of in game footage to go along with the storyline, but there isn't. Nor is there any cinematics. It's story is told via text and there is nothing that accompanies it other than voice over for it.MINI GAMES ARE NOT REWARDING - I found myself quickly bored and tired with the implemented mini-games in the skill trees. So much so as soon as I found out I can turn off certain upgrades and the mini-games, I did so immediately (Thankful to the dev to add this option) I know this isn't part of the core game play, but it is a significant enough feature through the game that I felt needed to be addressed. GAME PLAY BECOMES REDUNDANT - After the 30th level or so you get the gist of the game, and can start to feel where the time drains quite a bit once you're running through it. More-so once you start reaching NG ++.WAITING.... AND WAITING..... - When it comes to certain areas of the game, you can be waiting a LONG while. For example - when you start climbing the arena every round ends with you being showered in coins. As you get higher in levels  more coins shower you and it takes longer and longer for the next round to start. Suffice to say in this downtime I managed to watch a whole movie while doing a long arena run.WAIT WHAT? - Some skills are not explained thoroughly, or is quite confusing (For example, RED BARREL KICK I assumed meant you can just kick red barrels away from you without having to carry and toss it, but it seems to do with something with kicking yourself back? I'm still not sure), there is also no stats page that shows your progress in kills, collectibles etc etc. WHAT IT DOES WELL:LOOT VARIETY - Loot variety is incredibly robust in this game, and feels good when you get a gun with certain affixes and you feel nice shredding enemiesSOUND TRACK - Phenomenal work by Andrew Hulshult, kept me going a lot through the action and pacing of the game for sure.LEVEL VARIETY - Levels start to get a little more different and unique which adds a lot of flavor to the game. Ultimately though on enough time, this starts to matter less and less as you keep running through it.BFG - Feels damn good to be blasting enemies.LEARNING IS REWARDING - I can most definitely say once you learn the enemy varieties, the guns and their alternate firing, how to master grappling hook and move around the fighting platforms, you start to get really used to and good at the game. This feeling (Without being handed you a complete blue print on how to play) can be really rewarding in itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:There's a lot of things I like about this game.  Procedurally generated maps especially and random stat weapons is a rarity in an FPS and I'm a sucker for old school shooters.  I really like the mini games and arenas that give me an alternate activity to do.  In true rogue-ish form you have bad runs and you have god runs I've had some high highs in the weapon lottery!Cons:I suspect I'm most of the way through now and its only towards the end I'm getting a bit of repetition fatigue.------Closing thoughts:I'm happy to support unusual roguelites, I've not come across an FPS variant so far so that was novel, definitely would like to see more.   The story tackles mental health problems, specifically early trauma leading to mood/personality disorders in a plausible manner so respect for that.  Whether I'd recommend it for you is very much tied up in how much you like old school shooters, how much you care about graphics and RNG.

_childDocuments_.review: So I haven't beaten this game yet, but I have played it a lot. Like... a lot.It's real good. I'm not sure how I'd classify the game, but something something "kinda like a loot shoot" and "kinda like a roguelite"Basically: You go to sleep, enter a nightmare, and as you kill enemies, break ♥♥♥♥, and so on, you get Weapons. Weapons have random stats. There's also tier 1-3 weapons. You can use any of these weapons, but you are only allowed to keep one (two, much, much later down the line.) to take with you to the next level. Dying doesn't have a /huge/ consequence. It's just a timeset back, ultimately. You don't get to move forward, it resets the level and you don't get to sell any weapons. Maybe a hot take, but you know what? I like the fact that dying in this game doesn't set me back MASSIVELY. It's why a lot of roguelites honestly don't go down well with me at all. Generally, I just think this game is a blast. A lot of the guns are fun to use, it's always fun to see a new high tier weapon and go "What the ♥♥♥♥ is this?" and proceed to shred EVERYTHING in front of you, followed shortly by a wistful feeling as you have to wave the weapon goodbye until you can get the upgrade that lets you take higher tier weapons. And when you do get to tier 3, all the weapons just end up incredibly silly.How about a minigun that makes you prone when aiming, but just makes you wanna yell "I'M F***ING INVINCIBLE!" while you shred everything with explosive munitions? Or a funny metal "Infernal Rod" that just rains exploding rocks from above, capable of wiping rooms clean in seconds?So, I think for about half way through the game the levels are.. "Randomly" generated to a point. Like the tile generation, I guess? "Here's a bunch of rooms the dev has made, tiles, and now the game glues them together in ways that attempt ot make sense". But something weird happened after that.I died at a point. Loaded back into the level and said"Wait... the level didn't change. Are the levels predetermined now?" Yeah! I think they're still randomly generated, to a point. But yknow.Okay, so I mentioned "going to sleep"Basically, the Protag is in an Asylum, for whatever reason. All we know is "She did something bad, really bad, and her life was kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up."As time goes on, weird stuff starts happening in the Asylum. Doors open, keys are left in places. The documents on your table start seeming.. less like the doctor is talking to you, and something else is going on. It's neat.The enemies aren't too bad, either? There's only a few that really annoy me. Mostly flying enemies, actually. Or enemies that teleport. I thought I'd hate the guy that summons skeletons until it dies, but no! Not a problem. What I actually hate is the four legged spider robot that launches missiles at you. Or the flying guys that spit acid and explode into acid on death. Or the annoying jumpy boys that launch pink explody things at you. And when they die, they explode and launchy pink explody boys at you. Or the ghost guys that teleport behind you and leave shock orbs in their place that prevent you from shooting sometimes.I also mentioned an upgrade system. Okay, so, first things first. Do you like minigames? Do you like playing minigames to get upgrades? If no, go to options and disable the minigames you don't want. It just lets you buy upgrades without partaking in the minigame.Otherwise, there's 3 minigames. A platformer, a pokemon like game (which I honestly do not care for) and a side scrolling shoot.THere's 3 currencies for each one. The platformer just uses gold coins. The pokemon one, Amber (you get 100 a level.) and the side scrolling shoot uses Jade. Jade is acquired from doing the endless missions. My problem is that it feels kinda hard to get Amber and Jade? it takes awhile to get amber (which, understandable, you get Pills from the Amber tree and it makes the game harder in exchange for modifiers like more money, etc)Jade? I'm not really sure how you're MEANT to get large amoutns. From whta I could tell, money multipliers don't apply to jade and I'm at the point where it takes like... 30 minutes of endless to get one expensive upgrade. That being said, though, I honestly think this game is pretty easy even without Jade/Amber skills. Jade also gives you pets that you gotta buy skills. Don't like secret hunting? Get yourself the treasure pet. It points out breakable walls for you. A godsend.For the last bit of this, I want to let you know Andrew Hulshult did the soundtrack for Nightmare Reaper.is it good? I mean, has Andrew put out anything that wasn't a total banger as of late? Yeah it's good, why are we asking?

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is an excellent Roguelite Boomer Shooter Looter Shooter that hits all the right spots for the serotonin to kick in. There are small issues with it but are fairly minor when the action gets going.Your playthrough usually won't be the same as some else's playthrough, a level or two might be the same for continuity sake or for teaching something to you but other than that we've got some real random levels that are always able to be finished from beginning to end. Eventually some of these levels will lend itself well to some nice movement mechanics to get around easier.The movement is solid, not too floaty and not too slow, you'll move at a nice pace to get through levels and to get over obstacles in reasonable time. Eventually over the course of the game you will unlock dashing and grappling hook. The grappling hook is very nice since it both acts as a thruster from point A to point B, but if you use your movement keys you can swing around the point instead it's real nice, though only some levels are big enough to take advantage of that in the early game but late game you will get some open levels to swing around in.There are a LOT of weapons in this game, you will experience far less boredom after the first few early levels, I know that's quite a silly claim but there are a LOT of levels in the game, so much so it took me over 23 hours to get through and from my memory I didn't start getting most of the level 2 weapons around 7 hours, and the level 3 weapons around 15 hours in.The weapons are the primary reason to be stuck on this game, you don't know you needed a giant burst fire Howitzer, or infinite magazine Bazooka that shoots fireballs, or even a sawed off shotgun that fires sawblades. There are far more crazy combos to stumble on, just when you think a weapon can't get enhanced you will be pleasantly surprised.And if you're ever bored of shooting for a while, take a look at the minigames you get to play once you start unlocking new cartridges. They will not only spice up your gameplay but also have a challenge of their own, at least 3 minigames carts exist for you to play it's always a nice change of pace when you need to cooldown from fast paced shooting.So the issues I mention really stem from random generation slowing the level pacing down significantly, certain levers and switches may control doors far from the location they appear at though it doesn't happen too much but can be a little annoying have to backtrack. There are VERY few platforming levels in this game, but they are quite annoying without the grappling hook and double jump, get through them and you'll never see them again. Aside from that, I can't honestly think of anything else besides performance issues, which just happen in late game arena due to the sheer volume of things in a small space.Overall solid 8/10, no doubt in my mind. Completion of the game isn't the worst thing either, earning achievements grants currency in-game and aren't excessively annoying to get you will naturally earn them over the course of the game instead of being forced to lookup guides on how to do things properly. There's also plenty of silly secrets to find and they can have something really silly in them on occasion.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a ton of Rogues and R-lites, they comprise most of my steam library and game library at large.While this game has some assuredly rough edges, it has the IT factor.While stuff like stone soup, nethack, dredmor, ♥♥♥ Cogmind and ADOM are my typical fare, this game obliterates my admittedly lowered expectations of crossover R-lites. The combat is the star, if you've played Brutal Doom Rise of the Triad or Blood, you know what you're in for.Fast paced high lethality low ttk shooting that encourages, nearly requires reaching a flowstate to survive, The loot aspect actually serves to match the old FPS vibe in a way that STRAFE Gungeon and Nuclear Throne do not, as you continuously swap weapons, some intentionally (i think) disposable, giving you a John Woo feeling as you blaze into a room dumping carts, switching weapons, then swapping them with the quick menu to burn an ammo type you had in stock, or pulling out a melee weapon, then switching back after you've plied ammo from corpses. If you were a fan of those arsenal shooters you'll find an overwhelming amount of variety here that's tons of fun to play with.As for flaws in this early access state, the music is great but could use variety, some melee weapons aren't great but at least they don't cost ammo, even if they feel a lil less thought out. The first two biomes are a bit too similar but they are still fun and have interesting verticality to spice up the combat options. Lastly, I would like a bit more enemy variety, what's there already covers most of the bases, and perhaps I just want more pixelated abominations to deconstruct in more ways.Summarized I guess those arent really flaws, being my only desire is more of it, as the games early access still, and this game faaar outscopes most E-limbo fodder.No politicizing no obtrusive tutorials no meaningless padding, the game is lean , mean, and respects the player and their time.Don't let the emotionally frayed female protagonist put you off, this game is still pure, unbridled, testosterone.Great job! Don't leave us hanging for too long (cough cough wizard of legend cough cough) because you've created something truly special here, last time I was this pumped about a game, it was Enter the Gungeon, and I would argue that this combat is far more engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an underrated gem.I've recently been playing through some boomer shooters that I got in a bundle a while back, and had a blast with Dusk and Amid Evil, so started browsing around for something else to try.  I saw this mentioned by a few people as a good release from this year so jumped in.For the genre, a single run of this game takes a while, 25 hours or so for me.  The stages are randomly generated within a tile set, and generally are broken into three parts, before moving on to the next tile set.  You have basic puzzles involving coloured key cards and the like, but they rarely get in the way of the combat.  You move along, upgrading your character with coins that you earn along the way, and shoot the crap out of everything with a massively varied arsenal.The guns are also randomly generated in a sort of Borderlands style, and you can get some really silly and powerful options. For negatives, I would have liked to have had access to the ability to keep two guns at the end of the stage rather than one that you start out with much earlier.  In fact, I unlocked that one stage before the final boss, so for the first run it has been useless.  That said, there is a NG+ feature which I will be immediately jumping into so I suppose it will get some use at least.There are plenty of other things I could nitpick, and lots of great features I've not mentioned, but I really recommend just jumping in and trying things out.  There are a lot of neat surprises along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something else! It initially starts off a bit tough and slow to be honest. The first 2 to 4 hours feel like a typical lite horror FPS with interesting guns. However -- once you start unlocking more of the systems, weapons, upgrades etc, it starts to get WILD!!!It's insanely addicting. I can't stop playing it. The movement is crazy cool -- you get a grapple hook and they don't put 10million restrictions like most games. it can go as far as you want, you can hold it and hang as long as you want, there's no cooldown except for the retract speed which is REALLY fast. They have really awesome dashing too which can slow time. The guns....omfg the guns are so cool. Also there's a LOT of melee options which I absolutely love. I wish there were more melee first person games. The great thing is that even with how much the blank guns have personality, the stats can make them hyper unique. I had a shotgun that shot 2 foot long shurrikans instead of pellets and it was full auto so I could plaster a boss with literally hundreds of shurikans that would explode all over the map when the monster died. I also got a fun staff which had 700% knockback and 50% attack rate. I could hold up a boss in a corner like a bully, it was indeed fun. Then I sold it for a button of money to afford more innate skills from the skill tree. HUGE TIP: YOU CAN TURN OFF THE MINIGAMES FOR THE SKILL TREE -- I HIGHLY RECOMMEND TURNING OFF THE MINI GAMES FOR THE SKILL TREE. I haven't made it there yet but apparently there's a well made NG+ which offers loads of replayability. There's a youtuber who is on NG+10 and gets some pretty crazy weapons!Buy this game

_childDocuments_.review: Not enough meat on the bone.Nightmare Reaper is at first a cathartic fast-paced gorefest with good movement and cool, strong weapons. But it lost it's charm pretty quick for me. I hate being pretentious, and I recognize that this is a beloved game that the developers did a quality job with, but I'll still explain what I personally dislike anyways. Not saying the game is objectively bad, it's just not for everybody. Even those who enjoy the genre.Most of your time is spent with a shockingly slow trod through not-so enjoyable procedurally generated levels. Many of the levels feel exactly the same as each other, with the only differences being aesthetic. While some specific rooms are unique in the platform challenges they give you, they're never really incorporated into the gunfights you have to deal with, so you're left with an arbitrary way of adding "uniqueness" to different locations. These "challenges" aren't really challenging, and are even repetitive in of themselves.On top of that, for a looter shooter, you don't get to loot that much. You're only allowed to keep 1 weapon between levels, highly encouraging you to find something effective for your playstyle and never let go of it. I didn't do this because I was actively looking for new things, but repeats began popping up *very* quick. My gameplay would also be most effective if I just stuck to my favorite gun. There's no benefit to switching it up, and you have no leniency with even just a single "backpack" gun. And even if this were able to be changed in future upgrades (that I didn't come across)...The upgrade system is also pretty arbitrary and flow-ruining. Instead of choosing an upgrade from a skill tree, you instead play through Super Mario Bros. 3-esque levels to obtain upgrades, all through a pause menu (challenging the levels still costs money). This is a cute idea, but the charm of the gimmick does NOT have any staying power. Not only are the levels wildly easy to beat, you are able to challenge them nearly right after you did the last ones since you gain money at ludicrous speeds, and they aren't particularly short to play through. This almost forces a choice between ignoring them and staying weaker for a while, or do them and stop playing the "actual" game for an annoying amount of time.I wish Nightmare Reaper was streamlined to be more friendly with the time you give it. It's so frustrating to finish a shooter level just to go do some off-topic platformer bits for 5 minutes, knowing that when you get done with THAT, you'll be rinsing and repeating the same exact gameplay loop with the single gun you're allowed to keep.ADDENDUM: I gave the game a few more levels after turning off the minigames at the developers request, and while doing so does help with keeping the natural momentum of the game stable, I still stand by my other gripes (and wish the option to turn off minigames was made more obvious in the first place).Just to re-clarify from the beginning: I think the game deserves the positive attention it has gotten. It's objectively pretty good at the lowest bar. I just found myself personally disappointed with my purchase and time spent with the game, and wanted to point out the reasons why in case anybody was on the fence for buying the game and needed some subjective negative opinions.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a neutral or mixed review instead of a negative one, as there are multiple reasons why you should(n't) purchase this game. I only purchased this game because Andrew Hulshult created this soundtrack, and the soundtrack is high in quality. After playing DUSK (made by David Szymanski), I have found it hard to find another boomer shooter game of the same quality. Unfortunately, while this game puts lots of effort into weapons, enemies, music, and graphic design, Nightmare Reaper lacks replayability & compelling level design. This is a noticeable flaw, as each level begins to feel generic and loses appeal as the game progresses. Introducing a random-level generator has awkwardly cheapened the game's feeling, as levels do not feel carefully crafted - instead replaced with a visual theme for each set of levels. There is a considerable amount of focus put into areas where there probably should be none, and these efforts should be placed in balancing, careful level design (which you can do a lot with), and creating more exciting scenarios (actual unique bosses, for instance). There was lots of effort put into minigames - which I hated. While the idea of introducing minigames is not necessarily a bad idea, these minigames were annoying for a variety of reasons: they felt forced, they were intrusive in a way that required me to spend time playing a different game than a game I actually wanted to play and were not always super short (hence the term, mini), and they were not even games that were like the original game (you play retro minigames, such as Mario & Pokemon). Moreover, these minigames were required to improve your character, and there are many levels inside of them (which shows that the developers clearly put effort into Nightmare Reaper, but it felt wasted on the wrong things). If minigames were not bad enough, there are also annoying puzzle rooms on many levels, which are randomly generated that you should skip each time (as the reward is never worth the time spent). Personally, I didn't care for many of the game's features/mechanics. From the outset of the game, I prefer to be able to switch between all weapons, keep all of the weapons I earned each level (or at least not give most of them away, even if I do receive a small sum for being forced to sell my weapons), and be heavily encouraged to use weapons for different occasions. Using one or two weapons throughout my entire playthrough was possible, as there was a lack of balance/lack of incentive to use other weapons. While there were many weapons, finding random weapons at each level and still mainly using the weapon I spawned with created a very generic experience. Some people will say, "You can just play the game using different weapons throughout the level; no one is forcing you to play that way." While that is true, the player should feel encouraged to use different weapons in different situations rather than pretend to feel a false sense of pressure to use each weapon that spawns throughout a level. Also, many negative reviews focus on a story, which I found interesting, as I wasn't really disappointed that there was a lack of a story. While it felt cheap, the story aspect is not really the main concern of a boomer-shooter, imo. The gameplay itself had issues, so it wasn't a concern to me as much while playing (though it would be nice to have the story be told more creatively (I appreciated some of the weapons playing into her mental state)).T;Dr, This game is a good game for an on-sale price. While the developer clearly spent lots of effort on the game (especially in areas that were weak/not-needed), it loses lots of appeal after playing for a few hours. The first hour is fun as you progress, but the issues become glaring. I doubt that updates can fix most of these issues, as the game was designed this way, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: I now have over 40 hours into this game, so I suppose it is time to review.Nightmare Reaper is also a game that I just HAFT to compare with Deadlink. Why is that? Because I feel like this game does a better job at being a roguelite boomer shooter than Deadlink does, but on the other hand the combat in Deadlink is much more advanced, fast paced and intense, and also gives you the option to play 4 different classes.But if what you REALLY WANT is a ROGUELITE boomer shooter specifically, then I will recommed Nightmare Reaper over Deadlink any day for various reasons. One is that that this game has way more areas and sections than just the 4 ones in Deadlink, which get extremely repetetive quite quickly. Another is that this game drops guns, loot and have interresting events that occur during every level. The few ones Deadlink have here actually kinda suck NGL. Nightmare Reaper has mini-games that are mandatory for upgrading your player, cool mechanics in terms of pill-slots that affect your character both in a positive and negative way. The game has RPG elements and crafting taking straight out of such games, and even features an easter egg for Diablo 2, which totally makes sense. You are constantly trying to upgrade or find a perfect weapon for you and your playstyle, and then rerolling the stats when you get the option to do so during the main levels.The combat still holds up decently. The whole loop of the Andrew Hulshult soundtrack kicking in mixed with the combo meter and explosions from elite enemies is pretty good. You also have a hook to launch you forward and various other movement abilities that keep the game feeling intense and fast despite the of the roguelite nature. The survival arenas for farming Jade do make for a fun arena, but I still have yet to see a boomer shooter that has a better survial mode than Herald of Havoc. The good thing about this one is that you always get rewarded with currency on completing rounds in these arenas.As a Roguelite boomer shooter specifically, Nightmare Reaper is probably the best one out there! If what you are looking for is more about good combat and cool abilities, then you may consider Deadlink instead. I just dont think Deadlink managed to implement the roguelite mechanics that well compared to this game. Note that I DO NOT hate Deadlink at all. The key difference is that this game excels at replay value and has an addicting system with the roguelite mechanics, random level generation etc etc. Deadlink simply fails at replay value compared to Nightmare Reaper imo, but of course Deadlink has great combat.As there seem to be rumours about a Nightmare Reaper 2, my recommendation for that would be to make the COMBAT itself more interresting. The atmosphere, levels, roguelite mechanics and addicting gameplay loop are totally there, but it would make perfect sense for a Nightmare Reaper 2 to have much more refined combat than its predecessor while keeping all the interresting roguelite mechanics. If this game had as intense combat as Deadlink while keeping everything in the roguelite formula it would be one of the best video games ever created imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Fugly but exhilarating. Fast paced combat, tons of enemies, even more gore. Stars of the show - guns. Absolutely unsurpassable. They look about like Doom guns, so at first I wasn't expecting much out of flat sprites, but they all are at least as good as doom (I mean, who can beat the daddy super shotgun?) and at most - delightfully better. Animations, sounds - all perfect, every weapon is joy to use. This is worth picking up just for guns.One important thing to notice - structure of this game. I think most people would think this is your usual rogue lite - random levels, random loot, either endless levels or some course of stages with a boss at the end, after every death you start from scratch, some long term progression, and etc. NR is almost like that. There is  an actual campaign to beat. You still go through random levels but they are always themed to the episode of campaign you are at and when you die you don't start all over again but just repeat this level. The other thing - you don't start level from scratch per se, there's no crappy basic starting gun - you get to keep 1 weapon at the end of each level and it can be pretty good. You don't get the BEST (level 3) stuff but you can carry some well rolled legendary level 1-2 weapon through the enterity of the campaign and it will carry you through the enterity of the campaign. And that's just 2 big things I wanted to notice, there are more interesting twists up this games sleeve. Amount of content is very much immodest. Took me 20 hours to beat current 2 acts and by the end I still was finding a new gun ocasionally. And of course - music is by Andrew Hulshul. Do I need to say anything else?

_childDocuments_.review: I watched a friend play this some time ago and told myself I'd pick it up at some point. _childDocuments_.review: Best boomer shooter I've played in years. I liked it more than Ion Fury! Nightmare Reaper is a visually captivating game that combines retro aesthetics with modern design elements. The graphics are a unique blend of nostalgic pixel art and contemporary lighting and shading techniques, creating a visually striking and immersive experience. The enemy designs are creatively crafted, with over-the-top monsters that are sure to give players a run for their money.The real highlight of Nightmare Reaper is the extensive weapon customization system, offering players a staggering number of ways to modify their arsenal. With over 1000 weapon modifications available, players can create their own unique playstyle and tackle the hordes of enemies in a variety of creative ways. The intense action is complemented by an atmospheric and fitting soundtrack by Andrew Hulshult, adding to the overall immersive experience.In addition to the thrilling gameplay and weapon customization, Nightmare Reaper offers players secrets to uncover, mini-games that act as skill trees, and an arena mode for added replayability. The game presents a challenging and dynamic experience, keeping players engaged and on their toes as they navigate through the nightmarish levels.If you're a fan of fast-paced, retro-inspired shooters with modern twists and a wide array of weapon customization options, Nightmare Reaper is worth checking out. It's a game that offers a visually captivating and action-packed experience with plenty of replay value for those who are up for the challenge.I'm tossed as to rather I'd give it a 9/10 or 10/10 in terms of boomer shooters -- either way, I'd recommend not missing this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Nightmare Reaper

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, games that try to do things as "out there" as "FPS with proc-gen levels, a skill tree that uses a rudimentary NES-esque platformer as a basis, and legitimately unsettling background lore" don't end up being very good. Nightmare Reaper owns.You are in what seem to be the nightmares of a hospitalized young woman, and she has to shoot her way out. Each nightmare has its own traps and enemies, as well as treasure. Additionally, you can find weapons in various chests, opened with a quick melee punch. These weapons can have bonuses like a loot shooter, and can be color coded for rarity, but that's where the similarities end. You won't be worrying about a gear score, or building a character here.At the end of each level, you can save one of your found weapons to carry along with you. You then wake up, and use your fake Game Boy to spend your treasure on skills. These follow a map system like Super Mario Brothers 3, with each short stage (maybe 2 or 3 screens at the most) requiring very simple platforming. Once you finish the platforming, you unlock whatever skill the stage corresponds to. Early on, these are things like bonus ammo on pick-up, but later it grows to be things like "Dash by pressing Shift", and other more substantial things.Each completed nightmare also adds a page of notes to the woman's room. These tell the tale of how she got where she is, and are....not pleasant. While not professional writing, they are intriguing enough to incentivize the player to keep going.As players progress through the nightmares, things become increasingly, well, nightmarish, in both the hospital and in the main characters sleep. Without going into detail, what starts as a safe haven quickly stops feeling as such. As for the core game, red orbs will start spawning at random, and can cause various effects to take place. These can range from making a room low gravity, to a jump-scare style version of the main characters face roaming the room, attacking on sight. Nightmare Reaper is a chaotic mess of a game, and it's because of this that I enjoy it so much. The weapons quickly become both very cool and very silly, and the wide variety of them keep me playing. It might not be smart to try using a grenade launcher as my starting weapon, but hey, why not? A magic book that shoots lightning bolts? Seems like a good secondary. A chainsaw with a grappling hook? I think we've got a loadout.Make no mistake, this game is definitely a work in progress. The dual wield power up can mix with the Nightmare Reaper powerup and give you four arms, graphically. Sometimes the level generation makes the exit a bit of a pain to find. There are kinks to work out. The maniacal laughter of a tortured soul busting out whenever you gib 30 tumorous masses of flesh in a single explosion makes up for this.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't enjoyed a game this much in years! Out of all the games in my library I think it reminds me most of 'They Bleed Pixels'. The ludicrous gibs, the tortured female protagonist and the simplified graphics.Don't get me wrong though, I saw the basic looking screenshots and ramped all the game's settings up to max. To my surprise my machine ran like dog poo, so had to tone it all down a bit. Give the dev a break though as this is early access right now. Just turn down the res, turn off vsync and dynamic shadows and this will run just fine.The enemies can get overwhelming and if you're not careful and you don't have the correct pickup or weapon, death will come quite easily and you'll have to do the level again from scratch. Pretty annoying right? Nope - the entire level will have changed and your next play-through will be totally different. It's not a chore, but something you can happily do again and again. Each level will have different weapons (tons of them), new secrets to discover and a totally new layout. A new twist in this game is that you only get to keep one weapon between each level. So which weapon do I keep? The flame spell? The bazooka? The shotgun? Nope, the simple pistol. This play-though the pistol I have collected has life leech traits and sets enemies on fire. So check each weapon as you pick it up and you might be pleasantly suprised!As Gmanlives recommended this, I thought it'd be worth my time. I wasn't wrong. Please support the devs as this game needs your attention now!

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect blend of Retro FPS and RogueliteNightmare Reaper is a Retro FPS game featuring Rougelite elements, 90 degree walls, and lots and lots of treasure. Developed by Blazing Bit Games, This game recently came out of Early Access after a extremely successful Early Access run with 3 full chapters, a bazillajillion different weapons, and tons of enemies to turn into goop. While one might suspect that it being a rougelite with all the levels being randomly generated that the gameplay would get stale fast like a lot of indie rougelites unfortunately fall in but lucky Nightmare Reaper avoids such a fate for the most part.Gameplay of Nightmare Reaper at it's core is very much like the classic games that inspire it.  You move, shoot and kill everything in sight. Each level is constructed with predefined rooms with a start and a ending meaning you're actively reaching for a goal rather than it being a infinte-esque journey. You gain weaponry at random either from enemy drops or crates and this is where one of the prime rougelite elements comes into play as you're able gain random stats on your weapons which tiers them as well as well as weapons being classified in level from one to three. As a lot of these weapons get handed out like candy you're only able to carry a single level 1 weapon to the next level, sounds bad right? Well thankfully there's a full blown skill tree, actually there's 3 full skill trees that you can use to improve your character with the coin and treasure you collect from killing enemies and secret finding. With all of this combined you can get some seriously ridiculous weapons on top of very useful skills; you even get a grappling hook as well! You can even find a variety of powerups that also increase the absolute carnage you can deal. Yet despite all this the game still has it's difficultly with mega enemies with a single increased stat or random events that can shift the entire gravity, spawn a ton of barrels, or a merchant and a plethora of other options. Speaking of the Skill Trees would it surprise you that each one is their own minigame. The Default one is a platformer, the Jade is a space shoot-em up and the Topaz is a entire Pokemon-esque RPG. While you pay for the Default via the vast amount of coin you horde and the Topaz that you earn at the end of levels. Where do you get the Jade? Well Nightmare Reaper has enemy arenas that you find in the hospital you start the game in. Each provide a increasingly difficult wave of enemies and since it provides Jade instead of coin it's very much worth your time to battle in them.Style wise, Nightmare Reaper very much feels like a Wolfenstein Game with Rise of the Triad style of levels featuring those 90 Degree Walls, Height Variation and sightly more cartoony graphics. More so Rise of the Triad with the ludcious amount of blood and guts that fly everywhere. The game also provides such good atmosphere with it's lighting, sound design, and overall aesthetics. Although, I do not like the silent jumpscares in the Hospital, while I am thankful that they're silent they pretty much are more annoying than being scary. (Same with the Ghost Head random event)Overall, Nightmare Reaper is a fantastic Retro FPS game that blend classic elements with new ones to create a near perfect gameplay loop. While the randomness might turn away people the fact the levels are short encourages you to simply jump back in for another run. Plus if this much content wasn't enough you even have New Game+ to blaze through the game again with all your skills and the entire enemy roaster. For a game that started in Early Access is pleasing to see the game fully released and praised for it's shooting goodness.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper: MY EYES, THE GOGGLES DO NOTHING.In the realm of boomer shooters, I expected something like Nightmare Reaper to happen EVENTUALLY. With how the genre basically either embraces some older game or improves on a formula, and with the ready amount of kitbashing, someone WOULD do the randomly generated one. We saw it with Shadow Warrior 2 and 3 and we didn't like it there. So there's been an uphill battle of sorts. Nightmare Reaper puts a lot of things against itself. Randomly generated, looter shooter, boomer shooter, there's too many sales taglines here. The game feels like a marketing guy trying to make the most 2018~ era game possible. In a company's hands that'd be a problem, just look at the last few Borderlands. In the hands of Blazing Bit?It's a terrifying concept.Nightmare Reaper is a game that arguably knows the limitations it's hoisted on itself. It knows random generation's a gamble in any game, let alone one where you're supposed to be bouncing around the ceiling. As some counterbalance, it stuffs itself with enough side features to make up the gaps. Silly weapons, silly skill sets, and RNGesus that's loose enough to KINDA let you have fun. Sure it's a boomer shooter on flat-ish mostly cubic levels, you know that. And then you get into the weird extra movement mechanics that are both odd and horrifically fun. You start feeling the strange power creep as you bash different stats and skills together and find the thing that works. And that's what salvages this game, in my opinion.Any lesser game would try to stop you or prevent RNG from giving you some silly benefits. Because they don't want you to push the limits of what the game can handle. Nightmare Reaper doesn't have that. When it says randomly generated looter shooter, it means it. You can find some of the most hilariously overpowered weapons in here, scrunched up with some piddly poodle shooters. It takes one dumb stat bonus to make the average minigun into an overclocked death machine that turns anything that isn't a boss monster into paste, and when you acquire that weapon, all bets are off. The game entirely changes the minute you find the most busted weapon in the game. I have no idea what psychological monster in this woman's mind conjured said minigun with Overload, but I thank you because it made the boss fight for Act 2 last around a minute.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. It's a sorta Rogue lite FPS.If you like Heavy Bullets and similar, you will like Nightmare Reaper as well.It's rare to see such a well polished game TBH.There are tons of secrets, the random map generation doesn't get old since they have pre-made lots of rooms, the story is interesting, and the game loop amazing.Don't be put off by the graphics.It took me about 50 or 60 hours to finish the game once.Yeah, my time on Steam doesn't reflect that, since I was.. uh, playing at a friends house for the most part... right. Yeah. Anyway.Ended up buying my own copy because this game deserves it.So it goes like this:- When you sleep a random dungeon is generated- Reach the end portal to complete the dungeon- Kill everything for additional bonus- Find all the loot for more moneyThen, the money can be spent to buy permanent upgrades. These upgrades last forver.If you die in a dungeon, you wake up. No money is lost. No upgrades are lost.Just sleep again and try your luck again.And can pick up some random looted weapons. These weapons have random stats.Once a dungeon is completed, you can keep only one weapon for the next run.But you need to unlock this ability.This means that the begining of the game, you will mostly try out all kinds of weapons.And you will decide what your play style is, and stick with a main weapon most likely.And that's it! There's about 90 levels.When you complete the game... there's more.This is an extremely addictive game. I didn't even cover the mini games which get you the upgrades, or the Arena which is a special game mode you can unlock.Or the massive amount of options in the game. From graphics, to playstyle, to rebinds.Everything you could want is in there.Also the music is great, most are okayish and a couple tracks I really love.Trust me when I say that $20 is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper scratches a lot of itches. The game is difficult like a good roguelite should be. The increasing difficulty can always be mitigated both by roguelite reward elements as well as the player's own skill. The only time the game feels "unfair" is when the player intentionally puts themselves at a disadvantage in an attempt to get even more rewards.LIKES- Great weapon variety that affords many playstyles- Plenty of weapon attributes that really hammer home the roguelite charm- Progression/introduction of game mechanics is well-paced, complemented by a competent New Game + system- The hospital and the associated backstory offer great atmosphere without trying too hard- Headshot slo-mo kills rockDISLIKES- The Jade handheld skill tree is monotonous, both in getting jade through the arena and the actual skill tree gameplay itself. I wish I didn't have to play arena as much.- Some outdoor maps have a lot of invisible walls that try to keep the player on a somewhat guided path, but this ends up being clunky and inconsistentMy criticisms are specific and limited, so they are definitely outweighed by my love of many aspects of the overall gameplay. I strongly recommend Nightmare Reaper.

Use that money (goldpieces) to spend on skill points to get better each time you die and retry with a bit more advantage. The levels change after every reload and gives replayability, even though the theme of the level stays the same until you will pass them, The HUB area is a special place, without spoiling i would say it is a peacefull place to get your thoughts together. You spend skillpoints anytime you want by going to the menu and playing a cute little platformer game which also provides extra gold coins on itself, to master the platforms and earn the right to spend the skill point. It is a game in game. Nice little bonus if you ask me, i love that throwback gameplay of platformers! Then be ready for some more action, with enough variety in weapons and enemies this game really keeps you on the edge of your seat. One of the better FPS games. Plays like a nightmare (pun intended) and is worth every penny! Can't wait to see what this developer got for us in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY: A reto RPS/RPG that headily mixes retro shooting, bits of horror and psychology, and clever game mechanics into something truly unique.  Battle your demons in nightmares, unlock more of your past in a hospital, and level up using . . . a handheld video game?  Must-by for fans of RPSes and games with true creativity even in Early Access.Nightmare Reaper is a game that I ultimately describe as "The Suda 51 FPS that never was."  Like many Suda 51 games, it's a mix of love letter to games, psychological weirdness, atmosphere, and clever reuse of old game mechanics.    It's all about combining elements you love around interesting people.In this case the interesting person is you, a woman trapped in a hospital room.  Your surroundings give you clues to what's going on, but it's your nightmares where (most) of the game is.  Lie down in bed and enter a procedural nightmare realm where you find equipment, battle monsters, and solve puzzles in chunky retro FPS graphics, while listening to a grindy metal soundtrack.As you battle you'll recover weapons (many of which have extra randomized traits) and coins.  At the end of each level you get to keep one weapon, and then go back to the hospital.  If you die, no problem, you just wake up and have to do it again.Already this is a lot of fun, but the game takes it farther in immersive themes - your leveling up and management is done via a handheld game device.  Each character skill is unlocked with coins and playing a very light "Mario World" like game to get new skills.  It's a weird, perfect extra that helps keep you completely "in" the game.Its hard not to recommend the game as it's simply well-done, passionate, and clever.  However it is Early Access and it does need work:* Enemies are a mix of boring and overpowered.* Levels could use a bit more detail.* Weapon abilities aren't always clear.* Some levels have strange arrangements, unclear lighting, and other issues you see in procedural games.But these are issues of Early Access.Who's it for?  Pretty much if you love retro FPS games then just get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Proof that you shouldn't judge a book by its cover.Let us not sugar coat the dumpster-fire graphics. They’re awful, for about the first 10 seconds, because as soon as the game starts, you don’t care.The abysmal art-style was a strategic decision I’m sure, its not one I agree with, but it taught me an incredibly important lesson: You don’t need pretty things to make a good game, you need a good game.Nightmare Reaper is one of the coolest experiences I’ve ever had on a PC, and here are the reasons:PROS:- Gun-play is fast, reactive, frantic, but fair.- The loot system is carefully thought out, never leaves you overpowered, but is always satisfying.       1. Find weapons of varying quality,        2. Blast through the level and fall in love with them.       3. Sell all but one at the end of the map.- The weapons are inventive as hell, and there are a lot of them.- A mixture of handmade levels and procedural generation makes things identifiable, but never exactly the same on each run.- Interesting protagonist- Nice little RPG elements where you level up through a retro mini-game, it’s a refreshing take.- not a bad soundtrack, sound in general is done quite nicely for the style.- pays a lot of homage to retro games with easter-eggs and secrets everywhere.CONS:-	Art-style is clown vomit, but the game knows it.-	It can be a little tough sometimes to make out what you’re shooting at. Just turn off the bloom effect in settings.-	Um… -	Er…-	Nope, can’t think of anything else.It’s a good game, glad I got it.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightmare Reaper is a game that really feels like it's chasing its tail, as well as another example of why Steam should have review options other than do recommend or don't. It is game game full of good ideas, but the experience of playing it feels like those ideas are loosely tied together with string as opposed to forming a cohesive whole. What I mean by this is that, while individual mechanics are well executed, they rarely enhance each other when they come into contact and, in fact, often wind up detracting from one another instead.Here's a couple examples:There's a whole Hexen-esque array of cool melee weapons, each with a special alt-fire attack!...but the game quickly introduces enemies that explode on death and has to account for the possibility that you could have any combination of weapon types, which it does by giving you so much ammo of all types that running out is never a risk, making the melee weapons less than useless.You get a grappling hook about a third into the game that gives you more movement options!...but most arenas are pretty flat boxes, so you don't really need it outside of a few specific instances. Plus, you already have a dash that makes you invincible when you use it and is way easier to control, so why even bother?You get to play a fast-paced boomer-shooter!...but, due to being a rouge-lite, the levels are procedurally generated, so it lacks the clever enemy placement and unique layout that are some of the main appeals of the genre.Some of this might be more forgivable if the game were at least a reasonably tight experience, but the time it takes to get through is staggering, around twenty hours to the final boss, without much to show in the meantime. After the grappling hook, nothing about the game-play loop meaningfully changes, which means that the last two-thirds of the game are spent retreading the same ground over and over. Even the bosses are just regular enemy types with more health and a big red bar above them. Other than that, only one of the game's three skill trees gives you any new combat options, but they're doled out so agonizingly slow that by the time you get them you're not thinking "Wow! A cool new ability!" and instead thinking "Where was that ten hours ago when the game was getting stale?" And when you do go to buy new abilities, you have to play a little mini-game every time before they unlock, which makes the experience of powering up much more tedious and dampens the good feeling you get from finally being able to afford something you were waiting for.The mini-games themselves are, like many things in Nightmare Reaper, not bad, but superfluous, another thing that was put into the game just because and adds nothing to the rest of the experience, existing in its own little world. Honestly, if a sequel is ever made, the main thing I'd want out of it would be less content, with a greater focus on making the few interesting bits better, as it felt like this game was more fat than meat.All in, Nightmare Reaper is a game with a ton of cool ideas that come together to form something that is less than the sum of its parts. Nothing that stands out among the glut of FPS revival games, but nothing that bad either. I'd give it a 6/10, but the same game cut down to a third of the length could have easily been a 7 or an 8, which just adds to the frustration it gives me.

_childDocuments_.review: + As soon as you boot up the game, it goes straight to the point. No menu until you press the Escape key; you're straight into the hospital gown of the mentally-disturbed woman you play as. Once you press E on the bed, the game gets right to business— right to the nightmare. + To me, it's especially reminiscent (gameplay-wise) to DooM and Heretic, with the tiered, randomized weapons of Borderlands. It's the best of both kinds of shooters I like.+ There are little skills that you can get by collecting butt-loads of money and treasure throughout each level, all of which you have to unlock by playing a little Mario-like level. It's not too hard if you've played Mario before. + The neat little feature where you have to keep only one level 1 weapon after finishing a level. If you've got a legendary weapon of that level, it's even better. + A whole lotta Easter eggs and gags throughout, . + When you die, you keep the cash you collect from the level. + You can pet the dog in Nightmare Reaper.- Thanks partially to the procedurally-generated levels, the game doesn't really lend itself to creative secrets. All of them have you kick a cracked wall, some of which are either too easy or too hard to find, and none of which can be blown up with explosives like in Duke 3D or Blood, let alone this game's contemporary Dusk. - The game's only one episode long as of yet, due to being in early access. This sucks, because later in the  episode .- The protagonist's background of abuse and neglect (remarkably similar to a girl named Jeanie) can be a disconnect from the visceral carnage she causes in the gameplay. Overall, it's quite good, I like it. Gonna need some more episodes.
