_childDocuments_.review: Alright. No. I was really stoked to play this game, but no. I've only played for 90 minutes and I can't force myself to give this game any more time. I like the idea of a rogue-lite survival game where every run gives you more experience and supplies for your next run, but this is so poorly implemented/balanced that it's frustrating to play. I almost beat the game on my second run, was maybe literal minutes away but starved. Figured, okay, I can beat it on my third run --although that would mean the game is only an hour long, so lose/lose, I guess. Nah. Died in about ten minutes because there was nothing to eat, just had the worst luck. Also, I found a fishing rod and never came across a place to fish, despite deliberately traveling over the huge lake with a fish drawn on it every run. The RNG is wild. You really just have no control over what happens. I ain't playin that, sorry. Also, the story is insane. This lady really came out here with three bullets, one band-aid, a strip of wood for one single fire, and only enough food to last through lunch time just to... what? Embark on an extremely perilous journey to live in a house in the middle of nowhere? But why?? She literally drove out there in a van. She wasn't stranded or anything. Maybe just keep living where you already live and like, not starve to death or get attacked by bears?? Whatever. So anyway.Can you pet the dogs? Yes. Is the voice acting good? Yes. Did the MC over-narrate everything to the point that I set the dialogue volume to 0? Unfortunately, yes. Is the game beautiful to look at? Yes. Does it look just like The Long Dark and maybe you should just go play that instead because it's an infinitely better Alaskan wilderness survival game? Yes.

_childDocuments_.review: In principle, the game evokes positive emotions. This is really what I have been looking for for a long time, but after 30 attempts you already start to get nervous. Everything would be fine, learning from your mistakes is cool. BUT HOW CAN I INFLUENCE IF A BEAR JUST FLIES OUT ON ME AND I DIE? I can't even shoot! I have everything, resources are full, not far from home, but a bear runs out at me and all progress starts all over again. It's so stressful and all the taste and excitement of the game is lost! Maybe I'm just dumb, I don't know, maybe its a lag

_childDocuments_.review: If you love a cozy soundtrack, a gorgeous art style, fairly tense moments, and a semi-casual roguelite to tide you over, The Red Lantern is a solid choice. I say it's a semi-casual roguelite because - despite appearances - this game can be pretty difficult when luck decides you're not worthy, like many of the genre before it. However, the game is less traditionally skill based and more about what decisions you make with managing resources, meaning it's a lot more accessible to people who aren't great at games like Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon.That said, just because you can beat a run a fair bit easier than its ball-bustingly hard cousins - I only took 2.1 hours of attempts to reach the cabin - doesn't mean you can't have a good time. You're given plenty of reasons to go back out into the wilds once you've beaten the narrative; you can grab the dogs you didn't choose, each dog has their own story, etc. Oh, and if you were tentative like I was because you were worried about dog death --  Dogs will get hurt, but you see no graphical injuries, and nobody ever dies. And you can pet them repeatedly to make yourself feel better.All in all, give it a go. Especially at the 80% offer it's currently at (until 10th March). And always bring Stilton. Every dog is a good dog, but damn if Stilton isn't one of the best.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: First thing first: Press "C" and then wait when you need camping for food and rest!This game is for dog lovers.The game itself is about  dog sledding  in Alaska, the path is set but you get to choose to go left or right according to your location on the map. The highlight is the dogs are cute and you can watch them whenever you want. During the journey to your new home you get to pick all the dogs, pet them when taking a rest in a camp, encourage or comfort them, see how they react during incidents including chasing .However, keep in mind this is sort of a HARDCORE surviving game, reminds me of "This War of Mine '' as you really need to balance the resources carefully. Devs make sure players fail a couple of times before they know what action is proper, you need to balance the health and energy bar for both yourself and dogs, which can be tiring and many times I had to restrain the curiosity of checking on stuff to save energy so as to survive until I trigger some events to hunt meat, which is no fun and hinder the exploration. One mistake or unknown move may lead to a restart as manual save is supported.After 5 runs I finally reached the ending, more contents unlocked here including play ball-catching with dogs and dress dogs in new clothes. However the trip feels repeated after an hour of gameplay, but again the cute dogs win my heart, get it when it is on a major sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Red Lantern is one of those few games I encounter in life that feels hand designed for me, from the plot down to the atmosphere. Dog sledding across Alaska was always a childhood dream of mine, so when I realized the protagonist was trying to realize that dream in reconciliation of adulthood hardships it could not help but move me.Obviously this make for a deep bias towards the game, but I still think it makes for a nice experience for others. It is a bit buggy since the last update, and some things do not work as well since the original design was an infinite loop (not being able to pet Fin or do the story of any but the lead dog's in training runs for example), but if you are here for a light strategy rogue lite romp through the ice it will suit you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 6th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Exploring Alaska with doggos. If you like dogs, The Red Lantern may be the game for you.  The beginning of the game has players meet your character’s dog, Chomper.  From there you have to choose four more dogs to fill out your sled team from 9 or so stops that the player will make on the way to a sled.  Then the game officially begins with your character trying to get to the cabin with the red lantern.  This is a rogue-lite, with the main resources being your dog's hunger and your own.  The dog's hunger goes down as you ride on, and your hunger decreases when you explore. The problem is the game is more frustrating than interesting.  You’ll go through various scenarios, but eventually, you or your dogs will starve. The game is quite hard at first, but there are special actions that will be recorded in a journal, and that gives you more supplies at the beginning.  But with the initial supplies, it may be impossible to finish the game. That sounds like a normal rogue-lite  but the biggest problem is that on my second playthrough about half of the events were repeats from the original playthrough, and while this gave me a chance to try to fill in more of my journal, playing a third time would mean I’ve already found the optimal choices, and now was just repeating them because there’s not a lot of depth in most of these situations. Pick this up if you just want a game with dogs and sleds in Alaska, but I will caution people that the dogs in this game can get injured, though there is a big option in the menu to make it so dogs will always live.  Other than that, this is a really short game from what I hear, and on my second attempt, I was so close to finishing it.  Interesting concept but this needed a lot more content.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice game and the dogs are cute. It showed me the cutscene - without the voicelines of course - but no matter which button I pressed, the textbox did not close. Game didn't save, didn't recognize I reached the cabin, nothing. _childDocuments_.review: I've been meaning to get this game for a long time now. It was on Epic for the first year it came out, so I had to wait a little. Considering that it's now on sale (a little over € 10), I thought this was a good time to try it out.The art, environment and graphics are absolutely beautiful. In that way it's hard to not compare this game to the Long Dark (yes, there's auroras!), but it definitely manages to catch the same sorta vibe. Also, Ashly Burch is an amazing voice actress. At times I was worried that it was gonna sound awkward or forced, but it never did. I absolutely love her work. The writing isn't too bad - although there isn't really a "story" per se. It's more of a continuous self reflection of a woman trying to see what she's made of. And the interaction with the dogs is lovely!So why a bad review? The main problem with this game is that while it's story driven, the story itself is very short. I managed to complete the entire thing in less than 2 hours - and I definitely wasn't rushing through it. The whole story builds up to 'living in the wild' with your dogs, figuring out how to do and growing as a person. It starts with  That's the whole thing. Congrats, you've won the game. Imagine my surprise. There's a few things you can do after completing the game (which they've added later - I assume because people had the same criticism I have), but it's really just not that interesting because the story is already over.It's a shame because it definitely has potential, but it looks like the studio is working on a new game already and not actually updating this one anymore, besides bugfixing. I guess this is what to expect from studios with Epic deals.This is not worth € 10 and  not worth the full € 21. Though it's not really a "half-assed" game, it's just a very small game. I'd recommend it if you could get it for like € 5, otherwise it's not worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: The Red Lantern is a great casual game with an immersive, yet tragically short story. You play as a relatable woman, somewhat unsure of herself, who yearned for a practical challenge to alter her mundane (and failure-laden) life. Rather than scraping against the surmounting expectations that come with being a young adult today, she decides to take aim on the most raw requirements to sustain her own life, and that of her pups.Embark on a Walden-like foray into the Alaskan wilderness. By learning from quirky and imperfect sled-dogs that no one else wanted to adopt, the protagonist discovers aspects of her own self-confidence and value.Follow this one, or give it a try if you don't mind the brevity of one musher's quest for her own self-imposed survival. Suggestions:It would be wonderful to see more game-play options added. An ability to go inside of the cabin and decorate (or store food as a continued survival mode) would be a fantastic addition to the Alaskan wilderness, however there are no such options at the moment. Currently, if you finish the main story, you are still able to go on training runs with your adopted sled-dog team. There is the potential to play for a few hours, but after you complete the main plot and side stories, there is much to be desired from The Red Lantern.Even so, playing this game as it is offers a sweet experience that you won't regret.

The atmosphere was amazing and makes me a bit sad they didn't do more to invoke an emotional reaction out of me. I think it could have been an incredible journey if they had put more thought into the story.Also, DEVS PLEASE FIX THE ACHIEVEMENTS I WANNA GET THEM ALL THANK YOU

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard of this game briefly before I saw it on the Steam sale yesterday, but decided to take a leap of faith with it without much research. I can say that I'm glad I did. The Red Lantern has a bit of a learning curve that can be frustrating. Until you reach your destination at the end of your first true run, you can feel trapped repeating the same choices. The key is to let loose and take as many different routes as possible. Once you start gaining tools and learning how to ration your supplies, the game gets a LOT more fun. I love the art style. The clear Alaskan night sky is one of my favorite parts of the game. The dogs are distinctly different from each other and each bring something new to the table. You have the choice in the options menu to keep all the dogs alive if pet death is triggering for you, which I thought was a very nice touch. The tutorials are VERY fast, maybe a little too fast at times (it took me four runs and a guide on how to play this game on the switch for me to figure out the controls on my laptop with an xbox controller.) That being said, this game is controller compatible. I finished the main run in about two and a half hours of gameplay, but I still have many things in the journal to discover as well as the dogs' stories. I understand not wanting to spend the full price on this game just because it is so short, but if you are like me and happen to catch it on sale, it is absolutely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: The red lantern; You get to experience the life of an alaskan musher with her sledding team of 5. A woman who started with a lovely city husky, then vasks into a world of both glory and.. danger along the trail to your destination,, Known as the cabin. The genre feels oddly fitting for an adorable animal game. I'm an animal enthusiast myself -- But hunting is meant for the survival other than population control. It makes sense in a way that feels hard to explain. I'm not an experienced author or anything. Now let's end with my opinion to this game. Negatives first -- There could've atleast been multiple destinations & a bit more story. I ended the trail within only an hour.. Not much of a timekiller if you're looking for that other type of a game. Maybe more dogs, too? After you finish one story and get to the cabin.. all you can do is start over your trail and keep completing their stories. Once you complete EVERY story, i'm guessing all you can do is play with them, customize them and pet them.. And more hunting, getting to try out hunting can be fun and all but.. doing it so many times gets old. I moved onto another game so quickly due to the quick escalation of the story. Now for positives; The graphics are stupendously unique and the story feels unique although i said it was not very filled earlier. It reminds me of shelter; the models are just lovely and creative and it is also a survival game. Another thing is that my childhood youtuber, Seri, inspired me to play games like this. And the reality of it feels so cool. P.S You can pet the doggies !!  Anywho, if i could rate this game a " Mixed" Then i would. The positives and negatives explains it all. Another P.S, The musher says the s-word which explains the language warning & age rating. So don't play this if you're uncomfortable with the language

_childDocuments_.review: First of, this game is absolutely beautiful. The gameplay itself is entertaining, but only to a certain point and that point is finishing all the dog's stories. _childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much from this simple premise, but it has so much heart and is actually quite exciting. I can't name many other games that are thrilling, challenging, chill and heartwarming all at the same time - and as a dog lover, you really come to care for the dogs and their different personalities. It's a rogue-lite, which is very motivating after a hard run. I made it through the main story in 2.5 hours after finding some essentials (by chance?) that I can't imagine you can make it to the end without.I'm not normally an "adorable game" player, nor do I find any of the choices you must make "childish." The game is dedicated "to those who seek to find themselves" and some of those choices let you answer the question of "What kind of person am I vs. how desperately in need of food are we?" and it's truly unique. The voice acting is lovely too, and I can be rather critical of that usually.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for its adorable dogs, beautiful atmosphere and overall interesting idea to explore.However, I do not recommend this game if you are looking for something exciting with learning curve and rewarding experience, so if you are looking to play this once-twice per week to relax then I think it’ll work for you.The main issue I’d say is that the implementation of survival aspect and exploration-roguelite are bit conflicting here and paired with repetitive events leads to more boring than enjoyable result. Items that you find and keep for future runs are so impactful that you are sort of going into early runs with the idea to engage blindly with every event in order to find those items, die, repeat and once gathered enough you can breeze through survival aspect of this game with ease. What gives overall dull experience, since you are engaging with events because of possibility of finding item, not because of actual interest or survival aspect of the game, and you ignore the survival aspect of the game, because you know there is an item somewhere out there that will make your food 2x efficient, for example, so why bother, just engage with everything till you find it.There is other stuff, for example, questionable shooting mini-game, I guess they didn’t want this part of the game to feel too easy as “you just shot it and got food”, but at the same time they found out that rng based result would feel bad. However, I think implemented decision doesn’t benefit the game if compared to simple choice and result.Sometimes the choice is obscure and you don’t know what YOU will do, not how ENVIRONMENT will react, what's sort of weird as it doesn’t communicate properly YOUR actions and could lead to an end of a run.So, overall, you wanna pet a dog and relax from time to time? Then it’ll probably give you that.Other than that – look for other options.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the screenshots and gameplay trailer make it seem like the player has a lot more freedom of movement than they actually do. Almost everything is done via dialogue options, aside from the hunting and fishing, both of which involve very basic timing minigames. This didn’t affect my overall opinion, it’s just something I feel needs to be pointed out., and although my review may sound incredibly critical at times, I do lean somewhat on the positive side. I think it had the potential to be a pretty great game, but falls short due to the small amount of jank and sheer amount of grind needed for 100%.The first few runs are legitimately quite fun. You get to encounter all sorts of unique events as you interact with each of the dogs and try to figure out their individual stories, and it can honestly make for a pretty brutal survival experience. Your character can only sustain one injury without dying, and the choices you make in dangerous situations will often result in the end of your run. It can be a little irritating as certain progression mechanics are locked behind reaching the cabin for the first time, but roguelite mechanics are utilised to make subsequent runs easier, which is a fitting touch for a more story-focused title such as this. My first successful run came around the three hour mark, and I managed to finish three of a possible five dog stories during that run, which I was quite pleased with.After this point, the pace of the game rapidly declines. Once you reach the cabin for the first time, you’re allowed to go back and adopt the five other dogs you skipped at the start of the game, but only one at a time. In order to keep your newly adopted dog, you need to finish a run with them. This kind of sucks, but at least it gives you the opportunity to complete more dog stories along the way, right? Nope. After reaching the cabin, every run you do will have a head dog assigned, and the only story encounters you get will be from the head dog’s story. For me, this meant another six complete runs, but you’ll potentially have to do all nine depending on how many stories you skip on the way to the cabin for the first time. During these runs, you’ll no doubt run into the fire starter; a tool which persists through runs, removing an entire aspect of the game and making survival a complete joke. Seriously, I’ve died once since I found it and it was because I was paying more attention to Spaceballs playing on my second monitor than I was to actually playing the game.Once you have all the dog stories out of the way, you’ll probably still have a little cleanup to do. Coming in at a whopping 5.4% completion rate is the achievement for petting the dogs one hundred times at camp. Let me reiterate; petting the dogs one hundred times . That’s right, this achievement doesn’t work at the cabin where it can easily be automated. I know this for a fact because I measured the longest petting animation in the game and set an autoclicker to repeat for one hundred clicks without it popping, and this was after it had been indefinitely repeating for about fifteen minutes beforehand while I went to feed the cats. This means having to pet the dogs up to one hundred times in the middle of a run, and you have to do it manually because the camera resets after each action at the camp. I had to repeat this process forty-five times to get the achievement, and this was after the seven complete runs I needed to get the dog stories out of the way. It’s a total time-waster and one of the worst kinds of achievements in existence, but we’re still not done yet.Like many others, the very last achievement you’ll get in this game is the one for completing the journal. This achievement has a 1% completion rate, and from what I’ve read in the community forums, everyone who has it cheated. You get new journal entries by witnessing specific outcomes for specific events. These events are set to randomly occur, sometimes based on which dogs you have and which biome you’re in. The result is entirely based on your choices during the encounter; at least, that’s how it should be. In reality, some of the results are based on random chance; RNG within RNG. At the start, I was consistently getting journal entry after journal entry once I’d taken a look at the guide. It took me three hours to get it down to the last three entries, and another three hours to get it down to two. As of writing this, I have spent another seven and a half hours trying to get the last two entries with no luck. One is a random chance of encountering an ox who then has to charge at me. I saw this ox once every run for awhile, must’ve been more than ten times in a row, and he ran away from me every time. Haven’t seen him since. For the last encounter, I need to kill a squirrel, then find another squirrel later in the same run and let one of my dogs kill it. I’ve had this happen once in my entire nineteen hours of gameplay, and I accidentally clicked the wrong button, so I didn’t end up getting the journal entry. You know what the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up thing is? Those aren’t even the last two journal entries. Those are just the last two  journal entries. According to some datamining, there are still eleven journal entries which have yet to be discovered in the three years since release, and if that wasn’t bad enough, some of them are exclusive to dog stories which can’t be replayed after completion or so buggy that they don’t appear in the journal at all. So, even after all this extra grinding, unless an unlikely patch is released at some point in the near future, I’m afraid I’ll have to end up cheating in that achievement after all, because I know for a fact that two of my journal entries are gone for good. I think there’s potential for save editing as most of the save file is text-based, but someone will have to crack the small amount of raw data in each line to get it working properly.Now, onto something a bit lighter but still on the negative side of things; technical design. In my nineteen hours of play, I’ve consistently had a bug where audio cuts out for a second or two every few minutes, and the game has a few small issues with dynamic lighting, antialiasing, and render distance. Some shots can miss even though you hit the target dead centre with realigned ironsights, and some shots will land when they definitely should’ve missed, although this might be part of the strange RNG mechanics rather than a bug. Some dogs have obvious abilities (E.g. double food from traps, protection from wolves, etc.) whilst others seem to have none at all after their stories are completed, and the game could do with some QoL improvements; if I have Stilton on my team, it’s because I want double the meat from my traps. I shouldn’t have to scroll to select the option every time. Likewise, if I have the fire starter, I’m never going to use birch again, nor do I want to collect it.I’m probably gonna continue trying to get the last few known journal entries legit before cheating the achievement in, but I thought it would be a good idea to post this review before I tarnish my opinion any further.UPDATE: I've played an additional nine hours since posting this review. I got the ox journal entry about two hours in, and the squirrel one popped up not long after that, although I didn't get the RNG needed for the correct outcome and haven't seen a single squirrel since. This may be a bug, it may just be extremely bad luck. Either way, I'm sick of playing and have ultimately decided to cheat the achievement in.TL;DR - The Long Dark if it were a visual novel. Pretty fun for a few hours of gameplay, absolute hell if you’re an achievement hunter. It would be good if it were cheaper, and even better if it were shorter.

_childDocuments_.review: i liked this game, i really did! i just think that this game has a bit of confusion about it. If you go into this, expecting it to be a chill experience, youre not going to have a fun time, as the early runs just dont give you enough resources to survive. if you go into this expecting a challenge, youll be happy with the early runs, but as you play more and get more of the tools, the game gets easier and easier. its strange to have a roguelike experience and have no challenge mode, especially in a game where theres only so many encounters you can have. in my last run, trying to get my last dogs story, i knew the encounters well enough that i could sometimes tell what was going to happen solely based on what the musher would say, and i hovered around 16 food the entire run. theres several mentions across this game of a dog sledding race, its brought up multiple times in the beginning, its on the first page of the journal, and its weird that theres no mode for it. i wish i could properly put the knowledge ive gained to the test. the zen mode was a cool thing of the devs to add tho, ive used it a couple times as background noise, but i dont like that you still get the events triggers. you slow down and pan over to them like you can interact with them, but then you always move on.but i think thats just me wanting a challenge. if you go into it wanting to explore a scenic landscape with cute dogs by your side, learning the ins and outs until you become an expert in both your dogs and the land, then youll be happy with this. the sense of learning and progress is real and rewarding. i just wish that the end game was better. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty interesting roguelite'ish game, but a bit too thin in content. You'll probably fail the first few attempts to reach the end. Every fail gives you a little bit more starting supplies, so after you get enough starting supplies - all the runs become doable for the most part, unless the rng will have its say and will shout "you shall not pass!!" ^^.You choose 5 dogs out of 9, and go for an adventure to reach a cabin as an end goal. Each dog has some strengths and weaknesses and if you do all events correctly with them - they will permanently have their newly learned abilities for the future runs. You'll probably complete your first run in about 2h of gameplay. 1 run takes about 20-30 minutes. You hunt animals for food, scavenge items and their upgrades each run (if you manage to find them). And then you just do runs for the achievements and hope for some new unseen events here and there. But overall, the variety is not that big. Most runs will feel 90% the same after several attempts. Which is a bit sad, since the whole gameplay loops is quite fun. Reminded me of Darkest Dungeon in a sense.Only the shooting mechanics are a bit meh, sometimes it's impossible to get a good shot and you lose a bullet for nothing. Maybe after cleaning your weapon you get better rng, but I stopped playing the game after doing it, so maybe it's not that awful after that.Anyway. it's a cozy, small game that you can waste some hours with your cartoonish dogs.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really enjoyed this game! Beautiful scenery, very simple UI and easy to make choices that can result in some very very interesting encounters/stories. Having the journal to log special moments is a wonderful idea, I adore it. The animation is cute even though it is relatively simple. Voice acting is amazing. The atmosphere is divine.Pros:+ very adorable doggos with different appearances and personalities+ dogs have their own story lines and eventually + first person POV + voice acting really immerses you+ entertaining even as an adult player (and I could see it being very riveting for younger audiences, too). + encounters/events are a mix of choice and RNG, meaning you can have multiple outcomes to the same 'scene'+ survival system is simple to understand but mastering resources takes multiple runs+ beautiful story; hopeful, emotional, and heartfelt without having to resort to tragedyCons:- very short story. Once you reach the cabin that is pretty much it-- I was expecting to have at least a few other maps or even some trouble at the cabin to manage. Really get settled into the MC's new life as a musher, you know? - repeat runs are pretty fun for dogs you haven't yet gotten on your team, but their personal stories are very short and only need one good complete run to finish their part. - cost. I happily bought the game at full price (think it was about $27 USD for me), but for almost $30 I was expecting more content. Not a whole lot, but I think I finished a full run within 1-2 hrs of the game. The other hours I have spent running with other dogs to unlock their stories but it is getting repetitive. Hopefuls:~ being able to have different maps for different runs~ tasks to do at home (supply runs, working with the dogs, dealing with encounters around the cabin or at home)~ some dog sled racing story to continue on with the MC's dream. Nothing crazy long, but a mix of cooperation and antagonistic encounters for that kind of content would be so wonderful.- if other content is added, perhaps looking into some more systems for 'training/working' to become better? I love the way progression works in the game; doing practice runs or learning from races to learn how to build a good team (maybe include personalities/clashing dynamics, balancing resources for owning more dogs, etc). This game is beautiful and I have enjoyed the first 3 hrs immensely. If the price drops even to about $20 USD, I would be encouraging friends and family to purchase and try it out. It is the kind of game that sticks in your mind-- with some more content, I think this game could become very very memorable and even more emotionally connected with the players.

Controls are smooth, enhancing the game's relaxing atmosphere with an 8/10 rating. While there's a good variety in navigation options, the depth of gameplay scores a respectable 7/10. The game's balance, allowing for multiple attempts without excessive difficulty, receives another 7/10.Art Style: 9/10The game's adorable art style perfectly complements its wilderness theme, creating a serene and immersive experience. Its visuals contribute significantly to the overall atmosphere, earning a commendable 9/10.Performance: 8/10Performance-wise, The Red Lantern delivers admirably, with no notable issues or hiccups encountered during gameplay. It earns a solid 8/10 in this regard.Sound and Music: 7/10The game's score adds depth to the journey, effectively conveying the sense of overcoming the wilderness. However, some repetitive voice lines slightly detract from the experience, earning a 7/10.Story and Narrative: 7/10While the storyline is simple, it aligns well with the game's premise. The individual stories of your sled dogs add depth to the narrative, expanding upon the game's central theme. It earns a 7/10 in this aspect. Characters, from wildlife encounters to your loyal sled dogs, are intricately designed and evoke curiosity, earning a commendable 9/10. The voice acting breathes life into the characters, making them believable and relatable, garnering a solid 9/10.Replayability: 7/10The Red Lantern offers replay value with its multiple run approach, allowing players to unlock new content and equipment with each playthrough. This feature adds to its overall appeal, earning a 7/10.Overall Score: 8/10The Red Lantern delivers an engaging survival experience set against the backdrop of the Alaskan wilderness. With its charming art style, smooth controls, and immersive atmosphere, it offers players a captivating journey. While aspects like gameplay mechanics and story may be relatively simple, the game's strength lies in its ability to evoke emotion and create a connection with its characters. For those seeking a tranquil yet compelling adventure, The Red Lantern is a journey worth embarking on.

_childDocuments_.review: I always wanted to know whether a narrative focused roguelike could work. Red Lantern answers that question pretty definitively.You see, there is a really nice feel-good game about chilling with your dogs and traversing the beautiful Alaskan wilderness here. Encountering various animals, setting camp and petting your pals, in a women vs wild setting sounds like a cool little indie game, but for some reason, instead of an easy going light survival game, they decided a roguelike would be the best medium for this adventure. That means you get to do the same encounters, same hunts, same every thing over and over and over again. It's also the worst implementation of a roguelike system I have ever seen. You are basically forced to fail, and winning a game before dying multiple times is basically impossible, because the game arbitrary rewards you with more food, bullets and other items. Without these surviving Alaska is not feasible, so you aren't even winning the game by being smart, rather by grinding.Storybased content and grinding just doesn't work in the same sentence, the lines and monologues and encounters repeat far too often and the cool atmosphere of the game completely vanishes. ...and even the choices you make make no sense. At one point you encounter a caribou, and can shoot it, so I do the confusing mini-game, shoot at the right time wounding the animal, who then proceeds to walk away bleeding. Now the logical option would be to shoot it again or track it, but that option isn't even presented to you. Same with a nonsensical owl encounter, whereby you are randomly ran over by a reindeer. I guess the point is you have to memorize the right answer for each of these encounters, but that feels like such a boring forced game mechanic.It's really sad, because the game would be really cool! Just the survival aspect alone works well, and going out finding random animals, scratching the belly of your dogs and discovering abandoned locations would have been more than enough. The story about finding oneself and rediscovering our purpose would have been a touching one, had I only heard it once, not 17 different times. No idea why they added so much unnecessary gameplay elements, that actively work against the player's enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wasn't expecting too much from a dogsledding game, but I think this game did almost as much as possible with the subject matter. The roguelite approach offers satisfactory progress that makes it worth trying for multiple attempts, the voice acting is good, the encounters are interesting, and the dogs are sweet and have fleshed-out personalities. My biggest frustration was that I wasn't given a second medkit until the run I actually finished, and this ended up a major limitation on my last few runs, to the point I didn't even heal Barkley when he was injured by a wolf because I knew I needed to save it for myself. It would be nice if a second one was provided sooner or if it was easier to find one in the wild (I don't know if you can ever find one, because I didn't). Some of the encounters can also get a bit repetitive and it would be nice to be able to skip them. But overall I felt progression was good and the game stayed mostly fresh (not to the degree I even considered playing the post-victory content, though I did appreciate the devs providing this).

_childDocuments_.review: Only on sale.This game is cute, but I would give it more a hesitant positive than an eager positive. You start off in your journey in the wilderness of Alaska, and what are the cons and pros?Pros...-Goober dogs. Good woofs.-You can pet the dogs and uncover their unique stories, which can be quite cute (Fin my beloved).-GREAT voice acting. Amazing. 10/10.-Some fun mini-games and scenarios.-Some amount of strategy.-Pretty lighting and graphics. Not the best, but some animations (like petting the dogs!) are satisfying.-You can generally choose in scenarios.Cons...-Some circumstances are out of your control, or some choices are illogical. When a wolf attacks one of your dogs and you have no food/bullets, you can only wave the gun at it. I expected to at least swing the gun at it; you could argue that's too violent, but this game is T and involves shooting, injuries, etc. If you're in the Alaskan wilderness defending your dog, you're not just gonna wave it casually.-I know some games can be "unfair" at times, or depend on random RNG that can be quite unlucky, but with this one? Come on. I'm fine playing games where the RNG fates are against you, but at least in other games you can fight. You can't fight if there is literally no bark the whole run except for the starting bark- with no indicators. I love hard games and don't mind a challenge, but there's a difference between bad RNG and hard enemies against you and literally having no control.-Some corny dialogue, but I don't mind it too much. Still though. Girl, what made you think the Alaskan wilderness would be "extreme camping?"-I wish you could point better. It's not a huge problem, but it'd be nice if the pointer was more visible, or if you could walk closer to the dogs. Again, not a huge problem.-Maybe it's just not that kind of game, but I'd like if there was more control over your situations, yet more difficulty to balance it out.I know the cons are long, but it's a bit of me venting because I can. It is a cute game and I recommend it for sure, but 20$ is not worth ~2 hours of gameplay (possibly 10 if you like it). Get it on sale, but get it. I wouldn't put it on the top of your wishlist, though, but if you have some spare time and don't have much better to do and feel like it, I would get it.

_childDocuments_.review: As I've seen some bad reviews talking about the game mechanics, I wanted to point them out here as well.For me, this isn't a game that focuses a lot on big gameplay or impactful decisions. This game has a very simple structure: choose your path, explore different encounters on your way and make decisions based on the resources you need. This game is relaxing and cute with the many dogs you can adopt and their personalities, and it doesnt require any strong mechanics of the player. Its a story of a woman, trying to live her dream and learning the reality of what it means to survive alone in the wild and cold! Based on her lack of experience, her decisions may seem simple, but make sense. Some encounters have different outcomes, good or bad, but never frustrating or unreasonable. Its very "real", but uncomplicated.If you wish to take part in the story that is being told while enjoying the dogs company and indulging in the beautiful atmosphere of Alaska, you're at the right place. You can even change the setting if dogs are able to die during runs or not (I always have that turned on. I can't see them die) as nature can be brutal too!If you are looking for lots of decision making with very impactful results that go in a deeper level, you're at the wrong place here! This game is more of a relaxing game to play to chill out than anything else. You can play it with your mouse only as you just need to choose the options, nothing more.

_childDocuments_.review: The review hurts to write, as I REALLY wanted to like this game. I went ahead and broke down what I found to be the positives and negatives. I do think grabbing this game on a sale day wouldn't be bad, but overall it just wasn't what I was expecting.                                                                                                                                                                                     Positives:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Art Design: The game's art design is absolutely charming, with a cutesy and calming aesthetic that draws players into its wilderness setting. The attention to detail in the environments, from the snowy landscapes to the wildlife, enhances the immersive experience.Wildlife and Scenery: The inclusion of various wild animals and stunning scenery adds depth and realism to the Alaskan wilderness portrayed in the game. These elements not only serve as visually appealing backdrops but also contribute to the overall atmosphere and sense of adventure.Music and Sound Design: The music in "The Red Lantern" complements the game play perfectly, setting the mood and enhancing the emotional impact of key moments. Additionally, the voice acting is top-notch, bringing the characters to life and immersing players further into the narrative.Dog Companions: The selection of sled dogs and their distinct personalities is one of the game's standout features. Each dog feels unique and lovable, adding an emotional layer to the game play as players form bonds with their furry companions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Negatives:                                                                                                                                                                             Limited Dog Choices: The inability to change your selected dog after it's chosen can be frustrating, especially if you later on realize you'd preferred a different companion. This lack of flexibility may deter some players from fully engaging with the game's narrative and mechanics.Game play Mechanics: The core game play mechanics, particularly the emphasis on trial and error without clear guidance, can be a significant drawback for some players. While the game encourages learning through mistakes, the lack of instruction or tutorials may lead to confusion and repetition, detracting from the overall enjoyment.Lack of Resources and Guidance: The game's reliance on players dying and restarting to receive additional resources or insights on game play strategies can feel punishing and counter-intuitive. Without clear guidance or tutorials, players may struggle to grasp essential mechanics, such as allowing dogs to feed themselves, leading to frustration and unnecessary repetition.Repetitive Game-play: The necessity to replay the same scenes repeatedly in hopes of progressing further can become tedious and monotonous. The lack of variety in game-play experiences may detract from the game's overall enjoyment and longevity.

_childDocuments_.review: Very weak recommendation. I’ll give this a thumbs up for all the dog/animal lovers out there (which I am one). But to be honest, I almost gave up on this game after ~4 hours because of how incredibly repetitive it gets. Eventually, I did power through and finish the game in 5 hours. I have no intention of replaying it.The set up is you’re in the Alaskan wilderness, traveling with a pack of sled dogs. You’re trying to survive long enough to get to the safety of a cabin. The majority of the gameplay is just making yes/no decisions; though there is a hunting mini-game you play once in a while.The main drawback: for some reason they made this a rogue lite/like because… that’s how all games are now. This leads to repeating scene after scene because there really isn’t that much to do in the snowy wilderness besides hunt and eat. Yes, it’s very endearing to pet/play with your dogs, but again, it’s the same animations and voice lines over and over again. They really should have been a bit more generous with resources, and made this a linear adventure game.The graphics, to be blunt, look downright awful for 2021 standards. But to be fair, this isn’t the kind of game that relies on aesthetics. Check it out if you love dogs (and how can you not?), but temper your expectations on how fun it’ll actually be.

_childDocuments_.review: SummaryA beautifully illustrated and acceptably narrated game, with far too little content and almost no story or music for an inflated price tag. It's an enjoyable 2-3 hour experience, I'd say its worth picking up on sale for $5-10, or if you really like dogs.I'm trying out a weird way of rating stuff, so this is sorted weird. I'm sorting categories based on their weighted importance in this game. I wouldn't rate a text adventure game heavily on its illustration for example.    Illustration(32/35)The nature is gorgeous, but the sloppy level design holds it back. The map was so tiny that it gave the environment a closed small feeling during both encounters and sledding. I genuinely chuckled when the game gave me the option to "hunt" a squirrel by walking up to it and holding the tip of the rifle a foot away from its head, while the musher worried about whether they were going to miss the shot. So even though the illustration style was really nice, it was bottlenecked by the sloppy gameplay / level design.       Narrative(15/30)The description says narrative driven, but there's little to no real story other than an occasional reminiscent thought from the main character. The second adjective in the steam page description was narrative, and there was essentially no story. It might have been more accurate to say "fully narrated", cause I think that's more what they meant. 90% of the gameplay was just repeating simple tasks. Why not have more unique encounters, and kick the grunt work? Some sort of story or mystery? It built up a great mysterious tone, but had no actual mystery.     Gameplay(10/20)The game had a pleasantly simple gameplay system which they drove into the ground to stretch playtime. I feel like I could've finished the game in like 15 minutes if the musher and the dogs didn't need to consume 3 elks worth of meat to survive one night of in game time, forcing me to stop the sled every 15 seconds to get meat at every opportunity. The thing that was most enjoyable about the game was just sort of riding the sled and watching the landscape go by, so it was kind of irritating when the encounters would interrupt that.     Music and Sound(7/10)The music is a little basic, but nice. Could've used much more range, I read another review saying that there was only one track. Not sure if that's true, but it sure felt that way.     Marketing(2.5/5)Already mentioned it, but the lack of the promised narrative was frustrating. Chalked it up to be much bigger than it was. Also, the gameplay didn't feel clearly enough represented in the trailer.32+15+10+7+2.5 = 66.5All in all, I think the lesson to be learned here is that you should try to understand the strengths and weaknesses of your game. Find the core aspect of gameplay that makes the game fun, and connect the player with it as much as possible. In this instance, the illustration.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was intended for children, and I definitely recommend this for kids/teenagers who enjoy playing animal simulators. Zoos, national parks, doggy daycares, vet clinics, etc. You will collect a team of sled dogs and discover a special accessory for each dog. You can pet them and play fetch.I also recommend this game to artistic folk who don't have the energy to play. If you want to simply turn off your brain and watch cute low-poly animals in Alaska - the Red Lantern will refresh your eyes a bit. None of your actions have real consequences here, you and your dogs can't die.It lacks both gameplay and story. The idea had potential, but was poorly written. Our main character goes to Alaska with her pet husky Chomper, to gather a team of sled dogs, discover the purpose and character of each dog, survive in the wilderness and try her strength in the dog race. She knows almost nothing about what she is going to face, so you'll have to listen to tons of overdramatic monologues about how she never expected this to be so hard. Gameplay consists of you choosing where to turn and what to respond to animals on your way. You have to hunt and collect supplies to prevent starvation.

_childDocuments_.review: all the dogs are adorable and interesting in their own ways, and i ended up loving even the ones i didn't care much for at the start. the journey to the home (which can be considered the "meat" of the gameplay) gets a little repetitive after you've done it many times; you need to complete it 9 times to unlock all the dogs' accessories, and unless you're very efficient, several times more to check off everything in the journal. neither of these are really  however and the dog-specific events at least give the runs some variety.apart from that i found the survival aspect somewhat difficult at first but after a few (possibly failed) runs you start to get the micromanagement between food, bullets, etc. and never really have to worry about it again. after that it's just about exploring the different choices you're presented during the events, and trying to get all the outcomes to fill the journal.overall it's a very fun, chill game that i was able to complete (apart from a few remaining journal notes) in about 10 hours, although i did also take the time to pet each dog every time we set up camp and every time we got back to the house, which probably accounts for at least an hour. the only bugs that ever showed up were minor visual glitches that didn't affect anything.

Voice acting is so great that it is as annoying as these characters usually are, it really got on my nerves and even gave me a headache in the long run.Surely the graphics are great, the dog adoption and management mechanics are good too, but the exploration and survival aspects are below mediocre. The food consumption mechanic is not realistic. You don't consume the same amount of calories by visiting a small abandoned shed, simply observing an elk, or hunting. The poor rewards this offers simply break the survival aspects of the game.The choice system, and the shooting mechanics are extremely mediocre too. Sometimes, I would have probably chosen another path or choice, or simply have shot/acted faster or in an entire different way to get my dogs and myself out of danger.Sadly, I am asking for a refund in its actual state, but I do not see any reason for re-buying it again after some patches.

_childDocuments_.review: just copy the best review that shows everything:Beautiful art style and functioning gameplay, but not for me. The idea of rogue-like survival runs like this is actually pretty cool, but instead of letting you try your best to chose a loadout that you can afford, dealing with your own choices, it puts you into the shoes of the main character. A girl in an existential crisis who thinks that it's a good idea to pack 3 bullets in a rusty old gun for an adventure like this. Let alone from enough meat to not starve a day.I know this is the gameplay loop and makes for a quick end of runs, but I had preferred if that quick end came because of other means that don't have you sit in front of the screen and shake your head on the level of irresponsibility the protagonist puts her dogs into in order to "find herself".I'm not a fan of this premise - it's the typical american luxury life problem type of person who lost herself in consumption and now thinks that pulling six dog lives into her struggle and just go fully unprepared into the wilderness is a good idea.Like... how am I supposed to empathise with that?The description reads "learn from your failures to find your way home" - but they aren't my mistakes. It's not my mistake to get run over by a moose regardless of whether I keep going or check out the owl. It's not my mistake that I can't hunt for food anymore because I brought 4 bullets. It's not my mistake that I didn't bring a fishing pole, nor that I didn't bring an axe right away.For the gameplay loop this works, as you iteratively "automatically" learn from these mistakes. But it's a bit like a rail shooter. I just have to die often enough to get the good stuff, and there's no way around it. There is nothing to "survive" in this game. You can't make the right choices to survive because the character that you play, or rather watch running into her doom with little participation, has already made the wrong ones before you even start the run.For whom it's fun to spend hours on watching someone else make absolutely bonkers levels of stupid mistakes (Like who doesn't bring an axe. a fishing rod and a gun with a few packs of bullets with them?), just to live them out and be rewarded by the character iteratively realising her stupidity and incrementally "changing" them, then this game is for them.Like "Oh, in my "bad dream" we died because I just brought 3 bullets. Maybe I'll pack 4 next time" - sorry, this just doesn't work for me. Pretty visuals and lovely theme and setting set aside.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many dog sledding games so just this by itself is a good reason to check out what this game has to offer. _childDocuments_.review: The Red Lantern is a chill, narrative driven, survival sled dog simulator game. The objective is to build a sled dog team from a group of colorful dogs, each one with their own personalities and designs, and then ride through the arctic wilderness to your new home. Along the way you need to manage resources such as food and ammo while you encounter various events that will require you to make choices.A single run will take you maybe ten to twenty minutes to complete and a lot of that is spent peacefully watching the scenery go by as your sled runs through the arctic wilderness. Occasionally events will require your input like whether you stop to go hunting or investigate something shiny nearby, however the game can be comfortably played with just the mouse and scroll wheel or simple button presses.Each dog has their own story to tell and each one can be unlocked by focusing on that dog's actions during a run. There are no bad choices when it comes to building your sled team, but some can provide alternative outcomes to events or add unique encounters to the game’s choice pool. This is a game where you'll have to run through it multiple times to see everything there is to see and will probably take you about five to ten hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I uninstalled this game quickly and here's why.I played up till the first camp setup and have had a huge issue with the lack of interactivity in this game.When I saw that we have encounters I thought I'd have to look out for them. No, the game slows down and the character verbally says "there's a thing! what should we do?". I want the task of looking out for stuff to be on my hands because then I have an actual reason to look around. It's Alaska, there's nothing to see. My eyes aren't given a task and it draws me out of the game. This all could be fixed by making the player have to be active.All of the dog's info was given at the very start. Why? I don't remember a single thing about Barkley because his entire lore was dropped at our first interaction. During this interaction the main character does feel very alive which I like but I also do not have the patience to sit through so much dialogue when nothing is happening on screen. Some of this information should be given to me when I set up camp. That would space things out and give me time to actually get attached to these dogs. Speaking of getting attached...The first thing I did when I opened the game was check the setting because I expected it to be too loud. It wasn't too loud but I did notice what was at the very top of the settings: "Allow dog death" my response was "The dogs can die?". Some advice for anybody making a game with intense game beats like those: Don't spoil your own game. Now I missed out on genuinely being worried about what happens when a dog gets too injured. Fear of the unknown would layer on top of the tense situation. This is the kind of setting you give to the player after they've suffered once so that they don't remove that portion of the game for themselves or you could lock it behind another tab in the settings with a popup that says "Reading these settings may give you information about the game. You have been warned if you wish to play the game blindly." Then you could have something flash next time you enter a menu (after a dog dies) saying "You can stop this from happening again in the forbidden settings!" and if you're feeling really generous you can let the player revive the dog.Finally the art style. The dog's faces are unsettling. There's something wrong with them and I can't tell what. I love everything else visually though. I understand it is hard to make snowy plains look interesting so I don't plan on ripping into that. The dog's fur looks oddly like feathers for some reason but I still like that. The clipping can be very obvious sometimes. My biggest issue with the game's visuals is the limited view of it the player is allowed. When the player sets up camp they should be free to move and feel free. They are already given freedom of movement when getting onto the sled so the mechanics do exist within the game. If the player was able to move the dogs could react to the player. What if some of the dogs got excited when  approached or their focus snapped to the player. Each dog could have their own little way of reacting to the player.Overall, I don't like this game because it isn't very interactive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game's art style is adorable, and the dogs even more so, it was extremely frustrating at times because I needed to replay from the very beginning so many times simply because I ran out of bullets or food. If I'm being honest it probably took me 8 tries before I could reach the end (the second to last time I was extremely close but got killed by a bear). If you don't mind having to replay events over and over again, then this game would probably be fine. It's not free-roam so you're restricted to a lot of cut-scenes. It builds off of the experience you gain throughout the game, so if you find a fire starter while playing, the next time you die and restart from the beginning, you'll have that item to start with. This is a pretty cool concept but overall a little inconvenient for how easily you can end up dying in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Get on discount.Obviously the dogs are cute, but once I 100% the game I can't imagine replaying it.Just to 'beat' the game a single time you already need to do multiple runs, because the game just does not give you enough supplies to win at first. Basically every failed run you restart and have a few more supplies, or if you were lucky enough to find one, a tool. However, I haven't failed a single run since I managed to beat one. Other annoying things:- The dialogue, it isn't bad inherently, but your character will repeat a lot of stuff over and over, and along with the animations it can really start to drag.- RNG encounters, some encounters are up to chance, this would be fine, but again runs can drag on and to fill the journal you need to see specific events that you can just miss.- Dog Stories, the dogs each have a story to complete, but you'll basically only complete one dog's story per run, these reset between run if not completed, so your first few runs don't help this and you can't clear multiple dogs in a single run, so even more time.- Gameplay, some of your choices in encounters do matter, but the actual sledding is automatic. The game lets you lean, but this literally does nothing. There are shooting and fishing mechanics, but these are really simple. Also whenever you interact with something in the camp it takes forever for the reticle to come back.The good:- Dogs, they have fun stories and personalities- Art, the game looks really nice, the environments are nice, and I'm pretty sure where you are on the map actually changes your surroundings.- For some, the lack of skill required could be a draw, and it is definitely easy to just sit back and chill.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a random bundle I purchased, and this is one of the first games that stood out to me. Without any prior knowledge I launched the game and I was pleasantly surprised. It's comparable to games like "Road 96" but with a more simplistic execution. You're sledding through the Alaskan wilderness, while random events and encounters are occuring, and it's your job to manage your energy and hunger levels in a smart way based on what's happening. It's definitely light survival, but most of all it's a cozy and relaxing game. The overall story is satisfying, and each dog has its own personality, which is cool.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game.The dogs are cute and well animated and each have their own little personality.However you can lose this game simply because RNG screws you over and doesn't give you any birch, med packs or bullets. It takes several runs to get the tools you need to actually make it to the cabin. Because our character is an idiot didn't think to bring any non perishable food  and only one med pack to go sledding through the wilderness. Didn't even think to bring a box of matches. It's not a game of survival it's a game of will the game let you finish.You can find a fire starter which means you will no longer need the birch but again, finding it is completely up to RNG.  The devs had to purposely make it so you had to restart your runs multiple times just to boost total playtime hours.Expect to starve your first few runs because every encounter will make you hungrier for some reason, even just going to go look a squirrel makes you as hungry as shooting a caribou. Only good news if you lose a run you still keep all the tools you have found so far.You can find a fishing pole but there is no way to actually fish when you want, you'll fish when the game says you can fish. If you can get this game on a huge discount, it is cute to watch the dogs run through the snow. But there is not enough content to justify full price. You don't even get to drive the sled yourself, the game moves it for you, you just wait for prompts to pop up and click one. That's the game.I'm marking my review positive simply because it is cute and I did feel I got $7 worth of content. I have been eyeing this game, saw it was finally on sale and got it. If I had paid full price I would have been very dissapointed.Buy on sale only.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty zen, and it tells the story of a lady who leaves her old life behind with her dog to become a sled dog racer. You follow her story and build up a team and go through training runs, but first you have to make it home.It's not a very involved game. You don't steer the team you just decide to go left or right at checkpoints, but I like that as the visuals are quite pleasant to look at. The fun comes from completing the story of each dog and crossing your fingers that RNG is on your side. The game can become a grind, especially when trying to fill your journal. Over all you could probably beat the base game in 3-5 hours. That is completing the story of every dog and depending on if RNG is on your side.

_childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: 7/10 Good DogsThe Context:The Red Lantern is a short but sweet tale about crossing the Alaskan countryside via dogsled. While it is mostly a visual novel, there are some light aspects of both resource management and various minigames scattered throughout. The hook for most will end up being the dogs and their varied personalities that you learn about during your journey. It was a little sparse on content outside of that, but well worth the price of admission for a tight few hours, and for Bodega alone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute game is you love dogs. The personalities, art style, and animations on the dogs are by far the best part. It's basically like a RPG were you are assembling a party out of dogs.The gameplay loop, on the other hand, is extremely basic. You have to master a shooting minigame (click when the little circle overlaps the big circle) to be successful but otherwise it's just picking from mostly binary choices. The reward comes in completing each dog's story and getting an accessory like a toy or hat for each dog. Don't get this game thinking you're getting any more complicated gameplay than just "choose your own adventure." You'll start running into repetition in your runs almost immediately. If you are trying to complete the journal you will run into entries that require a sequence of random events in response to specific choice that can be extremely hard to luck into without going on dozens of runs (each of which takes half an hour or so). It's also of note that the challenges are kind of stupid... you only get a few bullets and must scrounge for more because the player character didn't bring even a box of ammo for her ancient, rusty rifle. Frankly, she's an idiot with almost no chance of survival - she decided to "live off the land" with no food and only a few bullets and bandages. Each run can yield additional future resources, so paradoxically this game starts out at its very hardest and then gets progressively easier until you've either lost interest or are willing to just repeat runs to try to fill out journal entries. With the right luck you could (in theory) get every journal entry and dog story in eight runs or less, but it's more likely it would take dozens of runs repeating the exact same events until you get the right dice roll to get bitten by a squirrel or such. Pay attention to your hunger meter and the dog's energy meter, though, as somehow you can starve to death in a matter of hours if you don't camp soon enough.So be aware of the limitations, maybe wait to pick it up on sale like I did, but it does have some some of the very best dogs ever to grace a video game in a lovely art style. I got a lot of joy out of their animated doggy happiness. Also note that for some reason, the game lets your dogs die by default unless you check a box at the top of the settings. I checked this before even trying the game, I have no desire to simulate sled dogs starving to death, being gored by elk, or being mauled by a bear, so you're on your own with that.For all its limitations, though, as a hard core dog lover who has been on a dog sled more than once, this was a great little offering to warm the heart that's worth some love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game.  Kudos to the entire development and production team.  I very relaxing and engaging game.  The visual setting and story were very good.  I never been to Alaska, but the visuals made me feel as though I was there.  I recently lost a wonderful pet - Mia, and the interactions with the dogs were more emotional than I expected.  Enough praise here are some suggestions.  I think this game has only scratched the surface for story telling.  The main character through which the story is told a woman.  I was especially pleased about the voice actress's delivery of the narration.  Add a male character; add more characters and add more accents.  And create a unique story for each one.  Maybe a veteran, someone dealing with addiction, or a loss, or a transition in their life.  I got faith in the team that made this game.  Wow me guys.  Give me more good stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, chill little dog game. Thankfully, at no point did this game become truly sad (during my runs) and the game keeps an upbeat atmosphere throughout. Get it if you'd like a relaxed experience trekking through the snow with your puppos.What on earth does leaning in the sled do? Weakest point IMO is having the encounters repeat and play out in exactly the same way. Once you find the best choice in an encounter, you never really need to select anything else (as long as you remember).
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: It's part part resource management, world exploration (beautifully animated Alaskan wilderness), part survival game (hunting, fishing, camping, a few predator fights), and part cute animal story (adopt a sled dog team and unlock their personalities(!) through wilderness encounters). It took me 5 attempts and about 4 hours to beat it, but at the end you unlock some more open modes where you can keep playing and finish the other dogs' stories.The story is very small-scale-- a woman fails out of med school, has a crisis of confidence and leaves her life in Seattle to prove her own strength in Alaska-- but that ties in really beautifully to the roguelite mechanic: every time you fail, some part of the experience stays with you and makes you better prepared for the next trip. (Something something "no part of your life is ever wasted" metaphor!!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, you can pet the dog.This game is adorable. I absolutely love the pups and their different personalities. It gets a bit easier with time when you unlock more stuff, but you also challenge yourself more so it doesn't get too easy and boring. Each run is different depending on how you want to engage with your dogs and the environment, which is really cool.
