_childDocuments_.review: Very short game, where you have to make your way through the icy wilderness to a cottage, which is supposed to become your new home. basic, yet good enough graphics. Enough loot to make it through, if you do not give up. Every turn matters - different loot in different locations make passing the snowy area easier. Do not give up! Obviously one is NOT supposed to make it through on the first try anyway! The better you get, the more skill perks you get, and this adds to your chances to survive. I liked this game very much! Only the price is a little bit high in my opinion, so better wait for a sale. Nevertheless nice story, great voice actress and good replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: This game taught me to kill every animal I encountered. And it's better to let the dogs hunt than waste ammo.The game is calm and relaxing, and bonding with the dogs is wholesome. However, it has some flaws. First of all, it's reasonable to expect that you could control sledding in a game about sled riding, but you can only choose the direction on a crossroad.Secondly, I don't see any strategy in choosing which way I go. If I need any resources, I need to count on luck because there is nothing I can do to improve my chances of finding the right thing.Thirdly, the minigames are terrible. Especially the hunting one.But it's still an interesting game. Nothing awesome but wholesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow!This game is so much more than I expected it to be... As of writing this comment I finaly arrived at the cabin for the first time (It took me about 10-15 runs). I was injured, without food and my dogs almost run out of energy but I made it! As you learn and grow with your character (and dogs), you slowly figure things out through your mistakes. The runs get easier and more free as you start to get how to survive harsh alaskan nature. But even when things go wrong, there is still hope that it can turn in your favor. And if not... well, you learn. The scenery is absolutely wonderful, every view screenshotworthy + cute dogos all with their different personalities and traits, which you can of course pet!! Enjoy the nature, watch the animals, learn more about them and notice all the small details!I can not wait to see more of what this game has to offer. ♥
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: The Red Lantern is an adorable and heartwarming story of a woman who's decided to leave big city life and challenge herself to live on her own in the wilderness as a musher(sled dog rider). The story is mainly focused around her journey to the Red Lantern(a cabin in the woods that her friend gave to her) and her dogs. You start out as a greenhorn and learn along the way. Each dog has its own storyline and somewhat of a character arc and including different dogs in your sled dog team will trigger different events, relevant to the dog's story. It offers a unique story and gameplay that engages you and your choices will decide whether you and your dogs will survive the journey. The game encourages exploration and being outgoing, which is inherent to the storyline and embodies a spirit of wonder and appreciating the little things.If you ever entertained the idea of heading out into the wilderness to challenge yourself and to escape the hustle and bustle of city life... or, like me, absolutely love dogs, this game will appeal to you. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I bought and played this game was hearing a familiar voice when I watched the preview video.   I was like, "What??? Chloe Price moved to Alaska!?!?"   So all the Ashly Burch fans gotta buy this game!The game is slow and mostly relaxing.   It's a good game for exploration and letting your imagination run around for some fresh (and frigid) air.   If you have no imagination or are addicted to twitchy adrenaline games - this one will be boring.If you do buy and play this game, you will need a lot of patience.   The controls are so basic yet if you miss an instruction such as what key to press to do a certain tasks, you are in trouble, it will only tell you ONCE.Like How to stop to set up Camp.   (Press C) I think.    Other reviewers have mentioned that they get stuck starving to death repeatedly because the camp would never trigger.    I had this problem too, until I stopped and started deliberately mashing keys until I got something to happen.   You can set up camp at ANY segment of the adventure.Remember "Haw" and "Gee"   They only tell you which is right and which is left ONCE.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I stared at that "Do you recommend this game?" thing for a LOT longer than I usually do.Here's the thing: The Red Lantern is a solid little thing, for what it is, and I'd say the price is right. But so much about it telegraphs a much larger experience that it then roundly fails to deliver.The musings about The Musher's friend the dog sledder tend to imply that this isn't a one-off jaunt into the Alaskan wilderness. More than that, the roguelite progression is a mechanic that implies a much longer gameplay arc. I, like several other reviewers, felt that as I finished the game I had finished only the first chapter of a much larger story. And then the credits rolled.Thing is, I mostly enjoyed my time being The Musher. Ashly Burch delivers a solid performance as The Musher, the dogs have personality (and yes; you can give them pets) and their own little story arcs to explore, and the game does a really good job of getting you to care about them as individuals and companions in a powerful and minimalist fashion.But in the three hours it took me to complete (with a single team of dogs; I may go back to pick a new team at some point) I had already noticed a repetition in the various encounter scenes. I ran into the same glove on a stump leading to an abandoned parka with a bullet sticking out of the pocket five or six times. I had an encounter with a musk ox resulting in an injury to one of my dogs four times. One of my dogs ran off after a porcupine and got stuck in the nose for his troubles on all but one run-through.All in all, it says something good that by the end of the experience I wanted more, but it also says something bad that I feel in its current state the game has very little left to offer me after three hours. With some content updates, this could easily be a fantastic game. As it stands? I can only classify it as a highly polished indie curiosity, albeit one worth the $5 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Decent concept, only it ends quickly. The main character is charming and the dogs have distinct personalities and abilities that make it entertaining. The first person experience isn’t “played” so much as observed while making decisions that steer the outcome. It would be better if there were more content that expanded the game with a grander adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say I recommend it only because I want to keep playing! I thought the first part, trying to reach the red lantern cabin was like an extended tutorial, and that once I'd unlocked all the tools and reached the cabin I'd get to be a dogsled racer. I was looking forward to multiple rounds of driving through to select dogs, dogs maybe gaining skills and traits as the game progressed, different maps to play through. I got none of that.I still say yes I recommend it, but be aware that my 7 hour playtime is the whole content.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I am absolutley in love with this game. For one, its adorable. The dogs are so so cute, and i love their personalities. (I adopted every dog in a row that's how much i liked them at first meet). Also if you're worried about picking dogs, you can go back and adopt them all when you reach the cabin! I'm very excited about this, i want them all. The graphics are very unique, and so pretty! My only issue with the graphics is that the dogs look kinda silly when they run, but its kinda charming at this point. The runs are relatively quick (about 30 min), and i enjoy the atmosphere! It's nice to be able to relax and just click a key every couple minutes. It's so much less stressful then the official videos make it seem (thank goodness). The outcomes for some of the choices are a bit silly at times, but it's honestly not that bad. Adds to the charm i think. I love trying to get all the things for the logbook, and figuring out the dogs story-lines (which appear as little achievement type things, there's about 3 different ones to get per dog). Sadly, if you do have to restart, any gained progress for the dogs story-line will be deleted (since it's no longer a "canon" happening) which is a bit frustrating. But the story-line's are simple enough that it's easy to regain progress! Also, I will admit, the price is a little steep for this game. If it was priced about $5-10 lower, i'd say that that would be fitting. Despite this, i do think that this game is so worth it, and if you're a dog lover or chill game enjoyer, this is definitely the game for you! <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a tough one since I really liked the game. Everything about the story and the gameplay is good, however as much as it pains me to say it, the game has a few problems that are annoying to deal with it.For example, I got soft locked out of a few instances in the journal, meaning that if I wanted to 100% I had to start a new save and make sure that didn't happen(which I ended up doing).On more than one occasion, my game bugged with no new event happening in a run, forcing me to lose whatever progress I've made that run.Will still recommend it for how beautiful the game is, but play it only if you can deal with those bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I went into The Red Lantern probably with the wrong mindset. I'd expect some open wilderness exploration, kind of like the Long Dark but with dog sled. What I got is more of an interactive novel like a choose your own adventure story that takes a bit getting used to. And the thing about choose your own adventure books is that the most important element is the story; rich character, imaginative setting, conflict, love, hate, all of that comes together like different ingredients and seasoning goes into a delicious meal. And so far the story of The Red Lantern just doesn't feel like it has that variety going. I really hope I'm wrong about it so far because from the bits and pieces of back story I'm getting so far I'm not sensing a lot of potentials; you play as a woman who for some unknown reason decides to go to Alaska and become a musher. So odds are aside from your 5 sled dogs there won't be any character interaction or much development.As far as game mechanics goes. some of the game's choices are basically just straight up punishment, and the only way to know it's a punishment is probably because you've seen it before. I've just ended my first run where I ran into a bear on both sides of the road. and there was some weird graphical glitches where the bear and tag line was snapping wildly and bear gets rendered at a weird distance/position before/after a cutscene. at the end of the first run I was told I'll start with more resource and more tools going forward so I'll have a bigger chance of succeeding this time around. However, even though I'll finish this at some point and each run will get better because every event and encounter will turn out to be a thought experiment when you failed and the story goes that you'll be better prepared for the "real" run when you actually made it to the end. I just shudder thinking about how the game will throw me random run ending stuff like falling into lake or tree crashing down or god forbid yeti leaping at your from the hills or something and say "aww. sorry to have ended your run. you'll probably made it next time".TL;DR: this is an interactive story/choose your adventure story game, no exploration. The story feels, subpar, compare to richer interactive story game like Life is Strange or the wolf or zombie story. I personally think the $29 is a bit high. I might get this for 50% or less or from Humble Bundle, but definitely not full price of $29.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: i haven't played this for a long time, and I really was not expecting it to be a choices matter adventure with QTEs,I could tell you that this game is easy, that the main character is hilariously unprepared, and that no musher would put a dog like chomper as a lead sled dog, that no sane person would travel the Alaskan wilderness with only 3 bullets.but this game isn't about that. this game is about a dog learning how to lead a sled, a dog who needs to learn about following her nose, and a dog that learns how to bark instead of bite.this game is full of heart, and you should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nice way to spend an evening. However, know what you're getting into. This game is pretty repetitive, and for 99% of people, I don't see how you could get more than maybe 8-10 hours out of this game without going insane. Then again, people dump thousands of hours and dollars into games that show them less respect than this one will, so I'm willing to bite my tongue here. If you're in the market for a wholesome little experience, try the game out. You'll pretty much be able to tell if you'd like to keep playing well before the refund window has passed. And even then, this game's trailers don't leave much to the imagination. You see what you get. I'd recommend waiting for a sale. If you want something that'll keep you playing for the gameplay, maybe skip this. Although I don't think I'm going to play much more of this game beyond my first playthrough, I can say I'm satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: A nice game to play after a stressful day to calm down and relax. Your goal is to reach your new home in the middle of nowhere. To reach it, you have to make the right descisions and use your supplies most effectively. You won't be able to do so in your first try, but in your next run you will start better prepared (i.g. you starved so you start with 1 extra meal).Every Dog has its own little story to uncover, but nothing too deep.I really like the graphic style.The controls felt a bit weird. The sensitivity of the right stick/mouse to look around is insane. You can set it from 1-10 but it felt all the same for me. Also, in the settings it is called right stick sensitivity, even if you play it with keyboard and mouse, but every other control are shown as the keyboard keys. The gamepad is not shown even if you are literally controlling the menu with it.I also didn't like the shooting minigame very much. Would I pay over 20 bucks for it as regular price? No, but I think around 10 in sale you can't do anything wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: The Red Lantern, a story about taking on the wilderness as a musher. You pick out your dog sled team from a limited selection of dogs. This list of dogs seems pretty small until you take into account a few things. First, if you're like me you pick EVERY dog to be on your dog sledding team. So, why when you only get a team of five it scarcely matters that there are only essentially two teams worth of dogs to select from.  Next, you will be playing the role of a musher who knows very little about survival and mushing. You will be working towards being a full-blown musher who goes and races. The intro/tutorial is quite good. It took me a short while to understand the hunting mechanic, because I'm very familiar with FPS games, less so with Telltale series. The single best choice the developers could make was an exceptional choice indeed. They cast the legendary Ashly Burch, as the main protagonist.  I really have enjoyed it so far, and I hope there is quite a bit more to engage me as I continue playing through to get ready for a race. I will update this review when I feel like I have considerable more time playing.Key features: You can switch off dog sledding team deaths (essential in my opinion when playing a game about a dog sledding team), diverse behavioral traits of dogs, teaching players to properly respect moose (trust me, just avoid moose in the real world), interactive narrative storyline gameplay for relaxing and enjoying without the need to worry about precise aiming.Total time at time of review: 3 hours in.Current rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game with cute graphics, but I'd never call it a survival game and it's not worth the full price. It's a simple resource management game where you make A-B-C choices to survive with your dogs. It all feels like a text-based story game with some nice graphics slapped on top of it. It becomes repetitive after three or four runs, same choices, same animations, same character dialogues. Shame, because there aren't many (if any) dog sledding games, and a good (real) survival game with dogs and exploration could be a hit.On the positive side, the graphic style is really cute and simple, the music is relaxing, and the gameplay is pretty chill.

_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and heart-warming, but very short and repetitive.If you love dogs, then yes you should buy this game, but wait for when it's on sale.FYI: This does not play like other traditional games. You can't freely move around and explore the map. You're basically on rails, only to choose left or right when the road splits. It's an interactive game.GOOD- Fairly good selection of dogs, each with their own personality, weakness and strength.- Dogs are cute and adorable, and you can pet them each time you set up camp.- Every dog have their own little "story".- Graphics looks good for this kind of simplistic graphical art style.- Voice-acting. Even though it could have been better, I still very much appreciate not having to just read some text on the screen.BAD- Play, die, repeat! This is the main fundament this game is built on and is one of it's biggest flaws. You do however earn permanent buffs for the next runs, like more supplies or additional equipment. It wouldn't be that bad if it wasn't for the next bad flaw which is;- Repetitive and fairly limited selection of encounters/events. As you try again in a new run, you will see many of the same things with the exact same outcome over and over again. Listening to the same dialogue each time becomes annoying too.- Shooting game mechanic is kinda bad! Press the action key when the dot is in the circle. Sometimes the dot will barely get inside the circle.- Map is borderline useless. It's mostly just to get an rough overview of your progress.- Very short. Took me about 4,5 hours. If you want to adopt all the dogs and complete the whole journal, then it will take a lot longer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of negative reviews for this game, but i honestly loved it. I would only reccomend buying it when its on sale, since it isn't really worth it at full price, since it gets a bit repetative.Its a very pretty game, the dogs are amazing. I wish there was more dogs to choose between, but its an indie game, so i understand why there isn't.Very calming game that you can play when you're stressed. After you've had a few runs you don't have to worry about much, just achievements. More suited for "chill" gamers, not those who are used to FPS shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I genuinely loved the communication with the pups and the beautiful storytelling, but I find it a huge frustration that there are too many intentionally malicious events that take your meds, bullets or energy. I understand that the devs must wanted to portrait the real life decisions that reflects the irreversible paths we make in the real life, but COME ON this is a storyteller game! A moose just popping out of nowhere only to strike me down or the shooting circles never meeting each other for all 4 rounds is something that I cannot make difference with my effort.Nevertheless, I'm fairly satisfied with the experience and sincerely wish that more various events to be added in the future updates, but with reasonable difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game while it was on a 60% off sale. I would say the value is definitely worth that, however I would hesitate to say that about it at full price because I don't think there is enough content to justify it. It is a great game - story driven with minimal controls. I thoroughly enjoyed it. It was an easy, ambient game to multi-task with while completing all the dog's story lines (the best part, in my opinion).
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and sweet. Choose your own adventure style gameplay made into a unique exploring and survival game. Never played anything like it and came out very pleasantly surprised. Gives me the vibe between The Long Dark and Firewatch, worth doing a lot of runs, very trial and error but never feels crushingly punishing as it rewards you for learning lessons through trying and failing. Cute content after finishing the story and the ability to complete side quests you passed on the main story run. The story isn't mind blowing or anything but it's kind and earnest. The dogs are all characters and are of course very cute and their personalities affect the events and outcomes of situations you find yourself in. The game is also so beautiful and very creatively stylized. Again, don't expect a WASD movement style survival game, you select dialog and choices that are acted out but do NOT let that deter you from playing. I feel like that style of gameplay is fitting for a dog-sledding game and is still compelling and immersive.Also, yes; You can pet the dogs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric game, gives me SO much nostalgia for my childhood in a cold part of the world. I really appreciated that it balanced the reality of wilderness survival without going over the top edgy about it; you have to respect the wildlife and the environment because it has genuine dangers, but at the same time, the vast majority of wildlife has no desire to go out of their way to hurt you unless you disturb them first. It's really sweet getting to know the different dogs' personalities and I love the little details that show up in the journal as you discover more about the dogs and the wildlife. It's obvious that a lot of care went into it.It's cool that I could totally imagine myself as a kid being obsessed with this game, and I still enjoy it a lot now. There's something refreshing about it just being a way to experience a journey through the wilderness with your dogs; a lot of different people can enjoy it for different reasons. I do think it would be most fun for people who like to play games through the eyes of the character and imagine their own story alongside what the game gives you. People who prefer more structure, or who like super strategic survival games, might not feel like it's the right kind of challenge for them. I absolutely love the more sentimental/creative/poetic vibe of this game, personally, and I would recommend it to anyone who also tends to like that kind of atmosphere.I think it'd be great to see a sequel or additional content where you either get to repair/maintain the cabin using supplies foraged during your runs, or where you can participate in long-distance races along different routes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: So I bought this game while it's 60% off since it looked really appealing. Unfortunately the game is quite disappointing. cons:- storyline makes is subpar; absolutely naive and gulliable main character (e.g. not bringing basic tools for survival while knowingly embaring on an "expedition" in Alaska)- very limited controls, could be technically called a visual novel with extra steps (no sandbox experience, instead you click through options such as investigating or moving on)- same events but with randomly generated outcomes - while hunting if you decide not to do anything and preserve your bullets, your MC will shoot anyway at air or groundpros:- if you have a problem with "action games" or you need a slow paced game with little engagement in controls then this is a game for you - ambience is alright and of course who doesn't like dogs :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO. CUTE!  It's very scenic and relaxing, the danger elements don't feel overwhelming, and I've had a lot of fun filling out the journal. For me the price was certainly worth it - I've payed way more than 25 bucks for way less than 6 hours of this kind of fun, and I haven't finished the game yet. If you want a challenge, high stakes, a deep, dark plot, if you hate collectibles or side quests - this game is not for you. It's chill, a little funny, and showcases a wonderful art style and gorgeous music. It's mostly quiet, and you can safely zone out and let the scenery go by between choices. It's a little bit like a visual novel, with the added bonus of getting to pet dogs periodically. If the devs ever release a DLC with new mushing routs or dogs, I will 10,000% be buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!I could go on and on about the story and mechanics and how amazing everything is. The character is relatable and, I mean, come on... FLUFFY DOGSMy only qualms is there is no guide to finishing the journal and I cannot for the life of me find what I am missing or how to get certain achievements that are for events on a randomizer and there seems to be no way to trigger these specific eventsOther than that this is a really fun strategy game and an enjoyable story
_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game for what it was, which is a largely on rails, light-survival rougelite. It doesn't give the player particularly complicated choices and it's a pretty easy game (you will lose at first, but that's only because you start out unprepared- not out of any inherent challenge), but I personally don't mind either of those factors. If you want a gritty, realistic survival experience, this isn't for you. If you want a fun, low-pressure game with some survival aspects and dogs that you can pet, you'll probably enjoy it. It's more of an experience than a challenge- buy it if you think you'll enjoy the beautiful atmosphere and themes of finding yourself, skip it if you want in-depth gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: The Red Lantern is a great game and I would diffidently recommend this game. It has a nice story and some awesome dogs to choose from to go sledding with you,  unfortunately once you reach the cabin there isn't much to do other than adopt other dogs to go sledding with you and start it all over again. I personally believe there should be more options added or when you reach the cabin and go out sledding again, that its different every time instead of it being the same things in the same places. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. I know it's going to be one I 100% complete. The art style, the dogs, the organization needed, it's all very enjoyable. I would not pay the full price for this game- I waited for it to go on sale, as it's a shorter game that's fairly repetitive. It takes a good few playthroughs to see everything it has to offer, which allowed me to sink a good 7 hours into this game to get all of the tools, but still not 100% the game.Although I ran into some issues with loading the game, like some others have, the support was very friendly in troubleshooting with me over 10 days. Zak, the person who I was conversing with over email, helped me find the files I needed to delete to reset my saves and make the game playable again, while staying patient with me having absolutely no idea where to start, as well as me having issues finding the right files to send so that the rest of the team could try and find out what's wrong. Overall, my very non-concise review wraps up into: it's a very pretty and amusing game to sink some hours into. It runs too expensive without a sale, though, so wait for one. Although it still has some issues, the support team is very friendly. if you're into any of the tags listed in the story page, it's definitely a nice game to check out, and I was overall happy with my purchase even with some issues.

_childDocuments_.name: The Red Lantern

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I did enjoy having adorable dogs with me - and listening to the main character talking here and there, the exploration part of this game is what let me down. Still, what I did enjoy was: the ambience, being able to choose my own team of dogs (there's quite a number to pick from), the dialogue spoken by the main character (although she can at times talk a lot) and the art style of the game overall.What I disliked however is: that you can't make any movements yourself - which I would have enjoyed rather than yelling "Mush on", "haw" and "gee" constantly, it is quite difficult to ration out everything you have resource wise (sometimes after dying you will get more resources added - but not necessarily the ones that you feel you really need to make a run), the map isn't the easiest to read at all and only seems to update once you've reached a marker.Still it is a fairly good game, but I just wish there had been more movement allowed as it felt so restrictive. _childDocuments_.review: The game is cute. It managed to take the roguelike formula and cleverly use it to make an ambient narrative experience. It does this by letting the experiences you have out on the trail turn into prep for future runs. This prep gradually reduces the boundary to fail, until you are a resource rich enough that most threats are a non issue. This way, it keeps even the least rigorous players moving through new content at a decent pace.There are only three downsides of this little gem:-Its pretty short? Both time wise, and in terms of content I got to see. I wanted more narrative, more character development. I really loved the parts of this character that were in the trailer, and the parts you see in game. But there just wasn't enough to make me feel like it was actually there. This was made better/worse by the fact that Ashley Burch did an incredible job, as always, with the voice acting. Got excited as soon as I heard her voice in the trailer.-You're not actually racing in the Iditarod. That was one of the things that made me want to play the game, was the idea of going on this super cool endurance race with my dog bugs. Instead you're going on like a three day training run to a cabin that was left to you. When you finish your 'training run', the credits roll, and its not like you can then race in an actual dog race. You can just replay the training run repeatedly.-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bears. Because the mechanics aren't really deep at all, and all of the progression elements you find SIGNIFICANTLY declaw said mechanics, whats left is to just punish the player by rolling dice. This takes the form of you just sometimes randomly getting mauled by a bear/gored by a muskox. In these events, you can sometimes walk away with some food, but mostly you just get injuries. Injuries are important because if you get 2, you die. You can fix them with medkits, but you only have 1 medkit until more than halfway through the progression ladder, and you don't really find more. This means that sometimes you lose your run, even though you have tons of food, extra bullets, and lots of other supplies, because you roll three unavoidable damage encounters in the same game, which is very common. I almost stopped playing because I lost two consecutive runs this way when I otherwise would have cruised through to the end. The first run I won was the run where I started with 2 medkits. It *really* feels like they did this just to prevent players from winning on their first try and refunding the game if I'm being honest, which is pretty frustrating. My last run wasn't really fun, and I was reading something on the other monitor while listening to repeated dialogue, and just clicking whatever. I finished with like 18 meat, 4 bullets, a wounded dog, and my character was also injured, meaning that I was one injury from losing, again. Major points lost for this sloppy design.

_childDocuments_.review: Game good! You can pet the dog.  Strongly recommend!For developers (minor issues I encountered):- Please add a reminder in the (options?) menu about the game's buttons. Whatever UX you have to teach us the controls wasn't sufficient for us, because we had to press random keyboard buttons to figure out that C is the "Setup a Camp at the next trail marker" button.- After several hours of playing, when we finally got to the end, we got soft locked at the "Welcome home." dialogue... so we never got any credit for beating the game. I think my Player Inputs were being consumed by something that wasn't the UI (Escape/Select was working though), so we couldn't progress and see the end credits. Doing "End Current Run" didn't fix the UI issue, either. Had to quit out the game and restart!- After getting the dog booties, the game became super easy. It feels like there's no point in trying to beat the game before you discover the dog booties! So there's a balancing issue there.- All I want is Zen Mode! It's frustrating that I can only do it by beating the game... and then when I _do_ beat the game, I get soft locked and then I can't do it. I recommend that you give me credit for beating the game _at the very beginning_ of the final cutscene so that I can ensure I will have Zen Mode even if something bad happens, like what happened to us!

_childDocuments_.review:
The Red Lantern is a story-driven, rogue-lite, survival game where you and your team of 5 sled dogs, lost in the wilderness, must navigate the ever-changing encounters of the Alaskan bush to find your way home. Features:
- A dynamic world that changes as you play
- Nearly 100 different encounters each with varied results
- Gain items and upgrades as you discover things about the world around you
- 8 different pups to add to your team, each with their own personalities.

name: Wingspan
detailed_description: Wingspan - Relaxing Strategy Card Game About Birds for 1 to 5 players. The officially licensed digital adaptation of Wingspan, the winner of the prestigious 2019 Kennerspiel des Jahres board game award. You are bird enthusiasts—researchers, bird watchers, ornithologists, and collectors—seeking to discover and attract the best birds to your network of wildlife preserves. Each bird extends a chain of powerful combinations in one of your habitats. Each habitat focuses on a key aspect of the growth of your preserves. In Wingspan up to 5 players compete to build up their nature preserves in a limited number of turns. Each beautiful bird that you add to your preserve makes you better at laying eggs, drawing cards, or gathering food. Many of the 170 unique birds have powers that echo real life: your hawks will hunt, your pelicans will fish, and your geese will form a flock. Features Relaxing strategy card game where your goal is to discover and attract the best birds. Single player and multiplayer modes for up to five players. Based on award winning, competitive, card-driven, engine-building board game. Hundreds of unique, animated birds with their real life sound recordings. Multiple ways to accumulate points with birds, bonus cards and end-of-round goals.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: I haven't played the board game version).Highly enjoyable, beautiful, relaxing strategy point-salad game!  It's fun right away and there is enough depth that you can spend time mastering if you so choose.What I do like:Replay-ability. I've now put in 30 hours and I'm still having fun. The end-of-round goals change per game, so you always have a new objective. You can play multiplayer (with other people or AI), automata, automata/multiplayer hybrid, and online. Lots of set-up options to keep it interesting.Game strategy. The tension in this game is trying to pick between which essential things you want to do (play a bird, lay eggs, get food, get cards) and having diminishing turns to get stuff done, while also competing for end-of-round objectives. Where it really gets fun is working out how to maximize bird powers/bonuses to build up chains of activities that extend what you can accomplish on a turn. Mechanics: There are a lot of detailed mechanics you can get into with this game. It's very clever. You can use food to buy eggs, eggs to buy cards, and cards to buy food. You can stack bird powers to cascade. The rules / gameplay all work seamlessly and are very well done.Art, Visual Design, and Music: The art is incredibly gorgeous, with beautiful bird and wildlife illustrations and animations. I LOVE that you can click bird cards to hear the bird songs. I love the bird animations. I love music and SFX. Super calming and relaxing.What I did not like:The tutorial. I found the tutorial to be very detailed, mechanics oriented, and long, while I wanted to understand the big picture strategy first before getting in the weeds. It is a very thorough tutorial, I just ignored it and learned by playing.I also read a review that says the end game is a bit underwhelming - I tend to agree with that. In the final round, it's difficult to focus on growing your habitat - the last few turns often feel like a slog to get eggs laid.The last thing I didn't like is a very minor complaint - in the bird archive, you can't see birds you haven't played at least once. I only have 5-6 unplayed cards, but I have no idea what they are and I can't be on the lookout in-game to collect and play them. The completionism in me finds this annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so pleasant both in person on the table and here on the computer. For players of the physical game, you may prefer the play format here that most imitates the real life game; however, the special format for the virtual version offers more interaction with the art backgrounds and fun animation of the birds. The virtual game plays the birds' real calls which is a lovely touch. The game's music itself is wonderfully peaceful. I find this game to be a perfect way to wake your brain up over a cup of tea or coffee in the morning. If you are new to Wingspan, the virtual game is both cheaper and perhaps more accessible than the physical game since it can directly walk you through the gameplay (but I recommend getting the real game!). Noteworthy, I used the discount code from the boxed game to purchase this. Looking to add the European expansion soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game with an identical flow to the physical board game. As someone who had first played the board game, it was easy to get into the digital version, there are comprehensive tutorials that outline all the functions and basics, however strategy is very much left to the imagination. It helps to have someone who has played before to guide a new player through in terms of strategy and long-term planning, since it is crucial to winning. The experience may be complicating and seem cluttered with the screen board layout, but once you have completed a few rounds you"ll be planning your moves ahead in no time! A soothing mellow soundtrack also puts you in a birbwatching mood!Highly recommend for casual board game enjoyers, birb enjoyers, and anyone who likes strategy based deck building games. Good birbs, interesting perks, and a refreshing experience everytime since the goals and opportunities are always randomised. Playable with friends IRL or online through steam (Though online can be shoddy at times). A fun and decent AI mode is included as well. (Where i spend most my time, mostly on the hardest difficulty)9/10 - Birb Game

This game has one of the worst interfaces I've ever seen.  We know the rules of the game well, but two of us played the first game side-by-side and time after time we couldn't figure out what to do or where to click.  Several times we somehow did the wrong thing and couldn't recover.  Many of the icons don't work at all, like the ones at the top where you supposedly can see other players.   We tried a second time with a third online player and after an hour we had to give up.  No one could figure out how to start the game.  Once we noticed that one player had a mysterious fourth player, while the rest of us had three.  Buggy as hell.   We play other online board games that we like a lot, like at dominion.games.  Online Wingspan was a complete waste of money.

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan is a beautifully rendition of the board game.  There are five different habitats (background graphics) where you can play the game.  The music is just soothing and wonderful.  The goal is to create an Audubon reserve of birds in their natural habitat.  There are three separate sections within your habitat where you can look for food, lay eggs and draw unique birds (over 170 different types).  The game has trivia about birds, the sounds the birds make and even geographical data inside the menu.  The game might look at first to be complicated, but its rather simple to learn - the in game tutorial is great to teach.  Points are scored in many different ways: from the value of birds placed, the amount of eggs you have laid, milestones to be met four times during the game, an objective card unique to each player, left over food, etc.  This makes it dynamically rich to plan your strategy and score points to be declared the winner.   Each card has a unique special ability that is activated during certain times of the game.  There are predator birds, but they do not interfere with another player's habitat, which makes it a rather friendly game.  If you like birds - its a must have game.  If you are looking for something a big more zen, that you can cozy up to with a hot chocolate or iced lemonade depending on the weather, its the game to play.  Average real-time play, about 2-3 hours with three online players (5 minutes in between turns) or you can pick a longer 24 hour per turn based option for meta gaming strategy.Plus an expansion is coming soon!  What's not to like?
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game! The art is fantastic, the music is soothing, and the gameplay is great. An excellent game to play either solo or with family and friends in local hotseat. The AI puts up a decent fight but I haven't seen it go above 90 or so points - after you put some hours under your belt you'll win most but not all of the games. Then there's the option to play vs the automa (a single player mode from the physical boardgame) which really puts up a fight, although I don't like it so much because it plays with a different set of rules. There's also multiplayer but I haven't tried it so far.

This game is highly recommended for those with a lot of free time.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art work and lovely instrumental soundtrack makes for a calming experience. Love the animations of the birds, and with the recent expansion, the ability to replay each bird's calls. The variety of birds is wonderful (even if the skills may be somewhat repetitive if you only have the base game). The gameplay itself can be quite strategic, and took me a while to get the hang of, but is something that I enjoy as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of my top-of-the-list board games. Beautiful artwork, catching theme and great game play. I was pleased to see that all the beautiful artwork was ported into this digital implementation. Also, very sadly, I have to say that the positive things about this digital implementation ends here. To be clear, this review is about the multiplayer implementation as this was the reason why I purchased this game - to be able to play it with friends remotely in these days (I own the original board game and we played it many times). So the multiplayer was essential for me and it is just terrible. We tried to set a 4-player game multiple times without success. First, the invitation goes via Steam, which may be inconvenient and little finicky, but ok, I can live with that. But the game is so buggy that we were not able to even make our first move. When I finally got into the game, I didn't know who's move it is, what are the player's names, what is the order.. And when it seemed it was my first turn (after selecting starting resources and bonus card), I just couldn't do anything despite I was getting tooltip hints what to do if you want to do this or that action. But the action just didn't work. It just blows my mind, how this multiplayer version could make it into public. One would think that if you are not even able to make it to the first move, the QA would catch it right away, no..?As mentioned earlier, I only tried multiplayer. Maybe the single player, or AI is great, but if you want to play this game with friends remotely, save your money. Sad :(
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: The digital version really helped me understand how to play the board game.  This game is pretty complex.  There is a limited number of turns each round and planning ahead (even for next round) is pretty essential to scoring.  Each habitat offers a unique reward type, which increases with the more birds you place in those habitats.  Habitats offer either food, eggs or draw cards.  The bird cards offer their own rewards when played.  No two games play the same at all.The art is pretty beautiful on the board game and the digital version has animated cards and bird sounds that adds to the enjoyment of the game.  This version should be in every board game lover's collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I had nine hours with this game to think about what kind of review I wanted to leave. If I had to describe this game in the fewest of words. It feels like a game that was made in Poland, then localised poorly to a north american audience by and art school graduate. I feel like I should be wearing lens-less glasses (while wearing my contacts) while playing this game. Vegan hipster monopoly? I'm not sure how to describe it. So, here are a few of my take aways.Concept - Sure. I dig it enough that I bought it.Execution - This game is both good and bad. It does have some decent strategy and can be fun. But the game is very not intuitive. And you know what? Fault on me, I didn't play the tutorial. I didn't notice it when I went in first, and had zero hand holding and no instruction. I failed my way through a couple games enough to learn some of the basics. I could almost functionally play the game at this point. By the time I found the tutorial it was so slow and insufferable that I couldn't stand to wait through it. Not because I wouldn't learn anything. I have to believe with how convoluted the rest of the game is, the tutorial has to explain everything. Maybe. But my takeaway here is that they don't have a glossary. Or again, maybe they do and I didn't find it. But when you see that certain skills activate "brown powers" (literally what it is called, brown powers), or just context-less symbols in a ability description with no idea what that symbol means and no quick way to reference it, the game becomes no fun.However, I thought it was balanced well enough based on my playing. There were some combinations that felt overpowered/broken, but my experience is limited and I never did get better at the game.The art is decent. The bird art is quite nice honestly, The bird sounds are very nice (and minimally varied, meaning you wont hear the same soundbite over and over), but the backgrounds and the rest of things I would say are passable. Nothing really special honestly, but they work.Here is the TLDR which I am deliberately putting at the end. I don't know who this game is for or what it is competing against. I wouldn't even call it as exciting as monopoly, and with great classics already I guess I don't see where this one fits in. I suppose the market is over-saturated as it is so what is another on the pile.But I don't have that feeling that this game SHINES in any unique way that you cant get elsewhere, except one. If you want a card game that you play with birds on the cards, with tiny pieces of sometimes oddly related trivia but really decent voices for the birds, then sure buy this game. But the game isn't super fun. It is kind of addictive, but I find you not really feeling any sense of accomplishment after. Sort of like Solitaire. I would call this Bird Solitaire.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I own the physical copy of the game as well and I have to say I love both versions! This digital one is well made. It's very easy to play and accompanied by beautiful graphics and music. I love seeing the birds move, listening to their calls and hearing the bird facts. Having this version of the game also allows me to play when the rest of my household is unavailable to join me.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I love the boardgame. I hate this implementation. The interface is incredibly clunky and annoying. If I hadn't gotten this as part of a package I'd return it. Fortunately, I got other games I enjoy in the package. I'll gladly delete this and just play the boardgame. They list it as "relaxing" but I think "frustrating" is far more accurate.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great board game and they did a really good job of converting it to a video game. I especially enjoy how they read out the little lore tidbits that are included at the bottom of the physical cards in the board game when the cards are played, rather than just having those few lines of text directly on the cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Loving this game! My friends and I started with the physical board game, but living far away from each other, this virtual version makes it easier for us to connect :)However, multiplayer really needs a few touch ups to increase the quality of life when playing with friends:- When a player creates a custom game and invites other players, please update the player cards with the players profile if they've accepted the invitation. As of right now, there is not way to tell if they responded to the invitation without verbally confirming with them.- The invitation feature for custom game is still a bit wonky and at times, some players fail to enter a game even if they accepted the invitation. Furthermore, if the custom game creator or any player enters the game before everyone accepted, then we have to restart the game because that person cannot join. Similarly, if an invited player click on the custom game before the creator launches the game, they cannot join the game thereafter.- Please allow all the players to take the first turn at the same time. Before the game actually starts, players need to select the bird cards and resources they chose to keep. As of right now, players have to wait and do that step one a a time. Please let us set up our game at the same time and start the game when we are all ready, or at least allow us to see our cards while we wait, so that we can make our decision and be ready when our turn arrives.TLDR: Multiplayer custom game needs a few improvements to make it more reliable and user-friendly, but the game is a joy to play alone or with friends and I highly recommend it! Graphics look beautiful, music is great, experience is amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Once you get the hanging of the game, it is addictive in a good way. You are able to learn at the same time you are playing. We went camping this past weekend and were able to pin point certain birds and their sounds. I wasn't sold on it at first, but now I can't put it down. The only draw back is I would like to play it on my android tablet too, but can't. If you want a good game for older children and to have them learn at the same time, get this. We a have the actual board game too that way we aren't always on our electronics. We didn't have great  internet connection while camping, so I was great to have the board game with us.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I held off on getting the board game for some reason I cant remember. I played it with four members of my family and they loved the game.  Now with my tendency to play a game over and over until everyone is sick of it I went and bought the digital version. I am very pleased with the purchase. The interface took a little time to get used to. Several family members have played hotseat with me and have yet to tire of it. I play quite often against four ai. Ai is competitive. _childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan Digital is a delightful game.  I've played the digital version solo only, and the board game with 2 & 3.  Both are highly recommended.  There is a healthy dose of luck in the form of which cards, food, and bonuses are available to you.  The strategy comes from the decisions you make regarding which types of birds to put in your aviary, what to focus on.  Some of the backgrounds have interactive elements, and I feel all of them should have that.  A minor quibble, however.  Worth buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to develop a round based strategy games which stays thrilling till the last round.Wingspan got it right.Easy to learn, hard to master.It's fun to play alone vs computer and with other people, which is possible via internet or locally on one machine.Drawings/Animations are beautiful to see and music is very calmy. A perfect game for a round after work/in the evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan might seem like a simple concept: Get food, play birds, lay eggs. But it is a deeply strategic game and winning takes a lot of planning and thinking.I only play against the A.I., but the game is still fun and enticing. The artstyle is beautiful and the birds and their "powers" are very well crafted.Love it and hope for expansions in the future, might even buy the boardgame, this is just so damn good.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Great implementation of one of the most pleasant boardgames to come out in the last few years.  The weird conditions in the achievements are fun to aim for, even if getting some in any given game requires a fair bit of luck.Beautiful artwork, as expected.Possible downsides - the AI is generally not very good.  I've had one or two games against four Normal AI opponents where one of them managed to get a decent score (high 80s), but otherwise they don't put up much of a fight.Sometimes struggles to start up.No in-game highlighting of which birds you have(n't) played yet - makes filling out the collection hard, since there are so many.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, calm and relaxing board game. Don't let yourself be fooled, its a strategy/engine building game. There is a automated mode with pre-defined action and a different scoring system. This automa mode make more sense if they didn't already have had an AI. There are two type of online gaming, in-real-time or delayed where the opponent can take his time to play. After all, this game was thought with the bird-watching mindset. The cards are meant to educated about birds in a useful manner and the added audio makes it fun to associate the songs and sounds to the actual bird without waiting in a bush for 4 hours. I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting, complex, engaging game with beautiful, and some not considered beautiful such a vultures, birds, scenery and realistic game operations.  It reminds me of poker in that if you get a good draw of birds at the start, such as one in the forest that provides additional food, you can go far.  Also, like poker, there are so many options that even if you don't start with great birds there are ways you can improve your situation.  It takes quite a while to get the feel for how to always do well, which I like.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I never knew of a board game. I am a birdwatcher and was excited to see all the birds. The tutorial kept "freezing" on me so I didn't get the full grasp of the game. After 5 games verses the computer AI I started figuring things out. The game goes fast, since basically you can only do 1 thing per turn. I guess there will be a picture mode one day? Maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Big board game player. Wingspan is an OK game. It's nice to look at and relaxing. The card engine is just OK. The Steam adaptation is quite faithful to the tabletop game. There just isn't enough meat on the bones for me to get excited about and it's fairly anti-climatic. I'll play it if I'm tired and don't want to have to use my brain a lot to enjoy a game. I tend to play it just after waking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t even know how to start this review. I guess that why Steam doesn’t have “mixed” option when submitting review. Because that’s what I would like to give this game the most.First the good stuff. Wingspan is very beautiful game. The art, the music, the commentary. It’s all so calming and pretty. It’s also very well polished. No lags, no bugs, everything’s smooth as butter. Controls are perfect and even tough this is originally a tabletop game you will have no trouble playing it on PC.What’s problematic is the actual gameplay. I find the biggest issues in multiplayer. The game offers asynchronous multiplayer (72 hours per turn) which is probably fine (haven’t played it) and real-time multiplayer. Except the real-time has 5 minutes per turn limit, which is way too much. In extreme cases, you will wait 10 minutes to make one move you had already planned out beforehand. One game of tabletop Wingspan typically lasts about 60 minutes, here you’ll play first 2 rounds this long.Another issue is karma system, which is extremely unrewarding. You start with 50 points out of 100 and it will take you 50 games to reach 100 karma. One point per game! There is no scaling. And the game treats everyone the same. You can finish 1000 games, still after quitting a single one you will loose 5 karma points. The biggest issue is, that reasonably skilled players have higher karmas, so even if you now how to play the game (i.e. you come from tabletop), you have to sit through at least 15-20 painstakingly long, slow and boring games to reach somewhat competent players. But, this is still nothing compared to the biggest issue of online games, which are the DLCs. Even if you don’t own them, DLC content will be part of online games. If you are like me, you only own the base game and you never player any DLCs, the game will just throw you in the game full of new mechanics without any warning. And there is no way to select which DLCs you want to play with. You have to either play with all extensions or don’t play online at all. For me this means I will never return to the online games, as I have no desire to play DLC content. I own the base game, I want to play my base game online but it’s simply not possible.Games against computer sadly aren’t a good enough remedy for multiplayer, as the AI is simply not good enough. Even the hardest AI is too easy. You have some chance of losing, but you will win approximately 95% of games.I can’t give a positive review. Wingspan is not bad. The game works flawlessly, has no technical issues and the gameplay in its core is fine. But, the multiplayer issues are a big deal and especially players coming from tabletop version need to know about them. They closely resemble some of the scummy practices of gaming industry and this can't be ignored. And devs, seriously… Why can’t I choose which DLCs to play with online? What the hell is that? Fix it…

_childDocuments_.review: An alright adaptation with a lot of quirks.The way this game wants you to play it is awkward and inefficient. You can see one habitat at a time. Thus, you have a limited view of your board state at any one time, and it unnecessarily takes multiple keystrokes to just look at another row of (up to) five cards. On a small screen, this is frustrating. On a larger screen, it's inexcusable. The space is just wasted.Happily, you're given options and there's a decent strategy view that works pretty well. You still cannot see all the relevant information on your own board at the same time, however a single keystroke provides the next best thing. That keystroke, as far as I can tell, is determined by the developer, with no in-game means to change the keybindings. This is a disgrace for a PC game (and is frustrating if you, like me, use a nonstandard keyboard layout). Fortunately, you lose little time by using mouse inputs. Viewing cards in hand is nightmarish if you build up a large enough hand. This needs immediate attention.Viewing other players' boards is cumbersome. It's definitely not a priority most of the time, in most games, but it's frustrating to go out of my way to do something that I do by just looking at a different board in real life. Thankfully, this isn't a deal-breaker due to the nature of the game, but when it comes up, it's noticeable.Multiplayer is messy. There is one mode where a game is completed in one sitting and another which allows 24 hours per turn. The latter needs players to be from similar time zones to avoid becoming cumbersome, however this feature is not present as far as I can tell. Thus, if you're paired with people from drastically different time zones (an inevitability for some people), then you won't have fun with this. The other game mode works well enough most of the time, but I've had some glitches arise that have broken games. I've seen some negative reviews here on the basis of the multiplayer, and if online play were a major concern for me, I could see myself hating this adaptation. As it stands, I'm happy with a decently difficult AI (though I'm not sure that's present either).Clearly, there are a LOT of flaws. It just so happens that there are straightforward ways around them or they are mostly in areas that I don't much care about. At the end of the day, I have a good time playing Wingspan because there's just enough leeway in the design for me to be thinking about the game rather than the interface 90% of the time. Ultimately, the experience is enjoyable, even if the execution is manifoldly flawed. Thus, I can recommend this adaptation to those who enjoy the board game and who, like me, are primarily interested in the single player experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite board games, and I appreciate that there is a digital version to play. The digital version plays pretty well, and if you appreciate the single player experience, it will do just fine. The AI feels relatively competitive from what I have experienced.As for the feel of the game, the way the birds move on the cards and the sound effects you hear throughout are really well-done. Everything is just lovely to look at (including the board background options - with new ones seemingly released every so often).The music is beautiful, and the soundtrack is absolutely worth it if you are looking for some soothing background music.If you are open to a mostly single player experience, then I would recommend this game for you. The main reason I cannot recommend the game in its current state is because of the multiplayer experience (that I believe others have commented on enough in the discussion boards). 1) Being limited to 3-player matches is frustrating when the physical game can be played with up to five players. I am not clear on what might be preventing the devs from allowing matching for any two to five player game.2) The timer options are too restrictive. Why are there no options for turn timers between five minutes and 72 hours? This functionality exists in other online asynchronous board games (e.g. Through the Ages) that have been out for longer. I lost 10 karma for games that I started five weeks ago and just got back from a ten day vacation where I did not have access to the game. The game could really benefit from async timer options between 5 minutes and 72 hours.IMHO, the game could also benefit from a turn log. This is a more minor point. I know you can see what your opponents have done because it briefly pops up by their avatar when you re-enter a game, but if you miss this, you need to click around a bit to see what they have done and what the results are.Whenever the devs address the 3-player limit on matched games and allow for more async timer options, I would happily change this recommendation to a positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very chill game, good for relaxing. It is entirely a card game - everything about it is something you could physically imagine and has real-world analogues. Even though some of the mechanics seem a little complicated at first, it's very easy to just pick up and learn in an hour or so. A game probably takes 15-20 minutes once you understand the interface. Music is awesome, and the voice-overs about the birds you play have tons of interesting and obscure facts for bird-lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a tonne of the board game with family, so am very familiar with how this game works. in this respect it's great when I want to play a game and other aren't available or I just want a game that's enjoyable but doesn't demand too much of my time, because the matches in this from can be played through fairly quickly. I quite like the music and bird sound effects, which i believe enhance the experience. Overall I think its a great game to chill out and relax with.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the board game. I'm really disappointed with this version.The interface is really hard to use (it seems to be designed for Xbox rather than PC). You can not see all the information at once, which makes it hard to play to beat the other players. The in-game help is just labels covering the game elements.Despite lots of patches, it seems quite buggy and unfinished. (For example, it often won't let me do anything but gain food.)
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Great adaptation of the board game! The interface is clean and intuitive. Also, there are a lot of pieces in this game, so the online version saves you set up and clean up time. The achievements are challenging, but doable, so it keeps you motivated to keep playing. Overall, I think it's a great game and worth the money. 5 stars for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great adaptation from the board game. You might get more enjoyment from this game if you are familiar with the board game, but if you don't have familiarity it can stand alone as a relaxing card game to pass the time. I haven't had much experience with online play but the AI seems solid and there are different difficulty settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It is so relaxing, it's become my new favourite thing to do during the pandemic. Some reviews mentioned it replacing Solitaire. I think it's better! I also love that it's educational, the ratio of eggs is on par to real life. The little things, like the changing seasonal backgrounds. The dev team has done a fantastic job. I just wish we could have more bird avatars to choose from!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: So laid back yet all the different combos and strategies are addicting. The animations and music are also really pretty. Online kinda sucks because of the 5 min turn timers, and a lot of people will just leave near the end of a game and it wont count. But still satisfying to play against tougher bots and automa. But what it all really comes down to is that Birbs are kinda neat. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a favorite of mine, but for the past several weeks it has been mostly unplayable on my Mac.  It seems that the latest so-called "hot fix" broke the game for people using Mac OS, and despite myriad complaints by multiple people on various Steam message boards Steam has been completely silent on the issue - no response, no effort to fix, and the support page just points you to Monster Couch, which has also been completely non-responsive. _childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played countless times with the physical version of the game I can strongly recommend this adaptation. Cute birds animations, sounds and lovely voice acting.Not only that it supports hot seat local multiplayer (like old school Heroes experience), and if that is not enough you can play with, AI, automa (single player variation), online multi player with 5 min to take a turn or even 24 h variety! You can even try yurself with weekly leaderboard :)So if you have friend who like to play physical Wingspan and dont live close enough to play on daily basis or even meet once a while to play it is definitely for you (or if you dont like engines like TTS or Tabletopia). And besides all this because it is standalone not some TTS adaptation it does every boring aspect of board game for you, so thats a huge plus :))
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: At first it is a bit complicated: why can I not win? You have different layers or the board together. But watching someone explaining the game on youtube helps a lot! So suddenly I was winning and I was understanding the mechanics. I also bought the real board game. But I must say I enjoy the digital version the most.I can play it on my own and I can play it with AI players. I like that the birds are making sound when you click on them. Also some woman is telling me some facts about the birds. I like the sound effects, it is just like outside my house at the feeding and breeding place. Different bird sounds, birds flying up and down. I also like the digital version because you do not need to think about what needs to be done now. Sometimes it works not intuitive, but clicking around till you have found the correct way helps. Also the undo button is a real help. Sometimes I really do not understand what the game wants me to do or which action I am doing. English is not my first language, but also the UI itself can be a bit confusing. But mostly I must sit back, relax, concentrate and just do exactly what I am told. After a while I get the hang for it.I also like you can change the background, but I liked it better when the game itself changes the background randomly instead of going to your picture. The game plays very smooth, but it depends on your pc setup ofcourse. I never had a crash or a bug (the software one ;)). I always turn the music off, it is nice, but after a while it is irritating. In conclusion: I really like the game. I always want to come back to play it better. And the expansian brings more options and they are different. It feels like there are more options to make the game easier/faster, but you pay a big price for it (ingame I mean). So there is the balance for me. I am mostly playing with 5 players and mostly I am winning now. But trying to change tactics resulted in loosing. Winning from the autonoma is still a bridge to far. It has a lot of replayability.I play it mostly in the evening after work. i also like to play it in the lunch break if I need to reset my brain. I have no regret bying this, it is a good adaption of the board game. It feels like you are playing the real game. So confusing at the start, but once you are past that, you can have great fun.I only play the single player part of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I've played almost 4 hours of this game and I'm so impressed at how easy this was to learn and yet how the gameplay isn't so simple it becomes quickly boring.- The art and overall feel of Wingspan is beautiful and comforting.  The illustrations are soft, watercolor style illustrations of birds and backgrounds featuring an assortment of different biomes. - The music is also soft and relaxing. It might not make a huge impression overall, but it's exactly the kind of music that works well when you'll be listening to it repeatedly while playing the game.  It's innocuous and never feels super repetitive.- It may seem a small thing, but HUGE appreciation for the achievement art and the names!- This game took me about 15 minutes to understand, which I appreciate because I'm not a person who wants to play anything so complicated I need hours to figure out what is going on.  That being said, it's not so simple that it becomes boring right away.  I've already enjoyed many games and will certainly continue to play this.- I love that when you first play a bird, they will play a nice sound clip featuring some facts regarding that bird.  I also love that when you click on them you can hear some of their natural sounds.- I have never played the board game version of this game, so I can't compare it to it's "real life" counterpart.  However, I've played a TON of PC games that were adapted from board games and many of them feel like they are missing something once they are on PC.  The translation isn't always smooth and often loses some charm.  I don't think that's the case here.  This game feels perfectly natural on PC and it doesn't seem to be lacking anything.- Highly recommend to people who enjoy card games or board games or people who - like me - just love BIRB.TLDR - Very good birb based card game with beautiful illustrations, soft and relaxing music and a very entertaining gameplay loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan is a wonderful game! It has a lot of moving parts, so there is a bit of a steep learning curve, but it's completely worth it once you get used to the mechanics of the game. Each bird card is well-designed, with various details and a colored image of each bird. It's equally fun to play with the max players as it is with only one other person. I look forward to getting each of the other expansions and having new features and birds to play with.
