I did not encounter any bugs and the AI is pretty decent.If you love the board game, this is a must have!Cons:- I'd like to know how many cards my opponents have in their hand (or say 0, 1 2+)- When playing online; if 1 opponent does not react/take his turn in 5 minutes the hole game becomes a local game vs AI... Can't just this opponent be an AI?
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: If you like birds and card style games, this is the game for you. It's based on a board game and you can very much tell. I, personally, love it. The only on I've found is in the online games there is a glitch that occasionally just skips my turn? Like, I'll wait ten minutes for the other people to take their turns and it'll just jump back to the first person with my turns dropping from 4 to 3 while I never had a chance to do anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Had to return it.  Couldn't get past the first round in the tutorial as the game keeps crashing.  Trying to go to main menu only results in the overlaying of various windows over the menus.  Have to restart the game to get rid of them.  Couldn't learn to play and just got too frustrated to keep trying only for it to crash in the tutorial . . . twice.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: After putting over 100 hours into this game I can say it is wonderful. It is peaceful, calming, lightly competitive, educational, and fun. The music is a highlight as it is very fitting for the source material. Gameplay flows well and mechanically is spot on from the board game itself. While it is not quite the same as playing the board game, for there is nothing like being in community with those around you in person (but there is local play), it is still a very enjoyable experience. Five stars for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Best board game I've ever played. I own every expansion online and in person. Great fun with 1-4 friends and can be played hundreds of times without getting stale. Every expansion is great too.One note is that this game is not the simplest game, and people who do not normally play games might struggle to pick it up. But if you're already a gamer, it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I play the physical version of this game quite a bit and the digital version does not disappoint. While it is only on the European Expansion, the fact that you can play a game anytime you want is quite nice plus the music is quite relaxing. The only downside is playing with "randoms" has often resulted in people leaving the game which replaces the rest of the players with AI. I wish the game would just replace the player with an AI instead of all the opponents. Otherwise excellent, bring some friends or meet some on the Discord!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the best. I first played Wingspan in board game form a few weeks ago and instantly fell in love. Since I'm often staying home due to the pandemic, I don't have a lot of chances to get groups together and play board games, so I gave in and bought this video game edition instead. I'm so glad I did.Fun, educational, and soothing--and a little competitive, if you're me--you collect and place bird cards to fill each habitat, lay eggs, meet your birding goals, and score points. Play against AI or other players. It's also a game (sort of like Dominion, if you've ever played that) which functions a little like "multi-player solitaire." Your board and moves do interact with other players, and I imagine you could play more defensively by snatching a card before someone else can, by making it so someone can't reroll the birdfeeder, etc., but in Wingspan, there are no truly  moves. I love games that let you focus on your own strategy and development to play your best game, and at the end, you size your game up against someone else's. My only complaint with this video game is with the interface: it's really annoying to try to mouse over the cards in your hand. The wrong ones always seem to pop up, and if you have your cursor in exactly the wrong place, they pop up and down wildly until you have it in the right spot.All in all, though, it's a really small issue with a game that I've already sunk a full day of my life into. Get it, play it. Happy birding!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This a great game my girlfriend and me enjoy relaxing with, however I finally fully filled my biomes and had the bonuses from 4 cards!Im for sure about to win, then the computer gets stuck in an endless loop on his turn not allowing the game to progress! Its a damn conspiracy the computer and my girlfriend don't want me to win ! This game is now banned from the house and I've been sleeping on the couch for a week. Also when are they going to release expansions for this edition !
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I've played and enjoyed the physical board game, so I jumped on the digital version the minute it went on sale. I love the artwork, gameplay and that I can play with my friends. I always learn something new about birds when I play and I have to admit I'm a bit addicted right now.I usually play with my keyboard and mouse, but when I moved to controller so I could relax on the couch to play, it was comfortable. It did take a little getting used to, but now I can play with either the controller or my mouse just fine.5/5 - Great for anyone who loves art, birds, strategy, and board games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: It might seem at first glance that there are lots of different parts to this game to learn, but I recommend sticking with it, because it's one of those one's that's really fun when you work it out, and it means there are lots of different strategies and approaches to try. The artwork is beautiful, the bird sounds and facts are really interesting, and honestly if learning-things-through-playing is your kind of thing then it's turned out to be really good at getting me better at identifying birds without that ever being something I was trying to do. Spotted a nightingale out on a walk today because I knew it from the game. It's a really wholesome and fun little game, and a lot more engaging than most of the others that I have got for that vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and I think this online version is fantastic! I've had a physical copy of the game for over a year, and now that I can play it on PC I can play with my friends again and still social distance. It's also a beautiful, soothing, and informative game that also involves a ton of strategy!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I got the digital version on sale to try out the game before investing in a physical copy, but now I think I might struggle to play that. The automatic scoring makes it so nice to just quickly play a round (obviously with no set up or cleaning up pieces after). Additionally, the added affects of the bird animations, bird calls, and the music make this an extremely lovely game.As someone completely new to Wingspan, my one major negative is that it feels like just as I get my engine running, the game ends. It would be nice if there were some customization options for number of turns per round/number of rounds to try to find a sweet spot.One smaller annoyance is the UI is just a little more clunky than I would like. So far, I've only played by myself against the AI, but I still need to click "begin turn" every. single. time. An option to turn that off would be nice. And there are other actions that could probably be a little less click-heavy.Still, this is a fairly easy game to pick up with lovely theming. I would highly recommend the digital version to check out the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I never really enjoyed board games, but since the holidays were coming up I figured I at least wanted to stand a chance playing so I downloaded the game on Steam and played a bit. Before I knew it I was looking forward to the family event and I thought I had a good chance of winning since by then I knew all do's and dont's. I ended up second, had lots of fun and I'm now looking forward to the next family event. This game is worth getting as a board game or digitally, playing with friends makes it even more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This game can look like it has a lot of rules and very intimidating to learn.The first game (30-45 minutes) is all I needed to learn the basic rules.I enjoy playing a round of Automa every morning because it is such a calm game to play. And it gets my brain up and running for the day =PAnother great part about this game is that the the game itself and visuals/audio play very smoothly.A lot of "board game" video games can feel very janky, the visuals and sounds feel off, etc...But Monster Couch did a VERY good job with Wingspan.I definitely recommend this game for anyone that enjoys board games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a fairly nice game but I think the experience might be best if played with friends. I only played against AI and it was fine but I felt frustrated at first as I was learning and then unfulfilled when I figured out how to win. The art and the music are both lovely. I felt that the turns/how many actions you could take each round felt too short and winning seemed to be more dependent on luck rather than strategy which isn't a bad thing but I prefer games that allow me to be more strategic. I loved learning about the birds and I think that was the best part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite board game, about some of my favourite animals has come to steam to be one of my favourite ways to experience the game. As a Fish and Wildlife student, The fact that this game actually teaches people about birds in such a non-intrusive way is something I cannot give it enough credit for, as it's not only done in a fun way unlike a lot of educational games, it's frankly addicting (even without my bias).The physical board game isn't complicated but can be a bit much at the start to figure out, but not with the steam release. the tutorial is good, but even just having the game tell you whether or not you can perform certain actions helps you learn the rules naturally without having to refer to a booklet.10/10 board game and I'd say as a port to video game format I'd also give the coveted 10/10 to the video game. Only downside is no physical wooden dice to toss in a physical bird house dice tower.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty and relaxing. I don't think it is worth ~$20 however. The tutorial on how to play the game took 3 times as long as it did to play the game. After I got the hang of what to do, each game was over pretty quickly. So for ~$20 you are getting about 10 minutes of play time and content. Can't say it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Beware... if you haven't ever played the physical game (I guess there is one) you're in for the roughest tutorial ever. Rather than teaching you slowly why you are doing a certain thing, the game orders you to click-click-click without really teaching you why you're doing anything. The tutorial is the most massive info dump without allowing you to put into practice what you're learning beyond, "click this" -> "Yay! Now here's something else!" I played for an hour, still could not get the game to make any sense, and even showed it to my SO just to be certain I wasn't being dense. We game and this game... without having some previous experience... is a hot mess. Pretty game, love the bird song, game play is confusing (and I just started Death Stranding, so trust me).

If you love birds, nature, or anything relaxing, Wingspan really is the perfect game, in either form (though the physical game is pricey). _childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan is wonderful, both as a board game and in this digital edition. It is easy to learn, yet with enough depth to be challenging. There are many ways to victory and, despite there being an element of luck in the drawing of bonus cards, the drawing of cards from the deck and the rolling of the food dice, making the right decisions is the main thing.The UI works well. The menus and gameplay are both easy to understand and navigate, the in-game information is easy to read. The only thing that is somewhat annoying is interacting with your cards in hand, the targeting of which seem to be shifted to the side. Leaving the cursor on one of the cards can also make it keep shifting between the hidden and hightlighted positions. This is no a big problem, though.As with the board game, the aesthetic elements are also pleasing. The music and sound effects, in combination with the visuals and the bird facts you get when playing a bird, makes it kind of a zen experience (and you might also learn something). A nice way to relax while having fun with a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: The level of complexity is medium and the time spending per round of game is ok (30-40 mins) compare to other board games. Feel chill when playing and I love the aesthetic style of this game soooooo much! I have wingspan on switch and this is the second copy on my laptop, and now considering to buy a third one on phone. You see how much I love this game. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This game focuses on the strategy to build up your board according to the bonus cards and objectives. What I like most is that when playing with friends it doesn't involves stealing or making them lose in order for you to win, so no bad vibes during the game :DThe music is so relaxing, I can play this without being rushed while playing other games as well
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Good stuff first: I love this game, it's gorgeous, and the sounds and trivia (though not always fun facts) are awesome. Gameplay requires a good amount of strategy and there are a lot of achievements.The only bad thing is the tutorial.As someone who had never played the board game and got the digital version to try it out, the tutorial is...bad. It's more of a "let's throw all of the mechanics at the player at once and talk about moving this cube around for some reason". Not going to lie, the tutorial kept me away from this game for months.However, going back and doing it again with the goal of "redo the tutorial" - not "learn the rules so I can play a game right now" made it a more bearable slog.After a game or two, the things from the tutorial make way more sense and it's actually a pretty straightforward game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable experience with immersive gameplay, both for relaxing time and also active thinking moments. Each bird card is sooo adorable and it has realistic birds' calls and fun trivia. Their movements are very well studied, it makes playing Wingspan can be seen as an ornithology retreat. _childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is just such a pleasant game to play with people. Pretty easy to learn how to play. It inspired me (I came to this game after seeing an Audoban Exhibit. _childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent video game rendition of one of my favorite board games. I love the simple yet strategic gameplay. As both a bird and board game enthusiast Wingspan is a perfect game for me. It is easy to learn/teach and has some very interesting progressive scoring engine building that varies in every game. The art and soothing background music are a perfect fit for the overall feel of this game. This is the kind of game you can just sit and relax and vibe with on a nice calm morning/evening. If that sounds appealing to you, I would definitely recommend you give Wingspan a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend the game. The gameplay is genuinely compelling with several polished mechanics working together and it's truly commendable how compelling learning about birds and their habitats becomes with this game. But the game itself has several shortcomings where the implementation doesn't carry the concepts involved. The big one: it crashes. Every now and then, a game cannot be continued (despite saves after every turn), because it will keep crashing. It's a bit unfortunate, but it's very rare. It is possible to overcome this.This game could learn a great deal from other card games out there. First of all, the UI is horrendous. After about 4 cards, you can no longer reliably see or select the cards, let alone see the important attributes at a glance. There's also no UI scaling option, so you're stuck with a game designed for half blind centenarians sitting on the opposite side of the room. As many good strategies revolve around card advantage, this makes playing well an exercise in frustration.  Furthermore, it has three habitats, which is nice, but there's no real reason to have them on separate screens. Especially as there are several abilities which require you to distribute objects (like eggs) globally. As for the mechanics, there are two problems. First, there's no way to mulligan. This means that if you don't draw any powering cards, like those that allow you to get extra cards/food/eggs, you're at a major disadvantage. It's the equivalent as drawing a hand of only 7+ cards in Hearthstone. You're not about to win that game unless a miracle happens.Secondly, the UI makes it very difficult to follow what other players are doing. Yes, you can see everything, but that's a large number of clicks, and you better remember everything correctly, as the game only aggregates a few things, usually things related to goals. But the main problem is, there's almost no way to interact with other players. I would have thought that a predator could eat their birds, but you can only interact via positives. There are many cards that give you resources when others do a specific thing. But, while they can be good, it won't help you catch up to a runaway player with a good start. I'm very much tempted to recommend this game anyway for the beautiful art and music, and the many hours of enjoyment that you can gain from this, but the port to PC isn't finished enough, and I cannot bring myself to support an industry that makes semi-broken products on the basis of boardgame IP.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing and surprisingly very informative as well! Highly recommend this game if you are a fan of board games that are a bit more intricate than your average Uno type board game. Very interesting game with calm and fantastic soundtrack. Great game for casual players who just want to sit down and relax to some slow paced game play and beautiful music. I have never played the physical board game but I wouldn't be surprised if this is a great adaptation of said board game. Highly recommend! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully designed game. It's engaging but not too addictive, with excellent replay value. I play mostly with the AI, which on its hardest setting can beat me occasionally. Without playing other humans, your strategic insight will plateau, but the AI game provides enough stimulation to be both interesting and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so first off the underlying game is good. It's a board game, so things like 'absolute number of eggs a given bird can lay' are slightly abstracted, but it takes its theme (birds) pleasingly seriously. e.g. the bonuses individual spp give relate to their irl behaviour and traits -- they aren't 'gamey' (no pun intended.) So, no handwaved e.g. 'building a road out of sheep' moments like Catan. Kingfishers get you fish, vultures score off other players leftovers, fruits seem to be a tad harder to acquire (being seasonal) etc. The underlying mechanics are sound, but it's this fidelity to the theme that makes it so cool imo. Furthermore, this is a really good adaptation, with lots of thought and care gone into it. The cards - already pretty due to the really solid artwork and stylistic direction of the board game version - are charmingly animated, and the reproduction of the birds' irl calls is an obvious but awesome touch. Not being able to see your whole board at a glance makes it a bit less convenient than the original version, at times, but it's not a huge hindrance or anything. I'm not mega into birds, but I like the game a lot and will for sure get my money's worth. I'll almost certainly get the expansioin once it's available. I can only imagine bird people get even more out of it than I do, so if that's you, you should def pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks and plays amazing, the artwork is great and the UI is easy to follow. The tutorial can be confusing at first but after a couple of games it's easy to learn the different elements and strategies. Every game feels different as the round aims change each time. If you enjoy competing against AI and gaining achievements this game is for you. It would also suit casual players as games take approx 20 minutes.I cannot however recommend the game in it's current state if you're purely wanting to play online with the community. The multiplayer is currently restricted to minimum round timers of 5 minutes & 24 hours. It makes the game drag out as your opponents are likely to AFK or play multiple games at once. This means in a game of 4 players it could take 20 minutes a round when in reality it only take 4-8 minutes MAX a round. You can invite steam friends which would eliminate this issue but if you're a solo player it's frustrating.Unsure if the developers are going to implement changes to the online play as there are a lot of forum posts complaining about the multiplayer needing to be changed but no action has been taken. I suspect they are prioritising an expansion/DLC rather than making changes the community is asking for... but hey which developer isn't doing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much a flawless port of a board game to a PC game.   Tutorial was pretty excellent, which is very important because the gameplay is a bit confusing.   Highly recommended for people that want a relaxing non-stressful turn-based game to play against Bots or human players.  Also recommended for people that want to learn how to excel at the board game.Minor quibbles:    1.  I think the tutorial should spend just a few more sentences at the beginning explaining what you are trying to accomplish.2.  I think the different between playing a bird and activating a bird is very confusing and should be explained better.3.  Selecting one bird card from my hand with the mouse was buggy and in at least two games it lead to me playing the wrong bird.   Meaning that as I move my mouse around and various cards jump up, sometimes it was difficult to get the card you wanted.Minor quibbles, though.  Excellent game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic adaptation of a stellar board game that adds to what is already in the game by having the audio of the various bird calls (usually more than one) per bird, voicing the trivia, and handling the tedious bits automatically.In addition, the developers have really worked to fix glitches and bugs. Yes, some took more time than desirable, but they did fix them. Further they continue to bring in the expansions that dramatically change the dynamics of play.Value: look up what buying even the base physical copy of this game costs and how often it is out of stock. If you know anyone that even slightly likes birds and plays video games this is an absolute steal. Finally, playing against the AI, has made this my version of solitaire. After a thousand plus hours, I think I can say I enjoy it with, or without people.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Great digital version of the amazing board game. Love the bird sounds/animations, ambient music, the sleek UI. The creators put a lot of thought and effort into making this game what it is, and when playing by myself I actually prefer it to the board game since the setup is much easier and the pace of play is faster.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I love the boardgame, but as a computer game it does not work for me. Everything is "too prompt" and I do not understand what exactly the opponent did (at least not without hard study). Shame, I really wanted to like it. Also, two questions: Why does it seem the AI has more than one move? And why do I always lose against it, even if I had the better cards and tactic? It is really annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since my friend introduced me to this game, I've been OBSESSED! Wingspan is quite possibly the best boardgame I've ever played and this digital edition is nice so you can play against the Automa and AI. It stays true to the board game's rules and allows you to play cross-platform which is really nice. I'm anxiously waiting the arrival of the European Expansion so completing the available achievements has been a nice challenge in the meantime. Some downsides I see to this digital edition is that I don't believe there are any statistics of your games being kept. There is a way to save your games so that you can see them later in the Preserve Archive, but what would really make the game amazing is the implementation of graphs and stats on all of your games. Things that would be cool to see is average points, minimum score, maximum score, average birds played, eggs layed, etc. It would be a cool feature to keep track of your progress in terms of strategy! One other critique I have is that the hard AI is just straight up broken. They will often score very low ~30s-40s and seem to be worse than the easy AI. I think there must be something wrong with the algorithm.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Editing my review now that I've played more.Pros: REALLY addictive gameplay and a super cool premise. I love strategy and I definitely recommend this game for those who like turn-based card games. The art is pretty and I like the trivia/bird sounds.I really love the singleplayer in this game and I love playing it while listening to music.Cons: Multiplayer is painfully slow since each person is given FIVE WHOLE MINUTES to take that turn. When against bots, or even against other people who can play faster, the game shouldn't take as long as it does - but matching up with people makes games drag on for so long that I just would rather leave.But I CAN'T, because the karma system punishes you for doing so. So multiplayer is basically untouchable.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice implementation of the physical game. I don't actually own the board game, but I believe it's a good implementation because I quickly understood what I was seeing despite having never played before. Just a nice clean, visible layout and you can get a graphical overview of the entire game with the click of a button.If you're not familiar with the game, it's basically laying down cards in a tableau to score points. There are 4 shared competitive objectives and you also have 1 or more personal objectives to help increase your score. You lay down birds which each have different point values, many of which also have powers which activate during play, some of those actions involve stashing food and utilizing other birds to gain points, there's also egg laying for scoring points and completing objectives. I highly recommend this one.It's a banger.Edit: Multiplayer is realtime 5 minute limit or asynch 24 hour limit.Edit: And it has turn notifications. Yay!Edit: No chat in multiplayer. Boo! But no dealing with insults from other playersl. Yay!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Good job making the card games I liked in the past look like dirt.This game is deceptively good, Don't let the bird skin fool you.The automa is great and so is the steam remote play.I also enjoy the bots and am glad there's a beta version of a hard mode bot.Great game overall.Works great on phone too. The zoomed in view makes it very clear on both mobile and pc screens.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I just played my first game of the new Digital port of Wingspan (which I purchased on Steam). What an amazing port! A notable bit of attention to detail: They implemented BOTH the Automa "bot" rules that came with the physical game and a video-game-style AI player (both with selectable difficulty).The music is delightful and the game is BEAUTIFUL. There's very well-recorded voice over of the 'flavour text' on all the cards about the birds that are read out when you play them. The UI takes a little getting used to but is well-featured with a lot of information available once you get the hang of it.It does feel a little more like "competitive solitaire" than the board game, since you can view other players' states, but they're not all spread out in front of you at all times.Overall, this may be the new high bar for electronic ports of board games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for hours and I absolutely adore this game. It took a few for me to fully understand how to play, but now I know how to. I even went ahead and bought the actual board game for Wingspan because I love it that much! The cards are beautiful and the whole game is fantastic! Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: As far as digital versions of table top games go, this is TOP. The game mechanics are essentially identical to the board game, however the audio visual, especially the animations and bird noises, in the game adds so much that you just can't get from the table game. The programmers and artists involved in this deserve an award.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I own and adore the physical Wingspan game. This electronic version is true to the original game but offers additional features, such as themed music in the background and the sounds of the birds as you play them. During the Covid shutdown, we were able to identify birds in our yard because of that feature just by listening to their song, even when we couldn't see them in the trees.  The play is smooth, and it even helped me realize a rule or two that I didn't have quite right in the physical game. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved the physical board game Wingspan for several years. The game is beautiful, and as a birder it compliments so well with my hobby! But I've had lots of friends who didn't know the first thing about birds love this game. The Steam version by MonsterCouch is everything I could have hoped for!!! It keeps the beautiful artwork of the game, and makes what is indeed a complicated game a bit more maneuverable for new players. I love the little sounds the birds make when you play them, or click on them, or even make in the background after you've played them. When your forest has a Downy Woodpecker, you can occasionally hear it, and remember who's in your nature reserve!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT PLAY MULTIPLAYER UNTIL THEY FIX THE -LEAVE- BUG.  When you play online sometimes it shows that the timer for another player is running out but in fact its your own timer. you ll be kicked and loose karma for it. ultimately making your online experience miserable because you ll be tagged a as leaver and matched with people with the same tag.  FIX IT ALREADY.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I played this first as the board game! It's a bit intimidating when you look at it for the first time but its very easy to learn and super fun :)All the birds are super cute and the mechanics of the game are very well balanced. Even if you're a beginner, you can easily play against someone with much more experience and not be left too far behind in the dust. Highly recommend getting the expansions as well, stuff like new birds and nectar are very handy and make the game even more fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Very strategic, peaceful, relaxing, interesting, informative, and fun. I highly recommend if you have any interest in birds or just enjoy chill games. I love the soundtrack and the illustrations. The information about all the different types of bird is cool and I love the fact that every time I interact with a card, that particular bird's song plays. Super fun and informative for someone who loves to play casual games and loves birds and beautiful artwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only recommending this because once on sale, the price is reasonable. This game is entirely reliant on multiplayer and good players because it's too small to be able to stand on its own. Progression is utterly bland, and the in-game objectives are uninspiring. It is however not a bad game, similar to how something like Mine Sweeper is not objectively bad. It's just that with how it's packaged, you would expect that there would be something more. Core game mechanics are good, and if you enjoy games that rely on foward planning, you will be satisfied here. But there is little that justifies the regular price. It's not as if they spent a great focus on ambience and scenery to meet the shortcomings, as both are just average, leaving more to be desired. The trivia is also rather shallow, not educating you all that much. And I would advise most to steer clear from the DLC because you get next to nothing for them. It's a direct transition from boardgame to PC, without bothering to integrate any elements of a proper video game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visually nice implementation of a great boardgame!What I love especially about this incarnation of the game:+ Sound - from the voice reading descriptions of birds, to background music;+ Ai as an option instead of (killing me both here and on the table) Automa;+ Hey, I can play with a controller! What bothers me:- Ai is waaaaaay too easy to beat. Please add more hardcore version;- Playing with a controller can be tricky when a habitat for a bird needs to be selected;- That I can't purchase the WHOLE soundtracks at once (please, take my money!)
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite board game! In the computer version I really pay 0 attention to what any of the other players are doing, I just try to do as well as I can on my own, so maybe you lose some of the competitiveness that way, but it's okay. It only lets you trade 2:1 food items when playing birds rather than at other times which I would change, but that's a very minor nitpick.
_childDocuments_.name: Wingspan

_childDocuments_.review: Wingspan is a relaxing, award-winning strategy card game about birds for 1 to 5 players. Each bird you play extends a chain of powerful combinations in one of your three habitats. Your goal is to discover and attract the best birds to your network of wildlife preserves.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could like this, I really do. So many people love it and I do see why. I hadn't been sold on the first one but I decided to go ahead and just try it anyway since I heard it improved so much and I got it on sale. Unfortunately, it just... misses the mark for me.The things I love:The controls - amazing. I love how ori moves. It's so fluid and responsive, it really is a joy to run and jump around without slowing down, especially when you get a couple abilities to make it that much more fun.The visuals - beautiful. I love the art style used, it really is whimsical and really feeds into the world's wonders.Unfortunately thats kinda where it stops for me.Firstly the combat. There's a lot of it. You'd think this shouldn't be an issue but if you so much as walk off screen and come back, the enemy you just killed is back. That is just plain a nuisance. This wouldn't be SUCH a problem if the combat was even enjoyable but it isn't. It's just button mashing over and over. This isn't fun.Secondly the gameplay itself. It's just... boring. Never ending running back and forth, it's not even actually puzzles. It's just painfully tedious trudging back and forth. That just plain isn't fun, especially paired with the boring and also tedious combat.Thirdly the story. There really isn't much of one. I know i'm playing blind since I only played about 30 minutes of the first but I'm pretty sure I have a decent enough idea of the story, regardless. It's not bad at all and normally would be totally acceptable, but paired with the otherwise boring game play and it just can't hold up.Overall, whenever I pick this up to play I just feel bored and like I'm just trying to push ahead to see if anything interesting is about to happen, and it never does.I'm not too far in, but I feel like I'm in enough hours in that it should be more interesting by now.I spent money i don't have to waste on this game so I'm going to keep playing it.But honestly I would wait till it's at least 75% off before buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Jump'n Run Games and you played Ori and the Blind Forest, buy it!!! One of the best Games I ever played.Edit 20.04.2020:I have now 61 Hours in this fantastic game and completed all Steam-Achievements. I had two or three times noted some bugs, were the game hangs, but this is not a minor issue for me. They added with the new patch the Track Quest, so you have to make a quest (which i didn't find) for quick travel now. This is okay I guess, but a little more help where it could be, would be nice.I still got wet eyes at some video scenes, as they are so nicely and emotionally done. The music is one of a kind and soooo wonderful.I definitely hope they will continue with this franchise. Still for me one of the best jump n run games.Thanks Moond Studios for this wonderful game. I will jump back to Ori and the Blind forest and try to achieve all achievements.Have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, it is an excellent sequel for the most part but there are some not so fun parts.PROS- Very pretty. I love the art and ambiance. The graphics separate the parts that glow and parts that don't in a beautiful way. The animation is also very smooth.- Good story, but makes you cry sometimes :(- Fun mechanics. Kind of difficult, but if you get the hang of it it's kinds fun to just zoom around.- Very cute bearCons- Bosses are ridiculously difficult. They take hours of grinding to beat if you do not have enough health cell thingies. They have 2-3 times the amount of health they should and feel almost unbeatable.*- Some areas of the map are generally difficult, but it is intentional, just maybe turn down enemy difficulty if you don't like grinding*I don't know if this was patched or not, but there is a glitch to become temporarily invincible. If I remember right, you dash  into an underwater enemy at the same time as drowning and when you respawn you should be invincible :)Overall, this game is very fun and I really enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up upgrade over Blind Forest. Firstmost the controls are so much better, remappable without going into .ini and actually making sense. That was a terrific change.Secondly, this game incorporated some little questing and treasure hunting with subsequent buying and upgrading, all that over a much larger map. Shame like half of the skills are utterly pointless.Last but not least, soundtrack is again amazing and amplifying the feelgoods as well as the feelbads.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: A great improvement to the original. The combat is a lot better, You have more and better options, and the movement system also got improved, making exploring more fun.Just like the first game, this game is also one of the most beautiful 2D games I have ever played.I do wish the world was even bigger, and if you wanna get all upgrades, you need to grind a lot of Spirit lights.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and The Will of The Wisps, simply just amazing.The graphics are even more breathtaking than before, being one of the best looking games I have ever played.Gameplay-wise, it improves on the first game and it does it in a good way.The music, amazing.The story, makes a grown man cry, also, very much, amazing.Although one thing does bug me:All in all, 9,9/10, just for that minor detail
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Has more bugs than Hollow Knight despite it not being a game about bugs, pun intended. I expected sth better from an established studio especially when this is a sequel. Ori and the Blind Forest didn't give me enough feelings to write a review for it, but this one is a big hot mess that I have to rant about. There is a scripted fight in Luma Pools where the game locks you in a room and spawns enemies. A fish spawned inside the ground and was stuck. I didn't know what I had to do until I watched a vid and found the fish (I had to wait for it to swim close to the edge and used bash to kill).Camera sometimes does not follow Ori, which is extremely annoying since we all know there are tons of traps and spikes in Ori games, and one time I almost died bc the camera took some good time until it moved while my Ori was taking damage offscreen.Visual got all messed up when I was doing one of the spirit trials. Seriously the screen was like some kinda of mosaic art or modern painting. It's ridiculous.I also want to comment on Ori and the Will of the Wisps' combat, which as compared to Blind Forest is indeed more interesting. Things become more fun when you unlocked grapple and bash. *But* the arena is sometimes poorly designed with safe spot that enemies have difficulties reaching you while you can hit them with your spirit smash. Bosses lack uniqueness as many of their attacks are fundamentally the same (Mora's laser and Kwolok's swallow attack both taking up part of the arena horizontally, projectiles of most bosses, etc.) I expected more diverse attack patterns from bosses. I wanted bosses that could leave strong impressions with both their character design and *the actual fight*. Since people praised the combat in this game a lot I guess I got overhyped and expected too much.If you take away Ori's visuals and platforming it really doesn't have much to offer except a tons of bugs. And they also ruined the fun of platforming by having some very annoying spirit trials.Edit: okay so I finished the game (last 2 bosses were more interesting, I'll give them that, but a bit too easy) and the map told me that I had 100%'ed every area but I didn't get the find all collectibles achievement. Apparently the map is bugged too. Great.I restarted the game, loaded my save file twice, and got the achievement, cool I guess?
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option. I can’t say this is a bad game. It is an improvement over the first part. However, I can’t also say this is a good game. It suffers from many of the same issues as the first part. Part 2 does go a few new places and is less annoying than part 1, but there are some new issues. The game gives you way too many weapons and add-ons without really have any place to use them. What’s the point of that? The game also has a tendency to be cryptic to the point that it’s not possible to figure things out. More than once I had to turn to the internet because I had no idea of where to go, what to do, or how to do it. It’s like the game developers didn’t beta test the game with real people. This game could have been outstanding, had they put more thought into it. I kept thinking about the Arkham games while playing. Now, those games were well planned out and designed. The mark of a good game is if you’ll play it again after beating. I will NOT be doing that.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely amazing game. While I'm a huge fan of Metroidvanias in general, this one really takes it a step beyond most others in terms of story. There were a handful of moments where I was unclear what to do next, but exploring stayed fun, and the upgrades kept things constantly fresh. A couple of the platforming parts had me scratching my head, but nothing was impossible. Don't worry if you didn't play the first. The story here is complete and shows you all you need to see to understand the world. I highly recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: So, out of a star system I would have to give this game a 3/5. Do I love it? yes. But it makes me SOO mad sometimes that it sucks the joy out of playing it and I literally have to stop. I think they over complicated the controls and moves. To do anything you literally have to press the dash,jump,bash,up, down, space, grapple ALL AT THE SAME TIME. I have spent HOURS wasted doing the same thing trying to get to a certain area FIFTY TIMES. And you literally can't progress in the game unless you progress to the next area. They seriously need to make some changes and make a bit easier to get from place to place in the game. I want to love it so bad because the graphics and story and overall gameplay are amazing. But I am quitting it for now unless they change it to be a bit more enjoyable and smooth gameplay instead of having to try the same thing fifty times and get so mad I quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommended! A huge improvement in every aspect of the game since the first game (which is fantastic too) the combat is fun and challenging, but not too hard, the platforming sessions are great and even though I died a few times it was so fun that you don't even care too much.the game itself looks fantastic and has an awesome soundtrack that grants you the best experience that you could ask for in a game.the story is appealing and connects the player with ori and many other cool characters all over the map. a great game overall 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game - A 10/10 in it's own right for the pure satisfaction the many challenges this game brings you, from movement to combat to puzzles that make you feel pretty smart.If you enjoyed the first game, you will LOVE this game. As for a Metroidvania game, this game really brings the spirit of the journey, and the trials and tribulations that naturally follow the genre, to life. The adventure is there, you will not find all the collectables easily on a first playthrough although there are elements to help you find said collectables. The combat is fun due to a mix of different abilities (using varying amounts of energy depending on the strength of the ability) and, although the melee combat isn't as naturally platformer-based as Hollow Knight, the combat is unique in its own regard and provides extreme satisfaction when combined with the movement. The movement is much more free flowing than the likes of HK, allowing a significantly higher range of motion during and outside of combat -  I even refrained from unlocking a fast travel option for quite some time, due to enjoying the movement so much.I played on Hard mode and I will attest that the difficulty was pretty challenging at times, but not hard enough to where it became overly frustrating. There ARE boss battles and as long as you have the patience to learn the move-set, it will be extremely rewarding when you finally succeed (I did all boss fights in approximately 15 mins, on average).(I also suggest playing on Hard mode if you enjoy challenging platformers - the difficulty is worth it, in my opinion)I appreciated this game so much that I used all of the abilities at my disposal to zoom around the map for that satisfying 100% profile (which I rarely have the energy to do) as soon as I completed the story. Unlocking an ability and instantly going to certain areas previously unreachable felt extremely fun, truly living up to the excitement the genre can hold.Highly recommend this game to anybody who loves Metroidvania titles, especially so if you favour them for exploration and movement - the combat is an extremely sweet cherry on top, more fun than competitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't common for a sequel to be better than the original. Ori and the Will of the Wisps is definitely an exception to this common trend as you jump back into the familiar world of the first game. While there are a couple of abilities that do make a return such as the bash and sentry attack, Ori is blessed with a plethora of new weapons, abilities, and seemingly endless ways to explore this somehow improvement to the Blind Forest. Whether you're new to platformers, or a seasoned veteran, this game caters itself to being enjoyable no matter how you play it. A definite 10/10 for anyone who is even considering not buying it, and I can't wait to replay it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Why have you not played this yet?That aside, this is one of the best games I have ever played. The setting is incredibly immersive, the art is jaw-dropping, and the music is astonishingly good. The gameplay doesn't fall short of that either. Nor does it fall short of the first game, Ori and the Blind Forest, which I'd recommend playing first. The combat is smooth, the controls are intuitive, and the metroidvania elements are very well set up. And the story? Oh ho ho. The story! Let's just say, I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: This is a two-dimensional puzzle type tower game that were so popular back in early 2000. But..- The art is insane- The music is inspired- The story is simple and satisfying- Progressing through the game is fun and smooth- Literally so many cool mechanicsThis is a two-dimensional puzzle type tower game the way it's meant to be designed.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a masterpiece. Everything from the gameplay to the graphics to the sound design and music is so well made to the point where I could probably consider it one of the best, if not the best singleplayer game I've played in a really long time. This game improves on everything from the previous installment of the series, from the smooth movement to the engaging combat. And the animations are even smoother and well tuned. The beautiful landscape and atmosphere are also much more prominent in this game.tldr: just buy it lol

_childDocuments_.review: ~ DIFFICULTY ~🔲 My grandma could play it🔲 Easy🔲 Normal✅ Hard🔲 A challenge to be reckoned🔲 In the heat of confrontation, treat your opponent with respect~ GRAPHICS ~🔲 MS Paint🔲 Bad🔲 Meh🔲 Graphics don't matter for this game🔲 Good (nothing special)🔲 An original artistic direction🔲 Beautiful✅ Masterpiece~ STORY ~🔲 This game has no story🔲 Basic element of the contractual requirements🔲 It's there for people who want it✅ Well written🔲 Leading to more in-depth researches/thoughts~ LENGTH ~🔲 Long enough for a cup of tea🔲 Short✅ Average🔲 Long🔲 To infinity and beyond~ MUSIC ~🔲 Just filling noises/No music🔲 Trivial and uneventful🔲 Memorable🔲 Transcending whispers of a forgotten world✅ Mesmerizing, Soothing and enthralling~ INTEREST ~🔲 I would rather watch paint dry🔲 Hard to enjoy🔲 Repetitive and/or uninspired🔲 A good moment🔲 Sticking out of the pack✅ You will remember it forever~ BUGS ~✅ Never heard of🔲 Minor bugs (Sound/ FPS drop issue at certain areas )🔲 Can get annoying🔲 Impacts the player's experience🔲 The game itself is a big terrarium for bugs~ REQUIREMENTS ~🔲 You can run it on a microwave✅ Low🔲 Average🔲 High end🔲 NASA computer~ PRICE ~🔲 Free✅ Perfect Price🔲 Could be cheaper🔲 Overpriced🔲 Complete waste of money~ WORTH BUYING ~🔲 No🔲 If you have nothing else to play🔲 Wait for sale✅ YesThis game was not what I was expecting. Seeing the screenshots and the style of visuals I was expecting a sort of cute take on Inside. However, what I found was a incredibly good atmosphere with even better game-play. Similar to the classic Sonic games, there aren't many things more satisfying than when you are gunning through a section of the map using dodges, double jumps, grapples hooks and much more all the while escaping purple projectiles with a mesmerising soundtrack playing dramatically in the background. This is easily one of my favourite games. Although there aren't as many abilities and variety as a game like Hollow Knight, it more than holds it's own with how it uses them, insisting that the world in which Ori travels through never becomes tiresome. The game is not "hard" however to those who are not versed in video game knowledge may struggle with the direction and the intention of some of the puzzles. But not once in the game did I ever feel as though as I was wasting time such is the beauty of this game. To conclude, once you fire up this game, you will be yearning to continue exploring through the brightly coloured lush of the forest and the game won't ever let you down. It is simplistic and yet has incredible depth which makes it a truly loveable game.

_childDocuments_.review: So good that when I first played it using familiy library sharing, I decided to buy it for myself just so i can leave a positive review.The story itself may not be too complex, but I easily forgot about it thanks to how beautiful graphics and OST wise this game is, and also because... It's just fun.If you're a sucker for a good metroidvania, then this is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the most frustrating game I have ever played.  It's just mindless bashing of buttons hoping you'll land in the right place or hit an enemy you're aiming for.  How on earth its rated so highly is beyond me.  Looks and sounds great, but game play is terrible.  Map is next to useless.  Very unclear as to what you can or can grab or walk on.  Extremely disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers for the story of Ori and the Will of the Wisps.Once upon a time I left a good review on this game. But I just can't do that anymore. The way the story dunks on so much of what Blind Forest set up is just awful. Not to mention how the antagonist of the game is portrayed in a surprisingly abelist way. She's a tragic villain, yes, but she has no retribution or self-healing of any kind. No happy ending. Just thrown away because she's the villain and thus must deserve a terrible end. All she did was be born disabled, get bullied for being disabled and acted in accordance to her treatment. The least they could've done was shed some kind of non-tainted light onto her.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is an incredible metroidvania. It's definitely much better than the Blind  almost every single way. The combat feels way more satisfying and controlled, and I love how you get more weapons and attacks as the game progresses. Also, the exploration is a huge step up from the original game, where the endlessly annoying Sein is always telling you where to go--meaning you don't really get a chance to explore at all. But now the map is bigger, and fortunately Sein doesn't exist to show you the way you're supposed to go. So that means you're free to mostly explore on your own...until you get another annoying sidekick! Another amazing change in the sequel is the addition of boss fights, which just didn't exit in Ori and the Blind Forest. The art and music was never a problem in the franchise, but I'm glad to see they're keeping the beautiful and stunning art style.Overall, I give Will of the Wisps a 10/10. It's nowhere near Hollow Knight, but it's still really good.It's not that I hate Ori and the Blind Forest, it's just that it was a little too linear and the combat was mid in my opinion. (I would give that game a 7/10 or an 8/10.)Usually the sequel is worse than the original game, but Moon Studios perfected almost every aspect of the Blind Forest.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite improvement over its already stunning predecessor. It has kept the bar sky high in terms of everything visuals and audio related, while also improving the combat making it engaging and fun (something that the previous game lacked) with a decent bit of variety and customization thanks to the shard system, a concept very much like the charms in hollow knight. In line with the first ori game, the platforming does not disappoint, with both returning abilities and mechanics as well as new ones, it allows for fluid and fast paced gameplay. There are some much welcomed quality of life improvements, such as the ability to warp to spirit wells from anywhere on the map or an improved saving system. All the new characters are loveable, setting the stage for a couple of emotional moments along the journey.Overall the game makes it easy to want to 100% it if only to spend just a bit more time in this stunning and fun to traverse world.

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is freakin fantastic and easily one of my favourite games ever.The game is a direct sequel to Ori and the Blind Forest and manages to evolve the gameplay and concepts that were established in the first game. Ori controlls and handles much like in the first game but with a much more expanded combat system. Instead of being stuck with a basic spirit flame attack you have access to a wide arsenal of weapons and skill to utilize, making the combat in Will of the Wisps really quite satisfying. The combination of fast-paced platforming and smooth combat blends together into a sort of chaotic dance, and it is so much fun. The game sports a larger world and expanded enemy roster which helps to spice up the experience. The forest of Niwen is a completely different land from Nibel. From gloomy swamps to vibrant springs, the game truly excells when it comes to the enviroment and level design.And I cant forget about the soundtrack. Oh boy. It's amazing, I'll just leave it at that. For me, Ori and the Will of the Wisps is truly a special game, and it will never leave my memory. It's something everyone should have the pleasure of experiencing on their own.So what are you waiting for? Get cracking and play these truly stellar titles (if you somehow missed out on the Blind Forest as well).

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first game.I mean, it's still very good. Pretty much everything that made the original good is here too! Beautiful graphics, a lush (albeit unmemorable) soundtrack, fast-paced platforming and metroidvania exploration, memorable setpieces, an emotional story, the whole lot. If you liked the first game you'll probably like this one too.I mean, it does also repeat quite a lot of what the first game had to offer. The graphics do look better but there isn't a lot that's visually distinct from the first game in the presentation besides that, and the story kind of focuses on the same plot beats... dying forest, first thing you have to do is purify the water, evil bird who is the main villain, someone is hurt/dead and that's the impetus for the rest of the plot. Even at the very end, the last bit of gameplay in this one is almost identical to the first game's ending.What this game does different is.... hollow knight. It's just hollow knight x ori. That's really it. An uncomfortable amount of mechanics are straight out of hollow knight here. The game moves towards having a proper combat system, which, well it's fine enough but a lot of the time bosses seem to heavily discourage melee combat in favor of ranged combat, which doesn't feel as good. The visuals are often way too busy for what they're going for - hollow knight and similar combat-oriented metroidvanias have very clean visuals that make it so much easier to parse what's going on onscreen.And this game has the shards system which is functionally identical to hollow knight's charms system. Start out with three slots,  about 32 or so different options, you can expand your slots as you go. No real problem with this as it's a good system and the upgrade mechanic associated with it is neat too.You also buy maps from a wandering NPC,  which, well in hollow knight it was cool because it would show you some things but not everything. Here, like the first game, it shows you pretty much everything except secrets. I have no clue how the map NPC got to all these places to make these maps. Cornelius in Hollow Knight reasonably would only give partial maps as part of the flavor, leaving you to fill in the gaps. I liked that. I know it's technically not a change from the first game, but still!On the subject of NPCs, yeah,  this game has them after the first game... well, didn't. And they give you quests and dialogue and worldbuilding and all that. Again not something that hollow knight specifically has laid claim to but it is styled pretty similarly as well.One other mark against this game is that it just does not run well, at least for me. Maybe it's my outdated GPU but I've run more graphically intensive games just fine, whereas with this one I have to downscale the resolution to get it to perform well, and even then there are some parts where it just... won't, no matter how much I downscale. I actually waited a month just for the performance patch, which only seems to have minorly improved things for me, but at least it made the game playable, which it originally just... wasn't, in places.I also wish the world was more interconnected like in the original - there were areas that jutted off to the side but there was a lot of connective tissue between them too, and the map was nice and dense for the most part. Will of the Wisps has a  more horizontal and linear map. It corrects for this by having an even further improved warp system from what even the DE of the original introduced, and I appreciate that change a lot, as well as changing to a normal save system instead of the "place your own" saves of the original, 'cause... yeah, that was a bit unnecessary. I also do like how at about the halfway or so point of the game, it shifts from a fully linear progression system to letting you choose one of four branches to go  down (albeit minus points for locking off half of one of those branches behind the other three).I also am not a fan of how stingy the game feels with spirit light - this time around, I had to actually farm for somewhere in the ballpark of 8k light just to finish up the last upgrades, which is TEDIOUS. That was after getting 100% completion everywhere else, mind you. Really feels like it should be more balanced around what's actually regularly available.As far as new mechanics they're again hit or miss. I really like the dig mechanics and the water dash as well, adds just more fast-paced energy to an already pretty fast game, and a lot of the slower mechanics of the original like rock pushing are minimized in this one. I do not at all like the grapple mechanic though. It's annoyingly context-sensitive and very delayed to the point where if you grapple twice, even before the first one activates, it will always grapple you a second time, usually back in the direction you came from. Especially annoying during chase sequences. I dunno, wish they just stuck to the bash.There's other mechanics they introduce and then abandon just as quickly related to combat mechanics. The bow and arrow is a good all-around weapon but aside from some early-game puzzles it's relegated only to combat after that. Same with stuff like the light aura and the energy sphere, and the gust mechanic the feather gives you is even moreso underutilized. The game feels a bit overstuffed with mechanics to the point where it can't give all of them time to shine, which, for as mechanically overstuffed as Guacamelee 2 felt as a sequel as well, still seemed to have a better grasp at how to juggle all its mechanics.What else. I really like the speed trials. I wish there were more of them, really. The boss fights are mostly pretty solid, and I dig the mini-chase sequences that occur in some of them. I don't like how you're only limited to three combat moves at a time, and one and two of them are always gonna be the melee and bow & arrow (at least for me), so the third is usually "whatever this level needs me to us for puzzles" unless I'm fighting a boss. That feels a tad limiting. I also wish quests were better indicated on the map - I had some quest-required NPCs not even show up on the map period and had to look up what to do next because I became completely stumped.Oh and I hope you liked the cameos from the first game's side-characters at the start because that's pretty much all the relevance they're ever going to have to the rest of the plot. A lot of the plot points felt a bit predictable overall really, aside from the ending which seems to come out of nowhere and probably exists just so people won't go "make ori 3!" I understand why they'd want to move on, but it seems almost like a late-production decision the way it happens.Anyways yeah. I liked this game. Maybe it'll even be one of my favorites of the year, as I do plan to replay it at some point for the remaining achievements. I don't love it quite yet, though, and it never captivated and impressed me in the same way the original did, but that's in part due to how much of a retread it feels like, and how the rest of its identity is pretty handsomely cribbed from a different game entirely. It doesn't feel like the game is as unique or special this time around, I suppose. It's still plenty worth the money, it's still a very good game, but for as much "more" as it gives it seems to lack focus and polish in some key areas. Not that the original was perfect - that's part of why a "definitive edition" exists at all, here, but regardless. Good, but not great.

_childDocuments_.review: Historic Review: Games I played months if not years ago – I decided to start reviewing right at the end of 2023! Memory of a trepanned, ADHD toddler with impulse control issues notwithstanding.Teaboy's Basic(ish) Reviews....I read a lot of reviews when looking at games on Steam, and it quickly gets tiring – those who write involved, down to the micron scale reviews, although helpful, end up like looking at War & Peace when you’ve only got time for a quick 5 minute dump! This is middle of the road and to the point – not easy for me as I tend towards sesquipedalian loquaciousness! Vociferously Verbose? Alright, verbal diarrhoea. (Although I hate panning a developer’s work and all the time, effort and love they put into designing these – it is their life after all – this is my honest, personal opinion of my level of enjoyment. Sorry devs!).A note on time played: My Steam clock does not seem to work properly, indeed, it even minuses time on occasion! Plus, I have a tendency to wander off and leave games running at times, so time played may not be entirely accurate!Teaboy’s Tonsil Titillators or Toenail Titbits! (Rating)Tonsil Tickler (Totally Tops): The frenchy of which you always dreamt! To quote a master, “She’s got a tongue like an electric eel and she likes the taste of a Man’s tonsils!”. An absolute masterpiece and joy to play.The Tits (Terrific): Everyone loves playing with these! Not THE best bit, but such fun on their own you can be lost for hours....mmmm. What most games you really like score – perfection is so rare after all.Torso Teaser (Taker of your Time): It’s a flat stomach....sure it’s nice to look at, run your fingers over, slobber on a bit, sometimes that bellybutton gets your motor running....but it's just basically the corridor between the two ‘gaming rooms’. The definitive ‘Meh’ - the middle ‘sideways thumb’ option for which everyone on Steam cries.Todger/Tadger & (scroTum) Taters (Tedious): Is it an ‘a’ or is it an ‘o’? Who cares! The meat can be fun to play with for about 5 minutes of your entire day, the rest it just hangs there and generally gets in the way of doing something else. The main problem of course, is the two veg sticking to your inside thigh. This is what this game feels like – the occasional/rare bouts of fun, the rest bobbing like a 19th century British Policeman (now you know why!).Toenail Tornado (Total Toss): A playthrough so appalling it’s like being trapped in a Turkish sauna with the ugliest, hairiest, fattest, sweatiest beast of a neolithic hominid who’s trimming his toenails using pliers and the splinters are reminiscent of a scene from the Normandy Landings. My god how did this get released!?Teaboy Touts (Score): TONSIL TICKLER!!!!!!!!!!!!The Review:This is for both Ori And The Blind Forest & Ori And The WIll Of The Wisps (they are effectively the same game).I think this is my Favourite Game Of All Time - hence the dozen exclamation marks above (my fave number)! When I played the 2nd one, I preferred the 1st, and I Still LOVED IT!This is an action platformer that is more platformer than combat but plenty of both - unlike things like Blasphemous which to me is just hack n slash. This one requires learning and skill with a bit of timing to boot. Both games have the same controls and movements and map type and controls. The differences are obviously a different map (same layout format) and a change in the skill progression. In the 2nd game you purchase upgrades from a couple of creatures and you have to juggle abilities by selecting appropriate ones as you go through the game (there are many more than 1st game). I'm not much of a fan of this, after playing Baldur's Gate on the Playstation 2 with my brother (we always pronounced it Bal Jers - sounds so much more fantastical than the Boulders they pronounce it in game!) so many times as we Loved it, then the sequel introduced crafting and we spent So Much Time in the selection screens reading n swapping n forging....it totally destroyed the flow of the game. Luckily, Ori is not like that, it's much more basic/easy, but due to my personal experience I don't like the interruption. But for others it adds choice. It also is necessary for progression on a few occasions.Other than that, both games are pretty much a continuation of each other. Playstyle is identical, which is the Perfect decision by the devs because the first game was Excellent. Don't fix it if it ain't broke! You increase a dual power bar as you level up, allowing more/stronger abilities. The abilities you get are great fun and vital at the same time - they get assigned to buttons of your choice as you unlock them.A lesson to newbies I learnt the hard way - if you can't do something/get somewhere, it is because you yet lack the ability! I tried for ages to get places until I finally learnt that I had to go somewhere else and earn an ability! So if stuck, go to another area of the map you've yet to do. Trust me, you'll find a new way to jump or whatever and then you go, "Ahhhhhh!NOW I can go to that other place." In the 2nd game I deliberately upgraded one skill tree to get a particular ability I knew from the 1st game makes it so much easier, however, I could not get it after getting all the upgrades it required....it was the same old story as above - some abilities are earnt through in-game progression, you have to open a part of the map/do something/complete some quest AND upgrade! Take note!Movement speed is super important in platformers as many games are so sloooow.  This game is, yet again, perfect!  You move quickly, and the abilities can boost that significantly.  This is important as the map is large and there are, in my opinion, too few jumpgates.  Still, going back and forth is a lot more acceptable than most games that force you to backtrack.  The hardest part of this game is finding all the hidden items which will be the greatest reason for backtracking.  There is sadly a single glitch in the 2nd game whereby about half of players, myself included, could not 100% the game as one 'complete the set' never goes above 97% (one gem short kind of thing even though you've found them all).  The action AND platforming can be frenetic at times, which is actually massive fun. Boss battles can be a bit annoying - like a side-scroller where you have to learn the right way by dying constantly and repeating. This the ONLY flaw in this otherwise perfect game in two parts!And the music....the opening title screen tune....It is heartbreaking that it is so short - it's one of the most brilliant little tunes I've ever heard. Pure joyous magic.Sadly, it seems from the ending that they will not be making another. I'd buy it without a second thought if they did. I wonder if it's like Batman and Halo - originators didn't want to spend their entire career developing the same game so handed it over....and they got worse. Still, I'd buy it and hope!Finest gaming experience of my life. Absolutely loved Ori - it's nothing like those nasty peeps from Stargate^^

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great platforming adventure. Art style is beautiful, we see new landscapes and ori can aquire new abilities in this game. I'm unhappy that so many commands are put so unintuitively into the keyboard though. When you play through the desert, and you learn digging, it's set on ctrl just as your ability sprint. The menu always put an exclamation mark next to any key that I'd try to assign instead. It feels buggy to have them both on the same key. When you miss lose objects in the air, that you need to dig into (they are more like a jump board when you hit it with digging), you gonna sprint away from your target, because yeah you sprint then, and lose so much proximity, that you often need to do a whole rerun of a race of obstacles. Also, objects on the minimap just disappear randomly. I'm certain there's a specific key for that as well, but on the map menu there are no keys assigned that would do that. It leads to portals not being shown, so I can't always port when I open the map. I'm also disappointed, that the plot building remained just as weak as in the first game, if not weaker. Sure, they gave you many npcs that you can now interact with, but usually they don't even have names, just their race name appear above them. Instead of letting a player choose when you level up abilities, you have to go to random store owners that trade your orange collectibles for abilities. They don't all own the same abilities, and also, there's no specific order in which they are represented. This is an unneccessary obstacle for upscaling abilities. An ability tree like in the previous game would give such a better understanding what to scale next. And generally, I wished there was more of an overview possible for this game, all the side quests feel kind of messy, they can only be checked on the map. They are discovered randomly, and most often also completed randomly. It's like the opposite of linear, you have so little need to focus on something specific, that there's no reason to explore one world entirely, except when you notice you should have improved certain abilities needed for that world, but bad for you, you need to look for one specific npc to get the abilities from. I'm sorry to give it a thumbs down, it's really not a bad game. But there are weaknesses I try to address. If there are only 2 options to rate, so be it.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this I 98% the game on normal in about 11hours take that as you will but I loved the game and I think it was worth every penny.PROS:- The gameplay is still super tight and fun.- The story is still fantastic.- The game is still like playing a beautiful painting.- Borrows solid game design from other popular 2d platformers- Still has plenty of speed-run potential as well as leaderboards for midgame time trials.CONS:- With the right combination of passives Ori becomes an unkillable god.I found the more actiony direction this time around made the game easier but that probably won't be the case for everyone and it's not necessarily a bad thing.I still loved the game and it's a solid buy if you enjoyed games like Hollow Knight and especially if you enjoyed the first one!

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a medium option for this game, I would give it that. The game does improve on the original in many ways, but left me unsatisfied as a whole. First, the storyline was just not as good. All of the dark moments had no meaning, as they could be fixed with the will of the wisps and the game never got me invested enough in these new characters to care. The ending was also just unsatisfying and felt like an incomplete end (and an early one) to such a franchise. Also, why was the best ability at the end of the game... when I barely have any chance to use it. This ties into another one of my most prominent issue; a lack of post game content meant you can't see the fruits of your labor (the land of niwen without corruption) and it makes the ending feel pointless, as the game will go on as if nothing happened, reverting to your last save when you finish. The gameplay was improved in many aspects, like the time trials, which were one of my favorite parts of the game, but I feel like they still didn't fully flesh the mechanics out and there was a major lack of original ideas, as most of them I had already seen in another game, which was surprising, as the first game introduced so many great ones.  Overall, its not a bad game, in fact its a pretty good one, but has a lot of wasted potential and doesnt feel as polished the masterpiece before it. (Ori and the Blind forest) Oh yeah, and I ran into a few bugs, but none of them were game breaking.
