_childDocuments_.review: Ori was and still is one of my favourite games of all time, alongside with the Hollow Knight. They are both games that give you a great impact with their wonderful unique gameplay and story that can hit you right in the feels. I've been awaiting this game for a long time and oh how hyped I was. I imidiately got the game the day it was released and so I began my journey with Ori once again. And oh gosh let me tell you getting into this beautiful world again was just, so good and nostalgic. All started well untill... it felt too much 'the same'. Exact same abilities, exact same enemies and environment. While of course, it's still Ori and it's just a continuation of the adventures - I expected more and something, well - fresh. I instantly picked up the similarities to the game I mentioned earlier 'Hollow Knight' with the shard system, and oddly enough - same designed/same behaving enemies just like in the HK. It gave me multiple mixed feelings about it. Let's talk about Shards - They are a great addition to the game and does bring in some new mechanics and new upgrades but. Majority of them feel absolutely useless and I found myself using only 3 [floaty orbs, dmg reduce and sticking to walls], and then as the slot number went up I simply had no idea what to do with these holes. While in HK they had a great impact on the gameplay and could really change your playstyle - here they just exist in form of colectibles. New skills you could learn were also something fresh, but again, exactly just like with the shards - I had no use of any of them other than again - 3, and situational ones when I had to quickly switch through them to have light in one certain area.   If you're a type of using loads of energy - maybe you'd fine use of the rest - but I simply didn't.NPC's are gorgeous and they give a LOT of life into the game and just make you smile to just see them there. Side quests and generall quest system is fine, but it's simply for you to interract with the NPC's you don't really get much from doing them other than a sentence or two of dialogue, which doesn't really add much to the story, because by then you already know everything.Secrets are incredibly easy to find, and game in general doesn't really seem challenging being played on normal difficulty. I've died total of 34 times, just because I love stupidly jumping into the spikes. Death from an enemy almost never happens. Speaking of enemies - well... There isn't much of a variety. You meet exact same enemies during your full playthrough and only different ones are the bosses, which also - aren't many of them. But let me tell you - they are so worth playing it for. They give you an amazing atmosphere and while they aren't too difficult, they sure have great mechanics and designs. Generally the game is absolutely great and I would recommend it to everyone that loves metroidvanias just like these ones, and if you're a fan of Ori. Be careful about the performance issues, as the game seems to have frame drops in random moments and quite annoying sound glitches as for now. I'd give this game a good 7,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Like most metroid-vania games, we have the classic: “where the ♥♥♥♥ do I go” problem. Sometimes because of the dim pause screen map, sometimes because sections don't make it clear they aren't traversable without later gained abilities. But it improves throughout the game, which is the tag line for Ori and the Blind Forest in general… it's not very good in the first few hours. The combat, the movement, and especially the story all start out clunky and feeling like a shadow of the first game. By the 5 hour mark, there's enough movement and combat options to make the game-play fluid and responsive. Most enemies are balanced and creative, but most can be walked past without a second thought. Fortunately, the boss fights take full advantage of your arsenal and while they aren't always fun, they are always rewarding to beat. The platforming fairs better, it's always challenging and always creative and certainly a highlight for the game. The story needs another 5 hours to obtain enough characters to become interesting, but it ends very strong and that's good enough. But I can't stress enough how dull and predictable acts I & II of the story are.Lastly, this game and the prequel are at least in the top 5 most artistic 2d games in existence. The attention to detail in the background is unmatched. From start to finish, there's an animated, desktop wall paper worthy, beautifully environment to get lost in.

_childDocuments_.review: This game stole my breath, sent me soaring, and ultimately broke my heart in several places.If you loved the original Ori game, then this is a must-play.  This game is everything Blind Forest was and more.   The stunning map is bigger, there's more to explore, more side characters to meet and interact with, the animations are fine-tuned, and the gameplay is definitely challenging.   There are some areas on the map that are harder to navigate than others, but as Ori's skillset and abilities increase, everything gets easier.  The game doesn't hold your hand, but it does equip you with what you need to succeed.   I will say in some areas, it is hard to figure out what the next step is.  And sometimes, the flashes of light and color are so intense that I've literally lost Ori on the screen ("I told you to go right--why are you stuck on the--and now you're dead.")  But if you know how to use your abilities, dash, bash, spirit's edge, wall cling, you can get through pretty much anything.  Gareth Coker's soundtrack for the game is phenomenal--he builds on Ori's theme, and weaves it into the fights and the escape sequences for a triumphant note that reminds you just how strong Ori has become in the world.  The story itself broke my heart and there are some elements I wasn't satisfied with, but it made sense for the progression and my complaints are minor.Essentially, this is a near-perfect game if you love Ori and the Blind Forest, and I love it just as much as I loved the original.  I didn't think a sequel could even come close to the magic of the original game, but this one did, and it's phenomenal.

The level design is more annoying, the combat and boss fights are either too simplistic or really frustrating, and various decisions in the game itself are also more frustrating and confusing overall. For example, in order to get additional abilities you need to purchase them with spirit light. But spirit light is not as abundant as it would seem. I unlocked the last 30-40% or so only after finishing the game. A lot of the collectibles are hidden behind all sorts of objects and the game doesn't really tell you how to unlock those. I thought they'd be hidden away behind an ability like stomp, and many were, mostly not, which just added to the confusion. And then there are the bugs, which at the time of this writing are not fully fixed, and you'll still get glitches in the game.So, if you haven't played the first Ori and want to play one of the two, I recommend the first one. _childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Blind Forest was, in my opinion, a masterpiece.  I've just cleared the game and 100% every collectable/quest in about 14 hours, so while everything is still fresh here's my thoughts.This game focuses more on combat than it's predecessor. There are a large array of abilities and augmentations to add new effects to those abilities or passives that allow you to tailor Ori to your personal preference. Escape sequences are still present, though they are replaced by boss fights in places. Story is pretty similar to last time, people gonna die. You go to a new forest with your adopted sister Ku, get separated. New forest has fallen into decay and you gotta bring the light to the forest to save everyone. Get the things, go to the place, fight the big bad bird, hug a golden light. Movement is crisp and about midway though the game... just getting around is a joy. Ori can also warp anytime he wants... so no more running to a shrine to get to the other side of the map. Quality of life! Puzzles are great and some of them are pretty creative. The bad90% of NPCs are these weasel looking guys called Moki... out of the 20ish of them there are 2 of them that have "names". They end up being pretty boring. Camera can have trouble keeping up when you're going fast, the grapple augmentation is more trouble than it's worth as it's tied to the same button as Bash. So instead of redirecting an enemies attack you may just fling yourself through the attack and then take damage for being too close to the enemy. Map can sometimes say NPCs are in places they are not, and I encountered minor audio and visual bugs. This is a fantastic game that tries to balance combat, speedrunning, puzzles, boss fights, and platforming. Most of which it does marvelously. Brace yourself, you're gonna die alot.

_childDocuments_.review: Throughout the entirety of the game, you will remain flabbergasted. This game looks gorgeous, thanks to the attention to detail and the hand-painted graphics that evoke a sense of awe and calm.The gameplay is different from Ori and the Blind Forest when it comes to battles, but it is still enjoyable. The overhaul brings new fighting styles, all complemented by new shop mechanics focused around the gathering of points. Additionally, apart from the main quest, there are intriguing side quests that bring life to the world, which is enormous.The story aspect of the game has not lost its touch. It is a worthy continuation for Ori and the Blind Forest, bringing the player closer to the universal aspects of life: kindness, friendship, sacrifice, family, and destiny.I consider this to be an exceptional piece of art, not just a game. It is a triumph in the era of stagnation for video game storytelling, graphics, and all accompanied by amazing music. I heartily recommend this game to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game came out at the perfect time. Lockdown had just started and world was going to ♥♥♥♥. I was excited everyday because i was so immersed in this beautiful world. I consider the first ori game as one of my favorites of all time, so i had a lot of expectations for the sequel. I am so happy to say that this game delivers and also has earned a spot on my favorite games list. Everything that was amazing in the first game is here also. The music is fantastic and plays such a crucial part of the narrative and overall experience. The animations are damn near flawless, with everything having subtle movements that really makes the world feel alive. The art style and color palette is as beautiful as the first game, with small improvements that makes it look even better than the first game. Every single frame of this game could be a windows computer background.I think that combat was the weakest part of Blind Forest because the lack of complexity and play styles. Moon Studios were clearly aware of this and they have improved the combat system in every single way. You can now choose what kind of combat moves you want to have, which opens up to a variety of play styles and combos that you can do. Last but not least we have the story. The narrative and storytelling in this game is top notch. You get so attached to the characters and the world that it's almost hard to let go. I felt melancholic at the end of the game and i didn't want to say goodbye to this fantastic world that i had fell in love with over the course of a couple of days. In conclusion this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. You can tell that the developers poured everything into this game and loved it as much as we do. Everything that was good in the first game is on par or even better in the sequel. I can't recommend this game enough. This is one of the few games that i have ever bought on release day and i am so happy i did! I'm kinda disappointed that this game isn't nominated for goty because it has earned it's spot there. Thank you Moon Studios for creating an experience that will surely stick with me for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly worthy sequel to Ori and the Blind Forest; Will of the Wisps takes everything I loved about the original game & dials it up a notch in depth & breadth, though it's not totally without fault.Presentation isn't one of those faults. The game is a treat for the eyes in every sense, & if you're fortunate enough to own an OLED screen, this is absolutely the game you need to play to show it off. The incredibly detailed yet clean presentation allows for visuals that pop beautifully while sitting in the overall scene well. The OST also hits the mark, as does the story, which ties in beautifully to the Blind Forest.The gameplay is brilliant, though there's definitely some inconsistency when it comes to difficulty. There's nothing here that'll cause much of a headache if you're a regular player of such games, but the increase in gameplay complexity compared to BF paired with a few oddly tuned boss fights make for an experience which can be a bit inconsistent at times.Overall though, it's a spectacular sequel to a stunning game. A treat for your senses with wonderfully tight gameplay & a charming story that compliments Blind Forest perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember buying this game for my sister a few years back. Didn't think much of it at the time, but I thought it would be a nice gift for her. I remember seeing her playing it from time to time, the message indicating that she'd started playing it popping up on the corner of my screen. There was always a certain small pride in seeing that, because to me it meant that she was enjoying my gift.Last September she committed suicide.After everything had more or less settled down from that, I sat down and booted up her computer. All that was on there was Chrome, Steam, Word, and a few games. One of them, of course, was Core keeper.She had played this game to pieces, clocking over 170 hours and owning practically everything the game had to offer. She had used every square inch to its maximum potential, and was making ridiculous amounts of loot. It was only then did I see just how much she loved my present. No other game she played quite captured her affection as much as this one. None of her friends really knew about it, however; it seems like she preferred to keep it to herself. Like it was her own little bit of heaven she could turn to whenever she wanted.And because of that, I can't help but smile whenever I play this game.I cannot recommend it enough; every bit of hard work the developer put into this masterpiece shows in every single aspect. The music is catchy and memorable (I'll often find myself humming certain tunes from it), the world feels lived-in and natural, and the gameplay is incredibly laid back and enjoyable. It's hard to stop once I get invested in the game; minutes can easily turn into several hours. And now, with the multiplayer beta, I play for even longer with my friends, each of us dedicated to our desired jobs. Most of all, however, we're all just happy to be together.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming straight from Ori 1 and expecting staple things to remain mechanically same, and being greeted with changes to things that weren't broken into a sidegrade at best, or a downgrade in a few cases. (specifically light burst throw). It was also rather overwhelming and even immersion breaking with how many things were going on at the same time, being given sidequests etc., it felt like so much compared to the perfected, more streamlined but not restrictive progress the first game.However, graphically the game is a straight upgrade, Ori controls the exact same, the most important and staple movements are present and the gameplay feels smooth and very satisfying when mastered.I can't not mention the difficulty spike, the game almost expecting you to have played the first game or get "punished" ( - learn through trial and error), especially if you hop straight into hard difficulty. Difficulty coming from not the enemies this time, as health and resource management in this game is a lot more lenient than before, as enemies now drop health and energy shards, but when it comes to bosses, they're pretty spongy. They take a while sometimes and you've pretty much mastered the whole bossfight by the time you're done, and it feels nice? I don't tend to enjoy these kinds of victories but it really feels nice against things that don't really use BS strategies to harm you (except in the finale :))*Note, I only played it on Hard, I don't know if enemies drop health on normalI recommend you play with a controller, as it feels natural for a 2d platformer. If you have prior controller experience, you really should try the Ori duology, even if you aren't that big on platformers. (Blind forest comes before Will of the Wisps)It's a journey and experience that I last remember experiencing as a kid, on the ps2. If you found this one, congrats! You found gold in the rough,

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Ori and the Will of the Wisps as a new fan of the first game after it released on Switch. I had a lot of the first game spoiled for me before I played it so I did my best to avoid gameplay videos and OST uploads before playing this, and I am so glad I did because there are so many moments in this beautiful game that caught me off guard and had me either smiling or crying genuine tears.Aside from some technical issues at launch that seem to have been mostly ironed out with a patch, I'd say this is one of those near-perfect games that surpasses its predecessor in almost every way.My only real gripe is that I wish there was a way to switch between pre-made weapon loadouts instead of constantly changing button commands with the quick select because it really prolongs the boss fights in the latter half of the game. I move with the control stick so if there was an option to toggle loadouts with D-pad that's be super.Really looking forward to whatever Moon Studios puts out next. Completing the Hand-in-Hand sidequest will reveal all of them anyway.If you use the "bounty" shard, unequip it for combat shrines because the enemies don't drop spirit light. Some bosses do drop spirit light o, in theory, you could equip it before dealing the final blow and still recieve 2X SL.Alt+U toggles the hud. Useful for screenshots. :)

Whether you're soaring through the lush forests or delving into the depths of dark caverns, the game consistently delivers a sense of awe and wonder that few others can match.🎮 Gameplay: ( 9.5 / 10 )The gameplay in Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a masterclass in platforming excellence. From exhilarating chase sequences to challenging boss fights, every moment feels finely tuned and meticulously crafted. The addition of new abilities and upgrades keeps the gameplay feeling fresh and engaging throughout, ensuring that players are constantly discovering new ways to navigate the world around them.📘 Story: ( 7.9 / 10 )While Ori and the Will of the Wisps may not have the most complex narrative, its emotional depth and heartfelt storytelling more than make up for it. Through its beautifully animated cutscenes and evocative musical score, it manages to evoke a powerful sense of empathy and connection with its characters, making their journey feel all the more impactful.📺 Visuals: ( 9.4 / 10 )Visually, Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a work of art. Whether it's the gentle rustle of leaves in the wind or the thunderous roar of a raging storm, the game's sound design adds an extra layer of depth and atmosphere to an already stunning world.--------------------------------------------------------------------------🏆 Overall: ( 9.1 / 10 )Ori and the Will of the Wisps is more than just a game; it's a work of art. With its breathtaking atmosphere, engaging gameplay, and heartfelt storytelling, it offers an experience that is as emotionally resonant as it is visually stunning. Whether you're a fan of platformers or simply appreciate finely crafted games, Ori and the Will of the Wisps is an absolute must-play. _childDocuments_.review: Game could be 10/10 but there are some parts that I felt is just not as polished when compared to the overall game. Ori and the Will of the Wisps is easily one of the best looking games and even after 10 years from now the it will still look great due to the art style and direction. Combined with solid gameplay that builds upon the first game, which is mainly about platforming, Will of the Wisps focuses more on combat with multiple weapons and skills to suit to how you like to play the game. There are some interesting skills and upgrades that can you can find by exploring.I play with a KB+M and there are some technical issues with rebinding the keys. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you're hesitating, don't. This game is worth whatever price they ask.Let me preface this review with:I remember being very fond of the first game.When this one arrived I bought it right away and I was initially bummed out about the new skill system and it's RPG elements.This made me put off playing this game for a while. Boy was I an idiot.When I finally got into the game, all of it's elements were at least as good as in the first ori or most of the time even better, much better. I couldn't put the controller down.It's music along with the visuals and story will pull on your heart strings in every imaginable way.And it's not just what you see and hear. The gameplay is just as impactful.You will laugh, cry, be vengeful, scared, anxious, at times a bit frustrated and much more.If we were to judge entertainment by how emotional it makes us, will of the wisps is unironically worth a 11/10 score.This game is the definition of "too good to be true" and yet it exists.The highest praise I can think of to give this game is that there were times I experienced pure joy.Akin to what you could feel when looking at a sunset over amazing landscape while being in the best mood you could possibly be in.I can't recall a game that has made me feel this way other than ori and the blind forest.

_childDocuments_.review: When I think of art in video games, Ori is one of the all-time standouts. This was true for the first game as well, but Will of the Wisps takes just about everything Blind Forest already did well and made it better. The world of Ori full of wonderful charm and some challenging dangers that show an incredible amount of artistic talent (both visual and musical) and imagination.Will of the Wisps' combat, one of the most expanded aspects, is solid with both variety and a lot of room for mastery. Whether its collectibles, time trials, doing quests, or sprucing up the haven with buildings and plants, there's a lot to do besides marvel at the environments, too. Its story is, like the first's, simple but moving, and there are a couple notes that can really pluck the heartstrings.Overall, Will of the Wisps is a game I can't recommend enough. Just be sure to enjoy the original before the sequel dazzles you

_childDocuments_.review: So after playing more than 14 hours, here is why I'm not going to recommend this:1) The game compared to "Ori and the Blind Forest" is much more frustrating, far too many "precision" areas, allot more combat than is typical for a plat-former game, and no direction with story.2) The save game system is VERY glitchy. I've now had to replay the sequence with the chasing entity (located at the Wellsprings), 3 times now because the save game is either deleted or corrupted (not sure which). Had to reload using saves from waaayyy in the past.3) The maps are great for finding things, just not to help you figure where to go to complete either side quests or the main quest. Confusion abundant. Map source and targets are not defined properly.4) Allot of sections of backtracking and/or repeating only after acquiring new piece of upgrade. Developers are using this technique to "stretch out" the game play, when if they had planned properly, would make this idea irrelevant.For now, I'm giving this a 6 out of 10, and let you decide if you want the hassle or if I feel that an updated review is warranted.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably not going to make a lot of sense, but beautiful, response and immersive though this game is...I don't like it. Basically this game seems confused as to what it wants to be. Ori and Blind Forest was basically a platformer...I actually recommended that. This one, is more metroidvania than the first, mixed in with Salt and Sanctuary with the bosses. I like the bosses. The gimmicks though, they are just unnecessarily brutal. There's just no way to figure things out without spending a tonne of time investigating the maps and trying to figure out what door unlocks trigger what doors. The Wisp positions are just a pain as well. I just went through the mouldwood depths and got the wisp...my word that was painful. The instadeath when the fireflies disappear is just over the top. The thing is, the platforming doesn't have to be this hard. Its hard to the point that its not enjoyable. It doesn't give you any direction either...I wound up in the desert at one point 'collect the four wisps'. Well the location I was at 'was one of them'. Now I'm not against games having a lack of direction...'Souls' games work on that premise...At the same time, this isn't soulsbourne. A lot of this seems like its just confused. Some people have the patience for a lack of direction...I do for Souls, because I like the combat. For this...I don't enjoy the platforming. I'm playing this because I wanted to see what all the praise was about and its on sale. I probably should have beaten Blind Forest before I bought this...neither are particularly my bag. Not a bad game, per-say, but I wouldn't recommend it. It's a solid 8/10 as a GAME (visuals, music, level design, etc)...that said, know what you are getting into. You will need a guide for this, and you will likely get frustrated with the platforming. Things to note: platforming movement is actually tighter than Blind Forest...but the platforming itself...much of it is like the lava level in the first one...its just brutal to a point where I definitely wouldn't sink my money into anything that these guys do again.ADDENDUM - Just finished this...the narrative is excellent (I like how it painted the villain and how they were a product of their environment - nicely done).  That said, I stand by my earlier commentary: Its  unnecessarly confusing fetch quests (wisps, hack the cancerous items, and hammer down pegs to open doors), all with gorgeous imagery. Ultimately, the imagery is just that,  a gameplay sense, it fairly poor that there is no clear pathway to a location. Its overly convoluted. I watched Honest Game Trailers commentary on this, and its spot on...the game is just brutal. The platforming is a killer...the combat is easy as. Again...it may be your thing...its not mine. Its a solid 8/10 though...I can't fault it as a game except for what I said. Its still a good game, but I wouldn't recommend it, if that makes sense (the positions do reconcile)

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same. The opening sequence is long, long, and just steeped in whatever this aesthetic is--painfully saccharine, knock-off 80s Disney? I am not generally inclined to use strong language in a game review, but it blows my mind that these games seem to be universally adored. (Is that market manipulation, or the truth? Where are the voices of dissent that come by sheer law-of-averages, even when a game is good?)  I love the metroidvania as a form, but this game and its sequel... feel dull, tedious, time-consuming... uninspired. I don't enjoy the feel of the game, or the mechanics. Always floaty, and never anything that feels like substantial feedback, either via haptics or just good ol' sound design. The music quite literally gives me nausea, like I'm adrift in a sea of dishwasher-safe blandness. This is a big, slick McMansion of a game, and--clearly--I do not understand its appeal. _childDocuments_.review: A great platformer and metroidvania, had a great experience overall during my playthrough. Definitely a worthy sequel that improves on pretty much every aspect from the first game.It has a lot of varied platforming due to its vast variety of abilities that you can unlock and utilize, makes the gameplay both fun and engaging which makes it a fast paced and smooth experience.First thing I noticed when I started playing was that the combat had been improved immensely, which was a pleasant surprise because I thought it was quite poor in the first game. Landing hits and combos on enemies feels very satisfying to do with the combat abilities the game provides you with, it kind of has a Hollow Knight-esque charm system where you can adapt your own playstyle. To an extent at least.The boss fights are really good and looks amazing visually, has mostly a varied moveset and whenever their next phase triggers it'll follow up with a chase sequence that often has some intense platforming, changing the area completely making the boss behave differently for more interesting gameplay. Probably one of my favorite things about this game.Graphics and visuals are gorgeous as usual. The artstyle is both colorful and beautiful, giving the game its own identity and charm to it.  Varied stages with immersive atmosphere that makes the world feel alive, eye-pleasing to watch. The soundtrack is stellar, just as good as the first game's OST. Without its dramatic and sometime emotional music, the game's great chase/escape and boss sequences would probably not have the same impact. It goes so well with the flow of the gameplay when you're running or fighting for your life. A real tear jerker at times during cutscenes as well. It does so much for the game in my opinion, without it I would probably not enjoy it as much.Now to the very few complaints I have about this game. First off, not the biggest fan of unlocking the same mobility abilites from the first game a second time, when you've already unlocked them once before. Kinda wish you start out with those whenever you start playing the sequel to a game. Just not very exciting unlocking the same abilities again and being so limited on what you can do when you start playing, especially in a platformer. Good thing they're introduced early into the game though, so there's that. Secondly, this game has some annoying audio problems, like distortions during dialogue and sometimes missing sound effects. Kind of ruined some cutscenes for me, like getting my eardrums ruptured during an emotional scene. Or having awkward and silent combat encounters. Restarting the game helps though, and I'm sure not everyone has had the same issues like me with the game's audio. Hopefully they'll fix it.That's pretty much all of them, despite of that I had mostly a bug free experience. Game's quite polished I gotta say, it also ran really well on my PC. So performance wise, I'm quite happy.This is a game I definitely recommend to anyone that likes platformers or metroidvanias, it is in my opinion worth full price. Took me about 15 hours to complete it, explored everything and got most of the collectibles and abilities first run. Not completely 100% though, so it's quite lengthy for its asking price and never felt like there was any filler content either (maybe except for some of the side missions).Really smooth and responsive controls (with a controller at least), great platforming and exploration that is both fun and challenging yet very rewarding. Overall had a pretty damn solid experience, will definitely revisit it again in the future. Hope to see more games like this from Moon Studios, they're very passionate and talanted game developers. More the reason to buy this game and show 'em some love and support.

_childDocuments_.review: Will of the Wisps somehow managed to take an already really great game and knock it out of the park. Everything about this game is a drastic improvement over the first from the visuals to the gameplay. This is easily one of my top 10 games now.The visuals in the first were stunning but my god they somehow outdid themselves, everything just looks so much more lively and the lighting really helps bring it all together, it is such a visual treat it actually gave me a headache at one point, by brain could not process the beauty of this game.The soundtrack was lovely, there's still tracks from the first game I love a lot more but this one is still overall better, it really gets you feeling.The gameplay was my biggest issue with Blind Forest so I am very happy that they improved it. The platforming was the only aspect from the first one that I think they got right so its still good here, and has been expanded upon with a few new and fun abilities, I also loved the new combat and enemies, so much more dynamic and far less slimes than in the first game. Bosses were a huge surprise and managed to be just hard enough that I felt like I just barely made it out alive while still not being too unfair. The escape sequences are far less trial and error which is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blessing as that was easily the worst part of Blind Forest. Overall the gameplay has been nearly perfected.The story and characters were also lovely, Moki were my favourite new characters and I was of course happy to see the old gang still here. Shriek brought back the feeling of dread that Kuro gave. The game was also really sad, like I have never cried at a video game before but my god that ending really hit me hard.This is the best sequel Moon Studios could have done. Amazing job, and congratulations for making me cry.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like its predecessor, this is a truly outstanding game. The visuals, the music, the gameplay are all top notch. In typical Metroidvania fashion the player navigates and fights their way through the world while discovering upgrades. Most important, controls are smooth and responsive. As this is a sequel to a highly acclaimed game, people will compare the two and I am no exception. Will of the Wisps (WotW) took the concept of Blind Forest (BF) and added new stuff, most notably more focus on combat, player choices and customization. Instead of a set skill tree, the player now can chose abilities and passive bonuses from a plethora of options that are either found or bought throughout the game.People call Will of the Wisps as an unquestionable improvement over Blind Forest, but I tend to disagree. It is different and refreshing, but it has its flaws, some brought by precisely by these changes. This of course doesn't mean, it is a bad game, for from it.In my opinion, compared to BF the story was less enthralling and immersive, the villain was less relatable and the music, albeit beautiful, was less memorable.Still, overall this game is a masterpiece and the things I mentioned pale compared to all the things it does good, great even. If you liked the previous game, you also will like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is the best game I have ever played. It is incredibly satisfying to master, and tells an enthralling story. This even tops Hollow Knight, which was my previous favorite game. If you enjoy a good platformer/puzzle game, this is for you.

Certain audio tracks just stopped working, certain "portals" you need to traverse through to progress straight up don't work half the time, and at one point Ori just became straight-up invincible. Like, I couldn't be hurt by anything; not even the corrupted water which is a one-hit kill. I theoretically *could* finish the rest of the game, and boy it would be easy with godmode, but that doesn't seem fun.I'm sure the game will be patched at some point in the near future and I'll finish it then. _childDocuments_.review: If i had to summarize Ori and the Will of the Wisps in one sentence:Every second is a beautiful wallpaper.Ori and the Will of the Wisps is everything the Blind Forest was but better, except one thing... the Soundtrack.Even better graphics, despite the Blind Forest already being beautiful, this game easily kicks it off its place and turns it up a few notches, everything is simply beautifully designed, every step you take presents you a new beauty to look at.Even more mobility, the Blind Forest had you double jump, triple jump, jump and dash off walls, climb, swim, glide, roll and bash off foes, Will of the Wisps tops this all by adding a grappling hook, more dashes, air dashes, airial combos, burrowing through sand and weapons that not only feel extremely different and have different applications, they can all be combined, and swapped out at any given time, you can stay midair and smash in near infinite combos with Ori's newfound mobility and it feels absolutely rewarding unlocking them all, every new move expands your moveset in a meaningful way, adds more depth and more ways to get around and combining all of them to create faster and faster routes feels smooth and looks absolutely beautiful in action. This goes very well with the newly added time trials which will test your ability to be creative and use precise timing of all your available moves.The new skills and traits (shards) all have a place, they can all be used for different situations and hot swapping them at any time works too, compared to the old level up system this feels way better.The soundtrack while still emotional and one of the games absolute highlights is sadly not as good as that of Ori and the Blind Forest, the devs must have known this so well that they even put the full Ori and the Blind Forest main theme as credits song after the game's end. Mainly the escape sequences are lackluster but by no means bad, they are still amazing but simply don't hold a chance against the Blind Forest's escape sequence soundtrack, sadly. The escape sequence soundtrack was basically the highlight of the first game.The story as awfully familiar as it is is still great and very emotional, once again they manage to make you cry rivers of manly tears, though this time the emotional parts kick in much later than in the first game, i'd highly recommend playing the first game to fully understand what's going on and what is happening to our beloved characters. As sad as it is but there probably won't be any more Ori games unless it's a spinoff.My only real complain about this game is that it is waaaaay too short. 12 hours and i was at the end, including completing almost all areas up to at least 90+% and collecting almost everything everywhere. The most beautiful 12 hours of my life probably, i just wish there was more. 3 More hours and i completed every quest and every area 100%. It was so fun yet i yearn for more, more time trials maybe, they are fun and using all available abilities is really fun.I can only recommend this game, it's an absolute must buy. The absolute best game in the past 20 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Just No. I was kinda iffy about Ori and the Blind Forest at first, because apart from the story and music and good looking art, the game was only ok, in my opinion. Having new mechanics like grapple hook are so weirdly bugged, literally does not work more than 50% of the times.If you are looking at the continuation aspect of the story, it is shown as continued from Ori and The Blind Forest's ending. This is from the story/cutscenes part. Gameplay wise, you have to learn all the abilities again. If the character had to learn the skills again, it would have been better to add some lore part which mentioned that Ori forgot to use the previously learned skills because he didn't have to use them for quite a while, although that would also break the logic, as the story seems to proceed without much break, continuing from Ori and the Blind Forest.I gave a negative review for the 1st part, but changed it later, because the gameplay bugs didn't matter as much to me as it was overshadowed by the great storytelling. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I adore the abundance of secrets. Visuals: stunning. Plot: so engaging. Music and sound effects: melodic and refined, respectively. It holds a myriad of fun, varying and useful abilities + shards you can use. I am so glad you can teleport with shrines. I also loved the different traits you could get from the willow trees. I also took note of how the trees were shaped like the ability they offered, the detail is phenomenal. The colour palette is very delightful. The achievements were the right difficulty, and perfecting the game was a very joyful adventure to embark upon, which took 6 full runs to earn them all, which could have been refined to 4. I was lucky to have successfully completed my first Immortal and Look At The Time runs separately.The only two pieces of advice for this impossibly amazing and immersive game play is that the willow stone boss near the conclusion of the game is underwhelming in normal mode on my first experience. Ori's healing ability makes it very hard to die when you gain a lot of energy and life fragments at the end; it should deal more damage, but I guess people might struggle if they don't like to grind spirit energy for Lupo's two life and energy maps, then gather all the halves. Immortal achievement grinders might not like this advice either. Secondly, not all abilities offered by Opher can break bridges like the spike upgraded. This makes a few other weapons less appealing to use, like the ninja star.Hope to see a third game, perhaps following Ku's adventures!

_childDocuments_.review: A really well done sequel to a game that was already good. The game builds upon what was already good on the first game and improves it further, soundtrack, graphics, puzzles and it's platformer mechanics. All well done like the first one, and then goes on and fixes the first game's problems, such as :- Lack of action in fights. In the first game you could literally spam attack and beat bosses and enemies pretty easily, it wasn't the actual premise of the game so it didn't really bother me, but it certainly did others.- Short gameplay time. Game is pretty long this time, last game was around 6-6:30 hours long, depending on your platformer skills and it could end up around 10 hours to finish. But after you reach to the Spirit Tree (i don't remember how it was called) in the first game, you have been given the main task you have to perform through out the game, restore 3 spirits and then - Boom! You have finished the game. Don't get me wrong, it was fun but it felt pretty short and it was short too.This time they brought much wider world with fun side missions + a longer main storyline. Which doesn't feel "short" like the first game.I gotta say, I'm quite impressed and I'm really happy that we recieved a sequel like this. You should definitely buy this if you played the first game and enjoyed it/didn't like those things I mentioned. If you never have tried out Ori before, if you like 2D platformers, I'm pretty sure you need to try these games out.I will never forget you, Kwolok. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Movement and combat is much more fun than the original, probably near the top of any game. The problems with the game come with those, however. The movement is super fun and unique, but the game is pretty linear (doesn't allow for sequence breaks which would reward players who master the movement options) and lacks the challenge/spectacle of the escape sequences from the original. Sadly, the game is fairly easy and feels very short when I compare it to the memories I have of the original. Still, the actual gameplay and feel improves on the original, and the story, world, and characters are all much more alive feeling than the predecessor. This is by no means a bad game, or even a mediocre one.

_childDocuments_.review: After being blown away by the first game, a friend generously gifted me a copy of Will of the Wisps.I thought that OatWotW wouldn't be able to top OatBF.I have never been so wrong before in my entire life. Ori and the WIll of the Wisps doesn't just meet Blind Forest's incredible beauty, it well exceeds it in almost every regard.- The Art: This goes without saying, but if you look up the word "gorgeous" in the dictionary, you'll find there won't be any words. Instead there will be a picture of the title screen of Ori and the Will of the Wisps. It's that incredible. Every time I enter a new area I am astounded by the wonderful backgrounds, the subtle hints in the terrain to secrets, the beautiful environments populated with friends and foes alike... it's all so mesmerizing. (The Luma Pools are my favorite area it's just so gorgeous aaah)- The Gameplay: Ori alone is already very mobile - able to scale walls and jump through the air with ease. But throughout the game you get more abilities that further increase this movement, culminating to points where you can fling yourself off of enemies, bore through the ground itself, and dash through the air without a care in the world. I have never played a game where I have had so much fun with simply moving around. The expanded combat mechanics are definitely a step up from Ori and the Blind Forest, allowing a full arsenal of upgradable weapons to use to beat up the baddies and bosses, and I couldn't help but run toward the nearest enemy to test out my new shiny toy every single time. Fighting enemies and bosses is definitely more fun than it was in Ori and the Blind Forest. Bosses are a fun challenge and feel great to finally beat, - The Designs: Like the first game, characters and enemies alike are wonderfully designed. Like I can't get enough, all these characters and enemies are just... so coooool! I mean you have bat-spiders, you have a giant half-ossified owl, you have burly four-armed gentle giants, frozen carnivorous plants awaiting spring, and so much more. The designs are just... so endearing. I don't want to kill them, I just want to sit and look at them!- The Music: I can't listen to this OST. Not because it's bad, far far from it. I can't listen to it because I CRY without fail. Every. Single. Time. It's just as gorgeous as the art, and sets the mood of every area perfectly - a choir of somber voices calling from the snow, awaiting a spring yet to come; a moody and tragic elegy of hallow decay, leaving nothing but infection within the stone-cold remains of what once was the protector of life; a curious symphony of bright instruments to punctuate the tropic beauty of a sea-side forest. It's just so PERFECT.- The Story: The story is very to-the-point but oh man does it grab your heart and catch your soul. But it refuses to shatter either. Instead it fills your heart with emotion and nourishes your soul with compassion.No spoilers, but the twists at the ending were absolute heart-wrenchers to me. The new contextualization helped me love the story even more.Needless to say, I cried. Many many times. But you know what? That's okay. This game is absolutely jam-packed with love. And I was honored to be allowed to experience that love, that compassion, that dedication and emotion that was poured into this game.I could rant on for hours more about how much I love this game, but I feel that I've said more than enough.In conclusion: Ori and the Blind Forest and Ori and the WIll of the Wisps are games well worth the price, and well worth the time. I love these games all my heart. Ori has definitely bashed his way into my favorites, and it couldn't be more well-deserved. I can't wait to play it again.Moon Studios, I love you. Thank you for these incredible games and the joy-filled experiences they brought.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid 7/10 game (9/10 presentation, 6/10 actual game) that shines in it's visual and audio design, and packs some fun platforming challenges to boot. I felt the combat fell a little flat for me, and the world did feel a little empty towards the end of the game, but I ended up enjoying it nevertheless. There are a couple games that get a better value for the $30 pricetag, but I ended up snagging it on sale and enjoyed my time with it. Worth your time if you can get it for cheaper.This is my first time playing a game in this series, and I ended up 100% it on Normal. I might revisit it for the Speedrun achievements or to play it again on Hard, but I don't really feel a strong urge to do so.PROS:- The game is visually stunning. Backgrounds look phenomenal, and the various details like the flora in each region help sell the game's world. The character animation is also incredibly good, both in gameplay and in cutscenes, doing a good job of selling emotion without dialogue. I wish more games looked like this.- The Sound and the Music of the game is also fantastic. A lot of work was evidently put into both the sound design for gameplay and the score for the game, and it really shines through. It reminded me a lot of the Armello SFX, which are also amazing.- The platforming feels REALLY good. The game gives you access to a lot of things that just chain together really well, and I think the complexity really works in its favor. Plus, I'm a sucker for anything bullet time, and bash tickles my monkey brain in a lot of different ways.- This game feels OK to 100%? There's not that much content, sure, but I'm grateful there's no 40+ minute endurance challenges or esoteric puzzles that I have to bash my head into for hours to solve. I do wish there was some more variety, but fully completing the game doesn't feel actively bad, which I enjoy.CONS:- Combat feels like an afterthought. Enemy variety is pretty low (I can think of maybe like 4 distinct non-boss enemies? There's a couple of variants but you get my point) and normal enemies never really feel like a barrier after a certain point. This game also gives you a ton of flat combat buffs (do more damage, etc.) that make the game easier without making it more fun/interesting.- Bosses were also super disappointing. None of them really feel engaging, and the game does a poor job of communicating both when you get hit and when you hit the boss back. -  Some late-game abilities kind of trivialize a lot of the platforming challenges, which is both a blessing and a curse. It makes traversing the map a lot faster and more fun, but also takes a lot of the puzzle solving out of the equation. Wish there were a few limits on it (use energy or something idk).- I didn't really mesh with the story at all. Part of this may be the fact that I didn't play the first game, but I never really got super compelled by the main story. You don't really get to interact with a lot of the main forces opposing you outside of hearing other people talk about how bad they are, which feels a little flat from a storytelling perspective.- The game is noticeably buggy. Several memory leaks just happen throughout my playthrough, and lag leading to input delay was also a thing that happens sometimes. For a game that is so polished otherwise, that was kind of shocking to me.- For a Metroidvania, it feels like backtracking is very underutilized. Never felt the need to go back to older areas until I was already trying to 100% the game. I think the game would have benefited if they had cut a few areas and put that effort into bulking up the remaining areas with more secrets, quests, and puzzles.This game felt very casual on my playthrough. Dying is never really a setback and you almost always have the resources needed to accomplish something nearby. This could be a positive or a negative depending on who you talk to, but it was definitely very prominent in my mind when I was playing through the game. The game is at its best as a platformer, the movement is well thought out and engaging and the map design helps accentuate the game's strengths. The combat feels very straightforward and would be where I would want to see the most improvement in a potential sequel. This game's presentation is a standout quality - the animation and visuals are heads and shoulders above other similar games. It was a good experience and I would recommend it to anyone interested in trying a new 2D platforming/exploration game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the will of the wisps, the sequel to Ori and the blind forest, is a game that I immediately purchased when I saw it available. The first installment brought tears of joy to my eyes; a video game that was a complete work of art both visually and musically. I expected the sequel to do the same; but I shouldn't have gotten my expectations so high.The music is great, but because it is part of the same story there were very few unique songs, so it didn't have as much impact on me as the first. Having said that, I still purchased the soundtrack. The story has been influenced by the shadows of the first game and I can see clear similarities. Still, the events tugged at the heart strings.The controls got a little complicated towards the end with all of the movement abilities one could use. I used a keyboard and mouse, but it might have been easier with a controller. (I should really invest in one...)Overall, I recommend the game.Keep up the excellent work Moon Studios. I can't wait to see what you come up with next!

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could recommend the squeal to one of my favorite games, but the game did not live up to my expectations.My main complaint is that Ori and the Will of the Wisps, which was supposed to be a squeal to Ori and the Blind Forest, instead seems like a Hollow Knight clone - as in, more so than usual. It seems that the devs. of the game took out a large chunk of platforming and replaced it with combat features, of which there were many.I liked some of the ideas they had - like the switching of weapons - but felt as if, with these features, that I was playing a different game overall. A large part of the original Ori game was its difficult, but rewarding, platforming, setting it apart from other platforming, and especially metroidvania, games. The game, with its use of Ori not being able to *directly* hurt or damage enemies, and needing a different, almost separately controlled, character to do the fighting, made the focus of the game using Ori's diverse non-combat skills in a way that tactically favored the player, which was a fun way to play - anyone who has bashed a enemy into spikes, instantly killing it, can sympathies.It seems like a lot of that has taken out of the game, replaced by quality's that any metroidvania has, not just Hollow Knight.I myself didn't like the game, but some people might like it - so sure, play it if you want.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game that truly touches the heart. It made me tear up several times, so deeply moving and emotional the story turned out to be. The magical world of Ori, with its breathtaking visual beauty, comes alive on the screen—each location is a masterpiece, filled with life and intricate details.But what really makes the game unforgettable is its heartfelt story. The relationships between the characters, their losses, and their search for meaning create an atmosphere that deeply resonates with the player. The soundtrack plays an immense role as well, heightening the emotional moments and crafting an enchanting atmosphere, filled with both light and darkness.It's a journey that leaves a mark on your soul and lingers long after the credits roll.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the blind forest set the standard for this type of game a few years ago, and this sequel improved on almost every aspect of the game. Traversal is even more challenging, and yet the difficulty modes allow you to fit the challenge to your liking. At first I was annoyed with the difficulty at some points of the game (especially when it comes to certain jumps), but by the end I realized, that if something is overly hard, then it's maybe not yet time to get there (there might be an ability missing, that could ease the pain). The soundtrack is once again wonderful and the story is beautifully written.The only gripe I do have is, that with Ori's newfound agility, the controls don't seem to be as precise as the ones from its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Will of the Wisps is the sequel to Ori and the Blind Forest. It improves on everything that its predecessor created and it isn't as simplistic as Blind Forest. There are a lot of subtle improvements but also some new major systems added in, like bossfights, main and sidequests, npcs to talk to and bigger world. Music is as amazing as ever, which led me to add it to my chill soundtrack to listen to when im off traveling or working. The world just feels more alive compared to the previous one and it still has that emotional gutpunch. In the end if you like metroidvanias and platformers in general its a must buy. However I do recommend to play the previous one since Will of the Wisps is a direct follow up, storywise, to Blind Forest.Moon Studios is an underrated dev team that deserves much more praise then they get, keep up the good work and can't wait to see what you cook next!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, here we go. Finally, after what felt like 15 years of waiting, we get the sequel to Ori and the Blind Forest. I bought BF back in the days on xbox, not knowing what I was getting into. I was surprised to find my actual favorite game of all time. Well, after finishing BF so many times, I was honestly not worried about WOTW, like, not at all.Though I didn't expect such a slap in my poor little face. It's fantastic. Everything is good so far. I'll make a list of the things that I REALLY enjoyed, after 10 hours of playtime.-  : 10 hours, and I feel like I still have some several hours to go. Main menu tells me I completed 50% of the game but honestly I'm starting to feel like the rest of the game is gonna take me at least 15 hours. We'll see, but so far it feels longer than BF, which felt a bit short.-  : I expected something good from the trailers I saw, different from the bashing on BF. I liked how you felt strong from the easy, spammy spirit on BF but here... It's completely different. You actually can COMBO enemies. Attack+UP to put enemy in the air, Attack+DOWN to slam it into the water, boom. EXTREMELY satisfying combat mechanics and honestly, they couldn't have done it better. Lots of different abilities as well! -  : I didn't know it could get any better than BF, well somehow yeah, they managed. The soundtrack feels somehow better, I have nothing much to say about it except that it fits the mood perfectly, just... so beautiful. The sound design as well, every little sound is extremely satisfying to hear, they remade the sounds of the already-existing abilities, and they feel good, same for the new ones. Games with satisfying little sounds when you pick up items tend to make me even more addicted to them!-  : I won't say much. Just... THE FEELS, UGH. SO GOOD. I CRY SO MUCH.- You can now teleport to each gate from anywhere. THANK YOU. THIS IS GOOD.- VERY Hollow Knight inspired (the shards system, the weapon, ).- THE TIME TRIALS. It's a small new thing, but it fits the game so well!- The new map, well done!- The side-quests, even though they feel a bit like "Take this. Bring to him. Thx", it's a great addition to a metroid-vania.- The inventory. You'll understand when you see it. It's gorgeous.- I run it pretty smoothly personally but needs a powerful PC. Might have some optimization issues, but those should get fixed at one point.- The "Escape/Run" phases that we had in Ori are back here, feels a bit redundant, even though they are very good and what made the strength of BF in the first place.Anyway... I could continue but honestly, I already said too much. Try it for yourself <3 If you liked Blind Forest, you're gonna LOVE this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games that have made me cry. The gameplay is amazing and a huge step up from the first game. It is so satisfying to string together movement abilities and attacks. The story, soundtrack, visuals, atmosphere are all incredible. To this day this game is still in my top 5 of all time. It is the perfect conclusion to the story and I strongly recommend it to anyone that likes to explore every nook and cranny of a map.Make sure to play Ori and the Blind Forest first. I know it's not as good as this one, but it is essential that you experience it first.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, just as the original. It starts simple enough, but later parts of the world require using all of your abilities to successfully traverse the world, just like the original. I cannot say if this one is easier, as I haven't played the original in a few years, but playing this feels like the right amount of challenging, especially in the later levels. Combat has been refined, and feels more responsive this time around, with the primary attacks being more direct. The world is designed very well, again. While, there is no sequence that arises to the Ginso Tree escape sequence level, it is still very memorable. Music is beautiful.TL;DR: If you liked the original, it's a no brainer; get this and you'll love it. If you are a fan of 2D platformers, play the original first, then play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I came across Ori and the Blind Forest when it was still in development and I was in awe when I played it on the release date. It was the most beautiful platformer I have ever seen, and even now I believe it is still the most beautifully done platform game ever. I have been looking forward to a sequel and they have delivered. Once again, it has been beautifully made, perhaps even better, and has left me in awe again.I believe with games such as the Ori series, visuals and sound are the most important elements to making it memorable and enjoyable. The art are wonderfully done as before and they have never failed on inserting the best sounds/BGMs for every area that Ori ventures through.The mechanics are I would not say are difficult to learn. In fact, it is pretty interesting that they changed parts of the concepts of Ori's combat style. Though I have to admit, being a huge fan of Ori and Hollow Knight, I got the impression of some mechanics in Ori and the Will of the Wisps being similar to Hollow Knight which is pretty interesting as it is somewhat different from Ori and the Blind Forest.What I believe may have been made more difficult are certain new monsters as they are made to be either stronger or more annoying at times, which I find being a rather fun addition to the game.There is actually only one problem I have encountered in the game so far, which is that the game tends to freeze at certain parts of the game. I am unsure of whether I am the only person having this issue but I think an optimization patch might be needed if I am not the only one encountering this. Other than that, there are pretty no problems at all, game is amazing as it is.I definitely recommend Ori and the Will of the Wisps and if you have never played Ori and the Blind Forest, get that first because this is a sequel to that and its a must play game nevertheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, like I did with the first game. However I can't. The World is visually good but it did not take me in like e.g. the world of Hollow Knight. And for a Metroidvania where exploring the world is part of the fun thats disappointing. Next are the "Boss-Fights". These really made me hate Ori and the Will of the Wisps. They are not fun. The Boss-Plattforming-Runs leave no room for mistakes. Do it right/perfect or die and start again. The fights themselves have their on level of bs thrown at you. Here are black smoky attack indicators in front of black smoke. Hope you use the 0.5 seconds to doge. It never really feels like the fight is in your control. Just hope RNG favours your run so you can beat the bosses. Never did I want to smash my controller against the wall more than fighting these bosses.I never felt such frustration while playing Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Hollow Knight or Armored Core 6 as I did while playing Ori and the Will of the Wisps. At the end I was just glad it was over and I can uninstall the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the Blind Forest was great and unique, but this sequel really completed what made the first one so awesome. Some mechanics feel weird, which is probably where most of the difficulty comes from. However, at the same time, they are super creative and unconventional. In terms of how this relates to other metroidvanias, it seemingly takes inspiration from a lot of the ones I played up until this point, but does it so well that it is hard to be upset about it. The visuals are perfect and the OST is a really awesome twist on the first game's sound track, as well as new tunes that make the journey feel much darker but still emotional. Gotta address the elephant in the room for differences between this and the first game . I kind of felt weird about all the different movement options towards the end of the game, because I often misinputted due to the time pressure, and forgetting that certain movements are mapped rather than LB or RB on the controller. Exploring in this game is great, and there's virtually no punishment for going the wrong way . This is very close to a perfect game in my mind, though some may find it surprisingly challenging. Awesome effort from the development team!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of a perfect sequel. A fantastic game for an insanely good and unforgettable series that has stolen my heart, making me love every moment from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 11 hours to finish the main story + a moderate number of side quests.Art, music, and gameplay were AWESOME. The story wasn't quite as good as everyone raved, but it was still definitely good enough. Seriously loved the game. I'm not much of a side scroller fan, but dang this game defied all expectations. I'd say you should definitely grab it when it goes on sale. The thing this game does REALLY well is make you feel like you're insanely good at the game. The screen scrolls by so fast, and you're just dashing and leaping from one thing to the other. They do an awesome job of teaching you slowly and adding on skills slowly so you never feel overwhelmed. Fun puzzles, pretty good story, great gameplay/mechanics (it feels especially good on a controller, I wasn't a huge fan of the keyboard + mouse), great art, and an awesome sound track. My only complaints are that the final boss fight was too easy, and the game wasn't long enough! But seriously they did a great job.

_childDocuments_.review: : I played the original twice, and I definitely remember a better, more confident experience, but gave it an 11.4/10 ...: was overwhelmed by this one; it's maybe even more of an Action RPG than I expected with all the NPCs vs. sidequests, combat, and there's a huge world to explore! As one of few who didn't like Bastion at all, there's definitely a bittersweet taste due to my preferences. However, having finished this game in Normal mode, and as an (inefficient) explorer/someone inspecting every 'nook and cranny', I managed to make the game rather underwhelming closer to the finish — compensating the intensity, but maybe a too relaxed experience while enjoying the view, and making enough screenshots = lack of balance/players too spoilt with abilities and such? I felt too invincible at a certain moment, and it was mostly the beautiful music, scenery and the emotive storytelling that prevailed for me in this sequel and kept me going! Where it was rather stressful for me in the beginning — not confident enough in a fight, because of the lack of affinity with battling in general — I think I found the borders of arrogance near the end 😇 As a result, an important message to potential players: even though you will face 'dead ends' if you start exploring as much as possible right from the start (like I did), if you want an easy experience in Normal mode, and it's in your nature to discover, go ahead! If you prefer to stay focused on your main path, aren't thát distracted by sidequests etc. (unlike me) in general, and want to have a more challenging/brave experience, you know what to do instead. Fun fact though: there are Leaderboards that don't seem to update after a finish anymore; I was @ 85% by then, but a few of my friends were @ 87%, and 1 even @ 98%, so 'OPri' for sure!Furthermore, it's rare, but even after so many hours, I'm still not 100% confident while playing this game with a keyboard (and so many buttons) ... Xbox Game Studios, right? I had expected the following notice: ". Talked about this with a friend, who initially started with keyboard controls, but soon realized the controller was the way to go. As a fan of both Super Meat Boy, and SMB Forever, I was excited for the Spirit Trials (races), but I wish there were just a few buttons mapped ... The escape sequences on the other hand were a breeze, and reminded me of aforementioned auto-runner.10/11.4 — overwhelming in a good and bad way, but I now only feel to play the original once more!New to the series? You definitely don't want to skip the original (Definitive Edition), but if you're very much into Action RPGs, combat, tactics etc., maybe think twice, and who knows start with the sequel ...

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10- Visuals are downright spectacular- Snappy and satisfying platforming through exceptionally designed levels (world)- Compared to Ori and the Blind Forrest (Also highly recommended):   - More content overall   - More story   - More "weapons"/skills, more upgradability of weapons adn skills for customization of your preferred playstyle. A "home base" exists with skill vendors and characters and such, which really gives Ori a sense of belonging in the forest.    - Worse "boss" battles. Ori and the Blind Forrest had challenging platforming escapes to punctuate milestones in the game, Ori and the Will of the Wisps has underwhelming boss fights as a substitute. They're still a great deal of fun and really awesome visually but don't feel like they close out a completed zone as well as the escapes in the previous game. These were probably used for the flexibility they afford to the story development.    - Generally easier than the previous game (played through both on normal). The platforming is substantially more forgiving (can be a good or bad thing because it is slightly less satisfying to clear difficult levels, but also a lot less frustrating on those sections that would otherwise take many, many attempts)    - Autosave compared to user-defined save in the first game. This definitely makes the game mostly easier but sometimes harder depending on the save points. - Game performance is good, I had no frame drops. I had a few in the previous game.

_childDocuments_.review: “Ori and the Will of the Wisps” is my favorite game of all time currently. While it’s not, in my opinion, the best game of all time, it is by far my favorite. The music by Gareth Coker is some of the best soundtracks I’ve heard, and the art style is 10 out of 10. While this game does focus on combat far more than the first game, the movement, exploration, and story are all still there in the fullest, and mesh with the combat fantastically. All the bosses are great and have some of the best boss music I’ve heard! If you haven’t played the game and are considering it, jump on it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. I already liked the Blind Forest a fair bit, and the sequel feels more polished and fleshed out. Should mention it's one of these sequels that feels interchangeable with its older sibling, though it is noticeably more combat oriented, and not only because of major encounters.Shouldn't forget the game isn't attempting to allure diehard metroidvania enthusiasts from what I've seen, so it doesn't get overly complex nor substantial. It's possible to focus the story entirely, leaving what else there is to rot - although it's advisable to explore every nook and cranny to find upgrades for Ori. Audio is quite nicely done. The cue that plays whenever you complete an objective stands out so much I just had to spare a sentence for it. I wish boss battles had way more pumped up music though, as they feel more of a thrilling exploration music tracks for me.Mobility is great and a standout feature for me. You will rapidly attain new, fun abilities throughout the game, gaining access to new places, as metroidvanias usually work. I even went for a 100% save file as I felt good about playing around with the endgame moveset.There are a lot more NPCs to interact this time around, making the sequel feel more alive than its predecessor. Then again loneliness played a big part in the Blind Forest. There's a quest system now, adding sidequests, which didn't feel too engaging as they're mainly just fetch quests or directions. The "Hand to hand" one was pretty fun though, unless you skip a beat which I imagine is quite easy to do. Checkpoint system is quite forgiving. For a relaxing platformer/action game this hits the nail on the head. Animations and artstyle are probably the main selling point of this game, and rightfully so. Despite small enemy variety, different environments felt full of life and unique. I did get a couple of extremely brief stutters every now and then, both in audio and video simultaneously, though it was not a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias. The game has a very large and beautiful world with a lot of additional tasks and items to collect. The storyline in the game is also very good. If you like games of this genre, then you should definitely play this game

_childDocuments_.review: They've done it again. _childDocuments_.review: Will of the Wisps is a beautiful sequel to Blind Forest, taking a lot of clear clues from Hollow Knight on bettering itself as a Metroidvania-esque title, but there are definitely some issues with the complete experience that left me with a weird aftertaste.I may have more to add to this review as I give it time to settle on me. I will say that I don't regret the journey, it's just that my hangups are a bit too loud to fully ignore.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing...Ori and the Blind Forest was fantastic. The storytelling without much dia/monologue, combined with superbly tight controls and mechanics, followed by a stellar score, make it one of my favorite experiences.Then came Hollow Knight and blew everything out of the water. Easily one of the best games ever created.Moon Studios most likely played Hollow Knight as well, and went "Oh man, this is awesome. These mechanics, this story, this world. This is just pure genius. We've got to have this."And so they went to work. Everything new between Blind Forest and Will of the Wisps is reflections of things that made Hollow Knight incredible. In my opinion, it breaks from the Ori I remember, as there's a whole bunch more characters that speak, other than the spirits. Nonetheless, it feels like Hollow Knight: Ori Edition. Or should that be Ori: Hollow Knight Edition?Either way, it is definitively worth your time.Round of applause to the team for making me cry for the antagonist, again.
_childDocuments_.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the original Ori or Hollow Knight, this is the game for you. It blends the two of them together in a beautiful, and creepy at times, game. It's got the combat of Hollow Knight, mixed with the color and visuals and escape sequences from the original Ori.The story is just as touching as the first game accompanied by an amazing score behind the whole game!It took me 13:50hrs to finish the game with ~98% on my file, all the life/energy upgrades, just missing a few minor things here and there. The previous Ori I didn't feel as inclined to get close to 100% as this game made me due to this game feeling more rewarding for the progress.I did have a few technical issues though, the underwater sections where you can Bash certain items and creatures, the games camera would go wild darting across the screen in an uncontrollable way. It wasn't common, but common enough that it's making this list. The only other major bug I ran into was the audio getting desynced and no longer playing combat sounds. This happened once or twice and required a full restart to fix, which is more of a minor nuisance but still not enjoyable.With all that said, I'd highly recommend the game! I loved almost every minute of it, once you get all the base abilites, the game opens up completely and you realize how much bigger than the previous it is!

_childDocuments_.review: "Ori and the Will of the Wisps" is an absolutely stunning masterpiece of a game that takes you on an emotional journey that will leave you feeling awed and moved. From the moment I started playing, I was completely swept away by the beauty and wonder of the game's art and music.The story of Ori and his quest to save his loved ones is both heart-wrenching and inspiring. The game takes you on a rollercoaster ride of emotions, from joy and wonder to heartache and sadness.But despite the emotional weight of the story, the game is also incredibly fun to play. While many platformer games rely solely on combat, making the game hard by throwing overpowered bosses, Ori games has always focused on the movement mechanics being challenging as well while also not being completely unfair. And the game's many side-quests, hidden areas, spirit trials, etc. kept me exploring every nook and cranny of the world well past the actual story. But what really sets "Ori and the Will of the Wisps" apart is the way it makes you feel. The game's themes of love, loss, and perseverance are woven into every aspect of the game, its "painting coming to life" like visuals and gorgeous music, to the characters and their struggles.Overall, a truly remarkable game that touched me in ways that few games ever have. It is a testament to the power of video games to tell deeply emotional and impactful stories, and it is an experience that I will never forget. If you're a fan of platformers, or just looking for a game that will move you to tears, I cannot recommend it highly enough.
