_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Hollow Knight that blew its entire budget on its visuals.The combat, while less ♥♥♥♥ than its more platforming based predecessor, is severely hindered by a lack of variety and the stupid equipment system. Speaking of equipment, you can now use 3 at a time, with all the cool ones (and most of the boring ones too) being locked behind both ridiculous prices and energy costs so steep that you'll never find a good use for them! And since any ranged attack takes energy, so you *have* to get up close and personal with the bosses, which are so incredibly awkward and boring to fight that they resemble puzzle sections more than actual boss fights! The awesome chase sections from the first game are back, so that's something at least.The unique saving system from the first game got replaced by a soulless autosave.Remember when I talked about equipment being locked behind steep prices in whatever currency the game uses? Well guess what, weapons aren't the only thing you can throw your meagre savings at! Options include:-Cornifer's map shop from Hollow Knight, except nearly useless, and also run by a creepy ghoul thing.-Salubra's charm shop from Hollow Knight, except the effects are worse and the seller is a weirdo.-Building houses for the annoying cat people, so they have a place to stay when they aren't interrupting gameplay by saying the same thing five times over.If you played the first game, you will probably be used to robbing the graves of your siblings. Well, in this game you do the same, except to total strangers! How delightful!And maybe, just maybe, I could have powered through all the bad, the mediocore, and the blatantly ripped from Hollow Knight, and enjoyed myself with a lesser, but nonetheless worthy title.Sadly, my game audio is 50% static and validating my files does nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the will of the wisps is an amazing and emotional game that surpasses the previous title Ori and the Blind Forest in many ways. The combat system has been given a complete overhaul as you no longer spam a button to use one type of attack. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel that has surpassed the first game in almost everyway!Pros:-There's so much more to explore.-There are now new side missions.-The combat has been improved.-New weapons/abilites to acquire.(Returning ones as well)-There are now actual boss battles.(These are probably the best part of the game, unfortunately there's only about 4-5 of them, and some of them go down pretty quickly. But still are amazing nonetheless)-The visuals and the soundtrack are just as amazing as before.(Sometimes I had a hard time leaving the main menu because of the soundtrack)Minor nitpicks/missteps:-The character Ku is absent from most of the game. There's so much more that could've been done with her gameplaywise, but she's only playable for a short period of time.-The bashing move, just like in the first game, seems to be a bit imprecise at times due to the controls.(1 button can do multiple things and sometimes it triggers the wrong move at a given moment)-Very silly complaint, but some of the enemy designs seemed a bit off, they look a bit cartoony.Not much to complain about, this is near perfect game! It's a must for metroidvania fans!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ori and the will of wisps was a game that brought so many emotions. It brings back the characters you know from the first game and puts ori and the new young owl, ku in a scary situation that causes ori to have to save the day. The soundtrack of this game is the main thing that brings me to tears but adding the story made me cry a huge amount once i completed the game. The new mechanics are alot like hollow knight, oris new main attack is a light sword and she gains shards to add different skills, such as wall climbing. These can be changed and removed for different play styles. Her main attack can be swapped out with things such as a bow and arrow and heath regeneration. The main skills have 3 slots for 3 different skills to pick and choose from, Some areas will need you to change these out to get to where you need to be.Overall Ori and the will of the wisps was a game that really grabbed me and took me into its world until i completed it. It is a game i would suggest getting as soon as you can to experience how great the art, music and story truly is.

_childDocuments_.review: 2020 had plenty of promising titles coming out during it, but basically everyone of them were shattered.. Still there were hope, as little shining lights started glimmering and blinding with their greatness. Indie scene did again what majority couldn't with Ori and the Will of the Wisps, Desperados 3 and Hades. Also should count in Indie multiplayers like GTFO, Deep Rock Galactic, Phasmophobia, Fall Guys and Among Us though it's not 2020 release. Wasteland 3 also sounded like it was a good game, but was broken at release, though fixed quite soon enough? Unlike many major releases..Ori and the Blind Forest is a game that consider being among best titles from the genre and Will of the Wisps goes there with it's predecessor. Both are so beautiful games with great atmosphere including stunning visuals and great sounds along with precise and impactful gameplay and story.World in both games shows that your cuteness doesn't matter, it's ruthless and wants to take you down with it. Instead Ori needs to stand up and learn means of survival and make and meet potential companions and friendly people on the way who will want help and in return give it back. In Will of the Wisps you will be basically growing a community as side quest, where all kinds of creatures come after Ori goes around the world doing all kinds of problem solving.And that problem solving is done by learning great amount of skills and finding shards around the world to become badass lightning bolt that shows nasties what lights soldier is all about, aka shining light where it doesn't shine! This means you go from dark caverns, to tropical pools collecting spirit light to make it whole while helping friends and community to survive from the decay and potential other predators and threats. Getting to those lights need some puzzle solving with skills Ori has or will usually find from the respective area.All around great experience and don't have pretty much any negatives about it, hmm besides starting area in Baur's Reach, it felt bit off, but otherwise really great experience and certain top release from year 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really great I would say.The movement when you unlock everything is very fun and easy to manage. This isn't to say that early game movement is bad, but it is a lot more free feeling the further you progress. There are a lot of movement features that are unique and fun to take advantage of. I found myself loving exploring the map because of this.The story was pretty good. It was compelling enough to keep playing for it and tugged at your heart in appropriate times. I would say that if you loved the first game you will probably enjoy this one too.The enemies are interesting. Hate the bats though for reasons that will become clear. The game has a combat shrine system that is very fun and I found myself activating them multiples times to see if I could make it without getting hit. The map layout if interesting and I feel like it does a good job to a point of looping you back to where you need to be for the story. I would say though that if you are going back through for collectibles, you may find yourself going long ways from the warp points for one spirit light.However, I would still say that getting all the items and such are not difficult at all, so if you like to 100% games then this will be fun. Though I will say that there are quite a few bugs in the game... I can't even tell you how many times my game glitched and soft-locked me until I reloaded. As a fair warning, Be sure to not use Bash when you are right next to a wall in the direction of said wall. This will put you OOB but there is no way to get back in bounds. This is the bug I ran into most and sometimes it wasn't even from Bash, it just happened. I don't know why this game feels buggier than the first but it is. All in all the game is fun and I feel like it is a good game to go in line with the first.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, beginning to end, start to finish. I have to say, this game is one of the best games I've ever played in my life. Truly a masterpiece in the video gaming industry. I would highly recommend purchasing this game and its predecessor as soon as you can. It's worth way more than what you pay for it, and it tells a wonderful tale of family, friendship, helping others, and, in the end, sacrifice. I would immediately buy another Ori project should Moon Studios come out with another one. I wholeheartedly believe that this game earns the right to be game of the year, and if not this, then the first game. Everything about it is so wonderful and rich and beautiful that words cannot express my feelings about it properly. I only hope that I may one day create a tale as compelling and story driven as Ori, characters so rich in lore and excellence that I could achieve even a fraction of what the Ori franchise has given to this world.Thank you, Moon Studios, for all your hard work in this excellent game. I don't think I'll be forgetting it soon, if ever. You are one of the few people who can actually make me cry, and one of the few I can truly appraise without seeing any faults in your creations. I can only hope that one day, I may achieve something even slightly comparable to what you have made. Until then though, I'll be taking my leave.And to you, Ori, who now lives on as the protector of Niwen and the giver of its life... I hope you're happy where you are. I'm sad your final adventure had to take place outside your home, but at least you've done something truly remarkable in your world. You are a wonderful spirit, and you truly deserve the title of a hero.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap. I didn't think that a game could top the original. There wasn't really anything wrong with it. The art direction is amazing; I haven't taken this many screenshots while playing a game in my life. The score used alot of themes from the original as well as unique music per zone like before.The gameplay is where the sequel shines. You still got bashing and dashing, but instead of the shooting mechanic from the first game, you wield heavy and light attacks. The key is, though, that those attacks can aid your movement which is the best part of the game. It takes some cues from Celeste by adding a 'pass-through' contextual movement for water and sand. Overall, its an improvement on what was otherwise a phenomenal game.The one gripe I have is that there are some audio and gameplay bugs. A couple times, I clipped into a wall and the last fight was completely devoid of the boss audio. Also, the chase sequences kinda got old, though they were fun. Also, it's a little bit easier than its predecessor. Course, it didn't have the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ canyon part or that final battle where you run from Kuro. But, in the same vein, I don't think it had a part like Ginso Tree though a couple points came kinda close.If it's not a 10/10, it's at the very least a 9/10 depending on whether you think perfection can be achieved or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I have so so many issues with Ori series and WotW in general. I hate both games but for different reasons. First game was kinda niche but fun take on metroidvania/platformer game (with slightly less emphasis on exploration and much more on the tight jump/timing mechanics). Second one... I guess it has a crisis of identity and does not really know what it want to be.I 100%-d it but it did not bring me any joy. To be honest I liked it much more when it tried not to pretend to be hollow knight/dark souls.=Story=Once apon a time a time there was a one-legged dog. It tired to pee and lifted a leg and felt down. What a sad game.Tonally this game is an absolute mess. It tries to be dark and moody and the family friendly disney faximilie at the same time, which ruins any attempt to tell a story.=Escape scenes and rubberbanding=Yes, there are escape sequences. They suck just as much as in the first game, but thanks god they cut the lengths of those sequences by 25%. At least this ♥♥♥♥ ends way before it overstays its welcome.=Gameplay=Remember in the first game you actually had to control your energy budget cause it was a pool from which your checkpoints were powered? Who cares now, you can have tonns of hp and energy by the first 10% of the game.=Weapons and skills and charms=You tried to copy everything from hollow knight, but let's be real, you have no idea why they were added there in the first place, right? Holy ♥♥♥♥ the weapons are so off the chart there. (Pro tip, just try to beat final boss with anything other than lightning spears and tell me how balanced this game is).=My general impression=There is a skeleton of a solid game buried somewhere here, but the game is underdeveloped, collectibles are barely sketched, the whole weapon/skill system should be scrapped and started from scratch, boss fights are laughable, and the balance is totally off. The game is like 35% done and should have stayed in pre-production for at least a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: To start: Ori and the Will of the Wisps definitely has a few technical issues. A sound blip bug on NPC dialogue, the occasional stuttering, and a couple events were unplayable without restarts.Hopefully all of that gets fixed in the next few days. If it does, I'll remove this part of the review. Regardless, the few bugs I've found weren't nearly enough to counter the rest of the game.Because otherwise, this game is amazing.They took all the things that people loved about the first Ori, expanded on them, give them to you fairly early, and pull in an entirely new combat/boss system. I've yet to find a single mechanic I haven't fallen in love with immediately.A lot of people are crying that they're stealing the RPG mechanics from Hollow Knight, but personally HK felt really janky from limited movement. Ori mixes the combat and movement in a way that blows my mind with how fun it is.A 2D platformer has no business being this fun.The visuals are gorgeous, the OST is beautiful. The plot isn't complicated, and intentionally a bit loose so the player gets to choose where they go next most of the time. There's tons of new, optional abilities that always either make things more interesting, or give you a little Quality-Of-Life boon. They range from bigger, stronger attacks that cost more to use, to simply being able to stick to and climb up walls without having to bunny-hop your way up them.Outside of the bugs, I honestly can't find anything to complain about. Ori and the Blind Forest was by no means a perfect game, but it was still pretty damn good, and Will of the Wisps has improved on it in every possible way. It's a fair bit more actiony than the first game, but the action flows so well with the platforming movement that it still feels natural. I'm just interweaving combat abilities between reflexive aerial movement. It's incredibly fun.Update: 100%'d (all quests/collectables/etc) the game on Hard, took roughly 21 hours. Take that into potential consideration in regards to price, if you're stingy about Price-Per-Hour ratios. Otherwise, I can say I enjoyed every single minute of playing this magnificent game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially better than the first game in every aspect.Just finished the game, essentially beat it 100% minus a few health and power orbs that I could have went back and get in under 30 minutes. It is clear that there is no filler to this game, it all connects together in a vibrant way that never makes you feel frustrated or that you are wasting your time.I'm a pretty sensitive person and this game's story really had me from start to finish. _childDocuments_.review: The little spirit Ori is no stranger to peril, but when a fateful flight puts the owlet Ku in harm’s way, it will take more than bravery to bring a family back together, heal a broken land, and discover Ori’s true destiny. From the creators of the acclaimed action-platformer Ori and the Blind Forest comes the highly anticipated sequel. Embark on an all-new adventure in a vast world filled with new friends and foes that come to life in stunning, hand-painted artwork. name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster
detailed_description: Special Offer About the Game 1993 LEWIS & CLARK COUNTY, MONTANA, US Ten years ago, teenager Nicole and her mother left the family hotel after discovering her father Leonard's affair with, and pregnancy of Rachel, a girl her own age who eventually committed suicide. Now that both of her parents have passed, Nicole hopes to fulfill her mother’s last will to sell the hotel and make amends to Rachel's relatives. With the will and determination to put that chapter behind her, she returns to the hotel with the family’s lawyer to audit the decaying structure. As the weather unexpectedly turns for the worst, Nicole has no way to leave the large mountain lodge, and finds support in Irving, a young FEMA agent, using one of the first radio telephones ever built. With his help, Nicole starts to investigate a mystery far deeper than what people in the valley thought. A story of love and death, where melancholy and nostalgia melt into a thrilling ghost tale. Explore the vast and detailed hotel, unravelling dark secrets of the family's past Binaural audio for a truly immersive experience Intriguing, touching and mature storytelling Multi-layered narrative thriller, combining elements of mystery and horror

_childDocuments_.review: I felt really betrayed by this game. It starts as an atmospheric cross between Gone Home and Firewatch, following Nicole as she returns to the hotel she grew up in and the bad memories that remain there. It ends practically endorsing the relationship between a 50 year old man and a 16 year old. Rachel is the central figure of the story, but beyond her dedication to playing the organ and her dyslexia we learn nothing about her. There are no real characters in this story at all, and in a walking simulator, that means there is no story.  The main thrust of the story is your conversations with Irving, a FEMA agent. This relationship might be enough to carry the game if it was resolved any better than anything else but it fails too. The hotel is massive but there's nothing in it. Comparing this game to Gone Home is ridiculous - every inch of that house was covered in personality and the remnants of the people who lived there. There are maybe 5 readable notes to find, and only a dozen or so items you discuss with Irving. You pick up a few devices but only use them once, maybe twice. This is the most hollow game I ever played. The only distinguishable theme is "love is love," even if it's clearly abuse of power.TLDR; This is not a good walking simulator. This is not a good story. It takes on a lot of difficult themes - abuse, suicide, guilt, trauma - and handles them with all the care of a bull in a china shop.EDIT: This game also has a weird habit of continuing to run in the background even after closing from the menu, hence why I have 100 hours in a game that takes like 6 max. I figured this out after 4 days and shut it down with task manager.

_childDocuments_.review: Changed my review to a thumbs-up. There's a lot to be desired with the plot, but something about this game, the locations, and some of the subtle scares... has me thinking about The Timberland hotel long after I uninstalled.Original review (thumbs down):They played the atmosphere so well. The story was so intriguing. They nailed the slow burn... it built the tension up and up, until every creak caused goosebumps... and finally when the story reaches this thrilling fever pitch... The third act never comes. It just fizzles and ends. Curtains down, goodbye, hope you're happy with that, see ya later, get out.There are games you play and can't stop thinking about afterwards... this is definitely one of them, unfortunately the thought is "Well. That was so unsatisfying it feels like I wasted 3 hours of my life."Nothing worse than a story that leaves a bitter taste in your mouth.

_childDocuments_.review: It hurts me a little to say I don't recommend the game, because you can see how much effort was put into it. It actually aces every technical aspect, but fails in the most important one when it comes to a walking sim: the story.PROS:The hotel is amazing. Seriously, one of the best game environments I've ever seen. And it's not only about the graphics: it really FEELS like a real-life hotel. Very immersive! The voice acting is also very good. The controls are a bit annoying (specially when trying to run), but that doesn't really detract from the experience.The ambiance and atmosphere are great. There are no jump scares, but the rising tension is well constructed and delivered.CONSWell, the story is too thin. No spoilers here, but some facts are simply told, but not explained: character motivation is lacking in many key happenings. The premise had so, so much potential, but the story turns out to be very underwhelming. They failed to flash out the characters well enough for us to really understand their motivations and care about them. Gone Home does a much better job here, despite being considerably shorter.It's really a pity. I'd love it if someone used the same hotel, same models, same everything, and just changed the dialogues to turn this into an outstanding walking simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Just another walking simulator. Similar to Gone Home, the game tries to bait-and-switch you into thinking supernatural stuff is happening by making your mind do all the work. The actual twist itself makes 0 sense, and relies heavily on basically every character involved, from the police to the families to have major brain damage.A lot of the game forces you to go at a VERY specific snail's pace. I'm pretty sure it expects you to stand still and do absolutely nothing when your character is talking on the phone. There were multiple times where I would find out what I needed to do at the beginning of the dialogue, walk to the location, and then stand in front of the object I need to interact with because I'm not allowed to interact with it until the game tells me I'm allowed to know the answer. Oftentimes, I would even have to leave and re-enter the room because the object's "Interact" button is still greyed out only to be greeted with ANOTHER phonecall that I have to sit through before I can continue. I already solved it. LET ME SOLVE IT.The game tries to promote you to explore but at the same time, large portions of the hotel will either never be visited, or visited maybe once, never to return. You'll find that you'll be going back and forth between a small number of the same locations over and over, namely the Master Suite and the Basement throughout the entire game while large portions of entire floors are basically ignored and have little to no reward for going out of your way to explore.The actual content tries so hard to appear "Deep" scattering books on astrophysics and the occult everywhere, talking about characters discussing religion over chess, and just generally trying to seem pretentious as possible without actually SAYING anything. The actual depth of the conversation is about a shallow as a painting. This game is bad. Even by walking simulator standards.

_childDocuments_.review: I really should have listened to the reviewers warning about how terribly the game handled its main themes. (Some spoilers ahead). Like others have said, the sexual relationship between a middle aged man and the sixteen year old girl he tutors is labelled as a "love" by the game and not condemned for its predatory nature, but instead seen as negative because it is an "affair". This framing gets worse as the game goes on, which was opposite of what I was expecting as I continued playing, thinking the main character would have some growth (since she was also a teenager at the time of the events) and realize that the girl she was so jealous of was clearly a victim here (and, as the title of the game tells us, tragically died). That does not happen. The game also strongly encourages you to, at the very least, attempt suicide.The story had some potential and could have been handled very differently and the game has some interesting visual elements, but I would strongly recommend that anyone that feels even mildly uncomfortable with the themes in its title and description skip this game entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Another case of wishing Steam had a moderate option for reviews rather than yes or no.My review WILL spoil the game--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------First of all, there were plenty of good things about this game. The atmosphere is pretty, the sound design is (usually) very well done, and  of the story is great. I had lots of fun just interacting with different set pieces and walking around the hotel. Where the game really stagnates for me is the weird pseudo-Firewatch thing they had going. Irving interacting with Nicole had its moments, but typically fell flat with an odd script and strange diction that made them feel "acted" rather than people. I found myself cringing at some of the early dialogue which felt unnatural at best. Though, this is never the issue of the voice actors as they're simply doing what their director wants.Of course, grooming is a major aspect of the story and is naturally an incredibly uncomfortable subject. The little it's touched on (before the final day) was rightfully disturbing and, I'd say, very well implemented. Unfortunately, there seems to be a reverence for the father's predatory actions that creeps up in the final day. It's gross and should have been written differently. None of your choices matter and, strangely enough, Nicole seems to hold ideals completely different from what you'd think a typical player would have, such as "pedophilia bad." It's clear that she resents her father for what he did which makes it all the more baffling that she suddenly runs to his defense whenever his "tendencies" get mentioned. My least favorite story beat is the very end when Nicole sets up her suicide in the car. The story absolutely does NOT adequately build up to this and how sudden it was removes any player agency. At the very least, you are allowed to stop the car after starting the suicide attempt, but it was incredibly jarring and left a poor taste in my mouth. All in all, worth a play if you get it on a major discount. Expect an uncomfortable story with a poor ending. Most of the game will be intriguing and interesting and all of that buildup will amount to nothing as any semblance of good that was there is entirely excised, leaving a story that seems to praise the very thing it originally condemned.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review here: Conclusion:The Suicide of Rachel Foster delivers a haunting narrative within a beautiful, yet creepy, isolated hotel. With only an unknown companion on the phone to keep you company, you’re trapped in the last place you’d ever want to be, surrounded by memories of the past and secrets best left hidden from the world. Although delivering a conclusion which left me with questions, the experience throughout the entire three-hour narrative had me intrigued, invested, and captivated as to what we’ll uncover next and what’s around the corner. If you play games via PC and you’re looking for a well-designed and interesting story to play through, check out The Suicide of Rachel Foster. I’m hoping the game also comes to consoles at some point in the future (which I believe it is doing), as it means I’ll get to relive the story again from the comfort of my sofa.We gave it a solid 8.7/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much potential. The concept was very reminiscent of Painscreek Killings, which I loved. They emphasize on exploration, but the only things you can "investigate" that aren't items integral to the plot are bottles of cleaner and toothpaste. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend The Suicide of Rachel Foster. This review will contain major spoilers for the game, and discussion regarding pedophilia and suicide.This game's locations are beautiful, and I felt immersed when I was exploring. The attention to detail in the world itself was breathtaking. I found the audio design and voice acting to be well done, and the lack of a map with a "You Are Here" marker really helped me to feel lost and a bit helpless, which is exactly what this game needs. There's a portion of the game where In one instance, I found a very important plot-related tape that re-used the same texture as a mix tape that the main character made when she was ten years old. This, combined with radio calls every five minutes a la Dead Rising, and gleaning absolutely no lore from objects around the house, means that your story progression is limited to picking up specific - very obvious! - items, and allowing the main character to remember something from her childhood that we, as the player, have no way of knowing. It feels incredibly deus ex machina-y. I felt like I wasn't finding information out myself, nor unravelling a mystery. It was just "point A to point B." Every matchbox is the same, every "mix tape" is the same, and every travel report is the same.Now, I have no problem with a game that delves into controversial topics. Indeed, I think that video games have a unique way of tacking sensitive issues in a way that allows for context, reflection and empathy for all sides of serious situations that often get ignored or drowned out.With that said, the way The Suicide of Rachel Foster handles pedophilia, grooming and suicide is careless at best. I wish I could recommend The Suicide of Rachel Foster, but it wasn't an experience that I can throw my support behind. I look forward to the developer's next game, as it's clear that they have the talent to bring something beautiful to the genre, but this particular attempt was, for me, a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: (I know it says I have little time on record for this game, I have played it before on a since lost steam account)There are very few games I'd consider to have no redeeming qualities about them but The Suicide of Rachel Foster is simply a terrible excuse of writing. I'm going to summarize a bit, without any spoilers to just try to explain how simply f'ed up this game is.You move in to your family's hotel, it's revealed in a note that your father had an affair with a "young woman" and due to it your family has pretty much been in shambles with most of them dead. right off the bat, your father seems weird, he has lots of math books about dimensions and spiritualism and such, but don't let this fool you into thinking the game has a good environment. Obviously with the title of the game and the story of your father's affair you as the player are going to wonder about the identity and situation that lead up to Rachel Foster's suicide.You find out very early on that she was the teenage daughter of a family friend, who left her to stay with your father when he left on a trip for months, Rachel is revealed to have a speaking disorder making it hard to communicate and your father "kindly" volunteered to assist with speech therapy and watch over Rachel while her father was gone. This is when their "relationship" startedA lot of reviews here will call this "controversy" but to put it simply, it's just terrible writing and the authors letting their own views seep into the world views of every character in game. Stories like Catcher of the Rye or more similarly L*lita tell horrific stories and while controversial, the controversy is whether or not the material is appropriate to be presented, not that the topics are poorly written.With The Suicide of Rachel Foster you are given a story where it is revealed to you as the player and your character that your father has groomed this teenage girl and it is undeniably poor writing as every single character has the same view on the subject that despite the terrible acts of your father he was actually a great person and the relationship was actually true love and this teenage girl, who reminder, has a speech impediment so cannot communicate with her family that is gone for months (also the only phone is in your father's room) is actually an old soul who is mature for her age and wise beyond her years. The whole situation is undeniably manipulative and inescapable for this poor girl and the whole time the writer is doing his best to tell you that this is actually romantic. There is heavy emphasis that this game takes place in an area with an age of consent under 18 and the writer has clearly tried to make this girl sound womanly and not child-like but the game itself constantly undermines it's own attempts of redemption by characters literally calling Rachel a child in game, and her room a "child's room"The "old soul" and spiritualism could have been an amazing writing point as it is shown time and time again that is a way that groomers convince children that they are mature enough to be making decisions about dating someone who is undeniably more developed. But the author sees this as romantic, and because of it, the writer makes every character romanticize this awful scenario. The story could have very easily been saved by the main character at the very least being in denial that her father was a p*do until the evidence was undeniable and she was forced to confront her father's sins but that never happens, Rachel's situation is only expanded upon and shown to be more and more manipulative and abusive as the game continues and the characters only seem to call it true love.Besides the awful story, while graphics can have some appeal the clipping is so insane that it's honestly laughable, The game opens up with you flipping through notes and your fingers clip into the back of them, another beautiful scene right at the beginning where you make your way through a crowd with of people with black umbrellas at a funeral and your umbrella actually just clips into every umbrella that you walk past.There are multiple dialogue choices but the responses literally are so obviously written to account for both inputs that it's honestly pathetic. for example there's a scene where you get to choose between saying "merry christmas" and "I like (being called) Nicky" and the person your interacting with will simply say "merry christmas Nicky" which at this point your character has only been referred to as her real name Nicole.There are some red herrings that some might find interesting but, they feel incredibly feel half-assed and as a player you can tell which way the story is going to go in the end.Don't buy this game, don't support these devs, this writing is so terrible that it only serves to normalize these abusive situations.//SPOILERthere is also an interactive suicide scene in this game which is genuinely just another level of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever seen the movie "The Shining", then you will be able to understand right from the beginning how this game is going to feel. The name of this hotel "Timberline Lodge" is taken directly from the hotel's name in Oregon, where The Shining was filmed.Your reluctant visit to this secluded hotel spans 10 days in a Montana winter, stuck inside due to being snowed in. The primary goal is to do a structural inspection before you can put it on the market to sell. As events unfold, you realize that this is a journey of self-discovery while digging through the remnants of your family's past. You become more and more entwined in the past with nothing but a voice on a phone to guide you through the hotel, your only lifeline in complete isolation.The hotel feels like an antagonist in itself. With foreboding, rustic 70s style architecture, literally everything that creaks and groans as you walk, and unsettling hints of paranormal activity, you have yourself a very chilling backdrop for a story. I was on the edge of my seat from start to finish.+ The story is decent and it got its point across well in a short span of time. + Voice acting is fantastic. Your character's voice did a great job conveying her emotions about being in the hotel from start to finish.+ Excellent atmosphere. The sounds of an old, creaky hotel are spot on. + The hotel itself is incredibly detailed and beautiful, giving off that perfect "frozen in time" look.+ Your exploration is not restricted. You're free to go wherever you like right from the start.- The map was difficult to read. You could zoom in and scroll around, but I still had difficulty with it. It would have been better to have some sort of "You Are Here" place marker to better navigate your way.- Some objectives on your "to do list" felt like broken English to the point I did not understand what was being asked. I wasn't sure if this was on purpose or not. I had to look up a few guides online to figure out where I was supposed to go. - Ephebophilia is an issue in this story and I felt like it was skirted around completely. The dev's included such a dark and horrible issue, but it felt like they were too nervous to actually speak about it. It made the issue feel like it was put on the back burner and "unimportant" to the story.Though a very short game, I still enjoyed what was there. I probably would not pay full price due to the length as it can be completed in a couple of hours. Maybe more if you have to go back for achievements. I am looking forward to any future titles from the developers!

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster has to be one of the greatest games I've ever played in terms of atmosphere and making the player feel a certain way. The story it tells is one of the most disturbing, dark, and twisted ones I've ever played through and it left me with my jaw dropped on more than one occasion. Yes, there are themes of pedophilia and suicide, so if either of these are too intense for you, do not play this game. While the game has an incredible atmosphere and a strong story, there are some minor issues with it such as head bobbing that cannot be turned off, and some slight pacing and world design problems but unless you get easily motion sick I didn't find them to be too much of an issue. This is without a doubt one of the best looking walking sim type games I've ever played and I have played quite a few. The graphics are very realistic, keeping you fully immersed in the experience. The lighting is spot on as well. When the game wants to be pitch black, it gets pitch black, with the only light coming from strikes of lightning or a ever so slightly open door. The sound design is breathtaking. The voice actors were absolutely fantastic, putting on incredibly believable performances which help you really feel as if you are the character, going through all of this yourself. This is helped by the fact that you never see your character's face in the entire game. Cut scenes only show your hands, never your face. There isn't much music in the game, instead the game's soundtrack is made up of the groans, whispers, and creaks of the empty hotel. These are done so brilliantly that the task of walking through a lit hallway became a tense and almost terrifying experience. The hotel becomes as much a character as any human in the game, an achievement few games are capable of. The gameplay is very simple. You walk through an empty hotel, looking for clues and completing tasks as you try and unravel the mysterious events of the past and the present. You get a couple items to help you such as a flashlight but these are very rarely used. The main focus is the story being told, leaving the gameplay limited to running around finding the next small puzzle or area to go to. There's nothing wrong with this, it is a walking sim after all but your movement speed is incredibly slow and head bobbing is always on with no way to turn it off. This only annoyed me personally but I've seen some people saying that it made them motion sick. During dialogue you will be given options to choose from but these have very little if any impact on the narrative. Unfortunately the hotel is absolutely massive, and it's not always clear where you're meant to go, and even at the end of the game I was getting lost, even while following a guide to help me know where to go next when the game didn't make it well known. I couldn't imagine trying to beat this game without a basic guide of where to go at times.  The story of The Suicide of Rachel Foster is one of the darkest, most twisted, and disturbing tales I have ever experienced in any kind of form of media. This combined with the horror like atmosphere and chilling voice performances made me do something I have never done with any video game ever. It made me so disturbed and uncomfortable that halfway through the game I took off my headset and played with the audio coming from the speakers instead because I genuinely needed just that small separation from me and the game. Part of why I had to do this is because the story, despite how dark it is, is almost 100% believable. I could see this exact thing happen in real life and that hit me on a personal note. So many people in this narrative have had their lives ruined or ended because of the actions of one or two people. It was a reminder of what humans are capable of that hit me in the chest like a sludge hammer. If you're easily disturbed I would be weary playing this game. The story had the potential to be one of the greatest in all of gaming but sadly there are some pacing issues. For the first 3/4 of the game the pacing is well done but the end of the game felt very rushed. Despite being rushed the ending was still able to end in a fairly decent way, but had the potential to be even better. This is one of those games that will stick with you long, long after you watch the end credits, and the final choice you make in the game is one of the best in any game I've played. In conclusion, The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a game that will leave a lasting impression on you. Despite some short comings, the pure evil and darkness present in the narrative and the absolutely stellar presentation creates a game that every fan of the genre who thinks they're mentally able to should experience. It is a walking simulator that pushes the genre to its limit with what a game narrative can be emotionally. I don't think this game is appreciated enough for what it accomplishes with its narrative and environment. The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a game that shouldn't be played by all, but should be played by all that can. For more reviews follow my

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a walking simulator that should last about 5 hours if you are super fastidious about examining everything.  The overall story is about as "fun" as you'd expect from the title, but the main gameplay is closer to The Shining than you might expect.The graphics, sound design and voice acting are all great, although the later is marred by some odd word choices in the script.  I should also note the particularly well done guitar theme.The two major complaints:The story is done well at first, but at least in English, it doesn't quite bring you to where it goes, so the ending felt rather forced.Technology-wise the game is also weak.  The actual gameplay is flawless - I never got caught up on polygons or fell through the floor, but the game is missing pretty much everything that brings "perfectly okay" to "great'.  No ability to change the control layout, no control of head bob, etc, has caused problems for some players.  Worse, to my mind, there is no ability to voluntarily save the game - you only get one save file, and it automatically saves when you reach the end of one of the days, whether you want it to or not.  This also means having to restart a chapter if you need to stop playing for whatever reason.  Likewise, almost all the story-telling is done through dialogue, but the way it is handled really only works if you sit and wait for the dialogue to play out - going directly to your next destination can cause some odd behaviour.  Further, many of the dialogues will only trigger on specific circumstances, e.g. on day X in room Y before performing action Z - with no reason to enter room Y ever, let alone in that exact time frame.  This leads to a fair bit of character development you are unlikely to know you even missed.  Finally, although this is more a nitpick, progress is fully linear, with various interactive elements literally not existing, or being non-interactive until the scheduled time.  It is handled fairly well in context, but there are a few times where it seems forced.Overall, a well-done production, especially at sale price, at least if you like walking simulators.  I genuinely hope to see what this team can do with a little more experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a complicated one so bare with me.While I enjoyed my time with The Suicide of Rachel Foster, and as much of a polished, solid game that it is, it ends off with a VERY problematic viewpoint, one where I HEAVILY question the writers.You play as Nicole, a young woman whose father  recently passed away. They were the owners of an incredibly fancy hotel that they now leave in your hands to sell off. As you arrive at the hotel, you are basically locked inside due a massive snowstorm outside. Luckily, you are not alone as your new good ol buddy and FEMA agent, Irving, has contacted you and helps guide you through the hotel uncovering its and your family's secrets.As you progress through the game, you begin to learn a bit about Rachel Foster, the girl in the title of the game. I'll spare the details just so this review doesn't go on for too long, but basically, there is a LOT to unpack and a LOT of things your character discovers that completely shook me during my first time playing through.Before I get into that, I just wanna mention all of the positives that this game has to offer, because there are quite a few. I really enjoyed exploring the hotel. Being able to walk around with a LOT of freedom let me take my time and progress where I needed to at my own pace. The environments were very detailed and decorated and teh atmosphere was absolutely fantastic. Every second, this game gave me a chilling vibe that something was going to jumpscare me, but alas, no jumpscares! Saves me the trouble of worrying. However, there isn't much GAME to it as its primarily a walking simulator where you find things, push buttons, ect. With that being said, here is my (and I think most of this games players) main problem with the game, specifically its story (spoilers ahead)All that being said, its a solid game for its pure exploration and gameplay but falling very VERY short on the message it is trying to get out to its audience. And I cannot recommend a game that promotes something like that.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like walking sims and mysteries, with very brief touches of horror, then consider picking this up when it's on sale. Don't pay full price. I paid less than five bucks for it, and that should 100% be your breakpoint.The Ramble: Not going to talk much about the problematic elements of the story (suicide, pedophilia, grooming, mental manipulation via grief, etc.), all of which are arguably displayed with a sympathetic lens (a touch f'd up, TBH).A very run-of-the-mill walking sim with some occasional moments of brilliance and good story telling, but most often, everytime it felt like it was opening up to something else, the gameplay would suddenly, abruptly stop and shift gears in a way that was very annoying. At first, it seems like there's going to be elements of survival and being unable to feed yourself and keep yourself warm. This is telegraphed very, very well, and then, abandoned entirely by Day 3. Then, there are elements of mystery and exploration, searching for 'ghosts', but the exploration is never fully realized. Yeah, walking around looking for 'ghosts' with a parabolic microphone feels really cool! ...and then, it just doesn't matter anymore. Finally, there are elements of horror, but the horror never really builds in a way that feels organic. It suddenly exists upon discovery of a secret room, and then the pay off for that is just... unappealing. This game's realization of the Firewatch 'voice-box-companion' is far inferior, and in the end, the game itself doesn't make the inclusion of the character feel well thought out. The inventory items are largely unnecessary. The motivations are absurd. The red herrings are, at best, dangled over the train before being tossed away.In the end, this is just another game which can't live up to the better games/media that came before it. Stuck in a hotel in the snow? Gee, I wonder which Stanley Kubrick movie that was drawn from. Companion is a walkie talkie? Hmm... What other walking sims have done that? Gameplay padded out to an extreme degree by putting goals as faarrrr apart as they can? You better believe it. The game doesn't respect your time, your effort, or your interest, and it feels only half-realized at best.Credit where it's due: The voice acting shines through in places, but it's obvious that the voice actors were working with a subpar script. "Oh, gosh, I'm legit worried!" into the 'Farting Ghost" being a prime example. It never really improves from that point, either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything else, I need to give a special warning. Above all else, this is a game about Stockholm Syndrome. This mental disorder was named after an infamous incident in Stockholm where the hostages not only began to sympathise with the bank robbers, but one victim actually married one of the robbers. The condition is common in abuse victims, and this game attempts to give you a glimpse of how Stockholm can twist you.In this game, you are Nicole, the daughter of a child predator whose victim (Rachel Foster) committed suicide ten years ago. It ripped your family apart, and now you're forced to return to where it all happened - right before a blizzard leaves you stranded and alone. Your only contact with the outside world is an inexperienced FEMA agent.As the days pass, Nicole begins to learn things about those horrible events that get darker and more twisted with each discovery. As Nicole's world begins to unravel, she starts grasping for anything that can help her keep her sanity. It's up to you to make her final choice.Most of the negative reviews say this game justifies child predation, but it doesn't. You're looking through the eyes of a victim who's been so scarred that she can't handle what she's now learning, and the two endings can only be appreciated if you recognise that this is a game about Stockholm Syndrome and how there are more victims in abuse cases than the one being directly abused. If you can't accept that, you'll hate this game. Otherwise, it's a very well-handled psychological horror that puts you in the mind of a victim reliving her worst nightmare.The game can be a bit slow at times, but it has its moments and even a few decent jumpscares. Its atmosphere is great, and keeps you on edge. While I would have liked a third, more positive ending, it just isn't possible without destroying the whole point of the player experiencing what it's like to have Stockholm Syndrome.All in all, I do recommend this game, but get it on sale since you likely won't have the stomach to replay it. And be warned, this one is NOT for the skittish or those who can't differentiate between having a severe mental illness and willful consent.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's talk about what I liked about this game before I go into a full-on rant about why this game is problematic.The game itself was beautiful to look at and the atmosphere of the hotel left me feeling very tense and uncomfy for most of my play through. I really felt the effect of wandering around a supposedly haunted hotel where a terrible crime was just waiting to be uncovered. As far as suspense went, this game gets a kudos from me; but that's where my compliments end.Moving onto the rant then.I had heard about this game, kinda. Enough that it was on my radar but not enough that I really knew what the story was about. So when it was on sale for less than $2, I went ahead and threw my money at it to finally mark it off my list of 'games I'm curious about but since I'm a frugal b**** I'll never pay full price for it'. I was initially excited to learn about the premise of the story upon playing through the first chapter but then it quickly went downhill from there. I cannot in good conscience as a person who suffers from mental illness and as a mental health care provider  e v e r  recommend this game to anyone. Even if I were only a basic human who has a mediocre grasp on right and wrong I couldn't recommend this.Prepare for spoilers in this next part.The story opens up with Nicole, our main protag, inheriting a hotel from her dead father. We learn that there was a (dark) (family) (secret) that ripped apart not only Nicole's family but the family of a respected local Christian family who ran the church that the hotel is connected to. Nicole comes onto the scene planning to sell the hotel and give the money to "the poor girl's family" (the surviving family members of Rachel Foster) to ease their suffering / pain due to the action's of Nicole's father who I started calling 'Bad Touch Leonard'. We quickly learn that 'Bad Touch Leonard' had an inappropriate relationship with the pastor's daughter, Rachel Foster, and this led to Nicole's mom fleeing from the hotel with Nicole while she was a child.Ok, cool. But then we find out more.The game framed the relationship as 'illicit' and 'inappropriate' but lets call it what it was. 'Bad Touch Leonard' groomed a sixteen-year-old girl into a pedophillic relationship by having speech therapy lessons with Rachel claiming to be treating her dyslexia in the attic of the hotel. Absolutely disgusting. I had hoped that the whole point of the game was for Nicole to find out about Rachel's age, about how her father was a criminal who should have been sent to prison while he was alive. Maybe she would reveal this whole crime and come to terms with having been an innocent party who will forever be associated with what her father did. But no. No no no no no.Turns out everyone knew about it and just saw it as an affair because Rachel "acted years beyond her age" and "dressed like an adult". At one point in the game we have to listen to the gross ramblings of 'Bad Touch Leonard' as he justified his actions saying basically that "no one understood our love" and "our love was pure". I really wanted to puke. BUT THEN we also learn that our companion during the game, Irving, who turns out to be the brother of Rachel, has been holed up underneath the attic of the hotel and has been leading Nicole along to uncover the secrets of what happened in the hotel and let Rachel finally "use her voice". Ok, good. Surely Irving is outraged by all of this? NOPE. At the end of the game we have to listen to the unhinged ravings of Irving who had apparently BEEN WORKING WITH 'Bad Touch Leonard' to reveal the truth about what happened to Rachel. He says things like "she was so pure" and "no one understood their love" except for Irving apparently. And also, we learn that Irving and 'Bad Touch Leonard' knew the whole time about what truly happened to Rachel. They knew the whole time that Rachel did not kill herself but that Nicole's mom had actually used Nicole's hockey stick to kill Rachel and then covered it up to make it look like a suicide. Irving just basically wanted to bring Nicole into this whole mess and have her realize what happened all while cultivating this weird romantic relationship with her.The game begins its climax by basically saying that Nicole and her mother only hated Rachel because they were "jealous" of her and that's why Nicole's mom killed Rachel along with the baby she was carrying. Oh yeah, Rachel was also pregnant but that only seemed to be a tacked on little detail that was supposed to add more tragedy to this whole effed up mess. And during this whole mishandled plot of a game, not once do we ever really hear anyone call out 'Bad Touch Leonard' for his crimes. If anything, Irving speaks of nothing but respect for the man and Nicole only seems to hold resentment for him due to him cheating on his wife. Everything ends with Irving killing himself by freezing in the snowstorm and him beckoning Nicole to follow him so everyone "can be reunited again". The final scene is Nicole sitting in her car which she has rigged tubing and duct tape to so she can redirect exhaust from the car through the window so she can kill herself. She talks about meeting her dead mom, 'Bad Touch Leonard', Rachel, Irving, and their dad in a diner in the afterlife and the player can choose whether or not to go through with the suicide. (By the way, you get an achievement for starting the car then turning it off apparently). TL;DR (I guess): I shouldn't have to explain why this is a completely inappropriate way to handle any of the topics covered in this game but here I am. It is a mishandling of the topics of pedophilia and grooming. It fumbled the topic of suicide. It glorifies underage girls for their "purity" and excuses sexual assault that happens to them because "they were mature beyond their years" and "look like an adult" in their own right. In summary, don't buy this game; even on sale. It is horrid on so many levels.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster (TSoRF, from now on) has left me with a very lasting, yet ambiguous impression. An impression of a game that tried to be way more than it could. Let's be frank, ok? The game looks like an illegitimate child of 'Firewatch' and 'What Remains of Edith Finch', served as a haunted hotel ghost thriller. Calling this a horror would be incorrect in many ways. Well, maybe a Japanese-style horror. A lion's share of spooks come in the form of creaky floorboards, sudden ruckus, ghostly whispers, and general stress from 'being' alone in a giant empty hotel. I won't talk much about the plot. It's weak enough as it is, so if I'll lay it out in front of you, there won't be any good reason for you to play the game. All I can say, it's not believable. The verdict such as this one is bad for the horror game and terrible for a detective story. The dead relative leaving the game's protagonist his estate is one of the oldest cliches in the book. But it still works, so fine. The snowfall trapping you inside with no connection to the outer world, but a strange phone with some clerk-guy on the other side. Now it gets more interesting! But... But! Now it becomes clear how 'B' this game is. Remember how good dialogs were in Firewatch? With charismatic and witty Delilah and multiple unique response choices? In TSoRF we get two-choice dialogs, that have no consequences in the future. They only determine how much of the jackass our heroine is. You can literally reach the dialogue moment, pick one answer, reload, and then pick the other one. You'll see that Irving's (the clerk-guy) lines won't change in most cases. That's an illusion of choice for ya!! And the voice acting is bad, really. It gets better in some game's sections, but generally, it's awkward and bland. The live-action bits weren't good either. And the game also fails to deliver any interesting gameplay features. The power shutdown part was the best one in my opinion. But for the most part of the game, it's phone talks and backtracking all over the hotel. But man, that hotel... The art design is where the game really shines. Every room in this old crumbling mansion-like hotel feels very real, feels lived-in, feels... abandoned. And the absence of a player's marker on the maps helps makes you feel lost, which also adds it's thrill. First, two floors are the most lore-rich. But you'll have to extract this lore yourself. By reading notes, examining paintings, and other objects of interest.  And most of them aren't interactable, which strikes me as an extremely imprudent game design. Yet, you can inspect pretty much every single one toothpaste tube and hair comb you'll wind along the way.  That takes out all the exploratory drive and turns strolling around the hotel into a chore on your way to the mission point. At the end, we get a game with an incoherent and poorly written story, beautiful but blank environments, little to none exploration, and weak spooks. An amateur's work. Racing after the Firewatch, What Remains of Edith Finch and Gone Home's success, The Suicide of Rachel Foster fails to deliver on all fronts. It's not a terrible game by any means. But neither a good one. I honestly regret pre-ordering it and advise you not to buy it at its full price. There are much better adventure games out there, but if you still decide to play TSoRF, then be real and don't get your hopes up.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting walking simulator, but an overall mediocre experience. It reminded me of Firewatch, but felt short on every single aspect, maybe except for the graphics which were very, very good.The sound design and soundtrack are top-notch, with good dialogs and voice acting. The story, which is the main interest for a game like this, manages to stay intriguing till the end, but ultimately feels without a real climax or proper weight. The game touches on some very sensitive matters of life, but does so a bit too light-heartedly that kind of puts off the pace of the story telling.The gameplay is also pretty stale, with the typical wandering around of walking simulators, but with some pretty serious backtracking that feels too boring, especially when you are invested in the story and want to find out the answers to your questions.A great attempt on a walking simulator, but nothing special really. Better handling of the story and (a better finale) would really increase the overall experience.5/10Recommended under heavy discount, and only for walking simulator fans that have nothing better to play. There are many and much better walking simulators out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I tend to like this kind of game (a cross between Gone Home and Firewatch, both of which I loved), I initially didn't pick up this game because of what I saw of the subject matter.  Not so much that the word 'Suicide' was in the title, but that the Store Page talked about an older man having an affair with and impregnating a high school-age child.  Did I really need to immerse myself into that kind of story?  They're either going to hit you over the head with how horrible this guy is, show you all kinds of disturbing stuff, or almost romanticize it and make it seem like it was just "natural."  Either way, it didn't seem like my cup of tea.But when it came out in the Humble Choice, it was easy enough to pick up, and I eventually gave it a shot.  I'm glad I did.  While it falls short of the two games mentioned above, it still had the game elements I was looking for, but without making it unenjoyable due to what I feared I'd see.I loved exploring the Timberline Hotel, in all its decay and 80s look and feel.  (No, not neon lights and acid wash jeans, but it really did look like what such a hotel might have looked like in the 1980s/90s).  I liked some of the spookiness, but it never went over the top and didn't hit you over the head with silly supernaturalism.  What really kept me from enjoying it more-- and putting it on a par with the aforementioned games-- was the voice acting of Irving, the young FEMA agent that the protagonist talks to throughout the game.  Maybe it was just bad dialog-- I'm not sure if Patrick Stewart could have pulled off a good performance.  But I'd just pick the responses that I guessed would result in the least dialog so I could get back to exploring in peace or advancing the story.But all-in-all, it worth picking up in a bundle and spending a few hours with-- or six, if you're like me and like to explore every nook an cranny, pick up and rotate every object, etc.Pros:(+) The Timberline Hotel is wonderful representation of an 80s/90s hotel.(+) Excellent both in graphical quality and sound, contributing to the ambiance.(+) Great detail in the objects you see, many of which you can pick up and rotate.(+) Excellent exploration gameplay.Neutral:(+/-) Interesting enough story.  Some surprises.(+/-) Some supernatural stuff, which I don't always go for.  But it didn't go off the deep end.(+/-) One "puzzle" where I had no idea what to do next, and the map / to-do indicator was disabled.  But I'll blame myself for missing something instead of the game itself.Negative:(-) Script and/or Irving's voice acting.(-) I still don't like checkpoint-based saves.  You can lose 30 minutes of exploration because you didn't trigger the next save.

_childDocuments_.review: I love walking simulators, they are the evolution of story telling. When I entered the Hotel I was curious and eager to spend time here, look into every corner, read every titbit of backstory, open every door, uncover every secret, just have a lovely mysterious time here. But way, way too soon I became clear, that there was not much to look into, the game is sadly short, there were so many corners, but the most of the exciting setting was left unused, it wasn't filled with life by documents, letters and all the other things, that could make the Hotel vessel for joy, live and tragedy; there was nothing, that made me believe in it's ability to awaken deeply buried memories. Doors were only opened (by the game, mostly, not me), when the game needed me to go trough.The whole plot felt forced, unrealistic and more than a bit lazy (they obviously didn't care for their own story enough to decide for a year the whole thing is happening in) and what was probably intended to be an OMG plot twist, was lingering in the air, screaming 'I am going to happen!' on day two already. I stuck along, hoping for more, that I ultimately did not get; then for closure, which I didn't get either, because half the strings were kept unsolved and what became of the other half was just implausible. Too much made no sense. Even if I would buy, that people act, how the game wants me to believe they would (which is a long stretch in the first place), the protagonist's reactions they want me to buy are beyond anything plausible. So I finished it for the achievements, which were, you might have guessed it: cheap and lazy. So, I love walking simulators, they can be the evolution of story telling, if there's a story to be told and pages to be turned. Unfortunately 'The Suicide of Rachel Foster' isn't a story worth telling.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: If you are suffering from suicidal tendencies, don't suffer alone, seek help in a friend or a professional. You're not alone. The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a narrative horror game where you explore a hotel during a major snow storm.Story:You play as Nicole, after her fathers affair with a teenager Rachel Foster becomes the talk of the town, she resents her father and Rachel. After Rachel commits suicide, Nicole and her mother move out and her father becomes a recluse. After Nicole's father passes away, he leaves her the hotel and she has to go back and look through it before selling, but she gets stranded there during a major snow storm and her only companion is Irving, a FEMA agent talking to her through a phone.The story in The Suicide of Rachel Foster is good, but it feels like the writers didn't fully flesh out the story and it leads to some questionable choices. The story of this game is pretty messed up and honestly people who are easily offended might find a lot of the characters irredeemable and absolute trash human beings. The game completely derails in the final hour of the game after the plot twist is explained to you. The plot is actually pretty engaging, it got to the point where I didn't want to stop playing until I saw the credits roll (with the games short length that was easy), but it completely lost me at the ending. I don't want to spoil it, but the game deals with situations like grooming and abuse and makes these characters seem like the good guys, yet in real life they would definitely not be considered that. It definitely makes me feel indifferent and it's can of worms the writers should not have opened and in the end it hurt the story.Graphics:The art style of The Suicide of Rachel Foster is really good and honestly I loved the look of the hotel. Every floor and room looks distinct enough with details thrown around to make exploring a fun thing to do. Since you're alone in the hotel it definitely gives off feelings that you're alone there, yet it also perfectly creates a feeling that you might not be alone. When you can find hidden items thrown around in certain rooms and explore remnants of previous hotel customers, which was really cool.Audio:Since the game is mostly two people talking to each other, so voice acting is incredibly important and the voice actors for both Nicole and Irving do a bang up job, especially Irving who I really liked. They both did a good job and their emotions come off clearly, they did a great job.Another great thing is the ambience sound effects. Since you're trapped in a massive hotel alone during a major snow storm there's a bunch sounds that help build an amazing atmosphere like floors creaking, branches hitting the windows and the wind howling outside, it helps you immerse yourself into this world and definitely makes you feel that you might not be alone there. The music is also really good. The tracks definitely help set up what they set out to do like relax you or scare the ♥♥♥♥ out of you. Gameplay:If I could compare this game to anything, it very closely resembles Firewatch. You basically explore a location and once in a while you talk on your phone with a person that is far away from you. You have some stuff you need to do in the hotel like looking for items and solving puzzles. You are given a map of the hotel and there's a bunch of ground to cover and in the early hours when you have to go through a lot of it, it becomes really difficult to figure out where to go, the map is really confusing and it's better just explore and remember where everything is. By the end, the map became useless as I mostly remembered where to go.The puzzles (if you can call them that) usually tend to be, go to some place and look for an item and then the game repeats multiple times. It actually is puzzle-y to figure out how to get to your objective than the actual puzzles. The gameplay definitely takes a backset to the story.Verdict:The Suicide of Rachel Foster is ok, it definitely doesn't reach it's full potential. The story is engaging, the setting is cool and it's definitely creepy. The whole finale of the game where the big reveals happen are weird to say the least and a lot of the writing is questionable to say the least. It's definitely a game not for everyone, especially for those who don't want a disturbing experience. Final Rating:7/10Pros:+ Engaging story+ The hotel is fun to explore+ Audio design is incredible  Cons:- Act 3 of the story contains some really questionable writing - Navigating the hotel might be confusing in the first hours of the gameIf you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this on Switch first, then bought it on Steam (discounted). So why don't I recommend it if I bought it twice?Story-wise, I enjoyed most of it. The voice acting is great, the atmosphere is great, and for what's essentially a walking simulator, I was intrigued throughout. BUT, two things I really didn't enjoy - first, as you might have seen from other reviews, it covers a very morally wrong topic, yet the story is written as if there's nothing wrong with it. I don't agree with the more extreme opinions on here, but I definitely got the feeling that it's a bit messed up to make a game like that. And secondly, the ending is AWFUL. For a game I largely enjoyed, the ending ruined it by being ridiculous, not making sense (as in, why the hell would they do that), and while there are TECHNICALLY two endings, they're both rubbish. This is the only game to ever leave me feeling like a bad ending ruined a decent game. The fact that I enjoyed the game up until the end is exactly why I (eventually) bought this on Steam.If I left it there, I might have recommended it, just about. But the Steam version is buggy as hell. The game overlapped two sections of audio which made me unable to progress, and in the final chapter I got a nice black screen which sent me back to the start of the chapter (when I was near the end of it).

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a 3 hours long narrative driven walking simulator with great but almost completely linear storytelling and poorly implemented free roam part.The story revolves around Rachel Foster's death that happened 10 years ago and this story is interesting enough to follow. Everything happens in a rather large semi-abandoned hotel in the mountains (like in "The Shining" movie/book).Technical part is very good - visuals, sounds, voiceovers, performance, nice atmosphere. The biggest disappointment of the promised cool things is the exploration of the hotel. There're next to no reasons to explore it besides the planned rail gameplay. Go there, trigger next piece of narrative, repeat. That's how it works. You won't get any valuable pieces of story via exploration and story won't be less linear than it is.You also won't get proper answers on many questions at all - ending seems clunky to me and whole story looks unfinished (not holistic/less valuable/without important explanations) because of it. It's not hard to guess most of those things, but it's not the case here.The Suicide of Rachel Foster leaves mixed feelings. It's a really good walking simulator without a doubt but I believe it could've been filled with more content, gameplay and exploration. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I recently tried playing The Suicide Of Rachel Foster and, frankly, it was a disappointing experience right from the start. After spending about 23 minutes with the game, I found myself completely uninterested and frustrated. Here's why:First off, the game is incredibly slow-paced. Within those 23 minutes, I spent most of my time wandering aimlessly around a dreary, poorly lit hotel with barely any sense of direction or purpose. The gameplay feels clunky, with awkward controls that make even simple tasks feel like a chore.The story, which is supposed to be the game's main draw, doesn't grip you from the get-go. The dialogue is flat, and the voice acting lacks the emotional depth needed to make the narrative compelling. Instead of feeling intrigued or curious about the mystery surrounding Rachel Foster, I was left feeling bored and disconnected.The graphics, while serviceable, aren't anything to write home about. The environments are bland and uninspired, failing to create the eerie atmosphere the game desperately needs. Combined with repetitive and uninspired sound design, the game fails to immerse you in its world.Ultimately, The Suicide Of Rachel Foster does little to draw you in or make you want to continue playing. With so many other engaging and well-crafted games out there, wasting time on this one feels like a mistake. In just 23 minutes, it became clear that this game is not worth the investment.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially a playable mystery novel, kind of like Myst. If you've enjoyed games like What Remains of Edith Finch or Gone Home, you'll probably enjoy this as well.Exploring the hotel is fun and the story is interesting, if short. However, I will say that some of the more sensitive topics this game explores are not handled particularly well. I was able to put that aside and just enjoy the game for what it was but I can see how it might be a deal breaker for some.My main complaint is that your character walks as if trying to go for the record for world's smallest steps. There's a run button but it gets deactivated any time you change directions or brush up against a wall so you end up constantly needing to let go and push it again. Even when it works, it doesn't even speed you up much.Overall, I'd say it's a decent game and worth the price if it's on sale.
