_childDocuments_.review: Now with a heavily story focused game you might think that everything is interconnected and every object, conversation or event has a lot of thought behind it, some do but there's just too much stuff that doesn't make any sense. The timeline is one of the most confusing things in this, some newspaper articles and some dialogues tell us that Rachel died in 1981, while others tell us that she died in 1983. This throws everything off balance and just confuses the hell out of anyone trying to tie pieces together on their own. I have no idea how this happened, since it's clearly not intentional. Minor spoiler!:  Major spoilers!:  Basically, there's too much that's really confusing if you think for yourself and try to figure stuff out on your own. The game will present it's version of the story to you so you might as well don't think at all while playing, just listen to dia- and monologues. The more you think about it the less sense it'll make anyway since it just doesn't match up a lot of times. I am absolutely not a fan of this.The location you're set in is a big hotel with the majority of rooms and objects not being of importance at all. You know that "inspect" feature from other games where you can look at an object (for example a piece of paper) in 3D to look for clues? This game has this too, except that less than 10% of objects you can pick up and inspect are  s o m e w h a t  connected to the story. The other 90%+ are random sponges, pencils, bottles and other irrelevant stuff that you can inspect for some reason.I replayed the game to get the other ending because I wasn't happy with the one I got, while ignoring that both endings are hella stupid and feel heavily out of place, I noticed that the game has zero replay value whatsoever. You don't do a lot except unskippable dialogues and walking, kinda boring if you already know everything. And it's not that choices actually have a big impact.One bug I encountered quite often is that after a cutscene the whole screen will turn olive green, basically a softlock. You'll have to quit and reload. The game only saves at the start of a new day so you can redo the whole day to get to where you were before. This is really annoying since, as I said before, it's really boring if you already know the unskippable conversations and where you need to go. This happened to me at least 4 times in 2 playthroughs (Which is way too often). Oh and while we're talking about the ingame days, I'll have to mention that they're kinda dumb and don't make any sense at all. Day 5 or something only consists of one dream, then the next day will start. Did the protagonist sleep all day or what?? The game starts at the 23rd of December according to several notes but you start celebrating Christmas (I don't remember the exact number of days) at least 6 days later, a bit late, dontcha think? The game also suffers the famous "I didn't think that dialogue option would lead to this outcome" illness many games are seemingly infected with. For example: Pick "I didn't know that" as a dialogue option and your character will go: "HOW SHOULD I HAVE KNOWN THAT YOU MORON, I DON'T WANT TO TALK TO YOU ANYMORE!!". Hate it, if you're not pleased with the outcome be ready to redo a whole ingame day.The graphics and the locations are a big plus, looks really cool. The sounddesign is good and the voice actors are a personal highlight.Some people will tell you that this game is not seriously adressing or even glorifying paedophilia. I don't think that's true. Yeah there's a few characters in here that excuse paedophilia. I repeat again, a few characters in here will excuse it. The game itself isn't excusing it. It's just a sad story where many people clearly need to go see a therapist (or go to jail) and the one who suffered the most is a poor soul who didn't do anything and certainly didn't deserve it.There's so much wasted potential here. The most important aspect of the game, the story, is lacking. There's a lot that doesn't make sense, which is a bummer, the story isn't even that complex so don't ask how this happened. I don't remember how I got this game honestly, I think it was really really cheap when I bought it a few years ago. I don't recommend buying this for the full price of 17€ now.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed The Suicide of Rachel Foster. I bought this with the idea of there being more to be afraid of in a traditional horror game sense but I was not disappointed because what I got instead was a mysterious journey through the main character's relationship with their family members and the telling of how a delicate situation unfolded which I thought the game's story handled well because it wasn't happiness that outlines the situation as a whole. The fear of thinking you might not be the only person that exists in a huge, strange building is met equally with the fear of not being able to reach out for help or escape because you are snowed in. And the long corridors, multi-floors, and dark corners really helped lay out this atmosphere, in conjunction with how the story progresses, that made me feel scared throughout playing.I found myself taking wrong turns most times because of the many doors and many halls that I couldn't remember what exactly to take to get there. And this added to my sense of anxiety and eagerness to get to where I thought I needed to go to see what happens next in the story. It compelled me to keep playing and I really enjoyed the ending. Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure why they made this game. The story is interesting enough but the execution here is awful. I think maybe this would have been an entertaining movie or television series but as a game it is an exercise in tedium. You are forced to play this game the way the developers want you to. That means you have to listen to dialogue that drags on or wander around aimlessly inspecting things that really don't matter before you finally progress. The movement is painfully slow and adds to the frustration. Maybe if you could move quicker it would be bearable but instead you are locked in and forced to experience this their way. In my opinion walking simulators are pretty boring as is but sometimes they can tell a story in a unique way. This one just did not do it for me. Also, the sensitive and potentially triggering subject matter is presented in a very strange way. I am not sure what they were wanting to accomplish here and I don't think anyone should play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an in-between option because recommending the game is difficult. On one side, it's a brilliantly built thriller, it always keeps you on the edge, and with your guard up, without being an actual horror game. The atmosphere is always creepy and weird and it does a good job of making you intrigued to discover the story, even tho all you really do is walk and walk from one part to the other of a hotel that's built like a labyrinth. The story itself is strange, and dark if you couldn't figure that out from the title. To keep the tension up there are always little sounds around you, implying the idea that the hotel is haunted. However, there's never a real visual clue for it, or a true in-your-face scare. There's also that one very polarizing and controversial thing in the game, that I'm not gonna mention since the reviews are already full of it. The finale, without spoiling it, in my opinion, is straight-out stupid and makes very little sense. And then there are the technical issues, which aren't many but are annoying enough. For once, you're kinda forced to use v-sync, not using it will, at least in my case, ripple the image immensely. And then there is the one thing that annoyed me the most, every time there is a small cutscene, there is also a chance that the game image will just bug out, the screen becomes a dark shade of blue and the game completely unplayable anymore. It only happened twice to me, but both times were towards the end of the chapter, which forced me to replay it all. So about 30-40 minutes of my playtime is just me replaying those two chapters, of which one was the very last one. Overall, I can't say I'd really recommend this game, but it's decent enough at being what it wants to be. The atmosphere is great, but the story and bugs pull it down. I'd say it's a little over a 5/10, but just enough that it's not necessarily something I would recommend against playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Boring and slow, an hour in and I have no plans to go back. The only other game like this I've played is Going Home, which provided a slow but steady stream of clues and story elements that built up gradually and I always felt hooked. But with this we get an entitled b*&%# that isn't content to wait out a blizzard in a hotel. It's never even really clear why she even went there, let alone in such dreadful weather. She doesn't have anywhere to be in a hurry. She just doesn't want to be there but she's stuck. It's just dumb to force the player to go through the motions of trying to leave when any idiot would know that's both foolish and impossible.There is a lot of nice attention to detail in the environment, but moving around is so darn slow, even with the 'sprint' button mashed down, that I found myself annoyed by it all the whole time. The voice acting is decent (it's not the actors' faults that the dialog is so absurd). But there is just nothing here to draw me in at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not "romanticize pedophilia" as so many negative critics claim (both on Steam and press) - from where people can draw such conclusions? The whole story focuses on how the affair / actions committed by the father destroyed lives of so many people. Sure, there are backstories depicting the father under a bright light - but none of them were about his affair but about the other things he was as a man: a father and a genius astrowhatever that people were looking up to. One does not prevent the other. Unless you are a basic blue-haired cretin, everybody knows that adultery is "something awful" - no need to state the obvious thousand times.Although clumsy and all over the place at times, I found the writing of this game not cringy as f*ck like most of games dealing with suicide / adultery usually are.  It won't get a Pulitzer either but it did the job pretty well. Also, awesome atmosphere, it felt like walking in The Great Northern Hotel from Twin Peaks!Unexpected game. Warmly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: The level design is great, and exploring this big intricate property and becoming more familiar with its hidden passageways feels great. The controls function well and you move about the hotel at an approriate pace with the run button. The music is great. The voice acting is top notch. The addition of a few (though under-used) item mechanics are a welcome addition to the the walking simulator genre. And the premise of the story is intriguing at first.The Bad: The writing, is so bad. The plot itself is alright and could have been done well, but the dialogue is so bad and constantly present that it overrides anything else. It seems like they were trying mimic the relationship between the two main characters seen in Firewatch, but there's not an ounce of chemistry here. Of all the jokes and quips going back and forth, I think I laughed one time the whole game. Beyond that, the dialogue is super inconsistent- Nicole, the protagonist switches on a dime back and forth between being flirty and friendly, to being totally ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and back again- and not exclusively dictated by your choices, the non-decision lines do this dance as well. When the characters AREN'T talking back and forth, the dialogue is long-winded, uninteresting and unearned, assuming the player will care much more about the characters, who have mostly just been annoying for the whole ride. The dialogue driven story is the core of this game... and when that's so constantly bad- though the voice actors do their damndest to try to breathe life into it- they really can't.Beyond that, the sound design isn't terribly effective- most 'spooky' sound effects don't seems to emanate from any specific location, so it just sounds like someone is playing a 'spooky sounds' CD in the background. And the storytelling through the environment sets up all these ideas... that don't mean anything in the end. I'm assuming they ran out of money to tell the full story they wanted to, and just replaced it with a 'shocking' ending instead, but it doesn't work.tl;dr: If you're looking for a game like this with great dialogue and heartfelt characters, play Firewatch. If you're looking for something like this with a heartfelt memorable story, play What Remains of Edith Finch.This game has all the bones to be a strong and enjoyable experience, the gameplay and level design is tight...but the writing drags the whole experience down till its underwhelming and unearned conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a hard time writing a review for The Suicide of Rachel Foster. On the one hand, I really loved the setting. The hotel just oozes atmosphere. It made me feel like I was exploring the Overlook Hotel from the Shining (albeit a smaller version). I love the Overlook so the first hour playing the game I was quite happy. The game looks great as well and the voice acting is fairly good. But the writing, the dialogue and the story especially just all fell flat for me. Basically you just go from room to room while you are talking on the telephone with a friend. These talks can be interesting, but they are VERY long-winded and repetitive and usually start immediately after ending them, taking away from the feeling of mystery and desolation. It got to the point where I just desperately wanted to continue the story but there was another three minute talk, not really adding anything to the plot. And without going into spoilers, the ending felt quite anticlimactic as well. It's a bit sad because there is so much wasted potential. If they'd just used the environment of the house more (by adding more scary scenes and even some interesting puzzles) and scrapped 33% of the dialogue it would have honestly been a much better game. It doesn't need to be another Layers of Fear or Resident Evil clone, I get that this is a walking simulator but Gone Home proved that you can make a game like that super interesting and captivating. As it stands, the game is hollow and boring and I can only recommend Rachel Foster if you want to check out a walking simulator of the Overlook Hotel. Which isn't a bad thing of course. In that case check it out when it's on sale. Maybe. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished The Suicide of Rachel Foster. The game was short (about 5 hours) and I didn't expect it to be much longer, but I liked it, despite some drawbacks. The hotel with all it's rooms and little details was really well made. It was't too big, but also not too compressed to save unnecessary walking. The hotel was just as big as it had to be and it felt quite realistic and believable from the construction point of view. Unfortunately there were some rooms that couldn't be explored.And this brings me to my first negative point: The game was not only short, it wasted some of it's potential. Many rooms and objects were simply used too little or not at all. They could have made the game much more extensive, concerning the tasks without making anything feel stretched. Some of the ingame-days (I won't tell how many there are ... but it's more than a week) actually have only one task that's done in about 5 to 10 minutes. I would have liked it if the game would have given me more reasons and tasks to explore certain areas of the hotel. Because for me the exploring and discovering things is incredibly fun in games like this.The second negative point: While the graphics are nice, the sound design as well, the barely configurable controls, the non-adjustable field of view and the far too low mouse sensitivity (I had to more than double the mouse speed in the mouse driver to make the game playable) are simply unnoying. There's also some head bobbing that cannot be disabled which might cause motion sickness for some people, especially in combination with the low FoV. These issues should definitely be fixed by the devs. Played from a few meters away with a gamepad on a medium sized TV it certainly works well, but not really with a mouse and keyboard at my desk with a 27" screen right in front of me. Good game, but sometimes uncomfortable to play for me. When there's an option to play with mouse and keyboard it should work without any flaws and that's not the case right now.Finally something positive again: I really liked the story a lot. I don't want to spoil anything here: It all starts quite harmless, but gets quite a bit more dramatic at the end. I also liked the voice acting. To wrap things up: A nice mix of Gone Home and Firewatch with lots of atmosphere, a nice story, great graphics but some technical flaws. If you liked those games, you should definitely take a look at The Suicide of Rachel Foster as well.

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY THIS GAME WITH A HEADSET, YOU WONT REGRET ITI can't even lie the story behind this game is incredible. It keeps you drawn in, the character growth is riveting, and the end twist left my heart twisted in the most emotional way possible. As you explore you can hear the emotion between protagonists growing further and further, and in multiple ways as well. There's a LOT of twists and turns among the story, despite it only taking me about 4 hours to complete. I'd personally recommend this game, and get set for a wild ride!
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: A moving, eerie game that reveals its story over the course of several days. You're stranded in the family hotel you inherited from your estranged father. Your father had an affair with a young student, who subsequently committed suicide. Over the course of your stay, you investigate her death in the dilapidated, creepy environment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: ONLY FOR MATURE GAMERS Subject matter is very triggering.The main character is an adult woman that after both of her parents die inherits their family hotel. She must make a final inspection herself before her lawyers can put it on the market and sell it. While she is doing this she gets caught by a very bad snow storm and is trapped in the hotel with only an old cellular phone to communicate with the outside world.She is in contact with an officer talking her through the difficult days ahead of her as she tries to survive in blizzard conditions in a hotel that has been shut down for years and empty for months. A caretaker- of sorts, had been living on premises and just passed away.As time passes your character begins dealing with memories and her life, both scared by the actions of both her parents. Her father falls for a younger girl (her being 16 makes the scandle even worse.) She is the town's preacher's daughter and a family friend. One year later she is found dead with a suicide note and was discovered to also have been pregnant. You play as the story deepens and more is uncovered.One thing I can say 100% is that the hotel is great! I thought to myself many times: "I could live here. This place kicks ass!!" The floor plan and everything about it is cool. One of the best game "house: locations ever.The voice acting is top notch. Pro quality!Visuals were nice. The story is good but the subject is one that you must take at face value. I don't think the devs were making a statement advocating for anything but saying look how your actions effect your loved ones. The affair is wrong but the results are worse. The game has a few plot twists and also a few puzzles but does not wow you with any of them, they are just their- then they pass.It took me 5 hours with me having to shut the game down and restart from an earlier save point because the game froze 3 times.The best part is the hotel itself. The worse is the hatred reviews, with the game somewhere in between. Get it on sale, wait till it is 10 bucks or less.-MrGrAnD

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool mystery thriller.  Walk through a creepy dilapidated hotel piecing together what when on there since you left and triggering your memories.  No combat.  No death / restart.  It's a first-person adventure game.  Not too difficult.  It is usually reasonably easy to figure out what you need to do.  I only had trouble with one sequence (finding the tinkling noise).  The thriller aspect is well done: mostly through audio, but there's some good visuals too (nothing gory, no jump scares).  I enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Mystery.  Intrigue.  Fart jokes.This game has it all.I was a bit on the fence on this but overall I have to give it a thumbs up.I nearly bounced off it completely as this game really doesn't make a good first initial impression.  Your character that you control comes across as the most deeply unpleasant person, which although realistic, doesn't endear you to the game at all, especially when you're being forced to be so hateful, even if it is for story purposes.  Also the dialogue between the protagonist and the person you talk to over a walkie talkie for most part of the game, at least initially, was really awkward.  The conversations were really cringey and it was really keeping me from being invested.  I noticed this less and less as it went on, a combination of the dialogue getting better and me getting used to it.  But having an editor run his eyes over the script certainly wouldn't have gone amiss.  The actors in fairness, do at least an above average job, given what they had to work with.I also encountered a weird save bug where I lost all my progress when I exited, despite seeing the save sign appear.  Thankfully I hadn't gotten too far, but honestly I recommend just playing the whole thing through all the way in one sitting.  There's only 3-4 hours of gameplay here and that's if you're being a completionist.The saving grace for this game comes in the fact that the story is well told, the twist is well delivered, and, barring the silly and jarring end-game binary choice moment, was believable and had me invested enough to make me want to hang on to figure out exactly what had transpired.  The game also really does nail the atmosphere and creepiness.  There were at least a few moments when I was startled, and it didn't feel cheap either.Where the game could have been better was if there was more to interact with.  You can explore nearly the entire hotel right from the off, and though it's realistically and lovingly and authentically created, it's also kinda empty.  I would appreciated if they'd filled the game with more optional interactables and lore, because as it stands the game is very linear, despite the fact you have full freedom of movement.  You can branch off from the main story all you want but all you'll find are some empty rooms and silence.Certainly not worth full price but worth a punt on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I loved how this game was paced. Usually games like this are very linear, forcing you to do exactly what needs to be done in order to follow the narrative. In Rachel Foster this linearity is interupted by the fact that the entire hotel is open to exploration from the start of the game. I thought that this was really interesting because it allowed me to have control over the flow of the narrative. I spent a lot of time observing the incredible amount of interactive elements within the game: books, magazines, pictures, toys, etc.... which taught me a lot about parts of Nicole and her father's personality that aren't adressed within the dialogue. Then whenever I felt like it I would return to the story and uncover the rest of the truth.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers. I really liked this game and the fact that I played it absolutely blind was a big part of the reason why. _childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5 - AverageIt's hard to rate this game because it's more of an interactive book than a game. The presentation is superb and the voice acting is also good. They recommend headphones and it's awesome if you have them for the atmospheric audio. The whole game takes place in an old hotel that is very detailed and fun to walk through (except for the slow walking speed). My problem with this game is that the story is very linear and there is not much gameplay at all, you just follow the indications, which are sometimes not clear enough. You hit the interactive items and move on to the next part. There was potential for fun gameplay elements with the flashlight and sound detector, but they don't do nothing with them. I'm glad I got it at 90% discount, I could never justify paying full price for this very shallow gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly, extremely bad on multiple levels. I don't understand how it has so many positive reviews. The voice acting is the most redeemable part, everything else is pure hot steaming garbage. The dialogue is clunky and amateurish. The voice actors are what elevate it to listen-able status through convincing emoting and good spin, but this game feels like it was written by a small child. The two characters you're exposed to in the game are prototypically simple in the construction of their personalities, and they consistently change their viewpoints and make decisions for no reason. The main character starts the game trying to leave the hotel as quickly as possible, but for some reason on the 3rd day she just decides to stay through the holidays, and suddenly wants to investigate the hotel rather than abandon it. Nothing happened except that she got stuck in a freezer. Stockholm syndrome?Also, I'm so tired of the "strong female lead is 'mean' that develops into a slightly-sarcastic good person when exposed to a shy man for a while" trope. It's not even a cliche; it's sooo boring. Oh and the story. There is no story. There's no character development. We don't learn anything. The game is bankrupt of meaning. I can only imagine that sunk cost fallacy is what's causing these good reviews to pour in. Nothing changes. There's no twist. It's not even clever enough to make the fact that there's no twist into a twist. This game's story content is bland unflavored mushy oatmeal with sawdust mixed in for texture. This game tries to shame a sad and bereaved mother for lashing out over her husband having an affair with a teenager and I just cannot even unpack that. How is someone expected to react to that sort of thing? Leonard was actually a pedophile! Why is this game defending pedophilia?! What did he do to deserve vindication!? He cheated on his wife with a child! The game and all of the characters in it forgive him for no reason with no development! It's not any more complicated than what's on the box! The game portrays this as the right thing! I literally don't understand!Oh yeah, 100% mouse sensitivity is too low. I'm constantly swinging my arm around trying to look to the left. I guess the developers wanted the game to "feel slow" and decided to remove your elbows to accomplish that.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my review after playing through...Pros:-Love the graphics-Love the hotel atmosphere of being creepy and not alone, but nothing will harm you-Love point and click-Love the narrating actors voices and the aesthetic of the eerie toneCon:-Horrible Pedo glorification -Ending is seemingly suicide inducing as main option, almost pushing player to do it for an achievement-Creeps out via how the story is being portrayed and who the villians were vs who they would be in real life-the lack of roaming in rooms you knew were going to be a new spot to visit next. AKA that screwdriver moment...-Just wish it moved through these sensitive topics with a true horror or thriller motif rather than a warm light on disgusting old men and suicide,Overall:-It had so much potential, but I get why its so cheap to play now. Be warned this is not scary in the sense you want to be scared, but rather at the developers mindset.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely do NOT understand from where people are pulling their reviews of this game, because I wholeheartedly disagree that it romanticizes or normalizes or excuses any of the dark subject matter that is relevant to the story. On the contrary, I think it perfectly shows just how extensive the damage can be when one individual makes a violent, selfish decision. It shows the consequences that others face even after the perpetrator is dead and gone, and the events are seemingly pushed from everyone's minds. I believe these stories are psychologically and socially important to be told, even despite their heavy-on-the-conscience topics. I personally say well done to the devs for the narrative, the gameplay, and the soundtrack and design. The game itself is quite beautiful, the main characters are charming, and the suspense can definitely get tense. Despite there not being any explicit horror, there were some moments that really gave me the heeby-jeebies. The overall emotional and thought-provoking effects were also something I appreciate at the end of a story. Finally, there's no unnecessary ambiguity in my opinion. You don't get every detail outright, but you get plenty enough to feel that the ending is complete.Side note replying again to other critical reviews: there is a VERY clear disclaimer at the beginning of the game that describes the kind of content players will encounter and to not play if you are sensitive to it. It's totally not fair to judge games or developers about dark themes when you've been warned not just once, but every time you load the game.If you're into a story and lore-driven experience with deep and dark psychological themes, and don't mind taking a bit of a backseat drive as far as gameplay, I'd highly recommend TSORF.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Ok.. so let me start off with the fact that motion blur shouldn't exist and it was almost a game destroyer for me with The Suicide of Rachel Foster. Everything, and I mean every single darned thing was blurry in the game and movement was nauseating beyond compare to any game I've played before. However, I was able to turn it off in the engine .ini file, and once I did the game was immensely better. I highly recommend that changing the graphics settings in the .ini file be the first thing you do if you purchase this game.Now, onto the business of the game itself. The story is intriguing - it's your basic family tragedy that you'd moved on from in life, only to be pulled back into it due to recent events. Ending had some twists, and overall it was decent I suppose. The game mechanics could be very clunky to the point where I had to click or use interact buttons multiple times before anything happened. This could be especially frustrating during conversations because I would have selected my answer only to have to wait for the timer to run out anyways.The graphics were nice overall and the sounds of the game were done well, especially with the headphone function.I think if you enjoy walking simulators then The Suicide of Rachel Foster is worth a try. It has some issues for sure, and I'd say I'm on the fence about recommending it, but I don't regret having purchased it (on sale) or having played it so for that it gets my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I love walking simulator type games where there are plenty of hidden secrets to uncover. This game presented itself as one that you would have to pay close attention to all details to unlock the full potential of the story. However, I'm about an hour and a half in and it seems way more like a "guided rails" experience. There's not much extra to find outside of main storyline items. If you make the mistake of picking up or interacting with something before you're ready to move on, you get a hard cut to the next day in the story and you are transported to somewhere entirely different in the hotel.I also found it extremely awkward that you are constantly picking up the radio to dial out to your FEMA agent buddy. Before the conversation is really complete, the protagonist will put the radio down, only to have to pick it up and dial again by interacting with another object seconds later.My other main beef is that the main character is dreadful. It makes the game less than desirable to play listening to her super negative, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ commentary the entire time. Plus, it's obvious they are going for the old "I am woman, hear me roar" schtick. No thanks.Aside from all that, the graphics are pretty and the environment is immersive. The voice actors are talented, although the dialogue seems awkward at times. _childDocuments_.review: In 1983 Nicole Wilson’s life was forever changed when it was uncovered that her dad, Leonard, had an affair with Nicole’s 16 year old classmate Rachel Foster. Not only was there an affair, but Rachel, discovering that she was 9 weeks pregnant, committed suicide, which sent shockwaves through the small community in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. Nicole and her mother, Claire, packed their stuff and vowed to never return. Fast forward 10 years and you, Nicole, are back at the Timberline Hotel, your home for most of your childhood. Your father has passed and has left everything to you. You have decided to do a once over at the hotel and then sell it, but a bizarre snow storm hits just as you arrive, and you find yourself trapped in the hotel, and in the memories of the past, this is how the game, The Suicide of Rachel Foster, begins.I think it’s pretty clear, but this game is going to take place in the hotel. As the game advances more of it will become available, and you are going to find that not everything that happened 10 years ago really happened that way. This game definitely falls into the category of walking simulator, however I really do hate that category because there’s more to this game than simply walking around and opening doors. You’re going to be tasked with uncovering the past, that means you’re going to be finding news articles, items, and more that will help advance the game. I will also admit that there were times where I got lost in the hotel because I decided that I wanted to explore a little more.The game is broken into days, and each day will uncover more of the story. You won’t technically be alone during your time in the hotel. You will have a voice at the other end of a radio phone named Irving. His voice will help you keep your sanity when things get a little too bleak. He’ll also be there to give you hints on what you should try to do next at scripted times during your day.You’re going to be playing this from a first person perspective, and I have to say that the game looks good from that perspective. The hotel definitely shows that it has been around for a while. You can definitely see that the developers made certain areas more “lived in” than others, you can also see that the hotel is in disrepair which fits in nicely with the story. There are tons of rooms, and of course not all of the rooms can be opened, but I was surprised by the amount of the hotel that ends up being open to you throughout the game. You’ll have access, by the end of the game, from the top to the bowels of the hotel.This is definitely not a game for everyone, and it does deal with the serious issue of suicide, which is a topic that many might not want to interact with. This isn’t a high action hack and slash game, so if you’re looking for that type of gameplay, you’re not going to find it here, but if you are looking for a story that has its twists and turns, and some of those twists are pretty big, you’re going to enjoy this game. I know I personally enjoyed the game when the credits rolled at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster isn't a bad game as far as it's actual game-play and it's story was decent, but nothing truly remarkable. It's a nice-to-look-at walking sim with decent exploration and interesting dialogue but was rather easy to get lost (at least it was for me) and at one point, you're almost completely left in the dark. (literally) I also found the ending to be quite depressing and even somewhat pointless. But I suppose that shouldn't be a huge shocker considering the title of the game and the themes the game delves into. Which was actually pretty interesting. Overall, I'd maybe give the game a 6 or 7 out of 10. Decent or maybe average, but nothing amazing. However, if you want an alright story, plot twists, (probably the best part of the narrative) and a game to easily get all of the achievements on, then it's not a bad buy. But after getting all of the achievements, I'm not sure if it's a game I'll ever return to. The original price isn't too much for this game I'd say, but if you can, I'd get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to say for sure if I'd recommend this or not...Pros: The environments are really detailed and interesting to explore, it's a good walking simulator style game if you like that.Cons: It has an odd save system that only saves at the end of chapters so you can potentially lose progress if you return to main menu by accident or reboot the game without having reached a chapter end. It also doesn't give you the achievement for completing the game unless you perform the action they want you to (but I was just curious to see what happens if I didn't and now have to play the entire game again to get the final achievement). I also felt like although it covers topics like child sexual abuse and suicide, it doesn't really acknowledge that these are nuanced and important, it instead seems to use them for more shock/controversy towards the end, but again like many have said, doesn't really acknowledge that grooming a 16 year old was bad. I also didn't particularly like the horror atmosphere considering this game isn't really a horror at all.I think it's worth playing to make up your own opinion about it, it is engaging and tells a story, that for the most part is good, it just seems to unravel towards the end and become something not so great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this for 10$ on Humble, this review will reflect the price value of this game.The voice acting and characters:The laughing and extreme emotions are forced and you can tell, cringy laughing and crying. The whole romance thing with Nicole and Irving seems really offputting and to soon, sometimes just outright creepy. You've been there 3 days and already into pet names. Cringe factor 100Atmosphere:The atmosphere is great and if this was an actual horror game I'd of probably ♥♥♥♥ myself a few times. The background noises of creaks and knocks at times is so unsettling. 10/10 on creepy atmosphereStory:Too much and too little. There is a lot of story but its needless information between the 2 living persons like flirting. Often times I found myself at the next objective and spinning in a circle waiting for the story to catch up to me so I could progress. Sometimes I'd be stuck in a 10 minute conversation already ready to get on with the next chapter sighing wondering when Irving would just shutup already. GraphicsWHY is my framerate at 23fps but the game set to Ultra???!!!??? I saw it drop to 13fps sometimes, did you not know how to make framerates? Yeah ooh pretty scenery but my god the framerates suck.Controls:Using a gamepad makes the turning painfully slow, if there was an enemy I'd of died a bajillion times to him because I couldn't turn quick enough to see what was hitting me. One of the achievo's didn't pop even though I did all I was supposed to do to pop it. It feels like a first attempt at a story driven action game after playing Finch and the creator got inspired. I hope this was a test and you[developer] will come back with a more polished presence and wow us with a better game in the future. For 10$ I feel this isn't worth it. Maybe 5$. There is no replay value except maybe going back to see if that achievo is forever locked. The outcome doesn't change per your choices on answers nor is there an alternate ending/ second ending. I took my time and got lost for a good half hour and beat the game in 3 and a half hours. I vote no on this for 10$, 5$ and its worth a grab. Though great ambiance and atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I think its interesting how certain games are trying to seperate from the standard fun gameplay to dive into more difficult subjects. Only a few games have done this, and I think more should because there's a great potential to use the videogame media to discuss and process unpleasant things that usually aren't talked about. Movies do it all the time, so why not games? And the way Rachel Foster approaches its themes, through a wonderfully dynamic dialogue that deals with rough emotions with finesse, is superb! Thanks One O One for developing.

_childDocuments_.review: The ending ruined my satisfaction with the game mainly because decisions of characters and what exactly has happened in the very end feels out of place compared to the rest of the game. 90% of it was fine but not the end. _childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed the simple, straightforward gameplay and the world that you spend your time in with your main character, but on the last chapter/night of the timeline, I started to lose interest in what was happening or going to happen with the story itself. While this game did a fantastic job of giving me the heebie-jeebies, I feel like the developers were trying to tell an emotional story that really puts the player in their feelings about the sensitive topics that this game centers on and they just..kinda missed the mark. The character development and story building just became a kind of jumbled mess that didn't make sense for the ending and it left myself feeling unsettled and disappointed, rather than the feelings of empathy and sadness that I was expecting to experience. Overall, I do not recommend if you're looking for a deep in your emotions, nitty gritty, type of game, but I did enjoy the 4 hours of gameplay it gave me to keep me distracted from the woes of IRL. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I am by no means a pro game player but for a mystery/thriller with a dark twist...it is one heck of a game, especially for the price (I payed $1.75). The game provides feeling, texture and empathy: in a dark way. (SPOILER ALERT)  You have to understand that with the plot of the game..it is not trying to "make" the audience feel bad for the father, it is showing how the specific character seen it. It does not mean the game is glorifying pedophilia and provided the DISCLAIMER below the title, you can test the game to your own theory. That being said, this is one of those games that you will probably only play once but remember for awhile, shake you a little bit, get you tense and your heart racing. Another spoiler alert, it only has one jump scare close to the ending. If you have familiar feelings with whats going on with the characters at the end, it could very well make you tear up a bit. This was my experience and for me, I was very pleased with the game. I think the ending was good and made sense.. some will say it was rushed. It's up to you to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, this is more of a neutral-to-negative review than just outright negative.I'm a big fan of games as a storytelling medium, and The Suicide of Rachel Foster does tell a story. Really well in the first half, but the later part of the game becomes a bit of a discombobulated mess. There's at least one huge loose end left dangling, and while the 'big twist' doesn't feel like it comes totally out of nowhere, the actual ending feels forced, abrupt and cheapens the rest of the story somewhat.Which is not to say it's all bad, what this game does really well is atmosphere. The abandoned hotel creaks, groans and makes all manner of creepy noises as you explore. The setting is legitimately creepy, especially if you happen to be doing your play through in a cabin in the woods as I was! There was a time or two I had to pop my headphones off to make sure the weird noise wasn't actually in the room with me. Strong Twin Peaks and The Shining Vibes.Overall, 5/10. Great setting let down by a story that starts out strong and goes off the rails. I didn't hate the 4 hours I spent playing the Suicide of Rachel Foster, but I'm not going to be doing it again. Grab it on sale for a few bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: No one should buy this game full-priced. I am sure I got it for under 5 euros. As much as I liked the game, 17 euros isn't justified. On sale, I do recommend it. Put it on your wishlist and wait.The achievements aren't hard to get. I remember I had to play it twice because of a phone interaction in a bathroom; you didn't have to be storywise. Suppose you want to avoid that, I would suggest looking at the achievements beforehand to be aware of them. There is no replay value. When I had to replay it, I muted the game and skipped through everything while watching a video. It would be incredibly boring without it. This game is only a one-time thing. The environment is enormous (which makes it hard to get around and tedious), and the graphics and sounds are fantastic. It got a suitable atmosphere for the story. It is spooky, and I got a bit jumpy here and there. The game just pressures you into expecting something to jump at you but doesn't act on it. For most of the game, you walk around and listen to the story. The camera flash was the most intense moment I remember.The best thing about the game is the soundtrack.Dream On (ft. Nadia Straccia) by Federico Landini is a terrific song. I do listen to this song long after having finished this game. I do not understand how this isn't more famous. The rest of the soundtrack without vocals is fantastic too. Federico Landini is an outstanding Composer who carried this game's atmosphere on his shoulders. Usually, I'm not too fond of the background soundtrack, but this one impressed me.

_childDocuments_.review: Firewatch is rolling in its grave. These writers played it once and said "I can do that" and then took a sweaty ♥♥♥♥ into their design team's open mouths. Spoiler-free review.Graphics are amazing, save for some bugs with lighting which really ought to be fixed (lights reflect even when turned off, etc.) The environmental design is also really quite well done - the hotel is really interesting to explore until you realize there's no danger or interesting stuff to find. Animations leave something to be desired, however - there are too many for small actions like walking through short doorways, and unlocking doors, but that's partially a personal preference regarding what I wish this had been.The gameplay really falls short of the graphical work. It's boring and walky, and there's very little to do except go to place, use thing - over and over and over again. You can pick up and look at things, but there's no puzzle solving unless you count solving maybe two or three riddles that you can reach the solution of before the voice line is finished. Overall, the gameplay was not worth the story, which we'll get to.Not much to discuss here. Some creepy noises that weren't effective since the game has no tension, and the voice acting was cringy at best. There are a few jumpscares in there where they boost the volume, so if you play despite reading this, keep an eye out for those.Here's the big one. The story is capital A Awful. It's inconsistent, predictable, and, like other aspects of the game, really uninteresting once you realize where it's going. The characters - especially the main character - are completely unlikable and grating to listen to. Moments intended to be tense or scary are easy to laugh at since nothing ends up being important, given the absurdity and unintentional comedy of the ending.EDIT ADDED: I completely forgot to specify that the game romanticizes pedophilia. So that's fun.All in all, the game looks great, but starts like a house propped up by a single poorly-made stilt; the writing brings everything crashing down as soon as the main character opens her mouth. The intrigue melts away to reveal a dull, uninspired narrative about a serious topic handled about as delicately as an anvil. Not a good game, unless you have money to burn and want to spend three hours high with your friends laughing at a hotel packed full of bad ideas.

It's messed up. I was actually invested in the story for more than half of the game but then it got bloody weird. No replay value to this game. Not a very good story. Neither ending made any sense and came out of left field. I feel like it did have potential, and if they changed everything after day 8, I probably would have in joyed it, because up to that point I was completely invested in the story. All in all, I cannot believe I actually finished this game, I should have never even started it.

This was painfully apparent by the TV, called something like "only link to the outside world" on it's label that the character did not interact with. So, you're free to wander around, but it's meaningless until Irving tells you to go there. The story was blotchy, days would randomly end and the dialogue options barely made sense. The character you play clearly has a chip on her shoulder but at some point its irritating to try and steer someone actively refusing to participate in the story. Everything about this could have been great if you were allowed to explore and discover things on your own. It also would have lasted longer. Maybe if you could play the lawyer or someone who had any actual desire to do anything. I mean, I found evidence of a seance in a bathroom and nothing could be interacted with except clicking on the moldy walls to whine to Irving. Twice. Then answer a phone, whine to Irving, and then the day ended out of nowhere.

I cannot overstate that this is not a game for people with taste, expectations, an appreciation for the genre.  It is very clumsy in execution. It gives food for thought.  I like that.  Good voice acting too. Game play wise there is not much to do. It is more an interactive story then a game. I did not know what to do from time to time, because I totally forgot to check the map, or simply did not pay attention (real life distractions while playing) .  The result of that was me wandering around from time to time until something happened that put me on the right track again.  A journal would have been nice. _childDocuments_.review: Although the setting is a classic for those who enjoy a spooky environment, and it looks alright depending on hardware and settings. I cannot recomend this because the 'plot' of the game is just not very good or engaging. Spoilers ahead, will try keep them minimal to get the point across. It's about the death of a young girl who went to the same school as the protaganist.... and the creepy love her father and everyone else seemed to have for a pregnant 16 year old classmate of hers. It tells one side of the coin without giving much insight into the world of anyone else including the protaganist's life after she had left the hotel.Plot dumps occur often to tell whole chunks of story instead of pacing it out, and sometimes it can be a chore to sit through.The lengths of the days are quite different and the autosave function only works at the end of the day, so don't think you can try this in your break or anything or you may just have to abandon your progress halfway through a long day. There is no manual save feature.The ending is the worst of all, even if you choose to sit there and do nothing the vengefull ghost does you in. Also ghost stuff was slighlty hinted at before, but the end day of slaming doors and possession just made it all very unbelievable.TLDR It's a good way to get frustrated at a depressing for no reason plot.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a walking simulator that tells a decent enough story. It took me about 2.5hrs to complete the game. The rest of my playtime is from letting the game idle while I did house chores and replaying one time to get all achievements. This game is all about the story. Unfortunately, you are given times where you can choose 2 different commentaries... neither affect the game. However, I liked the mystery and misdirection. If I had to compare this to other titles I'd say it's closest to Firewatch, but much quicker to complete, less exploration rewards and a much simpler storyline. At full price this game does not compel me to recommend it. However, I am leaving a thumbs up as this is a good game. Now, on to more about the game, that lends itself to spoiler type commentary, but I will not spoil the game. Just beware!The pace at which you walk is slow, but running feels like a normal pace in most other games. That's the rub though as you'll want to run everywhere, but the dialog takes so much time that you could have just walked to each place as you'll find yourself listening to conversations while you wait the chance to do the next objective (one that you arrived at 5 minutes prior). It would have been nice to see the hotel expand to more room or slower door opening animations or something to keep the tension building. Maybe even removing running would have helped pace the game better. Constantly you're getting ghost vibes or jump scare vibes. Sadly the game never does that. It tells you there's ghosts and other people get freaked at the ghosts and you're basically told you'll see a living, breathing ghosts to no avail. Something to really entice or wet that appetite would have been nice. Maybe let the player see something or have a draft pull a door shut out of the blue. Everyone tells you the dead girl is still alive. Make her live!Dialing into your phone every phreakin (old hacker pun) time is kind of annoying. It's bad enough you have long, unskippable dialogue sessions. Should I also have to endure the wait time to hang up the phone only to call right back with no reason to put it down? Length of playtime could have been extended by adding rooms or events or even more tasks as the game was very straightforward in its approach. I'd have liked to spent more time in this world. I'd have liked my choices to elicit at the minimum an initially different comment by the narrator. I'd like to have more to do with the tools given me. I'd like to find secrets and be rewarded with extra dialogue or achievements. I wish I could find out more about my Dad. This should have easily been a 6hr game! I applaud the Developer for what they created and I wish they had more in them to do more. I can't wait to see what else you have in store!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very easy to play. No difficult mechanics, or puzzles. They're bland if they lay all of the answers out in front of you, but others may find this a positive, as it was very easy to play.The story itself was intriguing, with all of the elements of a murder/mystery novel. A family's fall from grace, scorned lovers, and a mysterious suicide. I found myself intrigued and playing along just to find out the truth. I would recommend this game for the story, as well as it's easy playability, as long as you're not someone looking for a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a narrative game along the lines of Gone Home, Edith Finch, Firewatch etc. The protagonist, Nicole, is returning to her family’s hotel after she has inherited it from her father. The family has a dark past and was split apart after her father had an affair with a 16-year old who later killed herself while pregnant with his child. Nicole’s intention is to check the hotel out and prepare it for sale, but she gets trapped by a storm and ends up spending a few days in the hotel, learning more about her past and uncovering some dark secrets.Note: While I have 5+ hours of playtime on my account, a lot of that was just spent idle while I was doing something else. The game is actually 2.5-3 hours long.While I don’t think that The Suicide of Rachel Foster is quite as good as something like Gone Home or What Remains of Edith Finch, I did find it compelling enough to push through its shortcomings and overall, I enjoyed my time with the game. With interesting characters, an intriguing story and great sound design, this game is well worth several hours of your time; though it's not without issues. I'd recommend getting it on sale.If you found this review helpful, please consider following my curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: It’s basically Gone Home meets The Shining.Ok, let me be a bit more verbose. Still, that single sentence pretty much sums up the game in terms of what you experience. In a similar vein to Gone Home, The Suicide of Rachel Foster is about a young woman, Nicole, returning to her abandoned home and exploring it. Only this time, it’s a hotel way up in the mountains that gets cut off from the rest of the world by a snowstorm. That, as well as its possibly haunted nature give rise to my comparison to the Shining.Mechanically it too is a walking simulator. There are certain objects you can pick up that you can use elsewhere, but I’d hardly call any of these instances “puzzles”. It’s a fairly rigidly directed experience, given that in this game you have another character called Irving to talk to who gives you clues as well as telling you how to solve some of the problems that crop up in the hotel. And similar to Gone Home, The Suicide of Rachel Foster features a bewildering number of objects you can pick up and inspect that serve no purpose whatsoever. Is this a stipulation in your 3D and texture artists contracts, that they get to design a guaranteed number of objects and that players get to inspect in great detail?Anyway, as you might have guessed from the title of the game, the story centers around the death of a girl called Rachel Foster. The reason Nicole returns to the hotel is because both her parents have passed away and she inherited it. She used to live there when she was younger, but her father’s romantic engagement to a then 16-year-old Rachel, whom he tutored, caused her mother to file for divorce and she and Nicole ended up moving away. The aim of the story is to uncover the events that eventually led to Rachel’s demise. Now I’ve read some criticism that the game portrays the relationship between Nicole’s father and Rachel in a way that seems to condone ephebophilia. I personally can’t really come to the same conclusion. Sure, the game doesn’t seem to dwell on it and whenever Nicole discusses her father with Irving, the fact that this was a relationship between an adult and a minor is not often brought up. But honestly, that’s how you talk about family. I doubt every family member of a murderer constantly discusses their crimes whenever the topic of the convict is brought up. So no, I don’t believe that just because the characters don’t end every interaction with “Furthermore, I consider that Carthage must be destroyed” does it logically follow that either the game or its creators condone grooming of minors. I think mature media deserves the benefit of the doubt that it can present you with challenging subject matter without spelling out what you’re supposed to feel at every step. That’s not to say that the game does this subject, or even the secondary theme of suicide any justices. Because once the twists of the game are revealed, the presence of Irving and his actions become less believable by the minute. Given that the game deals with these fairly heavy topics, I feel that the indications that the hotel might be haunted are a bit off message. As with the Shining, it’s never made clear what actually happens there and if all you get to see is real, the lines are purposely blurry. But the narrative of this game isn’t enhanced by this, and it actively detracts from the real human drama.Ultimately, I found the experience average at best. It suffers from the typical problems of walking simulators in that there’s no gameplay there to enhance the story. And the story, while intriguing at first, is also completely unfocused and seems to be more interested in setting up a mystery and its subsequent plot twist at the end, rather than exploring the heavy topics it decided to tackle with any grace or intelligence. They seem included more for the shock value than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: A haunting and deeply disturbing story told by slow and careful exploration of a beautiful locale. Over time you really get to know the place, with all its little nooks and crannies. The sense of presence is outstanding. The atmosphere is pretty much perfect. I have never played a game that calibrates detail and the sum of all details so well, so much so that I dare call it a masterpiece in this respect.I would classify it as "psychoanalytical horror". There are no unfair jump scares, but your heart will definitely be racing at certain points in the game. It's creepy more than scary, but ... very creepy indeed.You'll notice a lot of negative reviews here focusing on a "bad story". I'm here to provide an opposite opinion. I found the subtlety and moral ambiguity progress cleverly and well. Nobody comes out a hero. Everyone comes out deeply flawed, deeply damaged, and deeply damaging to each other. The more I think about the story—and it definitely stays with you long after you play—the more I realize the horrors of what was left unstated in the game.I will readily agree that this is not for everyone. If you're looking for satisfying closure, you won't get that here. So, yes, read the negative reviews and take them into consideration. But I hope my different point of view will encourage some curiosity. For those of us who appreciate being disturbed, this game is literally breathtaking.Some negatives: performance is, indeed, miserable. So, go for "low" graphics settings if you must. I didn't feel like it detracted anything. Also, you absolutely want to enable vsync to avoid screen tearing. Unfortunately, for me vsync got turned off every time I reloaded the game. So just make sure vsync is on every time you start playing.Also, in spite of all the attention to detail, I felt it was too bad that the world was not more interactive. All you can do is pick up very specific things up and look at them and there was rarely anything interesting to learn from doing that. In short, the gameplay does not match the ambitions of the storytelling.Another negative: if you've ever played , it's hard not to notice the conceptual and thematic similarities. I think this game stands strongly enough on its own, but ... this kind of "borrowing" makes me uncomfortable. Is it really so hard to come up with truly original ideas? This game dances on the line between homage and rip-off.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have much kind to say about this game.The game is at least pretty detailed, and the production value of the game is high. Clearly someone cared about this game.But the overall experience I did not find palatable. I played this on recommendation of a friend who had mixed feelings and wanted to try to get some perspective on it.The first thing I found to be poor was how the game communicates objectives to you. The game is divided up into days, and on each "day" there is a certain number of objectives you need in order to advance the story and finish the day. The game rarely tells you what these are. Several times you miss an important item or point of interest and just walk right by, and the games makes no effort to bring you back on course. The very first day, there is a phone you must pick up. This is not super spoilery, it's at the beginning of the game. But I wasted so much time wandering around waiting for something to happen on multiple different days like this. The phone could ring, or it could fall over, or it could just be placed next to the keys and then included in the same sequence as picking the key up since you're  to be looking for the keys already. Later in the game there is a day with all of the items you're supposed to be interacting with all together. But because I didn't do exactly what I was supposed to and thought this part was over, I was able to just leave and wander the hotel for and hour before giving up and quitting. Just, why do you let people do this?You do get a map at some point in the game, and although for basically 90% of my first playthrough I did not know this, sometimes the map has a note on it with an objective labeled "TO DO." Even this sometimes during the game though is just blank with no helpful info. It's just such a messy, unguided experience that the constant waiting and confusion really drains the narrative of any power it would have had since you spend so much time annoyed, and then are kinda trying to rush the dialog to make up for lost time.The game also only saves after you complete whole days. This was way more annoying than you might expect for 2 reasons. First, when I got lost or didn't understand what I was supposed to be doing on a day and I quit to come back to the next day, it was disorienting because if I managed to trigger one of the little objectives for a day and came back they were all done when I thought they were. But also because, and this will segway into the next issue I had with the game, bugs caused me to have to replay levels multiple times and lose all progress.I encountered a few bugs during the game and some of them were not trivial and inexcusable. Any time I left the game and loaded it again, it would disable v-sync and I had horrible screen tearing without it. Which items I could interact with or take seemed to be inconsistent from playthrough to playthough. But by far my least favorite bug is the black screen bug. Sometimes in my game, after an in-game sequence that triggers when you do something and the camera shifts away from first person for a moment, the screen would go black and stay that way until you quit and reloaded. And every time this happened, I'd lose all progress for that whole day. You know what day this bug happened on every single time I played through? The last day. The last day has a ton of exposition but I ;grew to hate having to go through it over and over again just to see if this time the view would reset properly and allow me to continue. And let me tell you, again, when you are impatient and annoyed, you are not taking the story at face value anymore, you're not immersed.You could also get dialogs that were out of sequence and didn't make sense. On some days if you wander around you can get bonus dialog not related to the objective. And on subsequent days, you could trigger more conversation about that specific thing. Except later days would allow you to activate these dialogs even if you hadn't triggered the preceding dialogs, so the characters will just start talking about something you've never heard them mention before and can't understand. It's weird.The characters I found to be kind of grating. Nicole is a type of kind of trophy lead female character type who is clever, quick-witted, capable, and is originally abrasively sarcastic but can show a softer side once she warms up to you. It's fine, but I mean it's formulaic. Irving is the person who kind of uses a stumbling overly apologetic act to give the voice actor something to chew on and kind of make that his character. The voice acting quality was fine (except for a weird amount of audio in the car that has reverb artificially added even though car cabins are know for being insulated and quiet?) but something about how overwrought these archetypes are and how they're presented in this game made me very intolerant to them here.Without going into spoilers, the game in the opening scenes seemed really cool and stylized, with the letters and the umbrellas, but after you get into the game it becomes a bog standard first-person walking simulation type game. I think the game had potential, but after a really striking beginning just rests on familiar tropes for the rest of its runtime. It has serious technical flaws that will lose you progress and that detract from the immersion and storytelling from having to restart days over and over to complete.Story review:

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains spoilers.The exploration elements are fun though I don't know why they made it possible to pick up so many useless objects. I am used to combing each and every room in discovery style games like this, but they make every bar of soap and comb actionable and it's maddening. This means I missed things like the Christmas tree (tied to an achievement) because I got sick of clicking on every single thing only for the majority of them to be not at all relevant.The game does a good job of maintaining a spooky atmosphere. The sounds are quite good and even straight up jump scared me at one point. The setting is by nature creepy and they really lean into The Shining elements, including an axe missing from the tool board in one of the weird hidden rooms. The story. Well, it has its good and bad points. Irving was suspicious from the very beginning, but that's sort of subjective. Some people may not notice until later which would probably make the reveal more of a gut punch. But as soon as you start the game you are prompted to pick up a "strange telephone" and there's this supposed FEMA agent magically on the other side. Who put the phone there? And more importantly, who put the phone specifically in Nicole's childhood room? There's other signs as well where his real personality seeps through in subtle gaslighting and derision. Still, I found the mystery of who he really was interesting nonetheless.However, one of the problems with the narrative is that the other characters aren't well developed enough. You learn the most about Leonard, but one or two references to the Reverend (Rachel's father) being overbearing and abusive isn't really enough to support the rest of the story. For me to buy that Irving felt what was clearly abuse between Leonard and Rachel was actually a true love connection, I think I needed the contrast of the Reverend being so monstrous that Irving perceived Leonard as sincere and a step up from his own dad. I also wanted a radio response when Irving was giving his true love speech that was along the lines of Nicole telling him that no, it was an adult man abusing a child. I don't mind these darker themes, but Nicole seemed like the sort of person who would have called that out. I also kept waiting for the reveal that Leonard was also abusing Nicole. It wasn't needed, perhaps, but she seemed so against him and so needy for his love that I felt perhaps she had also been directly exploited by him. It would have perhaps added some complexity for her to tell Irving that actually Leonard was abusive to her also. In that vein, I would have liked to know more about Claire. Why she felt that a child impregnated by a grown man needed to die, instead of the grown man who was clearly raping a literal child that he groomed. A child who was the same age as his own daughter. Some other thoughts: I like Nicole and Irving's relationship. I wish she could talk him out of walking into the snow at the end. I didn't understand why she felt she needed to kill herself at the end but I guess it was the trauma of realizing her mother was a murderer (though I had her abort her attempt). It would have been cool to have some sighting of Rachel's ghost at the very end because while Irving engineered a lot of the events that seem ghostly, there were one or two he couldn't have been responsible for. So much is built up around other people having glimpsed her that I wanted to see it too. It's worth playing so I will recommend it but be aware of the way the themes are handled.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a decent story with decent graphics and decent voice acting. Overall it's decent. I wouldn't pay full price for it, but if you can find it for $5 or so and are interested in these kind of games, maybe it's worth it.The story itself is interesting and touches on subjects that are very taboo. I believe the developers handled it well at telling it, and the truth with what happened to Rachel is a nice little twist. I have two main issues with the game: the gameplay and the "horror" / supernatural element. First, the game play. Granted, these kind of games aren't known for their gameplay. But what little gameplay this has feels tacked on. There are certain items that you get in the game that you can equip, but after using them once for their seemingly one purpose, they just kind of get ignored for the rest of the game. There were also parts of the story that just felt contrived and artificially drawn out. For example, there's a section of the story where you're in the electrical unit in the garage. You see a screwdriver that you can't pick up but can "view". Immediately after this section a new day starts, and the game resets to one of the floors. You then have to go to a particular room which is screwed shut. It turns out that you need that screwdriver, and you have to walk back down to the garage and then walk back to the room. Just seemed unnecessary, and I feel like there could have been a better way to accomplish that.Additionally, there's so many rooms in the hotel where the game takes places that aren't even utilized within the story, which is a shame.Secondly, the horror aspect of the game. This isn't really a horror game, but toward the end it seems like they tried to incorporate horror and supernatural elements. For example, it's heavily suggested that Rachels ghost wanders around, and they explicitly reveal that with chalkboard writing at the end and doors shutting closed. I dunno, I love horror games, but it seemed really out of place - I would have preferred just finding out what the story was, and tied in the fact that Leonard, in his grief, went a bit mad, wrote in his notebook about seeing her, created a shrine, etc, rather than making it literal. It all just seemed really cheap.Overall, it's a decent game. I got it via Humble Choice, and quite frankly I'm glad for that. It was an interesting experience, but  wouldn't recommend it at full price (or even at half price).

The whole story was tragic, a family full of secrets, and the game is about navigating the mystery, both literally and figuratively. Helpful?  Yes  No  FunnyCaptain_Redbeard4.2 hrsPOSTED: 25 APRILFirst thing is first. Pedophilia is not something to romanticize, no matter the story behind it. It doesn't matter if it's true, pure love. It's still pedophilia and it is wrong. I spent 4.2 hours playing this game, exploring around and getting lost in the Timberline, and the atmosphere that the devs created in this game is exactly the kind of thing I want from a horror game.The story was pretty mediocre once you got past a certain point, but it was still alright (minus the romanticizing pedophilia thing).I do wish that there was more to interact with, and that there was more to do with each of the items you find. _childDocuments_.review: I don't feel like writing a proper review for this, so I'm just gonna drop a few bullet points off the top of my head.First off, on the technical side : the only graphic options you can change are the resolution, whether to turn VSync on or off (don't bother, it's bugged, it will never let you turn it on), and the graphics quality, ranging from Low to Epic. There's no in-game option to turn off the chromatic aberration, for example, absolutely amazing. Can't rebind your keys as well, so if you're a European AZERTY user like myself for instance, you're just gonna have to ctrl+shift every time you launch or alt-tab off the game, or resort to playing with a controller. And for the cherry on top : it's not optimized properly.As for the game itself, it never really makes a good use out of any of its interesting mechanics. You mostly use firewatch-style radio to get long and winding exposition on Nicole's family and Rachel, or to end the chapter, or at least that was my impression of it. The polaroid is an excellent idea on paper : you could potentially fear the next flash of bright light as it could reveal something that you don't want to see, but you do need it to make out your surroundings and see where you're going. The photographs that come out could've also given it another layer, with you unintentionally getting pics of creepy stuff invisible to the naked eye, or that which you only caught a glimpse of. It does none of those things. You use it for a ten minutes sequence on a clinical-looking section of the hotel with barely anything to catch your eye, and then you get a flashlight, effectively making the polaroid useless. You also get a directional microphone to play with, but again, it's too short lived; I would've expected a few audio easter eggs or uses outside of the mission parameters.The hotel itself is cool, but it reminded me of LA Noire in that the developers of the latter painstakingly recreated a huge portion of Los Angeles in the early 1950s only to hide one type of collectible across the entire area and making no other use of it. You never see more than a half of the map because you have no reason to go there. Same thing in Rachel Foster. The hotel is huge compared to the house in Edith Finch, but the same is so underutilized that I don't really have any reason to explore other than to go 'ooo pretty', something that I can get out of plenty of other games that do it better; so what's the point, exactly ?Spoilers from here on out. In summary, it's not very good either. Get another walking sim.The story and the characters were the most obnoxious things of the bunch. The game makes a point of characterizing Nicole, the protag, as a 2cool4school no-BS tough woman in the beginning, but comes across as just an unlikeable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in all her interactions. By the time she does a complete 180 from one conversation to the next with Irving, the damage is done. Speaking of Irving, I felt like his character progression was messed up. He went from obvious virgin and bumbling idiot to confident and joking to complete sociopath living in the attic (wow, the more I write about this game, the more I realize how much they just lifted from Firewatch) to melancholic and prone to blissful hallucinations. Over the course of 9 days ? Maybe. 4 hours ? Yeah, no. Maybe they talked some more offscreen, but I don't buy that.By the way, ♥♥♥♥ the ending.
