_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this if you actually want a interesting story and not just eye roll the whole time. Recommend watching Youtubers playing it instead as the game play is nothing to write home to as it IS a walking simulator and just a method of spoon feeding you the story. The story isn't great so just save your time and just hit up Youtube for more on it so you don't have to read spoilers. If you're a content creator who just wants to play a game with controversial subjects, then I say go for it. Just know what you're paying into. Spoiler Review:I love that the messaging is that your mom was awful because she was not okay with her husband wanting to groom a child. But the game also says its okay because the husband/the Main Characters Father, did it all in the name of love.Instead of BOTH mad mad at the father for basically ruining his family and the mother for taking it out on a child, the main character instead sympathizes with her father and looks down on her mother in the end. It takes on this very unnuanced point of view, black and white perspective, that the Dad was GOOD, and Mom is Evil. I think the writers believe they're smarter than that they are and believed they probably wrote something that was nuanced however just straight up was not. It's very much easy to tell what the story wants the viewer to believe and see.Never mind the ending before it was patched in, you were going to commit suicide regardless until they allowed the player to opt out of it. However, that just means the true ending, everyone just dies?This isn't some profound story. It just romanticizes a pedophile who groomed a child who was lonely as well as vulnerable. Its worrying that the writers wrote this in such a way to have a "clear" villain, the Mother, and a "clear" good guy, the Father. Typing this review up while the whole Rick and Morty situation is also kind of funny, just not "haha" funny. This kind of subject could land better if the story was written as the horror itself. While reading the internal dialogue and hearing her father speak about a child in such a fashion really gave me unsettling vibes that if it was just leaned into, would really make the game into a better end result than it is now. Like Lolita, it is not a love story. Lolita is social parody and some argue to be in the scope of horror due to it's subject and actions. I believe The Suicide of Rachel Foster could be in the same genre however either the writing from the dev's didn't land or they just tried to make a pedo into a sympathetic character for us to feel sorry for? Maybe the writers misunderstood what Lolita is about if they took inspiration from the novel.I'd much prefer seeing our main character go through with a high opinion of her father only to see it wither away before her as she finds out what the truth is, her father is a pedophile and her mother's scorn was misguided and hurt a innocent child instead due to her father's disgusting nature. Two characters can be wrong, the Father and Mother both can be bad people. To see the main character witness two downfalls of her parental figures would make the original ending of her committing suicide more understandable however why wouldn't she just want to deliver justice? Why not live and go lay Rachel to rest by speaking the truth? Instead we got a story about "wah is me, society looks down at me because they don't understand that I, a pedophile, is in love" and "My mother is jealous because she couldn't stand my father being happy with a child". ------------------Advice: Rework the game's story a bit. Exposing the father for being WRONG as well in similar fashions of Lolita to keep the story from straying too far. The Father can still view himself as being in the right and thinking he was in love but the commentary of the main character shouldn't be justifying and should criticize him. Validating the father from the MC's POV is just gross.OrJust go to therapy writers, its not normal to romanticize a grown man grooming a child because he "fell in love". There's nothing profound here besides your profoundly worrying beliefs being pushed here.

_childDocuments_.review: this is quite possibly the worst indie-narrative game I have ever played. _childDocuments_.review: This is a short game with a good story and completely terrible game from technical standpoint.So the story is about a Rachel Foster suicide obviously. It's spoiler sensitive so all i'm gonna say is that you arrive at the hotel and mysterious things start happening and you start figuring it out. There's a guy talking to you on a phone, similar to Firewatch, he kinda guides you. I don't know if it's just me but i kind of guessed how the story will end at mid-game somewhere. I loved the ending though.Gameplay is simple. It's a walking simulator with some light puzzles. Walking is painfully slow, even if you hold shift it's extremely slow. The hotel is quite big and it may be confusing so if you're lost you just waste your time slowly walking around until you find where you need to go. There's a map but it doesn't show where you are so it doesn't help at all.I also encountered a bug or maybe a design flaw where i couldn't progress the story. After googling for a minute i learned that you need to take a certain route to your destination, go through a certain room. That's just stupid.Also a huge thunder in cold winter? I know this could happen but how often? There's a blizzard. Developers probably thought it will make this game scarier. Speaking of scariness, it's pretty scary towards the end. Atmosphere is really creepy (in a good way).Now the reason why this is a negative review. Technically this game is a mess, a complete disgrace to PC platform, a low effort console port.There are no graphics options.No ultrawide support.No FOV slider, it feels like FOV is set to 30 or something. If you're sensitive and get nausea from playing games sometime this one will make you vomit.Chromatic aberration and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blur you can't turn of.Sluggish mouse movement where 60fps feels like 15fps.60fps lock.No manual saving and the game saves only when the day ends which means you can't save in the middle of the chapter.Terrible performance at ultra settings. Dear developers, your game has small areas, corridors and rooms, no visible characters, why even MSFS, Horizon or Detroit runs better? 35Fps, are you kidding?Sound is cool though. Sound makes this game pretty creepy and you feel uncomfortable if you play it alone in the dark. Nicely done. Voice acting is pretty good, not great, not bad either.This is a nice mystery game worth playing for the story. But playing it feels painful. Get this from a bundle or at an extremely low price.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a walking simulator. Walking simulators, almost by definition, are not very challenging and that is also the case of TSORF.Like many walking simulators TSORF is a misterious tragedy or a tragic  mistery and, as such, depends mainly on much the story grabs your interest,The game starts slow and, at first, you don't know what is the motivation of the protagonist. But, once you get to Day 1, the plot gets interesting and griping.It is a bit similar to Gone Home, I do prefer TSORF over GH: the settings are better, there are more places to explore (at least it feels like it) and, as mistery and drama, has more suspense and gravitas. I liked it.No glitches or bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Ok this game looks nice and awakens "The Shining"-vibes: An old hotel, up in the snowy mountains, long corridors, empty rooms etc. I liked the setting a lot!But: "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" is mainly a walking-simulator: Check the reception, check the 1st floor, back to the basement etc. It´s all about finding clues which will trigger the next part of the story. After some minutes of playing it all felt repetitive. There are no jumpscares in the game. The spooky atmosphere is caused by sounds and by the story o.c. Since the main character is not able to run properly your movements feel like walking through kneedeep mud.Fazit: I think it´s the story that makes the cake. Finding puzzle-pieces that finally reveal the truth behind the disappearing of Rachel. I liked the game but the movement could have been a lot more optimized.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most boring walking sims I ever played. The whole story unfolds in a hotel, and while it looks nice, most of the time you simply walk around or have a dialogue over a radio. There's no exploration, no puzzles, no cutscenes. and the game's story is kinda boring and predictable. But most of all, it doesn't bring out any emotions. So I suggest you pass on this one even if it's on sale with 90% off. Don't waste your time even though the game is just 2-3 hours long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting story and scary atmosphere, but not for people with depression or anxiety or victims of sexual abuse. Recommended for those who like book-like videogames with easy puzzles and immersive feeling.One thing I realized after finishing it is that for some the overall pieces of the puzzle will make little sense. I can't say it's a narrative masterpiece as some events and dialogues are a bit unconsequential or at least they just do not make sense when thinking back. I guess they help the suspense feeling but they left me with some quick and dirty holliwood script feeling.Reading reviews I realized it does touch heavy themes in a rather light way, I do not think who wrote it has any idea of what violence is and what are the consequences of a trauma. This can be interpreted as offensive or even criminal by some. So do not expect any real depth into mental health, they really confuse trauma and prejudices in an insane way. But I think it is intentional to make the player face the horror of a perverted mind that twists violence into love.

_childDocuments_.review: To put this short and simple, you will probably like this game if you enjoyed games like Firewatch or Gone Home. If you haven't tried either of those, then expect a fairly linear experience that focuses on a pretty good story-line.I've played quite a few games that fall within the "walking-simulator" genre and this one is pretty much par for the course. Expect the usual moving from story trigger to story trigger. Sprinkled throughout the game are various little details that you can use to piece together some foreshadowing if you are observant. Unfortunately, as with most games of it's ilk, there are a lot of random objects that you can pick up and observe. This wouldn't be a big deal if there was a point to looking at them but there is very little story attached to picking up a random kitchen sponge. This is something that I would like to see developers trend away from. If you have an object that you can interact with it would be nice if there was a purpose behind it or just an interesting detail tied to fleshing out the characters. Where this game does shine is in it's sound design. That alone will leave you feeling paranoid and on edge for the majority of the game. The story is well constructed but the banter can sound really forced or cliched at times. I definitely got a real laugh out of a certain VHS tape with super cringe inducing acting. (no offense to the actors, I took it as intentional)Overall, this was a very enjoyable game. Pick it up if you enjoy a good mystery full of suspenseful atmosphere and a tragic story to tell.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:*A beautiful highly detailed hotel to explore* Nothing feels rushed or low effort*Terrific voice acting, especially from the main protagonist *A refreshingly great story that 'unravels' over time*Excellent use of audio to aid suspense*Good optimisation, the frame rate never faltered. *Satisfactory game length (About 5 hours for me)Review:There are so many things this game did right. It provides us with a highly detailed and beautiful hotel that simply feels like it could exist in the real world, there is purpose in its design and many times I found myself just curiously looking around. It makes excellent use of sound with the music and mysterious ambience really playing an important role in the experience. It has a gripping story that unravels gradually building up the suspense and there were genuine moments where I found myself having to pluck up the courage just to turn a corner, unsure of what I might find. One of my favourite horror films of all time is Stanley Kubrick's The Shinning and I have to admit, the Timberline Lodge really gives off an 'Overlook' vibe. Pretty sure I recognised the carpet from somewhere XD. Closing: If you're a fan of really well done Walking Simulators in the vain of Firewatch or simply love exploration with great story telling then pick up this Gem.

_childDocuments_.review: The details and design of the gameplay itself are well done, so props to whoever on the team did that. Unfortunately, all of the work put into beautifying the hotel and environment can't make up for the sick goal of the story designers.----- Content Warning: suicide, rape, pedophilia -----The game follows the story of an adult woman who has to return to the Montana hotel she grew up in following her mother's suicide. This hotel happens to be where her father also groomed, abused, and got a 16 year old girl killed. The plot in itself isn't reprehensible and the game does partly portray how young victims of sexual assault can be vilified as "seducers" of upstanding middle-aged married men in popular narratives. Think of Humbert Humbert's defenders in the case of Lolita.However, the game clearly views this "relationship" as a "tragic romance" which was the only good in this poor little girl's life. The abuser, your character's father, is constantly deified and glorified, even at the end as you get to see his attic man cave with naked drawings of this dead child he assaulted. The ending changed what could have been a game which took a closer look at the psychological damage left on families by abusers and also how public narratives often focus more on the drama caused to families by this abuse as opposed to the impact it has the victims, into a sick justification of pedophilia and grooming.Bad game. 0/10. Don't play.

_childDocuments_.review: “The Suicide of Rachel Foster” is a short walking simulator game with amazing atmosphere that make it feel like a horror game, only that in this game nothing really happens like jumpscares or such.In this game you play as Nicole who is going back to the family hotel that she hasn't been to in many years but now her parents are dead so you are going to take a look at the place, but when you arrive a blizzard hits and you're stuck.This gives Nicole plenty of time to go around and look which leads to some mysteries, mainly the suicide of Rachel Foster.I enjoyed this game a lot, it has an amazing story, breathtaking atmosphere and really good graphics.I highly recommend this game.I rate “The Suicide of Rachel Foster” 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I can't put my finger on it but something about this game doesn't sit right with me. It feels like it has a conservative undertone running through it. For example, one of the choices early on is if you attended an ant-abortion rally. But there's some discussions of religion and the general lack of sensitivity in the game such as using the r word and the idea of being "crazy" so casually. Other than that it is just really boring. I'm all for Gone Home style walking simulators but this one opens up the entire hotel pretty much right away with only a few rooms and corridors later on and then lets you be bored and lost in it the entire time. The map doesn't even have a "you're here" icon. There are two twists and big revelations near the end and neither are surprising or interesting. The actual what happened to Rachel Foster is the most logical thing ever and yet the main character seems shocked as if it wasn't something the police should probably have assumed from the get go. Both endings also just don't resonate with me at all.In addition the save points are spread so far apart that I lost my first hour of play time by stopping right before I guess it would have saved again. Instead I watched the rest of it on youtube and I'm glad I did.Pass on this one. It's not worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mostly recommending this based on others' negative review that, to me, don't make sense.Pedophilia? Nowhere to be seen.Grooming? Not sure how it's in here.Vilifying a 16 year old? No idea how they got that.Yes, this story is NUANCED. It covers uncomfortable topics, but all it does is tells a story. It's not making a moral stance on anything, nor is it accusing anybody of anything. This story is really just a paranormal-meets-psychological-stress narrative. Everybody suffers somehow and in some way. Each character has their own demons to deal with. Don't come into this game hoping to stand on some soap box or moral superiority complex. Just...go on the journey and really explore the different perspectives of the different characters as you learn more about them.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a negative review on her before, but this game was just that upsetting that it had to be my first. The first 70% of the narrative is promising and I actually found myself relating to the two main characters quite a bit. As was to be expected, this game handles some very disturbing and sensitive topics. These include suicide (obviously), child abuse & molestation, unhealthy obsessions, and childhood trauma. Ultimately, it does not handle any of these issues in a inspired, or even a responsible way. Though the game sets you up to believe that at the end of this journey you will be enlightened in some way, at best it fails horribly at this, and at worst it portrays child molestation as a beautiful romantic tragedy. The characters that were delicately crafted for the majority of the game become so warped by the end that they are unrecognizable. But the cherry on top is the last 30 seconds of the game which are by far the most irredeemable from a character development stand point. Here is a non-spoiler spoiler: every character in the game is actually insane and stupid and unreliable and you just don't know it till the end.The voice acting is the one thing that is consistently awesome. Sadly, this just makes it even more upsetting that the narrative is so flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: Story aside for a moment, the "gameplay" is pretty slow and, as far as I can tell, any choice you make doesn't actually matter, so feel free to do whatever. I know the game has the content warnings, which is fine, but I cannot in good conscience recommend a game that promotes this.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a decent walking simulator with an interesting story and great voice acting. It closely follows in the footsteps of titles like Firewatch, relying on a radio/phone connection for dialogue with a character who is never seen or directly interacted with. Unfortunately, it does not come close to Firewatch's success, with its extremely linear story and lack of motivation for exploration. + Excellent voice actors (excluding that atrocious ghost tape).+ Large hotel to explore.+ Plenty of engaging dialogue between Irving and Nicole that kept me both interested and entertained.+ Decent graphics, brilliantly depicting an eerie, run-down hotel.+ Impeccable use of sound.+ Interesting story which incorporates thriller, detective and horror elements.+ Unnerving ambience throughout the game, intensified by its melancholy colour scheme and subtle background sounds. - Despite having a beautiful large setting to explore, it is extremely linear and lacking in objects to interact with, unless players only follow the main story.- Minor typos.- Abrupt ending with a low playtime, averaging around 3-4 hours in total.- Constant, and I mean constant use of the cell phone for every minor detail to 'report' and it became tiresome, fast.The main protagonist, Nicole, returns to  her old family hotel with the intention of  selling it, fulfilling her mother’s last wishes in her will. However, things do not go to plan and she quickly finds herself trapped inside due to a snowstorm. 10 years prior, Nicole and her mother fled the family home after her father, Leonard was discovered having an affair with a girl her own age, 16-year-old Rachel. Rachel subsequently became pregnant and later committed suicide after the affair was revealed.  Understandably so, the protagonist feels very uncomfortable being in this space and  relies on her trusty old cell phone, finding support in a FEMA agent named Irving. With little else to do, Nicole decides to inspect the damage to the hotel by herself and soon becomes engrossed in her family’s history, uncovering strange objects, ominous sounds, and ghost tapes that all lead back to the same source, Rachel. Without going into too much detail, what I cannot fathom is there being hardly any focus on the dad’s affair with an underage girl. There is a lot of talk about Nicole being jealous of how 'perfect' Rachel was and how she was blamed for tearing the family apart, but barely a mention of the abuse. There are even scenes where Nicole states her father was a good man with morals and just fell out of love, despite being completely aware of Rachel's age. Nevertheless, this whole component seems to be forgotten in the game, something that was mentioned once and never touched on again.Being a walking simulator, gameplay is exactly what one would expect, roam around the hotel to slowly progress the story and find objects of interest. Similar to Firewatch, players must report everything to Irving through the cell phone, however, it is all very linear and I often tried to explore other areas but there was nothing to interact with, no notes, no old mementos, no cupboards to open, nothing. Thus, I decided to stick to just the main story and go where I was supposed to.It is always very simple to know where to go next, with a map of the hotel being easily accessible and notes depicting exactly where to go. Along the way, players are usually kept company by Irving on the phone, describing what we see and having some general banter. These are both areas that are executed remarkably well and are almost solely responsible for players' immersion into the story. Some parts of the hotel give an extremely cosy aura, yet some others completely contrast this, making the place seem desolate and ominous. The bright colour scheme is also well utilised to focus on this contrast, bringing attention to luminous areas or the opposing drab rooms with mould accumulating over the walls, typically resembling an area linked with Nicole’s dark past.Sound is exceptional and commonly left me peering over my shoulder after hearing a creepy gasp from behind, or a door slamming closed in the distance. Combining this with the excellent voice acting and dialogue, the sound is surely a component that will heavily and positively impact players' experience in the game.Yes... and no. I enjoyed my playthrough and found myself captivated by the engrossing dialogue and story, yet simultaneously disappointed at the missed opportunity to further explore the hotel and delve deeper into such a convoluted family history. At 3-4 hours long, the experience is short-lived for a $AU25 game. However, the conversation system is extremely similar to Firewatch, so if you enjoyed that title, I do recommend The Suicide of Rachel Foster, but preferably at a sale cost due to the lack of replayability and motivation for exploration.This review copy was provided to the OCG-Curations curator.

_childDocuments_.review: There are already many reviews that share my view of this game, but I'll post anyway: don't buy it. The positives: great voice acting, very impressive graphics, decent story telling in practice (but not actual content, more below). The negatives: pretty much everything else. Navigating in the game was more difficult than it should've been, mostly because the hotel is way way way too big for the overall need of the game. I get it, it's a hotel and it should be spacious, but there's too much getting lost for no reason and exploring rooms with absolutely no value to the game. Add to that that the map is almost completely useless by design, if it hadn't have been for the amount of wandering I did I probably would've finished the game in under 2 hours. Also the character walks so slow that you have to hold down shift to run the entire time. My real issue is with the actual content of the story - I guess the title of the game would hopefully spare those who may be triggered by a lot of the things in this game, but it truly is astonishing how bad some of this story line truly is when it comes sensitive subjects. There are other reviews with spoilers that you can read if you like, but I'll forego that. I cannot fathom the conclusions that were jumped to by the end of the game, and it ultimately makes the entire game and all the characters unlikable. I think that the whole of the story was mishandled. All in all, glad i bought this severely discounted. Save your money. If you want a first person narrative that actually feels good at the end then you should check out "Gone Home" instead

_childDocuments_.review: This is a walking simulator in the literal sense.  A story on the level of "my immortal" fanfic with suicide, murder, and implied pedophilia at the center of the story.  The characters are completely unlikable and the "twist" is right there in the opening scene. It's got about 5-10 minutes of actual gameplay with about 3-4 hours runtime due to how horribly slow the movement is.  With the over exaggerated head bob as you walk (I took a lot longer because i'd leave it running in steam while I got bored and did something else).The "puzzles" and "gameplay" are virtually non-existent.  There's approximately 5 total puzzles (with maybe 10 minutes of actual thinking, or googling the vague stuff involved) and 3 hours of you, staring at a wall, listening to the obvious bad guy explain the entire story to you.   The setting is pretty and the hotel is very creepy, but, sadly NONE of this is used to build tension or create a compelling story.  This is quite literally the same bait and switch that the god awful game Gone Home did.  Marketing makes it sound like a thrilling horror/paranormal experience and never delivers.  It's boring.The writing is horrendous, at times the subtitles don't even match what the person is saying in the dialogue.  Setting aside all the political BS that surrounds this title with the central themes of pedophilia and suicide, the characters are terrible.  The story, which, could have been fleshed out into a 5-6 hour runtime with character building, more puzzles, etc, is atrocious.  This game, that I got for free with my humble bundle isn't even worth $1.  Watch a let's play if you really must see what this is all about and waste your time on a terrible story

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great experience with lots of downsides. First of all I was shocked to see that there are tons of negative reviews about the game. People are really angry about Leonard, who is according to story a pedophilia, but why the all hate and statements such as " game has glorification/justification of pedophilia" ? Even after beating the game I never felt like the game was injecting any elements like that to the player. I know pedophilia is a sensitive issue and should be approached as such, however, even if the game had those pedophilia elements somehow I never got to experience them nor I must have missed them out for some reason.I saw other comments about our protagonist Nicole as well though she had nothing to do with pedophilia at all. I guess Leonard being her father is enough of a reason for some people to go rage on her. It is really saddening because I believe game did a great job on creating an eerie setting, a satisfying story and gameplay. Especially sound design is above my expectations and I can assert that I almost had “eargasm” because of sound design of the game. Apart from everything, I guess what people really misinterpreted is emerged from the perception of our protagonist towards her father. She had a soft spot towards her father, and her father’s actions which is not appropriate in any way as pedophilia isn’t something you just can tolerate , and she had a really hard time while digisting the reality as she had been avoiding from facing with her past. BUT, it is a perspective of a daughter who had been through tons of stuff, it is so natural for a son or a daughter to try to soften the actions of their parents. And I believe this is what developers tried to reflect. Our protagonist never praised anything regarding to pedephilia  throughout the game. She had a sick old man who she loved instinctly and hate deliberately at the end of the story. So all in all, if you can approach the game with a pair of objective glasses you will have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into all the negative stuff, I do want to say that the game's sound design is excellent, and assuming the sound designer was a different person from whoever wrote the game's narrative, I feel sorry for them, because their masterpiece is trapped in what turns out to be a real mess of a game. There are a lot of subtle and well-thought-out details to it. For instance, after you receive a scary phone call, you'll sometimes hear the ringer of an old phone settling against its bell as you pass by, making you wonder whether it's about to start ringing again. The hum of various different machinery in the basement combines just right into a spooky chord as you pass between the rooms. Subtle, distant sounds from above or below often make you wonder if you're really alone in the hotel. Every floor surface has its own whole array of footstep sounds, little creaks and scuffs. If for some reason, you got the game for free or as part of a bundle and feel like installing it regardless, I would recommend just checking out the sound design on the first 3-4 days and doing your best to ignore the story, and then quitting sometime around when you make it into the room where the paranormal investigators were staying, because it's really all downhill from there. Maybe don't even mess with the garage door on day one, and just explore the hotel yourself. You'll get most of everything that was worthwhile in the game.Let's consider the setting as it's posed early on in the game (some spoilers, but they're things that are revealed pretty quickly). Your father, a fifty-something(?) Ph.D. physicist, was a pedophile whose 16 year old female victim, the daughter of a priest, committed suicide. This happened when you were 16 as well, and you and your mother ran away. Following your father's death, you've returned to the hotel that you lived in as a child, and which your father somehow continued to run for many years after he was exposed to the community for what he was. In an obvious nod to The Shining, you're snowed in at the hotel.The existential horror almost writes itself. It's hard to imagine how they could possibly screw this up too badly. Just being trapped in this place and being forced to really come to terms with who your father was should be horrifying enough. Combine that with a really well-thought-out sound design with a lot of small details that set the player on edge, and it seems like it should have been easy to end up with a horror experience that's worth playing. If the writing dealt with the inherent issues head-on and tactfully, there was genuine opportunity for a valid literary work that said something real about darker aspects of the human condition.Unfortunately, they decided to take the whole thing in a very different direction. The first sign that something is off is that the game starts mixing in some supernatural nonsense via some ghost hunters (who visited the hotel in the past, you're finding the stuff they left behind) and spooky lights and stuff. To their credit, it kind of works as comic relief against the dark background, and they managed to avoid really doing any blatant jump-scares. But one would have thought the premise and setting that was already established contained enough room for horror without introducing ghosts. It comes off as an awkward and pointless distraction.The worse thing however is what happens when they *do* start to deal with the issue of what happened to Rachel Foster. The characters in the game (or more to the point, the game's authors) seem to be oblivious to the problems inherent in a sexual relationship between a 50-something physics Ph. D. and a 16 year old girl that he was tutoring, apart from the fact that he was cheating on his wife. Neither the player character, nor the slightly mysterious fellow who she's talking to on a radio throughout seem to be able to recognise the father's crimes for what they are. It's described non-sarcastically as a "love affair", and the remainder of the game basically tries to argue that it was actually your mother who was the terrible person all along.Yep. Really.The plot only goes downhill from there. It's an incoherent mess which fails to hold any shred of sympathy or understanding of such serious topics as suicide, rape, and child abuse. I was left with the impression that whoever was responsible for this game's narrative should probably be on some sort of watch list, and it's kind of hard to believe that nobody involved in the publishing of the game ever said "hey, wait just a minute here" and somehow Devolver ended up okaying the whole thing.The awfulness aside, there are also a bunch of mechanical issues. The game is linear but the hotel is not. You can explore a large portion of the hotel, along with the chapel it's connected to by a creepy narrow underground passageway right from the start, find all kinds of stuff (though not everything), and your character will not react until you come back later in the game in the appropriate sequence. She's also talking on a radio phone with a guy whenever linear progress is being made, and claiming not to know where things are that the player may already be quite familiar with through nonlinear exploration. Because of this, I often found myself already standing directly in front of something while my character was saying that she wasn't sure where that thing is, because I'd made my way there during the conversation.When the game finally sees fit to discuss the suicide of the girl, rather than letting you discover a bunch of clues organically throughout the hotel, somehow you wake up on a new day, with a whole bunch of evidence arranged in front of you, which your character apparently collected while you weren't watching. The game designers don't seem to really understand how a walking simulator can reveal a story to the player in a nonlinear way through exploration, and instead force you along a particular path so that they can... have all the characters try to make excuses for why your dad was a good person or just generally be oblivious, at the same time as revealing just how obviously awful he was. If they just let you explore the evidence on your own without having the characters comment on it, there wouldn't be as much opportunity to try to acquit him, I guess.The game only saves at the start of each "day", and the "days" are of weird arbitrary lengths. The first couple are quite long as I recall, though perhaps that's just my own fault for not always doing what was expected of me and choosing to explore. Others are weirdly short, and all kinds of stuff seems to happen in between that we don't get to see.Anyway, yeah, I don't recommend this. There are so many better ways to spend your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game does not support sexual misconduct. That's an interpretation by some folk in the comments who clearly feel very strongly about the subject (probably shouldn't be engaged with stories with such dark undertones IMO). What is clear is that the broken characters dealing with a messed up situation are delusional and clearly traumatized, finding some sense of reason where there isn't any to find. I didn't find myself sympathizing with the "pedo" at all.My criticisms:- The story is dramatic, leaning on well known tropes, to deliver an experience that, well, missed its mark somewhat. - The use of the phone did not work well despite mirroring Firewatch in the idea of an unseen voice to help the narrative move. There was too much given in the "phone calls," while the numerous other implements that could have been used (such as books, journals, drawings, so on) were passed over, leaving what is essentially an exploration game feeling a little empty.- The protagonist is a bit of a potty mouth. I mention this because it somehow felt out of place, not matching the country setting (not that I care if some f-bombs are loosed). - Perhaps it was my  download, but my audio cut in and out. There were subtitles, so I could keep going, however, there is a  moment in the game where following the sound is key to progressing. I had to consult a guide to figure that bit out.- Honestly, the hotel is a bit too big with a few too many corridors to navigate. It's not horrible, just a waste of time. I believe the intention by the designers was for the wandering to be back dropped with the main conversation, but I often stopped and listened instead (my sound dropped in certain areas annoyingly).My praises:- The main voice actress did great and I enjoyed her performance. For the most part, her script made sense and she nailed it. (The second actor, well, I didn't care for his voice, so I doubt I can give him a fair shake.)- The touch of aberrations added to things for sure.- The story is a dark one and I applaud any that dare tackle such subjects in public. We can all see how easy it is for trolls to rip at a creator who dares be brave. There was nothing tasteless, lewd or unnecessary and I found my sympathy landing exactly where it should--with the protagonist, Nicole.- I didn't mind wandering the environment, listening to the creeks in floor planks and gentle music that shifted as the story became a bit more serious.I do recommend the game for a mature audience and people should be aware this game could be triggering. On sale, it's a good buy for fans of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It was creepy and thrilling without any gory moments. A true psychological thriller. There were so many moments that I found myself panicking from the fear of what could be, the horrors I might be facing ahead. TSORF did a lot of things right - the dialog was organic and realistic. The voice acting was above average. Lovely graphics and a nice sized POI to explore. The story was compelling and interesting. Fantastic music and ambiance; truly the tone of the soundtrack and the ambient sounds in this abandoned hotel add so much to the deep sense of dread and foreboding. The game opens with a trigger warning for folks who may find the subject matter difficult. Truly this is an impressive, well paced game, especially for a first product from this dev team. The bad: there's a few translation hiccups and a couple of times when the CC doesn't match the voice over. At one part in the game, there wasn't a lot of direction and I spent some time aimlessly wandering around.  (Not the end of the world, especially considering it's a walking sim.)  Overall, this game gets a hearty 8.5/10 from me. Glad I bought it. Glad I played it. Would definitely recommend to others.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide Of Rachel Foster, or TSORF as it's known had an immense amount of potential and could have gone in such a positive and knowledgeable direction, while still being eerily creepy and giving you those same psychological horror vibes. But instead, the game was just immensely disappointing.SPOILERS FROM THIS POINT ONAs a barebones explanation I quote another review by someone with similar views as myself: TSORF "is a walking simulator set in an abandoned hotel in Montana during a blizzard in the early ‘90s. You play as Nicole, the daughter of the hotel’s proprietors, who is returning to inspect the property before selling it. Her only companion is Irving, a FEMA agent who communicates with Nicole over a primitive cell phone. Together, they dig through the hotel, searching for the truth about Rachel’s death." As the story unravels you learn that Nicole's father Leonard had an "affair" with Rachel, a girl the same age as his daughter. And this so called "affair" getting out is what caused both the family to fall apart as well as Rachel to commit suicide. Now none of this situation is really true. What Rachel and Leonard have is not an affair but rather child abuse. The game uses it's main characters thoughts and dialogue to persuade players that what Leonard did was not wrong and that he and Rachel were simply in love. Not only is this untrue but it's downright disgusting, Leonard was using an abuse of power he knew he had from being Rachel's mentor and teacher. For the Devs to go create such a story while also trying to convince players it's okay is downright disturbing.And if that's not bad enough, Irving (Your helpful Fema companion from earlier) is actually Rachel's younger brother who had been working in the hotel with Leonard the child molester up until the old man croaked. and is even still living there and waiting for Nicole when she finally arrives after her mother's death.The story's big twist ending is that Rachel did not commit suicide but was rather murdered by Nicole's jealous mother Claire. This information is revealed while Irving is shaming Nicole for being jealous of Rachel and not seeing her own mother's jealousy of the 16 YEAR-OLD GIRL.***TRIGGER WARNING FOR SUICIDE***And finally, if all of that wasn't enough to turn you off to the situation, at the very end of the game Nicole is given a choice. Still dazed and confused after all that's happened the one thing Nicole is positive about is that her father did nothing wrong. Nicole sits in her car thinking over all that she has learned in the past ten days with an exhaust pipe taped to her closed up window. You are forced to turn on the car. This is where the players are given a choice. Turn the engine back off, or leave it on and let Nicole die.Both options are terrible.If you leave the exhaust pipe on, Nicole dies with out saying a word thinking she is responsible for what happened. The alternative is letting her live in which she then vows to live at the hotel for the rest of her life, happy forever.Two ♥♥♥♥♥♥ endings to an unacceptable excuse of a storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster offers a bold perspective on the topics of suicide and ephebophilia. Its presentation is amateurish, bereft of grace and needlessly confusing, yet fervent attackers bombard the game for entirely different – and misguided – reasons.In their inability to distinguish paedophilia from attraction for adolescents past the age of consent, reviewers shriek indignantly that a story like this will simply not do. They dismiss this game as pro-paedophilic or pro-suicidal but that is simply fallacious. Firstly, Rachel Foster was sixteen years old – an adolescent. As such, paedophilia is not, even marginally, what this game is about. It is about the implications following from a married man falling in love with a sixteen-year-old teenager, Rachel. While distasteful and arguably unethical, their relationship was neither illegal nor condoned by anyone – except for Rachel’s deeply disturbed brother who put the affair of his sister on a pedestal, calling it pure love. As eyebrow-raising as it is, his perspective is understandable. Rachel’s brother had been a naïve child who saw his sister as a beacon of light and a person who deserves happiness. In adulthood, he became deeply disturbed and nostalgic, which should be considered while appraising his continued approval of the relationship.Secondly, the game always links suicide with destructive effects on others – never the opposite. And though some outraged reviewers claim players are forced to commit suicide, they simply chose to blame the developers instead of own impetuousness.Now, despite its provocative concept, The Suicide of Rachel Foster has little to offer in terms of both writing as well as gameplay. The protagonist is needlessly belligerent, dialogues tend to lack logic, story progression feels lazy and haphazard, and the already questionable writing grows progressively strewn with misplaced tropes. The feeble finale failed to convey any lesson, moral, or a satisfying conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: I have VERY mixed feelings about this game. I think overall I'm going to give it a tentative thumbs down. It wasn't the worst game I've ever played, but the cons definitely outweigh the pros.PROS- Good atmosphere. It was a pretty game, with an expansive hotel to explore and decent graphics. The sound design especially made it really immersive, and had me on the edge of my seat at times.- Decent voice acting. A little cheesy at times, but I enjoyed the banter between the two main characters.- Pretty darn creepy. It's not a horror game, but it does the "subtle thriller" angle very well.- Well paced. Between the walking/jogging speed, the layout of the hotel, and the way the game has you navigate in order to progress the story, I thought it moved at just the right speed.- Promising story. The ending didn't deliver, but I was invested up until near the game's finale.CONS- VERY likely to trigger motion sickness. It was unplayable for me the first time I picked it up. I don't know if I got magically better or if the devs have since updated it, but I was finally able to finish it - despite the terrible head bobbing.- Weirdly romanticises pedophilia and suicide. Even after seeing this criticism in a LOT of the game's reviews, I went into the game thinking "how bad can it be?" ... yeah, the devs really missed the mark here.- Ending was a major let-down. It was predictable, strange, and some parts of it didn't make sense at all. - LOTS of useless items. The game tells you outright that interacting with items is the key to finding out the truth, but this is incredibly misleading. 99% of the items I interacted with had no purpose whatsoever, and didn't add anything to the story (e.g. the dozens of cigarette packs you can pick up and examine throughout the game).- Some unrealistic/disjointed dialogue. It also got a bit cheesy and over-the-top at times.- Unreasonably buggy. Items wouldn't appear until I interacted with them, prompts to interact with items would remain even after the item was picked up (e.g. after picking up a key from a table, I would still get the prompt that the key was on the table), had to click more than once to get some doors to open, etc. For a fully-finished game, I expected better.- Jarring transitions. It's often impossible to tell when doing something will trigger the end of a chapter, and it's very easy to miss things because of this.All in all, I wouldn't call it a waste of time, but as you can see it's got a LOT of issues. It sucks, because it had so much potential, but it just fell flat on the delivery (especially towards the end). And the devs REALLY need to take a more respectful approach to such serious topics in their future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good-Very good environment that is clearly intended to mimic the Overlook Hotel from The Shining.-Interesting and creepy story.  I'm puzzled by the negative reviews here that claim that the game glorifies pedophilia.  There are plenty of acknowledgments that the dad's relationship with Rachel was not appropriate and that it tore two families apart.-It's creepy and a little scary at times, but no real jump scares to worry about, which is my preference.-The cell phone conversations are similar to Firewatch and help to move the story along efficiently (I hate games where you have to read pages and pages of text to discover the plot), although they were disruptive as I mention below.The Neutral-This is a walking simulator, not a puzzle game.  Much of the game is literally spent walking from room to room with dialog interruptions.  While there are basic puzzles (push the button, find the object, etc.), they are a very minor aspect of the game.   I prefer mostly puzzles and less story, but I won't judge the game just by my preferences.-Along those lines, the few tools you carry with you are basically useless.  Some objects were carried the whole game and you literally used them once.The Bad-Getting around is tedious.  Walking is painfully slow and "running" is only slightly faster. It takes a long time to get anywhere and my fingers were cramped from having to hold shift so much.  -The cell phone conversations are painful.  Anytime you find something interesting, you have to "dial" the guy and the conversations take forever (and you can't skip them).  It really interrupts the flow of the game.  If you are partial to Myst-like games that are 99% solitary exploration, you will be frustrated with these constant disruptions.-Game is too dark (why do developers do this?) and the flashlight requires you to constantly click to make it work.-I may have missed it, but the paranormal aspect was a loose end that was never tied off.

_childDocuments_.review: Games like Gone Home and other walking simulators rely on a strong story and environment to push players to complete the game.  This one sort of got the environment right.  It gives off the appropriate amount of creepy in the setting (It definitely reminds me of the movie:  ).  Unfortunately this is where the praise ends.The story itself is problematic.  I love dark/mature stories as much as the next gamer, but this story's events just makes me feel... Dirty?  I'm not quite sure what kind of angle the developers were trying to hit with the premise of a father loving a sixteen year old kid...  I mean...  Ugh.  Was there another way to tell this kind of story outside of this gross setting?  Did they choose this setting because they wanted to be edgy or was this subject matter that was worth exploring?  Either way, I didn't enjoy it at all.What's worse is that they treat this disturbing backstory with nonchalance and a "what's done is done" kind of vibe that really disturbed me.  It's like the story wanted to focus more on a mystery rather than addressing that kind of depravity.Happily it's a quick game - I got through it in about 3 hours.  I have absolutely no desire to replay this for the one achievement I'm missing.  It's being deleted from the hard drive and never looked at again!  If you got this from a Humble Bundle monthly like I did, do yourself a favor and just move along.

_childDocuments_.review: This otherwise wonderful narrative experience is shattered by some very sudden poor narrative choices at the end, which undermines the prior five hours of storytelling. The first couple of hours of the game see the player arrive at an abandoned hotel in the middle of a snowstorm with only an unfamiliar voice on a cell phone turned two-way radio. The developers did a wonderful job building out set as one believable but spooky hotel, with several little things for players to explore and discover. Playing through those first several days it was hard to tell what the rules of the story really were, if this was just a game about exploring an abandoned hotel, or if this was a ghost story with specters to terrorize you as you progress. It was really exciting to be immersed in this isolated place with little to no one to interact with, and the thought that a poltergeist could leap out from some empty hotel room and start tearing apart my sanity and my character. All the while the voice acting was excellent, and made me want to care about the characters they were representing. All these things are great, so what is the problem? As stated in the name, this game is a narrative revolving around a suicide. It was the suicide of a pregnant sixteen year old with learning disabilities that had been involved with a man 30 years her senior (using language that the game provided). This can be a very tricky topic to approach in polite conversation, and it requires a fair bit of tact to do so sensitively. This end of this game does not deliver the tact necessary for this to be a positive, artful interpretation of these subjects. By the end of the game, we are supposed to accept that this relationship between an adult man, allegedly in his 40's, and a 16-year-old girl is fine if there is love. It is not fine with an advantaged and capable 16-year-old girl, and it is especially not fine with a disadvantaged girl that is forced to rely more on the adults in her life. The story betrays the player and the characters on the subject of suicide. While the whole story is built around the suicide of the titular character in an event that had taken place more than ten years before the start of the game, there are events near the end of the game as well that are not built up in any reasonable way through the narrative leading up to them and come across as arbitrary and confusing. I suppose that feeling itself could be some kind of metaphor for the feeling of those left behind, but honestly the feeling I have from the conclusion of the game are more akin to irresolution. The direction that was taken for the final chapters simply left me with a feeling that there was supposed to be more, but instead of a coherent ending the writers wanted something dramatic, so they sacrificed all of the prior work of building up these characters, the setting, and lost track of the ghost story to try to give the player an unnecessary moral choice for the final action in the game. (Also, where did she even find her car keys? Like, when did that happen? I explored that hotel up and down and never found them...)If the team at One O One wanted to try again to make an adventure around the ambiguity of the supernatural and exploring other isolated locales, I would certainly want to check that out, because the environment was nearly perfect. In fact, I am still not sure if the hotel really was haunted. Unfortunately for this particular game, the narrative failed to capture me, in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game itself is a atmospheric supernatural mystery solving game. "There's nothing to fear, but fear itself" sums it up greatly, however with that in mind, there are issues that part game, part not.  This inst a game a game to wonder freely and do as you please, you need the walk-through to do anything.The graphics are greatThe Music  is goodAtmosphere is creepyStory is interestingVoice acting is awesomeCharacters are greatJump Scares were okHowever the issues I have were one big glaring one.Game keeps freezing up during Day loading. I can't finish the game because it freezes at the height of the story near the end (End of Day 8.) This has happened several times in other places. There is no "Day to Day" save or a second save for you to use, nor is there a skip dialog or Choose Chapter option to go back and get things or do do a choice. This means that game freezing up forces you to replay the entire last day, go do everything and wait through dialog and HOPE it fixes itself. If it doesn't, you don't get the endings, achievements and well you just wasted a little bit of cash. It's 3 hours long and it felt more like they were showing off the game graphics, you pick up random items that hold no clue to anything at all. I feel they could have done more with it, so many items could have pupose and rooms we can't get into that would have been great to deepen the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst this story has been crafted to be viewed from a variety of character perspectives, my personal beliefs don't align with many of the creative decisions here. A character defending the love between an underage girl and a 46 year old man? Questionable. Vilifying the girl into an antagonistic spirit when she was in fact the victim? Also questionable. Having the main character grow to respect/become fond of her literal predator father over the course of the game, when she initially hated him for justifiably terrible reasons? Yeah, I can't defend all of this chief. Interesting story, but definitely not something I agree with personally.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, this game blatantly supports pedophilia. I genuinely don't understand what the writers were attempting to do -- we're supposed to sympathize with a pedophilic 58-year old man who takes advantage of a vulnerable 16-year old child, impregnating and drawing nudes of her, with the forced narrative of "true, pure, love." Nope, it's called grooming and sexual abuse. It's disgusting, and I've never requested a refund for a game in my life before this one. The writing and pacing is all over the place, the gameplay is rambling and often unclear, the characters are unlikable, but at the end of the day, it's the horrifying stance on child abuse that utterly ruins this game. _childDocuments_.review: Holy balls was this one a massive misfire. The game has so much potential that ends up getting wasted. I really enjoyed the first thirty minutes as I poked around the old hotel, picking up random objects and just enjoying the general "run-down and outdated hotel" aesthetic. Something seemed a little off early on with the game's pacing and long-winded monologues but I put that aside. The game's just getting started, so there's lore to explain. Got it....but then I picked up the cell phone. That's when it all comes apart in a hurry. MANY times did I get stuck in a spot, staring hopelessly at the next item or door or whatever that I needed to activate in order to advance the story as the guy on the other end of the phone prattled on and on and ON AND ON in long, completely unskippable, novel-length diatribes. Finally, the painful dialogue would mercifully come to an end and the phone would be put away. YAY! Click on the thing and......out comes the phone again. Hello, Irving. I get to listen to you again. Yay. The game continues to suffer from the afore-mentioned horrid pacing for it's 3 hour length. In a well-designed walking sim, the game will play dialogue or narration for a length of time roughly equal to or slightly less than the time it takes for you to walk to the next point of interest. Not here, though. Hoo boy... NOT HERE. Unskippable conversations spill way, way, WAY over the optimum time, forcing me to stand around and wait when I have already arrived at my destination and already know what I need to do next. The map is lovingly crafted, with a ton of searchable rooms and a series of interconnected crawlspaces that's intended to be a kinda-sorta quick travel system that doesn't really work. And all those rooms? Mostly there for show. Most of the game's action (such as it is) takes place in a very limited number of places. The big, beautiful ball room? Nothing happens there. The reception area? Nothing happens there. The fireplace room? Nada. Several of the guest rooms? The locker room? The servant's quarters? The museum? The dining hall? The arcade room?  Zilch. They are all effectively empty corridors for you to continuously backtrack through. Without spoilers, the game's story takes ages to get kick-started and then it's suddenly over, only rarely rising above the level of "dull". The mystery you're trying to solve is barely-there, with only a tiny number of evidence pieces to sort through. The ending is mostly predictable from the jump and the same spooky game tropes I've seen a million times before get rehashed. Whispering voices, a door slamming shut behind you... and mannequins. Really? Mannequins AGAIN? It breaks my heart to hack away at this game because it looks great, has a good atmosphere and is brimming over with potential. But unfortunately, as it stands, this one is a big, fat NO from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews on this game are simply butthurt that the game doesn't comdemn the main character's father's actions enough, which might be fair if you interpreted it that way but is also a stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason to leave a negative review for the whole game.   But. the truth is, this game just kinda... sucks.  I wanted to like it, I really did. I love walking simulators and this finally seemed like something that would scratch my Gone Home itch. First starting it up, I was excited. The hotel looked like it had a bunch of awesome rooms to explore and maybe find tidbits of lore in.  But you can't really explore anything. Most of the rooms are there just to exist and add nothing to the overall game. The number of notes you can find I can count on one hand, and none of them have anything to do with the plot. Like really, you'll find the one open hotel room out of like 50 and it'll just have a note that says "remember to fix water heater". It's stupid.   And you can clearly tell that they wanted this to seem like Gone Home, with the item pick-up system being basically the same. ...Except you can only pick up like, empty water bottles and dish soap, so there's basically no reason for this system to be in the game.  As for the rest of the gameplay... there is basically none. As I said, I love walking simulator games, but even the most gameplay-bare ones usually either have a fun and unique environment to explore or a story that gets you hooked. This has neither. You just walk around an empty hotel, talk to the guy on the phone, occasionally going and "exploring" a new area (which is probably just another boring room), so you can go around clicking on stuff so the guy on the phone can blabber on for another 10 minutes. And then just repeat that every day.  Oh, and yeah, why is this seperated into days? There is absolutely no reason for this. It really feels like they started with a movie script that got thrown out by a studio and just tried to make it into a game with minimal adaptation. This would have been so much better if  instead of just arbitrarily being told where to go by a voice on the phone, you could explore the hotel by yourself, exploring areas and finding notes and clues to solve the mystery.   And, of course, we come to the mystery. It sucks as well. Spoilers onward, but if you've read this far you probably don't care. The mystery starts with the setup that Rachel Foster might not be dead. You start getting hallucinations, get calls from mysterious people, see newspapers that claim she has been witnessed around here, find her lipstick  looking like it's brand-new and it seems like the main mystery you have to answer will have to be why all these things are happening.  The you get to day 9, and out of the blue, without you even expecting it, the mystery starts to get solved. You see mannequins posed to depict Rachel's death, and it turns out she was murdered after all and didn't commit suicide.   "Wait, what do you mean that wasn't the mystery? Of course she's dead. Don't worry about all the other stuff, that was just  a red herring!"  And the whole ending seems rushed as well. The meek, stuttering guy who just shyly asked you out on a date while you weren't really listening is suddenly a well-spoken, sort-of-sinister man. Why did he ask you out? Who knows.  Also apparently Irving and your dad were living in this hotel together the whole time and were waiting for you to come so you could solve their fun mystery. Why did they have a brand new Rachel's-favorite-lipstick? Why did he call you in a scary voice? Who knows. So you would wanna solve the mystery, I guess? But really the only thing you needed to solve it was going to the attic, so he could have just let you in from the start.  At least Irving's speech before he kills himself was really cool. If this were a movie or a better game, that would be very quotable. Too bad it isn't either.  All in all, this could have been so, so much better if it was just a different game. The hotel setting had so much potential. But as it is, I can't recommend it to anyone. It's a boring, confusing waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster starts out as one of the most promising walking sims I've played. A gorgeously realized environment, with some of the absolute best sound design I've had the pleasure of experiencing (the game recommends headphones and I could not agree more). The game has a wonderful set up for an intriguing ghost story, with the past haunting the hallways and corridors of the hotel. The game perfectly encapsulates that feeling of being alone in a house, the floor boards creak, wind hits the windows, occasionally, you hear something that you think shouldn't be there, and you have to rationalize what it was. It's all truly wonderful. Occasionally, I broke away from story beats and just explored the hotel, and the detail here is amazing. There are little details as well, the best making you ask yourself if a part of the hotel was the same as the last time you saw it. Basically want I want to convey is that this game has a level of polish to its environment that stands out among other walking sims, and it really shines.However, despite the pieces being there, as a straightforward narrative experience it fumbles. The mystery and mild-paranormal elements aren't the problem here; in fact, they are the best part. They are subtle, and build tension well. It becomes harder as the game goes on to find a rational explanation for everything, exactly what you want from this kind of game. No, the problem with the game comes from the story that focuses on it's human characters. While I don't believe the game glorifies pedophilia as other reviews stat, it clearly is dismissive of this fact in the overall completion of the narrative. This doesn't quite sit well with me, and it feels like some additional lines of dialogue was all the game needed to condemn Nicole's father's behavior. This is, however, I think made much more problematic by the games ending  This game's ending leaves a truly sour taste in my mouth, leaving me unable to recommend this title. Narrative walking sims live and die by their narratives and settings, so to fumble so key an aspect is a shame. With the depth of detail to the hotel, one can't help but wonder if this was to be a larger game, with more rooms to explore, more plot lines, etc. The sudden narrative shift and seemingly rushed ending makes the game feel like the hotel: initially beautiful and haunting, but quite empty. If you do decide to play The Suicide of Rachel Foster, you will almost certainly be sucked in to a well realized world, but be prepared for this ghost story to haunt you for all the wrong reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game left a rather interesting feeling in me and I'm hoping that maybe this review can help me make sense of it. Also, it will contain SPOILERS so read ahead at your own risk.     First off, the game looks great. I have a soft spot for games that let me inspect stuff in the world and this game has it in spades. There are even ways this mechanic is used to portray information that isn't directly spoken to the player (for example, the books around Leonard's room are very mathematical/science-y but the ones closest to his bed are more spiritual and ghost related...interesting.) The game does a great job putting you in the physical realm of an off-putting hotel, right down to its "Shining" inspired carpet (a nice touch).     Secondly, the sound design is wonderful. With nary a single jumpscare (kinda), the game really puts you on edge with random floorboard creaks in rooms you aren't in or window shutters slamming shut. You never truly feel safe walking through the halls, despite the main character, Nicole, having been raised here. It feels as alien as any random hotel you could hope to stay in and really does make the player feel uneasy. Also, the dialogue between Nicole and Irving takes a few in-game days to grow on you. I was genuinely involved and cared about Nicole's character.     This is the end of the compliment section of this review (lol). So many things made up this story that never payed off, in my opinion. The game leaned heavily into the supernatural and it felt like there might have been an ending in mind that made better use of those elements. You discover a team of ghost hunters visited the hotel and were spooked off (allegedly by the ghost of Rachel) and you use the parabolic mic they left behind to listen to actual whispers and other spooky sounds. You father, Leonard, is apparently a brilliantastro-physicist turned occult-dabbler and I honestly believed that maybe Rachel was still alive between dimensions or some sort of Schrodinger induced existence (Leonard alludes to this possibility by stating that stars can exist to us and be dead at the same time; we see their light, even though they are long dead).    There were certain sections of the story that made absolutely no sense to me. You discover that Irving was actually not a FEMA agent at all, but rather, Rachel's brother that you forgot about and he has been luring you around the hotel to discover the truth that he somehow suspected but also somehow needed you to uncover? And then once realizing the truth, that Clair (your mum) had killed Rachel, he accepts the truth and...kills himself? What? Even Nicole suddenly attempts to kill herself (which you can either stop her or let her, the ending doesn't change but the dialogue for stopping her is nice) which feels completely out of the character we spent the game discovering. There are also certain sections of the hotel that felt like there was more planned, but went unused; strange symbols in the crawl spaces that felt intentional but weren't used anywhere else and a doorway that went to a ski lift, but was unaccessable (to the best of my knowledge).     Now my main gripe with the story: the pedophilia. The game makes no attempt to paint Leonard as such. Nicole and Irving both paint Leonard with rose-colored glasses, as the poor, brilliant man with plenty of weaknesess but dangit, he just had so much love to give. Even Claire, the mother is ultimately made out to be the villain here; she was the jealous wife that couldn't handle the affair, not Leonard, a grown man who impregnated an ambiguously handicapped teenager and then made a shrine to her, complete with retainer and rocking horse.      I want to like this game and I think I ultimately do, but the ending left such a weird taste in my mouth. Where Firewatch left me with a "gotta carry that weight' feeling, TSORF has me wondering if there wasn't more of the story to carry.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a mystery walking sim where you play as Nicole, a woman trying to investigate the mystery behind the suicide of Rachel Foster, a classmate who had an affair with her father. The setting of the game took place in the big, empty Timberland Hotel, where she cannot leave because of the bad weather. The hotel is beautifully designed, with some parts inspired by Overlook Hotel from The Shining. Despite the look and tense atmosphere of the game, I wouldn't call TSoRF a horror game, as there are no explicitly scary moments.TSoRF has an interesting and tense mystery story, however the game is kinda short (finished it in 4 hours). Many areas of the hotel are not used optimally as well. Technical issues are also present. I finished the game in 3 separate sessions, and each session I have to manually end the game from the Task Manager because it won't close. I'd still recommend The Suicide of Rachel Foster, but don't set your expectations too high. Honestly, I think this game could be better if it had more horror/supernatural moments, as the environment provides a good set-up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed this game. I also find the reviews saying the game romanticised certain topics a bit unfair.  In my opinion it is very important to differentiate what you are seeing (what the game is showing you, form your own thoughts and opinions based on that) and what you are hearing (who is talking to you and why would that person feel a certain way about a certain situation). Nothing is coincidental. These things combined is what makes this game so special and daring, especially since it is about such a sensitive topic. It captures exactly how people deal with different experiences, point of views, trauma, denial, ... it makes the game very human and in my opinion it's that which makes the game so scary and confrontational.I do however agree the game is definitely not for everybody. As I understood it they changed the trigger warnings, which I think is very important and I am happy they did so. If you are sensitive to certain topics I would advise anyone to look into the story, inform yourself and decide based on that if it is something you are willing to experience. **Spoilers**By what you are seeing I am referring to the shrine (Rachel's room). It is clearly a children's bedroom, maybe even a bit too much so considering she was 16. Based on my own experience, when I was 16 all I wanted was 2 be *grown*, I had no interest in teddybears and things like the horse toy. Maybe she wasn't allowed to make any changes to her room, which could explain how Leonard was able to manipulate her. Tell her how he saw her as an adult, while nobody else did, eventhough we know she absolutely was not an adult. There could be multiple reasons however as 2 why her room looked like that. We don't know anything about Rachel's side of the story, so it is indeed purely speculation. However my first reaction 2 seeing the room was that it was clearly a children's bedroom. It emphasised Rachel's age to me again and how sick the whole situation was. There is also the multiple pictures/paintings of wolves around the hotel, a predator. By what you are hearing, Nicole explains how *grown* Rachel was but in the same sentence described her wearing a bow. A bow is usually something worn by children. I think it's important as a spectator to pick up on that since Nicole is describing how she remembers Rachel. Yes Nicole could of made note of it now as she looks back on the situation, but this is where the denial etc comes in. We have to remember that Nicole is a daughter, who once loved her father and looked up to the man. It is very hard to accept somebody like that could of done something so vile and disgusting. It Is far easier to try and justify something in your mind or even just straight up ignore it. Murderers/pédophiles/... are in the end people who also lead lives, often have people that love them etc. It's this what I was describing when I said the game is very human and that this makes the game so scary and confrontational. It's not something we want 2 face. It's far easier to think of them being monsters.Also Irving explaining it was love. Irving spend years in the hotel with Leonard. We do not know why. Maybe leonard was the only one willing to believe Rachel did not commit suicide? Maybe Irvings parents dismissed the idea completely and with him finding only support with Leonard, that could have lead him to being manipulated himself. Leonard could of convinced Irving it was indeed just love. We as spectators however know it is not.  Again this is just my opinion and how I experienced the game. I could be completely misunderstanding but based on the points mentioned I do believe the writer did not try to romanticise certain topics nor do I believe he was forcing a certain narrative upon us.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an entirely enthusiastic recommendation, but overall I feel the good outweighs the bad.Positives:-Graphics-  This is an almost flawless realization of a partly run-down mountain hotel.  I cannot rave enough about how wonderful the environments and overall feel of the game is.-Atmosphere-  This game completely nails its atmosphere (up until the final chapter.....).  The sound effects, combined with the dialogue and graphics, make you feel 100% like you are exploring a partially dilapidated, almost certainly haunted hotel, which may or may not have someone other than yourself living in it.  The game drips spooky, unnerving atmosphere.-Writing/Plot-  Up until the last chapter, the game is damn near flawless (unless you can't get over the fact that the protagonist's father had an affair with a sixteen year old classmate of the protagonist and thus the family broke  my opinion it's creepy and grossly inappropriate behaviour {probably qualifies as statutory rape to be honest}, but it doesn't really qualify as "pedophilia" as some reviewers have referred to it as in their negative reviews) in moving the plot forward and allowing us to feel the characters and their motivations.  It's not Firewatch good (that's a damn high bar!) but it's still pretty good.Negatives:-The Last Bloody Chapter-  There is a final twist (and then an even further dark turn during the denouement) that just plain old doesn't work.  It almost ruins the game (note that I'm talking about ).  And then there's the final scene, which while on the one hand is refreshingly dark and bleak, is on the other hand rather inconsistent with how tough the character has been thus far, and would accomplish absolutely nothing, even if she is convinced that .  It's almost senselessly grim and depressing, which would ordinarily make it my jam, but it just really doesn't work here.In the final analysis, this is a (mostly) well-done first-person exploration game with heavily creepy, possibly supernatural overtones that runs superbly before it stumbles as it tries to cross the finish line.  Still, I can definitely recommend the game.
