_childDocuments_.review: Let me ask you two questions. Do you like Firewatch? Do you like What Remains of Edith Finch? If you replied 'yes' to both - then you should be buying/installing/playing The Suicide of Rachel Foster in this very moment.Oh, you still here? Want to know more? Okay... TSoRF combines various things we love from aforementioned games. For starters, there is a big empty house to explore (actually a hotel, but it was home to the protagonist), and it's wonderfully designed. You'll have this particular feel of nostalgia while exploring it, thanks to exemplary use of music/sounds and requisites from '90s, among other things. Moreover, the environment has astounding amount of details in service of telling a personal story of a family torn apart by tragedy.With a blizzard raging outside, it can be scary to explore the vast building in mountains on your own, especially when power is going off and you are left in the dark. Mysterious sounds of wind, walls or floors also play major role in giving you the chills. However, the game is no horror and there is nothing supernatural in it.Fortunately, you are not entirely alone in this adventure. There is a friendly voice on the cellphone, guiding you through the hotel cut off by snowstorm and soothing Nicole's loneliness (and your anxiety). He gives you advice and lets the protagonist express her feelings. With stellar voice-acting, well written (and interactive) dialogues and charismatic characters, evolving relation between Nicole and Irving is no less interesting than the one of Henry and Delilah from Firewatch. And that means a lot.All in all, however, TSoFR is far from greatness of What Remains of Edith Finch. Repetitive walking around the same places in the hotel can be boring (particularly when it is unclear what you should do next in this 'open world' to push the story further and the plot's pacing gets ruined, especially considering Nicole's moving soooo slowly), also characters sometimes talk too much. And there are some minor technical problems here and there, with poor optimization on top of them.Anyway, to sum it all up, The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a solid adventure game and a brilliant thriller. I strongly recommend it, especially if you like titles that are not afraid of picking up on difficult subjects and use them with care, to enrich and deepen the story. TSoRF is a strong competitor in this territory, and this reason alone should be more than enough to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much promise as a story about delving into a dark history of a child's family secrets, however absolutely fails to deliver any semblance of themes or messaging. The pacing is terrible: you don't learn anything about the main story for the first half of the game, and then suddenly everything is revealed culminating in an unsatisfying and borderline disrespectful ending. The "dark themes" that this game promised to present are never truly explored, and the sensitive elements of the story are hardly addressed. Even worse, when they are rarely discussed it is with a startling lack of awareness and respect. (I'm looking at you, nude sketches of a 16 year old girl). I've seen people praise the setting, and again it had a lot of promise, but the hotel is so poorly designed that it feels unbelievable that anyone would design it like this, and you just end up getting lost in the senseless corridors. It feels like the game can't decide whether there is a paranormal factor or not, as ghosts will be hinted at, and then forgotten, only to be brought up at the end. I honestly cant decide if there actually was a ghost. If it was meant to be mysterious or ambiguous they just failed to deliver it because it came off as sloppy. Don't waste your time and money- if you want to learn the story just watch a let's play on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: It was okay.  It started off with a pretty heavy "The Shining" vibe and it was constantly hinting that it was going to be scary but never really got all that scary.  Which is fine given the theme and intent, but I think they could have taken the tease a little further.  But it's not necessarily that kind of game so it's all about story and that's my main complaint.  In a psychological thriller though I think it's important that the characters' reactions be believable and the in the end, for me at least, the main character goes WAY overboard in reacting to the events of the story just to make the conclusion extra dramatic.  It wasn't at all in line with the type of person she seemed to be as I was playing.  The whole story just came up a little flat at the end in my opinion.  Lots of sudden revelations at the end that seem to come out of nowhere, lots of stuff that seemed to be interesting and important at the beginning that turns out to be completely irrelevant.As a game there's not much to it.  There are no challenging puzzles or anything like that, it's mostly just a matter of wandering around the environment until you show up at the right location to trigger an advance in the story which can be a little frustrating.  And fair warning:  there is one part that relies on auditory cues if that's an issue for you.Oh!  I almost forgot!  You can get all achievements in one play through and I would have except I chose not to flirt with the dude who I was pretty sure was a creeper who was stalking me .  So that's kind of weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very big on short, narrative walking simulation games like What Remains of Edith Finch and Gone Home, and normally it doesn't take much to invest me in the story and evoke some sort of emotion (normally tears) from me, so I fully expected to be a blubbering mess by the end. Unfortunately, this one missed the mark and just left me feeling unsettled by the subject matter and how it was tackled. There are some good aspects, such as the environment, voice acting, and methods of moving the story forward, and I think that this could have been really good with some tonal shifts and fleshing out, but instead they chose to (SPOILER) Pros:- Great atmosphere that's both beautifully done and eerie- Nice sound design- Straightforward controls and story mechanics- Excellent voice acting- Creepy vibe, but nothing too scary or intense (for those like me who like it more chill)Cons:- Iffy storyline that is handled tactlessly- Not a lot to interact with that would flesh out the environment- Short playthrough - about 3.5 hours (this is actually a plus for me since I like short games, but I'm glad I got it in a bundle because I wouldn't have been happy paying full price for the experience I got)I wish I could rate with stars rather than an all or nothing rating, but I suppose I would say it would be worth a play for the pros listed because overall it was an interesting playthrough,  but I would definitely wait until a sale or a bundle, and if you really feel like dropping $20 on a narrative game, go with What Remains of Edith Finch instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The tag of "Walking Simulator" describe the game the best partially due to the fact that you can't sprint too fast which actually quite makes sense for a 4-hour-long crawling like a turtle walk-through experience to build the atmosphere.The story and the way in which it's trying to tell don't satisfy me at all.First of all, the whole story is boring and really old. _childDocuments_.review: It's a shame that you can only leave Positive or Negative reviews on Steam, because this would be a perfect middle ground. But if I have to go out on a limb, mine is negative.This is because, as a player, I didn't appreciate the way the story developed in the last parts/"days", not because of the themes that were dealt with (I think it's a mirror of certain realities and I think it's right to talk about them even in video games), but because of the way they were explained to the player.For example, SPOILERS will follow:CONS:- I didn't like Irvin's character. He changes his attitude from one moment to the next, without making the protagonist suspicious. I think Irvin's character is the weak point of this game, the problem is that he is the only person besides the protagonist we can relate to. - Another thing that really bothered me was the beginning of day 8 when the protagonist wakes up in the church. In this "day" she doesn't say anything, you can't access the inventory, there are no barks from the protagonist waking up in this church and everything seems normal. The problem is that neither the protagonist nor the game tells you what to do, and so you wander from room to room looking for something to do, until you try to go to your bedroom by exclusion (or logic?), and then you retrieve the inventory items there and call Irvin to explain what happened. It would have been really useful to have feedback from the protagonist, both narrative for what happened and gameplay to get to her room Jeez. - Finally, the thing that annoyed me the most was the protagonist's walking, which was extremely slow. Since it is basically a walking simulator, I would have preferred that the main action (walking) could be made a little faster. This is because crossing the entire hotel walking slowly (the sprint exists, but it's basically a slightly faster walk) turns out to be very frustrating.PROS:- Despite everything, I extremely appreciated the sound aspect of this game and the setting full of details of lore and books to read. It would have been very nice if all this exploration had been useful on a narrative level, instead of satisfying my mere need for curiosity. Many of the books that are out there want to wink at the paranormal/mystical/scientific aspect... but I think there has been a bit of confusion. I mean, maybe less was better?CONCLUSIONOverall, it's not a bad game, but I think the ending is a little disappointing, not very coherent, very absurd and a little crazy, like Irvin's character.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE walking simulator/visual novel type games. The Suicide of Rachel Foster is uninteresting and hard to follow. Figuring out the next step is near impossible in some sections without using a tutorial as they are nonsensical. With all of the hidden corridors and pathways (that are not able to be added to the map), it's very easy to get lost.I don't feel any emotion for or connection to any of the characters outside of annoyance with the mains. Weird behavior of them to to flirt constantly while investigating a dead girl they were apparently both close to. It doesn't feel like either of them have any care for the situation at hand. Voice acting leaves something to be desired. The main character has a funky forced transatlantic accent at times but speaks casually at others which is super annoying to me. It's cringe not quirky. Irving is fine but his script is still terrible.Had to close and restart the game multiple times due to game freezing up during cut scenes. Movement and dialogue are very slow. I'm all for exploration type games but there's no reason I should be able to pick up and observe random objects like pens and books but only be able to manually zoom in on interesting elements like actual  notes and photos.I would like to see Rachel and Leonard as more fleshed out characters rather than "pedo dad and child victim". Rachel is simultaneously portrayed as an adult woman and very young child throughout so I'm just confused and disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: Some players say the issue is unethical, yes that's true. It is a game whose subject develops within the framework of unethical events and hidden facts. The graphics are fine. The game is a bit short compared to other horror games, so I think the price is too high for this game, but it is a game that deserves the price when it is on sale. Even though the subject is not ethical, it is really beautifully fictionalized, and on the other hand, I had the feeling that I was watching a horror movie. In addition, I think he makes a nice finale with a surprise ending that is different from what is usually predicted.In terms of gameplay, the character does not have movements such as bending, jumping and the character progresses very slowly even when running. When I was going from one place to another in a huge hotel, I sometimes felt that I was just running. Even though it is a bit boring in places, it immediately draws me in afterwards. As some of our friends have stated, the sounds in the game are prepared in a way that you cannot find in every game. While playing with headphones, sometimes I couldn't tell if the sound was coming from the game or from the back room and I looked back. In addition, unlike other horror games, it can put the player into the mode without any jump-scare. As a result, the graphics are nice, the gameplay is not bad, the sounds are great, the fiction is well formed. If you do not play, you will not lose much, but especially for those who love the genre, you will spend a very enjoyable 4 hours with a discounted price. So it is recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mystery walking simulator game with creepy elements in the mix that has you play through a story full of grief, darkness and eeriness. This is about a woman (the protagonist) who inherits an abandoned hotel from her father in which something dreadful happened in the past. No, this isn't a ghost story, there are no jump scares and no heavy horror elements. But it is dark. It deals with themes of grooming, ephebophilia and suicide. The plot itself has a few twists that get unveiled near the end which improve the overall experience quite a lot. At the very end you'll have to make a choice between two options. Neither give you a good ending, which, again, emphasizes how dark this game is. It also is a very short game depending on how fast you can play through the "puzzles", but for a 2 euro game, getting about 5 hours of enjoyment seems like a fair trade.Now I want to address some of the hate this game gets. I understand how people might not enjoy walking simulators or the absence of other characters for you to interact face to face with, but the far leftists who come here saying this game DEFENDS those dark themes I mention above have no idea what this game is about. At no point did I feel like the main characters were defending any of it. If anything they were as disgusted by those themes as a normal person would be. As normal players who pay attention to the story are, in fact. So, ignore the extremists. This game is a truly enjoyable experience that will have you think about its plot and endings for a bit. It also won't drag on which is always positive.

_childDocuments_.review: 2023 REVIEWThe suicide of Rachel Foster is one divisive game. Some people like it, some hate it. I've played it 3 times so... I kind of like it! And not... read on!FIREWATCH WANNABE?The game is very derivative of Firewatch. It has all the main ingredients - an opening in text, a remote location and above all a walkie talkie with two people who only have each other's company.The characters are flipped, we now play as the woman Nicole and listen to the man Irving. These characters start off very awkwardly, but they do grow at least somewhat in the span of the story - even if it's not as good as in Firewatch.Being derivative of Firewatch is not a bad thing though since I love Firewatch.WHAT REMAINS OF EDITH FINCH WANNABE?The game is also reminiscent of What Remains of Edith Finch. A girl that inherits a house and comes to unveil its secrets, and there are crawl spaces in the house. How original...GAMEPLAYThis game is a 100% walking simulator. There is no bad guy, no survival horror, no complex puzzles just walking and talking and finding your way around a hotel. You have some dialogue options, but seemingly the impact is rather low on your dialogue choice. This is mostly just one story.SETTINGThis is where the game truly shines! The game takes place in 1993 and refers to events happening in 1983. Its only playable on Epic setting with a good PC, but the game does look quite good! The game takes place in a hotel which is basically The Overlook from the Shining, but all alone. Nobody has been living there for years except for your dad who passed away a few years ago and left it to your mother who dies in the opening of the game. There are several wings, dusty maintenance halls, offices and two full floors of hotel rooms.You never go outside, but you can "glimpse it" in a way through the windows. The game also takes place sometimes at night and in spooky hidden compartments.STORYThe story is in many ways absolutely great in the majority of days (I won't spoil how many) until the last day. You, 26 year old Nicole, the daughter and only living heir, go there to check on the hotel before selling it after having just inherited it. It hasn't been in use for years, but is still operational.Unfortunately it happens to be snowing and you are snowed in upon arrival, and you lose your car keys. Fortunately the FEMA agent Irving starts talking to you on the phone located in the Master Suite where you used to live while staying in the hotel as a kid.Memories start to come back, how your family was crushed after your father groomed a 16-year-old girl Rachel, who people saw as having an "affair" at the time. Rachel commited suicide and the disaster tore the family apart 10 years ago when Nicole was 16. Irving, the FEMA agent, had been to the hotel when your father lived there in you and your mom's absense and talked to him over the years before he died.This leads to a drama between you and Irving where he has knowledge of your father and you also depend on him for conversation since the phone lines are down and you are all alone.ISOLATIONThe first days are amazing! It's just you dealing with how to survive in an old hotel while being snowed in. It's a cozy, special setting where you just want to lock yourself up in your girl's room instead of being in the huge spooky hotel. It's you and your thoughts and the mystery of what happened really between your father and Rachel.You talk about family, isolation, love and fear, but mostly about Rachel and her death and your father.This is not great though, but the setting makes it better than it should be. It's a thrilling game where you truly get to know the hotel, and the sound effects are great! The dialogue  is where the Firewatch vibes truly fall apart, but as a game about isolation and spookiness in the first days I think it's great!CONCLUSIONAs a thriller about isolation and walkie talkie therapy mixed with exposure therapy in a hotel It's awesome! The ccharacters do grow even if their chemistry could have been better. The game is quite long to for a walking sim, around 4 hours, and only really the last 40 minutes are bad. You get a good 3h 20 minutes and this game is almost for free on sale.I'd say get it and try it for yourself!As for the ending.... well... Spoilers below...**********SPOILERS**************The last day... absolutely blow.The entire ending is one big horrendous slog. New clues are just thrust into your hands and the big shock can be seen a mile away. The finale "shock" comes in the form of repressed memory - like what the ♥♥♥♥?! Everything you did no longer matter, you just needed to un-repress a memory?It tells the story of that Irving somehow used you to pull that memory out, but that is simply not true and not how memory works at all, it's stupid. Your mom just happens to die while it's a blizzard? Does that make any sense? How is this planned?!You say that "OH MY GOD IT WAS MY MOM WHO KILLED RACHEL!!!" which... makes no sense at all. Rigor mortis anyone? She was supposed to have fallen down a cliff. There are so many plotholes you could ram the entire hotel through them.The whole shocking finale is really, really poorly made, poorly structured and poorly told. They basically copy the ending of Firewatch which is super obvious, but doesn't tie into the rest of the game. Irving was hiding in the hotel all along using you? Man it's dumb.Then Nicole commits suicide, the end. WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥?! She was not depressed at all in the game. Why does she do this?!Ugh... the entire ending just suck. Awful, awful, awful.CONTROVERSYThe game is often stated to condone paedophilia. I kind of see it as it is a story from 1983 in a small community. Lots of gossip etc. and we never ever know anything about Rachel. This is where the game truly stink, it is mostly told through the memories of Irving and Nicole, and some minor newspaper clippings that tells... nothing? There truly is no story to the game, it's a story of isolation and people meeting over the phone, all other character's voices are absent.You never come across Rachel's diary, but you really only get to know anyone else through Irving and Nicole's perspective. This makes the title character... not the main character at all.Now the game does use weird wording since there are some minor notes from Nicole's dad about love etc. and newspaper articles about "the affair" and the mom also talk about "the affair" but that's because the mom is the bad guy of the story. Many people on YouTube has gotten hung up on this, that the writer of the game don't talk about grooming and sexual abuse (the warning label in the beginning about grooming was added later). You also only got the ending achievement if you chose the suicide option... that is pretty messed up.Ugh... I more see the game as a mess than anything else. The last day absolutely destroy the entire game, but the first few days... they are great!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the love child of Firewatch and The Shining.  Set in the 1990's, a woman goes back to the hotel her parents owned and that she grew up in until her parents divorce. The past suicide of her fathers mistress leaves an unsettling air, especially when it constantly feels like you're being watched throughout the game. Due to a heavy storm, you're not able to leave and must stay alone in the decrepit hotel, piecing together pieces from your past while interacting with someone trying to help you through a primitive walkie-talkie type cellphone. The setting for this game is incredible, I'm a big fan of Gone Home and Firewatch type games where you can wonder through areas, picking up and looking at things as long as you like and this hotel is huge. It's structured very well and actually feels like it could be the blueprints for a real hotel. Sometimes I boot this game up just because I enjoy the atmosphere walking around the hotel. The story and puzzles don't really take advantage of the incredible setting, however. For every large intricate room you explore, you maybe have about 5-10 minutes of gameplay max. I like walking simulator type games that are focused on story rather than puzzles, but I feel like a big part of the hotel was either underutilized or irrelevant as nothing happened in several rooms I explored. I wish that this game was expanded and extended with more puzzles and events happening. Overall I loved this game, but recommend buying it on sale for the length.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING - THIS REVIEW MIGHT CONTAIN SOME SPOILERS - SO BE READY AND STEADY FOR IT:In a world where people encourage others to appreciate the past, sometimes it is better to forget it all. Unfortunately, forgotten memories might become a blessing, and the more someone unveils, the bigger a curse might occur in someone's life. That is not the only sad thing that strongly impacts our world. Another thing we forget pretty often is that not all relations between people are as healthy as they seem to be. Also, not every new connection might be what it looks like, but all of that depends not just on accident but a hunch and best of luck which some of us possess and some might not."The Suicide of Rachel Foster" seems to be one of those games where the more we move on, the further we walk through the past events for a better understanding of the present time. While our protagonist, female, seem invisible to us, all her experiences, connections and places where she grew up are well visible through the richly created interiors, possible for hours of exploring, without any focus on the main plot. Yes. All the elements of an old hotel building, walls, rooms, decorations and details are the only positivity in that game, making it worth buying. However, the "worth" and any value end when you want to start analyzing the storyline, plot, and consequences that the protagonist will have to face due to her choices and interactions. So let us focus on those for a moment to understand better the problematic nature of this game itself.First of all, the protagonist arriving at the old place of living, although many years had passed since she lived there, had no clue about the region's weather conditions or the proper preparation for the weather alerts. More illogical in the decision making also becomes the fact that after picking up the randomly made to her phone call, she listens to someone who introduces himself to her as a specific person, like a guard-keeper, we would say. Instead of verifying who truly makes the call, protagonists fall for the simple explanation and keep from having regular chats over the phone with a stranger - who, like some exemplar of a Stockholm syndrome definition - become closer to her and influential on her decisions, in the negative way of course. As the side effect, protagonist is dragged into the game with no ending and no positive outcome thanks to some stranger and phone interactions with him. The more we start analyzing the storyline from a psychological point of view, the further we see that even some tiny element of the Butterfly effect is added to the story. It is visible where, due to the interactions with a stranger, protagonists unlock such strong trauma memories that they have no other choice but to end their own lives, despite moving on. Instead of choosing for example to avoid the stranger and possibly experience a different outcome, there is only one way for passing this game, and that is done by having these phone calls information exchanges. What is more disgusting, due to them protagonist start to develop some warmth and more serious feelings toward her caller. In the "grande finale" those will be confronted with shocking truth, but still; this concept does not look healthy at all.Due to how the story and discovered pasts look like due to the investigation, players should have an option to choose the multiple variations of endings. Unfortunately, the game itself (ekhm ekhm, game creators) suggest players the only righteous path with a one-line end that will destroy pure satisfaction and enjoyment during the gameplay. Suppose we focus on how the time passes in the game and how the chronology looks. In that case, the system based on nine days of experience lacks fundamental mechanisms - such as saving the progress day by day in a way that could allow us to revisit each day separately. Instead, we cannot return to the previous one during one gameplay whenever we enter a new day. It would require starting the whole game again, without any possibility of a skip option, which makes it even more tiresome. "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" does a great job regarding the retro vibe. Indeed, all the interiors with small details such as posters, pictures, furniture and other things - does the job; it looks interesting, precisely done and worth just wandering itself. In addition, natural sounds, which are supposed to resemble the weather noises from the outside, or the typical old houses squeaking, is realistic. Those are the only things that made this game a worth purchase title for all the visually sensitive players. Otherwise, please do not make this purchase if you require a casual plot or a very rich storyline. None of those can be found here, which seems to be crazy, but it is accurate. "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" will waste your time thinking about possibilities or searching for hidden meanings. Creators have destroyed a hell of potential in that one game, leaving almost nothing worth giving it another go.Do I regret giving it a go? Yes, and at the same time, no. I like how the fictional place in this game is created and how much it resembles interiors like the one from "Shining", a movie, for example. That would match with some urban hotel exploration simulator definitely. But in that case... The situation looks way worse and shows us the lack of skill for mixing visual art with a well-made storyline. At least thanks to this game you all can learn what the game in total should not look like. "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" shall stay where it is and not be continued at all. In any sort of a way.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster has a good premise; go back to the old family hotel and uncover your family secrets. The hotel looks great and has lots of little details, and the voice acting is pretty good. That's about as much praise as I can give it. This is one of the games that lets you pick up things for no reason at all. You can pick every single damn bottle of cleaner in the hotel and turn it 360 degrees. Why? I couldn't tell you. The game tells you at the beginning to pay careful attention, but there is literally no extra information to be gained from anything you pick up. The game has arbitrary set points that ends that day and starts the next day, so if you wanted to keep exploring, too bad. The protagonist finds the clues IN BETWEEN days; you don't even get to gather the clues yourself. The game's resolution left a bad taste in my mouth and I have no idea what point it's trying to make about the main character or suicide in general. I feel bad about this review because I can tell the developers put a lot of effort into some aspects of this game but the overall execution fails.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is one hell of good story writing and intense atmosphere.Take the warnings seriously, though. Suicidal thoughts are not to be ignored. They are a serious warning sign. Get professional help.If you know anyone who seem to suffer in life, be there for them. You don't need to advice anything. Just be there. Give an honest hug.The story makes one doubt one's own thoughts. It has enough twists to keep one puzzled until the very end.The characters are written and voiced in a realistic manner. No typical stereotypes, no shallow freaking out or villain types.The map design gives off a feeling of uneasyness, with all its passageways and shortcuts, one thinks something or someone might just be behind a corner.One has the constant feeling of beeing watched. There seem to be enough hints, but there is never anyone there. Had goosebumbs for long periods durin playthrough.This game does an amazing job to blur the lines between walking through someones elses story and the immersion of beeing at this place.And then there is the end and everything is clear. (I don't know if it has a good/bad ending, though. There are some options during converstations, but I haven't tried different choices. Don't think this is the type of game for this.)[The game has these warnings for a reason. Even, when it seems to head into a supernatural direction for a while, know that the story does touch sensible topics. It may be scary for some people.People with suicidal thoughts might get a wrong impression, espacially if playing until the very end.Dealing with thoughts of death can be frightening. Death itself is a part of life. Personally, I can understand that life can seem like an overwhelming burden. A suffering one just wants to end. And that's ok. But there is no need to act on ithis overwhelming feeling.Before doing anything irrevocable, honestly ask yourself the serious question: is there really no other option? Get help. Get professional help. Don't just throw away every chance of making things better, how tiny that chance ever may seem. There is always a way. It will not get better over night, it will likely take a long journey. But even the smallest steps are steps. And let me, a stranger on a gaming platform, tell you: once you start this journey, it WILL get better. The suffering WILL slowly cease. It WILL be worth it. You and your live ARE worth it.The best way as a friend or relative to help people who feel like this, is to really just be there. They have to fight their demons on their own, but with just beeing there, you show them they can count on you. It makes inner demons less scary. Let them do the talking and just listen. Don't worry, there is no need for advice giving. If they won't talk, don't push. Don't judge. Just be there. It is ok. Don't expect anything from them or yourself. Things take time and that is okay.There is room for learning how to deal with things like that. For both/all of you. You as a friend/relative, you'll need to figure out a way of how to be there and protect yourself as well. You'll need to learn how to balance, depending of how close you are. But besides that, you don't need to do anything. Except give a hug more than usually, that goes a long way.]

_childDocuments_.review: Where does one even start with this title? This definitely is a complicated mess of a game that I would actually recommend. Maybe not for everyone, but give it a shot. I'll start with the lighter-hearted stuff.When I started playing this game, I thought it was almost a joke. Really cringeworthy dialogue between two mostly unlikeable characters, a sort of janky gameplay feel, no showcasing of what the buttons do and if you should be pushing any; don't get me wrong, I can figure out that WASD or the left stick makes your character move, but an indication that I stopped watching a part of the prologue and am actually meant to do something would not hurt. Then I start looking around and notice that the game actually feels okay when you get full "control" of your character, that the game looks stunning and things start making more sense. Really, the atmosphere, ambience and sound design of this game are breathtaking. Pulls you right into the story which gets increasingly more and more unsettling.Some questionable decisions were made regarding the gameplay mechanics. Why is there a "Observe" function that lets you spin an item around, if nothing you ever pick up reveals anything further about the object. Think you are going to turn this piece of paper around and reveal information hidden on the other side, or this artefact that is going to have a secret button, from which a key falls out? No, actually, let me just pick this trash up off the ground, spin it around a couple times and set it back down. So very pointless it actually hurt my brain.The game, at least to me, feels awkward and unpolished at times. Here are some examples. Subtitle mistakes transcript-, typo- and grammar-wise. Dark blue screen, which you remove by pulling out the map after finishing a day and waking up the next just to leave you wondering... have I been kidnapped, am I under the sheets still, is it so dark that I can't see? No, just a bug. Getting stuck in crawlspaces with blurried out vision... is it a feature, am I getting light-headed? No, just another bug. Even the descriptions, which try to be funny for some reason at times, stay where you once picked up an item that is no longer there. Cherry on top of the cake? Try very slowly walking only to the right or the left and discover the gnarly headbanging your character ends up performing.I had to replay the game in order to get every achievement. Non-skippable forced walking chats, illogical sequences of when you can actually progress the gameplay and when the game wants you to stay in a certain room for no reason other than commenting on something completely irrelevant to the story, that is bad design, especially considering there is no virtually no replay value to be found here. Once the cat is out of the bag (and this game has many of them, in fact), there is nothing to keep you going or exploring different options - there are none, except for the ending itself.Okay, now let's get to the heavier stuff and why this game is problematic, or even unplayable, for many people, as I found out by sifting through other reviews. Personally, I thought the main aspect of the game - the story - was really good and well thought out. Hear me out, I do not condone any of the hard-hitting topics this game tackles, but that doesn't mean I can't sit here for a few hours and watch a story unfold about people's very poor and life ruining choices. This is a game, not reality, and you should be able to tell the difference. A game doesn't have to (or at least try to) communicate, push, advocate or justify thoughts, ideas, anything. This game tells a story, so just sit there and listen to it because these things happen in real life, too. Tough luck if you can't take it and look the rotten nature of some people in the eyes, this game might not be for you, sure, but I'd suggest taking that on the chin. There is no need for bashing the writers and developers as if they commited these crimes themselves and as if they are horrible monsters who exist solely to ruin people's innocent little brains.As you progress through the game, the atmosphere, the writing, the dialogue, everything becomes increasingly more unsettling and you start getting this feeling that something is seriously wrong. The one big problem that I have with this game is that there are virtually no clues of what is going to happen next, which is a great surprise factor, but on the other hand not so great for making sense. Things just suddenly take a turn for the worst imaginable without you being able to pick up on any, albeit even subtle, clues that the game is heading in such a direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure a lot of effort and time went into the creation of The Suicide of Rachel Foster- I just wish it had resulted in something worthwhile. Tldr; The abject misery of enduring the storyline and gameplay denotes a negative review from me. Story: Everyone in this game is detestable. From the "sudden onset frothing at the mouth lunacy" mom to the "pedophile in twu wuv" dad to the "astonishingly moronic and conveniently forgotten" BLAH (who was literally adjacent to the keys to the car that held all of the secrets they were trying to figure out). But the worst one is Nicole. Nicole is wholly unlikable and you'll be waiting to hear her 2edgy4me dialogue with eyes destined to roll back into your skull after the very first day. I don't want to rag on the voice actress but a lot of my dislike stems from the delivery of the lines. I *think* we're supposed to be sympathetic towards her but I didn't feel that way at all- especially during the ending which was overwrought and, frankly, embarrassing.Gameplay:Most of my time was spent getting lost and running to the tune of squeaky leather (?) and other weird and jarring sound effects. The overall gameplay was essentially walk from Point A to Point B while nothing happens as Nicole grates on your last nerve and the story continues to flatline until reaching an ending that would be unremarkable if not for the way that the culmination was presented. It was somehow more disgusting than I expected even though I was aware of the sympathetic stance taken before playing the game and had been willing to keep an open mind to see how well the story was told. Spoiler alert: The story was not told well. Say Something Nice:There were two jumpscares that were effective. I liked the textures and graphics in some of the hallways and rooms. The lighting was done well. I got some good screenshots that will be confusing to anyone without context i.e. Rachel's blackboard. I also liked the Christmas tree. Conclusion:I typically love games like this- walking sims with mystery/horror elements. I can forgive a lot and often do overlook flaws in games if they provide at least one interesting and engaging aspect. I haven't played a game I've hated this much in a long time. My only consolation is that I never have to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew what kind of game this is. I was fully aware that it’s a story-driven experience without the stuff that I usually pick my games for. I played other titles that try to do the things which  (SoRF) goes for and ultimately do it much better, so I’m actually disappointed with this one.Pros:Cons:After the death of her parents, Nicole (that's you) returns to her family home. The place isn’t your typical house but a hotel instead, called , and, being the last living member of the family, Nicole now owns the place. Rather than moving into, and settling in the master suite of this very spacious and rather cozy-looking establishment, Nicole's visiting on business, doing a necessary inspection before she may sell the place. Even though it’s (mostly) functional, built at a remote location in the mountains, and looks like a perfect spot to spend an idyllic winter holiday, for Nicole it’s teeming with bad memories.Just as she’s about to leave, a big snowstorm engulfs the area, making the road treacherous and nigh impassable. Still determined to leave, Nicole heads back for her car but instead finds that her keys are not where she had left them, putting her in a tight spot, forced to spend the night at the hotel. Luckily, a friendly FEMA agent named Irving contacts her on a very retro-looking cellphone and is there to keep her company or provide help in case she needs it. From here on out, the only thing that you’ll be doing is walking from point A to point B, listening to a series of dialogues between Nicole and Irving. While you will often be presented with the option to say different things (or to at least deliver them in a certain tone), I felt like it ultimately didn't matter what I chose. I might be wrong as I’ve only played through the game once though. SoRF is completely linear. There are no two ways to complete an objective, or at least I never got the impression, nor felt like I had any say in how the story develops. The game is a walking simulator, it was tagged as one on the Steam page, but so were other games that managed to tell an interesting story and still make their gameplay incomparably more engaging than this one did.You won’t be given any puzzles to solve or be tasked with searching forany items. You’ll only be fetching things of which the position you already know or are told exactly where to find them. This means retracing and backtracking through the hotel over and over again, and while there are usually multiple routes to reach the same destination, this doesn’t do much to make the game more fun.The things that could make your time spent in Timberline more interesting is the amazing visual and audio presentation. The voice acting is just fantastic, even though I wasn’t particularly fond of Nicole's character at the beginning of the game.And it’s not just the characters voices, but the overall audio quality. I’ve recorded parts of the game and watched them using speakers as my audio output, and let me tell you right now that it doesn’t even come close to the headphones experience. . Also, I feel like I should warn you that what you hear can be pretty unsettling, and you probably won’t know for certain whether it's coming from the game or your room.Furthermore, exploring the place can be a lot of fun. These little chunks of lore will hint at certain things, if you're observant enough, and discovering the lore this way was more enjoyable than simply being taken through the story.The hotel also has a couple of items that can be held and examined from all sides, and some of those can even be picked up and used. There’s even an achievement that requires you to “get all items”, which should be an extra motivation for some of you to do some snooping around.The last thing that I want to mention is the lack of customization in this game. For a 2020 title, it’s absolutely barbaric not to feature the option to rebind controls. Personally, I have huge hands, and bending my pinky to constantly hold down the left Shift is physically painful for me, in the literal sense of the word. Not only that you can’t change that, or any other key, but you can’t even make it toggleable so that you don’t need to keep it pressed at all times. Even though most of you will be fine with the defaults, the lack of this feature is hard to justify, so the controller is probably a better way to play this one.Furthermore, you’re only able to choose between four visual presets, ranging from low to ultra. Even though ultra preset ran great on , I was stuck with effects like chromatic aberration and oversaturated depth of field that made the game look worse instead of better for me. To disable these while keeping the other benefits of the ultra preset, I had to write some code in one of the game’s  files. Here’s a simple-to-follow to do it (all credits go to the original creator). The field of view is rather narrow and often felt claustrophobic to me. This is probably just a personal preference, as I rarely settle for anything less than 90°, in pretty much any first-person game, but just like with other options, there’s no reason not to include it.One thing that I wish they hadn't done is to lock the game at 60 FPS. I’m sure that many of you that are using 60Hz monitors will roll your eyes at this one, but understand that once you get used to higher refresh rates, going back to 60 feels unbearable in some games. Again, no reason not to have the option to set custom refresh rate, especially since this game has no mechanics which could potentially be broken by having them go higher (in fact, it has no mechanics whatsoever).Even though the story – which is the primary reason to get the game – isn't half bad, it's not good enough on its own for me to recommend it. If I’m not mistaken, it also had some inconsistencies that I won’t mention here to avoid the spoilers.Going through the game would’ve been agonizing if not for my weird but rather customizable and macro-capable mouse, that allowed me to control the game more pleasantly. This, together with the fact that you can’t customize graphics settings would be enough to throw some people off, and if the game was longer than it is, I’d probably be one of them.So, despite it not being awful, it's unfortunately not that good either, and unless you really like what you see, have a thing for  influenced games, or you can get it for a steal of a price, I really couldn’t recommend .

_childDocuments_.review: A suspenseful, sad, even depressing game that creates constant anguish with its sound design. It's well done, really gets to you. I'm not sure if the game itself actually takes a stance on the morality of the relationship between an older man and a 16 year old girl that serves as the background story of the events of the game. It seems more to me that it is simply a subject of the game that isn't evaluated from the outside. One of the characters judges it as "just love", but such he would given who is is – and others take a (very) different stance. It's more of a "show, don't tell" approach, as art should be. _childDocuments_.review: Up front Rachel Foster is a pretty standard Gone Home-style narrative game. You walk painfully slow through beautifully rendered environments looking at items and having conversations with an unseen character.Where Rachel Foster flops hard is the narrative. 10 years after the suicide of Rachel Foster, a 16 year old girl groomed by the protagonist's father, you investigate the events leading up to her death after he passes away. The game's heavy themes are presented up front detailed in a letter from your dead mother who refers to Rachel as a home wrecker who split your family apart.A story this heavy could work but the game is completely uninterested in the victim's point of view. The titular Rachel Foster is a plot device that gives way to an insultingly eye-rolling series of events that sees the majority of the game leap from a ghost story to an hour of exposition on your father's actions as the plot unravels. The story portrays literally every character you come across as emotionally manipulative yet their actions are justified, yes even pedophilia, as being made out of love. The final scene basically fades to black hard cutting to credits being wholly unsatisfying.With no way to replay progress, the ending erases your save, this is a 3 hour one-and-done game with no secrets to find or explore. Avoid this game or at least play Edith Finch, Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, Ethan Carter, The Stanley Parable, and Firewatch first.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying the graphics are pleasing to the eye, and the atmosphere is genuinely creepy. I enjoyed uncovering the little glimpses into the backstory and piecing together the mystery; that being said, the compliments stop there. Walking/ brisker walking was painfully slow and clunky, very few items were interactable, and the ending left much to be desired. I believe the main character was supposed to come across as damaged and reserved, but I felt she was rude and had difficulty caring about her outcome. Ultimately, I could have forgiven some of the game's flaws if it weren't for the lackluster and unwarranted ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Suicide of Rachel Foster

_childDocuments_.review: Had I waited a bit longer post-launch to find that the basis of this story gives impunity and a sympathetic glow to a pedophile I would not have purchased this game. Normally walking simulators are no-brainer buys for me to enjoy in small chunks of spare time, but now this one's given me reason to take pause. And I think potential buyers who may be as easily put off by this as I am should be given fair warning in some way. (And to put it out there, no, I do not care what the age of consent is in Montana. Your age ends in '-teen'? You are a child.)For all the impressive graphical detail put into items and the layout of the hotel, the excellent voice talent and ambiance that provides my kind of no-jump-scare-anywhere horror, I just can't bring myself to give this a thumbs up. If this is all that it takes to impress you (and there's nothing wrong with that) then you will still enjoy the game despite its themes. But aside from the thinly veiled acceptance of pedophilia, I want to make a point that what walking simulators lack in interaction and stimulation compared to other genres, it's important that a solid, cohesive story take the spotlight. And frankly I don't think this story even knows what it's about. It tries very hard to stay a ghostly mystery and keep you guessing with clues that point in different directions just up until the end where they turn into a long row of question marks and smoke.In the end, all I can really say is there are better titles out there more worthy of the $20 price tag and your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Made me super uncomfortable, and not in a "fun spooky horror game" kind of way.Also, buggy, which is made more annoying by only saving once per day and no option to skip the dialogue. I had to do multiple playthroughs to get the final "you completed the game" achievement. This gave me some time to really think about why some people like this game, and others don't.For me personally, everything that would have made this game more fun and interesting is half-baked.Exploring the hotel? No reward for it other than looking around, being able to look at cleaning supplies up close, and getting a few more lines of dialog that don't give any more meaningful insights into the story.Ghost hunting? The sounds can be loud or quiet no matter where you are in the hotel.Choices matter? Nope. Might get a line of dialog different, but all dialog options end up with the same results regardless. Solving a mystery? Nope. You literally wake up one morning with all the clues pinned to the wall for you. And you couldn't have found these clues on your own anyway.In fact, on my second playthrough, I barely paid any attention. I was just scrolling on my phone and walking to different areas to trigger dialog. Didn't even click on the dialog options. The game just railroaded me through the whole story. The story is unsatisfying, odd, and creepy in a bad way. I feel like something was lost in translation. I don't understand how one character is universally praised by other characters when they're extremely deserving of criticism. It's not a great way to handle the subject matter. And while there is media that presents a shocking or backwards thought process without condemning it, it is odd that other characters are criticized heavily (including the victim) while this universally praised character is loved by everyone. A satisfying conclusion would have resolved that disconnect.It also genuinely felt like they didn't know what the end of the story was going to be, either. A lot of tension, buildup, and weird moments are never resolved or explained. Calling it "psychological horror" without those resolutions is lazy. It doesn't have to be a good explanation - it could be "xyz was so-and-so's imagination" but if it's never explained we just end up feeling lost.The warnings you'll see about the game's content also don't feel like they fit. It's one thing to have troubling topics in a game, it's another to shove people into first-person point-of-view traumatic experiences with no other options or ways to skip. Paired with the story leaving a lot unresolved, and criticizing the wrong people - it's super uncomfortable. It haunts you. It's not a good feeling. You're just left wondering why you did this to yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Its frustrating when a game skids so close to greatness so often to go from subtely and nuanced story to heavy handed and some things that could've been handled in a way that would've devasted you and disturbed but been a masterpiece: but instead those subjects go the whole game unchallenged, and unquestioned. Hell, even the mystery which builds up interest the game just gets bored of letting you uncover clues and decides to explain it to you instead multiple times with no room for interpretation. IT WAS ALMOST A MASTERPIECE, so often does its dark story go to disturbing places that would be perfect for the narrative to challenge the subject brought up, but instead...the moment passes, and turns out we're not supposed to question it when we very much should. The backstory events that set this all in motion are often teased but many of what causes what doesn't even get explored, in fact the biggest disappointment for this is the relationship of two particular characters from the past...which is barely touched on despite being the most important, and that dynamic being one that goes absolutely unchallenged and any nuance is projected by the gamer rather than the narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely review games and usually they have to be special in some way that makes me want to share it with other people. This case is a bit different because I think that while this game is not a masterpiece, it is a really misunderstood game that doesn't deserve to be ignored because of wrong perception. With that said, let's start talking about what this good game offers to its players.Walking simulators are usually a genre that has many arguments on it. Personally I consider this as a normal thing and I'm usually on the harsher side that thinks cautious when it comes to them. What I also think is that when this games are done right, they can amaze the player just like any other game. My personal examples are; Firewatch and What Remains of Edith Finch. These two games are among the best of this genre and guess what? This game is also has its place right there for me now. My first opinion is, if you loved "Firewatch" you will almost certainly love this game too.Let's get into the more unique characteristics of this game. The story starts when our protagonist "Nicole" goes to her now empty hotel that doesn't have a good and easy way to the city. She has to go there because her father recently passed away and she has some business to take care of. After she arrives, suddenly the roads are blocked with snow and Nicole cant get out of hotel as quickly as she wants. Then our next character "Irving" shows up to help Nicole not die with a help of cell phone (with one of its original prototypes). Our whole game happens on this haunted hotel that has secrets and backstory about Nicole, her father and a girl named Rachel that did suicide many years ago.The hotel's atmosphere is amazing and nicely designed. By the nature of it its definitely creepy and game uses this thrilling effect perfectly with its quests. Everything feels great to look at and even the little details are cool. I really loved looking to all items that had nothing to do about the story or gameplay :D. Game certainly delivers on this aspect.You can't make a walking simulator without a good story and The Suicide of Rachel Foster finds a good but wrongly told kind of story to tell to its players. But also the controversial part of the game is this vague story. The reason it is controversial is what makes this story good actually. It travels you to the mind of obsessive people. Nicole's father was one of those people and well, you can see it as you play the game. The story is all about Rachel Foster's death and the intriguing mystery that surrounds her death. It seems simple but the twists and the turn of events at the hotel are written well and I feel like even though its an ambigous way to tell what happened many years ago, it delivers that ambiguity nice. The climax of the story really feels great to uncover with all of the things surrounding it.By the nature of the story, the relationship of our two main characters was really important and they also didn't fail at this one. Their dialogues were real. Their tension was great to listen. The only thing that could be better was a little more freedom when or what to speak with Irving but it would require a much bigger game from this one so this level is acceptable. Another thing I was disappointed with was the fact that the game never used the full potential of a grand hotel that had nobody in it. The game revolves around specific places and the others are definitely left behind. Some rooms never matter and the point of putting them is just works for the creepiness level. I would love to run back and forth more at the hotel with sometihng to do. You can also do it by yourself with some limits but without any meaning, I see no reason to explore any other places than I must see. This is surely one of the biggest weakness at the The Suicide of Rachel Foster according to me.To conclude everything; even though it has some flaws, I think that this game is at the top list of its genre and if you enjoy a good walking simulator type of game, you should definitely give it a shot. Don't let the questionable reviews about morals fool you and look at it yourself. The games should be considered as games, not an example to guide the society with its content.And I think "The Suicide of Rachel Foster" is, a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mild spoilersTLDR - She knew but didn't want to admit it to herself the whole time.Longer version - I played it the whole way through, then uninstalled it.  I can tell you there is no replay value.  I'm grateful I got it heavily discounted.  It has it's tense moments but I can't really call it a horror game, it's more like a drama.  It takes under 4 hours to "beat".  If you read tones well and are genre savvy it is/seems predictable enough, but also seems to tease you a bit.  I certainly noticed that a pickaxe and axe were missing from their displays, but did the main character?  Nope.  Did I spend a chunk of the game waiting for someone to pop out with them in hand, purposed to murder me?  Yep.  And it was nothing more than paranoia on my part.  Looking at a lot of the books her father had regarding the occult, souls, celestial, ect., was there any real commentary regarding?  No, not really.  You get a small dose at the end of it all but it feels lackluster.  The background noises paired with my paranoia regarding "where did the pickaxe and axe go?" as I went along were the primary fear factory along the way.  I basically did a better job scaring myself then the game did.  They relied on the character snippy attitude and familial issues to make her interesting.  It didn't work.  Her old room has more character than here, it was also more interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster, or Firewatch: Overlook Hotel Edition, ticks all the right Atmospheric Walking Simulator boxes. Trapped in a dilapidated hotel with only a clunky mobile phone as company, our protagonist wanders the halls, driven to uncover more secrets that become more dangerous with each passing moment. And it starts out pretty great! The game does the horror of the mundane well, better than most in the genre. But the pacing leaves something to be desired, and ultimately the game gets the thumbs down because of the ending.I think that a lot of people are going to have a lot of different complaints about the ending, some more valid than others, but what I don't like is its sloppy construction. It's weirdly simplistic in terms of its storytelling, and doesn't do much to build upon the narrative that's come before. It's scary at points, but it muddles its way through in a manner that's unsatisfying.If you're fiending for a new Walking Simulator, this is a buy, but particularly if you're new to the genre, you might want to hold off until you're facing already a cold and lonely midwinter night and are looking for a ghost story to match your mood (and it's on a deeper sale).

I won't be able to fully put this game into words because it is an emotional roller coaster. In the end, the reason I am giving this a recommendation is because it's worth it to get it on sale (80%+) and play it through. It's about as long as a movie, but less expensive than going to see one.Overall, I enjoyed it. I think it could be much, much better, but I have a soft spot for what Daedalic publishes. I hope the dev team learns from this game and makes better products in the future.

This story was to tell what happened to Rachel and to uncover the truth about something that realistically could and does happen in the real world... To share a story about how horrible things can happen to the most innocent and naive of people...  This story is tragic, and the ending is just the same, ending with Nicole having some kind of Stockholm syndrome. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, I think this game is fantastic and I believe that anybody who is into this genre of games should play it. With that said, the game isn't perfect, but more on that later.As with others in this genre, this game is an interactive narrative. I hate to use the words "walking simulator" because it implies a game that lacks substance and quality. That is not the case here. Environments are exceptionally crafted and surprisingly varied despite the entire game taking place in a single, modestly-sized hotel. The story itself is intriguing and it peaked my interest right from the opening scene. I'm not a horror junkie, but they way those elements are implemented in this game are purely atmospheric, which I really appreciate; the game isn't reliant on jump-scares to earn its genre title. There are lingering feelings of dread and loneliness that are expertly paired with an unsettling sensation of being watched. It is peak atmospheric horror supported by a rich setting that feels familiar, yet still holds surprises. With that said, it's not without its flaws. First, there's head bob and you can't turn it off, which is unfortunate. Someone with more sensitivity than I for motion sickness might have problems, but thankfully by the time I finished the first section of the game I was used to it and it didn't bother me. Second, our player character, Nicole, is extremely hard to identify with at the beginning of the game because she's very angry about things that we don't understand yet as the player. As a result, she comes off as rude and unlikable. When more of the story unfolds you begin to truly understand why she is that way, but it takes a while to get there. It made me want to stop playing at the beginning because I couldn't take her attitude, but I encourage you to stick with it because it gets better. My last point, without spoiling anything, is just an opinion about the way the story wraps up. I found the way that the narrative seems to carry the weight of different story beats towards the end a little bit odd and unbalanced, such that the game is prevented from fully sticking the landing, narratively speaking. There is an attempt to make some sort of grand statement about the concepts of  that are completely undermined by the preceding beats of the story. With all that said, the game itself is an extremely enjoyable experience crafted with good intention and love for the art and industry of making games.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the outrage, but proceed with caution.This is one of those games where, after completing it, I felt relieved that it was over. I did not want to stop playing. It took me a little while to get into it, but once I did, I was along for the ride.This game goes out of it's way to set up a very dark, brooding mood. To put you on edge.Walking Simulator is thrown around a lot as a pejorative. This is a story based gamed, with interactivity coming second. Your choice don't 'matter' all that much. There are a few missable easter eggs/achievements, and a choice to make at the end. But this game is not all that concerned about Gameplay. It wants to tell a story, in it's own way. Given the nature of the subject matter, any other approach would have started to feel tacky.And the game DOES simulate walking around in a creepy, abandoned hotel, as you act out the main character uncovering some very dark secrets of her past in spectacular fashion. You can walk, very slowly, or hold shift, to walk slightly faster. The main character is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times, often to the point of being grating, but the story drops plenty of clues as to why she might feel this way, given her circumstances.A play through will take you around 4 hours, if you are thorough. I racked up seven, because I started again, to get one last achievement. There is not much in the way of replay value here. So that's what you get for your money, if you are a value conscious gamer.But it is a very intense, well constructed, atmospheric, immersive 4 or so hours. The art design is superb. The game is not a Triple-A masterpiece, but for an indie game, and maybe even setting that aside, it looks...well not gorgeous - this is a decrepit hotel. But it looks very much like that.And the binaural beats - this is the first time I had fully looked into what they were. The sound design in this game is amazing. Voice acting is good throughout. Sounds effects are on point. And every now and then, you hear a creepy little sound, like a pipe groaning, or someone scratching in the walls. With headphones on, I thought these were coming from the real world.Basically, the gameplay side of this is an experience Designed to be unpleasant, unsettling, but that is the point. The game is going that on purpose. I don't think everyone would see it that way. I got frustrated with pretty much every one of the above at some point. But having played through the game, I am glad I did, but I don't think I ever want to pick it up again.Now, the story:I don't want to spoil too much, but I have a few thoughts.The game does deal in a few cliches. Horror 'tropes'. BY the end, things do get a little...Melodramatic I think is the right word. But given the set up, the premise, and how much they needed to wrap up, I can't really fault the game for this. I am happy to chalk the more over the top plot elements up to 'poetic licence', given that they serve so well what the game seems to want to say.And what Does the game want to say?Well, there is a lot of outrage among the reviews about this game 'Normalising' abusive sexual relationships. The Dreaded P word is invoked. But the girl in question is 16. So there are other names for that. And yes, I am pulling a 'Well akshually it's hebephilia'. This game tackles some very difficult subject matter. It is far from being the first game to attract disapproval, because of moral concerns. I am sorry, though, for all the would-be censors and pearl clutchers. I get why you had a strongly visceral reaction to this game. But that does not mean you get to be loose with your terminology. If you want to condemn a game for supposed moral transgressions, you have to get your facts very straight.Does this game say Sexual abuse (Specifically, Statutory Rape) is OK?No, not even close.A lot of the out rage is about two points:The secondary character (there are only really two characters featured significantly in this game), expresses,  in flowery, somewhat romanticized words,  that HE sees what happened to Rachel Foster as a positive. to some extent at least. Not sure he is entirely happy with how it all ended. Yet this character is a victim too. Not of the same kind of abuse as Rachel Foster. But he was sheltered, overlooked. It was not hard for me to understand, from his warped perspective, why he would think the way he did. I would not say I AGREE with his perspective though. But, as the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ main character says at one point (if you choose) "I am not ten years old" - I don't expect to fully agree with every fictional character I encounter.The other problem most have is with the main character, that she did not LIKE Rachel Foster, and that this amounts to 'Victim Blaming'. But this is about a rivalry between two teen girls. At the time, Main character did not even KNOW what was going on. She was just a young girl herself. This is not what victim blaming looks like. Anyone who plays through to the end of this game and then thinks 'Wow, A sexual encounter with an underage girl sure sounds like an attractive proposition', is already damaged far beyond what the corrupting influence of ANY video game could ever hope to achieve.The game does not have a loading screen that says "Rachel Foster was a victim of sexual abuse, and that's terrible". This game did not insert a mouthpiece character, just to lecture the player about what is right and what is wrong. This game portrays a couple of very broken people, and establishes through backstory a bunch of other characters. It shows an important truth about abuse - that the victims, direct or indirect, do not often come to see themselves as victims until years after the fact, if at all. It shows that this kind of abuse does not happen in a vacuum, and that it affects everyone around it, in various tragic and insidious ways. I am reminded of the recent Joker Movie, all the Pearl clutching about how that would 'Justify' angry white man loner violence, even though it did nothing of the sort. I read an article about how Arthur Fleck had several of the most prominent risk factors for becoming a violent criminal.I suspect that the majority of people who are outraged, or 'raising concerns' about the Moral Fiber of this game have little to no experience with actual abuse. Good for them. They are just standing up and demanding that we 'think of the children'. They need to sit down, pay more careful attention, and stop shooting the messenger.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impressions: Story seemed good, didn't live up to its potential, and has one of the most nonsensical endings I've ever seen. Ruined the whole experience for me.At the beginning of the game, I was annoyed when I got constant calls from Irving, as he's explaining where things are and I already explored like an overly curious idiot... But then the game warms up REALLY well. You can explore, observe things, interact with Irving, figure out more about Nicole's childhood and context for the events of the game: what's happening now, what happened then, draw some conclusions about what might happen. Lots of mystery and intrigue during every chapter of the game, and even when things weren't entirely piecing together for me, I found myself at the edge of my seat and refreshed by the gameplay and story.This is where things get hinky, though.Rachel, a 16yo girl, and Nicole's father had an  abusive relationship because there is no healthy way for a literal child and 40yo man to be together. However, the game and its characters (even Nicole, who resents Rachel for ruining her parents' marriage) do not acknowledge the inherent abuse occurring, even when it results in Rachel's pregnancy and eventual murder at the hands of Nicole's mother. Again, yeah, let's blame the 16yo girl for being abused by a grown ass man who also held a fair amount of power over her. Definitely won't leave a bad taste in your readers' mouth, not at all! Even her little brother, revealed to be Irving, references Rachel and the dad's "love" and how he reconnected with the dad over the years over Rachel's death...instead of absolutely hating the man for abusing his sister to begin with? What???Add to this the ending, where the Irving you grow attached to outs himself as Rachel's brother avenging her from the grave so that Nicole will reveal the truth. Irving makes Nicole relive witnessing the murder and cover-up, which she'd repressed, then kills himself, basically guilt tripping her for everything she didn't do as a LITERAL CHILD. Nicole brings up the great point that her mother, father, and Rachel herself are all dead: it's time for her and irving to move on, whether that means tell the truth to the police, seek therapy, LIVE, etc. But nah, Irving says they're terrible people for not doing anything as children, and that's the problem: that children don't comprehend the terrible ♥♥♥♥ adults do and watch it happen rather than interfering bc, you know, THEY'RE CHILDREN. Basically, you're forced to either choose whether Nicole lives or dies, and she starts the process of suicide regardless, so you gotta act quick. it's hard to believe with her strong will and resolve at the beginning that she'd ever be the type to kill herself over something that happened 10+ years ago, but the writers decided to ignore that. If you choose to spare her, she does a monologue about her love for her parents and restoring the family hotel so they can all be together, and the game ends. That's it. Nothing more to it, and we really gloss over the fact she basically tried to kill herself.Oh, and don't get me started on all the stupid forensic logic this game has. A murderer will keep a key piece of evidence in her car trunk for years knowing they were gonna sell the building the car was located in? The coroner couldn't identify wounds made by a hockey stick versus a fall from a freaking cliff hours apart from each other, the latter being post mortem? Seriously? All logic goes out the window in this game.Regardless of all the trauma and drama discussed, I found this story to be overall unrealistic and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in several ways - none of them good. Again, very promising, intriguing, and terrifying as the plot thickens and game progresses, and then in the last half hour, everything goes to complete ♥♥♥♥, and I hated every moment of wasted potential. _childDocuments_.review: Its good...until its not. I love so much about this game. The storytelling and the general ambience. Its a walking simulator that gives me everything I want from a walking simulator. But...there' something off about certain things. Not the gameplay or the graphics or even how the story is told. But a very central plot point. Its not a spoiler as the game lists it right there in the description but the main character's father has 'relations' with a minor. A 16 year old girl. And for some reason the developers never came out at any point during this game to say -that- was what was wrong with the picture. It was always more focused on that the Father -cheated-. Well, yes he did do that. but with -an underaged girl-. And its just strange how they do tell you that yes, the cheating was wrong. And yes, this all leading to the girl's death is also wrong...They never find it important to explicitly call out that the pedophilia is also wrong. Hell, at some points I thought maybe it was all misconstrued and that the father had a more familial love for the girl but no, they closed that particular theory for me. So here we have a game that checks all the boxes except that the ending is...not -bad- but definitely not fitting for this game. It has a different taste to the rest of the game and gave me whiplash. And even -that- wouldn't have earned a bad review from me since Firewatch has a similarly bad ending yet I still love that game. No. Its that they never state that pedophilia was the problem despite listing several other things as morally negative. I really wanted to love this game to the end but with this major drawback I do not think I can. If that for some reason -doesn't- bother you, then maybe you'll enjoy this game. Or even if they left you with the ability to just assume these things were bad rather than calling out only certain things, I'd call it an artistic choice of the 'show don't tell variety'. "We don't have to call it out because of course its wrong" kind of thing. But they picked out some things and left -the biggest one- out. For that, I'm going to have to say no.
