_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster is a true walking simulator with minor puzzle elements, that's almost solely based on the storytelling and atmosphere. Off we go with the pros and cons.+ Pretty good, professional voice acting.+ Awesome storytelling via dialogue, exploration and reading the various notes etc. throughout the hotel.+ Really spooky atmosphere.+ Pretty big area to explore inside the hotel, coupled with a few secret passages.+ Nice graphics.+ Good audio and use of sounds, which enhances the spookiness factor.+ Great ending that will leave you satisfied. * You can walk and you can walk faster, meaning there's no running option. Kinda makes sense since there's no real reason for the character to actually run inside the hotel, it just takes you longer to explore and/or move from room to room and floor to floor. BUT the normal walking speed is VERY slow, like the speed of taking a walk outside while enjoying the scenery. I went through the game almost exclusively by speed walking. * No manual saving, just autosaving at the end of each day, meaning you can't save in the middle of a chapter. I wouldn't count this as a con, though, considering the kind of game this is.* There aren't any puzzles per se, basically fetch-quests in order to progress in the story.* A bit on the short side, considering the very slow walking speed. I finished it in about 7 hours, I guess someone could finish it in 5-6 provided you take the shortest routes and don't waste any time trying to find your way.- A bit underwhelming at the beginning storywise and atmosphere-wise, although it does pick up after the first couple days.- You do have a map, but it doesn't show where you are at the time you view it, so it's not really helpful. Just helps you understand the layout of the floors, but in order to navigate you'll have to use your memory basically.- The beginning of a particular day can be totally confusing and you could very well get stuck.  There's even a relevant thread in the discussion forum of the game.- Extremely linear. There's literally one way to play the game. The hotel can only be explored freely if you deliberately ignore the task you have at the time, because once you complete it the story moves on to another task/day.- Technical/performance issues. I had to lower the graphics to medium in order for the game to run somewhat smoothly without chopping every couple steps your character takes. Also, there is some overlapping in the dialogues between the characters if you attempt to walk or view an object during the talking and sometimes a dialogue choice will register by itself without you actually choosing it. Crappy performance is the game's biggest flaw imo, but it's not so bad that the game warrants a negative review.Solid interactive thriller that will reward you as far as the story and the atmosphere are concerned. I consider it time well spent and I definitely recommend it, preferably on sale though, as the game length doesn't fully justify the full price tag imho. Pretty good game if you're a fan of walking simulators.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: I do not recommend this game to anyone who has had bad experiences with sexual assault or similar attacks, whether personal or from a close friend.Firstly, the music and visuals for The Suicide of Rachel Foster are very well done, and you can always feel its high production value.  The game is definitely a walking sim, and takes heavy elements from a mix of Firewatch and Gone Home.  The story, like all walking sims, isn't super long, so don't expect to get more than, say, three or four hours, but those five hours make for a great immersive experience in which you play through a compelling story.  I don't want to get too much into the story, but it does get into some very deep topics, and not just the suicide that the title suggests.  Overall, it's rather well written, and I very much enjoyed listening to it play out as well as revisiting it a little.  As for gameplay, navigating the rooms is no easy feat, and pairing that along with some of the variance keeps the game feeling alive and not as dull as the walking sim names suggests to many.  There's a lot to see as you travel throughout the hotel, and many extra things that you can pick up on.  Overall, if you're not sensitive to the subject matter and are okay with a less interactive narrative experience, I can definitely recommend Rachel Foster.  However, I'd definitely recommend going in blind, as the game definitely has its twists.  I really enjoyed the narrative of this game, and playing through it was a good mix of emotions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wasted potential.  Most of the hotel rooms are permanently inaccessible, and those that are accessible are almost entirely pointless.  Examining items can burn through an hour or two of your life, but almost every item you can inspect adds nothing to the story or game.  I spent an hour reading the backs of every book I could find and, other than getting a kick out of the typos, I gained nothing from the experience.  You could simply run from objective to objective and the experience would not be lessened in any way.  That is, unless you honestly miss looking around and finding another cigarette pack, level, or sponge to pick up and twirl around in the hopes that this time your character will react.     The story is just as wasted.  It makes no logical sense at all and the pacing is so poor that the "emotional" ending wound up turning into a comedy because no effort was put in to ensure that the player supported the decisions made by the player character.  This effect was worsened by the decision to make the main character's mood highly abrasive and ignorant in the opening conversation of the game without providing strong enough evidence to justify her prejudices.  By the time we find out why she was behaving that way, too much time has passed and it has created an even broader gap between the player and the character.    As for suicide, it seems like the game just uses it as a marketing tool.  There is an opening warning for anyone that is considering the act to avoid playing this game alone, but I feel they've given themselves far too much credit.  At no point is the atmosphere of the game oppressive to the point where taking ones own life should even be considered, even if you consider it from the character's perspectives.  I cannot justify that claim without spoiling parts of the story, but suffice it to say that it feels like the story wanted to address suicide and wasn't actually concerned with trying to make sure it fit with everything else they had already created.

_childDocuments_.review: A sick mother, Claire Wilson, writes a letter to her daughter, Nicole, on her deathbed, which she then entrusts to the family lawyer, Mr. Jenkins, to only give to Nicole after her husband and Nicole's father, astrophysicist Leonard McGrath, has passed, by which time Claire is long gone. The letter informs Nicole that she has inherited the Timberline hotel that belonged to her parents and where she grew up in, but that Claire wants her to sell it after so many bad things had happened there that had made her take Nicole while she was still a teen and leave Leonard, never to return again. Bad things involving the affair he had had with a certain Rachel Foster that had ended with the girl throwing herself off a cliff. Claire wants Nicole to keep what's needed to pay off her college fees, and to donate the rest to Rachel's family. Now, ten years have passed. And Montana state law requires Nicole McGrath - now Wilson, the new property owner, to visit the property and make her rounds once before handing over the matters of sale to Mr. Jenkins. And so the game begins, in december 1993. With you, Nicole, reluctantly driving up a winding road in your car during a snowstorm to reach your inherited property in Lewis & Clark County near Helena, Montana. But as you are about to leave again, you get a call from a mysterious phone that had been placed in your former bedroom. There's a FEMA operator on the other end of the line calling himself Irving, urging you to stay at the hotel because the storm is worsening. Giving you more reason to explore the abandoned Hotel and find out the secrets it holds. Like what really happened all those years ago to Rachel. Sounds interesting, right?Not really, and here's why. You CANNOT SAVE your progress in the game until "the day is over" and you go to sleep and the game autosaves for you. This means that you have to keep playing until you reach the end of each in-game day (chapter) and cannot progress in the game at your own pace. You lose the entire day's progress if you quit the game before a day is over. This is terrible game design. Especially since there is no dynamic day-night cycle or a clock that tells you when the game will save for you. Nah, in-game progress triggers the end of a day. And if you play the game for the first time, you obviously wont know how fast or slow you are progressing. Add to this the fact that you cant interact with most objects in the game (protagonist's personal thoughts when clicking on an object, like in most point-and-click exploration games) and instead only turn the objects around in silence while examining them means it's just not worth it. Especially since the game has lots of objects in each room and you feel compelled to spend some time looking around in the hotel, studying all the objects (in silence) and even if you enjoyed doing that, like i said, you cant save the game and continue exploring from where you left off. To make things worse, you have the walking speed of a turtle and the running speed of a granny. And ultimately, this game is just a walking simulator with your Firewatch style walkie takie sending you on a goose chase to interact with certain objects all over the hotel over the course of this relatively short (2.5 hour) game, which however will last longer because you often dont know what to do next as there isnt always an objective marked on your floor plan. Furthermore, the engine does not support DSR/DLDSR downsampling, so if you have a 1080p monitor, you can only play in 1080p. And vsync kept turning off for me each time i started the game so i had to manually enable it each time to prevent screen tearing. Oh and one more thing: the game has depth of field and chromatic aberration effects that you cant turn off (there's barely any tweakable settings, just presets like low, medium, high and epic), so you will often find objects artificially blurred when trying to examine them closely. And finally, the questionable morality aspect which some people have found extremely disturbing, in that the game isn't heavy handed at all in condemning predatory behavior and instead, tries to look for blame elsewhere. And fans of horror and jump scares will also be left disappointed. So this game has literally nothing to offer for anyone except some good-ish looking graphics. Overall, an utterly skippable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Hot garbage. I've never seen a game glorify suicide before 'till this came around. Not only that, but I'm stunned, really, to see something this... insane. It's just awful. Drawing wonderful inspiration from "The Shining," "What Remains of Edith Finch," and "Firewatch" but it does nothing with those ideas and lets them mix into a muddy mess of a narrative.Pros:- Ambient noises are very nice- Hotel design is very well done and realistic- Music is somewhat interesting sometimes- Visuals are nice, but... really, that doesn't make or break a game.- Voice acting was pretty good once the MC drops the faux accent at the beginning of the game. If it is fake.... I can't tell. It changes later on.Cons:- It's easy to tell when the ambient noise is meant to be triggered and where specifically that is.- The music, especially some of the creepy ost's near the end, wind up looping and it's a little too obvious where it pauses and then starts up again.- The plot (more on this later)- Gameplay: I can't tell you how long it took for me to aimlessly wander until something triggers or I find out that I need to click on a specific thing to continue the plot. Not to mention that one day you wake up with no items and aren't given any directions. I was stuck wandering the place for thirty minutes before figuring out I needed to just pick my gear up again from my room. -Plot Spoilers ahead-TLDR: Don't buy, not even on sale. 2 and a half hour cakewalk if you don't get lost like I did. Avoid this and all the writing mistakes these people did if you want a good plot/game/whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game.As many people rightfully pointed out, this game deals with a very controversial subject - a thing I'd normally be fine with. I'm definitely against censorship and I think art (games included) should depict uncomfortable, dark, twisted topics if the creator wishes to do so. What's important is how they're handled, and how they make the reader/viewer/spectator/player feel. I felt disgusted and angry after playing this game, which again would be fine - I don't want to be blind and pretend these things don't happen. They do. But I was angry because the game's storytelling just left a bitter taste in my mouth, as it so very obviously tries to make you sympathise with the predator and leans towards victim blaming. It just wasn't handled well at all. And I'm not going to put this into spoiler tags, because this game should explicitly warn the players about it - this contains themes of emotional and sexual abuse, power abuse and grooming. I'm fairly sure it could be really triggering and harmful for people who've actually been victims of this. I'm sorry, but saying that this game 'touches on mature subjects' and a message about suicide hotlines at the beginning of the game just doesn't cut it.It could have been a pretty decent game otherwise. I ran into some minor bugs, there was a ton of typos and the headbobbing is atrocious (the devs really, really should do something about that), but these are things I'm willing to overlook in an indie game... not for its full price but in sale for 5 euro? Sure. The graphics are nice, the voice actors did a pretty good job and the atmosphere is great. I appreciate that the devs managed to make a spooky game without relying heavily on cheap jumpscares and instead used the sounds, lightning etc. But that just doesn't justify the trainwreck that is the story. Whoever wrote that the game 'manages to treat extremely delicate issues with extraordinary tact' was a moron. It doesn't. I'd even go as far as to call it distasteful. Stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: The Suicide of Rachel Foster has the makings of a decent horror game: a nice setting, good ambiance, curiosities and secrets for the player to find. What it does with those makings, however, is turn it into a story that glorifies the actions of a fictional pedophile and hold up the story of his sexual violence against a young girl as some kind of tragic romance that ended too soon. None of the characters are likeable and any of its merits as an atmospheric story-driven horror game are lost as soon as you realize how genuinely foul the story is and how contemptible the developers are for producing it. It's disgusting and vile.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed feelings about this game. I'll try and clear it up so that I can explain why I didn't like it at the end.It started out great, the exploration, the story (to an extent), the gripping moments, finding the truth about your past, your parents and everything in between. But the more you dig into the actual story the more I felt that it really just is a very...and I don't know how else to describe it other than sick messed up love story. Some spoilers regarding the story here so skip if you want to read more on the actual gameplay (which I had no issue with whatsoever): Gameplay wise it plays slow. Very slow. So slow, you feel vulnerable the whole time when trying to escape areas of the hotel and figure out the truth while just waiting for a call from a voice on the other end of a phone who's the only company you have. Short game, great initial story with a very, very sick twist and decent controls and immersion. I would honestly advise against this game because it kind of follows the same type of trend that 13 Reasons Why does and the same type of story that the Haunting of Bly Manor does. Both, in my personal opinion, are not even worth the hype. Yes there are issues nowadays facing people more prominently than in the older days, but I personally feel that my games need to stay away from real issues rather than including them in fictional works. Again, this is my opinion and we can always agree to disagree. The graphics and attention to detail is something that most of the other game development companies can take and learn from. Honestly had a bunch of tense moments in the game that had me on my toes and if you are a fan of jump scares/suspense/horror games, it could be one for you. It wasn't for me unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: It's my first review of a game ever done on steam or anywhere else and english is not my first language. I knew what this game is about. . I'am not easily off-put by serious and disturbing subjects in games or in art. I have professional knowledge in field of clinical psychology. I was curious - are the serious topics really handled poorly. There will be some spoilers, although I try to avoid specifics, but I have problems with plot and characters' building.I finished it, spend some time on hold, when I had to take care of sth and it lasted more than expected so I have a bit more on the record than I actually played - about 4,5 hours.Spoilers ahead.Why not recommend it? - The logic behind the plot is poor. Huge spoiler ahead.  In my opinion it is a very poor writing and in a solving mystery game is a serious flaw. - The characters are unrealistic. The way the main character is speaking about her father at first is convincing but fails when leading to the endgame.People who have had evil parent tend to recollect with tenderness some good pieces, and concentrate on those. They look for sth good in the evil parent, like "I wish I could play the piano, the way he/she played was mesmerizing." or "he knew how to be so charming, everyone instantly fell under his spell", "when she got mad well, that was hell, but she baked the best cinnamon cookies, I still can remember the smell" and so on, so no wonder the main character is also remembering the good things at first, it's natural and convincing. The storyteller fails to make reliable change in her when she's confronted with more evidence, places, memories of how the things really were back then. She doesn't really acknowledge the extend of his actions or condemn him for anything else than being with someone other than her mother and vaguely "ruining two families".  Also she and her mother left her father before Rachel's body was found and the revelation's about the "affair" and pregnancy was out in the open. A person who lived away from him and this subject for years would have her mind set on that even just to be able to move on The reasoning of a person who wants the main character to come to the hotel and dig into the story and how that involvement over some period of time took place is, in my opinion,  highly unrealistic. Spoiler ahead!. . - The gameplay: not much to do on your own, not much brain-usage needed. I really like walking simulators, detective staff. For example, I enjoyed Painscreek Killings, although the main plot was getting obvious pretty soon, it tied up rather nicely. But in The Suicide of Rachel Foster there is just slow walking, except from how to get somewhere - the game does almost everything for you, explains almost everything for you, not much deducing for you to do, no codes to remember, no boxes, safes, diaries with a lock to open,  just get here and there and click on specific underlined staff, the story will unfold a bit and abruptly get you to next chapter, sometimes change you're location. - The ending, there is very little choice, it's disturbing in general and for some reason I got the ending that I thought I managed to avoid.  I'm not sure why it happened but I don't intend to play one more time just to try doing one thing differently at the very end.Good sides: The hotel. The graphics are amazing, walking around the hotel without using your map is great - the staff passages and secret passages if you try to remember the right way to get to places add to immersive experience a lot. The sounds create atmosphere of uneasiness, creepy in good, solid way. Irving. A guy who is helping the main character over the old-fashioned cell phone. There are indications that there's sth to discover about his help. That is rather nicely done, not too obvious but generally possible to figure out.  Summing up:The surrounding is atmospheric. The subject of sexual abuse of a juvenile was romanticised way too much and not contradicted in a realistic way, which really hurts the game, make's it off-putting after all, uneasy in a bad way and disappointing. One anonymous hate note a character may find saying "pedophile" is not enough to address that. Apart from the subjects of different kinds of trauma - the game wants you to believe that something very obvious wasn't discovered for years. Maybe in a world in which you cannot put a flashlight you found into your pocket before "the time is right", but seems too far fetched even for that.It's a beautiful, atmospheric, badly written on a few levels game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I saw a negative review for this game, but I wanted to see what it was like for myself. I think this game has a lot of potential but falls short of what it could have been both in its narrative and in its gameplay.While this review will not focus on this I feel it is important to note that this game suffers a few bugs. Sometimes the screen will go fully dark and will not work until the player has brought up their map. Sometimes the game also doesn't respond to mouse input, though refocusing on an object will usually fix this. Also, while not a bug, the walking speed is EXTREMELY SLOW and you will find yourself permanently holding the shift key to "run" (aka walk at a normal speed). At its best the gameplay works to create a fantastic atmosphere. At one point in the game the player has to use a camera flash for light. The tension of pointing your camera to see something, anything, as you're stumbling around in complete darkness only to have to wait for when the flash becomes available again. While only seconds, those moments feel agonising and vulnerable. I have never seen a game do something like this and it is for that reason it was easy to work through the bugs because the gameplay works so well when it needs to.Ultimately, I'm hesitant to recommend this game or dismiss it outright. It's an impactful game, playing with fear and suspense well. However, I feel it may be upsetting and distasteful for some players. I've chosen to recommend it as that emotional tension, however divisive, gives the work merit. Listen to the content warnings. If you feel this game is something you could handle, give it a play. I can't say I regret it.Spoilers for the game past this point.This game presents us with five main characters:Though introduced to us as a young woman, Rachel is only 16 at her time of death. I hesitated even treating her as a character with agency in this story. Despite being the titular character, the narrative spends little time focusing on her and instead on the events and characters orbiting around her death. While I feel that the game could and should have explored her characterisation and agency more, I understand why it didn't. The characters all have their own opinions on who Rachel was, and all abuse her in their own way. The story is a tragedy, in part, because Rachel never gets her a voice.Leonard is the player character's father. The characters treat him as an unfaithful husband and father, but it becomes clear to the player that the "woman" he had an "affair" with was a child who he raped. Newspapers and notes call him a paedophile, something the player character chalks up as slander. Throughout the game, we view the world through the eyes of someone who cannot and will not reckon with the fact that her father is a child rapist. Leaving the player to reckon with this alone was a controversial move but not one that I particularly have a problem with. The game is for adults and adults  be able to traverse a game where the characters don’t hold the player’s moral framework. The game uses the trope of an unreliable narrator well. Our player character isn't lying, but we see the world through the eyes of a child who loves her father. We can see this when a shrine to Rachel is found in Leonard's basement. His daughter can't accept that her father was so obsessed with this child. She gets angry and lashes out trying to find any other explanation. While I find the hero worship in this game of such a sick man to be disturbing and upsetting, I have a feeling that that's the exact feeling this game is supposed to evoke.Claire's death and subsequent letter to our protagonist kicks off the events of the game. In her letter she refers to Rachel as a young woman and suggests that she did the right thing by killing herself.When I first read this letter the mother came across a cruel and unsympathetic woman. Through the story unfolding it is revealed that the mother killed this girl in act of jealousy and threw her body off a cliff before forging a suicide note. After learning this, the player is able to read between the lines more clearly when reading this letter. Claire is trying to absolve herself, trying to convince herself that doing so was the best thing for her family. But her guilt seeps through the pages. She later paradoxically urges her daughter to sell their family hotel and give a portion of the money to Rachel's family. This initially struck me as odd, but it makes perfect sense given Claire's role in Rachel's "suicide".Nicole is our player character. As mentioned prior, we see the world through her biased eyes. She is deeply traumatised by the events that transpired years ago. At the beginning of the story, her memory of her childhood is foggy and has many gaps. Her memory is suppressed as a coping mechanism. As we follow her through the hotel, she starts to remember more. After finding herself trapped in her old family home, she becomes obsessed with creating a narrative for the trauma she experienced as an adolescent. Some reviewers have found this change of heart to be evidence of poor characterisation, I disagree. I think it's perfectly understandable for a person who has dissociated parts of their childhood due to psychological trauma to want to find solace and answers to such a tragedy. I can empathise with avoidance turning into a desperate need for closure. What I can't understand is the ending. But we'll get to that. First, we need to talk about our final character.Irving is the only person we interact with directly in the whole game. He is our solace and, in the end, a manipulator and story weaver. The game does an excellent job of atmosphere. The game is legitimately creepy, having Irving at our side the entire time provides much-needed relief. On day eight, when Nicole wakes up in the church without her phone, having sleepwalked, it is genuinely distressing to be without Irving. The map is gone, there is no to-do list, no means of light. The player's first instinct is to scurry back to their room, the only place that feels safe. And that's exactly where the game needs you to go. Hearing Irving's voice wishing you Merry Christmas that day is instantly relieving. If I'm being honest, I saw the twist with Irving coming a mile off. But, his presence is so necessary to break up the tension that I found it easier to trust him. Like Nicole, Irving has deep psychological trauma. It is for this reason that I find his suicide so upsetting. Finishing this game left a bitter taste in my mouth. These two characters, the children left behind, all the game could offer them were two options: living with the ghosts of the past, or death. For these two traumatised victims there can be no healing and acceptance, only blame and death.There's one final part of this story which haunts me, and I honestly don't know how to deal with it. On the last day, Irving and Nicole have this exchange:The game never challenges this. The player is not allowed to offer salvation to the children caught up in this. In the next and final scene, the player is given an empty choice. Either Nicole also takes her own life, or she survives but has to continue to stay in the hotel. She is never given a chance to grieve. She must take full responsibility for her parents' actions or die under their weight. And in this dark game, for me, that was too much to bear.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this in a steam sale thinking it looked right up my alley: creepy mystery, maybe some dark drama, walking sim, clue-finding, Firewatch-esque. And in some ways it is...some of those things.What this game also is, however, is really messed up. And I don't just mean the content, cause I'm fine with some disturbing storytelling. As this unfolded little by little it just became more sick-- the entire story is woven with misogynist, grooming, adultifying language when it comes to young girls and one child's particular sexual relationship with a man 30 years her senior. And it feels intentional that these things are never really commented on as a bad thing and, in fact, are referred to as "a love like no other." In fact, other than praise, the issues are somehow sidestepped while also being the main focus? Sigh. This story is so misguided and I honestly hate that I ever paid for this game. I hope the writers have learned a few things about trauma and child sexual assault and who's really at fault in that scenario (the adult) since they wrote this.A great video essay here covering the issues in detail: Really f*cking concerning.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER ALERTthemes of child abuse and suicide. ____________________________________I quite enjoyed the game. I know there's a lot of criticism about it being a "walking simulator" which to be fair is an accurate statement, but I was more invested in the interactions between Nicole and Irving to really worry about the limited gameplay. I enjoyed exploring the hotel and I enjoyed seeing all the little details that expanded on the history of it and the family who lived there. The main criticism I have is how the developers handled the story, especially the ending. Nicole's father was in an extremely inappropriate relationship with Rachel, a minor. Regardless of the age consent laws in Montana, An adult man in his late 50's (according to the game), sleeping and impregnating a 16 yr old child is beyond disgusting and wrong. But the relationship is never condemned by the characters, in fact, they saw him as a loving and caring man, who showed affection to Rachel when no one else would. In fact, they blamed HER, the victim, for breaking up the family and the shame they endured. Nicole's father took advantage of a young girl in an abusive home and used that for his own selfish desires. That is not love, that is grooming.Even after learning the truth, they still see Leonard as a misunderstood victim when in reality the only victim here was Rachel. Everyone failed her in life, and now they failed her again in death. It's a shame. I enjoyed the experience and I'm glad I finally got to play it,  but I felt uncomfortable with the way the themes and subject matter were handled and I think it could have been done better.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to point out that this is purely a walking simulator, with zero puzzles present whatsoever and though there isn't much to say about the gameplay, the story is what holds this entire three-hour experience together as a solid thriller.If you're familiar with walking simulators, like Esther, you know how this goes: You can pick up most items and turn them around, so pointlessly so. There are a lot of smart, well-hidden easter eggs sealed away where it's not very obvious to look. Graphically, this game is solid... and everything is detailed to perfection.You take on the role of Nicole, who starts off by inheriting a huge hotel complex in a snowy mountain called Timberline. She reaches the hotel and she finds out that she's now stuck and can't leave because of a Blizzard that would last a whole nine days. Seeing as she was just there to take a quick look at the place and really carried nothing with her, she now has to survive on whatever was left in the pantry... but that's not the gist of this story. Having recently lost her father to sadness, caused by what seems to be his "mistress'" suicide, Rachel... she is contacted via a cellphone by someone called Irving; the only problem is the Timberline has got no phone line... So you're left guessing most of the time who this mysterious Irving is and halfway through you're introduced to the theme of ghosts; which, trust me, will literally have no bearing on the story whatsoever. Not to include too many spoilers, but this game fails in this aspect: you're given so many choices to make, but none of them have any bearing on the story or ending whatsoever.I kind of loved how the game ends on a suspenseful note, having you interpret the ending on your own. Is the game's narrative great? The voice acting is top-notch and the narrative has its plotholes... but can we compare it to "What Remains of Edith Finch", for the sake of examplification? No! This one relies too much on the premise that you would believe Irving to be something, right before shocking you with the truth... Except that, if you've played any Walking Simulators before, you'd have gathered the whole storyline by that point where the game makes the transition... It's a failed attempt at making something suspenseful out of something unexpected. I'll give this game a , it's short and delivers on the narrative but left so many questions unanswered by the end and the choices offered to the player had no bearing on the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to know where to start with this one. It's a walking sim, in the style of Gone Home or Firewatch, only without the charm or staying power of either.Very quickly after we get introduced to the protagonist and the "voice on the phone", who will be accompanying us through the game is where hit the first snag. Our heroine manages to come across as infuriatingly rude, while the companion character is a spineless milksop who constantly suffers her insults and permits her to walk all over him. These characters do grow a little as the story progresses, but those first impressions are bad and lasting.Lack of foresight when it came to the players pathing means that you will do a lot of backtracking, and in more than one occasion I found myself looking at a useful item I just knew would become critical at some point, but which I was not allowed to collect yet, which just exasperated the aforementioned need for pointless backtracking.The game is also rife with spelling errors, mistranslations, and in one case a central characters name was confused from "Solomon" to "Shepard". There was this persistent feeling that much of the narrative was written in a foreign language, then translated by someone with a poor grasp of English, resulting in a bunch of elements of the story being needlessly confusing and alien.Worst of all, however, has to do with the inconsistency of the world-building. We are led to understand that a 45 year old man groomed and knocked up his 16 year old student who then committed suicide. These events are all described in newspaper articles and first hand testimony, yet the fallout from this was little more than a "local scandal", indicating that apparently statutory rape is not something the locals bother prosecuting up in the Colorado sticks. This is a big enough plot point that I kept waiting for it to be addressed, or for the protagonist to be revealed to be an unreliable narrator, or some kind of reveal that would recontextualize things in a way that would make sense, but alas...So yeah, I'd honestly give this one a miss. It had some potential, and you can clearly see how it could have been better, but the bad outweighs the good here, by a significant margin.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; The game was a little dumb at times, but good overall. The storyline draws you in, and makes you care about Rachel. The biggest con: if you play this game, you WILL be disappointed by the ending. To me, it's worth playing just to get to know Irving, the guy keeping you company throughout the game, and finding out the truth of what happened to Rachel. This game does make you care pretty deeply about Rachel, but unfortunately the game doesn't offer you any way to even try to help her find justice, which is a pretty big slap in the face. And there is also a bit of a problem with pedophilia being treated like love? (But I guess the characters talking about it that way were kinda nuts so??)-I loved this game. I fell in love with Irving, and (nearly) the entire plot was so impactful. Seriously, I wanted to cry. The story is kinda predictable, but told very well and with a lot of atmospheric spooks. The only thing iiiisss...That ending. Seriously. Not the resolution of the mystery, just the ending to the story as a whole, makes me angry. The final choice seems like two bad options. There's an obviously better option, but then when you choose it, it seems like you made a bad call. But then the other option is just as bad and even more unsatisfying. It just sucks, and the ending failed to resolve a few questions. Then, after all of that, it's pretty stupid that you can't at least try the other option without replaying the whole game, especially because both endings were so unsatisfying it wouldn't be worth replaying in the slightest. But of course, let's lock an achievement behind the horrible ending that makes you feel nothing and has no value replay-wise outside of that. Okay.This game is worth playing for the experience, for getting to know Irving and delving into the past of your family and what happened all those years ago, but you almost 100%  be disappointed by the ending. Just saying. The ending makes so many assumptions about how the player is feeling, as if this ending should be sad, leaving me choked up. Instead, I'm ticked off that Nicole doesn't feel the same urgency I do to bring justice to the victims of this story. Up until that point it had done so well. But  This game gives you every reason to care about Rachel and what happened to her, but does not allow you to bring her the peace she deserves.Anyway. Rant aside. I still think this game is very good, and I still recommend it. I just wish the developers knew how to write a good ending to a good story.P.S.

_childDocuments_.review: (8.5/10)An interactive story (lovingly called a 'walking simulator') that focuses on an old abandoned hotel way up in the remote mountains of Montana.  Its a very solid entry in that style of game where the primary game play elements involve you uncovering bits of the past and determining what really led to events that caused your family to flee 10 years prior.Graphically and audio wise its really extremely well done. Having been out in these kind of remote places in real life, you can almost 'feel' what its like in there as your character walks around.  The texture work and styling is very on point and it has that combination of abandoned decay with former opulence you can sometimes get watching videos of people exploring abandoned places like this in the real world.The story is interesting/engaging but it is relatively 'on rails' with not a whole lot you can do to move things along intentionally other than walk around.  There are one or two little hidden or secret things to find but overall it is very much story first, interactive second, but that's not necessarily a terrible thing.  It does let them focus on the specific arc they have designed for you.Overall if you like this kind of more laid back chill interactive story aka 'walking simulators' like the vanishing of ethan carter, or what remains of edith finch, etc, you will probably enjoy/appreciate this as well and absolutely should give it a shot.  If you aren't as big a fan of that genre and want more player freedom and choices, probably best to skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to give this a bad review, because I think the genre of Walking Simulators gets enough bad rep as it is, but boy. Did this one leave a bad aftertaste. It gets so many things right from the start though. It's atmospheric with fantastic sound editing, has good voice acting and a superb set-up to an intriguing story. But then. Everything just falls apart. The two main cardboard characters have personalities that can change at the flip of a switch. The story has more plotholes than there are doors in the hotel. And that ending. Geez. My girlfriend and I were constantly spitballing endings that would have been SO much cooler. As far as gameplay goes, I've got one recommendation to this and all future walking simulators: either go full walking simulator and skip the gameplay elements, or have gameplay elements THAT WORK. What we end up here are horror and adventure game tropes that just don't work like you want them to. You don't need to be picking up hundred items if none of them mean or do anything. You don't want a dialogue tree if it doesn't change anything about the story. You want to explore? Too bad. We're sending you to this room and this room alone. If you wander off, too bad. There's nothing for you there. Just go back to where we sent you please. So there. I didn't want to give it a bad review, but I had to, as a fair warning to all the people that love these style of games. This will just end up frustrating you in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one thing The Suicide of Rachel Foster has taught me, it's that certain games can still be perceived as scary without being directly promoted as horror-themed. I just walked in with expectations of being confronted with a depressing narrative touching on a sensitive topic and in one way or another, that is what I got. But never would I have thought it could be THIS unsettling and terrifying, I actually froze up at times, caught up in fear of taking the next step. This might have something to do with my personal preference of being in a more grounded setting with less super-natural elements, because that is exactly what this game encapsulates. Stick with me, I'll elaborate on that statement below.The story is instituted with a short breakdown of the tragic events centered around Nicole Wilson's father, who's been involved in an affair with Rachel Foster, an underage girl. Eventually, her father's actions are exposed to the public and great shame is brought upon his family and Rachel herself, so much she decides to run off and take her life. In order to bury the past altogether and move on, Nicole's mother suggests to sell the hotel they used to run and share a cut with Rachel's family. With that being said, Nicole is involuntarily paying the hotel one final visit, but soon changes her mind to not stay there any longer. However, the seemingly endless winter storm outside and the disappearance of her car keys leaves her trapped in the walls of their family's establishment, with no one but a FEMA agent on the phone being her only guide. Might as well get some detective work done while we’re at it!The Suicide of Rachel Foster meets all requirements to pass as a classic example of a walking sim: there is walking, reading, investigating and exploring to be done. You do have a hotel map, but it doesn't point out your current location and the game is completely free of any pointers, your only clues are the notes Nicole leaves on her map and Irving’s consultation. Every time a day passes, the game auto-saves: if you are like me and plan on exploring from the moment you set foot in the hotel, you'll need to make sure to have at least an hour at your disposal, as the beginning appears to be longest portion. The hotel might be vast in size, but taking your time examining the interiors should be enough to memorize its layout, it’s rather hard to get lost. From the very first minute, there is that uncanny feeling of something sketchy in your surroundings: I mean, the hotel doesn’t even look like a rundown sh@#hole taken over by the homeless, it’s still in acceptable shape. But it’s the deliberate use of ambient sound and complete isolation that you don’t get over throughout the whole game. I just LOVE how subtle it is within its element, without ever resorting to cheap tricks such as floating anomalies or loud jump-scares. You are all by yourself and yet you’re possibly being watched or followed, as if your mind was deteriorating, along with Nicole’s. Of course, I’m most likely going to be in the minority to perceive this game that way and most will find it boring or not eventful enough, but I’d like to see more developers focusing on titles mimicking these very tropes. For a walking sim released last year, its graphics are definitely up to par and the art-direction is fantastic, with vividly bright colours and terrific texture work. The voice acting too is excellent and the actors do their best at making each dialogue feel convincing and plausible. What’s not as good is the lack of an FOV slider: yeah, you’ll see me bring that up in every review not including one, but first-person-anything should have it by default, especially in 2020. The so-called Epic graphics preset adds some lag, but don’t you worry: playing at the second-highest settings doesn’t worsen the image quality enough for you to notice, it is however the one to give you the smoothest performance. Then there is the small text on some of the documents, though that’s thankfully not as common. Not having mirror reflections is another little nitpick, a large amount of walking sims appear to “follow that trend”, but I do recall  having them! You don’t encounter any mirrors outside the bathrooms, but it is what it is. And I wish v-sync wouldn’t disable itself, every time I close the game. Most of the listed shortcomings aren’t aggravating enough to take you out of immersion and I’m most certainly hoping to see more from One-O-One Games and other developers going in the same direction: less in-the-face-spooks, more subtlety!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that fails to live up to the expectations it creates with its premise. The story feels like it could've benefited from some editing as there are typos and unresolved plot threads. There's also twists in the story that end up becoming far too obvious, while others come out of left field. Things like the professions of Nicole and Rachel's fathers are made out to be significant, but end up not really paying off. The beautifully crafted hotel is nice to explore, but being interrupted regularly by dialogue between the mc and Irving quickly became kind of grating. Be careful of day 4: there is a bug where if you interact with the evidence wall as the level starts, it'll overlap dialogue and you'll be forced to reload the level. Unfortunately due to the nature of the game there is no replayability either.I'd recommend What Remains of Edith Finch instead.

_childDocuments_.review: My overall experience with this game can really just be described as decent. There are things that I genuinely like about this game and there are things that I despise with an infuriating passion. The best way to do this review is to break it down by category:From a gameplay perspective, the game is pretty standard for an arena fighter in that most characters tend to follow button-spamming to win matches. However, unlike other arena fighters there is enough variation in the gameplay per character that each character feels different forcing you to adopt a different strategy from the standard block and attack. For me this is actually a really good thing because unlike other arena fighters I had to actually go into training mode to test out the character before playing as said character. On top of this, I will also praise the game for assigning different attacks to different buttons allowing you to string combos together so doing decent combos actually requires strategic thinking/timing unlike other arena fighters. As a result of the variation between characters, if your favorite character happens to be somebody who is a projectile-based character, but you are more centered around close-combat, you'll find that the character won't work for you at all. You really need to weigh what you value more: your gameplay style or playing as your favorite character. For a lot of these characters, you need to take the time to learn how they play since everyone in the game is unique with their own gimmick. That being said, the game is still friendly enough for new players to come in and play at their own pace.There are different game modes offered and for the most part are all decent. Arcade is your standard arcade mode where you can play as all characters through different paths, Story mode is the story of One's Justice 2 and focuses more on the Shie Hassaikai part of the anime rather than starting from the beginning, Mission mode which tried a new approach to going through each mission and levelling up your characters and online which has something for both competitive and casual players. - Is pretty standard and doesn't take that long to complete. It's nice that they have a villain side as well as the hero so it provides more content. It's nothing like the Naruto games (especially Ninja Storm 2) where you get to explore, but it's just a mode that's there and does the job. - The majority of your time will be spent in this mode and there is a lot to complete in this mode: from scouting all characters in the game to levelling them up to 99 and collecting all the symbols, the grind is absolutely ridiculous in this mode. What started off as a fun idea: scout your favorite characters, put them on a team and do a mission to level them up thus combining a fighting game with RPG elements ended up becoming the worst mode in the game. Repetition and tedious grinding absolutely destroy any fun you may have in this mode.  When you complete a mission with your group, you'll earn a symbol that can power up your character/group (additional attack, HP, earn more exp, hero coins, assists do more damage, etc.) or make completing missions easier (get rid of enemies lower than you at the start of the map, enemies do less destruction damage, take consecutive turns, etc.). There are a total of ~40 missions in this entire game and each mission can have anywhere from 3 - 24 opponents you fight against. On top of this, each mission has around 5 - 8 symbols per mission and you only get 1 symbol randomly each time you complete a mission. Doing just one of these missions is already time-consuming to do (especially the last ones where they put 24 opponents in the mission). However, to get every symbol, you have to repeat that same mission again 4 - 7 more times to get everything and it really becomes a tedious chore to do. There are several achievements tied to this mode so the bulk of your time will be in this mode especially if you are a completionist. The good news is that once you have collected all the symbols in mission mode, this mode becomes the fastest way to earn hero coins and exp to max out every other character and buy everything in the shop (costing well over 3 million hero coins to buy out all costumes, voices, etc.). 1) Equip the following symbols: Tomura fearless, Tomura confrontation, Tomura beliefs, Momo emotional and Momo matryoshka.2) Select your party of 3 that have a positive relationship with each other (viewable by the chart when selecting your party). An example that works is Kirishima, Kaminari and Bakugo.3) Play the mission "Best Agency Battle". The Tomura symbols will automatically remove enemies at the start of the map as long as your character's level is higher than theirs. The Momo symbols increase the number of coins at the end of an entire mission.In the "Best Agency Battle" mission, there are exactly 6 opponents to fight so when you have all of the Tomura symbols equipped all of the enemies will instantly be defeated meaning you will finish the entire mission in exactly 2 seconds. If you have both of the Momo symbols mentioned and you have a character that has a good relationship with your two assists you'll be able to get 3,056 hero coins every 2 seconds by simply clicking through menus and not actually playing through the mission.1) Equip the following symbols: Mirio: Face (makes you invulnerable for the first 10 seconds of the battle) and 4 symbols that specialize in EXP boosts (Gang Orca symbols).2) Pick 3 characters that have a positive relationship with each other to earn bonus EXP. 3) Play the magician map. The magician map has a gimmick where each opponent has 1 HP so you just need to hit them once and that earns you ~800 - 900 exp on your main character per round while supporting characters get around ~500 - 600 per opponent defeated. Some of the opponents you fight are invulnerable for the first 7 seconds of the battle which is why having the Mirio: Face symbol is necessary so you don't take unnecessary damage. Repeat this mission until your characters are maxed out.Just because there are strategies to earn fast money and fast exp does not make this game any less tedious and mission mode is absolutely one of those: good idea in theory, abysmal in execution type of modes. - Honestly the best way to start off the game is with arcade mode since you can play through rounds with any character you want and experiment with them the way you like. Nothing really bad to say about this at all. It's solid, no gimmicks attached and honestly this is probably the best mode in the entire game.MHA One's Justice 2 is a fairly standard arena fighter and if you are a fan of MHA you'll enjoy the game. As an arena fighter it offers enough of a variation in that you can experiment and see what character works for you, but if you are looking to just play as your favorite character, you'll find that you may or may not be good with that character depending on your playstyle. It takes a lot of time and investment in this game to learn the gimmicks of each character so play at your own pace and experiment in the way you like it. If you are not a fan of MHA, there are better arena fighters out there (especially the Naruto Ninja Storm games) and I would definitely recommend you skip out on this game. Regardless if you are a fan or not, if you are a completionist, save yourself the trouble and don't go for 100%. You'll be spending hours upon hours (well over 60) in just Mission mode alone and it is a tedious chore to grind in there. After everything, I personally give this game a rating of 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some ups and downs. If you're a fan of the My Hero Academia anime/manga, I think this game is worth playing if it's on sale. This game is not worth $60 in my opinion.62 hours and a 100% completion later, I think this game is decent to good, but not great.Campaign/Story: Like the first game, most of the story is told through still- images that resemble comic strips. A bit lazy and effortless I think. The game does have Dub and Sub, though.There are a few, but not many, fully- animated in game cutscenes for key moments in the story. These are really cool and really well done, but they happen so little throughout the story that it leaves a bit to be desired. All in all, I'd say just rewatch the anime if you want the full story experience. Only play the story for the few cutscenes, achievements, unlocks, etc..Gameplay: The gameplay is a lot better than the first game. It is more fast paced and fluid, and not as clunky and floaty as the first. I'd say one of this games biggest strengths is the roster, as each character feels unique and has their own playstyle. The gameplay isnt Naruto Storm level good, but it is decent. Plus Ultra cutscenes are a bit too long though, and aren't that flashy.Mission Mode: I think this mode will only be fun to those who really enjoy the combat to it's fullest. This mode is really grindy and can be downright unfair at times once you get to the 5- star missions. This will easily be the part of the game you spend the most time in if you really enjoy the combat and want to test your skills.  If not, this mode isn't anything special.Arcade Mode: Bland and forgettable. You chose a character and go through a series of fights, Typical fighting game stuff.Online: Online seems to be a bit dead as of October 2020, but when I did get into matches there was no issue with the netcode or lag or anything. Was pretty smooth.Overall, this game ranges from average to decently good, but not great. A huge improvement over the first game for sure, but they still have a ways to go before this can be the best My Hero fighting game it can be. The game definitely has potential, just lacking in content. Fully- animated cutscenes like Storm would be great for this game, as the story now is really bland and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Flash revised for steam sale 2020-06-20$36 is a fair price!I liked the first game, but this game is... bad. I play it a lot, and I enjoy my time with my part of the PC community, but we all wish the game was less bad.The game is not beginner friendly anymore, unlike its predecessor. It's about memorization. Make sure to pick the best characters or the game will not be fun, because matchups are also important!There was a core gameplay which was largely intact in the first game, where each option you could take in battle had advantages AND risks, and those risks were clear to the other player. But that's not true anymore; the risks your opponent is taking on are invisible and only revealed through experimentation, if indeed there are any risks at all to what they are doing. And that invisible risk profile for each moveset is different for each character and how each person plays each character, so I hope you like homework.The game is fundamentally evasive and defensive. The optimal strategy is to run away. Imagine designing a fighting game where the optimal move is to not fight? But since we're all here to play a fighting game, if you run away on health advantages, you are cancer, please uninstall. You are not smart for figuring out that this is the best strategy; everyone else already knows that but plays like a civilized person instead.They added more mechanics to this game which not only muddle and complicate the core gameplay, but now the core gameplay is totally inconsistent between different character matchups. Without even leaving the topic of unblockables, I can list off the top of my head:-Dodgerolls work against old generation unblockables as expected (moves ported over from the first game), but only work against new generation moves with a particular timing-Some unblockables can be parried, yes parried, unless they are performed at the perfect distance-Some unblockables are essentially impossible to punish unless you have a projectileIf you were looking to buy this game hoping that they had cleaned up the rough edges of the previous game's system, they made it dirtier. Perfect guarding is in the game but it's a mystery when and where it can be done, and it is very difficult to do even in controlled tests. Some moves have lingering hitboxes, so even if you dodge, you can't punish or you'll be hit by the move you successfully dodged, remember to memorize those and exhibit patience when they appear.Characters are a tragedy. The gap between the top characters and the worst is huge. The previous game was a hopeless ocean of Shoot Style Dekus and Endeavors, but with 41 characters in the base roster, now you'll encounter mostly Mirio, SSDeku, 100% Deku, Overhaul, and Shigaraki2. Mirio's exploits have been fixed so his popularity is declining, but even now his permeation can actually be cancelled out of. SSDeku is as annoyingly boring, brainless, and strong as ever. 100% Deku I'll let others tell you about. Overhaul can only be dealt with by certain characters. Shigaraki2 does unholy amounts of damage for no good reason. Be sure to memorize which of each of these characters' moves in which situations are safe or unsafe against which responses from which characters!Weak characters like Fatgum still have no tools to haul themselves over to spammers like Todoroki or Inasa.They raised the skill ceiling, but not actually to anyone's benefit. I'm referring to the sidekick system; if you study the arcana and learn how to use sidekicks to extend your combos you are rewarded and become a more dangerous player. There are only ~4 sidekicks who are useful to this end, so only pick Jiro, Bakugo, or Rappa, everyone else can go home. The existence of extended combos means that: where in the previous game, a newer player's odds of winning against an experienced player were not so bad, the chance of posing any threat to an experienced player is now very small.The sidekick system is further broken because they can be used as reverse cards. If the enemy has a support out, they can do whatever they want and if you punish them or outsmart them, it doesn't matter because suddenly you're eating a full combo. Due to these rewards for memorization, the game is very insistent on you picking a main and sticking to that one character for most of the time. Where the strength of Hero Academia is in its ensemble cast, your best bet here is to pick your one character, hopefully one of the handful of strong ones, and only by good fortune spot the weak characters in action.The core gameplay is still very fun! But only as long as you and your opponent are playing the same game. Are they using a strong character and not you? Unfun. Are they using combo extensions and not you? Unfun. Are they using infinites? Unfun. Are they using support covers all the time? Unfun. The players online are more than willing to use all of these things against you, which you will have no knowledge of as a new player. They seem to thrive on it, even.Playing all those unfun situations for most of the online battles is a serious headache.The online system itself is a bit of a headache. Matches will drop at random, queue requests will be denied at random, it's all very buggy.There is no proper ranking system; the only ranking system in the game measures how many 'ranked' battles you have won, and rather opaquely at that. That's it. There is no Elo system, no matches played record, not even a win rate.Online mode is the only substantial part of the game, but they seem to have dedicated an absurd amount of development resources to several other game components. Story mode is worthless pitched battles against bots as dumb as bricks in a meager imitation of Hero Academia's story season 3.5 to 4.5. Mission mode is a boardgame with no mechanics other than move here and do a battle (against a dumb bot you can catch in a loop). There are special attributes in effect during some of the battles, but that is equally as annoying as it is interesting. The agency concept is intriguing but doesn't really go anywhere. I did every mission without purchasing a single character for the agency. Arcade mode is more battles against the bots, though you are rewarded with two written lines of dialogue between the characters. There is a 4 player coop mode but none of us will ever play it because it requires someone next to you to play with someone online who has someone next to them.I'm being too harsh on the AI because I'm an advanced player. Bots will give new players good learning tools and you'll have fun starting out with them. But an experienced player cannot draw any enjoyment from them.The customization is nice. Good news is, they're not stingy with the hero coins, which you use to purchase all those customization items. It's not tied to real currency.The music is great. You cannot fully turn it off, only lower it.The game is now dubbed! Rejoice.The game is also stuck on the lowest graphics settings, so textures are PS1 era. There is a fix for this in the steam discussions though.The keyboard bug has been fixed.The game crashes at random every now and then.How did the developers understand their own game so little? It would be baffling if that weren't so common among AAA devs. This game could have been great if it had focused on the core gameplay and polished online and its leaderboards. Story mode is irrelevant, mission mode is someone's pet project, arcade mode is just to make sure the game isn't useless when the online scene is dead.I'm going to keep playing and see more characters and stuff but I'm very disappointed. I can't really even bring friends into this since it's so weirdly complicated. Lucky I love Hero Academia as much as I do.Overall, the first 10 or so hours most people will put in will be fun. Beyond that, the game is EXTREMELY tilting. But you can continue to have fun beyond that point once you come to peace with how crap it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a comprehensive review, but wow is this a total mess. Its almost exactly what it looks like from the trailers and gameplay; its the first One's Justice but it has a dozen more characters added in, yet somehow its actually worse than the first game in many ways, to the point I don't even know what it wants to be mechanically.---VISUALS:At it's best it's "fine", but at worst it's absolutely hideous. It looks pretty much exactly like the first game character model wise, but its the animations that really set it back. A majority of supers in this that weren't taken straight from the original game look , bordering on lazy. Everything from their pacing and choreography to their their animations and effects just yells rushed and lazy. One of the main appeals of these anime fighters is that they tend to be visually gorgeous and stylish to play, and OJ2 is neither. On top of that some of the textures in-game are extremely bad for no real reason, even the textures on the characters themselves are littered with gaudy compression and rubbish resolutions. Its almost embarrassing. To give credit where credit is due, Shoot Style Deku's new super is absolutely excellent, and Nomu's intros and outros look fantastic; they're examples of what this game could have been visually.----GAMEPLAY:It plays like the first One's Justice, but with an immense amount of game mechanic whiplash. So many things cause the game to slow down or freeze (not from performance, its intentional), like hard hits and assist calls for example, but when the gameplay isn't freezing, its barreling ahead at a full speed, almost to the point of feeling like chaos sometimes. Character's overall damage seems like its been nerfed across the board since OJ1, but you also feel like you gain zero meter whatsoever now so actually getting to decent damage feels like an absolute rarity. Couple all those things together and you have a game that seems like it wants to be a fast based arena fighter, but matches feel so insanely slow to complete. Constant freezing from specific moves coupled with how you do next to no damage while gaining such small pockets of meter creates such a weird sensation of pacing whiplash. I'd rather play OJ1 instead because at least it's matches were very consistent in terms of flow and pacing, OJ2 is just all over the place.Also, there's a new "parry" mechanic where pressing the armour input while you're in blockstun makes you do an instant counter move that launches you both back to neutral, Its honestly really horrible because it makes blockstrings entirely useless. Any clever pressure or okizeme capabilities characters have become entirely null when every player has the equivalent of DBFZ's sparking blast on standby for every blockstring. Oh, and you can still get out of any combo you want just by tapping an assist if they're available, just like in OJ1. ----STORYMODE:If you were expecting it to be better than OJ1's storymode, you'll be letdown here as well. Its the exact same thing pretty much, the same boring comic cutscenes and the same uninteresting 1v1 fights. Unfortunately its worse than OJ1 here as well, because it makes obscene small changes and omissions to the MHA story which feel very much like a fanfiction rewrite. It does everything it can to absolutely milk every fight they can squeeze in, an example would be Midoriya asking Mirio to fight him for permission to be brought to Nighteye's agency. Small things like this completely litter the storymode from top to bottom, making it also not serviceable as a way to experience the MHA story.----RAPID-FIRE COMPLAINTS:1: Their hit  is 2: The game uses your cursor in the character selection screen despite using a controller3: Character select screen takes about 10 seconds to load when in an online room match.4: A lot of the textures are 5: Its still  jank.6: Bandai can't keep it in their pants so we know  thanks to their code.7: So many moves still feel 8: On some maps the lighting is .9: They completely abandoned patching the first game, there's no saying they won't do so again here.10: Jiro still has her nonsensical apparating speakers that do the same thing her hero suit would do like wtf lmao----My Hero Academia fans deserve better, and Kohei's work deserves a lot more respect than this. If you enjoy it then go nuts, I won't stop you, but I can't recommend it. Its rushed, its lazy, mechanically a mess, doesn't have much respect for the source material, 40% of it is recycled from the first game, and its very clearly just a cash grab to cash in on the MHA license. This needed another three months of development at least.There's far better out there to spend your money on and it shouldn't be this. Despite all the jank it had I really liked the first game, and admittedly there's a handful that I do like about this one too, but its far too overshadowed by it's negatives. I'm going to wait for patch or two before moving on to Doom or Animal Crossing or whatever else this game decided it had a chance to compete with releasing in March.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the anime and, despite a lot of issues, I still really enjoyed the first game so I thought I'd grab this one while it was at £23.99. I have finished the 'hero' side of the story missions and I must say I am very impressed. At first, you start the tutorial with some of the same characters from game 1 and also in the same maps but as you progress through the story there's different maps in line with the narrative of the anime and so so many more characters than the first game. As well as that, it's more true to the anime rather that just including fights that never happened to pad out the story. They've fixed some issues with the AI from the first game and also made it more challenging by making it less likely to be able to spam a move to win the matches. And the final boss battle of story mode with Overhaul actually includes his different forms like in the anime which really surprised me, I just expected to have to fight his character over and over. Very impressed and well worth the £24 I paid for it. Loving it so far!

The characters are different enough that this one feels a little more interesting than some, and once you get past that jarring clunky phase and start getting a handle on your character and the controls, it's pretty darn fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun brawler with a low barrier to entry. _childDocuments_.review: Ones Justice 2 surpasses the original in every way that matters. Increases character depth, along with a greatly increased character roster pushes this series forward by leaps and bounds. _childDocuments_.review: This is my first actual review, so sorry if there's anything that's unclear.[DLC INFO BELOW][TL;DR] It should be stated right away that My Hero One's Justice 2 is, quite simple, an extreme improvement from the first game in essentially all aspects. Though it remains mediocre in some aspects, most importantly the balance. Is this worth the price? Honestly, no. It should be a lot cheaper, and this price is only worth it if you are a My Hero Academia fan.[GRAPHICS] Graphic wise, the game looks way more polished than the prequel, as expected. The animations are smooth, as well as the textures have been improved, and the effects are now spot on, but still holding onto My Hero Academia's characteristic animation style, even in 3D game form.[AUDIO] Audio wise, the sound effects are good, not much to be said about them, and the soundtrack is surprisingly good, though the usage of some of the official soundtrack could have made it even better. It should be noted that there are no in-game subtitles, or an English dub, so Japanese is all you're gonna get, and other than in the story's cutscenes, or the characters saying something in the mission mode, you're not gonna get much more.[STORY] The story is solid, very loyally but also liberally following the normal My Hero Academia story-line. The Hero story-line just follows the steps that were taken in My Hero Academia, though the transitions to combat are relatively choppy in most cut-scenes. The Villain story-line also follows the steps and is not really Alternative Universe, but it follows the timeline well enough to not be messed up.[GAMEPLAY] The gameplay remains mostly the same, other than some more moves that have been added, and a TON (double/triple?) of new characters added to the roster. Balancing is a bit of a hit-or-miss, there was an attempt in balancing a lot of the playable characters, especially Todoroki and most of all the Nomu, but spamming combos works just as well as it did in the previous game. Additionally, the PLUS ULTRA gauge is now harder to fill up, as some combos can reduce it, making increasing it and waiting to use it in a certain situation way more difficult than in the previous game. [CUSTOMIZATION] Character Customization has been massively improved, and now there's even more cosmetics you can use, and some exclusive gifts for owners of the original game, and owners of the Deluxe Edition and Season Pass, though I personally find them pretty mediocre. Make sure to choose the presets before starting a match, for whatever reason, they're usually not saved.[MULTIPLAYER] The multiplayer, as is with most relatively overpriced anime games, is expected to be alive for the first few weeks, even the first 2-3 months, and then I expect it's gonna start dying out. I already had trouble joining an Unranked match, and it's only the second day as of writing this.[FUTURE PLANS / DLC]There are no steam cards to speak of yet, so we're still waiting for that.It is also worth noting that there are 5 more characters to be released, and I hope that they're not gonna pull a Kill La Kill IF and just abandon the game half-way in.That's all. This guide is subject to change, depending on changes made in the game. Probably. Please comment if I missed anything worth mentioning![! DLC !]As of 26th of November (with the release being on March 11, 2020), only 3 / 5 of the DLC characters from the season pack have been released, and a couple more cosmetic DLCs that for whatever reason were never included. While not a dealbreaker, it's an incredibly bad practice. Not to mention the subjective opinion that they decided to release characters that aren't worthwhile.As of the 18th of March, 2021, 4 / 5 DLC characters from the season pack have been released. Cosmetic DLCs have also been released, but season pack owners have not been given them.As of the 30th of September, 2021, 5 / 5 DLC characters have been released. From Season Pack 1. Yeah, they made a second season pack. No, deluxe edition and pre-order buyers don't get access to that. ♥♥♥♥ you Bandai.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. this game has both it's pro's and con's. but before i get into that. let me just say that i do enjoy this game greatly. it's something that i have been wanting to get, and it is amazing, with only a few minor issues that could stand to be better tended to in the next installment.Pros:*great visuals.*diverse roster*fun customization for characters.Cons:*disorienting camera movement.*bland controls that do not always work.*no real variation or balance in attacking enemies, even among cpu.*mostly focuses on area destruction over the combat that causes it.This is a great game in all rights. but it feels like it's just tryng to be another naruto storm clone that has been watered down to take away some of the dynamic feel of it. which i can understand in it's entirety, but it generates a slightly lacking feel of power. Is the game still fun? yeah, it's great and i do enjoy the various game modes which helps it to be some what unique. Would i recommend getting it at full price? no, not at all, as fun as it is, it's still not really up there when compared to competing games like one-punch man or demon slayer. i'd really only get it at discount.What's the take away from this critique? While the game itself is something that can be fun to play with friends when you need a some-what senseless battler, it tries to be too flashy with weak substance to support. i'd still say get the game but only when it's in the lower price ranges because that's what i think it is currently worth.Reader: Oh you're full of it. _childDocuments_.review: Not really my cup of tea. After diving into Guilty Gear and Granblue Fantasy Versus, my bar for anime fighting games is pretty high – I'm talking complex gameplay and a serious challenge to master. But this game? It just doesn't cut it. It's super basic with just three buttons – the standard punch/kick and a couple for those unique character moves. It's set in a 3D arena, but honestly it doesn't make much use of that. Sure, it's kinda fun for a chill session to relax after a long day, especially with those insane scenes where you're flinging opponents into buildings – that part's actually pretty cool. But that's about as good as it gets. And the price? They're charging around 250 AED, that is roughly 70 USD, for all the DLCs and two season passes for a game from 2020. Seems a bit steep to me. The game feels more tailored for anime/manga fans who get a kick out of playing as their favorite characters and snapping a few screenshots. Sadly, that's not my thing.
