_childDocuments_.review: It has Moe Shop, Panda Eyes, Nitro Fun, Tristam, and Tokyo Machine, pretty fun although there is a bit of mod support, it is limited. The custom songs you can get are usually all in expert or XD difficulty which is fine if you play the game a lot but if you don't you're kind of screwed. It's no beat saber but it's worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: i've been trying to find some good rhythm games to play that aren't beat saber, since i don't personally own a VR system. i'm absolutely thrilled to report that my search brought me to this game!i was a little dubious of the control scheme at first, but from what i can tell the game does a great job easing you into it with the different difficulties. difficulties usually ramp up by introducing a new control mechanic, and then you have a bunch of songs to choose from as you try to get used to it. the songs seem to be organized more-or-less by difficulty, as per usual, so i have to assume that they get you acclimated well. i'm using all of these assumptions because i'm an impatient person who tried ramping up the difficulty fast. i'm not at expert level just yet, but i did push myself to try the "hard" levels before i had even tried all the songs on easy. honestly, i probably would have given into frustration if it wasn't for this game's really, really helpful practice mode; it lets you break the songs into chunks so you can tackle one bit at a time and loop parts that frustrate you. (it also lets you change the tempo, but my pride won't let me test this out.)if you like rhythm games and your wrists are up to it, try this out! worth noting i've been using my mouse for this; i think it's fun. i can't speak for the gameplay using the controller.

_childDocuments_.review: A quite unique DJ-themed rhythm game. I play every rhythm game I've managed to get my hands on and Spin Rhythm XD managed to be fresh and new enough with its controls that for the first few hours I felt like a beginner again. Usually when an experienced rhythm gamer picks up a new game they can skip straight to the highest difficulty - but here I had to humbly drop down to the middle one, and I can't think of a better compliment for how innovative SRXD is for the genre.My only issue so far was the gap between second hardest and hardest difficulty, as it felt there wasn't anything to prepare you for the latter, especially given each difficulty brings forth a new mechanic (note type basically). It'd be good to add a few easier charts for the highest diff. However, there is a practice mode already, allowing you to play songs or sections without risk of failure - something most rhythm games fail to include.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  Something is magical about this one.For one thing, I consider myself reasonably good at rhythm games, and Spin Rhythm XD is DIFFICULT.  Which is a good thing.  It's the epitome of the idea that a great casual game should be easy to pick up and difficult to master.  In about a half hour of playing so far, I've gotten comfortable enough with normal difficulty that I can pass stages but my palms will be sweating profusely by the end of them.  That either means overactive glands or the devs made a fine rhythm game.  Can't wait to play more.Suggestions for the devs:1. I love the mapping you guys do because it makes it really feel like you're part of the music.  That said, the music itself lacks variety, so I'm hoping there are plans to add a more interesting mix of stuff (even just other subgenres within electronica/EDM would be cool).2. I'm still unsure if I imagined this, but I recall there being a few bright white screen flashes while I was playing.  Might just be an overactive effect or something else strange but it was distracting and happened enough times that I started to notice.Otherwise though... keep building on this excellent foundation because the game is already a top tier rhythm game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first rhythm game since Project Diva: Future Tone that I've thoroughly enjoyed with virtually nothing bad to say. If you're skeptical of the concept, definitely take advantage of Steam's 2 hour grace period, because that's more than enough time for you to know if this game works for your sensibilities. Not sure how to format the rest of my review, so here's a list of everything I appreciate about this, that other games in the genre seem to struggle with.---------------------------------------------- The game gives you instant audio and visual previews of the songs prior to playing them. In some rhythm games this is atrocious, having to load the audio once you hover over a song, meaning you spend way too much time in menus waiting for things to happen. Spin Rhythm XD excels at this by not only giving you immediate audio previews, but also having a miniature preview of the beatmap to go alongside the audio, showing you exactly what you're about to be dealing with.- Many rhythm games have a pretty glaring issue in regards to easy beatmaps not accurately reflecting the rhythm of the song you're playing. Spin Rhythm XD cleverly sidesteps this issue by having a note type that only requires correct positioning, and doesn't require an input such as clicking or tapping spacebar. This means that even when a beatmap should have rapid fire notes to reflect what's happening in the song, easy difficulties can still have those rapid fire notes. This lets them avoid the disconnect that often happens when you're forced to play easy mode in a game you haven't yet learned.- The track list is just really solid and varied. This is way more subjective than what I've already said, but the high intensity EDM focused soundtrack just matches the DJ angle they're going for. There's plenty of interesting variations on that type of music though. Definitely listen to the tracklist and form your own opinion of course, but so much of this genre is filled with stuff I don't care for, so this was a refreshing thing to see. Could definitely use more songs, but that's not dogging on the quality of what's there already, because not everything can match the 200+ tracks in Future Tone for obvious reasons.- The game lets you fail out of a song during gameplay. This seems like a no-brainer, but I've purchased a game or 2 in the past that legitimately don't let you fail a song midway, and instead only determine whether you have failed or not at the end of the song, which means you can just cheese your way through difficult sections without understanding them. Spin Rhythm XD doesn't do anything new in this regard, but if I can hear the end of a song without playing it, then I won't play your rhythm game. Thank you Spin Rhythm devs for not doing something so dumb.- Has a very detailed UI that encourages improvement. A simple addition of a line graph showing your individual attempts, and what percentage you got on the corresponding attempt, goes a long way. It's just a whole lot of fun replaying a song you tried early on, failing at 22%, and then seeing that line graph go from 22% to 68%, then a sudden 94% when you finally attempted at the skill level required for the beatmap. Even just finishing a song up and seeing the "NEW BEST" text scrolling behind the letter grade is extremely satisfying.---------------------------------------------I've barely scratched the surface in this game, but every single thing I normally take issue with in rhythm games seems addressed here. I love the genre so much, but it feels like every single big name like DJ Max Respect has one or two pitfalls that make me immediately refund and never purchase again. Spin Rhythm XD finally broke that trend for me, and I can't recommend it enough. 10/10 experience all around.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of music/rhythm games are about accuracy and reaction time. Many of them are uncomfortable to play. Many feel jank and unresponsive at times, and you end up banging your head against the wall if you want to achieve greatness.Spin Rhythm is about learning its uniqueness. It doesn't require unreasonable accuracy or timing. You feel in control in a way that you can loosen up and jam out a bit, especially after you adapt to the coordination and your brain does plays automatically.It reminds me of playing DDR. I eventually learned to do the steps without much thought, and I could groove to the music comfortably and have fun.That kind of feeling you get of relaxing while also performing is what music games should be all about, and Spin Rhythm has it in spades.Every time you come back to the game you'll feel progress with coordination. And it's quick to start up and jump right into a song. You may even feel like making a routine out of it, because you'll probably have a bigger brain for it.

_childDocuments_.review: For the record, I had a miserable experience in the first hour, but that is not a reason for me to downvote this game.This game truly has potential. Innovative gameplay, beautiful, clean visuals...but overshadowed by it's difficulty. I played the two tutorials, they were easy to pick up, but then as I get constantly destroyed by the 3rd difficulty level I start to realize that this game is actually very challenging, and I think the following is the reason:In many rhythm games with the "falling/rising notes" mechanic, you usually pick a scrolling speed of choice to play, and focus your eyes mostly on only one part of the screen to read the notes, process it in your mind and just wait for the right moment to hit it, without having to move your eyes down or up. I don't think you can do that here. More than having to read the upcoming notes, you have to match the wheel colors to that of the next note, which force you to pay attention to two distant parts of the screen at the same time, which I find to be very difficult.A good experiment nonetheless, I wonder if the top players can just play without paying attention to the wheel colors haha.Will update when I play more.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game, but I hate a bunch of things about it as well.The charting is amazing on some levels and in other levels, it feels like it was automatically generated and has a red dot in the middle of a bunch of blue notes. When things like that happens, it doesn't feel intuitive at all. An otherwise perfected song ends up being ruined by what looks like a charting typo... Some of the early charting for songs were really intuitive and felt like you could get into the zone and hit the notes without looking at the screen. Then some hardcore players recharted them and the devs accepted them. After that, they just aren't as fun to play.On the highest difficulty, REMIXD, It feels like they threw out intuitive charting and just randomly moved things around, added things that don't make sense, etc. just to make it "hard". The way they handle difficulty is a mess. Each song is standalone. There isn't progression in the song list that "teaches" you how to do new things and eases you into them. This means you can perfect every song on one difficulty and then when you move up a difficulty, you could end up not being able to even come close to finishing a song. There should be songs in the game that have minimal instances of the new gameplay elements, such as crazy new note patterns and the beat bar. This way, players can get a feel for the new gameplay elements and work their way up the new difficulty, instead of slamming face first into a brick wall.The menus are terrible. Again, it was intuitive before and it became a complete mess in the rework. There's so much going on in the menus that it's overwhelming. The important bits of the menu are for some reason also the smallest parts of the menu...In the 1.0 version of the game, they randomly decided to reset the settings. I had to redo the calibration, which I'm not sure if it's quite right yet and I still have yet to find the mouse sensitivity that I had before... The colors I had chosen for the wheel are gone and I don't remember what I had before. The game also now defaults to "Steam Controller" on startup and I have to set it to "Mouse" every time, otherwise the sensitivity is out of wack.Some of the songs are just bad. Like bad for this style of a rhythm game, but also often just sounds like noise, instead of music.The game handles missed notes so poorly. It cuts out a massive portion of the track ahead of the missed note, so you don't continue to miss notes and fail them. It also turns down the volume of the song. However, this just means that you lose all rhythm/momentum to the song and are likely to miss more notes when you start playing again. There are settings to change this, so that notes aren't hidden/skipped, but that doesn't feel much better as there are a songs where there are so many notes in one spot that you basically instantly fail. Not sure why they couldn't just make it so a cluster of missed notes don't cause you to instant lose, like a reduced penalty when notes missed exceeds a certain threshold in a specific time frame, but lets you continue to play as intended. The score multiplier would still be going down.The characters/avatars seem completely pointless. They server no purpose. Worse yet, after selecting a song, the console in front of the character has to transform into a plane and the character has to hit a button on it to send it flying. This is just a waste of time. Before, it would just launch the song right away.Again, I love a lot about this game, but it just got worse and worse each patch.

_childDocuments_.review: ~~I received this game for free for offering to help test the level editing tools c:~~This game is a rhythm game like no other. It vaguely calls to other rhythm games, with a highway scrolling towards you, and notes moving along said highway, but past that, this is an all new dimension.It features (at time of review) 30 hand-crafted tracks, each with 5 difficulty levels, and more free content promised on the way. The difficulty of this game is unique, moving the difficulty from being super technical and mechanical, to being a lot more mental. This isn't a game about how fast you can hit buttons in a certain order, or how fast you can flick your wrist and cross your arms. This is a game about how well you can stay in a state of flow, and really bring yourself to control the wheel as if it were a part of you.Its simple control scheme makes it a very accessible game. 3 simple inputs: Tap the wheel to grab it, turn the wheel to match the colours, and hit the beat button to the beat notes.I personally play the game with a drawing tablet, many top players like to stick with mouse + keyboard, while others swear by their midi DJ wheels. It's a very open and customizable game.And speaking of customizability, custom tracks exist!With a built in-editor, (which, admittedly at time of reviewing is a little bit clunky and not super-intuitive) importing your own custom songs to hand-craft to your liking is very doable. There's no Workshop support, however, because the devs don't want to open that legal can of worms for dealing with musical copyright. Plus, there's tons of community around the game. With leaderboards, daily challenges, Spin.FM synchronized multiplayer lobbies for anyone to hop in/out of at any time, you're sure to make some friends and memories with this title.Overall, it's an exceptionally crafted game, which keeps getting better and better through its development. Packed with tons of replayability, love and care from the devs, and a great community, purchasing this game will not be a mistake c:

_childDocuments_.review: So, Spin Rhythm XD.I've played alot of music based games in my life from DDR, Guitar Hero, Frequency/Amplitude, Audiosurf and many more. All of which are good in their own rights; but I feel SRXD is probably the most evolved and accessible of them all to make a truly pleasant music experience casually or competitively.It does alot of things great that I wish many games (even outside the music genre) would do and make industry standard; like the accessibility options.What are some great strengths of the game?- Large track variety and support for custom tracks by users.- Clean and sleek interface, very little clutter and most can be turned off.- Multiplayer! (Brings me back to the good ole Guitar Hero days!)- Impressive accessibility options; from note color/contrast to track speed and visual effects, etc.(Added to that, it requires very few keys and motions to play; very low barrier to entry.)- "Flow"That last one is pretty confusing on its own, I know; what is "Flow"?It's just as hard to describe haha.With alot of music games, one aspect that can make or break it is how smooth the game and music experience move / sync together appropriately; coupled with how 'natural' it is to make such motions.A good majority of games lately lack a smooth and consistent flow.Playing SRXD not only is great for its music, but it feels good to play too.It's even more so when you are able to customize that experience to a degree of your liking.One of the few rhythm games that gives ample comfort to those who want to play casual coupled with lots of control and capability for those who wish to challenge themselves too; all without taking from each other.I love music games, always will even the older ones; that'll never change!The difference is, Spin Rhythm XD is one I always come back to and enjoy.It's a great game to recommend for anyone getting into the genre or who already is~Trust me, it's a worthwhile experience. ^..^

_childDocuments_.review: I learned about this game earlier this year from a YouTuber who was bringing to light that a bigger company shamelessly copied this game and turned it into a mini game contained in their main game. It was one of the coolest looking rhythm games I had ever seen and I knew it was right up my alley and boy was I more than right.This game is definitely an easy to pick up, hard to master scenario. I was definitely struggling with the sections where one set of color notes would follow right behind the other at first but I just kept practicing and now it's almost second nature. The spinning sections are also cool especially when a tap note follows. I'm willing to bet anyone who has a midi controller really feels like a DJ doing these parts. The soundtrack has not only been fantastic but I have discovered new musicians I regularly listen to now such as Panda Eyes and Teminite. "Highscore" is by far my favorite track. It's definitely got a lot of electronic music like you'd expect but for me it contains a lot of music with chiptune which I'm always a sucker for. Plus you can create your own charts for songs you'd like to play or possibly download through "Spinshare". I recommend downloading it to your computer for the easiest experience. Now I will admit the creative mode isn't the most user friendly at first and, I really struggled with it when I first tried it but, if you really want to make a song it's not too bad once you learn everything. However I do think the creative mode does need an overhaul.I have put 300 hours into this game and I'm still not tired of it and I still haven't mastered the hardest difficulty and am now just getting comfortable with the second hardest. I highly, highly recommend this game and just want it to succeed so please give it a try and if you want some type of guitar hero or DJ hero fix this game has got you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm is very interesting because it chooses to experiment with input in a way most rhythm games don't. It's so strange to see a music game making full use of analogue controls, but it results in something that doesn't feel like any other rhythm game out there. The presentation is slick, the default track selection is sizable and diverse, and in general it's a very solidly built game. It's absolutely worth the price with just how  there is, with every single track (of which there are already 44, and in early access might I add!) having 5 difficulties each. And even if you don't like the base songs, there's also a level editor! I never ran into the Rhythm Game Difficulty Syndrome, where there's a massive gap between intermediate and expert-level play and a drought of charts at that middle range of difficulty; it all flows very nicely together, and there's always going to be a chart that hits your current "Goldilocks" level of challenge.For problems, I think the game just...  off, in a way I can't really rationalize. Everything feels soft and not especially tactile, and it bothers me because I'm not really sure how one would fix it. Maybe the note "explosions" need to be flashier, maybe there needs to be more visual feedback given, whatever, it's hard to pin down. One thing I can say is that the timing windows are quite wide, and that adds to the feeling of "softness" - it might just be because I play Beatmania or something, but I've definitely had instances where I went "oh, that should not have been a perfect". Might be fixed by adding some sort of "Perfect+" judgement. It's also hard to tell if you're even getting perfects, as the judgement is tucked away and hard to read, so some better visual indicator would be appreciated.(...Also, why is there absolutely no turntablism hip-hop in here? It's literally a game you can play with a DJ controller, and you didn't even add ONE scratch-heavy song? Really? Come on. Some Q-Bert? Cut Chemist? Give me something to work with here.)

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  Now the game crashes everytime I load a track. Great game guys(!)A novel idea to bring the rhythm game genre to PC in a way that isn't completely janky, a la Clone Hero or those god-awful Stepmania games, but it needs a ton of work.The worst thing about this game is the way it handles difficulty. It adds entire mechanics with every step-up in difficulty which sounds fine, but you need to learn these new mechanics WHILST playing the harder chart than before. It isn't a static addition, the chart itself gets harder as well. This means that the player will be struggling to wrap their brain/muscle memory around a whole new gimmick, WHILST dealing with a much harder chart rushing toward them. There's no gradual addition of mechanics, and these harder charts are the ONLY place to learn the new mechanics. It's like they didn't even think about it.Also, while heavily-customisable, the controls are just outright poor. The "motion controls" for the mouse don't register half the time, so I've had to rebind them to a key, which feels like it's going against the intended design of the game, and making things WAY more awkward than if the intended control scheme just worked, in the first place.The charts are also wild. It's supposed to be a rhythm game, but you're never on an instrument for more than 10 seconds. Blue tap notes will go from the kick drum, to the melody on the piano, to the vocals and back again, then the red notes will do the same, and the intended "kick drum" mechanic added in hard mode will only SOMETIMES be the percussion. The exact same "Kick" (sound wise) will be on every kind of note during the duration of a song, and it's mind-bogglingly stupid. Finally, and some would argue it's the most important factor, is the music. It's 95% generic "MonsterCat" trash you can make in 5 mins on FL Studio, or as other reviewers have stated, dubstep/chiptune stuff that would've been cool 10 years ago.. Super disappointing. If I have to sit through another 5 mins of "Kitty" (some teenager who thinks mumbling through her nose is singing) abusing a microphone again, I'll top myself.The UI also needs work. The little "perfect" indicator and the star are WAY too far from the action, so if you wanna check your status, you'll almost certainly miss an incoming note. The health system makes no sense, because it's a flat rate of healing that isn't tied to your accuracy. You essentially have to not miss for an extended period of time to heal, as opposed to literally every other [more successful] rhythm game in the past.The note clear mechanic is to alleviate this, but it's just a lazy band-aid over the problem. It's also distracting on Expert/XD difficulties, where you'll miss something, the chart will clear and you'll suddenly need to drop back into it at full speed. It's.. bizarre.Play Clone Hero or something. This is really disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: My initial review was extremely out of date and I removed a couple details that are no longer accurate. I have since acquired a DJ controller and have been playing the heck out of this game. It's physically satisfying to play and the song selection is plentiful and full of good stuff. As with all great rhythm games, the skill ceiling feels unattainable. I've got one song left to clear on Expert, but XD difficulty is still beyond my comprehension in most cases. Fortunately, there is a very helpful practice mode which can loop sections of a song and modify the speed so that you can figure out patterns easily.---Initial review from early access:I'm very impressed with how polished and well-thought out this game is. The soundtrack so far is great and the charts and style of gameplay is very satisfying. (I've been playing with a mouse.)Whereas most rhythm games come down to performing an action with precision timing to a set of beats, Spin Rhythm varies the required skillset with a bit of the usual rhythmic tapping combined with an aiming/spinning mechanic that demands controlled positioning rather than simple timing.There are lots of control options which accommodate a variety of play styles and setups. I actually spent several hours mapping a wiimote as a controller for this game (though with my scripting experience, it never ended up being as reliable as a mouse).Anywho, this is a very polished and satisfying game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who likes and plays a lot of rhythm game, I highly recommend this game. It's a well-implemented and well-developed game because it has those little things and QOL stuff that rhythm games should have.At first glance, the gameplay stands out as it's very different compared to its contemporaries. The gameplay might look simple, looking at previews, but it's actually deep and complicated especially at high-level songs. What's more, it really gives you the feeling that you're actually <playing> the song especially those with excellent notecharts.The game runs really well, making it easy to just open the game and quickly start playing and/or practicing songs. It also offers a lot of helpful accessibility and customization options that can help you adjust the UI, HUD, notes, etc. to your liking. Another thing to of note is that this game can be played with multiple controllers and/or control schemes: You can use KB+M, Keyboard, Gamepad, even a turntable!The only minor thing this game lacks is the number of songs. At the time of writing this review, the game only has 60 songs but I am optimistic that the developers can now focus on bringing in more songs after the 1.0 launch. Fortunately, this is remedied by the game's capability to add custom songs.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. The soundtrack covers a wide range of genres and each song is great. The innovative gameplay is unlike any other, being extremely satisfying and fun. _childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be honest, I was on the verge to give up and ask for a refund but I said to myself "hey, lets just play one more song". Tell you what, I'm glad I sticked to it because I havent had this much fun playing a rhythm game in a long time. Now by all mean, I ain't a rhythm game expert, OSU and DJMAX still terrify me (Muse Dash too, but not for the same reasons) and the controls of Spin Rhythm XD gave me trouble at first but trust me, when you get them right, you feel like a 200 IQ music genius and its almost better than sex. Unlike most rhythm games that just requires you press the right input on the beat, Spin Rhythm makes you actually feel like youre playing an instrument. The visuals are great, reminiscent of what you'd see in an arcade place. The song selection is groovy and goes well with the control. If youre a fan of EDM, youll be served and if not, its still quite enjoyable and thats coming from someone who mainly listen to jazz and black metal. I'd say that the biggest let down at the moment is the number of tracks avaiable but the game is still in early access so theres more to come and the custom charts kinda makes up for it. I'd appreciate to see more game modes but all in all its already a great experience at a fair price and everything else will be icing on top.EDIT: been playing for 72 hours ( in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rhythm game!!!), I still like it. It's a magnificent stress relief game. Been playing regularly after works, it helps me to focus on other things than my problems. If I could buy it again, I would.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: At this time in development the game is passable and anyone who hasn't tried the game yet might get some mileage out of it, but I don't think it's going to wow anyone this far in. I will acknowledge that I used to be super hyped about this game a year ago, but now that the dust has settled I'm more lukewarm on its quality.The charts are fun, and I honestly like the music selection a lot, but for every good design choice there's a questionable one that takes the enjoyment out of it. The fact that they have added in a hidden timing window that's not visible to the players and adds an arbitrary amount of bonus points to their final score is already a questionable decision that throws out any legitimacy to a "perfect" score. Literally no other rhythm game I know of does this.Honestly I'd probably give this game a few more years of development and maybe it could even be viable for tournaments in the future, but as it is right now it's an OK distraction that doesn't really do much different as far as rhythm arcade games go.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: A unique style of rhythm game reminiscent of Sound Voltex, albeit a tad simpler but without the added cost of a pricey proprietary peripheral. It does support the use of MIDI controllers as a fun replacement for mouse and keyboard but the basic control scheme is more than serviceable. In addition there are plenty of accessibility features to fine tune your experience with coloring options for notes, note scroll speed, and audio latency adjustment. With its own spin (yeah I said it) on the genre and visual design to decipher it provides a fairly steep learning curve for the first 10-15 hours of play. I can not stress enough that when your brain synapses finally form the necessary connections to comprehend the rainbow smorgasbord flying at you this game becomes immensely satisfying to play.The base game's tracklist is solid overall, a few misses here and there but plenty of these tracks are quality content, enough so that I've added a number of them to my personal playlists. The charting is also solid, with 5 difficulty levels made to ease you into each of the mechanics which are notes, taps, holds, spins, scratches, beats, and beat holds. One of my only complaints is that they've redone the charting a few times to make them easier/less frustrating for more casual players, which ruined some of the enjoyment of mastering the harder, more mechanically demanding charts (not that I ever got good enough to PFC them myself). Nevertheless, there is still plenty of fun and challenge to be met in the base game.Even better though is the built in editor for making your own charts and support for downloading custom charts! Though you will need to download a separate application get other people's tracks (look up spinshare)For its price point and level of polish (they're still updating this game as it's still relatively new) you'd be a fool to pass up this game if you're even remotely interested in rhythm games. Just remember: "Step to the rhythm, move to the rhythm, slide to the rhythm, SPIN! Do it all over again!"
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of my favorite rhythm games I've ever played. The gameplay flows really nice and the songs have a nice difficulty curve. There's also an insane amount of customization and accessibility settings so you can really do whatever you want. I'm glad I came back and gave the game a second try after not enjoying it so much the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely my most favorite rhythm game I've ever played. It just feels so good to play, it's indescribable. The progression into learning new game mechanics feels natural and challenging, but still reasonably easy. Difficulties are spread out nice, except for a large skill gap between the Expert and XD difficulties. This isn't a big deal, though, as I feel like expert is as far as most casual players would want to go. The level editor takes some getting used to, but once you are familiar with the system, it's very easy to use, especially swapping between testing and building the level. Also, using custom music is simple.Updates are frequent and the developers are very communicative with the community. Overall, this is the most enjoyment I've gotten out of an indie game in a long time, so I would definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great fun and has a great idea, the only game I have played that just feels smooth to play. The around 30 songs you get with the base game are great and well charted, the main fun on the game seems like it is going to come from custom songs, which I have tried a few of and are fantastic. The game has fantastic potential and is great already, I 100% recommend it if you like rhythm games and if you are wanting to get into rhythm games this is a great place to start.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another title that reminds me why I love rhythm games the most.And this one is quite unlike other games in the category.The premise seems fairly simple. Catch the small notes, hit the big notes and the bar notes, spin as directed.If this is your first rhythm game this will probably be very easy to get good at rather quickly but if you're used to playing a lot of other rhythm games it's hard to see anything flying at your target area and NOT want to press a button. It's unique style of play is both a blessing and a curse in that regard. But it's fun and I promise you it's worth practicing. The official charts included with the standard game have great variety and, for the most part, make sense in the context of being in a rhythm game.EDIT: Forgot to mention, this game's accessibility and customization options are second to none. Wanna change the note, UI, and spin colors? Do it. Want the combo meter moved somewhere else? Knock yourself out. Need to make things bigger (or smaller) for your eyes? Go nuts. Does the winding track and flashing lights cause visual issues? Adjust or even disable them at will. This game **wants** you to feel as comfortable as possible playing it.Better still, with the 3rd Party Spin Share application you can add lots of new tracks to play that have been fully charted by the community.If you're still unsure maybe wait till it's on sale but if you're a rhythm game junkie like me and you're looking for something with a different... SPIN on the genre... cop this one today!

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to just wipe my old review wherein I mainly just had a complaint with the old audio filters that muffled the song when you made a mistake. The dev responded quickly addressing my issue and that attention to the players definitely earned my respect. That early access review is nearly 2 years old now and I figured I'd update it to be more concise after a good couple years of playing a half hour here, half hour there of Spin Rhythm.Spin Rhythm is a wildly visually appealing rhythm game with an amazing flow of movement that had me hooked immediately. When you get better at it, it really is quite easy to lose yourself in the flow of playing through a song. I mainly play on an xbox controller, which is kinda considered below optimal for high difficulties, but I like it pretty well. I've worked my way up from only being able to play Hard at most to completing the roster on expert to playing a good chunk of the roster on the game's highest difficulty: XD at around 50 hrs of gameplay. The pacing of each difficulty combined with the amount of songs you can now play is at a point where I think it's pretty effective at being challenging enough to improve your skill and stay fun/rewarding, but not extremely frustrating. The dopamine rush of that first completion of a favorite song on XD was monumental. Not to mention there is a community building custom songs for it. The game has continually been polished by its dev and still receives regular free content which always great. It's an absolute blast, and I recommend it to anyone that enjoys rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: Yo yo yo, what is up party peopleeeee!!! Time to move it and groove it, or you'll completely lose it. You'd definitely do best to play this games Hands-On though, not too sure a Hands-Off approach works when the controls feel this good. A true-to-life arcade experience at home, Spin Rhythm XD feels like it was plucked from the magical land of Japan's arcade cabinets and plopped down into my hard drive.The gameplay? Fresh. The music? Fresh. The presentation? Couldn't be better. Spin Rhythm XD is what it's all about, a sickeningly addicting game with so much room to grow. It features tons of EDM from around the world, and you have to play the tracks that accompany to get a high score. Competing with people on the leaderboards at a certain level feels really good, especially when you have friends to do it with as well. Spin Rhythm has a variety of options though, because not only are there the official tracks the game comes with, but an extensive chart editor which has lead to tons of custom tracks that you can download at Spinshare (google it) which is where the community uploads most of their work. Be warned, a lot of these tracks are for people who are keenly and intimately familiar with the game, but usually there is something for everyone!This game is definitely one of the biggest proponents of the PC Rhythm Game scene, elevating the keyboard + mouse experience to something that actually feels comparable to a special peripheral needed to play the game, which tends to be a huge issue with rhythm games on PC. Already having the BEST available controller ready to play with is excellent, however you can customize your experience as much as you like, as there are TONS of options including a race wheel if you even want to play with that.Spin Rhythm XD is easily one of the best rhythm games out there, and it's still in early access. Hop on it now before the official release so you can get your foot in the door, it's only 19.99 on Steam and it's well worth double the asking price for how much fun you'll get out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: ugh....this review hurts me to write because the game has sooo much potential but it feels absolutely squandered by 1 design decision made just before full release. Gameplay is nice and simple and many of the charts flow is very strong until the XD difficulty level and even then the charts are really well done just balls deep hard. Personally i was allways excited to see new charts released as i played on the expert difficulty (a level below XD) which was challenging but managable as most of the time the scroll speed was low enough i could read it. when 1.0 dropped though things changed, you needed xp and levels to unlock all of the songs and xp is very dependant on difficulty and how well you do, would be nice on paper but with how little you get on expert with just FC songs arround level 22-25 you'll get stuck to replaying songs to grind for xp or being forced to XD difficulty which is....where i draw the line. because many of my favorite charts are still locked and i cant manage to break into XD difficulty the game became unplayable. good game if you want a rhythm game that strays from the norm but the game will demand perfection and more from you in the late stages

_childDocuments_.review: Played this not long after it was released on early access, the game alone is fun enough but the fact that they kept updating this game for years with tons of regular updates and added tracks when plenty of early access games get abandoned shows how professional this team is. The track list has nearly tripled from the original 23 and even then it felt like a complete game for the $20AUD I paid.The game itself is awesome with very unique mechanics and stands up with some of the best rhythm games in the industry, especially with the added XD difficulty that wasn't in the initial early access release. This is the game DJ Hero was supposed to be as it makes you feel like a DJ without a DJ controller, the charts strike a good balance between challenge and being fun to play. But if you want insanely hard charts there are custom charts made through the community that do that too.This is the first time I have ever reviewed a game on steam, the professionalism in early access and quality of the game made me compelled to review it. Buy it now and reward good devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big VR person, thousands of hours across various headsets, and I use a Valve Index primarily. So far I've only tested a few songs but to me the VR mode is exceptionally well made and thought out and I've had no big issues with it at all in the time I've spent in it so far. That being said, 1) First, I was a bit surprised the demo did not allow me to test the VR mode at all. I wouldn't have had this game on my radar at all without the VR mode being advertised, and I will probably not play this game in any other format -- so my only goal with the demo was to test if my Valve Index would work with the game at all really. I was a bit surprised the demo didn't even let me test the setup on a basic level when I first opened the game, saying the VR mode isn't available in that version.The game was on sale, so I decided to take the risk and go ahead and buy it to test the setup and refund if it didn't work well. Thankfully, it works very well, so I'm obviously keeping it (and I even went ahead and bought all the existing DLC right now too haha). But I very strongly advise you allow at least the initial tutorial song in VR mode in the demo, just enough to test that a given user's VR setup can work with the game at all. I mostly use a Valve Index which is pretty standard still, but there are users with older MR headsets, or more experimental stuff like Pimax, etc... where if it will work or not at all is very much not a guarantee. Thus is the nature of the PC VR ecosystem.There are probably other users like me who are interested in this game primarily for the VR aspect, and I feel the purpose of a demo is mostly to see if the user's setup will work at all. With that in mind,  Literally just the starting practice song would be plenty imho. That's my biggest piece of feedback I have for the game so far.2) Smaller issue but thought I'd bring it up as long as I'm here. In VR mode, I would like to be able to pull the table even a bit closer to me than you can right now. I really appreciate having that option by the way! And it even works with the Knuckles controller grips, which I think is awesome that you guys accounted for that unique control feature. But after pulling it as close as the game would allow, I ended up also adjusting where my playspace was centered within SteamVR and physically walking forward from the center (I have a reasonably large playspace) to get as close as I would really like. I might record a video later showing about the position I found it most comfortable in (I Twitch stream, so I might play this on there later and link to a clip showing where I most ideally have it for myself, if that might be helpful for you guys).Other than that, . This is a very satisfying VR music rhythm game, and I can see myself playing it a lot in the future. Works fantastic with Index, to the extent of utilizing unique Knuckles controller functionality that other headsets don't have.

_childDocuments_.review: What a revolution! The feeling of flow here is unmatched in a rhythm game and the controls are sublime. It feels great to spin and it's easy to keep track of where you are. Including unlocks there are a lot of tracks on display (over 60) and the quality is amazing; there's a nice blend of dubstep, lo-fi chill, and drum and bass. Can see me playing this for a long time!

_childDocuments_.review: I got over a day of in-game time on a friend's system when I first touched it and lemme just say DANG this game is good! Had to get it for myself. I played a good bit of osu! in the past. This game is super refreshing for the genre. My preferred control scheme is using the mouse for the in-game wheel, Z for tap notes, and Space for beats. But it is also a lot of fun to plug in a MIDI DJ controller every now and then for the vibes.Even if you don't think you like rhythm games, it's definitely worth giving this one a shot if it is catching your attention at all. The tracks that come with the game are bangers; there are even a few that I added to my own personal Spotify playlist because they are just that good.On that note, the team even has an official playlist on Spotify, so if you end up wanting to get gud and be a true nerd about it (like me,) you can listen to the songs when you're not playing to better learn them. Really helps with your flow when you go back to playing.It's an awesome feeling when you're brain clicks and your fingers just start moving independently of each other - i.e. it can get you into a flow state really quickly.The Discord is active, which is awesome to see!The team also had a lot of fun with the achievements, some of them are just silly which I love.All in all this game was made with a lot of love. Definitely worth the purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:This is a good game, Still Early Access for now, but the core gameplay is solid. The music for 1.0 seems to be all set, but I wouldn't guarantee anything.Good:VERY simple to learn. There's a tutorial, but not many people are going to need it. (It's a good tutorial anyway.)Almost anything can be a controller. If it's an input device that Steam can detect, or uses the MIDI protocol, you can probably use it. (Plus your keyboard and mouse.) The game uses full Steam Input integration for gamepads, and there's already layouts set up for the most popular controllers.Music is enjoyable. I mean... ok, my taste in rhythm game music tends towards the Toshiba/EMI era of Bemani, so I'm not exactly represented here. But it's still nice to listen to.Bad:Custom content... which is not the developers' fault. Look, if you've delved into the customs communities of most rhythm games, like Ouendan (Osu!) or Dance Dance Revolution (Stepmania among others), you know exactly what the problem is. People just don't make content for lower-skilled players. If you can't play at XD difficulty, then you're pretty much limited to what the developers release. That's not a bad thing on its own. But when you see all the customs available, and everything you wanna play is only Hard and XD (and often enough just XD), it hurts.Neutral:Online multiplayer. It's... well, it's 99% like GHTV from Guitar Hero Live. No music videos, no Star Power, but if you've played GH Live before Activision took down GHTV mode, you get what I'm talking about. I haven't gotten to play against people yet. Empty channels, but I can't really assume that's normal.Controllers used:USB mouse (Logitech G300s, Beat mapped to Mouse Back)DualShock 4Steam ControllerExtra thoughts:Can't help but think this would make an amazing arcade game. Screen plus a physical spin wheel. Foot pedal or tapping the screen for the Beat button, or convert all Beats to Taps.Also thinking about the upcoming Switch version. I assume the touchscreen is going to be the best way to play. (If so, please make sure that there's an on-screen Beat button so that it can be played without Joy-Cons at all.)

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of Rhythm games, mainly Rockband and guitar hero through all of their years. DJ hero was the first rhythm game to feel a bit set on it's own, but was still missing something. Spin Rhythm XD seems to have found that exact something that was missing. With amazing visuals and the fun spins that feel so satisfying to land perfectly, I immediately fell in love with this game. I've played one session of it, but I can already see myself loosing so many hours into this game trying to get higher scores and get better to play the higher difficulties. I also very much like the fact the the tracks have extended versions on the higher difficulties, giving you a real reason to want to get better and play those difficulties aside from a higher score. If you see early access and think "Oh, i don't know if I should get in on this game yet", don't let that stop you! This game feels like a full release already as they put a TON of polish on it from the start. In short, the visuals are great, the game feels very unique and like a fresh breath into the genre, there is incentive to get better, and it just feels so smooth and fun to play even on the lowest difficulty.I've been looking forward to this game's release to the public (even if it is in early access at the moment) and it did not disappoint at all!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: The majority of the songs are absolute bangers, but some of them sounds like "gamer EDM" trash to me (only some). _childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Ok as a fan of Rhythm games im addicted. 5 hours in one day is a lot more time then i ussualy give one game. Im a fan and i cant wait to see where this goes. If they can add a custom songs workshop or mod support this game would become one of the best rhythm games to exist (besides beat saber, but that in VR so not included)

_childDocuments_.review: . I think that is important as many reviews are of earlier iterations and I think it has had a lot of quality improvements sine the early days which may make some negative reviews now irrelevant.Wow this game is awesome. Incredible amount of polish on this. I can tell it really benefited from the early access phase with tons of user input that was (obviously) well received by the devs.  I use an external DSP for my sound device which adds significant delay but this game has a fantastic calibration system that will let you dial it in perfectly. It even has separate video and audio offsets.I was a little confused about the controls just from watching trailers/videos, but it's actually quite simple. Granted I've only played Easy and Normal, but so far I can play the entire game with one hand on the mouse:If that sounds complicated, it's not. The visual cues are great and you quickly get familiar with it and enter an almost zen-like state where it feels very intuitive. The mistake I make the most right now is forgetting to tap on the dash notes after a long string of round ones. LOLThe visual options in this game are astounding. You can configure the HUD to fit your preferences (very granular, you can show/hide and reposition many HUD elements). You can also unlock all sorts of skins and visual things. I think it is the perfect balance of being visually busy but everything on the screen you need to see is very clear and the rest add a very cool aesthetic. I saw a negative review complaining about the song unlock system being too hard to unlock the best songs, but I think they must have fixed that as I'm only 4 hours into the game and I've unlocked 50 of 66 songs and have keys for 4 more already (most songs I have only played once on Easy) and you get to choose which songs to unlock next, so I don't see any issues with the way unlocks work. 66 songs at the start would be overwhelming.The music is also awesome. It is mostly EDM / Dubstep type stuff (which I love) but honestly that type of music fits this type of game perfectly. I mean you can even play the game with DJ controllers if you like.Perfectionists will appreciate you can sort songs by your best score, so the top of the list is the songs you need to improve the most.Someone said this is the next evolution past Rock Band / Guitar Hero. That seemed like a presumptuous statement when I read it, but now I agree. It combines a lot of what I loved about those games and adds to it, and I don’t need a room full of peripherals to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack if you like EDM. _childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, I encountered a nasty performance bug that ended up leaving me with 2 hours of playtime spent entirely troubleshooting. The devs were nice and helpful on their discord server, and it ended up being an isolated incident with my bluetooth drivers.Now that the game works, I cannot put it down! SRXD is a brilliant rhythm game that uses two buttons and a turning wheel to create charts that are both intricate and immensely satisfying. The mechanics are fairly minimal, which is a huge plus for rhythm games imo, but if you look closely you might be able to tell that the original concept for the game came from a touchscreen mobile demo. Now, I don't tend to like touchscreen rhythm games bc of the lack of feedback and difficulty with precision. SRXD, of course, is not on a touchscreen, but is instead played using a shockingly wide range of control schemes: from rudimentary gamepad and keyboard controls, to more accurate mouse and gyro controls, all the way to official support for Steam Controller touchpads and real MIDI jogwheels! All of which are customizeable with native Steam Input support. I'm one of the suckers who bought a Steam Controller, and this one game makes that purchase feel worth it. Rhythm games live or die by their soundtracks, and this is where potential buyers need to pay more attention. SRXD's soundtrack is almost exclusively Monstercat-style EDM, with occasional synthwave and electrofunk tracks for flavor. If you're looking for rock or pop music, you won't find it here in the base game. SRXD does have custom song support, but the track-making community is in its infancy. Most custom tracks are only available on the hardest difficulty, and they skew towards electronic genres similar to the OST.Don't let the lack of Billboard hits deter you from this game though. If you give the soundtrack a fair shot, you'll find a lot to love across the roughly 40 songs each with 5 charts of varying difficulty. There are elements here from some of my favorite rhythm games like DJ Hero, GH Live, and Sound Voltex. Spin Rhythm XD had me grooving full-body in time with its spins and beats. A must-have for indie rhythm game lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best rhythm games I've played mechanically (playing with a trackball mouse and a foot pedal) and it isn't dragged down by the tracklist at all. A lot of customization options for the UI.The charts are made so well and gradually increase the complexity as you go through the songs. The game teaches you the mechanics and eases you into the crazy stuff it has you do on the harder difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first PC rhythm game that truly got me hooked. Spin Rhythm XD has incredibly tight, fair, and satisfying mechanics. The complexity and difficulty comes in the combination of its elements rather than any one mechanic on its own being fiddly or unfairly difficult. I found that I needed to play from the easiest difficulty and work my way up slowly. I enjoyed the journey and I had a fun challenge right from the start.I highly recommend this game to any Rhythm Game fan, even for those who want a more relaxed challenge, as the incredible selection of difficulty levels really caters to everyone.

_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a new and innovative rhythm game experience, this is it! Unlike the traditional press SDF JKL controls, this one works best with your mouse and will have you flick, tap, press, and follow along with music. It's extremely engrossing and engaging gameplay. It's perfectly suitable for beginners but I feel like experienced players would enjoy a breath of fresh air like this the most. It also has custom tracks you can download if you want something to really challenge you.We really need more official songs imo, though we have at least have a quality selection with some big names like Haywyre and Moe Shop.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game for more or less than a year at this point and this is just absolutely my favorite PC Rhythm game. The gameplay has been so far improved since its original iteration back when it was first released into Early Access proper, and they have done an excellent job making the game far more accessible and friendly for those who are just starting rhythm games. Honestly, it's really hard to say more about what makes this game so satisfying to play and get better at. It's also nice to have one of those games where peripherals are not a necessity. While the game was designed for using a MIDI turntable in mind, this game plays just fine with plain ol' mouse and keyboard, so you don't have to worry about dropping an extra $100+ on this in order to play and get through the harder difficulties.That being said, there are still some caveats. They've always been rather slow on the updates simply because getting licensing for songs to make new charts from is really very difficult, so if you're holding out for the full release (which I do think might be sometime this year if recent updates are any indication!) you might still be waiting a little while for this to happen.While there are definitely custom charts available via Spin Share, the unfortunate fact is that for a good 90% of those, you're absolutely going to need to be able to play on the highest difficulty this game has to offer. While some songs are easier than others in this regard, it has personally taken me well over a year to even get through one song in that difficulty. Suffice to say, a lot of the custom charts take that and ramp it up to eleven, so it is extremely difficult to enjoy them without being rather skilled at games like this.However, all that being said, this is not a fault of the developers. These things are taking time to iron out for when the game is released proper, and even in this state, I would still wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who loves rhythm games. I wouldn't recommend this as your FIRST rhythm game, but if this isn't that, I'd happily say go right ahead!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: For me personally, this is the best rhythm game made for PC. It's easy to get into but really difficult on higher difficulties. If you're a fan of the Guitar Hero/Rock Band series, I highly recommend this as it fills that spot perfectly. For it's price, you'll definitely get your money's worth. With that in mind, I'm giving it a 5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Cool and new concept for a rhythm game. I like how the game is multiplayer friendly with lobbies and leaderboards. Makes it so much better and more competitive. You can also download custom charts from websites which is awesome, as most rhythm games (excluding osu) don't allow custom songs and your stuck with what they give you. Which sucks if you're not into the music genre they provide. One thing I can say is that this game would attract a much bigger audience if they included more genres instead of just electronic/house music. Adding rock and metal songs would be nice, but the issue with obtaining the rights of the songs (copyright) is where I can see a bit of a struggle with adding some more popular songs. Overall a refreshing game that pulls some other rhythm games concepts together and creates a unique DJ type spin mechanic. A lot of rhythm games face the issue of not being able to keep the user engaged and want to play continuously, but with Spin Rhythm XD, I can see myself and the rhythm gaming community getting into this game and staying engaged. This game truly deserves the recognition. I feel it will become a known game as more streamers/youtubers play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I saw how this game looked and I was immediately interested. I'm happy to say that I wasn't disappointed. The controls are intuitive and quick to pick up. The online mode is great as well, the connection seems to be great and I like the light competition implemented each song. As for difficulty,  it seems to scale reasonably, although I have only played normal, hard, and a few expert songs.My main concern is that with certain backgrounds, I end up getting very dizzy and can't focus on the notes due to the motion in the background. It would be great to have an option to turn off the background or make it a static background so I wouldn't have to worry about having to restart until I get a background that doesn't make me dizzy.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels amazing to play.TLDR: An amazing rhythm game. Even at it's current state, it's 100% worth picking up if you have any interest in the genre.Pros: - Well balanced difficulty levels that work you through the core game-play mechanics- Definitely an easy game to get into, but hard to master - A game that helps you achieve a flow state that is satisfying- A great blend of EDM, Trance, Techno, Outrun, and Electronic tracks to play through- Custom track creator for more community content- Amazing mouse and keyboard controls- Has many settings to tweak controls and graphics.Cons:- I have to make myself consciously blink more because I stare too hard.Overall 10/10. The only things I wish for are more tracks to come and steam workshop integration for tracks. Also it could be cool to have different background colors for tracks.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm XD is the game that reignited my rhythm game fire.I honestly forget that this game is in Early Access sometimes. It's got ~40 tracks at the time of review, and the gameplay and presentation are EXTREMELY polished. It's super fun, the music is great and covers a wide spread of the electronic scene, and feels super great to improve at. It's also got custom track support and a built-in editor, which is great, and it's very accessible--you can play with keyboard+mouse, just keyboard, just mouse, controller, DJ turntable, and there's tons of visual accessibility options (including complete color customization).The devs are engaged with the community, receptive to feedback/new ideas, and continue to make really cool stuff happen.This game is really, really great. Easily my favorite game this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: About as close to a PC version of DJ Hero as you can get. The control scheme is so intuitive and works beautifully with mouse and keyboard (although other controllers are supported I haven't tried anything else) the visuals aren't too flashy they give off a modern/retro synthwave vibe. The color scheme works nicely to differentiate the notes and help you learn how to play while still being slick and visually pleasing. The song choices are a bit limited to mostly electronic (Like it's ALL monstercat stuff) which fits very well with the gameplay. Friend and online leaderboards help push you to compete against your friends and to beat your own times. It is possible to get a "Perfect" score and there's a good range of difficulties to ease yourself into it. The editor to create your own custom song levels is still a work in progress; I toyed around with it a little bit and made a simple track, but probably won't touch it again until it is updated. I would love to see more rock/metal songs implemented into the official game, and maybe make sharing your levels online and option, but due to copyright issues they can't just use any song which isn't there fault. So for now if you want more songs you have to manually share custom level files (via the official discord server which is always poppin)I've only played a few hours at the time of this review, but I'm a huge fan of Rhythm games in general so I'm excited to see what else it has to offer. I suspect in the future once I get perfect score on all the levels I'll crave something more, like a proper custom level editor, maybe a progression system and acheivments but this game at the core is a ton of fun. MUST HAVE if you're into Rhythm games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great rhythm game and is definitely one of my favourites. It has great music and most of the mechanics work very well and are enjoyable. As someone who is very bad at rhythm games this one has great difficulty scaling allowing for a steady skill increase.If you are looking to get into rhythm games this is a great offering that has something for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Been wanting a rhythm game to sink my teeth into since the days old of Guitar Hero and Tap Tap Revenge. SR:XD captures that skill competency of Guitar Hero and style of Tap Tap Revenge. The thing you control is instrument agnostic so there are a lot more genres this can tap into over time. The devs have been adding more and more songs with the official song list as of this writing with the base game is 50 tracks.They are continually adding more and if you wish to support the devs further do have extra song packs if you are interested.There is also a custom track maker built into the game while posting the tracks with copyrighted music is an issue searching for custom songs online is a "your millage may vary" since there is no official channel by which you can download custom tracks from.The game supports a wide array of inputs from keyboard and mouse to game pad. You can even get the game to register MIDI devices as a controller. The official SR:XD forums and discord hosts a lot more information on DJ pads and other MIDI devices that work with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, just overpriced given how much work it takes to do custom songs. _childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I used to be really into the old Tap Tap Revenge games on android and since it shut down over a decade ago I have not been able to find something as good or fun. This is it. This is the best rhythm game I have ever played. Having started out playing on the Hard difficulty and now being able to play the XD difficulty is extremely rewarding and satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: there are some things i'd like to see improved but honestly this is a functional, fun, playable rhythm game right now. unfortunately, the game feels perfectly engineered to cause motion sickness, and the .i love rhythm games, but a primordial soup of disabilities keep me from playing...any of them that i've found on pc actually.spin rhythm is largely playable even with significant disabilities. if you can use a computer independently, you can Almost Certainly play this. i played one-handed with just my mouse.mouse control feels natural. the amount of force you have to put into intiating a spin is low. you can't initiate a spin unless you're on a spin prompt, so you don't have to worry about doing it by accident when rapidly shifting colours or following a right-angle hold bar.i played a rhythm game for one and a half hours, i had fun, and my hands don't hurt. you have no idea how big of a deal that is.the only reason i stopped playing to write this review is because of that motion sickness i mentioned at the top. there's some decent choice, including at least two camellia tracks you've probably never heard before. there are Some pieces with lyrics, which i didn't play because i despise lyrics in rhythm games. there aren't that many, which is great for me.spin rhythm has its own custom beatmap creator, but no browser. there is a website called spinsha, but the files downloaded from there don't appear in the music browser or custom page when situated in the custom folder, and there are no instructions on properly installing them. assume you can only play the default maps. i couldn't figure out a way to get customs to work.if you miss a note some of the notes turn invisible. you can turn this off under "clear notes after misses" in the general settings, though!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface by saying I am by no means an expert at rhythm games. Spin Rhythm XD is a unique take on what a rhythm game could be. What may seem is a gimmick quickly becomes an intense stimulation of music, colors, and beep boopy notes. It is very well made; I did not run into any issues of any kind. For an early access game, you wouldn't be able to tell that it was in early access. The price is fair for the 50 songs and tight mechanics the game presents. At risk of sounding like some sort of drug addict - playing this game while on acid is absolutely amazing. Unlike most other rhythm games having to require so much focus and hitting so many buttons (djmax/osu for example), Spin Rhythm XD completely sucks you into the experience. The colors and effects that sync on the sides of the track adds a level of depth to the game where you lose yourself. It is reminiscent of Tetris Effect where you are essentially playing a game, but the feedback from visuals, sounds, and music make it a rewarding experience. This is definitely a game that I will continue to be playing for the years to come. It looks daunting and intimidating but I believe it is something everyone should try regardless of skill level.

_childDocuments_.review: I play music games because I enjoy the flow-state. The combination of tactile control options with SRXD's unique mechanics and aesthetic makes this one of the best for flow-seekers. If you have a Steam Deck, you ought to try this game. When the touchpad sensitivity and haptics are dialed-in, it feels like manipulating an object in space (like a turntable). Even if you don't have a Deck or turntable--even if you don't like other rhythm games--I encourage you to check this out.The challenge isn't about tapping more buttons faster, the controls are more varied. That also means the maps are significantly more expressive and immersive than most rhythm games. The rotating wheel mechanic (which honestly looked like a stupid gimmick when I first saw it) adds a kinetic aspect to the experience that makes it feel more fully embodied, almost like a dancing game you can do in your seat (which you can actually do if you enable gyro controls). More than any other rhythm game I've played, I feel the map-makers for these songs are choreographing motion and expression to involve players in the music in a way that makes other games feel like simple, masochistic finger exercises. It actually seems like a Ring Fit controller would work with this (which I tried with limited success...maybe someone more determined can make it happen). This means that SRXD works for music you don't often hear in the masochistic keyboard-tapping games. Smooth R&B, dreamy pop, and even acoustic singer/songwriter fit the format perfectly. Although the official music/maps skew toward stereotypical EDM, the community creations showcase songs in styles that wouldn't work well in other games. I hope the game's developers do more with this potential in their official releases.I could go on about other stuff I love about this game, but the last essential point for potential players is the overall visual aesthetic. The skins/backgrounds are dynamic, abstract, "futuristic" visualizers that respond to the gameplay, making for a more coherent and engaging multi-sensory experience for the player. This not only enhances flow, but you can play this confidently knowing that no random anime erotica is going to pop up on the screen.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good rhythm game with interesting and difficult to master mechanics. My problem with it is it's control scheme. I never quite liked playing games like these with a controller (since they need some automatic correction to line up right when playing and to me that feels cheaty among other things), so I went with my go to, a mouse. The problem is there is no way to rebind inputs from L and R click onto the keyboard. This not only feels awkward, it starts tiring out your wrist really quickly, it is the reason my play sessions on this game were much shorter than other rhythm games (Osu, Project DIVA Mega Mix, even FNF) and my wrists just couldn't handle it. This is exceptionally bad since on "Hard" or harder difficulties, you are  to use the space key to hit one of the notes which removed, for me, any reason to justify this choice. If you have DJ gear, I'd definitely recommend this, if you are fine with playing this on controller I'd recommend this, but I cannot say, personally, I'd recommend playing this game with a mouse, no way no how.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently developed a an injury in my left hand that has made playing games in general difficult. I happened upon SRXD entirely by accident, but looking at the control scheme I realized I could probably play it just fine with one hand. I've been playing it with a Mixtrack Pro, and I do still need to use my left hand to tap for the green Beats, but I can do that without aggravating the injury; worst case I could probably set up a foot pedal or something if it did cause problems. The game can also be played with a mouse and keyboard which feels less fun, but it's still great and I actually find myself more accurate controlling it that way than with the Mixtrack.All in all the game is great; a good selection of songs, and the ability to make custom tracks. There's even a website full of custom tracks, but almost all of them are only mapped out for the game's highest difficulty. I've been getting better but it feels like a long road before I'll be able to manage that.

_childDocuments_.review: "Spin Rhythm XD" is a gem in the rhythm game genre, blending the charm of classics like "Guitar Hero" with modern aesthetics and a stellar soundtrack. The intuitive controls support various devices, including MIDI DJ controllers. With over 60 tracks from renowned artists like Nitro Fun and Anamanaguchi, and five difficulty levels, the game suits both beginners and pros. The customization options and advanced level editor enhance its replay value. Stunning visuals and responsive backgrounds make this a must-have for music game enthusiasts, ensuring hours of captivating gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: There are two perspectives in life in regards to rhythm games in general. The first is life before Spin Rhythm, the second is life after spin rhythm.What does this mean? It means that I can't go back to games like Thumper, Rhythm Doctor, Melatonin, Kovox Pitch or Invector after playing Spin Rhythm.First off, the programming and input calibration options this game has makes the gameplay feel super tight and responsive to button presses - it's on another level. Problems with latency are basically non existent.Second, the gameplay itselft is deceivingly simple yet has a visceral effect on you. Whoever's responsible for programming the input patterns for each song has a spot on sense of musicality. It takes the gameplay from simply pressing buttons on time, to feeling like you're playing with the music in real time.Finally, the difficulty ramp is logical, steady and doesn't feel like the developers are trying to impress you with complex acrobatics or frustrating skill checks.This is, by far, the best rhythm game there is. Period.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fabulous guitar-hero-like. They've done a lot of great things with attention to detail, and the whole experience is very smooth. One really nice thing is that they rate their songs in terms of difficulty as a number, and that number is universal. so for instance, one song might be '12' on 'hard' difficulty, but another song might be a '12' on normal difficulty - and you'll find that they are basically the same difficulty, even though they have a category difference - it's just that the second one is inherently harder. I really gives you a good sense of 'I'm about a [number], and if I try this song, it's easy to tell if it's harder or easier than I'm used to, even beyond the simple difficulty category.One thing I wish it had, though, was progression. It's very satisfying to play, and very satisfying to feel yourself getting better- that's progression in itself - but I do wish that there was maybe a number beside your name that gave you an indicator of how many songs you've played, and your point total - something to compare to your friends at a global level, rather than just at the individual song level.The radio feature is nice, although there aren't a ton of players there right now, so it feels a bit empty - definitely a cool idea, though!Overall - great experience, would highly recommend to other folks who have been wanting something like guitar hero on PC for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great rhythm game, currently in active development. You might need some fiddling to find a good input method.
