_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a fresh concept for a rhythm game, and it's executed extremely well. Some of the most fun in a PC rhythm game you can have. Songs and charts are good (though a bit annoyingly long at times), community is good, and the game does receive updates here and there. There's a good amount of in-game customization to suit the player's needs, and it also supports MIDI controllers.I have a few complaints though; The fact we still have to use workarounds to chart swing properly is very disappointing since the community is practically striving off of custom charts as far as I can tell.Due to the skill cap of this game, I believe it's more fit for casual play than competitive unless the charting meta changes in unconventional ways. If you enjoy being competitive there is plenty of freedom to this, however you may find the official charts limiting in difficulty at the higher end. Thankfully there are a lot of custom charts out there to keep you playing awhile.Regardless, this game is a must buy if you like rhythm games, it's incredibly fun and a very fresh take on the rhythm genre and I recommend it very highly.+ Unique take on the rhythm genre that works incredibly well+ The game is very fun no matter your playstyle+ The songs and charts are good+ Global leaderboards for some competition+ A fairly simple to use level editor+ Some gameplay customization to suit players needs+ Dedicated practice mode with scrolling+ Game occasionally receives updates+ MIDI controller support- They're limiting players skills on the high-end with the current official charts- There's not a huge selection of songs, and playing them can feel repetitive after awhile (note there is an editor)- The editor is missing some essential features
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for solid rhythm game for PC for a while now. I used to play a lot of Osu! but it didn't quite scratch the rhythm game itch that Rock Band and Guitar Hero used to. I found Spin Rhythm XD and I can honestly say (imo) this is the best PC rhythm game out there. To me, this is to PC as Beat Saber is to VR. I've owned this game for 2 days as of this review and I've played so much more than I thought I would. It feels like a finished game. It shows almost no trace of "Early Access."The art style is super fun and stylized but not distracting while playing. The track is clear and easy to see. The controls are incredibly fun to use and can really get you into the song you are playing. The game is challenging, but offers a really nice practice tool that can loop the whole song, sections, and even slow them down. All the songs are EDM/Monstercat (which I'm a huge fan of so this is the cherry on top).I'm hooked. I love this game. I'm Looking forward to more songs and features in the future.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: In some nations that icon, with the two VR-clad people dancing, would be legally considered fraudulent marketing. This isn't a dancing game, this isn't a moving game, this isn't even a standing up game. You sit down, and scroll a wheel trying to match 1 of 2 colors coming towards you. I would most probably not enjoy this game on PC with mouse, keyboard, and monitor, where it belongs, some might, but on VR it's terrible - and pointless as a port. Can't speak for other platforms, but if you use Pico 4, don't buy this game even if you think you'd like this kind of game. The controls are horrible, you just have to point to the wheel (100x easier with a mouse and screen than VR) and make it spin, with close to zero VR enhanced feeling, and some blocks you have to move it and click the block (it says to click the wheel but you have to click the block) which in VR is so slow so....yeah, it just doesn't work at all. You can also change settings so you don't have to click the wheel (you still have to click the special blocks though), you can click anywhere to spin the wheel. But it works even worse with that setting, it's fully broken. If you spin to one direction you can't change the direction, and have to keep spinning that direction. Well 9 of 10 times, 1 in 10 it actually changes direction. Calling it wonky is way too kind.

_childDocuments_.review: I have NEVER liked a rhythm game, which is frustrating, because I often WANT to, I love music of all kinds, and beat heavy EDM or cheerful dance songs that generally populate these games are often amazing tracks. I've discovered some great music by watching my friends play rhythm games.  I've also discovered i suck at them.  THIS game, though, i'm not having to memorize what color is under what finger, its way more intuitive to me, without making it seem like its dumbed down or easier, especially on the harder difficulties, there is plenty to keep track of and i'm still not very good, there are songs i haven't beaten on Normal yet.  But for some reason...this game makes me grin.  Like, honest to god, sitting at my computer, and i get the spin right and  i'm grinning like an idiot.  No Idea why or how, but the developers have somehow distilled happiness from music and mouse moving and poured it straight into my brain.   There is only 15 songs/tracks/levels to play at the moment, but none are boring, although I do have favorites.  4.Inject,  6.Highscore, 10.Twistsound and 14.Razorsharp being my current faves.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good and unique rhythm game. I like the depth to the difficulty curve. Each new level of difficulty doesn't just get faster and more complex, it adds mechanics. So you can have a fun time learning the mechanics and still playing a pretty difficult song until you're ready for the next difficulty. It's also very unique in that it has multiple dimensions? to track. Like most rhythm games, you have the "position + click (+ hold)" dimension. You also have spinning (right, left, or back and forth). And you have beat (+ hold). This allows a lot of possibilities for charts and mixes things up significantly more than just being guitar hero with a disc jockey wheel.Soundtrack is . . . good. Has a mix of a few genres of mostly electronic music. I don't like the heavy dubstep so much but there's something in the soundtrack for everyone. Plus you can always add custom charts extremely easily. And there is a built-in chart creator. I don't take built-in chart support for granted since Beat Saber breaks mods every damn minor version incrementation.I am a seasoned rhythm game player and was able to play my first XD (Expert+) song after 10ish hours. There's a lot more to go and learn though. I'm excited to keep improving!!

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr, This game is awesome. Play it. Now. I really like this game. It's got a great balance of mechanics that keep you on your toes at all times, and the difficulty curve makes for a really low skill floor that's very easy to get into. The game basically progress through a number of difficulties: Easy, then moving up to Normal, onto Hard, Expert, and then finally XD. The way the levels are laid out, the player is encouraged to complete each level at a certain difficulty before rising to the next, and with over 40 tracks, you can get a lot of variety out of just the base game. Once the inevitable time comes when you can beat the hardest track on the hardest difficulty, you may think you are finished with the game, but I have good news; there is a semi-official custom level sharing platform call spinsha.re (semi-official because the devs are not technically allowed to support the sharing of copyrighted music). This extends the replayability infinitely as there are thousands of user-created charts for you to play and enjoy. That being said, this game is generally difficult and patience is pretty necessary, so if you don't have patience (which you probably do if you've read this far), it's probably not for you. Other than that, just buy it, this game slaps and you can always refund if you don't like it ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm XD is probably one of, if not the best non-VR-exclusive rhythm game on the entirety of Steam right now. It gets almost every fundamental aspect right, and I'd be more than happy to go over all of them. However, since this is my first in-depth review, I'll be splitting it up into sections based on my own reception.Warning: This goes on for way too long lolThe gameplay of SRXD is best described as fluent, fitting, and very fun. To elaborate, however, there are many aspects of the gameplay that make it shine out over many other rhythm games. First of all, the originality presented by the control scheme itself its extremely refreshing, providing a relatively unique experience for those who have played a lot of rhythm games. For new players to the rhythm game genre, however, difficulty is gradually eased and thoroughly marked, making the game a welcoming experience to new players as well. Of course, unique doesn't always equal fun; in this instance, however, it surely does, and for multiple reasons. First of all, the actions of matching, tapping, flicking, and scratching all feel exceptionally synchronized and fluid with the songs themselves. Additionally, the gameplay incorporates both aim and timing to create a very balanced system. Lastly, the various difficulties and upcoming challenge modes provide (and will provide) an good amount of replayability. That's not even mentioning the maps themselves which are mostly fun and enjoyable, if not occasionally a bit stamina-testing. Regardless, SRXD's gameplay is extremely polished.The design of SRXD is extremely pleasing to look at. If the appearance of some of the images and the trailer looked rough or even very nice to you, you should be happy to hear that these images are very outdated. The current designs of everything in the game, including menus, charts, and all other interfaces, are very sleek, employing nice colors and textures to create an exciting vibe. Despite the menus looking nice, I think that the most well-presented parts are found within the charts themselves. Notes are extremely clear and easy to read, and the tracks are filled with valuable information and details that you become very thankful for. On top of the tracks having lots of movement and detail, simple, lively backgrounds accompany the piece, either moving with the track or the beats of the song. Although it does require decent software to run, SRXD's visuals are very enjoyable.I've never really considered the quality of a game being determined by its community, but it is definitely worth it to say that SRXD's community is an involved one. People frequently create charts via the chart editor in-game, and their Discord server is also decently active. (Yes, there is a chart editor, and it's good quality.) What makes the game's community better, however, is the developers' involvement within it. In fact, the developers frequently hold charting competitions, in which players can submit their own charts of in-game songs, which is honestly quite nice. Overall, the community of SRXD is friendly and contributory.This will be a short segment, but there is an abundance of customization in the options menu. You can change the colors of notes, alter controls, edit detail levels and buffering rates, and do various other things to make your individual experience far better. While simple, I still feel like it deserved some recognition.Depending on who you are, you might not be a fan of the music selection, which I honestly wouldn't blame you for. It's a lot of EDM, ranging from Chiptune to Dubstep in its tracks. There is basically nothing besides that, excluding the abundance of fan-made charts of exterior songs. Additionally, you may feel that the current 38 songs in the game are not a large selection. While I wouldn't fault you for this, in my experience, I found that the songs provided by the game are all very enjoyable and have enough variation through vocals and instrumentation to keep me interested. This may be my love for EDM influencing my opinion, but still, I enjoy the tracks and how they fit the gameplay. Also, this game currently has an original soundtrack that, while short, is filled with back-to-back bops. Of course, others are free to disagree.While the game frequently gets new, free songs added to the game, there has been paid DLC packs announced as a part of the game's tracks. Of course, this isn't necessarily an issue, as I would absolutely be willing to give money for additional content from the game. Furthermore, the developers have mentioned themselves that free tracks will continue production after DLC packs are published. Still, though, some concerns about the systems should be addressed. For example, possibly having DLC-specific challenges would be rewarding to buyers, but if they limited non-DLC challenges, then they wouldn't be fair. Additionally, if you needed these packs to get onto the in-game leaderboards, then another case would occur. I hope that Super Spin Digital plans on separating DLC scores and challenges from non-DLC ones.Unfortunately, the game is not perfect, and a flaw appears most evidently in the multiplayer mode, Spin FM. To summarize the issue, it is boring. Communication with other players, if any are online, is limited, and gameplay barely feels intertwined with the other players. However, I have trouble fully faulting the game for this, though, as most rhythm games seem to have lackluster multiplayer or online modes. Luckily, multiplayer is not a crucial part of SRXD, and if you gathered up some friends in a Discord call, I'm certain the experience would be far more enjoyable, which the official server facilitates. However, it would be nice to see the current multiplayer options expanded on in some way.Spin Rhythm is an extremely good rhythm game that employs fluid gameplay, eye-catching visuals, and a great community to make the experience it provides extremely memorable and enjoyable. While some factors, such as its song choice and its  future DLC, may be off-putting to some players, others will fully and enjoy and embrace these elements. Finally, while some elements, such as multiplayer, are currently lacking, the game is only in early access, meaning that there is still development to undergo. Completing songs has always been one of my favorite parts or rhythm games, and if you decide to purchase this game, then I hope that you find some of the same successes that I did while playing.ok its over now

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Spin Rhythm XD is probably my favorite DDR-type game on the market right now.  I don't play a ton of games inspired by DDR.  I do really like avoid-em-up rhythm games like Just Shapes and Beats and Soundodger 2.  I was really impressed w/ both the pacing of the game, but also how well balanced every difficulty setting is.  When I first started playing, I had zero chance of surviving a level on Hard, and found Normal just right.  Within a few hrs, I found Normal levels to be a bit too easy and started taking on Hard levels.  Right now, just after about 6 hrs of playing, I have completed every level on Hard and am starting to complete levels on Expert.  I love the selection of music and really enjoyed all of the cool unlocks from cosmetics for the menus to the unlock of more songs/levels.  Consensus:-Excellent Game (Tier 2 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This is going to be a game that I come back to for years to come.  If you have any interest in rhythm games or DDR inspired games, this is a must buy.  There is a DLC that offers more music and I've read that it's really easy to download custom songs.  There is a ton of content and replayability packed into this rhythm gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly genius, it takes inspirations from many other rhythm games and mixes them with a brilliant twist that's both simple and hard to master. The biggest highlight of this game is the color wheel. You control it in various ways such as the mouse, gamepad and even midi (the devices that DJ's use) in order to match the incoming color. Then you have the wide notes where you need click on time, sometimes even hold and release. And then to wrap all of that, you also have the green lines that requires a different button to perform the same actions as the long red/blue notes. And let's not forget about my favorite part, spinning! It's in the name after all, they can be registered with a left/right flick. Throw all of that together with some spicy bangers and you got yourself and addicting gameplay loop! What can I say, one of the most if not THE most awesome looking rhythm game out there. To me, they strike a nice balance of aesthetically pleasing and clarity. And don't get me started on the backgrounds, the devs clearly put a lot of effort into them and it shows. This gives each individual map it's own aesthetic and makes them even more memorable. And let's not forget about the UI, which has that arcade flare mixed with minimalist design. All of that combined makes it very satisfying for both the player and the viewer. The game features a hefty amount of songs, but may be lacking in variety for some people. However the inclusion of the chart editor and custom song support nullifies this issue. I'd like to also point out the practice tool, which is one of the best I've seen. It allows you to practice specific portions of the chart, slow down speed, a quick restart button and much more!Can't say much about the chart editor since I haven't used it personally, but from what I've seen it's pretty good. Overall a great addition to the ever expanding rhythm genre that stands out from the competition. If you're a fan of these type of games then you own yourself to give this a try. And in my opinion it's well worth the full price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing rhythm games since 2003 and this is one of the best. It has intuitive controls and an AMAZING track list. Do yourself a favor and get it. _childDocuments_.review: Early Access Review as of December 28, 2019:From the video previews the game looked really interesting as well as aesthetically pleasing, $20 seemed like a bit much for an EA game so I jumped on the game once it went for sale, but the game almost grabbed me merely from the developer roadmap and what's in store for this game... but that's when it comes out, how is it now? Suprisingly content filled and extremely satisfying to play. Not counting the tutorial song, the game has around 23 tracks available to play ranging from more slow, chill techno tracks to more faster and heavier EDM. 23 songs is fairly light for any music game, but the overall execution of the gameplay and the other modes and additions really make this game very promising. But before I go on, I guess I should mention the controls of how this game is played. It looks a bit odd from the trailers and maybe a bit overwhelming, but once you play a song or two and get your bearings on the controls, it's very easy and addictive, I would find myself grinding out songs just to reach a higher score or get a Perfect S rating. Gameplay is mostly controlling a dial that spins left and right in order to aim the correct color to the corresponding notes on the track, with the bigger note blocks needing you to click on time and the spin notes essentially asking you to move your dial either left or right depending on the corresponding note direction, once in hard mode you get the addition of another note to interact with known as the beat which is represented by a green line on the track where you must press the space bar. Again, I imagine this sounds weird explaining, but in execution it's very simple and very engaging. But I've only really described how the game is played with a KB+M, there's actually dozens of more possibilities when it comes to playing this game from controller to whatever midi device you have, and even theoretically DJ Hero controllers. However you wish to play, there's dozens of mapping options and control methods at your disposal which makes this game very customizable in regards to gameplay. Content is where this game is heading in a really interesting direction and what maybe the deciding factor for those who wish to buy the game now, or wait until its completion. There's only 23 songs, all with 4 difficulty modes. Along side the base arcade mode, you also have a live music feature where players can casually jump in and out of without worrying about failing the song. It acts as a bare bones multiplayer mode where players just worry about trying to get the highest score, it works really well as a warm up/practice session where you get a rotation of random songs in the game to play while other players also try their hand at playing the song along with you, it's neat for what it is. There's also a daily run mode where players compete to see how far they get on the song of the day that gets chosen, players who complete it are then displayed on a leaderboard of their highest score and if they've failed the song, the difficulty is random so there's not much incentive for many casual players to jump in if the chosen daily song is of a higher difficulty than they're comfortable with. Lastly, there is promise of custom songs being a thing once the game completes, but legal issues regarding the usage of custom songs is going to be quite a challenge for the developers, so it's not known how this concept is going to be implemented just yet. There is however a level editor that allows you to change the charts of the songs already included in the game, it's a bit confusing to use at the moment, but the developers are looking on feedback on how to improve the feature and its UI. If and when custom songs become a thing, I have a feeling this particular feature is going to be a huge selling point for the game, making the $20 a worthy investment. It's all in a matter of waiting for more songs and features to be added along side polishing up the other modes. I really like where this game is going, it 'has' potential, but whether or not those expectations will be lived up to will be in due time. I think the game is very well worth investing in, the game has an active discord and steam community that gives feedback on the current progress of the games development and the amount of polish and passion the game has gives me hope this will be a game I'm very much looking forward to seeing completion in the coming updates ahead. I will still find reason to recommend this game to people even now, the gameplay is extremely fun and addictive and I'm willing to trust the devs in hopes of delivering a solid game experience in the near future.Keep your eyes out for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: SPEEN! Re-review!The controls are very intuitive, but can take a while to master. This is not a game you can start at the highest difficulty, you will want to gradually work your way up there. I can say after almost 8 hour I went from barely able to do hard, to easily doing most expert songs. Even my girlfriend, who usually doesn't play games, especially rhythm games, loved it. She was hitting the hard songs quite well.There's a great selection of EDM songs available, even if most are from Monstercat. This includes "Checkpoint", which most may know from the Sonic Mania reveal trailer. Only 15 songs at the moment, but none of them are bad.Updated: Since release there have been a few QoL changes. You now don't have to hold left click to spin the disc, before the disc would only move if you held left or right click. This option can also be disabled if you prefer the older version. You get extra points for releasing holds at the right moment, which are clearly indicated. You can see your time progress through the song without having the pause the song! WACOM and Windows Touch is now supported.There is now two ways to compete with friends and everyone else playing. There is a daily leaderboard to play through and score the highest on a song. Also a synced up "radio" live multiplayer, akin to either GHTV or OSU where you play for the highscore, but can't fail out.Also added were 8 new songs, bring the total to 23 songs.After just under 2 months in early access, Spin Rhythm XD has gone from amazing to even more amazing and proven itself as a worthwhile investment. On Discord the developers are especially responsive to feedback.Updated 2:In an early build (using code 'earlieraccess') you can find the new hardest difficulty, XD. I can say that this is indeed a massive difficulty jump from Expert, and it works fantastically. Currently only the first 9 songs have the new difficulty, but I believe 5 or 6 more are coming over the next few days. (and then the rest eventually)

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I don't usually write reviews for games, but honestly this one has been a real surprise pleasure. So keep in mind for this whole review that I haven't played a "rhythm game" since Guitar Hero if you can even count that. I bought this sort of on a whim because of the Monstercat label associated with it and went in with zero expectations. When I first started playing I was playing around the "hard" difficulty and it was fairly easy for me with minimal rhythm game experience. Since then, I've played 24 hours at the time of this review and am starting to break into the hardest difficulty (XD). The difficulty seems insurmountable at first, but you quickly adapt thanks to the intuitive controls and you feel a great sense of accomplishment getting to the next difficulty. I wholeheartedly recommend this to anyone and if I had one suggestion, it would be for more music and/or modding support (to add in custom songs). By the way, this song is totally doable with keyboard and mouse as that's what I use if you're worried that it is made more for a midi turntable.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good. It controls really well with keyboard and mouse, and I'm glad it doesn't necessitate the use of a peripheral input device for natural-feeling play like some other rhythm games do (I will forever be disappointed in the Groove Coaster port). Separating mechanics into different difficulties is genius and encourages mappers to create maps that match the difficulty of other maps of the same level. I feel like a few things hold it back from excellence though.I know the music is subjective but there is a lackluster selection of genres to pick from. A solid two thirds of the music I simply hate, but the last third is really good stuff.This would be solved by user-generated maps, but there is no way to share them from within the game itself. I assume that the discord has a channel for sharing custom maps, but I'm not interested in joining a discord and having to deal with its ♥♥♥♥♥♥ searching tools. I know that there is a 3rd party website, but I'm also not interested in downloading a custom client, and the folder for custom maps is annoying to maintain. It would be better if each map had its own sub-directory within the custom folder, and the best solution would be creating a custom file type that encodes all relevant data into one spot (it could really just be a glorified zip file). I understand that sharing maps is likely a difficult issue due to licensing, but I hope it is somehow addressed.A lot of issues with the gameplay itself can be fixed with the admittedly wonderful accessibility options. Seriously, please look at them. Its criminal that the game doesn't start with a calibration test because the audio was a solid half a second off by default for me.Overall, this is a wonderful game that I think will only get better with updates. Wish I could give it two thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only a great rhythm game but honestly probably one of the best rhythm games I've ever played. I don't think watching a video trailer for this game is really sufficient since what makes this game so good is how it FEELS to play, and you won't get that from the video. But it does have a demo! You should give that a try. This one really gives me the feeling I remember from early rhythm games where I just feel compelled to master it. That could take a while, though. This game gets HARD.What I appreciate about the challenge and difficulty in Spin Rhythm compared to other rhythm games is that there are so many different types of input, and it's deeper than just adding more buttons for you to press. Every type of input is a different type of action with your hands. There are the classic presses and holds from any rhythm game, but there are also the idle "drive over" notes from games like Audiosurf in addition to inputs unique to Spin Rhythm, such as different types of swipes and scratches. And since the harder difficulties have you play with both hands, you can also have double inputs. The result is that Spin Rhythm feels much more like desk-drumming or hand-dancing than the average rhythm game.It also means that it alleviates one of my pet peeves about some rhythm games which is that the challenge in the harder difficulties is still derived from complex rhythms and doesn't just devolve into machine gun fired input assaults.Check out the demo. The keyboard/mouse controls feel great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great gameplay, a must try if you are looking to for a new experience after playing rhythm games with just tapping to the beat. The only thing holding it back is the (planned) track selection. The game has a total of 40 tracks for the base game (50 with a future DLC) planned for when it comes out. This is very little for the price compared to other rhythm games like Muse Dash, a game with 68 tracks in the base game for $2.99 and with dlc 250+ for about 1.5 times the price of Spin Rhythm XD.I must say that the tracks are crafted with much care and feel great to play. I must also note that most difficulties don't cover the entire song but only parts of it, which can be disapointing if you only play this cassually and/or don't get a grip of the controls very fast and only play tracks of about 1:20 min.Overall I would reccomend but I would also hope way more tracks are to be added in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This is the rhythm game version of a wet dream. I have played so many different rhythm games throughout my whole life but I really don't think one is this PHYSICALLY exciting to play. Throwing your mouse across the desk to achieve spins is so cathartic I cannot explain it with words alone. Besides the incredibly amazing feeling gameplay, the official charts are also really really well done, the devs know what they're doing with that part of the game. They're slowly adding more over the course of the early access period for free as well, along with other quality of life changes and additions. There's an official built-in level editor already and it's pretty damn good and is going to be getting an overhaul at some point (at least as of the point of writing) to make it even more intuitive to actually create charts. A few problems I have with the game at the moment are a lack of multiplayer lobbies, and not a huge diversity of music, as it's mostly electronic styled stuff along the lines of things you hear from Monstercat. I really can't think of many problems I have with the game. Nothing has ever really made me think "oh if this wasn't in it it'd be better" or similar.The game is fantastic, and if you like rhythm games at all you should definitely pick it up full price. 9.5/10 :)

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for less than an hour, and all I can say is, I want to be good at this game.There are only 2 colours to focus on, but the number of mechanics involved, that's what makes this game so difficult to play. But that's exactly how I like it.If I was to compare this to an existing game, DJ hero would be the closest, but still doesn't compare to this game. I've played a few different types of rhythm games, most of them consist of just hitting and holding notes, but this has 5 mechanics in play -- Hold, Tap, Rotate, Spin, Beat.Surprised that it's early access, it's rather flawless in both performance and design, even through a compatibility layer (Wine) for Linux. Really enjoying this game, will take time to learn how to play it, will likely need 10 hours of game play before I can even attempt hard songs.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to find new rhythm games that strike the right balance of elegant simplicity and difficulty that's easy to pick up but hard to master these days and this game nails it. It even passes the litmus test of a good rhythm game always having at least one Camellia tack in it's vanilla chart list. I was initially worried that this game wouldn't be fun to play unless I had a dedicated MIDI Turntable Controller to play it but I'm playing expert difficulty tracks decently well with just a mouse and keyboard only 9 hours into the game as I write this review , so you're probably gonna be fine on that front even if this game is screaming for you to get a dedicated controller of some kind. I'm having a lot of fun without one, though I do recommend a relatively large mousepad like a Fragmat so you can do wide swipes and a mechanical keyboard with a good click for hitting your spacebar for maximum comfort if you're gonna go controller-less.If I had one complaint which isn't even really the game's fault, it's that the community made charts are pretty much 90% XD difficulty only, so unless you see custom tracks as kind of a hybrid of both an intrinsic and extrinsic reward for getting better at the game, you're gonna be sticking to the vanilla charts of this game for a few hours to get the hang of a few things first.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of Rhythm games, but this is my first one that I've really been able to get into for PC. For those of you like me who was on the fence about getting this game, here's a few reasons why I think you should try it out: - Very fluid controls. Not the easiest to get the hang of but they're very satisfying and make me shiver when I get a really hard section right. Learning to hit beats and spins properly feels really good, especially if its in a hard passage. - Variety of songs. This game, unlike most I've played, isn't just loud and boring dubstep. There are the occasional dubstep songs in there to appease the masses, but this game also has some beautiful melodic songs, some retro songs, and even a straight up song you'd hear in a crossfit class. It really covers the genres that rhythm games are good for and the drops are awesome. - Evenly-spaced skill ceiling. Most rhythm games are either abhorrently easy, or just plain stupid. Spin Rhythm XD makes even easy and medium level songs feel satisfying to play, so you can still have fun while you're learning the controls. The jumps to each difficulty feel warranted, and also rewarding to get to. They'll take a while to get the hang of, but it's really easy to see your progress as you get better and learn to play the harder songs (The game organizes songs by difficulty, which is also really helpful for learning) - Graphics. Obviously when you're playing the songs you're at the level to, you won't have time to stop and admire the things that are happening in the background. But if you've already learnt a song or just wanna chill on a lower difficulty, you'll realize just how beautiful the background is. Some songs (not all) have beat maps in the background and it feels really cool to see, especially on hard songs and above that have more beats and taps.My only real gripe with this game is that there aren't enough tracks for me. Granted, almost all the songs on there are absolute bangers, but once you learn all of them, you'll lose interest kinda fast. Luckily for me I'm still working on getting to the last difficulty, so I've still got plenty more to play! I'm also really hoping more songs will get put in, as the game is still only in early release, so if everything works out, this could easily become my favourite rhythm game. :-)

_childDocuments_.review: If you own a MIDI DJ controller, you owe it to yourself to at least give this game a try. The devs have found a clever way to introduce novel mechanics to a music/rhythm game without having to invest in manufacturing plastic instruments. The keyboard and mouse control scheme is also perfectly usable and still plenty of fun, but this really uses the jog wheels of a dedicated DJ controller to great effect. Spinning and tapping the wheel feels responsive and, more importantly, precise. The game has incredibly flexible options for control setup and calibration for almost any MIDI controller you could possibly throw at it. This hits the rhythm game sweet spot: Easy concept to pick up, still fun on lower difficulties, but plenty of great challenge as you push yourself to higher difficulty levels. I'm really looking forward to the full release on this one. The devs have been very communicative and have a clearly defined roadmap for the future.p.s. if this does end up allowing for user submitted tracks, either through the workshop or through third party modding somehow, hot damn we are looking at the second coming of the rhythm game messiah

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews for games but had to write something positive about this one. I don't have the biggest background in rhythm games but what drew me to this one over alternatives like Osu is the gameplay and music selection. There's something very intuitive about how the gameplay is set up that after around 5ish hours, I found myself moving up from Easy to Normal to Hard, the game knows how to throw new challenges at you while also being somewhat forgiving. And I loved the added touch of tutorials for new mechanics the first time I decided to jump up to a new level of difficulty. It's a game where around Normal difficulty you can kind of turn your brain off if you don't have much capacity but requires some focus when you get into Hard/Expert territory. Beyond that, I was also blown away by the amount of customization to the gameplay, from changing your slider to menu colors, note colors, and more; the Devs really put the power to make this game feel very personal to the gamer. While I'm a big fan of the broad ranging selection of EDM songs in the library to choose from, I think at the moment the only thing I'd like to see in the future is a major expansion to the song library. After 6 hours of play, I was able to unlock all of the songs and play 3/4 of those that interested me multiple times on varying difficulties. Don't get me wrong, it's fun to continously challenge myself on the same song/level at different difficulties for added challenges, but I do see this getting old a bit soon. I think it'd be great if the Devs could find more opportunities for collaborations with music labels and artists or attempt to follow in the footsteps of a game like Geometry Dash where Robtob Games was able to ride that copyright-grey area for level creators to make custom levels for the community to access. I really think this game has the potential to be something similar in community structure to a Geometry Dash, but I think what's missing is a larger music library, and a community-driven custom-level editor and library as well. But overall, a super enjoyable game and I highly recommend!

I'm colorblind and trust me, they couldn't have added a better color selection system.- Compatible with million devices, with no advantage for people owning the more exclusive ones.- Mechanics are great, you keep coming back for more and really encourages you to get better.- Online functionalities and leaderboards that will probably get even better in the future.The music game genre is not dead and these devs made a huge step forward with this game. If you have some remote appreciation to rhythm games or are just curious, do yourself a favor and buy this gem!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the rhythm game I've needed for years. After dumping thousands of hours into others such as the Guitar Hero and Rock Band series, DDR/Stepmania, Beat Saber, Audiosurf, JSAB, and more, I had been on the lookout for something to continue to feed my desire for rhythm. This does so with flare and adrenaline.Spin Rhythm XD is a revival of the genre in a loud, boisterous way. 30 songs (with more to come) of some of the heaviest electronic, drum and bass, dubstep, house, trance, chiptune, synthpop, and more in music, with a playstyle that is exceptionally fun to use. Matching notes to a colored wheel alternating pink and blue, and timing taps, holds, spins, beats, and beat holds, increasing in intensity per difficulty, which ranges from the friendly Easy to the soul-crushing XD (Extreme Difficulty). Easy to learn, borderline insane to master. The game offers numerous ways to play, from M+K, gamepad, controllers, and even many models of turntables can work in tandem!The feeling of nailing notes on higher difficulties is phenomenal and I have personally FC'ed numerous Expert songs, which is a great sensation of victory. And the soundtrack gets better and better, with some of my personal favorite electronic artists making it in, and plenty of excellent tracks to discover. A nicely defined curve in challenge can allow veterans to adapt to gameplay quickly, while still being welcoming for newcomers, and the community is just awesome. Dedicated developers alongside fans and creators make for one great team, and I cannot wait until this game fully releases.SRXD is a gem and a wonderfully crafted production of music euphoria. Buy it. If you love rhythm games, don't even second guess it. 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: With eye candy graphics and a soundtrack that bops, I can confidently recommend this one. While it IS early access, and I'd usually advise against these, the developers are actually actively improving and adding to the game such as adding new songs, game modes, and potentially custom songs. The game is friendly to all skill levels and even has a practice mode where you can adjust the speed of the songs on each difficulty. There IS multiplayer as well as leaderboards for any of you tryhards that wanna do the impossible.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm XD has been a hallmark of gaming for myself over the past 2.5 years. The game, at its core, is a fluid, fast, and frantic rhythm game that puts emphasis on the movement as much as it does the rhythm. The unique angle that Spin Rhythm XD prides itself on is the implementation of momentum movement through flick spins and scratch notes, accurate movement with tap notes and match notes, and steady rhythm with the beat bar, usually played on a hand different from the spins and taps. These mechanics got me hooked instantly, and led me to over 2,700 hours and counting.The base game songs included with the purchase are a great way to understand the main mechanics and get you thinking about what possibilities could be made real with custom charting, which this game also has plenty of for those who seek a challenge. The music selection is great and filled with bangers and enjoyable listens. 5 difficulties ranging from easy to the flagship difficulty "XD" means that there is something for everyone and plenty of ways to improve. One of the best aspects of this game is its approach to accessibility. Nearly everything about your experience is customizable. from custom skins, track skins, and menu palettes, to changing note colors, to adjusting the background to be simpler or have no background at all, and even being able to disable track motion, track speed, and move around nearly everything on the in-game HUD to be as easy to read as possible. the in-depth options to make your experience as great as possible has a lasting effect on those who have those specific needs.Congratulations to the developers for finally leaving early access, and thank you for making a game that has had such a huge impact for me and for many others. And if you are reading this review and don't have this amazing rhythm experience yet, do yourself a favor and pick it up now.

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm XD is the logical next step past DJ Hero. In this game you control a wheel on the bottom of the screen by turning it left or right and tap, flick, and hold notes to the beat! While the game supports controllers and keyboard + mouse, the real heart of this game's controls lies within it's MIDI device compatibility. So long as you computer recognizes your device as a MIDI Controller, there is a high chance you'll be able to connect it, get the controls mapped appropriately, and get to spinning! I play the game with a Pioneer DDJ-200, which has two touch sensitive jog wheels and the game feels like a dream to play.Currently there are 15 songs in the game, which is a fairly small number, but the developers plan on steadily adding songs during Early Access leading up to the full release. With four difficulties to play on (With a fifth on the way!) the game gradually introduces you to additional mechanics, and sometimes more length of the song in a second boss phase-like fashion. If you are a fan of rhythm games the game will offer a fresh experience you're sure to enjoy, and so far I've loved every minute.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking for a rhythm game that connected with me for a while, playing a lot of different games such as Guitar Hero, Osu (and Osu mania), and various mobile games such as Deemo. Spin Rhythm has been the game that has connected with me the most and I have dedicated more than a hundred hours to this game.The game starts out slow, with the easy difficulty introducing you to the unique gameplay mechanic of spinning the wheel to match the appropriate color. The game then introduces other mechanics, such as taps, holds, directional spins, scratches (shakes? idk), beats, and, finally, beat holds. It is easy to learn, and the difficulty curve is smooth, with the highest difficulty introducing some of the best the game has to offer mechanics-wise.The game's customization is great. you can change the colors of any note, make the different color notes shaped differently, and also allows you to remove potentially distracting elements such as the background.Finally, the game's custom scene. You can play charts created by other users or create your own. Spin Rhythm can't host custom charts due to copyright/licencing issues, but you can easily access them online through third party tools such as . The only issue is that most of the charts are pretty damn difficult with no easier difficulty available, so unless you are at least able to play in XD difficulty in the base game, your options are pretty limited.Overall, this game is great. I have been happily playing customs and I am even considering entering a tournament in the future. If you have any interest in playing the game, give it a try. At best, you will have a new game to dedicate time to. At worst, you just return it after an hour or so of playing.

Just. Worked.I genuinely do recommend not using external controllers though, as playing this game with motion tracked controllers just feels like the way it has always meant to be. _childDocuments_.review: Very unique rhythm game which was designed around the concept of playing a rhythm game via MIDI using an actual DJ controller, although you can also play this game with many other ways too, including the standard KB+M and console game controller methods. The community of this game is extra special for having Pioneer'd some truly extraordinary ways to play the game... how about using an old retired HDD or DVD player's spinning disc as a MIDI controller for the jogwheel mechanism of the game? :D The #unique-controllers channel of Spin Rhythm XD's Discord server truly is a work of some god-tier custom gameplay pioneer art. :DAnyways, the way this rhythm game's mechanics have been designed around the use of a DJ controller makes the gameplay feel really intuitive and fun when you use an actual DJ controller! :DThe music selections for base game feature less Hardcore stuff and more different kinds of Bass Music songs but you do find a couple of licensed Camellia tracks and honestly the song catalogue is pretty cool. :D And who knows what music gets added in the future, especially with the future DLCs <3 SRXD does also have a very active community making custom charts, though obviously officially you can only do custom charts for the songs already built-in. ;3

_childDocuments_.review: the best quality of the famously doomed "pick a song from a list and play the track while hitting notes" genre of rhythm games was that interacting with the music in a tangible way made the experience of listening to the music that much better. you could play an entire album in rock band and explore your favorite music in a brand new way. better still was when that interaction involved physicality--moving your hands and your body, rather than just pressing a button on a gamepad or a touch screen. in that regard, spin rhythm kind of reminds me of dj hero, one of the most underrated rhythm games of that era, and a game we did not deserve. there was  like spinning and scratching that platter, flicking the track switch, and not rabidly button mashing the way guitar hero and rock band had you doing. i think the spirit of that design lives on in this game, in that moment when i flick the mouse and let go of LMB to watch the spinner spin infinitely until i hit the button to stop and keep hitting the notes. it's in slamming the space bar along to the green notes, and in tracking a held note from one side of the track to the other. it's in that moment when my heart is palpitating trying to keep up with what my hands are doing when the base drops on rattlesnake, or when my hand makes the wheel groove along to velours, or when reach you trades its first base drop for a small spiritual experience. the best rhythm games enhance your encounter with a song, or an album, and if good music makes life worth living, well then so does this game.edit 9/13/2020: now that even more tracks have been added, new gameplay features have been included, and a new difficulty has been introduced, the longevity of this game has skyrocketed. i kinda bottomed out after S ranking most of the songs on expert, but XD kicked my butt at first. the end goal of long term play on this game i think ends up being the XD difficulty, as well as the ability to download and create custom tracks for songs not included in the game. if more people get on this game and start tracking more different genres than just various flavors of EDM, then i think this game has the potential to become the perfect rhythm game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extremely fun game. It is a fresh take on they music/rhythm genre, and supports a variety of ways of controlling it.My main method is mouse + space bar. _childDocuments_.review: Good music, addictive gameplay, very accessible, and inexpensive. Spin Rhythm XD is what happens when you cross Guitar Hero with Beatmania, and it works beautifully. The music tracks are familiar to anyone who has used the internet in the last 5 years, but also the original tracks are a great listen, I find. Music taste is entirely subjective, but if you like EDM or just electronic music at all, there's definitely some tracks in here you'll enjoy.The gameplay is easily the best part of this game. Not only can you fine tune settings, but the range of controllers this game allows is insane. You can use traditional controllers, kbm, just keyboard, just mouse, or even an actual DJ controller. That last one I highly recommend because it helps to completely immerse you into the game. That said, don't go investing a significant amount of money into one just to play this game, but if you're really hardcore into it, I'd say there's no harm in at least getting a cheap one if you're so inclined.Back to the gameplay, like I said, its Guitar Hero mixed with Beatmania. Not 1-to-1, obviously, it's close enough while still deviating enough to be its own thing. The best part, I would say, is how each difficulty level adds new mechanics for extra challenge. It's not like other rhythm games that just add more buttons to push, it actively changes how you play. This works both ways, giving those that just want a more relaxed time less to worry about. Each song effectively gets 5 different charts, which adds a ton of replayability.With both the wide controller and gameplay options, this game is heavily accessible wherever it can be as well. You can fine tune audio, tweak how gameplay works across all difficulties, adjust the visuals, and not just in the normal way most games let you. You can change the colors of all the UI aspects to whatever you want, you can move UI elements to different positions, or just remove them entirely, and you can even change the way the UI looks with the different skins and background colors you unlock by playing. That being said, I wish there was more freedom on where to move UI elements, other than just the presets.All this said, the game is also only $20. I know that's asking a lot for an indie title, but compared to other rhythm games I've played, this offers more and asks for a lot less. It's definitely worth the price tag and if you like rhythm games at all, especially Beatmania, you should consider adding this to your collection.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this out by saying this game is VERY fun. I love, love rhythm games and this game is a dream to play. I love the DJ theme. I never really thought it could be fun to play a rhythm game with just the mouse, but this is exactly that game. Even though its still in development, its very well polished. The game feels good to play. I only have one complaint and this is something almost every rhythm game fails at, so its not really a problem specific to Spin Rhythm. I normally play every song on easy when I start a new rhythm game, just to get a feel for the mechanics and the songs themselves. I know a lot of veteran rhythm game players just jump to the highest difficulty, but i like to get a good feel for everything first, plus it helps me understand how a beginner would play the game. I think the easy mode is good and this game is very easy to pick up and play. The learning curve isnt super high. The problem arises when you move on from easy to normal. Rhythm games always ax one mechanic from easy mode that is in every other mode and in this game its the holds. By the time I got acquainted with all of the songs and moved to normal i completely forgot holds were even a thing because aside from the tutorial they aren't in easy mode. I think its very hard for new players to move on from easy mode because of this. I think holds should be included very minimally in easy mode. I wish every rhythm game included ALL mechanics in easier modes just to get players used to them so the transition from difficulty to difficulty is smoother. Like I said, almost every rhythm game struggles with this so  it doesn't make or break the game for me, but it is something to consider! Otherwise I really love it and am definitely excited to see what updates this game will have in the future. I cant wait for more songs and modes. I think the online stuff will be really fun once more people are playing the game. I'm really happy I decided to buy it, and if you love rhythm games with EDM based music you should too!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun take on the rhythm game genre. I would imagine it's difficult to compete with Osu since it has such a huge map library and it's free. The spinny dial gimmick for hitting notes to the beat is interesting, at first it felt awkward, but after a while it starts to click. The gameplay here feels more cerebral than most note-hitty games, it's taxing my brain a bit more than I expected to get the hang of it. There's the typical tap notes and hold notes, but they're constantly being combined and overlapped in a way that I have to stay focused to keep up with the beat. They incorporated the dial spin to hit directional notes which is pretty neat.  This game has taken big strides in the updates since early access. The user generated maps will make or break this game, so I hope that they make moves in the future to fully incorporate some kind of in-game map search. It's also missing some great features you'd see in Osu! like replays, difficulty modifiers, profile lookup, etc. If you like rhythm games, don't sleep on this title.

_childDocuments_.review: This game exemplifies the phrase "Easy to learn, hard to master". At over 100 hours played, I can safely say this is easily my most played game over the last couple of months, and I'll happily say it's time & money well spent! The difficulty curve, for the most part, is very nicely smoothed out. Easy up to Expert level is progressive, and while the jump to the highest difficulty "XD" is a touch jarring, the latest update brings in a couple of welcome features; the first of which being a numeric difficulty rating for each track & difficulty - allowing those making the leap to the highest difficulty, to have a better idea of where to start. The second is an Accessibility menu - enabling low-motion backgrounds for those who may find a lot of background movement distracting, customizable track speed & various graphical aids to assist in following the action.Alongside all of this, I'll say that the SR community is an absolute gem - nothing but positive vibes, and the developers are always working to improve what is already my top pick for 2020.Put simply, if you enjoy a good rhythm game, there's a very strong chance you'll love this masterpiece. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: My coordination is terrible, something I've learned playing Thumper. Knowing how much I suck at later levels of that game, it was obvious to me I'd be awful at the hard difficulty in Spin Rhythm. Why am I even mentioning it? Because my god, even if you do play like crap, it's still satisfying. I've found myself bobbing my head or swaying to the music more often than getting angry ALTHOUGH I have to say those thudding noises whenever you make a mistake are so discouraging, I lose focus. But then again, I had the same gripe with Thumper, so I could be alone in this. Another nitpick I have is the difficulty spike between normal and hard. You have more nuanced difficult levels, but only two easier levels of the same song. Maybe if the easy and normal songs could last longer? I burned quickly through the songs on those two modes, and hard is just.... really frustrating for me :D But again, I emphasize - I could just be sh*t at rhythm games and can't accept it, hahahaha.EDIT: I've now racked up around 16 hrs, and you DO get better without even noticing it. I laugh in the face of my old inexperienced, frustrated self. YOU WERE A FOOL. NOW YOU ARE ONE WITH THE SPINNING DISK THINGY.In all seriousness, after all these hours, I can now play any track on hard, and while some expert difficulty tracks are still a challenge, they're fun, even when you fail. The XD difficulty is still atrocious and I'm not even bothering :D //EDITAll that aside, I know this game is a keeper for me, because for the past three days, every time I sit at my computer I go: "Y' know what, I could do a song or two right now." And that happens to me SO rarely nowadays. That a game manages to frustrate me, yet drags me back the next day. AND IT'S JUST A RHYTHM GAME?! Anyway, thanks for a really cool and cute game, Super Spin team. Eagerly awaiting more songs because most of these are my favorite genres of electronic music! Keep doing the good work. Also, steam workshop for the level editors when? I can't wait to see what people come up with ♥

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best rhythm games I have ever played, and I have played many, ranging from OSU! on the DS (both the original and the western version – EBA) to Guitar Hero and Rock Band on consoles, to Cytus on Android. It offers a unique experience that diverges from the typical formula, and it takes some time to adapt and become proficient at. Despite my age, I still consider myself to be "good" at these types of games, and it took me over 25 hours to beat all 60 songs on XD (combining practice and actual play time). The playability is also great, as you can competently play it with either a mouse and keyboard or a controller. Additionally, the practice section is also excellently implemented. You can practice sections of a song at arbitrary speeds, which is especially helpful for higher difficulty levels (28 and above).If you like rhythm games don't miss out on this one. It's different, polished, and definitely worth a try. I highly recommend it, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play rhythm games but I've been trying new genres and picked this up during a sale.I really like this game. The game's unique twist is you rotate a disc to match the same color notes, like a DJ version of Guitar Hero. It sounds a little weird but spinning the disc is probably my favorite part. And when you're grooving it feels like you're actually playing the song. I don't play any instruments, but playing this I can catch a glimpse of what it feels like to jam out on an electric guitar.The game is very well polished and looks beautiful. There's support for turn tables, but just swiping a mouse is surprisingly satisfying. There's around 40 songs at this point, many from big name artists. I don't listen to much electronic so the selection is a bit hit or miss, but there's a few amazing tracks. Given I primarily only play a dozen or so songs, selection is my main gripe with the game. I hope they add a few more before release, but beyond that I think it'd be fair for the developers to start selling tracks in game or via DLC's.I don't usually leave reviews but I like supporting quality indie games. The developers seem responsive so I'm hopeful the game will continually get better!

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER TO POTENTIAL PLAYERS:  I think I hurt my wrist doing the Sliders (rapid horizontal mouse swipe) since there is no setting to reduce how much you need to slide the mouse without also increasing the  mouse sensitivity (I like playing on lower sensitivity to match the DJ wheel onscreen). _childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm XD is a promising and unique rhythm game in a genre that rarely changes, it’s a welcome change.IntroSpin Rhythm XD is a new rhythm game that’s currently making it’s way through it’s Early Access stage for the remainder of it’s development. It’s soundtrack is 100% electronic music, but this is pretty common among rhythm games, but if it’s a genre you’re not a fan of then you’ll likely be kinda disappointed. Onward to the preview!Song SelectionSpin Rhythm XD has a pretty varied selection of songs already. Even though they’re all some form of Electronic music, they’re all unique from each other and none of them sound like repeats of other songs. As of writing this preview there are 18 songs featured in the game with a planned track list of 30. You can also create your own custom tracks using the licensed music included. There’s a planned feature that will allow you to use your own music but this feature hasn’t been added as of writing this.GameplaySpin Rhythm XD’s gameplay is pretty unique compared to many other rhythm games. It puts a new “spin” on the genre, so to speak. To score points you must move the pink and blue wheel at the bottom of the screen to line up with the colors that flow towards it. This is really simple on easy but when you get to expert it proves to be an immense challenge due to how fast it moves as well as the crazy amount of things you have to do. It’s a multi-tasker’s paradise but I had quite a bit of trouble getting used to it. This is my first rhythm game in years so I’m pretty rusty. That said, I know a quality game when I see one and Spin Rhythm XD’s gameplay is not only unique but really fun too.One really nice thing about the game is that it supports a fairly wide range of control methods. You can use just a mouse, your mouse and keyboard together, a controller, or even a midi DJ’s turn table. Which is pretty impressive, and I can only imagine how it plays with a turn table, but it’s a pretty fitting method of playing the game, considering. I noticed there are videos of people using one on YouTube though.The game features 4 difficulty levels to play and each one not only increases the difficulty but also increases the length of the song. As an example, the first song in the game is 1 minute 30 seconds on easy but on expert it’s 2 minutes and 9 seconds. Hard and expert are the same length of time. The difficulty level also adds more things to the track that you’ll need to work through.There’s also a full leaderboard for each song, a daily challenge, and a weekly challenge with modifiers added to the song.Overall, Spin Rhythm XD is an incredibly promising rhythm game in a genre that very rarely changes. It already feels incredibly polished and has enough content to make it a worthwhile purchase right now. It even has a very positive rating on Steam, so it’s already pretty popular. I’m looking forward to seeing how the game turns out when it officially launches out of Early Access in the future. Definitely one to keep an eye on if you’re a fan of rhythm games.Be sure to visit  for in-depth reviews daily.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much exactly what I was looking for. The songs to pick from are awesome, the controls give a lot of freedom as well as customization (I use a PS4 controller but I suggest playing around a little to figure out what works for you - everyone seems to have a unique opinion here), and the practice mode is so easy to jump into and hammer away at a section that gives you trouble. The only real gripe I have with the game is that easier difficulties strip away certain mechanics and parts of the song, though that could be seen as a reason to try to improve as a player and it kind of makes sense why it was done this way. All in all, if you have any interest in rhythm games, Spin Rhythm XD is definitely worth buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique rhythm game concept.This game looks easy when you watch the trailers. Don't be fooled.There's a lot to think about during a song, and pulling off those tricky sections isn't easy. It's amazing how great the game is at teaching you though. Two concise yet detailed tutorials explain the basic and advanced mechanics, then 5 difficulties on each level let you go at your own speed (although my god the highest difficulty is ridiculous). The songs also have difficulty ratings as a whole, so the first song on expert is much easier than the twentieth song on expert.The scoring system is robust and rewards timing + combos with a letter grade from D to S. It's simple but it works. There's leaderboards for each difficulty of each song, and a daily song with it's own leaderboard which gets reset every day. Sadly, no unlocks or achievements for getting a top spot on a daily, but maybe that will be added. Nonetheless, chasing high scores is good fun.There's a level editor which is relatively easy to use and lets you make custom maps for any song in the game.The multiplayer is simple and casual, but fun to hang around and see who can get the higher score.This game has a ton of potential and I hope to see new modes, songs, and other features added soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of experience playing rhythm games, and Spin Rhythm XD is probably the most satisfying one I've ever played. It's such a unique concept that really sets it apart from the rest of the genre and is simply designed around a core mechanic that makes it feel great to play. All the note types are quite intuitive and flow well together. The song selection is pretty wide which really helps with difficulty scaling; if you play through most of the levels on one difficulty, you'll get substantially better at the game to the point of being ready to tackle the next difficulty up. Also, I found myself missing out on this a lot because I was so focused on the track, but the 3D environments in the background of each level are absolutely awesome. Additionally, creating/downloading custom songs is super accessible and easy, which is a huge plus for any rhythm game. I went into Spin Rhythm XD knowing I was going to have fun, and it still totally exceeded my expectations. Simply an outstanding game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played my fair share of rhythm games over the years, but Spin Rhythm has been the first one in a long time that felt almost natural to play, even on a mouse and keyboard. It's obvious the developers have put a lot of thought into the controls.It doesn't seem to focus on raw speed either, which is a great change of pace from many rhythm games out there, instead focusing on immersion with the music. Each and every track event lands on some form of strong event in the song, and builds/releases in the tension all flow with the charting perfectly.The song selection has grown substantially since 2019 as well, and the variety of music added to the game definitely fills a lot of gaps the setlist had back then. I look forward to future content from the developers, as nearly everything they've added thus far has been incredibly well polished and a total blast to play. The advent of Spin Share making it significantly easier to install custom songs has also been a welcome community effort, further expanding the potential setlist to thousands of songs, and the fact that custom songs even have leaderboards is an incredible forethought by the developers!I do wish there weren't fixed rate values in practice mode, as learning a difficult section in a song can be a bit of a slog with only being able to choose between 50/75/85/100/120%. I also wish there was a simpler method of calibration, as the current interface can be somewhat confusing for players who are new to rhythm games as a whole.In all, Spin Rhythm has accomplished what many rhythm games can only hope to achieve, and I look forward to seeing what happens in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: The more modern sleeker version of Audiosurf with a better matching system.In Audiosurf you match blocks in stacks to collect your points, a different take on music rhythm games. Whereas Spin Rhythm is a combination of spinning the wheel, tapping with the mouse, tapping with the spacebar, and probably something else I am forgetting. I've covered most of the easy/normal variants, not all, but making my way [downtown] having some fun with it.It's an addicting, fun for all ages, electronic dance music loving rhythm matching game.Super easy game to play, super hard game to master. So far it's a lot of fun on easy/normal - but dang if you like the competitive edge then you'll love hard+ | props to those players who can compete up there. They have leaderboards for friends/global, they update on the fly, and they have a decent selection of tracks (50 songs). I wish they had more songs or the ability for you to play your own music, I haven't figured out if that's possible yet. The create your own track tools are a bit confusing even with the guide they provide. Besides that, if they could figure out how to easily upload and play your own songs the game would be even better. Perhaps roll out DLC packs for more music, I don't know, but what I do know is that I look forward to whatever Super Spin Digital is doing with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, In first impression I did not like this new turntable mechanic.I thought they only causes frustration, annoyance, and confusion. along with "color matching system"(Audiosurf had it and I did not quite like it.)but when i picked it up and give it a go, I was pleasantly surprised.even only with keyboard and mouse, controls felt smooth and was not that hard to get used to.furthermore, small beam that comes up from currently active color part of turntable was in my opinion, genius design making this entire mechanic much less confusing.(I still mess up my combo quite a lot when color changes, but am pretty sure its skill issue :P)spin note and effects around it actually makes entire gameplay feel like you are the DJ playing the music, too.The only downside is that volume of vanilla tracks are small, but since quality of songs are decent and price is only 20$-ish,I do think I can give it a okay pass. and if you want to, you can fill the gap of vanilla music tracks yourself because this game supports custom track.My final verdict for this game is that it might have some Flaws, it worths its money considering its still in EA.and this game is criminally underrated.8.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great rhythm game for PC with a lot of unique features, the wheel spin feature feels very fresh and unlike any other rhythm games I've seen, which feels good to use during play and overall the mechanics are very customizable.I would have endorsed the game more had I written a review sooner, as I have some issues with the recent overhaul of the menu UI as of 1.0. Visual effects while playing a track are understandable, but the menu feels as though it has become form over function.Additionally, while the in-game background effects can be disabled- an option I MUST choose as I play from a laptop- the menu background and 3D effects cannot. I can only assume something about the scripts is prone to issues, as I have experienced numerous Unity crashes since returning to the game after a while of not playing. This always occurs when browsing the menu, or, when returning to the menu after finishing a song.I really hope some options are added soon to disable some of these effects. _childDocuments_.review: This game is great for people looking to satisfy that "itch" of playing a instrument game without an actual instrument. If you like EDM (Electronic Dance Music) even slightly and fantasize that your playing the music yourself, then look no further. Even if you don't like EDM per-say, You can always get on a community made website (non-steam though) download more that were made by players like you and I.There are very few things that make instrument games good but we will still break it down in a list.Gameplay: Rough at first for anyone new to the genre Im sure. but its easy to learn and hard to perfect. There are muliple difficulty choices starting from Easy>normal>hard>expert>XD (XD being basically expert+) and just like most games in this genre, it starts you off with the basic notes/controlls and gives you more control/note options as you progress through difficulty. (Example: Easy = 3/6 notes Normal=4/6 ,Etc)Music choices: Okay so music on the actual game is mostly EDM, but its titles that are easily recognized. Not obscure titles that you might only hear about from a friend of a friend of a friends friend my friend. there are over 53 songs that i know are on the game, If you unlock more as you progressively play, then i need to start to pay attention more. That said even if you do "unlock" songs, you can always go download songs from the community.Visuals: Like most Iconic Instrument games, (Guitar/DJ Hero, Rock band, etc) they are known for their visuals as well as gameplay. Giving you that feeling of euphoric falseness, i mean fantasy of being not only good at playing the game, but feeling like your actually playing the song yourself. This game delievers on that feeling in spades. Using an array of visual equalizers while playing in just the right way so not to overwhelm the senses but still stimulating them just enough. Even better, if you find some of the visuals daunting, there are several options to help accommodate with every players comforts/discomforts.Controls: You can play the game with just a mouse and/or keyboard or gamepad (Steam Deck maybe? I could see it playable for sure). If you have a set of MIDI turntable controllers or what ever they are called (like what DJ's use at the club) you can use them as the actual instrument (Results vary on what is used). I have not yet experienced this, once i do i will update this post with that info, but if your like me, more broke then a joke to poke yoke, then your in (somewhat) luck. I thought these devices were quite expensive until i looked them up. they are actually affordable to some degree.IN SHORT, Here is the score. on a scale from 0-10. 10 being bestGameplay: 11/10 -  Cause this is very important for this genre of games and they F#%@$!% NAILED IT!Music: 9/10 - But this is more a personal opinion then anything, Music depends on taste. Taste may vary person to personVisuals: 10/10 - OH SHINY! But not to distracting to actually play the game. Exactly what it should be.Requirements: 2/10 - This game does not require top of the line graphics, this low score is a good thing for potato PCsAddicting: 9.5/10 - I myself like this genre, so i found it hard to put this game down. My first song and I was hooked.Overall: 10/10 - This game has replay value up the wazoo, specially for players that are new to the genre.Worth: 10/10 - I would buy this game again and again, worth buying. Honestly should cost more.
