_childDocuments_.review: Man, the game has become extremely weird, visually ugly, and they even added a level system to unlock songs. I've spent over 20 hours on this game and I'm only at level 15? Is this some kind of joke? I've even made it to the top 10 high scores on some songs, and they just completely changed the game for the worse.Another thing is the 'Perfect+' requirement, you simply can't score higher if you don't get a 'Perfect+' on the song. Anyway, they ruined the game, and in its current state, I wouldn't recommend buying it. Get Muse Dash instead, which is infinitely better and cheaper.Speaking of level 15, why the hell did they lock songs behind levels? The song selection in this game is deplorable, with only a handful of good ones from famous artists. With the money they've made, couldn't they secure some decent partnerships? Out of over 50 songs, only 10 or 12 are genuinely good.Having said that, the game used to be mediocre, but now it's an atrocity, no doubt. There are more downsides than upsides.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing change to other rhythm games using the wheel mechanic translates well for multiple control methods including mouse, Keyboard, Controller & even MIDI DJ Controllers which is a really cool feature and once calibrated works pretty well!Got to chat to the devs at PAX AUS 2023 and they're pretty passionate so definitely keen to see where this game & other projects go in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Played 9 hours in my first day. I think it's honestly one of the best Rhythm games to come out recently. There's the problem of value right now as you're getting a small setlist. At the time of this review it's 23 songs with more to come later. A level editor is already partially implemented. The Graphics are gorgeous and the UI is really top notch. The soundtrack is all EDM, much of which comes from Monstercat. Not a complaint but something to note for sure if you're planning to play different types of songs. One big factor for some is that spin rhythm is going to take some getting used to if you have no experience with games such as DJ Hero, IIDX, or Sound Voltex. It can be overwhelming even for veterans of 4k mania games and osu. It's a blast to play on Keyboard and Mouse, I've also tested on Keyboard only and Gamepad, both work well. But as I said earlier I'd recommend this to any fans of rhythms games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely puts a new spin on rhythm games! From the trailers I was a bit sceptical at first on how this is going to play out, but the control scheme is unique yet easy enough to grasp. It's super fun but challenging enough to not be a typical  kind of game.With 15 songs that have 4 difficulties each at launch there isn't an infinite "set" yet, but as this is Early Access there surely are more things to come. An Editor is already present in the game, custom charts (for existing songs) can already made, probably paving the way for future workshop support etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: A really clean rhythm game with a really interesting and fun central concept. I was initially worried that aiming would be inconsistent on harder difficulties but it isn't at all. The concepts in the game build off of each other and are really fun to master. My only complaints are that the end screen doesn't show you your hit judgements or what score you need for which rank, which can make scoring difficult at times, and that the difficulty curve from the hardest Experts to the easiest XDs is very steep.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to get used to the controls but when you do and get into a groove then the game feels amazing. The only issue I have is that you only play the full song on higher difficulties and on lower difficulties its a cut down version of the song. I absolutely cannot stand that. I'm not very skilled when it comes to rhythm games, so it makes me sad that I most likely will never get to play the full version of these songs. It also feels just a bit off when the songs end because its clear that there is more to it sometimes.  I still recommend the game though because the game play is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, been playing since it hit early access, so my review is split. Yes the game is in a better place and looks a lot more stylized than when it came out, but my main problem with the game is the music and beat maps. (my opinion is from xd difficulty as i can clear most tracks on this difficulty) Not only are some of the new music hard to follow with random sounds, the quality of beat maps has decreased over time. It may just be muscle memory of the first few tracks, but the newer ones, even if they're marked as easier, are very hard to follow. I'm only recommending the game because if you're new to the game you won't notice these changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: the notes pop upcolor wheel go spini tap the notehold sometimesbrain feel goodBeen here since beta and it feels awesome to see this game officially come out. I think there's a lot of great rhythm games out there right now, but Spin Rhythm might be the best out of them all. There's a great song selection and the controls are really easy to pick up. There's tons of custom tracks out there that the community has created if the song list gets too stale. I've had so much fun over the last 2 years and now that I'm learning to use the in game chart mapper I think I'll have a lot more hours into this.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Really good rhytm game. Definitely worth it even for full price. I haven't had this much fun since I first up picked up Beat Saber in VR.Ton of good songs (can make custom levels as well), very responsive controls, great tutorial and difficulty scaling (each difficulty adds new mechanic into the mix), nice progression system.Works on Steam Deck too and darn well.I really like that there are basicaly no load times I can hop from song to song without any holdup.I've played 50 songs on Hard and I struggle on some of the later songs but I still can manage to get trough. I've tried Expert and XD and the earlier songs are doable for me on Expert but very difficult and XD is just too much for now.

_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Nice to see a early access game releace with the core game already finished. A very fun game that i would recomend to everyone! took me a good hour before i really started to understand the controls but after that everything felt so fluid. The only thing i can really see that game needing now is better UI and more songs; even though for a early access they do have quite a lot of songs!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim during quarintine, and I've been hooked ever since. I'm not really that much of an EDM or Electronica fan, but this game just feels so smooth. Every note and input makes you (or me at least) feel like the composer of these songs.  Whoever charted these songs is MAD Insane and also very talented. With several different ways to play the game, your options are limitless.MIDI, Mouse and Keyboard, as well as Controller (And several different YouTube videos of people making controllers and seeing what works.)5 Different Difficulties 30+ SongsSpinFM, A way to play with your friends and compete for HIGHSCORES (and not just the Panda Eyes song)Happiest purchase in awhile!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly underrated. The mechanics are quite unique so there's a very satisfying learning curve.If you're even remotely a rhythm game person this should be top of the list.Only issue I have is really a non issue, but since the game is so niche the custom tracking community is quite small. And the difficulty of custom tracks are more often than not much, MUCH harder than even the hardest stuff in-game. Like who are you even tracking for at that point? The small minorty of the small minority that play the game?
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Well thats a good amount of time put into this game I'd say.Unique and very fluid gameplay coming together with an amazing community, custom song and track support, a great base game soundtrack, and an impossibly high skill ceiling to reach. This really is everything you could ask for in a rhythm game and with continuous updates seeming to come down the line, there really isnt a reason to not pick this one up, unless you hate rhythm games of course, but if you hate rhythm games, why be on this page?

_childDocuments_.review: A truly great rhythm game with custom charts available on spinsha.re! Absolutely recommended to all types of players, I'm currently grinding through hard/expert difficulty hopefully soon to reach XD difficulty (the maximum in the game).Try it out! The only downside is that I wish there was online lobbies within the game but I understand introducing that would be a cost for the developers.Hopefully we will live long enough to see something like that happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun rhythm game that combines both your mouse and keyboard. I personally dislike osu! after playing that game for over 3 years because it just gets repetitive, and this game does the exact opposite. I love it so much because other people can make maps just like osu!, so the game doesn't get old quick, and it's still quite difficult. I've only just gotten to the final difficulties, and they're quite the challenge. All in all, money well spent, and it's an awesome rhythm game, I'd highly recommend it if you're into rhythm games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I have had Spin Rhythm for a WHILE now and I always come back to it. The control system is intuitive and easy to pick up, it's so satisfying when you play well, the graphics are gorgeous and tailored to each song. The songs themselves are diverse and incredible in their own right - I listen to a lot of them regularly now when I'm not even playing the game. It's one of the best rhythm games out there currently and I highly recommend it to anyone - the easy difficulty is easy enough for newbies to the genre to get used to how it all works, medium and hard difficulties are fun and let you enjoy the music (I genuinely just feel like *I'm* DJing when I play sometimes) and the expert and XD difficulties pose a true challenge that take some grinding to achieve. It's a fantastic game, so happy to see it come out of early access and become fully fledged. If you're not sure, take my word and the word of so many others - there's clearly a lot of love behind this game and it shows. You'll find a new addiction in Spin Rhythm XD.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing concept of a rhythm game while making it easy to pick up for newcomers. Early Access does mean you only have a select few songs but the potential for amazing maps and features to pop up make this game worth sticking around forAfter seeing it's showcase at PAX Aus I can't wait to see how this games' development progresses.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone was saying "If you've ever enjoyed a rhythm game, get this" or "it's the most like playing an instrument in a rhythm game". And for some reason, I put it off until now. It's an absolute blast. The tracks are bangin. The gameplay is simple in theory, but as you get better you start to understand how it works on a subconscious level, and it only gets more fun from there.I use a mouse and keyboard. I tried to use my Maschine Mikro, but unfortunately the touch strip doesn't work well as a wheel currently. Devs, I know it's a small niche to want to use a maschine controller, but if you can add some kind of support for it, that'd be amazing. Regardless, best rhythm game I've ever played. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Spin Rhythm is an extremely fun and addicting rhythm game and early access done right. It's quite different from any other rhythm game I've played. The devs are fairly active on the Discord server and always working to improve the game. The game is very polished, and visually appealing, with very few bugs. It's very customizable, especially the controls. I use keyboard and mouse, but a variety of controllers and rhythm game devices are also supported. As of this review, there are 30 songs with 5 difficulties each, and more songs are to be added for free as well as future DLC packs.The gameplay flow and learning curve are extremely smooth, aside from the highest difficulty. If you're playing casually, you might not even be affected. But rhythm game pros, be aware that you might get to Expert in your first day or two, but you almost certainly will not be playing XD charts without many hours of practice. Of course, this is something the devs are aware of and have worked to address during early access, while still allowing a challenging level of play.I don't plan on creating my own charts at the moment, but if that's something you're interested in, be aware that the track editor is still in a fairly early state as of this writing, although all the essentials are included. They're hard at work on improving it, though. Also be aware that there can't be an official mechanism for sharing custom charts because that would be copyright trouble, but you can still share and play custom charts. If you eventually find the base game easy, customs can be on a whole new level.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique rhythm games I've ever played,makes you feel like some cool y2K futuristic DJ and it's amazing!  Has an equally amazing set of songs and visuals that I wish I could appreciate more if not for me being so focused on not messing up!The world needs more rhythm games like this with fun mechanics,lots of style and great music!Might be hard to get into initially but once it clicks you're gonna love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I might not play this game often, but i love how easy it is to just open the game and start vibing to the music while playing.The controls feel unique from other rhythm games, which means that the game gets really challenging when trying to master the new controls in harder game modes.So far, i enjoy the game on hard difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: This rhythm game is super creative and really well made. The wheel concept is something that I have never seen before and is executed amazingly. The vibrant colours make this game very appealing and the choice of music is stuff that I love listening to. The different difficulties make this game something to keep coming back to and are well balanced.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: a super unique rhythm game that mostly focuses on you moving your mouse and clicking, instead of keyboard inputs like most rhythm games. the basics of the game is that you move the mouse to spin the wheel to catch colored notes, click to do hold notes, and flick the mouse to do a full spin. you will also use your space key in the later difficulties.there are already a ton of charts already prebuilt into the game, with a wide range of levels, as well as a full community making custom charts. you can also make your own chart with the in-game chart creator. if you are a fan of rhythm games, this is a must buy, especially if you are looking for something unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: I usually avoid early access games because they are unfinished, but the game's premise and my love or rhythm games made me take the plunge and I am very gad I did. As far as describing the game to anyone interested, you control a rotating disc that travels along a track full of colored gems and lines, and you have to make sure the disc colors match the gems colors as the disc travels through the track to the beat of the music. This idea of matching colored gems to an input as they cross some boundary is well established in rhythm games, but I think Spin RhythmXD stands out in that it doesn't try to stress your dexterity as much. You don't need to use all your fingers to press some ridiculous pattern because there are really two buttons to press . At the same time, having to rotate the wheel to match the incoming gems/beats is different enough to make the whole thing feel fresh.The game works great with all control schemes I've tried (mouse and keyboard, controller), so don't feel like you need MIDI gear to enjoy this game  because the controls are responsive regardless (though I personally have entertained the thought of buying a USD100+ peripheral to get more enjoyment out of this USD20 game. Make of that what you will). In fact, this is a distinct advatage over the likes of guitar hero and their ilk.On top of that, the music is varied within its context of electronic music and there are more tracks than I'd anticipate an indie project like this to have, the challenge is very real without feeling unfair (except maybe some songs on XD, but it is the highest difficulty) and most importantly, the game is very fun. It could be argued that the songs lack mainstream appeal, but I don't personally mind.Now that the game is finally complete, I feel it's fair to give this game a proper endorsement and recommend it to anyone with even a passing interest in rhythm games.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not the greatest music games I've ever played. Spinning with the mouse is really satisfying and fits perfectly into the well crafted DJ tracks. The sound track is not only fantastic but suites the game and unique control scheme perfectly.  The tracks are tricky and have a smooth progression so you really feel like you're steadily improving the whole way through.Rhythm games don't get a lot of love outside of japan but spin rythm brings a unique flavor to the genre and executes it perfectly. It seems novel at first but there's more than enough here for music game fans to sink their teeth into.100 Hours in and I'm still spinning away, the custom song community has done an amazing job making so many additional tracks available.
_childDocuments_.name: Spin Rhythm XD

_childDocuments_.review: Enter the Rhythm Dimension. Match colours and beats as you spin, tap, flick and flow through the juiciest beats in the universe.

name: Disaster Report 4: Summer Memories
detailed_description: Thrust into a tragedy that touches countless lives, you must now make the decisions that will determine who lives and who dies in the chaos stemming from a natural disaster. What will you do in the aftermath of calamity? When a massive earthquake strikes the city you’re visiting, you find yourself at the epicenter of a chaotic and catastrophic crisis. It’s up to you to rise above the calamity, gather your thoughts and your fellow survivors, and outlast the disaster. Aftershocks, fires, collapsing buildings and debris, and unstable ground are but a few of the threats you’ll face in these nightmarish circumstances. What will you do when every passing second and every snap decision could spell the difference between life and death? Your World in Chaos - In a city on the brink of collapsing, you’ll need to make split-second decisions that will impact your safety as well as that of others. Everybody's Got a Story - Meet your fellow survivors in a Japanese-inspired city devastated by a powerful earthquake, and see how the human spirit bends...and sometimes breaks. Danger at Every Corner - Navigate a multitude of crises—from collapsing buildings to raging fires—in a city aplomb with peril.

name: Langrisser I & II
detailed_description: Langrisser I: Follow the story of Ledin, a young prince whose home was invaded by the Dalsis Empire seeking to conquer the land. He'll have to confront his rival Lance and the Kaiser to reclaim his homeland and the Sacred Sword Langrisser. However, both sides will be observed closely by the watchful eyes of the darkness. The fate of Langrisser, Baldea, and the entire continent of El Sallia will be determined by the choices you make. Langrisser II: Elwin is a wanderer who finds himself caught in between the Descendants of Light, the army of darkness, and the Rayguard Empire in a battle for the Sacred Sword Langrisser and the Cursed Sword Alhazard. Which side will you join? Which will you deem worthy of the legendary swords, and consequently, the right to rule El Sallia itself? Both Langrisser I & II have returned with their classic stories of good and evil, complete with beautiful high-definition visuals, reorchestrated music, and quality-of-life improvements to the classic gameplay that made these strategy RPGs truly LEGENDARY. Key Features: A Blade Honed to Perfection - Experience two classic titles with new visuals, music, localization, and a new character with new story choices. Legendary Legions - Expanded character options across two games allow you to command 33 playable characters and customize them with 50 unique classes. Forge Your Path - Your greatest weapon is choice. Your decisions result in any one of 22 story endings and 560 character outcomes across both titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser 1 and 2 is a PC port of a remake of the old Genesis/SNES cult strategy games released in the early to mid 1990s. Of the series, only Langrisser 1 saw a Western release, titled Warsong on the Genesis. The sequel, titled Der Langrisser on the SNES, featured a branching storyline which is faithfully adapted in this version of the game. While it never saw a Western release, after several years and a lot of difficulty it saw a fan translation completed.The price for such an old series is a little bit high, but keep in mind for the cost you're getting an awful lot of game time out of it between two games with multiple playthroughs. In my opinion, it's worth it if you're hungry for a good strategy game or just really love Langrisser.The graphics are a bit... mobile-ish, but not terrible. They grow on you a bit. The music and sound is decent, with the option of using the old midi tunes if you like the retro aspect. Voice overs are done in Japanese with no option for dubbing.The lack of mouse control might be a drawback for some. I haven't tried using a gamepad. I personally used keyboard though, and it didn't take me terribly long to become comfortable with it. Still, if you're awfully attached to mouse support be aware that it's absent as of this writing.For those already familiar with the Langrisser series, do note that while gameplay is very familiar and you'll quickly pick it up, many balancing choices have been made. Among those include a change to the way stats work (such as hp no longer being 1-10), the removal of commander rest/treat making HP and MP more difficult to manage, and class changing has been completely overhauled, separate from level with more freedom to change class as you wish between missions without the rare Runestones.On the whole, while I was nervous and wary of a new developer picking up the reins, it's a good remake and a fair port. Not perfect by any stretch, but it does the job.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Warsong on the Genesis, but the update made it mirror the Mobile Game more than the original.  So in that regard, it's a very different game.  It tried to mix parts of the original, with the updated mechanics of the mobile game, and ultimately fails on both regards.  The original Warsong is a difficult game.  Maps are large, and stages can take almost an hour or longer to play.  There is a heavy reliance on using correct mercenary types - Archer > Horseman > Trooper > Archer - with one or two other special classes (mermen, flying, and monks).  Unit HP was 10, and functioned similar to advance wars since a full strength unit fought better than a damaged one.  Commander stat boosts could help if fighting against an equal or worse type but using correct troops was key to survival.  Magic was useful, but limited to a small number of heroes.  Items were minimal and provided minor but useful buffs, and characters could only equip 1 item.  Experience points were also limited, and there were no ways to replay levels.  It was very challenging. Overall this version is extremely easy.  Troop types matter early until you unlock higher tier mercenties, than it matters less and less.  Every hero can use magic with several spells which buff your troops or kill waves of enemies.  Hero characters stats can be heavily inflated by items, to the point you never need troops (especially on replays).  Also with the removal of unit hp caps, heroes can have health several times larger than troops and have little risk of death even after multiple attacks.  Speaking of which, Computer AI is pretty broken, and will not attack enemies it will lose to, which again in replays, can lead to enemies never attacking you because your too powerful.  Honestly there was only one fight that was difficult b/c the set up placed you in the center of 6 mages all able to cast a large AOE spell.  aside from killing many of my troops, but all my heroes were able to easily kill everything once they got out of the pit.  So ultimately, the only time the game is challenging is when it completely Cheeses you.  I was very excited about this remake, but ultimately, i'm disappointed.  It looks nice, it plays faster than the original, music is still great, but I feel it was modded to be more in tune with the recent mobile game, and it lost a lot in the process.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

Not sure what the heck they modeled the button scheme off of.Edit: Actually, it seems this only happens if you turn on your Xbox controller AFTER starting the game. Turn it on before starting the game at it works fine. Weird...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm have been a Langrisser fan as long as I have been an SRPG fan. The original Langrisser, localized as Warsong for the Genesis was the first ever SRPG I played. I played Langrisser 2 on the Genesis even if I couldn't undertand a thing of japanse. So this two games have a special place for me. Now, I reccomend this game to people that haven't played the old games, people that are looking for fun SRPGs to play and enjoy. This is not a hardcore strategy game, you're not gonna find crushing diffulty, complex maps with multiple objectives or even a complex set of game rules. You just move your units and see them crash into the enemy units, and then wipe the map clean with a meteor, that is how Langrisser rolls.On the plot department the game shows it's age, by today standarts the story is nothing to write home about but I was pretty decent when It was made, and it has multiple routes and endings based on who you choose to side with so there is that and it gets the job done to justify every battle.

_childDocuments_.review: Der Langrisser, also known as Langrisser II was my favorite game growing up. It never received a proper English port so I had a fan made translation patch that worked pretty well. I had always hoped to see this game given an English release proper. But this. I have never hated a game so much as I do this. A lot of my irritation comes from how lazy the graphics design is. It looks like they just stole assets from a cheap mobile game, and adjusted the hair and clothes so no one would notice. They no longer let you choose a class to start out with. You're just a fighter, so that's a huge part of character customization just gutted out. Then when you want to choose a weapon, there's no thought or concern about benefit and deficit or class. You just have very clear good and bad choices. No need to think here. God forbid you have to think in a strategy game.The worst offense, and the main reason I can't forgive the creators of this game for their lazy, simple, effortless work; is the gameplay. In Der Langrisser you had a variety of spells that were well balanced, attack and defense up spells, damaging spells, area of effect spells, summon spells, and they were very well balanced. Langrisser 1 & 2 just compeltely threw all that in the garbage and decided that making flashy lights and colors that RPG Maker Beta could beat. In Der Langrisser, your units healed  when standing adjacent to your leader, and your leader could heal HP and MP by using Rally. Which meant you had to stay stationary and not attack with your commander which is a tough tactical decision to have to make. Not in Langrisser 1 & 2 re-release though. You don't have to think that hard in this game, so they just completely removed the rally option. The gameplay is nothing like what it was in the original because of the changes to character, classes, equipment, spells, and combat. In conclusion, this isn't a Langrisser remake. It's a completely different game that was skinned to look like Langrisser, and I have never been so disappointed and offended to have paid for this awful, lazy, mobile game ripoff. Even as a standalone game, ignoring comparison to the original, Langrisser 1 & 2 feels lazy. Many people like the cutesy chibi art, and that is okay for small, $5 mobile games that don't have a lot of assets and finances to invest in a team to give anything more. But for $50  in 2019/2020, we should be expecting, and getting far more than what Langrisser 1 & 2 delivered. The gameplay is alright if you're not comparing it to the original. Very simple, easy and straight forward, which is what some people enjoy. The music is decent, fans of the original will recognize how similar it is, though it's been modernized a bit. I wouldn't call this bad or good. I wanted this to be a 10/10 game when I saw itI wanted to give this a 0/10 when I played itRealistically, I give it a 3/10 because they didn't try, and it shows. It is not worth the price, and unless you can get it for 75% off or better, just play the original.Edit: Another problem I just remembered. They completely removed personality from so many of the characters. Morgan's not a pervert. Rougha doesn't swear or get crude, and so many of the characters just feel like they were neutered to make it child friendly. I understand that Rougha isn't going to tell Vargas that he's going to ♥♥♥♥ his wife after he kills him, but they didn't have to take all his vulgar behavior away and just make him a 4Kids version of Guts from Berserk.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, I’m not surprised anymore that I love to play JRPGs even though I’m not exactly good at them. Maybe it’s the challenge that thrills me, yet, although I might struggle at one or another part of the game, I still refuse to give up. That’s not a bad thing at all though, since it just feels more rewarding when I finally happen to get past the part I’m stuck. During my playthrough, I noticed that Langrisser requires a lot of strategies although the main characters being quite strong since there are followers available here I will go in more detail with later on.Since this version of this game includes the first and second games, it’s very lengthy and it’s easily possible to spend a huge amount of hours when every scenario gets pursued. However, Langrisser focuses mainly on its gameplay and, therefore, the story might fall a little short on my expectations. Don’t get me wrong, I’m used to JRPGs not really having an in-depth story, yet I found the dialogue parts unusually little. Before and after every battle there is a short sequence in a visual novel style to understand the happenings better. Sometimes, I wasn’t really sure what was happening in the game but luckily the gameplay makes up for it.You see, I noticed a lot of people saying that Langrisser I & II is way too easy and even though I didn’t go through it as smoothly as I hoped, I have to agree on that aspect. Some characters were very strong and I managed to one-shot a lot of enemies. The problem here is that the hard mode only gets unlocked once the player finished at least one playthrough. Whilst it wasn’t a huge issue for me, since I tend to struggle with some games more than other people, I am not sure why this mode isn’t available right in the beginning. However, it's a relief that the player can at least just borrow a save file from another player who finished a playthrough so they can add more challenges right away.As aforementioned, I found that strategy was required in Langrisser. There are commanders available in your party although some might leave or join when progressing with the story depending on the events. Each commander can have a certain number of followers that help them during the fight. Of course, they aren’t as strong as the commanders itself, but in the end, I found that they’re definitely required or else the player will be outnumbered by the enemies since this system applies to them as well. Sometimes, they worked just fine as a shield as well, to keep the commanders alive. Although there is a fee for each follower per chapter, money was a thing that I was never short of.Each chapter contains short story sequences and a single battle where a certain goal has to be fulfilled. On the other side, there is a requirement as well for the own party to lose. The thing I like here is that the goal isn’t always to defeat all enemies but sometimes fleeing to a certain part of the map already successfully cleared the chapter. In fact, in the first battle, it’s very tough to defeat all enemies so the obvious easier choice would be to flee. However, sometimes beating them is the only way to win. Through the map, there are shiny parts available that provide an item when one of the allies stop their turn at this spot.That being said, as you’ve probably already guessed, Langrisser is a turn-based JRPG. After having a few commanders, I ended up finding it tedious to give an order to every follower so I stopped doing that soon. Luckily, there are commands players can set for each commander so they automatically perform it. It simply took too long to manually give orders, yet I liked that there was an option for both so I could still control them myself if I wanted something specific other than standing still or attacking. The special thing I noticed here is that during attacking, the attacker gets damaged as well. This made me rethink about some actions at times and be more careful.However, I didn’t really like the fighting animation because it might take a while for a turn to end if I watched every single one. It comes in handy that there is an option to automatically skip them so I could just attack without worrying at all. Overall, there are quite a few settings available that lets the player change between the old or remastered graphics. I noticed there was a separate option available for the battle maps as well and since I could either freely choose or mix both options altogether. I personally liked the modern graphics so I played this game with these options and I have to admit that I found the art style, especially the sprites, charming although the battles look rather simple.Sadly, Langrisser I & II doesn’t have mouse support. That, however, wouldn’t be a big problem if it wasn’t for the keybindings on the keyboard. My biggest issue here was that, whilst it is possible to play this game entirely with the keyboard, it was extremely uncomfortable for me. First of all, I found the default keybindings really weird and there was no way to change it in the in-game options. For instance, Z was the button for confirming whilst pressing C canceled the action.So that means that I had to move my hands every time depending on what I was intending to do, which greatly disturbed my immersion during the engaging battles. Whilst the controls for the keyboard can be found in the forums, the game doesn’t explain them but only shows its players the controller prompts during playing. The keybindings are adjustable in the game folder, however, that should definitely be an option in-game. A lot of people reported that the keyboard bindings didn't work for them, however, I didn't occur this issue.I had a lot of fun during playing Langrisser I & II even when I got stuck at times and had to replay the whole fight when I happened to lose the battle. This, however, only motivated me to beat it and when I managed to get past a chapter, I felt incredibly proud of myself despite getting frustrated before. Sadly, the story isn’t very in-depth, yet I liked every character and moment I managed to spend with them. It was very disappointing when I started the game and noticed that I wasn’t comfortable with playing this game with the keyboard at all, yet it worked just fine with the controller. That being said, Langrisser I & II is an engaging turn-based JRPG that managed to entertain me for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could make this a neutral review, I would. This review is mainly for Langrisser II, as it's the one I'm most familiar with.Game is a lot easier as compared to the original. I consider this a bad thing, but if you're new to turn-based strategy games, it could be a good thing.-You pretty much never have to care about managing your money. Go ahead and blow it all on the max number of mercs.-Case in point, you start with 500 gold in the original Der Langrisser, and the merc cost is similar in this game. However, in easy mode in this game, you start with 15000 gold, and on normal you start with 5000. At that point, you may as well have the system automatically buy troops for you, with you only selecting the type of troop you want.-Gold gain is much higher in this game, as compared to the original.-You can equip a weapon, armour, and an accessory in this game, whereas in the original, the armour and accessory took up the same slot. This would normally not be a problem, but the items all have similar stats to the original after the number-inflation. So in other words, you'd be doing the equivalent of equipping double the defensive/support options.-The questions at the start no longer determine your starting class or inherent attack/def/troop count/leadership buffs; they instead give you perks and equipment. A little bit of a shame, since I quite liked being forced to use a smaller number of troops who are quite a ways stronger than other such troops.For the good stuff, I quite like the remastered art and music, and while I do have a soft spot for retro music, I'd pick the remastered version over the old ones. The cutscene images were a pleasant surprise as well.I'd recommend this game if they released a hard mode that maintains the original game's difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser I & II. This is a remake of the classic masterpiece SRPG Langrisser 1 & 2. The original is one of the game titles representing the 1990s. Especially, most fans rank Langrisser II as the best in the series. This remake has been remastered to match the latest SRPGs, but it has certain advantages and disadvantages. Let's look at it together.The original illustration was designed by Satoshi Urushihara, but the new illustration design was painted by Nagi Ryou. Of course, each one has its own charm, but it is hard to deny that the original is quite impressive. Fortunately, using the classic mode, you can apply the original illustration partially, so you can choose the modes according to your preference. Whatever it is, once adapted, it won't be a big deal. The remake of SD character graphics was better for me.The most striking feature of this remake is that the part 1 story is revamped somewhat positively. 4 scenario route branches and new heroine added. And the characters in all scenarios support full voices. The battle visual graphics improved, but it gives some impressions that it's kind of like a mobile game. The battle balance is interesting early on, the difficulty level begins to be broken gradually. The BGM is partially arranged and quite good. Considering both Langrisser I & II, the scenario volume provides approximately 60 hours of game play time.Langrisser I & II. It is already the proven masterpiece SPRG. For old fans, it's a great way to meet new heroine and new scenarios. And for new users, it will be a great experience to be able to enjoy the Langrisser series. Of course, this is not perfect, but it's a pretty good remake. Why so many players were so enthusiastic about it, when Langrisser comes out on mobile. You will find the answer in this game. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ridiculously overpriced for the fairly low graphical and gameplay polish it contains (the music is fine but hey it was amazing in the original games too!).Even at 50% off it's still overpriced. I feel the "fair" price would be between $10 and $15.The new routes in Langrisser I suck because plot points get asspulled out of nowhere and lack the time to be appropriately developed. I ended up giving no s*** about what's going on in the first game.Langrisser II has much better fleshed out story and characters, but that's something that already existed in the original so there's no added value in this remaster.To break the original games one had to carefully milk all EXP on maps, which required some tactical skill on certain maps due to objective pressure (time limit, escort NPC etc.)Now, in this remake you just need to buy items in shop. That's it, game is broken and you can now mindlessly charge away at the enemy units with your bigger stats numbers, even though enemies are usually higher-leveled than you.It also doesn't help that you can promote classes quite a bit earlier than in the original game.Magic feels generally meh, until you inflate your MAG stat to ridiculous levels with items and cast meteor spell. Everything in the huge AoE will die or have ~10% HP left. Then your mage gets a level up that refills full MP and can do it repeatedly.In the original game, meteor dealt 3-4 HP damage out of 10 against units witth average magic resistance.One extra nitpick: lower tier mercenaries were useful in the original game because command range granted flat stat bonuses. Now, these bonuses have been changed to be percentage based, so the correct decision is to always hire the highest tier mercenaries - money will never be a problem anyway.Langrisser I & II can be a somewhat enjoyable game for a little while, then it drags on as it becomes ridiculously easy and broken. It's not "bad" but it doesn't have the charm of the original games and isn't worth the asked price.

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser I & II is a remake of Langrisser Dramatic Edition, which was itself a combined remake of the first two games in the series never released in the west, with only the first of the two games even being brought over at all in Warsong on the Sega Genesis.Dramatic Edition is one of my favorite SRPGs, and while I think Langrisser I & II is a great way for newcomers to get into the series, it is both an upgrade and downgrade from Dramatic Edition.I'll start with the good. The remake plays faster, and adds full voice acting as opposed to Dramatic Edition's partial voice acting, though currently without an English dub. It gives the player a flowchart to tell where you are in the story and allows you to jump to any point you've already completed to make different choices and experience all of the different routes the game has to offer. Whereas before, you had only a select few save slots to return to.Promotions happen a lot quicker, rather than having to grind up to level 10 repeatedly to gain access to new classes, you gain CP every level up that you save to select classes you want to upgrade into. You're also given a class tree to show what classes the unit can promote into rather than just having the player pick two classes that later branch into two classes and so on. Many of the units that were underwhelming or downright garbage between the two games were given substantial buffs. Usually in the form access to better classes at base, or higher level and/or a vast amount of CP to immediately let them reclass to whatever the player might need at the time they join.Then we come to the bad. As much as I like most of the new portraits, the unit sprites look like they belong in a mobile game. A lot of the utility spells were made much worse or more limited, while offensive magic was given ridiculous buffs. As a result, nine times out of ten, you're going to want to favor offensive spells like crimson tide and later meteor to wipe out swathes of troops rather than using utility spells except for maybe sharpen to increase your units' damage, or the various heal spells when your units get low.Ever since Warsong, the animations had a powerful effect on gameplay, instead of being a purely visual feature. Certain classes (usually infantry or mage classes) would attack enemies before they could damage your units, allowing you to weaken them before they could get to you and cause too much damage. This even allowed some characters who had poor defense to rely on their strong offense as a form of defense. Animations would differ greatly depending on what terrain you were attacking/defending from or what class you were in. for example, attacking someone on a wall would depict units climbing ladders and taking casualties as they climbed, while attacking *from* a wall would have your troops descending and taking casualties before they got to the enemy. With the remake, that's all been made far blander. Everyone attacks at the same time, and the units all swing at the air until the animation ends.There are a total of 8 routes in Langrisser I, and 13 in Langrisser II. Both games generally split the endings into Light/Imperial/Independent/Chaos routes, with varying degrees of good and bad endings, with the occasional ultra bad ending. While it's a lot of story content, a lot of the maps end up being reused (especially in Langrisser I, as Warsong originally didn't have route splits), and a few of the routes only end up being minor changes to the endings between each category. Even in those routes that don't change too much, there's still at least some variety to them, with different objectives, and even options to spare characters that the game goes out of it's way to acknowledge with additional dialogue. Though that occurs far more often in the second game than the first.TL;DR There's a lot of content to make it worth the price, some of the mechanics from Dramatic Edition were downgraded, some upgraded. As a fan of the series I considered it fully worth it to buy it day one and even 100% completed it, though as a newcomer it might be better to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Japan gamers were very lucky during the '90s. The original two games were masterpieces of console, tactical JRPGs... there were many popular titles of this genre, yet nothing played like the first two Langrisser games. And that's precisely why its unforgivable that they departed so much from the game mechanics and unit balance while doing this remake. Despite the similarities in the scenario maps and the script, its a completely different game, so the purpose behind this release is very suspect.If only the tactical depth and the serious challenge from the classics had been retained, one could be open, in time, to accept this new version as being its own thing. Sadly that is not the case... is a shallow and unsatisfying experience, not nearly as exciting, or fun to play, as the Super Famicom or Mega Drive versions, or even the other tactical RPGs from the era. This one is much closer to the experience from the mobile free to play, so despite everything, this version might still be to the liking of some players familiar with the mechanics of that. The rest of us, fans of the original, will sorely miss a "classic" gameplay mode, despite the presence of, cosmetic, classic options for both graphics and music.

_childDocuments_.review: Langriser I & II are remakes of the early titles in the series and were among my favorite when I was younger. I played Langrisser I (which was named Warsong in America) on the Sega when I was a kid and many years later I got to play a fan translated version Langrisser II (it was the Sega/Mega Drive version, not to be confused with Der Langrisser). I have played these games multiple times and I enjoyed their gameplay immensely and when I heard that the remake was coming, I automatically wished-listed the game and bought it and the DLC when it came out. Its one of the few games that I will fanboy for (alongside the Drakengard, Ys, and NieR series of games) and overall, I am happy to say that I was not disappointed with the game as it was everything I expected it would be plus some good changes/improvements to the game which made it better, in my opinion.The best parts about the remake, compared to the games I played years, were:For those of you that are new to the series and like SRPGs that are similar to Shining Force or Fire Emblem, this one is worth playing. Its story is relatively simple, so if you like story driven games with more complicated plots, you won't really find that here. However, if you just like the gameplay style, its pretty solid and would recommend giving it a chance. If you're still on the fence, be sure to play the demo first and/or watch gameplay videos to see if its worth your time/money.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the originals so this was my first experience with it. I've been playing Fire Emblem since the first NA releases so when I saw the gameplay, I had high hopes.Don't go into this game expecting it to be Fire Emblem. The gameplay and story may be really similar (tactics, demons and Roy 2.0), but if you're looking for a challenge, you won't get it. Even if this were to be compared to casual and easy mode for any FE game, Langrisser is still significantly easier. The graphics remind me heavily of Fire Emblem Heroes just from the art and sprite style, but this obviously has more substance. (Edit** FE: Heroes story lines have actually picked up a bit, so I'd argue Heroes is at least on par with story material now based on some of the recent books/stories). That being said, the story tree is a really interesting concept, but also absolutely maddening because of the back-tracking. The option to be able to completely change the way the story goes is something I've always been interested in because it gives you the opportunity to see what the "bad guys" are thinking and why they're doing what they're doing. Luckily there is an option to roll-back the story tree so if you're wanting to see all of the endings you won't need to start from the beginning each time. It hit a point where my main lords are so overpowered from rolling back for route branch levels that I can just clear levels without using anyone else so it can get pretty boring.I'm on the fence about between recommending it or not, because I am enjoying aspects of the game, but some of it can be absolutely mind numbing from how easy it is. Definitely try the demo out first before buying it because it'll give you a bit of an idea for what you'd be getting into. If you're looking for a challenge, you won't get it here unless you plan on beating the entire game then using your NG+ file to go into "Challenge Mode". I didn't have the patience for that because by the time I finished the game (and was working through all of the optional routes), I was ready to put it down and never pick it back up.I would still wait for this to go on sale because the 64.99 price point is steep considering what it is. Like I said earlier though, check out the demo before you buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I struggle writing this review because "Warsong" (as this game was called in its original US release on the SEGA Genesis) was my favorite game of its generation (yes, more than FF VII).  But while this game is a good update, and getting to play the sequel legally is great, the problems with the initial launch cannot be ignored.Frankly - this is a poorly done console port.  It's unplayable without a controller.  There is no key mapping and no directions on what mouse/keyboard buttons could have any impact.  Furthermore, when a controller is used the buttons don't actually map  (X is A, shoulder buttons don't work) and not all of the functions work.  For example, I've yet to figure out how to quit the game short of closing the app via Windows Task Manager.   While I love many aspects of what they've done and agree that a lot of the improvements are for the better, I can't recommend this game in the state that i's in.  And that makes me sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser is a pretty old series. The original game debuted on PC Engine and Sega Mega Drive in 1991, then later ported to Sega Saturn and other consoles.Langrisser I & II - completely overhauled experience. It's definitive edition from Sega Saturn and  even more content on top of it. Remastered soundtrack, character art/designs and x100 much better graphics are done in such a way, that's the traditional gameplay experience is not ruined. You also can switch between original art by Satoshi Urushihara and a new one anytime. Everything works perfectly with Windows 7/8/10 supported. I do recommend a gamepad/controller, though. While it's not really important (since the game is turn-based) and you can play with keyboard, i'm more comfortable with Playstation/Xbox-like controller. You can even use a cheap chinese one, the game recognises it without any problems. I did a LOLTEST for the memes and plugged my old logitech gamepad from 2004 and it works without any issues, all buttons/sticks including. Langrisser is a legendary sword (Excalibur-like level) and is currently sealed in the kingdom of light - Baldea. As you can guess, not many human beings can resist the temptation to steal it and Dalsis Empire is not an exception.Kaiser (aka king) Digos launched a surprise blitzkrieg attack on the Baldea Royal Castle. The game starts with Prince Ledin and his allies surrounded in the castle. They fought fiercely, but due to overwhelming numbers of attackers, Ledin is forced to run away, being ordered to do so by his father. The castle is fallen and Dalsis emperor obtained the Langrisser. His main goal is to "reunite" the continent under his rule (hello there, Adolf).It's up to Ledin now and his trusted allies to bring back the sacred sword Langrisser and fend off the invaders.Okay, let's stop here with story stuff. Langrisser I & II are extremely rich in terms of content and overall playtime hours. The main reason here is that your choices do matters and depending on your answers in dialogues and battle perfomances (example - kill X, don't kill Y, etc) will lead to specific story route/path. It's easily over 80+++ hours if you will try to clear all possible routes and collect all endings.The total amount of all possible routes is overwhelming, around 10+ or more, which provide a pretty amazing replayability & variation.  Okay, for a tactical strategy RPG Langrisser got a lot of stuff going on, even if it's super old. The main point of this game is that each character under your control can hire various mercenaries, which provide additional (meat)force during battles. The quality&class of those mercenaries depends on your unlocked character class. The more classes you unlock for your characters, the better mercenaries they can hire. However, top quality mercs also cost quite a lot $.Mercs will lead us to the most important mechanic in the game - Area of Command.Basically, it's a special zone around your hero. As long as your mercenaries stay that special zone, they'l receive additional buffs. As you can see from my screenshot, Ledin's mercs will receive a 115% ATK, 85% DEF, 65% MAG and 105% Magic Resist bonuses. This is extremely important, so keep it in mind. It's extremely disadvantageous and impractical to use mercenaries outside of their leader aura. It will make them super weak and easily killed.  This game also uses a Rock-Paper-Scissors-like system for weaknesses. Soldiers are strong against Spearmen, Spearmen are strong against Cavalry and Cavalry is strong against Soldiers. There's special type of units too, like "Flying" types, those are weak to your Dark Elf/High Elf archers. Don't bother with weak default Elf archers, they are complete sht. Dark Elfs are middle tier and High Elfs are top tier archers.In terms of healing you'l get single target and AoE healing spells and the units also can regenerate 20% HP per turn if they stay near leader. One of the most funny things is how Magic in this game is actually........DEVASTATING! It is not an exaggeration to say that you can obliterate AN ENTIRE SCREEN with one or two spellcasts (you get 2 mages anyway). However, it's hard to execute and can place your mages in a dangerous situation. This is because you can only cast spells WITHOUT moving, which means you either move + wait for next turn or you lure the enemy into a specific point and unleash a damn Meteorite on their arses.TL;DR Langrisser will present you a lot of choices of possible units & leaders combinations, available gear and classes.It's an extremely great classic SRPG, that retained it's original spirit, gameplay and epicness with a complete rework. Two games in one package, with around 80-100+ hours of Content and a lot of branching routes & possible endings, which provides great replayability (until you unlock them all). Definitely worth your money if you're a fan of good SRPGs like Vandal Hearts, Vanguard Bandits, Front Mission, Fire Emblem and so forth. - This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Warsong for the Sega Genesis. It was probably my most rented game at that period of time.I was pleasantly surprised when this bundle was announced. I couldn't hit buy fast enough.It's a turn based, fantasy themed, strategy game that has a branching story line. It's your typical good vs evil scenario. You start out with a minimal number of commanders and add or subtract them according to the choices you make and as the story progresses.Each commander has a level up path that determines what their class will be. Class will decide spells, strengths, weaknesses, type and what kinds of mercenaries you can use.Each scenario/mission you take on will show a splash screen showing your win/lose conditions as well as basic layout of map. You can allocation special items, gear and hire mercenaries. You'll be given a basic idea of what you'll be up against, but don't think that's all you are going to be up against. Langrisser series likes to throw out surprises such as reinforcements, ambushes, etc. Make sure you pay attention to not only enemy forces but also the map layout. If the map has spots where you think: "wow, if they do this, I'm screwed", you should take that into account, because there's a good chance it's going to happen.The sheer variety of classes, spells, and mercenary types, as well as different outcomes, offers a good amount of replayability. Campaign length is good. Friendly save mechanic.I have countless hours into this series on the Genesis version and emulators/roms. If you liked the original Langrisser games, get this - you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the series. Bought the game because I love the series. But make no mistake, this version is GUTTED compared to the originals. You have more skills and easier class changes and all that fancy stuff, but it's all pointless because this version of the game is brain-dead easy.In the original Warsong, there's a stage that introduces monster enemies. You have to use priests and monks to hurt them because holy damage is strong against monsters. In this version, while they still SAY that to you, it's actually not true at all. Any of your regular units can one shot the monsters. In fact, it's true for most of the game. I've just been running around 1-shotting nearly every enemy I come into contact with. It's all just so disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are completely fine with absolutely ignoring the storyline for both games, and pretending anything more than magic resistance ultimately matters, then this game is perfectly serviceable. The music is great, and it's fascinating to have the different music sets for DLC for listening to.Unfortunately, everything past that is increasingly more concentrated doses of annoyance. Every end map will always be the same. Sending out sacrificial troops to trigger the mages meteor spells that they all have, waiting for them to drain enough of their MP on that single decoy of a troop, and quickly rushing in and dispatching them before they regen MP, a skill you will never have.Equipment is completely meaningless, everything's just filler to pretend there is strategy here in your stats. The only real strategy is magic resistance. There isn't a big enough zoom level to adequately gauge the range of meteor spells, and in Langrisser II they absolutely love to have ambush troops pop up midturn. You WILL get screwed over until you beat your head enough times to memorize the map and where the trigger zones for ambushes are.Story is trash. The story changes so drastically and arbitrarily depending on your route that it's absolutely impossible to follow or care about anything. The big bad enemy could be a misunderstood bishōnen manga protagonist. The real enemy could actually be someone you never see or even address. People could die and randomly pop back up later.Play it purely for the gameplay. Sure it's samey, but it's workable. Story is just going to annoy.

However these 2 issues, mainly the graphic one, make this game only good and not excellent. So i would say something like 6,5-7/10

_childDocuments_.review: is a SRPG/turn-based strategy JRPG available of the two classic games from the nineties. This is a full remake of both games. I did not play the original games back in the day, but I have played much of the  series, and they are very similar. The game is a true gem, and I really love it. I am about halfway through  right now and have yet to play  except for trying it a little to make sure that the two games play the same way, and they do. I have put in 10 hours and am still enjoying every minute of it.There is a story and a good amount of plot development within, to be unlocked from chapter to chapter as you play. As we can expect for an older style game, the plot is less important than the actual gameplay and you can see the high fantasy generic story that doesn't matter too much. What adds to the importance of the story is developing points in the story where you have to make some decisions to alter the story and that affects the game progress, and giving the player some additional reasons to go back and replay the game through the different choices.The game is broken up into battle sequences. You control a few important characters who are your commanders. They are strong and you can also hire some mercenaries to act as meatshields for your commanders as you go through battle. As you go through battle, you will gain CP and you can adjust their classes. With improvement in classes, you can also hire better mercenaries, etc.You can control each commander unit as well as each mercenary unit. You start with two commanders but you will get a lot more later on. If you do not control the mercenary units, they will just follow the commander automatically after you end your turn. Every battle encounter displays a separate battle animation, and you can choose to turn this off because if you would rather not see it. This is good if you would rather not spend an accumulative long number of hours watching the animations. The game is turn-based and during your turn, you can move all of your commanders and mercenaries. If you use your units to engage in combat, you can see the outcomes before attacking, so you can decide whether or not to pursue the attack. keep in mind that if you have a chance to go after the enemy commanders, it would be wise to do that because the mercenary units surrounding a commander will disband if a commander is killed. Likewise, if your commander goes down, their associated mercenary units will leave as well.All of the mercenary units have strengths and weaknesses, they are stronger than some, but weaker than others. So it will be important to choose your fights strategically for the best outcomes. Because of these mercenaries on the screen, a fight involving a small handful of commanders on both sides will still make the screen look rather busy with everything going on. While this looks complex, the actual game mechanics is fairly simple and straight forward.There is a small help menu that you can use to explain some things about to game to you, but the overall baseline mechanics are simple and you should not need any more than playing for a few moments to see what's going on and to get used to it.At the start of each battle you will see the winning and losing conditions. You will earn money and CP from your battles, so you can upgrade your classes for the commanders or go to the shop to buy things to equip, etc.The game offers multiple save files, so you can easily save and load and so the branching-plot decisions mentioned above do not need to come with starting a new game each time.You can choose between remastered or the classic graphics. You have a few choices of doing this with the map and characters, so you can go through the game in a style that fits you. Everything looks so nice and smooth.The music is rather high paced and loud, and thus it made me rather nervous, so I didn't like that much. The Japanese voice overs are very well done. You can also choose between the classic soundtrack and the modern versions.I would advice using a controller. Look to the forums if your controller doesn't work and see what others have done to get theirs working. A standard DualShock4 controller worked at baseline. There are also a few button-configurations that you can choose from from the menu. Mouse controls are not supported, so you would have to use a keyboard if you do not use a controller. For me the controller worked perfectly.The price is a little steep. It's €49.99/$49.99US/£49.99, so regionally some people may feel a bit more of the price. But I think it's worth the full price of two completely remastered full games with so much new additions but also preservation of the older styles. There's enough gameplay within to justify the price.This is a true gem and I really love it so far. As mentioned above, I am halfway through the first game and only tried out the second a little bit. There's a lot of gameplay packed within. For people who want that older style music/art, you can get all of it here by changing the settings. Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser is a turn-based tactical RPG that requires basically no tactics and has poorly-told storylines.  (unless it's on-sale for <$10). For many people, the first thing you will compare this game to is the Fire Emblem series. Unfortunately, there is greater similarity between dogs and wolves than there is between Langrisser and Fire Emblem.I cannot even begin to describe how little strategical knowledge is needed to play this game. It does not matter how you position your units. Blindly charging your units towards whatever objective will guarantee you can beat the game. Spells are broken powerful (but not even necessary) and you can basically just blindly equip whatever the best gear you can buy and be alright. I cannot even say that you need to at least be able to tell if X is greater than Y. As long as you have up-to-date gear, you just straight up deal more damage than the enemies in every battle. Once you finish one story path, you can literally just use a single unit to win most battles.Some of your actions/choices in certain chapters will affect the subsequent chapters/ending. This would actually be a pretty cool feature, had there been a single decent storyline. Moreover, it is not just the storylines that are bad, but the method of storytelling is awful as well. Characters do nonsensical actions with no explanation in a given storyline and it is necessary to play all the storylines to get a full picture. Even then, a lot of things are just single line explanations trying to make the story seem less inane.Not everything about Langrisser is bad. As stated before, having your actions affect future developments is actually a pretty cool feature. Additionally, the graphics are a significant bump up from the original series. The voice acting is pretty good (to my untrained ears) and I quite enjoyed the background/battle music. This game gets painfully boring very rapidly as there is no challenge at all. I was able to force myself to get all the achievements (as I am a completionist), but it was a grueling and painful task. I would not buy Langrisser at full price. Had I known what I was getting into, I probably would not have even bought it at half price. If I really really enjoyed games like Fire Emblem and did not have a nintendo system/emulator, maybe I would buy it for <$10 to play for a couple hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Who is this game for? People who like classic srpgs and people who are busy. One route can be completed in about 20 hours. There are multiple routes and switching between them is quicker than other games because of chapter travelling. This game is a lot better than first impressions give it because the mobile-like art that was remade.Langrisser is an old series, like the fire emblem of sega systems. It eventually split off into growlanser. This is a remake with newer graphics and newer music but if you are a purist, you can change the character, map art and music to the original from the 80s complete with massive shoulder pads and 80s rock band hair. If you buy the dlc you have more tracks to choose from in game. You can switch all these whenever you want. Unlike most srpgs, you can hire a squad to battle with you, kind of like dragon force. If you don't want to, then don't. Your generic npc squad mates recover when next to you but your commander can only be healed by magic or leveling up. When you level up, you make a full hp/mp recovery. If that option can be turned off for those who want a harder game, I didn't see the option.Langrisser 1 was called "warsong" when it came out in English. This newer version adds multiple paths (or what ifs scenarios). If you don't like that what your character's heel turn, you can go back in time, and make different choices. Once you've cleared (or failed) a condition, the scenario list shows what that condition was so you can go back without starting a new game and fix it. You never lose gold, exp and once you collected an item on the battlefield, it stays collected even if you go back to the overworld. If you don't like that, make sure you save before battle and reload it so you don't become overpowered quickly or run out of money from hiring mercs. Langrisser 2 actually has someone explaining battle mechanics and is the better game (I didn't think 1 was bad but its more basic like you'd expect from an old school rpg from the 80s). The first few chapters are also more interesting so I actually recommend starting with 2, at least for the first few chapters. You can jump back to the first game after understanding the systems without any spoilers. Langrisser 2 also has even more branching paths and these tend to be more fleshed out, storywise. According to the global achievement, many people stopped at langrisser 1 and it's a shame because langrisser 2 has more variety of gameplay and people should judge this package after playing 2. conclusion: buy this so we get the other 3 langrissers and the 6 growlansers or at least a steam port of the mobile, FeH like game. These games are worth experiencing.If you like Japanese games, check out "Japanese games on PC"

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Langrisser 1 (or Warsong) and 2 (Genesis version, and enhanced Der Langrisser on Super Famicom) I have mixed feelings about this game but, as I had to choose "yes" or "no", my answer is more a yes.First, the games have a lots of changes compared to the originals.Gameplay wise, they've gotten worse. Original ones had extremely long and frustrating stages, yeah, but the balance seemed better. Taking out "commander healing" was a better choice to stop some abuses but at the same time balance in combat feels weird. Also strange is that enemies don't have any equipment (at least on normal difficulty) so once you can get higher level items you'll just destroy everyone even if underleveled. And I won't even talk about magic, you can easily destroy a whole army with some AoE spells while leveling up and having full MP again. AI isn't smart, though I think that problem carries on from the originals.You can switch to classic portraits, music and maps. I didn't like the new visual style, but I did enjoy the music so I ended up playing with only classic  portraits. It's a shame that the new cutscenes images are blurred in this mode, they could have gave us the option to be able to see them even if the styles clash. That felt really lazy. Also, classic maps don't really work when the sprites remain the same "mobile-looking" once.Overall, it was fun to replay the games and play the multiple routes, I'd complain some are extremely similar but that's not a remake's problem.Better combat balancing and visuals more similar to the original games would have helped a lot.For fans of the franchise I still recommend this, but maybe on sale. For casual players that want to try a game like this but not get too frustrated, I guess it's cool too for a lower price. But for SRPG fans in general, I think there are many better choices out there.
