_childDocuments_.review: This ended up just not being for me not that it is a bad game. I found the game very easy through 12 chapters of the first game. There is no perma death and your character units are extremely powerful. Each character also has mercenaries with them which is the bulk of the fighting. The mercenaries will move/act on there own to the character they are tied to without you doing anything if you chose to manually not move them. But the whole process is slow and just not much fun. Each game has multiple story routes for replay value. You can rewind the story at any point for easy access to routes. The game also tells you afterwards what you would need to do to finish the stage and go to the other route which is nice.The art is a bit of a mess. Most of the classic art look better but there are some exceptions (Jessica). There is no way to manually do it for each character. You either pick classic or not. Even if you pick classic the new art will appear in place where there was none before but is now.Battle map can be set the same way. But and this is a big one sprite work is only in the modern style. The worldmap is only in the new style and it looks bad. Sprite work battle animation looks terrible and should just be turned off. You can mix and match classic art with modern map though.Music has also been remastered with a choice. I actually liked the new music.Game also needs to be played with a controller if that is a deal breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: Highlighting some controls issues. Played the entire game on controller1) buttons clearly put in unintended places.2) game randomly flips the controls into the right buttons? i.e the start and select used to swap between characters become the L1 and R1 trigger. Worse part is that it flips back to the wonky controls so I have to change them backI really love this franchise and the visuals bothering me is just a nit pick but I feel sad that the world may not love it as much cause the controls are so annoying.>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>.TLDR: Nostalgia, game bastardized the battles and visuals but I like the tweaks to gameplay. Glad I have a way to pay these guys so we get more langrisser games. Please don't flop q-q.This franchise itself is something i hold near and dear to my heart as a kid.I've played the first stage of Langrisser I or Warsong for those lucky enough to get a copy and so far the visuals are quite dissapointing.The character models look rather... cheap? Reminds me of the harem game i played that had all the world's historical/mythological war heroes as women. Honestly prefer Volkov's OG red master swordsman sprite over this. The battles in the original game also featured smaller sprites which made it easier to watch the battles. The huge ones in this game are rather jaring cause I can't grasp everything happening at once cause the sequence is so short. Lack of sound effects for the battles is also a big miss for me and again the cheap, sped up 2D animations make the battle weightless and boring. Again the OG game had much more going on, the general's big move deleting soldiers before they get to touch him, the dying sounds of the soldiers, the soldiers pushing the general back and forth. All of this detail was done without having fancier or modern sprites.  I do like that they've tweaked some of the mechanics in the game and look forward to replaying them in their new form and hope the devs continue to make more Langrisser games/remakes whilst tweaking/reworking the battle visuals to make it awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I am one of the crazy ones on steam that brought the entire NISA RPG Bundle.Let me tell you what a grand disappointment this is.It has Trails in the Sky but missing second and third chapter. (it's already on steam!)It has Trails of the Cold steel but missing the first one and second one. (it's also already on steam!)For Disgaea it's missing the third game.For YS it's missing one of those in the middle.I don't personally much care for Langrisser 3 or 4 so I don't mind they not being in the bundle. Langrisser 2 was one of my all-time favorite game when I grow up and I lost count of the number of hours I spent playing that game. Funny thing is, it was Japanese version I got when I was a kid and even without knowing Japanese, I enjoyed that game so much that I just have to get it as soon as I found out it's on steam.So Why am I rating this thumb down? Because this game only looks like Langrisser I and II on the outside and inside it's completely changed.At first Glance it's a good remade and I was almost in tears of joy when I hear Characters I know and love start talking and art was quite well drawn. As the first 2-3 hours passed the excitement died down and I start wondering what went wrong.1. Story tree system. Original Langrisser has always had a linear system. You can only play the level once unless you go on game magazine or internet to found a set of special secret combination key stroke to go back and replay certain level. (left, right, start, c)Without knowing that key stroke player will need to be very careful when playing and always try to kill as many mercenaries as possible before taking out the enemy general to maximize experience gained so you will have an easier time with better developed character for later levels. For this remake you can just play any previous level you already cleared. At any time and you retain all the experience/item/CP you already gained. So, if you have trouble with a level you can just go back to previous level to grind if needed. You can just blast away playing without any future planning. 2. New Class CP system.Like the story tree this remake now have a new Class CP system. It's point you get by leveling up and being MVP when a level is cleared. As long as you have CP you can do class change at any time in this game. What original game did was once you pick a class it's final you cannot go back but this game made it so that as soon as a class is unlocked you can go back to it in between level. So, you can make your main character a knight one level and change him back to infantry next level. This again takes out the character planning we had when we play the original. 3. Multiple story end systemYes, now it's got many different endings as long as progression conditions are met. It's always nice to add a choice driven plot line to the base game and there are now multiple endings to be had. Something is just feeling off with this supposed good thing. When I read Rin Palora’s comment under story Route Guide it hit me hard.“Rin Palora: I lack the patience to try every route, I never liked playing the evil side anyway and I somewhat got disheartened with the game when I realized the endings arn't that fleshed out (text crawls with the combat models even), the game lacks cutscenes that were in the Dramatic Edition and that I already saw the best ending (the path of light). Even if some claim the Empire and Independent path are more interesting.”Yes. Story might be different for multiple ends but the level remains mostly the same. Still the Same maps all the way with very few changes and I certainly won’t intentionally have characters lost in defeats so I can see the different character ending. 4. Graphics and animation Hell, this is a remade and people buy it because of better graphics then original right? But why is the combat screen all nearly the same? Why I no longer see mages toss fireball in the sky and see it bombs on enemy unit? Why I no longer see knight shadow charge with after image? Why I no longer see dragon knight spit thunder? Why is every single combat looks exactly the same? The units don’t even throw their spear/axe at flying enemy. That combat cut scene is just not as well made compare to the original and it seriously feels slacking. I can go on and on for the things I don’t like about this remake. To me even that Gatcha Mobile version of Langrisser is a lot better than this one.（Zerida I love you) I will however continue to play this and spent time to see every ending once then hide it in the corner of my game library forever. In comparison I will still love and enjoy Langrisser 2 original and play it on emulator again and again in the future.4/10 and a Huge Disappointment. Steam, I will pay again if you just bring the original Langrisser 1/2 as it is to steam.Note added. Finish all route and get all ending will take about 60-80 hours to get all achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest speaking, I love the Langrisser series, and it's one of the few SLGs back then that's very influential and even considered "Legendary". Some even buy Dreamcast just to be able to play the game back then... It's that hyped. But yes, it has aged and like most game series in Japan, going on a down fall after their 3rd sequel... (3rd is always the best? o_O) but anyway... here's the "remake" of both L1 and L2 in combine. And oh boy... there's nothing wrong with the game itself, plain simple, and well... simple.. and.. erm.. plain... so... you see what's wrong here? The AAA title back then can't even be considered a "complete" game for nowadays standard. But they simply remake the whole thing with some new graphics with very little changes and add a bunch of story "routes" and more "endings" to it, and worse, they failed to initiate the story telling mechanism itself making everything "plain" and "boring". Even the "UI" of the game is badly made. The tactical game play alone is good, for SLG (SRPG/Tactic) lovers this is still a great game, only if you haven't played or seen the artwork of the game elsewhere. Yeah, this feels like a remake that's didn't aim to please the existing fans but rather aimed to get new players... and uh... asking for a near AAA title price while delivering very few contents compared to the existing AAA titles we have nowadays... It's not bad for a fresh new player, but the price isn't appealing to them. On the other hand.. the old fans of the series find the new artwork... "disturbing"... thus that mixed review we are getting now.Some of the Characters in game look like a complete different person.. even their age looks different than the original matured (hard boiled) look... o_O Honestly speaking... the art style in this remake is way too "NIS" imo... even the color went over to the light pastel color side while the original classic is using sharp bright colors, so even when we are using the "classic" remake sprites, they still look extremely weird with that pastel colored artwork. Not that i hate NIS with their pastel style artwork, just that it's not suitable for this type of game with matured (hard boiled) design and artwork, pastel is more for the cute style NIS mostly do, especially since this game is not "new" but a "remake", so we have the "original" to compare to and with that huge fan base... it's not hard to imagine the outcome... Especially after we've seen the Chinese made online mobile version of this game, I just have to admit ZLong did way better job at the "remastering" than this version, even the "voice acting" seems better on the mobile version. Langrisser M has more "animated" graphics and their art work stay true to the original design just made modern (not to mention that they actually "includes" the old Langrisser series in a summarized form in their game, and this remake feels less than that summarized form). Here on the remake, they simply turn the characters into another person in both look and age, and the art work feels very... amateur when they mix pastel colors on a serious looking artwork without making it cute... some doujin games nowadays did better job in the design... Oh well... here comes the lecture... back then, when games are turning from 8-bit (256 colors) graphic to 16 bit colors, and the storage technology's been improving to allow bigger data as they change from floppy to cd-rom, CG has under go a huge revolution, and most games, who only have good looking characters printed on the game's box cover but not inside the game, can now have those nice looking characters directly inside their games. Story telling and all that become easier for the game developers with the visual upgrades which leads to the evolution of other types of games as they started to separate RPG from Visual novels. Langrisser happened just around that corner, when the consoles finally able to take up big storage capacity (cd-rom) and their character designs become one of a kind in the industry and yeah, with the new trend (it really is a trend back then, for collectors and such) of pc wallpapers and all that (they gift those as extra in their package - aka "omake" in the past), they somehow left a big impression on the players as one of the games with the best looking characters. Especially the daring design they did with the armors and ahem... bikini... though they are not the 1st with such ideas, they showed the world how good they can look in high res CG art. That alone landed them in the AAA title category back then as these JPG files got around among the collectors and most of the SLG Gamers have them on their PC as desktop wallpaper just because those art looks real good. And Langrisser has been one of the most expensive games and brand since because of that... So, here comes the problem. This remake tried to change the original looks of those characters, they even tried to change the daring armor designs into something modest... That's why i said, for new players, they don't really mind since they've never experienced the good looking original ones before, but for the existing fans, this is a downgraded experience. Yet without all those selling points, this game is still asking for a AA grade price. That's why even to new players, this isn't really appealing for nowadays standard when the age old contents are no better than some hobbyist / doujin games. Even if we considered NIS brand power over the turn based tactic lovers to buy this game, it still leave a huge gap because this game isn't using the famous tactic system we see in Disgaea or other NIS tactic games but instead using the old Career-Masaya tactic system. So yeah... an age old gap...Like most of the Japanese games back then, Langrisser continued to L3 and up to L5, but goes down hill from the 3rd sequel... why must it always be 3? Well... for most of the cases, fans grew tired of the same things over and over again. But for Langrisser's case, Career Soft left Masaya after L3, developed and release L4 and L5 as indie titles without a huge fund and media backup. Masaya themselves later release Langrisser Millennium with another dev team (Santa Entertainment) which landed in quite a disaster on the change of art concepts and all that for the fans. Without doubt it tainted the original game's title and it's straight down hill from there. Career soft moved on to create  which inherited the world concept of Langrisser. Masaya themselves are handed over to Extreme in 2014 and Langrisser become forgotten by the history. Until later when Extreme outsourced the mobile project to Zlongame while outsourced the remake to Chara-Ani. Chara-Ani did a bad job as we see here and angered quite a lot of the fans, but Zlongame on the other hand, did a splendid job reviving the franchise and made it grow even bigger than the old franchise by bringing in a lots of old players while still pleasing the existing fans.Well, like i mentioned above, Langrisser M is free and it includes L1~L5 stories (with some of the alternative routes) in a summarized form and a new story of their own for that series keeping the original looks in design and all that, and better voice acting. So it makes it even less worthy to buy this game when you can actually get another better visual, better voiced, better story telling and way better executed in every way, for free... (other than the fact you need to grind, it's an online game after all, but judging from how tiresome and repetitive when we are getting all routes in this one, it's no different than grinding anyway...)So my advice will be, unless you are a true fan (who've spent a fortune on this series back then) and wanted this just for the collection purpose, else it's best to try out the online version. It's way better even for a fan. Langrisser M is there for fan service and because how well it's done, it's attracted more none fan based players than this remake here. Plus, there's Co-Op and PvP. :3

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just get this out of the way and say that the story is really bad.  It's one giant cliché but since many strategy games aren't necessarily known for their story I won't harp on it.  What makes this game really bad is the game play.  There are two main factors I look at when playing an SRPG, strategy and balance.TLDR:  Too easy and mindless.  No strategy beats “just run in there and attack”Strategy:  If it's too hard then it forces you to play a certain way and rather then develop a strategy your just do the one method that works.  If it's too easy then strategy is a waste of time and because you just run in and attack.  This game is way too easy to be considered a strategy game. Run in and attack is pretty much the only thing you need to do.  I didn't grind or go back to older stages but my team could just crush the enemies like they were nothing.  The game tries to put in terrain advantages or a paper rock scissors effect between units but the problem is it just doesn't matter.  There's what seems like a neat feature that each of your characters can pay to have mercenaries support you in battle but ultimately they don't matter either.  You're commanders hit so much harder than mercenaries and if you kill an enemy commander then all of their mercenaries die as well.  Mercenaries just and up taking up a valuable attacking positions on the grid and just give you more actions to take so you feel like you're doing something.  By halfway through the game I didn't use any mercenaries and the maps went faster; maybe an extra turn but because I wasn't micro managing 4 times the number of units it went so much faster.I can honestly say the hardest part of this game is there are certain spots on the map where if you stand, you will get an item.  This is the games only difficulty because it will be hard for you on some maps not to kill everything before you can run someone over there.  It's also rather annoying because many of the spots are areas you don't need to go so you're just slowing down your offense so you'll just waste turns waiting while you send someone over to the spot because you can clear the map faster than you can send someone across it.They fact that enemies WON'T ATTACK if the counter attack will kill them makes it stupid easy.  If you buff your character's attack so they 1 shot enemies, the enemies just won't attack them.  That means no one will try to even chip down his health, how is it even possible to lose?  I have had so many battles where my commander is surrounded with only half health but no enemies will attack because the enemy will die so I can just pick them off.Balance:  Classes are not balanced well in this game.  Mages will have difficulty for most of the game keeping up to level.  The issue is that while physical units can move and attack in the same turn, mages can't move and caste magic in the same turn.  Since you only need to run in and attack, it becomes hard for them to get kills if you don't purposely slow yourself down and let them.  Since virtually any character can learn heal skills and every heal skill is a % based heal, you can just use physical units and rush in and attack.  It's not more challenging to use mages, it just takes longer.  They get some pretty good spells later on but honestly by the end of the game it doesn't matter.  You might think it would be good to outfit them with mercenaries to help them get kills, and that will help, it's just there's no real value to going through the effort when you can run in with physical units and attack.The ability to change the story based on meeting certain conditions in a match could have been really cool.  But with a game so easy and a story so bland there's no point.  If for example there was something at the half way point in the game that branches the story, you can take path A all the way to the end, then go back to the branch and pick path B.  When you go back and start playing path B you keep your levels and items and if this game was easy before, when you're end game level at the mid point it's beyond boring.  And with such a bad story, what's the point?  Also, based on which story path you pick, it will start locking in your commanders and not let you pick your full team.  In one path, 5 of my 8 commanders were required in every fight, meaning I only got to pick 3 of my commanders, so many of the people I had been playing with and leveling had to get benched for the rest of the game.I played the first game, saw 3 branches and had enough and decided to try the second game.  After 2 missions I saw it was the same thing and just stopped.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself is good, there's a reason the game is still well known after all these years.But there are too many other problems.First of all a reamake of a game that age has no business being several Gigabytes big. Obviously there was a lack of optimisation when creating this remake.Also the quiz questions at the beginning of the game are badly thought out, the question about the players opinion on Demons for example can't really be answered without any previous knowledge about the nature of the Demons in the game world.As far as the new character designs go, getting rid of the needlesly large shoulder pads was good, making most female chracters even more scanty clad however is silly. These kind of designs started to be outdated in the 90's there is no reason to still see something like this today.But clearly the worst part is the key binding. First, there is no reason to keep the key binding a secret from the player. Second, not being able to change key binding is tedious. And third, l if a game doesn't allow to change the key binding the game has no business whatsoever making use of the Y or Z keys. This is an international release. Making use of either key is bound to be troublesome for either the qwertz or the qwerty keyboard users, alienating customers with that stupid nonsense is also something that was seriously getting old in the 90s.Needlessly big, questionable character desingns and tedious key bindings, I guess there's worse, but for a release of a professional company it's doesn't seem acceptable to me.

You CAN go back and do the level again. The soundtrack is also a banger, mostly. The game gets harder every time you beat it and restart on challenge mode. Allies that die are lost not, except for a few specific maps, but their deaths also change the course of the story. some Allies are also lost over the course of the game for story reasons.The Bad: The start of the Kingdom Knight theme is an absolute mess. The REST of the soundtrack is AMAZING. I have no idea what the composer was thinking on that one. There's no way to save a complete game and go back for the missed routes. You either have to load an older save and go back or start from the beginning The Ugly: The AI is fairly basic and the some battles seemed designed for you to abuse the AI by using single units to bait out spells like Meteor that deal heavy damage over a massive range. Having high magic resist units can do this without losing much HP.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it was worth while for me to buy on sale and play through once. Some problems are that the AI is dumb as a rock, romance options have only been expanded in Langrisser 1, not 2, despite there already being multiple characters that show romantic interest, still only one option, and that one option is unconsumated in the ending and entirely unsatisfying, bland, and extremely poor story telling. Many of the characters are interesting on their own, but the writing is so weak that their actions end up being nonsensical. Satoshi Urushihara's art is the great strength of the series, I would not have bought the game without it. They could have saved money and not bothered creating new art for the remake, and commission new set piece art scenes from Satoshi Urushihara possibly, or have hired a better writer. I did not play more than one route, but on skimming through a VOD of them, they seem lazy, unthoughtout, and thrown together, maybe I'm wrong about this, its just a surface impression. The music is good in some places, but for the most part is generic. The mechanics are fine as far as I can tell, the AI more urgently needs to be improved than any other mechanic. The units and class upgrades are cool and satisfying. Item upgrading gets a little tedious. Having to sit through 20 enemies each individually skipping their turn doing nothing is silly, these should all skip at once. You should also have a command available to have all your units stand still, rather than having to select the command on each commander, or each individual unit. It is an extremely easy game, so unless you really need a challenge you are unlikely to be frustrated at any point. I would prefer that upon beating the game once you have the option to just view all the game's content, essentially being able to see all routes without having to play through again. A huge pain point is the behavior of allied AI, often behaving in suicidal ways, and not even being coded to follow the rest of your army, just blindly attacking the nearest enemy. It may be shallow, but I'd have prefer a harem option, and the option to not kill enemy commanders if you want. This of course would lack drama and be a more base indulgent experience, but the writing fails to be of enough quality to take seriously anyway, so having the option to just go full positive power fantasy would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Fire Emblem: produced for the NES, released on April 20, Langrisser: produced for the Sega Genesis, released on April 26, The similarities are unavoidable, but that just means that if you like Fire Emblem, you'll probably like this.  What sets Langrisser apart is primarily the hired units: before each chapter, you can hire ~4 generic units for each of your characters.  The generic units have different stats/prices and are made available by leveling up your characters into higher classes.  The system overall has upsides and downsides, but I'd recommend it to fans of the genre who are looking for a unique perspective from an old classic.

_childDocuments_.review: I started with this game on Sega Genesis (where it is known as "Warsong") and just had to get this when I found out about it. It's a bit different from the Sega version, but it is at least as much fun. I'm enjoying the variety that these differences offer as I replay the first game and am also glad it is not frustratingly difficult and unforgiving like the Sega version, even though I was able to beat it on Sega.Anyway, it is a fantastic turn-based tactical RPG and my favorite in the genre. I would highly recommend it to anyone with an interest in either genre. I wasn't even a player of the genre before I discovered the game on Sega, yet it hooked me and became one of my all-time favorite games of any genre and on any platform.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent remake of these games. The gameplay transitions perfectly from the original and there is a lot added to Langrisser I to give it the same branching narrative of Langrisser II. It has a very particular art style that I like, but not everyone may enjoy, but there is the option to change to the classic art if preferred. The music is also an excellent remix, but the original score is available as well.The ability to reverse time and go back to old levels or try different paths of the branching narrative is great. It helps balance the difficulty to allow you to go back and gain more experience if you need it or just push on if you don't. For people who want more challenge, there are also higher difficulty levels that you unlock upon completion that keep increasing each time you beat the game.The only big drawback is the lack of English voice acting. During the main plot, there is text you can read, but level up, spell casting, and MVP dialogue have no text, so there is no way to know what the characters are saying if you only speak English.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun remake of the original.However they made the game a lot easier, which in my opinion is a good thing as the original games were brutally hard. Perhaps a bit too easy, except for the last levels where we are back to hard.The AI is a bit disappointing though, in the original the commander would always treat at 6 HP or less, however the new AI will happily suicide both its units and commanders on highly questionable engagements. The AI isn't there to win, it is there to lose.The originals also had bad AI, but the AI units were tougher to compensate, now the AI generally has weaker units than the player and is still bad, making most levels a slog rather than a challenge.If there is anything this game would need, I'd say a difficulty slider would be a good improvement.Also: Böser!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking about picking this game up because you've heard about the series and how there's a ton of different versions of the first two games, this is probably the easiest version to get into that you can buy today without emulating or modding. Controller support works great, Steam cloud for backing up your saves, some QoL improvements to keep the game moving. It's a good port and the whole game runs fine. You've also got the benefit of voice acting which sounds alright (Japanese audio only). Some people absolutely despise the gameplay changes from the original. Making battles shorter overall, screwing with some gameplay mechanics. You might hate it or might not care. But for the people who do, this is unfortunately a compromise you'll have to make if you prefer the convenience of buying this over just downloading something like a Windows 98 copy of Langrisser 1 (which is probably the definitive version of the first title) and going through the trouble of setting it up. You could just emulate but you will be using the fast forward button via emulation a lot to get through battles. But this game at least starts and plays without any technical problems and there are QoL improvements, for better or worse...However, know that the game is a bit misleading, specifically when it advertises options such as using the old music and original art style. I bought it because I thought I was getting the definitive version of choosing whatever graphics style and soundtrack I wanted, I was wrong.The OST is not complete like I had hoped, at least out of the box. I believe it has the original two OSTs and the new OST for this version, but you have to buy the other versions (Like the PC engine version) separately as DLC. These versions have different renditions of the original soundtrack and its down to personal preference as to which you'll prefer. Very frustrating as I was already on the fence about buying this game even on sale and now I have to dump more money on it for something that should be in the game anyway.But the art style. Good god, it's hideous. I heard you could change it, but you really can't. You can select the original character portraits, which are really good by the way. The original designs look amazing. But the character sprites for the map and battles? Unchangeable and hideous. You're stuck with the remastered art style's chibi look and it does NOT FIT AT ALL with the old portraits. You can't even select the old 16-bit style over it. I would've loved to have that over what we got here. It just looks comical now when mixed with the old character portraits. The battles also don't look as engaging as the originals.If you're new to the series, you should check it out, at least on sale, but if you're an older fan, it might actually frustrate the hell out of you. I didn't play the originals when they were new, nor did I play them that much but I know what it's like to have a beloved game absolutely destroyed on a visual (and even technical) level and spat out for a premium... 'cough' Warcraft III Reforged 'cough'.Check out our curator page if you wanna see our recommendations for games.Thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't really hold up very well. The pacing is very slow in both games is glacially slow, and you will spend a long time between turns just watching units "activate" and then standby without doing anything at all. There are lots of narrow corridors to slog through, and there is very little challenge. The story is cliched and terrible with almost no character development at all. The developers didn't even bother getting the control labels right, to show you how much they (don't) care about the quality of their game.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, but it really needs a challenge mode. The game almost seems designed to let you win, no matter how poorly you play. In principle, you're supposed to carefully utilize the terrain to your advantage and make thoughtful tactical decisions. In practice, your characters eventually get so overpowered that you can almost just throw them at the enemy and still expect to win. I even tried to handicap myself by using only three commanders per level, but all that happens is you turbo-charge your commanders by hogging all the experience points. If that doesn't bother you, then the game is otherwise really fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: While the remastered did a lot of things right, there's few things wrong. The graphical update in menus and whatnot is very nice.To the characters however, aren't the best. I played through the game (specifically the Langrisser 1) using the original art portraits because they have much more personality & character to them. Sadly the new redesigns feel a bit too dry and generic. Been there done that before-styled characters.Aside from character design, the only other issue I have with this collection was the lack of.. Well.. Collection ! Playing the 2 games is the only choice you have. It would've really been nice to have a "Extra" or something of the sort. Like a art gallery to see concept art, scrapped content, etc. Or a BGM/Soundtrack to listen to the songs ingame.Ultimately tho, it's a banger ! I enjoyed experiencing Langrisser 1, which I never got to prior to this !Certified hood classic !
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: So far I love this game! But for all thoes older Sega enthusiasist this game is a remake of an older Sega game called warsong! (langreisser 1) but unlike the original sega game there is the ability to replay paths and change the paths taken.  This game should offer the nostalgic gamer of turn based combat at least 24+ hours of game time!!! Great game!! I'll post another review after I play the second langrisser!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Great old school rpg one of the most fun games I have played similar to d2 in that you play it.. put it down then 10- 20 years later have to play it again.Can be slow paced and boring to some younger actiony players.. this is more slow paced turn based style of combat here.Great graphics.. good import that is done decently.Have played almost all of these and have several versions on emulators.Really miss these kinds of games hope someone makes more : )
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty tepid recommendation overall; I think you have to either be a Langrisser fan already to pay full price, or just a big SRPG fan if this goes on sale again.There's lots of content here with the branching story paths, and the two separate games. However, a good number of the story paths largely overlap, so even though there are 13 paths for Langrisser II for instance, about half of them are all variations of the Light path. With that said, the major variations are all pretty interesting, and there are more than enough of them to be worth it. The Story Tree also makes it pretty easy to see the alterations if you want to blitz through the game again, but it does so at the expense of the difficulty since your characters retain their levels and equipment. Even without the Story Tree, the difficulty is very low. Don't expect to be challenged by this game. Apparently NG+ enemies scale higher to match your units if you play it, but locking the difficulty until after you've completed the game is extremely silly. The game has this weird tendency to hide information from the player (i.e. sudden reinforcements, very rarely the objective changes, detailed information on new classes being withheld until you obtain it), but because the game is so easy I was never really upset about the game doing this. The other main weakness is the presentation. While I do think the portraits and backgrounds themselves look fine (there's a classic option for old school fans as well), the map sprites look straight out of a mobile game. I personally don't think that graphics are that important, but if they are to you, you should probably avoid this game. The gameplay itself is pretty snappy, with you being able to jump from battle to battle relatively quickly. There are some minor annoyances though, like the group AI getting stuck on corners and the game needing to go through every enemy's action even if they don't move (very stupid design choice). The story/writing easily carry this game for me. Every character is pretty fleshed out, even the bad guys, the dialogue is overall pretty fun (although it gets cringe-worthy a few times), the choices help with player engagement, and a lot of the conversations happen on the map which keeps things interesting. Also, the remastered OST is really enjoyable.Not a glowing recommendation, but sometimes you just want to sit down and make a bunch of guys explode.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: A graphic remaster of a 1991 game.  From my perspective as a fire emblem fan, This is a very good strategy game for 1991 standard. But very outdated for 2020 standard, compared to similar strategy games, such as Fire Emblem, Langrisser still needs a lot of improvement in the core gameplay and storytelling method. The monster/mercenaries are not unique at all, but the art is okay.Nevertheless, this game is still fun to play. Earlier chapters are laughable, but this game really gets better on later chapters with their unit / creature variation and multiple story branching.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Being Der Langrisser one of my most favourite games ever, I can't express the thrill that I felt when I heard that this game was going to be released on Steam, but right after that, my expectations fell to the ground, when I realized that it wasn't actually going to be the same thing.To begin with, it's nice that the graphics received an upgrade, then again, I didn't really like the new design of the characters, they look kinda "cute and innocent" compared to the original art style. The soundtrack received an upgrade as well, which was kinda cool, I must confess.Moving on to the storyline, which is one of the strongest points of the series (at least in my modest opinion), they've tried to create some extra branches and endings for the two games. Even though I praise the attempt to bring some innovation and refreshment, I can't really say that I liked all of them, especially because some seemed to be kinda pointless and redundant.Now, in the areas of gameplay and difficulty, this version is a cakewalk compared to the original one. You don't have to worry about saving money, or which class you're going to select, because it's a like a damn Final Fantasy game, where you can grind and play with different classes as much as you'd like. They've also changed the way the troops fight with each other, turned generals basically into tanks and made the AI as dumb as possible, to the point where they'd rather sacrifice an entire unity trying to kill someone they're weaker against, rather than attempting a different strategy.Overall, I'd say that it's an ok game, but despite the resemblance, it has simply nothing to do with the original game; if I could, I'd give a neutral mark without thinking twice about. That said, I still hope that someday in the future, a definitive version can be released, but after this disappointment, I really doubt that it'll ever happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing over the top, combat is simple but not boring. Not a fan of re playing the game just to meet that one specific codition to change the story but thats just me. Only issue i had with the game was that after 4-5 misions the Protag was so OP he could almost solo misions. Other then that i would recomend this game to anyone who likes FE style game go have some fun or just try the demo and decide for urself.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic job modernizing the game. The graphics and music have been remastered. The story has been expanded significantly and brings voice acting (Japanese only), while bringing many modern conveniences to the gameplay. It does seem a bit easier than the old Sega Genesis "Warsong" game, but still a blast. And if you're in the mood for a b it of nostalgia, you can play the game with original music, original graphics, and the older art that the games used to have. Funtastic!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: First off the Bad.  OMG this thing needs better Controller support, do better NIS!  Make sure you use the Steam game controller configuration tools to get the best possible controller support for this game.  Once I got that configured I have not had any issues with using my Xbox One Controller.The Good, I think I have been enjoying this game more than I anticipated.  It's good old school with a new school look.  Fight animations can be a little old but have enough  action in them to not be immediately annoying but they are easily skipable if you get impatient like I do.  I enjoy the branching story paths and the ability to go back to old maps and replay them.  Character progression and trying out different configurations has been enjoyable as well.  While this game is not incredibly deep, but the maps are engaging enough to keep  you from lounging on your laurels too much.I bought it on sale for $30 and is a pretty good price in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: A bit too easy compared to the originals on Sege Mega Drive. And the new style is too modern day anime. But. The good thing is that you can switch between the old graphic styles of the maps, and the characters. And all classical sountracks are available, too. But it should be included and not be sold as DLC. Nevertheless this new edition is fun to play with some nice additions. A well rounded game which may be interesting for newbies as well as classical gamers who enjoyed these gems back in the days. The greatest bonus of all is, that you are able to play Langrisser II in Englisch. The original Langrisser II was only available in japanese. As an oldschool gamer I prefer the originals.  But theses are definitely a must buy for every fan of this series.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Much more enjoyable than the original.. and I loved the original, warts and all. Let's face it.. Warsong and Der Langrisser had some pretty major flaws and mechanical issues. It was not a very enjoyable ride fighting with the gameplay constantly.This recreation gave the same feel as the original and kept the emotion and story. It removed the stressful bits that really took away from its potential and replayability. Well worth playing this version.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game at full price, no regret.This is a huge part of my childhood gaming. This along with Tactics Ogre and Fire Emblem were the games I found most fun to play. There's a significant lack of Japanese Turn Based Tactical Games ala Fire Emblem on the PC market, so am glad that NISA brought this to PC.This game is definitely no XCOM 2 WotC or Fire Emblem Three Houses, but it has its own character that strongly reminisce the 90s-2000s era of Tactical Games --- that alone is respectable. Thank you Chara-ani and NISA for bringing this game to PC!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Langrisser was a great nostalgia trip.  The old gameplay and new graphics was enough to capture my attention to fully complete every achievement, something I rarely do with steam games.  I can only hope other strategy games such as this get introduced to steam/PC. The only wish-list items I have is a way to increase difficulty, and a desire for magic damage to be toned down.-Configuring and using a PC controller did not take any effort on my part. It just seemed to work well. This is using a logitech controller.-While fun, the unit balance appears to be off/different than what I recall. It is very easy for your unit choice to be a tier higher and/or significantly better than the enemies' units, even during the first playthrough. -Magic is very overpowered. On every play through it was easy to just obliterate an entire map of units with one commander. This includes new game+ difficulty and regular game with commanders at an equal level to the enemy. -Similarly, to the above note, when you get to the end game scenarios, the enemy is heavy on magic, meaning that usually, your troops do not last long.  This removes a fun element of game play.-New game+ settings make completing every story branch a time-consuming task. I enjoyed the time consumption, but I could see that becoming a nuisance for other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of Langrisser (Warsong NA version) then this series is for you. As a throwback to 90's version you can swap the graphics, art and music back to that era. Warsong was solid turn based strategy game that I spent countless hours replaying.  Class changing and upgrading, troop selection, itemization just to name a few things you manage while playing. The update does it justice. It's definitely easier than the old version, and faster game play. I have not had any issues playing whatsoever. As some people have said you need a controller to play it, which is a bit of common sense as I wouldn't want to play it with a mouse and keyboard. That said I haven't had a single issue with the controller from first start up until today. If you are on the fence about the game and like turn based strategy I strongly recommend you try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Warsong (American release of Langrisser 1 by Treco in the 90s) might be my favorite video game of all time.  This beautiful remake allowed me to enjoy the story and similar, though upgraded, gameplay.  The bonus game Langrisser 2 with translation (subtitles) allowing an entire playthrough.  2 games in 1; I love all the upgrades, items, class trees, and story paths!  I just completed both games and I must say it was wonderful.  Thank you for bringing this style of play and this story back to life!  I hope to see more titles like this and perhaps more English versions and variations of the Langrisser story.  How I would love an RTS/TBS combo similair to Total War with the Langrisser Universe?!?  I can dream, but until then, maybe a few more play-throughs!  Buy this game and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

Challenge a little on the low end however. Great if you're a fan of the series, probably interesting if you haven't played similar games before.

_childDocuments_.review: Great strategy game which is a remake of a classic genesis game that i grew up playing.  This game lead me to playing Shining Force (hope they remake that too) and is the basis of my interest in strategy game.  I can't really find one negative thing about this game, but think you had to appreciate the classics to get into this game.  Newcomers to the genre might be put off on how the game plays, but if you spend time with it, you will see how more modern games came into being off this game. _childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Stuck at home because of the virus outbreak, I felt like playing a turn based tactics game, and this game just launched.  It does not disappoint.  Don't expect your favorite tactics jrpg though, there are barely any extras... in fact I had to check to make sure this was still a Japanese game and not one of those western anime-style indies.  But what they provide is pretty much straightforward, just the way I like it.  Besides a few event illustrations, the story gets told simply.  During battles some surprises often occur which are significant story-wise.  The whole game is relatively easy, save for the first few missions of Langrisser I where you didn't have chance to level yet and they hit you with powerful units and limited turns.In summary, I was expecting to just play a few battles and go meh, back to (insert favorite tactics game here), instead I was glued for 2-3 days all the way to the end.  This is as classic gameplay as you can get.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Background:Langrisser 1 has a few changes that are different from the original Warsong, mainly the gameplay and the story paths (similiar to what langrisser 2 has to offer). My review are focus on the comparison between Warsong and new remake.Graphic- I am glad they stick to 2D and you can toggle between remastered or classic characters. The remastered characters arts are great except for the main characters, where they look pretty kiddish.Japanese Voice Acting / Music- Good. Music had been remastered from the classics and you can toggle between modern or classic music.Shops- Now the game enable you to buy weapon, armour and accessories from a shop. The items get updated time to time after a few stages. Money is limited so spent wisely. (since the game is so easy, money is plenty)Character Class Tree- Most of the characters have a different tree and a unique class 5, however there are a few character that dont really suit that last class. Taylor has been surprising the best, other than Ledin in this game, and he can walk as fast as any non-horse type character despite being a serpent.Gameplay-  The story path now has Light, Imperial, Evil, Independent for Langrisser 1. 3/4 of the route are very easy, only the last 1/4 of the game where it spam you with magic attacks that is when the difficulty sudden spike up. The tactic element has been tuned down significantly, for example you can wipe the slimes without the need of priest type. The during-combat style has changed where everyone fights at same time and looks very messy as compared to Warsong. I kind of miss the "ugh" sound when an enemy died.Conclusion: If you havent play this before, I would suggest playing the classic Warsong. This game is great remake but it's nostalgia at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: awesome remake of a timeless classic, improved gameplay while keeping the old felling of the game. you can chose between old art, old maps, new art and new maps and mix those options. it also gives a bit of depth to the gameplay now that comandres can only heal through magic since there is no rest comand like before. all in all 8/10 game that would recomend to anyone who likes tactic rpgs or the older games serioulsy hope they remake all of them
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is very different from the previous versions of the PS and saturn consoles. Comparing it to the 16-bit cartridge versions or PC langrisser 1 would be unfair though I preferred the genesis version of langrisser most. I won't mention the new character designs and the game engine.The most noticeable changes are the HP points have changed from full health of 10 to hundreds and no rest or treat move to heal. There's no hidden shops, class changes and level caps of 10. In old console versions there's an item to revert back to first starting class while retaining the stats except the command range which is limited by classes. In this version you can change your class by earning CP points and able to switch without getting to max lv of 10 as of the old versions. Also missing are the Masaya stuff like hidden stage parodius Aniki stage in der langrisser from mega drive and some reference to the old NCS stuff(Masaya sword). The battle scenes are a hit or miss depending on the players, I hated langrisser 3 on the 3d battles. There are complains on the difficulty being too easy and playing through to new game for increasing the difficulty is a hassle. I have no issues on that part, it's mostly personal preference.There's still branching paths in the game just not as much from some SRW series and the paper, scissors & stone structure of the game is present. Voice overs and speed up on the cut scenes are new. The battles are loaded fast compare to 2 to 5 seconds loading on the CD based consoles. Music are better in quality and I prefer remakes though I can choose from the classic BGM.There are issues with controllers in this game, there are ways to fix it. From big picture mode controller setting to wipe the setting inside config.vdf (not everything just below "SDL_GamepadBind") also depending on the type of controller used. Troublesome, but not a factor for fans of this series or player used to this stuff. Nowadays there's so much games to choose from why this? If no one supports RPGSTG like this, then the devs and publishers have no reason to make or port over games of these type over to PC or localize them. Shinning force series remake, growlanser series and those lesser known games won't be seen again with gamers boycotting games based on these problems. Not they are in the wrong for there are tons of games to choose and play then wasting money on a game troublesome to make it work to play. I just kinda hope reviewers and discussions of the game would be kind and bearing than dismissing games in the early weeks of release.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: The game is for people who liked Wargroove.  The twist here is that each leader unit can have 4-6 mercenary troops for each battle.  The leader has gear and xp, but troops are disposable. Troops are entirely independent during combat, but perform better when only a few tiles away from the person that brought them.  Rock, Paper, Scissor is Sword, Spear, Horsey- but again a twist that a few other types exist- flying,  archer, demon.   I am pretty sure I owned Warsong on the Genesis, but I don't think it was that remarkable for me.   Standing on its own, this version is a good turn based game.I do not like to focus on price for reviews because everybody's situation is different, but the price point is not in line with the majority of other games on Steam.  My controller [xbox] works with the game, but definitely get the demo first to see if you can live with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Langrisser fan, the extra content is worth replaying for, and the option to switch to classic portraits/soundtrack is a nice bonus. If you've never played Langrisser before, this should work as an intro to the series. I had no trouble using a controller and I like the redesigned menus. I really hope we see some more Langrisser remakes like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially a little disappointed because I had thought the remake had thrown out the original awesome artwork but was pleasantly and immensely gratified when the first thing I found in the settings is that not only can you go back to the original artwork but you can also choose to use the original music.For a bit of background on why this seems important there was a game I found called Growlanser which as you may guess from the similarities of the name is made as a spiritual successor of Langrisser both of these series have one thing in common beyond amazing gameplay and deep narrative is the artist  Satoshi Urushihara who has made hundreds upon hundreds of varied characters and designs for games and anime, who has inspired and contributed shaping art styles in Japanese animated media for 40 years.Seeing a game this old be remade and with such care and dedication makes me hopeful that the other games from the series will get a remake, especially seeing as some games in the series never got a release outside Japan.Now while I want to sing unmitigated praise and wax poetic about the game I am not without understanding about technical problems, the main of which being no mouse and keyboard support, logically this should be a simple problem to solve and it baffles me that that this game requires a controller to play and launched on steam without such a simple feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played langrisser since i was a freakin teen. Theres not a lot of games out there that i could sit and play for several hours and this game is one of them. Yea i agree price is wayy too high but considering the amount of content.. and various playthrough.. you could pretty play this game for a hell long of time. My only problem is the ai is kinda retarded... other than that 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

_childDocuments_.review:
Langrisser I - Long ago, there was a terrible war over a legendary sword said to grant its wielder unlimited power. The blood of those who vowed to protect it and those who sought its power for themselves permeated the battlefields of El Sallia. That sword is known as Langrisser. Of those who swore to protect it, the royal family of Baldea has safeguarded it from the world for many generations. Thanks to Baldea, tales of Langrisser soon faded from memory.
However, Baldea's sworn duty would be called to action once again. Motivated by power and the conviction to rule the world, Kaiser Digos and the Dalsis Empire he commanded invade Baldea, seeking the enticing power of Langrisser. Ledin, the prince of Baldea, narrowly escapes the invasion, and devises a way to avenge his father, who had been killed by Kaiser Digos.
Now, Ledin must reclaim Langrisser, which his ancestors fought so valiantly to protect—thus beginning his journey that will test his loyalty to the Light.

Langrisser II - It has been centuries since the War of the Sacred Sword razed El Sallia. Now, incessant violence plagues the continent. Isolated battles arise all across the land, ravaging towns and nations, before creeping to the next. The Kingdom of Baldea is but a legend, and Langrisser is no more than a fairytale.
A young traveler named Elwin journeys the land with Hein, an amateur mage he met on his travels. One day during their travels, they decide to stay the night at an inn in Hein's hometown, a small village known as Salrath. In the middle of the night, Hein bursts into Elwin's room, pale as the night moon behind him. He claims that forces of the Rayguard Empire were seen on the outskirts of Salrath. They are searching for Liana, a young girl who lived there.
What business could the empire have with a village as peaceful as Salrath and a defenseless girl? Paying no heed to the precarious situation he was about to involve himself with, Elwin leaves for the countryside without hesitation to save her.
_childDocuments_.name: Langrisser I & II

name: Lair of the Clockwork God
detailed_description: WHY PLAY ONLY ONE GENRE OF GAME when you could be playing two slightly different ones at the exact same time? BEN is a die-hard, old-school LucasArts Adventure fan. He has one foot stuck in the 90s, his feet never leave the floor, and he’s happiest collecting any old junk he can lay his hands on, in the hopes of combining it all together to solve a satisfying puzzle. His cohort and sidekick DAN ...has aspirations to be the next big hit indie platform character. He's got everything he needs: he's hip, he's sensitive, and his nose is a different colour to the rest of his face. LAIR OF THE CLOCKWORK GOD sees you switching between both characters and using their unique abilities together in a race-against-time effort to stop all the Apocalypses happening simultaneously, by teaching an old computer about feelings. Solve classic point-and-click style puzzles as Ben to create unique upgrade items for Dan, so he can jump higher, run faster and blast away at everything with a shiny new gun. Then, run and jump as Dan to unlock new areas and exciting new puzzles for Ben! If you haven't played the old Dan and Ben games (you should), or you have but can't remember what happened, there's NO NEED TO WORRY! Lair of the Clockwork God is a STANDALONE Dan and Ben Adventure, which means you need to know absolutely nothing about Ben There, Dan That! or Time Gentlemen, Please! whatsoever. None of the original plot is referenced, the characters are re-introduced expertly, etc etc. It's all good.

_childDocuments_.review: The long-awaited follow-up to point-and-click classics  and  is a point-and-click platformer hybrid, and is both great fun and a very satisfying gameplay experience. With the purchase comes a copy of , which is an elaborate tie-in joke/puzzle to , but also a fun visual novel in its own right.Take turns controlling Ben through pure point-and-click puzzles, and Dan through platforming challenges, switching between the two with the press of a button. The game uses an action menu to present relevant action when playing as Ben, and is therefore best played with a controller, although a keyboard seems to be required for a certain puzzle. This doesn't mean that they've skimped on the puzzles though, as some of them are pretty difficult, and there are even several inventory puzzles. Often, Dan's platforming abilities will be required to solve puzzles as well, but they're not just a means to get around, as most of the platforming is genuinely fun. It is even difficult at times, with moving obstacles, crumbling platforms and deadly traps, although there are unlimited lives, and checkpoints are plentyful. and  are the developer's first games to officially support Linux. For the most part, I've not had any issues with this game, except I've not been able to play it using Nvidia graphics on my Optimus laptop. I expect this to be a problem with my drivers though, as I've not heard of other Linux players having similar issues.Overall, I've enjoyed the game a lot, and if you're a fan of both point-and-clicks and platformers, as I am, do give it a look. And if you decide to pick up this game, you can expect more over-the-top jokes, stabs at indie game tropes, and fourth wall breaking puzzles than you've ever seen in a single video game before.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I am friends with the devs. I've hung out with them several times at various events and really admire the both of them. That admiration is well earned because of games like this one, which I REALLY enjoyed. The humor and story is very unique and kept me smiling and laughing, both the adventure puzzling and the platforming were challenging (maybe a bit too challenging in the platforming department as I had trouble several times, but I am not usually a platform gamer), and above all - the game is FUN. The devs have been dissecting the adventure genre for over a decade and know what they are doing. I couldn't put it down.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure games I've played in a long time - which I do not say lightly since that includes Broken Reality, Lamplight City, Mage's Initiation, and Unavowed. Really impressive idea of mashing adventure and platforming, some of the funniest writing I've seen in awhile, and dunks on the Daily Mail. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockwork God is one-part 90s adventure game, one-part challenging platformer. It’s a mix that shouldn’t work, but it does. You play as Ben and Dan, the developers of the game, on an adventure full of indie-darling platforming and combining, *ahem* crafting, inventory items in order to help a computer feel emotions. It’s a bizarre game filled with wonderful writing that will you have chuckling your way through the game.Ben never really left the 90s, in his mind the gaming industry peaked with the likes of Full Throttle and Day of the Tentacle. Whenever you’re playing as Ben, you’re playing his old-school point-and-click adventure where puzzles are solved through combining inventory items and talking things out with interesting characters. Dan takes his cues from the likes of Super Meat Boy and Celeste, all he cares about his platforming, and in fact, it’s all he’s capable of. His hands are too chunky to pull a lever, even if he wanted to stoop to Ben’s lows. Dan solves his problems by launching himself from platform to platform, hurtling through a metaphorical level made to make you feel things. Platformers are an art-form you see, they’re very meaningful if you think about it.The two styles of gameplay here work well together, but taken individually they aren’t quite as strong as the games that they’re inspired by. In the grand scheme of things, it doesn’t really matter though, because jumping back and forth between the two styles works well and it keeps both parts of the game feeling fresh throughout. Above all else though, it’s the writing that really makes this game stand out. The interactions between Ben and Dan are top notch, the commentary on the games industry throughout is thoroughly enjoyable, and the great Brit humour throughout will at the very least keep a smile on your face throughout the game. Who would have thought platforming would work with a 90s style adventure game? Well, Ben and Dan, I suppose. The two styles of gameplay are enjoyable, but it’s the writing that really shines here. This is well-worth picking up. If you found this review helpful, please check out my other reviews over at
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny while also meaningful; it's sweet while being incredibly crude; and most of all it's very clever while being very, VERY stupid.  Both the platforming and the point-and-click puzzling is good, albeit not top of class - the platforming is all a bit short and simple to get too excited about, while the puzzles are neat and fair but possibly a little too readily hinted at by the dialogue.  However, it's the rest of the game - the dialogue, the setting, the grin on Ben's face whenever he gets his way, and most of all the brilliant puzzles that don't quite fit the traditional point-and-click genre that make this a fantastic game.It's not for everyone - the crass humour will be a bit too off-putting for some, but as long as it doesn't ruin the game completely for you, there's enough other (great) stuff that isn't based around bodily functions that it's still worth playing.  For everyone else, this is wonderful and well worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did :/The self aware jokes seem dated, and don't seem to carry and weight to them. If there are any stakes in the game the feel like they truly don't matter because the game is constantly making fun of itself. It's not clever enough to be funny or honest enough to be charming.The platforming is ok, mediocre. The character frequently glitches into the ground for no reason which makes the game feel cheap and unfinished. I would give this a pass but the game has been out for 18 months and apparently it's still not fixed.The click and point adventuring somehow manages to bring some of the worst bits of classic click and point of having obtuse clues and solutions; and makes them worse by adding the layer of self awareness. Ben literally recognises how weird it is an item continues to be useful in the prologue. Sure game, you got me REAL GOOD by going "ha ha isn't unintuitive puzzle design funny"Occasionally, when the two modes are kept separate the game is about playable; but the desperate justification that you need to do both platforming and point and click adds a lair of tedium to the whole experience. You constantly have to switch character to pick Ben up with Dan and then drop him then swap again to interact. This extra complexity is also intentionally joked about by the characters during the game, like the game is mocking you telling you it is putting you through all these tedious extra steps intentionally. If you chose to play with a controller, be prepared for a whole extra layer of frustration whilst you struggle the the point and click interface.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? YES, it is. There are only few games that take well-known game designs and mix them to something new that is still clever & fun. The game calls itself a mix of point and click adventure and platformer. This is true, and this means you have to enjoy both point and click adventures AND platformers, or you won't like it. Believe me, if you want a fast platformer, you probably will not even be able to start the tutorial because there are puzzles to solve before you can start to platform. On the other hand, when you don't know how to hold a controller, how to dash or double jump... you will also not get very far.The gameplay consists mainly of an adventure, there are many, sometimes funny, conversations between the main characters, and classic point'n'click (pnc) puzzles to solve. You play two characters in the game and can switch between them anytime. One is the (pnc) adventurer, he cannot pull large blocks, cannot jump, can't even climb over a waist high wall, while the other character, an ex-adventurer who has evolved into a platformer, has no inventory and cannot pull levers. Your aim is to guide both of them through the levels.Coming home from an expedition in the jungle you arrive in London when the apocalypse has broken out. To stop the chaos, you hide deep underground and have to learn a damaged computer the 11 basic human emotions (like fear or joy). To do so, you have to complete levels. The adventurer by solving classic pnc puzzles, the platformer guy by platforming. And of course cooperating, like the adventurer by producing new enhancements for the platformer (like double jump shoes or a drink to run faster), the platformer by going into places where the adventurer can never go and there opening doors, pushing things or by simply carrying the adventurer guy around on his back.The platforming part is not too difficult, it is far easier than in games like Celeste or Cuphead. There are also frequent save points and you have unlimited lives. Still, you need some basic skills and you have to be able to cope with reversed gravity and running on the ceiling or wall. The adventure part takes more time, at least I spent more time here. Combine items with items or the environement, talk to other characters and generally do nasty things. The adventurer is not a nice guy and has no problems to kill someone or steal items if required. He also has no problems to use half a head of a (dead) security guard or to tear out the whole arm of a (dead) lady... I still like his sarcastic remarks.Both of the characters have already been the main characters of two classic pnc adventures. It is not required, but makes many things easier to understand when you have played those games before. Plays best with a controller, it took me a bit to get used to the pnc controls, but they work fine. Unique, witty and humourous mix of adventure and platformer. More adventure than platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny, and it's clever,but it's not  funny,and it's not  clever,and unfortunately, there's not much else to it.Writing a negative review often feels like a pointless exercise, but for a two-and-a-half-year-old niche indie title that has received mostly positive reviews, it feels almost  I can't imagine it'll make a difference in anybody's purchasing decision, and it feels a little late to be offering constructive criticism. But I've been thinking about this game ever since I finished it a month or two ago, and I'm trying to nail down exactly I think it's about The Swindle.The Swindle is another game by the same developer. It's a Roguelite Stealth Platformer. It's novel, it's entertaining, and it got a score of  The Swindle is  a 62% game. It's a 79% game with some jank that could be ironed out to bring it up to an 86%. This game, meanwhile, is not a 94%. It's a 73% riding mainly on a small dedicated fanbase. Something is wrong, and I'm racking my brains trying to figure out what has happened here, and I understand this is preposterous. I understand my subjective views are of no real merit. I fully entertain the possibility that I am just a weird guy who likes certain kinds of genres and that The Swindle is made for me and LotCG's humour just doesn't land with my specific psyche. But  I feel like I'm There's this part of LotCG that involves thematically frustrating platforming. As in, the theme is that the platforming is meant to be frustrating. In actuality, the platforming was not frustrating, which I assume is by design. The thing is, that brief section was the single most enjoyable experience I had in the game. I don't know how big SFG is, or how the labor is distributed, but I'm starting to suspect they may be good designers, but bad writers.I believe, genuinely, that videogames are a terrible narrative medium. I think a good narrative requires author control, and a good game requires player control, and that these two factors are at direct odds with each other. I realize this is not a popular opinion, especially amongst game designers with a narrative background. I wish LotCG had changed my mind on this. It didn't.I kind of want to go over the rest of SFG's catalogue just to see if my suspicions about their areas of competence hold true. I also hope that their next game leans heavily on gameplay and less on writing. So if you're from SFG, and you're reading this review as part of some masochistic self-debasement ritual, if you could maybe devote the next several years of your life to addressing the barely-substantiated criticisms of a random lunatic in your review section, you'd be doing me a real solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s talk about this game.Dan is a platformer.  He likes running around, stomping on enemies, leaping across chasms, and collecting shiny objects that go “ding”.Ben is an adventurer.  He likes combining items in his inventory, talking to people, and being a self-centered jerk worthy of the worst point-and-click protagonists.After a short prologue, these two best friends survive an apocalypse and wind up taking shelter in a bunker.  There, they meet a computer who has the power to put things right again – but first, they need to pass a series of simulations to give the computer the emotional range it needs to do its task.Gameplay involves switching back and forth between platforming and adventuring to progress.  Dan is used to help access hard-to-reach areas and help Ben get from place to place, and Ben is used to help craft upgrades for Dan, among other things.  A controller is recommended.  The platforming sections tend to be of moderate difficulty.  It’s hard to say how tricky the puzzles are, but they will definitely make you think!  The devs have provided an “official hint through” in the Steam guide section that may assist you if you get stuck.The game shines with its humor.  There are jokes aplenty, and the jokes are great, but the jokes are not the only funny thing about this game.  This game makes the game mechanics themselves funny.  This game is so clever it will make your head spin.  It will subvert your expectations as a gamer. It will also make fun of every game you have ever enjoyed.  In some places, it is not afraid to push the boundaries of humor and compassion in a very South Parkian way.This game comes bundled with a short visual novel called Devil’s Kiss, which is also quite entertaining.  I would recommend starting with the main game.I will mention that I did experience a bug at one point and the developer responded almost immediately with a fix for my issue.  Please support size five, this is a stand-up company that has done nothing but good things.If you decide to pick this game up, if you are on the fence about it, the other thing I will say is please keep playing.  Don’t put it down too soon, because you will miss out on all of the fun ways it goes on to twist your expectations.
