_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: In the wake of the new patchwork fixing a lot (basically all) of the platforming issues I had, I'm going to change my review to a recommendation. As per Monkey Island bylaws this is, in fact, worth a full price buy.Old review is below.______Credits told me to post a review so sure, I'll bite.The puzzles are clever, the humor writing is on point (about as good as the previous Ben There, Dan That! and Time Gentlemen Please were), and overall the adventure gamey bits are all very well put together with the exception of a few badly-signposted segments like . Really, it was all quite pleasant. Length is fantastic for an indie adventure game, clocking in at about 6-8 hours depending on how willing you are to put up with platforming. Everything not Dan and those godawful  laser blocks looks pretty solid too.Platforming is , most notably . They're amateurish in design and follow the Super Meat Boy philosophy of SPIKES = HARD and honestly never prove engaging even at their best due to clunky physics, weird walljump interactions, and the controls suddenly reorienting themselves every time you pass a gravity changer- it just ends up an exercise in frustration  It's honestly a bit funny, because the writing goes out of it's way to ♥♥♥♥ on indie platformers for being pretentious and derivative, but itself ends up the same sort of complete tripe it mocks whenever you have to play as Dan.Additionally the  really felt like the result of just... running out of ways to make Lost Vikings get from a to b puzzles interesting and giving up. I'd have preferred if it showed up later in the game, rather than about 1/3rd in.Which leads me to my next point: The story takes a few sudden turns for the pretentious here and there, particularly at the ending, and while  the finale really manages no such thing and just comes off as Suddenly Being Very Dire And Serious for about... five minutes? But it does this through a  schtick, which I understand might be meant as a pisstake but wholeheartedly engaging in a cliche in an "ironic" fashion is still engaging in it, just with less genuine sincerity.Lastly, the humor has a lot of references to trends that range from "already dated" to "will be dated within three to five years", which might be fine now but honestly that's going to be cringeworthy for anyone who's late to the party. Ending song is a prime example of this, actually.This is a surprisingly ambitious game that tries really hard to do some really cool things and... mostly sort of halfway bumbles through them and, in Pierrot-esque fashion, crosses the finish line ass backwards. This is a ... marred by the completely needless addition that is all the jank-ass platforming segments. If this had leaned less Jumper 3 and more Lost Vikings, it'd be stellar, but it doesn't and I can't in good faith recommend someone buy half a game for the price of a full one.Get it on sale. Like, it doesn't have to be a huge sale but, you know, just as a matter of principle. Like a 25% off sale sort of sale.

_childDocuments_.review: "Lair of the Clockwork God" is yet another of literally thousands of 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.  It's a Nintendo Switch game that somehow landed on Steam as well.  This one is different, though, because half the game play isn't platforming, it's Monkey Island ripoff point and click adventuring.  I appreciate the blend of genres is a quirky idea and the writing for the game is kinda fun, so the letdown here is totally on a sloppy, godawful technical implementation and an eye wateringly ridiculous price tag for pixelcrap... look, if developers want to get paid the same money as actual game developers who can do video game graphics properly, they have to actually do video game graphics properly.  Pixelcrap is not okay, it's 2024. So this is a comedy themed point and click adventure platforming hybrid.  You solve platforming problems with one character, then switch to the other one to do the point and click adventuring.  Like I said, this is "okay", and the game does work, but there's a lot of problems.One important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.There's an overwhelming amount of mediocre Visual Novel/E-book style cutscenes in this game.  So you'll spend a huge amount of time not playing the game, but clicking through endless lines of poorly written VN text cutscenes because the developers couldn't work out how to relate their narrative through the game mechanics, and decided instead it would be better to compete with reading a book for your time.  We're here to play games, not watch hours of garbage intersituals.On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game."Lair of the Clockwork God" didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the game, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for talking to a Dragon to get his name (a joke), trivial to get, but less than 40 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"Lair of the Clockwork God" has the almost unethical price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Metro Exodus", "Dishonored 2" or "Kingdom Come Deliverance".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I will give this a recommend, though I will say the humor in this game is a very specific niche of meta humor, that I don't think will be for everyone. Plus getting used to shifting between the two mechanics will take some time to get used to. These comments aside, there is a really well done game. One section in particular had the most fun puzzles and one of the best meta jokes I've ever experienced. I will say that the game will be more fun if you treat it less as a narrative-driven game, and more like a series of sketch comedies one after another with a throughline. So as said before, it is still a recommend as I had fun playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Platforms + Stick and click adventure that for me fell flat on both accounts.It turns out that I do not like mixing action/thinking games at all... Plus lots of the puzzles were absurd, following the comical trope of the game.Kudos to the devs providing accessibility options for the platformer bits, but after disliking the games writing (too many jokes in my opinion) and suffering a nasty bug involving a droid, I had to refund.Just watch the trailer and if you find it funny go ahead, why not, but if you do not stay out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of Time Gentlemen, Please and Ben There, Dan That. Weirdly, they are some of the first point and click games I played. I missed Lair of the Clockwork God releasing entirely. Years later I stumbled into it and...it's different. Why is it a weird platformer? Why is the art style different? This isn't what I wanted. I purchased it anyway and a few months later I finally played it.This is probably my favorite of the series.The idea here is Dan wants to be platformer now. Ben wants to be a point and click still. They have to work in tandem to complete levels and ultimately prevent the apocalypses (all of them). It's how these two gameplay styles work in tandem that makes it great. It isn't even two different styles. Both of them together make a whole. This design encompasses how they make puzzles, jokes, story, and exploration.If you've been sleeping on this game because it looks different, you have nothing to worry about. You are going to have a good time. A couple moments blew my mind with how clever they were.Oh, and Devil's Kiss is required. You can play it before the start. Just keep it installed just in case you want to experience the story again for any reason.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I recently beat Lair of the Clockwork God and thought it was a fantastic little indie game. You play as Dan and Ben, one of whom interacts with the world in a 90s adventure game style and the other who is purely a run-and-jump splatformer. You work your way through the world alternating between using the two’s complimentary skill sets in an attempt to stop…all the apocalypses!(?)I think just describing it undersells it though. A lot of the dialog is actually quite funny — though definitely M for Mature at times — and the game marries its mechanics with its themes very well. One thing I think it does well is that each of the characters personalities and ethos are shaped by their gameplay abilities, and as those intersect with the broader themes the game is presenting it results in a really interesting marriage between the storytelling and the mechanics.It also isn’t afraid to subvert your expectations at times. It’s opinionated, and I won’t say that I agree with 100% of what was said, but in the end I think it was a great experience and kudos to the devs for pulling the whole thing off. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good platformer/point and click game. You play as two characters , one is a platformer and the other solves point and click puzzles. The game makes fun and gaming in general and the whole thing works very well,There are a lot of accessibility options and by a lot I mean more than in most AAA games. This is a big + and a proof that the developers understand and want to make their game accessible to people who have various disabilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this quite a bit, though I do tend to agree with the "I don't like platform games" reviewers that if you don't like platform games you won't like it, and for me some of the point-and-click adventure aspects were frustrating, but classic (combine wrench with mop-head, a fine callback to classic point-and-clicks where when you get stuck you just try combining everything with everything until eventually something works *then* you see the clue for it).The other point-and-click frustration, other than the occasional nonsense combo, came towards the end when I had no idea where to go because I hadn't noticed one interactable thing that looked like background. Because the platform guy is so much faster, I pretty much didn't walk the other guy anywhere (once not doing that becomes an option) except when something *looked* interactable, and things only get an indication that they're interactable when that guy walks by them.But the game more than makes up for that in fun sections and variety. It's a bit unfortunate that the different genre sections are extremely linear, a little bit of actual gameplay in them would have been nice. And I would have quite enjoyed the puzzle that the characters don't want to solve - I was going to do it anyway but then I noticed there was a duplicate tile so it's not actually possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It was a great game until out of nowhere I opened the game and it wouldn't let me run and jump to the left, I've done all the troubleshooting I can but nothing helps. I'm sure you might enjoy the game because the amount of story I got to see is great and the style of game is super fun but unfortunately if this glitch is there still you won't be able to continue past an early stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Picture this: You've died and gone to heaven. Except instead of heaven, it's the office of platformer reassignment. Where you get the deadly spikes removed from you, your paperwork filled out to figure out where your last checkpoint was, and you talk to other platform game characters like a girl with a paintbrush who changes powers and colours depending on her emotional state.Now imagine instead of a platform game character, you're a stubborn adventure game protagonist trying to scam your way through customs so that you can respawn at the final checkpoint instead of doing any platforming. So you steal an item from one of those platform game characters, kill and shower in the goo of a sentient blob, and turn yourself blue by making the painter girl sad and touching her magic paintbrush.Lair of the Clockwork God is the kind of game that's constantly willing to come up with creative new skits and angles for their jokes. With a sense of constant humour that mixes parody, satire, and comedic sociopathy, I couldn't put the game down as I was basically always interested in seeing what the next location joke, or gameplay mechanic would be. There's nothing quite like it, in terms of style or substance.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Despite disliking platformers, I thought this game was solid. Good puzzles, humor, and a story that's interesting enough to hold you over through the end. It's nothing ground-breaking, but the adventure and puzzle-solving aspects made the taste of platformer a little more palatable.I played this on Steam Deck and encountered a few frustrations, but I'm not sure whether these were exclusive to the Deck or not. First, the game locked up in some animations and wouldn't continue — the game wasn't  as I could still access the menu, but the animation would never end which forced me to quit and restart. Second, there's a puzzle which requires keyboard input which isn't exactly difficult to access but it was frustrating having to type on the Deck's input system instead of being provided an in-game keyboard solution.Regardless, I found myself liking the game more than I expected. Even with a few technical problems and challenges where I found myself saying, "I hate platformers," Lair of the Clockwork God was enjoyable and worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game that blends platforming and adventure games into a smooth mixture. It's got the sense to avoid the irritations of point and click games, with Ben gaining ways to move around quickly to compensate for his plodding walk compared to Dan's dash. None of the puzzles are horribly obtuse, and trying stuff out/examining things will often provide a subtle hint to push you in the right direction.Worth your time if you enjoy adventure games, but also want a little platformer gameplay to help break up those puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It's a platformer/point n click hybrid that's self-aware and takes cracks at game design culture, the state of gaming today and a little bit of everything else in the process. Lots of hilarity, clever moments and ridiculous shenanigans. Getting a flow with the controls can take a little getting used to (looking at you point n click). Highly recommend to anyone who likes any combination of the words I just wrote.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is very good! Lovingly made, funny, clever, tells a fun story, explores the human condition, and is really quite pretty.It's both point-and-click adventure and platformer, which works remarkably well — and has an accessibility slider to make the platforming easier for those not keen on double-jumping at no penalty.  There's also an excellent official hint guide for nudging you in helpful directions for if you get stuck.Have now played through the whole thing, and thought it brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Im.... not really sure what to think of this game. I certainly didnt deliver on what I was expecting, but thats not a bad thing.This game just... loves being meta, in a lot of ways, and never taking itself too seriously. This leads to some fun jokes and some very frustrating puzzles, since the game doesnt like... fully guide you on what you need to do as a meta move, if that makes senseI don't know. I liked this game well enough, the story and dialogue are entertaining, and its not something you'll see somewhere else thats for sure, so I do reccommend it. But the platforming doesnt feel good, and for the puzzles I definetly reccommend playing with a guide open in another window for the inevitable post-moon logic. So yeah, expect an interesting experience, if not a wholly fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big gamer but I found this fun and interesting. The puzzles were mostly solvable on my own (I used the walkthrough a few times) and, while it could be frustrating, the platform aspects were all achievable even if some took me a lot of tries. It's funny and endearing. I know enough about games to understand most of the references it makes. I haven't quite finished it yet but I'm excited to get to the end even while enjoying it enough to hope it won't end too soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't feel the need to join the chorus of praise for a game when it is already at Overwhelmingly Positive, but for Lair of the Clockwork God, I'll make an exception. I had a great time with this game, the combination of platforming and old school adventure games was a lot of fun, and to top it all off, this game has a great sense of humor as well, which led to me really enjoying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I personally think that one's attitude towards this game depends mainly on three factors: 1) Do you like point & click? 2) Do you like platforming? 3) Do you like the Deadpool movies (mainly for their humor)? If the answer to all three questions is "yes!", this might be your new personal favorite. Extra points of you have played the previous games and/or are an aspiring (indie) game developer. I wanted to try the game because it was praised over the top on certain internet platforms. While I love platformers, I am no fan of point & click. Because people claimed that adding platforming to point & click was kind of the next evolution of the genre, I was personally hoping that one would make the other one more appealing to me. It did not. I encountered a few bugs in the first 30 minutes while platforming (e.g. I fell through the ground and died), found the 4th wall breaking tiring, because it was too frequent (also I am no fan of 'funny' takes on cancer), and I found the art style not detailed enough to fall in love with the world. So that's why I can't recommend the game. If you, however, are a fan of the genres and the humor, why not give it a try when it is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard about Lair Of The Clockwork God and saw some trailers I thought it seemed genius. The concept reminds me of games like the old Gobliiins games, but perhaps more Lost Vikings where you have multiple characters with different abilities, and their different abilities are all needed in cooperation to solve puzzles and to finish levels. However, in this instance Dan is a playable point-and-click-character while Ben is is a platformer, so you’re mixing two completely different genres, which is a very original idea. So its kind of a mix between the ye olde classic point and click adventure game (ala LucasArts in the 90s), and a modern indie platformer, perhaps like Super Meat Boy. It's a pretty novel idea, and it is executed very well too! For the most part. It's not the developers first game as they made a point and click game. I have known about Ben There Dan That (2007) and Time Gentlemen, Please (2009), which are both cult indie point and click adventure games. Both of those are with Dan and Ben as the main characters, based on the two main developers, of course, just like this one. Having played through the whole game I can say I definitely liked it. It may not be perfect, or a masterpiece, but it's still a very good game.  I think the story was interesting, and the puzzles are fairly balanced and often inventive, graphics and music nice. There’s also a surprising amount of variety and the game has a lot of wacky surprises along the way. If there are any downsides? Err, I admit I was stuck for a while at the future part, and those puzzles were definitely a bit difficult cryptic and I got a bit tired of the game around here as I got a bit stuck. So I stopped playing for a while, but came back some weeks later and things went very smoothly after that part. The thing is there’s this «online store» announced on the menu where you can «buy hints» (with both in-game and real money), which I thought was strange, and I didn't realize it was a joke. I didn’t think I needed hints so I avoided it until I understood it was actually a necessary part of the game and just part of the puzzle. There’s actually a LOT of meta puzzles like this in this game, and not all are easy to figure out, and some are quite out there.. although I seemed to get through them all in the end. Also, some of the humor may be a bit infantile and sarcastic sometimes, which is something the older games with Dan and Ben also sometimes were criticized for. For the most part I thought it was funny and clever, and if that is your thing then its perhaps even a plus, yet sometimes perhaps it could get a little bit much, at least for me. For example the "wanking booth" and that you need to piss on a grave to solve a puzzle. Perhaps I'm just getting too old to find stuff like that very funny. Its a mixed bag, but mostly good. The game also does seem a bit undecided and confused as a game if it wants to be taken seriously or not with its story, or just goofy and sarcastic, so the balance is a bit uneven. There’s certainly elements it plays into which seems to be about something more profound, like an AI wanting to learn human emotions to save humanity from an apocalypse, and at one point figuring out humans aren’t really worth saving, some clever commentary otherwise too, and a lot of the backgrounds and music could be quite pretty atmospheric at times, but it seems the game never quite dares to take it self too seriously. At one point it even seems to take a whack at artsy pompous indie games. Fine, I guess. I also had mixed feelings about the ending but it was okay. Also, some of the platform stages are a bit tough too, but I actually enjoyed those personally — however, if you’re only a point and click adventure player, and you’re not into platform games at all be mildly warned the platform stages aren’t just for show. Some of them can be quite challenging, although never impossible.  The controls I also thought was passable, and I got used to them, but they still always were a little but bit clumsy and quirky. I would actually have loved it more if Dan had the old SCUMM interface like on the old LucasArts games, so that was a wasted opportunity, but alright. It works though!Anyway, all in all it was fun playing through, and there’s a lot to like in here, so I definitely recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: OMG - this game is so good.  It's actually blown me away, I've played so many point and click games and games in general, I didnt think I could come across one that was not only fresh in its gameplay, but that had such a clever meta commentary humour that wasnt cringy like most seem to be, but was so funny I actually laughed out loud more than once, rather than do that thing where I expel air through my nose which seems to qualify as laughter these days.  Even the mini game was hilarious 'bye p*edo' the devs should be really proud of themselves.  i only found this game by searching for obscure indie games, what a gem!!   AND I got it on sale for £3.87.  It's worth it's full price.  For those looking for an actual review - it's  a mix of platformer and point and click.  You control two characters who are both pinacles of each respective genre.  I am not afraid to admit I had to look up a walkthrough to proceed a few times, just because I am not used to the gameplay mechanics - THEY ARE SO CLEVER!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the idea was cool but somehow the gameplay didn't quite convince me. It's neither a tight platformer nor a very enjoyable point-and-click game. I commend the game's accessibility options, but the issues with glitching into the floor and some slow sections that punish you with tedium for dying ultimately turned me off.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Among the most achingly clever games ever made.The two previous Dan & Ben adventures are as smart and funny as any adventure game I've ever played. They also stuck pretty closely to genre conventions. Lair of the Clockwork God, meanwhile, is equal parts point-'n'-click and puzzle platformer, and it absolutely works. It shouldn't work. There aren't many people on this Earth who could make it work. But Ben and Dan two different genres, put 'em in one game where they support each other and neither overpowers the other, and it works.Sorry, I can't get over it. This bizarre experiment WORKS.And then they use that to comment on both genres! And games as a whole! And feeling out of place in a changing world! It's not just a weird goof; it's purposeful and meaningful! And angry at games that purport to be meaningful! And it's so very, very funny.I'd love it if everyone in the world bought and played it, but it's definitely not going to be for everyone. You need to have a certain knowledge of video games and pop culture to fully get it. You need to be comfortable with jokes about various bodily fluids. But the biggest potential issue, I suspect, is that the puzzle design is firmly rooted in '90s adventure sensibilities. I reached the end without ever having to check for hints online, so it's definitely fair and possible, but it's not easy. Like I said: achingly clever. Maddeningly clever. Occasionally even clever at the expense of fun, but you can do it if you're up to the task of thinking through everything you've seen. It's an uncompromising cleverness that's always rewarding.Advancing both the adventure and the puzzle platformer genres, Lair of the Clockwork God is a masterpiece that's both familiar and unlike anything I've ever played. An essential purchase that I'm confident I'll reinstall every few years, just as soon as I forget the puzzle solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot! It's a very specific kind of humor, making fun of modern platformers, old adventure games and everything in between and going deeply meta at some points. But I had a blast all the way through and would reccomend it to anyone who grew up on LucasArts and the like.Just... bring a gamepad because those platforming passages are not played well with a keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Makes fun of some aspects of the game industry and the world in general, but does so without forgetting that it still needs to be an actual game. The levels were fun and the puzzles challenging but almost always fair and required out of the box thinking. Overall, i got this game on sale and i can say it was 100% worth it. I think it's worth picking up at full price too. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most complicated and unique puzzle games that I have played in a very long time, up there with the likes of Portal for sure. Easily one of the best games that I have played to date. It has witty humor, unique game play, and enough character to keep you playing for hours. Get it, because unlike this game, that's a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a bizarre concept, but, it works.  Two best mates, one, Ben, is a traditional point and click adventure protagnist, while the other, Dan, is a platformer protagonist, so , the game is a mix of the two genres, with Dan often literally carrying Ben over to  objects that need examining/using, as Platformers don't  handle nerdy, thinking-related problems like that.The area where it really shines is the dialog. I laughed on numerous occasions, the interactions between the two are glorious, and well worth the cost of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: The funniest, most well-written game I've played in ages! (admittedly, as an ageing adventure game lover I'm right in the sweet spot for a lot of the humour) Some of the puzzles were astonishingly clever, too. And it has lots of rude words in it! What more could you ask for? Actually, the platforming was rock hard in places, which detracted from the overall experience a bit, but not enough to ruin things for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It's been at least ten years since I first played the original Ben & Dan games (Ben There, Dan That! and Time Gentlemen, Please!) I'm actually fairly certain the two of them, bundled together, were the very first games I ever purchased on Steam. If you haven't played those games, you absolutely should--they're hilarious, they're charming, they're well-designed, and they're damn near the only adventure games in all of history that have used LucasArts references in a way that actually worked. Point is, I love Ben and Dan, but I'd given up on seeing any more of them after the creators (I forget their names) appeared to rule out any future sequels in 2013 or so.You can imagine how excited I was for this game, then, and how apprehensive I was at the same time. The developers had made it pretty clear that, where they were concerned, they'd said all they felt prepared to say about the adventure genre in the first two games, and anything further would just be repeating themselves; I respected the hell out of that at the time, and on thinking about it I had to agree with them. It's a lesson that a whole crop of developers still refuse to internalize, but there comes a time when you have to stop just saying "Hey, remember Monkey Island?" in perpetuity; these guys had seemingly reached that point, and I was excited to see where they went next.Fast forward to a full decade after I played the original games, and Size Five have revisited those characters in a smart, hilarious game that foregrounds the very conflict that made them walk away in the first place. This is a game about looking forward and backward at the same time--about the constant push-and-pull between the desire for growth and the longing for comfortable nostalgia--about convincing your best mate to put on a glove covered in strangers' spunk in order to reach a new gameplay area. Half platformer, half old school graphic adventure, this game gives us a Ben and Dan who've grown older, but not up; more knowledgeable, but no wiser; more in tune with themselves but less in step with the world around them. All that is secondary, though. Lair of the Clockwork God is *fun*, it's *funny*, and it doesn't waste an inch of space or a second of game time where a joke might fit or you could have something to do. It's exactly what a Ben and Dan game would have to be a decade on--you don't have to have played the earlier games, but you'll find there's more to appreciate if you have. (And Jesus, they cost what, like 50 cents now? Come on. What else are you going to do with that much, invest it?) However you approach it, this is a hilarious game with tremendous replay value--there's too many great jokes to remember them all the first, second, or third time through--and you're only hurting yourself by not buying and playing it. EDIT: I remembered the developers' names! It was Ben Ward and Ben Ward's friend, Martin.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely funny, full of in jokes for those familiar with the main genres of the game (point and click and puzzle platformers). Obvious comedy is subjective, but its rare for me to actually laugh at a game that is trying to be funny, this is an exception.Beyond the humour, its got some really clever puzzles and is just generally a fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the older Dan and Ben games, but this one is the best yet. The writing is top-notch and the story is maybe a teensy bit more coherent this time. The game wears Dan and Ben's love of adventure games on its sleeve and now there is *gasp* platforming added. But don't let that scare you off - it is a nice addition and it doesn't affect the main reason I enjoy these games - the humor.Despite the added gameplay, the humor is top-notch: the witty barbs and breakdown of gaming tropes are still there and better than ever. The remorseless Ben adventure-games his way through the plot while Dan runs and jumps and carries on all on his own. The plot is great - the prologue has them curing cancer and you will forget all about that by the last chapter of the story. I don't want to get into any spoilers but the framework for the game is excellent and allows you to see all kinds of cool set pieces and have the guys do all kinds of crazy stuff - almost consequence free!A must for old school adventure gamers who can tolerate the lowbrow platforming elements. There are a few difficult and twitchy platforming sections towards the end, but persevere for an action-adventure packed conclusion that definitely doesn't have you fighting a dinosaur skeleton with a pulse rifle.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I thought it was slow, long winded and tiresome, but the more I played it, the more it grew on me.  Shame the later sections are much shorter, as just as I was beginning to enjoy it, it was over.  There’s lots of observational humour, but overall, it’s not that funny - making fun of everything is ok for a while, but some original jokes would help.  It’s self-indulgent, quirky and somewhat entertaining, but most of the dialogue fell flat for me, and the plot never really grabbed me.The platforming sections are fun and frustrating whereas the point and click sections are simple with traditional adventure game logic.  Having both game play styles intertwined is a great idea and works really well at times, but unfortunately, both are a bit clunky in their execution.  I did get used to over time, but the minor bugs and glitches throughout were disappointing.It does have a good soundtrack and their graphical style is good, but it never wowed me.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Very creative point&click adventure packed with tons of humor (albeit, a bit gamery. If you are not following gaming culture that closely, you might not get it). Platforming was decent. You can see that the puzzles are were the most creative experiments took place during development. Most of the time, they work. Sometimes however, the solution is a bit absurd.It took me around 10 hours to beat, so I think you get your money's worth here.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very meta experience that is definitely a bit cumbersome and possibly annoying initially but the humor and gameplay builds on itself as you go. It would say it is FAR FROM a 10/10 experience but ultimately very clever and worth the time. Your probably gonna get stuck once every hour or so just (something I expect from point and clicks) so do yourself a favor and just peak at a guide if you're getting frustrated.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: The pre-title cards are a meta joke on the state of gaming, and funny rude words. And those themes pretty much continue throughout the rest of the game.Reminds me of Disco Elysium in that they are both very, very good games that surprised and delighted me with alarming regularity. Adventure games are dead, long live adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A very entertaining combination of platforming and adventure-gaming. The controls for the platforming are a little finnicky sometimes, but checkpoints are frequent and spaced out reasonably to provide a challenge but not crush your will to live. The puzzles are all pretty logical, and a few of the solutions had me muttering "oh, you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" to myself when I figured out what it was that they were expecting me to do. Devil's Kiss is great, too-- all in all, well worth a purchase and playthrough!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: So, just finished Lair Of The Clockwork God.It is just so, so f'ing good.Honestly it took me about three playthroughs of the prologue to get into, but when I did it was Worth It.Most huge congratulations to the whole team.The music / audio in general was superb, really impressed with Tobey Evans's work.It’s also the best example of “it’s not a bug it’s a feature” I’ve seen in a long while. Casual reminder to never send “um are you sure” tweets to the devs - they know MUCH more about their game then the player, which is as obvious as it bears repeating.In an interview with Stealth Docs Dan Marshall (dev) essentially said “when I’m done with one genre of game I move onto the next” and LOTCG is such a melting pot of All Games Past Present And Future (a la Tim Rogers talking about Undertale)So yeah, Lair Of The Clockwork God - took a while for me to click with but it’ll stick with me forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I forget the list, but some "Best of 2020 in Adventure Gaming" listed this title as a must play, and I was intrigued. I was curious about how they would blend adventure gaming with platforming, but I was pleasantly surprised. This was really a lot of fun and I couldn't put it down. Would Highly Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun. Funny writing combined with some inventive puzzles, including one particularly ballsy one involving what you'd think was something very unintentionally in the game (though honestly, considering there's no dialog to acknowledge it early on, I feel like the game would be better off only introducing it early. As it was, it annoyed me for way too much of the game before it is actually used). Occasionally ran into a puzzle that stumped me, and some of the default controls (i.e. for swapping between interaction hotspots, or fast-forwarding dialogue lines) weren't the most inutitive. The platforming could also get a bit glitchy, particularly once you've got certain upgrades that let you slide down walls (even if you really don't want to). There's also at least a couple of platforming sections that felt overly hard to me. But overall the experience was extremely positive and full of laughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A hilarious and very clever mix of platforming and adventure. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it.I preferred the puzzle-solving parts over the platforming ones as the controls are not very tight, but apart for short sections the platforming is part of the puzzle solving and often very well integrated.Some jank here and there, and some performance dips in some sections (had to lower my resolution to get through one specific section that became too unresponsive because of the low frame rate). But not enough to distract from the experience.Would definitely recommend if you like puzzle solving, a bit of actions that's not too challenging, and most of all a hilarious story.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Very funny. Pretty janky. The wall grab in particular can make for some frustrating platform sections. You'll grab walls you're near, even if you're not pressing the direction, which can make falling down a shaft a pain. Jumping off a wall can sometimes double-jump instead. But comedy games pretty much get a pass on that stuff. And excluding the wall grab, the rest of the platforming flowed well. It's no Meatboy or Mario, but it really isn't aspiring to be either.The Adventure portion of the gameplay was mostly what you might remember from olden times. Sometimes the moon logic makes perfect sense in your head, sometimes it takes a while.In my opinion, while some reviewers have written that they thing the two genres don't mash well together, I disagree. You might look to games like Metriod Prime as a loose example-- you can absolutely blend an action-platformer with an investigative game. It really gets my own ideas flowing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the integration of the comedy and the game mechanics.  You don't just solve puzzles while the game tells you jokes; you solve puzzles by completing a joke the game has set up.  While this means that the jokes are rarely surprising -- you have to work out the punchline yourself, after all -- they bring the player into the humor performance, a rare feat for any comedy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Never heard of Ben and Dan before but I'd seen the good reviews about this so I gave it a try. It's a definite recommendation. The mixture of platforming and adventure really shouldn't work but it does and they've come up with a unique experience that puts a fresh spin on both. Like many other reviewers here I'm not a big platforming fan or adventure fan but I still enjoyed it and the difficulty level was fine. If I can get through the platforming sections then I reckon 90% of other gamers can. The game allows for KB+M but I reckon a controller (which I hate) is probably essential.The Good-----------* Great story. Completely off-the-wall, unpredictable, fun and tongue-in-cheek throughout.* Loved the humour (See "The Bad")* Difficulty level was just fine; no problem for people that aren't big on platforming but challenging enough.* The solutions for the adventuring section weren't too obscure. Anyone familiar with 80's / 90's adventure games will have no problems. When stuck you can generally figure it out by combining (I mean crafting) all the limited number of items with each other until a solution presents itself.* Each major level has it's own feel, keeping things fresh.* Cutesy graphics appropriate for the retro feel they're going for.* Great soundtrack; I particularly enjoyed the misanthropic song used for the end credits.* I figured out the solution for the 'Suffering' level without cheating, and it was brilliant. Lends new meaning to "thinking laterally"* Good game length. Should take you anywhere from 9-12 hours so you get your money's worth but it doesn't overstay its welcome* I just like the idea of "all the apocalypses happening at once". Why has nobody done this before?The Bad---------* Buggy. Really, really buggy. I lost count of how many times I had to restart the game. More than the last 10 games I've played put together, easily. (And I'm not talking about the deliberate glitches that are coded into the game)* The platforming is not particularly precise. Didn't really bother me because save-points are generous but those trying to go for 'not dying' achievements are likely to get frustrated.* Very British humour and ostentatiously meta; I enjoyed it but it might not be for everyone. It has ♥♥♥♥ jokes too though.* The solution in the 'Fear' section was far more obscure than anything else in the game, and was frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Delightfully whimsical game.Ben and Dan chatter on as if the fourth wall never existed but at the same time the whole thing is packed with action and... well... pondering.The puzzles are hard enough to get you thinking, and the platforming element just gives it just the extra touch. Also, it's hilarious :-)Despite the low-fi nature of the graphics, this game keeps coming up with fresh artwork throughout a well thought out story line and the the musical score just rocks.If you enjoyed that silly blue hedgehog as a kid but have moved on to a more cerebral class of games (or have lost the reflexes) you'll love this.Awesome indie effort. Looking forward to the next title
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is a comedy game that spares no expense or detour to land a joke. The wild, winding paths that it goes down to even set up *minor* blink-and-you'll-miss-them jokes *hours* down the line comes across as incredibly confident. It breaks the rules of the types of jokes you're supposed to tell in video games -- not in an edgy, pushing-the-boundaries-of-political-correctness kind of way (it airs of the side of decency in matters of real-world concerns) -- rather, it is unafraid to plant setups that may frustrate the player or give highly-targeted aspects of the game an unpolished feeling only to reveal that these are, themselves, gags paid off *hours* down the road. Given the high percentage of players that drop-off mid-game in any experience in this medium, I find it incredibly ballsy that they're willing to sacrifice initial impressions for pay-offs that many players likely won't experience (again, only in targeted and specific aspects; as a whole, the game feels very polished and mechanically sound).It's a  game that is less concerned with keeping a high laughs-per-minute count than intricately weaving its wild and off-beat humor through the entire timeline of its playtime, with even minor jokes receiving hours-long set-ups and hours-later callbacks. It's a feat of comedic planning and rule-bending that feels like it leaves no avenue unexplored. Again, the apparent high level of effort put into even low-impact jokes is fascinating with its "show your work" style of writing and planning.As a gameplay experience, you can feel the stretch-marks of its ambition. Platforming is a bit ropey and the occasional puzzle can be a bit of a moon-logic stumper, but it was never enough to dissuade me from the game. It is impressive how well it overcomes the challenging tasks that it set for itself. As a genre mashup, it seems like it would be unsuited for any control method -- platformers want to be played with controller, and point & click adventures want to be played with a mouse -- but it elegantly bridges that gap by using clever methods to make point & click adventuring comfortable and intuitive to play with a controller. It's a very impressive game in all regards.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful and hilarious game. It loves and mocks point-and-clicks and platformers both, it combines the two genres in a really weirdly brilliant fusion in gameplay, the script is a constant stream of wit and charm, and it somehow is also a heartfelt exploration of ageing from rebellious youth into the worst of all fates, *being a grown-up*. Absolutely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game, merging the indie darling platformers mechanics (and observing their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story points and heavy handed writing), with the old school point and click games (with similar observations about kleptomania and causing misery to NPCs).The two merge together rather well and neither felt they outstayed their welcome, or were undercooked in their implementation.The highlight as usual is the writing and humour in the game, and it had me laughing at quite a few jokes. Ben and Dan games do not disappoint in this regard, and if you've played the previous (Time Gentlemen, Please! or Ben There, Done That) then you know what you're expecting there. The outro song in particular was a good laugh.Overall a fun game and well worth the price for a fun point and click, there are interesting achievements and some collectibles that I have missed which would extend the game time, and I may revisit to attempt, but on the whole it was thoroughly entertaining for the main game alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like clever games? Do you like dumb games? If you answered yes to either or especially if you answered yes to both then you owe it to yourself to play this. The only downside to this game is the slightly weaker platforming segments, but the writing, puzzles and everything else makes up for that and a whole lot more.Game writers or any writers interested in games should definitely give this one a go ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with a great concept – and very, very funny to boot. So glad I was recommended this – the puzzles could be a little harder perhaps – but I'm only about a quarter in, so who knows what's coming. Best adventure game I've played since Day of the Tentacle (and even funnier), and yes, the platform part is fun too. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: To anyone who enjoys one or more of the following:- Point'n'clicks- Platformers- Puzzles- Adventures- Games- Laughing- Having fun (even remotely)- BreathingI simply cannot recommend this game enough.Lair of the Clockwork God is a surprisingly well crafted adventure. Full of narrative ideas. Packed with unexpected situations. Just long and “head-scratcher-y” enough to feel fresh and fun all the way till the end. And it baffles me that I haven’t heard of this gem before.I’m far from being a fan of point’n’click games but I loved it through and through. Okay *maybe* not the unskippable tutorial… but you’ll have to trust me on this…It’s worth it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this title; with this kind of concept it could have easily been a jack of all trades, master of none kind of situation but thankfully it nails both the point and click and platforming game-play. The puzzle design was excellent and the platforming just the right level of difficulty (although this can be tweaked to your liking) and the two styles are blended together seamlessly. There's also lots of great banter and 4th wall jokes, beautiful pixel art visuals, an excellent soundtrack, tons of accessibility options and a passionate dev team so this game really ticks all the boxes. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I've been really enjoying the game so far and I've only played short of 4 hours. I dig the pacing, humor and the way the devs were able to mix the genres. This is a must play if you're an old schooler like me that enjoyed Days Of The Tentacle, Sam n Max, Full Throttle, Monkey Island etc. and also want to try out something a little different with some platforming thrown on top. Thumbs up, give it a go. Besides, I had some doubts about how to pull off certain things using a controller and got immediate replies from the devs, both in the Steam forums and by mail, so kudos to them for that!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal game: witty, creative and meta as hell. The hilarious interaction between the characters (bantz!) is top notch, and I found myself starting conversations on the off chance that a new dialogue option had appeared. Puzzles are challenging, but not frustratingly so, and it was nice to see the effort that had gone into making unique responses for when you inevitably try using every item in your inventory on everything in the environment (memories of Eric Idle endlessly saying 'That doesn't work' in Discworld still haunt my dreams).A beautifully crafted labour of love made for anyone who lived through the golden point n' click and 2d platformer years.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: After recent experimentation with obscure chinese medicine alleviated a state of lifelong anhedonia, unlocking a series of complex emotions never before experienced, I thought that my life resembled a character in a really bad Star Trek episode. Thanks to LAIR OF THE CLOCKWORK GOD I have now come to understand that my life resembles a character in a really funny video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Feverishly inventive & relentlessly funny, Lair of the Clockwork God is an absolute gem.Showing appropriate reverence towards games & the gaming industry, while simultaneously kicking them in the metaphorical balls, the true power of LotCG is that the butt of the joke is almost always the protagonists themselves. It'll consistently surprise you throughout, in ways that'll either have you standing up & applauding, or shouting . The platforming isn't  as slick as the indie darlings little Dan with the Massive Hands seeks to emulate, but Ben's point & click chattering & combining (sorry, "crafting") is perfectly pitched. And somehow it all just...works. It shouldn't, but it really, really does.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant game that the trailers and descriptions can't do justice to.  Yes, the conceit of the game being half platformer, half old school adventure is where the game's initial mechanics lie, but this game get better cleverer and funnier as it goes along, in ways that are basically impossible to talk about without spoilers. This is also a game you will get more out of the more you are familiar with games in general, and more specifically indie games from the last decade or so. There is some jank in the game (I had to reload twice where weird bugs meant progress was impossible) but the writing in the game more than makes up for it. Highly recommended, and if you have already played and enjoyed it, you should check out "There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension" another puzzle / adventure games which shared both similar themes, and a not dissimilar sense of humour.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A real fun and funny game that actually made me giggle out loud a few times. The adventure game half is probably one of the better adventure games I played in recent years. The puzzles were just the right amount of hard for me, not 90s obtuse but not so simple that the solution was obvious. The platforming part is a little more straightforward but the game occasionally pulls out a few tricks to make it more interesting. The dialog between Dan and Ben is really what makes the game work, while not every joke lands it kept me amused all the through the story.Overall a great experience and not too long so you can complete it in a weekend or two (a very important feature for an old gamer with a job like me!)
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. The metacommentary (especially the "these damn kids with their Celestes, don't they know games aren't supposed to be art" jokes) got old before the tutorial was done, but the writing is otherwise good and it's an excellently designed and fun game; classic ben and dan content but now with keyboard support
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. A totally hilarious, loving burn on pretty much the entire indie games industry. Ben, the adventure game protagonist, is so into  collecting items and navigating dialogue trees that he won't hear of it when Dan decides he's going to be an indie platformer. As a result of this argument, Dan won't touch a single inventory item and Ben won't hop over even a small crack in the sidewalk as it feels too much like platforming. While in this impasse, they stumble across ALL THE APOCALYPSES HAPPENING IT ONCE! And they have to use their combined genre-powers to save the world. Switching back-and-forth between the two types of gameplay is fun enough to excuse that the puzzles can be a little frustrating and the platforming can be a little basic. But the real star here is the incredible comedy writing. I was literally laughing out loud playing this game and hell, you don't find that in games very often...
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I love the dynamic between the two characters, the writing is really funny and pokes fun at all sorts, including the gaming community and developers, some really clever stuff,The platforming sections are fun, the puzzle solving is great, even though I'm trash at puzzle solving, there's a real sense of achievement when you finally get the solution,Really enjoying this game and would recommend it to anyone, if you're thinking of buying it, pull the trigger!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly quite a fun game. The controls felt a bit clunky at first, but were alright once I got used to them. The puzzles were adequately challenging, and for the most part intuitive. Some of them I'd even consider quite clever. There's still a certain puzzle that I have yet to complete, and I'm definitely planning on taking a stab at it when I have the time.The humor in the game was kind of hit or miss for me, as humor tends to be, but I'd consider it a net positive, and it really does drive the narrative. I stumbled across a few bugs here and there, and actually managed to softlock the game a couple of times during my playthrough, but that wasn't too much of a problem. A quick reload would fix the issue every time, with barely any loss of progression, and I would move on.The music and artwork are definitely up there as far as indie games go, and coupled with how much personality the developers have put into the game, make the overall game feel like a labor of love. I suspect the game might not be for everyone, but if the game looks interesting to you, I strongly recommend giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Excellent Humeur. Meta complex multiplex.Wicked Object puzzles. Things well worth examining.Funny AF song if you win.Too much platformer.It rides the line between fun bouncy castle and throw your controller through the screen. Then again, that's part of the joke on you.Worth playin, at least once.Keep crankin out the goods, B&D!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Don't pass up on this game. It's a 10-15 hour adventure with some really great moments. 10/10LotCG is a fantastic game. Contained within this point and click/platforming adventure you'll find brilliant puzzles with some genius implementation/solutions, dry, self referencing humour and platforming that will sometimes be a joy and sometimes cause you anger. If you want some quick spoiler free tips to help you get along...- Play the visual novel first.- Practically everything is in the game for a reason. If you think something seems wrong, it's most likely intentional.- Pay attention to what the characters say. The solution to the puzzle you're struggling with is probably revealed in a characters dialogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockwork God is one of those rare games that does comedy right, with great writing and a well-paced story that doesn't drag or over-stay its welcome. Most of the humor plays on tropes of the game's dual genres: Point-and-Click Adventures and Platformers, along with some commentary on recent trends in indie games. If you like retro games and indies, they made this for you. (If you don't, wow, how'd you even find this game?)The blend of Point-and-Click and Platformer works well here; the game features plenty of opportunities to combine items in bizarre ways to solve contextual puzzles, without the infuriating pixel-hunting that too often plagued classic games of the genre. The platforming, mechanically, doesn't compare to the "indie darling" games that it lampoons, but its inclusion adds flavor to the adventuring, and is mined consistently and thoroughly for jokes.Without spoiling any parts of the experience, there are at least a couple of surprises that made me realize I had underestimated a game that I already thought was fairly clever from the start. This one is worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Greeto! (you'll get that later playing the game)Lair of the Clockwork God is a brilliant mashup of Lucasarts-style adventures and 2d platformers. The two mix seamlessly and generate some of the most unique puzzles you have seen in the genre, even if, like me, you have played loads of point-and-click games. Puzzles are never frustrating, there's plenty of witty banter as you would expect from their first games and the pacing is great.If I have to find an issue, platforming sections were a bit too prevalent sometimes (maybe it's me taking longer to go through those). Even if you're a veteran, I can guarantee you'll solve at least a few puzzles in ways you've never experienced before.Definitely worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: If a game were to ask if its install size looked big, Lair of the Clockwork God would tell them that, yes, yes it did, but that that’s okay and a game should never be embarrassed about how big or small it is. I laughed, I cried, I sang. Jumpy puzzly shooty silliness in a game that anyone who has a love for games would want to have made. Play it, it might just be the Citizen Kane of inappropriate Citizen Kane comparisons needlessly referenced in game reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool combination of adventure games and platformers, which is a send-up of the current gaming industry, but also a great game in its own right. The platforming was fun and reasonably challenging, although the controls could have been more precise. What really shines is the puzzle design and humour. There were moments where I genuinely laughed out loud when I found the solution to a puzzle, and there aren't many games where I could say that. Overall, highly recommended if you like puzzle games and sarcastic humour.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first couple Ben and Dan games. They were a bit juvenile, but juvenile point and clicks can be a lot of fun. I only just discovered that this game was from that series, and I tore through it all in a couple weeks. This is definitely a more mature creation than its predecessors. Don't worry, there's still tons of juvenile humor, but there's a purpose to it all. The game has something to SAY underneath the potty humor and meta-commentary. It's been a while since I played an adventure game that I have cherished the way that I think I'll cherish this one. I'm even writing a review, and I don't really WRITE reviews. Don't worry about the platforming, fellow point-and-click fans. This is YOUR platformer. There's a difficulty slider for the platforming, in case it drives you crazy (And it ALMOST did for me once or twice, but it was kinda supposed to in those moments) but I ultimately didn't need it. In it all beats the heart of an adventure game. One of the good ones. Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: The Ben&Dan series is one of the funniest adventure games out there, and the third episode does not disappoint. Unlike the point&click predecessors, it is weird mix of platforming and adventure games, with a few other genres thrown in as mini-games; and while the platforming itself is not particularly good, the hilarious jokes and media criticism it is a setup for more than makes up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Beside the great mix of platform/point&click which works perfectly. I really enjoyed the storyline, the character evolution through out the game, the acid humor and the sharp dialogues.  With a funny criticism to current society and a great explanation of how we humans live our lives, without showing any regrets for the consequences of our actions.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A delightfully charming adventure featuring a pair of buffoons. Ben wants to be in adventure games and Dan wants to be in platformers. Now they manage to be in both at the same time.Sometimes it's just pure idiot comedy as these two mess everything up. Other times its a metacommentary on games with a hint of criticism, or maybe just lighthearted ribbing, of tropes we've all come across in our time as people who play way too many video games.The game falls ever so slightly shy of being an instant classic. But I find myself hoping you'll disagree and say it went all the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and quite simply this was one of the most engaging, fun, clever, and at times emotional experiences I've ever had with a game. After reading that the game now includes platform elements, I was sceptical that the transition from the previous format in Time Gents Please and BTDT could retain the same sense of humour and creativity. I was so very very wrong. Its a masterpiece of game development that puts big budget games to shame for their lack of ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved playing this game.Its a beautiful blend of writing and gameplay, where a lot of the time you are coming across punchlines by playing the game. It has some chapters that last a few hours and some chapters that last a few minutes, which means that nothing over stays its welcome. It also has the confidence to include things in the game that seem like oversights only to reveal them to be part of the gameplay or narrative hours later.There should be more games like it in the world :)
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly one of the best games I've played in years. It's hilarious during so many moments, and the writing is really something else. The overall plot is fascinating - you feel as though you're unraveling a complex mystery, and the momentum is constantly building up to something big.The hybrid of game genre mechanics here is really good - not always perfect, but a really cool idea that is supported by really great writing. The fact that the game leans into breaking down the fourth wall really helps to embrace the initial idea, and there are many different avenues the game explores in trying to balance both mechanics at once. For the most part, Lair of the Clockwork God does it beautifully.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play a lot of Point and Clicks during the 90's, and in recent years I've been struggling to find one that could keep me invested. Lair of the Clockwork God is entertaining from start to finish, with multiple puzzles that put a smile on your face.The half platformer part is what I assumed would keep me playing, but in hindsight it served as bait for the rest of the game, for which I'm thankful.It's difficult to delve into the specifics of what makes this game great without spoiling it, but if there's one thing you could say is that it's very self-aware in all the good ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with it a lot. It's a hybrid of Platformer and Adventure games, and a rather successful one. It's pretty meta and up its own arse, but it does utilise the concepts that it wields well. The writing and creativity was easily the biggest draw. Some of the jokes are on the darker side, but I appreciated that it called itself out whenever it brushed up against something iffy. The platforming was sometimes a little more demanding than I'd have liked, but the game's generous enough with checkpoints that it never was a huge issue. The other thing I'd wanna note is that i don't think I ever really felt like I got a good grasp on the controls. The game has a lot of verbs, and that just ends up in a complicated mess, and the genre switching makes it harder to get used to. It was never bad enough to hinder my enjoyment, but I think it's something you might bump into too. If you are genre-savvy of the aforementioned game styles, and can stomach the occasional mean-spirited joke, it's certainly worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I've always had a fondness for platformers and point-and-click adventures so to find a game that blends both genres into one gloriously silly experience was a revelation. The platforming can be a little tricky in places - an assist mode is available for those who struggle - but the controls are nice and responsive, and there's decent checkpointing, too. The point-and-click element is satisfying and rarely strays into 'try everything in the inventory' territory. What shines out most of all for me, though, is the humour displayed throughout. It's daft, 4th wall breaking, occasionally scatological and extremely silly. It took me around 11 hours to complete (albeit on the Switch), and I'll be playing through again to see if I missed anything.  It's that good.I can't recommend this game enough, it's been one of my most enjoyable experiences in this awful year and it's a bargain!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this! The combination of action and platforming is really creative and fun, and as a point and click fan I thought the puzzles were reasonably complicated and super satisfying while only rarely getting into frustrating territory.Most of all though, it's the writing and humour that makes this stand out. This is the funniest game I've played in ages, both with the dialogue and with some of its mechanical twists and surprisingly delayed punchlines. Highly recommend!P.S. The music slaps too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: LotCG is a beautiful array of weird and wonderful levels, spending just the right amount of time mucking about with the conventions of the games it was (lovingly?) inspired by and punctuating it all with brilliant gags. The point-and-click bits are inspired, rather than obtuse, and the platforming is grippingly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Having played and loved "Ben There, Dan That" and "Time Gentlemen, Please" years ago, I've been waiting a long time for a continuation of those games, or even just another adventure game from this team. I had pretty much all but given up on this, especially after reading a few tweets and blog posts from them basically saying that it was never going to happen. Then I read that this game existed in an issue of PC Powerplay and rushed to buy it.I wasn't disappointed. This game is hilarious, and extremely clever with the  way it blends platforming and 'normal' adventuring. It even manages to fit in references to the earlier games without it being necessary to have played them to find the game funny or relevant. I especially loved the parts where they subverted your expectations of what the game should be doing, and it never played along with memes. Also, stray dogs are disgusting so I appreciated the part that made that clear.All in all, I loved this. The story line was fantastic, the overall message was well-delivered, and I genuinely got a feeling of closure for the entire trilogy. You did good work, Dan and Ben. Oh, I also thought the addition of the extra game was amazing. It's the perfect way to find out about the past of the characters... If it wasn't for how frustrating a couple of the platforming bits are, this would be a perfect ten from me. I give it a 9.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Played 3+ hours on PC, finished the game on Switch.What can I say? This game is comedy genius and fun to play.You control two friends, one a platformer guy, the other a point-n-click guy on an adventure to save the earth from ALL THE APOCALYPSES!!! It's this combo of point-n-click with platforming that creates some unique opportunities for gameplay and humour.If you're playing and find yourself thinking "what the ♥♥♥♥ is this!?" - well, the developers are always one step ahead of you. Be warned!Download, take off your pants, hit Play, enjoy.And if you don't like it get a refund, eh?
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Meta comedy is difficult to make funny, let alone actually incisive, but LotCG manages beautifully. It goes all-in on poking fun of indie game tropes and mechanics, while still being an actually enjoyable combination of platformer and point-and-click adventure. It's stunning how well the game balances these two and the pacing is perfect throughout. I also laughed. Quite a bit, actually.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Love old school click n point adventure games and think that combining a whatsit with a thingamajig to obtain a macguffin is the height of puzzles? Ben is your man. Love indie platformers and consider spike pits a perfectly valid metaphor for depression and anxiety? Dan's here for you. And together they're the unlikely duo who clash their genres mercilessly together.Lair of the Clockwork God - the big send-off finale to the Ben & Dan Series (play Time Gentlemen Please!) - is an absolute joy. The core gameplay is split between Dan's newfound love for platforming and his absolute refusal to do anything that doesn't involve jumping around, and Ben's classic adventure game wandering where he'd rather spend half an hour creating a convoluted series of events to allow him to progress rather than just go up a stair. The two are nearly constantly paired up and the 'levels' require the clever combination of both skillsets to advance - and even though you'd think that such a gimmick would be quickly squeezed dry, there's constantly another new twist around the corner that gives the central ideas a whole new spin. That describes Clockwork God in general - it's a constant surprise and delight, always throwing something new in your way and coming up with a way to mix things up, in a way that makes it completely unpredictable in the best of ways. During their adventure the duo not only pay tribute (and rip apart) their chosen genres but also go through several other set pieces and genre explorations, which allow for all manners of inspired hijinks. The best of all, it's all consistently excellent both in design and writing: never did it feel like it's running out of steam, and the fantastic dialogue is genuinely laugh out loud at times.There's a few scratches in the armour but nothing gamebreaking. There's a few technical glitches which prevented me from continuing but fixed upon restart, and the controls feel a little clunky beyond their intended restrictions: neither keyboard/mouse or a pad feel 100% right, which I guess is understandable given the wild genrebending. The platformer sections also seem a little tacked on at times and occasionally felt like filler between the more traditional adventure fare, but that is an absolutely biased opinion, given I'm coming into this game as a click n point adventure fanatic and generally find myself bored by the current wave of indie platformers, so your mileage may wary. But given Dan's utter refusal to interact, Ben's sections seem generally more fleshed out and provide much of the game's great writing and humour - and some standout puzzles that have found a spot in my Best Puzzles of Adventure Gaming list.Absolutely recommended - full of heart, laughs and charisma, and a brilliant finale(?) for the duo who brightened up the click n point adventure scene all those years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent, and I highly recommend it. I don't want to go into detail about some of my favourites, but there will be times where you wonder why something has been included in the game, and it was there for both a genuinely unique puzzle AND a bit of a goof.That said, do be ready for the occasional frustrating bit of platforming, especially if you're hoping to find everything the game has to offer.
