_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game during the steam sale and I started laughing out loud on the opening splashes. Kept laughing all the way through. The writing is fantastic, a recursive take on the evolution of computer games over several decades, and so thickly packed with in-jokes I probably should do another play-through to make sure I spotted them all. If you've ever played a Lucasarts adventure game, you'll enjoy re-experiencing all the best and most annoying bits of those games while the game makes fun of itself for being such a faithful reiteration of the genre. And the platforming bits, while fiddly at times, blend rather seamlessly into the point-and-click bits. It's funny. It's engaging. It's not too long. It breaks the 4th wall in ways that are only topped by Doki Doki Literature Club. And everything about it, including that 4th wall break, is a commentary on innovation and change in video games over the years. As a genuine Old, who has been around since long before Manic Mansion and still keeps up with the newest indie titles, this game felt like a fun conversation over drinks with some good friends.Absolutely recommend, especially if you're kind of a video game nerd who will get most of the jokes.

_childDocuments_.review: Going in to this game I was a little worried - I was a big fan of the earlier games in this series and I was concerned that the shift in gameplay from pure point and click to an adventure/platformer hybrid would lead to compromise and disappointment. Happily, my fears were quickly allayed. The gameplay style may be different, but the core of the experience is still built on the same foundations - puzzle solving, a ridiculous but fun story, and most importantly the quality writing and humour. It's impossible to give any examples of the comedy in the game without spoiling something, but suffice to say I was moved to genuine laughter on multiple occasions. There is a part of me that wonders if some of the more culturally specific jokes might not land with everyone, but a passing familiarity with British comedy should suffice in most cases and it's refreshing to see a game with an actual voice rather than one that feels like it was full of jokes written by a committee.In terms of the gameplay, both the point and click sections and the platforming worked and were integrated well. I personally preferred the old school adventure sections more, but the faster paced action never outstayed its welcome or caused any frustration - though I did note there is a menu option to reduce the platforming difficulty if you are struggling. It's worth noting the huge amount of accessibility options here as well, which some may find useful. The puzzles themselves were good (one or two actually very clever). I was never stuck for long as they generally have logical solutions, which is not a given in this genre - as anyone who's spent hours mashing inventory items together in a desperate attempt to fathom a developers' logic will attest.Overall, I would strongly recommend giving this one a try, particularly if you are a fan of the classic 90s Lucasarts adventure games (Monkey Island, Sam & Max, etc.) It is, as the protagonists would no doubt say, Brillo.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Humor is subjective, of course, but  found this game to be both funny and clever, and  I had a lot of fun playing through it over the course of a  few days. I'll probably play it again, once I've given it a bit of a rest, and it did make me want to play through the previous two Ben and Dan games again.I'm not sure combining (or should I say "crafting"?) platforming with point-and-click adventures is  a good idea - in fact, I'm quite sure it's not - but I think it worked pretty well here. And the platforming can't have been  difficult if someone like me, who rarely play platform games, could make it through it with only a few resigned groans of "oh, come !"

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockwork God is a mixture of a platformer and Point and Click Adventure Game wrapped up with some clever puzzles and humorous dialog. While the quality of platforming itself is perhaps a touch below serviceable, its inclusion (and indeed even its quirks) has merit and serves to drive several puzzles and story bits. Most of the game’s challenge lies in trying to solve the Adventure Game puzzles.There are two parts of this game which I really like. The first is is the dynamic between Ben and Dan who have taken positions on the opposite sides of old school point and click adventure games and the new school Indie Darling Platformer. Ben who will absolutely refuse to jump even a few inches off the ground and Dan who refuses to pick up any item that isn’t floating in the air. These extreme roles drive a lot of the humor of the game, such as Dan insisting that Ben call combing inventory items as “Crafting.” This commentary and humor on these common mechanics from games both new and old never gets old.The other part of the game I’ve liked is how a few of the puzzles are quite meta in often amusing ways. While its hard to talk about them without spoiling, the game does a good job of letting you know when its time to think outside the box, which is often a problem with such puzzles. So its less about figuring it out on your own and more about the game hitting you over the head that maybe you should consider doing X. This doesn’t discount their use, as the solutions are quite funny.In short, the humor, puzzles, and the dynamic between Ben and Dan make this worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game this. _childDocuments_.review: This is the third in the Bed and Dan games/adventures, following on from Ben there Dan that and Time please gentlemen. For anyone worried, you do not have to have played any of the previous games to play this as each stand alone but all are hilariously fun.This adventure sees a departure (ish) from the previous two which were classic point and click adventures. Lair of the Clockwork God, takes the Point and Click formula and fuses it with platforming to create something different. Our two characters each embody a different type of gameplay, Ben is stuck in his old Point and Click ways where as Dan  seeks the fast pace adventure and fun of platforming.This is how the game manages to merge these two genres so well, whilst injecting so much humour along the way. This is a game that is always mocking itself and its characters (creators) along the way. From some great jokes, to one liners to little nods and winks to other pop cultural things through the years. The game also is not frightened to break the 4th wall and knock itself for making its characters do stupid things that would only ever happen in a game. The developers also are not frightened to throw in a little 4th wall breaking during gameplay as well (I will leave that surprise for you to find), when I worked out the puzzle in the hungover section it was a moment of hilarity and brilliance.A lot of love and time has been put into the game to try and fuse these two different gaming worlds and I have to say it really does work and work well. That said there are a couple of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the controls, I had to change my control configuration a few times until I found a solution that worked best for me but even then there were a couple of moments in the game I found a bit tricky thanks to my setup. Those moments are very rare though and for the rest of the time the controls work well.The puzzles are good, the platforming, jumping and shooting are fun & thanks to the gravity moments add an extra puzzle side to things and the humour is funny and found throughout.  Ive always found that the best way to tell if a game is any good, is how much and often you want to play it. I only completed it last night and I already want to go back and replay it to see if there was anything I missed or jokes I didn’t get the first time around. This is another fantastic game by Size 5 Games and I really do hope that they continue on the Ben and Dan games as it would be great to see what the next evolution could hold in store for them.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you cross British humour and game industry humour?Not this game- of course it's this game, why else would I even say that in the first place? As well as being hilarious, this brilliant game manages to combine two very different genres, Sonic-style platformers (it even has its own Green Hill Zone ripoff- I mean *looks at script* completely original level that is not affiliated with any existing game!) and Lucasarts-style point-and-click games, in all their slow, methodical glory. Two genres that by all means should not be able to be mixed, but oh boy have the mad lads at Size Five Games done it.If anything, buy it for the one exposed buttock.It's a nice buttock, I swear.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game - if you likes the old Lucasarts point 'n click games, you'll probably love it - and if you found the endless back-and-forth and random inexplicable item combinations frustrating in those old games, you'll find this one a refreshing change. The script is amusingly wry, and the game is actually quite surprising in its ability to Go Where No Point-N-Click Adventure Has Gone Before. Thoroughly Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockword God is a brilliant adventure/platformer hybrid. You play as two characters with different gameplay styles. Ben is an adventure gamer, so he talks to characters, interacts with objects, and absolutely does not jump. Dan is a platformer, so he jumps, runs, and kills enemies, but does not interact beyond that.You must use the advantages of each character to jointly work past puzzles and challenges, with some sections being solely accessible by Ben and some solely accessible by Dan.The game design and writing is simply brilliant. There are so many good ideas here that you will want to keep playing and playing. The game is loosely split into levels based around human emotions, and this is a rich source of creativity - the game sometimes doesn't tell you what emotion a level is until a twist at the end, and other emotions are played with in surprising ways.The humour really is top notch. Up there with Paradigm and Clam Man for moments where I actually laughed at loud. If you enjoyed the comedy in Ben There, Dan That or Time Gentlemen Please then this is an even better, more polished version of that. Loads of jokes poking fun at platformers and adventure game tropes, and some well-placed fourth wall breaking, give nice variety to the laughs too.The music is decent and art is pretty enough - these aren't what makes the game special, but they support the experience nicely. The difficulty curve is still sliiiightly off. In particular, the platforming starts off relatively simple, but the adventuring has some obtuse puzzles from very early on. This is something the designers always seem to struggle with - Behold the Kickmen would have been a brilliant game if not for the horrible difficulty curve. Here, though, this issue is very minor, and it doesn't stop me recommending the game whole-heartedly.Lair of the Clockword God is brilliant. Highly recommend if you're wanting a game to remind you how creative, surprising, and downright fun games can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: It's surprising, light-hearted, pokes gentle fun at current trends in games, and challenges you without being too difficult. I did use the official hint guide a few times, but I appreciated how the guide didn't really give anything away. At times the commentary on gaming felt a little too navel-gazey for me, but not so much that I ever wanted to stop playing. Some of my favorite bits involved breaking the fourth wall and then some to solve a puzzle. I also really enjoyed the fact that there was different dialogue almost every time I tried to use something in the inventory on some new object. It wasn't just "I can't use this here," but actual new, funny writing contextualized for the object and inventory item you are trying to pair. That must have taken a long time to write, and I kinda want to go back and play it again just to see the dialogue that I missed. All in all a good purchase, and I'd like to play something like a mix of platformer and point-and-click again!

_childDocuments_.review: Very few games make you think _literally_ outside the box for the answers. It lays out immaculately constructed systems and rules of play, and just occasionally, leans on you to completely disregard them. It's some of the smartest game writing there is.AAAAAAAA++++++++ contains wanking booth; would recommend again.

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockwork God is a very funny, very meta game about two characters that don't agree on what type of game you'll be playing, either an independent platformer or an old school point-and-click adventure game. The game in itself is a joyful ride between tropes and references, and due to its premise - the two characters having to explore various emotions because of some end-of-the-world computery simulation business - manages to strike various emotional chords beyond the fun specific to its two heroes. The art is gorgeous, the soundtrack is magnificent, and it manages from beginning to end to stay light, acid, and engaging. I had the chance to receive is as a gift from a friend as part of a game exchange we made, but I would have purchased it for myself anyway, and would recommend it to practically anyone, with the fair warning that the game has a certain amount of dark humour (without being edgy, actually the question is adressed in a thoughtful way) and gore (without being disgusting), . It also features some tricky platforming sequences. It made me happy to play it, I believe it would make you happy to play it too, and that's all I can say about that game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a funny game and it's a clever game. It's funny and clever enough that there are points where you'll probably sit back, narrow your eyes at the screen, and say something like "ooh, you didn't." The laughs come thick and fast (there are even jokes before the menu screen!), especially if you take your time and investigate every dialogue option and inventory item, which is very rewarding for completionists.The platform sections feel challenging without requiring the lightning reflexes of a 14 year old, and the adventure sections are well written so you'll feel clever for finding the solution without yelling "well how on earth was I meant to know that?" Even if you struggle with either section, it's still brilliant fun because some of the best jokes in the game come from failing tasks.New twists to existing gameplay mechanics pop up fast enough that things never feel stale, while still introducing them carefully enough that you're never expected to do something you're not confident doing.This is a great game and for £15 it's an absolute steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: (For full disclosure: I was gifted a copy, but it's so bloody good I wanted to review it)It's very rarely that I enjoy a game so much I feel compelled to pipe up about it, but Lair of the Clockwork God is an absolute breath of fresh air. The way it combines modern platforming with traditional point-n-click puzzle-solving, interlaced with proper British humour, lush visuals, and an absolutely gorgeous soundtrack, makes for a truly original adventure. You can clearly feel the care and attention to detail in the game's writing. Small references made one minute become a part of the experience the next. Every item interacts uniquely depending on how you try to use it, leaving you entranced with spending even more time simply engaging with stuff just to see what dialogue it returns. As the resident platformer, Dan's sections rely on quick reflexes and 'intelligent'(?) pathing to clear them, though his vertically-challenged frame and obnoxiously-large gorilla hands mean the more intricate tasks like interacting with objects and pulling levers must be left to Ben. Ben's fervour for traditional point-n-clicks gift him with these skills, at the cost of being unable to navigate vertically-challenging obstacles such as small steps and slight inclines. However, with an empty bladder and a healthy dose of helium, Ben is able to piggyback his compatriot through such trials and tribulations. This is where the game really shines, as although the pair are often separated on their journey to save the world from ALL of the apocalypses, the sections where they combine and cover for each other's weaknesses make for some truly ingenious moments. The puzzle penny drop moments will make you go 'oh ffs', the awfully brilliant puns will make you go 'oh ffs', and the fact Clockwork God is only 15 quid (at the time of writing this anyway) SHOULD make you go 'oh ffs, how haven't I picked this up already? It's going right in my basket.'
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: If I have one hesitation about recommending this game, it's that it almost feels so hand-crafted to be on *my* wavelength specifically that I'm hard-pressed to imagine it's on anyone else's. But if you're like me (and heaven help you) and you're a fan of point'n clicks, platforms, the jumping thereof, actively hostile puzzles, and jokes so awful I still haven't stopped laughing, then you absolutely need to get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece.A bit clunky here and there but definitely a work of art in means of satire and humor.Overall i find the Puzzles better executed than the platforming, but the platforming in no means lessens the experience. It is only a bit clunky.So if that is something okay with you, play this game. It is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Guybrush Threepwood and Mario Mario didn't hang out but maybe if Ron Gilbert and Shigeru Miyamoto had done, maybe it wouldn't have taken until 2020 for us to finally get to experience this new genre of Jump n Click (or should that be Point-former?)Lair of the Clockwork God is a wonderfully inventive and genuinely laugh out loud mash up that skillfully brings together brain teasing point and click mechanics, inventory based puzzle solving, classic platforming and even progressive player upgrades. It's rare to find genuinely fresh ideas in game design but that is what the team at Size Five have achieved. Sorely disappointed not to have been able to spend more time playing it! The Dan and Ben series are reliably amusing so if you want some levity in these times make sure to check out their other games. But, be warned, there's a real chance you'll be left missing the added dimensions of playability introduced by Lair of the Clockwork God. Get on this game today.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: If you're even slightly interested after watching the trailer, buy this game - you won't be disappointed! The story is engaging, the jokes are silly (and often very witty) and the puzzles - while tough at times - are usually far more logical than your standard point-n-click adventure. The platforming aspect works super well too, much improved over floaty controls of the developer's previous game The Swindle.My only gripes are some occasionally fiddly controls (specifically the adventure game verb selection and inventory) and a couple of bugs I encountered, but nothing game breaking.Bonus points for also containing the most meta puzzle/set up for a joke I've ever seen in a game. No spoilers, but I genuinely had to pause for a minute or two to appreciate what just happened. You'll know when you get to it...
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent mashing together of platforming and adventure gaming. Witty dialogue throughout which had me in tears at one point, Super Meat Boy style platforming (but more forgiving, thank you) mixed with inventory puzzling and a rich layer of humour dribbled all over it like a thick gravy. Genuinely one or two moments of brilliance, don't make any assumptions about what the game is doing or expects of you when solving some of the puzzles. As ever, the conversations between the two main characters is the heart of the experience, Dan and Ben fans will not be disappointed. Everyone else should just get in on this anyway, come on. You know it makes sense. Smashing game. Good work. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: My full review is .Briefly: Lair of the Clockwork God is well worth your time if you like adventure games, British humour and/or games about games. It's at its best when it combines the adventuring and platforming gameplay into highly interrelated puzzles. The platformer aspect adds some variety, but it’s not something that I would recommend on its own, or something that should get in your way if you don’t usually go for it.The two earlier games in the series are also well worth it, and can be had for a very reasonable fee.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about an hour into Lair of the Clockwork God, and since I'm stuck on a puzzle, I'm here to tell you that it is a fantastic game and well worth the asking price. Witty, charming, free-flowing and easy to master, if you're a fan of old-school, point-and-click adventures but feel like they need a little more pep in their step every now and again, this is - quite literally - the title for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: There are not many funny games but this one made me genuinely laugh out loud on multiple occasions. A fun mixture of platforming and puzzles that never got too frustrating. I had a fun time with it and if you have any love for old school point and click adventures and/or pixel platformers I think you'll get a kick out of this. BUY IT!

The controls take a bit of getting used to (I played on an Xbox pad), and the platforming sections aren't as much fun as the genius puzzles, but this was a perfect paced adventure that I played over a long weekend. _childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following Size Five Games since they were under a different name. The Ben and Dan duo of adventure games are stellar, and are among my all-time favorites. When I heard that a third game in the series had been released I jumped on the purchase right away. This game continues their funny writing and clever puzzle-making, with the "modern" twist of making it a platforming hybrid. I find platformers tedious, but they've managed to make theirs fun and mostly in service of the game's puzzles. If you're looking for something a little different, you should look no further than the Lair of the Clockwork God.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the funniest games I have played in years. Video game humour is SO hard to do and I haven't seen many get the timing down as well as this. I could nit pick about some of the platforming issues, but I had such a good time overall I can't do anything but recommend this. If you happen to be British, in your 30s and grew up on Lucasarts adventure games and toilet humour, this game has been made for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a grand time.Yessh, that's an underwhelming sentence to start with, but it's true: I had a grand time from beginning to end.  That's increasingly rare for me in my increasingly creaky, bitter, cynical, tired, worldweary, threadbare, baby been done wrong before, down and out, no account, weak, stupid middle age.There's a weird poignancy in this game that seems to echo my age.  No other way to put it.  Some of that may not be apparent to those a bit younger or older than this sort of crummy fat about the middle point of life.As for mechanics, the platforming was a little challenging here and there but well thought out. Never boring and each room  demands a slightly different combination of jumps, slides etc to overcome.The adventure side of things?  As funny as always.  With puzzles that don't expect moon logic from you.

If, like me, you fit that niche, this will be your GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Lair of the Clockwork God is a smart combination of two seemingly incompatible genres, and a much-needed continuation of the Ben and Dan saga. The puzzle design quite effortlessly combines elements of platformer puzzles and point-and-click puzzles in a way that makes you wonder why it isn't more common.I played through 'Ben There, Dan That' and 'Time Gentlemen, Please' before starting this, and I feel like the humour has matured slightly in the intervening years. It still does as good a job riffing on genre tropes (and now there are two genres to riff on), but it feels a little less... puerile. It really hit the mark for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying - the puzzles are so well-constructed and logical, plus there's enough in-game hints that I've never been stuck for very long. It is also a little reminiscent of the Lost Vikings, due to the two characters having different problem solving abilities, which is something I really miss.I've been playing it with my two primary school-aged children, who love thinking through the puzzles and we always find a solution - even if I have to censor *some* of the cheeky british humour. _childDocuments_.review: You remember how Braid blew you away at the end with the crazy time rewind sequence that recontextualizes everything you've been doing? This game manages to do something similar.It's 60% point and click adventure game, 40% platformer. I'm not a huge fan of platformers, but this one managed to be inoffensive. Even in the trickier bits I felt like the game wanted me to succeed, and I never bashed my head on a sequence longer than a few minutes.The point and clicking is glorious, though. The puzzles are tricky, but immensely satisfying to figure out. The writing is brilliant, and several seemingly throwaway jokes end up paying off hours later in ways that had me bursting out in laughter. It's clever and self-aware, but not in a smug way. It punches through the fourth wall, but in delightful ways. There's a tiny bit of Kojima in here. Plus, the music is amazing throughout.It's a good video game.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game.Having grown up playing all the great Lucasarts point-and-click graphic adventures (and The Dig), I knew I was always going to like at least 50% of this game. But the mash-up of platforming elements makes 'Lair of the Clockwork God' so much more than the sum of its parts.Above all else, I was hoping that this game would make me laugh and, boy, did it deliver. I don't want to spoil any of the jokes in this review, but was laughing out loud from opening credits, which feature some brilliantly-named fake company logos. And then, there is the often puerile dialogue between the two main characters. I played this game with a perma-grin throughout. There's sight gags, creative swearing, pithy one-liners, meta commentary on the games industry and some tremendous pay-offs further down the line. I'm not sure I've ever played a game where I genuinely laughed at puzzle solutions before, but this has several moments of 'They didn't just do that, did they?'. Also, in classic point and click tradition, you are rewarded for being 'experimental' with your inventory. Fun has clearly been had in coming up with dialogue for the player's more random actions. A point-and-click game lives or dies by its puzzles. Many have failed in the past for being far too obscure - those who remember the original Discworld game will know what I'm talking about. The puzzles here are just right. The objects in inventory are used appropriately, mostly, but the platforming element gives this an extra dimension of lateral thinking. There is also a degree of fourth-wall-breaking creativity that I've never come across before ('Feeling Old' level, I'm looking at you).Hopefully, this will not be the last we'll see of Ben and Dan.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the funniest games I've ever played. It's a little slow to start, but once it gets going, it's utterly fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, painted with a palette of genres, on a canvas made of the Fourth Wall.This is an escalation and natural progression from the earlier Ben & Dan games. Much, MUCH slicker and friendlier, with what feels like a whole new dimension of humour - but playing them is not a prerequisite for enjoying this to the full.IF YOU KNOW POINT & CLICK ADVENTURES: This game embodies and parodies the genre perfectly, with a bunch of clever puzzles in the classic format, and nothing too unintuitive or any frustrating busywork. There is a significant amount of genre crossover - some proper platforming required - so it might not be for everyone, but I understand there are decent accessibility options.The writing is... *exceptionally* good. I always enjoyed Ben & Dan's classic British humour - very much Two Mates Down The Pub, being mercilessly cruel to each other and the world, but ultimately very kind. It's written with love & compassion, and a big dollop of self-reflection. Everything is fair game (the young, the old, the living & the dead) but nothing is completely dismissed as Just A Joke, and nothing is said with malice.  Example (spoiler): A poignant moment came up while trying to fit in with Yoof Culture, wearing a bra to get into a nightclub. Just as you're patting yourself on the back for completing the silly & humiliating tasks with wry humour in tact, you're approached by a young guy the game has thus far been mercilessly mocking for his strenuous hipster affect. He breaks character to wearily point out that the writing here is a bit tired, a bit cliche, a bit misogynistic... and the titular characters pause to realise that, yeah, they're getting a bit old, and maybe being a bit sh*t, because they're trying to fit in with a culture's norms for their own personal ends without genuinely engaging with it. That basically, they're the joke - not all the people they're knowingly mocking to the player. And then it becomes clear that *this was the whole point of the chapter*.The game is *full* of thoughtful moments like this, that use the fourth wall and genre tropes not just for cheap gags, but for deeper, richer humour, and sometimes for real introspection. I lost count of the number of times I laughed out loud, not at throwaway jokes but at clever, smart, unique Gotcha moments that were not just in the script but *built into the fabric of the game*. I repeatedly found myself thinking aloud, "Oh, you clever b*stards...!"Aesthetically and mechanically, this is a great game, and that would be enough, but Lair of the Clockwork God is also a genuinely impressive work that demonstrates a humour and understanding that has infused the whole thing at every step of its creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: So, Lair of the Clockwork God - A review... So far... Artwork is beautiful if you grew up playing on Lucas Arts adventures and Amiga platformers. The humour is right up there with the sarcastic whit seen in 'Beneath a steel sky' and the 2 character element merging of both platform and point'n'click adventures is certainly something new (the closest might be 'flashback'). Admittedly this is mostly for those of a certain age but I'm pretty sure even my kids would enjoy exploring this game (though most likely under supervision less I end up a controller short when the puzzles get tricky)..Long story short - it's a perfect distraction from current AAA games and certainly some lighthearted fun in these dark times.  Now go buy it! (seriously... do it.... do it now)
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the previous Ben and Dan games around a year ago, I jumped on this as soon as it came out. Then didn't get round to playing it for 3 weeks.If you're familiar with the previous games, or Lucasarts point and clicks in general, you'll know the score, but with an extra hook. Great dialogue, puzzles that aren't stupidly easy, but also make logical sense. I got stumped on a few areas, but never had to resort looking up any solution, so it's all extremely doable if point and clicks are your thing. Even if you do know the solution right off the bat, I'd recommend spending your time trying out other stuff, going through conversations etc so you get all the back and forth between Ben and Dan. Plus all the 4th wall breaking and meta comments, which the series has always done well, and this is no exception.The obvious addition to this over previous entries is the platforming, which I feel might be a bit divisive. For the most part it's great, as doubling back to areas isn't as laborious as the classic 'click to walk here at snails pace' The platforming itself is fun, not too tricky and makes sense when needed. There are exceptions where the amount of instakill spike traps and finnicky jumps to walljumps is kinda frustrating and will turn off some point and click fans. There are moments when I had to plug in a controller because keyboard movement was getting annoying, and I feel like the timing of some traps could be relaxed in its difficulty (maybe some gameplay setting) so not to put off anyone from finishing it (seeing as I was about 2/3rds through when it started to bother me)Overall a very good game. I'll get the next one if it happens

_childDocuments_.review: Ben and Dan might not make AAA gmaes, but they make some of the most fun games available. The humour is amazing, childish, self referential and still brilliantly funny. The gameplay is addictive, well balanced and rewarding without being annoyingly difficult. The knowledge of the genres is top notch, I'm sure a number of references have flown over my head (although I'm pleased I picked up on the Broken Sword 3 one in the tutorial!).It's just a wonderfully well put together game that deserves to be played by anyone that is a fan of adventure games, platformers and gaming in general. _childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the first two Ben and Dan games, I've been waiting for the sequel for a long time and I'm thrilled to say it surpassed my expectations, which is saying a lot, because I really, really, really wanted to play this game one day. What's always drawn me to these games is the writing and this game is no different. The banter between Dan and Ben is great and their commentary on everything is hilarious. It's a thrill to examine every single item and go through every single dialogue option. The story is pretty standard, but there are some fun twists and many times where I laughed out loud as I played. The witty writing is definitely one of the strong points of the game.The gameplay is solid. I was a little nervous when I heard that, instead of being a standard point-and-click adventure, it was mixing in some platforming because I'm  but honestly? It was done really well! Admittedly I think the earlier parts of the game were much better about blending the two gameplay styles as a cohesive experience, but later parts of the game where you switch between starkly separate Ben parts and Dan parts were still good. I just preferred the bits where you work with Dan to open pathways to get Ben into place to do his adventuring thing. (This gets negligible later on as you gain more powers like carrying Ben around with you or straight up teleporting to each other.)The logic puzzles on the Ben side of things are solid—you collect items in all manner of ways and use them with the environment, on yourself, or on others, or even combine them together to find new uses. You know, standard fare. You can never miss anything and if you really get stuck, the answer is usually in your inventory. As for Dan, even though I'm really bad at platforming, I found I was able to get through everything without too much trouble. I usually avoid platforming games entirely because I don't find them fun after I've died the umpteenth time on the same jump, but although the controls are superb in this game, even the hardest parts only stumped me for about 15 minutes or so. I see in the latest patch (which I didn't notice or update to when I played) has options to alleviate some of the platforming bits, so if seeing that it's a platformer is about to scare you off: don't worry about it! You'll be fine. It's still fun. In addition to the two characters, the game finds several meta ways for you to play it, including a store where you make "in-app purchases" to ease your adventuring and, well, the methods you use to get into that store. ;) The game is so clever about the innovative ways it makes you solve problems and get through everything and I had a lot of fun with that. (Also, if you ever do get stuck at any point in the game, as usual there's an official hint walkthrough that very vaguely hints at what you're supposed to do so you can still figure it out yourself, just with an extra pointer!)Speaking of gameplay, I really have to praise the fact that I have never seen a game with so many accessibility options! I follow the dev on twitter and I remember being really impressed that he asked about what options he should add into the game one day and I was even more impressed when he knocked out a whole bunch of the suggestions that very afternoon. The options include but are not limited to: control rebinding, font sizes, colourblind mode, text colours, and so on. Even if you don't usually need accommodations, I suggest glancing through the list because you might find an option in there that enhances your experience. :) The game also looks gorgeous. I admit I kiiiiinda miss the janky walk cycles from the earlier games because they were just so charming, but the art style in this game and the beautiful environments really make up for it. The character designs are quirky and cute, both for the main characters and the NPCs they meet along the way. They're surprisingly expressive and I just really loved the whole look. The music is great, too, and not only adds to the atmosphere, but I found myself pausing just to listen to it at times. I'd definitely pick up the soundtrack if it were added as DLC.I think maybe my biggest complaint about the game is the jumping-through-the-floor-glitch. I was one of the, presumably, dozens of people who sent in a glitch report about it because it was really aggravating me during the tutorial and seemed a simple fix, but . But that feels like a minor complaint, all things considered, in what is otherwise a completely fantastic game!I highly recommend this to anyone who loves adventure games and wants a more modern take on them. It's the perfect length and is just so phenomenally designed. I want everyone to play it so it becomes the new standard for the adventure genre. I'd love to see another game in the series one day and I really hope it happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that is both funny and a blast to play.The mix between Point & Click and Platforming works way better than i would have thought and there were no parts where i felt completely lost.The jokes were great and had me audibly laughing at some points.Overall a great experience and definitely worth the money!

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels aimed directly at me.  Reproducing the gameplay of the games I've been enjoying for decades, while modernizing them enough to feel like something new, ensures I have so far been entertained by every moment.  In addition, lovingly mocking them at the same time pushes the whole experience into one I'll likely replay after I've finished.On a final note, the banter alone earns the creators all of the pizza trophies I am allowed by law to bestow.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A great combination of point & click adventuring and platforming. I think it surpasses at least a similar attempt by legend Ron Gilbert. The humour in it is not always in my taste, but I grew accustomed to it quite quickly. The game has some really ingenious puzzles where you have to rely on out of the box thinking. I would even say that you have to go a bit farther away from the box than you've gone before. And while not all of the solutions came to me quickly, I never felt stuck like one could playing a pure point & click game. I think this is helped by the complete lack of pixel hunting. Overall, I would say this is a must play if you like both of the genres, and I would also recommend it to favourers of one genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure games I've played in years, far in excess of what I expected from these guys (admittedly I haven't played anything from then since "Time, Gentlemen Please!" which was, gee, ELEVEN YEARS AGO) If you loved the other Ben and Dan games it's an easy recommendation, if you liked some puzzle platformers such as "The Cave" but wishes there was a bit more it's an easy recommendation. If you loved classic LucasArts it's.... well, a likely recommendation. If you specifically loved Sam & Max Hit the Road but wish that energy was directed in a direction with three times the amount of crass humour and twelve times the wild genre-bending, then it's the easiest recommendation of all.This is one of those games where most of the jokes are well set up and integrated into the gameplay, so I feel like any plot details at all count as spoilers. Go in as fresh as you can. I'd also say, tentatively, stick with it. If you're playing on PC without a controller then the control scheme can be a bit clunky, and there may be frustrations with Ben being deliberately written as very pedantic about getting the correct inputs. The very opening of the game holds back a fair bit and may not grab you immediately. Dear god KEEP PLAYING. It's easy to get the impression that the game is nothing but fourth wall jokes. What you need to realise is how staggeringly high a ziggurat you can make by piling increasingly clever fourth wall jokes on top of each other.Gameplay is surprisingly changeable throughout, but the basics are that you switch between Ben, who wants to play a point-and-click adventure, and Dan, who wants to play a platformer. The game is a very well judged balance of both. The aforementioned frustrations can come from, among other things, Ben moving veeeeery slowly and not being able to jump which is cumbersome in big open areas, but the game is fairly quick to provide you with quick-travel options for the spindly slowpoke. There's a wide selection of levels and an unexpected Metroidvania bent to the design. The platforming I'd say is an intermediary challenge - tricky enough for adventure purists to get pissed off but not at all unfair.To me this is the biggest, pleasantest surprise for years. Incredibly funny, consistently surprising, somehow fresh despite such a high pisstake quotient. Anyone who wants a funny puzzle game with surprises, this is what you're looking for along with more stuff you'd never have thought to ask for.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really grown on me.  I was a little put off at first because some minor glitches and the platforming didn't feel great.  But the writing and puzzle design is superb.  And the game is a lot longer than I expected!  There's a lot of content here and I'm really impressed with how they are able to keep things fun and interesting.  And it's all hilarious.  I was already a fan of their previous games, but Ben and Dan have really out done themselves with this one.  Well done guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: There's a moment in Lair of the Clockwork God where a character who could be considered a game designer says that they "make statements *through* the established structures, not despite them."That's a pretty good summary of what makes this game great. The most memorable puzzles and jokes are based around the mechanics, not just grafted on top of things.And boy, are those jokes funny! It's rare that a game can make me laugh at all, much less this much. There are gags in this game that had me cackling embarrassingly loudly. Humor is subjective but, like, for example: I can't stand toilet humor, but Ben and Dan managed to make me laugh at their toilet humor. They are very good at what they do.I was skeptical about the point and click adventure/platformer hybridization, but it works, and it makes the adventure game parts mechanically satisfying. The platforming's not perfect, but it's perfectly solid (it reminded me a lot of Hue's platforming, except with a lot more things to do) and the fact that it's really a puzzle platformer means that the game is still heavily weighted towards puzzles even when you're not in the adventure game half of it. I'm probably going to try to speedrun Lair, which is something I wouldn't do for most adventure games.I don't usually write Steam reviews—especially because they mostly function as a "should you buy this game" and I don't like reducing my opinions to that—but I had to make an exception for this game because it's really good and I don't think it's getting the attention it deserves. It is more than worth $19.99. Please play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Is the platforming here as good as the great platforming games of our time, including the ones it references? No. It isn't. The building blocks are big, the controls a bit clunky, and I expected more original upgrades than bloody double-jump and wall-jump. Luckily (for me, not for enthusiasts) even a casual like me only had trouble with the platforming parts in a few sections.More importantly, the humor is still top-notch and as irreverent, gross and unapologetically stuffed with UK slang as you can expect from Ben & Dan. Just make sure the humor is what you're getting it for and not the platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Only played the first 30 minutes so far, but from what I've seen the game seems enjoyable and shows a lot of promise. A nice mashup a genres and asymmetric character types. Dry sense of humor works well, as well as the little references to indie gaming culture. Doesn't seem like you need to be familiar with the other Ben and Dan games to get the jokes. Will probably continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This game's humor is rude, crude and constantly breaking the 4th wall in ways I didn't even think possible! Gameplay is a really neat mix with one of the protagonists wanting to expand from their point&clicking roots to platformers, while the other prefers to stick to their old adventuring ways. The gameplay is mixed up really well with the player having the ability to switch charaters at will, creating an extra layer of puzzling having to work out who's turn it is to shine and when the two need to work together.If you like platformers, adventure games and clever writing that REALLY doesn't take itself too seriously, try the game out!P. S. The protags are literal self-inserts of the main dev and his co-writer friend and I think that's funny.P. P. S. Someone pointed out to the dev on twitter that BenDan means "idiot (literally DumbEgg) and the dev thought it was funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally do platformers anymore, but this isn't a normal platformer. It's two guys with a weird sense of humor who have collaborated on a totally original genre: part platformer, part point-and-click, and all wicked fun.To begin with, you see the usual corporate credits on the march. It goes on and on, and you may begin to feel you're being had... and you are! Then you meet the two guys, one of whom can jump like crazy and the other can cleverly manipulate objects but can't get up onto the sidewalk from street level. Their dialog is a stitch and the solutions to their problems will tie your brain into knots.Highly original and makes me smile (though my head is ready for a warm bath every time I get to a save point).
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the previous two Ben and Dan games and was pleased to see they made a new one in the series. It ended up being quite a fun little game. It's a very meta experience through and through, but done in a fun way that subverted my expectations a few times.If you like point and clicks and platformers give it a shot. This game has some of the frustrations from both of those genres (insta-death traps, and confusing puzzles), but a lot of the positives as well, mainly good dialog and fun jumps.Overall I had a good time playing thorugh the game. Would recomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A joyfully inventive game that will constantly surprise. The jokes commenting on gaming tropes with silliness and light puerility are great, but what really shines is how they impact on gameplay. There's some moments that made me stare slack-jawed and the combine stupidity and brilliance.As a combination on point-and-click and 2D platformer, maybe you can expect mild frustration if our of practise at one (or in my case both). of these gametypes. But nevertheless any frustration was soon over and on the next highlight.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eagerly awaiting another Ben and Dan game since playing Ben There, Dan That and Time Gentlemen Please a long time ago, the writing in these games are funnier than anything else I've played.Lair of the Clockwork God goes a slightly different direction than being a pure adventure game - what I've been pleasantly surprised to find having now completed it is that this direction is unbelievably smart, being an outright good, inventive game while retaining that sharp, funny dialogue throughout. The blending of styles is executed in a jaw dropping way - the platforming is fairly basic, but consistently fun, and the adventure game element of it is smart and entertaining, but where the game really shines is where it combines these to create amazing puzzles, using the limitations of each (though these are continually changing as Dan unlocks upgrades) - it's a concept that feels so simple and satisfying that it's surprising it hasn't been done before, the same way I felt playing games like Braid or Fez.   The consistent thread of fourth-wall breaking commentary on indie games and the self awareness shown throughout is great, funny but never mean spirited. There are a multiple times where this is taken to extremes or used in puzzles that are genuinely jaw dropping in an 'I can't believe they've done this' way. One of the best games I've played in a long time, it feels to me like this should be major.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished Lair of the Clockwork God and I was honestly sad to see it end. Consistently funny, sometimes even insightful, full of heart and that's just the atmosphere, jokes, dialogue and storyline.Then there's the gameplay. I'm a fan of indie platformers and equally so of traditional point&click adventure games. The platforming felt like a faster version of the platforming in The Swindle, but more tight. It did, however, sometimes feel like the platforming could have been more responsive, but that was mostly an issue in the beginning. I chose to play it with a controller, and both the adventure and platforming bits, once gotten used to, worked perfectly.When playing with Ben it did actually feel like an adventure game. When playing with Dan it felt like a platformer.Two genres I never thought would be seen in the same game, and here it actually worked. I need more of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever tried to tell a joke? Maybe recreate a bit you saw in a stand up act? How did it go? Absolute disaster, of course. Comedy is about timing, and inflection, and body language, and a million other bits that only come with practice. The stand up makes it look easy because he's done it hundreds of times. You can see the joke in your head, remember laughing your ass off at the punch line, but describing it in the lunchroom at work makes you look like a buffoon. What's great about written comedy is that you are kind of in on the performance. The joke's there on the paper (or screen,) and the timing of it is suggested, but ultimately it's your inner voice doing the delivery. Of course, that means it's that much harder to write the jokes. A comedy writer cannot rely on natural charisma or the trained tempo of a thousand performances. Lair of the Clockwork God has the funniest written jokes of any game I've played in the last few years. There is an easy confidence in the text as it drags my unfunny ass through joke after joke. Sitting in a dark room giggling uncontrollably at animal cruelty or grave robbing bits isn't exactly how I pictured life turning out, but here we are. The puzzles are just difficult enough to stump me every few minutes, but not obtuse enough to require checking a guide. The platforming ramps up in difficulty and complexity quite elegantly. I think it's clearly second fiddle to the adventure segments, but it's a nice change of pace. The art is bonkers good, and I really enjoyed the music. If you are an adventure game fan desperate for more content, this is a game for you. If you are a fan of written comedy, consider this a slightly more expensive than average ebook (or a shockingly good deal on a hardcover!) If you are an indie platformer person, you may feel personally insulted by some of the dialog but you'll still have a good time and if your honest with yourself the fact is that everything they say is true.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Lair is one of the funniest games in a good while, and it's consistently funny whether it's being a platformer or a classic point and click. It's not always a good platformer in my opinion (rather, competent and slightly irritating with its preponderance of sub-meatboy insta-deathtraps). But the rest of the package is absolutely stellar; the last game to so confidently express so many ideas and swagger between genres was What Remains of Edith Finch.The platform&adventure genre is not a crowded field, but it'd be hard to argue this could be the finest example yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely funny game with an interesting/unusual core conceit that managed to catch me by surprise numerous times - I'm fairly sure I exclaimed "oh you clever bastards" multiple times. It's got some rough edges, although I'm fairly sure some of them are intentional, and won't be for everyone because it's got a fairly leisurely pace and is crammed of crude jokes (which might turn some people off..? I was amused throughout). This feels like it was an ambitious undertaking where everything came together so well; the final result was very enjoyable.I've played and enjoyed most of dev's games (and been entertained by him on Twitter for some time now), and this one is unusual, surprisingly clever and entertaining enough that it's convinced me to write my first steam review as a way of throwing a modicum of well deserved extra support their way. _childDocuments_.review: You know it is good when it gets you laughing before you've even got past the loading screens. This is a work of mad genius. The humour is broad and relentless. Relentless in a good way in that even if you don't get the niche joke about the RIP on a gravestone it doesn't matter because you probably won't even realise it was a joke and you'll still be chuckling about the last one you did get.It has, like all the best irreverent comedy, a bloody huge heart to it. It is silly and disgusting and sooo wrong at times but it also reaches points of genuine poignancy. Ben Ward and Dan Marshall are basically the Simon Pegg and Nick Frost of games. Not dissimilar in terms of very British humour and there is such genuine heart in the games they’ve made together. It bears comparison to Shaun of the Dead in that this is the story of two buddies facing the apocolypse together but also the story of growing up and growing old. There isn’t such an imbalance between two central characters, where Nick Frosts character was the youthful influence that Shaun had to learn to contain as he grew up both the characters here are more well rounded. Ben is stuck in the adventure game past and refuses to change or grow whereas Dan is struggling to maintain a youthful relevance by becoming a cool platformer. They’re both right and they’re both wrong of course. You have to both grow and move with the times but also stay true to who you are and be comfortable with the fact that you maybe aren’t young and hip anymore and that is fine. If Shaun of the Dead was about growing up then maybe Lair of the Clockwork God is more about growing old. These points are made in a very straightforward but also humourous fashion, just like Shaun of the Dead did. It isn’t subtle but it is warm and funny and outragous so it never feels trite. There is no pretense that the game is saying anything profound or groundbreaking but it is saying something important and very relatable.The game itself then. The platforming is… fine. It isn’t hard and it doesn’t get in the way but it also isn’t the game’s heart and soul. And that is as it should be, thematically it wouldn’t make sense for Dan’s gameplay to be perfect because Dan is basically a wannabe. What is a little more grating is that Ben’s interface is more than a little clunky on mouse and keyboard. Not bad enough that I bothered to hook up a controller but not great.The puzzles though are frequently brilliant! The whole game is in part a love letter to old point-and-click adventures but that doesn’t mean it is afraid to innovate. It rather has a wild unapologetic freedom to it. I just read someone on Twitter saying that the solution to one puzzle literally made his jaw drop and the best thing, the absolute best thing, is that I don’t know which puzzle they mean because there are multiple candidates. The puzzles are also at a very good level. Interesting and challenging without ever really becoming a frustration.I do feel like I am close to the perfect player for this game: I’m a late 30s British-ish guy who fondly remembers the LucasArts point-and-clicks but also followed the 21st century indie scene and love to see people play with games as a medium. Your mileage may vary but I’m pretty confident that you could fall well outside the niche that I fall into and still love this game.Give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm barely an hour in, what I have seen has made me keen to promote this. Many are talking about this in the same breath as Lost Vikings, and that's a fair comparison. But there's so much more to it than that.Admittedly, I was a fan of the previous games which were pure point and click, but the hybrid gameplay really takes it up a notch, if I may use a suitably awful pun, it becomes a MetroidVaniac Mansion about a third of the way through.There are times that it flirts with satirising political correctness and good taste, but this is all don with a wink and a fair bit of respect. It's difficult to fully praise this without spoiling the content for newcomers but as hybrid games go, this is far more effectively done than most -  a true labour of love.This comes, of course with at Devil's Kiss, the other work here, but I hear it is a very detailed look at the early lives of Dan and Ben, which is potentially very useful beyond its own universe. Those who know their Size Five gameography will get a real lift from it, and to be honest it gives more of a backstory to these characters than even the characters themselves will give you in the main game, should you find that useful.There's very few games that can make me laugh straight from the splash screens, but this truly breaks the mould. Probably a bit concerning that I identify quite so much with the protagonists...EDIT: Having completed this now, I don't really having anything to correct here.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal, and I seriously can’t steer it enough. Dan Marshal’s and Ben Ward’s newest adventure, , takes two very different genres, Platforming and Point & Click, makes you play both at the same time,  Everything about this game kept me glued to it; beautiful pixelated environments, a wonderful soundtrack, and puzzles so clever and devious that it felt absolutely fantastic when I finally figured them out. Seriously, the solutions to some of the puzzles in this game are so absurd, they force you to think  of the game itself.  Another highlight of this game is the humor. The witty banter between the two protagonists, be it taking shots at each other, making jabs at pop culture, and their lampshading about the absurd scenarios they’re thrown into, are a blast to read, and some of these comments are subtle hints for puzzles down the line.The writing is also something to mention. The plot itself is both ridiculous and engaging at the same time. To my surprise, the game also actually got somewhat emotional, but the frequent humor kept it from becoming flat-out depressing, one part in particular. There’s also some parts that make you think about important issues regarding human emotion.There’s been an 11 year gap since the last Ben and Dan adventure,  if I had one nitpick, it was that callbacks to  and  were far and few between, which is a shame because you should definitely play those as well.  is a fantastic game and a wild ride I couldn’t recommend more.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I laughed out loud to a game. The dialogue is witty, the puzzles wonderfully off-beat and the platforming is... serviceable? Look, if you're here for another Celeste, maybe look somewhere else. If you miss the joy of LucusArts Adventure games, do yourself a favour and pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of this game for a sizeable chunk of time (read: following Dan on Twitter) and I gotta say, when I first saw the trailer I really,  didn't think I'd enjoy the genre-mashing as much as I actually do. It just works so well. And it's so well written. And it's a Dan end Ben game. And it's a platformer. And it looks and sounds so nice.Look, just buy it already.You know you want to.Or maybe you don't know you want to, but that's alright, I honestly didn't know either.But I'm glad I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: The third instalment in the Ben & Dan series after Ben There, Dan That! and Time Gentlemen Please! brings the same humour, gentle puzzling, and 4th Wall breaking to a new decade but this time as a vikings style action-puzzler. Although developing the "characters" of Ben and Dan further, it is in no way reliant on having played the previous games in the series. There's plenty of call-backs and references but none that aren't immediately explained.  All you need to know is that in previous games you've gained increasing amounts of control over Ben as he becomes more than just a side-kick to Dan. In Ben There, Dan That, for much of the game Ben's sole action is to flip a light switch. Now after the events of Time Gentlemen Please made him more active, Ben's ready to be a platform puzzle protagonist, begrudgingly assisted by Dan.Recommended (especially the Visual Novel that comes free with the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Really good Adventure / Platformer hybrid with the point and click parts being particularly excellent. The puzzles are great, the dialogue is fantastic and the platforming is pretty good but really not the focus here. Admittedly a bit bias since I've been waiting for it for quite some time but it really is something you should pick up.This is a standalone game but I would say if you like this to go back and play Ben There, Dan That! and Time Gentlemen, Please! to pick up a few neat nods and also for about 6 more hours of good fun adventuring
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: My experience so far:So it turns out you CAN mix adventure games and platformers and actually make it work, while also stay true to it's sources: The adventure parts doesn't shy away from the bizzare inventory puzzles that characterize the genre, but they (mostly) never feel unfair.Meanwhile, the plataforming bits are well designed, and new mechanics are introduced often to keep it from geting old.In short, no seccion feels like a gimmick or filler, and at the same time it doesn't feel like two different games stuck together.The changings in pace can feel a bit weird at first, but soon the game makes it clear you're playing one cohesive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant point and click game spliced with a platformer. I did find some of the platforming sections difficult, but that's due to my own skill more than anything else(you can now dial down the platforming in the settings, which is a lovely addition). The puzzles and jokes more than make up for those minor moments of frustration however. Some of the solutions are so clever it's a wonder they haven't been done before.If you enjoy games, especially Size 5 games, you need to buy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Been following development of this because I got a few snort laughs out of Behold the Kickmen, and thought this also might be a laugh. Yes, yes it is very much a laugh.It's gloriously written and very very funny, has an excellent set of strange core mechanics that work well together, and the soundtrack is a solid 10. It has some lovely nods to classic gaming of my youth, and a few on-brand self digs at game developer culture to boot.There's probably a load of Ben There, Dan That references I'm not getting, aren't there... maybe time to play that one, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my high expectations. Funniest game I've played in years! _childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This is excellent! I'm revising my review from "great" to just "pure brilliant possibly GOTY". Great character interactions, fun platforming and adventure in one game, very amusing dialogue, lovely music and graphics. Size Five Games - please don't let this be the last Ben & Dan adventure, it's so good.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, here's the thing - it's a damn good puzzle game. There are three specific puzzles that are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clever I can't even begin to imagine how they were devised, and when you solve them you'll feel like a genius AND be laughing out loud. The dialogue is brilliant - nobody else has come close to nailing the dry banter of Lucasarts at their peak, but the Dan and Ben games do it effortlessly. The art and audio is lovely, it is Dan and Ben at their best. BUT... It is also a platformer. It is not a great platformer. It makes fun of indie platformers and their tediousness, but then it does exactly what they do, except not as well. I almost gave up on two separate occasions because of the platforming, but I stayed because the rest of the game is so charming. If you love adventure games, this is a really, really good one, just grit your teeth through the fiddly jumping through spikes while gravity is reversed bits.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: The boys are back! But now they're old men and ready for some pointing-and-clicking combined with new fangled platforming-with-feelings.LotCG is funny and challenging. There are some platforming sections which made me do all the swears, but I made it through. Another great game in the Ben and Dan trilogy.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Rampant silliness! Subtle jokes! Unsubtle jokes! Single entendres! Even worse puns and puzzles than Ben There, Dan That and Time Gentlemen Please! Platforming! Adventuring! Smug hipsterism! Jokes at the expense of Ben! Jokes at the expense of Dan! Jokes at the expense of the entire genres of platforming and adventuring! Pointing *and* clicking! Jumping *and* doublejumping! Probably wallrunning, though I've not got to that yet! Gravity *and* the other gravity! Large hands! Large hair! Proper inventory management the way mother used to make it! Full bladders! Empty bladders! Bladder fluid level management! Rifts in space and time! Giant monsters! Probably a clockwork god, unless they're faking us all out!Who could ask for more? The band is back together and better than ever. Also Dan is extremely lovely to send bug reports to and hasn't told me to go away even once. Play this game. You'll probably love it. If you don't you can go back to playing CoD and shouting at twelve year olds.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: Good and fairly unique game which mixes platforming with point'n'click mechanics. The game is well designed, and has some really funny and clever moments. I can recommend it at full price as it lasted a good long while and made me laugh out loud a bunch of times.My only criticism would be that the platforming controls are a little frustrating in places, but not enough to put me off finishing the game and recommending it to others.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic mix of point & click and platforming. Some of the most absurd conversations and situations I've ever heard or had to deal with in a video game with genuinely laugh out loud moments and conversations. AND A FREE VISUAL NOVEL? WEIRD. The bugs only added to the game to be honest. Would recommend for the humour alone, but the cleverness of the overall vision and game play make it a definite play. Admittedly some of the platforming had me a but miffed at points, but those moments are few and far between.
_childDocuments_.name: Lair of the Clockwork God

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me feel very sad. See, I'm unfortunate enough to enjoy both adventure type game, and platformy type games, and so I find I'm really enjoying both aspects of this game, which combines both effortlessly. I feel I've missed a trick, as the more I play, the more I see that you're supposed to like one or the other, and you need to play this game with that one friend in your life who enjoys all the stuff you don't, so you can pass the controller back and forth, and maybe in the process form a lifelong bond of friendship that may or may not result in the two of you producing a game with some very on the nose meta commentary of gaming in general.But no. Not for me. I will just have to channel my efforts into producing a game about being alone. Maybe...maybe it could be called something like...Matty was alone? Yes, that seems like a plan.Edit: now done, still good! And I had to remove an inadvertent spoiler. Damn, I'm good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first adventure game I've ever played, but from what I've heard about them they're puzzle-y and pointy and clicky, which this is. The puzzles make me feel stupid, which I think means they're good puzzles?I don't like platformers much, and I don't like the platforming in this game because the camera is locked tight to the character and moves with him when he jumps, which can be jarring.I do enjoy humor, though. Oh wait, sorry--*humour*. Gotta get with the British spellings. The jokes are there on almost every line. I think British people would say the jokes are "brillo". Overall I'd say like an 8.5/10, you should buy it for the jokes alone.TL;DR: This review's not long, don't be lazy.

And you have to run all over the island arsing about with the pipe network?I also don't really go in for indie platformers especially the really famous one where the twist is that women obviously don't want to talk to you even if your writing is bad on purpose. _childDocuments_.review: Been a fan of adventure games since the old days and a fan of indie-darling platformers since they became a thing, so I was looking forward to see how a mash-up of the two would play out. I... was not prepared for what I got. This game is a trip, with some absolutely mind-bending conceptual set-pieces and amazing unpredictable humour. Several times this game has utterly astounded me with how far the creators were willing to go for a joke (pretty far).The game is currently a little bit rough around the edges, with some unfortunate glitches that are apparently being worked on. Seriously stop reading and buy.This is a brilliant game.  One that while being devilishly funny also manages to be a send up of the entire video game community, from AAA titles on down to indies.  It also somehow manages to combine a platformer with point-and-click adventure titles.  Trust me, it makes sense once you play it.The sound, music, and visuals are all there, with music so good it took me by surprise.Really give this one a go, and if you like it, pick up some of Size Five's other adventure titles while you're at it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a confluence. The old colliding with the new and neither making it out unscathed. _childDocuments_.review: Combining old-school point-and-click mechanics with a platformer has turned out to be one of the most enjoyable and surprising innovations. _childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan classic point-and-click adventures, but don't have the time for them anymore? (if you do still have time for them, that's fine too!) name: Conan Chop Chop
detailed_description: Enter the Wrath-a-Thon, a fiendish challenge created by the evil sorcerer Thoth-Amon to trap the heroes of Hyboria. Crush, kill and maim your enemies with an arsenal of savage weapons as you and your friends take on the minions of evil. Upgrade your village, upgrade your skills and upgrade yourself (seriously, this game will make you a better person). Conan Chop Chop is the most epic and realistic stick figure game ever to be set in the world of Conan the Barbarian. Discover a delightfully savage world full of epic boss fights, perilous dungeons, and endless amounts of loot and item combinations. While you can choose to save the world solo, Conan Chop Chop really puts the party in 'party game' when you step into its multiplayer mayhem. Featuring 1-4 player online and couch co-op, you can choose to play by yourself, with friends, or random people as you save the world from damnation. Want to get up close and personal, or shoot your opponents from afar? Choose from a cast consisting of the most famous heroes in Hyboria, from the sword-swinging Conan to the bow-bending Bêlit. Chop, shoot, or simply blast your foes into tiny bits. In Conan Chop Chop, what kills you also makes you stronger. Use the experience you earn from each run to unlock character-specific perks and abilities to conquer the enemies that defeated you. Build the skill tree for each one of the characters and discover their unique builds. Acquire new skills as you venture to the far reaches of the world, looting magical charms, weapons, and armors. Experiment with different item combinations to discover potentially overpowered abilities and new ways to play. No two runs through Conan Chop Chop are the same, thanks to procedurally generated maps and dungeon layouts. Discover new shops, challenges and treasures with every playthrough. Test your might against unique dungeon bosses, such as The Giant Sand Worm of Koth and The Frost Giant of Vanaheim. Some bosses may even roam the wilderness, guarding golden chests, powerful artifacts, and other riches.

_childDocuments_.review: Played with keyboard/mouse and with 3 other players, very fun game, it's responsive and there's room for creativity in the way you build your character for your run. If you manage to get a weapon and charm that have synergy then you can do much more damage and get more buffs for your character. The enemies all have a prompt that shows you when they are attacking and once you learn their patterns, you will have a good time.  I personally think the default controls are pretty good but it would still be nice if there was button mapping available (they might add it in later?) It's a bit hard to tell what are enemies and what are your allies in co-op, especially when there's pets involved as well, so i think an option to make your allies all one colour (e.g blue) and your enemies all one colour (e.g red) would be beneficial.
