_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is a great time. Great gameplay with an even greater soundtrack.There is however one massive issue that needs to be said: What you see in the demo is largely what you get, but they put in a valiant effort working with what they had. Likely because they spared no expense getting big name artists to make songs specifically for this game. For that, and because the gameplay is so good, I'll give them a pass on where it falls short.So what do I mean?--I have 5 hours in this game and I have completed all of the campaign and the bonus challenges. All there is left to do is replay levels and try for a higher leaderboard score. Which I will probably do. --I think only one new enemy is introduced beyond what you see in the demo. They do introduce variants of the existing enemies, which do a good job shaking up gameplay.--This is the same for the level bosses. All of them are the Aspect you fight in the demo (save for the last); they look the same and have one similar main loop. Again however, they did a good job making each of these a completely different fight in terms of arena and how they attack. Still, it leaves something to be desired.--After completing each level you unlock three challenge arena modes for that level. These give you perk unlocks, give interesting new gameplay twists, are fun.. And are absolutely padding to bump how much content is in the game.--The story is not completely resolved. They intend to continue it. No idea if this means new game or just DLC.So all of that with a $30 price, what does that tell me? That they need to break even with their spending on the music.Still... I'm typically fairly harsh as a reviewer thats quick to give a negative. So why am I giving this a positive review?It's really fun.It's got fast FPS gameplay like doom but without the burnout, and a soundtrack that makes doom look bad.No bugs.No monetization.It's just a good game, and a damn good game for a metalhead.  \m/

_childDocuments_.review: Rating - Absolute Banger/10TL:DR review - Like Metal? Like Doom? Like headbanging on beats? Not tone deaf? Then buy this right now.Pros:-1.) Music :- Each track is a banger.2.) Gameplay :- This isn't really a shooter. This is a rythm game disguised as a shooter. If you are tone deafor if you have a hard time tuning to beats, you are going to have a less than fun time in this game(unless you play on easy mode).You basically perform actions on the beats and shoot on the beats and you can increase your damage multiplier this way.3.) Vibe:- Most weapons and how they feel with the music is very tight. Incredible job integrating such nice rythm mechanics in a demon shooter. 4.) Fun factor :- Off the bloody charts.Cons:-1.) The last 2 weapons that you unlock don't really have the same "ooompf" to the music and feedback as the other weapons like the shotgun, the pistols etc. The shotgun is easily the best weapon to jam to the music. The pistols are pretty epic too.2.) The songs are nice but they are all in beats of 4. like 1-2-3-4, 1-2-3-4. This works in terms of gameplay since this makes the gamemore accessible/less difficult. but it would have been nice to have different beat mixups in triplets/etc. But I totally understand whythey didn't go that way yet and focused more on polishing the existing levels to the music in beats of 4.Overall, very very fun experience. Takes around 6-7 hours to beat and it feels like 30 minutes since its so fast paced and fun. Alsobecause you are too busy jamming out to the music and enjoying yourself to notice the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger is my first ever rhythm FPS game and let me just say, I'm impressed with how much these two genres blend together when done right. Although there are very few of them, I can see why this one is rated so highly out of both Bullets Per Minute and this (the only other one I know really).While short and sweet, with the exception of the Horde Mode of course, Metal: Hellsinger is an exceptional rhythm FPS game and a game that is the golden standard for these kinds of shooters. Couple that with a killer soundtrack and you'll be having the best time of your life, even if it's just for a few hours. If you love heavy metal, DOOM and boomer shooters, get this game. Thank you Outsiders for this amazing game, I hope there's more in store for us after the VR version comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: After doing BPM 100% I was extremely happy to get this game in a bundle, played it right away. Metal: Hellsinger is a solid rhythm shooter and the collabs for the metal songs are amazing, they seem to be adding more too. Modding to add your own songs is possible if you so wish. The arenas themselves are fine, the movement and the gameplay loop resemble the Doom dance, about the weapon arsenal I have to admit that some weapons felt way more natural for me to use in a rhythm context than others. Sadly the monsters don't make much noise so you have to keep moving at all times else you risk getting shotgunned to death and you'll never know until it's too late. Speaking about micromanaging your streak, the monsters and also shooting on beat it can get overwhelming sometimes especially if you have to play with a weapon that you don't really like (for challenges).Enemy variety could have been a bit more broad, I get the feeling that I shot the same trash mobs way too many times by now. The boss fights aswell, you fight the same aspect of the judge until the last level though each hell the boss unlocks new mechanics or attack patterns. Story's told through comic book style panels and the voice acting is good for the atmosphere that they are going for. It's a short game as far as the campaign goes, with added challenges to complete and the Leviathan mode (which follows more of a roguelike approach to progression instead of individual levels).Recommended, plus it's a good occasion to find new bands to listen to.

_childDocuments_.review: What if when the Doom music kicks in, so did you?In what I guess is just becoming its own genre, Hellsinger is in the company of BPM: Bullets per Minute and Hi-Fi Rush as an excellent rhythm/action hybrid. As someone who deeply enjoyed BPM, this was just the fix I needed. The gameplay is a bit more forgiving than BPM, but oooh... Just as satisfying.The story actually surprised me in that there is one. Narrated by Troy Baker as Paz, a talking skull with a smooth accent and no memory, the story managed to do juuust enough to transcend the bog-standard "Kill demons, kill more demons, then finally kill Satan" plot it first appears to be. Even when I thought that was all it would be, the sexy narration and charmingly simple cutscenes were still kinda doing it for me.Not that the game even needs much in story, as the pick-up-and-game style feels more at home in an arcade than a theater. Here, gameplay and soundtrack are king, and Hellsinger knows it.The music rocks, as should be no surprise, though I hope you like metal, as the soundtrack only barely transcends the genre of its namesake. Though if metal isn't your cup of tea and you bought the game with a demon glaring over the title "METAL: HELLSINGER", I do question your purchasing wisdom.Lucky for me, I do at least somewhat enjoy a thumping jam, and this game brings it. I'm no metalhead, but really anything with a solid beat would still be fun, and there a few songs in the soundtrack that even I as a filthy casual greatly enjoyed.The only negative notes I have are glorified nitpicks.The guns are pretty hit and miss.The first four work great. You start with a sword and a simple semi-automatic projectile weapon to learn the beat matching mechanics, and they each have unique strengths enough to remain relevant for most of the game. Next are a shotgun and akimbo revolvers. These are awesome. Satisfying, effective and intuitive.The last two (in the base game at least, I haven't tried the DLC) I feel very different about.First is something that seems like it should be good. A long range precision explosive crossbow. But it doesn't deal that much damage, so its use is more for mopping up hoards of smaller weaker enemies. But it only has two shots before needing a reload, which is the longest reload in the game (and is one of the few actions that feels off-beat, unless you nail the active reload). At the damage it does, it needed to have a lot more shots to be useful, or if you're dead set on only two, please give it some oomph. This crossbow had all the reload speed and explosive power of a water balloon launcher.The last weapon is a pair of boomerangs. Which aren't quite as terrible as they at least deal decent damage and can cut through multiple enemies. However, they are fairly close range and are easily surpassed in high single target damage by the revolvers or shotgun. Their flight path is too difficult to track to use in any way beyond occasional accidental extra corpses near your intended target.So yeah, bit of a bummer that after a certain point there's really no reason to try any other weapons beyond tried and true shotgun and revolvers.The challenge trials are fine I guess. Some feel pretty impossible, or arbitrarily testing skills that have little to do with the primary gameplay loop, but eh, better than nothing I guess.Don't let those two tiny little vestigial nubs hanging off this gem like skin tags hiding under the armpit of a supermodel stop you from taking it on the town. You'll only be in a position to notice if you've already gotten close enough that you're committed, and it's easy to overlook anyway. TL;DRFun gameplay, 70% good weapons, rockin' soundtrack make great game. If you liked BPM, you'll like this. If you liked Hi-Fi Rush, but wish it were more like Doom, you'll really like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game blows bullets per minute out of the water in every single way except for replayability. Two things to keep in mind; the game is short, about 5-6 hours of gameplay, and there is very little replay value besides trying to get high scores/replaying on a harder difficulty. Its a very satisfying 5-6 hours though. For the price you are definitely getting big bang for your buck. _childDocuments_.review: I plan on editing my review once I 100% the game but already from the start it feels like the developers put the best parts about all fps games over the years and just cut all the fluff. The closest i've got to the high BPM gave me in years and it just makes sense that these arena shooters have a rhythm component because WHY NOT it just adds a whole other layer to that satisfying aspect that we all crave from blowing demons up. WIll give a detailed review later but this game and the devs deserve the positive review especially early in the release when people are considering getting it most. Took me around 10 hours to 100% the game on the hardest difficulty (which isn't even necessary to getting all achievements.) I stand by my original statement in recommending this game to any fans of rhythm games or arena shooters! There was never a dull moment even though some waves felt a little long and on the highest difficulty you could spend 15 minutes just to die at the boss with no checkpoints. This is one of the only games where I would hit that restart button just due to the core gameplay loop just being tons of fun. Unknown is just fun to control and the weapons each have their own little quirk to them. At times with my loadout I would opt towards a certain weapon simply cause it was more enjoyable to use for the mission since all of them were pretty well balanced. It's important to note that personally I don't listen to any rock, punk, or metal and still thoroughly enjoyed and could tell the amount of love that went into the music and none the less made me feel like a badass the whole time. This game scratches all the itches I get from playing through all the new blood franchise and even titles like Boomerang X or BPM which have always left me wanting more. 10/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Update:It took me 21 hours to beat on Brutal difficulty. By the end, I was ready for it to be over because I don't think the game was balanced for this difficulty. For the very last mission, I switched to Goat difficulty because it was already starting to wear me down and then I got to the final boss and died within seconds. It feels like this mode was intended to be played once you're already familiar with the boss fights (which makes it odd since it's offered right away—unlike the new 4th difficulty). Some of the mini-missions were especially frustrating on brutal.All-in-all, I'd still recommend it. I do wish they'd have balanced the difficulties a little more because there's an ocean between Goat and Brutal. You can either breeze through it on Goat or suffer pretty hard through Brutal. Most of the time, it's not too bad. It only feels really unfair when the boss does enough damage to kill you within 5 seconds and you don't get a chance to learn the fight. But, some bosses I one-shot on Brutal. So, again, difficulty balancing is really my only complaint. The music is rad. The weapons feel pretty fun. Nothing ground-breaking, but it's a good time if you enjoy metal and shooters.Original Review: If you love metal, buy this... As everyone else has already said, the songs are absolutely incredible! I was literally dripping sweat as I played the first level (and I never do that). I've seen some people complain that's it's too short. I've been playing for 8 hours and I'm only 30% of the way through. I'm not practiced with the beat-based genre and I'm playing on the hardest difficulty "Beast." On this difficulty, you can't die so every mission is a one-shot gauntlet. On the medium difficulty "Goat," you can respawn twice and I can absolutely see how that would trivialize the game for many people, so I'd recommend playing on "Beast" difficulty if you want the stretch the game out and enjoy a good challenge.It really feels like there should be another difficulty between Beast and Goat because the difficulty spike is pretty intense.Fun is subjective though, so play however you want. The nice thing is that you can easily change the difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted that game when the first second of the first trailer came out.That is the first time in a while i was hyped and wasn't betrayed on release, Metal : Hellsinger delivers on its promesses.This isn't Doom Eternal, this isn't a AAA game, but it feels like a genuine love letter to FPS and Metal fans.Gameplay is brutal and fast, music is obviously amazing since that's the selling point, and the fact you have to play "well" in order to hear the entirety of the track, it just adds so much to the epicness of the fights.I wasn't expecting any story to be honest, and was surprised that it was actually pretty cool, the ending leaves you to want more, and i hope for The Outsiders that the game succeeds enough so that they can plan a sequel of this little gem.The game has a few flaws that aren't critical but still noticeable :- Bestiary is the same with variations, same for the bosses, some might find it cheap.- It lacks a few more weapons to unlock, not sure what kind of weapon but i felt like it was missing something.- There is a difficulty peek after the 2 thirds of the game, you can lower the difficulty at any point, but some players might find it frustrating to hit that wall.However, it is still a lot of fun.After unlocking every weapons i now want to restart the game from the first level and beat my highest score.

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda just a 'big' budget experiment and it's not really good tbh.The sound design is good, the music is fine too, but outside of that it doesn't do anything particularly well for me to recommend any of it.The combat ranges from "200 cannon fodder enemies get one hit by you" to "haha heres 400 projectiles and area damage with no clear telegraphing so youll take damage alright" all the while you gotta stay on beat and generally move around the arena. It's a lot at once thrown at you with very sloppy visuals.Like 90% of this game is orangey-brown. Enemies, the environment, everything. It quickly becomes very mushy and eh i am not a fan.Kinda spoilery? The bosses are like all the same with one annoying thing switching out between encounters. Shoot the boss, kill the weak enemies that waste your time, then shoot the boss some more. Incredible. The level of danger from each boss is very arbitrary? some you just kinda run in circles without taking damage and thats it, some have random invisible-feeling attacks that come from outside your field of view that chunk you for a third of your health, and nope not fun.In general suffers from the same issues as BPM, just because the concept of "DOOM, but youre forced to shoot with the beat of the music that plays" is fundamentally just very flawed? And worse than in BPM, except for the sword, sub-divisions of the 4/4 beat just do not exist at all in this game. Which for a rhythm game... is very disappointing. If I wanna shoot 3 8ths in a row, i should be able to do that with proper timing, rather than be forced to do 3 4th beats. It's a super arbitrary restriction that just makes the game worse.Story exists in this. The narration is... very... mediocre? It's not bad, not good, it's very predictable, generally uninteresting, but not bad enough for me to skip it, so i end up sitting through something i have no investment in with the cutscenes. the funny numbers:audio 8/10gameplay: 5/10story: 3/10overall enjoyment: 4/10Can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game costs $30 and only has 5hours of content.. this is an unacceptably low amount of content, for $30. Even a game like Titanfall 2, which has a notoriously short campaign, will give you 7hours of playtime for $30... and if you were to compare the graphics, gunplay, voice acting & story of this game with Titanfall 2, then Titanfall 2 absolutely obliterates this game... the only aspect where this game is superior, is the music.Cons:  The game freezes when you alt+tab The reload time on some of the guns is 4seconds+ You're given zero information regarding the difficulty settings Enemies spawn directly next to you The amount of content is tiny and you can complete the game in 5hours easily, with no replayability. You do 30dmg to an enemy when hitting it off-beat, and 120dmg when on-beat... this essentially forces you to hit all enemies on the beat, ALL the time. Forcing the player to play the game a certain way, or else they suffer a 400% damage decrease is bad. I wouldn't mind it if you dealt 50% less damage when hitting something off-beat, but 400% less damage is just unacceptable. You can play the game with cheats, which disables the off-beat mechanic partially, but that just makes the game feel trivial instead. The environmental detail is poor. It's very obvious that they spunked their entire budget on the music and the character detail (which are both great) and then left nothing for the finer details, like the environment. The regional pricing is terrible and the game is available in ruzziaThe game isn't bad, but it just doesn't justify a $30 pricetag. When you compare it to similar games like DOOM, Serious Sam, Bulletstorm, Titanfall2, etc. then you realize just how overpriced this game is, because the other games provide far more content (of equal or greater quality) for the same amount of money (DOOM is $10 more & Serious Sam is $10 less). The only thing this game has going for it, is the music, and if you're OK paying $30 for a game that has top-tier music but second-rate gameplay, then have at it... I myself would rather replay Bulletstorm or Titanfall2.For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games: My first impressions review:

_childDocuments_.review: Word of warning: despite the great looks and the stellar soundtrack (if you like metal), the game isn't for everyone. To get the most damage, highest scores and the most fun out of the game, you should be able to keep a rhythm - for quite a while :PWhile there is an easy difficulty, that is more forgiving with timing and faster combo meter, you still will have to move and keep a steady clicking pace for several minutes per level. This can be kinda straining. Best to try the demo first, if you're uncertain.The execution is excellent. Before you start, you can calibrate both sound and graphics for hardware (and your reaction time latency). Graphics aren''t too demanding but still looking great, it's one of those games which convince more with art style than with high-tech features. For an Unity game it runs surprisingly smooth, I get 90-100 FPS with Ultra settings @2K with DLDSR 2.25 (4K), no terrible hick-ups so far.The gameplay is very skill-orientated, this makes it fun to replay as your expertise grows over time and you learn more and more combos aswell as some perks to improve your former runs.Sound and music are excellent and the most prominent feature of the game. An outstanding narrator (a talking skuil, voiced by the Texan Troy Baker - you might know him best as Sam Drake from Uncharted 4) leads you through the story, music's building up dynamically to your combo score. First some steady beats from the rhythm section, then the lead guitar and at max of 16x bonus vocals and the full sound set in. You will notice immediately when you drop down in combos (for being hit, attacking out of rhythm too often etc.) and want that awesome song back! When your health gets too low, sound becomes dull (like hearing underwater).Boss fights are increasingly wild. Wear-down attacks, bullet hell sections, strong attacks, some trash mobs in-between to replenish health, combo and ammo. It's hard but fair. The most challenging part is combining your weapons while keeping the beat. Guns have different firerates, reload times (you can reduce them with timed reload prompts) and ultimates that are suited for different situations. Add in some well timed dodges and weapon swaps for special combos and you get a frenzied ballet of blades and bullets.To make things a bit easier, every finished level unlocks three torments, special, small challenge stages to get sigils (perks like losing combo counter to a certain level only, damage boost on timed kills etc.).The game codex not only offers all tutorial tips and a bestiary of all enemies encountered, it also holds all songs, cutscenes and narration segments.A lot of love went into this game and there's little to wish for (but more in the future).my system specs:i7-8700k, 32 GB, RTX 3080ti, Soundblaster Z

_childDocuments_.review: I thought that it couldn't get any better than the music music and gun play of Doom or the rhythm shooting of BPM, but here we are. A beautiful combination of both concepts and I am here for it.Its a beautiful game that plays really well with great combat however, I did find it easier to keep to the beat in BPM as the guns and their reloads seemed to play into the music, they were part of it its orchestra. In Hellsinger its important as it affects your score and damage output, but where I found myself shooting and reloading when I didn't have to in BPM because the sounds were intoxicating and I like making the music, that is absent from here. I go to the beat for the game's sake but it isn't necessary. I think that this could be changed by making the sounds of the weapons and executions louder and more prominent, as the game's music seems the compete with them or drown them out entirely instead of complimenting them as a rhythm game like BPM did. Definitely recommended as the gameplay is solid and I like having a story to play through, I just wish they would make that one small change.

_childDocuments_.review: OK so this is a hard review to write. The game is awesome. I love metal music and this game hits hard like the next Fit For An Autopsy album. Fast pace and powerful like the Doom Slayer in Doom Eternal. Cool looking game too. The music aspect of the game is great. Its cool to feel the game be your instrument as you slay your way through a death metal album. So thats why I give it a recommend. Now as a fan of FPS and high difficulty scale games like Sekiro and Elden Ring...... I have to give this a  negative mark. And its mainly because of the scaling of the game and the difficulty options. These I find very pour. I always play my games at the hardest difficulty and thats because thats where i feel the game really demands you to play by its terms and this game does do that. The hardest difficulty throws way more demons at you and ramps up the game play. But it has this annoying no check point thing. So if you get all the way to a boss fight and die to the boss all the way at the end of his health bar, you are stuck starting the level all the way over again. And ok lets say you dont like that so you decide to go down a difficulty level. Well now you arent seeing some of those cool enemies that really demand a lot of attention once they hit the floor, making the game feel very dry and boring. I feel like if they had added a extra difficulty level being hard with checkpoints and then a hard without checkpoints that would help with the game feeling to boring at the normal level and too hard and annoying to start over and over again at the higher level. I want the game to be hard and check me but its too repetitive to start the whole level again and hearing the same song over and over again for an hour because you are having a hard time with a boss fight. And im sorry this boss that shoots seeking balls of fire everywhere as a last stand move is very annoying. Other than that I absolutely love the game and would give it a 10/10 if it wasnt for the difficulty issue

_childDocuments_.review: Alright i don't really know where to begin here. i completed the whole game in 5.3 hours acording to steam, so let's go through my experience with the game.First of all to me the combat felt really good, the wepons had weight to them and the sound design for the guns reflect the weight, all the animations for them was very nice. dashing and evading enemy attacks was easy enough and felt really smooth when doing itJust as a footnote since i'm by no means an expert on graphics or stuff like it i must say that the game overall hold a very high quality in this regardSecondly the level design was nice and well thought through (maybe a bit too linear for my taste but oh well) and the devs was really generous with the amount of combo boosters and damage boosters around the maps.Thirdly the sound track. well the game features almost all of my favorite metal artists and the music each of them got is a blend between their own music style the games which complements the two parts perfectly. To me this game has one of the best soundtracks that i have ever heard though i am biased towards it since i am a metalheadSo overall this is a very high quality game with great gunplay and awesome soundtrack, so now maybe you would like to ask well is there anything wrong with it? well let me answer that question The boss design are very lazy, it's the same boss through all the levels but with a different head except for the last one wich was a really cool boss fight in my eyes.narratively the game is a bit lacking, there could have been a lot more of worldbuilding and lore to really get a good grip on what the story is about, the only explenation you really get is that the main character got her voice stolen by the red judge (aka the devil) this is in broad strockes what the narrative is to avoid to many spoilers. when the game is completed and you expect to get your voice back it really ends on a clifhanger, since ofc it wouldn't be that simple, you only got part of your voice and the other part is in heaven. I found this a bit strange since they could have started the narrative with that instead of waiting to the end of the game to tell the player, that only led to confusion for me at least though i get what why they did it if they are planing a second game that is but it felt like lazy writing, there really was a good chance in the beginning to get the player completly drawn into the story if they had given the player the whole picture on why you actually do all the thing in hell that you do, they should also have fleshed out the profecy of the Hellsinger way more since it is you. I would have loved to know more about it to fully understand what the main character is and what her purpous is.Take the doom games for example you know what you are, you are the doomslayer and hell itself is afraid of you because you have the power of a god, you are an imortal warrior that is fuled by your hate for hell and all the demons within and you have been waging an unending war until you where captured you waited millenia until one day your cage was broken and your war started again.the last thing i have to say about Metalhellsinger is that the game is short, unbelivebly short, the game is priced at 29.99 euro and i suspect i know why the game is so expensive even thoguh it's only 5 hours long. I do suspect that the price that has been decided is beacuse of the artist they hired, these are heavyhitters in the music industry (when it comes to metal at least) so in a sense i guess you pay more for the music than for the game itself.so what is my final verdict. Well i do recommend the game but that's also because of my biase, as a metal head it feels like i have a game that is made speciffically for me. but for all of the other humans on this world that isn't interested in the music itself but the gameplay, well like i said in the beggining of this review the game runs like a dream with very satisfying gameplay and nice graphics together with a well thought through level design. Though since it is such a short game i would wait for a sale. i payed full price for it and feel a bit cheated to be honest since i expected more content but i do like it. hope this rant helps.

_childDocuments_.review: A Rocking Concept, But Lacking ExecutionWhile Metal: Hellsinger certainly deserves credit for trying something different in the rhythm-shooter genre, it ultimately fails to deliver a satisfying experience. The concept of combining fast-paced first-person shooting with rhythm mechanics is intriguing, and I admire the ambition behind it. Unfortunately, the novelty wears off quickly, leaving behind a repetitive and tedious gameplay loop.The game's central "play to the beat" mechanic, which seems like a fun twist at first, becomes more of a chore the longer you play. The constant pressure to time your actions perfectly with the music's rhythm quickly turns from a thrilling challenge to a frustrating restriction. Instead of feeling like an immersive, fast-paced battle, it often feels like you're being forced to conform to an arbitrary beat, which is far less engaging than it sounds.Additionally, while the soundtrack is packed with talented artists and a mix of heavy metal tracks, it doesn't save the game from becoming monotonous. The music blends into the background after a while, and the lack of variation in the gameplay doesn't help in making each stage feel distinct.Visually, the game is solid, but the overall design and mechanics don't do justice to its artistic potential. There's a lack of depth in the level design, and the enemies, while appropriately chaotic, quickly become predictable. Despite the overwhelming positive reviews from others, I just couldn't find the fun in this game. The concept was great, but the execution left much to be desired.In the end, Metal: Hellsinger feels more like a one-note gimmick rather than a fully realized experience. It's worth a shot for fans of rhythm games or heavy metal music, but for most players, it simply isn't fun enough to justify its full price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: haven't even technically finished the game as of the time im writing this. maybe its just cause im a metal head who has a passion for rhythm games and loves the doom series, but i think this game is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I havent really found myself playing almost any video games for a while, which left me feeling kinda weird, but this game reignited my passion for them as a whole. i rarely play anything for more than an hour at a time anymore, but i played this game for 6 hours straight yesterday. hellsinger has easily cracked my top 5 favorite games of all time because of almost every aspect included within the game. whether it be the immersive and synergistic combination of game play and soundtrack, the fantastic way the music interacts with the multiplier system, the goofy references to metal classics littered about, the gradual - yet firm - skill curve presented throughout the game, there is just so much to be said about how well executed the making of this game was, and i dont think ill even be able to cover it all. im a pretty intense rager. ill rage at just about anything, however this game has is just feels fair. i havent raged a single time in the 20+ hours ive sunken in so far. i do have a few nitpicks, for instance: the lack of creativity with bosses. they're all just kinda the same. there are also a few bugs sprinkled here and there, but theyre sparse enough not to cause too much of a problem. and lastly, if this can even be counted as a critique, theres just not enough content. this game is so good that i think one of the few things wrong with it is that theres just not enough of it for me. even 100%ing it just isnt enough. i know theres dlc, and we'll see if there's more to come, but im already interested in a sequel. anyway, ramble over, hellsinger truly is worth a play if you havent dug in already.

_childDocuments_.review: I won this game through SteamGifts.I played it for Pay or Play 2nd Cycle of 2024 and it was picked for me by Escollo.Metal: Hellsinger is a rhythm based FPS game where you need to fire, reload, dodge, murder and mayhem to the beat of the soundtrack. It is really a lovely game, with amazing gameplay and smooth experience even for those of us who suck at rhythm based games.In the game you play as The Unknown, who has lost her voice to The Judge, and her journey is narrated by this skull, who you can also use as a weapon on your journey. She wants her voice back, and she's going to get it by force. The story was pretty good, I do think there was some things that could have been better, and I feel like the game doesn't shine in this aspect, but it was not bad at all.Many reviews on steam say that it's basically a really awesome album that comes with a free game attached. That's a pretty accurate statement in my opinion. The soundtrack is absolutely a banger and I really, really, really, REALLY need it to come to spotify. I am still hopeful, even after all this time since release.I played the game on the easiest difficulty and with the "always on beat" setting, because I remembered playing the demo when it was about to release and having rage quitted it, because I just couldn't do it. It's not you, it's me situation lmao. I can't do rhythm games, but this was absolutely one of those games that I had to experience myself.Now, I know i've talked about the game already a lot, but let me just say, the final battle with my favorite song from the soundtrack, No Tomorrow (featuring Serj Tankian), was SO GOOD! Like, the song makes it 100x times more amazing and cool. It's just so beautiful. I loved every second of this.It's definitely a game I'd recommend for anyone who enjoys rhythm based games, and FPS games similar to DOOM. It is absolutely worth every penny it costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It is theoretically made specifically for me. I play guitar and drums an unhealthy amount, and I exclusively play metal, I also play a absolute ♥♥♥♥ load of rhythm games from guitar/clone hero to beat saber I have been playing rhythm games since I was 12, and I love arena based shooters, I have at least a hundred hours in ultrakill and probably two hundred in doom 2016+eternal, not to mention I basically grew up playing classic doom mods on my laptop. So why do I not love this game, keep in mind I dont think its bad, pretty average really 5/10, its just not deserving of the 98% it has currently. Why? Well let me break it downA: The movement is complete trash. Sorry not sorry they really need to go back to the drawing board on this. You need evidence? The #1 movement tech in the entire game “soaring” that is basically the only thing you can do to gain any speed. Yeah that… basically no one uses it, only 24% of players have the achievement that you get for soaring 100 times (To put that in perspective I got that on the second level because I actually try to use movement). The movement system is so ♥♥♥♥ that 76% of players literally dont even engage with it. The only movement combo “Devils flight” Is probably the most janky thing ever. You do it by soaring and then dashing, but if you use your double jump first before dashing it doesnt work, and to make things worse double jumping completely removes all momentum from soaring. Also Soaring is extremely inconsistent, no matter what I do I seem to randomly fail it 20% of the time, keep in mind I am the type of person who knows how to do every single movement tech in ultrakill extremely consistently. To put that in perspective I can perform a glitched movement tech that involves pressing 3 buttons frame perfectly MORE CONSISTENTLY THEN A INTENDED MOVEMENT TECHNIQUE. The game also has no form of anything that would allow you to hold momentum, you get a dash jump and thats it. Thats not horrible I guess, there are games with less, but this is extremely below average. The dash also serves as the doge in the game, however the dash is best when performed on beat, and the enemies don't attack on beat… You can see where this is going, basically if something is attacking you off beat lol get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ you just cant doge it as effectively. B: Weapons. They are poorly thought out to say the least. The skull is useless except for the ultimate, the shotgun is fine but is out classed in ranged damage by the pistols and in crowd control by the crossbow. The boomerangs are just… Pointless, they don't do anything that the pistol or crossbow dont. Its the last weapon you get and it just doesn't add anything. Really the crossbow is massively overpowered, as long as you can reload on beat you have a fire rate almost equal to the pistols with a explosive that has a massive AOE. It really just seems the pistols and crossbow are the only weapons really worth using if you want optimal damage output. The pistols also completely out class the skull in everything but ultimate, and the crossbow entirely out classes the sword in terms of crowd control. C: The game play in general is slow and doesn't reward you for being aggressive. For the most part you are best suited standing a solid 20 feet away from anything you are fighting. Enemies don't really telegraph attacks amazingly, mostly due to the lack of sound ques for their attacks and they have perfect predictive aiming so you just need to keep your distance and doge attacks as they come to you. All your weapons including the sword have a very long effective range so you're not even punished for keeping your distance. Oh and your execution that is supposed to reward you for being aggressive has near infinite range on most maps. I only once ran into a situation where I actually had to close the distance to perform an execution. So the only thing that is supposed to reward you for closing the distance can be done from miles away with little commitment or risk since you can just immediately jump away after doing it and you are entirely invulnerable in the dash in and during the execution. D: The game is just slow. Why? Because the music is slow. I dont know why they decided the music needs to be like 120bpm but yeah most of the music is 120bpm (Granted I havent actually measured every song but the first 3 are 120). Thats fine for some music of course and is standard in a lot of genres. But it doesn't exactly lead to the heart pounding “gonna rip your head off” type gameplay. It would probably be alot more fun if all the music was closer to 160 or 180. Right now it feels like I need to actively slow down my gameplay inorder to stay on beat. And I dont know about you but the music holding me back is the exact opposite of the feeling I want. I want to feel forward momentum and a push to go faster! kill more! do stuff! Not “Yeah just hang back and click at a leisurely pace”  E: The music and rhythm game aspects… They were close I think. Very very close to making it something truly special. But currently your gameplay only affects the layers of music that are being played, that's it. You build up until you eventually have vocals. This is okay? I guess. But it is probably the laziest possible way to make a reactive soundtrack. wii Tanks did it better ffs. The only time this is broken is with the sword ultimate, it goes into a breakdown and you get to chug chug at double time. That is fun, honestly the most fun part of the entire game. Just imagine if they actually applied this to the various combos, if devils flight started a trill to allow you to shoot at tripple time, or if a execution caused the music to skip a beat but make the next beat louder and you deal quad damage, or if you get a triple kill it starts a solo and you get to shoot along with it. But no, they just took the laziest way and it kinda feels that way, the music doesn't actually react to your gameplay beyond being a little more intense when you are doing well. It would be cool if it at least reacted to the enemies that are around but it doesn't even do that. There were alot of opportunities to add various interesting rhythm game aspects to it but they didn't. So it just ends up being a metronome simulator. F: The music itself. I'm not going to claim the music is bad, it's quite good and they assembled a really talented group of musicians to make the sound track. The problem is these musicians clearly have not a single clue how to write music for a rhythm game like this. Half the songs have beats that are hard to follow in places. Most dont have any sort of heavy easy to follow beat that you would expect, and with a few songs you have quiet sections that nearly have no beat to follow. This isnt helped at all by the focus on vocals in alot of the songs. Vocals are fun for songs yes, BUT vocals are normally extremely trash at holding a beat by themself with a few exceptions. A song like “Army of the Night” by powerwolf is a great example of a metal song that has vocals that can hold a beat, you can isolate the vocals from that and easily tap along to it without needing to think about it. The songs in this game not so much, I found I would lose beat and have to actively think about the song to get back on beat. To put it simply this is no good. Some may say very no good. The point of music in a game like this is to get you pounding to the beat, it shouldn't be a struggle to stay on beat ever. The bass drum or guitar riff or something should be boosted so loud and hard that you have no choice but to follow the beat. For a game like this you want dance music for lack of a better termSo I dont think I will be finishing this game any time soon. This feels more like a proof of concept then a finished polished game

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Hellsinger shows that combining the best aspects of new era DOOM with the often underrepresented rhythm genre can blend seamlessly and ends up being a fantastic game. After beating it with all challenges completed in around 7 hours I can say this is a title worth buying. Movement and shooting both feel fast and fluid, there are 4 guns to choose from plus your skull and your sword which while a little underwhelming are still enough of a variety to work, and you'll be switching between them constantly to keep up your combos while also using the right tools for the nearest enemies, reloading, and charging specials, and once you get the hang of it its incredibly satisfying to clear encounters without missing a beat. As your combo continues your score multiplier increases, as does the number of instruments, until you max out at 16x and the lyrics come in. Soundtrack is an easy 10/10 standing up with some of my other favorites such as DMC Devil May Cry and Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance. The final boss song including  was an absolutely perfect choice. It is only eight main levels but on the other hand each one has 3 challenges that unlock afterwards for some extra content with fun modifiers such as having weapons change in the middle of combat. My only criticisms that come to mind were that 1.) some enemies can feel a bit spongy on how many hits it takes even while shooting on beat but it's not to an unreasonable degree and 2.) it would have been nice to have a checkpoint between the main part of the final level and the actual boss fight as it can feel like a bullet hell at times and I ended up having to restart from the very beginning of the level on my first 2 tries (about 15 minutes each), and neither issue is enough to be an actual problem. Definitely worth the price of admission and I look forward to seeing any eventual sequel.Update: After 3 more hours I have completed all achievements, absolutely worth it.Update: Nominated for Steam game awards

The narrator / voice of the skull in your hand shouldn't be left unmentioned either, since his witty remarks and pronounced accent carry much of the story and provide some depth to the cool looking but rather pale (mute) protagonist, a kick-ass demon lady without a name.9/10 Would whoop demons' asses to the sound of Alissa White-Gluz again.

And you know what? The story ain’t too bad, either, and is told with an enjoyable amount of style and personality.Metal: Hellsinger, as a whole, is polished, innovative, unpretentious, and most importantly fun, and the industry could certainly use more games like it. _childDocuments_.review: God I really want to recommend this but I can't, and unfortunately the game is getting an insane amount of praise just because the the genre of music is metal, which I feel isn't something to whole-heartedly recommend the game because of.  Y'know, Brutal Legend has a fantastic lineup, and absolutely kills it with it's theme, but the game was an RTS hack'n'slash. Sure I loved it, I love weird genre mashups, but the only reason it's still brought up today is because it has a cult following. But at the very least, let's talk the good, because there is in fact some good stuff in the game.Despite my rambling about people recommending the game purely because of the metal music, I do have to agree that the music is incredibly fantastic, especially the vocals. They did manage to get the core gameplay loop down, and I believe the cutscene artwork fits the metal aesthetic extremely well. I had the music video for Hellraiser by Ozzy Osborne (ft. Lemmy Kilmister) pop into my head when the cutscenes appeared, incredibly similar in style and feel. However, it really stops there. The enemy variety is really bad (especially the bosses at the ends of levels), the arenas and weapons are exceptionally bland. I don't think enemies attack to the beat either, which is extremely important unless I managed to miss it, because the tells for attacks are pretty much non-existent. But let's talk weapons, because you spend the entire game using them.There's only six weapons in total, and you might be thinking that's a lot. It could be if two of the six weapons weren't next to useless. Unfortunately, Paz, your friendly skull, kind of sucks to use, and so do the throw-able swords. There's no real rhyme or reason to use them at all. And your sword requires you to get in close, so why would you do that when all your other options are much better? So that leaves the crossbow, revolvers, and the shotgun. And once you unlock the crossbow and revolvers, there's really no going back. They are by far the best weapons in the game. The crossbow doesn't require you to aim well at all as long as you can hit something near your enemy since it has an AoE attached to it, and the revolvers keep you at range where you should be so you can avoid getting hit. The only reason you would use the other weapons is because of the torments, which are also bland in the long run.By the end of the game you pretty much get cornered into using those two weapons, and by the last two levels, just becomes, well, not fun. I think I read in a different review that this game is the perfect example of a fantastic game executed poorly, and I would have to agree. The music doesn't make up for the shortcomings in variety, not to mention that even its normal difficulty is incredibly easy. I think I died all of one time in the entirety of almost 100%ing the game and it was in one torment challenge where you can't heal at all. The cherry on top is that you get a cliffhanger at the end teasing DLC or a sequel, in which personally sucks and just means you don't even have a complete experience.If I were to give this a comparison, it'd be that this is the RE: Code Veronica of rhythm shooters. Sure, it's... okay? But it's a step down to whatever else is available. In this case, it'd be BPM: Bullets Per Minute, Crypt of the Necrodancer, the upcoming Gun Jam. Even Pistol Whip, the VR game, puts up a decent competition against this and it's technically not even a rhythm game. If they spent another year before release polishing up enemies and weapons, and even the boons you get, to give them an extremely distinct feel and particular use, I feel this would be a much better game. Unfortunately, it's too late. While right now the game sits at overwhelmingly positive, I do feel it's going to drop over time as casual players find their way here. If not, I'll eat my words and shove them back down my throat.Get it on a 50% sale at most if this seems like it's your type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Metal Hellsinger is a fantastic rhythm shooter and is probably the best one out there right now. In my opinion, it's everything that Bullets Per Minute should've been. It has a better atmosphere, a more distinct art style, better music, and tighter mechanics needed of both rhythm and shooter games. Although not everything about this game is necessarily noteworthy, I'll explain later.First, the story is simple. You are a demonette known simply as the "Unknown", and you are on a quest through the several Hell's to regain your voice. Along the way, Troy Baker gives you a comical commentary in a somewhat misplaced, but welcome nonetheless, cowboy demeanor. You have an array of weapons at your disposal to kill the demons you run into in each room ranging from the all-rounder shotgun, precision revolvers, explosive crossbow, and bladed boomerangs, to Troy Baker shooting little fireballs at demons and a sword that used to be a part of a greater demon's scythe. Each weapon has its place in any stage of the game and none feel useless at all, so long as that weapon jives with your playstyle. It pays to experiment and find out what works and what doesn't, as well as the ultimate abilities of each weapon and how you want to play with them. Keep in mind you have the sword and Troy Baker equipped at all times while you can equip a max of 2 of the other weapons mentioned.For shooter mechanics, everything is solid as it should be. Aiming and movement feel good and responsive, weapons impact as they should, and have satisfying sounds with each that become better when done on beat. After completing the main stage, you unlock 3 optional challenges to unlock Sigils, which are passive abilities such as streak protection, higher damage at low health, etc. Each of these challenges has a unique twist to it that keeps you on your toes such as restricting your arsenal, changing your weapon with every kill, only glory kills, only ultimate kills, etc. Each one challenges you to complete it as fast as possible while adhering to the rules it sets for you. These challenges are optional, as stated before, but if you're like me and you play on the higher difficulty settings, they may as well be mandatory.When I say this is what BPM should've been, I especially mean it when talking about the rhythm game elements. Attacking on beat, reloading on beat, avoiding damage, slaughters (basically glory kills with infinite range) all build up Fury which will increase your score multiplier, your damage, and as your fury builds up through the levels (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x) more tracks of the song begin to emerge; so the better you play, the more often you'll actually be hearing the vocals of the songs put into the game. On top of this, difficulty isn't just based on RNG and enemy counts like in BPM, there are no RNG elements to the game. Each level has a different tempo that might be slower or faster than the last, which means that tempo you need to be playing to will need to adjust to reflect that, unlike BPM where most levels are around 90-100 beats per minute if that. The music features a modern metal vocalist all-star cast who collaborate with the band that composed the music for the game. Even for those who aren't as much into the genre as others, it's a kickass soundtrack with some familiar voices you might be surprised to hear again.Onto the biggest issue with the game, it's performance. I've turned every setting down as low as I could, but when encounters really heat up, my FPS regularly tanked to the mid 30s which made staying on beat difficult. This issue is very much exacerbated in the later levels when they start introducing enemies with more dynamic ranged and AOE attacks. The game is definitely worth a buy, and if you're unsure, download the demo. It's free and you won't have to worry about wasting your money if you end up not liking it. If you enjoy metal music, Doom 2016 esque shooters, and lite-rougelike games, definitely give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, It has a kickass soundtrack from some of the best metal vocalists out there, but is rather lackluster as a game.I started out pretty hyped for this game, hearing the voice actor and vocalist lineup, but ended up disappointed by the end.Overall, the game took about 4 hours for me to complete the story and most of the Torment trials.The actual combat is a basic fps in a simplified style of Doom 2016/Eternal, but with the single added specialty that you shoot/attack on the quarter note and reload on a half note - for every weapon. Nothing special with eighth notes, triplets, or usable off beats. The limited weapon mechanic variety was a huge missed opportunity.Every level is the same repetition of shoot waves of enemies for several minutes in between Troy Baker's captivating dialogue followed up by a quick light bullet hell boss, all underneath original metal good enough to distract you from your monotonous left clicks.The bosses and levels never really add any layers of complexity to the gameplay beyond some superficial add-ons such as a spinning floor, or having to fight more than one of the same boss; its more of an endurance test of whether the player can keep up their quarter note clicks before the carpal tunnel sets in.The enemies aren't bound by the same rhythm mechanics, which makes sense story wise, but a more interactive dodge system than just press shift on the quarter notes was another missed opportunity.If it goes on sale for $10-15, it would be worth adding for the music.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, BPM was way better in terms of gameplay. Every weapon has the exact same rythm to it, while in BPM each weapon had a different fire rate which would have you shoot at different timings, it's a bit difficult to explain but overall, the shooting is always the same in this game (except for sword ultimate). I don't know if it was a bug, or the boss doing some kind of crowd control ability on you, but sometimes your character will get pulled in certain directions for seemingly no reason at all. It was very  frustrating especially when trying to dodge spells and fireballs.Soundtracks were decent, but the vocals were so loud it was difficult to stay on beat sometimes. Also, Throughout the whole game, except for final boss, every aspect (stage bosses) have the same song. Incredibly boring. The stage bosses also are pretty much the exact same except for different abilities.When pressing the reload button, sometimes there would be a delay if you don't start the reload sequence on beat. It felt like it would queue the reload, and start it on the next beat. While on BPM, the reload would start whenever you pressed the button, and it also had multiple reload stages. This means that you'd have to press the reload button on the beat for each reload sequence which I thought was incredibly fun, and looked alot cooler than on this game. The issue also with reloading in this game was that you HAD to look at the yellow beat indicators to get the perfect reload, while in BPM you could do it just with audio since you had to do each reload sequence on beat.The only reason I'd suggest playing this game over BPM is for the graphics. This game looks significantly better than BPM. BPM has this weird color schemes that are really not fun for the eyes. The color palettes are the only thing that I would choose this game over BPM. Enemy models and weapon models aren't particulary cool in one game or the other.Anyways, I don't really have anything else in mind but, that's it. GLHF out there.

_childDocuments_.review: So before I am totally drunk, I decided to write this review. (Don't judge!)Metal Hellsinger, oh yeah, this is pretty good. Is it the best Game ever? No? Is it super duper mega awesome? Eeeeeh! Ist it really good? Yeah, it is!Where to begin? Let me just say, I followed this Game/The Developers on Twitter because I love Shooter Games and also I love Metal. This is where I was intrigued.The idea of Metal: Hellsinger was nothing new to me, even though it seemed that many media outlets said that it was a super fresh idea. But before this Game came BPM: Bullets per Minute. And I have played it when it came out and revisit it from time to time.BPM is a really good Indie Game and they were basically the first to come up with the idea to combine Shooter and Rhythm Game. Is it bad that other Game Developers "rip off ideas of other studios"? Hell no! Because Metal: Hellsinger stands on it's own two feet.The Crosshair idea is almost about the same, but the guys who did Metal: Hellsinger had obviously a little bit of a bigger budget. (It still isn't AAA but I don't care about that anyways.) Because the Soundtrack here is overally really good.Let's just start with this: I LOVE Metal (also other Genres, but I am pretty much also a metalhead) so this was a buy anyways, regardless of how this Game would turn out to be.After I heard what singers were present I was "so so" on the whole concept, because I usually like some "older" Metal. But what I got here was still super fun to listen to.We have Tetjana Schmajljuk from Jinjer here who was pretty dope, also Serj Tankian from System of a Down and some other singers that are not new (their respective bands) but it still feels "new" to me.Short Version before I fall out into a big "Metal Discussion": I thought I would find the Soundtrack just okay, but it actually was driving me through the Game perfectly.Did I love it? No! Did I really like it? Definitely!What is Metal: Hellsinger? Metal: Hellsinger is a first person Shooter combined with a rhythm Game, and the rhythm you have to shoot to, is METAL!The Game is overall pretty short (took me around 5-6 hours to finish on medium difficulty and also I was drinking for over half of the Game) and I thought it maybe wouldn't be worth the price.Thought that 5€/5$ less would've been ok, but I changed my mind. What you get is an enjoyable Game that also has replay value and keep in mind, you also have a good soundtrack inside of the Game, so the price is more than worth it.Does it have more replay value than BPM? I think no. Not at the moment. But that stems from the fact that BPM is not also a Rhythm-Shooter Game but also a Roguelike/Roguelite. (I mean, if you like Leaderboards, go for it, there are a ton of scores to beat!)But it still has replay Value. (Sorry, I need to compare it to BPM, because as I said, many Media Outlets - not all of them - ignored this Game.)So who is this Game for? If you like Metal? Just buy it! If you like shooter Games?! Just buy it!The Game is not really hard (I mean, I could go up one more difficulty and probably beat it as well, but once you're in the groove, even this doesn't seem super challenging. If you die on the harder difficulty you just have to restart the whole level, but I didn't die once in the story, only for the achievement)  but it is great fun.I will revisit this Game from time to time, especially because the Devs tweeted that there will be "Music Mod Support" (or something like that) where you are able to play with the Music you want.That's great.Btw.: If you literally don't listen to music or can't keep up with a beat at all, this Game probably isn't for you. I have a little advantage because I was in a few bands, play the guitar (at least a little bit) and think that I have a little rhythm at all.I know there are people out there who don't have even the slightest rhythm, so if you are one of those persons, probably stay away. Not because the Game is bad or I think you wouldn't like it, but I know some people who really struggle with keeping up in rhythm and therefore wouldn't have that much fun.Oh yeah, a few more things before I stop this semi-drunk Review: - Graphics are servicable, but I don't care about that either. Game look good, not great, but it runs awesome and fluid.- Story: Well it was there but I didn't really care, it was nothing super special. Let's just say it didn't disturb me. Also Troy Baker was just okay in his Performance as Paz the Skull.Cool thing for me was the ending after the Credits. No spoiler here, but it COULD be that when this Game has done well, we MIGHT get some kind of sequel/series.And also props to all the persons involved in this Game, I watched the Credits. This is AA at best, almost Indie, maybe full Indie and I respect every person on there. Because I had fun. And so will you. So give it a shot, drink a few (only if you are of legal age of course) and have some fun slaying Demons in Hell!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The music is the only thing you are buying here, if to you nine songs are not worth whatever price is being asked, dont buy. Playtime: 5-6 hrsStory: Something, something, demons and hell and rage, oh yeah and METAL. The story has little to no impact on the "game" itself and consists of the very same boss being slain over and over again until the final boss battle.Level design and graphics:All levels are linear in design and allow for no alternate pathing, although i would not rate this to be a bad thing. Graphics are simplified and give of a more catoonish look, while being more forgiving in clipping and mapping. Nonetheless i encountered a good amount of bugs from enemies stuck in walls, being shot through walls, to clipping issues and flickering textures.Music:The music throughout the game is an absolute banger, but that is all the marketing for this game is about so it better be good.Gameplay:The single most infuriating thing about this game and main reason why i would not recommend buying it. The players move- and actionset is supposed to be on-beat, since this is necessary for combos, mulitplier and therefore damage. On its own and for probably half of the playtime this rythm concept works just fine. However i already noticed in the trailers for this game, that something felt off. Literally everything in this game is on-beat, but the enemy move- and actionsets are not. With the exception of AoE attacks enemies will move and attack you off-beat pretty much all the time which gets more noticeable the tougher enemies become later in the game.So first you are forced to move off-beat if you do not want to take damage or even die and second you can not dodge enemy attacks appart from simply running from them. There are no skill checks whatsoever to damage or dodge an enemy and since boss fights are a culmination of all the above, they are the least fun i played in quite some time.Conclusion:The music is fantasic and had me headbanging for most of my playthrough and the visual effects help elevate the beat to its best. However we are talking about a video game and the "game" portion underdelivers quite drasticly, so much so that the music loses a lot of its initial appeal. If you are in it for the music go ahead you will have a lot of fun, but if you came here for anything else stay clear.Much love, stay safe everyone

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun for the first two hours, then the novelty immediately wears off.The campaign is repetitive - go to this location, kill enemies here, rinse and repeat with barely any changes to gameplay flow or enemy roster. They introduce a couple new weapons in the first levels but other than that it's the same thing. Literally - they recycle the same stage boss 5 or 6 times at  ().Overall, the campaign is rather short, so it ends just as things start to get really annoyingly repetitive.As for the story itself - well, it's an interesting jab at the classical religious portrayal of Heaven and Hell, it's more or less a diet coke version of DOOM Eternal's implementation.You play as a female demon who lost her voice and is in a relentless uphill battle against overwhelming odds to reclaim it. Along the way, you meet Paz, your sidekick and the narrative voice of reason throughout your quest who has a southern cowboy accent. The judge is the keeper of Hell(s) and upon killing her you break through the barrier between Hell, Reality (Earth) and Heaven.Ugh, where do I even begin with this mess of a mode? Remember when I said the main story got repetitive and that was it's biggest flaw? Well, if you touch this mode you'll think the story is x10 times more fun. Why, you may ask? Simple.You are stripped of ALL your abilities. Let me rephrase - .That means no primary or secondary weapons - you only have your starter weapons: the borderline useless skull and your blade ().You have no DASH and your movement speed is severely impacted to make traversing the tiny-ass maps slower in order to not make you immediately notice how minuscule these set-pieces are. And to add insult to injury, you cannot perform glory kills to gain health back, you're essentially reliant on the crystal health drops but once those are gone, you're boned. The only things to help you long term are upgrading your health upgrades. (One increases Max HP, others increase crystal spawns which doesn't honestly help all that much and there is one perk that allows you to regen health when standing still, however it is painfully slow and borderline useless since you cannot regen between rounds either.With this in mind, enemies that you would mop the floor with such as the acid flies now are complete game-enders 'cause if you get caught in the acid you're slowed down even more ().The Altar: Okay so this is your typical horde/survival mode vendor/shop in between waves. You charge up the altar by killing enemies and once the meter is full it sends out a wave that kills any remaining enemies.The Altar will randomly give you a selection of 3 perks (4 if you have the upgrade). ()You can only pick one perk per round.So yeah, Leviathan is an unfair pile of garbage EVEN with a all of the upgrades.You can collect Void Coins in order to upgrade your abilities to make Leviathan mode even barely remotely fair.You have questionably complex skill trees for a game like this and you can upgrade either your health, weapons, abilities, etc.Considering you're spending loads of points on for example upgrading your revolvers, you'd expect the game to allow you to keep them permanently after maxing them out, but no, you're given one more wave to keep them before they expire ().There are only a handful of actually useful upgrades such as increasing your max health, adding back dash from the start (it should have been there to begin with, but I digress), enabling your ultimate or even increasing the amount of perks you can choose from from 3 to 4.Most upgrades are very pricey considering that you have to painful sit through and grind through with barely anything at the beginning. (for instance most upgrades are at min 20 points, max 150 pts and around 30-50 per average, finishing about 8 waves will get you 20 void coins to upgrade so it will take a VERY long time).To make matters more interesting you are capped at a max of 3000 points allocated total - this means you CANNOT exceed this range with your upgrades, so if you somehow manage to get a lot of points and are thinking of unlocking all the upgrades, no dice - you have to create a build and go with it.I respect the dedication to make such an intricate system, however if it is rigged against the player to this degree with such an abrupt curve in progression then there is absolutely no incentive to play the game to progress. At the end of the day, this is just a rhythm-based first person shooter.The game allows you to set up your loadout, which is only really useful in Story Mode since in Leviathan you're starting more or less bare-handed.You can change your outfit or weapons (The game has about 8 weapons)I got this game while it was on sale, however after an unsatisfying short and repetitive campaign and a horrible horde mode, I still feel robbed of $10. The concept of the game is solid, the gameplay is there, it just needs way more thought put behind it and a lot more refining. The developers have the soul for their game but somehow dropped the ball and implemented so many questionable design decisions that stained that great first impression I have and left me with a bitter taste.The only pros I can think of is that the DLC contains songs from Disturbed, Gorillaz (Don't ask me how or why) and Muse.Purchase when on sale, otherwise don't bother, it is not worth your time unless it is patched sometime in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I half-recommend it. It's fun and above average, but not outstanding. It's not worth the asking price, in my opinion, but I understand why it is that price because of the original music and overall quality of what it does have.- Shoot enemies to the beat of metal music. The better your rhythm, the better your score and damage output. Get a 16x multiplier and the song's vocals kick in (the true best reward).- Levels are basically a series of arenas with waves of enemies to defeat and short paths connecting the arenas, then a boss fight. There are only 8 or so main levels. My biggest gripe with the game is that fighting waves of enemies in each level is kinda repetitive, but new enemies are introduced throughout and the fighting areas are fairly interesting in that they aren't just open areas; there are platforms and walls and such.- There are short time-based challenges that can be accessed from the level select menu. Completing them unlocks bonuses (for example, combo forgiveness and high damage and low health), two of which can be equipped before starting a stage.- Generally, you can equip two weapons (there are four to choose from) in addition to a weak combo-maintaining-unlimited-ammo skull weapon and a sword which are always equipped. You choose these before starting a stage.- 3 difficulties.- Online leaderboards. If you like competing for scores, that could make this game extra worth it for you. If you just want to play through, it probably won't be worth it for you.- There's a story, with mostly static artwork and cowboy narration. It's kinda cringey, but I guess it's better than no story at all.- I personally like the soundtrack a good deal.- The visual design of the environments is quite cool and high quality. Even though the whole game takes place in Hell, the levels are mostly visually distinct.Personally, I think the gameplay of fighting waves of enemies in arenas is too repetitive and keeps this game from really standing out. But it's still pretty fun, the music is great, and if you like high scores or going for 100% completion on a harder difficulty, you'll probably get close to 8 hours out of it, or more for the score seekers.

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason why I can't play this game for very long sessions is due to how tiring the rhythmic shooting mechanic can actually get on my hand. Which is fine-- it probably has something to do with the way I'm holding my mouse, something I'll figure out on my own time.I'll skip the comparisons to other games in the genre and this game's obvious influences-- if you're looking at this page, odds are you have at least one of them in your library already. Hellsinger takes you into beautiful landscapes that could easily be found on the cover of any heavy metal album in the 80's and 90's, and lets you rhythmically, systemically murder demons. The controls are tight and fluid, and while comboing is obviously the way to play, you're never punished too harshly for dropping them.Not an inch of the arenas are wasted space-- you'll live and die based on how well you can weave through the landscape and avoid enemy fire, which gets quite lethal the deeper into hell you go. Failure will happen, but the soundtrack is what keeps you coming back.Special shoutouts to "Stygia"-- Alissa White-Gluz's vocals are a perfect combination with the crunchy guitar riffs and guttural growls from the rest of the band. Every single song fits the energy of the map associated with it wonderfully, but something about Stygia in particular keeps me coming back.Overall, a wonderful twist on the rhythm game format. It might not be for those who get motion sick easily, and I'm sure there are people who wish it was harder. However, everything about this game screams polish, and it's clear that from its inception to release, The Outsiders' team were incredibly passionate about the project. It's a huge success, both for them, and for the players. now let me buy the soundtrack in .flac format please and ty

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is f*cking amazing.Metal: Hellsinger is basically rhythm-based Doom with even better Heavy Metal music. The game has a ton of nice little features that reward you for rhythmically doing your actions and is actually insanely hard if you play on the 'hard' difficulty (called 'Beast').This is because not only you have to fire your guns accurately, but you must do so on the beat, with a very narrow tolerance, WHILE avoiding damage from very accurately attacking enemies that seem to use predictive targeting. Staying on the beat while trying not to die is really hard and if you take damage, you lose score and damage multiplier.This means that it's a bit like playing the drums in the sense that you have to do various things simultaneously, all while sticking to the beat, which for me is very exhausting and sort of brain-bending. However, that just makes it feel all the more satisfying when you succeed! It's a ton of fun and feels like a hardcore metal-based gamer workout. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wondered what happens if you mix a rhythm game, DMC, and doom together? Then fear not, this game is exactly just that.Expand your arsenal as you play. Shoot, stab, and slaughter your way through hordes of demons as you jam out to the amazing music in each and every single level.#1. MUSIC. Basically if Doom music and DMC music fused together, its heavy, its catchy, its metal. .#2. Each weapon is unique and have its own advantage / disadvantage.#3. Everything is synced to the beat and I mean  from the gun firing to the player movements to weapon reload and switching to the enemy movements.#4. Each level has its own aesthetic and music.#5. Leader Boards presents infinite replayability.#6. Add on runes allows for passive power ups during gameplay (as long as you finish their respective challenges).#7. Playing on the beat rewards the player massively with additional buffs on certain hit streaks and additional damage when hitting perfect notes. You can hit off beat but the damage of the weapons will become weaker.#1. No dynamic bpm. Each level has a set bpm and does not change even if the music is changed.#2. Lacks boss diversity (for the models atleast). Majority of the bosses are basically reskins with different movesets except the final boss.#3. There is a  challenge stage which is insanely hard to do because of the time constraints besides that everything is fine.#4. The story is alright, it serves its purpose of tying everything together but can be more fleshed out.   EDIT: Some format fixes.

_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger isn't just a shooter. It isn't just a rhythm game. It is an amalgamation of the two. It's Crypt of the Necrodancer meets DOOM meets Knotfest, and it does it an a way that just makes your brain melt in ecstasy. It even has an intriguing story to go along with everything.Every song in the base game (along with two of the DLCs as of writing this review), are completely original and made for the game by the amazing Two Feathers, with legendary guest vocalists adding their voice to the already headbanging instrumentals to seriously turn what was already a kickass metal track into a song that would make even God himself put up the devil horns and mosh around. Such metal legends include Alissa White-Gluz (Arch Enemy), Matt Heafy (Trivium), and even Serj MFing Tankian (System of a Down), making this one stacked cast of vocalist to provide voice to what is the BEST of the BEST Quake-like rhythm shooters out there.The gameplay might appear complex at first, but it's actually quite simple. All songs are in a 4/4 time signature and have varying BPM, which influences how high octane you want your gameplay to be (trust me, if you want to experience what it's like to be on speed after chugging a gallon of coffee, get the Essential Hits pack and put on Misery Business. You won't regret it). You time your shots, dodges, and even reloads to the beat of the song you use in the background, and the better your timing, the more powerful your shots are, or the faster your reloads are! The game rewards perfect timing, and ruthlessly punishes the off-beat player, although there is an option to make everything be at least on beat if you are extremely out of tempo.In the base game, there are six weapons, ranging from a skull that fires magical blasts of fire that crystallizes enemies in an explosive carapace to a gravity-defying explosive crossbow that you can absolutely annihilate enemies with. For the two genuine Hellsinger DLCs, they come with a weapon each, but you'll have to get the game to check them out for yourselves!All in all, Metal: Hellsinger is an absolute blast if you're a big fan of metal music, or a DOOM/Quake fan. If you're both, then this will DEFINITELY be up your alley. You'll waste many hours on this and realize that the time slipped by after bashing your neck sore from the intensity.Gameplay? 10/10Aesthetic? 10/10Performance? 10/10 (It lags a bit, but this is only because I have a baseline computer, and even then it was minimal.)Music? 100/10Get this NOW!
