_childDocuments_.review: This game is sick as hell. If you've played BPM before, think of it as a cross between that and Doom. It’s a crazy power fantasy and insane music like in Doom (plus the setting is literally hell), while also letting you push yourself to perform as technically as you can, and putting yourself in a mental state where you feel like you become one with the music.Now that it's clear I adore this game, here's where I think it could improve (note, this is nit picking, so there’s gonna be a lot):- Movement:The movement in this game is pretty good, but I've noticed a lot of times where if I land on something like an enemy or an oddly shaped rock, I'll sort of hover there and slowly fall. Usually, I still have my dash if this happens (as more often than not you get in these spots by soaring), but if you don't have a dash, you're sort of stuck awkwardly skidding down whatever surface you're on, like a cartoon character sliding down a window they just slammed into. Really kills the momentum of the game and takes you out of it. I also had a couple times where I clipped into areas I shouldn't have been, although I've never been unable to get out of either of these situations.- The sigils (specifically ghost ammo):The torments were pretty fun, although I kinda wished they'd somehow incorporate them into the regular hells or expanded them more. My main problem though is with a particular sigil, ghost ammo. That plus the crossbow is an unreasonably strong combo. For context, the crossbow only has 2 bullets, but in compensation doing a lot of fast AOE damage. This weapon can shoot every full beat, so when you don't have to reload for 8 shots, it just becomes oppressive. You don't even need to reload anymore, since you just switch whenever it would use actual ammo. You then just shoot the ground around you like crazy and win without trying. Obviously, this doesn't ruin the game as you can just... not do it... but, I think that sigil is too strong even on other weapons. I would've liked seeing some more risky sigils, or even ones that had a downside to them. Plus, there should definitely be one that makes you receive double damage and nothing else.- The achievements:Pretty simple, not enough/too easy to do (as seen by the completion percentage)- Enemy variety:Wish there were more, especially types of angels. Even model variety would be appreciated, although obviously that has more to do with building assets then it does anything programming or design related. Assets = SUPER hard to make.That being said, some really huge enemies would be sick (like the Tyrants in Doom), and really sell the power fantasy.- Boss variety:Cool that they all play pretty uniquely, but... yenno... they’re all kinda the same model.- Enemy behaviour/mechanics:♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the bug guys can eat my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ their gas cloud. Really, it's just the slowing part of it. If you could dash through the poison cloud and avoid the slow, they'd be fine (maybe you can and I'm just bad lol), or if they had just a bit less health. If I were to change them, I'd probably give them the same health that the ranged mooks have and reduce the number of pellets they shoot out with each attack. This would make fights with them easier, but then you could have more of them in each fight. They'd also be WAY less tedious to fight.Some attacks could be telegraphed a bit better, possibly with lights or other visual/audio queues, but you'd have to be careful not to mix it up with the slaughter lights or kill the flow. Although this is an extremely minor complaint among nit picks.- Enemy glitches:I've noticed that the angels, or any enemy that leaps, tend to clip into things a lot. The behemoths will sometimes leap into walls and become partially submerged, or angels will get clipped by a protrusion, and start spazzing out like they're in a washing machine. I found this happened a lot specifically in the torment “Death’s Edge: II”. Also, the wave attacks from the siege behemoth and the lightning guy not staying on the ground is super weird. This ground wave attack moving towards me in discrete steps, hovering in the air, is kinda silly. Plus, if they’re on a lower level it just clips into the incline and does nothing.- WeaponsThey're all really fun and cool, and intelligently thought out. Paz does 0 damage, but he can make high damage explosives, stun enemies and turn them into said explosives with his super, and keeps your fury up in lulls of combat. The sword is great for dealing with the shield guys (also ♥♥♥♥ those guys, but they're much more bearable in close range so they get a pass), and has the highest damaging super in the game. The shotgun does decent spread, plus a high damage long range super. The pistols are insanely reliable and set people up perfectly for slaughter kills (my personal favourite weapon), plus they have great range, and their super keeps your rage up if you need to run for health crystals. The crossbow is OP. The boomerangs are weird but really rewarding and their super is amazing at dealing with every enemy type (my second favourite). Alright I'm just kidding, the crossbow has unparalleled AOE capabilities and a great crowd control super for when things start getting too hectic.Now, something that bugs me, but I don't really know the answer to, is that I don't really get to see most of the weapons. Obviously in torments you use what you're given, but in regular hells I just use the two I like best every time. It'd be nice to have a game mode that restricts your weapon options or something, since they're all so fun to use. This can be fixed by just using the other weapons, but that feels more like you're doing it out of pity than appreciation. The switch weapons on kills torment augment would be a great way to replay hells, forcing you to play on your feet, especially if the order was random. This could also be fixed by having levels being filled with more enemies that were vulnerable to certain kinds of weapons. Although there really aren't many enemies that get countered by certain weapons, which I feel would be a great addition.More weapons would be nice, but honestly the ones in the game are so well tuned I don’t think it’s really that necessary.- DifficultyThe difficulty levels are well balanced, but I would’ve loved another level above beast. One where I’m not sure If I’m gonna make it through every room, and need to not only use my full arsenal, but intelligently incorporate movement into my combos, with almost every beat being the difference between life and death. I’m not sure how this would be done though, I just feel personally that beast is not hard enough.- Slaughters:Could be embellished a bit, kinda lame visually as is. Very satisfying mechanic though.Now that I’ve given the bad, I feel like I should give some good- Holy ♥♥♥♥...:This game feels like a dream come true to me. I almost feel like a kid again when I play this, your whole being gets sucked into this game when you play it. So much of your focus is required when you play, you can’t help but start to immerse yourself in the moment.The phrase “you are what they fear” from Doom perfectly describes how you feel while you play. None of the hells can stop you, all they can do is watch and die as you rip through each layer like a savage beast through flesh.If it isn’t clear from that description, I’m really into this game.- The music:I don’t need to tell you; this is literally the selling point of the game. Plus, Matt Heafy and Serj Tankian, jesus christ.- The weapons:Oh my god are they so fun to use. Each one syncs with the beat perfectly with everything. The reloads feel weighty when you time them well, and lackluster when you miss (as they should). The bullets have impact and feel powerful. The explosion from the crossbow sounds intense, and the swing from the sword visceral. I've run out of characters to use but this game is amazing

_childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger is a good rhythm-based first person shooter.The combat works surprisingly well. You only do significant damage by attacking to the beat and chaining successful beat-attacks will charge the more-awesome-music-meter. You don't get vocals unless it's fully charged, so it's helpful that they seem to have polished things since the demo. I was missing A LOT in the demo, but in the full game things seem a lot tighter and I was mostly sitting at 16x throughout, on the same normal difficulty. If it's still difficult for you: just use the swords, they're easy mode.The game has a decent little narrated campaign. It certainly won't win any awards for writing, but it's a neat enough way to progress from song to song through different environments. And there are some cool boss fights throughout.The optional challenge missions are where things get more interesting. These are a lot more challenging than the campaign itself by limiting you in certain ways, like forcibly rotating through weapons on each kill. It makes for a great way to provide some variety. What works a little less well is that these challenge missions then unlock upgrades that make everything else... easier. So the people most in need of those upgrades to progress are least likely to actually be able to unlock them...The music is simply phenomenal. They actually hired a bunch of fantastic artists form various famous metal bands to produce a lot of great original songs. There's a surprising amount of songs here, although it's unfortunate that it's one track per map and they're locked to that map and its challenge mission variants. The game is definitely worth it just for the soundtrack alone if you're at all a metalhead.Less well executed are the graphics. They look good and even HDR worked well out-of-the-box, but the performance is terrible. Sure, my video card is in need of an upgrade, but the performance is all over the place here, which makes rhythm-shooting a lot harder than it should be. It seems the various levels were made more with eye-candy than playability in mind when it comes to performance optimization. So if you're on the lower end in hardware, or have a slightly outdated GPU like me, then the game will be more difficult and less enjoyable than it should be.All in all, a great game if you have a decently beefy system and love metal music. Metal: Hellsinger easily wins best soundtrack of the year for me and is worth it for that alone.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eyes on this game for literally years, impatiently waiting for the release. The bar was quite high for me.I love rhythm games, and while I don't like FPS games in general, a rhythm shooter seemed like a dream.While I was following the development for this, I also discovered BPM: Bullets Per Minutes, which is another take on the rhythm shooter idea, so later on I will be comparing the two.Let's start with what you're here : Is the rhythm shooting cool ?Yes.Yes it is.The soundtrack is just brilliant. Some of the gameplay elements fit really nicely with it. For instance, I really like that the lyrics only play if you have the highest multiplier. The overall aesthetic... well I like it. It's nothing exceptional, but it fits just fine and is well executed.The execute mechanic feels amazing. Lunging to a low HP enemy to kill them to the beat... extremely satisfying, doesn't get old.Movement is actually very intricate and leaves a lot of room for skill expression.Shooting to the beat is fun...... Mostly.This is where some of the design decisions hold back the nervous gameplay I was looking for :- First of, the reload system, where you have to hit the reload button again at the right time to get a fast reload. Neat on paper, but I find that in practice, I have to be careful with my button presses, where I would rather just mash and hit all the button all the time (to the beat of course) while going on a rampage. That's what I mean with "nervous gameplay". It's not bad, I simply feel held back.- While the levels look great, I find that sometimes there's an enemy hiding somewhere and I'm running around trying to find them. Not a huge deal, but again, a small thing that I feel holds me back from the "nervous gameplay" I'm looking for, where I just shoot everything in my path without thinking.- Some of the weapons (sword 3rd hit specifically) hit sounds don't actually happen exactly on the beat, but are ever so slightly delayed. Mostly a non-issue, but makes me not wanna use the sword.Then there are small things that aren't deal breakers :- Story is plain and useless, and yet there are too many cutscenes and they're too long. I wish I could just keep jumping straight into the action. Writing is sub-par in my opinion, though that's very forgivable, that's not why I bought this game (but then again why are there so many cutscenes then).- Bosses are repetitive to say the least : it's always the same boss, but with a different arena and slightly modified attack patterns. Doesn't feel good.- Weapon balance is all over the place.Now let's compare it with BPM :- Metal Hellsinger's soundtrack is leagues above BPM's, in my opinion. BPM's was serviceable, this one is beautiful.- Metal Hellsinger's artistic direction is, in general, leagues above BPM's as well. Actual models, not re-used assets. Also BPM has that stupid red filter.- I like BPM's reload mechanic a lot more. In that game, my shooting goes "BOOM... BOOM... BOOM... click. click. tack." Here it's more like "BOOM BOOM... ... ... clack".- Despite being incredibly uninspired, BPM's dumb simple level design makes it easy to clear rooms without wasting time running around looking for enemies, like it sometimes happen here.- I wish this game had a more badass boss execute thing, like in BPM. I swear if you haven't tried BPM you should, just to see how cool it is too kill a boss. Also BPM actually has several bosses, not just one.Overall, a good game. My expectations were very high and I am somewhat disappointed, but a good game nonetheless. In many ways, this is the best execution of a rhythm shooter, but it still has a few lessons to learn to really hit that sweetspot of nervous gameplay in my opinion, then it'll truly be a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Put Doom and Bullets Per Minute in a blender and this is what you get. This is easily one of the best metal music given video game form pieces of art that exists. The design direction and music are some of the best I have seen, easily up there with the Doom reboots.The gameplay is fantastic, if not a little...floaty I think is the best term? I feel like the game doesn't do as good a job with the in-tempo combat lock in feel as BPM does as there aren't any obvious audio cues for your weapons reload and the firing isn't as powerful in terms of audio as they are in BPM. It's not bad don't get me wrong at all, I just feel it leans a little more into the shooter aspect more than the rhythm which means adjusting your play style accordingly.Replayability is excellent with the baked-in leaderboard system for the levels and just smashing enemies to the absolute (head)bangers of songs. You'll get about 5-6 hours out of it to complete the game and 100% the challenges. Also major props to the VA's as they were pitch perfect for this story.Grab this even if it's not on sale as it's worth it even just for the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Hellsinger is a materialized dream of every fps lover metalhead. The Beat mechanic is really amazing and makes you time your attacks to the songs and keep up with the beat. Keep this in mind because if you have absolutely no feel of the rhythm, you're going to suffer playing this. Two Fathers made a good job of writing great songs crowned by a bunch of great metal vocalists. The story is nothing extremely complicated but that's not the reason why I play frenetic first person shooters. The game have only two flaws. First are the boss fights where you basically fight the same boss over and over again just with slightly altered conditions and attacks in different surroundings. The second is the variability of the regular mobs. The number is kinda limited and throughout the game you encounter still the same monsters with one new tougher mob added in every other level. Overall a great fps and 8/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The only FPS where headbanging helps you win!Metal: Hellsinger a rhythm FPS? I had my doubts about how the combat loop would feel and am very pleased now that I've played it. For anyone who's played Doom Eternal and experienced the loop you need to keep going for replenishing ammo, armor, and health, it's not that far of a reach to transition that gameplay to a set tempo. Smart move. Hellsinger paces its rhythm combat loop out well. It starts out feeling simple enough as you just start by attacking on beat. As you grow in familiarity and new weapons come into play to show you more about how the combat dynamics work, you can really go deep honing your skills and the payoff is higher damage output, highscore, and feeling like a badass playing as The Unknown as she slaughters denizens of the hells and heavens. I didn't even get close to the depth of skill one could aim for in Hellsinger. This is a great title for leaderboards if that's your thing, and they are here.And what better music for all of the hellish action here than metal?! The game offers two original tracks per level that will carry you through all the action. One for battling through waves and arenas of enemies--Doom Eternal style--and a separate track for the boss fight of each level. Original tracks allow the game to offer the music in layers depending on how well you're doing keeping the action going. At a lower performance you may primarily hear the beat and heavy guitars of a track, step it up more and it starts to shred, get to max and the vocals kick-in for maximum effect. The vocalists are well established legends in the metal scene and pair well with the music, which stays consistently rooted in melodeath. DLC allows you to swap out some of the original tracks for other originals--or other artist's songs. If metal isn't your thing, or you still like your variety as I do, there are non-metal tracks you could get. So far, I only have the DLC that adds Cristina Scabbia and Will Ramos tracks, which are worthwhile. I've always felt Scabbia is generally underutilized in Lacuna Coil, and thankfully she gets to shine on this original track. The DLC also adds a new weapon.Weapons are fantastic here. They all offer something unique and interesting and they're all viable depending on how you want to play, how you want combat to feel, the tempo of the particular level, and how much score versus just blowing enemies away is important to you. I really enjoyed the DLC machine gun. I wasn't sure how it would work given the rhythm dynamics, but it's good!The game isn't necessarily big, but there's a lot to do, a lot of reasons to replay levels, especially with song selection options, and it surprisingly offers a bigger narrative than I expected. The story is told through a mix of motion-comic style cutscenes, that are well done, and brief in-game cutscenes and voiceovers. The narrator gives off strong Sam Elliot vibes from The Big Lebowski. I wasn't sure what to think of that at first... this isn't a western, but neither is The Big Lebowski! That said, ultimately it's a great thing. Back to content, I've gotten all of the achievements and there's still more secrets I could collect to unlock more weapon skins, as well as the hardest difficulty to play. One of the elite enemies only shows up on the hardest difficulty and I think that was a cool thing to bring something new into the mix rather than just make everything more challenging.I haven't even played the horde mode or any levels with the free bonus tracks from Dusk yet!I also have to add that the whole presentation is tight. Everything through and through looks and feels good."Now that's what a debut looks like!"

_childDocuments_.review: This leaves me wanting more in the best way possible. If it piques your interest at all, go for it, unless length is a big concern for you. It's about 3 hours to finish the story, with challenges giving another 2. You are given some toys on replays, but it's mostly just for fun. (Length shouldn't be a factor for game critique, but it's a completely fair metric for how to spend your money.) this isn't the first game to blend rhythm and shooting. (Though, incidentally, it's an easy recommend if you enjoyed BPM: Bullets Per Minute). Not only do you need to fire on beat to do even reasonable damage, but you need to be doing so frequently enough to build up your multiplier for both score and damage. There is room for error, you don't need to keep a perfect streak up, but keeping the streak earns perks, and a few slip-ups in a row will sink your multiplier and really cost you.Once that multiplier caps out though? You feel GODLIKE. Basic enemies are dropping in one shot. The vocals kick in, joining the guitar on the BGM that had just been drum beats when you started. It was fun before, but now it's positively enthralling. You're the unstoppable star of one hell of a music video. You unlock short challenge levels as you go. They add a good amount of replay value, and make you approach the central challenge differently, be it by limiting your weapons, or requiring certain types of kills. They give rewards that carry back to the normal game to give you perks. I went straight through the levels normally not doing challenges until I beat the final boss, but that was probably a mistake. (Take my comments on difficulty below with a grain of salt) Your protagonist, The Unknown, has an awesome design. Props for making a devil woman, but not going full succubus. Your companion, narrator and kinda pistol, Paz, has just an incredible voice that could make the phone book compelling. The story feels like an epic myth and has some surprising twists despite its simplicity. It does end in a sequel tease, but still has a satisfying finale. It's not always clear what's damaging you. This might be a consequence of the wave-based encounters, but I pretty frequently would back into enemies without realizing it. This would often cascade into taking a hit, panicking to correct, and losing my multiplier, which then left me doing less damage and struggling to get momentum back up. It does seem a little strange that I  know if there's a 12-foot tall monster behind me about to smack me, either through some kinda UI or sound cue. Put simply, it seems like instead of making bigger levels, the game's length is padded by making enemies come at you in a few too many waves in the same small area before you can progress. It's justifiable given how short the game would be otherwise, but creates its own problems with pacing. Most encounters ended with me thinking "finally!" instead of "that was fun, let's keep going!" Not that I wasn't enjoying it. Every boss *looks* the same except for the last one. This has a narrative justification and was definitely a budgeting choice, but it feels like a missed opportunity. They have distinct attacks and behaviors, but more differing designs and animations could have complimented them better. I can't be the only person who's sick of the "barely animated concept art" look. I'm not asking for Naughty Dog-level animation from my AA games, I understand why it looks this way, and the art is great on its own (seriously, your big bad is just a skeleton with wings and a fancy hat, but they actually make her imposing), but there had to be more interesting ways to present the narrative. Something like a proper motion comic could have worked really well. Trust me, I know metalheads love splitting hairs about genre, and thrashing drums and growlers aren't everybody's favorite. The soundtrack is all by the same artist, Two Feathers, and in general, it's not the type of metal I would listen to casually, but they pull in a variety of guest vocalists that manage to give each song a unique feel, and they end up being the key factor in making them memorable. Stygia's theme, featuring Arch Enemy's singer, is phenomenal, and they do not waste Serj Tankan's performance either. The rest was perfectly good in the demon-killing moment, but didn't stick with me as much. Why does every original gaming IP think it needs two titles?! "Hellsinger" is an amazing title, why clutter it with the generic "Metal"?

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so first of, I'm a total raving metalhead so I was very interested in this game. But I was also incredibly skeptical and I actually went in expecting to be disappointed not because of the music, or even the gameplay on its own. I expected to be disappointed because I was going to unavoidably be comparing it to BPM: Bullets Per Minute, a game that I absolutely adore. With that in mind, I actually really enjoyed this game! Looking back on it now, despite the obvious similarity of being a rhythm based movement shooter, it actually does a lot to separate itself from BPM, so much so that I can't actually make any fair comparison's between the two other than how they differ. So if you played BPM and had the same concern as I did then I'm happy to say this game is still worth your time!So, moving on to how this game holds up on its own. I was rather surprised when I started and was met with a story, usually stories in boomer shooters are an annoyance unless they are being told in the background, but the somber clean guitar notes in the background mixed with the sultry narration gives it some charm, and it's not a very obnoxious plot. It does its job at contextualizing the game and its setting without being in your face and for what it's worth, it has a couple of good moments in it that had me rooting for our hero, The Unknown.Once you get into the game you're met with some steady drum beats and a nice chunky bassline as you enter the tutorial. Once you get into combat you'll probably notice a lot of parallels to the newer Doom games as you're encouraged to weaken enemies and "slaughter" them to get your heath back. But if you are able to keep all of your actions on beat you'll be rewarded with a score multiplier that also buffs your damage. I like this a lot, as it really keeps the flow of combat on the rise trying to keep your score multiplier at x16 while also trying not to act so fast that you outright kill the enemies, since you want to keep them for health. There's also a perfect. But my personal reason for wanting to keep the multiplier at the top is because the higher your multiplier is, the more of the song you hear with vocals at the top x16 mark. Throw in the perfect reload mechanic in which you can reload your guns faster by timing your key presses right and you have a really solid core gameplay loop here! The level design is pretty good as well, most levels come down to a few different arenas broken up by little corridors. The corridors are interesting though because you'll have to run to the next arena as quickly as you can to keep your score multiplier up, they'll often place objects or enemies for you to shoot in these little stretches so that you can keep the multiplier up as well. The only time your multiplier stops is while you're on your way to the boss of each level, the music will usually come to a halt to build up the anticipation as well. For the first few levels you'll have the chance to unlock a few different weapon types that all work differently from each other, and some even have special functions (Such as the revolvers being able to fire on 8th notes.) After completing each level you also have the opportunity to play a little challenge arena to unlock a Sigil. Sigils work as little gameplay buffs that help you passively, such as landing perfect hits increases your Fury, or keep your streak going after messing up for up to 3 times. As you get further into the game you can make these Sigils more effective by completing more arenas and some of the later once feel pretty tense too!Now, I do have a few gripes. For one thing, the bosses at the end of each level are all based on the same model. They'll have slight variations in their design, and they all have different attack pasterns but it would have been nice to see more varied designs for these bosses. The game also feels a bit short for the asking price. Though I did enjoy my time with it a lot, once I got to the end I didn't really feel a reason to go on a second playthrough or anything. All I could really do, if I wanted was complete the Sigil challenges, which are fun, but can get pretty tedious. My other big complaint is that the soundtrack is absolutely killer, and I would love to have it! But, unlike many other games on steam, it doesn't seem like I can purchase it via steam. Many games will have their soundtracks on the steam page as DLC, and I would like to have that here as well because not being able to buy this soundtrack is a huge bummer! The last major complaint is that this game ends on something of a cliff-hanger. It feels like a set-up to a sequel or something, and though I would be willing to buy a sequel, once again I did really like this game, it just doesn't feel like a great way to end things off. I almost would have been willing to pay extra if they added a few more levels to the game to end the story off properly right here. It seems like that should be a rather minor complaint, considering that plot isn't what I came fore anyway, but after the big final boss with System of a Down's singer blessing my ears over it, it felt kinda weak to then have the story concluded. It felt more like the half way point, then the end.But despite my complaints I do still really like, and recommend, this game if you're a fan of shooters like this. If we do get a sequel I will be anticipating it, or even a DLC to finish things off. And please, PLEASE, release the soundtrack! They already have album mixes in-game that you can listen to, but give me something I can put on my phone and listen to on the bus! PLEASE!!!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played "Crypt of the Necrodancer" or "BPM: Bullets Per Minute" before, you'll have a pretty good idea of what you're getting into here. For those who haven't however, the concept behind these games is that acting to the beat of the music is the core gameplay gimmick. In Metal: Hellsinger you have several weapons at your disposal, and your goal is to not just kill enemies with them, but to do so as entirely on beat to the music as possible.Metal: Hellsinger's gameplay feels like a conceptual fusion between three games in particular; DOOM (2016), BPM, and Devil May Cry 5. I've already explained the similarities to BPM. It's very similar to DOOM in that you often find yourself in specific rooms gunning down waves of enemies to be able to progress, and even has something akin to the glory kills mechanic in the form of "Slaughter", which also acts as a source of healing. In DMC5 you have the ranked combo system that was also present in previous DMC games, but with the innovation of the music rising in intensity as you heighten your rank. Something akin to this ranking system exists in Metal: Hellsinger in the form of the "Fury" system, with the music becoming more intense as you rise up the fury ranks and the lyrics kicking in at 16x Fury.To keep up your Fury, you want to be staying on-beat with your attacks. However, different enemies are more vulnerable to different weapons, so you're going to be wanting to switch often, and getting used to the timing for each one to be able to attack efficiently without going off beat. It's okay to feel like you suck at this early on, everyone has to start their journey somewhere. You need to familiarize yourself with the basics to build the foundation that the rest of your skill will be built on later. Once you do start getting good however, success is very largely dependent on how well you're able to get into a mental flow state and how well you are able to keep your concentration under pressure. It's also important to remember that while the skull is your weakest weapon, it's also the only weapon that can contribute to your fury rank without landing hits on enemies. If you want to keep yourself at 16x without dropping under, this weapon is crucial.The story isn't anything particularly long, I completed my first playthrough in only about 4 hours, which is also how long I have played at the time of making this review. Depending on what your intentions are with this game, that could be where you decide to uninstall and move on. However, that is not the extent of the content. There are multiple difficulty settings for you to play on, with some enemy types being exclusive to higher difficulties. If you're here to experience the process of getting good and conquering challenges, or even just to encounter and defeat every enemy type in the game, you might be here for quite a bit longer.To summarize the story in a bit more detail without any heavy spoilers, you are "The Unknown", an entity that showed up in Hell one day with a score to settle. The Judge, the ruler of all of the realms of Hell, has stolen the thing most precious to you: Your voice. You must venture from one realm of Hell to the next defeating The Judge's aspects so that you can eventually face her in person and reclaim your voice.The graphics are quite nice. Each level is beautifully detailed and visually distinct from each other. The OST is similarly great in my opinion, although mileage can vary depending on how into Heavy Metal you are. The music all feels very professionally made and to a certain extent almost feels like a standalone album with a game attached to it rather than the other way around. As you progress through the game you'll also unlock the individual tracks to listen to. If you like this kind of music, completing the album is a pretty good progression incentive in my opinion.This type of game is definitely not for everyone. However, if what I've said about the game so far hasn't scared you off and especially sounds like the kind of thing you'd enjoy, this is probably an experience worth having. This type of game can be very frustrating to fail at, but it's also intensely satisfying to do well in. Patience is crucial to enjoying games like this, but if you meet that qualification then by all means give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Metal?If Yes.Buy the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.Metal Hellsinger is a Rhythm Doom-em up with a soundtrack that absolutely slaps. The fact this didn't win soundtrack of the year is downright offensive. The good:SoundtrackGameplay (Guns all feel and sound great) and playing on rhythm is even betterLevel DesignFinal Boss is insaneThe MehStory was palatable but nothing special overall. Go through hell to get to the big bad to win. You can play the game without it and have a great time.The game is a bit on the shorter side given there are only a few levels though each level has a set track and there are side challenges, a high score board and now a hidden collectable in each level on each difficulty to hunt which adds some replay value. Enemy Variety was a little lacking with 1 or 2 being added per level and some being modified versions of existing designs.The BadThe only bad thing I can really point at is the end bosses of each level. They're mostly the same but in different arenas with different attacks. If the game varied its bosses more it would have been even better. The end boss is great and I wish the prior bosses had as much flare. Overall this game accomplishes what it needs to and nails the soundtrack.Looking forward to a likely sequel where there's just more of everything present here. More guns, more bosses, more artists, more enemies and even more banging music.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: After 100% unlocks and level completion (minus some achievements) I have to say this game is unique and refreshing.  It wasn't since Super Hot since I really felt like a first-person-shooter felt way out in its own field.The game requires rhythm, but it also requires somewhat good aim.  You have to dodge, reload, and shoot on the beat to maximize your kit.  The levels are fairly demanding on the normal difficulty after 2 or 3 levels.  The challenges are fun and help you unlock new passive bonuses. Really good music, production value, fun weapons, and a solid feel.  If you're looking for something different, this could be it!
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fantastic game. Most negative thing is boss variety, final boss is the only thing that's really a big difference from the rest and it's done incredibly well, I'd love to see what this studio can pull off in the future for other boss fights. Overall this felt like doom but just leveled up into the music. I was already headbanging in doom without being much of a metal fan, but this game makes headbanging an entire mechanic, and it's one of the smartest decisions I've ever seen, super good.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game and found trying to keep a rhythm harder than the combat itself, but the game isnt totally about just one aspect of it. Its an amazing mix of the combat, setting, theme, being a rhythm game and the music, wow... the music is just amazing. Every track is so good, I love it all. The only thing that lets this game down SO MUCH is theres no official OST. I want an official OST with the mp4/flak/mp3/wav, whatever file versions of all the songs. So disappointed we cant just get the songs in a music format file to listen on other devices and such. Its SUCH a wasted opportunity that you can only enjoy the music in the game. I know the OST can be found on youtube, just cant believe the devs couldnt release one for whatever the reason is.I give it a: Excited, positive, profanity that steam wont allow / 10. \m/
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: A great rhythm game with a solid soundtrack. The boss fights are repetitive and the challenges become a little obnoxious by the end (so I skipped them). Have to say also that the ending boss felt pretty unfun, and like a drastic difficulty spike compared to the rest of the game (especially compared to previous bosses, which had a gradual increase in difficulty by comparison). But a great soundtrack, and a great gameplay loop overall - a sequel would really benefit from something like an arcade mode or endless survival mode, where you just get to shoot, run, and gun to the music for as long as you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: I suck at rhythm games, not a joke, but I still think this is a great game. Even if I'm trash, I still wanna keep playing. The music is so damn good, that I just get more into it, the visuals in game aren't anything special, but they still look good; the main menu and lobby sections look the best. The game has a few minor bugs, like the AI not always responding to my attacks or they get stuck, its rare and not a game breaking issue. I also wish they would let me tweak the response settings a little more, something feels off. (It could just be my lack of rhythm)Overall, it was worth the $30 and I hope they add some small dlc at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Nice narrative, but bleak gameplay surroundings — for me it's hard to see enemies in the monotonous background to keep the awesome music playing. I understand that the budget is not that of DOOM, but still the game feels more boring to me than, say, Crypt of the Necrodancer. Thus, I get why Hellsinger is so praised, but I'll pass — taking the music with me though, for a separate listening.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me... conflicted.While it is a very high quality game with a lot of polish, I dont think it's worth the amount of money they are asking for it.You can complete the campaign in a little over 3 hours, and I bet you could make it in two if you knew what you were doing; and for a game going at $30 USD, i'd say that borders on being a scam. Most games, you can complete in 8 hours and go for around $60, meaning you spend around $7.50 per hour on a first play through, For this you spend $10.00 an hour for a game which has very little replayability outside of collecting the relics; but after that, the game is complete. The bosses as well dont really have anything different between them to make them different, and of course there is a difficulty spike at the very end. The songs carry this game, and I must admit, I had fun with hit! It's a solid rhythem game for all you metalheads out there, and I loved hearing some guest singers like System of A Downed, and I may have heard Arch Enemy there as well, but that could have been someone else. All of that said, I dont think the LENGTH of the game makes this worth what they're asking.I would suggest adding in a hoard mode or a custom game-mode. Please add more onto this game, and for the love of god dont put it in DLC. This game is way too short and far too underwealming to consider me buying the sequel. Too bad I cant refund this.Edit: Okay so apparently Steam allowed me to refund this! Idk how, but thanks steam! Now I can spend that $30.00 on something that's actually worth that money.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Doom crossed with Crypt of the Necrodancer. Everything you do in this game feels so metalThe music is AMAZING! The final boss song is the best way to end the game.My only complaint is that the bosses all use the same model, except for the final boss. Would have been nice to have different boss models to go with their individual mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Dune + BPM with a little Darksiders mixed in there. Songs are fantastic, gunplay is great, story's pretty good as well. No game of the year story, but solid in it's own right. Different track for every level, which provides some slightly varied way each gun plays in each level. The only "cons" I would say is the boss design feels pretty stagnant, the boss music is set, and the game is pretty short (took me about 3 hours) if you don't feel the need to replay or do optional content. The boss arenas are gorgeous for the most part and very different from each other, it's just the design and soundtrack that can feel stagnant. HOWEVER: the last boss fight blows everything out of the water, and saves one of the best songs for it as well. Final boss is such a spectacle, and the fight design is top notch as well. Overall, if you're someone who loves this kind of game, this is definitely the highest quality rhythm shooter out there, and earns the $30 price tag. Also gets a bonus in my eyes since there's no greedy transactions. They let the game speak for itself and don't try to lure you in with preorder bonuses or mtx. Just the one price tag and you get everything the team worked on. Lastly, from how many people are looking forward to this, I'm also looking forward to see this game inspire a flood of rhythm shooters into the market. I can't wait to see how Outsiders uses the massive revenue that is sure to come from this game on their next installment.

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the campaign on medium (Goat) difficulty.I recommend playing this game even if you do not listen to metal in your day-to-day life. The gunplay feels really doom-like (most notably the finishing move mechanic, like DOOM's glory kill), but more focused on accurate and rhythmic shots rather than ammunition management (you need to reload, but your overall ammo capacity is infinite). There is a lot of combo opportunity depending on your loadout of 2 weapons out of 5, as well as 2 different Sigils that will eventually wildly affect your playstyle (e.g. switching weapons to have a lot of free ammo, or being rewarded more for accurate rhythm hits).The story is quite captivating, with ending having a really neat wrinkle in it. Troy Baker's narration as Paz the Skull feels natural.The bosses at the end of the missions feel somewhat samey, even though they really have different mechanics to them, they "look" similar (there is a story reason, but still felt uninteresting by midgame). Fortunately the levels themselves are different enough to feel engaging.Game crashed on me once, so far.Wish the sword ultimate did not override the music.Absolute recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely in love with this game! I'm personally into a lot of melodic metal so as soon as I saw they got Björn, Matt, and Serj (Lead signers of Soilwork, Trivium, System of a Down) and so much more talent, I was all aboard the hype train for this game and boy was I right to do so!If you love Doom, Killing Floor or BPM, this game is a must play! There's never been a better experience than slaying demonic entities in a stylish, badass, fast paced, action packed setting!However, there is a catch! The objective is to wipe the floor with the blood of your enemies to the sound of the beat! You deal most of your damage shooting, smacking and slaying in sync with the music.And did I mention how amazing the soundtrack is? God (or should I say hell), the production is just soooo good. Every track is just an absolute banger and just has you stomping to the beat and banging your head! Even if you're not a fan of metal, the music fits the atmosphere way too well that you'll still have an incredible experience playing this game.I could go on... but by now you should get the general idea. I'm absolutely hooked. Just absolutely flawless execution of the rhythm shooter idea. I really think this game has a lot of potential to expand too with dlc's, or a sequel! The amount of opportunities to collaborate with other bands is something that one can only dream of! While Soilwork are my favourite band and I'd love to hear more of them in the game, I'd love to see more of what they already have but also Demon Hunter, Pyramaze, Unleash the Archers hell even get Polyphia in there they've been bringing out banger after banger! I bet there's so many different takes on this you could do with so many different genres of music too!The only one flaw I could think of are the boss designs. Other than the final boss, all the other bosses looked almost the exact same but with different skill sets. And again except from the final boss, all of the bosses had the same soundtrack. I think it would be cool if you could select a specific song as a boss soundtrack in the main menu or if they gave each boss a different soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Being a huge Metal fan, I had to try this game. I've played it for a while on PS4 and then got it for steam.The game is pretty solid and has a rather interesting questline (nothing mindblowing, but it's there). The gameplay core is good, sound design is pretty cool with the combos building up the song. Sometimes playing with a PS4 controller gets a little "buggy", specially when you're shooting and changing targets the aim seems to get a little "slow". The songs are truly gems and I listen to them even off the game. Regarding the DLCs, Purgatory and Dream of The Beast are worth. I got the other Essential Pack as well but requested a refund since the only cool song to me was Disturbed and the timing is horrible.There is a small, but cool variety of guns. You can try different combinations that may suit your playstyle. But don't hope for a wide arsenal, at least not in its current state. One thing I hope they add in the future is the possibility to adjust the audio latency with negative values. You can do it trough the .ini settings (something like that) file, but I'd appreciate having something more practical. Replayability value : You can revisit the campaign levels in higher difficulty, try to get a higher score or go for collectables. When that gets boring, you can check the Leviathan mode, which is basically an arena setup where you can upgrade and buy skills for your character. Furthermore, I like to think about Metal Hellsinger as a guitar hero with guns. Often I see myself playing a level again just as I used to replay songs on Guitar Hero. Having said that, do I recommend this game? Yes. Would I buy it for the full price? Not actually. It's a great game and has much potential, but I don't think it's worth 79 R$ (roughly 15 USD). Wait for a 25-30% sale and then jump in this awesome experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic visceral heavy metal rhythm slasher with swords and ranged weapons. Enter hell with eyes full of primal hate and ride to meet your fate,  unleash fury to shoot and slash demons to the rhythm of great music. While it can be difficult at first, especially if you mistake rhythm for beat, assists and your reaction response calibration is available. Greater fury comes with great vocals. There's several layers of hells you must fight through, combos and executions to master, even reloading your shotgun to the rhythm while banging your head. As soon as your work is done, even more challenges await. It's a must-have for all heavy metalheads. Graphics are great, sound is pure perfection. Very well executed. Play with good headphones and a controller or keyboard/mouse. Go, play the demo now! Your destiny awaits. What, are you scared? Take my hand, we're going to hell!

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game.My only complaint is that it gets very repetetive after like 2 rounds ("Hells"), but other than that, I loved exploring the newly unlocked weapons and combos always right on beat.If you enjoy 100%-ing games, this has a lot of fun achievements, my favorite one was to finish a hell with one specific weapon (Paz).But the part that I loved the most was the very end. I'm not gonna spoil it - you'll have to see for yourself! But the bossfight was genuinely the best one ive ever played through in any game ever - I was so concentrated on every movement, it was perfect!

_childDocuments_.review: Reason on buying: Here for Metal music. Not disappointed, awesome bangers! My recommendation target: People who are fan of FPS AND Rhythm game.Pros:- DOOM-like gameplay mixed with rhythm. Easy to play, hard to master. Hit window is tight but not super tight. Calibrations for both audio and video are available to match your system and your reaction time.- Difficulty options including rhythm assistance (cuz Souls-Like difficulty is overrated)- Enjoyable mob fights (nothing is more metal than killing mobs of hell while headbanging)My concern as well as critics for the game:- Expect BULLET HELL. Not a fan of bullet hell on FPS games as you can expect to get hit out of nowhere.- Harder difficulty means bosses can almost one-shot you. Wish it just mean more enemies to kill rather than having hard-hitting, hard-to kill enemies.- Repetitive boss design (I can understand the devs were busy with the soundtrack more than the design, but COME ON!!!)- Frame Drops will ruin your rhythm, better to lower the graphical settings and having stable fps.- Story rather short for a $$ game. Hope there's another game mode in the future like gauntlet mode or something.This one could be 8/10, but my experiences in hard (but not hardest) difficulty made me lowering it to 7.5/10. There's a room for improvement to make the game better and much more enjoyable.After rage quitting from the final boss, I have to revise this review to 5/10. DISGUSTING BULLET HELL AND PLATFORMING. RHYTHM HIT WINDOW IS HIT OR MISS. NOT ENJOYABLE FOR CASUAL PLAYERS.

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a game. Shooting to the beat is always fun, and there's no better feeling than killing good and the song just gains lyrics. Game soon taught me to move as well while shootingAll up to the final boss with Serj Tankian singing No Tomorrow in the background and singing the main theme at the last phase.I absolutely loved it. I completed the game in one afternoon and it left me wanting for more
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Would highly recommend this game, even if you tried BPM and found that you couldn't enjoy it. IMO the gunplay in this game isn't as good as BPM but it's superior in pretty much every other way.I would recommend lowering the SFX and voice volumes and increasing your system volume when playing because I found that the sounds of demons and shooting were sometimes making it hard to hear the music. Even if I didn't realize it I'm pretty sure it was throwing me off-beat occasionally and since adjusting it I haven't had any problems.

The story... is there, can't praise or complain about it. Recommend it if you like FPS and Rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: i wait until i beat AD to write the review, so people wont call skill issue when i list what i dislike about this game (did not touch the always-on-beat tick box, not even once consider it). Game is a banger for sure, music and gunplay wise, just like everything everyone says. Now the 'bad' parts that hopefully see improvement in the sequel: -fast movement (only fast movement) is jank city, since the dash momentum seems to be tied with beat so sometimes it works, sometimes the character just stop mid air. If you play normally using only ASWD and dash it shouldn't be a problem. On the other hand, if you like to dash around room slapping mob with shotgun or do sick 360 mid air flicks with akimbo revolver, it will feel like orgasm cut short by someone squeeze your ♥♥♥♥ midway. It just doesnt feel good. I know this is a rhythm shooter, but part of it is also an area shooter so it's reasonable to expect smooth and tight movement.-collision needs to be addressed even tighter, i dont like seeing my shot getting block by 'invisible corners' around beams, tree trunks, broken brick walls, or weird looking rocks. This is more like nitpicking, but during the yhelm level, the outdoor part of the stage's collision is particularly worse. We play as a devil with firepower that tear through flesh and bone but tree branches is where we draw the line? I cant seem to shoot mob through the branches after rocket boost myself in the air and try to snipe them, and on my way down the branches also body block me, which bring us to the next one.-the player collision vs enemies and environment geometry: if i try to perform a dash jump from ground over some mob's head, seem like my character's feet will get stuck but the camera appears like im way above them already. One thing all players agree that annoys them hugely is when your character feel stuck but visually from their point of view doesnt appear blocked by anything. Character fails to mantle over small ledges, and weird looking rock, if this is by designed, it is too cumbersome to make this little knee-high gap a part of the intended difficulty. I saw my self die a couple time during my playthrough in AD by falling into pit and get repositioned into hot zone, because the character seem to be way above the ledge already yet just  an inch short. Then character get stuck on beams, slopes instead of being pushed aside or just kinda slide along it. Som small tiny hand-width ledges also have collision that block you from jump if you stand too close to the wall beneath them... etc I reckon if this is fixed, the experience will feel much smoother.-The pickup/powerup things seem to have weird collision for them. Sometimes i fumble to pick up a x16 4-5 times in a row, then i had to stop, breath in and look carefully if my character just dash through it or not. If they can be 20% larger or something, idk, just not too much people pick up stuff by accident. I can't be the only one who get this problem.-The crossbow ghost round cheese is just significantly more powerful than every other combo. It's doable with everything of course, but that one combo make the game a cake walk once you master it. This is obviously not fun, but it does have a unique play style to it, by rewarding being mindful of your ammo count and being proficient with weapon switching, so it's not a bad thing. If you can add more sigils and combo in the sequel that compliment different play styles and make EVERY/ANY combo powerful once the player master the trick the game will feel, idk, less cheap and more fun. Right now i dont think anyone prefer beating the game on AD with only akimbo revolvers, but i know those psycho exists out there, I bow to them. -On the other hand Beast seems way too ez in comparison. Not to boast (maybe a little) but i just clear beast in my first sitting ever on this game, and have no idea wtf sigils are, until i feel like i need more upgrade for the acheron level. Not complaining, beast difficulty feels just right, fun and some challenge. AD is a bit stressful, but that is intended.-Music, despite being top tier, actually dont always match with the in-game beat. At least the tempo matches perfectly so if you make a slip it is totally doable to readjust. I dont know how to fix it, but it's there and it's very noticeable, just imo, about 10% of the time, which is not a small chunk but maybe it's just me.Overall i really like this game, good core experience, just need to refine some more imo. Those were only what doesn't feel right and what i think it is, but idk for sure, the dev should figure out in the next one, hopefully.

The protagonist looks perfect and his partner skull is terrific in the lead, the voice acting is awesome.The game is well optimized, even on my 6 year old pc, the game runs on high settings at 75-80 frames at 2k.One drawback - Lack of cool guns(and designs of guns is dull, lazy concepting), and the game is pretty short and I want more!9/10 - Great game

We encounter the same bosses on all levels of Hell, only their names has changed, except for the final boss.  Their music is great, but if I just wanted to listen music, I could do it from my internet browser, although it is a fun and cool game, it is weak as a "game". I suggest you wait for the discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome in my opinion.The music in this game is fantastic and some levels I've played on repeat consistently just because of how great it feels to get the vocals going once you hit that max multiplier and keep it up.The gun play is about what you'd expect for a slaughter everything in sight in hell type of game, but with an added touch. The rhythm part adds to making the gun play even more fun and adds a bit of simple to learn yet hard to master vibes to it. Plus when you quick reload at certain parts with weapons it just adds a slightly magical touch to the sound of the music and carnage.The story is obviously not the focus point of the game and that's completely fine considering how fun it is to just mindlessly kill things.For me I give this a solid 9/10. They succeeded amazingly well with what they wanted to with this game. Story isn't the main point of replayability it is the amazing metal music and gunplay. I'd say the $29.99 value is well worth what the artists and developers put into this amazing project.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember how good it felt when you were playing DOOM, and sometimes the rhythm of ripping and tearing would get in perfect sync with Mick Gordon's BFG Divison? Well this game is designed entirely around killing stuff to the rhythm of METAL music and you get rewarded for doing it with more damage and more METAL. Needless to say, the music matches the gameplay perfectly, and just look at the names they got for the vocals! And they didn't just license some songs, they have all-new original songs tailor-made for the game. The downsides are it's a bit short: I'm writing this review with the campaign beaten, although there are unlockable optional challenges and difficulties if you want more of it. The other thing is since it's a mix of an FPS and a rhythm-game, it might feel awkward at first if you're used to regular shooters, but you'll feel right at home if you played Hi-Fi Rush in addition all of them FPSes. Either way, even if you're new to rhythm games, it's definitely worth giving it a chance - it feels soooo good once you get used to it. Just play the demo for 30-40 minutes and see how it works for you.On a side note, the skull talking like a cowboy is a bit silly, but whatever.I definitely wouldn't mind playing a sequel or a DLC with more levels and the story continued - it might not be something to write home about, but it does its job.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Looks good enoughMusic ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bangsPrice is rightDevelopers didn't take things too seriously -- I like that the Unknown (your character) throws up the horns at some points and is generally a heavy metal mamaCons-The rhythm doesn't vary from song to song/map to map -- you fire to the same beat the whole game even if the songs do sound differentThe weapons are fun but I found myself really only using two (the pistols and the throwing weapons). The first is just too good (good damage, range, great ultimate attack) and the second is almost broken (great damage, great ultimate, unlimited ammo)Upgrades are pretty whatever; I didn't change my playstyle using them even though I guess you could (e.g. do more damage at lower health, gain ultimate attacks faster, etc.)Story is kinda meh -- something about a prophecy and you're gonna wreck Heaven and Hell. Nothing wrong with all of that but it doesn't shine much either.Overall-Worth the price and lives up to expectations. You're going to have fun even if the variety isn't great in some regards. I found myself gripped by bullet hell moments while the music raged on, literally letting out a "whew" at one point when I managed to knock out a tough boss battle.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically like if someone crossed "Doom:Eternal" with "Crypt of the Necrodancer", with folksy narration a la "Bastion". TL;DR, I recommend buying this game (with an important caveat, see below). It's fantastic escapism, perfect for if you're having a rough time and need your mind somewhere else for a while.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Caveat: I encountered bugs with parts of levels not fully loading in the first couple of levels. You'd enter areas and the ground and walls would just be invisible. I almost quit the game early because of it, as there was what should have been a simple jumping puzzle that would have been trivial except the platforms were invisible now. I'm not sure what caused it, but I dropped my graphics settings to low, and while it didn't fix levels that were already broken, I didn't encounter it in any levels afterwards. And if I'm honest, the game still looked pretty good, so I didn't mind leaving the settings there on the off-chance it had helped. My brief search online didn't turn up anyone else having the same problem, so YMMV.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I was unsure how I'd like the game because I'm not usually into metal quite this heavy, but not to worry, it builds naturally and gradually as you get more kills. By the time you've got a high combo, when you've got the strong backbeat behind you and the metal vocals at full wail, the whole package feels *amazing*. I beat the main story on the easiest mode in just under 4 hours, and would say I'm pretty middling as an FPS player. If you too are mediocre at FPS, but still enjoy it, and are wondering if you've got the skills to be able to fully experience the game and beat the story, no worries, there is a difficulty that should be accessible enough for most people. If you want more of a challenge, there are two higher difficulty levels immediately available, plus a third extra hard difficulty unlocked when you beat the game. There's tons of other content I haven't fully explored, too, including an arena mode I briefly dabbled in, which looks like a fun way to come back to this game later if I just want to play for a short stints but don't have much time.(For those interested, said mode nerfs you back to the most basic powers and then as you beat successive waves of enemies lets you get perks and powers back until such time as you're overwhelmed. Looks like that mode has kind of a roguelite element too, where you can buy upgrades to the mode at the end of each run.)Besides the above-mentioned bugs, if I had to pick a specific thing to critique, the story doesn't make a *lot* of sense? I'd say it makes just enough to maintain intrigue and atmosphere throughout. I'd put it maybe on par with "Darksiders" in that respect, including the kinda nonsensical but entertaining and evocative theological themes.

_childDocuments_.review: Unknown waited. The lights above her blinked and sparked out of the air. There were demons in the base. She didn't see them, but had expected them, now for years. Her warnings to Cernel Joson were not listenend to and now it was too late. Far too late for now, anyway.Unknown was a demon for fourteen years. When she was young she watched metal concerts and she said to dad "I want to sing, daddy."Dad said "NO! YOU WILL BE KILL BY DEMONS!"There was a time when she believed him. Then as she got oldered she stopped. But now in the depths of hell she knew there were demons."This is Joson," the radio crackered. "You must fight the demons!"So Unknown gotted her shotgun and blew up the wall."SHE GOING TO KILL US," said the demons!"I will shoot at her," said the Stalker Demon and he fired the rocket missiles. Unknown shotgunnned at him and tried to blew him up. But then the ceiling fell and they were trapped and not able to kill."No! I must kill the demons," she shouted!The radio said "No, Unknown. You are the demons."And then, Paz was a Skull.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game with Humble Choice. Did not really know anything out it, but it looked interesting. As I usually play with speakers, it was a bit difficult to stay in rhythm, so switched to IEMs and the combat became much smoother.Regarding the music, though I'm not a fan of the "death growl", it did not bother me much in-game as the songs fit the gameplay pretty well.Combat if fun, even with the limited enemy variety, with the sword being the primary weapon of choice before getting the Hellcrow scythes - that stuff lets you mow down multiple enemies like the sword, but adds distance and rear/double damage, when they return like a boomerang after throwing, on top. The only reason to use any other, longer range weapon, is during the boss battles, when you have to keep your distance to be able to dodge their bullet hell attacks.Had some crashing, but it was caused by my aggressive 3060Ti undervolt. Going from 0.875v to 0.9v fixed that. Game runs and looks great overall.Did not try the additional game modes yet other than the story, but on that alone I think it's worth to get the game. Hopefully it was enough of financial success to develop the obviously planned sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: "What do you get if you mix Doom (2016) and a Metronome?"Is probably the question that the guys at The Outsiders asked themselves when they wanted to create a game that took the Metal of id's series revival, simplified the enemy designs, amped up the frequency of encounters and cut down on the length of the game to make Metal: Hellsinger.The result is the most captivating shooter that any metal fan could ever hope to play, creating an intensely satisfying loop between shooting, dodging, reloading, yes, even jumping to the beat of assorted bangers by scene legends such as Alissa White-Gluz of Arch Enemy, Matt Heavy of Trivium, and even Serj Tankian, whose band affiliation I won't even have to mention here.Add a sprinkle of a story that embraces the demonic, hellish tendencies of the genre, narrated by the equally legendary Troy Baker, that takes itself serious enough to be entertaining through its frankly paper-thin depth, and environments that pulse and react to every beat, pyrotechnics flaring at the highest multiplier as if you were at an actual concert yourself, and you get a short, 5-7 hour romp through a Hell the tunes of which you won't get out of your head soon.Metal: Hellsinger is certainly my surprise hit of the year, and I can't wait to see where The Outsiders take it in the future, with hopefully more bands, more levels, and much more of the same, satisfying slaughtering of the mortally challenged.This is an easy recommend and a solid 9/10 for me. 30€ (or your regional equivalent) very well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game twice now. Once from xbox game pass ultimate and then another from when i got it from humble bundle in their monthly choice games.   Had a blast playing this even a 2nd time and now they have the horde mode.  played it with the dlc Purgatory. New weapon and a few new songs.  This is a really good Mix of FPS , Music, and rythem.  You have to shoot to the beat to increase your damage points. Time Flies in this game without realizing it. They have a good story line narrated with voices and even if you skip the story scenes the game play itself is just no words. Play to the beat and when you get 16x you then start to hear the words as it rewards you as you play. Too many pros to list on this game so will skip strait to cons.Only cons i saw were 4 bugs that I still ran into then first and 2nd time i played. -on 2nd to last boss with the gears int he water the boss locks up invisible as if an enemy character  didnt die yet that may be under the gears or water. had to restart the level and beat it after that.-on a level where you pull the enemies to the door at the top of the stairway and turn they get stuck there and then easy frags. -last boss if play him repeatedly trying again sometimes it comes up with no health bar. the other bug was where i fell off a cliff but got stuck in between two rocks and couldn't move. had to restart the map. nothing big on that one just don't fall there. What's remarkable about this game is even with those bugs as those can easily get fixed I still rate this a 10 out of 10. Was going between a 9 and 10 the whole game mainly because I was looking for something to go wrong but even with those bugs I still love this game so much and it is re playable. after story mode you have other events int he story mode you can complete to unlock all abilities , Then there is horde more to build up your skills and unlock everything. _childDocuments_.review: Let me emphasize this with get this game on a discount. All the torments and the story together runs about 7 hours.I'm not saying that because it's short, I'm saying that because I was bored and frustrated for a good portion of those 7 hours.NegativesOnly enemy I hate is the shield one which reflects all projectiles. I hate that there's slow down mechanics on some enemy projectiles. That said the boss fights are terrible. You will fight the same boss with kinda different attack patterns a total of 8 times, every single time there is at least two add phases. Overall most the boss tracks sound similar.The maps are short. The latter half of the game the devs have put waves on top of waves of enemies so you'll be stuck in a single area for minutes at time in combat. That ends up feeling pretty boring since they just throw waves after waves of the same enemies.There's a lot of asset re-use everywhere. A ton of basic projectiles get re-used between bosses. Similarly most the projectiles in this game are just orbs, the difference is how fast they travel and how much homing they have. Further on that, tracking on enemies is crazy, I've noticed it pretty hard in the Leviathan Horde mode. It's not uncommon to see an enemy looking one direction and seeing the projectiles fire in a different direction.The torments (challenges), ♥♥♥♥♥♥' suck. Most of them anyways, there is one which gives you info ammo and swaps your weapon every kill and that's always great fun. Other challenges range from mid to awful due to the "challenge." It's not so much they're challenging so much as it is an endurance race. Don't ♥♥♥♥ up for like a minute or two straight or else you fail and need to redo it all over again. The enemies don't spawn until you destroy the last wave, so you end up with enemies in hard to reach places or you can just not find them. Or they give you short ranged weaponry and put you in an area with cliffs. It's challenging but it doesn't feel challenging for the intended reasons.One of the guns I loath for various reasons. Another gun while it's fun feels overtuned and overshadows pretty much every other weapon. This messes with the gunplay where you should be feeling encouraged to swap between weapons.ProsThat said when this game feels good it feels great. Not including the starter weapons 3/4 weapons I thought felt pretty good and have their own use cases. That said you're only allowed to bring 2 so all the weapons are fairly flexible. Sigils are pretty hit or miss but there's some good ones in there which have some cool synergies. I think the biggest issue is the descriptions on them can be so vague. Deal more damage on low health, what is low health? Am I at less than 50% or am I walking dead? Just a couple like that.When the music works it's great, you feel like an ultra badass slaughtering to the beat and each sound effect from your weapon highlights it. The sound of the guns firing just becomes a part of the song. Visually it looks great too since the map pulsates at rhythm. The rhythm mechanics are fun, you are rewarded for keeping rhythm constantly. Your score multiplier goes down when you aren't. The primary weapon, a skull will raise the multiplier as long as you fire it on beat. Alternatively you can fire a gun and reload repeatedly on time to keep the multiplier up as well. This isn't Doom, you are going to be racing through these maps rather than searching for secrets so it shouldn't be much of a problem. Plus doing this helps keep rhythm. At the best this game gets you'll be swapping through weapons firing off to the beat and it'll feel second nature.For what's there game looks good, enemies look fairly unique, and there's some good looking maps when it doesn't feel samey. Love the cosmetics for Unknown.Leviathan ModeIt's awful, it's doubled down on the base mechanics of the game to an obnoxious extent. If you're winning, you win harder, if you're losing get ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Add on a splash of RNG. The base weapons in this game are bad, well except the sword but more on that. Skull was never good, it was always intended to be something to keep beat and score up. Sword is good however in this game mode they take away your only ability to consistently regain health. Instead it's added to the pool of possible perks you get every wave.The enemies spawned are also pretty random so say you get a bunch of enemies with AoE. AoE with no consistent source of healing=death. You're gonna be pretty screwed with the sword, and the skull doesn't deal enough damage to keep pace.In this gamemode non-primary weapons degrade so there's always a chance by the time you lose your main non-primary weapon you don't have one to replace it and your run basically ends. Plus a bunch of perks boost weapon stats in categories, so say you lose your heavy weapon and all you have to replace it is a precision weapon then all those perks you have are useless. Weapons are bought with the same points you use on perks which also means for every temporary weapon you grab you are out an extra perk. Perks are mostly pretty boring too. Mostly it's a flat damage increase, if "x" occurs inflict bleed/slow/curse, boost damage by 20%, boost the healing you don't have by 20%, "x" chance to gain a little health on kill with "x" weapon, and so on. A weird amount of perks have a percentile chance of proccing, very little as actually consistent. Bleeding I don't see a use for because what use is DoT in a game where you want enemies dead by yesterday? So you've got RNG for the perks, RNG that you have the weapon to use them, and RNG that the perks actually do something. Not saying all of its boring, just a majority.Enemies scale up quickly, by wave 7/30 the enemies have their health buffed and you'll have encounter most the enemies in the game, and even enemies from new game+. So perks really should be significant.On the bright side if you grind out a tiny amount of echos over a few hours you'll be able to upgrade your character and buy back base game mechanics.Overall I'd say it's just a really painful gamemode to play and punishes you for playing any weapon that isn't just the sword because it's the one that doesn't break and can actually do damage.

_childDocuments_.review: To the point===================An FPS that's not quite a rhythm game, not quite a rouge-like with the weaknesses of all.Good Stuff===================+ Cleared on Normal difficulty +- The FPS portion of this game is solid, it controls great and, when you can actually focus on the rhythm and play it how it was intended, every comes together nicely.- The aesthetic and design of the world is very well done. Theme-wise the Hells are all very unique, too bad almost none of that leaks into the level design.Bad Stuff===================- The games biggest crime is it's sameness. The levels are all identical in how they play out: straight path, Arena, straight path to next arena, repeat 3 times, Boss. All the while fighting the same small variety of enemies, plenty of them reskins, using the same 4 weapon arsenal. - The weapons feel crappy. The shotgun fires like a pellet shooter (there's a DLC shotgun that I bet handles better, open those wallets) the pistols are really just sad in both damage and distance, the crossbow that takes so long between shots you may need a nap and these double scythes that are so janky I'm convinced they were added as an after thought. In a game about scouring hell I cannot believe they used such utterly boring and ineffective weapons.- The OST, which is the shining point for a game like this, really just all sounds very similar. Nothing against the genre but if you shuffled the order of the tracks it would make no difference. They're not unique to the level or represent any real theme except maybe using something said in a previous cutscene in the lyrics.- For a game that has sort of an arcade like presentation there sure aren't a lot of power-ups. You can increase your rhythm counter with pickups on the map and..... actually that's it.- The bosses are boring. Massive bullet sponges with the same pattern: Do 1/3rd of the health, enemy wave, another 1/3rd, enemy wave rinse repeat. They do vary attack patterns thank god and At least they have different hats on!!- The final boss seems like a competition to put as much ♥♥♥♥ on the screen as humanly possible and was the only real challenge in the game for me, killing me about 3-4 times. Even after that many attempts I can say it was never clear what was killing me.- There's really nothing to strive for after completing the game. Unlike something like Binding of Isaac, just about everything seems to be unlocked on your first playthrough so why would I go back and just play the same 8 stages with the same 8 enemies over?- You need to jump a ridiculous height to clear enemy shockwaves/ puddles/ persistent effects. Plenty of times I felt like I was clear and I would get hit.
