_childDocuments_.review: Stop reading, download the demo. Metal: Hellsinger looks neat in the trailers, gameplay videos, even on streams. However, none of those actually do the game justice. Feeling the gameplay and having to be ON BEAT is not translated well through a proxy experience. That being said, this game is NOT DOOM with a more metal, and less industrial, soundtrack. Metal: Hellsinger is a game of its own. For $29.99 USD, it offers 9+ missions, with 3 smaller challenge sub-missions (called Torments). The visuals are great. The weapons are great. The MUSIC is GREAT. I'm kind of a metal elitist and some of the songs aren't my taste. However, they make for great gameplay. If you're losing beat, start headbanging to the music to find it again. Not only do the weapon attacks gain a significant benefit from being on beat, but so does jumping, sprinting, and reloading. If done on beat, a player can achieve some chained abilities. The base game is a great foundation for more to come. I'm anticipating more. What *is* coming? Music modding has been officially confirmed to be in the pipeline. Happy slaying. 🤘
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw a trailer for this game I it looked like such a fun experience. And playing it was just like I imagined it would be: an amazing time. I mean what could be cooler than slaughtering demons to the rhythm of metal music? I assume the game won’t be so great if you don’t like the music used though. Metal Helsinger could be improved by more enemy variety and improving some of the existing ones. But the biggest problem for me are the boss fights at the end of every stage, it's the same boss every time with different attacks. I would have also loved for Metal Helsinger to be longer. Looking forward to an update or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is a fairly short game (took me 5 hours to beat all missions + torments) the quality of the gameplay and the music paired with the weapon and sigil variety offers great replay value. The rhythm and FPS mechanics are a match made in heaven (or hell), with tight and responsive combat allowing for complex movement and badass combos. Said combos add quite a bit of depth to the combat, as there are many bonuses and moves only possible with the right weapons and actions. However, as a metal lover, the music steals the show every time. Each guest artist does a fantastic job, and the OST manages to explore quite the range of sub-genres while never abandoning the general atmosphere of the game. Each hell and it's associated song have very distinct identities, which are only enhanced by the vocals when you reach max fury. Personally, I couldn't care less about score, but the music itself brought me to go to extreme lengths to maintain max fury. My only issues with Metal: Hellsinger are a little bit of jank during in-game cutscenes and the transitions between vocals/no vocals somewhat lacking smooth transitions, but the gameplay more than compensates; besides, while the story is interesting, it is not the focus. The focus is slaying demons and rocking out to some incredible music, and this game delivers. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Although im not very good at rhythm games, i do find some very fun, and as someone who loves BPM: Bullets Per Minute, i knew i'd love this too. Took me awhile to beat because i refused to play on lower than Beast difficulty. Also i think i would focus too much and not blink while playing, so my eyes would hurt after a level.The music is harder than anything i listen to, but with an open mind and open ears, it ended up not being a problem. In fact, I love the song Stygia and I've been listening to it almost every day for months now. Game was near perfect except for the boss of Acheron which gave me a black screen after it's cutscene the first run, and all audio became super distorted when i reached it the second run.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal Hellsinger is a rhythm FPS game set to the badass beats of the metal soundtrack. As a part human, part demon, you become The Unknown and have to fight through the domains of hell, mowing down demons to get an epic showdown with The Red Judge. Narrated by Troy Baker, you will gather an incredible arsenal to fight like HELL through this Doom-like game. The real winner here is this incredible soundtrack though. The songs are insane and keep you going, getting louder and more intricate the higher combos you have. I can't emphasize how good the soundtrack is, but as much as I wanted to enjoy it, this game is not Steam Deck ready.Max settings for this game is an immediate no-go as it will drop to 29 FPS and drain the battery significantly at 24.5W, though, no matter the settings we changed, the game was not able to stabilize at 60 FPS on the Deck. There are pockets where the game can hit 60, but these aren't as common as necessary and will disrupt the smooth flow a game like this needs. We were able to get a mostly stable 40 FPS with 2.5-3 hours of battery, but again, it doesn't feel the same as 60 FPS.Metal Hellsinger also seems to be a bit incompatible with Proton. Using Proton 7.0-4, the game does work, but has a couple cutscenes where the rainbow bars are around. These can be skipped by pressing a button, but cutscenes aren't great to be skipped. You can use Proton GE 7-33 to get around that, but the game will crash when loading into certain levels, including the tutorial. I also had my Deck client crash on me multiple times whenever I exited the game. Overall, I would focus on playing this game on desktop, streaming it, or playing with a Windows OS.
_childDocuments_.name: Metal: Hellsinger

_childDocuments_.review: Brutal, blood-pumping and brilliant combat, a unique approach to both the shooter and rhythm game genres, all tied up with an awesome aesthetic and one of the best soundtracks I've ever heard; what's not to love? Easily one of the best boomer shooters I've played - if you love Doom and you love metal (let's be real, if you like one you probably like the other) then this is for you. The main campaign is definitely where this game shines the brightest - Leviathan Mode, the game's "horde mode" or "roguelike mode" is pretty good too but, as a fairly seasoned roguelike player, does fall flat in certain parts (grindy metaprogression and, at times, a lack of the fluidity that makes the game so much damn fun, come to mind). All in all, absolutely awesome game. Definitely pick this up if you're looking for a fun shooter or just a good metal album. Also, devs, if you're reading this, make a DLC with Courtney LaPlante and my life will be complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge points for a demo. Play it before reading anything else, because these reviews are honestly not useful. I can say that I love the concept and the implementation etc, but the demo says it all. The soundtrack is excellent, and has an in-game player, which is awesome. I can't find the mp3s though, as they put them in an obfuscated format in the game data.The one thing I'm bothered by is the arcade style of the levels, where (on difficulty 3/Ultra-violence) they restart you all the way at the beginning. This is despite having set arenas, where a quicksave is 100% doable. I'd like a middle-ground between Difficult 2 and 3, where I have a restart available, but the same harder enemies. Maintaining a multiplier between arenas requires you to use the skull, which is fine as it keeps you on beat. I'd like if it auto-equipped it for you after you finish a zone.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger wastes no time putting you in the boots of the most important member of the band - the click track. This game sticks to a 4/4 beat which can be great for newcomers to rhythm gaming, but may be confusing to metal musicians. It's a Doom style demon rush game backed by the vocals of eastern death, nu, core, and djent legends. You have the ability to triple dash, quick reload, and get bonus damage if you can become the metronome. If not, you should probably stick to Doom. Graphics look polished and it's easy to get immersed in the hellscape the team created. I suggest picking it up if it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't be objective about that game, so that review's gonna be pretty short for now. Metal hellsinger promises one thing, to be a fast FPS with rythm games elements. And it DELIVERS. The gameplay is really simple to start, thanks to a consistent rythm and simple to use weapons, but the sheer amount of demons, the resource management of the ultimates, the various loadouts and the boon system give it a depth it has no business aiming for, and that's a wonderful thing.All of the OSTs i have heard for now were incredibly good, and their addition to Spotify can't come soon enough. I have been completely unable to play that game without leaving discord and listening to it only. The levels have all been pretty nice. We aren't on Doom Eternal's level, but this game doesn't need that kind of level design. The rythm and the music more than make up for it in level complexity: Navigating a level and dodging is a much different experience when you constantly gotta pick between dashing wherever you want, or dashing multiple times in a row. In looks, they look absolutely great, and the beat of the music reappearing in the levels with little flamethrowers adds a nice touch.The weapons are absolutely great. Altho i would love if the game motivated me to switch between them more, and didn't limit me to taking only two choosable ones in a level, they all individually feel great. All of them have an ultimate that absolutely DESTROYS all resistance in their own way, motivating you to save multiple ultimates for certain situations.Enemy diversity is pretty good. All levels introduce a new enemy for what i've experienced, and the game isn't scared to throw 2 or 3 at you at once. The more difficult ones require you to focus on them while beating them a certain way. It's wonderful, i was a bit scared all enemies would be beaten by "stay moving and shoot". The only problem i have with that game for now is the bosses. All bosses for the first 6 levels are flying bosses that spam projectiles, with 2 phases where they become invincible and summon adds, all of that on the same music. Sure, each of them adds its own quirk, and the music is very nice, but by the 4th boss, it starts feeling repetitive, and i haven't been finding myself looking forward to encountering bossesOverall, Metal: Hellsinger is an excellent game. It is more than worth the 30$ it goes for, and i really hope that more levels will be released along the way, even as DLCs. I want more of this, and i'm not even done with the main content.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a little more but it was good enough to enjoy the game while I played it. I am not sure if it is just me but I liked the Horde mode (Leviathan) more than Story mode. There are some things I really didn't like about the game but still you can be of different opinion.- First for sure is voice of Paz (narrator)... Doesn't fit the setting at all, complete fail. It almost looks like it tries to be interesting and fails at the same time. It is wrong narrative, wrong lines, everything... no connection at all with story and characters.- Not many different enemies, there are like 6 regular and 3 hard ones/elites, plus all bosses look the same - its just different environment and attacks. This is nowhere near to even 20 years old Painkiller.- Variety of weapons as well is very limited, and simply no rewarding experience to use some.- I get it that main selling point is rhythm shooting mechanics but still, excluding Leaderboards if you don't play by the book is stupid. There should have been separate one for those that play like regular FPS. Someone really likes that way and still wants to compare...The good side are:- Horde mode aka Leviathan. That is the only reason I recommend this game. Honestly. All that regular story offers is only to play on different level designs. The shooting mechanics and tension, shines in this mode not story. Completing is the real rewarding experience for me. OK, maybe if I also completed story on highest difficulty, but playing story again knowing how bad story is, is not something I wanted. I wanted to invest time in horde mode and found it fulfilling... and to say I don't regret playing the game.In general, if you are not really into rhythm games, much better to go with Doom or Shadow Warrior. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually the type of person for rhythm games of any sort, but I can definitely say that this one is one of the rare exceptions. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest. Don't have the negative review dissuade you from buying it, but read on if you want my reasoning for why I would strictly not recommend it outright.TL;DR: Metal: Hellsinger has everything it needs to be a fantastic release on the art and music side, but falls short in the rhythm and gameplay aspects.I have about 60 hours in the game's  only other counterpart, BPM: Bullets Per Minute, and have been an avid FPS gamer for longer than a decade now. This game's music is fantastic, the scoring system is great, the little side challenges hearken back to the Doom 2016 relic challenges and the Doom Eternal Slayer Gates. The weapons and viewmodel animations are fantastic.The gameplay, however is lacking a lot. Movement feels floaty, and after certain actions you lose all of your momentum seemingly from nothing. Firing and reloading your weapons isn't satisfying at all in comparison to similar games (BPM, Doom Eternal, etc,). It lacks the "little" touches. The noises that the reloads make, the non-overt animations, the fact that the guns barely stand out from the environment do the design a disservice. The shotgun racking automatically, reloading automatically finishing whether or not you hit the active reload timing, and other little "game does it for you" mechanics, while accessible, takes a lot out of the feeling of the "shoot on the beat" style gameplay, These are small things that add up to... really not a very satisfying game feel and a slightly boring gameplay loop overall. My biggest, 1000% largest gripe with the arsenal so far (Having unlocked all weapons) is that the Vulcan does rocket jumps, yes it does. Rocket Jumping feels flaccid. Rocket jumping feeling flaccid is probably the worst thing I can think of to put in a game, it's so feast or famine. Either its really good because its fun and effective, or you're better off not implementing the mechanic. Here, its the latter.The enemy types are also a pain to deal with. You have the generic fodder enemies that serve as health refills if you glory kill them, the generic ranged enemy that has a weak melee attack when you get close. The generic tank enemy that's slow, deals a lot of damage and has a gap closer. And the generic shield enemy that (for some ungodly reason) does more damage and has a higher HP total than the normal ranged enemy with a shield that you have to bypass to deal damage.Other enemy types are lifted straight from Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal in terms of enemy design. The Stalkers are Prowlers. The Heirophants are Summoners. The different between Metal: Hellsinger's encounter design and Doom 2016 and Eternal encounter design is that Doom's encounters were peppered with fodder to replenish resources and all of the other enemies were specialized enough to make target priority a real thing. A pinky would always rank higher than an imp, unless the imp was charging a big fireball. Here... it's kind of take care of what's in front of you? Behemoths are easily kited, which is fine but there's no real threat from a fast enemy. I'm not saying the Stalker is fast, I'm saying the Stalker just teleports where it wants to. There's nothing that really rushes the player down, trying to either corner them or force them to take a hit from the behemoth. Shield Cambions are a pain. You know how dangerous Shield guys in Doom are? You know how you can overload their shields with energy weapons? Yeah no, here its just get behind them. You know Guardians from BPM? You know how you can either get behind them if you're quick or you can wait for their downtime after their attack? Yeah no, here its just get behind them or just spam sword attacks until they die.A slight boost in the player's walking speed would also make the enemies less annoying to deal with. I can't tell you how many times I got clipped in arenas by an Eyeless because the aoe is way too large and the player moves way too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow.The bossfights so far, the first 4 hells, which are the ones I've played, are very lackluster as well. It can actually be boiled down into four steps: Introduction > Add Wave > Bullet Hell > Repeat at step 2. There's almost no rhythm to the bosses, or any of the enemies for that matter, and they kind of just do whatever whenever. This would be absolutely fine, had BPM not been released two years ago. If you've ever played, think Draugr. Draugr is a fantastic implementation of the rhythm mechanic in a boss fight. Slow projectiles, fast projectiles, floor AOE, side cleaves where you have to dodge left or right, and an adds attack that is dangerous enough to get you to clear them ASAP but not annoying enough to break the flow of the whole fight. Here, the boss says "I'm going to vomit projectiles, then I'm going to go invulnerable to give you a wave of adds, then I'll go back to vomiting projectiles."  Give me mechanics that actually matter. Make me juggle those mechanics with an add wave of smaller units. A boss arena is a stage for the boss, not for the boss to go take a water break 2 minutes into the performance for a can-can dance.That's it, if I go any farther I'll ramble on and on about how disappointing this game has been so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a good game for a 4K TV:The "beat indicator is too small" & "timing is too busy". The UI indicator runs a same loop flash unrelated to the music its tied to "BPM" not programming.Literally can mute the PC and observe the bouncing ball and win at any speed setting.You also can't scale the cursor UI for reading rhythms easier, so getting a feel is more "play it by ear" is a bit whimsy.Now that wouldn't be a bad thing if you were expecting the game to feel right like other shooter rhythm genres that use the music to include timing.However the music has a lot of variety of cues and misleading cues, and you more or less are expected to favor a design around a constant metronome; a Flashing UI instead of programming with the music on loop to guide the player for the proper timing. The enemies are basic / generic the music is not about them, not their animations or tells like weaknesses on a beat, only your gun and some flashing lights on screen are the "Rhythm portion". Would be like taking any game sticking a UI on it adding really busy dubstep and adding bonus points for timing the action with the flash. You can literally mute the game and just use the UI the music is just tacked on granted its a good hook and a great track.LSSMetal Hellsinger one of those we stuck a game about music called it rhythm based but really just placed a flashing beacon on some busy music to excuse the feel of being part of a well liked genre You can beat it in under 3 hours aka refund closed. It was just not as good as the other game its plainly trying to copy emulate ect, if you like the music you can't buy the OST on steam.. Idk for some legal reason? You may as well rip it from youtube. For a story about finding ones voice in hell, this one is tone deaf with flashy reflectors to find your way around.Not a music gameNot a rhythm game Great music

_childDocuments_.review: Saw someone else say "if guitar hero and DOOM had a baby" and that's not far off honestly.so I'll be upfront about my personal biases: I'm very much a metalhead so I am definitely a target demographic lolthat said, this game is a ton of fun. very easy to get sucked into it but it's not without its difficulty given that doing anything off-beat can be swiftly punishing if you're not careful and panic or spam. however once you get on beat, start hitting those perfects, get your fury to max and get the vocals to kick in, you know you're in the pocket and suddenly feel a euphoric zen as you continue to blast your way through the fights. the game has decent replayability with the challenges and different difficulty levels, but overall feels short. Movement in this game is smooth, but not slippery, given that it's a generally fast paced game.overall it's a 9/10 game. the music is great, the graphics are pretty, movement is good, and the gameplay loop is fun. it brought me back to when I'd play the original UT while listening to Carcass. my only real negatives are that I want more, and the other is that I personally dont care for the narration. not saying it's bad, I just feel like cowboy character narration doesnt really fit the overall game.

Keeping that hit-streak up unleashes the vocals and as I've told my friends..."Nothing felt better than getting my first x16 multiplier and having the lead singer rip her voice across that shredding metal riff. _childDocuments_.review: Decent Rhythm Shooter. Aesthetics are great.The music building up as you build meter is interesting but I did find it quite annoying trying to keep it at 16x to hear vocals. And the game has this issue imo where you have no enemies to keep the meter going. So you end up having to PERFECT shot the only breakables in the game while triple dashing just to keep it from running out by the time you reach more enemies. Sometimes enemies don't show up early enough when you enter a new arena and you gotta fight for some meter while you wait/look for them.I've had an enemy walk into a fence and then disappear, and proceeded with the game until the last room before the boss only to be locked out of the boss room because one enemy (the one that disappeared) was still alive. After many minutes of Jumping and dashing around trying to glitch into the boss room, i managed to fall into lava near the boss door and it triggered a cutscene for the boss and i was in the boss room when it respawned me. Keeping on beat is annoying sometimes. You'll be on beat getting perfects and then fall off of it and not be able to get back on point without taking a moment to get into the rhythm again. You're damage is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if your not getting perfects and it makes for some frustrating moments when you just can't land any perfect hits or when your trying to finish an enemy off for HP only to miss the timing and it stops you from trying again for a moment. Truly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying.Overall its a decent fun game when you get momentum going. Though I think the ending cutscene was kinda meh. Cutscenes in general are just Images with tween effects and such. Very Bland. They should've done some sick cutscenes with the models. I was hoping for some DLC but with that ending im not sure if it will be decent or not.

Leave Hud at 100% opacity (default) and for me at least this really made it come alive and feel natural.Not for every one, and maybe change just one or any combo or leave default. All I can say is what I wrote above helped me enjoy the game much more. It felt great! It may be useful, but I think, for me at least, it wouldn't have helped at the very first few plays. _childDocuments_.review: I don't often review games but I feel I need to be a dissenting voice on this one. It was very disappointing. The soundtrack is great, but I bought a game and the game is extremely short and shallow. I finished it in 5 hours and the content in those 5 hours was very lacking. You start with two weapons which you always have and unlock 4 more which you can only choose two of for every level. Doesn't really matter what you pick because the game has very little challenge. The only other way to change up the gameplay is with sigils which are passive buffs. You can unlock 6 and choose 2 to use in every level. They also don't really matter because they have very little impact. The sigils can be upgraded twice each but I gave up on doing the optional challenges to do so because it was same exact challenge over and over again for very little gain. The rhythm part of the game is really only important to enjoy the music and get a high score. If you're off beat you'll still do damage, albeit less and you'll still reload but slower. It'll only stop your dash and your execution kills. It's all 4/4, it's all the same beat, there's nothing there that mixes it up in any way. There's very little enemy variety. You've seen them all by the fifth of 8 total levels and they're not challenging enough to require you to change up how you must play around them. The bosses at the end of the levels are mostly the same. Same boss design, same music, same phases, no creativity. The story is barely there. You have a silent protagonist and two other characters. When I beat the final boss I was almost convinced I'd been bamboozled and hello there's more game. Nope. It stops right in the middle of the story. Nothing is resolved. I would not recommend Metal: Hellsinger. If you want to scratch the itch for an FPS rhythm game and you've not already played it then I'd suggest you give BPM: Bullets Per Minute a try instead. It explores the concept far more and does a better job of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Follow my YouTube Channel for more Reviews -Metal: Hellsinger is the banger of 2022, it’s a wet dream of metalheads, it is one of the best action games of this year. I’ve been playing Metal: Hellsinger for a while and it turned into a daily routine of mine, I choose a level, try to surpass my own or others scores while vibing to banger soundtracks and keeping up the tempo, dodging, shooting hordes of demons at the same time. I didn’t know I needed something like this in my life before playing it but man, every level, every well crafted metal song will give you chills, make your blood boil with high-paced action. If you are fan of metal music, can be Melodic death metal, Lamb of God or Trivium, you’ll love Metal: Hellsinger. If you love high-paced Action FPS like DOOM, Dusk or Quake, you’ll love Metal: Hellsinger.Starting from the cold wastes of Voke, Metal: Hellsinger presents us the story of a half human, half demon called ‘The Unknown’, who is trying to reclaim her lost ‘voice’. She is stripped of her own voice and only thing that she has is her own blade called Terminus and the Skull Paz that is voiced by Troy Baker, which also plays the role of being narrator. When ‘The Unknown’ sets her foot in one of the 8 hells, you’ll see indications on screen that shows you the beats and hear the rawest version of that hell’s own song. Starting from first to last level, each hell has it’s own metal soundtrack that are voiced by famous Metal Bands Vocalists, and Voke starts with Michael Stanne from Dark Tranquility. And in order to hear the vocalized version of that soundtrack, you need to start doing combos, killing demons according to the rhythm and avoid any attacks to keep up your fury by 16x. Thats where the real action starts.Starting with Michael Stanne of Dark Tranquility, we have Alissa White-Gluz of ArchEnemy, Tatiana Shmailyuk of Jinjer, Matt Heafy of Trivium, James Dorton of Black Crown Initiative, Bjorn Strid of Soilwork, Randy Blythe of Lamb of God, Dennis Ixyzen of Refused and Serj Tankian of System of a Down. So, let me tell you something. If we were to think differently, I might even say that we literally buy the most banger collaboration metal album that has a kick-ass game along with it, think it like that. As a fan of Dark Tranquility and of course Lamb of God, I enjoyed Stanne and Blythe’s stages most, played it over and over again in hard difficulty to raise my leaderboard score. Besides these, I also really enjoyed Bjorn Strid and Serj Tankian’s performances, however I really and I mean really wanted to see Tom Araya of Slayer by this project and I hope either by a DLC or by the sequel, we can also have him.  I was a real metalhead like 8 to 10 years ago, listening to Death, Cannibal Corpse, Carcass and all these band like non-stop, no joke here non-stop and Metal: Hellsinger reminded me of those times. Nowadays, I mostly listen to metal music to keep myself awake by my job, but all these soundtracks kinda reminded me how I used to enjoy this music genre, and I am totally happy with it.

_childDocuments_.review: NOT QUITE MY TEMPOI'm 26 years old. I'm definitely not healthy for my age. I'm fat, and likely on track to developing diabetes. I feel like I need to say all that when I mention that I've played pretty 'intense' games before. Of all of them, I felt that Sekiro or Doom Eternal were easily the most intense video games could ever get. After my usual several hour sessions of them, it was the first time I'd felt somewhat drained playing a video game.Metal: Hellsinger is the first game I've ever played where after thirty or so minutes, I can literally feel muscle fatigue from how hard I've been clenching while playing. The experience is something I can't quite explain. You know how sometimes you might play a game while listening to your favorite music, and you catch yourself trying to line up your movements and shots with the tempo of the song you're listening to? This game was designed around that concept being a core mechanic, and it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. When you match your attacks to the tempo and literally feel the music, you'll understand the feeling I'm talking about. It's exhilarating.It definitely isn't often that a game releases on Steam these days to Overwhelmingly Positive reviews, but in this case it's because this game is almost perfect for what it is. And of course the music is great, with some of the greatest metal vocalists of the decade.♥♥♥♥ the shield enemies though. They really stand out as a sore spot in the otherwise amazing combat as they literally break your flow. That's it. That's really the only complaint that stands out to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom tried to kill the metal. BUT IT FAILED! Sealed in an eternal tomb.TLDR: Decent game, takes some time to set up audio latency if you really want to shoot to the music rather than the beat indicator. Might be underwhelming for musicians (and anyone else) who really would love to play a cool rhythm with their weapons rather than just attacking on the beat. Some people said this game was too easy, I find Beast difficulty quite challenging personally as you have to use dash a lot to survive and attacking off a beat is more punishing as far as I can tell. Very nice metal.The splurge:I struggled a lot at first, the auto calibration set my audio latency to 120ms and it was impossible to chain the hits. I have been playing on Beast Difficulty since I started so i think being on time is more important. Anyway, after lots of tinkering, almost over an hour of trying. I finally found 20ms was good for my set up. I went from barely chaining 4 attacks to keeping up my combos up for 20-30 shots in a row. So if you are sure you are in time with the music but are struggling you should spend time tweaking that setting until it feels right. Try to sync the visual beat indicator to the music as best you can. What I have played so far is really fun, now that I have the set up right. You will be only playing to the full beats rather than any interesting rhythms which is a shame I mean... It's metal not techno. A not so comparable game that also does rhythm shooting,  Bullets Per Minute; in that game different guns sync to different divisions of the bar so you have some beat guns, and some half beat guns and the reloading has to be on time so with a faster gun you can basically jam out your own cool rhythm with the music and its really nice cuz the reloads are in time too. Really hard to describe via writing. The only time I have found something comparable so far is in the sword's ultimate ability but that encourages you to spam out 8ths due to it's short time.

_childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger is a rhythm based FPS, where adherence to the musical beat plays a vital role in killing your enemies and staying alive. You play as a demon called the 'Unknown', whose voice was taken by the ruler of Hell, the Red Judge. A fairly straightforward story will see you fight your way through the eight realms of Hell to reclaim your voice, with each stage taking about 20 minutes depending on your speed. Each level has its own unique and beautifully crafted aesthetic, which helps to set the grungy, immersive tone. Enemy variety is perfect for the length of the game (which is unfortunately a bit too short), but the waves of enemies you face never feels repetitive, thanks in part to great level layout. It won't take most players long to complete the game, but side challenges to improve your loadout help to stretch the play time.On a personal note, it was initially quite difficult for me to put more emphasis on attacking to the beat instead of when you feel you need to; but after about two hours, I was bobbing my head along with the beat and making sure I was in positions where I could afford to wait and time my actions. For those who give this game a shot, please don't be disheartened if you don't get it at first; it might take a bit of effort to change into that mindset, but once you get there, it's truly a great experience.And it absolutely deserved Best Soundtrack in the Game Awards, the music was phenomenal, it's just a shame it hasn't yet been appreciated by enough people to influence the vote.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, cool concept. But:Unknown is a dumb name. The music is very good, but it's on the safe side. Metal is an incredibly diverse genre and since this game seems to be a sort of celebration of the genre, I wish the music was more varied. The selection of songs here is very "safe". Very mainstream sounding metal. And it doesn't really correspond with the setting or the levels. There was one level with an egyptian theme, which would've been a great opportunity to bust out something like Nile or Shokran, but alas. On the bright side, some very famous performers with their unique and familiar voices.Perks are unimpressive. There's only a handful of them and they're all mediocre. Lost opportunities. All the bosses use the same model and their fights are incredibly similar. The look the same, they fight the same. Even the add phases. They're not just copy paste bosses, but it'd be very hard to differentiate them from each other. So overall, not very interesting.  Paz has a good voice but his lines are uninspired. He just spouts idioms and exposition. Also a lost opportunity. The story is there. It only exists to facilitate the gameplay really. On its own it's pointless and uninteresting.Gameplay is really good. It's like doom but better. There's something very satisfying about a rhythm based shooter game. Movement is fast and responsive, guns feel good to use. Overall, I got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: This game came on my radar during the Game Awards when Matt Heafy introduced it and said he was going to be in it. My attention was immediately grabbed. What followed after that was a trailer that absolutely hooked me. While I didn't know everyone on the list, seeing Matt, Randy from Lamb of God, Tatiana from Jinjer, and Alissa from Arch Enemy made this game one I had to follow. Then this summer they dropped the demo and I played the same level for hours getting better and better. Now that the game is out, I beat it in 2 days and absolutely love it.Every song in the game is fantastic, but if I had to choose my top songs it would be these, in no particular order:This Devastation ft. Matt Heafy of TriviumBurial at Night fr. Tatiana Shmayluk of JinjerStygia ft. Alissa White-Gluz of Arch EnemyAcheron ft. Randy Blythe of Lamb of GodDissolution ft. Bjorn "Speed" Strid of SoilworkThe best part of this game is when you hit the 16x fury point, the vocals kick in, and you fall into a flow state. At this point you don't even think about the beat anymore. You are just flowing through slaughtering all the demons that get in your way. For me it was in Yhelm. I had just gotten the weapon of the level, the music was blasting, and I was just vibing. These words don't do it justice, it was an amazing experience.And the devs know how great these songs are. I love that they added a music player in the codex extras so after you beat a level you can go back and listen to the songs. Would be cool for them to add an option to listen to the song for each fury level in game. If they ever release the music outside the game, I am buying it because it is that good and I want to support them so they make more because this can't end here. There's too much talent and potential here. TL;DR: Game is absolutely fantastic. pick it up ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet, fast paced rhythm FPS. All I gotta say is if that sounds appealing to you, do yourself a favor and get it. I normally am not a fan of metal but I found it really hard to focus sometimes without headbanging both in game and in real life. Gun sounds are chunky and satisfying but don't drown out the music, enemies are fairly varied and fun to fight, gameplay is as solid as can be.Overall a fantastic experience, the only gripe I have is most arenas are a bit too small and cramped, which isnt in itself an issue except the player is so fast and maneuverable its easy to get stuck or fall off a cliff.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally give games a lot longer than 1 hour before giving a solid recommendation or discouragement, because I am a reasonable person who understands it often takes a lot more than 60 minutes to really get a feel for something.However, this one time I wanted to break my rule because for anyone who happens to see this, I wanted to mention a couple specific things for anyone thinking of picking this up.First off, I don't like rhythm games. I'm bad at them. Second, I'm fine with Metal, but I would not call myself a 'fan' most of the time. I don't hate it, don't love it. I love the AESTHETIC of metal music, but don't listen to it much myself. As such, I'd literally only heard of, like, two of the people featured on the soundtrack.Even so and despite both those points, this game immediately clicked with me. If you HATE metal it might be a different story, but as someone who thinks of it as a Sometimes Food, the soundtrack fits the vibe and really amps up the moment-to-moment feel of what's going on. The way different weapons have different rhythms feels so damn cool, and I haven't felt this good pulling out a shotgun since 1994.The biggest thing I wanted to mention if you're like me and slept on this one when you saw 'Rhythm Game' and that I didn't see mentioned in the game's description is that there IS an Accessibility Mode that will force all of your actions to occur with proper rhythm. Don't be afraid to use it if you just wanna shoot demons to a great soundtrack that changes intensity based on how well you're playing, as if the game itself is cheering you on. You won't be put on the Leaderboards with that mode engaged, but if I get to the point where I need to switch it on (and if I'm being honest with myself, it will probably happen) I guess that just means the #34,616th person on the list for level 1 is safe from me overtaking them.Even if you just want to experience this game as a 'Ride,' I recommend it for that, especially if/when it's on sale. It's really well put together.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely astonishing concept for a game, however it does lack a few qualities. First of all, there are only really two bosses in the game, one of which you fight literally like 9 times with differing variations. Also majority of enemies you fight will be fought over and over. This is pretty typical of arena shooters but I feel like they introduce every variation of enemy too quickly so it really doesn't feel fresh after the first 4 or 5 missions. Also, and this is just a personal opinion, as an elitist metalhead I found the music choice to be a little bit disappointing. The first few artists who make a cameo are pretty good. We get singers from Dark Tranquility, Arch Enemy, Lamb of God, etc. But I was really hoping for some Cannibal Corpse, Amon Amarth, Sabaton, Iron Maiden, etc. Instead we pretty much get stuck with metalcore the entire game. Like I said thats more of a personal thing.However the game as a whole is pretty fun and I would absolutely recommend it at a discounted price.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts off pretty good, but it falls off hard.ONLY get this game on sale for the music, gameplay wise is really bad for fps rhythm genre.Last 3 levels are so so bad, like new** painkiller level of bad, where you are stuck in a tiny room killing 4 types of enemies for 15 minutes bad,Shooting encourages you to fire slowly instead of hitting each beat, feels ok with a shotgun and crossbow, but feels terrible with anything else. Songs fluctuating in BPM were also not fun to get use to, or maybe it just felt that way bcs under x16 vocals cut off?7ish enemy types and 2 different bosses (1 being the end game boss), and even then most of them are just annoying shield, slow area spam or hit-scan projectile enemy design that dont belong in a rhythm game fps. They also super pre-track you so have fun ADAD spamming for best efficiency.Because of tiny areas, mobs spawn and often hit you from behind with 0 sound effects to indicate you will take any damage... terrible decision for R-FPS, at least add a danger red line from the direction on UI you would get hit by an ability. Not to mention that most enemy abilities are super quick and have so little animation that you can only dodge upon seeing the projectile that goes 500miles an hour towards you.Regarding the bosses*, OMG were they terrible, its just the same 1-3 flying skulls (6 times or so) that become immune and invisible for long periods of time to monologue at you... Tho, final boss was decent, even pretty good imo.everything locks you in animations... you want to use your special ability? well you have to wait for your gun to reload...For people that will come in saying "get gud" i placed 2k on leaderboards on last levels, 4 hours to beat final boss with doing some of the side quests too, only died once the whole game on 3 skull boss fight that just spawned a skull inside of me to insta-kill me when it had 3 shots from pistol in hp... so its not that the game is hard, it's that its not fun after first few levels when the novelty fades.

_childDocuments_.review: I suck at anything involving rhythm, so that this game included accessibility features for the beat-blind was great. Gorgeous game and cut-scenes. Creative depictions of Hell and its denizens, one shame though is the pace is so quick that you don't have time to appreciate the gorgeous design throughout. Great soundtrack, amazing music, sound design, and supporting mechanics. Satisfying polished shooting, though engagements often felt too predictable and repetitive. Great feeling weapons except the crossbow seemed lacking. Repetitive boss design was a letdown. Poor protagonist, antagonist, and narrator design... art was technically good but voice and manner were off. The mute protagonist was bland, scrawny, & gender neutral nothing about her screamed metal. The antagonist looked great but sounded like a mother reading bedtime stories to her children, not metal at all. The sound designers should have listened to the growl of female vocalists for inspiration; a heavy metal lord of hell shouldn't sound like the girl next door. The antagonists mewling at the end was also decidedly not metal, did I just beat the lord of hell or queen of the emo girls? The narrator sounded thematically out of place, like he should have been narrating a western or a game called "Country: Prariesinger" ...He sounded like a cowboy and not in the "cowboy from hell" Pantera kinda way. He sounded so out of place in fact I kept waiting for it to be revealed that he had formerly been a country singer doomed to hell in a "devil went down to Georgia" gone wrong kinda way... which would have been a lot cooler... but nope just a jarring design choice. Despite its few artistic missteps, feminine slant, and short length this game is a commendable rhythm game.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I hecking love this game!Keep in mind, I've only played a few hours of it as of writing this review. But the game amazed me the whole time I played it. The aesthetic of the game is very well done. The skull narrating the game as you play is a very nice touch. The hellish environments, and quite terrifying demons to fight. This game has an adaptive/dynamic music system, which is one of my favorite systems in any game. Consider it like - as the action intensifies and you're fighting better, different layers get added on as you fight. It's a system I wish many games would use more often. However, this game's music system is truly next level and done super well. The transitions are super fluid and seamless. As for the music itself, they are some great tracks. The cast of people they got to compose them is very impressive - metal's top musicians. The music tracks are very good quality. I'm very interested in getting ahold of the game's soundtrack, including the dynamic versions. As for the gameplay itself, it is similar to doom. However, it also has a rhythm game component to it. During the levels, you'll have music playing. If you do an attack on beat (usually a standard 4/4 timing) the attack will do extra damage and also gain some additional mechanics. This applies to everything you do - if you reload your guns on beat, you reload faster. If you use the shotgun on beat, it gains area of effect, etc. While you're playing a rhythm game, it doesn't feel tedious like a rhythm game does (at least in my experience of rhythm games.) I only have minor complaints about the game: As far as I've gotten, there isn't a way to block attacks. Also, the dodge mechanic is explained to you a bit late into the game - I could have used it several levels back and it would have avoided some unneeded deaths. I am not certain if you get the ability to block or timed block, but the addition of such a thing would be lovely in my opinion. There are some other minor things, like this one type of demon that can hit about an entire screen that is rather difficult to dodge (behemoths I think.) But I am glad that the game is very challenging, and quite difficult (I am playing on goat difficulty, which is the "normal" difficulty.) The voice acting is very good as well. I love the narration by Nyx (I think I got the name right - the skull companion you get.) The skull will narrate levels for you as you play through them, and it is rather well done and helps the overall aesthetic of the game. As for the lore of the game, it is rather good. It's nothing that you can take 100% seriously, but if you're willing to embrace some of the campier tropes of "hell," it's pretty awesome. Another thing worth mentioning is that there is a global leaderboard for high scores that is counted among all steam players. I'm not certain if it's per level or total during playing, but the presence of a leaderboard is nice. If you love metal, like DOOM, and are willing to try something pretty fresh and new, I'd highly recommend this game. It's pretty awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game from the trailer alone! So, simply stated, I bought it. The game is so much better than I can describe, so, try as I may, this may be a bit confusing. In the game, you MUST fire the weapon and have it hit your adversary at the exact moment that the song plays an up or down beat. As a musician, this is totally my jam- the Heavy Metal music is a plus!One thing that I wish to point out to the developers, is that there is nothing built-in for the hearing impaired. Simply adding a feature that amplifies the subwoofer, or an overlay that doesn't interfere with the experience would be a start. _childDocuments_.review: Metal: Hellsinger is an intense (and intensely fun) first person shooter slash rhythm game hybrid that nails its presentation and thankfully also sports solid shooting mechanics, fluid character movement and a tracklist that boasts vocals by some true heavy hitters of the modern metal era.   Clearly I liked Metal: Hellsinger, so if I've failed to sell you on it that's understandable. You're in luck though, since this game has something that used to be pretty standard for PC game releases (and seems lately to be making a bit of a comeback): a playable demo. Take advantage of this fact, no game review can measure up to forming your own opinion based on personal experience. I'd break it down as follows:If you love rhythm games but don't like heavy metal or first person shooters, you probably won't like this. If you love rhythm games and heavy metal but don't like first person shooters, you may still like this but it will challenge you. If you love first person shooters and heavy metal but don't like rhythm games (I fall into this category), you'll probably still like or maybe even love this. Metal: Hellsinger is exactly what I expected it to be because it's exactly what it said it would be. A hellforged double metalhorns-up from me, but as always your mileage may vary.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal concept for a game, but it's miles away from its potential.The single biggest flaw this game has is that its rhythm game aspect doesn't change to match a song's tempo. Each song has a set "metronome" behind it that corresponds with its average beats per minute. You're supposed to match all your shots and kills up to this metronome regardless of how the song might change. Almost every song in the game has multiple tempo changes, but this metronome never slows or speeds up to match. It's extremely jarring to be on a kill streak only to have the song reach a quiet bridge section that makes you completely lose your timing.While I like metal music, and think most of the songs are great both on their own, and to accompany a demon shooter, I can't help but shake the feeling I would be better off playing this game without the sound on. The game gives a visual on-screen queue next to your aim reticle that's there to help you match up to the aforementioned metronome. It's easier to keep with this constant, never changing rhythm without having a song playing that might distract you into deviating from it.If anyone has ever played a Guitar Hero/Rock Band game, you'll remember the calibration settings. This game has that as well, but I found it extremely difficult to get right. I looked around on the internet a bit, and found that this is a common issue a lot of players have. I can't say exactly why this is, but I've found different songs feel better with different calibrations, even though I'm using the exact same pair of headphones each time.Outside of the rhythm stuff, it has other conventional gameplay issues.I was disappointed in the similarity of all the boss fights. Excluding the final boss, they're almost identical in design, even if the arenas and move-sets differ slightly. They all even play to the exact same song. I get the desire to have a "boss theme" for your game, but that type of repetition doesn't lend itself well to a game who's primary mechanic focuses on music.I also frequently felt like I was searching for more stuff to kill to keep my streaks going. The levels in the game are mostly made-up of a string of loosely connected battle arenas (a la Doom 2016/Eternal), and you're locked into each arena until the scripted number of spawns are slain. The problem is that the spawns don't continue until every single enemy (no matter how small) has been picked off from the previous spawn, and the AI is also prone to get stuck on walls. As a result, it wasn't uncommon for me to finish a wave of monsters and then lose my streak looking around the arena for scrub #999 who had his toe caught on a staircase somewhere.The other single worst contributor to its pacing issues are the shield-wielding enemies. They were harder and more annoying than any other enemy in the entire rest of the game, and it introduces you to them fairly early on. Their shields are too large too shoot around without a good amount of precision that many guns don't have (you have to shoot their left hand), hitting their shields doesn't count as a "hit" so it's easy to lose your streaks, and they aren't particularly easy to strafe around in some environments either. I can't tell you the number of times one of these guys would linger around after everything else was dead because I just couldn't kill it with a reasonable amount of effort. It was a great way to completely destroy some otherwise amazing action sequences, as my streak and music would die during all the extra seconds I would have to spend trying to jump around to get behind one of these guys' shields.Despite some of these glaring flaws, this is still a good, fun game. You will still enjoy it if you like metal music and can get past the feeling of handicapping yourself by leaving the music on. I'm giving it some tough love here because I WANT it to succeed and be better. I want Hellsinger 2 someday, and I want them to get the music matching right to make it the true rhythm shooter everyone dreamed this could be. I fully support what they're trying to do here, and what they have is still a lot of fun, it just has a lot of missed potential.

_childDocuments_.review: A Symphony of Metal Greatness!Metal Hellsinger is an absolute gem for fans of both rhythm games and metal music. From the moment I picked up the virtual microphone, I was completely immersed in its electrifying world. The combination of intense first-person shooting and rhythm-based mechanics creates an innovative gameplay experience that I've never encountered before.The game boasts an incredible lineup of metal tracks that not only serve as the backbone of the gameplay but also keep your adrenaline pumping throughout. The synergy between the visuals, the beats, and the action is simply mind-blowing. I found myself losing track of time as I tried to perfect my performance on each level, all while battling hordes of demons in a captivating underworld.Metal Hellsinger's attention to detail is astonishing. The devilish landscapes are meticulously designed, each level feeling distinct and immersive. The variety of enemies keeps you on your toes, requiring quick reflexes and a good sense of rhythm to triumph over the chaos. And let's not forget the epic boss battles that make you feel like a true metal hero.The character progression and customization options add depth to the game, allowing you to tailor your experience and enhance your abilities in ways that suit your playstyle. The integration of your actions into the music score creates a seamless connection between player and game, enhancing the feeling of accomplishment with every well-timed shot and note hit.As a metal enthusiast, Metal Hellsinger was a dream come true. It's more than just a game; it's a journey through an auditory and visual symphony of metal greatness. If you're looking for an exhilarating, unique, and positively head-banging experience, Metal Hellsinger is an absolute must-play. Horns up! 🤘

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a phenomenal game. Great music by great artists, fantastic visual design, and pinpoint accurate gameplay. This is a recommend for anyone who is a fan of music or shooters.Though I do have 2 issues... Well, one issue and one semi issue. The issue is that if you aren't really interested in leaderboard stuff, it's a short, short game. It only took me about 4-ish hours to fully beat it, 5 and a half hours if you include time looking at the codex and that thirty minute period I had to walk away to chase my dog. This isn't BAD, since it's the kind of game that could drag, but I still wish there was more modes or something. The short length is both a benefit and a curse, but people who don't care about leaderboards and speedrunning might not get much out of itThe other semi issue is that the game is clearly setting up for a sequel. The story is engaging, but be ready to end the game with as many questions as you entered.Still, very fun, great gameplay loop, great world design, and the best possible music for the game. Definitely a recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I am not usually one for rhythm... anything really. I can sing along well enough, but ask me to keep a beat and I'll usually get distracted and fumble things real quick. That said, this game quite literally pulls you into a beat (sometimes to my detriment as I'd get into a beat, but it would be precisely between the beats asked of me!). You find yourself falling into things almost subconsciously, shooting, dashing, reloading, and jumping to the music. You strive to keep the rhythm, because the higher your multiplier, the more awesome the music gets. You become an unstoppable murdermachine with your own backup band, and before you know it, all the targets in front of you are gone, but you are scrambling to find more targets, just to keep the music going. Thank god for Paz or I'd lose my sweet tunes!I do have a few minor nitpicks of the game, but they are really just that. Minor nitpicks.I'd love to see more weaponry to pick from, but the fact you can only have 2 guns plus your sword and Paz each mission, makes the lack of options more bearable.Enemy variety is great to start with, but then they become slightly altered reskins of earlier baddies, with changed mechanics. 2 of the reskins in question could have been worked into entirely new enemies.Which brings me to the bosses. I understand the story reason why they are all the same (7 reskins), but it doesn't change that they all use the same base mechanics with slight tweaks to environmental hazards, or a new gimmick, or similar ever-so-slight changes. If there could have been more overall variety, it would be amazing.Last nitpick. The game is a bit short. I blew through this entire game and all the challenges in roughly 5 hours, in a single sitting. Fortunately they cliffhangered a possible sequel, so more may be on the horizon.Really what my complaints all boil down to is a need for MORE. I NEED more! More music, more guns, more enemies, more levels, more bosses, more challenges! Honestly, probably one of the better problems a game could have.I highly recommend this game. The music is phenomenal, the combat is superb, and the story isn't half bad. I just need more of it!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the tiny amount of playtime I have on this game, this is a pretty damn good game.Let me just start this out by saying: This is if Doom Eternal and BPM: Bullets Per Minute had a crazy game child, and it worked out wonderfully.The artstyle is beautifully chaotic and really gives off that "marching through hell" vibe, the music is A+, albeit only a few songs really caught my interest as I'm not a huge metal head. For those metal lovers though, you'll LOVE this game's soundtrack.The gameplay is... well, it's not quite BPM, and it's not quite Doom, to say the least. The rhythm aspect feels very unforgiving, first of all. You need to be close to frame-perfect with a 10-ish millisecond window in order to hit a perfect, although it's mainly for extra style points.The gunplay is pretty alright! Nothing super special, however using the fourth weapon in the game is VERY fun. You got shotgun, dual revolvers, explosive crossbow (what), and dual tomahawks that boomerang back to you and have infinite ammo.You can probably tell which weapon is my favorite, and I'll give you a hint; it's not the shotgun!The story is pretty unique, and got the story writer in my head going absolutely insane. What if the Hellsingers were a special force that drove off invaders? What if the Hellsinger's weaponry was hand-crafted by the finest forges of the Devil's army?Obviously none of these are in the actual game, but it gave me GLORIOUS ideas, and for that, I like it!Now onto the... bad.First of all, there's little to no replayability or postgame. Sure, you can speedrun the different levels, or go for high scores on the leaderboard, but other than that, there's not really much to go for after beating the main story. You have the Sigils of the Archdevils, but those are typically grabbed alongside the main story, and don't have any form of leaderboard what-so-ever.Second, there's no other gamemodes except for the main story. Give this game a good endless mode, and the ability to make a playlist of music to jam out to while playing said endless, and I'm basically sold. However, there isn't currently.Third and finally: *♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ they're building up to a sequel already the game just came out-*Overall? Pretty solid game! Perfect for metalheads who love their music to be heavy and hardcore, but a 50/50 split for those who aren't metal lovers but want to play a rhythm game shooter (since the only other one on the market is BPM, and that's more rock-focused.)Anyways yeah, go buy it if you want!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! If you like metal music and like the idea of slaying some demons as you head-bang away then you're probably going to like Hellsinger.The music is top notch as is but you add to that vocals from the likes of Serj, Alisa and other excellent metal vocalists; truly eargasmic. I'd be happy buying this for the music alone.The rhythm and shooting elements are solid too. Once you get into the groove of things it's really satisfying getting kills to the music. Decent weapon variety and sigils (like modifiers/buffs) to experiment with and find a build you enjoy.There's a story to guide your through the levels, nothing ground breaking but it does the job well.The protagonist has a cool design though. It's not that long, you can beat the game in a few hours on the easy difficulty. Beyond that it's all bout trying to get higher scores on the leader boards.My one main gripe with the game is the random fps drops in the middle of gameplay. Sometimes this lasts a few seconds and you're back to normal, but other times it lasts the rest of the level.Mod support was added after launch and opens up the possibility to play to your own tracks. Props for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good, I wouldn't say "overwhelmingly good" but it's still good and if you like rhythm games and don't mind a bit of metal music I will recommendQuick overviewBasically this is BPM with a more heavy metal + vocals, and a slightly different combat system. I think the soundtrack is a bit too much screaming metal than what I'm into.And I will not say "This game is better than BPM" because both games have good things about each.Pros: Setting, graphics, gameplay. I'm satisfied with this. The attack on beat is forgiving as you still attack it's just weaker if you make a mistake.Voice acting for Pak is great. I'm not sure why they chose that voice but it's a nice decision. Story is very well written, it's pretty simple, but enough for myself to enjoy.Weapons are good and have reload bonuses for timing. I have favorites and it's nice to change up and use different things.Also a pro: the final song with Serj.Cons:Enemies do not all attack on the beat. I don't know why but I'm moving and shooting to the beat and some enemies do attack on beat (I think) but the ones that fire whenever they want are harder to fight, causing you to have to quickly do a off beat maneuver, jump or dash. This might not be a problem for everyone but it is a mild annoyance.I would like it if there are no enemies then the combo meter just pauses. If you're wanting to keep the combo meter high you have to have the skull out and always clicking to fire it to keep the combo going. I don't agree with this. Why not "any" weapon? Why only the skull? And while on this topic, why does it have to keep going between battle rooms? Like when exploring or such.Minor complaint: I would like a glory kill with the other weapons. When you hit E you dash forward and pull out the sword to finish people off. I would've liked to do it with the other weapons but this is just a nitpick and not a real problem.Con, but this is personal because of my taste in music so you don't have to consider this as fully part of my review score.I said it above, I really like the music but I don't like most of the vocals. It's fully a personal opinion, but I honestly cannot stand playing the game more than like 30 minutes at a time because of the screaming lyrics.Exception: Serj did a great job, and the female voice accompaniments for stage 2 and 3 are also really good. (I actually was looking up some of them).

name: UNSIGHTED
detailed_description: Traverse Arcadia your way. Save your friends. Time is ticking. Alma is an Automaton that awakens to a world in ruin after the war with the humans. Anima, the resource that gives Automatons sentience, is running out and turning Alma’s friends into mindless killing machines, the UNSIGHTED. UNSIGHTED invites you to master it over multiple playthroughs to find the real catharsis the game has to offer. Can you save everyone? Key Features EXPLORE YOUR WAY - The world of Arcadia is massive and ripe for exploration, with many shortcuts to discover and maps both above and below the surface of the world. When one path seems too tricky, find new uses for familiar weapons and tools. RICH AND VARIED COMBAT - Build your perfect loadout to suit your playstyle. UNSIGHTED allows players to equip weapons in various ways, from dual-wielding swords to shuriken and shotgun combinations. Alma will need to use perfectly timed combat actions to trigger faster reload speeds or a massively damaging parry to survive in the city. CRAFT AND UPGRADE - Upgrade Alma through an extensive upgrade tree via chips you’ll find throughout your journey. Chips can be crafted or discovered, and each offers different bonus effects. Experiment with nearly limitless builds from the fast and efficient to the powerful and stylish. CHOICES MATTER - Alma’s withering life force ticks away in real-time and is the driving factor in the story of UNSIGHTED. Tarry too long in one spot, and you may find that critical NPCs have already become Unsighted before you meet them. Save or drain other Automatons of their anima for your survival. The constant passage of time can result in vastly different endings and allows for further playthroughs to stay fresh and exciting. HIGHLY REPLAYABLE + CO-OP - In addition to the main story UNSIGHTED also features additional challenge modes, BOSS RUSH and DUNGEON RAID. You can also bring a friend along your journey through Arcadia through full-featured CO-OP.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I've already played through this with gamepass, so I have more hours played than listed.This game honestly surprised me with how incredibly well done nearly every aspect of it was. I can be very nitpicky and critical about certain aspects of the games I play, but for the most part Unsighted just plays very well.TLDR; ♥♥♥♥ the combat is smooth and fast with no true bullet sponges and the exploration is good too. You can turn off the timers if they make you too anxious too! I really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like this game and if I were well off financially I would be buying a copy for all my friends.The combat is very fast-paced and manages to never feel like it drags on, with mechanics that allow you to finish fights faster, rewarding the player as they get better at the game, with the main example being parries. In most games with parries, they tend to either be lackluster or difficult to pull off and in turn very risky to use. In Unsighted, while you still need to get a feel for the timing of enemy attacks, it's forgiving in that it's a block as well, so if you attempt to parry too soon you aren't punished as badly. Now when you *do* land that parry? It staggers the enemy and leaves them in a vulnerable state while also restoring your stamina, which allows you to one-shot (or nearly one shot) most enemies. For bosses and specific tough enemies, you will need to parry two attacks or more (sometimes subsequently!) to stagger them, but the game rewards you for it by letting you chunk a large portion of their life.The game doesn't get too fancy with how weapons work, having your two flavours of melee weapon having their own basic move set. This works in the games favour since combat can begin and end very quickly and more complicated movesets would bog things down or have players end up using a select few of the moves available, making anything more complicated pointless.Exploration is the bread and butter of metroidvania's and games that are similar to the legend of zelda, with Unsighted getting top marks! There are many clever ways to get around in it with hidden nooks and crannies to explore, giving the player a lot of things to find and do. All the areas of the game, including the dungeons, are interconnected in one way or another, letting you pop into one from another to take a look around. This is especially important for a game like Unsighted due to the time limit you may have heard about already.Unsighted is a little unique in that it has a timer running constantly (except when in any of the menus/conversations of the game) for each major NPC in the game and yourself. The timer represents how much Anima remains in their bodies, it being a substance that grants them and all other robots (or automatons as they're referred to)sapience. It may seem daunting at first, anxiety-inducing even, but it's very lenient in regards to some of them having significantly more time than others, so it doesn't become too much of a balancing act in extending it with a special item..Well, until roughly mid to late game, but it's nice that you're eased into everything initially and not left to run frantically, shrieking the entire way as you try to avoid letting anyone die (right? you wouldn't *intentionally* kill anyone off, would you, you sick ♥♥♥♥?) You also can elect to turn off the timer altogether if it's too stressful for you.Another neat thing about Unhinged is its crafting system, in that as long as you know the recipe for something, you can make it at any crafting bench whenever you want, so if you want to spice up a run and do a gimmick, or just want to sequence break it over your knee for your current run, you can!Chips and Gears replace your standard equipment and consumables respectively. Chips range from boosting your attack a little bit, to ones that enable different playstyles with one example being a chip that reloads 1 round in your ranged weapon every time you hit something with a melee attack, or another that lets you have two shurikens travelling in the air at the same time. Gears instead of just being a different word for consumables, instead have assorted effects that either have a timer that ticks down when activated or a certain amount of charges before it falls apart. You can only hold 4 gears at once, but their effects are handy and the gears themselves are easy to make more of at craftbenches. Some of their effects range from negating a specified number of hits, to not having to reload your ranged weapon when it runs out of ammo for X amount of times.Controls: I have only played through it with keyboard and mouse, with it controlling surprisingly well, though you will want to rebind the block key (left ctrl) to another asap, from how often you can and will want to try to parry moves (I ended up binding it to my middle mouse button which worked out pretty well). Platforming can be a little tricky at first, since you can't slow your forward momentum too well and overshoot platforms if you do a running jump. Once you learn which gaps are too small for a running jump it becomes easy enough to adapt to doing normal jumps for them instead.My only gripes about the game are: - Running takes stamina, which is kind of annoying when quickly going from area to area, but gives you a chip early on that makes running not deplete your stamina at all (regenerating normally too even).- Certain moves you can do for most of the game are never shown or explained to you until late into the game. While not necessary to progress for most of it, with one or two specific areas it's needed, it feels kinda crappy when the game reveals you could actually do a move that would have helped quite a bit earlier in the game. Conversely, the specific move I'm referring to would probably let people sequence break certain parts of the game pretty easily which probably wouldn't be too conducive to someone's first playthrough.- I found one combo that effectively could make me immortal that would be relatively easy to achieve early in the game. If you have poor willpower like I do, it could make the game far too easy if you can't make yourself stick to a rule where you cannot abuse it. Mind you, this isn't a terrible thing to have available for players that are struggling through the game or just in one area, which in addition to its other difficulty options, make the game very accessible to players of all skill levels.All in all, this is a great game that has had a lot of love poured into it. I've already written far more than most people will want to read and still haven't covered certain aspects of the game in much detail (guns/ranged weapons, the story, music, etc.), but hopefully what I have written will allow anyone reading this to make an informed decision with this game.Also important information if you do buy this game: The dogs you save cannot be hurt, let loose the dogs of D'aaww/

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. One of the best games I have played.Recommended for metroidvania fans, fans of hyper light drifter/crosscode and those who just think they might enjoy this game.Positives:+Finished, polished game. One bug in the entire playthrough.+Original time mechanic that keeps the player on edge.+Solid, simple, challenging combat.+Interesting exploration, with good shortcuts.+Story is nothing amazing, but is interesting and gets the job done. +Relatively rewarding exploration.+Beautiful pixel art.+A lot of characters.+Good soundtrack.+A lot of (not too much) secrets to find.+Easy, but fun puzzles.+Long, but very good final boss.Negatives:-A little too short. 100%-ed it, true ending in 10 hours. However, those 10 hours were fantastic.-Combat is good, but feels like it might be missing a mechanic. A little too simple.-Bosses were a little too easy for me. Only 2 took me more than 2 tries. -Only 2 main weapon types. Still more than hyper light drifter.-Characters are not developed.What is missing for the game to be 10/10:-5 hours more playtime-Time mechanic to be developed further, characters to develop as they get closer to dying/ as they are given more life. -More challening bosses, another option for combat (magic spell? for instance). 1-2 more bosses.-Maybe a few harder puzzles that require use of every game mechanic.This is clearly too much to ask for but I am sure it would be a thing with a bigger budget. Still, this is a fantastic game that I would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, just want to say this isn't a Metroidvania. This is a Zelda clone. And a good one!I bought this game because I heard it really put stress on you. You have limited time to complete the game and NPCs will begin dying if you aren't fast enough. Pretty crazy, right? Well, I do have a few gripes with that, but let me point out the good stuff first:+ Amazing combat. You have access to both guns and swords, but most of your damage will likely come from melee weapons since they have the ability to do an extremely-easy-to-pull-off PARRY! Parrying an enemy stuns it and gives your next attack against it a massive damage multiplier. All enemies, all bosses, and most projectiles are parryable, so this is what combat ends up revolving around. Even though I call it easy, you still get that cool feeling when you walk into an ambush and clear it without taking a hit, so it never gets dull as you go through the game.+ Good dungeon design. Since this game takes after Zelda, it's not shy about inserting a few puzzles into its dungeons. The overworld as well has quite a few surprising secrets and side quests that you won't be expecting when you play for the first time.+ Sequence breaks. This is mostly for New Game+ (or New Game Extra, a separate mode where you have access to major exploration items from the start, but not your whole endgame inventory), but it was interesting to find out how many secret paths and shortcuts there were, and how tightly they were managed. The devs thought of everything!So now for the bad stuff.- Underwhelming story. Guess how much is really explained over the course of this story. If you guessed "all of it", you would be completely wrong and here's your dunce hat. Unsighted ends up spending so much of its time on the protagonist's relationships that it fails to answer several of the more important questions concerning the game's backstory. Why was there was a war? Who started it? Where are the humans now? Why are they so disorganized? Why do they seem to have no chain of command whatsoever? How did the automatons ever win anything at all at any point when they seem so extremely outclassed? I guess it doesn't matter. Look, there's two robot-girls kissing.- Fake pressure. I heard there was going to be pressure before I started the game, so I decided to go DEFCON 1 from the get-go and rush everything. I ended up completing the game in 10 in-game days and I felt pretty good about it. Zero NPC deaths! Zero! I'm a super awesome amazing hero, right? Well, credits roll and... the only achievement I get is the one for beating the game. No one really cares and apparently you're meant to play through multiple times anyway. So... why did I ever care? Why is this mechanic even in the game? All it did was make me shy away from general exploration and side quests since all of those things are less important than, ya know, saving the world. You can call that interesting, but when it has no payoff, it ends up being frustrating.- No post-game. Did I mention, if you bumrush the game and finish with just hours left on everyone's timers, you don't get to do any extra no-timer exploring afterwards? No, the game's over. Load the save and you get set back to where you were before fighting the final boss. If you want to do any actual exploring, that's what "Explorer" mode is for. You know, that mode that makes you feel like you're cheating?Basically, Unsighted is another game filled with missed opportunities. I recommend this game because the core gameplay and level design is very well done and very well executed, but you should probably know this before you start:The only pressure here is the one you imagine. Since the game does nothing to acknowledge your successes, just play it at your own pace and don't be shy about using Explorer. Shame on the devs for hailing the agony of defeat, but not the thrill of victory.
