_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had getting truly lost and exploring an expansive, highly detailed, and treasure-soaked world in a long while. Collectibles are hidden in places that are always satisfying to hunt down with a great variety of puzzles, combat trials, observation and the like. And all the while, enemies and bosses are a delight to fight with the combat feeling fresh and difficult from start to finish, giving the player many viable builds to modify thanks to the game's Chip system which behaves similarly to Paper Mario's badges, meaning you're never locked into a build that isn't working for you and you have limitless chances to experiment. I found myself actually having to change things up several times throughout my run where in other games sometimes it's easy to just find "the build" that works for everything (I didn't feel truly OP until the very end game, which is how it should be!) The art's also fantastic with some of the best UI/pause screens I've seen, which carries over into its gorgeous cutscenes and atmosphere-soaked environments.Some dungeons had a few pacing issues due to a lack of proper shortcuts and teleports, and the soundtrack felt a bit sparse in certain areas where it felt like the songs looped pretty quickly. And ultimately I'm not sure if I was the biggest fan of the game's timed gimmick since I didn't find the characters I could potentially save all that interesting (you spend very little time with many of them outside of your main companion and plot-specific characters you mostly see in cutscenes) and I felt like I should just prioritize myself since it equated more towards feeling pressured than anything else. This was a bit unfortunate cause it made me feel like I really wasn't allowed to explore the way I wanted to, and I don't think the solution to this problem is the idea of replaying the game entirely with more knowledge/skill effectively forcing you to speedrun it.Since meteor dust only extends any NPC's life by about half an hour, and there's well over a dozen NPCs to possibly save, I felt I could not possibly save anyone, so I decided to just let people die if they weren't useful to me. This felt off. I think a better solution would be permanently saving any given NPC with some dust instead so you felt like you could actually make a difference instead of giving pitiful rations to people that are going to likely die anyway cause you weren't fast enough. And since several important vendor NPCs had similar NPCs later in the game that did pretty much the same job they did, I felt the consequence of letting one of the "important" NPCs die wasn't actually a big deal and I quickly learned to just not care about anyone but myself.But those things did not ruin the experience and I still enjoyed my time with the game and likely will replay it at some point simply cause it's a lot of fun. If you're a fan of Hyper Light Drifter, this game will likely scratch a lot of those itches.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has some very light story spoilers.I've got some nitpicks. The NPC who follows you around for instance. Telling me to go and check out the entrance to an area that I've already been to, or saying that I don't have the equipment to get through a place when I do, telling me to remember a password that they just repeat to me when I'm near the relevant door, or saying that I should stay away from a monster I've already killed five of and are pretty easy to deal with on their own. The most they help in combat is dealing 7 damage, which is not a lot. So being basically a tutorial NPC is about as much as they do gameplay wise, so when they talk in the ending about how they've been helpful it feels a little off. After I got the grenade shotgun and the chip that doubles your guns shots (Though I got that much earlier), every enemy but the final boss was a corpse that didn't know it was dead yet. Shooting them was just a formality. This is a nitpick because at the end of the day I could have easily nerfed myself with a worse build for more of a challenge. I've got an issue a bit above nitpicky. Some of the bosses just did the same attacks over and over again. Edit: I should clarify, I mean the exact same attack, not attacks, for instance one of the bosses did an attack where one of the platforms is electrocuted repeatedly, and not using other attacks.Despite my complaints about her I got invested in keeping Iris alive, and I hemorrhaged dust trying to keep her and Cleo alive. I like how varied the designs for some of the automaton are. Some were clearly made for a purpose, while others just look like people. I don't like how your own lifespan is so long. It doesn't feel nearly as urgent to prioritize yourself, so the mechanic of sacrificing other automaton felt (mostly) pointless. A lot of NPCs I didn't get much interaction with even when I intentionally tried to converse with them, so I think that made it harder to get invested with any of them. Near the end I stopped exploring and harvesting and beelined towards beating the game to keep the ones that I were invested in alive. Though whether or not that's an issue with game design feels a lot more like a matter of perspective. And ultimately there is an option to just not have NPCs run the risk of going Unsighted ever. The NPCs acting different when they are 24 hours or less from going Unsighted was nice. One detail I like is that in my playthrough BB42 goes Unsighted, and when Olga was about to go Unsighted she brings up the fact BB42 was gone in her dialogue, and it's details like that which I think are very good details to have in games like this. Some of the NPCs had so long to live it really didn't feel like they'd die in any normal playthrough.The small crates that you find all over the world can be stacked on top of each other to reach places that I'm pretty sure you aren't supposed to at the point in the game that you are at sometimes (I could also use them in certain puzzles). Except, sometimes even doing that and even when it looks like you should be over and obstacle it stops you. I think the devs might be well aware of things like stacking the boxes, and leave points where it is useful to make you feel good because you FEEL like you are outsmarting the game, when in actuality the devs are entirely aware of the fact you can do that and intentionally letting it be done so the player feels smart. Though this is (sort of) at odds with me pointing out whenever Iris would tell me I don't have what I need to get through someplace even though I absolutely do. I like how items like cogs and elemental weapons followed a similar formula, so if you pay attention to the blueprints of cogs for instance (4 of the same material in a diamond shape) you can craft the other ones.Edit: Having now played for more hours, and clearing both the dungeon raid and boss rush with 0 deaths, I'd like to update my review a bit again. The fusion of "rougelike" and "metroidvania" in the dungeon raid is, interesting. It ultimately still feels very similar to the rest of the game but there are some things that make it stand out. A few of the areas provide different materials for different things that the player might want to craft, and the fact that the areas generate with obstacles that you can't get through without items means in theory you would carefully pick areas to get crafting materials to make items like the hookshot so you can get through those obstacles, but all you get is more crafting materials which is useful for cogs. However if you already have every weapon and item you want that you can craft already there is no point in exploring unless you want cogs but I never really found them all that necessary and you are handed them for free anyways. And I just picked the areas haphazardly anyways. There was also some generation that seems completely impassable (For instance, only way to the rest of the floor being a lava lake) without certain items, but presumably something would keep that from generating if the player doesn't already have the items required. The boss rush is basically just more of the combat in the game, but it can force you more into certain builds you might not otherwise bother with which I think is good.In spite of my issues, I still enjoyed this quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stunning. Tight gameplay elements, interesting story and charismatic characters that feel really integrated with the world presented. _childDocuments_.review: Great top-down Metroidvania/Zelda-like with very snappy, responsive combat & movement (if you like parrying stuff this game is it), gorgeous pixel art style, great exploration, and overall fantastic atmosphere/worldbuildingThere is a really unique timer mechanic that adds to the tension and atmosphere where characters may eventually die off if you don't give them a specific item, but this can be turned off for first/casual playthroughs for those who want to take their time to explore the maps at their own pace (and I'd probably actually even recommend first time players do so)All in all, big recommend if you are into Metroidvanias and/or Zelda type games, and especially if you are a parry junkie (like me). +1 for lesbian robots

_childDocuments_.review: Backtracking can be frustrating at times, diversity in melee weapons is only provided through elemental variations, occasional perspective issues (which you get used to as you play), the difficulty curve of main bosses isn't smooth (though it's compensated in the final and secret boss), and there are certain level design choices that might annoy players, making them some of the game's biggest shortcomings. Apart from these aspects, everything else is equally good, even exceptional. The game feels like a open buffet, taking the best elements from various games and seamlessly integrating them into its own gameplay. Throughout the game, the introduced mechanics and corresponding puzzle, combat, and platform elements will truly captivate you. The puzzles are cleverly designed, ranging from easy to challenging, and they are integrated into the gameplay flawlessly. The Cyberpunk theme features a well-crafted story, although some parts may be cliché and predictable, the events happening within its world and the adventures you experience manage to engage you beyond gameplay. It was one of the finest games I've ever played. I highly recommend it to everyone. NOTE: I finished the game in approximately 15-20 hours, 103.4% completed. It was open in the background for 20 hours. Don't let the 41 hours fool you, though. The game promises an average of around 10 hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Words fail to describe the itch this game scratches. Unsighted is a magnificent addition to video games as a history and medium of art. I've never felt an indie game with more polish, attention to detail and amazing presentation. I deeply enjoyed my time with this world, these characters and the story that Studio Pixel Punk have created and told here. This Earth decimated by years of decay, while bleak, presents hope through the Automatons and the life that is ever present despite the humans having abandon it for so long. The love and care that went into creating every side quest, every side character and especially your main cast is beyond what most AAA studios will ever produce in their lifetimes. The story is so well paced and presented as well, with weight and stakes being at all time high. While I may have personally played on Explorer Mode, I certainly intend to return on a second and many other playthroughs on the normal and harder difficulties. And don't get anything mixed up, you still feel the rush of punishing combat and exciting gameplay while on Explorer. I simply enjoyed the reduced stress of not trying to keep everyone alive. Every character is so much fun to interact with. Upgrading weapons and health was relatively well done and balancing of the meteor dust is near perfect. Progression is probably my favorite aspect of the game as when you learn how to wall jump or when you grab your first hookshot, there is no larger dopamine dose in the world. Alma is an extremely well written and designed character. The backstories of those who needed one were well fleshed out. What an amazing package writing wise but let's start talking about the absolute bangers this soundtrack provides. As soon as I heard Urban Ruins from the demo, I knew this game was going to sound great but Oh. My. Goodness. From tracks like Blossom in Gear Village and Sambinha in shops with the side characters, to rockin' tracks like The Guardians whenever a boss is teased and Scorching Steelworks, my personal favorite alongside Crystalline, both ambient but grooving dungeon crawling themes. Even the sound effects are satisfying to listen to. From the sound when recharging at a terminal and finishing crafting an item, to the sound when perfectly parrying an enemy's attacks (doing this multiple times in a row is heavenly and feels like you are in fact a god gamer).Moving onto the visuals, woo boy what a delectable icing we got for this already well baked cake. A pixel artist dream come true, even with so many assets and movements going on, I maybe ONCE experienced a slow down during gameplay but that might've simply been the specs on my PC. This game runs beautifully and looking over so many of quieter moments or even more hectic ones yields so much appreciation for the work that went into every single input you make. The stunning moments in Automaton Factory, the frozen Aquarium and the underground ruins are eye candy and even sweeter are the areas in between with so much ruin and detail in its landscapes. Though I am no expert on game design, I try to recognize the limitations/problems of the games I play and it is hard to come up with those for Unsighted. Maybe you don't connect with the characters, perhaps the combat is too difficult for you to pick up (despite accessibility options), or if you just can't get into the gameplay loop. However, I think with the things I have listed here, I have to say it is hard to not want something nearly as polished, cared for and well made as Unsighted. Easily stolen one of my top 10 games of all time and I am EAGERLY awaiting what the creatives behind this game have in store for us. Thank you, Studio Pixel Punk for a masterpiece that will certainly be a (at the very least for me) bicentennial must-play. Apologies if I missed censoring any spoilers.

_childDocuments_.review: People pass on this game because of the time mechanic. They shouldn't.Unsighted is everything I love in a videogame: it has good and tight gameplay that rewards learning, it has an amazing level design with lots of branching paths and freedom to explore and solve puzzles however you choose, and it had a story that is intimately tied to the gameplay.The time mechanic is absolutely amazing: it ties well into the narrative, give weight to your actions, gives you good rewards for exploring and, most important, creates a trade-off between exploring and advancing the story. No game dared do this before, and it works wonders.After beating it the first time the possibilities are endless: doing boss rushes, playing on new game + or trying to 100%. Speed runs are particularly special: you can skip several sections of the game and solve puzzles using items you shouldn't have by then.The art and sound design are stunning and unique, while evoquing a sense of nostalgia. The story, while I didn't care for the text and how the plot is delivered, ties really well with the gameplay.Long story short: go play Unsighted. Now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good. I'm a big Dark Souls fan, and this game scratches my Dark Souls itch in a way no indie game ever has. The developers seem to really understand some of the things that help make a Souls-like: Enemies are varied, and going to a new area means learning new enemies. Enemy attacks are well-telegraphed.Timing accuracy is more important than fast reactions or fast button-mashing.Parrying is risky, but very rewarding.Feedback for parrying feels really good.Your health is low, but death is relatively non-punishing. Like in DS1, there seems to be some fun sequence-breaking available if you know what you're doing.Also, this game does some things well that Dark Souls doesn't. For instance: movement feels very clean and fast. If your stamina runs low, you can continue stunlocks using your sidearm pistol, which feels very cool and helps a lot against certain enemies.On top of all that, this game has some excellent queer representation and I love that.As for downsides of this game... I dislike the shuriken. It feels awkward and slow to control, and there are sections of the game that (seem to) require it. But thankfully those sections are fairly short.I think it'll end up being a decent bit shorter than a Souls game as well. But, if you're into Dark Souls, I'd highly recommend giving this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is a little more than the average indie game - but only a little more. Like most indie titles, Unsighted borrows heavily from other properties. It reminds me of Cave Story (in a good way), Hyperlight Drifter (in a bad way) and Dark Souls (in a ‘parry and dodge’ kind of way). Puzzle platforming and combat are the primary focus, as you explore and backtrack your way through a variety of pixelated environments. Frankly, there’s nothing new on display here, but that doesn’t have to be a bad thing. It just means that a lot hinges on the execution, which is fairly solid. Combat encounters are challenging but fair, puzzles are simple but require just the right amount of thought, and the controls are crisp and responsive. It’s not fresh, but it is well considered and delivered - the experience was a slight cut above what I expected from a small budget title.Having said that, I’m struggling to think of a reason to play this over something like Crosscode or Blasphemous, very similar games that simply do it better. I suppose one thing that Unsighted has over those games is the strong focus on sapphic relationships. The vast majority of the characters in Unsighted are robot lesbians, which is a bold narrative choice and brings something interesting to the table. The focus is totally on the women here, and when so few games regulate their women characters to the background or banish them entirely, that’s worth celebrating.Unfortunately that’s twice now that I’ve said “it’s unimpressive, but there’s stuff to like here!”, and that basically sums up Unsighted in a nutshell. It’s a 6/10 game when I expected a 4/10 game, which is hardly a ringing endorsement. I will concede that it has the potential to make some people very happy with what it has to offer. I just wasn’t one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game that I wanted Hyper Light Drifter to be.  If it looks at all interesting to you, get it.Which is not to say that HLD was bad; it was a good game, but a bit short and simple for my tastes.  Unsighted offers a similar post-apocalyptic, pixelated environment, but with a much, much wider varieties of weapons and power-ups.  There are large areas to explore and lots of secrets to find, and while the game seems to have an intended order for progression, it's also obviously designed with sequence breakers in mind, and you can do nearly anything in any order if you know what you're doing.  Combat is fun, fast-paced, and has a wide variety of ways to approach any situation.The developers have also been incredibly receptive to player feedback and are constantly making small tweaks to make the game more accessible to players.  The user interface, controls, and difficulty are all highly tweakable to make the game just right for you, and if there's any issue that might prevent you from being able to play the game, just let them know and they'll likely respond.

_childDocuments_.review: pros:- combat- exploration- puzzles- secrets- musiccons:- storySo, I was initially put on to this game by IronPineapple's Steam dumpster diving video where he mentions it in an offhand sort of way, and I was put off by the negative reviews which complained about the pacing and amount of puzzle elements. When I finally ended up playing the game myself, the best way I can describe it is a quintessential GBA action-adventure, a la Minish Cap or Boktai. It hits all of the sweet spots, mechanically and exploration-wise, and while, yes, there are a lot of puzzles, I think if you go into this game with the expectation it is like Minish Cap you won't be surprised. I haven't played CrossCode or Hyperlight Drifter, but what I can say is that this game has very polished mechanics coupled with GBA-like exploration. I was able to complete the game in 7 in-game hours on my first run and I ended up sequence breaking by accident several times. That's fun. I discovered a lot of things early on that apparently the game only tells you about much later, and because I explored so much I was able to find equipment that made early dungeons trivial, but it was still fun.The combat is very nice, however I never once felt like using a gun during a fight, which is a big failure I feel. The parry felt smooth and once you reach the endgame even the hardest monsters feel trivial to fight once you've mastered the parry. There are a few 'tools' that lose all utility outside of their respective dungeon. If you are going to play this game, play on Explorer Mode and disable the Character Timers on your first run. You don't need them, it doesn't add much to the game other than a story tie-in for urgency, and it actually takes away from the exploration. You can always do a New Game+ run or just turn it on later anyways. The only main con I had with the game was the story. It was meh, not terrible but not memorable in any way. The characters are forgettable and the motivations were lackluster. I don't care about the robot lesbians and is there a reason 90% of the cast is female? It was so overt that it stood out and when it stands out you've done something wrong. I haven't played Boktai in about 15 years and I can still remember the story, Lita, Zazie, Sabata, Camilla, Hel, Ringo, the vampire twins. I won't be able to say the same about this game's story, and it's another reason I recommend playing on Exploration Mode and getting over the feeling that you're somehow playing the game on easy when the timer doesn't make you care about the characters any more than without it. What this game did do though is make me stay up overnight to finish dungeons and keep exploring. It really does bring out that exploration addiction I had when I played GBA games as a kid. While I don't think I will revisit it as I'm not one to revisit and 100% a game just because the New Game+ is the same game but harder, I did get my money's worth and honestly it was the most fun I've had in a game in a long, long, LONG time.

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is a top-down metroidvania from the Brazilian studio Pixel Punk and it’s one of the best games I have played in this genre. You are Alma, an android and your goal is to save your fellow androids from running out of Anima, the energy which vitalizes all androids, and thus to prevent them from becoming “Unsighted”.It borrows game mechanics and visual style from the likes of CrossCode and Hyper Light Drifter. Tight combat, a good story, plenty of puzzles to solve, interesting boss fights and diverse weapons to use in order to progress to different parts of the map. Different areas have unique weapons, enemies and visual tones, all of which combine to a cohesive, beautiful world. I should mention that in the default mode, the androids run out of time quite fast and you will have to make decisions as to which NPCs to keep alive. You can, however, choose the Explorer mode and make the time run much slower. This will save you from the stress of rushing the game and you can still keep the difficulty otherwise unchanged. As much as the Explorer mode is not the “intended” mode to play the game, I have found it to be the preferable one for my taste. The difficulty is just right. Whether in combat or puzzles, you will always feel the challenge but not in a frustrating way.No part of Unsighted is a masterpiece, but it’s a very ambitious game. It tries too many things and I find it marvelous that it succeeds at most of them. Unsighted is the sleeper hit of 2021!

The story is pretty different and interesting. Would have loved a few more gun options. Overall this is one of my favorite games I've played this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is very good. I bought it because I recently replayed Secret of Mana and Secret of Evermore and was looking for similar gameplay. The gameplay in Unsighted is like a grownup version of those older games. Everything is more difficult, but also more interesting.To start, lets talk about the elephant in the room: The biggest reason why this game will never be very popular is that you have to finish the game in a certain amount of time. As a result you never just think "I'll just relax and play Unsighted for an hour." You always need to make progress. There was at least one evening where I didn't play because I was tired and didn't think I would play well. So instead of wasting time, I just didn't turn on the game. The pressure was never really big for me, I did explore all the dungeons pretty thoroughly, but you do always feel rushed.Combat is great, if a little overwhelming at first. You always have a melee weapon, a ranged weapon (with active-reload mini-game), plus dodge and parry buttons. Compared to the games I mentioned at the beginning, it's a lot. In fact I found combat to be more difficult at the beginning than at the end: I killed the last two bosses on my first attempt, where early in the game I would die to normal enemies. The controls just took some getting used to. While a more gentle introduction and better difficulty curve towards the end would have been better, I still enjoyed myself a lot throughout. If you have trouble early on, that's normal. I actually like the way it was balanced towards the end: Challenging enough that I had to really focus, but easy enough that I did beat the bosses on the first try.Puzzles and exploration are just interesting enough, without being too difficult on a timer. Maybe it's because I have played a lot of metroidvanias, but I could usually figure out where I had to go and what I had to do with only a little effort. I only got stuck once for like ten minutes before I realized what I was supposed to do.The story is fine. It's not going to keep you playing. But there is also nothing wrong with it.I liked the length of the game. It felt right. The only thing I wish I could have done more was explore. I feel like I missed some stuff. Maybe I should have played without the timer (this is an option) but I thought I should play the game as intended. As it is, I finished the game in a good amount of time and was very happy with the experience at the end.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: to everyone who thinks the game is bad due to timers on chars; play on explorer your first run through, or realize that you dont need everyone to survive to beat the game. theres also cheesy ways to get meteor dust other than exploration, and i dont mean the girl who generates it.i've got around 9 hours of play time in one file and 2 in another where im playing with my partner as of writing this, 30 hours or so with the game up, so keep in mind that ive spent a lot of time with the game idle or in menus or conversations, buuuuut; the combat is great, seriously stellar, one of those games where you hardly ever feel like you didnt deserve to get hit. attacks are telegraphed, but still the game keeps you trying harder and harder as it goes ontheres a decent amount of different styles of combat to try out, with my personal favorite being to parry and get several thousand damage every time you attack, but theres also ranged play, mixed, and so on.the soundtrack is alright, not the best ive ever heard, but pretty alright, nothing super catchy save for that damned fire area which will get stuck in your head if you let it.the art is great, though you can check that out easily enough.sequence breaks are available but not advertised, as should be the case. the "best end" is practically just begging for you to realize how easy it is to sequence break when you know the game's tricks already, though realistically if youre playing on explorer with the timers off i dont think you really need to do the work of the best end, and should save it for later.---------------the places i think that the game could use improvement are:allow people to turn off the timers on all difficulty levels; (maybe for a cut of their resources and bolts gained? _childDocuments_.review: Fans of the top down perspective "Legend of Zelda" games will find alot to like about this game. For the most part alot is similar but Unsighted manages to make it's own identity in allowing for an interesting amount of sequence breaks and shortcuts that open up as you get key equipment. Some of these items would be right at home in a Zelda game like the hookshot or jump boots.Combat:The combat and in Unsighted manages to be a bit deeper than the 2d top down Legend of Zelda games as you have analog aim of your ranged weapons, parries, charge attacks, jump attacks, and more. Parries are incredibly strong and the game knows this as you tend to be thrown into arenas with multiple enemies forcing you to pick off the smaller ones so you don't get clipped by an attack after parrying another one. Without spoiling too much you also get access to a few different weapon types (Sword, Axe, gun, flame/ice throwers, grenades, Shuriken which can be maneuvered mid throw, and even the hookshot) allowing for various ways to approach fights.Platforming and Puzzles:Platforming in this game opens up fairly early once you pick up the jump boots allowing you to do a small hop up walls. As you progress most of the platforming revolves around puzzles with switches and your various weapons that aid in traversal (like ice weapons for creating platforms on water or the hookshot for clinging to walls over pits). There will be familiar puzzles like pushing blocks around and there are a plethora of secret hidden collectibles that usually take some time and effort to find.Explorer mode vs normal mode:This characters in this game (including yourself) only have a limited amount of time to live which can be extended via finding meteor dust around the world and giving it to said characters. This adds a tension to each moment in the game and encourages the player to use their movement options and fast travel points to plot quick routes through the game. While I think this system can be alot of fun in forcing players to think about how they play, it can be very frustrating if you get stuck somewhere due to not knowing where/how to proceed. Anyone whose played metroidvania games knows about getting lost and when that happens here it can kill some of your favorite NPCs if you don't make copies of your save to rewind to after you find out how to proceed. That and this time limit does wind up discouraging you from exploring previously inaccessible hidden items as after a certain point extra equipment isn't really worth finding knowing that you might have several NPCs approaching death. All this might be discouraging to players that like to take their time which is why you are allowed to turn off the timer at any point in the game. I am unsure how this effects the games endings so you may need to look into that yourself.Replayability:After beating the story mode you can challenge yourself with a boss rush or a rougelite battle mode. You also gain access to a new difficulty, new game + with all your old equipment, and New Game Extra which lets you craft key equipment early if you know the recpies. New Game Extra seems to be a mode begging to be speedrun as you can seemingly play the game in any order you want.Closing notes:While this game is advertised as a Metroidvania it seems to be closer to a Zelda-like game with your progression through the game being inspired more by Metroidvania games. This game has high replay value with extra modes and difficulty. The combat (largely parry focused), platforming, puzzles, and planning quick routing seem to be the main draws of this title so if those seem like fun things to you then get this game. This indie title is well worth the price. This title begs to be speedrun with how much you can sequence break and how much mobility you get by the end game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just doesn't want to be ~8 hours long and on a timer. The amount of (what feels like) needless mechanical complexity put onto the player seems to suggest that this is supposed to be closer to Crosscode in length, and even that game has the decency to layer on that complexity slower than this. I am 2 hours into the game and already I have a sprint, a dash, a parry, 2 types of attacks, a crafting grid, crafting blueprints you can buy, items you can buy (which seem to have a huge overlap with those you can craft?), chips you can slot in for effects, gears which you can use for temporary effects, FISHING(?!?!?!), and I probably missed some of them. The inclusion of any of these mechanics would be neat in most games, but in a game where you are explicitly told to hurry the f*ck up or else people will actually (narratively) die? I am getting conflicting messages here. Should I take the time to explore these systems or should I focus on the goal. And even if I do explore these systems, there seems to be an absolutely minuscule amount of content on which I am apply these mechanics on. To have to learn all this at the start is just overwhelming. The pixel art is great (except for the character portraits, hate those), the music is groovy, and the story it tells... well the character writing I don't like but its not bad its just not what I like, the story itself is fine. The time limit, I like the idea but there is just too much complexity added on top. It feels like it forces me to stress and play the game in the most unfun way I can manage. I am turning the timer off and might update this later as I keep playing, but right now its just souring the experience. And the little fairy helper that tells you "I think you just died, have you tried actually using all your ♥♥♥♥?" is just a slap in the face, if there is a reason why I do not recommend this game, its that feature right there. I hate that with a passion.After beating the first boss (and playing a little extra): Outside of the timer I really don't think that this game does anything special. It combines a lot of mechanics that are fun together but that I don't find fun when all thrust on the player at the same time. I think hour 2-3 is about when I stop accidentally pressing the wrong button for an action and at that point in this game I am fully inundated with just too much stuff. I would like it more if it was a good deal longer and taught things to the player at a much slower pace, or just have less for the player to learn. Hyper Light Drifter felt like it had it right, with almost minimal mechanics for a maximal effect. Right now it feels like a 20+ hour game compressed down far too much.

_childDocuments_.review: UNSIGHTED is a special little Metroidvania. I am a massive lover of the genre and this is up there with the best.[Update after completion of the game: There is a special secret ending and secret final boss which is definitely the best way to beat the game.]The game blends a slightly Souls-Like combat with it's entirely own way to play. There's also some hints of Zelda in the game [here's looking at you double hookshot] among other things. The combat is very snappy and responsive and overall very satisfying once you get stronger to go through an entire dungeon without dying or taking a single hit. There's also ranged combat that works quite well with an "active reload" feature to time properly to get shooting again sooner.The story isn't groundbreaking or anything, but it works and I found myself moderately invested the whole way through. I've seen a small handful of people in the past claiming this game has some sort of SJW agenda but I don't think it does. I never once noticed the game trying to push any agenda. While yes, most of the characters seem to be female and/or of color, that doesn't really bother me, nor matter to me in the slightest and it doesn't impact the experience in any positive or negative way.Overall, this game is REALLY good and super fun to play. The soundtrack is on point and feels great to the ears the entire way through. The dungeon music is where it really shines. I honestly wouldn't have minded if the game were a bit longer. But this is one of the best Metroidvania's I've had the pleasure of playing in a long time, the last time I really enjoyed a game of this type this much was back when I played Rabi-Ribi which is also amazing and I would highly recommend if you're a head over heels lover for the genre, don't let the cutesy aesthetic of that game fool you, it's quite challenging and the gameplay is some of the best in the genre.This game deserves way more attention than it's gotten. All in all, I'd give it a solid 9/10. This is a must buy for any Metroidvania lover!

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe this game in a word, it would be...fun.If I had to describe this game in many more words, well... I loved it. It's been a long time since I've felt compelled to stay up late just to explore a bit more...only to end up exploring a LOT more. It was such a joy to play. I'll address the controversial part off the bat: I recommend playing Explorer mode the first time and opting out of the time limit requirement (where NPCs have timers and go "unsighted"/non-sentient when it runs out, which can only be increased by rare items) at least the first time around. I absolutely understand why the mechanic is implemented, and how it serves the story, but I just love exploration and being thorough (103% map completion woo!), so that was never going to work for me. Even if I wasn't inclined that way, I think it would be more enjoyable to play with a time limit after you're familiar with the basic mechanics, map, progression, etc. This game seems like a real treat for speed runners. Aside from opting out of the time limit requirements, Explorer mode offers some other difficulty options that can be turned on/off whenever you want. As far as I know, the other modes don't offer any such options. You could even play Explorer and use none of the recommended difficulty modifiers at first and then adjust based on how you feel as you progress. It seems to lock you out of certain achievements but would offer the same challenge as standard difficulty. As for more general game stuff: The plot isn't entirely groundbreaking but it still manages to be compelling with its lore. The characters don't get as much unique dialogue as I'd like but are, well, likable (especially Tobias, though maybe I'm biased because DOGS). The map is great--loved the ability to place so many markers to revisit after gaining new abilities. As you can tell just by looking at the preview images, the art is awesome. The combat is great, especially the parry mechanic. Upgrades, particularly chips and cogs, were interesting for strategy. Crafting was straightforward. The UI can be frustrating at times (would love to have the ability to sort things and have a button reserved for secondary weapon switching) but does the job. I haven't used it, but there is a multiplayer option. LOVE the dog companions, though I'm not sure how balanced they are in timed/standard mode (dogs fight alongside you, with their own unique stats, and require food (readily available) and time (for naps; 3hrs in-game) to stay with you). In general, one of the flaws of the game is its tendency to hide really useful mechanics/requirements. For example, there are combat mechanics that don't get revealed until late-game but could have been used the whole time . Perhaps more importantly, there are no indications that a "true" ending could be reached (if you didn't use a guide, you'd likely need to wall-hug the whole map, which is ridiculous), or what the specific criteria would be. As such, I highly recommend looking at the guides once you're reaching the endgame. This is an amazing achievement for such a new studio. I'm so impressed and delighted by this game, I've been trying to encourage all my friends to try it out. I really do highly recommend it, and I'm excited to see any future games from these developers!

_childDocuments_.review: UNSIGHTED is an absolute gem of a game that excels in several areas: great soundtrack, great combat, tight mechanics, and beautiful visuals. It is a lovingly crafted experience that goes above and beyond in regards to its metroidvania-ness (I've never seen anything quite like it, and I consider myself an afficionado to the genre).While, yes, the timer clashes with the exploration aspect of the game, I found that it greatly enhances the experience by providing a lot of tension. Once the timer gets low enough and you start paying more attention to it, you try your hardest knowing that if you mess up (being defeated in combat, for instance) your friends' lives could pay the price. To be fair though, the timer is very generous: in my first playthrough I managed to save everyone and still had considerable time left. That said, if you are really, really turned off by this, you can disable the timer at any time.As for the meat and bones of the game: they are superb. Combat feels great and snappy, and once you get used to the top-down perspective, controlling Alma feels great, especially when you unlock more movement options. With the way the game's map and mechanics are designed, future playthroughs allow you to completely crush the standard game sequence, specially if you stumble upon the game's secrets. If you are into speedrunning, this is a must play.As mentioned, the game excels presentation-wise. While the writing is somewhat subpar, the game makes up for it with beautiful pixel-art and a stylish soundtrack that sets the mood very well.If you are a fan of metroidvanias or are looking for a game with tight combat, I highly recommend UNSIGHTED.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, gorgeous game full of charming characters and very tight combat. The devs have a lot of love for many games, and it shows in all manner of delightful little similarities and callbacks. There's a load of mechanic-based accessibility options so that the game's story can still be experienced if you're having trouble. If you've enjoyed top-down Zelda games, Metroidvanias, Hyper Light Drifter, Hades, or Iconoclasts, you're bound to find something here to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: In short if you like Hyper Light Drifter and classic Zelda you should pick up this game.It merges fast paced, heavily parry-based combat system with Zelda-like exploration and puzzle solving.The art looks great and the OST is pretty bopping.The one nitpick I have is that there is a lot of going into the equip menu to switch between different items for exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: I just really like the game feel - I highly recommend picking up the demo and giving it a spin. Movement is fast and snappy, parry timing feels natural, puzzle progression is smooth, exploration feels rewarding...I don't think there's one gimmick to sell it on, but I think this game just nails the fundamentals in a way that many don't.I usually don't like this sort of time pressure mechanic, but the core gameplay works well when you're moving fast. Timing leniency for platforming/parries/puzzles don't feel excessively punishing. That said, I only just beat the first boss, and I haven't even touched any shops' inventory yet since grinding doesn't feel like an option, and haven't crafted much because I didn't buy blueprints and so on...I haven't tried "exploration mode" yet, so I can't comment on how much it'd loosen things up for people that really don't want to deal with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really like the game so far, haven't beaten it yet. Awesome pixel art and music, fun mechanics, interesting puzzles - the list goes on. It was hard, but got easier after learning the different fighting and movement techniques (parry is worth spending some time to learn properly early on). The puzzles were really fun. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing games for about 30yrs and I put off playing this game for a long time because I wasn't sure I'd enjoy a 2D Zelda-like, but it's so much more. It has Metroidvania progression and maps that open up shortcuts like Souls games, great movement and satisfying puzzles, with a really fun combat system. This is a beautifully designed game and deserves way more attention. The best part for me is that it's short and replayable, so not a huge time commitment and still really satisfying.The pixel art/isometric view can make it hard to see what is happening or where you're positioned sometimes, but it's not a dealbreaker - most of the time, it's fairly legible. I sometimes struggled with the pixel art where I would miss a path or climbable surface and spend ages running around trying to find a way to progress until I looked up a video, which is a problem when the game has a hard time limit - but missing those paths could just be a me problem.As you would've seen from other reviews, there is a time limit on characters' lives, including yours, but it can be extended with some items. This puts a really interesting twist on the genre, and this has tradeoffs in design as the player can't spend a lot of time exploring if they want to keep people alive. The urgency was really fun for me, but may not be for everyone, so you can choose to switch over to the infinite time mode if you really hate it.I would say for experienced gamers, the gameplay isn't extremely hard, but still takes some skill with timing as it has a small delay. For less experienced people, enemies do significant damage and dying can be relatively easy, though deaths don't feel that punishing because you can easily get back to the action and you don't lose any extra time (on normal mode, at least). I noticed from the achievements that only 1/3 of players have really got past the 4th boss and it may be too hard for some, but it's one of those games where you die a couple of times figuring out the pattern and then you're good to go. I will say, the end of the game ramps up in difficulty quite suddenly, and it's where most of my deaths happened, but it just took some patience and learning how to manage it.Please try it and give this developer some love.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is a wild ride in terms of satisfaction.An hour in, I was sure I was gonna be recommending this to everyone. Because it starts out strong, like super strong. Satisfying, smooth combat. Great exploration and movement. Amazing soundtrack. Perfect pixel art(for now...).But then, ever so slowly, the cracks start to show. For instance, the colour scheme. You'd think it'd be hard to mess that up, but especially during the night part of the day/night cycle, the contrast is super bad and in some areas it's literally hard to tell walls from floors. It started bugging me but... eh, it didn't really ruin the experience, since it's mostly bad in the first part of the game. As I started picking up more navigation options, I was having fun ducking back to areas and cracking them open... but the map is kind of bad, and with only one kind of pin, it's hard to leave good notes for yourself about what to return for.If that had been all, though, I would absolutely have loved the game, but near the end of the game, it drops the ball so hard you can see the crater from space. In order...The game smugly informs you that a navigation mechanic that's been available, but never pointed out or elaborated on, since the start of the game exists. Minor, but, you know. Still annoying.To access a certain area, you need to multi-parry an enemy, once again the game's never told you that some enemies need successive parries to stagger. I went through the entire game assuming that ones that didn't stagger after one parry were just unstaggerable.After an entire game of being a metroidvania/zelda-like heavy on navigation, and with puzzle-solving, even to the point of having two major boss battles that were all about using your grappling hook to zoom around the arena to avoid getting hit... the final dungeon is just a flat combat gauntlet. An insane letdown.But the biggest letdown, in fact, what shook me out of enjoying the game most of all, was the terrible story and characterization. It's a combination of multiple factors that make it so bad:- Clearly no dialogue editing by a native English speaker, the near-complete absence of contractions makes almost every sentence sound stilted and artificial.- As great as the overhead pixel art is, every "human-looking" character's up-close portraits and expressions just look ever so subtly off, like it's in some sort of narrow dimension between "incompetent" and "fetish art."- - Adding to the "am I playing someone's fetish game"-feel is the fact that 99 out of 100 characters are either female in appearance or genderless orbs. It gives this feeling like Unsighted was retrofitted from a porn game of some sort.- - For a game that's supposed to be partially about marshalling a limited resource to keep your favourite NPC's alive until the end... I never really found myself caring about any of the NPC's. Most of them have all of five lines of dialogue through the game, never really show up or contribute anything outside of being shopkeepers, or participate in any events, and what limited characterization they had feels extremely shallow and stereotyped for the most part.The tl;dr is:Play it for the combat, skip every single cutscene, hope you're not in some way sight-impaired.

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is really, really good - with a couple caveats.The game is basically a 2D Zelda clone with soulslike elements - you explore an overworld with a couple of villages, and half a dozen dungeons, each one based around a particular theme, where you will need a special item or items to progress.Combat involves stamina management and well-timed parries.  It's not nearly as demanding as Dark Souls - the challenge level is closer to Link to the Past than to Elden Ring.The dungeon design is top notch, the combat feels great, and there are some really fun (and occasionally genuinely challenging) puzzles.Now the bads:  There are a few noticeable rough edges in the map design and overall game feel.  Mostly it's great, but every once in awhile you might think "huh, they probably should have changed that".  More noticeably, the writing is pretty bad - the story is cheesy and cynical, and every character speaks with the exact same voice.  And sometimes it seems like you're taking a peak into someone's fetish sketchbook - every character is a big-breasted, long-haired, beautiful fembot and it feels a little skeevy.  Overall, 8/10.  Could have been  a true 10/10 with some better writing and a few small gameplay tweaks, but if you liked Death's Door or A Link Between Worlds, definitely don't pass this one by.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much a 7/10.  The art direction is great, the story is pretty good, and the characters are fine.  The gameplay is very Zelda-inspired, not very Metroid or Castlevania-inspired, save for the encouragement of sequence breaks.  That was really fun - especially once you stumble upon some creative methods to bypass challenge and save up a couple keys to accelerate through tedious sections of dungeons.Combat is far too trivial for its own good - there's effectively never any challenge at any point in the game.  The enemy variety is very lacking and every single attack possible in the game boils down to "press B when they flash red, press B when the projectile come towards you, don't stand in the hurtzone."  No instances where you'd be required to able to use dungeon items or unlock-able abilities to creatively kill an enemy, ala Zelda.  I'll avoid giving any specific examples that could have been cool and added more variety to the combat in order to avoid spoiling what abilities are in the game.Puzzles are rather boring and mostly involve backtracking linearly as routes become blocked off or unblocked based on rather basic states.  Exploration is legitimately very fun, but there's no real reward for engaging in it.  You do unlock an ability that allows you to move faster, which is an absolute must in any of these -vania games for me.  It even included some risk/reward, so that was nice.  Overall, I'd recommend seeing an LP of the game where you can fast-forward through the boring puzzles to see more of the gorgeous art.  I'm not a fan of the top-down Zelda games, or really Zelda games in particular, so I found this very boring.  I love my Metroid-esque games, like Hollow Knight and even Blasphemous (which suffered similar problems in both exploration and combat ease as this, but had slightly more enemy variety and a more interesting narrative and world), but this really failed to scratch that itch.  If you are a fan of Zelda-style games and have already played every single mainline 2D Zelda, this is an easy recommendation.  Otherwise, it's a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game, just not for me I guess.  I thought the story was cliche and trite, just a mish mash of every video game trope with a splash of robot-lesbian relations to spice it up. The combat is OK with good controls and interesting move set. Exploration and level design are average. Item and customizing/crafting are also all standard RPG fare. The main issue I have with the game is the Timer aspect. After the intro/tutorial, a timer starts counting down to your death and also for the NPCs in the story. A timer in a RPG/exploration game doesn't work for me. I don't want a developer forcing multiple play throughs and artificial replay value.  I only played a bit further and decided to return the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently completed this game. This was a well-made metroidvania pixel art game. I can tell that a lot of care went into character designs. There are a lot of different weapons to collect or craft. Also, certain types of weapons are used to access certain areas that were previously unreachable. Something that felt a little tiring to me personally were the number of locked doors. If you run into a locked door you have to go through an entire maze just to get another dang key and then traverse your way (all the way back) to the locked door you wanted to just go through. The number of times this came up started wearing thin on me. Also, there were many times that it took me a long time trying to figure out where the heck I was supposed to go next just to continue my progress. Sure there is a blinking light on the map showing where you need to end up but since this is a metroidvania you'll run into a lot of dead ends trying to get to that place because you didn't get the new ability or weapon to get past the obstacles on the way to that objective. You have to figure out where to get that new ability or weapon. It got frustrating at times.I'm not sure whether this would matter to you but there is a girl-girl romance element in the main story. I personally don't care. I just wanted a game to enjoy and I enjoyed this one. I don't think it would be fair to call this game "woke" because it's not trying to preach any kind of message to the audience, the characters just happen to be that way. Also the issue didn't even come up that much.Ultimately I give this game a thumbs up because I can tell how much care and creativity went into this game by the developers. The art style and music are really good. The areas you visit look very different from each other. The story isn't particularly profound but it has a good story in my opinion.Anyway, those are my thoughts. I think retro style original games like UNSIGHTED should be supported so that we can get more like this in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost all of the characters in this game are lesbian robots and I'm totally here for it.On a more serious note,  is just a great game overall. The combat and movement are fluid and satisfying, and there's a lot of room for creativity and customization in the loadouts you choose. The artwork is excellent, and the soundtrack is pretty decent too.What really sets the game apart is lifespan mechanic, which forces you to make tough choices about which characters you want to save and how altruistic you can afford to be while still ensuring you have enough time left to complete the game. On the normal difficulty, I didn't find it to be overly burdensome; if anything it could have been a little bit less forgiving. But I can't recall another game that does this, and it really makes your decisions feel more important and impactful, so I'd love to see other games take this and run with it.Looking forward to Studio Pixel Punk's next game, . It looks to be very similar to  (I suspect it probably takes place in the same universe), and if it can maintain the same level creativity and polish then it's sure to be a hit.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings regarding this game. On one hand, I am reasonably pleased with the content/value ratio, the story is ok and there is sufficient variability in regards to enemy and level design. On the other hand, especially the combat left a lot to be desired, at least for me. It is very clear that the game takes a lot of inspiration from the Souls series in terms of combat design and it shows. While there is nothing explicitly wrong about it, I feel like light and fast action would've made the game more fun, instead of the heavy and methodical approach. The visual design could've been more user friendly and easier to navigate, as going the completionist route was kinda tedious and pretty annoying by the end. Alas, enough work has been poured into this and I have encountered zero bugs so I can safely recommend the game. Just dont expect miracles.

_childDocuments_.review: The music is , the characters are flat, the visuals are bland, and this game does not surpass it's inspirations. You'd have better luck playing "Hyper Light Drifter" or "Sundered", in my opinion, and I only feel comfortable recommending this game to people who have already worked their way though several other metroidvanias and are looking for more.Still, the way the open world is layered is truly something to behold. This is the kind of game that inspires someone to become a speedrunner.This game clearly takes heavy inspiration from"Zelda: A Link to the Past" and "Zelda: The Minish Cap." Minish Cap famously had an extremely annoying tutorial character that follows you through the entire game, worse than the reviled "Navi" from "Zelda: Ocarina of Time."Well, Unsighted has it's own annoying fairy that constantly interrupts gameplay to tell you mostly inane or annoying things. It's truly awesome that the game designers let you skip rescuing the fairy in the intro, but I can't help but feel there was a better solution here. Perhaps if the fairy's boring text didn't have to stop your character constantly, but was instead overlaid on the bottom of the screen?Whatever the case, the game is plagued with typical Zelda irritants where it's stopping constantly. Teleporting, opening chests, flicking switches, entering arenas, winning combat challenges... so many things pause you for a couple of seconds and it really breaks the flow. Even mashing the "skip cutscene" button rarely yields instant results, and the screen transitions/opening title screens are inexplicably unskippable. You can only buy stuff at shops one at a time and will have to sit through the same dialogue to open the shop menu again, and the fairy will repeatedly remind you to use these stupid potions I didn't care about. I would have undoubtedly given this game a thumbs up if this was different.The puzzles are also quite boring, and are often the worse versions of stuff I encountered in Zelda games. I'm so tired of slowly pushing blocks on switches with maybe one or two extra layers of complexity at best. I was shocked to see a whole dungeon dedicated to pushing blocks on ice, something I was already tired of in the first room. It makes repeat playthroughs kinda drag, which is a shame. The combat system is serviceable, but the upgrades and weapons are all pretty snappy and cool.It's actually super impressive the way the upgrades and world is structured in an open ended way. I'm talking  work. Even though I didn't enjoy my time with this game,  (with no annoying fairy, of course).If I were an aspiring game designer, I'd probably buy this game just to check that out.I really wish you didn't have to do a normal playthrough to unlock it.It sucks. The sound effects and music are grating and sound lifted from Minish Cap (which was on the Gameboy Advanced). Though Minish Cap had inspired tracks, The aesthetic is also super boring. Water garden, fire factory, ice cave, sewers, mines, ruined citiy, abandoned mansion, it's all so uninspired and it's inviting direct comparison to the thousands of other games that did these basic themes better.The characters are all pretty ugly too,. Vana (blue robot, pink hair, green clothes. Check the 4th trailer at 1:07 to see) really looks like she's 5 and dressing herself for the first time. Maybe people enjoy these character designs, but I feel they're horrendous.It might not be clear to you at first, but Unsighted really is a story game. A huge amount of time will be dedicated to the characters, text logs, cutscenes, and dreadful . The only notable beat is the development of your character's past romantic relationship... which is spoiled in the opening moments of the trailer.Everybody is one dimensional at best, but most characters could have totally swapped dialogues and you wouldn't notice. The artificiality of your interactions is super striking too. Everybody accepts 4 life extenders from you before expressing you're a true friend, and whipping out yet another useless gift.It's not super great when the game's main premise of NPCs succumbing to madness has NO BITE whatsoever.The main story is a deeply cynical one, who's lesson can be summarized like this:  I feel it's a common artistic expression with those frustrated about climate change, so it's not all that interesting.____________All that being said, I'm honestly still pretty impressed this two person team managed to do so much with their first Steam game. I judged it as a $20 product that I was considering recommending, but when judging it for what it is, color me impressed.I'm looking forward to their upcoming game "ABYSS X ZERO" which appears to be inspired by "Megaman Legends" (as long as there is less pausing and blocks to push).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: - Dollar Store Cross-Code.-------This is a game with central gimmick (you and NPC have limited time) which does not really work. It has hillariously bad plot about saving the world with the power of your cyber-lesbian hornyness (is it a word?), clunky combat, soulesque mechanics (one developer did not create a Dark Souls Metroidvania clone and his butt exploded), pets (unused), different weapons (irrelevant), craft (meaningless), and coop around which game was not balanced.In fact, almost all of the game is unnecessary and can be cut off. Why the good review then?Mostly because the core of the game is here and it is very competent and all fluff stuff can be ignored or turned off, which is the game's biggest strength.So if you have better games (*cough* Cross Code *cough*) go play them, and if you don't have much else to do, you can as well give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Robot boobs still jiggle 10/10 Seriously though I bought this immediately after watching a review, but it took me a long time to get around to playing because I thought the Death Clocks would give me too much stress. While you can turn it off/on in game through difficulty settings, it is worth noting that the timer is not THAT bad. I restarted my first run because I felt too many people died, but I think a big point of the game is replaying multiple times to see how the story can turn out and saving whoever you can (potentially everybody). Game's not too hard, but it is challenging, and the sprite work is gorgeous. Story is straightforward but communicated in a way that feels meaningful. You could probably beat your first playthrough in 5-8 hours, and there's an achievement for speedrunning it under an hour. I really like Unsighted, the devs did great work. I would love to see more from them in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool metroidvania, i will definitely recommend playing it, as gameplay is really nice (it has this souls feeling of stamina management and parries).Biomes are different with different types of special mechanic and/or puzzles (like wind that can push you so you need to be careful when jumping, or water you need to traverse by creating ice cubes on it, or darkness that show/hides platforms), enemies are varied, tools and weapons are pretty fun to use. There are not many flaws in this game, but i can see two: garbage story (its very weak with woke flavor on it- bleh) and timer. Seriously, who thought that it would be a good idea to develop game around timer mechanic? Firstly, players usually dont like time limit in their games (just read forums, it induces stress and is annoying, and usually timed sections are rated worse than normal ones). Secondly- if some character dies (timer runs out) it doesnt have that big impact, as weapons/blueprints you can buy/find/craft elsewhere anyway. And because dialogues are bad and characters lame you dont feel any attachment to them. And lastly- this is metroidvania game, game based on exploration, why the hell would you want to limit exploration and encourage speeding and not exploring? I dont think developers made a good choice here, timer mechanic is pointless and irritating, gladly they added option to disable it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a "metroodvania" and I don't know why people are calling it that. Nothing about this game is anything like Metroid or Castlevania. Zelda would be a much better retro game comparison.With that major nitpick out of the way...Pros, nice 2D anesthetic, solid soundtrack and solid controls. The game looks good and controls well. This isn't a "bad" game despite the thumbs down. If the things below don't bother you, you may very well like this one. Cons: NO STEAM CLOUD SAVES. This seriously threw me off and is an impodement to me being able to play the game since I regularly switch between machines. For a while I couldn't figure out why I couldn't use the save from my pc on the steam deck. Well turns out this doesn't support syncing your saves. I don't even know why anyone would release a game on steam that doesn't support this and until now I wasn't aware that there were games on steam that don't.Second, hard pass on the timer mechanic. It is one thing to reward me for speedy play but I just can't enjoy a game that is punishing me for taking my time and exploring off the beaten path. Half the fun of this style game is messing around and exploring and you are heavily disincentivized to do this. Note: you can turn this off via the difficulty setting, however, I just don't like that it is a core component of the game.Finally this game is just a bit much for me difficulty wise. I feel like I am constantly running back to town because some basic enemies just mauled me. I'm sure I need to "git gud" or maybe I could just play something else. I really just wasn't feeling the core game play on this so I'm going to take a pass.Oh I'd also throw in that this game really hides the ball with how you save your game. It isn't hard to save your game. It just never bothers to tell you that you've saved, or how to do it, at least not as far as I can tell.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but there are some huge issues imo. There are so many systems in the game that I find really cool and accessibility options of enabling disabling what you want. At the start you can "soft lock" yourself by going in an area that requires a gun to shoot a trigger but the game recognizes that and puts a tutorial to where it will tell you to throw an object at the trigger instead. This insight is negated immediately by the fact that if you proceed 1 screen further, it'll spoil the story by referencing your name you don't know. And also the path back goes through a forced boss fight which players will most likely not be ready for. If they rested at the "bonfire" next screen further, they are stuck there until they "git gud". - This is just an example of lack of insight I feel this game has. The item you get from the boss fight may potentially be a negative in slowing your movement down. Run jumping everywhere is the fastest way to get around and doing so with the high boots feels slower. - There is also a gears of war style reload where you need to hit it in the center bar for a fast reload. Except they don't realize that there needs to be a punishment for failing. As it in the game, you are rewarded whether you fail or succeed. How it is implemented is the bar to try to hit the sweet reload spot is shown first and if nothing is inputted, a normal reload is then performed at the very end. So you can instead reload and instantly fail it to get the bar off as quick as possible for the same normal reload timing to play. - Holding down the fire button while waiting for the reloading to complete does not automatically start firing your gun.- There's a portion at the start where you interact to view a door where the game tells you a strong blast would open it. It then pans upwards and moves the camera right to have the player infer that this is the method to do the strong blast and/or progress with the main story. Well turns out the door has nothing to do with the main story then and there. Impressive that it doesn't seeing how it is placed right next to the gun pickup you need for that portion of the main story. Going up there did not lead me to find out what the hell I am supposed to do either. It didn't unlock a passage to allow me to backtrack, I just walked back and went an entirely different direction. - The biggest issue I have is the clarity. The environment isn't 100% clear on what it is. It's interesting to have this ticking clock with the day-night cycle but this leads to terrible visibility. It isn't 100% clear what the background us and it isn't 100% clear (it can be clear, but not crystal while fighting) where the enemies are and what they are going to do. On the front of the enemies, the window for how long a "tell" is is way too short for some actions. Feels pretty bad to get hit by those attacks. - A little annoying the gun doesn't auto reload outside of fights.- The UI navigation for controller is horrendous. You can't even mash A to load up the game. For some reason clicking continue will have the controller cursor on "Return" instead of a save file. Examples of this is everywhere in the game of just maddening cursor starting locations and movement. - The story setup is terribly explained. No idea why there was a conflict in which humans weren't allowed Anima. Except the humans that were allowed Anima and made automatons. Which is supposed to be distinctively different than any ol' 'AI' we have now where we assume their life holds the same amount of value or something? Who knows. All in all, great design documentation, poorly implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: People have compared this to HLD and CrossCode... i think this is pretty much on the same quaility as both of those. Blasphemous 2 is a bit better. Everything is better than blasphemous 1.This is a very light no-recommendation. This game really just has a lot of very minor problems that add up. I may be biased as i find myself increasingly dislikeing the 2D zelda genre.In no particular order:PROs:Basically all the bosses are fun to fight and well designed... except crab rematch.Clawshots are great and actually fast and fun unlike in LoZ:TP or OOT.CONS:1. Backtracking, get ready to do it a lot. not only do dungeons regularly have designs where you travel all the way through it and then hit a switch that requries you to backtrack all the way to the beginning (sometimes multiple times) but when you get to the end-game you are semi-required to rexplore the entire map.2. The Time Limit: i actually dont mind this in theory but the problem is there are a few specific characters that are insanely important and you dont actually realize how important they are. Iris is the only way to upgrade your chips, cog crafting mid fight, extra cogs, and perma suringes stand out as being comically important and you can defintely lose access to these things forever. 3. Cog Crafting mid fight is way overpowered but feels practically needed for how powerful some of the late game bosses are4. the meteor blade is oway overpowered but feels required for how insanely powerful some of the late game bosses are, it completely drowns out all other weapons5. Inventory swapping, having to reguarily swap between gun, doublehookshot, frost bomb, and fire shurkien is a bit annoying and those are just the REQUIRED to progress ones, if you want more variety and use the optional ones it becomes rather tedious6. Repeatative design, this is especially a problem in the end game but there are a lot of enemies where the far and away best way to fight them is to parry spam until they become vunerable and then one shot them. it was fun the first few times... the 100th enemy i had to do this too was exhausting. Especially in multi enemy fights like crab rematch.7. Movement: The Spinner blows but is only blows slightly less than running. Word of advice to all future devs: dont have a spirint button. just let the character run at full speed. Especially in 2-d games.8. The highway dungeon sucks. way too much waiting for either the wind, platforms, flipping switches. it's all very tedious.9. the story is so basic i have to wonder why they even spent time making flashbacks.10. ~~Navi~~ Iris is overused and annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, it's another bloody Souls-like. Oh boy, it's another bloody Metroidvania. Oh boy, it's another bloody top-down  "inspired" hack-and-slash. And, oh hoo bloody hey, it's all in pixel art. Games like , , and  all make me think "See, this is what the history of games has lead to. No longer being constrained by obsolete technologies of the past, games can now express themselves with smooth art styles that don't pierce eyeballs everywhere like needles." But no, we keep going back to this nostalgia bait.And, to put the cherry on it, this game has a mechanic where friendly NPCs are on a time limit until they become common enemies and you need to heal them before that happens. You know how Souls-likes are frustrating enough? Well, what if we gave those games ticking clock mechanics so every death you are most certainly going to suffer adds more and more stress as you run out of time? Although I suppose that does depend on you being emotionally invested in the NPCs, and that's most certainly not going to happen here. If the game gave the slightest toss about writing and characterisation, there might actually be a story here but no; the main character speaks so little and your little support friend puts questions in your mouth so often that you might as well be a silent protagonist like Link. The rest of the actual named cast isn't any better.So that's . It plays well, at the very least, but the threadbare context and deriative design and visuals just makes this not worth playing.
