_childDocuments_.review: Very good souls like making high use of parry mechanics, with og Legend of Zelda style puzzles and dungeons. Combat feels smooth and polished, there are enough upgrades and different items/mechanics to keep the game interesting all the way through. Built in speedrunning and challenge modes are a nice addition. Charming characters and a beautiful art style. Characters could have a tiny bit more depth perhaps, and the spinning top using the same button as jump/double jump are my only criticisms. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: There's a type of world design present in many games(like metroid and axiom verge) where you allow the player to explore a large open map, but block off many sections and levels by way of requiring an item or a skill of some kind. I really hate that kind of design because it always ends up being a frustrating time wasting mess full of bad puzzles, and there's always a point where I get stuck because the way to progress is by seeing a small detail on the map like a vine ladder or a platform that looks like it's in the background, and it makes me feel like an idiot because despite being small it's obvious and simple. I don't like wasting my time, and I don't like feeling like an idiot even if I am one.Unsighted is the only game with this type of level design that I don't hate. I can't tell if that's because its combat is engaging to the point that I forgive the level for wasting my time and making me feel like an idiot, if the level design is so good that I enjoy it despite me going back and forth and not knowing what i'm doing until I find that thing that lets me progress, or if the world is designed to be easily navigated so that even a child could do it, but for whatever reason I love this game, a game that by all accounts(except for the combat), I shouldn't like. This is a really good game.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay and characters are all great but what really sells this is that this is maybe the only game to successfully intertwine morality and mechanics, or at least one of the best. There are strong mechanical incentives to make hard choices, and the central dilemma of the game is how much you're willing to sacrifice and how hard you're willing to work for the greater good. This is best experienced blind, as is the entire game. Don't use any guides for routing or puzzles, don't even look up the amount of resources on the map - the uncertainty and the pressure to perform are what make this game such an excellent playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: The time mechanic was very unique and made me rush a lot more than I normally would. I didn’t feel attached enough to all the characters to make sure they’re all saved, but I did the ending sooner just to try and save as many people as I could.The combat is really simple, but I prefer it that way. I died multiple times, but there isn’t a major punishment for dying. The combat will punish you for freaking out and trying to spam any buttons, so you have to be willing to sit right in front of the enemies and time your parries. I didn’t find the bosses too difficult and only died on the second one (I did die more than once to it though).The puzzles were pretty easy, and the game is a bit short. It feels like it ends just a little before I really wanted it to. Overall, definitely worth a shot as long as you play with the time mechanic enabled.

_childDocuments_.review: While a bit rough around the edges, I found Unsighted to be a delightful Metroidvania. Now, it's deceptively linear, and some of the soulslike aspects don't really do it any favors (why does every game have the player lose materials/exp when they die now?) but I was able to overlook the flaws to enjoy the fun combat, great music, and heartwarming story.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun Zelda/Metroidvania game with snappy combat and a fun world to traverse. I didn't get particularly invested in the story or characters, but the moment-to-moment gameplay was great. My one major gripe is the choice of adding a particular Zelda item to the game as a 1:1 implementation, which I thought was really tacky... but overlooking that, rest of the game is solid.Checked it out after playing Crosscode and Hyper Light Drifter. Doesn't really scratch the itch those two do (Crosscode for story/RPG and HLD for extremely tight gameplay), but it's a fair middle ground if you like either of those games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute joy to play. _childDocuments_.review: Review 8/10 | Unsighted is a metroidvania light that feels a bit like the Witcher when it comes to combat mechanics. It's got a novel time system where you and NPCs have countdown timers--once they're at zero, bye bye.  There's a lot to love, but the focus on the parry system for combat drags down the pacing. -The time mechanic. The finite time system is great in that it pushes you to move, and also make decisions on how you want to divvy up limited resources to keep yourself and  NPCs going. After getting stuck in some areas and see the clock count down, I ended up switching to Explorer Mode (removes the time limit). This is great because it let me go at my own pace to discover things, and then let me push myself on a speed run in the future.-The view is a mix for me. The top down view is great for exploration, but the color pallete and maps can be confusing and lead to mistakes. (Especially when jumping, or when you are behind a boss and spawns attack.) Thankfully Unsighted is pretty forgiving on the jumps (you respawn near where you fell). The good thing is that there are so many different weapons available to help you traverse obstacles and puzzles that it makes exploring fun.-The combat system is diverse and lets you build your character the way you see fit. The only thing holding it back is Unsighted heavily relies on parries to damage enemies. This really detracted from combat, because standard attacks are pretty much useless unless you have an upgraded weapon. This really nerfs the enjoyment you get out of customizing your build, because the bulk of the damage you deal will be learning attack patterns, and waiting to parry and counterattack. The parry system also takes time to get used to, and can be a bit frustrating initially if you're used to dodging and hacking in other games.-Kudos to the upgrade, item crafting, and single-use ability enhancements. It makes the game feel like the Witcher in that the consumables will help keep you afloat against mobs and bosses. For perspective, my in-game playthrough was about 16 hours, while my total time was about 34 hours (spent in the menu crafting and so on). -Combat itself isn't too difficult if you're fairly accustomed to the genre. I didn't notice any difficulty spikes, as again, the bread and butter of the game focuses on using the parry system. Basically wait, parry, parry, and parry away until the enemy gets staggered, and then go in for a hit. Boss fights generally work the same way, and if you really want, you can chip away at them if you'd like. Due to the parry system, I found myself kinda annoyed with having to slog through some boss fights. (Once you learn the attack patterns, you just get out of the way until they perform an attack that can be parried, and then lather rinse repeat 100x.) Increasing regular attack damage would be nice, but that would also change the approach this game takes to combat. All in all, once you get use to the parry system, there's a lot going for Unsighted. It's a solid play with interesting puzzles and tons of secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Still a hidden gem, nothing groundbreaking but a nice game with puzzles (zelda like) and dynamic combat that tries to emulate souls games (hit,dodge,parry+counter attack), feels smooth and movement around the world is easy and refreshing.also the time mechanic is well made.the game is completely sequence breakable and therefore a good speedrun game.recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: pretty rad game, story doesn't exactly leave you flabbergasted but gameplay and narrative intertwine well, the core explore-fight-upgrade loop is delightfully smooth. The overall experience, while not incredibly long, is both demanding in execution and leaves the player feeling the world is impacted by their actions in a way that is motivating. Punched well above expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal piece of art. Tight combat system that blends Zelda, Dark Souls, and even some Metal Gear Rising. Dungeon design that too hearkens to early Zelda. Gorgeous pixel art aesthetic. Plus, it's full of robo-lesbians.I will say that I played the game with the major timer off. I was in the mood for a low anxiety experience, and I was worried I would bend myself into knots trying to get the best ending possible with a tight timeframe. The game offers you to turn the timer off soon after it starts, and it doesn't shame you for starting with it on. I actually recommend playing with the timer on: I feel that the bonds you form with the NPCs feel deeper and the events more affecting with the clock constantly ticking. I plan to do a 2nd playthrough with the timer on, but I fear I missed out on something special by keeping the timer off on the first run.Regardless how you play, the game looks, feels, and sounds superb.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Basically every aspect of this game is good. Combat is good, level/dungeon/puzzle design is good, visuals are great, and you get to play with a nice variety of abilities. The omnipresent time limit really helps focus the game and creates a good sense of tension, though it's not really that punishing of mistakes (the one-time buff items are cheap to craft if you waste them, and you don't lose extra time when you die, you just drop your money).
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing and surprisingly little known metroidvania with some very tight parry based combat reminding of Hyper Light Drifter with a touch of Crosscode.The game has a time mechanics that makes NPCs go mad irreversibly if you spend too much time in the game. It's a very interesting idea, though if you don't like playing on a time limit it can luckily be turned off with no consequences.It does get rather tough in the final stretch, but besides that it's a true gem and one of the best games in the genre in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. I am so impressed with this game! It is the perfect blend of hyper light drifter, old-school Zelda, and Dark souls. The combat is great. The build diversity is great. The dungeons and puzzles are great. The NPCs are like-able and interesting. You can have a pet dog and fish? Frick yeah. Even though I'm only 2 dungeons in this is very close to a 10/10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is a great mishmash of different genres with a special twist all of it's own.You play Alma, an amnesiac automaton, waking up in a ruined laboratory.Quickly you learn that a meteor has crashlanded into the planet, with a material known as Anima, which has awakened automatons and given them life.However, as humans wanted to use the anima for their own gains, they encased the metor in a huge towerlike-structure, cutting of all the automatons source of life.And that's where the most interesting of Unsighted's mechanics comes in.Every character you meet will have a small timer, showing you how much time left they have with the anima they have in them.Some may still have hundreds of hours, but some may have as little as a hundred.On your journey you may find meteor dust though, a rare ressource, which allows you to increase the time limit of a single character by another 24 hour. However, you may also use it to upgrade your own chances of survival...This is a fantastic way of giving the player a really impactful choice. What's more important to me, saving all the different automatons i meet or do i upgrade my own arsenal or increase my own lifespan?If this does sound too stressful for you however, worry not, as there is an option to disable these timers, allowing you to just take your time exploring, though i personally do recommend playing it as is for a unique experience.On top of that, Unsighted beautifully combines metroidvania map exploration with the combat flow of something like Dark Souls or Sekiro, allowing you to swiftly dodge out of the way of attacks or parry them.Parrying is especially satisfying, as it opens enemies up for a quick critical hit.However, sometimes you may be surrounded by half a dozen enemies, all attacking quickly after another.If you want to parry them all, you need to really pay attention to each enemies attack indicators.Attacks are always well telegraphed, both visually and audibly, which leads to the parry system being super reliable and satisfying to use.The game can be a bit stressful at times, as you may end up really having to race against time, trying not to get stuck or not knowing where to go next, as all these little timers keep running out, but i managed to finish the game in 9-ish hours with no automatons lost at the end, but i did have to hurry quite a bit toward the end as my supply of dust began to run out.Overall, this was a really unique experience though, so if this combination of genres sounds up your alley, definitely give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fantastic game. Honestly, I think it's almost perfect. The combat is super fluid and fun; there's tons of exploring to do; the music is great; the art is beautiful; the story is memorable; there's tons of secrets/unlockables throughout the game; and the game length I feel is perfect. On top of all that I mentioned, there is also a good bit of replayability due to a certain mechanic you can play with that puts a time crunch on everything. I recommend for your first playthrough you disable said time crunch though because it can be very hard to find things on your first run and you will waste a ton of that precious time if you arent sure where to go. The game feels like a mix of a metroidvania and zelda; I also felt like the game was very similar to the game Crosscode (but, while I loved CC, Unsighted was way more enjoyable). That's the best I can think to describe it right now. I wish more people knew about this game because it is absolutely fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art is grandiose. Movement is smooth and intuitive, you can get to places earlier than expected by finding the right tools or just making them yourself. The pressure of time made me really involved into making sure that everyone would make it through by the end of the game.Combat is simple but oh so efficient. Puzzles are enjoyable, somewhat quick to resolve, but it just blends amazingly well into the environment. Out of all the puzzles, only a couple felt like actual puzzles I had to stop and really think about, all while without being overly complicated.I have had a blast. I absolutely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply amazing. The retro graphics look incredible, and the music/sounds fit it perfectly. The combat feels great and there's a good variety of ways to play the game as well. As far as replayability goes, there's several mods to play, including alternate difficulties to the base game, and aside from the time-based ones, the achievements weren't boring to get at all.Although the timed-aspect of the game can turn a lot of people away, there's nothing wrong with playing the game in explorer mode. It removes the time limit on npcs and the player while also adding some optional settings to make exploring easier.The only thing I really found annoying about the game is that most of the bosses enjoy spawning minions/enemies during their fights. It's usually pretty manageable, as it's timed like a boss' attack, meaning the boss will let you battle them for a bit, but sometimes it can feel a bit unfair having to avoid several sources of damage at once.Overall, great game. There's everything to like about this retro/cyberpunk metroidvania. The time limit changes how the game is played a considerable amount, but not enough to warrant forcing yourself to play with it if you don't want to.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed it a ton. Lots of fun dungeon and world design. Combat can be a little simplistic in that I never felt pushed to experiment much, but there is some decent variation there. I wasn't overly invested in the characters, but it's definitely there for people that care more, and is understandably a big draw for the game. Don't craft a grappling hook unless you want to entirely negate like half the dungeon/navigational content tho, once you have even one, a lot of the design goes out the window.Got it on sale, but wouldn't be upset for full price
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Very good fast paced game with a very fun combat gameplay. The time limit can be a bit tricky, but it forces the player to help some NPC (and you should help some to the max, 4 hearts, it's worth it most of the time). Some skills are pretty broken, like  and the defensive chips. Overall a very fun game, clearly worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I played this, I did not finish the game, because I felt I was playing it wrong by playing with the character timer disabled. I just felt I was running the gameplay experience for myself, that I was playing the game wrong.I came back to finish it, the way I felt it was right, which was WITH the timer on. And if I might be honest, it barely made any change, granny died for me but aside from that I got what is essentially the good variant of this game's ending, and I checked around the internet about alternate endings, all of them are the same but with minor differences depending on what character died or you helped with by giving meteor dust.So, if you are indecisive about the whole timer option, I just recommend to turn them off, because aside from not being to explore as much by your own will (or doing it in exchange of your and everyone else's time), having the timer turned on won't change your experience as much as one would believe.Aside from this gripe, the game itself is really good, I really wish it had a bit more variety on melee weapons, since there' technically only two types: sword (light) and axe (heavy) (There's also a Shuriken but it isn't exactly a melee weapon), with several variants to them with stats and status effects, and when I hear "Souls-like" I do understand it as dodging and though enemies but I also like the Souls games because of it's great variety of melee weapons with different kinds of attacks and special moves. This does NOT ruin my experience with combat however, because although not having that many options for melee armament, everything in here feels REALLY good, the parry, the attacks, the charge attack, the guns... Well all except the reload, I never liked that kind of system, although you can get used to it with some training (with training I mean forcing yourself to get out of your comfort zone and actually using  the gun for combat instead of just using it for utility), and funnily enough, there is a bit more variety when it comes to guns compared to melee weapons, although most of these are not exactly very powerful on their own, so you'll mostly use it as a complement to your melee weaponry, unless you equip two guns at once, which... I have not tried actually, because swords can simply do a lot more damage thanks to the perfect parry system.Anyways, music good, beating bad guys good, story good, and gay robots good, go play the freaking game now.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game! I love the story and the concept of the energy source, Anima, giving sentience to machines and automatons. Combat is challenging but rewarding once you get the parry mechanics down. cool weapons, overworld, and the time mechanic adds a bit of urgency to the adventure. losing characters from running out of time has a very big impact on the atmosphere of the game. For first-time players, I would recommend turning off the timer mechanic, especially if you want to mostly explore. I plan on doing a second playthrough with this turned on, now that  I know which to prioritize.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs middle / buy it on a sale. The pixel art is great, as is the soundtrack, but the gameplay itself is very much so just "ok". It's half-Metroidvania, half-Soulslike, but should have committed to one or the other in my opinion, as it never really finds its identity in either one. Combat boils down to "abuse the -very- generous parry window" and then just run around in circles for a bit until the next chance, meaning everything feels kind of slow and not in a good way. The story was pretty forgettable, but then most Metroidvanias aren't really known for it either. However, with the mechanic of "saving everyone" and the frequent cutscenes, it's a bit harder to ignore "story bad" here as opposed to your typical game in the genre.There's some excellent sequence breaking potential, and the speedrun potential is actually pretty crazy. Even in a blind playthrough, it's not a terribly long game, but there are some extra modes and challenges you can do if you want to extend the replay value. Personally, I finished the game once and have no urge to go back to it, but feel I got my money's worth having bought it on a sale. You could do worse, but when it comes to both genres, you can definitely do better.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: beautiful game! Unsighted is perfectly balanced, its combat flows very well and the game presents some pretty charismatic characters. I'd say the only fault I've seen is the low-engaging story, which made me feel like didn't go deep enough to create an immersive experience. That said, I recommend Unsighted to every Metroidvania fan!
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Crosscode, Hyper Light Drifter, or any similar games, you'll probably like this one. The combat is really satisfying, the game challenges you to explore like a metroidvania, and the RPG elements make for some great customization. Definitely gonna be doing another playthrough once I'm done with my first.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning game all around. The combat is relatively simple and very satisfying. The story is also simple and enjoyable, with a cool, mysterious universe in the background. The exploration is similar to other Metroidvanias, with puzzles that are just hard enough and cool mechanics and abilities to help with traversal, but with the added bonus that it rarely requires too much backtracking.Personally, I'm not a huge fan of time restraints in games, because I tend to be the kind of player that takes their sweet time exploring every nook and cranny, so the Anima scarcity mechanic kinda of put me off at first, but I pushed through it, and it motivated me to get out of my comfort zone and try to finish the game way more quickly than I would have otherwise.Honestly one of the best medium-short games I've played, beautiful art and music, a hard recommend to anyone that enjoys the genres involved.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is good in general, it does suffer pretty heavily from the map design. The scenery and visuals are great, but the maps are quite poorly designed. At the beginning, the game claims you can go anywhere and there isn't a strict path to follow, however time and time again trying to go in the suggested order all the paths are blocked. It is so bad that I had to cheese a side boss to try to get to the area the second boss is, but of course that only opened up my path for a couple minutes before  being completely blocked again by rocks, water, puzzles that require certain abilities I don't have, or require the area to be opened. And the salt in the wound is this game does have a "time" feature, so being stuck wandering around trying to figure out how to get to the boss you are losing valuable time.Despite the overall highly frustrating map design, I would still recommend it because it is fun (when not wandering around). Note to Devs: take notes on good map design by looking at Crosscode's maps, those are actually good maps.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. It plays very much like a top-down Zelda game, even down to many of the equipment types, but it's faster paced and has more game mechanics going on than a typical Zelda game. For example, weapon upgrades, different equippable variations of weapons, and a few other things.The setting of the game is quite cool and unique, and the premise that everyone has a limited amount of time to live (which can be extended with a limited resource) is a really interesting twist. I thought I'd hate it and that it would stress me out (and it did stress me out somewhat), but it was balanced pretty well for me and I managed to finish with only one character dying to my knowledge. Also, there's an option to disable that aspect of the game, which is very welcome. Don't hesitate to use that if the time limit stresses you out.The story itself is, in my opinion, the weak point. The characters and cutscenes feel melodramatic and mostly just there out of necessity.The graphics and soundtrack, however, are excellent.The level design is also excellent, with very clever puzzles, satisfying movement and combat, and intentionally designed sequence breaks and alternate methods of doing things for clever or experienced players.It's got multiple modes, new game +, and co-op. It's got optional late-game content. It's got design that's just made for speedrunning. It's got everything you could want.Really, this isn't just a "pretty cool indie game". This is a legit very good game that is, in many ways, more enjoyable than the actual top-down Zelda games. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the best games I've ever played. It's a story about love and finding hope in the most dire of circumstances. The combat is tough and engaging. The characters are wonderfully designed and absolutely delightful. And the world is a beautiful place worth saving. As soon as I finished the game the first time, I immediately restarted, then I played all the way through it on stream. This is a game that I will keep coming back to over the years.

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY 2021.In May 2022, at the point of writing this review, I can perhaps best summarise Unsighted by saying that it's as brilliant as it is obscure. But I hope that more people hear about it in due time. It seems like utter madness to me that this game has sold so badly considering that it exhibits so many traits of popular genres; soulslike combat, metroidvania-style ability-gated exploration through an interconnected world, zeldalike dungeons and puzzling...this game has it all. What's more, it has a charming cast of characters, a good variety of enemies and environments, and excellent pixel-art and animation. Also, the time-limit mechanic is balanced really well and heightens the tension very effectively. There are various means of extending your time and I believe that you can switch to an 'exploration mode' if you're struggling with it. I played through the game on the default setting ('action girl') with the timer ticking down constantly throughout the game and I really felt like it really enriched my experience overall.Another thing I absolutely love in this game is how good the movement feels. There's an item you end up getting which is just so fun to use. I won't say any more than that.I'd probably say that I like this game almost as much as I like Hollow Knight. It's not the best comparison, as Unsighted is more of a blend between a 'metroidvania' and a 'zeldalike' than it is pure metroidvania. What I mean by this, is that in Unsighted the world map is comprised largely of dungeons with a strong focus on puzzling as well as platforming and combat, whereas Hollow Knight is focused more on platforming and combat and features very little puzzling. In other words, Hollow Knight is more of a traditional metroidvania whereas Unsighted is a hybrid of different genres. I definitely wouldn't describe Unsighted as a 'typical soulslike' but it does implement some similar mechanics, a stamina bar for example, an emphasis on dodging, and enemies that respawn at checkpoints. It'll likely be a while before I discover another hidden gem as brilliant as Unsighted.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: video review:Play as a gay robot on a quest to save your gay robot girlfriendPerfectly blends the best of Metroid's exploration with Zelda puzzles and combat. Dungeons all have multiple entrances and exits, and later ones will require you to find the other entrances in order to progress.Most of the items serve multiple functions, but some of them get outclassed.Took the spinner from Twilight Princess and made it a good and fun game mechanicThe loadout swap function is appreciated but probably could have been improved upon, I frequently had moments were I tried to go straight from puzzle solving to combat and accidentally threw out the wrong attack, and got hit by an enemy for it.Ending is alright but leaves a bit to be desired. Everyone goes back to school and joins the Honor Roll tier. I was hooked on the gameplay more than the story, so it's not much of a detractor from the game.I was really positive on the platforming (specifically ), but I ran into some skips I couldn't perform because of invisible walls. There are probably plenty of other skips if you look for them, especially if you replay in New Game Extra, a mode that lets you craft items you're meant to find in dungeons.has a stamina bar and dodge, and attacks are bound to the shoulder buttons just like your favorite video game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed RPGs back in the SNES days you'll more than likely really enjoy this. Same style, but with modern mechanics. I'm not sure if isometric platformers are a thing, but that is how I'd describe this - An isometric RPG platformer. A few of the puzzles took a second to figure out, but outside of that the direction you should take and the combat are fairly straight forward without totally holding your hand.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Hyperlight Drifter or more recently, Death Trash - then you're going to feel very welcome in Unsighted, an action/adventure isometric RPG dungeon crawler that is saturated in beautiful pixel art. Explore a finely detailed, post-human world taken over by androids and monsters. Slash and blast your way through tons of areas filled with puzzles, secrets, and danger. There is a very unique time feature that, fortunately, the devs allow you to turn off in order to enjoy the game at your own pace, and other items that allow you to tailor your gameplay experience, but some may revel in the challenge of keeping your companions alive and maxing out their bonds. With plenty of weapons, skills, upgrades and craftables to unlock, character relations, and an original, cohesive storyline, Unsighted is one to keep your sights on for any retro/indie fan.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a somewhat similar feel to Tunic (which I played first, but came out after Unsighted): Zelda-like, stamina bar, parry/counter combat, dash, passive benefits you can equip, etc. That said, this game feels more my speed and less harsh than Tunic so far. The dungeons also feel more Zelda-like so far.One of the hooks of this game is that automatons (NPC's that can be vendors/trainers/etc) have sentience, but lose it after a time. This time is kept track of in-game and the NPC's become inaccessible after the individual NPC's clock runs out. You can find items that will buy an NPC time but there are many NPC's. Your main character also has a timer. Not sure if you just lose the game if your timer runs out or if you get a new character and have a worse ending. Other than the in-game timer, certain activities (like dying or letting your dog nap) will take up extra time from all of the automatons. You can play without this pressure but the developers recommend to use it.Overall, I consider this a great game. There is a lot of customization between weapons, fighting styles, and upgrades to tailor the game how you want to play. There are also a lot of extra modes if you want to play time attack, boss rush, etc. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game get's a solid 7.5/10 from meThe gameplay was pretty solid and it was a good ol' metroidvania. You explore a large world which are split between 5 dungeons. Because of the timer, you are more focussed on completing the game rather than trying to find secrets and whatnot. In my opinion a plus, you don't miss much if you rush through the world. The story was decent. It's about humankind vs robots, but from the perspective of the robots. Some moments were very memorable, like discovering Iris' old workshop and the tower. Graphics are awesome. If you love pixelart games, this one is for you. Some scenes were surprisingly smooth for a pixelart game.However, the game becomes a little easy if you're used to harder indie games like Hollow Knight or CrossCode, where they spoil you with difficult and unique bossfights. Some bosses were pretty intimidating, but it does come down to just "Dodge their attacks, perfect guard, punish boss, repeat". That's not to say that this game is easy. Also, if you're a casual gamer and don't like the timer, you can just disable it. This doesn't lock you out from getting the ending you want or make the game a cakewalk.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Love that you can play in explorer mode and not have to worry about the time limit. Love that once you understand the game you can figure out how to skip a bunch of areas to try to finish it faster. Trying to beat the game on New Game+ Mode in an hour felt doable once I understood how to get to all the bosses in the shortest amount of time. Combat is enjoyable and never got boring.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game after I moved it to the "Explorer" difficulty solely to remove the time limit.It's an interesting zelda-like with exceptional combat feel & some pretty good puzzles, but while the idea of "rushing through the world before your robot friends or yourself dies" is a compelling one, it quickly became more frustrating and bothersome while lost on a first playthrough than multiplying the fun that was just playing the game in a standard fashion.Story is ok, world design is ok, but for what this indie game is trying to be it's a lot of fun. I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys zelda-likes and is looking for something that just "feels" good.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Is this the most slept on Metroidvania of 2021? No, because I basically didn't sleep at all on my first playthrough. This game is amazing. The combat is fun, the exploration is satisfy, and there is so much to do. The game's flaws are minor, and its successes are major. In some ways, I like this game more than Elden Ring. Point is, if you're a fan of Hollow Knight, or Dark Souls, or anything like that, this is a game you should play.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really good.I was expecting it to be a bit harder on if you can save everyone, i did it on my first run but I still had to work for it and got the best ending.I really enjoyed my time in this game. If I had any complaint it's the over reliance on the parry mechanic and then swarming you with enemies which all take turns with different timings on when to parry. But with some finesse you can obviously do it, but this game wasn't designed very well above fighting like 3 enemies and sometimes you'll be fighting around 6.Everything else about this game was really enjoyable and I thought exploring it's world on a time limit was executed really well.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted's level design is absolutely amazing. I'm not much of speed runner, but playing through this game, my mind was racing with all the possibilities for sequence breaking the developers accounted for! Not to mention the pressure put on by the real-time clock on every NPC's life, which really helps build an atmosphere unlike any other game out there!
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: A great metroidvania with a cohesive and highly-interconnected world to explore, and lots of replay potential. Combat is very satisfying, albeit with heavy emphasis on parrying (though it isn't necessary to master it on the default difficulty). Certainly one of the better action-adventure games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: This game falls into a category I long for. A love-letter to retro and pixel art while maintaining the depth of a Triple A RPG. I wish this was a thing, because then we could see games with the quality of Unsighted but the depth and story of Skyrim or Dark Souls.That being said, great game, definitely recommend. I qualify this as a nice pixel stylized souls-like with a sci-fi theme. What is not to love?
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game to play. the story is very interesting that would be nice in a second installment of the game, the difficulty wasn't hard to point of making me want to quit. the limited time was a well done mechanic that helped with the storytelling aspect as well as a constant pressure to keep you  moving forward. The characters have their charms to them which is fantastic. the puzzles weren't too difficult to complete which with the time limit mechanic is nice because the time puts stress which make you overthink. and the music and art style wrapped the whole thing together in a nice pretty bow, the soundtrack was amazing to listen to especially gear village. and the pixel art was really well done in my opinion. I would love to see more content from Studio Pixel Punk.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is an interesting game, typically I buy games that I feel look like they vibe with me and will be enjoyable but unsighted became a lot more than that to me, to start the game works on a time system, honestly? I wasn't too into this myself, there's so much exploring to be done, the game can almost seem directionless at times where even going to where you need to, you aren't at the place you need to actually be, they expect you to...well explore, I'm not saying it's impossible but I can see a lot of people being irked by this buuuut this is why I highly appreciate the devs going oh yeah you can turn that off, it made for a much more enjoyable experience at least for me and honestly I suggest at least on the first time around that people play it with the timer off but that's just me, they really did make this game in a way that's accessible for anyone and I do mean anyone dood.Okay onto how it plays, the button layout although changeable is a little awkward, although I'm sure peeps who played Dark souls and the like are used to melee being a trigger button, one trigger a melee weapon the other a gun, you aim the gun with the right stick, if you wanna aim that is, A is jump, X is run if you hold it, recharge stamina if you double press it, Y is to pick up things, use certain stuff or talk to people and B is parry  they take a second to get used to but when you do the game flows nicely, counters are awesome in fact and well worth learning the parry system for dood.The game expands nicely, as you keep going forward a variety of weapons and movement options open up, even going as far as having weapons that allow you to traverse areas you could not before, some easier to use than others, you also have three weapon slots to switch between seamlessly, which is handy because it's better than switching certain weapons out all the time to progress, you even have a chip system that allows for some interesting options, from more health, to more defence or offence, better parry's, faster speeds and more dood.The story is pretty interesting, to the point in fact that it's a shame each character doesn't really get that much history, despite having a history with the protage, I don't want to say too much more but I would like to say with the friendship system it would have been both a fun and clever idea to show us certain events, the bosses and enemies are fun to fight, a lot with a unique fighting styles, timing on attacks and even speed, some real fun visual designs too on top of that dood.The game starts off quite hard but as you get more chip slots and the like the _childDocuments_.review: A little on the short side, but all the same a ridiculously good game. The controls are tight, the artwork is  pretty, there's a multitude of different ways to customize your character and progress through the highly interconnected map, there's a good variety of enemies that never feel repetitive, and it does a fantastic job of weaving story decisions into the gameplay. Not to mention the rare treat of getting to play as a robot lesbian protagonist!I do think the central conceit of "everyone is slowly dying, save the world quickly please" manages to be impossibly ruthless on a first time playthough despite being fairly forgiving on replays, which can lead to a much more negative first impression than the game deserves. The game does at least give you the option of turning that mechanic off entirely, which is less ideal than simply slowing it down, but still preferable over spending eight hours on a game just to get a depressing ending presented as being entirely the player's fault rather than, you know, being an near-unavoidable consequence of playing the game for the first time. Which is a long-winded way of saying "don't let listen to the message box's lies, turn Explorer mode on".

_childDocuments_.review: The normal things this game does: Beautiful world, tons to explore, platforming challenges, combat challenges, hidden powerups, fast paced. Every zone has a strong unique identity, both aesthetically and mechanically. It's all really tight, minus a couple of minor complaints I won't go into. Lots of content included several game modes, online leaderboards for score and speed.Interesting things this game does: it has a very open and flexible world; I 'accidentally' sequence broke multiple times during my casual playthrough, and was always rewarded and even acknowledged. The zones and enemies all respond to abilities you get later on, and many challenges can be completed through a variety of different abilities. Though the game does not have a randomizer yet, it is super ripe for it--this is the perfect game for it. It does have a procedurally generated mode called dungeon raid, which also capitalizes on this, also super cool. It also has split screen co-op in a world where that's become rareI will also discuss the game's most controversial mechanic: lifespans. I call it controversial primarily because the game itself acknowledges it as a point of potential conflict with the player by asking if we would like it disabled. Basically, every character in the game, yourself included has a realtime lifespan, after which time that character dies (in your case game over and deleting your save). You will earn items to add realtime to any character's lifespan but these are very limited in number--you will not save everyone; you will feel continuous pressure to go faster. You yourself will likely have to make some hard decisions just to keep yourself alive. I think this could have been an interesting mechanic, but I think it's underexplored. I first pictured what the devs were doing with this design as making us choose which characters we got to know, due to limited time. That we'd get to know character X as we lived out our final couple hours together. And maybe on another play through, we develop a relationship with another character instead. But alas, characters don't develop over their lifespans as far as I could tell. Same dialogue from hour one to four (your soft lifespan)-during the final twenty minutes of their life or so, they go catatonic and plead with you to save them, but you still never really get to know anyone more than just the superficial details. If you give an npc a bunch of gifts they may chat for a couple lines, but meh. This could have been a great storytelling mechanic, but it really just makes you want to go faster out of guilt as npcs die.Overall, I think this is a amazing title that does every classic right and everything interesting pretty well. Give it a shot.I noticed many times this game draws very strongly from two games in particular: CrossCode and Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess, which is quite the pedigree. If you liked either game, I also recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent game. An 8.5 from me. High points;- Combat plays like a better Hyper Light Drifter. It's fast and can be strategic when you're ill equipped.- Little unexplained, but intuitive movement tricks allow for easy sequence breaking.- Persistent game over countdown, especially towards the end, constantly adds pressure and makes for ad hoc routing through the entire game. - Story is straightforward and both writing and presentation are unpretentious. - Game has no filler, any side quests are done alongside the main story.- Music is good. Pixel art is very good overall.Downsides are very minor because the game is really good. Particularly: - Most of the final boss fights were weak. Especially optional boss fights.- Gameplay becomes broken very early, a bit before half way through the game when you can start cloning equipment. - If you discover hidden movement tech early (likely if you read the game's achievements), you'll waste time on unintentional sequence breaks. - Game gives a lot of hand holding with the time mechanic, but doesn't telegraph whether or not it matters if people die, particularly if it'll impact the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea when starting this that it would be the best game I've played in years. I'm very busy, so I tend to only play games when my daughter wants to watch, but I made extra time for this one, and few other games got a look in until I'd finished it. I even ended up buying a copy for my friend just because I really wanted him to enjoy it as much as I had.I love the looks. It's pixelated but gorgeous at the same time. I say that after recently finishing Beyond: Two Souls. It's a strange contrast.The gameplay is top notch. Easy to learn but harder to master. I've enjoyed the challenge so I've taken the time to unlock all its secrets and obtain as many achievements as I can. The additional game modes are fun too, which is often not the case. I've lost count of the number of times I've beaten the final boss! Speed runners will have a field day here.A special mention has to go to the infamous time limit. It initially made me feel quite uncomfortable, but I stuck with it, and I'm so glad I did. It just wouldn't be the same game without it. That sense of urgency gives the story meaning and majorly influences your decisions. You're literally choosing who will live or die. I implore anyone starting this game to not disable it. There's plenty of meteor dust around, and as long as you keep some for yourself, you should have no difficulty completing the game. It's just a question of how many others you save. Abuse the save slots if you have to. There are also a couple of ways to extend the time, but I'll say no more about that. 😉The story doesn't dominate, but it's still engaging, and I did feel bad for not saving more characters in time. The character diversity is appreciated. Some have commented that all the characters try to hit on you, but I didn't think that at all. They're just happy to see you again, and appreciate all that you're doing for them.The music is good too. It's not Uematsu, but it's memorable and works well. I'd have only asked for a little more variety in the boss fights.I played the game on Linux. While it does run perfectly fine under Proton, I believe a game this good deserves a native Linux port. When you use the Unity engine, there's really no excuse not to do one! Studio Pixel Punk, please make it happen. If you do, I'll see about getting any DRM-free versions packaged in Gentoo Linux.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:Unsighted is a Metroidvania with an odd twist. It’s a top-down action game with the genre’s traditional elements of gear progression, backtracking, and intricate level design. The twist is time. The game is made with time in mind. On the intended difficulty and settings, the game puts the player on a timer that results in a game over when it expires. Including the main character, all NPCs also have timers which the player can change with various systems. Therefore, if the player is not quick enough, they lose. It’s made cleverly with accessibility in mind and a massive fun factor to support what it demands.Audience☐ Beginner☐ Casual Gamer☑ Normal Gamer☑ ExpertGraphics☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☑ Beautiful☐ FantasticMusic☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☑ Beautiful☐ Fantasticdifficulty☐ Easy☐ Average☑ Easy to learn / hard to master☑ Hard☐ UnfairBugs☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speed-run☑ Nothing encounteredstory☐ There is none☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐FantasticGameplay☐ Frustrating☐ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun & ☑ ChallengingGame time / Length☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☑ Short (4 - 8 hours)☑ Few hours (10 - 20 hours) [Completionist]☐ Long (40-60 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)Price / Quality☑ Full price☐ Wait for Sale☐ Don’t buy☐ Refund it if you canAudienceI’d recommend Unsighted to anyone unafraid of its time system. I’d like to reiterate the accessibility, options, and systems that help the player deal or account for the time limit. This game has that fun factor. It has gorgeous pixel art and vibrant soundtrack. Anyone who can handle the stressor of time, even if with difficulty, should play Unsighted. I love to praise games for specific elements, respect what is valuable, and condone what is not. However, Unsighted isn’t a victim of features but of a whole experience that is worth your time. It has several messages that hold value and are told well. Overall the Gameplay justifies what little it demands from the player.GraphicsThe 16-bit art and effects are visually satisfying. I wouldn’t say it is awe-inspiring, but it is impressive for a smaller studio. A modern-day mega-man (a good one) couldn’t look better with the same 16-bit style. It’s of high quality, and there’s plenty of attention to the setting. In many sections of the game, the environments actually feature story-telling. I’m not much of a graphics guy, but it has a unique art style. It is of excellent quality. It is, ultimately, attractive. MusicMelodic science fiction featuring electric guitar as a primary instrument compliments the game wonderfully. The post-apocalyptic and machine-dominated land benefits from electronic melodies that ramp up into combat music with electric guitar riffs. It is beautiful and epic, easily swapping between the two vibes. Personally, I loved it.The piano was another instrument that contributed significantly towards making each somber or emotional moment more impactful.The OST was epic in its BGM, melodic with the various tracks per area, and blue during emotionally packed events.GameplayUnsighted is a Metroidvania action game. Combat consist of dodging, parrying, and various attacks or movement options tied to equipment. Using the grapple hook allows the player to mix up combat by pulling enemies or the player to the enemy. There are chips that are an equipment type that provide passive bonuses. Equipment can also have elemental effects that can alter the environment or uniquely harm enemies. There’s a variety of options and tools to approach encounters. Enemies also have strong tells for parrying or dodging. Thus, encounters are fair. Enemies, especially bosses, can have interesting mix-ups and balance out their tells with speed, quantity, and or various attacks.DifficultyFair and challenging. All of the tells, tools, and information provided makes the game fair if the player is attentive. The few fights that can be difficult can be overcome with practice and pattern recognition. Nothing in the game feels impossible for a basic clear. I cannot speak for any difficulty aside from normal, but during my time with the game, my only frustrations were because of my own mistakes. The map is very forgiving and clever. There’s a marked and intended route of progression during the non-linear parts. It’s all brilliant and considering my biggest turn-off for these games is associated with getting lost in a map, I adore how it’s structured with this in mind.StoryThe story is not next-level or grand in the sense of a massive JRPG. It is functional and valuable and fits comfortably in the time allotted. The themes present are mostly generic but tasteful and well-done. The characters present are well designed in both visuals and their writing. I found them all likable. It goes almost without saying that clearing the game swiftly is encouraged by the mortality of the NPCs. The over-arching themes or the ones I noticed and found important are as follows:Time, the concept of limited time and time spent wisely. The mortality of robots can be conquered; throughout the game. There’s a message here about not denying time from others.Love, there’s a lot of love in this game. Some really gushy stuff. And while romantic love is touched on, it’s very much not the focus. Several characters surround an idea about family and friends. Overall, the game talks about love as a method of motivation. The player is asked to love the characters, who are indeed lovable, to motivate themselves to save them. At least that was my belief.Acceptance. And deeper than love, there’s another theme. Acceptance. Through greed and disregard for the automatons, the humans put the machines on a timer. They refused to coexist. They wanted to further themselves rather than value what they had and what the robots had gained. There’s also a diverse representation in the game among its cast. The leading romance duo is homosexual. I found it incredibly tasteful Typically, games with this message are too heavy-handed or attack their opposition too crudely for me. However, Unsighted was enjoyable and made this diverse cast relatable to me. And I appreciate it immensely because it is rarely done this well. They even acknowledge that not all humans are evil. Still, I appreciate that they don’t alienate or absolutely vilify all humans. My point is they did modern-day social justice Acceptance as a theme and did it extraordinarily well for an indie game.BugsNone, let’s go!Game time / Length & PriceThe game takes around 4-8 hours on its first run. A completionist run shouldn’t take more than 20 hours. And the WR run was around 20mins, and the Purist WR run was around 50min (times recorded online at this time. Source?)20$ USD. So from a completionist run perspective, there’s roughly an hour per dollar of a very high-quality 16-bit indie game. The game has plenty of replayability and room for skill expression via speed-running. Measuring quality with time seems fair for the game. And for a measure of quality on subjective terms:The game itself is without prominent issues. There are no noticeable bugs. Nothing felt severely unfair.Its design was robust. Visually and audibly, it’s beautiful. There are some incredible frames in this game that can easily be used as wallpapers or thumbnail material. There are some tracks I enjoy listening to, even independent of the game. The Gameplay was incredibly engaging. Parrying is satisfying. When engaging multiple enemies or attacks with many projectiles, dodging is satisfying. Traversing the map is by far one of the best elements present. There are several tools for quickly running throughout the map. Overall it is enjoyable to play.I think it was and is well worth its asking price-and. I know several reviewers who had this game contending for their 2021 GOTY spot!

_childDocuments_.review: A very good Zelda-inspired game that adds enough of its own twists on the formula to not feel like a clone. The story and writing are weak but that's not too much of a detriment since this isn't a story-heavy game.The time limits are probably the game's most infamous feature. Every character including you has a set amount of time before they turn Unsighted (basically dying). You can extend a character's time limit by giving them meteor dust, but meteor dust is a limited resource so at some point you're going to have to choose who to save and who to let die, and obviously you need to keep yourself alive to avoid a game over. Most NPCs have some gameplay utility (e.g. as a shop vendor) so it's not purely about which characters you like or don't like. Some characters will also give you useful bonus items if you max out their affinity by giving them enough meteor dust.If all that sounds too stressful, there is an option to completely disable the time limit, although I only recommend doing so if you think the time limit will severely negatively impact your enjoyment. The game is definitely intended to be played with the time limits on, and honestly it ends up being very forgiving when it comes to extending your own time limit to avoid a game over.Combat is pretty simple but fun. It primarily revolves around parrying enemy attacks, punishing them, and then backing off to wait for the next wave of attacks. Pulling off perfect parries and punishing with critical hits is very satisfying even if it's not extremely difficult once you learn how the enemies attack. There are a variety of melee and ranged weapons to choose from, with different weapons being more or less effective in different situations (although the swords are all the same outside of stats and elements, and same for all the axes). A recent patch added support for weapon loadouts so that you can quickly switch between different weapons as needed. There's also a chip system that allows you to customize your character's stats and perks using chips that you find throughout the world.Exploration is also fun. The world is smaller than it initially appears due to most of the space being taken up by the main "dungeon" areas, but it's also heavily interconnected, even between dungeons. There's a clear intended path through the game, but many obstacles have multiple ways to bypass them, so it's possible to do some things out of order - there are even achievements associated with some major sequence breaks so this is very much intended design. The dungeons themselves are pretty well-designed, with puzzles that do a good job of gradually becoming more complex as you progress through a dungeon. Each dungeon gives you a new item or ability midway through, and most items stay useful to some degree for the rest of the game.The writing is definitely the weak link here. All of the characters are completely one-dimensional including the amnesiac protagonist, and most NPCs don't have any dialogue except when you first talk to them and if you max out their affinity. The concept of having to choose who survives is cool storywise, but I found it hard to care about any of the characters beyond their gameplay utility. It's not a big enough issue to really drag the game down though.

_childDocuments_.review: Personal ranking: Slim chance at Game of the Year material!!!Imagine if the gba Zelda games, Bloodborne, and Devil May Cry had a post-apocalyptic, robotic child, that's this game==Combat==Combat in this game is, on the surface, very simple, you have a Melee weapon and a gun, but you can parry, do jump attacks, hit bullets back at enemies, charge attack, and easily switch weapons on the fly, as well as perform a few special commands to do things like restore all of your stamina, at the cost of opening yourself up to attacks==Exploration==I can't stress enough how much freedom this game gives you, there are so many ways you can sequence break, some of which are strangely easy, I currently have 3 hours in this game and I've gotten to at least 6 places I'm not supposed to yet, all with just the first movement upgrade!==Music==The music is great, it really fits the tone of the story and the world you're in, I love almost every track, even my least favorite, the shop and indoor theme, is still really good, even if it does sound like it drags on==Unique Mechanics==By default, there is a system where the npcs all have limited life, they're all on a timer, you can increase the time they have left with special items, but if they run out, they become UNSIGHTED, turning them hostile, and permanently gone (you can turn this setting off in explore mode)Healing is strange, but unique and actually really neat, from the start you have one heal, which refills at save points (kinda like Estus Flasks in Dark Souls) but you can also get them back by fighting and slowly regaining them. You can increase your healing items, but there's a catch, the only way to increase healing is by spending the same special item needed to extend lives of npcs, so you have to choose wiselyleveling doesn't really exist that much in this game, instead, you use different colored chips to increase your health, stamina, defense, attack, money gathering, combo buildup, etc, they're helpful but really not needed except in boss battles, so pretty much anyone could do a chipless run if they wanted the challengeCogs, holy crap the Cogs, you know how a lot of games have consumables that temporarily buff you? Imagine that, but instead of always being on a timer, they have uses (for example, the attack cog increases your attack, duh, but it has 20 uses, hit an enemy once and it goes down to 19 and so on) I really wish more games did this, some even act like automatic revives. The drawback is that you can only have 4 at a time in your inventory, but you can turn them on and off at will==Can you pet the dog?==YOU CAN PET THE DOG!!!==Is this game worth the money?==Absolutely, 100%, Heck yes, this is easily one of the most fun and unique games I've ever played, one of the coolest games on steam by farFinal rating: 9.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is friggin amazing. It's a blend of oldschool 2D Zelda and Hyper Light Drifter, with an open world you explore akin to a metroidvania. Gorgeous pixel art. Snappy and responsive controls. Solid combat mechanics with plenty of melee and ranged options, which so far are quite well balanced.This has got to be the most sequence-breaking friendly game I have ever played, and I'm loving it for that. Each tool/upgrade and even some of the weapons you find have multiple uses both in combat and for world traversal. While there seems to be an intended path through the game, it's almost as if it is openly inviting you to make your own path instead, and see how far you can go. Some of the applications of each tool are only hinted at, with the game very seldom outright telling you everything you can use them for.Up to this point, if some large gap or tricky jump seems remotely feasible with your current toolset, you can probably clear it with some finesse. I've also fished up some blueprints for tools that allowed me to sequence-break the game twice just by fishing in random spots, though this might have to do with having cleared the first boss before getting the dungeon item. I managed to reach the boss just by experimenting with wall-jumps and seeing how far I could go.If you have any interest whatsoever in metroidvanias, 2D zelda games, or you liked Hyper light Drifter, then this game is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: OVERVIEWUnsighted is a Metroidvania, though it borrows heavily from the Legnd of Zelda series as well, with as bit of modern "Soulslike" thrown in for good measure. It has a timer component to it, were everyone's life is counting down until they go "Unsighted" and have to be put down. The player character, Alma, is no exception to this.A lot of the game is build around the speedrunning community, even having different modes and leaderboards within the game. In an interesting twist, you don't need to sequence break to shortcut progression; you can craft all the movement tools as soon as the tutorial is over. A quick hop to a wiki or other website, and you've knocked a large portion of your playtime out.GAMEPLAYThe gameplay of Unsighted can be broken down into two parts, the overworld (exploration, combat, puzzles) and the menus. Let's start with the overworld.The movement and exploration in the game are phenomenal. Plenty of things to experiment with to get around. Of course, a certain piece of equipment completely trivializes the exploration, just like the Space Jump in the Metroid series. And there are several "hidden" movement mechanics that make progression faster, if you are skilled at pulling them off.Combat is largely good for a while, with a couple of complaints. Parrying is great and responsive, the faster movement option gets you out of trouble a lot. And it never felt like I was button mashing to beat the enemies. A complaint that arose in the game is that everything just turns into "parry > crit". The ranged combat was disappointing, considering the extremely low damage of ranged weapons that doesn't get improved.The puzzles are a bit lackluster. It felt like they were put in out of obligation rather than having their own place in the game. They're rather few and far between and all of them are very basic in terms of complexity.And then there are the menus, and if there was any single thing that I loathed about this game it was the menus. So you save up a haul of bits to upgrade your weapons a few times? Well, that's going to be stand at the NPC that upgrades, hit "Y", hit "X", hit "Down", hit "X" again, then hit "X" a third time. That nets you one level on that weapon. So if you've got enough for a couple of levels, which you won't know because the menu presentation is horrible, you have to got through the whole process again. Need to craft something? Same basic process. These aren't the worst things in the world, but it's something that it feels like the developers or quality testers should have noted and corrected before release.NARRATIVEThe game is well written, with nice intrigue sprinkled throughout. That being said, it isn't a good story, in my view. The overall plot is a personal quest, rescue your love, mixed with a save the world trope. There is an unfortunate issue with the storysense, trying, it seems, to replicate Dark Souls. It feels like very pertinent information regarding quite a bit of the world was intentionally binned. This is sad considering that the writing that we got was good writing of a bad story.VISUAL PRESENTATIONFor the most part, Unsighted's visuals are good. Nothing that steals the focus, but nothing that catches the eye, either. Maybe it's how I grew up, but I'm not a super fan of retro pixel graphics for the sake of retro pixel graphics. It's all competently done and it doesn't offend, but quite a bit of it is of far lesser quality than Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past. On the one hand, it seems that the developers were going for a SNES-esque aesthetic, with the color pallet and the transparencies. On the other, it seems that they landed between SNES and NES, in terms of art complexity. Again, none of it looks bad; it just looks as though there was a gap in skill level and goal, or that direction of the art in general was confused.AUDIO PRESENTATIONYour mileage will vary, but all the music was forgettable for me. The sound effects were pleasant, but were just enough to also not stand out and draw attention to themselves. Balancing was well done as well, considering there was no point in the game where things got too loud or too quiet. Best kind of audio in a game is the kind that you don't need to constantly fuss over the settings, and Unsighted certainly delivers there.FINAL THOUGHTSAll told, I recommend this game. That said, I was clearly not a target audience member. Unlike most Metroidvanias that I play again and again over the years, I think I'm going to leave this one at the 14.8 hours I've got in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels amazing in that way that only *souls games usually do.The world is tightly connected by either direct routes or elevators, and has loads of shortcuts to speed you through any replays or backtracks. Almost immediate access to terminal teleports also speed backtracking, and rarely makes area traversal feel like a chore.The battle system has tight, responsive controls and relies on telegraphed parries that will allow you to either heavily damage or completely kill enemies, including bosses. There are multiple weapon types (2 melee, and several ranged) that you can dual wield for a variety of different battle interactions (dual guns is surprisingly fun and makes the game feel very different).The timer mechanic is highly motivating and stems exploration, especially on the first playthrough, to locate meteor dust and max out your NPC relationships (which provides tangible benefits as well). If you are the type that gets anxious with time pressure, you can also turn this mechanic off.There's a lot of hidden techniques in the game that can make previously difficult areas or fights very simple by comparison. Setting up your cog/chip/weapons just right and 2 or 3 hit killing a boss feels fantastic, as does crafting dungeon-reward tools/weapons early on subsequent replays of the game.All of these factors combine to create a solid, fun game with high replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up after hearing some good talk about it, and I adore this game.You spend this whole game fighting against the clock, buying time for yourself and other characters, and it becomes a nail biting race against the clock. If the sound of a death timer on you and all you're friends doesn't sound like your thing, there's a game mode to basically disable that, which just leaves you with an amazing metroidvania. I almost played it without the timer, but  I'm glad I did. It led to me making hard choices, and pressing myself to move faster and fight more aggressively just to get ahead on time.Also, cute robot lesbians is an easy sell for me.I wish I paid full price for this game, I might buy it again for a friend just to support the devs more. World/Dungeons are impeccably designed.  Frustrating bits did pop up but they were few and far between and never lasted long.The devs took a HUGE risk by putting the time limit in the game on the "recommended" difficulty.  This was jarring at first until I realized it wasn't that bad and there were options for extending the time.  I stuck it out until I learned to enjoy what it brought to the experience. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. Gameplay wise, combat is satisfying, with each hit accompanied by just enough effects to have weight and not give players epilepsy. Movement and control is very smooth and tight, which speaks to the quality of games developed with the PC market in mind. In true metroidvania tradition, combat opens up a lot after getting a few movement upgrades. Mob encounters will be mostly dodging and spam attacks until one side die, while bosses require parries and mixing in ranged for additional DPS. Despite having limited healing, you actually gain back a (few) healing charge(s) if you defeat enemies, so it keeps tension high, rewards careful aggression and does not punish exploration in a metroidvania.Two things I would criticize is the lack of melee weapon variety and broken parry. You will spend most fights hacking away at enemies with either a sword or an axe, no exception. In hindsight there is thematic justifications for why our heroine can only use these two, but it feels a bit..lacking? especially compared to the abundance of ranged options we have by the end game.  While one could argue that ranged might be the intended way to play the game, our ranged DPS is pathetic compared to our melee DPS, especially at the end once we craft the Meteor Blade, not to mention how NPC quest rewards are mostly for melee anyway. Parries absolutely trivialize any fight as long as you are decent at it, since a success gives guaranteed crit with enormous damage, while a whif...doesn't actually punish you - it just knocks both parties back and reset combat flow. Given how generous the parry window is, spamming parries is a legitimate tactics. The narrative is nice if you take it at face value. Our MC's arc delivers a poignant take on the power of love prevailing over hatred and war (also corporate greed but eh). However, getting to it requires the true ending, which you definitely won't find on the 1st playthrough without help. That ending also opens up a ton of plot holes given its use of . Another story mechanic is "dust level", which requires players to choose between extending their own lifetime or NPCs. This could be combined with character sidequests to make it even more gut punching, but given that most of the ones we can give dust to are shopkeepers or lore-significant ones, this tends to miss more than hit. Some characters absolutely knock it out of the park though, like the girl who has a crush on us. At the end of the day, representation is always a good thing, I just hope the devs do more with the setting because "humanoid machines suddenly gaining sentience" is such a rich source of conflict and drama.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: More people need to play this game, it's incredible.In short: This is an open world Metroidvania with multiple ways to get into areas early and a combat system that's extremely satisfying.The most unique element of the game is that every character in the game is running out of life force - and have a predetermined number of in-game hours left to live. Every time you talk to someone, their countdown clock is displayed below their name. The protagonist is no exception to this rule, and hard choices must be made using the limited life-force-increasing resources you can find.I can't overstate how good the combat in this game is. It mixes stamina-based melee and reload-based twin-stick shooting. Most enemies are glass cannons that deal a lot of damage but attacks are well telegraphed and you have multiple options to avoid getting hit. Exploration in this game feels really good for two major reasons: The rewards you get for exploring are good, and that players have the ability to get into places early if they experiment with their equipment and find secret ways to use them.The story for the game is simple, but well written. Characters are likable, which is important in a game where the stakes are their lives. The game also has a ton of extra content after finishing the main story.Overall, I give this game a 10/10 and strongly recommend it to Metroidvania fans. It's seriously one of the best games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: UNSIGHTED

_childDocuments_.review: Unsighted is excellent on all fronts. Combat is challenging enough while still being able to choose from a large array of weapons, mixing and matching as you see fit. You can customise your build in simple but really effective ways adding a lot of versatility in gameplay styles. Movement is varied with the tools you gain all adding something new and fun- the spinning top for quick movement or the hookshot for a great way to traverse gaps. It all felt great to use. The great movement goes hand in hand with the metroidvanianess of the game. You want to explore because it feels good, but the addition of the Anima system, that puts you on a timer of sorts makes it so that you don't explore every nook and cranny, overpowering yourself in the mean time. Really well balanced and adds a lot of meaning to your choices with the potential for NPCs to disappear permanently. I played in the recommended order, but it speaks to the quality of the game that before finishing I was already thinking about the next play through and doing it in the not recommended way. Straight into the top 10 of the year
