_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story [[review]]Garden Story is a lightweight, hack 'n' slash adventure that's fun and well paced. While some elements feel unfinished and glommed on (gardening and crafting), they don't impact the core gameplay.The tag of 'cozy' is disputable. Yes, our protagonist is a cute little grape, the pixel art is lovely, most of the townsfolk are friendly, and interpersonal conflicts tend to get resolved in 80's sitcom fashion ('We were both wrong and I'm sorry'), but this is not 'Stardew Valley,' except for perhaps the mines, where the solution to problems is good old fashioned violence. There's no relationship-building (with perhaps one exception there aren't even any families), gardening is optional unless you're short on a particular inventory item, you don't have a home so much as a series of hotel rooms, and crafting is minimal. One curious design decision is the lack of gendered pronouns; Concord the grape is a 'they,' not a 'he'; Mandy the guardian is a 'they', not a 'she,' and so on. On the one hand, this causes some clunky, confusing dialogue and makes it that much harder to 'connect' with characters who are, after all, anthropomorphized fruits and vegetables (and frogs). On the other hand, the game's narrative is clear that we are playing in a broken, decaying world being overrun with 'the rot.' The absence of gender effectively reinforces the world's sterility, drought, and, ironically, literal fruitlessness. 'Fruitlessness', in fact, is the heart of the opening scene.As the game is only saved when you go to bed for the night, dying is a waste of time and re-doing everything is not fun; I don't recommend it. Use the option to set dying to 'off.' As it was, I only died twice. Once in the first boss battle because I was unprepared and woefully unbuffed, and second in the final battle because by this point I was a cocky, overpowered grape half-drunk on leafy dew.Boss battles require lightweight bullet-hell-type tactics: evade enemies and attacks until the boss becomes vulnerable and you can start pounding.The 'hot-bar' design for weapon-switching is fantastic and needs to be more widely adopted by similar games where rapid weapon-switching is important. PSA: If you are currently a game developer and force your players to repeatedly stumble around an inventory screen mid-battle to swap the 'sword' for a 'boomerang' and back again, please adopt the hot-bar or quit your job.As far as disposable amusements go, Garden Story is quite pleasant.

_childDocuments_.review: Two words: Cozy wholesomeness! This is a game I have seen in the periphery of the “Steam Algorithm” many times yet always put on hold due to the evergrowing backlog of unplayed games that haunts my library, so when a friendly neighborhood bear granted me a key I just had to push it to the front. When you first encounter the game it looks like a arguably cuter version of Stardew Valley that draws inspiration from the 16-bit era of whimsical gameplay that have become so popular lately, and you would almost be right.. This main connection between the two titles are the Community and how altruistically helping your neighbors will reap its own rewards.In Garden Story you play as Concorde, a friendly gardener in the Spring Grove that gets chosen to help the local Guardian with the tasks while they go on a search for another lost Guardian. Your task is the help out in the community solving tasks that range from gathering stuff to defeating rot that seeps in from the surrounding. Meanwhile the main storyline unfolds in bits and pieces and takes you on a journey to sandy beaches, dried up inlands and frozen forests all in the name of the greater good. The gameplay is simple enough and can at times be a bit monotonous but in the end it did not bother me too much since the storyline and general wibe of the game was so endearing. You get a bunch of houses and can do some minor refurbishings but in the end the core gameplay is to simply enjoy the story, and if your mindset is somewhat set for cozy wholesome storytelling you won't be disappointed. Another small yet crucial feature (for me at least) is the fact that everyone gets referred to as they, such a small thing that felt so monumental. Finally a game that did not bother to gender anthropomorphic fruit!  Garden Story falls in the same category as Pode or Yoku’s Island Express for me, a relaxing, cozy and well told story with an accompanying chill gameplay and a hidden depth. I do highly recommend it for those chill times when you want to unwind from work/study/life feeling like a superhero, this feeling alone is enough to get me onboard. Come to think of it, none of the games mentioned include humans, so it could just be my blatant misanthropy speaking.. Oh well..

_childDocuments_.review: Because it's based on fruits, I assumed this game was going to have a much stronger farming element similar to Stardew Valley. While I love SV, I was pleasantly surprised to find this wasn't the case. There's a lot of fun little 'fetching' quests, a fair bit of combat and a fairly interesting story. My main complaint is that some aspects, like the daily quests, start to feel really repetitive really quickly. I would recommend this game, but I will say that it's not particularly long (around 15 hours gameplay) for a $30 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game yesterday at the Nintendo's Indie  World Showcase, and just HAD to buy it. Played only for 2 and a half hours, but i'm already obsessed. It kinda feels like playing a mixture of pokemon, legend of zelda and harvest moon, which makes it pretty awesome in my opinion, the tutorial its a bit long, but once it's over and you get a hang of it, things start getting interesting really quick, the art and characters are adorable, and the music makes me feel nostalgic and happy, up until now, I'm really loving this game:)Edit: I saw a review stating the game doesn't tell you what you have to do, and that the first boss is "unbeatable", I don't know if we didn't play the same game or if they've never played an RPG before or maybe they just don't know that an RPG is, but there's nothing confusing about this game, you have your map with the names of every location you've been to, you can upgrade your sword really quick, you can upgrade your skills at home, etc. Dunno if they're a troll or maybe just not too bright, but that whole review was more confusing than the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game with a decent story. I'd give it a neutral review if I could, but I can't give it a recommendation either because of how many downsides it has.- Great pixel art and animations- Fairly decent story - Each area has it's own unique style and feel to it, and it's delightful to explore each one. - The music is nice and pleasant to listen to. I never felt like the music was invading my ears.- It's cute. Concord is a smol lil grape and I love him- The fetch quests to progress in the story are a serious hassle. It pulls you away from progressing until you have ALL the required items, unless you gather absolutely everything and manage it well as you play from the beginning - Characters are forgettable. I don't recall any of them as they never stuck out as memorable- Bosses are just as forgettable. You'll figure the trick to each boss incredibly quickly into the fight. Not that challenging - Too many mechanics and items to juggle. You cannot take a break from this game for too long. You will end up forgetting how to play and need to start a new save just to get a refresher - The game play is repetitive and lacks enjoyment after a few hours. This game is seriously held back by its own attempts to outdo itself. There's too many fetch quests/chores, and it could either do without them or a least make it less of a burden. I wish the characters weren't as hollow as they are. Just a name to a face for the sake of making the world feel full.I've given this game a good go, but it's missed the mark for me. If you're into slower paced games with many mechanics to utilise and seriously enjoy endless errands, you might genuinely enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Such a sweet, calming game. I saw that this game is praised for the visual and music but critiqued for underwhelming gameplay, but while I agree that the gameplay *is* repetitive, I personally think it allows for a relaxed gaming experience - this isn't a game to be finished in one sitting. I also appreciate that the dev gives the option to be invincible, since playing with keyboard is hard and getting too many game over can be frustrating and detract from the experience. The NPCs are adorable, and I enjoy seeing & interacting with them whenever Concord goes around to do errands for the community (Maraschino the cherry is my personal fave :) ). My only 'critique' for the game is probably the ending. It feels anti-climatic after all the build-up.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically Legend of Zelda in Fruit World.So cute it gave me diabeetus.The small slimes are the hardest enemy in the game and every enemy makes them when killed.The hardest boss in the game is only hard because it sprinkles said enemies everywhere like the salt bae guy. Git gud?Upgrading everything is fun.I wish you got something for maxing the towns.The Winking Eye at the end scared me.Solid. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: The artwork is cute, the story is reasonable, the music is great to listen to, the game play activities the usual thing I like to do: farm, fight, collect stuff...So why do I not recommend?I can't deal with the controls, they are giving me major RSI as my hands are lower on my keys, moving my hand uncomfortably from my wrist rest. There's no way to rebind them and they deviate from the usual WASD/E/I.I can play it fine on the switch, I purchased steam to play as my Nintendo Switch is out of space and it was cheaper to buy the game on steam than buy a bigger memory card.Sometimes the movement of the text boxes and fade out animation can cause motion sickness too.I do recommend playing this on the Nintendo Switch instead.

But I spent the time to remap the controls, and discovered a charming game.  There are a few bugs and some irritating quirks (like not being able to do other actions if you are in speaking range of a npc). _childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this at first but once I got to Autumn Town I just lost interest and I haven't played it since.Basically you just wake up and check the notice board then go around town doing jobs for people, following a specific quest or set of objectives to unlock new things/reach the new area.I wouldn't say it's a bad game but there isn't much to it and it couldn't keep me interested enough to keep playing for the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Art was great. Character and map design were both good, like there're many hidden path and shortcuts. (However it's not perfect like the summer village's maple there're many unnecessary obstacles&corners along your way. And there're corners where its seems that you could reach but in fact you can't) 2. Good good amount of cute cosmetics for ppl to collect. 3. The game play was fun but in order to collect some items you need you . The dungeons were very repetitive and there's no shortcuts. 4. _childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fun feel to it, a cute art style, and a novel premise. However, the repetitive mission structure makes a game that's already short feel way too long.The daily missions needed to upgrade each village are the same variations over and over. Some bridge has been mysteriously disabled (again), some enemies need to be vanquished from some area (again), some person needs some number of resources (again). Your backpack is way too small, so you spend a lot of time looking for village storage boxes to dump it out in.The village storage is bigger, but it fills up quickly, so then you go looking for a shop to sell off the stuff that doesn't fit. Then when you want to buy a minuscule upgrade, you head back to the village storage to see if you have enough of the necessary resource stocked up. Often times you're missing a couple, so now you've got to trek over the map to find the handful of spots you can harvest it. Hopefully, there's enough of them, otherwise you'll need to wait for tomorrow and do it again.Some resources are only available in a particular dungeon, so you end up traversing each linear dungeon multiple times for a handful of the resource, and fighting the boss at the end over and over. All of this makes what seems like ought to be a delightful little game into a tedious back and forth process.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant adventure RPG. You get quite a number of weapons and cards to fit different playstyles, some questing, some dungeon-delving (with a couple puzzles here and there), a bunch of hats for your grape, and even a bit of construction. The music is a delight. Pixel art is a wonder, with one amazing character after another.The overall formula is very nice:A day starts.You have your story quest goal(s), and the game hands you 2-3 daily "requests" for the current town that you can do if you'd like to upgrade gear that comes from this town.You also have descriptions for card unlocks (split into sections that you unlock along with story progression). These are mostly "do a thing in a way [X times]". Cards affect character stats in various ways or offer additional effects for tools/weapons.A thing that's quite distinct is that there's no rush - a day doesn't "end" until you're back home and gone to bed. Yes, a bunch more enemies spawn at night, but if you've spent all day doing the story quest and then decided that you'd still like to do the requests, you can.Things to be aware of:All in all I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a mix of time management (day/night cycle), daily tasks, and larger story goals. The different tools and vibes for each zone make the game feel fresh even though there isn't much change. And the dungeons are fair. Not too much of a challenge. However, the combination of different simple mechanics come together to make the game quite enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this is a very good game. It has nice art and a decent story, but a lot of the parts that make up the whole are very weak.TL;DR:- Combat feels slow and unresponsive- Perks are kiss/curse style, meaning few of them feel like actual rewards- Building is an awkward gimmick- Movement feels slippery and slow, even when sprinting- Can't rebind gamepad, can rebind keyboard buttons, but not use the mouse to attack/shield- Dialogue is awkward due to an insistence that not a single character in the game is genderedCombat feels really slow and unresponsive, which sucks, because you do a lot of it.What count as perks in this game almost all use a kiss/curse system, meaning very few of them feel like actual rewards for playing the game, because for almost every beneficial effect, there is a detrimental effect. But at the same time, you naturally get a lot stronger anyway, to the point that the perks don't even matter.There are also stats and stat upgrades, which I think were explained at the start of the game but then didn't seem to matter at all afterwards.At some point you unlock building, but you rarely need to build stuff, and there's almost no place to put down cosmetic stuff. On top of that, the game is kinda short, and by the time you unlock a decent amount of cosmetics, you're halfway through or further, so you won't even get much enjoyment out of customizing the very limited customizable space in the short time it takes to complete the game.Movement is slow. Eventually you will be running constantly as you'll have enough stamina, but even then it feels slow. You can upgrade it with the aforementioned perks, but you'll have to take some detrimental effects. Beyond all that, movement also feels sort of slippery and unresponsive.You can't use your mouse to attack or interact with the interface, even though it looks like an interface that should be able to be used with a mouse. You can rebind keyboard buttons, but you can't rebind gamepad buttons.And for a more subjective thing, every character in the game is referred to as them and they, even when their names (which are based on fruit, marine animals, or amphibians) are very clearly feminine or masculine, or when they visually look feminine or masculine. It makes all the dialogue really awkward, because even though the English language does include the singular them and they, when that's all you have to refer to people other than their names, it quickly becomes unsightly.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so much! I really wish I liked it. I also wish I didn't wait to see if it gets better and returned it. I was disapointed by the fighting mechanics, they are unprecise and frustating to play with. Fighting is suprisingly the most important aspect of the game, and its tideous. Switching weapons through a menu is annoying, and so slow for a fighting game. I mostly felt like I was missing something, rapidly you can't buy the items in the shop and i kept wondering if i missed an important dialogue or a detail, but i didn't. There's very little to no freedom,  the ''tasks'' are super repetitive, and its annoying that you have to wait until night to sleep when sometime there's not much to do. Don't expect to build or create anything, there sadly isn't much place for creativity. Garden story is often compared to Stardew Valley and Zelda, but it really doesn't have much to do with both of these great franchise. On the plus side, the music is good and the characters are cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is cute.  It's just... cute.  Outside that, it's repetitive and dull.  Playing it feels like a boring grind.  The most enjoyable part for me was fighting the first boss before I realized you could increase your health.  Once I added additional health and stamina, my interest waned.  The game play routine is mostly wake up, check the message board, get 2-3 repetitive fetch quests to level up your town.  Put things in places, blah blah, wait until night and start again.  Maybe it's just too cozy for me but I found it boring.  If you're looking for a cute, easy, repetitive game to fill your time, maybe this is for you.  Not for me, unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Well I gotta say this is right on the edge of a thumbs up and down, I will give it a recommend because it’s got a charm to it, if I were to give it a note it would be 6/10.Anyway, a big letdown was progression. It starts off strong, you get into combat, resource collecting and daily tasks to upgrade the town. But the more you progress the more you realize it is the same thing.For the combat, the game just does not have variety. Main enemies will be slimes, you got red slimes, purple slimes, green slimes, slimes with hat on, slimes hidden in a haystack….god lord, talking about recolor enemies, I dunno which is worse in this regard, this game or WoW. Even the bosses, they use about 2-3 abilities, and just rotate between them, AND the more you progress in the story, you will encounter the same bosses with just more HP and nothing else new.As for the combat gameplay, I didn’t like it. It feels stiff, it is one of those games where when you start attacking you cannot perform a dodge or other action until the attack animation finishes, making long winding weapons frustrating to make a use of them.Then there are the daily tasks, and guess what, they are recycle too. How many times it takes for the same chimneys, pipes, bridges to need repair! Eventually completing the same tasks over and over just gets tedious.Another point, the dungeons, they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reset EVERYTHING! Which ofc it means you gotta do all the puzzles every single time you go into one, and one of them stands out, F U Sewer Dungeon@@! Also if you plan on getting updates to weapons/health jars they drop specific items, so you gotta do em a few times.Alright enough for the negatives, what makes it tolerable. First is the style, the pixel graphics look good.The audio is good, and fits the different themes (the game goes for a 4 seasons theme, a season for each biome or town you go to). The story and characters are actually decent and well developed.  Then is difficulty, the game does a good job in taking it easy. Enemies are easy, bosses are easy once you learn their 2-3 abilities since they keep on cycling through them., puzzles are easy, pretty much this is a game which you can still play and win if you are half asleep or drunk.Ohh and you can play dress up with your grape, there are plenty of hats and backpacks you can combo around for your desired looks.So, all and all this is an alright game. It does get boring the more you progress, but if you pass by that point, you can squeeze a few hours out of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable. the art style is so cute and the music really brings you into the story. if i had to say anything is that the missions get really repetitive. weapons and items wont unlock unless you get to a certain level in each village in each category so by the time i got to the last area, i got bored of grinding to collect everything and just skipped to the final fight. The memory/perk mechanics are fun to mix and match. through out my play through, i kept finding mechanics of the game that I didn't know i could do. the first 10 hours i played i didnt even know i could run lol. its a very cozy game and its fairly easy. overally i do recommmend this game to anyone who loves more calming, cute, cozy, story driven, adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Repetitive from very beginning and super shallow in everything. Cute graphics - yep, but really nothing more. Long and boring dialogues, clearly written by a graphomaniac.Simple one-button combat system without any impact. Rare bosses are nice, but all other encounters is basically one encounter repeated infinite times.Grind for resources is boring and necessary. Every resource has its point of respawn and it will respawn there every day no matter what. So just go take it, skip the day, take it again...As usual you are the chosen one and have to safe the world, but actually you're just an errand boy. And you LITERALLY have 1-3 errands every day. And you will have to do all these errands in order to upgrade your gear to do even more errands in future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was revisiting fallout 4 before this for the sake of fairness, but this game is maybe one of the slowest games I've ever played.  So much character dialogue, seemingly little character.  No self exploration to start, you move in one direction doing boring tasks.  When I finally get the sword (pick) you get two swings before you become exhausted.  The tutorial enemies take three hits.  They can't hurt you.  They explode into another smaller version of themselves that take one hit.  I've seen it all before in other games, this one is just... slower... And it holds your hand so tight you have to move at it's pace.  Can't wait for the REMARKABLE SPECIAL ABILITY to swing my sword a third time... Maybe I'll revisit after I've detoxed from Fallout 4 but for now I'm just no longer excited to play this game...
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beat this game in 10 hours, wasn't trying to hurry, wasn't wasting time leveling stuff up, just playing the game. Despite hype saying that this will scratch your "Stardew Itch", this will not scratch your "Stardew Itch."There is farming in this game, but only to get resources to upgrade your tools. And only in very few designated areas.There is building in this game, but only in certain areas, and they're completely cosmetic furniture. Even the "non-cosmetic" furniture is rather useless because it does not add any new functionality to the towns.The 3 town bosses are nice fights, but the final boss I couldn't figure out at all. I had to cheat to figure out how to damage the boss.  It was not intuitive, and there weren't any hints. Nothing you used prior to the final boss suggested that this was the way to beat it.And postgame? Why do I want to level up the towns? It looks like there's more areas you could go to, but the paths are blocked off by rocks that you can't break. Maybe the developers are planning on adding DLC?Sorry, I'd rather have more than 10 hours of game play for $19.99.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After getting further in the game? I've actually decided that, yeah, no. It's just not a good game. The combat's terrible and comes to such a stand still. The way they handle dungeons and boss fights is atrocious. There's no salvaging this game with or without a controller. Reading furhter into this review will be my thoughts BEFORE getting a fix for the controller issue, but let me be clear; I am NO LONGER recommending anyone actually this game regardless of platform or control scheme. The devs clearly hit the mark on vibes and atmosphere, and failed literally everywhere else. So glad I got this game for free, because if I had paid a dime for it I'd be furious. This game is cute and the art style is incredible, and the soundtrack is to die for... but somethines went trerribly wrong in QA when they were deciding the control scheme. First of all, I don't know why they even bothered releasing this on PC when the default keybinds are violently  and horribly placed, and the only controller type that works with this game? Is an XBOX controller. Yeah. I'm not buying one of those just to play this game. My Switch and Sony controllers all work just fine with other games, so the fact they don't work with this one is almost funny.Now, that being said, the game would actually crash if I tried to connect my Switch controller. This didn't happen with my Sony controllers, so I'm super confused but it's worth noting. Upon booting up the game, it is insanely loud. There's only one other Steam game I've ever come across that requires me to keep it at 10 percent upon startup, and uh, yeah, it got a negative review too. I honestly have no idea what these devs were thinking! The combat in this game, along with all the movement and interaction, is so clunky and ugly on keyboard. So much of that would be fixed with literally any type of control scheme that implements a Mouse. I couldn't even bind my extra mouse buttons into the keybinds because the game just doesn't recognize the mouse! This game had my left hand ACHING after a few hours of playtime, just because of how bad the keybinds were. I tried rebinding them to a way that makes sense, but facts are facts: This entire game was built around how it would feel with a controller. Analog sticks, shoulder buttons, etc etc. It was NOT intended to be played with just the keyboard! The default keybinds and the playstyle itself are evidence of that.This game also has absolutely no regard for accessibility. The fonts are all hard to read, and sometimes the text is so small that even in fullscreen mode I struggle reading the weird fonts. There are absolutely no settings to increase the font size, and there's no voice acting to help either. So, that's just another pain in the butt just trying to play the game AT ALL!Needless to say? I wanted to badly to have fun with this game, especially since I got it for free! But unfortunately, the fact that just getting the game to work as intended is a nightmare? I can't in good conscience recommend this game to a single person UNLESS they own a functioning XBOX controller.Now, if you're okay with buying an XBOX controller, or you're getting it on another platform, or you just like broken fingers and sore eyes? Here are the positives in more depth.There's a very satisfying "grind" to unlock new items and equipment, including some fun cosmetics! Combat isn't that complex for as far as I got, and farming enemies is easy if you're short on money for a new item. The day/night cycle appeared to be useless and while untrackable up until completing the right side quest, the way the environments changed with the time of day was really nice to look at and added some variation for what is overall a very small explorable area early game. EDIT: There's also a really frustrating bug, where sometimes the game will ask you to use one key, but you actually have to use another one. This is a pretty glaring issue, as this prompt comes up multiple times in the tutorial, but, for some reason it's in the final version of the game.... Awkward. There's also another really awful bug, where sometimes the game just doesn't register whatever your speakers are and you have to literally close the game and boot it up again until it does register. Yikes!Overall, I'd probably consider picking this game up on a different platform. But if you have a functioning XBOX controller, disregard most of my negatives and live your life. This is cute, but, not rip your hair on their awful keyboard controls cute.

_childDocuments_.review: pros:-cute visuals-ambient music-heavily story-richcons:-simple (I found every aspect of the game to be too simple. i.e. combat, dungeons, quests, fishing, gardening, itemization, etc)-extremely repetitive (combat, quests and resource gathering were pretty much the same)-price (not worth $20 for how simple and short the game was. if you want to play it, get it when it's on sale)overall:would not recommend. the cons outweigh the pros. it's not a bad game, it just didn't really do it for me. _childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a story-heavy top-down relaxing game about gardening, harvesting and fighting.The game is casual and has a few settings to make the game easier. I've completed the game without grinding and without dying a single time, so if you're looking for a challenge this game definitely doesn't deliver in that aspect. If you want a cozy game with a cute story about helping communities rebuilding their villages, now you might have something!The story is good, not excellent, but like pretty good. The game is a solid 10 hours in length for the main story and if you want to complete everything it will be a lot longer than that. The game doesn't have as much gardening as I would've expected for a game with 'Garden' in it's title, I've only needed to grow 2 plants to finish the game; I would say it's 50% harvesting, 45% fighting and 5% gardening.The combat isn't very good, it's very unidirectional and slow-paced. The monster designs are poor and there are a total of maybe 10 unique enemies in the entire game... The tasks are equally repetitive and some of them are tedious due to their nature of having to move around the map. Some slimes even split in a different color than their original color, overall very unpolished in that department.The music is probably the biggest strength of this game, the tracks are really good. The ambience, the sounds, the seasons, the time of the day, the graphics... it's all really cute and nice. I'm not a fan of the fluidity of the game, I think it's running in 30 or 45 FPS? All in all, the world of Garden Story is very pretty to look at.Now for the long list of things that are wrong with this game: low variety of weapons (7 I think?), the puzzles reset when you leave dungeons and they're always the same... There's only 4 dungeons that takes about 10 minutes to complete each. The doors with locks in Autumn Town reappears whenever you restart the game (one attack and they're gone, but still weird). No mouse controls. You can't end the day when you want, you have to be 'tired' and you can only save when you rest in-game, which means sometimes you have to find a bench to wait in order to save, you can't stop this game when you need to.The game artificially locks you out of the previous towns until you're done with literally all the quests in that town. Having to wait 3-4 days in Autumn Town for the plants to grow before you leave the town is a waste of time. There's too much walking in this game and the waypoints are scarce, hard to find and unlocked really late in the game. Everything is slow, ressources are scarce, plant growth is way too slow, even stashing a full inventory with 2 stacks takes a solid 30 seconds... There's also a few oversights like holding the run button during transition screens prevents your stamina from being replenished.Overall, very mixed game. Good story, cute, amazing soundtrack, but too slow-paced and the combat isn't good.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Casual "cozy" game about rebuilding dying communities. Very cutesy 'good vibes only' aesthetic. It's not bad, but there's not any depth to any of the mechanics, and the story & characters are just as shallow. You will be performing the same 3-4 brain-dead tasks over and over in different themed locales to pad out play time. Only worth getting on sale or as part of a games bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to get into this game, from the controls/on-screen info to understanding the point of what I was doing, but I persevered! I found the progression and resource gathering concepts to be enjoyable, and there are plenty of optional extras along the way, however I found many aspects of the gameplay frustrating (stacking/storage limits, rare resources, daily progress limits).  Once I figured out how to increase stats, the combat was straightforward and not too challenging; the bosses were - not easy - but not hard either.  Overall I don't recommend this game; too many small frustrations with the gameplay.  If you love the genre or the look and feel I'd say give it a go, or pick it up on sale and just spend a weekend with it to see how far you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a well made ARPG game.Pros:+Very interesting story. As a grape guardian, your mission is protect the grove and people, repel any attack from rot. But finally you will fight alongside with rot.+Collect natural resources and use them to forge weapons. You can use fishing rod to find items from river and pond. If you have enough seeds, then you can sow them and wait for harvest. However, the number of fields is limited.+Use different weapons to fight against enemies. They include swords, hammer, sickle and more. My favorite level 5 lance is a beach umbrella.+Craft some useful tool boxes and place them on the special location of map.+Complete daily missions can upgrade towns level and buy more items.+Equip different memories can improve your ability or increase the drop rate of rare materials.+All puzzles are very easy.+After you beat the game, you still can play a special story and get some new items. The map also displays a new area, but I can't find the way.Cons:-The number of Steam achievements is not correspond to all actions in the game. I think there should have some achievements about collect all memories, finish library collections and upgrade all towns to level max.-No Steam cloud. Player must back up the save folder manually.

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY like this game so far. This game is just what i need right now after being burned out from Animal Crossing and Stardew with it being cute but full of adventure. While I haven't seen that much of the game so far I will give a list of pros and cons that I have encountered.Pros:1) Super cute - all of the characters and the game itself are wonderful and very nice to look at2) Great tutorial, gives the basics well while also setting up the story3) Controls, while I thought they were weird at first, are actually really nice how they are, and if you don't like them, you can obviously change them - I feel like I was a little against them at first because it has been forever since I have played a game with the arrow keys and not WASD and a mouse4) The villagers in Spring Hamlet have distinct personalities5) Everyone in the game goes by they/them pronouns which I think is really nice attention to detail considering how the characters are "born" (grown)6) The character accessories are really cute. I just got a hat and I am way too excited about it.7) Concord sounds really cute when he walks8) The music is fantasticCons: 1) In the beginning of the game and a separate time after, I encountered some dialog that wasn't grammatically correct with both times having the same mistake. Both sentences forgot the word "to" in the sentence where it was needed. I wish I wrote down the dialog and where it was but I'm sure there might be someone who did actually keep track or maybe someone who's about to start the game and is keeping an eye out for it. - For me, incorrect grammar/spelling does take me out of the story a bit, but this isn't that bad that you shouldn't get the game2) I don't know if this is on purpose, but I wish I could take wood and stone out of the community storage box. I can put it in but can not take any out, and I currently have over 100 wood just sitting in a box and I can't use any of it. 3) I'm definitely not a pro gamer so I am having a lot of trouble beating the first boss (the caterpillar thing) in the library area. I think I need a more upgraded sword and jar for sure, but I can't figure out how to get the materials for them as I have never seen that different kind of stone for the sword and the yellow stuff for the jar. I could also be taking a bad approach to the boss so I'm continuing to harvest materials and try my best.4) I'm past the point where I get the watch from Sili but I still cannot see the time displayed on the screen. I have to sit down on a bench or something to see it. I can't tell if this is intentional or if it should be at the top of the screen at all times after receiving it. Overall, my cons are mostly really trivial things or just questions for the devs and do not matter as the game itself in soooo worth it. Garden Story is something I really needed right now as I'm burned out from games at the moment and this cute little adventure with Concord is making me excited to play games again!!! This game seems super unique and refreshing to me, and I'm super excited to continue playing it!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was all busy work and I can't recommend it. I completed most of the game (and you can see how long it took to collect most of the powerups) but during that time there was too little content or challenge. I can't say I really enjoyed this game as much as shorter games that gave more diverse experiences.By the time I reached the final boss I had leveled up nearly everything, to level 4, but it was pointless! I had 4 bottles and I only drained one of them fighting the last boss (who I easily beat on my first try). I had expected there to be an optional boss later that you could only reasonably beat if you had grinded a lot and practiced dodging, but noooo!There is basically no post-game content, and collecting things doesn't feel very rewarding. There are a lot of half-baked mechanics in the game like the day and night cycle and the weather which do hardly anything. Except for making it so you have to wander around for a few minutes every time you want to sleep and save the game because your player "isn't tired yet."Combat was always clumsy, and even when I got upgrades I hardly used them or needed to learn mechanics to cheese the boss fights. There was seldom a reason to switch between weapons either, so leveling up most of them was pointless. I didn't feel very rewarded for exploring either, and the block moving puzzles were more lazy tedium than fun. Overall, the game needed more content and polish. If you don't want a pixel art game where you collect things that is "missing something," play Crosscode or Stardew Valley instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, sooo... I don't usually buy games at full price, especially on the day/week it was released...But I did that with Garden Story and I haven't had much regret from doing so. Garden Story is an extremely cute adventure game with similar features to the original Legend of Zelda as well as turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion. Compared to those games however, this game is stylistically more mellow and has more resource gathering/quest based  features similar to Stardew Valley (without the life/dating sim of course). Garden Story tells the tale of encroaching danger and the sort of "war hardened" desperation that comes with dealing with hostile beings such as The Rot. And it is all up to the tiniest sprout-Guardian Concord to save this world from total corruption and death. A main features that I love about this game would have to be the lore as well as the soundtrack and overall design. The developer's really delved into this world and created a rather effective story-line that allows the player to understand how strained these communities have become with the evolution of the Rot. It's a sweet game that feels in par with a lot of the Pokemon games in terms of story-telling and world-ending problems. There is some grind to partake in, especially if you want to 100% the achievements-- but I think my main complaint would have to be how easy some of the bosses are. In one instance I was able to complete two areas in a 2.5-3 hr sitting. The puzzles were decent in these areas, but I just found that the pacing teetered on the edge of "too easy" and average game play a bit. Just something to take note in if you don't care all that much about some other features that I liked. Besides that, the storage and fighting game play is pretty decent, if a bit tedious to maneuver at points. However, with that all said, I definitely recommend this game for any casual gamer (young or old), ESPECIALLY if there's a sale if the price is a major hang-up for you. If you're looking for a cute RPG, adventuring game to get into the genre, Garden Story is 100% a notable contestant for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and cute game. There are elements reminding me both of Zelda and Stardew Valley, though I'd say it leans more on the Zelda side, particularly in how you gain various items and weapons to use throughout the game against enemies and when exploring the overworld. The game starts out slow, largely because most of your actions (such as dashing, attacking, and rolling) are tied to a stamina meter. While this did make early game enemies feel like a bit of a hassle, as you gain more and more stamina over the course of the game it becomes less of an issue.Despite all the combat in the game, Garden Story still manages to be a very relaxing experience. Often times you'll be on the hunt for resources, materials, and the like in order to fill out village requests and fulfill favors. To be honest I wish the town customization and farming aspects of the game were a bit more fleshed out, but it still remains an satisfying process nonetheless. The presentation is wonderful, with charming animations and sprite art, colorful locales, and a calming soundtrack. Overall if you want a chill game to invest yourself in, I very much recommend Garden Story.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: ☑️Calm, slow & relaxing.❌Isn't a game for people who want ACTION.A tree of mana presides over the world, but it’s been infected by the slow corruption of the Rot. It’s up to you, a tiny little grape guardian, to save the world. To do that, you must rebuild the community and connect four areas named after the seasons.Garden Story feels like the game you get when you’re aiming for a relaxing action-RPG. People need your help, and they’d like to assist you too if they can. What ensues is a quest that merges elements from The Legend of Zelda and Stardew Valley into a very slow and gentle experience. If you're looking for something exactly like either of these games, this isn't what it tries to be. It has elements of both but in no way is a 1-1 clone or anything of that sort. Anyone looking for a particularly chill experience that isn’t very demanding may derive more pleasure out of Concord’s adventure than most players looking for something more action packed and fast. It’s hard to overlook how so much of your in-game work just feels like it doesn’t really matter. I personally did not enjoy the Daily tasks, and lackluster enemies earlier on in the game, it felt repetitive and boring. But I am the type of player who hates fetch quests. Still, it’s a very cute adventure to embark on. This isn’t a grand quest with almighty heroes, but about quiet, hard working spirit and the importance of learning responsibility as part of a community.If you're looking for a game to simply sit back and relax to, instead of having to think, craft or micro-manage, why not give this cute little game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story features a delightful soundtrack and art style. Too bad, you'll have to let the Rot kill you and lose 15% of your Leaflets just so you can do that, as "Concord isn't tired yet" and can't sleep. Then, let's suppose you don't want to lose your Leaflets - you'll either have to sit down and wait until night arrives or spend your time foraging materials and completing requests, which usually feels more like a chore rather than rewarding activity. Oh, and don't get me started on not automatically getting your Dew flasks replenished after dying.There are some crisp ideas, such as the Memories Journal, and I have no doubts that the devs put a lot of hard work into the game overall. Unfortunately, however, the gameplay loop turns out to be a mix of inconvenient, repetitive, and bland mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a pretty nice game; a relaxing Zelda-like I still enjoyed a fair amount, but it is not worth 20 dollars.I believe that it is "an action adventure game in denial." It sounds like it wants to be something a bit closer to Stardew Valley, but it definitely failed there. The gardening is a very basic and secondary aspect of the game. You prepare the spot, plant the crop, and go do other stuff while they grow over the course of a few in-game days. You don't even need to water them. It is about typical Zelda-y things, adventuring and fighting, but it is trying to specifically not center too much around those aspects, and ends up hindering the only real content it has.I know it wasn't trying to be hard, but it is so unbalanced that I really don't know what to say sometimes.However, I can say two of the most apparent places, two memories (perks), one incredibly overpowered, and another disgustingly underpowered.Amber dew is the equivalent of a fairy in a bottle. You can drink it for the highest healing value in the game, as well as some good buffs, or die while carrying it to resurrect after a short delay, replacing the rest of the dew in the jar with shallow dew, which heals 1 hp when used. Golden Insight is a memory unlocked by reviving with amber dew 5 times, and allows you to revive with  This, combined with tiny morning glory, a one day growth time crop which restores the dew in your currently equipped jar to full when harvested, can make you nearly invincible with little cost. Ultimately, it does something along the lines of multiplying your maximum health by the amount of amber dew you're carrying.The underpowered memory, Mist-Borne Insight, is ironically from the same guardian, and is unlocked alongside the game's final tool. So I don't unintentionally spoil some cool things, the rest will be spoiler tagged.Oh, also, there's the framerate issue. The game feels like it's moving in slow motion if you're not already used to it. That eventually stopped being a problem for me, but it seems like it didn't go away for many other people.I enjoyed Garden Story, but it's overall a somewhat mediocre game, and not worth its price. However, if there's a good sale where it goes for around 5 dollars, then I would suggest trying it.Oh, also, I just remembered,

_childDocuments_.review: Garden story is a cute, fun game, with a focus on the natural world and protecting it. It's framed in a way that I thought was kind of neat, and although when first introduced to certain elements I didn't quite pick up on the environmentalistness of it, I did upon reflection realise the metaphors and symbolism behind concepts. The first hour of playtime can be a little confusing, but it's not too hard to pick up. Before I bought the game I read some of the reviews, and I got the impression that the in-game daily quests were awful. They weren't that bad really. I mean yeah, they can be kind of repetitive, but they're kind of not completely part of the main-story. Yes, you will need to complete at least some of these quests, but you can choose to focus more on the storyline. I found that doing a bit of both each in-game day made them not seem so bad, and by the time I left the first town I had gotten enough familiarity with the game to complete all 3 daily quests, and do a bit of main quest. Another complaint that I saw people have was that your inventory was too small. And like, yes at first you do have to kind of prioritise what you are collecting, you have to use the town storage, but you can upgrade it. By the end of the game you are able to carry along a load of stuff, without running out of space at all, if you manage things - i.e. empty your bag into town storage each day and etc. The only time I did have trouble with storage, especially early on, was with glass shards. You get these by smashing jars that wash up on the beach, but generally, what I was actually trying to get was glass lenses, which are also dropped by smashing jars but are rarer. The drop rate of glass lenses was kind of weird, it felt like maybe there was some kind of daily luck level, that you were unable to tell until you had smashed 15 or so jars and failed to get a single glass lens. That and wax rot seemed to have weird daily cycles, where one day you'd get none, but then another day you'd get like 5 at once. Combat was pretty simple, you're able to pretty quickly figure out how to best deal with various mobs and bosses. The only exception to this would be the final boss fight, which I did have to look up how to do. Your weapons are pretty good, you can upgrade them throughout the game. Your weapons also (mostly) double as tools. While I would generally use the pick as my main weapon for fighting, the other weapons, such as the hammer, scythe and dowsing rod all had additional uses, for example to harvest certain materials or dig holes or were needed in a particular quest. I really like this, it meant I still had an incentive to use all of the weapons, rather than just focus on my trusty pick. The exception to this was the umbrella, which I used like once to unlock a memory. Memories are I guess kind of perks that you can unlock- think of it as you predecessors knowledge that you can tap into. You can change them out and check out what you need to unlock them at your bed. You had to find the guardian statue before you could actually use memories from a particular guardian (you can still unlock them before hand, if you do a certain thing, but you just can't see it or use it yet). They, along with the bubbles that you find scattered among the world which give you stat upgrades, are the primary way of improving your base character, and then you weapon, jar and storage updates make the gameplay easier. One thing I did enjoy was the way in which you upgrade towns- by doing daily tasks, each which will be worth between 1 to 3 stars, these go into 3 different aspects of the town, which would bring you perks, and unlock weapon and bag upgrades. The one gripe I did have is it's not always clear exactly how this impacts the world- for example I think levelling up one of the aspects means that more resources spawn, but I'm not sure. It would have been nice if this was more clearly communicated. I also did enjoy the repairing and editing certain parts of town, for example you could put in more lamps or chairs or harvest boxes in certain areas. I was a little bit disappointed at how limited this ended up being- I could only move a small number of objects in a small space, and certain houses and items, especially in the autumn part of the world were just left ruined. I would have liked to be able to fix these up, but it wasn't an option. I did like fixing bridges and stuff, that felt great and gave me new areas to go to, or easier access. I also enjoyed the side quests that characters would give, which I believe were called favours, that was fun, and I like how that also unlocks certain perks in-world- for example one character will go and guard the area around your home at night, meaning that mobs won't spawn there. I would have liked it if there were more of these. For some people I guess that the fighting aspect of the game might become a bit repetitive - there is essentially one main mob that has different versions that you fight. There is actually a second one, but its not as common and only has one iteration.  It wasn't a problem for me, I'm not that big on combat, but I guess for some people it might be a problem

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself was enjoyable, but the lack of numerous endgame and QOL adjustments made it an extremely frustrating experience. If you are not very particular about 100% completion, this game would be suitable for you. I reached 100% completion after 4 in-game months, but completed the main story line within the 1st in-game month. 1. No Progress Tracker & No Achievement for 100% Completion I couldn't check if I had bought every cosmetic, if I had found every bubble globe, and if I had repaired every structure without referencing a guide. Unlike other games which reward the players for reaching 100% completion like Stardew Valley, there was a lack of motivation for players to completely finish this game.2. Tedious Grind to Level Towns due to Time & Task MechanicsAfter fighting the Grove, I was left mindlessly grinding to level all towns to max level. To make matters worse, even after reaching max level in one particular aspect, I was given tasks for that aspect AND not given tasks for the aspects I wanted to level. This happened multiple times in a row for Winter Glade. Even after reaching endgame, I was given low difficulty tasks so level progression was so slow--it literally took 5 seconds to retrieve a resource and dump it in the collection box, but because the game did not allow me to go to sleep before evening, I had to waste my time away on a bench AND go in and out of the current map to make sure it transitions from morning to afternoon and from afternoon to evening. Most of the time, the benches aren't even located near the exits. I finished the main story-line within the first in-game month but had to spend three extra months in this mindless, boring cycle to reach 100% completion. I wish the developers could have made the experience better for those chasing 100% completion.3. Lack of Functions to Efficiently Handle Resources & Organize Inventory/Storage/CosmeticsThere is no function to mass deposit certain resources into the storage or drop certain resources with a single button press. Instead, I had to hold the Z key to deposit or drop each stack of resource individually. To make matters worse, if a resource is at max capacity in storage (which happens very often at the endgame!), I had to manually select the next resource using the arrow keys. I resorted to running to the general stores to sell undesirable resources due to the hassle of constantly sifting through my inventory, but again, because of the lack of a sorting function AND confirmation function, I almost sold rare items that I spent a lot of time finding (e.g. crimson shells, flow stones...) by mistake. Selecting the outfit that I wanted involved manually going through each and every cosmetic, and I really wished there was a way to view all cosmetics at once.4. Lack of NPC & Store Locations on MapI had to memorize the location of the general store, dew store, weapon store AND repair store in every town, which is a pain for the larger, messier towns like Autumn Town. 5. Lack of Prerequisites for Upgrades6. Lack of Ability to Skip Repetitive Dialogue Sometimes I chatted with an NPC by mistake and I had to manually tap through the entire dialogue. Honestly, towards the end of the game, I couldn't be bothered with the storyline, but I still had to sit through the dialogue and cut-scenes due to the inability to skip.7. Lack of Ability to Choose Between Interaction and AttackI used the Z key for everything and in the middle of a fight, I accidentally stepped on a teleportation tile and I couldn't attack until I moved away, which was mildly infuriating.8. Lack of Ability to Skip Through Dungeons for Resource MiningI had to go through every stage in the dungeon again just to collect certain resources or complete certain tasks. It was so repetitive pushing the same boxes and dowsing the same handles over and over again, .9. Lack of Separation Between Tiers of Resources in Storage & Inability to Withdraw Certain Resources10. Lack of Ability to Choose Items To Pick UpWhen standing over a pile of resources, I had to make micro movements to hopefully pick up the item I wanted in the sea of undesirable resources. There was no way to quickly pick up the resource I wanted.I probably left out some QOL adjustments that could be made but these were the more prominent ones.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 3.5/5Garden Story is a charming, cozy pixel art game where you play as Concord, a little grape tasked with saving a world overtaken by the invasive Rot. As you travel through vibrant, beautifully designed areas like lush gardens, bustling towns, and peaceful beaches, you’ll fight enemies, solve puzzles, gather resources, and help the adorable residents of the Grove rebuild their home.One of the standout features of Garden Story is how undeniably cute it is. The pixel art is vibrant and full of personality, from the tiniest berry creatures to the sweeping landscapes. Each area has its own unique atmosphere, and the NPCs are lovable in their design and dialogue. Whether you're upgrading your tools or completing requests for villagers, everything is wrapped in a wholesome, feel-good package.That said, the beach area was a bit confusing to navigate. The layout felt a little more complicated than the other zones, and it took me a while to figure out where to go and how to complete the tasks. Despite this, it’s still a fun place to explore once you get the hang of it.In terms of achievements, Garden Story offers a nice balance. They’re not too difficult, but you'll need some dedication to collect everything. With tasks like rebuilding the community, defeating enemies, and exploring every nook and cranny of the map, there’s a lot to do. It feels satisfying to chip away at the achievements over time as you become more familiar with the game’s world.Overall, Garden Story is a delightful, cozy game that’s perfect for pixel art lovers and fans of laid-back adventures. While the beach area could have been more intuitive, the overall experience is rewarding, with achievements that will keep completionists busy for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A small cozy game with great design, ideas and ambition, which fell flat on reaching its full potential. Which always makes me utterly sad, knowing the game could have been even greater with a bit more time and care!Positive:- Great Design- Interesting Story- Lovable Characters- Enjoyable EndingNegative:- No Incentive to complete the library & memory lane storywise- Rushed Creation of the "2nd phase" Dungeons and everything from winter town on forward- Introduced Areas stays unused for the story (probably because of cut content)- Music instrument stays basically useless for the story (again cut content?)In Between:- Dungeons(there is a concept behind of them and the summer one has a special speed strat to end him, but that is the only creative boss fight with strats... same dungeon layout again and again, and the "just beat the enemy until its dead" is not pleasant when the daily tasks are making you do the dungeons a bunch of times on repeat!)- Repairing the environment(it was a nice touch of staying equipped on those repair kits, but seeing those areas we couldn't fix up... made it overall being lackluster and felt like a shallow facade!)- Daily Tasks(they have no impact, only use is for enabling weapon updates and at the beginning difficult to complete, when you can't make it, then you'll be shamed for not doing them even though they told you that it's okay if you don't do it... anxiety and stress level to the max!!!)These are just a few things I noticed and comes to my mind immediately.I wonder if the devs keep on working on it or... leave it be... in its unfinished, unpolished state.I nearly lost my interest in playing it, when reaching the Summer area and ironically the Autumn area saved it!Yet the repeating "we don't allow you to leave the new area until will tell you" is a bit far stretched. We get the urgency BUT we also need to get stuff to update our weapons so get off my back!!!Bottom Line: It's an enjoyable game with a nice pacing issue. If you can overlook such details then please go ahead and play this game. A must-play for everyone loving mediocracy.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game. The music and artwork are cute, the concept is cute, and the story remains pretty mysterious until the final part of the narrative, but it's beautiful. Some "battles" and bosses, but very straightforward game play and I would definitely call this a cozy game. Overall gameplay moves along at a great pace and the character's stats are generally where they need to be to make the boss battles reasonable to beat.  Love the little puzzles in each of the dungeons (though I wish you didn't have to redo them so many times to get some resources). Near the end of the narrative, there is a little grinding to complete the levels for each town and to collect items needed to upgrade tools/storage, but it's mostly enjoyable and the mechanism for fast-tracking to the next day is helpful for that part of the game (I've also realized that you could leave this until after the cut scene/credits if you prefer). It's nice that there are different areas with different collectibles to explore and that you can swap between those areas while you grind to max out the levels for each area to keep some variety.

You can probably rush to the end of the game in a single sitting, but it's enjoyable to take things slower, growing the villages and collecting resources to aid in your adventure. The game doesn't innovate on much of what the genre has to offer, but it succeeds in what it strives to be and it's fun, what's more to ask? I could see it as a good entry-point game for newer players to the RPG genre. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a casual, cozy adventure, and despite its flaws other reviewers point out, I've really been enjoying it, even past the second village. This game might interest you, if: You'd enjoy a very simplified stardew valley that "focuses" on combat. You also might like this if you need a relaxing, simple game you can pick up for an hour and put down.Core Gameplay Loop:The other reviews are pretty divided over this topic, and it's definitely the make-or-break point for whether this game will land for you. The game has two objectives: a main quest, which you can always check to the left of your map, and a "requests" system, where the village "decides" chores for you to do that day. Yes, chores! They can be boiled down to three main categories: hunt X enemy type, resource gathering, and repairs. There are others I've found, but this is mostly what you'll being doing in the first two areas. The problem with this system is that there isn't a lot of variety. Each request is predefined in the game, not procedurally generated, so you'll end up doing the same task in the same part of the map multiple times before clearing a village. Requests don't necessary take up the whole day, though, you can complete them by mid-day. it's just about learning the village layout and how to go about each task.I ended up finding this loop to be very cozy. It becomes a sort of "go at your own pace" adventure.You clear the request board for the day, then you have the option of progressing the main quest, doing special repairs (different from requests), or just resource gathering to upgrade your own equipment. I'm playing through this on a Steam Deck, so when I have time to play it, I just play a few in-game days and suspend it after I save. It's actually a great game if you only have an hour to play.Combat:The combat isn't challenging, but it does take getting used to. The game uses a stamina system for your actions, such as running and swinging your sword. If you're a PowerGamer™, you'll need to slow down and be more methodical about how you fight. The starter sword only deals it's full damage after you completely charge it, represented by a bold white outline around your stamina bar. Your stamina is also incredibly low starting out, but you'll start getting a lot more as you progress.Dialogue:The hardest thing to get into in this game was the dialogue, but it grew on me. I can read fairly fast, but this game chooses to have text crawl at a speed slightly slower than I can read. This means I will instinctively press the button to make it all appear, but sometimes the text was almost finished and I end up skipping part of the dialogue. I guess it's an oversight/bug. If text speed could be set to instant, it'd be fine. Also, the dialogue itself isn't always great. The game sometimes has more words to say than it really needs to, I think. I'm used to it now, but it might just get better after the first area.Performance:A weird note, sometimes the game gets kinda laggy on my steam deck. It varies when and at what time it does it, and going through to another part of the map will usually fix it. It's not really a big deal either, since the game is pixel art, it only slightly shows. I guess this is the typically case of Valve only going through a tutorial and hitting Verified.Overall, if you can embrace the requests system, it's a simple, comfy game. If you don't think you can deal with repeated tasks, you should probably skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Garden Story through Humble Choice, and I'm glad I picked it up. If I had just judged it by appearances, I would have assumed it to be a short fluff piece, and I would be wrong.Garden Story combines RPG and farming mechanics, a bit like Stardew Valley or Forager with a little classic Legend of Zelda thrown in. The art is evocative and solid across the board, not just charming but regularly excellent and suited to the tone of the scenes and setting.While Garden Story is a cute game in a cute setting, and overall has a very positive and hopeful tone, the manner in which it delivers this is extremely interesting to me. It doesn't need 10-dollar words and novels of dialogue to convey an intriguing plot. The player learns more about the setting as you go, natch, and what you're introduced to is a world that is dying.You play a fragile young Greenling by the name of Concord - the youngest of all Greenlings, the last fruit of the Kindergarden vine. The game opens with you caring for the vine, and I assumed that would be part of the core content, but the opening scene is in fact a farewell. Not to the Kindergarden forever, but to the sheltered little grape who once had nothing more to do with their days than water a fruitless vine.What I really love about this game is how you can feel your character grow as you go, with enough freedom to make you feel like your decisions matter, though it does lock you into new areas until you complete the core task. When the game finally opens up fully, it feels like a realization of the matured and capable person Concord has become.What I also love is Concord and Plum's relationship, of child and mentor/parent. I love this because we actually see very little of Plum at the start, and as the game progresses, we learn about the state of the Grove and realize that Plum is being run . They're allowed a vulnerability and, for lack of better phrasing, a humanity that a lot of mentor characters don't get. The game is full of small touches that expand on characters, never letting them be completely 1-dimensional. Even side NPCs get their moments.Anyways, Garden Story is a wonderful game, with an excellent story, phenomenal artwork, great characters, and interesting twists and turns. The mechanics try some very interesting things, like letting you handle levelups in a very modular manner. It also lets you do things like turn off some puzzle timers, and death (which is replaced with a debuff) that can make the more difficult moments easier to manage. My only really complaint is for a rare bug or two and some clunky mechanics, but overall, it's a really good game.Would I recommend this game? Well, I got it for essentially a dollar, and knowing what I know now, I would gladly pay full price to pick it up again. If you like anything I've described, you won't regret it.
