The music is beautiful and the story is so enriching and I love the whole thing to bits. If you love pixel adventure games then I highly suggest getting this one into your roster.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: There's something relaxing about a tiny fighting grape in a big world. I gravitated towards this game during its development and stuck for the charming pixel art. The customization is a nice plus, it was fun to unlock the multiple accessories available to Concord. There is quite a lot of repetition when grinding, which people warned about, but I felt satisfied when I completed upgrades and equipment. It's a short and sweet simple game. I hope more adventures can be added for the little grape hero.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a cute game about helping your neighbors by completing different quests. The art style and music are especially cute, and I enjoyed gathering various resources to help the many characters. Quests felt rewarding, and it was fun to unlock the new areas with their own sets of enemies and collectibles. The combat is a little frustrating, more so because there is no way to easily switch weapons without opening menus (and thus leaving yourself open to attacks). I was disappointed that there were no rewards for completing the collectible lists, since as a completionist, my favorite part of a game is always filling out encyclopedias of the things I've found in the game. Despite my gripes with the game, though, I still enjoyed this game a lot, I just wish there was motivation to keep me playing to max out the stats. If you're not a completionist and you enjoy cute RPGs, this is an easy recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cute and has a surprisingly poignant story. I absolutely adore the art style and that each town is based on a different season, giving everything a distinct atmosphere while still feeling like a cohesive world. Lots of fun RPG elements including quests, boss fights, and resource collection. Played this for a while before life happened, but I recently came back to it to finish out the story and 100% the achievements and it was very easy to get back into the swing of things. Also, you're playing as the most adorable little grape named Concord! Would easily recommend this to anyone that likes a more casual and wholesome RPG style game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I've been obsessed with being a lil Concord grape going around and helping his lil friends around the glade! The tasks to complete in each town can get a little repetitive, but that doesn't bother me because it makes sense in the context of the story. I love helping everyone out too!!!! 10/10 nice lil cozy rpg to vibe with.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought the small stamina bar was too limiting of a factor. Once I did the main quests and beat the first boss, I started getting stats that let me break orbs to get more stats. Once that boost unlocked, it was a lot more freeing to play and it's a really enjoyable rpg. I haven't finished it yet, but it's good enough that I'm hooked and I want to play through the rest.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Totally loved this! Garden Story has the perfect mix of an engaging story, straightforward action-RPG combat, and puzzle solving. Navigating menus was difficult for me; I kept pressing the wrong buttons to move from sub-menu to sub-menu, which annoyed me. But the rest of the game was so much fun, those little frustrations did not impact the rest of the playing experience. Honestly, this took just the right length of time to complete, and it was rewarding to 100% this game. I don't really have much drive to play it through a second time, but Garden Story was more than worth the price, scaled its difficulty well throughout the game, and respected my time. Two thumbs up, absolutely recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a cute little hybrid that blends parts of Animal Crossing, Legend of Zelda, and Portia into a really interesting package. The game starts off super simple and it does not appear to be anything but a kids game on the face of it. Once you get an hour into the game the mask sort of comes off and it opens up being a much more compelling experience. It is kind of short and unless you achievement hunt, expect less than 20 hours out of it. I don't find it a negative however, the condensed and carefully curated experience is EXTREMELY WELCOME. Garden Story is not a game that demands 50 hours of your time and you get a fulfilling experience by the end of it all. Garden Story is a hidden gem, worthy of your time and I hope you will check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be fun and relaxing. As far as play time it is a short game with me clocking in at 38 hours, but some of that time may be when I had to put the game on pause to finish cook or something of the like. I like the fact you can change game play settings to make it even more casual with no death and slower day progression. These settings make for a nice relaxing games where you can go through and enjoy all the different areas of the games.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy-playing fetchquest indie. The characters are adorable (frogs!! veggies!!), the art style is great, and the music fits well. My favorite thing about this game is the pacing! There are a lot of different mechanics, but the game spoon feeds them to you so you dont get overwhelmed. I was also a big fan of the fact that the game lets you continue to enjoy the towns after the ending! so you dont need to jam every little thing in before the end. ((if i had one gripe, it would be the fact that driftwood only spawns in one place, in annoyingly low quantities, yet is required for more than one of the weapon trees.))the sprinkling of feels throughout this game was the cherry on top. thanks for taking me on your journey, Concord <3
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really lovely game that deserves to be spoken about in the same conversations as Spiritfarer and Stardew Valley.  It has those same cozy vibes with heavier meaningful themes sprinkled in.  The combat feels good, the NPCs are cute, and you can wear a bunch of silly hats!  What more do you want?
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a part of the Humble Cozy Games Bundle, and it alone more than made up for the price tag. I went into this expecting an experience similar to Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion- a fun, light-hearted but short romp in a pixelated world of fruits and veggies. Instead, I found myself in a 10 hr well-written story with game-play not too dissimilar to Stardew Valley, rather than an adventure Zelda game like Turnip Boy. This game has its own unique identity, a story and characters you come to care deeply about, and a sense of exploration in a small world I was not expecting. I only have a few minor issues with the game, most notably with two mechanics - gardening, and the quick travel system. Gardening I felt was underutilized and introduced too late in the story. If it was introduced in Spring Hamlet and used for a handful of progression quests, it would have been better utilized and feel more important to the overall gameplay. Same with the quick travel system, if this was introduced when the first new area was unlocked, Summer Bar, it would have helped with some of the monotony and back and forth you have to do with requests. And one last very very minor thing, when doing the Smog request in Winter Glade, all the villagers have the same dialogue after you give them dew. It is a little jarring hearing it repeated 3 or 4 times back-to-back.This game was delightfully charming and I love the art direction you took for the characters and environments. Everything feels soft without getting too lost or not having enough emphasis on things such as enemies or Concord. And seeing that this was mainly made by a single person, it makes it even more impressive! And props to the person who made the music as well, very catchy. I've already recommended this game to several friends and loved to see that you were supported by several organizations in the process!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Cute fetch-questy type game, with minimal fighting (you can just run around most fights), with pretty and cozy locations, and an interesting selection of tools and weapons that are their own mini-mini games. 🫐 First boss is the hardest, don't be put off by it, there's provisions made in the settings if you really can't get past them.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this little gem after going into it totally blind, and I can honestly say it's one of my favorite Steam games of all time. Is it some kind of giant, immersive masterpiece? No. But I've loved the sweet story, the graphics, the gameplay, and the obvious thought that was put into each tiny NPC.If you're looking for something relatively short and super casual to enjoy, pick it up. SUPER casual? You can even turn off dying in the settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: If I had a nickel for every time I played a food protagonist tasked with things big and small in this decade, I'd have 2 nickels. Which isn't a lot, but... Also there is a turnip in this game that looks a little like Turnip Boy (the one who evades taxes). So far I enjoy it, but think they could have done a better job implementing saves and travel. Perhaps we could have had a grapevine as fast travel since we're playing a grape. Only being able to save when its night and we're tired is annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this on Xbox Game Pass.The game is very simplistic in its feel, and there are time when it feels (*very*) indie-like. However this also gives it a bit of charm, and I enjoyed the overall chill nature of the game, and exploring and seeing the different cities. At 8€, I do recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, I've 100% it and let me say, it's probably my favourite game. The characters are lovable, the pixel graphics are just soooo cute, the music is amazing and it's a really relaxing experience. I had so much fun finding secrets and brand new parts of the map by fixing things! i think everyone should give this game a shot, plus your main character has quite a bit of cosmetic options so you can make him as drippy as your heart yearns. Also if the devs see this... the Concord plush is the best. Big love to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely tentative thumbs down?  If I could give a sideways "Meh" thumb, I could.The upside?  Gorgeous game.  Delightful music.  Cute aesthetics.  I honestly enjoy the feel of helping the community grow and thrive by doing small jobs for them.  The story seems interesting so far as well.Downside?  The controls.  Dear ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ god the controls.  Combat feels like piloting a drunken man with concrete shoes.  The controls are awkward, sluggish, and unresponsive.  Enemies have paper thin hitboxes and your attacks have wafer thin hurtboxes and all your attacks have *really bad* animation lock.  Expect to waste your very limited in-game stamina on missed attacks.  Don't expect to every get good use out of the dodge roll with how bad your animation lock is.On top of this is just general pain like the attack button and the interact button being the same thing, so expect to get slapped by enemies standing next to signs or npcs because you try to hit them and pause to read a sign instead.It's a sheer testament to how good the rest of the game is that I stuck with it for this long.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun little adventure game. Cute graphics, cute music, simple- yet fun gameplay.It is a repetitive game, but in my opinion it has just enough variation to keep me engaged, but if you aren't a fan of grinding, this probably isn't the game for you. If you ARE a fan, however, you'll love it. Cute charming characters, fun things to do, secrets to find. And the story is top notch, it's just complex enough to be interesting, without getting anywhere near a confusing degree.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming game. I was loving it until about 3 hours in when it became evident the remainder of the game would focus more on crafting/building than adventuring. I stopped playing then, which is a real shame. Still, if you enjoy crafting then this will go down a treat - if you don't though, be warned!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: My overall feelings on this game is it's just so Nice. This is such a nice game. A lovely, cozy, task-doing monster-slaying, world-saving experience with such a satisfying soundtrack to go with it. Due to the nature of the gameplay it was very easy to play this game for just a little bit at a time and return to it later (though I eventually found I didn't want to put it down). I couldn't recommend it more, I loved playing this game
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first things first: I loved the absolute heck out of this game! The characters are fun and the world is adorable, complete with an interactive quest that feet simply enough to understand while it left some things to be considered by others. The need to grind certain items defintely gets annoying in the late game portion, but I believe how simply enjoyable the game is makes up for at least part of it. It's a game you can play so much of without truly noticing simply because why wouldn't you play just one day more? There's so much to do after all, surely you have time! The ending did sort of take me by surprise, but it was open-ended enough that the player could see things contiuning on or simply ending with what we're given. I truly loved my playthrough of Garden Story, and I absolutely loved collecting all the hats! (What can I say? Cosmetics are my mortal weakness in any game...)
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely zeldalike/life sim hybrid, with many characters I got at least a little attached to, and the pacing meant i didn't get bogged down in side-stuff more than I let myself do. Nothing too challenging in this game, (I only died once and that was due to not paying attention in a minor fight) but the story and the flavour of the various areas was definitely the main interest for me If you want a fairly chill game, but also want to fight things occasionally, this one is definitely for you! ^w^
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: its very cute pixel art, i loved being able to buy cosmetics for my grape. for me, only the first boss fight was hard because you have so little health and stamina points, but the rest of the bosses are fine. i liked the gameplay and the story was interesting, sometimes a little dull, but i liked the end of the story the most. the only thing that i didnt like was you cant see your daily requests on the map and the maintenance requests in autumn town can be very annoying, like i had to fight the boss just to get my 5th screw, and always doing the same puzzles over and over again for screws or pipes... and if i forget to pick up a screw in the sewer its over i cant complete the request because they disappear.overall i loved the game a lot, i recommended it and i will probably play more to try and 100% everything for fun
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! Similar to Stardew Valley and TOEM. The characters are fun to talk to, and the story is interesting, it is so cute! The combat is also done well, and I enjoy having many choices and upgrades for weapons. I also like the power-up/memory slots you can choose at the beginning of each day depending on what you're planning on focusing on. I also enjoyed the boss fights, they were a bit tricky at first, but once I got the pattern down, they became pretty easy. I am a very achievement-driven person, and I am happy to say that there are so many things to do with the game, I love it. My only complaint is that I wish there was perhaps a fast travel option, because certain things are limited to only one specific place, and it takes a long time to go from one area to the next. (note: I have not finished the game yet, so maybe there will be one to unlock). Very satisfied with the game, am enjoying it immensely. Get this game if you like cute, whimsical graphics/music, and like storyline + combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is very cute, the controls are hard to learn and there is a lot of dialog that is redundant. I'm all for dialog that moves the game play along and fleshes out the story of the game, but there is so much meaningless back and forth between characters that you can't interact with as a character at all. Highly recommend if you have patience, but if not the game is tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game so much <3 !!!!!! i've just had so much fun playing it, it never fails to make me really entertained, and there's always so much to do !! (though i wish the steam save cloud was a thing in the game)overall: the art style is super cute, lots of little quests, lots of improvements you can do to your character, your weapons, to the towns, museums; lots of cosmetics for your character; the dungeons and boss fights were cool and not very difficult, the story and the characters are heartwarming... definitely worth its price !!!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Well,it is relaxing adventure action open world (with tile maps)  RPG;It is not stardew valley even close - it has farming, but you unlock it closer to the game's end and you don't really need itOne person stated that "you only have 2 stamina points and thats not enough" - that is true only for tutorial part, after which you start to upgrade your character (more HP/stamina)in general its slowly paced game, where you can take your time to advance, pretty relaxingbattle system is a bit straightforward, but it fits perfectly in the game
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: it has its flaws but it's so absurdly charming i have a hard time caringstrongly recommend noting the minor flaws so you can brace for them, then buy it anywayOnly issues to me were:Character feels like they move very slowly--this is mostly an issue early on because you eventually A: get used to it and B: get to sprintThe visual design of the game is extremely charming but it's sometimes hard to tell where the walkable areas are. For example, you can walk across lily pads, but only when they're big enough, and nothing else changes in their design except being big and filling up the space better. Some rocks/stumps aren't breakable and the only difference is a sparkling animation on the breakable ones. That sort of thing. The result is a world that's slightly harder to move through at a glance, but one that's an absolute joy to look at, so imo it was worth it.It might take a bit of mental adjustment if you're used to games that prioritize easy reads, but here the gameplay loop is well paced enough that you can definitely spare the time to look around properly instead of hurtling through days as fast as possible.Next--some materials you need to upgrade certain items are things you can only get in specific dungeons, you're only guaranteed to get them at the end of said dungeon, and you have to do the entire dungeon multiple times to get enough. This would be fine if you could eventually get strong enough to just brainlessly hack and slash your way through it, but that's not like this game at all, so you have to do little puzzles on your way through it that are cute and interesting the first time around and then eventually just get kind of irritating.Lastly, there's a building system that allows you to place useful objects in building plots scattered around the map. There are many areas that feel like you should be able to build in them, areas that would be much more convenient if you could build in them, and areas that are both... and you can't build in them. The building system is cute, there's just not a huge point to half of it. I wish aesthetic items gave you minors buffs in that area, and that all areas had at least one place to build.But none of these stopped me from having a great timeSo, yeah, if playing a cute and chill RPG about a grape doing their best to help their friends a-peels(heh) to you, just try it. It's adorable
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and wholesome game. Each character has a unique design and overall the vibes are good. I love the little outfits for Concord, though I didn't personally use them much.It's a shorter game which is definitely a plus since the endgame when I was getting all the achievements became somewhat tedious. The days are sort of the same and it kind of gives the illusion of having different "builds" with different stats and weapons but it doesn't really matter. A little heavier on combat then I expected but overall a decent game to relax with.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much! it's a chill rpg, adventure, and you can literally just take your time doing quests as a lil  grape & help ya fellow folks in The Grove. I will not spoil to much, but I highly reccomend it. the name of all the characters are charming and so witty, love that! Check it out for yourself. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Such a sweet and endearing game! I wish was there was more, quite frankly. It is brilliantly charming and such gorgeous pixel art. I think there is a little lacking in terms of satisfying gameplay, though towards the end the last biome was excellent. 8.5/10!I think the achievements were a little broken for me, however.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game !Cosy little adventure with a beautiful story and interesting characters. I absolutely loved this game !The controls and in game mechanics feel very smooth (and I,m picky about that !), fights a quite easy so it's pretty chill and still feels good !It's also beautiful and cute, I love the style ! The musics are very pleasant too.It's really an amazing game, I enjoyed every single thing about it!!!The only thing i found a bit frustrating is how slow the progression of the villages levels are after lvl 3. but since it's fairly optional if you don't want to do the game 100% it doesn't really matter if you are not a completionist freak like me x)
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is a really very sweet game where you can see the love in many details. Even though it's an RPG, I didn't expect many hours of gameplay at the beginning. But when the story went on longer and I clearly noticed that I wouldn't finish in the next hour, I was pleasantly surprised. You get a good 25 to 28 hours of play.There is not much negative for me. There is more than one area and there is also a choice of weapons and tools. I also found the music great and fitting. To level up the different locations, you have to do a rather big amount of quests, which got a bit annoying towards the end, but it didn't spoil my enjoyment of the game. However, you have to collect quite a lot in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely enjoyed my time with this game.However, the marketing sort of did not do it justice. I see a lot of comparisons to Stardew Valley, but quite the opposite. This game is more like a chill Zelda style game with a sprinkle of doing quests/favors and a day cycle that doesn't do much accept end the day cycle for new quests. If that peaks your interests still, then this game is for you. This game really shows the hero's journey through the mechanics, you're only able to swing your sword a few times before gaining more and more stamina and being able to swing more, hit harder... and it really shows your progression. You're never punished for not rushing into the main quest or doing things within a certain day. My only complaint is not having your daily quests from the board in your menu to quickly see what area/room I'm supposed to be killing enemies or doing a task in. All in all a good experience all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a game to scratch the Stardew Valley itch, and, while I understand the comparisons, I'd liken Garden Story to a simpler Legend of Zelda game. That's certainly not a problem, but there was a heavier combat focus than I was expecting going in. Overall, I had a great time with the game and would have no problem recommending it to someone looking for a chill adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Light action RPG with puzzle elements. Can feel a little grindy at times if you are trying to do everything in the first run, but never felt like a chore. Enjoyed the combat and the music. Concord is adorable and the art style is so cheerful, even when things get a little grim. I had a good time with this game and if you enjoy this style of game I think you will too. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I have troubles recommending Garden Story. It has a lot of bugs and grinding mechanic, which bothered me a lot during my playthrough. The pros weren't satisfying enough to me to compensate the cons.It's a cute game with a lot of lore, and graphics are amazing, but the final boss battle was a disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and easy gathering/fighting game, but I do recommend buying it when it's on sale because 20 euros for such a short game is straight up a scam. I played for 35 hours and I did all achievements and quests, gathered all the in game memories, got all the villages stats to level 5-5-5, maxed out the level of all weapons and collected the maximum amount of all items that I could fit in the storage for OCD reasons LOL.Just finishing the plot would probably require around 15 hours. Way too expensive for 15 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game to just relax. Great sound track, smooth movement and beautiful art style. Though there is a slow start the pace starts pick up with the more upgrades you have. There's a variety of combat methods, each one to progress in the story and each more different than the last. Calm, interesting story and cute art style. Overall 10/10 game, I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes a game similar to Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: "Perhaps what we needed was quiet, dedicated spirit like you."Garden Story has been my first 100% of 2023 and what a way to start a year. Never in my life have I thought 'damn I wish I was a grape' but watching Concord adventure out into the world, looking cute and doing wholesome grape things made me really wish I was a simple little grape wearing a cute little hat and backpack.Aesthetically there's a lot going for the game, the pixel art is all very well done and character animations add even more adorable charm to the game, tied together by a cohesive and pretty pastel colour palette. I'm not well versed on music so all I can really say about the soundtrack aside from it being highly enjoyable is that it tickled my brain in a specifically nostalgic manner that just made me very happy. Particularly Spring Hamlets day theme.I don't want to dive too deeply into the story of the game because I think it's best enjoyed as it gradually unfolds but the basic gist is that the world you reside in has been struggling with an encroaching darkness, known as the rot, and its up to you a simple gardener turned guardian to help restore and reconnect the various communities you travel to. The story is fairly short and the pacing might be a little slow for some but I found myself not wanting to step away. The quote from the start of the review really resonated with me, and there were many other moments just like it that left me Surprisingly Inspired by a game about sentient fruit. Gameplay wise it's a solid action adventure game in the old school Zelda style. It doesn't do anything groundbreaking or new but it controls well and progression was drip fed at a good pace to keep you engaged. I enjoyed each new weapon unlocked per area although I feel like more could be done with some of them. The flute for example was a neat little side quest reward that I would have loved to see be integrated more into gameplay, like in a puzzle, as I didn't ever have a reason to use it.I also appreciated how it was memories that were unlocked through gameplay that was used as the stat system. It made me feel like my actual in game experience was what was making Concord stronger rather than just a straight up leveling system. Overall I'm glad that Garden Story was the first game of the year for me, it was a wonderful experience that I highly recommend. Also all the frogs are Extra Friend Shaped 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great fun little game.  I sincerely thank the dev's for allowing Concord to have the ability to not die, as well as the ability to use dew for health.  I am not young any more, but love games and have terrible reflexes for battles, especially boss battles.   Not having to perish makes the game fun, instead of stressful and frustrating when trying to beat certain bosses as so many other games do.   The tasks/quests can be a bit repetitive, but once you reach different levels, and realize how they really affect Concord during rest, they become more understandable and the story and play makes more sense.  Although normally I prefer playing games with wasd computer keyboard, this one is best playable with a controller.  The music is a perfect fit for the game.  Well worth the money.  Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my favorites, it has a cute aesthetic and wonderful characters, sometimes the dialogue is poorly worded but I hardly minded it. The core gameplay is pretty fun, and I enjoyed building in, and improving the towns. the combat isn't very challenging, and it can be finicky at times, but it didn't impede my enjoyment of the game much, if at all. overall I loved the game and have reached nearly 100% completion as of writing this. However, I have ran into a glitch on multiple occasions that will corrupt your save files. I currently only have one working save file. I do also have one last criticism for the game, some of the areas don't take up the entire screen, which leaves behind large jarring black borders on the sides of the screen, which kind of broke my immersion. Overall, the game is wonderfully charming and its qualities highly outweigh its flaws, I'd heavily recommend giving this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: They're just a lil awkward grape trying their best to make life easier for everyone they meet! The art style is cute and soothing. Also everyone uses they/them pronouns since they're critters & produce and the binary means nothing to them. I'm excited to play more and explore more of the stat builds, leveling system, and of course..... find the root rot that's causing so much trouble!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, very relaxing game with some gameplay flaws. Audio and visual design is excellent. The narrative's focus on communitarian ethos is also a unique spin on the hero's journey. The main downside is that quest design is very repetitive with the same few tasks being recycled over and over. The game is very grindy if you want to get every upgrade. The other main flaw is with gamefeel. As others have noted, combat feels like framedrops are happening, which might be a flaw with optimization or simply with how hitstop is designed. Powerscaling feels wrong. For example, no matter how strong you upgrade your weapon, it always takes three hits to kill the weakest mob in the game. Damage values barely matter. You always have to hit the weakest mob twice, wait a brief period before it can be hit again after it breaks off into a smaller enemy, then kill the remainder. Endgame combat does not feel particularly meaningfully different from early game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: i like how you get a new tool in every town, but there are some downfalls: i had to select controller manually every time i started the game. the weapon switching is very janky because it takes so long and locks your walking direction, it would be fine if weapon switching wasn't so integral to the game. The "mists" (which is a lost woods kinda area) is very annoying to return to. The problem is that there is no way to return manually, you have to traverse 5 or so areas every time you want to leave.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I got my first computer in march of this year and this was the first game I bought for it, and it did not disappoint, love the color schemes and all of the fun, funny little friends u get to make along the way. Not to mention the great message at the end that ties everything back to what's actually going on in the real world today. The sound design is also SO satisfying!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what happened.  Seemed to be working fine, but while in the second town a nasty bug crept in.  Kept losing control.  The controller would work for Steam functions, but not game control.  Character would just get stuck and I would get killed by baddies.  It's a cute little game. _childDocuments_.review: Woo, now that I've completed the main story, I feel qualified to give a review.This is an amazingly cute game. A little bit of Stardew, a little bit of Zelda, and a loving spoonful of indie charm (As well as Dark Souls, but jokingly). Garden Story is an action-adventure RPG about little fruits in a garden fending off rotten goop and trying to rebuild their grove after the departure of their guardians who protected them from The Rot. They also got frogs and sea creatures as friends. It feels like a Zelda game when the protagonist Concord first get his Pick (primary weapon of choice) and you spend the day being shown where everything is and fight a few Rot. The game really railroads you on a certain path in the first few days, preventing you from wandering off into other areas for the sake of progression, but eventually you are given free reign and can open up additional areas. You can also get additional weapons from the store, and through various quests (including required story quests). Your day is spent taking up the mantle of guardian of the Spring Hamlet and helping around town, fighting Rot, gathering resources, and rebuilding parts of the town, and each request you finish will net you EXP for your town's three different aspects which can unlock bonuses such as increased village storage space and personal backpack space.The story builds up as you level up your town and then you are asked to open up the town's resident dungeon and fight off the Rot inside while retrieving a quest item found within. Usually these dungeons have some resources that only it can offer, so revisiting is worth it. They also have pretty decent puzzles worthy of a Zelda top-down game. Afterwards, you will be sent on a quest to visit other towns to help them rebuild and defeat the Rot in their dungeons.Now about The Rot: these globs of decayed fruit flesh have grown restless and have come to attack the peaceful inhabitants of the Grove. They come in several varieties that require different weapons and strategies to kill, such as the shelled Rot requiring you to use the Dowsing Rod to snatch their shell.At the end of each day, you go back to your home base and rest up to check on stats, save the game, and use mind slots to equip memories that give you stat boosts and bonus skills. A really solid roleplaying aspect that is well-implemented and effective at helping you do whatever you need to do.Overall this is a great game, and I recommend it to everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The story is cute and the characters are fun. My bigger gripes are that the combat is a little frustrating at times. Most enemies "die" and then you have to kill a secondary thing afterward which just really slows things down with you having to wait for the second thing to be killable. This game is definitely not a hard one, however, so it's more just a waiting game than anything. I still had a good time playing it, but it also does a poor job of making any weapon except the starting one feel meaningful to use in combat. There are enemies that require specific weapons to allow them to be killed (such as removing whatever is protecting them) but that just furthers the pains of slow combat as it's another step in the process of killing an enemy which isn't very challenging. I'd have liked if the weapons felt more meaningful to use as I just used my Pick (it's a sword) the entire game and only used other things if the enemy absolutely needed it. The sword just did way more damage and it's upgraded effect made it OP as hell - which also further removed the difficulty of the game.I know I'm mostly stating gripes in this review but I actually did still enjoy this game quite a bit. It has some lovely grindy elements to it which I know aren't everyone's thing but sometimes I just like grinding up resources to craft things and this game was extremely chill for that. It has some really great music too.

_childDocuments_.review: An action RPG with lots of heart and a solid foundation, but some unfortunate design issues as well. Excellent art and music, decent gameplay loop, and good progression systems are held back by tedious inventory management, problems in combat, and an underutilized building system. Gets a mixed opinion from me, but skews more towards a positive vote. Read the long version below or look at some more reviews before making a final decision.  is a game about restoring a small community of fruits and vegetables as they fight against an invasive force of creatures called the Rot. It's largely an action RPG sprinkled with elements of other genres, like dungeon crawler, city builder, and life sim. Many have compared it to , but the finer details of  design sets it very far apart from it--for better and for worse. I'll be honest, I was torn on which side of the "Recommended" coin to put this on while going through it. It's not a bad game by any means, but some design decisions made parts of the game underwhelming, if not frustrating. I'll start with the good stuff:As I said before,  has plenty of good things going for it, but now it's time to discuss the not-so-good things that bog it down. None of them are that bad on their own, but after wrestling with them for 10+ hours, it starts to sour the experience. , long enough to finish the story and unlock all the achievements--though I didn't 100% complete all the side content. It's been a real close call deciding where to put this one, and it's one of those times where I wish Steam offered a "mixed opinion" choice of some sort.  The game's already gotten a few updates to address prior issues people had, so it's possible that what I've described will eventually stop being an issue. Until then, though, I can't confidently steer you one way or the other on this one. Most other reviewers seemed happy with their purchase, so if you've gotten this far and still feel that it might be worth your time, give it a shot next time you see it listed at a price you think is fair. Despite the problems I had, it's clear that Picogram and Rose City Games put a lot of heart into making it, and that much is apparent throughout the whole of the game. Whether they opt to fine-tune this game further or move on to new projects, I'm interested to see what comes next for them.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, and here's why: it's like a "casual play" version of an early Zelda game. There are several locations on the map where you need to fight stronger enemies with an increasing collection of weapons and tools. However, the enemies you fight are never that hard to beat (at least once you get the right tools), and each dungeon boss (while playing out like Zelda dungeon boss fights) is relatively easy-ish. As someone who's generally terrible at video games, this makes me happy.The other enjoyable low-key aspect to this game is that it's also a material-gathering game. This is why it gets compared to Starview Valley a lot, as most materials can be found only in specific locations, some by fishing, others by chopping or planting. This is rewarding in part because tools and weapons and such can constantly be upgraded as well. There are always 2-3 errands to run every day, which are optional, but always help increase stats and give you an excuse to gather more items.One of my personal favorite features of Garden Story is that you can manually set the day/night cycle to be longer, which is especially nice when doing dungeon stuff, because in games like Stardew Valley, the day is always too short to get anything meaningful done in late-game play unless you're high on luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Very good. Think turnip boy commits tax evasion mixed with sims, stardew valley, and animal crossing,  but cute pixel art. If I had to pick one game to compare it to, it's most similar to animal crossing, but with a fixed world and combat, but maintaining the incredibly relaxing experience much more than something like stardew valley. I am impressed that they managed to make leisurely, relaxing dungeons that were still reasonably challenging.The story is pleasant and interesting, and can be completely ignored if you like, more or less, kinda like a kirby game (ex. someone hands kirby an incredibly powerful weapon but kirby just wants to eat cake). The art is beautiful and so is the music & sound design.  If you like this sort of thing it is absolutely worth the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is basically a cute, chill legend of Zelda game with a little sprinkle of farming at the end. It goes without saying that the art style is probably one of the cutest to come out in years while avoiding the pitfall of looking off-putting. The game isn't quite as good as something like Legend of Zelda, but by the end some of puzzling elements come close, and the final boss fight is of comparable difficulty. If a chill Legend of Zelda sounds good to you, this game probably won't disappoint.Aside from that, I'll provide one more notable con:I will say is that the control scheme (at least on keyboard) is a little wonky. By the end I was able to get a hold of it, and you could probably beat the game without ever getting a firm grasp over the controls.and one more notable pro:Your achievements or "memories" in the game give you an exchangeable set of upgrades that you can swap out at your home base and provided a surprisingly decent amount of gameplay flexibility. It's a nice change from Legend of Zelda, and I could easily see that being a major benefit over LoZ if they worked on it a bit more (if thy ever release additional content).
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delight to complete! I enjoyed the day-to-day atmosphere, and it felt very relaxing to play! If you like slow paced games with tons of items to collect then I think you'd love this one! The combat felt smooth and I liked collecting materials every day! Plus, I find the art style is really cute and nostalgic! Thanks for the great gaming experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's legend of zelda *lite*. Nice game on a chill weekend. _childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game very much overall. Chill with some nice messages in the dialogue. Collecting and upgrading aspects were fun. _childDocuments_.review: I would call this game a crossover between Stardew Valley and Legend of Zelda. The story line is good, if a little difficult to follow at times (it jumps around a lot, and sometimes certain ideas seem to come out of nowhere, like I missed a piece of dialogue or misunderstood something). Kind of like the community center in Stardew, there are multiple "collections" to complete, and there are tons of hats and backpacks you can collect to customize your character. _childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my gosh do I love this game! The art and characters are adorable. The music is relaxing and I could honestly listen to it all day long. I'm not sure how far into the story I am and I know there are more towns, but currently the first town has, I think about 8 or so daily quests that rotate. I only realized it when I ended up doing a fetch quest a second time, so I don't know how often a quest repeats as I haven't tested it.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game, wonderfull pixel grapics, nice relaxing soundtrack, easy-going and with a decently well written story overall. _childDocuments_.review: I do highly recommend this game. It's a sweet indie pixel game about a little grape that has the fate of the world on his back. You fight little adorable monsters called rot, collect a bunch of resources, and do daily tasks for villages in order to level them up. When you level up villages, you can unlock a bunch more stuff at the store, like weapons, shields, hats and backpacks. The villages are really pretty, with my personal favourite being the Summer bar area, because the village is beautifully designed in a beachy theme. Each village is completely different to each other, and each comes with it's own resources, charming characters and different tasks. To gain more stats, there's a bunch of orbs scattered around the world, which you must find and unlock. As in most games, each village also comes with a boss which you eventually get to. The first boss you face is tricky, but after you realize a couple of things (no spoilers!), it's one in the bag. The rest of the bosses become easy once you've upgraded The game is story rich, as well. Really enjoyed playing this game from beginning to end, and highly recommend it for anyone else to give it a try. If you enjoyed games like Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion, Friendly Fire, and also a little bit of Stardew Valley and Sun Haven, give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, fun, little casual game.  Probably a game best for someone new to video games, someone who is young, or someone who just wants something very casual to play.What I do appreciate about this game (beyond the adorable pixel art) is you don't feel rushed. Thank you! Seriously! When you reach sundown you don't faint or anything but there are things you can only get done during a certain time of day.  I also enjoy the character dialog and personalities.A thing to be aware of is that the game can feel repetitive (the daily quests) so it may not be everyone's cup of tea. The beginning is pretty slow and feels not very eventful. It does get better later. Note I said better but not phenomenal or anything. I do feel like the trailers give a good idea of what you are gonna get when it comes to how eventful it will feel.The combat does feel a little clunky but not unbearable or annoying, and sometimes it is hard to notice if you can walk behind something or not by only looking at it. You do have some options on weapons so you can choose one you like more so unless an enemy requires a certain one. Nothing is game breaking or a deal breaker for me. I am enjoying the game and don't regret buying it but if you feel unsure about this game, maybe take a peek on youtube or something first to get a better idea if it is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as Concord, a grape, who is now the newly appointed guardian of the grove. In your new journey, you'll meet a fruitful cast (literally - there's fuji, plum, and elderberry just to name a few!) and a whole lot of rot! You'll help locals with quests like fixing up broken areas, defeating intruders, and gathering resources. As a guardian, you'll slowly rebuild the towns and restore peace as the previous guardians did.The music brings me back to when I was younger and playing Pokemon on the game-boy. There's something about it that makes me feel young and excited about adventure in a fantastical world. Everything about this game feels light and comfy, and in the best way possible, sort of ordinary. I love the added options in this game - specifically the options to not perish in combat. I love video games, but I don't have much time or patience for combat. It's nice to have it as an added bonus to not worry about items or health. I also love that you can have time slowed down as well. The only gripe I'd have so far is that getting out of the first town seems a bit slower than the others, and the repeated "quests" can be a bit monotonous at times, but it was never to a point that would turn me away from the game. The stamina limitations in the beginning was also a bit annoying to get used to, but you get access to upgrades ("memories") pretty quickly. I liked that you can swap out your memories easily and customize your stats best for your play-style.Overall, I don't think that my opinion will change much upon finishing the game. If you liked the trailer, screenshots, or description, you should absolutely get it. What you see is what you get, and what you'll get is a wholesome, comfy, and digestible package of a sweet, good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I played Garden Story mostly while lying in bed recuperating from hip surgery, and it was really the perfect game for that: a simple, cozy, adorable Zelda-like action adventure.The best things about Garden Story are the things you can see in the screenshots and videos: the whole game is just charming and wholesome.Another review described this game as having a "downward-sloping difficulty curve" and I found that extremely accurate.  At the very beginning of the game you have access to very few upgrades, and the first boss might be moderately challenging if you don't have the few upgrades that are available.  After that, you start getting memories (upgrades unlocked with a sort of in-game achievement system), character stat upgrades, and equipment upgrades, all of which decrease the difficulty considerably if you're inclined to play in a completionist way.In a way, Garden Story's superficial inspirations from Stardew Valley really work against it: in Stardew Valley your various chores are a major part of the game and usually fairly engaging, and you'll want to keep doing them to advance through the game.  This trained me to think I should try to complete them all in Garden Story as well.  In Garden Story, however, the job board tasks are mostly tedious, and necessary if and only if you need to decrease the difficulty level from "easy" to "casual".  Even a mediocre gamer like myself could probably get away with doing very few of them, just enough to access the majority of the character upgrades.  Instead I ended up doing enough to upgrade the towns to mostly level 3 or 4, which is probably about 50% of the work to get _everything_ in the game, and this turned out to be way overkill: I found the second half of the game to be extremely easy with that many upgrades.There are a few other mechanics that ended up falling a bit flat: the game has a system for building stuff, which had me excited for about two minutes but turned out to be largely useless, and a farming mechanic that's useful only to farm some of the items you need for the tool upgrades you don't need.  These both ended up feeling superfluous. They don't hurt the game but they don't help it and the development time would probably have been better spent on other content.So my recommendation is:- Don't worry much about the more tedious aspects of the game like the job boards unless you get stuck. Just play the game to complete it and appreciate the cute characters and world. It'll be a somewhat shorter game, but probably a better one.- This is a small game by a solo developer.  It's a fun diversion for a weekend.  Go into it expecting that and appreciate it for what it is, and don't expect it to be Stardew Valley, and don't expect it to have the scope or scale of a Zelda game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a beautiful story and great game play. It took me 18 hours of off and on playing to beat it, and every hour was worth it. Some of the boss battles are a little difficult in the beginning, especially when your weapons are "under leveled" until you can get the proper materials to upgrade. The puzzles weren't too bad once I understood what I needed to do. If you like cozy games, I HIGHLY recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: At $20, this charming game's a bit pricey, but it's an interesting story played out with adorable characters. The game is a fun and interesting blend of 16-bit Zelda with farming games. There's a lot to like about this game.  There's also a lot the game -almost- gets right. The game feels incomplete and has little to no replay value. A majority of game play will be spent doing short semi-optional side quests that quickly become repetitive, and tedious. The farming aspect of the game is poorly developed and largely useless. One could be forgiven for thinking the game would be a lot stronger if the Developers scrapped the farming aspect, and just focused on dungeon crawling Zelda style.But even being fully aware of the game's flaws, there's just something fundamentally adorable and likable about the protagonist.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. I ended up playing through and beating it in a span of barely 2 days, not because the game was too short, but because I was practically glued to my seat the entire time. It's fun, positive, but doesn't shy away from the melancholy and sad stuff. There's a wide variety of equipment and weapons to choose from, and a great system of feat-related perks that you can pick and choose from at any save point, any time. In short, this is one of the best games I've played in a long time. I absolutely loved it. Can't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid RPG. It feels good to play, you have lots of options in combat, and you never feel rushed or lost.The town mechanics aren't as relevant as I was expecting, as you can only start customizing your towns about halfway through the game, and even then only in a few select spots. You also only get the ability to garden at the 3/4 mark. This is a little disappointing, as those mechanics have a lot of potential but Garden Story doesn't focus on themThe part I was most worried about was the timer. In a similar way to Stardew Valley, Garden Story tracks time and days. The good news is, though, that the day/night cycle is extremely lenient and the number of days you take to beat the game don't matter. At the end of the day, instead of passing out like in Stardew, you just stay in nightime with the downside being that there are more aggressive enemies.Again, this is a very very solid RPG and I'm happy with my time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story is lovely! It's a game about supporting/rebuilding your community in a way that I find *very* satisfying; progression just...really scratches an itch for me, idk how to describe it? I like doing the different tasks assigned each day, and so far the writing has been very charming. It also seems like there's a lot of game here with the different villages, which is exciting! I think my only complaint is combat/movement feels a little slow/clunky off the bat, but that's starting to be alleviated the more I play. (Wouldn't mind being able to move a little bit quicker, or spam roll outside of combat tho!)I wholeheartedly recommend this game, especially if you like games focused on restoring/repairing villages/communities! (a niche, to be sure lol)

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully charming little game, and one of my most anticipated for this year. Overall a well made and wholesome experience, perfect for a sappy person like me <3  I appreciate a game that knows exactly what it wants to be, with all the charm and quirks that may entail; it was a joy to discover all of the cute little animations, and several of Concord's more unique items! I'll for sure be listening to this soundtrack for a long time, and revisit the game once in a while just to chill, even after I've finished it!My only criticisms lies in the building system being a bit less expansive than expected, and how repetitive some of the village tasks ended up feeling if you're a completionist. With that being said though, the rewards for maxing out villages seem to be small, and in no way necessary for completing the game, so I wouldn't consider it a big issue for most!Overall, huge recommend for this lovely little grape game. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very charming game with a lot of similarities to older Legend of Zelda games Stardew Valley, but leaning more towards Zelda. At least in the first few hours there isn't any gardening going on but it still has that feel to it.Combat elements start of pretty simple and feeling very similar to older zelda games, but the combat does mix up a bit later on with different feeling weapons.Each day is spent doing odd jobs around town, looking for specific materials and progressing main story goals. The way the map opens up to you is very fun. Right about when you know everything about an area you open up a new path and have a whole new area to explore.The only real negative I have found is some slight frame rate issues. In my 6 hours so far i've seen 3 or 4 times where the fps has dropped to 20's during some fights, not game altering but noticeable. The combat is slow enough that its never caused any problem but wanted to make note of it. But overall a great experience so far. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a chill game with some simple combat and community building elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Garden Story tries to do a few different things, some work out better than others.At the core are daily tasks that have you gather resources and fighting rot. It's a good intro into new areas, having you explore the area. The length of the day feels short at first but is long enough once you have learned the ropes. A bit annoying is the lighting: In the morning and evening every character has a light around them and the background is slightly darker - that is 2/3 of the day where the background isn't fully visible for no good reason.Gathering resources is alright, they are used by the daily tasks and every specimen can be added to the library. The library is supposed to give you more building options, but these are under-utilised. There are few places where you can build and what you can build is either the same as what already is there or just a bit of decoration. Building repair kits to repair or clear ways comes up like ... 4 times.Fighting, while a bigger part of the game, isn't really smooth. Some attacks don't seem to hit what's in front of you. There are good few different weapon types that can be (and need to be) utilized, but the enemies mostly are the same throughout the game. The Story of Garden Story isn't to complex and is missing a twist, but is well told nevertheless. The characters have personality, but there is too little time getting to know many of them. Mostly they keep in the background.Boss fights can be a bit of a challenge, but over all the difficulty needs to be higher. The seed planting seems like it should work, but it just isn't needed - it doesn't feed into any other game loop. Money is never an issue (well, maybe because I haven't bought decorative items ever). There is a dire need for some kind of resource drain - a bit more grinding wouldn't be bad, the story really goes over too fast.If you like a easy and chill game after a day of work (or school), this game might be for you. If you expect something like Stardew Valley, this is not it.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

I also felt like some gameplay elements were unnecessary or that there wasn't enough reward for 100% completion of certain things. Overall I'd give it a 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a Stardew-style game. It's a Zelda-style game. I don't know why gaming articles kept calling it Stardew-like... The farming is more like Pokemon Ruby and Sapphire. You plant a seed and come back in a few days and it's done growing - that's it. You only unlock it halfway through the game.Anyway, this game is simple. The bosses are tough, but the dungeons are mostly about resource management, rather then the puzzles being complex. The combat has a variety of weapons you can upgrade through stores. I've used them all, and every weapon is unique in some way. That said, combat is fairly slow and you'll need to plan your escape. Mostly, combat is about managing your resources (attacking takes stamina, you need to prepare to escape if you run out. Potions take a few seconds to drink.)You can upgrade yourself by finding these fruit thingies and breaking them (increased stamina and health), you can upgrade your weapons by collecting stuff in the world and trading it in at stores, and you can upgrade the town by completing these daily quests called requests. You don't have to complete them, by the way, but the more requests you complete overall, the more the town is upgraded. An upgraded town has less monsters in it, and sells more item upgrades. Upgrades for upgrades.The pixel art is very simple, but cute. That basically sums up the game.The game is divided into days. Every time you want to save, you sleep in a bed. You can only 2-3 requests per day, by the way. Because of this, I don't recommend playing for hours without advancing the story at all, it can get grindy. I enjoyed it, but I play clicker games for fun, so. If you want a game you can play for hours at once, this might not be for you.This is the kind of game you play to relax, and if you feel that other games are too stressful and demanding. It doesn't require much of your time and it doesn't require you to play for hours to get through it. You can advance the story whenever you want, and the NPCs don't mind if you take a little while to move on. Like I said, relaxing. If you like to do a lot in a game, this game might not be for you.The pixel art is cute, but simple. Basically, this game is a simple, undemanding game that's very cute and you shouldn't play it for too many hours at once or it might get grindy.As for the plot, it's a melancholy story about the world slowly ending. The Grove (the place where everyone lives) is infested with rot and everything is just kind of getting worse. You, the player, can improve things by working at it and connecting towns together. While you don't solve everything, at the end you are able to make things fixable. Everyone you've met along the way helps too. I think you can complete this in about 20 hours, playing normally. Play it if you like simple and relaxing. It's not a game for everyone, but if it's for you it might be perfect.Also if you want a good farming game that isn't Stardew Valley, play Story of Seasons. This is not a farming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Although it can feel slow at the start, Garden Story is a wonderful game with a charming world and new discoveries at every corner. I'm not too far in yet, but I feel like the game progression is satisfying, with unique weapons and tools that help you gain access to new areas.My only real complaint is that there isn't much variety amongst the enemies, at least in the first two towns. Even this isn't a huge issue, as it feels like the unique design of the level bosses makes up for it.If you enjoyed games like Undertale, Legend of Zelda: Minish Cap, or Hades, I think this will appeal. It's a cute game about growing and learning while exploring the world around you. It does a good job of combining combat and story elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: Superbly charming game. The characters, environments, and music are wonderfully crafted and give the game such a nice, relaxing atmosphere. Combat mechanics aren't my cup of tea, but the accessibility features are really appreciated and help enjoy the game at my own pace. I never expected to fall in love with this little grape and fruit friends, but Concord and co. are so central to the game's atmosphere and easy to adore. Plus, the "going to sleep" animation is a blessing to this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, cheerful game, with enough pace to keep things interesting without getting stressful. The animation of Concord settling down to sleep always put a huge smile on my face, and all the worlds are really gorgeous and unique. I really enjoyed the mechanic whereby you could unlock memories from previous Guardians, and then use these to give yourself increased stats/special weapon buffs. This was so well done, and really meant you could tailor the game to your preferred combat/playstyle.Yes, there are a couple of things that feel grindy (e.g. there's not much variation in village errands) and I would have liked it if the errands had more of a visual impact on the towns. For example, if you've given some sap to mend a broken house, it would be lovely if you could actually see the house fixed in the world. But these are only small gripes in the grand scheme of things, because I really enjoyed my time with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely little game. Here are the pros and consPros- Great pixel art and an amazing soundtrack- Relaxing to the max- Story surprisingly engaging- Memory system felt rewardingCons- Really easy after an hour or so- Gardening and crafting are introduced a bit too late in the game- Some tasks can get boring after a whileGarden Story is definitely a great game. You can boost through the game quickly, but I'd say that the game has a lot to offer if the player takes it slow. The presentation is definitely the highlight and the story is engaging. The combat was the main focus of the game. It wasn't amazing, but it kept me entertained. I'd recommend this game to anyone who's a fan of action adventure games and to the fans of Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Garden Story

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game about a small grape helping the four seasonal towns. After the introduction the game follows a ready pattern: do some quests for the town, delve the dungeon, and fix the connection to the next town!You get an assortment of upgradeable weaponry, my favorite being the delving rod, that also act as your tools for getting resources and repairing things.My only gripe with this game is that for a game called 'garden story' you don't do a heck of a lot of gardening. You unlock the ability pretty far into the game and while each seed does give a different product depending on the area, not a heck of a lot of reason to actually do it.

_childDocuments_.review: visual: 9/10audio: 11/10gameplay: 8/10narrative: 8/10challenge: 7/10replayability: 9/10value: 9/10personal grade: 9/10pros:- phenomenal OST, go Grahm Nesbitt!- strong, inspiring narrative- great variety of gameplay mechanics that get sprinkled in at a good pace- outstanding pixel art thats cute and invitingcons:- clunky combat, iffy hitboxes- punishing in the beginning (not a con, but may be turn off for some players)- more focus on combat than farming (not a con, but may be turn off for some players)total score: 9/10please watch the full review at Do you ever get tired of the burdens of mundane life? Are you ready to embark on a journey graper than yourself? Your home has been desecrated by the mysterious Rot, and Guardian Plum has left your town, appointing you the new Guardian of Spring Hamlet. You are Concord, Guardian Grape, and the destiny of The Grove now lies in your tiny little stems!Garden Story, the newest game by solo developer Picogram, contains strong scents of Harvest Moon and My Time at Portia due to its beautifully hand-drawn pixel art and delicate musical score. However, upon closer inspection, Garden Story is more of a hybrid between a Zelda lite and Stardew Valley, with gameplay elements from an action RPG and a life simulator. The game deliciously weaves together themes of community, self-discovery, and personal identity.If it wasn’t clear already, you play as an adorable, stumpy, round, purple grape, who has spent its entire life in the Kindergarden, maintaining a single vine with the life essence of The Grove known as Dew. All the inhabitants of Garden Story live in The Grove, home to a massive tree full of mana and partitioned into four towns based on the seasons: Spring Hamlet, Summer Bar, Autumn Town, and Winter Glade.One day, Guardian Plum lets you out of the Kindergarden and informs you of his upcoming departure. He appoints you to be his successor, teaching you the basics of combat and how to help out neighboring towns. But you soon discover, unfortunately, that the very lifeline of The Grove is threatened by a dark force known as The Rot, and it is up to you to help rebuild each of the aforementioned towns and re-establish their communication with each other. So many games have you traveling from place to place without giving you opportunities to feel a sense of ownership. In Garden Story, however, you have a place to call home in each village that you visit! The main gameplay loop revolves around talking to main characters to progress the narrative and interacting with a bulletin board next to your house that assigns you daily quests to level up and rebuild the village. Some main quests require your village to be at a certain level before becoming available, so it is in your best interest to complete some every day! Of course, the higher your village’s level, the better items the shops will sell as well.Daily quests are divided up into three categories: combat in which you defeat some Rot; building. where you rebuild a bridge or fix a fence; and gathering where you collect resources to donate to the village. Though straightforward, the daily tasks vary from day to day so they aren’t mundane and tedious. In addition to the aforementioned main quests and daily tasks, there are also side quests from various characters found in the world and challenging dungeons to explore. Picogram did a fantastic job instilling a sense of hope, belonging, and community by deepening your connection with the inhabitants of The Grove. At first glance, Garden Story seems to focus heavily on resource gathering, town-building, and farming. However, there is a prominent focus on combat in the game that is reminiscent of vanilla Dark Souls. Unfortunately, the combat is a bit clunky as it feels slow and unresponsive. Hitboxes are also wonky and minuscule. Some enemies are weirdly unbalanced, especially the mini ooze Rots that deal on-contact damage and are extremely difficult to hit. As you fight the Rot throughout your journey, you have a stamina bar that depletes every time you swing your weapon or dodge roll. You are given a shield to use too, but I found myself rarely using it, if ever. Combat is surprisingly challenging initially and gets progressively lenient because you start with only 3 hit points and 2 stamina bars. Every time you defeat a boss, you are rewarded with a permanent increase to your hit points and stamina bar. Furthermore, as you explore, achieve weapon mastery, and help out townsfolk, you collect memories that can be equipped to further customize your playstyle, with memories that may further increase your health and stamina or give you better luck or healing potency. Alongside the combat, there are also mango-nificent puzzles to complete that keep you engaged. The puzzles start simple but get gradually more arduous. Still, they are never un-raisin-able!As you progress further into the game, every new village you visit will introduce you to a new gameplay mechanic that keeps tasks fresh and exciting. For example, by the time you get to the second town, you receive the dowsing rod that you can use to fish items out of the ocean and rip otherwise unbreakable shells off of Rot enemies. Then, when you reach the Winter Glade, you receive a pair of snazzy ice skates!Building structures and gardening resources also get introduced later on to scratch that Stardew Valley itch. Though more low-key and not as emphasized as combat, the ability to actually create structures and cultivate plants further drives the theme of belonging and community. The more you customize your town, the more lively and personal it begins to feel. Garden Story is really about building your home. A fiery maraschino cherry even offered to stand guard in front of my house at night to fight off any Rot that might wander in!To be honest, Garden Story and I got off on the wrong foot in the beginning. The tutorial wasn’t that helpful, the gameplay menus were overwhelming, combat didn’t feel smooth, and the PC key bindings were awkwardly placed. However, once I took the time to appreciate the luscious world and the fruits of my labor, the title began to feel zen. By the end of it, I couldn’t help but feel proud of Concord’s advancement from an isolated grape gardener to a world-saving guardian.On top of all those aforementioned points, there’s nothing better to do than relaxing in The Grove’s inviting atmosphere, conversing with my frog friend Rana, cultivating gardens, and listening to the cherry-sweet music of the Summer Bar. I cannot express enough love for the original soundtrack composed by Grahm Nesbitt. It truly immersed me into the plum-forgettable world to the point where I played the OST in the background as I wrote this review.Garden Story isn’t necessarily about what you do, since you mostly take on simple and tedious tasks. Instead, the game is about the people you meet along the way, the lives you touch, the connections you make, and ultimately not forgetting about your roots, no plum intended. It has honestly been a while since I’ve been emotionally moved by a game this sweet, especially one paired with a beautiful soundtrack. If you are looking for a cozy world-building game with some combat and a whole lot of charm and whimsy, then The Grove welcomes you like a home away from home. Concord, you’re truly one-in-a-melon, and you did a grape job raisin me!visit  for more reviews!

name: KATANA KAMI: A Way of the Samurai Story
detailed_description: The Way of the Samurai is forged in battle! Play as a ronin during Japan's Meiji Restoration in the volatile Rokkotsu Pass. The swordsmith Dojima falls into debt and his beautiful daughter is taken as collateral. Help repay the debt by crafting swords by day and exploring the mysterious, twisting dungeons of the Ipponmatsu Cave for valuable materials at night. Key Features Hone Your Skills - Over 100 different weapons and 9 fighting styles means you can fight any way you please! Mysterious Dungeons - An isometric hack and slash with randomly-generated dungeons to explore in a historical Japanese setting. Two Swords are Better Than One - Explore dungeons with others Balance of Power - Ally, betray, or maintain neutrality in dealing with the town's three factions. The fate of Rokkotsu Pass is balanced by the tip of a blade! Familiar Faces - Featuring fan favorite characters from the Way of the Samurai series!
