_childDocuments_.review: Fun for your money. An absolutely loveable setting where the world is literally built by written stories, but now the ink is fading and you have to do something about it.The basic gameplay loop is to pick a class ("aspect") and play through a rogue-like dive which takes somewhere between 45-75 minutes. In a dive you will make choices for upgrades/money/stats, and fight against continuously stronger enemies in a turn-based combat RPG fashion. Meta progression: Rather than unlock flat upgrades for future dives, you unlock new types of items that can appear in future dives. It is an online-only game, and even though it is in early access the game already sells a season pass for cosmetic unlocks. Therefore I think it would be best to consider this a 30$ purchase, which is the base game (20$) plus season pass (10$). You get enough of the mtx currency to buy future season passes by completing the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Having played a lot of different roguelites, I can definitely say that this one is quite the banger! I remember getting this game in Early Access seeing it's witty charm and having played it since then, I wholeheartedly recommend this one! They ended up getting rid of the in-game monetization (kudos to doing that) and in turn made the cosmetics from The Story Begins and The Starship of Terrors original battle passes into buyable DLCs (which all cosmetics from those tracks are unlocked from acquiring the DLCs). There's still a leveling system in which you can unlock various items, and each run now gives a chance to have a special container that houses a mystery item ranging from an emote to a cosmetic (all of which can be unlocked via the Arcane Dust shop, which Dust can be acquired through leveling up).The latest expansion also offers a bit of a rework to how runs operate with vestiges; each vestige now has a set bonus to them, and you can grind up vestiges you find in (what used to be Tether Shrines) to double and permanently add their set bonus for a run (keep in mind this stacks on top of what you're building vestige wise, so you want to aim to have a synergy between scrapping vestiges and finding new ones to help build something to your playstyle).The classes are semi easy to unlock; you start out with 3 (Magma Miner, Mosscloak, and Weaver) and then have to unlock the other 5 (Clairvoyant, Obelisk, Star Captain, Chainbreaker, and Godkeeper). Each class has their own versatile play style, and (for the most part) you can build them how ever you choose. During runs, you can augment your class abilities and even morph them into stronger forms at certain points. The old system used to mainly keep track of what your vestiges gave for the run, but I feel the new system actually has decent synergy by combining vestige powers with passive set bonuses.There are plenty of surprises to be had with Inkbound, and (can't stress this enough) it's definitely worth the price even if on sale too, it's one you want to add to your library if you're a fan of co-op games and roguelites!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This has been an amazing game for my boyfriend and I to play! I recently started a programming boot camp, so between working all day and having my weekends taken up this has been a fun activity for us to share as I don't have the time for MMO's atm but this gives a nice segmented block of fun that we can share (although I tend to keep wanting to play even after our self allotted time xD) and the game respects your time with each fight being fun and with no trash! Inkbound is worth a pickup now and I think its only going to get better as it is developed! If it looks interesting to you I would inkorage you to pick it up and join the discord as its a lovely community!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Very poorly balanced, wouldn't recommend honestly.+Decent story, but gets super grindy to get anything out of it.+Decent bit of cosmetics save otherwise bland player characters+A good bit of variety, but it's a shame most of it isn't viable later on.-Only a few viable builds per class-No passive stat gain from leveling or progression outside of each match-Leveling up you actively shoot yourself in the foot when you unlock vestiges that are hot garbage cluttering up your loot pool-Every fight is on a time limit making shields and durability builds useless-Higher difficulties add the most obnoxious and overpowered modifiers to enemies and/or make them extremely spongy to waste your time until the ink kills you moving in.-Enemies making lingering damage fields on top of the arena constantly getting smaller is horrendous game design.-Bosses are generally speaking very annoying with constantly spawning minions with undodgeable attacks. And the same time limit as normal fights, as well as being affected by stage modifiers like the 25% bonus damage per round they survive among others which makes you get one-shot later on. Not to mention on top of the arena closing in some bosses have massive aoe attacks with lingering damage fields.No progression besides unlocking cosmetics and vestiges as well as all these frustrating aspects of the gameplay completely ruin it unfortunately. The game had potential but I think I'm going to play something better now.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: If Monster Train was Slay the Spire + Tower Defense then this game is Slay the Spire + Action RPG Positioning. Shiny Shoe might be onto something! It's very much still a deckbuilding card game and if you're at all interested in those types of games this is an excellent one. The developers are listening to feedback and updating frequently, having just added complete offline play support and removed previously poorly received cosmetic monetization strategies. The game seems to always be evolving in a positive direction and I'm here for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely incompatible with this game's vibe. As a long-time fan of tactics games, roguelikes, and even Monster Train, I really wanted to enjoy this. It looked like a unique take on Phantom Brave, Hades, Dragon Age, etc. But when I launched it, I felt an immediate revulsion. Every design decision, whether it be graphics, world building, UI, but especially the gameplay was a huge turn off. That's not to say the game itself is bad. You may have better mileage. But for me? Absolutely not.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: The mtx shop and season pass in an early access game is disappointing but the game is a fresh and smooth feeling turn-based coop. I feel like it's price tag is justified as it currently stands. There is no P2W as of this review and is purely cosmetic.edit: the shop has been removed and there are no complaints with monetization.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This is an AMAZING co-op game, even without co-op it's really fun and refreshing. The battles are turn based but it's almost like valkyria chronicles, you can use 1 point to move in a circle, as soon as you do an attack it grounds you to that spot, but then 1 ap can move you in a circle again.The items are roguelike, each run is different and the item/bindings/augments really change every character each run. Seriously fun game, good jobs devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting idea but this just doesn't work. It's awkward and the turn based part just falls on it's face. You have four people playing 1v1 against the AI it feels like rather than a cohesive strategy going on like in For the King or something.This is probably something you play solo or MAYBE with one other person.It is also worth pointing out that when we had 4 people fighting the boss, each attack was doing 0.018% of it's max health, plus we had ads it spawned every turn we had to attack so we didn't even get to dump all that sweet, sweet .018% into the boss.Naturally, it was refunded because there are better single player games available and the co op didn't work out well for my group.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I love when a game exits early access and proves that some titles deserve the extra time to cook. I feel like I'm benefiting from a lot of love from the devs and the community when I load into a game. The party finding system is easy and seamless, and the voice acting took me by surprise in its quality, consistency and depth. To top it all off, it absolutely has the rogue-lite big damage numbers and complex combat that makes me want to dive back into the ink.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Game-play. Good variety in classes. Could use more bosses. I'm not a fan of season passes as I like to choose what game to play based on how I'm feeling, and anything that adds a feeling of obligation hurts my enjoyment. With that said, I enjoy the content available and feel I got my moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap this game is fun. Randomly bought it not really knowing what it was, but my god am I happy I did. Free-aim turn-based roguelite is basically how you describe this masterpiece. There are currently 5 classes that you can play and freely swap before starting a run. Something I didn't expect, it's coop! You can play with friends or alone and have an absolute blast. If you're interested even in the slightest, please support. You won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Low hour review:Take Hades then add multiplayer and make it async turn-based. Stellar formula for a fun game, especially with friends.In my opinion, Hades bullet hell and button-mashy playstyle was frustrating. Inkbound replaces both of those aspects with strategic movement and interesting combat decisions. I'm 5hrs deep and have only scratched the surface of the content in this game. Excited to sink 100+ hours!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from Shiny Shoe. Inkbound is a great co-op PvE experience that is fun with friends, alone, or even with randos. I played since alpha and the game has only got better and better. With many different classes, draftable abilities, unique random items, and ability augments, no 2 runs are truely the same. There are only 2 potential downsides to the game in its current state. Right now I think there just a bit too few draftable abilities, but considering we are still in early beta I expect this to be addressed before release. The game is going to be online-only. Considering the well built co-op and plan to regularly update the content, I think it's a small price for these things. Shiny Shoe is back with their fresh innovations and solid core gameplay loops. I have full faith that they will polish this gem into something fantastic. This is well worth a wishlist add.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A unique roguelike experience from the creators of Monster Train (which I loved).This game features a turn-based, position-based combat, where you have limited movement and limited actions during your turn, which you need to utilize carefully in order to prevail.The Orb system incentivises planning ahead and the build possibilities are plenty.Higher difficulties do tend to sometimes boil-down to certain OP builds, but that is what this game is about, the game will occassionally throw unfair situations at you, but you are able to build yourself into an OP beast - and when you do, it's very satisfying.My only qualms with this game is that it is a little bit unbalanced at the moment - poison and spike builds are easier to make into an OP build than other things, so you tend to shift towards those on higher difficulties.This game is 100% worth your money :)
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Solid early access game from the creators of Monster Train. If you take the core elements of what makes Monster Train successful (upgrading cards/skills, finding artifacts, making branching decisions, 'breaking' your build) and apply that to a 1-4 player, turn-based, hero-kills-arena-boss type game, you'll really enjoy Inkbound. Do not compare this game to Monster Train, because Inkbound stands out as its own game, not as a successor. The dev team is extremely receptive and dedicated to improving the game's experience based on the activity in their Discord. I'm really impressed by how quickly they acknowledged and addressed balance issues post-launch so far.I have played Inkbound for around 8 hours on PC and 10 hours on the Steam Deck and really love/prefer playing this game on the deck. I have mostly been playing single-player unranked runs to complete challenges and unlock vestiges to use for future runs. There's plenty of quest content and hero mastery to keep you busy for well over 20 hours. I haven't even played any ranked runs with friends yet, which is where I think this game will shine the most and is where most of my future hours will be spent.I'm really excited to see how this game evolves, what content is added, and how the devs approach balancing in the future. Well done Shiny Shoe!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I doubt the devs were reading my review specifically, but as of this writing they've promised to address most of the problems I've laid out here. Only time will tell if they make good on their promises, but I'm glad they're listening to feedback.This game breaks my heart. As a followup to the amazing Monster Train I expected the devs to have a bit more integrity, but instead they've shoved a bunch of Fortnite-style microtransactions ad battle passes into an otherwise promising early access game. The game mechanics are solid and the visual design is interesting, but it's all a bit undermined by just how many games there are these days screaming at you to do your daily quests and you to check to if the oh-so-magnanimous devs are offering you the *chance* fork over five bucks to buy that shiny hat you want. Especially when there's no assurance that the servers are going to be around after a few years. If this game were free to play, maybe I wouldn't mind so much. Hell, for twenty bucks I'd be fine if they nickle and dimed me in a honest way, by letting me see the whole list of cosmetics to buy instead of having a rotating selection of goods. I hope that Shiny Shoe does some soul-searching in this regard, because as long as they're trying to chase the "Live Services" bandwagon, I really can't recommend Inkbound.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: After having player the beta and now playing the EA i can say safely that this game is a blast and worth every penny for roguelike enjoyers that are looking for a party/co-op experience.although i will say the solo mode leaves something to be desired, mainly due to unavoidable damage from multiple sources, and since you are solo there is very few options to maneuver through these sticky situations.special mention:the battle pass is amazing , you receive premium currency for the free pass portion that lets you buy the premium portion for 3 euros ( or if you put the early acess code for completely free )and it only adds cosmetics to the game, so this is completely fair , i would disregard the discontent for this matter i think it's a good idea for the studio to keep getting money to fund further patches as long as it doesn't affect gameplay .
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this, you should buy this game and support this developer, then send some friends here too. I loved Monster Train, though I know deckbuilders aren't for everyone. Inkbound, however, is a tactical, turn-based, roguelike that's as if they combined Hades with the planning in Transistor - AND IT CAN BE CO-OP! This game is in early development and it is already amazing. As I mentioned, it is reminiscent of a Supergiant game, which is a great thing as we need more Supergiants and Shiny Shoes. If you like games that make you think and provide a canvas for creativity with a dash of random chance, give Inkbound a try.I am very excited to see how this game grows and hope to experience as much chaos as they can fit into it. More characters, bind choices, augments, trinkets, set bonuses! I love working with the hand that I am dealt. Keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I'm assuming this game is at mixed reviews simply due to people not having friends to play the game with. I have no comment on solo play but as a co-op game this one is absolutely fantastic. It truly nails the roguelike feel it's going for while at the same time being tactical and strategic when playing in a party. There's variety to builds and damage types and all the classes feel very unique and viable. As for the microtransactions and battlepass it's all cosmetics and it's not very expensive. Deep Rock does the exact same thing and that game gets non stop praise so you really can't win with some people.At the end of the day if you have a friend or two that are interested in this game I'd say go for it. There's a bunch of fun to be had here, especially if you enjoy roguelikes and turn based games.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Inkbound is a game with infinite complexity provided in a very simple and easy to understand package. There is a great mix of tactics and character building that works well solo. Add in other players and the battlefield becomes significantly more complex and interesting. One of the best aspects is how well the multiplayer combat works. Being able to take your turns simultaneously has really opened up the speed of a multiplayer turn-based game. I highly recommend Inkbound. It has much to offer and I look forward to seeing where Shiny Shoe takes this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game 10/10.I have played many many roguelike games over the years some I have enjoyed some that felt like garbage. Cons. Minor Bugs - all being fixed with regular patches. Some minor QoL issues - Not that they negatively impact the gameplay itself more to do with ease of use. No controller support.Some inconsistencies in the difficulties of fights.Pros.Interesting and diverse gameplay.Wide variety of classes with unique play styles. Works on Steam deck - Not optimised but easily playable Offline single playerNo microtransactions Co-op multiplayer.Things to remember the game is in Early Access so there will be minor issues but the dev team are pretty responsive on discord and they do listen to the player base.Go forth Needless!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Plenty of quests. Playing with your friends, working together on your builds, trading items and planning out combos. Negative reviews due to premium currency for cosmetics, which in no way effect the game. Negative reviews for the battlepass. Just dont buy the stuff? Its all cosmetic. You can earn other cosmetics just by playing the game and completing quests. Its like going bowling and saying bowling sucks because they sell alcohol there. Just dont buy it. This in no way takes away from how good the game actually is, and how much fun you can have playing with your friends.Recent server resets and hotfixes out of the blue while youre on a run right before the final boss is a disaster. Its basically a giant waste of time if theres a server reset while youre playing because you have to start over. This is a huge issue right now because of the nature of the game. Roguelike, always online. If the server resets youre screwed. Id imagine they have the hotfixes ironed out within a day or so and then they would be more planned out. But as of now theres only like a 15 minute warning. Which is no where near enough time to finish the run. Pretty game breaking tbh. But other than this, I personally have not ran into any issues or bugs. Quality game. Excited for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Really a great concept between all the build flexibility, different classes, and the modicum of objectives I can get done in one sitting. I've never been a huge fan of Rogue-like games just because I always feel I reach a "stale" point in my game-play but this game manages to keep me chomping at the bit with every update and the constant completion of one objective or another even when I fail my hardest runs. It's both fun to play solo and experiment with what you can find to best survive each situation thrown at you but also fun in Co-op as well to see how you and your friends can take on the every increasing difficulty of each run in the sea of ink as you delve to higher and higher challenge levels tacking on more fun "challenge" objectives to keep each run fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A very good and fun rogue-like experience which can be played in Coop.The combat is turn based and fairly simple, it was constantly improved in the Early Access Phase. I played the game in Beta and it has come a long way and I still liked it back then.Even though the game is EA, I haven't encountered ANY bug so far, it feels very polished.The cost is fairly low, but it has a season pass already in EA (with only cosmetics), that's why some reviews are negativ. I bought the first season pass and could buy the second one with the currency I had earned with the first one.I can recommend this game to have chill playthroughs with friends, but the new ranked version increasing in difficulty makes it also a great came for people pushing to the limit.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I've always loved the game, it is a very unique turn based system and entertaining for bouts of time when I was in the mood, but the daily system and battlepass leveling was very tedious and basically you needed to play even when you didn't feel like it. Absolutely thrilled that they reworked it and granted everyone the battlepass rewards that they bought and also removed monetization entirely. I will absolutely be getting future supporter packs to support the game that is, at its core, extremely fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept, played mostly early access, so many things have changed but not sure if changed for the better.I find way too many unwinnable situations.I am okay with being punished for a mistake, often i find you are being punished for bad RNG with items and spells.maybe i missed a tutorial between EA changes, but undodgeable attacks are not fun when they can 1 hit you or pile on fight to fight.Something is missing to balance out the RNG or at least getting stronger as you level to combat the bad RNG, IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure why all the reviews are complaining that the telegraphed moves and dodging attacks is gone when it's literally not. They just made some attacks only avoidable by defensive skills, so you actually have to pick some options that aren't pure damage or movement, or be prepared to offset the damage you take by spending money or sacrificing stat boosts to restore health. A lot of attacks are still avoidable through simply moving out of the way of the indicator, that part is far from goneThe game's only evolved for the better, in my opinion. Though there is still room for improvement, and there are mechanics from the demo I wish they would bring back, like enemies that would attack if your party takes too many actions. Exchange some of the new auto-hit moves for those, and the game would be amazingThe paid battlepass is a little strange, though, especially for a €20 indie game, but it's far from egregious and only affects cosmetics anyway. You're not losing any gameplay experience by not paying money beyond the initial €20
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: After having played this in an earlier testing stage, the new amount of unavoidable damage dealt to the player is too discouraging to want to play the game much more in solo.Update: I played another run after they put out the first EA Hotfix, whose patch notes start with the following two bullet points:- Reduced threat on some battles that were doing outsized average damage, generally by removing ranged direct attackers.- Replaced many Inkling Jabbers with Inkling Slashers in early encounters. This will result in fewer encounters w here most or all of the enemies directly attack players immediately.I didn't feel either of these changes were actually effective at addressing the issues with many, many more casts of enemies in fights having unavoidable attacks. The difficulty feels exceptionally front-loaded in this game, and any stat other than damage feels exceptionally unimportant.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Game keeps getting better and better. Been playing solo-only so far. Different characters each feel unique, ability upgrades are varied and interesting,  The new vestige system is great too.  Trinkets add even more variety each run, though i think the trinkets could use some more work. Daily runs add a nice variety too.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game during the demo and absolutely loved it. I could not wait for it to comes out in EA and I want to start off by saying that this game is extremely fun co-op. I highly recommend it if you have friends to play it with. With that being said, there has been a change between the beta and EA that makes it pretty frustrating to play solo. Previously, you could almost always find a way to avoid taking damage in combat. Whether that be by moving out of the way of the hit or by finding a way to redirect the aggro, it was possible to take zero damage at the end of a round. Now, however, there is unavoidable damage in almost every combat. The damage taken really adds up and it's not immediately clear where the damage is even coming from most of the time. To try to balance out this change, there is now significantly higher max health and the ability to heal after each combat. However, if you choose to heal afterwards you typically miss out on stat buffs or items and end up being weaker, thus more likely to need a heal again after the next encounter. Also, your options to heal or shield during combat are incredibly limited for most classes. I could understand having bosses that deal this kind of damage, but mobs being able to as well? It's rough. With this change, combat now feels like more of a dps check than strategy based. While playing co-op it is very manageable (especially if someone plays support), but it seems like there is a far greater difficulty spike with trying to solo. This change kind of takes away from what made the game so great in the demo.  If you have friends to play with, definitely get this game. If you plan on playing solo, maybe wait until they roll back the unavoidable damage since it seems to be a big complaint right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game. If Hades, Risk of Rain 2, and Stolen Realm had a child this would be it. The gameplay loop unlocks more items and progresses the story by doing runs and talking to NPCs in the hub world and in different worlds during runs. The ranked mode offers scaling difficulty which gives enemies different buffs. For an early access game it already has a lot more to offer than some "fully released" games. The seasons are similar to games like Apex Legends and POE where they last roughly 3 months bringing a new character you can unlock. You start with 3 from the get go and can unlock two other classes by progressing through the quests. Ignore the people crying about a battlepass and currency, the game has to be funded somehow. These people have no issue offering AAA devs $60-$70 for the game and more for a battlepass/skins.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! 100+ hours into it and still having fun. There are many ways to build your characters to win -and I haven't tried everything yet. Turn based combat is fast and brutal. Story gives you a sense of direction with all kind of quests. There are many things to unlock. A small warning: at start the can be a bit overwhelming but don't let that stop trying and learn to play. FYI. I did all games solo, but you can also play co-op
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, with a caveat.Core gameplay is great. Nothing too innovative, roguelike turn based RPG with a movement system that's been done before but it's still a lot of fun. Multiplayer is a bit too easy right now, you spend most of your time just mitigating damage and one shotting enemies. Unavoidable damage is a non issue, every class gets access to shielding which will eventually ignore all damage.The cash shop :/ Questionable in an EA game but it's fully cosmetic only which is fine. If it means they will continue to add content that you don't have to pay for like bosses and characters it'll be great.Caveat is a lack of content combined with cash shop. Only 3 bosses and 5 characters at the moment, with meta progression limited to unlocking vestiges and the 2 unlockable characters. As long as they add a few bosses, characters, augments, etc. it will be worth the purchase but at the moment it's definitely on the edge. Overall not disappointed, yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun. The season pass / microtransactions are for cosmetics only. Not perfectly balanced right now but it's literally version 0.1 in early access; I'm happy with what I'm seeing. Right now, multiplayer is very strong, so solo play probably doesn't feel as good. This is definitely a game to play with your friends on Discord. There's not a lot of coordination required, but there's enough that you can step on each others' feet if you don't know what people are planning. Loved Monster Train, and I can tell this has the same solid bones.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun take on the rouge-like genre that very much rewards co-op gameplay. For the negative reviews about the MTX, there was a patch released today addressing the communities concerns. For difficulty, it really is a mixed bag and that is half of what makes this game fun. The game is steets ahead easier when playing solo, but you will still find difficulty in making sure you can survive direct attacks. I've only played with 2 others, and then co-op with either of them, so I can't speak to 4-party difficulty but 2 and 3-party difficult scales impressively well.Highly recommend to anyone looking to enjoy a rouge-like with friends.Rounds typically take 1-1 1/2 hours depending on how long your party mates take during turns.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Inkbound is a great Turn Based Tactics game, with interesting gameplay and meaningful choices. Characters are balanced around multiplayer, which can make some units feel lackluster in solo play.Updated Review: The season pass got removed and replaced by paid DLC. While still questionable in an unfinished early access game, this seems to be a healthier choice in the long run, given that while good the game isn't captivating enough to grind a season pass all day all week.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This developer earned my support. I would have never found this game if it wasn't for all the hype of them making their game without all the predatory pay mechanics that other companies do. And they are offering extra support for those who supported them early. A true win-win situation for all.  Plus, the game is very fun. I have purchased it for my kids to play with me.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: After really enjoying Monster Train, I decided to trust that the developer would deliver a great experience after watching the trailer. I found it a tad too expensive at the time, but as soon as it went on sale I decided to grab it. It's totally awesome. The gameplay is as addicting and engaging as Monster Train, but instead of using cards to summon monsters, you control your character in small arenas, fighting with a turn-based combat system. The progression, unlocks, and upgrade aren't too different from what you'd expect with a roguelike, so after reading the various traits/ bonuses/ etc, you can get the hang of it pretty easily. After playing it for a while, I can say I'd have bought it at full price. Great job, Shiny Shoe!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I know nothing about this game besides appearing on the Daily Deal. Bought it on a whim because I saw it was made by the same creator as Monster Train. Oh boy oh boy what an unbelievably amazing find!To sum it up, its ultimately the same core roguelite game loop; You go in, you fight, you create a diverse set of builds and styles, you finish or die and you repeat the process with some new knowledge or unlocks. On top of that it integrates a player hub + seamless solo or coop gameplay which is unbelievably great! I guess a majority of issues probably lie in balance for now.Also of note, removing the in-game monetization as a concious decision because they "Respect and trust the players" is such a huge gesture with technically no pay off. Mad respects to them and they definitely earned at least 1 loyal fan for that (Whatever that's worth!)
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game, can't wait to see what they make of it. I only played solo so far, but it is great.I hope they reign in/cap some of the bonuses though. +1 power on dodge is stupid when you can just stay in a fight forever and dodge until you have +1000 power and one-shot everything.They fixed it, still a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A welcomed addition into the rogue-like community. Great replay-ability, engaging story-line and interesting graphics. Only critique would be that I would like to see more worlds/stories added to the game to make later game play more varied. Also, would like to see a way to reward builds that don't use shields/spikes as it is very easy to get stuck into this cycle.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: as of right now everything is heavily unbalancedonly certain builds can get through the game which is certainly not the point of a roguelikebosses easily have 10~20k hp when your strongest skill does like 300~500 damage, this makes the fight take ages and boringoh yeah, microtransactions and season passrun for your lifesedit: newest patch removed the option to use gold for rerolls.... basically pointless to play nowedit 2:EARLY ACCESS RELEASE DATE: 22 May, 2023RELEASE DATE: 9 Apr, 2024still no new content after over a year
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful mix of Divinity style combat (co-op, turn based, tactical) with Hades' roguelike aspects (aspects/augments, room-by-room rewards) that scratches a wonderful gameplay itch. The gameplay is smooth, the background soundtrack is delightfully soothing, the animations are charming, and the variations of play within each class adds for a great deal of replayability. Playing co-op with friends is a much easier experience to jump into and feels less clunky overall than Baldur's Gate 3 or Divinity. So, for any party looking to skip the dialogue, looting of barrels, disjounted exploration, and get straight to the meat: this is an amazing experience.All from a dedicated developer who has really put their heart and soul into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid roguelite that's wears out its welcome. Despite forcing the playing to deal with a excessively long story (almost 80 hours for me), the game doesn't have to content necessary to keep the player interested unless they really enjoy the core loop. And you're not getting much more than that. The remnants of the original live service model that stain the progression and quest system are also distasteful. Gameplay wise, it's just as the trailer shows, a turn based roguelite with a lot of emphasis on positioning. There are plenty of skills and items to give it that RNG feeling, but it falls a bit short in several areas.1. Total lack of likable characters (at least for me). Which wouldn't be a problem if it wasn't for the fact that the story is both long and a centerpiece of the game. You *will* have to interact with these people to unlock stuff, and I didn't like it one bit.2. Very grindy quest structure designed to force the player into specific builds and routes multiple times to go hunt for items and npcs. e.g. kill a specific boss > get an item during a run and finish the run > talk to an NPC in the hub. This would require you to do three runs, but if you reversed the order, it could be done with one. There's a lot of this and it feels very intentional.3. While there are lots of items to play with, all the classes are designed with two playstyles in mind. As you continue the quest grind, you'll likely find yourself repeating the same class + build over and over again just to speed things up.4. On a similar thread, since there are only three major bosses + one "true" boss, I ended up farming one particular boss  (Hi Argolath!) over and over again just to finish quests. IIRC, aside from a few balance changes and a handful of items, very little has been added to the base game since release, which makes me wonder how the original live service model would have worked. While it's certainly better as a stand alone game, the quest bloat and lack of encounter variety weigh down an otherwise solid core gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: It's...Bizarre to say the least.I couldn't tell anything at all about the game from the Steam page.Combat is like Hellcards without the cards, just ability cooldowns and consumables.Movement is kind of like Stolen Realm/XCOM where you get a tiny, free amount of movement per action to align yourself properly, but if you wanna move more, it'll cost you more mana, so you can choose to trade an action to get the f*ck out of an AoE damage coming up.Exploration/Rewards are your standard Roguelike, like Hades. Pick a card of 3, pick a doorway you know about, pick a combat difficulty you think you can take on.There really isn't any exploration, it's just a tiny area filled with a couple of nodes to touch per area, maybe if you're lucky, a fishing spot which is essentially a free potion. Same sort of overworld as Stolen Realms.Everything thematically is a book/pen pun. All of it. It's exhausting. Builds look like they could be enjoyable and synergistic, especially with friends. I wouldn't know cause I got my a$$ beat in the 4th combat in a 1v20. Probably wouldn't recommend the game to play alone (Even though it advertises itself as an MMO).The "MMO" features consist of...A lobby you can see others in...Aaaand that's all I can tell. So if you think standing in a lobby instead of waiting in a menu constitutes an MMO tag, then by all means.Negative reviews are mad cause there is an optional cosmetic battlepass and cosmetic shop, all optional, all unnecessary. The option of being able to spend some money for some particle effects and skins doesn't justify the review bombing.I'm sure it's better with friends though, I'll have to try to convince a few to buy it.Will update review when I've played and understand more.But for now, it seems fun, but not really unique, just a few handpicked mechanics from the genre, wrapped in a storytelling bow.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, really. There's fun to be had with it, but the practices employed leave me unable to recommend it.To not be overly negative and offer fair information to allow for an informed decision; the game is a roguelite, and follows the usual fare. Select your class, select a trinket that offers a strong passive bonus for that run, get into the world. Pick where you go, usual from a selection of up to three; do you want to go shopping, face a random event, or get some money? If you have to fight; would you like to fight an easy, or a difficult group of enemies; and if the latter, which rewards would you like, upgrades for your skills or glyphs that allow you to reroll rewards?Rewards are, as is tradition of the genre, randomised. There's a variety of skills to choose from, and the trinket you start with can nudge you in a certain direction, but it's still RNG what you end up with; same with upgrades for said skills, and the items you find over the course of your run. Items offer immediate benefits, but also progress a set bonus, so it's important to decide what you will be focusing on. In theory, this keeps things fresh. Meta-progression between runs only comes in the form of unlocking new items, classes and trinkets; there are no flat, permanent stat boosts, you simply unlock a bigger toolbox. Winning a run also means unlocking a new difficulty setting, which usually comes with some new detriment for you or boost for your enemies. Players of Slay the Spire or Monster Train will find the idea behind it quite familiar. Atop of just regular wins, there is a storyline to follow that necessitates quests that range from "kill a boss under certain conditions", "use this item X times in a run" or "kill X enemies in Y area". The quests are alright; sometimes leaning heavily on RNG, but not usually egregiously so. In theory, again, this all checks out.In practice, things shake out to be slightly less than the sum of its parts. Combat is reliant on positioning insofar that you shouldn't stand in damaging circles, and tactical insofar that you know what an enemy will do the round after, as most cycle through predetermined attack routines; in most cases, an enemy that uses an avoidable AoE this round will attack you directly in the next, no matter where you stand. There are no environmental hazards to use to your advantage, enemies can't friendly fire each other, and enemies that will attack directly will always run up to you both at the start of their turn and when they attack, so you can't outmaneuver them, leaving positioning to feel a bit hollow, and most decisionmaking to be "Which enemy do you kill now so it doesn't become a problem later", as there are no fun shenanigans to pull off with your positioning; you move out of AoEs and out of damaging puddles. That's mostly it.As for unlocking items, the problem is the same as with many roguelites that rely on unlocking new items; bloat. Most items you unlock are simply useless for your current build, and some are outclassed in what they do rather significantly even in their own rarity. Certain items are so broken they make your run a cakewalk; other runs are meandering and feel pretty slow and bothersome as the game doesn't fork over the items you need. Usually there would be a system to weigh the RNG pool in your favor somehow, by disabling relics you don't want or something along those lines, but Inkbound puts no such thing in place.It's all not  living up to its potential, but that wouldn't be a reason for me to leave a negative review.The negative review comes because of the random difficulty spike the devs decided to introduce. The game used to be pretty relaxing to play a few patches ago. And while I can understand roguelites are, by design, a genre predicated on failure being a very real looming threat, the way this was introduced was in my opinion rather lackluster.Firstly, it wasn't that difficulty settings were made more- well, difficult; it was a base increase of all enemy stats across the board starting from difficulty 0. Combine a bloated HP and upcrept damage pool with enemies that can attack you directly no matter what you do, and you may see a problem; you either get lucky with itemising and play smart to kill enemies quick, or you get whittled down and die. It is the laziest form of difficulty, not forcing the player to engage with any unique mechanics or forcing them to learn to use their environment to their advantage because there's nothing to use to your advantage aside from item and skill synergies.The game now necessitates careful planning ahead on top of getting lucky with items just to deal with the increased enemy damage and HP. It's not impossible, of course, and not brainless RNG, you still need to think; but it's a level of planning that is just not what I signed up for, and it's IMO the laziest way to make a game difficult. "Our players are succeeding too often. Should we add more difficulty ranks? No, let's just increase enemy stats on all difficulties, that's always a great kind of challenge. After all, there are item combinations that technically allow the player to snap the game over their knee, so it's balanced!"Upping the difficulty in this way simply invalidates too many playstyles and kills my drive to experiment; after all, if I've found a winning combination of items, why would I not go for those and instead try something new and funky, only to get whittled down over long and increasingly dull fights for not meeting the arbitrary DPS check the devs turned every fight into?I am aware I'm more of a casual player, but the thing that bothers me is that I didn't sign up for this. Had the game been in this state when I bought it, I would have simply refunded it, no harm no foul; now, however, refunding is no longer an option, and the game has been made just difficult enough that I just don't enjoy it as much anymore, which I think is just a slap in the face for trying to support the game prior to this. I am of course aware that games like StS and MonTrain have their appeal and their fans;but not only do these games feel deeper and more fleshed out, they also allow modding, which Inkbound traded in to instead plonk you into a lobby with other players, so you can engage in jolly cooperation, where the number bloat will be more apparent than ever.I'm fully willing to update this review of a balance patch is dropped, but right now, the devs have opted to instead go the route of dropping a newspost that explains "Well, balancing is difficult!" and the latest update increased some bosses' HP pools because they were not difficult enough.tl;dr:The game's fine, it just isn't as relaxing as I hoped it'd be (and as it was) when I bought it, and the main reason this review is negative is because I feel it's a horrendous practice to up the difficulty so steeply and without warning just because the chart says players are winning too often.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is super fun. if you liked monster train, if you liked slay the spire , and other rogue-style then you will love it. it took a few runs to get the hang of the mechanics but each class is fun, each power-up is neat and fun to learn how to use right; Can't wait to see more classes, maps, power-ups and trinkets but even as is it now , it was well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game that has taken a new spin to combatOne commendable aspect is the combat system, which manages to feel fresh and innovative in a genre where many games fall into predictable patterns. Inkbound stands out by delivering a combat experience that feels new and exciting, achieving something most games in the genre strive for but often fail to achieve. The developers have shown responsiveness by listening to the community, implementing changes, and even tweaking core mechanics to better align with player expectations. This dedication to refining the combat elevates Inkbound above its competitors.Gameplay Lack of BalanceHowever, the fast-paced nature of the gameplay reveals itself as a haphazard design choice that undermines any hope for a nuanced and balanced experience. Certain essential skills, like poison & bleed, become less a strategic choice and more a mandatory crutch, exposing a glaring flaw in the overall game design.Missing Bosses and Muddled Class SystemA significant letdown is the absence of challenging bosses, leaving players without the climactic encounters that could have injected excitement into the gameplay. Furthermore, the classes, while present, lack clear and informative explanations, leaving players fumbling in the dark with poorly defined roles.Lackluster Progression and Achievement SystemPost-run accomplishments are woefully underwhelming, contributing to a pervasive sense of futility. The absence of meaningful unlocks, stat increases, or skill point upgrades upon re-entry into the game renders the progression system lackluster at best, discouraging any sustained investment of time and effort.Unrealized Potential and Consistent ShortcomingsInkbound teases greatness but consistently disappoints with each update. The core elements necessary for an exceptional gaming experience are present but are repeatedly mishandled, leaving players with a lingering dissatisfaction and unmet expectations.Overall the game is fun, the developers ARE trying to make it a truly shinning game that has a fun combat system you wont see else were, would i say its worth the money? maybe? I found it fun, but waiting for more updates for it to fell more complete and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well made and very fun, especially considering it's early access. Pros:-Tons of items by default and that can be unlocked with lots of hidden synergies so runs rarely play out exactly the same-Builds are surprisingly diverse if you experiment. Don't get stuck on just 1 option every run thinking it's the best, everything is viable-Combat is fun and simple, but offers lots of room for skill expression, especially with more position dependent characters-Art style and voice acting are very nice-Ranked mode adds several unique effects that encourage planning and taking abilities/items you previously wrote off-Battlepass and Ingame Shop are purely cosmetic. Free version of pass+early access code give you exactly enough currency to buy the full Battlepass and in turn rewards enough currency to buy the next Battlepass+have a good chunk leftover so it's essentially free so long as you finish them.Cons(all very minimal):-Runs are short-ish and always the same length. For typical solo unranked games, about 45 minutes is a good ballpark. It's understandable why, since items are the main way of scaling lategame and once you have all of your slots filled that's all you need. But a gauntlet or endless style mode would be cool, albeit require some fine tuning to make viable.-Not fully voice acted, but it's in their roadmap-Multiplayer could use some tweaks to make it easier to tell what your allies are planning. Playing without voicechat is difficult

_childDocuments_.review: First off; there's a lot of downvotes due to the shop/season pass, but bear in mind that this is purely cosmetical. You do *not* need to spend extra money to get up to speed.Inkbound can be compared to a variety of games, but to me it feels most like a turn-based, tactical Hades, which by itself is worth looking into. The combat is short, tense, and really enjoyable. It does a great job of displaying how much you can move around with X amount of resources. Life is precious as free heals are rare and small, thus you must often contemplate whether you should spend your resources to line up and execute your attacks efficiently, or trade some damage to move less or out of danger yourself. Often it is tempting/necessary to pick up heals instead of a buff from combat rewards, which further extends the value of playing cautiously. Furthermore, there is already decent variety in paths to take, quests to start out with, and builds to go for to entice further runs.The game falls short on introducing mechanics, status effects, and stats, and there is a lot going on. Your first runs will be very confusing as you have no idea which skills to pick up or paths to progress on as you have no clue on how to weight the decisions. I get this is part of the roguelite experience, but to me the lack of proper explanations made it more frustrating than similar games. This is also reflected in the story; while Monster Train could get away with a simple intro to its theme and concept, this game is an RPG which should provide some proper atmosphere. And currently the dialogue is dull and unengaging. However, I think some simple animations and transitions would improve this a lot, and this is surely something which will be improved down the line. All in all the game needs a lot of polish, but it is early, early access and should be treated as such. Because of this I wouldn't recommend it to everyone at this point, but if you're really into this genre and tolerate some rough edges, this game provides an interesting spin to the usual card-based roguelites.Done right I believe the end product has the potential to become another masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic. It's an interesting rouge-like that has a lot of things going for it. The "classes" (Aspects) are fantastic and each one is unique and enjoyable with a few different ways to build them. The gameplay is fun and interesting with lots to think about each turn of combat but not too much that it's overwhelming. The art style and themeing of the game is fantastic. The VA work is also VERY good. Lots of voice acted lines that are done very well. The progression systems are also fantastic with lots of different quests and tasks that unlock either cosmetic items or "passives" (vestiges) to find in runs. The trinket system is also very well done with the trinkets both making it easier to find certain builds and also increasing the damage that build will do. The micro-transaction, while controversial, is very well done here. I'm a little disappointed they are removing it as unlocking things from the battlepass was one of my motivations to play it as much as I have. It was one of the best done battlepass and cosmetic stores i've seen. I understand that the battlepass i'm looking at now is most likely quite different from where it was a short time ago, but what is here currently is a very enjoyable pass that will eventually reward you with slightly more than enough currency to purchase a premium battle pass. They also keep battlepasses permanently and you can swap between them. They are going away and will be replaced with a non-monetization cosmetic shop that you earn currency from "seasonal" missions. I hope they add a lot more seasonal missions and content in order to keep me coming back. Currently my friend and I who are playing the game together feel like, without the battlepass, we will likely soon finish most of the content in the game and only return for a week or so each update before leaving. It's on the devs to make sure this isn't the case and they've done a great job so far so I'm optimistic about this game and it's future. Would recommend, still playing, enjoying it very much.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely and thoughtful game which provides a decent amount of variety in solo runs, and even more when playing with a group. _childDocuments_.review: This game used to be 10 times better.As a veteran player of the highest rank I can not recommend the game in its current state, sadly. Developers seem hellbent on ignoring every bit of community feedback, deadset on their specific vision for the game, which not only clashes with player expectation but also with the game's previous identity.In the past runs were fast, fun and enemy targeting was varied, meaning you had to think about your positioning and actions.Now, everything is a bulletsponnge, with some enemies having, I kid you not, upwards of 3x the amount of hp they used to have (this is outdated information. It used to be that an 8k hp boss turned into a 30k hp boss in an update. Now we have a 250k+250k boss. This is the most severe case of number bloat I've ever seen in a game), which turns runs into a slog. Targeting mechanics are cut, meaning you not only move through the run slower, you also have 0 reason to think about positioning. This effectively turns the game into a tedious dps race between the player and the enemy.Add to that the fact that only about 15-20% of abilities/stats/items/or mechanics are viable with the rest being purposefully weaker - your game boils down to: can I get lucky enough to get broken abilities or items? No? Dead run. Yes? Ok, time to turn off my brain and power through the run with 0 issue.It never was this bad.Also yeah, paid battlepass on a $20 game unreleased game with massive changes like this? Not a fan, to be honest.I'd recommend giving it half a year and see how the game is doing then.

_childDocuments_.review: Breaks my heart to leave a negative. The game has a lot going for it: interesting classes, enemies, relics, skill augments etc. However, the game is too easy - especially for a roguelite that is. I haven't lost a single run yet. I run daily challenges with no idea about the class I run, I misread the modifiers and I still win and finish Top 50/Top 100. This isn't a roguelite to me, maybe a rogueLITE.Let me be clear, that is my biggest problem with the game - crafting a great build just isn't fun if the challenge to overcome isn't meaningful enough. Normally in roguelites you die horribly until you git gud. Took me 25+ runs in Hades to first escape. I loved it. Here I haven't lost yet in 10 or so runs and the only times I've been close to were my very first run and when I misread a modifier realizing it dealt dmg per 100 currency to me each turn and I was running around with 800 currency in a boss fight. I should have never survived this, but I did.I looked it up and other people have the same problem. Supposedly when you level up your rank runs get harder but I don't wanna keep playing a game that's unfun until it eventually becomes fun. As best as I know/see there's no difficulty modifiers available off the bat which makes it non fun to me. I didn't touch this in very long and just wanted to see if I was being too harsh on the game, so I ran the daily challenge today on a class I didn't know with modifiers I misread and finished Top 50 - the fights being no challenge whatsoever.If they make it harder or the difficulty more adjustable I'm happy to come back. I know this is EA and balancing is part of EA, however I was disheartened to not see this addressed on the recently published Roadmap to 1.0.And other than that I really like the game. I mean, one more negative thing: I know it's supposed to give you story book vibes, but the graphics and color palette look childish and made for kids - which would explain the difficulty, in which case, I may just not be the target audience.As for the good parts, I must say the turn based combat system is very fun - enemies telegraph their intentions (think Slay the spire) and you can move around freely and go back without committing the action to see live how moving to a spot would impact the damage you take. That is an extremely well done UI that helps you optimize.The classes and enemies are meaningfully different and interesting to play around with. They look kinda odd, but have fun concepts - the weaver for instance is all about attaching and detaching threads. It's pretty cool to play.Your skills can get smaller augments that give them bonuses (different rarities of upgrades) but also full blown upgrades that might change how the skill works. That is one part of the build, the other is relics ("vestiges") that give cool maybe build altering bonuses. They're also part of sets which can net you even more bonuses.Overall, putting a build together is very fun.I also must say, some other things that they plan (controller support, steamdeck support) are absolutely great choices for this game - perfect steam deck game once that's in imo. Also their choice to cut out the microtransactions was great and made me check out the game (despite the childish looks that had kept me away so far).All in all, it's a good, fun and well designed game with lots of potential to grow - it's just way too easy in my opinion esp. when advertised as a roguelite (or even, erroneously "roguelike"). I hope they tune it or make difficulty modifiers more readily accessible, then I might be able to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: inkbound is an extremely fun coop turn based roguelike. at the moment there are three base classes with two able to be unlocked, a bunch of quests to unlock further items into the pool and three end bosses. there's a good bit of build variety and the difficulty curve isn't too bad once you get some runs under your belt. most runs are under an hour long. it does have a battlepass which is purely cosmetic so that might be a turn off. the plus side is that it can be purchased for free at the time of writing this. the code EARLYACCESSTHANKS gives you 300 shinies (the games premium currency) and you can unlock another 300 shinies on the free side of the pass since you need 600 to purchase it.highly recommend unless you hate early access games.

_childDocuments_.review: Inkbound is a very ambitious game created with a huge amount of love for the genre.  There are multiple classes and a large amount of variety in your build and the game mechanics.  There is a HUGE amount to learn when playing this game.   For context, I play a ton of these roguelike dungeon crawlers and have 60 hours in Inkbound and play it at max difficulty, single player.   The magic items are fun and interesting to use.  You can carry up to six of these at a time, and each of these items gives bonuses on their own AND gives bonuses to the 'sets' they belong to.  You can also sacrifice a magic item to give a permanent boost to the 'sets' they belong to as well as freeing up another slot.  This mechanic is very fun to play with and forces you make some tough decisions on what to keep, what to sacrifice, and what set bonuses to go for.  Very cool!The selection of what 'curse' to take when you pick your route, the various upgrades to your abilities, and the choices you make during the run are great.  I loved the custom upgrades on cards in 'Monster Train,' and I love the custom upgrades on your abilities here.  Just a fantastic mechanic that I enjoy every time.  The combat itself is turn based and each enemy has their own abilities that must be worked around.  Turns can get very complex because both yourself and your foes will have area of attack and direct skills that must be negotiated.  The problem with the 'positional combat' gimmick is that it can take a long time to calculate the optimal play.  As a result, the pace of the game suffers, especially at very high difficulties.My main issue with the game is that there is information overload.  There are so many status effects to juggle and enemies on the screen that it's difficult to figure out exactly what is the highest threat.  I have found myself multiple times affected by something bad with no idea how it happened.  For example, I'll have an apparently permanent debuff of -13 or so max HP and no idea where it came from.  The UI is not great. It's hard to tell how much damage you're taking, what buffs/debuffs are going to happen to you, and what enemy is doing what action and causing what negative effect.  The information overload applies to the quest system too.  There's so much to read that I end up just ignoring all of it.  I'm rather uncertain what exactly I'm 'supposed' to be doing and just hitting the 'new run' button.  I wish I had an 'unlock all' button.  I just want to do an endless amount of runs on max difficulty and play with all the toys!Overall, the game is very good.  I give it a solid 'B' and am happy to recommend it to people who enjoy this type of game.  It doesn't reach the stellar heights of 'Monster Train' because of pacing issues and information overload, but every time I boot this up, I end up having a great time.I wonder what cool artifacts I'm going to play with next?!

_childDocuments_.review: This is coming from a Rank 19:Unfortunately has a lot of potential but is a victim of devs not playing their own game. A lot of bad game design choices that are easily fixable, such as permanent big blight pools, unavoidable high damage from tanky targets, absolutely being forced to build sustain, but only have a very few sources of it, blight ring closing in too fast too early in some encounters etc.) There are also some ridiculous encounters that make you lose your run no matter how optimized your build is and how lucky you were with your finds, such as 1730 HP suicide bombers that don't actually die after they bomb you.

_childDocuments_.review: In general I have very much enjoyed this game, it's a lot of fun solo and co-op.The art work is charming and ticks all the right boxes for me.Game play is great in terms of combat, I love the mix of tactics in with roguelite and the blend has been done very well.I would (and have) recommended this game to quite a few people.However, I do have concerns like so many others about the AI and unavoidable damage.I have not played the demo so have no experience of anything beyond what is in the game at the current moment. The issue of enemy units having a mix of aoe zones to dodge, unavoidable attacks (single target) and map wide aoe attacks is simple.The game quickly becomes about how much damage the player can deal as an alpha strike to reduce the damage they are going to take in retaliation. This means as the player you have to have been lucky enough to get good options for your damage in addition to playing a character which is suited to the role. With the nature of RNG that isn't within the players control which makes it feel unsatisfying at times.Other minor issues are simple balance, some characters and their augments are quite underwhelming. In addition some status effects are just weak (looking at you Frostbite). I am almost sure most of this will be balanced and tweaked by release and even in it's current state I'd still recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a roguelite.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to revise this review, as I decided to keep playing.The core concept is great and the game plays quite well, but there are some bad decisions:- Day 1 Early Access Cash Shop- Day 1 Early Access Season Pass- Always OnlineUpdated Impressions after a lot more play time:After more play time and becoming more familiar with the mechanics (and a balance patch to the Weaver), I honestly enjoy this a lot. You'll lose runs if the game gives you bad skills or bad vestiges for your build but that's just roguelike/lite life.Winning runs isn't terribly difficult at this stage, and neither is unlocking either of the two locked classes. I do like the combination of turn based gameplay with non-grid-based movement based on action points that are also used for your skills. Gives you a lot of time to prioritize and plan which enemies to pick off each turn. My old review mentioned the Weaver being weak. It's now a powerhouse post-balance patches once you get some ability/magic damage bonuses rolling. They're not just releasing this to EA and sitting back, which is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: A classic case of I-wish-there-were-a-mixed-option.The game is unfortunately pretty middling I think. The mechanics and combat systems are pretty solid, but unfortunately there's little variation in terms of builds so the runs will feel very similar very quickly.Each class has 3 locked abilities and 2 variable abilities, thing is that the variable abilities are all on a CD and shared between the classes. The fireball is the same across all the classes and the pool of available abilities is frankly a little disappointing.What really made Monster Train (the developers previous game) truly great, was the build variety and the possibility of utterly breaking the game through insane combinations. Inkbound seems to lack both, little variety in builds and the power level seems to be capped at a reasonable level, which makes trying out new things somewhat boring, you're not going to discover anything wildly different or truly powerful as you keep playing. (Well, I didn't in the 14h I played).It truly is a shame that the game fall short of expectation, because Monster Train was something truly brilliant. The game is fine, not good, not bad, but I don't think I can recommend the game at full price I'm sad to say. If you're looking at this game and haven't tried their previous title of Monster Train, spend your money on that instead.

_childDocuments_.review: There just isn't enough to do here for me personally. Once you've unlocked all the classes, that's basically it; the main thing you continue to repeatedly unlock are vestiges, items you can find in your runs that boost your stats & give different bonus effects when completing sets, but there are SO MANY of these and an overwhelming majority of them feel beyond useless to me. There are only a handful of stages and each stage has exactly one boss, so you always know what you're gonna be up against, which means repetition set in early for me. The quest structure is mind-bogglingly bad; quests are often needlessly convoluted (i.e., "go to this stage with this class and use this ability/emote/item"), vague, (i.e., "Progress further in the story to unlock," with zero indication as to which point in the story the quest unlocks, meaning it could be potentially dozens of hours if you don't do the right story missions or talk to the right NPCs), or both (i.e., "go to this stage with this item," but the item is one you haven't unlocked and have no clue where to get it). The last class you can unlock is where you really see the problems with the quest structure, it is a complete slog to obtain and heavily dependent on RNG as it requires you to visit several different locations while using different classes and items. After unlocking all the classes, I honestly just didn't even want to bother with the quests anymore because the dialogue is not great, the story is obtuse, and 99.999% of the quests just unlock more damn vestiges. The graphical style is not great to me, but I realize this is personal preference. There's a lot of cosmetics to unlock, but it takes a while to grind the currency you need to purchase them and most of them are just so visually unappealing to me that I didn't feel any pull to try and collect them all. The game play is hit and miss for me. I like the overall turn-based, resource-focused combat, but I absolutely hate how limited movement is, which, combined with the Fortnite-esque ever shrinking circle of doom, makes the majority of combat encounters feel like they're more about positioning and DPS checks than any kind of real strategy. Balance swings wildly depending on the class you're playing and how many people are in your party. Playing solo feels like a complete joke most of the time, while playing with even just one other person can often be very frustrating due to how much enemies' health and damage scale in multiplayer. Runs are also heavily dependent on which vestiges and bonuses you get within the first few areas of a stage, to the point where my friends and I would often just immediately abandon a run if we didn't get good drops in the first stage, since there is zero penalty for abandoning a run. While I do have a lot of negatives here, this is another game where I wish we had a "Mixed" review option because, despite all of my complaints, I did have some fun with it for the first several hours. I want to reiterate that, excluding my gripes with the positioning, combat is pretty fun for a while and it was fun to unlock new classes up until the final one, which is just such an unnecessary pain in the ass to get. I'd say this is a decent enough game to get while I on sale, but between the limited amount of content (unless mindlessly grinding to unlock an ever-increasing array of useless items that mostly boil down to stat sticks sounds like your cup of tea), the confusing, vague, and meandering story that doesn't really go anywhere, and the absolute insanity that is the game's quest structure, I just can't recommend spending $30 on this. TL;DR - Get it on sale. Some fun to be had, but too much RNG in the quest structures, confusing and boring story, and not enough content IMO to be worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 4: This review tells quite a story huh? They have now removed all forms of in-game monetisation. No in-game store where you can purchase things for real currencies, no battlepasses, no fomo. There is now a currency, dust, which is used to purchase cosmetics, and this can only be earned from in-game progression. No 5 quid for just a lil extra dust to get that next item. You also earn cosmetics by just playing enough in a season or by completing enough challenges on the victory board, but even if you miss out on them, you can either buy missed cosmetics for dust later, or buy the DLCs. And I like this, even if you own the cosmetics you can still buy the DLC if you wish to support the game. This is a much more ethical way of monetising their game, and I'm really happy to see this.Also, the newest patch adds two new classes and revamps a lot of systems in general. Been having tons of fun with it now. Though I would - while being a hypocrite - advice to hold off on buying early access games, I would definitely put this on the radar for the full release if they keep up these good changes going forward.EDIT 3: They are changing the monetisation with today's patch at the time of writing. They will sell shinies (the virtual currency) in the smallest increment to help avoid overpurchasing larger bundles, they will make it so that the battle pass don't expire, and the rotating store front will go away. My only pain point left is what their strategy is for offline play, but I'm willing to hesitantly recommend the game now, as it at least seems that they are willing to make positive changes based on feedback from the community.EDIT 2: Despite some pushback from some people on their servers, the devs seem to have listened to some of our feedback. So far they have promised to remove the rotational store, to add 50 shinies bundles and to remove the possibility to buy battle pass levels. I'm still not sure if I can recommend it, but it's a very promising start if they go through with it!EDIT: I brought the topic of monetisation up in the official discord, and the topic got locked due to bad faith actors derailing the topic. It's clear that the game is not going to change the monetisation system, and I can't do anything but recommend everyone to stay away from the game and company until they change that up.It's a shame, as Monster Train is one of my favourite games. I can't in good faith recommend this, and I hope I'm able to get a refund one day.I actually find the gameplay very fun and complelling so far from my experience. They changed things up so that not everything is avoidable, but I've been able to get by with tankier builds instead of pure damage like in the playtests.However the monetisation is disgusting. Not only do you pay for the game, but also there's a battle pass and a rotating storefront. Three different systems, and the latter two are unethical. Until they change it I don't recommend buying it and wish I had realised before I played too much

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like after just 4 hours I've seen everything the game has to offer. There are not a lot of systems, not much depth to any of it. Despite having plenty of powers that grow over the course of a run, a single run is only 3 bosses long. (there might be an endless mode later, but neither the UI nor the game philosphy supports that, and I am not willing to play longer to find out). It feels like the devs are very scared to let the players run with fun and interesting powers, in favor of boring and simple ones that let them keep control over balance. It's a PvE roguelite, let me go wild with powers and interactions. The classes all feel obtuse and complex for no reason, at least at surface level. In the actual gameplay they are all "smash key one a few times, press the other off cooldown." There's little depth. The ranger class, which I liked most designwise, felt so incredibly weak. The class mechanic gave me a tiny bit more damage. Meanwhile the hammer wielding base class gets shield, percentage bonus damage, a nuke, good AOE and mobility basically for free in its kit. It's too perfect of an all rounder to ever consider playing other classes. It also bothers me that there are encounters where damage is unavoidable. if 5 enemies spawn that all attack  you at the same time with their single target attack, it becomes a gample of how many you can take out. In essence a DPS check, or a shield check if you can get enough shielding. It doesn't promote skill, or promotes mostly luck. I've had runs end where I play to the best of my ability but still lost. In fact, almost all loses felt like I could not have played them better, and are extremly frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great concept but really just disappoints.  It feels like a game that could be amazing but it falls short of that and needs some updates and work from devs to be a proper great game.  In it's current state, its fine.  Game starts off great, being challenging yet fair.  But as you progress and difficulty increases, that's where damage scaling and enemy bonus abilities get out of hand.  Enemies gain absurd stats and your stats get downsized, what you can actually do falls off a cliff.  It makes you feel like that strong hero you had a few levels ago is now just a useless baby.  After really, rank 7, if you aren't high rolling the OP abilities and items, you will lose.  So all the choices that exist, which is a decent amount, feel empty, since you HAVE to do the strong ones to win.  Poor balance and poor game design choices there makes the fun fade very quickly. Advice for devs:Get rid of the stupid difficulty settings, you don't know how to balance that properly with your multiple characters and abilities can actually do. Simplify or explain the over-convoluted stat system and damage calculations.  Nearly impossible to understand what magic damage does, vs omni, vs pure thorns damage for example. Work on getting all abilities and items to be winnable at all levels of difficulties, instead of just telling players to "pick better things" and "get good". The bad design and math you've put into the game is holding it back from being great.Multiplayer difficulty increase doesn't make sense.  Game should be as hard as single as with multi, not harder, but you seem to assume every player is pure god mode in decision making while playing with a mute teammate.  It just doesn't work with random parties.  Literally, you should start by making the single and multi-person the same monster strengths but 1 extra monster per room per extra player.  Bosses can get a % increase of about 33% health per player.   As it stands, I have no incentive to play multi, just to team with a mute idiot and a broken run from the start.
