_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. Tons of fun and I am always looking for a rogue like I can play with friends so multiplayer is a huge upside for me. Solo runs appear to be far easier than co-op from my limited (12 hours currently) playtime but they are so rewarding and very fun. Of the four starting classes I have played three and enjoyed each of them immensely. Of the 4 unlockable classes I have played two, and unlocked an additional one. My only gripe so far is that some of the story quests to get through the story and unlock the ability to play as the 4th unlockable character are just a bit too specific or random for me to really get them without paying attention. Of my 12 hours of playtime roughly 11 of it has been co-op and none of us had progressed the main story past a certain point because the quest (which didn't show in the quest tracker) was to go to a specific zone as a specific class and hit a single ability 7 times in one combat. So far that's my only complaint. 9/10 would recommend this to anyone that likes roguelikes and especially if they have a squad of 1-3 others to play with.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I was given Inkbound as a present from my partner. It's become probably one of my favourite games and my main complaint is arguably a positive one which is that I can't wait for more bosses, paths and content to get added. It's a challenging game that isn't easy to complete until you start to understand each character and how to build them up to fight what's ahead. I like games that involve some planning, puzzle solving and strategy and this incorporates all of that into one with a turn based combat system that still feels fluid and impactful. I've played this game alone (arguably easier alone) and with three friends. (Enemies seem much harder in coop and you have to utilise the fact you can trade drops with your friends so you can quickly optimise builds for your characters.) Highly recommend, I've still not completed this game and even though I've done the three 'boss fights' doing a new run doesn't feel too repetitive since you can change your build and path each time.  I really hope there's a lot more in store for this game! If a bunch more content come's out I'll probably showcase it on my stream.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacular game.  THE best combination of elements from SRPGs, MOBAs, and Rogue-lites.  The way the ability and character hitboxs interact, along with the movement make for a unique, accessible, and deep combat system, where full knowledge of status effects and their interactions as well as a firm grasp on spatial awareness are at the forefront.  I've played a lot of SRPGs, and for me this is up near Final Fantasy Tactics, Gladius, and Vandal Hearts as far as quality of gameplay.  Plus the art and sound direction are wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This is Risk of Rain meets Ember Knights in a turn-based party-oriented rogue-like. Linear as it is, the fun is fantastic!I'd been complaining about everything being poison damage for the last couple runs but then the Chainbreaker decide to monk-slap the boss into oblivion. Again, with poison. By inflicting thirty thousand stacks of poison and dealing 7.199 million damage while they were nearly dead.Oh, and forget the fact I had 43 Will (actions) to perform on that turn alone.Please, devs, don't change this! It's amazing fun and you get fantastic pay off for building well. I'm looking forward to the future of this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Just won my first co-op duo run. Playing together with someone and really planning both the builds and every move during a run makes for a very tactical and engaging experience. Solo might also be good, but haven't tried. Can't imagine it being particularly good with randoms, especially without mic.Only things I don't particularly like is the story (however you can skip through conversations) and the quests (there's a ton of them and they're not really engaging or fun, but you have to do them to get additional classes and stuff).Would recommend for great sort-of-deckbuilding and strategic gameplay, especially when playing premade co-op.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: You can easily win run after run and then lose a perfect run ONLY because you lost all movement points by mistake and then you find yourself inside some AoE ♥♥♥♥♥ just by one single f*ckin pixel. What a m*ronic design. Also game is cluttered with bazillion useless dialogues and quests you can't care less in a f*ckin roguelike.In addiction enemies variety is basically zero, and choices of the path is gated behind a useless cryptic book system for no reason at all, so you'll never have an idea what is coming next unless you read all the wiki and experience hours of useless frustration. Not my cup of tea, thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: this game has a really strong core and a lovely engine that complements the gameplay mechanics really well. Mechanically, this game is clean AF. Content is admittedly on the lighter side right now, but there is a complete game here all the same. It just starts to feel stale after fighting the same enemies and bosses over and over again. We need more types of room challenges to stop things from just blurring together. Hades does this too, but gets away with it by making each room have varied arenas that present reflexive challenges (such as avoiding damage zones). The blight blobs that appear in battles are essentially nothing and have never once killed me, and I believe I've only ever taken damage from it by being careless and clicking too fast.Again, I do recommend, the core is really solid and it has good promise. If this wasn't an EA game, though, that core alone wouldn't be enough to carry this to a recommend for me. Content should come in, but if it doesn't bear the above in mind.

I have never heard of a company doing this before, its amazing. _childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: In short, fun and repayable (Given you take some breaks).At the time of writing this I find the gameplay fun. Although there isn't that much content apart from running the same 6 or so "stories" again and again, the quests and different classes make up for that repetitiveness. Finding and unlocking all the class augments and ascensions is a great motivator for me to keep playing. However, the classes have the same gameplay loop of using your abilities in a specific order every time.When I had first seen the  I  didn't want to continue playing. But the Inkbound developers have made the battlepass similar to Fortnite's. That means if you purchase it once, grind out the pass, you'll be able tog et the next one for free. And by the looks of it, free-to-play players can even get the bp for free after 2 bp releases.The overall art style and feel of the game is also something I quite like. There's a good chunk of unique characters with voice acting as well that help with connecting you to the world and the characters in it. The story itself isn't that deep, but it is entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a fresh and exciting new gameplay experience! The classes are unique and fun to play. I love switching between different ones and experimenting. I'm not usually into tactical RPGs, but I'd definitely pick this one over any other. So far, it doesn't seem like a sterile grindfest, but rather a dynamic immersive world I can cozy up with by myself or with some friends. The music, art, and voice acting is top-tier! You won't find quality like this in any recent AAA game, that's for sure. This developer really does care about you as a player, not a mindless consumer.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game demo last winter and had a blast. Such an amazing rogulike with several distinct characters. tons of potential builds, and also great visuals and even a story (which I think in roguelites only Hades done right, but it's better to have something).But I didn't get the game initially when it was launched in EA since it had payed battlepasses and cosmetics, which seemed too greedy for an indie b2p game. Now that the developers listened to the community and made all content free (unlockable via in-game activities), it's definitely a must play for every rogulite fan.Even now, in early access, it has 8 character classes, several regions, tons of quests, and hundreds of different items and other unlockables to use in your runs. I usually get tired of rogulites in 20-30 hours (the only exceptions were Binding of Isaac, Slay the Spire and Hades, I think). But here in 10 hours I only played 3 classes out of 8, and even with those three I barely scratched the surface of their potential builds, it seems.The only downside is that there's still no proper offline mode, so you have to log in and play on the server even solo. But this offline mode is already in beta, and should be implemented before the 1.0 launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game overall I've enjoyed the gameplay a lot. but I like games of this style. It's almost a deck building game. You take the skills you have on whatever character class you're going to use and then you defeat enemies and manage your resources to buff your skills in a certain way to try to reach the end of a run. If you have some friends that play games regularly with you, it feels like it was balanced more around multiplayer. I haven't been able to find groups much and have done ok on my own. There are some strategies that perform way better than others so you'll have to experiment with whatever class you have and try to synergize your build.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: A new spin on the roguelike genre, this turn based combat focused game has lots of depth and replayability. The core mechanics are fun and you continue to unlock new vestiges for quite some time. Still in Early Access, the hope is that they continue to add more characters, realms and challenges. The ranked dives up the ante even more with increasing difficulty and restrictions forcing you to choose how to continue. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game 3 days ago and haven't stopped playing it yet. Unlike a lot of roguelites that give you a ton of trash rolls, most rolls you will get in this game can be used (obviously some will be better than others but I never got rolls and thought "well this is trash better restart!). Even the basic relics are really helpful as well especially if you can stack them.To sum up how you will be playing this game, you will pick a class and one of the three bosses in the game that you would like to fight for your run. There is just the regular run (good for getting quests done) and the challenge run which adds negative modifiers into the game the higher you go. The class you pick determines your ability set (3 of them per class) and each class actually plays differently from one another.I found it odd to read reviews stating that the game is boring and there is no variety. Well I just have to disagree. The classes have multiple play styles (you can even get augs that can make your DPS's into tanks), the game actually gets rather challenging the deeper you go into the challenge tiers and as you complete quests you get more relics to find as you progress (this is the real kicker, if you don't play the game you don't unlock relics that can and will change up your gameplay). While there aren't any stats that carry over, you do get to pick your starter aug that helps your playstyle whether you want to tank, do thorns damage, poison, a mixture of DoTs if you have a playstyle there is probably a starter aug for it.I would also like to say that on release (and the reason why I did not purchase this game) is because it had A LOT of paid content inside of the game from battlepasses to cosmetics. All of that has been removed, the battlepass is free you just need to play to progress it, and you'll be given currency to buy previous battle pass items (no more of that "I gotta play now or I miss out"! mentality). This is how in-game content SHOULD be offered to the player who already purchased your product, just like how it was in older games ie. you play to unlock content and cosmetics. This isn't a free to play game so it should not have that free to play transaction garbage in it. Thank you for actually listening to the community.If you like turn based strategy games that give you a good variety to keep you busy this game is a must buy. The sound design is good, the graphics/theme is good, it also offers offline play as well as group combat (do not start out with this, group combat is literally twice as hard as normal combat and I've had to carry quite a few folks who weren't playing as a team and were playing like they were solo. One big difference is if an enemy is going to use a basic melee or ranged attack, whoever hit them last takes the aggro and the damage from them that turn. Some allies just liked to face tank damage for no reason or attacked an enemy that was already being DoTed to death that turn and wasn't a threat anymore. If you see a skull to the right of their health bar they are dying at the end of their turn, if they aren't a threat then you can ignore them etc.). Overall it's a great game that I definitely recommend picking up for both hardcore gamers and our filthy casuals out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast alot of unique classes that can make insane builds using the different item set combinations in the game. I see alot of people complaining about camera not being moveable but apparently these people didnt take the time to find the controls in the options that tell you pressing Shift moves the camera with the mouse.  Movement in combat can be confusing as well  but as you play more it becomes very second nature on mastering how it behaves and I see no issues on how it has been implemented unlike other reviewers here. Multiplayer is seemless and fun, the difficulty can feel anywhere between impossible and too easy depending on some of the RNG you have, however this is mainly only a concern in the start of a run before the first boss. The story in this game is also very well done having you jump between different books and talking to a whole cast of characters in a way very reminiscent of Hades. Overall if the game is on sale its a clear buy for me and even if it isnt I would still not be mad at buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing and I've been having great fun.Edit: For completeness sake I will leave my original text below. But tpday they set up the following changes to monetization:- No shop rotation- Option to buy very tiny shiny amount so you don't have to buy a bigger pack/always have an uneven amount left to spend- No buying of season levels- Old season passes will stay available after season ends (more info pending)As this shows that they are actively listening and willing to change a predatory model to something acceptable, I'm setting my review to positive---The game is amazing and I've been having great fun.Why do I still not recommend it?Because the financing scheme is abhorrent. I am not completely opposed to keeping your game alive for longer by having options for players to purchase stuff. But the way they set up their season pass is just .. not good1. Free pass is very empty and halfway interesting stuff is very far in the end, causing FOMO and grind. (to make this even worse, the latest update "put items later in the season pass so players only get it if they've played for longer". Per their own patch notes. Wtf?)2. They don't even give an END DATE to their season pass, putting it as "to be announced soon" - so people can't plan ahead.3. You don't see how much EXP you even need for the levels. It tells you how much until your next but do they get more expensive to get later? Who knows. I don't.The game is great. But I truly, truly wish they had made sure that their monetization isn't the incredibly exploitative model it currently resembles.Easy fix in my opinion: If people buy the pass, don't make it go invalid at any point. Let me complete a pass I spend money on (not that I currently intend to do that with the current model). So later, there might be a small library of passes to buy and then complete at my pace.Also: Always online is unnecessary.

Lots of unlocks and free cosmetics. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not really big on turn-based strategies, but I'm having an absolute blast playing this game! I recommend this game to anyone who wants to play a turn based game with their friends and wants a story to follow along to it. There's so much potential for different builds for different "classes," so every run is not the same. (Rougelite) Character designs are pretty cool, combat is very satisfying, the voice acting is a really nice touch, and the UI isn't cluttered and complex, at least to me anyway.Again, I recommend this 100% to anyone looking for something new to try.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games that just hard to put down. I played quite a bit of the demo and have only just begun playing the Early Access version, but I'm already enjoying it a ton. It has varied classes, a decent amount of good voice acting to keep the text from being overbearing, and the enemies/combat are deep enough that it does a good job of making your decisions (and health) matter.My only complaint is that there isn't a "direct purchase" or equivalent for the battle pass. I'm aware of many pros and cons of having in-game currency, and the battle pass itself is (imo) perfectly reasonably priced and stocked. However, the only 2 options to purchase a battle pass are to buy 2 packs of the basic shinies ($3ish = 300) or purchase a larger pack to get a "bulk discount" ($8ish = 1,000). I don't mind paying about $6 for the battle pass, but the double-purchase or overpay-for-your-battle-pass options just "feel" bad to me (even if rationally I'm not mad about currently having 400 shinies left over).Overall, that's a rather small complaint compared to a very fun and polished experience (especially in early access). I definitely recommend this game for those that enjoy tactical and rogue-like experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell they really took notes on Hades' pacing and tried to incorporate that. It's honestly fantastic. It's the sort of roguelite where your experience with it will dictate your future choices and builds, and some of those builds are so satisfyingly broken. There's tons to unlock and the gameplay is super approachable. I'm really surprised; this game feels like a huge deal and deserves a bigger reaction. It's way better and more addicting than Monster Train, which I loved. I think this was a sleeper release that will get some heads turned after bigger reviewers pick it up and check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The developer (who made the fantastic Monster Train) has shown willingness to take and iterate on feedback from the game's community. The game launched in early access as a buy to play game with a battlepass and a cash shop, which for me and many players like me really tarnished what was otherwise a very enjoyable game.The developers have heard the feedback and removed all forms of monetisation from the game altogether, and incorporated the existing purchases into the game itself to be earned by regular play. This is a huge step in the right direction and shows that the devs are willing to listen to their community and genuinely care about giving players the best possible experience. This review stands as a vote of confidence for Inkbound and for Shiny Shoe. They have proven that they are willing to walk the walk, and have earned my support going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: "Eh, I'll boot it up before bed. give it a casual once-over..."4 Hours later, 3am:"Huh. S' pretty good, chief!"Let's all hope and pray that the Day 1 "battle" pass and cosmetic shop remain exclusively cosmetic. Beyond that: Great fun solo or with friends. Some form of voice chat required since, even though it's Turn-based, you and your allies all go at the same time, which is basically chaos in a PUG where you can only communicate through text. That said: It's thematic at least.The Three current bosses have their own challenges to overcome and feel very different and the Roguelike aspect of getting to them in the first place does require a fair bit of trial and error. (In general: Movement "bindings" are key. Get Blink: GG. Magma Miner's Leap? Top tier. Healing is available but near uselessly pitiful - nevertheless, if you can keep out of the nicely telegraphed danger zones, it will keep you topped up.The game occasionally gets a little bit confusing when several enemies use their telegraphed attacks and the battle area becomes some purple cubism nightmare but you soon figure out the save zones and enemy patterns.So far: 10 hours and I've barely touched anything but Weaver and Magma Miner. I suspect another 20+ on the other two I have unlocked and probably the 5th I've not yet. Easily justifies the price if you're dumb enough to merely look at Hours of gameplay per £££.Overall: 0/10. No dogs to pet. Yet....Alright, 8/10. Easy controls, good gameplay, neat cartoonish graphics and an abundance of replayability. The missing 2 points are: Lack of an offline mode (play exclusively with friends, It's apparently on the roadmap) and the day 1 BattlePass and Shop. No early access game should have those at all and are ripe for non-cosmetic Pay-to-win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a masterpiece with smooth and aesthetic gameplay. Customization is good, but it needs to continue to increase (from what I've read they plan to increase the amount of bindings). If they release those soon, I think it'll grasp more of an audience. The layering of multiple different upgrades and paths is extremely enjoyable, reminding me of old school WoW talent trees. Leveling up could be a bit more impactful, but overall rewards are enjoyable. Some may dislike the quests as they require certain things in a rogue-like (uncertain) environment, such as requiring a certain book to progress. Overall, extremely encouraging to see the developers listening to feedback and I think it's a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing. I am perfectly fine with supporting an indie developer if the only thing in a premium shop is cosmetics and the prices seem fair. Most of the time the combat feels well balanced but requires a few hours to unlock stuff to make the runs consistent. The game is easy to pickup but has a learning curve that is satisfying to go through.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommend this. I expected some surface fun for an evening or two with my friends. I got a lot more - the game has infinite replay potential which reminded me of Hades, except you can play coop and still meet a decent challenge. The game is broken, but in a good way - there is no single ultimate build to win a run, but dozens. It is well balanced for a different number of players. I enjoyed creating weird builds, from tons of damage via triggering burn or poison, to tanking and insane smite combos. The only thing I would change is quest book - it's hard to navigate at any time, I would expect some filtering based on current class or other conditions. If you enjoy roguelikes and tactics, go try this.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Binged this for 80 hours and have completed everything as far as the main campaign goes and 90% of unlocks.  My experience is that of a solo player only currently Rank 10 primarily playing a pincushion Obelisk.  Classes in solo play are not all viable more over when you start to do ranked play which adds stacking penalties it becomes even more obvious. Granted you can turn the rank on and off and choose any level of rank you have previously completed with any class for any other, so it is nice not having class specific ranks. Narrative is a lot deeper (If convoluted) than I imagined it was going to be for a rouge-like and dialog and VO are solid. Art styte is ok I would have prefered HI res 2d vs 3d but for cheaper 3d it looks pretty nice.  Enemies are interesting, but I wish a few more types existed, but given the runs onl;y contain 10 combat encounters each I can see why that isn't a focus. I would like a couple more stages (currently*6)  to add more Guardians which are level minibosses, and then after 2 stages you fight one of 3 villains which are your main bosses. Only having these three gets kinda boring they are fine the first 5 times or so but once u learn the pattern with them and are honestly easier than the minibosses or hard level encounters due to ink creep. I would l say the skills system is pretty good each class starts with 3 primary skills and gets 2 more skill slots that can be rerolled if you have the currency with about 10 options to choose. These additional skills can be combat, support, healing, utility ect. Each skill can have 3 upgrades and 1 acension which is a much stronger unique upgrade. About 15 upgrades exist for each skill so build diversity exists within reason. you are also given 7 equipment slots for gear u find or buy through the run and is lost after it. I feel there is a good balance of items for build types and quality. All of these items have "Set" bonus attached to them which I dont feel is explained very well in the game. You will see and item and it will show something like Smite and it shows a lvl3 next to smite. so I need to get more smite stuff i guess? yes and no, u find grinders which will break a single item down and you can get double the sets on that item, Note no more than 3 sets can be on a single item, normally I would say 2 is the most.  So its about deciding what you want to do and finding set items you want wear and others you want to break down to get there benefit. I will say the explanation of what the sets do and at what level is very clean and helpful with hover over.  Music isn't bad, I really like the spaceship music.  Overall I am really happy with the game and hope it grows and more content is added in time.  If you arent someone who binges like me and have friends I can see you and your group having fun with this for quite awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great, you'll see a lot of negative reviews talking about microtansactions and battlepass, they are 100% cosmetic and they give you enough currency through the free battle pass and free code they gave out to buy the premium one completely free. _childDocuments_.review: In a bloated world of roguelikes, Inkbound is a breath of fresh air. The developer that brought us Monster Train does so much right and little to nothing wrong. If turn based strategy tactic games are your thing I would HIGHLY recommend this game. Here are all the pros of this game:1) Combat is smooth. Doing away with the grid system all combat takes place on circular battlefields that decrease in size as the fights goes on. Characters have limited movement, but can always see their range as well as the enemies' intents.2) Abilities are customizable. Throughout the game you are able to enhance your attacks in a variety of ways, while also drafting two more during each run. This leads to incredible replayability. I played the first class for 8 hours before trying other ones and never felt like I was replaying the same type of build. 3) Classes are diverse. Some roguelikes/deckbuilders offer many classes but the overlap between them makes them feel like two shades of the same color. The classes I have played all feel like they have different strengths and playstyles, making each run feel distinct and new.4) Unlockables galore. With so many different quest trees, you are almost always starting each run with something new added to the game. Whether it is a new class or new vestige (what they call relics from StS) you are always opening up new possibilities to build.5) Great world building and music. The environment in this game is so pleasing to look at and the music fits well, enhancing the experience. The only con I can think of is that it throws a lot at you when you first boot it up. I can see how it could be overwhelming to a newcomer, but if you have any familiarity with deckbuilders/roguelikes, you should be picking it up fairly quickly. No severe punishments for dying (other than ending your run,) so experiment away.I am 23 hours into this game and would give it a 5/5. If you are a fan of this genre it is a must-have alongside greats like Slay The Spire and RogueBook.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really good so far. Consistent and flexible builds that allow you to work with whatever you end up getting on your run. The diversity in character abilities is refreshing, however, the actual upgrade that you get during the game as well as the trinkets, are somewhat underwhelming. I feel as though the challenge of the game comes more from decision making and route choosing, rather than actual strategy and skill. I enjoy the "auto-chess" style buffs that you get for having a synergistic build, however I am a sucker for skill trees and feel like the characters could be touched upon more to create more dynamic interactions between the different builds you could have.TLDR: Good game, excited to see what comes in the future. Could use more diversity in builds but is good for where it is at in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, this game is one to definitely keep on your radar if you are a fan of Rougelites. The game rewards you with bonuses like cosmetics and items for future runs for merely experimenting with different play styles that each character has. Playing with Friends adds another element to each run, as you won't be getting the same things as them which opens up more doors for experimentation, and coordination. The co-op element adds an additional replayable element that isn't in Monster Train, which I already loved playing. Another merit to this game is the developers. Shiny Shoe with the removal of extra monetization as they fulfilled their quota to finish the game has proven that they are leagues above other companies in the gaming industry. That move got me is what influenced me from being a follower of the game to a buyer of the Early Access. Shiny Shoe is transparent and works with the community to improve Inkbound. _childDocuments_.review: Extremely polished in terms of UI and presentation. Every element has its place and almost feels tangible. This level of quality is very rare these days.The visualisation of buffs, effects, trajectories, including tooltips always give you the full picture of what's about to happen.The NPCs have unique and funny personas and the voice acting is varied and entertaining. Usually I don't care much about these things (especially in this genre) but it's just so good it deserves being mentioned. The game doesn't bore you with unskippable cutscenes or scripted events either.The visual style is colorful, cute and consistent.As for the game loop itself: You pick a class with some base abilities, then you start what I'll call a "dungeon run". At the start of each run you already get some loot in the form of ability upgrades or equipment. Then you go into the first encounter zone and activate the battle once you feel ready. You take turns with the enemies, bashing each other's heads in. This is of course the bread and butter of this game. Using your energy, your cooldowns and your positioning strategically is what it's all about. After you're done you collect your rewards and go to the next zone which is either an encounter or another reward zone.Somehow the game manages to give you a constant stream of rewards and choices, without feeling overwhelming. Stats have very obvious purposes so your choices don't seem vague or arbitrary. Oftentimes when I play roguelikes I feel like I have no idea what I'm doing but here it's quite clear. Consumables are present as well, but you don't use them in every single fight, they are more like an "oh sh*t" button when you need to get your cooldowns back or whatever. Unlike 95% of games releasing in this genre, this is NOT a deck builder. So it needs none of the "hey do you wanna upgrade a card, OR delete one of your sh*tty ones?" or "hey you have this really cool skill right? Would be a shame if you never draw it" nonsense.Has some achievements and progression already.I didn't play the multiplayer, but singleplayer is fun.Already worth a purchase. Here's hoping that they keep up the high quality and integrated gamedesign throughout the early access.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique take on a Turn Based Roguelite. The freedom of movement and real time attacks among you and your team create really fun opportunities of strategy. The way they implemented the quest system as a way to unlock further Vestiges/items/etc for future runs is really cool, and definitely keeps you coming back for more.  I've seen plenty of reviews complaining about the monetization, and while I get a lot of folks don't like Season/Battle Passes, especially in an early access game, I feel this is one of the fairest I've seen. It's only $6 for the pass, which in the game for the premium currency is 600 Shinies. The free track of the pass gives 300 so if you wait for that, you can just throw in $3. But even with that, the full track gives about 1200 (I might be off by like 100). So you'll never need to buy a future pass if you save 600 of those for the next season.  They also did a recent update where they got rid of the FOMO shop where it rotated out, now they have a static shop where you can get anything you want, which is a huge improvement.  Because this Roguelite is being made as a Live Service game, and the way the multiplayer is built, it brings a lot of potential for unlimited future content.  Personal suggestions for the games future (Which I assume some of these are a given):-More environments (Along with combat areas having more obstacles/non-enemies that impact combat)-More bosses-Stat screen at end of match to show how much damage/healing/etc everyone has done, broken down by ability/bindings for all the number nerds out there (If a concern for public matches and toxicity, maybe just show your own only)-Expand on the way you see vestiges/traits/etc to bring down RNG, as the more you unlock, the harder it is to get what you want in future runs. Would be cool to have quests/levels/something to maybe lock certain vestiges to not show up/etc-Daily/Weekly challenges that come with a leaderboard be it a score system or simply time systemBig Wishes:  -Clan/Guild System, maybe weekly "raid"/"clan" boss that your clan can work on downing for cool cosmetic rewards or even a leaderboard/etc-Boss run where you can face boss after boss to see how far you can getOverall, right now a solid 8/10 from me with very easy potential to get to 9 or higher with future content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun multiplayer game for casual gameplay.Not a great solo experience, especially at higher level ranked modes.Matchmaking is as good as dead, so unless you bring your friends is a solo game.It's a squad-turn-based game. Combat is truly unique as the entire team is doing things in real time and there's various ways you can interact with foes and friends alike. UI tells you any damage you would do with a specific attack on a particular enemy - no RNG. .Classes all play differently. Some classes are more difficult to play solo in early portion of the run, because they are aimed at being a support class and it takes time to get the tools to work around that.It's way past release, but there are still some bugs to fix, minor kinks to iron out, UI improvements to make and potentially balancing changes. These are flaws I don't expect to be fixed, but they are not dealbreakers.It works great and has some nice QoL features (like reconnecting on disconnect, or damage projection, so you know who to protect).You can also share your items and help your team take their build to god-tier.Just keep in mind it's not a very lively game. Bring your friends or you might play alone.There are 2 really:With ~1h runs failing because half way through you started getting things that don't work with your build encourages cheesing using the cheesy builds.In short they are transitioning to Deep Rock Galactic style monetization, where most things are earnable in game and they release some cosmetic DLC every now and then.I would normally be an irrelevant section, but I wanted to point out this is one of the developers that ACTUALLY listened instead of doing the usual 2 steps forward 1 step back.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this game. I love the gameplay. I appreciate the way it emulates Hades by using dialogue to compel further runs. I love that I can play it while my wife watches television. I enjoyed the heck out of the demo as well. So, why hesitate to recommend it?Ultimately, I really dislike the always-online functionality of this game, especially since it plays so well as a solo. I don't appreciate spending time in a lobby with other players running around in circles, stacking on top of one another, and ultimately making me feel less unique ("oh look, 5 identical mosscloaks"), I don't want access to this game to be restricted by my connectivity and its longevity be hindered by the health of the company and servers which I have no control over or impact on.  I'd change my rating if it had an offline solo function.Update: Early release has seen a handful of changes which have dramatically effected the way the game plays, adding depth and simplifying movement. I still love the gameplay, but I've experienced enough server disconnects and shut downs to know that having a fun game dependent on a server I've got no control over is a recipe for unhappiness. Further update: Playing the game with my wife opened my eyes to its possibilities as a multiplayer game. I still REALLY enjoy it solo, but I can't really condemn it for including some solid multiplayer. The game's design has avoided the pitfall of more predatory monetary practices, and the new synergy system for vestiges makes embracing alternate styles of play a lot more fun. This game is excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: In the beta, this was a game where almost all enemy attacks were telegraphed with ranges, areas of effect, and controllable redirects. Combined with the freedom of movement around the field, this made for an interesting dynamic where most damage could be avoided if you played carefully and smartly. it was fun, still challenging at some times and simple at others, but it was a work in progress, I was eager to see it develop.This is no longer that game. The vast majority of attacks enemies use will either reach you with infinite range or will simply hit the entire room and everyone in it. Damage is now a matter of how much you take rather than how much you can avoid, which is one of the most annoying trends roguelites love to chase. The existence of the field is hardly even warranted to the point a Dudes In A Row format would honestly work just fine.Some people will tell you the game is "harder" now, more "tactical." There's nothing tactical about a situation where the only defense is to hit the other guy harder before he hits you. It also extremely strains this game's playability as a solo experience when there's no one else around to soak these now-unavoidable attacks. The fact that the upgrade choice after every fight now always offers a heal, when in the beta it did not, should be extremely telltale of this change in gameplay intent; and it also means you will now be weaker as you continually chase droplets of health rather than actual increases in strength.It's not very fun, and I will not play it at this time. Hopefully that changes.-------Oh yeah 1.0 has come out and apparently the game still does this all the time, so that's swell.

_childDocuments_.review: A difficult thumbs down/thumbs neutral for now, but with the framework to be a great gameI'll assume most people have played Monster Train, and talk about it a bit here. Part of what made Monster Train fun was variation between runs. You wouldn't draw the same cards each time, and you built around different cards, depending on which random power-ups you got, which game-changing items you got, etc. Whenever everything was clicking together and you made a broken deck that steamrolled through, it was dopamine hits galoreThe framework of InkBound is a bit different. In MT, each champion had a starting gimmick, plus different card pools to draw from to build around this gimmick. In IB, each champion has the exact same starting skills/cards, which never change, limiting variation. On top of that, every champion seems to have the exact same starting skills/cards to draw from to add to their arsenal, further limiting variation.Theoretically, the "roguelike" comes in from the random power ups you get for your skills, which provides variation, but since you're trimming down from hundreds of cards a la MT to just, I dunno, 10 skills (more or less) in IB, the power ups have to do a lot of heavy lifting. Which, unfortunately, they fail to do. There's very few total number of power ups, and some power ups are clearly better than others, so you're usually always trying to get the same few types of build (personally I have only had success with DoT builds, while pure damage builds lag behind, and defensive builds only work if you get really lucky with RNG. I dunno, maybe I just suck). Furthermore, upgrades always happen at a the same steady pace, with seeming small, incremental changes, interspersed at predictable timeframes. At the same time, all the power ups are kind of...muted? there's no zany fourth degree synergies between skills, no crazy gamechanging effects. this only changes when you get your "final" power-up/ascension, but again, since getting the final power up follows the exact same pattern every time (you get 3 power ups, then your next powerup is automatically the ascension one), there is no tension. Hades worked because there were some clearly gamebreaking builds, with a lot of synergy between power ups, and clearly superpowered power ups, plus the rate of getting rewarded with power ups was more random, so there was also the this tension of: will the next room have the type of power up i'm looking for? even if it has the type I'm looking for, will the power ups they offer synergize with what I have? will there  be an OP power up that changes my playstyle completely?There's also variation with the items you get, which is the only part that seems totally randomized, but honestly, none of these have the wow factor either. Many are flat bonuses/incremental upgrades. I would get like a few items that made me change my playstyle, only slightly (like, maybe I start using movement skills more because I got a few items that do "X with movement skills"), then totally forget what the items do and keep spamming those skills.Obviously, what worked for MT cannot just be copy pasted into IB. MT had hundreds of cards, and worked as you kept adding and trimming cards. If you introduced hundreds of skills into IB, a game where you can only use a few skills at a time, it would probably be a convoluted mess. Still, I think you could add a few more skills/more levels of variation without breaking the game. Balance will suffer, but who are you balancing the game for? It's PvE, with the most PvP element being leaderboards...forget balance! Add crazy, broken skills and power ups, go wild, that's what makes these type of games fun in the first placeIMO, these changes would recapture that magic:- more skills. not hundreds, like MT, but at least tens, like Hades. seeing the exact same skills every time is no fun. but of course, if some skills are better than others, this just makes it annoying when you get crappy skills. so, the next change...- give each skill at least a few routes to become viable. no need to balance it so every skill is equivalent, that's a waste of time and a losing battle IMO. instead, each skill should have some power ups that synergize with others to become really powerfull. to that extent, this can be helped with the next changes...- (1) introduce a lot more power ups. this increases inter-run variation significantly. (2) make these power ups synergize more with other power ups. (3) make a few of these power ups clearly more overpowered than other power ups, but NOT just in a +flat damage way, moreso in a "you should play the game this weird way instead". (4) make a very select few of these powerups clearly overpowered, and super rare, so when you get it you get a dopamine rush, and you start focusing your entire build on the playstyle those powerups use. (5) also, don't make power ups set in stone. make it so that you can replace one power up with a new one you found if you wannacurrently, the game loop is: gradually gather materials so whenever you get a chance to power up, you keep rerolling until you get the clearly better one out of three offered power-ups, then pick that one, then rinse and repeat.I feel like a better loop is: whenever you get a chance to power up, the options are drastically different every time, with better ones being rarer. sometimes the pickings suck/dont synergize so you just pick whichever. but (1) you start to look for certain synergies in the power ups and a certain "theme" if you will, and slowly phase out your crappier power ups (2) eventually, like once every few runs, you might land on a Big One that just makes you throw all your synergies out and start building around this new playstyleThere are other ways around it, but they would require drastically reshaping the framework of the game. This seems to be the easiest way to do it, without having to drastically change other game systems. It's essentially just adding a bunch more into one part of the system (power ups), and maybe a bit more in some of the others (more skill variation)My humble opinion :)

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay and buildcraft are fun. Enough to carry the rest of the, mostly bad, systems in the rest of the game. Maybe not the hugest build variety, but enough to keep you interested for a while. Co-op turn based games aren't the most common, and unlike story based games such as Baldur's Gate you're not left hanging if schedules don't line up for a while. The game starts off pretty easy, but as you win more runs higher difficulty ranks are unlocked. Also seems a lot easier solo, feels like you really need to synergize in coop to make it through. At least in 2 player, or it's just a skill issue tbh. I didn't give the game's story a chance, so it's not really fair for me to comment on it. I picked up the game solely for gameplay, and the very small amount of story I've read hasn't really made me regret that. The quest/unlock system is, to put it bluntly, godawful. It's like the worst parts of a bad MMO questing system. I honestly think the game would be better if quests were entirely optional, with nothing locked behind them. Riveting stuff like -"Go to X zone as Y character," as 5 different characters and zones. Also you might as well reroll the run if the zone doesn't show up as one of the 3 options at the start. Should just let us pick from all the zones tbh. -"Go to this zone and talk to this character," in a room/path that you probably don't want to go to since it misses out on a room you'd probably prefer to go to. Also after you do that, do it again next run. -"Complete another run to unlock more quests." Meaning immediately abandon a run to unlock stuff quicker. -I hope you didn't want to play the star captain class, because almost 40 hours in and I haven't unlocked it yet. tl;drGameplay good, quests very bad. Chill, low commitment coop with friends good. Get it on sale because they should be paying you to play through the quest system.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure at first, but the more I've played this game, the more it has grown on me. Meaning that while there's an overarching story with quests that build upon each other, you aren't locked into spending hours trying to complete tasks.  You can execute a quick run for 30-60 minutes or if you have more time, go through a deeper run with more challenge and depth.  The quests are interesting and varied and the vestiges (items) you pick up require meaningful and sometimes difficult decisions to choose.  Overall, I'm very pleased that I took a chance on this one and encourage others to do so as well!

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with microtransactions: I empathize with those who question the presence of microtransactions in this gem. It's a common sentiment to cast a skeptical eye towards developers seeking additional support beyond the game's initial purchase. However, please keep in mind that what's offered is 100% optional cosmetic stuff. The developers have been transparent in their intentions; they possess a grand vision and wish to offer players the chance to further support that vision. It's not about extra profit—it's about cultivating a game that continues to evolve and improve, fulfilling both the developers' aspirations and the players' enjoyment. Onto the actual game!Monster Train fans, rejoice! This game takes a unique spin on the monster trains turn based combat system; rather than selecting targets, you line them up Divinity: Original Sin style. All attacks are hitbox-based, each class offers three innate and two universal abilities gained throughout your journey. Moreover, every ability provides three augmentation slots, letting you select from two evolved ability forms.Combine these features with an array of zany artifacts and stat boosts collected along the way, you have a rich multitude of playstyles. Expect a varied monster roster with mechanics that demand your strategic attention. Sometimes you'll teeter on the edge, hunting for the perfect attack. Other times, you'll steamroll everything in your path when your build synchronizes.When you venture into "ranked" mode, the difficulty escalates. Every level introduces new rules and enemy augmentations for an increased challenge.Though you control only one character—no party play here—you can execute multiple moves per turn via "will". As with Monster Train, you'll find yourself instinctively choosing ability and attack upgrades for maximum synergy, reaping the benefits when it all clicks. If it doesn't, you plunge back in and try again.Hoho, but I kinda lied, because you can form a party! Just like in Divinity: Original Sin, the multiplayer allows each player to control their character, adding an extra layer of fun. Whether solo or in a party, this game shines.If you're a Monster Train enthusiast, don't hesitate to give it a shot. As of this review I have done a successful run with each of the starting classes, and am looking forward to seeing what other kinds of whacky builds I can pull of.

_childDocuments_.review: High production value from the makers of the fantastic Monster Train. Artistically captivating. Great music. Thematically interesting. So, why the negative review?The atrocious writing. Almost all the characters in this game speak like asinine, insecure, cringe-inducing, Genz halfwits. Their speech is choked with so many fillers, the writing basically constitutes a masterclass in “HOW NOT TO SPEAK”. It’s clear the writers desperately wanted to make the characters sound quirky, but they ended up creating some of the most annoying ensemble I have seen in a video game.The gameplay loop also lacks depth. While the game has build variety, the enemies are not that mechanically different. Enemy attacks come in basically two varieties—direct attacks that can’t be evaded, and AOE attacks that can usually be evaded by repositioning. It is fun at first, but it certainly doesn’t have the longevity of a game like Slay the Spire. And, even if you can put up with the gameplay’s mechanical simplicity, the cringey writing will probably ruin it for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my radar for a while now. Today, after I noticed it had come out, I decided to buy it and play it. I've always been fond of strategy turn-based games like Divinity: Original Sin, Wakfu, and even the older Baldur's Gate games. The same goes for roguelites; I've enjoyed them since I first played The Binding of Isaac many years ago.This game delivers.Sure, it's not fully there yet, and by that, I mean there's a definite lack of content variety. It only has one playable mode and five classes with a lot of overlapping skills. However, considering the amount of content available, it has great replayability. I've noticed that the multiplayer aspect will likely contribute to the game's replay value, but even in solo mode, I've had a lot of fun so far.The character creator is a delightful system that allows you to play around with movable face paintings as your main way of customization. It's a unique system that feels very rewarding when you invest time in creating your character. However, I would love to see the characters more prominently displayed. Personally, I find that I don't get to see my character up close very often. Perhaps having larger profiles that animate along with your character or having your character stand on the screen while choosing an upgrade would be a nice addition to showcase your character more.I love the combat; it feels nice and smooth while still being quite challenging. It's very reminiscent of games like Divinity, with movement being largely calculated based on how far away from your starting point you relocate. This system is very forgiving, allowing you to spend time adjusting your position before striking. There's often some leeway to exploit, which is incredibly rewarding for someone who plays a lot of games in this genre. Usually, going back and forth would cost you movement points, but in this game, movement only gets applied once you take action from your new position. No more hoping to relocate in the perfect spot and being disappointed by missing by a few pixels! The classes I've tried so far are very fun to play, with most of them having a somewhat high skill ceiling. Some are obviously easier than others, but that's to be expected!There's a lot of room for expansion as well, with slots left open for future classes and a game mode that has not yet been released. There's also plenty of room around the main hub for possible new locations. It's clear that this game is prepping for continued development, and I am absolutely here for it.That being said...The only three things that I actively didn't like were the lack of variety in the combat zones, the absence of in-depth settings, especially graphics settings, and how close the camera is. I would love to have actual environments and larger battlefields where I can fully utilize the Shift hotkey (which lets you pan your camera around the map more). Additionally, the game could benefit from more comprehensive settings options, including graphics settings, as I've encountered mild frame drops in the hub. Regarding the camera, I have a large monitor, so being very close to the character is visually appealing. However, because the character runs quite fast, it sometimes results in mild motion sickness. Zooming out a bit further or slowing down character movement would greatly alleviate this issue. Perhaps implementing camera smoothing could also help, but I'm not entirely sure.Some people are complaining about the existence of a battle pass and a cosmetic shop on day one. While I understand the concerns stemming from previous negative experiences with other games, this game offers a different approach. The battle pass is the good kind, where you can earn half the currency needed to buy the pass on the free line. This means that if you play through one season without buying the battle pass, you can purchase the pass for the next season using the money you earned. With the extra currency from the paid line, you can continue this streak as long as you want. So, you can join the battle pass without having to spend any extra money; you're not being extorted here. Moreover, the battle pass seems to be purely cosmetic, so even if you choose not to buy it, there's nothing in it to inconvenience you. The cosmetic shop is a rotating shop that offers various cosmetic items for purchase. It doesn't have any flashy bundle pop-ups or anything like that (at least as far as I have seen), and everything appears legitimate. The prices for items are also quite reasonable, with the battle pass costing around 6 bucks, equivalent to two purchases of the 3€ currency pack. Even with buying the currency, there doesn't seem to be any deliberately exploitative pricing. So far, the game has surprised me in almost every aspect, and I will likely continue playing it for a long while. With the fair pricing model in place, I'm more than happy to spend a few bucks on cosmetics or the occasional battle pass. Honest and fair pricing is the number one motivator for me to invest money in a game (in addition to receiving cool cosmetics, of course).Especially since the game is supposed to be live service, having a battle pass and cosmetic shop seems important. How else are they going to keep publishing new content? Relying solely on the box price wouldn't get them very far.Overall, the game has been incredible so far, and I can only imagine where it's heading. I do not regret paying 20€ for it; it's an absolute delight!Rating: 9/10If you are unsure, maybe because of the current mixed rating, give the game a try, play the tutorial and one run, and if you don't like it, you can refund it. It's worth the attempt, at least it was for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Inkbound is a refreshing entry to the multiplayer roguelike genre, offering a great deal of replayability due to the vast 'quest' system which allows the players to unlock new possible upgrades, characters, and cosmetics. The game has several different biomes that help to keep the visuals fresh; going beyond environments and having different types of enemies for each area. Despite using unique terms for the systems ("Glyph" = a currency used to re-roll, "Kwilling" = in-run currency, "Vestige" = items/cards that add to or enhance the characters abilities, etc.), Inkbound manages to be easily comprehensible and intuitive. There is enough dialogue between NPCs to explain the systems as they are steadily introduced to the player. Gameplay and character movement is smooth and, while playing with friends, we have not encountered any bugs. The game is definitely more challenging while playing solo, though very much doable. The character classes are each unique which provides diverse gameplay choices. The official roadmap from Shiny Shoes shows further implementation of even more unique classes to choose from in the future.Other future updates shown in the official roadmap include a 'trinket' system, which acts as a permanent progression system unlocked through achievements; allowing the player to further modify their builds before starting the run. I hope to see more roguelite systems like this introduced to the game in the future, as permanent progression offers even more creativity and player agency when fine-tuning builds. EDIT: As of October 6th, Shiny Shoe has stated that they will be removing ALL micro-transactions (that includes paid battle-pass) from the game. Instead, players will be able to EARN EVERYTHING IN GAME. Optionally, players will be able to purchase the seasonal cosmetic bundles from the Steam store as DLC. This change is MONUMENTAL! No more FOMO tactics or rotating shops... This removes my biggest concern for the game. There is now, officially, no reason not to get the game! Other studios could learn from Shiny Shoe. I cannot thank them enough for this change.
_childDocuments_.name: Inkbound

_childDocuments_.review: Right now, I can't recommend the game in its current state. The mechanical system is interesting and engaging, and the moment-to-moment gameplay is good... as a game it's pretty good!As a product, I have issues.-----Inkbound has a living story - new chapters of the story are released each season, with new quests and new story content... but the game's in early access and I THINK it's in season 3? I'm not sure, and there's no way to tell. However, what I do know is that characters keep yelling at me about something I did wrong last season, but I have no idea what that was.One of the story quests this season tells the player to "find the opal slab" and the quest description is "you've seen this recently"... but... I haven't seen it recently, because I didn't get to play that part of the story. The quest description leaves players at a complete loose end... talking to every NPC in the hopes that maybe something will happen. The solution later turns out to be "the gatekeeper will randomly show up during a run and throw it in the ocean" There's no option in the game to go back and play earlier seasons, so you're just locked out of an ongoing story... and the game isn't in full release yet! Imagine buying a game in early access and being told "sorry you already missed the boat."I understand that there's still a lot of content to add, but to avoid frustrating new players, it's vital that there's an option to go back to season 1, and play through all the story in order.-----My second gripe is the monetization. Battle passes and paid cosmetic shops are a phenomenon I associate with free-to-play games, not paid games. If I buy a game, I don't expect or want to be paywalled out of content.When you look at these systems in a game, I always ask myself "was this done because the developers were trying to make the best game they could, or was this done to squeeze the player out of more money?" This feels like I've been sold a product and then the game is immediately shaking the donation box asking for more. Offer me a "full price" option that removes all this junk and gives me all of the content, I'd happily pay a one-time price.There's not enough "shinies" to unlock both of the current battle passes if you unlock them in the *wrong* order, but there is if you unlock them in the *right* order. This is a really terrible design choice. It's compounded by the fact that the correct way to unlock both is to grind the season pass until you get 1000 shinies, then unlock the OTHER pass with those shinies. It feels like a deliberate trap to lock you out of content while being able to say "you can unlock everything for free by playing the game." - It feels underhanded and scummy.

_childDocuments_.review: Was initially turned off by the battle pass, like many others in the reviews. However, after actually looking at it, its really not bad. It costs 600 Shinies (this games real money currency) to pay for the premium battle pass. The free battle pass gives you 300 Shinies. You can buy 300 shinies for $3. The premium battle pass also gives you like 1400 Shinies. This means that after you pay for the battle pass one time, you would never have to pay for another one again, assuming you max out the battle pass.Not only that, but many cosmetics are unlocked through completing in-game quests, which actually took me a while to figure out. The game does not do a great job showing you this. Which i think also left a bad taste in player's mouths. The actual gameplay is really solid, having it always online might be bummer to some, but i personally like the community vibes. The ranking system is a nice touch to keep the game re-playable. I also love the simplicity of the character customization being basically just a face painting simulator, allowing players to create very unique looking faces. I'd say give it a shot, play for 2hours and if its not your cup of tea, return it.

_childDocuments_.review: Inkbound is a really good co-op game if you and your friends like playing strategy games. This game has one of the best implementation of Co-op mode in turn-based strategy game. All team members take the turns at the same time, unlike usual systems that we need to wait for other people to finish first. Often I need to discuss skill usage order with my friend in order to optimally damage the enemies.Skills are also unique to each character and are easy to understand, but gets more complex as you improve the skills via augmentations and artifacts.I wish the game uses more simple terms though, as this confuses me and my friend for a day or two. For anyone jsut getting into the game I recommend noting these down XDAspect = Character/ClassVestige = ArtifactBinding = SkillKwilling = Gold/Silver/Gil/Zeny/etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good! Turn-based gameplay is fun in solo and co-op. Runs take a little more than an hour which is reasonable for a rogue-like. Took about 50hrs to hit rank 20 and clear it. I recommend rank 10 to get the most out of difficulty balance while maintaining random enemy/region buffs that make each run feel unique. Rank 20 feels overtuned (see below). At 60 hours and still haven't finished story. That is slower than I'd like, I think Hades was too slow on 10 clears to finish story and this is even slower. The gameplay loop has remained very enjoyable though.  Constructive criticism follows for devs to future-proof game (would happily buy DLC for any of the below additions). Hopefully future content covers these issues. Many of the characters feel very similar without much to differentiate them; the clairvoyant's orb is very unique, but the others don't have much to really differentiate in a similar way. This results in the game feeling very same-y or repetitive. I think alt-bindings for each character, like the alternate skills in Risk of Rain 2 or aspects in Hades, would really freshen up the game and allow more controllable customization to the builds, even enabling specialization for co-op.I'd love a statistics page at the end of a run or a Run History - Monster Train had an excellent overview, run history, and scoring system. Re-use any parts of those and you're golden! Seeing the only accomplishment "did the most spikes damage" when I had 20 will on turn 1 and finished most combats on turn 1 was frustrating. Being unable to look back on that run, or give it a score, is saddening.Rank 20 feels over-tuned on damage with few survivability options to counter it, especially when some characters only have 1 or 2 binding augments that say "shield" or "heal". It gets frustrating that you need to re-roll for survivability options - runs die to luck of the roll rather than strategy, which hurts. This makes the shield wall trinket so much stronger than it should be. I think there needs to be at least one more alternative to shield or heal; daze and blur are too low impact to sufficiently mitigate.Cinder is really strong, the other villains feel particularly weak - the combat before villain fight has 40+ incoming damage per turn, but the villains other than Cinder rarely hit 20 damage on a turn. Consider adding more villains to make runs feel unique or improve my "choice" at beginning of runs (why can I always pick from the same 3 villains? Doesn't feel like a "choice", like all other "pick 1 of the 3" decisions in the game that have more than 3 possible options).And lastly, I think some characters just need some damage buffs, or enemy health in co-op needs nerfs. Star-captain's attacks look massive and barely budge the enemy's health-bar. Stack this with the mediocre damage of frostbite when compared to the other statuses and the star-captain does struggle to keep up, usually relegated to support - which doesn't mesh with either how the NPCs introduced the character as "too strong" or how his binding animations look powerful. If my co-op friend does not bring a high damage character and I play as star-captain or other low damage char, we cannot do enough damage to win.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disheartened when I saw all the negative reviews on launch day for this game, so I'd really like to weigh in on the 2 biggest complaints I saw.  100% worth the price of admission. The gameplay is not impacted by the presence of a cash shop for purely cosmetic items. Said gameplay is challenging, but generally if it feels "unfair" this is more the fault of the player putting themselves in a bad spot in combat and/or not playing to their build's strengths. 1. Early Access with cash shop: Yup. Don't care. Monster Train was an excellent game, Inkbound is developed and self-published by the same independent studio. I am more than happy to be able to throw more money at them for continued support in a game I played for nearly 12 hours the day I bought it. I will admit that at the time of writing, some of the particle effect cosmetics, whether footprints or head effects are pretty underwhelming or an absolute NOPE with how they interact with other parts of the character model. I will also concede, again at the time of writing, that I understand the disdain for the abundance of premium cosmetics up for sale out the gate, and do wonder if they may end up either scaling down the prices, or improving the rate at which you can earn Shinies.  Grind and unlock the free, more prestigious (IMO) cosmetics, ZERO impact on gameplay and no reason to doubt the devs the way I see so many people doing. Look into Monster Train and the cash-grab or other doubts should be assuaged. 2. Single player difficulty scaling: Git gud. I mean it. I got destroyed fairly shortly into my first 3, maybe 4 runs? I've only played the game solo so far and have completed several runs with one class (Mosscloak) and once with both the Magma Miner and the Obelisk (who feels a bit overtuned). The game can be very brutal and is absolutely unforgiving when it comes to mistakes, but also (almost) always feels like you can squeeze out a win. I believe every one of my deaths were due to negligence on my part (nuking myself on the Clairvoyant because I tunnel visioned on my orb while standing in an ink puddle) or kind of throwing together a very inefficient build or playing my build poorly due to being used to a different play style.  I don't know what to say, I'm no prodigy, and the game is absolutely winnable.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game and will probably be coming back as new seasons come out. It's a great roguelike if maybe a bit easy on solo. I got to rank 13 or so before losing and even at rank 20 I've got a better chance then not of winning the run. But the mechanics were fun to play with so it never turned into a slog to get the seasonal challenges/achievements.The story was good for a roguelike but it's telling is quite honestly, a mess. You'll leave a run, someone will talk to you and you'll have zero indication what part of the storyline anyone is referring to. And the words ink, bound, aspect get so jumbled up it's hard to track.Game is not without flaws tho. The only real multiplayer I did was with a buddy who got bored faster than me. But with what we did play, the balance just seemed off. Despite how often I was winning solo, at two players they more than double the enemies health (never tried with a bigger group). Without being able to clear a few enemies each turn, you can't get enough defenses to properly survive. It just felt bad when jumping between solo and multiplayer. I know I had more to say about the negatives but it's STILL great!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start the review off with saying that the battlepass is cosmetic only and you buy it with premium currency, it costs 600 Shinies (premium currency) and you get 300 in the free tier of the battlepass, if you choose to get it, then after completing the battlepass you'll basically have refunded the amount you used to get it as the pass gives you even more Shinies in the premium part. Currently Shinies are only for cosmetics and I hope it stays that way as Its one of the best and fair battlepasses / monetisation methods I've seen and is in no way needed to enjoy the game what so ever.Now that, that's out of the way, the game even at its earliest stage of release is polished quite well, I'm not saying there isn't any problems but in my opinion the positives of the current game completely outweigh the negatives. With time, those negatives could very well be ironed out, along with getting new content such as classes, items, perks, bosses, maps. The combat is turned based where enemies attacks and damage numbers are already displayed for you, some are telegraphed attacks which can be dodged and some are targeted attacks which always hit, unless you either reduce their attack, you gain a stack of evasion to dodge, or just plainly take them out. When you end your turn all the planned actions for the enemies activate. The 3 bosses currently in the game have unique mechanics which is fun to work around for your build.If your a solo player the game is much harder but still doable, adding even 1 more play makes the game much easier but more complex as enemies that targets aims against the last person that hit it, in addition you can build around making synergies.If you like the look of the game and/or you enjoy turn based games I'd honestly recommend the game, there is enough content in the game right now to easily justify the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game that merges deck building rogue likes with turned-based strategy in way that no other game has done so far. The first time I played the game I didn't set it down for 6 hours. Also, one of the classes was impressively unique--as in I don't think I have ever a class concept like the Weaver in any RPG or other video game, ever. So, hats off to ACTUALLY making a unique class. I haven't even seen the archetype before, but the concept was very fun to play. The other classes I have seen some variation in an RPG or MOBA. The achievements and quest are fun. Tips for improvements: At the end of a successful fun, everything just flashes WAY too fast,, I can't actually see the different achievements and stuff I accomplished.  Also, quest tracking is VERY, VERY cumbersome. Especially early in the game. Lastly, if a quest references an NPC to speak, it would be nice to know where they are (usually it does, but not always, like for Chronicler). Regardless, this is a solid 9/10 . Could be a 9.5 / 10 if they improved the post-run UX and quest tracking.  Want a 10/10?? Game needs more variety in bosses (Guardians and Villains).  Having more than one Guardian per book and having more Villains would up replay value and by extension the "just one more run" factor (the "hook"). Also, not sure why i am allowed to pick the final boss, it makes runs very easy even.

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem of a game! This game is a blend of card deck building with real time turn based. It sounds strange, but it just works so well. Don't listen to the negative reviews that say only a few augments are viable — you can create clever combinations and pivot each run as needed. Not to mention the coop runs are super fun. Wife and I love going in together and causing chaos where we can. Game developers seem greatly involved, and the fact that they removed microtransactions after playerbase said it wasn't for them was really cool in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: *** After 230+ hours, I wanted to just add, this is probably my favorite game, one of the few I play daily. Its so replayable and the daily challenges are so awesome. Whatever I wrote below, just add 1000X ... if you like the genre, buy it.As a big fan of deckbuilder roguelikes, I count their earlier work of Monster Train as among my favorite games, a peer of StS on my pantheon of god tier games. I say this for context when I tell you that Inkbound has the potential to be better than Monster Train, if they continue to build and improve the experience. The turn based combat is great, the three initial characters are all fun and very different. I do recommend watching a short video on tips for beginners as I did not feel like the game did a great job explaining how to play, FightinCowboy had a very good one that helped me hit the ground running. The game is awesome and with 5 playable characters and a ton of real estate in terms of regions and bosses I expect it to offer many many hours of entertainment with major replayability. It has super satisfying run build and meta progression with bunches of augmentations and buffs giving the player so much choice. Finally, it all comes together to whisper, "One more run, just one more run..." which is the true measure of any roguelike IMO SO yeah, if you like this sort of thing, get this game. If you don't have Monster Train, buy the bundle, you are in for some majhor fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The unlocks in this game are ridiculously stronger than anything you start with - this is a metaprogression and grinding game on top of what should really just be a cute multiplayer puzzle experience. The amount of power and versatility you have from the later items is far beyond what you'd even imagine when you start. We snap-grab certain items and the game turns from stat checks to a slog from having 'already won' the run, neither state is interesting.The difficulty does not scale quickly enough to meet your skill level, and it's impossible to skip that progression. all characters need to be used and played in order to advance your 'rank' (which has effects similar to 'Ascension' mechanics) which adds dozens of hours of playing through low rank characters at low difficulties to prove to noone you can do the bare minimum.The initial 'season pass' has 100 levels, and it's about one level every 40-80 minutes, which is quite a high number of hours for anyone without two months of summer vacation. It is just cosmetics, but it does display the level of engagement Shiny Shoe expects from its player base.'Quests' grant experience but are all repetitive tasks, or, in the worst case, a gamble that you will see a specific item in a run, and be able to use it, and use it enough times (which can often take two runs due to poor timing on finally finding the item), and all within a time limit when it comes to 'seasonal' quests. Many resets involved if you want to reach that arbitrary completion checkbox. Holy cow is this game nothing but a skinner box.  The core game doesn't deserve the grind imposed on it. I'd like to just skip the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and play with friends at a difficulty that's worth playing (without having us give up our other hobbies to get to that point!)
