_childDocuments_.review: PVE Player and my opinion- This is my first review from many games. I just thought enough of posting one for those considering buying. 1. The economy is broken. I have only spent money to repair my armor and pay crafting taxes. I have saved about 7k at level 32. Quest give most of the gold and the story line is only so long, mobs give very little gold with most giving no gold at all. I am unable to have a house ( which gives you the ability to increase your storage, a must for the serious crafting player ) because after I purchase it, I wont be able to pay the taxes to keep it. There are too many ways to spend money and not enough to earn it. When crafting, you have to pay a tax for each item made. If you use the trading post you are taxed. I'm not going to flame anyone who may have worked on this design, but a correction is needed quickly. Simple economics should to tell the devs we have an issue.2. If you are a hardcore gamer, you will run out of content quickly. Its been roughly two months since live and the player base is falling fast. I'm personally trying to keep my crafting up while leveling. This is helping me get a little bit more out of the game. If you want to go fast, prepare for a burnout.3. PVP concept is great, but execution has complications. Control of the map should be limited to a certain percentage. Another suggestion to the devs would be to have a starting area for each faction that is permanent. So I love the game to this point. I personally think if some changes are not made quickly, the player base will only decrease further. There are several other things I could write about, but the overall issues are:1. Bad economy2. PvP map issues3. Ability to make gold4. The cost of fast traveling5. Player base losing interest because all of the above.

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't regret my 200+ hours in the game, and for $40 you will get your money's worth in time before you likely give up in the 30-50 range.The best way to sum the experience so far though is that this feels very reminiscent of Anthem. You have a game that has game play that is rather fun and engaging, and an art department that killed it with the environments. However, you are left with a 1/4 baked game that could have used more development and testing. Where the development company is constantly saying "trust us, we are going to fix this" and with each patch introduces something that completely destroys the momentum of the game. Whether it is the numerous game breaking bugs that we've now had multiple economy shutdowns due to, or to the undocumented increases in end game difficulty to artificially inflate the grind further on an already shallow and poorly executed end game loop. It's just getting exhausting to watch this cycle happen. Also, if you like playing solo, good luck, that's been destroyed as of this review. Until AGS can come together and actually figure out what they want the game to be, it will largely be in a state of "what the hell is going on", and with server numbers consistently dwindling in a game that requires people to engage for the mechanics to function properly. This is likely a candidate for an Anthem situation where we get a "Look guys, we're sorry but we are shutting down production on this, learning our lessons, and thanks for the journey" email in the next year if they can't humble up in the boardroom and stop fighting feedback, but embrace it from their community.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont post reviews often but I really want this game to succeedNew World: Aeternum has been suoer enjoyable for me, offering a blend of solo exploration and group-based activities that keeps the game fresh and enjoyable. One of the standout features for me is how well it balances the need for solo play with the excitement of group activities. There are moments when I crave the solitude of the open world, and other times when I enjoy teaming up with others. New World threads this needle exceptionally well, allowing me to seamlessly shift between playing alone or joining up with friends without ever feeling like I'm forced into one playstyle over the other.The amount of content available in New World is staggering. From crafting and trading to PvP battles and group expeditions, there's always something to dive into. However, what I truly appreciate is that the game doesn’t pressure me to focus on any one activity. Whether I want to spend hours gathering resources, leveling up my crafting skills, or exploring Aeternum, I never feel like I’m on a strict path. This freedom to play at my own pace and pursue whatever captures my attention at the moment is one of the reasons I keep coming back.The world of Aeternum is a joy to get lost in. Whether I’m logging, mining, fishing, or just running around to uncover new areas, the world is full of little treasures. It’s one of those games where I find myself getting caught up in the simple pleasure of wandering, seeing what I can discover, and reaping the rewards of a peaceful, low-pressure play session.Overall, New World is a flexible experience that accommodates a wide range of playstyles. Whether you’re a solo player or someone who loves to group, there’s something here for you. If you're looking for a game that gives you the freedom to play how you want, while still offering plenty of depth and adventure, New World: Aeternum is definitely worth your time

_childDocuments_.review: As a decade+ veteran of WoW and multiple other MMO's, New World scratches the itch from a few next generation issues that other MMO's will *never* address. Most importantly (to me) is physics on capes and cloth armor pieces. You can't make an MMO feel modern without it. Secondly, active combat. Some skills can be a little too anime-inspired for the aesthetics of the rest of the game but combat is fun, and "easy to learn but difficult to master", there is a time and place for blocking, dodging, and pushing the offense. If you're looking for a story, this isn't the place to get it. If you're looking for engaging events that break up the grind, this isn't the game for you. If you need a perfectly seamless and completely bug free experience, this might not be your cup of tea. Things we still desperately need as of the time of this review: - A clearer picture of endgame content including more PvP modes, raids, solo-able endgame activities, etc.- Transmog.- More weapon types (though they have added quite a few since launch).*** As of 10/12/23Devs have delivered transmog in a satisfactory way, we have a new weapon (the flail) that I love. As for a clearer picture of endgame content, they have overhauled endgame gearing in a way that is incredibly user friendly and respects players time. PVP has added an "influence race window" that successfully encourages open world PVP.*** 06/08/2024- It has been some time since the first expansion dropped for NW, and there has been little meaningful communication from the development team about the next big steps. There were rumors of a "big announcement" in June, that many speculated would be confirmation of a console release. I thought this as well, but I was hoping to hear about a new weapon type or two, some new PVP/OPR maps, announcement of a major content drop to coincide with it? Well, to say I am disappointed is an understatement. When NW released it was a breath of fresh air for me as an MMO veteran. We had a new title with fresh modern graphics & fluid combat that existed entirely without the tab-target-tedium of MMOs of the past, the world was beautiful and fun to explore with resources to gather around every corner. Plenty of min-maxing to be had for the MMO player looking to scratch that itch, plenty of weapons to mess around with, we even had a projectile bow for skill-shots and a hitscan musket at the same time! The story took a backseat, this is an MMO after all not a single player RPG. Sure, story elements were there for those that wanted to read about them, but we're here to power through the grind and PVP along the way right? Everything I appreciated about NW's state on launch has taken a backseat to things I could not care less about. Instead of doubling down on what they did right they've taken years to overhaul the story (twice, essentially) to the detriment of PVP content. Sure we got "races" that don't work and consistently boot you back to the nearest town because the servers can't handle so many players at once. We're getting a swimming animation, because idk about you but when I boot up a new MMO all I really want to do is swim around in the ocean right? We're getting single player "soul trials", 5 minute little solo-dungeons with meaningless loot. We'll have a PVP-only island that will likely function exactly like the "races" do, and no new OPR map that people have been asking for forever. No new weapons.10/06/24 - We've had zero meaningful content updates since ROTAE and everyone who has supported the game from the start has been left to rot while they try to capitalize on a console release and an upcoming... update? It's certainly not an expansion. No new weapons, a single pointless PVP zone that will without a doubt run poorly and constantly kick players out. People who pre-ordered this update get a free mount, existing players supposedly get this mount too, yet the announcement regarding it makes NO mention of how to claim it, even in the "additional details" link, it doesn't exist in the in-game store or the item claim menu. There is no announcement about it when logging in. No one in chat will tell you anything about it. Once upon a time NW seemed like a beacon of hope for people that wanted to keep classic MMO's alive with a modern real time combat system, now it just feels like a lie and a cash grab. You lost me AGS.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a game review before, but in this game are so many misleading, addicted copium sniffers that will praise the game no matter what, that i felt like i should give an honest opinion, so people don't waste money on this glorified tech demo. Let's start with what some people praise the most - the combat. Combat in this game ranges from OK to slightly above average depending on the weapon. If everything works as it should that is, which is usually not the case. Untegistered hits, desync, buggy weapon swap, unreliable animation canceling while dodging is all too common for the combat in this game to be considered good. All of the above should be unacceptable in an "action combat" MMO. Mobs hit hard in this game, so if you are wearing light armor a failed animation cancel can easily cost you your life. I guess this isn't that much of a problem for most people since 95% of players run with Greataxe\Warhammer in heavy armor. If this wasn't enough there are also glaring balance issues(see GA\WH + heavy armor) and lag exploits. Crafting and GatheringI have to admit this was the part of the game that i really liked at the beggining and that kept me playing for some time despite the horrible combat. Lost of gatherable stuff in the world and many crafting disciplines, which feel rewarding. But then as you level up it quicklye turns into a grindy chore. When you get to make higher tier crafting mats you might think: "Ok now i'll get to gather some higher tier mats. Finally some variety". Nope, gather even more T1 mats, ya dingus. In fact you'll be mostly gathering T1 mats for the whole game with very limited amounts of higher tier mats. When i saw that higher tier refined mats require a lot of lower tier mats i realized how much of a chore the crafting will be and i've quit the game.Quests and StoryNew World has arguably the worst questing in any MMO i've played in last 15 years. There are only three types of quests: talk to someone, loot X chests, kill X mobs. Also the game makes sure that you'll have to waste hours of your time by deliberately placing the area where you have to do the quest extremely far away form the NPC that gave you the quest. Also there are no selectable rewards. Oh, you are wearing light armor with DEX stat? Too bad, take this heavy plate with INT and go away. Combine that with very meager exp and gold rewards and the quests almost always feel like they are not worth the effort.When it comes to the story there is not much to say because it barely exists.WorldThe world design is actually very good, especially when it comes to sense of scale. The soud design is also on point. But the thing once you have seen like 20% of the world you've seen all of it. There are tons of copy-pasted assets. In my journey to level 30 i've encountered literally 4(zombie pirates, wolves, boars, lynxes) enemy models. 4. FOUR. I know that in many MMOs developers often take existing enemy models and slightly change them to make new enemies, but this game is taking it to a level that i never thought i would see.EndgameI can't say anything about end game for myself because i was unable to play this chore of a game for this long, but from what i heard from my friends the endgame is either very limited(high pop servers) or non-existent(low pop serwers). The HWM system is one of the worst ideas i've heard of. Not only it's a monotonous grind, it's also timegated. WHAT??! But i guess "More hours for your money" right? "I spent 400 hours in this game so it's worts 40$". This arguments is so flawed that i don't even know where to begin. I could go to a local restaurant and pay them 5$ so i can do the dishes for them for 1000 hours. Does it seem worth it to you? If not, then a good portion of New World players would disagree with you.On top of it all there are also: automated bans(if some company doesn't like you they can get you banned by mass reporting you), automated customer service, undocumented changes, patches that often break the game and make it even more grindy, 0 faction balancing mechanics, horrible performance, tons of dead servers, developers astroturfing forums and completly ignoring community feedback.

You gather and craft to sell on the trading post for other players to buy. That is how you make your money. Bots are killing that economy because the low-level materials are getting cheaper and cheaper. So the person who goes out and farms for hours to craft gear or level up a gathering skill is getting close to nothing in return. Amazon Games does nothing; if they do, it's a 1-day ban. They let it go because it pads their numbers to say look how many active players we have and look how much money we are making on this game. I give this game maybe 2 years tops for its lifetime if something is not changed on either banning people or changing up the game entirely. _childDocuments_.review: While writing this review, I have 66 hours played on my character and 74 hours on record according to Steam, so I have been playing this game.The game is great. Everything feels well made, but there are these little things that stick out occasionally. Overall, I’m having fun. Didn’t get to play much on weekend since there was massive que but that’s not really a big negative for me. One of those things is running. You really don't get all the quests at once to one place, all side and main missions are chain quests, so there is so much running. Combat is nice, PvE mostly in my case. Nothing really to add. Only downside right now seems to be that at level 40, I've seen most enemy types. Same attack patterns repeat throughout the game, at least so far they have. Once you learn attack patterns, it’s pretty easy to just bash forward.Crafting seems pretty grindy. I have pretty much everything, except fishing, on 100. There is still much to learn about how to do things and where to find things, so can’t really go deep into this subject.TINK & CHOP. Pretty much the best part of the game for me. Gathering. It is just so satisfying experience in this game. I’ve spend days only farming things because it’s so satisfying. My ratings for this game:- Story: ??/10 (I just bash E to skip)- Graphics: 10/10- Audio: 8/10- Combat: 8/10 PvE, ??/10 PvP- Crafting: 6/10- Gathering 10/10Get it, if you enjoy grindy games and MMO games in general. Premium price, no subscription, much fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Take your pick on why this game is awful. Being forced to roll on other servers, away from your friends, because your friends are spread out on various servers that opened on release and all of which are currently locked or not accepting newer players to join. Horrific grinds for XP, professions, and crafting. Limited bag and bank space, both of which can quickly be filled with useless crap that you're not sure if you need or want to use at a later time. Shrinking economies and deflation of goods, making it not worth selling anything to other players. Vindictive streamers and their simp armies who help them rule (and ruin) every zone on the server. Company leaders who will raise taxes in a town by obscene amounts every time you kill them in PvP, to punish you for not worshiping them. All of the random quest bugs, horrific respawn times, pvp exploits, money duping, and various game-breaking issues. Not to mention the BS with server transfers, or some outright awful game mechanics that force players to play or suffer through horrible game design choices and grindy slog that is this game. I wanted to like New World, and it had a lot of promise. It's gorgeous, and could have been great. Unfortunately, it's just so unbelievably grindy and constantly punishes you if you play it casually and don't devote 40+ hrs per week into it like a full time job. It's not worth it. Save your money, avoid at all costs. Maybe check back in 6+ months later to see if it's fixed. Instead, you could go support an indie company or five and buy a handful of cheap indie games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of New World is a great one - PVP, PVE, territorial claims, faction politics, company competition, etc.  However, the execution is absolutely horrible.  Since launch, there have been serious gameplay issues that you've probably read about in other reviews or seen from streamers. One issue is exacerbated by the previous issue, and leads directly into the next issue.  Amazon was on a crusade to stop the cheaters and dupers and gold spammers, so their solution was to prevent the players from using the trade houses, effectively shutting down the economy.  By the way, there are no trash vendors - the game world utilizes an ENTIRELY player-based economy.  What happens when you shutdown a player-based economy? Hoarding, followed by markets flooded by goods, followed by extreme devaluation, leading to an upside-down world where an egg costs more than level 60 gear. So by attempting to fix the problem, they create new ones.  I swear the lack of foresight by the development team is like looking at medicine before the Renaissance.As of 22 November, the 50 v 50 territory war is completely broken. There is an exploit available to the users of a newly-introduced weapon, the Void Gauntlet. The Void Gauntlet particle effects create heavy lag/packet loss when cast into areas with more than 10 character (like a pvp war area...), so the team that spams the most AOE particle effects creates the most lag ON THE OTHER TEAM.  That's not strategy, that's a lagfest and an exploit.  So shame on the players who have used that to gain territory - but, get this: Amazon Games Studio is not only aware of the problem, they've admitted to it in their own forums! "Heavy lag" is how they described it. It's an ever bigger shame on you, Amazon, for allowing the exploit to continue. What makes this particular bug even more frustrating is that AGS has seen this problem in two other weapons (Life Staff AOE healing and Ice Gauntlet AOE attacks/CC abilities).  Their ingenious "fix" was to not allow stacked healing - so only the most recent heal counts and therefore cancels the previously cast spell, even if it came from a higher level player.AGS's track record of making their game better is a weekly downhill slide, and now it appears that they are so overwhelmed by the cascading effects of their errant fixes that all they can do is shrug their shoulders.Maybe they think they're too big to fail.  It appears to me that they are too big to care.I've put 606 hours into this game, grew a company from scratch, claimed and held a territory for over 6 weeks, hoping AGS would make this the MMO to play.  Now I'm convinced it is not.

_childDocuments_.review: New World is an awesome game, firstly I think it worth noting that the game is not in a “great” state right now and if you choose purchase the game I think it’s worth knowing that it might be a poor experience. Generally speaking New World is a lot of fun with plenty to do. If your coming in with a more casual mindset it think the game with be just fine but if your wanting to really enjoy experience the game to its fullest i feel it will be a challenging and problematic experience. As many are aware the game is has a good handful of bugs that are disrupting the player experience. This is really disappointing as Amazon games had an amazing opportunity to grab while the other MMO games start to decrease in popularity. This game is a “Live service” game so I have no doubt that the game will at least improve in some way or form in the coming months, the developers have already mentioned about various changes that are on the way. The best outcome for this game is to fix the issues and keep improving the experience, the player base has already dropped to an all time low at the time of writing due to a vast array of issues. Now that this part is out the way, the game itself is rather good! Firstly the combat in the game feels very responsive and complex there are tons of weapons to choose from and you can build out your own character kit however you want. The armour is a little more on the subtle side, nothing looks incredibly threatening or powerful that’s unless you want to buy cosmetics. This freedom in the character progression is a really good change and I have a really good time building my character to my liking. The PVE/PVP both feel free great to play, the PVE Questing can be repetitive and lack story depth but it’s at least acceptable in my opinion. Where New World actually makes up for it’s shortcomings is in the PVP side of the game, the game just feels a lot more engaging playing in a team and doing the PVP objectives. Fighting for power over the local land is a really great experience. That’s not to say there isn’t issues with PVP but I had fun with it during my time played. Moving onto the map and world in which you play on is really impressive it’s dense and full of detail the world feels really alive. The map has plenty of towns around this world and all the factions are fighting to maintain power over them. There is a current problem with the way the economy works. It’s all based of local sales which pretty much locks off all the rest of the players from trading certain items. It seems the developers are planning to change the way this system works which hopefully with resolve these issues. Another world based feature is “War” this game mode is strange, it’s actually good when the war is organised properly but normally it’s a mess due to how these wars are setup. Clan leaders are pretty much the deciders of the war now this ok when  this leader is but it’s not always like this. The wars mostly end up being scrambled and disorganised. This is because the clan leaders are fighting over who gets to participate in the war. There is also a good amount of other changes that need to happen to improve this mode. Moving into the dungeons, they are arguably better than the normal PVE. I didn’t play many of them but I did have a very fun time fighting through them with my friends, it actually challenged me and required me to approach with caution in many combat engagements. There is tons more in new world that I didn’t mention, it’s definitely worth looking at some gameplay or streams if you want to see the normal experience in New World.Coming away from the gameplay, the art is awesome it feels a little on the older side but that also could be down to the scale of the game. The lighting is great and the whole world feels incredibly epic in scale. Everything feels very alive in the world. As for performance it runs pretty well, you should expect to see good performance with most pc specs. The only one mention would be when in large scale war or in a town the frames can drop immensely due to all of players on screen but fortunately nothing unplayable. The sound in the game is incredibly surprising, I was not expecting it to be as good as it is. All the sounds are crisp and sound exactly as you would think they would. It’s definitely one of the strongest factors of the game. As for monetisation, it certainly could be worse there is plenty of cosmetics to buy but fortunately the game doesn’t even attempt to force any purchases on you which was a good thing to see. I feel this might change but right now the monetisation is on the better side. Overall, the game is “ok” if steam had a (purchase with caution) review option this game would certain be under that title. It’s a moderately good game but it needs time to become what it should of been at launch. Playing it later will allow hopefully give you more content to experience. It’s a rocky start but hopefully it gets smoother from here. Maybe wait for a sale or come back in 3 to 6 months.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great potential, but needs to be revised in its concept and balanceConcept:- looting mainly consists of chest runs, just come to high-lock and loot chests with a crowd in semi-afk mode. It is quite possible to transfer loot from chests to mobs so that people can farm them in competition in pvp, which will revive both pvp in the open world and farm- Static respawn resources need to be changed to random. The developers have already said that there is no such possibility, but, sorry, I do not believe this - they just set other priorities. However, the issue of spawning resources can solve the problem of an empty world, when you can meet no one at all on the outskirts of a location for half an hour, and this is much more important than adding another dungeon, which you go through a couple of times and forget about it.- HP bar, which displays the remaining 10k hp of the enemy, needs to be changed to full display. You do not feel the impact of your actions, which in any case does not give a positive experience in combat        Balance:- In my opinion, it needs a complete rework in a global patch. Completely uneven indicators of incoming damage and healing, a large bias towards defense (for example, 625 gs dd can stupidly not pierce the healing from the player’s HP potions in heavy armor). This affects not only 1v1 pvp, but also sieges - tactics are lost, the one who has a fatter burst wins, when the logic itself should be something like this: went into a frontal attack without thinking - lost.- Control... Since the release, there was not been added a cooldown for passing the same type of control on the player, which made sieges a bunch of hammers instead of a variety of classesOverall updates and content adding - this game needs more depth, variety. Adding new dungeons, alas, does not contribute to this. In the future, I would like to see marine content, the construction of ships and battles on them.While the game is raw, it has the above disadvantages, but I advise you to try it, you will like it for at least 100 hours

_childDocuments_.review: I believe the core issue with the game stems from its initial design philosophy, which prioritizes server-based social interactions. The game encourages players to forge friendships and rivalries, and to engage in intricate player-driven narratives within individual servers. However, each server has a limit of approximately 2,500 players, which presents a long-term sustainability problem for the game.As the MMO player base naturally fluctuates, servers risk becoming deserted, compelling players to migrate to more populated servers. Unfortunately, server meshing isn't a viable solution due to how the game's mechanics, such as wars, are fundamentally designed. This results in a cyclical problem: when major updates or events attract returning players, they often find they can't log in, or worse, their original server has been shut down. These are significant pain points that hamper player retention.The introduction of mounts is a long-overdue feature that many believe should have been a part of the game from the outset. The decision to package this crucial element as a $30 paid DLC is quite disappointing. Not only does it put a price barrier on something that could enhance the basic gameplay experience, but it also risks alienating the player base by making what many consider to be a fundamental feature an additional cost.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't tend to leave reviews but I think New World really requires insight before you buy especially with it being a new release.Here are a few facts of where I'm currently at in the game to give the context of my specific experience.- Currently Mid-Level 40.- Current Lvl Cap 60.- Played both Beta released.- Had moderate experience in other MMO RPG'sBeginning the game from release date I thoroughly enjoyed my experience, there were so many things to gather, chop, mine, and discover. Alongside learning the different Weapons, Armor types, Crafting, etc. It was a joyful treat every day, the game gave new experiences and allowed you to take things at your own pace whether you spent more time questing or focusing on trade skills, or balancing the two. It was all a delightful experience. Especially playing alongside friends!This experience was consistent up to around LVL 25. - 30. Through this leveling period, I felt that I was finally starting to experience the game. I did my first dungeon, got to some good soft-caps on trade skills allowing me to gather, chop, and my new thing and discover what they do and just felt it was going to progress well.UNTIL.... my current point in the game. (This could purely be due to overplaying the game but there are some undeniably boring concepts in the game).I've currently been playing through level 35. - 45. and just feel the game is becoming a chore. Here are my key experiences which I hope I've kept somewhat to TLDR standards;  -about as stale as a slice of bread you left out  - Search 6 Chests  - Kills 15 Mobs  - PVP Questing is, literally, standing in a field for 1 min 30 seconds on your own hoping a group of 6 people don't arrive.  - I actually don't think there has been one interesting quest in my experience so far. - I find this quite fun depending on the skill - Some skills are mind-numbing (logging) where you feel like you're a corporate company deforesting the rainforest but with an axe. - Gathering and Skinning is quite fun as there is variety in what you can collect/kill and what it's used for in the refining process. Alongside it feeling rewarding to kill larger more difficult animals or gather a variety of plants, herbs, and weird ♥♥♥♥. - The refining process is okay. you make things from your materials and can buff them or add beneficial traits or functions to the things you craft. - Fishing is good! (I'm Biased) but there are problems like your friends cant see how big your fish is when you catch it and it also seems counterproductive if you want to LVL as it takes forever! - Overall its a nice addition but has its minor flaws - They are pretty fun I have done 3 so far.  - LVL.25 was a simple but nice intro.  - LVL.35 was a good step up had some mechanics but still pretty easy.  - LVL.45 has mechanics and is fairly difficult... I still haven't killed the last boss. help. - I can see dungeons being stressful solo - Some simple mechanics arent clear. I'm playing a tanky role and I still have no clue how aggro fully work and there's no way to measure it that I know of (I'm pretty ♥♥♥♥ at games) - Mobs can be a bit buggy in some dungeons and just be unpredictable but its never been majorly problematic - Overall with friends this has been the most fun experience of the game - ITS F'D  - Economy is ruined  - You can buy light meals for 0.01 gold so you lose money putting them up with trade tax.  - I have legendary items that are only selling for 100 gold... which I can earn in 10 mins of questing. - Everything just sells for so little. Apart from bags which you have to spend money to make money and go gather which is fair. - This could change in the long run and I hope it does find a nice balance. - It's in a weird place. - You can do faction PVP quests but they're boring - You could make a company but no one will join because the companies that already own towns get benefits - Unless you're 60 you can't get into a war as a "participant" as there is a roster of 50 participants and higher levels are a priority - I did have one fun experience defending a region with a group of 60 from various factions but it's not a common occurrence - Dueling is pretty fun. But their aren't any arena-based PVP to compete in a more practical or competitive environment. -the map varies - some areas are brilliant look the part, easy on the eyes, feel like they're not as big as they are, etc - other areas are nightmares (Weavers Fen and Restless Shores, Brightwood) Even tho the aesthetic of these places is meant to be gloomy or extreme they just feel actually bad to play in. lots of water. no resources. not easy to navigate.  - Territory control is also a thing and I don't even fully understand it and there's not a chance to understand it cos only 5% of the player probably have owned one. (not particularly a bad thing)Overall, the game needs improvement but can be enjoyable if you pace yourself and don't rush. It has a lot of flaws that do hinder you but at the same time, you can still play, it's in a weird place. I honestly don't know who I would recommend this game to, casual play is okay but isn't exactly suitable.But hardcore play feels like it would be draining.Personally, I'm in between and I'm going to have to truly pace myself going onward but I really hope the game does become an enjoyable experience progressing into the late game and with some changes.But I do have to say it's nice to be at the beginning of a new MMO, it has the chance to develop and grow into something polished and cut with a solid player base of casual and hardcore players.I would give this game a rating of  in terms of enjoyment at its current state.BUT it has the potential in the future to be much greater.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a buggy mess with a myriad of problems. Combat is stale and changes very little as you continue progressing through the game, you will consistently repeat the same combos over and over again with little variation in between. The dodge mechanics are utterly worthless when paired with the fact that you can't use them to cancel attack animations and it creates clunky and frankly horrendous content that really just amounts to a level check for the players. It feels like Amazon had no idea what it wanted the identity of the game to be, all Gear is locked behind PVE quests and dungeons, yet there is a very present incentive and attempt (frankly hamfisted) attempt to push PVP on players.Weapon Mastery, Levels, it is all so artificially curated in a very specific linear fashion. Push into PVE quest line until you reach arbitrary level cap, exp gain is snails paced so players won't realize the game has about as much content as most Alphas release with. So you do your town quest boards or faction quests, which are literally like dragging nails on a chalk board.Go find and kill ten undead. Go back to where you killed undead, collect used tampons from chests: so kill more undead gremlins that sound like they were voice acted by Amazon torturing their sweatshop workers. After that, fetch 90 Leather, chasing the Buffalo that can run through water like it was raised as a fish while your character dredges through the water like a zombie at the inertia of the Earth's rotation. Don't even get me started on the amount of walking you have to do whilst looking at the same mind numbing scenery and reused textures. You mean to tell me that they thought we needed a crouch button, a prone button but not a sprint button?We all know mounts are going to be added and Amazon is going to charge half your soul for it. So why not just cut out the middle man and have them day one? The game feels like one gigantic unfinished mess that starts unraveling the more and more you push content. Don't even get me started at how they sold it as a "be anything you want" weapon system where you can just pick them up and use abilities, but the abilities are all conveniently created in such a way that your build still needs to have themes, effectively forcing you into the same exact class system that you'd have in any mmo regardless. Fire/Ice Wizard, Hatchet/Axe Barbarian, Hammer/Sword Tank etc...Unfortunately, due to my own self-loathing I will likely continue playing this game. Anyway, four dollars a pound.

_childDocuments_.review: _______________I hate MMOs. Like I really hate them. I think they're boring and make combat uninteresting with mostly cooldown based encounters. Everything is a roll that happens behind the scenes while I wait for a timer to count down so I can press a button again. Fetch quests get really old very quickly when combat is uninteresting to me. I absolutely understand how people can really enjoy that, but it just not for me. I've tried WoW, Runescape, and a few others but none of them were fun for me at all. The closest I got was playing Destiny 2 heavily for about 3 years.My friend who is a MASSIVE MMO guy told me to get this when it was on sale. He's been BEGGING me to get into one and was determined to find one we could play together with our other friends. I balked at it but he then just straight up gifted it to me bc he was so convinced this was the one for me.And he was right. Q you were right and I hate you so much for making me waste 150 hrs on this stupid game. I'm saying it publicly. You were right.New World is able to make everything I hate about MMOs fun and does a good job with all the stuff I like about them. The early game is a little easy, but it kept me zooming along to new areas. It really helps that the story is pretty engaging! I love Grace O'Malley to death and she is my queen. There's a lot of fun to be had following the main quest surprisingly and it's really refreshing that the game doesn't take itself so seriously. Nothing about the game is obtuse or confusing until the late game once you've sunk a good amount of hours in, and even then it's just fun systems to keep the game interesting. I've had a lot of fun getting into all of that and the late game grind is genuinely fun to do for the most part.Combat requires a little skill with dodging and blocking that is like how Pokemon is a super rudimentary version of turn based JRPGs but with Dark Souls combat. I don't really know if that makes sense, but the combat reminds me a lot of Dark Souls with dodge timing and blocking being crucial to encounters. It's a very very simplified version of it, but it's still really fun since it requires you to actually be invested in combat. There's even entire buffs dedicated to it! There's tons of fun builds to get into and it's pretty easy to respec at any time if you're not vibing with the skills you're rocking. The recent addition of registering gear setups to have on deck at any time makes this even easier to do; providing you with a lot of customization and flexibility for any situation. Getting your loadout just right right around end game is pretty easy and you can usually find something for cheap on the auction house. There's meta builds, sure, but it's still very fun to experiment with the plethora of weapons and skills at your disposal. Amazon tries to keep weapon balance pretty fair and has taken steps to fix broken combos as much as it can. It has resulted in some weapons not feeling very strong, but every one of them still have some sort of usefulness.The trade and crafting systems are a good time but get a little frustrating after a while. Some more advanced materials require a basic material to refine a resource. So to make a higher grade metal, you'll need iron to refine it. Easy enough, right? But there's a bad bot problem at times and basic resources in some areas are completely wiped constantly. I love the mindless grind of collecting resources, but it kills my drive when I see an area totally barren as if locusts have ravaged it dry via biblical plague. It's gotten  better as of late, but I still see it sometimes. It does take a very long time for your skills to grow, so be prepared to dump a lot of time into them if you want some cool stuff. Crafting items don't progress in step with your character progression, which can stifle being able to craft better gear for yourself. I really enjoy being able to craft my own gear to avoid using the trading post or having to grind for better stuff and I can't quite do that here since getting to a high enough level requires A LOT of grinding. Items can be really cheap in bulk via trading, but it's more fun personally to be able to gather it all yourself.Dungeons and social activities are a lot of fun and there's always groups to find if you're playing solo. Most groups I've joined for dungeons have been great and seasoned players have really helped me understand core mechanics a lot better. There's a few raids I haven't done yet, but they're full of simple puzzles and challenging boss fights. They're not exclusive to end game either, with a couple of them scaled to lower levels. These are built right into the main quest to encourage you to actually do them. When you're at the level 60 max and looking for options to grind out better stuff, World Tours (abbreviated to WT in chat) are a great way to do so. If you ever see WT or x for [location], join up for an absolute blast of a time. It's just a  of people running to various combat challenges in the open world to grind for better gear. People have gotten the paths down so well and it's just a game of Lemmings as the horde descends on groups of high level enemies. Def recommend it for any freshly level 60 looking for something to do. I haven't played PvP as it's not my thing, but I'm sure there's a salty teenager who can tell you all about it here in the reviews. There's also factions that you can rep that give you missions and cool gear as well. Players can influence the world through PvP activities or massive co-op activities that can challenge even seasoned players. Sometimes queuing up as a solo or newer player results in being kicked from these, and there's a lot of shadow companies that can make the influence system arbitrary, but Amazon is working on solving that supposedly.After completing the main story, the end game and free expansion content is open to explore. Brimstone Sands is a really cool location and I've had a good time exploring it so far. The recent addition of seasonal content has provided plenty of challenges to keep yourself busy and to push players to experience more of the game than they might have otherwise. The season pass system isn't scammy or scummy. If you're really into the game, worth the price. If you're more casual, don't sweat it as the rewards you get for free are still very good. I've played for about 6 to 9 months and I haven't had a bad time in events either. They're great ways for players new to end game to get tons of easy progression. Plus they can get really silly and goofy by including but not limited to giant killer turkeys, evil rabbits, and massive snow monsters. The only real negative I've experienced via the online experience. servers can be a little wonky with some lag every so often, and the constant merges can get a little annoying.Look, I know I got a lot written here, but I really want to flesh out the experience in case there's people like myself who might pass this up due to a distaste for the genre. All and all, New World is very approachable to anyone looking to get into an MMO. There's a lot here for everyone of all stripes and Amazon is consistently updating it with fun new things to do. I still have more to do and I've already sunk 150+ hours into it already. Thank you to the community in global chat for the laughs and thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: New MMORPG from Amazon.  You're some kinda 16th or 17th century sailor who washes up on the beach of this fancy magical island called Aeternum.  There are no classes or different races playable, everybody washes up as the same boring ol' human with very minimal Player Customization options (many of them quite unattractive).The weapons you use in game are what determine your playstyle- and each is customizeable through leveling up with 3 Ability Slots you can fill with the 6 available options.  You've a mana bar, which some classes use for casting spells, a HP bar, which is health and needs to be >0 at all times or you die, and a Stamina bar, which is used for things like Dodging and Blocking, as well as with some weapon skills for specific purposes.Light / Medium / Heavy armor classes change how much damage you take, as well as each category having a  different amount of +DMG or +CC added to them.  They also change how far you go with your dodge- Light armor can roll away, has +20% Damage, and when they get snuck up on by a great axe, get absolutely trucked.There is a huge amount of grinding in this game, in a gorgeous, immersive, magical land.  All skills are available to the player- all gathering, crafting, and weapon options, and it is only a matter of preference for which one(s) to level and max first.  Logging, Mining, Picking Flowers (harvesting, which uses a Sickle), Skinning, and especially not forgettably, FISHING.  There's a pretty fun fishing minigame, which is also almost entirely playable via sound only, if'n you wanna multibox a video or something.Its still new, and everybody's still learning, but overall I've been having a very good time playing this game so far.  There's complaints I've seen about lack of endgame content, but I'm not anywhere near there yet, won't have my skills maxxed for even longer, and I've seen plenty of things to do (invasions, outside-dungeons, area-chat PvP) so I'm not even slightly worried about it.The only problems I've found so far are with some of the other people playing, and their almost complete illiteracy and inability to think, but that's a problem with people in general and not New World specific.tl,dr:  9.5/10.  Very fun, very grindy, lots of PvP if you like that. No PvP at all if you don't wanna.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the game for over 300hrs at time of writing I have this to say:Ripping the bandaid off first... * Buggy - SO SO many bugs, from UI to actual combat bugs that require to re-log.* Unfinished or missing quests - As of 10/28/21 (at midnight) Quests such as the 580 gear score war hammer chain cannot be completed as the boss you need to kill was removed from the game due to exploits.* Missing content / lack of endgame - Fishing Hotspots are disabled as of typing, Wars are broken to the point that you can lag out the defending team so badly that you can win a fully 50v50 match by keeping 50 attackers on a capture point.  (now that the bandaid is off, let's fix talk about what's good)* The base game and leveling experience - flat out fantastic! you don't notice hardly any of the missing components from the con list as often during the leveling process and it's just a fun NEW experience.* Combat - If you've played Guild Wars 2, the weapons are somewhat like that. You block, roll and attack using stamina or mana. It's a fantastic and well thought out system that works well and feels GREAT!* Gear - You can craft your gear or have it dropped. It's a bit odd that you have intellect and strength on heavy armor or light armor, but if that's the build you want to run as? it's VIABLE! maybe, not so much in PVP at the moment, but play how you'd like!Now with the above being stated, i'd like to say while overall I RECOMMEND New World. I have to seriously urge AGS to listen to the community and squash these bugs NOW. a lot of the negatives can be fixed and save the game, but if they're allowed to continue for more than another few weeks... your playerbase will fall to zero. I like the game greatly, but i fear that it has quickly grown stale due to the fact that it should have been left in the oven for another six months.

_childDocuments_.review: New World has proven to be an outstanding value for the entry cost of buying the game.  Combat is fun but also features depth that comes with time spent.  Roles and responsibilities for difficult or organized group content fall in to the normal, "holy trinity" which consists of healer, tank and damage dealer.  However, I have managed to solo a lot of content with some parts being easy and some being difficult.  Also, its worth noting that there does seem to be some flexibility for hybrid classes.  A healer may be a sub dps character or a tank may deal a significant amount of damage as well.  There are a lot of tools and toys to play with as well as a ton of fun stories to find and experience.  I highly recommend giving this game a try.  The value proposition of the one time purchase to play New World is difficult to beat in a competitive MMO market which consists of, free but not free or, pay for convenience style games.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I had waited for the "right"  middle aged setting MMORPG for many years before joining back into the gaming community. Played Everquest, DAoC, WoW, so I was looking for something that combined those games. This has made the fit!!! I appreciate the intricacies of the armoring/weapon systems, plus the versatility to change between different classes/roles just by the gear you have, you're not stuck in one class ever, so you can gear up to be whatever your group needs... My time fluctuates from a PVP heavy play to PVE heavy play. I find myself enjoying the PVP content much more than PVE, but that's certainly preference. The game is still growing so there are many changes throughout the year, which can go two ways for people... either you like the changes and go with the flow and change up your builds for the new updates or you dislike it and it hinders your progress due to being stuck in the same build, not wanting to make changes or review the updates... I've been on both sides of the fence.. Overall the combat in both PVP and PVE has kept me in. You have to try it to understand it... The game combat is beautiful, the game itself is beautiful. The only downside I will note there are bugs that are being worked through continuously. It can be frustrating at times, but I still spend many hours on the game. The developers have been working through everything and are open to feedback from the community as well. I hope to see this game to grow on for decades such as WoW has...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun with friends don't get me wrong, but the number of exploits and bugs are horrible. It's so bad, that end-game content has just been turned off by the devs and the only thing left is to fight wars with other companies. Even this though comes down to who can exploit the most. I don't even know what to say in this review so I'm just going to go over all the stuff me and my company have discovered. Moving bags with % weight reduction around on your slots will lower the weight of the item over and over until it weighs nothing. For example, you can easily go out for a couple of hours and mine 40000 iron and have it not weigh you down at all. Swapping trophies that give higher gear scores on crafted items over and over in your house does the same thing. You can spend about a day using the exploit above to get a skill to 200 and then craft legendary items with a guaranteed max gear score. I've seen guilds running full Voidbent armor (some the best armor in the game) and the game had not even been out 2 weeks.I'm not 100% how much this game is handled client-side, but it's a lot since you can put your game in windowed mode wiggle your screen around and it will make you invulnerable in the game. Devs said they fixed it, but I still see people standing on points in Wars and you are unable to damage them.Speaking of being unable to damage people in wars. You can lag the war out by having a bunch of people cast ice gauntlets on the points. This will cause everyone to stand still where they are and nothing will happen. All you have to do is move the PvP group to the point, cast ice gauntlets, and get an easy victory.I don't even know at this point what talents and perks are correct and what aren't. It seems like almost none of the values when it comes to armor and weapons do what they are supposed to do. You could lose damage simply by selecting a passive perk in the perk tree that has nothing to do with how hard you hit and you will spend a lot of time, gold, and Azoth trying to get a build that does not gimp you. There used to be items/weapons that you could craft that let you change the secondary item it required. Changing this to a lower-tier crafting item would result in a chance for a lower weapon score, but you could take say a star-metal/orichalcum spear change it to Iron, craft it, and then dismantle it would give you star-metal/orichalcum bars. You could easily generate 1000's end-game materials in no time. I haven't even scratched the surface of bugs and exploits that you can find on youtube. Now to be fair, the devs say they are working on it, and a lot of stuff is getting fixed. The problem is, This stuff was supposed to take a lot of effort and time to get to, and if you are a new person to the game you will be at a severe disadvantage from people who already have maxed their skills and have the best gear in the game. What took people a day will take you weeks, if not months, to reach.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun for a few days, but then the grind just wore me down. It's like this. But even if you hurry up and get to 60, you have to to be CHOSEN to participate in wars. It's entirely possible to spend days grinding up to 60 and still be unable to participate because you didn't make the right connections. Remember, the head of a faction has to SELECT you for you to participate. The head of a faction is only going to do that if you're someone close to them or have a reputation for being a beast in PvP (a reputation you can only get by participating in wars.) PvP was why I was getting into this game, but it becomes clear around level 30 or so that open world PvP is a time waste, and there's no guarantee that your hours of grinding will ever get you into a war sooooo...... Considering the non-stop parade of problems and bleeding players like a scalp wound, I don't see this game still being relevant in a years time. If it is, maybe I'll come back and try it again, but until then, It's a hard pass from me. Game does some things right, but there's too much wrong with it for me to keep coming back and sinking hours into it with no way of knowing if there's any actual fun waiting over the horizon.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful but boring game.The Good:* The game looks pretty decent. The terrain is full of grass, rocks, bushes, it feels real unlike a lot of mmo's where it's just a flat ground with some trees placed around. Long distance scenery looks great and i didn't notice any pop ins. * The crafting system is interesting. Pretty much everything in the game is gatherable for crafting.The Bad:* Boring combat system. This is probably my main reason for not recommending the game. If i had to summarize the combat system i would say it's a discount Guild Wars 2 combat system. You can carry 2 weapons and each weapon has only 3 slots for skills (Total of 6 skills with both weapons). The skills themselves are the MOST UNDERWHELMING SKILLS i have ever seen. Almost every skill i tried was significantly worse than just using a normal or heavy attack. Low damage, high cooldown, useless CC effects. The combat also lacks the feeling of impact and i played with hammer. Enemies barely react to your hits, and CC effects seems just like some visual effect and nothing more.* Gathering materials is a nightmare. Ok so i said the crafting was interesting, unfortunately getting to the crafting is blocked by the longest gathering animations i have ever seen in a game. Several times i just minimize to watch youtube while i chop trees in the game.* The premise/story. Ok so the game starts with you seeking an unexplored land filled with magic and treasures, sounds fun right. An hour into the game the illusion is broken by cities, farms, outposts, factions. For all intents and purposes it's just another island, nothing special about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played over a hundred hours now, when I read the reviews at first glance the overwhealmingly negative reviews are a turn off, but please I implore you don't listen to them blindly. No game is going to be perfect, thats the nature of the industy. However I believe that judging an imperfect game harshly can be a detrimental thing. People argue that there is not a large player base however if all you see are overwhealmingly negative reviews you are not going to give a game a chance. Lets look at no mans sky in this regard. No mans sky was a mess starting out and recieved horrible reviews however after developing a sizable player base the developers did a lot of work on it and it became an amazing game.      I have not encountered bugs in New World as of yet; in fact the game seems to play very well. People argue that they have lost characters however I have yet to experience this bug. People also complain about crashes to desktop i also have yet to experience this. People also complain that there is not a lot of new content i als have to disagree. to this end I will talk about on of my favorite games. SWTOR had a lot of these same complaints, and the releasing of the new content was also excruciatinlgy slow. Howver release new content they did. I looked online and there is a roadmap for new world so they are still planning on releasing new content but the fan base is impatient. I would like to give you all some perspective. what happens when a developer is pressured to release new content? The wish is granted but the content is filled with bugs, and errprs; a good example for thiis is skyrim; it was a very anticipated game during development but the developers were pushed to release it; the outcome was a buggy mess.     Is it not worthwhile to have a poilished game but wait a little longer? That is my mindset. My point is It would be a good thing to give the developers a chance to fix the errors in the game rather than review bombing it into oblivion because of issues that can very well be fixed. Right now at least the game seems to be playable and i for one have been having a lot of fun playing it. Do i want new content? absolutely. Do i want them to fix some of the errors that may pop up eventurally? definately. and I am willing unlike many to play the game while they work on the fixes. i implore anyone who is reading these reviews to please don't give up on this game. we have so few mmmos that are still alive and kicking. The genre is doomed to fail if we don't give the developers the benefit of the doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no need for a lengthy review.The game is a bug-ridden mess with tons of exploits, bots and viruses that can be injected via global chat. By that I mean; this game is not a game, it is a chore. You have to grind to even get a key for a dungeon, you have to grind to fast-travel, you have to grind from the moment you enter the game to when you decide to finally quit in frustration. It isn't an MMO, it is an amazon warehouse simulator.Progression feels like you were dunked into the ocean and have to swim up with weights around your ankles, and occasionally more weights will be added so you're not sure if you are any closer to the surface than you were.The last thing I'll say is the game doesn't even know what it wants to be, does it want to be an adventure RPG with PVP elements or a war-time MMO with some PVE elements, at the moment it struggles to do one or the other as you cannot have both without some level of seperation. _childDocuments_.review: New World is absolutely fantastic -- for a bit. I don't know how AGS has messed this up, but the endgame is just so damn boring. The repeatable "dungeon" content is easily the best part of the game, but it's so expensive to replay them that most of the time you'll only ever do a dungeon a few times and not be able to afford to enjoy it anymore. That alone is ridiculous.PvE is great with friends, but with the recent updates to endgame PvE zones, PvE is *only possible with friends now.* I used to play tank, and while damage output for me pre-patch was scarce, I was able to solo most endgame zones on my own. Now? The enemies can't kill me, but I can't kill them. They are so tanky that it is impossible to kill a single enemy without a group of several. I play this game with friends only, but this presents a new problem: if I were to log on to play solo for a bit to increase my gear score (this game's representation of endgame progression) by looting chests, how am I going to be able to do that when I can't even kill the first enemy at the gate?It would be a disservice not to mention that this game has been riddled with problems since launch and they keep coming. It's a relentless torrent of bugs after bugs after bugs, from infinitely-spawning enemies to enemies who you literally cannot kill because their retreat range is smaller than a thimble. Oh, and that player-based economy? Nonexistent. Constant gold dupes, item dupes, botting for the auction house, and somehow randomly showering players with hundreds of thousands of gold (EU server) means that the game requires constant emergency fixes. To do this, the developers shut down nearly all forms of transacting gold. So now what? Well, during this time you could level up your crafting skills and go gather things -- but wait. They just made crafting even more tedious and difficult to level up. What went from a fun grind became a chore in nearly an instant, and the requirements to level up past the halfway threshold are insanity. If you want to level up all skills to 200 in this current gamestate, either have an entire company help you or shackle yourself to your desk for a few weeks.Last but not least, let's talk about the combat. PvE is seriously fun, again, as the game's combat really is not bad at all. It feels good to smack enemies around and combo them, clear out hordes, and work with your friends to take aggro and demolish a boss. However, because this game is a mixture of PvE and PvP, the balancing is spaghetti. Serious spaghetti. Meta weapons and builds for PvP are untouched while their PvE counterparts get severely nerfed. PvE healing is useless now, but PvP healing is still ridiculous. Fire Staff was great in PvP, and now it's unusable for everything. AGS has the audacity to release a new weapon during this time period when they really need to iron out the balancing first.New World could have been great. My friends and I were addicted for well over 15 days to this game. The team-based gameplay, joining a company and feeling like you're part of a real battalion, is amazing. In the beginning, wars were fantastic. Unfortunately, deaf developers and major bugs going unfixed led to exploits and lag becoming the norm in wars. Where strategy and valor once prevailed, only cheese and the same four weapons and builds remain. It's a travesty. New World had so much potential, and it pains me to see it go down in a ball of fire like this. Maybe one day we'll get something akin to this game with a more competent set of leadership. Maybe New World will be the next No Man's Sky. But for now, New World is neither of those things. New World is an unfortunate failure.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't New World, this is Queue World. It's a sad attempt at an online game from the company who runs some of the best server infrastructure in the world. As of this review, I have 44 hours. More than half of that is waiting in queue, and I'm not even trying to play on any of the streamer-simp servers like Olympus or Valhalla.The combat is passable. Many games in the past have done better at real-time combat. The only thing New World does differently is remove tracking from attacks, since the character models themselves are the hitboxes. Jumping is still weird, though. It's like gravity decides to turn up to 11 when you're at the apex of your jump.PvE is boring and not immersive in the slightest. The story had to have been written by some intern that was rejected by Blizzard, post-Shadowlands. Every enemy model is copy/pasted across every zone, with the exact same attacks from level 1 to 65. Dungeons are uninteresting click-fests, and most players trying to tank just don't bother socketing gems. Even if they did, the aggro mechanic is still busted from beta, so they'll peel off tanks immediately after the taunt ends and bum rush healers.PvP is equally boring. Either you stun-lock your opponent, or they'll simply run away and you can't catch them. If you're roving with a group, you might run into another roving group and take one or two of them before they all run away.The best thing this game has going for it is it's a one-time purchase, and the blind allegiance that Amazon seems to sink their claws into.

_childDocuments_.review: So to get started, the game itself isnt bad, it needs work to make the experience better for the players.Pros:-The crafting system is simple, easy to use, and shows you everything you need-Resources are abundant, and respawn fairly quickly.-Its very easy to meet up with friends and explore together-Combat is quick, easy to learn, and very simple for new players-The trade skills are simple, and only fishing has a mini game involved.-Companies are actually important. There are many mmo games that run their guilds as nothing more than trade factions and pvp groups, but in new world, the companies can take control of cities, building fortifications, giving their factions buffs while in the territory, and upgrading the crafting stations in the cities.-Player Based Economy. There is a player based trade system that functions fairly well. It gives you the freedom to determine how much an item is worth based on how hard it is to get, and not by how much the dev team wants it to be(looking at you black desert online)Cons:-The game has no sprint function or mounts currently. Player movement is far too slow for the insanely huge size of the map.-Town recalling is limited to once per hour. This and the lack of mounts or sprinting make travelling to new questing locations a huge chore.-Range weapons(the bow and musket) require ammunition, and ammunition is fairly rare without actually crafting the ammo yourself.-Quest enemies are difficult to kill because of the literal lines of people waiting for their spawns. a quest to kill sheep for example took nearly an hour to complete because there were large groups of people waiting to kill them for the same quest at their spawn points.-There is a lack of weapon variety, with weapons as the way you get your abilities, they really needed at least 2-3 more weapon types to allow for more build diversity. with only 11 weapon types, it really feels limiting. They could have added 1 more ranged weapon in the form of a single shot pistol, giving each weapon type 3 different options.-The character creator is extremely bare bones. You have a number of face presets, a bunch of hair styles and colors, and you can choose to be male or female. The only good thing about this is that you can add facial hair to the female models if you want to play a feminine looking male character.TLDR: I dont recommend the game, lots of early mmo game mistakes, slow travel system with extremely limited fast travel. If they add mounts, i'd recommend the game as a 6/10, but currently its a 4/10 mmo.

_childDocuments_.review: On reading reviews: don't forget to check hours played. If someone spent 100's or 1,000's of hours on a game, take that thumbs down with a grain of salt. Overall rating: Good | 8/10TL;DR: Fun combat, beautiful scenery, interesting dungeons, but a little grindy and some clear issues that AGS (even as a new studio) didn't address as well as I would've liked.Pros:- Enjoyable action style combat with a lot of emphasis on movement and resource management. If you liked Tera and were sad to see it shut down, this might be worth a shot. - Reasonably balanced (reasonably, not perfectly, don't get salted). Weapon diversity is great. Being able to switch from hammer to axe to sword & shield based on the individual fight is cool, and not feeling like there are clear best weapons by such a margin that others are not viable is a nice feeling.- Classless system with cheap respecs is great. I enjoy being able to swap from a healer to a tank to a glass cannon melee monster without a significant investment of time or resources.- Reasonable content releases. Even though the game has been out less than a year, new content is being released at a decent pace. It could be better, but overall acceptable.Cons:- Poor communication by devs. This got better as time went on, and I give some latitude for AGS being new, but I believe a big reason for the loss of player-base (beyond expected for a new MMO) had to do with unclear communications early on. I think that, if the game survives another year or so, this will likely be changed to a pro if they continue to improve.- Server load/economy/multiplayer content scalability. The game was designed to accommodate ~2k simultaneous players, but it seems they didn't account for the fact that the majority will be max level and trying to do the same pieces of content. This compounded with servers that fell far below that number struggled to maintain cities/crafting stations (an interesting game mechanic in theory) being in a rough spot that left players feeling that the server and/or game was dying. It seems to me that this could have been reworked to adjust to player populations, but instead servers were mashed together leading to new problems.- Toxic communities. I don't fault AGS for this (much) as it's the players who are doing wrong, but it leads to an undesirable outcome to have significant hostility and aggression to new or unskilled players in a game that is designed to be massively multiplayer. If you just want to chill and casually play a game with friends, the impetus is on you to seek our like minded people and build or join that community, which I consider to be an overall negative for a game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like some giant toxic social experiment.   There is so much about this game that I loved in the beginning. It’s beautiful, the sound is exquisite, there was so much to explore, crafting was gonna be of value, and the PvP was gonna be great. But there is some much about it that is toxic, downright unhealthy right now.1. Nothing good happens. It’s not the grind thats the problem, its the lack of positive rewards. There are lots of grind games out there, some of them adorable - Star Dew Valley, Animal Crossing come to mind - and what they have that this game doesn’t is positive feedback/rewards. Yes, you get stuff from chests and sack drops, but most of it is junk that you end up salvaging. Nothing positive comes from leveling crafts - nothing much sells in the AH and with a few exceptions, most of what you can make is pretty useless. Nothing good happens. Get a house? Pay taxes, grind furniture, it isn’t fun.2. Selfishness is rewarded, teamwork not at all. In another game I won’t name, when you fish with other people, the odds go up that you’ll get better fish. In NW, if other people show up at the hotspot you’re fishing, they just get fish you would have gotten if they weren’t there. You get the behavior you reward. In this case, it is better to fish alone than to fish with others. Pulling mobs to grief other players is being used for entertainment or for taking nodes, ganking people farming isn’t good PvP - its cowardly, selfish behavior and this game now officially rewards it. You get the behavior you reward and NW rewards selfishness and griefing.3. Bots, cheating, exploiting, mass reporting - the game design, bugs, and problems seem to bring out the worst in people and the lack of integrity in part of the player base (part not all) is alarming to me. It ought to be possible to design a game that provides solid competitive play without cheating. Cheating isn’t getting gud. Exploiting isn’t getting gud. It’s just nasty behavior. And being around it just makes me feel sad.PvP - I had hoped for some solid, team based PvP in NW and I was sorely mistaken. PvP in NW is just a free for all and if you farm enough and do the math, you too can run amok. That’s not about skill, it’s not about teamwork, it’s not about being competitive. For some people, I guess, thats fun. For me, not so much.So, I hope things change for NW in the future, I’ll probably log on to explore from time to time, but the madness has to stop.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there, I believe I have one of the highest play hours in game till now and I wish to help you before you purchase this "New World".As MMORPG which is supposed to have a concept and nice PvP, I rate this game to be; PvP: 3/10PvE: 2/10Fishing: 10/10Crafting: 7/10Company/Territory Claiming Idea (System is ridiculously bad though): 8.5/10Abstract: I believe this game has a lot of potential with a lot of new aspects of MMORPG however it's poorly designed to give much about concept and PVE. Spending time here is only getting worse however there are cool things to do makes it chaotic to understand if it's good or not UNTILL you hit 60 and grind for something ridiculous called Gear Score which gives a little extra help for End game activies.Pros: Unique territory claiming designs, governing cities with your friends or warriors with companies. Very cool ambiences, sounds of nature, animals, a lot of places to discover, good fishing spots, all harvesting, fishing, hunting, mining, are satisfying. And you can specialize in some crafting skills although you need to touch or grind other crafting skills as well for only one. Cons: PVP is ridiculously bad first of all open world PVP is limiting players to "enable" their PVP through the open world when they hit 60. PVP is one of the most important thing to keep MMORPGS alive in ENDGAME. And in New World you only PVP to get territorities which gives a little for a player who is already 60. There's no ranking system in PVP, no unique title for killing enemies, no rewards for killing enemies only a hundred or two hundred token for each enemies killed. The wars for claimiing cities are limited to 50vs50 which is also ridiculous.There's an influence system that allows you to declare war on cities which you can increase by doing PVP quests in few areas by enabling PVP. Which leads all factions to do all these quests instead of attacking each other defending or sieging the forts or settlements. Why would you give all factions same quests instead just let one of them and give different to other factions so it makes sense to fight...There is no PVE, there's no concept for Main Story quests, there are some boss that people kill only for Gear Score and some legendary items. There's not much to talk about PvE since this game wasn't even supposed to do PvE's I guess but still..Let us talk about "NO MOUNTS" well. This really turned a lot of people down. Walking simulator is not something everyone loves to play is it?

_childDocuments_.review: - no variety regarding the quests (kill or gather supply crates)- hardest grind ever, if you want to master only a single profession- bugfixes lead to new bugs (that harm the whole economy)The game was quite interesting at the very beginning, but only because it was new and you didn´t know the mechanics.The problem starts, when you reach the first town, then the grind starts.Everything gets repetetive, no matter if it is the main quest, side quests, crafting, gathering etc.A serious example for my "favorite" side quest:1. Walk to 3 different obelisks, check the crates on top and return2. Walk to 3 different obelisks, check the crates on top and return3. Walk to a specific area to kill some mobs4. Walk to 3 different obelisks, check the crates on top and return5. Walk to a specific area to kill some mobs6. Walk to 3 different obelisks, check the crates on top and return7. Followup-Quest for the first dungeonSummarizing, the whole game consists of two different quest types (no matter if main, side, town or any other quest type...:1. Kill specific enemies2. Browse supply crates for specific quest itemsCrafting seemed to be very promisingly, since you can master every profession.The usage of higher-tier materials was improving the gear score and you were able to get better results for the crafted equipment.But after reaching 75 / 200 skilllevel, you either have to start grinding for materials or you buy the equipment from the auction house.Example here is for leveling your engineering skill from 150 - 200 you need :1. Ironwood (T5-Wood) = 536372. Wyrdwood (T4-Wood) = 618893. Aged Wood (T3-Wood) = 463594. Green Wood (T2-Wood) = 92.7165. and other components6. plus the crafting fee, depending on the taxes, you pay to the current cityThis vast amount of wood, combined with the fact, that you get averagely  10 - 30 wood from one tree means, that you would have to (find and) cut down something about 12.000 trees...Last topic is the update-behavior of this game:Every update they implement, leads to new bugs which destroy the economic (gold-, item-dupes) or forces the developer to disable single modules of the game until the next patch (Auction-House, Item-Trading in general, Server-Transfer...)
