_childDocuments_.review: Hey, since i am waiting again in the queue for the open world, i thought i could write a review.First of all u have to know, that i am not the usual mmo rpg player. Normally i play shooter, mobas, tactical and singleplayer games, so this is my first MMO ever. Because some of my friends started to play New World i thought i could give it a try.Please remind i can only talk about my experiences so far.Servers:- Once the Server is full (which will happen in 1-2 weeks) u have queue waiting times between 20 and 80 min after 4pm in ur Region- Sometimes the Servers LagQuests:- There are only 2 Types of Quests beside the main story:         - Go where and loot amount x chests         - Go where and kill amount x enemies- These 2 Types of Quests make up at least 80 procent of the quests- Some other examples would be, get 80 wood/iron/fiber or catch a big salmonCombat PvE:- The combat system is quiete clunky- The person who deals the most dmg is always targeted first, which means if u play a dps mage build (ranged) and u deal the most dmg the mobs will target u, until somebody else deals more dmg than u- That means if u dont have any player in ur group who has a specific attribute on his equipment, the mobs will follow the rule aboveCombat PvP:- I didnt play any war until now, but i played some quest pvp- In my opinion the PvP has a huge potential but it is highly dependent on the level of each player- A lvl 20 player doesnt have a chance against a lvl 30 playerXP for Weapons:- To level up ur weapons u have to dmg enemys- U only get the XP and weapon XP, if u dealt a set amount of dmg- that amount lies round about 15% max health of the target or at least 3 hits- which means if u play healer and only heal ur mates u dont get any XP if u dont deal at least some dmg with ur autos- That also means if a boss spawns and there are 10 players around who wanna kill him sometimes u have to kill him 3 times to get the quest done, bc u couldnt deal enough dmg before he is deadCONCLUSSION:I think this game has a great potential.But because of the mentioned things above and the noticeable amount of bugs it feels like its still early access. If they fix all these things i would consider to recommend the game. But paying 40€ for a game which isn´t out of early access state (in my oppinion) is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to the player-based economy but I didn't do enough research beforehand to find out it is broken. It was a good learning lesson on what I need to study in greater detail next time when a game claims to have a "player-driven economy". The value of everything is just crashing down to near 0.01, unless the items are super-rare finds that you probably have to grind hours and hours just to find one of them. There are numerous reasons that are discussed in length online if you google "new world game economy is broken". The biggest thing for me personally is that anyone can be any profession unlike in classic World of Warcraft which limited how many primary professions you can take. Players are not going to value the things you gathered and crafted if they think they can just do it themselves instead, thus making trading between players grind down to a slow halt. Hardly a "player-driven economy" that I had envisioned.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: game is heavy in crafting and actually does a really good job on it. visuals are beautiful and very detailed. combat is not tab targeting and allows you to dodge and block. the game has no classes so you just lv up weapons you want to be good at. Overall stability and game play are very solid.Cons: There is no form of transportation aside from fast traveling which takes azoth and that takes time to get. Aside from the cut scene in the start of the game and the trailer the game has no story line what so ever and you will never get a cut scene or anything tying into the story line even when playing main story line quests. Combat is good but basic and the game highly favors PVP over PVE. Town board quests give more xp then faction or main quest by a long shot. Servers cap at 2,000 people which is why the wait times are so bad. Overall Amazon had an idea of what an mmorpg was but not really. ffxiv has server player caps of 18,000 while New World only has 2,000, hints the long wait times. the way they have done the attributes is terrible. it has nothing to do with how fast you hit or the power of your swing as much as health and specific weapon damage. No classes means you can literally just spend the time to lv up a ton of weapons and get really good while switching on the fly. NO STORY LINE WHAT SO EVER, no form of transportation. expensive fast travel fees and no clear way of how you obtain azoth. IN NO WAY WILL THIS BE A FFXIV KILLER. They need to raise the server cap by double as the very first thing. having no lore, beyond the trailer and start of the game and also having no classes or diffrent races makes the game boring quick. i do enjoy playing it and i hope they can fix this quick because they really dont have much time before the hype calms down and people get annoyed as the launch was similar to Cyberpunk 2077 with many not able to play. I love hate the game as of now.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have been enjoying this game I cannot in good conscience recommend it.EVERY SINGLE PERSON I KNOW WHO HAS PLAYED THIS HAS HAD SEVERE ISSUES WITH STABILITY.It does not matter how strong your PC is or what OS you are running this game will crash, this game may fail to launch, this game may fail to load communication within it.I have the most stable experience out of my friend group and I do not have the most powerful PC in the group, I also run linux so minor tinkering was needed to run at first. When an unsupported platform is the only one that doesn't crash like clockwork then I see that as an issue. Normally I wait a long while before reviewing mmorpgs however due to the performance I am making an exception. I am barely into the game having played for less than 3 days and only having reached the first major town. First lets get the major bad thing other than the performance out of the way, the character creator. When you first make a character expect to see less options than the repeatedly rereleased skyrim, this char creator is trash. While we're on the topic of customisation lets talk about armour. You cannot turn in game armour into a cosmetic item to place over other armour. There are dyes to change colours though so that's something and you can get cosmetic armour from the cash shop to put over your in game armour (but screw you if you like in game armour and want to use that as a cosmetic). Some icons do not match the appearance of the items so be careful. Housing customisation is also something you can do but I have extremely limited interaction with this system as of review time.The crafting and gathering is intuitive mostly. Gear has durability and needs repairs. Exploring the land is satisfying (better than ffxiv but not as good as archeage). Having quests voiced is a nice touch. There are some great accessibility features. Had a couple of fun sidequests already. I can't really say much for the story because I got distracted by collecting materials to craft with. Personally I greatly enjoy being able to wander off like a toddler in a candy shop. Also there are instruments and sheet music. Music performance opens up a minigame and gives buffs. It looks like you cannot write your own sheetmusic so that sucks but otherwise it's pretty good (unless you have lots of lag).As much as I have enjoyed this game so far I doubt it will ever live down its reputation for destorying gpus at luanch and being a glitchy broken game to this day. If you read this review thinking about buying it please do yourself a favour and wait for it to be at least 50% off. Remember to check 3rd party sites like humble bundle, do not pay full price for this as of review date.I am only playing this because archeage died (TERA doesnt exist anymore) and I'm waiting for Ashes of creation and the riot mmo.

_childDocuments_.review: After taking a break from this game for a year, I decided to come back and try it out with my friends. 169 hours later.. the game is way better. They fixed a good number of the issues I had with the game from launch. Don't get me wrong the game still needs some work, but its way better then it was so that's a good thing. They removed tuning orbs for dungeons (left them in for Trials) but this means you can actually farm dungeons with friends without having to grind hours and hours to get a single attempt. They are still missing mounts and a few base features like character customization, gender change, name changes. They have added a lot of new way points but still requires a lot of pointless running around. The monsters in the game still sprint full speed underwater, and you can get CC locked by mobs if your not careful. The server stability still needs a bit more work, but overall the game is pretty fun now. I'm glad i decided to give it a try again.

_childDocuments_.review: AGS really needs to address the damage this game is doing to people's hardware. I've been very cautious while trying this game out and even while setting my GPU's power limit to 80% it still frequently spikes to 110%. This is the only software I have ever seen cause this kind of behavior, and the fact that Amazon game studios is denying the issue is extremely frustrating. While many graphics cards will survive, the stress this is putting on VRM's is reducing the lifespan of people's GPU's, and in many cases this goes unnoticed. There is no reason for a game to cause 110% power draw when GPU usage is not capped, a lot of times my utilization was in the 70-90% range. The EVGA situation was more susceptible to this, but the underlying cause is still prevalent.If you are going to try this game, get software that can lower your GPU's power limit, and lower it by 20-30%. Just know that this software is damaging your graphics card if it doesn't cause it to outright fail.The gameplay is decent, I wouldn't say it's on par with many AAA releases, but it does offer some fun. I just don't think the gameplay justifies risking my graphics card at this time. If they look into and attempt to fix the game I may consider putting more time and possibly money into it to support them, but as of right now this is some of the shadiest activity I've seen from a game studio to date. EA might prompte gambling to kids but this is damaging people's property that they have worked hard to get, and denying it.Update: AGS still hasn't even began to look into the hardware damaging massive power spikes that players dont know about until their GPU fails. They've had multiple terrible patches that destroyed the economy, made crafting practically pointless with scaling, and intentionally sabotaged the only overlay minimap because a handful of people were throwing a tantrum. I regret that I bought this, it is an absolute train wreck. The only people giving positive reviews are in denial and simping for amazon, clinging to the hope that maybe their few weeks of playing 18 hours a day will be relevant. This game is dying, fast, and hopefully they take a loss on it overall, I may find some peace if that happens. Do NOT buy this game, it may entertain you for 10 hours or so but AGS will make sure to patch any enjoyment you have out of the game and break twenty things in the process.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun with friends and nothing beyond that. The PVP between factions for territories ends up harming everyone by destroying crafting stations in town. It is difficult to be almost max level but not being able to craft equipment for myself. In the same way its difficult to store all resources in town storage because not being able to refine materials down due to crafting stations not being upgraded. The game changes detection range and respawn rates in some zones and primarily after level 40. With those changes, it becomes very difficult to solo as enemies previously defeated will respawn and chase/shoot you from their own area. There is a very harsh fast travel system and no auto path to a next town. Auto run is a joke that will get stuck on a skinny tree or rock. Low level zones are thrown into the middle of the world map with higher level zones on most sides and so it makes travelling between zones an even bigger hassle. First come first serve resources create a massive opportunity for griefing and bot abuse. It is 2000 max concurrent players per server. There is no guarantee that all servers will continue to get new players. I can't imagine the in-game market will continue to be profitable enough to pay for property tax on 3 in game houses.

_childDocuments_.review: I am having so much fun!I really enjoy exploring/wandering in games, and I love gathering and crafting. I am having a whale of a time right now seeing a point on the horizon and just going out and finding it. I like the climbing. And the game is just BEAUTIFUL. I only have the graphics on medium I think as my pc is getting a little long in the tooth, but the views in the wilds are just breathtaking and so immersive. I could do nothing but wander for days and be blissfully happy.The game music is also very beautiful and really adds to the feel of the game. All the little incidentals and background noises really make you feel like you're in a living world.I've played just about every MMO out there over the years (excluding the Eastern ones). I've done Guilds/Orgs/etc to death and these days I mostly enjoy doing my own thing. You may think an MMO is not for me any more, BUT I really like playing AMIDST people. It makes a game feel more alive than just playing a single player game. Having said that, it looks like there's plenty for me to do if I do want to do any peopling, and it all seems optional. I'm sure there would be things I would miss out on if I don't opt to people, but it's nice to know I don't have to as you can do the whole story of the game on your own if you want to experience the story which is GREAT. No classes, you just level any of the skills you want and pick which ones you like best. No other races, only humans, and although the time period is not one I would normally gravitate towards, you know what it's really refreshing.And hands down my FAVOURITE part of the game - player musicians! Other games have tried it and never quite got it right, but New World absolutely nails it! Everyone can play any of I think 5 different instruments and it's a bit like a guitar hero minigame. You choose your music piece, choose which instrument part you want to play (other people can join you with other instruments if you want) and then you begin and do your best not to mess up. Players can tip you if they like your performance and you get a small buff of your choosing once you have finished playing. The songs are really genuinely very good and there are lots of them (which you collect) so if you come across a pack of minstrels it doesn't get repetitive. A genuinely delightful part of the game and I'm having a blast with it.Second favourite thing, and something I love in all MMOs - FISHING! And they've made it a little more involved than click the bobber, you have to hook the fish then real it in without snapping your line. Once you've caught your fish (or boot or whatever else) you hold it up (allowing you to screenshot if you want:P) and the fish LOOKS LIKE THE REAL FISH! If you catch a pike it looks like a pike. Catfish? Looks like a catfish. Piranha? From the lake you were just swimming in? Piranha.I have been on the fence about getting this game for so long due to all the negative reviews and bad press, but I'm SO glad I took the chance because this is the most fun I've had in quite a long time. I can see myself playing this for ages, so much so that I've decided to upgrade my PC (a little) so it runs better (I'm below minimum spec on the CPU, but by  George it's giving it all it's got).If you're on the fence, give it a shot. It's different. It's fun. It's a refreshing change (like that cider advert says).I'm going to go see what that is over there...

_childDocuments_.review: Explore a massive, beautiful, open world and uncover the secret truth of the Eternal Island and its strange inhabitants. The illustrious and proud cliffs upon which King Artorius founded his kingdom. The rocky terrain throughout is dotted with mines, and a newfound threat from Corruption. Lush pastures and deep woods fill a land that Medea strode through and tended in olden times. Upon the hills, broken windmills wait to turn once again to feed the starving masses. Eternally autumnal, trapped for better and worse on the edge of a winter that will never come. Here there is also a small yet important shrine for the Angry Earth, guarded by nature itself. Though once a bastion of hope and light for the inhabitants of the island, these forests have turned feral and dim. A horrible legacy is buried underground, still echoing into the present. Sodden and swampy, with a hint of plague lingering on the edge of perception. The architecture of the Ancients has fallen into disuse here, where the Corpse Crone resides.

name: Tamarin
detailed_description: Explore, leap and shoot to save your family from the insect invasion! Leap into action and discover nature in Tamarin, a third-person action-adventure game set in beautiful Nordic scenery, starring the world's cutest monkey. Pollution and destruction from ever-expanding insects sets the agile monkey into a fight for his family’s survival. Explore an incredible interconnected 3D world, brimming with primate platforming and bug-splattering shooter action. Leap with the agility of a tamarin as you journey into the Northern wilderness on scenic routes through forests, fjords and mountains. Along the way you will chase mysterious electrical fireflies, discover a secret underground world of dancing ants, rescue innocent birds, and restore the tamarins’ once idyllic natural habitat.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly what kills the game entirely is its high pricetag, it is way overpriced for what it is, I refunded after playing for over an hour discovering clipping issues and even at one point I escaped the map just by simply jumping over a wall. The shooting segments bring the platforming skills to a complete halt as the mechanics of the game completely change between the segments of shooting and platforming. There are also some very baffling design choices when it comes to the platforming it self. Like being able to jump to certain ledges but the only visual indication that you can do such things is a huge arrow that breaks the fourth wall as if to say "You can jump to here using our weird pounce mechanic dumby" but if that arrow isn't there, you can not jump that far on your own which is super baffling.There is no buildup to the story at all, I have no idea who I am or where this is and why I should even care. This game could of used a calm period intro before having the insects destroy everything so I could feel more invested and maybe even care about the characters.The protagonist has absolutely 0 personality other than looking cute. And that's what this is, they focused on looks first and everything else second, wait for a sale at the very least cause the price they are asking for is not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW EDITED NOW THAT I AM FINISHED WITH THE GAMETamarin is a game I was looking forward to for a while now. It's a game made by ex-Rare devs, and serves as a spiritual successor to Jet Force Gemini. I was hyped after seeing the trailers, and was honestly hoping this game would one of my favorite's of the year. Now that the game is out, I find Tamarin to be a mixed bag of a game. I found Tamarin to be a game that is fun, and has a lot of charm, but also suffers from some wonky platforming and aiming controls, frame issues, has a camera that takes some time to get used to, and suffers from some disappointing design choices (no final boss, combat and platforming levels separate not together, no completionist reward for collecting everything, etc). The game is very similar to Jet Force Gemini though. The enemy designs are almost exact. The shooting and aiming mechanics feel lifted from JFG. The enemies can kill the birds you need to save, like the enemies in JFG kill the Tribals. If you are looking for a JFG experience, this does a good job of it. But that also means it feels dated in the process. Tamarin FEELS like a N64 game, for better or for worse. Despite some wonky platforming, "dated" shooting combat, and a weak end game - there is fun to be had in Tamarin. If you know what you're getting into, and understand this isn't going to feel like a modern platformer, that you'll be getting a N64/Jet Force Gemini like experience, I recommend playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Force Gemini is still my favorite game for the Nintendo 64. This game quite clearly takes much inspiration from that game. The ants are pretty much asset rips including the sounds they make. And they even copy JFG's intro scene where it tells you about the enemies, item pickups, and who you need to save.Unfortunately it's lacking many options. Here is a picture of ALL the options: The game now has a warning on the Steam page that keyboard and mouse are not supported. That warning wasn't there when the game initially released, nor when I bought it soon after, and not when I made this review. Given the fact that they've had 7 years to develop this game and have put it on the pc, not including decent pc controls is still valid criticism.-Unable to turn on inverted controls for controller. Aiming is baffling inverted when using the mouse; can't change this either.-You can't even see what the keyboard or controller buttons are, and certainly you can't rebind them. With a controller plugged in the game does tell you what controls do what as you play.-If you have no controller plugged in and start the game, the game tells you that keyboard and mouse is limited and to plug in a controller. I prefer to play shooters with a mouse so this is disappointing.-You can't adjust the camera turn speed using the controller or mouse.-Lockon didn't seem to work right for me; it only seems to work on the purple sniper ants and not the blue ants. I don't know if this is on purpose or not. EDIT: it's supposedly on purpose. Ok then.-There is no autoaim like in JFG which wouldn't be a problem if we had smooth aiming controls, but we don't.-You lose air when swimming on the surface of normal, drinkable water. Why? You also have this tiny pathetic jump while in the water which means you can only leave the water at certain spots, adding to the frustration of falling in.-Not necessarily a fault of the game, but I wish they would add in at least the option to have cartoonish blood splatter like in JFG which was tons of fun. As it is now there are no blood splatters at all, although you can dismember the ants. Further disappointing is that the bodies disappear way too fast like in JFG, but where JFG had the excuse of limited hardware we don't have that excuse or limitation anymore. EDIT: People are saying there is blood and one even showed a screenshot. Well for me the first ants you meet didn't bleed even when I shot its head off and somehow made another explode. If it is there it needs to be more obvious.+I do like the cuteness contrasted with the violence of shooting ants. As I said above I wish it was even more extreme with blood. Graphics seem fine to me too; I don't generally care about such things as long as it's not blurry.Normally I wait to refund and leave a negative review, wait to give the devs time to acknowledge the problems and work on a fix. However the devs have been virtually absent from Steam, having only responded a few times and done nothing else here. So I don't trust them to be quick with these issues, and I have my doubts if they will even care at all and fix them. So I'm not waiting around and have already refunded.I cannot recommend this game in it's current state. Only when it's on sale and only if they bother to patch these issues. $40 usd is too much for what the devs have described as a 10 hour experience if you 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Awww this looks like a cute platformer…SUDDENLY GUN!!Daf*q this dude is a real gangsta!! They had us on the first half of the game, not gonna lie.Dev 1: I wanna make a childs game with cute and fluffy animals.Dev 2: But all children like to do nowadays is shoot things.Dev 1: Say no more!The game went from Crash Bandicoot style to Fortnite style in a few seconds.Tamarin is the spiritual successor to Jet Force Gemini. More specifically, it’s like Jetforce Gemini if the natives picked up a gun and didn't need the trios help.I love this game. Is it perfect? No. I have some frame drops here and there, the shooting controls and camera could be better BUT for an indie developer’s first game ever, it’s wonderful. Its cute, beautiful, has fun mechanics and a great world to explore. Soundtrack is great. It’s a platforming collectathon with some shooting elements. If you were a fan of old school Rare games on the N64, specifically Jet Force and Banjo then you'll enjoy this game. If playing waifu sim games and Minecraft are your thing then there probably isn't much here for you. Also, you can't knock David Wise's musical prowess in this game! It screams classic DK and yooka laylee vibes. If you are a fan of Banjo, Jet Force Gemini, Ratchet and Clank, I highly recommend it!7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Mind bogglingly mediocre. The worst part about Jet Force Gemini was the constraints of the N64 controller, but this game retains the aiming quirks that game had to make up for the controller, with really strange and frustrating auto-aim and a crosshair that moves within the screen. Why can't it just control like any modern third person shooter?And while keeping all the problems of JFG (and adding more) it retains none of the originality and charm. This feels like a student project by fans of Jet Force Gemini and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a sucker for 3D platformer games, I cannot recommend this game to anyone at all.  From a glance it looks like fairly decent platformer mixed with some intense shooting action but instead it's a frustratingly flawed piece of garbage.  I'll list off some good and bad points.  I'll also try and not compare this game to Jet Force Gemini too much because I don't think it's all that fair to make comparisons between two different games and judge it for not living up to that expectation, but it'll be hard not to since there are quite a few similarities, almost straight rips from JFG even.The plot of the game is that you and your Tamarin family of four are living happily in your forest like any other day.  Until the Insekt army begins their conquest of the world and expansion of their Queendom and your family is separated and captured.  Now it's your job to go out and rescue them while fighting through hordes of ants and along the way must rescue birds and collect Fireflies to advance further.  Now the game is split up into two sections.  The exploration platforming section, and the combat section.  You won't always have your weapons with you because as the game will tell you, they're too heavy to jump around with.  So you'll have set worlds where you can explore and jump around while collecting Fireflies and levels where you fight the ants while rescuing birds.Alright good points first.*GraphicsThe graphics are aesthetically pleasing and combined with the ambiance it's rather relaxing.*SoundtrackWhile the music isn't really out of this world it's easy on the ears.  The exploration music fits the atmosphere and the combat music is pretty good and fits the tension.  Okay now the bad points.*PlotThe story of the game is pretty bare bones.  Peaceful life is ruined by bad guys and now you must go save your loved ones.  That alone is sums up the whole plot right there.  The Insekt army shows up, you go around a few levels grabbing Fireflies to advance further and rescue your family one by one and then the credits roll.  No special ending or anything.  As soon as you save the last member the invasion is over.  At least you assume it's over because it ends with just you and your family playing and relaxing at home.  I guess the ants just decided to leave after losing their last prisoner.  And that's really it.  There's no special characters you meet apart from the hedgehog who helps you out every now and then, no in depth lore on the world around you, no explanation about the Insekt army with their society, structure and origin.  Only that they're just expanding their Queendom and consuming resources and it's ruled by two queens who don't even have proper roles in the game like you'd think they would.  They're spoken of only once and you see them only once at the very end of the game.  They also don't serve as the final bosses, in fact there are no bosses.  Instead the queens only serve as obstacles blocking a switch for a cell door that has one your family members inside.  Yeah I was really disappointed lol.*ControlsAt first the controls seem okay.  Movement is alright, so far so good.  Until you have to start jumping or fighting, you know, the main things in the game you're supposed to do.  I'll start with the platforming part.  You can barely control your jumps in mid-air which makes precision platforming frustrating.  It's almost like you have a set jumping path that you have to fight every time you want make a certain jump.  And if you do manage to fight it, you undershoot your jumps and fall to your death.  Now the combat part is where I think the game fails the most.  Your worst enemy isn't the Insekt army no, your worst enemy and greatest challenge are the controls for shooting.  Let me explain.  While in shooting mode you're limited to just normal not so high jumping so your primary focus is on shooting.  In order to shoot, you have to hold down the left trigger to bring up the cursor.  You then use the right thumb stick to aim the cursor around and pull the right trigger to shoot.  Sounds easy enough right?  Well every time you move, the aiming cursor resets to the center of the screen.  And when you're getting shot at you kinda wanna keep moving while also fighting back.  But if you want to do that you have to pick a fight with the aiming cursor first because it's a struggle to keep the cursor where you want to aim while it's constantly resetting to the center anytime you budge an inch and the control for it is very stiff.  This is a major flaw in the game, especially for the part people look forward to the most.  Jet Force Gemini had the same problem but the cursor was easier to control in that and much more manageable.  The game even lets you lock on to enemies like snipers who are above you because the game itself knows that mechanic sucks.  The only way you'll be able effectively fight is if you take your time, stand still and line up a single target.  That or just frag them all with grenades but you don't get those until near the end of the game.*Limited WeaponsThere are only five weapons in the whole game: the Uzi which is just a pistol with a short burst of fire at the beginning of each shot, the machine gun, the rocket launcher, shurikens and grenades.  Most of these weapons are situational, I found myself using the Uzi the most as well as the shurikens because they can destroy metal shields the ants carry like the ones from Jet Force Gemini.  The machine gun is inaccurate and the rocket launcher you don't get until the very last level so I didn't get much use out of it except for special switches.  The grenades are used for destroying wooden doors/walls mostly but they have their use in combat.  The game is pretty short but it would've been nice to have more of an arsenal to choose from.*Firefly GlitchYou need to catch Fireflies in order to open doors to advance further in the game like Power Stars and Jigsaw Pieces.  But in order to grab a Firefly you have to lock onto it and jump at it.  Kinda stupid by itself really, why can't you just walk into it to grab it?  Anyway, there were several times when I found a Firefly, locked onto it and jumped only to pass through it.  I could never get it no matter how many times I tried unless I left the world entirely and came back to it.  This was infuriating especially when you work hard to unlock it, like doing those stupid coin trail challenges, only to the have the game tell you that you simply can't have it even though you earned it.  A problem that probably could've easily been fixed if you could just walk into it.  There's also trying to save birds from execution but the game gives you barely enough time to get to them and kill the ants before they shoot them.  There's also a glitch where after killing a certain number of ants, a small cut scene will play showing the door you just unlocked, but during this time the ants can still execute the birds so you're unable to do anything.  I tried to 100% the game but because of these glitches I couldn't.  *Short GameI have 9 hours on record but that's because I tried to 100% the game.  But you can actually beat it in about 3-4 hours.  Considering the price and just the overall idea of the game I didn't expect a long adventure but still that's rather short for a 3D platformer.  That's all I can really say about Tamarin.  If you still want to give it a try, my advice would be to keep expectations low and wait for a sale to be just as low.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying this doesn't fully scratch the itch left by Jet Force Gemini, but it's a pretty good game otherwise. It's split between shooting levels and exploration levels. Honestly, I thought the exploration would just be interludes between ant annihilation, but I'm actually quite enjoying them.~PROS~* Graphics are decent.* Environments are lush and interesting.* Level design is fantastic. Some solid, 3D platforming, very reminiscent of the N64 era.* No map. Some players may find this difficult, and it is, but I find it refreshing. You really have to remember where you're at/where you're going.* Music is amazing! Not quite as driving as JFG, more whimsical like Banjo.* The difficulty is perfect! No hand-holding and there will be many times where you may be lost, but finding your way is that much more satisfying. It's not too difficult to avoid taking damage, which is good because there are very few health pickups through. If you come across crates, destroy them!* Minus the camera, controls are great (no kbm, keep in mind).~CONS~* The camera controls really frustrating. No choice for invert or speed and it recenters *aggressively*, even when aiming/shooting, making it difficult. It's bugged out a few times and even gotten me stuck.* The options are.. sparse. 1080p maximum resolution (but with 200% resolution scaling, which works nicely). NOTE: You CAN modify the settings.ini file, or local user_settings.config to toggle significantly more graphical options.* Not a lot of explanation. Which I'm partially fine with, reminds me of older games, but there are a LOT of collectibles and for a bit you don't even know what they're for.* Very short for the cost, unfortunately.* Though the levels are beautiful, there are some points, particularly during the exploration bits (and most notably in caves) where it's kind of... sparse. Many many empty rooms that look they could have had something but just.. don't.Overall, I really love it. It doesn't *feel* like Jet Force Gemini 2, but there are SO many callbacks and references (favorite one probably being the ant death sound being the same!).

_childDocuments_.review: Tamarin is a third-person action game about a fluffy monkey fighting for its home.The plot is as follows: in the native and beautiful forest of Tamarins, evil insects with laser weapons invade, which burn the entire forest, destroy all houses and destroy the inhabitants. After that, the forest is just teeming with armed ruthless insects that begin to build huge factories, polluting all around the nature. Along the way, our hero Tamarin meets an interesting character hedgehog, who will help us fight insects and warns us that we will not survive empty-handed and gives us his first weapon with which we will destroy pests.Our main task is to explore and free the forest from dangerous insects, while saving civilians and collecting crystals and valuable resources that will help us survive. On the way, we will meet mysterious electric fireflies that will help us discover the secrets of the underground world of evil ants.Enemies are divided into several types: ordinary enemies with guns, flying drones that move in groups and are very dangerous, enemies-snipers who are on high ground and can shoot with one well-aimed shot. Also, during the passage, we must save the innocent inhabitants of the forest of birds who are in trouble and need to release them, thereby restoring the natural habitat.Personally, I really liked the visual children's style and pleasant sound design. It is worth noting that playing this game is best with the controller/joystick.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely feel like like writing reviews, but here's my opinion on this game based on roughly an hour into the game, because i feel like the trailers don't represent my experience of the gameplay at all.In short:+ Charmingly designed cute characters+ fitting sound designo Okay platforming movement.o Visual styleo Okay graphics- Really uninteresting areas- Terrible lock-on aim- Restrictive moveset while holding gun- Obvious general lack of polish- Crazy high pricetagIn longer:Not having played Jet Force Gemini ever, i didn't really have specific expectations for the game. Off of the trailers I was under the impression that they put a lot of effort into the platforming, and well, when the game started out the platforming felt alright. Everything in the movement has been in other games, which obviously doesnt have to be bad. Sadly literally no part of the movement feels particularly interesting - especially weird though feels how they make the shooter parts so that you just dont have 90% of your movement skills.The shooter part seems very uninspired and lame from the first moment on. Enemies either fall like flies or are bullet sponges. Feedback of hitting them consists of them blinking weirdly. To me, not even the shooting itself felt any interesting + the aiming is slow and unresponsive. The Lock-ons idea to not just give you safe shots, but have the character shot somewhere in a field around the locked target is an interesting idea, but doesnt seem to work too well.Then though when i was through with the Tutorial (in which every area seemed well themed - but really lame in design), the game straightup showed me how few thoughts must have went into the platforming and exploration aspect. Death loses collected objects in the current area - like it last happened in the 90s. Very weird decision imo.Additional things that are weird / unoptimized:- The graphics, especially on the player character look super blurry, not actually any furry like it's supposed to be.- Theres no settings menu accesible fromt he pause menu, just from main menu.- The first bit of voiceacting in a cutscene is not even close to loud enough to be heard over the music playing. (not playtested once?)Overall a viewer of mine while streaming it put it in nice words: "Oh, to me this looked like a demo to a 12€ game"

_childDocuments_.review: My motto is that a bad game can be entertaining, but a boring game is just bad.Tamarin has the elements of a charming platforming and action game, borrowing from the Nintendo 64-era Rare classics such as Jet Force Gemini and the like, but fails to understand what made them great, resulting in a lackluster mess of a fur ball.The biggest gripe were the overly large open areas with no clear visual direction. After yawning and groaning with the game for six hours I couldn't bear to play the game any longer, as I didn't have any hope for it becoming good any time later. Sorry, Tamarin, your remaining family will forever remain in captivity.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first negative review, unfortunately. I was really excited for this game because I love 3D platformers where you can collect things and the graphics were gorgeous. It turned out to be a huge disappointment. Only 20 minutes into playing, the camera angles kept going into unflattering and unfixable perspectives, the 3rd person shooting mechanics were terrible (the camera forcefully auto readjusts when you're aiming, which causes you to miss shots constantly. Bullets are also finite...) From what I can tell so far, the world seems to be very barren. All you do is run around and either shoot insects or get collectibles like some red things and birds. There is no keyboard and mouse support and even with a controller the controls are barely responsive or do the opposite of what you want. There are barely any options in settings to tweak the game according to how you want to aim or camera controls or anything actually useful/important. The game in general is very bland and boring. I have no idea what any of the positive reviews are talking about because the controls, camera angles, and shooting mechanics make the game very annoying and pretty much unplayable. The only upsides are the graphics and I guess Tamarin is cute. If you want to play this game, wait until they patch these issues (if ever) and do not buy it at this price point.. Wait until it's significantly lowered. I really wanted to like this game but I just can't recommend it in good faith (unless it's at a non-expensive price point).

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to wait until I fully completed this through (At the time of writing this I feel like at the pen-ultimate end run) but I just wanted to share my thought at the current moment. In short, I absolutely love Tamarin! What it may lack in modern polish it more than makes up for with charm and fun, in gameplay and presentation. For those curious; Tamarin is an action-adventure with elements of exploration, platforming, occasional 3rd person shooter combat and collection of various items that help your progress (a new weapon, ability, opening a new area etc). The developer is made up of some old RAREWARE staff, famous for Banjo Kazooie, Goldeneye, many more classic N64 titles and prior to that, Donkey Kong Country trilogy for Super Nintendo. I admit I have a lot of nostalgia for this era of games so I had to check my brain wasn't being clouded by childhood memories. The thing is, Tamarin doesn't just rely on elements of those games, but also incorporates it's own mood in-which the world is a very vulnerable place. It seems to me the primary theme of Tamarin is the fragility of wildlife and nature in general, and the importance of it's preservation and protection. The opening sequence sees a small family of Tamarins (monkeys) having their home destroyed by an army of corporate-marauding insects. The titular character is bare witness to their home and habitat engulfed in flames, family kidnapped, and local birds killed. To get it out of the way, this game also borrows from a personal favourite, Jet Force Gemini, especially with the drone enemies and combat. It's very familiar yet holds it's own with the narrative focus not being on a bombastic space epic, but a realisation of how easy it is for one overly dominant force to wipe out an those endangered. Even on that sad note, the game also has it's emotional high, especially charging into combat in the shooter sections and blasting away drones while attempting to protect and save the several birds scattered around the levels. For me, "collecting" them wasn't for completion, it was "saving"them to preserve life, which for me is way more incentive yet makes me happy when I see the total birds I've liberated along them way. You also mostly have exploration with old-school platforming akin to a 3D Mario, full analog control for controllers too. On the topic of controls, it has been recommended to use a controller over keyboard and mouse but while I've been playing primarily with the former, I did have a go at K & M and it's still playable, just no huge customisation options for either or. I recommend a controller for now, the controls aren't too complicated yet there a 1 or 2 unmentioned acrobatic tricks that are fun to work out and execute. It's not overly long, but this is one of those games that I feel is just long enough, definitely leaves an impression each time you play and I've been purposefully taking my time over the week as to savour the time spent. It doesn't have an in-depth character but I feel the context and setting or more than enough for me to empathise and route for this little tike, not just because they're "cute" but I just want these critters to have some serenity from all the pollution and kidnapping nonsense! That being said, presentation is gorgeous. Nordic inspired design with (again very RAREWARE like) cute characters with big eyes! While I don't think Tamarin may be for everyone, I was more than happy with my fully-priced purchase and support Chameleon Games. I want them to find success from this project and possibly make a sequel or successor. This game got me invested within the first minute, it didn't take several hours of world building. Emotion expressed through body language, the music, desperation of the level at the time, everything comes together to make something that both a) borrows from old-school adventures games and b) conveys a real world message that isn't in your face, just makes you feel something. Thank you Tamarin, for making me smile, aswell as giving me a machine gun to shoot big bugs ;)

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard about this game few months ago, I thought it'll be a decent 3D platformer with some shooting elements thrown in. Well, played the game after getting it on sale and I was deeply disappointed in it. Finding out that ex-Rare employees worked on Tamarin, I had a little bit of hope getting into it. Boy, what a messy game.The controls are really terrible either in the platforming sections or during the Jet Force Gemini sections. As someone who's pretty forgiving of games that are throwbacks to 90's and 2000's platformers, this is one game I cannot be nice to because there's a lot of things I don't like about it.First off, it's inconsistent tone. It first starts off as a cutesy 3D platformer with an adorable protagonist searching for his family with bright colors, but as soon as the Jet Force Gemini ant aliens start causing chaos, the cute monkey protagonist is suddenly given a gun and starts brutally shooting the ant aliens down. I keep wondering whether or not this is supposed to be a kids' game or not. This is a perfect example of a game with an uncertain audience. Is it for kids despite the high violence and blood shown onscreen despite the cute monkey? Is it for fans of 3D platformers even though there's shooting sections in between? The Ratchet and Clank series did this mixture of platforming and shooting segments way better. Or is it for people that grew up on Jet Force Gemini, but will be put off by also being a 3D platformer with cute characters? As someone who never played Jet Force Gemini before, even I would've been fine with the shooting sections......if the controls were better.Which leads me to my second issue with Tamarin. The controls are way too awkward and very terrible. The 3D platforming parts have very slippery controls and you have no indication on where to go. The shooting parts are even worse due to stuff like the lock-on never being reliable and while at the same time, you keep aiming and shooting enemies while fighting with the controls. Very wretched stuff. And like the platforming bits, you have no indication on where to go and the controls are slippery.The only good things I have to say about this game are its cute protagonist, beautiful graphics for a small indie game, and awesome soundtrack from David Wise (huge fan of his work).Overall, this is a game I was hoping will be good in a world where 3D platformers are very rare, but unfortunately, it's a game that is very confused and doesn't appeal to either kids, fans of 3D platformers, or Jet Force Gemini and with very bad controls. If you want any good 3D platformers, there's always games like A Hat in Time, the original or remade versions of the PS1 Spyro trilogy, any 3D Mario game, or even any Crash Bandicoot title. Tamarin is yet another 3D platformer that came and went.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, when I heard there was a spiritual successor to Jet Force Gemini by ex Rare devs I was hype. The game had a lot of concepts and ideas which I think could actually make for an incredibly interesting modern title in the hands of the right developer. Tamarin is no where near that game. After a relatively short playthrough of 5 hours I felt just dumb struck by the sheer disappointment and unpolished experience I got. Graphically there are problems with the textures. Environments have very bland textures and look incredibly samey from one to the next. The biomes are basically all the same with the last just being a mountainous variant on what came before. On top of that some issues spring up with clipping, a weird blurry filter over everything like someone for got to render something out or turned something on they shouldn’t have. It has appealing character designs but that’s clearly where all the focus went. Notably cliff faces also look bank sometimes and it can interfere  with  platforming.Gameplay wise you get two different segments that are repeated over the course of the game. Third person Shooter segments and platforming segments. The shooting was the more enjoyable for me; but beware as I did play with a controller and the Keyboard/Mouse support is broken for the most part. Expect to hate it if you do play with that scheme. But the shooting segments tire real fast due to having only 3 enemy types in the whole game. Standard soldier ants, big beetles with rockets, and soldier ants with shields. Yeah that’s it. (Also there are no bosses and that hurt a HUGE AMOUNT considering what happens at the end of the game.) Gun also only take the form of Pistol, Machine Gun, and Rockets. Which are easily the most boring choices they could have gone with. Also grenades and Shuriken but both are just additional things to throw. Neither is completely satisfying due to grenades having a weird arc to them and the other only being for cutting down birds and breaking shields. Again, gets old fast and the aiming is wonky.Platforming is very very basic. Don’t expect any incredible new tools either. Your platforming kit really doesn’t expand IN THE SLIGHTEST besides jump pads, but they are used very generically. The geometry is also very obnoxious in a fair number of areas so expect to fall due to wonk. Also, when moving quickly Tamarin has the tendency to slide a bit and this can make it really annoying to try and nail consecutive jumps. There’s a story....I guess? Tamarin’s cute and you gotta kills bugs to save family. That’s it.Music is the best part of the game and very pleasing personally. It was one of the few parts I was consistently happy with. Also there’s a criminal lack of options and issues with the games accessibility due to lack of options. You also can’t manage them once in the game at all. (Seriously? WHO DOES THIS?) To cap it off the camera is pretty terrible as the dev team made it a physical object in the world. Yes, IT ACTUALLY HAS COLLISION PHYSICS WITH OBJECTS. At the end of the day, $40 USD is criminal for such an underwhelming under cooked experience. I struggle to believe this game was in development for 7 years like I’ve heard around the grapevine. This isn’t even close to acceptable. Yooka-Laylee wasn’t that great but it wasn’t what this experience was. Frankly I wish I could refund the game; but I can’t. So that’s how I feel. Don’t play this; even if the nostalgia of sound effects and design philosophies of JFG are here, this game is nowhere near a complete product.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is HEAVILY inspired by Jet Force Gemini. I feel the need to emphasize that, because you don't really get that impression from the trailer. Only at the end do the bugs and guns show up for a brief second. How is it inspired by JFG? You have your pistol, machine gun, ammo boxes and capacity upgrades around the world (and hologram forms of ones you haven't collected yet), your enemies are bugs, there are life force doors, you rescue birds (instead of tribals), hell, the first level is basically Goldwood Outset even. On the negative side, though, the developers apparently missed the memo that third person shooter aiming and controls have gotten a lot better in the past two decades. Also not supporting keyboard and mouse does not help.Where the game differs from Jet Force Gemini is the platforming sections. In these they take your guns away, and you now have some different controls for platforming. There are completely different enemies, and the areas have a different feel to them. It almost seems like they had two different games they wanted to make and merged them into one.At time of writing, I'm apparently 25% through the game, and have only been playing 1.5 hours, so it apparently isn't that long. Graphically, it is beautiful, and has been enjoyable to play. I would not recommend picking this up at full price. Given that it is short and lacking basic features, $40 does feel like too much. I had preordered the game, which had a 33% discount, and that felt closer to a fair price.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Force Gemini was one of my favorite games growing up, and as soon as I heard of this game I was extremely excited for it, and I've been actively following their Twitter anticipating this release. I even pre-ordered two copies of the game to support them and give one away. I was expecting that after it being delayed month by month for over a year that at least there would be a lot more content and/or polish, but I can't recommend people buy this game at the current price.Lets start with the good stuff:The graphics are very nice, everything looks pretty good, and the sound effects are great as well. The visual and audio experience playing this game is a good experience.For the content it does have, it is a pretty nice experience to play it. The level design is decent, the movement is fine and the shooting elements are okay as well. If the game was significantly cheaper, I wouldn't turn people away from the game.Problems that can be addressed in patches:The camera is just garbage. I literally had to take a break and take my motion sickness medication to keep progressing this game. The camera will always try to readjust to this "cinematic" angle which is very inconvenient for moving around and exploring, so you're constantly trying to fight the readjustment in order to play normally. And since they programmed it so that the camera is an actual physical object in the real world (you can see this by jiggling the bird cages with the camera), the camera will freak out when it's interacting with other physical objects like walls, doors, trees and such, making you need to fight it even more.You cannot tweak any controller settings. You're stuck with the camera rotation rate, the inverted camera controls and such.If you press quit game in the start menu, it will not ask for confirmation before quitting out to main screen, and there have been several times I just want to check the totals screen and accidentally press down twice and quit out, and lose progress because I hadn't reached a checkpoint yet.Small spoiler: More fundamentally bad things:The game is just really short, which in itself isn't necessarily a bad thing, but with the genre of the game and the price tag, it just leaves you feeling lacking. It would've been better if the different levels offered some more different environments and mechanics, but it all almost feels like the whole game is just one big level. That is another point, there isn't a lot of variety in the scenery, all the levels look very similar, and the insect lair levels are all the same generic factory design the whole level. As I said, combined with the fact that they're all pretty interconnected, it feels more like one big level rather than different areas.I really don't like how they separate the shooting and platforming completely, where you have exploration levels with nice movement, and then shooting levels where all your movement abilities are stripped from you. The thing I liked the best about Jet Force Gemini is how they managed to both make it a platformer, and also a 3D shooter that required being tactical with your weapons. But in Tamarin they're just basically two different games in one, you have the platformer game in these levels, and the 3D shooter game in the other levels.The fact that you basically have no platforming or movement in the shooting levels make the shooting levels extremely repetitive and boring. The shooting is not difficult at all, and your arsenal is very limited, and the enemy variety is scarce. The levels are also fairly linear to get to the end and there are very minimal puzzle elements, so you can very easily just breeze through the shooting levels.All in all, the game is perfectly fine, and I think would be an enjoyable experience for most people without any prejudices towards what it could be, and what it advertises. But it is just not justified the price tag right now. I would wait for them to at least fix the issues mentioned in the fixable issues.The game just feels more like a proof of concept of what a Jet Force Gemini spiritual successor could be like. I think if the studio had the resources to make it 3-4 times as long and thoroughly polish it, it would be amazing. If you think the concept looks cool, and you like the aesthetic, then pick it up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen a lot of people comparing this game to Jet Force Gemini. But realistically this is a game created by a group of indie developers(Some from Rare, I get it) and if this is their first game, I approve. If anything, it feels a bit like a PG version of Conker's Bad Fur Day to me.When the splash screen came up, I was amazed at how likeable the protagonist was. Watching the cutscene in the beginning got the point across. Once I started playing I was happier than I was annoyed. But there are a few things to point out:-I enjoy the overall character movement, but the camera movement is somewhat sluggish. I'm not a fan of how it rounds off when you stop turning, and comes back just a hair when you've finished turning the camera. I've had a few already where it's completely disoriented me as to where I am and it happens at times where I need the camera to be just right (leaping across cliffs, etc.) It gets worse when you start aiming at enemies, it's a very janky aiming system. -I'm not a fan at all of the cutscene introducing the insekts, telling you that you're going to explore the forest, getting checkpoints and saving birds. It seemed extremely artificial and didn't seem like it belonged in the game at all. Not to mention the visual cues when you take out all of the insects is a bit too much for me. -The music gets a little tiring after a short while. Running around outside with nothing going on, the music was constantly ramped up and sounded like we were going to war with the orcs. The chapter I just finished was actually missing music in some areas, and I'm not sure if it was deliberate, but to go from blisteringly loud guitar solos to dead silence kinda pulled me out of the immersion. I also think I'd prefer if the music was used as the cue for moving on to the next area instead of stopping the gameplay and showing the door. Even with all of these gripes, I haven't experienced game crashes or game-breaking bugs. I have enjoyed the game despite all of these things, and plan to finish it. If I experience any of the negatives that other people have pointed out, I will be sure to adjust my opinion. But I would definitely recommend Tamarin to anyone that likes 3D platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Tamarin Review: A Cute Game Hindered by Frustrating ControlsTamarin, a visually charming action-adventure game available on Steam, instantly grabbed my attention with its adorable protagonist and nostalgic vibes. With its colorful environments and playful character design, the game has all the makings of a lighthearted platformer that’s both fun and visually pleasing. However, while it excels in aesthetics, it struggles in one crucial area: the controls.Cute Character and Beautiful GraphicsAt first glance, Tamarin is irresistibly cute. You play as a small monkey navigating through vibrant landscapes, battling pesky insects, and exploring a world that’s brimming with colorful flora and fauna. The graphics are stunning, with lush forests, flowing rivers, and detailed enemies that look like they jumped straight out of a retro classic. The resemblance to Jet Force Gemini, especially with its focus on shooting ants, is hard to miss, making it a nostalgic trip for fans of older platformers.Frustrating Controls and MovementUnfortunately, the charm of Tamarin is marred by its clunky controls. Whether using a controller or the keyboard, moving the character and aiming the weapon feels stiff and unrefined. The camera often struggles to keep up with the action, making it hard to accurately aim at enemies or even navigate the terrain smoothly. As someone who loves platformers, the awkward controls were a major letdown, as they make even basic maneuvers feel like a chore rather than an enjoyable challenge.The aiming mechanic, in particular, is disappointing. It’s hard to achieve precision, which can be frustrating during shootouts with ants or when trying to target specific objects. The lack of smoothness in aiming makes combat feel less fluid than it should be, diminishing the potential for fun, fast-paced action.Nostalgia Meets AnnoyanceWhile Tamarin clearly aims to evoke a sense of nostalgia, particularly for fans of Jet Force Gemini, it doesn’t quite manage to recreate the magic of that classic. The graphics and theme are spot-on, but the control issues make it hard to fully enjoy the game’s homage to the N64 era. It’s a game that has the heart of a classic but struggles to translate that charm into modern gameplay mechanics.Beautiful, but Hard to Fully EnjoyDespite the gorgeous visuals and appealing world design, the frustrating controls make it tough to fully immerse in the experience. The game’s levels and environments are inviting, and it’s easy to want to explore every corner of this cute and colorful world. However, when the basic act of moving the character becomes a point of frustration, it’s hard to stay engaged for long stretches.Final ThoughtsTamarin is a game that’s hard not to root for. It has an adorable protagonist, beautiful graphics, and a nostalgic concept that should make it a hit with fans of old-school platformers. However, the cumbersome controls and awkward aiming mechanics create a barrier to truly enjoying what the game has to offer. If you’re someone who can overlook clunky controls for the sake of nostalgia and a cute art style, you might still find enjoyment here. But for those who prioritize smooth gameplay and responsive controls, Tamarin may be more frustrating than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Between 10 and 17 hours, it took me 17 hours to find all the collectables but a lot of people seem to be a lot faster. 5/10 1 No There is a guide available on the steam forums with an explanation for each achievement, there is not a guide yet for all collectables 1 on Astats No No No No No No No difficulty option No  This is a fun action-adventure game from some developers that worked for RARE back in the days of Jet force Gemini and Banjo-Kazooie. You can see the influences of both of those games, into this one, especially the former Jet Force Gemini.  You'll play as the title character, the cute  but very soon it gets a bit less cute because it gets a gun at the beginning of the story. You'll switch between levels this game is a pure 3D platforming action-adventure game. There are 3 levels of each kind and 2 kinds of hub worlds.  It is clearly inspired by Jet Force Gemini, as it also has the controls like it's straight from the old N64 games. At first, I initially had a hard time with the controls, as it has been a long time since I played an N64 game and so, I had to get used to that type of controls again.  I found the game very hard in the beginning because you can use checkpoints only once and there are not that many in the game. Once I got better with the controls the whole game became a little bit easier, as well.   Most of the achievements are for things you'll do during your normal playthrough. There are also achievements for getting every collectible. On the pause screen you'll see the option to view the menu to see which collectibles you're missing. I spent most of my time, searching for those collectibles but I took way longer than many others have, therefore, my game time is a bit high. Your game-time will also decrease by quite a bit once somebody makes an in-depth guide on where to find which collectible, so you may want to check for one first, before purchasing.   If you would have asked me in the first 2 hours how much I enjoyed this game, then my answer would be that it was just okay. However, after getting used to the controls and knowing what I was doing, the enjoyment I had increased immensely. I'm sure you can tell but I enjoyed this game a lot and perhaps you will too but you may need to give it time to grow on you.

_childDocuments_.review: there's a solid base somewhere in tamarin for a fun game but it just makes too many lousy decisions to ever end up actually fun. the primary offender being that even though the shooter and platformer sections are completely separated, and despite gun aiming being based on where you point the camera, there's aggressive automatic camera adjustment in both sections for some ungodly reason, which leads to you constantly missing shots you absolutely should've landed.but even if this is fixed, i still don't think i could recommend it. the shooter sections are pretty much the only parts of the game i had fun with and between each of them are the mind-numbingly boring platforming sections, featuring a character with a moveset not remotely strong enough to support an exploration-focused platformer. the vast majority of objectives in these parts of the game amount to little more than busywork, and those that aren't just a slog are downright frustrating. and it'd be hard to recommend a game that constantly forces you to spend ages slogging through thoroughly mediocre platforming to get to what is essentially just poor man's jet force gemini even without the lousy camera.thoroughly disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the whole game before writing this review, I feel it only makes sense to write a review after completing whole game. Only buy this game if you’re a die hard Jet Force Gemini fan like myself. I was pleasantly surprised by how similar to JFG it is. And considering that its so similar; im not too sure why they didn’t just make it a JFG game instead. If you havnt already played Jet Force Gemini, then just do yourself a favour and play that game instead. This game is… mediocre, as expected. Why do all games these days suck compared to old games? I should probly judge this game based on its own basis rather than comparing it to JFG, but this game even based on its own basis is still a bad game.Half of the negative reviews are from idiots who are for god knows what reason are using keyboard and mouse…The game is bare-bones, bland and uninteresting. The story is awful, there is little to no suspense and build-up (where are all the epic cutscenes and boss fights?) The ending is an absolute joke, im normally in suspense and awe when i get to the end of a game, but in this game i literally just rolled my eyes. Oddly all the levels have the same theme, instead of having different themes. There are levels that have an outdoor green country side theme and there is an indoors theme. They could’ve used a different theme for each level to make the game more varied and to make the levels more interesting and unique, they could’ve had snow or lava level for example. The music for each level also sounds similar and generic. Levels don’t have their own feel, their own theme and music.The platforming is serviceable but uninspired. The shooting is just as fun as it was in JFG, its nice that they made the Shuriken and Grenades on their own button rather than making them a different weapon. Theres now only 1 playable character, instead of 3, which thankfully removes the possibility of making it impossible to complete the game like in JFG by picking up the ammo capacity upgrades with the wrong character. There are less weapons than in JFG, but the weapons that they do give you are all you need, most weapons in JFG were useless. The weapons are now balanced in this game and you’re able to use Shurikens and Grenades more effectively due to them being on their own button. The difficulty is also more balanced, the game is actually difficult now as you can actually die, Jet Force Gemini was way too easy as you were basically invincible. The only difficult part of JFG were the boss fights. The economy in this game is better than in JFG, in JFG; you basically had an unlimited amount of money and just refilled ammo whenever you could, whereas now there are actually things to buy. A minor nitpick is that oddly when you shoot the Beetles rapidly, they don’t register half your shots, so they don’t bleed and flinch.The music is surprisingly not very good, its better than most games these days, but its not up to the standards of Rareware, a company that’s known to have amazing music in its games. But then again the music was done by David Wise, I prefer Robin Beanland, Grant Kirkhope and Graeme Norgate myself, I never thought much of Donkey Kong Countrys music. Jet Force Gemini’s and Perfect Darks music is really good, Banjo Kazooie’s music is alright. Music in Rareware games normally stands out and you normally associate the music with the level, but in this game; because the music is just all so generic and so similar, the music doesn’t stand out and doesn’t get tied to levels. My favourite song in the game is Lyngna Fjord, but its still not great. None of the shooting music is very good, which is surprising considering that JFG was solely a shooting game and the music on that was amazing.The game is very well polished, the animations are absolute butter. The controls are good, except for when aiming; for some bizarre reason the reticle centers when moving the left analogue stick, which means that you cant aim and move at the same time.Im not too sure what people mean when they say that theres a lack of graphical options. All the graphical options such as 16x AA and 16x AF are already turned on anyway, so its not a problem. If anything; this game actually has more graphical options than most games because its got a resolution scale option which most games dont have.

_childDocuments_.review: If you wanted a spiritual successor to Jet Force Gemini, this isn't it. It wants to be, you can see it in the screenshots... but it wants to be something else.  It wants to be Banjo-Kazooie and Jet Force Gemini. And it falls short in both.Every game has a certain feeling to it. A certain tone.  When you play Jet Force Gemini, the music gets you excited. You watch a cutscene that was awesome for the time.  And then the ants come out and you blast em! And the sound effects!  Fun!  The game only accelerates from there.So you start Tamarin.  A cutscene plays, you see the ants from JFG and you go "Oh yeah, I've missed this."  You get a blaster and you start blastin.  Ok, this is fun.  But... the music isn't so exciting.  But gameplay is familiar to JFG, ok ok.  You shoot a few more bugs, find some birds and golden bugs, and then you get the machine gun. Ok, I wanna use this! Then... suddenly, you're in a platforming area.  No guns.  And this is what kills the game.  The platforming isn't fun because it's not challenging. And you can't shoot anything. Your only attack is a ground pound.  What?  And the music just isn't getting me excited.The tone of this game... it does not feel like JFG or Banjo at all. It feels like... polished Early Access 3D platformer.  You know the feeling.  A good game is somewhere in this, but it's not quite there yet.I actually left the area and went back to get my guns from the mole guy.  I got my guns... but I can't actually go back to the gun area.  What?  And I stopped playing at that point.Cube World made this mistake.  You don't give me the Kokiri Sword and then take it away.  That's the kiss of death for your game.
