_childDocuments_.review: Tamarin is a great game that I had enough fun with to complete 100%.GAMEPLAYThere's no game quite like it. It's very unique in its combination of platforming, exploration, and shooting. I've played many classic 3D platformers, and Tamarin sets itself apart to provide a unique experience of its own.The shooting is inspired by Jet Force Gemini, but what sets it apart is that it has dedicated platforming areas more akin to something like Super Mario 64. This isn't just a novel blend of game genres, but it makes for a welcome change of pace and variety that keeps the game interesting throughout. The entire game is well-paced, and never felt dragged out.The game's platforming controls very well. The protagonist, Tamarin is well-animated, and the inputs are responsive. He feels agile but also with a good amount of weight. During dedicated platforming sections, the move-set borrows quite heavily from Super Mario 64- there's a dive, crouch jump, and the "side-somersault" (which is useless in this game). The only means of attacking is a roll move, which is simple, but fun to pull off and chain between jumps and dives. The most unique ability Tamarin has is this context-sensitive leap, where he can leap long distances in specific areas. My feelings on this mechanic are mixed. Sometimes, it was a satisfying surprise to discover a spot where I can use it. Other times, it felt asinine and that it would've been more fun to just do normal platforming.Tamarin can also climb specific walls and poles. The wall sections are fun obstacles that add to the exploration. The poles are fun too, but went heavily under-used, in my opinion.The game's shooting is also solid. It's a nice break from the platforming. It's third-person shooting, but with a unique control-scheme that attempts to capture the same feeling of shooters from the Nintendo 64- specifically Jet Force Gemini. It isn't by any means emulating those old controls though; it's more like a half-way point between old and new controls. I think the controls are fun and the game's challenges are well-designed with these controls in mind. Aiming vertically takes getting used to, but it never felt unfair. You rarely ever have to aim vertically anyway, as the game allows you to lock-on to enemies positioned on turrets/towers/balconies. The lock-on mechanic might confuse some players, as you can ONLY lock-on to these aforementioned enemies but not any ground troops. You also unlock new weapons along the adventure. I wont spoil any of them, but they're fun and well-used throughout the game. I found myself using every weapon I unlocked all the way through the game. It's well-designed. Shooting sections are generous with health and ammo as long as you explore, and I think the challenge is fair throughout.LEVEL DESIGNThe game is thoroughly well-designed. Progress between each main area is gated, requiring players to collect a certain amount of fire-flies (this game's main collectible). You find fire-flies by exploring during the platforming segments. It's a fun progression system that provides just the right amount of challenge and forgiveness. You don't need every fire-fly to progress and there's a healthy amount of room for choosing which you want to collect.The game is less forgiving when collecting blue birds, which are the main collectible during shooting segments (blue birds are exchanged for fire flies at bird-houses, (3 birds = 1 fire fly) so they're technically also fire-flies).The birds are held hostage and you have to rescue them. If at any point they're shot (by the enemy, or you), they're completely gone until you complete that area and then revisit it from the very beginning. It's easy to miss these or accidentally get them killed for first-timers. On top of that, shooting levels can last about 20-50 minutes depending on skill and thoroughness, so that's considerably punishing when going for 100%Fortunately though, for Any%, it's not an issue at all. It's only overly punishing if going for 100%, but this system is fair and rewarding for Any%. It's completely the player's fault if they don't have enough fire-flies to progress to the next area.The platforming levels are focused on exploration, while the shooting areas are linear with branching paths. Both are well-designed overall. GRAPHICSThe visuals are great. There aren't many platformers with this setting and style, so I also think it's unique.All the outdoor environments are simply visually pleasant, and there's enough distinction between areas to distinguish them. The textures and lighting are great, and everything's solid.I do think the in-door factory sections could've used more visual variety, as they look very similar to each other. With that said, the factory areas still look good though.MUSICThe music is very good. I found each song to be a good musical piece. The music overall is very dramatic and moody, and it does a good job scoring the game's settings. STORYThis game's narrative is relatively simple but serviceable. It's about saving Tamarin's family. Almost the entire narrative transpires through the gameplay. There are very few cinematics, which I think is a good thing. It's a gameplay first kind of game, and I appreciate that. I think any more cut-scenes would've worsened the game's pacing.The story is also competently executed. It sets up its conflict and the conclusion of the game resolves it. Its stakes are communicated through the game's challenge and settings. There's also memoirs which add personality to Tamarin by providing a little inner monologue in the form of text. They don't add much, but it's an appreciated detail that adds character to the game.This game's narrative delivers what it needs to. It's not a focal point, and it shouldn't be.LENGTHTamarin took me about 10 hours to beat normally, 13 hours to 100%. I think the game is replayable.FLAWS/ISSUES/DISLIKES-The game crashed on me, I think twice, over the course of my entire time playing it. Causes are unknown. It wasn't a big deal though as there is frequent autosave and I could just restart the game.-It's VERY nit-picky, but I noticed tiny issues with the geometry of some assets, such as missing tris on some surfaces. It was very infrequent, only found on some static meshes in the environment, and most people probably won't even notice though.-I think the birds being blue and the enemies being blue in the shooting areas can confuse first-timers in dim-lit caves and rooms. I've accidentally shot a bird because of it.-When doing the timed silver coin challenges, the camera showing where the coins are can be very disorienting. Because of this, later challenges felt somewhat trial-and-error.-Personally, I think the death animations and effects for the bug enemies is a bit much. I understand it's a throwback to Jet Force Gemini, but some might find it shocking and even inappropriate for younger audiences. -Collecting everything 100% beyond what is required to progress the main game lacks any extrinsic reward.CONCLUSIONLike I said, it's a great game. If it looks to you like a kind of game you would enjoy, you probably will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I've never had an N64 nor played any of the titles Tamarin is referring to. So I played it completely unbiased. It was a beautiful yet demanding experience.You play as a young tamarin ape and have to rescue your family members which are caged by armed ants. The game itself rotates in two modes, depending on the area in which you currently are: exploring (without guns, more jump skills) and action (with guns). I enjoyed both modes, though I had a bit of trouble with the gun controls in the beginning. Once you've managed it the action stages are fun and satisfying.There are different collectibles you have to find. Some are very well hidden and you surely need to play through the game more than once if you want to get them all. Basically it's a 3D metroidvania game, where every area is connected with each other. The more you progress in the game, the more doors and ways you unlock to quickly get to another area. Astonishingly there are no loading screens if you travel between areas. The game also runs at a smooth 60fps frame rate, so from a technical point of view this is really well done, especially if you consider this game has been created by a very small developer team. You really feel they've put their heart into this one.The check points reset if you leave the area, just like your energy meter. Unfortunately a map doesn't exist, so you have to keep the connections between the areas in mind. But there's a statistics screen you can check to see in which area you have missed the particular collectible. The overall time for your first play through  depends on your skills and how often you get a game over, but should be about 8 - 10 hours. If you want to find every hidden secret, this time approximately doubles.I really enjoyed the atmosphere of Tamarin. The landscapes are obviously inspired by the Scandinavian nature (fjords, mountains, forests) and are very pleasing to the eye. Together with the splendid soundtrack (which is btw done by David Wise, who also did the music for the Donkey Kong Country series), the game is really fun to play. The industrial ants' factories and caves add a good variety to the overall peaceful and relaxing impression I got from this world. : Tamarin is a beautiful 3D platformer and shooter at the same time. The game changes smoothly between the two modes which are fun to play but can also be demanding. You need to find different collectibles to proceed, unlock new skills or shortcuts and eliminate evil enemies. Wonderfully designed landscapes and the outstanding music create a joyful experience I am happy to recommend. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, I really loved this game.Jet Force Gemini was always my favorite N64 game, the first of admittedly few games that I have beaten on the console. While the controls have not aged well, there is something about the splatter-filled run-and-gun mechanics that is oddly satisfying and addictive.So when I heard about this game, meant to be a spiritual successor to Jet Force Gemini, developed by many ex-developers from Rare, I was instantly intrigued and pre-ordered it immediately. While the game was delayed nearly a year from its original intended release date, I never lost track of it and frequently went to check for updates. So, was it worth it?The Pros:Tamarin's game play is split into two main categories: the platforming and the run-and-gun segments.The platforming consists of an open hub world in which collectibles are spread about, with platforming challenges and secrets hidden around to encourage exploration and creativity with the mechanics. Tamarin is very fluid to control, and it is a blast to run, roll and jump around in these open segments to see what you can find.In the run-and-gun segments, Tamarin becomes equipped with heavy weaponry, and will come face-to-face with Insekts (primarily ants and roaches) that are armed and ready to fight. These segments are more maze-like, with many alternate paths and secrets to look for. The weapons are all distinct from each other, and it is a blast to fire away at the Insekts with nearly as much splatter as in Jet Force Gemini. The controls feel inspired by its predecessor, but feel updated and fluid. Targets in sniper perches or that fly can be targeted with a lock-on system, while infantry units will simply be targeted by aiming in their direction, with a mild auto-aim to help preserve the constant movement of Jet Force Gemini.Tamarin's sound design is quite lovely. From the peaceful, near atmospheric music in the hub worlds to the pounding, intense beats of the action stages, the music helps to absorb the player into the game. The gunfire sounds are satisfying and heavy, and coupled with the splatters of the blood of your enemies against the wall, the combat feels very visceral and exciting.Tamarin and his friends are very adorable. The character designs cause you to instantly fall in love with them, investing you in their plight. The enemies are menacing, and killing them can cause them to explode in spectacular fashion. The overall cartoonish design allows the adorable critters and extreme violence to mesh quite well.The game itself feels overall highly polished. From such a small, humble team, this obviously feels like a labor of love from them. The mechanics feel great, the controls are great, and I encountered very few glitches in my 20+ hours of playing the game. The ones that I did encounter were minor graphical issues that corrected themselves in less than a second and did not affect game play in the slightest.The Cons:No spoilers, but the final boss felt like a bit of an anticlimax, especially compared to the buildup of the levels leading up to it.The damselflies don't make a sound when you first impact them. Not a big deal, but a pet peeve of mine.While the two game play modes are great in their own right, they feel disconnected, so it almost feels like playing two separate games. While I can see why this is necessary to have two polished control schemes, I feel like having a mechanic where you can holster or draw your gun to switch between the two modes could allow for bigger and more intense level design.There are a couple platforming challenges involving collecting trails of coins that can be quite difficult since it is not entirely clear where to go some of the time in them. This can be frustrating if you don't know the maps very well before attempting them, and will require patience from the player.I did encounter a few minor graphical glitches. They quickly went away and did not affect game play.Overall, I was very pleased with this game. Should Chameleon Games announce DLC or a sequel, you can bet I will be the first in line to get them!

_childDocuments_.review:
SAVE YOUR FAMILY FROM THE INSECT INVASION

Explore an incredible interconnected 3D world, brimming with primate platforming and bug-splattering shooter action. Leap with the agility of a tamarin as you journey into the Northern wilderness on scenic routes through forests, fjords and mountains. Along the way you will chase mysterious electrical fireflies, discover a secret underground world of dancing ants, rescue innocent birds, and restore the tamarins' once idyllic natural habitat.

What kind of game is it?

Tamarin features a unique gameplay mix that alternates between 3D-platforming and exploration, and third-person shooter gameplay. The game is inspired by the more open 3D adventures from Nintendo and Rare, and by nature and all the wonderful plants and animals in it.

Players take command of Gunvolt and make short work of enemies using his high-speed techniques and command of electricity just like before, but in Gunvolt 2, a new character joins the fray! _childDocuments_.review: The Azure Striker Gunvolt series is Inti Creates' flagship spiritual successor to the Mega Man Zero and ZX series. However, unlike those titles of old, this is one franchise that does things quite differently. The games that make up this series are fairly typical action platformers at first glance, but what sets them apart are their focus on high-score. When playing as the titular Gunvolt, you're encouraged to "tag" as many enemies with your non-lethal bullets as possible before destroying them all at once with your special attack. The more enemies you take out at once, the higher your score. However, getting hit too many times makes you lose everything since the last checkpoint, which gives the game a nice risk vs. reward-type of feel.In this second game, Gunvolt is joined by, appropriately enough, a second protagonist, his rival Copen. This character plays completely differently from Gunvolt and his way of gaining points are likewise completely unique to him. Copen's gameplan is all about staying airborne. When in the air, Copen can dash in every direction except straight up or straight down. Dashing into an enemy causes Copen to rebound off the enemy and lock on, allowing you to finish it off in short manner. On the other hand, rebounding off the environment recharges the meter Copen uses to fuel his dashes, allowing him to maximize his air time. This cycle of ricocheting off of your surroundings while taking out everything in your path makes for an incredibly kinetic and flashy experience.As far as my personal thoughts go, Gunvolt's gameplay has a fun and unique gameplay hook, but once you take away the initial novelty, it kind of doesn't feel all that satisfying due to Gunvolt's slower paced way of tagging enemies. Copen's gameplay on the other hand is a fast and addicting rush of 2D action that plays like nothing else. The hightened difficulty and tighter stage designs featured in this sequel does help elevate Gunvolt's own side of the equation to something that feels significantly better than the first game, however.If it's pure gameplay you're looking for, the newer Luminous Avenger iX is the more polished game as far as Copen is concerned, but the higher amount of content that is offered through having two highly unique playable characters does make GV2 an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it. Just buy it. This game is addictive.Let's be honest: I liked AZG1. As a lifelong fan of the Megaman franchise since its distant origins back in the 1980s, it was my all-time favourite action platformer. AZG1 did a great job making me remember the experience...... But Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 is the true, perfect successor of that beloved series. Inti Creates just nailed it. Period.It should be no surprise, since the "Action Supervisor" is Keiji Inafune, who worked so long with the Megaman series, that at this point he knows by heart what makes a proper action platformer tick.Couple that with the awesome work of Inti Creates in crafting the gameplay, the stages, THE MUSIC (Indigo Destiny's... by the Septima!), the plot... It is not "just" an attempt at recreating the feel of Megaman; the tale, its plot, its characters and the direction it takes have depth. Real depth. The kind that should spawn several 26-chapter anime series, and fanfiction. What can I do but love this game?And I haven't even said anything about the gameplay, which is AWESOME. We know what GV can do, but in this game he does it even better,\; the controls feel responsive, and the customization of his gear is just right to give lots of possibilities. Particularly when you speed through a stage. What a rush!Speaking of speeding, our Adept Hunter, Copen, is the one who truly brings the 'Megaman X' feel with his weapons, his acrobatics, his dashing onto things. Such a wild style, our boy has. Double the fun.I cannot wait to play Azure Striker Gunvolt 3! Inti Creates are seriously crafting some cool franchises that bring that "gaming" feel we all grew up with, and grew up to love.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, it's here! I already beat the game on 3DS, so that's why my play time is low. My PC has very low-end specs and the game is running flawlessly, so I'd say it's a great port. Controller support is alright too.The action is pretty damn good. The art and music are on-point. The story is the weakest element, but it's not bad. While the game is short if you play each stage only once, it has high replayability through optimizing scores and getting better ranks. You have two playable characters, Gunvolt and Copen. Gunvolt builds up high scores by killing multiple enemies at once, and Copen by killing enemies in succession without stopping on the floor. Both need to get hit the least as possible to maintain a chain and increase score-making even more.If you enjoyed Gunvolt/Luminous Avenger, playing this one is a no-brainer. If you didn't, but want a good action 2D game, this is a solid option for you. The whole series is, so if you didn't play any, I recommend starting from Gunvolt 1 to follow the story properly. If you don't give a damn about story, you can play this one first, and then Gunvolt 1 or Luminous Avenger iX depending on whether you liked GV or Copen better (Likely the latter).

_childDocuments_.review: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 - a game I waited roughly three years for. I own a 3DS and Switch, but I always worry about the fragility of my 3DS' buttons, and the Switch doesn't play nice with headphones at a distance. When the PC port was finally announced, I may or may not have slightly lost my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ marbles. And I can promise you that it isn't just the excitement talking when I say that it was well worth the wait.ASG2 is divided into two different campaigns: that of the titular Azure Striker, "Gunvolt," and that of the Adept Slayer and Luminous Avenger, "Copen." Gunvolt plays much as he did in the first game: shoot enemies with your gun to tag them, then activate your Flashfield to send arcs of lightning towards them for major damage. Copen, on the other hand, plays much differently, as he locks on to enemies by dashing into them and dealing the majority of his damage with his gun and EX Weapons; the latter of which are obtained Megaman-style by defeating stage bosses. In addition, both characters come equipped with gear that allows them the use of "Prevasion," which automatically nullifies damage in exchange for some Flashfield energy or lock-on dash uses. There is also the special "Anthem" ability, which has a chance to trigger when the protagonist dies, reviving them and dramatically powering-up their abilities.In terms of gameplay and level design, I personally found both to be very enjoyable. Copen's playstyle of dashing all around the map and using enemies as springboards has taken some getting used to, but when you're able to pull it off, it feels great. Gunvolt's more adaptive style of blitzing through stages and striking several enemies from a distance is largely unchanged from ASG1, but still remains a blast. In addition, it might just be my imagination, but the stage design feels much more creative than the original, with multiple pathways and winding corridors designed to take advantage of the character's abilities.The music, as is to be expected, is stellar. Some of the tracks might not be your thing if you're not into J-Pop, but there's still plenty of groovy instrumental tracks to keep your ears pleased during most of the game.As for story, it may be a result of the dual campaigns, but it felt much more cohesive and well-put together in this game - which is a good thing. As for the quality of the story itself, while it is subjective, I personally liked it a lot. It does a great job of making you empathise for both of the characters, despite their war with each other. I won't go into much more detail than that, though, to avoid spoilers.Finally, the last thing I'd like to talk about is controls. While I had a bit of trouble with controller configuration at first - which I later found out was due to a mistake on my part - I found the controls to be intuitive and comfortable once things got going. I have no qualms with the porting, either: as far as I could ever tell, there aren't any odd bugs or issues to be seen.In conclusion, if you enjoyed the original Azure Striker Gunvolt, you'll have a blast with the sequel. It improves on the original, while keeping the best parts and adding new features to keep you on your toes. It also has a great amount of replay value, as there are a good number of rewards for improving your skills and clearing stages as flawlessly as you can manage - something which can end up bringing a whole new paradigm of difficulty to the game. All in all, I'd give ASG2 a 9/10, and would definitely recommend it to anyone who's played the original.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game _if_ you enjoy the prospect of replaying stages for high ranks and scores. If you just run through the stages then you'll blow through the game in 5 or 6 hours without much difficulty - the real fun comes from learning to play the stages well enough to get high ranks. The game unfortunately does not explain its scoring mechanics well at all so you may need to seek outside resources to learn how to rack up the most points.I'd strongly recommend this one over Azure Striker Gunvolt 1. The levels are much more interesting, the new character Copen is super fun to play as, the S+ rank thresholds are less draconian, and there are some much-needed QoL features like not needing to select individual challenges before you start a stage.It looks a lot like Mega Man Zero/ZX but it doesn't really play that much like those games beyond the basic controls. As Gunvolt, gameplay revolves around tagging enemies with your gun and then zapping tagged enemies with your flash field to do major damage, with you getting bonuses for killing multiple enemies simultaneously or killing fully tagged enemies while in mid-air. As Copen, you lock on to enemies by dashing into them and then damage them by shooting them with your blaster or EX Weapons, while getting bonuses for killing multiple enemies without landing on the ground. That's slightly easier than it sounds since your mid-air dash recharges every time you dash into a wall or an enemy, which allows you to bounce around the stages like a human pinball.The story is whatever, it's basically a collection of anime tropes and is really forgettable. Some nice artwork though.The one aspect I really do not like is the crafting system. You get materials whenever you finish a stage or complete a challenge and you can use materials to craft equipment. Some of the equipment is really useful, especially if you're going for S+ ranks, but farming for crafting materials is not fun at all.I did encounter one major technical issue which thankfully was easily resolved once I figured it out - after running once, the game would immediately crash on startup until I set the .exe to run in Windows 8 compatibility mode. I suspect this is a common problem with this game when running on Windows 10 in certain desktop resolutions.

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh Gunvolt 2, honestly the best thing about this game is the fact that Copen was introduced as a playable character, but that's mostly because I absolutely adore his playstyle as he's much faster and lighter on his feet compared to Gunvolt himself.If you've played the first game then Gunvolt is pretty much the same with the only difference being the maximum number of tags he holds is no longer tied to his guns but rather his equipment. Aside from that, this game introduces some 0SP skills for Gunvolt that don't reset Kudos and makes it so that healing no longer resets your Kudos. For those who haven't played Gunvolt, he has the ability to generate electricity which is used to interact with enemies and the environment uniquely and the same tagging and electrocution mechanics. An overall pretty slow and grounded fighter who relies on his equipment to vary up his playstyle.The real huge addition to this game IMO is playable Copen. He's the complete opposite of Gunvolt. Where Gunvolt is a specialist that has one power that does many things, Copen has the EX weapon system which is basically the same as Megaman's copying abilities and can LITERALLY FLY, well kinda. Copen has the bullit system where he will use up 1 bullit for an airborne dash that can be controlled very precisely to do very precise movements. Whenever he hits an enemy or a surface he will reload the lost bullit and in a pinch he can just reload it manually. This opens up tons of possibilities when it comes to his movement and combat. Additionally, Copen's tagging mechanic is tied to dashing into enemies which makes his playstyle overall faster and more aggressive compared to Gunvolt's, the game practically promotes the idea of you pinballing off of anything and everything and killing enemies while airborne in order to rack up more points. Extremely fun character that has a high skill ceiling, it's no wonder he became the protagonist of a sister game series.Aside from the playable characters the games pretty much more of the same compared to the first, a Megaman styled platformer that focuses on racking up points to get a high score and good time. As with the first game, this game also features vocal tracks that play when you rack up 1000+ kudos as either playable character which is very rewarding as a lot of the vocal tracks are great.The story this time round is a bit weird and hard to follow since there's completely different yet similar stories happening at the same time that don't quite line up very well. At the very least both stories are not the same which a lot of games with 2 concurrent stories tend to do but it definitely makes it hard to understand the first time round. Not a bad story but not the best by all means, it can do with a bit of reorganizing but overall the story was great.For a sequel this game is pretty much what you'd expect, a more refined experience compared to the first game and the addition of Copen as a playable character is amazing. I recommend playing the first game so you'd understand the story but otherwise this game is a good one, honestly Copen's gameplay alone makes this game way better for me than the first though I'm a bit biased since my introduction to the franchise is LAiX.

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything a sequel should be, while keeping what made the first game great. Let's start with the story, vastly improved over the first game. There's more conversations between the characters, allowing us to get to know these characters more. Bosses now even have conversations during the fights themselves, giving us a bit of insight to their characters or simply to trash talk GV or Copen. It's great. The story itself is very tightly knit, both sides have their own goals and motivations which eventually clash. It's simply well done.The gameplay is split into 2 sides, Gunvolt And Copen. However, they both retain the same scoring system where you get to hear different songs once you get 1000 kudos. For me, that's the main draw of the Gunvolt games. To simply enjoy the songs while doing okay in the fights. Speaking of, Copen is probably the best playable character in an action platformer. He is able to dash in 6 directions, target enemies that he dashes into with homing shots while using special weapons gained from bosses. His fast paced combat style is a stark contrast to the more methodical style of Gunvolt's gameplay. Though some stages are recycled, it's still amazing to see an entirely new playstyle alongside the original. He even comes with his own muse songs, that's quality right there. So much so that he even got his own spin off game.What else is there to say, everything is improved over the first game. Production quality is much higher, with voice acting for everybody. More songs to enjoy while playing on gutless since I'm terrible at these games. No matter what skill level you are at, you can tackle these games at your own pace. There's something for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: If you came from the first game, you will surely love this sequel that comes with tons of upgrades and quality of life features.Azure striker gunvolt 2 continues its story from the first game's good ending, this time you'll be able to play as copen, the story's anti-hero whose playthrough is more than just a palette swap of gunvolt; both may share the same bosses but their well-done routes are much different and even their stages' soundtracks are also different. I really loved the soundtracks, it feels as if themselves received upgrades, most of these soundtracks are graved in my memory and they also feel as if they fit in each stage's theme. I really like how most of Copen's soundtracks have some Synth instruments used in them to give some taste to his young scientist background. The visuals have received a huge upgrade from the first game, although it did annoy me sometimes that the story dialogue is played on the stage and takes a huge chunk of the screen, we have the choice to either disable or enable dialogues at will. Missions are now automatically activated, you don't need to manually activate them before starting a mission, which is one of the best QoL features we could ever receive, the crafting system is the same but with a small change : you don't need to craft the same item twice in order to upgrade it, instead : equip it and level it up through normal gameplay, I really like this approach but it's a bit slower in comparison to the old system, while the latter required a bit of farming through some RNG, so pick your poison.Copen's equipment gimmick is well done, giving you a limit on what perks you can equip and giving you also the ability to compress their "memory cells" in order to manage things easily, I like how it is quite different from gunvolt's, And that's not the only different thing about him, Copen pretty much plays like the original Mega man games in the rock-paper-scissors fashion: you get a boss weapon which can be a weakness to another boss. Due to the nature of having 2 playable characters, you would expect 4 endings, 2 bad endings and 2 good endings, the story is well crafted that both the 2 good endings are canon, and since there aren't really any plot changing collectibles, you get the good endings if you simply finish both playthroughs of Gunvolt and Copen, there is however a fifth ending with a much harder requirement, teasing the existence of the third game.The game comes packed with DLCs from the console counterpart, which is super neat, you get remixed versions of the levels you already played and depending on which level you chose, you can fight bosses from the first gunvolt game. Sadly the shovel knight bonus fight has been removed, for obvious reasons, and sadly the leaderboards function isn't present in the new port.I have the feeling that the way this game calculates the scoring has been casualized and made much more easy, on my first playthrough I could manage to get easy S/SS ranks on various levels. Speaking of levels they are well designed but they still keep think air of being straight forward, the absence of puzzles makes it a bit boring in comparison to the first game. There is a speedrunner mode which disables Prevasion, crafting and saving if you want some challenge.Sadly there is no auto-save function, all the saving is done manually and it kind of sucks because I see no harm in including it, I once lost around 40% worth of quests progress to this lack.Overall if you are a fan you will absolutely love it, if you are new to the franchise I think you might also enjoy it if you start here. I think I would recommend this game for what you pay for, you get around 40 hours of fun if you go for 100%. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 is a proper sequel to solid original 'Mega Man Zero'-Like title of INTI CREATES. While it maintains the core mechanics of the original game, it polishes them to feel fresh and adds new skills for Gunvolt. There is also another playable character we're all familiar with: Copen! His playstyle is very similar to X from Mega Man X series since he is able to replicate the abilities of defeated enemies with the aid of his personal robot Lola. However, his personality doesn't even come close to X because he is filled with hatred towards Adepts - humans with septimal powers. The plot twist at the end sends him in a state of "in-betweenness", though. I'd say he's very confused due to the fact that he believes that Adepts are a threat to nature and God while he forgets it was God who created them and dons the role of grim reaper. Gunvolt on the other hand is the Gunvolt we're all familiar with. Story starts off with Zonda assaulting the top Sumeragi Operatives with the aim of creating a world for Adepts and Adepts alone. She later captures Joule and plans to use her power for herself. How she does that is for you to find out. Both Gunvolt's and Copen's stories overlap until Tenjian's level, then they slighty change but end up concluding at the same spot with a twist. If you're planning to experience the full story, you must beat the game as both characters and complete at least 80% of the challenges for both of them. I haven't played Luminous Avenger iX games yet so, I don't know if they proceed where Copen's story left off or not. I hope they do, though. We certainly have to wait for the third entry to the series which is bound to come out soon to follow up Gunvolt's story. The game overall is also very easy compared to its predecessor due to newly adjusted prevasion system for both characters. Same goes for achievements as well. Ranking and scoring are a lot more flexible too. The majority of its music tracks were one dimensonal in the first game but the sequel offers some real bangers. I almost felt bad for hitting 1000 kudos in levels due to Joule's song cutting the soundtrack. In short, Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 is a wonderful sequel and a solid platformer title if you enjoy platformers that play like Mega Man, especially Zero series.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first 30 minutes of the game they have introduced no fewer than five loli characters.This is the third Gunvolt game on Steam (But in proper release order, the second game.) and man, Inti Creates loves Gunvolt. Just in the second game they create an entirely new playable character with unique mechanics and give him half the game! Who else puts this much effort in a new franchise? Gunvolt returns from Gunvolt 1 and he still has the same terrible scoring system and boring easy levels. He has gotten a new cooldown command skill to give him a new attack type that does not end your combo and it certainly adds quite a bit to the game but you're still nursing a chain combo that requires constant red-light-green-light stop and go gameplay to fiddle around the enemies to make irritatingly precise combo shots if you care about score.Copen is quite a bit more fun because he was designed by insane people. You remember Copen as GV's rival from the first game but he doesn't play at all like he looked in that game. If you've seen Luminous Avenger iX, he has the same playstyle here. Copen airdashes, careens off walls, bounces off enemies, he completely disrespects the level design by just flying through everything making giant combos without touching the ground.  GV's levels here are a bit more refined than they were back in GV1, but here Copen himself is a bit less refined than he was in the sequel Luminous Avenger iX, because this is his first outing of course, but it's still an incredibly fun time to play as this utterly insane character.Beyond that, it's standard Inti Creates these days. The levels are total snoozefests only there to make you play for score. The bosses are packed with unfair, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ patterns, but you have prevasion to make you borderline invincible. Unlike Luminous Avenger iX, I actually don't recommend you rush to turn off prevasion because some of these boss patterns are complete, indefensible, horsesh*t, requiring complete memorization of patterns that are unreadable and unpredictable from visual/audio cues.It's a shame, as the bosses are generally cool as always, but almost every fight has SOME form of this idiot nonsense. No boss has a fun EX move, they are all either total jokes or ridiculous spamming of so much random crap all over the screen that you practically need to go watch a video of the fight to see a safe path through. I honestly think this game has hands down the worst bosses of the franchise. The whole thing is still playable but playing this again now I remember why I never went back to clear Gunvolt 2 as often as I did 1.But this is still a score attack game, and you can see it in the giant combo meter and the challenges that unlock after clearing a level (Beat Level X to unlock the "Clear Level X 5 times" challenge. No, the first clear didn't count it merely unlocked that challenge.) and the MonHun style loot farm to buy equipment to unlock things like double jump or extra firing patterns. It still has the same complete lack of fun where Gunvolt is only enjoyable when played with meticulous precision and every single misstep will drop your combo and make you feel like you wasted the entire level. As with every game in this franchise they hinge so much on a score system that is incredibly punishing and only rarely fun.Above all else, it's still Gunvolt, only with a side helping of Copen's pinball bouncing platforming madness that was so good he got his own spinoff purely because he was such fun in this game. You know what you are getting into by now and if you hated or liked the previous games, you will still hate or like this one all the same. Having said that, I tend to prefer the other two Gunvolt games to this one. The plot and new design for the muse are both pretty lame. And despite this being a more refined product, I just find myself preferring the aesthetic of Gunvolt 1 or iX a bit more, but mostly for subjective reasons (And also fewer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss patterns)P.S. Copen is absolutely justified in his hatred of adepts and killing them all would undeniably make the world a better place and all three Gunvolt games are proof of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first game. Mostly because the new protagonist has levels that don't always take into account his abilities.	GV2 is a game about two protagonists. Gunvolt (GV) is back, and he plays much as he did in the previous game. Shoot enemies to tag them, and hit your ability button to auto attack anything tagged. Build up a score that is lost if you-depending on the difficulty-are hit 1 to 3 times. It's a score attack game. His levels always have a unique gimmick or obstacle that sometimes meshes with his electricity ability in unique ways.	Copen, the rival and anti-hero to GV, has a drastically more exhilirating playstyle. He dashes into enemies, which serves as a tag/lock-on function, and then fires his weapon or abilities. He can hover in air, so he can stay air-borne for a long amount of time. His style of play allows for prolonged airtime and constant dashing. The problem is that his levels aren't as creative as GV's and rarely interact with his ability in unique ways. There's one level where air currents mess with your flight trajectory, but that's it. 	Worse yet, because he can move such large distances so quickly and for so long, he can skip large portions of his own levels. You can't bee-line it to the end, but the level design doesn't seem to always take his abilities into account. Which is a shame, because he's exciting to control. His levels just aren't entertaining to traverse.	GV and Copen have 3 to 4 unique levels in each of their campaigns, with a shared level (might be 2) and the typical end-game levels. They have slightly divergent paths in those final few stages. The game is at its worst when they share anything, because the levels are purposefully stale due to how wildly different Copen and GV control. 	GV1 had a consistent level of quality that made for a solid experience. GV2 captures that for only a portion of this game. The other half is spent on a new idea that is both unique and exciting, but the design philosophy behind the levels isn't there yet. 	There's also the bosses, which have some wild attack patterns and moves that seem impossible to actually block. It's nothing huge to complain about, since i still passed it all with minimal difficulty. But I know I'm not the only one that was scratching my head at some of this.	Copen has a spin off, and I hear its a 'tighter' experience than this one. It gives me hope for GV3, which has already been greenlit. GV2 isn't bad, but I want an experience that matches GV1's consistency and even surpasses it. With GV3 coming soon, here's hoping.
_childDocuments_.name: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt's gameplay is a more shallow version of the games it was inspired by.GAMEPLAYThe game shifts away from platforming and into pointless combo farming. The characters are fun to control but their movement is heavily inspired by Mega Man Zero. Levels are mostly linear hallways with few obstacles and enemies that die with little to no effort. To make an already easy game easier, both characters default abilities allow you to ignore almost all damage and getting hurt only depletes your combo score. Sometimes the game just chooses to respawn you after death with superpowers that make you even more overpowered than usual. This makes going through levels and fighting bosses seem almost pointless if there is little to no chance of dying, and bosses only take 1-2 tries to defeat since you don't need to bother learning their pattern. I could never buy any of the upgrades because you get materials randomly at the end of each level but I never seemed to have enough. The game removes one of your abilities if you use the boss weapons, so I didn't experiment with any of them.PRESENTATIONAlmost all text is presented at a 30 degree angle which gives me a headache, but to make matters worse sometimes it expects you to read this slanted text during a level or boss fight, which makes you stop caring about the tacked-on plot. The music is mostly forgettable, bland techno-stuff and the only memorable songs were remixes from the first game. If you get a combo of 1000 or are resurrected after dying, it plays a Japanese pop idol song over the level music. What made me angry was that it forces you into that mode at the final level making the boss rush a joke and preventing me from hearing the music to the first phase of the final boss which was a genuinely good remix of one of my favorite songs from the first game, so to hear it I had to kill myself (which actually takes effort since I have to actively try to get hurt in this mode), and restart the boss fight. The best part of the presentation were Inti Creates spritework which is always great.VERDICTIf you like the feeling of playing Gunvolt, play Mega Man Zero instead.

_childDocuments_.review: My first exposure to Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 was a YouTube video from ZaffreRevolution praising it as his favorite 2D platformer of all time. At the time, it seemed a little hyperbolic, but I trusted the channel’s opinions - said channel is called ZaffreRevolution, if you're curious- so I bought this and the prequel on a Steam sale to eventually get to. After years of sitting on my Steam library, I've not only finally played GV2 but also 100 percented it to boot. Having done that, I can say with confidence as well that this is up there as one of the best platformers I've ever played. The game is short and sweet, but incentivizes you to replay stages and get better at the game by way of the ranking and kudos system.The story and characters are compelling and fun to follow The soundtrack and presentation are wonderful.Both playable characters are a blast to play, with seperate awesome gameplay styles and different campaigns Etcetera. Now is this game LITERALLY perfect? Sadly no. The lack of an English dub makes it hard to follow story-related conversations during stages. The challenge system is very fun and improved from the first game, but still can feel a little obtuse in the execution. And there is a notable technical glitch with the final boss related to the Steam Deck which crashed the game on me.Those negatives, for me anyways, are far outweighed by how much fun I had playing and replaying the game. Gunvolt 2 may not be objectively flawless, but in all the ways that matter to me, it's one of the most fun platformers I've played and is one I'm already looking forward to coming back to. This game comes highly recommended. 🙂

_childDocuments_.review: A step up from the first game. His gameplay and far more maneuverable moveset meshes perfectly with the score-attack nature and the more tactile approach of dashing into enemies to tag them(and the score multiplier being based on treating the floor like lava) encourages far more aggression Unfortunately he's also, y'know, Grand Wizard Batman so it's up to you if fun gameplay makes up for playing as a truly odious human being. Thankfully his alternate-universe spinoff(s) does not carry over this aspect of his character but here oh boy I hope you like playing as Batman if he was in the middle of a boomer great replacement theory panic attack.Anyway it's not bad overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the original Gunvolt if Copen was playable and had a jet engine strapped to his shoes. Copen is cool. No wonder he's fully playable in all three of his playable appearances compared to Gunvolt who got relegated to being Kirin's sidekick in GV3. Not counting Mighty Gunvolt/Burst. Yes I know LAiX2's Copen had software update problems and was severely nerfed thus not playing the same BUT STILL.GV2 is a pretty big sequel, and I think it's the most ambitious game in the franchise even to this day--I might even dare to say that it's the best game in the franchise; having two different playable characters with their own campaigns alone makes it that much heftier, the story is solid, the addition of two other Kudos gain settings(lost on hit, lost on three hits, or no loss at all) is great for those who like the Kudos system, but not the pressure of being perfect; all of the songs have both a Joule and a Lola version, and I don't think they've ever topped the concept of that true final boss, even with how simple its premise is.If there's something I find lacking, it's on the Copen side of the game: Copen has the Mega Man ability to develop weapons based on defeated bosses--kinda like his boss fight in the first game--but these weapons are kinda lacklustre; most of them fall simply under the category of "shoot a bullet". In fact, as of writing this, I can only remember two of them because they felt actually unique: the chargeable Prism Break that can deal massive damage, and the life-stealing Ferrous Fangs. Granted, "shooting a bullet" might be all that Copen needs given his high aerial mobility.

_childDocuments_.review: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 is simply a rock-solid follow-up to an already killer game. Although it's over before you can blink, the adventure is still one as exhilarating as what's come before it, and at times even more so with the introduction of Copen and his homing-attack-style gameplay variance stood apart from the titular character. All while trimming some of the fat from the previous game, the newly-founded duology becomes one that I cannot recommend enough to fans of the action-platformer genre who are looking to sink their teeth into something familiar yet unique.+ QOL improvements such as automatic Challenges and removal of cheap boss attacks+ Overall more forgiving in difficulty spikes and stage ranking+ Copen gameplay is awesome and feels distinct from Gunvolt- Grindy material-farming still remains
_childDocuments_.name: Azure Striker Gunvolt 2

_childDocuments_.review: A big step up in quality over the original, even if it didn't have to change much.The best change this game has over its predecessor is much stronger level design.I feel it may have less gimmicks, there's nothing really spectacular here, but it's the way it's designed that effectively takes up space on your screen. It's a fair bit more vertical, less blocky, and way more fun to tag enemies instead of just "see an enemy, jump over it to find another". It's designed to make you go fast and make use of the characters skillset, pretty alright.Now onto the new stuff, which is even better, the introduction of a new playable character, Copen.My god he's so much fun to play as! His gameplay style incentivises dashing into enemies and never touching the ground.With a multidirection dash for both mobility purposes and tagging enemies, with a gun that locks onto tagged enemies, he plays exactly how I wanted a lot of this game to be played. You see an enemy, and treat it as something to dispose of and move on. But since dashing into enemies helps you stay off the floor and maintain the pace, his gameplay style feels really satisfying to pull off.His dash also lets you bounce of surfaces so long as you hold down the button, turning hallways/corridors/ascents into fun zig-zag moments.Not to mention, unlike Gunvolt who gets new guns/ammo when he defeats a boss which are kind of annoying to swap to, and not the most useful? Rather than getting a whole new gun, Copen gets a new side weapon to use alongside his standard gun. He can just shred enemies with these tools.Commenting on a "meh" point, the game is even easier compared to the original.Not much to comment on and honestly, I think it's just because of how the game is designed in an effort to make you speed through things, but I figure it's worth bringing up.The game still prioritizes rankings above all else, so the low skill floor, high skill ceiling mentality still applies here.Now onto the bad stuff.The dialogue boxes are terrible, they obscure so much of your screen, easily obscuring bosses and their attacks/telegraphs. They also don't have an english dub to my understanding, so good luck reading all of the dialogue while gameplay is happening. You can turn them off on repeat playthroughs of levels, but I feel it's kind of lame to just brute force your way through the first time just because you can't see anything.The last two levels are also quite long, and I feel they could've been broken up a bit.Like the last level in particular is six boss fights in a row, and on Gunvolt, two of these will just waste your time.I view this as a negative because it makes repeat playthroughs feel like a slog, and it does not incentivise me to go back and get S+ ranks, when I have to get through 6 - 8+ minutes of action combat without getting hit.Having cinematic moments thrown on top of it that are a part of the fight just feels boring.But overall, I had a good time here.Will I S+ it all, nah.Am I tempted to get and S+ Luminous iX? Absolutely.Looking forward to seeing what the rest of this series has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Inti Creates are the kings of 2D action platformers. It is my headcanon that Capcom no longer makes new Megaman games because they know they can't compete with Inti. Playing as GV feels better than ever (thank you based Inti for adding Crashbolt and Dragon Sphere so we don't feel bad about not using skills on the minibosses) and Copen gives a very welcome new playstyle. Challenges are now actually tolerable although i'd still prefer that the harder versions of the challenges would be automatically cleared if you got the requirements for them on the easier versions instead of having to replay the stage for each one. Other than that, the game is amazing and highly recommended for anyone that enjoyed the old Megaman games, especially the Zero and ZX series.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Gunvolt 1, this is even better.If you haven't played Gunvolt 1, think of this as a genuine spiritual successor to the later Megaman X games. It's edgy in a "rated T for teen" kind of way, and you kind of just have to take the game's setting and characters at face value, but I don't think this is necessarily a bad thing. Or at least, it wasn't for me. I liked the plot.The major difference between GV 1 and GV 2 is that 2 lets you play as Copen. Gunvolt and Copen have fundamentally different movement mechanics as well as different plots and character-specific stages. Copen feels great to play. Gunvolt feels like hard mode.Movement is fast-paced, precise, and very easy to fumble-finger, just like in GV 1. With Copen this doesn't cost you much. You reset your score multiplier and lose a bullet, but you can reload those so fast as to be fundamentally invincible. With Gunvolt, you have to know when to let off the attack pressure to focus on dodging, because being in attack mode when you get hit causes you to take automatic damage.I didn't think either character felt bad, but I did find Copen's secret final boss annoying enough that I skipped out of the game and youtubed the ending.The ending is genuinely satisfying---sort of rare for the genre---and I'm eager to see where the series goes.Support these games if you can. Inti Creates is making something really excellent here.Also, if it'll help decide you on whether this game is right for you, there's a section where you are supposed to actually karaoke into the microphone in Japanese as a fight mechanic. It's not mandatory. You can cheese special attacks instead. But I love seeing games pulling wild stuff like this, and the moment itself is weirdly kind of hype.

_childDocuments_.review: gunvolt has been my hyperfixation for a few years so maybe im biased but gunvolt 2 is genuinely such a fun game. i originally played it on the 3ds when it came out at first and it’s been my fav game ever since. now...gv2 obviously got problems, for starter the writing can be hit or miss. actually i would call it kinda bad but tbh unless you get really into it, it probably wont leave a huge impact on you. this is def one of those games / serie that value gameplay over the story. which isnt really bad per se but you know what i mean, ie dont start this game thinking you'll find the best story of the century. it can still hit pretty hard at time despite everything thoughto continue, some call the mission system bad, but i personally find it fine as it give some replayability to it. having to complete most of them to unlock the true + special ending is not so great but i dont really mind it. might be deal breaker for someone who wants those achievement though. others will talk about the crafting system being grindy, but tbh you can go the whole game without ordering any special gears. also each briefings will tell you which level have which materials in the ending screen, so you can take note of it if a certain gear interest you. gv2 is really generous with the materials and money it gives you in my opinion.if you can bypass these though? then i would absolutely recommend it! if gunvolt’s playstyle is a bit slow and very much like the first game, copen’s playstyle is all about going fast and getting combos and kudos to get high scores, and its so fun to play as him. the ost is great both vocal and general wise, and while id say this is the only time ix top gv2, its still really solid. the bosses are a delight characters wise and seeing them being united together and interact with each others makes my heart warm. its definitely a contrast compared to sumeragi who has no ties to each other. if you enjoy the found family trope i think you’ll enjoy them! dont really have anything to say about the side casts, theyre fine. reading the chats between gv and copen with their respective casts was fun thoughhum i think thats it! gv2 is a very fun game and if you end up trying it i hope you enjoy it ❤

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the first game but from what I played in this one, it seems to be very fun. I chose this game over GV1 because a lot of people I knew recommended me the sequels so I decided to give this a shot. I hope one day I get my hands on GV1 but we'll see.I did know about Gunvolt for a while and was interested to play the games so I could form my own opinions, at first I thought they were pretty fine but as I kept playing the game, it got harder and required a lot from the player. It felt rewarding doing the perfect runs even though I still struggle with doing them consistently so I can keep hearing these songs by Joule/Lola because they sound really energetic and up to my Alley.The gameplay is split into 2 characters, GV and Copen. Both characters like X and Zero in X4 excell in gameplay equally. For some, Copen might be cooler but GV is also minimalistically cool too. His flashfield is also really useful as a secondary shield when getting attacked by bomb based projectiles. His darts or guns do offer new attacks but I have a feeling they are mostly situational. His EX skills also come in handy. Copen on the other hand is mostly focused on flying and man does it feel great to do that consistently, his copy abilities or special weapons are also useful in situational areas. Both characters have their own pros and cons and I think GV2 does a pretty good job with them. I kind of suck at doing no damage run but I hope one day I do the one perfeclty and master the gameplay.The level design is really solid but kind of can feel a little bit samey. But that's the only issue I have with the level design. It can vary in what it offers but still, I wish there were more remarkeable gimmicks for each stage.The bosses are really good, they have readeable pattern and are understandable to learn but hard to master. Their ex skills are also visually cool.The story is servicable, usual IntiCreates stuff if you have followed the series from GV1.Nothing much to say.The sound design and visuals are really cool too. I like the artstyle of the GV games and the sound effects fit well with GV. The music is no exception  as it also has bangers. The vocal tracks are the highlight most of the time and I can agree on that but I don't listen to it casually out loud because it would feel weird to some people.Overall, a blast of a game, I wish to play other GV games like 1 and iX and even 3 once it comes out but from what I experienced, it was pretty fun. It's far from perfect like any viday but still a reasonably consistent game.

_childDocuments_.review: The 2D high speed, old-school style side-scrolling action that you remember from Azure Striker Gunvolt is back. In this game, Gunvolt's rival Copen from the first installment returns to the fray as a playable character. Prevasion: This ability allows Gunvolt to neutralize enemy attacks at the cost of his EP energy. Copen also has an ability exactly like this. Kudos is a point system that increases whenever you deal damage to an enemy. Whenever you take damage, your Kudos are reduced to zero. When activating a save point, using a special skill or clearing a mission, Kudos are converted into bonus points. The Muse's song: For as long as you can maintain 1000 or more Kudos, the BGM will change and Lumen AKA The Muse (or in Copen's story, Lola) will sing for you. Anthem: When Gunvolt or Copen's HP reaches 0, the Muse's power can bring them back to life, with additional power-ups. In that state, the BGM will change to the Muse's song. [Nintendo.com]

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a mediocre game that feels like a PS3/Xbox 360 era game.The environments look great, the gunplay is alright, the characters exceptionally boring, and the story/lore leaves a lot to be desired.While playing this game, the player character would constantly get stuck on terrain. The scripted movement to and from different areas is absurdly restrictive for a game released in 2022. The upgrade system was boring and more of a chore. Such a limited skill "tree" lead to moments where I didn't care that I had an upgrade because none of them seemed interesting or seemed to make much of a difference gameplay-wise. The puzzles were tedious and boring, and the constant "loading" transitions took the pace out of the game.Going from area to area to fight another assortment of annoying, bullet sponge enemies became tediously formulaic after the first or second level. The weak spot mechanic was fine enough but oftentimes the window to hit the weak spot was too short. This game truly feels like it was designed a decade ago.  I finished Evil West because I paid $40 for it and wanted to get my money's worth. That being said, this game is maybe worth $20. Overall, Evil West is a boring, corridor shooter with some interesting moments, frustrating combat, and a weak story that ends up ending so abruptly you'll get whiplash. Save your money altogether or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The first few hours are overall pretty fun and enjoyable, up until the point where the game decides to stop playing fair and starts throwing at you multiple mini-bosses at the same time.And mini-bosses here don't just have more health: they are designed to be fought in a "duel" and require your full attention. They have attacks that you have to dodge or prevent (by shooting their weakspots) otherwise you'll take massive damge.So you're constantly having to juggle multiple of those, plus fodder enemies, while trying to engage them in melee (guns don't do much damage), which results in a lot of running around, waiting for cooldowns to grant you an opening.Bosses on the other hand are mostly fun to fight, although for a few of them wether or not you're alive at the end of their combos really comes down to luck.The combat does not help either. While it's kinda enjoyable and interesting, it is also very clunky. Often times it feels like walking through glue because the controls aren't responsive enough.It should also be mentioned that this is a fighting game, not a shooter: ranged weapons are relegated to shooting weakspots and objectives.The levels are...boring. Aside the fact that they're "linear", they all repeat the same pattern with little variety:Exploration/puzzles > arena fight > exploration/puzzles > arena fight > exploration/puzzles > level boss/arena fight.If it wasn't for the narrative, it would have become too boring to continue.It's kinda unfortunate because the games's premise was pretty good: you're a cowboy in the Wild West fighting vampires.The atmosphere varies from serious to comedic, but it was refreshing to have a badass main character that just yells "What the ♥♥♥♥ are you!?" when he encounters a new enemy, instead of having snarky remarks or one-liners (then again, it still gets cheesy towards the middle).It just seems like they dropped the ball with the combat encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first half of this game but it got extremely repetitive after that. They also rely on some extremely questionable enemies and bosses to make the game challenging. At first this game was a recommend, but some of the cons (outlined below) led me to change my opinion by the end of the game.Pros:- Combat has lots of variety, it is extremely fun at first, the game makes you feel like a badass and is reminiscent of games it clearly gets it's inspiration from (i.e. Gears of War, newer God of War game, among others)- I really enjoyed the art style of the game, I wouldn't say the graphics are as good as other games coming out in recent memory but everything is stylized well and thus makes it fun look around and explore the environments- The sound design is very good IMO, the gun/combat/explosions are very "crisp" for lack of a better word, this contributes to the first pro I mentioned, making the combat feel satisfying- Performance was great, I didn't watch frame-rates the whole game but was around 100-120 fps the couple times I checked and did not notice any drops (3440x1440, i7 13000K, RTX 3080, 32GB Ram, Epic settings, DLSS - Quality)Neutral: - New Game +, I didn't enjoy my first play through enough to bother with this but if it's your cup of tea I could see the appeal with a second play through on a harder difficulty and collectible/trophy hunting- The story is incredibly generic, characters are forgettable, this is a minor con for me, the games focus is obviously combat and I can forget a sub-par story if it's fun otherwise, but was another nail in the coffin for me- The game consists of 16 levels, roughly 30-40 minutes each (about 10.5 hours total) this is on the short side but in the acceptable range of an ideal length for me personally if I'm enjoying a gameCons:- While the combat itself had lots of options and variety, the encounters themselves got extremely repetitive, it's pretty much walk through an area, do a mundane puzzle a 2 year old could solve, 2-3 enemy encounters, maybe a boss, rinse and repeat- There are some enemies and bosses I personally took issue with, they have a tendency to take everything you've learned and all the upgrades and skills you've acquired and then throw out the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ window and make them useless, especially during boss battles, I'm sure the intent was to make the game feel more challenging but to me it made the game feel unpredictable at times and annoyed me- There were several occasions where I'd jump over a small barrier then not be able to backtrack for collectibles, even if I could see the path to get the collectible but could no longer access it. I'm not sure what the intent was here, if it was to "sandbox" areas/battles or just a cheap method of forcing you to play the missions more than once but I found it frustrating- Hive Crones -- these enemies (not bosses, just enemies) almost caused me to put down the game down mid-way, they basically make every other enemy in the arena invincible unless you shoot these floating orbs that revolve around them, this would be fine if aiming and hit boxes weren't atrocious in this game. Similarly the game relies on vast amounts of enemies and chaos for it's challenge so I found it extremely frustrating to crowd control a bunch of invincible enemies that were directly in the way of the single enemy I was obviously supposed to focus on. These Hive Crones show up A LOT in the later stages of the game as well which is why I almost rage quit (I played on normal difficulty)

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West: God of War gameplay set in a fantasy mythological Wild West.First I'd like to briefly touch on the story. The Story is okay, definitely on the upper tiers of storyline for this kind of game, it's certainly nothing absolutely outstanding but it's written well enough to keep you interested in what's happening in the world and where the story is going, thus giving credence to the missions that you're on. It can be a little cheesy at times, yes, whether this was deliberate or not is hard to tell; I just told myself that it was part of that old Spaghetti Western type dialogue from time to time, just to suit with the theme.The gameplay and art direction is 100% where this game excels. As mentioned before and in other reviews, the gameplay is similar to God of War except you have a lot more at your disposal in terms of items. You have a plethora of ranged weapons and melee weapons to use in your arsenal, and believe me, you will use them all. The game staggers how frequently you get weapons so you don't ever feel overwhelmed at having 8+ options at the one time going, which is definitely a good thing.Combat is satisfying and bloody, it's unapologetic in its fights, it reminded me of that same feeling of, for lack of a better word, "Manliness" that you feel when playing DOOM for the first time. Just constant shooting and battering and blood and bits flying everywhere, makes you feel pretty cool after dealing with a horde of vampire familiars. There's two types of "Perk/Talent" Trees in the game, for your weapons, your upgrade them with "Bucks" which is just money, which you'll find dotted around each level just ripe for the picking, which I'd recommend exploring the maps a little, as you'll almost always be rewarded with money. The other one is the Perk tree, basically just upgrades for your character and different moves you can use to ensure your survival; standard stuff.The Art Direction is absolutely phenomenal, the set-pieces are genuinely gorgeous. I don't know what they did with the colour palette and the lighting but it genuinely looks and feels great to be in these places. It's very high/dark fantasy in that respect. The way the ominous red glow of the mist paints the area in a blood like rain, or how the fire grows and roars around you, to the blue-green swirling of souls which all reflect on your characters armour, making the lighting feel more real; even if a -little- cartoonish, it's a great style and I wish more games did this. The game is very colourful and a lot of the maps feel very unique to the mission you're on, making you feel like you're advancing and seeing more of the world that the developers have built.What I will say is though, the game is pretty tough in some areas. It does suffer a little from the trope of, "This was a boss three levels ago, now it's just a mini-boss." Which isn't too bad because you get more powerful as the game goes and you can really feel it. There are some bosses as well in the game that you just need to grind out, die a bunch of time before you learn what works. I had a tough time against some of them and I was playing on Normal difficulty, god knows what lies ahead on the harder ones.There also seems to be a weird lighting glitch in the hub zone, when you're just sprinting around, little flicks of white will appear on the walls as if it's being rendered; it's weird, noticeable but not game breaking, other than that the only bugs I encountered was the occasional floating body after killing something in mid-air. Easily overlooked in my opinion but nothing game breaking at all.The game has a lot of actual pre-rendered cutscenes, which for me was a welcome surprise, felt like I've not properly seen that in a long time, most cutscenes nowadays are basically just the in-game engine and models but animated, these are more like cutscenes which we used to see in older games. A very welcome surprise and I always looked forward to the next one. Overall, the game took me around 10 hours to complete, which isn't bad for a £43 game. There is new game plus which I might go back to at some point, or if a friend picks it up I'll play Co-Op with them. And not to make a snide comparison but when some games are charging £59.99 for an old IP with no actual improvements, yes I'm looking at you Call of Duty and Fifa, I feel that £43 for something new isn't hard to justify.For me the game is a very strong 7/10, might have scored higher if certain parts of the game weren't repetitive, such as powering things up, the game being a little bit longer and with a stronger story. But generally, this is a great game that really held my attention and I enjoyed playing it to completion.Lastly I'd just like to say, in a day and age where most games are just Remakes, Remasters, Sequels or Prequels to already pre-existing franchising, be like Evil West, be something different and original, something made with passion and something fresh.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: you play as a cowboy vampire slayer with God of War like combat. Game is completely linear, with some story  sprinkled in just to tie the levels together. But that doesn't really matter because the main focus of the game is the combat. It's fast paced, smooth and satisfying. With a nice arsenal of weapons and combos, and an impressive enemy variety, the combat is what absolutely makes this game. The first time I launched a vampire in the air with an uppercut and superman  punched him into oblivion felt so good that i spent the entire level just running towards the next enemy encounter so i can "outcool" myself. And that's what the game comes down to in the end. Running from arena to arena, blasting monsters away and wondering what new monstrosity awaits so you can kill it in a cool new way. Puzzles, story, unlockables, lore and other fluff doesn't really matter. That might put some people off, but I found it refreshing that the game isn't pretentious, and just delivers good old kick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a tight and rather pretty looking package (graphics are nice, albeit nothing special, UE4 is the engine and the visual style is awesome imo). My only gripe with the design is that the arenas are too similar, you already know when you approach a relatively open area that a fight is about to go down. I was never surprised. It's: "Oh i jump down there with no way back up? Enemy time."Overall a solid game. It's not GOTY material, but it's worth it if you're into this type of action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game especially if you like the setting but i honestly expected more in terms of playstyle customization because with the default one the combat gets boring very fast and there isnt much outside of combat in this game. Also for that price i would expect a bit more than 16 very linear missions. Another issue  is that the main character is very unlikable at least to me. He is constantly very rude and arrogant to everyone that tries to help him especially to people that admire and look up to him. The Enemy variation is good but because of the default playstyle, most enemies are defeated the same way some are just defeated faster and some slower. Of course many things could be added like different outfits to really make Jesse feel like our character but i also understand that thats a secondary concern when making a game. The World of the game feels very interesting so its a real shame that the locations we visit are quite boring and dont make sense in terms of how they are built. It is very obvious that all of the locations you visit are made for combat which takes away from the realism and immersion of the world. I Tried my best to give some creative criticism in this review because i really thing that this game or at least this world have a lot of potential.TLDR: Good Quality but feels empty and quickly gets boring. Buy when on sale at 50% or more for a few hours for some cool fantasy cowboy vampire hunter time

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of fun! FWH trademark senseless over the top violence is working wonder here, the fight mechanics are very, very satisfying, controls are just right, and while it's possible to use the same tactics most of the time, variations are definitely rewarding. The perks and upgrade systems might seem a bit short at first, but it is in fact well thought and balanced. The game does a great job of explaining its mechanics, and is surprisingly very clear and readable, considering that some battles are bound to evolve into absolute mayhem by design. The art style might not be for everyone. I liked it, it's refreshing that they actually designed their characters to look like they're straight out of a comics. The tech is a bit meh, especially in the lighting department. Monsters designs are ridiculously gross and complex (in a great way), plentiful and varied. The script is actually not bad, it's pretty much a B movie with cocky punchlines and a pleasant plot. At least on par with most so called AAA titles in the genre. A good old fashioned action game with just enough modernity to fit nicely in this era. Get this!

_childDocuments_.review: Scenic locales, bloody finishers, boxcars, and bullets. It feels like a 7th gen, and I'm okay with that. Fun story, animated characters, and challenging odds. You'll need two playthroughs to get max upgrades, which you'll desperately need to finish the last few fights. I collected everything on easy and got what I could remember on the highest difficulty, and finished with about 100 bucks to spare right before I got to the final boss. You'll breeze through most levels, they're about 15 or 20 minutes each, and you'll need to balance high intensity melee and ranged combat. You get boxed in a lot and have to constantly move around a tight space, dodging everything and letting off as many shots as you can.
