_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It gives you a variety of tools and incentivizes you to use all of them for their intended purposes. The enemy variety is nice with all of them requiring different strategies. I expected the level design to be boring and generic and it kind of is, but the environments are wonderful. I expected it to be basically all western style towns and get repetitive, but there is way more variety. An oil field, snowy mountains, rainy forests. Way better than I thought. The story was decent enough with good characters and the cinematics were excellent and well-made. My only complaint is I feel the game as almost no replayability. You get NG+ and you can go through again with all these abilities and weapons you've unlocked, but the enemy variety doesn't change and it doesn't really change the experience. It feels a little clunky but I feel that is intentional and doesn't hinder the experience as much as feeling like the style of the game. The music is really good but used sparingly and I wish there was more. I think the biggest problem is that it gets very repetitive and is like Shadow Warrior 3. There is very little exploration from Point A to Point B and doesn't really offer much that is interesting. It is a hallway of a game that takes you between arena fights. I haven't played the Co-Op yet but I heard about problems from that as well so fair warning. I also think that, on higher difficulties the enemies feeling a little spongy and it can be annoying. Overall though I had a positive experience with this game, and would recommend it if you enjoy PS3-Era games or the God of War franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil west is a pretty good game, we don't have enough urban fantasy type games out there much less in the "Weird West" flavor.Its got style, flair, decent characters, good combat and simple but fun to use mechanics.So whats wrong with it? why isn't it a big hit like Devil May cry a series it clearly takes some nods from.I think it largely boils down to 2 factors.1. Boring arenas, Evil West feels like it would have benefitted greatly from more open ended combat like more traditional games but instead it leans heavily into the arena combat style where you enter a large and very obvious arena to fight baddies, most fights seem to boil down to 1 or 2 main bad guys with a handfull of lesser bad guys, sometimes its 2 big bads and when one dies minions start pouring in. It becomes REALLY by the numbers after a while to the point of boredom.It would have benefitted the game greatly to have enemies scattered throughout, we could still use the arenas for mini bosses or the like but the current format just feels really boring.2. The enemies themselves. Alot of the enemies, particularly the vampires feel dull, they aren't visually striking. Some are a chaotic jumble of metal and flesh and while on paper this sounds good the actual result comes off uninspired.Its a shame because theres some real talent here, animations are smooth and crisp, the fighting feels pretty good and the style of the weapons is the perfect flavor of steam punk meets practical weaponry, you even get some basic customization in the form of skins.Evil West feels like a game out of time, it feels like it would have been a PERFECT game for the 360 back in the 2010s but by today's standards it feels a tad late to the party.Its still a pretty good game and definitely solid from a mechanic standpoint but I just feel like its missing that one piece to make it really pop.

The story itself is great and the characters are extremely well made. Voice acting is 10/10, the cut scenes do a fantastic job engaging you in the story. Downside is that the story is too short and feels rushed around the halfway mark.Overall the game is good but could not rate it as such due to massive potential Flying Wild Hog's missed with this. They produced an awesome idea and great mechanics, would love to see them produce a Souls like with the same energy as the last two bosses. It's a very linear game where it holds your hand throughout the experience which some prefer and isn't necessarily a bad thing.The bosses that stood out the absolute most making this game enjoyable were, The Parasiter and the last two bosses. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a third person melee/shooter hybrid game about cowboys murdering evil vampires trying to take over the country. You play as Jesse Rentier, heir to the Rentier Institute (of murdering vampires or something, idk, I only remember Rentier Institute because it's etched on Jesse's gauntlet and has a cool animation on the main menu screen) on the hunt for a big bad vampire until the hunter becomes the hunted. And if that sounds like a fun action game premise for you, definitely buy it. However I am going to elaborate a little more on the game.First, the gameplay is sound & satisfying. One note though, this game is a primarily melee focused game. Your guns act more as abilities on cooldown with ammo being said cooldown regenerating over time. I was lead into believing this game was a shooter as are most games set in the wild west but I'll be honest, the realisation that this was something else halfway through the first mission was quite surprising. Modern games don't quite often surprise me, so this is a welcome change of pace. One gripe I have is that the whole kit is not available to you until you are halfway through the game, which is a disappointment because the combat & the enemies aggressive behaviour results in a fun encounter to overcome with your arsenal of melee combos & electrified steampunk weaponry. Each new addition to your arsenal or game changing perk upgrade for your weapons always generate an instant dopamine hit by just seeing the demo videos of what said perk can do in the upgrade screen. The last 3 missions are the only place where you can utilise your full kit which leads to a sense of just wanting more game from this game. My only hopes for a sequel(if there is one) is for more of Jesse's kit to available from the get-go because like I iterated before, the gameplay is really fun. The game has to offer a grand total of 4 unique bosses & yes that's not very much. The boss fights I feel are not a highlight of this game & that might be due to their not very challenging mechanics or just the fact that the regular encounters of smashing uber aggressive vampires into one another & overpowering them with your great arsenal is just infinitely more fun. There are mini bosses that start as a boss & become regular enemies but those are even less of a highlight in their solo fight & become much of a menace when they come in groups in the late game.Second, the atmosphere of the game is a beautiful immersion into an over-steam-punkified version of the wild west. Sure it's not as realistic as Red Dead's dynamic weather based horse balls, nor as mind blowing what any over budgeted AAA studio could conjure up but that doesn't stop it from creating beautiful landscapes with their limited resources. The game explores all kinds of environments from wild west deserts, to snowy mountains, to swamps & damp forests & back to some more wild west towns & even a mine. And all of those combined with the game semi-cartoony but still grounded in reality art style lends itself quite well to the experience of being a steam-punk vampire hunting cowboy. The character model of Jesse is quite standard wild west cowboy type but when you reach the endgame he looks like a poor burdened soul carry all these giant steampunk weaponries, you might like or dislike that but the only emotion it produced in me is amusement.Lastly, comes the story and in this part I have no props to give except that it produced no negative emotions in me. It's all quite bland & generic, it takes no risk, it doesn't fumble anywhere, it doesn't excel anywhere. It just gets the job done & that job being to get you from one mission to the next and maybe generate a chuckle or two here & there with one-liners & quips as in game dialogue. The cutscenes are quite well animated.In conclusion, Evil West is a very good action combat game & is definitely worth a buy if great combat is primarily what you are looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, at times, can be really fun. At other times, it is the most frustratingly broken experience I have had in recent memory.Design: It is  a series of corridors that connect a series of arenas. Exploration is limited, gather hidden perks and money to level up. The perk system is quite unbalanced, with many essential abilities outclassing other quirky ones. Combat is fast and fluid, reminds me of Doom Eternal in a way, with finisher animations giving health and energy. Progression could have been handled differently without requiring levels but through just progressing normally. Boss battles generally are a frustrating slog, in the late game it starts to throw a bunch of mini boss enemies all at once. Presentation: The graphics are really great, though the color saturation can be off putting at times. The gore and atmosphere are quite enjoyable. Environments are varied and fleshed out. The story is enjoyable though not deep. Cut-scenes are well crafted and the voice acting is fitting. *my biggest issue*My girlfriend and I played through this game co-op. The co-op was obviously tacked on and an afterthought. It is not true co op as player 2 plays as a clone. Co op is busted at times, with multiple visual glitches and getting stuck on geometry. Youtube co-op gameplay and you will see a multitude examples of it. Bottom line: Buy this when it goes on sale and play through it single player. Its fun, dumb fun, but fun. Like the cheezy horror film that's a guilty pleasure, enjoy it by yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the most fun game I've ever played! So far, I've only experienced it in co-op mode with my best buddy, but I can confidently say I've never had so much fun gaming before.Gameplay ExperienceEvil West captures the action-packed intensity reminiscent of Gears of War, but it uniquely blends elements of the Wild West with supernatural horror. The game offers a wide range of attack options, including a gunslinging revolver, a long-distance rifle, a sawn-off shotgun, and even a flamethrower. Each weapon feels thrilling to use, and combat is enhanced by various abilities and perks that allow for powerful hand-to-hand combat. One standout feature is the ability to grapple enemies, which adds an exciting layer to combat strategy. You can pull foes closer for devastating melee attacks or create space when overwhelmed. Additionally, there's a shocker ability that allows you to electrocute enemies, turning them into dust and adding a visually spectacular element to your attacks.Combat MechanicsThe combat mechanics are incredibly engaging, allowing players to tackle some of the craziest-looking and acting vampires, werewolves, and other terrifying monsters. The combination of grappling and electrocution keeps each encounter fresh and exhilarating. My friend has progressed even further in his single-player quests and has unlocked even more features than I’ve experienced so far. This means there’s always something new to upgrade and explore!ConclusionThe scare and thrill of this game for both my best friend and me are simply off the charts! With its unique blend of genres and exhilarating gameplay, I give Evil West a solid 10/10. If you're looking for an adrenaline-pumping experience with friends or solo, this game is definitely worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: Gamplay: If you're looking for something that just kill all the things with gratuitous violence, then this game is a great one. Reminds me a lot of Bulletstorm. The game is definitely designed with a controller in mind as the keyboard controls are a bit difficult and fiddly. I often wished my mouse had more buttons so weapons were a bit easier to select and use. There were times I just didn't end up using certain items or gear because it was too difficult to swap to during the action. I think however my biggest issue was constantly being knocked out of sprint and having to just be holding shift the entire game; a toggle to sprint option would definitely have been a benefit.Story: Story is a little predictable, but still enjoyable for what it was. The humor did remind me of old times while playing PS2 games.Bugs: Ran into a number of bugs, though most of the issues were just visual vs anything totally game breaking. There was a few instances where a sound from one particular monster would get stuck and constantly be playing and I had to back out to the main menu to get it to stop. I don't believe however this game was optimized for PC and ran a bit clunky. Even for my 3080ti, I had to turn down certain graphics in order to avoid some freezing.EDIT: 11/24/22 Was able to wrangle a friend to play the campaign coop. The game is definitely not designed for it. Both players play the same MC, both players are needed in order to proceed to next areas in a very odd way. There are enough bugs to really break the enjoyment of the gameplay for either players. Targeting is really broken when using melee or zapper abilities, in the early "tutorial" style areas where players are forced into a menu, the game itself does not pause and both players are attacked without any indication. I've also been unable to utilize a leveled character in multiplayer and end up having to build a new character for whatever reason. I also highly recommend playing on Hard or Evil as the normal 15hr campaign gets reduced to about 6-7 or less in coop.TL;DR: I'd rate it a good 6/10... definitely worth a play through in single player. At one point I played the game for 9hrs and didn't realize I had played for 9hrs. I recommend avoiding the coop.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could choose a middle way for voting Evil West, I would have chosen it, because Evil West gameplay in itself is good, but it misses in so many aspects, that I can't recommend it (at full price) for the general public. The arsenal of guns, the skill trees and gadgets at your disposal are easily the best aspect of the game, what makes a fight really fun to begin with...and I mean, punching vampires in their stupid faces with a electrocuting gauntlet is stupidly fun...but the game at some point falls shy on giving you a real challenge, and it becomes a tedious trial and error where you start to wonder if it was even a good idea to give both your time and money to it. Sometimes It feels like you don't have the same means that your enemies have, and it becomes a ruthless experience where you start rolling around praying to not get hit by a massive boulder or a fire blaze covering 1/3 of the screen while waiting for your abilities to recharge. I say this because Evil West becomes unfair and unrelenting in the very last chapters (some say even sooner), throwing at you ANYTHING it can. I really like a true challenge myself (playing NG+ on Evil difficulty right now), and this in fact delivers on it, but way too mindlessly and in a bad way, unlike Dark Souls or Doom nail at the entrance.Music score might be the worst part of the game tho. It's a droning and looping soundtrack in way too many encounters, to the point that it sinks in your brain becoming a white noise living in the back of your head. I'm really sorry for the composer, but, this is not even debatable, the OST is so very forgettable (except for a couple of soothing acoustic pieces).Voice acting and dialogues are surprisingly good and sort of belieavable, given the world they're set in, and Jesse is not a complete goofball. Story is ok in the end, mainly because some characters are just fit for it and not so poorly written.If I had to give a vote to it, it would be something barely scratching a 6/10.If you have an itch for games similar to Gears of War, Castlevania: Lords of Shadows or DMC, this is the bare bones of 'em, since it's even more linear and straight forward in every aspect, and I would suggest you to give it a try. Other than that, very skippable if you're not a fan of fast action centered games.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen some pretty mixed things on this game, and honestly I'm not sure I know why. the base price is lower than a standard AAA title to reflect its slightly lower budget, but like many games from the 2010s, there's a lot to enjoy  if you can look past the issues.Essentially a shlockier version of the Order: 1886 (and better for it), you play as Jesse Rentier, a member of the Rentier Institute, essentially a steampunk Van Helsing type organization. Functionally he looks kind of like a Belmont, which is nice to see, but he isn't super interesting, and in fact, the game's biggest flaw is how much it prattles on. I appreciate that it does take time to try and develop the characters, but the fact is they're all pretty basic archetypes that just so happen to have some solid voice acting behind them (I will say, there's a character who is a senator that is just a huge prick, and his voice actor consistently made me laugh for how over the top he gets). The story is completely fine, but not the main attraction.That would be the combat. Despite taking place in the old west, this isn't a shooter. Instead, it's a 3D beat 'em up that borrows elements from titles like God of War 2018 and Doom 2016/ Eternal to create a surprisingly fluid fighting style. The game wisely doesn't overwhelm you with all your options from the start and instead doles out new skills about once per level. It does take a while to unlock everything, but there's a very distinct power curve and honestly fights felt like tightly choreographed chaos; you always have multiple options at your disposal, and some of the unlockable perks push your abilities even further. For instance, there's a Hero Punch, where you uppercut an enemy into the air, then launch it into objects or other enemies. It's potent enough on its own, but combine that with the perk that makes slung enemies explode on contact, and you have a move that is just as fun the first time as it is the fiftieth.And at least on Normal, I think the game does a great job of making sure you use these abilities. Nothing in your moveset is limited; instead, everything is on a cooldown, and this means when you think you're out of one ability, suddenly you have another at your disposal. In a lesser balanced game, you might be overpowered by the end, but the large hordes the game throws at you force you to engage with pretty much every move you have. I've seen people say that the game devoves into a repetitive slug fest and while that's true depending on how you look at it, I saw the last couple of levels as an opportunity to play around with the arsenal. Honestly, when you successfully clear a wave of enemies, the encounter will likely only last a few minutes, and you find yourself playing a really enjoyable juggling act with your arsenal and the crowd. I never felt like the game was too much despite how much it throws at you, and the steady stream of unlocks big and small really kept me pushing forward.I got this on sale for twenty bucks and honestly I'd say it's worth it at that price. It's not a huge ambitious game, and that does reflect in its issues. There are some frame rate hitches every once in a while and I had a couple of frustrating glitches that forced me to reload checkpoints. But it's nothing game breaking by any means. It has some issues, but it does its combat system really well. This is very much the kind of game I could see becoming something of a cult classic in the future considering its generally strong art direction and shlocky B movie thrills in gameplay form. It's not high art, it's not a deep artistic experience, but it is a REALLY good time while it lasts.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is what I would classify as an absolute banger of a 7/10. If you watch a lot of campy horror movies or played PS360 era shooters like Lost Planet or Army of Two, think of those games but with the narrative tone and aesthetic of a movie like From Dusk Till Dawn. And it also plays like God of War 2018. And maybe as if it was made by Platinum Games, but an alternate universe Platinum where they were actually a AA Polish game developer. You follow me so far? I hope so, because this makes sense to me but might also make it a hard sell if you're not entirely sure if it's your cup of tea. So let's reel it back a bit and break the game down a bit more.Evil West is an action game where you play as a cowboy vampire hunter by the name of Jesse Rentier, part of the Rentier Institute dynasty. You go on adventures to stop the Big Bad Vampire lady by the name of Felicity D'Abano, and fight many more different enemies and characters on the journey to stop her from taking over the world. The story is entertaining with likable characters and fun cutscenes, but the story and plot are a bit forgettable imo. I played this game over the span of a couple months so the details a bit lost to me, but the plot and narrative are not super innovative or anything like that. It's just a means to move the player from each level and scenario, so if your focus is to get a God of War level narrative, don't expect that out of this game. I do however find the characters and dialogue to be fun and engaging in a campy over-the-top way.But if you're looking for a fun action game, then Evil West is right up your alley. I find that the combat is snappy, fun, and a good twitch shooter/beat-em-up hybrid. It's very similar to GoW in that regard, but with far more emphasis on third person shooting, which is a ton of fun and has fantastic progression with new abilities, weapons, and gadgets constantly being thrown at the player pretty much right up until the last couple levels where the game really tests your skills to use all these tools during the most intense fights. I can see this game being a bit of a slog if you tried to marathon it, but if you play in short bursts over multiple sessions, I think you will find a lot to love and mechanics to sink your teeth into.Overall I found the controls to work really well on a gamepad (and with Mouse Gyro enabled via Steam Input), but kb&m is apparently busted according to other reviews, so I would consider this a gamepad recommended experience before diving in. This game also performs well on a Steam Deck with mixed settings, but if you want stable framerates at 40 FPS, FSR is required for hitting those targets. It can run at 60, but for consistent framerates it's gonna require some major cutbacks and sacrifices, so I'd say aim for 40 FPS when playing on the Deck and you can play with close to native resolution. On a more caipable rig, this game hits 4K 120 fps easily (at least on my 3080/5600x build and DLSS set to Quality).Speaking of graphics and presentation, this is another aspect where Evil West shines. It's easily one of the most captivating and creative AA games I've played in a long time, with some incredibly striking and awesome art direction and overall very pretty graphics. Character designs and enemies look great, and the sound design is incredibly satisfying when wailing on enemies and firing all your weapons. The soundtrack is good but not YouTube playlist stand-out, just appropriate for the setting and does a good job building the atmosphere. I wish the level design was a bit more intricate and interesting, but it does enough to keep things varied and fun, with laser focus on providing good arenas for the combat.To wrap things up, I think this is going to be the defining cult classic of the decade, and has a lot of value in being a tight, fun, and engaging action game. I wouldn't exactly recommend getting this game at 60 bucks, as it's not a super long game at between 12-15 hours, and can be a little on the janky side in game. Nothing game breaking or unforgivable, it's just something you're going to notice when playing. God of War polish, this game does not have. But combat that's arguably more tight and fun than God of War, this game does have. For a good sale, this is a great game. It also has a co-op and New Game+ mode (neither of which I tried), which does add some value if you want to play the whole game with your friend. I recommend playing it to anyone who has an itch for mechanically rich, stimulating action games and/or likes the horror-western fusion aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West | ★★★★☆I'm recommending this game in hope for a potential sequel. It combines elements of God of War, Devi May Cry and some Red Dead gunplay, although it doesn't quite reach the same level of polish as those three. Nonetheless, it's a decently enjoyable linear game with satisfying combat and a wide range of weapons that become more chaotic as you progress.While the game is enjoyable, there are a few aspects that bothered me during my playthrough. Firstly, there are a lot of paths with invisible walls that hinder your exploration, and game objects tend to appear suddenly as you approach them, which can be distracting. Additionally, the puzzles in the game felt rather lackluster, failing to fully utilize the diverse arsenal of weapons you have for puzzle implementation. Furthermore, in-game characters don't animate their mouths when speaking, which detracted from the immersion.In terms of the story, it's decent and provides sufficient justification for your character's actions and motivations. If you're familiar with Shadow Warrior, another game developed by the same team, you'll notice similarities in terms of tone and style—it's like a third-person version of that game. Personally, I enjoy this kind of experience reminiscent of the fun-focused single player games like from the PS2 era.Despite its flaws, I hope that the developers address and improve upon these issues in a potential follow-up game. All in all, this game offers an enjoyable gameplay experience, and if you're a fan of action-packed adventures, it's worth giving a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I like this game so far, and I hope in the end it's worth the $50 price point. Here are my impressions in my first three hours of play-through. 1) The combat is fun, but it doesn't give you much incentive to use all the tools given to you. You can look at this two ways, you can say that it gives you the freedom to choose how you want to fight, or you can say that the combat is under-developed. I have had a lot of fun so far, but I have to say I lean towards the latter. For example, DOOM (2016) and DOOM Eternal both give you a lot of tools, then force you to constantly cycle through your weapons in order to kill your enemies with efficiency. In Evil West, cycling through your weapons can make the combat more interesting, but you can get away with exclusively using melee attacks and the occasional rifle shot. Using the shotgun, zapper, cross thing, etc. can be really fun but sometimes when I get caught up in an intense fight I result to just using the basic melee attack while spamming dodge, and the game lets me get away with it. Not a huge problem but it definitely feels like the combat has WAY more potential than its current state. Still fun though.2) The story/acting is sub-par for the $50 price tag. The voice acting is like 5/10 at best, the dialogue is not great, and the story so far seems so-so. It drops you in the middle of an on-going story (this is fine, stories do this frequently), but it does so without giving you any context. You just have to figure things out on the fly, and the lore blurbs do little to help you understand the full content of the story. If you are just looking for entertaining gameplay like me, this can easily be ignored. However if a truly attention grabbing story is what you're looking for, I'd hold onto your money and wait for at least a 50% off sale. 3) Graphics are amazing. The lighting can be a little annoying on certain levels but it does capture the "cowboys in the blazing desert sun" vibe so it's not terrible. But yeah, the game looks pretty great. not much to say otherwise except there is a snow level, and yes, you can draw a ♥♥♥♥ in the snow.4) Intended difficulty may be too easy. obviously this is a subjective statement and difficulty in games varies from player to player. That being said, I usually play games on the developer-recommended difficulty so I can play games the way they were meant to be played. However, I find that you can heal much too frequently, and it may be worth raising the difficulty so combat feels a little more engaging/challenging.5) Puzzle sequences are comparable to God of War. I wouldn't say they're as complex but honestly I personally find puzzle sequences in combat oriented games to be boring slogs no matter how complex, so part of me is grateful that you can complete the puzzle sequences a little faster in this game. 6) Co-op does not save the guest player's progress. If you are intending to play this game with a friend, you have to look at it the same way it would work when you were a kid. Think of it like going to their house to play Halo. Obviously when you come home your progress isn't going to save on your own Xbox, you're going to have to start all over again. This is something we should complain about, but I was legitimately surprised that this game had any form of multiplayer at all, so kind of a cool feature anyway. I would rate this game a TENTATIVE 7/10 (at three hours played). I may change this review if finishing the game changes my overall opinion of the experience of the game. I recommend this game if you are looking for a classic gaming experience, picking up a random game from gamestop and enjoying a unique setting and fun combat. I do not recommend this game if you are looking for a deep engaging story. I'm leaving a thumbs up review on this game because I personally have been enjoying it and I plan on completing the game. If you're still stuck on the fence after reading this review, I would say be patient and wait till this game is on sale for $30 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is watered down Doom Eternal, while at the same time being an enjoyable homage to 7th gen era action games. One of the best things you can say about this game is how straight forward it is. These days it is rare to see any games without extra fluff or micro transactions or whatnot, so this game is a refreshing breath of fresh air. The combat in the beginning starts out promising, offering interesting ways to take down foes, and menacing foes to take down. The problem is later in the game, when you realize that there are very little variety of enemies to fight. There are at least 10 types of enemies, give or take. Mini bosses you fight in earlier parts of the game become all too common in later arenas, which wouldn't be too bad of a thing if the weak point system introduced was not akin to a quick-time event, in which you wait for the enemy to do a specific thing that of which leaves it open to be shot at a highlighted point. This system becomes distracting when you're trying to fight 3 different mini-boss enemies at once, who if not given their attention, will drop you like sludge in the grease trap. Every item you acquire is on a cool down, not an ammunition/charge system, and some of these items are your heavy damage dealers. Instead of what could have been interesting ammo conservation being a factor of the combat, the cool down cycles end up leading you to play ring around the rosy with all the monsters, dealing menial amounts of damage with your guns, until your real weapons recharge. This being the case for every arena (and boss fight) after the first 3 hours, leads to the combat getting stale fast and leaving you dreading every arena on the horizon. The level design is good, i like the locations and the unique vibe each one had. There are plenty of little branch off paths, but they are extremely obvious, easy to access, and contain a fairly large chunk of the money in the game.The story is nothing to talk about.6/10, fun way to waste a day

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a straightforward linear action game that doesn't attempt to be anything special. The combat mechanics are generally solid, although I do have a few complaints. Throughout the game especially in the later missions, you'll find yourself facing hordes of enemies simultaneously, with multiple attacks happening all at once. This can sometimes feel overwhelming. Which pushed me towards adopting a more passive playstyle, waiting for weapon cooldowns and healing, rather than being as aggressive as I wanted to be. This was also due to the fact that as long as you are not attacking you can mostly just doge all over the place without taking damage. However, as I gradually expanded my arsenal, became more accustomed to the gameplay, and familiarized myself with the enemies abilities, combat began to feel much more satisfying during my repeat playthrough/New Game+ run.Evil West’s world is interesting, but the story falls short due to uninteresting characters. While to me a strong narrative isn't necessary for this type of action game, it's disappointing considering the big amount of existing cutscenes that could have added more to the experience.Between combat arenas, there are super easy puzzles that serve only as a breather from the fighting. At least the environments themself look really cool most of the times. I would go as far as saying Everything besides the actual combat in Evil West was boring to me, which is a pretty sizable part of the game. There are two short sections where you are going downhill in a minecart, shooting stuff to survive, which are the exceptions. They could really have done more stuff like this to spice the non-combat section up. Despite the issues I had,  this game was still pretty fun.

The story/setting is the "wild west" (late 1800s) with vampires who are bent on world domination. It's nothing new or original. You even find out that there's werewolves as well. Because you can't really have vampires without werewolves, it seems. I always like this time period, so much so that Red Dead Redemption as a franchise is among my most favorite video games just because of its setting, but I just don't see the wild west theme having such extreme supernatural elements to it and I don't think it's ever really been done properly except, ironically, with Rockstar's rendition of zombies in DLC for Red Dead Redemption.There's a cool mix of melee combat and shooter combat where you can chain together different combos between the two, creating unique methods to killing your foes as you juggle them a la Street Fighter and then blast them to bits with a sawed off shotgun before they can even land. I like the combat, just not how it is executed, however; and by this I mean that most of it takes place within "arenas." It requires some suspension of disbelief as you run through a map and then see a bunch of vampire dudes on the other side of a wooden fence, but you can't engage with them until you've hopped the fence to enter into arena-style combat. There's some sort of force field (invisible wall) that prevents you from being able to shoot these creatures until you've entered their arena. They'll even make comments like "I see him!" while you're outside of this designated arena but even they just stand within the confines of the barrier and pace aimlessly. I guess I much prefer to be surprised by enemies as I traverse the maps rather than seeing them behind an invisible wall where we can just stare at one another. There's no real element of surprise in that regard or having to improvise because you came around a corner and saw a giant spider awaiting you. I thought that the combat could sometimes be a bit too arcade-y with its mechanics as well. For instance, some of the bandits would just stand in one spot and before they shot at you, you'd see a ring around their body as a "weak spot" for you to aim at to deal extra damage and to alert you that you are about to be shot or attacked. The AI is predictable and just lazy. Bandits with ranged weaponry stand in one spot, while everything else just runs at you in a straight line, so you can generally dodge/block without much worry. This sort of plays into how much the game is guilty of "hand holding." Between all of the glowing objects to inform you of what can be interacted with as you're exploring a linear video game, the highlighted weak spots, etc., it makes it feel like it's a game designed for a kid or a newbie to video gaming. I don't want to be given the answer to puzzles because you've highlighted what needs to be pushed in order to solve the puzzle. It's not a puzzle at that point.More on map design, there's a number of puzzles that are just a huge waste of time to begin with. It's a bit odd to spend time rearranging these train carts on one chapter to access a panel to lower a drawbridge so that you can walk across it, only to see that you could skip the entire drawbridge because the train cart allows you to jump where you need to be, except there's wooden boxes blocking your path that you cannot jump over or destroy. So you have to press the button to lower the bridge, return to the train cart below, push it across the track to the other side, jump up to the second floor again and then cross the bridge to get to the side you were just on. There was also a moment where you had to activate a crane to move a pallet of boxes that were 'trapping' a bunch of people inside of a barn. There's five boxes on this pallet. You were really stuck behind it when you could just move the boxes out of your way or climb over top of them? It doesn't make sense and is just designed to waste your time.Annoyingly, if you are traveling these maps with an NPC, these NPCs will just stand to the side in the arena as you are bumrushed by a dozen vampires. They'll also teleport throughout the map. It requires more suspension of disbelief that these NPCs are somehow moving ahead of you, despite being unarmed while you also have to solve puzzles to progress forward. If these other characters are discovering the path of least resistance, then why are we not following them? Normally, I'd complain about having useless companions because they do attack but deal no damage. The friendlies here don't do anything at all which I've realized is infinitely worse. They don't even say "hey, good job!" as you cleared out the entire arena of five minibosses and dozens of generic mobs while they were standing on the roof in plain sight, but somehow hidden. Even having them as a sideline cheerleader would be better than what they currently are.Enemy variety is perhaps either lacking or just too annoying to deal with. What eventually turned this into a "not recommended" title for me was the obvious artificial difficulty added later on into the video game. These aforementioned battle arenas remain around the same size but are filled with more and more enemies as you progress with the game. And you'll have such an odd mixup of enemy types that it's really more reminiscent of the Serious Sam video games where the idea seems to just be to throw as much as it can at you. Later in the game, it gets to the point where they want to spawn three to four minibosses at you that are between multiple regular enemy types. The enemies get tankier (especially the bosses) and there's very few skills that you can unlock to improve your weapon damage. The balancing is just completely off and it results in a frustrating experience. You can tell that they wanted to make bosses similar to that of popular Soulslike video games but couldn't really figure out how to implement them in a way that was both fair and challenging. There's a lot of strategy between all of the weaponry and abilities you unlock that you can utilize and even a method to respec'ing your character if you feel your build is too weak, but there's just too much bad game design here to keep it fun after the halfway point. The last few bosses are a slog to deal with because they are just so tanky and surrounded by a dozen other creatures whereas your character will take massive damage.I never played the video game cooperatively, but I've heard that coop is even worse.There's also the female character who must make obligatory feminist remarks about how tough it is to be a lady scientist because people underestimate you, blah blah blah. You aren't assigned to field duty, lady. You're the privileged one here, not the men out there getting their throats ripped out by vampires so that you can sit safely in your lab doing scienc-y stuff and complain about how hard life your life is. Characters like this immediately remove a whole letter grade from the video game with how common they have become. Stop writing these female characters to be these whiny crybabies and start making them actual badasses.

_childDocuments_.review: There's an old-school vibe about Evil West. Its silly, over-blown combat reminds me of those hack'n'slash games from PS3 era, Darksiders, Heavenly Sword, Bayonetta etc. Evil West follows a similar vein, aiming to deliver the most stylish, most blood-rushing battles. Though its story sometimes feels out-of-time level of bland, and the combat late game can be brutally hard, I still recommend Evil West.P.S. Opinions below comes from playing on Hard difficulty for the first playthrough.This is just one of the combo you can pull off in the game. Evil West offers a variety of weapons and upgrades to enhance your ticks-beating therapy. It`s so satisfying to integrate every tool you have into a series of blood-rushing beat-down session: Dash attack to close distance, two normal attacks follow with one upper cut, slam it down, pulls out flamethrower or gatling gun and go nut, electric pull what`s left of your enemies, E-COMBO the living hell out of it, throw in a dynamite and watch it explode. The fun doesn`t end here. The game also offers you two skill trees to further enhance your playstyle. Though not in a game-changing way, these perks still provide either solid damage boost for normal attack or reliable way to replenish health and energy. The only problem is the time required to reach all these wonderful things. I have to admit, the game feels really underwhelming at first when most of the good things are still locked by progression. Yet, I guarantee you that everything is worth your time unlocking.I struggle to come up with any reason why shouldn`t Quick Turn be implemented in this game. Evil West is the third-person brawler equivalent of boomer shooter. The arena will spawn a great deal of enemies and will definitely overwhelm you considering you have little option for combat at first. It would help immensely when I could immediately turn around to the alarming arrow behind me rather than quickly dash forward and pray to god that it is just a swipe attack from regular foe instead of a large shockwave. This problem is especially nasty in late game section, when the game throws in several reused bosses at a time.I am talking about the major bosses(Parasiter, Bruch, William Rentier, and Felicity) rather than those being reused over the course of the game. These bosses have several invincible phases that feel really tedious and drag the whole fight down, especially the Parasiter and Bruch. For Parasiter, you can only damage the main head twice, by defeating both of its tentacles and dodging its mandatory puking phase. Otherwise the boss is completely invincible. For Bruch it is way, WAY worse. This boss just teleports out of the arena and stands at the edge of the map. It is immune to all kind of damage and will remain that way until you clean out all of the lackeys.To be honest, I was this close to rage quit at one of the late game arena session. That train yard level just throws way too many annoying enemies at once. Situation can spiral out of hand if you can`t handle these elite enemies fast enough. Even with 90% upgrades unlocked, I still find these sessions unfairly hard due to having no way to turn around fast enough, as well as the fact that enemies remain relentless even when they completely out of your sight.→I don`t like that at the end of level you just abruptly transit to the next level's loading screen.→I wish normal attack has a "pause between combo" system or upgrade. It would make fighting tankier enemies way more interesting.→I also wish flamethrower and gatling gun can be more combo-friendly rather than its own thing. Sort of like flame belcth from Doom or a faster switch speed.中文小簡評→超自然西部荒野動作遊戲，我的最愛。→相對於黑暗奇幻風，這遊戲用色相當鮮明。→各式炫泡誇張的武器技能與升級系統。→在戰場上自由搭配，靈活運用連技痛毆吸血鬼。→雖然缺點很多，但我仍然覺得其爽快的戰鬥孩時值得一玩的。→缺乏快速轉身，很容易被敵人從死角攻擊。→一些主要王戰非常拖沓，太多無敵階段。→後期戰鬥容易被多隻菁英怪圍剿。→故事有種上個世紀的廉價感。

_childDocuments_.review: From the same developer that made the Shadow Warrior reboot games. Evil West is a third-person action/adventure beat-em-up. Now mixing the western genre with the paranormal is one of my favorite combinations ever. The game scratches that itch but not completely. If you're expecting a huge amount of different monsters/cryptids sadly this is not the game. The main monster/villain of the game is vampires. You have regular human vampires, actual giant vampire bats, hybrid enemies and then your regular human enemies.What I find odd is why the developer didn't implement a combo/ranking system. Something accustomed to a game like Devil May Cry. For this reason there is zero consequences for playing poorly (besides dying obivously). The game also gets really repetitive because of this. The skill ceiling isn't too high so anyone can pick it up. Once you get the best overpowered upgrades the game does become a bit of a breeze. Even being able to play the hardest difficulty on NG+ makes it a cakewalk.While there are other weapons the gauntlet is your main bread and butter. The weapons/tools you get throughout the game just spice things up a bit or can save you in a dire situation. The developer took the glory kill idea from Doom '16 as a way to gather health/energy. There is a heal button but it has a cooldown.  The guns have infinite ammo but do weak to moderate damage depending on the enemy type. They are best used to shoot enemies in their weakpoints when they flash on screen.The story is nothing amazing and all the characters are pretty one note. I do like the whole idea of a guild of monster slayers operating in the 1800's. And it really opens potential for a sequel(s). If the dev was to consider the idea I would love to see wendigos/skinwalkers as the main monsters. They are extremely under utilized. They would fit the western setting pretty well.I played the game solo, twice, so I can't really comment on how the game is in co-op. But the game solely feels like a single player experience. I think the dev just added co-op because "everything is better with friends" adage. Good news for achievement hunters is the game's 100% is pretty easy. There is also no achievements involving mutiplayer/co-op so you're safe from having to drag a friend to help. The game can also be beaten in one sitting.All in all, I'd like to see a sequel but add in that combo/ranking system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrible. The fight mechanics are so janky. Right click is for aiming but for some reason the game does not register the click every time. _childDocuments_.review: The point on which this was sold: dynamic, visually stunning combat, atmosphere, cool character/monster designs are definitely here. THE MAIN thing to me is the balance between the melee and shooting. It's different from DMC where the character is so small you barely feel any danger and you're pretty removed from the experience. Here a lot is happening up close and personal. Love the dodges being those boxer like sidesteps with giant hammers smashing the ground two feet next to you. This is what I was missing for so damn long.The game is free of crafting, open world, "muh dark souls difficulty", or tedious sidequests.The plot does what it's supposed to do and so far the writing, dialogue and acting are better than expected. The linearity is quite visible here and I wish the maps were a bit more open to exploration, a minor sidequest that would actually be interesting wouldn't hurt. But alltogether that's a pretty minor complaint. I'm on chapter 4 I think and my only concern is whether the pace will maintain that same speed of ramping up cause so far the new weapons and functions appear at a pretty lively pace. Hope the game doesn't blow it's load too early. Difficulty is in that sweet spot where it's a challenge but I don't get frustrated when I die.To me whenever a title like this drops an arcade "mercenaries" mode with score points, pickup modifiers etc. is a must. Hope this picks up enough interest to warrant a hefty DLC and/or a sequel.Also I'm a firm believer in voting with your wallet. It's no a perfect game but still quite good and I'm having a lot of fun. Supporting it means I'm supporting fresh ideas, going against big publishers milking established franchises till their tits fall off. I'm supporting good designs, lovely aesthetics and kinetic combat.MORE LIKE THIS PLEASE

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for satisfying and straightforward monster killing game with great atmosphere that you can casually jump into, Evil West is worth checking out.While the game itself is very linear with a non-complex plot, each level's environment has a great, uniquely weird-west aesthetic and intricately grotesque enemies throughout. Gameplay might feel repetitive after awhile going from corridors to fighting arenas with little variation, but if you enjoy bashing your way through crowds of monsters while armed with a plethora of weapons and fighting abilities, the repetitiveness is not necessarily a bad thing.I'd compare the game to a Michael Bay movie that satisfies that "I want to see explosions" itch—Evil West lets me punch, shoot, rip apart and electrocute monsters when that's exactly what I feel like doing. Hopefully there will be a sequel.

And with the optics and the setting, that would have been clearly possible and would have quickly become a game of the year with maybe - a major franchise (see Darksiders). Okay for 10-15 euros, but making a full-price title out of it is completely excessive in my opinion.The areas, buildings, events and effects vary greatly between, "that's pretty nice the sunset" and "man, that's very lifeless" and "Hmmm... another covered area with an arena fight? okay...". For the big announcement years ago, I would have expected an AAA title. That is not the case here, sorry. More of an AA gap filler. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West isn't the most ground breaking game in any aspect.You could  even call it retro (or outdated if you are more calloused),it feels like a game from the early 2000s. But it shows that you don't need to heed modern game conventions to make a fun game.The game is very straightforward. Levels are nearly completly linear with some secret collecticables if you want to go for 100%. The story is fairly simple (though with interesting lore and a fun retronic-steampunk-west setting).The combat is mostly just mashing buttons, ocaccsionally using cooldowns or meter based abilities and hitting telegraphed counterattack windows. But... the game IS fun. Unapologetically fun. Throwing punches feels weighty, and combining everything in your arsenal is a blast. At hard difficulty, the game is simutanously easy to get into but still makes beating encounters satsifying.Evil West is the videogame equivalent of a great B-Movie.While it isn't the cheapest title arround, it's still better value than most AAA-releases nowadays.Unlike those, it runs well, and there are no malicous monetization models corrupting the game design.It's a neat linear story game that can be enjoyed solo and co-op.Depending on difficulty and whether or not you are a completionist, expect 7-30 hours of gameplay, with New Game + being an option for replayability.If that's worth the price tag is up to you, but you should definetly check it out if it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is short but interesting vampire action. For me it has more positive then negative moments, but fans of action games like Draksiders or God of War could be little disappointed(as i was). It feels like you are watching common vampire action movie - we have super main hero, his elder mentor, some sidekicks and clever doctor girl with whom our hero has some chemistry, evil nemesis, main government ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and semi-neutral informer. So here my list of pros and cons:+ Nice visual part and graphic + Epic death finishers and decent amount of moves and skills, especially when you open whole arsenal+ Cool shooting, i really felt like true western cowboy who can shoot fast and deadly+ Tesla technologies looking and implemented very good with story and roleplaying+ Funny dialogues and comedy moments+ We have cart races, lasso and easy/medium puzzles for feeling like Indiana Johns+ Interesting elite enemies fights(especially mega bosses and elite enemies on first encounter), so you really want to use you whole arsenal vs them.+ Free respec for perks and weapons upgrades any time(after initial tutorial maps), you can even return to base in middle of the mission with all items and level you gain, then respec and try it again. + Good optimization+- no open world, this straight forward corridor game(but for those who afraid to be lost on map this game is perfect because there no way you can  do it)+- Story is debatable - on one hand it has lot's of cliche and predictable story moves(for those who watch/play at least some of vampires), stereotypical heroes and villains. On other hand story so naive and simple that it feels very nice, especially if you want some light storytelling without any mind breaking things.+- Understandable 'New Game+' system, you finish the game 1 time than you go on higher difficulty, try to find missing collectibles, gain some level to open all perks and weapon upgrades. Repeatability not good,   playing more than 2 times is boring and makes no sense other than you want to collect all achievements in game.- Bad level design, especially mechanics with climb and jumping where you can't return back anymore after some moments. On pair auto-save only mechanic you can miss some corner then climb on top of a little rock and gg - you can't just return back, so go and restart whole level. One thing where you jump from one edge to another one and obviously can't return back, but completely different story when you can't return back over a simple wooden fence.- You can't jump, very restricted to go around map, so basically you can go under the train in special circumstances but jump over the fence or some boxes is impossible to super vampire hunter - feels like you Claptrap who see stairs often.- Collectibles is a headache, because you need to find all cash to upgrade your weapons but if you just run over the map later you will have trouble vs enemies and forced to rerun and find missing dollars. I understand mechanics with secret perks and weapons blueprint but problem with money is awful.- Too low amount of common enemies types, they don't progress with any new mechanics just more hp with higher difficulty. And after some time fight with them are more boring than interesting. So basically first time you encounter them it's wow effect but then it's meh...- Leveling system and perks/weapons upgrades mechanic is very weak. You don't feel that with higher level you become stronger, some upgrades and perk really makes you stronger but most of them not or make you stronger a very little. Even of you want to grind level it's not worth your time because exp gain very strange and on some maps common enemies won't give any of it.- All controls made for fu**** consoles so if you play on PC forget about extra buttons and try to adapt to console buttons limits. Even on controller it feel bad and uncomfortable.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game. I have been playing exclusively co-op and I can say very confidently that this game was not built for that. Levels won’t load. Progression is difficult. And starting over from the beginning every time I’m glitched into the ground is tedious. From a gameplay/storyline standpoint it is not very creative. I am almost 5 hours in at the time of writing and I feel no closer to an end goal than when I started. This game deals with a lot of new concepts that aren’t traditional in vampiric lore and I think that could be interesting if the plot didn’t feel so rushed. It feels like the characters already know everything there is to know about the vampires and I don’t get to learn along with them. All the characters feel shallow and I have a hard time connect with them and seeing where they stand morally. Our character is regarded as a sort of god and I have a very difficult time seeing why. He’s not just a quiet, “silent but deadly”, brooding type. He’s actively mean to everyone he engages with and they just roll over and take it. It makes it hard to root for our character and find things to connect with them about. Story progression is confusing. From what I have been able to gather, the antagonist of this game is the little girl we see at the start. But we hardly deal with her and the missions we go out on feel pointless to catching her. Actually, I don’t even know if we want to catch her. I have no idea what we’re supposed to be doing or what our end goal is. The level designs are okay. They’re not like tomb raider level puzzles, but they’re also not bad. It’s simple and I don’t really mind it but I think it really hammers home the fact that this game was built purely for the combat and not much else.It’s a pretty game. The graphics look nice and it runs smoothly. One small gripe I have with it is that most levels turn out to be very monochrome. Either all red or all green. It gets very confusing and it makes it harder to see.The combat is alright. I can see the inspiration from Doom and dark souls and the like. The block doesn’t work however, and my playing partner has not been able to make the dodge work once. I have not had that issue with the dodge but I feel it is important to note. You are given a kick option to stagger enemies when they are about to do a power attack, which to me feels a little counterintuitive. My first instinct when I’m about to get hit by a power attack is to dodge because in many other games that is what you must do. However I do not play a lot of heavy-handed combat games so there is a chance that I just don’t have the perfect skill set. You can spam the electric glove power to pull enemies to you (or yourself to enemies) and leave them stunned so you can click left click over and over without them being able to get a hit on you. Enemy introductions are a little strange. You’ll be fighting this huge scary monster in one level and it’ll be this huge deal and supposedly something you’ve never dealt with before and then there will be three at once in the next level. And then three more after that. I feel the developers were trying to create a feeling of urgency in the vampire threat but it comes off as more lazy. You go through the level, you do a puzzle or two. Then you have a boss fight with some crowd management. The first time you see these new monsters is genuinely exciting and interesting. They have attack patterns and weaknesses and such. But then you’re just given a death ring full of everything you’ve ever faced and it feels a little boring. Maybe that works for some people but it’s not really my thing. A small tidbit that really only bothers me but the game is set in the Wild West and I absolutely do not get that feeling. This game could take place anywhere at anytime and I wouldn’t know it. My first impression was that this took place during the real Wild West and there was a secret society of people who hunted vampires. During my play-through of the game did not feel like that. There is no outer world you interact with so the threat of the vampires feels very contained to a small area. You don’t see regular people doing regular things trying to hide from the growing threat. You see doctors and engineers treating the vampires like a persistent bug problem. You see government officials who drive blimps talking to the head of the vampire hunting division asking if the vampires are even worth it anymore. All that said. I believe this game could have been great. I think the ideas and new lore it creates for vampires is really interesting. I like the combat mechanics because they’re simple and easy to pick up and they make me feel cool. But it falls short in a very crucial area for me. The story. I don’t know what’s going on. Mission setups are just “get mad. Yell at person. Go to place. Punch thing. Come back. Repeat” I have a very difficult time investing myself in the world and I find myself wanting to skip most cutscenes because I simply don’t understand what’s happening and I don’t really care to know. I see the vision but it’s shrouded in glamour and my glamour glove is busted.I have a hard time saying that I don’t recommend this game because i see what it could have been. I like the ideas that were brought to the table. I just wish that they were expanded upon more. I wish that I felt connected to the characters and the world and that I really had a reason to fight the vampires. But I don’t. And if I was playing solo then I probably wouldn’t have made it as far as I have in the story.Anyways thank you for reading, sorry it was long, comments are on if you’d like to talk about it

The storyline is intriguing enough to keep you hooked with its mix of mystery and action.After a while, the missions start to feel a bit samey. More variety would have been nice. The characters look cool but lack depth. A bit more background and development would make them more memorable. There are some technical hiccups that can be annoying. Patches are needed to smooth things out. The game world feels pretty linear. It would be awesome if there were more open-world elements to explore."Evil West" is a good game with a lot of potential, but it falls short in a few areas. It's worth playing for the cool setting and fun combat, but don’t expect it to be a flawless experience. If you’re into Westerns and horror, you’ll probably enjoy it despite its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely needs more attention, than it's been getting since release. Don't get me wrong, it's not "best game ever" and it's never been "game of the year" candidate. But it's a really solid B-Game. You know, like B-Movie, but a game.The story is... There. It's ok, do not expect any plot twists here, characters are flat and, to an extent, stereotypical. Main villain is just a brat and is just annoying. The lore, though, seems interesting by itself, I would not mind exploring some proper RPG in this world, and the fact that it's also a western with vampires - it just adds more to it. But it is more about experience, I think. it is extremely linear, but environments do feel relatively unique, and they do present quite a few moments, that just feel good.What is really worthy in this game is combat. Yes, it's not Devil May Cry, not even by a longshot. But it does involve juggling between melee combat and several types of range weapons. What's more it feels satisfying. Like there is this "oomph" to your actions. You also feel a bit more vulnerable than Dante or Nero, so you may want to be a bit more strategic.It does have a few issues. Bugs with some achievements (I had one), low-resolution models inside the game (when you look at your character or weapons), periodic dips in performance... The switching between weapons is also kind of inconsistent: in some cases press of a button switches between several weapons, in some you literally "equip" a weapon, in some you just press a different button. You do get used to that, but something tells me it could have been done better, still.Overall, I am not sure if this game is worth replaying with its New Game+ mode, but as a one-time fun experience - definitely worth the time. Probably, at a discount in terms of price, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West feels like a game that was made in PS3/Xbox360 era when games were primarily built on a cool gameplay idea and did not care much about player engagement, playtime length, monetization or even story and characterizing etc. (also technology and level design similarities). This game aims to deliver cool combat, and it does but not without some flaws.Evil West is set in an alternate Wild West, where humans are at war with strigoi, which unlike your regular Twilight vampires, are violent and evil beasts like how the TV show The Strain portrays. The world setting is fascinating, even the existence of fantasy beasts, witchcraft and steampunk technology is teased, but the story is meh and the characters are very generic and forgettable even though there are a few well-written dialogues.Our hero is a vampire hunter/cowboy, who possesses a metallic knuckle that can perform melee and special moves, an electric gauntlet that can block, parry, teleport and pull enemies, 5 manual aim weapons and 2 auto-aim weapons. He can also do stun attack, rolling, kicking (to interrupt certain attacks), healing, ground pounding and enter a special power status. Tools and abilities are a lot and each of them is either bidden to a certain button or requires button combination to use, but in my experience beating the game on hard difficulty, none of them feels superfluous or useless. That said, the button management might be too much for some players considering the fast-paced nature of the game, as it does take skills to have a smooth experience, which is not always a good thing. I also think some abilities are flawed in design: teleporting and pulling require proper timing, but players usually don’t have it since the combat is often hectic, making them my least used abilities; the kicking is not rewarding enough (excluding final boss) compared to just rolling away, especially with the timing that easy to throw players off; the cooldown of some weapons/abilities are too long.Despite its complexity, the combat system is a success. Melee combined with shooting is not a new concept, but Evil West is one of the few games that reach a good balance between the two: one is not superior to another but equally important and powerful; the transition also is fast and seamless. Overall, the combat feels like a fun, innovative and exhilarating hack-and-slash game with a snappy shooting that greatly rewards skill and strategy. I really like it, but once the level design is factored in, I have some mixed feelings.Evil West follows a very basic linear design for most levels. You often can't walk back to where you just passed. And wherever there is a big and open area, it is going to be a fight, which soon feels stale and predictable as enemies rarely appear outside these areas, taking out the element of surprise. Besides, the game loves piling up enemies, to the point where it feels mildly offensive and annoying. Most previously fought bosses will become regular enemies later. They appear in duos, trios or quartets, or mixed match with others and let players fight many times along with tons of minions. I think it is lazy for both level design and difficulty and some might think the game is bloated because of it. What’s worse, balancing took a backseat in the process of stacking up the number. Like, I often died way too fast because it was too hectic to deal with so many enemies attacking at once (at hard difficulty). Consequently, the game might rely way too much on players’ quick reactions.Enemy number and button management are not the only factors causing the game to be too hectic: the aiming speed can really be 0.1 sec faster (easy to miss shooting opportunity); moving while aiming causes miss shots even it is perfectly aimed (you have to stand still); the attack frequency of some enemies can really dial back a little, like the nest monster. The nest monster fight is usually a clusterfxxk because it almost always appears in small arenas filled with protected minions and bombs, and while its weakness is exposed, it starts bombing way too frequently, causing little chance to shoot. By the way, the final boss has the worst boss design I’ve seen in a while, who is like a kid only to know spamming a few moves in a fighting game.Players travel back to the pub after a level is finished, where I think it was designed to be a central hub area for side quests originally but got axed. Therefore, you can’t fully upgrade in one playthrough. There are some upgrades you need to find to unlock, and then buy them with money or perks to activate, which is redundant in my opinion. A better way should be activating the upgrade once you find it, which not only makes exploring more rewarding but also lower the need of grinding for upgrades. And speaking of upgrades, some are obviously more essential for making the game easier, but the game leaves those to players to figure out. Also, some upgrades can actually make the ability worse. For example, the final upgrade of the supercharged mode causes it to consume one more gauge to trigger, which despite its powered up, makes the ability less practical to use.I am not a big fan of the art style of Evil West which uses high contrast and high color temperature, because it causes low brightness in some areas and the high saturated color tone feels a bit overwhelming for my eyes. It is not a game with good graphics either. In max setting at 1080P, the game looks very blurry with its low-res textures. Only when cramping up the render rate to 160% does it start to look acceptable, but that introduces lots of frame rate fluctuations (I settled at 150%). The game can use better optimization, as well as stability improvement (it crashes many times). It also has a few glitches like enemy getting stuck or not spawning, or cutscenes automatically skipped etc.Evil West is a low-budget 2A game that reminds me of a lot of goodies of PS3/Xbox360 era – game developers were less prone to risk-avert designs that have been used in so many games, but more dared to try on cool and new ideas. The combat is awesome, but the level design definitely tanks the experience a little. Regardless, I recommend having a try, but maybe at normal difficulty which is more forgiving to your reaction, instead of hard difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I bought it because its a western. That being said, slaying grotesque monsters isn't a negative. Within the first 10 minutes, from graphics to sound, you can easily see care was put into it. Pretty linear from most now a days, but that isn't bad. It knows exactly what it wants to be. Both have a heavy, crisp crack to it. Character design is top notch and I cannot complain about the acting neither. Seems like a fun shooter / horror / western. An old school, go hard, beat em up, shooter.After BeatingGood/Fun game. I 100% recommend. The people with low hours, played on novice (28% of the beaten trophies). Bolt fires only once even when holding down trigger. Requiring another press. 3. If enemy is pressed against Jessie, Jessie rolls / side steps in place. Especially side stepping. All in all! There isn't enough western games. Glad to add this one! However, now I want a true survivor horror set in the west. Like an RER2 VS RDR2... One can dream. Anyway! Get Evil West! Enjoy in the vampire slaying, foul mouthed gore-fest goodness! Two hours is more then enough time to decide in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: It's what it says on the tin, and I genuinely have been enjoying my time with it. It's goofy, over-the-top, and really fun to play. These are the devs behind the Shadow Warrior reboot trilogy, so (like those games) this game is really nice to look at, casual and fun to play, and straightforward in its presentation. It's not perfect, but it's not a AAA game asking for $70 either. It's a $40 that regularly goes on sale for $20, and its more than worth the asking price in my opinion. Its gameplay harkens back to the classic PS2 and early Xbox 360 beat-em-ups like God of War and Darksiders, and the story is just as ridiculous as some of that era's games as well. Not every game has to be a "forever game," and (if we're being honest) with the way AAA games are going these days, games like this are probably going to be the most interesting and engaging experiences we can have going forward. Give it a try, you'll have a good weekend playing to beat it at least.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10!A truly epic action-packed experience set in the Vampirical West! God of War + Devil May Cry meets Van Helsing in nutshell. The story is just about right with enough characters to keep things interesting and relatable. But the true focus of the game is really the immersive combat experience.It's so easy to get in the zone battling vampires and demons with all the tools and weapons available. All of the weapon types, moves and upgrades really add up to the combat experience each in their on way. This is the first time that I've experienced utilizing all of the weapons/tools available in almost every encounter without heavily favoring a few weapons/tools only. Once you're done with your first playthru and second (New Game+) playthru, I highly recommend starting a fresh save file on the highest difficulty (EVIL Difficulty) on True Death Mode (save file is deleted upon death) to really feel the true essence of the game. This is where the true excitement and challenge begins! A true test of mastery and skill utilizing all of the tools and weaponry the game has to offer!A solid 8.5 out of 10 in my book! Considering it is a new title and even has COOP play, I liked that they kept it simple and clean and laser-focused on the great combat mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a pretty generic action game. You play as a vampire hunting cowboy with an arsenal of different weapons and abilities. It's not an amazing game, but it's okay I guess. Multiplayer can be fun for a few hours, although prepare to be body blocked by your partner a few times due to bad game design. Similarly, if your partner enters an area whilst you're exploring, you'll also get dragged to their location whether you're ready or not. Evil West has nice maps, they all feel different and look pretty nice. The cutscenes and voice acting is decent too, and the story isn't bad although generic.Now for the reasons I don't recommend the game. Firstly there are too many game breaking bugs. In one chapter (Lightning In A Bottle) accessing the perk menu locks your entire PC (apparently only in multiplayer), and although many people have experienced this since release, it still hasn't been fixed in 2023. My friend and I also fell through the floor of the map several times when attacked by enemies, and monsters can be knocked outside combat zones where you can't kill them, meaning you have to restart from the last checkpoint.For me another issue was that there are way too many buttons to press, and combos to remember, I had a hard time with this and it feels like it was clearly developed for console.One of the worst things about Evil West is lack of variation in enemies. You face the same monsters and mini bosses over and over again which is boring as hell.  We must have fought some mini bosses over 40 times, really not fun. At all.  In the end we dropped the difficulty, not because it was too hard, but because we were bored and just wanted the game to come to an end.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West has been on my radar of games to check out for quite some time. I've always been a fan of the "Gothic Western/"Dark Western" theme. To make this review simple for one to base their decision on whether they should purchase Evil West or not, I'll simply list the Pros and the Cons.The Pros:1) The Map Design- Each level in Evil West has a very unique feel to it. None of the levels feel like they were copied and pasted. On top of that, the game just looks really damn good.2) The Enemies- I've seen some reviews state that there isn't much diversity when it comes to the mobs you'll be facing. However I tend to disagree as within the first ten minutes of the game I had already encountered quite a few unique enemies.3) The Weapons/Gadgets- If there's one thing I love in games like Evil West its the unique and exciting weapons and gadgets you unlock along the way. And Evil West doesn't disappoint. Everything has this steampunk vibe to it that really sets it apart from your average run of the mill game.4) The Story-  So while I admit the story isn't anything mind blowing, it's still a fun story to progress through. You play as a vampire hunter set in the Wild West. Pretty basic sure, but if you're into this sort of dark twist on the western genre, like I do, then you'll find entertainment in the story.The Cons:1) The Characters- Now while I don't flat out hate the characters in Evil West, I will say that I felt they were lacking. The character you play as, Jesse Rentier, is painfully dull and boring. I could tell there were some moments where they meant for him to be a loveable smartass, but it just doesn't work here given the dialogue he has. Again not a terrible character, just needs a little work if there were to be a sequel. 2) Button Input- So the the main fighting style in Evil West is button combos and then of course you have your gun play side of the games combat mechanics. I'm willing to admit that some occurrences of attack combos not registering is my fault, HOWEVER I also know bugs in a game when I see them. There will be many a times where you know good and damn well you pressed all the right buttons in the 100% correct way that you are meant to do so, but the game will not pick up on it which will 9 time out of 10 lead to you being killed, especially during a boss fight. Speaking of boss fights...3)Boss/Mini Boss fights- Now I already know someone will say I just suck at the game, but whatever I'm saying what I gotta say. I can appreciate difficult boss fights. Hell I played the game on normal and at times got my ass handed to me on multiple occasions. I don't mind a challenge. However what I do mind is setting the player up for some almost ridiculously stupid difficult boss fights. I found myself handling boss fight situations in Evil West as if I were a Dark Souls player. Just dodging and rolling 95% of the fight and then managing to squeeze off some damaging hits on the boss the other 5% of the fight. I found myself using guns more than anything during these boss battles even though it seems to me the game really wants you use your melee abilities. Over all there were a lot of instances where I felt frustrated and would sometimes have to give the game a break because of stupid deaths. Again I love a challenge, but this game went a little overkill at times. Especially for what it is.Overall I do like/recommend Evil West and would possibly like to see a sequel. That being said I'd say wait till it goes on sale some time in the near future. That doesn't mean it's a bad game, just not one that I would personally rush to purchase.
