_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give my two cents on this game because, frankly, I think it deserves more praise. Not sure how many people will actually view this particular review, but I'd at least like to get the word out there about this game.Evil West isn't a spectacular or ground breaking game to me. I think it's price definitely reflects that, especially since the release of another action game called Hi Fi Rush released with much more content and polish not too long ago. I wish the game had a bit more stuff to do aside from its campaign and the story, while trying to channel a Wolfenstein: The New Order approach, isn't what I'd call great either. That's not to say it isn't at least entertaining, but it's fairly basic in it's approach.With that said, I whole heartedly recommend this game if you can get it on a good sale. I've beaten it 3 times from normal to the hardest difficulty and I'd like to think I have a very good grasp of the game's mechanics. Where Evil West lacks in certain aspects, I believe it makes up for in many others. I don't know what the budget for this game was, but I think it's safe to say it wasn't extremely high. That's ok because many games do that. In fact, one of my favorite games, Sherlock Holmes Crimes and Punishments had a similarly low budget as well but made great use of it in very smart ways. When it comes to a low budget, I think developers need to put it in places where it counts. Thankfully, this game does that with it's core systems and its very fun combat. While I would hesitate to call the game deep, I think it does an amazing job of allowing a lot of freedom in how you craft combos and take out groups of enemies. Have a couple of shield enemies and only one charge of your shotgun in order to make them vulnerable? Well most of the time the game supplies you with several fodder enemies that can be grappled and then launched into their shield, stunning the enemy. Feel like some enemies have an overbearing amount of health? Well the game allows you to stun lock them if you get a specific meter high enough through blocking and attacking. The game also gives you and item that takes some time to recharge, but stuns every enemy in the arena. Put two and two together, and you can easily stun the tougher enemies twice and take them out very quickly. I could go further, but I believe that much of this game's enjoyment comes from discovering these things yourself.On top of having combat mechanics that are enjoyable to master, the weapons and tools the game gives you are just so much fun to use. Aside from your normal punches, you're given a variety of guns which all feel distinct in their purpose and feel punchy in both their animations and sound effects. There is also a DMC "trickster" style blocking system that rewards you for timing blocks at the right times as well. This game really clicked with me during my first playthrough after it introduced the electric grapple mechanic. With a press of a button, you could pull smaller enemies toward you, electrifying the and leaving them vulnerable to either be combo'd or launched. On the other hand, you could also use this mechanic to zip toward enemies as well, creating opportunities you can use to formulate what order your taking out opponents in, or simply just to create distance in a tight situation.The enemies in this game are also quite good, however that comes with a bit of a caveat. While pretty much every enemy is unique and requires a different strategy to figure out, the game also runs out of new enemies to give you about halfway through the campaign. I suppose this is fine as the challenge then became how to tackle different enemie combinations, but I couldn't help that it felt like the game was longer than the list of enemies it could provide. Still, I think the enemy design, in both their gameplay and artistic decisions, are very well done. This also carries over to the bosses, which all have patterns you have to learn, and opportunities you need to use in order to deal damage to them.Like I said, this isn't a groundbreaking game by any means. But I still found myself really enjoying the process of playing this game simply for the fact that the developers focused on the strongest aspects of the systems they had, and used them to their fullest. I'm speaking for myself here, but I'm personally so tired of endless walking sections in games, or a laser focus on storytelling that takes away from sharpening up the core of the game. A good story is fine, but I think mainly focusing on that leads to very short term gains for the game you're making. I personally want a game that I can go back to years later and enjoy for all of it's great gameplay, and while Evil West doesn't perfectly achieve this, I think it comes very close. I really hope this game gets a chance at a sequel, because I'd love to see what a higher budget and more experience could do for the developers. They have a ton of great ideas here, and I think it shows through and through.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and setting of Evil West are both really solid and captured my interest enough to keep playing, but the tedious combat, obnoxious characters, laughably bad dialogue, and restrictive environments really ruins the experience. The story of the game has a lot of potential and if put in the hands of a better or more experienced writer, I feel like it could have overshadowed some of the game's lesser qualities. The environment and world the game takes place in allows for so much cool stuff and interesting scenery, which is absolutely the best parts of the game. It really is hard to go wrong with a story in a western setting, but bad characters and terrible dialogue will do just that.Graphically the game looks outstanding, but I am assuming that is where most of the budget went into. Pre rendered cutscenes look fantastic, the environments look amazing even on older hardware, and performance wise the game runs really smoothly even on high settings.The combat doesn't feel good at all, especially on higher difficulties. Difficulty selections just add more enemies and gives them more health and damage, you fight the same 5-6 enemy types over and over and over and over, and combat only takes place in designated circular shaped arenas, with complimentary environmental hazards, of course. I found myself exclusively using the crossbow because the using melee when you are swarmed by enemies that are protected by another enemy just doesn't feel fun. You encounter a mini boss for the first time, kill it, and then the next combat area is that same mini boss plus just enough enemies to make it irritating to fight. There just isn't enough enemy variety in the game, so the fun of combat wears off really quickly. The majority of characters aren't fun or interesting to interact with, their dialogue is poorly written, and are just generally unlikable. Considering how the game is supposed to take place in late 1800s America, the characters sure don't act or feel like they belong in that world. The only character that I actually cared about was Emilia, because she felt like a real person that lived and existed in this fictional setting. That and her voice actress did a really good job with her lines, so props to whoever did it, consider giving her a bonus. Whoever was responsible for writing and voicing Vergil should be fired or demoted to scrubbing the toilets at the developer's office, because he is quite possibly the worst comedy relief character I've ever encountered in any game. The environments sure look great, but man are they restrictive. Restrictive to the point where you can physically see the playable area borders on the ground (I'm looking at you sawmill level). There is next to no sense of exploration in the game because you are extremely limited to where you can go. Any ((((secrets)))) the game has are marked by bright, shiny chains or TNT piles, so they are easy to find. Along with bright shiny indicators for where you can go, the entire world feels like it was child proofed so that you can't stray off the path the developers want you to travel. There are invisible walls everywhere to prevent you from actually exploring the zones you're in, and any climbing/falling/traversal area is clearly indicated. It feels less like creating a linear experience and more like constant hand holding and treating the player like they have never played a video game before. Easy puzzles are accompanied by the main character sounding like a moron and clearly stating exactly what you need to do in order to solve the puzzle. Every mission has 6-10 circles that you fight enemies in, and when you aren't fighting enemies in a circle you're slowly hiking your way to the next circle. All in all the game has a lot of potential that just isn't realized. There are a lot of good elements of the game that I enjoy, but there are also bad elements which take away from the experience. I gave up on the game after 5 hours because the game insisted on making me fight the same flying bug mini boss that I killed 3 minutes ago, so I would rather do anything else with my time. I'd recommend only getting it when the game goes on sale, probably around 20~ dollars or so. Wouldn't recommend getting it for co op though, co op mode seems shoehorned in and buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 2/5 StarsEvil West initially promises an exciting and enjoyable vampire hunting experience, with varied enemies and entertaining ways to dispatch them. However, the game quickly loses its luster after the first half, devolving into a repetitive and tedious slog that fails to justify its price tag.While the first 50% of the game offers engaging combat and enemy variety, the second half is marred by a lack of creativity and innovation. Players are forced to face the same enemies repeatedly, and even the once-challenging bosses become tiresome when thrown at the player in increasing numbers. This lack of diversity in enemy encounters detracts from the overall experience and leaves players feeling fatigued and unenthusiastic about continuing their vampire hunting journey.The story in Evil West is, unfortunately, nothing to write home about. With a plot that is laughable at best, and reminiscent of a subpar B-movie, it does little to hold the player's interest or provide any emotional investment in the game's world or characters.Another glaring issue with Evil West is the bizarre scaling of enemy difficulty. After the first half of the game, enemies transform into damage sponges, and even playing on easy mode does little to alleviate this problem. This unbalanced difficulty curve makes the game feel like a chore, rather than an enjoyable action-packed experience.Finally, the game's length and pricing are problematic. Evil West would have been better served as a shorter, more concise experience, with a more reasonable price tag to match. As it stands, the game feels overpriced for the level of enjoyment and content it offers.In conclusion, despite its promising start, Evil West fails to deliver a consistently enjoyable vampire hunting experience. With its repetitive gameplay, weak story, and unbalanced difficulty, it's hard to recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun and stress-free action game. Save your time and money, and seek out other, more engaging titles in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I overall do recommend it with caveats.Biggest issue, keyboard and mouse, it drops inputs like no bodies business, if you want to play this, a controller is REQUIRED. On controller, just the general issues with how the inputs are setup for queueing and a few things, minorly annoying here or there but mostly fine.So, on the game itself, nice interesting story, not great, pretty simple, but it's just here to support over the top action and vampire bug hunting.Characters, all pushed to 11 on what they are supposed to be, take a bit of getting used to, but overall they work in the story, over the top as it is.The vibe/atmosphere... the game has that bad a** western feel, but done over the top with you punching through stuff more than just shooting, you're a real over the top character who barely could be called human by what you do, despite what they say you are. Decently entertaining, gets a bit repetitive but you also get enough new enemies and weapons that while the core is similar, its got enough variety and changes to keep it from ever feeling too samey. And moment to moment, it's good high energy and pretty satisfying combat. _childDocuments_.review: The fighting system, graphics, and audio are 8/10, 9/10, and 10/10 respectively. I'm not crazy about the setting (wild west / late 19th early 20th century / vampires). The story. characters, and monsters are just whack and forgettable. I'm hours into this game and I can barely drum up any details about the story. The NPCs are either nearly useless or totally useless in game. They feel lifeless in a way that actually hurts immersion - it would have been better not to have them at all. They just teleport from spawn point to spawn point and talk nonsense. The cutscenes (outside of speech) actually look worse than the in-game graphics, and serve only to break what little immersion this game provides. Even the main character is completely shallow and lifeless. It's like the writers watched a single cowboy movie and the first 15 minutes of twilight and was like yea -- I got this.Navigating around is completely uninteresting, nearly on rails. The "puzzles" and objectives are laughable, simplistic, turn on 3 switches go to an elevator then rinse-and-repeat type stuff. Finally most of the monsters have nothing to do with the setting or plot. They took whatever random monster type from countless other games and remixed them. I'm not joking when I say 90% of the monsters would have felt completely at home in a zombie game. The only interesting looking monsters are gothic.The mechanics are incredibly good. There are SO many ways to defeat your enemies and it's often VERY satisfying to do so. The fight-difficulty felt about right to me. 10/10 in fight mechanics would be Doom Eternal for me, and Evil west is close in this regard. Unlike doom eternal, the enemy AI is dumb and "strategy" is no more than a mere collection of effective tactics for each enemy type.This game is frustrating. They got the EXPENSIVE stuff right (graphics, mechanics, audio engineering), but completely slacked off / underfunded the story, lore, cohesive world building, etc. From a development cost standpoint, like so many other modern games, it would probably have only cost 5-10% more to make a masterpiece -- but instead we just got a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall there are way more cons than there are pro's. Visuals: Excellent. I have a 4070ti and had zero issues running this game at full settings  (I do limit my FPS to 60 in most games just because I personally don't care about reaching 120fps while sacrificing a few visual settings). Gameplay: Extremely repetitive and linear. You absolutely know when you are about to be in a fighting spot. The map will open up into a "pit" of sorts and then a bunch of enemies rush at you. Pretty much every "ambush" feels scripted and predictable. Upgrades (perks and skills) for the most part feel absolutely useless. _childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game; I really do. But, it's the typical fare from companies like Flying Wild Hog, or for a better known example, the good folks behind games like Risen and Gothic, the companies: "Pyrahna bytes" or THQ Nordiq. The difference here is the absolutely stunning directing and production of the trailers and gameplay adverts vs what they actually released for gameplay. I am floored. I have never been fooled like this lol. I am 40 and have been gaming since 1986. My entire video game career has been deciphering what is legit gameplay and what is just fluff or CGI, or other forms of media-art to make a game look amazing. As I am writing this, the trailers on Steam are playing and despite knowing what I know, I am still intrigued. That takes talent. Kudos to FWH and Focus Entertainment for that feat. But once the facade falls off, which is quite literally the moment you gain control of your character, it becomes apparent that this is the typical low budget jank that has permeated the video game world in the last 15+ years. The graphics, for example, are beautiful... for about 10 seconds or less. Then the frame rate dips and the jankiness of combat comes roaring to its uneventful, sad existence. I find it very annoying that a game like Steelrising gets bad reviews and yet has far less flaws than flaming piles like Evil West, Risen, Technomancer, etc etc., and a much more creative story.Speaking of which, the idea of the Doom franchise meets the Wild West meets Bloodborne with guns, ( this is NOT a Soulslike, im just comparing the story) is a fantastic one. But it falls flat. This game kind of reminds me of Kane and Lynch and other crapfest games that try too hard to be funny and edgy as throwback 1980s/1990s action blockbuster films. The acting could be much worse, so I won't complain about that. I will, however, complain about the wooden player character and his incredibly under utilized partner. You should have been able to switch between both characters. One is a long range badass and the player character is more up close and personal. Yet another wasted moment of potential.You are clunky like a Gears of War character, lame like the protagonists from try-hard games like Kane and Lynch, and myriad others; of the last 25 years, and the gameplay looks dynamic but is incredibly repetitive and stale when you actually control your character. Game is a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: In the stylized world of Evil West you play as Jesse Rentier, the son of the leader of a national vampire hunting organization. The world is gritty and dark, but contrasted by the cast’s “potty-mouthed” language and general demeanor. Combat is wild and fast-paced and enemy design does not pull any punches. The story focuses on stopping the “big bad” from infecting the whole world with vampirism. Though this may be a generic premise, the presentation sets it apart from others, while also feeling familiar enough to be a comfortable experience.Characterization is relatively shallow. While the voice acting is solid, the development of the cast is practically nonexistent. Their relationships do not develop past the need to work together, however you can tell that this is not what the game focused on. The story attempts to tackle the “unrealistic expectations of a father” but it falls flat as the player does not see enough of their interactions to understand that dynamic. When a “major” character dies, the emotional impact is minimal as well. The nonexistence of character depth results in no emotional payoff for “big” moments however it does not harm the overall experience in an offensive way.The combat is wild and frantic. The game promises that you will feel like a superhero and it delivers. Initially you only have a couple powers, but as the game progresses you unlock many more. Utilizing all these tools in the combat scenarios is essential to your survival. Even playing on Normal, you can fail an encounter if you do not use your entire arsenal. In the mid-game there is a drought of new abilities and a boss encounter that feels like a difficulty spike, however after that fight, the steady stream of new abilities resumes. Uppercutting enemies and launching them into each other with the “Boom Balls” perk causes them to explode with viscera; this never gets old. One perk causes you to slowly lose health while gaining energy for your gauntlet which allows you to perform electrically charged super moves. There are other perks that change the way you can play the game and at any point you can reset your points to change your perks if you do not like how it changes the combat style. This flexibility allows you to experiment with builds to fully utilize the systems and customize your experience.The enemies you face come in a wide variety. There are werewolf-vampire hybrids, giant bugs with glowing balls that power up standard enemies, tunneling mole vampires, giant gargoyle vampires and encounters where they throw multiple of these enemy types at you at once. Each one you have to approach in different ways. This keeps combat fresh, however some enemy types are utilized more than others and can be tiresome to defeat. Late game this is not a huge problem, because you are very powerful and can utilize your tools to remove the most difficult enemy quickly. Early game, some encounters can be a slog, but it is not a bad introduction to the systems and ramps up quickly.Outside of combat there are some “environmental puzzles.” I use the term lightly as they are more “walk to this spot and press the interact button” than requiring you to think. Most interactable objects have an icon indicating such and are also marked by fence posts wrapped in barbed wire. There are stashes of cash and temporary power-ups in the crooks, rewarding those that take a few extra seconds to check around the corner. While the artistic style is pretty to look at, these environments are not meant to be explored. It would have been beneficial to keep the game “on rails” rather than having any “exploration” in the levels.The best way to describe Evil West is a “video game ass video game.” It does not do anything new, but is an entertaining way to spend your time. It took me 9 hours to complete and that is with a bit of retries as well as finding a few “collectibles.” The game would have benefited from either committing to the absurdity of the situation or actually developing characters. Some levels felt like they were too long, however the combat keeps the experience entertaining. The story beats miss the mark because of the character shallowness and though it is a generic plot, it keeps you moving forward to the conclusion. The main drive however is definitely the combat. There are many different ways to play and a wide assortment of perks and upgrades that allow experimentation with no penalty. Enemy design can be frustrating, but once your arsenal expands, you will have a tool to handle each one. Evil West is a fun experience with some frustrating aspects, but is well worth your time. It is not worth $50 however, so wait for a sale to give this game a shot. I give it a solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally I was very excited for this game and I honestly cannot recommend it. To be clear, this does not mean it isn't fun or enjoyable but there are a lot of reasons just from my 2 hours of gaming that I cannot in good conscious say this is something I'd recommend for people to buy. Pros: Stability/Performance: In a time where it seems like a lot of games coming out as of late have issues with bugs and performance, this game actually performs extremely well on Ultra 1440P. I only came across 1 bug and it was a collision bug that sent my character flying but that was more enjoyable to see than anything. Gameplay/Combat: If you like God Of War (2018) this is basically that, from the chest's being hidden in random locations, to the juggling in combat, to the bs hit boxes. And that's really it.. I have nothing good to say about the game.Cons: Story: From the very beginning I was disinterested with the world, the characters, the events, the anything that was being shown to me. This game has no explanation as to why anything is happening, you are simply thrown in as if you Sam-Beckett just Quantum Leaped yourself into the shoes of Jesse and awoke in the past to face mirror images that are not yourself and driven by an unknown force to change history for the better. You're only guide Edgar who wields a sniper that only Jessie can see and feel. And so Jessie leaps from boss to boss, punching and shooting hoping that the next boss will be the Final Boss. Combat: Unlike God of War the combat here is very sloppy and all over the place, the notifications when an enemy will strike are very small and out of view, the camera is WAY TOO CLOSE that it feels like you are playing Gears of War. And after 2 hours of punching my way through repetitive enemies I unlocked another item that would also conclude to me spamming.Color, Graphics?: I don't know exactly how to categorize this issue, but let me just say if you enjoy the blue ambient colors and cool tone of God of War, you will hate the Red, Hot, Sun blaring colors this game has to offer. Instead of being Cool and visible, everything is just Red and Yellow mixed with a taint of Orange. I genuinely wanted to believe this was a monitor issue, but Horizon Dawn still looks beautiful while this game just looks saturated to infinity. There was a moment where I finally arrived to a new green manor, only for it to burn down in seconds and the entire game be red again.And well that's about it, I'd say gameplay is somewhere around 4/10 and story is 2/10. I truly believe there is something here for a prequel if done right, but as this game stands it's just repetitive and boring. On my final words of this review I'd like to give you a metaphor of what this game is. Imagine you walking into a friend's house while he's watching a movie or season 3 of any show. What you are watching looks exciting and someone probably just died. But you have no context of why any of it is happening, only that it is. That's this game, Season 8 of The Walking Dead.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is probably best described as God of War meets Doom Eternal. You've got the meaty melee of GoW combined with the weapon swapping and resource management of Doom Eternal. It flows together really well and makes you feel like a proper badass as you become more adept with the game's combat mechanics. Punching the crap out of vampires has never felt better. On Hard difficulty, the game is actually hard. Like, really hard. As in, I probably died more in Evil West than all of the games not named Sekiro released in the past decade combined. The game throws a ton of enemies at you and although they don't all attack you simultaneously, enough of them do that the pressure is unrelenting. These aren't just cannon fodder enemies either. These are enemies that were bosses in previous levels. Remember the Valkyrie fights in GoW? That's basically every fight in Evil West, only harder (on hard difficulty, at least). You'll undoubtedly rage numerous times throughout the game but it feels really great when you do eventually succeed.If you like God of War and Doom Eternal, I highly recommend Evil West. It harkens back to the gloriously wacky AA titles of the X360/PS3 era with its weird west setting and non-pretentious writing while also delivering strong combat mechanics that provide a lot of room for mastery.

The Devs attitudes when talking about the game was quite revealing: THEY WERE OUT TO MAKE A FUN GAME, have fun doing it, and NOT TRY AND PREACH or LECTURE THE PLAYER. It was refreshing to see. I used to play DEADLANDS, a TTRPG waaaaaaaay back in the day, and this just hit all the right notes. This reminded me of a very expensive B Movie Vampire flick, and I LOVED PLAYING IT. Not perfect, but STUPID FUN. Flying Wild Hog did a great job and should be proud of their work. Worth checking out. If you're easily offended, though, pass on this. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West... it's quite hard to figure out if I should recommend this game or not.-It's a linear action game that puts you in an arena, then lets you walk for a bit after the battle is done and then right into the next arena. So it's quite clear the main focus of the game is its combat, wich constantly teeter totters between quite good and really awfull.The enemies are incredibly fast, can run up to you in a second and every single damned "big swing" that you're supposed to be able to dodge roll away from tracks you for  too long, leading to hits that feel unavoidable and unfair.Not to mention the fact that nearly all enemies have big AOE attacks (or just melee swings so damn huge they might as well be AOE attacks) that you can only avoid if you roll even before they start winding them up.-Now, this wouldn't be so much of a problem if you weren't (literaly) spammed to death with enemies. You'll get into fights that have about 4 enemies firing rapid ranged attacks at you, 6 enemies or more who demand all your attention to dodge becoure of their ridiculous speed, and 2 or 3 of the big dude fariaty of enemies who you must fill their stagger bar before you can stop them from spamming their AOE attacks or their lightning speed melee attacks.And they are all relentless, barbarian raged monsters who storm you right away and leave you with only barely enouch time to counter attack, block or dodge away from, if they leave you enouch time to do so. Wich is not very often at all.On top of all this, the game throws in low level miniors that you can kill to get some health back, but they often end up blocking your dodge from the other attackers and they themselfs can of course attack too. Wich again, would be fine if they diddn't hit you for Oh, and just in case you menage to dodge roll away, the fun is not quite over yet. See, you have no IFrames in your roll. Yeah, that ♥♥♥♥'s ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.-Then there are the tools you get. Or rather, the tools you'll eventualy get. The game's combat is clearly made with all the players tools and weapons in mind, wich is fine. But then when you start the game you'll only have a very small part of your arsenal in your possesion to use. So now every single fight is even more of an uphill battle becourse the items you'll need to fight off all these monsters are locked in story progression.It really feels like there are big gaps in your combat abilities when you just start out and it's just such a messy way to begin your game with. Now granted, the really difficult enemies don't appear before you get more toys to slay them with, but the progression of the enemy roster and your weapons feels very scewed. There were numerous moments where I had trouble with a new enemy type only to get the propper weapon to fight that particulair foe  the introductairy fight. What. Why?Not gonna lie, a big part of the game does quite piss me off. It plays just bit too often at the wrong side of unfair ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths for me to really enjoy the combat propper... But sometimes it does work. And when all the gears and pieces do aligne (wich happes way too rarely) it's quite great.-It's a great feel when you kill one monster with a fist, then electro-shotgun the upcoming enemy to stagger them for a bit, so you can pull out your rifle and pop a headshot on a ranged enemy and then kill the now unstaggerd enemy with a revolver shot in the gut and a fist in the face.There are indeed moment where your tools, your movement abilities and your snappy shooting can have you dodge-roll-dancing between kills on the field. But these moments feel more like getting a lucky break then the intended game design, wich just makes me sad.But apart form the occational moments of gleefull killing, there are other strong aspects of the game that kept me hooked to see it through to the end.The animations, the sounds, the music, the quite faried designs of the enemies. The game's presentation really pulls through on this one.The levels themself are gorgeus, look grand and epic while being quite detailed as well. This is a game that has some awesome scenes and fistas to show, should you keep playing.And, simple it may be, the story is not half bad eighter. Play a gritty cowboy with electricaly empowered weapons against an evil force of blood thirsty, monsterous vampires? what's not to like?-So, yeah... I'm at a bit of an impass. I did like the game but I know that it can be awfull too...So I guess my takeaway is this: If you like difficult, wild western themed, supernatural games with an steampunk-esc aestetic and you're done with huge, pointless open-worlds, live serves models and want a return to the days of the PS3/Xbox360 action adventure games for a bit, then I'd say give this a shot.But for heavens sake don't pay full price for this. Wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and snappy game play with a diverse main cast! Plot is about what you expect from an action game, though it does bare a fair bit of the less... well-aged aspects of the western genre with regards to race, especially how it handles "indian"/indigenous influences. Most references to indigenous culture and beliefs were either dismissed as nonsense myth in-game or explicitly connected to the baddies which isn't a great look for a game whose primary "side kicks" are black and chinese respectively. If you're going to try and incorporate more diverse casts into a genre like this in an attempt to tackle its legacies, both good and bad, it makes the entire attempt feel cheap when such glaring double standards are put in place.The character designs are all incredibly fun and I loved the way the final boss moved and attacked. The boss fights were all engaging and the variety of ways to approach problems/encounters was appreciated as it meant my skills were transferable from locale to locale, even when new mechanics were introduced. Vampires being called ticks and leeches is SUCH a cool worldbuilding choice and it all felt very fitting for the setting.Over all, would recommend for a fun time if like a fluid and snappy third-person shooter. Don't expect a master piece from the plot or the sensitivity, but it's a good game and I had my money's worth of a good time :)

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a gloriously over-the-top action game that throws you headfirst into a wild west monster apocalypse. You take on the role of Jesse Rentier, a gruff gunslinger with a heart of gold (and a penchant for extreme violence) who hunts down monstrous creatures with a brutal blend of firearms and fisticuffs.The game's true strength lies in its combat. It's a fantastic mix of strategic melee combos and satisfying gunplay.  Jesse's gauntlet punches like a freight train, and juggling punches, grabs, and throws with well-timed shotgun blasts to juggle hordes of enemies is immensely fun.  Mastering the flow keeps the combat fresh,  and the enemy variety ensures you're constantly adapting your tactics.Evil West isn't shy about its inspirations. It channels classic action titles like God of War and Devil May Cry,  but with a distinct western flair.  The visceral combat feels great,  and the "over-the-top" meter encourages stylish takedowns that unleash a satisfying slow-motion sequence.However, Evil West isn't without its flaws. The story, while serviceable,  is a bit predictable.  You're here to shoot and punch monsters, not win an Oscar,  but some more character development could have elevated the experience. The environments, while detailed,  can feel repetitive at times, with a lot of dusty canyons and abandoned towns.The co-op mode is a welcome addition,  letting you team up with a friend for some monster-slaying mayhem.  While it's a blast to tear through enemies together,  the lack of progression saving for the second player feels like a missed opportunity.

Little did I know that the monsters would wipe the floor with me, ha-ha! The first few levels on Evil mode were not too crazy, but once the story progressed into areas I knew I had trouble with on Normal mode, I was sweating bullets and wanting to rage quit. Different monsters were one hit, killing me, and no matter how much I leveled up my gear and spend my bucks on awesome weapon upgrades, it was still not enough to kill them without me having a long, drawn-out battle. I had to maneuver around very carefully, so I didn't end up in the line of fire when the game started to throw 3 or 4 boss monsters in with a horde of regular monsters, and my goodness, did those guys with the Gatling gun drive me INSANE WITH RAGE!! Why did this game want to torment me so much?!?! Finally, when I got to the end and beat the game on Evil mode, I felt like I had accomplished it all! I was a freaking vampire killing machine! I still have a few more achievements left to get on this game, but I'm going to ride the high of playing this game one both Normal Mode and Evil Mode back to back! So yes! After playing this for 54 hours, I recommend this game! have fun playing!

_childDocuments_.review: In every man there are two wolves. One follows the principle set by Maria Callas: life is too short to spend it on average [insert some product of culture and entertainment]. The other knows, that not everything has to be a 10/10 experience, a next Unreal / Half-Life 2 / Elden Ring / whatever-is-your-GOAT-game; and sometimes it is just as fun to enjoy a 7/10 product.If the first wolf dominates your approach to computer gaming - skip this title. If you're fine to pay an AA price (read: it tastes better when bough on sale) for a dozen and a half hours of solid enjoyment: yes, Evil West can be for you.This game will also smell very familiar to all of you, who played Shadow Warrior (well, apart from player's perspective ^^'). The protagonist is a cocky chap, who probably sniffed too much testosterone in a gym, in his younger years. The story is... there, but it is mainly an excuse to move from a battle arena to a battle arena and curbstomp some ugly fiends, using a mix of melee and ranged weapons mashed together into a high-octane cocktail. It is quite showing, that after obtaining your "uber-attack", the game actually encourages you to go for a build that will allow you to fire it thrice (if not even more often) every fight. Because why efff not.I've also seen some comparisons with Devil May Cry series; with Evil West posed to act as the "poorer brother" of Capcom's famous franchise. I think they sorta makes sense, both in terms of setting (an agency set to hunt monsters), atmosphere (cheeky, reluctant hero); and some play mechanics. It is however important to spot some differences. I think the biggest for me is almost total absence of combos, the playstyle so characteristics of all the Bayonettas, Dynasty Warriors and other japanese hack'n'slashers out there. Instead, it leans rather into a more brutal juggling of different powers. I imagine it might get tedious for some; it might lack a certain elegance for other people. I for once quite enjoyed the game, that didn't require me to be born a Hindu god as a way to be able to master its combat system on a keyboard.Finally, what sold me on giving it a positive review is a good balance of difficulty and feeling of power (albeit for it you really need to scavenge all the cash hidden around the maps, to afford subsequent upgrades and get bonus perks). It is quite a pleasant feeling, when by the end of the game, you can pretty much rolfstomp a baddie who several chapters ago acted as a mini-boss. But then the game throws three other similar baddies together playing against their strengths; and a cohort of chaff to keep you occupied even more. Thus, always being a bit on the edge; never over it as to get frustrated and enter some Souls-like areas, never too far from it to get bored.And for that, its 7/10. Lets make it a 7+, +5 to Charisma for being a first action game since ages that didn't have any QTEs :DP.S. Important note: if you are, like me, looking for a good "Weird West" game - this ain't it. It's not because it is a bad Weird West game - it is because it doesn't have a lot to do with Weird West itself. You only fight some more or less gross vampiric monsters, missing all the part related to shamanic magic, First Nations bestiary, occult etc... It could be as well set in Latin America, Europe (esp. Mediterranean) and whatnot. So: please manage your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I normally, don't write reviews.  I know when I'm getting into something good or something bad.  Although a few games make me think about it.  This is one of those cases.I went into this game 100% blind.  I've never even seen an ad before I saw it on steam.  My thought process went as follows.Western era Vampire Slaying sounds awesomeThe reviews are largely favorableI bought it, and frankly, It find it lackluster and disappointing. I started the campaign on normal and I found it was kinda challenging, but its everything else that kills me about this game.  The story is uninteresting and the characters are as stale as a month old open box of Frosted Mini Wheats.   I felt i was wisked off to strange places with minimal understanding why or what the point was.  the controls are all shoulder buttons which is fine, but you cannot re-map which is annoying.  Especially in a game where comfort with the controls matters.  Abilities are supposed to chain together, but I find constantly that I'm hitting the wrong button at the wrong time.  Bosses give you zero time to react or really learn their attacks.  And worst of all its as linear as the original super mario bros game.  Walk 10 feet forward and forget turning around.  It took me so far out of the game that I've landed here writing this review.If you take nothing from this review, take this, Bastion is essentially the same game (from a fundamentals perspective) and it has a better story, better soundtrack, and better controls than this game.Idk who paid for this game to get all these unreal reviews, but I just don't see what others see here.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is a complete game in an age where companies nickel and dime players for their cash and time. The game is a clear linear and fun experience. It has tons of weapons that you collect and can use anytime. Engaging and challenging (Sometimes too challenging) combat. Great graphics and sound design. Each of the animations feel like there's a lot of budget behind them. Cutscenes seem handmade with a lot of detail. Not just two statue NPCs standing in front of each other expositioning. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West is in other reviews often refered to as the title that reminds of PS3/Xbox360 era and it holds up to that title. Simple mechanics, no microtransactions, just pure linear gameplay. Gameplay is just as satisfying as shown in the trailers - at least for me that was the case. The story is about 10 hours and not the part where this game really shines. So you may want to decide your buy decision on whether you like the design and the question if you want to smash some vampires. But it also holds up to PS3 titles, because just like these it does come with some flaws. First it is too easy. Even on the highest difficulty it is handable until the last two missions or so. So if you're looking for a challenge, this game is probably not the right choice. And secondly the mechanics can feel a bit repetitive after time so replayability is usually not an option (except you're going for achievements).

_childDocuments_.review: : long cutscenes, closed-arenas-only combat, exploration done in GO HERE, DO YOU SEE THE BIG ICON PLAYER (why do they even make games that are apparently not for kids audiences—being gory beyond measure—but they lead you by the hand?)And, as a cherry on top, you will probably never know which doors, vaulting posts, ladders, etc. will close the rest of the map for you and when. You wanted to explore the whole map for the treasures, unlockables, and lore bits? Tough luck; this ain't the kind of game where you can explore freely. The word is there just to lure people in; you know, sohree (replay the mission, Bucko)? good graphics, okay sounds, no crashing. The action itself. I mean, it's not bad, it's okay even. But whether you use skills or not, everything feels kind of repetitive after some time. It's probably because every monster usually (but not always to be completely honest) takes bazzillions of punches before it's dead, and it doesn't matter if you've electrified it first, stunned it first, ignited it first, hitted from left, right, bottom, lifted, downed, shot with this, shot with that, etc. There's actually a notification telling you that you haven't used skills for some time and you might be forgetting. Jokes on you, game. I tend to forget to use the skills because they feel strangely forgettable despite many physical and visual effects they cause. long cutscenes (yeah, I feel it's both). Boss fights, some 'arenas' that allow you to move in larger spaces, or where you can use some environment. Combat on hard tends to be hard and demanding. The experiences, perks, and weapon upgrades all bring at least some feeling of progression, and that's always good in FPSs (sorry, 3rdPVSs :D ). The story seems, after a few hours of gameplay, engaging at times. The neatly crafted menus, the overal look, the atmosphere are... great, actually! I can't help but feel pangs of frustration. How come there was so much love being poured into the latter, but little of it was spared for creating well-thought-out gaming parts? I'll likely finish it for the said pros; I can't refund it now anyway. But boy, nah, I don't recommend it so that you people can save yourselves from spending bucks and time better to be used at other titles. So, unless you know what you're getting into (...the atmosphere), or unless you are starved of games to play, just don't bother or buy only heavily discounted.-----I judged the game a bit hastily. After some time, better skills actually allow for faster killing and for a variety that "matters". The more and more I play the better are the mission maps, the points of no return started to make sense and I rarely--if ever--make the mistake of closing the map before exploring everything, and the combat gets so significantly tougher, I almost chew the keyboard sometimes. I played the whole game on hard, and only tried normal once to see the difference. Turned out, the game actually really feelt boring that way. In normal, you can just button-mash and be done with it. On hard, healing is sparse or you have to fight for it, and you are forced to utilize most of the learned perks, acquired skills, understand how to use monsters against each other, and truly strategically choose which danger to get rid of first and how. Button mashing often results in accidental deaths. There's no shortage of that happening in under 3 seconds from the full HP bar. Generally, by a mere mob creature landing two weak strikes after you've forgotten to mind that somewhere behind your back a stronger enemy has probably just finished charging its extra-strong attack, eheh.There are healing monsters, monsters healing other monsters, monsters killing you with one or two blows, monsters with damage-reflecting shields, swarming monsters, tank monsters with AoEs, some(!) delayed stunning attacks (oh how I hate you again :), and on top of that, often the semi-boss (or two!) with their own skill-set of shenanigans. Banzaaai!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to review this game, because it feels like a rather strange game to rank.I played this with my partner in co-op and we both pretty much have the same impression about the game.First of all, we expected this game to be more shooty and less punchy when we looked at the trailers, but it truly is mainly a 3rd person brawler with some gunplay thrown in as a bonus. Aside from those mismatched expectations, allow me to present you some pros and cons from our experience:- Regardless of difficulty, even regular trash mobs feel too tanky, yes, even on the easiest difficulty.- The game has poor balancing, you get maybe 60~80% stronger at the end of the game than you were at the start, but the game just keeps spamming more and more minibosses at you in every level. These minibosses basically always feel like bosses, and never transition to a lvl were they feel like "elite monsters" such as special zombies in L4D, B4B or Dying Light. - The game was nearly released in 2023, but the exploration aspect (jumping down ledges, jumping over fences) felt more like that of a 2006~2010 game. Basically any ledge is gated with an invisible wall and you need to find the "official" path down, unlike basically any modern game where you can jump onto the arena from any ledge you happen to be at.- A lot of visual bugs, some can be mildly amusing for a while, but most simply break your immersion or are bothersome.- The controls for this game feel quite... Odd.. To say the least. - The audio is stupidly low for this game even at max settings, so you probably have to drastically increase your usual pc sound and drastically reduce the voice settings of your friends, which is bad for quality of life if you need to do this for several sessions.- You need to finish the tutorial by yourself before you can start an online campaign to play with your friend/family/partner.+ The story is solid, quite filled with archetypes and clichés but it is enjoyable and it works. Our MC Jesse, for example, is the stereotypical bruteforce hero with a blunt mouth but soft heart. + This could be considered as an addition to the story, but the world of this game is very interesting.Don't worry about spoilers, this is all tutorial content. We enjoyed how vampires are portrayed, we enjoyed their tricks and we also enjoy the portrayal of the arms race between humans and vampires. Humans embraced technology to get the edge, the stronger and "magic/ritual inclined" vampires struggle to change their traditions to survive as a species, until our main villain shakes things up. + The voice acting is quite nice. + The game is fairly linear in its level design, weapon unlocks and upgrades to your weapons and characters. You will go through the story at a nice pacing and it just feels comfortable to hide away from all the open ended games sometimes. As for the combat, music and visuals, these are fairly neutral points. Combat can start going down in quality as it gets repetitive to bully the same bullet sponge trash mobs and several bullet sponge minibosses at every corner, but it still feels mostly fine and functional enough to were it is not a deal breaker. Visuals and soundtrack are not bad nor good. To boil it down into a shorter and simpler answer:Play this for the story, not the gameplay. Fantastic gameplay is crucial? Don't get this game. Story is most important? It is worth a shot but don't expect another "the last of us."Additionally you can definitely get higher quality and/or longer games for the price of 50 bucks, so I would probably wait for a sale, that being said: 50 bucks for an 8 hour experience is still more bang for your buck than the cinema so do as you wish.

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West delivers a thrilling and unique blend of wild west and supernatural action, providing an exhilarating experience for players. Set in a reimagined frontier filled with monstrous creatures and dark magic, the game's world is both captivating and richly detailed. The graphics are stunning, bringing the eerie landscapes and nightmarish enemies to life with impressive detail and atmosphere.The combat system in Evil West is a standout feature, offering fast-paced and visceral action. Players can utilize a variety of weapons and special abilities to take down hordes of supernatural foes, making each encounter both challenging and satisfying. The game's protagonist, a gritty and determined gunslinger, adds depth to the narrative with his compelling backstory and relentless quest for justice.Evil West's storyline is engaging, weaving together elements of horror, adventure, and western genres seamlessly. The pacing keeps players on the edge of their seats, with plenty of twists and turns to maintain interest. Additionally, the game's upgrade system allows for meaningful customization, letting players tailor their abilities and gear to suit their playstyle.Overall, Evil West is a must-play for fans of action-packed adventures and supernatural themes. _childDocuments_.review: Evil West is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. You play as the American Wild West action hero version of Van Helsing, Jessie Rentier, and you kick the undying ♥♥♥♥ out of all kinds of monsters while fighting a secret war against vampires in the late 1800s. The combat is extremely satisfying, the sci-fi/comic-book-esque late 1800s weaponry is awesome, the kills are over the top and violent, and theme of the enemies, environments, and story are a horror fan's wet dream. In my experience, the combat is about 50/50 between ranged and melee, both of which are fun. It takes a few pages out of Doom Eternal's book in a number of ways including severely damaged enemies entering a "doomed" state where you can execute them for health or energy as well as putting a number of your weapons and equipment on cooldowns so you can easily rotate between them as they become available in ongoing brawls. That combat loop worked great in Doom Eternal and it works great here.Evil West really does feel like a modern game that embodies the best parts of what gaming in the 2000s was all about in the PS2/PS3 era before all the AAA games went open-ish world and focused on hitting you in the feels instead of focusing on providing engaging gameplay above everything else. This era also comes with rough edges in presentation and immersion and simple level design that barely hides unlockables and you'll find plenty of that here. Some examples of this are no animations when when NPCs talk to you, lots of glowing chains guiding your way into a pit that's clearly the next fight arena, and a fork in the road where a conveniently placed TNT barrel is very obviously only there so you can blow it up and get the optional "off the beaten path" gold pickup. If you're like me, these are really minor cons.As far as other cons, I find this over the shoulder with threat indicator arrows difficult to follow when in melee combat. I've gotten better but I still wish the camera was pulled a bit farther back when you're not aiming one of your guns for giving me a bit more spatial awareness. I also had the game crash a handful of times and one section repeatedly softlocked which I got around by quitting to the main menu and reloading my save. Hopefully the devs fix these bugs soon.If you're here for the combat, definitely check this out. I've got my fingers crossed that this sells enough that we get an Evil West 2.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, oof, I really wish Steam have a numeric ranking system rather than yes or no.Evil West absolutely delivers on the artistic aesthetic and lore structure. Traveling and fighting in many signature American landscapes and historical structures is fantastic. On top of that combined with the very deep Vampire lore Evil West is very unique I cannot get enough of it. Especially the Mineshaft under the desert with a blood-red reverse pyramid hidden within, if there is an Evil West 2 please expand on the culty aspect of it.Most of the weapons looks really hawt, when fully upgraded they become Teslapunk fantasy weapons, and I love all the details going into them.Enemy design is also great, I don't know the specific name of the genre, but I love the basic grunts with metal fused into the flesh, hinting that they were experienced and tortured by highborn. The inclusion of ancient beasts, insects and leeches, and the hint of flesh mechanical engineering for glamors revitalized the concept of vampire as a creepy and very resourceful foe is probably the biggest W of Evil West, especially after Twilight nearly all vampires became well-dressed but boring X-Men.Now here comes the L.The biggest complaint I have is that the combat actually feels flat. Being a skill check action game it is a combination of new DOOM and DMC, but at the end, it falls short of either one.First Evil West is by no means a very Dex game, the dodge is very fast and maintains attack but beyond that, there are no advanced in-arena traveling mechanisms. So most of the combat arena is very very and very bland, and the lack of mobility results in a lack of cool maneuvers. Shield dash is the only advanced traveling skill I can think of but enemies close the distance almost instantly due to the arena being flat and bland.To force the players to juggle the enemies, enemies are very bullet spongy under normal difficulty. Most of the upgrades and skills look cool but are not effective, making the first playthrough very painful, especially at the last quarter. Ground slam and revolver electrical ricochet are the two most disappointing upgrades IMO. They lack the damage and barely have any crowd control function as you would expect from other games' experience.Bullet sponge problem is also very painful when it comes to supposedly fragile enemies, such as the one spitting small bugs. They would just keep on tanking the damage, but they should serve more of an accuracy check that encourages players to take them out with well-placed shots.Skill tree also shows how devs forces the players to go for their desired play style, rather having extensive trees allowing for different styles. Generally in first playthrough with some extensive exploring character should achieve lv20 with serval perk points, and about half of the upgrades unlocked. Meaning there are plenty spaces for different styles available for players to try in NG+.Personally, rather than electric build I would hope for more gun build, such as allowing the players to use revolver for weakpoint hit in close distance. Especially considering how weak the revolver is in the late game.Lastly, for a skill-check action game, the control is extremely janky by the genre's standard. Electric shield is the most janky one IMO, the expand time is awkward and should base it on a charge gauge, and shield rushing and pulling often does not register well, especially when using it in a pinch. In the future it is vital to work on it.So in the end, I'm conflicted. I generally have many rage moments due to the system but the artistic aspects did keep me going. Granted I'm not good at skill-check based action game so I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt that I sucked not the game's problem. Therefore I'm keeping it as recommended.

For example:Why are there so many nonsensical barricades that need to be crossed together even when there was nothing waiting on the other side.Why does Jesse have a buddy that can not be played by the non-host, or any other Rentier-Institute Character for that matter. Why does the non-host not gain any progress even when we played 100% of the story togetherWhy are there sections in the game that Limit the playing to 1 Person when it easily could have been avoided.(Like the first cart-ride where you have a 3-part-Lorry but only 1 gets used for the host) So I believe this game runs best in Singleplayer.And some of the bugs can be fun in Multiplayer.And I generally enjoyed the game throughout the Playthrough.But it did fall a little short, which is a shame.Still recommend people to give it a Play. _childDocuments_.review: Thank you to the developer Flying Wild Hog and publisher Focus Entertainment for providing another exciting and challenging action game for me to explore, fight, rage and rage again. My Steam review rating: PositiveI have said forever Guns+Magic is a perfect recipe for any action game and Evil West proves that formula still works extremely well. It's reminiscent of some of my favorites in the genre(Outriders and Remnant from the Ashes) and never lets up in the action while told with a good story that is very familiar. Evil West is a re-imagining of the old west where vampires, werewolves and demons are real. You play as Jesse Reinterre, a member of a Gov entity called the REI institute. This was established by your father where it is your Co. job to rid the west of the evil that has plagued the land. It's a solid set up, good voice acting, writing, characters  and cut scene direction. The story reminded me of the movie Blade. There is even a scene early showing the two antagonists, an older Vampire Peter D’ Abano and his young daughter Felicity proclaiming to the elders, either rule the world or fall victim to the evolving humans who have reached the steam age. Their denial from the elders to start an all out war with humans chain reacts into the events that will be taking you across pretty exciting 16 missions and depending on difficulty 12-15+ hrs campaign(I have 60hrs thru 3 full playthroughs). One thing on cut scenes is they sometimes will end abruptly or you will even approach what is a cut scene, and then you are back in the game. While it doesn't affect the overall story, either scenes were removed(you only see the elders at the start) or maybe they were not completed? I Don't know, its just weird. *On Difficulty, you can choose from story, normal, hard, or Evil but the game is meant to be played thru multiple times. If you DON'T want to reach def-con 5 levels of rage, start on Normal. You will thank me later.The heart of all FWH games is fast, manage cool down, arena style combat and it is all here, maybe just not as fast. The difference here prior to their other games is this in 3rd person and while you still get that dash move, you also get to roll. All weapons are on a cool down and your special abilities and upgrades evolve around the power of the era, electricity. This is why I love their earlier titles such as Shadow Warrior and Hard Reset, and why I love this game. You will constantly be switching thru every weapon which includes revolver, rifle, crossbow, gatling gun, grenades, and flamethrower in almost every fight. However, the main weapon of the game is the Reinterre Gauntlet which is fully highlighted in the main menu. You will be pulling, throwing, slamming, punching everything in sight and it's fantastic. All weapons have upgrade trees which require blueprints and money to unlock but the gauntlet will be upgraded as you level. Its tree is unique as it will give special abilities to perform those massive damage combos by collecting glowing orbs that drop from defeated enemies.As an arena game the enemy variety, the mob and boss fights have to be fun and it does so here almost perfectly. There is a large variety of enemies to combat and early game is pretty manageable with basic cannon fodder but around mid game the real challenge begins with enemies who shield the mobs and also heals them. That’s to name a few of the many types you will encounter and all when mixed together provide a good challenge. You will be rolling, dashing and doing everything you can to collect orbs so you can unleash your ultimate. I can guarantee one thing in this game, in any fight you will never be standing still.I saw some early reviewers complain that the linearity of Evil West was a weak point but I totally disagree. While the game is very linear in design, this game proves that style can still work but having to get a button prompt to climb and jump in only highlighted designated places feels weird in 2023. As the levels are linear and decent size, there are many branching paths that could lead to extra fights, money needed for upgrades, or secret cases containing blueprints for weapons. This makes exploring every corner of the map a must and while there is no map for any level, there is a lore tab that provides info for how many collectibles  there are for each level. Some levels will also require solving a few puzzles that open a path which will require shooting an object or transferring electricity to power poles. These are not difficult in any way but are there to provide a breather from combat. You will be fighting in many different locations from the expected Old west town, oil fields, to lumber and train yards to name just a few. Each location will also  provide different weather conditions(just recalled that) and it will either be day or night.  I think the game looks amazing as the art direction is top notch and as it is an unreal game, expect a crash or two(always happens to me).  If you are a fan of the genre or of FWHs previous titles, then this is a no brainer. A solid story, great atmosphere and hard hitting combat from start to finish. I was never bored, but challenged and the pay off at the end of 3 full playthroughs, I wanted more. The game is priced at $40 and if I knew of the replayability that is a fair price but I got it on sale for $20. That was a steal. PositivesAwesome SP action game from start to finishComplete game, no DLC needed(last patch was a month after release)Jesse is a Hero we need todayStory, writing and characters Every location looks amazingGood variety of enemiesFun achievement list to 100%NG+, Chapter select and info on collectiblesNegatives2 late game mob fights feel addedPlayed at 3440x1440 High settingsAvg 100FPSRadeon RX 6700XTAmd Ryzen 5 360016GB Ram

_childDocuments_.review: Not very good GoW2018-like set in the Wild West.The story is forgettable, the characters are not very likeable, the levels are extremely linear and anything that isn't combat is pretty boring, but even the combat becomes not very good after a while.Honestly wish I could refund the game, but the first couple hours were just fun enough that I thought maybe it'd be ok, but no, after completing the game I regret spending both time and money on it.The combat starts off well enough, you can punch enemies, shoot them, juggle them in the air, launch them into spikes, other enemies or explosives, or knock them off the edge into abyss below; use electricity to either pull them close or dash towards them, shock enemies to stun them for a quick beatdown which is very useful against human-size enemies, you can shoot enemy weakpoints for extra damge and to interrupt their attacks, execute them to regain health, etc. As you progress you will find more guns and gear, and unlock different upgrades which, if you dislike, you can respec and change for free at special stations, usually found in the hideout you visit between missions. You have unlimited ammo, but you still need to reload your guns and some of the later weapons, like the shotgun and the gattling gun, recharge their ammo automatically after a bit of time.But some of the weapons, like the aforementioned gattling gun, take absolute AGES to recharge ammo, like, you'll use it in one fight and then you won't have it even half full by the time you get to the next one, and running from one arena to the next is filled with boring sections where you do extremely basic "puzzles" like...pushing a cart into place...or shooting a chain to make it fall so you can climb it...really mind bending stuff here...Also you will encounter more and more poorly designed fights the more you progress. The game only has a couple real bosses, ones that have a big on-screen health bar, the rest of special enemies that might seem like bosses are actually minibosses, and very soon you will start meeting all of them as regular enemies, and that'd be fine if they weren't such damage sponges, or if the game didn't just throw like 3-4 of these tankier enemies at you at once later on, aided by a dozen or more regular enemies.These bigger enemies don't flinch when you hit them(with exception of some special attacks), they take a long time to stun for a beatdown, and the beatdown barely deals any damage to them, anyway, even if you fully upgrade the beatdown skills.Later fights become so full of these tankier enemies that you don't even have time to do full melee combos on them cause you'll be too busy dodging all the attacks the enemies throw at you, you're kinda forced into chipping away enemies' health while frantically dodging until either they die or you manage to charge up your Gauntlet enough for the supercharge mode(basically like rage mode or smth) which is like the only effective way to deal with bigger enemies quickly, and even then most of the stronger enemies can survive a full combo of supercharged attacks, meaning you might have to do it two or even more times.And don't even get me started on the actual bosses, they are just really not fun to fight. They take forever to kill and their attacks are pretty hard to dodge, too. You will die while fighting them, but not because they're challenging, more so because their attacks are often kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And the last boss fight is SUCH a hassle, really just not fun at all.Also after you beat the game you get New Game+ and the menu tells you it will provide a "more challenging but rewarding experience", but that is a complete lie because it's a more easy experience since you start the game with whatever upgrades you had unlocked by the end of your playthrough, giving you a strong start, but the enemies are literally all the same - they don't have different placement, they're not made stronger, they don't come at you in bigger numbers - it's the exact same stuff, but you have a ton of upgrades right out of the gate.Also, speaking of upgrades, you will NOT unlock all of them in one playthrough. There's not enough enemies in the campaign to kill to level up enough to unlock all character perks, and there isn't enough money in the game to unlock all of the gun and gear upgrades.TL; DR Just don't buy it. Or wait till like 50% or more sale, idk.It starts off pretty fun but quickly becomes quite tedious to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: Although Evil West’s plot and pacing with the sudden jumps to different scenes gets exhausting, the plot is entertaining and one that you get invested in. This game is a classic example of what video games should be. It doesn’t try to be over the top nor does it fall flat and get boring. Flying Hog made a video game and that’s pretty much what this is. The combat is excellent, the world design and music really sets the mood. The character and enemy designs are beyond what you’d expect in $40 package. This game has a labor of love behind it and you can tell from the first mission on. Each level is masterfully crafted to make the pace flow and never does it drag on too long and they look so damn cool. Each combat encounter feels as though you are actually fighting harder and harder bosses, like the main villain is truly getting worried that you’re getting closer. So, they toss the biggest baddest guys at you constantly. It gets better as you keep going, which most games keep spamming the same boring enemies at you for hours. But once you get near the end of the game, some technical issues may start to pop up. By act 10 I constantly had audio issues when I went to level up, but other than that it was a smooth run. If you made it to the end of my honest review. Thanks for reading! Give this game a shot if you’ve been dying for a classic game, or if you find it on sale. I think this will go down as one of those hidden gems that will eventually get its recognition by word of mouth. 8.5/10 Cuhlassic game experience that I’ve missed.

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on the Van Helsing style of game. A lot of the vampires feel a bit more like zombie variants, but overall its fun to see the world and lore well developed and fight unique enemies. Combat is difficult enough to be a rewarding adrenaline rush that sometimes take a couple tries, but intuitive enough that tactics do matter and that can help avoid the grueling frustration of repeated deaths for the same encounter.The progression is at a rate that keeps new things added often enough to prevent gameplay from getting too repetitive, and overall its a beautiful world. Voice acting carries the story along in a way that was better than expected from this type of game, and its the most fun I've had in something like this since probably the Dishonored or Bioshock franchise.Only downside for me is the teleporting punches aspect of your gauntlet gets to be a bit too much for my personal preference. I want the gritty western feel of the guns, and I do love the tesla steampunk inspiration for a lot of it very much, but it veered a little too much into beat-em-up superhero level melee, which took some of the weight away from the weapons and the fact that vampires are meant to be stronger and faster than humans, and also broke away from the limitations of the time period a bit too much even for fantasy (for me.)  I'd have appreciated more customization options for character development as I was really looking forward to a more traditional Vampire Hunter loadout and while most or all of the weapons one could want for that do exist in this game, your actual talent tree is limited to either electromancer or anime boxer. But overall, a fantastic game.8.5/10. Looking forward to seeing some DLC content for this, could easily get it up to a 9 or higher.
