_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a pump shotgun(From the hit battle Royal game Fortnite!) You don't know Fortnite? We'll let me tell you a little bit about it,  In Fortnite, players collaborate to survive in an open-world environment, by battling other characters who are controlled either by the game itself, or by other players. The single-player or co-operative (played with friends) mode, called 'Save the World', involves fighting off zombie-like creatures. Also Fortnite has a very engaging story, to begin An orgonazation named IO made a battle royale island using the ZERO POINT. A big giant ball that connects every reality.This was a loop: 100 PEOPLE DROP IN AND 1 REMAINS.      Then On May 1st 2018, the Meteor struck the Island, destroying a Factory and half of Dusty Depot. Smaller shards of the comet crashed into different areas, creating craters near Fatal Fields, Snobby Shores, the Motel, in the center of Tilted Towers, near the Dirt Track, and even in the new drive-in theater, Risky Reels. Glowing geodes - Hop Rocks - peppered the map. These objects held strange powers within them, one of which when consumed would allow people to have temporary low gravity effects. However, there was much more power within them that could be harnessed.      On June 30th 2018, The Visitor launched the rocket. It's engine crashed into Anarchy Acres, and the rocket, after boosting itself up into the sky, began to fall back down, pointing lasers at Tilted Towers, shortly before a Rift appeared and swallowed the rocket. The rocket re-appeared above Moisty Mire, and started flying around the Island, before eventually being sucked into another Rift near a mountain by Greasy Grove. A bigger Rift appeared above Loot Lake, and the rocket flew out of it, creating a huge Crack in the sky before finally disappearing. After that The Crack in the sky started spitting out lightning in the desert as it slowly shrank and turned purple, on a silent hill of cacti. The Crack consistently shot lightning at each individual cacti on the hill, the last bolt of lightning eventually creating a CUBE, causing The Crack to vanish from the sky. The CUBE, a strange purple object illuminated with runes and shot lightning when threatened, started rolling around the map. On its path, it crushed a hut near Fatal Fields and creating seven runes in the ground across the map, causing low gravity zones. It also damaged a new building in Tilted Towers, one that replaced the old one destroyed by a meteor.      On September 19th, The CUBE eventually rolled into the Loot Lake, dissolving and making the water bouncy, remaining for multiple days. The reason for entering the lake was at the time unknown.     On September 27, the CUBE returned from The Sinking Event, turning the island in the middle of Loot Lake into a Floating Island, and turning Loot Lake into a Leaky Lake, the water dropping into a strange hole that could not be entered by the people of the island. The seven runes across the map blew up, creating Corrupted Areas. Traveling across the map, the Floating Island visited the Corrupted Areas, absorbing the power of the runes. Many weeks after traveling across the map, all the Corrupted Areas lifted from their places and floated to the Floating Island at the center of the island, sending it the rest of their power. A few days after, The Floating Island abandoned the Corrupted Areas and returned to Leaky Lake, and created a portal in the sky. Eventually, the CUBE gave off a small explosion, dividing the island into multiple pieces and sending multiple CUBE Obelisks across the island, summoning multiple CUBE Monsters. Vindertech introduced an ATV known as Quadcrasher.      Later On December 6, the iceberg from the distance hit the southwest part of the map, burying Flush Factory in snow and Greasy Grove under ice. Also  On February 28th, The Prisoner used his power to turn Wailing Woods into a large jungle biome, along with a large Volcano, and destroying Lazy Links and some parts of Tomato Temple. In the original place of Lazy Links, a Lagoon was created, a new location set to be the home for pirates, called Lazy Lagoon. In response to the creation of the jungle biome, a Expedition Base was set up in the original location of The Block. Vindertech introduced round glass vehicles called Ballers. But then On May 9th, the remains of Tilted Towers and Retail Row were replaced by Neo Tilted and Mega Mall, futuristic versions of the old buildings. The Volcano was also turned into a Pressure Plant controlled by The Unknown Investigation Agency. A few weeks after the futuristic change, Polar Peak slowly collapsed and a incredibly large one eyed monster came out, and fled to the water. Sightings of the monster could be seen swimming across the map occasionally, Polar Peak on its back. Not too long after its escape, it attacked a building in Snobby Shores that was defending from vikings. It soon attacked a modern building in Pleasant Park and destroyed a large building in Loot Lake, damaging the power cord to Neo Tilted.        The Zero Point, shortly after The Final Showdown Event, blew up and caused time to break, reverting Dusty Divot and Dusty Diner back into Dusty Depot and the Factory, only seconds before they would have been hit hit by the Meteor again, however it was frozen in midair. The UIA, who had helped construct the Mecha Team Leader developed a powerful mech known as the B.R.U.T.E.       Then in Chapter Two On October 15th, two days since The End Event, The black hole decays and rebirths reality and the universe. From this, the matter of the Island was reorganized, creating the new Chapter 2 Island that is heavily different to the old one, with some POIs remaining. On this Island, a faction called E.G.O. and A.L.T.E.R., who were possibly sent by The Seven or may be against them, are in constant wars between each other. The next season The constant war continued to February 20th between E.G.O., now known as GHOST, and A.L.T.E.R., now known as SHADOW. A mysterious figure known as Midas joins GHOST, becomes leader of the group, and also creates The Agency over Eye Land, the center of the island. Then season 3 the map flooded, thats it.        But then On August 27th, sometime after the Marvel characters arrived, they were quickly to lose their memories. From losing their memories, they seemed to lose most of their powers. But Thor knew he had to remember his purpose for bringing all of the heroes onto the island. All the characters set out on journeys to awaken themselves so they could regain their powers and defend their reality from the threat that was coming, Galactus. After defeating galactus In the aftermath of the battle to save reality, Agent Jones wakes up in his office and answers the ringing phone. A mysterious woman, likely his superior, tells him that although The Zero Point isn't destroyed, it is still exposed and unstable. Agent Jones must go into the Loop to reseal the bridge, stabilize The Zero Point, and not let anyone escape the Loop. On March 16th, Jones rode on top of a Battle Bus over the Island. His superior on his earpiece, known as Doctor Slone, ordered him to save himself and not go to The Seven after swearing an oath, but Jones continued to ignore her. He believed The Seven were the thing that would rescue reality, as long as he was able to work with them. A reality wave was shot out from The Zero Point, causing Jones to lose The Rift Device he used to enter and exit The Loop. And then after that aliens invaded the island the map did a flip. _childDocuments_.review: I would really like to give this game a positive review, but in its current state I’m not comfortable recommending it. Evil West is really fun, when it works, but it's riddled with so many bugs, often game breaking, and it doesn't look like the devs are doing any effort to fix those.Some of the issues I encountered during a single playthrough of the co-op campaign along with my s.o. are the following:Opening a chest sometimes results in getting stuck in place.Once I had the crosshair reticle somehow move offset resulting in none of my shots connecting because I was shooting half a meter below the location my crosshair was pointing at.Enemy falls off a cliff: softlock. (A good portion of the combat is melee centered, with the possibility of throwing enemies in the air and “cannonballing” them away, so it's fairly easy to accidentally throw one of them off an edge in open arenas).Teammate gets stuck behind an object (train cart), resulting in a softlock (and when they disconnected I got kicked out of the session). In some levels, opening the perk / upgrades menu first breaks the audio, then completely freezes the game and in one instance even crashed my whole computer with a black screen, I had to reboot.Weird graphical glitches both on AMD and Nvidia GPUs. With AMD (mainly) the snowy terrain moves (up and down when the character gets closer or further). On Nvidia items glitch on screen, there are floating weapons, and often an endless rope coming out of the other player (lol).In addition to all that, the usual Unreal Engine stutters are the cherry on top. At least I've been able to solve this issue when I switched to my Linux PC, which through the use of Vulkan somehow made the stutters go away.Some of these issues were so prominent that at some point we were on the verge of dropping the game altogether. In the end we managed to push through the critical areas and ultimately complete the campaign. And I must say, the game, when it works, is tons of fun! It mixes some souls-lite and beat ‘em up elements in a dark western setting, with vampires and werewolves to slain. Combats are challenging enough at normal difficulty and somehow gave me some kind of primordial joy when we finally managed to get past any new boss.The game also looks good and plays smoothly, with a pretty nice soundtrack which really fits the setting and really goes well along the game.The story is not important at all, but still kinda enjoyable, and the enemy design is really well put together. I'm so sad this is such a missed opportunity for an insanely fun game, which got crippled by so many technical issues. It wouldn't have been GOTY material for sure, but still a very solid and fun shooter. Unfortunately I cannot recommend it in its current state, so feel free to try it at your own risk, and be ready to put up with a lot of inconvenience if you do.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not in and of itself not that long took around 10ish hours, and overall is worth a pickup if you can find it on a decent enough sale. There were only a few bugs that occurred in my playthrough nothing gamebreaking but minor gripes like objectives taking a while to load in, but no major stutters or crashes.      While I think the level design, as it is rather linear, could use some variety, the enemy types more than makeup for it, and all the weapons feel unique and you will definitely need you're full arsenal as every enemy is weaker to certain weapon types than others. Big heavy bruises, small fast runts, projectile/vermin spewers, and a good helping of mini-bosses all take different approaches to combat.    The voice acting is very hit and miss, while some sound like a novice impersonating a poor western accent, others feel as though they are hitting their stride fairly well. However the ending seems to be wrapped up as quickly as possible without ever really feeling that all the unaddressed questions got their time in the limelight and does leave you with a sense that it was too abrupt.      In conclusion it was a great combat system with a fairly cookie cutter story, hit and miss voice acting, great enemy and art assets and if on sale worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a game that isn’t good or bad and is just simply mediocre? Well, that’s . This game takes inspiration from games like , and some shooting mechanics from . They just mashed them together adding nothing new to the table and decided to call it a day. I’ll of course go into detail about everything it has to offer and my experiences.In this review, I will be comparing this game to  and . I should add that I have only played GoW4 and none of the others, so only it will be mentioned.Taking place in the 18th century  works for the , a secret organization that aims to take out supernatural creatures like the . Vampires hunt and prey on humans and have special powers associated with them.  is equipped with a special gauntlet that is helpful in dealing with them. He works with his father and retired agent  and must take out  daughter, .The story and characters of  are shallow. Yes, they do have development and motivations for them doing what they are doing. However, they don’t have much to really like about them. The main villain in this game looks like a character you would see in a typical horror movie that you know is just evil, it’s uncreative. The other characters aren’t really better either and aren’t interesting in the slightest. I’ve never played a game where all the characters act like they hate each other but just agree that they have a mission to do, it’s like the  team. is an action beat 'em up that has some fun gameplay moments but has a slew of issues with it. You will use your gauntlet and a revolver to help take out enemies but you will also get your hands on other guns, there are no other melee weapons in the game. Most of the weapons you get are rather fun to use and actually do have usage to them, the only weapon I never found useful was the flamethrower. Except when I had to go out of my way to actually use it to burn an obstacle down. There will also be times when  can put himself into an overpowered state and he can kill enemies by teleporting and is invincible while doing it if you spam it. This will consume all of your batteries but one so use it wisely, you can also do a shockwave attack that consumes one battery. You get batteries by defeating enemies or finding items that replenish one.There will be times in combat when an enemy will do a certain attack and will show their weak spot, you can use the rifle or crossbow to hit the weak spot and do a big amount of damage. I highly recommend you attack them as you will also get health pickups. Overall, the gameplay is fun at times, there are some enjoyable moments to it that I do like, although I say fun at times, for a good reason.The gameplay, while fun can be tedious, as you are going to one part of the map, to an open space full of enemies to fight. There will be occasions where you may have to push something but this makes the gameplay rather lackluster. There isn’t really anything special or new that this game does, to make it stand apart from its predaceous in any way. I really wish there was a lock-on feature but there isn’t one and I did press every button on the controller. I’ve never played a game, where a basic feature is present in every  game (except the first one), and  is not included in a hack-and-slash game, I’m baffled by it.The enemies will also sometimes pull off their most annoying attacks, making you have to choose which targets to exploit the weak points. One attack may go off, unless you are lucky and happen to get them both but you may have to rely on dodging for the most part. There is an auto lock-on feature to point toward the enemy's weak points but sometimes other enemies may get in the way and take the bullet you were going to use to hit that enemy.The upgrades you get don’t really do much in terms of making you feel powerful, they have a use but all of them are just there. You can upgrade your weapons by funding bucks or really, it’s just gold and you can level up to get a perk upgrade. This also goes with the collectibles you can find, most of them aren’t really worth it. You can either find bucks, which does help in weapon upgrades, hidden perks, which is the best thing you can find in my opinion, or lore you probably don’t care about.I have to compare  and  again here, they have collectibles that are worth finding, you can get health upgrades,  meter extension, etc. In , there is none of that, there are perk upgrades that can increase your health by 15% and one that gives you one extra battery but that’s it. I’ve never played a game where I just don’t care about collectibles, that's two things that are missing from a typical hack-and-slash. graphics, while outdated, do look nice in some areas. I experienced a few glitches like me being taken out of the map, floating objects, enemies getting stuck, and a few others. I unfortunately tried to complete the game but I ended up putting the game on window mode, for me to revert it back but my frames dropped completely. I tried fixing it but to no avail, meaning I had to drop the game and there is no way I am playing another 10 hours of this game.Finding good things to say about  is difficult. I first saw the trailer for the game and I wanted to play it for me to only be disappointed.  isn’t a bad game, it’s just ok, it has some steep competition and those games are in my opinion much better and worth your money. _childDocuments_.review: This might get a bit rambly but bear with me. I am torn, I like the premise, characters, world, setting etc. The art design is wonderful. But everything else that makes this game a "game" is considerably flawed. It feels like a 2002 console game mechanically. 1. Graphics: As I said the art design is great. But everything else I cannot understand. The worst thing: Forced TAA. Performance loss and it looks like I smeared vaseline on  my monitor. So I disabled that sh*t (via config file). But now everything is shimmering. There is no alternative. Why is there no FXAA option? FOV slider was integrated by now so that's fine (and dearly needed). There is contant pop-in for no reason, You move the camera around and textures just change. They don't get more or less detailed, they are just different. Don't know why. Sometimes you just get 2D Textures instead of 3D trees, rotating and fixed to your camera. Like I said: feels very 2000s. I get a headache looking at the game. And I might repeat myself: It's not ugly, just feels like it was designed for a CRT monitor/TV. 2. Gameplay: There isn't much. I played Dark Souls, Elden Ring, Devil May Cry and never had any issues. But I had to set this game to Difficulty: "Story Mode" and am still dying regularly. I don't know, but somehow the combat system feels convoluted. There are systems upon systems you will likely never use but the game expects you to. Most upgrades are useless as they affect weapons and systems that, as I said, you will not use as you will never have the time. You are under constant attack and pulling any specialized moves takes time and will likely see you dead, And the upgrades affecting your used skills mostly don't do anything. I mean there is a Perk do drop a Health pickup instead of Energy and there is a Perk to drop an Energy pick up instead of Health. You can get both. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯3. Story: I have no idea. Feels unfinished, Like they completed some cutscenes but were missing some in between. I often find myself wondering why I am where I am and why people tell me they thought I was dead without any reason to, Then out of nowhere an NPC falls down from the heavens to assist me somewhere while they still thought me dead. And nobody moves there lips out of cutscenes, They talk audibly but the model remains tight lipped. Conclusion: I am unsure. If you have a 16:9 1080p monitor or are sitting across the room looking at a TV you might not notice the graphical issues. Try it, refund if you get nauseous. For anyone who cares about graphical clarity: stay away. Story is cool but it seems like parts are missing (large parts). Gameplay is practically non-existent and if it is you don't have enough fingers for it. Or I am just too old. It might be advisable to just look up a cutscenes compilation on Youtube, They are pretty cool, I really like the western vibe, the f*ck you attitude of the protagonist, the world, practically anything else BUT the game itself. Make a movie, write a visual novel. Feels like somebody wanted to tell a story and chose the wrong outlet. Or make a passable game. Or finish it. This one is so frustrating. I want to like it. I am torturing myself and am playing through it, just to see the end. I never set any game to "Story Mode" . I hate the game but love the world. Certainly not worth 50 "Bucks".

_childDocuments_.review: Evil West is an ARPG about cowboys and vampires. You play as Jesse Rentier, lead agent of the Rentier Institute; an organization focused on fighting vampires. The game starts with a derailed train full of blood sacrifices. This leads the Institute to finding a more powerful foe that threatens the country itself.The game is primarily action with light RPG elements and is surprisingly difficult. Although that was probably my fault as I chose to play on hard on my first run. Progression is decent with me reaching level 20 by end game and no real need to re-spec as you can unlock most abilities by 16. Some you will have to find throughout the levels and New Game+. The game is a mix of melee, range and special abilities with some enemies needing to be shot while they show their weak points. The wide variety of enemy types keeps the challenge fresh and interesting as some enemies requires specific strategies and priorities. By end game you will have a full arsenal of weapons though not all weapons are particularly useful, looking at you crossbow and maybe flamethrower. The game uses pre-rendered cutscenes, which can be jarring when the outfit you're wearing doesn't match the scene as well as the quality of the renders. Visually, the game looks alright though I feel that it's a tad bit over-saturated. It isn't bad at all for a AA game.Overall I find the game to be quite enjoyable with the highlight obviously being the combat. It's flow and enemy variety presents a game that is both fund and challenging. I recommend this game for those looking for a good time.7 out of 10 - too many vampires to kill.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I have to say that I liked this game very much, I got it on the winter sale for 40 bucks and although I have to say that I don't regret having purchased it, It's not worth 50$ and maybe not even 40$, that is what I paid for it.The developers tried to make a brawler beat 'm up that is pure action, and they succeed to a certain degree.The core of the game is the combat sistem, which is the best part of Evil West, a little bit clunky at times but fun and engaging.I've read many people complaining that the game is too short, and as this is true, my recommendation is to play it in one of the highest difficulty levels. If they were trying to make a pure action game, don't spend so maytime working in the story and the cinematics and put it in refining the action, more enemies, more levels, more weapons and more customization, specially enemies. _childDocuments_.review: My review for the Single Player experience:The pros: - Really fun combat after getting a couple of perks and weapon upgrades. - Good enemy variety. - Really good looking environments. - Really good looking particle effects. - Easy to pick up and learn how to play. - Really good sound for weapons, melee, effects in general.The cons: - Clunky unresponsive controls with KB+M. A lot of the time I get stuck with no action happening even when I string combos in a timely manner. Impossible to string an uppercut right at the end or at the middle of a combo, the game just doesn't register it. Lots of times I'm stuck with the rifle in my hand unless I re-press the button to un-holster it. Sometimes the game doesn't even register input for attacking after sprinting or dodging. - Boring incessant cutscenes with very bad voice acting and writing. Not kidding, half the gametime is just cutscenes, if you skip them this turns into a 6-7 ish hour game. - Bugs: lots of getting stuck in terrain in combat, getting stuck inside the floor (some enemies do this too), invisible walls where there shouldn't be. Puzzles getting stuck. - Pretty horrible balancing in higher difficulties: the game just throw every single enemy it has at you with no regard of balance or anything. On higher difficulties two hits an you're dead, while having to juggle enemies that have instant killing hits with almost no wind up, and sometimes the game just throws all bosses at you with no trash mobs, so you can't really regenerate enough energy to use special moves and have to just rely on the clunky melee and parry system.- No way to save manually (really??? in 2022????). Most of the time you have to reach a checkpoint before exiting the game or you'll lose your progress. As of now there's NO WAY to save manually so you're stuck with the game allowing you a checkpoint.Now..for the worst part of all...the coop experience:- Progression only for the host: I can't believe that in 2022 there's still games that do this. It's absolutely infuriating.- Whoever is client and not host will have horrible de-sync constantly at all levels. The execution animations are all de-synced, the UI doesn't reflect the current status of your cooldowns, the enemies will bug out and teleport, the enemies won't be able to hit you or have de-synced animations making it impossible to parry their hits.- Constant bugs when switching weapons. For some reason sometimes when you change to the flamethrower or the gatling gunt and press the attack button, you'll punch the air instead of shooting (this caused lots of deaths that felt horribly frustrating).- Host crashes to desktop. Crashes became more frequent for the host and client the further we got into the later stages of the game.- Crashes cause infinite loading screens for client. This happened when playing on one of the final missions, there was no way to fix this except making the host progress the story in single player to a next stage for me to be able to join again.- Bugs with puzzles: the puzzles were clearly not designed for coop so doing things "out of order" can cause softlocks, fliying and getting stuck on terrain, or making them impossible to complete without loading.- Same button for actions, and dodging used to revive partner: this is really mind-boggling, the same key you use to revive your partner is the dodge key, so unless you're standing still next to his body and press spacebar the game will register that you're dodging, making it near impossible to revive your partner while 20 enemies are attacking you. I've missed countless opportunities to revive my partner because of this, and died on many other, making the combat revive feel horrendous and stupid.Honestly the devs should be ashamed of themselves for releasing the game and claiming it has "coop" in the calamitous state it is in. If the game had none of all the issues described before it would be a strong 7/10 as the combat can be tons of fun, solo or coop. The story and piss poor voice acting and cutscenes can be forgiven, it's an action game after all (not forgivable that they are so long and destroy the pacing of the game though...at least you can skip them).I can't recommend this game to anyone until they fix the horrible amount of bugs and problems the coop experience and single player experience have.Some people are even reporting crashes that delete their entire progress half-way through their ng+ playthroughs.Avoid at all costs until it is patched, or avoid entirely if it's not patched at all. Not worth the asking price in its current state. A real shame because it's not a bad game at all.

name: REKT! High Octane Stunts
detailed_description: ⚡️ SUMMARY ⚡️ REKT! is a stunt, driving game inspired by the eternal classics like Rush and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater series. In quick gameplay sessions, you will complete various challenges to unlock cars, arenas, and customizations. Do outstanding tricks and stunts to get the highest scores and face other players - rule the leaderboard! The physics model in REKT makes performing tricks incredibly smooth and easy but don’t get too comfortable - it's easy to learn but hard to master. Over 170 000 active players and GROWING. ⚡️ MASTER ALL TRICKS ⚡️ Take on the challenge and master the most awesome stunts: aerial flips, barrel rolls, loops, grinds, drifting and much more - combine them all and break your best scores!! ⚡️ CHALLENGES ⚡️ Every time you enter the arena you will be given a set of challenges. Many variables can increase or decrease their difficulty creating an infinite amount of objectives, that will attract even the most seasoned players. Endless tasks include checkpoint races exclusively designed for different arenas. ⚡️ SOLO RIDE ⚡️ Practice your stunts, unlock various cars and discover arenas in 2 singleplayer game modes: HIGH SCORE: The main game mode, inspired by the old-school arcades, will allow you to take on the challenge of the global leaderboard - remember the time is running, although there are ways to extend it. PRACTICE: Practice makes perfect, in this game mode, time does not matter, train as much as you wish - get prepared to #GETREKT ⚡️ MULTI RIDE ⚡️ Face the opponents in a local competitive mode (up to 4 players) and battle them on the way to the victory. SCORE - challenge your competitors and get the highest score. VIRUS - spread the infection by crashing into other players or avoid being infected - last car standing wins! CHECKPOINT - first to hit a checkpoint gets a point - collect 5 points to win the race. CAPTURE THE CROWN - you have 90 seconds to defend the crown - don’t let others take it over - or you won’t reign supreme in the arena.

_childDocuments_.review: REKT! High Octane stunts is an arcade based stunt racing game that takes place in a retro styled arena. Your goal in this game is to gain as many points as possible by performing stunts using your special vehicle. Keep in mind that the clock is racing against you! The game was developed by Little Chicken Game Company and published by  Release Date : 6th November, 2020Last known update: 6th November, 2020There are lots of guys that have a suspect feeling towards REKT! and I am here to clear things out. This is a legit game, it doesn’t use any copied assets etc. It definitely has a lot of work and design behind it sure as hell provides some fun!As mentioned above this is a traditional Arcade stunt game. Easiest way to explain the idea for a genre like that is the gameplay of Rocket League and Skate games. You have the traditional movement of Rocket League but combine it with the point system and environmental interaction of a traditional Skate game. Let’s take a better look. Now that we got a good understanding of the basics let's go into detail. First of all you spawn at the start of a small ramp. After completing your first stunt the game awards you  a  for the amount of stunts you performed while being in the air and lastly after the successful completion of the stunt you get a . There are a plethora of moves you can try to get, what I really liked was the addition of an interactive map that allows you to use random objects in order to collect more points, for example you can drive through some boxes or perhaps slide your car on a pole while being in the air. Many skills to choose from but sadly it doesn’t make sense as far as points go, just spamming the backflip is so much more efficient and easy to farm points which takes away some of the magic this game can offer. My best run with a variety of moves would only give me around 5 Million points, using the spam tactic on the other hand awarded me nearly 14 Million points which proves that this method is the best at the moment. I personally do not consider it so good as this is one of the reasons this game gets a little boring after some hours. Let us talk about the vehicles in the game, my first thought would be that some cars would feel the same but I was very quickly proven otherwise, after unlocking quite a lot of vehicles I can confirm that almost all of them have at least a minor difference in their driving styles. For example, you can easily “feel” the difference between the Formula 1 based vehicle and the boxxy Street cleaner utility truck and so on.Speaking of vehicles, REKT! gives you the ability to further improve each vehicle. You can upgrade multiple areas of the game, for example the  and  category are in my opinion the most important ones as these are the ones that allow you to stack up multiplied scores and so on. If you have completely upgraded your vehicle you can start making it look nicer. Granted there aren’t many options obviously, only thing you can really change are the rims, some stickers and on some vehicles the aerodynamic wing which is in the rear obviously. Changing liveries would be a pretty cool addition!Here is another game using the well-known Unity engine. Not the greatest when it comes to visuals but the Performance is amazing. Keep in mind that my Thrustmaster T150 wheel did not work but I am sure that it would be worse playing this game with a Steering Wheel. On the other hand the XBOX One controller worked flawlessly even with all of the vibrations!REKT! is truly a fun game with its nice variety in stunts and the fact that it offers a cool interactive environment. Keep in mind that anybody can run this game even on a Low end device. At this moment this game barely gets a positive rating, it surely is a good game but the lack of Online features and some of the gameplay flaws make it a little bit of a chore after a couple of hours. Still this game is a very pleasant time-waster and I hope that online stuff will be added in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: puts simple controls into your hands to generate large series of impressive stunts with coupled with highly-dampened vehicles. In short spurts, you will experience physics-defying and death-eluding cars flipping around in midair. Limited by a countdown clock, you need to do your tricks, string them together before your combo ends, and also collect the additional clocks for added time to fully maximize your score. It's like playing the  games with cars.You will be given one vehicle to start and one arena to drive and to jump around in. You will have objectives given to you in sets of 3s so that you can try to achieve them and earn some in-game currency, which can be then used to unlock 3 other arenas, and you can also use the currency to upgrade your cars. The objective coin awards are also multiplied by the number of them you achieve. If you get 1 out 3, you only get the coins for that one. If you get 3 out of 3, you get all of the coins multiplied by 3. (There is also an fifth arena that seems to be locked away under a DLC that's not yet available for purchase as of writing. But you can see it in-game when making your selections.) There are 53 total cars/vehicles that you can have. Some are unlocked through cumulative point totals that will just unlock by playing, while the others are unlocked through in-game accomplishments, such as score a certain amount in a run, or finding an object, jumping through all of the hoops, etc. You can also play an in-game spin-the-wheel gambling game with your in-game currency to try to win a car or money. (There's an issue with the gambling game, I sometimes land on a darkened car-shadow, and it says I won, but it doesn't show up in my cars page.)The stunts are easy to pull off and I have been using a controller, which works well. You just push on the right joystick to spin left or right, or to do back or front flips. To do barrel rolls, you can use the shoulder buttons. You can also stabilize the card midair to prepare for a landing. You will be given points also for drifting or doing other special tricks with the arena's environment. There will be time to string tricks together for extra combo points and multipliers, leading to some potentially high scores. If you just drive per routine for a few seconds, your combo will end and that score will get added to the total. It's a simple risk-reward system, you can try to string together many stunts, jumps, spins, etc., but if you crash before your score is tallied, you lose everything.Fortunately crashing is just part of the game, it's going to happen. If you know you got a high score and just want to take that score, you can just stop doing stunts until your score is added and then you won't have to worry. But of course you lose the multiplier and will have to build it back up. It's an arcade-style game, you will never crash and destroy your vehicle so that it's unusable before the time is up. Or at least I think so. I tried crashing and destroying a couple of cars in practice mode, and could still drive them super smashed up.The physics is quite good, the jumps and landings feel smooth. The cars tilting based on weight distributions prior to jumps seem proper. The only things that don't make sense from a physics perspective is your ability to willy-nilly do spins and tricks mid-air or to stablize. But that feels totally fine as well. Nothing feels awkward playing this game.So as I mentioned at the very beginning, this is a mobile port.  You can find the game for cheaper on the Apple App store or free on the Google Play store, but with in-app purchases. There is a free demo here on Steam for people who are interested to try it out as well. So you might as well give it a go if you think you might enjoy it. The game runs well and seems to be a decent port altogether. It looks nice on a bigger PC monitor compared to the mobile screen.Do tricks, string combos together, gather clocks for more time and land to properly secure high scores. Unlock new cars and arenas through playing instead of in-app purchases. Only one arena as of right now seeminly planned for a DLC addition (not yet available). Online leaderboards will allow you to see the impossibly high scores some people get, but you can also track your own progress in the stats. Each arena will throw objects at you (3 per run) to complete and to collect the coins to use in-game.There is also a party mode involving local MP that I did not try out, but seems like it could be fun, for 2-4 players.Controller recommended. Keyboard works fine too.Not very complex but good enough. It works well for the different cars/arenas and how they interact with each other. The cars and environment details look fine as is.The music might get a little repetitive, the sound effects work fine. For me, I can play this game in short spurts, so the music doesn't bother me.For people who want to play with easy-to-control stunt cars doing crazy stuff and to try to achieve high combos and high scores within a time limit.Base price is $5.99, and launch sale reduces it by 20% right now. Pretty reasonable price for all of the cars you can unlock through playing and the 4 arenas to do stunts in. I know it's more expensive at baseline than on the mobile platforms, but the unlocked content seems to be more without shelling out extra real cash. It's the same price as PC on Nintendo Switch1. The spin-the-wheel lottery system doesn't always give the reward it promises.2. Repetitive music (could use some more tracks or less continuous beat looping).3. Gameplay will seem a bit repetitive after a while--even though there are so many cars and they react bit differently from each other, they don't feel significantly different enough; the game could also use more maps/areans. is quite fun, especially in short sessions trying to chase after some high scores. It seems like it would be quite fun with friends in party mode as well up to 4 players. There's good physics and the controls are easy to get used to. Overall quite a nice game.It does have flaws, the biggest thing that stands out is seemingly the lack of variety after a while. The game's many different unlockable cars do seem to react relatively similarly to each other, with minor tweaks, when it comes to moving around the environment. More arenas to play in would be nice also.But it's fairly cheap for what promises to be a good time. I did have a good time as well.Overall score: 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've probably been one of the few people who were actually waiting for this game to be released on PC. Saw a gameplay video of the Switch version a while back, and it looked right up my alley. It's exactly what it says on the box: An arcade stunt game that has you build up higher and higher combos while completing semi-randomly generated challenges in a few different arenas. I can see how some people might get bored by this easily, but as someone who enjoys arena/stunt modes in other racing games, I really appreciate the value that you get for 5 bucks. The only thing that I'd really like to see would be Steam Workshop support for custom levels and cars.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one underrated indie classic, I'm a very big fan of games like Tony Hawk and Rush and this is a great combination between the two! The awesome cartoon-ish graphics, the very fun stunt physics and vehicle handling, and great attention to detail really make this worth adding to your collection, plus if you have friends for Local play, you will pretty much have a blast, just like the Playstation and Nintendo 64 days. It could use more features such as arena creation, weather options, and paint job customization, but it has done a really good job in providing a good amount of content to play how you like. This is also one of those games where I launch from time to time and I still continue have lots of good stunt-ing fun with it because i'm a sucker for games like these.So what are you waiting for? Don't sleep on this one, for around 5 bucks, you cannot go wrong!

_childDocuments_.review: REKT! High Octane Stunts is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as a cash grab by greedy mobile devs.   This is a basic low poly, low fi arcade "racing" stunt game where you're in a Fischer-Price's My-First-Stunt-Course arena and you have to do stunts while an arcade machine voice yells stuff at you about your score.  What fun, mobile peasants can pretend they're playing video games. The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the game, and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.  The most likely explanation is just that the game is designed for iPhones and must cope with the limitations of the telephones this mobile app was designed for. There's no mouse support in the game, which is extremely frustrating, just navigating the menus is a headache.  Very little effort was made in terms of porting this mobile app to PC.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is an eye watering $6 USD, plus another $6 USD of crap DLC, on app stores, it's FREE. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a whopping $12 USD premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: Rekt is basically the ultimate in casual, mindless gaming and fun. Its premise is simple, simply collect clocks, do tricks, and just let your thoughts just roll away. Is it a rich, complex game? Nope, if anything, its one of those kind of games you would play kind of like on a cold winter's night (or just a winter's night if you live in the tropics) grab your blanket, a cup of coffee or tea, and just kick back and relax with the game. Just don't expect a deep racing game. The only dislike about the game I have is that it really has no other premise. I would like to see a bigger variety of tracks, there are two sets as of this writing. Perhaps a track editor? Or say a seasonal theme? (Halloween/Christmas/etc). But really no technical complaints. name: Waking
detailed_description: Locked in the darkness of a coma, you dream. In the recesses of your mind, voices call you home, beckoning you towards the light and the void beyond. But it is not your time. Not yet. Waking is a uniquely personal journey of self reflection and remembrance combining third person exploration and real-world meditation. Traverse the twisted pathways of your mind in a quest to wake, and make choices that shape a uniquely individual experience. Along the way, face your fears and desires as you summon memories of loved ones, and do battle with those who would have you sleep forever. Features A true meditative experience - Waking blurs the line between fantasy and reality, taking you deep inside your mind both in-game and out. Third-person exploration melds with guided meditation techniques to create a new type of experience at the intersection of reflection, emotion and memory. A uniquely personal journey - Battle the forces of entropy surrounded by the ones you love. Waking asks you to draw on your own experiences, fears and desires and bring them with you on your journey to wake. Here in the dream your memories are your protectors, your companions and your weapons. A world of dreams and nightmares - The Mindscape is a treacherous place, a shifting, twisted maze of shattered thoughts and errant memory. Explore the procedurally generated halls of your mind and experience a dreamworld unlike any other, rendered in stunning cinematic splendor. A fight to survive. A fight to exist - Trapped within your dying mind you face a choice: give in to oblivion or fight for your existence. Waking’s unique combat system provides a new breed of challenge as you confront your own personal fears and call on aspects of the world itself in your battle against the darkness. Use your memories and willpower to uncover the mystery of your dreaming, and return to the waking world.

_childDocuments_.review: Please, let there be an alternate universe where this game is amazing!  With everything unique and engaging this title has to offer, it completely gets derailed by control mechanics that baffle me in a game that looks this good.  I don't enjoy feeling this way.  This is a passion project.  It shows.  Anytime an indie by ONE developer comes out, it's automatically impressive in my book.  Waking has inserted guided meditations with personal choices, leading to an awesome idea of creating weapons and abilities geared towards each players own lives.  My childhood dog, Zelda, became my little ghost familiar!  There are tons of neat ideas in here!  Alas, it became clear that the controls and fighting mechanics weren't tested enough and became the games biggest issues.  Couldn't run without constant speed changes and invisible corner collisions.  Neuron collecting, which is integral to using attacks and abilities, is so cumbersome.  Waking is such a special idea stuck in an unfinished game.  This frustrates me.  Please continue development on this.  I want to see it succeed more than most games in recent memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Waking

_childDocuments_.review: Waking makes a good first impression. The visuals are moody, the game is atmospheric, and the overall experience just feels unique. Unfortunately, the gameplay and game structure squanders these positives. The game is completely based around circle strafing dull enemies, pelting them with objects, and then using melee attacks on them for a few seconds. The majority of the game has a rogue-lite inspired structure, where you need to clear a bunch of samey, randomly-generated levels where you do the same thing. They almost all boil down to "kill some of the same enemies, activate a thing, move down to a lower level and repeat steps one and two."Of course, it'd be acceptable if the gameplay was fun but it's kind of awful. Certain objects can damage all enemies, but you'll rarely have those on you and you have to pick up melee attacks. The majority of fights will see you entering an area and immediately running into an enemy and having few means with which to attack it. So you fling a piece of clutter at it, which stuns it and makes it drop a few melee powerups. You then run up and collect the melee powerups and wail on it until you run out of melee attacks. Rinse and repeat. Enemies drop energy that you can use to summon help or call forth more weapons, but you need this energy to progress, so it's not a great idea to use it like this.Additionally, the game constantly punishes you if you get hit. You enter an area and there'll be 2 or 3 special enemy emplacements that will give you a temporary boost. But only if you disable them without getting hit. If you get hit, which you often will, they get locked permanently. But once you start these areas, all of these emplacements can be right on top of you, leaving you practically no way to defend yourself. For one, you can't dodge at all, so avoiding three projectile attacks simultaneously while trying to fight enemies that aren't currently possible to hurt feels like a giant design flaw. The only way you can hurt them is if you use your energy to summon weapons or if you happen to find them in the environment without getting hit. The default clutter that functions as your most common weapon is useless against them.Waking's big hook is that it's "personalized" to you, but that's misleading. You get to name the game's crummy weapons, abilities, and summons after things from your life. They don't feel personal, they feel pointless and they're often named awkwardly and the names are never important. Overall, the game is just a dull, slog to play through that's loaded with crummy gameplay and repetitive levels. Also, if you die at any point during a level, guess what? You have to start the entire thing over from the beginning. Even if you're fighting the boss. I absolutely cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Waking is a beautiful game with good graphics and enjoyable music. But i'd still recommend this game. I like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Waking for 25 hours and completed around 75% of the game. Gameplay OverviewWaking is a gamified SELF-REFLECTION EXERCISE, that has 2 big parts: gameplay and meditation. Being the main character of the story, you will fight your way out of a coma by killing mobs and rebuilding memories. You will run, pick-up objects, aim, shoot, and continuously select different spells to fight.As objectives are completed, a voice asks you to CLOSE YOUR EYES and invites you to travel deeply into YOUR PERSONAL MEMORIES. Waking is not a traditional action-adventure gaming experience. To experience the game as it is meant to be you need to be opened to a self-reflection experience.Here are the review toplines:1.	Waking is a game about self-reflection, having fun is a consequence of how you will react to the meditation experience.2.	The game interface feels outdated and impacts at the pace of the gameplay.		3.	Grinding can be a factor for some as lacks novelty in most of its elements from mid game to end.		4.	Waking feels more like a therapy experience than a gaming experience.		If by any chance you want to read the full review and see gameplay videos: Happy to chat about it, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: a fascinating set of ideas, which are unfortunately absolutely gutted by horrid character controls, a frustrating controller scheme/layout making an already janky telekinesis game mechanic far more difficult, art assets such as unity heightmaps and what look like Free Models, long stretches of time sitting still waiting for the four big words on the screen to go away,i feel like i really tried giving this game a chance - i played a demo (or beta? i don't remember) and was hoping it'd be improved before release, because its a really bold idea! unfortunately, that didn't seem to happen. I played for over an hour until I got to what I'm to understand is a *second* set of tutorials. these second tutorials were far more concise than the original, *a definite plus*, but force you to slam your head against the control scheme by giving you strict time limits on carrying out the obnoxious controls - you can't back out either, you seem to be stuck in the tutorial until you beat it. when it told me to kill three enemies in a minute thirty, and i kept missing by a couple seconds because i messed up one control input earlier or was forced to go run for more Mind Barrels to throw at it, i finally gave up.i really want to be nice towards what clearly seems a very personal project (despite one that is nowhere near as universal as it thinks it is), but i think i ultimately feel irritated, manipulated, and sad that the game encouraged me to resurrect my dead irl cat, only to use that as a skin for yet another frustrating mechanic that is deeply unreliable and unpleasant to use.tl;dr: this game perfectly aligns with my idea of what a real hell/purgatory must be like: it feels sluggish and thoroughly unpleasant through/with which to move/interact, and all your hopes and fears and dead loved ones are used as gimmicks to mess with you

_childDocuments_.review: Waking is a game about duality.Duality of death? The other is a poor man's Control like combat game that feels really bad due to awful and convoluted controls and unclear gameplay.The philosophical experience starts out pretty strong and was really interesting until the point I had to choose a pet. That totally kicked me out of the experience, as I've never had a pet of any kind.Unfortunately the combat aspect of the game took over shortly after and asked me to do things within a time limit, and that's when I gave up. I could barely kill one enemy within the given time frame and the game asked me to kill three. Not sure what the enemy is or who the bosses are in the context of the game's story. It just felt like a forced addition, because "this is a video game and a video game needs enemies". Otherwise they should have just made an RPG with a lot more testing and freedom.

_childDocuments_.review: WakingWaking is a fantastic game, based around a subject that not many dare to touch; a subject of great importance, yet not easily explained - 'Mind'.An atmospheric adventure that took me to a very uncomfortable and surreal place, in which I wouldn’t dare to expect what might come before me. Blurred between fantasy and reality, this was a third person experience into my own thoughts and dreams. I felt like I woke up in a dark blurry world, unknown and quiet; a bit too quiet. As I started moving forward into the unknown, not knowing what to expect, my only companions were my thoughts and the fantastic atmospheric music that the game has to offer. After a brief journey, I came across a sacred temple; I moved with steady feet towards the Oracle of Desire, a temple of great importance. The Oracle of Desire showed me my deepest desires and dreams; the desires that have always clouded my decisions and judgements. The Oracle of Desire let me choose two things that I have always desired the most, besides love, - ‘Money and Knowledge’. In the darkness of a coma, unaware of my surroundings, I see a mysterious figure next to my body.  The mysterious figure releases me from my deepest desires; from now I am free of the struggles of obtaining my desires. Moving forward in my journey, again I find myself standing in front of a temple. I am given a chance to let go of my struggles, two struggles that have always plagued my living soul, - ‘Anger and Poverty’. Again I see a mysterious figure next to my body, releasing me from of these struggles. I wish I could tell you how it feels. I wish I could let you feel my experience. I wish, yet I cannot; it is something that you must endure yourself. I wish you luck in your own journey. Waking, what a fantastic gameplay experience. Smooth gameplay complemented with smooth movement mechanics, stunning visuals, and incredible music. The game promises a lot in the beginning, promises I was really looking forward to. Other than the instant Bloom effect, it was smooth sailing smooth in regards to the gameplay. Puzzles were a minor component and fit right into the game without hindering the gameplay; I won’t say they were perfect, but adequate. After experiencing the smooth gameplay and amazing atmosphere, the game soon became very repetitive with its poor world design and level-building. It felt like a very near miss; it could have been an amazing world, with a combination of smooth gameplay, amazing music, and good level design. At first the animations seemed just right and fit the game perfectly, but soon I found myself let down on that aspect, with poor animation transitions during jumping and combat. Speaking of combat, this element was just right, in my opinion. I won’t say perfect, but for the games’ theme and art style, I feel like was just right. Waking hasn’t done a great job in its combat mechanics – a poor amount of damage per attack, Melee attacks being very limited because of animation limitations. The combat system felt repetitive and downright torturous at times. Although Waking is flawed and nowhere near perfect, I can respect and appreciate what the developers have created. I strongly believe that it’s possible to make an incredible game out of Waking with more work being put into the game. And for what it is and the value it brings to the table, yes I have very much enjoyed my time in Waking. I can recommend this game. Positives: + Decent Story + Atmospheric  + Great Music and sound effects+ Solid Base gameplay+ Unique concept + Unique art style + Emotional/Personalized experience + Smooth gameplay experience Negatives: - Intense Bloom Effect and no way to lower it- Animation issues - Low damage output while attacking- Melee combat limited due to limited animations - Poor level and world design - Combat felt bland Overall, considering all aspects of the game, I must say that Waking provides an impressive player experience. If you can look past the minor issues, a good gameplay awaits you.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: Waking is an adventure game where the developer tries to be edgy, deep and psychological, and this is why art school dropouts should never be involved in the game industry.  The idea is that you answer personal questions then the game throws that back up at you try make you feel guilty because you're in purgatory and can't leave.  Whatever.  This is a bad premise implemented with fantastic graphics and weak gameplay. I know most of the time I'll find that a game isn't up to a high quality standard because the visuals are poor.  Here, the visuals get a pass.  It's the rest of the game that's a letdown.Trying to address social issues through the medium of video games is misguided and can be harmful.  While it's plausible to suggest the intention was noble, this can do more harm than good.  Game developers are not professionals in areas of mental health and social problems, and when they use video games to pretend they are, this can cause far more harm than good.  It's my opinion that it's improper to use video games to push political or social agendas.  Apart from the harm such hamfisted attempts at addressing social problems can cause, this offers zero benefit to PC gamers.  People suffering from health issues or other social problems should seek out professional help rather than going to crap shovelware video games attempting to get sales by exploiting such problems for their own benefit, as is the case here.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 19 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 100,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Waking has the pathetically optimistic price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Stray", "Age of Empires IV" or "Factorio".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this. The developer has colluded with Tencent backed interests to withhold some of their games from Steam in a brazen act of anticompetitive behaviour.  It's vital that our gaming industry remains an open and competitive marketplace, and direct actions by this developer were intended to destroy that. This is harmful to gamers and to the gaming industry, and is completely unethical behaviour intended to cause this harm for short term profit.  While games absolutely should be considered on their own merits, as I have in my review above, gamers must be cautious when buying games from unethical developers like this.  There's no telling when they will accept more bribes and pull their games off Steam again... they've done it once, they can't be trusted.  Gamers have a right to know about this.  If you buy this game you may be putting your money at risk.

_childDocuments_.review: If you already liked Continue?9876543210 or Skrillex Quest, then better odds of liking this. If you like existentialism but find walking simulators insufficiently stimulating, Waking may be a good fit for you. Waking is a strange game. It's what I guess you'd call a modern 3D platformer like Dark Souls or God of War. And in most games like this, you are the main character, i.e. you are Adam Jensen, Kratos of Sparta, or Sonic the Hedgehog, or the descendant of Erdrick/Loto, or whomever, but in Waking the main character is...you, of [your hometown], descendant of [your parents], etc. Also there’s guided meditation, and no, there is nothing on the screen when she tells you to close your eyes, so just do it. Waking isn’t unplayable if you’re a teenager, but it’s clearly aimed at adults, if for no other reason than the fact that you’re asked to reflect on who you are and where you come from. Or maybe it’s different if you input a different age, I haven’t checked. All of this makes Waking odd, and perhaps, in the Venn diagram of the overlapping space between the two groups that Waking is trying to appeal to (people who like Souls-like games, and people who like to meditate upon death in a serious way) it is a little narrow, but I still like the result. The reflective meditation and inputting of personal details makes the game play a bit intimate, and not ideal for playing in a group, but alone I find it really engrossing. All that to say I really recommend Waking. It’s a really different (personal) experience, Jason Oda’s perspective on death and meaning is really interesting, it’s actually quite beautiful, and at $15 not even on sale it’s cheaper than a lot of books I’ve bought but not yet read.(Seems to play fine using a PS3 controller on Linux)

_childDocuments_.review: So here is the thing, Waking is an incredibly artful game with mystifying visuals and a very personal approach to storytelling, and calling it thought provoking would be an understatement. That being said the game is nearly unplayable in its current state for content creators and streamers. The game has no options for setting frame-rate limits or V-sync which means that your pc will spend its processing power that could be spent processing the stream attempting to run Waking at hundreds and sometimes thousands of fps, leaving dropped frames on streams left and right. I attempted lowering the resolution thinking making it lower would make it easier to process the stream, but instead it make all text and UI implements illegible and quadrupled the FPS, lagging my stream even more. TLDR; if you are planning on recording or streaming this game, don't or wait for updates to do so. If not then enjoy the one-of-a-kind experience that waking is in all its 2700fps glory.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna headline this with - there's SOME subtitles in the game, but there's also NONE. Wrap your head around that, there's a long section of a literal black screen, and my guess is they talk about your pets. Because when I got control of the game, it asked me to choose my favorite pet ( and ferret wasn't an option, but I guess cat is fine ) The game deals with some pretty heady stuff, it reminds me of those really old clunky PC games that used intangible things for stats, bc in this game - it uses your memories, your struggles, dreams, hopes, knowledge - and literally turns them into equipment, junk to control telekinetically, and etc.The idea is admirable, and if you have a soft spot for deep emotional stuff, this is going to pull at your heart strings a bit.Mostly you are picking up clutter with your mind, to act as a shield - or launch as a projectile. You also manifest melee weps by grabbing and charging objects from enemies ( sometimes you find them hanging about )Your entire Psyche is a laundry list of stats, skills, and gear. It's worked in a neat way.The game will make you answer some pretty person stuff, so be prepared for that.then again, if you don't take any of it seriously - the point will be lost on you.pros : Very artistically interesting game, with some very deep themes going on, you might cry a couple of times. the combat system is neat, if a bit clunky; but it works.cons : the game isn't optimized very well, and there's literally no graphical options aside of resolution, and the font and UI do NOT scale properly when you downsize your resolution, so if you can't meet your monitor's specs to run smoothly, you will be dealing with blurry text. And no Subtitles. There's SOME. But not all. Clearly not a massive team on this game, so I'm not gonna be too harsh on it. I happened to enjoy those oddball retro PC games with the arbitrary stats, and this reminds me of that - albeit with a much more polished presentation, instead of crude MS Paint visuals.I'll recommend this for Streamers/Youtubers looking for something to engage a bit more personally on with your fans.There is copywritten music in the game, there's also an option to not use it. Devs, PLEASE ADD SUBTITLES.

_childDocuments_.review: Waking has a very unique feeling and atmosphere to it, supported by both the graphics, the audio, and the way that various concepts of the mind shape both the game world and the interactions in it. It's obvious that a lot of thought and effort has gone into this game, and it's definitely the kind of indie experience I think is worth exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Waking

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game with an introspective experience.When it was in beta I played it with gamepad and I enjoyed it.The pity is that now that full game is realeased, I wanted to try it with mouse and keyboard (my pref. gaming set) but controls resulted a bit clumsy.Seems this game was thought for gamepad firstly, then "translated" to mouse and keyboard.And seeing this game is also punishing on mistakes (you loose points and enemies became stronger), it's not the case to have a clumsy character or camera.That's how I ruined my gaming experience.So don't make my same mistake: play it with gamepad.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITED* So as this was a tough game to get started due to my controller not working. I can say tho I have finally figured it out after looking some stuff up and the advice of the Dev. I was unaware that I had to actually enable controller support so that was a thing I learned. Its super simple and super easy once you figure it out and if any one else is having the same issues I Had please try these steps, for the keyboard and mouse that one I am still unsure of.Go to settings in steam and click on controller.Click on General Controller settings. Make sure you have PS/XB Configuration Support Checked.Back out and restart the game and the controller should work now. I never knew this was a thing as 99% of games I have used a controller for have worked. I am really happy tho that I got this figured out. I have started to play the game and I am super stoked to play more. I do want to thank any one who reached out to me Dev included to help me fix this issue. I am super excited to know this fix and if this helps any one in the future I am glad I could help.

name: Narita Boy
detailed_description: Accolades About the Game Story Flashback to the 80s. The Creator, a genius of his time, creates a video game console called Narita One with its flagship title being a game called Narita Boy. Narita Boy becomes a tremendous hit! Copies of cartridges are flying off physical shelves worldwide. Within weeks Narita Boy is the best-selling video game of all time, critically acclaimed for its power-fantasy wielding Techno-sword and taking players on a journey like no other. Meanwhile, inside the binary code, the digital realm connects with reality. Him has returned and deleted The Creator’s memories. Supervisor program, Motherboard, and her agents have activated the Narita Boy protocol. The Stallions are coming, and the Digital Kingdom needs a hero. The Game Become symphonic in Narita Boy! A radical action-adventure as a legendary pixel hero trapped as a mere echo within the Digital Kingdom. Discover the mysteries behind the Techno-sword, lock swords with the corrupt and tainted Stallions. Save the world! Pixel perfectionist – The shining example of a perfectionist at work. Experience the visuals of a retro-era brought to life with hand-drawn animations. Explore the mysteries of the Digital Kingdom – Venture up, down, left, and right to discover the darkest depths of the broken binary code in this never-ending story *. Max out the Trichroma – Equipped with the only weapon able to defeat the Stallion threat, take the Techno-sword and plunge it into the digital hearts of your enemies. Do not let this empire strike back , be the true blade runner . Diehard enemies – Face foes only imagined from your darkest fever-dreams! Show those bosses the bytes – Face-off against tons of totally radical and awesome bosses. Become the boss terminator , by overcoming the deadly Crab, DragonBot, Black Rainbow, and so much more! Sounds of the retro-grade-times - Feel fresh waves of synth wash over you while travelling the Digital Kingdom. With kickin’ beats that will send you back to the future. *there is an end to the story.

_childDocuments_.review: NARITA! BOOOOYYY!!Oh boi! This is my new favorite game of this year!  But let's get rid of the awe and be critical and get the cons out of the way first.-Floaty controls. No platformer should have such slow descent from jump. I fall in pits like no-ones business. The downwards dash compensates but it is an awkward solution.-Blunt combatYou slash and you smash. The dodge is dodgy at times and the combos and combat is mostly woosh crikey light effects that look more epileptic than impressive.-''puzzles''Going around and coming around is not a puzzle, it's just faffing around. Running in same places when once might have done.But... I don't really mind. I am taken aback by the sound, the visuals. I am so immersed into the world that I forgive the jank to see what is beyond next pixelated horizon. This is art in a game form. It is beautiful, innovative and captivating and other praising words!I bought it, sat down with it and plowed 3.5 hours and I am rather hyperwired from the solid awesome I have been through. It's self aware 80's cheese is fun and the synth music is just over delightful.If you want perfect game mechanics, this game is not for you.If you want to go on an epic colorful adventure that will grab you by the throat and forcefeed you some 80's cool ...CLAIM THE TECHNO SWORD!
_childDocuments_.name: Narita Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: AverageClear Time: 4+ Hours100% Time: 4+ Hours (Missable Achievements)Summary: A visually stunning but severely underwhelming 2D hack'n'slash, Narita Boy is all style and no substance. Luckily, it's perfection of visual and audio design makes the overly basic gameplay and confusing story just enough to be worthwhile.A 2D hack'n'slash. This is NOT a metroidvania. There are roughly 5 areas; finishing one closes it off forever. You'll spend your 70% of your time walking left and right, finding buttons to hit to unlock doors and read dialogue while 30% is combat.I mean, the game is just AMAZING to experience. Every single screen in every area oozes with personality. They all have names, giving them more context to their place in the world. The amount of colour and detail in each character and environment is just amazing and no two areas are the same. The combat is satisfying, it's fun to slice up enemies with a multitude of techniques while listening to the great synthwave/retro soundtrack that was pulled straight out a compilation and upgraded to be worth listening to outside the game.The story is simple but it's told in such an obtuse and frustrating way you simply don't care. Because this game takes place in a "computer" or computerized world, all the NPC's talk in such a roundabout manner; they have to relate everything to some kind of programming or computer part. An instruction as simple as "go here and push this button" turns into "the motherboard requests Narita Boy disassemble the underlaying graphical computations of the related Trichroma button in order to bypass protolcols to allow mainframe access". EVERY NPC is like this and it gets very annoying VERY quickly. I get what they were going for when writing the story but it doesn't translate well to a playable experience. Otherwise the game has alot of fluff that simply isn't needed like a multitude of techniques and gameplay mechanics that may as well be one and done.The entire story needs to be re-written to make it less frustrating to read. It's not that it's hard to understand, it's just unnecessary over exposition. You can also get rid of 3/4 of the abilities in this game and it wouldn't change a thing. The Shoulder Dash is used on one enemy, the jumping attack never used, the colour changing mechanics are cool but pointless and so on. Take some of the focus off the combat because it's not very good anyway and put that effort into building a more interesting world to  rather than a world that's only interesting because it looks cool.The game doesn't know if it wants to be overly complicated or overly simple. There are a whole range of enemy types in this game, but you fight most of them about 2-3 times. Bosses are introduced with one line of exposition then killed and never seen again. There are so many combat unlockables and abilities but no reason to use them when you can get through the entire game mashing attack and healing up after battle, or even die because there is no consequence. They tried to go the middle ground and please all the players but unfortunately for me it just made me realise just how little substance this game has.You'll get 90% of them just by beating the game, while the other 10% require you to find hidden rooms which become inaccessible after you leave the world. I suggest having an achievement guide open to check where the rooms are at least because you'll have to play through the game again to have another chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Narita Boy

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game, but despite its spectacular visuals and soundtrack, the game has some serious issues regarding game design, and no good aesthetic can save bad design.The most annoying thing about the game and the one forcing me to leave a bad review is the fact that the game totally suggests that the map is open and that you can backtrack whenever you want, but that's not the case. Any designer can tell when their game has a Metroidvania smell to it and, if building a Metroidvania is not the aim, the player should be informed that backtracking is not a thing, and this is important because one of the first things the game suggests you to do is to collect the obvious good ending. Well I haven't been able to since I found myself not being able to re-enter a stage from what is obviously a hub.Once that's out of my chest, the game also makes you sometimes go to places to apparently do nothing, feels like it's adding extra steps all along the way just to make the game 2 minutes longer, I don't understand. Also, for a game that doesn't allow global backtrack is sure does love to make you backtrack every hallway you enter for the sake of walking a little more.Look, I liked this game, and I really hate to feel like I have to leave a negative review, but I'm tired of games that think that a good aesthetic saves them from all judgement. The language of video games is their design, and a badly designed video game is a bad videogame. If this game was all aesthetic and zero gameplay everything would be fine, but if it's an action-platformer game then it has to be judged like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Narita Boy

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to the reviews and the user tags, this game is not a Metroidvania, it's pretty linear, it has a hub world, and each level has a hub structure, but you can not go back after finishing a level, and there's no interconnections between rooms, you just backtrack through the same door you came in from once you finished the room.Overall a fun game, cool visuals and soundtrack, combat is kinda basic, the story was nice as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Be aware this game while a 2D sidescroller does NOT have dpad movement support which is like a cardinal sin of 2D indie games. Other than that+Fun combat+amazing soundtrack+Intriguing story-floaty controls-the bosses I have fought so far (3 total)  were all really easy and boringWill update later with more info, but so far so awesome :)Update 2: Seems to be on the shorter side, bosses are still a let down having fought 3 at this point. The atmosphere and soundtrack keep getting better though!Update 3: Oh my god, I never thought a single section of a game could change my review from a positive to a negative, but wow. The horse riding mini game ruins this game. There is nothing fun or fair about it, if I wanted to play a learn by repeat BS deaths over and over I would play I wanna be the guy. Hope this gets patched because Im done playing until it is
