_childDocuments_.review: As others have mentioned, Rogue Lords is the lovechild of Darkest Dungeon and Slay the Spire. It has inherited the difficulty of these games, leading to what many others deem as unfair gameplay. The difference with this game, however, is "Devil Mode" - this allows you to, at any time, trade your HP for various advantages in combat. Did an enemy just place a status effect on one of your characters, giving them a DoT? Well, with Devil Mode, you can pause the combat, and move that DoT from your character to the enemy. Now you can melt that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Rogue Lords seems similar to Slay the Spire in the replayability department, too. With 9 characters at your disposal to create your team of 3, you have plenty of variety in both the way your team comps are built, as well as how you tackle both combat and overworld events. The art assets are truly incredible. Sometimes I'll take a new or different spell JUST to see the character animation. (Baron Samedi in particular has some jaw-dropping movement). Overall, Rogue Lords is a great addition to the tactical roguelike genre. I'm really looking forward to both the improvements the devs make to the already excellent product, as well as what they work on next.

_childDocuments_.review: Short & lazy version . . . do you like a few or more of these games? If so, there is a very strong chance you will enjoy Rogue Lords!Monster Slayers, Slay the Spire, Monster Train, Griftlands, Gordian Quest, Roguebook, Pirates Outlaws, Blood Card, Trials of Fire, Banners of Ruin.Longer version . . . this and Roguebook are my two roguelike deckbuilding treasures of the year even though Rogue Lords is not really, actually, a deckbuilder! It nevertheless is so similar to deckbuilding games in the mechanics and playstyle that it deserves honorary inclusion amongst them.A few things really stand out, I will limit myself to the top 5!1. LOTS of contentIn the release state, this already clearly has a huge volume of content to experience. Probably more than say, Roguebook in its current state, or Griftlands, and most and many others. 9 characters and 6 unique stories at the least, and each character having a huge number of unlockable relics and skills to play around with. I estimate at least 50 hours playtime to 'complete' everything just once2. Great characters, great character developmentThis is standout. Characters have unique relics, their own unique and expansive set of skills to pick and mix between during a run, and their own 'event' stats that can be boosted during a run too. Plus they are real *characters*, absolutely unique and charming, with personality that matches their skills in game. 3. Dripping with consistent themeLove it or hate it, but the visuals, spoken dialogue, game lore and story all complement each other wonderfully well. You are absolutely playing inside a slightly camp mock horror world. I do wish I could get the devil to shut the heck up with the idle chatter nagging though . . . :-P4. High challenge tactical combatNot quite Trials of Fire, but definitely comparable to Gordian Quest & Banners of Ruin. There is a lot to do, and a lot to think about, and within the first few chapters of a run you really begin to pick up interesting build options and find yourself thinking through what best to do each turn, there is very little time spend doing a single obvious thing, which plagues the beginning of many other excellent roguelikes.5. Highly varied play style optionsI have so far had great fun and success with health damage focused builds, spirit damaged focused, builds with healing, builds with heavy debuffing, builds with heavy buffing. I am far away from understanding "optimal" but really enjoying that you can make great progress (some of the time) with highly variable approaches.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Rogue Lords, and I decided to write this review as I have a slightly different take from the others I read.It took me ~40 hours to finish all chapters, and I always played with the same team (the starters: Dracula "the Support", the Headless Horseman "the Tank", Bloody Mary "the DPS"). I think I had a total of two game overs, one at the second or third chapter, and one at the second-to-last (but see below).I read several reviews mentioning that the game is hard and RNG can hit hard. I think they are not wrong, but I did not find it THAT hard: I think it's more a matter of COMPLEXITY. Damage already starts in the double digits, and it is not unusual towards the end of the game to hit for 30-50 (multiple times). With 3 characters on your side and 1-3 characters on the other side, you can also have several status effects in play at the same time (probably the maximum I've seen is ~20). You accumulate this with relic effects and maybe even battle effects, and suddenly it becomes really easy to make a fatal mistake. I remember in one boss battle I accidentally made the Headless Horseman use an attack that steals HP and SP, while he was under the effect of a Zombie debuff (healing received becomes damage), so instead of healing him I made him Vulnerable with 0 HP and 0 SP. Fun times.However, what I did not see mentioned is: unless your mistake actually kills you, you can quit the game, and when you reload your save, the BATTLE WILL RESTART FROM THE BEGINNING. I used this quite a lot, sometimes because I misread the enemy's effects, sometimes because I forgot the relics: another fun anecdote, I was fighting against an enemy that gets +1 to attacks every time it receives damage, and passing the turn I triggered a relic that dealt it ~50 SP damage in increments of 5, so suddenly he went from 8x3 damage to 18x3. I had to reload :-DAnother important thing to keep in mind is that The Devil can also "cheat" outside of battles, adding branches to the map (to skip dangerous debuffs) and re-rolling random side activities. I also used this a lot.- The ideas behind the game are great, and "cheating" as The Devil in particular is original and super-fun- I liked the story, and the overall atmosphere of the game- Voice acting is top notch- Game balancing is ok, could maybe be improved as many reviewers mentioned- Art. I might not align with the many who praised the art, so maybe it's a matter of taste, but while I find it serviceable, it's just good, not GREAT. Seems a bit too generic, lacking distinctive traits, especially the character models- The game is engaging and kinda addictive, but in the end it's a Slay the Spire clone, 70-80% of game mechanics are heavily inspired by StS (which is not bad, it's just not super-innovative)- Every run felt REALLY long, when compared to StS, so dying in the last stretch might feel a little bit frustrating. However, I also enjoyed the multiple occasions for Disciples to grow and power up- I had to use a piece of paper and a pen, sometimes the math in the game becomes hard. I am attacking with 30x3, but the opponent has +8 defense, so it becomes (30-8)x3, but also the damage that goes through is halved by a Wall; not to mention, my attack Steals damage (so it heals me), but I also have the debuff that hits me for 5-8 HP every time I attack, etc. ...- Sometimes randomness hits hard, especially because you do not know in advance what kind of debuffs the opponent is casting. In one case, I had ~20/50 essence left, the enemy had one attack prepared that would have made all my Disciples vulnerable for SP, and one global (unknown) debuff. The global debuff turned out to be Depression, that at the beginning of my turn hit all the Disciples for 5-8 SP, and I got a total of 20+ damage, which killed me. A possible solution would be to make the debuffs explicit- In the episode above, I even had a hard time understanding HOW I died. With so many effects happening at the same time, a couple of times something went wrong and I struggled to backtrack and debug what happened. So, when something hits The Devil, maybe things should be slowed down and made more clear; they are already slowed down a bit, but in most cases it remains hard to understand- If you are idle for too long, The Devil starts to nag you. In a game where you need to make additions and subtractions with double digits, and if you screw up you are dead, this becomes just aggravating after a while. So, I turned off voices during combat, and turned them on again during all other events.- The only game mechanic bug I found was a weird occasion where a Relic that was supposed to double the damage of the Headless Horseman sometimes would randomly x3 (starting from ~25 base damage, expecting ~50 damage, I got ~75 instead)- Once I opened a Gate that did not work, but closing the game and reloading fixed the issue

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR One of the best roguelikes in years but crippled with bugs. Still fun enough at maybe half off, but since half of the characters (and therefore content) are heavily impacted, don't pay full price.------I so badly want to recommend this game, but I can't.The game play is very compelling, the different characters have lots of deep synergies that tie them together, and I found myself saying "oh, wow, that's neat" a lot as I tried different combos and found new build strategies.There are some design problems holding Rogue Lords back, like runs being far too long (mostly number of nodes on the map each run and that even easy combats end up taking quite a while without a really juiced party) or the shaky wording (possible translation issue? I do not know if the developers are native English speakers) on lots of abilities, but what kills Rogue Lords is how buggy combat is.It's not uncommon for attacks to randomly not effect enemies (even defenses lower it to "0 damage", so that's not the  issue. This happens most frequently when the 2 damage types, HP and SP, are dealt together. Also an issue is damage conversion: two status effects in the game either swap HP damage to SP damage, or change incoming healing to damage. Each has maybe a 90% chance of actually occurring, which seems high until you actually try to play with it and runs randomly end since you suddenly took 50 damage that should have been swapped. This is most obvious when playing the final 3 characters together, since they can build into a really fun and engaging strategy that uses both abilities until you lose since the enemy keeps healing through the status that should prevent it.It's a shame. When the game fires on all cylinders it is legit the most compelling roguelike I've played in a very long time. I'm not even a fan of the art direction or look or anything, so I came in biased against the game from the start and only tried it since I received it in Humble Monthly. But it won me over with it's really tight gameplay only to be ruined by bugs as the difficulty increased. Unfortunately the current patch (1.1.04.10) came out almost a year ago with no word from the developers since so they are likely done supporting it.On sale at $10 USD (60% off at time of writing), it's an easy recommend since you can easily get that much fun out of it, bugs aside. If they fix the bugs it's easily $20 USD (20% off).

_childDocuments_.review: This game needs heavy tweaking.So far I have absolutely no idea how you're supposed to play.I managed to get 2 of my runs rather close to the final boss of the first (!) chapter. And there was no way of making it past those fights.The first one died because I got into a Fanatic that can't die under normal circumstances. You need to get both of his bars down 3 times to kill him. And I had an MP damage build. Just greatSecond run died because "Combo" skill damage scales up with damage buffs. Even though my HH was 90% of the time getting himself to vulnerable state with it, it never dealt damage to my HP. And somehow it got through at some point. And, btw that fight was ridiculous. That elite summoned like 5 waves of 120 hp minions that dealt 80% of my HP pool in one turn. Some of those attacks were AoE too.What feels straight up wrong:1) Not being able to customize your characters with the skills you need. It's REALLY hard to get skills that you actually need. Dracula is absolutely useless with those starting skills btw.2) The whole idea of choosing between "Souls", "Skills" and Randomness ("Terror") is god awful. Take 1) into account. So if you want to be consistent with your runs just always go with souls. You can just visit a Reaper and buy skills, upgrades and relics from him. There's legit no point in choosing either, the skills or terror just because they're weak.3) Some enemies are so annoying that it's not even fun to play against them. Privateers numbers are 100% off, they should be doing like 33% - 50% less damage. Same goes for low tier Mediums etc. "Church" passive is ridiculous. If the whole idea is killing waves ASAP, then why do you put so many obstacles for the player that they can't even properly clear without being drained of their resources. You legit add enemies that have immunities and unfun stuff like temporarily "locking" disciples skill. Because it's great to have your character not be able to do anything for 2 turns. Not to mention the "Vulnerable" state that most often requires you to waste another 2 AP just to remove that enemy.4) Player can't counteract most of the stuff he's facing. Your best bet against a heavy attack would be taunting with HH, debuffing for half damage and using flat reductions. Great, you did some of those things. But what if a taunt is present on the enemy team? Well, you probably lost the run. _childDocuments_.review: Considering the overall visual polish, a capacity to get through the game successfully, and the general pleasing length of the game I can't help but give Rogue Lords a positive review. And unfortunately that's just about all the positive I can add until closing remarks.Well, Rogue Lords sure had a lot of promise. In it's current state it is still quite well done. Sadly, there are clear signs that any support for the game was dropped for indeterminate reasons. I won't say the developers cut and ran without more proof, but there is literally space for additional lords in the menus which just never got filled. As with many roguelikes, the game's flow can quickly turn from a trickle to a surge for the uninitiated, but the overall balance swings regularly between gruelingly difficult to exploitative depending on how familiar you are with the mechanics and how willing you are to build your teams for optimal synergy. Rather than attempt to balance it further or add additional lords, a dumbed-down difficulty was simply added in one of the game's final patches. Who knows what happened here for certain. I honestly wish that I could recommend this game beyond getting it on sale, because it has some clever ideas and the artwork oozes style. Yet ultimately a title with support is more worthy of the pricetag. Rogue Lords just another EA title which had an early bloom and an early exit, I suppose. Caveat emptor.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the review score fool you: This game is definitely fun.   Where it succeeds is in providing a challenge.  If you're looking for a game easier than slay the spire then move on.  This game is not for you.  If you've played Slay the Spire...  I encourage you to remember, that you probably didn't get to the 3rd or even 2nd act on your first playthrough.  You aren't going to succeed off the bat.  If you remember that and just learn from your failures, you'll enjoy this game much more.  If your intention is to just complain until the game is played for you, then move on and don't buy this.In slay the spire, you have one hero.  Once their health reaches 0 it's game over and you start over from the bottom.  It's different from slay the spire in that each encounter your disciples start off with fresh health.  Your "devil essence" is your health bar.  Once that reaches 0, you lose.  The disciples health bars are there to absorb hits in each battle.  Once they are vulnerable to Health damage (HP) or Spirit damage (SP) (vulnerable=0) then any further damage subtracts directly from your devil essence.  Plan. Plan. Plan.  I can't stress this enough.  If you go into this thinking you'll even GET to the final boss of the first chapter on your first playthrough, you are fooling yourself.  This is a whole new game with entirely different mechanics. You need to start your first few fights off with focusing on Terror.    Getting terror events and your terror gauge to level 2 as soon as possible is going to help you out far more than souls or skills will.  The only exception is if you have a beneficial terror event that encourages you to gain more rewards from a regular fight.  (Terror events on those will usually provide double skill or double souls bonuses if you choose that as your fight reward before starting).Lastly: pros and cons of the first 4 disciples you'll use...Pros:  Good buffs.  Good damage when vulnerable with certain skills.  Able to refresh entire teams skills for only 2 energy. Can manipulate energy with skills.  Has 1 cost damage skill to start off with (which is better than you think!)Cons: Hard to use with starting skills.  Makes you think he needs to go full damage route.  Early game analysis:  Useful as you get to know the game.  Better used as a buff/debuffer than direct damage until other skill/relic/team compositions open up to you.Pros: Really tanky.   Like really tanky.  Able to redirect attacks to him.  Able to steal health back after absorbing attacks.  Has some of the strongest multi-target skills early on (aka Burst of Anger).  Able to debuff enemies pretty well too.Cons:  Skills are expensive and often clunky to use.  You'll need cost reduction stuff, or relics that give you more energy to do well with him.Early game analysis: Great tank until you unlock Lillith.  Tip: Try to get the skill that self-damages himself.  It gives him stacks of bitterness but increases his max hp (at the cost of current hp) and lets you manipulate your stacks of bitterness easier and thus use his lifesteal skill more often.Pros:  Really strong combo character.  Able to easily go physical or spiritual damage based on the relics/skills/traits you get.  Can often hybrid and go both.  Consider sacrificing stabbing at an altar early on, to give her more skill slots and open up hybrid damage on her for utility.  Will be your early game carry until other characters unlock.  Cons:  Slightly expensive skills, Relies on mirror to be good. (Hint: This means you should 100% pick up the "pocket mirror" relic if it's offered to you.)  If you don't manage/plan your mirror well she's bad because her mirror is also her recharge skill, which costs 2)Early game analysis:  Sacrifice stabbing at an altar.  Get Pocket Mirror relic if offered to you.   Try to scale her physical damage up with traits, or get "eeny, meeny, miney, moe".  She also has some SERIOUSLY devastating multi-hit/multi-target spiritual damage skills that once you get the hang of her, I think are better for her to scale with.Pros: Strong debuffs.  Masks are effectively "passive" effects once used, so she can contribute damage over multiple turns, while still manipulating enemies with control skills.  Strong spirit damage skills.Cons: lacks any real physical damage.  Hard to build with any other way other than pure spirit damage.  Not a ton of life-regain options.Early game analysis:  I replaced Dracula with White Lady but ultimately I don't think one is better than the other.  White lady does give you early spirit damage which the initial team comp is lacking, so take it for what it's worth: either option will do ok, but I slightly preferred white lady over dracula.Overall: The game is great and challenging.  My only suggestions/feedback for the developer are this:* Grammar/spelling errors on skills/boxes need to be resolved.* Eventually game needs a mode that allows procedural generation or some sort of "infinite" mode.* Once you hit level 4 terror, there's no additional skill bonuses?  Seems odd.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw negative reviews for the first time, I thought ok, a bunch of casual players crying about balance, it happens with most of the games.I bought it, I played the game and from what I can tell, the game indeed has balancing problems. I won't tell that enemies one-shots you, etc. I was managing all this crap pretty ok, but I am still unable to bit the first chapter. What a noob you could say, but I will argue with that. The main problem for me is the fact that you are not able to have good full phys damage comp. I have had two nearly perfect runs with the starting team. It was not my first run, so I have had some more powerful skills and relics unlocked. I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by one particular encounter. An elite boss which should be killed in a weird way. You should deplete both SP and HP three times. Moreover, his minions are invincible for most of the fight. All my three characters were dealing damage to HP, only one skill out of around 15 was targeting SP. Thus, the fight cannot be won. No way, at all.Why is it a problem? Adjust the comp, etc. After the first time, I died from this boss I have tried several runs with alternative comp, where one character was only damaging SP. And guess what? All other encounters became way more challenging. Two characters were not able to kill an enemy in one turn and SP draining character is either not able to do it on their own.So, to summarize, the game lacks balance, I guess it is the most correct word. It pushes you into playing in a certain way, while it makes the overall experience more punishing.I have not seen the final boss of the first chapter yet. And it's only 1 out of 8 if I am not mistaken. 3 out of 8 characters are locked behind finishing chapters.As a side note, indeed it seems like the stats of the enemies scale kinda faster than yours. I guess the first chapter boss could be close to unbeatable.Update.I am glad that developers are actually managing reviews. Also, I re-read my review and I have not told anything good about the game. My bad. The art style is gorgeous. Cut-scenes are nice. There is indeed a story behind all the runs. Thus, it is not bad. Just lacks polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for players that enjoy roguelike deckbuilders who want something fresh. Despite saying that, this game is not a deckbuilder, but has similar mechanics. It has 8 (I think) characters that you combine in groups of 3 all with different abilities that you find randomly during a run similar to adding cards to a deck. If you're familiar with Slay the Spire you'll be at home with many of the ideas present in the game. I personally find the art to be pretty slick with some decent, if repetitive, voice acting sprinkled on top. I haven't finished the game so I can't comment on its replayability, but it has a good amount of content so far for the price even if it ends up being 100% linear. Also, you can "cheat" because you're the Devil. Thematic and interesting mechanics right thereMy main gripes are with the map and some of the tooltips. Instead of clicking on a paper map StS-style, you run your character around "exploring" in a fashion similar to the map exploration in Tainted Grail. It's better than Tainted Grail because it doesn't have the godawful blurring effects, but it's just as pointless and tedious. Just clicking on the room you want to go to is more than good enough.My gripe with the tooltips is that some of the status effects don't seem to read the exact same way they function. This could be due to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reading comprehension on my part coupled with preconceived notions of what it will do. Easily fixed in a patch if it's wrong or suffered by me until I learn to read better if it's right. _childDocuments_.review: There are many good things in this game, and if there were a middle ground on reviews, I would have taken it. However, in its current state, there are many frustrations I've had playing through. End-of-turn effects causing spikes or changes in damage is one issue, meaning the intention system isn't always accurate. Some enemies force you into specific damage or pattern, and if your current team isn't outfitted for it, you just lose. The fanatic elite fight exemplifies this problem of pigeon-holing team-comps. You MUST have physical damage AND spirit damage to pass him, even though having split damage types is a detriment throughout the game. However, you will lose in this one specific case if you are ill-equipped without a divided damage team. This fight also happens very late into a run, in which you have already finalized your comps damage and removed other damage options. This leaves you with the decision to make, do you leave physical damage on your team? Gimping the rest of your playthrough, just in case. This feels like a lose-lose situation that I have had end 3 out of 6 runs.Another issue is that SP damage seems to have much better control options, making using a purely physical comp near impossible as you will essentially face tanking all incoming damage. Again, there appears to be a pigeon-holing effect here. Balancing seems off in both the fights and the skills.Overall the gameplay feels fun, decision-making impacts outcomes, and the story is adequate enough to hold attention. If it weren't for the above issue, I would be making a much more positive review. However, I would wait for a sale or balance pass by the developers in its current state, which I hope comes soon.

_childDocuments_.review: +Great graphics  +Interresting story settingI'm really fond of the ambiance and concept of the game , that's what made me buy it on launch day , so love the idea but lets talk about the execution : - Almost no feeling of progression : you go up in level but you don't get stronger you unlock new skills but your disciples stay weak and you can't unlock some disciples without winning some book ( level of the game ) but you unlock skills for them, so you end up farming a level for a character you don't have ... kinda dumb. The skills you "unlock" , you just unlock the chance to maybe get them in a run you don't get to change your characters skills : they always start with the same skills and you change what you can in game ...so yeah feels really underwhelming.- Some encounter ( elites in particular ) are sooo unfair, you start the run and end up against opponents who negate 8 hit point in both SP and HP all the time while your party does 3-5 hit damages at the start or all the opponents decide to hit 22*3 damage every 2 turn when your tank start with 35 hp.... I call them "You lost the run encounter".-UI and pop up constantly annoy you and feel unpleasant to navigate- The devil mode is a very cool concept but you are so weak that it doesn't feel powerfull , it feels required , you have to cheat to not lose early to an overpowered encounter so it's less of a " yeah cheat and wipe the floor with punny humans " but more of a "Oh my god I have to cheat every fight to not die ! ". _childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of Rougelike Deckbuilders (yes this is a RD, just with the cards replaced with "skills") and this is probably the hardest one I've ever played. However, its not the fun kind of hard. Its the I-want-to-smash-my-head-into-a-wall kind of hard. After beating the first 2 "books" and unlocking 3 characters, I want to play the game more but I just cant stand it anymore. It has two "difficulty modes", being essentially what it describes as normal and easy. I played on normal for a while but didnt find it very fun so I switched to "easy" to see if its anymore fun. Its about 20% or so more fun, and only marginally easier. On easy the only thing you get is 50 more of the "cheat" resource (which half the time wont even help you in the really hard fights anyway) and your terror level grows faster, which probably on average leads to maybe 2 or max 3 more artifacts, which can be very hit or miss. For example, one artifact doubles the damage you do but you have -2 actions (action points, AP) a turn, and you normally start with 5 AP a turn. Most actions cost 2 AP to use, so you don't get much value unless you have other artifacts that grant more AP, of which there are few and almost all of them have a similar negative attached to use them. Heres just a few examples of the kind of BS you will see in this game:* Massive ramp-ups in health between chapters: each "run" has 6 chapters to complete, and the difficulty ramps up massively on each odd numbered chapter after 1. So chapters 1 and 2 arent too bad, with enemies having about 20-40 HP and SP each. You just need to reduce one gauge, either HP or SP, to 0 and then hit it once more and its dead. Your characters also start with around the same amount of HP and SP as well (but usually much closer to 20). But starting on chapter 3, guess how much HP/SP enemies start having? 80-100. Then by chapter 5 its usually around 150-200. So logically, the players should start getting around the same increases to HP/SP or at the very least, start getting massive increases to damage right? Wrong, not in this game. You'll be lucky if you find a +10 HP OR SP increase. And as for the damage, unless you get really lucky or really really known what you are doing, you are going to keep doing maybe 15-25 damage MAX per turn, and usually only to 1 enemy. * Moderate ramp-ups in damage on each odd chapter: This one isnt as egregious as the health but its still bad. By chapter 3, you'll frequently find enemies with multiple types of attacks that hit all of your 3 characters for 15-30 damage. Remember, you'll be lucky if you have 30-40 HP or SP in general so you better hope you have a good team comp, have healing skills (which are pretty rare) and have skills to mitigate damage, otherwise youre screwed.* The cheat system being more of a hindrance than a blessing: The cheat system, which allows you to edit certain things (mostly in battles) is an interesting idea on paper. As its implemented now though, its only really useful sometimes. The problem is that if you use it too much, you die easier. So its like the game devs are egging you on to use it but if you make just one mistake and dont account for frequently untelegraphed kills to your characters, your run will be over. Also, what you can change is surprisingly limited. If feels like you should be able to change much more than you actually can. For example, there is a status in the game that prevents up to 4 damage from each attack. Some statuses can be switched between characters, so if you dont like an enemy having that status, you might be able to take it from them and put it on your ally. However, there are multiple caveats to that. 1, if that status if one of the "special statuses" that cant be interacted with, then you're screwed and you just have to live with it, because nothing at all in the game can deal with that status. 2, there are 5 or so different categories of statuses and no one can have more than 1 status of each category on them at once. But the way the devs work around this with the cheat is to switch the statuses if you try to double up on one category. So if you try to take the "Aegis" status from the "Protection" category that is on one enemy and move it to your character have already has the "Mind fort" status from the same "Protection" category, it gives your ally the enemies "Aegis" status and gives the enemy your character's "Mind fort" status. So in many cases, what should be a debuff for the enemy can frequently just be making them stronger in a different way, instead of debuffing them. Why not just let you overwrite your own status with the enemies?Other generally unfair odds: Its really frustrating that if any of your 3 characters die, the run is over. Imagine if pokemon was like that? Its such an inane design decision that it just makes no sense. Well at least the enemies are held to the same standard right? Wrong, you have to kill each and every enemy in each fight to win. This is hard enough but where it really threw me over the edge was with minion bosses. In most other games, when a boss can summon minions to them continuously, the minions arent that strong or have enough numbers to annoy rather than overwhelm. Also in most other games, those same bosses clear the field when they die, so you can just focus on the boss and take the hits from the minions. Not this game. Here, have a 150 HP/SP boss with two 120 HP/SP minions that will just be called back to the field in 2 or so turns if you kill them. And if you kill the boss but the two minions just came onto the field with full HP/SP? Well I hope you're ready to continue to fight because killing the boss does nothing, you still have to kill all the minions. And lucky for you, the minions can still hit like a truck no matter when they come in.At the end of the day though, this game has a lot of potential and there is a huge nugget of great ideas that are just held back by design decisions that are just asking for players to hate the game or just suffer. If the devs fixed difficulty issues, general bugs and ironed out the cheat system more, this could be a really fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Lords was interesting to start, but quickly became repetitive and monotonous. The first time you play through a book, it is interesting to hear the story and learn about new abilities of both your followers and enemies alike. The devil's comments are the type of over-the-top evil which makes you laugh the first time you hear them, such as  . The minions abilities can feel powerful at times when you get the right setup, and the enemies continue to scale to challenge you. Lastly, the events which occur outside of combat in which your minions steal, make deals, and cause general chaos and terror are an interesting Choose Your Own Adventure mini-game to round out the feeling of being the devil.Now, this is a rogue-like game, so you are expected to die often, and that is where the problems come in. Those same voice lines you found amusing the first time are repeated over and over again until it ruins the humor. There are so few of them, that you will hear the same comments dozens of times throughout your playthrough. The story in each book remains the same regardless of how much terror you have raised, paths you have chosen, or disciples you bring with you.The disciples abilities are offered randomly but you still go for the same abilities for each disciples through each playthrough. If you don't get those abilities, you quickly feel punished for your bad luck as your damage does not scale adequately to the health or abilities of the enemies. I believe this is to force you to use your "devil powers" to affect the battlefield more, which quickly becomes a necessity to progress. The same goes for artifacts (items which provide boons to different parts of the game), where some artifacts feel overpowered, and others are a handicap. Overall, I do not recommend this game in its current state. The only reason I put in as much time as I did was to finish the game and see the end of the story.To the Developers, a few recommendations:* Disciples become more powerful throughout the book, but are inexplicably reset at the beginning of the next book. You may want to consider a "permanent reward" to disciples who complete a book the first time, perhaps a small artifact which augments the disciple or its abilities in some way for future books. This would incentivize players to play through a book again with multiple disciples.* Have new minion abilities tied to when the minion is unlocked. I was receiving Baron Samedi's abilities long before I had Baron unlocked, which made me wonder if I was missing something.* Add more voice lines to the narrator or reduce how often the narrator's voice lines play. Alternatively, have the minions occasionally make comments when entering a new zone instead of the Devil. Effectively, just more variety to keep things fresh. * Upon defeat, provide an option to go back to the beginning of the chapter or reset and return to the devil's layer. I know this goes against the idea of being a Rogue-like, but it may be a stop-gap until it feels better to restart from the beginning.* Walking from location to location largely feels unnecessary. Getting caught on small trees or realizing you can't fit through a small passage is tedious. If walking between and around locations is staying in the game, more mechanics to reward this behavior would be useful, such as stumbling across a hidden artifact or finding some lost souls.* To promote players trying out different group make-ups, consider adding a variable prior to starting a book which provides a benefit for doing X, Y, or Z. Examples of this could be "This area reminds the Headless Horsemen of where he lost his head. Headless Horseman receives +2 Damage in this book" or "This month has a blood moon. Hecate's first ability costs 1 less."* A rogue-like is supposed to make you feel like you lost, but that is okay because you are slightly more powerful for the next run. Abilities unlocking starts to provide that feeling, but is dulled by unlocking the abilities prior to the minion unlocking as well as the randomness of not getting that ability through the games RNG. Consider some options such as slightly increased Devil Power gauge, or keeping souls between runs, etc. This game has a good concept and decent mechanics, but needs some improvements. Hopefully some of the comments above are helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, engaging game.  The artstyle is gorgeous and spooky, and has a strong identity of its own.  The music's great, too, and adds a lot to the atmosphere, especially when coupled with the excellent voice work.  Everything comes together to be wonderfully immersive.Gameplay itself feels very natural and balanced-- each Disciple really does seem to bring something unique to the party that only they can provide.  It helps that just about all of them have unique mechanics to master.  And beside combat itself, I absolutely adore the events that require Disciples to use their social abilities.  Not only are there a lot of those, they can all be solved in a number of different ways, and even failure feels interesting.  But what I absolutely -- what really makes this game a favorite-- are the interactions between Disciples.  You really get the feeling that your little army of darkness is a bickering but ultimately united family of the damned-- call me sentimental, but there's something really sweet about the way they can compliment and praise each other after successes.  Their tendency to gripe at each other under the same circumstances, or failures, keeps things from getting  sentimental-- these  bad guys, after all.The key mechanic of "Devil Mode" manages to feel both very natural and very natural in the best way.  In combat, learning how to spend diabolical power is absolutely necessary-- you have to spend power to save power, in that if you don't carefully warp the odds in your favor, you'll lose everything.  Thanks to clever use of sound and graphic design, it really does feel like the Devil is twisting reality.Now for what I  like.  Traveling overland can be clunky at times, as paths aren't always clearly defined.  It doesn't seriously interfere with enjoyment, but it would be nice to spend a little less time with my ankles apparently caught up in the underbrush.A much bigger issue is that of repetitiveness, and I'm going to explain my feelings by way of comparison to another Roguelite, Darkest Dungeon.  DD often gets accused of being repetitive, but I never found that the case; each descent into a new Dungeon felt natural, yet another part of an ongoing campaign against the forces of darkness.  And the nice thing about that was that as long as you were playing on easier difficulties, you could take your time and dungeon dive indefinitely; endgame was there, waiting for you, when you felt like getting to it.As it stands, Rogue Lords has a risk of being genuinely repetitive, since you don't really have an option to just mess around fighting monsters in quite the same way; You can replay books, yes, but the narrative structure of the game hammers home the fact that you're repeating an old story.  Having to skip through old story beats can get a little tedious; Yes, the story is fun, but you can only experience it for the first time once; after that, I just want to fight monster hunters and watch my Disciples interact.  Then there's the matter that every time you successfully complete a story arc, the game gets harder.  This means you really need to be committed to playing through the story; in Darkest Dungeon, easier missions remain available alongside harder ones, which nicely compliments the aforementioned ability to just spend time messing around.  I feel like I'm being pushed toward the endgame.  I realize, though, that that actually might be a selling point for some people.  It's a matter of taste.I do hope eventually the game gets something like an Endless mode, where instead of progressing the story you can just fight and do social events.  If balance is a concern, perhaps the player won't earn xp in endless mode.  Just an idea.All in all, very much worth the price.  I hope this game sells well and we get some DLC, which I will definitely be purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever review and I'm making Rogue Lords my first because this game has so much potential. I've played around 50 hours of this game and I'm loving it, yes there's some issues but we will get to that soon. All I will say now is that you can tell this game has had a lot of love and thought put into it and it shows. It's a shame that people are making reviews with so much positivity, yet marking it as a negative because of minor things that can be easily fixed. If you just dislike the game (because that happens) then that's fine. So here it goes!A brief overview (NO SPOILERS):In Rogue Lords you play as the devil and your goal is to regain your power over the world with the help of his disciples. His disciples are well known people from myths and stories like Frankenstein and Bloody Mary.First off. The positives!Styling: The art style of this game is beautiful and I don't think anyone would disagree. A lot of inspiration from Tim Burton and Henry Selick brings the world of Rogue Lords to life and when looking at it, it's actually very minimal. The atmosphere, the contrast between light and dark and dull and bright, and how nicely animated it is. The backgrounds when you're fighting and doing side quests are beautiful and have slight animation to them so they aren't stiff which I love. It's a stunning game.Characters: There are 8 disciples: Dracula, the Headless Horsemen, Bloody Mary, the White Lady, Lilith, Hecate, Baron Samedi, and Frankenstein and his Creature and they all fit into 2 damage types. Either Health or Spiritual, some even do both. I've played with 6 of the 8 disciples and each of them are very unique and have a different play styles which keeps it fresh.Devil Mode:Devil Mode is the main mechanic that this game is built upon and I love this take. Some people dislike it but I personally love it and it's something I've not seen in a roguelike before. It acts as the Devil's health and throughout your run, you can spend it to buff and help yourself on the way (this game says "it ok to cheat"). Also when your disciples go to 0 health they don't die but become vulnerable and anymore hits to that character will take the health from the Devil. So whether you wan't to steal buffs from enemies, transfer debuffs from yourself to them or simply get your people off deaths door or take an enemy from max health to nothing. The possibilities are endless! But don't kill yourself.Challenging:Now this is a positive and a negative but I'll talk about the positives here. I love how this game doesn't hold anything back and when you manage to scrape past a fight or run, it makes me feel accomplished. You need to pay more attention to everything and each fight and run is completely different. The one thing I had to learn was going 100% offensive is risky and is sometimes needed but also don't be scared to play defensive for a turn if you are being bombarded by damage. It is brutally hard but once you get the hang of how the enemies work and how your team can synergise, it get's a lot easier.Ok now the negatives. I don't have that many and I wouldn't even call them negatives more like areas of improvement.Challenging:IT'S BACK! As I said before, this game doesn't hold back and I don't think that's a bad thing because I don't want to play an easy game, I want a challenge. However, I agree with the people that say that balancing needs to happen. The damage output in certain fights can sometimes be really off putting especially when you are near the end of the run and there's no way you can stop it. Also the difficulty ramps up SUPER fast and it's not a steady difficulty growth. It goes from 1 to 100 very quickly and if you don't keep up then you lose. I know some people will say "well that's how it works" but I do think it can be balanced slightly so players don't feel so overwhelmed all of sudden.Variety:Now this doesn't bother me too much but I think it should be mentioned. I've completed 4 books now and you come across the same enemies and the map doesn't change visually. This might be a problem for some people but because each run is so different you learn new things each time. I just thought i'd bring this up because this could be an issue for some people. However, I do want to point out that the bosses for each stage are completely different and each of them have their own special mechanic which is great. Overall I enjoy this game. When i first saw it pop up on my suggested several months ago I knew this would be one of my favourite games and it hasn't disappointed. A few minor tweaks and this game will be spot on. I look forward to see what else comes to this game in the future. Peace.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the initial Steam Fest Demo on stream awhile back, it was one of the few that stood out the most to me and was one I was excited for the release of. Having said that... the actual release didn't disappoint, as even more of the game is unlocked for me to enjoy and I can continue my evil adventure of revenge. That said, there are a few negatives to this rather quick release as well, which I'll note below, along with some things I feel should just be fixed up or added as time goes on. But first, the good parts.The [Devilishly Delightful] parts: This game is a subtle Deck Builder game that focuses on you building up three of your characters, starting with the Headless Horseless Man, Dracula, and miss Mary herself. Each character has their own playstyle that has even more things unlocked as time goes on, with all three having their own quirky style to them. The overall "theme" of this assortment of monsters mashing together to take revenge on Hellsing is handled well, though I'll admit I wish the actual combat system had more flavor to the characters interacting with each other. It would probably be hard to properly balance, but some characters already mesh together very well and it'd be nice to see some sort of actual combo system working with that; Dracula not being reflected in Mary's mirror and being able to attack people through it, or something.The Events in this game are also a subtle but effective way of building your character's stats up, allowing for a real sense of progression as the story goes on in each "Book" you're dealing with. By the end you end up having at least one character or all of them with triple their starting stats and it feels like your monsters are truly growing by spreading chaos through the world. Sometimes monsters can even be upgraded multiple times from one event, resulting in a huge burst of strength, so it's almost always worth it to take them on.The Combat System in the game is also smooth and relies on each character's own talents that you build through the Reaper, by using souls you harvest from events and battle to pay him off. That said, it's often hard to get those souls, so the way you can spend a small amount of souls to upgrade one skill and then pick it up later is rather nice to have, as some skills become easily a given to have once they're upgraded once or twice. The combination of skills all together lets you either play defensively, or just say "Whatever!" and throw caution to the wind to let yourself be a true monster. That said, the Vulnerability system is probably my favorite aspect of this, on the defensive and offensive side, as you can twist fate to your will just by reading the intentions of your opponents and what your skills can do. A monster with 1 health is not going to die from an attack that only does 30 damage once, but an attack that does 2 damage twice would kill them and you can plan around that.  Which also brings me to...Cheating. Plain and simple, it's the most unique mechanic this game has, though it uses it in a positive and negative way. Notably, the ability to just outright drain an enemy dry, refill your monster's health, or just swap some of the status effects in the game is really fun to do, though sometimes I wish it was a bit cheaper. The Events being part of that by twisting the % chance of victory in your favor is also handled well, though sometimes I'm surprised when there's no real risk at all. But that part mostly relies on your monster's stats; always look in the top right when starting an event to see what "skills" it may require.But now the [Bads] of this game... which are minor, overall, and I think most can be easily fixed.The Biggest issue right now is... The Bugs - Notably, there seems to be some issue with the audio file that involves text boxes; the little scribbling noise that pops up when you're reading things in the world. For some reason, there's just times where the noise... won't stop. At all. It'll just keep playing over and over, even if you get into another fight or event, and even if you turn off volume entirely in the options. Turning the volume off itself, via your audio settings, does work, but that also gets rid of everything else in the game. It doesn't seem to be tied to any specific event, though I did feel I got it more during the "Chapter" points where it hands you more story, but it's something you can easily fix by restarting the game entirely. Still, a minor annoyance that I hope to see fixed soon.The second bug is one that is mostly connected to the Combat system. I found it hard to actively select characters, both my own and my enemies when using a skill, to actually... y'know, do something. Sometimes it just wouldn't accept any clicks I made and this seems to mostly happen after some sort of transition. When it switches over to my turn, refilling my Action Points, sometimes the characters just don't want to be clicked on and actively fight me, /their master/, to be forced to do something. This is usually fixable by just clicking on something else or someone else, but it's still rather tedious.The third issue with the game would be the real understanding of how some effects work and a good representation of how much damage /you/ would do. How much damage your enemy does is usually represented well with hearts or spirit points above your monster's heads, but I found myself easily forgetting the enemy had a shield on because it just doesn't really indicate how much damage you're going to do before you do it. There were also a lot of times where some effects aren't properly explained, or at least I don't get it, and I have no idea what's doing damage to me. Notably, HP/SP being Polarized. I still have no idea what that does, but it's one of the key mechanics of a set of twins that you have to fight rather often. Brutality works best for them so I don't think much of it, but it's one of those small things that just goes over my head, I think partly due to just the amount of rather large words I don't hear often being used for some of the descriptions. Which is fine for the flavor of the game, but it makes it hard to really get what it's doing. The only other major complaint I have is how I had to finish the first two Books... which was being as ruthlessly cruel as I could be. Which is what the Devil should be, if he's truly evil, of course, but I found myself a little sad that a more patient and defensive method playing the game to be completely ruined against some enemies. One enemy in particular was the breaking point for me as they would constantly summon 90/100 health enemies; something that's usually a whole challenge on its own. After the second wave of carefully taking them down and with me at only 6 Devil points, I said "Fine, whatever!" And had Dracula karate chop them over and over into submission. One of his key features was his ability to just stack on damage when he's Vulnerable and after three turns... it worked. Dracula never fell, thanks to the Horseman taking most of the hits, and just kept pumping out damage. That's how the end of the book went too; just Dracula karate chopping, biting, and then repeating that four times before I'd have to gently nudge his health higher to get him to survive. Which is still fun, don't get me wrong, but the difficulty spike felt a bit ... sudden. More sudden than the tutorial one, if that's any measure.Regardless of all that, though, I think the game's flavor and overall style is pleasant. With a few bug fixes and maybe a bit more content to it, I think this would go down as one of the better Rogue-likes out there and it'll be devilishly delightful to see where it ends up and hopefully the developers don't just drop it now that it's officially released, but... I'm sure the Dashing Rogue developers won't Lord it over us.

However, after seeing some of the negative reviews for this game I had to put in my 2 cents worth.Many people say this game is just too hard.   Seeing as how I have already beaten the game on the hardest level with 2 different builds, I can't understand that argument.  Is it a hard game?  Of course, but in no way is is TOO hard. _childDocuments_.review: Rogue Lords is the perfect Halloween roguelike and a damned fine roguelike regardless of the season!The combat is very mentally stimulating and has a ton of depth. If Divinity 2 was a turn based JRPG-esque roguelike it would probably feel a lot like this. Most fights feel like puzzles. It's challenging, but mostly fair. The game has a novel 'cheating' mechanic that adds another layer to how the player approaches combat and story events. Despite sounding like something that could be abused, the cheating mechanic seems to be quite balanced.The game starts you off with 3 characters. Dracula, Bloody Mary, and the Headless Horseman. These 3 characters are a blast to play with! They have very interesting and unique skills that synergize really well and allow for a ton of creative options in combat. Outside of combat the game has random story events that gives the game an almost board game like feel. They're an effective and entertaining way to flesh out the world while giving players a mental break from the combat.The art direction is solid. The animations are smooth and expressive. The hand drawn character portraits and backgrounds are really nice too. The only area that could stand to be improved is in the overworked traveling sections. So far the maps just seem a little barren. Ultimately, this is a small point since the game isn't really about exploration. It's about the combat and that part is done incredibly well.The voice acting is also really good. The music so far hasn't stood out as being anything to write home about, but it's inoffensive and seems to fit the mood well. You won't be humming the songs from the game, but you also won't be muting the game so that could listen to a 'Gary The Bard' album.The game's one 'flaw' is that it doesn't save progress mid battle. This could be easily exploited and essentially allow for unlimited repeats of a battle. This might be a good feature for some, as it could cut down on the frustration of having to repeat runs over and over, but it just seems a bit at odds with the sort of permadeath focus of roguelikes. A minor complaint at worst.All in all, Rogue Lords is brilliant. The devs really did a great job here. It's clear they put a lot of thought into the game. I hope this game sells well so that we can get more games from the devs! If you liked Darkest Dungeon, Divinity 2, and/or you enjoy turn based rougelikes this game is well worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Lords is an enjoyable entry to the turn-based rouge-lite with a delightfully devilish cast of fiends and dark arts practitioners. Stylistically, Rogue Lords nails the macabre atmosphere and the battle animations are wonderfully done and full of character. It is easily the strongest aspect of the game.Instead of a deck of cards, Rogue Lords opts to use a standard skill system that needs to be recharged after use, which is fairly unique. It is still reminiscent of managing a deck on and off the battlefield, as you do have to decide which skills to use in a timely manner and which to permanently remove in the long run.A cool game mechanic to highlight is the devil mode, where you get to tip the scales in your favor when needed. Swap statuses here, remove a bit of health there… It’s incredibly useful in a game where you have effectively 3x2 health-bars to manage and you can avoid losing outright by just bumping a disciple’s health up so they can eat the excess damage that otherwise, you would have taken.Okay gripe time: the random damage range to any attack skill is ultimately useless and adds pointless RNG (I always take the lowest possible amount anyway). The overworld map, while cool looking, is also pointless in the grand scheme of things where a simple 2D map à la Slay the Spire would have sufficed (the kicker is there already is a 2D map present). There’s significant time wasted by watching your disciples walk around. Also, the time spent developing the 3D map assets could have been spent doing more QA. Thankfully, during my time with Rogue Lords there were no wiped saves or anything similarly game-breaking. Yet, I swear there are times where the damage calculation is a bit off, an enemy didn’t die as they should’ve, a status that should have been removed did not. A few precise patches wouldn’t hurt but as always, your mileage may vary.To conclude, I would like to address the people complaining about battle duration, difficulty, and RNG as a whole. It’s as if Rouge Lords is the only off-shoot Slay the Spire game they ever played. The move and relic pool in Rogue Lords is about the right size where it’s varied, and small enough to allow the player to almost always pick up the more busted options.  If that doesn’t quite cut it, devil mode can help out in a pinch. Even when starting out with nothing unlocked, winning was still manageable. Really, Rouge Lords is like any other turn-based rouge-lite (the RNG and difficulty comes as a package), maybe on the long side if you’re impatient. This makes it an easy recommend, to anyone who enjoys these types of games of course.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent but not good enough for a "recommend." The characters are interesting, with some degree of customization available during a run. The combat mechanics are not especially exciting, and you will be spending a lot of time with them in very similar fights. The storyilnes are meh episodic Macguffin chases with random vignettes. The tone and personality work more than the plot.Everyone seems to comment on the difficulty. This is harder than average, and the difficulty only goes up with no way to turn it back down (as of this writing; that may change, given complaints). You can put together a strong team composition with your own abusive combos, in a race against "well that's some BS" enemy abilities that start to develop. The ability to "cheat" as the Devil limits how bad things can get. The ability to restart fights (quit and reload) limits it further if you don't mind adulterating your rogue-lite experience; some people have ruled the game "easy" because you can save-scum your results on everything, at which point you might as well edit your save file. Which is also not hard, so if you like the game but don't like the balancing, there you go, increase your power level as if you were loading a mod. But if you're thinking of doing that, you probably don't really like the game.The social abilities in the game are somewhere between underused and really strong, which is also to say that they vary. The "book" encounters are a good variation on the comment "event" nodes in rogue-lites. There are separate abilities for those. Going through a book node yields a small upgrade; your choices and dice rolls within the nodes can get you more rewards and bonuses. Some of those bonuses are great; +damage on someone with multi-hits is big. Some of those bonuses are meh; +2 to a social ability you may never use again is of questionable value. And then all the social stats are irrelevant in the end, because of course everything always comes down to combat. But those little upgrades add up to making your characters tankier, as they are the main source of health upgrades.Interesting but not great. You can check the global achievements for what % of people drop off over the seven chapters. I am currently debating whether to finish the game. The last chapter is the only one where it seems like the storyline really connects with the other bookend of the story, instead of chasing the six infinity stones. The gameplay should be more of the same, so am I just bloody-minded enough to finish it out having come this far?And that's probably why I can't really recommend it. I am not eager to see it through, just wondering whether it is "worth it" when I am so close to the end. That is not a good reaction to have to a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its crazy this game is not getting more attention for how good it is. Rogue lords is a hard but extremely fun rogue lite card game like Slay the spire and your other favourites but has great team building with many different skills to choose from for each character and unique mechanics with the devil mode that allows your to remove status effects and give them to or from your enemies, outright kill an opponent and many other cool things. The art style is great, animations are really well done and music sets the mood.You also have to recharge your skills after using them which in theory doesn't sound all that fun but is actually a good mechanic as some characters have special effects when they recharge. Dracula can reload everyone's skills while bloody Mary can place a mirror behind an enemy that will do the same attack again to the opponent. So far I've beaten the first 2 chapters and its been really fun and i cannot recommend it enough. I do have to mention the difficulty though. A lot of negative reviews are saying the game is too hard. After 2 chapters i disagree at this point in time. Is it difficult? Yeah it can be. Things can go from 0 to 100 real quick if you miss a status effect that landed on you or you don't have a way to negate damage. Are there some hard elites/bosses that will give you trouble if not prepared? Yep. The game revolves around having a balanced team and learning what each character is capable of and having a bit of luck to get the skills/relics you want.  I really hope the devs do not make the game easier as in its current state it is great and challenging. Will update review after getting further regarding difficulty if my thoughts change. Just to mention as well the art style is great, animations are really well done and music sets the mood, but the combat is where the game really really shines.TLDR: If you want a challenging team building rogue lite with unique mechanics look no further, expands on what made SoS the great and will exceed your expectations, just don't expect a walk in the park.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Game is great but too difficult early on. 3 hours in and I have yet to reach the first boss in chapter 1 on 2 runs. In the current state it feels like an emotional rollercoaster of feeling insanely strong with skills, artifact synergies, and stat increases, but terrible when you get 1 shotted by normal enemies that are all suddenly dealing 3x24, 2x18, and debuffing one character. I'm also a little lost on how stats work during events. For instance, I have a character with 12 scare attempting a scare event and all the choices are 10-20%, not sure what these stats are affecting if not these chances?Recommendations for Devs:- I think lowering the difficulty especially earlier on is essential (in comparison to other rouge-lites)- Maybe consider possible tweaking to death and refresh mechanics? It feels weird to lose if one character is being targeted and dies - maybe just remove the character until the end of the fight and lose if all 3 characters wipe. - For refresh it sort of feels like I'm wasting a turn most of the time. I'd recommend lowering these costs or adding an additional effect on refresh. Bloody Mary (get a x2 damage mirror) and Headless Horseman (1 cost) feel fine as is, but Dracula feels pretty unnecessary and over-costed at 2 cost (refreshes entire team) when say White Lady and Bloody Mary both refresh themselves and/or have additional effects.- Clarify non-combat stat increases (i.e. Why should I care why I'm increasing these stats if they don't feel like they do anything?)These are my all opinions based on my rogue-lite experience and 3 hours of playtime, so please take my experience with a grain a salt.Overall mechanics and art style feel great and I really enjoy playing, I'd just recommend holding off until there's a balance update.  Love the direction the game is going and looking forward to more updates!

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying that the core of the game has a lot of potential, it is very fun and challenging even just getting through the tutorial run. It is also obvious that the developers put a lot of heart into the game: the voice-overs are fantastic, the Disciple have unique skill sets that allow for various party builds while still being faithful to their characters' story/myth.However, like many other reviewers have stated, the game balance is not yet there, and there are some glaring problems with this game that prevent it from being an Easy Recommend right now. Some of these problems are obvious just from playing the tutorial run and the first run (Obtain 1st Relic).Please note this review may have mild spoilers.1.  The initial fights are fun and allow the player to explore their powers and interactions, especially as new mechanics are introduced such as the skill leveling system and the random effects of Good and Evil. This suddenly ends right when you are just getting through your first real run (Obtain 1st Relic). Enemies will suddenly have double the HP/SP from previous fights, and now come new abilities (passive and active) that can just end whatever fight strategy you were going for (example: a straight up HP Block that prevents any damage below a certain threshold). Some of these skills are also somewhat frustrating and do not make sense especially with the pacing of the story. I feel these early runs are too hard artificially just by power-creeping fights, making it such that even normal fights near the end of the chapter felt and had to be played like Elite fights.2.  A lot is left to be desired in the UI, and makes it more obvious as you play more and more, especially since there is no in-game compendium/Guide that allows players to read up on all the Icons / buffs / debuffs / action markers and their effects that exist within the game. There is also no way to tell how your own skills will affect the battlefield, example:- How much damage an enemy would take if the attack happened (example, there is no way currently to tell if your attack would damage an enemy through a shield / HP block)- What debuffs would they receive- what debuffs would be  (this is important since the game only allows one of each subtype of buff/debuff to be active.- Which enemies you can target (this is more obvious during Taunt moves or for Bloody Mary). The only way to check is to mouse over every enemy and see if there is a red/orange outline (meaning they can be attacked).- Which enemies are totally invulnerable to damage (This should be different from cannot be targeted due to Taunt. The enemies also do not change in appearance)- What the debuffs/buffs will do each turn (This is made confusing by the wording of the tooltips and the lack of any indicator in the UI of their effects, ex: no way to tell how much bleed/burning damage to expect on the healthbars of the enemies)3.  One such setting is to mute the game in the background. There is no way to mute the game if it is in the background / not in focus. Everything I do on my computer is now done with the voice of the Devil yelling at me for being slow or to hurry up and take my turn in the fight. (Fair enough haha).4.  Moving around on the Overworld feels clunky and unnecessary. Why be forced to run down a hallway and do nothing except click on the next event / optional event? No reason other than to see the beautiful world you want to corrupt. The random obstacles like trees and lakes, also do nothing except force you to take a weird route that might end up sending you to the wrong pathway (almost happened to me as the trees forced me to skirt near the entrance to enter another path). While the overworld is nice to look at, it just does nothing but waste time (you can't even look at the map and think of your next fight while moving around).5.  There is no obvious trigger for the debuffs (how the Good people are ready for you) other than the text on screen once you enter an area. Once it's happens, it's too late, and you just have to accept that your next fight has whatever random debuff has been assigned to you. While it is a nice mechanic to play around, my first real run (the very first run where you encounter all of these mechanics), the debuff was already happening almost every other round of on the map. Again, this feels tied to the enemy scaling where you just suddenly have to play around random mechanics.Even with all these problems and challenges, the game is fun. This game has a lot of potential and could be up there with games like Slay the Spire, but I feel in its current state, I cannot recommend it to others without being very clear on what to expect. Watch some runs by Kripparrian in the Community Broadcast and see for yourself if this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Lords is an amazing turn-based roguelike. The art style is great and the combat is complex. I played the demo for about 10 hours back in June because I wanted to try out all of the available skills and learn the enemies. There are a lot of complaints about the difficulty being too hard but I found the difficulty to be in a good place. If you read all of the enemy passives and learn how to effectively use your devil powers you can win every fight. I finished all 7 books of the story in about 22 hours with no losses using a different team comp every run. I knew the normal enemies because of the demo but I still had to learn 6 new characters and 6 new bosses and a lot of new skills for the characters I had already played.My only real issue with the game is that the difficulty permanently increases for each book you beat, making some of the achievements harder to get if you don't do them early. All of the steam achievements also unlock skills or artifacts in the game, so I spent the last 12-15 hours of game time trying to win on the hardest difficulty without losing any demonic essence to unlock an artifact.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings here.The game is really cool, with really nice mechanics, graphics are cool, voice acting is cool, events are cool and I love "cheating" with devil powers :)The problems for me are the bugs and the balancing.Bugs:-> I lost in act 1 and had crickets (?) sound and an hourglass endlessly spinning, had to kill the game and relaunch it. It then restarted the last combat,-> Sometimes you summon a portal on the map, you "confirm" the cost in devil's power and you get the "sound" confirmation but the popup stays there and you can click again or click on cancel and nothing happens, so, close the game or back to lair,-> Kinda a spin off of above, you try to go through the portal and click on "launch", the button disappears but you are not teleported (so restart the game or back to lair),-> Some events add you two AP points, sometimes there is a big gap between the usual 5 AP points and the "bonus" AP points),There are a couple more but I forgot.Balancing:Sometimes you just trample everything and then you get wrecked by one single mob who endlessly gets additional damage each time you damage him. Or you have the artifact that removes SP points (5 SP per HP removing skill) but the mob(s) have an armor that has more than 5 protection that never goes away.And this can happen at the beginning of the run or at the end or at the middle.I mean, I'm used getting wrecked in FTL or Isaac for example, but at least you can "make your luck" on those games.Here sometimes it's just not possible, you just see yourself dead.Some stuff I'd like to see:-> Access the disciples skills in the shop (I think the "Book" button is disabled, it's whether in the shop or when you get a "free" skill during events),-> See more easily how many skills of the same rarity you currently have when you buy or get a new one for free (I don't think I saw it?),-> Possibility to exit the skill sacrifice once you are in it, in case you want to "cancel" (Or I did not see the option?),-> Have a way to "remove" armor from an enemy / transfer it (the ones that do not depend of status), there might be a skill that does that but I have not seen it yet,-> Is there a way to debuff / steal the status that gives + 1 dmg per damage received? This one is really broken when met early game.I feel like Steam should have "Maybe later" recommendation level. Bugs are annoying but I guess will be fixed.The balancing is another story. My feeling is that I'm having a lot of fun until I reach one of the fight I'm talking about, then you go "oh well, reset". There are unfair fights too in Isaac and FTL, but your skills can make the difference there. Here not really. If you don't have exactly what is needed, you're dead.And you can have what is needed for one type of fight, but not another right after.So would I play the game again in the long run? Maybe not, and that would be a shame, it is really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this one a thumbs up as I keep coming back to it.  However, there are a few caveats here:1. The runs do indeed take a long time to complete.  I've had to leave my laptop running to step away as I couldn't finish the run in the time I had allotted to sit and game.2.  Good luck finishing an entire run!  The run goes from "Man, this is a cake walk; I haven't taken a single point of damage" to "Welp, that just one shot my entire crew..."  After 20 hours, I've yet to finish a whole run without dying.  Maybe I just suck at it?3. Speaking of playing 20 hours... how the heck do I unlock more characters??  I've played the same 4 over and over with no clue how to unlock the others.  Even a Google search didn't seem to help as it seems not enough people have created guides here?  The game should have some sort of tracker to show you how to unlock characters as I desperately need a change of pace from these first 4...4.  Randomness is definitely a problem if you don't like luck based games.  I like randomness thrown it; keeps you on your toes.  But I can see how this could be a problem for some players.So... with all these negative marks against this game - why the positive review?  Well, it is really fun and I keep coming back to it.  If I were rating this game, I would rate it a 6/10 but there is potential here for a 10/10 with future patches.  Also, it's flippin' $25 and well worth that price tag.  I can't even get a burger at Five Guys for $25 (even though it's worth every penny).  This game will keep you entertained longer than a juicy burger and is WAY less cholesterol!

_childDocuments_.review: You might have read some of the negative reviews in which people complain about the difficulty, the repetitiveness and lack of depth. I wanted to adress some of these:It is more difficult than you might think at first glance. It is more like Darkest Dungeon or Iratus than it lets on (without the Hamlet/Graveyard). It might be humoristic at times and not take itself too seriously, but it IS difficult, especially for people who though this was a relaxed after-work game. Although it gets easier after leveling up (the meta progression) because you can unlock more characters, more skills and relics you can then find and use throughout a run which allow for more syngergy and therefore makes it easier, despite the enemies becoming stronger.And of course it is repetitive. It is a rogue-like. What do people expect? You fail, you start all over. Well, not entirely, once you beat a "book" you don't lose it ever again. Every character has two unique unlockable relics (items which alter how they function) and about a dozen skills, of which some have to be unlocked. So there is a lot of potential depth here to be had. Enemies also have two different health bars, like in Darkest Dungeon your character have, or in Iratus the enemies. Once these reach 0, they become vulnerable, basically "Death's Door", same goes for your characters as well. Enemies who can take while vulnerable die. Yours on the other hand don't die, but instead the Devil himself takes damage to his global health pool. Speaking of which: This global health pool, the "Devil's Essence" can be used to "cheat". You can pretty much alter every aspect of combat and on the campaign map using this resource. When, where and how much you use is up to you and makes for some difficult and tactical decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty game, fun theme, overall well made (I haven't encountered bugs at least)But oh my god combats last forever. Most of the time it feels like battle of attrition, especially on chapter bosses. I have to play on apprentice, and even then it is unbearably tedious. Even regular encounters can take forever with certain enemies always having shell or provoke on them. Dispell skills are very rare, so tough luck if you have none. At certain point, combat lasts so long and is so repetitive, that it isn't worth it. And other 3 characters being unlocked so late in the game is a bad idea. I get bored before I can get to them, which is a shame. I'd rather be able to experiment with multiple configurations at least, initial 4-5 characters don't provide enough variety in party compositing.If enemies had less hp overall, and if the whole set of all the heroes was unlocked earlier on in the game, my review would be positive. But as it is - RIP, sad. If it comes out on mobile, i'll probably play it, but on PC - nah.P.S. Oh yes, and boo-hoo, it's this long to balance for Devil Mode. Well, I don't think Devil mode is that fun. I would rather not have it, have 2 times less devil hp, 2 times less enemy hp, and faster combats. Sometimes, less is more.
