_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the cutest games I've played in a while. If you're looking for a puzzle game that can easily be consumed in 1-3 hours, this is the perfect game. The puzzles are difficult enough to warrant a few tries, but not so difficult that they can't be figured out by players of all ages. I haven't played the single player version of this game, but playing with a second person made this game so very entertaining. This is a game that requires teamwork, so be prepared to communicate with your teammate when playing. That being said, there really aren't negative consequences to how many times you fall off the map or how long it takes you to complete a level, so feel free to get creative in your solutions to the puzzles. I could see this game being one that you could replay over and over with different people and it would be like a different game each time. Plus, the challenge levels and time trials allow for an added challenge for the more serious players. The robot characters in the game are also extremely adorable, which is a plus. Their small emotes and personalities give the game a more wholesome feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Biped

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little game, and one of the most enjoyable co-op experiences I've had since Portal 2.I first played Biped at PAX 2020, and I was immediately hooked. The teamwork required in the co-op campaign is incredibly fun, requires a fair amount of coordinated teamwork/communication, and never fails to leave me laughing like an idiot. The gameplay is fairly simple and the game is not overly difficult, but it's always trying new things and keeping the formula fresh. In the pro levels, planning is rewarded, as is thinking on your toes when your plan inevitably goes sideways on you. My friend and I were reduced to maniacal giggling on more than one occasion when against all odds we managed to finish a pro-level by the skin of our teeth, one foot hanging out over the void. Every second spent in this game was a delight, and I only wish there were more of it.Which brings me to my one knock on the game: length. My friend and I got through all the co-op/co-op pro levels in ~5 hours. For $15, I think this is a decent price, but I would kill for player creation tools a la Portal 2 so that we can make/upload our own pro-levels. My mind boggles at the possibilities. tl;dr - great co-op experience, a bit short but incredibly fun, and would benefit immensely from user-creation tools.

_childDocuments_.review: BiPed is a refreshing take on co-op puzzle games with an adorable aesthetic and a good about of challenge.While you can play it solo, co-op is definitely the way to go and it has reliable local and online options.There really isn't another game like BiPed, both because of the variance in the types of puzzles you'll encounter and also because of it's unique controls. They highly recommend a controller because you control each of your characters legs individually in an analog fashion. While this sounds like it would be clunky and difficult in the way games like QWOP are, it's very smartly designed and while it will always present a bit of a challenge, you'll find yourself getting used to it quickly.You'll face a variety of different challenges in the game's short story mode and each level also has two additional challenge stages, which are notably more difficult. The uber cute aesthetic and relatively short progression to a solution for the puzzles (once you figure them out of course) means you won't end up frustrated out of boredom, at least most of the time. Each zone has a different environment, totally different puzzle mechanics and different environmental hazards. Even though the base campaign can be completed be reasonably skilled players in 4 hours or so, it feels tightly designed and not that it's lacking content, rather that it doesn't waste any time or overstay its welcome.This was a real pleasant surprise of a title and I'm very glad I had the chance to co-op it with a friend. If you like puzzle games with unique design, don't pass this up. Just make sure you have a controller and ideally, someone to play it with.
_childDocuments_.name: Biped

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe such simplicity was the reason for the whole family (including missus, wow) to enjoy this game quite a lot. We played, we tried, we failed, we laughed during this fun and clumsy adventure.  If you are looking for a good game to play with your small kids – give Biped a try, it will reward you with a number of great family evenings.+ Very accessible+ Stylish locations+ Clever gameplay mechanics+ Good for junior kids- (almost) No single player- Too short- Not much of a storyBiped is a new puzzle-platformer game from a Chinese developer Next Studios. It represents the light side of casual gaming – fun, easy, short, simple, and polished. Do not expect any serious challenge or cinema-like plot twists. It’s just not that type of game. This game is for you to have a few hours of hearty laughs together with your family while browsing stylish cartoonish locations.You play for two robots – Take Aku and Sila – who are sent to Earth to save it from going dark by lighting the beacons across the planet. From forests and swamps to mountains and deserts, you will have to use your cooperation skills throughout the journey.So. You take control of a robot that has two legs that are moved by using the respective thumbsticks. The robot can walk step by step, or more like left-right-left. It can also slide in some areas by holding two thumbsticks together. This comes as a relief since you move much faster 🙂The point of every level is to reach its end by moving from one obstacle to another, collecting coins, and looking for hidden stars. Most of the puzzles will test your reflexes, some of them will include a tad of logic. Biped is all about cooperation and you always have to combine your effort as a duo to solve these puzzles and move further down the level.The fact that legs of the robots live their own lives,  is allowing the game to use some clever and interesting gameplay mechanics. Some you just need to stomp the button at the very exact moment. Sometimes you have to move in sync with your partner. Sometimes your leg hangs in the air unless it is time to use yet another switch or step onto the panel of a matching color. Miss the moment – and the branch knocks you off the moving platform to a roar of joy from your kids  😀Let’s make this clear from the very beginning – Biped is not to be played solo. It’s just not as fun as when you are passing through the levels together. This is a pure couch co-op experience that should absolutely involve kids. Either as spectators (so they could laugh at their parents) or as players (so they could just laugh).The environment is user friendly – there are no enemies, no bosses, no scary moments or deadly traps. Thus Biped could be a very good game to start playing with your small kids. In my case, 4 y.o. girl (though as smart as some 6 y.o. 🙂 managed to get herself accustomed to unusual controls within one day. The clunky characters and the situations they get themselves into,  inspire pure emotions from kids. They were having even more fun when the almighty (in terms of gaming) dad failed to step on a button at the right time or missed the step sequence, dropping into a pit.What I liked about the game the most, is that it didn’t annoy me – or kids- even a single time during the playthrough.  It is simplified in every aspect. The difficulty provides enough challenge for you to solve the puzzle or complete the trial in 5-10 attempts. The landscapes are simplistic, but cozy lighting and attention to detail make it look cartoonishly sweet. There are some clothing items you can buy for characters, but they are only a few and easily obtainable.  And you can complete the main story in 4-5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing this game after 18 hours of play time. Biped is a very enjoyable co-op game for 2 players. The game is fully playable as solo, but co-op with a friend is 10x better. I only played through solo (after beating all of coop) for the remaining achievements.The graphics are cute, music is good, puzzles start of very easy and get more difficult, requiring voice chat with your friend. Some pro levels may test your friendship with failing so much haha, but with some patience and practice, it's all very fun. Also, you can use mouse & keyboard, or controller. _childDocuments_.review: On the face of it, Biped could have ended up something very much like Yoku's Island Express, which I was so enthusiastic about a short while ago. Superb tasteful visuals, good music and an interesting, novel gameplay - the perfect receipt for an indie hit. However, plans are one thing, while execution is quite another. Unfortunately, in this case.Biped's basic idea (control two legs of a creature separately) is not exactly new, but I haven't yet seen it in a 3D puzzle game - and spatial puzzles can be exhilarating fun if done well. Biped starts promising, but runs out of steam after like 10 minutes - the controls are not intuitive and tend to get super annoying (why is there no separate grab button?), the puzzles are repetitive and get old real fast, and for some reason, the game thinks it's important that if you make a mistake, then you should die and respawn. It took 2 hours to finish the 8 levels, and only half of it could be considered quality time.It still gets a thumbs up, for two reasons:- There is at least some great content, which is never a given- The coop gameplay could be more fun simply because dying in annoying ways is much more fun if someone else does itYou may want to give it a shot, but probably only at a hearty discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Biped is an excellent little co-op game. The adventure mode isn't very challenging, but it introduces the mechanics and the ways of coordinating required to succeed in the "pro" levels. Each stage of the adventure has two pro levels that are associated with it, and you must beat the first to unlock the second. In many ways, these pro levels are the "meat" of the experience, and they require precision and good communication. In one commonly used platforming obstacle, players are required to alternate their steps to match the changing color of a platform to successfully cross.I liked the game's physics engine, and found it satisfying to move objects around in the world, especially the barrels that must be smashed to reveal the coins they contain. I also found it fun to slide along the color-coded rails, swinging my foot this way and that to acquire the floating coins.The only irritation I had with the game lies with the "shrinking" platforms. Certain platforms will shrink until they disappear if the players don't keep the appropriate number of legs planted on them at all times. Even if you know what you need to do and have devised a plan here, it can be very difficult to prevent the platform from shrinking into a useless state. This is compounded by the fact that as the platform shrinks, your characters legs will often fall off of the sides. This will in turn increase the amount of time that you have the number incorrect, and the platform will therefore continue shrinking.Overall, I quite liked Biped. If you're looking for a cutesy, vibrant co-op game that requires communication and coordination to complete (especially the pro levels), NEXT Studios has you covered. I think the main campaign would could also be a fun experience for parents to have with their children.
_childDocuments_.name: Biped

_childDocuments_.review: Biped is a puzzle co-op game. It really requires 2 players. There is a solo mode although I haven't tried it. You will most certainly need a mic to play but you can grab it on Steam and a friend can connect via remote play. The mechanics require you to move each leg one at a time similar to games like Heave Ho so controls feel a bit clunky but that's part of the fun. The puzzles aren't overly challenging but the game is still fun. The main campaign is rather short at about 2-3 hours and there are some additional challenge levels. The challenge levels are fun and challenging but at times frustrating. They do require teamwork so don't play this game without a friend. If you are looking for a fun co op game, give it a go. I beat the campaign in a single sitting and enjoyed it all the way through.

name: Panzer Corps 2
detailed_description: Axis Operations Bundle All the Axis Operations DLCs in a single bundle. Play the entirety of World War II from the German perspective in a huge linked campaign, carrying your army over from one DLC to the next. About the Game Panzer Corps 2 is the ultimate Second World War strategy game! Enjoy the time-proven gameplay formula which has been appreciated by millions of players over the years, brought to a whole new level of refinement up to the latest technical standards. The king of wargames is back Easy to play and at the same time extremely deep, its fine-tuned turn-based gameplay style means that it’s the quality of your decisions, not the speed of clicking, which will determine the outcome of your battles. Don’t outpace your enemies, outsmart them! In-depth gameplay mechanics model unit movement, combat, spotting, encirclements, weather, capturing enemy equipment and much more. A massive amount of content Panzer Corps 2 is all about content. You can play for every major power in the European theatre of the Second World War, and unleash over a whopping 1000 unique different units on your enemies! Every single unit in the game has been painstakingly modelled and animated. No other game covers as many authentic World War II vehicles as Panzer Corps 2! All of World War II at your fingertips Panzer Corps 2 comes with a massive branching campaign including around 60 scenarios: lead the Wehrmacht in the entirety of World War II, carrying over your battle-hardened veterans from one battle to the next. 4 additional single player scenarios are available and another 10 scenarios carefully designed for a balanced Multiplayer experience. On top of that there is an advanced random map generator for Skirmish mode, offering six distinct map types and four mission types. The ultimate wargame online experience Challenge your friends or play on coop against the AI. Panzer Corps 2 offers a wide range of Multiplayer options: hot seat, server-assisted play-by-email (Slitherine’s PBEM++) mode, and a true online Multiplayer. In the latter mode it is even possible to play your turns simultaneously with your coop partner, which basically reduces waiting times to zero! A comprehensive editor Modding was always big with Panzer Corps series. For this reason, Panzer Corps 2 includes the most powerful Scenario Editor we have ever created, which is also very user friendly and easy to use. Using the Editor, you can create your own campaigns, single scenarios and multiplayer maps in no time, or you can enjoy content created by fellow players. If the prequel game is any indication, literally hundreds of user-made scenarios will be available for Panzer Corps 2 in no time, for unlimited replayability!

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING:  A very tepid thumbs up.  (I wish Steam had a middle option called meh, because that is what I would really give this game if I could.  Hopefully additional content will eventually change that)If you like Panzer Corps one, I give this game a very tepid thumbs up. If you haven't played the original Panzer Corps then buy that first as I think it is, as of right now, still the better game.  While the graphics are now 3D, to mee the map and units aren't much more than a cosmetic upgrade which isn't why you are playing this game in the first place.  I do believe that they did do a better job in balancing units overall than the first game. The interface is a bit more user friendly than the first game as well, which should be expected.  One major step back in this game is that the scenario objectives are you win or you don't.  There is no marginal or decisive victory, which I believe is a major loss to this game compared to its predecessor.  The map graphics, while enhanced with 3D are less clear than the original game which is a problem.  I find myself always having to look at each hex to see which terrain is this?  I didn't generally have to do that in the original game since terrain was fairly standard.  The new reserves system seems an entirely unnecessary addition unless they plan on doing more with it.  Heroes are better but far fewer than the original game.  They advertise so many new units but I feel there is no more units than the original game, perhaps even less. As the German player, you can't buy Italian units in the Afrika Korps portion of the campaign, at least not yet to the point I am at. Perhaps this is simply because they are counting their anticipated DLCs they will eventually put out.  The biggest problem with the game is that you are paying for a new game that is functionally similar to the old, just with better graphics and a slight decrease in quality of overall game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, they patched it and it runs a lot better.  Glad I was wrong.  Thanks devs.Revised: A dev PM'd me on the Slitherine forums when I posted an innocuous comment about how I was concerned about the graphics back in the beta, referring to the preorder.  He titled the PM "dude, really?" and was very defensive.  I paid the max price for the game to support the game, I wrote a good review, I've been active and constructive on the forums, and this dude incorrectly assumes there's a NDA from the pre-order 48 hour play period, and writes how it's hard to handle all the incoming reports and I should be quiet.  Maybe I want to play the game I bought without overheating my good computer? It wasn't addressed between the preorder beta and now, so why wouldn't I bring it up? Christ.I don't recommend until there is a patch that addresses the overheating issues.  The defensive dev response makes me concerned patches will be few and far between.Old review:Immensely replayable, addicting game. It's easy to pick up but mastering takes quite a bit of time.  The customization is top notch.  The game comes with a variety of campaigns and scenarios.  I see a lot of players starting with Poland, but I started with North Africa and had an amazing time.While I think Order of Battle handles the sum total of units better (naval, air, land) in any given scenario, PZ2 excels at land combat, and represents airfare and naval warfare well. The number of units and customization possible is amazing. It's an excellent game out of the box, with updates and DLC it may be superior to Order of Battle.  It runs hot on my system, but devs are working on it.  Otherwise my games have bug free.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are reading the reviews looking at if you should buy the game please read my review and maybe it can help.The price for the base game can be a bit pricey but I can promise you, that money is given back in play-time. This game has locked me in hour after hour and if you want to fight battle after battle as the Axis or Allied and follow through with historical or non-historical (Changing history) You can. The game can be as easy or difficult as you desire. The options are many and leave for a good time which you're in control of, whether your wanting to run through the game on easy or spend a while thinking strategy over every battle you can. The options are not locked into "Easy, normal" or "hard" you have more advanced options, controlling supply lines, weather, how battles are resolved etc... The game gives you a-lot more than what most newer games can offer in a single player environment. I've put 20 hours into the game now and have not even come close to finishing all of the single player content. If you are into strategic war games then I would highly recommend you try it, or just watch some videos and see if it's for you. The game works well for multiplayer or if you prefer single player.Now comes the 'Ok' side of Panzer Corps 2... Buying the pack with the music and skins; It really comes down to what you value. The skins are alright, I wish they were more historical to what was used, (mainly for the Germans) a lot of them feel like the "Golden AK-47" skin in an FPS, a more show off than an actual skin for war, but there are a few historical ones in it so that is nice. The music is fantastic, I am very happy with it and am 100% satisfied with owning a copy of it. I usually listen to my own music but I have found myself not wanting to with Panzer Corps 2.The graphics are stunning and the game play can be fast or slow which is good to be able to pick from. You can do without the bonus content but I am a Panzer Corps fan so I kind of wanted to own it all... Hope the review helped.Edit 2021/06/13: Just wanted to update my review on the skins for the game as they have changed. They seemed to have added in way more options over time and many of them being historical, I can say I am very happy with it, and glad they have been so up to-date with their game. This game's a great buy if you're one for turn based strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: Best strategy game i've seen in my life.Im 40. Been playing RTS and strategy games since i'm a kid. Played the first RTS(Dune 2) and all the following ones in the 90'(Command & Conquer, Warcraft, etc) until I discovered Total War(played the first Shogun demo, then bought the first Medieval Total War, then I no longer EVER cared for that crappy RTS primary school style where it's only about who can build his stuff the fastest). Still a Total War fan, but Panzercorps is the best, strategy-wise, even if it's not as shiny and polished as Total War. Played over 2000 hours combined with XCOM and XCOM 2, and even those are inferior tactical-wise to Panzercorps. Again, Panzercorps is not as a shiny and polished as XCOM of course, but who cares. Still waiting for a real XCOM 2 Long War mod...You get to learn alot of history details about WW2. And you know you'll learn alot when you see the point of view of the germans. Which nobody ever dared to do cause everyone is brainwashed to view this war in black & white, good vs evil, which is dumb as f*ck. Because of this, almost everyone today ignore how brillant the german army was. Definitly not a game for everyone, but that's the case with all the best games i've seen. Just like with music - the low IQ people prefer stupid crap. Talking about music, you guys should check the song Ghost Division from Sabaton. Which is about the 7th Panzer Division led by Rommel, going through France. Great band to listen while you play this masterpiece.EDIT: The only downside to this game is the AI. Its not horrible, but some behaviors make it average. Although the way the game works, the average AI is not as bad a problem as with other games. Because the AI units are well-positionned and they're usually defending in most missions. And when AI is attacking(in missions where you're defending), it has number advantage. So in both cases, it's not that bad and the game remains challenging.The one bad AI behavior that is most easy to fix is when an AI unit attacks when it obviously shouldn't. For example: an entrenched infantry in a town that will lose soldiers and have low chance to kill anything if it attacks, and it still does. Easy coding fix. Don't know why it wasn't fixed yet.The other bad AI behavior is more complexed to fix. Its the fact that each AI unit plays individually, with no regard to any plan by the AI general. Its why AI artilleries hit different targets, and same thing for the infantries and tanks. They won't even necessary attack what their arties suppressed. They each play individually, like each unit has a different brain with no clue what the other units did or will do.But don't let that discourage you. Once you've become experienced, theire's a ton of custom options to adjust the game to your level.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't find my long-winded, thesaurus-selling vocabulary entertaining, the TLDR:: is at the bottom.  I won't be offended (since I won't know) - and I write these up mostly for my own amusement.  The time you save will be your own -but, if you're a risk-taker, or an insomniac, read on.  :)  PzC 2Including many nice polish ups of features in PC 1, this is anything BUT just a polish-up!  Significant mechanics changes alter the underpinning of why mobility and static strategies make sense and reward or punish choices and techniques.  Paper-Rock-Scissors now to 7 degrees of freedom, a major rework of awards and heroes along with a player's "General traits" make replayability pretty good even before any DLC expansions add another partial to the calculus.  Known for slavish attention to bug and oversight problems, the title's Devs already have some excellent follow up patches and improvement work, and some nice innovation for the series (like variable unit makeup and placement for AI players in some scenarios- which help keep it fresh for those bored by always facing the same threat from the same directions).  As a veteran of the grandfather of the series as well as PzC 1, it seems to me a pretty good recall of the original intent with fresh ways of getting to a version of 'authentic' that feels like fun for present-day gamers.    Some people have complained about the map or the units being hard to tell apart, but for this gamer, the 3D look is pretty cool, and  whether a tank is a 'J' version or a 'G' would have taken some hard looking and learning from what it did to you on the RL battlefield.  In fact, because of heroes, awards, and experience some older units might have better stats than just-off-the-line or reserve units.  New-fangled bells and whistles without the benefit of hard frontline duty may not cut it alone, young whipper-snapper! :)Not your daddy's Panzer-General, but just as addictive, and quick to punish the sloppy and and the unbeliever if you dare to put the higher levels of difficulty to the test:... this new version includes all new ways to examine your need for self-hatred.  Combine every horrible case-scenario in any combination or even all at once - inexorable defeat and self-loathing is just a few box-ticks away if you just have to have it...  LOL  You can even play with a slider for what level the actual results adhere to game rules, or real condition- so if just hard isn't enough, those with a desire for the hair-tearing unpredictability of the actual battlefield can increase RNG-induced hell in all new combinations.  TLDR::As usual in my reviews, my first and last recommendation is not to read these reviews too long or too often, but find a few good PzC 2 playthroughs that won't bore you to death.  Two excellent players and fun to listen-to are You Tubers GreenKnight (his review of General's traits is possibly the best) and Edmon (who has an ineffable reveal of encirclement for pikers like me).  They represent some of the best free-lance players who go  out of their way to help other players.  Das Tactic, who has done some of the official tutorial and intro Let's-Play vids for the PzC 2 title, is loads of fun to watch, but hasn't much beyond the original content I mention here.  ~~Either way, if you watch one or two and find yourself wanting to find another one, com'on man, you already know you just need to buy it. :)I have 127 hours in as of this review, and that number is going to be way higher before I realize I haven't eaten in a while!  ~Al

_childDocuments_.review: I remember many years ago when the forerunner to this series 'Panzer General' was previewed with the words: 'For every armchair general out there'. It worked back then and it works again now: This game is for you who dig the WW2-setting, but prefer a wargame at your own speed, calculated strategies and the option to have a beer/coke in one hand while you play it.I have to say that so far this game looks like a rare combo of playability and good finish. The campaign puts you in the right, historical mood, the eye- and ear-candy graphics and music supports it well. Varied music even - it changes from France to the desert!Units can earn as well experience as special abilities and heroes with special abilities. I normally hate the hero-stuff, but it works very well in this game and just adds to the feeling of being able to tune your army all the way down to the colour of their shoe laces!I have only run into a few quirks, but no real bugs. This is very rare for new games! I can't remember the last time I bought a game 1 month after release and it had no bugs! I read that some players had crash bugs etc., but I had zero of anything. Thumbs up for that. This is what every game developer should do too (watch and LEARN, Paradox!).Downsides? Of course there are, but it is really searching for the smallest hair in the soup IMO. As some have mentioned, the campaign is sequential and basically leaves you no choice other than play section 1 or 2 of the same scenario. And if you would rather play a stand-alone scenario, then there's only 4 in the standard game to chose from (in single player). You can buy the larger editions, but it's still just a handfull.Some sound effects are totally off. The trucks and a lot of the vehicles for example sounds like tiny, electric, toy cars. Some of the animations look ridiculous too.Certain tooltips in the game need updating and are ill explained. I guess they forgot to change the text when something was altered (?). Fortunately one can find the right explanations in the forum. Or just consider it something to explore.Also, the historical correctness is so-so. But it's still fun, so who cares?Oh, and the game has reintroduced 'PBEM' - a disciplin long forgotten by the game industry. Kudos for that.In all I can clearly recommend this game to any player out there who likes a steady tempo rock-paper-scissors game in a WW2 setting!

Panzer General veterans will remember how fast you were thrown to 1945 when u were "too" successful in the early stages of the war. This is no longer the case. _childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Very GoodDISCLAIMER: I WAS A BETA-TESTER FOR THIS GAME:I put almost 700 hours into the original game, and I beta tested this sequel, but I held off on purchasing as I burned out on the genre. Running on Unreal engine, PC2 is the modern-era’s version of Panzer Corps.You play as the Nazis during WW2 as you go through the campaign to invade most of Europe. You have a host of infantry, tanks and various other units you can build as your core army that you take from battle to battle.There are quite a few upgrades to the gameplay, notably an overhaul of the use of planes, making more use of Anti-Tanks and Artillery units, a more important role for recon units and so on. The changes are implemented with a brand spanking new campaign, which starts with the invasion of Poland and then allows you to choose to go to Afrika or Russia, and if you do well enough, you branch off into a-historical Nazi victory scenarios.There is plenty of meat in the campaign, many early scenarios offer alternative routes and tactical styles, whilst the a-historical and historical routes mean that there are lots of opportunities to replay the game.Overall, it is a solid package, that is worth the entry price for both new and old fans of the game.For those wanting to know the changes more in-depth;Aircraft now ‘base’ at an airfield on the map, and always refuel and rearm every turn, so you don’t have to keep tracking them. You just launch them into their sorties as you want. As you progress, you rebase them to other, better airfields.Anti-tanks now offer counter-fire, like an artillery unit, but only against tanks/vehicles, which makes them more useful as a defensive and offensive tool compared to the first game, where their towed nature made them fairly difficult to use on the offense. Artillery now counter-fires against soft targets only (infantry) unless they are the type artillery that can offer anti-vehicle fire, in which case they will counter-fire against tanks, or both tanks and infantry. Some artillery even counter-fire against artillery fire!Recon units now offer an accuracy bonus vs enemy when nearby, making them useful forward observers for planes, artillery and your other attacking units. There are even recon planes now!The upgrade tree is now a flat cost to upgrade across all variant units, rather than cheap if you upgrade ‘in class’ and expensive ‘out of class’. Which should allow for force flexibility and army building.You even get to create your general avatar and add conditions, such as strengths and weaknesses, which can radically change the flow of the game. For example, you can put in a rule that prevents you from ever owning an air force, or make your AA units super-powered. There’s a lot of thought and flexibility put into this sequel, and they are working on the DLC Grand Campaign, so this is a game with a lot of long term potential as well. Definitely one for war game fans.Downsides: Originally I complained about performance issues, but these seem to have been fixed as of August 2021. Downsides: The Grand Campaign modules seem to be getting a bit of a mixed reception, unfortunately, but ignoring those, the base game makes up for a solid campaign experience so far, and is a worthwhile entry. Do more research before jumping into the DLC however.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after 50hrs of game play I need to advise players about my experience with the game.  The ground warfare is very good!  If you played Panzer Corp (PC) and like it you will be pleased with PC2.  But, YES there is a BIG but. Naval combat is totally stupid!!  It's like whoever built the naval combat, just decided.  I am too lazy to make it realistic or I just need to get the game out. So, I will just use the same land combat results and experience for naval combat.  Example: I attack an enemy vessel of 10 points - it losses 3 now it's 7.  Next I attack the same vessel with two other ships (supposedly getting a mass attack type of advantage) yet my losses do not reflect this advantage. One of my ships losses 3 points and the other two.  While the enemy lost only 2 more points; so now it is a 5 point vessel. I attack yet again and lose 2-3 more points on my ship and they lose another point or maybe two.  Totally unrealistic!!  Ships cannot have the same type of loss and experience settings as land forces.  A ship does not fight better when it is heavily damaged.  Sure, it will fight somewhat better from gaining experience.  However, in this game 3 and 4 point ships fight better and sink more ships than when it is full strength (10 points).  Once a ship is damaged to 5 points or less it is super hard to kill.  Instead of losing combat ability because guns are knocked out, fires burning, killed men, taking on water and lost speed due to damage. It fights better! To add fuel to the fire - I am only playing on level 2 one up from the lowest easy skill level setting of the game.  I can only image the super unsinkable enemy ships I would face if playing at average or better skill level. Ships are not like land units, when damaged they can't out run an enemy attack or retreat to a better defensive position.  It's in the ocean, so how is it becoming dramatically better when heavily damaged.  I am so livid about the POOR naval combat that I am considering not playing the game.  Oh, by the way I am only speaking of the naval combat in the Norway scenario.  If the other scenario's which involve naval combat play this way I would want to ask for my money back!!  This from a person who has over 3,000hrs of playing Panzer Corp.  I actually went so far as to reinstall Panzer Corp just to compare it to the new version of the game.  Did no one who programmed this version of Panzer Corp even check out how naval game play was handled in the original Panzer Corp???  I hope someone fixes the naval combat.  If they do, I will be glad to recommend the game then.  BUT, as it is; with this gross naval combat model - I can only say past it up. If you want to get the game and play just the land combat scenario's then fine.  I feel they have done a good job with it.  Sooo, disappointed!!!Ok, update after 103hrs played.  After playing for hours  (approx. 47hrs) on level two>  I changed to the easiest level one.  Now after playing an additional 50hrs plus. I am ready to tear my hair out!!!  Land combat has flawes which should have been revealed in any play testing that might have been done (I have to emphasize MIGHT have been done). Because they are very easily spotted\observed issue(s). Example: When attacking in the Paris scenario there is a law caliber Arty stationed in Paris.  When I went to attack an enemy fighter in Paris adjacent to the arty. unit with my fighter it gave 7-1 odds (7 being my losses projected).  The enemy fighter I was attacking wasn't even a regular fighter; it was a fighter\bomber.  Now if that arty. had been a German 88 artillery then I could see the possibility.  I had to eliminate the artillery unit first before I could make my air attack.  Another glaring issue: I encircled and attacked a Matilda II tank which ran out of ammo.  Then at the start of the next round (even though still encircled) it had been somehow resupplied to full ammo.  Really, how the blank did that happened some french air supply drop in the night.  This has happened multiple times with different units which have been encircled.  Granted, I could see the possibility of a unit getting one or two rounds of ammo simulating found ammo from a knocked out tank unit found at night etc... being simulated (but even then not a completely encircled unit).  I won't even go into how effective the French units fight (which should be reduced by a low morale effect after the first day of attacks). They on the easiest level fight like hard core units (full fury).  Is there no moral or real world option that a player could choose to at least simulate real events.  Then on then on the German side how about an option in options similar to what I just mentioned for the French but giving the Germans an 12-18 month biltz bonus. I mean if the French had fought like they do in PC2 in WWII they would have been able to at least stalemate the Germans into another WWI repeat. I played the game in it's SUPER short two day open beta play test or at least that is what they called it.  I did not give any feedback at the time because I wanted more time to evaluate and be able to give some honest good feedback about the game. Now I have to wonder if the product needed to be play balanced more but since a release date had all ready been announced they figured we'll just fix it after it's released.  Well, it time to fix some of these MAJOR issue(s).  I no longer can even recommend the game for it's land combat only!!!  I now recommend, players stay with Panzer Corp (even though PC2 has some really nice features added).  PC2 just has not been played tested and some glaring issue(s) fixed that should have not made it into the released version.  I do not make many reviews of games; but when someone takes such a great game (over 3400hrs with PC, and those are just the Steam documented hours, hundreds more played just not though Steam) and ruins the simple yet entertaining game play I knew and loved in PC.  I have to stand up and be heard - to warn those who may be thinking of paying for a product that has such flaws in it's basic game play.  ONCE again I am willing to change my review to thumbs up if things are worked on and fixed.  So, Dev it's up to you.  I am still willing to even play test it; in hope the game can be brought to the glory of Panzer Corp!!!

Transport gets an update, with the possibility of some transport travel and dismounting in the same turn (if not traveling full distance). Army size depends on not only the number of units, but also their calibre. That killer OP unit may take up the same space as 2-3 lesser units. Choices need to be made. _childDocuments_.review: As a rule I don't review games, since expectations and tastes are so different from player to player. In this case however I make an exception.I've been playing hex- and turn-based strategy since the well aged Panzer General came to PC in the early nineties. I tried many others, like the complete Five Star Series back in the day, or the numerous Order of Battle campaigns. I've played through the whole Panzercorps 1 campaigns, even the very long LEgacy of Versailles mod. Some of these lived up to their promises, others fell short; but all had to slug it out with the venerable Panzer General.So as a vet, I was really looking forward to this new title in the genre. With over 100 hours dumped into it, however, I must admit that it feels shallow. This is based on the fact that the only really new aspect is the leaders feature. Some are interesting, others rather not. Also the feature of the general traits which can be chosen at the start of a new campaign, with goodies and baddies. But while some just make it hard in a way that is ridiculous (no airforce? no artillery? no movement into unexplored territory? who came up with these??). But that's a question of taste as well. I simply don't like this feature.The "supply" system just feels wrong. One enemy unit in an isolated city still counts as "supplied", just because one hex towards your(!) lines is not in your ZOC. Can enemy supply transports go hundreds of miles around my troops, through forests and hills, so that this annoying engineer can still replace and regain ammo day after day? This was one of the aspects already annoying me in the old PG, and which was only satisfyingly resolved on the Order of Battle series.But the most boring aspect here is the fact that you just need to win a scenario on the last day in order to progress through the campaign until you reach the Pacific. One day later, you are bumped. Two weeks early? Tons of prestige, but no strategic consequence whatsoever. This was THE feature in PG that was most intriguing. Hurry up, really give those Frenchies a beating, and you end up on the shores of England in 1940. Stroll through the Loire valley -> chance lost. It should depend on your performance which path you are strategically able to go. But not so in PC2. Why? It makes the game just an arcade-style "hammer-the-enemy". If I wanted that I could play Tekken or whatever. I don't need a "strategy" game for that purpose.To add this "strategic depth", they introduced choices after certain scenarios. So after Stalingrad, you can choose whether you want to go the way of final defeat or final victory. And it's a one time decision. You don't get a second chance. In other games, this path was decided by your performance. Here, it is a choice. Again, who came up with this concept?? It simply ruins the game experience. It's the same feature that made the Grand Campaigns in PC1 dull and destroyed replayability, in contrast to the basic campaign.The rest of the game ist just pushing around units from A to B. Care for a game of chess with tanks and hills? Then this is for you. If you like a special challenge as never seen before in any game of the genre, like trying to conquer Europe without an airforce or whatever, then this is for you (you could just play PG or PC1 without buying planes, but that's your choice...).If you like a real struggle whose outcome depends on your tactical choices and performance on the battlefield? Just walk away and find your luck elsewhere. Maybe it's possible to mod this feature into the game or a DLC (too much money, anyone?) will add it, but so far it's just not there.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Corps 1 was an important step bringing the Panzer General genre back to life, it was a conservative approach but a successful one. PzC 1 had a massive amount of content and a nice emersion making you very attached to your units, tough it suffered from a limited engine and poor A.I. PzC was nice until OoB came out and did almost everything better.Panzer Corps 2 feels like an evolution in the right way, the developer emboldened by its success and experience in PzC 1 has well has the changes in recent games of the genre, took the PzC formula further, building a superior experience without losing the game cohesion.This game and its genre face big challenges, since the wargame community is kind of a niche. First it has to present a product that satisfies its niche audience and second needs to appeal to potential new players (in my case I need something that makes me invade Poland for the 50 time). Overall, I think that both objectives have been achieved, wargamers will be satisfied by improvement in gameplay and rules while less hardcore players will be attracted to the graphical quality.The new game engine seems to hold great potential and based in PzC 1 experience I know that the game will be supported and updated for a long time, promising to get better and better has it matures, returning the gold standard of the genre to the PzC franchise.Not everything is perfect tough there’s a very important area of the game that seems neglected and is holding back the overall experience, immersion! I actually feel less connected to my units even having trouble telling the difference between the several infantry types in the field.Its not like the developer didn’t made some improvements in this area, the new heroes and award are a nice addition so is the players Character customization, but the almost free chance between unit types is a emersion breaker. I like that the H.Q. give you back full prestige but there’s should be a prestige cost for turning an infantry battalion into a Pioneer one. I would suggest that a percentage of the new unit should be paid for retraining purposes, even with new tanks and art pieces the crew would need to be retrained to use the new equipment, exempt from that would be upgrades in the same line like a moderner version of the same tank.The retraining cost percentage could vary the bigger the change in unit role, like for example 10% from Infantry to Heavy Infantry, 25% from Infantry to Fallschirmjagers. This would give more identity to units I think.Still in the field of immersion would be nice to get a window at the start of a new map with the new units available has well has their entering service date. Real life data about the equipments would also be great, I remember from PzG franchise that you could even see pictures of the inside of tanks with their components names. I will elaborate about this in the future, commenting the new chances 1 by 1 and presenting my suggestions.To finalize, the expectation of the players get higher has more games come out in this genre, because the focus of the game is mainly the same since some decades ago. To make a successful new game its essential to raise the quality otherwise the potential players see no reason to play the new game. PzC 2 is a clear improvement in the genre with a potential to become a masterpiece and define the genre.2 Days after release i give it 80%.I expect it to reach over 90% has the game matures i have great expetations for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually like this game a lot better than PZ1, I at times miss the scale and scope of PZ1, though I am enjoying this more so, it's much more flexible and provides better replay. Currently there are five nations in the game, US, UK, Italy, Germany and Russia with a combined 1,000 units or so between them. My favorite part so far is the editor and the random mission creator, both are so much more dynamic and fluid to what the previous game offered. I bought the Field Marshal Edition, one of things it comes with is about a 100 different camouflage paint schemes for you to select from, never gets old trying all the unique schemes out. I like the engineering and bridging aspects of the game, this game puts a big premium on movement and terrain feasibility, you can get easily stuck if you don't plan your routes accordingly. Graphically the units at times look amazing, though others aren't as much, they're not as detailed as I would like them to be, they kind of have a soft look to them, even at true 3840x2160 (4K). I'm able to run the game with all settings maxed using a 1080ti with zero issues. I like how destroyed units now remain on the battlefield, nice addition. Sound could definitely use improvement, unit sounds are much too low compared to the PZ1, they are very muted. I turn the music down to about 15% of the volume, if not, it would overwhelm the problem even more. Some things to fix, sooner than later.- AI does not use planes or AAA in random scenario creator, played 8-10 games, have yet to see the first one.- Sound - units lack punch right now, just really takes away from the game.- Units should look grittier, harder edged, right now they have a soft look as if they are overly stylized to a degree.- Should be able to set the amount of turns you want for the random scenario creator, sometimes I don't want to play 28 turns, just want something quick or maybe a longer game on the weekends, should be able to determine this in the options.- Unable to select the nations you want in your random scenarios.- Update the help options in the editor, right now most of the toggle buttons for help are not functional, or there is no corresponding guide to assist you, I'm referring to the (?) for each option, most of them are currently disabled. Devs are aware of most of what I referenced below, I'm confident these issues will be addressed. Overall, Panzer Corps 2 is an excellent game that I will get many years of enjoyment out of, highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: Started playing these types of games with Panzer General on PC, Advanced Daisenryaku on Megadrive (Sega Genesis), Advance Wars (GBA), Order of Battle, etc. So quite a few.- Core combat mechanics are intuitive and addicting. I haven't played these type of games for years but jumped right in. Overruns are so satisfying with tanks. Softening entrenched units with artillery support is like peeling a defensive onion and is so sweet when you reach and devour the soft meaty core.- Visuals are utilitarian yet still surprisingly beautiful. Zooming in and out provides nice detail.- Heroes are a fun (if not overpowered) addition providing variety to your units.- Whatever flaws I felt, I was still glued to the game to the end of the campaign--neglecting my wife, my dog, my sleep for those 60+ hours. If you like this type of genre, go and buy it. - Lacking epic scale: While it would make sense that some battles are more limited in scope, some (like invading the US) feel too small in map and unit size. All map sizes feel more or less the same, so it's a bit samey.- No victory variation based on speed: I confess I'm a filthy scum saver on occasion, but even then one of the greatest sense of accomplishments was getting that "Decisive Victory" message when beating a map. Sorely miss that mechanic.- Infantry balancing: I swear the enemy AI cheats especially with infantry. The game has a feature where you can preview what the losses will be if the enemy attacks. One time, the combat preview showed that a 3/5 experience US Army Ranger 2 hexes away would get demolished 9-0 by my max-experience, heroes-stacked Tiger II if they attacked (open field, so no defensive cover/bonuses). Lo and behold, during their turn they attack, and I somehow lose 2 Tiger IIs to their 5 infantry. Conversely your max-exp infantry seem to get consistently slaughtered, meaning there's not much point to using infantry, aside from cannon fodder. Makes for frustrating planning with such unbelievable outcomes.- Scripted AI: There are very obvious points, usually near key victory hexes, where the enemy suddenly pushes forward. Sometimes it seems to be triggered even if you're not even visible in their fog of war. Sometimes it works, sometimes it feels cheaty and too scripted.- Flawed resupply/reinforcement: I played so many of these type of games that I don't remember which is which, but some games limit how many units you can reinforce if there is an enemy adjacent, or penalize based on supply line. I like this mechanic and it makes sense. When an enemy paratroopers drop deep into my territory, and somehow reinforce 40% of their strength in one turn it's a bit ridiculous. Order of Battle has a much better supply line mechanic.- No ending: As Germans I successfully take over the U.S., and it just goes straight back to the menu screen! At least a single jpg image and a short message would be nice. Almost felt like a bug or something was missing.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend!I'm a big fan of turn based WWII games. I've played them all Panzer General, Panzer General II, Panzer Corps and all the DLC, Order of Battle. At first I was a little worried because the maps are small in the first scenarios, but things quickly open up at the campaign progresses. I think they accomplished exactly what they set out to do. This game is as much fun as any of the others I mentioned, but has a completely new UI and graphics. The animations are flawless. I haven't found any bugs, so testing must have been robust or they are fixing them quickly. The AI is absolutely brutal, if you leave a unit exposed, it will be killed. This can be used to your advantage by using a cheap unit to lure out the AI and then counter attacking. Those bastard devs also made sure to have the horrible combination of dug in infantry supported by anti-tank and anti-air with an armoured counter attack waiting for every city by a river. Totally frustrating in the best possible way! Even though I'm a veteran of this style, I ended up having to play on Lieutenant difficulty because I wasn't able to achieve Major Victories on some of the scenarios that unlock non-historic scenarios. The scenario tree is very impressive and fun to work through. High replayability due to several scenario tree choices that take you in different directions. The heroes feature is very well done. I found that it worked best to elect 1 Panzer and 1 Infantry to be "Super" units, that always received elite replacements and the best heroes. That increases later in the game. Another big replayability feature is the "Strengths and Weaknesses" settings for your commander. These aren't just trivial, they have a huge impact on the design and play style of your forces. It's also not reverseable, so if you pick something you don't like, you are stuck with it or restart the campaign. Has anyone played with the one where you can't send any units (including air) through fog of war? I tried that for about 2 turns before restarting, lol. That's a good example of one that would be TOUGH. A huge shout at to the devs for the implementation of UNDO! No one has ever gotten that right until now, well done! I love the way artillery works, where some guns are better for direct infantry support and some are meant for assault and counter battery. That's another feature I've never seen done better. I also love the way they assign unit slots. There are some types of units, such as anti-air, strategic bombers, and anti-tank guns that I never use in other games because they just are not as valuable as an infantry or tank unit. With the new core slot feature, these auxiliary units can be purchased and used exactly as they should be.I for one will be voting with my wallet and plan to buy every DLC they produce. Buy it and give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Like many here I've played all the predecessors of Panzer Corps 2. I've spent 1000's of enjoyable hours and have a solid understanding of the game mechanics and its long history.So is PzC 2 good? Nope. Is PzC 2 bad? Nope.I can't really put my finger on why this game misses the mark but it does. I think a lot of the problem is that everything feels familiar but just doesn't improve anything. Its like buying your favourite curry from a different restaurant, everything is ok but its just not as good.This game was never about the graphics and while it looks just about OK they add nothing. I want information and clarity and the new graphics distract from that. Everything seems a bit rounded, blurred and soft. Its like I'm playing on my TV.Some of the new mechanics are ok, I like the way the planes work, I really like overrun. These were nice tweaks and have been well balanced.There are a few bugs but I have no doubt these will be ironed out, I've had nothing game breaking yet. The worst was losing the battle predictions for one entire map and nothing I tried would get them back.I've used the word OK a lot in this review and that's where I'm at with this game, it's OK. If you've never played before I would not recommend starting here, I'd still say PzC1 is a better game. If you've played that to death and want a new challenge then you will get some fun out of this but I really wouldn't recommend anyone pays full whack for this, its just not worth it. I bought this over Half Life Alyx, I wish I hadn't.Update: If I spend over £50 on the pre-order top shelf edition it is a total rip off to be stung for DLC that should have been included. Absolutely stinks.

_childDocuments_.review: I really would like to enjoy this game.  The general idea is sound and the campaign progression is really cool.  I have a major problem with some of the combat mechanics however.  There is no reason units in mountain tiles should be taking high ground penalties defending against a unit in a hills tile, or another mountain tile.  That just doesn't make sense, the units aren't ziplining between mountains to be above eachother, they would have to move from their mountain into another mountain, which would negate the "high ground."  unless you are paradropping on the mountain, there is no real way to attack a mountain from above.  the surrounding mechanics are a bit wonky as well.  My unit should not be cut off if I have a unit behind them on the railway to where they are.  How exactly would they be cut off if I own the rail connection?  Being bombed through the fog of war by the AI is pretty annoying as well, as there should be no way they know the unit is there, but honestly I'm pretty used to AI omnipotence at this point.  The turn limit is pretty stupid as well.  I get it, it would make no sense to have an operation take super long like 100 turns, but some of the turn limits only allow for like a turn or two at the best of times, a few unlucky rolls can screw you.  This especially is stupid because of how often actual offensives got bogged down and went over the "time limit" in real life, especially in the Pacific, which will be the next DLC at the time of this review.  There also is little sense for a time limit in defensive battles, like the first mission in Italy.  Why do I have a time limit, as long as I can push the Americans back it should be fine.  There are also certain units that basically just suck and have no reason to be used, like the Ju88, but there was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ equipment in real life as well so that is what it is.  On the other hand, I really like parts of the game as well.  The trait mechanic is pretty cool, and can make for some interesting challenges, even if some are completely impossible, like the no arty trait.  being able to capture equipment is cool, as it was pretty frequent in real life, but I do not really understand the numbers that go into when a unit surrenders when surrounded, most of the time they just die for me.  The prototypes are cool for the same reason, being able to toy with cool units like a flammpanzer is fun, even if the use is very limited.  The Air force mechanics as a whole are really fun, minus the planes randomly flying off into the middle of nowhere occasionally.  I like using Ju87s and A20s, and the fighters serve their purpose well.  tactical bombers as a whole don't really serve a purpose, as the only real advantage I see is that smaller aa can't hit them, which usually isn't an issue anyway.  All in all, I would love this game if some of the things with odd logic were fixed, but until then I just get pissed everytime I fight in mountains and get cut off for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent sequel, but really brings nothing new to the table, but refinement of systems.  The upgrades and unit purchases are now down to a science.  This works.The combat system and air systems are good.The campaign allows for some branching, including the options to select or avoid a-historical paths.Where this game missed the mark is they could have made it much more dynamic.  Take the African campaign, for example.  Instead of having the traditional historical battles all play out, they could have had dynamic pathing to where you fought offensive or defensive battles in Libya or Egypt, depending upon results of the previous battle.  So, the see-saw desert war could have been one of your own making instead of BattleAxe-->Crusader-->Gazala-->El Alamein, etc...The way the game plays is you MUST win ever battle or the campaign ends.  PERIOD.  And I disagree that a dynamic campaign is too difficult to do.  You have a map and either A) Attack or B) Defend, and your unit/point selection matches the timeframe of the game you're in.  Why didn't they do this?So, a worthwhile purchase but could have been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is worthy of a recommendation. Sane gameplay, good graphics, no frills, but also not primitive (after all, games should be beautiful). Interesting campaign scenarios, with a branching plot, which gives an excuse to play again. Funny characters of advisers who even manage to twist novels there). Convenient settings of the general's perks, with wide possibilities of changes to your taste. A rare advantage, among such games - useful heroes. It is very interesting to figure out how to apply them better and to whom to attach them. I liked the detailed detailing of the campaigns, where there are many episodes. This is what I've wanted for a long time. The disadvantage can be considered, except that, relatively low historical accuracy. "Order of battle", wins this. The game is good, very addictive and has a lot of reserves for exploring the "depths" and releasing a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent upgrade from the classic Panzer General game I used to play as a kid. It's pure strategy and order of operations. Some mechanics are a little hard to get used to such as pulling off a mass attack, but it quickly becomes second nature after a few runs. The game is quite challenging even on normal mode. You're encouraged to use interesting features like putting units into reserve. Managing the economics of the game is quite challenging but overall well balanced. I do wish there was a bit more deviation in the campaigns based on your degree of victory. Panzer general would give you "major" or "minor" victories that would determine the course of the war, but this version seems to go more so by win/lose conditions. Being able to select your approach is nice, but leaves me doubting and regretting not being able to see more. Overall, I highly rank this game. It has just enough graphics and sound to keep the combat fun and is still all about the strategy I fell in love with playing PG.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

My AA has no effect on the Hurricanes. In clear terrain Norwegian Mountain infantry inflicts twice as many damage on my Wehrmacht, my Grenadier, or any of my Panzers, even after being soften up with my artillery. _childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: So, obviously this game is a hexagonal grid strategy game with a turn based system. It is also very obviously a Wehraboo jerk off and tbh? All of that is fine. The mechanics (with an exception I get to later) is great and it isn't even remotely subtle about being Wehraboo food and I have no issues with that.The maps, terrain and units are very varried and fun to play around with, the AI isn't ground breaking but you're still going to face a decent challenge if you intent to get the alt history scenarios. The only thing that bothers me mechanically are the self propelled guns and TDs. They basically just function as cheaper tanks that can either only fight against tanks or infantry. This is really weird in my opinion and feels off (it also makes them completely useless imo).All of the above is largely fine tho, what really bothers me is how incredibly lazy the game is. The first point where you can go ahistorical is in Africa where you can sink the HMS Hood and press all the way into the caucasus from where you advance to moscow. After the fall of the USSR you begin operation Sea Lion. Here we face the issue that greatly upset me:My victory in Africa was completely worthless and was ignored, apparently Italy was invaded from Africa like irl despite the fact that I took it all. There is also no reasonable way for the Allies to retake Africa without killing the player in Russia as your supply lines go through Iraq etc.It was never mentioned that Africa fell and I think the devs just didn't care to adjust the Sea Lion mission in case that the player goes to Africa. In other words, I just wasted a lot of time on an alt history scenario that has absolutely zero impact.You may also remember how I mentioned that I sank the Hood? The only Admiral class ship ever built? Yeah guess what was back at Sea Lion. Not even my sinking of the Hood mattered even though it should've already been sunk by the Bismarck anyways. Why does the Hood exist in 1943? You also for some reason get the Bismarck so I guess that also survived.After that absolute mood killer we go on to the naval invasion of the USA which is obviosly the most absurd scenario so far but I mean, I already said that the game is a Wehraboo jerk off. The invasion of the USA is exceptionally boring. It just drags on forever and the USA basically puts up no resistance. I must also add that I did not finish the US invasion because of how long and boring it is.The naval mechanics are also absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Submarines are near invincible with I believe only one ship type being capable of damaging it. You also always have the same level of experience on your ships and for some reason experience matters much more on naval units than anythign else. The Hood can effortlessly 1v2 your Bismarcks and even the H class you get for the USA is hardly able to put up a fight against anything. This is not to say that any of the three naval engagements I had were hard, they were just boring. I think I could recommend the game if ANYTHING you did mattered but at this moment it doesn't. Don't bother to go to Africa, you will just waste prestige (yes you have to buy the alternative missions with prestige). I can look past the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ navy and I can look past the fact that TDs and SPGs are worthless and illogical, I cannot look past the fact that I spent hours on an extended scenario for it to not matter in the slightest. It is otherwise a fun game but this is a dealbreaker for me, especially considering he horrendously high price of the game and the alt missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: As advertised, the gameplay is mostly unchanged from PC2. Some nice additions add complexity to this version but all in all in a positive direction.  But what made PC1 special was the constant pressure to succeed rapidly so the overall campaign didn't pay a price for your dallying around. Win this battle but lose too many units? You'll never see Moscow. Win this battle but take too long so you conserve units? You'll never see Moscow. Pressure, pressure, pressure.In PC2 you won't be faced with this situation. Imagine doing all the above right and taking Moscow and when the next scenario in the campaign boots your introduction to the situation says, "Ach du lieber, we don't know what happened, we are needing to defend the Vistula crossings you took took at the start of the campaign. And we don't have any points to refresh your units let alone upgrade them. Golly, look at all the Russians. Good luck, see you at Nuremburg! ".So to me all campaign flavor is gone. And that was the best part.VIf you like playing the discrete battle scenarios, give this a whirl. If looking for a strategic reason to be fighting those battles based on previous performance?  Pass on by.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

Recommended to buy on a sale for sure if you want to play through a fun campaign, which has branches and things to allow for multiple playthroughs. Not to mention I enjoyed getting the hang of it then beating it on the hardest level, which was challenging and also enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: 9/10Well at first I really thought this was not as good as PzCorps 1, the campaign is bland and graphics improvement is not that important especially for a hex based wargame, but after being addicted to it for some time I really started to actually enjoy the game more and moreFirst, how many games nowadays, especially these wargames, offers player to actually paint their armies. I know it is actually sounds dumb af but apart from dawn of war I can't think of any other games that easily allows a player to customize his army, I can have a kv2 with a soviet paint job fighting as germany in britain, and even a Maus in US paint job...As a wacky modeller myself I really appreciate that and...for historical accuracy? Well who cares about that when you can have gay stripes Tigers running around....very fun indeed...Secondly, the UI so many complain about is just not true...Much better and improved from PzCorps 1. I never played Pz General (probably because I am a bit too young for that) so I cannot compare to that classic, but for the bonus to actually show themselves like 'mass attack' and 'recon' is really good. My first 100 hrs of PzCorps 1 is just fooling around without knowing those things really exist, especially support fire from arty and aa but this game shows everything, the tutorial is much clearer and it WILL help noobs to learn about all mechanics...Alright, here comes the good part, aka trophies of war. Look at my 1200+ captured enemy tanks in my personal museum from derpy trubias which is basically a tractor with a gun to the mighty kv2 and char 2c. They are especially good because you can actually field them and watch them shooting around (Well I guess I just love watching little army men blowing each other up, which this game graphics did a great job). Sure in HOI you can go capture enemy stuff with wrench battalion (I know it is maintainence but I love to call it wrench btn for some reason) but it never really felt too different with your own, usually you just send those pieces of junk thru lend lease to some TPLACs to get rid of them. But here it definitely works in a positive way. I know it sounds ahistorical and would be a logistical nightmare if you run a char b1, a somua s35, a pz3, a pz4, a kv2, a verdeja2, a matilda2 and a cruiser mk4 in your army but if you really care about historical accuracy and stuff like that then go read and research on actual history stuff rather than sit in the basement and try to 'reenact' thru a game that is made so that people can have FUN with it. It is like playing an all-boyz ork army or all dreadnought space marine army. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing!9/10- Nice Graphics, they go very well with the theme of the game.- Good soundtrack and decent sound effects.- Complex combat system that is VERY easy to learn and incredibly satisfying to use- Impeccable unit variety and I love the way you can tailor each of your units with a transport of your choice.- Despite a large variety of units, Individual units feel very important on their own. I kept finding myself looking for my veteran troops and they are very easy to find thanks to the UI and the fact each unit has a unique name.- The integration of Land, Naval, and Air combat feels very good. Very well balanced, in my opinion.- Terrain modifiers and special terrain features/traits add to the balance and satisfaction when you get to use them to your advantage.- Personally, I really love the General Trait selection. Being able to pick between good traits and bad traits feels very nice and it gives you a bit more compromise rather than just having buffs for being a human player.- If there's anything I can say is bad about this game, is MAYBE the AI. It feels like they do not prioritize their targets in such a way to really cripple me. However, maybe I am not taking into account the Fog of War. Perhaps they are indeed making the best decision they can based on what they see. However, it is not like a human player and therefore doesn't possess "game sense". Overall I think the AI is OK. Very enjoyable to play against, but definitely lacks a challenge. Turning up the difficulty level did it for me (:- There are many campaigns and historical and non-historical battles available, and although you can only play Germany campaigns, the editor is a nice solution to any fears you may have of "lack of content".- There's mod support. Again, amazing!9/10Will add my thoughts on the multiplayer once I play some more of that!

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit that I bought this game initially just for the cool looking new models of the units, expecting the game to be just a "glammed" up version of Panzer Korp and its predecessor, the old Panzer General game from SSI. My assumption was that essentially this would be the same game and in a sense, it is; at least in spirit.BUT... this is not the same game as its forerunners. It has much in common in terms of the basic mechanics but it is in many ways much better. Specifically:1/. Your units are no longer "uber" and you cannot simply overrun opponents like butter in the old games.2/. The AI plays a lot better and it really pays to recon the situation and plan your moves in advance.3/. Entrenched opponents are tough making objectives a lot more challenging to pry from their positions.4/. The terrain can make a big difference to successful operations.5/. Your air force is, compared to the older games, weaker making the game actually much more challenging. 6/. There are new mechanics such as the tank overrun feature that opens up new tactical opportunities.7/. You can customize units be either changing their skin or adding heroes to improve their performance.8/. Once you get used to the new UI (and it does take some getting used to) it is really decent.9/. The UI gives you the option of examining each tactical situation from a variety of views. Use these lliberally as some enemy support units can be easy to miss otherwise.10/. Units are more role specific so it really pays to use combine arms attacks.11/. The prestige system works differently, forcing you to make hard choices in terms of core unit selection. However, this system does tend to force you to focus on certain types of units and forgo the opportunity of using specialist units such as AA and AT guns.12/. Your commander needs to be set up with characteristics which can alter each campaign's balance. Honestly, I am not that a big a fan of this feature but it is what it is...To re-emphasize,  it more like Panzer Korp on steroids. The cautionary note is that the game does play differently and better in many ways from my limited experience with it. For example, the Norway campaign used to be a real chore but in this reiteration, it is really much, much more fun. Also, each scenario, perceptively at any rate when compared to the same scenarios in the older games are shorter but takes longer to complete. This is actually a good thing.Honestly, I just love what they have done with the game. Not only have the developers brought the game up to contemporary standards but they managed to do it while improving the game play and yet it has not lost its connection with the older games that many of us have loved for so many years.If you have trouble telling the difference between your ME 109 and your Stukas, either zoom in and have a closer look or simply change their skin. I do this also with my Pz IIIs so I don't mistaken them for my Pz IVs.Don't just click and move without planning. The new AI will happily take advantage of any mistakes you make and usually in an intelligent way. The AI isn't perfect by any stretch as strategically it is still weak, but tactically it does seem to do a much better job.My game did crash once; might more be a Windows 10 issue but it did happen. but by the same token, I am not uninstalling the original Panzer Korp. The two games play differently enough to keep both; which is a good thing. Panzer Korp 2 is not  but it is really nicely done and well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one for me to review.  It is a good WWII strategy game.  It's Panzer Corps and Panzer General-esque, but I don't really know if it is a true sequel to those games.   Those games were easy to learn, hard to master.  I feel like Panzer Corps 2 is complex to learn and hard to master.  New mechanics have their own learning curve and feel separate from the base game.  I don't like the RNG hero mechanic dictating your strategy.  The encircle mechanic trivializes holdout defensive units, and feels unhistoric. It does lead to other playstyles though.Maybe that was necessary.  Maybe for players like me, who already mastered the mechanics in Panzer Corps I, this was the only way to make a sequel interesting.  I don't know.  I think it's a good game.  I think it does somethings better than PC1, but as a strategy game I don't think it's as good as the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, extremely well executed.  If you like a corps/divisional game like Panzerblitz or Panzer Leader, this is the closest you are going to get!  After playing for an additional 339 hours, I would still recommend the game, but for SINGLE player only.  The developer has really fallen short regarding multiplayer.  They do not actively support the community when it comes to making new scenarios for multiplayer and it is overly complicated to get them installed (heard from many of my friends who play the game but arent Windows saavy).  Additionally, while adding new DLC for single player, none of it comes for multiplayer.  Once you play the less than a dozen multiplayer scenarios, you are stuck with random games that end up feeling the same over and over.  If they would put just a little more effort into multiplayer, the game would be so much better.  Lastly, the armies are not balanced well and while this can be made up for in scenarios through design, in multiplayer, it is apparent that they believe the only armies worth a crap were the Germans and Soviets.
