_childDocuments_.review: It was a long wait for this game, after the excellent Panzer Corp. I was therefore expecting big things. The graphics look nice, the sound is fine and matches the gameplay. But the playability that got me going back time and again for PC1 is just not there.  Each campaign game seems more of a race to hit every option perfectly to get to the goal with not a turn to spare. As such it seemed an exercise in clock watching more than tactics or enjoying the battle. The multiplayer started off glitchy but improved on that aspect with patches. A bewildering array of artillery and anti-tank support fire makes many moves completely futile, if not completely suicidal  - and with little finance to replenish the troops there is little option but to stare at the enemy and hope they get bored before you do. A battle I ended up happy to lose on many occaisons. Perhaps this game rewards a great deal more research and planning than the previous one, there is a lot more detail but in doing so it takes away much of the enjoyment  - at least for this player.  I did like the addition of heroes with special abilities and the map editor looks like it may see some good mulitplayer content being created by users. I will give it a bit more time, but to date this game feels more of a chore than a good time to be honest. I've certainly not rushed to play it since the initial discovery day or two, even going back to play the well worn original battles in favour.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done.  I almost didn't buy this game because I have been steering away from games with dlc.  But Panzer Corps 2 addresses all the complaints that I had with Panzer Corps 1 and the developers added in some elements that really enhance game play.Positives:1. A significant amount of content (scenarios) which make the purchase worthwhile.  Hopefully, the devs will keep up the content quantity and quality in their dlcs to come.2. Excellent organization of information so it is easier to play and follow the game now.  UI takes a little bit of getting used to when transitioning from Panzer Corps 1 but once you get the hang of it then it becomes an asset to the game.3. Great replayability in the use of new game mechanics.4. A Manual.  Any game that has a manual anymore gets a big thumbs up from me.  As the matter of fact, the manual for Panzer Corps 2 has really helped me understand Panzer Corps 1 a lot better.5. Very customizable game.  Not just the editor and random scenarios but also the main screen.  Good job devs on that one.*I'm sure that I could go on about positives but I'm getting tired and old.  :-)Negatives:I can't really find any here as far as I'm concerned.  I'm honestly surprised that anyone is posting a negative review here.Three Thumbs Up on a one scale.  Glad I made the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game that rewards real life tactics. A huge plus is that you can set the core game rules. The AI generally does what one might expect, with the sole odd exception that arty doesn't always lead an attack. I expect that will be patched eventually. The devs are active and open to constructive feedback on the steam forum.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the base game, and found it severely lacking. Promises were made. We've listened to the feedback and we're gonna improve. Now with the first DLC coming out. None of the improvements that were talked about made it into the DLC.Promise and advertising about different degrees of victory: not in the game (secondary objectives aren't degrees of victory, and there are precious few of them).Promise about proper end briefings: not in the game (summaries from wikipedia aren't a proper end briefing)Improvement of sound, like units firing etc: not in the game.No improvement on graphics issue and exceptionally high GPU usage.No balancing of heroes or game prestige economyNo improvement on modifying difficulty. (Panzer corps 1 had sliders for each aspect: prestige/enemy strength etc. Why doesn't PzC2 have this?)DLC is still riddled with bugs, even a week after field marshall users have had access. (like the deadly grip specialty not working) Why doesn't any self respecting publisher test their own game before releasing anymore?Providing the player with info is still one of the weak points in this game: Why didn't you tell people in the base game about the prestige wall unexpectedly and randomly put into the game without any explanation?It would for example be nice to know the "rommel" or Europe on a shoestring" difficulty doesn't work in the DLC before starting the game.I could go on and on, but i think the picture is clear.Sadly the first DLC sees the game make the bare minimum of improvements on the base game. And it looks as if it was done reluctantly so. In case of end briefings, done so bad, almost as if to spite players for not liking their game concept of not having end briefings. It shows a lack of....imagination or the will to really tell a compelling and exciting story or immerse people within WW2. To sum it all up: the base game failed to excite me to play. The DLC is slightly better, but not by a longshot enough for me to actually recommend this game. Smaller teams/budgets like Starni Games with Panzer Strategy and the makers of Unity of Command 2 show they can do far more, and better than PzC2 did with less resources.

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction : the whole saga of strategy games like honeycombs has been ground by me, games with hexagonal maps have always been good and will be good ,25 years of experience in this section , I know what i am talking about.1.Dune 2 Amiga 5002.Panzer general 1 SSI on 436SX (first PC with NC System before windows)3.Panzer general 2 which was for plenty of years on the market with plenty of mods and many other generals at the time.I remember when Panzer Corps 1 was new and many admins complained about the cheated 2D graphics in Panzer corps 1, despite this I bought the entire saga on CD and I have it to this day and I do not regret it.Review : Panzer Corps 2 is a great game and I do not regret buying it, it is the best of all editions and fills all the holes and gaps that were in earlier versions, personalization of commanders, units, camouflages, experience and prototypes, as well as new solutions such as political successes for big points that can give us transfers of famous commanders between front lines and new tank models for testing plus Main general perks before each campaign.We also have a large number of mods and cosmetics for the game and free campaigns as a mods.Only one problem is with Slitherine Ltd. which uses every next mod as a money grabber and they shouldn't be as expensive as they are, it's something that frustrates and starts to discourage you from playing.If you are a fan of the Panzer General saga then buy this game and don't look at the money and you will be happy , this is the way.Game 100% ScorePublisher 10% Score for poor customer service which is stabbing you in the back financially and asking to pay pay extra for every extra extras which should be extra free as standard content ,no one buys a car and then buys an engine and wheels for a premium price later on.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving the sequel so far, takes what worked in Panzer Corps 1 and improves upon it in almost every case.  The main campaign is huge, with multiple branching paths which should give the game a lot of replayability.  Some of the unit changes have really helped, certain units like anti-air and anti-tank now seem to have much better roles.  The core army make-up and slot costs for units makes the army composition more interesting as you can't just take the best unit each time.  One of the best features from the first game that is back,  you can make the game as difficult (or easy as you like).  Turn Limits, Fog of War, Undo Actions can all be turn on/off at the users discretion as well as some off the added difficulties (less credits, stronger enemies, etc.).  Also when starting a campaign you can select certain bonuses for your army (such as more credits when capturing a flag) but there is a cost associated with them, and you have to take a negative trait to offset it (such as poor mechanics, some units will lose there actions on your turn..... don't take this, it sucks!!!) which add some flavor and again replay value.The 3D graphics look great, and you can customize the view of your units with a bunch of different paint/camouflage patterns.  Minor quibble is that air units can be a little difficult to see when the battle field gets crowded, but there is a separate view to handle that.All in all a fantastic game, if you like turn based strategy games, this is as good as it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Corps 2 improves the traditional panzer gerneral series by combining the best concepts of the past and  adding some significant improvements. For me the most important aspect is that units consume different degrees of core slots with more advanced units taking a bigger share. The consequence is that your army is a mix of strong and average / old units. Army composition requires careful balancing now. In addition to that new rules now have made recon units and especially anti tank units finally useful resulting in a more divers army.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - Recommend for the enjoyment of rock/paper/scissor; with tanks ruling the plains vs infantry guarding the cities, hills, and trees, and artillery as the glass cannons with low initiative attacking second.  The scenarios suck you in to complete them like a puzzle, adding a hero once per turn randomly.    However, even with good graphics and excellent mechanics, after awhile you don't believe the campaign or that you are a general.  You wipe out half your tanks in one attack, no problem, one turn they are up full health with elite troops.   Lose  our top tank unit, no problem, we'll send you a full regiment of the best tank unit by the end of the day across the ocean in Africa.   Lose all your units or none of them as long as you take 3 hexes of the map in 20 turns, "great job, Herr General." However, doing well doesn't mean anything but "$".  Completing early only gives you "$" called prestige, it doesn't affect your future.  Oh, yea, and here's a randomly generated hero, given each scenario, not dependent upon your play.  He's either nearly useless or one that will carry the game ensuring all enemies retreat.     I chose to play through the campaign, completing scenarios 10 turns early, defeating every Russian unit on the board, and still it led to Berlin.  Hugh?  No draw or stalemate with the Russians.  The meta narrative left me wanting some reason to actually win, like I did in every region, Poland, France, Africa, and Russia.  It felt rushed and unfinished overall, but the base mechanics and 3d graphics are better than the last game.  Felt more like a graphic update on a game, adding heroes and small supply changes, with worse campaign play and no improvement in multiplayer.  The multi-player doesn't allow campaign play.   Give it a play and wait for the player community to get it beyond the C grade in a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best turn-based war games out there. I recommend all the DLCs, I personally have gone from Spanish Civil War to Amerika 1946 and it was quite a ride. Not going to sugar coat it, but this game is not easy even on Major. I did it on Colonel and had to do a number of battle more than once to get the most out of my army. The story arch is well done and the Alternate History is compelling. I wonder if there will be another DLC based on a conflict between japan and Germany.....you know the two biggest kids on the block, their going to fight eventually. You really grow attached to your units, bringing them through one campaign to another. If you love this genre and do not play this, well, your missing out.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow,what could have been. This could have been a great game,as it is it hardly compares to the original. There is no way to compete with the russian army. Your constantly outnumbered 5 to 1, which is okay but  you can not earn enough prestige to repair or expand your army between scenarios. and thats if you manage to reach all the objectives before turns expire which is near impossible for nearly all the scenarios. German tanks are a joke with really no real value, most battles are led with infantry with tanks in a back up role because they are ineffective unless attacking a depleted unit. The biggest problem is the lack of prestige when you do manage to win. After repairing your army there is nothing left for upgrades or the purchase of new equipment. They added some really cool stuff like earning hero's after scenarios along with the medals you earned in PC1. It is fun, but its replay abilities fall way short of the first version, not worth the 50 dollar price tag maybe half that. I wish I could recommend it but cant, after 200 hours of game play I'm finished with it where as I can still have a good time with the older game.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing all the SSI Panzer General titles on my 286sx (I think).  This game is its spiritual successor.  I enjoy this game so much.  I have all the DLCs and wait with baited breathe for 1945 DLC.  Graphics are very nice.  Game play is challenging.  One of the game mechanics that I fondly remember from Panzer General was the upgrading and heroes.  Panzer Corps 2 has that and added a few things.  The "slot," part was a bit hard to understand at first, but I got the hang of it and like it now.If you like Turn-based games and WWII military vehicles you'll like this game.  This is my first review of a game and this is my favorite.  Only two negatives.  I wish there were more scenarios in each of the Axis operations campaigns.  I'd pay for that.  The other other Negative is that unit experience caps at lvl 5 with 5,000.  It should never cap, but get harder to  exponentially harder i.e., lvl 6 costs 2,000, lvl 7 costs 5,000, lvl 8 costs 10,000.  You'd probably never reach those exp point levels but it invests you in your units.  Same with the awards there shouldn't be caps.

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 6 1/2 hours to complete the tutorial.With googling and using the forum and so on.If you liked Panzer General, yeah, get it. For all others:You have to create a core army of different types like infantry, tank, recon, bombers, fighters, AA, artillery and so on to be able to win the battles.You keep your core units during a campaign and they collect XP over time and get better and better.You can upgrade a unit to a new variant of the same type.Meaning, you can upgrade normal infantry to pioneers or old tanks to new tanks, but not a recon tank to a fighter airplane.Everything is turn bases, so there is no stress.You'll want to weaken enemies with bombers and artillery, then either use pioneers to attack infantry in close combat or use tanks to kill them in flat terrain. Attack a unit from multiple sides for bonuses etc..It is fun.The interface is good.The units are a bit ... the same. I sometimes don't see enemy units because they are mixed with mine or don't see mine because they are in an area where they are not easy to see.No idea why anyone would create units from different sides that look so much the same that you really have to look with intent to be sure.Nevertheless, it IS turn based, so you will not be in a hurry and there should be no problem.If you like tactics and 2nd world war and a little bit of management, get it. It is good.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a big wargamer by any means. I usually find them dry, and without good direction, and painfully obtuse and occasionally even pointless. There's plenty of depth - more than your Wargrooves and Advance Wars, about on par with Iron Storm (Sega Saturn). If you like Turn Based Strategy games, but perhaps never actually got into a war game, PC2 is probably a great choice.Panzer Corps 2 is a war game, but it's also a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: TBS isn't for everyone which is very important to know. It could be boring for some people or it could be a blast to waste your time on. If you wanted a good introduction do the more serious aspect of TBS games, I would highly recommend this one. It's got quite the difficult campaign which adds a really interesting element to the bowl for difficulty wise where in the beginning of any campaign or even starting first to the last campaign; You start with a basic early war (if you start in Poland for early war troops) army and depending on how your units do and gaining Prestige (Money), live or die that's how they will be in the next mission. You get to upgrade them between mission and heal them if you have the money so hopefully you have some funds saved up or you'll be attacking never ending Russian hordes with your batter up troops.     Multiplayer on the other hand is really fun! There's all sorts of scenarios to choose and if you'd like to have custom settings, there's an entire setup with randomly generated maps. Every year date will have their own factions depending on the WW2 era too but there's one major thing about this game which makes it so enticing for multiplayer.... FFA! You can have up to 8-way Free For All's with all of your friends! With full on A.I. support as well so you can still experience those big battles even without so many people. There's plenty to do in this game and it really just depends on your willingness to purchase this game at it's full price. If your not too sure, I'd recommend waiting on a potential sale. Great game but rather pricey!

_childDocuments_.review: PC2 improves upon PC1 to a significant degree.Better:+ Supply no longer takes an action turn+ Recon as a new mechanic+ Overrun creates a real sense of Blitzkrieg+ General traits bring in some customization optionsWorse:- Degrees of victory removed. _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. As a fan of Panzer General 1 & 2 and a fan of the prior Panzer Corps release, this game is to PC what PG2 was to PG1. Better graphics, better game play, and more options to customize your army in ways previously unimaginable. Heroes and medals have more effect, encirclement, overrun, reserves, overstrength from map 1, anti-tank guns matter more, prestige management - it's all better and makes for a challenging game which is more interesting. The soundtrack is good and various effects are satisfying to hear and see. No more guessing where indirect and counter fire is coming from, surrenders actually matter in free equipment, and so on. Oh and instead of number of core units you get core points which you can spend to customize your army. Depending on your leader traits, some units cost less or your tank will easily tackle rivers. Maybe upgrading to the latest tracked transport isn't worth a core point? Maybe stick to horses and truck and use the extra couple points for that fancy mobile artillery which costs 4. Maps start much smaller. Comparing Poland in PC to this game, it's split into two areas of operation - North and South. But by Leningrad the maps get much larger. Prestige is harder to manage. Often one has to balance between reinforcing and waiting until deployment. The UI is better but it takes some getting used to. Some of the clicking around and hitting 'I' for information when everything else has a button is weird. Update: Found it! I am hoping for more campaigns and more of everything. If you're a fan of the hex style, turn based combat then this is the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of PzC1, this game improves on it in a lot of areas, it now features a supply system and surround/encircle mechanics, units have varying core slot costs, making you choose between more smaller units to fill out your army or fewer powerful units, aircraft now return to their home airfield at the beginning of each round, you can customize your units with heroes instead of them being locked to the unit they generated in.... All in all if you were a fan of PzC1 or Order of Battle, this is probably a good purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried liking this game. First, all the things that I enjoy: - The battle mechanics are cool. Beyond "you have five HP, I do six damage, you die", there's encirclement, fire support (Arty and AA), suppression, fortification... which adds a nice learning curve and a ton of opportunities.- The units: I've only played a couple of scenarios but there's a bunch of different infantry, artillery, planes and of course tanks that are all good at different things and, again, create options.- The air force mechanics in particular. You place your planes in an airfield and they have a range. So once a turn the move from their airfield to a specific spot (in range) and take an action. At the end of the turn they return to their airfield. This is great because in your headcanon this covers the need for planes to refuel instead of just hovering over your troops indefinitely. Even better, it forces you to conquer strategic positions like airfields to ensure air support and deny it to the enemy which adds a great aspect!However, what killed the game for me is the *drumroll* TURN LIMIT. Imagine Xcom with a turn limit! Imagine Jagged Alliance with a turn limit. Yes, that. -->- You push a specific area and realize there's more opposition than expected? Prepare to save scum because retreat, reform and reinforce will eat turns and then you run out of turns and lose. - You just conquered a position and want to continue your attack on the next position? Just take whatever is in range because forming a task force and starting a concerted push will eat turns and then you run out of turns and lose.- You need to conquer three objectives in three different directions? Prepare to attack them simultaneously with the bare minimum of troops because, guess what, three separate, consecutive concerted assaults WILL EAT TURNS AND THEN YOU RUN OUT AND LOSE FOR ♥♥♥♥'S SAKE!So what does this mean for gameplay? Essentially it turns the game into a puzzle game. You restart every map until you know all enemy positions and units and know the optimal unit setup and moves. Then you execute the strategy that you know will solve the level in the required amount of turns. Releasing a strategy game in 2020 that has a "correct" way of beating a level is just sad. Can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to Panzer Corps 2 but I was truly disappointed in the game. I basically played this game under a different name 25 years ago but that game was better then this example. The music score was 10 times better, unit historical information was available with just a highlight of the unit. There was even historical battle videos of the units firing during combat when you started the combat phase of the game. Also at times historical videos played during unit movement of the actual unit. The biggest disappointment is in the poor effort that was put into the combat phase and general balancing of the units in game play. I will give a few examples of failure or poor design but the are many more just to numerous to cover. The German Flak 88 was the most versatile weapon on the German side during WWII not only was it a great anti-aircraft weapon it also excelled in anti-tank and light artillery. The way the game restricts the 88 in game is just horrible and the 88 armed tanks is just not accurate either. The German 88 was powerful yes but the true fear of the 88 was its killing range it was not a knife fighting weapon. Another point I would like to make is Infantry in open ground no matter the anti-tank weapons they have can stand against armor in open movement combat. The Sherman while not the best anti--tank weapon was a great infantry support killer. Watch the Chieftains hatch on Sherman's what tanks do to infantry in the open ground combat. Last point what in the heck did they think they were doing with Combat engineers???? I'm sorry while they do one hell of a job in their limited area of combat expertise in setting up bridges or crossings, preparing defenses or penetrating enemy fortification positions they are not combat infantrymen period if they are not able to use their engineering equipment from prepared defense they are just ground beef against Combat infantrymen. This is just my opinion but after 25 years I just expected better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like the old-school Panzer General 2, but with better graphics and more features. Also, I like the fact that it's easy to change the variables in the excel unit file (C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Panzer Corps 2\PanzerCorps2\Content\Data\units.cvs). Just open up the unit file with excel and change things to your liking; for instance, I like to give my heavy infantry (grenadiers) the machine gun trait  (traits are on the 29th tab to the right labeled traits). The possibilities are limitless, change attack strength, movement, faction, year available, etc.. I even played one time swapping many of the German units for American units (I also changed the flag to American by editing the factions.cvs file...remember to always save the original files, so you can always switch back in case you mess up). Again, I really like the fact they made this game easy to mod units.Below is a list of modifications I like to make to various units:Fallschirmjager - Camouflage trait (because paratroopers are sneaky as hell...I know, because I used to be one)Gebirgsjager - PhasedMovement trait (because alpine infantry walk past the enemy like ninjas)Grenadier - MachineGun trait (because heavy infantry uses heavy weapons...hello...MG 34)Kradschutzen - I like to change their class to infantry and add the Overrun trait (nothing funner than watching a heavily armed military biker gang over-run a group of weak units...oh the sound of Harleys (actually BMW R12 Combos) and machine guns bring happy tears to my eyes).As I previously mentioned, this game is wicked fun and modding units makes it even more wickedly fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but I'd say it is pretty tough.  It plays very similar to Order of Battle but the time limit is shorter which makes it all quite challenging. It can be almost impossible if you bring the wrong troops (like too many tanks into Norway).  The budgeting of prestige is also something to get used to.  If you use too much of it in a current battle you might be understrength in the next one.  So even if you win a battle you might need to redo it because you spent your prestige poorly.That's a long way to say the game can be frustrating but just keep trying different things and you'll figure it out. _childDocuments_.review: So, I played lots of similar games: Panzer General, Panzer General 2, Fantasy General, People's General, and of course, Panzer Corps. Panzer Corps was easily the best of them all. I have all the campaigns and I have played them all and loved them. So, my expectations for this game were for it to be a Panzer Corps, but with new mechanics... Unfortunately, the 3D virus has gotten to Flashback Games / Slitherine. Why? For getting some new players, because of 3D? Great, but maybe you will also lose a few of the old players....The BAD:- because of the 3D graphics and view, it's very hard to distinguish units at a glance. All infantry units look almost the same. In order to see them easily, you have to resort to ugly workarounds, like: give engineers/pioneers red camo and regular infantry blue camo. This looks ugly as hell, but at least works.- tanks and planes have exactly the same issue: good luck finding out which is the Ju87 and which is the BF109. Good luck finding out which is Panzer 3 and which is Panzer 4. (hint - use red/blue camo trick again)- because of 3D, a lot of times you select another unit, unless you zoom in. If you zoom in, you lose the view of the entire battlefield...- 3D units look great ONLY on very high settings. Even so, the sprite based graphics in Panzer Corps 1 look crisper and you can tell at a glance which unit is which. For small objects, 3D graphics WILL NEVER LOOK BETTER THAN SPRITES! NEVER!- Panzer Corps 1 runs great on an old laptop, so I used to play in bed, on the couch, etc. (It's an I5 460 with integrated graphics and 6 GB RAM). It's absolutely impossible to play Panzer Corps 2 on that laptop, on lowest settings. Even if it looks absolutely terrible on those settings, it's still not playable... IT'S A TURN BASED GAME, FFS!- 3D units have strange proportions. Of course the infantry appears very large compared to tanks and airplanes, but that's acceptable because you couldn't see them if they were proportionate. But, at least inside a class, the proportions should be more realistic. The British MK VI looks bigger than Panzer 3/4 ???????? Come on...The GOOD: all the new mechanics- the new plane mechanic is great, airfields are very important now- the Anti Tank units are finally very useful and they bring variation to the game- the different artillery features are also great, you need to decide if you buy a high caliber artillery which could defend against both armor and soft units, but which is very expensive and takes a lot of slots, or stay with lower caliber artillery which can only protect against soft units- the leader traits are very interesting, you can give yourself different challenges- the unit variety is great- the heroes bring very effective modifications to units, a lot more than the old heroes from Panzer Corps 1- the unit slots mechanic is very challenging and makes you try units you wouldn't try in Panzer Corps 1So, even if basically I have a lot of PROS and only one CON (3D graphics), I cannot recommend this game. Call me old school, whatever. But I know that I had weekends when I played Panzer Coprs 1 for 4-5 hours at a time and I cannot play Panzer Corps 2 for more than 1 hour because it's very tiring... It's tiring to try to see which unit is which. It's tiring to select a plane instead of a tank, and so on.I have the Pre-Release Field Marshal Edition, but I cannot see myself buying more addons.The ideal game would have been Panzer Corps 2 with all the new changes, but with the Panzer Corps 1 sprite graphics. Maybe a patch? One can hope....

_childDocuments_.review: Its great. I read some negative reviews by some old pricks same age as me apparently who spill their hate cuz the game does not do 1 or 2 things exactly the same as the old games and who claim that there was nothing new. Duck them. There is plenty of new great features and mechanics that really innovate the game. my favourites: AT and AA guns finally are worth buying as they support same as artillery. the slots system rewards you for using older equpiment, you cant have that snowflake tiger only corps anymore. air force does not hang around a hex like a statue anymore but flies back and forth from missions. troops next to each other help each other out with support fire or special abilities. tanks overrun again as in dynasty general. encirclement is a way to pocket whole areas. _childDocuments_.review: 66 hours into the game I have some comments, pros and cons compared to PC1 (200+ hours).Pros:Panzers can now overrun again (hint: try to optimize a single pazer, and you will see it blitz through as many units as it have ammo in one round after just a few missions). This is so cool and is like playing the old Panzer General.Planes are much less effective now. Only used 2 bombers total, but 4 fighters to keep the opposition down.Cons:Infantry and artillery are not really developed through the game. You end up using mostly the same as in the first mission.Despite all the diversity of units, the point buy system limits your use of new exciting units severly. This is perhaps my biggest regret. The best end-game composition seems to be 4 overpowered tanks, 4 starter pioneers, 4 starter artillery. +2 AA (again starter units as the 88s are the best, and the planes mentioned above). Everything now serves as support for your uber-tanks. Just as it did in the old Panzer general.They actually cut down the number of missions from the magnificent Grand Campaign DLC we all played in PC1. I guess they save that grand experience to the endless DLC's in Steam games we all dread so much.Well I did sound a bit negative here, but I really enjoyed the game. There are just some things that could be better (in my subjective opinion). BTW: Be sure to disengage the Nvidia in-game utilities as they crash the game all the time. Just a hint.Try this game if you liked the first PC or if you liked the old Panzer General. It actually reminds me a lot of Panzer General 2 where they also did the 3D trick. Here it just works a bit better. And the starting campaign is rather cool, with some fun alternative history missions at the end. Thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely the most authentic unit interactions game of its genre on the market today! For the first time: Artillery primarily suppresses rather than kills (a necessary action to minimize attack losses)- but should be able to remove all remaining movement points from infantry for that turn;- but should be able to provide defensive support fire/FDF (Final Protective Fire) WITHIN RANGE (vice    adjacent) IF remained stationary during turn;Anti-aircraft artillery (AA) primarily suppresses rather than kills, and for the first time, a distinction is made    between light AA, able to more effectively engage low altitude/tactical air attacks, and heavier AA- heavy AA (>70 mm) still too lethal versus strategic bombers;Mounted units are now able to move mounted then deploy (but not attack);Significant distinction between Tactical and Strategic bomber effects- but Strategic bombers can't move off their target to simulate massed area bombardments;Anti-tank units now provide AT support fire to adjacent units- but soft attack values too low;

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this even in an ironic way, it's atrocious.The UI is excessively dense for an entry to a saga which has always been quite straightforward.In the graphics department, more of the same: 3D scenarios and units whose level of detail bury essential information no longer accessible at a glance, instead requiring side menus and constantly zooming in. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this sort of game since Panzer General II in 2002 and continued through the years with Panzer General III, Open General and Panzer Corps 1. This definitely still scratches the same itch, BUT it has many new innovations, some truly new and some borrowed (See Open General). The addition of cores slots certainly makes managing your army a more interesting task as even in the older games, usually part way through the campaign your army had no limits due to excess prestige. For those who aren't familiar with the series, it offers a decent blend of tactical/strategic level gameplay, where you take your core force from scenario to scenario in the campaign, upgrading them and getting more experience to get a stronger army, participating in many historical battles. Battles are hex based and turn based. The emphasis is on properly employing combined arms operations to overcome your enemies. The heros also can lead to so truly broken combos for those who like to min/max.The game has many DLC already that offer hours and hours of more content and has built-in support for mods. This game will have legs for many years.

_childDocuments_.review: well what can i say THE COMBAT the combat feels brilliant and the battles flow well. the old panzer corp was fun but the battles could become a slog fest with clunky movement however in panzer corp 2 when you charge a tiger 2 in open terrain and punch a hole in the enemy lines it feels like a tidal wave has broken through a dam and the armour can keep pushing. in short the combat is leagues better The Campaign the campaign at the moment follows all of the major and minor german operations of ww2 giving you hours of world conquest fun with even a few what ifs thrown in.Multiplayer this part of the game is probably the most improved as it not only offers a custom game mode it allow up to 8 player free for all which is one thing you dont generally see in ww2 turn based gamesTHE CON the only thing i can think of is the ability to choose what factions you fight against in the AI skirmish mode as its a bit annoying to fight your own faction sometimes Final Vote 10/10 - hoping for more campaigns in the future all in all Leagues better than Panzer corp 1 and worth the timeNOTE - the Devs have improved most of the bugs and added more features since release this game is just getting better and betterNOTE - 2 - the main feature of this game i love at the moment is the random battle mode as to be honest the campaign i really cant be asked to play as its ww2 at the end of the day but with the recent updates regarding the random battle mode has made the game leagues better and worth the buy

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed feelings about this game to be honest so I want to say up front that this is a good game but it just doesn't scratch the itch for me.  It just isn't as good as the original in my opinion, though there are some really nice changes.Pros:1.  The new graphics are nice, even though I actually like the old style a little more.2.  The new hero system is simply better than the original.  Hero abilities are much more creative than +1 attack or +2 defense.  You can also add them to any unit you want to and move them to another unit for a different scenario.  Very well done and well thought out.3.  Unit purchase system is much improved.  Way better than the original.  Instead of a limit to the number of units you can field you have a point limit and the units cost different points.  For example in the beginning a BF-109e will cost you 3 points but bridging unit will cost you 1 point.  I really liked this because it allows and encourages you to use units that are not really good at combat and you wouldn't have necessarily used in Panzer Corps.4.  The Trait system when you first start the game.  Haven't played around with it too much yet but really liked the ability to take some different traits and give myself some positive and negative traits.5.  The implementation of encirclements is done really well.  The ability to cutoff large pockets of enemy units and just attrit them away is really nice.  Cons:1.  Implementation of air units.  Really don't like this at all.  They seem much less capable compared to how they were in Panzer Corps.  Loved my air force in Panzer Corps and in Panzer Corps 2 you could honestly probably get away with not taking them at all.2.  Graphics, yes they are objectively of higher quality,  but I don't really dig the change.  This is a personal preference and I can easily see a lot of people disagreeing with me.  My biggest gripe is that the more soomed out you are it isn't so easy to tell the difference between a Stuka and a BF-109e.  I also really don't like that you can zoom into the strategic view of the battlefield.  I would prefer it was a separate button.3.  It just isn't the Grand Campaign.  If you have played and enjoyed the Grand Campaign from Panzer Corps, this just doesn't give you the same epic feeling.  Now in some respects that isn't a fair critique because they aren't pretending it is the Grand Campaign and they will most likely release something like that in the future but it is something to consider when buying the game.  If you are looking for the something like the Grand Campaign you may want to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is targeted at veteran war-gamers like myself.After 10 hours of playing this game I was convinced it was the worst in the panzer/allied general/corps games. At 20 hours I realized that it was as good as any of them. At 30 hours I came around to thinking it is the best one out of all of them.They made some really controversial adjustments to the known tried and true formula of the series that I thought were/would be bad at first but turned out to be improvements over all. The game took some of the mechanics from their Order of Battle series and greatly improved upon them. (supply lines turned into encirclement.) And they found a happy medium between Panzer series' short but sweet scenarios and Order's Grand theater size scenarios. And lastly because I hate long reviews I will say that the graphics are beautiful and the level designs are their best yet IMHO. As much as I want to hate Slitherine I have to love them because the games are damn decent despite the insane price tags.

_childDocuments_.review: In general it is an improvement across the board on Panzer Corps 1. Better graphics, better scenarios, better mechanics for the most part. For those complaining about not being able to play US, Russia, etc. in campaign mode yet, I say learn the product and genre you are buying. _childDocuments_.review: PC2 is my go to game when the others just aren't right for the mood. I think being a WWII buff is a big part of it. Overall; as a board game Pnzr Cor 2 excels in realism and strategy. It's unforgiving and relentless AI will keep you vigilant, watching your back always, seeking high ground and cover. Your victories will be joyous and well earned. Your defeats will hurt and have you grasping for reinforcements... losing experienced troops with special skills, having to back up just when you thought you had the advance... humbling to be sure. Micro management is kept to a minimum, units are respectfully rendered both graphically and within their roles. Misuse a certain unit in a certain way... and perish - much the same in actuality. This lends to the games true purpose...  recreating the most epic battles of WWII. The UI is well done, though the strategic map is a bit...underdone. I only use it briefly. It's all I can handle..Options for difficulty are very handy for beginners. Maps and missions are realistic and most are historically referenced. I've gotten though most campaigns on a med diff. I watch the pros on utube - they make it look so easy, yet this game continues to challenge them on some of the most unthinkable difficulty levels. Still, helpful tips and hints to be found there. Daunting game for those not familiar with this genre. But if you loved Axis and Allies (dating myself here) and those types of board games - you will enjoy PC2.  I'm sure now they're known as "Bored Games" - but surprisingly, I find a diverse player base while scrolling forums. I think there could be more content in the base game, reviews for DLC agree - should've been incl...but I'll prob get the DLC's anyway. Different modes of play and choice of nation adds to replay.  Fun and challenging, all elements of warfare come into play with PC2. For this genre of game I give it a 8/10. Price is fair. DLC's often on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Corp 2 has the same addicting 'rock,paper'scissor' tactics as Panzer General, Allied General, People's General and Panzer Corp 1. There have been some rule changes that I initially found confusing, but after a few hours they became second nature. Some of the improvements:1. Purchasing units has an added dimension. In Panzer corp 1 all units cost 1 core point, so you always choose the most powerful units.  But in Panzer corp 2 different units have different numbers of points, so there is more strategy in choosing units. For example small tanks cost 2 points, regular infantry costs 3 points, heavy infantry costs 4 points. So suppose you have 10 points: do you buy 5 tanks, 3 infantry or 2 heavy infantry and 1 tank? You have to examine the objectives and terrain and your style to choose units.2. You can now choose leader traits, both positive and negative, to further customize your army and play style. Do you want stronger infantry or armor? do you want more offensive capability or better defense, or better battlefield intelligence? What are you willing to give up to get your advantage? I have spent hours playing with different possibilities.3. Random scenario generator means endless replay.4. Better graphics. This is just bling, but bling is nice. When you blow up a tank it sits on the battlefield and burns. The closeups are amazing.5. You might think that the panzer general/panzer corp scenarios have been done to death. How many times can you invade Poland without it getting boring? But in panzer corp 2, while you still have the same strategic situation, the tactical situation is different in each scenario. So it does not feel repetitive to once again invade Poland (so sorry guys, but here comes Germany again, and again, and again).6. DLC take you to new battlefields: Spanish civil war, and a hypothetical invasion of Czechoslovakia.Definitely a good successor to Panzer Corp 1, and worth the money if you like WW2 and tactical games.

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a great turn based strategy with lots of great ideas.... except there is a elephant sized BUT.The infantry combat is broken, and i mean UTTERLY broken, to favor the AI which is just a cheap way to increase difficulty. Now we  re all accustomed to games having some kind of AI boost, but rarely have ive seen such one sided atrocity as in panzer corps 2. No matter the terrain , no matter the unit, experience, support arms(artillery or else that give some kind of accuracy/support buff) your infantry units are lemmings that suffer HORRENDOUS one sided casualties in DEFENSE situations that should have obliterated the attacking enemy infantry unit without even making a dent in yours. Your 2 star 15 strong grenadier unit in a forest, supported by arty (one hex behind) is attacked frontally by a 15 strong unit with no experince, weaker stats, no support, charging from an open field.... yeah you are lucky if you get a 1 on 1 exchange in casualties...and this happens as a norm, not an exception. (when i think about it i dont remember a situation where the AI infantry got decimated in a stupid frontal attack i always had to replenish my infantry after almost every encounter, loosing between 3 and 7 points of strength on average, the only time my infantry "rocks" is if i unload suppression fire on enemy infantry ).  Of course when its time for your infantry attacks, DONT EVEN DARE, DONT EVE THINK about doing it without crazy arty preparation or your unit gets you guessed it, mowed down.This is such  big deal that i stopped playing in the mid of the campaign because infantry combat was a one sided travesty.Avoid it until patched or if you alreay bought it wait for a mod that will fix this nonsense.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, a game where i regret there's no "neutral" rating.Panzer Corps 2 has quite a few things going for it, but has just as much questionable design decisions.So, the GOOD:-The game is quite beautiful, with animated units actually moving between hexes, instead of just magically teleporting between them, like in older wargames, with a lot of different and well-made sound effects for guns blazing, bombs falling and tanks exploding. Not to mention, the models themselves are pretty great too, even if a bit too clean for the endless war that happens on-screen. The interface is highly-customizable and mostly inobtrusive, even though it may feel too cluttered at times. I'll also add that the sountrack is pretty good and i listen to it from time to time even when not playing the game.-:Your units, just like in Panzer Corps 1, have limited supply and ammo, which they replenish at the start of your turn. However, this time it is also tied into the new surround system, where supply flow along roads from supply hubs, and if you manage to block off the supply routes for enemy units, they won't replenish fuel and ammo and get stacking combat penalties as long as they remain cut off. Yeah, we know which game they took the idea from (looks at Order of Battle), but it has its own quirs in this game and works quite well, giving you more ways to overcome the mounting numerical superiority your enemies will have most of the time.-:Actually, not as much as a "player character", as a point shop for bonuses/penalties you can access one time when you start the campaign. In it, you initially have 2 points, which you use to get global improvements for your army, such as an additional move point for your panzers, permanently revealing enemy positions around mission objectives, and so on. But, if 2 points is too few for you, you can take a penalty (like less unit slots, slower supply replenishment, etc.) to get more bonus points. Depending on which bonuses/penalties you take, your playthrough may end up pretty different, which is a good thing-Think your panzers suck? Want to use that shiny T-34/French Somua you've seen? You actually can, as the game features a fully fleshed-out way to capture enemy equipment. Make the enemy unit retreat by attacking it with overwhelming force, and it will retreat. If it has nowhere to retreat to because of either terrain or your units blocking the way, they surrender, yielding you a 1 hp worth of equipment per 1 hp they had left when they surrender. When you have 10 hp worth of surrendered equipment of the same type, you can field it as a unit! But be careful, as you gotta keep a stockpile of extra parts to replenish this unit, so keep on capturing!Now, onto the BAD:-So, you know how difficulity is usually balanced in those kinds of games: your enemy might have more hp, more units to take down, stricter time limits... But this game went further: on difficulities above Normal (3rd one out of 5), the enemy units will just deal more damage, making units that get damage often, like infantry, nearly totally obsolete on higher levels and making turns where a random machine-gun armed tankette one-shots your forward panzer unit all too common, which is a lame way to balance a strategy game in a somewhat-realistic setting, as making every enemy unit into a superhuman blows that "somewhat-realistic" feeling out of the window.-Every mission you clear awards you a random hero, which you can attach to any of your in-game units, but instead of boosting its stats, it awards a special ability, like increasing the unit's defense per hp lost, being able to attack twice per turn, repairing a few HP for free if a unit didn't attack... While it does sound pretty cool, what ruins it are two facts: that you can attach up to 3 heroes to each unit, and that once per mission cleared is a bit too often, as it leads to absurd amounts of heroes, which can make absurdly overpowered combinations with each other, or even by themselves. Want to capture every piece of equipment you see? Here is the hero that turns every enemy retreat into surrender. Want even more broken tanks for the complete "wehrmacht power fantasy" experience? Here you are, a hero that removes the only weakness of a tank-class unit, which is a defense penalty against infantry in close terrain. With so much of those they stop feeling special, and abilities being that absurd do not help the "historical" flavor.-"Capture this hex there, then over there" is all there is to mission objectives. Granted, they tried to fix that in the "Axis Operations" series of DLC, but given that enemy scripting is nearly nonexistant, most of the time you will simply repel waves of random enemy units trying to charge in your general direction, sometimes even doing stupid things like placing their artillery at the frontline. Enemy scripting is important, as it was one of the major things that made the other wargame, Order of Battle, feel fresh across numerouf missions and DLC's. -Yeah, i admit that writing during mission briefings is not the most important thing in this genre, but given the fact that the game, and especially the DLC campaigns try to get into character-driven narrative, it all feels pretty rushed and "same every time".Now, with all that being said, i still do enjoy the game for what it is and will probably buy the DLC's that get released in the future, but it is far from being the "King of wargames" how the game description says, doesn't earn its 86-point Metacritic ranking and won't be THE game i will remember first when my friend will ask me to recommend a wargame. Yet, it is still pretty decent, and if you didn't play wargames before, Panzer Corps 2 might be a good place to start, as it tries pretty hard to be new player-friendly, even though Panzer Corps 1 is still the superior game.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer Corps 2 is a direct upgrade from Panzer Corps 1 in nearly every way. PC2 has a lot of quality of life changes that were sorely needed, as well as a few new gameplay mechanics that make the game feel even better, as well as old gameplay mechanics being improved upon even more [Heroes, for instance, are amazing].Slowly but surely the old content that was in PC1 is being added into PC2, and PC2 is turning into a proper successor to PC1. There are, however, just a few things I still think PC2 is missing. I'm going to compile those into a little "Cons" list but, honestly, some of it is very subjective.Pros-Superior technical quality [The game can handle Alt+Tabbing!]-WAY better graphics [Graphics weren't always a big sticker for me when playing PC1 but the new look of PC2 makes it hard to go back]-Far easier to actually play the game [The buying screen is a lot easier to go through, it's easier to cycle through units, etc etc]-Great new gameplay mechanics and improved old mechanics [Overrun, Heroes, Equipment Capture, and Commendations are all very welcome additions/improvements]-Unit Customization [Unit naming and camo editor is great and I love using it]-Far easier scenario editor [PC2 has a very simple scenario editor and I greatly appreciate this]ConsMost of these are going to be subjective to just myself, and are mostly "flavor" in nature, but a few actual cons are here too.-Medals are now named things like "Tank Killer Badge" and "Close Combat Legend". It makes me sorta miss the actual named medals of PC1 [i.e. "Iron Cross"]-Villages and Towns are unnamed. In the original PC1 I remember all the villages and towns having their own unique names. In PC2 only some of the cities have names. It just feels a little weird, but I feel like this is nitpicky.-Difficulty editing is not as extensive as in PC1. I remember in PC1 you could edit experience gains, prestige gains, and even AI and Player unit strengths to really customize your own difficulty. Difficulty customization does exist in PC2, but it's not nearly as extensive.-Multiplayer can get pretty laggy and is also somewhat buggy. I definitely now I'm in the minority when it comes to playing Panzer Corps multiplayer, but it's still a little disappointing.-No coop campaign. Coop scenarios exist, and they're amazing! But I really wish a coop campaign existed in some functionality. As of right now, you can make coop scenarios yourself, but it's not possible to create a coop campaign, which is disappointing.Overall, though, despite the cons, I don't at all regret buying Panzer Corps 2. The base game is great, and the DLC heavily improves it. I'm loving the Axis Operations so far. If you were a fan of Panzer Corps 1, or just like wargames, I can definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love it but it can be DAMN frustrating. Scenario design often focusses so heavily on tanks that almost every fight is a tank head to head, "heroes" and "nemesis", especially such enemies that attack twice or become tougher and stronger the more damage they take, ruin a lot of scenarios. And the AI cheats. It CHEATS like there's no tomorrow. You can use balanced attack randomness, and (I ran some statistics with 10 attempts each) often it will assign itself attack bonuses in 70 per cent of throws and givesd itself defense bonus in 50-60. I don't even want to know how much it will assign itself advantages if you mess with the balance. Units sometimes become extremely resilient to prevent their death, violently stronger to damage crucial units, and rarely you'll even see infantry run as fast on foot as tanks drive to give you some surprise attack from the rear or against a defenseless unit in the back. The enemy ALWAYS sees you, and will always target invisible vulnerable units like artillery or trucks by "coincidentally" as the devs put it, flying over the hexes and then bombing away. Had it not been for the design being so almost cunningly cheaty that it seems intentional that the AI gets so many dirty tricks and gimmicks, it could be a ton of fun. _childDocuments_.review: I've come back to this franchise in large part because of the recent DLC about the Battle of the Bulge. Between the updates to the game, the improvements to the AI and, frankly, a campaign that doesn't feature the Nazis as the playable faction I've decided to flip my review to a thumbs up. This is now very enjoyable to play and I am having a blast. Kudos to the team!Original review is below the asterix. *** I play OOB, PzC1 and Unity of Command (1 and 2) on max difficulty and did the same with PC2. I think this is easier, but ok as a game after playing through the first few missions. I dislike that it is Nazi only. I don't want to play as a bunch of racist morons who murdered a huge chunk of Europe. I am downrating it until Allied campaigns come out. You are welcome to disagree with me on that, but for me a PG clone is not particularly fun if I have to play as Nazis. If you'd like to see the opinion of someone who doesn't have that bias (at least I'm up front about it) check out NightPhoenix on youtube, who I largely agree with. I think the encirclement mechanic is very dysfunctional. I had my tank adjacent to an enemy artillery and both were encircled. You can't plan around such a random system, so why is it in the game? Unity of Command 2 does this much better, as did OOB. PzC1 had a simple system based on surrounding the enemy/preventing them having a viable move path to surrender them. This was rudimentary but much better than PzC2 system. The graphics are bad, especially when compared to OOB (much older) and especially Unity of Command 2. It is not substantially different than what you see on youtube. I am playing on maximum graphics, so why is that the case? I'm sure they're blah blah high res blah blah, but what they aren't is easily differentiated. PzC1 did this much better with sprites. No real change in the mechanics. Biggest change from original was the UI, that engineers share their bonus with other attacking units and that recon gives a bonus to other units. The UI is excellent. It gives you pretty much all info you could want and the designers behind it should receive a lot of praise. My only complaint was that I had a hard time finding the detailed combat prediction option. I especially like the detailed combat log that tracks the outcomes of all battles. Extremely nice feature. The air system is incredibly annoying. Constantly sending airplanes back to where you put them is a click intensive mechanic that doesn't add value. If you want to do an airstrike system go with UoC2 model of limited strikes as action. If you want to do planes as core component go with Panzer General system of leaving them over an area. Realism should always and everywhere be in the service of good game design and this isn't it. Scenario design is very weak and I felt better handled in PzC1. Compare US Corps first three mission to PzC2 Nazi first three mission and you will see a world of difference in scenario and map complexity. If you like this type of game and are OK with only having a Nazi campaign go for it. I'd personally prefer Unity of Command 2 or Order of Battle WW2 and have no real desire to play this further.

_childDocuments_.review: The extremely unbalanced Moscow Scenario is bad enough for me to not recommend this game. The game was fun up to this point, but Moscow is just hell. The enemy has unlimited numbers and ressources and is entrenched as well as armed with everything. If you did not bring enough or the right equipment you just lose right there. Extremely bad balancing on this part. I understand that the german equipment was not as good as T-34, but Russia hardly had such extreme amounts of highly advanced equipment like su-100. Besides the AI can do extremely dumb moves like  suicide rushing your artillery and get away with it. They dont care if they lose 10 units because their reserves are near limitless. But for you every point lost hurts. Conscripts are extremely OP versus infantry because they can reinforce 10!! strength every turn and just spam every infantryman dead. Plus a very short time limit to make the mission even more annoying.As long as this game remains so imbalanced and so inaccessible to normal players that do not wish to invest days for a single mission I cannot recommend it. Which is a shame because the units look good, and some mechanics like heroes or capturing equipment are fun.Heroes are also a problem though because a good hero can vastly improve your units while a bad one does not matter at all.Maybe buy it on very very big discount or play Order of Battle instead.

The heroes add things like unit takes 50% normal core slots, unit prevents adjacent enemy support attacks. Heroes can be assigned to the unit you think they will do the most good they are not randomly assigned. They also finally allow two units to swap places rather than having one move then the other move, thus making it impossible to have to adjacent units just swap spots. _childDocuments_.review: This review is  for both the base game and the GC DLCs.After playing PC2 for a while and being undecided over some features i tried playing PC1 again - and it just hit me what an enormous improvement PC2 is in almost every way. I like that aircraft is tied to an airfield now, i LOVE the overrun ability for tanks, the overall upgrade in video and audio appeal is enormous, the game just feels much more responsive when many actions in PC1 felt really clunky and delayed.Most baseline mechanics are very close to PC1, i already mentioned the two most obvious changes, airfields and overrun, but there are other, too, like encirclement and auto-supply for non-encircled units, most of which improve the flow of gameplay by a lot, i think.Of course, there are also things i don't like:- Visual clarity. While i DO like the overall visual appeal of the game and would still rate it positively, i do find myself in a LOT of situations where it is very hard to see stuff. Moving a tank into a cluster of enemies and just seeing a "bubble" of battle-prediction-plates which are almost impossible to match to any specific enemy without zooming in extremely? Check. Having WHITE movement icons on snowy ground, which feels like the game is trying to give you an eye-exam? Check. Trying to rebase aircraft and your desired airfield not being a viable target  Check. There are MANY of these situations. It is the most obvious flaw of the game, in my oppinion, and the developer should spend more time here for PC3, i think.- Unit splitting. A new feature which allowes you to split a unit in half and have both parts act independently, being able to recombine them later. This is a great feature on paper, but the actual implementation is really, really lacking. Examples: You split a unit and both halves score kills before recombining it. The total kill-count (and therefore progress towards medals) is now the AVERAGE of both parts. This should obviously not be the case. The statistic should simply stay unified even while split. Many unit-specific mechanics or statistics simply behave "wonky" when splitting. So this feature quickly devolves into splitting units that provide non-strength-based buffs, primarilly recons. The feature needs more work. Or it should just be removed from anything but recons and made part of their base toolkit.- Encirclement. Great addition in general, but most maps do not give the germans enough time to use it. There are several noteable exceptions in the GC DLCs which encourage you to use it, but generally speaking you will not have the turns required to utilise it and are better off optimising your Blitzkrieg instead. Also, the UI could do a better job of telling you where you need to have units to enact an encirclement.- Unit balance. This last point is true for PC1 and PC2 and is, of course, in part a requirement for the historical aspect of the game: Some unit-classes are just FAR more useful than others. Anti-Tank-Guns, for example, absolutely suck until very late in the war. In fact, the best AT Gun is the 88-AA-Gun for a VERY long period...which may be historically accurate, but it just seems strange to have this category of units be so underwhelming.- RPG aspects. PC2 makes a great leap in that regard compared to PC1 and i love it. I just want to encourage the developers to go further in PC3. There really should be better voice acting in the briefing and debriefing (or at all, for the DLC). Again: The improvements made from PC1 > PC2 are there and they are HUGE - i just want to see more in that direction.- Menus. Again, huge improvement over PC1 - but still not quite as good as they should be. For example, i am allowed to change the difficulty between scenarios. Great. But i can also change the number of commander-traits there, which is not applied until after finishing a complete campaign. The setting should simply not be there at all and the transition from campaign to campaign where you CAN change your traits should be improved.- Between-Scenario-Stuff. This was not present in the original Panzer General, but i think it would serve the game to have a "base camp" screen between scenarios where you can browse the latest improvements, see your units, enter the command-post to start the next briefing or just have some RPG banter with NPCs.---Conclusion: PC2 is a HUGE improvement over PC1 in almost any regard. I like this game and its genre. I still think some aspects should be improved for PC3 - which i hope will happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Second:I bought the Field Marshal edition with extra camo and insignia. And now I can't use them anymore. They're all gone. Such a simple thing get's broken. Sorry but this was the straw that broke the camel's back. Can't recommend this game until you fix it.It is baffling that with each year game deployment is getting worse every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time. We have Agile, TDD, BDD and all the other methodologies and tools to make sure that everything works fine in software development...And here we are again. The simplest stuff just doesn't work.First:HmmmThis is a hard one. Although I love the fact that they brought back features from PG2 like overrun and created loads more like recon planes, heroes, encirclement, etc....The game somehow feels unpolished and not worth the price tag.So here is what I love:- Overrun- Heroes (they give actual new abilites instead of extra damage, initiative, etc...)- General's Customisation- Full 3D (better than PG3D was)- Camo and insignia selection (FInally!!)- Vehicle unmount in a certain distance with soft units- The new core slot system make sure you can't OP your troops even when you have millions of prestige. You can have a big army with a couple of OP units, or a small one with the newest and best equipment.- Recon Planes! (Finally!!!!)The Bad:- If you want same units to have the same camo (like Heavy Tanks), you are in for a world of hurt as selecting a camo is crap. You have to scroll down every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time if it's down on the bottom. A favourite system and/or search and/or filter by nation would be nice.- The UI is horrible. I mean it's really bad. Feels very clunky and unnatural. They moved everything from right to left and everything is just too big and messed up.  Maybe it takes time until one gets accustomed to it.- (Under UI) The unit list is BIIIG. You can shrink it to one column, but it always opens up as two and you have to resize it every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time. I play on a 1440p monitor and it just takes up soooooo much space. At least give the option to make it smaller or something. And there is no filtering of units, so you don't have to scroll down to your planes.- Scrolling is bad. As you zoom in, the screen scroll gets really bad. Sure they are going to fix this, hopefully.- The new unit experience system feels more punishing when you buy inexperienced crew.- Planes flying back to base by the end of the turn sounds like an interesting concept, but it's so annoying. As when you have the battle far away you have to scroll back to the airfield to select them, or you can use the HUGE unit list, which is slow AF. Why not just make it like in PG2 where there is no fuel value for the planes and they can move freely? They took away the fuel limitation and now we have a distance one. I liked the fuel limitation better as it was more strategic and you could lose planes if you weren't careful.So far for now.  All in all it's a good game. The UI is bad AF. It needs more work. Planes need to be re-imagined a bit, or just bring back either the PG2 no-fuel style, or the PG1/PC1 fuel one. Or make it a choice. Camos are great, but hard to manage. I give it a recommendation, but you might want to wait a bit until it has all the problems ironed out, or it's on sale again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been many years (decades) since I played Panzer General, Fantasy General, and every other General there was at the time. Apparently I'm not very good at it, because even on easy level I had to use a cheat to get some prestige to upgrade my army, and even then getting through it was a tough slog. Then when I got to the Kursk scenario I had to back it down to Very Easy. Usually I don't like to cheat as using cheats usually causes the challenge to go away and I lose interest. With this game it doesn't bother me. I'm still early in the Kursk scenario, and I'm not far enough in to see if it's lost its challenge. I think prestige income is ridiculously difficult to come by. Honestly, I have no idea how anyone can go through the kind of attrition over time and still have enough prestige to even replace units, let alone upgrade or buy new units. _childDocuments_.review: Ever since the release of Panzer Corps 2 I was counting the days, the hours, the minutes and seconds. I even played the beta/demo when it came out. I signed in for the marshal edition of the game.For me two things stand out as negatives;First, The game suffers from "Panzer General 3(D)" syndrome. They tried to be innovative with the addition of more 3d graphics, for me it feels it is counterproductive.For instance, selecting a unit can be cumbersome. It is hard to distinguish which unit is which (a BF-109 looks too much the same as a JU-87. This will result in "misclicking". Especially considering that the distinction between ground and air units is not as distinguishable as it was in Panzer Corps.Secondly: I somehow mis engagement. The missions feel shallow (said before), the path through the campaign feels empty, the heroes are hard to add, and difficult to keep overview and I miss the battles that cover more ground, the larger battles. Most battles are on a tactical scale now.Ok, I admit, we have gone into more detail, and the second complaint were actually five-in-one.So a third and final one: as much as I tried to get used to the interface, I feel it is defragmentated. Searching for options, which items are placed, which not, core vs not core, placed-vs-not placed, etc. Okay, since you insist a fourth gripe: the gameplay is somewhat slow. In Panzer Corps I you were able to play in a relative nice and cripsy pace. This game, on a high specced machine even, seems to play sluggish. Even with animations slower, the clicking and sometimes waiting to make your next move as part of a sequence is not only cumbersome (see above) but it has some delay. It lacks "crisp" and "momentum" in your gameplay. I like the hidden strategic and tactical understanding you need to play this game and it's predecessors, and now both strategy and "beer-and-pretzel-pace" playstyle seem to be lacking.In short: I understand the effort for innovation, but the strategy part for me is kind of lost in well-meant effort. The goal seemed to add more innovation, instead of more in depth gameplay. Of course it should not play as Order of Battle, but I expected more depth somehow. As an old-school-die-hard-panzer general-panzer corps-veteran, I am pretty much disappointed. It feels like the aforementioned Panzer General I/II to Panzer General 3D move, which was an arguable faillure. (I am going back and replay the Original Panzer Corps, which was good, satisfying and replayable from the day it was released until now)

_childDocuments_.review: After two decades of buying Matrix/Slitherine games at full price (before they ever discounted anything), I was sitting on the fence with this game like no other. And yes, my profile is open and it embarrassingly just scratches the surface in terms of wargames.I still play PC1 with excellent mods like Modern Conflicts and that great East Front mod, but after all these years, pushing around the counters has become kind of rote for me. And that was my concern with this game: pushing around 3D counters instead of 2D. Well, the new game is a lot more than 3D so far.With less than five hours in, I am in no position to comment on campaign structure or bugs (none so far). But the FEEL of the game is brand new. My eyes were having trouble with the old game's tiny counters, but now we have Zoom. I would recommend accessing the Manual on the Store page and reading the What's New section. I was so afraid of a "rehash" but the changes and additions they made make it feel like I'm playing a "new" game. And that's what we pay for, right?I am also enjoying learning the new UI. I, for one, love lots of stats and in-game info, and the devs raised the bar on this. Before, at least for me, it was, yeah push your units forward, attack, attack, onto the next one. There is more to consider now, and a really impressive suite of customization options. Yes, my computer fan tends to "whir" even on lower settings, but assume it will not break my rig and they will optimize as needed.Considering all the changes, the game plays very well so far right out of the box. And because it one of the most important products Matrix sells, it will get better and better. For this game anyway, the patches are like death and taxes - we can count on them!Of course, I might be led astray because it's all so new and shiny. Well, shine on...I can't wait to start modding the text files, no less the editor, although the latter will take some effort, as they added a lot of stuff.Anyway, I will update this initial review (for what it's worth) should I find something horrible hidden beneath the surface. But based on the more in-depth reviews, that is unlikely. I was really prepared to refund the game as needed, which is why I bought it on Steam, but it turned out quite different, for me at least. And I am a pretty jaded old wargamer.Best to all!****************** Updated after 14 hours **********************The designers have done an exemplary job with this new game, but it is still Panzer Corps. Meaning it gets a bit repetitive - move, kill, move, kill, etc. This is not John Tiller's Squad Battles. While the devs have added considerable chrome, it still boils down to a beer-and-pretzels game for me, which is kind of expensive at $40.If you have the discipline not to open the Chat menu and use all those lovely cheats, the single-player game might get pretty tense and add to the immersion. Or it might get pretty frustrating. Not sure.So maybe MP is the way to go? I tried it today through my Slitherine account and it didn't work. Maybe just me, as the forums would be flooded with complaints if MP didn't work.Again, the devs have had to walk a tightrope to improve the game (which they did immensely) while not turning it into Squad Battles. For me, it is just not deep enough to be a favorite. I don't examine the map and carefully ponder my next move. That is what Field of Glory 2 is for.  However, an MP match against a human might change my thinking a bit.Finally, the editor is amazing and will guarantee some (great) scenarios down the road. So far just playing the Afrika campaign and the devs have done a lot to flesh things out, but again I get tempted to just win the game via the cheat and move on to the next scenario.Still a "thumbs up" for the player who liked the previous games. Love the more complex UI and all the data available for perusal and customization. But it is Panzer Corps, albeit with a few tactical nuances added in. It's not a game that will keep you up at night thinking about your next moves, unless you are a complete noob. Few of us are.

_childDocuments_.review: This game limits the campaign flow significantly and has less campaign options than game one. Existing maps are simply split in two and you are limited to a win Russia and than US with Germany or Germany fights loosing battles to the Berlin defeat. Africa Option is not developed. In Axis Operations you don't get a victory over Russia, just a cease fire, you conquer India to liberate it to Indian Independence, and you attack the US from Japan, giving Japan total control. Axis Operations is historically very unrealistic. German pride caused the 2nd World War, as well as the perceived humiliation of Germany by the Allies France and Great Britain. Germany was not the democratic state of today, but a conservative authoritarian society. Germany feared the Great Powers of France and Great Britain, as they had reduced Germany in size, surrounded Germany with democratic states loyal to them, and had demanded crushing World War 1 reparations under threat of military occupation. Germany thought that without friendly states surrounding it and a natural barrier such, as the Atlantic or the Ural mountains it would be under constant threat of invasion. Germany feared the US more as creditor, as Germany was virtually owned by the US thru the credit it had received, than a Great Power let alone the Super Power it would become. The threat of a nuclear bomb is overplayed, as it is more likely that a stable military situation for Germany would have resulted in a US-German nuclear standoff, as it historically did with the Soviet Union.  Navel combat is lacking combined unit effects that are present on land thru hero units. After such a long release time for this game this game is a technical upgrade from its previous version, but nothing more. You also have lots of errors in this game, such as no deployment possible in the Colorado Conference deployment.
