_childDocuments_.review: PANZER CORPS 2 a war game with layers upon layers of intricate detailed game play. So much well thought out masterfully crafted depth some which is not visually seen thus making things perhaps seem more simplistic or obtuse then they really are. For example when a unit say a tank attacks a infantry unit in forest cover the tank is actually entering the enemy hex and not firing from long range thus tanks being naturally bad in jungle terrains will suffer along with not dealing as much damage while the infantry unit will have the advantage. So it is better to just to do nothing with the tank luring the infantry into attacking them by just staying next to their hex due to both units types having a range of 0. Now some units will have a range of 1 which means they will shoot into the adjacent hex but not enter it making things safer.Such a visual game and yet so much is underneath the surface.Suppression and encirclement play major roles in getting a positive outcome. If you expect to just charge in wiping out enemy after enemy without lowering their moral with encirclement which also cuts off their supply lines, artillery bombardments and air strikes you will suffer many losses to the point of making victory unattainable. Attrition and siege tactics will win the day many times.Naval units are great for suppression which they excel in but for heavy kill results you are better off using air and ground troops unless going up against other naval units. Its this kind of variety and differences in ones forces which give a strong character and personality to each combatant but one has to have at least an idea of what is going on under the hood of the game mechanics to truly appreciate the amazing amount of in depth thoughtful design creation which went into PANZER CORPS 2. Plenty of quality of life enhancements are available including a excellent user interface where you can deploy units held in reserve as well as purchase new ones, upgrade existing units, do easy to understand comparisons of the different forces stats such as strength and range etc. You can also upgrade them to over strength level making them very powerful units on the battlefield. I really love the user interface which makes everything very intuitive and easy to get into.Air units now return automatically to their air base after a turn thus eliminating have to return each individual one yourself and not worrying about fuel consumption. You can also make other air bases your main base after capturing them thus getting yourself closer to strike at the enemy as you go deeper into their territory.At the start of the campaign you get a screen where you will be given many choices on what to have in your game from limited turns to achieve a victory to turning off the option to have no time limits and play with a more relaxed pace. This is only possible to do at the start of the campaign so make sure to turn this off before then if you don't like turn limits. You can choose to have or not have over strength units. You can set dice randomness to show exact results or not. I have mine set to a hundred percent to know exactly how much damage i will deal out and receive though not always totally accurate it gives me enough info to let me know whether to commit to attack or not.  There are many many more options to choose on the campaign set up screen. Having this in PANZER CORPS is pure genius and reminds me of character creation in rpg games where you can even choose weaknesses.Graphics and audio are delicious eye watering mouth quivering master chef quality cooked steak for the gaming senses. Seeing the smoking wreckage of enemy units in all its devastated beauty from tanks on the field to battleships sunk by serpent like submarines brings home how video games take tabletop gaming to a new level of immersion. So realistically brutal is the on screen carnage i was expecting the devastating impact of ship to ship battles to bring forth heroic final screams of, " Remember me Momma! " as sailors leaped into shark infested waters.You can zoom in on the maps capturing all the highly polished miniature levels of detail of the map and military forces. I did have problems sometimes telling the differences of terrain when it came to things like elevation moving a unit to a dead end where they had to turn around. Pressing L for the strategic map solved this problem and after awhile i no longer needed to use the strategic map as i knew right away what was what.Many thanks to my friend Strategikal who let me know about all the intricate workings of PANZER CORPS 2. Thanks to him and the excellent strategy guide he created for PANZER CORPS 2 i am completely enjoying and appreciating the incredible design of PANZER CORPS 2. Definitely check out his strategy guide it will make knowing and understanding the under the hood game mechanics in a very easy to understand intuitive manner.PANZER CORPS 2, BUY IT! PLAY IT! Feel the steel of burning lead and thundering bombardments in a time of grand world conquest where men of forged iron will fought on courage soaked battlefields of absolute victory and deafening defeat!

_childDocuments_.review: Having initially really enjoyed this game I sadly cannot recommend it.  A lot of the game is great - there is a lot to manage and the limited resource/ too many demands mechanic is well done and requires a thoughtful approach to building your army. Gameplay is fairly quick, the key principles are easy to pick up, the scenarios are challenging but not impossible (more on that in a moment), the UI is pretty good though it would be nice to be have more zoom out so it is possible to see the entire map without scrolling. So why don't I recommend it? Because after a while it seems the devlopers got lazy. This is not a quick game - it requires thought, weighing up competing strategies and the committment of sometime, including in the planning/ army construction for each scenario. That is great if the scenarios are rewarding enough. However, the alternate history Kuybichev scenario ruined it for me. The briefing makes a point of telling you that persistent snowy weather will greatly limit the use of your airforce. This strongly encourages players to favour other units. by this point in the game you have probably built up a fair number of experienced air units and may have limited prestige (game currency earned by military success) to spend on buying new land units and may have to disband some of your air units - getting their prestige but loosing their experience and skills. Even if you don't you are probably going to put a lot of thought, and thus time, into revamping your army for this scenario dominated by bad weather and land units. What do the developers then deliver? Almost constant perfect weather and an enemy who have a huge air force which will slaughter you if you don't have air units or a haven't put a lot of your prestige into anti-air defenses. Which the briefing specifically highlights as the wrong thing to do. Losing scenarios can be part of the fun of a game and make a subsequent victory more rewarding - i've had to restart several scenarios in PC2 and never felt the game was unfair - but a game that encourages you to spend a lot of time preparing for the opposite of what happens is not just frustrating, its a massive waste of the time involved. Sure you can restart and this time go with a lot of air power but you're restarting not because a challenging game beat you and your back for another go at testing your skills but because the developers wrote a really lazy intro that doesn't match the scenario. Maybe this is the only scenario affected this way but there are many other games out there and spending more time on this one to find the same thing happen again just isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 hrs of play I recommended PC2 unfortunately after 40 hours I cannot.I was a big fan of PG2.  I liked PC1 but felt it feel short in many categories.  PC1 virtually had no lines of supply, very basic battle mechanics, unlimited range paratroopers and there were very few quality balanced MP scenarios.  PC2 has made many changes that make it more like PG2, some work many don't.I bought PC2 to play multiplayer so I have no comments on the AI game.MP Platform: I have found the MP platform to be quite stable, when I had an issue the slitherine support group was very responsive and fixed my problem.  Large MP community, easy to start a game.Graphics/Gameplay: The 3D graphics are fine.  The unit style & color makes it very difficult to differentiate between your troops and enemy troops.  Troop selection & movement is left click/left click which leads to many unintended movements.Supply:  PC2 smartly introduces supply rules to increase the realism.  In some respects the supply rules are a big improvement and others fall short.  First PC2 units have limitless supply unless they are encircled, this takes away all the the decisions of how to use various units with different attributes.  The worst change is that all 4 borders of the map provide supply as long as there is a path to the border.  The result in MP is players buying recons sending them way behind enemy lines (obviously way out of supply) with a path to the border so they are still in supply.  Your opponent can then actually go behind your units and cut off your supply, so units that should be out of supply are cutting off supply.Encirclement:  I initially liked the encirclement rules and felt they improved the battle mechanics.  After playing longer I realized there are way to many ways for the MP player to game the system and unrealistically encircle units.  Zone of control rules are lacking and again the recon issue.Paratroopers: Big problem, paratroopers have a limitless range and supply.  They can fly forever.  No map is big enough that they can't go from one end to another.  In MP it results in many un realistic outcomes, there just aren't enough units to engage and cover all key hexes in the rear.   Slitherine's response is well both players have the same capability but in the MP scenarios the importance is far from equal.Multiplayer:  There are 8 scenarios which is ok when you start.  I prefer balanced historical games, there are 3 maybe 4.  Some of the fictional games dont have enough units for the map size IMO.   There is a random map generator which can produce multiple scenarios, I have found these to be very cookie cutter and boring. You'll never complete a 4 player game unless you are playing with people you know.  People have now realized you can game many of the scenarios using out of supply recons and LONG range paratroopers so I stopped playing.  I dont want to spend my time chasing recons and paratroopers around the extremes of the map.  Additionally, the MP community is far from reliable.   Maybe 40% are reliable and the rest abandon the game.  If they are winning they may continue if they are losing the game goes dormant.  Maybe 20% of people losing continue or surrender.I really wanted to be able to recommend PC2 at this point I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR an excellent turn based WWII game ,better than its already great predecessor Panzer Corps Gold. Panzer Corps Gold is my most played game in Steam with some 360 hours so I bought this as well plus all DLC (minus the General Edition. Have not bought Fall of Poland yet either).It's a considerable improvement over its predecessor. I was skeptical at first about the 3d graphics but I changed my mind : they are very nicely done and they improve the immersion.There are two drawbacks though : a) you could play Panzer Corps Gold in a potato PC but for this one you ll need a more modern GPUb) because of the 3d perspective, at times, it is a tad harder to distinguish what you are looking at. For instance, an air unit may partially cover a ground unit behind it and you need to pan/zoom the view a bit to see things better More importantly there are new and improved mechanics and quality of life improvements such as :- optional buffs/debuffs selection for your general- richer customisation of gameplay and difficulty level- nice briefing per scenario - commendation points- unit awards- improved AI that feels more alive and dynamic ( in previous game AI was largely static, sitting and waiting for you)- mechanics such as : encirclement, overrun, high ground, forced march, recon units buff attacks of adjacent friendly units, recon planes, anti aircraft guns now support not just adjacent units but everything within their attack radius, anti tank units provide support to adjacent units against hard attacks, phased recon unit movement, special artillery with counter artillery support, engineers buff entrenchment build speed of adjacent units, mass attacks, two types of airfields plus option to relocate aircraft, split units, exchange units.Another major change is that now, in each scenario, you have a given amount of unit slots, say, 50 slots. Now, a not so good tank may require 2 of these slots. A better one might require 3 or 4. So you get to choose, you can have more but not so good units or fewer but better ones. Which I think gives one more option to customise your play and improves replayabilty.Having completed the first DLC Spanish Civil War I can now provide some more input :- scenarios, overall, last longer. Turn limit is typically around 20 turns (if u dislike turn limit however it can be switched off). Last scenario of that campaign had a massive 36 turns limit. It felt epic but also dragged a tad longer than I should like to be frank, alas, not much spare time for gaming anymore - AI feels better than its predecessor: it is very active and alive on the battlefield and it makes less mistakes. Bombers will almost always be supported by fighters. Air units will try to avoid your anti-air umbrella if they can help it. Recon units will use their phased movement to slip through gaps of your front line and hit vulnerable units. Artillery and AA guns will reposition to attack your units. They will think twice before attacking your units if they are supported by artillery or anti-tank guns.That said, AI remains far from perfect:- infantry will sometimes attack tanks in open space- tanks will sometimes attack infantry having close defence - units may move and remain on vulnerable positions - units near death, instead of retreating & repairing, will sometimes go ahead and perform doomed suicidal attacks- units will move within encircled space getting encircled themselves - infantry will abandon the safety of close defence and/or entrenchment to attack some badly wounded enemy but, in doing so , expose themselves to painful counter attacks - AI units seem to behave each on their own. They don't seem to be aware that they have their buddies around them. (Fighters which will support their bombers are excluded from this). AI also seems to only consider the circumstances of current turn only. Does not "look ahead" at what might happen in the next turn

_childDocuments_.review: It's great and Ill support it because it's PC and Slitherine, but it isn't as good as the first game. Some DLC missions seem farcical like don't kill any units...really? And one of the bonus objectives is to take all of the AI cities? Just leave out the Czech "invasion" and add another mission from the actual war.  A back and forth love story type thing with a Spanish Nationalist woman in the Spanish Civil War DLC?  Baby sitting allied AI controlled forces? Come on man...stick to the formula that worked. Encirclement's are plain wierd and don't always make logical sense. But what about the cool mods that were such an integral part of the first one? Don't hold your breath. It says a lot that there are way fewer mods for this game than for PC1 even though this one has a workshop here on steam. Man, did they somehow blow that opportunity! All of that said, the core game play mechanics and graphics are top rate. The strategy is solid when the script isn't getting in it's way, and it is from a great publisher. I hope the remaining grand campaign DLC is good, although it appears you have no option in them to disable the obnoxious turn limit and most of the missions have you hold victory hexes while the AI spawns waves of enemies, mostly planes and cavalry (yes you can forget air superiority, it will just keep spawning planes)...cheap huh. Skip the DLC if you aren't a fan of the genre or watching waves of cavalry inexplicably overrun your tanks lol, and while it may sound like I hate the game, the base campaign is solid and is done the way it should be done, imo. In the base game you attack(!), there is an option to disable turn limits, the AI doesn't just continually spawn units to throw at you while you defend 4 hexes(!), you can achieve air superiority and the missions all seem like more than cheap tower defense levels for filler. PC2 is still the king of "Panzer General" type games and it's easy to see why some "loyalists" like it and hope it gets better...and why some people don't and hope for more competition. Get it on sale for the decent base campaign, the only reason for the thumbs up, but forget the ridiculous DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge disapointment. I'm a huge Panzer Corps fan and I could'nt wait for this game to come out. I have played this game and have run into some errors that need to be adressed Let me start with what this game gets right. 1. AT guns act like artilery when defending against hard targets, ei tanks, which is a good feature that makes both Tank destroyers and AT guns usefull and instrumental both attacking and defending. 2. The option for troops to use a transport and then dismount is also a very welcome feature. 3. The ability to split units in 2 is also very great feature that makes encirclement and making enemy units surrender easier and satisfiying. 4. The encirclement system is good, you can create big pokes and just capture many troops, speaking of which, 5. Being able to capture enemy equipment and use it in your army is an awesome feature, thought I would 6. I also like that recon units improve the artilerry, bombing runs, air strikes, and attacks. It makes them very usefull on the battle field. Now with all the positives out of the way, lets get to the negatives and why they break the game1. Artillery sucks: artillery, has been nerfed compared to the original. I do like that if artilery fires on another artilerry unit, said unit will fire back, a good feature since artilerry duels were a thing, especially in WW1. But how is artilerry nerfed? Well It doesnt do a good job and protecting your infantry or your tanks, I can get the reason for this was the following philosophy: artillery for soft targets, wile AT guns for hard, however this is a silly interpreteation as in WW2 artilerry fired at advancing tank formations defensively, and some times even efectively. They are firing rounds that if they fired directly at tanks would destroy them at one hit, even landing close would incapasitate tanks. So the reasoning for nerfing arty against armour is silly in my opinion. But there are so many times I have artilerry defending my troops, and mind you this is enemy infantry unit with no support, they atack my infantry with atrilery support and they end up either, inflicting more casualties, despite the atrilerry support, they rout my infantry despite being supported. So in the area were artilerry is supposed to excell in, soft targets, it completly flops.Which leads to my next point2. Infantry combat is broken: Infantry combat feels broken, its not like the original. Here in Panzer corps 2 infantry have at minimum 15 points instad of 10, I guess the idea was to represent the size of infantry divisions in the war but what ends up happening is this : Infantry feel like meat bags you have to punch with your own infantry. YOUR infantry take horendous casualties, even in full strength defending in close terrain. Its frustraiting to see the enemy charge its infantry with out carring about the concecuenses against your own, and despite yours having artillery or good terain to defend take horrible casualties. Mean wile I have to blast the hell out of enemy positions with my artilerry if not, my assults produre horrific assaults. Because he who had the most guns had the most fire power and had a big advangage on the battle field. In Panzer corp 1 if you attacked a full strengthed infantry unit with another unit with equal stregth, and there was artilerry defending it the assault would end terribly for the attacker. Artilery was a good shield, protecting tanks and infantry as the turn passed from both infantry and tanks, infantry stupid enought to attack, or because they could not see it because of line of sight would get destroyed, and that was in the open, in close terrain it was even worse. Tanks, wile rearly sufering damage, were supressed, thus making their attacks useless. Now artilerry feels weak and useless. In the original if I had 2 pieces the assault would be stopped altogether because the supretion and casualties were so bad on the infantry, that is a huge diference in the way the game plays. The attack defend system of infantry aslo feels broken. In my opinion it should be even, both in attack and defendese, the only things affecting the out come being, terrain, which should have a 25% affect on the out come of any engagement, as the saying goes "geography is destiny' not just for countries, but for hole battles through out history. The initiative, the experiance, and finaly support, recon, atrillery, air support, naval tanks etc should then be the deciders in the out come of an engagement. Im playing in marshal dificulty. I decide to go to africa 1. thing I dont like, no italian units into the corp. Why?  The reason I loved africa corps was because of that, having my German and Italian units fight together as brothers, covering eachothers backs and each bringing something to the table.  But Im getting of topicI get over that. Im in africa kicking ass. Then at Gazala I complete all my objectives, including the bonus ones. I then get a decision, either to go after the allies into egypt or go to el alamein, esentialy just giving up the initiative and letting the british take the tide of the war. What I love about this the message "this decision will have irreversible consecuances on the war" But then when I click to go to egypt, it tells me I need 5000 perstige in order to "persuade" high comand to go to egypt. What the ♥♥♥♥!? Im sorry for my languege but this complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Whats the point of this? There is not a single scenario in any Panzer corp campaing or dlc were it requiers you to have x amount of prestige to go to the next mission, that is pure bull, and it pisses me of and makes no scense. If your playing this game, your in it to win, so why would a rational person choose a campain path of inevitable defeat? This absolutely infutriating, in the following scenerio I was reminded about how I lost the initiative of the war, not because I dint fullfil all my objectives in time, not because I dint fight hard enought, no, because I dint have enought stupid prestige to "presuade" some ignorant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at high comand to uh, o yea, win the damn war! I just dint even bother and I just let my army be destoyed because whats the point of fighting on if I lost already? On top of that, once I lost the scenario, the campaing ended, wtf? In the original Panzer corp, if you got marginal victories, and even full deafeats in others you would go down the historical path, however there were still chances, twists and turns, but the campaing continued till the defense of the Reich, which I like looking back. Now you mite be thinking, based on what I said above, why would I then praise this? Well because at least in Panzer corps 1 you would fight to the last man or with a truce with the Soviets or the western Allies, which I like the idea. Also there was not a prestige cost... I was suprised there was not a "defeated" campaing were you fight say the invation of sicily or the ardenss like the original. Once its over its over. Wile you can say there were missions in panzer corps 1 were you lost it was over period and its true, however there were battles that even if you lost, you could still continue the fight and bounce back, here you dont get that. So yea thats my rant, review of Panzer Corps 2, I dont say this to attack the devs or slitherine, I think the devs care about this game and that they are trying to improve the game. Please any dev that reads this, consider doing the following, just a sugestion as a fan.1. Buff artilerry so it feels more like it did in the original2. Re work infantry: a make them have 10 points of strenght like the rest of the units in the game, or at the very least make terrain more influencial in an outcome of a battle. Re work the combat between infantry vs infantry as I have described above.  3. No prestige barriers for missions. Just no, get rid of them for they should not exist. Thats literally it, if you do those things I garante people will love the game more and the combat will be near perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a long time fan of the beer and pretzels Panzer General and Panzer Corps series. So I have waiting with great anticipation for Panzer Corps 2. Is it a serious wargame? No. Is it fun? Yes. It is an incremental change in the series with some fun new aspects that change gameplay. I dove right in to the Polish Campaign chose some handicaps (like fog of war limitation and occasional equipment failure) and started off. Got to the Dijon scenarion and suffered crushing defeat several times which necessitated a restart due to poor choices early on. Now I just have one handicap on normal. Remember folks prestige is king. Panzer Corps 2 will hurt you if you don't gain and use it properly. I like the aggressive AI. Units will no longer just sit there and be bypassed. They will seek to flank you and more than ever artillary is the target. I love the new recon feature this has definitely changed my play style. The game rewards you for surrounding opponants so do it. The heroes feature can be played with and makes the units more interesting. And the camouflage feature makes it so easy to differentiate units from each other. As the campaign progresses one has to give thought to what units are put on the field and how one needs to progress much more than the previous version. Sometimes you just have to put units in reserve in order to meet the unit cap and field the correct team. The briefings are pretty good at describing how to plan for the mission but there is some imagination needed still in how to compose, field and move your force. I read some professional reviews and i think that some of the complaints are just quibbles it definitely does take some time to get used to a new interface and presentation but it is worth it. I did an early purchase buying the field marshal edition so I hope the developers don't fall down with the upcoming DLC's.Update after 1942 DLC

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up with war gaming using military miniatures and board games like Panzer Leader in the years before the advent of home computers and the internet, this turn based game combines ease of use with many of the features I liked about board games and miniatures. The infantry, armor, ships, and planes look like little miniatures. I even like the way the turrets on the tank turn prior to firing at the enemy. It's also neat to see vehicles explode and become smoldering wrecks. The game map is overlaid with a hex.  Each unit has a different number of available moves. When you click on a unit, white dots appear around it to show the range of movement that's available. As units fight, they take casualties which is shown by the unit's decreasing strength. During your turn, you have the option of moving your unit, moving and fighting, or reinforcing it. Each ground unit has a zone of control. You can surround an enemy unit simply by placing two of your units on opposite sides of the opposing unit. Units that are cut off CANNOT resupply. Air units include scouting planes, fighters, and bombers. The planes are based at airfields. As with the ground units and sea units, they have a range of movement. As with the ground units, fighters and bombers (but not scouts which are unarmed) have the ability to fly and fight or fly and bomb or strafe. If your forward lines have advanced beyond the Air Force's ability to provide support, the planes may be staged forward if you have overrun an enemy airfield. This game may be played at various levels. Prior to playing I strongly recommend that you go through the tutorial. Each tutorial is linked to a short YouTube video that provides detailed information about the type of game play in question. I like this game because of the combined arms feature. An enemy unit can be destroyed using combined arms by first hitting it with a tactical bomber like a Stuka. Artillery fire can then pound this target. Infantry may launch close assaults. If the unit is entrenched combat engineers or pioneers have access to demolition charges and flame flowers. Tanks could also be used though they're better in open terrain than against a fortified position or an infantry unit that's in a city. It's a lot easier to destroy an isolated unit than a unit that's in line abreast with other units. It's also a lot easier to use your tactical bombers if you've first wiped the enemy fighters from the sky. You may do this by combining multiple fighter attacks upon enemy fighters. If you have anti-aircraft guns within range, they can also provide supporting fire. Each time you take an objective, you receive funds. Funds are used to pay for reinforcements. You may also use these funds to purchase replacement units if you lose units in combat. There are all sorts of scenarios that may be played. You may also play in campaign mode and invade Poland, France, Russia etc. All in all, this is a fun game that I would recommend to anyone who likes the old board games or war gaming with miniatures.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Slitherine product solo player I have enjoyed playing this version of PC(Panzer Corps) over the original for basically two reasons; better animations and campaign diversity. Between each round each flight returns to base instantly so that you start with a fresh air force, even though they remain on the map/location during the opponent's turn. It adds more depth in that you can consider the missions a single strike and return as opposed to area loiter until fuel/repairs needed.On the campaign aspect there are some good choices during your battles to choose your own path when given a choice between two fronts - such as either defending in Kiev or Italy's underbelly. However, most battles progress with historical accuracy even if you kick serious...enemies.  I much enjoyed Sea Lion though, and crossing all of the USA in furthering the Reich.  I also like the Generals card aspect for the units - which allow you to assign a general with certain bonus traits to any company pretty much. This gives you a bit more character to your units as you toy with giving your few generals to units in both land and air.I hope they follow up with more material.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry but PC2 does not deliver anything exciting to the genre. Just more of the same with new graphics. Boring is the word. After a few turns or one hour every scenario feels the same. A tremendous amounts of objectives spread all over the map with race against time. It is the same every single scenrio. No alternative victories. Either you win or loose. Doens´t matter how many losses you inflict or how little losses you sustain. The so called new supply rules are almost worthless. You neither have the time or the ability to actually starve out your opponents since there are towns with supply almost everywhere.But worst of all. The A.I makes suicidal attacks with weak units against strong and perishes in the attempt. The A.I can only control the units immediately around your forces. The rest of the huge enemy units are waiting for you to advance on them and just passively stare at you during the time you slowly progress from one victory point to another and repeat the same boring procedure for every new town.There is no new ideas implemented. No reinforcements during battle for you or the A.I. No alternative victory. No exciting missions. Very boring mission descriptions which lacks atmosphere and historical context. The enemy ALWAYS outnumbers you so there is no historical accuracy at all. Too bad. PC was very good when it was launhed. I cannot see that PC2 brings anything new to the table. Still if you have never played PC or Order of Battle you might like this game. For me it is just more of the same but with better - but much slower graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I enjoy the fact that your units are carried over from mission to mission, gain experience and can be upgraded as new equipment becomes available. _childDocuments_.review: A good game. I would rate it 3/5. My review concerns the campaign mode only.Like most of Matrix' wargames, I think this game was primarily built for online competition against other players, not campaign-players against an AI, as Matrix often arranges tournaments for this game. You should keep this mind.On the negative side then:It is quite unbalanced as a whole - one scenario is rather easy while the next feels impossible, and so on. So it's uneven in terms of challenge, but that's common in games like this. On default gameplay settings, there are only one or two "solutions" in each scenario. So there's a lower level of strategic freedom when compared to games like Strategic Mind and Order of Battle, you are very limited with what you can play around or tinker with. However this sometimes depends on the units you have collected and levelled up for yourself, as the scenarios will give you the choice of two alternative grand strategies, for example: attack through mountains or hills (ideal if you have lots of strong infantry), or big open terrain (ideal if you have lots of tanks and planes).The RNG is odd on default setting, revealing the board-game basis of this game, and it contradicts the RPG aspects of the gameplay: what's the point of levelling up your units when the outcome is decided by fickle and unconvincing RNG, ... however you can adjust the RNG to be more logical in the settings.Likewise the turn-limit is strange on default, either you have lots of time or too little time. Again, a common annoyance in games like this. While you can disable the turn-limit in the settings, it would have been much better if you could simply adjust it for each scenario as in Valor & Victory. Lastly there are things that don't make any sense; in some maps, when my tanks and the enemy's infantry are both (!) out in open plans, my tanks will do literally zero damage againts this infantry. In cities I can understand it, but in open plains? and absolutely zero damage? Open plains are supposed to be the ideal place for tanks and the worst possible place for infantry. On the positive side, most of my issues with this game can be adjusted via the gameplay settings. And that's a huge plus in my opinion, that you can adjust the gameplay to suit your playstyle or skill-level. As a potential buyer of the game you must keep this in mind.The atmosphere, presentation, and visual effects are all excellent. It's a highly immersive game. Likewise the menue-system and the mechanical gameplay are both very intutive, it's an easy game to get into. I really like the RPG elements, where you can choose different approaches for the mission/scenario, adding directly to the replay value. As a whole, because of the gameplay setting options, I think this is a good game.However, the Strategic Mind and Order of Battle games are better in my opinion, if you are looking for a game like this. They were more fun in terms of gameplay mechanics and offered more strategic and tactical options. However if you have already played those and are looking for something similar, this is not a bad option by any means.

_childDocuments_.review: I am mad at myself that I've waited so long to buy and play Panzer Corps 2. It is great turn based strategy game. In comparison to 1st part, when it comes strictly to gameplay, changes are subtle, yet very important and make playing the game so much more fun in comparison to it's predecessor (which was solid game in itself). First of all developers changed the way air forces works - now planes are assigned to specific airfields and automatically return to them after completing their maneuvers in given turn. To expand your air superiority you need to conquer new airfields and assign to them your planes - making it somehow satisfying game of "frog leaps" during scenarios. Secondly it looks like AT guns now give adjacent units supporting fire when they are attacked by armored units. It is small, but logical and pleasant new element of the game.The next change comes from the fact that your army gain heroes after each campaign mission. Those guys got randomly generated skills and can be assigned to specific units - these guys can be pretty powerful and juggling them between your units can be a pretty fun game in itself. For example by assigning heroes you can make your heavy tank unit ignore enemy zones of control or automatically heal one point of strentght after each turn it didn't participate in a fight.I don't like the fact that there is no longer a library (where you could read a lot of interesting stuff about game's units and their actual history) but it is compensated by the fact that there is really clean info about gameplay mechanics that given units provides in-game.Scenarios are another important aspect that in my opinion makes Panzer Corps 2 better than it's predecessor. They are better structured, provide certain "flow" (as I am writing these words I finished the base campaign) and each one felt unique in some way. It is testament to how great it feels to play Panzer Corps 2, when failure in mission didn't make me mad or frustrated but instead it just made me wanting to try another strategy and another units composition.Of course it goes without saying that new 3d maps and unit models looks really nice and move smoothly around the map. Panzer Corps 2 is not only great to play but also to look at.To sum it up, I wholeheartedly recommend Panzer Corps 2 - it is really great game, and even without DLC's it provides a ton of fun and replayability.P.S. Some tips for starting players that will make your life much easier:- use artillery and strategic bombers to soften up enemy targets (especially those entrenched, in cities or well defended positions);- be conservative with spending prestige points during scenarios, it is much cheaper to reinforce your units during deployment phases - try to do it then. Also you can use "shift" key to replenish your troops to certain strenght number;- overstrength is a great tool for tactical and strategic bombers, but also for ground units, especially stuffed with heroes and medals;- don't forget to buy AA units, they provide great defense against enemy planes but also they can be switched to anti armor mode, making them great and flexible element of your army;- a key to win in a lot of scenarios was to have at least two balanced groups of units starting missions in "separate" parts of the map.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Loved PC 1, and am enjoying this even more.  Having a blast trying to figure out "working" strategies and tactics for the campaigns and scenarios. Careful use of your Heroes can really make a huge difference in your success.Over Strength -Don't hesitate to build "super" units.  It costs extra command points and reduces your available maneuver units, but you'll learn to do more with less.  If you can keep them stocked with veteran replacements they'll really kick some butt by the time you're fighting off the Americans or Russians. Anti-Tank-Especially in the Russian campaigns and North African campaigns, you'll need to learn to use Anti-tank units to back your advance.   Towed guns are okay if that's all you can afford, but try to upgrade them to SP units as soon as you can. The AI doesn't seem to always notice (or maybe doesn't care about) an AT unit lurking behind your front line units. And there's nothing so nice as watching an annoying Churchill or IS2 tank lose 4 points before it can launch it's attack.In a cost pinch for multirole, some of the German mobile AA units do a decent job in the early war of killing marauding tanks if you have to assign them to that role.  They're less effective as the enemy tanks improve and you'll have to choose between strict anti-tank support or support against tactical bombers.Good AT units are pretty tough and dependable, but remember you can't use them for overruns. Tac bombers/ Ground Attack - Stukas are your friend, keep the latest in your arsenal, but watch the stats, and don't assume the later variants are better at their jobs.Think of them as artillery with a really long range and they'll stand you in good stead. Later in the war the HS129s provide the punch you need to stop a Soviet or Allied armor advance.  Make sure you give them adequate fighter cover if you haven't got air superiority yet. The FW tac bombers have the advantage of being able to attack enemy aircraft if you're forced to choose between strict ground support and something that can finish off that last annoying point in an allied fighter. Recon-German recon units, bump em to 15, use em.  If you get the hero that allows moving through a ZOC, put him in the recon.  A 15 point recon unit is surprisingly good at single handed attacks on infantry and various pieces of towed equipment.    One of these units can walk behind enemy lines, smash a support unit, and get back out without becoming a sacrifice.So you'll want to prioritize punch and movement points.  This unfortunately leaves the later war PZII out of your arsenal.  The 6 and 8 wheelers are best in this role. Use the recon unit to provide the attack bonus by moving them from point to point and backing your attacks.  It can change an attack from almost 'overrun' to an overrun certainty.Pair that with the hero that prevents you from taking damage during an assault and you'll find the recon unit to be a reliable powerhouse that helps you push through a tough line. They excel at getting around behind and cutting off an enemy unit often allowing you to destroy it rather than see it retreat.  It's great to watch a 6 strength battered IS2 unit 'surrender' because it has nowhere to run, and that's one (or more) less enemy maneuver unit for the AI to restock and hit you with again.In the later years -In general, don't be afraid to surrender victory squares to an overwhelming enemy.  You just can't be everywhere in enough force to stop them.  Pick the places you can defend, let them smash themselves on your position, then breakout and take back the squares you surrendered.  The Recon units are particularly helpful with roving 'behind' enemy lines, snatching unoccupied air bases and towns and earning you those extra points you need to keep your force at strength. Keep an adequate air force and don't let it get burned up at the start of a scenario by trying to halt an advance in it's tracks.  Rather than deploy weak units you were unable to provide replacements for, rotate them to the reserve and hold them there till you can put replacements in them.  There's nothing so frustrating as watching the AI target an experienced but weakened unit and wipe them out. On the other hand as the scenario winds down, avoid the impulse to feed replacements to your units.  Save the points till you've won and replacements are cheaper to buy during the next deployment stage.And as you're falling back towards Berlin and you need a good defensive line, if you can get the "fire support" hero, pair him with a Grenadier unit, and stack it behind or adjacent to an enemy objective you've got occupied with an infantry type. - a good Grenadier unit and this hero will peel off  around 5 enemy infantry strength points with fire support before the actual attack phase, and it probably won't be barraged into insensibility by enemy artillery units in the prep fire for their assault.

_childDocuments_.review: Polished map + unit graphics and UI that is not usually seen in these types of strategy games. It takes a few rounds in the campaign to get familiar with how to best utilize the various units and mechanics, but once you're comfortable with it all (doesn't take long to learn, just a few matches), it makes you appreciate the smoothness of the core gameplay. Easy to jump into for a scenario without eating up your whole day or making you feel like an accountant.If starting out, I would recommend turning off the turn limit while learning the game, as there will be a bit of trial and error so treat this first play-through as a learning sandbox. After that, you can restart a new campaign and set turn limits back on, although I leave it off anyway, don't like playing the clock.

_childDocuments_.review: Panzer corps 2 ticks most of my boxes for a Second World War strategy game. good selection of units reasonable AI, graphically fine, campaign is playable, but some units appear immune to damage when entrenched, good game play options, but a few things could do with a little polish. Why oh why do devs feel the need to add turn count limits which always leave me feeling I could have done better, but had to rush it, on the later campaigns the small amount of turns given are just unrealistic, if you must put this option in then at least give us the option to turn it off. The choice of unit colours (light grey/green) makes spotting enemy and friendly units difficult, how about an option to recolour them?. Finally a flag to show visually which units have spare unused move points available or not as the case maybe. That said on the whole it gets a thumbs up from me

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat skeptical at first - this game rocks!  I've been a fan since its original inception and Slitherine has done an outstanding job capturing the essence of the Panzer General series while incorporating the nuance of more modern strategy games.  Rendering of individual units is extremely well done - and the ability to individualize each unit right down to historic period camo & unit ID marking is a welcome addition to the game.  Additionally, unit enemy AI is much improved (perhaps, too much), and the variety of units is incredible.  There may be some wrinkles yet to be ironed out, regardless, the game is outstanding and well worth your investment!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Has some improvements over the last version, though auxilliary forces are less common. Currently can only play as NSDAP. The two maps for the Poland scenario I've played are very rectangular, which is a departure from past mapping conventions for this sort of game. At the end of each scenario, you receive a hero who can be added to any unit (click on the i on the units icon; was a bit tricky to find). Units can also split into two, and later re-merge, which helps provide frontage. Additionally, units have different slot sizes, scaling in part with reinforcements. You can immediately overstrength units, though infantry seem to start at 15 anyway (but can go up to 20!). I did have some problems with saving until I realized it was a problem with Windows Defender. I paid full price due to COVID-19 cabin fever; I usually wait six months to a year until after a title is released. If this were a normal season, I'd have waited, but at the same time don't feel disappointed in the purchase. For a miser like me, that is saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was an option for "neutral", I'd probably tick that box.I think what disappoints me with this game is the feeling that it could easily have been better - there are some nice touches like the supply and some of the options but I think some of my gripes are:- optimisation - I think I've seen some other comments about how this runs way slower than what you would expect for a turn-based strategy game- the AI - is not good at all in my view and sometimes just does incredibly stupid things - like in a scenario where the AI literally just has to defend, and it uses a decent tank to attack an infantry in a city?? it isn't even really capable of mounting a proper defence - I'm not sure I see the AI as any better than the original Panzer/Allied generals and that was a long time ago. As a result I think the single player is really just about how many advantages you have to give the AI for it to be competitive, given that it is actually quite poor at playing the game.- some of the gameplay mechanics I just don't think work well in practice e.g. it's interesting to be able to use captured equipment but inevitably you then just can't replace it so I'm not sure what the point is in paying to upgrade to captured equipment if after a very short period of time the unit will have to be changed back to equipment you can actually replace. - the DLC. I'm simply not ever going to pay these kinda prices, particularly not for a game which feels like they could have tried a bit harder to get just right.Just to give a clear example of why I thought the AI was really poor - I was playing the main campaign and had selected no core air force option - this was broadly fine until I got to Sea Lion at which point I realised that this mission was really really impossible without a decent air force (see the bit above about gameplay mechanics which seem like a good idea but have some flaw in them). Basically to me it looked hopeless cos without an air force I couldn't get even close to taking on the British navy and trying to invade across the Channel with the British dominating the sea and air....yeah that should be hopeless. But basically after some attempts and spamming some save games I managed to sneak some units across cos the British navy wasn't doing a good job of actually blocking me off and then the British navy just kinda ignored my invasion and mostly carried on beating up my units in North France rather than simply returning to the British coast and bombarding my invasion into submission, and I managed to grab the objectives along the south coast of England. I was relieved to finish the mission so I could continue with the campaign with my by now pretty battered core army but I was just left looking at it thinking how on earth did I win - without a decent German air force the British navy was absolutely dominant and even a pretty poor AI in my view should have been able to hold me off pretty easily. I think it kinda killed my enjoyment cos I just felt like, what is the point in playing against the AI when the AI is quite this bad.I guess my overall feeling is that it's an OK game but they really could have put more effort into some specific areas - I think in particular the fact that the AI is not very good just made me really "meh" about the idea of playing any more single player cos I'm just really not sure it's an interesting challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiplayer is up to a good standard now.Played a couple of coop games all the way through with almost no issue. Only one weird desync was found which will display very different information to each player. We compared by phone pictures. My friend showed units in places I did not see. No idea why this occurs but it only happened in one play through. It also gives no indication that it has happened other than your friend asking what the hell you are doing. With that exception, it was a lot of fun coordinating attacks and achieving victory together. Worth the money.They now have right and left click mouse button commands. So no more left clicky left clicky missclicky.While I got this game mainly for the coop, the single player is really where they focused. The game is well polished and has a lot of neat features. The carry system is my favorite and allows you to keep your units over a campaign and customize them. Now you can paint your units black and give them edgy names like the Despoilers of Worlds... OR something historical. Whatever makes you happy. Very enjoyable strategy game only made more fun with a friend. The coop maps are few right now but hopefully that will expand later.Developers, could you add in a marking system for multiplayer? Be nice to be able to highlight and coordinate attacks. Some strategy games have a mini map ping or a highlighter pen. Anything would be better than me and my friend trying to describe which infantry unit in a group of four similar infantry units is the one that needs the Arty Slapping.OLD REVIEW:Multiplayer is a BUGGY MESS!!!Coop game lasts MAYBE 15 turns before crashing. Coop scenario Minsk fails to share prestige and fails to do asynchronous turns. Tries to treat it as two separate players and starves one player of all resource needs.No save feature for multiplayer means you will NEVER complete a scenario or match before this mess desyncs and ruins all your hard work.Almost every strategy game out there has Left click for select and Right click for command. This game makes selection and command as the same left mouse click. Which means you will constantly be accidentally sending things to their death as you try to look over your units. This occurs with planes all the time and their is NO UNDO in multiplayer. We are in the era of half baked products for customers. Another addition to the,"will patch it" and make it playable in the next couple months pile. AAAVVOOOIIIDDD till they fix their problems.

_childDocuments_.review: This closest analogy for this game I have (never played PzC1) is XCOM but this is more like XCOM on steroids. I find it far more engaging and fun over OOB for example, which is not a bad game in any sense. It doesn't have a massive learning curve like HOI4 but checking out a few tutorial videos on youtube will help immensely - I've also reset a couple of campaigns mid-way back in the low 10's of hours (600+ as of writing) but once you understand you can start playing around with various strategies, approaches, unit composition, challenges, buff/nerfs etc. Seeing some of the other reviews it's worth pointing out (May 2022) the main campaign and the Grand campaign in Axis Ops follows exclusively Germany (duh.. PANZER CORPS?). [edit  2024 - Pacific has been put on indefinite hold and likely isnt happening]. You can play single scenarios with other nations but if you want their campaigns OOB is the way to go. All of that being said the main campaign is lots of fun and also offers historical and ahistorical outcomes, as well as optional paths for which battles you will participate in. Axis Operations started on a rocky start personally I've never finished SCW to the end, 1939 can get sloggish, but with 1940 and by now 1943 it's far improved and loads of fun. I'm sure these will keep getting better as more come out. And at ~8 EUR for ~15 hours to experience every scenario once in an AO the DLC is definitely worth it. (I'd skip SCW but that's just me, since then there is a no ally AI mod which helps) I've only ever had a few crashes that required a re-install a year ago, otherwise the game runs ok - my mid-range laptop runs is perfectly fine on adjusted high settings but some framedrop is to be expected in larger scenarios if you fast forward the enemy turn with dozes of units and during load-ins. Nothing ever as severe as 'some' Total War titles. Overall it's an excellent game with fun mechanics, just enough flavour in terms of background 'story', and a wide variety of units, tweaks, strategies, paths, and approaches to explore - highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.  Balancing issues.  No reason why a bunch of infantry  should kill heavy tanks when they are supported by infantry.  If infantry is in an adjacent hex, or any unit for that matter, they should receive the benefit of the adjacent unit.  That means heavy tanks supported by TDs(or the inverse), supported by infantry, artillery, and air support, should not lose HALF their composition to a lone infantry unit.  Right now the only hex interaction is with artillery and air support, and friendly units to not benefit at all from being adjacent to other unit types.  Granted, there is a slight modification to attack damage, but it is completely unbalanced.  Also, everything is OP, fighters don't support fighters, just tac bombers and strat bombers(which also doesn't make sense).  It's like the hex bonuses from friendly units, is completely non-existent, and not just 'not fully implemented'.  But if you are the kind of person that likes getting your ass kicked because of strange game balancing, and you like WWII nostalgia strat games, this game is great.  It could do with a few more units.  Feels sort of limited.  Also, many of the units become totally inconsequential when something has higher armor.  There are plenty of cases in armored warfare in which tanks with lower caliber weapons defeated tanks with higher caliber and higher frontal armor.  Many tanks have glaring weaknesses, and that tactical element is totally unrepresented thus far.  There is a 'RNG' balancing option, but damage should be based more on probability, resulting in more random outcomes with an emphasis on 300mm effective armor not being taken out by hand-grenades.  Devs: Re-look at game balance, RNG, and friendly assistance from adjacent hexes.  Right now artillery is the only unit with any noticeable effect.  Also, some arty does NOTHING.  Why isn't arty killing anything?  A direct hit from artillery can kill nearly any tank in existence, because the tops of tanks in WW2. and also the slope of armor, was such that a direct arty hit would have substantial effect.  often arty only does suppression damage, and that doesn't make sense.  Same thing for bombers and planes.  The balance isn't there, and friendly unit assistance is either poorly implemented or non-existent.Love the game, just work out the game balance?

The maps are very small, and you are limited to a certain amount of turns to take.Each map has you start on the left and move across 'the board' to the right until reach your goal.  Aaannnddd..... that's it.... that's all there is to the game.Start each board or map with different resources, and then find a way to get to the right side of the board.Sadly, I requested a refund from Steam and was simply ignored.   Not sure why my refund request was ignored.... but whatever.... now I have a game that I will probably never play again.2024 Update:  I wanted to come back to this game to go a little more in depth.  Since I'm stuck with it, I decided to approach it a different way.  While I had higher expectations, I have since lowered them.  Now when playing this game, I simply look at it as a WW2 themed chess game.  Would I recommend it?  yes and no.  I still lean over to the NO side, ONLY because you are forced to a limited amount of turns.  If I completely decimate the enemy down to one capture point and run out of turns, I lose.  War is not so black and white. There needs to be a mod that gets rid of this and let's you just enjoy playing the game.  If it takes longer than the number of turns, then lower my morale or limit my resources, but don't end the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I would definitely recommend this game for the axis operations alone. I'm honestly not a fan of the grand campaign as a lot of the missions are quite bland overall with bonus objectives hardly mattering in the grand scheme of things and the stupid amounts of enemies the enemy starts to throw at you once you hit the Soviet campaign. Axis operations on the other hand start off quite weak with Spain and 1939, but are easily an amazing experience as you watch your units get stronger over time and bonuses from side objectives can have game changing effects which do indeed make it feel like your making some difference in the war. The prestige system is really cool and  starting in the 1940 campaign they start to give you a lot of fun hidden bonuses like captured planes and armor as it seems that the game designers start to populate the maps a lot more with things to do besides capture/hold objective. Overall your mileage and enjoyment of the game really does stem from the traits you pick at the beginning of the campaign with traits like secure perimeters, flexible command, and something grasp (I can't remember the one that double encirclement penalties) really maximizing my enjoyment of the game and making me feel like a big brain strategist for encircling huge swathes of enemy forces and picking them apart and getting a ton of equipment and prestige. The negative traits are also really fun since they change up your force composition a lot, with things such as trench slog really forcing me to use strategic bombers and artillery to break units and making them appreciate these units a lot more than I did beforehand. In terms of the meat and potatoes of the gameplay, I really like how support fire works from artillery and anti-tank and general stat system, though I think that some stats could be elucidated upon like accuracy and imitative. I think splitting is the coolest thing ever. Though I generally dislike the latter half of strategic mind blitzkrieg for it's puzzle game tier bonus objectives and it's ridiculous alt-history, I really wish that Panzer Corp 2 (PC2) took some inspiration from that game in terms of naval combat, air combat recon, and infantry. Naval combat is more focused upon ship modules with clear ship roles and functions that is much more thought out than one ship having one attack and that's it. This makes the distinction between dive bombers against naval targets versus naval strat bombers an important distinction since the you are far more likely to hit the system that you want to hit. I think that strategic mind also does air combat somewhat better with unspotted anti-air guns being able to ambush airplanes that pass over and potentially stunning them for a turn making them a more meaningful deterrent that requires scouting out. I also like how you can move planes one tile after they strike to allow for multiple strikes against a single target in a turn and how they can go further from bases with a more thought out fuel system, but this is more a preference since PC2 air is well balanced as a whole. The same could be said about recon units providing information about hidden stats or the layout of enemy formations on capturing enemies instead of a accuracy bonus, though this again is preference. Finally when it comes to infantry, I really think that PC2 really missed an opportunity to make infantry something interesting since they firstly have a high core-slot cost restricting their deployment on a lot of maps to a handful of units at most with infantry as a whole all being inferior to the pioneers/engineers. In Strategic Mind, the equipment you would provide your infantry with would determine their role and cost which broadly separated reserve infantry designed to simply garrison a point or provide vision from dedicated panzerjagers or assault forces. I could see capturing support equipment from enemy infantry and providing it to your formations to specialize them as a part of an alternative PC2 instead of the bland sidegrades and upgrades that we have in game. In terms of the Axis Operations DLC that I've played so far: SCW: Skipable but has some really great missions like Ebro and Barcelona. Infantry is AI controlled, but you get auxiliaries composed of Italians at the expense of prestige (handed out like cotton candy if you are good at capturing units). 1939: A eclectic set of missions that range from great to puzzle missions. Czechoslovakia is easy if you know what you are doing, but I would never want to replay it. Saarland is really fun though has restrictive maps. Poland has great missions as a whole that are open ended. Finland is terrible and can be skipped and Denmark is a easy stomp. 1940: Norway: Gimmicky and worse than the one in the grand campaign. Ardennes is a Warcraft 3 dungeon( I had fun). Belgium/Netherlands are solid missions and the remainder of the missions into France are excellent. Abbeville and Arras stick out in my mind as examples of this. Sealowe is pretty fun until you get to the London map which is a 30 turn slog. The Balkan maps that you play on are an anticlimax with few bonus objectives and are quite drab. 1941: The Balkan maps start off weak with a mission that exists to show you how mud works. The invasion of Yugoslavia through to Crete are quite fun and give you an opportunity to gear up and abuse paratroopers before you take on the Soviet Union. The opening missions are rather lack luster, but once you hit the Kyiv bonus mission series, the game really picks up with missions that are super fun back to back. I do find that the lack of in-mission dialogue for Moscow to be be rather lack luster and the reward for actually taking the Kremlin is similarly underwhelming, but the mission itself was incredibly fun itself and I felt like my forces were being pushed to their limits. The mission following Moscow is one of the most boring missions they could have possibly made and covers the retreat to Rzevh. 1942: It starts right off from the last mission on the Rzevh salient and you get some more terrible missions. The new character introduced is rather likable and this is where the discussions between your commanders starts to really kick off and become something interesting. I honestly feel that most of the missions in this series are boring as they build you up for Stalingrad which is good fun. The final mission is rather boring; however. 1943: The series of missions immediately after Stalingrad mission set and I chose the alternate history path. The path has you perform a breakout action combined with an escort mission and it is Rzevh but good. Following that shenanigans in Persia and the Caucuses occur which are really fun since you aren't fighting the Soviets before you hit Operation Citadel(Kursk). I think the fact that I'm blanking on this DLC really indicates that the entirety of it is very middling. 1944: For alternative history you spend the lions share of the time being Hitler's fireman. You spend most of the year counter attacking or defending and I thought that it was a really nice change of pace. I thought that this was by far the best DLC in terms of mission quality and story telling and the final mission was very difficult, but was very satisfying to conquer. Balance starts to go out the window here with the introduction of the Panther. Though the unit is really fun to use, it genuinely eats away at a lot of the strategy as the Panther and later models becomes your go to unit and effectively replaces every tank in your arsenal. This was balanced generally by having really difficult scenarios and with stat inflation of the enemies. 1945: Alt his- is narratively bad and the missions are weaker. 1946: No gameplay innovations for new tech and few new units, boring. Overall Score: 7/10. Great overall with some things that are done better by it's competition. Mileage can strongly vary based on the map in question.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I read another review describing Panzer Corps was that it's essentially a card game. I picture a board game with fields for the battles and each military unit being a card with stats. That captures the dynamic. I'm pretty sure that a certain type of person really likes that game.For myself, I had hoped to have more strategic intrigue (rather than playing cards strategy). I had hoped that the terrain would make for really interesting strategies and perhaps strategic placement of units to create impenetrable defenses. The game has a clock. There is only a limited time to finish a scenario. So every scenario has to be played with speed. All scenarios in the campaign that I played were purely offensive without building defenses, creating traps, or carefully tipping the balance of stalemate positions.The scenario clock requires constant advancing. As far as I played, the advancing requires using a mix of different unit types and orchestrating them to move in the right order - always fast but without exposing specialty units to strong enemy units.The "bulk" of the army are tanks and infantry troops. You want to have a mix of both because tanks against infantry in an open field favors the tanks. Infantry dug in during urban warfare causes a lot of damage to tanks. There is a kind of "strategic damage" that doesn't hurt units but lowers their strength. Artillery and strategic bombers dish it out. So the preferred sequence to attack an enemy unit is to soften them with strategic damage so that the infantry/tank can take them out easily without incurring a lot of damage.Bombers (air force) are like a trump card. They allow to dish out damage without really taking damage. There are a number of limitations. An enemy unit can only be attacked by one bomber at a time. (Exceptions exist.). The opposing air force needs to be decimated by fighter planes first. Planes have a limited range. So they have to spend turns getting re-shuffled to better airfields.That's as far as my interest in learning the game went. There are probably better strategies by learning all the unit stats in more detail. However, do I care about learning the detailed stats of twenty different tanks in a game? If I wanted to be a bean counter, I would have become an accountant and would bill people lots of money for bean-counting.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Panzer Corps 2 on and off since release, and I'm confident in saying that this is one of the best WW2 operational turn-based titles, the other being the excellent Unity of Command 2. Panzer Corps 2 offers a very solid campaign experience with mechanics that make sense and plenty of modifiers for those who want to tweak their experience or the difficulty. I also have to praise the persistent units through your campaign, as losing ace tank units really can mean a lot; experience builds slowly, and it pays to really think about your moves before you make them, lest you lose that infantry brigade that's been with you since the beginning.tl;dr if you like the wargaming genre, there's a pretty good chance you'll like Panzer Corps 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Spanish Civil War, Axis Operations 1939 and 1940 dlcs and just quit at the end of 1940. The weakness of the game is that the fictional military and political decisions are not dealt with in detail. The player cannot influence these logistical, military and political decisions because the high command constantly intervenes and prevents the player from decisive victory. Examples are e.g. Dunkirk and the invasion of England, which must be cut short even though I had won every battle. Also, as previously mentioned, important battles that set the stage for the invasion of England, such as the Battle of Britain, are left out. Regardless, I've played about 89.9 hours and it's been fun, but it's frustrating to know that the game doesn't seem to want me to win. Don't get me wrong, I'm not a right-wing extremist, but I want to win. The game AI has weaknesses. During the invasion of Poland, the Soviets are also involved in the final phase and they don't behave cooperatively and attack you, during the invasion of the Czech Republic there are skirmishes with the Czech army, in general I found this operation unnecessary. Perhaps my criticisms of the game  will be handled better in Hearts of Iron. I'll watch this game when I get a chance. I also don't understand why the player can only play the Allied side in a limited way.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a good reviewer so please don't expect an amazingly written piece. Big fan of first Panzer Corps game.  Finally got PC2. Is it a good game that sticks true to the first one? Yes. They carried over most if not all the core mechanics of the first game and expanded on them and did a fairly good job overall. Biggest improvement is of course the graphics. The update looks amazing. Overall a really good Panzer Corps experience and If you liked the first one, then I think you will love this. However, there are a few things that I don't like or should I say am not used to yet. The entire user interface is really clumsy feeling compared to PC1. It's like they took player feedback on what everyone liked and decided to fill the screen with it. Now this is not necessarily bad just "busy" with too much going compared to PC1. It also feels less "crisp" to me as there are some things that have added steps to do from PC1. The other thing that I am trying to "get used to" is the air movement. After every turn planes return to base automatically. In PC1 you could station your aircraft to provide a "cap" or cover for ground units on next turns or even extend the airplanes to hit targets further afield as long as they had the fuel to make the round trip or more. There may be an option to turn this off or change it I don't know yet. So that's about it I guess. It really is a great game if you like the genre, Plus there are cheat codes. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Does the idea of Tiger and Panther tanks blasting M4 Shermans and T-34s appeal to you?  Then this is your game!  In all seriousness though, Panzer Corps 2 is an amazing game and is truly a spiritual successor to the old SSI Panzer General series.  Graphics are great, music is great (the Africa Corp theme is great) and is a blast to play.  The one minor downside to the game is the limited voice acting.  In the old Panzer General, you would get a briefing before and after the mission.  In this, you only get a briefing before the mission.  Despite this, it is a great game and highly recommended to any fan of the Panzer General series

_childDocuments_.review: There's lots of deeply unwise stuff going on this game that were problems in Panzer General 25 years ago and really should've been changed. Instead the developers write weird melodrama briefings/debriefings starring Franco. The game and its tone are extremely condescending, the AI is not very well designed, and only manages to challenge the player by resorting to blatant cheating like seeing through fog of war and hidden map sections, drawing from unlimited resource pools, and using immortal units. Why are stacking limits still a thing? Because that's how it was in Panzer General. Why are unit caps still here? Because Panzer General. Why is the AI still allowed to cheat and just draw from an endless prestige pool? Because thats how it worked in Panzer General. Twenty five years after that game and all the current developer can come up with is better textures and sound effects. Some ideas are cool-like unit splits-but an unwillingness to compromise the basic elements of the PG mechanics means it's use is fairly dubious in a game which builds such imbalanced scenarios all the time. There's no real freedom in how you play, just optimal strats you can look on up a YouTube playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is highly similar to the predecessor games.  The base game has decent scenarios.  The modules (Spanish Civil War, years 1939 to 1947) were all decent, particularly as an extended campaign game.  Yes, the Spanish Civil War is particularly difficult, as all your units start "green" with no experience, and it takes time to accumulate leaders.  But by the time 1939 rolls around you should have a good core force for future endeavors.  Playing at the more difficult levels can be challenging - time and credits are both in short supply!  The leader special abilities can be critical, and that's luck of the draw as far as I can tell.  Good replay value as you crank up the difficulty.  There are some good guides out there to hidden caches and now to use your prestige points - worth looking for and reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Panzer Corps 2

_childDocuments_.review: so something i noticed with smaller developers (and weirdly any game i ever bought from the slytherin group) is that the way these games get balanced is usually that your enemy outclasses you in terms of quantity and quality and the challenge comes from finding ways to defeat that.(i'd not advice anyone to buy it anyways but my complains only start showing around mission 7 or so, too late to get a refund)it's a game you'd think encourages you to attack the enemy in fast movements as in some sort of...blitzkrieg, but out of the fog of war will come massive amounts of enemy units suicidally attacking the one unit they can destroy right now.other reviewers have called it a puzzle game and i agree, to explain why:if this game taught me anything then its that the best german tanks where always heavily outclassed by its french and british counterparts. the enemy will attack you with more, stronger and more experienced units than you have, and round for round it will be your job to single out, along your frontline, 2-3 units you can hammer down with artillery and/or air and then attack to destroy.it's just silly to me that the best tank or tank destroyer i can buy (early game at least) the Stug III or panzer IV has a losing matchup against british tanks. and i am not a wehraboo and i know the british had some pretty strong tanks as well, but in this game they only have those. it's not like you have the tank advantage and the enemy has the better air, they have the better everything and you have to slowly grind them down.you can of course win a scenario first try, but winning it good is a matter of knowing what ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the game is about to throw at you and reload for that one.it's really a shame, panzer general and the likes where some of my favorite games growing up and this game wears it's skin so well that you can get really into it (the first 3-4 missions are fun) before the flaws show up.
