_childDocuments_.review: The game does suffer from various designing mistakes and lack of basic content. The game I did play in beta was way better.The economy nerf during Early Access was simply an overkill,it did make the game flow too slow.Way-find is the worst I have seen in years.Usually a professional game developer would make his units small and able to turn around themself.Usually a unit has a circle around itself, so by turning around it won't block other units.In air units would stay very close to each other.By Crossfire: Legion Units are shaped like big squares and rectangles, this means by turn around they do block each other, even in the air. Even the air units to block each other from fluent moving. Such design is for RTS very unusual and leads to very bad wayfind, as units do get stuck at each other corners. or block each other. There are frequently situations where you do command your units to attack, but the front unit does block the units behind, so several units instead to attack start to run in opposite directions. Even just by 4 tanks, tank 1 does attack while tank 2, does go backwards and blocks tank 3 and 4 to move forward. Another big design mistake is the small unit limit. A unit in games with unit limit does usually take 1 till 5 population. Here by Crossfire: Legion a unit does take 10 till 20 population. Like 2 or even 4 times more than the normal. Max population is by same game mods merely 150. In PvP its 200. So by buy 5 units, you do reach half of the possible unit limit. Problem is by RTS, you kind of need to generate enough units to wrestle down your opponent, this game fails at this basic.As you can't make enough units for proper gameplay experience. OK, designing mistakes are one thing, another is how very little content there is to play the game.  The story mode takes like 3 till 4 hours to finish.Brawl and co-op can not be played, you don't have the AI for it.The game modes that do have AI, have a very bad AI. The AI does simply rush early 2 times with handful of soldiers, after that AI does send units 1 by 1 to die.The AI is even on medium and hard setting, very easy to beat up. The AI on easy setting is same as on hard, the developer did not fix itThe to do list is quite long, which makes overall game very unplayable.-the game needs a better zoom out-the game needs various AI settings-the game needs higher unit limit setting-the game needs better economy desing-the game needs functional way-find-the game needs to change sizes of most vehicle and air units. -the game needs to remove that odd deck build system, which allows only 7 unit typesand that's just to fix basics and fundamental thingsConsidering with Early access, Crossfire: Legion was already for over 6 month in development,and was launched without to address those problems,it doesn't look like the developer can fix the issues and mayor problems the game has.No game can be perfect, but usually an indie game might have not the best graphics, but has a good gameplay.AAA, might have not the best gameplay, but it works well. This game is on all merits a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Major Issues:-Basic path-finding for units (get stuck behind other units or boxed in completely, never seen it this bad in a modern RTS)-Severe lack of units-Additional units need to be unlocked-Units need balancing (Aircraft unlocked at base tier 3 can be easily shot down by basic infantry / base defenses cant stop basic waves of enemies)Pros-Something new, plot seems interesting-Base building has potential Will return after alpha to monitor progressFor the developer:-Game looks great, the art style is smooth, voice acting is great -Consider tiered upgrades for base defenses/turrets-Heavily rebalance unit damage -Have BOTH aircraft and land vehicle factories available at tier 2-Fix the pathfinding-Add more buildable units to all three factions-re-examine the difficulty on that COOP mission, the population cap makes fighting waves of titans too difficult to maintain a supply of forces fast enough to take them down, even with 3 "experienced" players

_childDocuments_.review: Unpolished would be an understatement. So many things are just unnecessarily bad. Unnecessarily because most of them are mistakes, other games made decades ago and one should think devs learned from them. Like putting the autosave point during camgaign missions BEFORE a cutscene and making cutscenes not skipable! On top of that, you cannot save manually! So if a mission is hard and you resume from the last savepoint, you´ll have to watch the (very much uninteressting, cause campaign story is lame AF) cutscenes over and over again!On top of that:-unit movement is terribel, vehicles turn/spin on the spot while "sliding" around (and no, not hovercraft, BUGGYS and TANKS)-pathfinding is atrocious because units block each other constantly, so they turn around and search for another path, but all do that the same time, apart from the ones at the firing line (looks like as ant hive)-no "stances" (hold position, defend, etc.) what makes this so frustrating because EVERY unit rushes into combat, including your support or low HP units!-you can adapt you army roster prior match, but the units have no values whatsoever (like atck dmg, hp, armor, etc.) which makes this adaptation kinda pointless. -graphics look kinda 2010 ish. I don´t mind "retro" but this is not it.Overall the hoped "C&C feel" is not to be found and you just feel annoyed by the uncapability of your units due to the bad control/unit behavior.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this game is in early access I'll review it over time with periodic updates. I have been an rts gamer since the 90s starting with warcraft 2/starcraft 1 and branching out to other franchises like c&c, aoe, sup com, dawn of war, battle for middle earth, and some indie titles. I heard about this game via a sponsored article for like ign or something. I'm also signed up for the frost giant beta. Point is - I love the rts genre. Since it's hanging on by a thread, I'm down to try anything. INITIAL REACTIONS: The following reflects 2.5 hours played and completed act 1 of the campaign on normal. Pros: -controls are intuitive as they are basically the same design philosophy of all blizzard rts games. -runs well on my potato PC (for reference this pc was made to play borderlands 2 on ultra settings. it's that old.)-sound effects are appropriate, not overwhelming or underwhelming. acknowledgement voice-lines could be more varied/not trigger with every input.-the main menu navigation is clear and uncluttered.Cons:-loading times are longer than I'd like, could be my computer, could be lack of optimization. In any case it's unclear because it will show 100% but a 5 minute countdown timer? -clicking on a specific unit from the group select deselects all others which is not ideal when i'm trying to use individual unit abilities in succession. I was trying to avoid making a ctrl group for every unit type. -it's not always very clear what's happening at any given moment in a campaign level. It can be annoying to lose half your units before you realize what's even killing you, particularly stage hazards like spotlights that shoot missiles, or no indication of how long a turret is "hacked" until it starts shooting you again. -too many units with abilities can be overwhelming. consider making more abilities toggle to auto-cast or simply be passive. -often I find myself supply blocked by the blue resource while I have more orange resource than i'll ever need. With no way to increase my blue resource income it bottlenecks my ability rebuild and thus play the game and you never want your player waiting around for something to do. Consider adding a main base ability to convert one resource to the other (perhaps inefficiently and/or with a significant cooldown) so i can get back into the action faster. Let me die not from hunger, but in combat!UPDATE 1:I'm now 4.5 hours played and completed act 2 of campaign on normal difficulty. Due to size limitations i will delete redudant feedback from initial review.Pros:-I continue to be impressed by the usage of recognizable VO's (Global Risk leader is Adam "I never asked for this" Jensen himself! Instant <3) and the cut-scenes continue to surprise and delight. -The mission design is commendable overall. Some are obviously more original and inspired than others. The time limits provide a sense of urgency while being completely fair, but most anything can be overcome with mass air alone which could be addressed (eg by having AI actually use their ensnares). -I LOVE the dichotomy of the three factions which are instantly distinguishable by aesthetic in the campaign. I wouldn't have believed going into this that three "human" factions could manage to be this distinct. -The music and overall "look" of the game (in addition to the above mentioned Adam Jensen) gives me serious Deus Ex vibes which for me is a big plus. -Little post mission lore bits also make me want to learn more about the universe, but I feel like they could use more depth.Cons:-I've noticed some lack of polish in various places within the campaign such as a mission loading screen that repeated itself, a post mission lore thingy with missing ) and even an "audio log" that had no audio attached to it. These may seem minor but that also suggests to me they could be EASILY and quickly corrected. Polish is important for making people take a new IP seriously. -Pathfinding and more critically "crowding" as i'll call it, continue to plague the efficiency of army in game. I had tanks bouncing around like headless chickens while my infantry soaked up damage and got mowed down by enemy armor because the two unit types shared a max range and the tank couldn't find a way around them. It would really benefit the units to push each other when actively engaging the enemy, or even having armor and infantry not share collision (the way air has zero collision) but leave armor-to-armor and infantry-to-infantry collision active. This should be a priority for the devs.-I don't love the building upgrade system as a gate for unlocking units to construct. I assume the point was to declutter bases by not having so many extra buildings just for unit upgrades or supply, etc. (btw is there something that controls population cap?) However, I end up spending a lot of idle time waiting for upgrades just to build something, and when my building dies, I have to research the building tier AGAIN to get to build the units I need to counter the enemy, making snowballing very prevalent. Honestly, i'm not sure how this can be addressed. Perhaps once a particular building upgrade has been researched, any built afterwards start at that level?-Static defenses (turrets) are absolutely worthless in the campaign. Does this hold true for pvp? No one likes tower rushing in rts games, but at least in your own base one should be able to hold off a 2-4 man infantry push or 1-2 armor/air units. The campaign is most exciting when I'm not guarding my base from a handful of distraction units, so at least make static defense worth investing in during the campaign by buffing them.Suggestions:-Focus on continuing to polish the presentation of the game by fixing the errors mentioned above and improving the loading times as well as game-engine so that there are fewer hiccups and stutters when an event triggers or new assets load. -As in the previous review, I now very much want to see an appendix added to the game that allows you to review any post-mission lore thingy's without having to replay a level, in addition to character bios, location dossiers, historical events references in the campaign missions, army unit descriptions and lore, etc.-I would like to see a testing ground (aka live fire arena) where I can spawn in units and compare them against one another to study their combat effectiveness and test strategies. No rts has ever had this outside of map editors which are separated from the proper game, but i would LOVE to see something like this break ground here. Fighting games have long featured "training mode" which continue to improve in quality and enable new players to better understand the game and jump online into pvp, why not have the RTS genre do the same since multiplayer is fundamental to rts success, even pve coop. -Don't stop making updates, i'm really getting attached to this game and find myself thinking about it when I'm at work. TL;DR: 7/10, would recommend a combination of deus ex, c&c generals, starcraft 2, front mission, and dawn of war appeals to you. Needs polish, has rough edges, but devs appear committed to updates.

_childDocuments_.review: So, they wanted to make the new Starcraft using a popular in Korea Counter-Strike imitation series. Realizing nobody wants grind and unlocking units to premium the developers disavowed that idea. Nowadays realizing that most folks want a singleplayer fun experience and multiplayer scene is pretty small, they are trying to pivot to that, while still steadily adding variety of content, rebalancing and fixing things. They're a very commendably dedicated and passionate team but I wonder, can this RTS really be "saved" somehow?For starters, this game is kinda like... near future Starcraft? What Victory Games wanted to do with CnC Generals 2 would be a pretty accurate comparison too, lack of garrisoning aside. There's extremely classic RTS resource collection points, researches and such involved, and there's three factions - the standard military with a love of going defensive and long ranged, the ambiguously terrorist freedom fighter guerrilla group with stealth and hit and run options, and hi-tech faction that's, well, corporate human Protoss. Overall every faction, character in campaign and unit is something you have seen somewhere else before if you've played plenty of games like this, I won't lie.Now, the main selling point is that everyone gets a very modest roster of units, and there's quite a variety of unique ones for each faction, plus different commanders offering special abilities. Conceptually it's sound, Starcraft 2's monobattles have proven you can have and depth with one unit type per player in a big team battle, and it keeps gameplay accessible for rookies by maintaining lighter focus, and allows more experienced players to have fun with unusual or smarter builds. Thing is, this leads to battles feeling less varied than in many other RTSes, and some unit types like transports ended up super neglected, so they later on walked back and added those in as a unit you can train from base instead of requiring to be picked, and allowed barracks to have an extra slot. It's nice but just shows how questionable this loadout mechanic can be. Maybe it would have worked better in faster games like what Command and Conquer Rivals on mobiles is, with more tight and fast paced combat, but this game has very standard for an RTS map scale. Also, regular play has a limited pool of energy for all the calldowns and special commander abilities, once those are used up you can't get them back. Huh, why? You'd expect at least a lategame structure or research unlocking ability generation but nope, once gone it's all gone. So it all boils down to units and those... don't have any common fun interactions like cover or special terrain, and abilities while often fun aren't that outstanding to carry the game.One thing I really want to commend is the art. While units are fine, distinct and readable, they're still just mostly isngle colour dudes. But environments? Environments are super sweet, the maps this game has are all varied and got nice pleasant details to it. And the cinematics the campaign has? While the story itself doesn't go anywhere and is mostly a tutorial to try all three factions, the cinematics it has got a fantastic style and flair to it. This game's artists are the real MVPs, wish the story had more to it than this though.I wish this game's team didn't (have to?) game for it to become the next big competitive online RTS so it could reveal itself as singlepalyer or co-op experience earlier, overall it's a functional and competently made RTS but it always feels like it's offering less, plain less, without the whole less is more expression applying to it, and despite a nice loadout mechanic idea nothing else actually is that fresh, it's disappointingly stagnant.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending approximately 12 hours with the game, I have to say, I see some potential with it. It still has some rough edges with respect to the unit path finding and balance, but that is sort of expected at this stage. The sound effects are cool, the voice acting is quite decent, and the factions seem cool. Having said that, at the game's current stage, I feel that some of base building and teching is a bit too simple. Virtually all units have a single, specific upgrade to them which sometimes feels a little extraneous. Most of the unit upgrades are interesting enough, but some feel like they were put for the sake of simply having an upgrade (e.g. the Javelin armor upgrade). Moreover, researching upgrades doesn't feel like too big of a commitment so naturally you'll find yourself getting them all by the mid to late game.Which brings me to my next point. Maybe I am really bad at the game, but I find myself having far too many resources banked up. I try to be aggressive and keep my units active, but no matter aggressive I play I just always have extra resources. Building a new army as my enemy comes barreling towards me isn't a major issue either. It just feels a little strange and maybe unfair. There is a unit cap to the game so simply making more when you're maxed isn't an option. Maybe they could put some kind of penalty such that if your stockpile gets too high, your workers start collecting at a reduced rate. Or maybe make units more expensive. I'm just spit-balling ideas.Another piece of feedback to the devs, the combat lacks some nuance. Although not completely so, I feel some of the time I can get away with winning games by simply zerging hard. There aren't too many situations where I need to micro my units carefully (other than dumping all my abilities in a fight). Maybe there should be some units that are designed to easily deal with grouped up enemies (so as to discourage players from making giant deathballs; something similar to the High Templar from SC II). I know that easier said than done, but it would really shake up the game in a nice way.Having said all that, I still do think this game has the potential to shine. It's awesome that you can select which units you want before beginning the battle. Pre-planning before playing is an interesting idea and I'd like to see where that goes. Some themes for the factions like Black List's use of stealth and ambushing is really fun and I enjoy that mechanic a lot. Global Risk units seem to be designed to work in groups that compliment each other well. e.g. shield troopers taking the front and having some kind of artillery in the back. I could go on but I think you get the idea.Please don't be so quick to judge the game. I noticed many reviewers hadn't even played the game for more than an 1 hour and already they are writing scathing reviews. I doubt you could get any understanding of the game in such short time; even for veterans too. Doesn't seem justified to me and I really do hope the devs make this into a great game. I've been dying for another fast paced RTS!

_childDocuments_.review: An okay RTS.There's a campaign with 15 missions. The briefings are quite barebones though. Most of them only show an animated map and what you're supposed to do. There's not much character interaction, so when there's a rare scene involving characters, they come across as cliche. It doesn't help that the ending has a main character meeting the villain at the top of a skyscraper and things play out almost exactly like a certain RTS with a similar scene.Compare that to the classics where before a mission, there's character interactions, then when the mission starts. the map pans around to show what to do where.The units don't have much personality either. Some don't seem to have voice lines. Some units like the Hades don't even seem to have firing and projectile impact sounds.The game looks and sounds good. It's pretty well put together, and easy to get an idea of what each unit is supposed to do just by looking at it. Air units seem to be a little too big though.Deck creation is a slight minus. The game features a deck creator to customize your factions. It wasn't immediately obvious that each slot only covers one faction. For one they're poorly named, i.e. "Default 1". It looked like the factions were tabs so I saved 3 times, then wondered where my edits for the first 2 factions went, before going Also, the deck editor doesn't provide enough unit information to make a decision, and there's no wiki out there. Range, sight, movement speed, resource and supply cost and damage type are important stats that aren't shown.It's fun the same way most RTSes are fun. Lots of rockets and lasers flying around and explosions. But so many missed opportunities.The deck creator could have been part of the campaign. It would have been so fun to play through the campaign, unlock new units for the deck, and plan out what to bring for each mission. That would have added so much replay value but nope, units are pre-decided.Decks themselves are way too small. Important units end up fighting for the same spot. For instance, air superiority shares the same slot as dropships, so you can clear the skies but then there's nothing to drop afterwards. Repair vehicles fight for the same slot as main battle tanks, so there wouldn't be a whole lot to repair since there's no frontline presence. The options are too few for strategic choices, so it feels more like a poker draw.Then there's the RTS genre. Just about every other RTS out there follows the same old formula of basic campaign that functions as a tutorial, then go all in on multiplayer PvP esports. Following this is kind of like sending a bunch of squishy units up a fortified ramp. It's very difficult to build up the same features enough to break through. The campaign is shorter, there's less units on the map, decks are tiny so there's less unit variety, and the worst part is the gameplay has less features than 10 year old classics. For example no garrisons or bunkers, no unit veterancy, no faction-wide gimmicks like Burrow or Liftoff etc.The esports push isn't even subtle! Automatch is a ginormous button right in the center of the menu, everything else like Campaign and Custom Game (i.e. Skirmish) is half the size and pushed off to the corners.On top of that, campaign mission design is kind of cryptic. A few times you're given a tiny force next to a ramp, but if you go up the ramp there's a ridiculous amount of enemy troops that melt your army so you have to restart, then it turns out you're supposed to go down another path. Or there's an escort mission and you don't expect the escort unit to be so stupid as to keep advancing suicidally by itself after a checkpoint but it does, so a restart is needed. Overall the campaign is doable though.Also the pathfinding isn't great, units seem to traffic jam on each other easily. Even when they can easily turn and drive around other units, they insist on waiting for a straight line that's blocked.Overall 6/10. If you like RTSes, it's okay. Nothing that feels super new or interesting, a little bit janky, quite limited but fun to mess around for a bit. Buy it on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial impressions are "so far, so good".It's definetly on the "early" side of early access - Unit animations, movement and pathfinding is wonky and need work, the zoom in is claustrophobic, some menu screens need more polishing and love in terms of feedback, but it seems to be a pretty decent game overall.It has an interesting unit loadout mechanic (unless you're a type of player who gets a seizure whenever they see a soft currency in game) that lets you customize your armies to a degree, decently varied factions, and a neat overall gameplay style - Imagine a weird mix of Starcraft and Command & Conquer (of the Generals variety).  After a few skirmish and multiplayer games I can see a lot of potential here. I wish some details were different (e.g. I hate hovering jets, I'd prefer if they actualy behaved like airplanes) but most of them bog down to the game's style and not objective gameplay issues.The graphics are nice, sound design is surprisingly strong (great music and positively apocalyptic soundscape), you get a fully fledged multi with an OK-ish selection of maps across 2 competetive modes, a PvE mode plus full fledged 15 mission campaign. For the price tag - It's a solid package, I think it's worth a shot. Especialy given how very few RTS games we're getting it deserves a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of RA2 and SC2 and it pains me to say this but I am really not enjoying this game.Unit pathing is terrible.  There are no unit formations or options to use them.  For a game that is supposed to be low on micro management I found myself constantly making sure my armies could move close enough to the enemy so that all of the units could shoot.  If I auto attacked an area unsupervised my whole army would be destroyed with the faster units running to their deaths and the slower units lagging behind.  I would expect this from older games but it is 2022 and I am still having to micro manage more than I did in SC2 back in 2010.There is no ability to change the hotkeys, this was a big issue for me as the campaign focused a lot on commander abilities which for some reason they have hard-coded to Alt-W and Alt-E (absolutely terrible hot key idea) and you cant change it in the options menu.  I found myself constantly having to click the screen to give commands rather than use hot keys which is an RTS gamer's worst nightmare.  The campaign mode has no checkpoints or ways to save.  I played on Normal difficulty and had to replay the second mission 4 times in a row because my units kept dying and I did not have a base.  That mission in particular felt way harder than it should have compared to the missions before and after, and it would have been nice to add at least a checkpoint so players don't have to keep playing the mission over again in it's entirety. I can tell they were going for a mix of SC2 and RA2 in the game, and while the overall game play is similar to those games, Crossfire: Legion just feels like a cheap knockoff of both of them when it comes to the gameplay itself and the lack of QoL features.  Maybe they will fix these issues in the future but I am refunding the game until then.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels and looks pretty good, I especially like the presence of multiplayer coop content.The game is pretty simple, you can only take a small selection of units with you in a game and they're all extremely specialized. Stripped to its bare bones it's kind of like rock, paper, scissors but more layered. Perfect for people who have no experience with RTSs.The game has a full campaign. I think a good single player (or co-op) campaign is the basis for a good RTS. That's how most people got started with them. It's not a placeholder campaign either, it has a story with voice acted characters and cutscenes.The game looks great, very clean, very sharp look. You can easily tell the units apart from the environment. You can really zoom in and appreciate the units' animations. Everything from how units move, to how buildings upgrade, to death animations, they're just great.The sound design is also great. Boom-y explosions, Bwoom-ing lasers and RATATATATA-ing machine guns. When you have fights with diverse unit compositions they sound so chaotic and impactful, you can tell something is dangerous by the sound it makes, and you can hear gunshots in the distance.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential. I enjoy RTS mainly for PVP and base building/combat. Heavy C&C vibes here which is a good thing. For under $30 this is a good pick up if you are a fan of RTS base building games. I hope people give it a chance because these games live or die on player count. If it gets a healthy player base i believe it will do very well. There is a lack in active communities for base building RTS games right now. (AOE SC2) C&C3/red alert is dead. The units are cool, the upgrades are cool, and i like the the defensive turrets. One of my favorite things to do in these games is build up heavy defenses around choke points. As far as base building RTS games go this one is pretty good. Id say give it a shot. The game is in early access so i'm interested in seeing what they implement down the pipeline. Very Powerful, interesting additional tactic choice here.Cons.:- It is not as polished as a release should be IMO. Pathing of units, Interface, Menus, Settings, Rebinds etc. should have been working at release IMO. Mouse speed is not changeable. -> But this will all be fixed in upcoming patches and so it'll be much more relaxing to play, there I have no worries.- Not quite that much player queuing ranked. But that'll change as the patches come in. Also through Discord you can always find someone to playtest and have fun :)-----I really whish for creative people who make some more maps, also that more people come in, giving it a try and getting together in Discord. _childDocuments_.review: Sowas wie ein Light C&C für die stunden zwischen durch..Was ich an den Game ändern würde:Freies bauen und nicht so wie es jetzt ist, Base Stützpunkt gebaut und nur 5 Sammler pro Ressource?! Also es ist nicht so wie bei den C&C Teilen wo jeder sein MBF hinstellen kann wo er will und Tiberium zum sammeln rum liegt, schade...Bauen ist beschränkt, weit kommt man nicht, jedes Gebäude  (Kaserne, Panzerfabrik, Luff Fabrik) kann nur 3 unterschiedliche Einheiten produzieren.Kampf, auch hier gibt es Beschränkung denn wer denkt erstmal aufbauen und dann mit der Masse den Gegner platt machen, der wird das hier leider nicht finden... schade.Zum Schwierigkeitsgrad, sobald man das Rushen der KI überlebt hat, ist es easy und machbar... danach hat die KI nichts drauf! Auch die KI der eigenen Einheiten ist dumm, weil sie keine anderen Laufwege nimmt sobald der weg versperrt ist.Trotz allem, eigentlich für die 20€ ein gutes Spiel für den kleinen hunger zwischendurch.Mit mehr Spielern und weniger Limitierung würde es bestimmt richtig Spaß machen.EN ::::Something like a light C&C for the hours in between.What I would change about the game:Free build and not the way it is now, base base built and only 5 collectors per resource?! So it's not like the C&C parts where everyone can put his MBF where he wants and tiberium is lying around to collect, too bad...Building is limited, you can't go far, each building (barracks, tank factory, air factory) can only produce 3 different units.Combat is also limited here, because if you think you can build up first and then flatten the enemy with the masses, you won't find that here, unfortunately... too bad.As for the difficulty level, once you've survived the AI rush, it's easy and doable... after that, the AI has nothing! _childDocuments_.review: I am a really big fan of the RTS genre. AOE (1 and 2), Warcraft 3, C&C 1 and Starcraft Brood War rocked my childhood and adolescence. And I continue to play AOE 3, Red Alert 2 and 3 and Stacraft 2 during a very long time. So I think I know well the RTS genre. Crossfire Legion for me fell somewhere between Starcraft and Red Alert, but is way closer to the second one in my opinion. It bring one new feature, which is the roaster system, which I will talk about later.  For me, when I saw this game out, I was so much hyped. It offer a genre that is currently pretty much dying on the market and plus they bring back the C&C flavour which very pleased me. So I bought it, after a lot of hesitation, while it was in special. My review : Graphics : its okay. It do the job. But sometimes it feel a little bit too much cartoonish, like a mobile game. But I dont blame the devs for that. After all, AOE 3 and 4 and Stacraft 2 went for the same approach aesthetically. But at the same time, some things were odd : some vehicles are way too small if compare to infantry or even buildings. Gameplay :- The pacing is pretty fast, keep that in mind. The match look very short in general. Prepare for early rush. - The path system is not good. You will rage against your unit that block each others and advance in disorganized horde. - Be prepare for a very high micro managing experience. Because each units can have 1-2 abilities. - You will have to use a lot of hotkeys. Which is well done by the devs, but it is intense and korean lvl.  - The UI is standard. I feel like it should stand out more of the background because for me it shade out a little and sometimes I searched for obvious things. - The ressources system is way too much like starcraft (fixed ressources of steel/mineral and gas/fuel). There is not much buildings and the base building and economy is very narrow and shallow, pretty boring. You feel like you saw everything after 15 minutes in game. There is not much buildings or tech.- I thought that the roaster would be rock paper scissor style, but it didnt feel like that. It really feel like the high tier units are simply OP and very hard to counter specially when they are spammed. The units are okay. I think there should be way more of it. Some are a little cliché and very generics. But some are interesting and unique. I like the roaster system. But at the same time, each ''card'' in your roaster offer you a choice of only 3 units. And you have about  7-8 total cards I think in your roaster. You can only choose one unit by card, and each units are only available in one card. Which mean that yes you may ''custom'' your roaster but there is not so much variety and again the IA seems to always use the same roaster. By example, you cannot go with a roaster full of vehicles or infantry. And you cannot give a lot of thematic to your army.Now, the real big problem for me. The IA and solo play is horrible, atrocious, stupid and broken. In fact, it is a pain in the ass (sorry for the words). Even on the easiest difficulty, the IA is way too hard. When on normal, it look like the enemy replenish almost all its army in a very short time if not instantly. It did it in every game I played while I was in their base destroying buildings. I played 3 match and I was unable to win once. I even attacked an enemy base with a full stack of tanks fully upgraded (I was desesperate) and wasnt able to beat them. The enemy just spam fully stack of high tier units again and again until I rage quit. I controled all the ressources spot on the map and cornered the enemy in its starting position, sieging it there, trying to use an atrition war, sending in the meat grinder my armies, but it did nothing. This frustrated me, because I dont understand how the IA could still survive this control of the map from me and all the firepower I threw at it constantly. This is simply not fun at all. And the patch seems to be almost only multiplayer balances, bugs corrections and some new units. But I dont feel this is what the game need right now. So I assume the game is focus on online play PVP. Which I like, but I want my RTS games to offer me a good solo experience (in campaign and skirmish or custom) before going on the online experience. Right now the game can only be started online. I finish this review by saying that the game is pretty much low on player base right now and there is like 10-30 players online I think which is pretty low. So for a game which focus so much in the online gameplay, it became its weakness.

_childDocuments_.review: Crossfire Legion is an Action fast-paced RTS game I love this type of RTS, it is a mix between C&C and Starcraft, and its gameplay speed is close to a game called Act of War, there are many units to choose from, and The best thing about this game is its units design with excellent artistic appearance, I think the game well balanced but need more maps for its classic skirmish mode and also I hope team color will come in the next update

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a modern cross of C&C & Terran-based StarcraftImmersive, good graphics, fun and easy to pick up.The factions offer a bit of variety, and the card load out system is interesting. The starting commanders and units are powerful.More unit and commander options would be great.Earning the in-game currency feels fair and rewarding.It is earned by playing games and achieving objectives, you can't spend money to skip or get more.The campaign is very short (First act, takes only a few hours to finish) but the quality is good.if the rest of the missions are similar, it will be good value.The game mode variety is good, the AI is serviceable, to get started.Overall, I'm interested to see where this goes.Pretty good, fun RTS!

_childDocuments_.review: Torn between recommending this or not as it's more of a "mixed" impression.Pathfinding is a nightmare, gameplay can be a bit jarring and doesn't feel completely smooth. That said, it's a neat concept, cool factions and the story is predictable, but interesting enough.Decent narration and voice acting. It's.. an okay game. Some MP issues with the co-op scenarios, but that might just be us. If you are in need for RTS and you don't have anything else to scratch the itch with, this does an okay job.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, absolutely, as an RTS fan, I strongly recommend it. I was very pleasantly surprised by CL, three very diverse factions, each with about 20 units or more each, commander powers, the units and all look fantastic. Game plays exceptionally well, playing all settings maxed at 4K, played the demo then just bought the game, this is an absolute steal for the current sale price, to me, worth it at full price. Didn't know what CL was prior glad I discovered it, truly a labor of love. Many are saying skirmish doesn't work, I don't get that, just played three skirmishes offline with the AI and the AI built and handled its abilities on a very impressive level, constructed all of its units, deployed, created defensive areas, etc. Definitely an overlooked gem, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: It is fine. But weirdly laggy even on decent hardware. I even reduced the graphics to the lowest settings, but there are no difference. It keeps rubberbanding (slows down then suddenly fast then normal) which is very annoying. Even on an SSD, it lags. It is very, very laggy at times, and i cant say it is because of the hardware because I can play heavy spec requirement games just fine.As for being a CrossFire game, it is kinda disappointing it does not have much connection to the FPS game aside from the factions and mentions of Ghost and Shadow kits. I was expecting to see some form of appearance of several FPS character/avatar styles on infantries (well BL variety Matahari looks lik Jackal or something at least)As for being an RTS, it feels like a weird mix of Red Alert 3 and Total Annihilation, I guess. _childDocuments_.review: I am going to refund this game after less than 0.5h of play. While being a huge RTS fan this game doesn't really feel that great. It doesn't have any charm to it that sets it apart from other RTS titles.I can forgive the clunkiness of the units, the controls, the pathfinding of the units at this early stage of the game, i do believe those things can be fixed in the future and i don't even mind the currency ingame to unlock new units as you progress through the game, i don't think its really necessary since you can introduce players to new units through your campaign missions, but trying something out that isn't a standard for the RTS genre...okay, whatever...may aswell try it out and see what the feedback is.But the dealbreaker for me is that it doesn't provide me with a great story/setting/style, it just feels so generic like i have played this same exact game for the 100th time now while i haven't even played that many RTS games in my entire life. Starcraft and Warcraft had great stories, were set in unique universes and even had unique factions and units to set the factions/races apart from eachother in their universe. This game has none of that, its sadly very boring, monotone and generic. I wish the developer best of luck since i'd like the RTS genre to stay alive, but this particular game simply isn't ment for me.

_childDocuments_.review: + 3 unique factions with a good variety of different units+ Campaign with cutscenes (beautifully made – BBI style), quite interesting story, proper voiceover and varied enough mission styles+ I do enjoy graphics and art style in this game – especially environments and mechanical units+ Many different game modes – standard skirmish, brawl, payload, battle lines + Sound effects of guns are top-notch in this game+ OST fits atmosphere of the game nicely (even though it’s not really special) + Game runs really smoothly for me and I didn’t encounter many bugs + Card system is actually quite interesting and lets you improvise with different strategies+ Decent price for content -  Would love more options when setting up skirmish game with AI – choosing difficulty for each AI player, choosing color for each faction, maybe even choosing battle cards for each player- View is a little bit too zoomed in for me- Pathfinding of units needs more work- 9 or 10 battle cards for army would be perfect (7 is not enough)- Would love to see infantry scaled down a bit - immediate immersion improvement and maybe it would even help with pathfinding a bit
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: Card system kills the vibes man, once I got ingame and realized that I could not use the all of the units designated to each faction I had to dip. If there were more selections as in C&C then this might be somewhat acceptable, but in the state it's currently in - armies feel small and bland. Honestly, why even add in soo many cool units and then only let people select a few ? Really bad design option IMO, though I'm sure there will be a few who "like" it. You guys almost had a C&C successor and you dropped the ball, this game is not worth $30. Honestly I wouldn't even give $20 for it.If I catch a 50% off sale at some point ( which I'm sure I will, as you can see the game is not doing too great on sales) I'll probably pick it up to gather dust in my library, all-the-while hoping developers realize their missed opportunity and remove the stupid boundaries they set in place.

_childDocuments_.review: Skirmish vs AI feels horribly unbalanced and tailored towards going with exact key of actions to be able to survive and even then I'm not sure it's gonna be possible. And that's on "Easy" difficulty... and I "comp-stomped" expert AI's in CoH1 and CoH2. _childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the single player campaign in this game and have observed the developers making good changes on the multiplayer side to prepare the game for release. _childDocuments_.review: For 20€ its ok, but i would still not recommend it to my friends.I just played a few rounds vs. AI to learn the game and the units, its quite nice if you into that genre. It feels like Starcraft with a C&C skin, but without the charme of either of them.A few rounds skirmish was ok, but i would not play this against higher difficulty or even Multiplayer, its not polished enough for that.Examples are: - Units dash into terrain instead of the destination.- you can adjust the sound in the comma section, but it is always at 100% no matter the setting until you get to 0.- Invis units lurking for an ambush with a short dmg buff after they leave invis, but they get kicked out of there own mates when they walk buy due to collision physics.- Pathfinding is at bare minimum, with units stuck in a loop if they cant reach destination. Goes well with the huge invisible hitbox small infantry has. Once a single infantry blocked a whole road for my big tank. - I once got defeated for unknown reason and was back in the lobby and every selection button was deactivated with a small "!" but without a tooltip.- Micro managemend is fiddly.- Unit balance is atrocious, Anti-Infantry unit gets easy killed by infantry.- The bigger/expansive the unit the more underwhelming it gets.- Repair time of buildings is so long, its better/faster to just build them again.- little bugs/glitches as weird explosions even nothing is shooting, or buildings who are fresh droped suck dust in, insteand of blowing it away.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally unbalanced where even on easy mode my troops are getting slaughtered or overwhelmed by huge numbers at the very start of the campaign or skirmish mission. Movement is terrible where units will not always go where you tell them to or they go there and suddenly turn around and go back to where they are previously while the rest of my force is facing the enemy and getting destroyed. Build times are really slow so when the above happens it means waiting to get a nice size force raised up again only to get butchered once more by a too powerful force despite the fact that even when facing smaller numbers they are like bullet sponges taking huge amounts of damage compared to my units.Way too frustrating which is not why i play games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I would like a neutral option for review since it's neither good nor bad. It's basically a mediocre casual RTS game you can pick up and finish the campaign on a weekend.The in-game graphics and effects look quite nice and shiny. Cinematics were obviously made on a budget though so they don't look good.The gameplay mechanics in the campaign are pretty casual. You have infinite resources on one base and you gather resources so fast from that one base that you can essentially just spam units from one base and win. There is no need to expand. In the missions where you have no base, you sometimes need a bit of micro but nothing too hard. I played the whole campaign on hardest difficulty and finished it in like 6 hours without much trouble.The story of the campaign is not bad but it is not good either. It's pretty short and shallow and doesn't really make the effort for any serious world-building or character development. The campaign seems to be designed more to introduce the units than to tell an engaging story. It's just kind of bland.The multiplayer is interesting as you have fewer and slower moving units compared to games like Starcraft and Red Alert so it could be less dependent on APM which I like but unfortunately, there aren't really enough players playing MP at the moment so I'm not sure if MP will be relevant.There are some coop missions as well but I haven't tried them.In conclusion, if you are expecting something like C&C or Starcraft, you will be disappointed. This game, while it is inspired by those, is not anywhere near that good. However, if you are interested in a casual RTS with shiny graphics and mediocre story, you could give it a try. There aren't many RTS games out there these days so I appreciate that they at least made one even if it is mediocre.Overall score: 5.5 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: While I want to recommend this due to being an RTS and relatively polished, I just don't really think I can. Based on my experience with the campaign and multiplayer thus far - mind you not a truly extensive amount - the devs want to go full in on multiplayer. While there's nothing wrong with that, I find the card system to be ridiculous. I get what they're trying to do, but this should be something done during a match, not at the beginning. This would allow players to adapt their play style based on their opponent - something similar to Company of Heroes. The gameplay itself leans very heavily on StarCraft. It's nearly a carbon copy but simplified. Bases are upgraded the same way the Zerg would do in StarCraft akin to upgrading to a Hive. The factions don't benefit from the asymmetry that StarCraft has. They're just reskins of one another. I have a feeling this game will have the same pitfalls as Iron Harvest.  The devs create a half-baked version of another legendary RTS, and that's what it feels like. The campaign just feels bad. Voice acting is bad. Characters feel empty, and you don't really care about them. It feels very 90s action with no backbone. I find it hard to believe the same developer made Deserts of Kharak. Damn that campaign was good. On an end note, not sure where the money went for advertising, but no one saw this coming, and that's bad for multiplayer. I only heard of it because of Zade. With such a small review pool, players most likely will stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: It looks like this feedback was never looked at or considered, and upon release I can't recommend the game sadly.________This is without doubt the first time that I've played a modern RTS and felt that there is now the potential for a modern successor to Command & Conquer. Crossfire: Legion could potentially serve the massive global RTS base that hasn't been served by EA or Blizzard for over a decade, it's just sat there waiting. With a polished product on main launch with a good sized marketing budget this could really fly. So to BBI I want to say please, please continue to follow your vision on this, the potential is too great to risk not to - the foundation, engine and concept here are solid.Feedback below:- General Aesthetic / vibe = Fantastic- CGI Cut Scenes = Fantastic and high quality- Music & Sound Design = Phenomenal and again captures something that's been lost to the ages for a long time. The rich tone of gunfire/blasts is a breath of fresh air and adds a sense of realism to the battlefield.- Graphics are clean but the buildings and units could do with some more detailed textures as they look a little toy-ish compared to the beautiful environments.- The gentle camera sway on close-zoom is a really nice engaging touch.- The unit sizes need to be smaller (maybe 70% of current size?), they dwarf the buildings and it really takes you out of the world you've built. Also makes the screen more of a mess than it should be when in big battles.- Add the ability to save and load up offline custom games.- Add free team colour choices in custom games / Skirmish.- Not keen on the limited pre-match unit selection system, it feels over-simplified once you're in the game. Would like free choice of all units to create more interesting strategies in-match.- It's a simple one but when I click off of a unit/building, de-select the last thing selected so the screen is clean of selections.- Not a fan of the harvester units all being yellow rather than the team colour at all, could have a yellow embellishment to still differentiate from other units but should be the core team colour primarily.- Keep improving the general presentation of the menus for mass appeal, it's a clean start but looks too basic for final product.- Only played a couple of campaign missions so far but it's looking really good, and as I mentioned before the CGI cut-scenes in there (as well as post-match stat screens) are perfect. Looking forward to playing more.- The building tree system still feels a little basic, hoping this is something that's an early version of the system?- On the colour note, take it a step further and create unlockable skin packs for buildings and units. Could be really cool in the future and don't think I've seen it in an RTS. i.e. think of how Call of Duty create such varied and interesting skins for their weapons (flowing radiation green / neon with black etc. rather than block colour).I hope some of these points are helpful and can be considered during the development. Going to be playing a lot of this and can't wait to see how much it continues to grow. Thanks guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: Game definitely needs more time in oven, no denying that. Unit pathing is wonky, animations can be glitchy, no way to rebind controls. But in terms of gameplay, what's present in this version is a solid foundation to build upon. Most of my gripes with the game can be easily adjusted as the development continues.That said, I do believe that some core aspects of game/UI design carried over from Starcraft just because they were in Starcraft. Like building supply depots to increase pop cap. Or small unit queue. Or horizontal UI. Like, what's the deal with that? 16:9 screens became mainstream at least 10 years ago and we're still sacrificing horizontal space for UI. Bro please.

_childDocuments_.review: Releasing this game on Early Access was a mistake.Now that it's hit the full release its a great RTS game with a lot to offer. However, when it first launched incomplete without the full unit roster customization most players either tried it once and forgot about it or left negative reviews. _childDocuments_.review: It's a decent RTS game just don't expect anything new or groundbreaking. Think of it like Grey Goo, good production value, interesting factions, sound design is ok although during the campaign might overpower the voice acting when there's a lot going on. Art is beautiful, especially the cutscenes. Story is what you'd expect from a RTS game.Sadly enough the multiplayer is dead. With a marketing push it might be salvageable though.
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★☆☆☆(Just another mediocre RTS)============Review:Crossfire: Legion is an real-time strategy game that feels like a hybrid between Starcraft and the curse word "C&C 4".It's like they wanted to make a new Starcraft, but ended up making a C&C 4.You can notice the Starcraft inspirations especially from the units of the game.There's practically copy pasted siege tanks, sentries with their shield bubbles and infantry with stim packs.Now, audiovisually the game is good. I really like the art style - the terrain looks nice, the units look good and the explosions and stuff are nice too. The sounds also have some ooomph which I appreciate.Music is generic and boring, it practically brings nothing to the game. But you could always listen to something else while playing... IF the game was actually good.But.. it's not good. It's like extremely simplified - you just pump resources in place like in Red Alert 3, and you can build like 5 different buildings. Like.. really?Practically you just can build your typical Barracks-Factory-Airport, Command Center and a Turret. That's all.. there is nothing else.It also has very small armies - which is why it feels like C&C 4 for me. It has a supply cap like in Starcraft, but when all your units take like 10-30 Supply, you really can't make much of an army composition.And when units die about as fast as in Starcraft, the gameplay itself becomes like a small army skirmish thing where you constantly just lose and rebuild the same army over and over.============The Campaign is playable but for some reason the skirmish mode didn't work.Also the Automatch doesn't find matches and there are no multiplayer lobbies.So it's practically a broken or dead game already.Campaign mode is extremely generic and boring, filled with gimmick missions.Also the campaign cinematics audio and video are not in sync, which made them really annoying to watch. Just really half-assed work in general.Overall, it feels like a mediocre RTS and a broken game. I think the game COULD have been good, if the army sizes weren't so limited, and they fleshed out the bases some more. Right now it's just way too simple and too limited.In its current state, I cannot really recommend the game. Even on sale it's quite iffy, when you consider you can only play a generic and boring campaign.============Summary:The Good 👍+ Looks good+ Sounds have some oomphThe Bad 👎- Extremely simplified- Too small armies- Boring Campaign- Broken Skirmish / Multiplayer- Half-assed general feeling
_childDocuments_.name: Crossfire: Legion

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and presentation are quite nice. But the Units feel uninspired, movement, animations and pathfinding are quite clunky and the whole experience is kinda basic. _childDocuments_.review: I’m a n00b (and pr0ud!) when it comes to RTS games I prefer to play campaigns or against bots so I started playing the campaign. The first Act is divided in to four missions, currently that is all that is available. There will be another three acts and I believe a total of fifteen missions over the four acts when they are finally released. The game is in Early Access and the developers have said that the other acts will follow in the future with Act 2 coming in the next update whenever that is. You can choose the difficulty of the game prior to starting any of the missions. There is a small amount of information about the mission upon selecting it on the campaign screen. Upon completing a mission successfully then next mission will then unlock.  There are three factions in the game and in the campaign, you currently play as the Black List who are leading an assault against the Global Risk. The first couple missions you follow some orders and you’ll gain a few new folks as you progress, there is no building your forces or a base. You will start building a base and start to create your forces in later missions.  Your base will require resources, Fuel and Materials in order for it to grow, these can be found around the map in crates. You can then place these within your base area allowing workers to collect the resources and transport them to your base. This will then allow you to build and create new buildings, combat units and vehicles. There are a few objectives to complete in each of the missions, completing one objective will have you move on to the next objective found somewhere on the map. Because the campaign is short at the moment, I was left a little bit miffed so I thought I’d try my luck against some of the bots. Sadly, this didn’t pan out very well for me, I first tried playing the Standard Versus mode, me against one other team. You’re able to set the games difficulty, chose your faction, a map and a few other options to help you customise your game should you wish too.  The game started so naturally I got to building and creating some units, however, within a very short amount of time I found my base under attack. The few units I had created weren’t enough to withstand the assault but then they withdrew allowing me to recover somewhat. It wasn’t long after before they were back again however this time they came in vehicles and that was it my botty was spanked good n hard and it was game over.  Thinking it’s just me and my n00bness I thought I’d try again but this time I lowered the difficulty to easy. The game started as before however, the first attack came just as quickly as before, although this time I was attacked by flying vehicles. I had no way of defending my base at this point as I had three scout units and hadn’t even collected enough resources to start building land vehicles never mind flying units.  It’s at this point I gave up for now, I do like the looks of the game so far and I look forward to continue the campaign when it’s available. So, I would suggest that if you are interested in the game just take in to consideration that the campaign is only four missions long currently. The game is in Early Access so there may be some issues with balance especially when playing against the AI. There is an Online PVP and Online Co-op modes but I haven’t tried playing those.  In the settings you’ll find options for Display - Resolution, Refresh Rate, Full Screen, Graphics - Frame Rate Target In-Game and Main Menu, Antialiasing, Shadow, Texture and Particle Effects Quality, SSAO, Bloom, Vertical Sync, Graphics Occlusion, Level Decals On and Soft Particles. Audio - Master, Music, Sound Effects and Speech Volume Sliders. Controls - Key binds for General, Army and Army Selection. Game - Confine Cursor, Always Show Decorators, Show Decorator on Selected, Show Decorator on Damage, Show Subtitles, Camera Zoom Speed, Use Mouse 3 Camera Pan, Smooth Look At, Smooth Look at Speed, Mouse Camera Speed, Mouse 3 Camera Pan Speed, Keyboard Camera Speed. Language - English, Korean, Chinese, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Polish and Japanese. Positives  + Nice graphics + Multiple factions + Online PVP and Co-op Negatives  - Short campaign currently - AI bots may need balancing - No achievements currently - No cards currently The Black List faction is fighting against the Global Risk, their ideologies and dominance in a world in conflict, maybe the newcomers New Horizon can a change and bring peace in the RTS game Crossfire: Legion. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Crossfire Legion is a very promissing Early Access Real Time Strategie game. While you can clearly see, that it is still early Access, since there are only 1-2 maps per gamemode, only 4 Missions from the campain, some known buggs, occasional pathfinding issues and obiously a big imbalanced gamestate, you can still see a great RTS game under all the EA-issues. The sound and presentation is phenominal, starting to fight small skirmishes with a few infantery troops at the start of the game, and ending in huge endgame battles with huge titans facing each other, feels really amazing and while the presentation of the campain can of course not keep up with a title like StarCraft 2, who was developed by a huge developer compared to the developers from Crossfire Legion, it still made a very good first impression on me. The factions and the world they play in look really interesting to me, and im exiting to find out how the story continues once the next missions will be released. Even certain areas that i dont care about to much in most games, like the UI of the menus, look really good - it has some form of "class" for the lack of a better world, that put me into a good "grove" even when im just browsing through the menus to select my next game. You can clearly see that the developers deeply care about making the best game possible with the team that they have and i can only compliment them! I am exited to see, how they can further improve this game! But i also have to adress some elefants in the room. First of all: The game has an ingame shop! I dont know if this was planned as a form of pay2win monetary system, that got so much critique that they removed it already even before it went to the Early Access state, or if the current implementation was really what they always were going for, but what remains is that at the start of the game you can only play with certain commanders (that give you hero-like Abilities) and units and if you want to play with the rest, you have to buy them first from the shop. The currency is a pure-ingame currency, which means, that you get it from simply playing the game and fullfilling mission but NOT from having to use real money to buy it. And the ingame currency is very fair so far. I could buy every single unit that you could buy at this time after only 5 hours of playtime. But the question remained why they implemented this shop in the first place. Since you can only select 7 Units that you get from a kind of "unit-deck" having  all units dont give you a nessesary advantage against a opponent that doesnt have all units yet, since every player will always have only 7 fighting units-kinds that they can send into battle, but it gives them more options. But non the less this is in my opinion not a good system. Limiting new players from using the units they want to use, and forcing them to unlock them by making missions just doesnt feel like something that really fits into an RTS game. And i can totally understand why it makes many players mad, even though its not a big deal yet. I just hope that the developers react to the massiv bad taste that this ingame shop left on many players. While unlocking stuff and having daily missions can be a very rewarding game mechanic and i like the idea that the developers trying to implement it a bit into the game, i would be way more happy if the rewards are purely cosmetic in nature, like a cool banner, a profile picture or possibly unit-skins. I think by doing this you could have the players engaged into coming back the next days to finish some missions to get cool stuff without loosing people who dont want to play a game for a certain amound of hours, before they can play with the units they want to play. Well and the other Elefant is...its an Early Access game with all its issues! As i have mentioned before, with only 1-2 maps per gamemode, and only 4 campain missions the game really lacks content to keep the majority of players engaged in the game. And since it is just released and no developer can enticipate what broken tactics players can come up with, it is save to say that there will be still many tactics, and unit-combinations who are just to strong and can be horribly abused. One tactic that understandibly gets into the nervs of many players is a rush tactic, in which you build your barracks, (from which you build your basic infantery units) on the other side of the map, next to the base of the enemy, to surprise him early on with many units that will kill him even though the game only started 2-3 minutes ago. So you simply have to expect that there are many overly strong tactics in this game, who dont create the most exiting games. But its nessessary that every RTS game goes to  a phase of balancing before a state of the game is created, that creates fun games for the majority of the playerbase. So all in all i can say that i am really exited about the game, and how it will turn out in the future. But you have to keep in mind that this is an early Access RTS and should be seen as such! Dont buy this game and expect a nicely balanced, fully developed game. If this is what you are looking for, then wait for a while but please keep an eye out for it, because i am sure, that it will be an amazing RTS once it is fully developed.  I would say to give it a try, if the idea to try out an RTS in its early stages is an idea that pleases you, to help the developers find issues when it comes to balance,  or buggs they havent found etc. If you like the idea to be a part of the making of an RTS title then i would recommend to give it a try, enjoy the chaos that comes with an RTS game in its early stages and help making the game into a fun state for everyone. I personally enjoy every minute i have played it so far, and i am exited about the many more to come!

_childDocuments_.review: I think it is a solid rts with potential. It uses more of a deck system to customize your army. To unlock those units you need to earn soft currency which can be earned against AI or pvp. The amount of currency you get is quite generous so doesn't take long to unlock what you want. Though it does seem they have opted for more responsiveness than fluid animation, as sometimes units will snapp out of their animation cycle when given a new order, which is quite noticable. Not a dealbreaker for me personally thought. Balance is a bit up in the air as the game just launched and I am sure will be adjusted during it's lifespan. In pvp there are a couple of pitfalls, most of the games I've played have had lag. There is also for some bizarre reason region locking on automatch, which for a niche genre as RTS is a pretty bad idea. Hopefully the devs will fix this. I will edit this as things change and I get more time with the game, but the base gameplay especially pve and campaign seems solid. The game is early access after all.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game? Well... here it goes.Gameplay:The fact that you can customize what units you use is really cool, but in practice it makes the learning curve a lot higher. This is both a good and a bad thing. The good side of it is it makes the game have much more replayability and more depth. The bad news is if your build doesn't work, it will give you no options to counter the enemy composition if you didn't bring the right units.Graphics: It is actually quite nice with a mix of low polygon units for higher performance and the fact that a lot of them are mechas it makes them being blocky polygons work out. The biggest problem is it makes you crash to the desktop quite often and I'm playing on a 1070 GTX graphics card so it makes me question how often it crashes for most players, but probably most people crash to desktop while playing this game. RTS:There isn't really that much "strategy" in that this feels like a starcraft clone where you have some choices over which units you are bringing but there's literally just a few variations on what a unit does, whether it has stealth, whether it shoots air or ground or both, and whether it has an ability. All unit variations are based around these factors. So strategically not that varied. Overall a good effort. Do I recommend buying it? If you want I guess? But it makes me question why wouldn't you just play Starcraft II which is free and higher quality and won't crash to desktop every 2 minutes?

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this is just another boring and poorly optimized isometric modern military RTS. And there are several other reports of poor optimization in the Steam discussions. There is also no manual save, nor do checkpoints actually save. So, you must play an entire campaign mission in one playthrough. Graphics are also outdated, the environments look flat, and you cannot rotate the camera. The difficulty is not balanced very well either. For example, when skirmishing the AI, your base can easily get attacked and wiped out within minutes and you are quickly attacked by enemies with full body shields that easily wipe out your troops- even on so called "easy" mode. You also have to sign in online in order for the game to save progress in the single player campaign. Overall, I did not enjoy my time spent with this game so I cannot recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Currently I cannot recommend this game.Interface is bugged, not to mention unpolished and missing some core features. I can't change certain options like camera speed. I have to click twice on some interface options to confirm that I pressed. I can't change hotkeys like control group selection to Shift + A for example because Shift button is hardcoded for queueing. They should rework hotkey section to be easier to navigate and configure, like for example having command card interface to configure hotkeys. Health bar below units is super confusing to me, especially if I have to heal or move low health units. Option to change it doesn't exist.Gameplay is weird. Economy system in this game is off to me. Economy feels super fast while production is slow. There is no balance to gradually play the game because you're constantly stacking a lot of resources that you can't use at one point and then you're missing them when you need them, regardless of how you expand and if you have fully saturated bases.I like the game style combination of Starcraft and C&C. Commander Powers are cool feature, however I would tweak them for multiplayer to be able to gather points over time and have first ability on 50 points and second on 100 points. And to gather these points over certain period of time, for example 1 point on every 30 seconds or so, because currently you can use one or two abilities for entire match and that's it, which in my opinion kills their purpose in game. You have to think when you have to use them, keep them for specific situation and then regret not using them at other situation.Regarding factions, Global Risk and Black List feel very similar, where New Horizont is most different of them. If the goal is to make three different factions, Global Risk and New Horizont should be as they are and Black List should be changed to be different from these.There's no many players to play multiplayer as far as I can see. I guess that game should've been F2P for multiplayer and to buy campaign, especially that you don't have demo for this game, which again, F2P multiplayer should be instead for.Also, for full release of the game, it's weird that ranked is done very sloppy. You don't even have qualification matches, and you can't realistically see your skill level. Also there is no automated unranked. Entire UI/UX of automated matches is done very lazy.
