_childDocuments_.review: WHO'S RECOMMENDING THIS?Not me. Here's why...- Desperately needs unforced errors slider for both CPU and user individually. The avg ATP UFE is 20 per set for both players. You'd be lucky to get 2 from the CPU.- You need a microscope to see split steps- Players programming pivots on the centre of the body and not on their feet like in real life. Almost every sport game gets this wrong this is no exception- There's no deceleration (muscle compression) and acceleration (explosive leg/footwork) - "game speed" game slider needs to be reduced to near zero otherwise the CPU will track every ball down- "Ball speed" game slider needs to be near 100 for it to be any near realistic- Intro cut scene looks nice but never change- same with outro cut scene except one from everyone disappears from the court... spooky- crowd models are pretty poor. like Playstation 2 graphics- top spin on the ball is the same on ever shot. no player in real life hits with the exact same spin on every shot- smashes/volleys margin for error is crazy small- It would be nice to have weighted hard hitting shots and fast low compression shots. Some players in real life hit it hard which causes opponents to error- Would be nice to have string patterns, string types and string tensions affecting shots like in real life but maybe correct the simple things above first- CPU unforced errors don't increase when at full stretch or on the run, like in real life. Instead they can slap an angled fast pace winner to the opposite corner as if the ball landed sweet in their strike zone.Don't get your knickers in a knot its still a pretty good game. The players graphics are pretty top notice so don't take it too negatively but there's a lot of room for improvement before i can recommend this to all of my tennis mates.Thanks

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest -- I'm looking for the next Top Spin 4.  Is this game it?  I'm not sure yet.  3.5 hours in on the first day, and there's some pros and cons.  Side note: I play tennis IRL, and being this is more of a simulator, I think that helps the critique a bit.Pros:-Even at lower difficulties, shot mechanics are important, which I'm finding is a good way to train up on this game.-Lots and lots of configuration, especially gameplay modifiers, helped me to enjoy this more.-Character creator has insane amount of detail.-So far, the career mode extras are a nice touch (press conferences, tweets, etc.)-Doubles matches are pretty great.Cons:-Out! Out! Out! Out!  Me: 16 unforced errors. Amateur-ranked opponent: one.  While I like how mechanics are reinforced, they incur some heavy penalties.  I feel like every other shot I make is out, and AI very rarely misses, even on Semi-Pro difficulty.  And since timing is everything, it might be helpful to provide more user feedback.  I'm not even sure how to hit a well-timed shot, which is why so many go out.-To help with the above, the visual could be a little nicer when it comes to the shot power meter and the target of where my ball is going.  I'm either looking at one or the other -- it's nearly impossible to focus on both.-I feel like volleys in doubles go a little fast, even with the 'game speed' option slowed down to 50.  And the animations seem a bit off, too.  If a player reaches up for a backhand above their head, I doubt it goes 100MPH like it seems to here.-UX is a little rough around the edges.  While it's nice to have options, seeing all of them at once is a bit much.  And I wish I could use my controller d-pad for everything in menus :(I recommend this one.  I haven't played TS4 in years, and some of the clunkiness in AOT2 brings me back to those days, but it's got something a lot of games don't these days: I takes a bit of skill.  Sure, I could be Nadal every match and just play on "Rookie," but if I want more of a challenge, it seems like AOT2 is going to make me work for it.  Thanks Australia!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, AO Tennis 2 has stood the test of time and remained the best tennis sim/game on the market. With new releases coming out relatively often these days, they all fail to meet the standard of depth that AO Tennis 2 has achieved. While there are still some clunky animations and player movements, AO Tennis 2 has the most accurate shot & serve animations. Additionally, the visuals of different venues within the game, the player models, the gear available to players, and the individual court surfaces all exceed any of the other Tennis titles that have been released. Although the official list of licensed players within the game is slightly limited, the ability to create and download players allows us to compile a complete and playable roster of the top 100 players in the world if we so choose. This, in my opinion, is what makes this game so great. Until a new tennis game that exceeds the caliber of this game is released, I will continue to avidly play AO Tennis 2, and I highly suggest you all do as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics behind the controls are great in theory, but terrible in practice. It wouldn't be a problem if the game didn't feel like it was trying to cheat you at every turn. You'll find yourself losing due to the following reasons:... and on and on it goes.When you add up all these issues, you're giving away entire games in the blink of an eye due to no reason but forced errors. This is amplified because the opposing AI doesn't miss -- or at least it almost never does. Get ready to see ratios of 1:5 or 1:10 unforced errors between the AI and you. In 3 set matches, it can be as high as 1:30 or even more.Online isn't much better. The system matched me with someone with 175ms ping. The feedback from the meter is exceptionally laggy. Expect your character to stand there stupidly and miss some shots. The only redeeming factor is that your opponent will probably also seem to play stupidly every so often. I lost my first online match 2-1 -- not bad.I've heard it said that this is the best modern tennis game to date. That may be true, but unless the devs plan on tweaking the mechanics, the best we have just isn't good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I need to preface that though I've chosen to give this a bad review, I actually DO recommend this game. I know I've selected no to the answer and it might sound misleading, but for multiple reasons I cannot justify giving this a positive review, even though I did have fun with it. TLDR, if you're a tennis fan or have an urge to play a tennis video game like the old Top Spin series, essentially this is your only current option that you'll have some fun with for a few hours before it gets stale. Not worth its full price, definitely only buy it on sale.This game reminds me of fifa in a lot of ways. It's the only real option out there, It has decent enough gameplay that will bug out seemingly randomly (for example if your player is charging up a shot as the ball is coming to you, sometimes you'll end up slightly too close to the ball and you'll suddenly forget how to play and not swing at all. This would happen to me every single game for the first 3 hours before I got a feel for it, but still sometimes will lose me a point or two in big games). The game really doesn't have much too it, career mode being the most interesting is really poorly fleshed out like most career modes these days.I want to touch specifically on career mode because reading most of the reviews career mode gets the most praise, even though they point out its negatives, most people seem to settle for it. This is such a basic ♥♥♥♥♥ career mode if I've ever seen one. The original top spin did it better! Sure, it's a clean and easy to understand system, and I do like the way you level up with money and training, plus organising your schedule around tournaments and resting... but to do that over and over and over again... It feels so limited. For example, at the end of a match on a loading screen there's all these generic twitter posts that usually aren't even about you, and you see the same one nearly every time. Something like "Badminton is the superior sport #tennissucks" or "My daughter wants to play tennis! What school should I send her too?". A really nice touch would be if you could respond to those tweets, have a selection of 4 options to tweet out, similar to how the press conferences go, or have a follower count- just give some sort of online presence! It's like they're dangling some depth and personality to the career mode in front of us as players. That's a very insignificant feature I'm suggesting, and most people would ignore it I'm sure- but add something interesting. I don't want to go through 1 hour matches, sweat blood and tears, just for it to feel like I've achieved close to nothing. There's some really short cutscenes that kind of give a story to your character whenever you win something like a tournament. I've seen people not like that, but that's honestly one feature I do like because I'd rather the character be playing my own journey, not a linear one the developers made. I just wish that it was more than *play matches* *get points* *rank up* *win trophy* *repeat*. Even some depth with the sponsorships would be nice. You don't really get much from having a sponsor besides just money. It sounds restricting, but I wish there was a clause when you have a particular sponsorship you have to use their racquet or wear the sponsors clothes- just something like that would give the game more personality which is what it lacks. I guess what I'm trying to say is while fun, career mode got stale for me very quickly, and so I went on to the other game modes... of which there's pretty much nothing else to do... I do like that you can create, share and download other peoples creations. If I were to compare that to a game I played recently, It's basically WWE 2k19 but done well. The downloads are quick and are unlimited (WWE have a 20 downloads a day limit, I assume for the sake of bandwidth). This is great because there are plenty of BIG tennis names that aren't licensed for this game. Federer, Djokovic, the Williams sisters etc aren't in it, but player created versions of these players can be downloaded! Character creator is pretty basic as well... They give plenty of templates and you can make interesting looking characters, as well as they do have a Playface feature where you can upload a picture of yourself or other people- though I've yet to do this because I don't know what the dimensions of the picture should be. There are plenty of sliders, but it's certainly not the best customisation I've seen in a video game. That honour still belongs to WWE 2k19 by a landslide. Finally the graphics. I won't talk to much about it because I'd be reiterating what most say, but honestly it's a good looking game. Not amazing, but certainly passable. Things to work on would be the crowd- while it's not a massive focal point for me, the crowd is essentially from the N64 era, and it's the first thing my viewers picked on when I streamed this game. Also side note, the ball boys don't move, and I don't understand why. AO arenas looks great, every other arena looks fine, but not amazing. THERE ARE NO ASIAN CHARACTERS! This really shook me because no matter who you come up against, Japanese, Chinese, Korean. I get that it's randomly generated players, but why does everyone look like the same model? I looked into the customisation options and you can make asian looking players, so I don't understand why the random generator cant... I have an idea why being that there aren't many options to make your character look asian so it'd be rare for the generator to make someone look like that, but man. That kinda sucks. Anyway, I've rambled enough. Buy this game at your own risk. I don't think it's for everyone. I liked it, and to the right person, sure I'd recommend it... but otherwise, probably avoid, or again, wait till you can get it on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 18 hours playing this game, I give AO2 a thumbs-up recommendation . Since the good outweighs the bad, I can recommend it as a decent buy, if you want to play a tennis game with decent gameplay and a good career mode. However, there are a number of drawbacks, and also several pretty glaring bugs, for a game that has been out for 3 years.I have now played for 2x as long (39 hours), and I wish to update some of my review. See below.Visuals - I find the graphics, animations, and character artwork excellent. The subsurface scattering on the skin for the models is outstanding, and for once the characters look as good if not better in the in-game light as they do in character creation.Sounds - I think the sounds are good... Vocal effects, ball bounces, racket swings, crowd cheers, and music are all perfectly serviceable. Controls - The controls for game-play are (mostly) intuitive (but see below!). In about 10 minutes, I knew enough about how to serve, rally, volley, and run around the court that I could play a match. Not win, of course, but play.Character customization - This is game has some of the best and most in-depth character customization controls I have ever seen. You can make your character look exactly as you want. In addition to looks and wardrobe, you can customize everything else about your character including how well they serve, volley, hit groundstrokes, etc.Career Mode - I'm putting this in as a positive and a negative because it has some of both. You start as a newbie with very low skills and stats, and then "earn" more stats by training and playing matches. It's pretty deep for this sort of game, as you have to factor in fatigue, take rest weeks, and be careful how tired you will become from traveling. Difficulty settings - There is FAR too much spread between the lowest (Rookie) and 2nd lowest (Amateur) difficulties. On Rookie, even after only a few minutes, I was able to win every set at love in match after match. I figured OK, time to move up to Amateur. And at that level, I then lost every set at love.  There should not be this much of a spread in difficulty when bumping up one difficulty setting. Unrealistic opponents - Even opponents with bad overall ratings in the 40s (a good player like Bouchard would have around an 80, a GOAT like Sampras would have 90s) will almost never make an unforced error. Update - This isn't actually true. You can tire them out or wear them down into making unforced errors. It does take many strokes (12+ per rally) most of the time, but you can do it. And pressuring them at the net can also cause errors. These are often "forced" rather than unforced, but they are still errors. I had not seen this when the computer was blowing me out, but I can win reliably on amateur now, against low-quality (<50 overall) opponents.Career Mode - I had to put Career mode in both good and bad, because although it is mostly good, there is a major flaw in it. Training increases your MAX allowable score in a skill, but it does NOT increase the skill. So, if you have 60 Forehand Slice, with 70 max to start, and you train FH Slice 5 times, successfully, you will +30 total to your max. Thus, you now have a max of 100 with slice, but . Which means training slice for 5 straight weeks has . This is utterly illogical. So how do you raise the actual skill? You "buy" it with money earned from winning matches. That is, to win, you need to raise skills, but to raise skills, you need to win: Catch-22. Now, you can cheese this... you could play rookie for a few rounds, and then switch to amateur, losing in the semis but earning a tiny bit of $. But that's not a very satisfying way to advance. It's also illogical. If you lose a match 0-6, 0-6, you presumably made many mistakes you could learn from. If you use slice a lot in a match, even if you lost the match, the skill should go up (or at least, you should have that option) - win or lose. Rather than "buying" it up only if you win.Wardrobe selection - I'm not sure if winning in career mode unlocks more shirt, shorts, dress, skirt, hat, eye-wear, etc. options, but I don't think it does. The number of choices for clothing is pretty anemic, at least compared to something like Top Spin 4, which came out 12 years ago. This was pretty disappointing, especially with all the physical customization they gave us.In addition to the above "bad" things that I think are badly designed or poorly executed, I have experienced several bugs to this game.The  bug: sometimes, even though, yes, my PC is connected to the internet, and I can browse websites, read Steam reviews, download files, etc., AO 2 decides that I am not online. When this happens, no controls or buttons work, not even escape to get you out of the gameThis is just poor. First of all, I'm online, so why doesn't the game detect this? But even granting that there may be some glitch the game is not responsible for, my second problem with this is that there's no reason they could not have made some sort of escape option to close the game down or even click a "help" button to get help on how to troubleshoot this. To have the game just basically freeze if you are not online, is unacceptable. The  comes in Career mode. Several times now, I have set up a 4 or 5 week ahead schedule, but when I finish training (this so far is the only event that triggers this), all the next 4-5 weeks are blank. If I re-select the events, it puts me back on the training I just did - and then I am stuck in an endless loop. Now, on the one hand, all that training gets me free XP without advancing time, which I guess is cool. But on the other hand, can I please advance to the next week? I was able to work around this, so it’s not game-breaking, but mildly annoying.Overall, the Bad and the Bugs were not enough to sink this game for me. I still enjoy it enough to keep playing it -- for now. YMMV, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best tennis game I've played in years.Pros - Career mode is good. It's deep and you start from 1000+ rank and work your way up. Obviously could be better but this is definitely good. - Gameplay - When it works (which it does most of the time), it works super well. It takes some time to get used to but it's definitely addicting for a tennis fanCons - Random bugs like not hitting the ball which is right in front of you happens a bit too often. Not enough to affect the overall game but just enough to be slightly annoying- The animations are clunky - They are by far the most realistic animations from any tennis game but they still lack a flow in some aspects and end up looking clunky- Lack of variation in strokes and movement. All players move the same and the backhand/forehand variation options are very limited. Would've helped to have had more variations. Same with voice overs. Half the players sound like Rafa Nadal which is weird since he has a very unique grunt. - Most annoying bug has been the  "You need to be online to play" requirement which did not allow players to play the game for many days at once. I'm hoping this is fixed but if not, this will easily continue to be a major problem. You shouldn't have to be online to play career mode. Overall - I'd give this a game a solid 7/10. It's not the best sports game ever but it's definitely the best tennis game in a long long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Two tennis games were released in 2020, this one, AO Tennis 2 and TWT 2020.  Honestly, it was a toss up as to which one I would buy, but ultimately, I went with this one.  I am mostly happy with my choice.TL;DR - 7/10First off, the game is difficult.  Very much so.  I played a few random matches on "amateur" difficulty (one up from the easiest), and didn't win a point for a long time.  When I play on "rookie," I don't lose points unless I try something cute and fail.  You will need to practice and get better before you can win regularly.  The game looks pretty good.  The graphics are probably a B- or so.  Some of the models lack detail unless you're really up close.  Player movement is really good though, aside from a few glitchy moves or lack of moves - you'll try for a ball and just stand there - and the different types of strokes are well represented.  To me, the sound is the star of the show here.  With headphones on, it really sounds like a live tennis match.  If you can get past how tough the game is to master, it's a lot of fun.  You can download (free) just about any player you like, or like I did, a list of old-school greats (Conners v. McEnroe is a fun match).  Player and venue customization is outstanding even without the Player-Face thing which I haven't figured out yet.  I give it a 7/10 and despite a few shortcomings, I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike many modern tennis games, AO Tennis tried hard to be good and enjoyable.Did he achieve that? Kind of...Overall the strong element of this game is the community content, where you can download players (the ones that don't come with the game like Roger or Djoko) and download brand logos. It allows for some of the best customization for your career mode.The main problem is how your opponents play especially in high-difficulty modes. With the Rookie difficulty you can always perfectly hit every ball, but as you get better and raise that difficulty, your opponents, even in ITF Challengers or Futures, as they call them, will hit winners like prime Roger Federer or defending like prime Rafael Nadal. It makes absolutelly no sense at all. Even with an almost max out Player, with high difficulty, the game is barely unplayable and not funny at all, you playing against walls with infinite stamina and the backhand of Bjorg.But don't get me wrong, this is the best tennis game out there (my a mile) and the customization allows you to play for hours and hours. I am not putting more hours in AO cause I am constantly choosing between winning by 6-1 6-1 or raising that difficulty and losing by 6-3 6-3, all the time...The mechanics are OK, you will see the athlete "sliding" to adjust to the ball, some weird slide techniques that are atrocious to the technique purists, and overall that classic 20min rally that your opponent wins with a world-class backhand to the line. It is a solid game, I would love to see an AO 3 with better movement and better AI that would punish you but not by making you play against a wall. Overall a solid 7.5/10 (compared with the rest of the tennis games out there, like Tennis World Tour, the worst tennis game ever made by humanity)

_childDocuments_.review: Endorsed, but with caveats...PRO:- Strong career mode with a lot of extra bells & whistles that make it a bit more immersive than most tennis game career modes, e.g. having a chat with your manager after tournaments.- Pretty good player creator.- Gameplay in general is good.- It's currently the closest thing you're going to get to having a Top Spin game on Steam.CON:- You may experience lag during matches, and this WILL cost you points.- Your player will occasionally stop and stupidly let the ball go by when he/she should have hit it.- Nothing special seems to come from endorsements.YMMV:- The game carries on the fine Top Spin tradition of some very odd looking generic opponents.- The little sit down breaks during matches can be a source of amusement, as both players will suddenly "get up" for a split second so their models can participate in the replays.- When playing in the small courts, sometimes after making a successful play or using the "nice" emote option, your player may smile and wave at an empty wall.WARNING:- Do NOT play on Rookie difficulty. It's effectively a built-in god mode cheat, and when you finally get bored of absolutely cleaning the clocks of every single opponent in blowout matches and decide to raise the difficulty, you will discover how little you truly know when even the lowest level scrub opponent makes you look like a fool on the court.

_childDocuments_.review: Tennis games are going through their worst period ever. Tennis World Tour was a good idea very poorly realized, AO Tennis 2 is the opposite.The gameplay makes no sense, it is so obvious that any game designer in the world would have told the team to revamp it totally. The aiming feels like aiming in a multiplayer FPS with a gamepad.The only phase where the gameplay kind of works, even if the aiming is pathetic, is the baseline fight. Once you enter the court for a volley, catching up a dropshop or catching up a shortball, you enter a world of bugs and inconsistencies. The fact to have a slow aiming does not work when you have very little time to react, and the synchronization of the shot is ridiculously difficult when the exchange speeds up.Dropshots are usually a great moment of gameplay for a tennis game, here they are just laughable. On a successful dropshot, your player will sprint towards it and stop before reaching the ball, not even trying to catch it desperately. And if you do catch it, good luck trying to guess when your player will actually hit the ball for the sync.A final word on services: I can easily and consistently hit 75% of aces with Nadal vs the IA in Legend. It is way too easy to hit a super fast corner service, especially when using the lift.Returning services is also funny, if you choose the wrong direction for a split of a second, your player will get stuck on his feet, allowing tons of stupid aces.I doubt the dev team can fix these issues, this game is screwed and leaves us with no alternative.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played it for long enough, can now leave some feedback but overall, I would not recommend.Why?  unforced errors!If you happen to play career mode, which I really wanted to, Rookie mode will make you untouchable. Do that, and it's game set and match.  However, dare to venture into the Ameture league and you will be reminded of how bad you really are.  Suddenly everything matters and then you are introduced to the dreaded "unforced errors" statistic.  I'm at a point where I wish I had not bothered.  But there is one redeeming point...find a friend who is as bad as you, and you'll have a great laugh, whilst learning the game on the way.Go up from Ameture and risk throwing your controller at the screen.Two more points worth noting if you're a dev reading this and deciding what to fix:1 - please please please fix the spectator animations so 70% or more of them don't all decide to cross their legs (or some other random animation) all at the same time because it's so distracting and looks ridiculous.2 - for the life of all those using controllers, please disable controllers from moving the cursor or do something about the cursor moving when a match is in progress because it is so damn annoying for those with multiscreens.  The cursor ends up on the other screen (due to joystick inputs on controller) and the game tabs out in the middle of the game. Why is the controller able to control the cursor???  Mouse should be the only thing able to move it.Will update review if things improve but for now I'm done playing.  Please update when you guys decide to fix this stuff.

Most cons of the negative reviews are simply just not there, the gameplay gets misunderstood or it's already patched ...What almost prevented me from buying. First of all AOT2 is not a (boring and easy) arcady tennis game! AOT2 is a simcade with a very good learning curve, emphasized by a solid career mode, tutorials and beneficial training sessions. When you first play, have in mind that one important core mechanic of tennis is how you stand to the ball before hitting it and that is exactly the same in AOT2. In detail, your position to the ball plus the specific shot skill of your player affects the required hit strength and this again affects the target spot you wanna hit. As I've never played AOT1, the controls concept of seeing the target spot of your ball while simultaneously pressing and releasing the shot button is a really welcomed addition to the genre! And gives this tennis game some more depth regarding becoming a real digital tennis pro. There are also lots of gameplay options (assisted movement, etc) which you can customize for your personal needs. Also worthy to mention are the free  which are a really enrichment. PS: Works great with a friend on steam remote play - if you have the necessary upload bandwidth. + great gameplay+ great AOT2 Tools ()+ very good depth/complexity+ very good controls+ good career mode+ good atmosphere+ good animations+ good sound+ okay graphics+ learning curve+ regular patches/fixes+ 8 different difficulties+ local+online mutliplayer+ option: ball trail disabled+ start roster of 297 players+ free player created content*+ you can challenge (hawk eye)+ content/options/customizations- no AAA (if you got a problem with that)- no steam workshop- static ball boys/girls- "old" looking textures- stil needs a bit of tweaking- the ground textures are a shame- AI makes too less (unforced) errors- *3rd party account requ. for add. content

_childDocuments_.review: Up until now, there have been no perfect tennis games. While AO Tennis 2 is far from flawless, it emerges as a solid title, arguably the most complete to date.In numerous aspects, it reminds some old titles from the FIFA franchise. Graphics, menus, game modes, soundtrack, and even the font used in various competitions within the career mode give off those FIFA vibes, just transposed onto the tennis court.As many have already pointed out, the gameplay can be unforgiving, especially when starting with a low-stats player in career mode. Also, the main mechanics are tricky and difficult to master at higher difficulties. This means that in the initial 6-8 hours, frustration may tempt you to uninstall straight away. Resist the urge. Once you grasp the mechanics, you will find out the game is quite enjoyable, and the mechanics actually make sense (they try to replicate key elements of tennis, such as movement, aim, and coordination).While not flawless, its strengths outweigh the weaknesses, and (especially when discounted) it is clearly worth considering.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so many flaws it is difficult even start talking. I won't even review the career mode depth and accuracy, the graphics (not that bad), the "content" (which is by large part provided by users, not what you pay for). To say "stay away from this game" it is sufficient to talk about one thing, the thing we all should care the most, that is: gameplay.When you finally get on the court, matter of fact, this game could not seem a tennis match less than this. It feels awkward and just... "different" in any means.First of all, either you have full help with movement or you have none (and then you won't be able to catch a ball). Second: the situations that happen in this game are totally awkward: smashing is extremely difficult compared to other shots; volleys are practically non-existant, you can hit a volley shot of course, but the mimics are those of a forehand or backhand 90% of the times.When serving, there is no way you or the opponent can send a return out of bounds: sure you can be aced; sure you can frame a shot, and then the ball ALWAYS fall to the ground (it doesn't bounce anywhere else) or you can hit the net. But in no way your return will fly out of bounds, no matter out ot of time you return the ball.On the contrary, when rallying it is practically impossible to net the ball: if you don't get there with the right time you will send the ball in the lanes or too deep, but you will never-ever hit the net. Maybe I hit it a couple times in 25 hours, but it was only because I was trying to save an attacking ball, never when rallying.It just feels "fake".And then, patches come out from time to time, and what do they fix? The gameplay? HA! No, they fix "stadium sponsors"... go figure.
_childDocuments_.name: AO Tennis 2

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game, I really do. But there are many things that just don't make it for me. The graphics are OK, although I don't like there's no option to take out the cut-scenes as they are not the best looking and quite dumb (celebrating like crazy after the first point of the match for example).The physics are weird in many cases, particularly the movement of your player, it can be very random somtimes and not very fluid. Also the shot-making from the AI is not good, powerful slice shots? What is that? Topspin drop shots? Makes no sense.The editing is good, there are plenty of community made stuff (players, venues, etc) that help make it look more realistic. Is a good feature. Overall I was having fun, but what ruined the experience was the difficulty. I started in Pro and it was a bit difficult to start with, losing my two first matches. But after improving my player I won three out of the next four Futures and reached the final of the other one. In the last two the matches were all really easy even if my player's rating was 47, which was similar to my opposition. So I increased it to Veteran and man, the difference was abysmal, was like a totally different game. Every shot that went in in Pro started to get in the net or go out and the players out of a sudden got winners from every single position. I was playing Challenger lever at that stage, as I felt it was good to increase the difficulty when going a level up in competition, and I just got recked, 6-1 6-0s, never holding serve, with 3 to 1 unforced errors to winners. I thought it was the level of the opposition (much higher than mine, so it made sense). But then I went back and played a couple of Futures and it was silly just how better the opponents were and just how bad I was. 6-2 6-1 the first one, 6-1 6-1 the second one against two players with levels below mine. It just stopped being fun! I made errors all the time.And I understand I shouldn't review it badly because I'm bad at it, but it's just that the progression in difficulty is badly done: all you learn in a previous level is useless in the next. There's simply no progression. Might as well start at the highest level and learn the hard way because there's no point in playing at a difficulty and then just having to learn the game from scratch in the next one. Make the AI better? Yes. Make your player miss every single shot you used to make? It's simply not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The main "timing reticule" mechanic is inconsistent, janky, and never properly explained in tutorials. Movement is clunky and your player gets stuck in an animation lock frequently. Net play is made practically impossible due to the jankiness of the animations and general gameplay. There are some good ideas like the challenge system and interactions between points, but these are far outweighed by the frustrating mess that is the core gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty can be adapted to suit your tastes: you can play very arcade tennis, as you remember from Tennis elbow 4, or you can play in simulation mode.In simulation mode, the level of the AIs is very poorly regulated: either they're all Nadal, or you can beat Nadal with your eyes closed.The variety of possible hits is perfect, and the progression of the player in career mode is perfect, neither too long nor too short. Career mode is great, and you can really feel the sunny tennis ambiance.The graphics are magnificent, the avatar creation is very detailed, and I always enjoy playing with my little starlet. I'm lowering the level a little because I can't see all the balls.For the stadiums, the devs haven't made much work, but they've come up with the same editor that's often found in big ants games, and it's really very simpatico, so we can create realistic tennis complexes or not. The outdoor scenery is limited, but the stadium and courts are quite pleasant.Big Ants is an Australian development studio and therefore offers very high prices for certain countries, but their games are always of good quality and they sometimes offer sales on some of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game and of course it's only just come out but my current issues so far are sometimes my character won't automatically run for the ball when most of the other times he will so i'm dropping needless points with just that.On top of that i'm hitting a lot of unforced error's which is realistic on my part with a low levelled player but low levelled CPU's rarely miss and i've tried this on multiple difficulties. i'm going through 3 set matches with CPU's only having around 2-3 unforced error's while i'm at around 18-20+ error's.Basically the CPU's hit a lot of pinpoint down the line shots and can be pretty consistent with it throughout a match and these are low levelled CPU's so hopefully an update can change some of these things which are defintely issues.Viewing a replay in game is ridiculous, the default game cam view would be great but you're given this flimsy free cam mode that makes the whole thing completely awkward instead.Was previously a positive review but due to how game breaking the CPU are in this game I've had to turn this into a negative as currently i've pulled my difficulty down from World class all the way to Semi Pro and the CPU still hit blinders with their eyes closed despite being ranked 800th in the world or something crazy like that, this is truly game breaking and needs fixing before i play this game again. _childDocuments_.review: I really tied to play this game. It's just broken. The character movement is unresponsive and the animations don't know what they want to do often resulting in a sped up animation that forces the shot meter to be a quick shot even though you are responding to a slow shot on the base line. If you do play turn "assisted movement" all the way off as it helps but it still is a mess. Half the time the character wont even move when you've told it to. Other times, like I said the animation doesn't know what it's doing resulting in a weird glitched shot that is all of a sudden requiring a super fast release on the shot meter even though the shot is a normal slow shot just like any other on the base line. If you rush the net it's really 50-50 on what timing you'll need to complete a shot. You can get volleys that require the longest button hold down in the game and other volleys that require instant release even though they are exactly the same. Such a shame the game play is so broken. Also after a few hours it gets tiring having to manage the aiming circle and the shot meter for every single shot. This game is more of a micro-management of each shot rather than a game where you are thinking about the sport of tennis. Also the ai rarely makes mistakes. To the point where it is completely unrealistic. you will have 20+ UE a game and the ai might have 3. You rarely get rewarded for good shots but somehow will win a shot that was basically normal and the ai just stops running. Meanwhile a god tier shot will be returned and often won because the ai will return with an almost impossible shot. But your average forehand somehow beats the ai who was basically there to hit it back.It's just not a good game, The ability to download players and stadiums should be in every tennis game made but the game play of this game, broken animations and shot timing meter and the ridiculous ai make this game horrible. Don't waste your money like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping the consensus might be wrong and there could be a good tennis game hidden somewhere in here, but it turns out everyone was right–this game just isn't very good.Gameplay is a built around a risk-reward system of power and placement. A perfectly placed power shot can often win the point, but if mistimed, the ball will go out. This makes sense in theory, but is frustrating in practice due to how small and sometimes unpredictable the timing window can be. The result is more unforced errors and out of bounds plays than all the other tennis games I've played combined.The Career mode is supposed to be AO Tennis 2's saving grace, and I also found it underwhelming. The novelty of cutscenes and press conferences wear off quickly based on how often they repeat, and the management options and other features are light at best.If you're looking for a good tennis game, I'd keep looking.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I refunded this game, but not for the reasons you'd think.Pros:The gameplay itself is amazing. The hit detection is smooth, the movements are realistic, the sounds and animations are clean, and the character creator is VERY in depth. Career mode seems like it would be a blast if you were given specific attributes and upgrade them over time as opposed to giving them 99 at every rating just because.The online play is smooth with no hiccups. Cons:There is no way to search for online doubles.There is no way to search for anything other than quick match.The menu system is a bit wonky and needs to be simplified and made more pleasing to look at.Commentary during the matches would be a HUGE upgrade, as it's just silence.Better crowd movements and crowd interaction would be ideal(it is 2020, btw).Honestly, I think this is a really good game at its core. It's the most realistic tennis experience I've had since Top Spin.That being said, there are too many things I don't like to convince me to keep the game at the moment. I'll be keeping tabs on this game for updates and hoping they fix some things. Once that happens, I'll gladly purchase again.

_childDocuments_.review: While I will continue to play this game because I love tennis and there is no meaningful competition on the market (TWT was an instant refund), I cannot recommend it. While features like the ability to create players and venues as well as the career mode add depth, their ham-handed implementation lessens the replay value they provide. A lack of meaningful stat tracking in career for both your player and AI players saps much realism that a 52 week calendar and imported ATP and WTA players provide. All this is details compared to how buggy the game play is. The game's "featured bug" includes your player simply standing still and letting easy shots sail right past them. While this bug has been seen in other tennis games over the years, it is given a starring role in AO Tennis 2 and, needless to say, it rears its head at all the most rage-quit-inducing moments (and just so you know, this is not my first video game tennis rodeo and at 45 hours on this game, this is not a case of git good).TLDR...This game is just not very good compared to the best tennis games of a generation ago or basically any other sports game on the market right now - except for Tennis World Tour. It is because of that last fact that I will still play it and you may buy it, but I don't think Big Ant should be proud to sell this second rate 2009 product in 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like Big Ant have taken a step back with this, honestly, considering where they ended up with the original - and I don't know whether this is actually any better than AO Tennis.There's simply no excuse for my controlled player to be repelled by the ball, but that's exactly what happens. How can my player just completely stop in their tracks, or even run the other way? It's actually game breaking as it can occur multiple times a game (and by that I do mean game, not match). There's absolutely nothing you can do about this, and player movement assist is already set to 99 by default. Not promising...Even on semi-pro difficultly, the CPU makes some quite frankly absurd shots across their body which you have no hope in returning (your player couldn't even move fast enough if they tried). Also, their unforced errors are almost non-existent.The original AO (International) Tennis had so much potential when it launched, and it gradually improved into a decent title. AO Tennis 2 is, so far, a disappointing buggy, flawed mess.I just wonder if we've all been starved of a first party tennis game for so long that we call a mediocre game a good one, because this isn't good. It could be, but right now it just sucks.Finally, Big Ant are notorious for not incorporating ultrawide (21:9) support, and to nobody's surprise, it has been left out once again.At the end of the day (or night), yes, AO Tennis 2 is enjoyable. It's bugs and lack of polish really hold it back as, they're game-breaking, and Big Ant have had time to work on it.I'll keep playing, and I'll hope for patches, but I'm not sure what else I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original AO Tennis game quite a bit, and I have played AO Tennis 2 now for a few hours since it released; thus far this is almost identical to the first AO Tennis game, no real improvements to mention and on the most part it feels exactly the same in terms of gameplay.  The only exceptional standout element is the Career.The Career appears to have had a complete overhaul, but only in the sense that you now have dialogue from your coach and the press and your responses to their questions and match performances ultimately make a difference to how you are perceived in the media, potential Sponsors and perhaps even your fans?  At this stage I cannot confirm or deny that having a good/Bad persona makes any difference to anything other than how people supposedly feel about you (no impact on player skill or ability).There are some additional elements to consider, purchasing one-off upgrades for travel and accommodation which will reduce fatigue and eventually injuries & of course if you have the money you can hire better staff to give you further perks.Injuries are another NEW feature which I think needs some tweaking.  In every match I have played both the AI and I have sustained injuries, knee & ankle strains appear to make no difference to anything??  AND I would like to have injuries have more impact too!  At the moment it is no more than a short animation and a bit of text.So if you are looking for a more involved career then AO Tennis 2 will provide that, but if you were hoping that it would have improved you will likely be disappointed.However like the Original AO Tennis, AO Tennis 2 does offer some great Tennis moments, combined with some jancky player animations and missed shots due to limitations within the game itself.- Career mode with interactive Persona.- Injuries (Although they don't appear to make a lot of Difference TBH).- Some NEW Shot types (few new animations).- Some NEW Career management options (better but still limited).- Unresponsive player (wont play a shot when asked).- There are some Audio Issues (echo and reverb).- Changing direction is laboured and will lose you points.- Jancky and missing animations (various missed shot issues for you and AI - REALLY POOR).- Seems you CANNOT Dive.- Can't bounce the ball, no animations/options (shame).- NEW Career Features; cutscenes, Coach and Press Dialogue is all pretty poor.- No Significant or Noticeable improvements to anything other than Career.- Injuries (Career only) do not mean ANYTHING.  4/5 injuries per game make no difference.- Lots of Stutters in video cutscenes (RESOLVED).- Career Mode Training is STILL NOT YOUR Character (RESOLVED).- MP would cause game to CRASH. (RESOLVED).For £20 the career feature is worth the investment (if that is something you are interested in) but otherwise it is the exact same game with the exact same positives and negatives from the original.I do NOT recommend this game for £39.99, as there are too many issues but there are legitimate places where the game can be purchased for 50% Cheaper...(Link removed by Developer Request):But so far as I know  are a Legitimate Games Seller? _childDocuments_.review: This game is the quintessential tennis game. If you are knowledgeable about tennis and its many many rules, play this game. You will not be disappointed, the animations are so fluid and natural that I simply looked outside my window and saw one of the characters stride past my home before clipping through the pavement into the deep depths of the core of the earth. He deserved it. His CPU was far too lenient not aggressive enough and did not make enough perfect moves to counter my strategy of tossing a brick at him as he passed. My GPU exploded at the sheer number ( over 200? flashing images on my screen at once ) Gaming has come very far from when I was but a child. The visual quality of AO Tennis is unmatched, the cinematography is truly enrapturing. The NPCs are so hand crafted with so much love, that it is impossible to actually play against them because you may hurt and actual human beings feelings. The controls I especially enjoy, remind me of other such classic games as Star Wars Battlefront II and Just Dance 1 for the Nintendo Wii. This game is a step forward in the right direction. I hope we see an even better ( impossible ) AO Tennis for the next Australian Open. Which I hope is founded on the season of which we used to hunt Australians for playing Tennis at the ports of entry for their sad little island.This morning I ate a sandwich and thus, twas physically satiated. My existential nightmare was lifted, upon launching this game this afternoon. I abandoned my local church in awe of the splendor before me. I have never seen ( rendered in glorious 720p ) this many Tennis-related assets on screen in decades. My father would enjoy this game alas he too knows nothing of Tennis, but he enjoyed similar games when he was playing such classics as STALKER: Clear Skies.I would recommend this game thoroughly to anyone who has the brain capacity to understand how hard game development is. I cannot believe they had to crush so many developers under the giant gears of this games demanding requirements so that we, the plebeians of the public might play some after the summer sale begins. This game controls again very smoothly, like gliding an oiled baby down a greased chute. The ball physics are groundbreaking for the time. The online multiplayer function is unmatched by any other game I have played. It is so stable in fact, I believe we should base our new economy on such sales and trades of this game. The AO-Tennisocracy will be the newest world order, and we will in the next game hopefully enjoy actual gameplay that feels as satisying as this masterpiece of gaming creation. Pat on the back, kiss on the cheek. Carry on, lovely developers :)

I used to be able to play this game on Windows 10 using an RTX3080 and i9-9900k processor at a full 60fps in 4k resolution, as long as vsync was disabled in the in-game settings. Then I switched to a pc with Windows 11 and an RTX4080 with an i9-14900k processor. However, now the frame rate drops down into the 30s-40s in 4k resolution in Windows 11 once a match actually starts. The only way I can get the frame rate back to 60fps in Windows 11 is to completely disable shadows, which makes the game look terrible. _childDocuments_.review: While it is difficult to find any tennis game out there that can represent the reality of the game well while also being fun, this one can be quite irking. There seems to be an unwieldy amount of momentum behind your character as you try to force them to move to where the ball will be and to set up for a good approach to the net. But there will be times when your avatar will just stop running at the baseline then animate tripping over themself, where you would want them to continue moving after the ball. There are Game Modifier and General Settings that can be adjusted to make the experience more enjoyable, but you will likely need to set it to a low difficulty if you are not already acquainted with the AO Tennis franchise. Even so, when setting it to a Rookie setting, you basically remove any sense of challenge. Overall, just an okay tennis simulator with a steep learning curve.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Only buy this on sale and if you're looking for better graphics than the alternatives.I picked up this game on a 60% off Australia products sale which was good since I've been eyeing this game for a while and didn't want to pay full price for a game with mixed reviews. It definitely has its upsides, in particular its graphics, sounds, and character creator. For the first time in a while, I can play a tennis game that doesn't say "GAME, PLAYER ONE", can actually pronounce player names (including your own created player!!), has characters that look like humans, has really well made motion captured animations, and overall looks like tennis. In addition, the presentation of the Australian Open within the game is very impressive. The game supports cosmetic modding with custom stadiums and the ability to create and upload your own creations for use among the community, something which is sorely lacking with its competitors.Make no mistake, this game is not up to standards when it comes to "gameplay realism" of tennis. My player is a lightning fast god that can cover the court with no problems, does Monfils style jumping smashes multiple times per rally, Kyrgios style tweener volleys, and can ace like Isner all day long. The tennis on display here is very much style over substance, quite literally an arcade for tennis. Additionally, the AI opponents never seem to hit unforced errors. Either you miss or you hit a winner. The AI only gets aced or hits a serve return into the net. I have played many matches where I have 14+ unforced errors but the AI has one or zero. There are also some unfixed bugs that force players to stand still instead of returning a ball, leading to very frustrating (or hilarious, when it's the AI doing it) points being lost.There are a lot of tennis fans desperate for a good looking and sounding modern, AAA tennis game that is playable. It can't be understated enough that this game is buggy, unpolished, and unbalanced. The most fun part for me, the character creator, isn't even unique to this game since you can download the character creator for free (AO Tennis Tools). Even still, the game IS fun for a few hours at a time. It could be much better, but it's never going to be updated again so this is the best we will get for this title. Due to these issues, I cannot recommend this game UNLESS you can get it on sale like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to recommend this game and the only reason I am is because at the end of the day I am 50 hours in and still "enjoying" it. This comes with some massive caveats though. I don't care much about the creation or game modes, this review is 90% based on the mechanics of the game.The AI is simultaneously godlike but easily exploitable. All the people saying this game is in any way difficult are a mystery to me. Almost every point can be won with a slow slice return followed by rushing the net, regardless of the difficulty setting. Or the drop shot which seems to break the AI as even if it is placed where they can get to it they often run over to it but then just stand there watching it bounce until they do this hilarious sideways stumble like they just missed it.The mechanics of how the shots work are great in theory. You hold the shot selection and your player will automatically get into position, which allows you to have a lot of control over shot placement. When it works it feels great. Even when it works and you misplayed by holding the shot too long so you know it is going to go out. However, it really often does not work. Sometimes your player will decide to let the ball bounce for no reason instead of volleying, so you release the shot way to early and he flubs it. Sometimes he will just bloody stand there (this seems to happen A LOT on service returns) and do nothing even whilst you are holding the shot. Sometimes (and this is my favourite) the game will change it's mind IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SHOT as to what the correct timing should be.  It's utterly maddening. The vast majority of points I lose (unless playing way out of my depth by ranking up too quickly), I feel like I lost to the shot system rather than the opponent. So there you have it. I recommend the game purely because I'm still enjoying playing it. Try it on sale maybe, but if you are prone to getting aggravated by losing to the game design instead of the opponent sometimes, then give this a miss.

name: Weakless
detailed_description: They say friendship comes about when two people complement each other. In Weakless, this is not just a mere observation about interactions, it’s a very palpable thing. Lead two characters – one without the sense of hearing, the other with no sense of vision – through a beautiful, organic, fantasy world filled with challenging puzzles. Use the extraordinary set of skills they’ve developed because of their disabilities, and witness the growing bond between these two very remarkable companions. The beauty of a true friendship. In Weakless you can control only one character at a time, which means you can’t use the senses of both of them simultaneously. Because of this, you get a unique perspective on how differently they perceive the world around them and at the same time how the two support and complement each other. Deaf being his usual “whizz in a pinny” brings joy to the slightly defensive and introverted Blind . While Blind on the other hand, with the power of his calmness, takes care of the ubiquitous Deaf. Find strengths in your weaknesses. In our world, people with no vision or hearing often have other, sharper, senses. The same is true for Weavelings. Discover the extraordinary set of skills your heroes have, and prove to the world that what’s always been considered a weakness can, in fact, be a mighty advantage. Fairytale-like world. The game takes place in a world full of wonderful, distinctive landscapes. Your path will lead through caves full of glowing fungi, natural basins, forgotten ruins and more. Traveling through this extraordinary world will lead the Weavelings to experience the adventure of their lifetime and discover the mysterious past that led to their home teetering on the edge of destruction. Resin is your source of life. Protect the village and the Weavelings' civilization by restoring the steady flow of Resin , the life energy for every living creature in this world. Save the land from the advancing Rot . In Weakless you will: Follow the story of an unlikely friendship that develops wordlessly between the stoic Blind One and the energetic Deaf One; Peek into the Deaf One’s sketchbook and gain a unique insight to what he thinks about this whole ordeal; Enter the beautiful, organic, bioluminescent world of Weavelings, filled with the curious life forms and mysteries of a bygone civilization waiting to be uncovered; Get a glimpse of the artistic vision of how visually impaired and hearing-impaired people perceive the world; Become a part of non-trivial narratives and satisfying exploration enriched with arcade puzzle elements; Experience stunning music composed on instruments from all around the world, such as the marimba, rav vast or udu.

short_description: Weakless is a beautiful, puzzle-adventure game with stunning organic environments, filled with curious life forms and a bioluminescent glow. Play as two Weavelings – carefree, wooden creatures – one of which is deaf, the other blind. Switch between the two, solve unique puzzles and save their world!

_childDocuments_.review: Hand drawn graphics play a significant part in telling the story and there is an unusual soundtrack playing throughout which gives the game an earthy and natural feel. Instruments such as the marimba, rav drums and udu are used to create the weird but spiritual acoustics.The trouble with story telling through the medium of pictures is that the meaning can often get lost or interpreted in different ways. To be honest I wasn’t sure what the story was until I read the synopsis on the store page afterwards. It lacked cohesion due to there being no narrative or voice acting. Weakless is a single player co-op adventure where you take control of either a deaf or blind woodland creature called a Weavling.   Deaf has no disability in the game at all. You would not know he was deaf unless you were told. His deafness does not affect gameplay in any way. Even the music and special effects can be heard when you are under his control. The blind person has more of an obvious disadvantage and controlling him is difficult because your view is affected. He is not completely blind however and can see small distances ahead, which can be enlarged by banging his staff. A kind of sonar arrangement, I guess. Whilst solving these puzzles using the blind man I just kept thinking to myself why make a puzzle game character blind? It just became annoying rather than challenging. The camera view was terrible creating even more visibility issues and the “sonar” ability did not always work. The camera angle is almost as bad for the deaf person and often Blind obscures your view as he tags along behind you. Blind will always try and meet up with you when not being controlled which often involves him getting stuck or walking into deadly goo. The game is predominantly a puzzle game but the puzzles weren’t that difficult and the game can be completed within four hours. There are some collectibles to achieve which might add another hour on gameplay but be prepared that the game is quite short. Your civilization has started to deteriorate due to the vital flow of resin stopping. Every creature needs the resin to survive so you are tasked to restore the flow by travelling through different lands solving puzzles to continue your journey.Along the way you meet up with a blind creature who aids you in your task. The story was very disappointing and felt a bit inevitable. I was confused throughout my playtime and was unsure what was happening in regards to plot. There are some cut scenes depicting hand drawn events but they weren’t successful in portraying the story effectively. They looked impressive but the lack of any narrative, subtitle or voice acting left me slightly perplexed.Character development was quite weak also. Yes they helped each other out, but all you really learned about the characters was that deaf was keen on art and blind was keen on music. I didn’t feel a connection between the two characters or care about their journey.  Weakless is a puzzle game and each character has special abilities.  Deaf can make Lily pads grow to create paths to walk over water, he can remove thistles to make a path for the blind creature, he can climb ledges Lara Croft style, and build bridges for Blind to cross. Blind is stronger and can move boulders and bridges into place for Deaf to walk over and can help Deaf reach higher ground by standing on his back. He also has the ability to use his staff to open doors by hitting the correct musical notes in order. Later you have puzzles involving switches and platforms. Quite often Deaf will lead the way and you have to work out a path for Blind to reach you. Pressing switches will raise lifts for Blind. Other puzzles involve manipulating beams of light to open pathways and navigating conveyor belts. Occasionally Blind and Deaf have to stand and watch a reenactment on a screen for visual clues on how to solve a puzzle.There were a couple of challenging puzzles but mostly they are moderately difficult and shouldn’t pose too much trouble. The hardest part is navigating the levels. They feel quite claustrophobic and narrow in certain places and it can be hard to find the correct path sometimes. You can only control one character at a time so you will need to work together to accomplish your objectives. Annoyingly, Blind will try and reach Deaf when he is inactive. You cannot ask him to wait like in some other games of this type. Inevitably he gets lost, stuck or dies trying to get back to Deaf. Very annoying! Apart from the puzzles, Deaf can sit down and draw scenes at certain spots and Blind can locate and play strange musical instruments. They don’t have any bearing on the story or progress and are purely achievements. Once collected they appear in your diary for you to view.   The sound is incredibly original and atmospheric but it doesn’t have a tune. It is just random notes playing in no particular order. I would describe it as jungle jazz. Lots of woodwind instruments, drums and wind chimes. It isn’t annoying but it’s not melodic either and there is no tension or drama created by the “music” when needed. This makes you feel like you are one with nature but it also makes the game feel flat and emotionless.   Weakless looks great and environments are interesting to explore. Deaf runs like he has soiled his wooden pants but character movement is generally realistic. The hand drawn story elements look impressive and the whole package appears professional and high end.Curator Info: This game was received for free through curator connect.

_childDocuments_.review: The art & design of this game is really nice. But that's about the only thing that it really has going for it.The primary conceit of this game is there are two playable characters. One deaf, one blind. But rarely do the puzzles actually make use of this. Most of the puzzles require both characters, but usually because they are either tall&strong or can activate controls. The deaf/blind aspect doesn't really crop up except in one puzzle mechanic that I've come across.Some of the puzzles are made more tedious by one of the characters being blind, but it hasn't really made it more difficult or tricky to solve.The game also has a lot of bugs, particularly in the levels where a lot of things start moving around with platforms and conveyors, resulting in me getting stuck in the world. There is a reset to checkpoint option, but any well designed puzzle game shouldn't require the player to use that.

_childDocuments_.review: How could I not recommend a ? Those are the main themes of Weakless and the game succeeds (somewhat) in sending a meaningful message about them. It also has an interesting art direction and great music.If you value aforementioned aspects in games (just as I do), then you should enjoy Weakless. It is a 100% indie game, , but clearly lacking in some terms, due to developer's little experience. Therefore, if you're looking for complex gameplay, challenging puzzles or engaging narrative... well, then you might want to look somewhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Weakless

_childDocuments_.review: A short adventure game, quite good for a single evening, when you need to rest and do some serene stuff, but not a good pick if you expect challenging puzzles or a longer, clearly narrated story. I would say that of all the games I've played, this one is most similar to Abzu and Brothers: Tale of Two Sons, although much shorter.I've gone through the whole game quite quickly, but I liked it, even though it has had its share of flaws. The pros - the race of protagonists is original and interesting. Deaf moves in a super cute way and watching him run made me smile everytime. What I really dig are the aesthethics of the world - both the visuals and the audio. For me, that is the main point of playing Weakless - leisurely enjoying an original world and a story through art and music, and for me it worked well. Although, unfortunately, with this also comes the biggest, in my opinion, flaw of the game - when you control the Blind character, you cannot see the visuals well, and when you control the Deaf one, you cannot hear sounds and some parts of the music. Due to playing almost exclusively with Deaf to enjoy the surroundings, some parts of the music do not play for most of the game, which makes it monotonous after a while. The puzzles are quite easy and only sometimes serve a real purpose, and by that I mean that I do not feel like the disabilities of the characters were shown enough - gameplay-wise they are more of Strong and Agile than Blind and Deaf. I've also encountered some bugs with movement, camera, and being followed by the second Weaveling. The game also crashed once.
_childDocuments_.name: Weakless

_childDocuments_.review: So this game was a thing.I didn't NOT enjoy my romp through someone's work they put into this but this game and it's mechanics just miss for me.I don't wanna play as the blind character because hes slow and you miss out on all the visuals but playing as the deaf character was slowly driving me insane with the bing bong music playing on and on and on.Puzzles were straight forward though most of them didn't require a deaf/blind duo more like a tall / short guy.Recommended on sale but I wouldn't be opposed to checking out how the developers games grow and change as they continue with their craft. ^_^Have a good day, watch out for goop!
_childDocuments_.name: Weakless

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review: A wonderful story about two unlikely hero’s discovering the reason for the corrupted sap in the life tree. A wonderful mechanic where switching from blind to deaf heightens your senses to the other upon switching and makes you appreciate the environment or the music more, when you switch. This game has puzzles that are not to difficult to find out, but your more or less coming for the story. This story is not giving much information only pictures, small clips of moving pictures, and is truly up to your interpretation at the end. So don’t be upset when in the end you may not get what the ending means. Its up to you to put together what you found exploring the world and connect the dots to find your meaning. A beautiful game with a unique overall presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Weakless

_childDocuments_.review: is a beautiful tale about two weavlings who help each other save the world together, The story in the game is like being in a narrative storybook without any dialogue, The developers try to tell the tale with a cute use of art and drawings on walls throughout for you to piece together the story, Albeit a bit hard to understand what the tale is actually about at some points and what actually is your goal, But there is still something about this tale that you only can't help fall in love with the main characters and want them to reach their goal.The games mechanics and concept is the strongest point of the game and i like the direction they went in with the mechanics that fits the characters. With one weavling being Blind so when you are using this character the world transforms into black and white scene and your visibility is very limited. So you will then need to use the weavling who is Deaf to help who can see the world in full colour but you will still need both to solve puzzles. They have implemented it very well and as the tale is about friendship and helping others, It really adds to the vibe of the game when your in each different characters reality.The whole game design in general is a beautiful masterpiece and visually stunning to look at, The whole levels are very linear and with only a few places to check for those collectables making it very easy game to navigate  but this doesn't take away from the game as the whole point is to make it to your final destination and with the levels connected it truly feels like you are on a journey. With the nice sounds/music the chill atmospheric vibe of the game carries throughout .Overall a solid adventure that has a unique concept and feels refreshing. i just feel with the story being confusing at times the game doesn't really make you want to play the game after one playthrough but i  know you will still enjoy your time in this one for something different.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Weakless

_childDocuments_.review: is a short and relaxing puzzle-adventure game set in a beautiful organic environment. The player adopts the role of two carefree, wooden creatures called Weavelings, one of which is deaf, the other blind. However, the characters find strengths in their weaknesses and collaboration is the key to solving unique puzzles and saving their world.Overall, it is a serene and relaxing experience with a disappointingly vague narrative and fairly minimal mechanics. Its visuals and soundtrack are the game’s best features with the style of gameplay allowing the player to enjoy these at a leisurely pace. The cute characters and simple puzzles give the game a very casual feel, making it easy to play but unfortunately, much harder to get immersed in. Weakless was an enjoyable experience overall but the short playtime of around 3-5 hours and technical issues mean that the price tag is a bit too steep. With that in mind, I’d only recommend it cautiously, and definitely on sale.My full, detailed review of this game is available on .

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah so...this game isn't worth it. That's the short answer. As for the long answer...well..I mean...lets get into it. But if you'd like a more fun look at the game which includes actual gameplay please check out my video on youtube (link below)But here's the thing. It's just your standard duo co-op singleplayer game. You play as these two tree guys who have to navigate through a forest and its puzzles. But the problems are, well...I'm not gonna spoil the "twist" but the game has its issues. First off this is an atmospheric puzzler game. And it doesn't do either of those very well. It's atmosphere is kinda nice at first, but the longer you play and the more that constant repetetive music blows through your ears you'll find yourself annoyed. With the lack of a cognitive plot/story you find yourself confused most of the time and constantly asking yourself, why am I even doing this?Then you've got the puzzles. They're too easy. I normally suck at puzzle games. I tend to avoid them. And I mean like...I'm really bad at puzzle games. And yet I was able to solve all the puzzles I met in this game in my gameplay time. I will be getting a refund as this game didn't immerse me at all, and it didn't engage with me at all. It just left me feeling bored and confused and wondering "why the hell am I even doing all this" the whole time.This game had an interesting idea and an interesting take on this thought process but overall it was executed poorly.  Also I've heard several rumors from other players that the game only lasts 2-4 hours. So...there's that too...

name: Before We Leave
detailed_description: Rediscover what was lost and nurture your reborn civilisation in Before We Leave, a city building game set in a cozy corner of the universe. Grow, gather and manage resources to help your settlements thrive, and share goods between the hexagonal lands and planets around you. Relax and expand the fabric of your growing societies and create a solar system of happy planets at your own pace. Not everything will go your way, though - use your wits and research solutions to overcome the challenges that your ancestors once faced. FEATURES Build settlements for the newly emerged Peeps Discover and research the ancient technologies around you Manage resources, pollution and happiness to avoid the mistakes of your ancestors Trade between your settlements by sea and by space Explore six unique biomes on islands of all shapes and sizes Protect the Peeps from ancient beings that guard the galaxy THE STORY Your Peeps have spent generations underground. They’ve missed the caress of sun on skin, the squelch of soil between toes, the tickle of flies on noses. They emerge, full of wonder, but with no idea how to grow anything - except potatoes. Start rebuilding their lost civilisation by providing shelter, uncovering ancient technology, and expanding this reborn society to other continents and planets. But the universe is not safe. Ancient, ancestral guardians demand attention and challenge your settlements - it’s up to you to circumvent these creatures that hamper progress and disturb your newfound peace. There are no weapons, no battles with neighbours for control of resources - just you, and a solar system full of opportunities.
