_childDocuments_.review: There's not a whole lot of content overall right now, at least from what I can tell and what the devs said in the forums. However, with the price and general polish I don't mind personally. I think what's there has a lot of potential and it's a lot of fun. Even if it's a fairly simple game overall.The game is about summoning and desummoning monsters for it's combat system. You don't directly fight yourself, you use up to 4 monsters. The monsters do their preset action before running back to you and going away. Or you can manually call them back so they don't take any damage, this costs stamina. So the main thing is knowing when to summon and call back your monsters so they avoid damage.They aren't tanky at all, so you're meant to summon them back. It's an interesting way to do combat, it's more micromanage-y in that way. You take damage independently and when your monsters die. You can dodge from damage at the cost of stamina. There are some permanent upgrades to get. I think the one in the shops that randomly appear unlock different items to buy, I've only unlocked one there. I unlocked all the permanent general upgrades [3 total], and so far have unlocked 2 more types of monsters to appear. Both of which are awesome. I assume there's 3 unlocks per type, so 3 items and 3 additional monsters like there are 3 general unlocks.The generated levels can get a bit repetitive and annoying at times. Particularly since when you switch screens it puts you really far forward of where the door actually is. I don't know if this is intentional or a glitch, but sometimes it will place you behind a wall or skull decoration and it just makes getting around more annoying and can place you directly in a fight in a new screen.  They fixed it in a patch~ I'm really enjoying the game though. If they fix the above controller issues it'll feel like a pretty fair challenge as it is right now. I've yet to beat the final boss[?], but I've gotten to him multiple times. Getting further in that battle each time. I'd definitely recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't want to read my entire review, just trust me and know that THIS GAME SUCKS! It's so bad that I will flat out say you shouldn't even download it if they make it a free game.I went into this game expecting a $20 game.I did not get that experience whatsoever. YOU WILL NOT ADORE THIS GAME!I got bored after I played the first area and already saw a repetition in the map, but you open up new areas and progressively unlock more stuff easily, so I figured I should give it a full try, thinking that maybe, just maybe, they expand the maps a bit, or add more parts to it. So I played it up to an hour, and let me tell you, it didn't get better.Pros- Visually wonderful! From the artwork loading screens to the character designs, this game nailed the visual for this game. It gives off a Diablo 1 feel that is intriguing for a creature collector game.- The music great to the point where I didn't completely turn it off.- There's a decent combat style you can dig deep into and explore, setting up various different styles of gameplay to make your experience unique.The pros are there to deceive you into buying this crap.Cons- The storyline tries to joke about itself, and it falls flat at every turn. You interact with NPCs who don't know who you are, how you got there, and don't believe anything you say... but they welcome you into their small town and completely help you become this all powerful being to go fight and control legendary creatures that they think killed a God. Yeah, okay. - This feels 100% like a phone port, and not even a good one. All the maps are procedural generated. Each area uses the same I'd say 6 different tile sets, and makes you grind through them to progress. These spaces are TINY! One screen of a dungeon in Diablo (I reference Diablo a lot because it's made to mimic the style of the first game) has more content than the entire map of one encounter does if you'd put them all together. You get put into a tile, fight your way through 2-6 monsters, then you can move onto the next one that could be the one you just did, or one of the five others with the same amount of encounter, and maybe one item on the map. The lack of content in the maps followed by the constant repetition makes me despise this game as much as i hated Jade Cocoon 2. No, even Jade Cocoon 2 was better than this garbage. This game had promise; Creature Collecting with a dungeon crawler throwback feel so you can relive those old school Diablo glory days mixed with a unique character progression based off the creatures you put in your party, but then they did this crap where they put so little effort into the level design that you can't help but wonder if they paid people to give them positive reviews. - They put your encounters on a limited time where they switch scenarios. What I mean by scenarios is the missions you teleport to where the tiny procedural generated map puts you into fights through the whole area which is about 5-8 little procedural tiles that I explained before, and when you finish your objective, you town portal back (Yes, this is literally how you move through the entire game). That counts as 1 day passing. The encounters are on a time limit of a specific number of days when they spawn, and if you don't do them, they'll disappear. Multiple times in this one hour, I had to choose between doing my main mission, or to collect more stuff to be able to capture something, or to be able to open a chest, or find a creature I wanted. Since each encounter lasts maybe 5 minutes if you're milking it, you get a total of maybe 3 items the entire run. It's overworking the situation to get too little of a reward.- This game is tagged as difficult. I did not ONCE feel any sort of difficulty the entire time I played. I fought a boss, I got attacked by 6 monsters at once, and I ran around with one monster as my attack for multiple levels because I kept getting missions that didn't give me the orbs or whatever they were to capture new creatures for 3 missions straight before I realized you can switch between missions on the same map. Not once did I feel like I was in danger. Not even a little bit. I felt like I was playing as a lvl 50 walking through the beginning of the game the entire time. My attacks one shot enemies. I could roll into an attack and not be hit by it. The monsters are slower than you are, and they're so incredibly predictable AND stop completely to take a second or two when they're about to attack. Every enemy did this. Nothing about this was difficult.I really don't understand how this game isn't a free phone game and is instead $20 on Steam. I got it in a Fanatical bundle, and I still regret wasting a slot of my bundle on it. If I could take back anything from this game, I would. I want my time back from watching the trailer, from downloading it, and from playing it. This was such a disappointment that I would say this is THE WORST game I've played this year, and I literally play idle games for fun. Your game is the epitome of awful gaming, and I hope people find my review and avoid it because it doesn't deserve to be played.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea with what feels like sloppy execution.I made it most of the way through the game, keeping myself going on feeling like if I just stuck with it and I got powerful creatures, then maybe I'd enjoy it. The creatures themselves are very well designed and I think that really kept me on the hook, but it's just not really held up.---Some gripes I've had with it:1. Start with a fairly light one, translation/writing from a technical perspective. Has a decent amount of poor sentence structure and typos and not in a way that feels intentional for the tribal characters/setting.2. Has a pretty significant pacing problem, on multiple fronts. The first and most glaring one is how tedious it is unlocking storage space for your creatures. It takes a rather notable amount of these shard items that you only get 1-2 of per map traversed. You also need these shards for other things, which doesn't feel as tedious (these upgrades are more powerful, so having to grind a bit doesn't feel too bad).The second pacing issue is in some of the little mini-quests. For example, there's a common mission where you have to get 2 energy orbs from one spot to another. While doing so, enemies continuously spawn 1-2 at a time, and every time they get near the orb, it stops moving. These missions are not -difficult- in the slightest, just extremely tedious, forcing you to stop and fight easily dispatched enemies over and over at what feels like a snail-crawl pace, and you have to do it *twice* per mission. Another mission features just standing on buttons and waiting for them to charge.3. Randomized nature of the trait system (effectively, your creature's skill tree) feels needless and annoying. Any one of them can get randomly assigned traits that are sometimes completely useless to the creature in question. Considering how luck-based acquiring your best creatures already is, it's annoying to have to go find another one when them popping up on the map at all is already a waiting game.4. Balance issues. The combat feels like it distinctly favors certain types of creatures over others, favoring a hit-and-run strategy with speedy hard-hitters that you quickly recall after deploying. Healing is scarce enough that you really can't afford to let creatures stay out and take hits, and tanky creatures have virtually no way to sustain themselves unless they get lucky with the previously-mentioned very unreliable trait system. In creature-collector games it's pretty normal to have some that are better than others, that's fine. But this is moreso an issue of "classes" feeling unbalanced. Tanks or otherwise slow hitters don't feel viable at all in my experience.---What I liked:1. The creature design. The vast majority of creatures in this game are very well designed imo. They have a decent variety to them but all of them have that "buddy" feel to some degree. From a gameplay perspective, they also do a decent job of making each of the creatures feel pretty distinct from each other.2. Synergy system. A neat idea that I would've liked to see expanded on, you can effectively infuse the energy of some creatures into other creatures, and the infused creature will get bonuses if another creature that matches it's infused energy type in your party. Nice way to encourage seeking out a party that actually functions well with itself while giving the flexibility to make that happen outside their innate abilities.---Overall, I wouldn't recommend it, but I'd maybe give another game by them a try in the future. This game had pretty strong "first project" vibes and maybe was just ambitious for the skill level of the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game so far, the only problem is that the Early Access factor of it -an incomplete game- can be felt after 10 or so hours. The repetition of the grind starts to kick in then, even when you have "new" objectives from the main story.Pros:- For a creature collecting game, I like that all creatures are well thought, useful and unique. Even the starting creatures have their uses, there's no creature that is a direct "upgrade" of another. Even the first creature you get (Meera) is pretty strong late game! This is a major positive!- Beautiful art style, although they need to do more with it! It has a "wow" potential they haven't reached yet!- Pretty smooth mechanics and fluidity for an EA game. Very responsive- The legendary creatures are rewarding and challenging to obtain, it feels earned when you finally capture one! Specially if it's BlessedCons:- Repetitive after a few hours. The maps don't reward exploration after you clear the areas, there's nothing "unexpected" to keep things fresh and the visuals, while beautiful, have no "wow" moment. Not a beautiful cliff or waterfall to stare at.- There are several minor bugs, mostly visual or sound related so not game breaking. Only once I had a "major" bug that prevented me from summoning one of my creatures for the rest of the mission I was doing, which was an inconvenience but not terrible. Bugs are to be expected of an EA title.- For Super Blessed Legendaries the difficulty is a bit much, almost impossible to capture them before dying because of their damage and no way to incapacitate them (no way to put them to sleep or stop them for an extended period of time to make it easier to capture them). It'd be good to have a way to incapacitate them or apply a "debuff" to them to make the capture bar faster to fill.For the price is worth it, it'll keep you entertained for several hours before the repetition gets to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This game's concept is really, really interesting. However I can't continue playing for now with how unbalanced it is. Quick events need to be fixed. They should first be optional, and second be something that offers a strong reward. Or they should be adjusted to be just a change of pace and not a crippling difficulty spike like they are now. It's by far the hardest part of my runs, and the lack of reward is frustrating. My other problem is how combat plays out right now. All your creatures can be separated into two broad categories: melee and ranged.Melee combat is entirely built around attack speed. The creature with the faster attack speed deals damage first, interrupting the other creature, and there-by wins the fight. On the other hand ranged creatures will deal damage but provide no interruption, and so the enemy powers through and either unconditionally hurts them or you recall the creature.And then you face the most broken part of the combat. Your own player character. If you recall your creature before the enemy attacks, their attack won't stop. It'll simply veer to you and try to immediately attack. You can't always avoid this and so you face a situation of always taking damage with little counterplay. This is because melee creatures don't register attacks when they launch them, but only when they encounter the enemy. So if you dodge, their attack won't trigger, and instead they'll continue to run up to you and then attack you. If you wait until the last moment to dodge, monsters with multi-chain attacks will still hit you with their subsequent attacks.So the only way to avoid this is to have a melee creature that has faster attack speed then the creature attacking you, and only if that creature kills the enemy in 1 attack. And even then it all falls apart once you start facing 2 or 3 or more enemies. Every combat feels like a race against time where you're trying to kill them as quickly as possible before the other mechanics come into play and force you to take damage.That's why from my perspective combat is really broken right now. It feels bad with the way the game punishes you because of its mechanics and not your own mistakes. However I really like this game, and I enjoyed my time with it. I'm still recommending it because I believe with some adjustment it'd be a great experience. I really hope it does become that.Really interesting game, enjoying it so far. I wish the level system for creature had more interesting choices than stat changers. If you look at the game RAD, for all its flaws, it had an incredible method of combat evolution that would work well in this game. You could draw inspiration from there. I also really hope you consider having the creatures evolve at certain levels, with multiple choices on the evolution direction you take. That'd be more interesting then just more creatures.Quick Events need to be re-balanced. I'm fighting up to 10-20 enemies each time depending on how unlucky I get with the map layout. If you consider that most map sections have 3-4 enemies at most, this is a huge difficulty spike.I don't think it's a good idea to be able to 'save' tamed creatures for the next run. It defeats the purpose of the rogue-like nature of the game, as you stop exploring the different creature possibilities and stick to the creatures that work for you. It discourages creativity and flexible gameplay. This feature is a direct clash against your game design.I had a lot of fun and I hope to see the game grow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid foundation for an early access game. You run around fighting creatures with your captured creatures to get special orbs that allow you to upgrade and capture more creatures. These creatures serve as MMO-like abilities (Q, W, E, R), with different effects for every type. Upgrading can create synergies between creatures, which is cool but definitely deserves some more work. The devs are pretty active and they clearly listen to feedback, so I have high hopes for the future. New creatures are implemented fairly often and the game feels like it is expanding with every update. It's a good value for $10, and it will likely only get better.

_childDocuments_.review: So they just released a new patch that greatly impacts the balancing of the game. I played about 4 hours prior to the patch and 2 after it and while part of my early failures were purely me learning the game, I've had far more success post-patch. Having noted that, the game itself is very unique. It plays like an ARPG but instead of spells or items you collect monsters to fight for you. These monsters are summoned for only a few seconds but each has unique spells and powers that make finding the right combination, or adapting to bad luck, a real fun time. The randomness of each run and stage leads to a lot of replayability, though I am 6 hours in and while I'm not bored yet I could see it happening around 10-12 hours but the game is still in early access so more is expected to be added.Overall the game wasn't like anything I've played before, it is fun and enjoyable and while the balance was rough early on it seems the developers have gotten closer to where I would like it. Overall a good time at a low price.Value metric: Does it have a value of $1 per hour of gameplay? Yes

name: Falcon Age
detailed_description: Bond with a baby falcon and go on an adventure. Falcon Age is a first-person, single-player action adventure where you’ll play as Ara in her fight to reclaim her cultural legacy in the lost art of falcon hunting against a force of automated colonizers. The game starts on a dying colony planet with its culture destroyed, resourced depleted, and turned into a desert by machine invaders. Ara’s been wrongfully thrown in jail for a minor infraction. While she awaits her fate in a lonely cell, she passes the time by befriending a young falcon. Together they escape and set off on an adventure to help the resistance reclaim their freedom and drive off the invaders. Features Take back your life: Rebel against robot colonizers and reclaim your culture. Bond with a bird companion: Name, pet, feed, teach, and dress up your falcon. Hunt with your falcon: Various animals roam the land and can be hunted for precious materials. Craft falcon snacks: Farm, hunt, and cook snacks to feed, buff, heal and strengthen your falcon. Accessorize your falcon: Make your falcon look dreamy with different hats and scarves. -also equipment for gameplay like sonar and armor. Fight robot colonizers: Use your trusty stun baton to fight off drones and robots with the help of your falcon. Reclaim your land: Take back multiple locations from the colonizing faction and rebuild your community. Imprint Mode: Play the story mode with optional combat. Dedicated pet button: Give and take items, high-five, fist bump, and sooth your falcon. Has optional PC VR support fur a fully immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is written after roughly 3 hours of playtime. It is written at its initial release.The game is relatively fun to play and overall I can see it being a very fun experience bonding with your falcon companion. Though I do have a few issues with the game.-The idea; it is very interesting and refreshing to have a bird companion to have as a help. There is also a variety of cosmetics for your birds which you can buy with free in-game currency to customize your companion however you like. On top of that, cute animations and interactions you can have with your avian friend really makes you bond with her.-The setting; a completely off-world planet that has its own earth-like species and terrain, it is really cool to see what the planet has to offer.-The mechanics of the falcon; they are very well thought-out in theory and I can see what was the intention, however I have some issues with it. -The writing is lackluster. Don't get me wrong, it is not bad for sure, but the dialog and their deliverance are without any weight to them, especially for the main character (mc). You get a few choices for the answers you want to give, but the answers barely change the course of the dialogue and even if they do, for a very linear story branching dialogue is a bit out of place as it seems there is no "wrong" way of talking, most characters' tones are unrealistic as of the time of my playthrough, and it feels like you are just randomly clicking dialogue options to cut to the chase, as your answers to characters has no effect on the mc's reputation or character. This causes the story lose its engaging narrative.-Which brings me to another small issue I have. The mc has no characteristics. You are left to guess what kind of a character you are playing as from the dialogue options you are provided with. This makes immersing yourself in the character and the story very hard, as it does not feel like it concerns you, just like it wouldnt matter to you what happens to a stranger in real life. There is no introduction to who you are, where you belong, and it would be fine if there were initial world building or as such but there isn't. Eventually some dialog with a major character reveals mc's name but that is about it. The game is supposed to be the bond between the falcon and the mc in my opinion, but it feels more like the mc is the falcon and the mc is just a floating hand. -Another very small warning I have is that even though game supports keyboard and mouse gameplay, it can be seen that the main audience that was being aimed for is the VR audience. this leads to wonky animations and player environment interaction related bugs. For example when using the hammer in tutorial, often I missed even though I was aiming exactly at the target. The targeting system for the bird also is wonky which I assume the vr to pc optimisation is the cause of. So if you are a pc player, definitely be wary of those.-The combat is a bit repetitive, but the different types of enemies with the different ways of defeating them kind of counteracts this issue.-Last of my complaints are the tooltips and notifications. The tutorial was confusing for me as there may or may not be tooltips for what you are supposed to do, and some only appear once even on tutorial so you are left on your own. The biggest offender for me was learning how to use the whip. I did not even see a tooltip so I am going to assume it did not exist. Though sometimes due to the vr nature of the game text or some of the text go out of screen since the game thinks you are looking away. The tooltips make you refer to the controls options very frequently. I think the game is very cool concept wise, I do not care much for great or bad graphics but I can say that the game has very pleasing visuals. Your falcon becomes a very fond companion and her customizability surely improves the fun you can have from the game. The gameplay is fun enough and makes playing through the game not become boring. Though lack of a good tutorial with consistent tooltips coupled with uninspiring writing of the dialog and the characters, as well as leave the main character being devoid of any depth at all and leave a lot to be desired in the story and game design department. Even though the there are definitely some issues, since the concept and execution of that concept for the game is well done and very interesting, I would recommend this game to anyone for its low price to-good gameplay comparison. I'd also like to say that there arent an abundance of bugs and the ones I've encountered were never game breaking and were probably caused by a vr adaptation bug.

_childDocuments_.review: VERY cute, but sadly short game.  Finished it in 5 hours (non VR) - and that included a lot of just idly admiring the bird, dressing her up, hunting with her, getting screenshots, etc. Things that were not required for the storyline at all.You are pretty limited in where you can go, as you cannot jump or climb over terrain. Quests were simple retrieval quests, there were maybe a dozen of them total.NPC enemies were scarce and easy to defeat. You're given one single weapon to use, but your bird can fight for you or with you.The birds animations were very smooth and well done. She knows some tricks, can wear various different hats and clothing items, can help you by locating landmines and hidden objects, can retrieve items out of your reach, and can be used to drop bombs on certain locations.  She cannot die, but can be injured - and her feathers will reflect it.  Overall, I enjoyed the game and would recommend it... I just wish it was a bigger world, lasted longer, had more quests with perhaps a higher difficulty, etc.  I enjoyed it enough I want more of it!

_childDocuments_.review: Falcon Age is the only VR game that has ever given me a genuine and original connection with a virtual pet. That being said, I highly recommend everyone try this game in VR to accomplish that specific niche void in all of us.To start out with the game's quirks, this was originally an Epic Games store exclusive, built-up as a basic Unity game and expanded from there. While this game is compatible with Steam VR, it does not feel like it's built for this platform. I'm using a GTX 1060, baseline VR hardware, and I needed to tweak with the options during the Prologue to adjust the game's performance while compromising visual resolution. The game should boot and be configurable natively with Steam VR Bindings, but in case something's weird, there are some other toggleable options to force the game to let Steam adjust. One other yellow flag happens every time I close the game, either in the main menu or by Alt+F4; the game never closes gracefully without having  an error. Save data's not affected nor does my computer crash mid-game, but problems when closing this game are odd things that always happen.Despite tweaking visual options in VR mode, the world and character models feel standard and minimal. There is polish and this feels like a finished game, but not enough depth and detail has been placed in both the world and the characters around me. Yes, there is a world of life, but I never intrinsically feel a part of it, nor does your companion bird. It only feels that enough has been put to show off what the bird is and can do.  Supposedly the Falcon Hunters are a dying breed in this world, but there's not enough detail in the overworld to suggest that any others besides my own falcon were here at all. As for the story, erm let's say there are two. First story: I play as a female prisoner on a remote planet (I think) inhabited by robots exploiting humans for labor. With some help from a baby falcon, I escape and find a refuge to recover and train how to fight back against the robots, and I cooperate with the Resistance to destroy key operations of my captors and save/escape the planet! Second story: baby falcon gets assaulted by robot, mom sacrifices life to save baby. Baby falcon grows up and plots revenge against the robot race who killed her mom. Which story sounds more interesting? I knew you'd pick the bird's.Did you know that you can name the bird? I completely forgot! It's one opportunity post-prologue to name her, but no one (not even the MC!!) acknowledges her by the new name throughout the entire game. Calling her "the bird", how racist...The bird who accompanies me is the spotlight in this entire game. She can do so much! Idling, she flies above and around me ready for my next command. I can whistle to have her come to me and sit on my glove where I can feed her, pet her, equip clothing or armor, and play with toys. With a point and a click, I can send her to a target to rest on a perch, to fetch a far-away item, to attack an enemy, to drop a bomb on an enemy, and to dig up buried treasure. With a call, I can have her drop an item she's holding down onto me while ready for another command, or she can swoop down to quickly pick up an item I hold and want her to use. These are many of the actions that the bird can do very well, and it's always satisfying to watch her pull them off. Some animations may have needed extra transitions and sometimes the bird tends to look the other way while performing actions, but she is by far the best looking, sounding and acting piece in the entire game.As for the main character, well she gets to do some things. Her primary defense is an electric whip, with which she can bash or stun ground targets, and the whip can attack or draw in targets from a set distance, somewhat similar to the Gravity Gloves. Physical attacks with the baton definitely do not feel like a crowbar from Half Life, however. It's important to look where I swing, but there are many moments when the swings sometimes do not connect. The bird cannot attack all enemies by herself; depending on the enemy, a certain order needs to be done between the player and the falcon, such as remove the armor, ground them and reveal the weakspot, or stun them. It helps keep the game from being a point-and-click simulator, but the physical combat needed some more tuning to make the teamwork combat work very well.I started playing this game with the Vive Pro headset and Index Knuckles controllers. Being able to freely look around and use my hands in real time to interact with the bird and the world around me has made this game into a very immersive demonstration of the awesomeness of Falcon Hunters. After a while, I transitioned to the Desktop Mode of the game to play with Mouse and Keyboard. While the keys and mouse look function perfectly, it definitely is not as immersive as the VR option. The hardware limitations are their own downfall in defeating what I believe the purpose of this game is. This is not a difficult game; death is a slap on the wrist with save points in between all key areas of the world, and I'm encouraged to care for the bird if she becomes injured before moving on. That being said, it's worth investing or renting VR equipment to take full advantage of its power to immerse players into a world I do not often see, to fight with a falcon that kicks robot ass.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is a pretty neat game, even if a bit gimmicy, although one could say that is the point.Just as a heads up, I played this game without a VR headset and with mouse and keyboard. Aside from a little control jank it's completely possible to play like this. The only issue I had with the non vr version was the interaction with the map, being a bit tidious and sometimes I couldn't see animations fully due to the limited field of view. I beat the game just fine tho, so those are minor complaints.This game is essentially a Falconeer simulator if you will. You play as this girl Ara in this dystopian world, where everything is controlled by this massive cooperation, sending you into a prison to learn to be a better person.That is where you meet your bird. You start out by caring for your bird, watching it grow up and then escaping from prison, which offers the start into the real game. With your bird all grown up, there are a variety of things you can do with it.You can give it commands to attack, collect, dig or throw stuff. You can call it back to your arm at any time to pet, play or feed. There are a bunch of different animations and toys that you can do with your bird, which really helps you feeling like you're bonding with your little fella. The story is okay. It's nothing special and the writing struck me as a bit corny at times, but I didn't expect anything huge anyway. It is a small 2-3 hour long VR title about a bird after all. You get a bunch of main objectives as well as a couple sidequests. The game is fairly focused around combat at times, but it feels fairly decent. Aside from one enemy, you could defeat everyone without your bird, but using your bird properly makes this a lot easier.All in all, I had a lot of fun with this game. Having your own falcon, giving him commands and bonding with it, is a nice feeling, especially as someone who is into birds in the first place and even has some experience with falconry.So if you're into fun little games, and the possible small jank or corny story doesn't scare you, I'd say give it a try, but maybe wait for it to be on sale first since it is fairly short.All that being said, please let there be more games with bird companions, it's such a cool concept :)

_childDocuments_.review: I initially thought that this game would be a game where you can raise your own baby falcon, so I thought that you would feed it and care for it as it grew. This isn't the case. Every time you sleep, it skips time for days or months- so the baby falcon grows up to be an adult within the first twenty or so minutes. The gist of the game seems to mainly be about fighting robots and taking over refineries for your people, which are placed there by what the NPCs call "colonizers". Other than that, you can hunt a little and cook recipes, but there are only about 5 plants to cook with and maybe 7-8 animals to hunt, and the game only lets you cook a small set of recipes, but nothing inventive or new. Along with there being barely anything to cook, there's also barely anything to do. The landscapes are pretty, but barren and barely traversable considering there are invisible walls practically everywhere. You can't climb or jump at all (at least with keyboard & mouse), nor can you swim. You basically only walk around the same areas over and over and hunt the same two or three animals that respawn in that specific location over and over. The "story" and dialogue is pretty lackluster as well, and even though you have choices to pick what to say, the game remains very linear. The promise of choice that affects the story is basically just an illusion. The game also seems to not be optimized very well for keyboard and mouse (or PS4 controller) because some achievements are virtually impossible to get without VR controls. There's a mechanic for your baton that allows you to use a lightning whip, but you can't flick your wrist or anything with a mouse, so you're doomed to fail the Lightning Golf minigame and probably other things. You can't shake your falcon's claw or any other cute little actions with your mouse either, obviously. There are also barely any enemy types, and the AI on the NPCs is terrible. I blew up boulders blocking a path for two NPCs, but instead of acknowledging what I had done they kept just trying to get through the now nonexistent boulders. The game is very cute, but boring. I don't think it's worth $20 personally, and if you like getting every achievement I suggest playing with a VR headset. It's also only about 5 hours long according to other comments. Pretty much the only redeemable aspects are the charming stylized graphics, and the ability to command your own falcon and fight alongside it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Falcon Age is a very unique game with great mechanics; could do with some polishing.I'll start by saying that the falconry mechanics in VR are out of this world. Whistling for my falcon when she flies off too far, holding out my hand for her to land, or directing her to kill a rabbit all feel very intuitive. The slight haptic feedback when the bird lands or takes off adds to an overall feeling of presence that makes this game a worthwhile pickup.Other positives: the pace of the combat is very well done - combat feels like a puzzle, where you work with your falcon to maximize both of your strengths. The art style is also very appealing - I especially enjoyed the adorable baby falcon, Auntie, and the robot overlords which feel like they're really there in front of you The music and sound is also very intuitive, allowing you to sense where your falcon is even when you can't see her. The individual finger tracking with the Index controllers was also spectacular, as you could interact with the falcon by making it hop between fingers, shake a pinky, etc.There were a few negatives, however. Most of these are minor gripes and didn't substantially impact my experience, but in the off chance the devs read this I'd rather be thorough. First, from the perspective of VR mechanics: I played the game on a Valve Index (HMD and controllers) with a 2070S. I didn't encounter any of the more extreme issues noted in other reviews both here and elsewhere (thought based on another Steam review it looks like they've worked pretty hard on Index implementation over the last few days). I used smooth locomotion and turning which seemed to work well, except that my tool belt (inventory and zap-stick holster) didn't turn with me, meaning that I often had to search around for my weapon in the middle of combat. The default button mappings also weren't as intuitive as they might have been - my natural instinct would be to "point" the falcon where to go using my index finger/the trigger, but instead you point with your fist and hit "a" or "b," and I had occasionally had trouble interacting with an object (like talking to a person) by using the grip/release gesture.Second: from a techincal/animation perspective: Some of the textures do not render properly. For example, inside the stone huts right after you break out of prison, some of the stones are transparent. They display correctly from the outside, but from the other direction you can see right through the wall. Additionally, the baby falcon got stuck several times (mostly inside the corner of the scrap metal sheds when going to hunt rabbits for the first time) requiring me to restart the game. I'm not sure if she got stuck between the meshes, or if the pathfinding was such that it couldn't find the door. My last gripe would be from a story/gameplay perspective. The prelude when escaping from prison was very compelling. Likewise, battling through enemies to reclaim area is a fun puzzle. But there's a pretty big disconnect between the two. I immediately bonded with the baby falcon - it's adorable - and then one day I woke up and it was full grown! I think the bonding aspect could be much more compelling if the falcon slowly "grew up" over time. I'm not sure it would even require that much detail - each chapter of the story could have the falcon be a little bigger, a little stronger, etc. It would help tell the story of teamwork and development that seems to flatten out once you've earned her a name. All that said - I'm greatly enjoying the game. I would wholeheartedly recommend it to someone looking for a charming, casual puzzler with some light combat. With a small amount of polish, I think it could go from a fun couple hours to a really powerful VR experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so far. I love the interactions with the bird. I can't think of any other game I have played that's like it either. It seems unique.Pros:I like the art style, the music is enjoyable, the bird is cute as a baby and badass looking as an adult. The combat is interesting because you have to juggle when and how you attack directly versus when to send in the bird. You can craft little snacks for the bird to boost her abilities. You feel really good about helping her, and really bad when she comes back injured from battle.Some minor cons:It has some small annoyances, that I see in pretty much every smaller VR title just due to the medium still struggling to establish standard systems, for how to handle basic things like movement and inventories.I'm not a fan of teleport, which is the default, though you can change it to smooth locomotion (I recommend slowing the speed to something like 85% though, full speed is a bit jarring). It's clear the game was intended for you to use teleport, because when you talk to NPCs, it places you in a specific spot, and some places that look walkable wont allow you to go there. The floating inventory pouch is occasionally not in a convenient place, but its a minor issue (honestly, I had way more problems with the Boneworks inventory by far).Overall, a good little adventure so far, I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game took me 4 hours to complete but would need a few more hours to collected all the extra stuff, the game also features NPC's I have found is often absent in VR games, though they act like borderlands 1 NPC they stand in a single spot and act as a vendor quest giver or a little fluff dialog.I found this games narrative focused story a bit short and rushed, mostly the beginning and end, at the start I expected a little more time with little falcon and possibly to watch him grow over time, and in the end I expected a bit more of a conclusion with a bigger finally.The game is mostly a linear story with a few short side quests along the way use to unlock cosmetics but I can't help but feel that the game might have benefited from a more open and survival type game in design, in a similar vain to Subnatica or Solus Project, as this would give us more time to bond with the bird though the cosmetics certainly improved my connection, the game features a ton of cosmetics to unlock and customize the bird, as well as a few items that actually improve the birds abilities.Graphics & Presentation: Graphically this game is simple but the art style helps hide or make up for this however I would have been nice to see some higher resolution textures because even the highest option was quite blurry Sound FX & Music:The Music in the game is nice but certainly not much to write home about, there were also a few looping issues in the music that would sort of cut at the end really only a tiny nit pick, the game has partially voiced NPC's mainly just the one main one which is a bit of an odd choice but understandable as this is quite an indie game Gameplay & Immersion:The gameplay is rather simplistic too but quite effective is mostly consists of telling your bird to attack something, stunning it with your baton and then mindlessly beating it to death, this might have gotten old if they game was longer however in the time I played I thought it was fine, the game only features about 5 enemy types with some electrical variants.The game also has a cooking system to collect animal meat and Fruit to make treats to heal or improve the birds performance (speed, stealth, defence etc.) however what you can create is carefully limited by only allowing you to food from recipes you have found rather than allowing you to explore and discover them on your own.The cooking was mostly a moot point though as I found combat quite easy the whole time and never really needed many cooked items.Also the bird has a gyro stable head when perched on your hand which is a nice touch.Controls: The Controls for this game were better than expected for a VR Supported title, UI elements are 2d but the game features a physical maps and pouch at your hip to store items.there were a few bugs in my play though the biggest one was under certain circumstances my rotation would be no longer tracked and the baton holster and pouch would no longer follow me, this happened a few times in my play though but was fixed by a quick restart.Value & Replayability:Ultimately and unfortunately  this game offers little Replayability, sure you can collect all the cosmetics and recipes but there is not much point as you will probably have a few choice cosmetics you you wont need to gather the recipes as really only the healing once is necessary There are a few different endings I suppose this could entice those to replay the game however the game will be the same except for a final ending card. Final Thoughts: There is a lot to love about falcon age, though it is a little rough around the edges it was a ton of fun to play, I just wish the game was longer possibly be implementing more survival elements and we could spend more time in the world raising and caring for our falcon.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: All the issues described in the previous iteration of this review have been resolved, including a long list of controller issues related to the Valve Index specifically, somebody have obviously been working overtime.The game is now perfectly functional with the Valve Index and has only minor issues worth noting. Playing through the tutorial and all early game, graphical glitches seem to be fairly common (encountering one about every 15 mins) with texture surfaces being either missing or flipped the wrong way around making the object/environment see-through in certain places.If you can live with these minor problem taking jabs at your immersion occasionally and this game looks interesting to you, then this should be well worth your money at the given price.Original Review:If you were looking at this game for the reason of playing it in VR you should definitely look elsewhere. The VR controls are an unacceptable level of clunky even with the huge number of settings they give you to tweak locomotion, rotation and the interactive controls, none of them get close to being reasonable for a good VR experience. You either have to deal with tank controls that do not take the direction you are facing into account, or you need to deal with your equipment just floating in space with it have no regards for the direction you are facing, meaning that your equipment does not rotate with your body and instead just sits in space somewhere, you have to choose one of these options of which none are good.The hand-tracking is near perfect, including even finger-tracking on the Valve Index controllers, however the level of clunky  when you have to interact with the game goes so far that it is near impossible to finish the tutorial (the first hour) in VR because some of the controls simply do not function at all in VR mode, to the point where you need to hold a button, hold your hand in a very particular spot close to your body (almost inside of it) pointing in a very particular angle out in front of yourself (you can't point up, down, left or right while doing this, you need to let the auto-aim do that for you and hope it knows what you are thinking) in order to command your falcon to do something, breaking any of these steps will simply not have the guide line (for pointing at what your falcon should interact with) appear. That took approximately 20 minutes to figure out through trial-and-error. Oh, and for VR (not the case for desktop mode) the controls are remapped on a local webpage hosted by the game itself for you to look at on your desktop and find that you cannot see it because the website is blocked for seeming malicious in nature by both web browser and virus software, making it a huge bother to try and reconfigure or just look at the controls of the game.This was done on the Valve Index with SteamVR. If you are hoping to play this in desktop mode, then this could well be worth the money, but as a VR game this is quiet simply not recommended under any circumstance at this stage, for that it needs some serious patch-work.

I did have an achievement bug out, apparently due to an item being removed in an update after I'd already fulfilled the other requirements, but the developer was responsive and resolved it! _childDocuments_.review: I didn't play this in VR which might give a different experience. My review is based on a desktop playthrough.As someone who works with Birds of Prey in his free time I was really interested in this game and it's near okay. Why the negative review? Well there're a few things:Gameplay:They found a good way to implement the falcon into the "puzzles" and fights. But there is no real variance. Just go catch this and bring it to me or attack that. Of course there're some interactions that aren't based on reality since hey, it is a game. But maybe they should've used the game side more often to shake things up.I liked the customization options to change the plumage though.Fighting:While it starts interesting with "use the bird to knock down this flying enemy and then finish him off" and "give the bird a bomb to throw" it ends here as well. There're not much enemies and most of them are fought the same way: stun them with your weapon, let the bird expose their weak spot and hit it. Rinse and repeat.This gets boring real fast, especially when the enemies get a bit stronger and take more hits. Combine that with the bad targeting/movement of the falcon, which you could base on RL since they have around a 30% chance to hit their prey, it just gets frustrating, not hard, to stand there, stun your enemy and wait for the bird.World:Sure, it is mostly a wasteland which is being destroyed by machinery but at the end they just reused most assets to create a small map which results in a meh scenery.Story:The game itself is pretty short. Probably around 3.5 - 4h if you just play the story. If you do it like me and do a big pause between your play sessions (nearly 2 years)  it will obviously take longer to backtrack. So the before mentioned points are not helping to fill this short game with fun and the script just drags it down.While there're enough critic points to make on industrialisation, capitalism etc. like you can do with all things, this is not the way. Seems like the responsible person has just the worldview of "capitalism bad" and has a pretty bad relationship with their family. Don't know how else you could write such a mess of unlikable persons in such a short time frame to fill. It reeks of "my mum is a narcissistic pos and only I am right!".The worse thing is the typical "different options to answer but it won't matter"-method. If it doesn't matter what you pick just let it be one liners. Artifical bloating just sucks.

After planting stuff, your filter buttons will disappear from your inventory. So until you use a cooking station or restart your game, you won't be able to change your inventory filter (and if you had a filter enabled, you're locked on that category of items)2. Physical 360 rotation bugged out twice for me, locking my UI and movement to be facing the same direction (i.e. if in real life I turn left, and then try to move forward, my character would actually move right, as the game did not register my left turn. UI would also appear to my right.). At this point I could only properly rotate using analog stick.Otherwise the game is very short, simple, and straight-forward, with little variety in objectives.The ending is a huge letdown, to put it simply (no spoilers, look it up if you want to know).Would not recommend in non-VR mode.Worth trying in VR, considering it's a very cheap title and you can still get some enjoyment out of it... just temper your expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is and was very fun to play. It is VR compatible though I played it without a headset. The games design is both realistic and cartoon like. The blend gives it a unique feel and touch. The controls are easy to use and the mechanics for the most part are fun and not complicated. The game is relatively short only really lasting about 10 hours so in that aspect if you're looking for a game to play over the course of multiple days this game isn't very suited for that. It's more of a fun short game you play alongside more lengthy and tedious games to have a break from.The game follows a prisoner on a planet where robots have taken over. While in the cell you befriend a young chick whose lost its parents. You and the chick navigate the planet together, all while taking down robots and reclaiming land. You'll watch and help your chick grow and when the time is right eventually release the bird and say goodbye. There are plenty of customisation's for your bird as well as little fun mini-games to play.The downsides of this game is more to do with lag spikes and certain mini-games being a little too difficult to complete perfectly which is required for certain achievements. The lag spikes tend to occur when you are fighting robots, specifically when you are reclaiming robot campsites/facilities especially in the larger more end game fights. These lags spikes aren't a huge problem but they do make completing the game a little difficult when your bird decides not to attack or the game freezes for a couple of frames. Besides that the game is relatively easy and not a difficult or rage inducing game. If you like short, quite and relatively chill game play with a cute companion and some action then this game is for you. It's a bit pricey for a game that can be completed in under 12 hours however there aren't many games like it and with the VR compatibility you can really immerse yourself in the game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: Its very buggy. I couldn't get past the tutorial section without the game softlocking. I tried multiple times, each time I encountered a different bug where the game didn't register an event happening and failed to trigger the next objective etc. The game does not save progress frequently, so each bug results in the player having to restart the game from the beginning.So I can't really comment on if its any good or not, other than saying that the games intro was fine the first time up until the point it broke, and frustrating beyond that.
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a neutral review rather than a positive one.Falcon Age has interesting promise and satisfying controls but it is dragged down by boring combat and lackluster world and characters.Interacting with falcon using gestures in VR is fun and immersive, watching it hunting down prey or just flying around does not get old during game's 3-4 hours campaign. And there are a lot of customizing options to bird's appearance and toys that it can play with.But despite all the joy you get from interacting with the falcon, fighting in team with it is not that fun. Combat is slow and repetitive especially near the end. Electric whip is a big let down: its basic and unresponsive nothing like the whip in Eye of the Temple. Story and characters are very barebones so playing in combatless mode is also not very rewarding.Environments look good even if they a bit lacking details and the engine is very optimized. But there are quite a lot of invisible walls and no verticality in player's movement making the world feel flat.Overall, I wish someone took the idea of gesture controlled animal side-kick and implemented it in some better VR game:)
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: I had such a hard time getting this game to work properly in VR. Most of the time I'd turn it on, it would get stuck in some sort of halfway VR/desktop "mode", that'd pick up my HMD's movements, but refuse to pick up my controllers, or even switch between modes at all, forcing me to restart and try my luck again. It was frustrating as hell to get running.And yet I liked it enough I'd dance the dance every time!In spite of it's many quirks and rough patches, the game has a lot of charm! The story is touching, taking over facilities honestly had my blood pumping sometimes, and I absolutely fell in love with my falcon! The story and mechanics are simple, but - since the game is only ~6 hours - they never manage to overstay their welcome.The game is far from perfect, of course -- it doesn't really have any memorable characters, and it's graphics sometimes sometimes do look a little half-baked, but it has _just enough_ going for it to make up for these shortcomings.tl;dr: Is the game worth it's price of admission?Absolutely** if you're playing in VR.If you don't have a VR headset, then unless you really like birbs, you might want to consider waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with this: Is this a bad game: No. Is it a good game: well....To get the bad out of the way first things aren't necessarily explained the best, the ending for me at least falls flat, it doesn't feel like you done anything epic or changing, only one character has really any personality. If you're in this for story or epic fights or have trouble figuring out things on your own, maybe not for you.However on the bright side! The bird is excellent, stunning and all around really cute. Theres different little outfits and toy you can get for them, or you can cook little snacks and thats really nice. While Im not a fan of the telling of the story, i do like its general vibes and some of the stuff it tries to get at. Also, really not too bad to play on mouse and keyboard. I don't have a VR headset but tbh i didn't feel like i was at any huge disadvantage playing with out one. I would guess it would be better on it though. I don't believe I found a single bug or crash. And if combat  really isn't your thing, there is a mode where it's optional, though I didn't personally try it.All in all not a terrible expirence but i think it could have benifited from either being trimmed back a touch, thus letting somethings get more attention, or letting bake more/being backed by a big studio, though I understand dev's don't always have that privillage. I would say 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: Story wise: I would like to say about this game its more focused upon the bird, there's not really much to do, it's very simplistic in its design focused on the story, I tried to pay attention to the story but really just fell off in the first part of the game, which I don't really mind that a whole lot but it does suck that it seems you have a bird for no reason but just to dress up, and help you out with things that you could already do, if you had the right equipment, it's not really cool that the whole training process with your bird is skipped, it seems like some better character development could've happened between MC and the aunt, which probably would've made me care enough to go save her, now she is doomed forever. (once again pay attention to the story so I really don't have anything on this topic)Gameplay: Gameplay, meh, it's probably the worse I've ever played its not fun. This is how fighting a robot goes normally: "*Spam whip* *hit robot (robot is either immune or gets destroyed in 3 hits)* *bird flies somewhere gets shot* *visual confusion* *act like im crying now that bird looks like he just got smoked, and spam e until hes healed*" there you go, thats the combat system, not a fan of it.Birdy: :) tis is what makes it not get a negative review, they KILLED it, KILLED it, with the bird, you can do amazing interactions with the bird, one of favorites are: "Skate board w/ Waterbottle flip" "Hammer (secret item found clearing out I think UVA, far west tower once there, look around the area holding right click until blues show up, there should material, and a hammer outside hidden or sparking something like that.)" "Dabbing when pressing E with no item" "A blue sword that has two animations that I've gotten" *DONE*You can cook food for your bird which will improve certain statsYou can dress your bird either for the looks, or the stats, because you have clothing that will boost certain stats such as: The dragon mask, which improves I think 15% defense AND MIGHT, MIGHT IMPROVE attack. Barb helm which improves I think attack, and so forth. But you could give your bird a doggo mask, which is kinda cute, not my cup tea, AND A KITTY ALSO NOT MY CUP OF TEA.Anyways that's basically all of the game besides the side quests, easily getting lost, hunting (which just sucks), mine fields, sonar detector, claws, beaks, just everything feels kinda useless, like no reason feed your bird just press e, and no reason to kill robots unless they get near you, it doesn't feel as if the things you do have a significant impact on the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience, would definitely pick it up without a doubt. There are a few bugs here and there, like for example I got infinite gems from a container once, got me infinite money, so it can be really overpowered if it happens, but it really never happens. Great artstyle, adorable companion, nice customizable accesories, has a nice feel to it, and is overall just great. However, the game is a little bit short and the ending could make you cry, all that you worked for basically goes down the drain in the ending, and is really sad, it'll stick with me for awhile. Other than the ending and length, everything else is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very tentative recommendation, based mostly on the game's potential. Because as it is, it's an OK game with the potential to be a LOT more (whether in sequels or other games by the dev or whatever).I enjoy the story, but it feels like a first act without a followup. _childDocuments_.review: I've had Alyx Completion Syndrome for months now and haven't been able to find anything nearly as fun.  Falcon Age is not like Alyx, but it is really fun. _childDocuments_.name: Falcon Age

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique and fun game well worth playing in VR. It is a little rough around the edges, the animation could use some smoothing out and controls need fine tuning but it's made by a small team and you can't expect the level of polish a larger studio should (but still often doesn't) have. name: TOHU
detailed_description: Experience a brand new adventure game set amongst a world of weird and wonderful fish planets. Explore beautiful environments and solve intricate puzzles as a little girl, joined by her mechanical alter-ego, Cubus. Together they will discover the truth about themselves and the mysterious Sacred Engine that powers their world. Explore vivid and atmospheric locations, meet intriguing characters, and solve elaborate puzzles - all on your quest to repair the Sacred Engine. As The Girl you are light and nimble, and so can reach areas of the world that others can't. At any time you can transform into The Girl’s mechanical friend, Cubus. Need something heavy lifting? Need big strong arms to catch lightbulb flies as they pass by? Need to win an impromptu arm wrestle with an arcane and somehow tangible mirror image of yourself? Cubus has you covered. Each fish planet in TOHU is brought to life through bewitchingly beautiful artwork and is packed with detail. Meet a cast of bizarre characters and uncover cute critters to collect! You'll need your wits about you to solve TOHU’s unique and wacky conundrums. From a simple search for critters needed to power your expanse-traversing fly-ship, to learning how to operate a moustache-imbuing mole cannon. TOHU also features a musical score by Christopher Larkin, the award winning composer responsible for the soundtrack of Hollow Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game. A bit short, but an enjoyable feel-good experience. I'd recommend it for people who like a visual spectacle, but would suggest skipping for players looking for a puzzley challenge.Tohu's a lot like Botanicula, but a bit more puzzle-focused like Machinarium. It's similar in a lot of ways to Puzzle Agent too; the puzzles don't have any thematic links and almost feel placed at random. I didn't mind this as I fully expected it before purchasing, just note the game is effectively a random collection of simple puzzles.The game is divided into a series of hubs, each generally around 1-3 screens wide, and they're all self-contained. Unlike similar point and click games, it's a fully linear experience. I didn't mind how linear it was as it meant I never floundered around confused - I always knew where to go next and what the game was expecting me to do.The puzzles are largely very simple things - suitable for younger gamers even - but a couple of the logical puzzles are crazy difficult. If it wasn't for a few of them (hello bamboo puzzle) I'd even recommend this for young children. On the whole they're possibly a bit too easy, as the solution was immediately visible on most screens. A lot of the time the solution was interacting with the only clickable thing. Thankfully these puzzles don't require any logical leaps - don't expect to combine rubber ducks with clothes lines to fish for keys. The visual spectacle resulting from solving a puzzle was frequently bizarre though, but in a charming and enjoyable way. Watching the solutions play out was one of the best parts of the game.The story and characters are all forgettable, though their animation and 'voices' are fantastic. I'd happily spend dozens of hours exploring this world.Also worth noting that I purchased this game as it has the same composer as Hollow Knight. Whilst the music is decent in Tohu, I don't think it holds a candle to the Hollow Knight score.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: 4.1h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (16 achievements, all are missables). No. is a point-and-click game that focuses on problem-solving. You'll be given a scenario to clear one objective after another to proceed with the game. Some minigames will also be thrown in the mix to add variations.- Thinking outside the box is needed to solve most problems- In-game solutions for those who are stuck- It can be hard to check interactable objects since some areas will be restricted in the same screen- Some puzzles are not intuitive and require trial and error to solveIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The 13 GB storage that is needed for installation seems to be spent mostly on the visuals. The game was displayed with animations with a lot of layers, full of unique creatures that are inhabiting the area. The cute-looking creature and dream-like landscapes give a relaxing feeling whenever you solve challenging puzzles. However, the presentation of the dialogues between characters feels cheap with a dialogue box used to cover the whole page to show what they are talking about.There isn't much to the story. You'll be given a premise where you have to travel around the planets to clear an objective. Dialogues will mostly cover your objectives and don't add any depth to the story. The ending gives a surprise with the sudden revelation though, especially with the presentation that gives a nice conclusion to the game.Unlike other point-and-click games, 's objectives are mostly straightforward. You'll be given a main objective as soon as you reach a new area, which will be divided into some sub-objectives to help you accomplish it. The game will then move on to another location and repeat the whole process all over. This limits the solution of any puzzles to 1-3 screens, making it easier to figure out the solution without going too far. Still, it doesn't make the puzzles to be any easier than other point-and-click games though.It's easy to get stuck. The game usually tells what to do when you enter a new location for the first time, but there are cases where you are forced to open the menu and check the objective list manually. Some objects might also be hard to find due to the area range - most locations in  are layered, and you can't hover your mouse on the second floor to search for interactable objects when you are in the first floor. This makes it hard to check for interactable objects, especially since some objects can be easy to miss. The game can turn into a hidden object game sometimes when you need to find these things. features 2 characters that can be changed at any time you want. The Girl can pass through small passages and climb objects, while Cube can lift heavy objects. You need to change characters accordingly to solve some puzzles, although some objects might not be obvious to interact with when you are playing the character that wasn't meant to do it. It blocked my progression several times at first, especially at the beginning of the game.Some puzzles need to be brute-forced to solve - you'll be given some switches that you need to press, and there is no way to figure out the correct one unless you try out all combinations. Some minigames are also not intuitive. There were times when I had no idea what to do when the game opened a popup for a certain minigame, and there are no instructions that can help you to understand. Luckily, in the puzzles' case, the game offers an in-game solution that will provide you with a drawing that consists of the solution. You need to play a minigame to unlock it first though, and it can be annoying sometimes; you need to click whenever a pointer moves to a certain position, but the game tends to register the input in the wrong position, especially when the pointer goes faster.The game is very short - I finished it in 4.1h after obtaining all achievements. The game can be challenging to finish, especially because of the obscure objectives and some annoying minigames - I had to spend some time clicking buttons randomly in one minigame just to position everything in the right place. The in-game solution also helps whenever I was stuck, although I wished it would be given in the form of hints instead of solutions. Achievement hunters also need to be wary of their playthrough since all optional achievements are missable.Some puzzles require you to go to a precise spot, but you can only move to a predetermined spot. It's hard to guess the intended spots because of this. The controls for the point-and-click section also feel rough due to the slow walking speed and animation. Lastly, the subtitle tends to be hard to read due to the background color.It's hard to rate . I adore the cute presentation and calm-looking visuals, although I hated some of the puzzles. I mostly didn't aware of the interactable objects in each area, whether it was because I hovered the item when I was in another layer on the same screen or I was using the wrong character when I did it. Moreover, it was annoying when I had to look up the solution just because I missed a single thing. The game can be fun when I managed to solve something though, especially since most puzzles are tricky to solve. I can recommend it to those who like challenging puzzles, although I won't recommend it at full price due to the length and animation speed.

_childDocuments_.review: Sweet game with lovely animation and graphics. BUT there's a timed puzzle on the 3rd fish island, and this is a deal breaker for me.My kids played it first a couple months ago and got stuck there as well, and stopped playing because it's so frustrating. I thought I'd give it a try, and enjoyed it up until this point. I hate point and click adventure games that suddenly throw timed puzzles at you. It's so different from the rest of the game play, and is really limiting for people like me who struggle with timing. Basically a guy swings his flashlight around and you have to switch between the little girl and robot, using a mix of their skills. You have to jump up, jump down, move the stool, move it again. And God forbid you get caught, the entire things starts over again and moves the stool back. There are other cute games with a similar style, see Frog Detective series, Botanicala, Chuchel, Luna the Shadow Dust, that don't punish you with timing.

_childDocuments_.review: Back when I played  and , I placed Amanita Games high up on a pedestal - I really loved them. I’ve played similar other adventure games, but none of them seemed to raise up to Amanita’s standards - until now that is, after experiencing the wonderful game that is . It takes inspiration from their signature style, but the puzzles are more intuitive and in some ways less abstract.Several fish-like islands inhabited by peculiar beings comprise the universe of . It's a world in which machinery not only coexists with life, but blends with it to create fantastic creatures: a helicopter powered up by bees - BeeCopter, a street lamp whose bulb is a firefly jar etc. At the center of this world lies the Sacred Engine - the one and only heart of . The story starts one day when this Sacred Engine is attacked by a masked person - The Stranger - who comes to this realm with the intention of destroying it. You play as a little girl who, after witnessing this incident, embarks on a quest to find the necessary tools to fix it. Her path will lead you through each of ’s marvelous islands where you will meet fantastic beings and each of them will bring you one step closer to your goal after enlisting your help in solving their issues.  is a point and click adventure with a straightforward and linear storyline split into 8 short chapters, each following the adventures of The Girl on one of the islands. They are quite small and each consists of 3 screens only, thus there won’t be much back-and-forth happening, plus once you leave the island you won’t have the option to go back. In tone with the core idea of the game (machines and life merged together), The Girl can transform into Cubus - a bulky yet cute robot. As The Girl, you can climb surfaces or squeeze through tight spaces, while as Cubus you can lift heavy objects. The puzzles will often have you switch the character between its two shapes and when you’re not puzzling you will be able to continue your adventure in any of these forms. The game is played solely with the mouse (it also doesn't have controller support at the moment), and clicking on objects will either pick them up or interact with them, while clicking on NPCs will trigger a scripted dialogue sequence (you won't have any dialogue options to pick). ’s universe is full of life and while some of the creatures you click will act as collectibles, the others are purely cosmetic and will react to you with a charming animation and with an adorable sound. The world will in return interact with you if you interact with it, or rather respond to your clicks and this might as well be the most fun part when exploring a brand new location. Most of the puzzles are fairly easy, but there are some that require more effort (more iterations to solve it) and finally there are some that require you to have very fast reactions or click at a pixel-precise moment, with a couple of them being timed - all these have the potential to become frustrating and irritating, also considering the fact that the animations take a long time to finish for some of the movements. One of the things that  is lacking is a skip button, which means that if you won’t manage to complete one of these puzzles, you’ll not be able to continue / finish the story.Most of the achievements are easy to earn, but are usually missable. Apart from 2 collectible achievements, the rest are awarded for doing things in an uncommon way and at specific moments in your gameplay. There is no chapter select after you finish the game and you can't go back to a previously visited island, but apart from the built-in autosave, a save / load feature exists and I highly suggest making use of it if you're an  achievement hunter. Save as much as possible so you can reload later and get the achievements that you missed during your initial playthrough.  is a marvellous game that will keep you entertained for hours (between 2h and 7h, depending on your play style or if you're using a guide). The art is amazing and the soundtrack is exquisite too. If you're a fan of Amanita games, I'd say that this is a must-play, but keep in mind that while the puzzles are pretty intuitive, they're not always trivial and some require skill.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from a few small interface problems, I thought the game was very enjoyable. TOHU does not offer much in terms of compelling narrative, but it makes up for it with many cute and genuinely funny visual interactions. I didn't have many significant glitches during my playthrough, however, I had one softlock which I managed to fix by using the save file. You can complete the game in around 4 to 5 hours, depending on how often you will use the optional hint system. Unlike traditional adventure games, this game focuses more on the puzzles, while the narrative is mostly irrelevant to the overall experience. The puzzle logic was somewhat surreal, sometimes you have to click on everything until the solution becomes obvious. To give the game some well-deserved credit, the puzzles were more creative than many games in the genre. You can transform into 2 characters that will interact with the environment in unique ways, such as climbing or lifting heavy objects. Surprisingly,  both of the characters are fully animated and have specific animations for each task. Unfortunately, the game uses predetermined hotspots for walking, while it's not a huge problem, sometimes it can waste time if you get locked in the animation. Even though you can beat most of the puzzles using the hints, there are a few forced sequencing & timing mini-games that you can't skip - most of them are pretty easy, I only struggled with the bamboo puzzle. There is a good variety of locations, not just when it comes to aesthetics, but also in terms of game mechanics, such as using time-travel and mixing substances. As for the music, I thought it worked well within the context of the game, it certainly wasn't distracting. I won't say that game had a very immersive atmosphere because the story is just too basic to care about anyone, but I still enjoyed the lighthearted mood. + animation is very detailed, with many unique interactions for characters+ it's not too short, even with occasional hints it took me almost 5 hours+ very big range of puzzles with different mechanics + optional hint system, even has some nice sketches+ decent achievement support  - I had one random softlock in the pirate area (should be fixed according to the latest update). When you hover a puzzle item over the correct area, sometimes it does not show that you can drop the item in that location (I know it usually highlights the object, but it's not always the case). Personally, I don't like predetermined walking spots, sometimes I had to hunt for those areas. The stick puzzle where you build bridges is a bit clunky. On that note, the bamboo puzzle is a bit difficult in my opinion.The game is just a big eye-candy, and even though the story is kinda meh, it's so pretty that I would still recommend it for anyone that likes cute adventures. The puzzle design was very creative, granted the logic can get very surreal. It could use more polish with hotspots and how the game shows them when you hover the items, but overall I don't have much in terms of objective criticism. Cuteness overload... if you into that.
