_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a very good adventure game.Having played a lot of point and click adventure puzzle games like this, I'd say Tohu deserves about a C. Maybe a C minus. The background art is gorgeous, and the soundtrack - written by the same composer as Hollow Knight - is lovely. But that's about it. If you want the soundtrack, I'd suggest getting it directly from Christopher Larkin on BandCamp.All the art that isn't in the background is jarringly pixelated. It looks like the backgrounds were done with vector and the foreground with raster graphics. The main character constantly coos and giggles, which took about five minutes to turn extremely irritating. Worse from a visual perspective, there are constant animations of virtually all on screen elements. Characters, the background, objects, everything bobs and sways like the sort of cartoon designed for infants, constantly in motion to hypnotize the little sprogs into calming down in front of the tv.The puzzles so far aren't anything special. What enjoyment I would have gotten from them has been sapped by incredibly obnoxious directions that demand the whole screen to give you instructions like an unruly child who doesn't pay enough attention. Early on, the main characters comes to a locked door. She pulls and tugs on the door, miming that it is locked, before sighing in frustration. Immediately after, the entire screen dims and waits for you to acknowledge its very important message, "looks like the door is locked." This is the level of respect the game has for its audience's intelligence: none.I enjoy point and click puzzle games enough I expect I'll finish this one. But there's a good chance I'll be turning off the sound before I do. And if I'd known all this before buying the game, I wouldn't have bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: An insanely adorable adventure game that will make your heart flutter more than once. The creative influence of Amanita Design is evident, which once again proves just how powerful an influence they have on creators around the world. A mysterious villain descends on a small world, spread across the fish planets, who destroys everything around, disrupting the quiet life of local inhabitants. A girl who knows how to become a huge strong robot will help everyone, so the journey begins! The design of the planets is simply excellent, many inventive things can be found everywhere, strange and very cute locals constantly surprise and delight the player, surprises do not end until the very last location. There are certain questions about the design of some puzzles, but this will be discussed below. The game is characterized by a sincere cheerfulness, which easily brings a smile on the player's face, improving the mood. The main character is very kind and sincere, even the villain causes a kind smile, the absence of violence in the game in general is its important qualityThe level of puzzles in the game fluctuates quite a lot - from very simple to those that are almost impossible to solve without a guide. Many solutions delighted me with their elegance, I was not very pleased only with the final section of 3 puzzles, where a not very successful design solution forces you to go through kilometers of extra space just to interact with the elements of the puzzle. And in itself, the riddle with lanterns and locks is very nasty. In all other respects - my sincere applause. Everything is very diverse, not boring, with a great influence of the player's intuitive decisions and subtle work with logic. Well, if the decision never comes to mind, then there is always a system of hints that can help in a difficult situation. A bright impression and a smile on your face - that's what remains after passing "TOHU". A very high quality and interesting thing, suitable for players of all ages. We really need such bright and kind games, thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Tohu: A Fishy Frenzy of Fun!Just finished my first adventure in Tohu, and let me tell you, it was a wild ride!Eye Candy Planet Hopping: This game is gorgeous! Imagine swimming through giant fish planets, each one bursting with color and weird and wonderful creatures. It's like playing inside a crazy, beautiful cartoon.Brain Tickling Puzzles: The puzzles were like rollercoaster! Some had me feeling super smart when I cracked the code. Others...well, let's just say they had me muttering to myself for a bit. But hey, that's half the fun, right?Music to My Ears: Instead of characters talking all the time, Tohu uses music and sound effects to tell the story. It's pretty cool, and the music itself is fantastic! Catchy tunes that will be stuck in your head for days (in a good way!).Hints for the Win: Sometimes your brain needs a little help, and that's where the hint system comes in. It gives you a peek at the answer, but not the whole solution, which is kind of like having a friend give you a nudge in the right direction.Little Bummers: Using the controller to point and click wasn't always perfect, and there were a few times I missed things because they blended into the background a bit too well.Thumbs Up! Overall, Tohu is a super charming and unique adventure game. The world is a blast to explore, and the puzzles, even the tricky ones, are super rewarding when you figure them out.Who Should Play: This is perfect for puzzle fans who don't mind a challenge and love a game that's easy on the eyes (and ears!).

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr DO NOT BUY THIS, IT IS BAD.First the good parts, the animation is gorgeous. Though as a slightly sad note, all that gorgeous animation is a 13GB download so maybe start it a bit before you want to play. The music is also quite nice, though in places extremely derivative of Amanita games, specifically Botanicula and Machinarium (the later of which seems to have been a major :cough: influence on the whole game).The bad part: the game itself. The puzzle design wavers between atrocious and probable plagiarism. The latter first, and these might technically be spoilers but you can't spoil something this gross. They do the "wolf, goat, vegetable" puzzle played completely straight, no complexities and new angles, it's even literally a wolf, a goat, and a turnip. Also one of the last puzzles in the game is literally the water jug puzzle from Die Hard 3, the same size jugs and everything. Many of the other puzzles have extreme time pressure on them. You can repeat them as many times as you need but if you aren't exactly as fast with a mouse as the devs, sucks to be you. Do you have any kind of mobility issues in your hands? Don't even bother, you won't get more than half-way through. This is especially glaring giving the lovely chill tone the animation and music work so hard to create. Two of the puzzles I have absolutely no idea how you were supposed to solve them, other than brute force. I _think_ one of them had audio cues on the first run but if so I didn't hear them over the movie I was watching on another screen and again, sucks to be me. There are a few interesting puzzles mixed in, like exactly one fun use of a time travel mechanic, it's the same puzzle as everyone always does with time travel but at least it wasn't a literal copy of something as old as puzzle books themselves. On top of uncreative or outright obstinate design, the controls are rather fiddly which only amplifies the difficulty of a few timed sections and makes a few solutions very hard to notice (hint: many small objects have multiple interaction zones, often with no indication of this). One of the headline features of switching between the girl and her robot form serves literally no purpose I was able to discern other than making you sit through slow animations when you misclick. There is never a puzzle where you need to careful switch from one to the other in some special order, or any reason to not have a single character that can both lift heavy things (robo-mode) and climb on short boxes (girl). It's cute that many interactions have different animations for both forms but they just never do anything interesting with it.The 6.7 hours for this was to beat the full game and that includes stopping for dinner and leaving it running. Maybe 2-3 hours tops depending on how long you're willing to be frustrated before using the hints system (which is a dexterity minigame, again I hope you're quick with a mouse or no hints for you). Short would be fine if it wasn't laughable at times. The end of act one has the voiceover saying "and they having gathered all the tools she returned" and I actually shouted out loud "but I only got one tool". Maybe they planned more and had already recorded it, who knows. Short games are great but when half of it is already recycled content, you're getting into "maybe next time just make a short animated video?" territory.If you haven't played Machinarium, go play that instead and if you have, maybe just go play it again, it's still great.

_childDocuments_.review: (spoiler free) This is a game for patient people. Often times you make the wrong decision and get punished by long animations. There's also needless time draining such as jumping down four platforms and having to point correctly at each one instead of just clicking the ground and being done with it. Having to be pixel exact and standing in the right place to do things is important in this game. My main issue was that if you're stuck on a puzzle you've probably missed an item that blends in with the rest of the world! The world is great and I adore all the weirdness and funny critters. But overall as a game experience I was mostly annoyed. It's not that I dislike hard puzzles, which there weren't any of. But with the difficulty of finding items it kind of became the genre of: "spot five differences".Another strange point is the achievements which you get for, being bad? Not being able to immediately solve a puzzle rewards you. I like the thought of it but if you did solve something instantly then you might want to do it again, worse.I enjoyed playing as two characters! The ending however was very lackluster and I don't feel like I gained anything from playing other than cute art, which I could have gotten from looking at pictures of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: - Cutscenes are in video format and are somehow rubberbanding (stuttering) while also looking compressed (and still the game size is 13 GB?).- Most bare bones settings page I've ever seen, not even a separate slider for music/sfx.- A decent amount of the puzzles are just solved by trial and error, most range from boring to terrible.- Looooooong animations for everything, I know this is like a staple of the point & click genre but it doesn't have to be and it's also really bad here.The game has some sort of a mission log to track what you need to do which sounds nice but it just shows you a bunch of random tasks before you've even gotten to them.For example, it's like it'd say "Release the yellow elephant from the cage" but you just started a new chapter and didn't even see any elephants or cages.It's like the game is spoiling itself by showing you a bunch of things you're supposed to do before you've even talked to someone about them, bizarre. Even the achievements are dumb, I never understand games that have achievements that require you to purposefully do something wrong that you wouldn't normally do when it's not an interesting or fun interaction and this game has a bunch of achievements that require you to do those things 5 times in a row (they're also missable and there's no chapter select, you gotta use manual saves for that), what's the benefit of it besides just wasting time?My played time is inaccurate, it took me around 4 hours to get 100% but it felt way longer.But hey, at least it's got nice art.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually looks really good, and the music is also nice. Why the negative review then?I was planning on playing tohu on a train ride. About 2/3 hours in (which don't show up since I played in offline mode) I hit a bug in which my save couldn't progress. Since I only had the autosave I couldn't continue playing which was annoying to say the least.I emailed the devs with the problem asking for a solution on July 10th. I sent the saves, logs and everything as requested. Two weeks later, I still had no response so I made a post in the discussion forums here on Steam. Now, over a week since the post and three weeks total I have yet to hear a response.What I ended up doing was start a new save following a guide, which took me about an hour to reach the point where I was (yes, with the guide which told me exactly what to do).Other complaints:There's a puzzle with a samurai that needs really good timing and mouse speed. This was really hard to do on a trackpad. I am not sure how folks who some assistance might be able to do it (or some kids for that matter).Requesting a hint in the game is quite hard to do. Like the idea, hate the execution. I am glad it is not automatic, but it is REALLY hard. You need to be quite precise on a moving slider to hit it at the right time, four times in a row. If you miss one of those, you go back to square one. If you manage to hit all four, you get the hint! But remember it well, because if you close it, you need to be precise four times in a row again!Honestly, at this point I am not even sure if I want to continue playing until the end, or just leave it running to get the trading cards...

_childDocuments_.review: The art was good, the plot was poor and the puzzles were at times tiring.Tohu started off with a very weak and simplistic plot that felt too kiddish for my tastes. You play as a mouse tasked with repairing a broken board game, but the story failed to hold any interest. The puzzle aspects were a mixed bag - some challenges had creative ideas and were enjoyable to solve. However, other puzzles became tiresome fairly quick, often feeling like repetition over substance. While a few unique puzzles were entertaining, the overall weak narrative and hit-or-miss gameplay drag Tohu down. With its alternatingly easy but dull challenges and an unsatisfying plot, I cannot recommend Tohu. Another thing that bugged me was the continuous endorsement of headphones in the loading page as you start the game, etc. As if that changed a thing about the experience. Sure it looked Pretty and cute but the puzzles lacked consistent fun to make up for the kiddie story.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a lot of patience, I recommend. The game is gorgeous, It feels like every tiny action on every panel has 3 animations for each character, they put so much effort into the details...and that right there is the biggest flaw, they REALLY want you to see that. You want to pick something up? Well, Cubus is going to pose, then step back, then step forward, then grab it, then step back, then forward, congrats! you've picked up the thing! you'll see that 15 more times this puzzle. The game is really good at making you feel clever, but has a problem with 'well I felt really clever 2 minutes ago'The game has a few other flaws, namely 2 puzzles. There's no place for quicktime minigames in a point and click, and the green and yellow in the color puzzle are near identical in the one color puzzle. Even worse, the hints are in black and white pictures, I'm not colorblind but I did not notice the difference until an online guide pointed it out, if you're colorblind you're just screwed on that one. Most of the other puzzles I struggled with were just from me not seeing the interactable in the detailed and pretty screen. Outside that, the game genuinely is quite nice. It's carrying itself almost entirely on charm, but at about 4 hours it can get away with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from a few small interface problems, I thought the game was very enjoyable. TOHU does not offer much in terms of compelling narrative, but it makes up for it with many cute and genuinely funny visual interactions. I didn't have many significant glitches during my playthrough, however, I had one softlock which I managed to fix by using the save file. You can complete the game in around 4 to 5 hours, depending on how often you will use the optional hint system. Unlike traditional adventure games, this game focuses more on the puzzles, while the narrative is mostly irrelevant to the overall experience. The puzzle logic was somewhat surreal, sometimes you have to click on everything until the solution becomes obvious. To give the game some well-deserved credit, the puzzles were more creative than many games in the genre. You can transform into 2 characters that will interact with the environment in unique ways, such as climbing or lifting heavy objects. Surprisingly, both of the characters are fully animated and have specific animations for each task. Unfortunately, the game uses predetermined hotspots for walking, while it's not a huge problem, sometimes it can waste time if you get locked in the animation.Even though you can beat most of the puzzles using the hints, there are a few forced sequencing & timing mini-games that you can't skip - most of them are pretty easy, I only struggled with the bamboo puzzle. There is a good variety of locations, not just when it comes to aesthetics, but also in terms of game mechanics, such as using time-travel and mixing substances. As for the music, I thought it worked well within the context of the game, it certainly wasn't distracting. I won't say that game had a very immersive atmosphere because the story is just too basic to care about anyone, but I still enjoyed the lighthearted mood.Pros:+ animation is very detailed, with many unique interactions for characters+ it's not too short, even with occasional hints it took me almost 5 hours+ very big range of puzzles with different mechanics+ optional hint system, even has some nice sketches+ decent achievement supportFeedback:Some Nitpicks - I had one random softlock in the pirate area, I triggered the one on the bottom right while also getting the one on the top left, and then the hypnosis item became unresponsive. When you hover a puzzle item over the correct area, sometimes it does not show that you can drop the item in that location (I know it usually highlights the object, but it's not always the case). Personally, I don't like predetermined walking spots, sometimes I had to hunt for those areas. The stick puzzle where you build bridges is a bit clunky. On that note, the bamboo puzzle is a bit difficult in my opinion.Overall Thoughts: 8/10The game is just a big eye-candy, and even though the story is kinda meh, it's so pretty that I would still recommend it for anyone that likes cute adventures. The puzzle design was very creative, granted the logic can get very surreal. It could use more polish with hotspots and how the game shows them when you hover the items, but overall I don't have much in terms of objective criticism. Cuteness overload... if you into that.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Presents itself as an adorable adventure game, and the art holds that up, but the difficulty of tasks largely depends on how familiar you are with the type of puzzle or if you catch the references. There are bog-standard adventure game staples, but presented with no explanation, which is likely to be confusing to players new to the genre, and admittedly clever new puzzles, but again, no indication of even which elements on the screen are involved until you play the irritating mini-game to get a hint (or consult a walkthrough).More damning in my eyes, I really wish there was some way to know when a game leans heavily on timed-click minigames that require a moment's thought and an extended period of actually executing the solution. If i wanted that, I would be playing something like Tetris. The many minigames are heavily weighted to the end of the game, making it very unlikely that a player will run into them early enough to get a refund if they dislike them, and giving me the impression that they were thrown in due to requiring fewer dev resources.The ending also seems rushed, with zero emotional impact and an explanation that rips holes in the plot even such as it is. I received this as part of Humble Choice, and it was one I was specifically looking forward to. Having played it, I actively recommend against it.

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a cozy-looking puzzle point n click game with an art design reminding me of Hollow Knight and Don't Starve. It got various interesting puzzles and environments with a story of saving the world. While some puzzles might be hard and not very logical, I'd say it's still reasonable and eventually solveable. The soundtrack is good and the narrator fits well.I do recommend this game and it would be nice to see similiar games from the dev studio in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute point & click puzzle-adventure game. The puzzles were challenging, I honestly hated the 'Water Bamboo' puzzle, but I loved the 'Wolf, Sheep, Plant' & 'Water Pouring' puzzles. The game features 2 characters: The Girl & Cubus. Both have different abilities, with Cubus being strong & able to carry heavy objects, while The Girl can't. There were puzzles that required the player to switch between the 2 characters to solve.I loved how its visuals were mostly purple, which looks stunning, beautiful, and creates a sense of mystery that fits well with its story. The narrative voice is also good (headphone recommended for better experience). However, the story was a bit confusing to me that maybe my conclusion could either be right or wrong. Also, the narrative voice and subtitles were not always synced in cutscenes. In addition, achievements can be achieved in just one-run.In either way, it's a well-crafted game & still offers a cute and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This. Is. So. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 4th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A point and click adventure in the “What was the dev” thinking variety.Tohu looks great, yeah again I’m going to talk about the graphics, because look at this game, it’s a feast for the eyes.  Every area, every level, every object has so much care and detail in it, I’m amazed.  The art shines and it is fun to just click around the level to see what you can move even if it’s just a small idle animation.Tohu is about clicking around a level and trying to figure out what the dev was thinking.  It’s a style of point-and-click game where players are supposed to figure out how to manipulate the world to achieve their goal.  However, what that goal is can be part of the puzzle.   Overall, it’s a good concept but it’s going to resonate with only some people. Pick this up if you like Machinarium or Samorost both by Amanita Design, sorry if I’ve butchered any of that.  I thought this might also be from the same company because of how similar the style is… it’s not.   At the same time, this is a short adventure, about four to five hours, and it can be very obtuse at times.  If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Tohu is neat little point and click adventure game.Pros:-Nice art design with fluid and very alive animations.-Neat little different worlds with different goalsCons:-The story is a bit of let down, it teases as if there's a deeper meaning but it doesn't really expound upon it.-Puzzles are mixed bag, for the most part very standard puzzles, but some kinda be a bit finicky.-Sound design is cool, but a lot of the time you're just listening to insects buzzing or random babble speech on loopOverall, the presentation of this game is very cute and enjoyable, but the actual gameplay is very standard. There's plenty of "lore drops", but you never really feel the impact of the "story" beyond the game shoving some random messaging at the end out of nowhere. I enjoyed just exploring parts of the game, and I think it would've fared well enough without them trying to force some deeper meaning in there.Rating: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly don't get the love this game seems to be getting here on Steam. I play so many point and click adventure games and this is definitely one of the poorer ones I've experiences since the genre began.First of all, the game is horribly unoptimized. 13 gigs for a game this minimalist screams bad programming from the start, and that's what I encountered from beginning to end. From Click Boxes that overlap or are too small, hampering your progress, to badly designed puzzles that require excruciatingly exact placement so that even being a pixel off is registered as an incorrect solution in a TIMED puzzle - there's just no excuse for this level of sloppiness in a genre that is pretty easy to get right. The entire illusionist level is the perfect example of badly done puzzles, with the Ouija board planchette is by far the worst, but the gear puzzle (which SHOULD be pretty easy with some really obvious solutions) is hampered by those exact pixel placement issues I talked about earlier. What should have taken me a few seconds took about fifteen minutes because the game would not accept the placement despite being the right solution. I had to spend several dozen times trying to get it to accept the gear in that spot before it finally did, and thus move on. Another awful example is with the stealth/trampoline bit. The exact spot to change into Cubis (your other self) is also the same click box spot for "jump up/down" several times in this puzzle, causing you to mess up and have to start over - which at least nets you an achievement in the end. So much of this game needs to be tightened up and while it took me about three hours to slog through this, it felt like ten times that because it was so bad.Also, don't me get started on the awful ending. The core theme of the game was cute and interesting, if shallow, but that ending. I don't want to do spoilers but oh man, was it the cherry on the top of this fecal sundae. This is one of my least favorite ending tropes along with "it was all in the protagonists mind" or "it was all a dream." I had really high hopes for this game thanks to the ratings and screenshots, but this was an utter disappointment from beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a lovely little title where the world is one of a kind, our protagonist is a charming and mysterious character, and the puzzles are the right kind of fun for a point-and-click adventure. The game has its minor flaws, but they take a seat backstage when compared to everything the game does right.This is a title that can easily sit next to giants of the genre like Machinarium, Monkey Island, and Grim Fandango. I know these types of games are not everyone’s cup of tea, but if you are a fan and are looking for that next point-and-click fix, then look no further than TOHU and its immaculate world and adorable characters.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: I found TOHU to be a cute and whimsical point-and-click adventure game. The puzzles were interesting and of good difficulty. I did have some issues with interacting with objects, particularly what could be interacted with and where to find the interaction zones to climb objects. I recommend TOHU to players attracted to its world and character design, that are looking for more freeform puzzles.TOHU is a point-and-click adventure game set in a whimsical world where the characters living on flying fish and other aquatic animals. Players take on the role of The Girl and her companion Cubis to set out in search of help when a mysterious stranger damages the sacred engine keeping their fish planet alive. To do so, they have to convince a number of odd neighbors to help them, doing everything from participating in a magic show to turning a lizard into a dragon.The puzzles in TOHU usually focus on being presented with a single screen of interactable parts and trying to determine what interactions will yield results. There are some puzzles that require finding hints elsewhere or finding a key item, but most focus on the player's ability to figure out what needs to be done. A fair number of puzzles do require a decent reaction time, and a small reaction time puzzle is required to unlock the hint sheet for each area.One thing I found a little troublesome was how often it was unclear what the player could interact with. This was particularly annoying in one section with a guard where failing to identify the task and execute it with quick reaction time would force the player to have to start over. Interactable locations to jump up or climb down terrain were also finicky and often not in the spot I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is an attractive point-and-click puzzler in the vein of Chuchel, Gobliiins, or Luna: The Shadow Dust, but with a dash of Dr. Seuss.  Our story in this game is quite loose.  The game is set in some sort of cosmic school of giant fish, and on the back of each fish, there is a unique explorable world.  A nefarious cloaked figure is running around causing trouble, and has destroyed an important machine.  We play as an unnamed little girl whose goal is to repair the important machine and to set things right again.  This gives us an excuse to visit each of the fish planets in our bee-powered aircraft to solve inventive puzzles and locate the necessary materials. Our hero is cute and cheerful, and giggles her way through each area.  She is nimble, and can crawl through small openings or climb steep walls with ease.  For situations involving a bit more muscle, she has the ability to transform into a large robotic golem that can lift and carry large objects or toss aside bulky debris.This game is not really a narrative adventure game, and it is not the type of game where you will need to solve "combine X with Y"-type puzzles.  The game is very linear, and at any given point, you will only have a single goal and access to 1-3 screens.  Generally, you click around the area, and experiment with the interactable objects, marvel at all of the lovely little animations, and piece together what it is you are meant to be doing and how to go about doing it, with little to no specific directions.  The puzzles strike a good difficulty balance overall; in my opinion, they are neither too easy nor too hard.  There is an in-game hint system if you get stuck, but I would encourage you not to use it, as that may make the game go by altogether too quickly.  If I get temporarily stuck in an area, I put the game down for a few hours and I generally solve the puzzle as soon as I come back to it fresh.I am not finished this game at the time of this writing, as I find it lovely to dip in and out of rather than rush the whole thing in a marathon sitting.  While working from home, it's a lovely treat to be able to leisurely play through a screen or two on lunch break.If you are in the mood for a vibrant, artsy experience with a good soundtrack, and don't mind solving some puzzles, this is a solid pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Was captured by the charm of this game and the visuals did not disappoint. It's a beautiful looking game with great locations, creative characters and clearly a great deal of love in it's making. The game plays nicely as well in the opening segment and the ability to switch between the two characters/personas with their different skills was a nice gimmick that added a lot to the gameplay. However... I'm leaving a negative review because I found the game became increasingly frustrating as I progressed. Not because it got harder necessarily but things just seemed to make less sense as the game continues. I've played a great deal of similar point and click adventure/puzzle games so not much is new to me these days but I found myself confused on a number of occasions regarding what I was expected to do or how to do it. This was made even worse at times when it turned out the idea I had had was correct all along but I wasn't clicking in the perfect place or timing it just right... There is no explanation of anything at any point in the game (including why we have this split personality in a box) and the hint system that does thankfully exist is a frustration in itself. It takes an infuriating minigame to open and usually only tells you how to do the stuff you've already done... Audio is strange in places with a particular pirate scene repeating the same obnoxious chant so often and loudly that I muted the game for that section. Speech between islands is also ridiculously quiet compared to all other game sounds which is an odd choice, almost inaudible without subtitles. All in all this IS a good game and I enjoyed it a great deal starting out. Sadly for one reason or another, that feeling waned as I trudged through roughly 4 hours to completion... Definitely worth appreciating for it's art and design but the puzzles and gameplay can be hugely frustrating at points, enough to rob me of that initial enjoyment. Ultimately I'm leaning to a negative review simply because that is the minority at the time of writing. I feel like the frustration and occasional lack of direction is enough of an issue that potential buyers should be made aware of it. I WOULD recommend it however, provided you usually enjoy this kind of game and have a good amount of patience. Just be prepared for some headscratching, and headbanging, moments as you go!
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Soft pass.It is wonderfully animated and it's an interesting setting but I'm getting so tired of the "puzzles that make 'sense' to the developers" that amount to trying everything until something works. If the world was somewhere I knew to do something like 'capture the bugs to turn on a light so the grass fries so you can see the signs', then I imagine it might have less difficulty, but this isn't logical and calming, it's exhausting and tiresome. Perhaps I'm expecting too much and the developer thinks that people will be able to discern their puzzles' arcane logic, but when you rely on a world that I don't understand so heavily, stumbling into the solutions don't make me feel like I earned the solution, just a headache. Thinking outside the box is nice and all but when I don't even know what the box's dimensions are, I won't know when I'm thinking outside of it. The hint system even has hit-detection issues; when it's clearly over the tooth of the wheel-lock that it should hit, it sometimes won't.Yet another point and click adventure game that's too obsessed with its own cleverness to rise above the genre's bad trappings. Pity.

_childDocuments_.review: A good little game with an infuriating whack-a-mole mini-game around halfway through. As a result, 3 out of 4 players give up (I haven't made this number up, you get the 'It's Showtime' achievement for passing that level, and currently only 24.4% of players have it). There are hints in the discussions section how to beat this bone-crushing and nerve-wrecking challenge. I managed to complete it concentrated on the bottom right tiles while holding my mouse with both hands, spending maybe as much time on this one mini-game as on the whole first half of  the main game. But, apparently, you could just jump to the tiles where a hammer just fell, as it won't fall on the same tile twice (can't confirm). Would recommend the game if the developers made the whack-a-mole mini-game skippable or at least playable with buttons instead of a mouse.

_childDocuments_.review: "Adventure as a little girl, or transform into the mighty Cubus." That seems to be the unique selling point of this game.But:- Don't think that playing a little girl means this is a game for children; the subject matter is child-friendly, but most puzzles would be far too difficult.- That mighty alter-ego is severely under-utilised. It will always be clear when to use one character or the other, so that 'puzzle' can then be solved by one click. If the girl had been strong, the 'mighty Cubus' could have been left out of this game entirely, apart from his role in one unnecessary non-interactive scene at the end.The puzzles themselves range from original to horrible. There are puzzles that nicely use background details in unexpected but fair ways, but due to the nonsensical setting, it is hard to know how objects will react when you click on them. As a result many puzzles just consist of clicking on everything and seeing what happens. And the puzzles that DO make sense are way too often unoriginal, have to be solved multiple times, or are just busywork or brute-forcing.Also note that there are a number of arcade-like segments that require quick and precise clicking. These segments are made more difficult by hotspots that are not always where you would expect them, the climbing animation being particularly horrible.I finished the game in about 4 hours, but used a walkthrough for four puzzles: - I had overlooked an object- My reasoning was correct but my character did not stand in exactly the right place (some puzzles require almost pixel-perfect clicking) - My reasoning was correct but I didn't expect the need for such quick and precise clicking.- And the final one : I have no clue how I could have found the solution of that one without spending an hour with graph paper. (And all streamers/guides that I saw afterwards also just brute-forced it, without any explanation.)So basically this is an Amanita-like adventure (weird world/story, click everywhere, largely without text) with less charming animations, more illogical puzzles and shorter runtime. I can't recommend it for the few original puzzles alone.

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU can be viewed, if not as a masterpiece of ambience, than as a beautiful adventure. Although on the shorter side, the game offers a lot of amazing features: 1. I just have to acknowledge Christopher Larkin's phenomenal contribution to this project. As always, his music makes the gaming experience like a fantastic dream. 2. The artstyle is unique and beautiful. It creates a nice fantasy world mixed with steam punk elements, arguably a one of a kind world.3. The gameplay is basically a simple but good click-and-point adventure with challenging puzzles.4. The story is heart-warming and unique.However, since TOHU is a very short game, the price is too expensive.

_childDocuments_.review: Tohu gave me a very strong Amanita game vibe and if you've ever played something like Machanarium or Botanicula you'll find this game feels sort of similar to those. It does have its own unique artstyle and setting though it's just more in the actual gameplay where it feels more like playing one of those games.It's a pretty good game overall. You play as a girl who can also transform into a rocky cube man travelling between different fish worlds in order to save the fish world she lives on. This sounds like a pretty crazy premise but its a pretty charming game all the same.The puzzles, other than a couple, manage to have a good balance of being a bit challenging but not frustratingly so. In fact the few times I got stuck was more because I hadnt realised there was an item I could interact with and pick up as its not always immediately obvious unless you hover your mouse over the object.Other than that though I dont really have any other major complaints. If you played and enjoyed any Amanita games then I think this is a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Tohu is cute!! I love this game, it is such a comfort game to me! It feels just as nostalgic as playing one of those fun point & click game from your childhood, but it's a new(ish) game! Specifically, I really loved all of the worlds, the art, the environments and animations, they're all just so beautiful and well done! Its distinct art style perfectly encapsulates a beautiful and quirky fantasy world. I put off reviewing this game because I didn't really know how to explain why this game is good. It's just satisfying, clicking on things and seeing the cool animations. The developers really put their all into this and it shows. The puzzzles and mini games are really fun too, it's very involved point and click, I was never bored. I really liked the ability of swapping between characters, it's such a great mechanic! The animations, the music, the gameplay, just everything is just so solid! I'd love to discuss more about this game's story, why I like it, and why I feel it works so well, but that'd be spoilers. Please, do yourself a favor and play it when you can afford it!

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly recommend TOHU, but it's a mixed bag.The good:- excellent visual design- very nice music- nice animation- some nice puzzlesThe bad:- some puzzles are in the wrong game (whack a mole, cut the power cables are purely speed puzzles, and no fun for me, took me way too much time to beat them)- for some reason the mouse lags! it's annoying at best, but also makes the speed puzzles even harder- I wonder if some puzzles can be solved without being recognized (mostly filling the jar)- the need to place certain things precisely with zero visual clue is irritating- the story ending is quite disappointing, it feels like it was rushed because production ran out of money- the "Girl" should have a name, other characters have one!- in some areas (machines at the end, illusionist) the noises are just plain obnoxious, shouldn't this be a relaxing game?- on the illusionist planet, there is just one area... so autosave never triggers :(- in many cases, just use the random object with the random thing to make progress, it feels arbitrary and not really funGet it on sale, play it for the visuals and the cute and (sometimes) relaxing vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely worth your time, though I don't think this game is designed well. Considering it's a puzzle game, it becomes very cumbersome for a few reasons: even for the short time it will take you to finish this game, telling the difference between objects with which you can interact and not interact isn't easy; any sort of character animation and movement is fairly slow; specifically the idle animations and background noises are too noisy; and if you get stuck, the hints generally explain the easy-to-figure-out portions of the puzzle and ultimately are useless. That being said, there are some nice aspects of this game. Tohu's composer, Christopher Larkin, is pretty incredible, and you might know him from a different game. The soundtrack is great and the graphics are likewise, but fairly challenging puzzles and slow, confusing gameplay is a bad combination.

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a charming, lovely, polished puzzle game that quickly becomes a slog in the second half. I'd give it a soft 6/10.If you're a fan of PnC adventure games, if you have the patience for those sorts of mechanics, you'll probably enjoy it. It does have Baby's First PnC elements here and there, like bringing in some classic balancing puzzles like the fox-chicken-corn across the river etc.The big problems with this game are 1) you have no direct control over the character actions and 2) a significant chunk of the puzzle solving starts (and often ends) with "click on things that let you click them until something happens". It's not really intuitive until you get a dotted line between point A and B with big arrows pointing at them, or you get lucky.Still, the game was pretty enjoyable... until the swamp. The first puzzle there is absurdly fiddly with absolutely no grace or pity, which involves mostly waiting, clicking, and hoping to get lucky. Pretty much the only other actual puzzle there is also the kind of thing that mostly involves brute-forcing or looking up a guide. It's a shame because aside from those the area actually has a pretty cute quest with pretty intuitive actions attached to it, but it burned through all its grace in the first five minutes (and the following thirty before I could move on past that first 'puzzle'),This combined with a story that also becomes unintuitive in the beginning of the same act makes for a less than pleasant experience, and it just continues until the end. It's really strange because the game is pretty polished despite that - it's like the devs got married to some ideas and never asked the question "does the game really need this?"The animations are swell, but because you have no direct control, they lose charm really fast since you're forced to wait through them before you can actually accomplish things. The audio is decent, but a lot of really annoying sound effect have very, VERY short loops, usually in areas with time-consuming elements.For real, though, if you don't love Point and Click games like this, really think about whether you want it. (At least it's low on wacky Moon Logic?). I actually was going to Recommend this game and then got to a part that assumes you can guess how much liquid some vessels can hold when the measurements are slanted more to fit the art style than actually be helpful, and the liquid is the exact same color as the background (black, in a dark area). This is exactly as annoying as it sounds. Even more than, because you have to wait on your heavy robot body to sloooooowly clunk from one side of the screen to the other, multiple times, and that even if you manage to do it perfectly on the first try.Oh, and if you're color-blind you might want to give it a pass, there's a few color-dependent puzzles with no accessibility settings or real way to tell what you're looking at.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend for good players with fast machines, but have reservations for beginners like myself or those with slow machines. I honestly hope the devs do an update to allow for an 'easy mode' so people like me can see the whole story despite our slow machines, inexpert gameplay.I love the art, and am intrigued by the world and the story. However, I don't have a fast PC and some minigames are impossible to beat with a slower machine and mouse setup (even after almost an hour of trying). There is no setting to bypass a minigame or to make it slower, nor does the system recognize that you aren't able to beat a fast minigame and slow it down.  I know some players love hard to beat games, and some game devs think they shouldn't allow their game to be 'dumbed down', but that just means a lot of players (like me) even though they try hard will not be able to finish the game; and won't bother buying another from that game company. Wouldn't it be better to give all players (even ones that buy the game for the story but don't have 'game machines' nor expert reflexes) a chance to finish the game and see the story in its entirety?  So in my case, a waste of money since I don't have a fast enough machine to be able to beat a fast minigame blocker.  Hoping their will be an update that allows for 'easy' or 'bypass' mode so I can finish the story sometime in the future. (Else, this is a dead game for me at this point, sadly.)
