_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play point and click adventure games, but this one reminded me of some of my favourites from Amanita, so I thought I would give it a crack. The sound design and art style are fab, with a great amount of whimsy which, in my opinion, keeps this type of game style from feeling stale. Completion time is only around 3-4 hours if you take your time like I did so it isn't particularly long, but I still think it's worth it, especially if you can get it at half off or so.UPDATE: Having now finished the game (at around 4 hours as stated, because I missed a specific button that held me up for a minute) I have to say that by the end, I was definitely getting frustrated. The art direction and sound are still gorgeous, but it got tiresome completing some of the later puzzles considering just how SLOW your character/s move, really dragging everything out. Still worth a play, but towards the shine definitely wore off a little.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: The pacing is solid throughout most of the four to five hours of playtime, and you are never stuck on one puzzle for more than a few minutes. There’s only about three or four exceptions to that rule, but despite that, I enjoyed solving them. Some of the late stages of the game felt like a drag to me, simply because of the aforementioned lack of a clear narrative, but I pushed on nonetheless. The excellent visuals and the large variety of creative puzzles are the reason why I pushed through and finished Tohu, they’re also why I adored its quirky and whimsical world.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect cozy game. No combat, great puzzles, no time limit, and no pressure. I play TOHU when I am feeling overwhelmed, and I like it so much that I am going to buy it on a separate console. The art, story, and narration are all incredible; you can tell a lot of effort was put into this game. I'm particularly fond of the in-game hints offered if you get stuck, that was a really nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Technically you have two game characters for the price of one in this game. TOHU is a nice puzzle game which makes you scratch your head a few times in order to figure out, how to achieve some things. This game really IS cute. The puzzles are challenging enough not to make the game boring. It is built up nicely, so that in order to advance, the player has to do certain things first. A short but nice game.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game inspired by Amanita studios (there is a achievement which sugest that). My daughter really enjoyed the whole world with strange animals. The soundtrack of this game is amazing. I love the story. I can recommend this game to anybody who would like to play the game with his/ her child. The approach of the game to the adults and to the kids is very good balanced.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Cartoonish point and click adventure with pleasing graphics and somewhat interesting story. I was surprised with the game size given the short playtime, could be all the characters and movements.As for the achievement difficulty you can get it all in one playthrough, given that you look up a guide to dont miss some hidden challenges. A save feature will help with backwards hunting for these elusive tasks even if you dont look for it from the start.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a roughly 5 hours long point & click game that stands out with its very charming style and design but lacks polish in many aspects. I felt like the sound hasn't been mixed well at all which results in a big mess of background noise while you try to focus on a riddle. At one point I encountered a bug that forced me to restart and redo a puzzle. It offers the player an actually extensive hint system for most of the puzzles. The story, while very basic, kept me entertained and motivated throughout the playthrough and actually had an interesting ending in my opinion.I'd still give TOHU a recommendation if you like the point & click genre. It isn't too easy but also offers assistance should you ever get stuck. It's got its flaws in terms of playability but I really enjoyed the design of the world and the riddles were overall well done.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Very Beautiful game that is great to play if you want something to play that will only take a day. Gorgeous graphics and in some cases the puzzles are forgiving in how you do them (depending on the puzzle type itself)I suppose my one gripe was the cupboard/drawer puzzle in Juncle's house which I felt wasn't very obvious that it was a puzzle and only by using the hints (which isn't easy to access but I guess is kinda the point) did I find out that it was a puzzle). The bamboo water puzzle was rather difficult for where it is in the game but maybe I just suck at mathematics and any 5th grader could figure that out.I hope there are more games like this from the same studio
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Full of fun, abstract puzzles and an interesting plot behind it all, Tohu is a relatively short game that, surprisingly, made me think a bit after it was all done. The weird animals around the worlds add to the odd nature of this universe, and immersed me for a few hours of game play. Recommended for all puzzle people!
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: This really could have fooled me for an Aminita Designs game. If you are a fan of Machinarium, or others by that team, you will enjoy this. I really bought it to hear what Christopher Larkin could do outside of the Hollow Knight world, and he did fine. Luckily, I am a big fan of Machinarium, so I continued and finished it. It's short, 3-4 hours, maybe more if you're not getting a puzzle and your stubborn to not use the in game hints minigame. I am ultimately interested to see what else this team comes out with, we could really use more point and click adventure games in the world right now, totally refreshing from the open-world sagas that span 100+ hours.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game. That being said, I understand some of the critiques it's gotten.There are times (not many) when it's really not intuitive what you should be doing or looking out for. I needed to use the built in hint tool two times throughout the game to be able to progress, and sometimes the revealed answers seemed kinda gimmicky to me.I can also understand that some reviews say that the animations take too long. It's true that when you are clicking away trying to find out what you can do in each scene it can be a nuisance, but it didn't bother me too much.What led me to try this game is the soundtrack composer Christopher Larkin, the same composer for the Hollow Knight OST. It's not the same style or genre of game, so don't expect the same type of music, but the characteristics of Larkins compositions are all there while you are solving some puzzles.Overall a really nice experience. Relax, play and enjoy the beautiful animations and music.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Surreal and surprisingly subversive.Couple of the puzzles are not mechanically intuitive, there isn't anything in the conventions of the genera or the game itself to set up what needs to happen. Not an enjoyment killer, just leaves one banging one's head against a wall for a bit then wondering how the hell one missed something so simple.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: A nice short story with numerous puzzles. Recommend on sale. Took roughly 5-7 hours at a very relaxed pace but could be done in far less than that if you are determined to speed through it. Don't expect a in detail long storyline but it is a welcome breath of air from many of the other games out there today. If you can stream to a tv and play with friends the game and puzzles become infinitely more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: <kinda spoilers>i wanted to recommend this, but it has 2 really frustrating moments, where is not about joy, but precision to the last millimeter - part with sticks while creating a bridge (this was semi acceptable) but second i encountered enraged me a bit (bottom right seal while releasing amplifier) this took me like 15 mins to adjust correctly. you should kick in a head person responsible for programming this part as 2 other seals worked smoothly.outside of this quite enjoyable game, similar to Karma. Incarnation 1 but not as smooth.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Pretty graphics, some charm.Cons: All puzzles are tedious. Half of them make no sense and rely on clicking everything until something works. Every single thing has a tiny hitbox and a too-long unskippable animation; thus, if you misclick, you have to watch the animation before you can try again.I really wanted to like the game, as it does seem like a labor of love, but they needed to think more about making it fun.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little point-and-click adventure game. I felt that the story was a bit lacking, but I definitely enjoyed the four and a half hours I spent playing this game. I also really enjoyed the score, though at times it was hard to hear it due to sounds being made by the characters. Would definitely recommend this for anyone who is a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: The main praise I have is for wonderful fluid animations and great atmosphere. It's just a beautiful game, worth playing just for that. Every environment and "room" design is very well put together. And I really love that most interactable objects are done in the same style as the backgrounds and everything else as too often P&C suffer from the "obvious interactables syndrome".Now, it's very childish, which just means I'm not the target audience, so I won't judge the game based on that either way.The actual puzzles and P&C aspects are fine. The main problem is not having enough information a lot of the time and there being no redundancy. You can't examine anything, the character never says anything. And there's a good reason why P&C games have the character do voice lines about things. Because it's impossible to guess what crazy string of logic the designers intended or what clunkiness had been introduced due to game-specific engine. And unfortunately, it's all alien world stuff, so it's hard to relate with anything and guess what crazy logic things follow. Normally, this might be okay as long as it's within a consistent ruleset you can learn, but here all rules are out of the window as anything goes. Thre is some feedback though and it's very neatly integrated into the game world with animations and custom reactions. There's also no hotspots so it's too easy to miss something, especially when it all blend together. It's also one of those god mouse games where you must click some things, but must use characater for other things with no consistency. The puzzles also have inconsistent difficulty as they don't get harder or nuanced or based on previous knowledge. Some puzzles are clever but waaaay too many are just reaction or precision based and too many are just brute force combinatorics. So many puzzles have great premise, but they are over way too soon and their mechanics are way too underutilized. How many wolf-sheep-cabbage and 4-units-from-3-and-5-containers puzzles can one solve. Plus, you go from area to area and everything is very self-contained, meaning complexity never really rises past "here's a bunch of things to click, figure out the sequence". There's also a great deal of clunkiness as you can't really queue actions and have to wait for a lot of animations and transitions to do something. This gets old fast with some repetitive puzzles.The story is very simplistic and childish and there's not much to say. Characters are just random one-dimensional charicatures. The game is also rather short so you don't get to learn much. The lore is non-existent besides exposition narration. The very ending had an interesting twist/point, but it never carried over into gameplay, so it didn't really matter at all.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: A point and click adventure with classic game-play and likeable characters. The cute art style adds to the games charm. Due to the low difficulty of this game it is suitable for players who are not used to point and click adventures or younger gamers, there is also a in game hint system that practically gives the solution to puzzles when used.Game time is about 6 hours depending on "skill" and how quick you resort to using the hint system. For most of the game twitch reflexes are not needed and lateral thinking will solve the problem.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and highly whimsical point n click. Animation and art is definitely the highlight, especially with 2 main characters to animate. Story has minimal logical pretense so enjoy the ride. Puzzles are serviceable but can be very "moon logic" (the fantastical setting sadly aggravates this) and can require trial and error. Thankfully, there is an in-game hint system that is very gracious and easily guides you through any difficult areas.Absolutely avoid if you have zero inclination towards any point n click game :)
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 - If you want to relax for a couple of hours with a puzzle game, I recommend TOHU:-incredible level puzzle design with lots of unique mechanics in each part of the game;-amazing animations, even for the idle stances;-the characters are ingenious and their "speaking" is cute and funny;-even pressing 2 buttons next to each other has different animation, clever thought!-the ending seems a little rushed
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: This game was cute, I liked the art and the story. As other people have said, you can feel love just pouring out of the game through the environments, with something interesting to look at wherever your eyes settle on the screen. Gameplay was mixed; some of the puzzles were lacking signposting which could get pretty frustrating, and the game slows you down via it's animations and movement to compensate for limited puzzle elements. Some puzzles are based on timing and dexterity so if you have limitations with these things, you might not find parts of this game enjoyable (or even doable). Otherwise the mechanics were interesting.Overall an enjoyable enough few hours if you're into point and clicks and are willing to do some out of the box thinking.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this review, I am an avid player of indie puzzle games. I enjoyed the art style, immersive music, and the story of the game. I loved how interactive the environments were, it kept me engaged in the game. The puzzles were challenging but not so easy that I could speed through them, which was nice. Overall I highly recommend this game, especially if you liked Machinarium. (It has similar vibes) It's a shorter game but still took me a couple of days to complete. Definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: 6/20Pros:+ Cute game+ No bug encounters (mb because it takes like 4 hours to beat)Cons:+ Super slow progression. Each movement you character do start an animation, which is super slow. You have to climb 5 crates? Good, let's click 5 times, and see 5 time the same animation. It take ages to climb a stair. Ever worse on puzzles where you need to move your character though the screen.+ Terrible sound design. Most sounds creatures/characters emit are ok. But some are so annoying, you just mute the game to not having to hear them one more time.+ Terrible game design. Almost all puzzles make no sens. Either you don't know what to do, or the puzzle you're facing is a classic of puzzles games you already did 50 times. Like wolf sheep and cabbage enigma. The game dev knew what they where doing ! And you want to know how I know it ? There is a "hint" screen you can access though a mini-game (which is not fun), where you can find the solution of the room you are in.Well, the game is cute, and that's all it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER AHEAD. This game wasn't for me. On top of having to restart the game a bunch because characters/dialogue/actions wont load or work I had to play through the game multiple times just to get the game to register I actually talked to everyone. There is no chapter select which is mind blowing to me. The puzzles were brilliant but because of the bugs it really took away from enjoying the game. Its hard to enjoy when you have to redo puzzles over and over because of bugs. The final straw for me was the ending of the story. It was dull. Uneventful. I did all of this work for what? Because future me is a JERK lol? I wish the ending was as brilliant as the puzzles. This game was a let down because I really loved the way it looked and was hoping for a good story to go with it.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: A nice point and click game. I really liked the artwork, which reminds of machinarium and samorost. Some of the puzzles did not make any sense to me without the provided hints (e.g. the bagpipe). This game seems to me like it tries to stay  accessible to younger players, which is why I recommend this game. Otherwise, it's a fairly short game, without too much challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: There are puzzles. The art is OK. If you *really* like puzzle games, you might be able to ignore all the bad parts of the game.The controls are infuriating, often doing something completely unintentional. The story is a hot mess. The whole game design does not "respect the player", slows down puzzle solving with slow animations, extra steps that add nothing but slow down the game play, and sound design that can be really harsh on the ears.Total time to completion is ~5 hours. I'm glad it's over. This is NOT a game that'll make you wish there's more, or even to want to come back to after a session.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, cute little experience you can complete in a weekend or one sitting. It has wonderful art direction that reminds me a lot of things like Machanarium and other Amanita Design games. Some of the puzzles can be surprisingly hard! I enjoy that many of the hardest puzzles are single-screen which cuts down on wasted time going between areas. Although it does a have a few multi-screen puzzles. Overall worth a play through for sure.My only gripes are that the character change mechanic is more tedious than it is fun. Having to watch a "no" animation when you forget to switch is annoying. It should just switch automatically and do the thing. I also feel like too many sections were pixel hunts just trying to find what you could interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a click-and-move puzzle game. The objective is to solve puzzles to get to the end of the story.Gameplay-wise, mouse. Click on the girl to swap to Cubus and vice versa. Puzzles are simple to solve logically but some may stump you.Conclusion, do try TOHU. The art is imaginative and creative. The storyline is a little tricky but I won't spoil it for you. The ending is a little tropish but it's enjoyable.1. The ArtMostly for the creative world-building.1. 4 hours longReally short if you just look at the guide.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorably crafted animations and sound design. Makes me believe the devs really cared. Interesting and cute story. Puzzles are not too easy and not too challenging and if you find them too challenging there is a nifty little hint system that makes you solve a timing minigame before you get the solutions. Really really well done. Buy recommendation at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute game about a little girl saving the world with the help of her robot friend.  The art is very pretty, the voices and sounds are well fun done and the music is nice. The puzzles are fun but on the easy side and nothing we haven't seen before. I did get stuck a couple of times in the world itself, but the hint system saved me every time. It's great that the hints require some effort to open so you don't rely on them too much.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: As point and click games go, Tohu is charming but ultimately extremely short and simple with the main difficulty stemming from obtuse mechanics and fiddly controls rather than interesting or inventive puzzles. Inoffensive but so crushingly bland and without unique texture that it cannot be recommended to anyone who isn't desperate for a way to kill a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Tohu is a Beautifully made puzzle game that will test your Smarts, Wits, Puzzle solving skills and reflexes. The Game Looks Beautiful will lots of colors, characters that looks lively and very unique characters designs. The music is pretty catchy too. The Puzzles are pretty tough but not unfair at times, they are puzzles that you need to think about plus there is different types of puzzles to keep you on your toes. The hint system is pretty annoying to use however, In order to get a hint you have to hit on the red marks while the Arrow is swinging back and forward and if you miss you have to start all over, Although the hints do help you if you stuck at any point and there's no penalty for using one. I ended up using two hints, The first one helped me and the second only made me realized I could have done that from the start. Overall If you are looking for a brilliantly made puzzle game with cute and unique characters with catchy music this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: It was a really fun game! I really enjoyed playing through it and completing it 100% in one stream! The story is great and so is the plot twist. Some of the levels were a bit confusing to me, so I had to use the hint, but even the hint mechanic was interesting, that being said, I wish people luck who have slow reaction time.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Really adorbale point & click adventure.Beautiful art, pleasent soundtrack and most of the puzzles are at a nice level of difficulty. There was maybe 2 puzzles i couldn't quite wrap my head around, but that's more likely just me being too smoothbrained.If you've got a few hours to kill and like point & click games, check this out
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another solid Point and Click AdventureI played the demo for TOHU a while ago and loved it. I appreciated the overall bounciness of the animation and some of the puzzles featured intrigued me. So a couple months later I picked the game up and I got exactly what I thought I would get from playing the demo.More of that cute and bouncy animation, better and more challenging puzzles, and great music.The Point and Click aspect is just what you would expect from the genre: Find and pick up items to use them later in a scripted sequence, but what separates TOHU from other games in its genre is the setting that the game takes place in. The environment is full of surreal creatures and structures that are both weird, interesting, and very appealing to look at. I could take a screenshot of any area in this game and hang it on my wall. The character designs are just as surreal as the environments, and you can guess the personality of a character from their design alone.Although the characters themselves and story leave something to be desired, it's very obvious that those 2 things weren't the focus.I vigorously enjoyed my time with TOHU, although that time was short.TLDR: If you like bouncy animation, surreal art, and using your brain, TOHU will be a fine addition to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: I found it to be a very charming and fun game, however slightly tedious at times with all the little animations making everything move along very slowly. The art is beautiful, the character designs are cute and the music is very nice. Personally the voice acting and little repetetive sounds here and there got a bit annnoying to listen to, but not so much that it`s a problem. It`s definitely worth playing if you enjoy some small puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: TOHU is a wonderful game. I enjoyed the playful artwork and animations, the cool soundtrack and sound effects, and the interesting, not very difficult puzzles. I fell in love with the diverse mechanimals and the fish-worlds. I highly recommend TOHU to players who love point-and-click puzzle adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this whimsical game.  The puzzles are more akin to machnimarium than a traditional point and click.  The animation is so beautiful and adorable.  I mean if you can't find joy in light bulb bugs and screwdriver bugs..and accordion bugs I can't help you.  I love how everything is clickable and makes noise and does different things.  The puzzles aren't overly difficult but they aren't super easy either.  I was thoroughly charmed by this game.  I would love to have another trip to this whimsical word.  The music is quite lovely as well.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so abstract it's hard to know what's going on a lot of the time. It also has the problem that sometimes you know exactly what you're supposed to do, and you're correct, but the hit boxes to do the action are finicky. That being said, the game has a lot of visual charm, the hint system is nice, and it's a fun adventure. Recommended!PS: The game also finished when I thought it was halfway over - I thought we were going to play the character from the ending as a whole other segment (and the sociopath in me was totally ready for that!); but instead, roll credits!
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: if you love Amanita Design's games (especially Machinarium) and have played all of them, then you should be installing TOHU at this very moment. If not, then I suggest completing the "back catalogue" first.. It's world is mesmerizing, filled with funny little details, as well as wonderfully odd and meticulously animated creatures. Also puzzles are diverse and interesting.However, it quickly becomes clear that the game . Many of main character's animations are too slow (and uncancellable), while puzzles sometimes are frustrating and usually don't have any logical explanation. It's essentially a random collection of challenges, tied together with a very simple, childish story.Anyway, TOHU still stands out of the crowd of point-and-click games thanks to it's . I recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle game with cute graphics and a nice soundtrack. A couple of the puzzles were fairly obscure, primarily due to there being actions you can take where it doesn't seem like you can. And there's one very cliche puzzle that should be banned from games for the next decade (at least it wasn't Towers of Hammurabi). But overall a solid, short, game.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Cute point and click adventure! I wish the Studio behind it good luck for their future games! :DJust have some minor gripe I have with the game is that the audio in the final cutscene sounds a bit scuffed and in one scene a sound effect just plays constantly and overlaps with the beautiful soundtrack.Otherwise there where some scenes that put a genuine smile on my face :)
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, perfect for those who enjoyed other modern point&click adventures like Machinarium, Botanicula or Broken Age. The game takes about 5 hours to complete and is full of a wide range of puzzle types. The in-game hint system is also very cleverly done, with each hint set locked behind a mini-game. Dan Gartman's whimsical art shines in the setting and the story has a sweet charm and wholesome ending.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles 9/10Story 5/10Designs 10/10Total score 8/10TOHU is a pretty cute point and click game with amazing designs, the design style reminded me of Machinarium. The puzzles are challenging and fun. The story feels a bit like it's written to connect the puzzles and doesn't always make sense, but that doesn't matter you shouldn't play the game. Play it for the puzzles, the soundtrack and de designs! It's also a lot of fun to play around with both The Girls's perspective as Cubus'. I love the way Cubus gets up and down on stairs.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game! Once I started, that was it - I had to play it until I finished it that same day. The game is extremely user friendly, with a simple point and click action you can get through the whole game. The mini games throughout are awesome, as they make you think logically, but they don't become frustrating because they can be solved within 5 mins on average, which is enough time to enjoy it properly. The story is good, and the artwork is SUPER CREATIVE - I loved looking at it. Overall super happy with it and can't wait to see what The Irregular Corporation release next!
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Short review:A cute little point and click adventure game with pretty art and a lovely soundtrack by Christopher Larkin (of Hollow Knight fame). This game invites you to explore it's creative environments and characters with childlike wonder. When it comes to gameplay though, don't expect too much more than your average point and click game, it mostly shines as a nice piece of eye candy and ear candy.Long review:As said before the art and music really shine in this game. The settings are creative and it is clear there is attention to detail in every single screen. The characters are equally creative and show character through their animations. I particularly like seeing Cubus smugly strut around. When it comes to the music it is clear Christopher Larkin gave it his all despite this being a smaller game and the music really inspires you to explore these strange worlds.So in short, all the aesthetic aspects in this game are great, the art, the music, the atmosphere, the characters. But when it comes down to the gameplay I must say I am not quite as impressed, and I'll into all my nitpicks here:The puzzles are fine but nothing really interesting or creative, with some of them having some fairly unintuitive solutions. Nothing really egregious, but you would think developers would know to avoid that by now, as it's such a trope of the genre.One thing I noticed is that moving around is just a bit too slow. I get that it helps with taking in the atmosphere, but sometimes you are trying to backtrack and it's just kinda tedious.The final gameplay point is that some of the hitboxes are not great, in some cases two hitboxes will overlap and it'll be hard to click on one of them. In one case it made a time based puzzle harder than it should have been (the samurai) and in another I thought something wasn't possible when it was, I had just clicked wrong (climbing with the icicles).I will continue my nitpicking with the sound. Sometimes certain objects or characters make really repetitive sounds, which can be quite annoying if you are trying to concentrate. It is also louder than the music, which you can change nothing about, there is just one slider for the master volume. So often I had a hard time enjoying Larkin's amazing soundtrack.And to close out my complaining I want to say that the plot wasn't really that interesting. The different worlds are all really disconnected and it doesn't feel like anything you do has any arc to it, you're just doing menial tasks for these characters you've never seen before. The ending was kinda interesting, but I didn't really feel a sense of accomplishment by the end of it.Okay I swear that is all my complaints. I'll admit that these are all fairly minor nitpicks, but they definitely add up, and together they made this game more of a 'good' experience for me, rather than a 'great' experience. I will say this though: This studio is just starting out and I see great potential, so I encourage them to keep it up and I'm sure we'll get more great games from them in the future.So in conclusion, should you get this game?If you like exploring and you like the art definitely go for it, if you want good puzzles and fun mechanics maybe skip this one (and just listen to the soundtrack). Either way the price is not a problem, there's definitely your money's worth in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

_childDocuments_.review: Experience a brand new adventure game set amongst a world of weird and wonderful fish planets. Explore beautiful environments, solve intricate puzzles and discover the truth about a mysterious little girl and her mechanical alter-ego, Cubus.
_childDocuments_.name: TOHU

name: Bite the Bullet
detailed_description: Development Roadmap About the Game Bite The Bullet is the world’s first Run & Gun & Eat. In this roguelite RPG shooter you must eat enemies, bullets and more to powerup your character, weapons, and abilities. Gun down zombies, robots and giant mutant bosses with a barrage of bullets before chowing down on their corpses to craft new weapons, unlock new abilities and special attacks, and transform into a powerful Zombro form to smash foes. Explore four character classes and a skill tree based on your diet – and remember, you are what you eat! How you play is driven by how you choose to eat. The carnivorous Gorivore or vegan Slaughterer of the Soil that have their own unique abilities and perks, changing how you defeat enemies and navigate levels. Customize your character with every choice and every bite. Maximize your build for your playstyle, run the world again with a different diet for a new challenge, and team up with a friend in co-op to ramp up the bullets and the calories. Devour enemies to powerup your character, weapons, and abilities! Chow down on everything - enemies, walls, even bullets! Play solo or with a friend in local co-op. Four character classes (Carnivore, Herbivore, Omnivore, and Robovore - which means you eat metal) that have their own unique abilities and perks. Gorge yourself on 50 Levels. Customize your character with a deep, branching skill tree. Loot powerful weapons with fun modifiers, like Spicy Critter Cannons and Organic Meat-Seeking Missiles! Craft exotic new weapons by wolfing down special types of characters and enemies! Eat enemies so you can burn calories to energize your skills and special attacks! Use a highly advanced shield to protect yourself from oncoming fire or knock enemies away! Earn action hero bandanas by fully completing each world! about_the_game: Bite The Bullet is the world’s first Run & Gun & Eat. In this roguelite RPG shooter you must eat enemies, bullets and more to powerup your character, weapons, and abilities. Gun down zombies, robots and giant mutant bosses with a barrage of bullets before chowing down on their corpses to craft new weapons, unlock new abilities and special attacks, and transform into a powerful Zombro form to smash foes. Explore four character classes and a skill tree based on your diet – and remember, you are what you eat! How you play is driven by how you choose to eat. The carnivorous Gorivore or vegan Slaughterer of the Soil that have their own unique abilities and perks, changing how you defeat enemies and navigate levels. Customize your character with every choice and every bite. Maximize your build for your playstyle, run the world again with a different diet for a new challenge, and team up with a friend in co-op to ramp up the bullets and the calories. Devour enemies to powerup your character, weapons, and abilities! Chow down on everything - enemies, walls, even bullets! Play solo or with a friend in local co-op. Four character classes (Carnivore, Herbivore, Omnivore, and Robovore - which means you eat metal) that have their own unique abilities and perks. Gorge yourself on 50 Levels. Customize your character with a deep, branching skill tree. Loot powerful weapons with fun modifiers, like Spicy Critter Cannons and Organic Meat-Seeking Missiles! Craft exotic new weapons by wolfing down special types of characters and enemies! Eat enemies so you can burn calories to energize your skills and special attacks! Use a highly advanced shield to protect yourself from oncoming fire or knock enemies away! Earn action hero bandanas by fully completing each world! Chew carefully - every enemy has its own nutritional information, and your body type will change based on the types of enemies you consume! Transform into your powerful Zombro form and smash enemies into bite-sized bits! Gobble up an exciting plot with a ton of sidequests! Join our Discord for discussion, news, and updates!
short_description: Run, Gun and Eat your way through this roguelite RPG shooter. In a world where every enemy is edible, what you eat and how much you eat drives everything from your waistline to branching skill trees to weapon crafting. Shoot fast. Eat big. Satisfy your appetite for destruction.

_childDocuments_.review: is an RPG shooter that peaked my interest with it sharing a similar visual style with . However, what I played was an absolute mess with so many issues and faults with the gameplay that it made the majority of my experience wishing that the game would finish sooner.• Gives off Metal Slug feel with its visuals• Some amazing looking levels• One thing I can vouch for is the games soundtrack• Areas feels overly repetitive since each mission has 3 to 5 levels to complete the mission• Some pathways lead to dead ends leaving you to aimlessly look for the right way to go• Can get lost in the labyrinth-like levels which have dead ends and no real guide to show you where to go• Weapons are as generic and bland as you can get• Environmental hazards can sometimes be placed in such a way that it stun locks you• Skill tree is overwhelmingly big• Bosses never had that much depth to them and didn’t feel satisfying to battle• Controls feel very stiff in your normal form and too floaty in your bulky form• Whilst in animations you can still take damage• The nutrients you gain to upgrade weapons you lose a certain amount of them every time you jump, despite this game being a platformer...• Everything stopped moving and stayed in their idle animation, had to force close the game• Music skips when proceeding with dialogueUnlike  the missions on  are mediocre at best with very little differences between them. Level design is a major disappointment with parts of levels clearly being copied and pasted over and over again. The levels themselves are either too big to navigate so you’ll just run through the level effortlessly or are too labyrinth-like where you'll get lost. The level design is so bad that sometimes you might get lost as to where to go and your only indication is the checkpoints that you find.If the level design in missions weren’t bland enough, the game decides to have 3 to 5 levels per mission just to stretch the game out. These levels don’t serve much purpose besides allowing you to upgrade your character, which the upgrade tree is overwhelmingly massive to be able to plan ahead as to which path you’ll focus on. The only difference between these levels within the same mission is that  you might find yourself in a different location. The new enemies will be shown off within the first level and rarely does a new mechanic get introduced to make the game interesting.Your objective in each level is to get from point A to point B whilst shooting a bunch of zombies and robots that ‘stand in your way.’ But they don’t really get in your way at all as you can just run past them, it feels like they’re there just to distract you from running through the entire level ignoring all the enemies. The game tries to ‘increase’ the difficulty by cramming in more enemies on the screen which does take a toll on your health if you play effortlessly but still isn’t challenging enough to make you have to think about what you’re doing.Bosses are just as bland and boring as the rest of the game, they lack any sort of depth in their attack patterns to make it satisfying to defeat. Even though the designs of these bosses look amazingly detailed, it seems that they completely disregarded all of the attack patterns. The biggest insult to injury is the final boss, it’s extremely difficult compared to the rest of the game because it just transforms into all the bosses you’ve previously fought up to this point expecting you to defeat them with the three lives given to you. Even one of these enemies can stun-lock you because of the way the platforms are designed, and if you die using all your ammo, you’ll have to go and grind for more as the game doesn’t give it back to you.Despite how cool some of the weapons might look, the majority of them are underwhelming and generic. You have your standard rifle, shotgun, flamethrower, all the weapons you’d have in every shooter game. The game really lacks any sort of creative weapons that would be interesting to use.The main mechanic that this game has to offer is being able to eat enemies and food, which restores your health, gain certain nutrients (protein and fat) and also fill up a bar that transforms you into a bulky blue version of yourself. Since health drops are uncommon to find, you’ll rely on eating enemies and food to restore your health. However, the mechanic is very short-lived as quickly showed more problems and issues that the game had.First off, every time you eat something you get stuck in a short animation that not only interrupts the flow of the game by having to wait a few seconds every time you eat, but you can also take damage from enemies whilst in this animation. So the health that you gain from eating enemies can be negated by an enemy shooting you whilst you’re eating.The nutrients that you gain from eating is used to upgrade your weapons, you can find food products that will give you a massive boost in fat or protein. It’s a nice detail when you have way too much fat your character feels a lot heavier, walks slower and looks fat, whilst if you have a lot of protein your character has more muscles. However, this mechanic is flawed since it takes thousands of both protein and fat to just upgrade one weapon and since eating enemies doesn’t give you much you won’t upgrade your weapons very quickly. But, what’s even worse is that every time you jump or take a hit you lose a certain amount of fat and protein. This not only discourages players to look for secret areas but forces them to not jump that much despite this game being a platformer as well. The only way I could upgrade my weapons was when I found a secret area with a bunch of boosts and then would have to immediately upgrade my weapons before I lost all of it from jumping too much in a platforming game...When you whilst your character eats, however you can still take damage from enemies around that pretty much negates that health you just replenished from eating. It’s the same with every animation in this game, a certain enemy can grab you and hold you for a few seconds whilst dealing damage, on top of that other enemies can also shoot you if they are close enough. It’s frustrating and annoying, make the animations shorter (at least for eating) or make me invulnerable for a short amount of time.The soundtrack is probably the only part of the game that I enjoyed the most, it’s heavy metal and would’ve suited the game perfectly if it was more fast-paced. But even then, it definitely added some tension to the game even though half the time it was way too easy.The art style of  is the best thing this game has going for it, the pixel art is surprisingly high quality, the especially the bosses have a lot of attention to detail in them. Unfortunately, because there are so many levels in one mission you’ll probably get bored seeing the same environments over and over again and will want a change of scenery by the time you complete the mission has no substance to it besides mindlessly running through the level and shooting enemies that you come across. There’s no depth to its mechanics and it feels like the game was stretched out purposely, which still only amount to around 8 to 10 hours playtime. It might look appealing with its  like visuals, but the gameplay is extremely boring, repetitive and just not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Its unbelievable how you can ruin a really interesting and nice looking game.Seriously, I don't understand why it gets positive reviews at all.I was really looking forward in playing Bite the bullet. But then...Ok, I will not torture you with the full story of the adventure to get the game "running".So here in "short":Almost everything is on you to find out. As good as nothing is explained at the beginning. Even the briefing is poorly explained. The so called "tutorial" shows you how to jump, shoot and eat. Sounds easy. ...as long till you find out that the game uses every single button of a full grown XBox controler. And you will need it even.The layout is crap. Even the alternative layout. If you play by keyboard and mouse you are able to aim correctly at least. But even the kb-layout is cruel. And you can't remap anything. (I still don't know, which key is used for the map, since I dont have such a sign on my kb, nor ever seen it.) ...or switch off the vibration of the controller.Then the game itself. Nothing of your HUD is explained either. The first bar is your health, the second... I am not sure: the zombometre? And I still do not even know why I should transform into a mutant at all. Have fun finding out yourself what all the other counters are for. Plus it looks like you can only read the calories in the mainmenu (ESC key). I am not even sure what you need for what, what causes you to loose something or from which point you start getting too fat (but the goal IS to eat as much as you can - or not; you dont get a hint whats good and what not).At least somewhen during the game you will get some oversized Infoboxes streight overlayed over your running game where you learn that you can doublejump and other "unimportant" stuff. The missions are divided into different levels. Think  somewhere I read 3 each. If you have to exit the game during a mission, your char-progress will be saved. But not your level progress. So if Mom, waifu or the pizza-guy calls for dinner and you exit, have fun starting from the total beginning of the mission. "Exiting" is another good point. You can't exit the game from the main screen. You have to do it from the main menu. But the main menu is only accessable during a game. Ha ha. And may I add the german translation in general is ok, but there are whole dialogues where you cant even guess anymore what they mean.Originally I wanted to finish the first mission at least to give the game a fair chance to convince me. Sadly there was a bug which took my last hope away: suddenly I could not use the eat/interaction key anymore. Sorry, but game breaking bugs are my personal reason no. 1 to really hate a game. Paying users deserve a fully working, easy to handly and understandable game. Or at least a manual. Like on consoles in the good old retro days. Especially Mega Cat studios should know this.Its really rare that I find such bitter final words for a review. Especially for a game that looks so interesting and fun like Bite the Bullet and where the devs have such a good intention. But: ...sorry. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, a rather dull game that doesn't bring the white-knuckle action as advertised. On the surface, the "eating/looting" system is a neat gameplay element but bogs down the game instead of focusing on action like a Metal Slug or Contra game that it aspires to be like. This game lacks that purpose and simply tasks you with eating stuff......just to eat them and get new stuff. Disappointing to say the least. The game had great potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, some good and bad here. The game is not perfect, there's plenty of rough edges - but if you can overlook them, there's an enjoyable game to be had here.You are basically eating everything, this is a weird game where you are what you eat, somehwat literally.stun a mob, and then devour them to refill HP, add to your GUT meter, and stats of carbs, fats and proteins.depending on how you eat, your character might get nimble and fast, but weak and needing a TON of food to maintain, eat fatty stuff ( liek a jar of mayo ) and you become a super fatty - slow, but heavy defense. They also mix it up a bit by making some enemies " liek mold ' and you vomit instantly, which allows you to upgrade your weps using resources ( don't ask me how this works, it just does ) I get the feeling there's a bit of a a fetish goin on here, namely eating - but it's not sexual in nature, so it's fine.Basic gameplay is contra styled with you being able to shoot in any direction ( by aiming with your L stick, which works pretty badly, tbh ) you get an air dash which can damage and stun enemies ( goes in any direciton you want ) and various weps throughout levels.you find challenge rooms, little teleporters that might bring you to a shop, a collecitble, a specific challenge ( reach the end goal, eat only ONE of every enemy type in room, etc ) there's a few of these.you progress through the level, at the end you vomit up your GUT and can then spend your accrued points on a massive skill tree. ( it's VERY hard to navigate this thing, slightly touching the control stick makes it FLY any direction. ) each level is set up in a few parts ( which seemed to just drag on and on, train, go underground, go up, train, go back underground, train, go back underground, then train and finally the boss.there's some technical hiccups, some frame drops here and there, the audio fell out completely a few times, some clipping issues here and there - Liek i said before, the game isn't perfect. but what you get is not bad at all, it's very similar to Dungeon munchies ( especially in the regard that you have to aim your attacks with the same stick you control your character with, and there's no lock in place button, either ) I'd say for the price, you're getting a decent game. And the devs have already posted an update, which very well might address the issues I had in my playtime.50/50 on a recommend - you'll know if it's the game for you though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you think you are gonna just grab a controller and shoot bad guys point A to point B. You are mistaken. _childDocuments_.review: This game has the undesirably quality of both over, and under-explaining things.It was a near constant-tutorial, while also feeling like I never knew what was happening.The idea of your body changing is neat! But there is SO much else going on, that it was the furthest thing from my mind. I had to stop and read a tooltip, or item description, or a food's nutritional breakdown, or new weapon abilities, every 2 seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Bite the Bullet is a cool game with captivating pixel art and interesting mechanics. It can get pretty tedious to progress your character but it's one of the concepts that add up to the game's comedic and niche approach. It can sometimes be punishing if you're not exactly familiar with the controls of the game. I highly recommend it if you are into games like Megaman ZX, Metal Slug and modern platformers. It requires you to respond fast because there's a lot of things happening and the game does not run out of dull moments. I like how it supports ultrawide screens which makes the game more crisp in detail. It's a fair game for the avid platformer gamers, and the background music suits the mood of the game. It offers a wide customization of playstyle because of the skill tree, it can be a bit overwhelming because of the UI animations. The power ups have unique effects to them which somehow gives you an edge every level. My overall experience for the game is good so far, it's nowhere near perfect but the game definitely has a unique directive to it that you won't see in any other games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game _is_ a solid run & gun with good graphics and some interesting mechanics based around eating all enemies.The three counters -calories, protein and fat- are basically three currencies that you use to upgrade your weapons - or that's what I managed to find out so far (I finished first two missions). Thing is - all three decrease as you do stuff in the game. Dash costs few tens of protein, jumps and double jumps cost about 40 fat, and everything costs calories.Now consider that in order to do some weapon upgrades, you pay 1000 (!) fats, few hundred of proteins, and most of enemies give you only between 8-20 fats.There are mayo buckets and protein buckets that immediately upgrade you 'one tier' (ie. 1000x), but - there are also some pickups that simply just _nullify_ these stats! And some are put in really awkward positions so that its hard to avoid them._MAYBE_ some of them give you something in return, but this leads me to the next problem - I am not really sure what any of that even means. Game mechanics aren't communicated very well.There's a note that teaches you to "double jump" - but I've been successfully multi-jumping by simply mashing the space button, then dashing occasionally - you can basically fly this way.There's a tutorial, but I am 99% convinced its made up to be a joke. Shotgun tutorial - you spawn in a level, with one monster in front of you. Text says - Shotgun has low range, but a lot of damage. Kill the monster with the shotgun. You kill the monster, tutorial complete. Say what :-D?Missions are very, very long, with multiple levels each, and teleporters to previous parts or hidden levels. Notice I played 3.8h at time of this review, and have only finished the second mission - out of 10 or 12, not sure.Map is confusing to read and honestly I still have no idea what various colors on it mean - they don't seem to match anything in the game world. I find myself often going towards what I think is progressing, but I end up backtracking - or going through similar area enough that I'm not sure whether enemies respawned, or this is just a new area that looks like an old one.Controls aren't the top notch - true, but unless you play these games all the time, you'll barely notice it. Not that it matters at all, game isn't really a platformer, AND to begin with you have multi-jump and dash, so...To sum it all up - the game has a LOT of content, but it _seems_ unfinished. There's a ton of good ideas, but they _seem_ half implemented, as if someone had really grand plans, and then was just like "Ah ♥♥♥♥ it, this is good enough."If you can look past this and _just_ focus on running and gunning - its feels very good, it looks gorgeous, and the soundtrack is great.I got it on special for 9$, and I have a many way worse games I paid that amount of money.So, if you like run&gun, and you've already played other better titles, this one _probably_ won't disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: It misses some of the finer points of game and level design. One thing I noticed while playing is it's really difficult to know what is going on on screen and it makes decisions and mechanics available to you feel really unimpactful on play. _childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game, albeit I encountered a few control issues that should be easily fixable once you actually get to know the scheme. It has a certain charm to it that you can't find in other games, it easily brings you the nostalgia when you were playing Metal Slug or Broforce back then, but mix that up with modern VFX and fun mechanics additionally. - The game offers a friendly world environment for the players, definitely gets the player accustomed to the dystopian-esque vibe of the game. The pixel art aesthetic of the game is really good and I never fail to look at the details. - I like how the player has good mobility on top of its side-scrolling shooting mechanic, the dash and wall slide is absolutely my favorite thing to do, allowing me to experiment with my moves and get into tight places. - The game does not punish the player for exploring, because there are always secret levels and easter eggs to be found throughout the game. It does not force you to go from point A -> point B and isn't quite linear especially when you progress level by level - The controls could use some work, it was confusing at first but once you actually get the hang of it you wouldn't have any issues - The pacing of the game starts slow at first, but eventually picks itself up during skirmishes and the effects/animations just makes it better and better as you progress - The UI art is great, it's not too distracting and not too overbearing. It could use some tooltips in the long run but other than that I like its simplicity and its aesthetic - Boss fights are unique per level, and you actually need to practice the patterns per end of the level. It's possible to just stand and shoot but it's not always 100% the case because you always need to be moving around otherwise you'd end up dead - The SFX and music is just awesome, you get the option to play the game with metal/rock genre or synthwave genre and it's great because the choice is accessible anywhere It's worth a look for platformer fans because of the mechanics it offers and the unique vibe that it gives off when playing. I'm slowly progressing through the game and I'm hoping to see more of what the game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Bite the Bullet is a somewhat broken console ported 2D retro pixel side scrolling shooter.  There's a few gimmicks like a mechanic that allows you to "eat" your enemies to recover health, but this doesn't make the game remotely better or more interesting than any other shovelware 2D retro pixel game.  The game is broken for many users under recent builds of Windows 10 and 11, launching past the first splashscreen into an endless black screen... you can terminate this by switching desktops (win + -> keys) and then launching task manager to kill the stalled process.   Surely the pinnacle of game development... not testing their game or making sure it runs on Windows. If you can get it to work, from a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.Because this is a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Bite the Bullet has the utterly unrealistic price of $15 USD (for pixelcrap! They can't even do graphics properly but they want $15!), for which you could easily get any number of older, working AAA games, let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Bite the Bullet

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the mixed reviews I decided to pick this up as it was really cheap in a bundle. Wish i hadn't bothered. Like almost every other user says, this game has a lot of potential: an original and intriguing premise, decent pixel art and music, and an interesting sounding upgrade path. But this is all for nought if it doesn't control well and it doesn't. There are only two controller configurations to choose from/grapple with and they are not very intuitive. Your character's movement just feels off and kind of janky. And there's something about the sound design or the animations that make it so you don't really know if you've hit or are hitting an enemy so it's just not very satisfying. Oh, and the wall jumping feels odd too and i found myself getting accidentally stuck to the sides or just slipping about. So in the end even the short time i spent with it just felt really frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Multiple times I mentioned the controls should feel responsive and easy to handle. If a player already has fun by just controlling a character, the Devs have done a solid start creating their game. "Bite The Bullet" isn't one of these games.I always thought the movements of the characters in this game would be similar to the ones in the Metal Slug series: fast, responsive, flexible, fun! Well, the controls feel the exact opposite.I will admit right now I didn't play a lot because of this issue…and some other ones. One another major problem I had was the amount of info you needed to take into account to play the game. A tutorial level exists but it doesn't help at all.I had this game on my bucket list for a while and I was ignoring the 'Mix' score it has on Steam. Well, I am at fault for this.2/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, get's a little boring after a little while, so unless you're SUPER SUPER into these kinds of games, I would suggest playing for a few hours and then taking a break. The talent system is a little janky, and it doesn't really go into details on the controls so you might start off confused on how to do specific abilities. But all in all, it was an okay game.

_childDocuments_.review: It has flaws, but It was enjoyable to zone out to. The writing isn't spectacular, but it is at least creative.As you play the game and level up, you get points you can spend in skill trees that can slightly change the way the game plays.However, at the game's core, it is still a 2D Side Scroller Shoot 'em Up like Contra and Metal Slug, and so the game will primarily involve you shooting everything with an added mechanic of eating your enemies, or their ammo if you upgrade your skill tree to basically let you eat literally everything.I am not far into the game, but my time spent with it so far has been enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:Great Ideas, "Pro Controls" recommended. The game is a great twin stick shooter with some unique mechanics and leveling system, changing your player to either a meat eater or a plant eater or some sort of combination. Twitch integration works extremely well and adds a lot to the game. Presentation is nice, lighting effects can be toned down however for more clarity.CONS:In many points in the game, it seems like some ideas overstay their welcome. Level environments feel same-y and you should expect to play the same level for 45 minutes to an hour so the game can seem very repetitive. Not very diverse mobs or environments in the first couple levels. Overall: The mechanics of the game are solid and legitimately fun to play, however the game can get boring rather quickly due to the length of time youll be spending on a level and how little the level changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Bite the Bullet

_childDocuments_.review: I got the chance to play this for the community yesterday and wanted to provide my feedback on it. This game has absolutely amazing pixel art. It's absolutely stunning. The challenge is that the art quickly blends into the background and becomes a bit of a muddied mess. It's hard to decipher end points for platforms and enemies. There's a lot of lens flares, artifacts, and similar colour palettes that make the game a bit muddy to look at.Overall, I give this a 6.5/10At first, this game is described as a roguelite, but doesn't really have enough roguelite elements to fall into that category. Randomly generated stats and items doesn't justify the flag. There is no permadeath in the starting modes, so it's more of an RPG Platformer.Getting past that, we get into controls; The shooting is 8-directional, but enemies have a lot of free move, which can lead them to sticking into corners or spaces that you have almost no access to shoot. As well, there aren't substantial iFrames (which is fair to create some difficulty) but this leads into getting trapped easily by bosses.Stages are somewhat repetitive with similar music throughout them. Lots of dead-ends and a feeling of old NES style platformers where the goal was to make you spend time in the game when there wasn't lots of content to deal with. The Fat/Protein system seems interesting at first (a set of stats that change as you play through the stage, reminiscent of Gauntlet) but has almost zero information in the game to teach you on the use and management of these. In almost 2 hours, the stats were used for modifying weapons and that was it. The talent system is extremely vague and overly complex; Tons of talents that are meant to waste points and not give much overall value. Huge talent trees like this don't give a proper feeling of success and growth when completing tiers, but rather give miniscule increases that don't seem to appear. The platforms themselves are not spectacularly well defined, so walking off of them into pits is super easy. This goes back to the graphics section up above and doesn't allow for a good platformer experience.Overall, I have to give the gameplay a 3/10When I went to play this game, I was truly excited to play. It had a lot of the features I enjoy (I've played Gungeon and other roguelikes that I absolutely enjoy) and just failed overall to deliver. I'd love to see some adjustment to some of these features and make the game a much faster experience, not having too much information and not enough time to parse. There's a lot of management of numbers that get lost in the experience; KISS principle would do well to refine this game.

So far the gameplay is smooth; with no bugs or technical issues found within my hours of gameplay. Kudos to development team that spent hours of effort in making this wonderful game! _childDocuments_.review: Overall Bite the Bullet is an enjoyable and well made game. When I first played it, it reminded me of Contra, which is why I would definitely recommend this game to other people. It may not be entirely the same but there is no doubt that you would get addicted to Bite the Bullet. The game design was very well made, it gives off a retro vibe and at the same a modern one. The gameplay is also very nice, unique in most ways. There are also a lot of upgrades and such that makes the game much more interesting. Like how some upgrades on your gun depends on the things that you eat. Another thing I love about this is the amount of action there is, there are no dull moments unlike other roleplay games. The game is still kind of new but I can already see so much potential for this game.

name: Roguebook
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game The ancients speak of a Book written since time immemorial containing all the world's legends. After many fabulous adventures, recounted in Faeria – Chronicles of Gagana , this relic was lost in a well of Faeria. Through contact with this source of magic, the Book developed a wicked free will of its own and became the Roguebook! You are trapped in the Book of Lore of Faeria , and each page represents a new challenge. Lead your two heroes to victory in this roguelike deckbuilder developed in partnership with Richard Garfield, creator of Magic: The Gathering ™. Put together the best synergies between cards, relics and abilities, and take on the Roguebook. LEGENDARY HEROES 6 hero pairs – Choose 2 heroes to start a game. Each hero has a collection of over 50 cards, a personal relic and a unique skill tree. Maximise synergies – The hero at the front protects the hero at the back. Switch the positions of your heroes and combine their strengths to unleash powerful combos. Strategic battles – Skilfully anticipate and queue up your actions to defeat over 40 bosses and enemies. BUILD YOUR DECK AS YOU PLAY Dynamic deckbuilding – Over 200 cards to cleverly assemble as the game progresses. You will never play with the same deck twice. Relics with unique powers – Upgrade your cards with 30 special gems. Collect 80 relics with extraordinary effects. More cards, more power! – Each hero has a unique skill tree to unlock. Collect cards and select the best skills! EXPLORE A WORLD THAT CHANGES WITH EACH NEW BRUSHSTROKE The Book changes each time you open it – The map along with its mysteries and dangers are procedurally generated for a brand-new challenge every time. Paint the world – The Roguebook's pages are composed of hexagonal tiles. Use magic inks that reveal different patterns to fully explore each page. A range of encounters – Merchants, travellers, ruins, quests, etc. Lots of chances to obtain cards and relics… or to fall into a trap! EACH RUN COUNTS IN THE QUEST TO DEFEAT THE ROGUEBOOK Hours and hours of fun – 20 hours on average to beat the game, hundreds of hours to unlock everything. Progress at your own pace – Collect pages and use them to buy upgrades. Level up your heroes to unlock new cards. 20 difficulty levels – Defeat the final boss to unlock the Epilogue level. Each level grants access to new relics, gems and encounters, but also spawns tougher enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: The card battling is good, however most classes have little flexibility in their playstyles. The cards themselves are mostly generic, not a single one made me interested in using it in battle. This is more of a problem when viewed in combination with the  biggest flaw of the game, the traveling system. I hate this "painting" to explore the map, it's tedious and there are no payoffs to motivate the player. Overall, I just wished I played a different deck roguelike game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roguebook

_childDocuments_.review: There's way too much variance in the game.  Don't get unless you're already tired of STS and monster train.Unlike STS or Monster Train which I have a decent amount of hours in, a run of Roguebook lives or dies on whether you get allies and sometimes you find none. If you get relevant talents, relics, sustain, and energy gen your run will go fine, otherwise it's dead before it even starts. Everything is expensive in the shops, you don't get to buy too much. The amount of "55%" decisions you have is very small where you don't really improve your win rate, and your run is already doomed as soon as you click the gate on the lowest difficulty. All the good players will explore the same spots given an identical map gen. It's like playing magic and getting mana screwed/flooded a third of the time. Compare that to STS where a well played watcher has an 80% winrate on ascension 20 and a 99% winrate on A0.  In addition they decided to balance a solo roguelike card game by making things too weak. One of the cool things about STS or Monster Train is you do get runs that just pop off. In roguebook you get runs that suck ass or are just ok. In STS you can scale up to 10 orb slots on defect dealing upwards of 10 damage each to every enemy. In roguecraft you're happy to get 20 damage a turn from allies, maybe you get the ally that doubles its spirit every turn and ways to buff its spirit but it's unlikely. They tried to balance the classes but the balance between classes isn't even good. The rat and pig are way better than the girl with the sword at least early on. As you unlock more stuff maybe the game gets easier for her. You can't even get extra energy on the first turn before unlocking it. Why is that an unlockable? Did they even test their game?  Some of the mobs are way stronger than a normal enemy should be, stronger than elites or bosses. This was a problem in STS and monster train too. Even hearthstone solo adventures had Haro Ending Run. But it's frustrating right now.  Often the amount of life you lose is not worth the paint brushes on normal or elite enemies  There are very few ways to remove cards from your deck  Don't get the swap on the right turn? lose a ton of life  I'm not sure how much more I'll play. If I find my views change I'll edit the review.
_childDocuments_.name: Roguebook

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I should have listened to the negative reviews on this one. Each run just consists of 3 chapters, which are not particularly challenging once you get the hang of it, even without the unlockable permanent upgrades. Unlike StS/MT, there is no additional end-game content despite one of the NPC characters hinting for it. It is almost as if they had something planned, but abandoned it. It almost feels like a scam to keep you going.Still, the 5 hours it took me to beat the game twice with 4 different characters were quite enjoyable, but sadly there is not much else to keep me playing anymore. The scaleable difficulty system just does not cover it enough for me.If you are looking to scratch the deck-building itch after playing StS/MT, I recommend to go with Tainted Grail: Conquest. It has its shortcomings too, but unlike this game it kept me entertained for 20+ hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun deckbuilder that increases in difficulty with each run, seems like build variety is a bit lacking but enemy variety is defenitely there and it is very easy to understand, no super deep mechanic unlike some other deckbuilders but that can also be fun if you don't feel like doing advanced trigonometry while building a run.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I can give a ringing endorsement for this game. While I did like the concept, especially the concept of exploration it ultimately seems to lack polish. There are a myriad of crashes for me and a lot of really small but minor QoL issues (like it's so easy to accidentally miss-click something important and waste a brush or exit a mine).Many of the monsters are repetitive except for bosses. I also felt that the game was short, I wish that there was another board to explore before the final boss and more than four characters would have been great. If you can find the game on sale (less than $15) I'd say give it a shot, but there are other deck-builders out there that I found far more gratifying like Monster Train or Slay the Spire.
_childDocuments_.name: Roguebook

_childDocuments_.review: I got a refund as soon as I saw the giant metaprogression skill tree. Terrible idea for a roguelite. I'm ok with Slay the Spire style metaprogression in a roguelike deckbuilder, where you add new cards to the card pool but aren't actually unlocking power, but this one has character power upgrades and mechanics locked behind grinding currency over dozens of runs. Unless you like the grind, go play Slay the Spire, Monster Train, or the recently released Trials of Fire. Those will respect your time.
