_childDocuments_.review: As much as I would like to to give this game a positive rating, I ultimately came to this. At first,  was a wonderful little indie package. The game has a gorgeous and heartfelt presentation that would not look out of place on a Saturday morning cartoon; it also has a nice soundtrack to go with it. The story was passable and I was willing to look past the tropes it was taking advantage off. But two-thirds into the game and that's where I was beginning to see more negatives. The interesting mechanic of being able to turn an enemy unit into its past or future self becomes negligible. By end game, normal fights can be brute forced and boss fights rarely need their past/future selves to be invoked outside of certain gimmicks. And the numerous status ailment inducing skills you have become moot as bosses are immune to almost -if not all- of them. Then we get to the moment where the game would just hang on me. I'm talking about after taking a turn, the enemy -usually bosses- would just sit there and do nothing. Or sometimes, my character would just disappear and the game would just sit there while the music continues. To be fair, I did try waiting it out, but eventually I gave up and just reloaded. And this happened numerous times on different bosses. This even happened against the penultimate enemy. Thankfully, I managed to get to the end of the game because I was already in it for the long haul. I was way passed the point of no return for refunds so I may as well see the ride to the end.That said, it wasn't all bad. I did enjoy the game from the beginning up till two-thirds of the way. The game actually has a solid foundation. The cast was interesting and diverse. If they had more story arcs to develop their characters, it would have made them more memorable. The Antagonist were written better than you'd expect. Sure, the stereotypical, money-grubbing, megalomaniac could be found. But there were those with a reason and a will to back up their actions. The main plot has a good foundation but suffered from lack of development, pacing, and transition. I didn't mind I was able to sus out a lot of the plot while playing and I was inwardly pleased that the characters would sometimes act or say things I'd have expected them to -either logically or downright hilariously-. At the end of my 30 hour run, I've come to this conclusion. In  lies the seeds of a good JRPG; it's artwork and presentation give it a beautiful cover, but it's marred with the flaws of bad game design and story development.Can I recommend this game? To the normal JRPG enthusiast, i say "no". Unless you're willing to look past the flaws and enjoy what the game has to offer, you may end up getting frustrated with the design choices the developers had taken.But if you've managed to convince yourself to give this game a shot, I'd suggest to wait for a sale. There's still an enjoyable experience to be had here, just make sure to temper your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales is quite the journey; one in which everything aside from the beautiful art style, and the overall premise, seems like an afterthought. The euphoric rush of its opening cinematic is only matched by its totally bonkers plot. After the approximate 25 hours it takes to beat the game, you will feel exhausted - whether in a “good” or bad way is up to you.The game starts off slow, with a cliché set-up and a cringe factor you’ll need to overcome. You play as Crisbell, an orphaned girl who, after meeting a time travelling frog, discovers that she’s a Time Mage – an individual capable of manipulating time, as well as being able to see into the past and future. Shortly after, her hometown is coincidentally attacked by the Time Empress - another, more experienced Time Mage; one who, quite literally, seeks to blow up the world. Thus, with a couple of companions, Crisbell sets off to master her newfound powers and save the world from impending doom. The first area of the game does too good of a job at teaching you how exactly the rest of the game will play out. Among other things, you learn how Crisbell’s powers serve a purpose both in and out of combat. If you’re playing on a keyboard, the first thing you’ll notice is how awkward the controls are. You’re best-off switching to a controller, as the game was clearly intended to be played with one. While moving across the world outside of combat, your screen will be divided into three areas, each showing your current location, and nearby characters, across different points in time. The left side of the screen will be showing you the past, the right side the future, while the middle will be showing you the present. While these will sometimes inconvenience your navigation, it’s quite an interesting visual. You’ll also be able to see your surroundings change depending on which choices you make in the story, but these aren’t nearly as dynamic as the store page would have you believe. Your time travelling frog companion is sometimes able to travel into the past or future and interact with the scene you’re in, which helps solve many a plot hole and keeps the story going whenever the writers needed it to. In combat, enemies attack you from the left and right side of the screen, with your party being in the middle. Crisbell can send the enemies on the left side into the past, while the enemies on the right can be sent into the future. Not only will this change the enemies into their past or future selves, each with different stats, but it also synergizes with some of your companions’ abilities. These examples are sadly quite limited, and the time mechanic is severely underplayed. It’s never necessary to win a fight, and most of the stronger enemies are completely immune to it. You’ll mostly be using your precious turns to pump out damage or heal up. You also have the option of using consumables, both on yourself and enemies – though the latter never comes up, as all of the consumables provide benefits. It seems to be only there to screw you over should you accidentally misclick. The weird rhythm mechanic from JPRGs of old, where if you press the A button in sync with the attacks happening on screen to either deal more damage with yours or parry that of an enemy, also shows its face. It’s quite inconsistent however, as there’s no general rule of when to press the button, so you’ll have to guess the sweet spot of each animation individually. To further add to the confusion, Parrying sometimes negates all of the damage, but most of the time it doesn’t. Most of the time, it negates a status effect an attack might carry with it, but sometimes it doesn’t – with no explanation as to why. Also, there are two states of blocking an attack; Deflect and Parry, though what the difference between these two is, I have no idea. The whole mechanic is poorly explained and overall has terrible feedback. The second thing you’ll notice is how painfully slow all of this is. Walking takes ages, and you’ll frequently be ambushed by monsters when traversing the world. All of the quests in Cris Tales are structured the same way. Walk from point A to B, talk to people, bring them things. Then, get sent into a dungeon – either to fight a boss or fetch the final thing you need. Walk to the end of the dungeon, all the while you’re constantly ambushed by filler, easy fights. Then, take on the boss that’s more of a test of patience rather than skill, or grab the thing you were sent for, after which you’ll have to backtrack, all the while getting ambushed over and over again. The ambushes are such a nuisance, that later on in the game you’re given an item which lets you avoid them entirely when equipped. Since the main cast is composed of children, a lot of Cris Tales’ story is stitched together haphazardly by childlike logic. They’re shallow characters, but fun, which is a shame as their visual design is quite creative. Even if there isn’t a single bad performance to be found in the entire game, the voice acting sounds too much like an episode of a kids’ show, where characters have the need to extensively narrate everything they do. On the opposite, the soundtrack was barely able to catch my attention.The biggest clash, and the point where you’ll start losing your mind, is when Cris Tales starts covering some rather complex themes. These include, but are not limited to: the struggles of the working class, immigration, environmentalism, traditionalism vs. progressivism, the ethics of genocide, and the meaning of life. You’ll have to make in-game choices around all of these themes, which are so ill informed, as they don’t get the proper coverage they deserve, that it makes the whole experience all the more cathartic. It all starts feeling very surreal, grim occurrences start happening in the story, and for a good while I actually felt quite hopeless about the Time Empress blowing up the world. The writing of the game also takes a more sarcastic tone, almost to the point of parody, as the game takes jabs at itself and the childlike logic it’s been following up until that point. Characters start calling out each other’s obliviousness, mock their over-narration, and even go so far as to characterize the main character as stupid at one point. I don’t even know what’s happening anymore. I don’t know what anyone’s motivations are. I’m just along for the ride and seeing where it takes me. For a good while, Cris Tales is a fun game, the writing of which is so bad, it becomes good. That is, until the final act hit; an ordeal so stretched out, it gives you a choice of giving up and getting the bad ending should you die during it. It makes you go three times around the entire world map, back and forth between the same locations, each time completing a different task, and topping it all off with some recycled boss fights, and a final boss that takes around half an hour of uninspired combat to beat.Those couple of hours of fever dreamlike goodness aren’t enough to recommend Cris Tales, especially not at a 40€ price tag. Reviewed on the following system:Although I’ve experienced no performance issues with the game, there were a couple of visual and audio glitches: objects flickering and combat sounds not playing – not nearly enough to be immersion breaking. At one point the game froze on an enemy’s turn, forcing a restart. Save points are numerous, so it only cost me about ten minutes of progress.

Maps feel too big for how slow you move. The loading screens are a nightmare, who the HELL thought having a slow loading screen for each random battle was a good idea. _childDocuments_.review: I'm almost 4 hours in and have been having a good time with it....Pros:-Beautiful design and graphics, the gimmick of seeing time is wonderfully shown and done and really shines on its own. I can't stop talking about this aspect. It's gorgeous and so well done it leaves quite the impression. -Combat is mostly tried and true basic JRPG turn based combat. I don't personally like the dodge/parry mechanic. More on that later-Zero issues running this on PC-Amazing soundtrack and I enjoy the Voice Acting as wellCons: -Story is haphazardly put together. While good, and probably more exciting than it seems, its chopped up in such a way, its jarring, and this is especially so in the first few minutes of the game. It makes me wonder about the rest of the story. -Dodge/Parry Mechanic, this is not my favorite mechanic. In a turn based game I enjoy the slower pace. Having this as a mechanic, while yes makes turn based more exciting, it's also a hit or miss if it works correctly. Timing it with the look of the attacks was a failure for me, it didn't always match. As a controller player however, it matched the vibrations almost perfectly IF the vibrations happened at all. I'm not sure the issues here, but it could do with slight refinement especially since some controllers do not have a vibration function. -The game lends a lot to you paying attention not just to how things are described but the imagery of the game as it explains it, esp with the time mechanic, take notice of what happens to the monsters when time changes are applied. Some get weaker/stronger. While not necessarily a con this provides a steeper learning curve than some people may be prepared for, lending this issue on top of the poorly pasted cutscenes, it will provide a poor first impression of the game itself. -No graphical settings for PC. Not entirely surprising, however the game runs so well on its own, I'm not bothered by it, but it may bother some of you. Overall:For a $35 game it's living up to my expectations, even with some of the issues I have with the game. Overall it is a beautiful experience which helps distract you from the problems within the game itself. If anything, this would be worth a sale purchase in the future, just to admire the beauty that they aimed for in this game based on time travel. Just be warned, it's not a perfect game. 7/10 and will update this as I progress the story if needed.

_childDocuments_.review: -----------Cris Tales has a lot of good ideas. Unfortunately, Dreams Uncorporated and Sycks' inexperience really shows in what would have been a solid RPG. Good visuals and voice acting do not make up the well intention but clumsy writing, good overarching story but boring characters, interesting but unrealized combat mechanic, deliberate but slow-pace gameplay as well as short but padded content, And if you know your RPGs, it lives and dies on the strength or weakness of the story, the combat and the characters, the 3 things that Cris Tales have the most problem. Despite all of that, Cris Tales does have good bones and good genes; there is definitely some semblance of a good JRPG here. If the developers get a second chance, and learn from this experience, they could possibly have a comeback like Ori And Will Of The Wisp. That is a big if though. The problem with Cris Tales at the moment is that, for the price, there are so many other JRPGs that are more worthwhile and so, I can only recommend it if it’s on sale. --------------------The 2 good things, and what I suspect most of the funds where allocated to, are the artwork and voice acting. These 2 things are very good. The art is reminiscent of early 2000 Cartoon Networks’ Samurai Jack, while the voice acting for the most part is high production. --------------------The time mechanic is very interesting, looking at past, present and future simultaneously is a neat idea but it is somewhat under utilized. The combat mechanic too is also interesting but the combo’s that you can do with the past/future invocation is very limited. Also, why limit the Synchro attacks with Crisbell? Why not have all party members sync with each other like Chrono Trigger and Suikoden? Speaking of which, why only limit the party to 3 members? This is 2021, we should have 6 party members. The writing too, is clumsy. Many of the later surprises and twists that happen had no forehadowing and rather unjustified. It’s unfortunate because there is a very interesting main plot that isn’t well developed, rather, it gets bogged down by all these other subplots that happens in each town you visit. The game have interesting villains but it did not take the extra time to develop them. Instead, the game focuses way too much on side characters of each town with a lot of unnecessary dialogue and banter. For example, Cristophers’ family relationship did not need that much attention. On top of this, Crisbell, Cristopher, Wilhelm, are quite boring characters to play. They don't have much charm or charisma. Contrast that to Zas and K who are more charming and have distinct personalities. --------------------The one thing that cannot be fixed here and you are going the feel it, is the slow pacing of the game.   1 hour feels like 3, and you don’t feel like you accomplished much. Towards the end of the game, you fight some of the same bosses which is padded content. Now I understand that the studio probably ran into budget constraints, but they chose to prioritized the graphics and the voice acting rather than putting the resources into making a better game. That’s a choice they made and it did not pay off. ---------Final Words----------Like I said, despite these problems, there is an inkling of a good game here, but there is a multitude of other good JRPGs that are more worthwhile. Get Cris Tales on sale if you really want it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: Crystale is difficult to praise.It has a great art style and because I'm a lover of RPG, a friend who knew that excitedly recommended it to me.I had my fun with it, but ultimately I can't recommend it, it had insane potential with its characters and the main gameplay idea of time manipulation both insight and during the exploration. It sadly couldn't deliver, the gameplay in the end is just *punch the enemy until it dies*, the strategic aspect completely gets lost, especially during the boss fights. The game could have balanced itself around the status affects and manipulating them with the time spells. But they made nearly every boss immune to status, and there was basically only one synergy at the tutorial boss fight that was relevant. The dungeons as well felt really drawn out simply because you can't sprint, I'm sure if there was a sprint button you could finish the game 1-2 hours faster.TLDR: Great Potential didn't deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, I really do, but I can't in the state it's in right now. I hope this changes in the future, honestly. It's not that the game is bad or has some giant flaw, it's just that it feels extremely unpolished due to lack of time, budget or ability and you can feel it around every corner. It's a constant presence that diminishes the game's enjoyment steadily and constantly and it just too much to overlook in the end.- The story falls apart at the end. It's very clear that the writer wanted some story beats to play out but did not know how to properly connect them together. The party keeps getting teleported for some story beats. In one scene, right after killing a boss, one of the characters goes „Hey, I need to check something.”, cut to a past area on a different continent, and at the end when the character realizes that they made a mistake, we get teleported into a black void with some contraption and another character goes „Use this time machine to go back.” Like, wait, what, where did this come from? It's not commented on at all. The last quarter of the game is filled with contrivances like that and the „big bad evil guy” is just standing there, waiting for who knows what. I saw a few instances of text dialog being completely different then spoken dialog near the end, and some of the conversations making little cohesive sense in general like they were edited late in the development after voice lines could not be re-recorded.- Small graphical errors everywhere, usually combined with transitions. Like, watching a cutscene of a floodgate opening seeing it open again in the background after returning to normal gameplay. If you open a chest and get into a battle while the opened chest is on screen you'll see it pop open when you come out of battle. Whenever there's dialog in battle, the last textbox always appears again for a brief second instead of fading out properly.- Speaking of transitions, there are no battle transition. You just walk and randomly get a loading screen. A pretty lengthy one at that (especially the first time before the assets load) considering they happen all the time. Very often I didn't know if I triggered a fight, or a cutscene.- Let's talk about the battles. They're in the Super Mario RPG style of „press a button at the right time to do some more damage or block attacks”. This is fine by itself, but the timings feel very inconsistent. The animations are pretty, but for this system a lot of them are not functional. Too floaty and not snappy enough. Several other people complain that there's no separate on screen indicator for the timing, but I disagree with this criticism. The game does have a black flash to teach you the timing, it's just that they feel very inconsistent between attacks. Most times you tab when the attack connects, but sometimes the timing is at weird points, like right when the windup ends, or even during a windup. There's one enemy that has an attack where it bites 3 times in a row and instead of taping when the bite connects you have to tap in the middle of his windup to each bite. This inconsistency and the floatyness of certain attacks are what makes the fights feel off. Another thing is that the battles always last pretty long, and feel like they waste your time after a while. Your party members don't just stand in a staggered row for instance. They insist on having the current character in the middle, and jumping between foreground and background as turns go. Some boss in particular had a stance change mechanic that took like 10 seconds before each of their turns to execute, even if they decided to stay in the same stance they were in. Most of the characters are very gimmicky, but the gimmicks often don't work well in practice, like a character that can poison, but to take advantage of the poison fully you need to combo it with another character and it's just not worth the resource investment. Another character has access to a lot of varied attacks, but their default, normal physical attack for some reason almost always does more damage. There are interesting ideas for characters to combo of each other but they are just not rewarding enough to bother using so battles become tedious. Oh, and after my main character learned a slow spell I never found a boss that was not immune to it... Oh, and one of the boss fights had no sound effects at all...- A bunch of other random things, like the game using the dialog system for shops, saves and boats. Click on a save point and listen as a character ask you if I want to save, pick an option that yes, you do, hear a reply that you do want to save, and only then get to the save menu. Same thing for boarding or getting off a boat, or going to the shop. If I talk to a shopkeeper, why can't they just have a line of dialog and open the shop? Why do I have to pick if I want to shop, upgrade weapons or cancel and get an empty text box before the shop loads? And here's a funny thing: Some shops and save points have the same options in different locations then others. For no reason other then it probably being hand coded each time.- Finally, I want to talk about the most recent, at the time of writing, update that added a new character and dungeon, as well as how I see the developer is handling post launch support for the game. I made it clear that the game has issues, but it was released anyway. I do not condone releasing unfinished games, but I realize that making games is hard. Things happen. But I expect some communication, some noticeable effort being made to address peoples concerns if things didn't work out. As far as I can see the developer is dead silent about the game post launch. Maybe they are active on Discord, I don't know. They only released one bug fixing patch a month after release, and then another small bugfixing patch combined with a content update just last month. It is now half a year since release and the game still has a lot of problems. In fact, the latest update even broke one of the achievements and made it unobtainable. And what did that update contain? A coliseum that has 30 battles in a row that take like an hour to get through because of the slow battle system. The patch notes state that the coliseum has a new enemies and a new boss but it doesn't. It's the same enemies and bosses that you can find in the main game, but with higher stats. Some attacks may now inflict status effects or there might be some adds with the boss you have to kill, but the strategies don't change. I don't even know of the new character is good or not, cause when I saw how much setup she requires in the tutorial battle I never used her. She unlocks so late into the game that I already had all my party composition set in stone. The new dungeon has new enemies and an interesting boss at the end, as well as an interesting puzzle gimmick, but it's being brought down by, again, dialog based interactions with a button. After the dungeon you get a nice, but short cutscene with no dialog and get unceremoniously plopped back out on another continent with no dialog about what just happened. I have to suspect this was another bug, cause I can't believe this was intentional. None of the characters, even the new party member, act any different. It's like I never did the dungeon. Voice acting all the characters also seemed to pose a problem when adding this new content. Only the main character and the new party member have any dialog. Everyone else is mum about the events that transpire. There's very little dialog in the new content in general, making everything feel especially hollow. The dialog that the merchant has when you ask him about the coliseum is very clearly recorded by a different voice actor. In the end, the entire game is worse off with this content then without it. The developers should have focused on polish and not giving the impression that they want to bury the unfinished game under some more unfinished content.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this on my radar since the demo.  I really wanted to give this a positive rating.  I just cannot.If the developers read this: I want you to actually take the feedback to heart.  Don't take it as me bashing you, because I can tell that a lot of love and care went into the game.  But I think you really need a better QA team.✅ Obviously the graphics are something to behold and a lot of time was spent on the art direction.  Very nicely done.✅ Some really good music tracks to be found here as well.✅ Finally, a unique story that doesn't insult the gamer with a bunch of random nonsense.✅ While there is padding, there's not a lot of it.  You can mostly progress the story at your own tolerance.✅ The voice actors do a very good job with each character.  Especially impressive given the price of the game.⛔ The battle engine plays like a slowed down version of Indivisible, or like Romancing SaGa 3.  I wasn't a fan of it, despite what it was trying to do.  There are parts where it's fun (rusting armor to make it weaker, for example) but in general it's just not fun.⛔ This game is SLOOOOOOOOOOW.  I had to toss a 2x speedhack on it, which ironically made the game much more playable and fun.  Unfortunately it also made the game slightly unstable, and I experienced my first crash, which made me not want to ever play the game again.  A better option would be for the developers to understand that everything is just too damn slow and fix it at the source (even if it's just a toggle).⛔ I'm not a fan of the level balancing in the game.  The maximum you can be is level 60, yet at that level and with fully maxed weapons, you're struggling to do 200 damage on anyone.  That should NOT be the case.⛔ I agree with other reviewers that the fun factor seems to decline as you go.  The first segment of the game (basically, the entirety of the demo) was fun and interesting, but nothing else was nearly as fun except for one small segment that was an unwinnable battle a bit later in the game.  There are also some unique skills that Cris gets that adds a bit of strategy to the exploration, but nothing earth shattering; reminds me a lot of Magic Knight Rayearth, actually.⛔ Character development is near null.   This is a big thing for me - I have to care about those in my party and those I meet.  Here, the people come and go and there's no real story to any of them, and that drives me nuts.⛔ There are a few points with unclear instructions.  The soil circle is explained at the beginning as a key to advance, but then in the very next segment you're at a camp and you're using it to save your game.  Next you're using it to advance.  I'd rather they just used a save point - or even better, a save anywhere mechanic - rather than dual-purposing the soil circle.  This stumped me at the Walled City for a bit.⛔ I'm not sure why, but on the Switch, the audio balancing is WAY off.  Cris sounds 3x louder than anyone else.  It's annoying - which caused me to actually buy it on PC despite preferring to have it on Switch (I'd rented it).⛔ Speaking of audio, it's unpolished in certain places.  There's one cutscene where you can clearly hear audio distortion that happens when you have cheap speakers that are cranked to the max.  This tells me that when they worked the audio for this game remotely, someone didn't clean things up.  It's not part of the cutscene.  It's obviously bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales is an RPG that presents a nice story, melodious soundtrack, and brilliant artwork!Not only that, it brings a new perspective to the genre! But there are some things that just cannot be overlooked, follow this review and find out!The story feels like following a fairy tale book. We play the role of Crisbell, an orphan, who finds out she has time mage powers and decides to use them to help the world. There is a war going on and the evil Time Empress wants to rule all kingdoms! It is a mainstream story for RPGs, but the developers do make it engaging with neat turns and interesting companions. The newly added time mechanics truly add to the story when your quests alter the possibilities in the future.The dialogues and the script are very well written, and most parts include incredible voice acting performances.There is a gigantic problem with the story though... and the problem with the story is not the story... it is the pace of the game! The pace is too slow and drags down taking away from the story. The streamlined back and forth makes the player lose interest in the actual story... The time mechanics are interesting and combine well with other magics, but they end up being nothing more than a useless gimmick. The basics for winning battles are stalling and constant recovering.This is one of the most frustrating parts..Instead, you have to be prepared to fight swarms of enemies in small areas in a cheap tactic to make the game lengthier. Especially in the beginning, when you will have to recover constantly, because enemies are faster and attack before you even have the chance to flee. A full party of enemies may explode at first turn, stopping you from recovering in battle at all.And then get ready to walk through gigantic areas with barely any enemy.The mix of battles and story is not well balanced. The player will get bored from lengthy story parts and then bored of walking long distances and then bored of fighting flocks of enemies...Apart from the pace, be ready to deal with massive hand-holding followed by missed essential tutorials or guidance.The hint button is there, but you will be forced to read every instruction and direction multiple times. Just to give one example:You go from one city to the time mage's house and there the time mage will point out that you can use your magic to make a seed turn into a tree by using your future magic. He will show you the ground mark where you can plant a seed. There will be a seed on the floor, but you will not be able to get it yet. Then you go back to the city and the path will be blocked. The frog pops up and tells you that you may be able to find an alternative way. Walk a little and you will see a ground mark, then the frog dialogue pops up again and he will tell you that you can plant a seed there to climb the tree and enter, so you should go back to the time mage's house to get the seed. When you get back to the time mage’s house, the dialogue pops up again and they say: look, a seed, maybe we can plant it to get in back in the city, grab that seed and head back to the city. After grabbing the seed and going back, another dialogue: look, let’s plant the seed in this ground mark. All unskippable dialogue!Meanwhile, the game will not explain that during battle you can only use future magic to your right and past magic to your left. You can turn the character to either side, but this right and left constraint is fixed to the player’s perspective and will not change.Another issue in battles is that the turns shift too quickly, so many times you won’t even be able to realize which enemy is attacking who before they do, which hinders your ability to block.To make matters worst, the block defense timing is unclear and fails often. The animations are too subtle and the hit detection is not on point.Apart from battles, there are a few bad design decisions that take away from the experience.To give an example:There is a side quest to collect special flowers, but this quest only starts at a certain point. You will be able to see the flowers flashing when you pass by, but it is not possible to collect them until the quest starts. And then you have to go back to the same places just to collect those flowers you already saw, but was not able to collect before.All this back and forth is very time consuming considering that it takes a long while to go from one place to the other. There is no run or teleport.And then you get some bad guidance that may hinder you progress, like: The path is blocked, we need to go to the West. So you go to the West part of the city and nothing happens. From there you get out of the city and try to enter the city from the outer West part to no avail. The next move is to go West of the map, right? Wrong, it was actually to go to the left of the blocked gate... which isn’t really in the West part of the city..There is also a missed opportunity within the game. At some point one of your characters learns to scan the enemies, which will allow you to analyze their stats, strengths and weaknesses (in the past, present and future). This is really neat and could be coupled with a scan database book to enable a collection aspect to the game.Which brings us to another part to point out about the game: there are just a few open world enemy sprites that get recycled with different colors. It is understandable given how much storage the graphics and voice acting must take, but it would be nice to see some more variety.Moving back to the fundamentals, the player cannot save from anywhere. There are fixed save points when exploring cities and dungeons, which is a terrible choice given that you will face your battles and progress the story in these areas.Lastly, this game needs more save slots. Or else it needs to implement fixed save states to return to. There are some events that can only take place depending on your choices at specific points. Having to replay everything with unskippable dialogues just to get an achievement or a few different dialogue boxes is a terrible choice!Doing the research, the devs have been improving the game since release, so I hope this review can shed some light on how to improve the gameplay mechanics. The game was developed with love by an indie studio and some parts of it are masterpieces.The audio is really good and the voice acting is superb!The visuals are on another level. Artistic, beautiful, terrific blend of colors, past, present and future!Ambience, dialogues and cutscenes are all masterpieces! It really takes you inside of a fairy tale book!• Stunning graphics, a work of art.• Terrific voice acting.• Great music.• Interesting concept.• Story is very well written.• Game pace is too slow.• Battles are dull. Should make (better) use of the new time and magic mechanics.• Battle mechanics for blocking are broken.• Too much hand-holding and useless back and forth.• No run, fast travel or teleport.• Cannot save anywhere, need to find save points.• No save state and limited save slots in a game with a few different paths.• Unskippable dialogues.Cris Tales feels like a masterpiece that should have been, but ended up falling short in multiple core aspects.The pace does not work well and turns what should have been an awesome experience into a boring one. The battles do not take advantage of the new mechanics and end up being bland and unappealing.Last, but not least, the game misses every possible target audience.Rating: 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: After I finished Cris Tales journey, I couldn't believe what I was going through.I think this game was added about 2 years ago on my wishlist primarily because of a good-looking trailer and what the developers promised. I even played the demo and was wowed by its art style and the time jump mechanic. The demo was a little bit rushed, 15-20 minutes for the entire introduction, and the first problem that I encounter was the parry thing (which I will come back later, on this thing). But overall, it was great, and I was really excited about buying this game on day 1. That being said, year and months of waiting and a delay later, here is my verdict:OK, it’s 2021, I bought it, but I didn’t start to play it immediately, which is kind of good since I saw a lot of discussion about audio and visual glitches. After a few weeks or a month, I started to play it. When starting this game, first what you will see is its art. Bwooah, I can’t express my thoughts about it other than it’s as pretty as a picture. The characters, the cities, whole background even during combat are consistently great. The mix of hot and cold colors makes landscapes feel pleasing and I’m not going to even mention the cutscenes “Holly crap, I wish the cutscenes were even longer”. The biggest downside for visuals was the areas outside of city safe zones. Especially the “forest” or should I say plains because it literally looks like that. When I came across an enemy team out of nowhere, first what I asked myself what was happening. A few seconds later I realized that “Oh yeah it’s a forest, you know, in the forest you can get lost and encounter monsters”. The second thing I really liked about this is its voice acting. Sometimes it felt it was hammy and sometimes really powerful during banter between characters and party members, although the voice quality of the microphone is sometimes awful (but I can forgive them considering most of them worked from home). The first few areas of the game do teach you genuinely good how to use your magic, normal attacks, and other movements which will play out exactly for the rest of the game. I am not sure why Steam says action game when clearly from trailers and other videos you can see it’s more turn-based game. After the introduction, combat mostly works well and looks simplistic but from the middle part of the game till the end it felt repetitive and boring and reaalllly sloooooow. I wish it had a fast-forward button like most other turn-based games. Interesting but overall unrealized combat mechanic. Time manipulation looks awesome in the beginning, sadly the percent of using it during combat is like 10%, so most of it here and there during the game (murdering enemies with attacks is ten times more effective than using Time-jumps in an impactful way) and the penultimate boss. Using it during non-fights is ok really, so basically seeing the past and the future of the city/characters and gossiping or taking some stuff from the past.Parry combat in start feels awful, you don’t even feel when you click the button because the game doesn’t tell you other than “look at the animation and judge for yourself”. Afterward in the game, you still get the feeling that the correct time to block has zero relationships with the on-screen animation. The locations in the map section of the game are not labeled, and the hint system does not give you any actual direction if you get lost (sometimes) or forget it after putting this game on a week of a pause. The inventory and equipment system is pretty overwhelming to beginners like me. Also walking around the city felt like you were kind of a snail or a sloth especially when the game tells you “Hey go there pick this and come back, then the character will tell you to take this and go on the other side of the city and give another character that and then which you will need to go back or go somewhere else to finish other task and then come back to pick your prize”. Some side characters even have side quests which are ok, but there are more missions that I didn’t even notice till the finish of the one city. I needed to go on YouTube to realize that there are more missions to do in order to get the best sub ending for that section. Funny thing is that it’s not hard to find it but the world and whole gameplay doesn’t even give you a hint or some kind of feeling to talk around “Hey, I should go to this character and talk to him, maybe he will tell me or demand something from me”.And here are the worst things: Ok, maybe it was kind of my fault that I played that like for 6 hours in one sitting (usually playing games less than that one day) and felt really exhausted, but that’s also one of really bad gameplay or I should say more questionable design.For me, the characters were ok, not that I will remember them other than Zas and Rysa Oroitz. Plot points vary wildly between “ooh the plot thickens” and “wtf was that?”. And a general series of bizarre phenomena that make me wonder if this was rushed out the door, especially the ending.The music was good, actually.Performance-wise, It didn’t stutter or anything like that and I still don’t understand the system requirements list. Like what resources is this game using that it needs GTX 650Ti or 750Ti, I know these GPUs are old, but a lot of other indie games don’t even ask for this today lowered end GPU. On the other hand, visual and audio glitches occurred even after a few updates, nothing game-breaking since this game has a lot of checkpoints. I’m going to be straightforward, it’s too much, too much for this type of game. I am really sorry, but 40€ paying for this, like nooo. I even considered buying a physical edition which is 100€ and I'm grateful I didn't buy it though. In my opinion, this should have been at max 20€ maybe just maybe 25€, but who knows, you are developers and publishers you probably have a better reason.Strange and really hard to say it, but YES, I am recommending it with BIG Disclaimer -

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up, but only because I do not want to give it a thumbs down. I would struggle to recommend this, but I would struggle more to say I disliked it.This game feels like an incredibly clear example of what happens when immensely talented, passionate and ambitious people run screaming, at top speed, directly into a wall called Budget Limitations. There are some incredible strengths here, (graphics, worldbuilding, fully voiced dialogue, characters) and some utterly baffling shortcomings. (bad UI, poor combat mechanics, missing sound effects, badly paced story)I'd love to see if their next game can deliver something other than extremely mixed feelings.

_childDocuments_.review: Really tried to give this game a fair shake, but ultimately wasn't drawn in enough by what I could reach within the first 2 hours of gameplay to really want to continue playing this. The game is gorgeous make no mistake, but all that production value spent on the art seems to have sucked away production from other areas of the games. There's no sound effects in the menu, using heal spells from the menu also doesn't have sound effect. If you go to talk to the vendor in the second town, you can't just exit the dialogue, you have to pick an option *then* exit. There's dialogue between Crisbell and Matias any time you want to save your game or rest at a soil spot. Things like this are minor nuisances but they'd definitely add up over the course of a 30 hour RPG or however long this is.The presentation of the game also is not good at all, and I don't mean the art style. When you launch the game, you're thrown into a random battle with no context, then get thrown to before that battle starts and you can actually control Crisbell. The plot of the game also isn't super compelling, maybe it gets more fleshed out later but it starts out as your generic chosen one RPG story, at least the game gets points for me from Crisbell being reluctant and scared instead of "gosh golly gee I'm the chosen one!" Volcano and whatever the other evil twin is called also seem to be set up as recurring unwinnable fights which is also such a tired JRPG trope, do they really add anything this way? The time mechanic is cool and all and I'm sure it has implications beyond just the main story, but as a battle mechanic I'm not sure how much it really adds. Basically you always have 3 views going in towns, you see the present state, but also past states and future possibilities, which you can make decisions with sidequests to influence. A specific aspect, Time Hopping with Matias to interact with the past or future, is annoying as hell to use though because not only does Matias have to be physically close to Crisbell, he doesn't teleport to your current location, and his movement speed in the past is painfully ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow (yet another production nuisance). The game also forces in Paper Mario style blocking and "perfect" hits which I don't really feel adds anything to the combat. Speaking of which, even with the time mechanic the combat feels incredibly shallow, not really having many options.Overall, this game just feels like there's a lot of wasted and/or misplaced potential. The art style is gorgeous, but that's really the only positive I can list in comparison to everything else. Oh, also, the settings are sorely lacking, only allowing you to change the sound settings. No resolution settings, no option to play the game windowed or borderless, no ability to rebind keys. So a bad PC port on top of an already mediocre game. Do yourself the favor and avoid this one imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game. Played the demo last year, wishlisted it and preordered it with the soundtrack. Seeing that the game got mixed reviews at launched, I hoped it would mostly be about bugs and postponed it for a few month, hoping that the experience I would get then will be a great one. It is a shame that I can't say it is.The best thing about the game is certainly the artstyle and even that can be quite flawed, as soon as it comes to animation.The number of mediocre to bad things though is... long. Lets start with the combat. The idea of using time to change the flow of combat, as represented in the demo had me really intruiged and I was interested to see where the game would go with it. the anser is: Nowhere! Seen the little thing about rusting the bosses armor in the demo? thats as complex as it gets. you have a binary choice of timeline on each side of the combat and thats it. And in most fights you don't even have that(or rather, you don't need to bother with it). Is it better with puzzles outside of combat? Nope! the game is incredibly handholdy with puzzles, to the point where they basicly don't exist. Need to do anything? Have the characters tell you exactly, step by step, what you need to do. Which is weird, because when you use the "tip"-function of the game, it quite often tells you something completly useless. I asked to frog for a tip about where to go on while I was in the sewers. know what he told me? "It is weird that there are no people around!" is it now!?My main-issue though is probably the writing. It's pretty bad. A lot of the time, interarction between characters feel REALLY forced, their lines are clichee and a lot of the time, the game doesn't realize what happend yet. Several times, I talked to NPCs and they referenced interactions we didn't have. And even if everything works as planned, the writing is just bland and clichee. This is the thing you absolutly can not  mess up in your RPG imo. I can overlook the story not making much sense and stuff like that, as long as the writing makes me forget that in the moment and the characters are interesting, but thats just not the case here.It's such a shame, because the game certainly has some potential, but it fails at every step to realize it.Edit: Oh and I almost forgot one of the worst things about combat! there is a basic crit and parry system, like there was in paper mario. press the button while you hit the enemy or get hit, to deal increased damage and take reduced damage. the problem with it here: SO MANY MOVES OF ENEMYS DON'T CONNECT WITH YOUR CHARACTER!!! your characters jumps over to the opponent, so dealing increased damage is pretty easy, but parrying is a pure guessinggame, while your enemy makes some kind of animation on the spot and you have no choice but to assume when you need to hit the button.
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: I've always loved the JRPG genre, and started following it in 1987 with the NES Dragon Warrior. So you'd think I'd be enraptured with Cris Tales....and for a while I was. The visuals were amazing, the music was nice, the storyline kept me interested, and the combat was simplistic enough to feel like an old JRPG. However, around the 10 hour mark, the cracks started to appear.Buying Tents for 10,000 gold, over-reliance on quick time events in combat, maddeningly slow running speed (Especially for your frog friend), useless and unbalanced/improperly priced equipment, and most of all....the god awful quest progression that seems to deliberately conspire to make you fail to complete side quests.Which is a huge problem, since the true ending, and a good portion of the story content, only unlocks when you do *all* the side quests. It's infuriating when you are warned not to progress through the main quest because they'll lock your side quests, yet you go back to finish those side quests and find the journal description for their requirements doesn't at all match what the game or the NPCs are telling you to do. In all my 34 years of playing JRPGs, I've never been this confused in a game.Cris Tales had a lot of potential, but I cannot recommend it at all. It's confusing, unbalanced, and tries to mimic classic JRPGs rather than be its own entity and build upon their legacy. Yes, it sounds corny, but that's the best way I can put it. Purchase at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: Its uh... Its not good guys.CONS-The game is sloooooooooow, the combat, travel, exploration, dialogue, etc are all very very slow.-Quests will have you backtracking between points back and fourth repeatedly, presumably to artificially extend the life of the game, made worse by the first point.-Core time travelling mechanic is very clunky and once again, slow. The supposed synergies it brings in combat are cumbersome to set up and not worth the effort almost always.-Combat is HEAVILY influenced by a timed button press/QTE system. I cannot overstate how much this effects combat... With good timing the game difficulty is an absolute joke and with poor timing its basically impossible.-The game has very clearly been ported to PC with little thought put in. Any sort of graphical options are almost entirely absent.-The price of the game (as of launch) is extremely high considering what it is. Again this is something made all the more worse by the fact another indie title has released on the same day for half the price and is being showered with praise whilst Cris Tales sits on "mixed" reviews, dissapointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it so far, the game starts off weirdly since its just the demo pasted as the beginning of the game but it gets a lot better after like the 1st hour or so after you get the basic abilities you need to play the game well for example healing. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, while the mechanics of the game are very interesting and I could see them being developed further in many unique ways, the actual plot is incredibly poorly executed, especially in terms of pacing and it just completely stopped me from being able to get immersed in any way.I had this game on my wishlist for about 2 years before its release and was following it closely. I played the demo and was completely wowed by the art style and the innovative time mechanics. I did however have one major issue with the demo, in that it felt incredibly rushed, taking about 20 minutes for the entire introduction, padded out by a half an hour fetch quest to introduce you to the mechanics. So I mentioned this in the feedback form the devs made and waited for the main game to come out.Playing through it today I found that the intro portion was exactly the same. Given there was a delay in release and because of the pandemic, I gave the benefit of the doubt and just assumed they hadn't had the time to touch up the dialog in the introduction. After getting through everything in the demo however, a character that showed up out of the blue with no explanation gives his entire life story at the first question you ask him. The game had in no way convinced me that this kind of trust was earned between any of the characters and it immediately made me turn off the game. It showed me that pacing was never going to be considered in the writing, and there was never going to be any set-up and pay-off because nothing is left to the imagination.Normally I wouldn't bother writing a review, much less one this lengthy. But I'm sure this game has something special in it, and I'm upset that the rushed and lackluster dialog is preventing me from reaching it. I know this game could've been so much more than it is. if you're only here for the gameplay then by all means, buy this game. The mechanics are inventive and have a lot of potential. If you're here for a good story, I personally don't think you'll find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game and it's just not good.  This has some of the worst boss fight design I've seen since the 1990s.  You don't do enough damage, even with fully upgraded everything, to finish fights in a reasonable amount of time.  They're not HARD fights - you will win - they just take so long that you'll be asleep, or have to go to work or school by the time you're done. The slogfest gets worse the further in you go, as later bosses start to apply regeneration effects to themselves that do as much healing in a single turn as your team can output.  (It was at this point that I uninstalled.)The blocking mechanic is a failure.  Too many attacks don't seem to have intelligent block timings.  The correct time to block has zero relationship with the on screen animations.  A lot of them just do a ton of damage even if blocked.  It wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the fact that regular enemies do tons of damage even when you have optimum equips.You. Move. So. Slow.  Walking around is a chore.  Game needs a run button.  Which is a sign of bad design.  And when you possess the frog, you move even slower.  It's painful.  If the game had double walkspeed it would still be slow.Your 5th characters is uselessYour 4th character is beyond useless.  Doing regular attacks causes him to blow up.  This would be fine if he did reasonable damage.  He doesn't.  He does very low damage relative to when you pick him up AND has a self destruct issue.   One of the worst designed characters I've seen in years.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing this game's first trailer and putting it on my wish list on it's art alone. the game is gorgeous, but I fear that's where the praise ends.   The biggest issue is game balance. Early on, you find a mix of enemies that either feel appropriate for your level and those who are way to strong for the early game. Even if you master the parry system ( a requirement, due to how much damage you'll end up taking otherwise) some basic enemies are doing 40,50 points of damage when your HP is only 150 to start with. Ultimately, you'll either find the game to easy or too hard, depending on what you're fighting at the time. Save points don't restore health, but instead use a tent system; this would be fine by itself, but the cost of tents are prohibitively high, prevent you from buying or upgrading equipment, and you'll discover its better to just use healing magic till you get to town, ultimately making tents useless.   Pacing is also another big issue (ironic for a game about time). Some enemies have long pauses before attack animations start, some bosses jump from side to side on screen for seemingly no reason (I would say its connected to the time mechanics in game, but some bosses aren't effected by Crisbell's powers, making the point moot), and their being a brief pause between characters jumping from the back to the foreground to make their moves (its only a beat of waiting, but this is a turn based RPG, they add up.) The game also clearly runs out of steam by the end of the second act, as you are just returning to old locations and fighting the same bosses again.  The story is ok up until the third act, when it just kinda falls apart; again, a pacing issue, as the third act feels really rushed.  User Experience (UX) is also something i had issues with. My two biggest gripes are: needing to hit a button when moving screen to screen (just let me walk to the edge and go to the next area [some areas to do this, highlighting the problem further]). When reaching a save point in the field, you have three options: rest, save, do nothing. clicking each option brings up a dialogue box with Crisbell repeating that option that you then need to click out of before she takes the option. Again, this seems minor to read, but you're doing this CONSTATLY, just to save. There is also no autosave, so you need to save often (with the save points sometimes blending into the environment, which bit me on the second to last boss.) There is no fast forward feature for dialogue, and there is slight lag when trying to mash through, so mashing doesn't really work.    The art style is what carries this game, and is why I played for so long, despite not really enjoying myself. With the final boss full of some BS, I just decided to stop; none of the rest of the game carries its weight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lovely little adventure with gorgeous art, adorable characters and an interesting mechanic that makes exploring the world feel very rewarding.That being said, it simply is not very accessible. For one, it's difficult to navigate-- the locations in the map section of the game are not labeled, and the hint system does not give you any actual direction if you get lost. I find myself longing for quest markers. The inventory and equipment system is pretty overwhelming to beginners like me; it's just a wall of text that navigates awkwardly (also, for some reason the menu is bound to enter instead of escape, and it took me a very long time to get used to that). It also falls into the usual RPG trap of requiring you to grind for your life all of a sudden to defeat a boss, and that gets boring very quickly. Credit where it's due, the combat mechanic is well done and allows for a lot of creativity in the combos, but even that gets exhausting when you're doing nothing but fighting the same enemies over and over again. EDIT: I forgot to address the timing for the parry/critical mechanic. The game determines the severity of attacks based on whether or not you can hit a button at a certain point in the character's animation, but the correct moment to do so is not well visually indicated, and missing your cue can make an attack against you SIGNIFICANTLY more powerful. Further, some bosses use both blockable and unblockable attacks, and there is no way to visually differentiate the two (and many unblockable attacks were powerful enough to TPK me, making me have to grind... again). There's no way to turn this off or set up an auto-parry that I could find.The bar for entry is high, and that sucks because if you put the work in, the game has a lot of great things. The characters are funny, the lore is interesting, the politics of each new area are intricate and fun to explore. But you can't just sit back and enjoy the ride, you have to beat your head against the wall until you stumble on the right direction you're supposed to go. It's a good game, but with all that in mind I really don't think it was worth the 30$

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Buy it on sale. Full price is not worth it. This game's time shenanigans aren't overshadowing its flaws. It's fun if you play it for what it is: a mediocre JRPG with a neat art style.The following may contain information that could be considered spoilers by some.This game is another "love letter" to an entire genre. Those usually compare to the real thing like watching someone play a sport compares to doing it yourself. Cris Tales is a lot like that. Let's do a Pro/Con List because nobody is sick of that stuff from school, am I right?Pros:+The art is pretty.+Some attacks get stronger if you hit a button at the correct time during their animation.+The voice acting is pretty good+All characters are very different from each other and mostly useful.+The music is pretty nice+The Time mechanic has lots of potential but....Cons:-The Time mechanic has so much wasted potential and isn't even useful in 90% of the fights  because straight up murdering enemies with attacks is ten times more effective than using  Time-jumps in an impactful way.-Battles are either a snooze fest, at an enjoyable difficulty, or the enemy is trying to   cheese you. That's at a 60/30/10 split btw.-This game likes to remove one or two of your characters temporarily/permanently at a time  including their equipped gear and stuff several times throughout the game. -You get a character that can "catch" enemies later on. There's an achievement to collect all  the enemies.  The game doesn't tell you what enemies you still need for that. I'm fairly sure there's a cut-off  point for a specific enemy about 5 dialogue boxes after you get that character. Screw me, I  guess?-The last 30% of the game are a slog. The devs thought it'd be super fun to structure the  endgame in a very tedious way: Go to the final map's new "hub" -> "Let's visit every city  we've been to so far for X reason!" -> Go to the final map's hub again -> "Let's visit every city  we've been to so far again for Y reason!" -> Return to the hub again -> "Let's visit every city  we've been to so far AGAIN for Z reason!" -> I wake up from this unending nightmare and  realize reality is merely a construct created by a fatty blob inside of a bone and flesh  structure -> I wake up from my boredom induced nap to return to the Hub again.-The timing to "press A to deal double damage" and "press A to not eat as much doo-doo"  is  not really obvious 50% of the time. The only indicator for that is a slight flashing on the edges  of your screen.While that may sound like I'm pooping on the game (which I am to a certain degree), I don't actually hate it. It's a fun game with a lot of flaws.I'd give it a 6,5/10 with 0 being "this should be a crime" and 10 being "this is one of the most memorable video game related experiences of my life".I hope the devs take what they've learned and will create a solid JRPG (and not a "love letter to JRPGS") in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game has a very colorful art style, and even the mechanic for being able to see into the past present and future at the same time being a unique concept, unfortunately the execution was poorly done, and by this I mean is that the current version is just very gimicky, and you are not allowed to use it all the time, you are only able to when the developers allow you to use it, and this game doesn't give you the freedom to play exactly like you want, since you could be a very clever person and think ahead for some quests and stuff, but because the developers did not program sequence breaking into the game, even though you might know how to move the story forward, you are not able to unless the NPCs or events in the plot, give you permission to interact with whatever objects you had already found, and this is just very tedious and frustrating because a beautiful game world just begs to allow for free exploration, but all the linearity in everything you are allowed to interact with just kills the immersion and fun factor. The only thing that I can honestly praise this game for, is the combat system because you can form some pretty great strategies, with the unique time jump in battle mechanic, and despite the characters starting out real weak and simple, by the time you start to unlock skills that give the team synergy, you can have a blast with all the different combinations you can pull off. It is sad though that unfortunately some battle segments are completely unwinnable, because they are supposed to be scripted losses, but you you are not really told which are like that, because some segments where you could have lost, if you actually won them you can get some worthwhile goodies, like the one at the start with the wolves where despite it being challenging, if you manage to win it then you can save a lot of money with the reward you get.While I'd like to talk about the game more, I haven't finished it but based on what I played so far, while I've had some fun with it, I do not like being caged in areas forced to complete mandatory quests and sidequests,  so I cannot really recommend that experience to people, I also do not think that the game is worth the $40 at full price, so only if you are interested in a JRPG type of game that has some unique stuff, can I recommend this game but only mostly if you manage to get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game demands my full attention, without rewarding it. I felt like I was wasting my time.This features every trope you would expect in a JRPG, but lacks some of the main benefits, like freedom, exploration and rewards for... well, anything.I played as much as I did and I feel like I didn't REALLY get to play, because the game kept pestering me with crappy dialogs (like "I suspected you're a super mega time wizard and it seems I was right") and tutorials that teach you things only your grandmother might not know.Maybe there's a good game behind that wall of hyper-casual cartoony (in terms of plot) intro, but I didn't feel like wasting my time anymore.I rarely rate these things, and it's even less common I take story into consideration when recommending/not recommending a game. I think it would be unfair to bash games for element I very rarely enjoy. With that said, this one felt so low effort it I decided to make an exception.Story feels like cartoon tier fan fiction. Some(not all) of the voice acting also sells that fanfic idea REALLY hard. The game treats you like a kid with negative attention span, as it repeats the same things over and over again.  You (a little girl) save a town from monsters, while guards and grown men watch. A villager complains that it must be this other villager who set this up to buy their farm for cheap (a legitimate interest to set this up). - Wait! - says a random woman in a crowd (who looks futuristic in comparison to others). Let's not be hasty. An external party that's working with the main villain had to set this up.- YOU, the girl who lived here your entire life and just saved us! I know it's not Salem trials times, but where did you get that sword and who are those 2 new names you mentioned? GUARDS! BURN THE WITCH!!!!!!!!Moments later, as you escape:- You are so special. You're a child of prophecy!1 camping night later you lose your time powers (still have the super sword) and enter a city. A boy is using sewage system as a pool and gets swept away by a current.- I wish I could help, but I just lost MY POWERS (ones she didn't have not even 24 hours ago).One of characters you travel with the son of heads of the city. Not a single guard knows him and there's a dialog to show that too.Character are written to be a parody of their dominant trait dialed to 11. Imagine a pompous rich girl stereotype in a cartoon. Yeah, so she insults you the first time you meet without you even interacting with her. Quality writing...I'll preface this by saying, this might be fine for casual people entering the genre. It's far too slow and simple for me. mechanics are your generic turn based JRPG, with 2 "twists".While on that topic of game being slow... REALLY slows the experience down.Mind you none of the above is a bad thing on its own, it's the whole package. The game overall felt weird to control and I probably can't even explain most things.One of the contributing factors is that input lag on dialogs, that I already mentioned. Art style creates another problem, which prevents you from accurately judging positions. You effectively can't tell if you're close enough to interact with NPCs just by looking.In the overworld entrances to areas aren't distinct enough. A bunch of clumps of objects I thought were entrances to areas weren't that. They were just decorations.I can praise the game for its art (even if it's unpractical in places) and music, but as a game it doesn't feel very well designed.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10I think this game deserves its current Mixed ratings. This game is visually gorgeous with an inventive combat system and a great plot. However, I can't help but feel that it was rushed and didn't have enough playtesting before release. Story is wonderful, but the endgame is one of the most anti-climatic events I've witness recently. They had something, but lost it completely. It's if the developers just said "Yea I'm tired, let's just wrap it all up and call it a day, I don't care". I can see that the writing team is talented as the majority of the game is wondering. But man what the heck is that ending pace.... Overall, I still enjoy most of my time with the game, and thus giving it a thumbs up. The world was easy to get lost in. The voice acting is great for the most part. Describing the game in one word would be "Charming". However, it is far from an excellent experience just from the endgame alone. Looking back, I feel sitting and waiting for the game after playing the demo a few years back was more exciting than actually finishing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing art for this game can't save it from uneven difficulty curves, poor game design, and late game padding.The game starts strong, with the first few hours showing you all the seeds of a good RPG, interesting gameplay mechanics, enough hints of an interesting world/story, and showing off its great art. But despite seeming like it has all the pieces, they never come together. The limited time demo that they had put out showcased the strongest point in the game... But the game slowly goes downhill from there and never really recovers.Maybe you could put up with this if the story was amazing, but it ultimately comes across as fine. It wasn't amazing, but I wouldn't mark it as a negative or as anything to write home about.I could probably rant a lot about my many issues with the game design, but instead I will simply say that the premise and the strength of the demo made this one of my more anticipated games of the year. But what could had been a real indie sleeper hit instead left me disappointed. Which is a real shame, as I really did hope to like this game. But for all its flaws, I really do like the art of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I saw Cris Tales, something in the trailer compelled me to anticipate it, that being the art style, and it being too wonderful for me to let it slip in my radar. That being said, months of waiting and a delay later, here is my verdict:Let's get the first thing out of the way, the visuals: I'm glad to say that the gorgeous art is consistently great throughout the game, every design felt... immaculate to my eyes, each place, each character and each enemy. The striking, picturesque choice of serene and hot colours makes the landscapes feel pleasing to the eyes and makes for some visually iconic moments, certainly ones that made me audibly go "Holy crap, this art style", and the few bits of cutscenes make you wish there were more. The only real issue that I've only noticed later is the lack of shading which leads to some places feeling a bit too bright, and the use of 3D in the landscapes looking quite obviously that they were made in Unity engine can turn some off.With the art out of the way, does the game itself hold itself up without it? What about the story and more importantly, what about the gameplay?The story follows Crisbell, an orphan who through happenstance, gets her to meet a talking frog Matias, which through visiting the cathedral in her home village, gives her the power of time-bending, later meeting with compatriots who get sequenced into a journey to stop the upcoming assault by the Time Empress from taking over the world, it is pretty straight-forward but a few twists are added for engagement, it does however suffer from its own issues and plot holes that leave your head scratching but at the same time does have a few of its touching moments, it does leave a lot, I mean a lot to be desired.The characters I like, they put nice effort into making them distinct from one another, both visually and gameplay-wise. The voice-acting can range from hammy to rather powerful, altogether I'd evaluate it as good, and it helps with the dialogue and the banter between the party members. Speaking of the dialogue... the text in the game is littered with typos and some voice lines do not follow what's written, an egregious mistake for a finished product made even less excusable for a finished product that was delayed.The gameplay is turn-based RPG, part of the game being made as a love letter to JRPGs particularly from 4th generation consoles. It plays into an elemental rock-paper-scissors where if the enemy is fire, throw some water, etc. The added thing to the mix is Crisbell's main power, the time-bending, as enemies are shown in different forms and ages with their own abilities and weaknesses, of which breaking the time crystal could change the battleground and allow even for certain attacks to change. Theoretically, it leaves room for experimentation with the enemies, except that whether through gaining new powers through level progression, or the sheer lack of variety with (albeit well-designed) enemies, combat starts to get monotonous knowing exact strategy to wipe the floor without withstanding a single blow, with it, the time-bending power fades away into a simple gimmick. And considering how turn-based RPGs involve lots of grinding, the issues are doubled.Outside of combat, the game touts that what you do in the present can alter the future you see, it is satisfying to complete certain quests and see how the future vision changes to accommodate it, and it is moving to see cities deteriorate in the future when nothing's done, but it is unfortunately with its issues; the whole "choices matter" thing gets dashed really quickly after Narim, as completing all the side-quests gives you an option that fulfills both choices, rendering all the dilemmas around them meaningless. Not helping that the side-quests are thoroughly un-engaging, as all of them are fetch quests made to sink your time, an especially missed opportunity.The music is good, while upon further listening, it sounds like it was all done on a computer, but it pays a good homage to its inspirations and it fits with different places like a boot. Only issue is that it doesn't bode well on loop, which to be fair is true for almost all compositions.Conclusion:+: Art style, animation and design that makes Renaissance painters weep in joy, great characters, charming dialogue, good music, good voice-acting, some good story moments, nice title.-: Gameplay and combat starts well but gets monotonous, shallow execution of the central mechanic, side-quests have little worth, too many typos, glaring technical issues that I forgot to mention.With its strengths in design but weaknesses in technicality, Cris Tales I feel would have made a great animated film instead, it just does not seem like it started life as an RPG but something else. Giving a verdict to this turned out a lot harder in the end than I expected when I began the game. I really wanted it to be better than it actually turned out to be, and a bit embittered by that, yet at the same time, it charmed me through its art and the characters and the way the story went.It is with that in mind I went with recommending this game, as in "play it for the art", but if you're someone whose JRPGs are not your thing (RPGs I actually kind of despise playing), this won't change your mind in the slightest, as it inherits some of its... less liked attributes.P.S. While nearing the end of the game, I triggered a bug in St. Clarity's ruins that caused the game to soft-lock and unable to progress further, rendering my entire save hollow and having to start almost all over again through a backup save I saved near the end of chapter II. So hear from me, do not leave St. Clarity's ruins before deactivating the terminal before saving right before it. Oh and the 40€ price tag... no way.

_childDocuments_.review: Whew!!! That was a ride! Ok, the artstyle is gorgeous, the voice acting gets the point across wonderfully for my tastes, the time travel gimmick was well handled and I loved every single character (Except Willheim). Turn-based RPGs are my favorite genre and this one didn't dissapoint in that front, though the beguining with your characters without much options was a bit more of a slog than some others of the genre, but once you get your feet running the combat feels superv also there is a guard and strong attack mechanic where you press a button when a hit connects so that you recieve less or dish out more damage making the combat a bit more involved. There is a big problem I need to say, the pure white and bright loading screens have to go, there are too many of them and maybe it's my pc but they were also long, I haven't feel my eyes so tired after playing a game since the CRT days. And this is minor but I had a glitch where the quest log stopped recording my progress, I could still finish all side quests and could keep moving forward in the story normaly despite the quest log thinking I was still at the middle of the game and missed side quest.Now, not only I'm a weeb that loves turn based combat, I'm also an achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ and well to anyone that wants the blue ribbon please keep in mind that there are a LOT of missable achievements. I had a guide besides me and I kept at it, there is an achievement for getting all treasure chests in the game and there is a certain point in the story (like 16 hours in) where you can't go back for some them, ALL 10 side quests are missable if you finish the town's story line before finishing them you're bust, be careful about selling equipment pieces since there are some that aren't available in any shop so if you sold them that made you miss the achievement of having all pieces of equipment on your inventory and the one that got me making me restart the game when I was already 14 hours in  Making missable the "upgrade all weapons to the highest tear" achievement if you didn't upgrade that weapon. If you're going for all achievements a guide is a must, if you like unique artstyles please give this a chance, if you want something that you haven't seen before then this game was made in Colombia and is heavily influensed by it and I'm dang sure that isn't something common so then please give the game a chance if that interest you and if you're a fan of turn based RPGs then this one is just right.
