_childDocuments_.review: This games really good on paper, and hell the beginning is really good with how the volcano sisters make you actually use your time abilities, but after that it feels like those abilities feel like a flashy mechanic for the sake of continuity with the over worlds constant shoe horning in of that ability. The game outside of the starting section feels like a beta. with the fact that it has no animation for getting into random encounters, either make an animation for it, or make the enemies visible on the over world and make them chase you down Paper Mario style. For an example, the tar boss which i believe is the 3rd boss, i can tell there was meant to be a gimmick there, but there no point in getting rid of the tar pits since its not hindrance to you, along with the fact that, that boss can also soft lock your game... not a good look for a full release version of the game. To recap, the beginning is great but the rest feels incomplete for being a 1.0. The bosses gimmicks don't seem important enough to actually make the boss unique or challenging in anyway. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game very much. You need to pay attention to the stats, so you must examine it. In this game you need to have a skill to see the statistics, which is also I like. In the beginning of the game, you do not have such skills, and you just need to test and remember the vulnerabilities of the enemy and this is also very exciting.I like that all your actions in side quests affects the future. I spent only 2 tents during 2 runs of the game)You can heal your party members outside the fight and remove harmful conditions with your abilities.Every character has own skills, some skills are present in several characters, this is very useful, you can manage the party and change members with no harm.Each character has the personality, and the story. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying this game is good, but it definitely has some pacing and writing issues. None of the dialogue is cringy or too much, but it suffers from what feels like a lack of polish at the beginning. But at a certain point, the writing improves significantly things around you begin to fall into place and some elements of the world that were left fairly vague begin to make more sense. And ultimately that's what I believe Cris Tales largest weakness is in general, small lacks of polish here and there. One of the most jarring examples being no lead in to random encounters. The first time I entered a random encounter I didn't know if it was a scripted fight or if I had entered a load zone.That being said, the combat feels good, it's no Paper Mario and the Thousand Year Door, but when you learn the rhythm and the timings it's a lot of fun to mess around with. The time mechanic felt useful and interesting throughout the course of gameplay which was very refreshing when trying to determine the best strategies to fight through enemies. Overall this game gets a very solid recommendation from me, and I look forward to what the studio produces next.

_childDocuments_.review: A Colombian old-style JRPG with limited time manipulation.Visually this game is heavily stylized, inspired both by anime and latin-american art. It looks great. The animations are more basic, but it comes with using 2D sprites. Music is excellent, voice acting ranges from goot to a bit jarring in some side characters.From the gameplay perspective, this is classical JRPG. There is an overworld with no activity but passing between locations. There are cities where you can pick up quests, buy equipment and talk to people. Then there are combat zones, with random encounters and boss fights. The amount of random encounters is not excessive, but they can cause considerable attrition during early game. The fights themselves are turn based, with initiative of individual characters determined by their speed stat. There are physical and elemental attacks and resistances. And there are QTE - every attack of your characters can be boosted by well timed button press and a lot of enemy attacks can be parried or deflected in a similar way. Doing this may be critical during late boss fights. The time control mechanic that is one of the draws of the game can be used in the combat. Unfortunately, its utility drops sharply during the later half of the game. Add to that that lot of later bosses are completely immune to status effects and their fight can be repetetive slug fests. I strongly recommend that you learn to manipulate turn order, as it is crucial to be able to finish some of them, especially the final boss. Saving is limited to special save points in dungeons and cities, but it is free in the overworld. The story is fairly interesting, but do not expect any serious time paradoxes. The world runs on mix of magic and technology and rules of time travel bend to the needs of the story. Characters are interesting and well written. The game is supposed to have multiple endings, depending on resolution of situation in major cities. To achieve the best outcomes, you have to finish all sidequests in the area. This is unfortunately not tied in the story very well. On the bright side, point of no return for each these is reported beforehand.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played this game once on Xbox Gamepass. Got something like 20-40 hours into it, before it was taken off it. That said, normally when you put that much time into a game (or at least for me), it usually makes you want to see that time and effort reach fruition, or be rewarded. Instead, I logged on, saw it was removed off Gamepass and shrugged it off with a "Meh." It has interesting gameplay concepts and the art is unique, but that's all it's got going for it. The dialog and story in general feel... bland, and a bit cringe at times. Like a bad fanfic someone wrote, or the cringiest moments of RWBY. I don't really have a word to describe it at the moment. Honestly though, if that were all I had to complain about, I wouldn't care enough to write this out. My opinion on the story is subjective, and even if I didn't care enough for it, I wouldn't go out of my way to not recommend it. No, I only do that because it's just completely unplayable for me.I got this game as like a bonus (though not free) from a recent Humble Bundle. Didn't know it was included in the list, saw it and figured "Oh, well, I guess I own it now, I might as well see how it ends." That said, I couldn't even make it past the tutorial battle. Played it 6 times. There's supposed to be a brief cutscene following that fight, and the screen would transition to a white load screen with music, aaaand nothing. Tried looking it up. Not an entirely uncommon problem, but not really a solid fix for it. I saw somewhere that I needed some kind of codec packet you might need. Downloaded and installed that. Same result. Heard it might have to do with switching or turning off and on the controller? Again, same result. I tried looking in various forums, including the Steam ones, various other areas online, and even the developer's own Discord channel, within their own bug reporting section, MADE FOR THIS GAME. There are plenty of others reporting similar cases, but seemingly no response at all.In a last ditch effort, I had the idea to try to stream the game over GeForce Now, using Nvidia's systems. Maybe their configuration was better or maybe their setup just had whatever mine didn't. As an aside, I'm running a 3080, the game loading from an M2 SSD, and even when I get the game to work, the game's performance feels as sluggish at times as Pokemon Scarlet or Violet does running on a Switch. Not even 4k, but 1080p. Anyways, once I made it through the queue (as a free user), the game loaded, and to my surprise, I WAS able to make it past the intro and eventually save. I thought that would be the end of my troubles, but no, as it turns out, this bug occurs at EVERY one of these kinds of cutscenes with my PC. And there are more than I originally remembered. Enough, that when coupled with lackluster story/dialogue, GeForce queues (and with limited time sessions and my crappy internet speeds), and no communication, let alone any sign of an update, from the developer at all in over a year, just make this not worth it at all. Just hot garbage.TLDR; Bad performance, silence from devs, no patches and limited workarounds. Add that to what I consider a mediocre story with cringe dialogue and this game is just a pain to deal with. Not worth the time, money, or frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an engaging game!I've only just started so far, but I still wanted to get some knowledge out to anyone who's thinking about buying this!  Hopefully I'll remember to update this review as I keep playing.First off, the game immediately looks amazing.  The visuals are all colorful and beautiful, and it's fun to explore the sort of 2.5D world.  The music is nice too, and there's voice acting for almost every line of dialogue, so the environment feels pretty fleshed out.As for the gameplay, it's definitely interesting since it's takes a spin on the usual RPG turn based battles.  It allows you to mess with the past and future in order to weaken your opponents, and so when combined with an array of skills, helps to add a layer of puzzles and complexity to the battles.  I'll have to see whether it escapes the usual trope of just pressing "fight" as I continue to play, however.  In an attempt to escape this, you have the ability to perform a quick time event and try to either parry an enemies attack or make your own stronger.  Unfortunately, the timing on these events isn't super well illustrated, so it can be frustrating to learn when to click at first.  Nonetheless, it still succeeds in giving you something other to do than wait until it's your turn to attack.One thing that is really cool is how the time powers interact with the regular world.  As you move around, you get to see the past, present, and future versions of whatever place your in.  However, they're all shown to you at once, which, contradictory to how it sounds, makes it less confusing to see into these different time periods than if you had to switch back and force.  Plus, it makes for some fantastic visual storytelling as you get to see the different areas' stories unfold.The last thing I want to touch on since I've seen many other people mention it in their reviews is that the intro is kind of shaky.  I would agree with this, since it definitely is a bit confusing at first.  It throws you into a cutscene (that is super cool) right after opening the game, which seems like it's trying to hype you up, but it's pretty easy to get lost in all of the ideas it throws at you.  Then right after you actually start a save file, you're thrown into a battle straight away without any introduction to the characters or the mechanics.  Luckily, it's fairly easy to ride along until the game throws you into a flashback that serves as a tutorial and backstory for the aforementioned battle.  Overall, the opening wasn't a game breaker for me, but it probably could have been handled better. Overall, I wouldn't say that it had the best start of any game I've ever played, but it's definitely got me interested enough that I'm excited to keep playing!  Then again, I'm not super hard to please when it comes to most things, so maybe this is just me.  Still, if you like story driven RPGs, this will definitely hold your attention!  I hope this reviews helps you in your decision of choosing whether this game is right for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Lost in time itself.This game has a great start, one where you feel like you can play it over and over again, but as you get towards the end, you may want to cast Regression on yourself to understand what may have went wrong. That is not to say this game is bad, but the design of it is what makes this a challenge to enjoy. First, let's highlight the great things that this game has...1) Love Letter to JRPGsThis holds true in many aspects from music, art, gameplay, and storyline. Simple, engaging, memorable2) Unique charactersEvery character has a play style that is completely unique. From support to all out damage (magic or physical) with a mixture of random attacks and monster skill attacks (blue mage of Final Fantasy series)3) Voice lines for all NPCsThis is rare to see, but the team did put a lot into this.Now on to the faults of this game. As memorable as this game can become, so can its faults especially when it ruins an experience.1) Mismatching dialogue and voice lines (also some spelling mistakes)While minor, I am a stickler for this. Please review your entire story to avoid having memorable mistakes like this.2) Game-breaking bugsSome magic spells completely ruin the game (you can find this in their discord). Equipments will 'degrade' a character over time if they have negative status effects and other items that ruin the experience overall.3) AchievementsIf you are going for the 100% achievement, you will need to prepare multiple save files as you will need the best scenario for the 'perfect' end, and you will need to make some bad choices to make monsters available to complete the achievement (this is a reported bug). You can say this goes with 2, but if you're that hungry for achievements, this is what you will need to do.4) Side questsThis is perhaps amongst the worst. Needed for the achievement and 'best' ending (I don't think there's really anything to it). You even get a tutorial to know there's a side quest but there are backgrounds that blend into the icon making it hard to know if it is a quest. You need to make that deduction that because it's not an item you can consume or equip, it's meant for a quest. I know, you can say 'duh', but it's easy to miss sidequests because the icon is simply not there let alone not everybody wants to spend time memorising all NPC namesI would think that with a time game like this, you would have new game + (saw it in a screenshot), but apparently it does not exist. Simply having this would solve a lot of stuff, but I suppose it has been overlooked. I was looking to replay this again after messing up a story arc, but now I will have to wait for that Future crystal to show me that this game will be enjoyable. There are a lot of elements in this game that can be made better with both fixes and DLC, but as it stands, I can only recommend this if you are OK with moving on with mistakes that you are completely not at fault for.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales was a very fun experience my first time playing, up until late game at least.And I'll try to keep this spoiler free for the most part for people looking to purchase this game.I don't mind the loading times at all, really. What bothers me is that the time mechanic had barely any reason to be used in battle late game. Eventually they just stopped adding different forms for some people, which makes sense when it comes to time empress I guess because no spoilies and all that, but some regular enemies just have one form which is kind of annoying. There are also some status effects that are hardly used, "Doom" is a great example of this. From what I've heard it kills the victim in three turns unless it's a boss, however I only got this status effect put on me once in one of the end game ruin dungeons, and I never had any reason to put doom on someone else because I would always kill them in three turns or less anyways. Another thing I dislike is that if you miss the chance then you can't get the achievement for getting all weapons maxed out, which ended up being a big issue for me. I liked The Empress plot twist, that does make sense and it was quite clever, but I don't like how near those times they also have story elements that force you to redo things, it was kind of annoying. And the final boss also was annoying because of his classic magic increase combo that just kills you if you missed a parry, and don't even get me started on the fire one because I'm not even sure you can stop that, I never deflected or parried it. Those are the biggest flaws in my opinion, the only other one I can recall is a bug where I couldn't bring out Matias in Wilhelm's house. On to the positives, the concept and world development is great and the characters are quite likeable, although very corny at times. I wish that some spells had more reason to be used, like why use Segnitas when you could just use Celeritas but hey, if they give me a busted spell I'm gonna use it. The character design is fantastic, especially for the mother superiors. Even though the final boss was annoying, I liked how strategy-based you could make it. The soundtrack is phenomenal as well, very intense. For the most part the voice acting was very well done, however there were sometimes where I got lost because of the way they delivered lines and had to read it over a few times. I think if you wanted to up the difficulty a bit, Zas' wheel is a bit slow and easy to time, but maybe that was intentional. The cut scenes were beautiful, but somewhat choppy at times. Overall this game was pretty good, maybe an 8/10, it's definitely better while playing it than thinking back on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I've played it twice though already. Here is my breakdown:What I love:-The Main Characters: I love just about every character in this game, even many of the villans. They are interesting, dynamic and just have fun interactions with each other.-Critical hits/Parries: Rather than having critical hits be rng based, it allows you to deal them if you time your second strike correctly. Same on defense, if you block with the right timing you can severely reduce damage. Its fun to practice and learn the timing-The Art: I love the style and atmosphere of the game. Its clear a lot of love and attention went into each location, character, and monster.-The sound track. Its just really goodWhat I like:-The story: It is a good story with interesting twists and turns. There are some questions that are brought up and never answered though. -Time mechanics in battle: It can be fascinating to see the older/younger versions of each character, and also fun to combine your time powers with the other characters, though it becomes less useful in late game where most enemies are unaffected by them.What I dislike:-It takes a while for some side quests to become available in some areas, which is fine, but it can be unclear when exactly they ARE available and often require a lot of running back and forth. Still this is a minor issue as it will warn you when the cut off point for completing side quests is so you have a chance to go back and double check.-some of the side character voice acting and line reads are pretty bad, though most are fine-Quite a few typos in descriptions, sometimes even switching between she/him within the same description-Occasionally, what the text box says and what the voice actor says don't match up.What I hate:-For two whole dungeons and two bosses, you are forced to have a character for whom ALL of her attacks are rng based. Her basic attack is okay sometimes, Her physical attack skills have a chance of hitting you, and since many enemies (including both bosses) heal when hit with fire, her magic has a 25% chance of HEALING these enemies. This is the only area where you are forced to use the new character, and while I can see wanting to make the player learn the new character, 2/3rds of the dungeons and bosses in the area is a bit much. First play through I actually had an easier time fighting the bosses by just letting her die and stay dead for the fight. I hate it. But its a relatively small part of the game, and does not make me hate the game as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales is an RPG that presents a nice story, melodious soundtrack, and brilliant artwork!Not only that, it brings a new perspective to the genre!But there are some things that just cannot be overlooked, follow this review and find out!The story feels like following a fairy tale book. We play the role of Crisbell, an orphan, who finds out she has time mage powers and decides to use them to help the world. There is a war going on and the evil Time Empress wants to rule all kingdoms!It is a mainstream story for RPGs, but the developers do make it engaging with neat turns and interesting companions. The newly added time mechanics truly add to the story when your quests alter the possibilities in the future.The dialogues and the script are very well written, and most parts include incredible voice acting performances.There is a gigantic problem with the story though... and the problem with the story is not the story... it is the pace of the game! The pace is too slow and drags down taking away from the story. The streamlined back and forth makes the player lose interest in the actual story...The game plays nice, but the gameplay is a big issue...The time mechanics are interesting and combine well with other magics, but they end up being nothing more than a useless gimmick. The basics for winning battles are stalling and constant recovering.This is one of the most frustrating parts, because the combination of time and magic mechanics introduced was an outstanding fresh intake to the genre!Instead, you have to be prepared to fight swarms of enemies in small areas in a cheap tactic to make the game lengthier. Especially in the beginning, when you will have to recover constantly, because enemies are faster and attack before you even have the chance to flee. A full party of enemies may explode at first turn, stopping you from recovering in battle at all.And then get ready to walk through gigantic areas with barely any enemy.The mix of battles and story is not well balanced. The player will get bored from lengthy story parts and then bored of walking long distances and then bored of fighting flocks of enemies...Apart from the pace, be ready to deal with massive hand-holding followed by missed essential tutorials or guidance.The hint button is there, but you will be forced to read every instruction and direction multiple times. Just to give one example: You go from one city to the time mage's house and there the time mage will point out that you can use your magic to make a seed turn into a tree by using your future magic. He will show you the ground mark where you can plant a seed. There will be a seed on the floor, but you will not be able to get it yet. Then you go back to the city and the path will be blocked. The frog pops up and tells you that you may be able to find an alternative way. Walk a little and you will see a ground mark, then the frog dialogue pops up again and he will tell you that you can plant a seed there to climb the tree and enter, so you should go back to the time mage's house to get the seed. When you get back to the time mage’s house, the dialogue pops up again and they say: look, a seed, maybe we can plant it to get in back in the city, grab that seed and head back to the city. After grabbing the seed and going back, another dialogue: look, let’s plant the seed in this ground mark. All unskippable dialogue!Meanwhile, the game will not explain that during battle you can only use future magic to your right and past magic to your left. You can turn the character to either side, but this right and left constraint is fixed to the player’s perspective and will not change.Another issue in battles is that the turns shift too quickly, so many times you won’t even be able to realize which enemy is attacking who before they do, which hinders your ability to block.To make matters worse, the block defense timing is unclear and fails often. The animations are too subtle and the hit detection is not on point.Apart from battles, there are a few bad design decisions that take away from the experience.To give an example:There is a side quest to collect special flowers, but this quest only starts at a certain point. You will be able to see the flowers flashing when you pass by, but it is not possible to collect them until the quest starts. And then you have to go back to the same places just to collect those flowers you already saw, but was not able to collect before.All this back and forth is very time consuming considering that it takes a long while to go from one place to the other. There is no run or teleport.And then you get some bad guidance that may hinder you progress, like: The path is blocked, we need to go to the West. So you go to the West part of the city and nothing happens. From there you get out of the city and try to enter the city from the outer West part to no avail. The next move is to go West of the map, right? Wrong, it was actually to go to the left of the blocked gate... which isn’t really in the West part of the city...There is also a missed opportunity within the game. At some point one of your characters learns to scan the enemies, which will allow you to analyze their stats, strengths and weaknesses (in the past, present and future). This is really neat and could be coupled with a scan database book to enable a collection aspect to the game.Which brings us to another part to point out about the game: there are just a few open world enemy sprites that get recycled with different colors. It is understandable given how much storage the graphics and voice acting must take, but it would be nice to see some more variety.Moving back to the fundamentals, the player cannot save from anywhere. There are fixed save points when exploring cities and dungeons, which is a terrible choice given that you will face your battles and progress the story in these areas.Lastly, this game needs more save slots. Or else it needs to implement fixed save states to return to. There are some events that can only take place depending on your choices at specific points. Having to replay everything with unskippable dialogues just to get an achievement or a few different dialogue boxes is a terrible choice!Doing the research, the devs have been improving the game since release, so I hope this review can shed some light on how to improve the gameplay mechanics. The game was developed with love by an indie studio and some parts of it are masterpieces.The audio is really good and the voice acting is superb!The visuals are on another level. Artistic, beautiful, terrific blend of colors, past, present and future! Ambience, dialogues and cutscenes are all masterpieces! It really takes you inside of a fairy tale book!Cris Tales feels like a masterpiece that should have been, but ended up falling short in multiple core aspects.The pace does not work well and turns what should have been an awesome experience into a boring one.The battles do not take advantage of the new mechanics and end up being bland and unappealing.Last, but not least, the game misses every possible target audience. The age rating removes kids from the audience. The slow pace and dragged battles are an obstacle to regular players. Meanwhile, the slow pace, hand-holding and lackluster battles drive away more seasoned RPG players.Even though these are major flaws, if devs are willing, there are still ways to resolve them with updates without having to re-write the whole game from scratch. The story is well written, the soundtrack and voice acting are engaging, and the art is superb!Time to beat: 37.8hRating: 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time overall with the game, but I also see how rough it is in some places and how that can turn people off.Let's start with the combat system: you fight enemies on both sides and can send the ones on the left to the past and the ones on the right to the future, changing their stats and abilities.It's a neat system, but I'm a bit disappointed with how it handles status effects: the first thing you learn is that sending Soaked enemies into the future turns their defense down, since they rust. It's fine, but that's the only status effect that interacts with time because every other status just gets removed instead. Sure, various party members have abilities that have different effects depending on the time period, but still.It doesn't help that Some skills also seem to lack sound effects in certain cases.The visuals are pretty nice and probably the best part of the game. I also liked how the characters in the party were nice to each other, with no heavy dramas between them.I don't have much to say about the dungeons: they aren't long and have some light puzzles. Later on you get the ability to repair or break certain objects, but such puzzles are still pretty simple.The first half of the game is probably the best part: you get new abilities and party members, see new places and enemies, all the good stuff.The later half, however, screams "We finished our budget/We have no more time" due to how it's set up: without spoiling too much, the game makes you backtrack through old dungeons to open new paths, beat a boss and get the Mcguffin you're searching for. Rinse and repeat four times. What's disappointing is that the game recycles old bosses without adding anything new.After this, you go to fight a boss... and backtrack to an area again to enter a small dungeon, now with exposition, with a recycled boss fight at the end. Rinse and repeat four times.To be fair, the dungeons add a new puzzle or two and only half of the bosses are recycled in this case.I've also had a game-breaking bug at one point: when you are in Neva Tulira and have to go to a dungeon to get pieces of a thing,  If you do, you'll face a boss earlier than intended and your Quest Log will become unselectable!There are also some rough edges here and there: first, Save menus are kinda inconsistent: the first one you see is "Save-Rest-Back", but then they become "Rest-Save-Back" for most of the game. At a certain point, one will be "Back-Save-Rest" and the remaining one "Save-Rest-Back". It's a small thing, but it did stand out for me.Some skill descriptions are kinda inaccurate, either the menu or the battle ones. (e.g. A skill says in battle that it can heal enemies, but it actually doesn't)In battle, the game darkens the screen for a second when you have to press Z for a timed attack/defense. This is oddly absent in a couple places.Now, why do I recommend the game despite all the issues above? Well... I had fun with it, despite the low points, and the music is nice too, especially the battle tracks.If you can gloss over the various rough edges, you might have a decent time with this little tribute to JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, but I understand why this game is not to everyone's liking. The soundtrack and art style are the best part of the game. The gameplay outside of battle is nice having to go into the past and future to complete task to get better endings for the regions. However the way the camera is angle just makes it really wonky at times as some parts are not visible without you having to walk in the dark, sometimes you can find a chest sometimes you find absolutely nothing wasting your time. There's no real exploration in the game either most of the chest are visible and they just make you walk back and forth specially in the forge. The worst offender this game has is the combat, yes you have that unique ability to go into the past and future within combat which affects enemies and some bosses, but for 99% it either is not necessary or doesn't do anything, since you can just one shot most of the enemies instead of wasting a turn using the crystal. There's only about 2 bosses that truly get affected by using the time crystal. Outside of that the combat just lacks, it feels boring as enemies just feel like sandbags, they just take up your time. Some enemies do have dumb gimmicks such as kamikaze which just goes to show how much of a sandbag the enemies really are, as the kamikaze function is only really dangerous in the Colosseum due to the status effects it leaves. But even then it's relatively easy to win. The story is mediocre, they try fixing it with the extra content with Adri which gave us a better true ending, but it's still a pretty forgettable story. I would only recommend to get it while it's on discount or if you can find a key for cheap, at most this game is worth $20

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Cris Tales and it was a good experience playing the game. It fell short in a few areas but overall it's a good experience that's beginner friendly and has an innovative take on time travel powers.The characters, from the main cast to the minor background people and the villains all have personality. It's fun seeing characters interact or seeing the villains with strong motivations. It really gives you the feeling that it's a world you're trying to save, and not just a bunch of static characters.The time mechanics in this game are fun to use and it's creative. You jump to the past to hear conversations from people who aren't alive anymore or jump to the future to get the immediate result of years of research. Problem solving is fun and it really does feel like you're using your powers in a smart way.Combat is also enjoyable because you can come up with a number of cool strategies to take down opponents. Even boss fights are less about high levels and more about having proper strategy to win.This isn't a hard game and you don't have to grind. It's a good beginner's game.That being said, this game does have some notable flaws. The premise is great but the welcome wears thin after a while. There are some good moments in the story but by the end of the game you can feel fatigued because the charm's worn off and you're just doing what feels like game padding.The game is simple, but often really simple. Some of the fun mechanics stop being used and you're able to one-shot your way through enemy groups.There are also a few bugs (like the Quest Log suddenly becoming inaccessible for no reason) that should be addressed at some point.I'd give this game a 7/10. It is a good experience, but not great. The developers tried some things and they really paid off, but in other areas it didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is an edit from someone that first played the game in its demo and then played the game on its release date.  The review was edited to 1). Help people looking into this game if its for them) 2). Update my review to remain concurrent with the current patch) 3). Become more clear to assist in both numbers 1 and 2) 4).Although I had a great time playing this game when it first launched, a considerably large amount of people were upset with its lack of settings, bugs, and general imbalance.  The new patch seems to have fixed some of these issues leaving the game in a much more playable stateCris Tales does not pioneer much when it comes to Role Playing Games (RPGs).  The game is very linear where you move from one area to another, with each area having something unique about them.  At every area there is always at least one dungeon and one town.  A dungeon will have enemies that you will to beat with usually a boss or two in said dungeon.  You will spend a majority of your time in the town, buying items, talking to npcs (which are all voice acted), completing side quests, and progressing the main quest.  However, what makes Cris Tales unique among the RPG genre is its unique mechanic to see in the past, the present, and the future.  This mechanic allows you to see in real time how your quests and your choices affect the future.  This mechanic is used exceptionally well in all towns where you can see someone's bright or dark future.  This (at least for me) is what made side quests particularly interesting as I would see in real time someone's fate change for the better.I will not lie, the majority of the cast remains static and are your boring heroic stereotypes.  There are some exceptions, but they don't enter your party until much later into the game.  I've also read complaints about one character being an "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥"; however, I never felt this way with him simply because the other two characters were so boring that it was somewhat refreshing to actual hear some amount of humor, even if it was just making fun of what they said.  Now for the good.  There is one character in particular that upon joining the party he/she just is a breath of fresh air.  He/She is MUCH more unique then the rest of your party members and I always loved his/her humor as it was genuinely funny most of the time.The combat is very exciting and unique in the beginning (due to the player being able to put enemies into either the past or the future), but becomes less intricate the longer you play as it just becomes easier to simply, "hit the bad guys until they die" then actually use the mechanics in place.  The combat also requires the use of quick time events (QTE) to both deal and defend against damage.  Although I personally liked the use of QTEs as they added another thing I can control (instead of it being random) and therefore master, if you are exceptionally good at learning timings then it will become incredibly boring and easy; however, if you are terrible at timing specific actions the game will become incredibly difficult due to you simply dealing less and taking more damage.After the new patch it seems that a very big complaint I had with the game has gone away; however, since I have not gone through to see if there are any more large bugs I can't comment if there are still any.  If the patch notes are to believed then it is now possible to 100% the game (which was impossible before).  There should be considerably less, even maybe no spelling errors and no incorrect text (Though that is being hopeful).  Certain fights should now be considerably less tedious as well, which is a nice change.  They also added a couple of new settings and adjusted the balance of some items to make them more viable during gameplay.As I stated earlier, a considerable amount of the cast is quite boring and none change throughout the story.  To add on to that, many of the npcs are completely forgettable (I can't remember a single npcs name).  Many people have also complained about a lack of enemy types in the game, although it is true that there are not a lot of different enemies (slightly different models or recolors) I was never bothered by the lack of variety.  A major issue I encountered while near the end of the game is the voice acting.  It wasn't inherently bad, but there would be times where the voice lines would switch to a noticeably worse quality.  The worst about the quality switch is that it would happen constantly during that characters dialogue.  Thankfully, the issue is short lived but definitely takes you out the experience.  The biggest issue plaguing this game right now has to be the lack of settings and the game's controls.  Based on the newest patch notes you have volume settings, aspect ratio settings, and vSync settings.  That is it.  The settings options in this game is atrocious.  You can't even change your keybinds.  Although a lack of options never impacted my gameplay.  You better like the controls of this game (z for interact, x for cancel, arrow keys for movement) because you don't get an option to change them.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend giving this game a good play through as it is an RPG I really like, however I will say to not get it if you are not a fan of JRPGs. The early game is Tough, as the parry mechanic will be the only way to mitigate damage you intake as your defense stats are not up to par with the attack of some enemies. Once you get through the first couple bosses though, the rest of the game is easy, excluding final boss. The music for this game is fantastic and I plan to use a lot of it for my own DnD campaigns, and the time based mechanics are really well done. Plus you don’t need to grind in this game at least from my blind play through. This game is nowhere near perfect though and has quite a few things holding it back. There are a couple of softlocks in the game that can be annoying, but usually the game is generous enough to give save points right before bosses for every boss. The major downside to the game is that the quest design is not very good, as every area is essentially a point of no return. Meaning in order to get the “best” ending, you have to do every side quest possible and most side quests are usually towards the end of an area, making it a bit annoying to do them. The other unfortunate thing is that the endings are barely different depending on what you pick story wise, so the only reason to make a second play through is to get every achievement. Combine that with no new game+ and the game falters a bit. The game is amazing for its world building, music, characters, and gameplay mechanics but falls short on its pacing and lack of meaningful decisions. I would say that this game is a 7/10 and would hope that more games like this become more fleshed out and made.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales is one of the most beautiful JRPGs I’ve ever played, artistically and musically, but it is certainly not without its flaws.  So, let’s run through 5 things you need to know in 5 minutes (or read at your own pace below). *For those questioning my playtime, I had to play on an alt account due to some pre-order confusion.Watch my 5 minute review here: Ornate Art Style-Cris Tales shines with a brilliant ornate art style.  I kept going back and forth over adjectives to describe the world.  It’s pretty, it’s smooth, it’s sexy, but I settled on ornate due to the abundance of intricacies.  The buildings and landscapes are layers upon layers of 2.5D beauty, all drawn in a sort of vector style.  The color combinations and themes are so satisfying, the character animations silky smooth.  I felt like I always had something to gawk at wherever I was walking around, and there are so many details in the background scenery to add to this wonderful world.  The creatures you’ll fight against, and their past, present, and future versions (we’ll talk more about that later) are unique, and all characters in battle will start to show their own signs of wear when taking damage, and celebrate in their own way upon a victory too.No Graphical Settings-With all my adulation of the art and graphics, you probably thought I would move onto another category entirely, but I cannot review Cris Tales without mentioning its utter lack of any graphical settings.  You cannot change the resolution, there are no quality sliders, there’s not even an option to play windowed or full-screen.  Thankfully, it seems as though it plays standard in a windowed full-screen mode, but having no graphical options, in an indie game which costs $40, seems like the largest oversight.  It’s like buying a car, but it doesn’t come with a steering wheel.  Sure you can still drive it, but you have no idea what you’re getting yourself into, or if you can even handle it.  Catch my drift?  Minimum, you need to be able to change the resolution.  I hope we’ll see this implemented in an update as soon as possible.Excellent Soundtrack-Back to the things that I love about Cris Tales, the soundtrack is nostalgic but also fresh.  With its use of piano, violin, flute, and others, the orchestral themes will sound familiar to you long-time fans of JRPGs, but not to the point of copying any specific game.  The composer Tyson Wernli said he grew up listening to Nobuo Uematsu and Koji Kondo, and you can clearly hear those legendary inspirations shining through in Cris Tales.  In no time at all, I found myself humming to the tunes as I walked around the large cities and forests.  The soundtrack changes drastically when you enter a battle scene, switching to a faster pace, and also when you change locations, you’ll notice the flavor of the music changes too.  In the second city you’ll encounter on Crisbell’s journey, the scenery and music turn to a sort of Spanish theme, using acoustic guitar, flute, and tambourine to set the scene musically.  This will surely be a soundtrack that I listen to outside of the game.Standard JRPG StructureFourthly, Cris Tales is built on a standard JRPG structure.  Crisbell, the time mage and main character of the game, is a child of prophecy, as you’ll quickly learn in the early moments of the game.  She will meet some friends on her journey, some will stay, some will leave, some will leave and then come back later because that’s just how JRPG friends are.  There is an overworld to explore, and when not in the overworld or cities, you will randomly encounter enemies.  Battles are turn-based, using elements and the past, present, and future time windows to manipulate the age of your enemies, and also the potency of certain effects that you can apply.  You can’t change your party, you just accept whoever’s there and ready to fight with you, but there are times when you can set up tents and rest, during which you can chat with and get to know your comrades a little better.  The one major difference from JRPGs I’ve played is that you can complete side quests (stay with me) in order to change later decisions and options.  For instance, in the second city, you can find three side quests, and each one you complete will give you more options as to who takes over control of the town once you eliminate the not-so-hidden fake-ally opponent.  This not only adds incentive to completing side quests, which I never need, but it also gives you impactful choices should you choose to complete the side quests, which I think is uncommon in the traditional JRPG sense.Dumbed Down Time Travel-The last thing you need to know is that the super cool time travel mechanic is dumbed down  beyond reason.  This is probably the biggest kicker of the game for me, in that the game holds your hand for a lot of things.  The mechanic of having all three time frames - past, present, and future - on-screen simultaneously is ingenious, and many quests rely on this feature.  But instead of being something for you to use cleverly and investigate with, things are instead highlighted with a certain symbol when you see them that alerts you to send Matias the frog into that dimension, or one of your party members will blatantly tell you to do that.  This could have been something that added so much replayability to the game, finding little secrets or quests that you missed the first go-around, but sadly, almost everything is handed to you.  It’s not just the time travel though.  At one point, I walked into an open underground cavern, where there was a closed gate, and a mounted lever standing in the middle of the room, and nothing else in sight.  A character actually says “it looks like we need to find a lever that opens this gate”.  Hmm, no kidding!  I understand that the game doesn’t want players to feel held back by not knowing what to do, and that has been a complaint of mine in the past concerning other games, but there has to be some middle ground between being blind in the dark, and your friend Captain Obvious pointing out every next move.  The time manipulation in the battle sequences is really fun and interesting though, in that you can, say, poison enemies, and then send them to the future where the poison has taken full effect, and some other fun combinations of the like that you’ll unlock over time.If you like JRPGs, you’ll probably really enjoy this as it is a refreshing take on the genre.  Gameplay-wise though, it’s pretty standard after several hours, although there are always new people to meet, items to find, and quests to explore.  If you’re not a JRPG fan, Cris Tales probably isn’t going to turn you into one, simple as that.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don’t write reviews, but I feel compelled to defend this game after playing over 100 hours, completing the game 2.5 times, and earning 80% of the achievements: This game brought fond memories of the turn-based RPGs I played in the 90’s as a child.  It has been a long time since I had that child-like wonder for a video game.  From my perspective, CrisTales is made for 80’s babies who have been drowning in the ocean of early access roguelites and hack-n-slash ARPGs.  I am disappointed, but not surprised, that this game has mixed reviews. If you’re into rogue-lites or think hack-n-slash nature of Final Fantasy Remake is better than the turn-based combat original, then – newsflash - CrisTales ain’t made for you.I thought the story and writing was phenomenal and, at times, moving and emotional. I sincerely hope the developers won’t let the haters prevent them from pursuing a much-needed sequel or other projects.  CrisTales is an exceptional game with good writing, gorgeous art style, and excellent voice acting (the voice actor for Crisbell was particularly good).    Representation matters.  I loved the inclusion of Spanish heritage and culture in the game.  I also liked there were black and brown NPCs in the game.  However, given that the producers and writers of CrisTales were people of color, it was a missed opportunity for not having a person of color in the party.  While Christopher inferred to be  POC, there isn’t one party member who doesn’t pass the paper bag test (if you don’t know what the “paper bag test” is, google it).   As a POC who enjoys these games, I was disappointed that there was no black or brown characters to play.There are some minor spelling/dialogue errors in the end part of the game as well as sporadic crashes during boss battles.   I thought combat was good though I rarely used the time crystal.  For me, this was OK, since I preferred to brute-force attack to kill enemies; however, I would have liked to a tad bit more combos for the time crystal.  While I think CrisTales could have gone through a bit more playtesting before release, I think the final product is excellent and worthy of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: Vanilla JRPG with some fun gimmicks. I enjoy the lead character being a support rather than a generalist or bruiser, but still becoming stupidly strong by the late game through time-themed support abilities. It's far from ideal; there are no real puzzles to speak of despite your time manipulation powers creating the opportunity for such. There are fun time gimmicks in battles, but it still boils down to competent but cookie-cutter JRPG.The music is a 9/10, from the different town themes to the battle tracks that change moderately over time as not to become stale. The music is excellent.The 2D artwork is a full 10/10; there really isn't another game out there that looks like this, and it's gorgeous to look at from start to finish. Towns and enemies being split into past, present and future versions of themselves adds even more of said gorgeous artwork.The story started out as a 6/10 for me. A lot of important things go unexplained in the beginning; why is Crisbell the Chosen One? Where did her powers come from? Why is there a talking frog? But by the end it jumped to 8/10 when there was a good explanation and payoff for all of it.This game is a decent JRPG and an amazing art gallery.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like RWBY's and Netflix' She Ra's best moments, you can see Cris Tales was written for women by women, and I welcome this refreshing point of view in narrative. All those Dungeons and Dragons' detractors that keep trying to twist the game in pretzels trying to "fix it"? Cris Tales shows you the right way to do it. Furthermore, if you look past all the frilly storybook visuals, you'll see that, just like Shoujo Manga, Cris Tales tackles some hard topics without flinching.Also, any writing that involves time travel shenanigans requires some  to do it right, the kind of writing that, like writing Superman, only a few have the skill to do it right, and Cris Tales does it.Gameplay-wise, Cris Tales is a pre-dork age JRPG (the ones that still had a world map and otherwise the "illusion of choice") writ small, but that didn't keep me from squeezing a nice 52 hours of fun out of this game, and it's fun enough with novel mechanics.Finally, the music is rather homogeneous in tone kinda the way Constantine's music score was, but it's still good music and accomplishes its purpose.Play it if you can. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game so much. I adore turn-based JRPGs, they're my favorite genre of game and it really upsets me when other gamers crap on them and/or talk about how its a "dead" genre, bc it totally isn't. It may not be mainstream anymore, but it's still a very fun genre of game to play and some of the best and most influential games of all time belong to it. You CANNOT deny its influence, even if you have a distaste for turn-based gameplay.That being said...this game is incredibly mediocre and underwhelming.I like the music, art style, and the voice acting, but everything else is just bleh. Execution of the story from what little I played is just...lazy. Its very generic chosen one stuff with your typical "flesh out party member X by showing their hometown and their struggles with their parents, family, and fellow townspeople" subplots sprinkled throughout. In good turn based JRPGs this trope is written well enough to let you forget that, but here...yeah not really it just comes off as genericThe battle system is painfully dull, and the time mechanics are shallow and surface level at best. Really just seems like a gimmick as opposed to anything new or innovative. Combat has its moments every now and then, but honestly I just found battling a chore, which is NOT a good feeling to have in an RPG like this where that's like, the entire point.Even little things that I would normally be able to forgive in a much better game (poor translation of the subtitles, unskippable character dialogue that happens every single time you wanna save or use healing spells outside of battle or etc, high encounter rate, random difficulty spikes) bother me immensely with this one because the basic act of battling just isn't fun and the story and characters aren't engaging.It really pains me to trash this game, I was so hyped and SO ready to jump to its defense after its initial reception was mixed to negative, but every time I try to pick it back up again, I just feel...bored. And disappointed. I've played FAR worse, don't get me wrong, but like...it's just really mediocre. This game had potential, it just didn't live up to it imo. Maybe it gets better once you get past the opening slog, but tbh I just find it too boring to power through. Just skip this one and go back to FF7 or Chrono Cross.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a middle option for recommending this game, I would choose it. There is so much good and heartwarming stuff in this game. No, I'm serious, despite all of its flaws I really love it. But since I can't pick that option...I am glad I got this game for 4 bucks. In my personal opinion, this game is not worth what it is being sold for. When I saw the trailer in 6th grade, I was amazed to see the different systems and gimmicks used in the game as I was watching the trailer. Now as a teenager...meh. As a little indie game, it can somewhat stand on its own. It has cool things such as voice acting, a clean and functional UI, an amazing art style, and some sweet tunes (I like the music a lot more than I say). Other than that it then becomes a dry game, attempting to replicate classic JRPGs while leaving all the things that make those games feel old (The story is somewhat memorable though).Chrono Trigger a game made in 1995 is also based on time and it is much better than this will ever be. The characters are all somewhat interesting, all of them are unfortunately subpar to some of the other great characters in other RPGs. The only thing that kind of makes up for this is the fact that in battle all the characters work in different ways, which is always appreciated. Battles and the characters are all pretty basic but good enough for my liking. The voice acting - which is entirely good - is sometimes unbalanced with the music in the background (I don't know if that is just a me problem). The game has this gimmick in which your frog friend - Matias - can travel through the past, present, and future and can observe problems that the main character - Crisbel - can fix in the present. This does nothing for the game and does not affect anything. I am so serious, this literally does nothing for the story at all which is so sad (I mean I guess it gives you the TRUE TRUE ENDING, I have YouTube though, and before the update of the game, it was never shown anyway). To finish off my complaints, the maps are big and deserve a run button to traverse them (can be debated though) and this game, for one of the strangest reasons, has abysmal loading times. I don't know why, again it's probably just a me problem. Pokemon has cleaner transitions than this game. Not everything has to have a loading screen to progress through scenes or battles. Either that or it just cuts to the next scene. The only pseudo-transition they have is where you pause in battle and it says, "Time has stopped its natural flow!" Lastly, this game needs more cutscenes. Some of the "fights" or emotional moments are very poorly conveyed using the in-game text boxes. This game has SOOOO MUCH POTENTIAL, and as indie developers, they had tons of time to do something about it. The game is just under the bar. If you want a really nice indie RPG though, I highly suggest Bug Fables or Sea of Stars. I am 99% sure you will be satisfied with either of those.

_childDocuments_.review: Cris Tales is an ode to an bygone era of turn based RPGs, with some modern flare to keep things interesting, set in a gorgeous world with a fitting story. If you've been missing that type of game, I'd recommend Cris Tales. The rest of this review will get into some more details about what I liked, as well as a few things to watch out for.I won't get too deep into the story to avoid spoilers, but I thought it was an interesting and cute story, but it does get a little convoluted by the end, but what story involving time manipulation doesn't? The game has a *lot* of characters and I felt almost every one fit well into the story. What's more impressive is nearly every single line of dialog is voice acted.The environment and animations are absolutely gorgeous. The art style really is something to behold. The soundtrack is amazing as well and perfectly fits the atmosphere.I felt the game does a great job of introducing new mechanics and unraveling the story at a pace that makes you want to keep playing to try out that new thing, or to see what happens next. It's definitely inspired by classic turn based RPGs, with a bunch of references to accompany that inspiration, but adds some some of it's own flare to keep things a bit more interesting. Attacking and defending have additional active-input windows which can help you do more damage, or take less damage so you're constantly engaged during the battle. Crisbell's ability to shift time within the battle adds another interesting layer to strategy. Unlike most RPGs your squad is actually in the middle of the battlefield and you might have enemies on either side (there's no related penalty though). This creates some interesting strategy as attacks on the left side tend to revolve around sending enemies into the past and attacks on the right side revolve around sending them into the future. You can also move enemies to opposite sides if that will help whatever strategy you've cooked up.The playable characters all feel fairly unique and offer different strategies you can apply to use them, but any combination can work, which I think is a plus. I like that you can swap the party at any point, but I don't love that characters not active in battle don't gain any experience, but that's not too surprising given the inspiration.A few of the boss battles ramp up difficulty quite quickly, so you might get stuck once or twice and need to grind for a bit to get past them. Some of the boss battles have more custom mechanics, but some also last a long time (like 20-30 minutes).There are some weird bugs that start popping up later in the game, particularly around the DLC characters:- The biggest issue being if you equip the Spiked Keychain with JKR it will softlock the game when his heat meter gets to 100 because the over-heat never triggers and the game doesn't account for this. - Some of JKR's moves won't have any sound. - Adri can also prevent some of the achievements from popping up. - There are also some minor inconsistencies when characters pop up to say lines when they shouldn't; for example, when they are no longer with the party and one case where that character has died in the story. - Another issue I would very rarely run into: attacks would seemingly do no damage. This wouldn't apply to an enemy who nullifies that type of damage either. I only had this happen 3-4 times though.- Only once, I ran into an issue where I killed an enemy, but it never disappeared and couldn't take further damage. I managed to work around it by healing it and then killing it again. I wasn't able to reproduce this though. Outside of the JKR softlock though, these don't impact the experience too much and were pretty rare.While the game does have a few issues that I would love to see fixed, overall I really enjoyed my time playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: CrisTales is a delightful return to the classic JRPGs we fans have sorely been missing. It has a great story with very three-dimensional characters, and the sheer scope of it for an indie game is just impressive.I wish more games would attempt a 2D hand-drawn style like CrisTales does, because it looks beautiful. Complemented by a gorgeous soundtrack and excellent animated cutscenes. My only complaint with regards to its presentation is the sound design. The game really lacks ambience when certain sounds like footsteps can't be heard and certain voice actors like the innkeeper robots don't even remotely sound like robots. But I will praise the effort and variety of voice actors all across the board.The concept of seeing Past, Present and Future at once is a marvellous idea, and the game's presentation uses it to its best advantage. I had great delight simply looking at every character's version in their Past and Futures. Huge props to the character designers and environment designers for creating a world so detailed and lived-in, that it was possible to see 3 versions of it at once. It's absolutely stunning.Combat is great, although I do have some gripes. I like the need to press the button upon impact for extra damage, and for the most part it really works (with a controller at least). Parrying and deflecting is also a good challenge to get right, but I hate how even when you block an attack, you still get hit with status effects. Not to mention some attacks do huge damage even when blocked and few attacks are even unblockable!The characters have their unique gimmicks, but that in turn is also their biggest problem. Crisbell's ability to use time crystals is a marvel idea and she is a great team supporter, but she could really use some strong attack abilities. Cristopher is the only real damage dealer in the game, and that's a problem. Willhelm is very helpful in team support, although his Yucandras take FOREVER to sprout, almost to the point of uselessness, and he too could also use some strong attack moves. JKR is terrible; he is more of a hazard to the team than a help. He may be fast and do great damage, but his Overheat gimmick really kills any usefulness he may have. The fact that there's an achievement to have JKR kill everyone in the team by overheating is not a good thing. Zas is also terrible. The random attack thing seems like a two-sided affair, but considering all the bosses from that point forward require strong attacks and strong healing at all times to stand up to them, having a character that sometimes, or most times, do next to nothing is not useful. And finally Kari Hudo is actually really good. Her gimmick of capturing enemies a la Pokemon seems troublesome, but the only real drawback is simply capturing the monster. Once she has it, she's an incredibly effective party member.I suppose my real issue with most of the party members is that they RELY on their gimmick to do battle, and having a gimmick isn't necessarily a bad thing, but when they lack the basic moves for them to be useful, unsurprisingly, they won't be used a lot. Oh, and this game does not share EXP with party members, so you better know who you're using.Some of the later bosses are honestly kinda... bloody awful as well. Don't even get me started on the Volcano Sisters. And the Time Empress honestly seems kinda broken to me. I ALMOST ragequitted at these bosses, and that's not a good thing.Still though, this was a marvellous experience. I'm so glad I took the opportunity to play this game and explore it to its fullest content. I even got most of the achievements, save for the ones that require multiple-choice decisions and a lot of grinding.This was a fantastic RPG. If you miss games like these as I do, you owe it to yourself to play CrisTales. It is an adventure like no other.BEST PARTS-Visually stunning, with a striking art style, excellent character designs and gorgeous hand-drawn animation-Excellent sountrack-Time-based mechanic is clever and is put to good use against most of the enemies-The sheer amount of effort put into portraying every character and setting in each timeplace is outstandingWORSE PARTS-All new Party Members rely SOLELY on gimmicks in combat-Party does not share EXP-Characters seriously need more effective special attacks-The Volcano Sisters... UGH...
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: Art direction: Fantastic. One of the strongest parts of the game, with its well animated cutscenes, charming 2.5D style, and pretty designs for the world and its characters.Honestly, if you're on the store page, you already know it's amazing.Music: Very pleasant. Nothing too memorable, but does a good job creating tone and and a sense of an important adventure.Gameplay: Decent. Not the best execution of RPG mechanics I've played, but not the worst either.Items aren't the most plentiful, but I'm only 2 hours in, so that may change. Enemy encounters aren't the smoothest in transition, and I can't tell how much health the enemies have.General gameplay has a nicely executed theme of time manipulation to it, including combat and exploration/quests.Voice acting: Great! Very well done voice acting, and there's a lot of it, as nearly every text is voiced, and there's a lot of characters.Writing: Honestly, its weakest point. It's not terrible, but it's not great either. That may improve later on, but right now, characters say a lot of off-putting things. Like asking you who you are, only to say there's no time for names. Kids thinking stickers on poison bottles are collectables. Or people accusing you of attacking a farm, just because you have a sword, even though you were helping them fight the monsters.It all feels very first draft with how things flow and what they say and do.Overall, there's a lot that could've been improved, specifically in the gameplay and writing, but I still find it to be a very charming and neat experience so far. And I'm honestly looking forward to play more of it soon.If anything comes up that are worthy of an update to this review, I will update it.

_childDocuments_.review: even as some one who likes the game, I can't give it a positive review. Let's begin at the positives. The game has charm. The dialogue is funny, the enemy designs are great, and the artstyle is amazing. The game has this child-like logic to it, yet still manages to fit appropriate dark moments in, that it has so much potential.However everything else is poorly executed. The gameplay is overly simplistic, with little synergy (especially between teammate pairings that don't include the main character) with little strategy required. The grinding even less so as there is no equipment levels of any sort like in Final fantasy 9 or Materia in Final fantasy 7 that makes you think about what to take long term. Exploration is also minimal with no real puzzles that deserve any attention.I will give it some credit though, as for the first half, it doesn't impact the game too much, as it's just a between for story.But that's also where the major flaw in the game comes in. In the latter half the game relies solely on repetition, dropping a lot of dialogue in exchange for revisiting past areas two times in a row, back to back.There is some charm left, in particular one of the playable characters has a nice moment, but it becomes far too much of a pain to be worth it. There is value to the game, you can enjoy it, and I would be happy to have the game get more attention. But I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 35 hours of Cristales, I really like it. If you are into RPGs that make you think and learn a new mechanic, then Cristales is for you.Gameplay: It's really unique since it adds the time travel element, but it does present a learning curve throughout the game, especially when you get new characters. In addition, I have to learn how to crit and parry the enemy by timing it right. In addition, you would need to take into consideration the position of your enemy and sometimes your strategy gets disrupted throughout the story. Even if you grind, some bosses won't have it easy either way because it has a neverending healing strategy. There are bosses immune to different element magic, time magic, and more. Overall, it's an RPG made harder to the point that you do need to think like a strategist. (9/10)Story: The story felt really magical like a Disney movie, but with real life references. If you look into the lore in St Clarity, Neva Tulira, and Cinder, you realize that they are similar to the situation in Brazil, US, and Cuba. It's really enjoyable since I am also a history nerd. Overall story is similar to Kingdom hearts where the main character sets off trying to save something personally dear to them and along the way save the different worlds they visited. However, I did wish that my choices had more impact to the overall story. In addition, there were some plots holes. (8/10)Art: This is where the game shines the most. I really like the art work. I can't describe it words, so go see for yourself (10/10)Character: I think they developed all the characters very well. Crisbell and her struggles to feel confident in herself and bear the unfairness of the world. Wilhelm was a mentor figure all the way through to the end. Christopher struggling to understand if revenge is the answer. JKR721 trying to figure out his past. And Zas being hilarious. They even developed the villains pretty well except for the very last one. Some I can understand their point of view.  (9/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Cris Tales

_childDocuments_.review: Did you know that people who thumbed down this game, thumb up overrated trash like... the Android remakes of Final Fantasy 5 and 6? lolCris Tales is an RPG that reminds me a lot of Valkyrie Profile, in the way it's got some mild platforming sections. You take on the role of Crisbell, a young, beautiful girl that lives with her sisters in a "sisterhood", who figures out she's a Time Mage after awakening some crystals and learning of the prophecies involving herself. She goes to an adventure to stop a very power-hungry evil force; the Empress, who's poised to conquer the whole world.Cris Tales is also a party RPG, and it retains some of the mechanics that you can find in Mario and Luigi RPG games, such as you can deal more damage just as your attack is about to connect... or you can deflect a projectile by pressing the attack key just as a bullet is about to hit your character. Crisbell, after being awakened, finds quite the likeable cast of characters such as Cristoph and Wilhelm... I guess it's called "Cris Tales" because most of them have a name starting with Cris... part of the prophecies and whatnot.The voice acting, you could argue, is a bit on the childish side... but for me, it's very cute and edgey at times. Those who said the "voice acting is amateurish" are LYING through their teeth, these voice actors are famous for doing some very known voices... I will not spoil it, but I could identify Crisbell's voice anywhere lolI've got absolutely no complaints about the game whatsoever; it's a  amazing story with no big difficulty spikes like in the early Final Fantasy games; the graphics just work and the amazing mix between platforming and battle sections is very well done... Will look forward to more games from these devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Just for reference..I am a 56 year old man, old school gamer...I got the game as part of a pack of games. i've played all the great JRPGs from back in the day so when i saw Cris Tales, i did not think i would like it and i was right....i LOVED it!  What a fresh, innovative game...the graphics are fresh and vivid, the story great, interesting fight system and just a fun game to play. if you love new takes on story telling, Cris Tales is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: a fun and fascinating take on the late snes/early psx rpg.visually, its quite stunning. fluid animations, consistant and unique character designs. beautiful environments. the overall style is flat like paper mario, and the colours are cold and sharp. the characters all have strong visual identities and there are some really interesting ideas that explored at length, like dual wielding shields. in safe areas the screen is divided into thirds, with the left side of the screen showing the past, the middle showing the present, the right showing the future. it makes for some stunning vistas. this division however is not present in dungeon zones, and thus those areas also dont have time travel puzzles.mechanically, its one of the few innovative iterations of the genre. several of the characters are time mages, including the chief protagonist, so time manipulation is a central component to puzzle solving and combat strategy. world puzzles are simplistic, and at their most complicated are things like 'go back in time plant a seed then return to the present and climb the resulting tree,' and tend to be present only in towns and other similar safe areas. dungeon puzzles are more navigation based: noticing obscured pathways, remembering to move into the foreground, finding keys, opening one way paths. there is also the occasional classic rpg style puzzles, your sliding tile mosaics, turn all the switches to be in the same direction. the non combat puzzles are not bad, they arent too hard, or too easy. it kind of rides this perfect line of moderation, that leads dungeon areas to feel empty and obligatory, even if beautiful.where this game really takes off is in combat, it complicated and elegent, like stained glass. random encounters consist of the party facing off against groups of enemies. characters can choose to attack, defend, use items, use spells or special abilities, delay, flee, etc. taking turns charges a meter that powers double and triple techniques that strongly evoke chrono trigger. each character has a very specific and unique skillset. additional damage or increased defense can be triggered with active inputs during combat animations (timed hits). each monster has three forms, a past, present and future form. time affects creatures differently, their stats will change, they may have different abilities, or changed weaknesses. the combat field is divided into thirds, just like safezone exploration screens. monsters can appear on the left or right side of the screen, and frequently appear on both at the same time. at the beginning of each combat each third is in the present tense. the left side of the screen can be time shift to the past and back to the present, while the right can be shifted to the future and back to the present. the time shfit effects everything in that third of that screen. a damage over time effect, if moved forward in time (from past to present on the left, or from present to future on the right) will deal all of its damage at once. some characters place traps or plants in an area, that can be triggered instantly by moving time forward. the combat is very good, satisfying.the weakest part of this game is the directing. the story is told through quests in different towns, you visit the town, follow the story of the town, make a choice about the future of the town, collect a new character to your party. the plotting is frequently baffling, causal relationships between events are muddy, and the connections between adventures are tenuous at best. sometimes it can be quite confusing, to understand your character's motivations in a given scene. it feels like a YA series, except the beginning and end of each book has been cut out, and the middles of each book are pasted together. there is a distinct progression of time, and the same characters populate each story, but it always feels like some context is missing. its jarring, and disjointed. ultimately its a fun game, most rpgs in this style have poor directing. but very few have such fascinating combat systems and well designed characters. this game was a gift from a friend, and i might feel differently had i paid for it.
