_childDocuments_.review: I truly had high hopes for this game. From the preview videos, to the initial game play, the tracks are nice, the semi-open world casual game play is nice, and i feel like if you have a dedicated multi-axis motorbike simulator you would enjoy this game a lot. I WOULD recommend this game to people who have NEVER ridden a motorbike before, want to experience a challenge in perfecting game control, and want to experience what it would be like to race/race in TT.However, as a weekend racer this is the most frustrating game i have ever played... As a casual gamer with only a controller/keyboard this is the most frustrating game i have ever played... I'm not sure if its just me, but i feel like the way the rider in game reacts to cornering, breaking, throttle and clutch control, its seems un-natural? BUT THE BIGGEST FLAW is how it seems like the riders head is the centre of the bike, leaning into a corner and its your head that seems to stay on the chosen line, which is what you want the bike to do, it seems like the bike is trailing behind? I'm not sure how to explain it? But its almost like there is this giant lag between the rider and the bike, made more obvious with the basic input of a controller?This game is not for me, and i feel like anyone who has any experience as a rider would feel the same. Not sure if i can recommend this game to ACTUAL motorbike riders.Therefore, take my recommendation as a suggestion, If the game is on sale, like when i purchased it, i would say it may be worth it? if its not, then maybe keep this in your cart until it does go on sale. But if i were to spend my money again, i would wait for a nice weekend and use the money to put fuel in my ACTUAL motorbike!
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: The only way this game could feel more realistic would be if you actually died each time you slammed your bike into a stone wall/lamppost/hedge at 150 mph. It is stupidly, stupidly difficult. Dark Souls on two wheels. Success is getting a single lap in without coming off. But then again, if you thought riding something with 200bhp which weighs about the same as a bag of peanuts on public roads in rural Ireland was going to be easy, maybe you should stick with Need For Speed. It's brutally difficult but not unfairly so. The handling model is a huge improvement over Ride on the Edge 1, which was already brilliant. I don't think I know any racing game which conveys a sense of horrifying speed as effectively as Ride On the Edge.  A superb game. Hats off to the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a neutral recomendation. Its not bad its not good either but as a new release the developers should show more care to the details. With many positive aspects and improvements it feels unfinished and despite promises of simulation its very arcady even on top no assists simulation level. It is a big shame because it could be perfect if some things were included, improved or fixed.When I started to play IoM TT2 my first thoughts were: it feels sooo goood. The handling of the bike, thanks to introduced gyroscopic effect gives realistic feeling of moving bike. The faster you go the slower bike turns, under heavy braking or on bumps the bike wobbles and try to regain stability. If you break hard the rear of bike moves up or even flip over if there is too much force aplied to the front brake. On bumpy Snaefell Mountain course you feel every bump thanks to improved suspension physics. Combining it with fantastic helmet camera, good sounds, helmet movement and proper field of view, player gets unforgettable feeling of racing at TT. No doubt that there is no better game in that aspect.Except tracks which were present in TT1 we get a new open world, which can be ridden in free roam mode or can be divided into smaller circuits. With dynamic weather (mist + cloud cover), the tracks and sceneries are simply beautiful. Especially with improved graphics everything around looks realistic and very nice. Also the TT course was upgraded and looks even better. Career mode was fully redesigned to create more realistic experience. Unfortunately you can't even create your own rider. All you can do is to choose name and country. Bike can be customised only by choosing from few of preset liveries which are simple and not very nice. You follow calendar races to reach Tourist Trophy as your ultimate goal and earn money to buy new parts for bikes. Each new part improves bike performance and allows to set parameters like suspension settings, engine brake power, gear ratio or disc brakes power. Unfortunately the career becomes boring very fast. Once you learn the tracks and upgrade your bike you simply win every race by few seconds. AI was improved but its not competitve at all. After completing 2 sesons I dont want to touch career anymore.I rarely play career mode in any game. I do only if I am forced to unlock bikes or parts. For me the most important is multiplayer. Unfortunately in case of IOM TT2 is one of the worst features. The interface, lack of options and features make it dead empty just in the day of release. There is no lobby browser, each time you want to change world or bike class the lobby must be restarted. After few tries to play online I simply want to stop, because the number of things to do are very annoying. You even have no possibility to use your career bike or anything what would make you feel individual in world of racing. Just racing to be precise, because you can't create any chamoionship, qualification or event. Thankfully the net code is much smoother than in TT1 so playing in multiplayer is possible without problems.From official game I would expect more bikes and better attention to details. There are no sidecars, only 5 classic bikes and few modern bikes. The list is so short that in career events we race with 2 or 3 the same riders - like there are 2 or 3 Hickmans on the grid.. ridiculous. As we speak of bikes and attention to details, Kylotonn failed on this one too. Bike models have flaws and some are just bad. Honda CBR1000RR looks like harley davidson electra glide with ridiculously wide front fairing and thin body, BMW S1000RR has small rear wheel looking like a rim without a tyre or front fender hanging meters above front wheel, Norton V4 RR has mix of oneside swing arm with standard racing swing arm, few bikes have wet weather tyres despite in game you will never race in wet/rainy conditions. Also there is one rider model. Even if real life rider is using Shoei or Shark helmet he still has Arai on head with another paint and logo. Very disappointing that developers didnt work on that. Just like on the animations which are poor and plain. Replay cameras are also basic and do not look good if you want to watch your race or make a screen shot from other than onboard or chase cam perspective. No photo mode which feels like a basic feature to show beautiful landscapes of the game. In the end I come to the biggest flaw of the game in my oppinion - In game trailers we were told that game will be a simulation. Unfortunately despite it features tyre and disc brake temperature the effect on how bike behaves is very small. From racing point of view its doesnt change anything. You can't highside, lowside, loose grip under havy acceleration or braking. Game does not simulate loss of cornering grip - even in full sim mode you have full grip all the time! Some bikes even cant perform wheelie. It feels like all aids were turned on all the time. You feel from controller vibrations that tyre might loose grip but it never happens. Is it a bug? Or was made on purpouse to hide unfinished physics code? Its the biggest disappointment and makes the game boring just after you learn the tracks. You can go into corner with full speed, full brake, downshift to 1st gear and bike will never fall unless you hit a bump.There are also many other aspects that I am surprised were not fixed, improved or changed. For example: -why there is no free roam in multiplayer? everyone would like to ride round with friends around the track and compete. -why there are no tear offs? with so many bugs on the visor in real life riders use tear off very often. Its a must to improve onboard cam experience.-why look back view in onboard cameras change perspective to chase cam? It brings unnecessary confusion and distracting change of perspective-why we cant use our custom career bike or change flag for multiplayer? -there are copy paste bugs from TT1 like reseting graphics options or constantly visible rider names in multiplayer.So what can I say about TT2 in short form? It is beautiful, has the best onboard experience among all motorcycle games, have some very nice features, but as a new game and sequel it fails. Its unfinished and quickly becomes boring due to arcade physics, lack of any challange once you learn the track. Buy it if you want unforgettable onboard/helmet cam racing experience riding at Snalefell Mountain Course or you are casual player looking to kill some time. If you expect something more, played a lot TT1, look for a challange or you are advanced motorcycle games player, better wait for game fixes or buy at sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely do video game reviews.  Fact is, the one major reason I would a review is if the game is great. These days great video games speak for themselves and are well known.  I thought I'd leave my experience with this lesser known racing simulator because of its rewarding and difficult nature.  It's the DARK SOULS  of motorcycle racing sims.  Lol!!  I'm half kidding, because this trope is also applicable here.  It is d##n hard.  It takes a lot of tweaking, practice, and failure to get the hang of it and fall in love with TT 2.  After about 20 hours of mediocre racing,  I finally broke through to a higher tier of skill and learned to appreciate it to it's fullest.  If you don't mind a high learning curve and you like to be challenged, this game is in my opinion better than the other motorcycle games by far in all areas.  The graphics, the AI, and especially the physics makes you feel like you're literally fighting for your life on the windswept landscape and fighting the other players to get that trophy and cash to level up your bike and eventually qualify for the Isle of Man race at the end of the season.   The first Isle of Man from what I've experienced lacks the realistic physics in turns that breaks the game for me.  I got it for one dollar on fanatical though, so I have no regrets getting it.  It's basically the same game in other areas to its sequel.  I'll leave it there. I could say more, but I wanted to vet this game personally and help those that aren't sure whether it's a game worth getting.  For the competitive and patient, it most definitely is.  Great job Big Ben.

_childDocuments_.review: Default controller settings are a deadzone of 10% and sensitivity turned all the way down.What this does is leave you with all or nothing steering that has you see-sawing from one extreme lean angle to the other. I ride a bike in real life, that is not how you ride a bike.Its obnoxious. I shouldn't have to spend my time fixing controller settings for a game that is obviously going to be played with a controller.The AI also leans far less than you do. Part of how you lean in bike games is by taking visual cues from the AI and leaning accordingly. If I have to get my knee down to make a turn while the AI at the same speed only needs 20 degrees, then that is an obvious disconnect and its very jarring.The racing line and braking markers are frequently wrong. Braking points in the middle of a turn you can take flat out. Other times braking point way too late leaving it impossible to make the turn no matter how hard you brake.4 races in and i have no bike upgrades/parts, but i do have loads of cards with stupid things like reputation improvements etc. Thanks i guess.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: The main drawback of TT IoM 1 was the handling of the bikes being quite unpredictable, but after many hours of practise you could hone your skills and drive quite well with few accidents, however this iteration is much more forgiving, and a very worthy successor as the handling has definately been improved without sacrificing the hardcore nature of the bike handling compared to games such as MotoGP and Ride Series which feel totally arcade by comparison.Graphics are very good. Isle of Man TT circuit detail is exceptionally fantastic and the feeling of speed is horrifying!.I play mostly racing games and simulators, and this definately feels more a sim than a game, and I recomend it as the challenge of the difficulty will keep you practising for many many hours. And the practising is great fun!. I give this title, 8/10. Things to improve I think would be bigger selection of bikes as very few have been added since the IoM1 bikes.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - it does work on Steamdeck absolutely fine. No issues.As once an aspiring road racer myself and now safety conscious family person this is the only way I'm going to experience The Mountain at such speeds. I've had this title on PS4 for a while and decided to get it on Steam Deck too for travel convenience. I spent hundreds or hours in it. Here is the basic lowdown:Superb: - Sound design is second to none, the bikes, the wind, the crowd the atmosphere- Experience of riding a superbike at speed- Consequence of making a mistake and crashing at such speeds - Sense of achievement when you finally complete your first lap without crashing- The only way us mere mortals will come close to experience racing at the Isle of Man TTPassable:- Competition and AI on other road courses, they make mistakes, they crash , most of the time allow you a clean race- Graphics, a few years ago it was superb, now it's ok. Still best representation of the mountain course out there.- General riding and handling, just about ok but in no way represents reality. (See below)Stinks:- Physics, as a rider and racer myself I can not fanthom what on earth is going on there. Infinite grip aside (yup full traction at all times) - Bikes have a turning circle of a train.- There is no feel or feedback visual or otherwise from braking.- Weird and unexplicable crashes on what was a perfect line just last lap- Odd POV camera gimball location makes you feel like you just pivoting around riders stomachSaying that I would 100% recommend both this and first game (for sidecars) The sense of achievement is immense when you finally master it the experience of riding a motorcycle is out of this world! Especially for those who have not ridden in real life.Just don't go out on the road after this thinking you can do 200mph down your local village - you can't 😂

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the first game as soon as I discovered it because no one else had created the entire TT course. Fair enough, glaring physics bugs never really addressed. Whatever...I bought the second game as a pre-order based on the preview vids looking like it's better! Fooled me twice, or whatever G.W. Bush said. Please, please, please! First, fix the setup so that it's available in the restart menu without having to go to the main menu first. Second, please improve the interaction with the ground physics!  It used to be that you would corner and dig into the ground and hook into a turn if you happened to be on the brakes or in negative throttle. Now, if you hit the brakes you dive into the ground and clip the plane and wipe out that way.  Oh, the hubris! Please, at least respond and tell us you're counting money or that there is no plan to fix it like last time! I'm proud I didn't swear at you!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought rally drivers were the most reckless people on the planet before I found this game for cheap on the internet and learned about the Tourist Trophy (TT) Isle of Man races. Seriously, wtf?!This is the official game of the TT, and it is a tough-as-nails motorbike racing game/sim, depending on the level of assists you select. It's never gonna be easy though. It takes some time getting used to (several hours for me, it was my first ever motorbike racing game), but once you get the hang of the controls, it's absolutely great.Pros:* racing is fun once you get the hang of it* graphics are good, not up to latest standards maybe, but I like them.* The original tracks are there in full length -- that Snaefell mountain course is 60 km, and modeled in every detail! Check the videos on youtube from the real event and compare to the track in-game, it's really amazing!* Races take long (many between 10 and 25 minutes) and feel very meaningful, restarts are punished (slightly, not too much) with 10% reduced prize money per restart.* Good game modes: career, free roam, time attack, custom, challenges on the free roam map. I would say the main part is the career. The free roam is nice and not exactly tiny, but this is not Forza Horizon 4 or something.* You can buy lots of bikes (3 classes: supersport, superbike and classic) and parts, as well as liveriesCons:* hard in the beginning* may not be yours if you do not like motorbikesNeutral:* some of the longer tracks require quite a bit of dedication to learn. that's the price to pay for getting the real tracks, I guess.* It's for a niche audience.Overall 8/10, maybe 8.5 for you if you are a fan of motorbikes and/or the TT. I was neither when I got this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's put 13k miles on a 2013 ZX-6R (and ridden a handful of other sport bikes), I can safely say this is the best motorcycles game out there. It may lack in bikes and track variety but the physics make it all worth while. I recently picked up RIDE 4 the complete set with all 15 DLC packs for 70% off and I played that for 9 minutes until I asked for a refund. I also bought TT at full price which is still a far better deal than it's competition. Also it should be noted, I have yet to play RIMS and the recent MOTO GP entries but after seeing how RIDE 4 felt to play I'm not sure I intent do branch out. This review is largely based off RIDE 4 and TT2 comparatively. Other than the few bikes to select the only other thing this game does not do well is wheelies. Nearly any wheelie that's not corrected will result in a crash. Don't buy this game expecting to do wheelies. That being said, RIDE 4 you can do wheelies so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ easily it's not even fun. TT2 is NOT easy and the AI will kick your ass and force you to ride beyond your limits so it can be understandably frustrating for some but riding beyond your limit successfully is extremely satisfying. Track length in the career can also be a concern as you may be participating in races lasting over an hour (most races are between 10 to 30 minutes). Once a race is started it's started. Restarting will result in a 10% penalty loss. Playing poorly will hurt your progression and ramps up pressure. Luckily if you quit or your game crashes you can resume right where you left off in the current race. To end on a happy note i'll bring up the physics again, The front and back brakes both feel accurate to how the bike would respond in heavy braking especially while in a turn. though you'll need to turn off the synced brakes in the options to use each brake individually. The turning and leaning is the real star of the show and handles the closest to a real motorcycle than I've seen in any other game. In RIDE 4 you can only turn so much and it feels very off and unrealistic, in TT it seems you can always turn tighter and push the bike harder. What TT2 does so well is allows you to push and "ride on the edge" to such an extreme it makes RIDE 4 look like a cheap arcade racer. It's something you'll need to work at to achieve but when you are literally riding on the edge there's no other bike game that can compare. There's certainly a lot of room for improvement but this is the motorcycle game to get IMO, Hopefully the studio keeps making motorcycles games. I should also mention I did try the multiplayer a few times but never found anyone else on.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I raced bikes for many years and this game brings back the memories so vividly.  The immersive feeling and sensation of speed is amazing.  I'll be going into a corner, realize I've made a mistake and my heart will be in my mouth just like the old days ;-)It doesn't just have the TT circuit: the free roam riding in Ireland is almost worth the price by itself.  Don't be confused by nerdy reviews about "the physics", it's realistic and in quite a few ways (great weather, no cars, no speed limits, crashes that don't hurt) the game is actually better than the real thing :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a pretty decent, if flawed, motorcycle game. Fantastic recreation of the Isle of Man. There is a real sense of speed in my opinion and at times it's almost actually like riding a bike, especially at the top end of speed with a good pair of earphones or decent sound system. However, slow riding feels weird - probably due to the pendulum effect... Whilst this is fine at high speeds due to the fact that it is kind of like this for real (the swinging of the wheels feel a touch exaggerated in the game), it just doesn't translate properly at slow speeds... Slow speed cornering feels off. Also, there's next to no feedback from the bike - ie; there's no rattling, no shaking of the front stuff (like the brake fluid reservoir)... this is a thing when going at high speeds and the game would benefit greatly from it. Braking also feels off, I should have gone over the front of the bike more than I actually did... BUT HEY, IT'S A GAME AND IT'S PRETTY GOOD!! Remember that folks, if you want REAL real, get out on your bike yeah? I sure do, but I would never do some of the stuff I can do in game and that's what makes gaming fun.Anyway...The game could do with qualifying / practice laps... Bit of an oversight if you ask me.You will fall off. A lot. Turn off that racing line, play in headcam and read the roads whilst you're learning the track(s), much better this way as the line is very distracting imo.I'm nitpicking. It is still a great game, hoping some updates will improve some of its downsides, especially the fact there is no practice/qualifying etc. Is it a sim? is it arcadey? I'm undecided, but it still feels great, especially at high speeds and I feel there are aspects that kind of reflect real life riding.If you're a biker (despite some of the games downsides to handling, mostly slow speed), and/or a TT fan, this is a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR:Great idea, great graphics/sounds and game play let down by physics and controller calibration that really puts this into the realm of simcade at best. RIMS Racing does the physics sooo much better with far more realism, in fact if the two developers joined forces and put TT2  game with RIMS physics....you'd have the best sim ever produced, by a country mile....it's a real shame that unlikely to happen. So I've been eyeing up TT2 for a while and finally took the plunge. There's a lot to like about this game and there's a few things they could have done a whole lot better.....First off the reproduction of the TT course is simply brilliant, with heaps of detail and as far as I can tell it's a pretty faithful reproduction of the real thing.....that in itself is massive and the other road circuits are equally realistic and that's one of the biggest draws of the gameSo lets start with the good bits. Awesome game play with good progression through the game, The graphics are top notch and I really can't fault them and the feeling of speed is really well done, with tree's zipping past you at 200mph it really does "feel" like it, likewise the sounds have been well done with good attention to detail, the Triumph sounds like a Triumph. The other road circuits are equally well reproduced and that kept me coming back for more. There's a lot to like about TT2 and I don't regret buying it......however.....The physics are mediocre at best.....having ridden bike for 35 years (at pace I might add) the devs have missed the mark on this one and the obvious comparison would be RIMS RACING which does bike physics so much better, with so much more detail and so much more realism. TT2 just does weird random stuff, hurtling down a straight and hit a wee bump bolt upright...watch your bike cartwheel down the road for no apparent reason (this isn't what happens IRL) The bike never gets upset, whereas in RIMS, push too much and the front will tuck, gas too much coming out of a corner over some bumps and she'll shake her head at you, carry too much speed cranked over as you breast a crest and you WILL be going sideways. These are ALL the things that TT2 SHOULD HAVE BUT DOESNT and it's a real shame, it takes what could have been a phenomenal sim and relegates it to a simcade and thats a real shame because TT2 deserves to be more than it is......
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I only play it for learning the layout of tracks. Would love it if it was a great game that I could play just for fun, but there are some extremely lazy shortcuts taken in development that make it constantly irritating to play.The mouse pointer is always there, every time you start an event you have to move your mouse to the edge of the screen so it's no in your FOV during play.Control input support is poor. No joystick support and limited tweaking options for keyboard. Occasionally the game will revert to default control layout on startup, meaning your controls won't work when you start playing and you have to navigate through the menus to fix it.Menu navigation is atrocious. Perhaps it makes sense when using a controller, but keyboard navigation is some of the worst I've ever seen. Mouse doesn't do much but move around, it's useless for navigation so why it is even there I don't know.Stupid glitches happening - bike randomly crashes at a particular point riding through the Highlander in the Snaefell course (as though an invisible obstacle on the roadway), LH steering input lagging at times and every now and then terrain spilling onto the racetrack and glitching on/off.At its core there are some decent mechanics and the tracks are nicely built. I could put up with the bugs if there was even a moderate level of effort put into PC controls an menu navigation. And having a mouse pointer floating around during gameplay is just inexcusable.EDIT:This nvidia driver problem (oct 2021) is completely insane. Devs have gone silent as people have been unable to launch the game for weeks now. I don't know how any publisher or developer could find that acceptable.EDIT 2:driver problem is resolved, but the game is crashing nearly every time I try to play it. I stopped trying for several weeks but as of Oct 22 the problem persists.I really want to keep practising the IOM track and to be able to give the game a positive review but the issues just keep coming.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first game to see if I liked bike racing. I was a huge fan of the dirt rally games and this seemed like something that would also interest me. Just like dirt rally it was a bit frustrating at first learning how to control the bike smoothly but after a couple of hours I was having a lot of fun racing around and trying to win.The career mode doesn’t make much sense to me. I can place 1st but end up 5th after the other riders finished and I’m not sure what or why this happens. Maybe someone knows and can post in the comments. Not sure if you get a penalty for crashing or not. It doesn’t say when you do crash. I’ve also finished races without crashing and still lose. Maybe I just suck? Let’s go with that.First person riding is really intense and the preferred way to play. It was makes you feel fast and looks somewhat realistic. You can buy and upgrade bikes and also tune them to desired riding styles.Despite still figuring out how career works the game is quite fun regardless. I wish multiplayer was still alive but sadly it is very dead.Plays great on steam deck but does randomly crash at times but it’s not often. More than likely a compatibility issue within proton.EDIT………I figured out what was happening. It’s was time trial courses and normally on these type of tracks they put you solo on it but in this game it does not, so I was getting confused how I was losing when in the lead.Now that I know this I was able to adjust to it and get better times.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so close to being great but one major issue and a few minor that seems to keep this game out of the spotlight. The physics are just wrong and the controls are just too sensitive and no matter what you do in setting you can't change it. Just google others having the same issue. You will be constantly having to make micro adjustments in turn which will unrealistically have your character bobbing up and down mid turn which is immersion breaking for a moto sim. For those of us who ride you will quickly realize that you can make twitchy movements with your bike at speeds that in real life you just ca not do. This ultimately kills the fun and immersion of the game and for this reason I cannot recommend. Some races are long and with the ridiculously bad driving physics you will crash and there is no second chances. The computer will almost never crash and you will get gapped and never recover. I understand it's supposed to be difficult and if the physics were better and we had more control over the bikes I could be ok with this but it's infuriating when you can't hold a line in a turn due to terrible sensitivity and you crash. The assist lines are pretty bad as well. Sections will say red so you slow down and the PC will full throttle through it. Other sections will be go section and there will be a bump which will crash you and your lead that you held the last X amount of time is gone and you will never get it back. If you want a Moto game just get one from the Ride series.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels so good when you can make full laps around the TT without crashing, let alone "win" the Senior TT on the same bike you own in real life, or even break Peter Hickman's time...You'll have to play with the gearing and suspension later in the game when the parts are unlocked to squeeze out the performance where you need it.I also have Ride 3 and MotoGP 20, but I have the most fun with this game.Some things I think would put this game over the top:1. Optional replay view (after race completion) from perspective of the people spectating on the side of the road as you pass by at 203 MPH or like the YouTube videos at least. Maybe keep your fastest stats per turn where even the Legends get nervous and show those replays of how you've been faster through that area or turn. I would even pay for this as DLC, since this isn't actually crucial for the game to play. This feature could even allow friends to view on the sidelines as you're racing and then notify you that someone was watching after the race - so not to distract you.Which brings up issue number 2 - Online.2. Online is there, but it's not there. The menu is setup too specific and there is pretty much no one ever online at the same time when you want to play against someone random. I've had the privilege of playing online once when the game was new and it was actually quite fun. It would be awesome if a developer could just make an open lobby to show who is hosting a public race and easy to join. That would be an amazing first start to playing online.3. I want to feel the experience of being at the TT and know how special it is to race in it. Maybe a single player mode how EA does their career modes in sports games, if that makes sense? After that, the game should proceed how it is now. I just feel that would add some connection and teach some history to what the TT is all about. For example, people still think TT stands for Time Trial...4. A practice lap before the race (at least) AND the ability to re-tune the bike before the race starts instead of having to go out and to the garage, test it, then go back to the calendar to race. I get it that you aren't allowed to make any changes once you've started the race (including restarting), but it's kind of a task to test out new changes as it is and I find it's really only possible to test major changes if you know the roads without the assistance lines. If you don't remember the route or don't know the Irish roads without the guidance lines, then good luck testing your changes. Unless I'm missing something...?Other than the things mentioned above, this game rocks!

_childDocuments_.review: A terrible game. I know the game is supposed to be hard, in order to recreate at least a bit the real life Isle of Man, but that, that is freaking unreal. You try to exit a turn(if you eventually manage to make it) - boom, you crash again. Why? Again because of the dumb game's delay in controls. When a turn comes, I begin much  earlier than the NPCs, we drive at the same speed, but guess what - I still crash. Reason? The game is dumb. No matter how well i control the cornering and braking, I always end up *dead*. I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who loves his nerves.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels more like version 2.0 rather than a true sequel. The goal is ultimately the same as the first. Rise through the ranks and win the Isle of Man TT in the biggest fastest bike you can manage to stay on for 80 minutes.The biggest changes have been to the physics and the bike handling. It's still very easy to come off the bike and lose a race but the handling is much smoother and far fewer issues with being frequently dismounted for no logical reason.It's not quite an arcade racer but not quite a full on sim either. It's somewhere in between and for me it strikes a great balance between realism and fun. Well worth a look if you're into bikes.

_childDocuments_.review: After sinking a couple dozen hours in TT Isle of Man Ride on the Edge 2 (or TTIoMRofE2 when you're in a slight hurry), here are my thoughts.The Snaefell Mountain Course is the focus of the game and it shows. The circuit is beautiful and has a very precise and awesome 3D modelling. You can buy the game only to race this track and will get well enough for your money, it is frankly impressive and when watching bikers filming the TT with onboard cameras you recognise everything everywhere and most of their comments can apply to the game.There are two other playfields : England, a collection of small tracks of various styles but nothing superlative about it, and Ireland, a large free-roam map with assorted landmarks where sections can be closed to create new tracks. They are usually larger than English ones and prettier too, arguably more technical too but I like them more. Not a fan of doing laps on a 3km tracks but at least they thought of everybody. Free-roaming is good to test new bikes and vent, touring curiosities, although the "free" part ends with asphalt and trying to ride to the beach or across the hills will reset you to the road. Kind of a fun killer but hey, at least it's there.I am no polycount ♥♥♥♥♥ or nex-gen graphics afficionado, though I do care about artistic direction and overall care. And while individual models have a certain plastic feel, overall the game is gorgeous. Lights effects are beautiful, coming from forest darkness to a plateau showered in sun rays never gets old, and the overall tone is pleasantly realistic. Having the sun in your face is a real drawback, Manx moors bathing in mist is a sight to behold and all the towns and buildings you pass at 200km/h are well modelled and could warrant a slow lap simply to enjoy the scenery. Soundscape is also good, with the sound of wind that reverb on props. All great.But the engine sucks a little, has a forced 60fps count and can suffer from micro-stuttering at times. There are Steam guides to fix it (in short : force 60fps in your GPU software), and well enough graphics settings to accommodate all hardware, but come on.There is a decent rooster of bikes in three categories : supersports, monstrous superbikes and classical ones. You can choose freely from either for quick play. They all seem to be well-modelled, not that I know anything about bikes, and there should be enough choice to please everybody. You can then unlock or buy upgrades for them in career mode, some higher tier parts allowing you to fiddle with gearbox ratios or suspension settings for example. Upgrading is very arcade-y, parts are tiers A B C D S and getting higher is always better. No real room for compromise or part synergy. There is no damage model on bikes, but considering that the average crash will send you straight to the grave it is no big deal.Yes you can. And that's a mixed bag. On one hand high speed driving is exhilarating and unforgiving, with lot to learn and master. On the other low speed is comically bad, the lower the worst. Taking hairpins is always stressful because you never know how the engine will react. Usually you end up turning on yourself, sometimes you swerve in some random way. You never really feel you're on a bike, more like you're some swinging bullet train. The default sticks settings are terrible and you MUST spend some time tinkering with sensitivity and deadzone to find an acceptable middle-ground. There default control scheme is not very good, I'd recommend using the "classic" one with gear change on LB and RB and throttle on right stick, removing all other controls stupidly bound to it.The good news is that there are several difficulty settings you can change at will with no impact on game or progress. You can tailor all that mess to find your favourite experience and have good fun. Except at low speed.There is a career mode. You choose a starting bike and play seasons, each around 20 races you can enter or discard. Depending on your sponsor you get money or parts by fulfilling objectives : noobs such as myself can choose to complete a certain number of races, regardless on your final position or on how many time you wrecked your bike, spine and self-esteem. Good players can play for points or reputation. Entering enough Irish Trophy races can get you signatures to enter the big bad Tourist Trophy at the end of the season, but you can still race the track or some sections in other events. You unlock boons and money to buy bikes and parts and liveries, as well as new challenges on the free-roam map, each of them giving you more shiny stuff to plaster to your bike and run head first into some concrete post. Overall it is laid back and fun, and considering you usually buy the game to play the Snaefell Mountain Course (what you can do anytime in quick race mode) it is a nice bonus.Feels pretty good isn't it ? What could ruin such a nice experience ? Well there's must always be one show stopper and that time it's the AI. It is infuriating. They run on rails and will not hesitate to ram your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ speed if you have the insolence of staying in front of them in corners. They always have wondrous acceleration without wheelies, a kamikaze approach to turns, are incredibly stable, and while you can manage to send them in the meadows most of the time you'll be the one flying at the smallest shock. They do crash themselves at time but respawn very quickly. Higher difficulty level seems to be only higher average speed. I wish you could remove collision with them and not have to deal with robotic psychopaths plowing their way in. Unfair and unfun, this is hands down the worst point of the game. Thankfully the time trial races and the possibility to choose the number of opponents in quick race mode allow you to run for fun when you're not in fight-club mood.This is a nice game that is very pleasant to launch when you're in the mood for racing in beautiful and challenging tracks, with no hassle or complex setup. Learning your way around the 60 kilometres of Snaefell Mountain Course is a terrific experience well worth itself buying the game, driving gets real fun at high-speed and overall this is a nicely wrapped-up package that delivers its promise. If you could mount machine-guns on your bike to dispatch the AI it would be perfect, otherwise it is a 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: The new one is out now which I haven't played yet but this one is good if you can pick it up cheap. The sense of speed is crazy and better than just about any other racing game. The handling is a little weird but pretty good once you get used to the feel of it. It is a bit unrealistic in some ways, like you can just mash the throttle on full lean out of corners and you won't slide out the back, even with no assists. A few other times when it seems overly forgiving. However bumps on the road will send you flying almost every time, you need to learn where all the bumps are and be ready for them or you won't get around a lap. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. The physics is all wrong. I constantly feel like I'm wrangling some kind of 200hp Harley Davidson, as opposed to a top of the line superbike. Going from lean left to lean right seems to take forever. The bike frequently lowsides apparently out of nowhere, when there was little lean angle or much to upset the bike at all. And it gets particularly bad at slow speeds, such as on Ramsey's hairpin or the Governor's bridge hairpin -this latter one I find extremely hard to take without pathetically bumping against the wall and falling off the bike at 20km/h like some drunk. After a lot of grinding, I managed to do an entire lap on the IOMTT track without falling in 17:13, but I have very little interest to go on trying to adapt to this game's wonky physics.It's a shame that this game series seems to hold some kind of monopoly on the IOMTT course -I don't see this with for instance the Nurburgring, which has been depicted on several different racing games. This monopoly ends up being its best quality. I'm glad to have learned the IOMTT to a certain degree, but unless the devil himself tells you that he's gonna kill you unless you manage to do a sub-20 minute IOMTT lap within a week, I don't see much of a point in getting this game.

_childDocuments_.review: One step forwards and two steps back.The random crash bug from the first game seems to be fixed but now the physics feel janky and arcade. These are just some of the issues:1. 1000 cc bike can go full throttle at high lean with no loss of traction?!2. bike doesn’t wheelie in a straight line...but coming out of a corner..guess what wheelie time?!3. bike still can't handle jumps still 50/50 chance of just crashing.4. incredible sense of speed the first IOM game had seems less in this one5. rear brake super unreliable makes bike crash for no reason6. _childDocuments_.review: This game is hard and limited in scope, but it is worth having in your collection because it is outstanding in the areas it focuses on.The first selling point is of course the fact that you get the full Isle of Man course, which at least to my knowledge no other game has the full route. That is a big deal, really.It's a fairly bare-bones sim with a somewhat realistic but tedious career, but the per minute gaming experience is very high. Personally, I didn't enjoy the career mode, it is very tough and unrewarding. But I can see how some may enjoy this level of challenge.What makes this game so remarkable is its sense of speed and for me it's accessibility for me as a causal, even though this game is clearly crafted for a hardcore audience.  For example, using combined brakes in this sim doesn't totally ruin your ability to compete, at least at lower levels. And by tweaking my settings, I was able to get the bikes in this to be manageable, predictable, enjoyable, and fun.The experience when riding is amazing. Its very fun, addicting and all around exciting. It's executed well from a visual standpoint, with convincing camera movement, audio cues (largely) and controller feedback. This game has the best FFB of any bike game I have played. It is much more nuanced than newer games...There are some newer bike games with better lighting and graphics, but this game's visuals are still very satisfying and perfectly good at high speed. Those newer bike games don't feel as good as this, I've tired most of them.I rarely get a podium on the lowest difficulty. But when I do, I'm stoked. In honesty, as long as I don't finish last, I am pretty satisfied most of the time in this sim. At this point I spend most of my time in quick race or free roam. Sadly free roam is only available for one map in this game. (and no, the free roam map is not the namesake either...)If every map in this game had a free roam option, I'd buy it again just for that. But they would need to add some traffic AI of course, because right now it's just you. Traffic in freeroam would be heaven though.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: It looks like the developers of IOM TT 2 have made some good steps forward with the physics of the game. I really like the graphics and the attention to detail in a lot of the textures is great. For me, the best bit about the game is the way you can back the bikes into corners hard on the brakes, very satisfying. I should say that I would consider myself an average gamer that pretty much exclusively plays motorcycle racing games, mainly because I can’t get out on track on my real bike. I’ve been playing the game with the most realistic physics turned on, unlinked brakes and a manual gearbox.So there have been some good steps forward with this version of the game but there are some notable issues in my opinion. There are most apparent when you compare the game to its closest rival in the very limited Motorcycle Racing genre, the MotoGP and Ride series by Milestone. In my opinion, what MotoGP and Ride do very well is they are very playable games with realistic enough physics to be convincing but not so tied down, in reality, to make the game overly difficult and ultimately frustrating to play. A good example of this if we compare the IOM TT 2 to either of Milestone’s latest titles (MotoGP 19 & Ride 3) and the ability to pull wheelies. On the IOM TT 2 game, it seems near on impossible to wheelie the bike without it randomly falling over to one side, whereas in Milestone’s efforts you can loft wheelies the lengths of long straights with relatively little practice at them, again this is very satisfying. This might not seem much when it comes to the business of making motorcycling simulators but let’s be honest, who doesn’t like to see a bike on the back wheel? In racing terms though this lack of influence over where the bike is going when the front wheel is in the air translates to inspecting the shrubbery any time a random, unseen, bump lifts the front wheel coming out of a corner or a rolled curbstone is touched. The most frustrating part of the wheelie physics is getting going after the inevitable high-speed crash and the bike lifts the front wheel and then just falls on its side or ploughs into another bush. Other notable physics issues are how the bike reacts to the bumpy roads, at best this often results in a random trip to one side of the track and then the other after the bike seems to just randomly stay on its side. At worst it ends up in a crash accompanied by the feeling of ‘I have no idea what happened there’ and then the inevitable frustration of getting the bike going again. In the 16 hours I’ve been playing it, I would say the more often than not, when you have one crash you’ll have two or three more as a result of getting going again. Having just completed my first Superbike TT race (a full 6 laps or nearly 2 hours) there seems to be crosswind on the mountain but there is no way to feel that from my chair so the bike just seems erratic and randomly moves about the place. I’ve ridden the mountain course four or five times on a bike and it is windy up there and it is bumpy but I think this is where the game is almost too realistic. My issue with that is, I’m sat in my chair using an Xbox controller, not sat on a bike feeling the pitch, yaw, roll and the associated G forces that go along with it. Perhaps these things aren’t an issue if you play it in less realistic physics mode? I must admit that when I installed the game I just set it to its most realistic setting and haven’t tried anything else, so maybe there are some options there for me? Lastly on the physics, to me, the bikes feel slow to turn. Yes, it’s true that once you gain speed on a bike it becomes harder and harder to turn. Once it does start turning it wants to keep moving in that arc, especially as you gain speed, this is the reason you see some riders on the opposite side of the bike to the way it’s leaning as they exit some turns. It helps get the bike to straighten up or turn in the other direction, there are some excellent pictures of Michael Dunlop and Skakey Burn doing this online. However, this again feels like a place where the simulation aspects could be dialled back to compensate for the fact the user is sat in a chair and not on a bike doing 90 MPH.Like most racing games these days there is a suggested line feature which is colour coded to help the play know if they are barreling into a corner way too fast. There are various ways in which this type of information is conveyed, colour coding, graphical shapes or a combination of the two. In IOM TT they use red and yellow for this feature and also a change in a graphical shape. All seems reasonable so far, however, there are some issues with it. On most of the tracks, I’ve played there always seems to be one or two corners which are wide open visually and in terms of the throttle but get marked in red as if I am going too fast. The result is I end up slowing down and going through the corner way too slowly, or conversely, I’ve had some tracks where the corner isn’t marked in red before but there would be no way of making at the speed I was travelling. This isn’t the worst of things because it can be overcome with time and track knowledge, however, it is exceedingly frustrating and does extend the time it takes to learn the circuits. Hopefully, this will be fixed in a patch because it just seems to me there needs to be a tweak in the algorithm that works these things out. It does point to the possibility that this game perhaps wasn’t tested extensively by someone who races bikes on the roads, at speed to a reasonably high level and also plays video games. I suppose it might be that the person doesn’t exist, who knows.My last major issue with the game is the camera angles on offer. For me, the only viable choice are the third person cameras. It’s what I am used to and to be honest, the onboard cameras to me don’t give you enough of a view. In real life, you’d be looking way up the road, through the corner and for the limited time I tried the helmet camera it just seems to look around the front of the bike. This could possibly be improved by using VR goggles, although I’d be wary of trying that because all the cameras move around, very fast and very frequently and I’d be concerned about losing my lunch.The third person cameras move based on what the bike is doing and do a good job of representing how a bike moves in real life. Most people see bikes on TV and see that it is pivoting around the contact patch of the tyres on the ground. From a physics perspective, they actually rotate around a point that is in line with their centre of gravity, think of a jet making a banked turn and you won’t be too far away from it. For the game though, while this adds to the sense of speed and drama, it also means that the camera is often in a place which makes it very difficult to see where you are going, like right on the ground. The worst of these camera angles is where a corner is lined with hedgerows or walls and the point of view for the player is in the hedgerow or in the wall and you’re left without any site of the bike or the race track. Again, this normally results in a crash and the inevitable issues getting restarted, which all combine to leave me at least feeling very frustrated with the game.Overall this game is a vast improvement on the original, but that wasn’t hard because the bar was so low in my opinion. However, if they keep moving in this direction I can see them having a very good game and base in about two or three versions time. I would have liked to have had a rewind feature like Milestone do. I feel like this speeds up the learning process by being able to experiment on parts of a track which are causing difficulties. I think it also keeps the game moving in a positive way and would help prevent rage quitting. I think for me the balance between the simulator and a playable game hasn’t been struck yet and this game leaves me feeling more than a little bit disappointed with my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, pay no attention to my play time, I recently got it on Steam, but I've been playing it for a good while. Who's idea was it to give the contract to make a motorbike racing game to a development team that has never made a motorbike game?? Ok that's not entirely true, they made "Motorcycle Club" back in 2014, never heard of it? There's a reason for that . . . it stinks. Why not Milestone? Who have made the 'Ride' series and a list as long as your arm of motorbike racing games going back to the mid 2000s. Including MXGP, MotoGP and WSBK titles.   IOMTT the game feels like a motorbike game made with car physics. The bikes feel like two wheeled cars. Hardly surprising since the Dev team specialise in car games. And as an irl rider (owner and abuser of a 2015 Honda CBR1000RR Fireblade) this frustrates me a lot. We get the short end of the stick us motorbike fans, car fans can fill their boots with a plethora of racing and free-roaming 4 wheeled titles, we get. . .  . this. In terms of a game that came out first quarter of 2020 it looks pretty poor to be honest. Maybe I've been spoilt by RDR2 and its picturesque vistas but this is a racing game, Assetto Corsa Competition (2019) and even PCars 2 (2017) look better. In racing games there isn't much 'game space' to really render so there is no excuse for making a 2020 game look like it came out 6 years ago. The general lighting is very flat making the visuals generally feel very Ride 2. But the graphics aren't really where my main problem is, I can generally look past that.The way the bikes handle is so . . . so wrong. Just plain wrong. This is not at all how bikes handle, please dont go away from this thinking this is how bikes behave, dear lawd almighty it couldnt be farther from the truth. Is it arcade? I personally think the learning curve is too steep to be an arcade racer, but it's too wrong to be a sim. I dont know what this is. Get on the throttle in a tight turn with TCS off and it wont even spin the tire, slam on the brakes with ABS off and it wont lock the front wheel, and believe me you can lock up a front on a bike easy and slide the tail end around on a 200hp Superbike with relative ease. The bikes feel heavy and unresponsive in turns and over uneven surfaces then snap to being too responsive in other scenarios, low sides come out of nowhere into corners, trail braking apparently isnt a thing to KT Racing and the way the game engine handles traction is .. ugh. You've basically either got grip or you're in the hedge. Again, this is NOT accurate. I've adjusted settings, raced with everything on, raced with everything off, had some stuff on and some stuff off and nothing solves the horrible way the bikes handle. Nothing feels right to how a bike would actually behave. And this is the biggest issue. Dont feel bad if you crash a lot because 9 times out of 10 it seems the game engine is just like "seems you've not crashed in 2 minutes, how about a nice trip through the hedge when cresting this tiny ridge for no apparent reason at all". Everything is a switch in the game engine I swear, the throttle is an on off, the brakes, it plays like an arcade racer form the 90s wrapped in the exterior of a "sim" title that it's trying to be. Do I recommend it? No. It doesn't do justice to the bikes or the course which is arguably the oldest and one of the most prestigious motor sporting events on the planet. Get Ride 4, hell.. get Ride 2 over this.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Immediate purchase regret, I will explain why for me it is so:I only play with a first person camera, and in this Ride on the Edge 2 there is no possibility of modifying the FOV, so in each curve there is CLIPPING with your own body. To the right and left, part of your synthetic body seen from INSIDE appears on the screen.I have read here on Steam the comment from other players, that the FOV cannot be changed.The most striking thing is that this did not happen in the first game.But if you are one of those who play in the third person, this problem does not affect you.Fortunately development team of the third part is already another. Let's hope they correct everything not well done.Another big problem and without a solution, because it is not possible to correct it in the configuration section, is the sudden movement of the camera, which suddenly goes up and down depending on whether you press or release the accelerator a little. It's immediate, without any smoothness in the transition, suddenly you're crouched down or fully up.With which the screen becomes a blender that after five minutes gives you a headache and eyestrain.Negatively note that the lines of the road are drawn in front of the motorcycle at about ten meters, so they cannot be used as a reference to position the motorcycle. Not only do they not help but they distract.In the first person the bike, the dashboard and the handlebars, it looks like a cartoon (Even at max graphic settings), it has worsened brutally compared to the first part of the game, where everything looked pretty good. This is one of those times when a sequel to a game is worse than its predecessor. No matter how cheap they sell you this second part of the Isle of Man, the first is better in almost everything (the second part has more circuits, but if you can't enjoy them, what good are they for you?).Uninstalled. The thing is that I won't buy the third part straight away, I'll wait to see the reviews. KT Racing, please don't come back.

_childDocuments_.review: So firstly I would like to say that initially I gave this game thumbs down, and didn't like it at all.I've gone back to it many times hoping IT WILL GRIP ME AS MUCH AS THE FIRST GAME DID...BUT IT DIDN'T.As a Isle of Man TT fan for years, being able to feel even a fraction of thrill involved in riding virtually Snaefell Mountain Course was a dream come true. And so I've gone back to it again recently and yes, you've guest it... I LOVE this game :D Now about the game itself:IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR:  - HARDCORE SIMULATION (like GP BIKES) - EXTENSIVE RIDER AND BIKE CUSTOMISATION (like RIDE 4, 5) - ENORMOUS BIKE SELECTION (like RIDE series) - FAMOUS SHORT CIRCUIT RACE TRACKS - STUNNING NEXT GEN GRAPHICS - GAME THAT WILL HOLD YOU'RE HAND AND ALLOW YOU TO MAKE PROGRESS WITHOUT ANY EFFORT - IF YOU DON'T LIKE LONG PUBLIC ROAD RACE TRACKS AND LONG RACES - IF NAME JOEY DUNLOP DOESN'T RING A BELL you probably won't like this game.BUT if you gone past that part now time for what you will find here. # PHYSICSIn my opinion it's a good balance between simulation and arcade. Yes tires have unlimited grip and yes you can slam brakes mid corner without much consequences but equally once you'll master steering you won't be doing it much.  # TRACKSSo if you've played first game you get all the track from the first one plus new Irish tracks and of courseSnaefell Mountain Course 37.73 miles long, represented with every detail.   # FREE ROAMIn this mode you can ride on Irish roads which is basically all Irish tracks connected together. Also in this mode you get to do challenges that unlock bike upgrades # BIKE UPGRADESThis topic is main reason why initially I didn't like this game. All I can say is that top tier upgrades are locked behind season goals, some behind challenges in free roam mode so don't expect to get you're bike to be handling well  and go fast without grinding. # CAREER Bread an Butter of this game. You start a season by selecting to ride for a team and complete objectives that unlock upgrades for bikes or give you money to buy bikes and lower tier upgrades and liveries, also to buy perks that give you slight bonus during race.Normally you get three types of events which are represented in you're racing calendar with different colours that represent different difficulty level.Of course main goal it to qualify for the TT at the end off the season. # BIKESSelection of bikes is same as the first game with the addition of three CLASSICS and some 2019 versions of R6, CBR1000, and S1000RR!!! Controller is mandatory. You can change sensitivity in controller options.    CONCLUSION:                          I've played all three RIDE ON THE EDGE games and in my opinion it's the best overall, 1st requires less grind and has more challenging physics, 3rd is more realistic but has no real career mode, less bikes and its missing all the fun tracks from the first two games.

_childDocuments_.review: A great racing game and worthy of the title. Overall excellent, accurate reproduction of the TT circuit, the first time you do a faultless lap is very satisfying. Good amount of general control and difficulty settings to tailor the game to you liking.Like any other bike racing game if you're used to another bike title it will take an hour or two to tune-in to this games specific feel, when you have the bikes all handle and feel unique with good handling characteristics at speed and feel about as realistic as is possible in a game (very difficult to do in bike games).Only 2 real negatives for me...1. Ultra slow speed bike handling is far too slow, at walking pace bikes can turn MUCH faster than they can at speed. Makes the first time you try to navigate a hairpin bend an interesting experience. Really needs fixing.2. The manual respawn feature is utterly pointless. You can only activate it if you've gone off-road and takes a few seconds of holding the button to actually do anything. As going offroad for more than a second results in an insta-crash 99 times out of 100 (and you CAN'T manually respawn haf way though a crash event), you just don't use the feature. I only did it once to get the Steam achievement. Time rewind or track section reset etc would be much more useful.One other thing I don't really see as a fault but really don't like in a racing "sim" is the perks system. Just no.Overall highly recommended especially if you're into bikes, bikes games and or the TT races. Just be warned the game can be quite difficult and unforgiving, however it's worth the occasional frustration for the rewards.

_childDocuments_.review: Here to update my review:There's a lot of things that work in this game, but after a play-through or two it's obvious this was rushed and there haven't been ANY major updates since.The Good:-Graphics are great-Sound is fantastic-Lots of cool bikes to chose from (classic bikes are great! gearing them for the TT is horrible)-Beautiful representation of the courseThe Bad:Limited livery choices on bikes (C'mon there's plenty of teams that compete here.)-Multiplayer doesn't work, never has, and never will. (The previous game didn't either)-The perks you unlock don't make sense sometimes(Increase fuel consumption, why? Increase weight, why? The weight would make sense if it would allow me to add another perk for a race when I'm at minimum).-The replays are great, how about some tools to edit them/camera placement?-Random gusts of physics wind will send you into a pole out of nowhere.-Since you don't get a warm-up or practice on the smaller races, the mini-map doesn't reflect the course you're racing.  Side roads that you use in other races will look available, but guess what! Hairpin when you don't expect it.  Better study that course map you get for 4 seconds on the loading screen.-The AI becomes obsolete when you start getting better parts, even on the hardest settings.-The Leader-Boards have plenty of people cheating, insane lap times which make the minimal connection to other people playing the game impossible.  There's no policing to this either.Summary:Despite all the draw backs, the game functions and is the perfect tool for what I need as in learning the course.  However, without any updates it feels the developers REALLY cared for making the game, but not so much in making it any better afterwards.The Isle of Man prides itself on it's rich history, and very deep culture and customs.  There's no other place like it in the world.  It would have been awesome to have a place in the game in which you could tap into that, and learn a bit about each of the sections land marks.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - a reasonably fun experience with the iconic TT Course as the centrepiece.The Good:- What else? The whole TT Mountain Course with high detail and accuracy. Ridiculous sensation of speed at times, almost unmatched by anything else. If you are tired of Forza Horizon style 'roads' that feel like nowhere in the real world, this is the antidote. With the sound of the scenery passing so close it often gives you a real adrenaline rush in a way that isn't common with games.- Decent selection of bikes with reasonable handling. Obviously bike games are a little hard to judge given that it's hard to recreate all the subtle actions in riding a motorbike with a controller or keyboard.  There are plenty of aids and the game seems aware of how hard it its - the resets are fast, and the driving line is clear to follow without being intrusive.- Championship mode is agreeably open ended without any obvious pressure to win every race. You can run your own bike while simultaneously racing for a team. Not every race counts for points, there are Easy, Medium and Hard races, and a clear 'Perk' system for strategic bonuses, as well as the standard prize money for upgrades. It does feel like you are progressing from rookie to pro.- Nice selection of fantasy tracks clearly channelling some real-world courses they sadly don't have the license for (that NW200-alike Triangle Course is fooling nobody). Some of the Ireland tracks especially are properly fun in their own right. The Bad- Just a general lack of spit & polish for a modern day game. There are games from twenty years ago that manage more in some areas. Check out those cropped and pasted rider pictures (seriously guys you couldn't source a colour picture of Joey Dunlop or Steve Hislop?). The championship mode is very much 'use your imagination' in parts, with a set of dull menus being mostly all you get. All the rider models look and act the same, very notable during a race start. And I see female names in the entries - very PC and all but would it have been difficult to model a female rider avatar too? Replays seem to be absent from Time Attack mode, so why even bother, just do a single race and if any crazy moment happens (and it will) you can at least watch it back. Most disappointing is that the fantasy tracks just don't have the detail of the TT course. Tying the locations together into a 'Free Roam' map is a nice gesture and all, but without traffic or a road version of the bikes, what's the point? All the courses use the same recycled textures and models, detracting from their individual characters. Maybe that's beside the point as the TT course is the centrepiece, but it's a shame that some really nice course design is a little wasted without that same feeling of immersion.

And it should have been very easy to save those ghosts to compete against them in future sessions for every track at will.

_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: My only wish is that it had more bikes/riders and — though not congruous with the theme of the game — I would really love some place to drive an F1 or any other race car through the Snaefall Mountain Course. Mod access perhaps? The other added courses are a great touch also, as I only expected Isle of Man to be represented here. I feel like I got more than I set out for.So far this the hardest and most realistic bike simulation I have played, coming mostly from Milestone games and Ride 2-4. I am a novice rider in real life and can’t do a 135 MPH average lap, but the realism is excellent. Handling feels accurate as does representation of the wind hitting your helmet. Not to mention the inherent sense of danger around every turn that some of us seek in life, in order to truly live. Very happy with this purchase and got it on sale for a bargain. Wife less so because she expects me to run the Snaefall course someday using the information gleaned from this sim.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: To start, this game is certainly far from perfect. If you are used to the Ride series of games, be very prepared to completely re-calibrate your brain for its unique handling physics. At first it feels maybe sluggish, or that the rider swings wide just to initiate a turn. But after coming to grips with it, I've come to enjoy it. The smaller loops and tracks are pretty easy, but tackling the full Snaefell Mountain Course is insane. Even with rider aids I have yet to complete a superbike lap without a crash. Take a jump with slightly too much lean angle and you're on the deck. But it's a rewarding challenge, you generally know where you went wrong. It is the "final boss" in a sense, so it honestly SHOULD be difficult. Definitely worth picking up on sale, but $30 isn't a terrible price either.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Very fun game! The isle of man course is breathtaking, The other maps are fun as well to learn the game with.- More customization with fov in 1st person and a better looking cockpit would make it even better, I play this game in 3d person while I like to enjoy other modern motorcycle games in 1st. - Vibrations in this game does not work with my PS4 controller on PC.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly kinda feels a little under polished. The bike physics are decent, but the movement is sluggish and you can’t change your riding style like you can in other motorcycle games (how far you hang off the bike, weather you stick a leg out while braking, etc) I’ve had much more fun with many more bikes in Ride 4 on its southern 100 map (along with other street circuits in the game). The only aspect I can see my self booting up the game for again is that it’s the only game with the full TT circuit and the free roam feature. I’d say pick it up if it’s on sale by a decent percentage but if not you might feel a little disappointed by it.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Havent played too long but I have dabbled in pretty much all the features. True to realistic physics, but has enough assistance of controls for new players. I love the camera angle inside the helmet they did such a good job immersing you by making the head actually move in a way an actual rider would. _childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time ever playing a proper motorbike game so I cannot really compare it to others. But damn is it enjoyable. I gotta say for all newbies, there is a steep learning curve and even with all the assists I still have on I still fall a lot even after 16 hours of game. Although I prefer riding the superbike so it is much harder to ride than a sports bike due to the insane speed. And talking about speed, the sense of speed in this game is nothing like I've experienced before in racing games. Nothing feels as exhilarating as going almost 200mph through narrow twisty country roads on a bike. As a newbie it can get quite frustrating constantly falling off but believe me, stick with it and you'll find out how satisfying it is to go at super high speeds twisting and turning through the narrow country side roads.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I've been lucky enough to have ridden the TT circuit a number of times in real life, I rode it when the entire course was open to the public between race days,  ( no speed limit on the mountain...very scary) I also worked at the TT as a volunteer race marshal and as a result I have gotten to know the TT course relatively well. i'd say that this game has faithfully captured the things that make the TT so very special. Its got everything that would be racers want, there's a good selection of modern and classic sport bikes, some great names like John McGuiness, Joey Dunlop and Mike Hailwood not to mention the bikes, I do however think that it could do with a few more classic motorcycles although I was more than happy with the Ducati 900 DLC. The bike physics have been vastly improved over the earlier TT game, the steering feels more precise and its possible to feel what the front end and rear of the bike is doing which helps a great deal when cornering at speed over bumps and dips, the brakes also work pretty well providing you take care of them. I started to learn the course on the MV Augusta 500 three and worked my way up to the more powerful 1000 cc superbikes. its extremely satisfying when you get to grips with the modern bikes and you can watch your lap times improve. I like the various views that can be selected although it does take some practice to get used to. The dangerous nature of the TT is reflected well in this game, absolutely no room for mistakes like I said earlier, it is however very rewarding when you get it right. I have never played a racing game that requires my full concentration like this game does, it requires lazer like precision to get a good lap.Having played most of the MotoGP games and others like Ride2 I'd have to say that Ride on the edge 2  stands head and shoulders above the rest, in my humble opinion its worth the price and if you are a fan of the TT or motorcycles in general then this is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Its a decent bike game with a bit of a wobbly physics engine behind it.For example some parts of the course seem to be set with a hard limit, so even if you have a clear line through parts of it the game is like NAH NAH NAH you cant go through that part that fast, buckaroo time!Bar that its the best Isle of Man  TT race game out there ;)
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive how they managed to rebuild the Isle of Men and all the other tracks. The bike selection is great as well.The riding physics are pretty good too, but only as long as you're faster than around 100km/h, slower corners are much harder than they are in real life. Those don't feel like riding a motorcycle at all. It's more like you're trying to steer a heavily loaded shopping cart.That was already the case in the first game and it's beyond me why they didn't fix that.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Game but with a steep learning curve, trying to perfectly control a motorbike on a normal twisty road at any speed higher than 80 mph with kerbs walls and lamp posts is a challenge using just a normal PS3 controlleri dont know if it would be easier in a different view like third person but as a Biker myself i can not possible play it in any other mode apart from 1st person to get the closest feel to riding a real motorbike around the  Isle of Man TT circuit..you need to have that view of the handlebars clocks and fairing and i have to say the graphics are great it look amazing and the sound of the bike engines are of the real life Bike..so i play with headphone and with the music switched off and the sound of the engine switched up so i can make the experience as authentic as possible.I love older  motorbikes so it s a real treat to be able to ride a  Norton, an MV Agusta, a Yamaha TZR 750 and a  Suzuki 1000 racing bikes all from the 80's and early 90'sthe only issue i have so far is that the bikes are so sensitive in the handling department( as they should be for thoroughbred racing machines) that i am not yet able to ride them smoothly enough just using my left thumb on the thumb controller..i am currently looking in other ways to control the bikes in a smoother way at 150 miles an hour when the slightest twitch is the difference between staying on the road and crashing outIm having loads of fun but really don't feel i am competative with my current controller set up

_childDocuments_.review: A good game, but I'm very glad I got it discounted. Like every KT game it seems, it's a good foundation, but doesn't have that complete polish.Basically, expect the physics to do some wacky s-hit from time to time and worst of all, there is NO practice or quali in career mode. You are just thrown into the races, therefore you can't try out setups before a race. You basically have to gamble and have good track knowledge if you want any chance of doing well consistently...or just restart the race over and over, which in turn penalises you, so that ain't recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game - it's very entertaining, it's frustrating, it's absolutely the most head knackering game ever! If you don't get headache after that you need to go stand in a corner and have a word with yourself for not trying hard enough!My favourite is the Classic TT as they insist on calling it now, Manx Grand Prix to me and many others. A relaxing ride in the country.It works unlike the first one, bikes go round corners without throwing you off for no apparent reason.BUT!For me, it's too console in its layout, in it's menu's and in it's whole feel. In short, it's made for a console controller really which I can't use. I just use the four arrow keys, my fingers are not dexterous enough to get to any of the other mapped keys (my problem not the game maker).They should have fixed the original game not made a new one and kept that content. It just stinks of money making for the sake of it. The sort of thing I expect from Codem*****s, Ubicrp and the like in my opinion.Having said that - I still enjoy it and it is worth getting in a steam sale. _childDocuments_.review: Got it on Fanatical in that bundle for a fiver.Really enjoying it. First bike simcade game I have took to.
