I am no expert but engine sounds are satisfying and the high speed sounds are great. UI is functional. Have had zero issues on a low end system. Seemed easy enough to quickly tweak graphics for a constant 60 fps.Online seems completely dead in matchmaking terms.Overall a fun and playable game with just enough realism to make it fun. You will crash but it is nearly always obvious what the mistake was. Campaign is straight forward. Just always check race lengths before you commit. Full TT is over an hour of non stop racing.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been obsessed with the Isle of Man TT race for over 20 years. I even had a 2000 Audi TT back in the day. I bought Ride on the Edge 1 and got a refund for it. This one though is amazing. It's really hard at first, but I am getting better. I have no clue how people are doing 14-15 min lap times though on the mountain course. I'm still 3 min slower than that, but I will keep grinding. As someone else said, therapy is expensive and this game is therapy for me. My 3 year son also loves it and he's learned a lot about motorcycles from it. I was about to buy it for Switch for $60, but saw it cheaper on Steam and can play via steam link on the TV, so all good there. It's really a great game and wouldn't hesitate buying it if you like motorbikes and/or the Isle of Man TT race.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game play, the riding simulation feels like a motorbike.However.AI opponents can seem a little too aggressive and could do with tempering I have been knocked out of the race by AI crashing into me a lot. Also the bike setup could be reviewed for the next incarnation. Simple stuff like sprocket changes for gearing setup or being able to change the rake angle for changing rate of steer. Buying more advanced or tuned kit for the bikes doesn't have to include weight saving. It would be good if the developers go race meetings from club level up to see how bike development progresses and maybe puts that into the next generation.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Although the graphics are OK, This versions bike physics are totally not realistic at all.   This game and a lot of others like it now have changed the way the bikes handle and it is so fake and arcade like, it no way resembles how a real bike would behave. You get the the feeling that the bike is floating off the tarmac, and when leaning,  the rear Tyre actually seems to float from side to side without touching the tarmac at all.  A poor way of getting the bike to seem like its leaning over more than it really is.  The original "Ride on the edge" game got  so much right apart from the crash detection system which can be annoying.   This title looks like it should belong in an arcade along with the old Hang On games by Konami back in the day. Whistles and bells is just not going to save this one. Joysticks are not recognized on PC versions either.   Watch out...Not recommended....Get the original and best......Sadly only 2/10 for what should have been an improvement, but they got so much wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game, with a very good Career mode (Ireland Championship). Graphics are great, speed sensation is waaaayyyyy better than TT 1. Very nice Sponsors management.The only thing I regret in the end is the bikes customization. The Garage and parts management is a nightmare honestly, as you don't clearly see what's missing on your bike, what you can buy or win. This whole "customization" module needs to be recoded from scratch.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I've beaten every race and won every TT all in the same season.  It is an unfinished game.  Some of the mechanics they lay out don't even work.  The ballasts perk don't add weight to your bike like they say they do, which would be amazing perks if they worked correctly.  You won't be able to stay on your bike.  Ever.  Certainly never for a full lap.  I play on the easiest setting and still found myself wiping out on perfectly even ground going in a straight line.  No matter how much you learn the track, you just won't be able to stay on the bike which makes hardcore mode pretty much impossible because if you wipe out once your season and career is over and you start from scratch.  It's fun when it's fun, but that's only because I love the real life race and want to race on it.  The game takes away from the experience for sure, but if you wanna ride superbikes on the isle of man in a video game, this seems like the only way :/The devs also, like the first one they made, completely ignore any and all complaints, even if there are like legitimate problems that they advertise as functioning correctly.  They will never update the game, even to address simple issues like making gameplay match in-game descriptions.  It's like saying "we are making an open world iron man game" and then not making it open world.  Honestly I don't even care about the bad graphics or the fact that the crowd look like OoT NPC's, I just want to be able to stay on the bike and have the game function correctly.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to racing, I mostly play simmy car games. I've always felt that motorbike games are slow and boring, but I decided to try Isle of Man on a whim, and it was awesome. The sensitivity and subtlety of the physics. The sense of speed.My eyes had been opened. I proceeded to try a couple of other motorbike games. But, no, they were still slow and boring.As far as I can tell, it's just this series.Strongly recommend.(Now please make TT Isle of Man - Ride on the Edge 3 - with VR)
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game this is great and a good strong sequel if you are a fan of bike racing games. The tracks are beautiful and I feel this is the best gaming bike feeling I have had as it feels like you can feel the dips and bumps in the road.I just wish they would get with the times and include a VR option.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have this game on the Xbox, I was fortunate enough to play the test version of the game on Steam, though. My family race bikes in real life, and between us we have played every bike racing game known to man to a high standard, so I like to think I have half a clue of what im talking about with respect to this game. Do yourself a favour and ignore the people saying the physics are better than or even similair to the milestone franchise, this game is good as a TT game, it is more playable than the first one, but the physics are still quite clearly made by people who make car games. Milestone has much more realistic physics, and its more playable and doesnt crash in mysterious ways. The TT game does a superb job at recreating the TT mountain course, if you want a TT game, obviously this is your choice unless you want to play on the old PS2 games. But if you want actual wheel to wheel racing, choose Ride3/MotoGP20.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic motorcycle game!It lets you race the famous Isle of man at 300 kph and lets you experience how big balls the riders must have to participate in the event every year. The controls are a bit weird at first,but after I found my good old joystick and dialed in the following configuration: Forward = Throttle, Backward = Brakes, Lean left and right with the x-axis and set the multiplicer of the lean to +- 2 it's awesome, but you need to practice, practice, practice to be able to race at 300 kph between the small streets and trees.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played Tourist Trophy (Pholphony) and a very old Isle of Man on PS2 before. Now I've recently bought this and MotoGP 20 and if I were to compare the two, I'd actually be playing this a lot more. The sense of speed is there - debated to be turned down a bit from previous version. The texture and sound quality are very nice and crisp. Be warned however, this game is indeed challenging. Such as having to lift when going over a pot hole or crest, which are hard to see. The weight of each bike might seem marginal on paper, but has a very obvious difference when changing direction or trying to brake hard, which I think is an important factor. The Snaefall Mountains is not the only course in this game. It is easy to enjoy if you don't have the time, to jump onto a few other courses they have on airstrips. Very flat and easy to remember and also get to understand your bike more.The downside, there are a few bugs that keep the game from easily becoming the best and some will say the physics are off. They are not wrong, but I'm not nearly as distracted with how the bikes handle as I am in MotoGP to see for myself. The curbs are something you have to stay well away from or it will certainly throw your bike off if you're going anywhere above 100mph. The AI are fairly easy in career, but easily spread out just half way through the race. I think of it as over compensating for the players to keep you "in the pack feeling competitive".Overall, the game is not fully polished like it could be, but when given a chance with some patience, this can be fully immersive. When doing the full course, even in career, I believe it would be wise to first run a time trial. That's a lot of ground to cover and it's important to know where you're going at such speeds.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: What an exhilarating experience!  The since of speed is awsome.  The learning curve is steep.  The tracks take time and practice...PRACTICE.  You will come off the bike often until you learn.  You must memorize the tracks including all the holes and dips.  I give the sound a solid 8 or 9.  I use a butt kicker and it really adds to the immersion.  You can really feel the bike with it.  This sim is a 9 out of 10 easy.  I never give 10's.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Most satisfying game I have played in a long time.   Really captures the feel of speed, and with simulation settings is quite unforgiving.  Just really enjoy shaving seconds off my lap records and improving.  Can't say i have encountered any glitches so far, and i generally try to break games.Nerds complaining with .2 hours lol, that was me until i customized my controls and changed driving assists.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Is this early development or what?Controls are weird, and it's hard to do anything with it as the bindings menu is unreadable, and it responds to some weird fashion. I didn't find a way to get the throttle to the controller as every attempt to bind the axis ends up in the menu moving somewhere else. The tutorial looks unfinished too.Otherwise, it's a bike simulator on PC. What can you expect?I was riding bikes for more than 20 years, the last bike simulator I played was MotoRacer in 1997. I wouldn't say the experience is miles away...While car simulators can get very realistic, this still has nothing in common with riding the bike, maybe except to show how dangerous it can be.If you have plenty of time, love bikes, and they fix the menus and controls, then probably it can be fun.Just don't expect that, unlike car simulators, it'll actually be like riding a bike.I only tried it during the free weekend, but I'm uninstalling it right away as there's nothing interesting for me here. But thanks to Steam and the developers that they allow such testing so that we can quickly learn if the game is for us or not.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very promising once you get the hang of the controls and don't try to go flat out all the time and crash! Yes, frustrating but the thrill level brings you back. Only play in first person so that makes it harder. The much complained about first person views are exaggerated. Just needs a custom championship and AI custom difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: MASSIVE THUMBS UP FOR THIS GAME.Bought this game last night with mixed thoughts because of the way the first game was.i watched heaps of game play on youtube for this game for a few days and last night decided to bight the bullet.it is now 2am and i have got a solid 3 hours into the game so far and i am loving every second of this game.the handling has and is 100% changed now. the bike feels alot more grounded now.I tried a few times with the first game but just didnt like it.but i recommend this one for sure.while i am racing the game looks so bloody beautiful i dont no what to look at, the bike the scenery, the road, the crowds, the trees, the water, the sun, lol every part of this game just look amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Good motorcycle simcade racer. Gorgeous graphics and impressive track details, not only on the IoMTT track. I really love how this game looks. The Snaefell mountain course is the highlight of course, but lapping a lake in Ireland or free roaming along the Irish coast line in the sunset is immensely enjoyable too.Physics and controls are way better compared to part 1, but not on the level of Milestones MotoGP 2019.Content wise the career mode is better but could easily be improved further. I would also enjoy more bikes. There is no R1, no GSX-R 1000, no Panigale V4...In the end this game is about the IoMTT though, and about the rush of speed. Blasting around the Snaefell Mountain in this game feels absolutely great. So if this is what you are looking for, I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good improvement to TT 1.  There are black tar dots on my motorcycle wind guard. Does anyone know how to reset as not to have the spots hindering your vision? Messing around with settings to get the best smooth play on some of the NVidia graphic cards GTX1070 (OK), RTX2080Ti (Having video issues) ta little bit of rubber-banding video surrounding trees/shrubs when accelerating and slowing down. Gives me a headache/vertigo within 30+ minutes.  has something to do with distance camera or NVidia G-Sync while V-Sync is turned on in the game. I'm sure it'll be optimized sooner or later. For some reason KT Racing has this issue (WRC 8, V-Rally 4) when titles 1st come out for some reason. They usually fix it within a reasonable amount of time.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: In general this game is great! The sense of speed and thrill is amazing! I didn't read all the reviews, but for me a few things stand out on the bad side. The learning curve is very steep... I understand in the real deal, there is no respawning etc, but I would of liked a bit more options in terms of difficulty. Like next to raceline enabling, also show a gear indicator for corners, so you can judge the corner better when you didn't remember all 60km's of the track (or whatever track). Those simple corner lines show some degree of what is coming, bit still very hard to judge.  Maybe even a rewind option (yes that is very arcady I know)? You want hardcore? Just turn it off. Now it's very frustrating at times. The handling sucks a lot of times. The unexplained wipe outs are very very very annoying, even game breaking!I own a simrig with Fanatec and Heusinkveld gear, and I got it to run with the steering wheel and pedals, but without forcefeedback. I know it might sound stupid, but the controls with a wheel are much much smoother. I just can't get used to the controller, after spending years racing with a wheel and normal gaming with mouse and keyboard. If somehow forcefeedback could be intergrated, this would be epic for sure! Really amazing when done right I think.All in all the game seems a bit rough on the handling and graphics side, like it was rushed to finish. I hope some (or all) above will be adressed in the future asap. 7 of of 10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: First impression was "not again same crap", but after couple days I found this new version way better than the original one. No more those stupid rear wheel slides, bike is better to ride and AI don't overrun you anymore like raging bunch of crazy bulls. Mountain course looks as good as ever, new tracks are ok and speed really feels. Little tweaking needed here and there, but overall I like this.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: + the graphics are just a bit sharper and the physics and 3th person cameras are realy well done.+ the carreer mode is nice and there are some nice and fast tracks to compete at.-2 days after release only found 1 guy playing online.     tryed a few times to see if there was anyone hosting.     but no success there.-there are NO ghost times to download AT ALL ...  driving with first person cam  feels somewhat harder, but all that sayed, i think its all a matter of practice ;)
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: i love it great bike handling , nice graphic with awesome weather changing .Still need some patches the sound bug from the first one is back and some other things but nothing game breaking .the best and realistic bike game 10000 times better than this milestone garbage .hope they will get the Motogp license too
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not a biker in life but my god what a fantastic sense of speed you get in this game i am loving it so far it's pretty beautiful in motion too and runs at a locked 120fps @ 3440 x 1440p on my setup.Would be nice if they could add rain or damp conditions at some point in the future.Defo worth a buy imo and i have only played it for 49mins.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic physics, little to zero safety cushion, but once you start getting used to the bike it gets a lot easier to avoid crashes. Take it easy initially, do some free roam to get used to the bikes handling and you will improve. Love the free roam mode, lets you get out and have a nice relaxing ride (at 150 mph) around the country side. Career seems well stocked with plenty of race options and upgrades. Would have been nice to be able to buy named bike parts ala Ride 3. Have to use cockpit mode, it literally feels as close to riding an actual bike a game has got. I have been riding motorbikes for 25 years and played nearly every bike racing game in this time, for sheer simulation I would go for this one every time, exhilarating experience. Great simulation and as there is no TT this year, it will more than fill the void until next years.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: TT 2 takes what made the first game great and made it even better! There is simply no other motorcycle game that makes you feel like you're going 250 km/h like TT does (in first person view). From the sound effects to the rider/player perspective shaking from the wind to the bumps in the road throwing you all over the place. This game makes you feel totally out of control; in control.With a great improvement to the career mode that actually makes it worth while whilst adding a bit more variety to the roster is nice it would have been great to see a bit more in terms of the actual bikes themselves. I feel as though RIDE has this downpat in comparison but the actual riding in TT is way better and much more challenging. The only real flaw I have at this point is the effect of bumps or crests of hills seem to be a lot more unforgiving in this game which is fine as its something to get used to but when using the race line to learn the tracks it seems to think there are bumps etc. and tells you to slow down where there really arent any.I would definitely recommend picking up this game if you're a fan of motorbikes or simply want to push yourself to the limit to see how fast you can go before you send your motorcycle over the fence and into someones backyard or perhaps of a cliff. Its still too early to get any deeper than this and ill update my review after I've played a bit more but I hope this helps :)
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle of Man: Ride on the Edge 2

_childDocuments_.review: Meticulously detailed Mountain Course replicated with each stretch and bend of the circuit. OFFICIAL RIDERS AND THEIR SUPER-POWERED BIKES - 24 riders, 38 bikes, and sidecars rocketing along village and mountain roads at 200 mph.

name: Before Your Eyes
detailed_description: Before Your Eyes is a first person narrative adventure which tells the story of a soul’s journey into the afterlife using a new and innovative form of interaction—your real-life blinks. The story begins after your death, aboard the ship of a mythical Ferryman tasked with shepherding souls to the afterlife. In order to help you pass on, he must first learn the story of your life. And so, he sends you back to relive your most important moments. The game uses your webcam to immerse you in this story in a way you've never experienced before. You will learn to control the flow of the narrative with your actual eyes–blinking through precious memories of family, first love, and the rise of an artistic career. But soon the Ferryman will suspect you aren't showing him everything he needs to see. So he will force you deeper into the dark recesses of your most repressed memories, ultimately revealing a heartbreaking truth. By combining its innovative blink interaction mechanic with a charming world and a fully voice-acted story, Before Your Eyes is a deeply emotional and relatable journey—one about the impossible expectations we place on ourselves and the regrets we carry with us. An earlier version of the game, titled  Close Your , received the Game Developers Choice award at Indiecade and the Student Award at the Independent Game Awards (IGF), before receiving funding through a successful Kickstarter campaign. CW: Before Your Eyes deals with themes of death, illness and grief

_childDocuments_.review: A long time ago, a game called "That Dragon, Cancer" was released. It might not have been the first, but it marks a change to me - of games being more than just toys or distractions, of them trying to tell real stories.(I actually think TDC fell a little flat - apart from one brilliant scene that actually managed to combine interactivity and the painful notes of the story).This is one that does it right. It wasn't without flaw, but I laughed, I cried, and the simple hook just... worked. I forgot I was even playing something.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Before Your Eyes with high expectations, I mean how could I not with all the praise this game gets. But I wasn't ready for what was in store.My expectations were beyond exceeded. The story is a 10/10, the art style is super unique and fits this game so well, and the blink mechanic is one of the most unique and immersive things I've ever experienced in a video game. If you have never played this game before the $10 price tag is 100% worth it. Games don't usually make me emotional, but I balled my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ eyes out at the end of this game. Before Your Eyes is a master peace that well beyond exceeded my expectations. defiantly a 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: My all time favorite game, and with less than 2 hours of playtime. Along with the first time I've cried in 3 years. I love this game more than any other. Plus I had to hug my mom and girlfriend afterwards. If you are reading this deciding whether to buy It or not. BUY IT. it will be the best  $19 you have ever spent
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you do a story driven videogame. It is a story that can ONLY be told through the interactive medium, it's not just throwing narratives and cutscenes at you. You struggle to keep yourself from blinking to linger on moments that you feel for. You rapidly advance through moments as you blink and hold back tears when it gets overly emotional. Absolutely perfect use of mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot put into words how beautifully sad this game is. Be prepared to cry many tears at the conclusion of this game. Also having to work to jeep your eyes open to experience more of the game's story is brilliant, and makes it a fun challenge to see how much you can experience on your first play through. If I could lose my memory of this game and experience it again, I would, nevertheless it is an experience and story that will stay with me for a long time. Please play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: The game is by far both an amazing concept of game play and ability of story telling. The story is so amazing that you wish you couldn't feel your eyes get teared or dry because you wish to stay in some moments, "Stay Here" with some people. I haven't played through the multiple story lines I'm assuming occur, and won't spoil any events, but the journey amounts to the same destination and is beautiful even viewed through altered perceptions of just how "great" we could be if we get there.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games i've ever played.It really shows how you don't need crazy mechanics to make an enjoyable game.just look around and blink.I really like the option to disable the blinking thing, so people who have trouble keeping their eyes open can still enjoy the game.10/10 would reccomend fs fs
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to stream the first play of this game... Big mistake, now people saw me crying on live.This game is a piece of art, in every way. Not only it has an amazing story, but an awesome art direction and the accompainment music fits perfectly and helps you feel the story even more.If you are doubting to make the purchase, go ahead, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: There are very few games that have the ability to make us realize our own mortality. Before Your Eyes is one of them. And more importantly, why it's worth living. It's less of a game but more of an experience. You will find yourself reliving scrapes of your childhood, and seeing it through someone else's life.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of a game controlled by blinking seems like a gimmick, but it really just adds a lot of immersion to the game. Using the player's inability to stop themselves from eventually having to blink is an extremely clever way to relate to the character's inability to stop the passing of time. You will involuntarily miss parts, but that's just life, isn't it?I can't exactly class this as a walking simulator, since there really isn't any walking, but it was completely narrative driven and the depth of story reminded me greatly of games like What Remains of Edith Finch and Firewatch - both of which I also enjoyed greatly. It isn't a long game, but it was absolutely worth my time and it was worth the money I paid for it. There are many reasons to re-play this game from making different choices and getting achievements, to simply trying harder to not blink my way through conversations i wanted to hear. I'd recommend this for anyone who particularly enjoys story-driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this simple narrative game that is played by blinking? Man life is put into perspective after this.The game is a beautiful story, that takes you through the life of a man named Benny. The story takes you through the person life and hardships. You see them as if they were something everyone goes through but this game shows you that there is more to every story than you think. It shows you how much the people in our lives mean to us. I dont want to say much because I dont want to spoil any thing for this game but IT IS A MUST PLAY!!!! I only wish it didnt make me cry as much because thanks to the tears I blinked much more than I should have.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a heart warming yet tear jerking story you need to play this game. 100/10 this game made me bawl my eyes out and I loved every moment of it. I definitely recommend playing with a webcam, the eye tracking is almost integral I'd say to enjoying the full depth and feel of the story. The pressure to not blink in such beautiful moments. *p l e a s e* play this game, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Back in college, I wrote an argumentative paper for why video games should be considered art. During my research, I learned that a lot of idea behind what a piece of art actually is is about the experience you get from it. But one major criticism against the idea of games as an artistic medium was the fact that games were made up of many different mediums of art and that the player has control over the experience and therefore lessens the experience unless you boil it down to an interactive film/movie. And when looking for examples of games that could be considered art that combat this stance, many different games caught my eye for different reasons because they used interactive elements to enhance the experience rather than take away from it. Games like Gris, Flower, That Dragon Cancer, and Journey all checked the boxes I was looking for.2 years later and after playing this game, I wish I could've added Before Your Eyes to that list. Its about an hour and a half and pretty cheap. If you're not pressed for cash, buy it at full price. If you are, wait for a sale. Regardless of how much you buy this for, I think you'll be hard pressed to put a price tag on the feelings you'll be left with once you finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. I could kinda predict the story, but I loved how they played with the mechanics. The webcame-mechanic was really fun and it mostly worked pretty well. When it didn't, it was probably my own fault for being too close to the window. The graphics were a lot of fun and the characters were interesting. I played the game for 1,9 hours, and probably will replay it sometime in the future. I recommend the game for people who like storydriven games and fun minigames.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before your eyes is one of the few games these days that has made me honestly cry. The game is a beautiful tale of the fear of a life that didn't live up to its full potential, and it exceeds every word that could ever be written about it. Please go play this game. It deserves your attention and is a beautiful story worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game that gets you frustrated if you cant hold your blinks! The game is really really good, well made and the blink interaction works flawlessly. Please use a webcam as it is really needed to get the full experience.This game is personally a nostalgia trip for me and the emotions i felt in this game felt real!I was crying at the end of the game and had a breakdown. It's completely worth the money i spent!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this. It’s an intriguing concept, which tells a story about childhood and a little bit of adolescence though exploring the blinking mechanic and the philosophy of time passing in the blink of an eye. The ending is powerful, although I thought a different story could have said something more insightful about life had it gone further into adulthood and dug deeper into the themes it was exploring. I encourage the developers to continue making games that explore the complexities of life and emotions.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished a blind playthrough and cried like a baby for the last 10 minutes. Bought it because it was on sale and I thought it looked neat, but I would absolutely have paid full price. It's about a two hour long experience and is really best enjoyed in one sitting if you can.Absolutely incredible game. Don't read any walkthroughs or guides or spoilers until you're finished, it's absolutely worth going in without knowing anything (though if the themes discussed in the content warning are things you're sensitive to, be aware that this game does not pull any punches.)
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much! I'd recommend this to everyone. The story was beautifully told and thought-provoking. The eye tracking integrated into the gameplay was unique and a change of pace from other games. It was hard to keep my eyes open by the end of the story when I was crying. This was such a great experience and well worth the money. I'm looking forward to other games like this from the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review for a game before, but I had to for this. I can't remember the last time I was moved this much by a story. It's beautiful, moving, sad, and touching all at the same time. This is a wonderful work of art. Go into it knowing as little as possible, and just give it the attention it deserves. So glad I decided to give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I spent the whole game thinking, "Yeah, this is pretty good, don't know how invested I am though," and then the last scene hit and the tears started flowing. Made it very hard not to blink, not that it mattered anymore. Absolutely incredible way to tell a story. Had very few issues with blink detection.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect, but this game certainly touched on emotions I didn't even know I had, the story is so emotional and told in such manner I fought against my eyes not to blink those moments away. The ending absolutely broke me and I found myself crying like a baby when I first realized what the game was really about.Recommend it 100%, wish I could forget it just so I could experience it again, the time really did go by in the blink of an eye.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Not exeagerating nor lying when i say this; i have never cried so hard due to any piece of media nor storytelling out there.Theres a reason for this games BAFTA award, this game truly trancends what a game is, and has such incredibly fleshed out and empowering storytelling. Its pure art, i highly reccomend it to anyone out there, especially with how cheaply it goes for on sale. _childDocuments_.review: A first-person story-based game that's somewhere between a movie and a walking-simulator, with the gimmick that you can control the scenes by blinking.• The story is delightful and emotional.  The beginning is a bit slow, but the setup is worth it in the end.• Every character is fully voice-acted, and the voice acting is done well.• The modeling and art-direction were also good.• The blinking feature is absolutely terrible , but fortunately you can play with normal mouse-clicks instead.• There is no walking in this game. The only interaction you have is looking around with the mouse, and clicking (or blinking) on things.• There's about two hours of content.  There is some replayability, but given how this game is purely story-driven, I think most people will not replay it.• At one point I got soft-locked and had to reset my game.  Fortunately there was an auto-save about a minute prior.  Aside from this , the game was not buggy.• While I really enjoyed the ending, I know some people will be upset about it because (spoilers!) • The gimmick for this game is that you can control the scenes by blinking.  I bought a webcam specifically to try this out.  Unfortunately, . Even after getting the lighting perfect and calibrating for 20 minutes, the game frequently struggled to determine whether or not I had just blinked.  In particular, when I looked down at the bottom of the screen, the game frequently incorrectly registered a blink. The way this game is setup, that's absolutely . Which brings me to my next point...• For some reason the devs thought it would be a good idea to allow scenes to be skippable halfway through the scene, meaning if you accidentally blink you miss a bunch of content. Even worse, some of these scenes are tied to achievements. This means that, even if the blinking feature actually worked, you'd have to hold your eyes open "Clockwork Orange"-style in order to not miss content/achievements.  I get the metaphor - that life passes you by in the blink of an eye - but as a feature in a video game it is frustrating and unfun.• The indicator that a scene can be skipped is shown at the bottom of the screen.  Remember, every time I looked at the bottom of the screen, the game thought I blinked. This means that every time the scene became skippable, I would look down and ** the scene would be immediately skipped.  Argh!I think this game is worth the price for anyone looking for a good story.  Just make sure to disable the atrocious blinking feature.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've struggled with depression and serious suicidal thoughts in the past, and would not describe myself as a "happy" person. However, this game inspired me to take life seriously and believe that at the very least I can work on being happier, even if it takes a long time. There's always going to be issues and I may never get fully to a state of feeling "whole" but that doesn't mean that life isn't worth living, or that I'm failing at life. It's okay to feel like your life is one giant series of mess ups and that when you die you'll be filled with regret at what you haven't had a chance to do. But this game affirmatively states that this is not the case; that whenever you do die, prematurely or not, you'll have already live a great life, a whole life. And honestly, for me that was something that was so relieving to hear. There's so many expectations about what the right life lived is supposed to be, what checkpoints and goals you need to reach for your life to count as "well-spent". But in reality, just living in the moment, being alive, making memories, no matter how mundane they may be, that is enough in itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I love, love, love arty, beautiful, narrative video games that make me cry... And this is definitely one of them. In the beginning of the game, you open your eyes on a boat in the afterlife, awaiting judgment. The boat is piloted by a blue coyote man, a Charon-type character, who is trying to understand the narrative of your life so that he can explain it to the Gatekeeper (I don't want to spoil it, but you'll love seeing the "god" of this world once she appears). The game takes you on a beautiful journey through memories, and when you physically blink (your computer webcam captures your eye movements), your memories leap forward in the story that was your life. The mechanics of the game are cool and really unique, focusing on blinking as your primary tool. It's neat and also frustrating because it takes away some of your control of the pace of the story since it's hard to control when you blink. I also played it without the blink function on, just using the mouse, which was fun too and gave me a lot more flexibility -- but I'd definitely recommend using the camera for the first run through. The story that unfolds is so lovely, funny, deeply sad, and sweet. It's a short game that's possible to complete in about 2 hours. About an hour in, it gets very sad and moving, and I sniffled through the extremely compelling second half of the game. The graphics are simple but beautiful, and the memories are revealed in sort of bubbles or clouds, just a bit at a time, which does give everything a really dreamy, memory-like quality. There aren't really puzzles or action -- the game is very focused on creatively unfolding narrative through navigating with the mouse and blinking -- but the story really pulls you along and doesn't drag or feel repetitive. I highly recommend this lovely game.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is one of the best story games I have ever played. It's an incredibly emotional game that is easy to immerse yourself in. It's a well-written story where each choice you make will affect your life in different ways. This is the second game throughout my entire life that brought me to tears. I really enjoyed this game, and for the price of $6 CAD it is one of the best short story games you can get.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I've left both serious and sarcastic reviews for games here on Steam before, and I have only played through Before Your Eyes once, but that's all I need to play to put this game into words. This game is extremely well written and executed, and I found the new blinking mechanic to actually end up taking a backseat to what is an unbelievable story. I would recommend this game based off of the mechanic alone, but the melancholy nature of the story and the twists and turns that are in store for those that play it are completely worth the price of the game. You learn to love the characters and the story finds ways to make you think and appreciate what is in front of you, as it could be gone in an instant.I'm not going to spoil the game by any means, but the story will have you left with many questions that can only be answered by playing the game again. There were a couple of times where my camera picked up a blink that didn't happen, so it could be optimized just a bit better, but it really hammers home the point, time passes by so quickly. I can't recommend this game enough, and I will be playing through it again to see what other things I missed within this beautiful story.Story: 10/10Mechanics: 8.5/10Overall: 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a masterpiece of a game. The game is cheap and you can get a full movie's worth of tears, laughs, and overall a great experience. The ending is what truly made this game something special. I recommend it to anyone who's seeking a new adventure into the world that is another's life. 10/10

THAT BEING SAID, I absolutely, unequivocally, 100% would not ever in ten million years have played this game if I had known that there was a scene involving the death of multiple pet animals. I'm not spoilering this because I wish I had known about it before going in, and I imagine many others would like to know as well. This scene is not warned about before-hand, and is really unnecessary and uncalled for in how graphic it is. Call me a ♥♥♥♥♥ about it all you want, but this scene is really something that should've at least had a trigger warning because it's pretty graphic, and is one of two scenes that the game actually FORCES you to watch.I liked the game overall, but I can't recommend it to people who don't know what they're getting into, and have seen zero other reviews talking about this.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin?If you love a good story, this game is for you.If you want something you can sit down and play in one sitting, this game is for you.If you love a good soundtrack, this game is for you.This game is amazing. Every little detail in this game matters in the most amazing way possible. The attention to detail the developers added to scenes is amazing. This game is stunning to look at, and even the smallest interactions have some amazing effects on the environment. Take your time to look at everything since it's the only thing you can do. The game uses every tool at it's disposal to make you treasure what's around you by using sight alone. All it takes is a single blink, and that thing that caught your eye or that touching moment could be gone in an instant. I have never wanted to hear the end of a meaningless conversation as badly as I have playing this game. Knowing that what you're experiencing can be gone the second you close your eyes puts weight I cannot explain on every choice you make. I actually found myself struggling to keep my eyes open at points just so I could stay in the moment longer. The story is such a masterpiece too, and the choices available add replayability to the game (though nothing beats the magic of that first time). Each character feels alive, each scene deepens your connection even if just a little bit. There's so much more I wish I could say about this game, but I fear spoiling it.Moving on to what I liked and disliked about the game. The game is fairly short, but due to the price I wasn't bothered by it. I honestly would've gladly paid more just because of how amazing this game was.Liked-cheap game-short run time, can be played in one sitting-great with friends, backseat gaming is fun for choices-great alternative to a movie if you want something interactive-amazing soundtrack-top tier voice acting for some of the main charactersDisliked-if you stream, be aware you have to give the game webcam priority-has an onscreen webcam feature, but the dimensions are weird-blink detection isn't perfect, can sometimes ruin a moment. I suspect a better camera might helpI played this game start to finish live on stream. If you'd rather watch it than play it, feel free to check the recording out at .

_childDocuments_.review: The game's narrative is both heartwarming and heartbreaking, filled with moments of pure joy and profound sadness. The simple act of blinking becomes a powerful tool, propelling you through Benjamin's life, emphasizing the rapid passage of time.The game's visual style is charming and evocative, perfectly complementing the emotional depth of the story. The soundtrack is equally impactful, underscoring the poignant moments with its gentle melodies and somber tonesHowever, it's the innovative control scheme that truly sets Before Your Eyes apart. By using your blinks, you become an active participant in Benjamin's journey, feeling the weight of each passing moment. It's a truly unique and immersive experience that will stay with you long after the credits roll. TBH I was so full of emotions i sticked out and check the credits roll out to the end myself. It was on my wishlist and i was trying to find my free time to try this game out , and today was the day i played and completed this wholesome game , It is a game that will make you laugh, cry, and reflect on your own life. It's a reminder to cherish every moment, no matter how small, and to live life to the fullest. This is a game that deserves to be experienced, a game that will stay with you long after the final blink.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is much less of a game than it is an experience; however, what this game is able to achieve in such a small amount of playtime is truly incredible. Its beautiful narrative combined with the special and interesting gameplay mechanic create an emotional and “eye-opening” experience. As you take on the life of a boy named Benjamin Brynn, you will find yourself immersed in his story. The voice acting, graphics, soundtrack, etc, all beautifully paint the picture of Benjamin’s life and engross you in it. For its small price of ten dollars (compared to some other games), I was given a short, 1 hour emotional and impactful experience that was worth every penny. If you give this indie game a chance, you will be pleasantly rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I like the idea, professional voice acting and the story, definitely. But something completely broke my immersion.1) At first, the blinking system was like fresh air. You just need to control the mouse and leave the rest to your eyes. However, I found it hard to not blink (which I think that it's a personal issue). Whenever I want to read the story, I just couldn't help but blink. The tempo of reading the story is not good for me. So I disabled it at the first quarter of the game.2) I will try not to spoil here. At certain point of the game, an ambient sound will take over the whole auditory experience. I just can't stand the bad volume balance at that point. Low-mid range frequency is a mess. It's pretty disastrous. I guess the idea is to make players feel overwhelmed (which corresponds to that scenario), but it's totally not working for me. No sound options to adjust.3) Glitches and clipping. BYE should have the emphasis on storytelling. When the story comes to a climax, I often see characters making moves that cause clipping. It's like at some point I just need a little bit more to cry, but that ruins everything. From my perspective, most of the clippings happened in mo-cap moves. And another thing to mention is the lighting, a serious problem in my playthrough. I don't know the problem comes from 2D lighting sprites z-fighting or what (there's probably minimum dynamic lighting usages in BYE), the shadows just keep flickering.4) Black screen. I couldn't remember how to reproduce it, it just happened randomly about 2 times. I like story-rich games, I really do. Nevertheless, technical issues everywhere.I don't recommend this one if you are looking for total immersive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a first person, narrative-centred game that has a run time of only around one and a half hours, but manages to pack a punch and tug at your heartstrings even in this short span of time. Though gameplay wise it is a pretty simple adventure game, Before Your Eyes implements blink interaction mechanics that impact the gameplay which is fascinating and something I've personally never seen before.(NO SPOILERS, THIS IS JUST A SUMMARY)You play as a soul on a ferry, on your way to be judged based on how you lived your life before you died. The player gets to watch their character's whole life unfold, and though this sounds daunting the game very conveniently and very smoothly moves us through digestible stages of our character's life each time we blink. From his childhood, to his teenage years, adulthood, and so on.I found myself relating a lot to some of the characters in this game, and as I read reviews it seems many other players felt the same way. We are pulled into the family's dynamic and grow a relationship with all of them - some we grow to love, others not so much, but no character in this narrative is a binary "good" or "bad". This is one narrative strength of Before Your Eyes; every individual is complex and neither good nor bad. They're so organically human that we almost forget they're pixels on a screen.Another factor playing into this realism is the phenomenal voice acting. Sarah Burns' performance as Elle was so, so poignant and deliciously heartbreaking. Due to there being such a small team behind the game, Stephen Friedrich has to voice four characters, but you wouldn't be able to tell unless you looked it up! Each character is distinct and vastly different; his performance as The Ferryman is particularly stunning, though.The game keeps giving reasons to adore it, having incredible visuals on top of a harrowing storyline and impressive voice acting. The graphics of the game are dream-like, reminiscent to me of other indie games like Kind Words. Though characters don't have defined or realistic facial features, the art style is dreamy and heartwarmingly childish - vivid purples, blues and oranges provide a feeling of warmth that game styles don't often provide. Specifically scenes by and on the sea are beautifully surreal and whimsical in a way that cannot be described, only seen.In contrast to its art style, Before Your Eyes deals with daunting concepts like death, failure and the dread of vocation. This is largely a spoiler free review, so all I will say is that it deals with these themes beautifully and commendably. To fully understand the depth of this game's plot and the way it unforgivingly sucks you in and spits you back out, I implore you to play it yourself.Just remember not to blink too much. You don't want to miss a thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes, my friend, is not a play, it's a journey of emotions. 🌟When I play this game, it's as if my eyes slide like a movie. I can relive memories with the blink of an eye. That's why the name of the game is so apt: Before Your Eyes.At first, this may seem like a mechanical game, but you'd be wrong. This is an opportunity to relive life's most important moments. First love, loss, success, frustration... Each blink of an eye captures a memory and leaves a mark on my heart.But of course, not everything is perfect. Some memories can be painful. Losing a friend, experiencing a disappointment... But this is where the beauty of the game comes in. It's an opportunity to live these memories, to accept them and to grow.Favorite Aspects:Emotional Depth: The play is not only a visual experience, but also an emotional journey. I got tears in my eyes, man.Music: The soundtrack touched my soul. Especially the piano pieces have timbres that made me shiver.Narrative Style: The storytelling is warm and sincere. I felt as if a friend of mine was narrating.What Could Have Been Better:Gameplay Time: It felt a bit short. I would have liked to experience more moments.Graphics: Simple but impressive. But some scenes could have been more detailed.In conclusion, Before Your Eyes left a mark on my eyes and a place in my heart. Playing this game reminds me once again of the beauty and hardships of life. My friend, don't miss this play! 👁️🎮

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a lovely, heartbreaking game for those who are willing to tolerate its somewhat buggy controls. I picked up this game with the Story-Rich Mega Bundle and was immediately captivated by its summary. As someone who has somewhat limited use of both hands, finding games that are point and click only has been my only real way to enjoy gaming without causing myself intense pain. This seemed like a level up: a game that only used my *eyes*? What a perfect game for people in my situation, or with other injuries or disabilities making hand use a challenge. For those who have zero use of their hands, I will unfortunately inform them that there is still some mouse use required. (The game requires dragging the mouse around screen in order to view surroundings, and some small, constrained motions to engage with the environment.) That said, an Xbox or other adaptive controller could provide a simple alternative. The blinking mechanics are a bit unreliable, which is unfortunate for a game that relies on them so heavily. I attempted to calibrate before my first runthrough and ended up irritated before I'd even started. Any dramatic motion seemed to be registered as a blink at first; then, upon toning down the sensitivity, even very deliberate blinking was only intermittently recognized by the system. Fortunately, upon actually playing, these issues seemed to die down a bit--or, at least, I was immersed enough in the story that I didn't mind too much. I won't comment on the story in detail, because it is best to come into the narrative with no preconceived notions. That said, I will say that it is clever, and there are some truly interesting bits of character design. I've played a lot of small, indie games with sentimental stories; this one will be memorable, if only for how thoughtfully the story and the design interweave. I do wholeheartedly recommend it for people who are looking for something simpler, sweeter, not necessarily polished, but absolutely made with love.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: for those whose game crashes around the middle or later chapter of the game, and found out that changing the game resolution or quality settings didn't help. I have been contacted by the developer and they have provided me with a new solution. Track down and delete the file webcaminfor.json located atDelete C:\Users\username\AppData\LocalLow\Goodbye World\Before Your Eyes\webcamInfo.jsonOnce you do so and booted up the game again, you should be able to continue the chapter where you left off. I hope this helps. I am so frustrated, I want to give this game a Yes but the game keep crashing on me. I am on chapter 13, I want to know what happens next so badly and I cant continue the game. Whenever I clicked the continue button, I am met with a with black screen and the unity error message pops up and the game closes :( Idk if this is a me issue or if someone else out there have the same issue I do. I am giving this game a No for now because I don't want other people to get the same immersion breaking experience I did because the game crashed on them. Please wait for another patch to see if this issue is resolved before buying it.

It's a personal and moving story that's immediately sold with fantastic voice acting and some real hard hitting dialogue that's not afraid to go into some dark places. It should take about 2 hrs tops, which feels just right for the kind of story that it wanted to tell. Really can't recommend it enough.   PROS+ Great voice acting+ Hard hitting script+ Pleasing cartoony artstyle + Cool use of audio mixing+ Perfect running time (2-2.5 hrs)CONS- Blinking isn't as substantial as advertised - Many technical issues and frustrations took me out of the experience - Can dig a tiny bit too deep to get tears out of you Overall: 9/10 (without tech issues)              8/10 (with)Its a story that's gonna stick with me and maybe even something to come back to just to experience again. Please give it a look even if you're just the tiny bit interested. Just make sure your PC is up to the task!

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a unique narrative experience unlike any other I've played before. It put me in the shoes of a child and reminded me of how it felt to be young, to make choices and have choices made for me. Yet, the main choice that's made in this game is whether or not to blink. On average, we blink 14,400-19,200 times a day, 100,800-134,00 times a week, and 5.2-7.1 million times a year. How many times have you blinked since you started reading this review? Since you opened Steam? Since you woke up this morning?We blink as easily and naturally as we breathe, yet this game makes blinking a conscious and active decision, because each time you physically blink in the real world, you're transported in the game to another part of your life--it could be a few minutes, or it could be a few years, and you can never be sure which it will be.There were moments I wanted to hang on to, just a little bit longer because they were so wholesome.There were moments I wanted to blink away because of how awful and sad they were.Then, there were moments I completely forgot about the mechanic of the game and blinked because I was so lost in the scene.This is a deeply beautiful and emotional game about life, and what it means to have lived. It asks whether a person is great because they've done great things, or if only because they existed. It's a story about family, memories, expectations, passion, love, and how we perceive our experiences.Though Before Your Eyes is only about an hour and a half long, the trip was was worth every cent.

_childDocuments_.review: General Impression: Because 'Before Your Eyes' uses your blinks as a command prompt in the game, your experience has the potential to frustratingly stumble beneath an ill-timed webcam malfunction. However, with enough patience and troubleshooting, the game can work absolute wonders with its 'blink' mechanic, leading to one of the most emotional endings I've experienced in a game.SPOILERS****The story of Before Your Eyes is a simple one. However, by fixing that story beneath the lens of "post-death recollection", each moment you witness becomes a precious one.Despite the sharp specificity with which the characters are painted, I found myself substituting moments and feelings that the characters were undergoing with my own past experiences. Similar to great stories like "It's a Wonderful Life", "What Dreams May Come," and "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind", Before Your Eyes encourages you to reflect on potentially upsetting memories, and ultimately seeing them for the precious rarity that they are. It was a gift to play this game.I was extremely frustrated, at points, with my webcam. It would mistake my glances to the left and right of my screen for blinks, so there are crucial moments that I never got to see. In fact, a big choice the character made at one point was accidentally chosen for me, thanks to a misread "blink" from my webcam. Hopefully, your experience won't contain these kinds of frustrations, but if it does, I recommend you be patient. The story is short enough to get through that it's worth a couple pauses to re-calibrate, or even reboot your game.I had had a rough day before purchasing and playing this game. It was tough to get out of the hole I was in. But 'Before Your Eyes' coaxed me into a wonderful escape with it's beginning moments, and eventually led to a powerful and very real mirror of my own feelings. I heard what I needed to hear, and I made sure to get in touch with all those people I'd ignored who had tried to get in touch with me. This game broke the dam, and I wept, open-eyed before my webcam as the credits rolled. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Interesting mechanic that might not work for everyone (glasses wearers beware?)The blink detection is an interesting mechanic.  I was expecting scenes to change while my eyes were closed, but it's more like an alternate way of clicking that you biologically have to do, which has you fighting against your own impulses to try to hear more.  ...If only the detection worked...  I spent about 75% of the time I played trying to calibrate the blink detection, and eventually I gave up, and since that was the whole point of the game, I gave up on it too.  I wear glasses, so that was probably a large part of the issue, and it might work for others better.

_childDocuments_.review: A touching game with a meaningfully integrated concept (blinking). Definitely worth your while if you like narrative-driven games.Story- The story centres on the protagonist revisiting memories (predominantly from his childhood). I don't want to spoil anything here, so let me just say that its poignant and touches on several complex and universal themes (there's humour, sweetness, and  tragic turns). The story is short but has a lot of heart and leaves a strong impression. Gameplay- This is a 1.-2 hour narrative experience, the gameplay centres on you using your eyes (blinks) to drive exposition of particular memories or leap forward on to another memory. This was all seamless for me , I had no issues with my webcam.Visuals - A beautiful cartoon-style aesthetic which lends towards the focus on childhood memories and imagination. I had no issues running this on my PC, it doesn't seem demanding to run and I didn't experience any glitches or hitches. Very polished.Sound and Music - The voice acting is incredible in this short game. The delivery is fluid and very believable. I was thoroughly impressed. This was critical in really selling the emotional impact of the story told. Music plays an important role in the narrative (the piano in particular) and complements the tone of the memories that you revisit. Kudos to the developers for this moving game. It's also refreshing to see such a well implemented concept, it could so easily have been an annoying gimmick but in my experience it not only works flawlessly, it makes sense in terms of the story it delivers.

_childDocuments_.review: Eye detection is not something I've seen as a gameplay mechanic before so upon seeing the trailer for Before Your Eyes, I was immediately intrigued. This does mean you need a webcam if you want to play through the game with eye detection enabled, but this is an optional method. Keyboard and mouse without a webcam is an option as well.If you decide to use a webcam for eye detection, certain segments of the game will have you direct your mouse to an icon and upon blinking, more of your surroundings is unveiled. The rest of the time you're trying desperately to not blink, otherwise you'll progress through a cutscene without fully viewing it. This sounds stressful and frustrating, which it is slightly, but more akin to a memory slipping away that you're desperately trying to hold on to.This is very much a story-driven game with few choices to be made. There is some replayability if you want to try and view more from the cutscenes which you accidentally blinked through. The is an autobiography of the main character, watching as he grows from a baby onward. There is a balance of hope, love, and despair throughout the story, but I personally didn't find it as emotional as other players have.I definitely recommend just for the unique gameplay experience. It's rather short so if you buy it on Steam, beat it, and dislike it, chances are you can still get your refund.

_childDocuments_.review: "Before Your Eyes" is not just a game; it's an emotional journey that transcends the boundaries of traditional interactive storytelling. From the very start, this game captivates players with a unique and innovative mechanic that hooks you in a deeply personal way – by tracking your blinks. But it's not just the gameplay that makes "Before Your Eyes" exceptional; it's the profound and introspective narrative that unfolds as you blink through the protagonist's life.At its core, "Before Your Eyes" is a poignant exploration of the fleeting nature of life and the importance of cherishing every moment. The story weaves through the life of a character as they reflect on their past, relationships, and the choices they've made. The narrative is expertly crafted, guiding players through various stages of the protagonist's life, each moment imbued with emotion and significance.The theme of embracing the present instead of dwelling on the past or worrying about the future is beautifully portrayed throughout the game. As players blink to transition between memories, they are forced to confront the reality of time's passage. This clever mechanic serves as a poignant reminder that life is a series of fleeting moments that should be treasured and lived fully.The brilliance of "Before Your Eyes" lies in its ability to evoke genuine emotions. As you witness the characters' growth, struggles, and triumphs, you become intimately connected to their experiences. The voice acting, music, and art style all work in harmony to amplify the emotional impact of the narrative.The story's bittersweet twist at the end is where "Before Your Eyes" truly shines. Without giving away spoilers, the conclusion delivers a powerful message about memory, reflection, and the inevitable nature of change. It forces players to question their own experiences and the moments they choose to hold onto."Will I remember?" This haunting question lingers long after the game ends. It encapsulates the heart of the game's message – that our memories, experiences, and relationships are what shape us, and it's up to us to choose how to remember them.In a world saturated with video games that focus on action and competition, "Before Your Eyes" stands as a remarkable departure. It's an interactive masterpiece that engages the player's heart and mind, leaving a lasting impact that extends far beyond the screen. This game reminds us that life is a beautiful tapestry of moments, both big and small, and it encourages us to embrace them all with open hearts."Before Your Eyes" is a testament to the artistry of game developers who dare to push the boundaries of storytelling. It's a triumph in its ability to make players not just think, but truly feel. If you're looking for a game that challenges your perspective on life, love, and the passage of time, "Before Your Eyes" is an experience you won't want to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: If you got about 2 hours to spare, make sure you do it with this one.It's been a while since I played that game. But every time I just think about it, it brings me to tears.This game allows you to play purely with your mouse; the webcam is OPTIONAL. It advertises strongly on you needing a webcam to play it, and while it adds to the experience, I feel it's not necessary.Now this game is another one heavy on the story side. What I almost love more than the game itself is the music. Its implementation of the webcam is unique, but that's about it for gameplay. You're just there to witness, and tell your story.You have died. A ferryman fishes your soul out of an eternal sea. While you're travelling, he wants to hear your story. What do you remember of your life? What made your life so great? What made your soul so valueable?So you go back to the very beginning... and you start telling your story. About the decisions you've made. How you grew up. What interests you've had. The people you've met and loved. The life you pursued and the dreams you chased.This story filled me with all sorts of emotions. It was so fun, and colorful! So happy and loving! It almost makes you sad for how perfect it all was.But... this is life. You will find that good things can't always stay this way.And it is frightening. It is very, very frightening. I swear I have never seen any game deliver the feeling of death as strongly as this one. It took my breath away.In the end, it helped me. To understand; all of this.This game delivers a message most powerful. If you are struggling, take a seat, and take a look within.

I'd love to play the game, but the way the game is designed literally won't let me.

_childDocuments_.review: Blinking as a novelty mechanic to emphasize an existentially emotional narrative like this is brilliant. I've played through it multiple times, and did in fact cry. Talking about the story in a review feels like it would genuinely lessen the impact of a blind playthrough, so I'll just say that it is a short but unique experience that's worth trying for anyone who values video games as a medium for art. Also, credit to the developers for including accessibility options for anyone with potential issues involving the physical act of blinking (you can use the mouse to blink if necessary), even though it could theoretically undermine the central mechanic of the game. Definitely in my top 5 games that tell a story in a way no other medium really could!

_childDocuments_.review: If the incredibly heartfelt and well written story with twists and turns and tearjerker moments doesn't convince you, at least play it because it's unique from a gameplay/storytelling perspective.Cinema began to blossom once screenwriters and directors fully used the potential of the new visual medium (show, don't tell!). In gaming, we see a similar trend of stories that go beyond just "telling" and "showing". This game's blinking mechanic is more than just a gimmick, it's the central action to further the story. If you just happened to blink accidentally, you may skip the memory, which is equivalent to not remembering too well, and if you want to stay in the memory, you try and keep your eyes open, straining yourself to hold on.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this is going to be something of a hot take. The story here didn't really hit me hard. Don't get me wrong, it's sad and all that, it just didn't do anything for me.What I will praise this game for is the phenomenally innovative mechanics. Tracking your blinks to progress the game? What a wonderfully novel idea! And the fact that it's so accessible and does it so well is something else. The story may hit you harder than it hit me, it may hit you less hard than it hit me. Regardless of the impact it has on you, I would seriously recommend playing this game just for the extremely innovative mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic look into human emotion, the story was expertly written and masterfully applied to this format. The use of the webcam and its blinking mechanic is not only a great nod on the age old trope of "Life can pass you by in the blink of an eye" but it also gives you a deep connection to the game. Rather playing with your hands you play with your eyes and sometimes are forced to strain them to hold on to every moment and other times you are encouraged to rest your eyes. It gives this fantastic sense of connection to the story and the characters.  I also reccomend playing on high volume, and i know it will be tempting to go into your volume mixer to turn it down as it is quite loud but there are moments (and i will not spoil them) that overwhelm you with sound adding another level of sensory connection to the characters. Please play this game. It is short but well worth the 9.99. In fact i would've been satisfied paying 30 or even 40 dollars for somthing this high quality. The game is truly unique and is a masterclass in not only game design but also literary writing, sound design, and art design.Fantastic job to the whole team! 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Seven games had made me cry before I played this one. The Sexy Brutale, What Remains of Edith Finch, Pentiment, Journey, To the Moon, Finding Paradise, Spiritfarer. All potent experiences, especially that last one. And all longer than Before Your Eyes (which lasts around 90 minutes), a game I also fully expected to be trying to make me cry. But it did make me cry. It made me stare at the screen with tears flowing freely like the scene in Interstellar. This isn't just an innovative step forward for games as a medium for storytelling, it is a perfect little experience that encapsulates why I love games in the first place. Please play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game's store page by pure chance right before release day and was immediately really interested in it so I bought it as soon as it came out. I couldn't help but get curious about the blinking mechanic, and the fact that it was used for a more story-telling based game. I was really skeptical about the blinking mechanic, though. I don't have a good streamer setup with a great camera and good lights and all that, so I was worried it wouldn't work out nicely. However the game has a very intuitive calibration menu for the webcam stuff, and it ended up that I didn't have any major problems with it after doing a few minutes calibrating. The only thing is that during the calibration I decided that it would be far better to play the game without glasses as the reflection of my screen directly on my glasses seemed to really get in the way of the blinking detection, which is understandable; since I don't have that much trouble seeing up close without glasses anyway it wasn't a big deal for me.The storytelling kind of reminded me of something like Last Day of June (perhaps due to the fact that it also has a very unique cartoony art style). It's emotional, maybe a bit generic in that sector, but I think the way it's played out elevates it to a higher level and I was very invested in it while playing. It's also pretty thoughtful and powerful though, and some aspects of it... I felt resonated very strongly with me and my life on a personal side, which surely is bound to happen to many people with those kinds of stories, but I guess that's also why I have a soft spot for them.The game is pretty short, you can finish the entire story in one sitting easily. And then, afterwards, you'll feel weird about blinking for a while, which is something I don't think you can say about many other games. It's a worth it experience.
