_childDocuments_.review: The phrase “in a blink of an eye” refers to the passage of time, often used when speaking about how time has slipped away from us much too quickly. Before Your Eyes, by developer GoodbyeWorld Games and publisher Skybound Games, is a game that holds that sentiment close in its game design and just about succeeds in producing the same somber and sentimental notes. On the surface, the game distinguishes itself through its unique game mechanics: blinking allows players to interact with objects and skip forward in time. At its core, it is an interactive narrative experience about the wonders and tragedies of dreams, ambitions, and responsibilities as you witness the events of your life pass by at blindly fast speeds.Gameplay At its best, Before Your Eyes wonderfully aligns its gameplay mechanics and the narrative elements to create an immersive experience, which engages all the player’s senses. At its worst, these mechanics not only distract from the gameplay, but result in disruption of the plot and storytelling. I was enchanted by moments where the game elegantly places you in the shoes of the protagonist: being prompted to close my eyes to eavesdrop on my parents quietly argue about me in the room over, or being asked to not blink in moments of tension and fear. With those snippets of wonder, there comes an equal number of scenes where the only thought on my mind was “ahhhh my eyes are burning.” This was primarily an issue in the first half of the game where at times blinking causes time to jump forward. In these instances, the mechanic was disrupting the time that should be spent on building character through literally cutting the scene short or through physically distracting the player.It’s really a tragedy when those tender moments of character building and carefully placed beats of storytelling are undermined by the gameplay mechanics. Along with those issues, the mechanics can feel gimmicky when, for example, the player is prompted to pick up their phone by blinking at it. Despite these blemishes, this was a satisfying sample of what could be an incredible mechanic if better incorporated with traditional ways of controlling the player character. In the end, the blinking controls did become highly endearing to me because it greatly amplified a major theme of the game: “life slips by in a blink of an eye and we take for granted the time that’s been given to us.” Story Other themes within the story also struck a chord: the loss of childhoods to responsibility and ambition, broken dreams, but also hope, contentment, and forgiveness. The story follows your life. Your mother is an accountant with broken dreams of being a pianist which she subsequently pushes onto you. Your parents are loving, but your childhood is not without its tragedies and trauma. Within points of the narrative, the player makes choices between fulfilling expectations of your loving mother or living out the carefree childhood every child is meant to have. Although the story was simplistic, its themes are so universal and relatable that you will likely find yourself attached to the story and invested in the life of the protagonist. There’s a sense of nostalgia as the player character interacts with objects and struggles with issues many of us would have likely had witnessed in our own childhoods.The developer succeeded in writing a solid emotional narrative, but since the game relies almost entirely on the power of its narrative, I was just a tad disappointed. I would love to see future projects with more developed, interesting, and unique characters and a more sophisticated story working in tandem with the mechanics they’ve developed to fully immerse the player within another world.Conclusion The game’s colorful visuals, digestible characters, and sentimental story leads the player to somber moments of self reflection if they are willing to give 2-3 hours to play through the story. There is no amazing grandiose plot with twists and turns at every corner, but perhaps that’s what drives the feelings of nostalgia and heart aches within this simple narrative. Anyone can enjoy Before your Eyes as everyone has likely felt such subtle traumas as faced by the player character.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying I don't usually post reviews, nor am I good at writing reviews.  With that being said, I went into this game blindly.  I had never heard of, seen, or even read up on the game. But with the ratings being so high and lots of positive feedback, I thought sure, why not. Let's try it out.First of all, the blinking mechanic is so cool.  Sure, you can just use your mouse instead, but where's the fun in that when you can make up tiny staring contests along Benny's journey?  Second, if you're not the type to indulge in a good ol' story-telling game, I wouldn't recommend this game. Buuut, for those of you who do enjoy a game that puts you in the character's shoes, force feeds you their emotions (done exceptionally well), and makes you want to sob like a Sims character, then follow Benny, a boy who lives in an ordinary family and has an ordinary life. And that might sound boring, but there are aspects of this game that almost all of us can relate to: failure, not living up to expectation, feeling as if our parents are demanding, first loves, so on. But the part that I loved most was flipping through Benny's life like we would our own memories. There's so much in our own lives that happen so fast, it feels as if it happened yesterday. And this game encapsulates that feeling.  Just...knowing that you've accumulated years upon years, but every moment you've ever lived remains so fresh in your mind.  There's a plot twist, of course. There's always a plot twist. And it caught me so off guard, but I understood, and immediately, I was done. Not fed up, just emotionally wrecked.  .  I work with kids, and one day, I hope to be a mother, so to see this story unfold the way it did, I couldn't help but cry and think of the pain and tragedy of Benny.  How could I keep myself together as a parent if I couldn't stop crying with this?And I don't mean just a little tear or two. I broke down.  I sobbed for half an hour.  I went through this journey with Benny.  There was just so much emotion near the end. It's the simplicity of the game and the normality of every day life that just sucks you in.  It's how you're reminded that life is a fragile thing filled with moments that become core memories. How it can crumble in an instant.  How the people in your life shape who you become.  How even though you are met with awful moments, those moments are washed away with positivity soon enough.  If I could, I would give this game beyond the standard max rating. It deserves 12 gold stars and all the love I can give.  Everything about this game is simply amazing. Thank you to the creators, the writers, the ones who were in charge of the visuals and game play and so many more. This is one of my favorite games of all time, with no doubt.  And everyone did such a splendid job.  I hope to see more titles like Before Your Eyes. And to everyone who read this: Happy Holidays!

_childDocuments_.review: This...this game is something else. I've never felt so empty yet so fulfilled after I finished a game. Before Your Eyes has one of, if not THE best story I've played in a video game (and I've played a lot of video games). The fact that no matter what, you'll eventually have to blink and move on with life is so simple yet so powerful. Every moment is fleeting, and no matter what, you're going to miss something. Its so real and so sad. Yet, after that ending, I could do nothing but smile as the credits rolled. This is one of the greatest games I've ever played. Also, do NOT look anything up. If you go into this game blind, it will be one of the most moving experiences of all time. It can be completed in less than 2 hours, but this game is so good that I will not refunding it. God, what a beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the first time a game had me truly crying (and several times). I know I've come somewhat close in some other games, but nothing was as emotionally intense as this for me. My experience might not be your experience; a lot of details in the story happened to line up closely with my own life in ways that made some of the plot points hit really REALLY close to home. I'd say the story is really good regardless of how much it will reflect on your own history, though.The blink mechanic and its variants were really cool too. Detection wasn't perfect but good enough. No complaints whatsoever.The only caveat I can think of is that you'll need to have a good grasp of spoken English because there will be bits where you can't read the screen, and therefore can't rely on subtitles. (There is a "full subtitles" option, but I don't know what it does, but it does come with the disclaimer of it modifying the experience, so it probably bypasses that.)This is probably my GOTY 2021 (at least so far, since I'm writing this in late June).
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: By the time I reached the end of this game, I felt surprisingly neutral—no rush of emotions like the comments had suggested. But then, 9000 miles away from my family while studying abroad, I picked up the phone and called my mother. That’s when it hit me. Tears started flowing before I even knew what I was feeling. This game truly is a masterpiece.It’s the kind of story that sneaks up on you. There were moments I wanted to hold onto, to rewind or pause, but my eyes gave it away; it hurt because it felt so real. Time slips away, whether we want it to or not, and every step we take, every small decision, shapes who we are. And that’s the beauty of it: we only get one life, and that’s what makes it worth living. This game reminds you to appreciate that—appreciate the people you love, let time pass naturally, and don’t cling too hard. Just live.I highly recommend this to anyone who needs a reminder of life’s fleeting, beautiful moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing the trailer and the videos is not enough. _childDocuments_.review: Ever wished you could control a game with just a blink of an eye? Well, Before Your Eyes makes that dream a reality! And trust me, it's not just a gimmick – it's a mind-blowing emotional rollercoaster that'll leave you reaching for tissues.This indie gem takes you on a whirlwind journey through a lifetime of memories, from childhood giggles to tear-jerking goodbyes. The catch? Each blink propels the story forward, leaving you hanging on every flutter of your eyelids. It's a ridiculously clever concept that adds a whole new level of immersion.The graphics are stunningly simple yet evocative, like watercolor paintings brought to life. The story is heartfelt, relatable, and surprisingly hilarious at times. You'll laugh, cry, and everything in between as you relive the highs and lows of a life well-lived.But here's the kicker: this game isn't just about the feels. It's also a testament to the power of interactive storytelling. The blink mechanic isn't just a novelty; it's a brilliant way to make you feel like an active participant in the narrative. Each blink is a choice, a moment of reflection, and a reminder of how fleeting life can be.So grab a box of tissues, charge your webcam (yes, it needs one!), and prepare to have your heartstrings tugged like never before. Before Your Eyes is a masterpiece that proves video games can be so much more than just mindless entertainment. It's a touching reminder to cherish every moment, because life truly does flash before your eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: i really loved this game. I had no clue what it was about before going into it other then it tracked your blinks and that was enough for me to be interested. _childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: All I knew about this game prior to playing is that game play was based around blinks. There was an option to use the mouse button instead of eyes, but I think it would defeat the purpose. I was determined to play the whole thing with a camera.It wasn’t easy, that’s for sure. First, I have narrow eyelids, which makes difficult for cameras to register blinking. I had to sit the whole time with a “surprised” expression to make camera’s work easier. Second problem was the lighting. The natural light outside is weak this time of year, so I had to combine light from two lamps to get a nice and balanced lighting on my face. However, since I wear eyeglasses, the light would be reflected from certain angles. I had to adjust my posture to account for that too. In addition, the calibration felt awful. Even though the game detected my blinks perfectly after adjusting, after 5-10 minutes it lost track of my eyes. It says a lot when I got achievement for calibrating 10 times despite the game lasting 1.5 hours. Finally, not blinking is just painful. I wanted to see as much possible, so naturally I blinked as little as possible. Combined with intense light, my eyes were not pleased.Despite all the issues I brought up, the game itself is cool. I couldn’t relate to the story but I thought it was engaging enough. Although, I’ll definitely remember this game for its unique game play and pain it caused more than anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Not too many games have made me cry, but when they do they hit hard and leave me with a moment I will never forget.I don't want to give you spoilers for the game, but I do wanna leave you with some sort of synopsis to give you some sorta of understanding even if it is to the minimal extent  :VVVVV:You are a soul floating around the darksea until you get picked up by the Ferryman, he kind of acts as your lawyer to see whether or not you can get into paradise by trying to convince the Gatekeeper, before meeting the Gatekeeper you both will have to go through the memories of your life (Benjamin Brynn) so the Ferryman can build up a defense. Gameplay is a really cool idea, it uses your webcam to see whether or not you are blinking in order to interact and move on in the game. I however don't have a webcam so I had to opt in the click method. It's not really a walking simulator as you are in one spot at a time, but you do move the camera around and click on objects, more like an "on rail" waliking simulator when your character does move. Everything else I like too even if I don't have a lot to say about it like the art style they went with is nice, it definitely throws you off a little cause you think it's gonna be all good based on how cute and friendly everything looks. The voice acting is really good too, Eric Edelstein (Richard) and Sarah Burns (Elle) do a really good job of making the parents feel like real people instead of just characters, Stephen Friedrich does a good job with the Ferryman and the few other characters he does as well.Overall I would recommend this game even if you don't have a webcam. Everything is just so interesting and will make you feel full of emotions, I get that to some people the "gameplay" itself might be a thing that causes them to turn away, but if you like a really good story just try this out. Worked great on Linux as well so anyone using a SteamDeck or are just a penguin this will work fine.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an awesome gimmick: you control it by blinking (via a web camera). It works very well technically, telling you the life story of Benny and his struggles. Blinks are used either as interaction or a way to move to the next scene — which means that if you have to keep experiencing the current one, you'll have to struggle to keep your eyes open. And sometimes you'll blink accidentally and do things you didn't necessarity want to. It creates a very powerful feeling of immersion, and I recommend the game for it alone.The story itself is very mediocre. I trust the credits that make it clear that it's very personal to the creative lead — but it doesn't  personal, throwing every possible tear-jerker at you. It has stray pets, dead kittens, dead children, music that's supposed to tug at your heart's strings, family drama, sickness... oh and everyone is either artistically inclined or from academia (because ordinary people aren't interesting enough, I guess). It's all neatly tied and competently presented, but I stuggle to take stories that have nothing but emotional manipulation seriously.I guess among stories with the kind of plot that would star Robin Williams as a 90s movie  has a better reason to be as sappy as it is: the game clearly tries to make you cry, which in turn would make you blink, which would facilitate the game's main feeling — of a life flashing before your eyes (since every blink propels the story forward), in turn hurting even more because you inevitably missed some parts of the scenes...I respect this design. It didn't work on me, but I understand the logic behind it and how it  work. It makes sense to make this kind of story for this kind of gimmick. I enjoyed the parts where you need to close your eyes completely — it makes you feel lost and vulnerable, which again feels the story very well.Consoles, VR, and even mobile games experiment with unusual input, but PC doesn't do it enough. I recommend  for that alone, and I think it's a very coherent piece of game design. As for me personally, I'm eagerly waiting for a game with a better story or imagery to try something with this gimmick.

_childDocuments_.review: This game changed my life (seriously like I embarked on a different career path after I played it) and its so weird calling it a 'game' because really its an experience, anyways, it inspired me in ways I simply cannot articulate. _childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Despite mild frustration in calibrations, Before Your Eyes is an absolute game changer in a way that connects the player to the storyline, employing a tactic never seen quite before, and it achieved it's goal. Similarly to another review's words: it's hard not to blink when you're crying. The entire plot is a punch in the gut, and it hits you so hard. It went from being a game about doodling, an idiosyncratic best friend, and an overbearing mother to a story much more intricate and bittersweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. The sound design and pacing is phenomenal and perfectly captures the story that is being told. I would also 100% recommend a webcam. The blinking mechanic was used in an amazing way to progress the story. There are some neat parts where if you can manage to keep your eyes open, you get just a little bit more, but missing it doesn't detract from the gameplay at all. I really felt like I was in the shoes of the character, with certain game mechanics really helping to emphasize a certain part of the game (those who have played it through will know what I'm talking about). The blinking also played a great part of story telling at the end. Maybe a spoiler? Idk i'll mark it to be safe: Like the other review say, it's a short game, took me about 1.5 hours to get through the whole thing, but it's completely worth the $10 pricetag. The developers did a great job in writing the story, and I didn't encounter any issues whatsoever. Thank you to the devs for creating such a neat story
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a storytelling game where you blind to play the game. _childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and emotional are words to describe this masterpiece. Play as if you are young again with an open mind, where everything that happens to you starts crafting your perceptions of reality and hopes of your future. _childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Game Itself, Absolutely stunning. But on the bright side I have what is essentially a 5 dollar webcam and the blinking system worked perfectly with no issues.Final verdict: 8/10, amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the most incredible experiences I have had in the last 24 years of gaming, and in general life. This game will not serve to make you smile, laugh or be comfortable during the experience.  But if you can put aside your feelings, focus and feel what the game is telling you. You will come out a much better person, the message in this game can be viewed as sad.But it is the truth.Life happens before your eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little hesitant about purchasing Before Your Eyes given that in terms of price to length, it's straddling the boundary of what I would consider reasonable. But I am happy to say it is well worth the asking price. The eye tracking gameplay is more innovation than gimmick and the story is heartfelt and moving. Plus, I'm a sucker for any game that offers narrative decisions. And it's all wrapped up in quality art and music. I encountered some minor graphical and blink-detection issues but they didn't affect the experience. If you're on the fence like I was, this is a risk worth taking.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Saying that playing this game was emotionally heavy is true, but an enormous understatement. There is a content warning on the store page, but I wish it had been a bit more specific about the context of the death and grief themes. I understand that it's difficult to do that without spoiling a large part of the story. The mentioned, spoilery, context: My personal connection to the story, spoilery: The game is beautiful. The style, the art, the voice acting, the story, the believable dialogue. There are few games where the game mechanics are an integral part of the storytelling - something the blinking mechanic of Before Your Eyes manages with flying colors. Wanting to stay in a scene, a moment, but being unable to. Do I recommend the game? Yes. Do I regret playing it? Yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game of 2021, and the most emotionally impactful game I've played in... years? ever? I genuinely can't remember anything that hit me nearly as hard as Before Your Eyes.I don't want to talk about it at all beyond that, and I'd recommend you avoid learning anything before playing. It's only 90 minutes or so, and it's best enjoyed blind.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've ever done on here, but I believe it is well worth it. I knew as soon as I saw the trailer for this game that it was going to make me cry. Not a lot of media/art really does that for me, so I was quite impressed when this game made me cry multiple times. As a person who struggles with not feeling "good enough" a lot of the time, as well as being a struggling artist myself, this game really hit home. This is an easy 10/10 recommend from me for anyone who is interested in an emotional, very well crafted story.My only wish...is that it could've lasted a little longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Caution to all gamers: keep those tissues handy and embrace the no-blink challenge with this rollercoaster of emotions! Picture this: a game so heartwrenching that it tracks your tears through a webcam-triggered progression system. Blink, and the story moves forward, but hey, tears may make that a bit tricky!It's been ages since a game pulled at my heartstrings like this one. I laughed, I cried, and yes, I accidentally blinked a few times while dealing with the emotional rollercoaster. The immersive experience and rich storytelling are top-notch. Kudos to the developers for crafting such a masterpiece! Grab this gem as soon as you can — your emotions will thank you later. Happy gaming!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: God, this game was beautiful. Saw this game advertised about a week ago and the mechanic of blinking to get through a narrative sounded really cool and unique to me. I knew that the whole "travelling through memories at death's door" was going to give me a punch to the gut, I just didn't expect to be so appreciative of it? _childDocuments_.review: ok...so i bought a web cam just to play this game, as i didn't find anything saying i actually needed one or not to play, but i did want to get the full game experience. it sounded fun.and at first it was kind of amazing as my eye blinks substituted for mouse clicks.  then my eyes got tired blinking, and the feature became a bit annoying. it really worked perfectly though, reading my blinks. i am unaware if the mechanics of my blinking did anything more than register a mouse click as opposed to drawing some inference about whether i was emotionally reacting, but i dunno.i read a lot of reviews first about people crying and getting involved in the story. personally, i'm usually sensitive to tear jerkers, but the only crying i did was from my eyes being sore from blinking! haha! sorry, but i really didn't get into the story. anyway, sale price was good, game was fun, but it seems very much like a video movie with clicking than a game.  which is ok...i did read that in advance. since it took me 2 hours to finish, i know it is simple and more of a movie than game. it was so innovative though with the eye blinks in the game mechanics, i have to give it a 3.9 out of 5.  i do like strange and weird games with no killing nor action.  this game does get a bit dark though in spots.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. The blink interaction was a really good idea and experiment. If you can't get the blink interaction to work or don't want to use it then the game does allow you to enable left clicking instead of blinking. The game doesn't use the keyboard at all unless you want to pause or recalibrate the blink interaction.I really enjoyed the story and the game does offer some choices for you to choose from throughout the story. I did at times find myself sad at times when I blinked past something. The game also has points where you have to keep your eyes closed and where you're tasked with not blinking. 10/10 in my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: I was never compelled to write a serious review of a game until this one. Wow. What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. _childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free review: It's a 2.5h hour genre mashup with a gimmick - think "to the Moon" meets a walking simulator like Dear Esther or What remains of Edith Finch. If you liked either or both, you'll love this. Slight cons: framerate is capped at 60fps and resolution doesn't support ultrawide (max i could get was 1440p). Seems the PERFECT game to demo ultrawides so i was a bit taken aback by that and hope the devs patch it down the road. There are also a couple of bugs/inconsistencies: if you stare fight your screen too long at the doctor, the game crashes to desktop. It also thinks you deserve the 'redo' achievement even though you took the immediate same path. At one point the webcam stopped tracking completely and I got the '10 recalibration achievement' from it. Hopefully they can pour some of that future game money into sorting these out, too.Finally, the 'twist' (yes there is a MASSIVE TWIST) is delivered in a way which initially took me aback as - after all, there are a couple of inconsistencies in the game play (.PS: one could argue the whole webcam thing wasn't needed at all. And you can in fact play without it, which speaks volume. Choices don't really matter - actually they don't matter at all - and replay value is extremely low. All that being said, it's still a fantastic game and any 'walking simulator' fan like myself who enjoy story-rich environments should get this game. Maybe just wait until all the bugs are fixed or a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever been conscious of what your eyes were doing whenever you were playing a game? It's just one of those things we never really take a step back and think about. We're focused on what challenge the gameplay's presenting, or what story's gonna unfold. Only this time, both those things were directly related to blinking, to the point that even after I was done with the game, I felt as if I had gotten slightly more conscious in realizing every blink of mine. Every moment counting slightly more. That's what the core of this game sort of comes down to - blink and the moment's gone. And it ties this novel mechanic which could've been easily been a gimmick, and ties it to the core themes it wants to express. It's kind of hard to put down a "number" here, per se. I don't know if it's the kind of games I've played so far in this year - Journey and Before Your Eyes, but I've felt rather restricted by my own system of rating different aspects of these games like this. I'm not sure if it's the specific type of games they are that invoke this feeling, or me having drifted away from this system. All things said, the game has a very novel "gameplay loop", if we could even call it that, that it uses solely to tell the story. There are moments which are gone the second you blink, there are choices you make in the story. I do feel that the choices making a difference could've added some value to the story in this case. I certainly wish they had been more than a aesthetic choice changing a dialogue or two. But anyway, less I talk about the story, the better. It's best experienced blind (no pun intended). I played this game high lol, while also having previously thought about themes that this game is very much talking about, of living a moment vs recounting a moment. I'd recently read an extract in Jean Paul Sartre's Nausea which says that for a moment to become an adventure, a memory, one must only start recounting it. But when we do the recounting while it's still happening, the moment ceases to exist. And despite my little qualms, this game will always have a special place in my heart for doing what it does, and how it does it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game revealed itself something I wasn't expecting. I picked it mainly to its very interesting mechanic of blinking. It is a great concept, and well implemented. It's responsive and detects the blinking with no problems. Right from the start that is a great accomplishment.Then, the story. It threw me off-guard. The game can be split into two parts. The first time you recount your life, when the ferryman picks you up from the water. Since you cannot talk, you comunicate by blinking. You recount your life, some moments are good, some are less good, you faced challenges, like everyone.You think that is it, when your story finishes. But that wasn't all. Then ferryman defies you to go back again, and recount more specifically some moments. And then you unlock powerful memories that you had shut down. The story defies society's imposition on doing something, becoming someone, reaching a level and leaving a legacy. What does it really mean? And why do we have to follow a certain path to be considered worthy of remembering? It ends with the lesson that you don't, society pressures you to, but however you lived your life, if you did the best you could, that's what matters. The story is deeply sad, and deals with (major spoiler, and trigger warning) . Deals also with self-worth and expectations imposed by others and ourselves onto us.In the end, it is a truly beautiful story, though not heartwarming. It's a great experience, and I can't recommend it enough.The only thing that annoyed me was the ferryman, his attitude and demeanor is annoying, and he got in my nerves. Especially when barking (actual barking).There is also a one-eyed cat in the story, which is super cute <3

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a game that brilliantly illustrates the immense potential of narrative in the gaming industry. Thanks to a unique webcam feature, it draws you into a heartfelt, engaging and moving narrative. _childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes offers an experience unlike any game I’ve ever played before. Basically, you control the game with your eyes by blinking to progress. It’s not a mindblowing mechanic or anything but it’s a fresh forum of interactivity that really adds to the immersion of the game, along with supporting its message of savouring every moment life throws your way because before you know it, that moment could be gone in the blink of an eye. The story is a beautiful tale of a dead soul reliving his life through his memories, and It conveys all sorts of feelings of nostalgia, happiness, sadness, success, regret, and loss. I was pleasantly surprised to discover that this game utilizes its blinking mechanic in multiple different ways, and even though none of which are mind blowing by any means, I really appreciated that extra layer of intractability these types of control provided. The artstyle of this game is similar to other low-poly art styles with their use of minimal texturing and simplified geometry but that doesn’t prevent this game from looking absolutely stunning. The way it conveys feelings with light and colour are masterful and greatly added to the experience. This game also hits it out of the park with its soundtrack, it's truly amazing and doesn’t feel too intense, like it's trying too hard to force a particular emotion onto you. The music is just beautiful and excellently compliments the dialogue and visuals. The voice acting for this game is also super charming, every character speaks like a real person and I especially loved the blue cat man who frequently speaks to you on the boat. He was a delight to listen to, and so was the rest of the cast.Before Your Eyes is a masterful game that contains outstanding music, graphics, voice acting, and tops it all off with a truly moving story. This game is an emotional rollercoaster and even though it went by in the blink of an eye it’s one of the few gaming experiences I don’t think I’ll forget.

_childDocuments_.review: At first the game's original mechanic felt a bit uneven and gimmicky, and required multiple recalibrations until the camera detection finally felt right and worked as expected. As consequence, a few scenes disappeared too soon. Though I didn't always get to make the choices I really wanted, once the game's more emotive scenes kicked in, I could hardly stop myself from weeping to the end.Though the webcam is optional, I can't imagine this game truly having the same sensitive impact without it. There are a few scenes that require some dexterity, which would have been nicer to follow with eye tracking instead, and even fewer others favor a staring contest level of concentration, while the majority of interactions feel entirely simple and natural. I found myself holding my breath in some instances to make sure I would not blink when it mattered, or maintaining my eyes closed and sobbing silently in different segments. is best experienced in a single session, in my case just under two hours. Some players may want to replay the game to try out a few different narrative options, but I feel entirely satisfied with my reasonably short single playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Roy: A Life Well LivedIn all seriousness, this game IS incredibly similar to that one Rick and Morty gag; you're experiencing someone's life in an incredibly condensed manner, and there's a few decisions that lead to differing outcomes. When I initially played it, I had an intense emotional reaction to it, and it left a strong impression. Then a friend told me about their experience, and it didn't strike them as hard. To elaborate, there's a few situations where you're given a choice between multiple options. However, none of the decisions have significant lasting consequences outside of a few differing scenes. Between our playthroughs, me and my friend experienced 90% of the same content, just different dialogue that was incredibly easy to miss due to the game's pacing based on your blinks. I really would've appreciated bigger differences based on the decisions we made, even if it meant fewer decisions to make. I know multiple paths in games are time consuming and frustrating to map, but this game could've really benefitted from it. If I seem harsh, it's because I love a lot about this game. I got really immersed quickly due to the game's mechanics. I can't think of another game using a camera to affect gameplay based on a player blinking. The concept is genius, and the execution is wonderful. I never had any problems with the camera picking up on my face, though it made several scenes shorter than I'd hoped - which is also the developer's intention, which I like. Art style is cartoony and lively, and the voice acting is phenominal. Animation is well done and accurate, though the motion capture is a bit weird at times with the cartoony characters not directly matching the real-world motions the actors performed. Scenes are comprised of little 'bubbles' that are either revealed or hidden based on where you look, but can make it easy to miss details that really bring the world to life. In general, the game is an experiment; I'd be curious to see if there could be a longer experience made of this type of game without losing steam, but as it stands, it's amazing.

If you've never experienced anything like that, you might get a lot more out of the game, but as someone who lost his father at a young age, I've already processed a lot of these feelings and contemplated these ideas in a much more personal way.I will admit the ending got to me a little, but not as much as other story driven games have.  I know the game is already short, but if it was tighter and under an hour I would definitely recommend it.If you're into story games, and are down for an experiment, give it a shot. _childDocuments_.review: for more reviews like this.Before Your Eyes is one of the greatest games I have ever played. This is not me being over-exaggerating either. I will keep this review spoiler-free because I truly believe that every person should play this game. When I first saw the blinking mechanic this game markets itself with I thought to myself, hmmm how can blinking be used effectively, and how much of a difference can it make in how you play a game? I got my answer about 20 minutes in when I blinked without realizing and missed out on something I wanted to hear more about. Don't worry, this is what the game wants. The game wants you to feel like you're being ripped away from what's happening, it wants you to be frustrated with yourself for blinking, and missing out on that extra line of dialougue. That's what makes this game so special. This game shows you how your life can change with the blink of an eye, how you should take nothing for granted, how the little things in life, can change who we are, and the people around us, it shows you about what it means to live. The story this game tells is beautiful, it's happy, it's nostalgic, it's gut wrenching, and when you're done experiencing it, all you can do it sit back, listen to the credits and think. This is a game that will make you think about how you live your life each and every day. The creativity and innovation that the blinking mechanic brings to the game is undoubtedly a game changer, and I had no issues with it the entire game. If you are someone who loves video games, or someone who's never touched one in your life, you should play this game. It's one of those rare games that only come out once every few years and if you blink, you might miss it.

Gameplay is very limited and simple (as to be expected). Choices matter yet don't matter. You should precisely spend as much time as desired on things and nothing more. I don't think it serves as an exemplar of game design but it certainly does its job and does it well. Sure, it's like a movie but it's an  movie, one that truly does benefit from your inclusion in it. The gameplay really does write itself at this point... Graphics are very "artsy fartsy" and stylistic. I believe they look good and serve their purpose well. Characters look cool too. Story, writing, and setting are well-crafted. It's about everything that you would expect for an "emotional story singleplayer" game of à la "To the Moon." I didn't notice any big writing or characterization flaws. It's fabricated very well to feel "homely" and "down-to-Earth" in my opinion and obviously created to be heart wrenching which I admit that I love that kind of stuff and felt that it succeeded very well. Now, initially, I was once hesitant to purchase this $10 game because I was afraid I wouldn't "get enough out of it." At the same time, I was afraid that I would "lose out on the full experience" by just looking up a playthrough on Youtube. I can confidently say that, for $10, that'll cost you around a trip to the movies or one of those "museum experiences" that you can additionally purchase. I have done both of those things recently (Inside Out 2 and I went to the Vincent Van Gogh museum and purchased the VR experience) and I would say that I liked this game better than those other two combined. I wouldn't praise this game as "something you'll remember your whole life" but it certainly is a nice (and economical) roller coaster ride of emotions if you're into that sort of thing!So, wait for a sale or get it now! _childDocuments_.review: Genuinely the most emotionally moving game I've played in a long time. I came having heard great things about the game, expecting to be left slightly melancholic and thoughtful. What I actually got was full crying, a greater appreciation of the fleeting nature of life, and an experience I will likely think about for a long time to come.The blink controls enable an experience that is mildly adversarial to the player, but not in a frustrating or overbearing way. The feeling of crying while trying not to blink while not wiping away the tears so the software doesn't lose sight of your eye position while trying to complete a minigame to get more dialogue is truly a unique one, and it puts the player in the POV character's position: wanting to stay in this moment, even if it is difficult, because the thought of passing it by is too much to bear.The short runtime absolutely does not take away from the experience of the game. Perhaps a much longer game would have felt like a drag with such simplistic controls, but the 1.5-1.75 hour runtime of Before Your Eyes is absolutely perfect. If you have time to watch a movie, you have time to play this game, and you absolutely should.10/10. Absolutely would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is a narrative adventure game telling the story of Benny, a newly departed soul on his way to the afterlife. After being fished up by a wolf to be brought before the Gatekeeper, Benny and the wolf review Benny’s life so they can plead his case to the Gatekeeper. There is very little in the way of actual gameplay in Before Your Eyes. Instead, the player is carried through a narrative, the speed of which is controlled by when they blink. It’s an interesting mechanic, and this feels like one of the few stories in which a mechanic like this could work. By cuing story progression to blinking, the game’s only challenge becomes a physical one. When I wanted to stay in a scene longer, or see how it played out, I had to keep my eyes open. As each scene represents a particular memory, this challenge played nicely with the challenge of memory itself. When recalling our lives, we inevitably lose track of some memories, or wish a moment could have lasted longer. How our brains conceive of our past and who we are is fragmented, cutting some things in favour of others, or lingering too long on those things that never mattered in the first place. I barely remember my wedding day, for example, but I remembered losing a North Carolina trivia contest to Jacob de Witt in 4th grade. This is the fickleness of memory.Though it may initially seem gimmicky, by setting the pace of a narrative on something involuntary, the game captures some element of what Benny feels when reviewing his own life. There are the moments where you remember to hold on and not blink, and then there are the moments that flash by, probably important, but not imprinted in the brain at the time, and so lost. The mechanic does an incredible job of placing the player in the mind and memory of Benny, of wanting to hold on to something fleeting, but knowing it will slip away.This isn’t to say the mechanic is without frustration. The eye tracking sometimes said I blinked when I didn’t, causing me to miss a scene entirely. It was also exceedingly bad at recognising when my eyes were closed. However, the rest of the immersion is good enough that I was happy to peg these issues to Benny and not the mechanics themselves. It was Benny who didn’t remember something that might be considered important in hindsight, not the game refusing to recognise I didn’t blink. It was Benny who didn’t want to close his eyes to hear a conversation, not the game not finding my eyelids. This, to me, is the mark of a story well-told, when I can set aside the issues with the actual mechanics and plausibly chalk them up to story choices. It bears repeating that the story behind Before Your Eyes is a fantastic one. It understands what the purpose of its structure is, and how to use it to tell its story to the fullest. By the end, the experience of being fully locked in to this story had been a deeply emotional one. Its commentary of what life is and how we perceive it is incredible, and I loved it. I held on to these moments of Benny’s life as long as I could, and in doing so, reflected on my own moments. I held on to Benny’s memories, and my own, and gained a greater appreciation for what the story was doing.Before Your Eyes may seem gimmicky, but I’d argue its blink mechanic is the best possible way to tell its story. Memory is fleeting. Life is fleeting. Capturing that essence through something fundamentally uncontrollable is a brilliant way to capture the essence of life itself.

It does a perfect job of also relating back to the player, or at least it did for me, and that's almost impossible to do through a video game. At the end of the story, it doesn't leave you on a cliff hanger - it doesn't leave you at a dead end, but fills you with an emotional inspiration and closure that is so clearly deserved. It's a good reflection on how fast life can flash by and how important it is to make memories and not worry about tomorrow or not to worry about living up to impossible standards. I don't know - maybe I'll look back at this review I left as the cringiest thing I've ever written, but no matter how awful my review may sound, this game is definitely more than just a game.
