_childDocuments_.review: I just lost my ♥♥♥♥.I walked into this game knowing very little, I had wishlisted it a while back and wanted to play it for myself. I forgot any sort of playthroughs I had watched in 2020-2021.The game begins with your character being fished up from the sea. The ferryman tells you that you're going to be given to this entity called The Gatekeeper, who will judge you based on your life. So, you go through your life to tell this so-called gatekeeper what you have accomplished.Or so you THOUGHT you had accomplished.This game tells a happy tale of how you as a human lived life trying to become what your mother wanted, and ultimately, having hardships with that. Instead, you begun to draw exquisite masterpieces over time, catching the eyes of many people over a lifetime. You see your mother die, and your father desperately grasping at what little life he has left.Actually, scratch everything. Everything past, let's say, eleven years old? During a certain point in the game, you figure out you get sick. This foreshadows the main plot twist of the game, which is that YOU DIED. You died at age eleven, writing about your life as you thought it was, and how you fitted in with the rest of the world, knowing that you were a rotten coward. Your mother and father were the only ones to correctly fixate yourself and your final few thoughts into knowing you would've been even greater without catching what horrid disease killed you off.I absolutely lost it. I felt pure happiness seeing my character grow, and seeing all these weird events offset me to a point where I kept it in the back of my head, but I figured it all out. When the cat gave birth to its litter, we (the characters in the story) apparently left them outside. You figure out way later they were EATEN.That's not even the worst part, the worst part is that you figure out you were a FAILURE. You listened in to your mother and father and learned the truth. The eldritch abomination that is near-death consumes you and the white light expels the red and you perish.Emotion wise, I don't think I've connected more to anything in my life. I wish I could see life like this instead of just being told words, I wanna be able to experience what you felt, instead of just knowing what you felt, because I've learned today that simply listening is not enough.Oh, I bought this on sale, and I regret it because I should've bought it at full price. Absolutely worth my five bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is seemingly a first of its kind, its core mechanic weaving narrative storytelling (the story within the game) with its own immersive structures (the intense interactive story formed around me, as a participant). It's pure lightning in a bottle, begging the player to form connections to their own life. This wonderful piece of art has left me better for playing it. There is every reason you should experience this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. With my ancient webcam (and with me wearing glasses) it still worked perfectly. Just make sure your face is well lit and there is nothing in the way. Also, not only do you have to blink but at some point also close your eyes and keep them shut. This I didnt understand at first, which broke the flow of the game. Just be aware of that.There is nothing else to say. This game is a masterpiece and a must play for anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write to many reviews, but this game is nothing short of incredible. This game has some of the most incredible storytelling I have ever experienced. The concept behind the story and how to ties to the blinking mechanic makes it an experience truly worth your time. I would recommend this game to anyone who is looking for an experience to truly remember. If you have the slightest interest in playing this game, do it. You will not regret it. I've never been so engaged and captivated by a game quite like this. Truly a beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This was a brilliant game that you can probably finish in 2-3 hours. It brought me through so many different emotions, and was unique in the way that you had to play with your blinks. The one build I'd like to add is that it would've been great if there was facial tracking on top of blink-tracking, so that I could move my head instead of my mouse towards the different choices. Created a little game review on Tiktok for it too:
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: just incredible. quite the short story, sitting around the two hour mark of playtime, but so worth it. best to go into this game knowing nothing about it except that there's a blinking mechanic; it's most enjoyable that way. almost didn't want to replay it a second time purely because of how much it impacted me the first time, knowing that I wont get to experience the game like that again. overall very worth the time, so sit down and enjoy this if you're available to.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is absolutely amazing. The story, the characters...just everything! Admitedly I have no camera so I didn't get the full expirience but even so it was a delightful journey. The music, the ferryman... everything was beautiful! Definitly would play it again if I ever get a camera installed!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my favorite experience ever playing a video game. I could even call this one of the best experiences I've had in my life. The mechanic of this game forced me to feel more emotion when I accidentally skipped a scene, and I got super invested in the story line. Every bit of this game I played I loved, and I believe I will feel that way for a long time. If you prefer story over gameplay, I highly recommend this. Enjoy it
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: While many people paint an absolute picture of a fantastic game, i found the gameplay mechanic of using the blink via webcam to be irritating. Forcing yourself to keep your eyes open in every scene you are interested in hearing more is straining. Did i miss something interesting or even relevant to make the story great? In my opinion the answer to this question should always be no. And with that in mind, the things i saw were a good game, an innovative game, but not a great game that many others made it out to be.Enjoy your little journey through the life of Benjamin but do not expect an absolute master piece.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly one of a kind. You can only experience this game for a first time once, and be sure that you get the chance to do so. $10 was an absolute steal for this masterpiece of storytelling. The voice acting in this game is phenomenal, and I love the art style. The blinking mechanic really takes it to that next level immersing you in the story. I really didn't know what I was getting into when playing for the first time, but boy do I know now. Buy it. Play it. I promise you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Well ♥♥♥♥ if it is not me crying like a little b*tch once again. it's one of those games that grips you tight and drags you through an immersive experience. Benny is in all of us, Benny is a liar, a dreamer, a talent, Benny is gifted in something so special that only you can name it.I haven't slept enough at the day I played this game, and believe me even if he said don't fight it I splashed my face with cold water just to keep my eyes open in some scenes. God... What an amazing experience. If you haven't played it yet, the heck are you waiting for?
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the story is very important for games like these and on that end it did told a very compelling story that'll stick with you after the credits. It's different for everyone but personally I don't feel the eye blinking tracking with the camera helps with the story telling or the enjoyment of the game. In fact it was the opposite for me, it became very intrusive to the storytelling if you blink in the scene when there was still clearly a few lines left to be told. I personally would recommend turning it off so you wouldn't miss out on an otherwise strong plot and character backgrounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous. Genius. Heartbreaking. Just three of the words I think describe Before Your Eyes. A charming art-style accompanied by a way of playing that I've never seen before, and a story that will make even the most emotionally cold people shed a tear.I want to say much more about this game, but its one of those that just has to be played. Saying anymore would ruin it. Just play it. Its short, its cheap, and its brilliant. There's no reason not to.10/10Unforgettably unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a great story that truthfully brought me to tears to the point i was struggling not to blink at times during it. I highly recommend this game. Whether you buy it and play it yourself or watch someone play it this story is very important and very beautiful. Like many other reviews for this game I will not spoil beyond just that.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: this game has one key selling point; the blink interactions. take this away, and it feels very mediocre. i feel harsh saying it; after all, the music is soothing, the graphics are charming, but the story was lacking 'bite'. Before your eyes is a very short game that i got on sale. i don't think it's worth the full price. OK to buy if you want to check out how good the eye/blink interaction is - i had no issue with it, worked perfectly fine for me. one downfall of this blink interaction is that at certain points you have to blink to move on to the next scene. if you blink too fast accidentally, you can miss dialogue that adds more layers to the story. it's a nice little game but the story wasn't satisfying (or even that sad, as heartless as that sounds. i've seen sad indie games done well, this ain't it). but you can't expect too much when the game's only about 2 ish hours. i got about 6 hours play time because it doesn't save your progress so i left it open whilst doing other stuff. nonetheless, Before Your Eyes appears to be the first game to use blinking as a key function in a game. will be interesting to see if further games follow suit.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing makes me cry, I don't mean that as a statement about how strong and stoic I am, this is actually a thing I struggle with and work through in therapy, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game did something to me, I only finished it like 20 mins so I'm probably in that post game phase but I still seriously suggest you play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant game! This game takes what seems like a stupid gimmick, and basically perfects it. The story is about looking back at your life and apprechiating it. It's so moving, I think anyone would like this. Just, please play this game. It's wonderful! (also, the blinking mechanic works really well. It does not glitch or stop working)
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Blink once and a few seconds have passed. Blink twice and it's the next morning. Sure you lived through the intervening time but it doesn't feel like that way now that we're well into next month. You will blink and your summer will be over. You strain your focus to stay aware and stay here in this god awful present. As always no matter how hard you will your eyelids to stay open, even pulling them upright with your fingers, inevitably they shut for only a second and...Now you realize that it's tomorrow already. You had things you wanted to do yesterday when it was still today. You feel a bit guilty for not accomplishing them but then it dawns on you. There really isn't anything you can do about it. You can feel guilt or not but the past will only keep getting further away. Cringey middle school memory? What am I to do 7 years from that moment. You forgot to brush your teeth? Okay you should really brush your teeth. You are kinda stuck with them for life please take care of your body and mind. This game is about time. What it means to have lived a long fulfilling life. What it feels like to perfectly envision the life you want to have only to come back to the actuality of what your life really turned out to be. It's a great game. It uses your camera to track blinking in a way no game has ever done before. It's incredible. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Really short and sweet experience. If you have a webcam the games mechanic functions as another level of immersiveness which does ample amount to heighten the key emotional notes and moments throughout the game. It was only around an hour and a half in length and I was sobbing through out. Voice acting is really good, and I suppose the fact it was so relatable as an experience made this strike a chord with me in particular. One of my favourite games and I'll recommend forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the more unique experiences I've had the pleasure of playing through with the tracking of blinks to pass through memories. The story is really well thought out and hits in the feels towards the end. Only thing I think I would change is allowing the option of 2 blinks for each metronome as sometimes I would miss a massive chunk of the dialogue because I happened to blink the moment it popped up. Overall a fantastic game and deserves more attention. Even at its short length, it was well worth the playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an experienceThe voice acting was incredibly well done, the art style was charming, music was powerful and the narrative was beautiful, the characters and the story all felt so natural and real. All of that, told in a very unique style. Highly recommended to play with the webcam first, and it's worth the second play through, to hear the full dialogue and/or see the other choices. But disclaimer, I dunno if it's just me, but it's more emotional the second time man
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough. This is like a 100/10 game. Such a unique idea to control a game, although this can become a bit uncomfortable. But the story is one of the most beautiful and touching one I have ever seen and it must be experienced by everyone. If I could forget this game's entire plot I would be grateful. It would be a pleasure to experience this again for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to try this game. I never buy games on steam, so for me to get a game on here, I really have to want to try something. The storyline was good, and the concept was awesome. But I am very disappointed. I kept having issues with the game glitching and showing a black screen. I tried restarting the game and recalibrating several times, but it seems to me that the creators have not came up with a feature for you to troubleshoot. Sad because now I am going to just watch gameplay of the ending on youtube. Very disappointed, and wouldnt recommend until problems are fixed. Felt as if I threw my 10$ away just for a hour and a half of frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers an unforgettable experience. Since playing Red Dead, I haven’t come across a story as moving and thoughtfully crafted as Before Your Eyes. Despite its short playtime of under two hours, it delivers an emotionally powerful journey that brought me to tears and made me reflect deeply on the people and things I cherish. If you're considering buying this game, I highly recommend it. Take your time and make choices that resonate with you. Beautiful game you won't regret the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS: I'm generally one to enjoy artsy games, but the story and themes of this one did nothing for me. Reading the reviews, I'm surely in the minority, but the story felt very forced in its pursuit to make me feel sad, and it wasn't effective to me. I felt like I had just watched an average movie student final project, very eager to make me feel things, but not sure why or how. The blinking mechanic was interesting though.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I will cherish throughout my whole life. Such an interesting mechanic used in such an effective way. The story left me speechless, crying, alone at 2 in the morning. You can play the game without blinking, but I strongly advise you to enable the webcam for this experience. Life comes at you fast, really fast...
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully constructed little game with a ton of emotional depth. The blinking mechanic, despite being a little gimmicky at times, is pretty innovative and ties into the narrative quite nicely. It is a very short experience, but I got my money's worth out of it.Pros:-Great art style and sound design-Excellent voice acting, especially from the ferryman and the mother character-Beautiful narrative. I cried and so will you.Cons:-Very short. I completed the game in under 2 hours.  -Blinking mechanic was buggy at times. Maybe I just had poor lighting for my webcam, but I found myself having to calibrate the eye detection every 20 minutes or so. Some of the narrative beats in the game fell flat as I was struggling to get the game to detect my blinks.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: You will strain your eyes thinking you can beat time. You will curse yourself when you blink and let a moment pass too soon. You will cry. Before Your Eyes is a simple game in its core, solely operated by your mouse and eyes. This simplicity however comes only to its benefit. Few games are able to use that interactive to create a truly moving experience, but Before Your Eyes does just that. It hooks you in and doesn't let go until the very end. Do not expect a long game, expect a beautiful one.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: SUCH a heartwrenching game .. I hardly feel sad or emotional playing games, but this takes the cake. All I can say is that It’s a tearjerker..  The story is sad and tragic but strangely soothing and beautiful at the same time.I absolutely loved the concept of blinking (via webcam) that makes time pass in-game. So innovative and one of a kind! the game has been so well made.. I can clearly see how much of thought and emotion has been put into it. Truly deserving of the awards it got!If you’re feeling the emo vibes, go play this game :( you won’t regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I played through, and I was loving the story; however, I read the reviews before I played (there weren't spoilers in what I read, luckily), and they all mentioned how the tears naturally would come. I made it so far, and I was thinking about how I was going to say I made it through without crying, and then I finally reached the end, and the tears came. Fantastic little story, really makes you want to avoid blinking, and sometimes you'll even find it hard not to blink, but you'll feel like you can't. I would recommend you use a webcam for the game if possible, it really does enhance what you feel.tl;dr: Amazing story, cool gameplay concept, I toughed it through till the end, but I couldn't avoid the tears in the end. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the best games I've ever played. I've been playing games for the past 20 odd years. This game will make you happy and cry at the same time. It has the best story I've every played! It was truly amazing, I wish I could forget about this game and play it again it was that good. I can not recommend this game enough, it truly has the best story I've every played. The price of this game is so under-rated, It truly is worth the £9.00! Well done to everyone that created this game, truly a master piece!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before your eyes plays out like a visual novel that tugs on the heartstrings. You find yourself as a lost soul out at sea only to be reeled in by a canine orator. You are found out to be Benjamin Brynn and his story is truly amazing. Through your webcam, the game tracks when you blink which allows you to progress through a wonderful narrative adventure with amazing visuals and a wonderfully crafted world with  many fleshed out characters.By blinking, you’ll jump days, weeks, and sometimes years forward in Ben’s life. The moments are fleeting and sometimes you may find yourself relishing and cherishing beautiful moments for them to well... disappear in a blink.I will avoid going to deep into the story as to not ruin your personal experience but I will say this game does tackle  narrative themes of depression, the desire for self fulfillment and existentialism. The game even delves into relationship dynamics in relation to how they shape the life of a child and how they may see the world.This is a game I will hold close to my heart and will continue to share with others. It's beautiful and I hope you find the experience to be just as memorable and charming as I do.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: one of  the best interactive story games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. very surprised the idea has never been used before as it adds a whole new level of immersion into the rich and vibrant storytelling they use throughout the game. this is not so much a game as it is an experience and therefore it will not be for every one  you are looking for something that is going to leave with a sense of wonder and with a puddle full of tears I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Please play this game. I was terrible at it and blinked way too much and probably missed half the story and will have to replay it another time but it's moving and beautiful and feels like it means something. The mechanics are fun and make it feel more interactive then just a point and click game is usually able to achieve, although I guess you're not really clicking at all. Puts things into a perspective, and is honestly worth the ten bucks if you have it to spare.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely love this game and think that everyone should play it, this game hit me on such a deeply personal subject for me which I wont say as I dont want to spoil, but because of that this game had me crying for more than just like a couple seconds after beating it. I was still thinking about this game like an hour after beating it. This game, although I cant pinpoint how, definitely changed a lot of the ways I thought at the time and helped me through one of my rough patches. Im so excited for whatever this studio works on next as I will buy it as soon as it releases no questions asked.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: "Before Your Eyes" is a brilliant game that beautifully illustrates how fast time flies (before your eyes haha), reminding you to treasure every moment. The unique technological use of the camera function, which reads your blinks, is creatively and intelligently integrated into the story, blending reality with fiction in a beautiful philosophical dance.The narrative is deeply moving, and the gameplay mechanics are innovative, making it a truly immersive experience. The way your blinks control the flow of the story adds a layer of depth and intimacy that is rare in games.10/10 – I would always recommend this game. Additionally, I had the privilege of game-testing their upcoming title, "Goodbye Universe," and I can't wait to fully play it when it releases soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: As every living being is bound to, we are ultimately going to be drifted away by time and will cease to live. Before Your Eyes has an amazing way of portraying such a powerful, albeit rather scary, concept. For such a short experience, it is a great reminder of how important it is to live our lives as ambitiously as possible.Cherish the life you breathe and hold your loved ones close because life will flash right Before Your Eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Where the heck do I begin with this game.Okay this game will make you feel a lot of emotion and that is true! You will laugh, be angry, happy, worried, scared, and the biggest of all cry. I will of course not spoil the game at all but what I will say is, its not just a single story you can choose what you want to do and change the way of the story based off your choices.The fact the story keep moving when you blink is smart! We humans blink a lot sometimes without knowing. You could be wanting to know more about whats happening but then you accidentally blink and skip that and you are left to wonder what was going on.I high recommend buying this game you will feel a lot of emotions and they feel good even the sad part feel good... it felt good to be happy seeing the cute things in the story and it felt good to cry for the hard stuff in the story.BUY THIS GAME NOW
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This was honestly such an immersive and emotional experience. It has a really unique gameplay gimmic (blinking) and it works so well and makes this game just so much more immersive.The story is also really good. It has you go through the life of a boy with a lot of time skips. There's some really great twists and turns the story takes and while it's not a very long story, it's a very good and emotional one.I totally recommend checking this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game so much for making me cry so much.And after you think things are going a certain way, it keeps going, and then it makes me cry even more. So... that's cool, I guess.And I hate that I had the camera view enabled in the corner, so that it could track my eye blinks. Because it meant I had to look at my dumb face crying. Dumb game, I hated it. Would cry again.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is one of those games that feel like a hidden gem. It's unique mechanics and art style set it apart from most modern games, however, that's not where this game truly shines. GoodbyeWorld Games took all of those unique elements and combined them to tell a truly captivating story. Never has a game made me feel such emotion for characters in such a short time. Every award this game has won is truly deserved. If you are looking for a game that breaks the modern game stereotype, this is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I have no other words to say other than Before Your Eyes is simply fantastic. A must buy for anyone looking for an emotional story told in a unique way. While you could play this game without a webcam, I'd strongly urge to play with one otherwise you'd miss out on a wholly unique experience that can't be found anywhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone should play this game. Simple, quick, yet deeply impactful and filled with emotion. It gives To The Moon such a run for it's money they aren't really in the same league. If you're avoiding playing this game because you don't want it to make you cry, I was the same way. But now that I've gone though it I'm so glad I did and I bet you will as well. Simply an unforgettable experience.I loved how shot and tight-knit everything was. I beat it in under 2 hours and could easily get a refund. But honestly I want to buy the game all over again just to support the devs. They earned the 8 or 10 dollars. I can't wait to share this story with everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Before Your Eyes is probably one of the most impressively written games I have ever played. Though you, the player, are not expected to do much mechanically-wise, B.Y.E allows you to become fully immersed in a story that can be told millions of different ways... but all end up in the same, rocky road to the ending. With it's adorable art style, phenomenal voice acting, and memorable story writing- this game is one that is unforgettable. It's emotional, honest, and brutal, allowing the audience (the player) to fully immerse and enjoy themselves as they begin to pose as the main character and see themselves through his eyes. The main metaphor of the game is that everything doesn't last forever. When something happens, you cannot change or effect that thing once it has taken place. The player learns to accept the things around them by being told a truly moving story that flows smoothly from beginning to end.DEFINITELY recommend this game to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I wishlisted this game for the webcam interaction, and bought it on a sale without looking much at it. I hadn't even read the game's description and thought I signed up for a "trippy experience". Boy I was not ready for this.I could tell you that Before Your Eyes tells a story about loss, but it's more than that. It makes you live through it. The first person and blink interaction does wonders for the immersion, it really makes you feel the same way as the protagonist.And when you think the story was over, that it only got you a bit emotional at the end the game presents a twist that it stabs you out of nowhere and twists the knife until you cry.We need more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: That was intense! Highly recommend. I have never wanted to keep my eyes open so badly. I went from the sahara desert to the nile all in one sitting. Bravo, will be playing again. I don't think the game would be quite so immersive and powerful without the webcam, but still worth playing! Excellent story and unique game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: Oh damn... the story and design of the game captures that feeling of being in a dream and trying hard not to wake up because you want to see what happens next. Or that feeling of trying to focus long enough to remember the details of something distant but really important to you. Great story, Voice Actors, Visualsdamn
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A true work of art...  I had been meaning to play this game for a while, but had never got to do so. It was an emotional journey. The story is delivered beautifully, and the utilization of the blink mechanic provides the opportunity for you to fully immerse yourself and relive Benny's memories. I was having such a hard time playing the final 30 minutes of the game because I couldn't stop crying. I never imagined a game could bring me to tears in the way this one did. Thank you GoodbyeWorld Games; your masterpiece is absolutely worthwhile to play. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: A work of art and a very emotional game that unfolds in layers, with different emotions at every stage. A masterpiece that you should definitely play. Just be prepared for an emotional roller coaster.Made me genuinely cry at the end and considering the fact that i'm away from my parents in a totally different country, working, made me realise how much i miss my family.I give it a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: No matter how much I tried to "calibrate" the camera, the detection doesn't work correctly, it "blinks" as soon as the possibility for that appears. I know I could cheat and play with the mouse, but that seems like it will render the experience pointless.I am sure the game is as amazing as people say they are, but it's clearly incompatible with at least  set-ups. And mine's just a simple laptop!If you  buy it, please play it immediately upon purchase to ensure the camera detection thing works on your machine, just so that you can refund it if you end up in a situation like mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most beautiful game I have ever played. First time I ever actually cried while playing a game. The story is so sad, but so beautiful at the same time. Literally only gripe I have with before your eyes is that at some points the motion capture is weird and that can take out from the experience, but the characters, story, voice actors, music and everything else is just so good that you don't even notice it in the first play through.I sincerely recommend this game, it's only 2 hours, and 2 hours very well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews but upon finishing this game I decided that I needed to, at least this once, because this is an important narrative that should be shared.Before Your Eyes is a beautifully written masterpiece that features a simple mechanic: time will pass in the game each time you blink. This will inevitably happen regardless of how much you try to hold on to the moment, not unlike the fleeting present.I type this next to the piano I am currently learning. The piano is a key instrument to the story, which is probably why it struck such a chord with me. I aspire to be an artist someday and create music that inspires others. And maybe it will live on in people after I am gone, much like this work of art. Nevertheless, even if I don't succeed, this story is mine and I must own it before it disappears. Perhaps that is what this game is about.You should play it.It's short.Like life.BYE.
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: what games should be and should do is all in games like this one a beautiful masterpiece. stunning art style, new game play ideas. it really makes you count every blink you do. this game taught me that time slides faster than we know. and no matter how we like the sometimes are, we can't stay there. we have and will move on. so we just need to enjoy it, and let it slide. I send my gratitude and appreciation to every genius worked and worked on this game to deliver this phenomenal experience to us
_childDocuments_.name: Before Your Eyes

_childDocuments_.review: This game has beautiful art and an immersive and well-written story 10/10“It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it. Life is long enough, and a sufficiently generous amount has been given to us for the highest achievements if it were all well invested. But when it is wasted in heedless luxury and spent on no good activity, we are forced at last by death’s final constraint to realize that it has passed away before we knew it was passing. detailed_description: Just Updated The Walking Dead Onslaught Combat Rebalance Patch is Now Live, swing over to our Steam post to read the full patch notes Digital Deluxe Edition Includes Iconic Show Weapons Skins Pack: Lucille, Rick’s Mace, The Red Machete and Tyreese’s Hammer, Alexandria Crafting Starter Kit, The Walking Dead Onslaught Mini-Soundtrack and Art Book. About the Game There’s no rest when survival is on the line. Step into AMC’s The Walking Dead and prepare for an onslaught of walkers as you assume the roles of your favorite characters from the show, and confront the horrors and humanity of this apocalyptic new world. RECLAIM YOUR HUMANITY The war with the Saviors has finally come to an end, but the damage lingers in the hearts of those who survived it. It will take risk and sacrifice to mend this broken society and rebuild what remains of Alexandria for future generations. Are prepared to do your part? STEP INTO AMC’S THE WALKING DEAD Play as Rick, Daryl, Michonne, and Carol and set up your home base in the Alexandria Safe Zone. Here, you’ll play through chapters of an all-new story, embark on Scavenger runs, upgrade your player stats, modify and customize weapons, trade in resources to grow your community, and interact with your favorite characters. Successfully complete supply runs, and you’ll see Alexandria transform as you rebuild the settlement into a fortified bastion of hope for humanity’s future. ULTIMATE COMBAT FREEDOM Stave off the walker threat wielding 24 ranged and melee weapons—including iconic pieces from the show— with realistic handling and intuitive VR motion mechanics. Experience the visceral Progressive Dismemberment system that realistically depicts your every attack against the undead. Discover a variety of modifications for each weapon to fine-tune and suit your combat style. FAST-ACTION SURVIVAL Leave nothing behind. Every trip beyond the walls of Alexandria means a chance to collect valuable weapons, food, materials, and other resources for the community. But beware: every supply run provides unpredictable walker encounters, resource availability, and obstacles to test your sense of flight or fight. CAMPAIGN STORY Play as Daryl Dixon through an original campaign story about a supply run gone awry and an ensuing encounter with a watchful stranger in a mysterious town.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Decent melee combat.- Supply raids: grabbing all you can with limited time and tons of zombies around can be thrilling.- Lots of upgradable weapons.Cons:- Boring and short story (7 chapters of walking around as Daryl with some zombie killing).- Tons of reused assets (supply runs use same levels over and over again, only loot changes).- Outdated VR shooter design (weapon is glued to your dominant hand, changing them with radial menu, etc).- Invisible walls (especially the moving one during supply raids).- Almost zero interactivity (you only interact with zombies and doors/switches).- Awful guns (revolver, crossbow and assault rifle are somewhat fine but still useless) - up to 3 headshots to kill a walker.- Unpolished and glitchy (walkers sometimes fly away to the moon from a single arrow or glitch around violently).- Graphics - not bad, but 2d sprites of walkers in supply runs and 2d fire in Alexandria...- Physics - weapons are basically weightless, light poke with fireaxe will decapitate a zombie. Objects on levels don't have physics at all.- Random lags and stutters on walker kills or just turning around.- No turning speed adjustment.- Very easy, walkers are harmless even on max difficulty.I don't know what happened during the development of the game, so my best guesses would be zero budget, zero effort or a mountain of compromises. Remember all those awful licensed games that were released at the same time the big movies hit the theaters? Onslaught feels just like any of them, just in VR. Game is basically just smashing zombies with a hammer while playing as one of TWD characters. Everything else was just thrown in to make it longer or look like a more complete game.So much weapons - only fireaxe is really good, broken even. Machete is decent, revolver, assault rifle and crossbow are usable.Weapons are upgradable - they just suck a little bit less with them. And fireaxe becomes even more broken.So much resources to scavenge - literal waste of time, since upgrading Alexandria is useless (weapons mostly too).Maybe the core is so good all of this is not important? Sadly, no. While fun, melee combat is barebones as well. You can smash or stab through heads, cut off limbs and hit zombies with offhand or grab them by the neck (grabbing is off when you hold ranged weapon). Aside from slow-mo/berserk modes with some weapons, that's it. Cut off a leg - walker will die instantly, cause you need effort to make a crawling animation. Slice a body with katana - nothing will be cut off. As a result, after couple of hours combat becomes boring.Thanks to regional pricing, game cost me about as much as couple of meals, and it's probably worth even less. 30$ for this would be an unfunny joke. If you really want to check it out - wait for a 80% plus sale. Hoping for fixes is usless IMO, technical issues can be fixed, but it'll remain a super-turbo-zombie puncher-2000 with some walking anyway. And the existence of Saints and Sinners makes this game a complete embarrassment.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED 10/28/20Graphics☐ Perfection☐ Great☐ Alright✅ Mediocre☐ Superman 64Sound☐ Musical Perfection☐ Great✅ Alright☐ Bad☐ Knives Scraping on Rusty Garbage BinsStory☐ Breathtaking☐ Very Good✅ Alright☐ Uninspired/Bad☐ Death StrandingGameplay☐ Perfection☐ Very Good☐ Alright✅ Repetitive/Boring☐ Skyscraper SimulatorControls☐ Perfect☐ Very Good☐  Alright✅ Wonky☐ Bubsy 3DBugs☐ Clean as a Whistle☐ Hardly Noticeable☐ There's a few☐ There's a lot✅ Feels UnfinishedDifficulty✅Opening the Game is the Most Challenging Part☐ Easy☐ Alright☐ Tough but Fair☐ Dark SoulsVR-ness☐ Feels Perfect in Every Way☐ Feels Great☐ Feels Alright☐ Feels Disconnected✅ PainfulOVERALL SCORE: 4/10The Walking Dead Onslaught is the most frustrating kind of game. It's a game with so much potential that is executed so inefficiently. The voice actors for Eugene, Carol, and Darryl are the only Walking Dead characters that have the appropriate voice actors. The voice actors for Rick Grimes and Michonne are painfully bad. The difficulty is frustrating. It isn't a hard game, it's just very tedious and irritating to play. If you use the combat knife (the first weapon you get in the game) you might as well just quit. While players are encouraged to use the combat knife, it gets stuck in zombies and refuses to come out no matter how much you tug. It goes in effortlessly, but won't come out for at least 5 or 6 seconds. Even after 4 hours of play on the hardest difficulty, I never once took a single point of damage (or if I did, it wasn't made clear I was taking damage). The developer's idea of difficulty is, "oh, just make add more zombies and give them more health." The armored zombies don't feel armored, just that they have more health. I've had armored zombies take 10 or 11 stabs to the head before they finally die to being pushed away. Guns have been improved, as walkers now are one shots to the head, however this is only at point blank range. Character animations are uncomfortable and wonky and riddled with desync that constantly pulls players out of the experience. The levels feel uncomfortably linear and are designed to discourage and refuse to reward exploration. The main campaign is also strangely chopped up and feels disconnected from from everything else in the game. Alexandria, which acts as a sort of hub for the game, feels strangely devoid of life for a community that is supposed to be thriving with close to 60 people living there. It also feels incredibly restrictive and you can't explore the town at all. I paid $40 for the deluxe version, but I haven't seen any content that extra $10 purchased. Combine all of these issues with archaic VR controls and laughable index support, and you have a game that fails to deliver on most accounts. I cannot recommend you spend $30 or $40 to buy this game in it's current state. If anything, the recent update made the game worse. Don't buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been sat in my Steam library uninstalled since I got it in a bundle forever ago because the reviews made it out to be a non-functional sh*tshow. A lot of the reviews just encourage you to buy Saints and Sinners instead which is where I think the problem lies: when compared to S&S it's less polished and goes for a less stylised look more grounded in realism, a much more arcade-like style of gameplay, far less emphasis on a storyline, and throws in some "meh" settlement-building mechanics on top. A game being rough around the edges compared to similar games doesn't mean it's worth burning to the ground and salting the earth like some of these reviews imply, though.Seriously, to reiterate, the game is neither dogsh*t-awful  the second coming of VR Christ. It's just firmly decent:- I haven't experienced any of the bugs other people have mentioned, or any at all besides small inane ones that were so inconsequential that I only noticed them when I actively went looking for bugs- It runs without a single hitch on my mid-range PC- Controls are fine. Swipe-to-turn being the only turning method on Vive wands regardless of which turning option you choose isn't super fun, but it took me less than 10 minutes to get used to it. To be honest, I can't bring myself to be mad over the controls for a relatively new VR game being clearly optimised for thumbsticks considering almost every modern VR controller uses them. Slightly bothersome at worst.- All the options are highly configurable, and doing so is both straightforward and easy- It uses a physics system as the basis for its melee combat and gun-handling, which feels pretty nice and intuitive if you're not going in expecting it to be exactly like S&S or Boneworks. Thanks to this physics system, zombies react fairly believably to being hit with most things which makes melee weapons satisfying to use (something a lot of cheap zombie shooters don't seem to bother much with), though their reactions don't have a huge amount of depth. - I will say that headshots with guns not being a guaranteed one-hit kill utterly sucks the fun out of taking the time to aim for it. Like sure, I get it's to encourage you to use heavier guns, but  much ammo can be wasted clearing a relatively small number of zombies this way that it becomes an annoyance more than anything. If it's more convenient for me to shave some seconds off by body-shotting something to death then there's a flaw in the design.- Guns being tied to the dominant hand and not allowing for deeper controls commonplace in modern VR shooters kinda sucks, but it's fine.- The storyline I've experienced so far (while not being all that engaging) is passable. Definitely better than other VR zombie games that barely bother to write a plot at all.- Environments and assets are frequently re-used to varying degrees, but that can be said about countless games and this is far from being the most egregious use of it I've seen.Basically: If you go into this understanding that it's not really trying to be Saints and Sinners then you'll probably be pleasantly surprised, especially if you enjoy the show.EDIT: I've now completed the game and had a ♥♥♥♥-ton of fun with it, and I'll be completing the few achievements I have left to 100% it. My time with this made me realise some of y'all getting genuinely angry in your reviews are either children or just have no idea how to enjoy a game for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I have officially 100%ed both The Walking Dead VR games, them being 'Saints and Sinners' and 'Onslaught'. This game really does lack creativity and plays everything hella safe, but it's still incredibly fun to me and I personally believe that the 20 USD that i paid for the game on sale was worth it! I got 15 hours of decent exercise and a good amount of fun, along with a crap ton of details for Walking Dead fans to enjoy and nerd out about.This Walking Dead game really does seem to take an approach similar to the television show; This game is very action based with little to no substance. What you're paying for is an arm swinging simulator with a lot of love and attention to detail for fans of the series. Unfortunately, that's about it! I'd not have paid for this if it was not on sale. But since I did, I have no regrets. I absolutely love getting to hear these characters get voices and to see all of the references to the storylines from the comics and show (but mostly the show).For characters, this game features the voices of Walking Dead TV stars Melissa McBride as Carol, Norman Reedus as Daryl, and Josh McDermitt as Eugene. Newcomers to the franchise voice Rick and Michonne, and they both do a great job! Keith Ferguson takes on the role of Rick whilst G. K. Bowes does an INCREDIBLE MICHONNE!!!! There are also references and missions from a lot of awesome characters like Maggie and Negan and Siddiq (yes even Siddiq) that make side quests in the game more interesting to do! And there are plenty of graffiti references to groups from the series!So nerd stuffs aside, I've never seen the TV show. I've only played every game and read the comic series up to issue 178. So unfortunately I may be biased, but I still don't understand a lot of the references since this game is based entirely on the AMC TV show. I still think the game is incredibly fun even without understanding a lot of it! The seven mission campaign is of decent length and was fun to play through twice, even if it really is just a walking and swinging simulator. The side missions are bite sized versions of the campaign missions essentially with less goals. So really, both the campaign and side activities are the same thing. Don't like swinging and shooting and walking for hours upon hours? Might not be your game.If you want a more immersive role-playing experience set in this universe, definitely play Saints and Sinners as that is an incredible game. This game is much more simple and small. Even 100%ing it only took me less than 15 hours, whilst doing the same in the other game took me 35 hours. Getting this game on sale is basically the only way I suggest anyone buy it!TL;DR This game is great (to me only) and I love it. I really hope it gets DLC featuring some of the cut features such as multiplayer co-op or a potential continuation of the game's campaign since there are absolutely ways it can be continued (and it even seems kinda hinted at by the ending heehee) but from the reviews and general reception of the game and sales I highly doubt it will be continued. I absolutely will be keeping my eyes open for future updates though, because I crave the hunt and desire MORE SLAUGHTER OwO

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like an app-game they decided to convert to VR at the last second. After playing The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners, I thought that this would be more like that game, but was I absolutely wrong. In story mode you will mostly find yourself running through a linear level listening to an occasional narration while trying to grab all the shiny resource materials for upgrades and "base building". The non-story mode missions are pretty much the same thing with the narration replaced by annoying lines from other characters and an encroaching barrier wall chasing you (it's just a sort of red wall with black zombie silhouettes). Speaking of story, without giving any spoilers (not that there seems much to spoil), it was pretty unsatisfying. It was left open ended and unfinished. Maybe they're hoping for DLC or a sequel to continue it, or maybe it ties into some obscure part of the comics or TV series. I'm no expert on obscure Walking Dead lore. Either way I found it very disappointing.The "base building" is just getting enough resources to craft and upgrade buildings for their perks. You have a very limited area to walk around. The buildings you make are basically just a background element.Admittedly I did find if fairly satisfying to upgrade the Katana and slice though walkers, even if you can't actually chop them in two. Also, despite the screen-shot (and I'm pretty sure there used to be a scene of it used in the video too) I never found any grenade launcher. And I did get the achievements for finding all weapons (in the armory) and killing a walker with every weapon in the game.I bought this game on sale, but still think I paid too much for it. If you looking for a sort of mindless app-like game where you mostly run around linear levels listening to flat line readings and grabbing shiny items for grinding out upgrades, this might be worth it if it goes on sale for a buck or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited until I had gotten all of the achievements to write a review - which took 14 hours and 30 minutes of playing this mess. In that entire time playing, I only died a total of 2 times; the first time I did a scavenger mission - not realising how quick the herd was - and once in the story mission by getting stuck in the middle of a pack of walkers.A lot of people have been saying that you shouldn't compare the game to Saints and Sinners since they are completely different genres which is understandable, but there is no doubt that Saints and Sinners is clearly the more superior Walking Dead VR Game. Pros: - Decent Visuals - Daryl's story is where the game shines best - Melee and Gun Combat is alright (Melee is way better though) - A lot of movement options to choose from - Walker models look really good Cons: - The main story is way too short (you can finish it in about 3 hours) - Game is definitely not worth the price it has been given - Very glitchy and buggy at times (Melee weapons not working, model stretching, walkers popping in and out of existence and so on) - Voice acting is terrible (only good ones are Daryl and Eugene) - No reward for doing everything you can (all weapon upgrades, all requisitions, story on veteran) - End game is really boring - Game feels rushed and unfinished - Combat is really repetitive - Game becomes ridiculously easy once you get the axe, katana and the python (Rick's gun) 0.9% of people who have played this game have unlocked every single achievment (me included) which really does go to show just how much people are refusing to play the game after completing the story. The achievements aren't that hard either, they just mainly playing the story on different difficulties, killing walkers (sometimes in specific ways, or with specific weapons) and just completing all upgrades.That's pretty much all that came to mind when writing this. I'm sure there are a lot more negatives and positives I haven't thought of about this game. If you are wanting to get a Walking Dead VR game, I'd suggest going for Saints and Sinners instead of this one as this is no where close to being as good as that game was. If you are hellbent on getting this game, wait until it's on sale (the game feels like it should be worth £5-£10)

_childDocuments_.review: 1st off this is not Saints and Sinners. This is more of an arcade style RPG light Shoot, loot and scoot. They have fixed the one big problem which was needed 3 or more shots to the brain to kill a zombie with a pistol. Now as long as it's a well placed shot it's a 1 hit kill even with level 1 weapons. They also rebalanced the melee so you can just run around stabbing. Melee weapons get stuck and it's easy to get swarmed. These new updates take the game from crap to very fun. I just hope they bring back the multiplayer they had planned.This game with up to 4 player co-op would be amazing.My one main complaint about this game is that it's not set for a lefty. You should be able to hold a gun in any hand no matter the control setup. Being a lefty I am use to a righty movement setup in VR while dual gunning or single but in the left hand. So if you are a lefty until they fix it you either have to use the lefty controls which don't work well for me or you have to be a good shot with your right hand. Fix this and it could be great.Overall it is a very fun game. Just don't expect S&S story or RPG depth.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good as long as you do not expect it to be Saints and Sinners v2.0. It is a different type of game... yes they are both based on the same franchise and yes this one is newer and uses the known characters from the series (while S&S does not). I believe those combined created the expectation that it would be a better version of S&S, which is not.This is a more arcade experience. It has a story (which is straightforward - just follow the path and get to the other side alive) and mission based gameplay to gather resources and improve your base, weapons and armor. It is good for what it does. It has good graphics and enjoyable gameplay, but as said earlier it is more of an arcade than an adventure. So if you like mindless zombie killing action, with both ranged and close combat (mostly close as the bullets are limited) this is a good choice, but if you are looking for an adventure with puzzle solving and investigation you won't find it here. I like both types of games so I accept it for what it is and I am glad that I gave it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game had excellent potential, but it seems the developer completely skipped game-play testing and Q/A, and then just moved on to different things. They definitely deserve all the negative reviews the game has gotten. But, if you can pick this game up for less than a few bucks, then it might be worth it.I got this game for €1.50, but was still rather skeptical given the mostly negative reviews that this game has gotten. I must say, I'm a bit torn. On one hand, the game is arguably worth €1.50. But if I had paid more than €5 for this for this game, I would be sorely disappointed. This game is really weird. The best I can guess is that the developers ran into a hard deadline and some manager or executive mandated that the game be released "as-is", without fixing all the little bugs that makes the whole difference between an enjoyable and unenjoyable VR game.The game definitely has a lot of things that could work really well and be a great fit for a "The Walking Dead" game. Things like base/home-town building, weapon modding, a progression system, etc. And of course, killing zombies is always fun.But then, the game is also riddled with things that negatively affect the gaming experience. The most immediate you will notice is the poor locomotion controls. The game supports three types of locomotion: Teleport, "move around with the thumb stick", and "run with your arms". None of these are implemented properly. 1. The teleport will often be "white" when you are about to teleport, only to turn red right when you let go of the X button, thus cancelling your teleport and leave you to be consumed by zombies.2. Moving around with the thumbstick is slow, and the game doesn't register "click to sprint" well at all. It would probably work OK if sprinting was always enabled, or if you could "click to toggle". But the game will often stop your sprint, switching you back to "walking", and not register further clicks to re-enable sprinting. 3. And finally, "swing your arms to move around" is just horribly broken, and would probably not work in a game like this, since it doesn't enable you to move sideways relative to the way you are looking. (But hey, here's a free idea, how about instead of holding X to move forward and Y to move backwards, you move the thumbstick the direction you want to go, and swing your arms fast or slow to go that direction fast or slowly).Oh, and you cannot combine means of locomotion, e.g. mix "teleport" and "move around smoothly using the joystick", like you can in many other games. You have to choose one. Even though e.g. "running" and "teleporting" are on different keys, and you could easily have both. That would also alleviate some of the bugs, since if a teleport "fails", you could still move a little using the thumbstick. But nooo, we wouldn't want anything to make the experience less terrible.  So, locomotion is really bad, and in a game like this, having bad locomotion controls will literally mean your death.There are other negative things as well. For instance, I kept taking damage when I had just stabbed a zombie in the scull, and with no other zombies nearby. I don't know if this is because zombies can still damage you for a short while after you've killed them or something, but if that was the case, it is really something that should be taught in the tutorial. Especially because in order to get your knife free from the zombie you've just stabbed in the scull, you have to "shake" the zombie to get it off your knife.Also, when you take damage/get bitten, there is no indication of where you are taking damage from. I would often stand in a place, looking around, wondering where the hell I am taking damage from (behind? below? No?)The ammo is also ridiculously limited, but what is even worse is that even if you've just literally picked up three packs of ammunition that clearly contains a lot of rounds, you still only have maybe just 10 bullets in total. I originally set out writing this review with the intention of giving it a positive rating. But now that I've had time to put my feelings into words, the more I feel like the developers just really dropped the ball on this game. And even though I paid next to nothing for this game, I really don't want to "recommend" it to anyone, especially when there are so many other great VR games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than people say it is. I think the majority of the negative reviews come from expectations set by Saints and Sinners, and a buggy launch. I really enjoy the game a lot when I'm looking for a great, hectic zombie slaughterfest. Essentially, if you really enjoy the combat from The Walking Dead: Saints and Sinners (and possibly don't like the durability system), or want a more polished take on something like Arizona Sunshine with some upgrades and progression, you will really enjoy this.I understand why some people don't like this game, but the "Mostly Negative" score it has at this time is absurd. It is far better than the majority of VR titles I've played. I think, again, that the brunt of the negative reviews are because it's not Saints and Sinners, and it had a buggy launch. S&S is more slow-paced (most of the time) and methodical. It is more survival gameplay-oriented and Onslaught is more action combat-oriented. Both games also have a time limit imposed by an encroaching horde, but in Onslaught's case it acts like a physical, moving wall of death. You still scavenge materials like in S&S, but must do so as fast as possible and under constant attack. Luckily, there is no inventory system to manage while doing so. There is also crafting, but in the form of upgrading your weapons (which are permanent and never break) and improving your survivor camp, which is basically a series of permanent upgrades to your stats.If you've played other Survios games (such as Raw Data), you should have better expectations of what this game will be like. The combat is fast and satisfying and more streamlined than other games like it. There is still detailed firearm interactions like reloading magazines, pulling slides, and working bolts. The motions are more "curated" and easier to do than in other games that simulate these things, which can reduce the immersion you feel, but helps to make it easier to keep up with the pace of the combat. The melee combat is also similar to Saints and Sinners, with bladed weapons able to kill in one strike, but requiring effort to dislodge from zombie skulls, and blunt weapons not getting stuck, but usually requiring more than one strike. Best of all, all these fun-to-use weapons never break, which saves you some of the tedium that S&S has.There's also a crafting system you engage in between scavenging missions. Various types of crafting components you collect will be used to upgrade your weapons and build or upgrade buildings for your survivor camp. Essentially, weapon upgrades will increase damage or make your weapons more effective in other ways. Building structures will give passive bonuses like increased health. I find all the weapons to be fun to use, but some are not so effective before upgrades. Another oddity is that your left hand is your dedicated "interaction hand" and you do all your looting and reloading with that hand. You also use a weapon wheel instead of virtual holsters, and can never drop your weapon to free your right hand. Again, overall more "arcade-y" than S&S.So now for the things I don't like: The storytelling, writing, and voice acting feel kind of phoned-in. I actually would have preferred that they used original characters rather than characters from the series/comics. The bland characters are made worse by being bad imitations of their show versions. The between-missions hub, the survivor camp, also feels pretty low-effort. It's tiny and uninteresting. You are apparently growing the population of the camp, but you only ever see three other people, and you can't even walk through the camp. That said, it does serve its main purpose just fine. Last, this game really feels like it was made for co-op play, but there is none. Still fun without friends, though.Overall, if you are looking for more high-action zombie slaying in the same vein as Arizona Sunshine, but with progression, melee, and fun weapon mechanics, this is a great pick. If you are looking for more Saints and Sinners, this is not a great pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Has anyone seen Carl?? The Walking Dead Onslaught, walkers in VR, Daryl's crossbow, Michonne's Katana, even 'Lucille', step into the roles of Rick Grimes, Michonne, Carol Peletier or Daryll Dixon and help expand Alexandria. The game offers a prologue level before you start a campaign divided over 7 chapters, in this campaign you will take on the role of Daryl Dixon who is in pursuit with a driver of a police car in the middle of the apocalypse. In addition to the campaign, you will also need to do supply hunting to find food, resources, medication, and other items in order to unlock the campaign's chapters, as well as expand Alexandria with new buildings and new residents. Before starting these supply hunts you will also have to choose between Rick Grimes, Michonne or Carol Peletier as character to do the supply hunt with. During these supply hunts you will have to make rapid progress because behind you is an unstoppable horde of walkers on its way and once you get into this horde of walkers you can still get out but you have to be quick. At the end of each supply you will also have to hold out until the gateaway arrives. Then when you get back to Alexandria you can also use the items to add upgrades to your collection of weapons, and also to build new buildings in Alexandria, these buildings will make the items you find have a higher number like for example more ammo in an ammo box, or that you can have more HP and others. Both the campaign and the supply hunting are without a doubt replayable. The game has the atmosphere of the TV series, it is fantastic as a walking dead fan to experience this in VR. One of the best VR games of 2020!

_childDocuments_.review: This title is amazing if you work out on a VR treadmill. An absolute must buy for and KatVR user. It's more of an arcade style game at times, but overall i was very satisfied with this title. Unlike the wildly more popular, Walking Dead: Saints & Sinner's series, this one doesn't focus on the open world survivor element. This is its own game with a dedicated story and the option to do supply runs in order to boost your killing ability. You can select different courses to charge through from your base map, then go out and scout the distance while collecting as many supplies as possible. No backpack, no complicated reloading, special perks that you can upgrade on any weapon you acquire in your armory, Quick Warning for Virtual Desktop users; This game has a strange bug that makes your wrists turn inward in way that makes it ridiculously uncomfortable to attempt to play. This only seems to happen when using Virtual Desktop when launching Steam VR first and then selecting Onslaught from your games list within Steam VR. If you launch it from Virtual Desktops side menu however, this bug seems to be non existent. Same with running this game through Oculus Rift, even if you are using Steam VR through Oculus Rift. Very randomly this bug will just fix itself. There is no current explanation for this bug.

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad... but not good either. Pros-Fast paced-Looks decent-Familiar characters (average voice acting)-Guns feel accurate and reactiveCons-Not scary (like at all; color palette is too bright and enemy placement is random and horde like, but you can see everything, and nothing sneaks up on you in an intimidating way; really disappointing)-Red wall that follows you forcing you to constantly move forward in a linear fashion (Like stride... but this is the Walking freaking Dead. This mechanic was a TERRIBLE choice and probably the worst part about the game; absolute trash decision for a game like this)-Average physics (slicing a zombie is like cutting through paper)-Walkers take 4-5 headshots to kill (just stick to blunt weapons, although they aren't very satisfying to use)Could be good or bad-Arcade-like (not open world, but level based; could be ok, but the wall chasing you looks terrible and is just an awful mechanic in general. It really ruins everything and throttled the level design as well; prepare to get trapped between a wall/fence and the red wall of death while gathering and the only way to get back to where you can make forward progress is to run through the death wall and most likely die; although the level design is pretty bad, the environments do look decent)-More focus on looting and getting through the level fast than actual combat (looting was fine, but I really felt no incentive to kill zombies... In a game that should be about killing zombies! When I did take the time to focus on killing zombies (because I wanted to try and actually have some fun), it left me either out of ammo or being consumed by the red wall of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ core gameplay.This game is really a mixed bag for me, there are things it does really well admittedly. I do like that it is more fast paced and I'm not crawling around like a slug in TWD: SAS, but that is really where the praise ends. I hate that the focus isn't on combat and/or horror and that the game isn't an open world exploration experience, but a liner push down a lane like Rayman or something. A wall of death chasing you is fine for a platformer or sidescroller, but definitely NOT a story driven zombie shooter like the Walking Dead in which I was expecting to have a deeply immersive experience with. I wanted to feel like I was fighting for survival in the world of the Walking Dead alongside Daryl, Rick, and crew, but although the characters were there, I just didn't feel the connection. I can't really speak on the story as a whole because I didn't play much and I am probably refunding, but the first few scenes definitely did not capture my attention. Verdict: A slight step up from Arizona Sunshine maybe, but a major downgrade from TWD: Saints and Sinners 100%. I'm giving it a recommendation to be fair. On its own it is a decent game (minus the wall of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanic) and new VR users will probably enjoy it, but compared side by side to Saints and Sinners and as a Walking Dead trademarked installation, it is just plain worse and not a good execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously 'Walking Dead Saints & Sinners' is the superior game in this case, with better graphics, lighting, physics and overall just the freedom the game gives you, this game is the absolute opposite with very linear levels and no choices that will impact the story, the voice actors of Rick and Michonne sound awful to say the least (generic impressions) I do love that they got Norman Reedus and Melissa McBride to actually voice their characters, but it just feels a bit cheap without the other two. The graphics are decent in my opinion, I just feel that the lighting makes everything look brown and cheap, gunplay, melee kills and such feel pretty satisfying and look VERY brutal, but the light-weight goat simulator-esque physics really throws it off, if you just added some weight and realism to the walkers physics, it'd really improve the gameplay experience. And as you can see I've played this game around 11.8 hours at the time of this review, I've found all the weapons (with the exception of 1), finished the story/scavenge missions and 100% built the town, this was all before the new update and I will get to that soon in this review.  Now this is going to be a very un-popular opinion but I genuinely enjoy this game for what it is, a simple, arcade-style, walking dead based game, and it's one of those games you can hand over to your friends if they are new to VR because it's simple, easy to learn and fun, sometimes I just want to run around shooting and killing zombies without a limiting stamina bar and tough survival gameplay. So if this is your kind of VR game, go ahead and get it, but I definitely don't think it's worth it for the price of $29.99, in it's current state I believe it should be $10 to $15 max.  Alright before I end this review I need to add a couple things, the gore in this game is pretty impressive, stabbing or shooting walkers will cause dynamic body and clothing damage, and sometimes creating holes and wounds that you can see-through, with intestines and other organs being revealed,  which is absolutely EPIC for psychopaths like me who love video game gore done right. And about 2 days ago they updated and patched the game because of many suggestions and the negative backlash, and through the discord server I sent a lengthy 'paragraph' or two- of suggestions, asking for them to remove the mechanic of after you grab a walker and kill them, they instantly start dropping causing your arm to glitch/stretch, and I said they should just allow you to hold the walker and cut this feature out completely, which THEY DID so I'm really happy they listened to me and many others who left suggestions, big props to you Survios for that. Anyway, this review is longer than I expected but I did have alot to say about it, negative and positive, if a member of the Survios developer team is reading this, I hope that you guys will add some sort of horde/survival mode for players who completed all the story and scavenge missions, and I feel like with the arcady-esque gameplay it'd fit perfectly with the game, so please consider adding this in the future. Thank you for reading, have a wonderful day everyone <3

_childDocuments_.review: The Red Line Ruined the Experience – Refund on the WayThe biggest disappointment in The Walking Dead Onslaught? The infamous red line. Instead of thrilling zombie encounters, you're stuck running ahead of this ridiculous red line that just moves through the map. Step behind it, and boom – you die. No real zombies to fight, just the sound of them taunting you as you rush to stay in front of an invisible death zone. It's baffling how they thought this would create any tension or fun.You can hear the zombies, but they’re nowhere to be found. The entire experience feels cheap and lazy, with zero immersion. For a Walking Dead game, where's the sense of survival or fear? I wanted to fight hordes of walkers, not play a poorly executed running game with a red line mechanic that destroys any potential fun.I’m already getting my refund on the way. Don’t waste your time on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this from fanatical for $1.67 and it's a must buy at that price, as I write this the sale is still on. I think I'm 5/7ths done, 6 hours in. Played on a VP2/ i7 6700/ 3060ti+. I had to turn down just a few graphics options to make framerate. The game is very realistic looking. Vive controls with smooth locomotion are well implemented, you can choose from hand or head oriented. One must swipe the touchpad to snap turn, I'd prefer a simple click, but it's a small point. Initial weapons are weak, because progression is about upgrading them. Unlocked new weapons bring new game mechanics into play (unlocked blunt melee weapons don't stick into skulls, unlocked guns penetrate multiple enemies (line them up!), or one-shot the head, or have recoverable ammo, etc).The gameplay alternates between unlocked story campaign levels, and scavenging levels. The story levels are all completely unique and have no time pressure. The scavenging levels introduce new types of areas as you advance - first backyards, then upstairs, then basements, and have a time pressure. I found the time pressure of scavenging levels not so much fun until I turned down the difficulty setting, which can be chosen at the start of any level. Scavenging levels can be replayed at any time, so you can go back to see the parts of the map you had to skip the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: my words of wisdom are:1. Get the knife2. Get the knife3. Get the knife(not relevant anymore, check the update at the end)You can kill almost everything by just stabbing everyone with the knife like Michael Myers.One in the head? Nah, more like 2, unless you are talking KNIFE! Your first 2 pistols kill zombie only with 2 shots in the head, you don't get much ammo most of the time, compared to the number of zombies and it's easier to kill zombies with starting knife cause it's 1 hit kill and the updated version gives you resources on kill, who made this game? Maniac from "Scream" movie?Also sliding trackpad on VIVE, like you turn the page on a fokken smartphone to turn in game instead of pressing or touching the sides is an ass, It's easy to accidentally to turn to the wrong side or turn too much.But seriously, it's inferior to Saints and sinners, that game had it's own stuff that some people didn't like, but if you want a walking dead VR game, just get Saints and sinners.UPDATE:GIVE ME MY KNIFE BACK!It's almost like they read this and similar reviews and thought "hmm, people found a way to have some fun in our game, let's ruin it". They decided to "rebalance" the knives and other weapons. Now they made the knifes completely unreliable. You used to be able to end a zombie with 1 quick stab with the knife to the head and it was a reliable way to kill a zombie with no damage to yourself. Now the knife gets stuck in a zombie and even broad swings won't save you from that, no matter how much you struggle, it may take some time to get the knife out AND IT STILL WON'T KILL THE ZOMBIE. Now, stabbing a zombie in the brain won't guarantee it's death. AND zombies are now dealing instant damage on contact, they used to only deal damage when they actually grab you, and if it's only 1, you could prevent it by grabbing the zombie or punching it to push it away, which I thought was fair, making single zombie easy to deal with but mind the groups and be cautious to not get surrounded. But now as soon as the zombie gets close enough to you, even if you grab him before they get a chance to grab you, boom, you took damage, which forces you to avoid any close combat at all, making a knife a last chance weapon. But hey guns now actually 1 shot zombies with headshots, so why not just use guns instead? Well, they reduced the ammount of ammo on start and in ammo pickups, so there is even less ammo to deal with big amounts of zombies on your way, so what's left? The CQC will lead you to a slow death and you don't have enough ammo for a long and middle ranged combat, especially if you encounter armored zombies, so you just fail and die.Earlier you used to be able to steamroll the game trough all its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ by using a knife, but now they have left you with nothing, it became barely playable.
