_childDocuments_.review: *Disclaimer* After recent update on the 19th of October, they have pushed out a lot of needed changes. To test it and rewrite my review, i will be replaying the main story shortly.I have fully completed the game. I wanted to complete the Daryl story line and get the achievements. *Spoilers Ahead*The Daryl story line was fun, i enjoyed that and if they focused on more story and not forcing you to do the annoying time supply runs, this review might of turned out a little different. I used melee weapons the whole game due to it being a one stab to the head originally, however after a major update, they changed the way the weapons work, making the firearms much more enjoyable to use. They did make the melee weapons significantly more awkward to use, but in the last case scenario when you have to use melee, it adds to the danger of the situation. Using the firearms is far more important now, and i'd have to say they are fun to use.I felt the story was incomplete, and i would of maybe given this game a positive review if it had a satisfying end. _childDocuments_.review: I played this game initially through oculus but got a refund, then read that a lot of the issues were virtual desktop specific. I ended up getting it cheaper through steam. As a result it shows only 30 minutes play time but it's probably closer to 2 hours.First things first. Most negative reviews, particularly those with specific gripes are almost all 100% correct. This game is a bit of a mess. However, I do believe that for the price there is value for money (though it might be worth waiting for a sale), and I hope that the developer starts getting fixes out ASAP.One complaint I have which I've not seen in other reviews is the sprint system. Every time the character touches the scenery, and sometimes seemingly for no reason the sprint stops. As far as I know there is no stamina bar and I can't see any reason for this but it makes the scavenger missions difficult. I'd recommend that Quest users play this Via usb cable instead of virtual desktop until the fix is out because I had an unfairly low opinion of the game before I'd tried both. With USB it's almost a different game.It's far from perfect but it is still fun. Running in to a room of 10 zombies and killing them all with a single light strike to the head with a machete is fun, even if it is easy.Also, please don't compare this to saints and sinners. If you have a choice between the two, get s&s. It is a better game, but Onslaught has its own place as an arcade slaughter fest which allows you to have the fun of killing masses of zombies with no concern for stamina, breaking weapons or a power sense of dread. It's just silly, messy fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead Onslaught

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the numerous negative reviews, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Yes, it's arcade and the challenge is very casual, but the game is zombie hack, slash, and shoot fun! I don't really agree with many of the negative reviews on here. This game is not the WORST VR game, not by a LONG shot. This game is more fun than Arizona Sunshine, and that game has great reviews. The story is bare here, but the gameplay is arcade-y fun. However, it is very overshadowed by the excellent zombie survival game, Saints & Sinners.Now, if they added coop to this game, I would imagine many people would change their reviews from negative to positive. Who knows, we might have a coop mission pack coming sometime in the future.Anyway, I would say if you are in the mood for a casual arcade zombie game experience, then you will definitely like this game. I did, I beat the game and still am enjoying the looting side-missions while trying to fully upgrade every bit of my arsenal. Don't let the negative reviews deceive you, it's a good game; easy, but fun none-the-less.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/14/21*I'm giving this a yes only to say i believe in the developers and to say keep an eye on this game in the future. wish-list it.Despite all the negative reviews, i wanted to give this a try and give an honest review. The concept of this game is a "Yes, i recommend this game" but the controls, combat and story implementations make it a "No, i don't recommend this game".Controls - locomotion is okay, but needs to be able to be tweaked.    -Changing the degrees you turn around in   -For smooth, making it less "motion blurry" and changing sensitivityCombat - Gun mechanics feel really good right now, melee weapons needs tweaking.   -pulling a knife out of a skull almost ripped my arm out of my socket.   -bigger melee weapons weigh nothing which isn't a bad thing to some people but a balance would be nice   -Guns, i don't know what the guns were like before but i really like them now the pull away to release the gun for your      second hand is amazing and firing is nice!Story - the story kind of feels like if you were playing a tower defense game. You see these characters from the show Rick, Daryl, Michonne, etc.  You play as them, but you don't have a real connection to them. And i get it, some people wanted this game to be even better than Saints and Sinners like making it a story, open-world game, but i don't think the game deserves a thumbs down for that reason.Overall, I'm sure i missed some things but i think you should wish list this game or wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, it is arcadey obviously but still good graphics (not the best but still good), although I dislike the red mist for the wave coming, missions are limited by the approaching horde (which sucks, come on survios) you are definitely rushed...You can't explore Alexandria, seriously devs..As from the name itself WD:Onslaught, while you can fight quite abit, I haven't found a true meaning of the name in this game, sure you kill many zombies before leaving, but you are rushed, it'd be great if it was like overkills walking dead, zombies just keep coming from the mist or wherever, although not all levels should have hordes of enemies, it should be stricted to areas like cities, towns etcHowever $30 for a neat zombie killer isn't bad, while I understand their's some negative comments, I don't believe they are fully justified, I haven't encountered no bugs, no issues, just concerns about the timed scavenging hunts.Some missions allow you to have a last man standing at the end of the mission which is fun, and you don't have to leave but it is advised if you want to progress with the progress of alexandria.Guns are okay, I dislike you can't keep every weapon you find, you can keep guns etc but I was using a hatchet, doing amazing with it when I finished the level I couldn't keep it.Please read the negative reviews if you still haven't decided if this game is for you, some people whine about guns or index controllers not having full function which is dumb just to give it a negative review for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Boring, repetetive and overall mediocre at best. Doesn't know what it wants to be. It is no survival game neither an action game or adventure. The comparsion of a mobile game is pretty fitting. Remember Dead Trigger 1 and 2 on mobile? They are better and even looks nicer. I guess one of the selling points of Onslaught instead of Saints & Sinners were to play and meet the cast of the tv show and the game beeing set in said universe. But character models are ugly, voice actors sounding bored as hell. This game gives you nothing to work with.Wanna feel bad ass killing walkers? To bad ammuntion and weaponhandling feel bad. Want an intense survival game? To bad as looting supplies is hollow and not satisfying. Want immersed in the world and story of Deryl and Rick? To bad story is a joke and completely forgettable.Sometimes it baffles me how developers sometimes think "Yeah...this will make gamers happy." I mean it is not the first game Survios released, there are plenty of other VR games which did specific game mechanics so much better where you could get inspiriation or build upon. On the other hand seeing the past games you just get the feeling they really don't care anymore about good game design and more a desperate attemp to get the next paycheck. Looking back at Raw Data or Sprint Vector you feel the passion behind VR game design from that Studio...but now... I just don't see it anymore.Bottom line... If you want a good Walking Dead VR game (even if it has not the cast of your beloved tv show in it) stick with Saints & Sinners.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing, This isn't like The Walking Dead: Saints and Sinners. The weapon feel and everything is different, I recommend Saints & Sinners more but when this (Onslaught) is on sale (40+%) I would say to buy.. or buy a code online.The original version of the game was trash by looking at past reviews but the current build is unique and playable, some features are annoying such as waiting time for a sharp weapon to leave a walker and that weapons that use two hands require some pulling to retract one of the hands. I like the feel of the weapons but more for a 'relaxing' afternoon, the starting pistol takes roughly 1-2 headshots to kill a walker, which seems reasonable, although I have had points where I am flooded with ammo while I'm taking a more careful approach with melee based action.So far, I've only had an hour to play and I enjoyed it, although the Scavenger runs are mixed, I have only done the first two and enjoyed the second one a lot more than the military holdout. The second run, on the street filled with stores is what I love about the idea of apocalyptic worlds, it's a good rush to gather supplies without the hoard catching up, although my immersion was ruined by a unique bug that froze my VR in place, although on my monitor, I was still moving around and being eaten alive.Just buy the game when on a big sale or buy a code for a lower price.. and buy Saints & Sinners first.

_childDocuments_.review: So.... where do I start..Listen, I hate giving negative reviews on VR games, mostly because I know it's a new market and even the devs are learning how it works, but for a company like Survios they should have it down.. yet they should miss some important features.1. Reloading is pretty much automatic. The game auto ejects your mag when it's empties and you have to hover your hand over a icon to spawn a new mag, which you can't drop or anything. Then once you put it in the game, it auto chambers itself. I thought we were past the whole auto reloading phase back in 2016 - 2018, but I guess not with Survios...2. For Index owners the grip is so off. The grip itself on the controller is pretty much useless and you only use the trigger to grip anything.I want this game to be good, but at the moment I can't recommend this game at it's current state. Once, they fix some things like reloading and the grip, then I will be more than happy to give it a go again.

_childDocuments_.review: Knife Simulator...Well I would not call it a mostly negative game, but it definitely did not catch my attention like Saints and Sinners did. The first Run & Supply Mission - the first real mission that you play in the game, or at least I did - was definitely a huge let-down. Then I played some of the Story-Missions which were decent. But the fact that I was only using the over-powered Knife felt weired, especially having a gun with me where headshots needed three bullets. The pick-up mechanics are bit bugged and off. Overall the scaling of the world does not match the size of the player.I like the idea with leveling up and building yourself a base and I also like the gunplay - which is not to be underestimated in a VR game obviously. So why am I giving the game a negative review? It is simply that I do not feel that the price for the game is right and that there was so little review information before release that I was even pre-ordering it and now I feel even more disappointed. Does this make the game a negative review game? Probably not, but does it justifies a positive review, rather not.Maybe I would give it a neutral review if I could, by adding, only if you have nothing else to play on VR and you enjoy melee combat over firearms combat. Furthermore I purchased Saints and Sinners after everyone was praising it so much in the reviews of Onslaught - kind of forgot it existed to be honest - and I am so much more amazed by Saints and Sinners than with Onslaught. The first mission of Saints and Sinners feels so comfortable, the atmosphere is spooky and calm at the same time and the supply runs are simply normal gameplay elements and do not feel like taken from a mobile phone game. But yeah we should not compare games only because they have the same Name Tag in them. And maybe this does not do justice to either of them. But on the other hand I was expecting a game similar to how I experienced Saints and Sinners. Less arcade, more adventure, at least the gameplay footage pre-release made me believe in this.Last but not least, I consider coming back to Onslaught in some months for a cheaper price tag and when the developers have improved some game mechanics (knife overpowered, zombies spawn, run and supply missions, red zombie crowd). But for now I will refund it and do not continue my gameplay with it. It is the right thing to do and I was hesitating actually a bit before taking this decision. Playing Saints and Sinners however reinforced me however in this intention.If you have the choice between Saints and Sinners, Onslaught is not recommended. If you have really nothing more to play on VR and you are looking for a very quick melee-combat zombie slasher in VR it might be worth a look. Everyone else waits out if Survios - developers I actually had a lot of trust in since Raw Data was my first love in VR before Onward, Pavlov etc came out - improve the game.In short, not a recommendation for this price and at this point in time. Maybe a bit later down the road. Keep it on your watchlist.

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason, every single Walking Dead game that is based on the show turns out bad. The only good ones are based on the comic series. Strange.Their producer was misleading in marketing this - he did a pre-launch interview saying "you can carve into the skin of the walkers", and you absolutely cannot do that. He made it sound very well polished, and it's sort of jank and very unbalanced. You stab someone and you can feel the auto aim on your melee weapons - that's weird. He talks about morals and ethics but in this game you feel nothing, whereas in Saints and Sinners you deal with these concepts much, much better, because the game sets things up well and gives you decisions to make.That interview is on "PSVR Without Parole" on YouTube. Video title "The Walking Dead: Onslaught | Developer Interview with Andrew Abedian from Survios", timestamp 18:03. I actually pre ordered after watching that - praise the Steam refund system! At least I now know to take Survios marketing less seriously.If you compare this game to the good ones based on the comics, like Telltale's TWD games, and Saints and Sinners, you can see that Onslaught just has no life to it. Daryl doesn't sound that into it, and Rick sounds so wrong. Eugene sounds good, as does Michonne. You build Alexandria but cannot explore it. You have to do filler "supply missions" between the story missions, which were the only decent part of the game - because I got it to play Daryl's story, but it all just feels so lifeless next to Saints and Sinners.Yeah, Saints and Sinners is a completely different game and they don't want to be compared to it, but that game had a solid story, it had decisions that felt meaningful, it was more immersive, and achieved all of this with cartoon-like visuals. This game probably wouldn't have been rated so poorly if not for Saints and Sinners, because obviously, that's what Survios had to live up to.This game is probably a 4/10. It's not completely awful - there are worse games out there with better ratings, but this got judged against the incredible work done by Skydance on Saints and Sinners. Survios made a game below their typical standard, and even worse, they had to compete with a masterpiece. If they got Andrew Lincoln to voice Rick, I may have kept it.It may be worth playing on a deep sale, if you are a big fan of Daryl.

_childDocuments_.review: My only issue with this is the price a bit to high for what it is "currently." but most Walking Dead titles are like this so i'm not surprised.but i did enjoy what i played, its more on the arcade side of things when it comes to combat. the knife play is actually a lot of fun in my opinion, you are not going to go guns blazing in most situations with "walkers" around so making the melee feel good is important, and i think its VERY well done here. i feel a lot of folk expect too highly of the zombie genre and being "one bullet to the head and dead" when it comes to these kind of games. think about of house of the dead when you go into this game.in fact for anyone new to VR i recommend this as one of the first games you should play if you can. its simpler style of controls is perfect for anyone's first go on a action based VR game.but i think this is pretty fun and i plan to spend some more time on it. if you are looking for super ultra realism, you are not going to find it here, but don't hate on it for not being this way

_childDocuments_.review: play through about 4 hours in here:   OK> Wow. This game is getting a ton of hate!  And I think much of it is very understandable.  This title is definitely NOT the quality that I would expect from SURVIOS.   But that being said is it still worth playing?  Well I have 4.9 hours in so far and I must say I really don't hate playing this game.  I think the first thing we have to do is come to terms with the fact that this is NOT Saints and Sinners.  Not anywhere remotely close.   This is more of an arcade type experience that feels more like an upgrade to Arizona Sunshine feature wise (although Arizona Sunshine is more polished that this title for sure).  Let's break this down with the good the bad and the ugly,. and yes there is a lot of ugly here.  Graphics:  Honestly, the graphics seem inconsistent through out the game.  Some things look great but are ruined really by other things.  Like From what we are used to now, seeing things like 2D flowers and 2D fire animations just seems like it should be illegal any more.   The character models look fine,. but they also kind of remind me of a model you'd build in some free 3D character creation app or something.  Deryl and Michone (sorry bout spelling here)  Look kind of like their actual characters, but certainly not to the amazing level of detail and facial animation capture that we saw in Survios's Westworld Awakening.  I don't see much of an excuse for that really since they never move from their spots on the Alexandria map area.  Can't really tell with Carol since she just spends the whole game looking at the flowers, which might explain why there are no children in Alexandria.. LOL.  The mouths of the models seem to be pretty bright inside when they talk.  and weird shadows just pop on their faces when you barely move.  The Walkers look pretty good except for the terrible 2D hair maps they have on them.  And then the animations of the walkers are pretty damn jankie.  Saints and Sinners walkers may have been stylized, but their animations were so realistic and smooth.  I noticed like areas where the exact same texture map was just copied and pasted along the ground and not even rotated or anything so you have these obvious patterns repeating and it just looks amateurish.   The outside areas look fine, but they are all the same really. even the insides of the building from area to area are pretty much the exact same layout.  It's like they didn't even bother moving shelves around or anything.  It even feels like the cars in the street are placed in the exact same area from map to map.  Also the walkers seem really tall.  And most of them are construction workers and cops and bikers,.. OMG the walkers are all from a Village People convention!!!  But seriously.. everything looks fine just not great.  It would have been impressive 4 years ago.  Sound:  Once again,. this is ok.  The guns aren't loud enough.  The walkers all sound pretty much the same.  The voice overs are ok but really not needed.  It kind of feels like, especially on the scavenger missions, that they are only there to try and tie the game to the TV series.  Mostly just "YOU CAN DO IT!"  (I really wish they would have gotten Rob Schneider to voice that in) or warning you that the "horde" is getting to close.  The guy that voices Rick does an ok job,. even though I read some guy said he sounded like Nick Cage doing a bad Rick impression and now that's all I hear.  haha!  Controls:  Your standard controls here.  My only problem is it's press to move and not touch to move on the vive wands, and the button to bring up the weapon wheel to chose your weapons is the grip button so I'm accidentally swapping out my melee weapon for a gun which really sucks in a tight situation. LOL  but no issues with the controls other than that.  They have all the different comfort levels that you'd expect from Survios.  Game play:  OK this is where I think this game works... kinda,..  Don't expect the fantastic physics that you got in Saints.   These walkers have extremely soft skulls and it takes next to nothing to put a knife through their heads.  They have the whole grab them and stab them thing, like in Saints you feel it's almost a must to grab the walkers to get the force needed to push the blade through, but in this title you don't at all so I kind of forget that I can do that.  Then that brings you to the guns.   I can look at these walkers ♥♥♥♥ eyed and show them a spoon and they will die,. but it takes 3 to 4 head shots to kill them.  At the point I'm at in the game in the above video, I have the burst pistol which will kill them with one blast but that takes 3 rounds a shot.  The SMG is pretty fun to use.  Really the guns feel like something you pull out now and then to just have fun shooting walkers but most of the time you're better off just using the knife or the machete.  You can upgrade all the weapons you find in Alexandria after each mission by using stuff you scavenged on you run and it happens pretty quickly and give the weapons more power, ammo capacity or the ability to scavenge different items off the walkers,. or  slow them down time wise ,. very arcade like.  There is no inventory to worry about which is nice in a game like this,. and my favorite thing, no stamina.  You can run everywhere all the time which is nice.   my biggest TWDSS complaint is that I always feel like I'm dragging dead walkers behind me when I go anywhere you move so slow.  You can also build Alexandria up with items you scavenge and each facility you build adds to things that happen on your runs.  lIke increases the crafting materials you bring back or increases the amount of food you bring back.  All these points add up to equal people that you save on your runs and they bring talents and gifts with them to help Alexandria grow.  You don't get to go explore your buildings though.  they just pop up behind Carol looking at the flowers.  There are 7 Deryl missions where you go through areas looking for a little lost girl.  These missions feel like an Arizona Sunshine run.  There's a story there.   Not really much of one,. like I said feels like it was just a way to try and tie the game to the show.  but they are enjoyable enough to play through.  You have to unlock each mission by adding people to Alexandria,. which gives you incentive to go scavenge and grind.  When you are on the scavenge missions this big red wall with a flat animated silhouette of a walker horde chases you through the level keeping you on your toes.  If you get stuck in the giant horde fart cloud,  or  GHFC, you start losing health.  It sounds silly but really I think it kind of works and get a bit of a thrill out of it trying to find all the best stuff and not get caught in the GHFC. Summation:  This is not a great game.  It's not really even a good game,. BUT I'm still having fun with it.  It just feels like they saw how great TWDSS was and were like,. crap... well,.. here you go.   It feels rushed, and unfinished and doesn't have that usual attention to detail and love you feel that was put into other Survios titles.   That being said it is entertaining to just jump in and play and you definitely don't have to worry about being scared or stressed out. One thing that would greatly improve this game is Multiplayer co-op.  It really feels like that is what this game should be.  The Walking Dead elements of this game really just feel kind of tacked on as an after thought. I don't feel bad spending 30 bucks on this game but if you don't want to I totally understand.    Wait for a sale.  Don't get stuck in the GHFC!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get this game.I don't even know where to begin...If you like exploring fairly open levels with a lot of interactive objects and items and avoiding being seen by hordes of zombies... then this game isn't for you.The levels are VERY linear, and if you see an alternate path and try to go down it, chances are you'll hit an invisible wall. The 'supply run' levels are VERY linear, and you don't even get to explore all of the buildings that are around, because if you spend too long looting a red fog closes in and just kills you off like in pubg or fortnite...YOU DON'T OPEN DOORS, YOU PUNCH THEM... yep.. even if it's a pull door or a toolbox you want to open. You punch it.You don't get to pick up items like in Saints and Sinners. If an item is collectable, you HAVE to use your left hand and force pull it towards you (playing as right hand dominant). This goes for weapons too; they will end up in your right hand, but you have to 'force-pull' them towards you with your left hand to equip them.You don't get to grip your weapons, or even reload manually. You just sort of move your non-dominant hand next to the gun or two-handed weapon and then it sticks to it. When you're shooting, you have to use all your bullets before it auto-ejects the mag for you.Just buy and play Saints and Sinners instead unless/until they update the hell out of this game.

They had thousands of positive reviews on every game and not a single negative review and have only played for a few minutes apart for one of them who had nearly 8 hours on a game that was released 30 minutes before he made his review, which seriously makes me think that these are paid good reviews to decieve people. Also the review made by Homelander is a troll. DO NOT buy this game. Its worth maybe 10 Euro at the most. The game is just terrible. A complete failure. Terrible audio for the voice actors, sounds like some of them were recorded over a phone on speaker. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I love Survios. They hold a special place in my heart as the first dev team to acknowledge the channel. I will always love them for that.That being said... Even I can recommend The Walking Dead Onslaught in its current state. A few of those key issues are:Object scale is very off which is exceptionally immersion breaking. Model of Daryl looked very out of place and deformed at the camp.Grip snapping is incredibly too strong. Why is there no toggle/slider for this? The disconnect between where my hand is and where it's snapped to is also incredibly immersion breaking.Reloading feels bad. Hand snapping exacerbates this issue. Reloading is clunky and too much is done for me. Don't take control away from me. It breaks immersion.Difficulty, even on the hardest mode, is laughably easy.The knife is overpowers next to the firearms. Fire arms are painfully weak. Gunplay was weak and weightless. Firearms did not feel good to use.Visually the game is kind of weak.No Index finger tracking. No grip to grab option.Scavanger missions have a random death wall that pushes you through the level. It contains no zombies for being a 'hoard' but rather just ticks down your health while you're in the red area. This red mist of death just feels lazy.Invisible walls all over the place.Now that all of those complaints out of the way.... That's not all of them, just the big ones.I did like the city building idea. I loved Dark Cloud and it reminded me of a simpler version of that. I did also have fun with the game when I could look past the above issues. Slaughtering walkers and experiencing the story was enjoyable. This just needs a lot more work before it can be recommended.If Steam had a neutral option I would opt for that here. If the game was in the $10-$15 I might even excuse some of these issues and give them a pass. At the current price with all these issues I have to lean towards a negative reviews as much as I hate to do that.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean wow. This is just bad. The Walking Dead: Onslaught gives VR a terrible name, as this game will serve as an introduction to VR for many that got a headset for Half Life: Alyx and/or the Oculus Quest 2. There are so many better experiences you can play at the moment (HHH, Half Life, S&S, Boneworks, etc.) for about the same price. I feel horrible for the VR community, as I have been an advocate since the beginning and this may be the worst game i have ever played. Pros:- Melee combat can seem satisfying at moments. Breaking down doors is fun- Graphics are not TERRIBLE (more in Cons)Cons:- Story and voice acting are atrocious (VA never gets to me usually but this is bad)- Gunplay is terrible (hand gets stuck to gun when holding with 2 hands and the guns are just not satisfying) Also reloading is horrible.- Graphics are an insane downgrade when compared to the trailer- No physics at all except for hitting zombies- Game is most definitely not worth the price tag.- Game has an open world feel without the open world (invisible walls)The game would have been a decent seller for the VR community about 3 years ago, but with people actually moving up to the next step when developing games for VR, this just doesn't cut it. Saints and Sinners is one of my favorite games for VR right now (another Walking Dead game) so go give them support instead of this mistake of a game. To anyone who just got a headset or just put it on again after a while to try this game, don't lose hope, the future looks pretty bright.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like the game, but even after only an hour I can say: the controls are the worst I have seen in any VR game:- you collect things by pointing your left hand at them, no grabbing of any sorts- basically no gun manipulation: you automatically drop empty mags and a fresh one spawns in your hand after you put it to your left side and you reload by bringing your left hand near the gun... no manual relase, no gripping of the new mag, no real inserting of the mag, no racking of the slide- gun sights are bigger than a head, and the damage drops a lot after the first few meters. headshots kill in one shot in the 2m range, but you need two shots after like 3-4m...- melee is frustrating: knives sick in walker-skulls but you can only jerk it out after about 2 seconds, regarldes of the motions you are doing. resulting in walkers falling down with your knife in them, but you still have your hand high IRL- you switch weapons by button presses and even the way you hold a knife. - no option to use both hands for weapons, like right for a gun and left for a knife- game supports snap turns, but not when you are held by a walker- NO manipulative items, you cannot grab anything in the game, not even drop the things you equip. Equippable things just port in your right hand after you point and click at with your left one... WTF??So half of the time you lose any connection between your VR- and IRL hands, this robs this game of any immersion it could have.Besides the horrible controls I like the concept of dealing with hordes of slow walkers, but it is not enough to save this game

_childDocuments_.review: after a lot of anticipation I can't recommend this, for several reasonsExplorationYou can't open most doors and the ones that can be opened  you have to smash open with a weapon, not all buildings are accessible and some of the areas look very repetitiveThe scavenging missions are extremely short and the maps are tiny, there isn't really anything to explore granted i only played the first two scavenging missions and two of the story missions, the horde on the map isn't really a horde at all it's basically a red line that sweeps the map making the already very small areas smaller, if you go inside the red line you take health damage, I feel that this takes away from any feeling of immediate threat and turns the game into a repetitive hack and slash loot-fest.Alexandria feels empty and very tiny you can see but you can't touch, not what i expected at all.LootingLooting feels very uninvolved you basically grab every lootable in sight, there's no inventory management or choices to make just loot and shoot, also your non dominant hand is used to grab all loot including weapons, which feels a bit restrictive for a VR gameCombatThe combat isn't fun, after playing saints and sinners i feel as though the combat in this game is really clunky and arcadey grabbing zombies by the neck feels awkward and pushing them away feels very disconnected overall the combat is much faster paced which may be fun for some but feels very shallow and lacks challenge, i can see how some may enjoy it but it's not for me personally.There is also no weapon holstering, the game uses a weapon wheel similar to half life alyx which is fine but seems very lazy for VR a platform that is supposed to immerse you in the game world.VR/locomotion settingsThe locomotion options were great though with a decent variety for everyone, I did however find that smooth turning was awkward with vive wands since I had to swipe the track pad rather than touch the pad left or right, i ended up just turning IRL to face the zombies.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing two levels, I had just about had it. I don't doubt there are some cool weapons that you can get later, but I just cannot get past how under developed the game play is. As a VR title, you take a risk making the controls as immersive as possible. However, this game makes almost no effort in this regard, for the following: weapons are permanently gripped to your hands there are no body holsters (seriously, weapon wheel?) your stabilizing hand is glued to the gun unless you yank it off aggressively  button press weapon orientation toggle baby reload (automatic reload slowly, and with big white arrows and guidelines) EVERYTHING in this game is COMICALLY out of proportion (immersion breaking and sad) guided item pickup (you can also only pick up items you need)The list goes on, but nothing like the zombie game I was expecting. You cannot throw an object to distract a zombie, throw your knife etc it is truly a 3D arcade zombie killing game akin to Resident Evil for the Wii.The game play is not only the opposite of immersive, it's simply not fun. A lot of people have on point critique about the "fog" mechanic that encroaches on the level, which makes you move quickly  and hurries you through a run. However, the movement is ***. The movement is so bad, that I found myself frustrated to the point of just wanting to be done  with the level. The sprinting is simply broken. I will reiterate what other people are saying about the fog, it is pretty lame, and not at all fun.The character design is shockingly low resolution and uninteresting. The game play is slow and uninspired, the graphics are not even close to other VR titles on the market. It feels like a chore to play. Avoid this title if you are looking for an immersive VR title, and stick with saints and sinners, that game is infinitely better.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 20 minutes of gameplay - I've played about an hour and a half so far & having just completed Half Life Alyx & having previously played The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners I have to say this is a far more arcade style VR experience. No physics based objects, non player controlled animations for reloading instead of actually reloading yourself, pointing at items to pick them up rather than actually picking them up... It's definitely not the survival horror experience of Saints & Sinners but if you look past the rough edges & take it at face value there's fun to be had here. The closest thing I can comfortably compare Onslaught to is Arizona Sunshine, we'll see if that opinion changes with time but for now that is exactly what it's reminding me of.It's worth knowing what you're getting into before purchasing: A run & gun, simplistic action game that is no where near as immersive, good looking & VR optimised as games like Half Life Alyx, Saints & Sinners or Boneworks!

_childDocuments_.review: Played a few hours so far, definitely fun but a little too easy and the writing & level design seems a little poor. We'll see if it improves, but it's hard to not enjoy hacking and slashing zombies.Update:Changing this from originally recommended to a no. I really wanted to like this game, and as a big walking dead fan, I had high hopes for a VR version of one of my favorite apocalyptic franchises.Finished this game today, though I have a handful of achievements left, the production, writing, and gameplay seemed very weak. Clunky controls, tons of glitches with walls and zombies, super, super linear in terms of gameplay. The storyline is also quite short, with no replay value whatsoever. I played it on the "veteran" difficulty which was still way too easy.The weapons were ridiculously weak and the "upgrades" were hardly noticeable. Michonne's sword? Takes multiple hits to kill a basic zombies, the best weapon ended up being one of the knives, at least you could one shot and keep moving. Ended up avoiding the ranged weapons throughout the better half of the game just because the knife ended up being the only decent option.I'm a bit baffled honestly, it's as if they got Norman Reedus voice acting and then rushed the entire game. So many re-used textures and rooms, aside from the graphics and some of the voice acting (okay, not great - Rick's was awful) it feels like total amateur hour. I am disappoint.One sad fact I must admit is that I didn't realize you could run (holding the left joystick down) until the very last mission (lol). Would have made the game even easier!Sorry Survios, not your best work.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a way better game than the reviews might have you believe. I think the problem is that everyone wants to compare this to Saints & Sinners, which is a bit more of a polished game. If this hadn't come out soon after and didn't have the Walking Dead name on it, I think people would be able to give it a much more fair and honest review. That being said, I'm also going to make a few comparisons to S&S, and also show you why this game is worth checking out.It may not have all the crafting and upgrading of S&S, but there are still plenty of things to craft/modify. It also does seem to be shorter than S&S, although I haven't finished yet after 3 hours and still seem to have quite a bit of gameplay ahead.There are a couple of things I actually like more about Onslaught than S&S. It just looks better. The characters, the environments, everything. I also like the urgency of an approaching horde on scavenging trips, which forces you to prioritize your search area and get to the extraction as soon as possible with as much stuff as you can find before the horde is on top of you. In S&S you can't enter most houses, and there are just random walkers in the mostly identical streets, leaving you not much to do or much urgency to get it done quickly.I may not be able to recommend this at the full price, but I'm also a cheap b*stard, so maybe it's worth it. I got it in a bundle and in 3 hours I've already got way more than my money's worth from this game. Because of the reviews, you can probably get keys for 10 bucks on other sites at any time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game within an hour and a half has made me realize quite a few things that could be changed for the better and not only heighten the experience but make the game more unique to other players in general. First off I would like to explain the way this game was set to be played. You are in an arcade, this game is meant to be played in an arcade. The story is made to be played in an arcade! You cant put weapons away and there are no immersive moments unlike saints and sinners where you can change the moments in the game. Health is like an arcade as well, there is no backpack to carry things, it takes more than 3-4 bullets to kill a walker in a universe where head shots are 1 shot kill once again ruining the experience. There is also a stupid walker gas fortnite circle that closes in on you in the scavenger mission which should be completly removed or should be asked by the player at the start of the game. If you want an arcade like experience play this game, if you want a immersive and fun walking dead experience play saints and sinners, I would also like to add there is no tension in this game, if they just added an insane amount of walkers to come an attack you when you were in the walker fortnite circle then the game would be more tense as well. The guns are fun but are way to arcade like as well, when you upgrade the guns they should look more realistic. knifes and blunt weapons just get weird passive abilitys along with absolute no visual upgrades which i was sad about. They need to add a hardened mode of some sort but even then I dont think it will be enough to change the game. The alexandria you are trying to rebuild has no exploration so you really cant see what you are rebuilding. They need to add more changes to this game, Im still very disappointed in the arcade style they went for especially in vr where there are plenty of games out that are like it and better then it. I hate how you cant grab items with both hands that even saints and sinners does. They really didnt know what game people wanted from the walking dead universe because if I could develop a game on this it would be more like saints and sinners. Hopefully they will patch and improve this game over time but I would wait for a sale. im giving this game a 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I will get it out of the way, so unless you really like the show, get Saints and Sinners is a better Walking Dead game. The guns used to not one shot to the head and melee was overpowered, but they have made changes to fix it. It's still not perfect, but it's a lot better than what it was before. I do like the scavenger missions, but I do wish the "horde" were real walkers and not the storm from Fortnite. The story was just meh, you play as Daryl and have to help a stranger find a girl, it was kind of boring. Voice acting was good for some characters and bad for others. Wasn't a big fan of Rick's voice actor, but Daryl was good, obviously because he was voiced by Norman Reedus. I know I only touched on a few things, but overall the game is mediocre. _childDocuments_.review: The game had promise from early information, could have been a vr left 4 dead, if early info was to be believed. Was looking forward to possibly hacking and slashing my friends and zombies, but the entire thing only has 3 saving graces, Norman Reedus, a faithful recreation of the walking dead environments, and it takes up less gigs than Saints & Sinners.I played through the tutorial, and the first scavenger mission and my level of disappointment has never been so thorough.- The VR interactions are on par with a mouse and keyboard first person shooter- I can randomly flail my arms to remove any real walker threat- Weapons may have amo but the knife is all you really need, or you could just punch randomly ruining the immersion- You are limited to using your primary hand for your weapons- The graphics are okay, not super realistic. I personally prefer more stylized looks- There is a settlement building mechanic but the rest of the game doesn't make me want to put in the time- The not meant to be funny cardboard cut out hoard that follows you through a linear level where you can easily get stuck and dieit would be a okay game in a vacuum but there are better zombie games out there, and as many people will compare it to of course Saints & Sinners.I have no plans to return to this game unless there are some major updates.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my THIRD time writing a review and honestly I don't need to go as in depth as I did.If you LOVE AMC's TWD then you'll like this gameIf you are coming from Saints and Sinners... you won't like this gameOnslaught is what I first expected out of S&S. I expected a fast paced, tons of zombies game where you had to pick up anything you could find. That's what Onslaught is.Saints and Sinners is a slower paced Walking Dead game in which there is more meat on the bone for story.Onslaught is a good game when you look at it sideways as it caters to the viewers of the show questioning the characters actions. Why does everyone have infinite ammo? Its laying all around. How can Rick keep fighting walkers without getting tired? We don't see that on screen so why would we see it in a game? How can they get through large hordes of walkers without getting a scratch on themselves? 1 hit melee headshots. I think the creators of this game planned for it to be a flop as they probably didn't want to pay a TON of money for Rick or Michonne to come back as their real life actors. They did get Daryl, Carol, and Eugene which is nice... But it's just enough to  draw people in to buy the game and experience it. If the game flopped, they wouldn't have lost as much money as they would casting Rick or Michonne.Overall... I rate this game a 7/10 for the sole reason that you are stuck in the SHOW WORLD and not a comic book world. If you wanna feel like you are fighting to save the cast of AMC's show, this game is for you. If you are looking for a more in depth, longer story line with character development... get Saints and Sinners.Buy this game if its on sale, DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE

_childDocuments_.review: You thought the legendary BFG was the most powerful weapon in gaming? Think again.......the knife in this game slays!Look the game's $29.99, it's a low budget zombie slashing arcade style game that Survios is known for. This isn't Saints and Sinners nor is it trying to be. There's some nice fan service in the form of recognizable characters from the show and the hub base Alexandria, which is your central hub that connects you to both the story mode and the scavenge mode. The whole overall point to the game is to get resources from your scavenger missions to build new structures in Alexandria which in turn levels up your character. There's also weapon modifications/upgrades for every weapon. My biggest gripes with the game however are. The guns in the game are far weaker than the melee weapons. They lack so much power that it takes 3 shots to the head of a zombie to kill them which is absolutely ridiculous! The starting knife which is literally the first weapon you get in the game is also the best weapon in the game. Even if you're surrounded by zombies the quick downwards stab of the knife to zombie heads is so overpowered you will feel unstoppable. Another thing of note is the game doesn't take advantage of the Valve Index's finger tracking which is disappointing. Overall I wish Steam had a neutral rating to give this a sideways thumb but being this game is getting unfairly ripped apart on Steam by a lot of users who only played the game for 40 mins I felt I should show it some support and give it a thumbs up as I've been enjoying my time with the game despite it's flaws. Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Index controls are terrible. You need to click on the trigger to pick stuff up (not just pull a bit, literally pull all the way until you hear a click). Editing them is a bit hard because actions don't have namesZombies don't die from one headshot,Voice acting is pretty bad (except Daryl, which is actually voiced by his real actor)You can't interact with any objects outside of what the game wants you to interact with (e.g. you can't throw cans around, or open car doors).You can only pick up stuff using your off hand, trying to use your main hand won't do anything even if you are not holding any weapon. And when you pick something up, it instantly absorbs the item into your body (there is no backpack or holster or anything you need to place them into). Weapon switching is done using a wheel in your UI (a bit like in GTA).Loot runs are timed.You can't explore Alexandria, and the world is pretty closed so you can't explore much (maybe it changes in later levels, but don't count on it).Reloading feels weird. You don't need to ♥♥♥♥ your weapons (load bullet into chamber) when reloading with 0 ammo left, and the mag just appears in your handThe graphics are okay and I didn't run into any technical issues or performance issues in my short gameplay time, but overall the dev team needs to re-do a lot of mechanics in the game.If all you care about is killing zombies and the controls don't bother you and you don't care about acting, then go ahead and buy the game. But this is not as good as it was advertised.

_childDocuments_.review: My honest review of this game after 1.2 hours..  The good:-Graphics are on point. -Character modeling is fantastic.-Game sounds are great.-Knives work well. -Materials are easy to pick up.The Bad:-Gun mechanics are 1st gen vr game basic. _childDocuments_.review: Played this game for about 2 hours now. I personally don't really understand all the hate and quite enjoy the game. I feel like I got exactly what I expected from Survios. Most of their games are Arcadey and this one isn't different. I'm pretty sure they made it clear before release that this game was going to be more on the Arcade side as well. Which in my opinion they did pretty well. Yes, there are a few flaws in the gameplay and most of them have already been addressed in other reviews, but I don't think these flaws justify a 80% negativity rate on steam. I've seen a lot more VR games that are way worse and I think this game is done quite well based on the genre it represents. It somehow feels like a lot of people expected this game to be TWD Saints and Sinners 2. Which I don't think it's fair. They are two completely different games that happen to be in the same franchise. I expected an arcade game and I got an arcade game that I quite enjoy. I think people can enjoy both games depending on what mood they're in and what type of game they want to play. I certainly recommend TWD S&S and TWD Onslaught both depending on which mood you're in and what type of game you want to play. - Fun gameplay and killing mechanics. - It's nice you can stab the zombies in their entire body (even their jaw) but to actually put it down, you need to stab/shoot the brain. - No stamina so I can go on until I get tired ;)- Pretty gory which looks quite good actually. I personally think that the zombies in this game might look better than the ones in Saints and Sinners although I think they're both quite good for the art style the devs tried to represent. - Upgrading Alexandria is nice idea although would be great if I had the ability to explore the town more. - It does feel like I'm in an episode of TWD when I play this game which is great as I am a fan of the show. - Wish I could explore more of Alexandria instead of being stuck behind the fence but this is kind of expected from an arcade style game, they are usually not as open world as other games. However would be nice to explore the town + see the people you rescue. - Some melee weapons are a bit overpowered which makes the game not to difficult even on veteran. I think they might need to make the zombies a bit stronger to even that out.- I think the graphics are good but the textures here and there (especially the trees in Alexandria) could be better. - Maybe make it a bit harder by adding zombies that are stronger and faster (I'm only 2 hrs in so this might come later).Overall I quite enjoy the game and don't think all the hate is justified. I feel like a lot of people believed this was going to be TWD S&S2 but that isn't a fair comparison to make as they are two completely different type of games. I think based on what the devs were going for (which is the arcade style game), this game is quite well done. Gameplay is fun, stabbing the zombies all over their bodies to slow them down works well and the gore is great. Maybe lift the restrictions to explore to explore Alexandria more instead of the limited area you put us in. The game can also be quite easy even on Veteran so maybe add in stronger/faster zombies to make it more challenging (haven't made it past chapter 3 so it might get harder and will adjust my review if I believe it should be different). I'm sure the developers at Survios worked hard on this game and it must be tough to see people tear down this game because they had different expectations. I personally think you guys did a good job and I would like to thank you for your hard work during the creation of this game. Best wishes!

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10 ONLY BUY THIS ON SALE! (I paid 6.79CAD... I wouldn't pay any more than that.)Lot of negatives.Headshots don't insta-kill zombies.. yes, you read that correctly. Despite years and years of examples from George Romero, or the LITERAL SHOW The Walking Dead as an example.. they decided that shooting a zombie in the head doesn't instant kill. Unless the barrel is in the zombies mouth.. good luck dude. The movement is infuriating to say the least. Holy s#it. You're surrounded by zombies being yelled at over the radio to hurry up and my character REFUSES to go any faster besides a brisk walk.. even calling it that is a stretch. I must've looked so stupid in my room because I was repeatedly flailing my arms yelling "RUN FFS"(If they have a toggle they didn't explain it whatsoever.)  The voice acting... wow. I seriously can't explain just how bad it sounds. This game is partnered with AMC yet they couldn't get Andrew Lincoln to play Rick, and it sounds like they just use audio snipets from the show for the rest of the characters besides Michonne. Now with that being said, you'd think they'd use audio snipets for Rick.. NOPE! it's so confusing. It's honestly so terrible that it turns into a comedy a little bit.. it sounds like watching a Youtube video of someone trying to do their impression of Rick Grimes.The only real positives I experienced. - Weapon skins are really good looking and I like the feeling of simulated weight on them. - The mechanics of reloading is a lot more arcade-like and user friendly than other VR shooters. It took a moment for me to get used to not having to do everything. - Zombie ragdolls are really fun to mess with. Stabbing, shooting and pushing around. It made me chuckle.- They made a 3d VR model of Daryl. I really like Daryl and I ended up spending way too long sitting at the campfire with him.Do not and I repeat, DO NOT buy this at full price. This game is not worth what they're asking and I seriously hope they drop it down to $15 or lower, because this game is seriously disappointing. Fix it or drop the price.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me say I think this game gets a bad wrap because of what people think it is. It is NOT Saints and Sinners. There are several games, vr and non, that I have seen get bad scores from people because its not like such and such game. So going into it with an open mind, this is one you could have fun with. So what I liked: the action based combat and interactions. Its fun to hit a zombie with a hammer and quickly switch to the knife and stab it. Grab a zombie and stab it or beat it senseless. You can shove and punch them, even beat them with you rifle when you run out of ammo. I Like the graphics and feel the facial features are well done. You have 2 types of levels in the game, story and scavenge. In the story mode you can take your time but you cant select your characters. The scavenge level you can chose one of 3characters, the only difference seems to be just the skins, and the level is timed due to the "horde". I always chose Rick, and the "horde" doesn't seem to move to fast that you need to panic the whole level. Based on what you collect each weapon can be up graded with mods. What I don't like: people straight up saying this is one of the worst games they have played because it not what they expected(S&S). The detection for grabbing a zombie seems off, its harder to grab one outside of the tutorial. It seems I always get bit before I can grab them. The timer on the weapons when they get "stuck" in the zombie. Head-shots don't seem as powerful as you would think. Automatically switching weapons when you grab a new one. This happened to me when I was in the middle of reloading my gun, I was left with ammo and a knife, and my gun was no longer in my inventory. Only having the weapons in your dominate hand. To sum up: If you like fun vr shooters with light rpg elements, then you might like this one, especially if you can get it on sale like I did for less that 11$

_childDocuments_.review: It's a hard one, because I can see how this could be fun, but it's just such a drab world. My main complaints are how small the world feels, and this includes but is not limited to the fact that you can barely explore anywhere, and this is especially disappointing in the case of Alexandria, which feels completely devoid of any life. The looting areas are disappointing, and while I personally don't have a problem with the "click and pick" looting system that some find too arcadey, I could see why some would find this offputting. The voice acting is not as terrible for me as others have found it, but it is still fairly dull listening to the characters talk and does not draw me into the story whatsoever.The moving "Fortnite wall" is the most immersion breaking part, and could have been done so much better, perhaps with smaller hordes like in saints and sinners (though I hate comparing it to S&S as is shouldn't be a simple clone) and the combat is clunky, with walkers jumping around when you stab them, animations don't play properly, especially with weapons where you automatically grip with two hands, you can't switch dominant hand on the fly, and the guns...don't get me started on the guns. They feel almost pointless, as they are so weak as to be unusable (the pistol for example takes 3 headshots to kill) and a personal nitpick of mine - walkers do not have to be killed with headshots, knifing one repeatedly in the stomach killed it for me, though this may be a bug. The combat is far too easy, which could easily be fixed in the future, but as of the time of this review, I felt I had already experienced the best of what the game had to offer - I had no trouble killing a large group of around 15 walkers simply with the starter knife, so I see no reason why I should search for weapons in the future.Put simply, there is no driving force for me to continue playing - if you want a mindless hack and slash, then you may enjoy this, but if you are looking for a fun, realistic physics based VR game, check out saints and sinners, or Arizona Sunshine.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game for 2,5 hours, did some scavenger missions, played the first 3 story chapters and built some houses.CONTROLSA variety of vr games thougt us some kind of general intuitive vr controls (like grab something with grip, grab with both hands etc.). this game ♥♥♥♥♥ that up completely. your right hand is your weapon hand (like in Alyx), you can't grab anything with that hand and have to grab everything with your left hand (EVEN WEAPONS THAT GO INTO YOUR RIGHT HAND). also (with vive controls) you have to swipe over your touchpad to turn around instead of just clicking the direction. also walking and sprinting needs a click / doubleclick insteag of using the touch feature. then there is no inventory /backpack and the reloading is done by clicking a button and draging a magazine from your hip to your gun. you don't even have to touch the slide etc. it feels like a VR start up game of the early days.GAMEPLAYThere are only 7 very linear and short story missions. between them you have to collect a number of resources to unlock the other story parts via scavenging missions. These are also very linear run, loot & shoot missions with a battle royale curtain mechanic which is very cheap. the guns are very unsatisfying and pretty much useless (u need 3 headshots to kill a zombie but just one thrust with your starter knife). so basically you will do the same thing all the time, stab or chocke&stab zombies in the head and to that all over again, guns are obsolete. Overall it just isn't fun at all and also playing on the hardest difficulty is still too easy and zombies are no threat.WALKING DEAD FLAIR AND FEELINGThere are 5 characters of the series in-game: Carol, Rick, Michonne, Daryl. Eugene drives the truck but you never see him. Your base is a veeeeery little area inside of alexandria with invisible borders, so you can't even walk through alexandria at all. The story itself is very weak too. Hard that I had to refund despite being a walking dead fan :(

_childDocuments_.review: Not as bad as people say.I'm seasoned in VR and I've played, I think, all of the top sellers. But what the hell, steam community? Why all the hate? Is it because this is a AAA production, so you held it to higher standards?I'll admit, it does have a few drawbacks, like, how piercing a skull requires you to wait a couple seconds, before you can remove your knife. And there is also no way to change smooth rotation speed. Weapon reloading is a bit lame but it's better than push button reloading.But under these flaws, you have a game with a lengthy story, good direction, a progression system, crafting/modding/upgrading, great optimization and professional voice acting. The IK body is just awesome and your shadow is pretty cool to look at, as well. The tutorial is also very straight forward and to the point. It's done before you feel too anxious.I've been spoiled by all the other VR games. Surv1v3 and saints & sinners, to name a couple, but this game gets my full attention. There's a tonne of content and so much to keep you busy. It looks beautiful and I can see me playing this through til the end. And hopefully again. For something with so many negative reviews, I sure am entertained.Buy it on sale! Full price is a little absurd.Dead GroundZ... A game that is half as good and twice as buggy (likely more) gets "mixed" reviews...Let that sink in.Update: My controller is garbage, so in case you're wondering, this is why I haven't played in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game as a walking dead fan, however after playing through the tutorial and doing the first campaign chapter I was left wondering 'is that it?'. The game basically consists of two modes, scavenge and campaign. Both of these modes can be selected from the main hub area, which is pretty small and only has limited options within, which you don't even need to move around in as you can select all areas from the in game menu. Once you eventually load into the main hub area (yes there are loading screens and a lot of them, and they take a while) you can talk to Daryl to do story missions, these are more 'relaxed' in that they don't seem to have a time limit, but they follow a narrative between Daryl and Rick.To access scavenge mode you go to the map which is next to Michonne and select an area to transport to, you can change the difficulty of the mission to easy, normal or hard with the harder the mode the more loot but harder to kill etc once you select the area you go sort your loadout then go to the van. However this is were the game is very much a let down. The scavenge mode is a time based event, you are constantly being chased by a 'hoard' of zombies... however this is basically a red wall with 2d zombie blobs chasing after you, it is also incredibly loud and obnoxious. I understand the need to make the player be mindful of time management, however giving them a big red wall to stay ahead of isn't the way to go. When I tried out the scavenge mode, I just found it more of a chore than actually fun, I didn't have enough time to explore and actually look around the maps, or really take in anything of my surroundings as I just had to keep sprinting away from the loud red wall chasing behind, bare in mind I was only ever on normal difficulty, I don't even want to imagine how hard mode was. Oh also remember this is meant to be a VR game, nowadays most VR games utilise player space and room scale so you can interact with your environment, such as bending down to pick up items or crouching and hiding behind objects etc. This game however don't worry, you just bump into objects and they open, and if you have your controller anywhere near the object you want to pick up just pull trigger, and voila instantly grabbed the item! great right?! But yeah it feels very arcadey and not up to date with how most VR games are currently. You should be able to actually interact properly with objects you are picking up and not have them instantly teleport into your hands..... especially for a game that is £24.....Overall the game just feels like an arcade game you would play at the cinema or a mobile game you play when on the go, since the gameplay mechanics themselves are very simple, you go out get rescources bring them back and click a button to 'build' something for Alexndria, which you never go to or see beyond the hub. The combat itself also feels very janky, guns are very underpowered compared to melee, taking up to 3 headshots to kill a zombie, but a tiny knife can take out anything with one quick stab. There also isn't any 'weight' behind combat, you don't really feel any resistance when fighting. I can not recommend this game at its current price, it is just not worth £24 at all!TLDR: not worth the price, too arcadey, very basic graphics akin to mobile games!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATEThey have fixed almost all my issues i had with this game as of October 19! I would now recommend this game and thumbing it up but I still want to keep this review up.Me and my buddies where talking about Onslaught and I just wanted to get things off my chest after completing it and maxing most the guns and weapons.( I only play on veteran difficulty so it might just be my experience, I have not touched the other difficulties)Expectations:TWD Onslaught is not Saints ans Sinners. I was never expecting it to be. I think many people who are buying into this game got spoiled with how good and immersive all the new vr games are and how much detail has been put into them(Boneworks, Saints and sinner, half life alyx). However, I think it is a good and healthy for arcade like games much like Onslaught to release in vr to freshen up the experience. Sometimes you just want to turn on your headset to destroy things much like Arizona Sunshine and Robo Recall which I go back to frequently.Ranged weapons:That being said TWD onslaught is not a great game due to the amount of bugs and balance issues in this game. It does not deserve all the negative reviews since half of them are just thumbing it down for not being saints and sinners and the other half didnt even get to the half way point when you start getting good guns. In the Beginning of the game the guns are very weak but they get a lot stronger through out the game. This was intentional I am pretty sure as it gives players a reason to keep playing and upgrading their guns so they can eventually one to two shot walkers to the head. If all the guns in this game one shot to the head people would only be using the base pistol as the other weapons are just clunky compared to it. For people hating on weapons if they played enough they would unlock the revolver which is basically fixes all their complaints as it one taps to the dome and explodes their heads. There is only one flaw with the guns in this game and that is ONLY SOME OF THEM HAVE AP ROUNDS. This makes the guns useless against armored walkers since now you cant even kill them with your guns so what does that make you do? Switch to a melee weapon.Melee:The melee in this game feels clunky and idk if its just me and if its by design. I don't feel any weight when swinging these heavy weapons which makes it unsatisfying to kill a walker in this game with melee. Not only that but you cant grab armored zombies. I understand not grabing spiked zombies but the armored ones? They only where Bullet proof vests there necks are still exposed. I am also a believer that the melee weapons in this game are BROKEN. As much as i like shooting the guns the melee weapons how perform the guns in every single way. There is no punishment for using a melee weapon. The gun has so many flaws such as reloading, aiming, early game dmg, armored and spiked zeds, cqb combat, horde clearing, ammo. You know what doesnt have that, melee weapons. You can literally clear out a entire backyard of SPIKED ZOMBIES with just a single melee weapon without getting scratched. A huge horde in front of you? just swing like a mad man with a melee weapon and problem solved. There is no risk reward for using melee weapons. On top of that, they promote this melee spam since a lot of the melee weapons grant bonus loot which is the main drive of the game on kill. There needs to be a risk for using melee weapons as of right now there is none but the guns in this game have a ton of risks and low reward. Also, give these weapons weight it does not feel satisfying waving around a wooden stick that can one tap walkers.The Horde:Why is it a red wall of nothing? This game can render in a ton of zombies at once so why not make it idk a actual horde? The only reason why i think they did not make it a actual horde is the player will just mow them down without worry and if so that just shows even the devs know the melee is op in this game. Make the horde a actual walking horde you have to deal with with the suggested balances and maybe it might make it more fun and immersive.Balancing:I think I see what they were going for here, I like the idea of switching between guns and melee. It is a healthy dynamic but I think it is executed wrong here. I am fine with melee weapons being op but there needs to be a risk for using them and I propose a stamina system. I get they are trying to go for a more arcadey experience but I think this will do the game good. It will promote the use of guns to deal with zombies and only use melee weapons on the special zeds. Duel wielding, why isnt this in the game? They want you to feel like a badass mowing through zombies but they dont have duel wielding? Let us wield two guns, two melee, a melee and a gun. VR has two hands not one and it does duel wielding better than any other device out there without even trying. Just let the player use both hands and we will do the rest. Give all the guns AP rounds, it is a good concept on paper that you should switch to your melee weapon in order to take down special zeds. This makes game play more interactive but the current state of melee just makes them broken. Since the weapon switch system in this game is a wheel it does not feel satisfying switch weapons. Like once I pull out my machete why would I want to switch back to my other weapons might as well stick with it since I know it can do everything.In the end TWD onslaught isnt bad, you just have to chew it first in order to swallow. The guns get better in the end but they still get out performed by the melee weapons. The arcadey aspect does not feel rewarding. IDK if I am going to go back and play with game since the replay value isnt that high since the combat itself does not feel satisfying. Unlike Arizona sunshine I go back to that since that gunplay is so good and satisfying same with Robo recall.Would recommend for $20 or cheaper

_childDocuments_.review: I can't fathom why every officially licensed AMC video game is terrible, maybe they have someone who doesn't play them in charge of giving projects the go ahead.In any case, this is a pretty lackluster edition to the walking dead universe, the levels are uninspired and your forced to do the same maps over and over to collect resources to access the main campaign (which is just 7 levels long, thankfully in this case)The combat isn't good (gunplay particularly bad on HTC Vive Cosmos so avoid it if you have that HMD). _childDocuments_.review: I think this is a fun game. I didn't say great nor bad, but it's fun. I feel it's more for those who are looking for an arcade style zombie game that also has story and other unique aspects. There are some things about this game that need refining or polishing, some things that need to be added or done so that it could become better. If you're looking for an amazing zombie game with good voice acting and a bit of a realistic style to it, this isn't your game chief. The voice acting can be a bit wonky at times and there are many bugs where the zombies end up flying around, then your hand follows and you're surrounded by walkers with one empty hand and your weapons hand is 50 feet away. I enjoy supply runs and the story, I'm not saying the story was great and all, it could use some work, but it's definitely enjoyable. The supply runs have you on a time limit that's represented by a decently-quick moving herd (or horde, whatever you want to call it.). Don't get all excited though, the herd is just a red wall with some 2D silhouettes of walkers. When inside it, you just slowly lose health. It does give this sense of "Hurry before they catch up and surround me!", but has a bit of a disappointing execution when it happens. Guns are kinda useless, it's not head shot to kill, it's more like 3 shots to kill unless you have melee, crossbow, or you continuously upgrade your guns. Overall the game is okay, personally enjoyed it, and the developers seem to be really passionate about making this game better. Maybe not worth the big $30 price tag but I'm remaining optimistic.

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: It took me approximately 8 hours to complete this game, including fully upgrading Alexandria. Anyways, this was my worst fear for this game. I am completely disappointed by Survios. This is nowhere near the quality of TWD:SS. This is a completely linear experience, with very simplistic combat and survival elements.The good is that this does put you in the familiar world of The Walking Dead TV series. It has the main characters from the TV show, in a familiar setup from the TV show. The voice acting is okay. The game ends in the middle of the story. Because the survival missions interrupt by the main story campaign by design, the story feels disjointed and lacks proper pacing. Unfortunately, the lack of depth to the story and character development, make the dialogue sound distant and doesn't grip you at any moment in the telling of its tale by Daryl.  You do have full locomotion, swing, teleportation, all the rotation options you'd want as well as sound and some graphical settings. Although, I would have liked to have had more graphical options to tailor the experience towards my particular rig. The graphics are similar to the quality of Arizona Sunshine, maybe even a slight downgrade from them. That is to say, it's rather underwhelming after having played HLA. The interactions are very basic and perhaps the most disappointing part. You point and click on objects and they automatically get used or go into your inventory. There are many objects that you cannot interact with. You magnet hand a weapon with your left motion controller, it auto goes into your right hand. You don't charge weapons. You pick up any ammo you have from your belt. You have very limited ammo so you'll want to melee whenever you can. Unfortunately, the melee here is nowhere as satisfying as TWD:SS or Boneworks. You'll basically be using your Darth Vader type choke hold grip on zombies while you knife them on the head. You'll be repeating this action frequently. While some weapons, like the Katana and Battle Axe are fun to use, especially when fully upgraded, for most of the game the combat will feel not realistic enough for a sim or survival type gameplay and not satisfying enough for an arcade type combat mechanic.The survival element is just basically scavenging stuff from dull looking environments while a red line keeps advancing towards your spot. It's an odd gameplay loop that is not very satisfying to experience. You pick up materials to upgrade your base and as you do so, you unlock chapters to play (the story campaign).  The gameplay does get better towards the end once you have a nice array of weapons and upgrades. The gore is nice when using the Katana and you can really slice & carve up their bodies quite nicely when it is upgraded. However, the gameplay always lacks depth and is never on par with what we've come to expect with the combat in other major VR titles. Even the story campaign is marred by all the off-hand motion controller grab clicks you'll have to do to scavenge the highlighted objects around the environment. This is a step backwards for VR and Survios. This game would have been better titled: The Walking Dead: ABS. Always Be Scavenging.

_childDocuments_.review: I was fine with all the other broken parts of this game but after finally unlocking the baseball bat (a weapon I was looking forward to using) I've had enough. Most of the weapons in the game are just broken, I know it's a new game and they might still have to fix some ♥♥♥♥, but when the weapons don't work right the game is unplayable. My last hope is the katana, if that doesn't work right either then I will just have to wait for them to fix the game...However, if you like arcade like zombie games and mediocre weapons, then you should definitely get this game!If not, best to stay away if or until they make some changes to the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Played with Valve Index. Based on all the negative feedback, I wasn't expecting much. I actually enjoyed this for a light workout using the arm swinging movement and stabbing. Arm swinging movement definitely adds to the experience of running! A pity it takes 3 head shots to kill one walker. Hopefully this is fixed in an update because otherwise the pistol is far less desirable than stabbing, which does become tiresome. I also hope they remove the looming red barrier during scavenging. Losing health to it doesn't make sense when you could simply be overwhelmed and be ripped to shreds by a horde of walkers if you take too long. That should be enough motivation to hurry. A little disappointing not to be able to smash car windows or interact with the few objects in the environment. I also wish I could use the knuckles controllers to grab and holster weapons as in other games using controller grip instead of the selection wheel. Game play is fairly shallow, and limited to a linear path though the labyrinth of each location. Despite it's flaws, I am enjoying it so far and give a thumbs up, especially for fans of the show.
