_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game for a while I think I can give my opinion on this game. I’ve seen a lot of negative comments but I think it’s not as bad as people think it is. Its very fun to kill the Zombies and there are two "modes" to play the game. First, you got the main campaign which is very fun to me because while sitting at a campfire a guy tells you an old story and you can then play what he was going through while they talk in the back. I think this way of telling the story is fine and the story is not as bad as people say it is. Then there is the part where you gather resources and I have to say that this "mode" is not as fun as I thought and it feels a bit lacking because the reward isn’t worth it and the environments are pretty boring and it helps you to build your own houses for people to live in which makes sense in a zombie apocalypse but it just feels like a mobile game in that sense. Overall the "mode" feels like a boring and lackluster task. The story part of the game is very fun tho and I don’t get why this game has such a negative rating. I have to say that I expected more and that I don’t like the building of the houses but its ok.

_childDocuments_.review: I am in awe of how lazily put together and pointless this game turned out to be. Onslaught is a shamefully dumbed-down version of the gameplay in Saints and Sinners with a very boring story.Gameplay: The first and only weapon you need in this game is the knife. One stab to the head. That's it. Guns for some reason take 3-4 shots to the head to kill a normal zombie. Then the missions are either blatant mazes for padding the game's runtime (the campaign) or missions where you are urged to go pick up supplies in random buildings (the filler side missions). Story: Only two missions into the story and it is painfully boring. There is no hook, nothing to keep the player interested. It's just Rick and Daryl arguing with each other at first. Then the end of the second mission finally brings up some conflict about a random missing person that no one has ever heard or cared about before. At that point I was just too exhausted from wandering around a maze of nothing. I immediately turned off the game. I'm going to refund this so I can buy Red Dead Redemption 2 on sale for $40.And the graphics are really bad too I guess. Like, that alone is reason enough to refund.

_childDocuments_.review: As a hardcore walking dead fan who started watching the show back in 2013 (season 4), I was really excited when they announced this game based off of it. To begin I can't stress enough how the walking dead saints and sinners is a completely different game and shouldn't be compared to this. But regardless I think we're all a bit underwhelmed having played that masterpiece of a game before this.I feel this game has a lot of fan service in it, but its to the extent that it breaks the TV shows lore which it is trying to follow. Although these minor lorebreaks don't make the biggest difference I still thought I'd point them out.Although iconic to the show, Rick never does continue wearing his pre-apocalypse police uniform especially in Alexandria so for any buffs it just feels weird.Throughout the game you unlock blueprints to build certain buildings such as the town hall, though a nice idea. It makes no sense in that Maggie and Rick had all the blueprints as they were given them by Georgie.This game has very much been grinded down by the devs to what feels like a very barebone run and stab game. The supply run (scavenge) missions in this game are complete garbage as you're rushed the entire time so there's no chance of using any stealth whatsoever. You're often left just full sprinting throughout houses quickly grabbing whatever you can before running back out which leaves you no time to actually look around.I can't talk to much about the campaign as I never was able to really get into it but from what I played it felt extremely bland.The reason I said run and stab instead of  "run and gun" before is because this game's gun system is just complete ass, shooting is FAR from enjoyable especially since walkers often take two or three HEADSHOTS to kill which makes me cringe. Reloading guns in this game is very automated which is completely stupid, when I'm playing a VR game I want to be able to  manually load it and ♥♥♥♥ it.Overall just avoid this game until it receives a major content update or a major ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ price drop. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: (((If you don't like the wall of text, just read the summary)))This game isn't perfect, and I feel like people are making the "cons" of the game much bigger than they are, most of the nit-picks in other reviews and personal problems like "bad voice acting" or "no finger tracking for index" both of which don't affect the game play.Pros: Decently fluid combat - Compared to Saints and Sinners (or S&S) the combat isn't as polished but is more hack and slash focused, trying something like that is S&S would most likely get you killed. Combat is faster paced in this game and has a free form dismembering system, allowing better use of bladed weapons. The combat is also very responsive, minimal to no weapon clipping.Difficulty Selection - Just a nice feature to allow casual game play for newer players or hard for fast paced action.Mechanics -  The picking up system is quick and easy, so no need to break your back over picking up things on the ground, just point and pull the trigger. Weapon switching is very quick and clean, similar to Half-Life: Alyx pressing the weapon wheel button slows down time a little, and just move your hand to weapon you want. (you can hold four different weapons)Opening doors just by slamming open with your hand or a weapon is easy too.Looter Shooter Vibes - There's lots of things to be found around the level, but in scavenger mode your on a time crunch, a horde of zombies is just behind you, so be quick and be smart to get as much loot as you can. There's also a story mode.Cons:A couple bugs here and thereThe pistol isn't as useful as you would think.The price is a little highSummary:The Walking Dead: Onslaught is a mostly polished hack and slash, looter shooter about killing a S**t ton of zombies. The melee combat is nice and feels good, and the mechanics are simple. This isn't the immersive game you may be looking for, it might have corny voice acting (never watched the show so IDK) But at face value, if your looking for a game where you can hack, gun, or beat down crowds of zombies, it might be worth giving the game a try.I enjoy the game for what it is, combat, loot, weapons, and zombies. Don't take my word for it though, I recommend trying the game out.In my opinion ignore other reviews and play the game for yourself, just because other people don't like the game doesn't mean you'll dislike it either.

_childDocuments_.review: The big ballance patch fixes a lot of issues the youtubers had with the gameplay.  Was it worth the hype? No. Is it fun to run around in a shlocky C-movie version of Saints and Sinners? Yes. Did I grab Daryls crotch to see if he would punch me? Yes multiple times and I have to say that the collision meshes on the NPCs are surprisingly well done. They put a lot of work into some aspects of the game while others look like it was made 10 years ago. It's like they ran out of time/funding halfway through. Play it on Veteran to actually feel like the zombies pose a threat. Running away is the best choice in a lot of situations which is what a real zombie game should convey. Guns are powerful now and I prefer them over melee but with limited ammo melee is a good choice for low numbers of zombies. My only real annoyances in the early game are the many helmet wearing zombies making guns useless and the twitching/glitching zombies making it hard to hit headshots. (edit: shoot the knees so they fall over and stun lock them on the ground with the hammer or just get the slo mo hammer upgrade making every armored/spiked zombie no longer a threat)Get it on a sale. Edit: After finishing the game on veteran I have to say that the upgraded hammer is op af and kinda breaks the game. I wish they gave me the katana+upgrades earlier so I didn't have to one shot bonk regular zombies or bonk/slomo/hammertime my way through armored and spiked zombies the entire game. Late game 2 handed weapons are kinda annoying because I use my off hand to scavenge. I kept using my starter pistol, one handed submachine gun and hammer all the way through.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade Crafter.  Auto eject magazines, magazine grab reload, thumb pad weapon choice.  I know there's a lot of people who 'prefer' arcade reloading over realistic weapon charging, so this is for you.  A hotfix has already been released for some crash issues, but I have to leave a positive review for this, because I know there's a lot of old arcade gamers who love VR, but get put off by 'inventory management' and 'gun sims'.  I like both, but again, this is more arcade.  On another note on the weaponry, they are underpowered 'before' you upgrade them, again, made for arcade players, but the weapons have their own fun special attributes, like slow-mo for the knife, chance to gain life and crafting materials per zombie kill... stuff like that.  I have to admit that the tutorial mission (which is a scavenger mission.  Basicallly a 'phantom horde' timer, which drains your energy, and I can see was made to add a bit of spice to the scavenging aspect, making you run around for more health (which can't be stored for later))... er yeah anyway, the tute mission was probably a bad choice, because the Main Campaign, which is Daryl's story, does not have the 'zombie horde'.  There were a lot of reviews that kinda knocked it for the 'scavenger mode' thinking that this was for every mission.  I can see that the devs have really looked into the 'Walking Dead' mythos, but again, tried to keep it arcadey, which was their target market, so I gotta leave a suggestion that should please comic readers, gamers and devs, alike... and Marvel Zombie writers, too... The Walking Dead are attracted to noise.  In a future update, please make the horde slow down or speed up, depending on whether you're using a melee weapon, inciting zombies by toying with them, or going all out with rifle-crackers.  If possible, make it like a 'reverse Battle Rotale' circle collapse', the more noise you make, the bigger the circle gets...  I think I actually got that from a character in The Walking Dead comic.  Thanks for the advice, Mr. Kirkman :)

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing I can think of is that graphically it's pretty nice. Not the best but you can tell a lot of effort went into the areas, the characters and the Walkers. A good 7 out a 10. The music, or what little music there is, is okay. Hearing the  opening theme when starting the game up really makes you feel like you're entering the world of The Walking Dead, and the game tries it's best to make you feel tense in certain situations.The big let down are the controls. You are forced to stick to one play style as all weapons are locked onto your dominant hand, and with some weapons your non-dominant hand automatically 'assists' in holding the weapon up when it gets too close (there is no point to this as items in this game have no 'weight', so whether you hold it with 1 hand or 2 it does the same amount of damage).The knife is OP compared to the ranged items. I used a gun during the story once, and that was when you have to during the prologue. All other times I only used the knife as it's much more effective than ranged weapons as you can take Walkers down with one hit, whereas when using a gun (even if it's a headshot) it takes you at least 2 shots. It's much quicker to just run up and stab them, rendering the ranged weapons useless. The only issue I found with the knife is that it often goes off-key. As in, even when I perfectly stab an enemy in the head, the knife will instead stab the shoulder, or even the enemy's back. It's very frustrating and says a lot about the controls.The voice acting is very try hard. Not much more I can say to that.The whole point of VR is that it's immersive. The player actually feels like they're running around in that area and interacting with the environment and the characters. You don't get this with Onslaught. An example is during the prologue just as you find Daryll, he looks over to you. Or more, he looks over to the place where you're supposed to be standing. If you walk away from that point, he doesn't follow you, but stares at the spot where you're supposed to be. It's a small detail but it does a lot of break the immersion.I play with HTC Vive controllers, so the controls are naturally much more limited compared to the Index controllers, but even with that limitation the controllers aren't being used as much as they should be, and from what I've seen the same issue goes for the Index. You can't pick up or put down items, instead you just point and click (which, again, breaks immersion), and any weapon you choose automatically goes to your hand.Whilst the Walkers look very good, they don't feel threatening at all. The icon that pops up whenever you're being attacked isn't helpful, it's just annoying. Even when surrounded you don't feel in any danger because they take very little health off of you and they're easy to take down.Of what little I saw of the story, it's not very engaging or exciting. Your main goal is to expand Alexandria (which from what I can see you can't explore), and you do this by going out on supply runs that take no more than 5 minutes. You collect food, items for upgrades and ammo, which are in abundance everywhere you go, even when playing on Novice difficulty. It doesn't feel like a survival game when everything you need it literally being thrown in your path.TLDR; In it's current form, this game is hard to play. It's not fun or immersive, and a lot of things need updating. I don't think I'll be picking this up again until the issues are fixed. If you want a fun The Walking Dead game, play Saints and Sinners.

_childDocuments_.review: I know everyone's talking about how bad the game was, especially compared to Saints and Sinners, but Onslaught isn't a bad game. I've played about 5 hours now, and it's probably one of my favorite VR games so far. Everyone is criticizing the game for stuff like Andrew Lincoln not voicing Rick, the arcadey play style, the fact you don't physically pick items up or open doors, how it't just a "Arizona Sunshine Reskin", and most annoying of all, how it isn't as good as Saints and Sinners. The game is arcadey because that's what it's meant to play like, and it's different from SaS because SaS and Onslaught are going for 2 different tones. Onslaught is meant to be a lighthearted "shoot 'em up" style game that you can pick up and play without the need for a lengthy tutorial, and Saints and Sinners is meant to be a more complicated and in-depth game. All in all, if you're going to criticize this game, don't criticize it for not being as good as an extremely different game and being "arcadey" and criticize the game for something worth criticizing. Also, the biggest need for improvement in the game is an online mode. That  would make the game more enjoyable for a wider audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I've played this game for about 2 hours, and here are my thoughts on it, as well as some pro's and con's.So far, I haven't ran into any bugs and the game runs smoothly for me, sadly as an index user, the controllers do not work as they're intended, I mean don't get me wrong, they do work, but they work more like oculus controllers (maybe it'll change in the future?) But overall, I find the game fun, I would say it looks a lot better than S&S, Combat features are better (except reloading). Now here are what the pro's are in my opinion, and the con's-Pro's--Sticks to the Lore of the TV Series-Dismemberment is very well done-Graphics are very good-Models are done well, and have a good amount of detail-Story (if you want to call it that) is fun, makes you feel like you're in an actual episode of the walking dead-Melee weapon gameplay is amazing-Con's--Rick's voice actor sounds terrible, and I mean terrible, now you can tell he tried, but it has to be the worst version of ricks voice I've ever heard-Gunplay seems to be a downgrade from S&S-Reloading is very arcade-ish (I mean this game was made sorta in that style)-When you go on the supply runs (not the story missions) there is a timer where the "hoard" is behind you, but if you walk into it, you lose health, you don't have to fight off a hoard or anything-You can't explore Alexandria, even tho you spend most of the game upgrading it-Not much open world compared to S&S-Index Controllers do not work how they were made to workand here are some that honestly depends if you think they're bad or not.- The supply run missions you do have a hoard you have to stay ahead of, and if you get caught in the hoard you start to lose health- Most of the time you spend in the game is doing those supply runsOther than all the pro's and con's, I do recommend this game. It may not be as good as S&S, but for casual players or people that just want to slash at walkers and loot building to make Alexandria a safe place again, than this game is for you. There were a lot of complaints on S&S about how much the game asked for from the player, and this game doesn't do that. Now one thing they may have focused on a little too much, but makes the game better in the end, is the melee combat. I cannot say this enough, it IS an amazing work of art. Top that melee combat system off with all the blood, gore, and dismemberment, and you feel like you're fighting in the show. I personally think, this game is worth it for the price, but I do recommend waiting for a sale if you're unsure. Anyways, hoped this helped :)

_childDocuments_.review: So right off the bat, I think the problem with this game and how it’s being perceived by the community right now is the expectation Saints & Sinners set or that people expected a more fully fledged open world game.As someone who completed Saints & Sinners I see a LOT of similarities in terms of gameplay between these two titles with the difference being those elements are split up rather than indirectly blending together.  You have a separate storyline but also a time based looting area called "Supply Runs" you travel to which are fast and designed to help you farm resources and gather new survivors which you need to advance to the next campaign mission. There is less dependence on crafting, instead you find weapons out in the world would I think I prefer as it feels more rewarding. You can upgrade weapons and your town by collecting resources in either the campaign maps or supply runs (the time based runs). Weapons are the big hit and miss here, Guns (pistols can require up-to 3 headshots to take down a walker. They can be upgraded but still guns early game do feel kind of worthless. On the flip side melee weapons are VERY overpowered and once you get the machete you become an unstoppable killing machine. Because there is NO stamina OR weapon integrity you can just keep swinging left and right. In comparison guns feel like an annoyance. AGAIN I expect this might change when I find a Machine Gun or Shotgun maybe. This does make for VERY repetitive gameplay where you are just slicing through walkers again and again but is this a bad thing? The reason it feels repetitive is because of the massive number of walkers in comparison to the amount in Saints & Sinners. You cannot afford to play this way in Saints because you can only melee a few zombies before you run out of stamina forcing you to sneak and avoid walkers a lot more. Here you just clear them out whenever you want. These are two different styles of gameplay both with their own intention and here I'm ok with it because it makes for a more action packed game. Take it for what it is, an Action zombies shooter not a survival horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not quite too sure why this game got as much hate as it did. It's an entertaining game that has great graphics, a good story, and great voice acting. There have been a few bugs and shortcomings I've witnessed while playing this game as it's not nearly as polished as the other Walking Dead VR Title , however what it does bring to the table is a unique adventure based on the Walking Dead TV Series by AMC (rather than the Walking Dead Comic Series that S&S is based on).Controls may be funky but the game gives you an arsenal of helpful settings. This includes a left handed mode (useful for any of us lefties or ambidextrous), comfort controls like vignette, teleportation, etc. The games combat is admittedly one of the shortcomings this game has. It takes 2 bullets in the head to kill a walker, if you shoot anywhere else it'll stunt the walker for a bit before moving on. Melee combats feel much much better as it takes on stab to the head to kill a walker or 3 jabs with a hammer. Reloading feels off and arcadey.The story is easy to follow along for new and old viewers from the Walking Dead TV Series. The Hub is quite small but in it you have a campfire (where you begin the story mode missions), a billboard where you can see letters and quests from the people of Alexandria, as well as the staff credits. You can make and upgrade buildings, go on looting / scavenging hunts to bring back supplies, go to the armory to test new weapons you found and upgrade them. For the story mode missions you'll be playing as Daryl and for the scavenging missions you'll be able to play as Rick, Michonne, or Carol.I have really enjoyed my time with this game so far and would recommend this game even at the default price of $29.99. I, however, would even more-so recommend waiting for this game to go on sale on Steam or websites like Humble Bundle and Fanatical. I've seen it go for $13.49 alone and for $5 along with 2 other games in a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as indepth as Saints and Sinners, but honestly I didn't go into this game expecting that. If you want instant gratification and just a simple good time killing walkers? Yeah, this is a decently fun game.The voice acting isn't horrible, but it is a little lack lustre in places. _childDocuments_.review: Never before in my time on steam have I been more confused by a games 'mostly negative' rating. I have played through the tutorial, 2 scavenging areas, and about 3 or 4 main missions at the stage of the game that I am up to, and as of now I am yet to see any major issues with the game, which is why I'm baffled by the awful user reviews as of now (  ).Don't get me wrong, the faces of the living humans in this game look really bad, and I have seen a few issues with shadows so far, but for the most part the walkers look great and the environments look good too. On top of that I have had no issues running the game on my set up, perfectly smooth with my: Valve Index, RTX 3090, I7-8700K, and 32GB RAM.Now the biggest issue I have seen with this game so far, according to most people, are how the firearms work. Multiple shots to the head to kill a walker. Yes indeed, this is extremely unsatisfying when playing the game, however I believe this was done to benefit the upgrading system the game revolves around. You upgrade your weapons as you collect materials, and it would make sense that by the end of the game you can become a killing machine with the guns through upgrades. I don't know this for a fact of course, but that's usually how these sort of games go.Where the most satisfying game play is for me so far, is with the knife. A knife one hits walkers with a hit to the head, and the knife can be quickly upgraded to give you most materials you could need by killing with it (leading to the gun upgrades, and more, that I mentioned earlier. Now the main point I wanted to make about the mostly negative reviews this game has, is about why I believe it has this rating. I honestly believe that most people went into this game expecting another Saints and Sinners, but this confuses me, because this game was never advertised like that to my knowledge. This game has always looked like an arcade style walking dead game, but people seem to point this out as a huge complaint about the game! The above point does not stand necessarily true for Quest players however, I have heard many times that this game is completely unplayable on the Quest due to the controls outright not functioning. This complaint in particular is legitimately a huge issue, and people who leave the game with negative reviews because of it are justified. Developers, if you read this, get this fixes, its absolutely unforgivable that some of your market literally cant play the product they purchased.It has been made aware to me in the comments of this review that I did in fact fail to comment on the very controversial 'mist'. This mist follows you on certain scavenger missions and basically acts as your time limit to scavenge before the horde catches you. The problem that people have is that the horde is represented by this red mist, and the 2D zombies within it, rather than a horde of fully rendered zombies. I personally have mixed opinions on this mist.Firstly yes, it does seem very lazy to, instead of keeping with the immersion of the game, have this mist instead of a huge terrifying horde. The spectacle and fear this would induce in the player would be amazing, and make you really feel like you need to move fast.On the other hand there are reason that I back the idea of this mist over a rendered horde.Firstly it serves the purpose of a horde without having to render lots of zombies. This could be essential when running the game on lower end machines, the stress of loading a full horde of zombies could very well make these missions unplayable on machines with weaker hardware.Secondly it gives the player a chance. Keeping with the arcade nature of the game, the mist gives the player a chance to survive if they fall behind, this panics the player while still giving them the relief of surviving. In the walking dead universe, you are dead in a horde, this much better fits a more survival horror game rather than an arcade game.Thirdly, material farming. In the game you can upgrade your knife to gather materials when you get kills with it. These range from common, all the way up to rare materials. I feel like if the horde was rendered, and could be interacted with, you could farm a ridiculous amount of materials from these walkers as they continued to spawn, this would over power the players weapons extremely quickly leading to balancing issues as they continue down the main quest line.Walking Dead Onslaught is a very misunderstood game for reasons yet unknown to me. Maybe it was advertised poorly by the game company, maybe consumers ignored the advertising and just assumed what they were buying was another Saints and Sinners, I have no idea.What I do know is that if you want a fun fast paced arcade style walking dead game, with a weapon and base upgrading system, then you will enjoy this game. It has minimal bugs from what I have seen so far besides a couple issues with shadows, and poorly rendered faces, but these are made up for in the main meat of the game, the game play itself.If you have a Quest, you should absolutely avoid this game for now, it will not work for you. Contact the developers, get the controls fixed, and then I will recommend it to you too.As I progress further into the game, if I run into any severe issues I WILL absolutely be updating this review, but as for now, it gets a positive rating from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Even after all of the negative news and the complaints, I can't believe I'm finding myself having fun with this game.  I've played Arizona Sunshine, Contaigon VR, Surviv3 (favorite Coop zombie VR game), Walking Dead Saints and Sinners, and Killing Floor Incursion.  This game is below all of those but it's still a lot of fun.  I guess it's because compared to all of those, this is just as arcadey as Killing Floor Incursion.  Guns really suck but smacking zombies around with a hammer is quite satisfying.  Story is super meh and the scavenging missions with the "big scary red wall" but the saving grace is being able to punch, grab, throw, and just smack zombies around.  If all you wanted to do in Saints and Sinners was go fisticuffs against the zombies, this game will let you do that.  Also, out of all the previously mentioned zombie games, this game has the best looking zombies.The weird part of the game's graphics is that human characters look bad and the whole world    Hazy? Film Grainy?   It's like the brightness and contrast were turned down and there is no way to increase it.  The option menu is very very limited. Also seems like the devs abandoned the game.So, even with all of that said, I can only recommend this game if its  10 dollars and under.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight soI did like this game, but it's been abandoned by the devs. Yep that's it. You're looking at a campaign that is at most 8 hours, possibly a few more hours to unlock everything and then... literally nothing else. No arena, no endless/survival mode (like meat grinder in Saints and Sinners) and just very little here to offer for the price. The combat is fun I actually preferred it to SnS because no annoying stamina bar. However you really just don't have much game here to speak of. The levels and enemies are repetitive, like they got a great idea to make a game and then just half-assed it and did about 20% of what they could've. The story just ends abruptly without much closure, like they were planning to do more but decided to just push it out for release without finishing it. I was fully expecting DLC or some kind of episodic content updates but it's just been 100% dead silence from the devs.edit: sure enough about a year later and absolutely zero communication from the developers. They are infamous for abandoning games and leaving them unfinished (like Sprint Vector). Get this on sale if you like some good zombie bashing but don't expect a finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game. Honestly I enjoyed it. While sure it is true it is not as fun or addictive as Saints and Sinners, I feel like the negative reviews are a bit harsh. I did not experience some of the issues reviews talked about, so I think some balancing may have been done with an update. I enjoyed the story parts of the game where you can play at your own pace as Darryl, with a nice narrative approach. The supply runs were not all that exciting, with the exception of finding new weapons. As you play and progress looking out for new weapons is rewarding because it really does improve your ability to take down walkers. You start from being afraid of large hordes, to a master at slicing zombies. Only a few melee weapons are good at taking down the really armored zombies, but I enjoyed finding which weapons were most effective. Yes I would recommend. I will say that I don't think the replayability is there, but I think the game is worth a playthrough if you enjoy killing zombies in VR.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this game gets so much hate.  I have this game as well as saints & sinners.  Personally I find the style, graphics, story, and most importantly the fun factor much higher in Onslaught than s&s.  The gameplay loop of switching between story mode and scavenging is pretty decent. The story sections are well told. And the scavenging sections are a bit more unnerving with the oncoming red swarm.  It can get a little repetitive to do scavenging a bunch, but I find if I breakup play sessions, I came back wanting to scavenge to see my town get better, level-up, and unlock more story. So for me it was actually a more addictive gameplay loop.The graphics are quite crisp on a good gaming rig; for me overall the game was stable and seemed well optimized on settings turned all the way up on my 2070S (which cant be said for a lot of AA VR Games).  One of the complaints I see is often about the melee weapons being over powerful relative to the guns. That's true and certainly a bit unrealistic. But honestly I found that to be fun, once I figured out the mechanics. There are plenty of gun ranged zombie games, so being forced to be more physical with close combat came to be something I really enjoyed about the game.My only real complaint, is this game would be even better if it included the co-op mode the devs were talking about before it was released.  I don't mind it since I play multiplayer so rarely, but if they managed to include it, I'm sure it would have really set it apart.In the end, it's really sad the game released at the same time s&s did, and it just got lost in that mix. Had they released it before, or just waited a while before they released it to let the s&s hype cool off, maybe people wouldn't compare them so directly, and I think the game would have done much better.  It's too bad, because for me I have dozens of VR games and Onslaught is in my in top 10.Oh and the last point good point on this game is it goes on sale frequently. So if you get it for $20 or under, it's a great value. Pick it up!FINAL SCORE: 5 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: I've updated this review from thumbs down to thumbs up now that I've sorted out the XY/AB buttons not working using an Oculus Quest over Virtual Desktop. That was a Virtual Desktop issue not a TWD Onslaught issue which I fixed by updating the Virtual Desktop Streamer App in Windows. I have no idea why everyone is recommending S&S over this, I mean Onslaught definitely could have been better but S&S absolutely sucked balls & if I could get a refund on that I 100% would. The game itself is great albeit with some mechanics which could have been better. I'm not a big fan of having a zombie horde bearing down on you the whole time putting undue pressure on you to scavenge in a hurry but it's considerably better done than Saints & Sinners, especially considering you can slow down the horde speed with a lower difficulty level & that some missions are flash backs that don't have a horde bearing down on you at all & you can play / kill zombies at your own pace. Weapons last in this game as they would in real life, none of this absolute bs / highly frustrating melee AND firearm weapons breaking after minimal use like S&S but yes the firearms should probably do more damage than a knife. And yeah the Rick voice acting sounds like a comically bad impression of Andrew Lincoln doing an impression of an American but the other voices sound good enough for me. The graphics are good but definitely could have been better, at least the game's trying to resemble real life & looks much better than S&S which is trying to look like a comic book. I'm only 4 missions into the game but so far it's a pleasure to play compared to TWD S&S which I absolutely despised.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead Onslaught is a game I've been hyped for a really long time about.  At first it felt alright, with the way the knife worked, but as soon as they give you a gun it goes downhill.  Your non-dominant hand will auto snap to your weapon when you put your hand close, and you don't have to push any buttons to grab or hold a weapon.   Gun play in general in WDO is disappointing, in most "realer" zombie games, it's rule of thumb to aim for the head, however, in Onslaught, aiming for the head is hardly more effective.  Reloading is disappointing as you just eject your old mag with a button and hover a new one under it.  Why even use a gun when you can run at a zombie, push it so you don't have to worry about any others, and just stab it in the head for a one shot?  It's much more effective then wasting 3-4 bullets on a head shot.  I may buy it again, after a couple updates, but for now,  my personal recommendation  is wait until it's better, or go play Arizona Sunshine.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review Here: Written summary for those who dont want to watch the video.If all you want to do is kill lots of zombies you may enjoy it. Personally I found the game incredibly repetitive and grindy along with a few other issues that could be tweaked out.Weapon handling:Melee weapons stick into the zombies now like saints and sinners but they are just on a timer, stick a combat knife in a zombies head and you have to wait a couple of seconds to pull it out. It stops your from walking through hordes of zombies like before but it needs more work.2 handed melee weapons like the fire axe are way to easy to stick in, you can use them one handed and literally just flick the wrist.Guns feel fine when holding and shooting them and you can now kill zombies with one shot to the brain unlike before when you needed 3-4 bullets. The reloading needs work as they have animations that take control of your hands which feels wierd and break immersion.Hand Interaction:There isnt any, well very little. You have to use your offhand to pick stuff up and weapons warp into your dominant hand. you just suck up health and supplies, you cant dual weild.You can use your offhand to push zombie back and grab them though.You also punch your way through the enviroment including punching open doors, ammo boxs and fridges.Gameplay Loop:This is the worst part for me. Even if they fix all the other stuff the game is very grindy because to access the story missions you have to unlock a certian number of survivors and to unlock survivors you have to go on scavenge runs through the same areas sucking up supplys over and over again.Graphics:Zombies look OKish, enviroments not so much, low res textures in areas with some poor lighting and it has a mobile game look to it.If you dont mind grindy games and just want to kill zombies you may find some fun in this game but it wasnt for me.Video has more detail and shows examples of what im talking about.

A solid 5/10, I'd recommend it if you want a casual zombie-killing experience.A lot of the reviews for this game are pretty vicious, it's kinda funny. It's a VR game, I don't expect stellar graphics. The voice acting isn't great, sometimes it's comical, though I can't imagine how much money it'd cost to rent all these actors to get all these voice lines done. Norman Reedus isn't cheep.The gunplay isn't great, I avoid it entirely, guns certainly need a buff. Melee can be fun, but that's really just 1 or 2 weapons. DON'T buff the fireaxe, that just ruins the fun of it. My biggest gripe with this game is they somehow ♥♥♥♥♥♥ UP the katana! Instead of actually making contact, it just slices over the zombies or removes something. You can't do the classic Michone over-the-head downswing where you lodge the sword in the zombies head, then pull it out. Even cutting zombies heads off isn't fun. My favorite thing in Saints  and Sinners - which this game clearly took notes from, it's obvious -  is the Katanas. The 'horde' is a swing or a miss and I don't mind it. I'd prefer an *actual* horde, but c'est la vie. Overall, for a $30 game, it's not terrible. It's not as good as Saints and Sinners, it lacks the open-world exploration that Saints and Sinners had, so I'm not sure what the replay value is. Still, I'd recommend it. Just don't have crazy high expectations, it isn't Alyx or Saints & Sinners.

Killing zombies is always great. If the Devs choose to stick with this game and update it with the community, there is a lot of potential. The looting system is already there, just need to make it set in a big map with crafting and base building and make it so the game doesn't slow down when your beating those walkers. I won't be returning this game for the pure reason that it has some really good potential. I do on the other hand hope that these bugs and glitches will get fixed. All I know is I will be sticking around. Can't wait to see what the Devs have in store. I haven't had a more fun time killing walkers. The story line, btw, is actually really good. _childDocuments_.review: Setup:  Ryzen 9 5900X // 94GB RAM // RTX 3060 Ti // Quest 2It's not as terrible of a game as others make it out to be.  Could it had been better?  Absolutely.  Is it the worst game I've ever played?  Absolutely not.  I bought it for $7 so I figured I'd give it a shot.  I had zero issues at all while using a Quest 2 on the highest settings.  No bugs/glitches except the one time when I shot a zombie & he bounced off a barrier then yeeted himself onto a roof...but I don't count that since it was funny as ♥♥♥♥.Pro tip:  the hammer is OP.  ...nah, like for real...the hammer is OP.  ESPECIALLY after it's fully upgraded, which doesn't take long at all.  Prepare for your arm to hurt.I haven't fully played Saints & Sinners yet.  I've played the tutorial so far (I'm fairly new to VR) but there's no reason to even compare the two, other than the "Walking Dead" in the title.  This, to me, is more along the lines of "a Horde Shooter with a little bit of a story" than anything else.  There's no inventory management -- it's like every other shooter, you get weapons, you pick up ammo for those weapons & when you run out, you use melee weapons until you find more ammo, then repeat the cycle.  There's no openness to explore, other than in the story missions (but even then you're limited), so you're not saving up anything to do exploration before you finish a new task -- in the manner that Saints & Sinners is.The story is terrible.You play as Daryl searching for the daughter of a survivor.  That's it.  That's the story.  You don't run into anybody from the group that might've kidnapped her (you don't run into any survivors at all, actually), you have no clue why Daryl is so desperate to find her besides the survivor saving his life (...even when he initially said he wouldn't do it), & you don't know anything about the girl besides her name.  The survivor doesn't talk about her at all besides her keeping a journal.  It feels very rushed & incomplete.The "side missions" are nothing more than a horde survival but they aren't bad.  Only problem is, they're mandatory to proceed with the story.You basically just gear up & try to collect items for the base upgrades without dying.  That's basically it.  Zombies are everywhere & there's an ominous "horde" cloud that follows you around the map.  The worst thing that happens is, if you're caught in the cloud, you lose health.  However, while you're running to, in & out of buildings, the zombies can present a challenge if you're not paying attention & clearing a path for yourself.  I did have fun with them at first but after a while it got boring for me since I hate "survive the horde" activities in games.My only real gripe is that I wish they had focused on solely making this a campaign based game & fleshing out the story since they had dropped the co-op aspect they initially had.  At that point this could have been a great game instead of just an "ok" one.  It's decently long at 10hrs but the mandatory side missions feel like filler.  If you can catch it on sale for <$15, I'd recommend it.

I played for roughly 13 hours and got all achievements and beat everything on veteran difficulty. The game, in my experience, was fairly glitchy, but nothing game-breaking, just thoroughly immersion-breaking and frustrating. The voice actor for Rick Grimes, a main character, is absolutely not Andrew Lincoln and is painful until the end to listen to. Also, I don't care what Judith said, obviously-not-Michonne.The saving grace of this game: A fun campaignThe campaign of this game is, while fairly simple and unvaried, actually fun. The story is decent, and the level design is pretty good. If you have the deluxe DLC, the baseball bat's skin is, by default, Lucille, though this can be changed if, for some reason, you'd prefer not to look like a bada*s. Once you obtain it in the campaign, bashing walkers' heads off their shoulders (or into them), with the occasional "Back to it!" is pretty fun.Overall verdict: If you're a die-hard The Walking Dead fan, it's not hard to have a good time playing this, but for those who don't care all that much, this is probably a skip. I, personally, recommend skipping this one if you don't have to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I've decided to give this game a negative review, it's important for me to also mention that it wasn't *all* bad. However, like many other players, I personally found it to be rather unpolished and lacking in a few surprisingly simple aspects.Let's start with the obvious limitations on moving around Alexandria. There's simply no option to explore the garden area where Carol is working or the many buildings that are added as the game progresses. Instead, the player is confined to a small 'circuit' that only grants access to the bare essentials required for completing the game.There are also no additional NPCs placed around Alexandria as the population grows to its maximum of 25 (why is this even limited?). It's almost like they don't actually exist within the community outside of a posting/requisition on the board placed behind Daryl. It would have been nice to occasionally see these characters and perhaps even interact with them to obtain their requisitions.I was essentially set to finish the entire game as soon as I upgraded the machete. This includes all seven chapters with "Veteran" difficulty selected. While I did have fun mixing it up with the guns occasionally, I found them to be comparatively under-powered and a bit awkward to reload -- .TWD:O was based more directly on the television series than other TWD alternatives (e.g. S&S). This added a certain amount of 'expectation' regarding the major characters and their resemblance to any television counterparts. While Survios have done a reasonable job modelling *most* of these cast members (sorry, Michonne… you still needed more work), many of the voices -- including that of Rick Grimes -- simply didn’t match up.If you are looking for an  TWD VR game that makes you feel intrigued, terrified, and more fully invested in the storyline; then you simply can't go past "Saints & Sinners". From its underlying design right through to its gameplay experience, it really did leave "Onslaught" for  .

_childDocuments_.review: I deleted my previous review, which was grudgingly positive.  Since that earlier review there have been two developments.  First, support was added for Virtual Desktop, which is huge to me as I much prefer to play wirelessly.  Second, there was a major re-balancing of the game which greatly improved the combat.  Ok, so I've read a lot of the negative reviews, and while I agree with a lot of the points, I do think this game suffers greatly from the existence of Saints & Sinners,  Saints & Sinners is unquestionably a better game, and I'll say right now, if you're only going to get one, get that one.  That being said, if you take this game for what it is and don't crucify it for not being Saints & Sinners, it's enjoyable.  This game takes a different approach.  It's much more arcadey which it states up front.  The physics are basic, more reminiscent of Arizona Sunshine than Saints & Sinners.  I found it did a pretty good job of maintaining a high tension level during missions.  Graphicly I thought it looked very good, better than Saints & Sinners in some ways, not as good in others, but overall I was satisfied with the graphics.The Melee combat was pretty decent.  Again not as good as Saints & Sinners, but certainly better than everybody's favorite game Half Life Alyx which had none.  Gun play was vastly improved following the patch, and again not as good as S&S but good enough.  Now for some of the valid criticisms, Alexandria is basically a cardboard cutout.  You can't explore the town go into the buildings talk to the characters (other than Michone and Darrel who never seem to move from their assigned spots).  The other thing I had an issue with was the "zombie hord" red wave with no zombies in it.  It more or less worked like a poison mist.  If you're in it, you lose health.  If not you're ok.  I guess it served it's purpose, but it just seemed to be a lazy way out.  The game engine is capable of throwing a LOT of zombies at you which you'll see in the last missions, so I don't get why they didn't put some actual zombies in the zombie hord.  They could have kept the red mist as a way to reduce visibility and keep the numbers manageable, but the way they did just kind of leaves a funny taste in your mouth.And lastly, yes the voice of Rick is cringe worthy at times, and the dialog during missions was extremely repetitive.So taking all the positives and negatives, I would say this is a pretty good zombie game that gives you a chance to play as one of your favorite characters from the show.  No it's not as good as Saints and Sinners, but if you can forgive it for that and take it for what it is, it's a pretty decent game and definitely not the abomination some people are saying it is.  I give it a B, and if you love Zombie games it's worth a shot to play for an hour and see if it's for you.  I don't regret my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to like this game. I really, truly did. but I knew something was wrong the moment I got to the control select part of the tutorial. None of them are convenient. I use an HTC vive and the touch feature on the pads is nice for gimmicky stuff in games, but not a core component to movement. Next on my big list of things wrong with this game is the dominant hand feature. I'm right handed so I selected the right hand option. What I didn't know would happen is that every interaction I would have with the world environment would be done with my left hand which is really annoying. Third is the walkers themselves. Hordes aren't scary or seem like that much of a threat. The starting knife goes into them and comes out super fast making quick work of as many as you can find. This is a problem because the core of all zombie fiction is to make you feel completely helpless and at a constant numbers disadvantage. You wont get that here. While I'm talking about combat lets look at the guns. Now I know there are more weapons but I couldn't bring myself to play this anymore. The pistol takes two shots to the head to kill a walker. Why? When I bought this I was hoping for large environments and places to explore and loot I was wrong. The levels are designed like I'm a mouse in a maze that sometimes fills with water that forces me to get to the end faster. These are mostly just my rambling thoughts on why I don't like this game and would tell you that'd you be better off playing saints and sinners.Please go play saints and sinners if you want a good zombie vr game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. From reading reviews others try to compare it to Saints & Sinners which is entirely different game. Onslaught intended to be a fast-paced arcadey action, instead of survival and lurking in dark corridors kind of game, which is Saints & Sinners. Here you slash and smash some walkers, while keeping the pace. Gives you quite a bit of workout and fogged up my VR goggles. My complaint is that ranged weapons are too underpowered and melee weapons, especially with upgrades are overpowered. All you need is a battle axe with all upgrades and you can swing through walkers without an effort, while my fully upgraded assault rifle will take several shots, even to the head, just to take down one regular walker. Against armored walkers ranged weapons are pretty much useless. Nevertheless, I would recommend this game to any fan of Walking Dead and otherwise. Haven't started campaign yet, just the supply runs, maybe my review will change.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is terrible.  The tracers when you sprint actually make me sick and I never get motion sickness.  The sprinting seems to cancel if you look the wrong way, or face your controller the wrong way, or bump into something... way too many things interfere with that.  The knife is the only weapon you need, actually guns are worse to use.  Why does a walker take three shots to the head to kill, that's not even consistent with walking dead lore.  You can tell they made it that way because everything else was so laughably easy.  There is virtually nothing to interact with, not even doors.  Wonky physics for both zombies and weapons.  Glitchy as hell.  Terribly dumb mechanic to pressure you through the levels (a red wall that has cardboard textures of zombies walking towards you that if you cross you'll just lose hp). The game just feels like they never once thought about why they were building the systems they were building.  Like they never stopped to ask what makes a game fun underneath all the dressing.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky and Fundamentally unfun. I barely managed 30 minutes of this game before I wanted to rip my headset off and refund it.The concepts of the game aren't bad, in fact, they are quite intriguing and tap in the essence of a zombie survival experience, scavaging for supplies, fighting off the undead and rebuilding society.But unfortunately, Onslaught barely passes in aspects I should thrive in and fails in others.In many ways, this game feels like the VR equivalent of TWD Survival instinct and fails in arguably the most important department for me, the combat. Where one TWD Saints and Sinners' most enjoyable aspects were its combat and scavaging, Onslaught tries a similar style but does so in the most unenjoyable and clunky way, with stabbing walkers feeling like a passing a 1000 degree knife through soft butter, and Walkers taking multiple headshots from the starting pistol, even at point-blank range.Part of the problem might be the practically non-existent sound effects for melee'ing zombies, and the experience could be drastically improved if the sound effects had some crunch too them.Scavaging is simplified which does fit the games more arcade-style which does make the process more streamlined and fast, which isn't a negative in its own right, just different stylesLastly, the whole, Alexandria part, of the game, the rebuilding aspect of the game. To be fair i haven't truly played enough to see all of it, but if its as bare-bones as it appears, then my god, why even bother including it, its just window dressing, you cant explore Alexandria, your stuck behind a fence, and you have a small area about maybe 20 meters square to move around in.I don't doubt that a lot of work has gone into this game, and I have no illusions about how difficult game development is, especially with our little pandemic going on, but the main problems with this game go back almost to the original design documents and pitch for the game.Unless some major patches roll through and rework almost the entire game, I can't see myself ever picking this thing up again even at 70% off.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that most of the reviews here were expecting a VERY different game than what was advertised.What this game is not:-The walking dead: saints & sinners 2-An open world survival RPGWhat this game actually is:a Level based, zombie hack and slash  with looting mechanicsThe graphics are actually ok for what we are given. They aren't ground breaking or amazing, but they do get the job done.The gameplay is a tad clunky at first, but feels really good when you get going. what most people seem to forget is that this is a arcade experience; so don't expect things like stamina. the ranged weapons are a bit pitiful but I do understand why they are so weak; its to offset the fact that ammo is plentiful. This game is meant to be played as a stupid fun arcade experience rather than a story driven RPG. if you start treating this game less like a survival sim and more like an arcade action game; then you will have loads more fun with it.The voice acting is kinda bad but it doesn't really matter to me all that much since this game is meant as a arcade experience.The main problem is the price. If this game was $20 or $15; it wouldn't be so bad. $30 for the standard game is kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥. and its $40 for a deluxe edition that only contains some skins and a soundtrack; which seems a bit to steep for me to recommend. The deluxe edition is the same price as the base edition of TWD: SS; which is really bad for a game like this.as a side note; the game seems to crash often. IDK if it's just me, but i've experienced a few too many hard crashes that have hurt my experience. most of these seem to be out of memory errors or are generic UE4 errors. Either way, I cannot continue from where i'm at in the game since it keeps crashing at the end of the level; which seems to reset all my supplies.

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty  hyped for this game.. Bought it, found out that the Oculus Quest controls weren't even working properly. I was playing it through SteamVr wirelessly (VD), and for some reason the game messed up the controllers and as a result the buttons weren't mapped and I couldn't even make it through the tutorial. How do you release a game without even installing the proper controls? It does run through Oculus Link right now, but the reason most people play with an Oculus Quest on Steam is to play wirelessly. This works absolutely fine for other VR games (like Half Life Alyx, Saints and Sinners, and Boneworks). So yeah.. Asked for a refund. Regarding the gameplay itself: this does not feel or play like a AAA title. The trailer looks way more fun than the game actually is. Combat is very (very bland), there are no proper reload movements (just pop in the magazine, and the gun magically loads the rounds in the chamber), and the zombies are so weak that I'm quite sure you'll be able to finish the game with the knife you start out with. Maybe I was just expecting too much because the trailer really hyped it.. But this game felt more like a slightly newer version of Arizona Sunshine.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to change what I said about my review. First off, do I think this game is worth the $30 price point that I paid for? No, I do not. I think there were many problems about this game at launch for everyone, which should never be a studio's intentions. However, Survios has heard everyone's complaints and have in fact worked on polishing the game and making it better. I play on a Quest and Quest 2, and at launch I could only use Oculus Link, even though I was hoping I could use Virtual Desktop. Survios heard my complaint and fixed this issue, and even though it's not perfect, they at least took a chance on it and implemented it for Quest users. I could tell you the things I like about this game, like the satisfying walker kills, and the story mode, but I think there needs to be more added into this game in order to make it worth it for everyone. People want to see the Walking Dead Onslaught for what they were hoping for, not a game that has a bunch of holes in it. For example, maybe they could make the levels less linear. They could open up Alexandria instead of it being just one small area to where you build different buildings. And about that, I really see no point in me building alexandria and upgrading weapons when they honestly don't even do anything to effect the game. I never use guns because it takes 2-3 bullets to kill a walker, when it should take one to the head. As much as I enjoy the melee, I want to see better gunplay. I enjoy what I'm seeing so far in the game, but hopefully Survios decides to add more content to the game to make it really worth it because they're on the right track.Update October 19th:Survios is trying really hard to improve this game which I love. I personally love the walking dead and to see that they're really trying to fix this interpretation of it is amazing to me. With the new update, there are a lot of fixes to the game that people have been requesting, and I'm excited to try it out when I get the chance. Good work Survios.Update 10/28: I tried playing the new update for the first time and I think that Survios has honestly WORSENED THE ENTIRE GAME. The kills are no longer satisfying because when I pull out my melee weapon, the weapon doesn't even come out of the head most of the time. This game has became unplayable and I hope they can fix it because it was honestly better beforehand. The only good thing about this update is that guns are mostly one shot to the brain. I'm sad that the crossbow no longer one shots most of the time tho:( But serious the melee needs to go back to how it was because it was actually satisfying to go through all of those walkers.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are comparing this to saints and sinners, i wont. I will review this game based on my own likes and dislikes. Likes:- Close quarters combat: (The combat falls in both categories) Ive always wanted to decapitate a zombie with such a smooth cut... and i did, kudos to that. I liked some weapons like the axe and the katana.- Locomotion: Movement was fine they give you several varieties of turning and moving back and forth. I didnt experience any motion sickness or dizziness.- Graphics: The visuals of the game were ok. The lighting and the shadows are well implemented. The atmosphere change from the dark with red lights tutorial room to a mostly green park kind of threw me off guard and my eyes had to adjust for a little while.  -Sound effects: The sounds are pretty good and i love the fact that you can hit a container and make it clang.- Voice acting: i liked daryl's voice acting andddd thats itDislikes: - Close quarters combat (again): When i kill i zombie i want to feel like i killed it. When i clubber a zombie over the head with a massive wrench it akwardly slumps to the ground as if i barely grazed it with a tree branch. The knife mechanics are wonky, sometimes i dont directly stab a zombie, i either push them away or slash at their heads. - Guns: Guns are an abomination, shooting a zombie in the head once is useless and kind of gets on your nerves the longer you play the game. It was so bad in fact that even after i got the heavy pistol i stuck to my trusty swordplay.-"Alexandria": Every time you finish a mission the game spits you out in a basic cube where you can either talk to Daryl, rebuild Alexandria and go on a supply run. Why? - Hack and slash: I dont like the supply runs, i dont like timed trials in general especially in VR. Hurring up could throw you off balance and completly ruin the immersion. I want to enter a landmark like the workshop on the town street and explore it, not just run through it like a madman while smashing zombies' heads in.There is a bunch more i can cover but those are the only things i could think off at the top of my head.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I really wanted this game to be good but unfortunately fell short it almost every category I could think of. First of all I do want to thank Servios for making this game in the first place, I may not agree with a lot of their design choices but It is still neat to see our favourite walking dead characters brought to life in VR.1) The first major issue for me is the combat, the walkers seem to have very little presence and it honestly feels like I'm fighting paper enemies with how lazily I can stab my knife around and bop dozens of walkers without raising my heart beat even slightly. Melee weapons are just ridiculously strong compared to fire arms, 3 headshots with a pistol? Who signed off on that? Reloading is also automated to the point where the mags eject themselves and you hover your hand over your belt to pick up ammo and then to your gun to watch an animation play out of you loading the pistol and the gun cocking itself which is so immersion breaking. There are also no human enemies in this game which honestly signalled the beginning of the end for me, TWD haven't focused on walkers since season 2. Season 3 and beyond have been about how humans are the true threat and even though the human AI sucked in S&S I much prefer that to nothing at all2) The second issue is the lack of content, similar to saints and sinners you have story missions and the option to weave supply runs in between. I haven't played enough to see the whole story but after 40 minutes of playing I just didn't have the heart to keep playing because I knew after chapter 1 and the first supply mission I had experienced 90% of the game.3) The last issue is what the game 'tries to be' and what it ends up being. The game was advertised very similarly to Saints and Sinners in that its a walking dead game where you collect resources while progressing through a story but Onslaught ends up being much more of an arcade shooter than anything else. Running from the wall of walkers during the supply runs feels very uninspired even though it's very similar to the herd mechanic in S&S. I thought S&S felt cramped until I played this and I understand why multiplayer was cut, fitting up to 4 people on those tiny maps would be near impossible without no player clipping.In conclusion I feel like the IP was wasted on a game like this. Without multiplayer it opens up Onslaught to more direct comparisons with S&S and they are not flattering. With S&S outshining Onslaught in almost every category I cannot recommend this game until these issues are worked out because in the games current state I'm considering a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Played the game for another hour and I think they should rename it Walking Dead : Stabbing Walkers Til your Arm Falls off...Played the game for 2 hours give or take, As of now I can not recommend the game. I expect they will need to address some of the issues with a few updates so it might be best to wait it out or wait for a sale. You'd be better served going with Walking Dead Saints & Sinners. And I compare this game to that because they're both vying for the same thing. A single player experience. If co-op would have been kept in the game, there would be no competition from S&S but alas.. here we are.Pros:1. Weapons never break like they do in Saints & Sinners2. I got to rub Daryls headCons:1. The combat mechanics are terrible and unrealistic2. Guns take multiple head shots to take down a zombie at point blank range while you have them in a choke hold(This is probably stemming from their upgrade system and having to upgrade your guns to make them effective but geez louise you might as well just get practicing with your knife. It will be your best friend. I love the blade... The blades a part of me..) UPDATE: Even after upgrading to do more damage it STILL takes multiple head shots at point blank range to take down a walker. 3. There is a red line of death chasing you down a set path on every excursion you go on. This is annoying. S&S did it right by having a timer that would unleash an actual horde if you took too long but you had full freedom of movement to explore.4. No Co-Op (S&S didn't have co-op either but they didn't promise it early on either)5. Can't flip the direction of the knife im holding for stabbing zombies in the chin through the head.6. Grabbing and choking mechanics are not that fluid. Most of the time when going for a grab, you see the telltale bite icon indicating you just got bit. 7. No Valve index finger tracking support 8. No immersion. You aim at an object and hit the trigger to grab it. 9. Zombies flail around like they're completely weightless causing you to stumble as well trying to stab the f****rs!10. Can't cover yourself in zombie entrails to avoid detection like you can in Saints & Sinners.11. Zombies trip over other dead zombies  and fall right into you or fall backwards stumbling but not quite falling over(watch out for this because you may overextend your arms and hit any nearby solid objects in the real world). They have no weight.I will continue to play it and update this review as I go because I feel like 1 hour isn't really enough to form a solid opinion. Plus a lot of these issues are minor and can be fixed in future updates. Feel free to check out my initial gameplay footage from my Twitch VOD feed (NSFW)To the devs, If these issues get ironed out I will change my review to a recommended. I highly suggest you add the co-op mode because that is the only thing that will set this game apart and make it worth getting.
